2:200.arabic: لا فيما يظهر في الدنيا مما لا بقاء له ولعمري هذا الخطر مشترك بين المتكبر والمتكبر عليه ولكن حق على كل واحد أن يكون مصروف الهمة إلى نفسه مشغول القلب بخوفه لعاقبته لا أن يشتغل بخوف غيره فإن الشفيق بسوء الظن مولع وشفقه كل إنسان على نفسه فإذا حبس جماعة في جناية ووعدوا بأن تضرب رقابهم لم يتفرغوا لتكبر بعضهم على بعض وإن عمهم الخطر إذ شغل كل واحد نفسه عن الالتفات إلى هم غيره حتى كأن كل واحد هو وحده في مصيبته وخطره فإن قلت فكيف أبغض المبتدع في الله وأبغض الفاسق وقد أمرت ببغضهما ثم
2:200.english: The second matter: the scholar knows that pride befits none but God Almighty and Majestic alone, and that if he becomes proud, he becomes an object of God's wrath and abhorrence. God has loved from him that he humble himself, and has said to him: "You have standing with Me so long as you do not claim standing for yourself; but if you see standing for yourself, then you have no standing with Me." Thus he must inevitably impose upon himself that which his Master loves from him — and this removes arrogance from his heart, even if he were certain, for example, that he has no sin, or had imagined such a thing.
2:200.section_title_en: On the Eradication of Pride and the Cultivation of Humility — Section 869
2:200.anchors:
- Root: كسر (kasara)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To break, shatter, fracture; the breaking of a thing's integrity or resistance.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): انكسار النفس (the breaking of the self) denotes the crushing of egocentric haughtiness, a spiritual state wherein the soul's pretension to autonomy is shattered before divine majesty.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah) for physical breaking; metaphorical (Majaz) for the humbling of the proud heart — "انكسرت نفسه" as the soul's collapse from its vaunted station.
- Root: خطر (khatara)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To pass through the mind (خطر بباله); also peril, grave risk, momentous consequence.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): الخطر denotes the weighty stake or standing; in eschatological context, the ultimate peril of one's final end (خاتمة) — the decisive outcome that determines rank before God.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal for a thought crossing the mind; metaphorical for the magnitude of a matter's consequence — "الخطر العظيم" as the immense stakes of salvation or perdition.
- Root: ختم (khatama)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To seal, stamp, conclude; the final impression that fixes a thing's end.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): الخاتمة — the sealing of one's life-course; in Kalam, the terminal state (khatimah) that alone determines felicity (sa'adah) or misery (shaqawah), utterly hidden from creatures.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal for sealing a document; metaphorical for God's conclusive decree over a human's ultimate destiny.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد (Restriction & Focused Predication) — Constructions like "إنما يمكن بالتفكر" and "لا ينظر العاقل إلا إلى العاقبة" restrict the predicate exclusively to one term, emphasizing that humility is attainable solely through contemplation of the final end, and that the intelligent man looks only to the outcome.
2:200.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Condemnation of Pride and Conceit'

2:201.arabic: ربنا آتنا من لدنك رحمة وهيئ لنا من أمرنا رشدا ربنا آتنا في الدنيا حسنة وفي الآخرة حسنة وقنا عذاب النار ربنا إننا سمعنا مناديا ينادي للإيمان إلى قوله عز وجل إنك لا تخلف الميعاد ربنا لا تؤاخذنا إن نسينا أو أخطأنا ربنا إلى آخر السورة (3) رب اغفر لي ولوالدي وارحمهما كما ربياني صغيرا واغفر للمؤمنين والمؤمنات والمسلمين والمسلمات الأحياء منهم والأموات (4) رب اغفر وارحم وتجاوز عما تعلم وأنت الأعز الأكرم وأنت خير الراحمين وأنت خير الغافرين وإنا لله وإنا إليه راجعون ولا حول ولا قوة إلا بالله العلي العظيم وحسبنا الله ونعم الوكيل وصلى الله على محمد خاتم النب
2:201.english: And employ me in righteous deeds which You will accept from me. (1) O God, I ask You for pardon, well-being, good certainty, and soundness in this world and the next. (2) O You Whom sins do not harm and from Whom forgiveness does not diminish anything — grant me that which will not harm You, and give me that which will not diminish You. Our Lord, pour upon us patience and cause us to die as Muslims. You are our Protector in this world and the next; cause me to die as a Muslim and join me with the righteous. You are our Protector, so forgive us and have mercy upon us, and You are the Best of forgivers. And write for us good in this world and in the Hereafter — indeed, we have turned to You in repentance. Our Lord, upon You we rely, to You we turn in repentance, and to You is the final return. Our Lord, make us not a trial for the wrongdoing people. Our Lord, make us not a trial for those who disbelieve, and forgive us, our Lord — indeed, You are the Mighty, the Wise. Our Lord, forgive us our sins and our excesses in our affairs, make firm our feet, and grant us victory over the disbelieving people. Our Lord, forgive us and our brothers who preceded us in faith, and place not in our hearts any rancor toward those who believe — our Lord, indeed You are Kind, Merciful. Our Lord, grant us from Yourself mercy and prepare for us from our affair right guidance. Our Lord, give us good in this world and good in the Hereafter, and protect us from the chastisement of the Fire. Our Lord, indeed we have heard a caller calling to faith — to His saying, Mighty and Majestic: {«إنك لا تخلف الميعاد»} [آل عمران/ 194] — Our Lord, do not take us to task if we forget or err. Our Lord, to the end of the surah. (3) My Lord, forgive me and my parents, and have mercy upon them as they raised me when I was small; and forgive the believing men and the believing women, and the Muslim men and the Muslim women, the living among them and the dead. (4) My Lord, forgive, have mercy, and overlook what You know — and You are the Most Exalted, the Most Generous, the Best of the merciful, and the Best of the forgivers. And indeed, to God we belong and to Him we return; and there is no might and no power except through God, the Exalted, the Magnificent; and God suffices us, and He is the Best Disposer of affairs. And may God send blessings upon Muhammad, the Seal of the Prophets, and upon his family and his companions, and grant them abundant peace. (5)
2:201.section_title_en: Section 252 — Supplications for Morning and Evening: Comprehensive Prayers of the Prophet (ﷺ)
2:201.anchors:
- Root: لهم (l-h-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of swallowing/ingesting (iltihām); from this derives the sense of something being cast directly into the innermost recess of the heart (al-rawʿ).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الإلهام: إلقاء الشيء في الروع" — ilhām is the casting of a thing into the innermost consciousness, specifically from God or the higher assembly (al-malaʾ al-aʿlā). It is that which the Prophet (ﷺ) called "the touch of the angel" (limat al-malak) and "the breath of the Holy Spirit in my innermost heart" (nafth rūḥ al-qudus fī rawʿī).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): "ألهمه الله الخير: ألقاه في روعه" — God inspired him with good: He cast it into his innermost consciousness. Metaphorical (majāz): A horse that "swallows the ground" (yaltaḥimu al-arḍ) in swiftness; thus ilhām is the swift, direct ingress of divine guidance into the soul without intermediary effort.
- Root: حمد (ḥ-m-d)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The root denotes praise arising from recognition of voluntary excellence and beneficence; al-ḥamd is commendation of the beloved for their attributes and acts of goodness.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Praise (ḥamd) is the acknowledgment of beneficence (niʿmah) with reverence and love; it is distinguished from mere thanks (shukr) in that it is directed to the essence and attributes of the praised one, not solely to the benefit received.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "أحمد الله تعالى بجميع محامده" — I praise God with all His praiseworthy attributes. Metaphorical: "أحمدت صنيعه" — I found his deed praiseworthy; thus the tongue's praise must be matched by the heart's recognition of the praised one's perfection.
- Root: غفر (gh-f-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The root denotes covering and shielding; al-mighfar is the helmet that protects the head in battle.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الغفر: إلباس ما يصونه عن الدنس" — Forgiveness is the clothing of that which shields from filth. God's forgiveness (maghfirah) is His shielding of the servant from the touch of chastisement, covering the sin so that it is as though it never were.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "اللهم غفرًا" — O God, forgive. Metaphorical: The she-beasts that "did not forgive" their heedlessness (lam taghfir la-hā ghaflātuhā) — i.e., they did not shield their young from destruction; thus forgiveness is active protection, not mere erasure.
- Root: نفس (n-f-s)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The self, the soul; that which breathes and has vital spirit; also used for the very essence of a thing.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "النفس: الروح" — the soul is the spirit; and in God's saying {«ويحذركم الله نفسه»} [آل عمران/ 28], "His Self" means His very essence (dhāt), which — though grammatically expressed as an annexation implying distinction — is in reality identical, with no multiplicity in the Divine Essence.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "شيء نفيس" — a precious thing. Metaphorical: "دفق نفسه" — he poured out his blood/life; thus nafs is the seat of life, passion, and moral responsibility.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الدعاء والخبر (The Chapter of Supplication and Assertion) — Supplications (duʿāʾ) are grammatically constructed as optative sentences (inshāʾ ṭalabī) using the imperative (rabbighfir), the jussive (lā tuʾākhidhnā), and the vocative (rabbanā), yet they may embed assertive clauses (khabar) of praise (al-ḥamdu lillāh) and attestation (lā ilāha illā anta). The periodic structure of these prayers alternates between direct address to God (munādāh) and self-referential confession, requiring the translator to preserve the vocative force of "O God" and "Our Lord" without flattening into mere description.
2:201.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications, prayers, and their spiritual power, from 'On Invocations and Supplications'

2:201.arabic: الأعز الأكرم اللهم آتنا في الدنيا حسنة وفي الآخرة حسنة وقنا عذاب النار ويمشي على هينة حتى ينتهي إلى الميل الأخضر وهو أول ما يلقاه إذا نزل من الصفا وهو على زاوية المسجد الحرام فإذا بقي بينه وبين محاذاة الميل ستة أذرع أخذ في السير السريع وهو الرمل حتى ينتهي إلى الميلين الأخضرين ثم يعود إلى الهينة فإذا انتهى إلى المروة صعدها كما صعد الصفا وأقبل بوجهه على الصفا ودعا بمثل ذلك الدعاء وقد حصل السعي مرة واحدة فإذا عاد إلى الصفا حصلت مرتان يفعل ذلك سبعا ويرمل في موضع الرمل في كل مرة ويسكن في موضع السكون كما سبق وفي كل نوب
2:201.english: Upon ascending al-Ṣafā, he should face the House (al-Bayt) and say: "God is Greater, God is Greater. Praise be to God for what He has guided us to. Praise be to God with all His praises, for all His graces, all of them. There is no god but God alone, with no partner. His is the dominion, and His is the praise. He gives life and causes death; in His hand is all good, and He is over all things competent. There is no god but God alone; He fulfilled His promise, aided His servant, and honored His soldiers; He alone defeated the confederates. There is no god but God, devoting religion sincerely to Him, even if the disbelievers detest it. There is no god but God, devoting religion sincerely to Him. Praise be to God, Lord of the worlds. So exalted is God when you reach the evening and when you reach the morning. And His is the praise in the heavens and the earth, and at nightfall and when you are at noon. He brings forth the living from the dead and brings forth the dead from the living, and He revives the earth after its death, and thus shall you be brought forth. And of His signs is that He created you from dust; then, behold, you are humans spreading out. O God, I ask You for enduring faith, sincere certainty, beneficial knowledge, a humble heart, and a tongue that remembers You. And I ask You for pardon, well-being, and perpetual immunity in this world and the Hereafter." Then he sends blessings upon Muḥammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and supplicates God, Mighty and Majestic, with whatever need he wishes, following this supplication.
2:201.section_title_en: The Yemeni Corner and the Stone — The Beginning of the Saʿy and Its Rites
2:201.anchors:
- Root: سعي (Saʿy)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The root denotes striving, running, or rapid walking; it is the exertion of effort in a matter, whether good or evil.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "السعي: المشي السريع، وهو دون العدو، ويستعمل للجد في الأمر" — Saʿy is swift walking, less than running, and is used for earnest exertion in a matter. In the sacred rite, it signifies the ritual traversing between al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah, an act of devotional striving.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Ḥaqīqah): "سعى إلى المسجد" — physical exertion toward a goal. Metaphorical (Majāz): "هو يسعى على عياله" — he strives to provide for his family. In the ritual context, the physical traversing is the literal embodiment of devotional striving.
- Root: حمد (Ḥamd)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The root denotes praise, commendation, and the acknowledgment of beneficence; it is the opposite of blame (dhamm).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Praise (ḥamd) is the acknowledgment of beneficence with reverence and love, and it is due to God alone in His absolute perfection.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "أحمد الله تعالى بجميع محامده" — praising God with all His praises. Metaphorical: "أحمدت صنيعه" — I approved of his deed. In the supplications of the saʿy, the pilgrim's praise is both literal acknowledgment and the metaphorical "approval" of God's decree.
- Root: رمل (Raml)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The root denotes rapid walking with a slight trotting motion, a form of hastening in movement.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Not a primary theological term, but in ritual context it signifies the prescribed hastening between the two green markers, emulating the Prophet's action.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical hastening. Metaphorical: The rapid pace is a visible emblem of spiritual earnestness and the rejection of the polytheists' claim that the Muslims were weakened by fever.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Restriction and Specification (al-Ḥaṣr wa al-Taqyīd) — The phrase "وإنما ذلك شرط في طواف الركن" employs restriction to delimit a condition exclusively to the circumambulation of the pillar (ṭawāf al-rukn), thereby negating its applicability to the saʿy.
2:201.topic: Al-Ghazali on the journey of the soul, death, and the Hereafter, from 'Mysteries of Hajj'

2:201.arabic: الخزي في الدنيا والآخرة ويقول بين الركن اليماني والحجر الأسود اللهم ربنا آتنا في الدنيا حسنة وفي الآخرة حسنة وقنا برحمتك فتنة القبر وعذاب النار فإذا بلغ الحجر الأسود قال اللهم اغفر لي برحمتك أعوذ برب هذا الحجر من الدين والفقر وضيق الصدر وعذاب القبر وعند ذلك قد تم شوط واحد فيطوف كذلك سبعة أشواط فيدعو بهذه الأدعية في كل شوط الرابع أن يرمل في ثلاثة أشواط ويمشي في الأربعة الأخر
2:201.english: **The first:** that he observes the conditions of prayer (shurūṭ al-ṣalāh), namely: purification from ritual impurity (ṭahārat al-ḥadath) and from filth (al-khabath) in the garment, the body, and the place, and the covering of the nakedness (satr al-ʿawrah). For the circumambulation of the House is a prayer, but Allah Most High has permitted speech within it. And he should perform the iḍṭibāʿ (exposing the right shoulder) before beginning the circumambulation — which is to place the middle of his cloak (ridāʾ) under his right armpit and gather its two ends upon his left shoulder, letting one end hang behind his back and the other upon his chest. And he should cease the talbiyah (proclamation of "Labbayk") at the beginning of the circumambulation and occupy himself with the supplications (adʿiyah) which we shall mention.
2:201.section_title_en: The Fourth Section on the Circumambulation (al-Ṭawāf)
2:201.anchors:
- Root: طوف (ṭ-w-f)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "طاف بالشيء يطوف طوفا وطوافا: دار به. والطواف بالبيت عبادة."
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الطواف: الدوران حول الشيء، وخص في الشرع بالدوران حول البيت الحرام تعظيما له."
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "طاف بالبيت يطوف طوافا: دار حوله." Metaphorical: "طاف الخيال: ألمّ بالخاطر."
- Root: ضبع (ḍ-b-ʿ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الاضطباع: أن يدخل الرجل رداءه تحت إبطه الأيمن ويلقيه على منكبه الأيسر."
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الضبع: العضد، ومنه الاضطباع في الطواف وهو إبداء العضد."
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "اضطبع الرجل: أبدى عضده." Metaphorical: "اضطبع في الأمر: تشمر له."
- Root: رمل (r-m-l)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الرمل في المشي: سرعة المشي مع تقارب الخطى. والرمل في الطواف: سنة."
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الرمل: الهرولة في الطواف، وهو من سنن الحج."
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "رمل في مشيه: أسرع." Metaphorical: "رمل الحديث: زخرفه."
- Root: حجر (ḥ-j-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الحجر الأسود: حجر في الركن من البيت الحرام، يستلمه الطائف."
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الحجر: الجوهر الصلب المعروف، والحجر الأسود أشرف الأحجار."
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "الحجر الأسود: الحجر المعروف في الكعبة." Metaphorical: "رمي فلان بحجره: قرن بمثله."
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The rule governing the placement of prepositional phrases and their objects, ensuring grammatical coherence in complex ritual descriptions.
2:201.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications, prayers, and their spiritual power, from 'Mysteries of Hajj'

2:201.arabic: وقال الحسن في قوله تعالى {ربنا آتنا في الدنيا حسنة وفي الآخرة حسنة} إن الحسنة في الدنيا هي العلم والعبادة وفي الآخرة هي الجنة وقيل لبعض الحكماء أي الأشياء تقتنى قال الأشياء التي إذا غرقت سفينتك سبحت معك يعني العلم وقيل أراد بغرق السفينة هلاك بدنه بالموت وقال بعضهم من اتخذ الحكمة لجاما اتخذه الناس إماما ومن عرف بالحكمة لاحظته العيون بالوقار وقال الشافعي رحمة الله عليه من شرف العلم أن كل من نسب إليه ولو في شيء حقير فرح ومن رفع عنه حزن وقال عمر رضي الله عنه يا أيها الناس عليكم بالعلم فإن لله سبحانه رداء يحبه فمن طل
2:201.english: And al-Ḥasan, may God have mercy on him, said: "The ink of the scholars will be weighed against the blood of the martyrs, and the ink of the scholars will outweigh the blood of the martyrs."
2:201.section_title_en: The Book of Knowledge — Section 6: On the Virtue of Teaching and Learning (Continued)
2:201.anchors:
- Root: شغل (sh-gh-l)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Occupation, preoccupation, that which engages one entirely
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Preoccupation that veils one from perception of other things
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — physical occupation; Metaphorical — absorption of the heart that blinds the senses
- Root: حسن (ḥ-s-n)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Beauty, goodness, excellence
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الحسن: عبارة عن كل مبهج مرغوب فيه" — that which is pleasing and desirable, of three kinds: rational, appetitive, sensory
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — beauty of form; Metaphorical — the ḥasanah in the Qur'anic supplication denotes knowledge and worship
- Root: علم (ʿ-l-m) — [Note: recently used, but required by text; applied per governing rule]
  * Lisan / Ayn: Knowledge, perception, cognition
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "العلم: إدراك الشيء بحقيقته" — apprehension of a thing in its true reality
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — direct perception; Metaphorical — knowledge as a garment of honor from God
- Root: موت (m-w-t)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Death, cessation of life
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Death as the lifting of the burdens of this world; awakening from the sleep of heedlessness
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — physical death; Metaphorical — "الناس نيام فإذا ماتوا انتبهوا" (people are asleep; when they die, they awaken)
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — applied in the ḥadīth "إنما العلم بالتعلم" (knowledge is only attained through learning), restricting the means of acquiring knowledge to learning alone.
2:201.topic: Al-Ghazali on the journey of the soul, death, and the Hereafter, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

2:255.arabic: جبريل عليه السلام ويشاهده ومن حوله لا يسمعونه ولا يرونه (3) ولا يحيطون بشيء من علمه إلا بما شاء فإذا لم يخلق لهم السمع والرؤية لم يدركوه الأصل الثالث عذاب القبر وقد ورد الشرع به قال الله تعالى النار يعرضون عليها غدوا وعشيا ويوم تقوم الساعة أدخلوا آل فرعون أشد العذاب واشتهر عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم والسلف الصالح الاستعاذة من عذاب القبر (4) وهو ممكن فيجب التصديق به ولا يمنع من التصديق به تفرق أجزاء الميت في بطون السباع وحواصل الطيور فإن المدرك لألم العذاب من الحيوان أجزاء مخصوصة يقدر الله تعالى على إعادة الإدراك إليها الأصل الر
2:255.english: For they, despite their distinction in eloquence and rhetorical perfection, aimed at reviling him, forbidding him, killing him, and expelling him — as God, Mighty and Majestic, informed us about them — yet they were unable to produce anything to rival the Qur'an. For it was not within the capacity of human beings to combine the grandeur of the Qur'an's diction with its harmonious order, especially given what it contains of the accounts of the ancients, while he was illiterate, never having practiced the study of books — and [given] its announcement of the unseen in matters whose truthfulness was verified in the future, such as His saying, Exalted is He: {«لَتَدْخُلُنَّ الْمَسْجِدَ الْحَرَامَ إِنْ شَاءَ اللَّهُ آمِنِينَ مُحَلِّقِينَ رُءُوسَكُمْ وَمُقَصِّرِينَ»} (You shall surely enter the Sacred Mosque, if God wills, secure, with your heads shaved and cut short) [Al-Fatḥ 48:27], and such as His saying: {«الم غُلِبَتِ الرُّومُ فِي أَدْنَى الْأَرْضِ وَهُمْ مِنْ بَعْدِ غَلَبِهِمْ سَيَغْلِبُونَ فِي بِضْعِ سِنِينَ»} (Alif Lām Mīm. The Romans have been defeated in the nearest land, and they, after their defeat, shall be victorious within a few years) [Al-Rūm 30:1-3].
2:255.section_title_en: The Fourth Pillar: On Matters of Hearing (al-Samʿiyyāt) and the Verification of the Prophet ﷺ in What He Reported — Comprising Ten Fundamental Principles
2:255.anchors:
- Root: حشر (ḥ-sh-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To gather, assemble, drive together; al-ḥashr is the gathering of creation on the Day of Resurrection.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-ḥashr is the bringing together of a people from their various places of dispersal; it is used specifically for the resurrection gathering.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) for driving cattle together; metaphorical (majāz) for the ingathering of souls for judgment.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Conditional Protasis (al-sharṭ) — "If you are truthful, then rise..." (fa-in kunta ṣādiqan fa-qum...) — the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) functions as the proof of the protasis, establishing necessary knowledge (ʿilm ḍarūrī).

- Root: نشر (n-sh-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To spread, unfold, revive after death; al-nushūr is the revivification of the dead.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-nashr is the spreading of the soul back into the body after death; it is the opposite of al-ṭayy (folding up).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal for unfolding a garment; metaphorical for the resurrection when the earth "spreads forth" what it contains.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Coordination (al-ʿaṭf) — "al-ḥashr wa-l-nashr" (the gathering and the spreading) — two coordinated nouns forming a single compound concept of resurrection.

- Root: مكن (m-k-n)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To establish, empower, give firm footing; makkana means to make something firm and stable.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-makān is the place that contains a thing; tamakkun is the firm establishment of a thing in its place.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal for physical placement; metaphorical for divine power — "God is able" (qādir) means He has full capacity and authority over all things.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Possibility (al-imkān) — "that is possible" (dhālika mumkin) — the predicate of possibility is established by the absence of logical contradiction, not by empirical observation.

- Root: عذب (ʿ-dh-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Sweet, pleasant (of water); al-ʿadhāb is the punishment that is "sweet" to the inflictor but bitter to the recipient — used predominantly for divine chastisement.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-ʿadhāb is the infliction of pain that deters; it is specifically the painful consequence of disobedience.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal for sweet water; metaphorical (majāz) for punishment that is "appointed" as a deterrent.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Exception (al-istithnāʾ) — "except as God wills" (illā mā shāʾa) — the exception clause restricts the scope of human perception, not divine action.
2:255.topic: Al-Ghazali on the journey of the soul, death, and the Hereafter, from 'Contemplation'

2:255.arabic: وجل في كلام يردده في نفسه كما لو سمع وهو يقول {إنني أنا الله لا إله إلا أنا فاعبدني} فإنه ما كان ينبغي أن يفهم منه ذلك إلا على سبيل الحكاية الصنف الثاني من الشطح كلمات غير مفهومة لها ظواهر رائقة وفيها عبارات هائلة وليس وراءها طائل إما أن تكون غير مفهومة عند قائلها بل يصدرها عن خبط في عقله وتشويش في خياله لقلة إحاطته بمعنى كلام قرع سمعه وهذا هو الأكثر وإما أن تكون مفهومة له ولكنه لا يقدر على تفهيمها وإيرادها بعبارة تدل على ضميره لقلة ممارسته للعلم وعدم تعلمه طريق التعبير عن المعاني بالألفاظ الرشيقة ولا فائدة لهذا الجنس من الكلام إلا أ
2:255.english: Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ, may God be pleased with him, said to his son ʿUmar — having heard him composing sajʿ — "This is what makes me dislike you. I will never fulfill your need until you repent." This was said when his son had come to him seeking a favor. And the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to ʿAbd Allāh ibn Rawāḥah when he spoke in sajʿ of three words: "Beware of sajʿ, O Ibn Rawāḥah." Thus, the forbidden sajʿ is the artificially contrived kind that exceeds two words. For this reason, when a man spoke concerning the blood-money for a fetus — saying, "How shall we pay blood-money for one who neither drank, nor ate, nor cried out, nor wailed? Such a one's blood is void" — the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, replied: "Sajʿ like the sajʿ of the bedouins!"
2:255.section_title_en: On the Etiquette of Preaching: The Condemnation of Artificial Sajʿ, Excessive Poetry, and the Perils of Shataḥ and Taʿwīl
2:255.anchors:
- Root: سجع (sajʿa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Rhymed prose; from the root meaning "to coo" (as a dove), indicating a measured, melodious cadence in speech.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In theological discourse, sajʿ is permissible when natural but blameworthy when artificially cultivated (takalluf), as it shifts focus from meaning to ornamentation.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) — natural rhythmic speech; Metaphorical (majāz) — the "sajʿ of the bedouins" (sajʿ al-aʿrāb) as a pejorative for empty, affected eloquence.
- Root: شعر (shiʿr)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Poetry; from the root denoting perception and fine discernment (shuʿūr), as the poet grasps subtle meanings.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Poetry is blameworthy when it stirs base appetites, but praiseworthy when it conveys wisdom (ḥikmah), as in the prophetic saying "Indeed from poetry there is wisdom."
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — metered, rhymed speech; Metaphorical — the "poetry" of the heart's inclination, where listeners project their own passions onto what they hear.
- Root: شطح (shaṭaḥa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To overflow, to gush forth; originally of a water-skin bursting, then applied to ecstatic utterances that overflow the bounds of conventional discourse.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In Sufi terminology, shataḥ refers to utterances arising from overwhelming spiritual states (ḥāl) that, when voiced to the unworthy, cause corruption.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — physical overflowing; Metaphorical — the soul's overflow in speech that exceeds the speaker's intentional control.
- Root: أول (taʿwīl)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To return something to its origin or end; interpretation that traces a word back to its intended meaning.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Taʿwīl is legitimate only when supported by textual (naqlī) or rational (ʿaqlī) evidence; arbitrary taʿwīl that severs words from their established senses destroys religious trust.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — the apparent sense (ẓāhir); Metaphorical — the inner sense (bāṭin), which is only valid when the literal sense is impossible or when transmitted authority sanctions it.
- Sibawayh Rule: Bāb al-Ḥaṣr wa al-Taqyīd bi-innamā (Restriction and Focused Predication) — The text repeatedly uses restrictive constructions (innamā, laysa...illā) to delimit permissible preaching, poetry, and interpretation, distinguishing the praiseworthy from the blameworthy with syntactic precision.
2:255.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications, prayers, and their spiritual power, from 'Arrangement of Litanies'

2:255.arabic: الحياة والقدرة وأنه تعالى حي قادر جبار قاهر لا يعتريه قصور ولا عجز ولا تأخذه سنة ولا نوم ولا يعارضه فناء ولا موت وأنه ذو الملك والملكوت والعزة والجبروت له السلطان والقهر والخلق والأمر والسموات مطويات بيمينه والخلائق مقهورون في قبضته وأنه المنفرد بالخلق والاختراع المتوحد بالإيجاد والإبداع خلق الخلق وأعمالهم وقدر أرزاقهم وآجالهم لا يشذ عن قبضته مقدور ولا يعزب عن قدرته تصاريف الأمور لا تحصى مقدوراته ولا تتباهى معلوماته العلم وأنه عالم بجميع المعلومات محيط بما يجري من تخوم الأرضين إلى أعلى السموات وأنه عالم لا يعزب عن علمه مثقال ذرة في
2:255.english:
- **Root: خلق (khalaqa)**
  - *Lisan / Ayn:* Core meaning of measuring, proportioning, and fashioning; al-Khalil notes the root's application to the act of creation as bringing forth upon a measured determination.
  - *Al-Raghib (Mufradat):* "الخلق أصله: التقدير المستقيم" — Creation fundamentally signifies right/straight measurement; used for bringing into being from nothing (ibdāʿ) as in {خلق السماوات والأرض}, and for bringing forth from something as in {خلقكم من نفس واحدة}.
  - *Al-Zamakhshari (Asas):* Literal (ḥaqīqah): the craftsman's measuring before cutting. Metaphorical (majāz): "خلق الله الخلق: أوجده على تقدير أوجبته الحكمة" — God's creation is bringing into existence upon a measure necessitated by wisdom.
2:255.topic: Al-Ghazali on the journey of the soul, death, and the Hereafter, from 'Foundations of Belief'

2:255.arabic: وعنه العبارة بقوله تعالى {ولا يشفعون إلا لمن ارتضى} وبقوله {من ذا الذي يشفع عنده إلا بإذنه} وبقوله {ولا تنفع الشفاعة عنده إلا لمن أذن له} وبقوله {فما تنفعهم شفاعة الشافعين} وإذا انقسمت الذنوب إلا ما يشفع فيه وإلا ما لا يشفع فيه وجب الخوف والإشفاق لا محالة ولو كان ذنب تقبل فيه الشفاعة لما أمر قريشا بالطاعة ولما نهى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فاطمة رضي الله عنها عن المعصية ولكان يأذن لها في اتباع الشهوات لتكمل لذاتها في الدنيا ثم يشفع لها في الآخرة لتكمل لذاتها في الآخرة فالانهماك في الذنوب وترك التقوى اتكالا على رجاء الشفاعة يضاهي ان
2:255.english: If you say: "He, peace and blessings be upon him, said after his words to Fāṭimah and Ṣafiyyah: 'I cannot avail you against God in anything, except that you have a tie of kinship which I will moisten with its moisture'" — a ḥadīth [reported as]: "Do you hope for my intercession, while the Banū ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib do not hope for it?" — narrated by al-Ṭabarānī in al-Awsaṭ from the narration of ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jaʿfar, and in it is Uṣayrim ibn Ḥawshab from Isḥāq ibn Wāṣil, and both are extremely weak — so that indicates that he will single out his relatives for intercession.
2:255.section_title_en: Section 882 — On the Limits of Intercession, the Vices of Pride in Lineage, Numbers, Wealth, and Opinion, and Their Treatment
2:255.anchors:
- Root: شفع (Sh-F-')
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning is pairing or joining; intercession (shafā'ah) is the joining of one's plea to another's cause.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Intercession is the seeking of benefit for another; its acceptance is contingent upon divine permission and good pleasure, as restricted by the Qur'anic qualifiers.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (haqīqah) is the act of making a number even (from watr, odd); metaphorical (majāz) is the mediator's plea before authority.
- Root: عجب (ʿ-J-B)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Astonishment arising from an unknown cause; self-admiration (ʿujb) is a blameworthy state of being pleased with oneself.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "العجب والتعجب: حالة تعرض للإنسان عند الجهل بسبب الشيء" — a state that overtakes a person due to ignorance of the cause; hence, it is impossible regarding God.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: a wondrous thing; metaphorical: the one who performs marvels (taʿjābah). Self-admiration is the root of every error and innovation.
- Root: رأي (R-'-Y)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Opinion, view, or judgment formed through reflection.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Ra'y is the considered opinion that may err or hit the mark; it is blameworthy when it becomes an object of ʿujb (self-admiration).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: sight/vision; metaphorical: intellectual insight. The ḥadīth "إعجاب كل ذي رأي برأيه" (the admiration of every man of opinion for his own view) is cited as a sign of the age's corruption.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد (Restriction and Qualification) — The conditional clauses (in-sharṭ) governing intercession, e.g., {إلا لمن ارتضى} and {إلا بإذنه}, impose necessary restrictions that negate any absolute reliance on intercession.
2:255.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Condemnation of Pride and Conceit'

2:255.arabic: الذي لا تأخذه سنة ولا نوم لم يسأل الله تعالى شيئا إلا أعطاه وقال بعض السلف من أطعم مسكينا يوم الجمعة ثم غدا وابتكر ولم يؤذ أحدا ثم قال حين يسلم الإمام بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم الحي القيوم أسألك أن تغفر لي وترحمني وتعافيني من النار ثم دعا بما بدا له استجيب له السابع أن يجعل يوم الجمعة للآخرة فيكف فيه عن جميع أشغال الدنيا ويكثر فيه الأوراد ولا يبتدىء فيه السفر فقد روي أنه من سافر في ليلة الجمعة دعا عليه ملكاه (1) وهو بعد طلوع الفجر حرام إلا إذا كانت الرفقة تفوت وكره بعض السلف شرا
2:255.english: Know that among the proprieties of Friday is that one should be excellent in watching for the noble hour. For in the well-known report: {«Indeed in Friday there is an hour in which no Muslim servant asks God, Mighty and Majestic, for anything but that He grants it to him»}. And in another report: {«No servant coincides with it while praying»}.
2:255.section_title_en: The Revival of the Religious Sciences — Section 151: On the Virtues of Friday and Its Proprieties
2:255.anchors:
- Root: ر-ق-ب (raqaba)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To watch, observe, lie in wait for; the watcher (rāqib) is one who awaits expectantly.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Moral vigilance (murāqabah) is the soul's persistent attentiveness to what it anticipates, whether of benefit or harm.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: watching a road or pass. Metaphorical: the heart's standing guard over the appointed time, as one watches for the crescent moon.
- Root: ن-ف-ح (nafaḥa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To blow gently, to emit a breeze; nafaḥāt are gentle, diffusive emanations.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Divine effusions of mercy that sweep over the servant unexpectedly.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: a fragrant breeze. Metaphorical: the breaths of divine mercy that pass over the days of time.
- Root: خ-ط-ب (khaṭaba)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To address, deliver an oration; khuṭbah is the formal sermon.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The prophetic address conveying command and prohibition.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: oration. Metaphorical: the preacher's ascent to the pulpit marks the threshold of the answered hour.
- Sibawayh Rule: Interposition of the conditional clause (jawāb al-sharṭ) — the apodosis may be delayed or elided when the protasis is governed by a particle of expectation, as in "whoever does X, God forgives him," where the response is the reward predicated upon the condition.
2:255.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications, prayers, and their spiritual power, from 'Mysteries of Prayer'

2:259.arabic: أعلم أن الله على كل شيء قدير وأن الله قد أحاط بكل شيء علما وأحصى كل شيء عددا اللهم إني أعوذ بك من شر نفسي ومن شر كل دابة أنت آخذ بناصيتها إن ربي على صراط مستقيم (1) دعاء الخليل إبراهيم عليه الصلاة والسلام كان يقول إذا أصبح اللهم إن هذا خلق جديد فافتحه علي بطاعتك واختمه لي بمغفرتك ورضوانك وارزقني فيه حسنة تقبلها مني وزكها وضعفها لي وما عملت فيه من سيئة فاغفرها لي إنك غفور رحيم ودود كريم قال ومن دعا بهذا الدعاء إذا أصبح فقد أدى شكر يومه دعاء عيسى عليه ال
2:259.english: And it is related that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said to him: "O Buraydah, shall I not teach you words which, if anyone desires good through them, he is taught them, and then he never forgets them ever?" He said: "I said, 'Yes, O Messenger of Allah.'" He said: "Say: 'O Allah, I am weak, so strengthen my weakness in Your pleasure, and take me by my forelock toward goodness, and make Islam the limit of my contentment. O Allah, I am weak, so strengthen me; and I am abased, so honor me; and I am poor, so enrich me, O Most Merciful of the merciful.'" (2)
2:259.section_title_en: The Revival of the Religious Sciences — Section 248: Supplications of the Companions and Prophets (Peace Be Upon Them)
2:259.anchors:
- Root: دعو (d-'-w)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of calling, invoking, summoning; du'a as the act of calling upon God with humble petition.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance of du'a as the essence of worship ('ibadah), the creature's acknowledgment of need (iftaqar) before the Creator.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (haqiqah) — to call out; Metaphorical (majaz) — the soul's inward turning to God, transcending mere vocal utterance.
- Root: وقي (w-q-y)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To protect, guard, preserve from harm; the root of taqwa (God-consciousness) and ittiqa (self-preservation from divine displeasure).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The theological state of being shielded by God's grace through the performance of obligations and abstention from prohibitions.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — physical protection; Metaphorical — spiritual safeguarding of the heart from worldly attachment.
- Root: حول (h-w-l)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Power, might, capacity to change or transform; the ability to effect motion or cessation.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In the formula "لا حول ولا قوة إلا بالله" (lā ḥawla wa lā quwwata illā billāh), it denotes the creature's absolute incapacity and total reliance on divine power (quwwah) for all acts of obedience and avoidance of sin.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — physical strength; Metaphorical — the spiritual power granted by God to overcome one's lower self (nafs).
- Root: فقر (f-q-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Poverty, neediness, lack of possessions; the state of one who requires what he does not possess.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The ontological poverty of all creatures before God — "يا أيها الناس أنتم الفقراء إلى الله" {O mankind, you are the poor in need of Allah} [Fatir: 15]. This is the existential need that defines creaturehood.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — material poverty; Metaphorical — the soul's recognition of its utter dependence on God for guidance, sustenance, and salvation.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The permissibility of interposing elements between a preposition and its object when the intervening phrase constitutes a complete and meaningful utterance, as seen in the extended invocations where multiple clauses are joined by conjunctions (wa) before the governing verb's object is completed.
2:259.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications, prayers, and their spiritual power, from 'On Invocations and Supplications'

2:259.arabic: شيء يسير فقال له عمر حسبك بصحبته يوما أو بعض يوم شؤما وشرا وقال الفضيل ما ازداد رجل من ذي سلطان قربا إلا ازداد من الله بعدا وكان سعيد بن المسيب يتجر في الزيت ويقول إن في هذا لغنى عن هؤلاء السلاطين وقال وهيب هؤلاء الذين يدخلون على الملوك لهم أضر على الأمة من المقامرين وقال محمد بن سلمة الذباب على العذرة أحسن من قارئ على باب هؤلاء ولما خالط الزهري السلطان كتب أخ له في الدين إليه عافانا الله وإياك أبا بكر من الفتن فقد أصبحت بحال ينبغي لمن عرفك أن يدعوا لك الله ويرحمك أصبحت شيخا كبيرا قد أثقلتك
2:259.english: As for the reports: When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, described the tyrannical rulers, he said: "Whoever opposes them is saved, whoever withdraws from them is safe — or nearly safe — and whoever falls in with them in their worldly affairs is of them." (1)
2:259.section_title_en: The Sixth Chapter: On What is Lawful and Unlawful in Associating with Tyrannical Rulers, and the Ruling on Frequent Their Assemblies, Entering Upon Them, and Showing Them Honor
2:259.anchors:
- Root: ظلم (Ẓ-L-M)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning is placing something in other than its proper place; darkness as the absence of light.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الظلمة: عدم النور" — darkness is the absence of light; used metaphorically for ignorance, polytheism, and transgression, as opposed to light (نور) which represents knowledge and justice.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): "الظلم ظلمة كما أن العدل نور" — injustice is darkness just as justice is light. Metaphorical (Majaz): "أرض مظلومة" — land never dug or watered, indicating the deprivation of benefit.
- Root: وهي (W-H-Y)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Weakness, fissure, or slackening in a structure; a crack in leather or a wall.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الوهي: شق في الأديم والثوب" — a rent in hide or cloth; "وكل شيء استرخى رباطه فقد وهي" — anything whose binding slackens has become weak.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "وهى الحائط" — the wall cracked. Metaphorical: "واهي العزالي" — clouds pouring forth rain, i.e., their water-skins have burst open.
- Root: خبر (KHB-R)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Knowledge of a thing from report or direct experience; testing and ascertaining.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الخبر: العلم بالأشياء المعلومة من جهة الخبر" — knowledge of things from the channel of report; "الخبرة المعرفة ببواطن الأمر" — experiential knowledge of the inner realities of affairs.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "خبرت الرجل واختبرته خبرا وخبرة" — I tested the man and gained knowledge of him. Metaphorical: "تخبر عن مجهوله مرآته" — one's mirror reveals his unknown state.
- Root: وفي (W-F-Y)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Completeness, fulfillment, and reaching full measure.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الوافي: الذي بلغ التمام" — that which has attained completion; "أوفى: إذا تمم العهد ولم ينقض حفظه" — fulfilled the covenant and did not breach its preservation.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "درهم واف" — a full-weight dirham. Metaphorical: "أوفى على المائة" — he surpassed a hundred; "توفاه الله" — God took him in full, i.e., completed his term.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — Governing the exclusive restriction of predication, as in "فليس مني ولست منه" (he is not of me, nor am I of him), where the negation establishes complete disassociation.
2:259.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'The Lawful and Prohibited'

2:286.arabic: قوله عز وجل إنك لا تخلف الميعاد ربنا لا تؤاخذنا إن نسينا أو أخطأنا ربنا إلى آخر السورة (3) رب اغفر لي ولوالدي وارحمهما كما ربياني صغيرا واغفر للمؤمنين والمؤمنات والمسلمين والمسلمات الأحياء منهم والأموات (4) رب اغفر وارحم وتجاوز عما تعلم وأنت الأعز الأكرم وأنت خير الراحمين وأنت خير الغافرين وإنا لله وإنا إليه راجعون ولا حول ولا قوة إلا بالله العلي العظيم وحسبنا الله ونعم الوكيل وصلى الله على محمد خاتم النبيين وآله وصحبه وسلم تسليما كثيرا (5)
2:286.english: And employ me in righteous deeds which You will accept from me. (1) O God, I ask You for pardon, well-being, good certainty, and soundness in this world and the next. (2) O You Whom sins do not harm and from Whom forgiveness does not diminish anything — grant me that which will not harm You, and give me that which will not diminish You. Our Lord, pour upon us patience and cause us to die as Muslims. You are our Protector in this world and the next; cause me to die as a Muslim and join me with the righteous. You are our Protector, so forgive us and have mercy upon us, and You are the Best of forgivers. And write for us good in this world and in the Hereafter — indeed, we have turned to You in repentance. Our Lord, upon You we rely, to You we turn in repentance, and to You is the final return. Our Lord, make us not a trial for the wrongdoing people. Our Lord, make us not a trial for those who disbelieve, and forgive us, our Lord — indeed, You are the Mighty, the Wise. Our Lord, forgive us our sins and our excesses in our affairs, make firm our feet, and grant us victory over the disbelieving people. Our Lord, forgive us and our brothers who preceded us in faith, and place not in our hearts any rancor toward those who believe — our Lord, indeed You are Kind, Merciful. Our Lord, grant us from Yourself mercy and prepare for us from our affair right guidance. Our Lord, give us good in this world and good in the Hereafter, and protect us from the chastisement of the Fire. Our Lord, indeed we have heard a caller calling to faith — to His saying, Mighty and Majestic: {«إنك لا تخلف الميعاد»} [آل عمران/ 194] — Our Lord, do not take us to task if we forget or err. Our Lord, to the end of the surah. (3) My Lord, forgive me and my parents, and have mercy upon them as they raised me when I was small; and forgive the believing men and the believing women, and the Muslim men and the Muslim women, the living among them and the dead. (4) My Lord, forgive, have mercy, and overlook what You know — and You are the Most Exalted, the Most Generous, the Best of the merciful, and the Best of the forgivers. And indeed, to God we belong and to Him we return; and there is no might and no power except through God, the Exalted, the Magnificent; and God suffices us, and He is the Best Disposer of affairs. And may God send blessings upon Muhammad, the Seal of the Prophets, and upon his family and his companions, and grant them abundant peace. (5)
2:286.section_title_en: Section 252 — Supplications for Morning and Evening: Comprehensive Prayers of the Prophet (ﷺ)
2:286.anchors:
- Root: لهم (l-h-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of swallowing/ingesting (iltihām); from this derives the sense of something being cast directly into the innermost recess of the heart (al-rawʿ).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الإلهام: إلقاء الشيء في الروع" — ilhām is the casting of a thing into the innermost consciousness, specifically from God or the higher assembly (al-malaʾ al-aʿlā). It is that which the Prophet (ﷺ) called "the touch of the angel" (limat al-malak) and "the breath of the Holy Spirit in my innermost heart" (nafth rūḥ al-qudus fī rawʿī).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): "ألهمه الله الخير: ألقاه في روعه" — God inspired him with good: He cast it into his innermost consciousness. Metaphorical (majāz): A horse that "swallows the ground" (yaltaḥimu al-arḍ) in swiftness; thus ilhām is the swift, direct ingress of divine guidance into the soul without intermediary effort.
- Root: حمد (ḥ-m-d)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The root denotes praise arising from recognition of voluntary excellence and beneficence; al-ḥamd is commendation of the beloved for their attributes and acts of goodness.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Praise (ḥamd) is the acknowledgment of beneficence (niʿmah) with reverence and love; it is distinguished from mere thanks (shukr) in that it is directed to the essence and attributes of the praised one, not solely to the benefit received.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "أحمد الله تعالى بجميع محامده" — I praise God with all His praiseworthy attributes. Metaphorical: "أحمدت صنيعه" — I found his deed praiseworthy; thus the tongue's praise must be matched by the heart's recognition of the praised one's perfection.
- Root: غفر (gh-f-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The root denotes covering and shielding; al-mighfar is the helmet that protects the head in battle.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الغفر: إلباس ما يصونه عن الدنس" — Forgiveness is the clothing of that which shields from filth. God's forgiveness (maghfirah) is His shielding of the servant from the touch of chastisement, covering the sin so that it is as though it never were.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "اللهم غفرًا" — O God, forgive. Metaphorical: The she-beasts that "did not forgive" their heedlessness (lam taghfir la-hā ghaflātuhā) — i.e., they did not shield their young from destruction; thus forgiveness is active protection, not mere erasure.
- Root: نفس (n-f-s)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The self, the soul; that which breathes and has vital spirit; also used for the very essence of a thing.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "النفس: الروح" — the soul is the spirit; and in God's saying {«ويحذركم الله نفسه»} [آل عمران/ 28], "His Self" means His very essence (dhāt), which — though grammatically expressed as an annexation implying distinction — is in reality identical, with no multiplicity in the Divine Essence.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "شيء نفيس" — a precious thing. Metaphorical: "دفق نفسه" — he poured out his blood/life; thus nafs is the seat of life, passion, and moral responsibility.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الدعاء والخبر (The Chapter of Supplication and Assertion) — Supplications (duʿāʾ) are grammatically constructed as optative sentences (inshāʾ ṭalabī) using the imperative (rabbighfir), the jussive (lā tuʾākhidhnā), and the vocative (rabbanā), yet they may embed assertive clauses (khabar) of praise (al-ḥamdu lillāh) and attestation (lā ilāha illā anta). The periodic structure of these prayers alternates between direct address to God (munādāh) and self-referential confession, requiring the translator to preserve the vocative force of "O God" and "Our Lord" without flattening into mere description.
2:286.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications, prayers, and their spiritual power, from 'On Invocations and Supplications'

2:286.arabic: بقوله {لا يكلف الله نفسا إلا وسعها} فظهر به أن كل ما لا يدخل تحت الوسع من أعمال القلب هو الذي لا يؤاخذ به فهذا هو كشف الغطاء عن هذا الالتباس وكل من يظن أن كل ما يجري على القلب يسمى حديث النفس ولم يفرق بين هذه الأقسام الثلاثة فلا بد وأن يغلط وكيف لا يؤاخذ بأعمال القلب من الكبر والعجب والرياء والنفاق والحسد وجملة الخبائث من أعمال القلب بل السمع والبصر والفؤاد كل أولئك كان عنه مسئولا أي ما يدخل تحت الاختيار فلو وقع البصر بغير اختيار على غير ذي محرم لم يؤاخذ به فإن أتبعها نظرة ث
2:286.english: The proof that the mere thought and the initial inclination are not held against the servant is that which is firmly established from the Messenger of God — peace be upon him — that he said: "God has pardoned my community for what their souls whisper to them, so long as they do not speak of it or act upon it." And he said — peace be upon him: "When two Muslims meet with their swords, then the killer and the killed are both in the Fire." It was said: "O Messenger of God, this is the killer — but what of the killed?" He said: "Because he intended to kill his companion." {«التقى المسلمان بسيفيهما فالقاتل والمقتول في النار»} — and his being held accountable was solely for his intention (niyyah) and his resolution, not for the mere thought that crossed his heart, for the thought of killing is not within one's capacity to prevent, while the resolution to kill is.
2:286.section_title_en: Exposition of What the Servant is Held Accountable For from the Whispers of the Hearts, Their Anxieties, Their Thoughts, and Their Intentions — and What is Pardoned and Not Held Against Him
2:286.anchors:
- Root: وسوس (w-s-w-s)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The faint, concealed sound; the subtle, indistinct voice that inclines one toward something
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The insinuation that enters the heart covertly, whether from Satan or from the self's inclination
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — the faint jingling of an ornament; Metaphorical — the secret prompting that stirs within the breast
- Root: خطر (kh-t-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To come to mind; the passing of a thought across the heart without deliberate pursuit
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The sudden occurrence of a notion in the mind, whether invited or uninvited
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — something that presents itself; Metaphorical — the fleeting thought that crosses the heart like a passing traveler
- Root: هم (h-m-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The intention that inclines one toward an act before resolution is firmly settled
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The initial stirring of the will toward an action, preceding the firm resolve ('azm)
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — to intend; Metaphorical — the heart's leaning that, if unchecked, hardens into determination
- Root: قصد (q-s-d)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The deliberate aiming toward a goal; the firm resolution that governs the limbs
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The settled intention that directs action and for which one is justly held accountable
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — to walk a straight path to a destination; Metaphorical — the will's firm orientation that constitutes the essence of moral agency
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين المبتدأ والخبر (The Interposition Between Subject and Predicate) — governing the periodic structure of conditional accountability clauses where the protasis (condition) and apodosis (result) are separated by explanatory parentheticals, preserving the logical dependency of moral judgment upon the specification of the act's nature.
2:286.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Disciplining the Soul'

2:286.arabic: خلافا للمعتزلة ولو لم يجز ذلك لاستحال سؤال دفعه وقد سألوا ذلك فقالوا ربنا ولا تحملنا ما لا طاقة لنا به ولأن الله تعالى أخبر نبيه صلى الله عليه وسلم بأن أبا جهل لا يصدقه ثم أمره بأن يأمره بأن يصدقه في جميع أقواله وكان من جملة أقواله أنه لا يصدقه فكيف يصدقه في أنه لا يصدقه وهل هذا إلا محال وجوده الأصل السادس أن لله عز وجل إيلام الخلق وتعذيبهم من غير جرم سابق ومن غير ثواب لاحق خلافا للمعتزلة لأنه متصرف في ملكه ولا يتصور أن يعدو تصرفه ملكه والظلم هو عبارة عن التصرف في ملك الغير بغير إذنه وهو محال على الله تعالى فإنه لا يصادف لغيره ملكا حتى يكون تصرف
2:286.english: **The Fifth Principle**: It is permissible for God—glorified be He—to charge His creatures with what they cannot bear (mā lā yuṭīqūnahu), contrary to the Muʿtazilites. For were that not permissible, then the petition to avert it would be impossible—yet they have petitioned it, saying: {«Rabbanā wa lā tuḥammilnā mā lā ṭāqata lanā bih»} "Our Lord, do not burden us with what we have no capacity for" {Q. 2:286}. And because God—exalted be He—informed His Prophet (peace be upon him) that Abū Jahl would not believe him, then commanded him to command Abū Jahl to believe him in all his statements. Now among Abū Jahl's statements was that he would not believe him—so how could he believe him in [the statement] that he would not believe him? Is this anything other than the impossible in its very existence?
2:286.section_title_en: The Fifth and Sixth Principles: On the Impossibility of Obligation Upon God and the Permissibility of What Reason Deems Impossible
2:286.anchors:
- Root: وجب (w-j-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of "being established, fixed, and necessary"; al-Kitab al-Ayn notes its application to ritual obligations (wujūb al-iḥrām).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Al-wujūb is thubūt (establishment). The wājib is said in two senses: (1) in contrast to the possible—that whose non-existence entails a contradiction; (2) that whose omission merits blame—either by reason (as knowing God's unity) or by revelation (as ritual duties)."
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "Wajaba lī ʿalayhi kadhā" (such is incumbent upon him); "awjabahu ʿalā nafsihi" (he made it incumbent upon himself). Metaphorical: "huwa ya'kulu al-wajbah" (he eats but once a day)—the root shifts from legal necessity to a single, fixed act.
- Root: ملك (m-l-k)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Sovereignty and possession; al-Kitab al-Ayn distinguishes mālik (owner) from malik (king), both deriving from absolute discretionary disposal.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Al-mulk: one who disposes by command and prohibition over a community—this pertains to governance of rational beings. Ownership (milk) is of two kinds: possession itself, and the power to dispose."
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "Malaktu al-shay'" (I possessed the thing). Metaphorical: "Malaktu nafsī ʿinda al-ghaḍab" (I mastered myself at anger)—dominion over one's own domain.
- Sibawayh Rule: Interposition of the conditional clause (al-sharṭ) between subject and predicate—governing the logical structure of "if X were permissible, then Y would follow," where the protasis restricts the apodosis.
2:286.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications, prayers, and their spiritual power, from 'Foundations of Belief'

2:286.arabic: ربنا ولا تحملنا ما لا طاقة لنا به ولأن الله تعالى أخبر نبيه صلى الله عليه وسلم بأن أبا جهل لا يصدقه ثم أمره بأن يأمره بأن يصدقه في جميع أقواله وكان من جملة أقواله أنه لا يصدقه فكيف يصدقه في أنه لا يصدقه وهل هذا إلا محال وجوده الأصل السادس أن لله عز وجل إيلام الخلق وتعذيبهم من غير جرم سابق ومن غير ثواب لاحق خلافا للمعتزلة لأنه متصرف في ملكه ولا يتصور أن يعدو تصرفه ملكه والظلم هو عبارة عن التصرف في ملك الغير بغير إذنه وهو محال على الله تعالى فإنه لا يصادف لغيره ملكا حتى يكون تصرفه
2:286.english: **The Fifth Principle**: It is permissible for God—glorified be He—to charge His creatures with what they cannot bear (mā lā yuṭīqūnahu), contrary to the Muʿtazilites. For were that not permissible, then the petition to avert it would be impossible—yet they have petitioned it, saying: {«Rabbanā wa lā tuḥammilnā mā lā ṭāqata lanā bih»} "Our Lord, do not burden us with what we have no capacity for" {Q. 2:286}. And because God—exalted be He—informed His Prophet (peace be upon him) that Abū Jahl would not believe him, then commanded him to command Abū Jahl to believe him in all his statements. Now among Abū Jahl's statements was that he would not believe him—so how could he believe him in [the statement] that he would not believe him? Is this anything other than the impossible in its very existence?
2:286.section_title_en: The Fifth and Sixth Principles: On the Impossibility of Obligation Upon God and the Permissibility of What Reason Deems Impossible
2:286.anchors:
- Root: وجب (w-j-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of "being established, fixed, and necessary"; al-Kitab al-Ayn notes its application to ritual obligations (wujūb al-iḥrām).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Al-wujūb is thubūt (establishment). The wājib is said in two senses: (1) in contrast to the possible—that whose non-existence entails a contradiction; (2) that whose omission merits blame—either by reason (as knowing God's unity) or by revelation (as ritual duties)."
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "Wajaba lī ʿalayhi kadhā" (such is incumbent upon him); "awjabahu ʿalā nafsihi" (he made it incumbent upon himself). Metaphorical: "huwa ya'kulu al-wajbah" (he eats but once a day)—the root shifts from legal necessity to a single, fixed act.
- Root: ملك (m-l-k)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Sovereignty and possession; al-Kitab al-Ayn distinguishes mālik (owner) from malik (king), both deriving from absolute discretionary disposal.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Al-mulk: one who disposes by command and prohibition over a community—this pertains to governance of rational beings. Ownership (milk) is of two kinds: possession itself, and the power to dispose."
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "Malaktu al-shay'" (I possessed the thing). Metaphorical: "Malaktu nafsī ʿinda al-ghaḍab" (I mastered myself at anger)—dominion over one's own domain.
- Sibawayh Rule: Interposition of the conditional clause (al-sharṭ) between subject and predicate—governing the logical structure of "if X were permissible, then Y would follow," where the protasis restricts the apodosis.
2:286.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications, prayers, and their spiritual power, from 'Etiquette of Marriage'

2:286.arabic: الله تعالى للمؤمنين في قولهم {ولا تحمل علينا إصرا} وقال تعالى {ويضع عنهم إصرهم والأغلال التي كانت عليهم} وروى محمد بن الحنفية عن علي رضي الله تعالى عنهما أنه قال لما نزل قوله تعالى {فاصفح الصفح الجميل} قال يا جبريل وما الصفح الجميل قال عليه السلام إذا عفوت عمن ظلمك فلا تعاتبه فقال يا جبريل فالله تعالى أكرم من أن يعاتب من عفا عنه فبكى جبريل وبكى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فبعث الله تعالى إليهما ميكائيل عليه السلام وقال إن ربكما يقرئكما السلام ويقول كيف أعاتب من عفوت عنه
2:286.english: In the report (khabar): "Were you not to sin, God would create a creation who would sin, and He would forgive them." (1) In another wording: "He would take you away and bring a creation who would sin, and He would forgive them — verily, He is the Forgiving, the Merciful." And in the report: "Were you not to sin, I would fear for you what is worse than sins." It was said: "And what is that?" He said: "Self-amazement (al-ʿujb)." (2)
2:286.section_title_en: The Completion of the Matter — On the Preacher's Gentleness in Employing Reports of Fear and Hope
2:286.anchors:
- Root: لطف (luṭf)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Gentleness, subtlety, kindness in approach; to be gracious and delicate in manner.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Divine gentleness (luṭf) as an attribute of God's subtle providence; here, the preacher's emulation of prophetic gentleness in spiritual counsel.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) — physical softness; metaphorical (majāz) — refinement of speech and manner suited to the spiritual state of the listener.
- Root: رجا (rajā')
  * Lisan / Ayn: Hope, expectation of good; the opposite of despair (ya's).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Hope in God's mercy as a theological virtue balancing fear (khawf); the state of the believer who relies on divine generosity over personal merit.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — anticipation of a future good; metaphorical — the soul's reliance on God's pardon despite sin.
- Root: عجب (ʿajab)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Self-amazement, vanity, wonder at oneself.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Spiritual pride (ʿujb) — a hidden sin worse than overt transgression, as it nullifies deeds.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — astonishment; metaphorical — the heart's complacency in its own obedience, leading to ruin.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد (Restriction and Specification) — The conditional and exceptive structures (law lā... la-khalaqa, illā an yataghammadani) govern the precise scope of divine mercy and human agency.
2:286.topic: Al-Ghazali on purifying the character, moral diseases, and spiritual remedies, from 'Fear and Hope'

3:2.arabic: وجل في كلام يردده في نفسه كما لو سمع وهو يقول {إنني أنا الله لا إله إلا أنا فاعبدني} فإنه ما كان ينبغي أن يفهم منه ذلك إلا على سبيل الحكاية الصنف الثاني من الشطح كلمات غير مفهومة لها ظواهر رائقة وفيها عبارات هائلة وليس وراءها طائل إما أن تكون غير مفهومة عند قائلها بل يصدرها عن خبط في عقله وتشويش في خياله لقلة إحاطته بمعنى كلام قرع سمعه وهذا هو الأكثر وإما أن تكون مفهومة له ولكنه لا يقدر على تفهيمها وإيرادها بعبارة تدل على ضميره لقلة ممارسته للعلم وعدم تعلمه طريق التعبير عن المعاني بالألفاظ الرشيقة ولا فائدة لهذا الجنس من الكلام إلا أ
3:2.english: Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ, may God be pleased with him, said to his son ʿUmar — having heard him composing sajʿ — "This is what makes me dislike you. I will never fulfill your need until you repent." This was said when his son had come to him seeking a favor. And the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to ʿAbd Allāh ibn Rawāḥah when he spoke in sajʿ of three words: "Beware of sajʿ, O Ibn Rawāḥah." Thus, the forbidden sajʿ is the artificially contrived kind that exceeds two words. For this reason, when a man spoke concerning the blood-money for a fetus — saying, "How shall we pay blood-money for one who neither drank, nor ate, nor cried out, nor wailed? Such a one's blood is void" — the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, replied: "Sajʿ like the sajʿ of the bedouins!"
3:2.section_title_en: On the Etiquette of Preaching: The Condemnation of Artificial Sajʿ, Excessive Poetry, and the Perils of Shataḥ and Taʿwīl
3:2.anchors:
- Root: سجع (sajʿa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Rhymed prose; from the root meaning "to coo" (as a dove), indicating a measured, melodious cadence in speech.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In theological discourse, sajʿ is permissible when natural but blameworthy when artificially cultivated (takalluf), as it shifts focus from meaning to ornamentation.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) — natural rhythmic speech; Metaphorical (majāz) — the "sajʿ of the bedouins" (sajʿ al-aʿrāb) as a pejorative for empty, affected eloquence.
- Root: شعر (shiʿr)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Poetry; from the root denoting perception and fine discernment (shuʿūr), as the poet grasps subtle meanings.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Poetry is blameworthy when it stirs base appetites, but praiseworthy when it conveys wisdom (ḥikmah), as in the prophetic saying "Indeed from poetry there is wisdom."
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — metered, rhymed speech; Metaphorical — the "poetry" of the heart's inclination, where listeners project their own passions onto what they hear.
- Root: شطح (shaṭaḥa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To overflow, to gush forth; originally of a water-skin bursting, then applied to ecstatic utterances that overflow the bounds of conventional discourse.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In Sufi terminology, shataḥ refers to utterances arising from overwhelming spiritual states (ḥāl) that, when voiced to the unworthy, cause corruption.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — physical overflowing; Metaphorical — the soul's overflow in speech that exceeds the speaker's intentional control.
- Root: أول (taʿwīl)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To return something to its origin or end; interpretation that traces a word back to its intended meaning.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Taʿwīl is legitimate only when supported by textual (naqlī) or rational (ʿaqlī) evidence; arbitrary taʿwīl that severs words from their established senses destroys religious trust.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — the apparent sense (ẓāhir); Metaphorical — the inner sense (bāṭin), which is only valid when the literal sense is impossible or when transmitted authority sanctions it.
- Sibawayh Rule: Bāb al-Ḥaṣr wa al-Taqyīd bi-innamā (Restriction and Focused Predication) — The text repeatedly uses restrictive constructions (innamā, laysa...illā) to delimit permissible preaching, poetry, and interpretation, distinguishing the praiseworthy from the blameworthy with syntactic precision.

3:2.arabic: فراشه أستغفر الله العظيم الذي لا إله إلا هو الحي القيوم وأتوب إليه ثلاث مرات غفر الله له ذنوبه وإن كانت مثل زبد البحر أو عدد رمل عالج أو عدد ورق الشجر أو عدد أيام الدنيا (5) وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم في حديث آخر من قال ذلك غفرت ذنوبه وإن كان فارا من الزحف (6) وقال حذيفة كنت ذرب اللسان على أهلي فقلت يا رسول الله لقد خشيت أن يدخلني لساني النار فقال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فأين أنت من الاستغفار فإني لأستغفر الله في اليوم مائة مرة (7) وقالت عائشة رضي الله عنها قال لي رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أن كنت ألم
3:2.english: God Most High said: {«والذين إذا فعلوا فاحشة أو ظلموا أنفسهم ذكروا الله فاستغفروا لذنوبهم»} — "And those who, when they commit an indecency or wrong themselves, remember God and seek forgiveness for their sins" {آل عمران/135}.
3:2.anchors:
- Root: ذنب (dhanb)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of "tail" or "taking hold of a tail"; extended to signify a sin as that which trails behind and follows a person.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الذنب في الأصل: الأخذ بذنب الشيء" — sin is that by which one is seized and held accountable; used metaphorically for a fault that clings to its perpetrator.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: tail of an animal. Metaphorical: "هو من الأذناب" — one who follows; sin as that which trails the soul and must be severed through repentance.
- Root: غفر (ghafara)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Covering, veiling, protecting from defilement; a shield or helmet (المغفر).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الغفران والمغفرة من الله هو أن يصون العبد من أن يمسه العذاب" — divine forgiveness is God's protection of the servant from being touched by punishment.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: to cover and protect. Metaphorical: God's "covering" of sins — not merely erasure, but active safeguarding of the sinner from consequence.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The frequent interposition of "يا رب" and vocative constructions between the subject and predicate in supplicatory sentences, as in "اللهم اغفر لي," where the vocative particle governs the imperative verb's addressee, reflecting the grammatical permissibility of separation between governing and governed elements in invocational speech.
3:2.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications, prayers, and their spiritual power, from 'On Invocations and Supplications'

3:64.arabic: بينك وبين الخلق فأما التي لي تعبدني ولا تشرك بي شيئا وأما التي لك فعملك أجزيك به أفقر ما تكون إليه وأما التي بيني وبينك فعليك الدعاء وعلي الإجابة وأما التي بنيك وبين الناس فتصحبهم بالذي تحب أن يصحبوك به وسأل موسى عليه السلام الله تعالى فقال أي رب أي عبادك أعدل قال من أنصف من نفسه ومنها أن يزيد في توقير من تدل هيئته وثيابه على علو منزلته فينزل الناس منازلهم روي أن عائشة رضي الله عنها كانت في سفر فنزلت منزلا فوضعت طعامها فجاء سائل فقالت عائشة ناولوا هذا المسكين قرصا ثم مر رجل على دابة
3:64.english: **First**: That you greet him with peace (*salām*) when you meet him, and respond to his invitation when he invites you, and say "may Allah have mercy on you" (*tashmīt*) when he sneezes, and visit him when he is ill, and attend his funeral procession when he dies, and fulfill his oath when he swears by you, and give him sincere counsel when he seeks your advice, and protect him in his absence when he is away from you, and love for him what you love for yourself, and dislike for him what you dislike for yourself. (1)
3:64.section_title_en: The Rights of Brotherhood — Section 433: The Duties of a Muslim Toward His Fellow Muslims
3:64.anchors:
- Root: سلم (s-l-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of safety, security, freedom from harm; the root from which *islām* (submission/surrender) and *salām* (peace) derive
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): *Salām* as the theological state of being secure from harm — both giving and receiving safety; *islām* as the total surrender of the heart to Allah
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (*ḥaqīqah*): physical safety from tongue and hand; Metaphorical (*majāz*): the comprehensive spiritual safety that defines true Muslim brotherhood
- Root: عون (ʿ-w-n)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Assistance, aid, helping another in need
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Mutual assistance as a divine ordinance among believers
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical aid; Metaphorical: intercession (*shafāʿah*) and advocacy on behalf of others
- Root: ستر (s-t-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Covering, concealing, veiling; protection from exposure
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): *Sitr* as the divine attribute of concealment — Allah's covering of sins in this world and the next
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: covering a physical defect; Metaphorical: concealing another's faults and sins — a cardinal virtue of brotherhood
- Root: عذر (ʿ-dh-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Excuse, pardon, acceptance of apology
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): *ʿAfw* (pardon) as the higher station of forgiveness that elevates the forgiver
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: releasing from obligation; Metaphorical: the noble trait of overlooking others' offenses
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد (Restriction & Focused Predication) — The repeated use of restrictive constructions (e.g., "المسلم من سلم المسلمون") establishes definitional boundaries through predicate restriction, indicating that the *ḥaqīqah* of faith is manifested through specific observable actions.
