3:64.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'On Invocations and Supplications'

3:95.arabic: محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم وملة أبينا إبراهيم حنيفا وما كان من المشركين (9) اللهم بك أصبحنا وبك أمسينا وبك نحيا وبك نموت وإليك المصير (10) اللهم إني أسألك أن تبعثنا في هذا اليوم إلى كل خير ونعوذ بك أن نجترح فيه سوءا أو نجره إلى مسلم فإنك قلت {وهو الذي يتوفاكم بالليل ويعلم ما جرحتم بالنهار ثم يبعثكم فيه ليقضى أجل مسمى} (11) اللهم فالق الإصباح وجاعل الليل سكنا والشمس والقمر حسبانا أسألك خير هذا اليوم وخير ما فيه وأعوذ بك من شره وشر ما فيه (12) بسم الله ما شاء الله لا قوة إلا بالله ما شاء الله
3:95.english: When you rise in the morning and hear the call to prayer (adhān), it is recommended for you to respond to the caller of prayer (mu'adhdhin) — and we have already mentioned this, along with the supplications for entering and leaving the privy, and the supplications of ablution (wuḍū'), in the Book of Purification. When you set out toward the mosque, say: "O Allah, place light (nūr) in my heart, and light in my tongue, and place light in my hearing, and place light in my sight, and place light behind me, and light before me, and place light above me. O Allah, grant me light." And also say: "O Allah, I ask You by the right of those who ask of You, and by the right of this my walking unto You — for I have not gone out in insolence, nor in vanity, nor for show, nor for reputation. I have gone out seeking protection from Your wrath and seeking Your good pleasure. So I ask You to deliver me from the Fire and to forgive me my sins — verily, none forgives sins but You."
3:95.section_title_en: Section 254 — Supplications for the Hours of Day and Night: From Dawn to Sleep
3:95.anchors:
- Root: ن و ر (n-w-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: النور: الضوء المنتشر الذي يُبصر به، وهو ضد الظلمة
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): النور في القرآن يقع على ضروب: منها المعقول كالإيمان والحكمة، قال تعالى: {قد جاءكم من الله نور وكتاب مبين}، ومنها المحسوس كضوء الشمس والقمر
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): النور حقيقة في الضوء المحسوس، ومجاز في الهدى والإيمان والعلم — فدعاء النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بطلب النور يشمل المعنيين جميعاً
- Root: س ج د (s-j-d)
  * Lisan / Ayn: السجود: وضع الجبهة على الأرض تعظيماً، وأصله التطامن والانخفاض
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): السجود ضربان: سجود عبادة وهو وضع الجبهة على الأرض تقرباً، وسجود طاعة وهو الانقياد والخضوع — قال تعالى: {ولله يسجد من في السموات والأرض طوعاً وكرهاً}
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): سجد حقيقة في وضع الجبهة، ومجاز في الخضوع والانقياد — وقوله "سجد لك سوادي وخيالي" من المجاز المرسل
- Root: ذ ك ر (dh-k-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: الذكر: نقيض النسيان، والذكر: الصوت الذي يُذكر به الشيء، والذكر: الشرف والصيت
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): الذكر ضربان: ذكر بالقلب وهو التفكر في عظمة الله، وذكر باللسان وهو التلفظ بأسمائه — وأعلى مراتبه ما اجتمع فيه القلب واللسان
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): الذكر حقيقة في استحضار الشيء بالقلب أو اللسان، ومجاز في الصلاة والدعاء والثناء
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — جواز تقديم المعمول وتأخيره مع بقاء العامل عاملاً في المعنى، كقوله "لك الحمد" حيث تقدم الجار والمجرور على المبتدأ للاختصاص والاهتمام
3:95.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications, prayers, and their spiritual power, from 'On Invocations and Supplications'

3:135.arabic: قال عز وجل والذين إذا فعلوا فاحشة أو ظلموا أنفسهم ذكروا الله فاستغفروا لذنوبهم وقال علقمة والأسود قال عبد الله بن مسعود رضي الله عنهم في كتاب الله عز وجل آيتان ما أذنب عبد ذنبا فقرأهما واستغفر الله عز وجل إلا غفر الله تعالى له والذين إذا فعلوا فاحشة أو ظلموا أنفسهم الآية وقوله عز وجل ومن يعمل سوءا أو يظلم به ثم يستغفر الله يجد الله غفورا رحيما وقال عز وجل فسبح بحمد ربك واستغفره إنه كان توابا وقال تعالى والمستغفرين بالأسحار وكان صلى الله عليه وسلم يكثر أن يقول سبحانك اللهم وبحمدك اللهم اغفر لي إنك أنت التواب الرحيم (1) وقال صلى ال
3:135.english: God Most High said: {«والذين إذا فعلوا فاحشة أو ظلموا أنفسهم ذكروا الله فاستغفروا لذنوبهم»} — "And those who, when they commit an indecency or wrong themselves, remember God and seek forgiveness for their sins" {آل عمران/135}.
3:135.anchors:
- Root: ذنب (dhanb)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of "tail" or "taking hold of a tail"; extended to signify a sin as that which trails behind and follows a person.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الذنب في الأصل: الأخذ بذنب الشيء" — sin is that by which one is seized and held accountable; used metaphorically for a fault that clings to its perpetrator.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: tail of an animal. Metaphorical: "هو من الأذناب" — one who follows; sin as that which trails the soul and must be severed through repentance.
- Root: غفر (ghafara)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Covering, veiling, protecting from defilement; a shield or helmet (المغفر).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الغفران والمغفرة من الله هو أن يصون العبد من أن يمسه العذاب" — divine forgiveness is God's protection of the servant from being touched by punishment.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: to cover and protect. Metaphorical: God's "covering" of sins — not merely erasure, but active safeguarding of the sinner from consequence.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The frequent interposition of "يا رب" and vocative constructions between the subject and predicate in supplicatory sentences, as in "اللهم اغفر لي," where the vocative particle governs the imperative verb's addressee, reflecting the grammatical permissibility of separation between governing and governed elements in invocational speech.
3:135.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications, prayers, and their spiritual power, from 'On Invocations and Supplications'

3:147.arabic: لنا ربنا إنك أنت العزيز الحكيم ربنا اغفر لنا ذنوبنا وإسرافنا في أمرنا وثبت أقدامنا وانصرنا على القوم الكافرين ربنا اغفر لنا ولإخواننا الذين سبقونا بالإيمان ولا تجعل في قلوبنا غلا للذين آمنوا ربنا إنك رؤوف رحيم ربنا آتنا من لدنك رحمة وهيئ لنا من أمرنا رشدا ربنا آتنا في الدنيا حسنة وفي الآخرة حسنة وقنا عذاب النار ربنا إننا سمعنا مناديا ينادي للإيمان إلى قوله عز وجل إنك لا تخلف الميعاد ربنا لا تؤاخذنا إن نسينا أو أخطأنا ربنا إلى آخر السورة (3) رب اغفر لي ولوالدي وارحمهما كما ربياني صغيرا واغفر للمؤمنين والمؤمنات والمسلمين والمسلمات الأحياء منهم والأموات
3:147.english: And employ me in righteous deeds which You will accept from me. (1) O God, I ask You for pardon, well-being, good certainty, and soundness in this world and the next. (2) O You Whom sins do not harm and from Whom forgiveness does not diminish anything — grant me that which will not harm You, and give me that which will not diminish You. Our Lord, pour upon us patience and cause us to die as Muslims. You are our Protector in this world and the next; cause me to die as a Muslim and join me with the righteous. You are our Protector, so forgive us and have mercy upon us, and You are the Best of forgivers. And write for us good in this world and in the Hereafter — indeed, we have turned to You in repentance. Our Lord, upon You we rely, to You we turn in repentance, and to You is the final return. Our Lord, make us not a trial for the wrongdoing people. Our Lord, make us not a trial for those who disbelieve, and forgive us, our Lord — indeed, You are the Mighty, the Wise. Our Lord, forgive us our sins and our excesses in our affairs, make firm our feet, and grant us victory over the disbelieving people. Our Lord, forgive us and our brothers who preceded us in faith, and place not in our hearts any rancor toward those who believe — our Lord, indeed You are Kind, Merciful. Our Lord, grant us from Yourself mercy and prepare for us from our affair right guidance. Our Lord, give us good in this world and good in the Hereafter, and protect us from the chastisement of the Fire. Our Lord, indeed we have heard a caller calling to faith — to His saying, Mighty and Majestic: {«إنك لا تخلف الميعاد»} [آل عمران/ 194] — Our Lord, do not take us to task if we forget or err. Our Lord, to the end of the surah. (3) My Lord, forgive me and my parents, and have mercy upon them as they raised me when I was small; and forgive the believing men and the believing women, and the Muslim men and the Muslim women, the living among them and the dead. (4) My Lord, forgive, have mercy, and overlook what You know — and You are the Most Exalted, the Most Generous, the Best of the merciful, and the Best of the forgivers. And indeed, to God we belong and to Him we return; and there is no might and no power except through God, the Exalted, the Magnificent; and God suffices us, and He is the Best Disposer of affairs. And may God send blessings upon Muhammad, the Seal of the Prophets, and upon his family and his companions, and grant them abundant peace. (5)
3:147.section_title_en: Section 252 — Supplications for Morning and Evening: Comprehensive Prayers of the Prophet (ﷺ)
3:147.anchors:
- Root: لهم (l-h-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of swallowing/ingesting (iltihām); from this derives the sense of something being cast directly into the innermost recess of the heart (al-rawʿ).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الإلهام: إلقاء الشيء في الروع" — ilhām is the casting of a thing into the innermost consciousness, specifically from God or the higher assembly (al-malaʾ al-aʿlā). It is that which the Prophet (ﷺ) called "the touch of the angel" (limat al-malak) and "the breath of the Holy Spirit in my innermost heart" (nafth rūḥ al-qudus fī rawʿī).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): "ألهمه الله الخير: ألقاه في روعه" — God inspired him with good: He cast it into his innermost consciousness. Metaphorical (majāz): A horse that "swallows the ground" (yaltaḥimu al-arḍ) in swiftness; thus ilhām is the swift, direct ingress of divine guidance into the soul without intermediary effort.
- Root: حمد (ḥ-m-d)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The root denotes praise arising from recognition of voluntary excellence and beneficence; al-ḥamd is commendation of the beloved for their attributes and acts of goodness.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Praise (ḥamd) is the acknowledgment of beneficence (niʿmah) with reverence and love; it is distinguished from mere thanks (shukr) in that it is directed to the essence and attributes of the praised one, not solely to the benefit received.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "أحمد الله تعالى بجميع محامده" — I praise God with all His praiseworthy attributes. Metaphorical: "أحمدت صنيعه" — I found his deed praiseworthy; thus the tongue's praise must be matched by the heart's recognition of the praised one's perfection.
- Root: غفر (gh-f-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The root denotes covering and shielding; al-mighfar is the helmet that protects the head in battle.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الغفر: إلباس ما يصونه عن الدنس" — Forgiveness is the clothing of that which shields from filth. God's forgiveness (maghfirah) is His shielding of the servant from the touch of chastisement, covering the sin so that it is as though it never were.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "اللهم غفرًا" — O God, forgive. Metaphorical: The she-beasts that "did not forgive" their heedlessness (lam taghfir la-hā ghaflātuhā) — i.e., they did not shield their young from destruction; thus forgiveness is active protection, not mere erasure.
- Root: نفس (n-f-s)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The self, the soul; that which breathes and has vital spirit; also used for the very essence of a thing.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "النفس: الروح" — the soul is the spirit; and in God's saying {«ويحذركم الله نفسه»} [آل عمران/ 28], "His Self" means His very essence (dhāt), which — though grammatically expressed as an annexation implying distinction — is in reality identical, with no multiplicity in the Divine Essence.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "شيء نفيس" — a precious thing. Metaphorical: "دفق نفسه" — he poured out his blood/life; thus nafs is the seat of life, passion, and moral responsibility.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الدعاء والخبر (The Chapter of Supplication and Assertion) — Supplications (duʿāʾ) are grammatically constructed as optative sentences (inshāʾ ṭalabī) using the imperative (rabbighfir), the jussive (lā tuʾākhidhnā), and the vocative (rabbanā), yet they may embed assertive clauses (khabar) of praise (al-ḥamdu lillāh) and attestation (lā ilāha illā anta). The periodic structure of these prayers alternates between direct address to God (munādāh) and self-referential confession, requiring the translator to preserve the vocative force of "O God" and "Our Lord" without flattening into mere description.
3:147.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'On Invocations and Supplications'

3:169.arabic: إليه لا ينافي ذكر الله عز وجل وقال تعالى ولا تحسبن الذين قتلوا في سبيل الله أمواتا بل أحياء عند ربهم يرزقون فرحين بما آتاهم الله من فضله ويستبشرون بالذين لم يلحقوا بهم من خلفهم الآية ولأجل شرف ذكر الله عز وجل عظمت رتبة الشهادة لأن المطلوب الخاتمة ونعني بالخاتمة وداع الدنيا والقدوم على الله والقلب مستغرق بالله عز وجل منقطع العلائق عن غيره فإن قدر عبد على أن يجعل همه مستغرقا بالله عز وجل فلا يقدر على أن يموت على تلك الحالة إلا في صف القتال فإنه قطع الطمع عن مهجته وأهله وماله وولده بل من الدنيا كلها فإنه يريدها لحياته وقد هون على قلبه حياته في حب الله عز وجل وطلب مرضاته فلا تجرد لله أعظم من ذلك ولذلك عظم أمر الشه
3:169.english: If, therefore, he had grown intimate with it, he delights in it and takes pleasure in the cessation of the impediments that had diverted him from it. For the pressing necessities of needs in this worldly life divert one from the remembrance of God, may He be mighty and majestic, and after death no impediment remains. It is as if he has been left alone with his Beloved, and so his joy is immense, and he is delivered from the prison in which he had been prevented from that which was his source of intimacy. For this reason, he, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "The Holy Spirit (Rūḥ al-Qudus) breathed into my heart: Love whom you will, for you shall surely part from him." {«أحبب من أحببت فإنك مفارقه»} By this he intended everything connected to this world, for that perishes with respect to him at death. For {«كل من عليها فان * ويبقى وجه ربك ذو الجلال والإكرام»} [Everything upon it is perishing, and there remains the Face of your Lord, Possessor of Majesty and Honor]. And this world only perishes with respect to him at death, until it perishes in itself when the Book reaches its appointed term.
3:169.section_title_en: Section 240 — The Station of Remembrance (Dhikr): On the Transformation of Habit into Nature, the Intimacy of Remembrance After Death, and the Excellence of Martyrdom as the Seal of One's State
3:169.anchors:
- Root: ألف (Alifa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of reconciliation, familiarity, and the formation of habit through repeated engagement.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The theological nuance of 'uns' (intimacy) as the soul's acquired disposition of comfort in the presence of its Beloved, contrasting with 'wahsha' (estrangement).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Distinguishes the literal sense of social familiarity from the metaphorical (majaz) sense of the heart's deep-seated repose in the remembrance of God, which becomes a 'second nature' (ṭabʿan ākhara).
- Root: ختم (Khatama)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To seal, stamp, or conclude; the final impression left upon a thing.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The theological sense of the 'seal' (khātima) of one's life—the terminal state upon which one departs from the world and which determines the nature of the afterlife.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): The literal act of sealing a document versus the metaphorical designation of one's final spiritual condition as the determining factor of one's eternal outcome.
- Root: شهد (Shahida)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To witness, to be present, to testify.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The specific theological elevation of 'shahāda' (martyrdom) as the ultimate act of witnessing the truth of God through the sacrifice of one's own life, rendering the martyr a living witness (shahīd).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): The literal sense of legal testimony versus the metaphorical reality of the martyr whose very being testifies to the sincerity of his devotion, being 'alive' with his Lord.
- Root: قطع (Qata'a)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To sever, cut off, or detach.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The essential spiritual operation of severing worldly attachments ('alā'iq) to achieve the unadulterated focus of the heart upon God.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): The literal cutting of a physical tie versus the metaphorical severance of all internal and external impediments that distract the soul from its sole Beloved.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Restriction and Specification (Bāb al-Ḥaṣr wa al-Taqyīd bi-innamā) — Governing how the exclusive focus of the martyr's intention is syntactically and logically restricted to God alone, as exemplified in the phrase "no god but God" (lā ilāha illā Allāh), which requires the complete negation of all other objects of intention before affirming the sole Divine Object.
3:169.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'On Invocations and Supplications'

3:169.arabic: فوالذي نفسي بيده ليودن رجال قتلوا في سبيل الله شهداء أن يبعثهم الله علماء لما يرون من كرامتهم فإن أحدا لم يولد عالما وإنما العلم بالتعلم وقال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما تذاكر العلم بعض ليلة أحب إلي من إحيائها وكذلك عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه وأحمد بن حنبل رحمة الله وقال الحسن في قوله تعالى {ربنا آتنا في الدنيا حسنة وفي الآخرة حسنة} إن الحسنة في الدنيا هي العلم والعبادة وفي الآخرة هي الجنة وقيل لبعض الحكماء أي الأشياء تقتنى قال الأشياء التي إذا غرقت سفينتك سبحت معك يعني العلم وقيل أراد بغرق السف
3:169.english: And al-Ḥasan, may God have mercy on him, said: "The ink of the scholars will be weighed against the blood of the martyrs, and the ink of the scholars will outweigh the blood of the martyrs."
3:169.section_title_en: The Book of Knowledge — Section 6: On the Virtue of Teaching and Learning (Continued)
3:169.anchors:
- Root: شغل (sh-gh-l)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Occupation, preoccupation, that which engages one entirely
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Preoccupation that veils one from perception of other things
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — physical occupation; Metaphorical — absorption of the heart that blinds the senses
- Root: حسن (ḥ-s-n)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Beauty, goodness, excellence
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الحسن: عبارة عن كل مبهج مرغوب فيه" — that which is pleasing and desirable, of three kinds: rational, appetitive, sensory
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — beauty of form; Metaphorical — the ḥasanah in the Qur'anic supplication denotes knowledge and worship
- Root: علم (ʿ-l-m) — [Note: recently used, but required by text; applied per governing rule]
  * Lisan / Ayn: Knowledge, perception, cognition
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "العلم: إدراك الشيء بحقيقته" — apprehension of a thing in its true reality
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — direct perception; Metaphorical — knowledge as a garment of honor from God
- Root: موت (m-w-t)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Death, cessation of life
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Death as the lifting of the burdens of this world; awakening from the sleep of heedlessness
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — physical death; Metaphorical — "الناس نيام فإذا ماتوا انتبهوا" (people are asleep; when they die, they awaken)
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — applied in the ḥadīth "إنما العلم بالتعلم" (knowledge is only attained through learning), restricting the means of acquiring knowledge to learning alone.
3:169.topic: Al-Ghazali on the journey of the soul, death, and the Hereafter, from 'Book of Knowledge'

3:173.arabic: وسلم تسليما كثيرا دائما إلى يوم الدين والحمد لله وحده وحسبنا الله ونعم الوكيل
3:173.english: Ibrāhīm al-Khawwāṣ, al-Junayd, and a group [of the pious] held the view that taking from voluntary charity (ṣadaqah) is superior. For in taking the obligatory alms (zakāh), there is a jostling with the poor and a constriction upon them. And also because perhaps one's attribute of eligibility (ṣifat al-istihqāq) is not fully complete in his taking it, as it was described in the Mighty Book {«إِنَّمَا الصَّدَقَاتُ لِلْفُقَرَاءِ وَالْمَسَاكِينِ»} (Verily the alms are for the poor and the needy). As for voluntary charity (ṣadaqah), the matter therein is more expansive.
3:173.section_title_en: Section 184 — The Book of the Secrets of Almsgiving (Zakat): On the Concealment and Open Display of Charity, and the Superiority of Taking from Voluntary Charity (Sadaqah) versus Obligatory Alms (Zakat)
3:173.anchors:
- Root: صدق (ṣ-d-q)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root denotes truthfulness and veracity in speech and action; the voluntary charity (ṣadaqah) is so named because it is a truthful manifestation of one's faith and sincerity.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الصدق والكذب أصلهما في القول... ولا يكونان بالقصد الأول إلا في القول" — Truth and falsehood are originally in speech; ṣadaqah (charity) is that which verifies and proves the truthfulness of one's claim to faith.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): "صدقته الحديث" — truthful in speech. Metaphorical (Majaz): "رجل صادق الحملة" — one who is true/steadfast in battle-charge; thus ṣadaqah is that which truthfully manifests inner conviction through outward action.
- Root: زكا (z-k-w)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "زكا الزرع يزكو: ازداد ونماء" — growth and increase; purification.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "أصل الزكاة: النمو الحاصل عن بركة الله تعالى... أو لتزكية النفس، أي: تنميتها" — The root of zakāh is growth from divine blessing, or the purification/growth of the soul.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Zakāh is the obligatory alms that purifies wealth and the soul; its taking is a legal right (ḥaqq wājib), not a favor.
- Root: وجب (w-j-b)
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الوجوب: الثبوت" — Obligation is fixedness/establishment. "واجب من جهة الشرع كوجوب العب" — Obligatory by divine law (Sharʿ).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "وجب البيع، وأوجبته" — the sale became binding. "استوجب العقاب" — he merited punishment.
  * Lisan al-Arab: "ومُوجِبٌ: من أَسماءِ الـمُحَرَّم" — from the names of the sacred/preclusive.
- Root: حمد (ḥ-m-d)
  * Al-Raghib (Al-Mufradat): Praise (ḥamd) is the acknowledgment of beneficence with veneration; the Book of Secrets of Fasting opens with praise to God.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "أحمد الله تعالى بجميع محامده" — I praise God with all His praises. Metaphorical: "أحمدت الأرض: رضيت سكناها" — I found the land praiseworthy (approved its dwelling).
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — The phrase "إِنَّمَا" restricts predication, as in the legal maxim that zakāh is exclusively a right of God (ḥaqq wājib lillāh), not a discretionary favor of the giver.
3:173.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications, prayers, and their spiritual power, from 'On Invocations and Supplications'

3:191.arabic: وتقول عند النظر إلى السماء ربنا ما خلقت هذا باطلا سبحانك فقنا عذاب النار تبارك الذي جعل في السماء بروجا وجعل فيها سراجا وقمرا منيرا وإذا سمعت صوت الرعد فقل سبحان من يسبح الرعد بحمده والملائكة من خيفته (7) فإن رأيت الصواعق فقل اللهم لا تقتلنا بغضبك ولا تهلكنا بعذابك وعافنا قبل ذلك (8) قاله كعب فإذا أمطرت السماء فقل اللهم سقيا هنيئا وصيبا نافعا (9) اللهم اجعله صيب رحمة ولا تجعله صيب عذاب (10) فإذا غضبت فقل اللهم اغفر لي ذنبي وأذهب غيظ قلبي وأجرني من الشيطان الرجيم (1) فإذا خفت قوما فقل اللهم إنا نجعلك في نحورهم
3:191.english: When you rise in the morning and hear the call to prayer (adhān), it is recommended for you to respond to the caller of prayer (mu'adhdhin) — and we have already mentioned this, along with the supplications for entering and leaving the privy, and the supplications of ablution (wuḍū'), in the Book of Purification. When you set out toward the mosque, say: "O Allah, place light (nūr) in my heart, and light in my tongue, and place light in my hearing, and place light in my sight, and place light behind me, and light before me, and place light above me. O Allah, grant me light." And also say: "O Allah, I ask You by the right of those who ask of You, and by the right of this my walking unto You — for I have not gone out in insolence, nor in vanity, nor for show, nor for reputation. I have gone out seeking protection from Your wrath and seeking Your good pleasure. So I ask You to deliver me from the Fire and to forgive me my sins — verily, none forgives sins but You."
3:191.section_title_en: Section 254 — Supplications for the Hours of Day and Night: From Dawn to Sleep
3:191.anchors:
- Root: ن و ر (n-w-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: النور: الضوء المنتشر الذي يُبصر به، وهو ضد الظلمة
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): النور في القرآن يقع على ضروب: منها المعقول كالإيمان والحكمة، قال تعالى: {قد جاءكم من الله نور وكتاب مبين}، ومنها المحسوس كضوء الشمس والقمر
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): النور حقيقة في الضوء المحسوس، ومجاز في الهدى والإيمان والعلم — فدعاء النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بطلب النور يشمل المعنيين جميعاً
- Root: س ج د (s-j-d)
  * Lisan / Ayn: السجود: وضع الجبهة على الأرض تعظيماً، وأصله التطامن والانخفاض
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): السجود ضربان: سجود عبادة وهو وضع الجبهة على الأرض تقرباً، وسجود طاعة وهو الانقياد والخضوع — قال تعالى: {ولله يسجد من في السموات والأرض طوعاً وكرهاً}
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): سجد حقيقة في وضع الجبهة، ومجاز في الخضوع والانقياد — وقوله "سجد لك سوادي وخيالي" من المجاز المرسل
- Root: ذ ك ر (dh-k-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: الذكر: نقيض النسيان، والذكر: الصوت الذي يُذكر به الشيء، والذكر: الشرف والصيت
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): الذكر ضربان: ذكر بالقلب وهو التفكر في عظمة الله، وذكر باللسان وهو التلفظ بأسمائه — وأعلى مراتبه ما اجتمع فيه القلب واللسان
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): الذكر حقيقة في استحضار الشيء بالقلب أو اللسان، ومجاز في الصلاة والدعاء والثناء
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — جواز تقديم المعمول وتأخيره مع بقاء العامل عاملاً في المعنى، كقوله "لك الحمد" حيث تقدم الجار والمجرور على المبتدأ للاختصاص والاهتمام
3:191.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications, prayers, and their spiritual power, from 'On Invocations and Supplications'

3:191.arabic: قال الله تعالى الذين يذكرون الله قياما وقعودا وعلى جنوبهم ويتفكرون في خلق السموات والأرض فأثنى على الكل ولكن قدم القيام في الذكر ثم القعود ثم الذكر مضطجعا قال علي رضي الله عنه من قرأ القرآن وهو قائم في الصلاة كان له بكل حرف مائة حسنة ومن قرأه وهو جالس في الصلاة فله بكل حرف خمسون حسنة ومن قرأه في غير صلاة وهو على وضوء فخمس وعشرون حسنة ومن قرأه على غير وضوء فعشر حسنات وما كان من القيام بالليل فهو أفضل لأنه أفرغ للقلب قال أبو ذر الغفاري رضي الله عنه أن كثرة السجود بالنهار وإن طول القيام بالليل أفضل الثاني
3:191.english: If he recites without ritual purity, reclining upon his bed, he also has merit, but it is below that [of the one who is pure and seated properly]. Allah Most High said: {الَّذِينَ يَذْكُرُونَ اللَّهَ قِيَامًا وَقُعُودًا وَعَلَىٰ جُنُوبِهِمْ وَيَتَفَكَّرُونَ فِي خَلْقِ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ} ("Those who remember Allah standing, sitting, and upon their sides, and reflect upon the creation of the heavens and the earth") — and He praised all of them, but He mentioned standing first, then sitting, then remembrance while reclining.
3:191.section_title_en: The Book of the Etiquette of Qur'an Recitation — Section 223: On the Manners of the Reciter, the Measure of Recitation, Division into Portions, Orthography, Tartīl, Weeping, Rights of the Verses, Invocations, and Vocalization
3:191.anchors:
- Root: قرا (Q-R-A)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To read, recite, gather together; the core act of assembling letters into articulated speech.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Recitation (tilāwah) is the following of the Qur'an in obedience and belief; qirā'ah is the articulation of the letters. The term carries both the physical act of vocalization and the spiritual act of devotion.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (haqīqah): to read from a written text or from memory. Metaphorical (majāz): "qara'a al-rajul" — to become religious, devoted, as the reciter is characterized by the state of worship.
- Root: سجد (S-J-D)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To bow, prostrate, lower oneself; the physical posture of placing the forehead on the ground.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Prostration is of two kinds: voluntary (ikhtiyārī) — exclusive to humans, by which reward is deserved; and subjugated (taskhīrī) — universal to all creation, as in {وَلِلَّهِ يَسْجُدُ مَنْ فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ}.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the physical act of prostration. Metaphorical: "shajarah sājidah" — a tree bending over; "ʿayn sājidah" — a languid, drooping eye. The prostration of recitation is the literal act performed in obedience to the command of the verse.
- Root: تلو (T-L-W)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To follow, to recite; the reciter "follows" the letters in sequence and "follows" the commands contained therein.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Tilāwah is following the Qur'an in deed as well as in word; the true reciter is he whose recitation is a following of the divine command.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد (Restriction & Focused Predication) — The conditional and restrictive structures in the prophetic sayings (e.g., "من قرأ القرآن في أقل من ثلاث لم يفقهه") establish a causal link between the act and its consequence, requiring precise parsing of the conditional clause to extract the legal ruling.
3:191.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'On Invocations and Supplications'

3:191.arabic: وأثنى على المتفكرين فقال تعالى الذين يذكرون الله قياما وقعودا وعلى جنوبهم ويتفكرون في خلق السموات والأرض ربنا ما خلقت هذا باطلا وقد قال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما إن قوما تفكروا في الله عز وجل فقال صلى الله عليه وسلم تفكروا في خلق الله ولا تتفكروا في الله فإنكم لن تقدروا قدره (1) وعن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه خرج على قوم ذات يوم وهم يتفكرون فقال ما لكم لا تتكلمون فقالوا نتفكر في خلق الله عز وجل قال فكذلك فافعلوا تفكروا في خلقه ولا تتفكروا فيه فإن بهذا المغرب أرضا بيضاء نورها بياضها وبياضها نورها مسيرة الشمس أربعين يوما بها خلق من خلق الله عز وجل لم يعصوا الله طرفة ع
3:191.english: I say: God — exalted be He — has commanded reflection (tafakkur) and deep contemplation (tadabbur) upon His Mighty Book in places beyond enumeration, and He has praised those who reflect. For He — exalted be He — says: {«الذين يذكرون الله قياما وقعودا وعلى جنوبهم ويتفكرون في خلق السموات والأرض ربنا ما خلقت هذا باطلا»} — "Those who remember God standing, sitting, and upon their sides, and reflect upon the creation of the heavens and the earth: 'Our Lord, You have not created this in vain'" (Āl ʿImrān 191).
3:191.section_title_en: The Virtue of Reflection (Tafakkur) Upon the Creation of God — Section 1257
3:191.anchors:
- Root: فكر (F-K-R)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root denotes the movement of the mind, turning a matter over in the heart/mind; "الفكرة" as the power that drives knowledge toward its object.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الفكرة: قوة مطرقة للعلم إلى المعلوم، والتفكر: جولان تلك القوة بحسب نظر العقل" — Reflection is the circulation of the intellect's power over what can be apprehended, seeking a mental form (ṣūrah); it is exclusive to humans and is forbidden regarding God's essence, as He transcends all form.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): "ما دار حوله فكري" (what revolves around my thought). Metaphorical (Majaz): "فكرتك مغاص الدرر" — reflection as a diver's plunge into the sea of meanings to extract pearls of wisdom.
- Root: خلق (KHLQ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root: "التقدير المستقيم" — precise, straight measurement and estimation; bringing something into being upon a measured pattern.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الخلق أصله: التقدير المستقيم، ويستعمل في إبداع الشيء من غير أصل ولا احتذاء" — creation as origination (ibdāʿ) from nothing, without prior model or pattern, as in {«خلق السماوات والأرض»} (Al-Anʿām 1); also used for bringing forth from something, as in {«خلقكم من نفس واحدة»} (Al-Nisāʾ 1).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "خلق الخراز الأديم" — the leather-worker measures the hide before cutting. Metaphorical: "خلق الله الخلق: أوجده على تقدير أوجبته الحكمة" — God's creation is bringing into existence upon a measure necessitated by wisdom.
- Root: قال (Q-W-L)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root: speech, utterance, saying; in the technical sense, the transmission of prophetic and scholarly dicta (aqwāl).
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Prepositional Interposition (باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور) — Governing the syntactic flow of reported speech chains (e.g., "قال ابن عباس... فقال صلى الله عليه وسلم"), where the narrator's interposed clauses do not break the grammatical dependency of the quotation, preserving the continuous chain of transmission (isnād).
3:191.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Contemplation'

3:193.arabic: وفي الآخرة حسنة وقنا عذاب النار ربنا إننا سمعنا مناديا ينادي للإيمان إلى قوله عز وجل إنك لا تخلف الميعاد ربنا لا تؤاخذنا إن نسينا أو أخطأنا ربنا إلى آخر السورة (3) رب اغفر لي ولوالدي وارحمهما كما ربياني صغيرا واغفر للمؤمنين والمؤمنات والمسلمين والمسلمات الأحياء منهم والأموات (4) رب اغفر وارحم وتجاوز عما تعلم وأنت الأعز الأكرم وأنت خير الراحمين وأنت خير الغافرين وإنا لله وإنا إليه راجعون ولا حول ولا قوة إلا بالله العلي العظيم وحسبنا الله ونعم الوكيل وصلى الله على محمد خاتم النبيين وآله وصحبه وسلم تسليما كثيرا (5)
3:193.english: And employ me in righteous deeds which You will accept from me. (1) O God, I ask You for pardon, well-being, good certainty, and soundness in this world and the next. (2) O You Whom sins do not harm and from Whom forgiveness does not diminish anything — grant me that which will not harm You, and give me that which will not diminish You. Our Lord, pour upon us patience and cause us to die as Muslims. You are our Protector in this world and the next; cause me to die as a Muslim and join me with the righteous. You are our Protector, so forgive us and have mercy upon us, and You are the Best of forgivers. And write for us good in this world and in the Hereafter — indeed, we have turned to You in repentance. Our Lord, upon You we rely, to You we turn in repentance, and to You is the final return. Our Lord, make us not a trial for the wrongdoing people. Our Lord, make us not a trial for those who disbelieve, and forgive us, our Lord — indeed, You are the Mighty, the Wise. Our Lord, forgive us our sins and our excesses in our affairs, make firm our feet, and grant us victory over the disbelieving people. Our Lord, forgive us and our brothers who preceded us in faith, and place not in our hearts any rancor toward those who believe — our Lord, indeed You are Kind, Merciful. Our Lord, grant us from Yourself mercy and prepare for us from our affair right guidance. Our Lord, give us good in this world and good in the Hereafter, and protect us from the chastisement of the Fire. Our Lord, indeed we have heard a caller calling to faith — to His saying, Mighty and Majestic: {«إنك لا تخلف الميعاد»} [آل عمران/ 194] — Our Lord, do not take us to task if we forget or err. Our Lord, to the end of the surah. (3) My Lord, forgive me and my parents, and have mercy upon them as they raised me when I was small; and forgive the believing men and the believing women, and the Muslim men and the Muslim women, the living among them and the dead. (4) My Lord, forgive, have mercy, and overlook what You know — and You are the Most Exalted, the Most Generous, the Best of the merciful, and the Best of the forgivers. And indeed, to God we belong and to Him we return; and there is no might and no power except through God, the Exalted, the Magnificent; and God suffices us, and He is the Best Disposer of affairs. And may God send blessings upon Muhammad, the Seal of the Prophets, and upon his family and his companions, and grant them abundant peace. (5)
3:193.section_title_en: Section 252 — Supplications for Morning and Evening: Comprehensive Prayers of the Prophet (ﷺ)
3:193.anchors:
- Root: لهم (l-h-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of swallowing/ingesting (iltihām); from this derives the sense of something being cast directly into the innermost recess of the heart (al-rawʿ).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الإلهام: إلقاء الشيء في الروع" — ilhām is the casting of a thing into the innermost consciousness, specifically from God or the higher assembly (al-malaʾ al-aʿlā). It is that which the Prophet (ﷺ) called "the touch of the angel" (limat al-malak) and "the breath of the Holy Spirit in my innermost heart" (nafth rūḥ al-qudus fī rawʿī).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): "ألهمه الله الخير: ألقاه في روعه" — God inspired him with good: He cast it into his innermost consciousness. Metaphorical (majāz): A horse that "swallows the ground" (yaltaḥimu al-arḍ) in swiftness; thus ilhām is the swift, direct ingress of divine guidance into the soul without intermediary effort.
- Root: حمد (ḥ-m-d)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The root denotes praise arising from recognition of voluntary excellence and beneficence; al-ḥamd is commendation of the beloved for their attributes and acts of goodness.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Praise (ḥamd) is the acknowledgment of beneficence (niʿmah) with reverence and love; it is distinguished from mere thanks (shukr) in that it is directed to the essence and attributes of the praised one, not solely to the benefit received.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "أحمد الله تعالى بجميع محامده" — I praise God with all His praiseworthy attributes. Metaphorical: "أحمدت صنيعه" — I found his deed praiseworthy; thus the tongue's praise must be matched by the heart's recognition of the praised one's perfection.
- Root: غفر (gh-f-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The root denotes covering and shielding; al-mighfar is the helmet that protects the head in battle.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الغفر: إلباس ما يصونه عن الدنس" — Forgiveness is the clothing of that which shields from filth. God's forgiveness (maghfirah) is His shielding of the servant from the touch of chastisement, covering the sin so that it is as though it never were.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "اللهم غفرًا" — O God, forgive. Metaphorical: The she-beasts that "did not forgive" their heedlessness (lam taghfir la-hā ghaflātuhā) — i.e., they did not shield their young from destruction; thus forgiveness is active protection, not mere erasure.
- Root: نفس (n-f-s)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The self, the soul; that which breathes and has vital spirit; also used for the very essence of a thing.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "النفس: الروح" — the soul is the spirit; and in God's saying {«ويحذركم الله نفسه»} [آل عمران/ 28], "His Self" means His very essence (dhāt), which — though grammatically expressed as an annexation implying distinction — is in reality identical, with no multiplicity in the Divine Essence.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "شيء نفيس" — a precious thing. Metaphorical: "دفق نفسه" — he poured out his blood/life; thus nafs is the seat of life, passion, and moral responsibility.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الدعاء والخبر (The Chapter of Supplication and Assertion) — Supplications (duʿāʾ) are grammatically constructed as optative sentences (inshāʾ ṭalabī) using the imperative (rabbighfir), the jussive (lā tuʾākhidhnā), and the vocative (rabbanā), yet they may embed assertive clauses (khabar) of praise (al-ḥamdu lillāh) and attestation (lā ilāha illā anta). The periodic structure of these prayers alternates between direct address to God (munādāh) and self-referential confession, requiring the translator to preserve the vocative force of "O God" and "Our Lord" without flattening into mere description.
3:193.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications, prayers, and their spiritual power, from 'On Invocations and Supplications'

3:194.arabic: والفضيلة والدرجة الرفيعة وابعثه المقام المحمود الذي وعدته إنك لا تخلف الميعاد وقال سعيد بن المسيب من صلى بأرض فلاة صلى عن يمينه ملك وعن شماله ملك فإن أذن وأقام صلى وراءه أمثال الجبال من الملائكة فضيلة المكتوبة قال الله تعالى إن الصلاة كانت على المؤمنين كتابا موقوتا وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم خمس صلوات كتبهن الله على العباد فمن جاء بهن ولم يضيع منهن شيئا استخفافا بحقهن كان له عند الله عهد أن يدخله الجنة ومن لم يأت بهن فليس له عند الله عهد إن شاء عذبه وإن شاء أدخله الجنة (5) وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم مثل الصلوات الخمس كمثل
3:194.english: Praise be to God, who has inundated His servants with His subtle graces (laṭāʾif) and filled their hearts with the lights of religion and its ordinances — which descend from the Throne of Majesty to the heaven of this world as one of the outpourings of His mercy. He has distinguished Himself from [earthly] kings through His unique possession of Majesty and Grandeur by encouraging His creatures to ask and to supplicate, saying: {«هَلْ مِن دَاعٍ فَأَسْتَجِيبَ لَهُ وَهَلْ مِن مُّسْتَغْفِرٍ فَأَغْفِرَ لَهُ»} (Is there any supplicant that I may respond to him? Is there any seeker of forgiveness that I may forgive him?). And He has set Himself apart from [earthly] sovereigns by opening the door and lifting the veil, permitting His servants to engage in intimate communion (munājāh) through the prayers, however their states may fluctuate — in congregations and in solitude. Nor did He content Himself with mere permission, but He graciously encouraged and invited [them]. Other kings, even the weakest among them, do not permit private audience except after the presentation of gifts and bribes. Glory be to Him — how great is His majesty, how mighty His dominion, how complete His gentleness, how all-encompassing His beneficence!
3:194.section_title_en: The Book of the Secrets of Prayer and Its Essential Matters — Section 120: On the Virtues of the Call to Prayer (Adhān) and the Prescribed Prayers
3:194.anchors:
- Root: صلو (Ṣ-L-W)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The root denotes the act of supplication, blessing, and the prescribed ritual prayer; its core sense involves "connection" and "turning toward."
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الصلاة" in its theological sense is the act of drawing near to God through prescribed devotional acts comprising bowing, prostration, and remembrance — a covenant (ʿahd) between the servant and his Lord.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): the ritual prayer with its known conditions and pillars. Metaphorical (majāz): supplication (duʿāʾ) and blessing (raḥmah), as in "the angels send blessings (yuṣallūn) upon the Prophet."
- Root: أذن (A-Dh-N)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To listen, to give ear; the mu'adhdhin is one who makes the call heard publicly.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The adhān is the public proclamation summoning the community to the prescribed prayer — a declaration of the time of worship.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the act of making known. Metaphorical: the call to prayer as a summons to the Divine presence.
- Root: ملك (M-L-K)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Possession, dominion, sovereignty.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الملك: هو المتصرف بالأمر والنهي في الجمهور" — The king is one who disposes by command and prohibition over the multitude. God's sovereignty (mulk) is absolute and unshared.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: ownership and dominion. Metaphorical: "ملك عليه أمره" — mastery over one's own affair, self-possession.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Prepositional Interposition (باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور) — The periodic sentence structure in the opening doxology employs suspended clauses (ḥāl) that qualify the subject while maintaining syntactic cohesion through the governing verb's semantic reach.

---
3:194.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'On Invocations and Supplications'

3:194.arabic: وقوله تعالى وتجعلون رزقكم أنكم تكذبون أي شكر رزقكم وقوله عز وجل وآتنا ما وعدتنا على رسلك أي على ألسنة رسلك فحذف ألسنة وقوله تعالى إنا أنزلناه في ليلة القدر أراد القرآن وما سبق له ذكر وقال عز وجل حتى توارت الحجاب أراد الشمس وما سبق لها ذكر وقوله تعالى والذين اتخذوا من دونه أولياء ما نعبدهم إلا ليقربونا إلى الله زلفى أي يقولون ما نعبدهم وقوله عز وجل فمال هؤلاء القوم لا يكادون يفقهون حديثا ما أصابك من حسنة فمن الله وما أصابك من سيئة فمن نفسك معناه لا يفقهون حديثا يقولون ما أصابك من حسنة فمن الله فإن لم يرد هذا كان مناقضا لقوله قل كل
3:194.english: I say: The Prophet (peace be upon him) was asked about the means of deliverance from these trials, and he said: "The Book of Allah — act by what is in it, for it is that which delivers one from them." The questioner repeated this three times, and he (peace be upon him) said three times: "Learn the Book of Allah, Mighty and Glorious, and act by what is in it, for in it is deliverance."
3:194.section_title_en: The Book of the Etiquette of Recitation — Section 233: On Understanding the Meanings of the Qur'an and the Limits of Interpretation
3:194.anchors:
- Root: ف-ه-م (f-h-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الفهم: هيئة للإنسان بها يتحقق معاني ما يحسن" — comprehension as an inherent faculty by which one ascertains meanings
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الفهم: هيئة للإنسان بها يتحقق معاني ما يحسن... وأفهمته: إذا قلت له حتى تصوره" — comprehension is a cognitive disposition; distinction between understanding (fahm) and making understood (ifhām)
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "تقول: من لم يؤت من سوء الفهم أتى من سوء الإفهام" — literal usage; failure of understanding often stems from failure of communication
- Root: ف-س-ر (f-s-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "وكل شيء يعرف به تفسير الشيء ومعناه، فهو تَفْسِرَتُه" — that by which a thing's meaning is made known
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "التفسير قد يقال فيما يختص بمفردات الألفاظ وغريبها، وفيما يختص بالتأويل" — tafsīr concerns lexical surface; taʾwīl concerns deeper meaning
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "هذا كلام يحتاج إلى فسر وتفسير" — literal: exposition of what is obscure
- Root: و-ج-ل (w-j-l)
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الوجل: استشعار الخوف" — the sensing of fear; used of hearts trembling at divine mention
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "لو واجلت فلانا لوجلته: لغلبته في الوجل" — literal sense of fear; metaphorical extension to overpowering in fear
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — the particle innamā restricts predication, essential for parsing the Prophet's saying "innamā al-aʿmālu bi-l-niyyāt" and analogous restrictive formulations in the ḥadīth cited herein
3:194.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Etiquette of Quran Recitation'

4:69.arabic: المقربين من النبيين والصديقين والشهداء والصالحين وحسن أولئك رفيقا ولما كان الوسط الحقيقي بين الطرفين في غاية الغموض بل هو أدق من الشعر وأحد من السيف فلا جرم أن من استوى على هذا الصراط المستقيم في الدنيا جاز على مثل هذا الصراط في الآخرة وقلما ينفك العبد عن ميل عن الصراط المستقيم أعني الوسط حتى لا يميل إلى أحد الجانبين فيكون قلبه معلقا بالجانب الذي مال إليه
4:69.english: I say: The soul (nafs) that belongs to the human being — that by which he is distinguished from the beasts — for he is not distinguished from them by the power of eating, copulation, sight, or any other such thing. Rather, he is distinguished by the knowledge of things as they truly are. And the Origin of all things, their Existentiator and their Inventor, is God, Mighty and Majestic — He who made them things. So if one knew everything but did not know God, Mighty and Majestic, it would be as though he knew nothing at all. And the sign of knowledge is love: whoever knows God Most High loves Him. And the sign of love is that one does not prefer over Him this world nor any other beloved thing. As God Most High said: {«Say: If your fathers, your sons, your brothers, your spouses, your clans — the wealth you have acquired, commerce whose decline you fear, and dwellings you find pleasing — are more beloved to you than God and His Messenger and striving in His cause, then wait until God brings about His command»} [Q 9:24]. So whoever possesses something more beloved to him than God — his heart is sick. Just as any stomach to which clay has become more beloved than bread and water, or whose appetite for bread and water has fallen away — it is sick. These are the signs of sickness. And by this it is known that all hearts are sick — except what God wills. Yet among sicknesses there are those the sufferer does not recognize; and the sickness of the heart is among those the sufferer does not recognize. For this reason he is heedless of it. And even if he recognized it, patience upon the bitterness of its medicine would be difficult for him — for its medicine is opposing the appetites, and that is the tearing out of the spirit (nafs). And if he found in himself the strength of patience upon it, he would not find a skillful physician to treat him — for the physicians are the scholars, and sickness has overcome them. So the sick physician rarely attends to his own cure. For this reason the malady has become chronic and the sickness chronic. This science has become effaced, and the medicine of hearts is denied entirely, and the sickness of the heart is denied. And creation has turned to the love of this world and to deeds whose outward form is acts of worship but whose inward reality is habit and ostentation. These are the signs of the roots of sicknesses.
4:69.section_title_en: The Soul's Distinction, the Sickness of the Heart, and the Path of Moderation
4:69.anchors:
- Root: نفس (n-f-s)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The self, soul, or spirit; that by which a thing is distinguished in its essential reality
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The soul (nafs) as the principle of rational discrimination and knowledge, distinguishing humans from beasts
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the self or person; Metaphorical: the rational soul as the seat of knowledge and moral responsibility
- Root: مرض (m-r-d)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Departure from the state of health and equilibrium
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Sickness of the heart as a metaphor for moral and spiritual vices — ignorance, cowardice, avarice, hypocrisy
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: bodily illness; Metaphorical: spiritual malady whereby the heart inclines toward what is harmful and away from what is beneficial
- Root: قلب (q-l-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The heart; that which is ever-turning and fluctuating between states
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The heart as the seat of understanding and moral perception; its "turning" (taqlīb) signifies its instability between soundness and sickness
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the physical organ; Metaphorical: the spiritual faculty of cognition and moral discernment
- Root: خلق (kh-l-q)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Measured, proportioned disposition; character and temperament
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Moral character as the inward form (ṣūrah bāṭinah) corresponding to the outward physical form
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: measuring and proportioning; Metaphorical: the ingrained disposition that governs action
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — The use of restrictive constructions to isolate the defining characteristic of the human soul as knowledge of God, not animal appetites
4:69.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Remembrance of Death and Afterlife'

4:69.arabic: {فأولئك مع الذين أنعم الله عليهم من النبيين والصديقين والشهداء والصالحين وحسن أولئك رفيقا} // حديث سادات المؤمنين في الجنة من إذا تغدى لم يجد عشاء الحديث عزاه صاحب مسند الفردوس للطبراني من رواية أبي حازم عن أبي هريرة مختصرا بلفظ سادة الفقراء في الجنة الحديث ولم أره في معاجم الطبراني ألا يا أخي متى جمعت هذا المال بعد هذا البيان فإنك مبطل فيما ادعيت أنك للبر والفضل تجمعه لا ولكنك خوفا من الفقر تجمعه وللنعيم والزينة والتكاثر والفخر والعلو والرياء والسمعة والتعظيم والتكرمة تجمعه ثم تزعم إنك لأعمال البر تجم
4:69.english: O you who are deluded! Have you not known that your fear of plunging into ambiguous matters (shubuhāt) is higher, more virtuous, and greater for your rank with God than acquiring ambiguous wealth and expending it in the path of God and the path of righteousness? This has been conveyed to us from some of the people of knowledge, who said: "That you abandon a single dirham out of fear that it might not be lawful is better for you than that you give in charity a thousand dīnārs from ambiguous wealth, not knowing whether it is lawful for you or not."
4:69.section_title_en: The Book of Lawful and Unlawful — Beginning of the Discourse
4:69.anchors:
- Root: شبه (Sh-B-H)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of resemblance and ambiguity; what is not clearly distinguished from its opposite.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-Shubhah denotes uncertainty in discernment between the lawful and unlawful — a state where the heart cannot attain decisive knowledge (yaqīn).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal usage pertains to visual resemblance; metaphorical (majāz) usage applies to moral and legal ambiguity that clouds the conscience.
- Root: ورق (W-R-ʿ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Abstinence and scrupulous avoidance; the root conveys turning away from what is doubtful.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-Waraʿ is the highest station of the God-fearing — abstaining not only from the unlawful but from the doubtful to safeguard one's religion.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical avoidance; metaphorical: the soul's restraint from contamination by ambiguous gains.
- Root: حسب (H-S-B)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Reckoning, enumeration, and accounting.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-Ḥisāb on the Day of Resurrection is the divine scrutiny of one's deeds — its severity is proportional to one's wealth and worldly engagements.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: arithmetic computation; metaphorical: the moral audit of one's life before God.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب النداء والتحذير (The Chapter of Vocative Address and Warning) — The repeated vocative "ويحك" (Woe to you) functions as a rhetorical warning (taḥdhīr) and lamentation, structuring the author's direct admonitory address to the deluded soul.
4:69.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'Remembrance of Death and Afterlife'

4:69.arabic: النبيين والصديقين والشهداء والصالحين دون الذين غضب عليهم من الكفار والزائغين من اليهود والنصارى والصابئين ثم التمس الإجابة وقل آمين فإذا تلوت الفاتحة كذلك فيشبه أن تكون من الذين قال الله تعالى فيهم فيما أخبر عنه النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قسمت الصلاة بيني وبين عبدي نصفين نصفها لي ونصفها لعبدي ولعبدي ما سأل (1) يقول العبد الحمد لله رب العالمين فيقول الله عز وجل حمدني عبدي وأثنى علي وهو معنى قوله سمع الله لمن حمده الحديث الخ فلو لم يكن لك من صلاتك حظ سوى ذكر الله لك في جلاله وعظمته فناهيك
4:69.english: For this reason, he, peace be upon him, said: "Give us rest, O Bilāl" (1) — meaning, give us rest through it (the prayer) and through the call to it, for his delight, peace be upon him, was in it.
4:69.section_title_en: The Inner Works of Prayer: Unveiling the Heart's Secrets in the Ritual Prayer (Asrār al-Ṣalāh)
4:69.anchors:
- Root: قلب (Q-L-B)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To turn a thing over, to revolve it, to divert it from one state to another; the heart as that which is constantly turning and fluctuating.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "قلب الشيء: تصريفه وصرفه عن وجه إلى وجه" — The heart is that which is turned and diverted; its rectitude lies in its orientation towards God, its ruin in its turning towards other than Him.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): "قلب الشيء قلبا: حوله عن وجهه" (to turn a thing from its face). Metaphorical (Majaz): "قلب المعلم الصبيان: صرفهم إلى بيوتهم" (the teacher turned the boys towards their homes) — thus the heart's turning is its direction and intent.
- Root: وجه (W-J-H)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The face; the foremost, noblest, and most apparent part of a thing.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "ولما كان الوجه أول ما يستقبلك، وأشرف ما في ظاهر البدن استعمل في مستقبل كل شيء، وفي أشرفه ومبدئه" — The face is used metaphorically for the essence and the direction of a thing; the "face of the heart" is its intention and aspiration.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "واجهته مواجهة ووجاها" (to face one another). Metaphorical: "هذا وجه الثوب. ووجه القوم، وهؤلاء وجوه البلد" (the face of a garment, the chiefs of a people) — thus the "face" of the heart is its foremost orientation.
- Root: وجل (W-J-L)
  * Lisan / Ayn: A trembling of the heart from fear or awe.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الوجل: استشعار الخوف" — The sensing of fear; the heart's tremor before the majesty of the Divine.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "رجل وجل، وقوم وجال، وقد وجل وجلا" — A man trembling with fear.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — The particle "innamā" restricts and confines the predicate to the subject alone, negating it from all else. This is crucial for understanding "إنما هذه الظواهر تحريكات للبواطن" — the outward acts are *only* movements to stir the inward realities, nothing more.
4:69.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications, prayers, and their spiritual power, from 'On Invocations and Supplications'

4:80.arabic: فضيلتك عنده أن جعل طاعتك طاعته فقال عز وجل من يطع الرسول فقد أطاع الله بأبي أنت وأمي يا رسول الله لقد بلغ من فضيلتك عنده أن أخبرك بالعفو عنك قبل أن يخبرك بالذنب فقال تعالى عفا الله عنك لم أذنت لهم بأبي أنت وأمي يا رسول الله لقد بلغ من فضيلتك عنده أن بعثك آخر الأنبياء وذكرك في أولهم فقال عز وجل وإذ أخذنا من النبيين ميثاقهم ومنك ومن نوح وإبراهيم الآية بأبي أنت وأمي يا رسول الله لقد بلغ من فضيلتك عنده أن أهل النار يودون أن يكونوا قد أطاعوك وهم بين أطباقها يعذبون يقولون يا ليتنا أطعنا الله وأطعنا الرسولا بأب
4:80.english: God Most High has said: {«Indeed, God and His angels send blessings upon the Prophet. O you who have believed, send blessings upon him and greet him with a greeting of peace»} (Q. 33:56). And it is related that he, peace be upon him, came one day with the signs of glad tidings visible upon his face, and he, peace be upon him, said: "Gabriel came to me, peace be upon him, and said: 'Are you not pleased, O Muhammad, that no one from your community sends a single blessing upon you except that I send ten blessings upon him, and no one from your community greets you with peace except that I greet him with peace ten times?'" (1) And he, peace be upon him, said: "Whoever sends blessings upon me, the angels send blessings upon him as long as he continues to send blessings upon me — so let him reduce or increase at that." (2) And he, peace be upon him, said: "The people most deserving of me are those who send the most blessings upon me." (3) And he, peace be upon him, said: "It suffices a believer for miserliness that I am mentioned in his presence and he does not send blessings upon me." (4) And he, peace be upon him, said: "Multiply your sending of blessings upon me on the day of Friday." (5) And he, peace be upon him, said: "Whoever sends blessings upon me from my community, ten good deeds are written for him and ten evil deeds are erased from him." (6) And he, peace be upon him, said: "Whoever says upon hearing the call to prayer and the iqāmah: 'O God, Lord of this perfect call and the established prayer, send blessings upon Muhammad, Your servant and Your Messenger, and grant him the means (al-wasīlah) and the excellence (al-faḍīlah) and the lofty rank (al-darajah al-rafīʿah) and the intercession (al-shafāʿah) on the Day of Resurrection' — my intercession becomes permissible for him." (7) And the Messenger of God, peace be upon him, said: "Whoever sends blessings upon me in a book, the angels continue to seek forgiveness for him as long as my name remains in that book." (8) And he, peace be upon him, said: "Indeed, upon the earth there are traveling angels who convey to me the greetings of peace from my community." (9) And he, peace be upon him, said: "No one greets me with peace except that God returns my soul to me until I respond to his greeting." (1) And it was said to him: "O Messenger of God, how do we send blessings upon you?" He said: "Say: 'O God, send blessings upon Muhammad, Your servant, and upon his family, his wives, and his descendants, as You sent blessings upon Abraham and the family of Abraham; and bless Muhammad, his wives, and his descendants, as You blessed Abraham and the family of Abraham. Indeed, You are Praiseworthy, Glorious.'" (2)
4:80.section_title_en: Section 244 — On the Virtues of Invoking Blessings upon the Prophet (Ṣalawāt) and the Excellence of His Rank
4:80.anchors:
- Root: صلو (Ṣ-L-W)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root denotes prayer, blessing, supplication; al-ṣalāh from God is mercy (raḥmah), from angels is seeking forgiveness (istighfār), from believers is supplication (duʿā').
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-ṣalāh from God is pure mercy and beneficence; from angels it is their petition for forgiveness; from humans it is humble supplication. The divine ṣalāh upon the Prophet is an elevation of his mention and an increase in his honor.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): supplication and bending in worship. Metaphorical (majāz): God's ṣalāh upon the Prophet is His mercy and His exaltation of him before the angels; the believers' ṣalāh is their invocation and reverence.
- Root: سلم (S-L-M)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Root denotes safety, peace, deliverance; taslīm is the greeting of peace and submission.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Salām from God is His safeguarding; the greeting of salām upon the Prophet is an acknowledgment of his prophetic rank and a prayer for his perfect safety.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: greeting of peace. Metaphorical: the angels' conveyance of the believers' salām to the Prophet even after his death, indicating the enduring bond.
- Root: حمد (Ḥ-M-D)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root denotes praise, commendation; maḥmūd is the one praised.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Ḥamd is praise for voluntary beneficence; al-ḥamd li-Llāh encompasses all praise due to God's perfect attributes.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: to praise for good. Metaphorical: to find praiseworthy (aḥmadtu al-arḍ: I found the land agreeable).
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Interposition (al-faṣl bayna al-jār wa al-majrūr) — The periodic structure of the ḥadīth reports here follows the canonical pattern of embedding quoted speech within narrative frames, maintaining syntactic cohesion across multiple levels of reported discourse.
4:80.topic: Al-Ghazali on the journey of the soul, death, and the Hereafter, from 'On Invocations and Supplications'

4:103.arabic: وقال تعالى فإذا قضيتم الصلاة فاذكروا الله قياما وقعودا وعلى جنوبكم قال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما أي بالليل والنهار في البر والبحر والسفر والحضر والغنى والفقر والمرض والصحة والسر والعلانية وقال تعالى في ذم المنافقين ولا يذكرون الله إلا قليلا وقال عز وجل واذكر ربك في نفسك تضرعا وخيفة ودون الجهر من القول بالغدو والآصال ولا تكن من الغافلين وقال تعالى ولذكر الله أكبر قال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما له وجهان أحدهما أن ذكر الله تعالى لكم أعظم من ذكرككم إياه والآخر أن ذكر الله أعظم من كل عبادة سواه إلى غير ذلك من الآيات وأ
4:103.english:
- Root: ذكر (dhakara)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning is "to remember, to mention, to recollect." The root carries the dual sense of mental recollection and verbal utterance. In Kitab al-Ayn, the root denotes the opposite of forgetfulness (nisyan), and its verbal form encompasses both the internal act of remembrance and the external act of mentioning.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الذكر: حضور المعنى في النفس، وقد يطلق على إبقاء المعنى باللسان. والذكر ضربان: ذكر بالقلب، وذكر باللسان. وقال تعالى: {فاذكروني أذكركم} [البقرة/152] — فذكر العبد ربه بالتعظيم والثناء، وذكر الله عبده بالإنعام والإكرام." The theological nuance distinguishes between the creature's remembrance (which is petition and praise) and the Creator's remembrance (which is response and reward).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): "ذكرت الشيء: حفظته ووعيته. وذكرت فلانا: جريت بذكره على لسانك." Metaphorical (Majaz): "ذكر الله العبد: أثنى عليه وأجزل له الثواب. ومن المجاز: قوله تعالى {ولذكر الله أكبر} — أي ذكر الله إياكم أعظم من ذكركم إياه." The rhetorical distinction is crucial here: when Allah "remembers" His servant, it is an act of grace, not cognition.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين المبتدأ والخبر (Interposition between Subject and Predicate) — In the verse {ولذكر الله أكبر}, the grammatical structure allows for the subject (ذكر الله) to be read as either the creature's remembrance of Allah or Allah's remembrance of the creature, with the predicate (أكبر) applying to whichever reading is adopted. This syntactic ambiguity is deliberate and productive of multiple valid interpretations.
4:103.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'On Invocations and Supplications'

4:103.arabic: قال الله تعالى إن الصلاة كانت على المؤمنين كتابا موقوتا وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم خمس صلوات كتبهن الله على العباد فمن جاء بهن ولم يضيع منهن شيئا استخفافا بحقهن كان له عند الله عهد أن يدخله الجنة ومن لم يأت بهن فليس له عند الله عهد إن شاء عذبه وإن شاء أدخله الجنة (5) وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم مثل الصلوات الخمس كمثل نهر عذب غمر بباب أحدكم يقتحم فيه كل يوم خمس مرات فما ترون ذلك يبقي من درنه قالوا لا شيء قال صلى الله عليه وسلم
4:103.english: Praise be to God, who has inundated His servants with His subtle graces (laṭāʾif) and filled their hearts with the lights of religion and its ordinances — which descend from the Throne of Majesty to the heaven of this world as one of the outpourings of His mercy. He has distinguished Himself from [earthly] kings through His unique possession of Majesty and Grandeur by encouraging His creatures to ask and to supplicate, saying: {«هَلْ مِن دَاعٍ فَأَسْتَجِيبَ لَهُ وَهَلْ مِن مُّسْتَغْفِرٍ فَأَغْفِرَ لَهُ»} (Is there any supplicant that I may respond to him? Is there any seeker of forgiveness that I may forgive him?). And He has set Himself apart from [earthly] sovereigns by opening the door and lifting the veil, permitting His servants to engage in intimate communion (munājāh) through the prayers, however their states may fluctuate — in congregations and in solitude. Nor did He content Himself with mere permission, but He graciously encouraged and invited [them]. Other kings, even the weakest among them, do not permit private audience except after the presentation of gifts and bribes. Glory be to Him — how great is His majesty, how mighty His dominion, how complete His gentleness, how all-encompassing His beneficence!
4:103.section_title_en: The Book of the Secrets of Prayer and Its Essential Matters — Section 120: On the Virtues of the Call to Prayer (Adhān) and the Prescribed Prayers
4:103.anchors:
- Root: صلو (Ṣ-L-W)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The root denotes the act of supplication, blessing, and the prescribed ritual prayer; its core sense involves "connection" and "turning toward."
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الصلاة" in its theological sense is the act of drawing near to God through prescribed devotional acts comprising bowing, prostration, and remembrance — a covenant (ʿahd) between the servant and his Lord.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): the ritual prayer with its known conditions and pillars. Metaphorical (majāz): supplication (duʿāʾ) and blessing (raḥmah), as in "the angels send blessings (yuṣallūn) upon the Prophet."
- Root: أذن (A-Dh-N)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To listen, to give ear; the mu'adhdhin is one who makes the call heard publicly.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The adhān is the public proclamation summoning the community to the prescribed prayer — a declaration of the time of worship.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the act of making known. Metaphorical: the call to prayer as a summons to the Divine presence.
- Root: ملك (M-L-K)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Possession, dominion, sovereignty.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الملك: هو المتصرف بالأمر والنهي في الجمهور" — The king is one who disposes by command and prohibition over the multitude. God's sovereignty (mulk) is absolute and unshared.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: ownership and dominion. Metaphorical: "ملك عليه أمره" — mastery over one's own affair, self-possession.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Prepositional Interposition (باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور) — The periodic sentence structure in the opening doxology employs suspended clauses (ḥāl) that qualify the subject while maintaining syntactic cohesion through the governing verb's semantic reach.

4:110.arabic: الله إن الله يغفر الذنوب جميعا إنه هو الغفور الرحيم وقال تعالى ومن يعمل سوءا أو يظلم نفسه ثم يستغفر الله يجد الله غفورا رحيما ونحن نستغفر الله تعالى من كل ما زلت به القدم أو طغى به القلم في كتابنا هذا وفي سائر كتبنا ونستغفره من أقوالنا التي لا توافقها أعمالنا ونستغفره مما ادعيناه وأظهرناه من العلم والبصيرة بدين الله تعالى مع التقصير فيه ونستغفره من كل علم وعمل قصدنا به وجهه الكريم ثم خالطه غيره ونستغفره من كل وعد وعدناه به من أنفسنا ثم قصرنا في الوفاء به ونستغفره من كل نعمة أنعم بها علينا فاستعملناها في معصيته ونستغفره من كل تصريح وتعريض بنقصان ناقص وتقصير مقصر ك
4:110.english: For Allah, exalted is He, has said: {«إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَا يَغْفِرُ أَنْ يُشْرَكَ بِهِ وَيَغْفِرُ مَا دُونَ ذَلِكَ لِمَنْ يَشَاءُ»} (Indeed, Allah does not forgive that partners be associated with Him, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills) [Al-Nisa' 4:48]. And He said: {«قُلْ يَا عِبَادِيَ الَّذِينَ أَسْرَفُوا عَلَى أَنْفُسِهِمْ لَا تَقْنَطُوا مِنْ رَحْمَةِ اللَّهِ إِنَّ اللَّهَ يَغْفِرُ الذُّنُوبَ جَمِيعًا إِنَّهُ هُوَ الْغَفُورُ الرَّحِيمُ»} (Say: O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of Allah. Indeed, Allah forgives all sins. Indeed, He is the Forgiving, the Merciful) [Al-Zumar 39:53]. And He said: {«وَمَنْ يَعْمَلْ سُوءًا أَوْ يَظْلِمْ نَفْسَهُ ثُمَّ يَسْتَغْفِرِ اللَّهَ يَجِدِ اللَّهَ غَفُورًا رَحِيمًا»} (And whoever does evil or wrongs himself, then seeks forgiveness from Allah, he will find Allah Forgiving, Merciful) [Al-Nisa' 4:110].
4:110.section_title_en: Sealing the Book with a Chapter on the Vastness of Allah's Mercy, by Way of Seeking an Auspicious Omen (Tafa'ul)
4:110.anchors:
- Root: فأل (Fa'l)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The core root denotes a good omen or auspicious sign, as opposed to الطيرة (tiyarah, ill omen); the Prophet ﷺ loved the good omen.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The term carries a theological nuance of hopeful expectation (rajā') grounded in divine benevolence, not in superstitious causality.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): a favorable sign perceived by the senses. Metaphorical (Majaz): the act of framing one's closing deeds around a hopeful sign of divine acceptance.
- Root: غفر (Ghafr)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Covering and shielding from defilement; forgiveness as concealment of sin.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الغفر: إلباس ما يصونه عن الدنس" — Divine forgiveness (maghfirah) is that Allah shields the servant from the touch of chastisement.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "اللهم غفرا" (seeking pardon). Metaphorical: the sweeping away of sins entirely, as in the verse {إِنَّ اللَّهَ يَغْفِرُ الذُّنُوبَ جَمِيعًا}.
- Root: رحم (Rahm)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Tenderness and compassion; the womb (rahim) as the seat of kinship-mercy.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Mercy (rahmah) as an attribute of Allah denoting His will to bestow beneficence and withhold punishment.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: compassion felt by a creature. Metaphorical (Majaz): divine beneficence (ihsān) and graciousness (karam) that overflow to all creation.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The periodic structure of supplication (istighfar) with repeated "من" (from) clauses allows for expansive enumeration of sins sought for forgiveness, each governed by the initial verb "نستغفره" (we seek His forgiveness), maintaining syntactic cohesion across the long sentence.

4:110.arabic: ومن يعمل سوءا أو يظلم به ثم يستغفر الله يجد الله غفورا رحيما وقال عز وجل فسبح بحمد ربك واستغفره إنه كان توابا وقال تعالى والمستغفرين بالأسحار وكان صلى الله عليه وسلم يكثر أن يقول سبحانك اللهم وبحمدك اللهم اغفر لي إنك أنت التواب الرحيم (1) وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم من أكثر من الاستغفار جعل الله عز وجل له من كل هم فرجا ومن كل ضيق مخرجا وارزقه من حيث لا يحتسب (2) وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم إني لأستغفر الله تعالى وأتوب إليه في اليوم سبعين مرة (3) هذا مع أنه صلى الله عليه وسلم
4:110.english: God Most High said: {«والذين إذا فعلوا فاحشة أو ظلموا أنفسهم ذكروا الله فاستغفروا لذنوبهم»} — "And those who, when they commit an indecency or wrong themselves, remember God and seek forgiveness for their sins" {آل عمران/135}.
4:110.anchors:
- Root: ذنب (dhanb)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of "tail" or "taking hold of a tail"; extended to signify a sin as that which trails behind and follows a person.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الذنب في الأصل: الأخذ بذنب الشيء" — sin is that by which one is seized and held accountable; used metaphorically for a fault that clings to its perpetrator.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: tail of an animal. Metaphorical: "هو من الأذناب" — one who follows; sin as that which trails the soul and must be severed through repentance.
- Root: غفر (ghafara)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Covering, veiling, protecting from defilement; a shield or helmet (المغفر).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الغفران والمغفرة من الله هو أن يصون العبد من أن يمسه العذاب" — divine forgiveness is God's protection of the servant from being touched by punishment.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: to cover and protect. Metaphorical: God's "covering" of sins — not merely erasure, but active safeguarding of the sinner from consequence.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The frequent interposition of "يا رب" and vocative constructions between the subject and predicate in supplicatory sentences, as in "اللهم اغفر لي," where the vocative particle governs the imperative verb's addressee, reflecting the grammatical permissibility of separation between governing and governed elements in invocational speech.

4:142.arabic: وقال تعالى في ذم المنافقين ولا يذكرون الله إلا قليلا وقال عز وجل واذكر ربك في نفسك تضرعا وخيفة ودون الجهر من القول بالغدو والآصال ولا تكن من الغافلين وقال تعالى ولذكر الله أكبر قال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما له وجهان أحدهما أن ذكر الله تعالى لكم أعظم من ذكرككم إياه والآخر أن ذكر الله أعظم من كل عبادة سواه إلى غير ذلك من الآيات وأما الأخبار فقد قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ذاكر الله في الغافلين كالشجرة في وسط الهشيم (1) وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم ذاكر الله في الغافلين كالمقاتل بين الفارين وقال صلى ال
4:142.english:
- Root: ذكر (dhakara)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning is "to remember, to mention, to recollect." The root carries the dual sense of mental recollection and verbal utterance. In Kitab al-Ayn, the root denotes the opposite of forgetfulness (nisyan), and its verbal form encompasses both the internal act of remembrance and the external act of mentioning.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الذكر: حضور المعنى في النفس، وقد يطلق على إبقاء المعنى باللسان. والذكر ضربان: ذكر بالقلب، وذكر باللسان. وقال تعالى: {فاذكروني أذكركم} [البقرة/152] — فذكر العبد ربه بالتعظيم والثناء، وذكر الله عبده بالإنعام والإكرام." The theological nuance distinguishes between the creature's remembrance (which is petition and praise) and the Creator's remembrance (which is response and reward).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): "ذكرت الشيء: حفظته ووعيته. وذكرت فلانا: جريت بذكره على لسانك." Metaphorical (Majaz): "ذكر الله العبد: أثنى عليه وأجزل له الثواب. ومن المجاز: قوله تعالى {ولذكر الله أكبر} — أي ذكر الله إياكم أعظم من ذكركم إياه." The rhetorical distinction is crucial here: when Allah "remembers" His servant, it is an act of grace, not cognition.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين المبتدأ والخبر (Interposition between Subject and Predicate) — In the verse {ولذكر الله أكبر}, the grammatical structure allows for the subject (ذكر الله) to be read as either the creature's remembrance of Allah or Allah's remembrance of the creature, with the predicate (أكبر) applying to whichever reading is adopted. This syntactic ambiguity is deliberate and productive of multiple valid interpretations.
