  * Lisan / Ayn: The root denotes covering and shielding; al-mighfar is the helmet that protects the head in battle.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الغفر: إلباس ما يصونه عن الدنس" — Forgiveness is the clothing of that which shields from filth. God's forgiveness (maghfirah) is His shielding of the servant from the touch of chastisement, covering the sin so that it is as though it never were.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "اللهم غفرًا" — O God, forgive. Metaphorical: The she-beasts that "did not forgive" their heedlessness (lam taghfir la-hā ghaflātuhā) — i.e., they did not shield their young from destruction; thus forgiveness is active protection, not mere erasure.
- Root: نفس (n-f-s)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The self, the soul; that which breathes and has vital spirit; also used for the very essence of a thing.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "النفس: الروح" — the soul is the spirit; and in God's saying {«ويحذركم الله نفسه»} [آل عمران/ 28], "His Self" means His very essence (dhāt), which — though grammatically expressed as an annexation implying distinction — is in reality identical, with no multiplicity in the Divine Essence.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "شيء نفيس" — a precious thing. Metaphorical: "دفق نفسه" — he poured out his blood/life; thus nafs is the seat of life, passion, and moral responsibility.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الدعاء والخبر (The Chapter of Supplication and Assertion) — Supplications (duʿāʾ) are grammatically constructed as optative sentences (inshāʾ ṭalabī) using the imperative (rabbighfir), the jussive (lā tuʾākhidhnā), and the vocative (rabbanā), yet they may embed assertive clauses (khabar) of praise (al-ḥamdu lillāh) and attestation (lā ilāha illā anta). The periodic structure of these prayers alternates between direct address to God (munādāh) and self-referential confession, requiring the translator to preserve the vocative force of "O God" and "Our Lord" without flattening into mere description.
12:101.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'On Invocations and Supplications'

13:11.arabic: تعالى {إن الله لا يغير ما بقوم حتى يغيروا ما بأنفسهم} وإنما التغير تكثير الشهوات فهي مرتع الشياطين ومرعاهم فما دامت مخصبة لم ينقطع ترددهم وما داموا يترددون لم ينكشف للعبد جلال الله سبحانه وكان محجوبا عن لقائه وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم لولا أن الشياطين يحومون على قلوب بني آدم لنظروا إلى ملكوت السموات (3) فمن هذا الوجه صار الصوم باب العبادة وصار جنة وإذا عظمت فضيلته إلى هذا الحد فلا بد من بيان شروطه الظاهرة والباطنة بذكر أركانه وسننه وشروطه الباطنة ونبين ذلك بثلاثة فصول
13:11.english: To proceed: Fasting is one quarter of faith, by virtue of his saying, peace and blessings be upon him: "Fasting is half of patience" — and by virtue of his saying, peace and blessings be upon him: "Patience is half of faith" {«الإيمان»}. Then it is distinguished by a particular characteristic of its attribution to Allah the Exalted, above all the other pillars — for Allah the Exalted said, in what His Prophet narrated from Him, peace and blessings be upon him: "Every good deed is multiplied tenfold up to seven hundred times, except fasting, for it is Mine, and I shall reward it." And Allah the Exalted has said: {«Only the patient shall be paid their reward in full without reckoning»} (Q 39:10). And fasting is half of patience — so its reward has surpassed the law of measure and reckoning. And sufficient for you in knowing its excellence is his saying, peace and blessings be upon him: "By Him in whose hand is my soul, the change in the breath of the mouth of the fasting person is more fragrant to Allah than the scent of musk. Allah the Exalted says: 'He only abandons his appetite, his food, and his drink for My sake — so fasting is for Me, and I shall reward it.'" And he said, peace and blessings be upon him: "Paradise has a gate called al-Rayyān, through which none shall enter except the fasting ones." And the fasting person is promised the meeting with Allah the Exalted as a portion of his fasting. And he said, peace and blessings be upon him: "For the fasting person there are two joys: a joy when he breaks his fast, and a joy when he meets his Lord." And he said, peace and blessings be upon him: "Everything has a gate, and the gate of worship is fasting." And he said, peace and blessings be upon him: "The sleep of the fasting person is worship." And Abū Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, narrated that he, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "When the month of Ramaḍān enters, the gates of Paradise are opened, the gates of the Fire are closed, the devils are chained, and a caller calls out: 'O seeker of good, come forth! O seeker of evil, desist!'" And Wakīʿ said concerning His saying, the Exalted: {«Eat and drink in satisfaction for what you sent forth in the days past»} (Q 69:24) — these are the days of fasting, for in them they abandoned eating and drinking. And the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, gathered in the rank of divine boasting (mubāhāh) between renunciation of the world and fasting, saying: "Allah the Exalted boasts to His angels of the young worshiper, saying: 'O young man who abandons his appetite for My sake, who devotes his youth to Me — you are to Me as some of My angels.'" And he said, peace and blessings be upon him, concerning the fasting person: "Allah the Exalted says: 'Look, O My angels, at My servant — he has abandoned his appetite, his pleasure, his food, and his drink for My sake.'" And it was said concerning His saying, the Exalted: {«No soul knows what comfort has been concealed for them, as a reward for what they used to do»} (Q 32:17) — it was said: their deed was fasting, because He said: {«Only the patient shall be paid their reward in full without reckoning»} — so the reward of the fasting person is poured out upon him without measure, and is dealt out to him in bulk, not falling under any imagination or estimation.
13:11.section_title_en: The Book of the Secrets of Fasting — Section 185: On the Excellence of Fasting and Its Distinction Among the Acts of Worship
13:11.anchors:
- Root: صوم (ṣ-w-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core linguistic root meaning — abstention from any act, whether eating, speaking, or walking; a horse that refrains from movement or fodder is called ṣā'im.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological/Kalam semantic nuance — "الصوم في الأصل: الإمساك عن الفعل" — fasting is fundamentally the restraint of the self from action; it is an inward act of the heart, invisible to creation.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal vs Metaphorical distinction — Haqiqah: the month of fasting, "فمن شهد منكم الشهر فليصمه" (Q 2:185); Majaz: "صام الفرس على آريه" — a horse standing still at its tether, refusing fodder, metaphorically "fasting."
- Root: عله (ʿ-l-h)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core linguistic root meaning — to feed or pasture; related to cultivation and nourishment.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological/Kalam semantic nuance — not directly attested in Mufradat for this root; the root pertains to the means by which the body is sustained, which is precisely what the fasting person abstains from.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal vs Metaphorical distinction — literal feeding and satiation; the fasting person's abstention from these becomes the very means of spiritual nourishment.
- Root: الي (a-l-y)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core linguistic root meaning — to convey a message; the angel (malak) is so named because the message is "chewed" (yu'lak) in the mouth, as a horse chews its bit.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological/Kalam semantic nuance — "المألكة: الرسالة" — the angelic function is the conveyance of divine communication; the fasting person's hunger narrows the channels through which the devil (who runs like blood through the veins) reaches the heart.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal vs Metaphorical distinction — literal conveyance of a message versus the metaphorical "message" of the devil's insinuation (waswās) through the pathways of the body.
- Root: صبر (ṣ-b-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core linguistic root meaning — to restrain, to hold back in constriction; "صبرت الدابة: حبستها بلا علف" — to hold an animal back without fodder.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological/Kalam semantic nuance — "الصبر: الإمساك في ضيق" — patience is restraint within constriction; it is the holding of the soul upon what reason and law require, or from what they require it to abstain. Its names vary by context: in battle it is courage, in calamity it is patience proper.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal vs Metaphorical distinction — Haqiqah: "صبرت على ما أكره وصبرت عما أحب" — patience upon the disliked and patience from the beloved; Majaz: "صبرت يمينه" — to bind one's oath severely, and "هو أصبر على الضرب من الأرض" — more enduring of striking than the earth.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — The particle innamā restricts and confines the predicate exclusively to its subject, as in the divine saying {«إنما يوفى الصابرون أجرهم بغير حساب»} and {«إنما يذر شهوته وطعامه وشرابه لأجلي»}, where the restriction elevates the restricted matter to a rank beyond all quantitative measure.
13:11.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

13:11.arabic: حسن التوفيق والتأييد والتسديد وإن الله لا يغير ما بقوم حتى يغيروا ما بأنفسهم فمن العبد المجاهدة ومن الله الهداية ومن العبد قرع الباب ومن الله فتح الباب والله لا يضيع أجر المحسنين وإن تك حسنة يضاعفها ويؤت من لدنه أجرا عظيما المقام الثاني في دفع العارض منه في أثناء العبادة وذلك لا بد من تعلمه أيضا فإن من جاهد نفسه وقلع مغارس الرياء من قلبه بالقناعة وقطع الطمع وإسقاط نفسه من أعين المخلوقين واستحقار مدح المخلوقين وذمهم فالشيطان لا يتركه في أثناء العبادات بل يعارضه بخطرات الرياء ولا تنقطع عنه نزعاته وهوى النفس وميلها لا ينمحي بالكلية
13:11.english: So when the harm and injury of these causes is firmly settled in his heart, his desire [for them] slackens, and his heart turns toward God. For the intelligent person does not covet that whose harm is abundant and whose benefit is scant. It suffices him that if people knew what is in his inner self—the intent of ostentation (riyā') and the display of sincerity—they would abhor him. And God will surely expose his secret until He makes him odious to the people and makes them know that he is a show-off, abhorrent to God. Had he been sincere to God, God would have unveiled his sincerity to them, made him beloved to them, subjected them to him, and loosened their tongues in praise and commendation of him—even though there is no perfection in their praise, nor deficiency in their blame. As the poet of Banī Tamīm said: "My praise is an adornment, and my blame is a disgrace." The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said to him: "You have lied—that belongs to God, there is no deity but Him." // [Hadith: A poet of Banī Tamīm said, "My praise is an adornment, and my blame is a disgrace." He (the Prophet) said: "You have lied—that belongs to God." Ahmad narrated it from the hadith of al-Aqra' ibn Ḥābis—who was the speaker of that verse, excluding the phrase "You have lied"—and its narrators are trustworthy, except that I do not know of Abū Salamah ibn 'Abd al-Raḥmān having heard [directly] from al-Aqra'. Al-Tirmidhī narrated it from the hadith of al-Barā' and deemed it sound (ḥasan), with the wording: "A man said, 'Indeed, my praise...'"]
13:11.section_title_en: The Revival of the Religious Sciences — Section 827: The Second Station: Repelling the Accidental Promptings of Ostentation During Worship
13:11.anchors:
- Root: كذب (kadhaba)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: falsehood, lying, saying what is contrary to reality; also used for "to declare someone a liar."
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In theological context, kadhb is the antithesis of sidq (truthfulness); it is a moral and epistemic vice, often linked to hypocrisy (nifāq) and false claims.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (haqīqah): to report what did not occur. Metaphorical (majāz): attributing to God what is unworthy of Him, as in the Prophet's rebuke of the poet's self-praise.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Predicate Emphasis (Bāb al-Tawkīd) — The Prophet's reply "كَذَبْتَ" (You have lied) functions as an emphatic categorical refutation, structured as a nominal sentence with implied subject, establishing a permanent verdict rather than a transient rebuke.
13:11.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Condemnation of Status and Ostentation'

13:11.arabic: سفره ووقفة في حركته فإن الله لا يغير ما بقوم حتى يغيروا ما بأنفسهم وإذا زاغوا أزاغ الله قلوبهم وما الله بظلام للعبيد ولكنهم يظلمون أنفسهم ومن لم يؤهل للجولان في هذا الميدان والتطواف في متنزهات هذا البستان ربما سافر بظاهر بدنه في مدة مديدة فراسخ معدودة مغتنما بها تجارة للدنيا أو ذخيرة للآخرة فإن كان مطلبه العلم والدين أو الكفاية للاستعانة على الدين كان من سالكي سبيل الآخرة وكان له في سفره شروط وآداب إن أهملها كان من عمال الدنيا وأتباع الشيطان وإن واظب عليها لم يخل سفره عن فوائد تلحقه بعمال الآخرة ونحن نذكر آدابه وشروطه في بابين
13:11.english: And to this journey God — exalted be He — has summoned [us] by His saying: {«سَنُرِيهِمْ آيَاتِنَا فِي الْآفَاقِ وَفِي أَنْفُسِهِمْ»} [We shall show them Our signs in the horizons and in their own selves — Fussilat 41:53], and by His saying — exalted be He: {«وَفِي الْأَرْضِ آيَاتٌ لِلْمُوقِنِينَ * وَفِي أَنْفُسِكُمْ أَفَلَا تُبْصِرُونَ»} [And in the earth are signs for those who are certain; and in your own selves — do you not then see? — Dhāriyāt 51:20-21]. And upon sitting back from this journey, censure fell by His saying — exalted be He: {«وَإِنَّكُمْ لَتَمُرُّونَ عَلَيْهِمْ مُصْبِحِينَ * وَبِاللَّيْلِ أَفَلَا تَعْقِلُونَ»} [And indeed you pass by them in the morning, and by night — do you not then comprehend? — Ṣāffāt 37:137-138], and by His saying — exalted be He: {«وَكَأَيِّنْ مِنْ آيَةٍ فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ يَمُرُّونَ عَلَيْهَا وَهُمْ عَنْهَا مُعْرِضُونَ»} [And how many a sign in the heavens and the earth do they pass by, while they are from it turning away — Yūsuf 12:105]. So whoever is facilitated this journey, he never ceases in his traveling to take pleasure in a Garden whose breadth is the heavens and the earth — while he is still with his body at rest, settled in his homeland.
13:11.section_title_en: The Book of the Etiquettes of Travel — Being the Seventh Book of the Quarter of Customs from The Revival of the Religious Sciences
13:11.anchors:
- Root: سفر (s-f-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning is "unveiling/disclosure" (kashf al-ghitā'); also denotes journeying across land, and a group of travelers (safar/qawm musāfirūn).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-safar: "the removal of a covering," specialized to physical unveiling (e.g., removing a turban from the head). Its theological extension: the journey as a means of unveiling hidden realities — both outward horizons (āfāq) and inward selves (anfus).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (haqīqah): physical travel with the body, provisions for a journey (sufrah). Metaphorical (majāz): "a face radiant with joy" (wajh musfir); "the morning brightening" (asfara al-ṣubḥ) — the inner journey as illumination of the heart's countenance.
- Root: وفي (w-f-y)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Fullness, completion, fulfillment of a measure or covenant.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-wāfī: "that which has reached completion/perfection." Awfā bi-ʿahdihi: to fulfill one's covenant completely without breach. Theologically: the complete fulfillment of the servant's journey — arriving at the full measure of human perfection.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: a full-weight dirham, complete measure. Metaphorical: "to reach completion of years" (māta wa-ant bi-wafā'); "to come upon/arrive at" (awfā ʿalā) — the journey's end as arrival at full term.
- Root: نفس (n-f-s)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The self, soul, spirit; that which is precious and valued.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-nafs: the spirit (rūḥ); in God's speech "He knows what is in your selves" — the inner dimension of the human being, the seat of the divine secret.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: a precious thing (shay' nafīs). Metaphorical: "the soul's blood" (nafsuhu = damuhu); the inner landscape (āfāq al-anfus) as the terrain of the inward journey.
- Sibawayh Rule: Prepositional Interposition (al-faṣl bayna al-jār wa-al-majrūr) — governing the periodic suspension of meaning across clauses, as in the verse {سَنُرِيهِمْ آيَاتِنَا فِي الْآفَاقِ وَفِي أَنْفُسِهِمْ}, where the dual prepositional phrases (fī al-āfāq / fī anfusihim) are syntactically parallel yet semantically interposed, requiring the translator to preserve the balanced suspension of the two terrains of divine signs.
13:11.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Etiquette of Travel'

13:11.arabic: وإلى حالك ويغبطونك فى حسنك وجمالك والملائكة يمشون بين يديك ومن خلفك وينادون على رءوس الأشهاد هذا فلان بن فلان رضى الله عنه وأرضاه وقد سعد سعادة لا يشقى بعدها أبدا أفترى أن هذا المنصب ليس بأعظم من المكانة التى تنالها فى قلوب الخلق فى الدنيا بريائك ومداهنتك وتصنعك وتزينك فإن كنت تعلم أنه خير منه بل لانسبة له إليه فتوسل إلى إدراك هذه الرتبة بالإخلاص الصافى والنية الصادقة فى معاملتك مع الله فلن تدرك ذلك إلا به وإن تكن الأخرى والعياذ بالله بأن خرج من صحيفتك جريمة كنت تحسبها هينة وهى عند الله عظيمة فمقتك لأجلها فقا
13:11.english: Know that none is saved from the peril of the Scale except him who, in this world, called his own soul to account, and weighed therein — by the scale of the Sacred Law — his deeds, his words, his passing thoughts, and his glances, just as ʿUmar — may God be well pleased with him — said: "Call yourselves to account before you are called to account, and weigh yourselves before you are weighed." Indeed, his calling himself to account consists in his repenting, before death, from every act of disobedience with a sincere repentance (tawbah naṣūḥ), and in his making up for what was neglected of his shortcomings regarding the obligatory commands of God — may He be exalted — and in his restoring rights to those he wronged, grain by grain, and in his seeking absolution from everyone whom he harmed by his tongue, his hand, or his evil suspicion harbored in his heart — and this by winning their hearts' contentment — until he dies with no outstanding wrong against him, nor any neglected obligation.
13:11.section_title_en: The Perils of the Scale and the Reckoning of Wrongs Against Others
13:11.anchors:
- Root: وزن (w-z-n)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning is weighing, measuring, and balancing; al-mīzān (the Scale) is the instrument of equitable judgment.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In theological context, al-mīzān is the divine instrument of justice on the Day of Resurrection, weighing deeds to manifest equitable recompense, not a corporeal balance.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) usage denotes physical weighing; metaphorical (majāz) usage extends to moral and spiritual accounting, as in "weighing one's deeds by the scale of the Sacred Law."
- Sibawayh Rule: Conditional and Exceptive Constructions (الشّرط والاستثناء) — governing the protasis-apodosis structure in "whoever's scales are heavy... whoever's scales are light," and the exceptive force in "none is saved... except he who reckons."
13:11.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Remembrance of Death and Afterlife'

13:11.arabic: الكعبة فقلت ومن هم قال الأكثرون أموالا إلا من قال هكذا وهكذا من بين يديه ومن خلفه وعن يمينه وعن شماله وقليل ما هم ما من صاحب إبل ولا بقر ولا غنم لا يؤدي زكاتها إلا جاءت يوم القيامة أعظم ما كانت وأسمنه تنطحه بقرونها وتطؤه بأظلافها كلما نفدت أخراها عادت عليه أولاها حتى يقضى بين الناس (1) وإذا كان هذا التشديد مخرجا في الصحيحين فقد صار من مهمات الدين الكشف عن أسرار الزكاة وشروطها الجلية والخفية ومعانيها الظاهرة والباطنة مع الاقتصار على ما لا يستغنى عن معرفته مؤدي الزكاة وقابضها وينكشف ذلك في أربعة فصول الفصل الأول في أنواع الزكاة وأسباب
13:11.english: To proceed: God Most High made alms (al-zakāh) one of the pillars of Islam, and joined its mention with prayer (al-ṣalāh), which is the loftiest of symbols. He said Most High: {«وَأَقِيمُوا الصَّلَاةَ وَآتُوا الزَّكَاةَ»} — "And establish prayer and give alms." And he, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Islam is built upon five: the testimony that there is no god but God and that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger, the establishment of prayer, and the giving of alms." And He intensified the threat against those who fall short in it, saying: {«وَالَّذِينَ يَكْنِزُونَ الذَّهَبَ وَالْفِضَّةَ وَلَا يُنفِقُونَهَا فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ فَبَشِّرْهُم بِعَذَابٍ أَلِيمٍ»} — "And those who hoard gold and silver and do not spend them in the way of God — give them tidings of a painful chastisement." And the meaning of "spending in the way of God" is the payment of the due right of alms (zakāh).
13:11.section_title_en: The Book of the Secrets of Alms (Zakat) — Section 167
13:11.anchors:
- Root: زكا (Z-K-Y)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "Zakā al-zar'u yazkū zakā'an: it increased and grew." Core meaning: growth, increase, purification.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "The origin of zakāh is the growth that occurs through the blessing of God Most High... and from it is zakāh: what a person pays of God's right to the poor, so named for the hope of blessing in it, or for the purification (tazkiyah) of the soul, i.e., its growth."
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (haqīqah): growth and increase. Metaphorical (majāz): the purification of wealth through payment of the obligatory due.
- Root: نعم (N-'-M)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "Na'ima 'ayshuhu: his life was pleasant." Core meaning: bounty, well-being, grace.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Al-Ni'mah: the good state... and al-Ni'mah (with kasrah) is used for the genus, said of both little and much."
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "Jallat ni'mat Allāh wa na'mā'uh" — God's grace and bounty are immense. Metaphorical: "Khāfat na'āmatuhum" — their ostriches departed (i.e., they fled), showing the root's extended usage.
- Root: ظهر (Z-H-R)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "Zahara: to become apparent, to be victorious." Core meaning: back, outward appearance, manifestation.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Al-Zahr: the back (body part)... and it is used metaphorically for the surface of the earth."
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "Rajul muzhir: a man strong of back." Metaphorical: "Qalabtu al-amra zahrān li-baṭn" — I turned the matter over back and belly (examined it thoroughly).
- Root: سرر (S-R-R)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "Sarra: to conceal, to keep secret." Core meaning: secret, inner self, joy.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Al-Isrār: the opposite of al-i'lān (declaring)... and al-sirr is the speech concealed in the soul."
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "Asarra al-ḥadīth: he concealed the speech." Metaphorical: "Aṭaytuka sirrah: I gave you its choicest part (the secret/core of something)."
- Sibawayh Rule: Bāb al-faṣl bayna al-jār wa al-majrūr (Prepositional Interposition) — The permissibility of interposing elements between a preposition and its object when the intervening clause is complete in itself, as in "fa'āfa 'alayhim min ni'matihi mā..." where the prepositional phrase is completed after an intervening relative clause.
13:11.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications, prayers, and their spiritual power, from 'Mysteries of Zakat'

13:13.arabic: وإذا سمعت صوت الرعد فقل سبحان من يسبح الرعد بحمده والملائكة من خيفته (7) فإن رأيت الصواعق فقل اللهم لا تقتلنا بغضبك ولا تهلكنا بعذابك وعافنا قبل ذلك (8) قاله كعب فإذا أمطرت السماء فقل اللهم سقيا هنيئا وصيبا نافعا (9) اللهم اجعله صيب رحمة ولا تجعله صيب عذاب (10) فإذا غضبت فقل اللهم اغفر لي ذنبي وأذهب غيظ قلبي وأجرني من الشيطان الرجيم (1) فإذا خفت قوما فقل اللهم إنا نجعلك في نحورهم ونعوذ بك من شرورهم (2) فإذا غزوت فقل اللهم أنت عضدي ونصيري وبك أقاتل (3) وإذا طنت أذنك فصل على محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم
13:13.english: When you rise in the morning and hear the call to prayer (adhān), it is recommended for you to respond to the caller of prayer (mu'adhdhin) — and we have already mentioned this, along with the supplications for entering and leaving the privy, and the supplications of ablution (wuḍū'), in the Book of Purification. When you set out toward the mosque, say: "O Allah, place light (nūr) in my heart, and light in my tongue, and place light in my hearing, and place light in my sight, and place light behind me, and light before me, and place light above me. O Allah, grant me light." And also say: "O Allah, I ask You by the right of those who ask of You, and by the right of this my walking unto You — for I have not gone out in insolence, nor in vanity, nor for show, nor for reputation. I have gone out seeking protection from Your wrath and seeking Your good pleasure. So I ask You to deliver me from the Fire and to forgive me my sins — verily, none forgives sins but You."
13:13.section_title_en: Section 254 — Supplications for the Hours of Day and Night: From Dawn to Sleep
13:13.anchors:
- Root: ن و ر (n-w-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: النور: الضوء المنتشر الذي يُبصر به، وهو ضد الظلمة
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): النور في القرآن يقع على ضروب: منها المعقول كالإيمان والحكمة، قال تعالى: {قد جاءكم من الله نور وكتاب مبين}، ومنها المحسوس كضوء الشمس والقمر
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): النور حقيقة في الضوء المحسوس، ومجاز في الهدى والإيمان والعلم — فدعاء النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بطلب النور يشمل المعنيين جميعاً
- Root: س ج د (s-j-d)
  * Lisan / Ayn: السجود: وضع الجبهة على الأرض تعظيماً، وأصله التطامن والانخفاض
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): السجود ضربان: سجود عبادة وهو وضع الجبهة على الأرض تقرباً، وسجود طاعة وهو الانقياد والخضوع — قال تعالى: {ولله يسجد من في السموات والأرض طوعاً وكرهاً}
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): سجد حقيقة في وضع الجبهة، ومجاز في الخضوع والانقياد — وقوله "سجد لك سوادي وخيالي" من المجاز المرسل
- Root: ذ ك ر (dh-k-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: الذكر: نقيض النسيان، والذكر: الصوت الذي يُذكر به الشيء، والذكر: الشرف والصيت
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): الذكر ضربان: ذكر بالقلب وهو التفكر في عظمة الله، وذكر باللسان وهو التلفظ بأسمائه — وأعلى مراتبه ما اجتمع فيه القلب واللسان
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): الذكر حقيقة في استحضار الشيء بالقلب أو اللسان، ومجاز في الصلاة والدعاء والثناء
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — جواز تقديم المعمول وتأخيره مع بقاء العامل عاملاً في المعنى، كقوله "لك الحمد" حيث تقدم الجار والمجرور على المبتدأ للاختصاص والاهتمام
13:13.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications, prayers, and their spiritual power, from 'On Invocations and Supplications'

14:27.arabic: وثبتني بالقول الثابت في الحياة الدنيا وفي الآخرة ولا تضلني وإن كنت ظالما سبحانك سبحانك يا علي يا عظيم يا بارىء يا رحيم يا عزيز يا جبار سبحان من سبحت له السموات بأكنافها وسبحان من سبحت له البحار بأمواجها وسبحان من سبحت له الجبال بأصدائها وسبحان من سبحت له الحيتان بلغاتها وسبحان من سبحت له النجوم في السماء بأبراجها وسبحان من سبحت له الأشجار بأصولها وثمارها وسبحان من سبحت له السموات السبع والأرضون السبع ومن فيهن ومن عليهن سبحان من سبح له كل شيء من مخلوقاته تباركت وتعاليت سبحانك سبحانك يا حي
14:27.english: It is narrated that Yūnus ibn ʿUbayd saw a man in a dream — a man who had been killed as a martyr in the lands of the Byzantines — and he said to him: "What is the most excellent deed that you witnessed?" He replied: "I witnessed the glorifications (tasbīḥāt) of Ibn al-Muʿtamir holding a station with Allah, Mighty and Majestic." And they are these: "Glory be to Allah (subḥāna Allāh), and praise be to Allah (al-ḥamdu li-Allāh), and there is no god but Allah (lā ilāha illā Allāh), and Allah is the Greatest (Allāhu akbar), and there is no might and no power except through Allah, the Most High, the Magnificent — to the number of what He has created, and the number of what He is creating, and the weight of what He has created, and the weight of what He is creating, and the fill of what He has created, and the fill of what He is creating, and the fill of His heavens and the fill of His earth, and the like of that, and multiples of that, and the number of His creation, and the weight of His Throne, and the utmost extent of His mercy, and the ink of His words, and the limit of His good pleasure, until He is pleased, and when He is pleased, [then] the number of what His creation has remembered Him with in all that has passed, and the number of what they will remember Him with in what remains, in every year, and month, and Friday, and day, and night, and hour of the hours, and breath of the breaths, and age of the ages, from eternity to eternity — the eternity of this world and the eternity of the Hereafter — and more than that, whose beginning does not cease and whose end does not come to an end."
14:27.section_title_en: The Supplications of Ibn al-Muʿtamir (Sulaymān al-Taymī) and His Glorifications, and the Supplication of Ibrāhīm ibn Adham — May Allah Be Well Pleased with Them
14:27.anchors:
- Root: سبح (s-b-ḥ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of swift motion (in water or air); extended to the act of prayer and glorification.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "التسبيح: تنزيه الله تعالى. وأصله: المر السريع في عبادة الله تعالى" — Glorification is the declaration of Allah's transcendence; its root is the swift passage in worship of Allah.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "سبحت الله وسبحت له" — to declare Him transcendent. Metaphorical: "والنجوم تسبح في الفلك" — the stars glide in their orbits, a metaphor for their obedient motion.
- Root: حمد (ḥ-m-d)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of praise and commendation for a beneficial act.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Praise (ḥamd) is the acknowledgment of beneficence with reverence; it is due to Allah alone in His absolute perfection.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "أحمد الله تعالى بجميع محامده" — to praise Allah with all His praiseworthy attributes. Metaphorical: "أحمدت الأرض: رضيت سكناها" — to find a thing agreeable, extending praise to non-verbal contexts.
- Root: لهم (l-h-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of swift swallowing or devouring.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الإلهام: إلقاء الشيء في الروع" — Inspiration is the casting of a thing into the heart/mind (al-rawʿ), specifically from Allah or the higher assembly.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "ألهمه الله الخير: ألقاه في روعه" — Allah inspired him with good. Metaphorical: "جواد يلتهم الأرض" — a swift horse devours the ground, extending to rapid comprehension.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The permissibility of interposing elements between a preposition and its object when the clause remains grammatically sound, as seen in the extended supplicatory sentences.
14:27.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications, prayers, and their spiritual power, from 'On Invocations and Supplications'

14:27.arabic: فعزمت على تركه فنوديت من جانب البيت يثبت الله الذين آمنوا بالقول الثابت في الحياة الدنيا وفي الآخرة وقال الشعبي ما أدري أيهما أبعد غور في النار الكذاب أو البخيل وقال ابن السماك ما أراني أوجر على ترك الكذب لأني إنما أدعه أنفه وقيل الخالدين صبيح أيسمى الرجل كاذبا بكذبة واحدة قال نعم وقال مالك بن دينار قرأت في بعض الكتب ما من خطيب إلا وتعرض خطبته على عمله فإن كان صادقا صدق وإن كان كاذبا قرضت شفتاه بمقاريض من نار كلما قرضتا نبتتا وقال مالك بن دينار الصدق والكذب يعتركان في القلب حتى يخرج أحدهما صاحبه وك
14:27.english: Among them is the hadith: "And three whom God hates: the trader or seller who swears much." Ahmad narrated it, and the wording is his. In its chain is Ibn al-Aḥmaṣ, whose condition is unknown. Both Ahmad and al-Nasā'ī narrated it with another wording through a sound chain. And al-Nasā'ī has, from the hadith of Abū Hurayrah: "Four whom God abhors: the seller who swears much" — the hadith — and its chain is sound.
14:27.section_title_en: The Book of the Revival of the Religious Sciences — Section 676: On Lying (al-Kadhib) — Hadith Reports and Traditions (Āthār)
14:27.anchors:
- Root: كذب (Kadhaba)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to report a falsehood, to utter what is contrary to reality; al-Kadhdhābah: a variegated cloth that deceives the eye into thinking it is part of the ceiling — indicating the deceptive semblance of truth.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Kadhib applies to both speech and action. God says: {«Only they forge falsehood who do not believe in God's signs»} (Q 16:105) — the hypocrites' speech was true, but their inward conviction was false, so God called them liars (kādhibūn) regarding their belief.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqīqah): "He is kadhib, kadhūb, kadhāb, kaydhabān" — one who lies habitually. Metaphorical (Majāz): "He carried [the burden] then lied" — i.e., he cowardly retreated, making his charge a false one; "the she-camel lied" — her pregnancy proved false.
- Root: حدث (Ḥadatha)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to originate, to bring into being after non-existence; al-ḥadīth: speech that is new/recently originated.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Al-Ḥudūth: a thing's coming to be after it was not — whether accident or substance. Its creation (iḥdāth) belongs solely to God. Al-muḥdath: what is brought into existence after non-existence." God says: {«There comes not to them a fresh reminder (dhikr muḥdath) from their Lord»} (Q 21:2).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "He spoke a ḥadīth; fresh in age." Metaphorical: "They became aḥādīth (topics of talk)"; ʿUmar was called muḥaddath — one whose intuition is divinely inspired, as if truth were spoken into him.
- Root: ويل (Wayl)
  * Lisan / Ayn: An expression of intense woe, destruction, and chastisement; a word of threat and condemnation.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Wayl denotes severe affliction and ruin; it is a declaration of impending punishment.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "Woe to him" — a cry of ruin. Used in threats: "Waylun lahu" — destruction is his due.
- Root: شنأ (Shana'a)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Intense hatred and abhorrence.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-Shan'ān: intense hatred that drives one to shun the object.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "He hated him with shan'an" — vehement hatred.
- Sibawayh Rule: Bāb al-Ḥaṣr wa al-Taqyīd bi-innamā (Restriction and Focused Predication) — The particle innamā restricts the predicate to the subject alone, negating it for all else. Applied in the verse: {«Only they forge falsehood who do not believe»} — restricting fabrication to the disbelievers, affirming that the believer does not lie.
14:27.topic: Al-Ghazali on purifying the character, moral diseases, and spiritual remedies, from 'Remembrance of Death and Afterlife'

15:36.arabic: أحدكم من الدعاء ما يعلم من نفسه فإن الله عز وجل أجاب دعاء شر الخلق إبليس لعنه الله إذ قال رب فانظرني إلى يوم يبعثون قال إنك من المنظرين الثامن أن يلح في الدعاء ويكرره ثلاثا قال ابن مسعود كان صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا دعا دعا ثلاثا وإذا سال سأل ثلاثا (1) وينبغي أن لا يستبطىء الإجابة لقوله صلى الله عليه وسلم يستجاب لأحدكم ما لم يعجل فيقول قد دعوت فلم يستجب لي فإذا دعوت فاسأل الله كثيرا فإنك تدعو كريما (2) وقال بعضهم إني أسأل الله عز وجل منذ عشرين سنة حاجة وما أجابني وأنا أرجو الإجابة سألت الله تعالى أن يوفقني لترك ما لا يعنيني وقال
15:36.english:
[Root: دعو]
  • Lisan al-Arab: "الدعاء: الرغبة إلى الله تعالى، والابتهال في المسألة. والدعوة: الكلمة التي يدعو بها. وأصل الدعاء: طلب الإقبال من الغير."
  • Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الدعاء: ضربان: أحدهما دعاء العبادة، والآخر دعاء المسألة. فدعاء العبادة: هو توجه العبد إلى الله تعالى بالطاعة. ودعاء المسألة: طلب الحاجة من الله تعالى. قال تعالى: {وقال ربكم ادعوني أستجب لكم}."
  • Al-Zamakhshari (Asas - Haqiqah/Literal): "دعا فلان ربه: ابتهل إليه بالسؤال. ودعا الله: عبده. ومنه قوله تعالى: {إن الذين يستكبرون عن عبادتي} أي عن دعائي."
  • Al-Zamakhshari (Asas - Majaz/Metaphorical): "دعا عليه: سأل الله أن يصيبه بمكروه. ودعا له: سأل الله أن يحسن إليه. ومن المجاز: دعا الأمر إلى كذا، أي أدى إليه."
15:36.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'On Invocations and Supplications'

16:2.arabic: الروح من أمره على من يشاء من عباده} وأحال الإغواء على إبليس فقال تعالى {ليضل عن سبيله} والإغواء هو استيقاف العباد دون بلوغ غاية الحكمة فانظر كيف نسبه إلى العبد الذي غضب عليه والإرشاد سياقه لهم إلى الغاية فانظر كيف نسبه إلى العبد الذي أحبه وعندك في العادة له مثال فالملك إذا كان محتاجا إلى من يسقيه الشراب وإلى من يحجمه وينظف فناء منزله عن القاذورات وكان له عبدان فلا يعين للحجامة والتنظيف إلا أقبحهما وأخسهما ولا يفوض حمل الشراب والطيب إلا إلى أحسنهما وأكملهما وأحبهما إليه ولا ينبغ
16:2.english: Thus was the beginning of this matter and its end. And do not understand it unless you are worthy of it. And if you are worthy of it, the eye is opened and you see, so you have no need of a leader to lead you. The blind man can indeed be led, but only to a limit. For when the path narrows and becomes sharper than a sword and finer than a hair, the bird is able to fly over it but is not able to drag a blind man behind it. And when the field becomes narrow and subtle — subtle as water, for example — and crossing is possible only by swimming, then the one skilled in the art of swimming may be able to cross by himself, and perhaps he is not able to drag another behind him. These matters bear the same relation to walking upon the way of the common masses of creatures as walking upon water bears to walking upon earth. Swimming can be learned; but as for walking upon water, it is not acquired by instruction, but rather is attained through the strength of certainty (yaqīn). For this reason it was said to the Prophet, peace be upon him, that Jesus, peace be upon him, was said to have walked upon water, and he, peace be upon him, said: "Had his certainty increased, he would have walked upon the air." {«حديث قيل له يقال إن عيسى مشى على الماء قال لو ازداد يقينا لمشي على الهواء»} — This hadith is rejected (munkar) and is not known in this form. What is known is what Ibn Abi al-Dunya narrated in the Book of Certainty from the saying of Bakr ibn Abd Allah al-Muzani, who said: The disciples lost their Prophet, and it was said to them: "He has headed toward the sea." So they set out seeking him, and when they reached the sea, behold, he was coming toward them walking upon the water. And he mentioned a hadith in which Jesus said: "If the son of Adam had a hair's breadth of certainty, he would walk upon the water." And Abu Mansur al-Daylami narrated in the Musnad al-Firdaws with a weak chain from the hadith of Muadh ibn Jabal: "If you knew God with true knowledge, you would walk upon the seas, and the mountains would be removed by your supplications." These are symbols and allusions to the meaning of aversion (karāhah) and love (maḥabbah), and good pleasure (riḍā) and wrath (ghaḍab), and gratitude (shukr) and ingratitude (kufrān) — more than this is not fitting for the science of practical conduct (ʿilm al-muʿāmalah). And God, exalted be He, struck an example of this to draw it near to the understanding of creatures, since He knew that He created the jinn and mankind only to worship Him, and their worship was the ultimate purpose of wisdom (ghāyat al-ḥikmah) with respect to them. Then He informed that He has two servants: one whom He loves, whose name is Gabriel — the Holy Spirit and the Trustworthy One — and he is with Him beloved, obeyed, trustworthy, and honored; and another whom He hates, whose name is Iblis — the accursed one, reprieved until the Day of Judgment. Then He delegated guidance (irshād) to Gabriel, saying, the Exalted: {«قل نزله روح القدس من ربك بالحق»} "Say: The Holy Spirit has brought it down from your Lord with truth" (16:102), and said, the Exalted: {«يلقي الروح من أمره على من يشاء من عباده»} "He casts the Spirit of His command upon whom He wills of His servants" (40:15). And He delegated misguidance (ighwāʾ) to Iblis, saying, the Exalted: {«ليضل عن سبيله»} "That he may lead astray from His path" (4:119). And ighwāʾ is the halting of servants short of attaining the ultimate purpose of wisdom. So observe how He attributed it to the servant with whom He was wrathful; and guidance (irshād) is the conduct of them toward the ultimate purpose — so observe how He attributed it to the servant whom He loves. And you have an example of this in custom: when a king is in need of one to give him drink and one to cup him and to clean the courtyard of his house of filth, and he has two servants, he does not appoint for cupping and cleaning except the ugliest and meanest of them, and he does not entrust the carrying of drink and perfume except to the best and most complete of them and the most beloved to him. And you should not say: "This is my act, and his act was not without my act" — for you have erred when you attributed that to yourself. Rather, He is the One who directed your motive (dāʿiyah) to the specification of the disliked act to the disliked person, and the beloved act to the beloved person, as a completion of justice (ʿadl). For His justice is sometimes completed through matters in which you have no entry, and sometimes it is completed in you — for you also are among His acts. So your motive, your power, your knowledge, your action, and all the other causes of your movements in expression — all of this is His act, which He arranged with justice in an arrangement from which moderate acts issue forth. Except that you see only yourself, and so you suppose that what appears through you in the world of witness (ʿālam al-shahādah) has no cause from the world of the unseen and the dominion (ʿālam al-ghayb wa al-malakūt). Therefore you attribute it to yourself. And you are only like the child who looks at night at the play of the juggler (mushʿabadh) who brings forth figures from behind a curtain that dance and scream and rise and sit, composed of rags that do not move by themselves — rather, they are moved by fine hair-like threads that do not appear in the darkness of night, their ends in the hand of the juggler, who is hidden from the eyes of the children. So they rejoice and marvel, supposing that those rags dance and play and rise and sit. As for the intelligent ones, they know that this is a moving (taḥrīk) and not a self-movement, but perhaps they do not know its detailed modality. And the one who knows some of its detail does not know it as the juggler knows it, to whom the command belongs and in whose hand is the pulling. Likewise, the children of the people of this world — and all creatures are children relative to the scholars — look at these persons (ashkhāṣ) and suppose that they are the movers, and so they attribute [action] to them. And the scholars know that they are moved, except that they do not know the modality of the moving — and they are the majority. Except the knowers (ʿārifūn), the scholars, and those firmly rooted in knowledge (al-rāsikhūn), for they have perceived, with the sharpness of their sight, fine spider-web threads — nay, much finer than these — suspended from heaven, their ends attached to the persons of the people of the earth. Those threads are not perceived, due to their fineness, by these outward eyes. Then they witnessed the heads of those threads in their suspension-points (manāṭāt) to which they are attached, and they witnessed for those suspension-points handles (maqābiḍ) that are in the hands of the angels who move the heavens. And they also witnessed the angels of the heavens directed toward the bearers of the Throne (ḥamalat al-ʿarsh), awaiting what descends upon them of the command from the presence of Lordship (ḥaḍrat al-rubūbiyyah) — "they do not disobey God in what He commands them, and they do what they are commanded" (66:6). And He expressed these witnessed realities in the Qur'an, and it was said: {«وفي السماء رزقكم وما توعدون»} "And in the heaven is your provision and what you are promised" (51:22). And He expressed the waiting of the angels of the heavens for what descends upon them of decree and command, and it was said: "He created seven heavens and of the earth the like of them; {«يتنزل الأمر بينهن لتعلموا أن الله على كل شيء قدير وأن الله قد أحاط بكل شيء علما»} 'the command descends between them, that you may know that God is powerful over all things and that God encompasses all things in knowledge'" (65:12). These are matters whose interpretation (taʾwīl) none knows except God and those firmly rooted in knowledge (al-rāsikhūn fī al-ʿilm). And Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, expressed the exclusivity of those firmly rooted in knowledge to sciences that the understandings of creatures cannot bear, when he recited the saying of the Exalted: {«يتنزل الأمر بينهن»} "The command descends between them," and said: "Were I to mention what I know of the meaning of this verse, you would stone me" — and in another wording: "You would say he is an unbeliever."
16:2.section_title_en: On the Degrees of Proximity to God and the Hierarchy of Those Who Perfect Divine Wisdom
16:2.anchors:
- Root: سير (s-y-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "السير: الذهاب والسفر، وسار يسير سيرا ومسيرا، والسيارة: الرفقة المسافرة"
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "السير: الانتقال من مكان إلى مكان، ويستعار للسلوك في الدين والطريقة"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): [Literal] "سار القوم: مشوا" — [Metaphorical] "سار فيه السير: مضى في الأمر، وسار ذكره: انتشر، ومنه: سيرة فلان: طريقته"
- Root: مشي (m-sh-y)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "المشي: تردد الأركان على الأرض، والماشية: الإبل والغنم لانتقالها في المرعى"
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "المشي: الانتقال من مكان إلى مكان بإرادة، ويكنى به عن النميمة، وعن شرب المسهل"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): [Literal] "مشيت وتمشيت، وهي حسنة المشية" — [Metaphorical] "مشى بطنه، وأمشاه الدواء، واستمشيت بالدواء، ومنه: مشت المرأة: كثرت أولادها"
- Root: خلق (kh-l-q)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الخلق: التقدير، والخلق: الناس، والخليقة: الطبيعة، والخلق: السجية"
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الخلق أصله: التقدير المستقيم، ويستعمل في إبداع الشيء من غير أصل ولا احتذاء"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): [Literal] "خلق الخراز الأديم: قدره قبل القطع" — [Metaphorical] "خلق الله الخلق: أوجده على تقدير أوجبته الحكمة"
- Root: نفس (n-f-s)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "النفس: الروح، والذات، والشيء النفيس"
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "النفس: الروح، وتطلق على الذات، قال تعالى: {ويحذركم الله نفسه} فنفسه: ذاته"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): [Literal] "شيء نفيس ومنفس" — [Metaphorical] "دفق نفسه أي دمه، وأصابته نفس: عين"
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — Used to distinguish exclusive attribution of actions to God versus creatures, as in "إنما أنت مثل الصبي" (You are only like a child), restricting the simile to the creature while preserving divine agency.
16:2.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'Remembrance of Death and Afterlife'

16:2.arabic: وجل في كلام يردده في نفسه كما لو سمع وهو يقول {إنني أنا الله لا إله إلا أنا فاعبدني} فإنه ما كان ينبغي أن يفهم منه ذلك إلا على سبيل الحكاية الصنف الثاني من الشطح كلمات غير مفهومة لها ظواهر رائقة وفيها عبارات هائلة وليس وراءها طائل إما أن تكون غير مفهومة عند قائلها بل يصدرها عن خبط في عقله وتشويش في خياله لقلة إحاطته بمعنى كلام قرع سمعه وهذا هو الأكثر وإما أن تكون مفهومة له ولكنه لا يقدر على تفهيمها وإيرادها بعبارة تدل على ضميره لقلة ممارسته للعلم وعدم تعلمه طريق التعبير عن المعاني بالألفاظ الرشيقة ولا فائدة لهذا الجنس من ا
16:2.english: Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ, may God be pleased with him, said to his son ʿUmar — having heard him composing sajʿ — "This is what makes me dislike you. I will never fulfill your need until you repent." This was said when his son had come to him seeking a favor. And the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to ʿAbd Allāh ibn Rawāḥah when he spoke in sajʿ of three words: "Beware of sajʿ, O Ibn Rawāḥah." Thus, the forbidden sajʿ is the artificially contrived kind that exceeds two words. For this reason, when a man spoke concerning the blood-money for a fetus — saying, "How shall we pay blood-money for one who neither drank, nor ate, nor cried out, nor wailed? Such a one's blood is void" — the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, replied: "Sajʿ like the sajʿ of the bedouins!"
16:2.section_title_en: On the Etiquette of Preaching: The Condemnation of Artificial Sajʿ, Excessive Poetry, and the Perils of Shataḥ and Taʿwīl
16:2.anchors:
- Root: سجع (sajʿa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Rhymed prose; from the root meaning "to coo" (as a dove), indicating a measured, melodious cadence in speech.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In theological discourse, sajʿ is permissible when natural but blameworthy when artificially cultivated (takalluf), as it shifts focus from meaning to ornamentation.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) — natural rhythmic speech; Metaphorical (majāz) — the "sajʿ of the bedouins" (sajʿ al-aʿrāb) as a pejorative for empty, affected eloquence.
- Root: شعر (shiʿr)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Poetry; from the root denoting perception and fine discernment (shuʿūr), as the poet grasps subtle meanings.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Poetry is blameworthy when it stirs base appetites, but praiseworthy when it conveys wisdom (ḥikmah), as in the prophetic saying "Indeed from poetry there is wisdom."
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — metered, rhymed speech; Metaphorical — the "poetry" of the heart's inclination, where listeners project their own passions onto what they hear.
- Root: شطح (shaṭaḥa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To overflow, to gush forth; originally of a water-skin bursting, then applied to ecstatic utterances that overflow the bounds of conventional discourse.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In Sufi terminology, shataḥ refers to utterances arising from overwhelming spiritual states (ḥāl) that, when voiced to the unworthy, cause corruption.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — physical overflowing; Metaphorical — the soul's overflow in speech that exceeds the speaker's intentional control.
- Root: أول (taʿwīl)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To return something to its origin or end; interpretation that traces a word back to its intended meaning.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Taʿwīl is legitimate only when supported by textual (naqlī) or rational (ʿaqlī) evidence; arbitrary taʿwīl that severs words from their established senses destroys religious trust.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — the apparent sense (ẓāhir); Metaphorical — the inner sense (bāṭin), which is only valid when the literal sense is impossible or when transmitted authority sanctions it.
- Sibawayh Rule: Bāb al-Ḥaṣr wa al-Taqyīd bi-innamā (Restriction and Focused Predication) — The text repeatedly uses restrictive constructions (innamā, laysa...illā) to delimit permissible preaching, poetry, and interpretation, distinguishing the praiseworthy from the blameworthy with syntactic precision.
16:2.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications, prayers, and their spiritual power, from 'On Invocations and Supplications'

16:77.arabic: حق وأمر جزم استعير له لفظ القضاء وقيل إنه كلمح بالبصر أو هو أقرب لفاضت بحار المقادير بحكم ذلك القضاء الجزم بما سبق به التقدير فاستعير لترتب آحاد المقدورات بعضها على بعض لفظ القدر فكان لفظ القضاء بإزاء الآمر الواحد الكلي ولفظ القدر بإزاء التفصيل المتمادي إلى غير نهاية وقيل إن شيئا من ذلك ليس خارجا عن القضاء والقدر فخطر لبعض العباد أن القسمة لماذا اقتضت هذا التفصيل وكيف انتظم العدل مع هذا التفاوت والتفضيل وكان بعضهم لقصوره لا يطيق ملاحظة كنه هذا الأمر والاحتواء على مجامعه فألجموا عما لم يطيقوا خوض غمرته بلجام ا
16:77.english: ...in the light of the sun, but due to a weakness in the eyesight of the bats. Thus those whose eyes had been opened to behold its majesty were compelled to borrow, from the lowly depths of the world of those who converse in languages, an expression that might convey, from the first principles of its realities, something exceedingly feeble. So they borrowed for it the name "power" (qudrah), and we, by reason of their borrowing, grew bold in speech, and said: "To God most high there is an attribute which is power, and from it issue creation and invention." Then creation, in its existence, divides into kinds, and into specific attributes; and the source of the division of these kinds and their being distinguished by their specific attributes is another attribute, for which was borrowed, in like manner to the necessity that preceded, the expression "will" (mashī'ah). For it suggests of it something obscure to those who converse in languages—which are but letters and sounds by which people understand one another—and the inadequacy of the word "will" to indicate the inner reality (kunnah) of that attribute and its true nature is like the inadequacy of the word "power." Then the acts issuing from power divided into what sweeps on to the terminus which is the goal of its wisdom, and into what halts short of the goal. And each of these had a relation to the attribute of will, by virtue of their reversion to the specifications (ikhtiṣāṣāt) through which the division and the differences are completed. So for the relation of that which attains its goal, the expression "love" (maḥabbah) was borrowed; and for the relation of that which halts short of its goal, the expression "aversion" (karāhah) was borrowed. And it was said that both of these are included within the description of will, but each has another particular property in its relation, which the words "love" and "aversion" suggest of them as something summarized for those who seek understanding from words and languages. Then His servants—who are also of His creation and invention—divided into: one for whom the eternal will (al-mashī'ah al-azaliyyah) had previously decreed that He would use him to halt His wisdom short of its goal, this being compulsion (qahr) in their regard, by the subjugation of motives and incitements upon them; and one for whom it had previously been decreed in eternity that He would use him to drive His wisdom to its goal in certain matters. So each of the two groups had a particular relation to the will; and for the relation of those used in completing wisdom through them, the expression "good pleasure" (riḍā) was borrowed; and for those by whom the causes of wisdom were halted short of its goal, the expression "wrath" (ghaḍab) was borrowed. Thus there appeared, upon him against whom wrath was decreed in eternity, an act by which wisdom was halted short of its goal; for this, the expression "ingratitude" (kufrān) was borrowed, and it was followed by the infliction of curse and blame as an increase in chastisement. And there appeared, upon him whom He approved in eternity, an act by which wisdom swept on to its goal; for this, the expression "thanksgiving" (shukr) was borrowed, and it was followed by the robe of praise and eulogy, as an increase in good pleasure, acceptance, and approach. So the outcome was that He most high gave beauty, then praised; and gave chastisement, then made ugly and destroyed. And His likeness is that a king should cleanse his servant of his filth, then clothe him in the finest of his garments; and when he has perfected his adornment, he says: "O beautiful one, how beautiful you are, and how beautiful your garments, and how clean your face!"—so that in reality, he is the one who beautifies, and he is the one who praises beauty; thus he is the praised one in every case. And it is as though, in meaning, he praised none but himself; the servant is merely the target of praise in respect of the outward appearance and form. Even so were the matters in eternity, and even so do causes and effects string themselves in sequence, by the decreeing of the Lord of lords and the Causer of causes. And that was not by chance or deliberation, but by will, and wisdom, and a true judgment, and a decisive command, for which the word "decree" (qaḍā') was borrowed. And it was said: it is like the glance of the eye, or nearer still. Then the seas of measured destinies (maqādīr) overflowed by the ruling of that decisive decree, with what predetermination (taqdīr) had previously passed. So for the ordering of the individual determined things (al-maqdūrāt), one upon another, the word "measure" (qadar) was borrowed. Thus the word "decree" (qaḍā') stood in correspondence to the one, unitary command, and the word "measure" (qadar) stood in correspondence to the detailed differentiation extending without end. And it was said that nothing of all this lies outside decree and measure. Then it occurred to some servants to ask: "Why did the division necessitate this differentiation, and how did justice cohere with this disparity and preference?" And some of them, due to their deficiency, could not bear to observe the inner reality of this matter or to encompass its totality; so they were bridled, from what they could not bear to plunge into its deep, with the bridle of prevention, and it was said to them: "Be still—for this you were not created. He is not questioned about what He does, but they shall be questioned" {«لا يسئل عما يفعل وهم يسئلون»}. And the niche (mishkāh) of others was filled with light borrowed from the light of God most high in the heavens and the earth; and their oil was at first pure, well-nigh luminous, even had no fire touched it; then fire touched it, and it blazed, light upon light, and the regions of the dominion (malakūt) shone before them with the light of their Lord. So they perceived all things as they truly are, and it was said to them: "Be disciplined with the disciplines of God most high, and be still." And when...
16:77.section_title_en: The Borrowed Language of Divine Attributes: On the Inadequacy of Human Terms for the Realities of Qaḍā', Qadar, and the Eternal Decree
16:77.anchors:
- Root: قدر (q-d-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root denotes measuring, determining, and ordaining a thing's extent and limit; al-Farahidi records its sense of precise appraisal and decreeing.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "القدرة" when ascribed to God negates incapacity ('ajz) absolutely; it is not a modality of acquisition as in creatures, but the sheer source whence creation issues—here Ghazali uses it as a borrowed term (isti'ārah) for an ineffable divine reality.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (haqīqah) sense is "ذو قدرة" (possessor of power); metaphorical (majāz) extension appears in "فرس بعيد القدر" (a horse of far-reaching stride)—so too here, "القدر" is extended to the serial ordering of ordained particulars, not a spatial or physical measure.
- Root: قسم (q-s-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Division and apportioning of shares; al-Farahidi ties it to partitioning lots.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "القسم: إفراز النصيب" — the separation of portions; Ghazali exploits this to show how creation's division into kinds and specific attributes demands a further attribute (the will) that specifies each portion.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: dividing wealth among parties; metaphorical: "قلبه متقسم" (his heart is divided by cares)—likewise, the division of acts under the will is a conceptual, not physical, partition.
- Root: لفظ (l-f-ẓ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Utterance as a casting out from the mouth; al-Farahidi notes its source-verb sense of ejection.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "اللفظ بالكلام مستعار من: لفظ الشيء من الفم" — speech-utterance is borrowed from physical ejection; Ghazali applies this to show how terms like "power," "will," "love," and "wrath" are merely cast-out approximations, not containers of divine essence.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Not separately cited; the root's rhetorical force lies in its inadequacy—words are sounds and letters, unable to convey the "kenne" (inner reality) of the divine.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — Ghazali's repeated "إنما" constructions (e.g., "وإنما العبد هدف الثناء") restrict the predicate to a single focused truth, isolating the apparent agent from the real one, per Sibawayh's rule that "إنما" confines judgment to what follows it, negating all else.
16:77.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

16:77.arabic: الأول الذي هو كلمح البصر أو هو أقرب وترتيب تفصيل المسببات على تفاصيل الأسباب على التدريج والتقدير هو القدر والذي قدر الخير قدره بسبب والذي قدر الشر قدر لدفعه سببا فلا تناقض بين هذه الأمور عند من انفتحت بصيرته ثم في الدعاء من الفائدة ما ذكرناه في الذكر فإنه يستدعي حضور القلب مع الله وهو منتهى العبادات ولذلك قال صلى الله عليه وسلم الدعاء مخ العبادة (1) والغالب على الخلق أنه لا تنصرف قلوبهم إلى ذكر الله عز وجل إلا عند إلمام حاجة وإرهاق ملمة فإن الإنسان إذا مسه الشر فذو دعاء عر
16:77.english: "O God, whatever blessing has come to me this morning, or to any of Your creatures, it is from You alone, with no partner to You; to You is praise and to You is thanksgiving."
16:77.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'On Invocations and Supplications'

16:123.arabic: محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم وملة أبينا إبراهيم حنيفا وما كان من المشركين (9) اللهم بك أصبحنا وبك أمسينا وبك نحيا وبك نموت وإليك المصير (10) اللهم إني أسألك أن تبعثنا في هذا اليوم إلى كل خير ونعوذ بك أن نجترح فيه سوءا أو نجره إلى مسلم فإنك قلت {وهو الذي يتوفاكم بالليل ويعلم ما جرحتم بالنهار ثم يبعثكم فيه ليقضى أجل مسمى} (11) اللهم فالق الإصباح وجاعل الليل سكنا والشمس والقمر حسبانا أسألك خير هذا اليوم وخير ما فيه وأعوذ بك من شره وشر ما فيه (12) بسم الله ما شاء الله لا قوة إلا بالله ما شاء الله
16:123.english: When you rise in the morning and hear the call to prayer (adhān), it is recommended for you to respond to the caller of prayer (mu'adhdhin) — and we have already mentioned this, along with the supplications for entering and leaving the privy, and the supplications of ablution (wuḍū'), in the Book of Purification. When you set out toward the mosque, say: "O Allah, place light (nūr) in my heart, and light in my tongue, and place light in my hearing, and place light in my sight, and place light behind me, and light before me, and place light above me. O Allah, grant me light." And also say: "O Allah, I ask You by the right of those who ask of You, and by the right of this my walking unto You — for I have not gone out in insolence, nor in vanity, nor for show, nor for reputation. I have gone out seeking protection from Your wrath and seeking Your good pleasure. So I ask You to deliver me from the Fire and to forgive me my sins — verily, none forgives sins but You."
16:123.section_title_en: Section 254 — Supplications for the Hours of Day and Night: From Dawn to Sleep
16:123.anchors:
- Root: ن و ر (n-w-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: النور: الضوء المنتشر الذي يُبصر به، وهو ضد الظلمة
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): النور في القرآن يقع على ضروب: منها المعقول كالإيمان والحكمة، قال تعالى: {قد جاءكم من الله نور وكتاب مبين}، ومنها المحسوس كضوء الشمس والقمر
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): النور حقيقة في الضوء المحسوس، ومجاز في الهدى والإيمان والعلم — فدعاء النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بطلب النور يشمل المعنيين جميعاً
- Root: س ج د (s-j-d)
  * Lisan / Ayn: السجود: وضع الجبهة على الأرض تعظيماً، وأصله التطامن والانخفاض
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): السجود ضربان: سجود عبادة وهو وضع الجبهة على الأرض تقرباً، وسجود طاعة وهو الانقياد والخضوع — قال تعالى: {ولله يسجد من في السموات والأرض طوعاً وكرهاً}
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): سجد حقيقة في وضع الجبهة، ومجاز في الخضوع والانقياد — وقوله "سجد لك سوادي وخيالي" من المجاز المرسل
- Root: ذ ك ر (dh-k-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: الذكر: نقيض النسيان، والذكر: الصوت الذي يُذكر به الشيء، والذكر: الشرف والصيت
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): الذكر ضربان: ذكر بالقلب وهو التفكر في عظمة الله، وذكر باللسان وهو التلفظ بأسمائه — وأعلى مراتبه ما اجتمع فيه القلب واللسان
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): الذكر حقيقة في استحضار الشيء بالقلب أو اللسان، ومجاز في الصلاة والدعاء والثناء
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — جواز تقديم المعمول وتأخيره مع بقاء العامل عاملاً في المعنى، كقوله "لك الحمد" حيث تقدم الجار والمجرور على المبتدأ للاختصاص والاهتمام
16:123.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications, prayers, and their spiritual power, from 'On Invocations and Supplications'

17:24.arabic: إلى آخر السورة (3) رب اغفر لي ولوالدي وارحمهما كما ربياني صغيرا واغفر للمؤمنين والمؤمنات والمسلمين والمسلمات الأحياء منهم والأموات (4) رب اغفر وارحم وتجاوز عما تعلم وأنت الأعز الأكرم وأنت خير الراحمين وأنت خير الغافرين وإنا لله وإنا إليه راجعون ولا حول ولا قوة إلا بالله العلي العظيم وحسبنا الله ونعم الوكيل وصلى الله على محمد خاتم النبيين وآله وصحبه وسلم تسليما كثيرا (5)
17:24.english: And employ me in righteous deeds which You will accept from me. (1) O God, I ask You for pardon, well-being, good certainty, and soundness in this world and the next. (2) O You Whom sins do not harm and from Whom forgiveness does not diminish anything — grant me that which will not harm You, and give me that which will not diminish You. Our Lord, pour upon us patience and cause us to die as Muslims. You are our Protector in this world and the next; cause me to die as a Muslim and join me with the righteous. You are our Protector, so forgive us and have mercy upon us, and You are the Best of forgivers. And write for us good in this world and in the Hereafter — indeed, we have turned to You in repentance. Our Lord, upon You we rely, to You we turn in repentance, and to You is the final return. Our Lord, make us not a trial for the wrongdoing people. Our Lord, make us not a trial for those who disbelieve, and forgive us, our Lord — indeed, You are the Mighty, the Wise. Our Lord, forgive us our sins and our excesses in our affairs, make firm our feet, and grant us victory over the disbelieving people. Our Lord, forgive us and our brothers who preceded us in faith, and place not in our hearts any rancor toward those who believe — our Lord, indeed You are Kind, Merciful. Our Lord, grant us from Yourself mercy and prepare for us from our affair right guidance. Our Lord, give us good in this world and good in the Hereafter, and protect us from the chastisement of the Fire. Our Lord, indeed we have heard a caller calling to faith — to His saying, Mighty and Majestic: {«إنك لا تخلف الميعاد»} [آل عمران/ 194] — Our Lord, do not take us to task if we forget or err. Our Lord, to the end of the surah. (3) My Lord, forgive me and my parents, and have mercy upon them as they raised me when I was small; and forgive the believing men and the believing women, and the Muslim men and the Muslim women, the living among them and the dead. (4) My Lord, forgive, have mercy, and overlook what You know — and You are the Most Exalted, the Most Generous, the Best of the merciful, and the Best of the forgivers. And indeed, to God we belong and to Him we return; and there is no might and no power except through God, the Exalted, the Magnificent; and God suffices us, and He is the Best Disposer of affairs. And may God send blessings upon Muhammad, the Seal of the Prophets, and upon his family and his companions, and grant them abundant peace. (5)
17:24.section_title_en: Section 252 — Supplications for Morning and Evening: Comprehensive Prayers of the Prophet (ﷺ)
17:24.anchors:
- Root: لهم (l-h-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of swallowing/ingesting (iltihām); from this derives the sense of something being cast directly into the innermost recess of the heart (al-rawʿ).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الإلهام: إلقاء الشيء في الروع" — ilhām is the casting of a thing into the innermost consciousness, specifically from God or the higher assembly (al-malaʾ al-aʿlā). It is that which the Prophet (ﷺ) called "the touch of the angel" (limat al-malak) and "the breath of the Holy Spirit in my innermost heart" (nafth rūḥ al-qudus fī rawʿī).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): "ألهمه الله الخير: ألقاه في روعه" — God inspired him with good: He cast it into his innermost consciousness. Metaphorical (majāz): A horse that "swallows the ground" (yaltaḥimu al-arḍ) in swiftness; thus ilhām is the swift, direct ingress of divine guidance into the soul without intermediary effort.
- Root: حمد (ḥ-m-d)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The root denotes praise arising from recognition of voluntary excellence and beneficence; al-ḥamd is commendation of the beloved for their attributes and acts of goodness.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Praise (ḥamd) is the acknowledgment of beneficence (niʿmah) with reverence and love; it is distinguished from mere thanks (shukr) in that it is directed to the essence and attributes of the praised one, not solely to the benefit received.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "أحمد الله تعالى بجميع محامده" — I praise God with all His praiseworthy attributes. Metaphorical: "أحمدت صنيعه" — I found his deed praiseworthy; thus the tongue's praise must be matched by the heart's recognition of the praised one's perfection.
- Root: غفر (gh-f-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The root denotes covering and shielding; al-mighfar is the helmet that protects the head in battle.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الغفر: إلباس ما يصونه عن الدنس" — Forgiveness is the clothing of that which shields from filth. God's forgiveness (maghfirah) is His shielding of the servant from the touch of chastisement, covering the sin so that it is as though it never were.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "اللهم غفرًا" — O God, forgive. Metaphorical: The she-beasts that "did not forgive" their heedlessness (lam taghfir la-hā ghaflātuhā) — i.e., they did not shield their young from destruction; thus forgiveness is active protection, not mere erasure.
- Root: نفس (n-f-s)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The self, the soul; that which breathes and has vital spirit; also used for the very essence of a thing.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "النفس: الروح" — the soul is the spirit; and in God's saying {«ويحذركم الله نفسه»} [آل عمران/ 28], "His Self" means His very essence (dhāt), which — though grammatically expressed as an annexation implying distinction — is in reality identical, with no multiplicity in the Divine Essence.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "شيء نفيس" — a precious thing. Metaphorical: "دفق نفسه" — he poured out his blood/life; thus nafs is the seat of life, passion, and moral responsibility.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الدعاء والخبر (The Chapter of Supplication and Assertion) — Supplications (duʿāʾ) are grammatically constructed as optative sentences (inshāʾ ṭalabī) using the imperative (rabbighfir), the jussive (lā tuʾākhidhnā), and the vocative (rabbanā), yet they may embed assertive clauses (khabar) of praise (al-ḥamdu lillāh) and attestation (lā ilāha illā anta). The periodic structure of these prayers alternates between direct address to God (munādāh) and self-referential confession, requiring the translator to preserve the vocative force of "O God" and "Our Lord" without flattening into mere description.
17:24.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications, prayers, and their spiritual power, from 'On Invocations and Supplications'

17:110.arabic: ادعوني أستجب لكم إن الذين يستكبرون عن عبادتي سيدخلون جهنم داخرين} وقال عز وجل {قل ادعوا الله أو ادعوا الرحمن أيا ما تدعوا فله الأسماء الحسنى} وروى النعمان بن بشير عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال إن الدعاء هو العبادة ثم قرأ ادعوني أستجب لكم (1) الآية وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم الدعاء مخ العبادة (2) وروى أبو هريرة أنه صلى الله عليه وسلم قال ليس شيء أكرم على الله عز وجل من الدعاء (3) وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم إن العبد لا يخطئه من الدعاء إحدى ثلاث إما ذنب يغفر له وإما خير يعجل له وإما خير يدخر له (4) وقال أبو ذر رضي الله عنه يكفي من الدعاء مع البر ما يكفي الطعام من الملح وق
17:110.english: Allah the Exalted has said: {«وَإِذَا سَأَلَكَ عِبَادِي عَنِّي فَإِنِّي قَرِيبٌ أُجِيبُ دَعْوَةَ الدَّاعِ إِذَا دَعَانِ فَلْيَسْتَجِيبُوا لِي»} (And when My servants ask you concerning Me — indeed I am near. I respond to the invocation of the supplicant when he calls upon Me. So let them respond to Me — Qurʾan 2:186). And He the Exalted said: {«ادْعُوا رَبَّكُمْ تَضَرُّعًا وَخُفْيَةً إِنَّهُ لَا يُحِبُّ الْمُعْتَدِينَ»} (Call upon your Lord in humility and privately; indeed, He does not like transgressors — Qurʾan 7:55). And He the Exalted said: {«وَقَالَ رَبُّكُمُ ادْعُونِي أَسْتَجِبْ لَكُمْ إِنَّ الَّذِينَ يَسْتَكْبِرُونَ عَنْ عِبَادَتِي سَيَدْخُلُونَ جَهَنَّمَ دَاخِرِينَ»} (And your Lord said: Call upon Me; I will respond to you. Indeed, those who disdain My worship will enter Hell humiliated — Qurʾan 40:60). And He, Glorified and Exalted, said: {«قُلِ ادْعُوا اللَّهَ أَوِ ادْعُوا الرَّحْمَنَ أَيًّا مَا تَدْعُوا فَلَهُ الْأَسْمَاءُ الْحُسْنَى»} (Say: Call upon Allah or call upon the Most Merciful. Whichever [name] you call — to Him belong the Most Beautiful Names — Qurʾan 17:110).
17:110.section_title_en: The Book of Invocation — Section 241: The Second Chapter on the Etiquette of Supplication (Duʿāʾ), Its Virtue, the Virtue of Certain Transmitted Supplications, the Virtue of Seeking Forgiveness (Istighfār), and Invoking Blessings upon the Messenger of Allah (Peace Be Upon Him)
17:110.anchors:
- Root: دعو (Daʿā)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الدعاء: الرغبة إلى الله تعالى، والاستعانة به. وأصل الدعو: الإقبال على الشيء بالرغبة والطلب. والدعوة: الكلمة التي يدعو بها. والمدعوّ: الذي يجيب. والداعي: الفاعل. واستدعاه: طلب منه الدعاء."
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الدعاء: الرغبة إلى الله تعالى في قضاء الحاجة، وهو ضربان: دعاء عبادة، ودعاء مسألة. فدعاء العبادة: هو التوجه إلى الله تعالى بالطاعة والإخلاص، ودعاء المسألة: هو طلب الحاجة. قال تعالى: {وقال ربكم ادعوني أستجب لكم} — فجعل الدعاء عبادة، إذ قال: {إن الذين يستكبرون عن عبادتي} فعطف العبادة على الدعاء، فدلّ على أنهما واحد."
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas - Haqiqah/Literal): "دعوته دعواً ودعاءً: ناديته وصحت به. ودعا الله: ابتهل إليه بالسؤال. ودعا الرجل: استنصره. ودعا الناقة: استدبرها."
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas - Majaz/Metaphorical): "الدعاء في العبادة: استعارة من دعاء المسألة، لأن العابد كأنه يسأل الله الثواب والقبول. ومنه قوله تعالى: {إن الذين يستكبرون عن عبادتي} — أي عن دعائي، فسمّى العبادة دعاءً."

- Root: سحر (Saḥara)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "السحر: طرف الحلقوم والرئة. وقيل: السحر: آخر الليل عند الصبح. والسحور: الأكل في السحر. والسحرة: السحر الأخير من الليل."
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "السحر يقال على معان: الأول: الخداع وتخييلات لا حقيقة لها... والثاني: وقت السحر، وهو آخر الليل، سمي بذلك لأنه وقت يكون فيه تنفس الصعداء واسترواح من ظلمة الليل، أو لأنه وقت خفاء الناس وسكون الأصوات."
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas - Haqiqah/Literal): "لقيته سحراً وسحرة وبالسحر وفي أعلى السحرين وهما سحر مع الصبح وسحر قبله."
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas - Majaz/Metaphorical): "السحر في قوله تعالى: {وبالأسحار هم يستغفرون} — هو الوقت الأخير من الليل، وهو أشرف الأوقات للدعاء، لأنه وقت غفلة الناس وخلوة القلب."

- Root: عرف (ʿArafa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "العرف: الطيب. والمعرفة: العلم بالشيء على وجه التدبر. وعرفة: جبل بمكة، سمي بذلك لأن الناس يتعارفون فيه، أو لأن جبريل عليه السلام عرّف إبراهيم المناسك فيه."
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "عرفة: اسم للموقف الذي يقف فيه الحجاج، سمي بذلك لأن آدم وحواء تعارفا فيه بعد الهبوط، وقيل: لأن جبريل عرّف إبراهيم المناسك فيه."
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas - Haqiqah/Literal): "يوم عرفة: اليوم التاسع من ذي الحجة، وهو يوم الموقف."
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas - Majaz/Metaphorical): "عرفة في قولهم: يوم عرفة — اسم للموقف، سمي بذلك لتعارف الناس فيه، أو لتعريف جبريل إبراهيم المناسك."

- Root: غفر (Ghafara)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "المغفرة: ستر الذنب والتجاوز عنه. والغفر: الستر. والمغفر: ما يستر الرأس في الحرب. والغفور: الكثير المغفرة."
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الغفران: ستر الذنب والتجاوز عنه، وأصله من الغفر وهو الستر. قال تعالى: {وإن تغفر لهم فإنك أنت العزيز الحكيم}. والاستغفار: طلب المغفرة، وهو ضربان: استغفار باللسان، واستغفار بالقلب واللسان معاً، وهو النافع."
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas - Haqiqah/Literal): "غفرت الذنب غفراً ومغفرة: سترته وتجاوزت عنه. واستغفرت الله: طلبت مغفرته."
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas - Majaz/Metaphorical): "الاستغفار باللسان مع الإصرار: استعارة للكذب، لأن المستغفر الحقيقي هو التائب المقلع عن الذنب."

- Root: صلو (Ṣalā)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الصلاة: الدعاء، وقيل: العبادة، وقيل: الرحمة من الله، والاستغفار من الملائكة. والصلاة من الله: الرحمة، ومن الملائكة: الاستغفار، ومن المؤمنين: الدعاء."
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الصلاة في الأصل: الدعاء، قال تعالى: {صلوا عليه وسلموا تسليماً} — أي ادعوا له. ثم غلب استعمالها في العبادة المخصوصة، والصلاة من الله: الرحمة، ومن الملائكة: الاستغفار."
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas - Haqiqah/Literal): "الصلاة: الدعاء. ومنه قوله تعالى: {وصل عليهم إن صلاتك سكن لهم} — أي ادع لهم."
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas - Majaz/Metaphorical): "الصلاة على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: استعارة للدعاء له بالرحمة والتعظيم، لأن أصل الصلاة الدعاء."

- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication)
  * Governing Rule: "إنما" تفيد الحصر والقصر، فإذا قيل: "إن الدعاء هو العبادة" — فالمبتدأ والخبر معرفتان، والجملة تفيد الحصر والتأكيد. وإذا قيل: "الدعاء مخ العبادة" — فالإسناد فيه تشبيه بليغ، حيث شبه الدعاء بالمخ الذي هو لبّ العظم وجوهره، فالدعاء هو اللبّ والجوهر الحقيقي للعبادة.
