17:110.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'On Invocations and Supplications'

17:110.arabic: وقالت عائشة رضي الله عنه في قوله عز وجل {ولا تجهر بصلاتك ولا تخافت بها} (11) أي بدعائك وقد أثنى الله عز وجل على نبيه زكرياء عليه السلام حيث قال {إذ نادى ربه نداء خفيا} وقال عز وجل {ادعوا ربكم تضرعا وخفية} الخامس أن لا يتكلف السجع في الدعاء فإن حال الداعي ينبغي أن يكون حال متضرع والتكلف لا يناسبه قال صلى الله عليه وسلم سيكون قوم يعتدون في الدعاء (12) وقد قال عز وجل {ادعوا ربكم تضرعا وخفية إنه} {لا يحب المعتدين} قيل معناه التكلف للأسجاع والأولى أن لا يجاوز الدعوات المأثورة فإنه قد يعتدي في دعائ
17:110.english:
[Root: دعو]
  • Lisan al-Arab: "الدعاء: الرغبة إلى الله تعالى، والابتهال في المسألة. والدعوة: الكلمة التي يدعو بها. وأصل الدعاء: طلب الإقبال من الغير."
  • Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الدعاء: ضربان: أحدهما دعاء العبادة، والآخر دعاء المسألة. فدعاء العبادة: هو توجه العبد إلى الله تعالى بالطاعة. ودعاء المسألة: طلب الحاجة من الله تعالى. قال تعالى: {وقال ربكم ادعوني أستجب لكم}."
  • Al-Zamakhshari (Asas - Haqiqah/Literal): "دعا فلان ربه: ابتهل إليه بالسؤال. ودعا الله: عبده. ومنه قوله تعالى: {إن الذين يستكبرون عن عبادتي} أي عن دعائي."
  • Al-Zamakhshari (Asas - Majaz/Metaphorical): "دعا عليه: سأل الله أن يصيبه بمكروه. ودعا له: سأل الله أن يحسن إليه. ومن المجاز: دعا الأمر إلى كذا، أي أدى إليه."
17:110.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'On Invocations and Supplications'

18:10.arabic: سبقونا بالإيمان ولا تجعل في قلوبنا غلا للذين آمنوا ربنا إنك رؤوف رحيم ربنا آتنا من لدنك رحمة وهيئ لنا من أمرنا رشدا ربنا آتنا في الدنيا حسنة وفي الآخرة حسنة وقنا عذاب النار ربنا إننا سمعنا مناديا ينادي للإيمان إلى قوله عز وجل إنك لا تخلف الميعاد ربنا لا تؤاخذنا إن نسينا أو أخطأنا ربنا إلى آخر السورة (3) رب اغفر لي ولوالدي وارحمهما كما ربياني صغيرا واغفر للمؤمنين والمؤمنات والمسلمين والمسلمات الأحياء منهم والأموات (4) رب اغفر وارحم وتجاوز عما تعلم وأنت الأعز الأكرم وأنت خير الراحمين وأنت خير الغافرين وإنا لله وإنا إليه راجعون ولا حول ولا قوة إلا بالله العلي العظ
18:10.english: And employ me in righteous deeds which You will accept from me. (1) O God, I ask You for pardon, well-being, good certainty, and soundness in this world and the next. (2) O You Whom sins do not harm and from Whom forgiveness does not diminish anything — grant me that which will not harm You, and give me that which will not diminish You. Our Lord, pour upon us patience and cause us to die as Muslims. You are our Protector in this world and the next; cause me to die as a Muslim and join me with the righteous. You are our Protector, so forgive us and have mercy upon us, and You are the Best of forgivers. And write for us good in this world and in the Hereafter — indeed, we have turned to You in repentance. Our Lord, upon You we rely, to You we turn in repentance, and to You is the final return. Our Lord, make us not a trial for the wrongdoing people. Our Lord, make us not a trial for those who disbelieve, and forgive us, our Lord — indeed, You are the Mighty, the Wise. Our Lord, forgive us our sins and our excesses in our affairs, make firm our feet, and grant us victory over the disbelieving people. Our Lord, forgive us and our brothers who preceded us in faith, and place not in our hearts any rancor toward those who believe — our Lord, indeed You are Kind, Merciful. Our Lord, grant us from Yourself mercy and prepare for us from our affair right guidance. Our Lord, give us good in this world and good in the Hereafter, and protect us from the chastisement of the Fire. Our Lord, indeed we have heard a caller calling to faith — to His saying, Mighty and Majestic: {«إنك لا تخلف الميعاد»} [آل عمران/ 194] — Our Lord, do not take us to task if we forget or err. Our Lord, to the end of the surah. (3) My Lord, forgive me and my parents, and have mercy upon them as they raised me when I was small; and forgive the believing men and the believing women, and the Muslim men and the Muslim women, the living among them and the dead. (4) My Lord, forgive, have mercy, and overlook what You know — and You are the Most Exalted, the Most Generous, the Best of the merciful, and the Best of the forgivers. And indeed, to God we belong and to Him we return; and there is no might and no power except through God, the Exalted, the Magnificent; and God suffices us, and He is the Best Disposer of affairs. And may God send blessings upon Muhammad, the Seal of the Prophets, and upon his family and his companions, and grant them abundant peace. (5)
18:10.section_title_en: Section 252 — Supplications for Morning and Evening: Comprehensive Prayers of the Prophet (ﷺ)
18:10.anchors:
- Root: لهم (l-h-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of swallowing/ingesting (iltihām); from this derives the sense of something being cast directly into the innermost recess of the heart (al-rawʿ).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الإلهام: إلقاء الشيء في الروع" — ilhām is the casting of a thing into the innermost consciousness, specifically from God or the higher assembly (al-malaʾ al-aʿlā). It is that which the Prophet (ﷺ) called "the touch of the angel" (limat al-malak) and "the breath of the Holy Spirit in my innermost heart" (nafth rūḥ al-qudus fī rawʿī).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): "ألهمه الله الخير: ألقاه في روعه" — God inspired him with good: He cast it into his innermost consciousness. Metaphorical (majāz): A horse that "swallows the ground" (yaltaḥimu al-arḍ) in swiftness; thus ilhām is the swift, direct ingress of divine guidance into the soul without intermediary effort.
- Root: حمد (ḥ-m-d)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The root denotes praise arising from recognition of voluntary excellence and beneficence; al-ḥamd is commendation of the beloved for their attributes and acts of goodness.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Praise (ḥamd) is the acknowledgment of beneficence (niʿmah) with reverence and love; it is distinguished from mere thanks (shukr) in that it is directed to the essence and attributes of the praised one, not solely to the benefit received.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "أحمد الله تعالى بجميع محامده" — I praise God with all His praiseworthy attributes. Metaphorical: "أحمدت صنيعه" — I found his deed praiseworthy; thus the tongue's praise must be matched by the heart's recognition of the praised one's perfection.
- Root: غفر (gh-f-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The root denotes covering and shielding; al-mighfar is the helmet that protects the head in battle.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الغفر: إلباس ما يصونه عن الدنس" — Forgiveness is the clothing of that which shields from filth. God's forgiveness (maghfirah) is His shielding of the servant from the touch of chastisement, covering the sin so that it is as though it never were.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "اللهم غفرًا" — O God, forgive. Metaphorical: The she-beasts that "did not forgive" their heedlessness (lam taghfir la-hā ghaflātuhā) — i.e., they did not shield their young from destruction; thus forgiveness is active protection, not mere erasure.
- Root: نفس (n-f-s)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The self, the soul; that which breathes and has vital spirit; also used for the very essence of a thing.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "النفس: الروح" — the soul is the spirit; and in God's saying {«ويحذركم الله نفسه»} [آل عمران/ 28], "His Self" means His very essence (dhāt), which — though grammatically expressed as an annexation implying distinction — is in reality identical, with no multiplicity in the Divine Essence.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "شيء نفيس" — a precious thing. Metaphorical: "دفق نفسه" — he poured out his blood/life; thus nafs is the seat of life, passion, and moral responsibility.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الدعاء والخبر (The Chapter of Supplication and Assertion) — Supplications (duʿāʾ) are grammatically constructed as optative sentences (inshāʾ ṭalabī) using the imperative (rabbighfir), the jussive (lā tuʾākhidhnā), and the vocative (rabbanā), yet they may embed assertive clauses (khabar) of praise (al-ḥamdu lillāh) and attestation (lā ilāha illā anta). The periodic structure of these prayers alternates between direct address to God (munādāh) and self-referential confession, requiring the translator to preserve the vocative force of "O God" and "Our Lord" without flattening into mere description.

18:39.arabic: وشهد الله والإخلاص والمعوذتين وليقل بسم الله ما شاء الله لا قوة إلا بالله حسبي الله توكلت على الله ما شاء الله لا يأتي بالخير إلا الله ما شاء الله لا يصرف السوء إلا الله حسبي الله وكفى سمع الله لمن دعا ليس وراء الله منتهى ولا دون الله ملجأ كتب الله لأغلبن أنا ورسلي إن الله قوي عزيز تحصنت بالله العظيم واستغثت بالحي الذي لا يموت اللهم احرسنا بعينك التي لا تنام واكنفنا بركنك الذي لا يرام اللهم ارحمنا بقدرتك علينا فلا نهلك وأنت ثقتنا ورجاؤنا اللهم أعطف علينا قلوب عبادك وإمائك برأفة ورحمة إنك أنت أرحم الراحمين الثامنة م
18:39.english: He ought to seek out a righteous companion, one who loves goodness and assists in it: if he forgets, the companion reminds him; if he remembers, the companion aids him; if he fears, the companion emboldens him; if he weakens, the companion strengthens him; if his breast narrows, the companion enlarges his patience. He should bid farewell to his resident companions, his brothers, and his neighbors — taking leave of them and seeking their supplications, for God Most High places goodness in their prayers. The Sunnah of farewell is to say: «أستودع الله دينك وأمانتك وخواتيم عملك» — "I entrust to God your religion, your trustworthiness, and the seal of your deeds." And he, peace and blessings be upon him, used to say to one intending travel: "In God's protection and His care — may God provide you with piety, forgive your sin, and direct you toward goodness wherever you may be."
18:39.section_title_en: The Book of the Etiquette of Travel — Section 199: On the Comprehensive Etiquette of the Journey (From Provisioning to Guarding)
18:39.anchors:
- Root: س ف ر (S-F-R)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "السفر: كشف الغطاء" — unveiling, uncovering; the traveler is one who uncovers the veils of distant lands.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "السفر: كشف الغطاء، ويختص ذلك بالأعيان" — the journey is a literal uncovering of horizons, yet the spiritual journey unveils the soul's veils.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Haqiqah: "سافر سفرا بعيدا" (to travel far); Majaz: "وجه مسفر: مشرق سرورا" — a face radiant with joy, as the traveler's face brightens with divine trust.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — governing the permissible separation between the preposition and its object for rhetorical emphasis, as in the supplications' structural pauses.
18:39.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications, prayers, and their spiritual power, from 'On Invocations and Supplications'

18:39.arabic: التوفيق ولا حول ولا قوة إلا بالله العلي العظيم فأما ما ذكرت لي أني آكل الرقاق وألبس الدقاق وأحتجب وأجلس على الوطىء فنحن نفعل ذلك ونستغفر الله تعالى فقد قال الله تعالى {قل من حرم زينة الله التي أخرج لعباده والطيبات من الرزق} وإني لأعلم أن ترك ذلك خير من الدخول فيه ولا تدعنا من كتابك فلسنا ندعك من كتابنا والسلام فانظر إلى إنصاف مالك إذ اعترف أن
18:39.english: ...that he intended that (i.e., the debate) rather than formal learning. So he entered his house and did not come out to the people for forty days. When Hātim entered Baghdad, the people of Baghdad gathered around him and said: "O Abā ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, you are a man, but you are a foreigner (aʿjamī), and no one speaks with you except that you cut him off (in argument)." He said: "I have three traits (khiṣāl) by which I overcome my opponent: I rejoice when my opponent is correct, I grieve when he errs, and I guard myself from acting ignorantly toward him."
18:39.section_title_en: The Story of Hātim al-Aṣamm and the Letter of Mālik ibn Anas — On Renunciation of Worldly Adornment
18:39.anchors:
- Root: ع-ج-م (ʿ-j-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The core meaning denotes one who is non-Arab, or one whose speech is unclear/ungrammatical; also used for the unintelligible.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In theological contexts, it distinguishes the foreigner (aʿjamī) who lacks the eloquence of the Arabs, yet may possess wisdom.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) for non-Arab; metaphorical (majāz) for one who is silent or whose argument is weak.
- Root: خ-ص-ل (kh-ṣ-l)
  * Lisan / Ayn: A trait, quality, or characteristic (khiṣāl) inherent in a person, whether praiseworthy or blameworthy.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Used for moral and spiritual attributes that define one's character in the path of salvation.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal for a natural or acquired quality; metaphorical for a portion of good or evil.
- Root: ز-ي-ن (z-y-n)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Adornment, ornament, or beautification (zīnah); to decorate.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In the Quranic verse {قل من حرم زينة الله} it refers to permissible worldly beautification, which is not forbidden but can distract from the Hereafter.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal for physical ornament; metaphorical for spiritual adornment through piety.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحكاية والمحكي (Narration and the Quoted) — When quoting speech, the syntactic case of the original utterance is preserved, as seen in the direct quotes of Hātim and the letters exchanged.
18:39.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications, prayers, and their spiritual power, from 'On Invocations and Supplications'

19:3.arabic: بها} (11) أي بدعائك وقد أثنى الله عز وجل على نبيه زكرياء عليه السلام حيث قال {إذ نادى ربه نداء خفيا} وقال عز وجل {ادعوا ربكم تضرعا وخفية} الخامس أن لا يتكلف السجع في الدعاء فإن حال الداعي ينبغي أن يكون حال متضرع والتكلف لا يناسبه قال صلى الله عليه وسلم سيكون قوم يعتدون في الدعاء (12) وقد قال عز وجل {ادعوا ربكم تضرعا وخفية إنه} {لا يحب المعتدين} قيل معناه التكلف للأسجاع والأولى أن لا يجاوز الدعوات المأثورة فإنه قد يعتدي في دعائه فيسأل ما لا تقتضيه مصلحته فما كل أحد يحسن الدعاء ولذلك روي عن معاذ رضي الله عنه أن العلماء
19:3.english:
[Root: دعو]
  • Lisan al-Arab: "الدعاء: الرغبة إلى الله تعالى، والابتهال في المسألة. والدعوة: الكلمة التي يدعو بها. وأصل الدعاء: طلب الإقبال من الغير."
  • Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الدعاء: ضربان: أحدهما دعاء العبادة، والآخر دعاء المسألة. فدعاء العبادة: هو توجه العبد إلى الله تعالى بالطاعة. ودعاء المسألة: طلب الحاجة من الله تعالى. قال تعالى: {وقال ربكم ادعوني أستجب لكم}."
  • Al-Zamakhshari (Asas - Haqiqah/Literal): "دعا فلان ربه: ابتهل إليه بالسؤال. ودعا الله: عبده. ومنه قوله تعالى: {إن الذين يستكبرون عن عبادتي} أي عن دعائي."
  • Al-Zamakhshari (Asas - Majaz/Metaphorical): "دعا عليه: سأل الله أن يصيبه بمكروه. ودعا له: سأل الله أن يحسن إليه. ومن المجاز: دعا الأمر إلى كذا، أي أدى إليه."
19:3.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'On Invocations and Supplications'

20:14.arabic: وجل في كلام يردده في نفسه كما لو سمع وهو يقول {إنني أنا الله لا إله إلا أنا فاعبدني} فإنه ما كان ينبغي أن يفهم منه ذلك إلا على سبيل الحكاية الصنف الثاني من الشطح كلمات غير مفهومة لها ظواهر رائقة وفيها عبارات هائلة وليس وراءها طائل إما أن تكون غير مفهومة عند قائلها بل يصدرها عن خبط في عقله وتشويش في خياله لقلة إحاطته بمعنى كلام قرع سمعه وهذا هو الأكثر وإما أن تكون مفهومة له ولكنه لا يقدر على تفهيمها وإيرادها بعبارة تدل على ضميره لقلة ممارسته للعلم وعدم تعلمه طريق التعبير عن المعاني بالألفاظ الرشيقة ولا فائدة لهذا الجنس من ا
20:14.english: Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ, may God be pleased with him, said to his son ʿUmar — having heard him composing sajʿ — "This is what makes me dislike you. I will never fulfill your need until you repent." This was said when his son had come to him seeking a favor. And the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to ʿAbd Allāh ibn Rawāḥah when he spoke in sajʿ of three words: "Beware of sajʿ, O Ibn Rawāḥah." Thus, the forbidden sajʿ is the artificially contrived kind that exceeds two words. For this reason, when a man spoke concerning the blood-money for a fetus — saying, "How shall we pay blood-money for one who neither drank, nor ate, nor cried out, nor wailed? Such a one's blood is void" — the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, replied: "Sajʿ like the sajʿ of the bedouins!"
20:14.section_title_en: On the Etiquette of Preaching: The Condemnation of Artificial Sajʿ, Excessive Poetry, and the Perils of Shataḥ and Taʿwīl
20:14.anchors:
- Root: سجع (sajʿa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Rhymed prose; from the root meaning "to coo" (as a dove), indicating a measured, melodious cadence in speech.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In theological discourse, sajʿ is permissible when natural but blameworthy when artificially cultivated (takalluf), as it shifts focus from meaning to ornamentation.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) — natural rhythmic speech; Metaphorical (majāz) — the "sajʿ of the bedouins" (sajʿ al-aʿrāb) as a pejorative for empty, affected eloquence.
- Root: شعر (shiʿr)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Poetry; from the root denoting perception and fine discernment (shuʿūr), as the poet grasps subtle meanings.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Poetry is blameworthy when it stirs base appetites, but praiseworthy when it conveys wisdom (ḥikmah), as in the prophetic saying "Indeed from poetry there is wisdom."
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — metered, rhymed speech; Metaphorical — the "poetry" of the heart's inclination, where listeners project their own passions onto what they hear.
- Root: شطح (shaṭaḥa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To overflow, to gush forth; originally of a water-skin bursting, then applied to ecstatic utterances that overflow the bounds of conventional discourse.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In Sufi terminology, shataḥ refers to utterances arising from overwhelming spiritual states (ḥāl) that, when voiced to the unworthy, cause corruption.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — physical overflowing; Metaphorical — the soul's overflow in speech that exceeds the speaker's intentional control.
- Root: أول (taʿwīl)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To return something to its origin or end; interpretation that traces a word back to its intended meaning.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Taʿwīl is legitimate only when supported by textual (naqlī) or rational (ʿaqlī) evidence; arbitrary taʿwīl that severs words from their established senses destroys religious trust.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — the apparent sense (ẓāhir); Metaphorical — the inner sense (bāṭin), which is only valid when the literal sense is impossible or when transmitted authority sanctions it.
- Sibawayh Rule: Bāb al-Ḥaṣr wa al-Taqyīd bi-innamā (Restriction and Focused Predication) — The text repeatedly uses restrictive constructions (innamā, laysa...illā) to delimit permissible preaching, poetry, and interpretation, distinguishing the praiseworthy from the blameworthy with syntactic precision.
20:14.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications, prayers, and their spiritual power, from 'On Invocations and Supplications'

20:14.arabic: لا إله إلا أنا كما أوردناه في الأول فمن دعا بهذه الأسماء فليقل إنك أنت الله لا إله إلا أنت كذا وكذا فمن دعا بهن كتب من الساجدين المخبتين الذين يجاورون محمدا وإبراهيم وموسى وعيسى والنبيين صلوات الله عليهم في دار الجلال وله ثواب العابدين في السموات والأرضين وصلى الله على محمد وعلى كل عبد مصطفى
20:14.english: Muḥammad ibn Ḥassān said: Maʿrūf al-Karkhī — may God have mercy on him — said to me: "Shall I not teach you ten words — five for this world and five for the Hereafter? Whoever supplicates God — Mighty and Majestic — with them shall find God — Most High — present with them." I said: "Write them down for me." He said: "No, but I shall repeat them to you as Bakr ibn Khunays — may God have mercy on him — repeated them to me:
20:14.section_title_en: Section 249 — Supplications of the Righteous (Adʿiyat al-Ṣāliḥīn)
20:14.anchors:
- Root: حسب (ḥ-s-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of counting, reckoning, and sufficiency — "ḥasb" denotes that which suffices or is enough
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الحساب: استعمال العدد" — the theological nuance of ḥasbī Allāh ("God is my Sufficer") carries the sense of complete reliance upon God's reckoning and provision, transcending mere numerical counting to signify total trust in divine sufficiency
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): "حسب المال" (he counted the wealth); Metaphorical (majāz): "خرجا يتحسبان الأخبار" (they go out seeking news) — in the supplication "ḥasbī Allāh," the literal sense of "sufficiency" is intended, yet it carries the metaphorical extension of complete trust, as one who has God as his Sufficer has no need of any other reckoning

- Root: اله (ʾ-l-h)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of worship, devotion, and seeking refuge; "ilāh" denotes that which is worshipped
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الله: قيل: أصله إله فحذفت همزته، وأدخل عليها الألف واللام، فخص بالباري تعالى" — the name Allāh is the proper name of the Creator, distinguished from generic "ilāh" (any object of worship); in these supplications, the divine names invoked (al-Karīm, al-Ḥalīm, al-Qawī, al-Shadīd, al-Raḥīm, al-Raʾūf, al-Laṭīf, al-Qadīr) each specify particular attributes of the divine essence
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "فلان يتأله: يتعبد" (he worships); the supplications employ the divine names in their literal theological sense, each name invoking a specific attribute relevant to the particular need mentioned

- Root: انا (ʾ-n-y)
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "أنا ضمير المخبر عن نفسه" — the first-person pronoun; in the divine self-declaration "innī anā Allāh," the repetition emphasizes divine self-identification
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "أنى الطعام أي إدراكه" (the food ripened/reached its time) — the related sense of something reaching its appointed time appears in "عند المسألة في القبر" (at the questioning in the grave), indicating appointed moments of divine reckoning

- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The supplications employ repeated prepositional phrases (ʿinda al-mawt, ʿinda al-masʾalah, ʿinda al-ḥisāb, ʿinda al-mīzān, ʿinda al-ṣirāṭ) in parallel construction, each governing a distinct divine name, creating a rhythmic liturgical structure where each clause stands as an independent invocation

20:25.arabic: اللهم اشرح لي صدري ويسر لي أمري وليقل اللهم رب الحمد لك الحمد كما تقول وخيرا مما نقول لك صلاتي ونسكي ومحياي ومماتي وإليك مآبي وإليك ثوابي اللهم إني أعوذ بك من وساوس الصدر وشتات الأمر وعذاب القبر اللهم إني أعوذ بك من شر ما يلج في الليل ومن شر ما يلج في النهار ومن شر ما تهب به الرياح ومن شر بوائق الدهر اللهم إني أعوذ بك من تحول عافيتك وفجأة نقمتك وجميع سخطك اللهم اهدني بالهدى واغفر لي في الآخرة والأولى يا خير مقصود وأسنى منزول به وأكرم مسئول ما لديه أعطني العشية أفضل ما أعطيت أ
20:25.english: On the Day of 'Arafah, the first thing with which one supplicates, let him say: There is no god but God alone, with no partner; His is the sovereignty and His is the praise; He gives life and causes death, and He is Living, He does not die; in His hand is all good, and He is over all things Omnipotent. O God, place in my heart a light, and in my hearing a light, and in my sight a light, and in my tongue a light. O God, expand for me my breast and make easy for me my affair. And let him say: O God, Lord of the praise, to You is the praise as You say, and better than what we say. To You is my prayer, my sacrifice, my living, and my dying; to You is my return, and to You is my recompense. O God, I seek refuge in You from the whisperings of the breast, the scattering of affairs, and the torment of the grave. O God, I seek refuge in You from the evil of what enters in the night, and from the evil of what enters in the day, and from the evil of what the winds bring, and from the evil of the calamities of time. O God, I seek refuge in You from the withdrawal of Your well-being, the suddenness of Your retribution, and all of Your wrath. O God, guide me with guidance, and forgive me in the Hereafter and the First. O Best of all sought goals, and Most Exalted of all that is alighted upon, and Most Generous of all who are asked — whatever is with You — grant me this evening the best of what You have given to any of Your creatures and pilgrims of Your Sacred House, O Most Merciful of the merciful. O God, O Raiser of degrees and Sender of blessings, O Originator of the earths and the heavens, voices have clamored to You in diverse languages, asking You their needs. And my need of You is that You not forget me in the abode of trial when the people of this world have forgotten me. O God, You hear my speech and see my place and know my secret and my public, and nothing of my affair is hidden from You. I am the wretched one, the poor one, the seeker of aid, the seeker of refuge, the fearful, the apprehensive, the confessor of his sin. I ask You with the asking of the destitute, and I supplicate to You with the supplication of the abased sinner, and I call upon You with the call of the fearful and distressed — the call of one whose neck has bowed to You, whose tears have flowed for You, whose body has humbled before You, and whose nose has been rubbed in the dust for You. O God, do not make me, by my supplication to You, O Lord, wretched, and be to me kind and merciful, O Best of those who are asked and Most Generous of those who give. My God, whoever has praised his own soul to You — for I am one who blames his own soul. My God, sins have silenced my tongue, so I have no means of intercession other than deeds, and no intercessor other than hope. My God, I know that my sins have left me no standing with You, nor any face for excuse — but You are the Most Generous of the generous. My God, if I am not worthy to attain Your mercy, then Your mercy is worthy to attain me, for Your mercy encompasses all things, and I am a thing. My God, though my sins be great, yet they are small beside Your pardon, so forgive them for me, O Generous One. My God, You are You, and I am I. I am the one who returns to sins, and You are the One who returns to forgiveness. My God, if You show mercy only to the people of obedience, then to whom shall the sinners flee? My God, I turned away from Your obedience deliberately, and I headed toward Your disobedience intentionally. Glory be to You — how great is Your proof against me, and how generous is Your pardon toward me! By the necessity of Your proof against me, and the severance of my excuse from You, and my poverty toward You, and Your richness from me — forgive me, O Best of those whom a caller has called, and Most Excellent of those whom a hope has hoped in. By the sanctity of Islam and by the covenant of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, I seek intercession with You, so forgive me all my sins, and turn me away from this standing place of mine with my needs fulfilled, and grant me what I have asked, and realize my hope in what I have wished. My God, I have called upon You with the supplication that You taught me, so do not deprive me of the hope that You made known to me. My God, what will You do this evening with a servant who confesses to You his sin, who is humble before You in his abasement, who is submissive in his offense, who pleads to You concerning his deed, who repents to You from his transgression, who seeks Your forgiveness for his wrong, who supplicates to You for pardon of him, who asks of You the success of his needs, who hopes in You at his standing place — despite the abundance of his sins? O Refuge of every living thing, and Protector of every believer — whoever does well, it is by Your mercy that he triumphs, and whoever errs, it is by his error that he perishes. O God, to You we have come forth, and in Your courtyard we have alighted, and You alone we hope, and what is with You we seek, and to Your beneficence we expose ourselves, and Your mercy we hope for, and from Your chastisement we are fearful, and to You with the heavy burdens of sins we have fled, and to Your Sacred House we have performed the pilgrimage. O You who owns the needs of those who ask, and knows the consciences of the silent — O You who has no lord with Him who is invoked, and no creator above Him who is feared, and no minister to whom one comes, and no chamberlain who is bribed — O You who increases not by the abundance of asking except in bounty and generosity, nor by the abundance of needs except in favor and beneficence. O God, You have made for every guest a hospitality, and we are Your guests, so make Your hospitality to us Paradise. O God, for every delegation there is a gift, and for every visitor there is an honor, and for every asker there is a giving, and for every one who hopes there is a reward, and for every seeker there is with You a recompense, and for every...
20:25.section_title_en: The Supplications of the Day of 'Arafah — Section 206
20:25.anchors:
- Root: دعو (d-'-w)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to call, summon, invoke; du'a is the act of calling upon God with humble petition.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In theological usage, du'a is the essence of worship ('ibadah), the creature's acknowledgment of need (iftiqar) before the Creator, and a means of drawing near (taqarrub).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (haqiqah): vocal calling. Metaphorical (majaz): the soul's inward turning to God, even without utterance.
- Root: نور (n-w-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Light; that by which one sees physically and, by extension, that by which the heart perceives truth.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Light (nur) is of two kinds: sensory (hissi) and intellectual ('aqli). The prophetic prayer for light in heart, hearing, sight, and tongue seeks the illumination of all faculties for obedience and gnosis (ma'rifah).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical luminosity. Metaphorical: guidance (huda) and clarity of perception in religious and moral matters.
- Root: عفو ('-f-w)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To pardon, to efface, to leave unpunished; to exceed in generosity.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): 'Afw is the erasure of sin and the lifting of its consequence; it is an attribute of God's mercy (rahmah) that supersedes His justice when the servant repents.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: to obliterate a trace. Metaphorical: God's complete remission of sin, leaving no mark of accountability.
- Root: رجا (r-j-w)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Hope, expectation of good; the opposite of despair (ya's).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Raja' is the heart's confident expectation of God's bounty, paired with fear (khawf); it is a station (maqam) of the sincere.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: to await. Metaphorical: the soul's reliance on divine mercy despite unworthiness.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Conjunction and Apposition (al-'Atf wa al-Badal) — The repeated vocatives "Ilahi" (My God) and "Allahumma" (O God) function as independent invocations, each followed by coordinated clauses that build a cumulative structure of petition, confession, and praise, requiring faithful preservation of each unit without conflation.
20:25.topic: Al-Ghazali on the journey of the soul, death, and the Hereafter, from 'Mysteries of Hajj'

20:25.arabic: رب اشرح لي صدري ويسر لي أمري وتقول عند النظر إلى السماء ربنا ما خلقت هذا باطلا سبحانك فقنا عذاب النار تبارك الذي جعل في السماء بروجا وجعل فيها سراجا وقمرا منيرا وإذا سمعت صوت الرعد فقل سبحان من يسبح الرعد بحمده والملائكة من خيفته (7) فإن رأيت الصواعق فقل اللهم لا تقتلنا بغضبك ولا تهلكنا بعذابك وعافنا قبل ذلك (8) قاله كعب فإذا أمطرت السماء فقل اللهم سقيا هنيئا وصيبا نافعا (9) اللهم اجعله صيب رحمة ولا تجعله صيب عذاب (10) فإذا غضبت فقل اللهم اغفر لي ذنبي وأذهب غيظ قلبي PageV01P
20:25.english: When you rise in the morning and hear the call to prayer (adhān), it is recommended for you to respond to the caller of prayer (mu'adhdhin) — and we have already mentioned this, along with the supplications for entering and leaving the privy, and the supplications of ablution (wuḍū'), in the Book of Purification. When you set out toward the mosque, say: "O Allah, place light (nūr) in my heart, and light in my tongue, and place light in my hearing, and place light in my sight, and place light behind me, and light before me, and place light above me. O Allah, grant me light." And also say: "O Allah, I ask You by the right of those who ask of You, and by the right of this my walking unto You — for I have not gone out in insolence, nor in vanity, nor for show, nor for reputation. I have gone out seeking protection from Your wrath and seeking Your good pleasure. So I ask You to deliver me from the Fire and to forgive me my sins — verily, none forgives sins but You."
20:25.section_title_en: Section 254 — Supplications for the Hours of Day and Night: From Dawn to Sleep
20:25.anchors:
- Root: ن و ر (n-w-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: النور: الضوء المنتشر الذي يُبصر به، وهو ضد الظلمة
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): النور في القرآن يقع على ضروب: منها المعقول كالإيمان والحكمة، قال تعالى: {قد جاءكم من الله نور وكتاب مبين}، ومنها المحسوس كضوء الشمس والقمر
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): النور حقيقة في الضوء المحسوس، ومجاز في الهدى والإيمان والعلم — فدعاء النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بطلب النور يشمل المعنيين جميعاً
- Root: س ج د (s-j-d)
  * Lisan / Ayn: السجود: وضع الجبهة على الأرض تعظيماً، وأصله التطامن والانخفاض
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): السجود ضربان: سجود عبادة وهو وضع الجبهة على الأرض تقرباً، وسجود طاعة وهو الانقياد والخضوع — قال تعالى: {ولله يسجد من في السموات والأرض طوعاً وكرهاً}
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): سجد حقيقة في وضع الجبهة، ومجاز في الخضوع والانقياد — وقوله "سجد لك سوادي وخيالي" من المجاز المرسل
- Root: ذ ك ر (dh-k-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: الذكر: نقيض النسيان، والذكر: الصوت الذي يُذكر به الشيء، والذكر: الشرف والصيت
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): الذكر ضربان: ذكر بالقلب وهو التفكر في عظمة الله، وذكر باللسان وهو التلفظ بأسمائه — وأعلى مراتبه ما اجتمع فيه القلب واللسان
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): الذكر حقيقة في استحضار الشيء بالقلب أو اللسان، ومجاز في الصلاة والدعاء والثناء
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — جواز تقديم المعمول وتأخيره مع بقاء العامل عاملاً في المعنى، كقوله "لك الحمد" حيث تقدم الجار والمجرور على المبتدأ للاختصاص والاهتمام
20:25.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications, prayers, and their spiritual power, from 'On Invocations and Supplications'

21:25.arabic: وجل في كلام يردده في نفسه كما لو سمع وهو يقول {إنني أنا الله لا إله إلا أنا فاعبدني} فإنه ما كان ينبغي أن يفهم منه ذلك إلا على سبيل الحكاية الصنف الثاني من الشطح كلمات غير مفهومة لها ظواهر رائقة وفيها عبارات هائلة وليس وراءها طائل إما أن تكون غير مفهومة عند قائلها بل يصدرها عن خبط في عقله وتشويش في خياله لقلة إحاطته بمعنى كلام قرع سمعه وهذا هو الأكثر وإما أن تكون مفهومة له ولكنه لا يقدر على تفهيمها وإيرادها بعبارة تدل على ضميره لقلة ممارسته للعلم وعدم تعلمه طريق التعبير عن المعاني بالألفاظ الرشيقة ولا فائدة لهذا الجنس من ا
21:25.english: Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ, may God be pleased with him, said to his son ʿUmar — having heard him composing sajʿ — "This is what makes me dislike you. I will never fulfill your need until you repent." This was said when his son had come to him seeking a favor. And the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to ʿAbd Allāh ibn Rawāḥah when he spoke in sajʿ of three words: "Beware of sajʿ, O Ibn Rawāḥah." Thus, the forbidden sajʿ is the artificially contrived kind that exceeds two words. For this reason, when a man spoke concerning the blood-money for a fetus — saying, "How shall we pay blood-money for one who neither drank, nor ate, nor cried out, nor wailed? Such a one's blood is void" — the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, replied: "Sajʿ like the sajʿ of the bedouins!"
21:25.section_title_en: On the Etiquette of Preaching: The Condemnation of Artificial Sajʿ, Excessive Poetry, and the Perils of Shataḥ and Taʿwīl
21:25.anchors:
- Root: سجع (sajʿa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Rhymed prose; from the root meaning "to coo" (as a dove), indicating a measured, melodious cadence in speech.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In theological discourse, sajʿ is permissible when natural but blameworthy when artificially cultivated (takalluf), as it shifts focus from meaning to ornamentation.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) — natural rhythmic speech; Metaphorical (majāz) — the "sajʿ of the bedouins" (sajʿ al-aʿrāb) as a pejorative for empty, affected eloquence.
- Root: شعر (shiʿr)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Poetry; from the root denoting perception and fine discernment (shuʿūr), as the poet grasps subtle meanings.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Poetry is blameworthy when it stirs base appetites, but praiseworthy when it conveys wisdom (ḥikmah), as in the prophetic saying "Indeed from poetry there is wisdom."
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — metered, rhymed speech; Metaphorical — the "poetry" of the heart's inclination, where listeners project their own passions onto what they hear.
- Root: شطح (shaṭaḥa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To overflow, to gush forth; originally of a water-skin bursting, then applied to ecstatic utterances that overflow the bounds of conventional discourse.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In Sufi terminology, shataḥ refers to utterances arising from overwhelming spiritual states (ḥāl) that, when voiced to the unworthy, cause corruption.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — physical overflowing; Metaphorical — the soul's overflow in speech that exceeds the speaker's intentional control.
- Root: أول (taʿwīl)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To return something to its origin or end; interpretation that traces a word back to its intended meaning.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Taʿwīl is legitimate only when supported by textual (naqlī) or rational (ʿaqlī) evidence; arbitrary taʿwīl that severs words from their established senses destroys religious trust.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — the apparent sense (ẓāhir); Metaphorical — the inner sense (bāṭin), which is only valid when the literal sense is impossible or when transmitted authority sanctions it.
- Sibawayh Rule: Bāb al-Ḥaṣr wa al-Taqyīd bi-innamā (Restriction and Focused Predication) — The text repeatedly uses restrictive constructions (innamā, laysa...illā) to delimit permissible preaching, poetry, and interpretation, distinguishing the praiseworthy from the blameworthy with syntactic precision.
21:25.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications, prayers, and their spiritual power, from 'On Invocations and Supplications'

21:87.arabic: له وأشهد أن محمدا عبده ورسوله سبحانك اللهم وبحمدك لا إله إلا أنت عملت سوءا وظلمت نفسي أستغفرك اللهم وأتوب إليك فاغفر لي وتب على إنك أنت التواب الرحيم اللهم اجعلني من التوابين واجعلني من المتطهرين واجعلني من عبادك الصالحين واجعلني عبدا صبورا شكورا واجعلني أذكرك كثيرا وأسبحك بكرة وأصيلا يقال إن من قال هذا بعد الوضوء ختم على وضوئه بخاتم ورفع له تحت العرش فلم يزل يسبح الله تعالى ويقدسه ويكتب له ثواب ذلك إلى يوم القيامة ويكره في الوضوء أمور منها أن يزيد على الثلاث فمن زاد فقد ظلم وأن يسرف في الماء توضأ عليه السلا
21:87.english: Know that the use of the tooth-stick is a confirmed Sunnah. It is reported concerning its virtue from the ḥadīth of Ibn ʿUmar through a weak chain of transmission, and Abū Dāwūd and al-Ḥākim narrated it, and the latter declared it sound (ṣaḥīḥ). Al-Bayhaqī, however, deemed it weak from the ḥadīth of ʿĀʾishah, and he weakened the version containing the wording "from seventy prayers." There is the ḥadīth: "Were it not that I would impose hardship upon my community, I would have commanded them to use the tooth-stick at every prayer" — agreed upon (muttafaq ʿalayh) from the ḥadīth of Abū Hurayrah. There is the ḥadīth: "Why do I see you entering upon me with yellowed teeth? Use the tooth-stick!" — al-Bazzār and al-Bayhaqī narrated it from the ḥadīth of al-ʿAbbās ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib; Abū Dāwūd and al-Baghawī from the ḥadīth of Tammām ibn al-ʿAbbās; and al-Bayhaqī from the ḥadīth of ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās — and it is disordered (muḍṭarib). There is the ḥadīth: "He used the tooth-stick multiple times during the night" — Muslim narrated it from the ḥadīth of Ibn ʿAbbās. And the ḥadīth of Ibn ʿAbbās: "The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not cease commanding us to use the tooth-stick until we thought that something concerning it would be revealed to him" — Aḥmad narrated it.
21:87.section_title_en: The Book of the Tooth-Stick (Siwāk) and the Etiquette of Ablution (Wuḍūʾ)
21:87.anchors:
- Root: س و ك (s-w-k)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The root denotes rubbing or cleansing the teeth with a stick (siwāk); al-Farāhīdī notes its use for the act of friction against a surface to remove residue.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In the religious lexicon, siwāk is a purifying act (taṭhīr) of the mouth, tied to devotional hygiene and the Sunnah's emphasis on preparing the body for prayer.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) usage refers to the physical stick (ʿūd) and the mechanical action; metaphorical (majāz) extension applies to spiritual purification, as the mouth's cleanliness mirrors the heart's purity.
- Root: و ض ء (w-ḍ-ʾ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Wuḍūʾ signifies washing specific bodily parts for ritual purity; al-Khalīl links it to brightness and radiance (ḍawʾ), as the washed limbs shine on the Day of Resurrection.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): It is a legislated act of cleansing (ṭahārah) that removes minor ritual impurity (ḥadath), preconditioning the soul for communion with God in prayer.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: washing with water; metaphorical: the inner purification of the heart from vices, as the outward washing symbolizes inward renewal.
- Root: غ ر ر (gh-r-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Ghurrah denotes a blaze or white mark on a horse's forehead; al-Ayn records its use for a prominent, shining feature.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In the ḥadīth, "ghurrah" refers to the luminous mark on the forehead of the believer from washing in ablution, a sign of honor on the Day of Judgment.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the white star on a horse's brow; metaphorical: the radiant trace of worship on the believer's body, visible in the Hereafter.
- Sibawayh Rule: Bāb al-ʿAṭf ʿalā al-Sabab (Coordination of Causes) — When linking actions or supplications (duʿāʾ) with fa- or thumma, the syntactic sequence mirrors the chronological order of ritual acts, ensuring that each clause is semantically complete and temporally precise.
21:87.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications, prayers, and their spiritual power, from 'On Invocations and Supplications'

21:87.arabic: تسيل على لحيته جعل يقول {لا إله إلا أنت سبحانك إني كنت من الظالمين} اللهم إني أستعديك عليهم وأستعينك على جميع أموري وأسألك الصبر على ما ابتليتني وفاة علي كرم الله وجهه قال الأصبغ الحنظلي لما كانت الليلة التي أصيب فيها علي كرم الله وجهه اتاه ابن التياح حين طلع الفجر يؤذنه بالصلاة وهو مضطجع متثاقل فعاد الثانية وهو كذلك ثم عاد الثالثة فقام علي يمشي وهو يقول اشدد حيازيمك للموت .
21:87.english: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Salām said: I came to my brother ʿUthmān to greet him while he was besieged, and I entered upon him. He said, "Welcome, O my brother. I saw the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, tonight in this niche"—and it was a niche in the house—"and he said, 'O ʿUthmān, they have besieged you.' I said, 'Yes.' He said, 'They have thirsted you.' I said, 'Yes.' So he lowered a bucket containing water, and I drank until I was quenched, until I felt its coolness between my chest and my shoulders. And he said to me, 'If you wish, I will grant you victory over them, and if you wish, you may break your fast with us.' So I chose to break my fast with him, and he was killed that very day, may Allah be pleased with him."
21:87.section_title_en: The Martyrdoms of ʿUthmān, ʿAlī, al-Ḥasan, and al-Ḥusayn (May Allah Be Pleased with Them)
21:87.anchors:
- Root: قتل (q-t-l)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of killing, slaying, or putting to death; the act of taking life.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In theological context, distinguishes between lawful execution (qisās) and unlawful murder (qatl ʿudwān), often tied to martyrdom (shahādah) when the victim is righteous.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) for physical killing; metaphorical (majāz) for spiritual death or the "killing" of the soul through sin.
- Root: شهد (sh-h-d)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To witness, testify, or be present; also denotes martyrdom (shahīd) as one who bears witness with their life.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Shahīd in the Quranic sense is one who is killed in the path of Allah, their testimony being accepted by Allah; also the Prophet as a witness over his community.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: presence at an event; metaphorical: the martyr's soul is "present" with Allah, alive in a spiritual sense.
- Root: حصر (ḥ-ṣ-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To confine, besiege, or restrict; a state of being hemmed in.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In Kalam, denotes physical constraint (ḥaṣr) versus spiritual freedom; the besieged believer remains inwardly free.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: military siege; metaphorical: the soul's confinement in worldly trials.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Conditional Clauses (Bāb al-Sharṭ) — The protasis (sharṭ) and apodosis (jawāb) structure in "إن شئت نصرت عليك" (If you wish, I will grant you victory), where the conditional particle governs both clauses, requiring precise temporal and modal sequencing.
21:87.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications, prayers, and their spiritual power, from 'Remembrance of Death and Afterlife'

21:87.arabic: والشهادة رب كل شيء ومليكه أشهد أن لا إله إلا أنت أعوذ بك من شر نفسي وشر الشيطان وشركه (4) وقل اللهم إني أسألك العفو والعافية في ديني ودنياي وأهلي ومالي اللهم استر عوراتي وآمن روعاتي وأقل عثراتي واحفظني من بين يدي ومن خلفي وعن يميني وعن شمالي ومن فوقي وأعوذ بك أن أغتال من تحتي (1) اللهم لا تؤمني مكرك ولا تولني غيرك ولا تنزع عني سترك ولا تنسني ذكرك ولا تجعلني من الغافلين (2) وقل اللهم أنت ربي لا إله إلا أنت خلقتني وأنا عبدك وأنا على عهدك ووعدك ما استطعت أعوذ بك من شر ما صنعت أبو
21:87.english: "Glory be to my Lord, the Most High, the Most Exalted, the Bestower (al-Wahhāb). There is no god but God alone, with no partner. His is the sovereignty and His is the praise, and He is over all things powerful."
21:87.section_title_en: The Fourth Chapter on Supplications Narrated from the Prophet (Peace Be Upon Him) and His Companions (May God Be Pleased with Them)
21:87.anchors:
- Root: لهم (l-h-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of swallowing/ingesting (iltihām), from which ilhām (divine inspiration) derives—that which is cast into the heart
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الإلهام: إلقاء الشيء في الروع" — divine inspiration is the casting of something into the inner faculty of consciousness (rawʿ), specifically from God and the higher assembly (malā aʿlā)
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (haqīqah): "ألهمه الله الخير: ألقاه في روعه" (God inspired him with good: He cast it into his inner consciousness). Metaphorical (majāz): "جيش لهام: يغتمر من يدخله" (an overwhelming army that engulfs whoever enters it)
- Root: غيب (gh-y-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: That which is hidden from sensory perception
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الغيب: مصدر غابت الشمس وغيرها: إذا استترت عن العين" — that which is concealed from the eye; applied to all that is absent from the senses and from human knowledge. Notably: "ويقال للشيء: غيب وغائب باعتباره بالناس لا بالله تعالى، فإنه لا يغيب عنه شيء" (it is called ghayb relative to people, not relative to God, for nothing is hidden from Him)
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "وتكلم بذلك عن ظهر الغيب" (he spoke of that from behind the unseen). Metaphorical: "أتونا في غابة أي في رماح كثيرة" (they came to us in a thicket—i.e., amidst numerous spears like dense trees)
- Root: علم (ʿ-l-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Knowledge as the apprehension of a thing's reality
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "العلم: إدراك الشيء بحقيقته" — knowledge is the apprehension of a thing in its true reality; two types: apprehension of the essence of a thing, and judgment upon a thing regarding what exists for it or is negated from it
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "ما علمت بخبرك: ما شعرت به" (I did not know of your news: I was not aware of it). "وهو من أعلام العلم الخافقه" (he is among the lofty banners of knowledge)
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — governing the permissible separation between the preposition and its object for rhetorical emphasis, as in the construction "عالم الغيب والشهادة" where the attributive relationship is maintained through the genitive construction (iḍāfah)
21:87.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications, prayers, and their spiritual power, from 'On Invocations and Supplications'

21:90.arabic: السادس التضرع والخشوع والرغبة والرهبة قال الله تعالى {إنهم كانوا يسارعون في الخيرات ويدعوننا رغبا ورهبا} وقال عز وجل {ادعوا ربكم تضرعا وخفية} وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا أحب الله عبدا ابتلاه حتى يسمع تضرعه (3) السابع أن يجزم الدعاء ويوقن بالإجابة ويصدق رجاءه فيه قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لا يقل أحدكم إذا دعا اللهم اغفر لي إن شئت اللهم ارحمني إن شئت ليعزم المسألة فإنه لا مكره له (4) وقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا دعا أحدكم فليعظم الرغبة فإن الله لا يتعاظمه شيء (5) وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم ادعوا الله وأنتم موقنون بالإجابة وا
21:90.english:
[Root: دعو]
  • Lisan al-Arab: "الدعاء: الرغبة إلى الله تعالى، والابتهال في المسألة. والدعوة: الكلمة التي يدعو بها. وأصل الدعاء: طلب الإقبال من الغير."
  • Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الدعاء: ضربان: أحدهما دعاء العبادة، والآخر دعاء المسألة. فدعاء العبادة: هو توجه العبد إلى الله تعالى بالطاعة. ودعاء المسألة: طلب الحاجة من الله تعالى. قال تعالى: {وقال ربكم ادعوني أستجب لكم}."
  • Al-Zamakhshari (Asas - Haqiqah/Literal): "دعا فلان ربه: ابتهل إليه بالسؤال. ودعا الله: عبده. ومنه قوله تعالى: {إن الذين يستكبرون عن عبادتي} أي عن دعائي."
  • Al-Zamakhshari (Asas - Majaz/Metaphorical): "دعا عليه: سأل الله أن يصيبه بمكروه. ودعا له: سأل الله أن يحسن إليه. ومن المجاز: دعا الأمر إلى كذا، أي أدى إليه."
21:90.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'On Invocations and Supplications'

22:7.arabic: حق ومنكرا ونكيرا حق ووعدك حق ووعيدك حق ولقاءك حق والساعة آتية لا ريب فيها وأن الله يبعث من في القبور على ذلك أحيا وعليه أموت وعليه أبعث إن شاء الله اللهم أنت ربي لا إله إلا أنت خلقتني وأنا عبدك وأنا على عهدك ووعدك ما استطعت أعوذ بك اللهم من شر ما صنعت ومن شر كل ذي شر اللهم إني ظلمت نفسي فاغفر لي ذنوبي فإنه لا يغفر الذنوب إلا أنت واهدني لأحسن الأخلاق فإنه لا يهدي لأحسنها إلا أنت واصرف عني سيئها فإنه لا يصرف سيئها إلا أنت لبيك وسعديك والخير كله بيديك أنا لك وإليك أستغفرك وأتوب إليك آمنت اللهم بما أرسلته من رسول وآمنت اللهم بما أنزلت من ك
22:7.english: It is narrated that Yūnus ibn ʿUbayd saw a man in a dream — a man who had been killed as a martyr in the lands of the Byzantines — and he said to him: "What is the most excellent deed that you witnessed?" He replied: "I witnessed the glorifications (tasbīḥāt) of Ibn al-Muʿtamir holding a station with Allah, Mighty and Majestic." And they are these: "Glory be to Allah (subḥāna Allāh), and praise be to Allah (al-ḥamdu li-Allāh), and there is no god but Allah (lā ilāha illā Allāh), and Allah is the Greatest (Allāhu akbar), and there is no might and no power except through Allah, the Most High, the Magnificent — to the number of what He has created, and the number of what He is creating, and the weight of what He has created, and the weight of what He is creating, and the fill of what He has created, and the fill of what He is creating, and the fill of His heavens and the fill of His earth, and the like of that, and multiples of that, and the number of His creation, and the weight of His Throne, and the utmost extent of His mercy, and the ink of His words, and the limit of His good pleasure, until He is pleased, and when He is pleased, [then] the number of what His creation has remembered Him with in all that has passed, and the number of what they will remember Him with in what remains, in every year, and month, and Friday, and day, and night, and hour of the hours, and breath of the breaths, and age of the ages, from eternity to eternity — the eternity of this world and the eternity of the Hereafter — and more than that, whose beginning does not cease and whose end does not come to an end."
22:7.section_title_en: The Supplications of Ibn al-Muʿtamir (Sulaymān al-Taymī) and His Glorifications, and the Supplication of Ibrāhīm ibn Adham — May Allah Be Well Pleased with Them
22:7.anchors:
- Root: سبح (s-b-ḥ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of swift motion (in water or air); extended to the act of prayer and glorification.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "التسبيح: تنزيه الله تعالى. وأصله: المر السريع في عبادة الله تعالى" — Glorification is the declaration of Allah's transcendence; its root is the swift passage in worship of Allah.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "سبحت الله وسبحت له" — to declare Him transcendent. Metaphorical: "والنجوم تسبح في الفلك" — the stars glide in their orbits, a metaphor for their obedient motion.
- Root: حمد (ḥ-m-d)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of praise and commendation for a beneficial act.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Praise (ḥamd) is the acknowledgment of beneficence with reverence; it is due to Allah alone in His absolute perfection.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "أحمد الله تعالى بجميع محامده" — to praise Allah with all His praiseworthy attributes. Metaphorical: "أحمدت الأرض: رضيت سكناها" — to find a thing agreeable, extending praise to non-verbal contexts.
- Root: لهم (l-h-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of swift swallowing or devouring.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الإلهام: إلقاء الشيء في الروع" — Inspiration is the casting of a thing into the heart/mind (al-rawʿ), specifically from Allah or the higher assembly.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "ألهمه الله الخير: ألقاه في روعه" — Allah inspired him with good. Metaphorical: "جواد يلتهم الأرض" — a swift horse devours the ground, extending to rapid comprehension.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The permissibility of interposing elements between a preposition and its object when the clause remains grammatically sound, as seen in the extended supplicatory sentences.
22:7.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications, prayers, and their spiritual power, from 'On Invocations and Supplications'

22:7.arabic: وهذا أمر ينكشف يوم تبلى السرائر ويوم يبعثر ما في القبور ويحصل ما في الصدور فعند ذلك تتميز السبيكة الخالصة من البهرجة فنعوذ بالله من الخزي يوم العرض الأكبر السادس وسخ البراجم وهي معاطف ظهور الأنامل كانت العرب لا تكثر غسل ذلك لتركها غسل اليد عقيب الطعام فيجتمع في تلك الغضون وسخ فأمرهم رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بغسل البراجم (1) السابع تنظيف الرواجب (2) أمر رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم العرب بتنظيفها وهي رءوس الأنامل وما تحت الأظفار من الوسخ لأنها كانت لا يحضرها المقراض في كل وقت فتجتمع فيها أ
22:7.english: **The first** is what accumulates in the hair of the head of dirt and lice; cleansing from it is commendable (mustaḥabb) by washing, combing, and oiling, as a removal of dishevelment. The Messenger of God, peace be upon him, used to oil his hair and comb it every other day, and he commanded others to do so. He said, peace be upon him: "Oil your hair every other day." And he said, peace be upon him: "Whoever has hair, let him honor it" — that is, let him protect it from filth. A man entered upon him with disheveled hair and a tangled beard, and he said: "Did this man not have oil with which to settle his hair?" Then he said: "One of you enters as if he were a devil."
22:7.section_title_en: ** The Book of the Etiquette of Bathing and the Removal of Filth — Section 115

22:7.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'On Invocations and Supplications'

22:40.arabic: أهل الأرض التي يذكر فيها اسم الله تعالى كما تتراءى النجوم وقال سفيان بن عيينة رحمه الله إذا اجتمع قوم يذكرون الله تعالى اعتزل الشيطان والدنيا فيقول الشيطان للدنيا ألا ترين ما يصنعون فتقول الدنيا دعهم فإنهم إذا تفرقوا أخذت بأعناقهم إليك وعن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه أنه إذا دخل السوق وقال أراكم ههنا وميراث رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقسم في المسجد فذهب الناس إلى المسجد وتركوا السوق فلم يروا ميراثا فقالوا يا أبا هريرة ما رأينا ميراثا يقسم في المسجد قال فماذا رأيتم قالوا رأ
22:40.english: I say: The Messenger of God, may God's peace and blessings be upon him, said: "No people sit in an assembly wherein they remember God, Mighty and Majestic, except that the angels surround them, mercy overwhelms them, and God, Exalted is He, mentions them to those who are with Him." {«ما جلس قوم مجلسا يذكرون الله عز وجل إلا حفت بهم الملائكة وغشيتهم الرحمة وذكرهم الله تعالى فيمن عنده»} (1)
22:40.section_title_en: The Virtue of Assemblies of Remembrance (Majālis al-Dhikr)
22:40.anchors:
- Root: جلس (J-L-S)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning denotes sitting, but etymologically derives from seeking elevated, firm ground (jals) upon which to seat oneself; also signifies what is rugged and elevated from the lowland.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The root signifies the act of directing one's sitting place toward elevated ground; then generalized to any act of sitting (quʿūd). A majlis is any place where one sits. The term carries a sense of deliberate assembly and settled presence.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): physical sitting and companionship. Metaphorical (Majāz): "jalis nafsihi" — one who is a companion to himself, i.e., a recluse; also "jalasat al-rakhamah" (the vulture crouched). Here, the "majlis" is the locus of a spiritual gathering, not mere physical posture.
- Root: ذكر (Dh-K-R)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The tongue's utterance and the heart's presence; remembrance, invocation, and mention. It is the opposite of forgetfulness (nisyān) and also signifies honor and renown.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Remembrance (dhikr) is the presence of a thing in the mind, whether by utterance or by heart. It is graded: remembrance of God by the tongue, by the heart, and by both. The highest is when the heart is wholly present with God, which is the reality of dhikr.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: to mention, to recollect. Metaphorical: dhikr as the act of glorification and praise that elevates the servant. In the prophetic traditions below, "dhikr" is the collective act of praising God, reciting the Qur'an, and seeking His face.
- Root: حفف (Ḥ-F-F)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To surround, encompass, or encircle on all sides. A thing that encircles another is said to "ḥaffa" it.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Not explicitly listed, but the root implies comprehensive encircling, used here to denote the angels completely surrounding the assembly as a mark of honor and protection.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical encircling. Metaphorical: the encompassing of divine mercy and angelic presence, signifying total spiritual envelopment.
- Root: غشي (Gh-Sh-Y)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To cover, overwhelm, or envelop. It implies something that comes over a thing and covers it entirely, like night covering the day.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Not explicitly listed, but the root implies an overwhelming covering. Here, "ghashiyat-hum al-rahmah" means mercy overwhelms and covers them completely.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical covering. Metaphorical: the descent of mercy that envelops the hearts, leaving no part untouched.
- Root: سوع (S-W-')
  * Lisan / Ayn: Evil, corruption, or that which is displeasing and harmful. Its opposite is good (ḥusn).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Evil (sūʾ) is that which causes grief or harm, whether in this world or the next. It is the opposite of good (ḥusn).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: that which is bad. Metaphorical: "majālis al-sūʾ" — assemblies of evil, i.e., gatherings that lead to sin, heedlessness, and moral corruption.
- Root: ستح (S-Y-Ḥ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To travel, roam, or journey freely upon the earth. A "sāʾiḥ" is one who travels for worship or purpose.
  * Al-Raghib (Al-Mufradat): Not explicitly listed, but the root implies free movement. Here, angels "roaming" the earth signifies their mission to seek out assemblies of dhikr.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical travel. Metaphorical: the angels' ceaseless, purposeful movement across the earth in search of those who remember God.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Restriction and Focused Predication (al-ḥaṣr wa al-taqyīd bi-innamā) — The phrase "إلا حفت بهم الملائكة" (except that the angels surround them) uses the restrictive particle "illā" to negate any outcome other than the angels' encompassing and mercy's descent, affirming the exclusive, guaranteed reward for such assemblies. Also, the conditional constructions (mā... illā) establish a universal, binding correlation between the act of sitting in remembrance and the divine response.
22:40.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'On Invocations and Supplications'

22:40.arabic: وقال في قوله تعالى {ولولا دفع الله الناس بعضهم ببعض} قال بالرغبة والرهبة والحياء والمداراة وقالت عائشة رضي الله عنها استأذن رجل على رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال ائذنوا له فبئس رجل العشيرة هو فلما دخل ألان له القول حتى أن له عنده منزلة فلما خرج قلت له لما دخل قلت الذي قلت ثم ألنت له القول فقال يا عائشة إن شر الناس منزلة عند الله يوم القيامة من تركه الناس اتقاء فحشه (4) وفي الخبر ما وقى الرجل به عرضه فهو له صدقة (5) وفي الأثر خالطوا الناس بأعمالكم وزايلوهم بالقلوب وقال محمد بن الحن
22:40.english: A man defended him, and the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: "Whoever defends the honor of his brother shall have it as a shield for him against the Fire." (1)
22:40.anchors:
- Root: رد (r-d-d)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To return, repel, defend, avert; al-radd ʿan al-ʿirḍ is to repel defamation from one's honor
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Defense against false accusation; the theological nuance of divine recompense (al-mukāfaʾah) for defending a brother's honor
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal repulsion of physical harm extended metaphorically to verbal defense of honor (ḥaqīqah vs. majāz)
- Root: عطس (ʿ-t-s)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Sneezing; al-tashmīt is the invocation of mercy upon the sneezer
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The sneeze is attributed to God (min Allāh) as a sign of divine favor, while yawning is attributed to Satan
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): The response "yarḥamukallāh" is a supplication, not an assertion — distinguishing literal invocation from mere congratulation
- Root: عاد (ʿ-w-d)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To visit repeatedly; al-ʿiyādah is the visitation of the sick
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Returning to someone in his affliction; the reward is measured by the intensity of compassion shown
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): The "return" (ʿawd) is literal in visitation, but the reward is spiritual — a metaphorical extension of recompense
- Root: شيع (sh-y-ʿ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To accompany, follow; al-tashyīʿ is the funeral procession
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Following the bier with the intention of honoring the deceased and taking admonition (al-iʿtibār)
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): The qīrāṭ is a measure of reward — metaphorical weight, not literal coin
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Conditional Protasis (Bāb al-sharṭ) — The construction "man ... fa-..." (whoever does X, then Y) establishes a causal nexus requiring the apodosis to be a new sentence, often carrying the force of divine decree.

23:14.arabic: أسلمت سجد وجهي للذي خلقه وصوره وشق سمعه وبصره فتبارك الله أحسن الخالقين اللهم سجد لك سوادي وخيالي وآمن بك فؤادي أبوء بنعمتك علي وأبوء بذنبي وهذا ما جنيت على نفسي فاغفر لي فإنه لا يغفر الذنوب إلا أنت (5) أو تقول سبحان ربي الأعلى ثلاث مرات (6) فإذا فرغت من الصلاة فقل اللهم أنت السلام ومنك السلام تباركت يا ذا الجلال والإكرام (7) وتدعو بسائر الأدعية التي ذكرناها فإذا قمت من المجلس وأردت دعاء يكفر لغو المجلس فقل سبحانك اللهم وبحمدك أشهد أن لا إله إلا أنت أستغفرك وأتوب إليك عملت سوءا وظلمت نفسي فاغفر لي فإنه لا يغفر الذنوب إل
23:14.english: When you rise in the morning and hear the call to prayer (adhān), it is recommended for you to respond to the caller of prayer (mu'adhdhin) — and we have already mentioned this, along with the supplications for entering and leaving the privy, and the supplications of ablution (wuḍū'), in the Book of Purification. When you set out toward the mosque, say: "O Allah, place light (nūr) in my heart, and light in my tongue, and place light in my hearing, and place light in my sight, and place light behind me, and light before me, and place light above me. O Allah, grant me light." And also say: "O Allah, I ask You by the right of those who ask of You, and by the right of this my walking unto You — for I have not gone out in insolence, nor in vanity, nor for show, nor for reputation. I have gone out seeking protection from Your wrath and seeking Your good pleasure. So I ask You to deliver me from the Fire and to forgive me my sins — verily, none forgives sins but You."
23:14.section_title_en: Section 254 — Supplications for the Hours of Day and Night: From Dawn to Sleep
23:14.anchors:
- Root: ن و ر (n-w-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: النور: الضوء المنتشر الذي يُبصر به، وهو ضد الظلمة

  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): سجد حقيقة في وضع الجبهة، ومجاز في الخضوع والانقياد — وقوله "سجد لك سوادي وخيالي" من المجاز المرسل

23:14.arabic: الإنسان من سلالة من طين ثم جعلناه نطفة في قرار مكين إلى قوله ثم أنشأناه خلقا آخر أي نفخنا فيه الروح ثم تلا قوله تعالى في الآية وإذا الموءودة سئلت وإذا نظرت إلى ما قدمناه في طريق القياس والاعتبار ظهر لك تفاوت منصب علي وابن عباس رضي الله عنهما في الغوص على المعاني ودرك العلوم كيف وفي المتفق عليه في الصحيحين على جابر أنه قال كنا نعزل على عهد رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم والقرآن ينزل وفي لفظ آخر كنا نعزل فبلغ ذلك نبي الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فلم ينهنا (1) وفيه أيضا عن جابر أنه قال إن رجلا أتى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال إن لي
23:14.english: **The third:** Fear of excessive hardship (ḥaraj) due to the multitude of children, and guarding against the need for toil in earning a livelihood and entering into evil means of acquisition. This also is not prohibited, for the paucity of hardship assists one in religion. Indeed, perfection and excellence lie in trust in God (tawakkul) and confidence in God's guarantee, where He said: {«وما من دابة في الأرض إلا على الله رزقها»} "And there is no creature on earth but that upon Allah is its provision" [Hūd: 6]. Without doubt, in this [trust] there is a falling from the summit of perfection and an abandonment of what is more excellent — but looking to consequences and preserving wealth and storing it up, despite its contradicting tawakkul, we do not say it is prohibited.
23:14.section_title_en: ** On Coitus Interruptus ('Azl), Its Intentions, and the Etiquettes of Childbirth and Divorce
23:14.anchors:
**
- Root: عزل (ʿazl)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Separation, removal, setting aside
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Withdrawal to prevent conception
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical separation; Metaphorical: preventing pregnancy
- Root: وأد (waʾad)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Burying a female infant alive (pre-Islamic practice)
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The killing of daughters by burial
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: burial alive; Metaphorical: any prevention of life
- Root: طلق (ṭalaq)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Divorce; dissolution of marriage bond
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Legal dissolution of the marriage contract
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: releasing/loosing; Metaphorical: dissolution of marriage
- Sibawayh Rule: Conditional clauses with "فإن قلت" (objection-response dialectic structure)

23:86.arabic: العرش العظيم لا إله إلا الله رب السموات السبع ورب العرش الكريم (10) فإن أردت النوم فتوضأ أولا ثم توسد على يمينك مستقبل القبلة ثم كبر الله تعالى أربعا وثلاثين وسبحه ثلاثا وثلاثين واحمده ثلاثا وثلاثين (11) ثم قل اللهم إني أعوذ برضاك من سخطك وبمعافاتك من عقوبتك وأعوذ بك منك اللهم إني لا أستطيع أن أبلغ ثناء عليك ولو حرصت ولكن أنت كما أثنيت على نفسك (12) اللهم باسمك أحيا وأموت (13) اللهم رب السموات ورب الأرض ورب كل شيء ومليكه فالق الحب والنوى ومنزل التوراة والإنجيل والقرآن أعوذ بك من شر كل ذي شر و
23:86.english: When you rise in the morning and hear the call to prayer (adhān), it is recommended for you to respond to the caller of prayer (mu'adhdhin) — and we have already mentioned this, along with the supplications for entering and leaving the privy, and the supplications of ablution (wuḍū'), in the Book of Purification. When you set out toward the mosque, say: "O Allah, place light (nūr) in my heart, and light in my tongue, and place light in my hearing, and place light in my sight, and place light behind me, and light before me, and place light above me. O Allah, grant me light." And also say: "O Allah, I ask You by the right of those who ask of You, and by the right of this my walking unto You — for I have not gone out in insolence, nor in vanity, nor for show, nor for reputation. I have gone out seeking protection from Your wrath and seeking Your good pleasure. So I ask You to deliver me from the Fire and to forgive me my sins — verily, none forgives sins but You."

23:86.arabic: حين ينام وهو واضع خده على يده اليمنى وهو يرى أنه ميت في ليلته تلك اللهم رب السموات السبع ورب العرش العظيم ربنا ورب كل شيء ومليكه (2) الدعاء إلى آخره كما ذكرناه في كتاب الدعوات فحق على العبد أن يفتش عن ثلاثة عند نومه أنه على ماذا ينام وما الغالب عليه حب الله تعالى وحب لقائه أو حب الدنيا وليتحقق أنه يتوفى على ما هو الغالب عليه ويحشر على ما يتوفى عليه فإن المرء مع من أحب ومع ما أحب العاشر الدعاء عن التنبه فليقل في تيقظاته وتقلباته مهما تنبه ما كان يقوله رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لا إله إلا الله الواحد القهار رب السموات والأرض وما بينهما العزيز الغف
23:86.english: Then it is recommended, after the salutation of the witr, that he say: "Glory be to the King, the Most Holy, the Lord of the angels and the Spirit. You have enveloped the heavens and the earth with majesty and dominion. You have manifested Your might through power, and You have subdued the servants through death." It is related that he (peace and blessings be upon him) — until he died — most of his prayer was seated, except for the obligatory prayers (1). And he said to the one who prays seated: "Half the reward of the one who prays standing," and to the one who sleeps: "Half the reward of the one who prays seated" (2). This indicates the validity of the supererogatory prayer in all states.
23:86.section_title_en: The Fourth and Fifth Wirds (Portions of Night Devotion): On Sleep and the Final Sixth of the Night
23:86.anchors:
- Root: ليل (Layl)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Night; the period of darkness from sunset to dawn; its plural forms include layālī and layalāt.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Night is a divinely ordained sign (āyah) of Allah's power; sleep is described as a form of death (tawaffā) in the Qur'an, linking the nightly cycle to resurrection.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (haqīqah) for the astronomical night; metaphorical (majāz) for spiritual darkness or heedlessness.
- Root: نوم (Nawm)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Sleep; slumber; a state of rest.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Sleep is "death in a light form" (al-mawt al-khafīf), and death is "sleep in a heavy form" (al-nawm al-thaqīl). Allah says: {«Allah takes the souls at the time of their death, and those that die not during their sleep»} (Q. 39:42).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: bodily rest. Metaphorical: heedlessness (ghaflah) or spiritual inertia; "the market slept" means it stagnated.
- Root: عله (Alaha/Ilah)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To worship; to seek refuge; the root for ilāh (deity) and Allāh (the Supreme Deity).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The root denotes the act of devotion and the object of ultimate veneration; al-ulūhiyyah is the state of being worshipped.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: deity. Metaphorical: that which one is utterly devoted to or enslaved by (e.g., one's desires).
- Root: الي (Alā/Yalū)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To be occupied with; to manage; related to al-ālah (instrument) and ma'ālah (consequence).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The root conveys the idea of returning to a state or being entrusted with a matter; al-ālah is that by which one accomplishes an affair.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: instrumentality. Metaphorical: the means by which one draws near to Allah.
- Sibawayh Rule: Restriction and Focused Predication (al-Ḥaṣr wa al-Taqyīd bi-innamā) — Used to distinguish the specific legal scope of actions (e.g., the witr prayer's status) and to restrict general statements to their precise conditions.

25:61.arabic: النار تبارك الذي جعل في السماء بروجا وجعل فيها سراجا وقمرا منيرا وإذا سمعت صوت الرعد فقل سبحان من يسبح الرعد بحمده والملائكة من خيفته (7) فإن رأيت الصواعق فقل اللهم لا تقتلنا بغضبك ولا تهلكنا بعذابك وعافنا قبل ذلك (8) قاله كعب فإذا أمطرت السماء فقل اللهم سقيا هنيئا وصيبا نافعا (9) اللهم اجعله صيب رحمة ولا تجعله صيب عذاب (10) فإذا غضبت فقل اللهم اغفر لي ذنبي وأذهب غيظ قلبي وأجرني من الشيطان الرجيم (1) فإذا خفت قوما فقل اللهم إنا نجعلك في نحورهم ونعوذ بك من شرورهم (2) فإذا غزوت فقل اللهم أنت عضدي ونصيري و
25:61.english: When you rise in the morning and hear the call to prayer (adhān), it is recommended for you to respond to the caller of prayer (mu'adhdhin) — and we have already mentioned this, along with the supplications for entering and leaving the privy, and the supplications of ablution (wuḍū'), in the Book of Purification. When you set out toward the mosque, say: "O Allah, place light (nūr) in my heart, and light in my tongue, and place light in my hearing, and place light in my sight, and place light behind me, and light before me, and place light above me. O Allah, grant me light." And also say: "O Allah, I ask You by the right of those who ask of You, and by the right of this my walking unto You — for I have not gone out in insolence, nor in vanity, nor for show, nor for reputation. I have gone out seeking protection from Your wrath and seeking Your good pleasure. So I ask You to deliver me from the Fire and to forgive me my sins — verily, none forgives sins but You."
