27:32.arabic: يقول في الاستغفار اللهم اغفر لي خطيئتي وجهلي وإسرافي في أمري وما أنت أعلم به مني اللهم اغفر لي هزلي وجدي وخطئي وعمدي وكل ذلك عندي اللهم اغفر لي ما قدمت وما أخرت وما أسررت وما أعلنت وما أنت أعلم به مني أنت المقدم وأنت المؤخر وأنت على كل شيء قدير (1) وقال علي رضي الله عنه كنت رجلا إذا سمعت من رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم حديثا نفعني الله عز وجل بما شاء أن ينفعني منه وإذا حدثني أحد من أصحابه استحلفته فإذا حلف صدقته قال وحدثني أبو بكر وصدق أبو بكر رضي الله عنه قال سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول ما من عبد
27:32.english: God Most High said: {«والذين إذا فعلوا فاحشة أو ظلموا أنفسهم ذكروا الله فاستغفروا لذنوبهم»} — "And those who, when they commit an indecency or wrong themselves, remember God and seek forgiveness for their sins" {آل عمران/135}.
27:32.anchors:
- Root: ذنب (dhanb)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of "tail" or "taking hold of a tail"; extended to signify a sin as that which trails behind and follows a person.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الذنب في الأصل: الأخذ بذنب الشيء" — sin is that by which one is seized and held accountable; used metaphorically for a fault that clings to its perpetrator.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: tail of an animal. Metaphorical: "هو من الأذناب" — one who follows; sin as that which trails the soul and must be severed through repentance.
- Root: غفر (ghafara)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Covering, veiling, protecting from defilement; a shield or helmet (المغفر).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الغفران والمغفرة من الله هو أن يصون العبد من أن يمسه العذاب" — divine forgiveness is God's protection of the servant from being touched by punishment.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: to cover and protect. Metaphorical: God's "covering" of sins — not merely erasure, but active safeguarding of the sinner from consequence.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The frequent interposition of "يا رب" and vocative constructions between the subject and predicate in supplicatory sentences, as in "اللهم اغفر لي," where the vocative particle governs the imperative verb's addressee, reflecting the grammatical permissibility of separation between governing and governed elements in invocational speech.
27:32.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications, prayers, and their spiritual power, from 'On Invocations and Supplications'

28:16.arabic: الجبار (10) سبحانك اللهم وبحمدك لا إله إلا أنت عملت سوءا وظلمت نفسي فاغفر لي ذنبي إنك أنت ربي ولا يغفر الذنوب إلا أنت (11) اللهم ألهمني رشدي وقني شر نفسي (12) اللهم ارزقني حلالا لا تعاقبني عليه وقنعني بما رزقتني واستعملني به صالحا تقبله مني (1) اللهم إني أسألك العفو والعافية وحسن اليقين والمعافاة في الدنيا والآخرة (2) يا من لا تضره الذنوب ولا تنقصه المغفرة هب لي ما لا يضرك وأعطني ما لا ينقصك ربنا أفرغ علينا صبرا وتوفنا مسلمين أنت ولي في الدنيا والآخرة توفني مسلما وألحقني بالصالحين أنت ولينا فاغفر لنا وارح
28:16.english: And employ me in righteous deeds which You will accept from me. (1) O God, I ask You for pardon, well-being, good certainty, and soundness in this world and the next. (2) O You Whom sins do not harm and from Whom forgiveness does not diminish anything — grant me that which will not harm You, and give me that which will not diminish You. Our Lord, pour upon us patience and cause us to die as Muslims. You are our Protector in this world and the next; cause me to die as a Muslim and join me with the righteous. You are our Protector, so forgive us and have mercy upon us, and You are the Best of forgivers. And write for us good in this world and in the Hereafter — indeed, we have turned to You in repentance. Our Lord, upon You we rely, to You we turn in repentance, and to You is the final return. Our Lord, make us not a trial for the wrongdoing people. Our Lord, make us not a trial for those who disbelieve, and forgive us, our Lord — indeed, You are the Mighty, the Wise. Our Lord, forgive us our sins and our excesses in our affairs, make firm our feet, and grant us victory over the disbelieving people. Our Lord, forgive us and our brothers who preceded us in faith, and place not in our hearts any rancor toward those who believe — our Lord, indeed You are Kind, Merciful. Our Lord, grant us from Yourself mercy and prepare for us from our affair right guidance. Our Lord, give us good in this world and good in the Hereafter, and protect us from the chastisement of the Fire. Our Lord, indeed we have heard a caller calling to faith — to His saying, Mighty and Majestic: {«إنك لا تخلف الميعاد»} [آل عمران/ 194] — Our Lord, do not take us to task if we forget or err. Our Lord, to the end of the surah. (3) My Lord, forgive me and my parents, and have mercy upon them as they raised me when I was small; and forgive the believing men and the believing women, and the Muslim men and the Muslim women, the living among them and the dead. (4) My Lord, forgive, have mercy, and overlook what You know — and You are the Most Exalted, the Most Generous, the Best of the merciful, and the Best of the forgivers. And indeed, to God we belong and to Him we return; and there is no might and no power except through God, the Exalted, the Magnificent; and God suffices us, and He is the Best Disposer of affairs. And may God send blessings upon Muhammad, the Seal of the Prophets, and upon his family and his companions, and grant them abundant peace. (5)
28:16.section_title_en: Section 252 — Supplications for Morning and Evening: Comprehensive Prayers of the Prophet (ﷺ)
28:16.anchors:
- Root: لهم (l-h-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of swallowing/ingesting (iltihām); from this derives the sense of something being cast directly into the innermost recess of the heart (al-rawʿ).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الإلهام: إلقاء الشيء في الروع" — ilhām is the casting of a thing into the innermost consciousness, specifically from God or the higher assembly (al-malaʾ al-aʿlā). It is that which the Prophet (ﷺ) called "the touch of the angel" (limat al-malak) and "the breath of the Holy Spirit in my innermost heart" (nafth rūḥ al-qudus fī rawʿī).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): "ألهمه الله الخير: ألقاه في روعه" — God inspired him with good: He cast it into his innermost consciousness. Metaphorical (majāz): A horse that "swallows the ground" (yaltaḥimu al-arḍ) in swiftness; thus ilhām is the swift, direct ingress of divine guidance into the soul without intermediary effort.
- Root: حمد (ḥ-m-d)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The root denotes praise arising from recognition of voluntary excellence and beneficence; al-ḥamd is commendation of the beloved for their attributes and acts of goodness.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Praise (ḥamd) is the acknowledgment of beneficence (niʿmah) with reverence and love; it is distinguished from mere thanks (shukr) in that it is directed to the essence and attributes of the praised one, not solely to the benefit received.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "أحمد الله تعالى بجميع محامده" — I praise God with all His praiseworthy attributes. Metaphorical: "أحمدت صنيعه" — I found his deed praiseworthy; thus the tongue's praise must be matched by the heart's recognition of the praised one's perfection.
- Root: غفر (gh-f-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The root denotes covering and shielding; al-mighfar is the helmet that protects the head in battle.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الغفر: إلباس ما يصونه عن الدنس" — Forgiveness is the clothing of that which shields from filth. God's forgiveness (maghfirah) is His shielding of the servant from the touch of chastisement, covering the sin so that it is as though it never were.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "اللهم غفرًا" — O God, forgive. Metaphorical: The she-beasts that "did not forgive" their heedlessness (lam taghfir la-hā ghaflātuhā) — i.e., they did not shield their young from destruction; thus forgiveness is active protection, not mere erasure.
- Root: نفس (n-f-s)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The self, the soul; that which breathes and has vital spirit; also used for the very essence of a thing.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "النفس: الروح" — the soul is the spirit; and in God's saying {«ويحذركم الله نفسه»} [آل عمران/ 28], "His Self" means His very essence (dhāt), which — though grammatically expressed as an annexation implying distinction — is in reality identical, with no multiplicity in the Divine Essence.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "شيء نفيس" — a precious thing. Metaphorical: "دفق نفسه" — he poured out his blood/life; thus nafs is the seat of life, passion, and moral responsibility.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الدعاء والخبر (The Chapter of Supplication and Assertion) — Supplications (duʿāʾ) are grammatically constructed as optative sentences (inshāʾ ṭalabī) using the imperative (rabbighfir), the jussive (lā tuʾākhidhnā), and the vocative (rabbanā), yet they may embed assertive clauses (khabar) of praise (al-ḥamdu lillāh) and attestation (lā ilāha illā anta). The periodic structure of these prayers alternates between direct address to God (munādāh) and self-referential confession, requiring the translator to preserve the vocative force of "O God" and "Our Lord" without flattening into mere description.
28:16.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications, prayers, and their spiritual power, from 'On Invocations and Supplications'

28:16.arabic: استطعت أعوذ بك اللهم من شر ما صنعت ومن شر كل ذي شر اللهم إني ظلمت نفسي فاغفر لي ذنوبي فإنه لا يغفر الذنوب إلا أنت واهدني لأحسن الأخلاق فإنه لا يهدي لأحسنها إلا أنت واصرف عني سيئها فإنه لا يصرف سيئها إلا أنت لبيك وسعديك والخير كله بيديك أنا لك وإليك أستغفرك وأتوب إليك آمنت اللهم بما أرسلته من رسول وآمنت اللهم بما أنزلت من كتاب وصلى الله على محمد النبي الأمي وعلى آله وسلم تسليما كثيرا خاتم كلامي ومفتاحه وعلى أنبيائه ورسله أجمعين آمين يا رب العالمين اللهم أوردنا حوض محمد واسقنا بكأسه مشربا رويا سائغا هنيا لا نظمأ بعد
28:16.english: It is narrated that Yūnus ibn ʿUbayd saw a man in a dream — a man who had been killed as a martyr in the lands of the Byzantines — and he said to him: "What is the most excellent deed that you witnessed?" He replied: "I witnessed the glorifications (tasbīḥāt) of Ibn al-Muʿtamir holding a station with Allah, Mighty and Majestic." And they are these: "Glory be to Allah (subḥāna Allāh), and praise be to Allah (al-ḥamdu li-Allāh), and there is no god but Allah (lā ilāha illā Allāh), and Allah is the Greatest (Allāhu akbar), and there is no might and no power except through Allah, the Most High, the Magnificent — to the number of what He has created, and the number of what He is creating, and the weight of what He has created, and the weight of what He is creating, and the fill of what He has created, and the fill of what He is creating, and the fill of His heavens and the fill of His earth, and the like of that, and multiples of that, and the number of His creation, and the weight of His Throne, and the utmost extent of His mercy, and the ink of His words, and the limit of His good pleasure, until He is pleased, and when He is pleased, [then] the number of what His creation has remembered Him with in all that has passed, and the number of what they will remember Him with in what remains, in every year, and month, and Friday, and day, and night, and hour of the hours, and breath of the breaths, and age of the ages, from eternity to eternity — the eternity of this world and the eternity of the Hereafter — and more than that, whose beginning does not cease and whose end does not come to an end."
28:16.section_title_en: The Supplications of Ibn al-Muʿtamir (Sulaymān al-Taymī) and His Glorifications, and the Supplication of Ibrāhīm ibn Adham — May Allah Be Well Pleased with Them
28:16.anchors:
- Root: سبح (s-b-ḥ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of swift motion (in water or air); extended to the act of prayer and glorification.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "التسبيح: تنزيه الله تعالى. وأصله: المر السريع في عبادة الله تعالى" — Glorification is the declaration of Allah's transcendence; its root is the swift passage in worship of Allah.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "سبحت الله وسبحت له" — to declare Him transcendent. Metaphorical: "والنجوم تسبح في الفلك" — the stars glide in their orbits, a metaphor for their obedient motion.
- Root: حمد (ḥ-m-d)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of praise and commendation for a beneficial act.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Praise (ḥamd) is the acknowledgment of beneficence with reverence; it is due to Allah alone in His absolute perfection.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "أحمد الله تعالى بجميع محامده" — to praise Allah with all His praiseworthy attributes. Metaphorical: "أحمدت الأرض: رضيت سكناها" — to find a thing agreeable, extending praise to non-verbal contexts.
- Root: لهم (l-h-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of swift swallowing or devouring.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الإلهام: إلقاء الشيء في الروع" — Inspiration is the casting of a thing into the heart/mind (al-rawʿ), specifically from Allah or the higher assembly.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "ألهمه الله الخير: ألقاه في روعه" — Allah inspired him with good. Metaphorical: "جواد يلتهم الأرض" — a swift horse devours the ground, extending to rapid comprehension.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The permissibility of interposing elements between a preposition and its object when the clause remains grammatically sound, as seen in the extended supplicatory sentences.
28:16.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications, prayers, and their spiritual power, from 'On Invocations and Supplications'

28:16.arabic: أنفسهم لا تقنطوا من رحمة الله إن الله يغفر الذنوب جميعا إنه هو الغفور الرحيم وأنيبوا إلى ربكم أمرهم بالإنابة وقال تعالى وإني لغفار لمن تاب وآمن وعمل صالحا ثم اهتدى فإذا توقع المغفرة مع التوبة فهو راج وإن توقع المغفرة مع الإصرار فهو مغرور كما أن من ضاق عليه وقت الجمعة وهو في السوق فخطر له أن يسعى إلى الجمعة فقال له الشيطان إنك لا تدرك الجمعة فأقم على موضعك فكذب الشيطان ومر يعدو وهو يرجو أن يدرك الجمعة فهو راج وإن استمر على التجارة وأخذ يرجو تأخير الإمام للصلاة لأجله إلى وسط الوقت أو لأجل غيره أو لسبب من الأسباب التي لا يعر
28:16.english: Every soul shall taste what it has earned. And {«وَأَنَّ كُلَّ نَفْسٍ بِمَا كَسَبَتْ رَهِينَةٌ»} — "And that every soul is a pledge for what it has earned." So what has deluded you concerning God, after you have heard and comprehended? They will say: "Had we but listened or reasoned, we would not be among the companions of the Blaze." Thus they will confess their sin. So away with the companions of the Blaze!
28:16.section_title_en: The Anatomy of Hope (Rajā') and Delusion (Ghurūr): A Kalamic Dissection of the Soul's Two States
28:16.anchors:
- Root: نفس (Nafs)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The self, soul, or spirit; that which desires proximity and discourse; the locus of breath and life.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Nafs denotes the rūḥ (spirit) and, in divine attribution, the very Dhāt (Essence) of God—as in {«وَيُحَذِّرُكُمُ اللَّهُ نَفْسَهُ»}—entailing no real multiplicity despite grammatical annexation.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah) usage refers to the living, breathing self; metaphorical (Majaz) usage extends to "blood" (nafs sā'ilah) and the "evil eye" (nafs as 'ayn). Here, it signifies the moral agent bearing responsibility.
- Root: توب (Tawb)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Return, repentance; the act of turning back from error.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Tawbah is abandoning the sin in the most excellent manner—the third and highest form of excuse (after denial and pretext). In Sacred Law: forsaking the sin due to its ugliness, remorse for the past, resolve against recurrence, and restitution of what can be restored.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "The servant repents to God from his sin; God turns in mercy to the servant." The reciprocal dynamic—God's acceptance (tawbah) meeting the servant's return (inābah)—is operative in this text.
- Root: ذنب (Dhanb)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The tail of an animal; what trails behind; by extension, a fault or crime as the "consequence" one drags after oneself.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In origin, "taking hold of a thing's tail"—i.e., seizing the outcome. Sin is that which trails the soul and binds it as a pledge (rahīnah).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Metaphorical: "He is among the tails (adhnāb) of the people"—the laggards. The sinner is one who follows his lower tail, and the verse {«كُلُّ نَفْسٍ بِمَا كَسَبَتْ رَهِينَةٌ»} makes the soul a hostage to its own trailing deeds.
- Root: غفر (Ghafr)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To cover, shield, or protect; the Ghifār tribe's name; a helmet (mighfar) that shields the head.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Ghufrān from God is His shielding the servant from the touch of chastisement—a protective covering, not mere erasure. It may also mean outward forbearance.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "O God, forgive (ghufrānan)!"—a covering over the stain. Metaphorical: Zuhayr's beasts "did not forgive" their negligence—i.e., did not shield the offspring from destruction. Hope of forgiveness without repentance is thus not ghufrān but ghurūr (delusion).
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين العامل والمعمول (Interposition between Operator and Operand) — The periodic structure of verses like {«إِنَّ اللَّهَ يَغْفِرُ الذُّنُوبَ جَمِيعًا»} delays the predicate to heighten rhetorical impact; the conditional "if you say... know that" (fa-in qulta... fa-'lam) governs the entire dialectical sequence, requiring the apodosis to resolve the protasis with logical necessity.
28:16.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Fear and Hope'

28:30.arabic: رواه عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال إن الله تعالى يمجد نفسه كل يوم ويقول إني أنا الله رب العالمين إني أنا الله لا إله إلا أنا الحي القيوم إني أنا الله لا إله إلا أنا العلي العظيم إني أنا الله لا إله إلا أنا لم ألد ولم أولد إني أنا الله لا إله إلا أنا العفو الغفور إني أنا الله لا إله إلا أنا مبدىء كل شيء وإلي يعود العزيز الحكيم الرحمن الرحيم مالك يوم الدين خالق الخير والشر خالق الجنة والنار الواحد الأحد الفرد الصمد الذي لم يتخذ صاحبة ولا ولدا الفرد الوتر عالم الغيب والشهادة الملك القدوس السلام المؤمن المهيمن العزيز الجبار المتكبر
28:30.english: Muḥammad ibn Ḥassān said: Maʿrūf al-Karkhī — may God have mercy on him — said to me: "Shall I not teach you ten words — five for this world and five for the Hereafter? Whoever supplicates God — Mighty and Majestic — with them shall find God — Most High — present with them." I said: "Write them down for me." He said: "No, but I shall repeat them to you as Bakr ibn Khunays — may God have mercy on him — repeated them to me:
28:30.section_title_en: Section 249 — Supplications of the Righteous (Adʿiyat al-Ṣāliḥīn)
28:30.anchors:
- Root: حسب (ḥ-s-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of counting, reckoning, and sufficiency — "ḥasb" denotes that which suffices or is enough
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الحساب: استعمال العدد" — the theological nuance of ḥasbī Allāh ("God is my Sufficer") carries the sense of complete reliance upon God's reckoning and provision, transcending mere numerical counting to signify total trust in divine sufficiency
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): "حسب المال" (he counted the wealth); Metaphorical (majāz): "خرجا يتحسبان الأخبار" (they go out seeking news) — in the supplication "ḥasbī Allāh," the literal sense of "sufficiency" is intended, yet it carries the metaphorical extension of complete trust, as one who has God as his Sufficer has no need of any other reckoning

- Root: اله (ʾ-l-h)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of worship, devotion, and seeking refuge; "ilāh" denotes that which is worshipped
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الله: قيل: أصله إله فحذفت همزته، وأدخل عليها الألف واللام، فخص بالباري تعالى" — the name Allāh is the proper name of the Creator, distinguished from generic "ilāh" (any object of worship); in these supplications, the divine names invoked (al-Karīm, al-Ḥalīm, al-Qawī, al-Shadīd, al-Raḥīm, al-Raʾūf, al-Laṭīf, al-Qadīr) each specify particular attributes of the divine essence
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "فلان يتأله: يتعبد" (he worships); the supplications employ the divine names in their literal theological sense, each name invoking a specific attribute relevant to the particular need mentioned

- Root: انا (ʾ-n-y)
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "أنا ضمير المخبر عن نفسه" — the first-person pronoun; in the divine self-declaration "innī anā Allāh," the repetition emphasizes divine self-identification
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "أنى الطعام أي إدراكه" (the food ripened/reached its time) — the related sense of something reaching its appointed time appears in "عند المسألة في القبر" (at the questioning in the grave), indicating appointed moments of divine reckoning

- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The supplications employ repeated prepositional phrases (ʿinda al-mawt, ʿinda al-masʾalah, ʿinda al-ḥisāb, ʿinda al-mīzān, ʿinda al-ṣirāṭ) in parallel construction, each governing a distinct divine name, creating a rhythmic liturgical structure where each clause stands as an independent invocation

##
28:30.topic: Al-Ghazali on purifying the character, moral diseases, and spiritual remedies, from 'On Invocations and Supplications'

30:50.arabic: وهو مع ذلك قريب من كل موجود وهو أقرب إلى العبد من حبل الوريد وهو على كل شيء شهيد إذ لا يماثل قربه قرب الأجسام كما لا تماثل ذاته ذات الأجسام وأنه لا يحل في شيء ولا يحل فيه شيء تعالى عن أن يحويه مكان كما تقدس عن أن يحده زمان بل كان قبل أن خلق الزمان والمكان وهو الآن على ما عليه كان وأنه بائن عن خلقه بصفاته ليس في ذاته سواه ولا في سواه ذاته وأنه مقدس عن التغير والانتقال لا تحله الحوادث ولا تعتريه العوارض بل لا يزال في نعوت جلاله منزها عن الزوال وفي صفات كماله مستغنيا عن زيادة الاستكمال وأنه في ذاته معلوم الوجود بالعقول مرئ
30:50.english:
- **Root: خلق (khalaqa)**
  - *Lisan / Ayn:* Core meaning of measuring, proportioning, and fashioning; al-Khalil notes the root's application to the act of creation as bringing forth upon a measured determination.
  - *Al-Raghib (Mufradat):* "الخلق أصله: التقدير المستقيم" — Creation fundamentally signifies right/straight measurement; used for bringing into being from nothing (ibdāʿ) as in {خلق السماوات والأرض}, and for bringing forth from something as in {خلقكم من نفس واحدة}.
  - *Al-Zamakhshari (Asas):* Literal (ḥaqīqah): the craftsman's measuring before cutting. Metaphorical (majāz): "خلق الله الخلق: أوجده على تقدير أوجبته الحكمة" — God's creation is bringing into existence upon a measure necessitated by wisdom.
30:50.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'On Invocations and Supplications'

30:50.arabic: الأصل الأول العلم بأن صانع العالم قادر وأنه تعالى في قوله وهو على كل شيء قدير صادق لأن العالم محكم في صنعته مرتب في خلقته ومن رأى ثوبا من ديباج حسن النسج والتأليف متناسب التطريز والتطريف ثم توهم صدور نسجه عن ميت لا استطاعة له أو عن إنسان لا قدرة له كان منخلعا عن غريزة العقل ومنخرطا في سلك أهل الغباوة والجهل الأصل الثاني العلم بأنه تعالى عالم بجميع الموجودات ومحيط بكل المخلوقات لا يعزب عن علمه مثقال ذرة في الأرض ولا في السماء صادق في قوله وهو بكل شيء عليم ومرشد إلى صدقه بقوله تعالى ألا يعلم من خلق وهو اللطيف الخبير أرشدك
30:50.english: **The Eighth Principle: Knowledge that He, Exalted is He, is established upon His Throne (mustawin ʿalā ʿarshihi) in the sense that God, Exalted is He, intended by istiwāʾ — which is the sense that does not contradict the attribute of Majesty, nor does any mark of origination (ḥudūth) or passing away (fanāʾ) attach to it. And it is the sense intended by His saying — istiwāʾ toward the heaven — where He said in the Qur'an: {«ثُمَّ اسْتَوَىٰ إِلَى السَّمَاءِ وَهِيَ دُخَانٌ»} ("Then He directed Himself to the heaven, and it was smoke") [Fussilat 41:11]. And that is only by way of subjugation (qahr) and dominion (istīlāʾ), as the poet said:
30:50.section_title_en: The Revival of the Religious Sciences — Section 90: The Ten Principles Concerning Knowledge of the Divine Attributes
30:50.anchors:
- Root: ع ل م (ʿ-l-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root denoting the faculty of perception and comprehension; the mark or trace by which something is known.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "العلم: إدراك الشيء بحقيقته" — knowledge is the apprehension of a thing in its true reality, divided into apprehension of the essence and judgment upon it.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Distinguishes literal knowledge (ḥaqīqah) from awareness (shiʿr); here, it denotes certain, verified cognition of theological verities.
- Root: س و ي (s-w-y)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Root indicating straightness, equality, and levelness; from it derives istiwāʾ (establishing oneself upon, ascending to).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Istiwāʾ upon the Throne (al-ʿArsh) is a divine act of sovereign dominion, not corporeal settlement.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal sense of physical sitting is impossible for God; metaphorical sense (majāz) of qahr (overpowering) and istīlāʾ (dominion) is necessitated by reason and consensus.
- Root: ر أ ي (r-ʾ-y)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Visual perception; also opinion and discernment.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Ruʾyah (vision) of God in the Hereafter is a mode of disclosure (kashf) and knowledge (ʿilm), more complete than intellectual cognition, not conditioned by spatial direction.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal vision requires corporeality and direction; its application to God demands theological specification (takhṣīṣ) without nullifying the veracity of the scriptural promise.
- Root: ق د ر (q-d-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Power, measure, decree; the capacity to bring about an act.

30:50.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'On Invocations and Supplications'

33:7.arabic: فقال عز وجل وإذ أخذنا من النبيين ميثاقهم ومنك ومن نوح وإبراهيم الآية بأبي أنت وأمي يا رسول الله لقد بلغ من فضيلتك عنده أن أهل النار يودون أن يكونوا قد أطاعوك وهم بين أطباقها يعذبون يقولون يا ليتنا أطعنا الله وأطعنا الرسولا بأبي أنت وأمي يا رسول الله لئن كان موسى بن عمران أعطاه الله حجرا تنفجر منه الأنهار فماذا بأعجب من أصابعك حين نبع منها الماء صلى الله عليك بأبي أنت وأمي يا رسول الله لئن كان سليمان بن داود أعطاه الله الريح غدوها شهر ورواحها شهر فماذا بأعجب من البراق حين سريت عليه إلى السماء السابع
33:7.english: God Most High has said: {«Indeed, God and His angels send blessings upon the Prophet. O you who have believed, send blessings upon him and greet him with a greeting of peace»} (Q. 33:56). And it is related that he, peace be upon him, came one day with the signs of glad tidings visible upon his face, and he, peace be upon him, said: "Gabriel came to me, peace be upon him, and said: 'Are you not pleased, O Muhammad, that no one from your community sends a single blessing upon you except that I send ten blessings upon him, and no one from your community greets you with peace except that I greet him with peace ten times?'" (1) And he, peace be upon him, said: "Whoever sends blessings upon me, the angels send blessings upon him as long as he continues to send blessings upon me — so let him reduce or increase at that." (2) And he, peace be upon him, said: "The people most deserving of me are those who send the most blessings upon me." (3) And he, peace be upon him, said: "It suffices a believer for miserliness that I am mentioned in his presence and he does not send blessings upon me." (4) And he, peace be upon him, said: "Multiply your sending of blessings upon me on the day of Friday." (5) And he, peace be upon him, said: "Whoever sends blessings upon me from my community, ten good deeds are written for him and ten evil deeds are erased from him." (6) And he, peace be upon him, said: "Whoever says upon hearing the call to prayer and the iqāmah: 'O God, Lord of this perfect call and the established prayer, send blessings upon Muhammad, Your servant and Your Messenger, and grant him the means (al-wasīlah) and the excellence (al-faḍīlah) and the lofty rank (al-darajah al-rafīʿah) and the intercession (al-shafāʿah) on the Day of Resurrection' — my intercession becomes permissible for him." (7) And the Messenger of God, peace be upon him, said: "Whoever sends blessings upon me in a book, the angels continue to seek forgiveness for him as long as my name remains in that book." (8) And he, peace be upon him, said: "Indeed, upon the earth there are traveling angels who convey to me the greetings of peace from my community." (9) And he, peace be upon him, said: "No one greets me with peace except that God returns my soul to me until I respond to his greeting." (1) And it was said to him: "O Messenger of God, how do we send blessings upon you?" He said: "Say: 'O God, send blessings upon Muhammad, Your servant, and upon his family, his wives, and his descendants, as You sent blessings upon Abraham and the family of Abraham; and bless Muhammad, his wives, and his descendants, as You blessed Abraham and the family of Abraham. Indeed, You are Praiseworthy, Glorious.'" (2)

33:41.arabic: منه وقالوا كيف تعلم ذلك فقال إذا ذكرته ذكرني وقال تعالى اذكروا الله ذكرا كثيرا وقال تعالى فإذا أفضتم من عرفات فاذكروا الله عند المشعر الحرام واذكروه كما هداكم وقال عز وجل فإذا قضيتم مناسككم فاذكروا الله كذكركم آباءكم أو أشد ذكرا وقال تعالى الذين يذكرون الله قياما وقعودا وعلى جنوبهم وقال تعالى فإذا قضيتم الصلاة فاذكروا الله قياما وقعودا وعلى جنوبكم قال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما أي بالليل والنهار في البر والبحر والسفر والحضر والغنى والفقر والمرض والصحة والسر والعلانية وقال تعالى في ذم المنافقين ولا يذكرون الله إلا قليلا
33:41.english:
- Root: ذكر (dhakara)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning is "to remember, to mention, to recollect." The root carries the dual sense of mental recollection and verbal utterance. In Kitab al-Ayn, the root denotes the opposite of forgetfulness (nisyan), and its verbal form encompasses both the internal act of remembrance and the external act of mentioning.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الذكر: حضور المعنى في النفس، وقد يطلق على إبقاء المعنى باللسان. والذكر ضربان: ذكر بالقلب، وذكر باللسان. وقال تعالى: {فاذكروني أذكركم} [البقرة/152] — فذكر العبد ربه بالتعظيم والثناء، وذكر الله عبده بالإنعام والإكرام." The theological nuance distinguishes between the creature's remembrance (which is petition and praise) and the Creator's remembrance (which is response and reward).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): "ذكرت الشيء: حفظته ووعيته. وذكرت فلانا: جريت بذكره على لسانك." Metaphorical (Majaz): "ذكر الله العبد: أثنى عليه وأجزل له الثواب. ومن المجاز: قوله تعالى {ولذكر الله أكبر} — أي ذكر الله إياكم أعظم من ذكركم إياه." The rhetorical distinction is crucial here: when Allah "remembers" His servant, it is an act of grace, not cognition.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين المبتدأ والخبر (Interposition between Subject and Predicate) — In the verse {ولذكر الله أكبر}, the grammatical structure allows for the subject (ذكر الله) to be read as either the creature's remembrance of Allah or Allah's remembrance of the creature, with the predicate (أكبر) applying to whichever reading is adopted. This syntactic ambiguity is deliberate and productive of multiple valid interpretations.
33:41.topic: Al-Ghazali on constant remembrance of God and contemplative invocations, from 'On Invocations and Supplications'

33:41.arabic: وقد قال الله تعالى يا أيها الذين آمنوا أنفقوا من طيبات ما كسبتم ومما أخرجنا لكم من الأرض ولا تيمموا الخبيث منه تنفقون ولستم بآخذيه إلا أن تغمضوا فيه أي لا تأخذوه إلا مع كراهية وحياء وهو معنى الإغماض فلا تؤثروا به ربكم وفي الخبر سبق درهم مائة ألف درهم (3) وذلك بأن يخرجه الإنسان وهو من أحل ماله وأجوده فيصدر ذلك عن الرضا والفرح بالبذل وقد يخرج مائة ألف درهم مما يكره من ماله فيدل ذلك على أنه ليس يؤثر الله عز وجل بشيء مما يحبه وبذلك ذم الله تعالى قوما جعلوا لله ما يكرهون فقال تعال
33:41.english: The heart is not treated save with the compound electuary (maʿjūn) of knowledge and works. And this condition among the conditions of almsgiving runs in the same course as humility (al-khushūʿ) runs in the prayer. This is established by his saying — may Allah bless him and grant him peace: "A man has nothing of his prayer save that of which he was conscious." And this is like his saying — may Allah bless him and grant him peace: "Allah does not accept the charity of the one who bestows it with reproach (al-mannān)." And like His saying — Exalted is He: {«لا تبطلوا صدقاتكم بالمن والأذى»} ("Do not nullify your charities by reproach and injury"). As for the legal opinion (fatwā) of the jurist that the alms fall in their proper place and that one's liability is discharged without this condition — that is another discussion, and we have already pointed to its meaning in the Book of Prayer.
33:41.section_title_en: The Inner Conditions of Charity — Section 175 (From The Revival of the Religious Sciences, Book of the Mysteries of Almsgiving)
33:41.anchors:
- Root: قلب (q-l-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "To turn, overturn, transform a thing from one state to another; to rotate, to flip"
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "قلب الشيء: تصريفه وصرفه عن وجه إلى وجه" — the heart is so named because of its constant turning and transformation between states
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "قلب الشيء قلبا: حوله عن وجهه" (to turn a thing from its face). Metaphorical: "رجل قلب حول: يقلب الأمور ويحتال" — one who turns matters over and manages them; "قلبوا لك الأمور" (they turned matters against you)
- Root: وجل (w-j-l)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "Fear, dread, apprehension that strikes the heart"
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الوجل: استشعار الخوف" — the sensing of fear; cited in {«إنما المؤمنون الذين إذا ذكر الله وجلت قلوبهم»}
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "رجل وجل، وقوم وجال" — a fearful man, a fearful people; "وفي قلبه وجل" — in his heart is dread
- Root: عجب (ʿ-j-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "Wonder, amazement; self-admiration, vanity"
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Self-admiration (al-ʿujb) is a destructive spiritual ailment that nullifies deeds
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: wonder at something extraordinary. Metaphorical: self-conceit regarding one's own acts of obedience
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد (Restriction & Focused Predication) — governing the precise limitation of general categories (al-ṣifāt al-khāṣṣah within al-aṣnāf al-thamāniyyah) and the conditional structure of acceptance

33:56.arabic: وروى واثلة بن الأسقع أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال إن الله وملائكته يصلون على أصحاب العمائم يوم الجمعة (2) فإن أكربه الحر فلا بأس بنزعها قبل الصلاة وبعدها ولكن لا ينزع في وقت السعي من المنزل إلى الجمعة ولا في وقت الصلاة ولا عند صعود الإمام المنبر وفي خطبته الرابع البكور إلى الجامع ويستحب أن يقصد الجامع من فرسخين وثلاث وليبكر ويدخل وقت البكور بطلوع الفجر وفضل البكور عظيم وينبغي أن يكون في سعيه إلى الجمعة خاشعا متواضعا ناويا للاعتكاف في المسجد إلى وقت الصلاة قاصدا للمبادرة إلى جواب نداء الله عز وجل إلى الجمعة إياه والمسا
33:56.english: Ibn Masʿūd said: "Whoever trims his nails on Friday, God—mighty and majestic is He—brings forth from him an ailment and brings into him a healing." And if he has entered the bathhouse on Thursday or Wednesday, then the intended purpose has been achieved.
33:56.topic: Al-Ghazali on purifying the character, moral diseases, and spiritual remedies, from 'Mysteries of Prayer'

33:66.arabic: نار جهنم دعا ويوم يسحبون فى النار على وجوههم ويوم تقلب وجوههم فى النار ويوم لا يجزى والد عن ولده ويوم يفر المرء من أخيه وأمه وأبيه ويوم لا ينطقون ولا يؤذن لهم فيعتذرون يوم لا مرد له من الله يوم هم بارزون ويوم هم على النار يفتنون يوم لا ينفع مال ولا بنون يوم لا ينفع الظالمين معذرتهم ولهم اللعنة ولهم سوء الدار يوم ترد فيه المعاذير وتبلى السرائر وتظهر الضمائر وتكشف الأستار يوم تخشع فيه الأبصار وتسكن الأصوات ويقل فيه الالتفات وتبرز الخفيات وتظهر الخطيئات يوم يساق العباد ومعهم الأشهاد ويشيب الصغير ويسكر الكبير فيومئذ
33:66.english: So prepare yourself, O wretched one, for this Day of immense magnitude, of prolonged duration, of overwhelming dominion, whose appointed time is near — a Day when you shall see the heaven split asunder, and the stars scattered in its terror, and the shining planets extinguished, and the sun folded up, and the mountains set in motion, and the pregnant camels neglected, and the wild beasts gathered together, and the seas set ablaze, and the souls paired with their bodies, and the Hellfire ignited, and Paradise brought near, and the mountains pulverized, and the earth stretched out — a Day when you shall see the earth shaken with its quaking, and the earth casts forth its burdens. On that Day shall people issue forth in scattered groups to be shown their deeds — a Day when the earth and the mountains are lifted and crushed with a single crushing. Then on that Day the Imminent Event shall come to pass, and the heaven shall split open, for on that Day it shall be frail, and the angels shall be at its edges, and eight shall bear the Throne of your Lord above them on that Day. On that Day you shall be presented — no secret of yours shall remain hidden. A Day when the mountains shall move and you shall see the earth laid bare — a Day when the earth shall be shaken with a violent shaking, and the mountains crumbled to dust, becoming scattered particles — a Day when people shall be like scattered moths, and the mountains like carded wool — a Day when every nursing mother shall forget what she nursed, and every pregnant female shall cast down her burden, and you shall see people drunk, yet they are not drunk, but the chastisement of God is severe — a Day when the earth shall be changed to other than this earth, and the heavens, and they shall appear before God, the One, the All-Compelling — a Day when the mountains shall be blown away as dust, leaving a level, bare plain, wherein you see no crookedness nor curve — a Day when you see the mountains and suppose them solid, yet they pass by like the passing of clouds — a Day when the heaven shall split open and become rosy like molten oil. Then on that Day no human nor jinn shall be asked about his sin. A Day when the disobedient shall be prevented from speech, and shall not be asked about their crimes, but shall be seized by their forelocks and their feet — a Day when every soul shall find what it did of good brought forth present, and what it did of evil, wishing that between it and that evil there were a far distance — a Day when every soul shall know what it has sent ahead, and shall witness what it has forwarded and what it has left behind — a Day when tongues shall be struck mute and the bodily members shall speak — a Day whose mention turned the hair of the Master of the Messengers white, when al-Ṣiddīq (may God be pleased with him) said to him: "I see that you have turned white-haired, O Messenger of God." He said: "Sūrat Hūd and its sisters have made me white-haired" — namely, al-Wāqiʿah, al-Mursalāt, ʿAmma Yatasāʾalūn, and Idhā al-Shamsu Kuwwirat.
33:66.section_title_en: The Names and Attributes of the Day of Resurrection — An Exhortation to the Negligent
33:66.anchors:
- Root: يوم (yawm)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "اليوم: وقت طلوع الشمس إلى غروبها، وقد يعبر به عن مدة من الزمان أي مدة كانت" — the day as a temporal span, extended metaphorically to any epoch or era.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "اليوم يعبر به عن وقت طلوع الشمس إلى غروبها. وقد يعبر به عن مدة من الزمان أي مدة كانت" — theological usage denotes the appointed time of reckoning, magnified by divine attribution (أيام الله).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): a measured solar period. Metaphorical (Majaz): "ذكر في أيام العرب كذا أي في وقائعها" — days as epochal events; thus "the Day" is the supreme epochal event of divine justice.
- Root: نفس (nafs)
  * Lisan / Ayn: النفس: الروح والذات — the self, soul, or very essence.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "النفس: الروح... وقوله: ويحذركم الله نفسه فنفسه: ذاته" — nafs as the innermost reality of a being; in the eschatological context, souls are "paired" (زوجت) with bodies for judgment.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the soul as life-principle. Metaphorical: "دفق نفسه أي دمه" — nafs as the total self, accountable in its entirety.
- Root: ارض (arḍ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: الأرض: الجرم المقابل للسماء — the earth as the corporeal substratum beneath the heavens.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الأرض: الجرم المقابل للسماء... ويعبر بها عن أسفل الشيء" — the earth as the lowest register of creation, subject to total transformation on that Day.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the physical earth. Metaphorical: "تأرض فلان: لزم الأرض" — to cling low; on that Day the earth itself is leveled, flattened, and replaced.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد (Restriction & Focused Predication) — The repeated "يوم" clauses function as temporal restrictors (ẓurūf) binding each predicate to that single, all-encompassing moment; the accumulation of names (أسامي) serves not as mere repetition but as focused predication upon the multifarious realities of a single event.
33:66.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Remembrance of Death and Afterlife'

33:66.arabic: يكونوا قد أطاعوك وهم بين أطباقها يعذبون يقولون يا ليتنا أطعنا الله وأطعنا الرسولا بأبي أنت وأمي يا رسول الله لئن كان موسى بن عمران أعطاه الله حجرا تنفجر منه الأنهار فماذا بأعجب من أصابعك حين نبع منها الماء صلى الله عليك بأبي أنت وأمي يا رسول الله لئن كان سليمان بن داود أعطاه الله الريح غدوها شهر ورواحها شهر فماذا بأعجب من البراق حين سريت عليه إلى السماء السابعة ثم صليت الصبح من ليلتك بالأبطح صلى الله عليك بأبي أنت وأمي يا رسول الله لئن كان عيسى بن مريم أعطاه الله إحياء الموتى فماذا بأعجب من الشاة المسمومة حين كلمتك وهي
33:66.english: God Most High has said: {«Indeed, God and His angels send blessings upon the Prophet. O you who have believed, send blessings upon him and greet him with a greeting of peace»} (Q. 33:56). And it is related that he, peace be upon him, came one day with the signs of glad tidings visible upon his face, and he, peace be upon him, said: "Gabriel came to me, peace be upon him, and said: 'Are you not pleased, O Muhammad, that no one from your community sends a single blessing upon you except that I send ten blessings upon him, and no one from your community greets you with peace except that I greet him with peace ten times?'" (1) And he, peace be upon him, said: "Whoever sends blessings upon me, the angels send blessings upon him as long as he continues to send blessings upon me — so let him reduce or increase at that." (2) And he, peace be upon him, said: "The people most deserving of me are those who send the most blessings upon me." (3) And he, peace be upon him, said: "It suffices a believer for miserliness that I am mentioned in his presence and he does not send blessings upon me." (4) And he, peace be upon him, said: "Multiply your sending of blessings upon me on the day of Friday." (5) And he, peace be upon him, said: "Whoever sends blessings upon me from my community, ten good deeds are written for him and ten evil deeds are erased from him." (6) And he, peace be upon him, said: "Whoever says upon hearing the call to prayer and the iqāmah: 'O God, Lord of this perfect call and the established prayer, send blessings upon Muhammad, Your servant and Your Messenger, and grant him the means (al-wasīlah) and the excellence (al-faḍīlah) and the lofty rank (al-darajah al-rafīʿah) and the intercession (al-shafāʿah) on the Day of Resurrection' — my intercession becomes permissible for him." (7) And the Messenger of God, peace be upon him, said: "Whoever sends blessings upon me in a book, the angels continue to seek forgiveness for him as long as my name remains in that book." (8) And he, peace be upon him, said: "Indeed, upon the earth there are traveling angels who convey to me the greetings of peace from my community." (9) And he, peace be upon him, said: "No one greets me with peace except that God returns my soul to me until I respond to his greeting." (1) And it was said to him: "O Messenger of God, how do we send blessings upon you?" He said: "Say: 'O God, send blessings upon Muhammad, Your servant, and upon his family, his wives, and his descendants, as You sent blessings upon Abraham and the family of Abraham; and bless Muhammad, his wives, and his descendants, as You blessed Abraham and the family of Abraham. Indeed, You are Praiseworthy, Glorious.'" (2)
33:66.section_title_en: Section 244 — On the Virtues of Invoking Blessings upon the Prophet (Ṣalawāt) and the Excellence of His Rank
33:66.anchors:
- Root: صلو (Ṣ-L-W)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root denotes prayer, blessing, supplication; al-ṣalāh from God is mercy (raḥmah), from angels is seeking forgiveness (istighfār), from believers is supplication (duʿā').
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-ṣalāh from God is pure mercy and beneficence; from angels it is their petition for forgiveness; from humans it is humble supplication. The divine ṣalāh upon the Prophet is an elevation of his mention and an increase in his honor.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): supplication and bending in worship. Metaphorical (majāz): God's ṣalāh upon the Prophet is His mercy and His exaltation of him before the angels; the believers' ṣalāh is their invocation and reverence.
- Root: سلم (S-L-M)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Root denotes safety, peace, deliverance; taslīm is the greeting of peace and submission.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Salām from God is His safeguarding; the greeting of salām upon the Prophet is an acknowledgment of his prophetic rank and a prayer for his perfect safety.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: greeting of peace. Metaphorical: the angels' conveyance of the believers' salām to the Prophet even after his death, indicating the enduring bond.
- Root: حمد (Ḥ-M-D)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root denotes praise, commendation; maḥmūd is the one praised.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Ḥamd is praise for voluntary beneficence; al-ḥamd li-Llāh encompasses all praise due to God's perfect attributes.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: to praise for good. Metaphorical: to find praiseworthy (aḥmadtu al-arḍ: I found the land agreeable).
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Interposition (al-faṣl bayna al-jār wa al-majrūr) — The periodic structure of the ḥadīth reports here follows the canonical pattern of embedding quoted speech within narrative frames, maintaining syntactic cohesion across multiple levels of reported discourse.
33:66.topic: Al-Ghazali on the journey of the soul, death, and the Hereafter, from 'On Invocations and Supplications'

33:66.arabic: وقال صالح المري قرأت على رجل من المتعبدين {يوم تقلب وجوههم في النار يقولون يا ليتنا أطعنا الله وأطعنا الرسولا} فصعق ثم أفاق فقال زدني يا صالح فإني أجد غما فقرأت {كلما أرادوا أن يخرجوا منها أعيدوا فيها} فخر ميتا وروى أن زرارة بن أبي أوفى صلى بالناس الغداة فلما قرأ {فإذا نقر في الناقور} خر مغشيا عليه فحمل ميتا ودخل يزيد الرقاشي على عمر بن عبد العزيز فقال عظني يا يزيد فقال يا أمير المؤمنين اعلم أنك لست أول خليفة يموت فبكى ثم قال زدني قال يا أمير المومنين ليس بينك وبين آدم أب إلا ميت فبكى ثم قال زدني يا يزيد فقال يا أمير المؤمنين ليس بينك وبين الجنة والنار منزل فخر مغ
33:66.english: Al-Ḥasan [al-Baṣrī] passed by a young man who was completely absorbed in his laughter, sitting with a group of people in a gathering. Al-Ḥasan said to him: "O young man, have you crossed the Ṣirāṭ [the Bridge]?" He said: "No." He said: "Then do you know whether you will go to Paradise or to the Fire?" He said: "No." He said: "Then what is this laughter?" He said: "And that young man was never seen laughing after that."
33:66.section_title_en: The States of Fear and the Severity of Khawf — Accounts of the Early Pious (Section 1062)
33:66.anchors:
- Root: ضحك (Ḍaḥika)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning is laughter, arising from a state of heedlessness or joy; its opposite is weeping (bukā') which accompanies khashyah.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Laughter is a human accident (ʿaraḍ) indicating the heart's occupation with worldly pleasure, contra the state of the God-fearing whose hearts are preoccupied with divine threat.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) for audible laughter; metaphorical (majāz) for the soul's levity and forgetfulness of the reckoning.
- Root: خوف (Khawf)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Fear, dread, anxiety of anticipated harm; in the Kalam context, it is the soul's perturbation due to probable punishment.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Khawf is distinguished from khashyah — khashyah is specific to knowledge-based fear of Allah's majesty, while khawf is broader; here, the accounts blend both as the engine of righteous action.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal for fear of a known threat; metaphorical for the "fear" that severs the liver (qataʿa al-kabid), i.e., a spiritual state overwhelming the corporeal frame.
- Root: أمن (Amn)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Security, safety, freedom from fear; its root denotes tranquility of heart.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Amn is the cessation of fear, which in this world is only proper for the prophets and angels in specific contexts; for the sinner, it is a delusion (ghurūr).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal for physical safety; metaphorical for spiritual complacency, which is blameworthy — as in the saying of Ḥammād: "That is the sitting of the secure one."
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Restriction with إنما (Innamā) — as in "إنما جعل الله هذه الغفلة" and "إنما أغبط من لم يخلق" — where the predicate is restricted to the subject, emphasizing exclusive causation or exclusive object of envy, per the canonical pattern of ḥaṣr.
33:66.topic: Al-Ghazali on the journey of the soul, death, and the Hereafter, from 'Fear and Hope'

34:2.arabic: الأرض وما يخرج منها وما ينزل من السماء وما يعرج فيها ومن فتن الليل والنهار ومن طوارق الليل والنهار إلا طارقا يطرق بخير يا رحمن فقال ذلك فطفئت شعلته وخر على وجهه (1) وقال الحسن نبئت أن جبرائيل عليه السلام أتى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال إن عفريتا من الجن يكيدك فإذا أويت إلى فراشك فاقرأ آية الكرسي // حديث الحسن نبئت أن جبريل أتى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال إن عفريتا من الجن يكيدك الحديث أخرجه ابن أبي الدنيا في مكايد الشيطان هكذا مرسلا وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم أتاني الشيطان فنازعني ثم نازع
34:2.english: If you say: "What then is the remedy for repelling Satan, and is the remembrance of God—exalted is He—and one's saying 'There is no might and no power except through God' (lā ḥawla wa lā quwwata illā billāh) sufficient for that?" — Know that the remedy of the heart in this matter is to seal these entry points by purifying the heart of these blameworthy traits. And that is something whose full exposition would be lengthy; our purpose in this quarter of the book is to explain the remedy for the destructive traits (al-ṣifāt al-muhlikāt), and each trait requires a separate book, as will be explained later. Yes — when the roots of these traits are severed from the heart, Satan may still make incursions (ijtiyāzāt) and pass through it with fleeting thoughts (khaṭarāt), but he has no stability therein. And what prevents him from passing through is the remembrance of God—exalted is He—because the reality of dhikr cannot take firm hold of the heart except after the heart is built up with God-consciousness (taqwā) and purified of blameworthy traits. Otherwise, the dhikr is but the whisper of the self (ḥadīth nafs), having no authority over the heart, and so it does not repel the dominion of Satan. For this reason, God—exalted is He—said: {إِنَّ الَّذِينَ اتَّقَوْا إِذَا مَسَّهُمْ طَائِفٌ مِنَ الشَّيْطَانِ تَذَكَّرُوا فَإِذَا هُمْ مُبْصِرُونَ} "Indeed, those who fear God — when an impulse touches them from Satan, they remember [Him], and at once they are insightful" (Q 7:201). He specified thereby the God-fearing (muttaqī).
34:2.section_title_en: The Revival of the Religious Sciences — Section 603: On the Remedy for Evil Presumption and the Repelling of Satan
34:2.anchors:
- Root: شيط (Shayṭ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of burning, scorching, or being consumed by fire; also used for one who is destroyed or whose blood is shed in vain.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): الشيطان (Satan) — the one who is far removed from divine mercy, derived from the root indicating his being burned or destroyed.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): "شاط اللحم" — meat that is burnt or spoiled by fire. Metaphorical (Majaz): "شاط دمه" — his blood was shed in vain (i.e., destroyed); "أشاط السلطان دمه" — the ruler declared his blood lawful to shed. Thus, Satan is so named for his being "burned" or "destroyed" by divine curse, and for his causing others to be destroyed.
- Root: قلب (Qalb)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The heart; also the act of turning, overturning, or revolving a thing from one state to another.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "قلب الشيء: تصريفه وصرفه عن وجه إلى وجه" — the turning and directing of a thing from one aspect to another. The heart (qalb) is so named for its constant fluctuation and turning between states.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "قلب الشيء قلبا: حوله عن وجهه" — to turn a thing from its face. Metaphorical: "رجل قلب حول: يقلب الأمور ويحتال" — a man who turns matters over and devises stratagems. The heart's "suwaydāʾ" (core/blackness) is its innermost center where Satan seeks to establish his seat.
- Root: ذكر (Dhikr)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Remembrance, mention, recollection; the opposite of forgetfulness (nisyān).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): الذكر is the presence of a thing in the mind, whether by utterance or by heart; true dhikr is that which takes root in the heart, not mere speech of the tongue.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: uttering with the tongue. Metaphorical: the heart's presence with God, which alone has authority over the soul and repels Satan's incursions.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — The verse {إِنَّ الَّذِينَ اتَّقَوْا إِذَا مَسَّهُمْ طَائِفٌ مِنَ الشَّيْطَانِ تَذَكَّرُوا} restricts the efficacy of dhikr in repelling Satan to the God-fearing (muttaqūn), whose hearts are emptied of passions, thereby specifying the condition for its effectiveness.
34:2.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'On Invocations and Supplications'

34:2.arabic: أعوذ بكلمات الله التامات التي لا يجاوزهن بر ولا فاجر من شر ما يلج في الأرض وما يخرج منها وما ينزل من السماء وما يعرج فيها ومن فتن الليل والنهار ومن طوارق الليل والنهار إلا طارقا يطرق بخير يا رحمن فقال ذلك فطفئت شعلته وخر على وجهه (1) وقال الحسن نبئت أن جبرائيل عليه السلام أتى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال إن عفريتا من الجن يكيدك فإذا أويت إلى فراشك فاقرأ آية الكرسي // حديث الحسن نبئت أن جبريل أتى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال إن عفريتا من الجن يكيدك الحديث أخرجه ابن أبي الدنيا في مكايد الشيطان هكذا مرسلا وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم أتاني الشيطان فنازعني ثم نازعني فأخذت

And that is something whose full exposition would be lengthy; our purpose in this quarter of the book is to explain the remedy for the destructive traits (al-ṣifāt al-muhlikāt), and each trait requires a separate book, as will be explained later. Yes — when the roots of these traits are severed from the heart, Satan may still make incursions (ijtiyāzāt) and pass through it with fleeting thoughts (khaṭarāt), but he has no stability therein. And what prevents him from passing through is the remembrance of God—exalted is He—because the reality of dhikr cannot take firm hold of the heart except after the heart is built up with God-consciousness (taqwā) and purified of blameworthy traits. Otherwise, the dhikr is but the whisper of the self (ḥadīth nafs), having no authority over the heart, and so it does not repel the dominion of Satan. For this reason, God—exalted is He—said: {إِنَّ الَّذِينَ اتَّقَوْا إِذَا مَسَّهُمْ طَائِفٌ مِنَ الشَّيْطَانِ تَذَكَّرُوا فَإِذَا هُمْ مُبْصِرُونَ} "Indeed, those who fear God — when an impulse touches them from Satan, they remember [Him], and at once they are insightful" (Q 7:201). He specified thereby the God-fearing (muttaqī).
