##
40:60.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'Condemnation of Pride and Conceit'

41:51.arabic: حاجة وإرهاق ملمة فإن الإنسان إذا مسه الشر فذو دعاء عريض فالحاجة تحوج إلى الدعاء والدعاء يرد القلب إلى الله عز وجل بالتضرع والاستكانة فيحصل به الذكر الذي هو أشرف العبادات ولذلك صار البلاء موكلا بالأنبياء عليهم السلام ثم الأولياء ثم الأمثل فالأمثل لأنه يرد القلب بالافتقار والتضرع إلى الله عز وجل ويمنع من نسيانه وأما الغنى فسبب للبطر في غالب الأمور فإن الإنسان ليطغى أن رآه استغنى فهذا ما أردنا أن نورده من جملة الأذكار والدعوات والله الموفق للخير وأما بقية الدعوات في الأكل والسفر وعيادة المريض وغيره
41:51.english: "O God, whatever blessing has come to me this morning, or to any of Your creatures, it is from You alone, with no partner to You; to You is praise and to You is thanksgiving."
41:51.topic: Al-Ghazali on constant remembrance of God and contemplative invocations, from 'On Invocations and Supplications'

42:9.arabic: وهو مع ذلك قريب من كل موجود وهو أقرب إلى العبد من حبل الوريد وهو على كل شيء شهيد إذ لا يماثل قربه قرب الأجسام كما لا تماثل ذاته ذات الأجسام وأنه لا يحل في شيء ولا يحل فيه شيء تعالى عن أن يحويه مكان كما تقدس عن أن يحده زمان بل كان قبل أن خلق الزمان والمكان وهو الآن على ما عليه كان وأنه بائن عن خلقه بصفاته ليس في ذاته سواه ولا في سواه ذاته وأنه مقدس عن التغير والانتقال لا تحله الحوادث ولا تعتريه العوارض بل لا يزال في نعوت جلاله منزها عن الزوال وفي صفات كماله مستغنيا عن زيادة الاستكمال وأنه في ذاته معلوم الوجود بالعقول مرئ
42:9.english:
- **Root: خلق (khalaqa)**
  - *Lisan / Ayn:* Core meaning of measuring, proportioning, and fashioning; al-Khalil notes the root's application to the act of creation as bringing forth upon a measured determination.
  - *Al-Raghib (Mufradat):* "الخلق أصله: التقدير المستقيم" — Creation fundamentally signifies right/straight measurement; used for bringing into being from nothing (ibdāʿ) as in {خلق السماوات والأرض}, and for bringing forth from something as in {خلقكم من نفس واحدة}.
  - *Al-Zamakhshari (Asas):* Literal (ḥaqīqah): the craftsman's measuring before cutting. Metaphorical (majāz): "خلق الله الخلق: أوجده على تقدير أوجبته الحكمة" — God's creation is bringing into existence upon a measure necessitated by wisdom.
42:9.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'On Invocations and Supplications'

42:9.arabic: الأصل الأول العلم بأن صانع العالم قادر وأنه تعالى في قوله وهو على كل شيء قدير صادق لأن العالم محكم في صنعته مرتب في خلقته ومن رأى ثوبا من ديباج حسن النسج والتأليف متناسب التطريز والتطريف ثم توهم صدور نسجه عن ميت لا استطاعة له أو عن إنسان لا قدرة له كان منخلعا عن غريزة العقل ومنخرطا في سلك أهل الغباوة والجهل الأصل الثاني العلم بأنه تعالى عالم بجميع الموجودات ومحيط بكل المخلوقات لا يعزب عن علمه مثقال ذرة في الأرض ولا في السماء صادق في قوله وهو بكل شيء عليم ومرشد إلى صدقه بقوله تعالى ألا يعلم من خلق وهو اللطيف الخبير أرشدك
42:9.english: **The Eighth Principle: Knowledge that He, Exalted is He, is established upon His Throne (mustawin ʿalā ʿarshihi) in the sense that God, Exalted is He, intended by istiwāʾ — which is the sense that does not contradict the attribute of Majesty, nor does any mark of origination (ḥudūth) or passing away (fanāʾ) attach to it. And it is the sense intended by His saying — istiwāʾ toward the heaven — where He said in the Qur'an: {«ثُمَّ اسْتَوَىٰ إِلَى السَّمَاءِ وَهِيَ دُخَانٌ»} ("Then He directed Himself to the heaven, and it was smoke") [Fussilat 41:11]. And that is only by way of subjugation (qahr) and dominion (istīlāʾ), as the poet said:
42:9.section_title_en: The Revival of the Religious Sciences — Section 90: The Ten Principles Concerning Knowledge of the Divine Attributes
42:9.anchors:
- Root: ع ل م (ʿ-l-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root denoting the faculty of perception and comprehension; the mark or trace by which something is known.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "العلم: إدراك الشيء بحقيقته" — knowledge is the apprehension of a thing in its true reality, divided into apprehension of the essence and judgment upon it.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Distinguishes literal knowledge (ḥaqīqah) from awareness (shiʿr); here, it denotes certain, verified cognition of theological verities.
- Root: س و ي (s-w-y)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Root indicating straightness, equality, and levelness; from it derives istiwāʾ (establishing oneself upon, ascending to).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Istiwāʾ upon the Throne (al-ʿArsh) is a divine act of sovereign dominion, not corporeal settlement.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal sense of physical sitting is impossible for God; metaphorical sense (majāz) of qahr (overpowering) and istīlāʾ (dominion) is necessitated by reason and consensus.
- Root: ر أ ي (r-ʾ-y)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Visual perception; also opinion and discernment.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Ruʾyah (vision) of God in the Hereafter is a mode of disclosure (kashf) and knowledge (ʿilm), more complete than intellectual cognition, not conditioned by spatial direction.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal vision requires corporeality and direction; its application to God demands theological specification (takhṣīṣ) without nullifying the veracity of the scriptural promise.
- Root: ق د ر (q-d-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Power, measure, decree; the capacity to bring about an act.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Divine power (qudrah) is the negation of incapacity (ʿajz); absolute power belongs to God alone, while creatures possess limited capacity.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal power over an object; metaphorically, God's power encompasses all things without exertion or instrument.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Prepositional Interposition (باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور) — governing the permissible separation between the preposition and its object for rhetorical emphasis, applied here to the parsing of "إلى السماء" in the verse on istiwāʾ, where the prepositional phrase is delayed to highlight the divine act of sovereign direction toward the heavens.
42:9.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'On Invocations and Supplications'

43:14.arabic: وما لم يشأ لم يكن سبحان الذي سخر لنا هذا وما كنا له مقرنين وإنا إلى ربنا لمنقلبون اللهم إني وجهت وجهي إليك وفوضت أمري كله إليك وتوكلت في جميع أموري عليك أنت حسبي ونعم الوكيل فإذا استوى على الراحلة واستوت تحته قال سبحان الله والحمد لله ولا إله إلا الله والله أكبر سبع مرات وقال الحمد لله الذي هدانا لهذا وما كنا لنهتدي لولا أن هدانا الله اللهم أنت الحامل على الظهر وأنت المستعان على الأمور السادسة في النزول والسنة أن لا ينزل حتى يحمى النهار ويكون أكثر سيره بالليل قال صلى الله عليه وسلم عليكم بالدلجة فإن الأرض تطوي بالليل ما لا تط
43:14.english: He ought to seek out a righteous companion, one who loves goodness and assists in it: if he forgets, the companion reminds him; if he remembers, the companion aids him; if he fears, the companion emboldens him; if he weakens, the companion strengthens him; if his breast narrows, the companion enlarges his patience. He should bid farewell to his resident companions, his brothers, and his neighbors — taking leave of them and seeking their supplications, for God Most High places goodness in their prayers. The Sunnah of farewell is to say: «أستودع الله دينك وأمانتك وخواتيم عملك» — "I entrust to God your religion, your trustworthiness, and the seal of your deeds." And he, peace and blessings be upon him, used to say to one intending travel: "In God's protection and His care — may God provide you with piety, forgive your sin, and direct you toward goodness wherever you may be."
43:14.section_title_en: The Book of the Etiquette of Travel — Section 199: On the Comprehensive Etiquette of the Journey (From Provisioning to Guarding)
43:14.anchors:
- Root: س ف ر (S-F-R)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "السفر: كشف الغطاء" — unveiling, uncovering; the traveler is one who uncovers the veils of distant lands.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "السفر: كشف الغطاء، ويختص ذلك بالأعيان" — the journey is a literal uncovering of horizons, yet the spiritual journey unveils the soul's veils.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Haqiqah: "سافر سفرا بعيدا" (to travel far); Majaz: "وجه مسفر: مشرق سرورا" — a face radiant with joy, as the traveler's face brightens with divine trust.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — governing the permissible separation between the preposition and its object for rhetorical emphasis, as in the supplications' structural pauses.
43:14.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications, prayers, and their spiritual power, from 'On Invocations and Supplications'

45:36.arabic: اللهم باسمك أحيا وأموت (13) اللهم رب السموات ورب الأرض ورب كل شيء ومليكه فالق الحب والنوى ومنزل التوراة والإنجيل والقرآن أعوذ بك من شر كل ذي شر ومن شر كل دابة أنت آخذ بناصيتها أنت الأول فليس قبلك شيء وأنت الآخر فليس بعدك شيء وأنت الظاهر فليس فوقك شيء وأنت الباطن فليس دونك شيء اقض عني الدين وأغنني من الفقر (1) اللهم إنك خلقت نفسي وأنت تتوفاها لك مماتها ومحياها اللهم إن أمتها فاغفر لها وإن أحييتها فاحفظها اللهم إني أسألك العافية في الدنيا والآخرة (2) باسمك ربي وضعت جنبي فاغفر لي ذنبي (3) اللهم
45:36.english: When you rise in the morning and hear the call to prayer (adhān), it is recommended for you to respond to the caller of prayer (mu'adhdhin) — and we have already mentioned this, along with the supplications for entering and leaving the privy, and the supplications of ablution (wuḍū'), in the Book of Purification. When you set out toward the mosque, say: "O Allah, place light (nūr) in my heart, and light in my tongue, and place light in my hearing, and place light in my sight, and place light behind me, and light before me, and place light above me. O Allah, grant me light." And also say: "O Allah, I ask You by the right of those who ask of You, and by the right of this my walking unto You — for I have not gone out in insolence, nor in vanity, nor for show, nor for reputation. I have gone out seeking protection from Your wrath and seeking Your good pleasure. So I ask You to deliver me from the Fire and to forgive me my sins — verily, none forgives sins but You."
45:36.section_title_en: Section 254 — Supplications for the Hours of Day and Night: From Dawn to Sleep
45:36.anchors:
- Root: ن و ر (n-w-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: النور: الضوء المنتشر الذي يُبصر به، وهو ضد الظلمة
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): النور في القرآن يقع على ضروب: منها المعقول كالإيمان والحكمة، قال تعالى: {قد جاءكم من الله نور وكتاب مبين}، ومنها المحسوس كضوء الشمس والقمر
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): النور حقيقة في الضوء المحسوس، ومجاز في الهدى والإيمان والعلم — فدعاء النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بطلب النور يشمل المعنيين جميعاً
- Root: س ج د (s-j-d)
  * Lisan / Ayn: السجود: وضع الجبهة على الأرض تعظيماً، وأصله التطامن والانخفاض
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): السجود ضربان: سجود عبادة وهو وضع الجبهة على الأرض تقرباً، وسجود طاعة وهو الانقياد والخضوع — قال تعالى: {ولله يسجد من في السموات والأرض طوعاً وكرهاً}
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): سجد حقيقة في وضع الجبهة، ومجاز في الخضوع والانقياد — وقوله "سجد لك سوادي وخيالي" من المجاز المرسل
- Root: ذ ك ر (dh-k-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: الذكر: نقيض النسيان، والذكر: الصوت الذي يُذكر به الشيء، والذكر: الشرف والصيت
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): الذكر ضربان: ذكر بالقلب وهو التفكر في عظمة الله، وذكر باللسان وهو التلفظ بأسمائه — وأعلى مراتبه ما اجتمع فيه القلب واللسان
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): الذكر حقيقة في استحضار الشيء بالقلب أو اللسان، ومجاز في الصلاة والدعاء والثناء
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — جواز تقديم المعمول وتأخيره مع بقاء العامل عاملاً في المعنى، كقوله "لك الحمد" حيث تقدم الجار والمجرور على المبتدأ للاختصاص والاهتمام
45:36.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications, prayers, and their spiritual power, from 'On Invocations and Supplications'

46:21.arabic: وإلى حالك ويغبطونك فى حسنك وجمالك والملائكة يمشون بين يديك ومن خلفك وينادون على رءوس الأشهاد هذا فلان بن فلان رضى الله عنه وأرضاه وقد سعد سعادة لا يشقى بعدها أبدا أفترى أن هذا المنصب ليس بأعظم من المكانة التى تنالها فى قلوب الخلق فى الدنيا بريائك ومداهنتك وتصنعك وتزينك فإن كنت تعلم أنه خير منه بل لانسبة له إليه فتوسل إلى إدراك هذه الرتبة بالإخلاص الصافى والنية الصادقة فى معاملتك مع الله فلن تدرك ذلك إلا به وإن تكن الأخرى والعياذ بالله بأن خرج من صحيفتك جريمة كنت تحسبها هينة وهى عند الله عظيمة فمقتك لأجلها فقا
46:21.english: Know that none is saved from the peril of the Scale except him who, in this world, called his own soul to account, and weighed therein — by the scale of the Sacred Law — his deeds, his words, his passing thoughts, and his glances, just as ʿUmar — may God be well pleased with him — said: "Call yourselves to account before you are called to account, and weigh yourselves before you are weighed." Indeed, his calling himself to account consists in his repenting, before death, from every act of disobedience with a sincere repentance (tawbah naṣūḥ), and in his making up for what was neglected of his shortcomings regarding the obligatory commands of God — may He be exalted — and in his restoring rights to those he wronged, grain by grain, and in his seeking absolution from everyone whom he harmed by his tongue, his hand, or his evil suspicion harbored in his heart — and this by winning their hearts' contentment — until he dies with no outstanding wrong against him, nor any neglected obligation.
46:21.section_title_en: The Perils of the Scale and the Reckoning of Wrongs Against Others
46:21.anchors:
- Root: وزن (w-z-n)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning is weighing, measuring, and balancing; al-mīzān (the Scale) is the instrument of equitable judgment.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In theological context, al-mīzān is the divine instrument of justice on the Day of Resurrection, weighing deeds to manifest equitable recompense, not a corporeal balance.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) usage denotes physical weighing; metaphorical (majāz) usage extends to moral and spiritual accounting, as in "weighing one's deeds by the scale of the Sacred Law."
- Sibawayh Rule: Conditional and Exceptive Constructions (الشّرط والاستثناء) — governing the protasis-apodosis structure in "whoever's scales are heavy... whoever's scales are light," and the exceptive force in "none is saved... except he who reckons."
46:21.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Remembrance of Death and Afterlife'

46:21.arabic: الكعبة فقلت ومن هم قال الأكثرون أموالا إلا من قال هكذا وهكذا من بين يديه ومن خلفه وعن يمينه وعن شماله وقليل ما هم ما من صاحب إبل ولا بقر ولا غنم لا يؤدي زكاتها إلا جاءت يوم القيامة أعظم ما كانت وأسمنه تنطحه بقرونها وتطؤه بأظلافها كلما نفدت أخراها عادت عليه أولاها حتى يقضى بين الناس (1) وإذا كان هذا التشديد مخرجا في الصحيحين فقد صار من مهمات الدين الكشف عن أسرار الزكاة وشروطها الجلية والخفية ومعانيها الظاهرة والباطنة مع الاقتصار على ما لا يستغنى عن معرفته مؤدي الزكاة وقابضها وينكشف ذلك في أربعة فصول الفصل الأول في أنواع الزكاة وأسباب
46:21.english: To proceed: God Most High made alms (al-zakāh) one of the pillars of Islam, and joined its mention with prayer (al-ṣalāh), which is the loftiest of symbols. He said Most High: {«وَأَقِيمُوا الصَّلَاةَ وَآتُوا الزَّكَاةَ»} — "And establish prayer and give alms." And he, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Islam is built upon five: the testimony that there is no god but God and that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger, the establishment of prayer, and the giving of alms." And He intensified the threat against those who fall short in it, saying: {«وَالَّذِينَ يَكْنِزُونَ الذَّهَبَ وَالْفِضَّةَ وَلَا يُنفِقُونَهَا فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ فَبَشِّرْهُم بِعَذَابٍ أَلِيمٍ»} — "And those who hoard gold and silver and do not spend them in the way of God — give them tidings of a painful chastisement." And the meaning of "spending in the way of God" is the payment of the due right of alms (zakāh).
46:21.section_title_en: The Book of the Secrets of Alms (Zakat) — Section 167
46:21.anchors:
- Root: زكا (Z-K-Y)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "Zakā al-zar'u yazkū zakā'an: it increased and grew." Core meaning: growth, increase, purification.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "The origin of zakāh is the growth that occurs through the blessing of God Most High... and from it is zakāh: what a person pays of God's right to the poor, so named for the hope of blessing in it, or for the purification (tazkiyah) of the soul, i.e., its growth."
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (haqīqah): growth and increase. Metaphorical (majāz): the purification of wealth through payment of the obligatory due.
- Root: نعم (N-'-M)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "Na'ima 'ayshuhu: his life was pleasant." Core meaning: bounty, well-being, grace.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Al-Ni'mah: the good state... and al-Ni'mah (with kasrah) is used for the genus, said of both little and much."
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "Jallat ni'mat Allāh wa na'mā'uh" — God's grace and bounty are immense. Metaphorical: "Khāfat na'āmatuhum" — their ostriches departed (i.e., they fled), showing the root's extended usage.
- Root: ظهر (Z-H-R)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "Zahara: to become apparent, to be victorious." Core meaning: back, outward appearance, manifestation.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Al-Zahr: the back (body part)... and it is used metaphorically for the surface of the earth."
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "Rajul muzhir: a man strong of back." Metaphorical: "Qalabtu al-amra zahrān li-baṭn" — I turned the matter over back and belly (examined it thoroughly).
- Root: سرر (S-R-R)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "Sarra: to conceal, to keep secret." Core meaning: secret, inner self, joy.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Al-Isrār: the opposite of al-i'lān (declaring)... and al-sirr is the speech concealed in the soul."
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "Asarra al-ḥadīth: he concealed the speech." Metaphorical: "Aṭaytuka sirrah: I gave you its choicest part (the secret/core of something)."
- Sibawayh Rule: Bāb al-faṣl bayna al-jār wa al-majrūr (Prepositional Interposition) — The permissibility of interposing elements between a preposition and its object when the intervening clause is complete in itself, as in "fa'āfa 'alayhim min ni'matihi mā..." where the prepositional phrase is completed after an intervening relative clause.
46:21.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications, prayers, and their spiritual power, from 'Mysteries of Zakat'

46:21.arabic: عثراتي واحفظني من بين يدي ومن خلفي وعن يميني وعن شمالي ومن فوقي وأعوذ بك أن أغتال من تحتي (1) اللهم لا تؤمني مكرك ولا تولني غيرك ولا تنزع عني سترك ولا تنسني ذكرك ولا تجعلني من الغافلين (2) وقل اللهم أنت ربي لا إله إلا أنت خلقتني وأنا عبدك وأنا على عهدك ووعدك ما استطعت أعوذ بك من شر ما صنعت أبوء لك بنعمتك علي وأبوء بذنبي فاغفر لي فإنه لا يغفر الذنوب إلا أنت (3) ثلاث مرات وقل اللهم عافني في بدني وعافني في سمعي وعافني في بصري لا إله إلا أنت (4) ثلاث مرات وقل اللهم إني أسألك ال
46:21.english: "Glory be to my Lord, the Most High, the Most Exalted, the Bestower (al-Wahhāb). There is no god but God alone, with no partner. His is the sovereignty and His is the praise, and He is over all things powerful."
46:21.section_title_en: The Fourth Chapter on Supplications Narrated from the Prophet (Peace Be Upon Him) and His Companions (May God Be Pleased with Them)
46:21.anchors:
- Root: لهم (l-h-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of swallowing/ingesting (iltihām), from which ilhām (divine inspiration) derives—that which is cast into the heart
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الإلهام: إلقاء الشيء في الروع" — divine inspiration is the casting of something into the inner faculty of consciousness (rawʿ), specifically from God and the higher assembly (malā aʿlā)
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (haqīqah): "ألهمه الله الخير: ألقاه في روعه" (God inspired him with good: He cast it into his inner consciousness). Metaphorical (majāz): "جيش لهام: يغتمر من يدخله" (an overwhelming army that engulfs whoever enters it)
- Root: غيب (gh-y-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: That which is hidden from sensory perception
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الغيب: مصدر غابت الشمس وغيرها: إذا استترت عن العين" — that which is concealed from the eye; applied to all that is absent from the senses and from human knowledge. Notably: "ويقال للشيء: غيب وغائب باعتباره بالناس لا بالله تعالى، فإنه لا يغيب عنه شيء" (it is called ghayb relative to people, not relative to God, for nothing is hidden from Him)
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "وتكلم بذلك عن ظهر الغيب" (he spoke of that from behind the unseen). Metaphorical: "أتونا في غابة أي في رماح كثيرة" (they came to us in a thicket—i.e., amidst numerous spears like dense trees)
- Root: علم (ʿ-l-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Knowledge as the apprehension of a thing's reality
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "العلم: إدراك الشيء بحقيقته" — knowledge is the apprehension of a thing in its true reality; two types: apprehension of the essence of a thing, and judgment upon a thing regarding what exists for it or is negated from it
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "ما علمت بخبرك: ما شعرت به" (I did not know of your news: I was not aware of it). "وهو من أعلام العلم الخافقه" (he is among the lofty banners of knowledge)
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — governing the permissible separation between the preposition and its object for rhetorical emphasis, as in the construction "عالم الغيب والشهادة" where the attributive relationship is maintained through the genitive construction (iḍāfah)
46:21.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications, prayers, and their spiritual power, from 'On Invocations and Supplications'

47:19.arabic: وثلاثين وكبر ثلاثا وثلاثين وختم المائة بلا إله إلا الله لا شريك له له الملك وله الحمد وهو على كل شيء قدير غفرت ذنوبه ولو كانت مثل زبد البحر (6) وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم من قال سبحان الله وبحمده في اليوم مائة مرة حطت عنه خطاياه وإن كانت مثل زبد البحر (7) وروي أن رجلا جاء إلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال تولت عني الدنيا وقلت ذات يدي فقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فأين أنت من صلاة الملائكة وتسبيح الخلائق وبها يرزقون قال فقلت وماذا يا رسول الله قال قل سبحان الله وبحمده سبحان الله العظ
47:19.english: He — peace and blessings be upon him — said: "Whoever glorifies Allah (subḥān Allāh) thirty-three times after every prayer, and praises Him (al-ḥamdu lillāh) thirty-three times, and magnifies Him (Allāhu akbar) thirty-three times, and completes the hundred with 'There is no god but Allah alone, with no partner; His is the dominion and His is the praise, and He is powerful over all things' — his sins are forgiven, even if they were like the foam of the sea." (6)
47:19.section_title_en: Section 238 — On the Virtues of Tasbīḥ, Taḥmīd, Takbīr, and the Remembrance of Allah
47:19.anchors:
- Root: سبح (s-b-ḥ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning is swift movement through water or air; extended to the motion of celestial bodies in their spheres.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "التسبيح: تنزيه الله تعالى" — the theological sense is the declaration of Allah's transcendence above all imperfection; its origin is the swift passage into the worship of Allah.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Ḥaqīqah): "سبحت الله" — to declare Him transcendent. Metaphorical (Majāz): "والنجوم تسبح في الفلك" — the stars glide in their orbits; the tongue "swims" in remembrance as the horse "swims" in its gallop.
- Root: حمد (ḥ-m-d)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Praise that is a response to beneficence; commendation for voluntary goodness.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Praise (ḥamd) is the acknowledgment of beneficence with reverence; it is more specific than shukr (gratitude) in that it is only by the tongue, but broader in that it is for both good and virtue.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "أحمد الله تعالى بجميع محامده" — to praise Allah with all His praiseworthy attributes. Metaphorical: "أحمدت صنيعه" — I deemed his deed praiseworthy; the earth is "praised" when its dwelling is found agreeable.
- Root: كبر (k-b-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To be great in magnitude, rank, or dignity; takbīr is the verbal declaration of Allah's supreme greatness.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Kibriyā' is the attribute of absolute greatness that belongs to Allah alone; takbīr is the tongue's affirmation of this exclusive majesty.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: declaring Allah greater than all things. Metaphorical: the heart's magnification of Allah such that nothing else looms large in comparison.
- Root: هلل (h-l-l)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The root denotes appearing after being hidden; tahlīl (lā ilāha illā Allāh) is the declaration that nullifies all false deities and affirms the One.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The phrase "lā ilāha illā Allāh" is the most excellent of remembrances; its meaning is the negation of all that is worshipped besides Allah and the affirmation of His sole divinity.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the utterance of the shahādah. Metaphorical: the heart's purification from all allegiance to other than Allah.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Conjunction and Coordination (Bāb al-ʿAṭf) — The repeated formulaic phrases are coordinated by wa (and), each standing as an independent clause of invocation, with the final phrase "wa huwa ʿalā kulli shay'in qadīr" serving as the concluding predicate affirming Allah's omnipotence, completing the hundred with a declaration of divine power.
47:19.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications, prayers, and their spiritual power, from 'On Invocations and Supplications'

47:19.arabic: ولا إله إلا الله والله أكبر ألف مرة وإن قرأ المسبعات الست في يوم الجمعة أو ليلتها فحسن وليس يروى عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه كان يقرأ سورا بأعيانها إلا في يوم الجمعة وليلتها كان يقرأ في صلاة المغرب ليلة الجمعة قل يا أيها الكافرون وقل هو الله أحد وكان يقرأ في صلاة العشاء الآخرة ليلة الجمعة سورة الجمعة والمنافقين (3) وروي أنه صلى الله عليه وسلم كان يقرؤهما في ركعتي الجمعة وكان يقرأ في الصبح يوم الجمعة سورة سجدة لقمان وسورة هل أتى على الإنسان (4) الخامس الصلوات
47:19.english: Know that among the proprieties of Friday is that one should be excellent in watching for the noble hour. For in the well-known report: {«Indeed in Friday there is an hour in which no Muslim servant asks God, Mighty and Majestic, for anything but that He grants it to him»}. And in another report: {«No servant coincides with it while praying»}.
47:19.section_title_en: The Revival of the Religious Sciences — Section 151: On the Virtues of Friday and Its Proprieties
47:19.anchors:
- Root: ر-ق-ب (raqaba)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To watch, observe, lie in wait for; the watcher (rāqib) is one who awaits expectantly.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Moral vigilance (murāqabah) is the soul's persistent attentiveness to what it anticipates, whether of benefit or harm.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: watching a road or pass. Metaphorical: the heart's standing guard over the appointed time, as one watches for the crescent moon.
- Root: ن-ف-ح (nafaḥa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To blow gently, to emit a breeze; nafaḥāt are gentle, diffusive emanations.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Divine effusions of mercy that sweep over the servant unexpectedly.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: a fragrant breeze. Metaphorical: the breaths of divine mercy that pass over the days of time.
- Root: خ-ط-ب (khaṭaba)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To address, deliver an oration; khuṭbah is the formal sermon.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The prophetic address conveying command and prohibition.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: oration. Metaphorical: the preacher's ascent to the pulpit marks the threshold of the answered hour.
- Sibawayh Rule: Interposition of the conditional clause (jawāb al-sharṭ) — the apodosis may be delayed or elided when the protasis is governed by a particle of expectation, as in "whoever does X, God forgives him," where the response is the reward predicated upon the condition.
47:19.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications, prayers, and their spiritual power, from 'On Invocations and Supplications'

47:19.arabic: وهو قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم بني الإسلام على خمس شهادة أن لا إله إلا الله (1) إلى آخر الحديث لأن الواجب هذه الخمس فيجب العلم بكيفية العمل فيها وبكيفية الوجوب والذي ينبغي أن يقطع به المحصل ولا يستريب فيه ما سنذكره وهو أن العلم كما قدمناه في خطبة الكتاب ينقسم إلى علم معاملة وعلم مكاشفة وليس المراد بهذا العلم إلا علم المعاملة والمعاملة التي كلف العبد العاقل البالغ العمل بها ثلاثة اعتقاد وفعل وترك فإذا بلغ الرجل العاقل بالاحتلام أو السن ضحوة نهار مثلا فأول واجب عليه تعلم كلمتي الشهادة وفهم معناهما وهو قول لا إله إلا الله
47:19.english: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: "Seeking knowledge is an obligation upon every Muslim." {«طلب العلم فريضة على كل مسلم»} He also said, may God bless him and grant him peace: "Seek knowledge, even unto China." {«اطلبوا العلم ولو بالصين»}
47:19.section_title_en: The Exposition of the Knowledge That Is an Individual Obligation (Farḍ ʿAyn)
47:19.anchors:
- Root: علم (ʿalima)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning encompasses both perception of a thing's essence and judgment upon it; knowledge as apprehension of reality.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Knowledge is of two kinds: apprehension of the essence of a thing, and judgment upon a thing regarding what exists or is negated for it. The first is transitive to one object; the second to two.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Distinguishes literal knowledge (ʿilm) from awareness/perception (shiʿr); knowledge as the mark (ʿalam) by which one is guided—here, the knowledge that guides to obligatory action.
- Root: وجب (wajaba)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To be due, necessary, obligatory; to fall (as a duty); the root carries the sense of established necessity.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Obligation (wujūb) is of two kinds: that which is necessary by reason (ʿaql), and that which is necessary by sacred law (sharʿ). The knowledge that is farḍ ʿayn pertains to the latter—what the Lawgiver has made due upon every accountable individual.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal sense of falling due; metaphorical extension to what is incumbent upon a person—here, the knowledge whose acquisition becomes due upon the occurrence of its cause.
- Root: عهد (ʿahida) — AVOIDED per instruction; not employed.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Restriction and Focused Predication (al-ḥaṣr wa al-taqyīd bi-innamā) — The Prophet's statement "طلب العلم فريضة" (seeking knowledge is an obligation) is a general predication whose referent (musammā) requires specification (takhṣīṣ) through contextual and definitional analysis, not lexical transfer (naql). The article (al-) in "العلم" indicates the known, designated science—here, the science of obligatory practice.
47:19.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications, prayers, and their spiritual power, from 'On Invocations and Supplications'

48:2.arabic: آخر ولم يسه فيهما غفر له ما تقدم من ذنبه وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم أيضا ألا أنبئكم بما يكفر الله به الخطايا ويرفع به الدرجات إسباغ الوضوء على المكاره ونقل الأقدام إلى المساجد وانتظار الصلاة بعد الصلاة فذلكم الرباط ثلاث مرات (2) وتوضأ صلى الله عليه وسلم مرة مرة وقال هذا وضوء لا يقبل الله الصلاة إلا به وتوضأ مرتين مرتين وقال من توضأ مرتين مرتين أتاه الله أجره مرتين وتوضأ ثلاثا ثلاثا وقال هذا وضوئي ووضوء الأنبياء من قبلي ووضوء خليل الرحمن إبراهيم عليه السلام (3) وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم م
48:2.english: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: "Whoever performs ablution and does it well, then prays two rakʿahs in which he does not speak to himself of anything of this world, will come out of his sins like the day his mother bore him." In another wording: "And does not err in them, his past sins will be forgiven him." He, may God bless him and grant him peace, also said: "Shall I not inform you of that by which God erases sins and by which He raises degrees? The perfecting of ablution despite hardships, and the taking of many steps to the mosques, and the waiting for prayer after prayer — that is the ribāṭ (the constant guarding of the frontier)." He said this three times. And he, may God bless him and grant him peace, performed ablution once each (washing each limb once) and said: "This is an ablution without which God does not accept the prayer." And he performed ablution twice each and said: "Whoever performs ablution twice each, God will give him his reward twice." And he performed ablution three times each and said: "This is my ablution, and the ablution of the prophets before me, and the ablution of the Friend of the Merciful, Abraham, peace be upon him." And he, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: "Whoever mentions God at his ablution, God will purify his entire body; and whoever does not mention God, only that which the water touches will be purified." And he, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: "Whoever performs ablution while already in a state of purity, God writes for him ten good deeds." And he, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: "Ablution upon ablution is light upon light." All of this is an encouragement to renew the ablution. And he, peace be upon him, said: "When the Muslim servant performs ablution and rinses his mouth, the sins exit from his mouth; when he snuffs water into his nose, the sins exit from his nose; when he washes his face, the sins exit from his face, until they exit from beneath his eyelashes; when he washes his hands, the sins exit from his hands, until they exit from beneath his fingernails; when he wipes his head, the sins exit from his head, until they exit from beneath his ears; and when he washes his feet, the sins exit from his feet, until they exit from beneath the nails of his feet. Then his walking to the mosque and his prayer are an additional merit for him." And it is related that "the one in a state of purity is like the one who is fasting." He, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: "Whoever performs ablution and does it well, then raises his gaze to the sky and says, 'I bear witness that there is no god but God alone, with no partner, and I bear witness that Muhammad is His servant and His Messenger' — the eight gates of Paradise are opened for him, and he enters through whichever of them he wishes." And ʿUmar, may God be pleased with him, said: "Indeed, the sound ablution drives the devil away from you." And Mujāhid said: "Whoever is able to not spend the night except in a state of purity, remembering God and seeking His forgiveness, let him do so, for the souls are raised according to the state in which they were seized."
48:2.section_title_en: The Virtue of Ablution (Faḍīlat al-Wuḍūʾ) and the Manner of the Major Ritual Bath (Kayfiyyat al-Ghusl)
48:2.anchors:
- Root: وضو (W-Ḍ-W)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The root denotes cleanliness, brightness, and perfection; al-wuḍūʾ is the specific act of ritual purification with water for prayer.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The term is used for the specific act of washing the limbs in preparation for prayer, a divinely ordained purification that removes both physical and spiritual defilement.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) usage refers to the physical washing of the limbs; metaphorical (majāz) usage extends to the purification of the soul from sins, as sins are said to "exit" with the water.
- Root: غسل (Gh-S-L)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To wash, to remove dirt or filth by pouring water over something.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "غسلت الشيء غسلا: أسلت عليه الماء فأزلت درنه" — to pour water over a thing to remove its filth. Al-Ghusl is the name for the act of washing the entire body, and al-ghusl (with damma) is the water used for washing. The root also yields "al-ghislīn" (غسلين), the filth-washing of the bodies of the disbelievers in Hellfire.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) usage is the physical washing of the body. Metaphorical (majāz) usage is found in phrases like "تلطخ بعار لن يغسل عنه أبدا" (stained with a disgrace that will never be washed away), indicating that which cannot be cleansed or absolved.
- Root: راس (R-A-S)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The head; also used for a leader or chief.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الرأس معروف" — the head is well-known; it is used metaphorically for the leader (al-raʾīs).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) usage refers to the physical head. Metaphorical (majāz) usage is found in "رأس الدين الخشية" (the head of the religion is God-consciousness) and "هو رأس قومه" (he is the head of his people).
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The rule governing the permissibility of separating a preposition from its object, which is relevant for correctly parsing the grammatical relationships in the hadith reports, ensuring the subject of the verb is correctly identified.
48:2.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications, prayers, and their spiritual power, from 'Mysteries of Prayer'

48:2.arabic: استأنف العمل فقد غفر لك ما تقدم من ذنبك ورفع الله سبحانه عنك عذاب القبر وضيقه وظلمته ورفع عنك شدائد القيامة ورفع له من يومه عمل نبي (4) يوم الخميس عن عكرمة عن ابن عباس قال قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم من صلى يوم الخميس بين الظهر والعصر ركعتين يقرأ في الأولى فاتحة الكتاب وآية الكرسي مائة مرة وفي الثانية فاتحة الكتاب وقل هو الله أحد مائة مرة ويصلي على محمد مائة مرة أعطاه الله ثواب من صام رجب وشعبان ورمضان وكان له من الثواب مثل حاج البيت وكتب له بعدد كل من آمن بالله سبحانه وتوكل عليه
48:2.english: **Sunday:** Abū Hurayrah — may Allah be pleased with him — narrated from the Prophet — peace and blessings be upon him — that he said: "Whoever prays on Sunday four units (rakʿāt), reciting in each unit the Opening of the Book {«فاتحة الكتاب»} and {«آمن الرسول»} once, Allah will write for him, for every Christian man and woman, good deeds; and He will give him the reward of a prophet; and He will write for him a Pilgrimage (ḥajj) and an ʿUmrah; and He will write for him, for every unit, a thousand prayers; and Allah will give him, in Paradise, for every letter, a city of pure musk." And it is narrated from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib — may Allah be pleased with him — from the Prophet — peace and blessings be upon him — that he said: "Declare the oneness of Allah (waḥḥidū Allāh) by multiplying prayer on Sunday, for He — Glorified be He — is One (wāḥid), having no partner. Whoever prays on Sunday after the noon prayer (ẓuhr) four units after the obligatory and the sunnah — reciting in the first unit the Opening of the Book and {«تنزيل السجدة»}, and in the second unit the Opening of the Book and {«تبارك الملك»} — then gives the greeting of peace (tashahhud wa salām), then stands and prays two further units, reciting in them the Opening of the Book and the Chapter of Friday {«سورة الجمعة»}, and asks Allah — Glorified be He — for his need, it is incumbent upon Allah to fulfill his need."
48:2.section_title_en: The Revival of the Religious Sciences — Section 159: On the Virtues of Prayers for Each Day of the Week
48:2.anchors:
- Root: يوم (yawm)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core temporal unit; from sunrise to sunset, or any extended period.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "اليوم يعبر به عن وقت طلوع الشمس إلى غروبها. وقد يعبر به عن مدة من الزمان أي مدة كانت" — denotes the period from sunrise to sunset, or any duration whatsoever; when added to Allah (أيام الله), it signifies His mighty deeds and epochs.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): the solar day. Metaphorical (Majaz): "ذكر في أيام العرب كذا أي في وقائعها" — used for notable events and battles.
- Root: ركع (rakaʿa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To bow; the act of bowing in prayer.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الركوع: الانحناء، فتارة يستعمل في الهيئة المخصوصة في الصلاة كما هي، وتارة في التواضع والتذلل" — bowing; used literally for the specific prayer posture, and metaphorically for humility and submission.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "شيخ راكع: منحن من الكبر" — an old man bent with age. Metaphorical: "لغبت الإبل حتى ركعت" — camels weary to the point of collapsing on their front legs. In prayer, a ركعة (rakʿah) is a unit named after its bowing.
- Root: فتح (fataḥa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To open; to unlock.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الفتح: إزالة الإغلاق والإشكال" — removal of closure and obstruction; perceptible by sight (opening a door) or by insight (removing distress).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: opening a physical door. Metaphorical: "فتح الله عليه: نصره" — Allah's granting victory; "فتح على فلان" — prosperity and worldly success.
- Root: احد (aḥad)
  * Lisan / Ayn: One; unique; the first of the six roots of the triliteral system.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Used for Allah's absolute oneness; "وحدوا الله" — declare His unity.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: numerical oneness. Metaphorical: exclusive uniqueness, as in the divine name "الأحد" (The One).
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد (Restriction & Focused Predication) — The conditional clauses (من صلى...) followed by apodoses (كتب له...) establish a restricted causal nexus: the reward is bound precisely to the specified action, its time, and its prescribed form.
48:2.topic: Al-Ghazali on the journey of the soul, death, and the Hereafter, from 'Mysteries of Prayer'

48:2.arabic: قدماه فقيل له أما قد غفر الله لك ما تقدم من ذنبك وما تأخر فقال أفلا أكون عبدا شكورا (6) ويظهر من معناه أن ذلك كناية عن زيادة الرتبة فإن الشكر سبب المزيد قال تعالى {لئن شكرتم لأزيدنكم} وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم يا أبا هريرة أتريد أن تكون رحمة الله عليك حيا وميتا ومقبورا ومبعوثا قم من الليل
48:2.english: As for the Qur'anic verses, there is the saying of Allah Most High: {«إِنَّ رَبَّكَ يَعْلَمُ أَنَّكَ تَقُومُ أَدْنَىٰ مِن ثُلُثَيِ اللَّيْلِ»} — the verse (Al-Muzzammil: 20) — and His saying: {«إِنَّ نَاشِئَةَ اللَّيْلِ هِيَ أَشَدُّ وَطْئًا وَأَقْوَمُ قِيلًا»} (Al-Muzzammil: 6), and His saying, Glorified and Exalted: {«تَتَجَافَىٰ جُنُوبُهُمْ عَنِ الْمَضَاجِعِ»} (Al-Sajdah: 16), and His saying: {«أَمَّنْ هُوَ قَانِتٌ آنَاءَ اللَّيْلِ»} — the verse (Al-Zumar: 9), and His saying, Mighty and Majestic: {«وَالَّذِينَ يَبِيتُونَ لِرَبِّهِمْ سُجَّدًا وَقِيَامًا»} (Al-Furqan: 64), and His saying: {«وَاسْتَعِينُوا بِالصَّبْرِ وَالصَّلَاةِ»} (Al-Baqarah: 45). It is said that this refers to night prayer — one seeks aid through patience upon it in the struggle against the soul (*mujāhadat al-nafs*).
48:2.section_title_en: The Virtue of Reviving the Time Between the Two Evening Prayers (Maghrib and ʿIshāʾ) — The Virtue of Night Prayer (Qiyām al-Layl)
48:2.anchors:
- Root: ليل (Layl)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The root denotes the night, from sunset to dawn; its plural forms include *layāl* and *layālī*. Al-Farahidi notes its archaic derivation from *laylāh*.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The night is a divinely ordained sign and period of worship; Allah says {«وَسَخَّرَ لَكُمُ اللَّيْلَ وَالنَّهَارَ»} (Ibrahim: 33) and swears by it in {«وَاللَّيْلِ إِذَا يَغْشَىٰ»} (Al-Layl: 1). It is the chosen time for the *nāshiʾah* — the prayer that rises by night.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (*ḥaqīqah*): the night as a temporal span. Metaphorical (*majāz*): "a night of hardship" or the soul's "night" of heedlessness. Here, the night is the literal arena for supererogatory worship.
- Root: وفي (Wafā)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Completeness, fulfillment, and reaching full measure. A thing that is *wāfin* is complete and whole.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): *Al-Wāfī* is that which has reached completion. Allah says {«وَأَوْفُوا بِعَهْدِي أُوفِ بِعَهْدِكُمْ»} (Al-Baqarah: 40). The night prayer is described as {«أَقْوَمُ قِيلًا»} — more upright in speech and more complete in its effect upon the heart.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: a full measure or complete thing. Metaphorical: "he reached the hundred" (*awfā ʿalā al-miʾah*), i.e., surpassed it. The night prayer "fulfills" the soul's potential for nearness to Allah.
- Root: نفس (Nafs)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The self, soul, or spirit; that which breathes and has life. Al-Farahidi connects it to *nafas* (breath) and *nufūs* (precious things).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The *nafs* is the rational soul and the seat of moral struggle (*mujāhadah*). Allah says {«إِنَّ النَّفْسَ لَأَمَّارَةٌ بِالسُّوءِ»} (Yusuf: 53). The ḥadīth describes the one who prays at night as becoming "good of soul" (*ṭayyib al-nafs*), while the sluggard becomes "evil of soul" (*khabīth al-nafs*).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the self or person. Metaphorical: "he poured out his soul" (i.e., his blood). Here, the *nafs* is the battlefield between the worshipper and the devil's whisperings.
- Root: خبر (Khabar)
  * Lisan / Ayn: News, report, or information; also experience and knowledge of a thing's inner state.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): *Al-Khabar* is knowledge of things through report. The *akhbār* (plural) are the prophetic traditions cited as evidence alongside the Qur'anic verses.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: to test or try a thing to know its state. Metaphorical: "his mirror reports of his unknown" — i.e., reveals what is hidden. The *akhbār* here are the authoritative reports from the Prophet (ﷺ).
- Sibawayh Rule: The rule of *al-ʿaṭf ʿalā al-sabab* (coordination on a cause) — when multiple conditions are linked by *fa* (then), each is a consequence of the preceding, as in the ḥadīth of the three knots: "If he wakes and remembers Allah, a knot is untied; if he performs ablution, a knot is untied; if he prays, a knot is untied" — each act builds upon the previous, and the *fa* indicates sequential causation.
48:2.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Contemplation'

48:2.arabic: سبعين مرة (3) هذا مع أنه صلى الله عليه وسلم غفر له ما تقدم من ذنبه وما تأخر وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم إنه ليغان على قلبي حتى إني لأستغفر الله تعالى في كل يوم مائة مرة (4) وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم من قال حين يأوي إلى فراشه أستغفر الله العظيم الذي لا إله إلا هو الحي القيوم وأتوب إليه ثلاث مرات غفر الله له ذنوبه وإن كانت مثل زبد البحر أو عدد رمل عالج أو عدد ورق الشجر أو عدد أيام الدنيا (5) وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم في حديث آخر من قال ذلك غفرت ذنوبه وإن كان فارا من الزحف (6) وقال حذيفة كنت ذرب اللسان على أهلي فقلت يا رسول الله
48:2.english: God Most High said: {«والذين إذا فعلوا فاحشة أو ظلموا أنفسهم ذكروا الله فاستغفروا لذنوبهم»} — "And those who, when they commit an indecency or wrong themselves, remember God and seek forgiveness for their sins" {آل عمران/135}.
48:2.anchors:
- Root: ذنب (dhanb)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of "tail" or "taking hold of a tail"; extended to signify a sin as that which trails behind and follows a person.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الذنب في الأصل: الأخذ بذنب الشيء" — sin is that by which one is seized and held accountable; used metaphorically for a fault that clings to its perpetrator.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: tail of an animal. Metaphorical: "هو من الأذناب" — one who follows; sin as that which trails the soul and must be severed through repentance.
- Root: غفر (ghafara)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Covering, veiling, protecting from defilement; a shield or helmet (المغفر).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الغفران والمغفرة من الله هو أن يصون العبد من أن يمسه العذاب" — divine forgiveness is God's protection of the servant from being touched by punishment.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: to cover and protect. Metaphorical: God's "covering" of sins — not merely erasure, but active safeguarding of the sinner from consequence.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The frequent interposition of "يا رب" and vocative constructions between the subject and predicate in supplicatory sentences, as in "اللهم اغفر لي," where the vocative particle governs the imperative verb's addressee, reflecting the grammatical permissibility of separation between governing and governed elements in invocational speech.
48:2.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications, prayers, and their spiritual power, from 'On Invocations and Supplications'

55:26.arabic: في حقه بالموت ف كل من عليها فان ويبقى وجه ربك ذو الجلال والإكرام وإنما تفنى الدنيا بالموت في حقه إلى أن تفنى في نفسها عند بلوغ الكتاب أجله وهذا الأنس يتلذذ به العبد بعد موته إلى أن ينزل في جوار الله عز وجل ويترقى من الذكر إلى اللقاء وذلك بعد أن يبعثر ما في القبور ويحصل ما في الصدور ولا ينكر بقاء ذكر الله عز وجل معه الموت فيقول إنه أعدم فكيف يبقى معه ذكر الله عز وجل فإنه لم يعدم عدما يمنع الذكر بل عدما من الدنيا وعالم الملك والشهادة لا من عالم الملكوت وإلى ما ذكرناه الإشارة بقوله صلى الله عليه وسلم القبر إما حفرة
55:26.english: If, therefore, he had grown intimate with it, he delights in it and takes pleasure in the cessation of the impediments that had diverted him from it. For the pressing necessities of needs in this worldly life divert one from the remembrance of God, may He be mighty and majestic, and after death no impediment remains. It is as if he has been left alone with his Beloved, and so his joy is immense, and he is delivered from the prison in which he had been prevented from that which was his source of intimacy. For this reason, he, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "The Holy Spirit (Rūḥ al-Qudus) breathed into my heart: Love whom you will, for you shall surely part from him." {«أحبب من أحببت فإنك مفارقه»} By this he intended everything connected to this world, for that perishes with respect to him at death. For {«كل من عليها فان * ويبقى وجه ربك ذو الجلال والإكرام»} [Everything upon it is perishing, and there remains the Face of your Lord, Possessor of Majesty and Honor]. And this world only perishes with respect to him at death, until it perishes in itself when the Book reaches its appointed term.
55:26.section_title_en: Section 240 — The Station of Remembrance (Dhikr): On the Transformation of Habit into Nature, the Intimacy of Remembrance After Death, and the Excellence of Martyrdom as the Seal of One's State
55:26.anchors:
- Root: ألف (Alifa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of reconciliation, familiarity, and the formation of habit through repeated engagement.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The theological nuance of 'uns' (intimacy) as the soul's acquired disposition of comfort in the presence of its Beloved, contrasting with 'wahsha' (estrangement).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Distinguishes the literal sense of social familiarity from the metaphorical (majaz) sense of the heart's deep-seated repose in the remembrance of God, which becomes a 'second nature' (ṭabʿan ākhara).
- Root: ختم (Khatama)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To seal, stamp, or conclude; the final impression left upon a thing.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The theological sense of the 'seal' (khātima) of one's life—the terminal state upon which one departs from the world and which determines the nature of the afterlife.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): The literal act of sealing a document versus the metaphorical designation of one's final spiritual condition as the determining factor of one's eternal outcome.
- Root: شهد (Shahida)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To witness, to be present, to testify.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The specific theological elevation of 'shahāda' (martyrdom) as the ultimate act of witnessing the truth of God through the sacrifice of one's own life, rendering the martyr a living witness (shahīd).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): The literal sense of legal testimony versus the metaphorical reality of the martyr whose very being testifies to the sincerity of his devotion, being 'alive' with his Lord.
- Root: قطع (Qata'a)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To sever, cut off, or detach.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The essential spiritual operation of severing worldly attachments ('alā'iq) to achieve the unadulterated focus of the heart upon God.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): The literal cutting of a physical tie versus the metaphorical severance of all internal and external impediments that distract the soul from its sole Beloved.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Restriction and Specification (Bāb al-Ḥaṣr wa al-Taqyīd bi-innamā) — Governing how the exclusive focus of the martyr's intention is syntactically and logically restricted to God alone, as exemplified in the phrase "no god but God" (lā ilāha illā Allāh), which requires the complete negation of all other objects of intention before affirming the sole Divine Object.
55:26.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'On Invocations and Supplications'

55:60.arabic: وهي كلمة طيبة وهي دعوة الحق وهي العروة الوثقى وهي ثمن الجنة وقال الله عز وجل {هل جزاء الإحسان إلا الإحسان} فقيل الإحسان في الدنيا قول لا إله إلا الله وفي الآخرة الجنة وكذا قوله تعالى {للذين أحسنوا الحسنى وزيادة} وروى البراء بن عازب أنه صلى الله عليه وسلم قال من قال لا إله إلا الله وحده لا شريك له له الملك وله الحمد وهو على كل شيء قدير عشر مرات كانت له عدل رقبة أو قال نسمة (1) وروى عمرو بن شعيب عن أبيه عن جده أنه قال قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم من قال في يوم مائتي مرة لا إله إلا الله وحده لا شريك له له الملك وله الحمد وهو على كل شيء قدير
55:60.english: The Prophet, peace be upon him, said: "The most excellent words that I and the prophets before me have uttered are: There is no god but Allah alone, with no partner." (1)
55:60.section_title_en: The Virtue of the Declaration of Divine Oneness (Fāḍīlat al-Tahlīl)
55:60.anchors:
- Root: اله (ʾ-l-h)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root denoting worship, servitude, and the act of deifying; the name "Allah" is the specific designation of the True Deity, distinguished from all false objects of worship.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الله: قيل: أصله إله فحذفت همزته، وأدخل عليها الألف واللام، فخص بالباري تعالى" — The name is exclusively reserved for the Creator, and "ilāh" is that which is worshipped; the declaration "lā ilāha illā Allāh" negates all false objects of worship and affirms sole divinity for God.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) usage denotes true worship and servitude; metaphorical (majāz) usage applies to anything taken as an object of devotion. The tahlīl is the verbal embodiment of sincere worship.
- Root: شرك (sh-r-k)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Partnership, sharing, or association; in theological context, the ascription of partners or associates to God in His divinity or worship.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الشركة والمشاركة: خلط الملكين" — The mixing of two ownerships; in Kalam, shirk is the association of another with God in that which is exclusively His, namely divinity and worship.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal usage denotes partnership in ownership; metaphorical usage in the phrase "lā sharīka lahu" (no partner has He) affirms God's exclusive and unshared sovereignty, kingdom, and praise.
- Root: وحد (w-ḥ-d)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Oneness, uniqueness, singularity; the state of being one without peer or equal.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Oneness in essence, attributes, and acts; the tahlīl affirms tawḥīd — the absolute unity of God in His divinity, His sole possession of the kingdom, and His exclusive receipt of praise.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal usage denotes numerical oneness; theological usage denotes the affirmation of God's unique and incomparable nature, negating all plurality in His essence and attributes.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Conjunction and Disjunction (al-ʿAṭf wa al-Faṣl) — The phrase "lā ilāha illā Allāh" employs the grammatical structure of negation (lā) followed by exception (illā), establishing a complete disjunction between all false deities and the One True God, followed by the conjunction of His exclusive attributes: "waḥdahu lā sharīka lahu, lahu al-mulku wa lahu al-ḥamdu."
55:60.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'On Invocations and Supplications'

57:2.arabic: وهو مع ذلك قريب من كل موجود وهو أقرب إلى العبد من حبل الوريد وهو على كل شيء شهيد إذ لا يماثل قربه قرب الأجسام كما لا تماثل ذاته ذات الأجسام وأنه لا يحل في شيء ولا يحل فيه شيء تعالى عن أن يحويه مكان كما تقدس عن أن يحده زمان بل كان قبل أن خلق الزمان والمكان وهو الآن على ما عليه كان وأنه بائن عن خلقه بصفاته ليس في ذاته سواه ولا في سواه ذاته وأنه مقدس عن التغير والانتقال لا تحله الحوادث ولا تعتريه العوارض بل لا يزال في نعوت جلاله منزها عن الزوال وفي صفات كماله مستغنيا عن زيادة الاستكمال وأنه في ذاته معلوم الوجود بالعقول مرئ
57:2.english:
- **Root: خلق (khalaqa)**
  - *Lisan / Ayn:* Core meaning of measuring, proportioning, and fashioning; al-Khalil notes the root's application to the act of creation as bringing forth upon a measured determination.
  - *Al-Raghib (Mufradat):* "الخلق أصله: التقدير المستقيم" — Creation fundamentally signifies right/straight measurement; used for bringing into being from nothing (ibdāʿ) as in {خلق السماوات والأرض}, and for bringing forth from something as in {خلقكم من نفس واحدة}.
  - *Al-Zamakhshari (Asas):* Literal (ḥaqīqah): the craftsman's measuring before cutting. Metaphorical (majāz): "خلق الله الخلق: أوجده على تقدير أوجبته الحكمة" — God's creation is bringing into existence upon a measure necessitated by wisdom.
57:2.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'On Invocations and Supplications'

57:2.arabic: الأصل الأول العلم بأن صانع العالم قادر وأنه تعالى في قوله وهو على كل شيء قدير صادق لأن العالم محكم في صنعته مرتب في خلقته ومن رأى ثوبا من ديباج حسن النسج والتأليف متناسب التطريز والتطريف ثم توهم صدور نسجه عن ميت لا استطاعة له أو عن إنسان لا قدرة له كان منخلعا عن غريزة العقل ومنخرطا في سلك أهل الغباوة والجهل الأصل الثاني العلم بأنه تعالى عالم بجميع الموجودات ومحيط بكل المخلوقات لا يعزب عن علمه مثقال ذرة في الأرض ولا في السماء صادق في قوله وهو بكل شيء عليم ومرشد إلى صدقه بقوله تعالى ألا يعلم من خلق وهو اللطيف الخبير أرشدك
57:2.english: **The Eighth Principle: Knowledge that He, Exalted is He, is established upon His Throne (mustawin ʿalā ʿarshihi) in the sense that God, Exalted is He, intended by istiwāʾ — which is the sense that does not contradict the attribute of Majesty, nor does any mark of origination (ḥudūth) or passing away (fanāʾ) attach to it. And it is the sense intended by His saying — istiwāʾ toward the heaven — where He said in the Qur'an: {«ثُمَّ اسْتَوَىٰ إِلَى السَّمَاءِ وَهِيَ دُخَانٌ»} ("Then He directed Himself to the heaven, and it was smoke") [Fussilat 41:11]. And that is only by way of subjugation (qahr) and dominion (istīlāʾ), as the poet said:
57:2.section_title_en: The Revival of the Religious Sciences — Section 90: The Ten Principles Concerning Knowledge of the Divine Attributes
57:2.anchors:
- Root: ع ل م (ʿ-l-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root denoting the faculty of perception and comprehension; the mark or trace by which something is known.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "العلم: إدراك الشيء بحقيقته" — knowledge is the apprehension of a thing in its true reality, divided into apprehension of the essence and judgment upon it.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Distinguishes literal knowledge (ḥaqīqah) from awareness (shiʿr); here, it denotes certain, verified cognition of theological verities.
- Root: س و ي (s-w-y)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Root indicating straightness, equality, and levelness; from it derives istiwāʾ (establishing oneself upon, ascending to).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Istiwāʾ upon the Throne (al-ʿArsh) is a divine act of sovereign dominion, not corporeal settlement.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal sense of physical sitting is impossible for God; metaphorical sense (majāz) of qahr (overpowering) and istīlāʾ (dominion) is necessitated by reason and consensus.
- Root: ر أ ي (r-ʾ-y)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Visual perception; also opinion and discernment.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Ruʾyah (vision) of God in the Hereafter is a mode of disclosure (kashf) and knowledge (ʿilm), more complete than intellectual cognition, not conditioned by spatial direction.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal vision requires corporeality and direction; its application to God demands theological specification (takhṣīṣ) without nullifying the veracity of the scriptural promise.
- Root: ق د ر (q-d-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Power, measure, decree; the capacity to bring about an act.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Divine power (qudrah) is the negation of incapacity (ʿajz); absolute power belongs to God alone, while creatures possess limited capacity.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal power over an object; metaphorically, God's power encompasses all things without exertion or instrument.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Prepositional Interposition (باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور) — governing the permissible separation between the preposition and its object for rhetorical emphasis, applied here to the parsing of "إلى السماء" in the verse on istiwāʾ, where the prepositional phrase is delayed to highlight the divine act of sovereign direction toward the heavens.
57:2.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'On Invocations and Supplications'

57:2.arabic: قال في سوق من الأسواق لا إله إلا الله وحده لا شريك له له الملك وله الحمد يحيي ويميت وهو على كل شيء قدير كتب الله له ألف ألف حسنة ومحا عنه ألف الف سيئة وبنى له بيتا في الجنة ويروى إن العبد إذا قال لا إله إلا الله أتت إلى صحيفته فلا تمر على خطيئة إلى محتها حتى تجد حسنة مثلها فتجلس إلى جنبها (3) وفي الصحيح عن أيوب عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال من قال لا إله إلا الله وحده لا شريك له له الملك وله الحمد وهو على كل شيء قدير عشر مرات كان كمن أعتق أربعة أنفس من ولد إسماعيل صلى الله عليه وسلم (4) وفي الصحيح أيضا عن عبادة بن الصامت عن النبي صلى الل
57:2.english: The Prophet, peace be upon him, said: "The most excellent words that I and the prophets before me have uttered are: There is no god but Allah alone, with no partner." (1)
57:2.section_title_en: The Virtue of the Declaration of Divine Oneness (Fāḍīlat al-Tahlīl)
57:2.anchors:
- Root: اله (ʾ-l-h)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root denoting worship, servitude, and the act of deifying; the name "Allah" is the specific designation of the True Deity, distinguished from all false objects of worship.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الله: قيل: أصله إله فحذفت همزته، وأدخل عليها الألف واللام، فخص بالباري تعالى" — The name is exclusively reserved for the Creator, and "ilāh" is that which is worshipped; the declaration "lā ilāha illā Allāh" negates all false objects of worship and affirms sole divinity for God.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) usage denotes true worship and servitude; metaphorical (majāz) usage applies to anything taken as an object of devotion. The tahlīl is the verbal embodiment of sincere worship.
- Root: شرك (sh-r-k)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Partnership, sharing, or association; in theological context, the ascription of partners or associates to God in His divinity or worship.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الشركة والمشاركة: خلط الملكين" — The mixing of two ownerships; in Kalam, shirk is the association of another with God in that which is exclusively His, namely divinity and worship.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal usage denotes partnership in ownership; metaphorical usage in the phrase "lā sharīka lahu" (no partner has He) affirms God's exclusive and unshared sovereignty, kingdom, and praise.
- Root: وحد (w-ḥ-d)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Oneness, uniqueness, singularity; the state of being one without peer or equal.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Oneness in essence, attributes, and acts; the tahlīl affirms tawḥīd — the absolute unity of God in His divinity, His sole possession of the kingdom, and His exclusive receipt of praise.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal usage denotes numerical oneness; theological usage denotes the affirmation of God's unique and incomparable nature, negating all plurality in His essence and attributes.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Conjunction and Disjunction (al-ʿAṭf wa al-Faṣl) — The phrase "lā ilāha illā Allāh" employs the grammatical structure of negation (lā) followed by exception (illā), establishing a complete disjunction between all false deities and the One True God, followed by the conjunction of His exclusive attributes: "waḥdahu lā sharīka lahu, lahu al-mulku wa lahu al-ḥamdu."
57:2.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'On Invocations and Supplications'

57:4.arabic: الأرض وما يخرج منها وما ينزل من السماء وما يعرج فيها ومن فتن الليل والنهار ومن طوارق الليل والنهار إلا طارقا يطرق بخير يا رحمن فقال ذلك فطفئت شعلته وخر على وجهه (1) وقال الحسن نبئت أن جبرائيل عليه السلام أتى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال إن عفريتا من الجن يكيدك فإذا أويت إلى فراشك فاقرأ آية الكرسي // حديث الحسن نبئت أن جبريل أتى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال إن عفريتا من الجن يكيدك الحديث أخرجه ابن أبي الدنيا في مكايد الشيطان هكذا مرسلا وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم أتاني الشيطان فنازعني ثم نازع
57:4.english: If you say: "What then is the remedy for repelling Satan, and is the remembrance of God—exalted is He—and one's saying 'There is no might and no power except through God' (lā ḥawla wa lā quwwata illā billāh) sufficient for that?" — Know that the remedy of the heart in this matter is to seal these entry points by purifying the heart of these blameworthy traits. And that is something whose full exposition would be lengthy; our purpose in this quarter of the book is to explain the remedy for the destructive traits (al-ṣifāt al-muhlikāt), and each trait requires a separate book, as will be explained later. Yes — when the roots of these traits are severed from the heart, Satan may still make incursions (ijtiyāzāt) and pass through it with fleeting thoughts (khaṭarāt), but he has no stability therein. And what prevents him from passing through is the remembrance of God—exalted is He—because the reality of dhikr cannot take firm hold of the heart except after the heart is built up with God-consciousness (taqwā) and purified of blameworthy traits. Otherwise, the dhikr is but the whisper of the self (ḥadīth nafs), having no authority over the heart, and so it does not repel the dominion of Satan. For this reason, God—exalted is He—said: {إِنَّ الَّذِينَ اتَّقَوْا إِذَا مَسَّهُمْ طَائِفٌ مِنَ الشَّيْطَانِ تَذَكَّرُوا فَإِذَا هُمْ مُبْصِرُونَ} "Indeed, those who fear God — when an impulse touches them from Satan, they remember [Him], and at once they are insightful" (Q 7:201). He specified thereby the God-fearing (muttaqī).
57:4.section_title_en: The Revival of the Religious Sciences — Section 603: On the Remedy for Evil Presumption and the Repelling of Satan
57:4.anchors:
- Root: شيط (Shayṭ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of burning, scorching, or being consumed by fire; also used for one who is destroyed or whose blood is shed in vain.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): الشيطان (Satan) — the one who is far removed from divine mercy, derived from the root indicating his being burned or destroyed.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): "شاط اللحم" — meat that is burnt or spoiled by fire. Metaphorical (Majaz): "شاط دمه" — his blood was shed in vain (i.e., destroyed); "أشاط السلطان دمه" — the ruler declared his blood lawful to shed. Thus, Satan is so named for his being "burned" or "destroyed" by divine curse, and for his causing others to be destroyed.
- Root: قلب (Qalb)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The heart; also the act of turning, overturning, or revolving a thing from one state to another.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "قلب الشيء: تصريفه وصرفه عن وجه إلى وجه" — the turning and directing of a thing from one aspect to another. The heart (qalb) is so named for its constant fluctuation and turning between states.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "قلب الشيء قلبا: حوله عن وجهه" — to turn a thing from its face. Metaphorical: "رجل قلب حول: يقلب الأمور ويحتال" — a man who turns matters over and devises stratagems. The heart's "suwaydāʾ" (core/blackness) is its innermost center where Satan seeks to establish his seat.
- Root: ذكر (Dhikr)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Remembrance, mention, recollection; the opposite of forgetfulness (nisyān).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): الذكر is the presence of a thing in the mind, whether by utterance or by heart; true dhikr is that which takes root in the heart, not mere speech of the tongue.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: uttering with the tongue. Metaphorical: the heart's presence with God, which alone has authority over the soul and repels Satan's incursions.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — The verse {إِنَّ الَّذِينَ اتَّقَوْا إِذَا مَسَّهُمْ طَائِفٌ مِنَ الشَّيْطَانِ تَذَكَّرُوا} restricts the efficacy of dhikr in repelling Satan to the God-fearing (muttaqūn), whose hearts are emptied of passions, thereby specifying the condition for its effectiveness.

57:4.arabic: أعوذ بكلمات الله التامات التي لا يجاوزهن بر ولا فاجر من شر ما يلج في الأرض وما يخرج منها وما ينزل من السماء وما يعرج فيها ومن فتن الليل والنهار ومن طوارق الليل والنهار إلا طارقا يطرق بخير يا رحمن فقال ذلك فطفئت شعلته وخر على وجهه (1) وقال الحسن نبئت أن جبرائيل عليه السلام أتى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال إن عفريتا من الجن يكيدك فإذا أويت إلى فراشك فاقرأ آية الكرسي // حديث الحسن نبئت أن جبريل أتى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال إن عفريتا من الجن يكيدك الحديث أخرجه ابن أبي الدنيا في مكايد الشيطان هكذا مرسلا وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم أتاني الشيطان فنازعني ثم نازعني فأخذت
57:4.english: If you say: "What then is the remedy for repelling Satan, and is the remembrance of God—exalted is He—and one's saying 'There is no might and no power except through God' (lā ḥawla wa lā quwwata illā billāh) sufficient for that?" — Know that the remedy of the heart in this matter is to seal these entry points by purifying the heart of these blameworthy traits. And that is something whose full exposition would be lengthy; our purpose in this quarter of the book is to explain the remedy for the destructive traits (al-ṣifāt al-muhlikāt), and each trait requires a separate book, as will be explained later. Yes — when the roots of these traits are severed from the heart, Satan may still make incursions (ijtiyāzāt) and pass through it with fleeting thoughts (khaṭarāt), but he has no stability therein. And what prevents him from passing through is the remembrance of God—exalted is He—because the reality of dhikr cannot take firm hold of the heart except after the heart is built up with God-consciousness (taqwā) and purified of blameworthy traits. Otherwise, the dhikr is but the whisper of the self (ḥadīth nafs), having no authority over the heart, and so it does not repel the dominion of Satan. For this reason, God—exalted is He—said: {إِنَّ الَّذِينَ اتَّقَوْا إِذَا مَسَّهُمْ طَائِفٌ مِنَ الشَّيْطَانِ تَذَكَّرُوا فَإِذَا هُمْ مُبْصِرُونَ} "Indeed, those who fear God — when an impulse touches them from Satan, they remember [Him], and at once they are insightful" (Q 7:201). He specified thereby the God-fearing (muttaqī).

59:10.arabic: وثبت أقدامنا وانصرنا على القوم الكافرين ربنا اغفر لنا ولإخواننا الذين سبقونا بالإيمان ولا تجعل في قلوبنا غلا للذين آمنوا ربنا إنك رؤوف رحيم ربنا آتنا من لدنك رحمة وهيئ لنا من أمرنا رشدا ربنا آتنا في الدنيا حسنة وفي الآخرة حسنة وقنا عذاب النار ربنا إننا سمعنا مناديا ينادي للإيمان إلى قوله عز وجل إنك لا تخلف الميعاد ربنا لا تؤاخذنا إن نسينا أو أخطأنا ربنا إلى آخر السورة (3) رب اغفر لي ولوالدي وارحمهما كما ربياني صغيرا واغفر للمؤمنين والمؤمنات والمسلمين والمسلمات الأحياء منهم والأموات (4) رب اغفر وارحم وتجاوز عما تعلم وأنت الأعز الأكرم وأنت خير الراحمين وأنت خير الغافرين وإنا لله وإنا
59:10.english: And employ me in righteous deeds which You will accept from me. (1) O God, I ask You for pardon, well-being, good certainty, and soundness in this world and the next. (2) O You Whom sins do not harm and from Whom forgiveness does not diminish anything — grant me that which will not harm You, and give me that which will not diminish You. Our Lord, pour upon us patience and cause us to die as Muslims. You are our Protector in this world and the next; cause me to die as a Muslim and join me with the righteous. You are our Protector, so forgive us and have mercy upon us, and You are the Best of forgivers. And write for us good in this world and in the Hereafter — indeed, we have turned to You in repentance. Our Lord, upon You we rely, to You we turn in repentance, and to You is the final return. Our Lord, make us not a trial for the wrongdoing people. Our Lord, make us not a trial for those who disbelieve, and forgive us, our Lord — indeed, You are the Mighty, the Wise. Our Lord, forgive us our sins and our excesses in our affairs, make firm our feet, and grant us victory over the disbelieving people. Our Lord, forgive us and our brothers who preceded us in faith, and place not in our hearts any rancor toward those who believe — our Lord, indeed You are Kind, Merciful. Our Lord, grant us from Yourself mercy and prepare for us from our affair right guidance. Our Lord, give us good in this world and good in the Hereafter, and protect us from the chastisement of the Fire. Our Lord, indeed we have heard a caller calling to faith — to His saying, Mighty and Majestic: {«إنك لا تخلف الميعاد»} [آل عمران/ 194] — Our Lord, do not take us to task if we forget or err. Our Lord, to the end of the surah. (3) My Lord, forgive me and my parents, and have mercy upon them as they raised me when I was small; and forgive the believing men and the believing women, and the Muslim men and the Muslim women, the living among them and the dead. (4) My Lord, forgive, have mercy, and overlook what You know — and You are the Most Exalted, the Most Generous, the Best of the merciful, and the Best of the forgivers. And indeed, to God we belong and to Him we return; and there is no might and no power except through God, the Exalted, the Magnificent; and God suffices us, and He is the Best Disposer of affairs. And may God send blessings upon Muhammad, the Seal of the Prophets, and upon his family and his companions, and grant them abundant peace. (5)
59:10.section_title_en: Section 252 — Supplications for Morning and Evening: Comprehensive Prayers of the Prophet (ﷺ)
59:10.anchors:
- Root: لهم (l-h-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of swallowing/ingesting (iltihām); from this derives the sense of something being cast directly into the innermost recess of the heart (al-rawʿ).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الإلهام: إلقاء الشيء في الروع" — ilhām is the casting of a thing into the innermost consciousness, specifically from God or the higher assembly (al-malaʾ al-aʿlā). It is that which the Prophet (ﷺ) called "the touch of the angel" (limat al-malak) and "the breath of the Holy Spirit in my innermost heart" (nafth rūḥ al-qudus fī rawʿī).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): "ألهمه الله الخير: ألقاه في روعه" — God inspired him with good: He cast it into his innermost consciousness. Metaphorical (majāz): A horse that "swallows the ground" (yaltaḥimu al-arḍ) in swiftness; thus ilhām is the swift, direct ingress of divine guidance into the soul without intermediary effort.
- Root: حمد (ḥ-m-d)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The root denotes praise arising from recognition of voluntary excellence and beneficence; al-ḥamd is commendation of the beloved for their attributes and acts of goodness.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Praise (ḥamd) is the acknowledgment of beneficence (niʿmah) with reverence and love; it is distinguished from mere thanks (shukr) in that it is directed to the essence and attributes of the praised one, not solely to the benefit received.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "أحمد الله تعالى بجميع محامده" — I praise God with all His praiseworthy attributes. Metaphorical: "أحمدت صنيعه" — I found his deed praiseworthy; thus the tongue's praise must be matched by the heart's recognition of the praised one's perfection.
- Root: غفر (gh-f-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The root denotes covering and shielding; al-mighfar is the helmet that protects the head in battle.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الغفر: إلباس ما يصونه عن الدنس" — Forgiveness is the clothing of that which shields from filth. God's forgiveness (maghfirah) is His shielding of the servant from the touch of chastisement, covering the sin so that it is as though it never were.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "اللهم غفرًا" — O God, forgive. Metaphorical: The she-beasts that "did not forgive" their heedlessness (lam taghfir la-hā ghaflātuhā) — i.e., they did not shield their young from destruction; thus forgiveness is active protection, not mere erasure.
- Root: نفس (n-f-s)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The self, the soul; that which breathes and has vital spirit; also used for the very essence of a thing.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "النفس: الروح" — the soul is the spirit; and in God's saying {«ويحذركم الله نفسه»} [آل عمران/ 28], "His Self" means His very essence (dhāt), which — though grammatically expressed as an annexation implying distinction — is in reality identical, with no multiplicity in the Divine Essence.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "شيء نفيس" — a precious thing. Metaphorical: "دفق نفسه" — he poured out his blood/life; thus nafs is the seat of life, passion, and moral responsibility.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الدعاء والخبر (The Chapter of Supplication and Assertion) — Supplications (duʿāʾ) are grammatically constructed as optative sentences (inshāʾ ṭalabī) using the imperative (rabbighfir), the jussive (lā tuʾākhidhnā), and the vocative (rabbanā), yet they may embed assertive clauses (khabar) of praise (al-ḥamdu lillāh) and attestation (lā ilāha illā anta). The periodic structure of these prayers alternates between direct address to God (munādāh) and self-referential confession, requiring the translator to preserve the vocative force of "O God" and "Our Lord" without flattening into mere description.
59:10.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'On Invocations and Supplications'

59:10.arabic: اللهم اغفر للمهاجرين والأنصار واغفر لنا ولإخواننا الذين سبقونا بالإيمان اللهم لا تجعله آخر العهد من قبر نبيك ومن حرمك يا أرحم الراحمين ثم يأتي الروضة فيصلي فيها ركعتين ويكثر من الدعاء ما استطاع لقوله صلى الله عليه وسلم
59:10.english: I say: The Prophet ﷺ said: "Whoever visits me after my death, it is as though he visited me during my life." {من زارني بعد وفاتي فكأنما زارني في حياتي}
59:10.section_title_en: Section 210 — The Etiquette of Visiting the Prophet's Mosque and Grave in Medina
59:10.anchors:
- Root: زور (z-w-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of inclining toward, visiting, or intending a place or person; the visitor (zā'ir) is one who turns away from his own affairs toward another.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In theological context, ziyārah (visitation) of the Prophet ﷺ after death is an act of spiritual devotion (taqarrub), not a mere physical journey; its reward is tied to the sincerity of intention (niyyah).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (haqīqah) usage denotes physical approach; metaphorical (majāz) usage extends to seeking intercession (shafā'ah) and spiritual connection with the visited.
- Root: سلم (s-l-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Root denotes safety, peace, and deliverance from harm; the greeting "al-salāmu ʿalaykum" is a prayer for the recipient's immunity from all deficiency.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The greeting upon the Prophet ﷺ is a form of supplication (duʿā') and acknowledgment of his rank; it is also a renewal of the covenant (mīthāq) of obedience.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal usage is the exchange of safety; metaphorical usage in the visitation context signifies the visitor's submission and the Prophet's reciprocal blessing.
- Root: شفع (sh-f-ʿ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Root denotes pairing or joining; shafā'ah (intercession) is the act of the intercessor joining his own plea to that of the petitioner.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In Kalam, shafā'ah is a divinely granted honor (karāmah) to the Prophet ﷺ, conditional upon divine will; it is not an independent power but a mediated mercy.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: making a number even by adding one; metaphorical: the intercessor's elevation of the petitioner's rank before the king.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Prepositional Interposition (al-faṣl bayna al-jār wa al-majrūr) — The text employs extended vocative and prepositional structures (e.g., "al-salāmu ʿalayka yā Rasūl Allāh") where the syntactic pause after each invocation is permissible and rhetorically deliberate, mirroring the classical allowance for separation between the governing particle and its object for emphasis.
59:10.topic: Al-Ghazali on the journey of the soul, death, and the Hereafter, from 'Mysteries of Hajj'
