59:22.arabic: منيبا أشهد الله وأشهد ملائكته وأنبيائه ورسله وحملة عرشه ومن خلقه ومن هو خالقه بأنه هو الله الذي لا إله إلا هو وحده لا شريك له وأن محمدا عبده ورسوله صلى الله عليه وسلم وإن الجنة حق وأن النار حق والحوض حق والشفاعة حق ومنكرا ونكيرا حق ووعدك حق ووعيدك حق ولقاءك حق والساعة آتية لا ريب فيها وأن الله يبعث من في القبور على ذلك أحيا وعليه أموت وعليه أبعث إن شاء الله اللهم أنت ربي لا إله إلا أنت خلقتني وأنا عبدك وأنا على عهدك ووعدك ما استطعت أعوذ بك اللهم من شر ما صنعت ومن شر كل ذي شر اللهم إني ظلمت نفسي فاغفر لي ذنوبي فإنه لا يغفر الذنوب إلا
59:22.english: It is narrated that Yūnus ibn ʿUbayd saw a man in a dream — a man who had been killed as a martyr in the lands of the Byzantines — and he said to him: "What is the most excellent deed that you witnessed?" He replied: "I witnessed the glorifications (tasbīḥāt) of Ibn al-Muʿtamir holding a station with Allah, Mighty and Majestic." And they are these: "Glory be to Allah (subḥāna Allāh), and praise be to Allah (al-ḥamdu li-Allāh), and there is no god but Allah (lā ilāha illā Allāh), and Allah is the Greatest (Allāhu akbar), and there is no might and no power except through Allah, the Most High, the Magnificent — to the number of what He has created, and the number of what He is creating, and the weight of what He has created, and the weight of what He is creating, and the fill of what He has created, and the fill of what He is creating, and the fill of His heavens and the fill of His earth, and the like of that, and multiples of that, and the number of His creation, and the weight of His Throne, and the utmost extent of His mercy, and the ink of His words, and the limit of His good pleasure, until He is pleased, and when He is pleased, [then] the number of what His creation has remembered Him with in all that has passed, and the number of what they will remember Him with in what remains, in every year, and month, and Friday, and day, and night, and hour of the hours, and breath of the breaths, and age of the ages, from eternity to eternity — the eternity of this world and the eternity of the Hereafter — and more than that, whose beginning does not cease and whose end does not come to an end."
59:22.section_title_en: The Supplications of Ibn al-Muʿtamir (Sulaymān al-Taymī) and His Glorifications, and the Supplication of Ibrāhīm ibn Adham — May Allah Be Well Pleased with Them
59:22.anchors:
- Root: سبح (s-b-ḥ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of swift motion (in water or air); extended to the act of prayer and glorification.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "التسبيح: تنزيه الله تعالى. وأصله: المر السريع في عبادة الله تعالى" — Glorification is the declaration of Allah's transcendence; its root is the swift passage in worship of Allah.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "سبحت الله وسبحت له" — to declare Him transcendent. Metaphorical: "والنجوم تسبح في الفلك" — the stars glide in their orbits, a metaphor for their obedient motion.
- Root: حمد (ḥ-m-d)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of praise and commendation for a beneficial act.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Praise (ḥamd) is the acknowledgment of beneficence with reverence; it is due to Allah alone in His absolute perfection.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "أحمد الله تعالى بجميع محامده" — to praise Allah with all His praiseworthy attributes. Metaphorical: "أحمدت الأرض: رضيت سكناها" — to find a thing agreeable, extending praise to non-verbal contexts.
- Root: لهم (l-h-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of swift swallowing or devouring.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الإلهام: إلقاء الشيء في الروع" — Inspiration is the casting of a thing into the heart/mind (al-rawʿ), specifically from Allah or the higher assembly.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "ألهمه الله الخير: ألقاه في روعه" — Allah inspired him with good. Metaphorical: "جواد يلتهم الأرض" — a swift horse devours the ground, extending to rapid comprehension.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The permissibility of interposing elements between a preposition and its object when the clause remains grammatically sound, as seen in the extended supplicatory sentences.
59:22.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications, prayers, and their spiritual power, from 'On Invocations and Supplications'

59:22.arabic: القلوب فوالله الذي لا إله إلا هو ما ذلك إلا لأن المعلمين علموا لغير الله تعالى والمتعلمين تعلموا لغير الله تعالى وفي التوراة والإنجيل مكتوب لا تطلبوا علم ما لم تعلموا حتى تعملوا بما علمتم وقال حذيفة رضي الله عنه إنكم في زمان من ترك فيه عشر ما يعلم هلك وسيأتي زمان من عمل فيه بعشر ما يعلم نجا وذلك لكثرة البطالين واعلم أن مثل العالم مثل القاضي وقد قال صلى الله عليه وسلم القضاة ثلاثة قاض قضى بالحق وهو يعلم فذلك في الجنة وقاض قضى بالجور وهو يعلم أو لا يعلم فهو في النار وقاض قضى بغير ما أمر الله به فهو في النار (2) وقال كعب رحمه الله يكون في آخر الزمان علماء يزهدون الناس في الدنيا ولا يزهدون ويخوفون الناس ولا يخافون وينهون عن غشيان الولاة ويأتونهم ويؤثرون الدنيا على الآخرة يأكلون بألسنتهم يقربون الأغنياء دون الفقراء يتغايرون على العلم كما تتغاير النساء على الرجال يغضب أحدهم على جليسه إذا جالس غيره أولئك الجبارون أعداء الرحمن وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم إن الشيطان ربما يسوفكم بالعلم فقيل يا رسول الله وكيف ذلك قال صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول اطلب العلم ولا تعمل حتى تعلم فلا يزال للعلم قائلا وللعمل مسوفا حتى يموت وما عمل (3) وقال سرى السقطي اعتزل رجل للتعبد كان حريصا على طلب علم الظاهر فسألته فقال رأيت في النوم قائلا يقول لي إلى كم تضيع العلم ضيعك الله فقلت إني لأحفظه فقال حفظ العلم العمل به فتركت الطلب وأقبلت على العمل وقال ابن مسعود رضي الله عنه ليس العلم بكثرة الرواية إنما العلم الخشية وقال الحسن تعلموا ما شئتم أن تعلموا فوالله لا يأجركم الله حتى تعملوا فإن السفهاء همتهم الرواية والعلماء همتهم الرعاية وقال مالك رحمه الله إن طلب العلم لحسن وإن نشره لحسن إذا صحت فيه النية ولكن انظر ما يلزمك من حين تصبح إلى حين تمسي فلا تؤثرن عليه شيئا وقال ابن مسعود رضي الله عنه أنزل القرآن ليعمل به فاتخذتم دراسته عملا وسيأتي قوم يثقفونه مثل القناة ليسوا بخياركم والعالم الذي لا يعمل كالمريض الذي يصف الدواء وكالجائع الذي يصف لذائذ الأطعمة ولا يجدها وفي مثله قوله تعالى ولكم الويل مما تصفون وفي الخبر إنما أخاف على أمتي زلة عالم وجدال منافق في القرآن (1) ومنها أن تكون عنايته بتحصيل العلم النافع في الآخرة المرغب في الطاعات مجتنبا للعلوم التي يقل نفعها ويكثر فيها الجدال والقيل والقال فمثال من يعرض عن علم الأعمال ويشتغل بالجدال مثل رجل مريض به علل كثيرة وقد صادف طبيبا حاذقا في وقت ضيق يخشى فواته فاشتغل بالسؤال عن خاصية العقاقير والأدوية وغرائب الطب وترك مهمه الذي هو مؤاخذ به وذلك محض السفه وقد روي أن رجلا جاء رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال علمني من غرائب العلم فقال له ما صنعت في رأس العلم فقال وما رأس العلم فقال صلى الله عليه وسلم هل عرفت الرب تعالى قال نعم قال فما صنعت في حقه قال ما شاء الله فقال صلى الله عليه وسلم هل عرفت الموت قال نعم قال فما أعددت له قال ما شاء الله قال صلى الله عليه وسلم إذهب فأحكم ما هناك ثم تعال نعلمك من غرائب العلم (2) بل ينبغي أن يكون المتعلم من جنس ما روي عن حاتم الأصم تلميذ شقيق البلخي رضي الله عنهما أنه قال له شقيق منذ كم صحبتني قال حاتم منذ ثلاث وثلاثين سنة قال فما تعلمت مني في هذه المدة قال ثماني مسائل قال شقيق له إنا لله وإنا إليه راجعون ذهب عمري معك ولم تتعلم إلا ثماني مسائل قال يا أستاذ لم أتعلم غيرها وإني لا أحب أن أكذب فقال هات هذه الثماني مسائل حتى أسمعها قال حاتم نظرت إلى هذا الخلق فرأيت كل واحد يحب محبوبا فهو مع محبوبه إلى القبر فإذا وصل إلى القبر فارقه فجعلت الحسنات محبوبي فإذا دخلت القبر دخل محبوبي معي فقال أحسنت يا حاتم فما الثانية فقال نظرت في قول الله عز وجل وأما من خاف مقام ربه ونهى النفس عن الهوى فإن الجنة هي المأوى فعلمت أن قوله سبحانه وتعالى هو الحق فأجهدت نفسي في دفع الهوى حتى استقرت على طاعة الله تعالى الثالثة أني نظرت إلى هذا الخلق فرأيت كل ممن معه شيء له قيمة ومقدار رفعه وحفظه ثم نظرت إلى قول الله عز وجل ما عندكم ينفذ وما عند الله باق فكلما وقع معي شيء له قيمة ومقدار وجهته إلى الله ليبقى عنده محفوظا الرابعة أني نظرت إلى هذا الخلق فرأيت كل واحد منهم يرجع إلى المال وإلى الحسب والشرف والنسب فنظرت فيها فإذا هي لا شيء ثم نظرت إلى قول الله تعالى إن أكرمكم عند الله أتقاكم فعملت في التقوى حتى أكون عند الله كريما الخامسة أني نظرت إلى هذا الخلق وهم يطعن بعضهم في بعض ويلعن بعضهم بعضا وأصل هذا كله الحسد ثم نظرت إلى قول الله عز وجل نحن قسمنا بينهم معيشتهم في الحياة الدنيا فتركت الحسد واجتنبت الخلق وعلمت أن القسمة من عند الله سبحانه وتعالى فتركت عداوة الخلق عني السادسة نظرت إلى هذا الخلق يبغي بعضهم على بعض ويقاتل بعضهم بعضا فرجعت إلى قول الله عز وجل إن الشيطان لكم عدو فاتخذوه عدوا فعاديته وحده واجتهدت في أخذ حذري منه لأن الله تعالى شهد عليه أنه عدو لي فتركت عداوة الخلق غيره السابعة نظرت إلى هذا الخلق فرأيت كل واحد منهم يطلب هذه الكسرة فيذل فيها نفسه ويدخل فيما لا يحل له ثم نظرت إلى قوله تعالى وما من دابة في الأرض إلا على الله رزقها فعلمت أني واحد من هذه الدواب التي على الله رزقها فاشتغلت بما لله تعالى علي وتركت ما لي عنده الثامنة نظرت إلى هذا الخلق فرأيتهم كلهم متوكلين على مخلوق هذا على ضيعته وهذا على تجارته وهذا على صناعته وهذا على صحة بدنه وكل مخلوق متوكل على مخلوق مثله فرجعت إلى قوله تعالى ومن يتوكل على الله فهو حسبه فتوكلت على الله عز وجل فهو حسبي قال شقيق يا حاتم وفقك الله تعالى فإني نظرت في علوم التوراة والإنجيل والزبور والفرقان العظيم فوجدت جميع أنواع الخير والديانة وهي تدور على هذه الثمان مسائل فمن استعملها فقد استعمل الكتب الأربعة فهذا الفن من العلم لا يهتم بإدراكه والتفطن له إلا علماء الآخرة فأما علماء الدنيا فيشتغلون بما يتيسر به اكتساب المال والجاه ويهملون أمثال هذه العلوم التي بعث الله بها الأنبياء كلهم عليهم السلام وقال الضحاك بن مزاحم أدركتهم وما يتعلم بعضهم من بعض إلا الورع وهم اليوم ما يتعلمون إلا الكلام ومنها أن يكون غير مائل إلى الترفه في المطعم والمشرب والتنعم في الملبس والتجمل في الأثاث والمسكن بل يؤثر الاقتصاد في جميع ذلك ويتشبه فيه بالسلف رحمهم الله تعالى ويميل إلى الاكتفاء بالأقل في جميع ذلك وكلما زاد إلى طرف القلة ميله ازداد من الله قربه وارتفع في علماء الآخرة حزبه ويشهد لذلك ما حكى عن أبي عبد الله الخواص وكان من أصحاب حاتم الأصم قال دخلت مع حاتم إلى الري ومعنا ثلثمائة وعشرون رجلا يريد الحج وعليهم الزرمانقات وليس معهم جراب ولا طعام فدخلنا على رجل من التجار متقشف يحب المساكين فأضافنا تلك الليلة فلما كان من الغد قال لحاتم ألك حاجة فإني أريد أن أعود فقيها لنا هو عليل قال حاتم عيادة المريض فيها فضل والنظر إلى الفقيه عبادة وأنا أيضا أجيء معك وكان العليل محمد بن مقاتل قاضي الري فلما جئنا إلى الباب فإذا قصر مشرف حسن فبقي حاتم متفكرا يقول باب عالم على هذه الحالة ثم أذن لهم فدخلوا فإذا دار حسناء فوراء واسعة نزهة وإذا بزة وستور فبقي حاتم متفكرا ثم دخلوا إلى المجلس الذي هو فيه وإذا بفرش وطيئة وهو راقد عليها وعند رأسه غلام وبيده مذبة فقعد الزائر عند رأسه وسأل عن حاله وحاتم قائم فأومأ إليه ابن مقاتل أن اجلس فقال لا أجلس فقال لعل لك حاجة فقال نعم قال وما هي قال مسئلة أسألك عنها قال سل قال قم فاستو جالسا حتى أسألك فاستوى جالسا قال حاتم علمك هذا من أين أخذته فقال من الثقات حدثوني به قال عمن قال عن أصحاب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال وأصحاب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عمن قال عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال ورسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عمن قال عن جبرائيل عليه السلام عن الله عز وجل قال حاتم ففيما أداه جبرائيل عليه السلام عن الله عز وجل إلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وأداه رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إلى أصحابه وأصحابه إلى الثقات وأداه الثقات إليك هل سمعت فيه من كان في داره إشراف وكانت سعتها أكثر كان له عند الله عز وجل المنزلة أكبر قال لا قال فكيف سمعت قال سمعت أنه من زهد في الدنيا ورغب في الآخرة وأحب المساكين وقدم لآخرته كانت له عند الله المنزلة قال له حاتم فأنت بمن اقتديت ابالنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وأصحابه رضي الله عنهم والصالحين رحمهم الله أم بفرعون ونمروذ أول من بنى بالجص والآجر يا علماء السوء مثلكم يراه الجاهل المتكالب على الدنيا الراغب فيها فيقول العالم على هذه الحالة أفلا أكون أنا شرا منه وخرج من عنده فازداد ابن مقاتل مرضا وبلغ أهل الري ما جرى بينه وبين ابن مقاتل فقالوا له إن الطنافسي بقزوين أكثر توسعا منه فسار حاتم متعمدا فدخل عليه فقال رحمك الله أنا رجل أعجمي أحب أن تعلمني مبتدأ ديني ومفتاح صلاتي كيف أتوضأ للصلاة قال نعم وكرامة يا غلام هات إناء فيه ماء فأتى به فقعد الطنافسي فتوضأ ثلاثا ثلاثا ثم قال هكذا فتوضأ فقال حاتم مكانك حتى أتوضأ بين يديك فيكون أوكد لما أريد فقام الطنافسي وقعد حاتم فتوضأ ثم غسل ذراعيه أربعا أربعا فقال الطنافسي يا هذا أسرفت قال له حاتم فبماذا قال غسلت ذراعيك أربعا فقال حاتم يا سبحان الله العظيم أنا في كف من ماء أسرفت وأنت في جميع هذا كله لم تسرف فعلم الطنافسي
59:22.english: Know that the scholar who does not act upon his knowledge is condemned by the Book, the Sunnah, and the sayings of the sages. God, exalted be He, said: {«يا أيها الذين آمنوا لم تقولون ما لا تفعلون * كبر مقتا عند الله أن تقولوا ما لا تفعلون»} ("O you who believe, why do you say what you do not do? Most hateful it is to God that you say what you do not do"). And He said: {«أتأمرون الناس بالبر وتنسون أنفسكم»} ("Do you command people to righteousness while you forget yourselves?"). And He said: {«ومن الناس من يعجبك قوله في الحياة الدنيا ويشهد الله على ما في قلبه وهو ألد الخصام»} ("And among people is he whose speech pleases you in the worldly life, and he calls God to witness what is in his heart, yet he is the fiercest of opponents").
59:22.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'On Invocations and Supplications'

59:22.arabic: الأقصد فيما نراه والعلم عند الله عز وجل فيه وهو عالم الغيب والشهادة وهو الرحمن الرحيم بيان دواء الرياء وطريق معالجة القلب فيه قد عرفت مما سبق أن الرياء محبط للأعمال وسبب للمقت عند الله تعالى وأنه من كبائر المهلكات وما هذا وصفه فجدير بالتشمير عن ساق الجد في إزالته ولو بالمجاهدة وتحمل المشاق فلا شفاء إلا في شرب الأدوية المرة البشعة وهذه مجاهدة يضطر إليها العباد كلهم إذ الصبي يخلق ضعيف العقل والتمييز ممتد العين إلى الخلق كثير الطمع فيهم فيرى الناس يتصنع بعضهم لبعض فيغلب عليه حب التصنع بالضرورة ويرسخ ذلك في نفسه وإنما يشعر بكونه مهلكا
59:22.english: Bearing witness to ostentation and to these causes — that they are what impel the ostentatious person — is what Abū Mūsā narrated: that a Bedouin asked the Prophet, peace be upon him, and said: "O Messenger of God, a man fights..." // The ḥadīth of Abū Mūsā that a Bedouin said: "O Messenger of God, a man fights out of zeal (ḥamīyah)" — the ḥadīth is agreed upon [by al-Bukhārī and Muslim]. Its meaning is that he disdains being overpowered or being blamed as one overpowered and vanquished. And he said: "And a man fights to show his position (līurā makānahū)" — and this is the pursuit of the pleasure of status and power.
59:22.section_title_en: The Revival of the Religious Sciences — Section 825: On the Night Prayer of Tarāwīḥ, the Blending of Intentions, and the Cure for Ostentation (Riyā')
59:22.anchors:
- Root: صلا (Ṣ-L-Y)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core sense of "igniting with fire" and "enduring heat"; extended to the ritual prayer as an act of "burning devotion" or standing in worship.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "أصل الصلي الإيقاد بالنار" — the root denotes exposure to fire; in religious usage, ṣalāh is the act of turning wholly toward God, burning away distraction.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) = kindling/roasting; metaphorical (majāz) = the prayer as a spiritual "roasting" of the ego's pretensions.
- Root: فرض (F-R-Ḍ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "Cutting into something solid" — a decisive incision; hence a divinely ordained obligation as a fixed, incised decree.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الفرض كالإيجاب لكن الإيجاب يقال اعتبارا بوقوعه وثباته، والفرض بقطع الحكم فيه" — farḍ is obligation with a decisive, cut-off determination; it is the binding command that severs excuses.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal = the obligatory act itself (farīḍah); metaphorical = a "huge, weighty" matter (līḥyah fāriḍ) that presses down — here, the weight of divine command on the soul.
- Root: بعث (B-ʿ-Th)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "To rouse, stir up, and send forth" — the awakening of a motive.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "أصل البعث: إثارة الشيء وتوجيهه" — the incitement and direction of a thing; in moral psychology, the internal impulse (bāʿith) that moves one to act.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal = sending a messenger or rousing from sleep; metaphorical = the stirring of intention (niyyah) that propels the will.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — Used to isolate the sole efficient cause of an act (e.g., "the obligation alone did not suffice as a rousing motive"), distinguishing what is predicated exclusively from what is merely concomitant.
59:22.topic: Al-Ghazali on purifying the character, moral diseases, and spiritual remedies, from 'Condemnation of Status and Ostentation'

59:23.arabic: منيبا أشهد الله وأشهد ملائكته وأنبيائه ورسله وحملة عرشه ومن خلقه ومن هو خالقه بأنه هو الله الذي لا إله إلا هو وحده لا شريك له وأن محمدا عبده ورسوله صلى الله عليه وسلم وإن الجنة حق وأن النار حق والحوض حق والشفاعة حق ومنكرا ونكيرا حق ووعدك حق ووعيدك حق ولقاءك حق والساعة آتية لا ريب فيها وأن الله يبعث من في القبور على ذلك أحيا وعليه أموت وعليه أبعث إن شاء الله اللهم أنت ربي لا إله إلا أنت خلقتني وأنا عبدك وأنا على عهدك ووعدك ما استطعت أعوذ بك اللهم من شر ما صنعت ومن شر كل ذي شر اللهم إني ظلمت نفسي فاغفر لي ذنوبي فإنه لا يغفر الذنوب إلا
59:23.english: It is narrated that Yūnus ibn ʿUbayd saw a man in a dream — a man who had been killed as a martyr in the lands of the Byzantines — and he said to him: "What is the most excellent deed that you witnessed?" He replied: "I witnessed the glorifications (tasbīḥāt) of Ibn al-Muʿtamir holding a station with Allah, Mighty and Majestic." And they are these: "Glory be to Allah (subḥāna Allāh), and praise be to Allah (al-ḥamdu li-Allāh), and there is no god but Allah (lā ilāha illā Allāh), and Allah is the Greatest (Allāhu akbar), and there is no might and no power except through Allah, the Most High, the Magnificent — to the number of what He has created, and the number of what He is creating, and the weight of what He has created, and the weight of what He is creating, and the fill of what He has created, and the fill of what He is creating, and the fill of His heavens and the fill of His earth, and the like of that, and multiples of that, and the number of His creation, and the weight of His Throne, and the utmost extent of His mercy, and the ink of His words, and the limit of His good pleasure, until He is pleased, and when He is pleased, [then] the number of what His creation has remembered Him with in all that has passed, and the number of what they will remember Him with in what remains, in every year, and month, and Friday, and day, and night, and hour of the hours, and breath of the breaths, and age of the ages, from eternity to eternity — the eternity of this world and the eternity of the Hereafter — and more than that, whose beginning does not cease and whose end does not come to an end."
59:23.section_title_en: The Supplications of Ibn al-Muʿtamir (Sulaymān al-Taymī) and His Glorifications, and the Supplication of Ibrāhīm ibn Adham — May Allah Be Well Pleased with Them
59:23.anchors:
- Root: سبح (s-b-ḥ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of swift motion (in water or air); extended to the act of prayer and glorification.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "التسبيح: تنزيه الله تعالى. وأصله: المر السريع في عبادة الله تعالى" — Glorification is the declaration of Allah's transcendence; its root is the swift passage in worship of Allah.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "سبحت الله وسبحت له" — to declare Him transcendent. Metaphorical: "والنجوم تسبح في الفلك" — the stars glide in their orbits, a metaphor for their obedient motion.
- Root: حمد (ḥ-m-d)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of praise and commendation for a beneficial act.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Praise (ḥamd) is the acknowledgment of beneficence with reverence; it is due to Allah alone in His absolute perfection.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "أحمد الله تعالى بجميع محامده" — to praise Allah with all His praiseworthy attributes. Metaphorical: "أحمدت الأرض: رضيت سكناها" — to find a thing agreeable, extending praise to non-verbal contexts.
- Root: لهم (l-h-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of swift swallowing or devouring.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الإلهام: إلقاء الشيء في الروع" — Inspiration is the casting of a thing into the heart/mind (al-rawʿ), specifically from Allah or the higher assembly.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "ألهمه الله الخير: ألقاه في روعه" — Allah inspired him with good. Metaphorical: "جواد يلتهم الأرض" — a swift horse devours the ground, extending to rapid comprehension.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The permissibility of interposing elements between a preposition and its object when the clause remains grammatically sound, as seen in the extended supplicatory sentences.
59:23.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications, prayers, and their spiritual power, from 'On Invocations and Supplications'

59:23.arabic: القلوب فوالله الذي لا إله إلا هو ما ذلك إلا لأن المعلمين علموا لغير الله تعالى والمتعلمين تعلموا لغير الله تعالى وفي التوراة والإنجيل مكتوب لا تطلبوا علم ما لم تعلموا حتى تعملوا بما علمتم وقال حذيفة رضي الله عنه إنكم في زمان من ترك فيه عشر ما يعلم هلك وسيأتي زمان من عمل فيه بعشر ما يعلم نجا وذلك لكثرة البطالين واعلم أن مثل العالم مثل القاضي وقد قال صلى الله عليه وسلم القضاة ثلاثة قاض قضى بالحق وهو يعلم فذلك في الجنة وقاض قضى بالجور وهو يعلم أو لا يعلم فهو في النار وقاض ق
59:23.english: Know that the scholar who does not act upon his knowledge is condemned by the Book, the Sunnah, and the sayings of the sages. God, exalted be He, said: {«يا أيها الذين آمنوا لم تقولون ما لا تفعلون * كبر مقتا عند الله أن تقولوا ما لا تفعلون»} ("O you who believe, why do you say what you do not do? Most hateful it is to God that you say what you do not do"). And He said: {«أتأمرون الناس بالبر وتنسون أنفسكم»} ("Do you command people to righteousness while you forget yourselves?"). And He said: {«ومن الناس من يعجبك قوله في الحياة الدنيا ويشهد الله على ما في قلبه وهو ألد الخصام»} ("And among people is he whose speech pleases you in the worldly life, and he calls God to witness what is in his heart, yet he is the fiercest of opponents").
59:23.topic: Al-Ghazali on the journey of the soul, death, and the Hereafter, from 'Remembrance of Death and Afterlife'

59:23.arabic: وكقوله تعالى الملك القدوس السلام المؤمن المهيمن العزيز الجبار المتكبر فليتأمل معاني هذه الأسماء والصفات لينكشف له أسرارها فتحتها معان
59:23.english: Ali, may God be pleased with him, said: "There is no good in worship that lacks understanding (fiqh), nor in recitation that lacks reflection."
59:23.section_title_en: The Third Book on the Inward Acts During Recitation — Ten in Number
59:23.anchors:
- Root: دبر (d-b-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The rear, the back part; what comes after; to turn one's back; the end or sequel of a thing.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): That which is opposite of "front" (qabal); used metaphorically for what follows or comes after; "adbar al-nahar" — the latter part of the day; "adbar al-sujud" — the concluding portions of prayers.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the back or hind part. Metaphorical: what comes at the end, the sequel, the consequence of an affair.
- Root: قلب (q-l-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To turn over, to overturn, to transform; the heart as that which is constantly turning and fluctuating between states.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The turning and directing of a thing from one face to another; al-taqallub — the constant changing and fluctuation; the heart (qalb) is so named for its perpetual turning about of resolutions and states.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: to turn a thing over from its face. Metaphorical: to ponder, to examine thoroughly, to turn a matter over in the mind — "qallaba al-amr" — he examined the affair from all sides.
- Root: ختم (kh-t-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To seal, to stamp, to imprint; the seal or stamp itself.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Sealing and stamping — used both for the act of impressing and the impression left; metaphorically employed for securing a thing and preventing access to it, as in {«ختم الله على قلوبهم»} (God sealed their hearts).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: placing a seal upon something. Metaphorical: to conclude, to finish, to bring to an end — "khatama al-Qur'an" — he completed the recitation of the Quran.
- Root: بقي (b-q-y)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To remain, to endure, to persist; the lasting and continuing of a thing.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The persistence of a thing upon its original state; that which remains (al-baqi) is of two kinds: that which remains by itself without limit — and that is the Creator, may He be exalted — and that which remains by another, which is everything other than Him.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: to remain, to stay. Metaphorical: "baqiya al-shay'" — the enduring of a thing; "ma baqiyat minhum baqiyah" — not one of them remained.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — When the construction "innama" is employed, it restricts the predicate to the subject alone, excluding all else. This is pertinent here as the author delimits the inward acts of recitation to precisely ten, no more and no less.
59:23.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Etiquette of Quran Recitation'

60:4.arabic: حسنة وفي الآخرة إنا هدنا إليك ربنا عليك توكلنا وإليك أنبنا وإليك المصير ربنا لا تجعلنا فتنة للقوم الظالمين ربنا لا تجعلنا فتنة للذين كفروا واغفر لنا ربنا إنك أنت العزيز الحكيم ربنا اغفر لنا ذنوبنا وإسرافنا في أمرنا وثبت أقدامنا وانصرنا على القوم الكافرين ربنا اغفر لنا ولإخواننا الذين سبقونا بالإيمان ولا تجعل في قلوبنا غلا للذين آمنوا ربنا إنك رؤوف رحيم ربنا آتنا من لدنك رحمة وهيئ لنا من أمرنا رشدا ربنا آتنا في الدنيا حسنة وفي الآخرة حسنة وقنا عذاب النار ربنا إننا سمعنا مناديا ينادي للإيمان إلى قوله عز وجل إنك لا تخلف الميعاد ربنا لا تؤاخذنا إن نسينا أو أخطأنا ربنا إلى آخر السورة (3) رب اغفر لي ولوالدي وارحمهما كما ربيان
60:4.english: And employ me in righteous deeds which You will accept from me. (1) O God, I ask You for pardon, well-being, good certainty, and soundness in this world and the next. (2) O You Whom sins do not harm and from Whom forgiveness does not diminish anything — grant me that which will not harm You, and give me that which will not diminish You. Our Lord, pour upon us patience and cause us to die as Muslims. You are our Protector in this world and the next; cause me to die as a Muslim and join me with the righteous. You are our Protector, so forgive us and have mercy upon us, and You are the Best of forgivers. And write for us good in this world and in the Hereafter — indeed, we have turned to You in repentance. Our Lord, upon You we rely, to You we turn in repentance, and to You is the final return. Our Lord, make us not a trial for the wrongdoing people. Our Lord, make us not a trial for those who disbelieve, and forgive us, our Lord — indeed, You are the Mighty, the Wise. Our Lord, forgive us our sins and our excesses in our affairs, make firm our feet, and grant us victory over the disbelieving people. Our Lord, forgive us and our brothers who preceded us in faith, and place not in our hearts any rancor toward those who believe — our Lord, indeed You are Kind, Merciful. Our Lord, grant us from Yourself mercy and prepare for us from our affair right guidance. Our Lord, give us good in this world and good in the Hereafter, and protect us from the chastisement of the Fire. Our Lord, indeed we have heard a caller calling to faith — to His saying, Mighty and Majestic: {«إنك لا تخلف الميعاد»} [آل عمران/ 194] — Our Lord, do not take us to task if we forget or err. Our Lord, to the end of the surah. (3) My Lord, forgive me and my parents, and have mercy upon them as they raised me when I was small; and forgive the believing men and the believing women, and the Muslim men and the Muslim women, the living among them and the dead. (4) My Lord, forgive, have mercy, and overlook what You know — and You are the Most Exalted, the Most Generous, the Best of the merciful, and the Best of the forgivers. And indeed, to God we belong and to Him we return; and there is no might and no power except through God, the Exalted, the Magnificent; and God suffices us, and He is the Best Disposer of affairs. And may God send blessings upon Muhammad, the Seal of the Prophets, and upon his family and his companions, and grant them abundant peace. (5)
60:4.section_title_en: Section 252 — Supplications for Morning and Evening: Comprehensive Prayers of the Prophet (ﷺ)
60:4.anchors:
- Root: لهم (l-h-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of swallowing/ingesting (iltihām); from this derives the sense of something being cast directly into the innermost recess of the heart (al-rawʿ).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الإلهام: إلقاء الشيء في الروع" — ilhām is the casting of a thing into the innermost consciousness, specifically from God or the higher assembly (al-malaʾ al-aʿlā). It is that which the Prophet (ﷺ) called "the touch of the angel" (limat al-malak) and "the breath of the Holy Spirit in my innermost heart" (nafth rūḥ al-qudus fī rawʿī).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): "ألهمه الله الخير: ألقاه في روعه" — God inspired him with good: He cast it into his innermost consciousness. Metaphorical (majāz): A horse that "swallows the ground" (yaltaḥimu al-arḍ) in swiftness; thus ilhām is the swift, direct ingress of divine guidance into the soul without intermediary effort.
- Root: حمد (ḥ-m-d)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The root denotes praise arising from recognition of voluntary excellence and beneficence; al-ḥamd is commendation of the beloved for their attributes and acts of goodness.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Praise (ḥamd) is the acknowledgment of beneficence (niʿmah) with reverence and love; it is distinguished from mere thanks (shukr) in that it is directed to the essence and attributes of the praised one, not solely to the benefit received.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "أحمد الله تعالى بجميع محامده" — I praise God with all His praiseworthy attributes. Metaphorical: "أحمدت صنيعه" — I found his deed praiseworthy; thus the tongue's praise must be matched by the heart's recognition of the praised one's perfection.
- Root: غفر (gh-f-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The root denotes covering and shielding; al-mighfar is the helmet that protects the head in battle.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الغفر: إلباس ما يصونه عن الدنس" — Forgiveness is the clothing of that which shields from filth. God's forgiveness (maghfirah) is His shielding of the servant from the touch of chastisement, covering the sin so that it is as though it never were.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "اللهم غفرًا" — O God, forgive. Metaphorical: The she-beasts that "did not forgive" their heedlessness (lam taghfir la-hā ghaflātuhā) — i.e., they did not shield their young from destruction; thus forgiveness is active protection, not mere erasure.
- Root: نفس (n-f-s)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The self, the soul; that which breathes and has vital spirit; also used for the very essence of a thing.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "النفس: الروح" — the soul is the spirit; and in God's saying {«ويحذركم الله نفسه»} [آل عمران/ 28], "His Self" means His very essence (dhāt), which — though grammatically expressed as an annexation implying distinction — is in reality identical, with no multiplicity in the Divine Essence.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "شيء نفيس" — a precious thing. Metaphorical: "دفق نفسه" — he poured out his blood/life; thus nafs is the seat of life, passion, and moral responsibility.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الدعاء والخبر (The Chapter of Supplication and Assertion) — Supplications (duʿāʾ) are grammatically constructed as optative sentences (inshāʾ ṭalabī) using the imperative (rabbighfir), the jussive (lā tuʾākhidhnā), and the vocative (rabbanā), yet they may embed assertive clauses (khabar) of praise (al-ḥamdu lillāh) and attestation (lā ilāha illā anta). The periodic structure of these prayers alternates between direct address to God (munādāh) and self-referential confession, requiring the translator to preserve the vocative force of "O God" and "Our Lord" without flattening into mere description.
60:4.topic: Al-Ghazali on the journey of the soul, death, and the Hereafter, from 'On Invocations and Supplications'

60:4.arabic: وإذا قال عليك توكلنا وإليك أنبنا وإليك المصير ولم يكن حاله التوكل والإنابة كان حاكيا وإذا قال ولنصبرن على ما آذيتمونا فليكن حاله الصبر أو العزيمة عليه حتى يجد حلاوة التلاوة فإن لم يكن بهذه الصفات ولم يتردد قلبه بين هذه الحالات كان حظه من التلاوة حركة اللسان مع صريح اللعن على نفسه في قوله تعالى إلا لعنة الله على الظالمين وفي قوله تعالى كبر مقتا عند الله أن تقولوا ما لا تفعلون وفي قوله عز وجل وهم في غفلة معرضون وفي قوله فأعرض عمن تولى عن ذكرنا ولم يرد إلا الحياة الدنيا وفي قوله تعالى ومن لم
60:4.english: And at the mention of God, His attributes, and His names, he bows low in humility before His majesty and in apprehension of His greatness. And at the mention of the disbelievers' sayings — those things impossible for God, Mighty and Majestic, such as their attributing to Him a son or a consort — he lowers his voice and inwardly recoils in shame at the ugliness of their speech. And at the description of Paradise, his innermost being surges forth with longing for it. And at the description of the Fire, his limbs tremble in fear of it. For when the Messenger of God, peace be upon him, said to Ibn Mas'ud, "Recite to me," he said: "I began reciting Surah al-Nisa'. When I reached {فكيف إذا جئنا من كل أمة بشهيد وجئنا بك على هؤلاء شهيدا} [How then shall it be when We bring from every nation a witness, and We bring you as a witness against these?] (4:41), I saw his two eyes overflowing with tears. He then said to me: 'That is enough for you now.'" And this was because the witnessing of that very state had wholly overwhelmed his heart.
60:4.section_title_en: The States of the Heart During Qur'anic Recitation — The Condition of the True Recieter
60:4.anchors:
- Root: وجل (w-j-l)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root meaning of trembling fear, trepidation of the heart
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الوجل: استشعار الخوف" — the inward apprehension of fear; cited in {إنما المؤمنون الذين إذا ذكر الله وجلت قلوبهم}
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): "رجل وجل، وقوم وجال" — a man fearful, a people fearful; the state of the heart's trembling before divine majesty
- Root: وصف (w-ṣ-f)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Describing a thing by its attributes and qualities
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الوصف: ذكر الشيء بحليته ونعته" — description is the mention of a thing by its adornment and attribute; may be true or false
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal vs Metaphorical: "وجهها يصف الحسن" — metaphorical usage where the face itself "describes" beauty; likewise, the tongue may "describe" falsehood, as in {ولا تقولوا لما تصف ألسنتكم الكذب}
- Root: وفي (w-f-y)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Completeness, fulfillment, reaching full measure
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الوافي: الذي بلغ التمام" — that which attains completion; "أوفى: إذا تمم العهد ولم ينقض حفظه" — fulfilled the covenant without breach
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "درهم واف" — a full-weight dirham; Metaphorical: "أوفى على المائة إذا زاد عليها" — surpassed the hundred
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The separation between the governing preposition and its object by intervening clauses, as in "فلما بلغت {فكيف إذا جئنا...}" where the temporal clause governs the narrative sequence
60:4.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Etiquette of Quran Recitation'

60:4.arabic: بالتقوى وغيره ومن هذا النوع قوله عز وجل حتى تؤمنوا بالله وحده إلا قول إبراهيم لأبيه الآية ومنها المبهم وهو اللفظ المشترك بين معن من كلمة أو حرف أما الكلمة فكالشيء والقرين والأمة والروح ونظائرها قال الله تعالى ضرب الله مثلا عبدا مملوكا لا يقدر على شيء أراد به النفقة مما رزق وقوله عز وجل وضرب الله مثلا رجلين أحدهما أبكم لا يقدر على شيء أي الأمر بالعدل والاستقامة وقوله عز وجل فإن اتبعتني فلا تسألني عن شيء أراد به من صفات الربوبية وهو العلوم التي لا يحل السؤال عنها حتى يبتدئ بها العارف في أوان الاستحقاق وقوله عز وجل أم خلقوا من غ
60:4.english: I say: The Prophet (peace be upon him) was asked about the means of deliverance from these trials, and he said: "The Book of Allah — act by what is in it, for it is that which delivers one from them." The questioner repeated this three times, and he (peace be upon him) said three times: "Learn the Book of Allah, Mighty and Glorious, and act by what is in it, for in it is deliverance."
60:4.section_title_en: The Book of the Etiquette of Recitation — Section 233: On Understanding the Meanings of the Qur'an and the Limits of Interpretation
60:4.anchors:
- Root: ف-ه-م (f-h-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الفهم: هيئة للإنسان بها يتحقق معاني ما يحسن" — comprehension as an inherent faculty by which one ascertains meanings
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الفهم: هيئة للإنسان بها يتحقق معاني ما يحسن... وأفهمته: إذا قلت له حتى تصوره" — comprehension is a cognitive disposition; distinction between understanding (fahm) and making understood (ifhām)
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "تقول: من لم يؤت من سوء الفهم أتى من سوء الإفهام" — literal usage; failure of understanding often stems from failure of communication
- Root: ف-س-ر (f-s-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "وكل شيء يعرف به تفسير الشيء ومعناه، فهو تَفْسِرَتُه" — that by which a thing's meaning is made known
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "التفسير قد يقال فيما يختص بمفردات الألفاظ وغريبها، وفيما يختص بالتأويل" — tafsīr concerns lexical surface; taʾwīl concerns deeper meaning
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "هذا كلام يحتاج إلى فسر وتفسير" — literal: exposition of what is obscure
- Root: و-ج-ل (w-j-l)
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الوجل: استشعار الخوف" — the sensing of fear; used of hearts trembling at divine mention
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "لو واجلت فلانا لوجلته: لغلبته في الوجل" — literal sense of fear; metaphorical extension to overpowering in fear
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — the particle innamā restricts predication, essential for parsing the Prophet's saying "innamā al-aʿmālu bi-l-niyyāt" and analogous restrictive formulations in the ḥadīth cited herein
60:4.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Etiquette of Quran Recitation'

64:1.arabic: إلا الله وحده لا شريك له له الملك وله الحمد يحيي ويميت بيده الخير وهو على كل شيء قدير لا إله إلا الله وحده صدق وعده ونصر عبده وأعز جنده وهزم الأحزاب وحده لا إله إلا الله مخلصين له الدين ولو كره الكافرون لا إله إلا الله مخلصين له الدين الحمد لله رب العالمين فسبحان الله حين تمسون وحين تصبحون وله الحمد في السموات والأرض وعشيا وحين تظهرون يخرج الحي من الميت ويخرج الميت من الحي ويحيي الأرض بعد موتها وكذلك تخرجون ومن آياته أن خلقكم من تراب ثم إذا أنتم بشر تنتشرون اللهم إني أسألك إيمانا دائما
64:1.english: Upon ascending al-Ṣafā, he should face the House (al-Bayt) and say: "God is Greater, God is Greater. Praise be to God for what He has guided us to. Praise be to God with all His praises, for all His graces, all of them. There is no god but God alone, with no partner. His is the dominion, and His is the praise. He gives life and causes death; in His hand is all good, and He is over all things competent. There is no god but God alone; He fulfilled His promise, aided His servant, and honored His soldiers; He alone defeated the confederates. There is no god but God, devoting religion sincerely to Him, even if the disbelievers detest it. There is no god but God, devoting religion sincerely to Him. Praise be to God, Lord of the worlds. So exalted is God when you reach the evening and when you reach the morning. And His is the praise in the heavens and the earth, and at nightfall and when you are at noon. He brings forth the living from the dead and brings forth the dead from the living, and He revives the earth after its death, and thus shall you be brought forth. And of His signs is that He created you from dust; then, behold, you are humans spreading out. O God, I ask You for enduring faith, sincere certainty, beneficial knowledge, a humble heart, and a tongue that remembers You. And I ask You for pardon, well-being, and perpetual immunity in this world and the Hereafter." Then he sends blessings upon Muḥammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and supplicates God, Mighty and Majestic, with whatever need he wishes, following this supplication.
64:1.section_title_en: The Yemeni Corner and the Stone — The Beginning of the Saʿy and Its Rites
64:1.anchors:
- Root: سعي (Saʿy)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The root denotes striving, running, or rapid walking; it is the exertion of effort in a matter, whether good or evil.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "السعي: المشي السريع، وهو دون العدو، ويستعمل للجد في الأمر" — Saʿy is swift walking, less than running, and is used for earnest exertion in a matter. In the sacred rite, it signifies the ritual traversing between al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah, an act of devotional striving.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Ḥaqīqah): "سعى إلى المسجد" — physical exertion toward a goal. Metaphorical (Majāz): "هو يسعى على عياله" — he strives to provide for his family. In the ritual context, the physical traversing is the literal embodiment of devotional striving.
- Root: حمد (Ḥamd)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The root denotes praise, commendation, and the acknowledgment of beneficence; it is the opposite of blame (dhamm).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Praise (ḥamd) is the acknowledgment of beneficence with reverence and love, and it is due to God alone in His absolute perfection.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "أحمد الله تعالى بجميع محامده" — praising God with all His praises. Metaphorical: "أحمدت صنيعه" — I approved of his deed. In the supplications of the saʿy, the pilgrim's praise is both literal acknowledgment and the metaphorical "approval" of God's decree.
- Root: رمل (Raml)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The root denotes rapid walking with a slight trotting motion, a form of hastening in movement.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Not a primary theological term, but in ritual context it signifies the prescribed hastening between the two green markers, emulating the Prophet's action.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical hastening. Metaphorical: The rapid pace is a visible emblem of spiritual earnestness and the rejection of the polytheists' claim that the Muslims were weakened by fever.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Restriction and Specification (al-Ḥaṣr wa al-Taqyīd) — The phrase "وإنما ذلك شرط في طواف الركن" employs restriction to delimit a condition exclusively to the circumambulation of the pillar (ṭawāf al-rukn), thereby negating its applicability to the saʿy.
64:1.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications, prayers, and their spiritual power, from 'On Invocations and Supplications'

64:1.arabic: ويقول لا إله إلا الله وحده لا شريك له له الملك وله الحمد وهو على كل شيء قدير آيبون تائبون عابدون ساجدون لربنا حامدون صدق الله وعده ونصر عبده وهزم الأحزاب وحده (3) وفي بعض الروايات وكل شيء هالك إلا وجهه له الحكم وإليه ترجعون فينبغي أن يستعمل هذه السنة في رجوعه وإذا أشرف على مدينته يحرك الدابة ويقول اللهم اجعل لنا بها قرارا ورزقا حسنا ثم ليرسل إلى أهله من يخبرهم بقدومه كي لا يقدم عليهم بغتة فذلك هو السنة (4) ولا ينبغي أن يطرق أهله ليلا فإذا دخل البلد فليقصد المسجد أولا وليصل ركعتين فهو السنة (5) كذلك كان يفعل رسول الل
64:1.english: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, when he returned from a military expedition, or from the Pilgrimage (ḥajj), or the Lesser Pilgrimage (ʿumrah), would proclaim the greatness of God (takbīr) upon every elevated point of the land, three magnifications, and would say: "There is no god but God alone, with no partner; His is the sovereignty, and His is the praise, and He is powerful over all things. Returning, repentant, worshipping, prostrating, to our Lord giving praise. God fulfilled His promise, and aided His servant, and defeated the confederates alone." {«لا إله إلا الله وحده لا شريك له له الملك وله الحمد وهو على كل شيء قدير آيبون تائبون عابدون ساجدون لربنا حامدون صدق الله وعده ونصر عبده وهزم الأحزاب وحده»} And in some narrations: "And everything is perishing except His Face; His is the judgment, and to Him you shall be returned." {«وكل شيء هالك إلا وجهه له الحكم وإليه ترجعون»} It is therefore fitting that one should practice this sunnah upon his return.
64:1.section_title_en: Section 212 — On the Sunnas of Returning from Travel
64:1.anchors:
- Root: قفل (qafala)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To return from a journey; the root denotes turning back from a course of travel.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Return to a point of origin, whether spatial or temporal; here, the homeward journey after pilgrimage or expedition.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) usage — the physical act of coming back from travel.
- Root: حمد (ḥamida)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To praise; core sense of commendation for beneficence.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Praise directed to God as the sole recipient of ultimate gratitude; distinct from mere flattery.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — "ḥāmidūn" (those who praise); metaphorical (majāz) extension to all acts of grateful acknowledgment.
- Root: سجد (sajada)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To prostrate; physical lowering in submission.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Prostration as the bodily expression of self-abasement before God; here, the voluntary prostration of the believer in worship.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — the ritual act; metaphorical — any posture of humble obedience.
- Sibawayh Rule: Prepositional Interposition (الفصل بين الجار والمجرور) — The phrase "لربنا" (to our Lord) is fronted for emphasis, governing the sequence of praise and worship, maintaining syntactic cohesion across the supplicatory formula.
64:1.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications, prayers, and their spiritual power, from 'On Invocations and Supplications'

64:1.arabic: وهو مع ذلك قريب من كل موجود وهو أقرب إلى العبد من حبل الوريد وهو على كل شيء شهيد إذ لا يماثل قربه قرب الأجسام كما لا تماثل ذاته ذات الأجسام وأنه لا يحل في شيء ولا يحل فيه شيء تعالى عن أن يحويه مكان كما تقدس عن أن يحده زمان بل كان قبل أن خلق الزمان والمكان وهو الآن على ما عليه كان وأنه بائن عن خلقه بصفاته ليس في ذاته سواه ولا في سواه ذاته وأنه مقدس عن التغير والانتقال لا تحله الحوادث ولا تعتريه العوارض بل لا يزال في نعوت جلاله منزها عن الزوال وفي صفات كماله مستغنيا عن زيادة الاستكمال وأنه في ذاته معلوم الوجود بالعقول مرئ
64:1.english:
- **Root: خلق (khalaqa)**
  - *Lisan / Ayn:* Core meaning of measuring, proportioning, and fashioning; al-Khalil notes the root's application to the act of creation as bringing forth upon a measured determination.
  - *Al-Raghib (Mufradat):* "الخلق أصله: التقدير المستقيم" — Creation fundamentally signifies right/straight measurement; used for bringing into being from nothing (ibdāʿ) as in {خلق السماوات والأرض}, and for bringing forth from something as in {خلقكم من نفس واحدة}.
  - *Al-Zamakhshari (Asas):* Literal (ḥaqīqah): the craftsman's measuring before cutting. Metaphorical (majāz): "خلق الله الخلق: أوجده على تقدير أوجبته الحكمة" — God's creation is bringing into existence upon a measure necessitated by wisdom.
64:1.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'On Invocations and Supplications'

64:1.arabic: الأصل الأول العلم بأن صانع العالم قادر وأنه تعالى في قوله وهو على كل شيء قدير صادق لأن العالم محكم في صنعته مرتب في خلقته ومن رأى ثوبا من ديباج حسن النسج والتأليف متناسب التطريز والتطريف ثم توهم صدور نسجه عن ميت لا استطاعة له أو عن إنسان لا قدرة له كان منخلعا عن غريزة العقل ومنخرطا في سلك أهل الغباوة والجهل الأصل الثاني العلم بأنه تعالى عالم بجميع الموجودات ومحيط بكل المخلوقات لا يعزب عن علمه مثقال ذرة في الأرض ولا في السماء صادق في قوله وهو بكل شيء عليم ومرشد إلى صدقه بقوله تعالى ألا يعلم من خلق وهو اللطيف الخبير أرشدك
64:1.english: **The Eighth Principle: Knowledge that He, Exalted is He, is established upon His Throne (mustawin ʿalā ʿarshihi) in the sense that God, Exalted is He, intended by istiwāʾ — which is the sense that does not contradict the attribute of Majesty, nor does any mark of origination (ḥudūth) or passing away (fanāʾ) attach to it. And it is the sense intended by His saying — istiwāʾ toward the heaven — where He said in the Qur'an: {«ثُمَّ اسْتَوَىٰ إِلَى السَّمَاءِ وَهِيَ دُخَانٌ»} ("Then He directed Himself to the heaven, and it was smoke") [Fussilat 41:11]. And that is only by way of subjugation (qahr) and dominion (istīlāʾ), as the poet said:
64:1.section_title_en: The Revival of the Religious Sciences — Section 90: The Ten Principles Concerning Knowledge of the Divine Attributes
64:1.anchors:
- Root: ع ل م (ʿ-l-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root denoting the faculty of perception and comprehension; the mark or trace by which something is known.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "العلم: إدراك الشيء بحقيقته" — knowledge is the apprehension of a thing in its true reality, divided into apprehension of the essence and judgment upon it.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Distinguishes literal knowledge (ḥaqīqah) from awareness (shiʿr); here, it denotes certain, verified cognition of theological verities.
- Root: س و ي (s-w-y)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Root indicating straightness, equality, and levelness; from it derives istiwāʾ (establishing oneself upon, ascending to).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Istiwāʾ upon the Throne (al-ʿArsh) is a divine act of sovereign dominion, not corporeal settlement.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal sense of physical sitting is impossible for God; metaphorical sense (majāz) of qahr (overpowering) and istīlāʾ (dominion) is necessitated by reason and consensus.
- Root: ر أ ي (r-ʾ-y)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Visual perception; also opinion and discernment.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Ruʾyah (vision) of God in the Hereafter is a mode of disclosure (kashf) and knowledge (ʿilm), more complete than intellectual cognition, not conditioned by spatial direction.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal vision requires corporeality and direction; its application to God demands theological specification (takhṣīṣ) without nullifying the veracity of the scriptural promise.
- Root: ق د ر (q-d-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Power, measure, decree; the capacity to bring about an act.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Divine power (qudrah) is the negation of incapacity (ʿajz); absolute power belongs to God alone, while creatures possess limited capacity.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal power over an object; metaphorically, God's power encompasses all things without exertion or instrument.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Prepositional Interposition (باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور) — governing the permissible separation between the preposition and its object for rhetorical emphasis, applied here to the parsing of "إلى السماء" in the verse on istiwāʾ, where the prepositional phrase is delayed to highlight the divine act of sovereign direction toward the heavens.
64:1.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'On Invocations and Supplications'

65:3.arabic: الله عليه وسلم يا أبا هريرة مر أهلك بالصلاة فإن الله يأتيك بالرزق من حيث لا تحتسب (13) وقال بعض العلماء مثل المصلي مثل التاجر الذي لا يحصل له الربح حتى يخلص له رأس المال وكذلك المصلي لا تقبل له نافلة حتى يؤدي الفريضة وكان أبو بكر رضي الله عنه يقول إذا حضرت الصلاة قوموا إلى ناركم التي أوقدتموها فأطفئوها فضيلة إتمام الأركان قال صلى الله عليه وسلم مثل الصلاة المكتوبة كمثل الميزان من أوفى استوفى (14) وقال يزيد الرقاشي كانت صلاة رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم مستوية كأنها موزونة (1) وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم إن الرجلين من أمتي ليقومان إلى الصلاة وركوعهما وسجودهما وا
65:3.english: I say: Now, the five prayers extinguish sins just as water extinguishes filth (1). And the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Indeed, the prayers are an expiation for what occurs between them, so long as the major sins are avoided" (2). And he, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Between us and the hypocrites is the witnessing of the night prayer (al-ʿatamah) and the dawn prayer; they cannot bear them" (3). And he, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Whoever meets God while neglecting his prayer, God will not regard any of his good deeds" (4). And he, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Prayer is the pillar of the religion; whoever abandons it has demolished the religion" (5). And he was asked, peace and blessings be upon him, "Which deed is most excellent?" He said: "Prayer at its appointed times" (6). And he, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Whoever preserves the five prayers, perfecting their purification and their appointed times, they shall be for him a light and a proof on the Day of Resurrection; and whoever neglects them shall be gathered with Pharaoh and Hāmān" (7). And he, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "The key to Paradise is prayer" (8). And he said: "God has not obligated upon His creation, after monotheism (tawḥīd), anything more beloved to Him than prayer; and had there been anything more beloved to Him, His angels would have devoted themselves to it — among them are those who bow (rākiʿ), those who prostrate (sājid), and those who stand and sit" (9). And the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Whoever deliberately abandons a prayer has disbelieved" (10) — meaning: he has nearly been uprooted from faith by the unraveling of its rope and the collapse of its pillar, just as one who has nearly reached a town is said to have arrived at it and entered it. And he, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Whoever deliberately abandons a prayer has absolved himself of the covenant of Muhammad, peace be upon him" (11). And Abū Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him, said: "Whoever performs ablution and perfects it, then sets out deliberately for prayer, he is in a state of prayer as long as he intends the prayer; and for each of his steps, a good deed is recorded for him, and by the other, a sin is erased. So when any of you hears the call to commence (iqāmah), he should not delay — for the one with the greatest reward among you is the one whose dwelling is farthest." They said: "Why, O Abū Hurayrah?" He said: "Because of the abundance of steps." And it is narrated: "Indeed, the first thing examined of a servant's deeds on the Day of Resurrection is the prayer. If it is found complete, it is accepted from him, along with the rest of his deeds; and if it is found deficient, it is rejected upon him, along with the rest of his deeds" (12). And he, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "O Abū Hurayrah, command your family to pray, for God shall bring you sustenance from whence you do not reckon" (13). And some scholars said: The likeness of the one who prays is the likeness of a merchant who gains no profit until his capital is secured; likewise, the one who prays has no supererogatory prayer accepted until he has performed the obligatory one.
65:3.section_title_en: Section 121 — The Virtue of Prayer and the Completion of Its Pillars
65:3.anchors:
- Root: صلو (ṣ-l-w)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root denotes supplication, blessing, and the act of prayer; the ﷽ prayer (ṣalāh) as the established ritual worship.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Ṣalāh in the theological sense is the act of drawing near to God through devoted worship, encompassing both the physical postures and the inward humility (khushūʿ).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) usage refers to the ritual prayer with its prescribed bowings and prostrations; metaphorical (majāz) usage extends to supplication and divine blessing.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The syntactic structure allows for separation between the preposition and its object to emphasize rhetorical weight, as in the prophetic narrations where conditions and exceptions are interposed for clarity.
65:3.topic: Al-Ghazali on the journey of the soul, death, and the Hereafter, from 'Mysteries of Prayer'

65:3.arabic: نسينا ربما عرض من حيث لا نحتسب وإن تجردنا لذكره كنا قد أهملنا ذكر الله فالجمع أولى وقال العلماء المحققون غلط الفريقان أما الأول فقد تجرد لذكر الشيطان ونسي ذكر الله فلا يخفى غلطه وإنما أمرنا بالحذر من الشيطان كيلا يصدنا عن الذكر فكيف نجعل ذكره اغلب الأشياء على قلوبنا وهو منتهى ضرر العدو ثم يؤدي ذلك إلى خلو القلب عن نور ذكر الله تعالى فإذا قصد الشيطان مثل هذا القلب وليس فيه نور ذكر الله تعالى وقوة الاشتغال به فيوشك أن يظفر به ولا يقوى على دفعه فلم يأمرنا بانتظار الشيطان ولا بإد
65:3.english: ...and the world, which is the source of trials and tribulations, the mine of forbidden pleasures and lusts. And Moses, peace be upon him, said—as God Most High has related concerning him—{«هذا من عمل الشيطان»} ("This is of Satan's doing" — Qur'an 28:15). For this reason, God warned all of creation against him, saying: {«يا بني آدم لا يفتننكم الشيطان كما أخرج أبويكم من الجنة»} ("O children of Adam, let not Satan tempt you as he brought your parents out of Paradise" — Qur'an 7:27). And He, Glorified and Exalted, said: {«إنه يراكم هو وقبيله من حيث لا ترونهم»} ("Indeed, he sees you, he and his tribe, from where you do not see them" — Qur'an 7:27). The Qur'an, from its beginning to its end, is a warning against Satan. So how could one claim security from him? And taking precaution against him, in the manner God has commanded, does not contradict occupation with the love of God. For part of loving Him is obeying His command. He has commanded vigilance against the enemy just as He commanded vigilance against the disbelievers, saying: {«وليعأخذوا حذرهم وأسلحتهم»} ("And let them take their precautions and their weapons" — Qur'an 4:102), and saying: {«وأعدوا لهم ما استطعتم من قوة ومن رباط الخيل»} ("And prepare against them whatever you are able of power and of steeds of war" — Qur'an 8:60). So if, by God's command, you are obligated to be wary of a disbelieving enemy whom you can see, then it is all the more fitting that you be obligated to be wary of an enemy who sees you while you do not see him.
65:3.section_title_en: On the Necessity of Vigilance Against Satan and Its Harmony with Trust in God and Remembrance of Him
65:3.anchors:
- Root: شيط (Shayṭ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root denotes burning, scorching, or spoiling (as meat over a fire), and by extension, perishing or being ruined.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الشيطان" (Satan) is derived from this root, signifying one who is burned, ruined, or cast away from mercy—the archetype of the adversary who destroys through temptation.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): "شاط دمه" — his blood went in vain (was wasted). Metaphorical (Majaz): "أشاط السلطان دمه" — the ruler declared his blood permissible (wasted). Thus, Satan is the one who causes spiritual ruin and waste.
- Root: حذر (Ḥadhar)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Caution, wariness, and taking precautions against a feared harm.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الحذر: احتراز من مخيف" — vigilance is a protective withdrawal from what is frightening. It is a commanded state, as in {«خذوا حذركم»} (Take your precautions — Qur'an 4:71).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "حذرته وحاذرته" — I was wary of him. Metaphorical: "حذار من أرماحنا حذار" — a poetic imperative to beware. Vigilance is both a physical and spiritual act of self-preservation.
- Root: قلب (Qalb)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To turn, overturn, or flip something from one state to another.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "قلب الشيء: تصريفه وصرفه عن وجه إلى وجه" — the heart (qalb) is so named for its constant turning and fluctuation between states.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "قلب الشيء قلبا: حوله عن وجهه" — to turn a thing from its face. Metaphorical: "رجل قلب حول: يقلب الأمور ويحتال" — a man who turns matters over and devises stratagems. The heart's occupation is decisive: it turns either toward God or toward the enemy.
- Root: وكل (Wakal)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To entrust, delegate, or rely upon another.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "التوكيل: أن تعتمد على غيرك وتجعله نائبا عنك" — trust (tawakkul) is reliance upon another as your deputy. God says: {«وكفى بالله وكيلا»} (And sufficient is Allah as Disposer of affairs — Qur'an 4:81).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "وكل إليه الأمر" — he delegated the matter to him. Metaphorical: "فلان وكل" — a weak man who leans on others. True tawakkul does not negate taking means; it purifies the heart's reliance.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد (Restriction & Focused Predication) — The particle "إنما" and restrictive constructions (e.g., "ليس ... إلا") are used to delimit predicates, as in the author's argument that vigilance is not a contradiction of love or trust but a fulfillment of the divine command.
65:3.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Condemnation of Status and Ostentation'

65:3.arabic: يجعل له مخرجا ويرزقه من حيث لا يحتسب} ولن يعدم المتورع عن الحرام فتوحا من الحلال فلا يأخذ من أموال الأتراك والجنود وعمال السلاطين ومن أكثر كسبه من الحرام إلا إذا ضاق الأمر عليه وكان ما يسلم إليه لا يعرف له مالكا معينا فله أن يأخذ بقدر الحاجة فإن فتوى الشرع في مثل هذا أن يتصدق به على ما سيأتي بيانه في كتاب الحلال والحرام وذلك إذا عجز عن الحلال فإذا أخذ لم يكن أخذه أخذ زكاة إذ لا يقع زكاة عن مؤديه وهو حرام الرابعة أن يتوقى مواقع الريبة والاشتباه في مقدار ما يأخذه فلا يأخذ إلا المقد
65:3.english: The second: that he thank the giver, supplicate for him, and praise him; and his gratitude and supplication should be such that it does not remove him from being a mere intermediary, but rather he is a channel for the arrival of God's blessing to him. And the channel has a right, insofar as God made him a channel and an intermediary — and that does not negate seeing the blessing as from God, Glorified be He. For he, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "He who does not thank the people has not thanked God" {«من لم يشكر الناس لم يشكر الله»}. And God, Mighty and Majestic, has praised His servants in places for their deeds, while He is their Creator and the Originator of the capacity for them — such as His saying, Exalted is He: {«نعم العبد إنه أواب»} ["Excellent is the servant. Indeed, he is penitent."] — and other similar instances.
65:3.section_title_en: The Etiquette of the Recipient of Wealth: On the Virtue of Poverty and the Conduct of Taking from Others
65:3.anchors:
- Root: كرم (karuma)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root meaning: nobility, generosity, honorableness of origin and character.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: Divine Generosity (al-Karam) as an attribute of God entailing beneficence (al-Ifḍāl) that is pure grace, not obligation.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: nobility of lineage/character. Metaphorical: God's abundant giving without recompense.
- Root: فضل (faḍala)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root meaning: surplus, excess, superiority, that which remains beyond need.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: God's Bounty (al-Faḍl) as gratuitous favor exceeding what is merited; distinct from justice ('Adl).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: excess/surplus. Metaphorical: divine favor and grace.
- Root: نعم (ni'ma)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root meaning: well-being, bounty, benefaction; state of goodness.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-Ni'ma as the good state (al-ḥālah al-ḥasanah) bestowed by God; its genus encompasses both little and much.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: pleasant life and bounty. Metaphorical: "خفت نعامتهم" (their ostriches departed) — i.e., they went away, indicating the fleeting nature of worldly boons.
- Root: قدر (qadara)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root meaning: measure, extent, power, decree.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-Qudrah for God is the negation of incapacity; for man, a capacity for specific acts. Al-Qadr: the divine measure/decree.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: measure, amount, power. Metaphorical: "فرس بعيد القدر" (a horse of far-reaching stride) — extended reach.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — Governing the precise restriction of agency and causation in statements like "إنما المنكر أن يرى الواسطة أصلا" (The only objectionable thing is to regard the intermediary as the origin).
65:3.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications, prayers, and their spiritual power, from 'Disciplining the Soul'

65:3.arabic: قوله تعالى ومن يتوكل على الله فهو حسبه فتوكلت على الله عز وجل فهو حسبي قال شقيق يا حاتم وفقك الله تعالى فإني نظرت في علوم التوراة والإنجيل والزبور والفرقان العظيم فوجدت جميع أنواع الخير والديانة وهي تدور على هذه الثمان مسائل فمن استعملها فقد استعمل الكتب الأربعة فهذا الفن من العلم لا يهتم بإدراكه والتفطن له إلا علماء الآخرة فأما علماء الدنيا فيشتغلون بما يتيسر به اكتساب المال والجاه ويهملون أمثال هذه العلوم التي بعث الله بها الأنبياء كلهم عليهم السلام وقال الضحاك بن مزاحم أدركتهم و
65:3.english: Know that the scholar who does not act upon his knowledge is condemned by the Book, the Sunnah, and the sayings of the sages. God, exalted be He, said: {«يا أيها الذين آمنوا لم تقولون ما لا تفعلون * كبر مقتا عند الله أن تقولوا ما لا تفعلون»} ("O you who believe, why do you say what you do not do? Most hateful it is to God that you say what you do not do"). And He said: {«أتأمرون الناس بالبر وتنسون أنفسكم»} ("Do you command people to righteousness while you forget yourselves?"). And He said: {«ومن الناس من يعجبك قوله في الحياة الدنيا ويشهد الله على ما في قلبه وهو ألد الخصام»} ("And among people is he whose speech pleases you in the worldly life, and he calls God to witness what is in his heart, yet he is the fiercest of opponents").
65:3.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Book of Knowledge'

65:3.arabic: عز وجل كفاه الله تعالى ما أهمه ورزقه من حيث لا يحتسب (7) وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم أوحى الله عز وجل إلى إبراهيم عليه السلام يا إبراهيم إني عليم أحب كل عليم (8) وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم العالم أمين الله سبحانه في الأرض (9) وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم صنفان من أمتي إذا صلحوا صلح الناس وإذا فسدوا فسد الناس الأمراء والفقهاء (10) وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا أتى علي يوم لا أزداد فيه علما يقربني إلى الله عز وجل فلا بورك لي في طلوع شمس ذلك اليوم (11) وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم في تفضيل العلم على العبادة والشها
65:3.english: How He, Glorified and Exalted, began with Himself, then seconded with the angels, and thirded with the people of knowledge — and sufficient for you is this as honor, excellence, splendor, and nobility. And God, Exalted, said: {«يرفع الله الذين آمنوا منكم والذين أوتوا العلم درجات»} — "God will raise those who have believed among you and those who have been given knowledge, in degrees." Ibn ʿAbbās, may God be pleased with them both, said: For the scholars there are degrees above the believers, seven hundred degrees, and between each two degrees is a distance of five hundred years' journey.
65:3.section_title_en: The Book of Knowledge — Section 4: The Excellence of Knowledge and the Scholars
65:3.anchors:
- Root: علم (ʿ-l-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root meaning of knowing, perceiving a thing in its true reality; the act of apprehension and judgment.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "العلم: إدراك الشيء بحقيقته" — knowledge is the apprehension of a thing in its true reality, divided into apprehension of the essence and judgment of existence or non-existence.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) usage denotes genuine knowing; metaphorical (majāz) usage extends to signs, landmarks, and traces that guide to knowledge.
- Root: درج (d-r-j)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Degrees, steps, ascending stations; the root denotes gradation and progressive elevation.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الدرجة نحو المنزلة، لكن يقال للمنزلة: درجة إذا اعتبرت بالصعود" — a degree is a station considered by ascent, not horizontal extension.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical steps of ascent. Metaphorical: "لفلان درجة رفيعة" — lofty rank; "امش في مدارج الحق" — walk in the paths of truth.
- Root: يوم (y-w-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: A day; a period of time from sunrise to sunset, or any duration whatsoever.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "اليوم يعبر به عن وقت طلوع الشمس إلى غروبها. وقد يعبر به عن مدة من الزمان أي مدة كانت" — the day denotes the time of the sun's rising to its setting, and may denote any period of time whatsoever.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the solar day. Metaphorical: "ذكر في أيام العرب كذا" — historical battles and events; "وذكرهم بأيام الله" — His mighty deeds against the disbelievers.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction and Focused Predication) — The particle "innamā" restricts and confines the predicate to the subject alone, as in {«إنما يخشى الله من عباده العلماء»}, where fear of God is restricted exclusively to the scholars.
65:3.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'On Invocations and Supplications'

65:12.arabic: ينزل إليهم من القدر والأمر فقيل خلق سبع سموات ومن الأرض مثلهن يتنزل الأمر بينهن لتعلموا أن الله على كل شيء قدير وأن الله قد أحاط بكل شيء علما وهذه أمور لا يعلم تأويلها إلا الله والراسخون في العلم وعبر ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما عن اختصاص الراسخين في العلم بعلوم لا تحتملها أفهام الخلق حيث قرأ قوله تعالى {يتنزل الأمر بينهن} فقال لو ذكرت ما أعرفه من معنى هذه الآية لرجمتموني وفي لفظ آخر لقلتم إنه كافر ولنقتصر على هذا القدر فقد خرج عنان الكلام عن قبضة الاختيار وامتزج بعلم المعاملة ما ليس منه فلنرجع إلى مقاصد الشكر فنقول إذا رجع حقيقة الشكر إلى كون العبد مستعملا في إتمام حكمة الله تعالى فأشكر العب
65:12.english: Thus was the beginning of this matter and its end. And do not understand it unless you are worthy of it. And if you are worthy of it, the eye is opened and you see, so you have no need of a leader to lead you. The blind man can indeed be led, but only to a limit. For when the path narrows and becomes sharper than a sword and finer than a hair, the bird is able to fly over it but is not able to drag a blind man behind it. And when the field becomes narrow and subtle — subtle as water, for example — and crossing is possible only by swimming, then the one skilled in the art of swimming may be able to cross by himself, and perhaps he is not able to drag another behind him. These matters bear the same relation to walking upon the way of the common masses of creatures as walking upon water bears to walking upon earth. Swimming can be learned; but as for walking upon water, it is not acquired by instruction, but rather is attained through the strength of certainty (yaqīn). For this reason it was said to the Prophet, peace be upon him, that Jesus, peace be upon him, was said to have walked upon water, and he, peace be upon him, said: "Had his certainty increased, he would have walked upon the air." {«حديث قيل له يقال إن عيسى مشى على الماء قال لو ازداد يقينا لمشي على الهواء»} — This hadith is rejected (munkar) and is not known in this form. What is known is what Ibn Abi al-Dunya narrated in the Book of Certainty from the saying of Bakr ibn Abd Allah al-Muzani, who said: The disciples lost their Prophet, and it was said to them: "He has headed toward the sea." So they set out seeking him, and when they reached the sea, behold, he was coming toward them walking upon the water. And he mentioned a hadith in which Jesus said: "If the son of Adam had a hair's breadth of certainty, he would walk upon the water." And Abu Mansur al-Daylami narrated in the Musnad al-Firdaws with a weak chain from the hadith of Muadh ibn Jabal: "If you knew God with true knowledge, you would walk upon the seas, and the mountains would be removed by your supplications." These are symbols and allusions to the meaning of aversion (karāhah) and love (maḥabbah), and good pleasure (riḍā) and wrath (ghaḍab), and gratitude (shukr) and ingratitude (kufrān) — more than this is not fitting for the science of practical conduct (ʿilm al-muʿāmalah). And God, exalted be He, struck an example of this to draw it near to the understanding of creatures, since He knew that He created the jinn and mankind only to worship Him, and their worship was the ultimate purpose of wisdom (ghāyat al-ḥikmah) with respect to them. Then He informed that He has two servants: one whom He loves, whose name is Gabriel — the Holy Spirit and the Trustworthy One — and he is with Him beloved, obeyed, trustworthy, and honored; and another whom He hates, whose name is Iblis — the accursed one, reprieved until the Day of Judgment. Then He delegated guidance (irshād) to Gabriel, saying, the Exalted: {«قل نزله روح القدس من ربك بالحق»} "Say: The Holy Spirit has brought it down from your Lord with truth" (16:102), and said, the Exalted: {«يلقي الروح من أمره على من يشاء من عباده»} "He casts the Spirit of His command upon whom He wills of His servants" (40:15). And He delegated misguidance (ighwāʾ) to Iblis, saying, the Exalted: {«ليضل عن سبيله»} "That he may lead astray from His path" (4:119). And ighwāʾ is the halting of servants short of attaining the ultimate purpose of wisdom. So observe how He attributed it to the servant with whom He was wrathful; and guidance (irshād) is the conduct of them toward the ultimate purpose — so observe how He attributed it to the servant whom He loves. And you have an example of this in custom: when a king is in need of one to give him drink and one to cup him and to clean the courtyard of his house of filth, and he has two servants, he does not appoint for cupping and cleaning except the ugliest and meanest of them, and he does not entrust the carrying of drink and perfume except to the best and most complete of them and the most beloved to him. And you should not say: "This is my act, and his act was not without my act" — for you have erred when you attributed that to yourself. Rather, He is the One who directed your motive (dāʿiyah) to the specification of the disliked act to the disliked person, and the beloved act to the beloved person, as a completion of justice (ʿadl). For His justice is sometimes completed through matters in which you have no entry, and sometimes it is completed in you — for you also are among His acts. So your motive, your power, your knowledge, your action, and all the other causes of your movements in expression — all of this is His act, which He arranged with justice in an arrangement from which moderate acts issue forth. Except that you see only yourself, and so you suppose that what appears through you in the world of witness (ʿālam al-shahādah) has no cause from the world of the unseen and the dominion (ʿālam al-ghayb wa al-malakūt). Therefore you attribute it to yourself. And you are only like the child who looks at night at the play of the juggler (mushʿabadh) who brings forth figures from behind a curtain that dance and scream and rise and sit, composed of rags that do not move by themselves — rather, they are moved by fine hair-like threads that do not appear in the darkness of night, their ends in the hand of the juggler, who is hidden from the eyes of the children. So they rejoice and marvel, supposing that those rags dance and play and rise and sit. As for the intelligent ones, they know that this is a moving (taḥrīk) and not a self-movement, but perhaps they do not know its detailed modality. And the one who knows some of its detail does not know it as the juggler knows it, to whom the command belongs and in whose hand is the pulling. Likewise, the children of the people of this world — and all creatures are children relative to the scholars — look at these persons (ashkhāṣ) and suppose that they are the movers, and so they attribute [action] to them. And the scholars know that they are moved, except that they do not know the modality of the moving — and they are the majority. Except the knowers (ʿārifūn), the scholars, and those firmly rooted in knowledge (al-rāsikhūn), for they have perceived, with the sharpness of their sight, fine spider-web threads — nay, much finer than these — suspended from heaven, their ends attached to the persons of the people of the earth. Those threads are not perceived, due to their fineness, by these outward eyes. Then they witnessed the heads of those threads in their suspension-points (manāṭāt) to which they are attached, and they witnessed for those suspension-points handles (maqābiḍ) that are in the hands of the angels who move the heavens. And they also witnessed the angels of the heavens directed toward the bearers of the Throne (ḥamalat al-ʿarsh), awaiting what descends upon them of the command from the presence of Lordship (ḥaḍrat al-rubūbiyyah) — "they do not disobey God in what He commands them, and they do what they are commanded" (66:6). And He expressed these witnessed realities in the Qur'an, and it was said: {«وفي السماء رزقكم وما توعدون»} "And in the heaven is your provision and what you are promised" (51:22). And He expressed the waiting of the angels of the heavens for what descends upon them of decree and command, and it was said: "He created seven heavens and of the earth the like of them; {«يتنزل الأمر بينهن لتعلموا أن الله على كل شيء قدير وأن الله قد أحاط بكل شيء علما»} 'the command descends between them, that you may know that God is powerful over all things and that God encompasses all things in knowledge'" (65:12). These are matters whose interpretation (taʾwīl) none knows except God and those firmly rooted in knowledge (al-rāsikhūn fī al-ʿilm). And Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, expressed the exclusivity of those firmly rooted in knowledge to sciences that the understandings of creatures cannot bear, when he recited the saying of the Exalted: {«يتنزل الأمر بينهن»} "The command descends between them," and said: "Were I to mention what I know of the meaning of this verse, you would stone me" — and in another wording: "You would say he is an unbeliever."
65:12.section_title_en: On the Degrees of Proximity to God and the Hierarchy of Those Who Perfect Divine Wisdom
65:12.anchors:
- Root: سير (s-y-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "السير: الذهاب والسفر، وسار يسير سيرا ومسيرا، والسيارة: الرفقة المسافرة"
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "السير: الانتقال من مكان إلى مكان، ويستعار للسلوك في الدين والطريقة"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): [Literal] "سار القوم: مشوا" — [Metaphorical] "سار فيه السير: مضى في الأمر، وسار ذكره: انتشر، ومنه: سيرة فلان: طريقته"
- Root: مشي (m-sh-y)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "المشي: تردد الأركان على الأرض، والماشية: الإبل والغنم لانتقالها في المرعى"
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "المشي: الانتقال من مكان إلى مكان بإرادة، ويكنى به عن النميمة، وعن شرب المسهل"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): [Literal] "مشيت وتمشيت، وهي حسنة المشية" — [Metaphorical] "مشى بطنه، وأمشاه الدواء، واستمشيت بالدواء، ومنه: مشت المرأة: كثرت أولادها"
- Root: خلق (kh-l-q)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الخلق: التقدير، والخلق: الناس، والخليقة: الطبيعة، والخلق: السجية"
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الخلق أصله: التقدير المستقيم، ويستعمل في إبداع الشيء من غير أصل ولا احتذاء"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): [Literal] "خلق الخراز الأديم: قدره قبل القطع" — [Metaphorical] "خلق الله الخلق: أوجده على تقدير أوجبته الحكمة"
- Root: نفس (n-f-s)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "النفس: الروح، والذات، والشيء النفيس"
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "النفس: الروح، وتطلق على الذات، قال تعالى: {ويحذركم الله نفسه} فنفسه: ذاته"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): [Literal] "شيء نفيس ومنفس" — [Metaphorical] "دفق نفسه أي دمه، وأصابته نفس: عين"
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — Used to distinguish exclusive attribution of actions to God versus creatures, as in "إنما أنت مثل الصبي" (You are only like a child), restricting the simile to the creature while preserving divine agency.
65:12.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

65:12.arabic: ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما في قوله عز وجل الله الذي خلق سبع سموات ومن الأرض مثلهن يتنزل الأمر بينهن لو ذكرت تفسيره لرجمتموني وفي لفظ آخر لقلتم إنه كافر وقال أبو هريرة رضي الله عنه حفظت من رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وعاءين أما أحدهما فبثثته وأما الآخر لو بثثته لقطع هذا الحلقوم وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم ما فضلكم أبو بكر بكثرة صيام ولا صلاة ولكن بسر وقر في صدره (3) رضي الله عنه ولا شك في أن ذلك السر كان متعلقا بقواعد الدين غير خارج منها وما كان من قواعد الدين لم يكن خافيا بظواهره على غيره وقال سهل التستري رضي الله عنه للعالم ثلاثة علوم علم ظاهر
65:12.english: **Know** that the division of these sciences into the hidden (khafiyyah) and the evident (jaliyyah) is not denied by any possessor of insight (baṣīrah). Only the deficient deny it — those who snatched up something in the earliest days of youth and then froze upon it, having no ascent to the summit of sublimity (shaʾw al-ʿalāʾ) nor to the stations of the scholars and the saints (awliyāʾ). And this is evident from the proofs of the Sacred Law.
