##
112:3.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications, prayers, and their spiritual power, from 'Duties of Brotherhood'

113:2.arabic: يجاوزهن بر ولا فاجر من شر ما خلق فإذا جن عليه الليل يقول يا أرض ربي وربك الله أعوذ بالله من شرك وشر ما فيك وشر ما دب عليك أعوذ بالله من شر كل أسد وأسود وحية وعقرب ومن شر ساكن البلد ووالد وما ولد وله ما سكن في الليل والنهار وهو السميع العليم السابعة في الحراسة ينبغي أن يحتاط بالنهار فلا يمشي منفردا خارج القافلة لأنه ربما يغتال أو ينقطع ويكون بالليل متحفظا عند النوم فإن نام في ابتداء الليل افترش ذراعه وإن نام في آخر الليل نصب ذراعه نصبا وجعل رأسه في كفه هكذا كان ينام رسول الله ص
113:2.english: He ought to seek out a righteous companion, one who loves goodness and assists in it: if he forgets, the companion reminds him; if he remembers, the companion aids him; if he fears, the companion emboldens him; if he weakens, the companion strengthens him; if his breast narrows, the companion enlarges his patience. He should bid farewell to his resident companions, his brothers, and his neighbors — taking leave of them and seeking their supplications, for God Most High places goodness in their prayers. The Sunnah of farewell is to say: «أستودع الله دينك وأمانتك وخواتيم عملك» — "I entrust to God your religion, your trustworthiness, and the seal of your deeds." And he, peace and blessings be upon him, used to say to one intending travel: "In God's protection and His care — may God provide you with piety, forgive your sin, and direct you toward goodness wherever you may be."
113:2.section_title_en: The Book of the Etiquette of Travel — Section 199: On the Comprehensive Etiquette of the Journey (From Provisioning to Guarding)
113:2.anchors:
- Root: س ف ر (S-F-R)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "السفر: كشف الغطاء" — unveiling, uncovering; the traveler is one who uncovers the veils of distant lands.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "السفر: كشف الغطاء، ويختص ذلك بالأعيان" — the journey is a literal uncovering of horizons, yet the spiritual journey unveils the soul's veils.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Haqiqah: "سافر سفرا بعيدا" (to travel far); Majaz: "وجه مسفر: مشرق سرورا" — a face radiant with joy, as the traveler's face brightens with divine trust.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — governing the permissible separation between the preposition and its object for rhetorical emphasis, as in the supplications' structural pauses.
113:2.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications, prayers, and their spiritual power, from 'On Invocations and Supplications'

2:16.arabic: بالذي هو خير فأولئك الذين اشتروا الضلالة بالهدى فما ربحت تجارتهم وما كانوا مهتدين وأما المخلصون فإن الله تعالى اشترى منهم أنفسهم وأموالهم بأن لهم الجنة فلما رأوا أنهم تركوا تمتع عشرين سنة مثلا أو ثلاثين سنة بتمتع الأبد استبشروا ببيعهم الذي بايعوا به فهذا بيان المزهود فيه وإذا فهمت هذا علمت أن ما ذكره المتكلمون في حد الزهد لم يشيروا به إلا إلى بعض أقسامه فذكر كل واحد منهم ما رآه غالبا على نفسه أو على من كان يخاطبه فقال بشر رحمه الله تعالى الزهد في الدنيا هو الزهد في الناس وهذا إشارة إلى الزهد في الجاه خاصة وقال قاسم الجوعي
2:16.english: ...or the attainment of the rank of martyrdom (al-shahādah). And whosoever among them died upon his bed would grieve bitterly over the loss of martyrdom — so much so that Khālid ibn al-Walīd, may Allah Most High be well pleased with him, when death approached him upon his bed, kept saying: "How often did I deceive my soul [into battle], and charge upon the ranks, coveting martyrdom — and now I die the death of old women!" When he died, eight hundred wounds from the marks of injuries were counted upon his body. Such was the state of the truthful ones in faith — may Allah Most High be well pleased with them all.
2:16.section_title_en: Exposition of the Degrees of Asceticism (Zuhd) and Its Divisions — Relative to Itself, to That Which Is Renounced, and to That Which Is Sought
2:16.anchors:
- Root: زهد (Z-H-D)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root meaning: scarcity, paucity, and abstemiousness; al-zuhd is also "estimation/assessment" (al-hazr), as in assessing a palm-crop.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الزهيد: الشيء القليل" — the ascetic (al-zāhid) is one who turns away from a thing, content with the little (al-qalīl) thereof; theological nuance: renunciation is a voluntary contentment with the lesser in exchange for the greater.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Haqiqah (literal): "زهد في الشيء: رغب عنه" — to turn away from a thing with aversion. Majaz (metaphorical): "رجل زهيد: قليل الخير" — a man of little good; "اد زهيد" — a valley that takes little water. Thus zuhd is literal renunciation, but its degrees vary by the object renounced.
- Root: قصر (Q-S-R)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To restrain, confine, hold back; also shortness as opposed to length.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "القصر: خلاف الطول" — shortness is the opposite of length; both are relative terms (mutadāyifān) defined by comparison to another.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Haqiqah: "قصرته: حبسته" — I restrained him. "وقصرت نفسي على هذا الأمر" — I confined myself to this matter, not aspiring beyond it. Majaz: "أقصر المطر: أقلع" — the rain ceased; "قصر الأمل" — the shortening of hope/aspiration, a metaphorical restraint of the soul's reach.
- Root: نفس (N-F-S)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The self, the soul; that which one desires to be near.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "النفس: الروح" — the soul is the spirit; in divine attribution, "نفسه" denotes His very essence (dhāt), not a separate entity.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Haqiqah: "شيء نفيس" — a precious thing. Majaz: "دفق نفسه أي دمه" — "he poured out his self" meaning his blood; thus nafs can denote the entire vital being given in sacrifice.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد (Restriction and Specification) — When multiple predicates are attributed to a single subject (zuhd), each speaker's definition is a restricted specification (takhṣīṣ) of one division, not a comprehensive definition (ḥadd) of the whole genus. The syntactic pattern "إنما هو كذا" effects exclusive predication, signaling partial scope.
2:16.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Poverty and Abstinence'

2:61.arabic: وسمعة فليحذر أن يستبدل الذي هو أدنى بالذي هو خير وأما قطع العلائق فمعناه رد المظالم والتوبة الخالصة لله تعالى عن جملة المعاصي فكل مظلمة علاقة وكل علاقة مثل غريم حاضر متعلق بتلابيبه ينادي عليه ويقول إلى أين تتوجه أتقصد بيت ملك الملوك وأنت مضيع أمره في منزلك هذا ومستهين به ومهمل له أولا تستحي أن تقدم عليه قدوم العبد العاصي فيردك ولا يقبلك فإن كنت راغبا في قبول زيارتك فنفذ أوامره ورد المظالم وتب إليه أولا من جميع المعاصي واقطع علاقة قلبك عن الالتفات إلى ما وراءك لتكون متوجها إليه بوجه قلبك كما أ
2:61.english: For this reason, the monastics (al-ruhbāniyyūn) in the past religions separated themselves from creation and withdrew to the peaks of mountains, preferring wild solitude away from people in pursuit of intimacy (uns) with God — mighty and majestic is He. They abandoned for God's sake the pleasures of the present and imposed upon themselves arduous spiritual exertions (mujāhidāt), hoping for the Hereafter. God — glorified and exalted is He — praised them in His Book, saying: {«ذلك بأن منهم قسيسين ورهبانا وأنهم لا يستكبرون»} — "That is because among them are priests and monks and because they do not behave arrogantly." Then when that [way] became effaced, and creation turned to following appetites, abandoned devotion to the worship of God — glorified and exalted is He — and grew languid in it, God — glorified and exalted is He — sent His Prophet Muhammad — may God's peace and blessings be upon him — to revive the path of the Hereafter and renew the way of the messengers in traversing it.
2:61.section_title_en: The Noble Stations of Pilgrimage and the Manner of Contemplation Upon Them — From the Beginning of Hajj to Its End
2:61.anchors:
- Root: فهم (f-h-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Comprehension, understanding, grasping the reality of a thing
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Intellectual apprehension that penetrates to the essential meaning, not mere surface awareness
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — understanding speech; Metaphorical — understanding the inner reality and wisdom of sacred acts
- Root: سفر (s-f-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Journey; also uncovering/disclosure — the traveler is one who uncovers distant horizons
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "السفر: كشف الغطاء" — uncovering the veil; the journey of hajj is both physical travel and spiritual unveiling
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — journeying across land; Metaphorical — "سفر عن وجهك الشر" (uncovering evil from your face), i.e., the hajj journey unveils the secrets of servitude
- Root: رهب (r-h-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To fear, to be awed; monastic withdrawal (rahbāniyyah) from worldly attachments
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Fear that drives one to solitary devotion; the monastic impulse redirected by Islamic law
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — fear; Metaphorical — the disciplined retreat from worldly pleasures for divine communion
- Root: بيت (b-y-t)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Place of nightly habitation; the Ka'bah as the primordial house
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "أصل البيت: مأوى الإنسان بالليل" — the house is where one dwells at night; the Sacred House is where hearts find nocturnal rest in God
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — physical structure; Metaphorical — the locus of divine presence and the object of spiritual yearning
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — "إنما" restricts the predicate exclusively to the subject, as in "إنما بعث الله نبيه لإحياء طريق الآخرة" — the sole purpose of prophetic mission is specified with exclusive focus.
2:61.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Poverty and Abstinence'

2:120.arabic: هذه العلة قد تبقى مع سقوط الشهوات بل يحب الإنسان من العلوم ما لا يصلح للتوصل به إلى الأغراض بل ربما يفوت عليه جملة من الأغراض والشهوات ولكن الطبع يتقاضى طلب العلم في جميع العجائب والمشكلات لأن في العلم استيلاء على المعلوم وهو نوع من الكمال الذي هو من صفات الربوبية فكان محبوبا بالطبع إلا أن في حب كمال العلم والقدرة أغاليط لا بد من بيانها إن شاء الله تعالى بيان الكمال الحقيقي والكمال الوهمي الذي لا حقيقة له قد عرفت أنه لا كمال بعد فوات التفرد بالوجود إلا في العلم والقدرة ولكن الكمال الحقيقي فيه متلبس بالكمال
2:120.english: For this reason, he — peace and blessings be upon him — said: «مَنْهُومَانِ لَا يَشْبَعَانِ» ("Two are insatiably craving and never satiated"). Thus, what hearts seek is perfection, and perfection lies in knowledge and power; and the variance of degrees therein is unbounded. So each person's joy and pleasure are proportionate to the perfection he attains. This, then, is the cause of knowledge, wealth, and status being loved — a cause beyond their being loved merely as means to satisfying appetites. For this cause may persist even when appetites have fallen away; indeed, a man loves sciences that are of no use in attaining his worldly aims — nay, they may even cost him a host of his goals and appetites — yet nature still demands the pursuit of knowledge in all wondrous and perplexing things, because in knowledge there is a domination over the known, which is a kind of perfection belonging to the attributes of lordship. Thus it is naturally loved — except that in the love of the perfection of knowledge and power there are errors (aghalīṭ) that must be explained, God — exalted be He — willing.
2:120.section_title_en: The Love of Knowledge, Power, Wealth, and Status — and the True vs. Illusory Perfection
2:120.anchors:
- Root: قدر (qadr/qudrah)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core sense of measuring, determining, and enabling; qudrah as the capacity to bring about an act.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Qudrah attributed to humans is a disposition (hay'ah) enabling specific acts; attributed to God, it negates incapacity ('ajz). Absolute qudrah belongs to God alone; human power is always restricted and mixed with weakness.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "possessor of power" (dhū qudrah). Metaphorical: "far-reaching steed" (faras ba'īd al-qadr) — extended stride, indicating that "power over" something is figuratively an "extension" of one's reach.
- Root: علم (ʿilm)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Knowledge as the apprehension of a thing's reality; also traces/markers (aʿlām) by which one is guided.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): ʿIlm is "apprehension of a thing by its true reality" (idrāk al-shay' bi-ḥaqīqatihi) — either grasping the essence (dhāt) or judging its attributes.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "to be aware/informed." Metaphorical: "lofty banners of knowledge" (aʿlām al-ʿilm al-khāfiqah) — knowledge as a raised standard of honor and conquest over the unknown.
- Root: قلب (qalb)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Turning and overturning a thing from one state to another.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Taqlīb is the constant turning of a thing; the heart is so named for its perpetual fluctuation (taqallub) between states.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: to flip a garment or coin. Metaphorical: "a man who turns matters over" (rajul qalb ḥawal) — one who skillfully manages and dominates affairs; hearts are "subjugated" (taskhīr) only through love, which itself follows perceived perfection.
- Root: طبع (ṭabʿ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Stamping, impressing a seal upon a surface.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Ṭabʿ is to impress a form upon something, broader than khatm (sealing) and narrower than naqsh (engraving). God's "sealing" of hearts is a metaphor for their being rendered impervious to truth.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: coining a dirham. Metaphorical: "stamped by nature upon generosity" (maṭbūʿ ʿalā al-karam) — an ingrained, fixed disposition; here, the natural (bi-al-ṭabʿ) love of perfection is an innate impress of the divine attribute within the human subtlety.
- Sibawayh Rule: Restriction and Specification (Bāb al-Ḥaṣr wa al-Taqyīd bi-innamā) — The particle innamā restricts the predicate to the subject alone, as in "the object of hearts is perfection alone" (fa-innamā maṭlūb al-qulūb al-kamāl), eliminating any other motive.
2:120.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Poverty and Abstinence'

2:120.arabic: تعالى بتخصيص الإضافة إليه وإن كان الكل من جهته تعالى فقال تعالى {قل إن هدى الله هو الهدى} وهو المسمى حياة في قوله تعالى {أو من كان ميتا فأحييناه وجعلنا له نورا يمشي به في الناس} والمعنى بقوله تعالى {أفمن شرح الله صدره للإسلام فهو على نور من ربه} وأما الرشد فنعني به العناية الإلهية التي تعين الإنسان عند توجهه إلى مقاصده فتقوبه على ما فيه صلاحه وتفتره عما فيه فساده ويكون ذلك من الباطن كما قال تعالى {ولقد آتينا إبراهيم رشده من قبل وكنا به عالمين} فالرشد عبارة عن هداية باعثة إلى جهة السعادة محركة إليها فالصبي إذا بلغ خبيرا بحفظ الم
2:120.english:
PageV04P107
But if one does not know what constitutes the welfare of his hereafter—so that he even supposes corruption to be welfare—then from where would mere volition benefit him? There is no benefit in volition, power, and causes except after guidance (hidāyah). For this reason, God—exalted is He—said: {«ربنا الذي أعطى كل شيء خلقه ثم هدى»} "Our Lord who gave everything its creation, then guided." And He said—exalted is He—: {«ولولا فضل الله عليكم ورحمته ما زكى منكم أحد أبدا ولكن الله يزكي من يشاء»} "And were it not for God's bounty upon you and His mercy, not one of you would ever be purified; but God purifies whom He wills." And the Prophet—peace be upon him—said: "No one enters Paradise except by the mercy of God—exalted is He—," that is, by His guidance. So it was said: "Not even you, O Messenger of God?" He said: "Not even I" (1). And guidance (hidāyah) has three stations (manāzil):
2:120.section_title_en: The Degrees of Divine Guidance (Hidāyah), Righteous Discernment (Rushd), Straightening (Tasdīd), and Divine Support (Ta'yīd)
2:120.anchors:
- Root: هدي (H-D-Y)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of gentle, gracious direction (dalālah bi-luṭf); the root also yields "gift" (hadiyyah) and the leading beasts of prey (hawādī) that guide the herd.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Guidance is "directional indication with gentleness" (dalālah bi-luṭf), distinct from mere intellectual proof; it is a divine act that may be general (to all) or specific (to the elect), and its withholding is a form of abandonment.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): "He guided him to the path" (hadāhu lil-sabīl). Metaphorical (majāz): "He guided him" meaning "he preceded him" (taqaddamahu), as a leader precedes the caravan; hence guidance is not merely pointing but active leading.
- Root: رشد (R-SH-D)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The state of being rightly directed in one's affairs; integrity of judgment; names Rāshid, Rushayd derive from it.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Rushd is the opposite of ghayy (error/ruin); it is used like hidāyah but with a nuance of practical, executive discernment—knowing the good AND being moved to pursue it. Al-Raghib explicitly distinguishes the rushd of Abraham (given before, as a special gift) from the mere legal competence (rushd) of an orphan.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "A man is rāshid or rashīd" (possessing rightness in conduct). Metaphorical: "He is of sound lineage" (huwa li-rushdah), i.e., legitimate—showing the root's extension to ontological soundness.
- Root: سدد (S-D-D)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To aim correctly, to hit the mark; the arrow that flies straight (sadīd); the opposite of deviation (ighrāḍ).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): (Not in the retrieved scholia, but by extension from the root's usage in the Qur'an, e.g., {wa-saddidū}, "and be straight/aim rightly")—it denotes the divine facilitation of the creature's movements so they align with the intended good.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "He aimed the arrow and it went straight." Metaphorical: "He was granted success in speech and action" (sudda li-l-ṣawāb).
- Root: أيد (A-Y-D)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Strength, support, reinforcement; the "aid" (ayd) of God is His empowering of His servant.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): (By extension from {إذ أيدتك بروح القدس})—divine reinforcement through a holy spirit, i.e., an immaterial power that fortifies both inner perception (baṣīrah) and outer action.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "He strengthened him" (ayyadahu). Metaphorical: Used for the conferral of spiritual power that makes the servant invincible against error.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Gradation and Specification (Tartīb wa-Takhṣīṣ) — The author structures a sequence of terms (hidāyah → rushd → tasdīd → ta'yīd) where each subsequent term is syntactically and semantically superordinate, building a hierarchy of divine acts. The particle "wa-ammā" (وأما) marks a new topic with contrastive focus, and the anaphoric references (هو، وهي) bind the exposition into a single periodic argument.
2:120.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

2:268.arabic: وخافون إن كنتم مؤمنين وقال عز وجل الشيطان يعدكم الفقر ويأمركم بالفحشاء والله يعدكم مغفرة منه وفضلا والسؤال من الفحشاء التي أبيحت بالضرورة وحال من يسأل لحاجة متراخية عن يومه وإن كان مما يحتاج إليه في السنة أشد من حال من ملك مالا موروثا وادخره لحاجة وراء السنة وكلاهما مباحان في الفتوى الظاهرة ولكنهما صادران عن حب الدنيا وطول الأمل وعدم الثقة بفضل الله وهذه الخصلة من أمهات المهلكات نسأل الله حسن التوفيق بلطفه وكرمه بيان أحوال السائلين كان بشر رحمه الله يقول الفقراء ثلاثة فقير لا يسأل وإن أعطي لا يأخذ فهذا مع الروحانيين في عليين وفقير لا يسأل
2:268.english: But if his opportunity to ask would be lost, and he would find no one to give him if he delayed, then asking is permitted for him, because the hope of living a year is not far-fetched. By delaying his asking, he fears that he will remain in dire need, unable to obtain what would aid him. If his fear of being unable to ask in the future is weak, and that for which he asks falls outside the domain of necessity, then his asking is not free from disapproval (karāhah). And the degree of that disapproval corresponds to the degrees of the weakness of his dire need, his fear of missing the opportunity, and the remoteness of the period in which he would need to ask. All of this admits no precise delimitation (ḍabṭ); it is entrusted to the servant's personal striving (ijtihād) and his own discernment for himself, between him and Allah the Exalted. So let him consult his heart concerning it and act upon it, if he is a traveler of the path of the Hereafter. And whoever's certainty (yaqīn) is stronger, whose trust in the coming of provision in the future is more complete, and whose contentment (qanāʿah) with the provision of the moment is more manifest — his rank with Allah the Exalted is higher. Thus, fear of the future — when Allah has given you the provision of your day for yourself and your dependents — arises only from weakness of certainty and hearkening to the intimidation of Satan. Allah the Exalted has said: {«فَلَا تَخَافُوهُمْ وَخَافُونِ إِن كُنتُم مُّؤْمِنِينَ»} "So fear them not, but fear Me, if you are believers" (Q. 3:175). And He, Glorified and Exalted, said: {«الشَّيْطَانُ يَعِدُكُمُ الْفَقْرَ وَيَأْمُرُكُم بِالْفَحْشَاءِ وَاللَّهُ يَعِدُكُم مَّغْفِرَةً مِّنْهُ وَفَضْلًا»} "Satan promises you poverty and commands you to indecency, and Allah promises you forgiveness from Him and bounty" (Q. 2:268). And asking is among the indecencies (fawāḥish) that have been permitted by necessity. The state of one who asks for a need remote from his day — even if it is something he needs within the year — is worse than the state of one who possesses inherited wealth and has stored it for a need beyond the year. Both are permissible in the apparent legal ruling (fatwā), but both originate from love of this world, length of hope (ṭūl al-amal), and lack of trust in Allah's bounty. And this trait is among the mother of all destroyers (ummahāt al-muhlikāt). We ask Allah for beautiful success through His gentleness and generosity.
2:268.section_title_en: The Revival of the Religious Sciences — Book on the Etiquettes of Poverty and Asceticism: Section on the Degrees of the Askers and the States of the Poor
2:268.anchors:
- Root: س-أ-ل (sa-ʾa-la)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root denotes asking, requesting, or petitioning; the act of seeking something from another.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In theological usage, 'suʾāl' (asking) is tied to need (ḥājah) and is morally neutral in itself, becoming blameworthy when it exceeds necessity or arises from weak trust in Allah's provision.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) sense is the verbal request for an object; metaphorical (majāz) extension applies to asking of Allah in supplication (duʿāʾ), which is always praiseworthy.
- Root: ف-ق-ر (fa-qā-ra)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root denotes poverty, neediness, or lack of means; also spinal vulnerability (faqār), implying one broken by need.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): 'Faqr' is the existential state of being in want; in the Kalam framework, it contrasts with divine self-sufficiency (ghinā), and the poor (fuqarāʾ) are ranked by their inner state, not mere outward lack.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal sense is material destitution; metaphorical sense is spiritual poverty before Allah, the highest station of the knowers (ʿārifūn).
- Root: ي-ق-ن (ya-qī-na)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root denotes certainty, firm conviction, and the absence of doubt.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): 'Yaqīn' is the apex of faith (īmān), comprising knowledge (ʿilm), state (ḥāl), and action (ʿamal); it is the antidote to fear of future provision.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal sense is settled knowledge; metaphorical sense is the heart's repose in Allah's guarantee of sustenance, rendering anxiety a form of disbelief in that promise.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Conditional Restriction (al-sharṭ wa-l-jazāʾ) — The protasis (condition) and apodosis (result) structure in "If he is able to ask and does not miss his opportunity, then it is not lawful for him to ask" governs the legal determination, where the condition specifies the scope of the ruling.
2:268.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Poverty and Abstinence'

2:268.arabic: بد لهم منه وذلك لأن الشيطان يعدهم الفقر ويأمرهم بالفحشاء فيصغون إليه ويجمعون ما لا يأكلون خيفة الفقر والله يعدهم مغفرة منه وفضلا فيعرضون عنه ولا يرغبون فيه الأمر الثاني القيلولة وهي سنة يستعان بها على قيام الليل كما أن التسحر سنة يستعان به على صيام النهار فإن كان لا يقوم بالليل لكن لو لم ينم لم يشتغل بخير وربما خالط أهل الغفلة وتحدث معهم فالنوم أحب له إذا كان لا ينبعث نشاطه للرجوع إلى الأذكار والوظائف المذكورة إذ في النوم الصمت والسلامة وقد قال بعضهم يأتي على الناس زمان الصمت والنوم فيه أفضل أعم
2:268.english: Now, the first watch (al-wird al-awwal) is that which extends from the dawn prayer (ṣalāt al-ṣubḥ) until sunrise (ṭulūʿ al-shams). When the servant has completed his obligatory prayer, he should remain seated in his place of prayer, occupying himself with the remembrance of God most High, until the sun has risen. For it has been reported that the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "That I should sit in my assembly, remembering God most High therein, from the morning prayer until sunrise, is more beloved to me than freeing four slaves." {«لأن أقعد في مجلسي أذكر الله تعالى فيه من صلاة الغداة إلى طلوع الشمس أحب إلي من أن أعتق أربع رقاب»} And it is related that he, peace and blessings be upon him, when he had prayed the morning prayer, would sit in his place of prayer until the sun rose; and in some versions [it is added] that he would pray two rakʿahs—that is, after sunrise. Concerning the virtue of this [practice], an incalculable number of reports have come down. Al-Ḥasan related that the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, used to mention, among what he recounted of his Lord's mercy, that He said: "O son of Adam, remember Me for an hour after the dawn prayer and for an hour after the afternoon prayer, and I shall suffice you for what lies between them." {«يا ابن آدم اذكرني بعد صلاة الفجر ساعة وبعد صلاة العصر ساعة أكفك ما بينهما»}
2:268.section_title_en: The Daily Liturgy of the Devout Servant: The First Watch (After Dawn Prayer until Sunrise)
2:268.anchors:
- Root: ذكر (dhakara)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Remembrance, invocation, mention; the opposite of forgetfulness (nisyān).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Remembrance of God (dhikr) is the heart's presence with the Divine, ranging from the tongue's utterance to the heart's contemplation; it is the noblest act when accompanied by presence of heart.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): verbal mention. Metaphorical (majāz): the heart's steadfastness in knowledge of God, which is the reality of dhikr.
- Root: صلا (ṣallā)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Prayer (ṣalāh); root meaning of supplication and blessing; also "to kindle a fire" (as in ṣalā al-nār).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Ṣalāh is the servant's standing before God in humility and devotion, comprising praise, recitation, bowing, and prostration; its perfection lies in the heart's presence.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the ritual prayer with its pillars. Metaphorical: supplication (duʿā') and blessing (taṣliyah) upon the Prophet.
- Root: ورد (warada)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To arrive at water; a portion or share of something that comes regularly.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The daily portion (wird) of devotion—a set liturgy of prayers, recitations, and remembrances that the servant regularly performs at appointed times.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: arriving at a watering place. Metaphorical: the soul's regular approach to the fountain of divine grace through prescribed acts of worship.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Restriction and Specification (al-ḥaṣr wa al-taqyīd) — governing the precise enumeration of the four functions (adʿiyah, adhkār, qirā'ah, fikr) after the dawn prayer, each specified by its own governing verb and object.

2:268.arabic: ويجمعون ما لا يأكلون خيفة الفقر والله يعدهم مغفرة منه وفضلا فيعرضون عنه ولا يرغبون فيه الأمر الثاني القيلولة وهي سنة يستعان بها على قيام الليل كما أن التسحر سنة يستعان به على صيام النهار فإن كان لا يقوم بالليل لكن لو لم ينم لم يشتغل بخير وربما خالط أهل الغفلة وتحدث معهم فالنوم أحب له إذا كان لا ينبعث نشاطه للرجوع إلى الأذكار والوظائف المذكورة إذ في النوم الصمت والسلامة وقد قال بعضهم يأتي على الناس زمان الصمت والنوم فيه أفضل أعمالهم وكم من عابد أحسن أحواله النوم وذلك إذا كان يرائي بعبادته ولا يخل

2:268.arabic: الرجيم ثم تلا قوله تعالى الشيطان يعدكم الفقر ويأمركم بالفحشاء (1) أخرجه الترمذي والنسائي (2) حديث قلب المؤمن بين إصبعين الحديث تقدم فالله يتعالى عن أن يكون له أصبع مركبة من لحم ودم وعصب منقسمة بالأنامل ولكن روح الإصبع سرعة التقليب والقدرة على التحريك والتغيير فإنك لا تريد إصبعك لشخصه بل لفعله في التقليب والترديد كما أنك تتعاطى الأفعال بأصابعك والله تعالى يفعل ما يفعل باستسخار الملك والشيطان وهما مسخران بقدرته في تقليب القلوب كما أن أصابعك مسخرة لك في تقليب الأجسام مثلا والقلب بأصل الفطرة صالح لقبول آثار
2:268.english: The angel is an expression for a created being (khalq) whom God, Exalted is His majesty, created—whose very attribute is the effusion of good, the bestowal of knowledge, the uncovering of truth, the promising of good, and the commanding of what is right. He created him and subjugated him to that. The Satan is an expression for a created being whose attribute is the opposite of that—namely, the promising of evil, the commanding of indecency, and the frightening with poverty at the moment of resolving upon good. Thus whispering stands in opposition to inspiration, the Satan in opposition to the angel, and divine success in opposition to abandonment. And to this points His saying, Exalted is He: {«وَمِن كُلِّ شَيْءٍ خَلَقْنَا زَوْجَيْنِ»} (And of all things We have created pairs) [Quran 51:49]. For all existent things are paired and opposed—except God, Exalted is He, for He is the One (al-Fard) who has no opposite. Rather, He is the One, the True, the Creator of all pairs.
2:268.section_title_en: The Heart's Attraction Between the Angel and the Satan: On Inspiration and Whispering
2:268.anchors:
- Root: خطر (khaṭara)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The passing of something through the mind; the occurrence of a thought or notion.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The initial stirring of the heart toward an action—the first movement of intention.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the striking of an idea upon the heart. Metaphorical: the very inception of volitional acts.
- Root: ملك (malaka)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Possession, dominion; the angel as a created being entrusted with a function.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The angel is a subtle spiritual reality (laṭīfah) created for the effusion of good and the conveyance of divine command.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: one who possesses and governs. Metaphorical: the spiritual power that inclines the heart toward truth.
- Root: وسوس (waswasa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The faint, hidden sound; the subtle, insinuating call.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The whispering of the Satan—the evil suggestion that invites to transgression.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the quiet, indistinct voice. Metaphorical: the insinuation of evil into the heart.
- Root: لطف (laṭufa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Gentleness, subtlety, refinement.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The divine subtlety (al-luṭf) by which the heart is prepared to receive inspiration—a spiritual, immaterial reality.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: that which is fine and delicate. Metaphorical: the divine grace that disposes the heart toward good.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — The restriction of each cause to its specific effect, and the pairing of contrasting terms (inspiration vs. whispering; angel vs. Satan; success vs. abandonment) to establish the precise correspondence between spiritual causes and their consequences.
2:268.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'Disciplining the Soul'

2:269.arabic: ومن يؤت الحكمة فقد أوتى خيرا كثيرا} وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم كلمة من الحكمة يتعلمها الرجل خير له من الدنيا وما فيها (2) فانظر ما الذي كانت الحكمة عبارة عنه وإلى ماذا نقل وقس به بقية الألفاظ واحترز عن الاغترار بتلبيسات علماء السوء فإن شرهم على الدين أعظم من شر الشياطين إذ الشيطان بواسطتهم يتدرج إلى انتزاع الدين من قلوب الخلق ولهذا لما سئل رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عن شر الخلق أبى وقال اللهم اغفر حتى كرروا عليه فقال هم علماء السوء (3) فقد عرفت العلم المحمود والمذموم ومثار الالتباس وإلي
2:269.english: Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ, may God be pleased with him, said to his son ʿUmar — having heard him composing sajʿ — "This is what makes me dislike you. I will never fulfill your need until you repent." This was said when his son had come to him seeking a favor. And the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to ʿAbd Allāh ibn Rawāḥah when he spoke in sajʿ of three words: "Beware of sajʿ, O Ibn Rawāḥah." Thus, the forbidden sajʿ is the artificially contrived kind that exceeds two words. For this reason, when a man spoke concerning the blood-money for a fetus — saying, "How shall we pay blood-money for one who neither drank, nor ate, nor cried out, nor wailed? Such a one's blood is void" — the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, replied: "Sajʿ like the sajʿ of the bedouins!"
2:269.section_title_en: On the Etiquette of Preaching: The Condemnation of Artificial Sajʿ, Excessive Poetry, and the Perils of Shataḥ and Taʿwīl
2:269.anchors:
- Root: سجع (sajʿa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Rhymed prose; from the root meaning "to coo" (as a dove), indicating a measured, melodious cadence in speech.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In theological discourse, sajʿ is permissible when natural but blameworthy when artificially cultivated (takalluf), as it shifts focus from meaning to ornamentation.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) — natural rhythmic speech; Metaphorical (majāz) — the "sajʿ of the bedouins" (sajʿ al-aʿrāb) as a pejorative for empty, affected eloquence.
- Root: شعر (shiʿr)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Poetry; from the root denoting perception and fine discernment (shuʿūr), as the poet grasps subtle meanings.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Poetry is blameworthy when it stirs base appetites, but praiseworthy when it conveys wisdom (ḥikmah), as in the prophetic saying "Indeed from poetry there is wisdom."
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — metered, rhymed speech; Metaphorical — the "poetry" of the heart's inclination, where listeners project their own passions onto what they hear.
- Root: شطح (shaṭaḥa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To overflow, to gush forth; originally of a water-skin bursting, then applied to ecstatic utterances that overflow the bounds of conventional discourse.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In Sufi terminology, shataḥ refers to utterances arising from overwhelming spiritual states (ḥāl) that, when voiced to the unworthy, cause corruption.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — physical overflowing; Metaphorical — the soul's overflow in speech that exceeds the speaker's intentional control.
- Root: أول (taʿwīl)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To return something to its origin or end; interpretation that traces a word back to its intended meaning.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Taʿwīl is legitimate only when supported by textual (naqlī) or rational (ʿaqlī) evidence; arbitrary taʿwīl that severs words from their established senses destroys religious trust.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — the apparent sense (ẓāhir); Metaphorical — the inner sense (bāṭin), which is only valid when the literal sense is impossible or when transmitted authority sanctions it.
- Sibawayh Rule: Bāb al-Ḥaṣr wa al-Taqyīd bi-innamā (Restriction and Focused Predication) — The text repeatedly uses restrictive constructions (innamā, laysa...illā) to delimit permissible preaching, poetry, and interpretation, distinguishing the praiseworthy from the blameworthy with syntactic precision.
2:269.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications, prayers, and their spiritual power, from 'Poverty and Abstinence'

2:269.arabic: والحكمة هي التي أثنى الله عز وجل عليها فقال تعالى {يؤتى الحكمة من يشاء ومن يؤت الحكمة فقد أوتى خيرا كثيرا} وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم كلمة من الحكمة يتعلمها الرجل خير له من الدنيا وما فيها (2) فانظر ما الذي كانت الحكمة عبارة عنه وإلى ماذا نقل وقس به بقية الألفاظ واحترز عن الاغترار بتلبيسات علماء السوء فإن شرهم على الدين أعظم من شر الشياطين إذ الشيطان بواسطتهم يتدرج إلى انتزاع الدين من قلوب الخلق ولهذا لما سئل رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عن شر الخلق أبى وقال اللهم اغفر حتى كرروا عليه فقال هم علماء السوء (3) فقد عرفت العلم المحمود والمذموم ومثار الالتباس وإليك
2:269.english: Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ, may God be pleased with him, said to his son ʿUmar — having heard him composing sajʿ — "This is what makes me dislike you. 2:273.arabic: ديارهم وأموالهم} الآية وقال تعالى {للفقراء الذين أحصروا في سبيل الله لا يستطيعون ضربا في الأرض} ساق الكلام في معرض المدح ثم قدم وصفهم بالفقر على وصفهم بالهجرة والإحصار وفيه دلالة ظاهرة على مدح الفقر وأما الأخبار في مدح الفقر فأكثر من أن تحصى روى عبد الله بن عمر رضي الله عنهما قال قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لأصحابه أي الناس خير فقالوا موسر من المال يعطي حق الله من نفسه وماله فقال نعم الرجل هذا وليس به قالوا فمن خير الناس يا رسول الله قال فقير يعطي جهده (4) وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم لبلال الق الله فقيرا ولا تلقه غنيا (5) وقال صلى الله
2:273.english: As for the verses [of the Qur'an], that is indicated by His saying, the Exalted: {«لِلْفُقَرَاءِ الْمُهَاجِرِينَ الَّذِينَ أُخْرِجُوا مِنْ دِيَارِهِمْ وَأَمْوَالِهِمْ»} [To the poor emigrants who were driven out of their homes and their wealth] (59:8), to the end of the verse. And He said, the Exalted: {«لِلْفُقَرَاءِ الَّذِينَ أُحْصِرُوا فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ لَا يَسْتَطِيعُونَ ضَرْبًا فِي الْأَرْضِ»} [To the poor who are confined in the way of Allah, unable to travel in the land] (2:273). He directed the discourse in the context of praise, then He advanced their description with poverty before their description with emigration and confinement. In this there is an evident indication of the praise of poverty.
2:273.section_title_en: The Virtue of Poverty: Scriptural Evidences and Their Interpretation
2:273.anchors:
- Root: فقر (F-Q-R)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of need, indigence, and the state of lacking possessions; also the notches of a vertebra or the joints of the back, indicating structural dependence.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Poverty is of four degrees: (1) essential neediness before God (universal to all creatures), (2) lack of worldly goods (the subject here), (3) voluntary renunciation (zuhd), and (4) the perfection of the heart's detachment. The praise of poverty here targets the second and third degrees, not destitution that breeds discontent.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah) poverty is the absence of wealth; metaphorical (Majaz) poverty is the soul's humility and its "notches" of dependence on God. The Prophet's praise of the "poor" (fuqara') must be read as praise of the virtuous poor (mutafaQQir), not the covetous.
- Root: هجر (H-J-R)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To abandon, emigrate, or sever ties; the act of leaving one's homeland for a religious purpose.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Hijrah (emigration) is a physical act of devotion, but the Quranic verse pairs it with poverty, elevating the state of neediness as a spiritual station above the mere act of relocation.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): The verse's structure (taqdim) places "poverty" before "emigration" and "confinement," signaling its superior rank in the divine estimation.
- Root: قدر (Q-D-R)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Measure, decree, power, and estimation; the act of determining a precise limit or quantity.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): When applied to God, Qadar is His eternal decree; when applied to the Prophet's speech, it denotes precise, divinely-inspired measurement—never arbitrary or haphazard.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: to measure out (qaddara). Metaphorical: the "measure" of a thing's worth or rank. The Prophet's numerical estimates (e.g., 500 years, 46 parts) are literal measures of spiritual realities, though their exact rationale may be hidden from non-prophetic intellects.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — The Quranic construction {للفقراء المهاجرين} uses prepositional fronting (taqdim) to restrict the praise to a specific class, and the sequence of descriptors (poverty before hijrah) establishes a hierarchy of virtues through syntactic ordering.

3:7.arabic: علما وهذه أمور لا يعلم تأويلها إلا الله والراسخون في العلم وعبر ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما عن اختصاص الراسخين في العلم بعلوم لا تحتملها أفهام الخلق حيث قرأ قوله تعالى {يتنزل الأمر بينهن} فقال لو ذكرت ما أعرفه من معنى هذه الآية لرجمتموني وفي لفظ آخر لقلتم إنه كافر ولنقتصر على هذا القدر فقد خرج عنان الكلام عن قبضة الاختيار وامتزج بعلم المعاملة ما ليس منه فلنرجع إلى مقاصد الشكر فنقول إذا رجع حقيقة الشكر إلى كون العبد مستعملا في إتمام حكمة الله تعالى فأشكر العباد أحبهم إلى الله وأقربهم إليه وأقربهم إلى الله
3:7.english: Thus was the beginning of this matter and its end. And do not understand it unless you are worthy of it. And if you are worthy of it, the eye is opened and you see, so you have no need of a leader to lead you. The blind man can indeed be led, but only to a limit. For when the path narrows and becomes sharper than a sword and finer than a hair, the bird is able to fly over it but is not able to drag a blind man behind it. And when the field becomes narrow and subtle — subtle as water, for example — and crossing is possible only by swimming, then the one skilled in the art of swimming may be able to cross by himself, and perhaps he is not able to drag another behind him. These matters bear the same relation to walking upon the way of the common masses of creatures as walking upon water bears to walking upon earth. Swimming can be learned; but as for walking upon water, it is not acquired by instruction, but rather is attained through the strength of certainty (yaqīn). For this reason it was said to the Prophet, peace be upon him, that Jesus, peace be upon him, was said to have walked upon water, and he, peace be upon him, said: "Had his certainty increased, he would have walked upon the air." {«حديث قيل له يقال إن عيسى مشى على الماء قال لو ازداد يقينا لمشي على الهواء»} — This hadith is rejected (munkar) and is not known in this form. What is known is what Ibn Abi al-Dunya narrated in the Book of Certainty from the saying of Bakr ibn Abd Allah al-Muzani, who said: The disciples lost their Prophet, and it was said to them: "He has headed toward the sea." So they set out seeking him, and when they reached the sea, behold, he was coming toward them walking upon the water. And he mentioned a hadith in which Jesus said: "If the son of Adam had a hair's breadth of certainty, he would walk upon the water." And Abu Mansur al-Daylami narrated in the Musnad al-Firdaws with a weak chain from the hadith of Muadh ibn Jabal: "If you knew God with true knowledge, you would walk upon the seas, and the mountains would be removed by your supplications." These are symbols and allusions to the meaning of aversion (karāhah) and love (maḥabbah), and good pleasure (riḍā) and wrath (ghaḍab), and gratitude (shukr) and ingratitude (kufrān) — more than this is not fitting for the science of practical conduct (ʿilm al-muʿāmalah). And God, exalted be He, struck an example of this to draw it near to the understanding of creatures, since He knew that He created the jinn and mankind only to worship Him, and their worship was the ultimate purpose of wisdom (ghāyat al-ḥikmah) with respect to them. Then He informed that He has two servants: one whom He loves, whose name is Gabriel — the Holy Spirit and the Trustworthy One — and he is with Him beloved, obeyed, trustworthy, and honored; and another whom He hates, whose name is Iblis — the accursed one, reprieved until the Day of Judgment. Then He delegated guidance (irshād) to Gabriel, saying, the Exalted: {«قل نزله روح القدس من ربك بالحق»} "Say: The Holy Spirit has brought it down from your Lord with truth" (16:102), and said, the Exalted: {«يلقي الروح من أمره على من يشاء من عباده»} "He casts the Spirit of His command upon whom He wills of His servants" (40:15). And He delegated misguidance (ighwāʾ) to Iblis, saying, the Exalted: {«ليضل عن سبيله»} "That he may lead astray from His path" (4:119). And ighwāʾ is the halting of servants short of attaining the ultimate purpose of wisdom. So observe how He attributed it to the servant with whom He was wrathful; and guidance (irshād) is the conduct of them toward the ultimate purpose — so observe how He attributed it to the servant whom He loves. And you have an example of this in custom: when a king is in need of one to give him drink and one to cup him and to clean the courtyard of his house of filth, and he has two servants, he does not appoint for cupping and cleaning except the ugliest and meanest of them, and he does not entrust the carrying of drink and perfume except to the best and most complete of them and the most beloved to him. And you should not say: "This is my act, and his act was not without my act" — for you have erred when you attributed that to yourself. Rather, He is the One who directed your motive (dāʿiyah) to the specification of the disliked act to the disliked person, and the beloved act to the beloved person, as a completion of justice (ʿadl). For His justice is sometimes completed through matters in which you have no entry, and sometimes it is completed in you — for you also are among His acts. So your motive, your power, your knowledge, your action, and all the other causes of your movements in expression — all of this is His act, which He arranged with justice in an arrangement from which moderate acts issue forth. Except that you see only yourself, and so you suppose that what appears through you in the world of witness (ʿālam al-shahādah) has no cause from the world of the unseen and the dominion (ʿālam al-ghayb wa al-malakūt). Therefore you attribute it to yourself. And you are only like the child who looks at night at the play of the juggler (mushʿabadh) who brings forth figures from behind a curtain that dance and scream and rise and sit, composed of rags that do not move by themselves — rather, they are moved by fine hair-like threads that do not appear in the darkness of night, their ends in the hand of the juggler, who is hidden from the eyes of the children. So they rejoice and marvel, supposing that those rags dance and play and rise and sit. As for the intelligent ones, they know that this is a moving (taḥrīk) and not a self-movement, but perhaps they do not know its detailed modality. And the one who knows some of its detail does not know it as the juggler knows it, to whom the command belongs and in whose hand is the pulling. Likewise, the children of the people of this world — and all creatures are children relative to the scholars — look at these persons (ashkhāṣ) and suppose that they are the movers, and so they attribute [action] to them. And the scholars know that they are moved, except that they do not know the modality of the moving — and they are the majority. Except the knowers (ʿārifūn), the scholars, and those firmly rooted in knowledge (al-rāsikhūn), for they have perceived, with the sharpness of their sight, fine spider-web threads — nay, much finer than these — suspended from heaven, their ends attached to the persons of the people of the earth. Those threads are not perceived, due to their fineness, by these outward eyes. Then they witnessed the heads of those threads in their suspension-points (manāṭāt) to which they are attached, and they witnessed for those suspension-points handles (maqābiḍ) that are in the hands of the angels who move the heavens. And they also witnessed the angels of the heavens directed toward the bearers of the Throne (ḥamalat al-ʿarsh), awaiting what descends upon them of the command from the presence of Lordship (ḥaḍrat al-rubūbiyyah) — "they do not disobey God in what He commands them, and they do what they are commanded" (66:6). And He expressed these witnessed realities in the Qur'an, and it was said: {«وفي السماء رزقكم وما توعدون»} "And in the heaven is your provision and what you are promised" (51:22). And He expressed the waiting of the angels of the heavens for what descends upon them of decree and command, and it was said: "He created seven heavens and of the earth the like of them; {«يتنزل الأمر بينهن لتعلموا أن الله على كل شيء قدير وأن الله قد أحاط بكل شيء علما»} 'the command descends between them, that you may know that God is powerful over all things and that God encompasses all things in knowledge'" (65:12). These are matters whose interpretation (taʾwīl) none knows except God and those firmly rooted in knowledge (al-rāsikhūn fī al-ʿilm). And Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, expressed the exclusivity of those firmly rooted in knowledge to sciences that the understandings of creatures cannot bear, when he recited the saying of the Exalted: {«يتنزل الأمر بينهن»} "The command descends between them," and said: "Were I to mention what I know of the meaning of this verse, you would stone me" — and in another wording: "You would say he is an unbeliever."
