4:77.arabic: الصلاة التي هي أعلى الأعلام فقال تعالى {وأقيموا الصلاة وآتوا الزكاة} وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم بني الإسلام على خمس شهادة أن لا إله إلا الله وأن محمدا عبده ورسوله وإقام الصلاة وإيتاء الزكاة (2) وشدد الوعيد على المقصرين فيها فقال {والذين يكنزون الذهب والفضة ولا ينفقونها في سبيل الله فبشرهم بعذاب أليم} ومعنى الإنفاق في سبيل الله إخراج حق الزكاة قال الأحنف بن قيس كنت في نفر من قريش فمر أبو ذر فقال بشر الكانزين بكي في ظهورهم يخرج من جنوبهم وبكي في أقفائهم يخرج من جباههم وفي رواية أنه يوضع على حلمة ثدي أحده
4:77.english: To proceed: God Most High made alms (al-zakāh) one of the pillars of Islam, and joined its mention with prayer (al-ṣalāh), which is the loftiest of symbols. He said Most High: {«وَأَقِيمُوا الصَّلَاةَ وَآتُوا الزَّكَاةَ»} — "And establish prayer and give alms." And he, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Islam is built upon five: the testimony that there is no god but God and that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger, the establishment of prayer, and the giving of alms." And He intensified the threat against those who fall short in it, saying: {«وَالَّذِينَ يَكْنِزُونَ الذَّهَبَ وَالْفِضَّةَ وَلَا يُنفِقُونَهَا فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ فَبَشِّرْهُم بِعَذَابٍ أَلِيمٍ»} — "And those who hoard gold and silver and do not spend them in the way of God — give them tidings of a painful chastisement." And the meaning of "spending in the way of God" is the payment of the due right of alms (zakāh).
4:77.section_title_en: The Book of the Secrets of Alms (Zakat) — Section 167
4:77.anchors:
- Root: زكا (Z-K-Y)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "Zakā al-zar'u yazkū zakā'an: it increased and grew." Core meaning: growth, increase, purification.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "The origin of zakāh is the growth that occurs through the blessing of God Most High... and from it is zakāh: what a person pays of God's right to the poor, so named for the hope of blessing in it, or for the purification (tazkiyah) of the soul, i.e., its growth."
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (haqīqah): growth and increase. Metaphorical (majāz): the purification of wealth through payment of the obligatory due.
- Root: نعم (N-'-M)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "Na'ima 'ayshuhu: his life was pleasant." Core meaning: bounty, well-being, grace.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Al-Ni'mah: the good state... and al-Ni'mah (with kasrah) is used for the genus, said of both little and much."
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "Jallat ni'mat Allāh wa na'mā'uh" — God's grace and bounty are immense. Metaphorical: "Khāfat na'āmatuhum" — their ostriches departed (i.e., they fled), showing the root's extended usage.
- Root: ظهر (Z-H-R)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "Zahara: to become apparent, to be victorious." Core meaning: back, outward appearance, manifestation.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Al-Zahr: the back (body part)... and it is used metaphorically for the surface of the earth."
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "Rajul muzhir: a man strong of back." Metaphorical: "Qalabtu al-amra zahrān li-baṭn" — I turned the matter over back and belly (examined it thoroughly).
- Root: سرر (S-R-R)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "Sarra: to conceal, to keep secret." Core meaning: secret, inner self, joy.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Al-Isrār: the opposite of al-i'lān (declaring)... and al-sirr is the speech concealed in the soul."
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "Asarra al-ḥadīth: he concealed the speech." Metaphorical: "Aṭaytuka sirrah: I gave you its choicest part (the secret/core of something)."
- Sibawayh Rule: Bāb al-faṣl bayna al-jār wa al-majrūr (Prepositional Interposition) — The permissibility of interposing elements between a preposition and its object when the intervening clause is complete in itself, as in "fa'āfa 'alayhim min ni'matihi mā..." where the prepositional phrase is completed after an intervening relative clause.
4:77.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications, prayers, and their spiritual power, from 'Mysteries of Zakat'

4:77.arabic: عنها لم يردها ولذلك لما كتب عليهم القتال قالوا ربنا لم كتبت علينا القتال لولا أخرتنا إلى أجل قريب فقال تعالى قل متاع الدنيا قليل أي لستم تريدون البقاء إلا لمتاع الدنيا فظهر عند ذلك الزاهدون وانكشف حال المنافقين أما الزاهدون المحبون لله تعالى فقاتلوا في سبيل الله كأنهم بنيان مرصوص وانتظروا إحدى الحسنيين وكانوا إذا دعوا إلى القتال يستنشقون رائحة الجنة ويبادرون إليه مبادرة الظمآن إلى الماء البارد حرصا على نصرة دين الله
4:77.english: The third degree — and it is the highest — is that one renounce willingly, and renounce his very renunciation, so that he does not see his asceticism, since he does not see that he has abandoned anything, having come to know that the world is nothing. {PageV04P225} He is thus like one who casts away a potsherd and takes up a jewel — he does not regard that as an exchange, nor does he see himself as having abandoned anything. And the world, in comparison to God Most High and the bliss of the Hereafter, is baser than a potsherd in comparison to a jewel. This then is perfection in asceticism.
4:77.section_title_en: The Degrees of Asceticism (Zuhd) and Its Divisions
4:77.anchors:
- Root: زهد (Z-H-D)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: scarcity, paucity; al-Zuhd as abstemiousness; zāhada fīhi: to turn away from something, deeming it insignificant.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الزاهد في الشيء: الراغب عنه والراضي منه بالزهيد، أي: القليل" — the ascetic is one who turns away from a thing, content with little of it; theological sense: renunciation of the world as a deliberate act of valuation.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): "زهد في الشيء: رغب عنه" — turning away. Metaphorical (Majaz): "رجل زهيد: قليل الخير" — one of little good; "اد زهيد: قليل الأخذ للماء" — a valley taking little water. Here, al-Ghazali employs the literal sense of deliberate aversion, extended metaphorically to the soul's turning from all worldly appetites.
- Root: دنا (D-N-W)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Proximity, nearness; al-dunyā (the lower world) named for its nearness to us or its lowness.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الدنو: القرب بالذات، أو بالحكم" — nearness by essence or by judgment; al-dunyā contrasted with al-ākhirah as the inferior and nearer realm.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: proximity in place or rank. Metaphorical: the world as "lower" (adnā) in value — the sense operative in al-Ghazali's comparison of the world to a potsherd.
- Root: درج (D-R-J)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To walk step by step; to pass away (daraja: died, passed on); degree/stair.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الدرجة نحو المنزلة، لكن يقال للمنزلة: درجة إذا اعتبرت بالصعود" — a station considered as ascent; used for ranks of honor.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "درج قرن بعد قرن" — generations passed away; "رقي في الدرجة" — ascended in rank. Metaphorical: "لفلان درجة رفيعة" — one has a lofty degree. Al-Ghazali uses darajāt as ascending ranks of spiritual attainment.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد (Restriction and Specification) — the repeated use of "إنما" (only/but) in the Quranic citations (e.g., {إنما الحياة الدنيا لعب ولهو}) functions as restrictive predication (qasr), confining the reality of the world to play and diversion — a syntactic key to al-Ghazali's argument that all worldly goods reduce ultimately to one thing: caprice (hawā).
4:77.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Poverty and Abstinence'

4:125.arabic: وقال أبو سليمان لما اتخذ الله إبراهيم خليلا أوحى إليه أن وار عورتك من الأرض وكان لا يتخذ من كل شيء إلا واحدا سوى السراويل فإنه كان يتخذ سراويلين فإذا غسل أحدهما لبس الآخر حتى لا يأتي عليه حال إلا وعورته مستورة وقيل لسلمان الفارسي رضي الله عنه مالك لا تلبس الجيد من الثياب فقال وما للعبد والثوب الحسن فإذا عتق فله والله ثياب لا تبلى أبدا ويروى عن عمر بن عبد العزيز رحمه الله أنه كان له جبة شعر وكساء يلبسهما من الليل إذا قام يصلي وقال الحسن لفرقد السبخي تحسب أن لك فضلا على الناس
4:125.english: ʿĀ'ishah, may God Most High be well pleased with her, said: "Forty nights would pass over us without a lamp or fire being lit in the house of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace." It was said to her: "Then by what did you live?" She said: "By the two black things: dates and water." (1) This is the abandonment of meat, broth, and condiments.
4:125.section_title_en: The Revival of the Religious Sciences — Book on Poverty and Asceticism (Kitāb al-Faqr wa al-Zuhd): Section on the Ascetic's Conduct Regarding Food, Clothing, Dwelling, and Furnishings
4:125.anchors:
- Root: طوي (ṭ-w-y)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To fold up, to roll up; to pass the night fasting (ṭawā); to traverse a distance.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Implies enduring hunger by "folding" the stomach over itself—abstaining from filling it.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: folding a garment. Metaphorical: the ascetic "folds up" his days in hunger, i.e., passes them without food.
- Root: لبس (l-b-s)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To cover, to clothe; to become confused/ambiguous (il tibās).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Clothing as that which covers one's shame (saw'ah); extended metaphorically to the spouse as a "garment" (libās) for the other.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: wearing a garment. Metaphorical: "wearing" a people's manner/dress (ziyy) entails becoming one of them—hence the Hadith cited: "Whoever imitates a people's dress is of them."
- Root: بني (b-n-y)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To build, to erect a structure; binyān: edifice.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Building beyond necessity is a sign of long hope (ṭūl al-amal) and worldly attachment, antithetical to zuhd.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: construction with mortar and brick. Metaphorical: "raising" oneself in pride (ʿulūw) — condemned in the Qur'anic verse cited.
- Root: سكن (s-k-n)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To dwell, to be tranquil; maskan: dwelling place.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The dwelling is for repelling harm (heat, cold, eyes) — its measure is necessity (ḍarūrah), not luxury.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: a place of residence. Metaphorical: the heart's "dwelling" on God (sakīnah) — contrasted with physical dwellings that distract.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — Used to delimit the degrees of zuhd: "The least degree is only what repels heat and cold..." (innamā yuqṣad), restricting the licit to the necessary.
4:125.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'Poverty and Abstinence'

5:54.arabic: وإن اشتركوا في مصيبة الحرمان من حقيقة الأمر فالحقيقة فضل الله يؤتيه من يشاء والله ذو الفضل العظيم وحكمته يختص بها من يشاء ومن يؤت الحكمة فقد أوتي خيرا كثيرا ولنعد إلى الغرض فقد أرخينا الطول وطولنا النفس في أمر هو أعلاى من علوم المعاملات التي نقصدها في هذا الكتاب فقد ظهر أن رتبة الهلاك ليس إلا للجهال المكذبين وشهادة ذلك من كتاب الله وسنة رسوله صلى الله عليه وسلم لا تدخل تحت الحصر فلذلك لم نوردها الرتبة الثانية رتبة المعذبين وهذه رتبة من تحلى بأصل الإيمان ولكن قصر في الوفاء بمقتضاه فإن رأس الإيمان هو التوحيد وهو أن لا يعبد
5:54.english: The fire of Hell is the coldest of fires [in comparison to the fire of separation]. And you should not deny this in the world of the Hereafter, for it has a witnessed parallel in the world of this world. Indeed, one has been seen who was overcome by ecstasy (wajd) and walked upon fire and upon the roots of cane, his feet being cut, yet he did not feel it, due to the extreme dominance of what was in his heart. And you see the angry man, when anger overcomes him in battle, receiving wounds and not feeling them at that moment, because anger is a fire in the heart. The Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, said: {«الغضب قطعة من النار»} "Anger is a piece of fire." The burning of the heart (iḥtirāq al-fu'ād) is more severe than the burning of bodies, and the more severe annuls the sensation of the weaker, as you observe. For destruction from fire and the sword is only inasmuch as they separate between two parts that are linked one to the other by the bond of composition (ta'līf) possible in bodies. So that which separates between the heart and its Beloved, to which it is linked by a bond of composition far more firm than the composition of bodies, is more intensely painful—if you are among the people of insight (abṣār) and the people of hearts. And it is not far-fetched that he who has no heart should not perceive the severity of this pain and should deem it trivial in comparison to bodily pain. For a boy, if he were given the choice between the pain of being deprived of a ball and a polo-stick, and the pain of being deprived of the rank of a Sultan, he would not feel the pain of deprivation from the Sultan's rank at all, nor would he count that as a pain. And the enemy in the field with the polo-stick is more beloved to him than a thousand thrones of the Sultan with sitting upon them. Nay, even one overcome by the lust of the belly, if given the choice between porridge (harīsah) and sweets (ḥalwā) and between a beautiful deed by which he conquers enemies and delights friends, he would prefer the porridge and sweets. All of this is due to the absence of the meaning (maʿnā) by whose existence rank becomes beloved, and the presence of the meaning by whose existence food becomes delicious. This is for one whom the attributes of beasts and predators have enslaved, and in whom the attributes of the angels have not appeared—those attributes which are not suited by, nor delight in, anything but proximity to the Lord of the Worlds, and which are pained only by distance and the veil (ḥijāb). And just as taste is only in the tongue and hearing only in the ears, so this attribute is only in the heart. So he who has no heart has no such sense, like he who has no hearing or sight has no pleasure in melodies or the beauty of forms and colors. And not every human has a heart; were it so, the saying of God, Most High, would not be sound: {«إن في ذلك لذكرى لمن كان له قلب»} "Indeed in that is a reminder for whoever has a heart" (Q. 50:37). Thus He made the one who does not heed the Quran devoid of a heart. And by "heart" I do not mean this [organ] which the ribs of the chest encompass. Rather, I mean the secret (sirr) which is of the world of the Command (ʿālam al-amr). The flesh which is of the world of Creation (ʿālam al-khalq) is its Throne (ʿarsh), the chest is its Footstool (kursī), and the rest of the limbs are its domain and kingdom. And to God belongs the Creation and the Command altogether. But that secret, concerning which God, Most High, said: {«قل الروح من أمر ربي»} "Say: The Spirit is of the Command of my Lord" (Q. 17:85), is the commander and the king, because between the world of the Command and the world of Creation there is an ordering, and the world of the Command is commander over the world of Creation. It is the subtle divine reality (al-laṭīfah) which, when it is sound, the rest of the body is sound for its sake. Whoever knows it has known his own self, and whoever knows his own self has known his Lord. At that point, the servant smells the beginnings of the fragrance of the meaning folded under his saying, peace and blessings be upon him: {«إن الله خلق آدم على صورته»} "God created Adam upon His image." He looks with the eye of mercy upon those who adhere to its literal wording and upon those who are obstinate in the path of its interpretation (ta'wīl). And even though His mercy for those adhering to the letter is greater than His mercy for the obstinate interpreters, because mercy is proportional to the affliction, and the affliction of those [literalists] is greater—even if they share in the affliction of being deprived of the reality of the matter—for the Reality (al-ḥaqīqah) is the bounty of God which He gives to whom He wills, and God is the Possessor of Great Bounty. And His Wisdom is singled out for whom He wills: {«ومن يؤت الحكمة فقد أوتي خيرا كثيرا»} "And whoever is given wisdom has been given much good" (Q. 2:269). Let us return to the purpose, for we have drawn out the length and lengthened the breath in a matter that is higher than the sciences of transactions (muʿāmalāt) which we intend in this book. It has become clear that the rank of destruction is only for the ignorant deniers. And the testimony of that from the Book of God and the Sunnah of His Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, is beyond enumeration, so we have not cited it.
5:54.section_title_en: The Ranks of the Hereafter: On the Distribution of Degrees and the States of the Saved, the Punished, and the Victorious
5:54.anchors:
- Root: ح ر ق (ḥ-r-q)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of burning, scorching, and the fire's consumption of its fuel.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The fire of the Hereafter (Nār) is a created reality, but its perception is tied to the spiritual state of the perceiver.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah) for physical burning; metaphorical (Majaz) for the burning of the heart (iḥtirāq al-fu'ād) by overwhelming love or anger.
- Root: ق ل ب (q-l-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To turn, overturn, or transform a thing from one state to another.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The heart (Qalb) is the seat of perception and understanding, distinct from the physical organ.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal for the physical heart; metaphorical for the spiritual subtlety (Laṭīfah) that is the locus of divine knowledge and love.
- Root: ع ل م (ʿ-l-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To know, to perceive a thing by its true nature.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Knowledge (ʿIlm) is the apprehension of a thing's reality, which is the basis for distinguishing the ranks of the believers.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal for acquired knowledge; metaphorical for the "unveiling" (Kashf) knowledge granted to the knowers (ʿĀrifūn).
- Sibawayh Rule: Restriction and Specification (Bāb al-Ḥaṣr wa al-Taqyīd bi-innamā) — Used to distinguish the specific referents of terms like "heart" (Qalb) and "faith" (Īmān), ensuring the precise meaning is not conflated with common usage.
5:54.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Poverty and Abstinence'

5:54.arabic: لانفضوا من حولك ووصف أولياءه فقال أذلة على المؤمنين أعزة على الكافرين وكذلك قال صلى الله عليه وسلم فيما رواه العباس رضي الله عنه يكون قوم يقرءون القرآن لا يجاوز حناجرهم يقولون قد قرأنا القرآن فمن أقرأ منا ومن أعلم منا ثم التفت إلى أصحابه وقال أولئك منكم أيها الأمة أولئك هم
5:54.english: The second aspect by which the vice of pride is magnified is that it calls to opposing Allah the Exalted in His commands. For the arrogant man, when he hears the truth from a servant among the servants of Allah, disdains to accept it and girds himself for its denial. For this reason you see the disputants in matters of religion claiming that they are investigating the secrets of the religion, yet they engage in mutual denial—the denial of the arrogant. Whenever the truth becomes clear upon the tongue of one of them, the other refuses to accept it out of pride, girds himself for its denial, and resorts to every stratagem to repel it by whatever obfuscation he can muster. This is among the moral traits of the disbelievers and the hypocrites, for Allah the Exalted described them, saying: {«وَقَالَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا لَا تَسْمَعُوا لِهَذَا الْقُرْآنِ وَالْغَوْا فِيهِ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَغْلِبُونَ»} (And those who disbelieve said: "Do not listen to this Quran and make noise therein, perhaps you may prevail.") So whoever disputes for the sake of victory and silencing the opponent—not to seize the truth when it appears to him—has shared with them in this moral trait. Likewise, this pride drives one to refuse admonition, as Allah the Exalted said: {«وَإِذَا قِيلَ لَهُ اتَّقِ اللَّهَ أَخَذَتْهُ الْعِزَّةُ بِالْإِثْمِ»} (And when it is said to him, "Fear Allah," pride in sin seizes him.) It is narrated that ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him, recited this verse and then said: {«إِنَّا لِلَّهِ وَإِنَّا إِلَيْهِ رَاجِعُونَ»} (Indeed, we belong to Allah and to Him we return.) A man rose to enjoin good and was killed; then another rose and said: "They kill those who enjoin justice among the people"—and the arrogant one who opposed him and the one who commanded him was killed out of pride.
5:54.section_title_en: The Second Aspect by Which the Vice of Pride (Kibr) Is Magnified: That It Leads to Opposing Allah in His Commands
5:54.anchors:
- Root: كبر (K-B-R)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of bigness, magnitude, and seniority; al-kibr is the internal disposition of self-magnification.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-Kabīr and al-Ṣaghīr are relative terms (mutadāyifān); kibr as a moral vice is the soul's claim to a station above its due, entailing disdain for others.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) usage concerns physical or quantitative magnitude; metaphorical (majāz) usage here denotes arrogance and haughtiness—"كبر عليه" (he disdained it).
- Root: علم (ʿ-L-M)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Knowing a thing's reality; the root also carries the sense of a mark/trace (ʿalam) by which one is guided.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): True knowledge (ʿilm) is apprehension of a thing's essence or judgment about it; the highest form is knowledge of Allah, the self, and the Final End—this engenders fear (khashyah).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: perception and awareness; metaphorical: the "marks" (maʿālim) of religion—the distinguishing signs of guidance.
- Root: نفس (N-F-S)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The self, soul, or spirit; that which is valued and precious.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-Nafs denotes the soul or self; in theological usage it may refer to the essence (dhāt) of a thing.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the soul; metaphorical: self-worth and self-regard—the arrogant man "magnifies his own soul" (istaʿẓama nafsahu).
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — The verse {إِنَّمَا يَخْشَى اللَّهَ مِنْ عِبَادِهِ الْعُلَمَاءُ} restricts true fear of Allah exclusively to the learned, delimiting the predicate to the subject.
5:54.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'Condemnation of Pride and Conceit'

5:54.arabic: وقد قال الله تعالى يا أيها الذين آمنوا أنفقوا من طيبات ما كسبتم ومما أخرجنا لكم من الأرض ولا تيمموا الخبيث منه تنفقون ولستم بآخذيه إلا أن تغمضوا فيه أي لا تأخذوه إلا مع كراهية وحياء وهو معنى الإغماض فلا تؤثروا به ربكم وفي الخبر سبق درهم مائة ألف درهم (3) وذلك بأن يخرجه الإنسان وهو من أحل ماله وأجوده فيصدر ذلك عن الرضا والفرح بالبذل وقد يخرج مائة ألف درهم مما يكره من ماله فيدل ذلك على أنه ليس يؤثر الله عز وجل بشيء مما يحبه وبذلك ذم الله تعالى قوما جعلوا لله ما يكرهون فقال تعال
5:54.english: The heart is not treated save with the compound electuary (maʿjūn) of knowledge and works. And this condition among the conditions of almsgiving runs in the same course as humility (al-khushūʿ) runs in the prayer. This is established by his saying — may Allah bless him and grant him peace: "A man has nothing of his prayer save that of which he was conscious." And this is like his saying — may Allah bless him and grant him peace: "Allah does not accept the charity of the one who bestows it with reproach (al-mannān)." And like His saying — Exalted is He: {«لا تبطلوا صدقاتكم بالمن والأذى»} ("Do not nullify your charities by reproach and injury"). As for the legal opinion (fatwā) of the jurist that the alms fall in their proper place and that one's liability is discharged without this condition — that is another discussion, and we have already pointed to its meaning in the Book of Prayer.
5:54.section_title_en: The Inner Conditions of Charity — Section 175 (From The Revival of the Religious Sciences, Book of the Mysteries of Almsgiving)
5:54.anchors:
- Root: قلب (q-l-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "To turn, overturn, transform a thing from one state to another; to rotate, to flip"
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "قلب الشيء: تصريفه وصرفه عن وجه إلى وجه" — the heart is so named because of its constant turning and transformation between states
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "قلب الشيء قلبا: حوله عن وجهه" (to turn a thing from its face). Metaphorical: "رجل قلب حول: يقلب الأمور ويحتال" — one who turns matters over and manages them; "قلبوا لك الأمور" (they turned matters against you)
- Root: وجل (w-j-l)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "Fear, dread, apprehension that strikes the heart"
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الوجل: استشعار الخوف" — the sensing of fear; cited in {«إنما المؤمنون الذين إذا ذكر الله وجلت قلوبهم»}
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "رجل وجل، وقوم وجال" — a fearful man, a fearful people; "وفي قلبه وجل" — in his heart is dread
- Root: عجب (ʿ-j-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "Wonder, amazement; self-admiration, vanity"
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Self-admiration (al-ʿujb) is a destructive spiritual ailment that nullifies deeds
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: wonder at something extraordinary. Metaphorical: self-conceit regarding one's own acts of obedience
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد (Restriction & Focused Predication) — governing the precise limitation of general categories (al-ṣifāt al-khāṣṣah within al-aṣnāf al-thamāniyyah) and the conditional structure of acceptance

5:54.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Duties of Brotherhood'

5:54.arabic: فقال صلى الله عليه وسلم ذلك فضل الله يؤتيه من يشاء (1) وقد استشهد ابن عطاء أيضا لما سئل عن ذلك فقال الغني أفضل لأنه وصف الحق أما دليله الأول ففيه نظر لأن الخبر قد ورد مفصلا تفصيلا يدل على خلاف ذلك وهو أن ثواب الفقير في التسبيح يزيد على ثواب الغني وأن فوزهم بذلك الثواب فضل الله يؤتيه من يشاء فقد روى زيد بن أسلم عن أنس بن مالك رضي الله عنه قال بعث الفقراء رسولا إلا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال إني رسول الفقراء إليك فقال {مرحبا} بك وبمن جئت من عندهم قوم أحبهم قال قالوا يا رسول الله إن
5:54.english: Evidence for this may be found in what is related in the report (khabar) that the poor complained to the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, that the rich had preceded them in good deeds, alms, pilgrimage (ḥajj), and holy struggle (jihād). So he taught them words of glorification (tasbīḥ) and told them that by these they would attain what surpassed what the rich had attained. Then the rich learned these words and began to say them, so the poor returned to the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, and informed him [of this]. He said, peace and blessings be upon him: {«ذلك فضل الله يؤتيه من يشاء»} — "That is the bounty of God; He gives it to whom He wills." (1)
5:54.section_title_en: On the Relative Excellence of Poverty and Wealth — A Detailed Exposition
5:54.anchors:
- Root: فقر (fa-qā-rā)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of neediness, destitution; the state of one lacking provision or means.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Fourfold division — (1) essential need before God (universal to all creatures), (2) lack of acquired possessions, (3) contentment of the soul, (4) metaphorical usage. Here, the operative sense is the second: absence of worldly goods.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah) — absence of wealth; Metaphorical (Majaz) — "فقرة الكلام" (a rhetorical gem/point), showing the root's capacity for extension. The discussion here remains in the literal register of material need.
- Root: غني (ghayn-nūn-yā)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of sufficiency, independence, freedom from need.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Threefold division — (1) absolute freedom from all needs (God alone), (2) fewness of needs (the praised "wealth of the soul"), (3) abundance of possessions. The debate here pivots between senses (2) and (3).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — "أغنى عنه" (to be independent of); Metaphorical — "تغنته القيود" (fetters "enriched" him, i.e., clung to him), showing that attachment, not mere possession, is the real issue.
- Root: صبر (ṣād-bā-rā)
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Restraint of the soul in the face of hardship; steadfastness in obedience and abstinence from sin. The "patient poor" (فقير صابر) is the one who holds fast without anxious striving.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — endurance of affliction; the compound "صابر محتسب" (patient and reckoning on God's reward) is the technical Quranic-Hadith register.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — The Prophet's saying {«ليس الغنى عن كثرة العرض إنما الغنى غنى النفس»} uses "إنما" to restrict true wealth to soul-contentment, negating the apparent sense of abundance. This syntactic restriction governs the entire argument: the "wealth" that matters is a state of the heart, not of the purse.
5:54.topic: Al-Ghazali on constant remembrance of God and contemplative invocations, from 'Poverty and Abstinence'

5:119.arabic: وقال عز وجل {رضي الله عنهم ورضوا عنه ذلك لمن خشي ربه} وكل ما دل على فضيلة العلم دل على فضيلة الخوف لأن الخوف ثمرة العلم ولذلك جاء في خبر موسى عليه أفضل الصلاة والسلام وأما الخائفون
5:119.english: As for the path of derivation (iqtibās) from the verses and reports, what has been transmitted concerning the virtue of fear is beyond enumeration. And sufficient as an indication of its virtue is that God—may He be exalted—has gathered together for the fearful (khāʾifūn) guidance (hudā), mercy (raḥmah), knowledge (ʿilm), and good pleasure (riḍwān)—and these are the sum total of the stations of the people of Paradise. God—may He be exalted—said: {وهدى ورحمة للذين هم لربهم يرهبون} "And guidance and mercy for those who of their Lord are fearful" [Al-Aʿrāf: 154]. And He—exalted is He—said: {إنما يخشى الله من عباده العلماء} "Only those of His servants who possess knowledge fear God" [Fāṭir: 28]—describing them with knowledge on account of their fear [of Him].
5:119.section_title_en: Exposition of the Virtue of Fear (Khawf) and Encouragement Thereof
5:119.anchors:
- Root: خوف (Khawf)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root denotes trepidation, apprehension, and the state of being overtaken by dread of a feared outcome.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الخوف: توقع مكروه عن أمارة مظنونة، أو معلومة" — the anticipation of something detestable based on a probable or certain indication; it is the direct opposite of amn (security) and applies to both worldly and otherworldly matters.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): "خفته على مالي خوفا وخيفة" — fearing for something. Metaphorical (Majaz): "تخوفه: تنقصه" — to diminish gradually, as fear consumes the soul piecemeal.
- Root: فضل (Fadl)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Excess, superiority, or merit beyond the baseline of sufficiency.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الفضل: الزيادة عن الاقتصاد" — increase beyond moderation; the praiseworthy type is like the surplus of knowledge and forbearance, and it is measured by its end (ghāyah).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "مال فلان فاضل: كثير يفضل عن القوت" — surplus wealth exceeding necessity. The virtue of a thing is gauged by its instrumental efficacy toward a noble goal.
- Root: علم (ʿIlm)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Certain cognition and apprehension of a thing as it truly is.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "العلم: إدراك الشيء بحقيقته" — apprehension of a thing's reality; it is the root from which khawf branches as its fruit.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "ما علمت بخبرك: ما شعرت به" — to have cognizance. The scholars (ʿulamāʾ) are so named for their knowledge, which necessarily engenders fear of God.
- Sibawayh Rule: Restriction and Focused Predication (باب الحصر والتقييد) — governing the exclusive attribution in {إنما يخشى الله من عباده العلماء}, where the predicate restricts fear to the knowledgeable, and the syntactic fronting of "whom they fear" (لربهم يرهبون) emphasizes the object of reverential dread.
5:119.topic: Al-Ghazali on the journey of the soul, death, and the Hereafter, from 'Love, Longing, Intimacy and Contentment'

5:119.arabic: آلاف درهم لا أفعل ذلك أبدا رضي الله عنه
5:119.english: The Messiah, peace be upon him, said: "With difficulty shall the rich man enter Paradise."
5:119.section_title_en: The Virtue of Poverty and the Condemnation of Wealth — Section 1071
5:119.anchors:
- Root: دخل (dakhala)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of entering, penetrating, or intruding into a space or state.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Often used for entering into a condition or abode, including the afterlife states of Paradise and Hell.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal for physical entry; metaphorical for entering into a spiritual state or reckoning.
- Root: فقر (faqara)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To hollow out, pierce, or be in a state of neediness; the poor one is "hollowed" of worldly goods.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Denotes the state of one lacking sufficient means; in the Kalam context, it signifies a spiritual station of utter dependence upon God, not merely material lack.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal for material destitution; metaphorical for the soul's essential neediness before its Lord.
- Root: غني (ghaniya)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To be rich, self-sufficient, or free from need.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In theological terms, absolute Ghina (Self-Sufficiency) belongs to God alone; human wealth is a relative accident (ʿaraḍ) that often breeds heedlessness.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal for possessing abundance; metaphorical for the false sense of independence that veils one from God.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Prepositional Interposition (باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور) — Governing the syntactic flow of conditional and circumstantial clauses, ensuring the periodic structure of the narrative remains unbroken across multiple embedded quotations.
5:119.topic: Al-Ghazali on the journey of the soul, death, and the Hereafter, from 'Poverty and Abstinence'

6:125.arabic: ومن يرد أن يضله يجعل صدره ضيقا حرجا كأنما يصعد في السماء إن ينصركم الله فلا غالب لكم وإن يخذلكم فمن ذا الذي ينصركم من بعده فهو الهادي والمضل يفعل ما يشاء ويحكم ما يريد لا راد لحكمه ولا معقب لقضائه خلق الجنة وخلق لها أهلا فاستعملهم بالطاعة وخلق النار وخلق لها أهلا فاستعمله بالمعاصي وعرف الخلق علامة أهل الجنة وأهل النار فقال إن الأبرار لفي نعيم وإن الفجار لفي جحيم ثم قال تعالى فيما روى عن نبيه صلى الله عليه وسلم هؤلاء في الجنة ولا أبالي وهؤلاء في النار ولا أبالي (1) فتعالى الله الملك الحق لا يسئل عما ي
6:125.english: I say: Know that when the Shayṭān prevails and the heart inclines to its own kind among the parties of the Shayṭān, turning away from the party of God—Exalted is He—and His saints, and aiding the party of the Shayṭān and His enemies, then there flows upon its bodily members, by virtue of the prior decree, that which is the cause of its distance from God—Exalted is He. But if the angelic attributes are predominant over the heart, the heart does not lend its ear to the Shayṭān's seduction, nor to his incitement toward the immediate world, nor to his belittling of the matter of the Hereafter. Rather, it inclines to the party of God—Exalted is He—and obedience appears upon its members in accordance with what has preceded in the decree. Thus, the heart of the believer is between two fingers of the fingers of the All-Merciful—that is, between the mutual tugging of these two hosts—and this is the meaning of "turning" (taqlīb): the transition from one party to another. As for perpetual constancy, whether with the party of the angels or with the party of the Shayṭān, that is rare on both sides. These acts of obedience and disobedience emerge from the treasuries of the Unseen into the world of witness by way of the treasury of the heart, for it is among the treasuries of the Malakūt. And when they do emerge, they become signs by which the masters of hearts recognize the prior decree. For whomever is created for Paradise, the means of obedience are made easy for him; and whomever is created for the Fire, the means of disobedience are made easy for him, and evil companions are given sway over him, and the rule of the Shayṭān is cast into his heart. For by various kinds of deceptions he beguiles the foolish, saying: "God is Merciful, so do not care"; and "All people do not fear God, so do not oppose them"; and "Life is long, so be patient until you repent tomorrow." He promises them and fills them with desires—{يَعِدُهُمْ وَيُمَنِّيهِمْ وَمَا يَعِدُهُمُ الشَّيْطَانُ إِلَّا غُرُورًا} "He promises them and fills them with desires, and the Shayṭān promises them nothing but delusion" {النساء/120}. He promises them repentance and fills them with hopes of forgiveness, and thus destroys them, by God's permission, through these ruses and what runs in their course. So he expands their hearts to accept delusion and constricts them from accepting the truth. And all of that is by God's decree and destiny: {فَمَن يُرِدِ اللَّهُ أَن يَهْدِيَهُ يَشْرَحْ صَدْرَهُ لِلْإِسْلَامِ وَمَن يُرِدْ أَن يُضِلَّهُ يَجْعَلْ صَدْرَهُ ضَيِّقًا حَرَجًا كَأَنَّمَا يَصَّعَّدُ فِي السَّمَاءِ} "Whomsoever God wishes to guide, He expands his breast to Islam; and whomsoever He wishes to lead astray, He makes his breast narrow and constricted, as though he were climbing into the sky" {الأنعام/125}. {إِن يَنصُرْكُمُ اللَّهُ فَلَا غَالِبَ لَكُمْ وَإِن يَخْذُلْكُمْ فَمَن ذَا الَّذِي يَنصُرُكُم مِّن بَعْدِهِ} "If God helps you, none can overcome you; and if He forsakes you, who is there to help you after Him?" {آل عمران/160}. He is the Guide and the Misleader; He does what He wills and decrees what He desires. There is no repeller of His judgment and no reverser of His decree. He created Paradise and created for it its people, and employed them in obedience; and He created the Fire and created for it its people, and employed them in disobedience. And He made known to creation the mark of the people of Paradise and the people of the Fire, saying: {إِنَّ الْأَبْرَارَ لَفِي نَعِيمٍ وَإِنَّ الْفُجَّارَ لَفِي جَحِيمٍ} "Verily, the righteous shall be in bliss, and verily, the wicked shall be in the Blazing Fire" {الانفطار/13-14}. Then He—Exalted is He—said, as related from His Prophet, peace be upon him: "These are in Paradise, and I do not care; and these are in the Fire, and I do not care." Exalted is God, the King, the Truth! {لَا يُسْأَلُ عَمَّا يَفْعَلُ وَهُمْ يُسْأَلُونَ} "He is not questioned about what He does, but they shall be questioned" {الأنبياء/23}.
6:125.section_title_en: The Explanation of the Heart's Rapid Fluctuation and the Division of Hearts Between Change and Constancy
6:125.anchors:
- Root: قلب (q-l-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of turning, overturning, and revolving a thing from one face to another; the heart is so named for its constant oscillation.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "قلب الشيء: تصريفه وصرفه عن وجه إلى وجه" — the heart's essence is its perpetual turning and redirection; its fluctuation is not accidental but constitutive of its nature.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): physical overturning. Metaphorical (Majaz): "رجل قلب حول: يقلب الأمور ويحتال" — the heart's movement between the two hosts (jundān) is a real, dynamic turnover of allegiance.
- Root: شيط (sh-y-t)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Burning, scorching, or spoiling meat by over-smoking; blood going to waste.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The Shayṭān is so named for his being burned and banished from mercy.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Metaphorical: "شاط دمه إذا بطل" — the Shayṭān's work is to render the servant's spiritual life wasted and nullified, as blood spilled in vain.
- Root: حزب (ḥ-z-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: A group or party with cohesion and strength; al-Ḥayzabūn (the old woman) shows the root's extension to a gathered mass.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الحزب: جماعة فيها غلظ" — the party of God (ḥizb Allāh) versus the party of the Shayṭān (ḥizb al-Shayṭān) are two opposing, organized camps in cosmic conflict.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: a band of partisans. Metaphorical: "قرأ حزبه من القرآن" — a portion assigned; here, the heart is assigned to one of the two parties by divine decree.
- Root: خلق (kh-l-q)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Measuring and smoothing; creating as precise estimation.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الخلق أصله: التقدير المستقيم" — creation is origination upon a just measure; God's creative act entails the pre-ordainment of ends.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: shaping leather before cutting. Metaphorical: "خلق الله الخلق: أوجده على تقدير أوجبته الحكمة" — God's creation of Paradise and Hellfire and their inhabitants is an act of wise, pre-eternal determination.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — The phrase "إنما ذكرنا منه ما يحتاج إليه" restricts the author's purpose: only the necessary measure of the heart's wonders is expounded, not exhaustive treatment, signaling a deliberate boundary of the science of practical religion (ʿilm al-muʿāmalah).

6:125.arabic: الذين أراد الله أن يهديهم فشرح صدورهم للإسلام والهدى والمغترون هم الذين أراد الله أن يضلهم فجعل صدرهم ضيقا حرجا كأنما يصعد في السماء والمغرور هو الذي لم تنفتح بصيرته ليكون بهداية نفسه كفيلا وبقي في العمى فاتخذ الهوى قائدا والشيطان دليلا {ومن كان في هذه أعمى فهو في الآخرة أعمى وأضل سبيلا} وإذا عرف أن الغرور 2 هو أم الشقاوات ومنبع المهلكات فلا بد من شرح مداخله ومجاريه وتفصيل ما يكثر من وقوع الغرور فيه ليحذره المريد بعد معرفته فيتقيه فالموفق من العباد من عرف مد
6:125.english: Thus the shrewd ones (akyās) and the possessors of inner sight (arbāb al-baṣā'ir) — their hearts are like a niche (mishkāh) in which is a lamp (miṣbāḥ), the lamp in a glass, the glass as though it were a pearly star, kindled from a blessed olive tree, neither of the east nor of the west, whose oil would almost glow even if no fire touched it — light upon light (nūrun 'alā nūr). But the self-deceived (maghrūrūn) — their hearts are {«كَظُلُمَاتٍ فِي بَحْرٍ لُجِّيٍّ يَغْشَاهُ مَوْجٌ مِنْ فَوْقِهِ مَوْجٌ مِنْ فَوْقِهِ سَحَابٌ ظُلُمَاتٌ بَعْضُهَا فَوْقَ بَعْضٍ إِذَا أَخْرَجَ يَدَهُ لَمْ يَكَدْ يَرَاهَا وَمَنْ لَمْ يَجْعَلِ اللَّهُ لَهُ نُورًا فَمَا لَهُ مِنْ نُورٍ»} (Q. 24:40) — like darknesses in a vast deep sea, covered by a wave, above which is another wave, above which is a cloud — darknesses, one above another; when he stretches out his hand, he can scarcely see it. And he to whom God grants no light, for him there is no light.
6:125.section_title_en: The Book of Censure of Self-Deception (Kitāb Dhamm al-Ghurūr) — Book Ten of the Quarter of the Destroyers from The Revival of the Religious Sciences
6:125.anchors:
- Root: غرر (gh-r-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core sense of an overlooked flaw, a heedless state, or a deceptive glitter; the "white blaze" on a horse's forehead that draws the eye but conceals the animal's true nature.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Ghurūr" is a heedlessness (ghaflah) in wakefulness, rooted in the pursuit of a perceived gain (ghurrah) that is in fact a loss; it is the state of being deluded by the apparent good while the inner reality is ruinous, as in {«مَا غَرَّكَ بِرَبِّكَ الْكَرِيمِ»} (Q. 82:6).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): to approach someone off-guard (ghirrah). Metaphorical (majāz): the "white-blazed day" (yawm agharr) of intense heat — a dazzling surface that misleads; the deluded man is like a gazelle that grazes in moonlight, deceived into thinking it is daylight, until the predator seizes it.
- Root: نور (n-w-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Light that renders things visible; the first thing created by God to dispel darkness.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Two kinds: sensory light (perceived by the eye) and intellectual/divine light (perceived by the inner eye of insight, baṣīrah) — the latter being the light of reason and of the Qur'an, as in {«قَدْ جَاءَكُمْ مِنَ اللَّهِ نُورٌ وَكِتَابٌ مُبِينٌ»} (Q. 5:15).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: illumination of a lamp or fire. Metaphorical: clarification and manifestation — "nawwara al-amr" (he made the matter clear); the light of guidance is that which makes the path of salvation evident to the heart.
- Root: صدر (ṣ-d-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The chest, the seat of the heart; also the "foremost" part of anything.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Literally the bodily chest; metaphorically extended to the "front" of a thing (ṣadr al-majlis, the head of the assembly). When used of the heart's expansion (sharḥ al-ṣadr), it denotes the spiritual opening of the breast to receive divine light and guidance, as in {«رَبِّ اشْرَحْ لِي صَدْرِي»} (Q. 20:25).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: to return from water (ṣadara). Metaphorical: the beginning or origin of an affair — "akhadha al-amra bi-ṣadrihi" (he took the matter from its very outset); the "sources and returns" (mawārid wa maṣādir) of all things.
- Root: ربع (r-b-')
  * Lisan / Ayn: Four; the fourth part; a place of dwelling and spring pasturage.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The root of "four" and its derivatives; used for the four categories or classes into which a thing is divided.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: to dwell (raba'a bi-l-makān). Metaphorical: to raise and restore (rabba'ahu Allāh — God raised him up); here, the "Quarter of the Destroyers" (rub' al-muhlikāt) is the fourth part of the Iḥyā' devoted to the vices that ruin the soul.
- Sibawayh Rule: Interposition of the Prepositional Phrase (bāb al-faṣl bayna al-jār wa al-majrūr) — The periodic sentence structure in the opening doxology ("الحمد لله الذي بيده مقاليد الأمور") places the prepositional phrase "bi-yadihi" (in His hand) before its governing noun to achieve rhetorical emphasis (takhṣīṣ) and to signal the theological priority of divine agency over all affairs.
6:125.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Condemnation of Delusion'

6:125.arabic: الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قوله تعالى فمن يرد الله أن يهديه يشرح صدره للإسلام فقيل له ما هذا الشرح فقال إن النور إذا قذف في القلب انشرح له الصدر وانفسح قيل فهل لذلك من علامة قال صلى الله عليه وسلم نعم التجافي عن دار الغرور والإنابة إلى دار الخلود والاستعداد للموت قبل نزوله (2) ومنها أن يكون أكثر بحثه عن علم الأعمال وعما يفسدها ويشوش القلوب ويهيج الوسواس ويثير الشر فإن أصل الدين التوقي من الشر ولذلك قيل عرفت الشر لا للشر لكن لتوقيه .
6:125.english: As for the fear (al-khashyah), it is from His saying, the Exalted: {«إِنَّمَا يَخْشَى اللَّهَ مِنْ عِبَادِهِ الْعُلَمَاءُ»} — "Only those of His servants who possess knowledge fear Allah" (Fāṭir 35:28). For khashyah is a fear suffused with veneration, and it arises only from knowledge of the Mighty and Majestic — for whoever knows Him fears Him, and whoever does not know Him does not fear Him.
6:125.section_title_en: The Book of God's Book — Fear, Humility, and the Preference for the Hereafter
6:125.anchors:
- Root: خشع (Khasha'a)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of lowliness, submissiveness, and being lowered to the ground.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الخشوع: الضراعة" — Khushū' is a state of supplication and humility; most often used for what appears on the limbs, while ḍarā'ah is for the heart. When the heart humbles, the limbs follow.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): "خشع له وتخشع: ذل وتطامن" — to be lowly and submissive. Metaphorical (Majaz): "أرض خاشعة" — a land that is low-lying; "خشعت الأصوات" — voices lowered in awe.
- Root: خشي (Khashiya)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Fear mixed with awe and reverence.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الخشية: خوف يشوبه تعظيم" — Khashyah is fear suffused with veneration, and it most often arises from knowledge of what is feared.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Distinguished from mere fear (khawf) by its component of reverential awe.
- Root: خلق (Khuluq)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Inherent disposition, character, nature.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الخلق أصله: التقدير المستقيم" — Its root is right measure and proportion; used for the creation of things and for the moral constitution of the soul.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "خلق الخراز الأديم" — the leather-worker cutting and measuring hide before cutting. Metaphorical: "خلق الله الخلق" — God originated creation upon a measure required by wisdom; "وله خلق حسن" — he has beautiful character.
- Root: زهد (Zuhd)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Abstinence, renunciation, disinclination.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الزاهد في الشيء: الراغب عنه والراضي منه بالزهيد" — The ascetic is one who turns away from a thing and is content with little of it.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "زهد في الشيء: رغب عنه" — to turn away from something. Metaphorical: "واد زهيد" — a valley that takes little water; "رجل زهيد" — a man of little good.
- Sibawayh Rule: Restriction and Focused Predication (باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما) — The particle "innamā" restricts the predicate to the subject alone, establishing a definitive causal linkage between knowledge and reverential fear.
6:125.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Poverty and Abstinence'

9:34.arabic: المقصرين فيها فقال {والذين يكنزون الذهب والفضة ولا ينفقونها في سبيل الله فبشرهم بعذاب أليم} ومعنى الإنفاق في سبيل الله إخراج حق الزكاة قال الأحنف بن قيس كنت في نفر من قريش فمر أبو ذر فقال بشر الكانزين بكي في ظهورهم يخرج من جنوبهم وبكي في أقفائهم يخرج من جباههم وفي رواية أنه يوضع على حلمة ثدي أحدهم فيخرج من نغض كتفيه ويوضع على نغض كتفيه حتى يخرج من حلمة ثدييه يتزلزل وقال أبو ذر انتهيت إلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وهو جالس في ظل الكعبة فلما رآني قال هم الأخسرون ورب الكعبة فقلت ومن هم قال الأكثرون أموال
9:34.english: To proceed: God Most High made alms (al-zakāh) one of the pillars of Islam, and joined its mention with prayer (al-ṣalāh), which is the loftiest of symbols. He said Most High: {«وَأَقِيمُوا الصَّلَاةَ وَآتُوا الزَّكَاةَ»} — "And establish prayer and give alms." And he, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Islam is built upon five: the testimony that there is no god but God and that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger, the establishment of prayer, and the giving of alms." And He intensified the threat against those who fall short in it, saying: {«وَالَّذِينَ يَكْنِزُونَ الذَّهَبَ وَالْفِضَّةَ وَلَا يُنفِقُونَهَا فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ فَبَشِّرْهُم بِعَذَابٍ أَلِيمٍ»} — "And those who hoard gold and silver and do not spend them in the way of God — give them tidings of a painful chastisement." And the meaning of "spending in the way of God" is the payment of the due right of alms (zakāh).
9:34.section_title_en: The Book of the Secrets of Alms (Zakat) — Section 167
9:34.anchors:
- Root: زكا (Z-K-Y)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "Zakā al-zar'u yazkū zakā'an: it increased and grew." Core meaning: growth, increase, purification.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "The origin of zakāh is the growth that occurs through the blessing of God Most High... and from it is zakāh: what a person pays of God's right to the poor, so named for the hope of blessing in it, or for the purification (tazkiyah) of the soul, i.e., its growth."
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (haqīqah): growth and increase. Metaphorical (majāz): the purification of wealth through payment of the obligatory due.
- Root: نعم (N-'-M)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "Na'ima 'ayshuhu: his life was pleasant." Core meaning: bounty, well-being, grace.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Al-Ni'mah: the good state... and al-Ni'mah (with kasrah) is used for the genus, said of both little and much."
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "Jallat ni'mat Allāh wa na'mā'uh" — God's grace and bounty are immense. Metaphorical: "Khāfat na'āmatuhum" — their ostriches departed (i.e., they fled), showing the root's extended usage.
- Root: ظهر (Z-H-R)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "Zahara: to become apparent, to be victorious." Core meaning: back, outward appearance, manifestation.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Al-Zahr: the back (body part)... and it is used metaphorically for the surface of the earth."
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "Rajul muzhir: a man strong of back." Metaphorical: "Qalabtu al-amra zahrān li-baṭn" — I turned the matter over back and belly (examined it thoroughly).
- Root: سرر (S-R-R)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "Sarra: to conceal, to keep secret." Core meaning: secret, inner self, joy.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Al-Isrār: the opposite of al-i'lān (declaring)... and al-sirr is the speech concealed in the soul."
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "Asarra al-ḥadīth: he concealed the speech." Metaphorical: "Aṭaytuka sirrah: I gave you its choicest part (the secret/core of something)."
- Sibawayh Rule: Bāb al-faṣl bayna al-jār wa al-majrūr (Prepositional Interposition) — The permissibility of interposing elements between a preposition and its object when the intervening clause is complete in itself, as in "fa'āfa 'alayhim min ni'matihi mā..." where the prepositional phrase is completed after an intervening relative clause.
9:34.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications, prayers, and their spiritual power, from 'Poverty and Abstinence'

9:34.arabic: وقد قال الله تعالى يا أيها الذين آمنوا أنفقوا من طيبات ما كسبتم ومما أخرجنا لكم من الأرض ولا تيمموا الخبيث منه تنفقون ولستم بآخذيه إلا أن تغمضوا فيه أي لا تأخذوه إلا مع كراهية وحياء وهو معنى الإغماض فلا تؤثروا به ربكم وفي الخبر سبق درهم مائة ألف درهم (3) وذلك بأن يخرجه الإنسان وهو من أحل ماله وأجوده فيصدر ذلك عن الرضا والفرح بالبذل وقد يخرج مائة ألف درهم مما يكره من ماله فيدل ذلك على أنه ليس يؤثر الله عز وجل بشيء مما يحبه وبذلك ذم الله تعالى قوما جعلوا لله ما يكرهون فقال تعال
9:34.english: The heart is not treated save with the compound electuary (maʿjūn) of knowledge and works. And this condition among the conditions of almsgiving runs in the same course as humility (al-khushūʿ) runs in the prayer. This is established by his saying — may Allah bless him and grant him peace: "A man has nothing of his prayer save that of which he was conscious." And this is like his saying — may Allah bless him and grant him peace: "Allah does not accept the charity of the one who bestows it with reproach (al-mannān)." And like His saying — Exalted is He: {«لا تبطلوا صدقاتكم بالمن والأذى»} ("Do not nullify your charities by reproach and injury"). As for the legal opinion (fatwā) of the jurist that the alms fall in their proper place and that one's liability is discharged without this condition — that is another discussion, and we have already pointed to its meaning in the Book of Prayer.
9:34.section_title_en: The Inner Conditions of Charity — Section 175 (From The Revival of the Religious Sciences, Book of the Mysteries of Almsgiving)
9:34.anchors:
- Root: قلب (q-l-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "To turn, overturn, transform a thing from one state to another; to rotate, to flip"
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "قلب الشيء: تصريفه وصرفه عن وجه إلى وجه" — the heart is so named because of its constant turning and transformation between states
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "قلب الشيء قلبا: حوله عن وجهه" (to turn a thing from its face). Metaphorical: "رجل قلب حول: يقلب الأمور ويحتال" — one who turns matters over and manages them; "قلبوا لك الأمور" (they turned matters against you)
- Root: وجل (w-j-l)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "Fear, dread, apprehension that strikes the heart"
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الوجل: استشعار الخوف" — the sensing of fear; cited in {«إنما المؤمنون الذين إذا ذكر الله وجلت قلوبهم»}
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "رجل وجل، وقوم وجال" — a fearful man, a fearful people; "وفي قلبه وجل" — in his heart is dread
- Root: عجب (ʿ-j-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "Wonder, amazement; self-admiration, vanity"
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Self-admiration (al-ʿujb) is a destructive spiritual ailment that nullifies deeds
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: wonder at something extraordinary. Metaphorical: self-conceit regarding one's own acts of obedience
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد (Restriction & Focused Predication) — governing the precise limitation of general categories (al-ṣifāt al-khāṣṣah within al-aṣnāf al-thamāniyyah) and the conditional structure of acceptance

9:34.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Duties of Brotherhood'

9:34.arabic: وأما هؤلاء فإنهم يصدون عن سبيل الله ويجرون الخلق إلى الغرور بالله بلفظ الرجاء فيزيدهم كلامهم جراءة على المعاصي ورغبة في الدنيا لا سيما إذا كان الواعظ متزينا بالثياب والخيل والمراكب فإنه تشهد هيئته من فرقه إلى قدمه بشدة حرصه على الدنيا فما يفسده هذا المغرور أكثر مما يصلحه بل لا يصلح أصلا ويضل خلقا كثيرا ولا يخفى وجه كونه مغرورا وفرقة أخرى منهم قنعوا بحفظ كلام الزهاد وأحاديثهم في ذم الدنيا فهم يحفظون الكلمات على وجهها ويؤدونها من غير إحاطة بمعانيها فبعضهم يفعل ذلك على المنابر وبعضهم
9:34.english: But as for these [deluded ones], they turn others away from the path of God and drag creation into self-deception concerning God (al-ghurūr billāh) by means of the word "hope" (al-rajāʾ). Thus their speech increases them in audacity toward sins and desire for this world — especially when the preacher is adorned with fine garments, horses, and mounts, for his very appearance bears witness from his hair to his feet to his intense greed for this world. So what this deluded one corrupts is more than what he reforms — nay, he reforms nothing at all, and he leads many people astray. Nor is the aspect of his being deluded hidden.
9:34.section_title_en: The Categories of the Deluded Among Preachers and Hadith Transmitters
9:34.anchors:
- Root: أ-ص-ل (ʾ-ṣ-l)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of foundation, root, and origin; to set right what is corrupt.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): اصلاح (iṣlāḥ) as the act of bringing something from a state of corruption (fasād) to soundness (ṣalāḥ), whether in belief, action, or speech.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) usage denotes rectifying a physical object; metaphorical (majāz) usage applies to moral and spiritual correction of others.
- Root: غ-ر-ر (gh-r-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: غرور (ghurūr) — deception, delusion, vanity; from غرّ (gharra), to be heedless or deceived by appearances.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): الغرور (al-ghurūr) is the delusion that leads one to rely on false hopes, particularly regarding God's mercy while persisting in sin; the state of one who is deceived by Satan or by his own vain fancies.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: a thing that deceives by its outward show; Metaphorical: the soul's self-deception through false reliance on divine forgiveness without repentance.
- Root: س-م-ع (s-m-ʿ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: السمع (al-samʿ) — hearing; the auditory faculty and its act.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Hearing as the means of acquiring transmitted knowledge (samāʿ); in hadith terminology, the formal act of hearing a tradition from a shaykh, which is the first stage of transmission.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the physical act of hearing; Metaphorical: attentive listening with the heart, as in "ألقى السمع وهو شهيد" {«وَأَلْقَى السَّمْعَ وَهُوَ شَهِيدٌ»} [Q. 50:37] — one who listens with full presence of mind.
- Root: ح-ف-ظ (ḥ-f-ẓ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: الحفظ (al-ḥifẓ) — preservation, guarding, memorization; keeping something safe from loss or alteration.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): الحفظ is the faculty of the soul by which what is understood is retained; its opposite is forgetfulness (nisyān). It also denotes vigilant care and protection.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: guarding a physical object; Metaphorical: committing knowledge to memory such that it is preserved from distortion.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The rule governing the separation of a preposition from its object by intervening clauses, as in the periodic structure "فإذا لم تحفظ لا بالقلب ولا بالكتاب وجرى على سمعك صوت غفل" where the conditional clause (فإذا) governs a sequence of coordinated conditions, each requiring its own apodosis, demonstrating the classical pattern of layered conditional sentences.
9:34.topic: Al-Ghazali on purifying the character, moral diseases, and spiritual remedies, from 'Condemnation of Delusion'

10:7.arabic: فقد أخبر الله عنهم إذ قال تعالى ورضوا بالحياة الدنيا واطمأنوا بها والذين هم عن آياتنا غافلون وقال عز وجل ولا تطع من أغفلنا قلبه عن ذكرنا واتبع هواه وكان أمره فرطا وقال تعالى فأعرض عمن تولى عن ذكرنا ولم يرد إلا الحياة الدنيا ذلك مبلغهم من العلم فأحال ذلك كله على الغفلة وعدم العلم ولذلك قال رجل لعيسى عليه السلام احملني معك في سياحتك فقال أخرج مالك والحقني فقال لا أستطيع فقال عيسى عليه السلام بعجب يدخل الغني الجنة أو قال بشدة وقال بعضهم ما من يوم ذر شارقه إلا وأربعة أملاك ينادون في الآفاق بأربعة أصوات ملكان بالمشرق وملكان بالمغرب يقول أحدهم ب
10:7.english: When it was unveiled to the friends of God (awliyā') — exalted is He — that the servant destroys his own soul by his deeds and his following of his soul's caprice, even as the silkworm destroys itself, they rejected this world (al-dunyā) entirely. Thus al-Hasan said: "I saw seventy of the Badr veterans who were more ascetic (azhad) among what God made lawful for them than you are among what God made unlawful for you." In another wording: "They were more joyful in affliction than you are in comfort and ease. Had you seen them, you would have said: 'They are mad.' And had they seen your righteous ones, they would have said: 'These have no share of goodness.' And had they seen your wicked ones, they would have said: 'These do not believe in the Day of Reckoning.'"
10:7.section_title_en: The Exposition of the Signs of Asceticism (Zuhd)
10:7.anchors:
- Root: زهد (Z-H-D)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root meaning: scarcity, paucity, and abstention; al-zuhd is also "estimation" (al-hazr), as in estimating a palm-crop.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الزهيد: الشيء القليل" — the ascetic (al-zāhid) is one who turns away from a thing, content with the little (al-qalīl) of it. Theological nuance: zuhd is not mere abandonment but a reorientation of desire away from the worldly toward the divine.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Haqiqah (literal): "زهد في الشيء: رغب عنه" — to turn one's desire away from a thing. Majaz (metaphorical): "رجل زهيد: قليل الخير" — a man of little good; "اد زهيد" — a valley that takes little water. Thus, zuhd as a spiritual state is a metaphorical extension of scarcity applied to the heart's attachment.
- Root: قلب (Q-L-B)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The heart (al-qalb); also "turning/transforming a thing from one face to another" (taṣrīf al-shay').
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "قلب الشيء: تصريفه وصرفه عن وجه إلى وجه" — the heart is so named for its constant turning and fluctuation between states; theological nuance: the heart is the seat of volitional orientation, capable of being turned toward or away from God.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Haqiqah: physical overturning. Majaz: "رجل قلب حول: يقلب الأمور ويحتال" — a man who turns matters over and manages them; thus "corruption of the heart" (fasād al-qalb) is a metaphorical overturning of its proper orientation.
- Root: أنس (A-N-S)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Sociability, familiarity, intimacy; al-uns is the opposite of loneliness (al-wahshah).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The soul's tranquility and familiarity with something; theological nuance: al-uns bi-Allāh is the heart's intimate repose in God, exclusive of all else.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Haqiqah: human companionship. Majaz: intimacy with God as the heart's true companionship, displacing worldly attachment.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — The phrase "إنما مسرة أحدهم معرفة الناس حاله" restricts delight solely to public recognition, isolating the motive that invalidates claimed zuhd.
10:7.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Poverty and Abstinence'

10:7.arabic: قال تعالى {إن الذين لا يرجون لقاءنا ورضوا بالحياة الدنيا واطمأنوا بها} الآية وقال تعالى {يعلمون ظاهرا من الحياة الدنيا وهم عن الآخرة هم غافلون} وقال عز وجل فأعرض عمن تولى عن ذكرنا ولم يرد إلا الحياة الدنيا ذلك مبلغهم من العلم فالجمع بين كمال الاستبصار في مصالح الدنيا والدين لا يكاد يتيسر إلا لمن رسخه الله لتدبير عباده في معاشهم ومعادهم وهم الأنبياء المؤيدون بروح القدس المستمدون من القوة الإلهية التي تتسع لجميع الأمور ولا تضيق عنها فأما قلوب سائر الخلق فإنها إذا استقلت بأمر الدنيا انصرفت عن الآخرة وقصرت عن الاستك
10:7.english: They left [the vessels] upon the road — why do you not return them to their places? So they said to him: "Those vessels are in their places; rather, it is you who cannot find the way, due to your blindness. The wonder of you is that you do not attribute your stumbling to your blindness, but rather attribute it to the shortcoming of another." Such is the relation of the religious sciences to the rational sciences.
10:7.section_title_en: The Heart's Relation to the Divisions of the Rational, Religious, Worldly, and Otherworldly Sciences
10:7.anchors:
- Root: عقل (ʿaql)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The faculty prepared for the reception of knowledge; also the knowledge acquired by that faculty.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "العقل يقال للقوة المتهيئة لقبول العلم، ويقال للعلم الذي يستفيده الإنسان بتلك القوة عقل" — the intellect is the power prepared to receive knowledge, and the knowledge one acquires by that power is also called ʿaql.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "ما لفلان مقول، ولا معقول" — one who has neither speech nor understanding. Metaphorical: "نخلة لا تعقل الإبار" — a palm that does not accept pollination, i.e., does not take it in.
- Root: قلب (qalb)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The heart; that which is ever-turning and fluctuating.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "قلب الشيء: تصريفه وصرفه عن وجه إلى وجه" — the turning of a thing from one state to another; the heart is so named for its constant turning of resolutions and states.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "قلب الشيء قلبا: حوله عن وجهه" — to turn a thing from its face. Metaphorical: "رجل قلب حول: يقلب الأمور ويحتال" — a man who turns matters over and devises stratagems.
- Root: دنا (danā)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Nearness in place, time, or rank.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الدنو: القرب بالذات، أو بالحكم" — nearness by essence or by judgment; the worldly life (al-dunyā) is so named for its nearness and precedence.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "هو دنيء من الأدنياء" — base and contemptible; the dunyā is that which is lower and nearer.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — used to restrict the predicate exclusively to the subject, as in the Prophetic statement restricting the majority of Paradise's inhabitants to the "bullah" (those seemingly foolish in worldly matters).
10:7.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Love, Longing, Intimacy and Contentment'

12:8.arabic: حسد إخوة يوسف عليه السلام وعبر عما في قلوبهم بقوله تعالى {إذ قالوا ليوسف وأخوه أحب إلى أبينا منا ونحن عصبة إن أبانا لفي ضلال مبين اقتلوا يوسف أو اطرحوه أرضا يخل لكم وجه أبيكم} فلما كرهوا حب أبيهم له وساءهم ذلك وأحبوا زواله عنه غيبوه عنه وقال تعالى {ولا يجدون في صدورهم حاجة مما أوتوا} أي لا تضيق صدورهم به ولا يغتمون فأثنى عليهم بعدم الحسد وقال تعالى في معرض الإنكار {أم يحسدون الناس على ما آتاهم الله من فضله} وقال تعالى {كان الناس أمة واحدة} إلى قوله {إلا الذين أوتوه من بعد ما جاءتهم البينات بغيا بينهم} قيل في التفسير حسدا وقال تعالى {وما تفرقوا إل
12:8.english: The Prophet ﷺ said: «إن المؤمن يغبط والمنافق يحسد» — "The believer aspires emulously, and the hypocrite envies."
12:8.section_title_en: On the Reality of Envy (Ḥasad) and Its Degrees — Section 720
12:8.anchors:
- Root: نعم (n-ʿ-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root meaning of "bounty, benefaction, grace" — that state of goodness and well-being bestowed.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "النعمة: الحالة الحسنة" — bounty is the excellent state/condition; it is the genus term applying to both little and much, as in {«وإن تعدوا نعمة الله لا تحصوها»} [Ibrahim: 34].
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): "جلت نعمة الله ونعماؤه" — bounty as actual bestowed good. Metaphorical (majāz): "خفت نعامتهم" — departure/removal, relevant to the envier's wish for the bounty's removal.
- Root: حسد (ḥ-s-d)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Envy — the desire for removal of another's good.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الحسد: تمني زوال نعمة من مستحق لها" — envy is wishing the removal of bounty from one who deserves it, sometimes accompanied by striving to effect its removal. Cited: «المؤمن يغبط والمنافق يحسد».
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "حسده على نعمة الله" — envying someone for God's bounty. "إن الحسد يأكل الجسد" — envy consumes the body.
- Root: نفس (n-f-s)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The self; also value, preciousness.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): النفس: الروح — the soul/spirit; also الذات (essence/self).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "شيء نفيس ومنفس" — a precious thing. Metaphorical: "دفق نفسه أي دمه" — poured out his self, i.e., his blood. From this root derives المنافسة (emulative competition) — the striving for precious things.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد (Restriction & Specification) — The definition of ḥasad is given as a restricted predication (ḥadd), delimiting its essential meaning: "كراهة النعمة وحب زوالها عن المنعم عليه" — the hatred of bounty and love of its removal from the one upon whom it is bestowed. This is a formal definition (ḥadd), not merely a lexical gloss.
12:8.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'Poverty and Abstinence'

12:20.arabic: وبالإضافة إلى العوض عنه رغبة فيه وحبا ولذلك قال الله تعالى وشروه بثمن بخس دراهم معدودة وكانوا فيه من الزاهدين معناه باعوه فقد يطلق الشراء بمعنى البيع ووصف أخوة يوسف بالزهد فيه إذ طمعوا أن يخلو لهم وجه أبيهم وكان ذلك عندهم أحب إليهم من يوسف فباعوه طمعا في العوض فإذن كل من باع الدنيا بالآخرة فهو زاهد في الدنيا وكل من باع الآخرة بالدنيا فهو أيضا زاهد ولكن في الآخرة ولكن العادة جارية بتخصيص اسم الزهد بمن يزهد في الدنيا كما خصص اسم الإلحاد بمن يميل إلى الباطل خاصة وإن كان هو للميل في وضع اللسان ولما كان الزهد رغبة عن محبوب بالجملة لم يتصور إلا بالعدول إلى شيء هو
12:20.english: Know that asceticism in this world (al-zuhd fī al-dunyā) is a noble station (maqām sharīf) among the stations of the wayfarers (al-sālikīn). This station is composed of knowledge (ʿilm), a state (ḥāl), and action (ʿamal), just like all other stations — for all the gates of faith, as the predecessors (al-salaf) said, reduce to a creedal affirmation (ʿaqd), a utterance (qawl), and an action (ʿamal). It is as though utterance, due to its outward manifestation, was made to stand in the place of the state (ḥāl), since through it the inner state becomes manifest. Otherwise, utterance is not intended for its own sake; if it does not issue from a state, it is called "submission" (islām) and is not called "faith" (īmān). Knowledge is the cause that produces the state, running in the manner of a fruit-bearing tree, while action runs from the state in the manner of the fruit itself. So let us mention the state together with both of its two extremities — knowledge and action.
12:20.section_title_en: On Asceticism (Al-Zuhd) — Its Reality, Conditions, and Degrees
12:20.anchors:
- Root: زهد (Z-H-D)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: scarcity, smallness, and abstemiousness; also estimation (kharṣ) of fruit.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الزهيد: الشيء القليل، والزاهد في الشيء: الراغب عنه والراضي منه بالزهيد" — the ascetic is one who turns away from a thing, content with little instead of it.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): "زهد في الشيء: رغب عنه" (to turn one's desire away from something). Metaphorical (Majaz): "رجل زهيد: قليل الخير" — applied to one of little worth; "واد زهيد" — a valley that takes little water. The term is conventionally restricted to renouncing the permissible (mubāḥāt), not the forbidden.
- Root: رغب (R-GH-B)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Root denotes spaciousness and amplitude; "رغب الشيء: اتسع" (the thing became wide).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "أصل الرغبة: السعة في الشيء... والرغبة والرغب والرغبى: السعة في الإرادة" — desire is an expansion of the will toward something; "رغب عنه" implies turning desire away (the very definition of zuhd).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "هو راغب فيه وراغب عنه" — one can be desirous of a thing or averse to it. Metaphorical: "واد رغيب: كثير الأخذ للماء" — a valley that takes much water, contrasting with "واد زهيد" (one that takes little). Thus, zuhd and raghbah are relative terms defined by their objects.
- Root: دنا (D-N-W)
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الدنو: القرب بالذات، أو بالحكم" — nearness in essence or by judgment; used for place, time, and rank. The "nearer" (adnā) life is the worldly life, contrasted with the "farther" (ākhirah), which is superior and more enduring.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — The term "zāhid" (ascetic) is not applied absolutely but is restricted by convention (istiṣlāḥ) to specific objects of renunciation (worldly goods), just as "mulḥid" (heretic) is restricted to one who inclines to falsehood, though the root meaning is broader. This governs the author's analysis of how names are conventionally specified.
12:20.topic: Al-Ghazali on purifying the character, moral diseases, and spiritual remedies, from 'Poverty and Abstinence'

12:24.arabic: وهم بها لولا أن رأى برهان ربه} وعنه أيضا ما هو أعجب من هذا وذلك أنه خرج من المدينة حاجا ومعه رفيق له حتى نزلا بالأبواء فقام رفيقه وأخذ السفرة وانطلق إلى السوق ليبتاع شيئا وجلس سليمان في الخيمة وكان من أجمل الناس وجها وأورعهم فبصرت به أعرابية من قلة الجبل وانحدرت إليه حتى وقفت بين يديه وعليها البرقع والقفازان فأسفرت عن وجه لها كأنه فلقة قمر وقالت أهنئني فظن أنها تريد طعاما فقام إلى فضلة السفرة ليعطيها فقالت لست أريد هذا إنما أريد ما يكون من الرجل إلى أهله فقال جهزك إلى إبليس
12:24.english: ...which one is ashamed of and fears to plunge into. And the abstention of most people from its requirements is either due to incapacity, or fear, or shame, or concern for preserving one's body — and in none of these is there any reward, for that is merely preferring one share of one's worldly desires over another share. Yes — from divine protection (al-ʿiṣmah) is that one is not able [to sin]; so in these obstacles there is a benefit, namely the repulsion of sin. For whoever abandons fornication, its sin is repelled from him by whatever cause his abandonment occurred. Rather, the virtue and abundant reward lie in abandoning it out of fear of God — may He be exalted — while possessing the ability, with the removal of obstacles, the facilitation of means, and especially at the height of genuine desire. And this is the station of the veracious (al-ṣiddīqīn). For this reason, the Prophet — peace be upon him — said: "Whoever loves passionately, then remains chaste, then conceals [his love], then dies — he dies a martyr."(1)
12:24.section_title_en: The Book of Breaking the Two Desires — Section 654: On Chastity, Guarding the Gaze, and the Virtue of Restraining Desire
12:24.anchors:
- **Root: ع ف ف** (ʿaffa)
  * **Lisan / Ayn**: Core meaning of abstaining from what is unlawful, refraining, and remaining chaste; al-ʿafāf is the state of one who abstains from forbidden things.
  * **Al-Raghib (Mufradat)**: Theological nuance — ʿiffah (chastity) is a virtue of the soul that restrains the appetitive faculty from pursuing what is not permissible; it is a station of the ṣiddīqūn (veracious ones).
  * **Al-Zamakhshari (Asas)**: Literal (ḥaqīqah) — physical abstention from unlawful acts; Metaphorical (majāz) — the heart's abstention from coveting what God has forbidden, which is the higher reality of chastity.

- **Root: غ ب ق** (ghabaqa)
  * **Lisan / Ayn**: The evening drink (al-ghabūq) — the milking or drink given at nightfall; contrasted with al-ṣabūḥ (the morning drink).
  * **Al-Raghib (Mufradat)**: In the hadith of the three men in the cave, the term marks the temporal precision of filial devotion — serving parents before any other claim, even at the boundary of night.
  * **Al-Zamakhshari (Asas)**: Literal — the evening milking; the narrative use in the hadith is literal, denoting the exact act of service delayed out of reverence.

- **Root: ه م م** (hamma)
  * **Lisan / Ayn**: To intend, to resolve upon a matter; al-hamm is the initial stirring of intention before full determination.
  * **Al-Raghib (Mufradat)**: In Q. 12:24 {«وَلَقَدْ هَمَّتْ بِهِ وَهَمَّ بِهَا لَوْلَا أَنْ رَأَى بُرْهَانَ رَبِّهِ»} — "And certainly she desired him, and he would have desired her, had it not been that he saw the proof of his Lord" — the term distinguishes between a passing inclination (hamm) and a settled resolve; Yūsuf's hamm was repelled by divine proof, while Zulaykhā's was consummated in action.
  * **Al-Zamakhshari (Asas)**: Literal — the inward movement of intention; the rhetorical force lies in the contrast between the two hamm-s, one punished and one pardoned.

- **Root: ن ظ ر** (naẓara)
  * **Lisan / Ayn**: To look, to gaze; al-naẓar is the act of sight, whether physical or intellectual.
  * **Al-Raghib (Mufradat)**: The gaze (naẓar) is the gateway to desire; the Quranic phrase {«يَعْلَمُ خَائِنَةَ الْأَعْيُنِ»} — "He knows the treachery of the eyes" (Q. 40:19) — indicates that the look which steals toward the forbidden is itself an act of betrayal recorded by God.
  * **Al-Zamakhshari (Asas)**: Literal — the first glance that occurs unintentionally; Metaphorical — the second glance is the "treachery of the eyes," for it is a deliberate return to what the first glance stumbled upon by accident.

- **Root: ر و د** (rāwada)
  * **Lisan / Ayn**: To seek, to desire, to solicit; murāwadah is the act of soliciting someone for an unlawful purpose.
  * **Al-Raghib (Mufradat)**: In the Yūsuf narrative, murāwadah denotes the persistent solicitation toward sin; the term carries the weight of repeated, deliberate pursuit.
  * **Al-Zamakhshari (Asas)**: Literal — the physical act of solicitation; the narrative contexts in this section use the term literally for the woman's pursuit of the young man.

- **Sibawayh Rule**: **Bāb al-ḥaṣr wa-l-taqyīd bi-innamā** (Restriction and Focused Predication with innamā)
  * The particle innamā restricts and confines the predicate to the subject alone, negating all else. In the woman's statement "innamā urīdu mā yakūnu min al-rajuli ilā ahlihī" — "I only desire what comes from a man to his wife" — the restriction (ḥaṣr) intensifies the gravity of the solicitation, making the young man's resistance all the more virtuous.
