He said: "No." He said: "I know." He said: "What is it?" He said: "Chicory with vinegar." Then he said: "Do you know of anything less than quince that can take its place?" He said: "No." He said: "I know." He said: "What is it?" He said: "Levantine carob." Then he said: "Do you know of anything less than isfīdbāj that can take its place?" He said: "No." He said: "I know — the water of chickpeas with cow's ghee serves in its place." Then ʿAbd al-Raḥmān said to him: "You are more knowledgeable than I in medicine, so why did you ask me?"
46:20.section_title_en: On the Discipline of Appetite and the Etiquette of Eating — From the Revival of the Religious Sciences, Section 647
46:20.anchors:
- Root: شهو (Shahiya)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning is desire, craving, longing of the soul for something; appetite as an innate inclination.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In theological usage, شهوة (shahwah) denotes the lower appetitive drive of the soul (nafs) which must be disciplined and subordinated to reason and revelation; it is not inherently evil but becomes blameworthy when it dominates.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah) — the natural craving for food, drink, or copulation. Metaphorical (Majaz) — the soul's excessive attachment to worldly pleasures that veils it from the divine.
- Root: قلب (Qalb)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The heart; the organ of perception and understanding; that which fluctuates and turns (taqallub) between states.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The spiritual heart (al-qalb al-rūḥānī) is the locus of knowledge (maʿrifah), faith (īmān), and intention (niyyah); its hardness (qaswah) is the loss of receptivity to divine remembrance.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — the physical organ. Metaphorical — the seat of spiritual cognition and moral disposition; "hardness of heart" (qaswat al-qalb) is a metaphor for spiritual insensitivity.
- Root: ضر (Ḍarūrah)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Necessity, compulsion, need; that which cannot be dispensed with.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In the scale of human need, ḍarūrah is the minimum required for the preservation of life and health; it is the limit to which the ascetic restricts his consumption.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — genuine need. Metaphorical — the legal principle that necessity permits what is otherwise restricted, but only to the extent of the need.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Condition and Exception (al-sharṭ wa al-jawāb) — The conditional structures in this passage (e.g., "if he craves... then he should...") establish normative sequences where the protasis (condition) governs the apodosis (result), indicating that the discipline of appetite is contingent upon the specific state of the soul.
46:20.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Poverty and Abstinence'

46:35.arabic: محبوبها ثم لم يرض إلا أن يكلفني ما كلفهم فقال فاصبر كما صبر أولو العزم من الرسل والله مالي بد من طاعته وإني والله لأصبرن كما صبروا بجهدي ولا قوة إلا بالله (6) وروي عن عمر رضي الله عنه أنه حين فتح عليه الفتوحات قالت له ابنته حفصة رضي الله عنها البس ألين الثياب إذا وفدت عليك الوفود من الآفاق ومر بصنعة طعام تطعمه وتطعم من حضر فقال عمر يا حفصة ألست تعلمين أن أعلم الناس بحال الرجل أهل بيته فقالت بلى قال ناشدتك الله هل تعلمين أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لبث في النبوة كذا وكذا سنة لم يشبع هو ولا أهل بيته غد
46:35.english: Allah the Exalted said: {فخرج على قومه في زينته} [He went out to his people in his adornment] up to His saying, the Exalted: {وقال الذين أوتوا العلم ويلكم ثواب الله خير لمن آمن} [And those who had been given knowledge said, "Woe to you! The reward of Allah is better for he who believes."] Thus He attributed renunciation (al-zuhd) to the learned, and described its people as possessing knowledge—and this is the ultimate praise. And He said, the Exalted: {أولئك يؤتون أجرهم مرتين بما صبروا} [Those will be given their reward twice for what they patiently endured], and it came in the exegesis (al-tafsīr) that this refers to renunciation of the world. And He said, Mighty and Majestic: {إنا جعلنا ما على الأرض زينة لها لنبلوهم أيهم أحسن عملا} [Indeed We have made that which is on the earth adornment for it that We may test them as to which of them is best in deed]. It was said its meaning is: which of them is most renunciant (azhad) in it. So He described renunciation as being among the most excellent of deeds. And He said, the Exalted: {من كان يريد حرث الآخرة نزد له في حرثه ومن كان يريد حرث الدنيا نؤته منها وما له في الآخرة من نصيب} [Whoever desires the harvest of the Hereafter—We increase for him in his harvest. And whoever desires the harvest of this world—We give him from it, but he has no share in the Hereafter]. And He said, the Exalted: {ولا تمدن عينيك إلى ما متعنا به أزواجا منهم زهرة الحياة الدنيا لنفتنهم فيه ورزق ربك خير وأبقى} [And do not extend your eyes to that which We have given enjoyment to categories of them—the splendor of the life of this world—that We may test them thereby. And the provision of your Lord is better and more enduring]. And He said, the Exalted: {الذين يستحبون الحياة الدنيا على الآخرة} [Those who prefer the life of this world over the Hereafter]—thus He described the disbelievers with that. So its understood implication (mafhūmuhu) is that the believer is the one characterized by its opposite, namely, that he prefers the Hereafter over the life of this world. [PageV04P219]
46:35.section_title_en: The Book of Renunciation (Kitāb al-Zuhd) — Section on the Virtue of Despising the World
46:35.anchors:
- Root: زهد (z-h-d)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of abstaining, forsaking, and turning away from something, deeming it insignificant and paltry.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: الزهد is the voluntary turning of the heart away from the world (al-dunyā) as a deliberate act of spiritual preference for the Hereafter, not mere physical poverty.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah) usage denotes abstention from a thing due to its worthlessness; Metaphorical (Majaz) usage in the religious context signifies the heart's detachment from worldly allurements while the body may still function within it.
- Root: دنا (d-n-w)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Nearness, proximity; the world (al-dunyā) is so named for its closeness and lower station relative to the Hereafter.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): الدنو: القرب بالذات أو بالحكم; al-dunyā is the lower, nearer abode, contrasted with the ultimate and enduring one.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: spatial or temporal nearness; Metaphorical: the world as the inferior, immediate realm that precedes the eternal one.
- Root: عقل (ʿ-q-l) — implied in "مفهومه" (its understood implication)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Understanding, intellect, that which binds and restrains.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The intellect perceives the conceptual implication (mafhūm) of a statement, deriving the necessary opposite or corollary.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the articulated text; Metaphorical: the understood converse (mafhūm al-mukhālafah) which the author here employs to establish the believer's trait.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The periodic structure of the author's argumentation, where the governing verb (e.g., "قال تعالى") is separated from its quoted object by lengthy parenthetical citations, mirrors the classical allowance for interposition to maintain rhetorical flow and emphasis.
46:35.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Poverty and Abstinence'

47:36.arabic: الأموال والأولاد ثم رده تعالى في موضع آخر إلى اثنين فقال تعالى وإنما الحياة الدنيا لعب ولهو ثم رد الكل إلى واحد في موضع آخر فقال ونهى النفس عن الهوى فإن الجنة هي المأوى فالهوى لفظ يجمع جميع حظوظ النفس في الدنيا فينبغي أن يكون الزهد فيه وإذا فهمت طريق الإجمال والتفصيل عرفت أن البعض من هذه لا يخالف البعض وإنما يفارقه في الشرح مرة والإجمال أخرى فالحاصل أن الزهد عبارة عن الرغبة عن حظوظ النفس كلها ومهما رغب عن حظوظ النفس رغب عن البقاء في الدنيا فقصر أمله لا محالة لأنه إنما يريد البقاء ليتمتع ويريد التمتع الدائم بإرادة البقاء فإن من أراد شيئا
47:36.english: The third degree — and it is the highest — is that one renounce willingly, and renounce his very renunciation, so that he does not see his asceticism, since he does not see that he has abandoned anything, having come to know that the world is nothing. {PageV04P225} He is thus like one who casts away a potsherd and takes up a jewel — he does not regard that as an exchange, nor does he see himself as having abandoned anything. And the world, in comparison to God Most High and the bliss of the Hereafter, is baser than a potsherd in comparison to a jewel. This then is perfection in asceticism.
47:36.section_title_en: The Degrees of Asceticism (Zuhd) and Its Divisions
47:36.anchors:
- Root: زهد (Z-H-D)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: scarcity, paucity; al-Zuhd as abstemiousness; zāhada fīhi: to turn away from something, deeming it insignificant.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الزاهد في الشيء: الراغب عنه والراضي منه بالزهيد، أي: القليل" — the ascetic is one who turns away from a thing, content with little of it; theological sense: renunciation of the world as a deliberate act of valuation.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): "زهد في الشيء: رغب عنه" — turning away. Metaphorical (Majaz): "رجل زهيد: قليل الخير" — one of little good; "اد زهيد: قليل الأخذ للماء" — a valley taking little water. Here, al-Ghazali employs the literal sense of deliberate aversion, extended metaphorically to the soul's turning from all worldly appetites.
- Root: دنا (D-N-W)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Proximity, nearness; al-dunyā (the lower world) named for its nearness to us or its lowness.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الدنو: القرب بالذات، أو بالحكم" — nearness by essence or by judgment; al-dunyā contrasted with al-ākhirah as the inferior and nearer realm.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: proximity in place or rank. Metaphorical: the world as "lower" (adnā) in value — the sense operative in al-Ghazali's comparison of the world to a potsherd.
- Root: درج (D-R-J)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To walk step by step; to pass away (daraja: died, passed on); degree/stair.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الدرجة نحو المنزلة، لكن يقال للمنزلة: درجة إذا اعتبرت بالصعود" — a station considered as ascent; used for ranks of honor.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "درج قرن بعد قرن" — generations passed away; "رقي في الدرجة" — ascended in rank. Metaphorical: "لفلان درجة رفيعة" — one has a lofty degree. Al-Ghazali uses darajāt as ascending ranks of spiritual attainment.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد (Restriction and Specification) — the repeated use of "إنما" (only/but) in the Quranic citations (e.g., {إنما الحياة الدنيا لعب ولهو}) functions as restrictive predication (qasr), confining the reality of the world to play and diversion — a syntactic key to al-Ghazali's argument that all worldly goods reduce ultimately to one thing: caprice (hawā).
47:36.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Poverty and Abstinence'

47:38.arabic: فإنهم محتاجون إليه ليمدوا وجودهم بالدوام وإلى هذا الحصر الإشارة بقوله تعالى {والله الغني وأنتم الفقراء} هذا معنى الفقر مطلقا ولكنا لسنا نقصد بيان الفقر المطلق بل الفقر من المال على الخصوص وإلا ففقر العبد بالإضافة إلى أصناف حاجاته لا ينحصر لأن حاجاته لا حصر لها ومن جملة حاجاته ما يتوصل إليه بالمال وهو الذي نريد الآن بيانه فقط فنقول كل فاقد للمال فإنا نسميه فقيرا بالإضافة إلى المال الذي فقده إذا كان ذلك المفقود محتاجا إليه في حقه ثم يتصور أن يكون له خمسة أحوال عن الفقر ونحن نميزها ونخصص كل حال باسم لنتوصل بالتمييز إلى ذكر أحكامها الحال
47:38.english: Know that poverty (al-faqr) is an expression for the loss of that which one is in need of. As for the loss of that which one has no need of, that is not called poverty. And if that which one is in need of is present and within one's power, then the needy one is not poor. Once you understand this, you will not doubt that every existent other than God — exalted is He — is poor, because it is in need of the continuation of existence in the second moment [of time], and the continuation of existence is something derived (mustafād) from the bounty of God — exalted is He — and His generosity. For if there were in existence an existent whose existence were not derived from another, that one would be the absolutely Rich (al-ghaniyy al-mutlaq). And it is inconceivable that such an existent be other than one. Thus there is nothing in existence except one Rich, and everyone other than Him is in need of Him to sustain their existence with continuance. And to this exclusive enumeration points His saying — exalted is He: {«والله الغني وأنتم الفقراء»} (Q. 47:38) — "And God is the Rich, and you are the poor." This is the meaning of poverty absolutely. But we do not intend here the exposition of absolute poverty; rather, poverty specifically with respect to wealth. Otherwise, the poverty of the servant relative to the kinds of his needs is not delimited, for his needs have no limit. And among the totality of his needs is that which is attained through wealth, and that is what we intend now to expound exclusively.
47:38.section_title_en: The First Part of the Book on Poverty: Its Reality, Its Virtue, and the States of the Poor
47:38.anchors:
- Root: فقر (fa-qāf-rā)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning is "need" or "want" — the state of one lacking what is required; also a hollow or indentation (as in the back's vertebrae), suggesting an ontological emptiness or lack.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Poverty (al-faqr) is of four kinds: (1) necessary need inherent to all contingent existents, as in {«يا أيها الناس أنتم الفقراء إلى الله»} (Q. 35:15); (2) lack of possessions (the worldly sense); (3) contentment with little; (4) spiritual poverty before God. Here Ghazali distinguishes the absolute metaphysical sense from the specific economic sense.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (haqīqah): "ليس بفقير ولكن يتفاقر" — one who feigns poverty is not truly poor. Metaphorical (majāz): "فقر الكلام" — the "joints" or "pithy points" of speech, like beads on a spine. Ghazali uses the literal sense for economic poverty and the metaphysical sense for creaturely need.
- Root: غني (ghayn-nūn-yā)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Riches, sufficiency, independence; the opposite of faqr.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Ghinā is of three kinds: (1) absolute lack of needs — belonging to God alone, as in {«إن الله لهو الغني الحميد»} (Q. 22:64); (2) fewness of needs — the praiseworthy "richness of the soul" (غنى النفس) mentioned in the Hadith; (3) abundance of possessions.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "أنا عنه غني" — I am independent of it. Metaphorical: "تغنته القيود" — shackles "enriched" him, i.e., held him fast. Ghazali deploys the absolute sense (al-ghaniyy al-mutlaq) exclusively for God.
- Root: طلب (ṭā-lām-bā)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To seek, to search out, to demand; also "أطلبه الفقر" — poverty made him needy, i.e., drove him to seek.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الطلب: الفحص عن وجود الشيء" — seeking is the investigation into the existence of a thing, whether concrete or conceptual. Cf. {«ضعف الطالب والمطلوب»} (Q. 22:73).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "طلب الشيء طلبا ومطلبا" — to seek earnestly. Metaphorical: "السراج يطلب أن ينطفيء" — the lamp "seeks" to go out, i.e., tends toward it. Ghazali uses the literal sense for the poor man's active pursuit of wealth.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Specification and Restriction (باب التخصيص) — When a general term (الفقر) is qualified by a restrictive phrase (من المال على الخصوص), the subsequent division of states (aḥwāl) applies only to the restricted sense, not the absolute metaphysical sense. Ghazali explicitly signals this shift with "ولسنا نقصد بيان الفقر المطلق بل الفقر من المال على الخصوص."
47:38.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Poverty and Abstinence'

47:38.arabic: كالمتكفلين بالثغور والمرابطين بها والغزاة المجاهدين في سبيل الله فمنهم المقاتل ومنهم الردء ومنهم الذي يسقيهم الماء ومنهم الذي يحفظ دوابهم ويتعهدهم ولا ينفك أحد منهم عن أجر إذا كان قصده إعلاء كلمة الله تعالى دون حيازة الغنائم فكذلك العلماء قال الله تعالى {يرفع الله الذين آمنوا منكم والذين أوتوا العلم درجات} وقال تعالى {هم درجات عند الله} والفضيلة نسبية واستحقارنا للصيارفة عند قياسهم بالملوك لا يدل على حقارتهم إذا قيسوا بالكناسين فلا تظن أن ما نزل عن الرتبة القصوى ساقط القدر بل الرتبة العليا للأنبياء ثم الأولياء ثم الع
47:38.english: By this I do not mean the belief which the common man picks up by inheritance or by rote acquisition, nor the method of theological disputation and argumentation for fortifying one's creed against the evasions of opponents—as is the ultimate aim of the scholastic theologian (mutakallim). Rather, it is a kind of certainty which is the fruit of a light that God—may He be exalted—casts into the heart of a servant whose inward being has been purified by spiritual striving (mujāhadah) from all impurities, until he attains to the rank of the faith of Abū Bakr—may God be pleased with him—whose faith, were it weighed against the faith of all created beings, would outweigh them, as the Master of mankind—peace and blessings be upon him—bore witness for him. For in my view, what the common man believes and what the theologian arranges—who exceeds the common man only in the craft of speech (kalām), and for that very reason his craft is named "kalām"—is not that rank. Indeed, ʿUmar, ʿUthmān, ʿAlī, and the rest of the Companions—may God be pleased with them all—fell short of it, until Abū Bakr surpassed them by that secret which was deposited in his breast.
47:38.section_title_en: The Revival of the Religious Sciences — Section 43: On the Ordering of the Sciences and the Duties of the Seeker
47:38.anchors:
- Root: ذوق (dh-w-q)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Perceiving by taste; experiential apprehension
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Direct, unmediated perception—contrasted with mere cognition or hearsay
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal tasting vs. metaphorical "savoring" of knowledge
- Root: سلك (s-l-k)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Entering into a path; threading through
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The spiritual wayfaring (sulūk) toward God
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal road-taking vs. metaphorical spiritual journeying
- Root: كشف (k-sh-f) — AVOIDED per constraints; substituted with Root: غور (gh-w-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Depth, profundity; the deep bed of a sea
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The unfathomable depth of divine knowledge
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal deep water vs. metaphorical inaccessibility of ultimate truth
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — Governing the periodic suspension of meaning across clauses for rhetorical emphasis
47:38.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Book of Knowledge'

50:16.arabic: البعد حجابا فإنه أقرب إليك من حبل الوريد وليس هو في مكان حتى تكون السماوات والأرض حجابا بينك وبينه فلا حجاب بينك وبينه إلا شغلك بغيره وشغلك نفسك وشهواتك شغل بغيره وأنت لا تزال مشغولا بنفسك وبشهوات نفسك فكذلك لا تزال محجوبا عنه فالمشغول بحب نفسه مشغول عن الله تعالى والمشغول ببغض نفسه أيضا مشغول عن الله تعالى بكل ما سوى الله مثاله مثال الرقيب الحاضر في مجلس يجمع العاشق والمعشوق فإن التفت قلب العاشق إلى الرقيب وإلى بغضه واستثقاله وكراهة حضوره فهو في حال اشتغال قلبه ببغضه مصروف عن التلذذ ب
50:16.english: Beyond these five conditions there is a state that is higher than asceticism, namely: that wealth's existence and its loss become equal in his sight. If he finds it, he does not rejoice over it, nor is he harmed [by its presence]; and if he loses it, [his state] is likewise. Rather, his condition is like the condition of ʿĀʾishah — may God Most High be pleased with her — when one hundred thousand dirhams of [state] stipend reached her. She took it and distributed it all that very day. Her maidservant said to her: "You were not able, in what you distributed today, to buy us even one dirham's worth of meat to break our fast with." She replied: "Had you reminded me, I would have done so."
50:16.section_title_en: The Fifth State: The Truly Independent One (Al-Mustaghni) — Beyond Asceticism
50:16.anchors:
- Root: غني (gh-n-y)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of freedom from need, sufficiency, and wealth; the opposite of faqr (poverty/need).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Ghina is of three grades: (1) absolute freedom from all needs — belonging to God alone {«إن الله لهو الغني الحميد»}; (2) fewness of needs — the praiseworthy richness of the soul (ghina al-nafs); (3) abundance of possessions.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): "لي عن هذا غنية" (I have no need of this). Metaphorical (Majaz): "تغنته القيود" (fetters made him independent of movement) — here Ghazali extends this majaz to describe one independent of both possession and loss.
- Sibawayh Rule: Restriction and specification via the construction "ليس... بل" (negation followed by corrective reassertion) — used to progressively refine the semantic boundary of the term "ghani" versus "mustaghni."
50:16.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Poverty and Abstinence'

50:16.arabic: ولقد خلقنا الإنسان ونعلم ماتوسوس به نفسه ذكر ذلك تحذيرا وتنبيها للاحتراز منه في المستقبل وروى عبادة بن الصامت أنه عليه السلام قال لرجل سأله أن يوصيه ويعظه إذا أردت أمرا فتدبر عاقبته فإن كان رشدا فامضه وإن كان غيا فانته عنه (1) وقال بعض الحكماء إذا أردت أن يكون العقل غالبا للهوى فلا تعمل بقضاءالشهوة حتى تنظر العاقبة فإن مكث الندامة في القلب أكثر من مكث خفة الشهوة وقال لقمان إن المؤمن إذا أبصر العاقبة أمن الندامة وروى شداد بن أوس عنه صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال الكيس من دان
50:16.english: And some have said: "Grant that the wrongdoer has been pardoned—has he not still missed the reward of the righteous?"—pointing thereby to the loss and regret. And God Most High says: {«يَوْمَ يَجْمَعُكُمْ لِيَوْمِ الْجَمْعِ ذَٰلِكَ يَوْمُ التَّغَابُنِ»} ("The Day He will gather you for the Day of Gathering—that is the Day of Mutual Loss") (Al-Taghābun 64:9). So this is his counsel to his soul concerning his hours.
50:16.section_title_en: The Revival of the Religious Sciences — Section 1232: The Soul's Covenant with Itself and Reckoning Before Deeds
50:16.anchors:
- Root: نفس (n-f-s)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The self, soul, or spirit; that which breathes and animates; the essence of a thing.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-nafs denotes the rūḥ (spirit) and, in theological contexts, the very dhāt (essence/self) of a being—as in {«وَيُحَذِّرُكُمُ اللَّهُ نَفْسَهُ»} (Āl ʿImrān 3:28), where "His self" means His essence, not a separate entity.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): the soul as the seat of desire and action. Metaphorical (majāz): "دفق نفسه" (he poured out his self = his blood); the soul as a recalcitrant entity requiring discipline.
- Root: يوم (y-w-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: A day, from sunrise to sunset; also any span of time, especially the Day of Reckoning.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Yawm signifies the period of the sun's course, but metaphorically extends to any era—most critically "the Day of Gathering" (yawm al-jamʿ) and "the Day of Mutual Loss" (yawm al-taghābun), where God's attribution of the day to Himself signals its supreme gravity.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: a 24-hour cycle. Metaphorical: "أيام الله" (the days of God) = His punitive acts against the disbelievers, as in {«وَذَكِّرْهُمْ بِأَيَّامِ اللَّهِ»} (Ibrāhīm 14:5).
- Root: حسب (ḥ-s-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To count, reckon, or compute; also to suffice.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Ḥisāb is the employment of number; the Day of Judgment is the day of reckoning where deeds are weighed. The "ḥusbān" (computation) of the sun and moon (Al-Anʿām 6:96) marks time for human accountability.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: counting wealth or deeds. Metaphorical: "احتسبت ما عند فلان" (I probed what so-and-so possesses) = testing and examining, as the soul must examine its own intentions and acts before God's scrutiny.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — The text uses conditional and imperative constructions (e.g., "فإياك ثم إياك" and "ليشترط على نفسه") to impose binding covenants, where the predicate restricts the soul's scope of action, demanding a precise, self-imposed legal obligation.
50:16.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Monitoring and Accounting'

51:22.arabic: مع شدة الاجتهاد في غالب الأمر في الدنيا وينسى قوله تعالى وفي السماء رزقكم وما توعدون فنعوذ بالله من العمى والضلال فما هذا إلا انتكاس على أم الرأس وانغماس في ظلمات الجهل وصاحب هذا جدير بأن يكون داخلا تحت قوله تعالى ولو ترى إذ المجرمون ناكسو رءوسهم عند ربهم ربنا أبصرنا وسمعنا فأرجعنا نعمل صالحا أي أبصرنا أنك صدقت إذ قلت وأن ليس للإنسان إلا ما سعى فأرجعنا نسعى وعند ذلك لا يمكن من الانقلاب ويحق عليه العذاب فنعوذ بالله من دواعي الجهل والشك والارتياب السائق بالضرور إلى سوء المنقلب والمآب
51:22.english: **The First Rank:** That the disobedient one repents and remains steadfast upon repentance until the end of his life, so that he makes up for what he let slip of his affair, and does not prompt himself to return to his sins — except for the slips (zallāt) from which human beings are not free in their habitual ways, so long as one is not at the rank of prophethood. This is steadfastness upon repentance, and its possessor is the one who races forward in good deeds, exchanging his evil deeds for good ones. The name of this repentance is "sincere repentance" (al-tawbah al-naṣūḥ), and the name of this soul is the "tranquil soul" (al-nafs al-muṭma'innah) which returns to its Lord, well-pleased and well-pleasing. These are those to whom the Prophet, peace be upon him, pointed when he said: {«سبق المفردون المستهترون بذكر الله تعالى وضع الذكر عنهم أوزارهم فوردوا القيامة خفافا»} — "The solitary ones have outstripped [all others] — those who are engrossed in the remembrance of God Almighty, for remembrance has lifted their burdens from them, and they arrive at the Resurrection light [of burden]." For in this there is an indication that they were beneath burdens which remembrance lifted from them.
51:22.section_title_en: The Four Ranks of the Repentant — On the Degrees of Tawbah and the States of the Soul
51:22.anchors:
- Root: توب (T-W-B)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Return, turning back; the verbal noun denotes the act of reverting from a state.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "التوب: ترك الذنب على أجمل الوجوه" — abandoning sin in the most beautiful manner; the most complete form of apology, comprising abandonment of the sin due to its ugliness, remorse for what passed, and resolve against return.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): "تاب العبد إلى الله من ذنبه" — the servant's turning to God from his sin. Metaphorical (Majaz): The mutual relation of divine acceptance (تاب الله على عبده) as a response to the servant's turning.
- Root: نفس (N-F-S)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The self, soul, spirit; that which animates and distinguishes.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The soul (النفس) as the locus of divine address and self-reproach; its states (mutma'innah, lawwāmah, ammārah) are graded by its orientation toward God or toward passions.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the self as animate entity. Metaphorical: "دفق نفسه" (his blood/life) — the soul as the seat of life and moral agency.
- Root: ذنب (Dh-N-B)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The tail; that which follows behind.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الذنب في الأصل: الأخذ بذنب الشيء" — sin as the act of seizing the consequence; the trailing fault that follows the agent.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the tail of an animal. Metaphorical: "هو من الأذناب" — one who follows; sin as the trailing mark of the soul's deviation.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — Used to delimit the four ranks precisely, ensuring each category is mutually exclusive and exhaustive in its defining condition.
51:22.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Poverty and Abstinence'

51:23.arabic: ثم قرأ {وفي السماء رزقكم وما توعدون فورب السماء والأرض إنه لحق مثل ما أنكم تنطقون} وكان أبو ذر رضي الله عنه يوما جالسا في الناس فأتته امرأته فقالت له أتجلس بين هؤلاء والله ما في البيت هفة ولا سفة فقال يا هذه إن بين أيدينا عقبة كئودا لا ينجو منها إلا كل مخف فرجعت وهي راضية وقال ذو النون رحمه الله أقرب الناس إلى الكفر ذو فاقة لا صبر له وقيل لبعض الحكماء ما مالك فقال التجمل في الظاهر والقصد في الباطن واليأس مما في أيدي الناس وروي أن الله عز وجل قال في بعض الكتب السالفة المنزلة يا ابن آدم لو كانت الدنيا كلها لك لم يكن لك منها إلا القو
51:23.english: The Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Blessed is he who is guided to Islam, whose livelihood is sufficiency (kafāf), and who is content with it." And he, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "O company of the poor! Give God satisfaction (al-riḍā) from your hearts, and you shall attain the reward of your poverty — and if not, then not." Now the first [mentioned] is the contented one (al-qāniʿ), and this [second] is the satisfied one (al-rāḍī). And one might almost sense from the very wording of this [hadith] that the greedy striver (al-ḥarīḍ) has no reward for his poverty. However, the general pronouncements (al-ʿumūmāt) reported concerning the merit of poverty indicate that he does have a reward, as will be verified later. Perhaps what is meant by "lack of satisfaction" is aversion (al-karāhah) toward God's act in withholding the world from him. For there may be one who craves wealth intensely, yet never entertains in his heart any objection to God Almighty, nor any aversion to His act — and it is that very aversion which nullifies the reward of poverty.
51:23.section_title_en: On Contentment (Qanāʿah) and Satisfaction (Riḍā) with Poverty — Section 1072
51:23.anchors:
- Root: قنع (Q-N-ʿ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning is "to be content with one's portion, to accept sufficiency without excess"; al-qanūʿ is the one satisfied with the bare minimum of provision.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: qanāʿah is the virtue of the heart that restrains covetousness (ṭamaʿ) and affirms God's distributive justice in apportioning sustenance (rizq).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): satisfaction with what suffices. Metaphorical (majāz): "qaniʿa" as the soul's settling (sukūn) into God's decree — a state of inner stillness, not mere outward patience.
- Root: رضي (R-Ḍ-Y)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Raḍiya means to be well-pleased, to approve willingly without resentment; riḍwān is the settled state of approval.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Riḍā is the soul's acquiescence to the divine decree (qaḍāʾ) — a higher station than ṣabr, for the patient one endures while the satisfied one embraces.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: approval of what befalls. Metaphorical: "riḍā bi'l-qaḍāʾ" — the heart's harmony with God's will such that no trace of aversion remains.
- Root: طمع (Ṭ-M-ʿ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Ṭamaʿ is eager craving for what is not one's due; its opposite is qanāʿah and yaʾs (despair of what others hold).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Ṭamaʿ is blameworthy covetousness that enslaves the heart to creatures, whereas yaʾs (giving up hope in creatures) is the gateway to true wealth in God.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: stretching the hand toward another's possession. Metaphorical: the soul's restless reaching — a form of inner poverty.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Predicate Emphasis (Bāb al-Tawkīd bi-al-Ḍamīr al-Munfaṣil) — In "هم جلساء الله" the separated pronoun "hum" before the predicate "julasāʾ" restricts and emphasizes, signaling that the poor are exclusively God's companions on the Day of Resurrection, with no share for the wealthy.
51:23.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Poverty and Abstinence'

53:3.arabic: الله عليه وسلم إلا بحقيقة الحق فإنه لا ينطق عن الهوى إن هو إلا وحي يوحى وهذا كقوله صلى الله عليه وسلم الرؤيا الصالحة جزء من ستة وأربعين جزءامن النبوة (2) فإنه تقدير تحقيق لا محالة لكن ليس في قوة غيره أن يعرف علة تلك النسبة إلا بتخمين فأما بالتحقيق فلا إذ يعلم أن النبوة عبارة عما يختص به النبي ويفارق به غيره وهو يختص بأنواع من الخواص أحدها أن يعرف حقائق الأمور المتعلقة بالله وصفاته والملائكة والدار الآخرة لا كما يعلمه غيره بل مخالفا له بكثرة المعلومات وبزيادة اليقين والتحقيق والكشف والثاني أن له في نفسه صفة بها تتم
53:3.english: As for the verses [of the Qur'an], that is indicated by His saying, the Exalted: {«لِلْفُقَرَاءِ الْمُهَاجِرِينَ الَّذِينَ أُخْرِجُوا مِنْ دِيَارِهِمْ وَأَمْوَالِهِمْ»} [To the poor emigrants who were driven out of their homes and their wealth] (59:8), to the end of the verse. And He said, the Exalted: {«لِلْفُقَرَاءِ الَّذِينَ أُحْصِرُوا فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ لَا يَسْتَطِيعُونَ ضَرْبًا فِي الْأَرْضِ»} [To the poor who are confined in the way of Allah, unable to travel in the land] (2:273). He directed the discourse in the context of praise, then He advanced their description with poverty before their description with emigration and confinement. In this there is an evident indication of the praise of poverty.
53:3.section_title_en: The Virtue of Poverty: Scriptural Evidences and Their Interpretation
53:3.anchors:
- Root: فقر (F-Q-R)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of need, indigence, and the state of lacking possessions; also the notches of a vertebra or the joints of the back, indicating structural dependence.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Poverty is of four degrees: (1) essential neediness before God (universal to all creatures), (2) lack of worldly goods (the subject here), (3) voluntary renunciation (zuhd), and (4) the perfection of the heart's detachment. The praise of poverty here targets the second and third degrees, not destitution that breeds discontent.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah) poverty is the absence of wealth; metaphorical (Majaz) poverty is the soul's humility and its "notches" of dependence on God. The Prophet's praise of the "poor" (fuqara') must be read as praise of the virtuous poor (mutafaQQir), not the covetous.
- Root: هجر (H-J-R)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To abandon, emigrate, or sever ties; the act of leaving one's homeland for a religious purpose.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Hijrah (emigration) is a physical act of devotion, but the Quranic verse pairs it with poverty, elevating the state of neediness as a spiritual station above the mere act of relocation.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): The verse's structure (taqdim) places "poverty" before "emigration" and "confinement," signaling its superior rank in the divine estimation.
- Root: قدر (Q-D-R)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Measure, decree, power, and estimation; the act of determining a precise limit or quantity.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): When applied to God, Qadar is His eternal decree; when applied to the Prophet's speech, it denotes precise, divinely-inspired measurement—never arbitrary or haphazard.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: to measure out (qaddara). Metaphorical: the "measure" of a thing's worth or rank. The Prophet's numerical estimates (e.g., 500 years, 46 parts) are literal measures of spiritual realities, though their exact rationale may be hidden from non-prophetic intellects.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — The Quranic construction {للفقراء المهاجرين} uses prepositional fronting (taqdim) to restrict the praise to a specific class, and the sequence of descriptors (poverty before hijrah) establishes a hierarchy of virtues through syntactic ordering.
53:3.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Poverty and Abstinence'

53:29.arabic: قوله عز وجل وهم في غفلة معرضون وفي قوله فأعرض عمن تولى عن ذكرنا ولم يرد إلا الحياة الدنيا وفي قوله تعالى ومن لم يتب فأولئك هم الظالمون إلى غير ذلك من الآيات وكان داخلا في معنى قوله عز وجل ومنهم أميون لا يعلمون الكتاب إلا أماني يعني التلاوة المجردة وقوله عز وجل وكأين من آية في السموات والأرض يمرون عليها وهم عنها معرضون لأن القرآن هو المبين لتلك الآيات في السموات والأرض ومهما تجاوزها ولم يتأثر بها كان معرضا عنها ولذلك قيل إن من لم يكن متصفا بأخلاق القرآن فإذا قرأ القرآن ناداه الله تعالى مالك ولكلامي وأنت معرض عني دع عنك كلامي إن لم ت
53:29.english: And at the mention of God, His attributes, and His names, he bows low in humility before His majesty and in apprehension of His greatness. And at the mention of the disbelievers' sayings — those things impossible for God, Mighty and Majestic, such as their attributing to Him a son or a consort — he lowers his voice and inwardly recoils in shame at the ugliness of their speech. And at the description of Paradise, his innermost being surges forth with longing for it. And at the description of the Fire, his limbs tremble in fear of it. For when the Messenger of God, peace be upon him, said to Ibn Mas'ud, "Recite to me," he said: "I began reciting Surah al-Nisa'. When I reached {فكيف إذا جئنا من كل أمة بشهيد وجئنا بك على هؤلاء شهيدا} [How then shall it be when We bring from every nation a witness, and We bring you as a witness against these?] (4:41), I saw his two eyes overflowing with tears. He then said to me: 'That is enough for you now.'" And this was because the witnessing of that very state had wholly overwhelmed his heart.
53:29.section_title_en: The States of the Heart During Qur'anic Recitation — The Condition of the True Recieter
53:29.anchors:
- Root: وجل (w-j-l)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root meaning of trembling fear, trepidation of the heart
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الوجل: استشعار الخوف" — the inward apprehension of fear; cited in {إنما المؤمنون الذين إذا ذكر الله وجلت قلوبهم}
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): "رجل وجل، وقوم وجال" — a man fearful, a people fearful; the state of the heart's trembling before divine majesty
- Root: وصف (w-ṣ-f)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Describing a thing by its attributes and qualities
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الوصف: ذكر الشيء بحليته ونعته" — description is the mention of a thing by its adornment and attribute; may be true or false
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal vs Metaphorical: "وجهها يصف الحسن" — metaphorical usage where the face itself "describes" beauty; likewise, the tongue may "describe" falsehood, as in {ولا تقولوا لما تصف ألسنتكم الكذب}
- Root: وفي (w-f-y)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Completeness, fulfillment, reaching full measure
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الوافي: الذي بلغ التمام" — that which attains completion; "أوفى: إذا تمم العهد ولم ينقض حفظه" — fulfilled the covenant without breach
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "درهم واف" — a full-weight dirham; Metaphorical: "أوفى على المائة إذا زاد عليها" — surpassed the hundred
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The separation between the governing preposition and its object by intervening clauses, as in "فلما بلغت {فكيف إذا جئنا...}" where the temporal clause governs the narrative sequence
53:29.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

53:29.arabic: وقال عز وجل فأعرض عمن تولى عن ذكرنا ولم يرد إلا الحياة الدنيا ذلك مبلغهم من العلم فالجمع بين كمال الاستبصار في مصالح الدنيا والدين لا يكاد يتيسر إلا لمن رسخه الله لتدبير عباده في معاشهم ومعادهم وهم الأنبياء المؤيدون بروح القدس المستمدون من القوة الإلهية التي تتسع لجميع الأمور ولا تضيق عنها فأما قلوب سائر الخلق فإنها إذا استقلت بأمر الدنيا انصرفت عن الآخرة وقصرت عن الاستكمال فيها
53:29.english: They left [the vessels] upon the road — why do you not return them to their places? So they said to him: "Those vessels are in their places; rather, it is you who cannot find the way, due to your blindness. The wonder of you is that you do not attribute your stumbling to your blindness, but rather attribute it to the shortcoming of another." Such is the relation of the religious sciences to the rational sciences.
53:29.section_title_en: The Heart's Relation to the Divisions of the Rational, Religious, Worldly, and Otherworldly Sciences
53:29.anchors:
- Root: عقل (ʿaql)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The faculty prepared for the reception of knowledge; also the knowledge acquired by that faculty.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "العقل يقال للقوة المتهيئة لقبول العلم، ويقال للعلم الذي يستفيده الإنسان بتلك القوة عقل" — the intellect is the power prepared to receive knowledge, and the knowledge one acquires by that power is also called ʿaql.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "ما لفلان مقول، ولا معقول" — one who has neither speech nor understanding. Metaphorical: "نخلة لا تعقل الإبار" — a palm that does not accept pollination, i.e., does not take it in.
- Root: قلب (qalb)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The heart; that which is ever-turning and fluctuating.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "قلب الشيء: تصريفه وصرفه عن وجه إلى وجه" — the turning of a thing from one state to another; the heart is so named for its constant turning of resolutions and states.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "قلب الشيء قلبا: حوله عن وجهه" — to turn a thing from its face. Metaphorical: "رجل قلب حول: يقلب الأمور ويحتال" — a man who turns matters over and devises stratagems.
- Root: دنا (danā)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Nearness in place, time, or rank.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الدنو: القرب بالذات، أو بالحكم" — nearness by essence or by judgment; the worldly life (al-dunyā) is so named for its nearness and precedence.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "هو دنيء من الأدنياء" — base and contemptible; the dunyā is that which is lower and nearer.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — used to restrict the predicate exclusively to the subject, as in the Prophetic statement restricting the majority of Paradise's inhabitants to the "bullah" (those seemingly foolish in worldly matters).
53:29.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Poverty and Abstinence'

57:20.arabic: الآخرة إلا متاع} وقال تعالى {اعلموا أنما الحياة الدنيا لعب ولهو وزينة وتفاخر بينكم وتكاثر في الأموال والأولاد} الآية وكل ذلك ذم لها فنسأل الله السلامة فأولو الحزم من أرباب القلوب جربوا قلوبهم في حال الفرح بمؤاتاة الدنيا فوجدوها قاسية نفرة بعيدة التأثر عن ذكر الله واليوم الآخر وجربوها في حالة الحزن فوجدوها لينة رقيقة صافية قابلة لأثر الذكر فعلموا أن النجاة في الحزن الدائم والتباعد من أسباب الفرح والبطر ففطموها عن ملاذها وعودوها الصبر عن شهواتها حلالها وحرامها وعلموا أن حلالها حساب وحرامها عقاب ومتشابهها عتاب وهو نوع عذاب فمن نوقش الحساب في عرصات القيام
57:20.english: And beyond it lie afflictions greater than this—namely, that the soul rejoices in comfort within this world, leans toward it, and becomes tranquil in it with insolence (asharan) and pride (baṭaran), until it becomes intoxicated like a drunkard who does not awaken from his intoxication. And that joy in this world is a deadly poison that courses through the veins, expelling from the heart the fear (khawf) of God, sorrow (ḥuzn), the remembrance of death, and the terrors of the Day of Resurrection. This is the death of the heart. God, Exalted is He, said: {وَرَضُوا بِالْحَيَاةِ الدُّنْيَا وَاطْمَأَنُّوا بِهَا} ("And they were pleased with the life of this world and felt secure in it") (Q 10:7). And He, Exalted is He, said: {وَمَا الْحَيَاةُ الدُّنْيَا فِي الْآخِرَةِ إِلَّا مَتَاعٌ} ("And the life of this world, compared to the Hereafter, is but a [passing] enjoyment") (Q 13:26). And He, Exalted is He, said: {اعْلَمُوا أَنَّمَا الْحَيَاةُ الدُّنْيَا لَعِبٌ وَلَهْوٌ وَزِينَةٌ وَتَفَاخُرٌ بَيْنَكُمْ وَتَكَاثُرٌ فِي الْأَمْوَالِ وَالْأَوْلَادِ} ("Know that the life of this world is but amusement and diversion and adornment and boasting among you and competition in increase of wealth and children") (Q 57:20)—to the end of the verse. All of this is censure of it. So we ask God for safety (salāmah).
57:20.section_title_en: On the Afflictions of Permissible Things and the Discipline of the Soul
57:20.anchors:
- Root: س ك ت (s-k-t)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root meaning: silence, stillness, cessation of speech.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: silence (sukūt) as a positive act of worship when it restrains the tongue from falsehood and excess, aligning with the Quranic command to guard one's speech.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal vs Metaphorical: Literal silence (ḥaqīqah) is the absence of audible speech; metaphorical (majāz) silence is the restraint of the heart from vain desires and the tongue from all but the remembrance of God.
- Root: ش ه و (sh-h-w)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root meaning: desire, longing, appetite; the inclination of the soul toward what pleases it.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: shahwah (appetite/desire) is a neutral faculty; its blameworthiness lies in its direction toward the forbidden (ḥarām) or in its excess beyond the measure of necessity (ḍarūrah), which enslaves the heart.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal vs Metaphorical: Literal desire is the physical craving for food, drink, or sensual pleasure; metaphorical desire is the soul's craving for status, comfort, and the fleeting adornments of this world (dunyā), which is the root of spiritual ruin.
- Root: ف ط م (f-ṭ-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root meaning: to wean, to cut off from suckling; to abstain from a habit.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: fiṭām (weaning) is used analogically for the discipline of the soul—cutting it off from worldly pleasures (shahawāt) to accustom it to the remembrance of God, just as a child is weaned from the breast.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal vs Metaphorical: Literal weaning is the physical act of separating an infant from milk; metaphorical weaning is the soul's training (riyāḍah) to abandon the "milk" of worldly comfort for the "food" of spiritual devotion.
- Root: أ ن س ('-n-s)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root meaning: to be sociable, familiar, at ease; to find comfort in company.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: uns (intimacy/familiarity) with God is the highest station of the heart, achieved only after severing intimacy with the world; it is the soul's true home, contrasted with the alienation (waḥshah) of worldly attachment.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal vs Metaphorical: Literal intimacy is human companionship; metaphorical intimacy is the heart's tranquil repose (ṭuma'nīnah) in the remembrance of God, as cited in the Quranic verse {أَلَا بِذِكْرِ اللَّهِ تَطْمَئِنُّ الْقُلُوبُ}.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The rule governing the separation of a preposition from its object for rhetorical emphasis, as in the periodic structure of the author's conditional clauses (e.g., "فمن أراد... فحقه أن يلزمه"), where the protasis is extended to clarify the subject's intent before the apodosis delivers the ruling.
57:20.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Poverty and Abstinence'

57:20.arabic: الله خير} وقوله {والآخرة خير وأبقى} وقوله {وما الحياة الدنيا إلا متاع الغرور} وقوله {فلا تغرنكم الحياة الدنيا} وقد أخبر رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بذلك طوائف من الكفار فقلدوه وصدقوه وآمنوا به ولم يطالبوه بالبرهان (1) حديث قول من قال له نشدتك الله أبعثك رسولا فيقول {نعم} فيصدق متفق عليه من حديث أنس في قصة ضمام ابن ثعلبة وقوله للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أرسلك للناس كلهم فقال اللهم نعم وفي آخره فقال الرجل آمنت بما جئت به وللطبراني من حديث ابن عباس في ضمام قال نشدتك به أهو أرسلك بما أتتنا كتبك وأتتنا رسلك أن نشهد أن لا إله إلا ا
57:20.english: Know that the saying of God Most High — {«fa-lā taghurrannakum al-ḥayātu al-dunyā wa-lā yaghurrannakum billāhi al-gharūr»} (So let not the life of this world deceive you, nor let the Deceiver deceive you concerning God) — and His saying — {«wa-lākinnakum fatantum anfusakum wa-tarabbastum wa-irtabtum wa-gharratkum al-amānī»} (But ye tempted your own souls, and ye waited, and ye doubted, and vain desires deceived you) — is sufficient for the blameworthiness of self-deception (al-ghurūr). And the Messenger of God, may God's peace and blessing be upon him, has said: "How excellent is the sleep of the intelligent and their breaking of the fast! How they outwit the wakefulness of the foolish and their striving! And verily a mustard-seed's weight [of faith] from a possessor of piety and certainty is better than the earth filled with the self-deceived." And the ḥadīth: "The intelligent man (al-kayyis) is he who takes account of his own soul and works for what is after death" — this ḥadīth was transmitted by al-Tirmidhī and Ibn Mājah from the ḥadīth of Shaddād ibn Aws.
57:20.section_title_en: Exposition of the Blameworthiness of Self-Deception (Al-Ghurūr), Its Reality, and Its Examples
57:20.anchors:
- Root: غرر (Gh-R-R)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The core meaning is "an apparent trace or mark of a thing" (al-athar al-ẓāhir), from which derives "the blaze of a horse" (ghurrat al-faras). To deceive (gharra) is to strike one's heedlessness (ghirrah) and attain one's sought desire from him, as if folding a garment upon its original crease (ṭawāhu ʿalā gharrihi).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Ghurrah is heedlessness in wakefulness, and ghirār is heedlessness with drowsiness." Theologically, it is the soul's repose upon a false semblance (shubhah) that pleases the caprice (hawā), rendering one oblivious to the true state of affairs—as in {«mā gharraka bi-rabbika al-karīm»} (What deceived thee concerning thy Generous Lord?).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): "A gazelle in a moonlit night is called agharr" because it ventures out thinking it is day and is devoured by beasts—heedlessness in perception. Metaphorical (majāz): "A day agharr muḥajjal" (a white-browed, white-legged day) for intense heat, transferring the blaze of a horse to the day's visible intensity.
- Root: جهل (J-H-L)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "Jahila bihi" — to be ignorant of it; "jāhala ʿalā qawmihi" — to act foolishly/insolently against one's people. The pre-Islamic era is "al-jāhiliyyah al-jahlā'" (the utterly ignorant age).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Ignorance (jahl) is of three kinds: (1) the soul's emptiness of knowledge (this is the root); (2) believing a thing contrary to what it is; (3) doing a thing contrary to what it ought to be, whether one's belief is sound or corrupt. Ghurūr is a species of the second kind—a false belief arising from a corrupt semblance.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "Kafā bil-shakki jahlā" (Sufficient is doubt as ignorance). Metaphorical: "Istajhalat al-rīḥ al-ghuṣn" (The wind made the branch sway violently) — transferred from mental foolishness to physical agitation.
- Root: حدث (Ḥ-D-TH)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "Al-ḥudūth: the coming-to-be of a thing after it was not." "Al-ḥadath: the novel event." "Ḥaddatha: to speak/communicate."
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Ḥudūth is the existence of a thing after non-existence, whether accident or substance. Iḥdāth is bringing it into existence. The iḥdāth of substances belongs to God alone." The "ḥadīth" (report/speech) is so-called for its temporal novelty.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "Nazalat bihi ḥawādith al-dahr" (The vicissitudes of time befell him). Metaphorical: "Kāna ʿUmar muḥaddathan" (Umar was one inspired with true discernment) — as if he were spoken to (ḥudditha) by what he conjectured.
- Root: دنا (D-N-W)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "Danā fa-huwa dānin" — he drew near. "Al-dunyā" (the lower world) is so named because it is nearer (danat) and precedes the Hereafter.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Al-dunūw: proximity by essence or by judgment, used of place, time, and station." The "adnā" (lower/nearer) is contrasted with the greater and with the better: {«a-tastabdilūna alladhī huwa adnā billadhī huwa khayr»} (Will ye take the lower in exchange for what is better?).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "Huwa danī' min al-adniyā'" (He is base, of the base ones) — but this is the homonym danu'a (baseness), distinct from danā (nearness). The dunyā's "nearness" is its temporal immediacy versus the Hereafter's deferral.
- Sibawayh Rule: Bab al-faṣl bayna al-jār wa-al-majrūr (Prepositional Interposition) — The particle "bi" in {«wa-lā yaghurrannakum billāhi al-gharūr»} governs the deceiver (al-gharūr) as the agent of deception, while "billāh" (concerning God) is the object of the deception. The syntactic structure permits the deceiver to be named after the prepositional phrase, indicating that the deception is *about* God's attributes (His forbearance, His respite) — a grammatical subtlety showing the ghurūr deceives *by means of* false notions of God, not that God Himself deceives.
57:20.topic: Al-Ghazali on the journey of the soul, death, and the Hereafter, from 'Condemnation of Delusion'

57:20.arabic: الأموال والأولاد ثم رده تعالى في موضع آخر إلى اثنين فقال تعالى وإنما الحياة الدنيا لعب ولهو ثم رد الكل إلى واحد في موضع آخر فقال ونهى النفس عن الهوى فإن الجنة هي المأوى فالهوى لفظ يجمع جميع حظوظ النفس في الدنيا فينبغي أن يكون الزهد فيه وإذا فهمت طريق الإجمال والتفصيل عرفت أن البعض من هذه لا يخالف البعض وإنما يفارقه في الشرح مرة والإجمال أخرى فالحاصل أن الزهد عبارة عن الرغبة عن حظوظ النفس كلها ومهما رغب عن حظوظ النفس رغب عن البقاء في الدنيا فقصر أمله لا محالة لأنه إنما يريد البقاء ليتمتع ويريد التمتع الدائم بإرادة البقاء فإن من أراد شيئا
57:20.english: The third degree — and it is the highest — is that one renounce willingly, and renounce his very renunciation, so that he does not see his asceticism, since he does not see that he has abandoned anything, having come to know that the world is nothing. {PageV04P225} He is thus like one who casts away a potsherd and takes up a jewel — he does not regard that as an exchange, nor does he see himself as having abandoned anything. And the world, in comparison to God Most High and the bliss of the Hereafter, is baser than a potsherd in comparison to a jewel. This then is perfection in asceticism.
57:20.section_title_en: The Degrees of Asceticism (Zuhd) and Its Divisions
57:20.anchors:
- Root: زهد (Z-H-D)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: scarcity, paucity; al-Zuhd as abstemiousness; zāhada fīhi: to turn away from something, deeming it insignificant.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الزاهد في الشيء: الراغب عنه والراضي منه بالزهيد، أي: القليل" — the ascetic is one who turns away from a thing, content with little of it; theological sense: renunciation of the world as a deliberate act of valuation.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): "زهد في الشيء: رغب عنه" — turning away. Metaphorical (Majaz): "رجل زهيد: قليل الخير" — one of little good; "اد زهيد: قليل الأخذ للماء" — a valley taking little water. Here, al-Ghazali employs the literal sense of deliberate aversion, extended metaphorically to the soul's turning from all worldly appetites.
- Root: دنا (D-N-W)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Proximity, nearness; al-dunyā (the lower world) named for its nearness to us or its lowness.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الدنو: القرب بالذات، أو بالحكم" — nearness by essence or by judgment; al-dunyā contrasted with al-ākhirah as the inferior and nearer realm.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: proximity in place or rank. Metaphorical: the world as "lower" (adnā) in value — the sense operative in al-Ghazali's comparison of the world to a potsherd.
- Root: درج (D-R-J)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To walk step by step; to pass away (daraja: died, passed on); degree/stair.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الدرجة نحو المنزلة، لكن يقال للمنزلة: درجة إذا اعتبرت بالصعود" — a station considered as ascent; used for ranks of honor.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "درج قرن بعد قرن" — generations passed away; "رقي في الدرجة" — ascended in rank. Metaphorical: "لفلان درجة رفيعة" — one has a lofty degree. Al-Ghazali uses darajāt as ascending ranks of spiritual attainment.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد (Restriction and Specification) — the repeated use of "إنما" (only/but) in the Quranic citations (e.g., {إنما الحياة الدنيا لعب ولهو}) functions as restrictive predication (qasr), confining the reality of the world to play and diversion — a syntactic key to al-Ghazali's argument that all worldly goods reduce ultimately to one thing: caprice (hawā).
57:20.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Poverty and Abstinence'

57:21.arabic: وإن اشتركوا في مصيبة الحرمان من حقيقة الأمر فالحقيقة فضل الله يؤتيه من يشاء والله ذو الفضل العظيم وحكمته يختص بها من يشاء ومن يؤت الحكمة فقد أوتي خيرا كثيرا ولنعد إلى الغرض فقد أرخينا الطول وطولنا النفس في أمر هو أعلاى من علوم المعاملات التي نقصدها في هذا الكتاب فقد ظهر أن رتبة الهلاك ليس إلا للجهال المكذبين وشهادة ذلك من كتاب الله وسنة رسوله صلى الله عليه وسلم لا تدخل تحت الحصر فلذلك لم نوردها الرتبة الثانية رتبة المعذبين وهذه رتبة من تحلى بأصل الإيمان ولكن قصر في الوفاء بمقتضاه فإن رأس الإيمان هو التوحيد وهو أن لا يعبد
57:21.english: The fire of Hell is the coldest of fires [in comparison to the fire of separation]. And you should not deny this in the world of the Hereafter, for it has a witnessed parallel in the world of this world. Indeed, one has been seen who was overcome by ecstasy (wajd) and walked upon fire and upon the roots of cane, his feet being cut, yet he did not feel it, due to the extreme dominance of what was in his heart. And you see the angry man, when anger overcomes him in battle, receiving wounds and not feeling them at that moment, because anger is a fire in the heart. The Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, said: {«الغضب قطعة من النار»} "Anger is a piece of fire." The burning of the heart (iḥtirāq al-fu'ād) is more severe than the burning of bodies, and the more severe annuls the sensation of the weaker, as you observe. For destruction from fire and the sword is only inasmuch as they separate between two parts that are linked one to the other by the bond of composition (ta'līf) possible in bodies. So that which separates between the heart and its Beloved, to which it is linked by a bond of composition far more firm than the composition of bodies, is more intensely painful—if you are among the people of insight (abṣār) and the people of hearts. And it is not far-fetched that he who has no heart should not perceive the severity of this pain and should deem it trivial in comparison to bodily pain. For a boy, if he were given the choice between the pain of being deprived of a ball and a polo-stick, and the pain of being deprived of the rank of a Sultan, he would not feel the pain of deprivation from the Sultan's rank at all, nor would he count that as a pain. And the enemy in the field with the polo-stick is more beloved to him than a thousand thrones of the Sultan with sitting upon them. Nay, even one overcome by the lust of the belly, if given the choice between porridge (harīsah) and sweets (ḥalwā) and between a beautiful deed by which he conquers enemies and delights friends, he would prefer the porridge and sweets. All of this is due to the absence of the meaning (maʿnā) by whose existence rank becomes beloved, and the presence of the meaning by whose existence food becomes delicious. This is for one whom the attributes of beasts and predators have enslaved, and in whom the attributes of the angels have not appeared—those attributes which are not suited by, nor delight in, anything but proximity to the Lord of the Worlds, and which are pained only by distance and the veil (ḥijāb). And just as taste is only in the tongue and hearing only in the ears, so this attribute is only in the heart. So he who has no heart has no such sense, like he who has no hearing or sight has no pleasure in melodies or the beauty of forms and colors. And not every human has a heart; were it so, the saying of God, Most High, would not be sound: {«إن في ذلك لذكرى لمن كان له قلب»} "Indeed in that is a reminder for whoever has a heart" (Q. 50:37). Thus He made the one who does not heed the Quran devoid of a heart. And by "heart" I do not mean this [organ] which the ribs of the chest encompass. Rather, I mean the secret (sirr) which is of the world of the Command (ʿālam al-amr). The flesh which is of the world of Creation (ʿālam al-khalq) is its Throne (ʿarsh), the chest is its Footstool (kursī), and the rest of the limbs are its domain and kingdom. And to God belongs the Creation and the Command altogether. But that secret, concerning which God, Most High, said: {«قل الروح من أمر ربي»} "Say: The Spirit is of the Command of my Lord" (Q. 17:85), is the commander and the king, because between the world of the Command and the world of Creation there is an ordering, and the world of the Command is commander over the world of Creation. It is the subtle divine reality (al-laṭīfah) which, when it is sound, the rest of the body is sound for its sake. Whoever knows it has known his own self, and whoever knows his own self has known his Lord. At that point, the servant smells the beginnings of the fragrance of the meaning folded under his saying, peace and blessings be upon him: {«إن الله خلق آدم على صورته»} "God created Adam upon His image." He looks with the eye of mercy upon those who adhere to its literal wording and upon those who are obstinate in the path of its interpretation (ta'wīl). And even though His mercy for those adhering to the letter is greater than His mercy for the obstinate interpreters, because mercy is proportional to the affliction, and the affliction of those [literalists] is greater—even if they share in the affliction of being deprived of the reality of the matter—for the Reality (al-ḥaqīqah) is the bounty of God which He gives to whom He wills, and God is the Possessor of Great Bounty. And His Wisdom is singled out for whom He wills: {«ومن يؤت الحكمة فقد أوتي خيرا كثيرا»} "And whoever is given wisdom has been given much good" (Q. 2:269). Let us return to the purpose, for we have drawn out the length and lengthened the breath in a matter that is higher than the sciences of transactions (muʿāmalāt) which we intend in this book. It has become clear that the rank of destruction is only for the ignorant deniers. And the testimony of that from the Book of God and the Sunnah of His Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, is beyond enumeration, so we have not cited it.
57:21.section_title_en: The Ranks of the Hereafter: On the Distribution of Degrees and the States of the Saved, the Punished, and the Victorious
57:21.anchors:
- Root: ح ر ق (ḥ-r-q)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of burning, scorching, and the fire's consumption of its fuel.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The fire of the Hereafter (Nār) is a created reality, but its perception is tied to the spiritual state of the perceiver.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah) for physical burning; metaphorical (Majaz) for the burning of the heart (iḥtirāq al-fu'ād) by overwhelming love or anger.
- Root: ق ل ب (q-l-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To turn, overturn, or transform a thing from one state to another.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The heart (Qalb) is the seat of perception and understanding, distinct from the physical organ.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal for the physical heart; metaphorical for the spiritual subtlety (Laṭīfah) that is the locus of divine knowledge and love.
- Root: ع ل م (ʿ-l-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To know, to perceive a thing by its true nature.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Knowledge (ʿIlm) is the apprehension of a thing's reality, which is the basis for distinguishing the ranks of the believers.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal for acquired knowledge; metaphorical for the "unveiling" (Kashf) knowledge granted to the knowers (ʿĀrifūn).
- Sibawayh Rule: Restriction and Specification (Bāb al-Ḥaṣr wa al-Taqyīd bi-innamā) — Used to distinguish the specific referents of terms like "heart" (Qalb) and "faith" (Īmān), ensuring the precise meaning is not conflated with common usage.
57:21.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Poverty and Abstinence'

57:21.arabic: فقال صلى الله عليه وسلم ذلك فضل الله يؤتيه من يشاء (1) وقد استشهد ابن عطاء أيضا لما سئل عن ذلك فقال الغني أفضل لأنه وصف الحق أما دليله الأول ففيه نظر لأن الخبر قد ورد مفصلا تفصيلا يدل على خلاف ذلك وهو أن ثواب الفقير في التسبيح يزيد على ثواب الغني وأن فوزهم بذلك الثواب فضل الله يؤتيه من يشاء فقد روى زيد بن أسلم عن أنس بن مالك رضي الله عنه قال بعث الفقراء رسولا إلا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال إني رسول الفقراء إليك فقال {مرحبا} بك وبمن جئت من عندهم قوم أحبهم قال قالوا يا رسول الله إن
57:21.english: Evidence for this may be found in what is related in the report (khabar) that the poor complained to the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, that the rich had preceded them in good deeds, alms, pilgrimage (ḥajj), and holy struggle (jihād). So he taught them words of glorification (tasbīḥ) and told them that by these they would attain what surpassed what the rich had attained. Then the rich learned these words and began to say them, so the poor returned to the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, and informed him [of this]. He said, peace and blessings be upon him: {«ذلك فضل الله يؤتيه من يشاء»} — "That is the bounty of God; He gives it to whom He wills." (1)
57:21.section_title_en: On the Relative Excellence of Poverty and Wealth — A Detailed Exposition
57:21.anchors:
- Root: فقر (fa-qā-rā)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of neediness, destitution; the state of one lacking provision or means.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Fourfold division — (1) essential need before God (universal to all creatures), (2) lack of acquired possessions, (3) contentment of the soul, (4) metaphorical usage. Here, the operative sense is the second: absence of worldly goods.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah) — absence of wealth; Metaphorical (Majaz) — "فقرة الكلام" (a rhetorical gem/point), showing the root's capacity for extension. The discussion here remains in the literal register of material need.
- Root: غني (ghayn-nūn-yā)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of sufficiency, independence, freedom from need.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Threefold division — (1) absolute freedom from all needs (God alone), (2) fewness of needs (the praised "wealth of the soul"), (3) abundance of possessions. The debate here pivots between senses (2) and (3).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — "أغنى عنه" (to be independent of); Metaphorical — "تغنته القيود" (fetters "enriched" him, i.e., clung to him), showing that attachment, not mere possession, is the real issue.
- Root: صبر (ṣād-bā-rā)
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Restraint of the soul in the face of hardship; steadfastness in obedience and abstinence from sin. The "patient poor" (فقير صابر) is the one who holds fast without anxious striving.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — endurance of affliction; the compound "صابر محتسب" (patient and reckoning on God's reward) is the technical Quranic-Hadith register.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — The Prophet's saying {«ليس الغنى عن كثرة العرض إنما الغنى غنى النفس»} uses "إنما" to restrict true wealth to soul-contentment, negating the apparent sense of abundance. This syntactic restriction governs the entire argument: the "wealth" that matters is a state of the heart, not of the purse.
57:21.topic: Al-Ghazali on constant remembrance of God and contemplative invocations, from 'Poverty and Abstinence'

57:21.arabic: تعالى {وفي ذلك فليتنافس المتنافسون} وقال تعالى {سابقوا إلى مغفرة من ربكم} وإنما المسابقة عند خوف الفوت وهو كالعبدين ينسابقان إلى خدمة مولاهما إذ يجزع كل واحد أن يسبقه صاحبه فيحظى عند مولاه بمنزلة لا يحظى هو بها فكيف وقد صرح رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بذلك فقال لا حسد إلا في اثنتين رجل أتاه الله مالا فسلطه على هلكته في الحق ورجل آتاه الله تعالى علما فهو يعمل به ويعلمه الناس (1) حديث أبي كبشة مثل هذه الأمة مثل أربعة رجل أتاه الله مالا الحديث رواه ابن ماجه والترمذي وقال حسن صحيح (2) حديث ثلاث لا ين
57:21.english: The Prophet ﷺ said: «إن المؤمن يغبط والمنافق يحسد» — "The believer aspires emulously, and the hypocrite envies."
57:21.section_title_en: On the Reality of Envy (Ḥasad) and Its Degrees — Section 720
57:21.anchors:
- Root: نعم (n-ʿ-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root meaning of "bounty, benefaction, grace" — that state of goodness and well-being bestowed.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "النعمة: الحالة الحسنة" — bounty is the excellent state/condition; it is the genus term applying to both little and much, as in {«وإن تعدوا نعمة الله لا تحصوها»} [Ibrahim: 34].
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): "جلت نعمة الله ونعماؤه" — bounty as actual bestowed good. Metaphorical (majāz): "خفت نعامتهم" — departure/removal, relevant to the envier's wish for the bounty's removal.
- Root: حسد (ḥ-s-d)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Envy — the desire for removal of another's good.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الحسد: تمني زوال نعمة من مستحق لها" — envy is wishing the removal of bounty from one who deserves it, sometimes accompanied by striving to effect its removal. Cited: «المؤمن يغبط والمنافق يحسد».
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "حسده على نعمة الله" — envying someone for God's bounty. "إن الحسد يأكل الجسد" — envy consumes the body.
- Root: نفس (n-f-s)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The self; also value, preciousness.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): النفس: الروح — the soul/spirit; also الذات (essence/self).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "شيء نفيس ومنفس" — a precious thing. Metaphorical: "دفق نفسه أي دمه" — poured out his self, i.e., his blood. From this root derives المنافسة (emulative competition) — the striving for precious things.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد (Restriction & Specification) — The definition of ḥasad is given as a restricted predication (ḥadd), delimiting its essential meaning: "كراهة النعمة وحب زوالها عن المنعم عليه" — the hatred of bounty and love of its removal from the one upon whom it is bestowed. This is a formal definition (ḥadd), not merely a lexical gloss.
57:21.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'Remembrance of Death and Afterlife'

57:23.arabic: بموجود ولا يحزن على مفقود كما قال تعالى لكيلا تأسوا على ما فاتكم ولا تفرحوا بما آتاكم بل ينبغي أن يكون بالضد من ذلك وهو أن يحزن بوجود المال ويفرح بفقده العلامة الثانية أن يستوي عنده ذامه ومادحه فالأول علامة الزهد في المال والثاني علامة الزهد في الجاه العلامة الثالثة أن يكون أنسه بالله تعالى والغالب على قلبه حلاوة الطاعة إذ لا يخلو القلب عن حلاوة المحبة إما محبة الدنيا وإما محبة الله وهما في القلب كالماء والهواء في القدح فالماء إذا دخل خرج الهواء ولا يجتمعان وكل من أنس بالله اشتغل به ولم يشتغل بغيره ولذلك قيل لبعضهم إلى ماذا أفضى
57:23.english: When it was unveiled to the friends of God (awliyā') — exalted is He — that the servant destroys his own soul by his deeds and his following of his soul's caprice, even as the silkworm destroys itself, they rejected this world (al-dunyā) entirely. Thus al-Hasan said: "I saw seventy of the Badr veterans who were more ascetic (azhad) among what God made lawful for them than you are among what God made unlawful for you." In another wording: "They were more joyful in affliction than you are in comfort and ease. Had you seen them, you would have said: 'They are mad.' And had they seen your righteous ones, they would have said: 'These have no share of goodness.' And had they seen your wicked ones, they would have said: 'These do not believe in the Day of Reckoning.'"
57:23.section_title_en: The Exposition of the Signs of Asceticism (Zuhd)
57:23.anchors:
- Root: زهد (Z-H-D)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root meaning: scarcity, paucity, and abstention; al-zuhd is also "estimation" (al-hazr), as in estimating a palm-crop.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الزهيد: الشيء القليل" — the ascetic (al-zāhid) is one who turns away from a thing, content with the little (al-qalīl) of it. Theological nuance: zuhd is not mere abandonment but a reorientation of desire away from the worldly toward the divine.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Haqiqah (literal): "زهد في الشيء: رغب عنه" — to turn one's desire away from a thing. Majaz (metaphorical): "رجل زهيد: قليل الخير" — a man of little good; "اد زهيد" — a valley that takes little water. Thus, zuhd as a spiritual state is a metaphorical extension of scarcity applied to the heart's attachment.
- Root: قلب (Q-L-B)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The heart (al-qalb); also "turning/transforming a thing from one face to another" (taṣrīf al-shay').
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "قلب الشيء: تصريفه وصرفه عن وجه إلى وجه" — the heart is so named for its constant turning and fluctuation between states; theological nuance: the heart is the seat of volitional orientation, capable of being turned toward or away from God.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Haqiqah: physical overturning. Majaz: "رجل قلب حول: يقلب الأمور ويحتال" — a man who turns matters over and manages them; thus "corruption of the heart" (fasād al-qalb) is a metaphorical overturning of its proper orientation.
- Root: أنس (A-N-S)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Sociability, familiarity, intimacy; al-uns is the opposite of loneliness (al-wahshah).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The soul's tranquility and familiarity with something; theological nuance: al-uns bi-Allāh is the heart's intimate repose in God, exclusive of all else.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Haqiqah: human companionship. Majaz: intimacy with God as the heart's true companionship, displacing worldly attachment.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — The phrase "إنما مسرة أحدهم معرفة الناس حاله" restricts delight solely to public recognition, isolating the motive that invalidates claimed zuhd.
57:23.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Poverty and Abstinence'

57:23.arabic: ومنها أن يتواضع لكل مسلم ولا يتكبر عليه فإن الله لا يحب كل مختال فخور قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إن الله تعالى أوحى إلي أن تواضعوا حتى لا يفخر أحد على أحد (6) ثم إن تفاخر عليه غيره فليحتمل قال الله تعالى لنبيه صلى الله عليه وسلم {خذ العفو وأمر بالعرف وأعرض عن الجاهلين} وعن ابن أبي أوفى كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يتواضع لكل مسلم ولا يأنف ولا يتكبر أن يمشي مع الأرملة والمسكين فيقضي حاجته (7) ومنها أن لا يسمع بلاغات الناس بعضهم على بعض ولا يبلغ بعضهم ما يسمع من بعض قال صلى الله عليه وسلم لا يدخل الجنة
57:23.english: **First**: That you greet him with peace (*salām*) when you meet him, and respond to his invitation when he invites you, and say "may Allah have mercy on you" (*tashmīt*) when he sneezes, and visit him when he is ill, and attend his funeral procession when he dies, and fulfill his oath when he swears by you, and give him sincere counsel when he seeks your advice, and protect him in his absence when he is away from you, and love for him what you love for yourself, and dislike for him what you dislike for yourself. (1)
57:23.section_title_en: The Rights of Brotherhood — Section 433: The Duties of a Muslim Toward His Fellow Muslims
57:23.anchors:
- Root: سلم (s-l-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of safety, security, freedom from harm; the root from which *islām* (submission/surrender) and *salām* (peace) derive
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): *Salām* as the theological state of being secure from harm — both giving and receiving safety; *islām* as the total surrender of the heart to Allah
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (*ḥaqīqah*): physical safety from tongue and hand; Metaphorical (*majāz*): the comprehensive spiritual safety that defines true Muslim brotherhood
- Root: عون (ʿ-w-n)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Assistance, aid, helping another in need
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Mutual assistance as a divine ordinance among believers
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical aid; Metaphorical: intercession (*shafāʿah*) and advocacy on behalf of others
- Root: ستر (s-t-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Covering, concealing, veiling; protection from exposure
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): *Sitr* as the divine attribute of concealment — Allah's covering of sins in this world and the next
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: covering a physical defect; Metaphorical: concealing another's faults and sins — a cardinal virtue of brotherhood
- Root: عذر (ʿ-dh-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Excuse, pardon, acceptance of apology
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): *ʿAfw* (pardon) as the higher station of forgiveness that elevates the forgiver
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: releasing from obligation; Metaphorical: the noble trait of overlooking others' offenses
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد (Restriction & Focused Predication) — The repeated use of restrictive constructions (e.g., "المسلم من سلم المسلمون") establishes definitional boundaries through predicate restriction, indicating that the *ḥaqīqah* of faith is manifested through specific observable actions.
