##
57:23.topic: Al-Ghazali on purifying the character, moral diseases, and spiritual remedies, from 'Duties of Brotherhood'

57:23.arabic: فأما المذموم فكالحزن على ما فات قال الله تعالى لكيلا تأسوا على ما فاتكم والحزن على الأموات من هذا القبيل فإنه تسخط لقضاء الله تعالى وتأسف على ما لا تدارك له فهذا الحزن لما كان مذموما كان تحريكه بالنياحة مذموما فلذلك ورد النهي الصريح عن النياحة (1) وأما الحزن المحمود فهو حزن الإنسان على تقصيره في أمر دينه وبكاؤه على خطاياه والبكاء والتباكي والحزن والتحازن على ذلك محمود وعليه بكاء آدم عليه السلام وتحريك هذا الحزن وتقويته محمود لأنه يبعث على التشمير للتدارك ولذلك كانت نياحة داود عليه السلام محمودة إذ كان ذلك مع
57:23.english: As for the blameworthy, it is like grieving over what has passed away. God — exalted — says: {«...lest you grieve over what has escaped you»} (Q. 57:23). Grieving over the dead belongs to this kind, for it is discontent with God's decree and regret over what cannot be retrieved. Since this grief is blameworthy, stirring it up through wailing is likewise blameworthy. For this reason, the explicit prohibition of wailing (al-niyāḥah) has been transmitted.
57:23.section_title_en: On the Permissible and Forbidden Uses of Melodies, Rhythms, and Mourning Songs — Section 493 of the Book of the Revival of the Religious Sciences
57:23.anchors:
- Root: خدع (kh-d-ʿ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To deceive, delude, or trick; the act of concealing a corrupt intent beneath a fair exterior.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The deception of the lower self (al-ṭabʿ) is its presentation of the forbidden as permissible and the harmful as beneficial, thereby veiling the intellect from the true end.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) refers to actual trickery; metaphorical (majāz) applies to the soul's inclination that "deceives" one into error, as here.
- Root: رجز (r-j-z)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Rhymed, rhythmic verse (rajaz); a metrical form used in battle to spur courage.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Rhythmic utterance intended to stir resolve; its permissibility follows the permissibility of the act it motivates.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the rajaz meter of poetry. Metaphorical: any rhythmic chant (like war-cries) that agitates the soul toward action.
- Root: حزن (ḥ-z-n)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Roughness of the ground; figuratively, the soul's contraction and distress (ghummah).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Grief is a "roughness" of the soul; it is blameworthy when directed at what has passed (i.e., God's decree) and praiseworthy when directed at one's own shortcomings.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical roughness. Metaphorical: a "grieving" voice (ṣawt ḥazīn) is one that is soft and plaintive (rakhīm), which softens the heart.
- Root: ناح (n-w-ḥ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To wail or lament (niyāḥah), specifically for the dead.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The vocalization of grief; its ruling follows the ruling of the grief it expresses or incites.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the act of wailing. Metaphorical: any sound that "mourns" or evokes sorrow.
- Root: طرب (ṭ-r-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Intense joy or agitation of the soul, often accompanied by melody.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): A movement of the soul toward expansion (in joy) or contraction (in sorrow); here, it is the pleasurable agitation excited by song.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the state of being moved. Metaphorical: the "transport" of delight that melodies produce.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Causal Consequence (Ḥukm al-Dalālah ʿalā al-Sabab)
  * The ruling on the means (wasīlah) follows the ruling on the end (maqṣad). Thus, what leads to the forbidden is forbidden, and what leads to the obligatory or commendable is likewise ruled by its consequence. This governs the entire taxonomy of sounds and melodies in this section.
57:23.topic: Al-Ghazali on constant remembrance of God and contemplative invocations, from 'Audition and Ecstasy'

59:8.arabic: أما من الآيات فيدل عليه قوله تعالى {للفقراء المهاجرين الذين أخرجوا من ديارهم وأموالهم} الآية وقال تعالى {للفقراء الذين أحصروا في سبيل الله لا يستطيعون ضربا في الأرض} ساق الكلام في معرض المدح ثم قدم وصفهم بالفقر على وصفهم بالهجرة والإحصار وفيه دلالة ظاهرة على مدح الفقر وأما الأخبار في مدح الفقر فأكثر من أن تحصى روى عبد الله بن عمر رضي الله عنهما قال قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لأصحابه أي الناس خير فقالوا موسر من المال يعطي حق الله من نفسه وماله فقال نعم الرجل هذا وليس به قالوا فمن خير الناس يا رسول الله قال فقير يعطي جهده (4) وق
59:8.english: As for the verses [of the Qur'an], that is indicated by His saying, the Exalted: {«لِلْفُقَرَاءِ الْمُهَاجِرِينَ الَّذِينَ أُخْرِجُوا مِنْ دِيَارِهِمْ وَأَمْوَالِهِمْ»} [To the poor emigrants who were driven out of their homes and their wealth] (59:8), to the end of the verse. And He said, the Exalted: {«لِلْفُقَرَاءِ الَّذِينَ أُحْصِرُوا فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ لَا يَسْتَطِيعُونَ ضَرْبًا فِي الْأَرْضِ»} [To the poor who are confined in the way of Allah, unable to travel in the land] (2:273). He directed the discourse in the context of praise, then He advanced their description with poverty before their description with emigration and confinement. In this there is an evident indication of the praise of poverty.
59:8.section_title_en: The Virtue of Poverty: Scriptural Evidences and Their Interpretation
59:8.anchors:
- Root: فقر (F-Q-R)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of need, indigence, and the state of lacking possessions; also the notches of a vertebra or the joints of the back, indicating structural dependence.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Poverty is of four degrees: (1) essential neediness before God (universal to all creatures), (2) lack of worldly goods (the subject here), (3) voluntary renunciation (zuhd), and (4) the perfection of the heart's detachment. The praise of poverty here targets the second and third degrees, not destitution that breeds discontent.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah) poverty is the absence of wealth; metaphorical (Majaz) poverty is the soul's humility and its "notches" of dependence on God. The Prophet's praise of the "poor" (fuqara') must be read as praise of the virtuous poor (mutafaQQir), not the covetous.
- Root: هجر (H-J-R)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To abandon, emigrate, or sever ties; the act of leaving one's homeland for a religious purpose.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Hijrah (emigration) is a physical act of devotion, but the Quranic verse pairs it with poverty, elevating the state of neediness as a spiritual station above the mere act of relocation.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): The verse's structure (taqdim) places "poverty" before "emigration" and "confinement," signaling its superior rank in the divine estimation.
- Root: قدر (Q-D-R)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Measure, decree, power, and estimation; the act of determining a precise limit or quantity.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): When applied to God, Qadar is His eternal decree; when applied to the Prophet's speech, it denotes precise, divinely-inspired measurement—never arbitrary or haphazard.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: to measure out (qaddara). Metaphorical: the "measure" of a thing's worth or rank. The Prophet's numerical estimates (e.g., 500 years, 46 parts) are literal measures of spiritual realities, though their exact rationale may be hidden from non-prophetic intellects.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — The Quranic construction {للفقراء المهاجرين} uses prepositional fronting (taqdim) to restrict the praise to a specific class, and the sequence of descriptors (poverty before hijrah) establishes a hierarchy of virtues through syntactic ordering.
59:8.topic: Al-Ghazali on constant remembrance of God and contemplative invocations, from 'Poverty and Abstinence'

62:4.arabic: وإن اشتركوا في مصيبة الحرمان من حقيقة الأمر فالحقيقة فضل الله يؤتيه من يشاء والله ذو الفضل العظيم وحكمته يختص بها من يشاء ومن يؤت الحكمة فقد أوتي خيرا كثيرا ولنعد إلى الغرض فقد أرخينا الطول وطولنا النفس في أمر هو أعلاى من علوم المعاملات التي نقصدها في هذا الكتاب فقد ظهر أن رتبة الهلاك ليس إلا للجهال المكذبين وشهادة ذلك من كتاب الله وسنة رسوله صلى الله عليه وسلم لا تدخل تحت الحصر فلذلك لم نوردها الرتبة الثانية رتبة المعذبين وهذه رتبة من تحلى بأصل الإيمان ولكن قصر في الوفاء بمقتضاه فإن رأس الإيمان هو التوحيد وهو أن لا يعبد
62:4.english: The fire of Hell is the coldest of fires [in comparison to the fire of separation]. And you should not deny this in the world of the Hereafter, for it has a witnessed parallel in the world of this world. Indeed, one has been seen who was overcome by ecstasy (wajd) and walked upon fire and upon the roots of cane, his feet being cut, yet he did not feel it, due to the extreme dominance of what was in his heart. And you see the angry man, when anger overcomes him in battle, receiving wounds and not feeling them at that moment, because anger is a fire in the heart. The Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, said: {«الغضب قطعة من النار»} "Anger is a piece of fire." The burning of the heart (iḥtirāq al-fu'ād) is more severe than the burning of bodies, and the more severe annuls the sensation of the weaker, as you observe. For destruction from fire and the sword is only inasmuch as they separate between two parts that are linked one to the other by the bond of composition (ta'līf) possible in bodies. So that which separates between the heart and its Beloved, to which it is linked by a bond of composition far more firm than the composition of bodies, is more intensely painful—if you are among the people of insight (abṣār) and the people of hearts. And it is not far-fetched that he who has no heart should not perceive the severity of this pain and should deem it trivial in comparison to bodily pain. For a boy, if he were given the choice between the pain of being deprived of a ball and a polo-stick, and the pain of being deprived of the rank of a Sultan, he would not feel the pain of deprivation from the Sultan's rank at all, nor would he count that as a pain. And the enemy in the field with the polo-stick is more beloved to him than a thousand thrones of the Sultan with sitting upon them. Nay, even one overcome by the lust of the belly, if given the choice between porridge (harīsah) and sweets (ḥalwā) and between a beautiful deed by which he conquers enemies and delights friends, he would prefer the porridge and sweets. All of this is due to the absence of the meaning (maʿnā) by whose existence rank becomes beloved, and the presence of the meaning by whose existence food becomes delicious. This is for one whom the attributes of beasts and predators have enslaved, and in whom the attributes of the angels have not appeared—those attributes which are not suited by, nor delight in, anything but proximity to the Lord of the Worlds, and which are pained only by distance and the veil (ḥijāb). And just as taste is only in the tongue and hearing only in the ears, so this attribute is only in the heart. So he who has no heart has no such sense, like he who has no hearing or sight has no pleasure in melodies or the beauty of forms and colors. And not every human has a heart; were it so, the saying of God, Most High, would not be sound: {«إن في ذلك لذكرى لمن كان له قلب»} "Indeed in that is a reminder for whoever has a heart" (Q. 50:37). Thus He made the one who does not heed the Quran devoid of a heart. And by "heart" I do not mean this [organ] which the ribs of the chest encompass. Rather, I mean the secret (sirr) which is of the world of the Command (ʿālam al-amr). The flesh which is of the world of Creation (ʿālam al-khalq) is its Throne (ʿarsh), the chest is its Footstool (kursī), and the rest of the limbs are its domain and kingdom. And to God belongs the Creation and the Command altogether. But that secret, concerning which God, Most High, said: {«قل الروح من أمر ربي»} "Say: The Spirit is of the Command of my Lord" (Q. 17:85), is the commander and the king, because between the world of the Command and the world of Creation there is an ordering, and the world of the Command is commander over the world of Creation. It is the subtle divine reality (al-laṭīfah) which, when it is sound, the rest of the body is sound for its sake. Whoever knows it has known his own self, and whoever knows his own self has known his Lord. At that point, the servant smells the beginnings of the fragrance of the meaning folded under his saying, peace and blessings be upon him: {«إن الله خلق آدم على صورته»} "God created Adam upon His image." He looks with the eye of mercy upon those who adhere to its literal wording and upon those who are obstinate in the path of its interpretation (ta'wīl). And even though His mercy for those adhering to the letter is greater than His mercy for the obstinate interpreters, because mercy is proportional to the affliction, and the affliction of those [literalists] is greater—even if they share in the affliction of being deprived of the reality of the matter—for the Reality (al-ḥaqīqah) is the bounty of God which He gives to whom He wills, and God is the Possessor of Great Bounty. And His Wisdom is singled out for whom He wills: {«ومن يؤت الحكمة فقد أوتي خيرا كثيرا»} "And whoever is given wisdom has been given much good" (Q. 2:269). Let us return to the purpose, for we have drawn out the length and lengthened the breath in a matter that is higher than the sciences of transactions (muʿāmalāt) which we intend in this book. It has become clear that the rank of destruction is only for the ignorant deniers. And the testimony of that from the Book of God and the Sunnah of His Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, is beyond enumeration, so we have not cited it.
62:4.section_title_en: The Ranks of the Hereafter: On the Distribution of Degrees and the States of the Saved, the Punished, and the Victorious
62:4.anchors:
- Root: ح ر ق (ḥ-r-q)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of burning, scorching, and the fire's consumption of its fuel.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The fire of the Hereafter (Nār) is a created reality, but its perception is tied to the spiritual state of the perceiver.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah) for physical burning; metaphorical (Majaz) for the burning of the heart (iḥtirāq al-fu'ād) by overwhelming love or anger.
- Root: ق ل ب (q-l-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To turn, overturn, or transform a thing from one state to another.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The heart (Qalb) is the seat of perception and understanding, distinct from the physical organ.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal for the physical heart; metaphorical for the spiritual subtlety (Laṭīfah) that is the locus of divine knowledge and love.
- Root: ع ل م (ʿ-l-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To know, to perceive a thing by its true nature.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Knowledge (ʿIlm) is the apprehension of a thing's reality, which is the basis for distinguishing the ranks of the believers.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal for acquired knowledge; metaphorical for the "unveiling" (Kashf) knowledge granted to the knowers (ʿĀrifūn).
- Sibawayh Rule: Restriction and Specification (Bāb al-Ḥaṣr wa al-Taqyīd bi-innamā) — Used to distinguish the specific referents of terms like "heart" (Qalb) and "faith" (Īmān), ensuring the precise meaning is not conflated with common usage.
62:4.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Poverty and Abstinence'

62:4.arabic: فقال صلى الله عليه وسلم ذلك فضل الله يؤتيه من يشاء (1) وقد استشهد ابن عطاء أيضا لما سئل عن ذلك فقال الغني أفضل لأنه وصف الحق أما دليله الأول ففيه نظر لأن الخبر قد ورد مفصلا تفصيلا يدل على خلاف ذلك وهو أن ثواب الفقير في التسبيح يزيد على ثواب الغني وأن فوزهم بذلك الثواب فضل الله يؤتيه من يشاء فقد روى زيد بن أسلم عن أنس بن مالك رضي الله عنه قال بعث الفقراء رسولا إلا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال إني رسول الفقراء إليك فقال {مرحبا} بك وبمن جئت من عندهم قوم أحبهم قال قالوا يا رسول الله إن
62:4.english: Evidence for this may be found in what is related in the report (khabar) that the poor complained to the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, that the rich had preceded them in good deeds, alms, pilgrimage (ḥajj), and holy struggle (jihād). So he taught them words of glorification (tasbīḥ) and told them that by these they would attain what surpassed what the rich had attained. Then the rich learned these words and began to say them, so the poor returned to the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, and informed him [of this]. He said, peace and blessings be upon him: {«ذلك فضل الله يؤتيه من يشاء»} — "That is the bounty of God; He gives it to whom He wills." (1)
62:4.section_title_en: On the Relative Excellence of Poverty and Wealth — A Detailed Exposition
62:4.anchors:
- Root: فقر (fa-qā-rā)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of neediness, destitution; the state of one lacking provision or means.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Fourfold division — (1) essential need before God (universal to all creatures), (2) lack of acquired possessions, (3) contentment of the soul, (4) metaphorical usage. Here, the operative sense is the second: absence of worldly goods.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah) — absence of wealth; Metaphorical (Majaz) — "فقرة الكلام" (a rhetorical gem/point), showing the root's capacity for extension. The discussion here remains in the literal register of material need.
- Root: غني (ghayn-nūn-yā)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of sufficiency, independence, freedom from need.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Threefold division — (1) absolute freedom from all needs (God alone), (2) fewness of needs (the praised "wealth of the soul"), (3) abundance of possessions. The debate here pivots between senses (2) and (3).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — "أغنى عنه" (to be independent of); Metaphorical — "تغنته القيود" (fetters "enriched" him, i.e., clung to him), showing that attachment, not mere possession, is the real issue.
- Root: صبر (ṣād-bā-rā)
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Restraint of the soul in the face of hardship; steadfastness in obedience and abstinence from sin. The "patient poor" (فقير صابر) is the one who holds fast without anxious striving.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — endurance of affliction; the compound "صابر محتسب" (patient and reckoning on God's reward) is the technical Quranic-Hadith register.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — The Prophet's saying {«ليس الغنى عن كثرة العرض إنما الغنى غنى النفس»} uses "إنما" to restrict true wealth to soul-contentment, negating the apparent sense of abundance. This syntactic restriction governs the entire argument: the "wealth" that matters is a state of the heart, not of the purse.
62:4.topic: Al-Ghazali on constant remembrance of God and contemplative invocations, from 'Poverty and Abstinence'

62:8.arabic: قال الله فيهم قل إن الموت الذي تفرون منه فإنه ملاقيكم ثم تردون إلى عالم الغيب والشهادة فينبئكم بما كنتم تعملون ثم الناس إما منهمك وإما تائب مبتدئ أو عارف منته أما المنهمك فلا يذكر الموت وإن ذكره فيذكره للتأسف على دنياه ويشتغل بمذمته وهذا يزيده ذكر الموت من الله بعدا وأما التائب فإنه يكثر من ذكر الموت لينبعث به من قلبه الخوف والخشية فيفي بتمام التوبة وربما يكره الموت خيفة من أن يختطفه قبل تمام التوبة وقبل إصلاح الزاد وهو معذور في كراهة الموت ولا يدخل هذا تحت قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم من كره لقاء الله كره الله لقاءه (2) فإن هذا ليس يكره الموت ولقاء ا
62:8.english: Know that the one engrossed in this world, bent over its delusions, loving its lusts — his heart is inevitably heedless of the remembrance of death, so he does not remember it. And when he is reminded of it, he detests it and recoils from it. These are they of whom God said: {«قُلْ إِنَّ الْمَوْتَ الَّذِي تَفِرُّونَ مِنْهُ فَإِنَّهُ مُلَاقِيكُمْ ثُمَّ تُرَدُّونَ إِلَىٰ عَالِمِ الْغَيْبِ وَالشَّهَادَةِ فَيُنَبِّئُكُم بِمَا كُنتُمْ تَعْمَلُونَ»} — "Say: Indeed, the death from which you flee — it will surely meet you. Then you will be returned to the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, and He will inform you of what you used to do." Then people are either one engrossed [in the world], or a penitent beginner, or a gnostic who has reached the end.
62:8.section_title_en: The Book of the Remembrance of Death — Section 1282: The First Part on Its Premises and Consequences up to the Blast of the Trumpet, Containing Eight Chapters
62:8.anchors:
- Root: موت (m-w-t)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of death as the cessation of life; Al-Khalil notes its usage as a natural disposition (ka-l-ṭabīʿah fīhā), with derivatives like *mayyit* (dead), *mawtān* (deathly state).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Death is the opposite of life; in theological terms, it is the separation of the soul from the body, and the Quranic usage extends to spiritual death — the heart's heedlessness of God.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (*ḥaqīqah*): physical death and dying. Metaphorical (*majāz*): "reviving the dead land" (i.e., barren earth) and "dead-hearted" man — one lacking spiritual vitality.
- Root: ذكر (dh-k-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Remembrance, recollection, and mention; also used for praise and invocation.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): *Dhikr* is the presence of a thing in the mind; in the Quranic context, it is the heart's vigilance against forgetfulness (*nisyān*), and its highest form is the constant awareness of God.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: verbal mention. Metaphorical: inward remembrance that produces fear and longing — as in the *dhikr* of death stirring the heart.
- Root: توب (t-w-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Return (*rujūʿ*) from sin; the penitent (*tāʾib*) is one who turns back to God.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): *Tawbah* is returning from error to obedience, requiring three elements: remorse, cessation, and resolve. Its completion (*tamām*) is the state of unwavering commitment.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: turning back. Metaphorical: the soul's aversion from worldly allurements toward the divine presence.
- Root: عرف (ʿ-r-f)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Knowledge, acquaintance, and recognition; *ʿārif* is one who knows by direct experience.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): *Maʿrifah* is the soul's apprehension of realities; the *ʿārif* (gnostic) is one whose knowledge has become a settled state of witnessing, not mere report.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: knowing something after ignorance. Metaphorical: the *ʿārif* who "knows" death as the tryst with the Beloved — knowledge transmuted into love.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — The particle *innamā* restricts predication to a single subject, as in "إنما يخاف فوت لقاء الله" — confining the penitent's fear solely to missing the divine encounter, not to death itself.
62:8.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Remembrance of Death and Afterlife'

62:8.arabic: وأما المنافقون ففروا من الزحف خوفا من الموت فقيل لهم إن الموت الذين تفرون منه فإنه ملاقيكم فإيثارهم البقاء على الشهادة استبدال الذي هو أدنى بالذي هو خير فأولئك الذين اشتروا الضلالة بالهدى فما ربحت تجارتهم وما كانوا مهتدين وأما المخلصون فإن الله تعالى اشترى منهم أنفسهم وأموالهم بأن لهم الجنة فلما رأوا أنهم تركوا تمتع عشرين سنة مثلا أو ثلاثين سنة بتمتع الأبد استبشروا ببيعهم الذي بايعوا به فهذا بيان المزهود فيه وإذا فهمت هذا علمت أن ما ذكره المتكلمون في حد الزهد لم يشيروا به إلا إلى بعض أقسامه فذكر كل واحد منهم ما رآه غالبا على نف
62:8.english: ...or the attainment of the rank of martyrdom (al-shahādah). And whosoever among them died upon his bed would grieve bitterly over the loss of martyrdom — so much so that Khālid ibn al-Walīd, may Allah Most High be well pleased with him, when death approached him upon his bed, kept saying: "How often did I deceive my soul [into battle], and charge upon the ranks, coveting martyrdom — and now I die the death of old women!" When he died, eight hundred wounds from the marks of injuries were counted upon his body. Such was the state of the truthful ones in faith — may Allah Most High be well pleased with them all.
62:8.section_title_en: Exposition of the Degrees of Asceticism (Zuhd) and Its Divisions — Relative to Itself, to That Which Is Renounced, and to That Which Is Sought
62:8.anchors:
- Root: زهد (Z-H-D)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root meaning: scarcity, paucity, and abstemiousness; al-zuhd is also "estimation/assessment" (al-hazr), as in assessing a palm-crop.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الزهيد: الشيء القليل" — the ascetic (al-zāhid) is one who turns away from a thing, content with the little (al-qalīl) thereof; theological nuance: renunciation is a voluntary contentment with the lesser in exchange for the greater.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Haqiqah (literal): "زهد في الشيء: رغب عنه" — to turn away from a thing with aversion. Majaz (metaphorical): "رجل زهيد: قليل الخير" — a man of little good; "اد زهيد" — a valley that takes little water. Thus zuhd is literal renunciation, but its degrees vary by the object renounced.
- Root: قصر (Q-S-R)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To restrain, confine, hold back; also shortness as opposed to length.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "القصر: خلاف الطول" — shortness is the opposite of length; both are relative terms (mutadāyifān) defined by comparison to another.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Haqiqah: "قصرته: حبسته" — I restrained him. "وقصرت نفسي على هذا الأمر" — I confined myself to this matter, not aspiring beyond it. Majaz: "أقصر المطر: أقلع" — the rain ceased; "قصر الأمل" — the shortening of hope/aspiration, a metaphorical restraint of the soul's reach.
- Root: نفس (N-F-S)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The self, the soul; that which one desires to be near.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "النفس: الروح" — the soul is the spirit; in divine attribution, "نفسه" denotes His very essence (dhāt), not a separate entity.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Haqiqah: "شيء نفيس" — a precious thing. Majaz: "دفق نفسه أي دمه" — "he poured out his self" meaning his blood; thus nafs can denote the entire vital being given in sacrifice.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد (Restriction and Specification) — When multiple predicates are attributed to a single subject (zuhd), each speaker's definition is a restricted specification (takhṣīṣ) of one division, not a comprehensive definition (ḥadd) of the whole genus. The syntactic pattern "إنما هو كذا" effects exclusive predication, signaling partial scope.
62:8.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Poverty and Abstinence'

65:7.arabic: هذا الرجل واجب أن يقضى من مال بيت المال ومن الزكاة وقد قال تعالى ومن قدر عليه رزقه فلينفق مما آتاه الله قيل معناه ليبع أحد ثوبيه وقيل معناه فليستقرض بجاهه فذلك مما آتاه الله وقال بعضهم إن لله تعالى عبادا ينفقون على قدر بضائعهم ولله عباد ينفقون على قدر حسن الظن بالله تعالى ومات بعضهم فأوصى بماله لثلاث طوائف الأقوياء والأسخياء والأغنياء فقيل من هؤلاء فقال أما الأقوياء فهم أهل التوكل على الله تعالى وأما الأسخياء فهم أهل حسن الظن بالله تعالى وأما الأغنياء فهم أهل الانقطاع إلى الله تعالى فإذن مهما وجدت هذه الشروط فيه وفي المال وفي المعطي فليأخ
65:7.english: And one of those residing near the Sacred House [in Mecca] said: I had with me some dirhams which I had set aside for spending in the path of God. Then I heard a poor man who had finished his circumambulation (tawaf) saying in a faint voice: "I am hungry as you see, naked as you see — so what do you see in what you see, O He who sees and is not seen?" I looked and saw upon him two worn garments that scarcely concealed him. I said to myself: I find no place for my dirhams more excellent than this. So I carried them to him. He looked at them, then took from them five dirhams and said: "Four are the price of two waist-wrappers, and one dirham I shall spend — three [remain]. I have no need of the rest," and he returned them. He said: Then I saw him the second night wearing two new waist-wrappers. Something stirred within me concerning him, so he turned to me, took my hand, and made me circumambulate with him for a week — every circuit of it upon gems from the mines of the earth, crunching beneath our feet up to the ankles — among them gold, silver, ruby, pearl, and precious stone — and this was not shown to the people. He said: "All of this has been given to me, and I have renounced it, and I take from the hands of creatures — because these are burdens and tribulation, while for the servants therein is mercy and grace."
65:7.section_title_en: On the Perils of Accepting Excess Wealth and the Discipline of Contentment — Section 1080
65:7.anchors:
- Root: أ-خ-ذ (akhadha)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of taking, seizing, accepting with the hand; implies volitional acquisition.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In theological context, taking (akhdh) is tied to what is lawfully permitted (halal) versus what carries spiritual liability; the act itself is neutral, its moral weight determined by intention and need.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (haqiqah) — physical taking; metaphorical (majaz) — accepting provision as from God, not from the intermediary agent.
- Root: ف-ت-ن (fatanah)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Trial, affliction, testing; originally from burning (fatn) — the fire that tests gold.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Ibtila' (trial) is God's testing of the servant's obedience; the trial is not for God's knowledge but for the servant's self-disclosure and recompense.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — smelting to purify; metaphorical — wealth as a trial that reveals whether one acts with gratitude or ingratitude.
- Root: ز-ه-د (zuhd)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Abstinence, renunciation, regarding something as insignificant.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Zuhd is not the absence of wealth but the absence of attachment in the heart; it is a station of the soul, not a condition of the purse.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — turning away from; metaphorical — taking wealth only to discharge it immediately to the needy, which is the zenith of zuhd.
- Root: ر-ف-ق (rifq)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Gentleness, ease, kindness; the opposite of harshness (unf).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): God's rifq with the servant is sending provision exactly sufficient to need, without surplus that would burden accountability.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — softness in manner; metaphorical — divine gentleness in apportioning sustenance.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — The Prophet's statement «لا حق لابن آدم إلا في ثلاث» restricts rightful claim exclusively to three categories, and the subsequent "فما زاد فهو حساب" is a conditional consequent establishing a universal ruling on surplus.
65:7.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'Poverty and Abstinence'

79:40.arabic: تحمل عليه يلهث أو تتركه يلهث وقال عز وجل فيمن نهى النفس عن الهوى وأما من خاف مقام ربه ونهى النفس عن الهوى فإن الجنة هي المأوى وسيأتي كيفية مجاهدة هذه الجنود وتسليط بعضها على بعض في كتاب رياضة النفس إن شاء الله تعالى المثال الثاني اعلم أن البدن كالمدينة والعقل أعني المدرك من الإنسان كملك مدبر لها وقواه المدركة من الحواس الظاهرة والباطنة كجنوده وأعوانه وأعضاؤه كرعيته والنفس الأمارة بالسوء التي هي الشهوة والغضب كعدو ينازعه في مملكته ويسعى في إهلاك رعيته فصار بدنه كرباط وثغر ونفسه كمقيم فيه مرابط فإن هو جاهد عدوه وهزمه وقهره على ما يحب حمد أثره وإذا عاد إلى الحضرة كما قال ا
79:40.english: But whoever turns away from this path is like the one of whom Allah, the Exalted, said: {أفرأيت من اتخذ إلهه هواه وأضله الله على علم} — "Have you seen the one who takes as his god his own desire, and Allah has led him astray out of knowledge?" (Q 45:23). And He, the Exalted, said: {واتبع هواه فمثله كمثل الكلب إن تحمل عليه يلهث أو تتركه يلهث} — "And he followed his desire, so his example is like the example of a dog: if you drive him away, he pants, or if you leave him, he pants" (Q 7:176). And He, the Exalted and Glorious, said concerning the one who restrains the soul from passion: {وأما من خاف مقام ربه ونهى النفس عن الهوى فإن الجنة هي المأوى} — "But as for he who feared the standing before his Lord and restrained the soul from passion, then indeed, Paradise will be the refuge" (Q 79:40-41).
79:40.section_title_en: ** The Body as Kingdom: The Governance of the Soul's Faculties — Section 577
79:40.anchors:
**
- Root: نفس (n-f-s)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The self, soul, breath; that which is breathed forth; the essence of a thing
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): النفس: الروح — the soul as the immaterial spiritual reality; when attributed to Allah, denotes His very essence (al-dhāt), not a separate entity
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the self/essence; Metaphorical: نفس سائلة — a "flowing self" (blood) as the criterion for ritual purity
- Root: عقل (ʿ-q-l)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Intellect, reason; that which restrains and binds
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): العقل يقال للقوة المتهيئة لقبول العلم — the faculty prepared for receiving knowledge; and the knowledge acquired through that faculty
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: intellectual apprehension; Metaphorical: نخلة لا تعقل الإبار — a palm that does not "accept" pollination (i.e., does not receive)
- Root: غضب (gh-d-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Anger, wrath; the boiling of the blood of the heart desiring vengeance
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): ثوران دم القلب إرادة الانتقام — when attributed to Allah, it means retribution alone, not an emotional state
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: anger toward the living (غضبت لفلان); Metaphorical: anger toward the dead (غضبت به) — the preposition shift marking the distinction
- Root: نصح (n-s-ḥ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Sincere counsel; to be pure and unadulterated; to sew (as a tailor)
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): تحري فعل أو قول فيه صلاح صاحبه — the earnest pursuit of action or speech containing the welfare of its recipient
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: sincere advice; Metaphorical: نصح الغيث البلاد — rain "counseling" the land (i.e., giving it its due generously)
- Sibawayh Rule: باب التشبيه التمثيلي (The Chapter of Illustrative Simile) — extended analogical comparisons (tamthīl) where multiple relations are mapped across domains, governed by the syntactic pattern of predicate assignment (isnād) to establish parallel structures

79:40.arabic: الله عز وجل وأما من خاف مقام ربه ونهى النفس عن الهوى فإن الجنة هي المأوى فعلمت أن قوله سبحانه وتعالى هو الحق فأجهدت نفسي في دفع الهوى حتى استقرت على طاعة الله تعالى الثالثة أني نظرت إلى هذا الخلق فرأيت كل ممن معه شيء له قيمة ومقدار رفعه وحفظه ثم نظرت إلى قول الله عز وجل ما عندكم ينفذ وما عند الله باق فكلما وقع معي شيء له قيمة ومقدار وجهته إلى الله ليبقى عنده محفوظا الرابعة أني نظرت إلى هذا الخلق فرأيت كل واحد منهم يرجع إلى المال وإلى الحسب والشرف والنسب فنظرت فيها فإذا هي لا شيء ثم نظرت إلى قول الله تعالى إن أكرمك
79:40.english: Know that the scholar who does not act upon his knowledge is condemned by the Book, the Sunnah, and the sayings of the sages. God, exalted be He, said: {«يا أيها الذين آمنوا لم تقولون ما لا تفعلون * كبر مقتا عند الله أن تقولوا ما لا تفعلون»} ("O you who believe, why do you say what you do not do? Most hateful it is to God that you say what you do not do"). And He said: {«أتأمرون الناس بالبر وتنسون أنفسكم»} ("Do you command people to righteousness while you forget yourselves?"). And He said: {«ومن الناس من يعجبك قوله في الحياة الدنيا ويشهد الله على ما في قلبه وهو ألد الخصام»} ("And among people is he whose speech pleases you in the worldly life, and he calls God to witness what is in his heart, yet he is the fiercest of opponents").

80:1.arabic: قريش فشق ذلك على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فأنزل الله تعالى عبس وتولى أن جاءه الأعمى وما يدريك لعله يزكى أو يذكر فتنفعه الذكرى يعني ابن مكتوم أما من استغنى فأنت له تصدى (4) يعني هذا الشريف وعن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال يؤتى بالعبد يوم القيامة فيعتذر الله تعالى إليه كما يعتذر الرجل للرجل في الدنيا فيقول وعزتي وجلالي ما زويت الدنيا عنك لهوانك علي ولكن لما أعددت لك من الكرامة والفضيلة اخرج يا عبدي إلى هذه الصفوف فمن أطعمك في أو كساك في يريد بذلك وجهي فخذ بيده فهو لك والناس يومئذ قد ألجمهم العرق فيتخلل الصفوف وينظر من فعل ذلك به فيأخذ بيده ويدخله الجنة // حديث يؤتى بال
80:1.english: The Messiah, peace be upon him, said: "With difficulty shall the rich man enter Paradise."
80:1.section_title_en: The Virtue of Poverty and the Condemnation of Wealth — Section 1071
80:1.anchors:
- Root: دخل (dakhala)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of entering, penetrating, or intruding into a space or state.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Often used for entering into a condition or abode, including the afterlife states of Paradise and Hell.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal for physical entry; metaphorical for entering into a spiritual state or reckoning.
- Root: فقر (faqara)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To hollow out, pierce, or be in a state of neediness; the poor one is "hollowed" of worldly goods.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Denotes the state of one lacking sufficient means; in the Kalam context, it signifies a spiritual station of utter dependence upon God, not merely material lack.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal for material destitution; metaphorical for the soul's essential neediness before its Lord.
- Root: غني (ghaniya)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To be rich, self-sufficient, or free from need.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In theological terms, absolute Ghina (Self-Sufficiency) belongs to God alone; human wealth is a relative accident (ʿaraḍ) that often breeds heedlessness.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal for possessing abundance; metaphorical for the false sense of independence that veils one from God.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Prepositional Interposition (باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور) — Governing the syntactic flow of conditional and circumstantial clauses, ensuring the periodic structure of the narrative remains unbroken across multiple embedded quotations.

83:15.arabic: قال الله تعلى كلا إنهم عن ربهم يومئذ لمحجوبون ثم إنهم لصالوا الجحيم فرتب العذاب بالنار على ألم الحجاب وألم الحجاب كاف من غير علاوة النار فكيف إذا أضيفت العلاوة إليه فنسأل الله تعالى أن يقرر في أسماعنا ما نفث في روع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم حيث قيل له أحبب من أحببت فإنك مفارقه (1) وفي معنى ما ذكرناه من المثال قول الشاعر كدود كدود القز ينسج دائما .
83:15.english: As for the one who restricts himself to the measure of necessity and the essential — he cannot be attributed to the world (al-dunyā). Rather, that measure of the world is precisely the essence of religion (dīn), because it is a condition for religion, and the condition is part of the conditioned. Evidence for this is what has been related: that Abraham, the Friend (al-Khalīl), peace be upon him, was struck by a need, so he went to a friend of his to borrow something from him, but he did not lend him. He returned distressed, and God — exalted be He — revealed to him: "Had you asked My Friend, He would have given you." He said: "O Lord, I knew Your wrath against the world, so I feared to ask You for anything of it." Then God — exalted be He — revealed to him: "Need is not of the world." Thus, the measure of need is of religion. Whatever is beyond that is a burden (wabāl) in the Hereafter, and in this world as well it is likewise — known to whoever examines the conditions of the rich and what they endure of tribulation in earning wealth, amassing it, guarding it, enduring humiliation in it, and the utmost of their happiness with it being that it is handed over to their heirs, who eat of it — and perhaps they are enemies of them, and perhaps they use it to aid them in disobedience, so that he becomes their helper in it. For this reason, the collector of the world and the follower of lusts is likened to the silk-worm (dūd al-qazz): it ceaselessly spins upon itself a thread, then it seeks to emerge but finds no escape, so it dies and perishes because of the work it wrought upon itself. Likewise, whoever follows the lusts of the world — he only fastens upon his heart chains that bind him to what he desires, until the chains accumulate upon him: wealth binds him, and status, and family, and children, and the gloating of enemies, and the ostentation of friends, and the rest of the shares of the world. If it occurs to him that he has erred in this, and he resolves to exit the world, he cannot do so; he sees his heart bound with chains and fetters that he cannot cut. And if he abandons one beloved of his beloveds by his own choice, he nearly kills himself and strives toward his own destruction — until the Angel of Death separates him from all of them at once.
83:15.section_title_en: The Middle Path Between Poison and Remedy: The Necessity of Restraint and the Peril of Attachment to the World
83:15.anchors:
- Root: ن-ف-ع (N-F-ʿ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of benefit, utility, and that which yields advantage; opposed to ḍarar (harm).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: benefit (nafʿ) is that which brings one nearer to God or secures one's ultimate felicity; harm is its opposite in the scale of the Hereafter.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): physical or material utility; metaphorical (majāz): spiritual benefit accruing to the heart and soul.
- Root: ض-ر-ر (Ḍ-R-R)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Harm, injury, distress; the opposite of nafʿ; also denotes constriction and hardship.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In Kalam usage, ḍarar is that which obstructs the soul's journey toward God or corrupts its state.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: bodily or worldly injury; metaphorical: that which damages one's religious state (dīn) or severs one from divine proximity.
- Root: ح-ج-ب (Ḥ-J-B)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Veiling, screening, concealing; the barrier that prevents vision or access.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological: the veil (ḥijāb) separating the creature from the Creator; the state of being veiled (maḥjūb) from God is the essence of divine wrath and the precondition for the Fire's dominion.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: a physical curtain; metaphorical: the spiritual obstruction of the heart from the vision of God, as in the Quranic verse cited.
- Root: ق-ز-ز (Q-Z-Z) [as in دود القز — silk worm]
  * Lisan / Ayn: The silk-worm (dūd al-qazz); its action of spinning silk thread around itself.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Used as a parable (mathal) for the soul that weaves its own bonds of worldly attachment until it is trapped.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Metaphorical: the worm's self-imposed cocoon parallels the sinner's self-forged chains of desire; the imagery is purely figurative, not literal.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Restriction and Focused Predication (باب الحصر والتقييد) — Governing the conditional and exceptive structures (e.g., "فمن احتاط فإنما يحتاط لنفسه") where the predicate is restricted to the subject's own benefit or harm, emphasizing moral self-accountability.

98:8.arabic: وقال عز وجل {رضي الله عنهم ورضوا عنه ذلك لمن خشي ربه} وكل ما دل على فضيلة العلم دل على فضيلة الخوف لأن الخوف ثمرة العلم ولذلك جاء في خبر موسى عليه أفضل الصلاة والسلام وأما الخائفون
98:8.english: As for the path of derivation (iqtibās) from the verses and reports, what has been transmitted concerning the virtue of fear is beyond enumeration. And sufficient as an indication of its virtue is that God—may He be exalted—has gathered together for the fearful (khāʾifūn) guidance (hudā), mercy (raḥmah), knowledge (ʿilm), and good pleasure (riḍwān)—and these are the sum total of the stations of the people of Paradise. God—may He be exalted—said: {وهدى ورحمة للذين هم لربهم يرهبون} "And guidance and mercy for those who of their Lord are fearful" [Al-Aʿrāf: 154]. And He—exalted is He—said: {إنما يخشى الله من عباده العلماء} "Only those of His servants who possess knowledge fear God" [Fāṭir: 28]—describing them with knowledge on account of their fear [of Him].
98:8.section_title_en: Exposition of the Virtue of Fear (Khawf) and Encouragement Thereof
98:8.anchors:
- Root: خوف (Khawf)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root denotes trepidation, apprehension, and the state of being overtaken by dread of a feared outcome.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الخوف: توقع مكروه عن أمارة مظنونة، أو معلومة" — the anticipation of something detestable based on a probable or certain indication; it is the direct opposite of amn (security) and applies to both worldly and otherworldly matters.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): "خفته على مالي خوفا وخيفة" — fearing for something. Metaphorical (Majaz): "تخوفه: تنقصه" — to diminish gradually, as fear consumes the soul piecemeal.
- Root: فضل (Fadl)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Excess, superiority, or merit beyond the baseline of sufficiency.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الفضل: الزيادة عن الاقتصاد" — increase beyond moderation; the praiseworthy type is like the surplus of knowledge and forbearance, and it is measured by its end (ghāyah).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "مال فلان فاضل: كثير يفضل عن القوت" — surplus wealth exceeding necessity. The virtue of a thing is gauged by its instrumental efficacy toward a noble goal.
- Root: علم (ʿIlm)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Certain cognition and apprehension of a thing as it truly is.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "العلم: إدراك الشيء بحقيقته" — apprehension of a thing's reality; it is the root from which khawf branches as its fruit.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "ما علمت بخبرك: ما شعرت به" — to have cognizance. The scholars (ʿulamāʾ) are so named for their knowledge, which necessarily engenders fear of God.
- Sibawayh Rule: Restriction and Focused Predication (باب الحصر والتقييد) — governing the exclusive attribution in {إنما يخشى الله من عباده العلماء}, where the predicate restricts fear to the knowledgeable, and the syntactic fronting of "whom they fear" (لربهم يرهبون) emphasizes the object of reverential dread.

2:22.arabic: مناكبها وقال تعالى الذى جعل لكم الأرض فراشا وقد أكثر فى كتابه العزيز ممن ذكر الأرض ليتفكر في عجائبها فظهرها مقر للأحياء وبطنها مرقد للأموات قال تعالى ألم نجعل الأرض كفاتا أحياء وأمواتا فانظر إلى الأرض وهى ميتة فإذا أنزل عليها الماء اهتزت وربت واخضرت وأنبتت عجائب النبات وخرجت منها أصناف الحيوانات ثم انظر كيف أحكم جوانب الأرض بالجبال الراسيات الشوامخ الصم الصلاب وكيف أودع المياه تحتها ففجر العيون وأسال الأنهار تجري على وجهها وأخرج من الحجارة اليابسة ومن التراب الكدر ماء رقيقا عذبا صافيا زلا
2:22.english: For the beast has no power over that; but as for man, God created for him the power, then he disabled it and disbelieved in God's grace therein. So those are like cattle — nay, they are even further astray from the way {فَأُولَٰئِكَ كَالْأَنْعَامِ بَلْ هُمْ أَضَلُّ سَبِيلًا}.
2:22.section_title_en: On Contemplating the Earth, Its Rivers, Mountains, and Minerals — Section 1273
2:22.anchors:
- Root: فكر (f-k-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: التفكر: تأمل القلب وتدبر الشيء، والفكر: إعمال النظر في الشيء
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): الفكر: قوة العلم التي بها يدرك الإنسان، وقيل: هو ترتيب أمور معلومة للتأدي إلى مجهول
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): الفكر: تصرف القلب في النظر — literal: إعمال الروية؛ metaphorical: التفكر في ملكوت الله
- Root: ارض (arḍ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: الأرض: التي عليها الناس، وجمعها أرضون
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): الأرض: الجرم المقابل للسماء، ويعبر بها عن أسفل الشيء
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): literal: الأرض المهاد والفراش؛ metaphorical: تذلل الأرض وسكونها
- Root: دحا (d-ḥ-w) / مهد (m-h-d)
  * Lisan / Ayn: مهد: وطأ المكان وهيأه، والمهاد: الفراش الموطأ
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): المهد: الموضع المهيأ للصبي، والمهاد: الأرض الموطأة
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): literal: فرش الأرض وتمهيدها؛ metaphorical: جعلها قارة ساكنة لا تميد
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — the interposed clause "فانظر" after "إلى الأرض" maintains grammatical continuity while allowing rhetorical pause.
2:22.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Contemplation'

2:116.arabic: وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم يستغفر للعالم ما في السموات والأرض (3) وأي منصب يزيد على منصب من تشتغل ملائكة السموات والأرض بالاستغفار له وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم إن الحكمة تزيد الشريف شرفا وترفع المملوك حتى يدرك مدارك الملوك (4) وقد نبه بهذا على ثمراته في الدنيا ومعلوم أن الآخرة خير وأبقى وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم خصلتان لا يكونان في منافق حسن سمت وفقه في الدين (5) ولا تشكن في الحديث لنفاق بعض فقهاء الزمان فإنه ما أراد به الفقه الذي ظننته وسيأتي معنى الفقه وأدنى درجات الفقيه أن يعلم أن الآخرة خير من الدنيا
2:116.english: How He, Glorified and Exalted, began with Himself, then seconded with the angels, and thirded with the people of knowledge — and sufficient for you is this as honor, excellence, splendor, and nobility. And God, Exalted, said: {«يرفع الله الذين آمنوا منكم والذين أوتوا العلم درجات»} — "God will raise those who have believed among you and those who have been given knowledge, in degrees." Ibn ʿAbbās, may God be pleased with them both, said: For the scholars there are degrees above the believers, seven hundred degrees, and between each two degrees is a distance of five hundred years' journey.
2:116.section_title_en: The Book of Knowledge — Section 4: The Excellence of Knowledge and the Scholars
2:116.anchors:
- Root: علم (ʿ-l-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root meaning of knowing, perceiving a thing in its true reality; the act of apprehension and judgment.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "العلم: إدراك الشيء بحقيقته" — knowledge is the apprehension of a thing in its true reality, divided into apprehension of the essence and judgment of existence or non-existence.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) usage denotes genuine knowing; metaphorical (majāz) usage extends to signs, landmarks, and traces that guide to knowledge.
- Root: درج (d-r-j)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Degrees, steps, ascending stations; the root denotes gradation and progressive elevation.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الدرجة نحو المنزلة، لكن يقال للمنزلة: درجة إذا اعتبرت بالصعود" — a degree is a station considered by ascent, not horizontal extension.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical steps of ascent. Metaphorical: "لفلان درجة رفيعة" — lofty rank; "امش في مدارج الحق" — walk in the paths of truth.
- Root: يوم (y-w-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: A day; a period of time from sunrise to sunset, or any duration whatsoever.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "اليوم يعبر به عن وقت طلوع الشمس إلى غروبها. وقد يعبر به عن مدة من الزمان أي مدة كانت" — the day denotes the time of the sun's rising to its setting, and may denote any period of time whatsoever.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the solar day. Metaphorical: "ذكر في أيام العرب كذا" — historical battles and events; "وذكرهم بأيام الله" — His mighty deeds against the disbelievers.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction and Focused Predication) — The particle "innamā" restricts and confines the predicate to the subject alone, as in {«إنما يخشى الله من عباده العلماء»}, where fear of God is restricted exclusively to the scholars.
2:116.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'Contemplation'

2:164.arabic: وجنات ألفافا وقال تعالى إن في خلق السموات والأرض واختلاف الليل والنهار والفلك التي تجري في البحر بما ينفع الناس وما أنزل الله من السماء من ماء فأحيا به الأرض بعد موتها وبث فيها من كل دابة وتصريف الرياح والسحاب المسخر بين السماء والأرض لآيات لقوم يعقلون وقال تعالى ألم تروا كيف خلق الله سبع سموات طباقا وجعل القمر فيهن نورا وجعل الشمس سراجا والله أنبتكم من الأرض نباتا ثم يعيدكم فيها ويخرجكم إخراجا وقال تعالى أفرأيتم ما تمنون أأنتم تخلقونه أم نحن الخالقون إلى قوله للمقوين فليس يخفي على من م
2:164.english: The First Principle: the knowledge of His existence, the Exalted. The first thing by which one is illuminated from among the lights, and the path of reflection (ṭarīq al-iʿtibār) by which one proceeds, is that to which the Qurʾān has guided. For after the explanation of God, glorified be He, there is no explanation. He, the Exalted, has said: {«أَلَمْ نَجْعَلِ الْأَرْضَ مِهَادًا وَالْجِبَالَ أَوْتَادًا وَخَلَقْنَاكُمْ أَزْوَاجًا وَجَعَلْنَا نَوْمَكُمْ سُبَاتًا وَجَعَلْنَا اللَّيْلَ لِبَاسًا وَجَعَلْنَا النَّهَارَ مَعَاشًا وَبَنَيْنَا فَوْقَكُمْ سَبْعًا شِدَادًا وَجَعَلْنَا سِرَاجًا وَهَّاجًا وَأَنزَلْنَا مِنَ الْمُعْصِرَاتِ مَاءً ثَجَّاجًا لِّنُخْرِجَ بِهِ حَبًّا وَنَبَاتًا وَجَنَّاتٍ أَلْفَافًا»} — "Have We not made the earth a resting place, and the mountains as pegs, and created you in pairs, and made your sleep a repose, and made the night a covering, and made the day for livelihood, and built above you seven strong heavens, and made a blazing lamp, and sent down from the rain-clouds pouring water, that We may bring forth thereby grain and vegetation, and gardens dense with foliage?" (Q 78:6–16). And He, the Exalted, has said: {«إِنَّ فِي خَلْقِ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَاخْتِلَافِ اللَّيْلِ وَالنَّهَارِ وَالْفُلْكِ الَّتِي تَجْرِي فِي الْبَحْرِ بِمَا يَنفَعُ النَّاسَ وَمَا أَنزَلَ اللَّهُ مِنَ السَّمَاءِ مِن مَّاءٍ فَأَحْيَا بِهِ الْأَرْضَ بَعْدَ مَوْتِهَا وَبَثَّ فِيهَا مِن كُلِّ دَابَّةٍ وَتَصْرِيفِ الرِّيَاحِ وَالسَّحَابِ الْمُسَخَّرِ بَيْنَ السَّمَاءِ وَالْأَرْضِ لَآيَاتٍ لِّقَوْمٍ يَعْقِلُونَ»} — "Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth, and the alternation of the night and the day, and the ships which sail through the sea with that which benefits people, and what God has sent down from the sky of water, thereby reviving the earth after its death, and dispersing therein every creature, and the directing of the winds, and the clouds subservient between the heaven and the earth — are signs for a people who reason" (Q 2:164). And He, the Exalted, has said: {«أَلَمْ تَرَوْا كَيْفَ خَلَقَ اللَّهُ سَبْعَ سَمَاوَاتٍ طِبَاقًا وَجَعَلَ الْقَمَرَ فِيهِنَّ نُورًا وَجَعَلَ الشَّمْسَ سِرَاجًا وَاللَّهُ أَنبَتَكُم مِّنَ الْأَرْضِ نَبَاتًا ثُمَّ يُعِيدُكُمْ فِيهَا وَيُخْرِجُكُمْ إِخْرَاجًا»} — "Have you not seen how God created seven heavens in layers, and made the moon therein a light, and made the sun a lamp? And God caused you to grow from the earth a growth; then He returns you into it, and brings you forth a bringing forth" (Q 71:15–18). And He, the Exalted, has said: {«أَفَرَأَيْتُم مَّا تُمْنُونَ أَأَنتُمْ تَخْلُقُونَهُ أَمْ نَحْنُ الْخَالِقُونَ»} — "Have you considered what you emit? Do you create it, or are We the Creator?" — up to His saying: {«لِلْمُقْوِينَ»} — "for the settlers" (Q 56:58–73).
2:164.section_title_en: The Pillars of Faith: Knowledge of God, His Attributes, His Acts, and the Audibles — Section 87
2:164.anchors:
- Root: وجود (w-j-d)
  * Lisan / Ayn: [Core linguistic root meaning: to find, to perceive, to be; existence as that which is found or discovered]
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): [Theological/Kalam semantic nuance: al-wujūd as necessary existence (wujūb) versus contingent existence (imkān); the self-evident reality of the Creator's being]
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): [Literal vs Metaphorical distinction: haqīqah — existence as affirmed reality; majāz — "finding" as in discovery, not applicable to God's necessary being]
- Root: خلق (kh-l-q)
  * Lisan / Ayn: [Core linguistic root meaning: measuring, proportioning, fashioning; origination of a thing upon a measure]
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الخلق أصله: التقدير المستقيم، ويستعمل في إبداع الشيء من غير أصل ولا احتذاء" — creation as origination from nothing without prior model
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): [Literal: خلق الله الخلق: أوجده على تقدير أوجبته الحكمة — brought into existence upon a measure necessitated by wisdom; Majaz: not applicable to God's act as pure origination]
- Root: فطر (f-t-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: [Core linguistic root meaning: to split, cleave, rend; to originate, to bring forth as a new creation]
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "فطر الله الخلق" — God's origination of creation as a primordial act; "الفطرة" as the innate disposition
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): [Literal: فطر الله الخلق، وهو فاطر السموات: مبتدعها — originator without precedent; Majaz: "رأيه فطير" — immature opinion, not applicable to divine]
- Root: ارض (ar-d)
  * Lisan / Ayn: [Core linguistic root meaning: the earth, the lower sphere; that which is beneath]
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الأرض: الجرم المقابل للسماء" — the body opposite the heaven
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): [Literal: the earth as a resting place (مهادا); Majaz: not applicable in this context of divine creation]
- Root: ركن (r-k-n)
  * Lisan / Ayn: [Core linguistic root meaning: corner, pillar, support; that to which one leans for strength]
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "ركن الشيء: جانبه الذي يسكن إليه" — the side of a thing to which one repairs; used metaphorically for strength
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): [Literal: physical pillar/corner; Majaz: "فلان يأوي من عز قومه إلى ركن شديد" — one who repairs to a mighty support; here, the "pillars" (أركان) of faith as structural supports]
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The syntactic structure "مداره على عشرة أصول" (its circuit revolves upon ten principles) employs a prepositional phrase governing the verbal noun, establishing the necessary grammatical dependency that mirrors the ontological dependency of the created upon the Creator.

2:261.arabic: مطوقة لعناقيد الرطب ومتى كان فى حبة واحدة سمع سنابل فى كل سنبلة مائة ثم انظر إلى أرض البوادي وفتش ظاهرها وباطنها فتراها ترابا متشابها فإذا أنزل عليها الماء اهتزت وربت وأنبتت من كل زوج بهيج ألوانا مختلفة ونباتا متشابها وغير متشابه لكل واحد طعم وريح ولون وشكل يخالف الآخر فانظر إلى كثرتها واختلاف أصنافها وكثرة أشكالها ثم اختلاف طبائع النبات وكثرة منافعه وكيف أودع الله تعالى العقاقير المنافع الغريبة فهذا النبات يغذي وهذا يقوي وهذا يحيي وهذا يقتل وهذا يبرد وهذا يسخن وهذا إذا حصل في المعدة قمع الصفراء من أعماق العروق وهذ
2:261.english: For the beast has no power over that; but as for man, God created for him the power, then he disabled it and disbelieved in God's grace therein. So those are like cattle — nay, they are even further astray from the way {فَأُولَٰئِكَ كَالْأَنْعَامِ بَلْ هُمْ أَضَلُّ سَبِيلًا}.
2:261.section_title_en: On Contemplating the Earth, Its Rivers, Mountains, and Minerals — Section 1273
2:261.anchors:
- Root: فكر (f-k-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: التفكر: تأمل القلب وتدبر الشيء، والفكر: إعمال النظر في الشيء
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): الفكر: قوة العلم التي بها يدرك الإنسان، وقيل: هو ترتيب أمور معلومة للتأدي إلى مجهول
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): الفكر: تصرف القلب في النظر — literal: إعمال الروية؛ metaphorical: التفكر في ملكوت الله
- Root: ارض (arḍ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: الأرض: التي عليها الناس، وجمعها أرضون
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): الأرض: الجرم المقابل للسماء، ويعبر بها عن أسفل الشيء
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): literal: الأرض المهاد والفراش؛ metaphorical: تذلل الأرض وسكونها
- Root: دحا (d-ḥ-w) / مهد (m-h-d)
  * Lisan / Ayn: مهد: وطأ المكان وهيأه، والمهاد: الفراش الموطأ
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): المهد: الموضع المهيأ للصبي، والمهاد: الأرض الموطأة
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): literal: فرش الأرض وتمهيدها؛ metaphorical: جعلها قارة ساكنة لا تميد
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — the interposed clause "فانظر" after "إلى الأرض" maintains grammatical continuity while allowing rhetorical pause.
2:261.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'Contemplation'

3:190.arabic: وجنات ألفافا وقال تعالى إن في خلق السموات والأرض واختلاف الليل والنهار والفلك التي تجري في البحر بما ينفع الناس وما أنزل الله من السماء من ماء فأحيا به الأرض بعد موتها وبث فيها من كل دابة وتصريف الرياح والسحاب المسخر بين السماء والأرض لآيات لقوم يعقلون وقال تعالى ألم تروا كيف خلق الله سبع سموات طباقا وجعل القمر فيهن نورا وجعل الشمس سراجا والله أنبتكم من الأرض نباتا ثم يعيدكم فيها ويخرجكم إخراجا وقال تعالى أفرأيتم ما تمنون أأنتم تخلقونه أم نحن الخالقون إلى قوله للمقوين فليس يخفي على من م
3:190.english: The First Principle: the knowledge of His existence, the Exalted. The first thing by which one is illuminated from among the lights, and the path of reflection (ṭarīq al-iʿtibār) by which one proceeds, is that to which the Qurʾān has guided. For after the explanation of God, glorified be He, there is no explanation. He, the Exalted, has said: {«أَلَمْ نَجْعَلِ الْأَرْضَ مِهَادًا وَالْجِبَالَ أَوْتَادًا وَخَلَقْنَاكُمْ أَزْوَاجًا وَجَعَلْنَا نَوْمَكُمْ سُبَاتًا وَجَعَلْنَا اللَّيْلَ لِبَاسًا وَجَعَلْنَا النَّهَارَ مَعَاشًا وَبَنَيْنَا فَوْقَكُمْ سَبْعًا شِدَادًا وَجَعَلْنَا سِرَاجًا وَهَّاجًا وَأَنزَلْنَا مِنَ الْمُعْصِرَاتِ مَاءً ثَجَّاجًا لِّنُخْرِجَ بِهِ حَبًّا وَنَبَاتًا وَجَنَّاتٍ أَلْفَافًا»} — "Have We not made the earth a resting place, and the mountains as pegs, and created you in pairs, and made your sleep a repose, and made the night a covering, and made the day for livelihood, and built above you seven strong heavens, and made a blazing lamp, and sent down from the rain-clouds pouring water, that We may bring forth thereby grain and vegetation, and gardens dense with foliage?" (Q 78:6–16). And He, the Exalted, has said: {«إِنَّ فِي خَلْقِ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَاخْتِلَافِ اللَّيْلِ وَالنَّهَارِ وَالْفُلْكِ الَّتِي تَجْرِي فِي الْبَحْرِ بِمَا يَنفَعُ النَّاسَ وَمَا أَنزَلَ اللَّهُ مِنَ السَّمَاءِ مِن مَّاءٍ فَأَحْيَا بِهِ الْأَرْضَ بَعْدَ مَوْتِهَا وَبَثَّ فِيهَا مِن كُلِّ دَابَّةٍ وَتَصْرِيفِ الرِّيَاحِ وَالسَّحَابِ الْمُسَخَّرِ بَيْنَ السَّمَاءِ وَالْأَرْضِ لَآيَاتٍ لِّقَوْمٍ يَعْقِلُونَ»} — "Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth, and the alternation of the night and the day, and the ships which sail through the sea with that which benefits people, and what God has sent down from the sky of water, thereby reviving the earth after its death, and dispersing therein every creature, and the directing of the winds, and the clouds subservient between the heaven and the earth — are signs for a people who reason" (Q 2:164). And He, the Exalted, has said: {«أَلَمْ تَرَوْا كَيْفَ خَلَقَ اللَّهُ سَبْعَ سَمَاوَاتٍ طِبَاقًا وَجَعَلَ الْقَمَرَ فِيهِنَّ نُورًا وَجَعَلَ الشَّمْسَ سِرَاجًا وَاللَّهُ أَنبَتَكُم مِّنَ الْأَرْضِ نَبَاتًا ثُمَّ يُعِيدُكُمْ فِيهَا وَيُخْرِجُكُمْ إِخْرَاجًا»} — "Have you not seen how God created seven heavens in layers, and made the moon therein a light, and made the sun a lamp? And God caused you to grow from the earth a growth; then He returns you into it, and brings you forth a bringing forth" (Q 71:15–18). And He, the Exalted, has said: {«أَفَرَأَيْتُم مَّا تُمْنُونَ أَأَنتُمْ تَخْلُقُونَهُ أَمْ نَحْنُ الْخَالِقُونَ»} — "Have you considered what you emit? Do you create it, or are We the Creator?" — up to His saying: {«لِلْمُقْوِينَ»} — "for the settlers" (Q 56:58–73).
3:190.section_title_en: The Pillars of Faith: Knowledge of God, His Attributes, His Acts, and the Audibles — Section 87
3:190.anchors:
- Root: وجود (w-j-d)
  * Lisan / Ayn: [Core linguistic root meaning: to find, to perceive, to be; existence as that which is found or discovered]
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): [Theological/Kalam semantic nuance: al-wujūd as necessary existence (wujūb) versus contingent existence (imkān); the self-evident reality of the Creator's being]
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): [Literal vs Metaphorical distinction: haqīqah — existence as affirmed reality; majāz — "finding" as in discovery, not applicable to God's necessary being]
- Root: خلق (kh-l-q)
  * Lisan / Ayn: [Core linguistic root meaning: measuring, proportioning, fashioning; origination of a thing upon a measure]
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الخلق أصله: التقدير المستقيم، ويستعمل في إبداع الشيء من غير أصل ولا احتذاء" — creation as origination from nothing without prior model
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): [Literal: خلق الله الخلق: أوجده على تقدير أوجبته الحكمة — brought into existence upon a measure necessitated by wisdom; Majaz: not applicable to God's act as pure origination]
- Root: فطر (f-t-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: [Core linguistic root meaning: to split, cleave, rend; to originate, to bring forth as a new creation]
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "فطر الله الخلق" — God's origination of creation as a primordial act; "الفطرة" as the innate disposition
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): [Literal: فطر الله الخلق، وهو فاطر السموات: مبتدعها — originator without precedent; Majaz: "رأيه فطير" — immature opinion, not applicable to divine]
- Root: ارض (ar-d)
  * Lisan / Ayn: [Core linguistic root meaning: the earth, the lower sphere; that which is beneath]
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الأرض: الجرم المقابل للسماء" — the body opposite the heaven
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): [Literal: the earth as a resting place (مهادا); Majaz: not applicable in this context of divine creation]
- Root: ركن (r-k-n)
  * Lisan / Ayn: [Core linguistic root meaning: corner, pillar, support; that to which one leans for strength]
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "ركن الشيء: جانبه الذي يسكن إليه" — the side of a thing to which one repairs; used metaphorically for strength
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): [Literal: physical pillar/corner; Majaz: "فلان يأوي من عز قومه إلى ركن شديد" — one who repairs to a mighty support; here, the "pillars" (أركان) of faith as structural supports]
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The syntactic structure "مداره على عشرة أصول" (its circuit revolves upon ten principles) employs a prepositional phrase governing the verbal noun, establishing the necessary grammatical dependency that mirrors the ontological dependency of the created upon the Creator.
3:190.topic: Al-Ghazali on the journey of the soul, death, and the Hereafter, from 'Contemplation'

3:190.arabic: تعالى على في هذه الليلة إن في خلق السموات والأرض واختلاف الليل والنهار لآيات لأولى الألباب ثم قال ويل لمن قرأها ولم يتفكر فيها (3) فقيل للأوزاعى ما غاية التفكير فيهن قال يقرؤهن ويعقلهن وعن محمد بن واسع إن رجلا من أهل البصرة ركب إلى أم ذر بعد موت أبى ذر فسألها عن عبادة أبى ذر فقالت كان نهاره أجمع في ناحية البيت يتفكر وعن الحسن قال تفكر ساعة خير من قيام ليلة وعن الفضيل قال الفكر مرآة تريك حسناتك وسيئاتك وقيل لإبراهيم إنك تطيل الفكرة فقال الفكرة مخ العقل وكان سفيان بن عيينة كثيرا ما يتمثل بقول القائل إذا المرء كانت له فكرة .
3:190.english: I say: God — exalted be He — has commanded reflection (tafakkur) and deep contemplation (tadabbur) upon His Mighty Book in places beyond enumeration, and He has praised those who reflect. For He — exalted be He — says: {«الذين يذكرون الله قياما وقعودا وعلى جنوبهم ويتفكرون في خلق السموات والأرض ربنا ما خلقت هذا باطلا»} — "Those who remember God standing, sitting, and upon their sides, and reflect upon the creation of the heavens and the earth: 'Our Lord, You have not created this in vain'" (Āl ʿImrān 191).
3:190.section_title_en: The Virtue of Reflection (Tafakkur) Upon the Creation of God — Section 1257
3:190.anchors:
- Root: فكر (F-K-R)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root denotes the movement of the mind, turning a matter over in the heart/mind; "الفكرة" as the power that drives knowledge toward its object.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الفكرة: قوة مطرقة للعلم إلى المعلوم، والتفكر: جولان تلك القوة بحسب نظر العقل" — Reflection is the circulation of the intellect's power over what can be apprehended, seeking a mental form (ṣūrah); it is exclusive to humans and is forbidden regarding God's essence, as He transcends all form.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): "ما دار حوله فكري" (what revolves around my thought). Metaphorical (Majaz): "فكرتك مغاص الدرر" — reflection as a diver's plunge into the sea of meanings to extract pearls of wisdom.
- Root: خلق (KHLQ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root: "التقدير المستقيم" — precise, straight measurement and estimation; bringing something into being upon a measured pattern.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الخلق أصله: التقدير المستقيم، ويستعمل في إبداع الشيء من غير أصل ولا احتذاء" — creation as origination (ibdāʿ) from nothing, without prior model or pattern, as in {«خلق السماوات والأرض»} (Al-Anʿām 1); also used for bringing forth from something, as in {«خلقكم من نفس واحدة»} (Al-Nisāʾ 1).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "خلق الخراز الأديم" — the leather-worker measures the hide before cutting. Metaphorical: "خلق الله الخلق: أوجده على تقدير أوجبته الحكمة" — God's creation is bringing into existence upon a measure necessitated by wisdom.
- Root: قال (Q-W-L)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root: speech, utterance, saying; in the technical sense, the transmission of prophetic and scholarly dicta (aqwāl).
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Prepositional Interposition (باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور) — Governing the syntactic flow of reported speech chains (e.g., "قال ابن عباس... فقال صلى الله عليه وسلم"), where the narrator's interposed clauses do not break the grammatical dependency of the quotation, preserving the continuous chain of transmission (isnād).
3:190.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Contemplation'

4:170.arabic: يفعل وهم يسئلون وامتلأت مشكاة بعضهم نورا مقتبسا من نور الله تعالى في السموات والأرض وكان زيتهم أولا صافيا يكاد يضيء ولو لم تمسسه نار فمسته نار فاشتعل نورا على نور فأشرقت أقطار الملكوت بين أيديهم بنور ربها فأدركوا الأمور كلها كما هي عليه فقيل لهم تأدبوا بآداب الله تعالى واسكنوا وإذا
4:170.english: ...in the light of the sun, but due to a weakness in the eyesight of the bats. Thus those whose eyes had been opened to behold its majesty were compelled to borrow, from the lowly depths of the world of those who converse in languages, an expression that might convey, from the first principles of its realities, something exceedingly feeble. So they borrowed for it the name "power" (qudrah), and we, by reason of their borrowing, grew bold in speech, and said: "To God most high there is an attribute which is power, and from it issue creation and invention." Then creation, in its existence, divides into kinds, and into specific attributes; and the source of the division of these kinds and their being distinguished by their specific attributes is another attribute, for which was borrowed, in like manner to the necessity that preceded, the expression "will" (mashī'ah). For it suggests of it something obscure to those who converse in languages—which are but letters and sounds by which people understand one another—and the inadequacy of the word "will" to indicate the inner reality (kunnah) of that attribute and its true nature is like the inadequacy of the word "power." Then the acts issuing from power divided into what sweeps on to the terminus which is the goal of its wisdom, and into what halts short of the goal. And each of these had a relation to the attribute of will, by virtue of their reversion to the specifications (ikhtiṣāṣāt) through which the division and the differences are completed. So for the relation of that which attains its goal, the expression "love" (maḥabbah) was borrowed; and for the relation of that which halts short of its goal, the expression "aversion" (karāhah) was borrowed. And it was said that both of these are included within the description of will, but each has another particular property in its relation, which the words "love" and "aversion" suggest of them as something summarized for those who seek understanding from words and languages. Then His servants—who are also of His creation and invention—divided into: one for whom the eternal will (al-mashī'ah al-azaliyyah) had previously decreed that He would use him to halt His wisdom short of its goal, this being compulsion (qahr) in their regard, by the subjugation of motives and incitements upon them; and one for whom it had previously been decreed in eternity that He would use him to drive His wisdom to its goal in certain matters. So each of the two groups had a particular relation to the will; and for the relation of those used in completing wisdom through them, the expression "good pleasure" (riḍā) was borrowed; and for those by whom the causes of wisdom were halted short of its goal, the expression "wrath" (ghaḍab) was borrowed. Thus there appeared, upon him against whom wrath was decreed in eternity, an act by which wisdom was halted short of its goal; for this, the expression "ingratitude" (kufrān) was borrowed, and it was followed by the infliction of curse and blame as an increase in chastisement. And there appeared, upon him whom He approved in eternity, an act by which wisdom swept on to its goal; for this, the expression "thanksgiving" (shukr) was borrowed, and it was followed by the robe of praise and eulogy, as an increase in good pleasure, acceptance, and approach. So the outcome was that He most high gave beauty, then praised; and gave chastisement, then made ugly and destroyed. And His likeness is that a king should cleanse his servant of his filth, then clothe him in the finest of his garments; and when he has perfected his adornment, he says: "O beautiful one, how beautiful you are, and how beautiful your garments, and how clean your face!"—so that in reality, he is the one who beautifies, and he is the one who praises beauty; thus he is the praised one in every case. And it is as though, in meaning, he praised none but himself; the servant is merely the target of praise in respect of the outward appearance and form. Even so were the matters in eternity, and even so do causes and effects string themselves in sequence, by the decreeing of the Lord of lords and the Causer of causes. And that was not by chance or deliberation, but by will, and wisdom, and a true judgment, and a decisive command, for which the word "decree" (qaḍā') was borrowed. And it was said: it is like the glance of the eye, or nearer still. Then the seas of measured destinies (maqādīr) overflowed by the ruling of that decisive decree, with what predetermination (taqdīr) had previously passed. So for the ordering of the individual determined things (al-maqdūrāt), one upon another, the word "measure" (qadar) was borrowed. Thus the word "decree" (qaḍā') stood in correspondence to the one, unitary command, and the word "measure" (qadar) stood in correspondence to the detailed differentiation extending without end. And it was said that nothing of all this lies outside decree and measure. Then it occurred to some servants to ask: "Why did the division necessitate this differentiation, and how did justice cohere with this disparity and preference?" And some of them, due to their deficiency, could not bear to observe the inner reality of this matter or to encompass its totality; so they were bridled, from what they could not bear to plunge into its deep, with the bridle of prevention, and it was said to them: "Be still—for this you were not created. He is not questioned about what He does, but they shall be questioned" {«لا يسئل عما يفعل وهم يسئلون»}. And the niche (mishkāh) of others was filled with light borrowed from the light of God most high in the heavens and the earth; and their oil was at first pure, well-nigh luminous, even had no fire touched it; then fire touched it, and it blazed, light upon light, and the regions of the dominion (malakūt) shone before them with the light of their Lord. So they perceived all things as they truly are, and it was said to them: "Be disciplined with the disciplines of God most high, and be still." And when...
4:170.section_title_en: The Borrowed Language of Divine Attributes: On the Inadequacy of Human Terms for the Realities of Qaḍā', Qadar, and the Eternal Decree
4:170.anchors:
- Root: قدر (q-d-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root denotes measuring, determining, and ordaining a thing's extent and limit; al-Farahidi records its sense of precise appraisal and decreeing.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "القدرة" when ascribed to God negates incapacity ('ajz) absolutely; it is not a modality of acquisition as in creatures, but the sheer source whence creation issues—here Ghazali uses it as a borrowed term (isti'ārah) for an ineffable divine reality.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (haqīqah) sense is "ذو قدرة" (possessor of power); metaphorical (majāz) extension appears in "فرس بعيد القدر" (a horse of far-reaching stride)—so too here, "القدر" is extended to the serial ordering of ordained particulars, not a spatial or physical measure.
- Root: قسم (q-s-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Division and apportioning of shares; al-Farahidi ties it to partitioning lots.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "القسم: إفراز النصيب" — the separation of portions; Ghazali exploits this to show how creation's division into kinds and specific attributes demands a further attribute (the will) that specifies each portion.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: dividing wealth among parties; metaphorical: "قلبه متقسم" (his heart is divided by cares)—likewise, the division of acts under the will is a conceptual, not physical, partition.
- Root: لفظ (l-f-ẓ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Utterance as a casting out from the mouth; al-Farahidi notes its source-verb sense of ejection.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "اللفظ بالكلام مستعار من: لفظ الشيء من الفم" — speech-utterance is borrowed from physical ejection; Ghazali applies this to show how terms like "power," "will," "love," and "wrath" are merely cast-out approximations, not containers of divine essence.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Not separately cited; the root's rhetorical force lies in its inadequacy—words are sounds and letters, unable to convey the "kenne" (inner reality) of the divine.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — Ghazali's repeated "إنما" constructions (e.g., "وإنما العبد هدف الثناء") restrict the predicate to a single focused truth, isolating the apparent agent from the real one, per Sibawayh's rule that "إنما" confines judgment to what follows it, negating all else.
4:170.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

4:170.arabic: وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم يستغفر للعالم ما في السموات والأرض (3) وأي منصب يزيد على منصب من تشتغل ملائكة السموات والأرض بالاستغفار له وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم إن الحكمة تزيد الشريف شرفا وترفع المملوك حتى يدرك مدارك الملوك (4) وقد نبه بهذا على ثمراته في الدنيا ومعلوم أن الآخرة خير وأبقى وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم خصلتان لا يكونان في منافق حسن سمت وفقه في الدين (5) ولا تشكن في الحديث لنفاق بعض فقهاء الزمان فإنه ما أراد به الفقه الذي ظننته وسيأتي معنى الفقه وأدنى درجات الفقيه أن يعلم أن الآخرة خير من الدنيا
4:170.english: How He, Glorified and Exalted, began with Himself, then seconded with the angels, and thirded with the people of knowledge — and sufficient for you is this as honor, excellence, splendor, and nobility. And God, Exalted, said: {«يرفع الله الذين آمنوا منكم والذين أوتوا العلم درجات»} — "God will raise those who have believed among you and those who have been given knowledge, in degrees." Ibn ʿAbbās, may God be pleased with them both, said: For the scholars there are degrees above the believers, seven hundred degrees, and between each two degrees is a distance of five hundred years' journey.
4:170.section_title_en: The Book of Knowledge — Section 4: The Excellence of Knowledge and the Scholars
4:170.anchors:
- Root: علم (ʿ-l-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root meaning of knowing, perceiving a thing in its true reality; the act of apprehension and judgment.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "العلم: إدراك الشيء بحقيقته" — knowledge is the apprehension of a thing in its true reality, divided into apprehension of the essence and judgment of existence or non-existence.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) usage denotes genuine knowing; metaphorical (majāz) usage extends to signs, landmarks, and traces that guide to knowledge.
- Root: درج (d-r-j)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Degrees, steps, ascending stations; the root denotes gradation and progressive elevation.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الدرجة نحو المنزلة، لكن يقال للمنزلة: درجة إذا اعتبرت بالصعود" — a degree is a station considered by ascent, not horizontal extension.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical steps of ascent. Metaphorical: "لفلان درجة رفيعة" — lofty rank; "امش في مدارج الحق" — walk in the paths of truth.
- Root: يوم (y-w-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: A day; a period of time from sunrise to sunset, or any duration whatsoever.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "اليوم يعبر به عن وقت طلوع الشمس إلى غروبها. وقد يعبر به عن مدة من الزمان أي مدة كانت" — the day denotes the time of the sun's rising to its setting, and may denote any period of time whatsoever.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the solar day. Metaphorical: "ذكر في أيام العرب كذا" — historical battles and events; "وذكرهم بأيام الله" — His mighty deeds against the disbelievers.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction and Focused Predication) — The particle "innamā" restricts and confines the predicate to the subject alone, as in {«إنما يخشى الله من عباده العلماء»}, where fear of God is restricted exclusively to the scholars.
