4:170.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'Contemplation'

6:12.arabic: وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم يستغفر للعالم ما في السموات والأرض (3) وأي منصب يزيد على منصب من تشتغل ملائكة السموات والأرض بالاستغفار له وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم إن الحكمة تزيد الشريف شرفا وترفع المملوك حتى يدرك مدارك الملوك (4) وقد نبه بهذا على ثمراته في الدنيا ومعلوم أن الآخرة خير وأبقى وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم خصلتان لا يكونان في منافق حسن سمت وفقه في الدين (5) ولا تشكن في الحديث لنفاق بعض فقهاء الزمان فإنه ما أراد به الفقه الذي ظننته وسيأتي معنى الفقه وأدنى درجات الفقيه أن يعلم أن الآخرة خير من الدنيا
6:12.english: How He, Glorified and Exalted, began with Himself, then seconded with the angels, and thirded with the people of knowledge — and sufficient for you is this as honor, excellence, splendor, and nobility. And God, Exalted, said: {«يرفع الله الذين آمنوا منكم والذين أوتوا العلم درجات»} — "God will raise those who have believed among you and those who have been given knowledge, in degrees." Ibn ʿAbbās, may God be pleased with them both, said: For the scholars there are degrees above the believers, seven hundred degrees, and between each two degrees is a distance of five hundred years' journey.
6:12.section_title_en: The Book of Knowledge — Section 4: The Excellence of Knowledge and the Scholars
6:12.anchors:
- Root: علم (ʿ-l-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root meaning of knowing, perceiving a thing in its true reality; the act of apprehension and judgment.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "العلم: إدراك الشيء بحقيقته" — knowledge is the apprehension of a thing in its true reality, divided into apprehension of the essence and judgment of existence or non-existence.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) usage denotes genuine knowing; metaphorical (majāz) usage extends to signs, landmarks, and traces that guide to knowledge.
- Root: درج (d-r-j)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Degrees, steps, ascending stations; the root denotes gradation and progressive elevation.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الدرجة نحو المنزلة، لكن يقال للمنزلة: درجة إذا اعتبرت بالصعود" — a degree is a station considered by ascent, not horizontal extension.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical steps of ascent. Metaphorical: "لفلان درجة رفيعة" — lofty rank; "امش في مدارج الحق" — walk in the paths of truth.
- Root: يوم (y-w-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: A day; a period of time from sunrise to sunset, or any duration whatsoever.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "اليوم يعبر به عن وقت طلوع الشمس إلى غروبها. وقد يعبر به عن مدة من الزمان أي مدة كانت" — the day denotes the time of the sun's rising to its setting, and may denote any period of time whatsoever.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the solar day. Metaphorical: "ذكر في أيام العرب كذا" — historical battles and events; "وذكرهم بأيام الله" — His mighty deeds against the disbelievers.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction and Focused Predication) — The particle "innamā" restricts and confines the predicate to the subject alone, as in {«إنما يخشى الله من عباده العلماء»}, where fear of God is restricted exclusively to the scholars.
6:12.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'Contemplation'

6:12.arabic: الله تعالى لم ينظر إليها وتقول يوم القيامة يا رب اجعلني لأدنى أوليائك اليوم نصيبا فيقول اسكتي يا لا شيء إني لم أرضك لهم في الدنيا أرضاك لهم اليوم (1) وروي في أخبار آدم عليه السلام أنه لما أكل من الشجرة تحركت معدته لخروج الثقل ولم يكن ذلك مجعولا في شيء من أطعمة الجنة إلا في هذه الشجرة فلذلك نهيا عن أكلها قال فجعل يدور في الجنة فأمر الله تعالى ملكا يخاطبه فقال له قل له أي شيء تريد قال آدم أريد أن أضع ما في بطني من الأذى فقيل للملك قل له في أي مكان تريد أن تضعه أعلى الفرش أم على السرر أم على ا
6:12.english: It has been related that the Messenger of God — may God's peace and blessings be upon him — passed by a dead sheep and said: "Do you see this sheep as contemptible to its owners?" They said: "It was due to its contemptibleness that they cast it away." He said: "By Him in whose hand is my soul, this world is more contemptible to God than this sheep is to its owners. And had this world weighed in God's sight the wing of a gnat, He would not have given a disbeliever from it a single drink of water." {«الدنيا سجن المؤمن وجنة الكافر»} (1)
6:12.section_title_en: The Verses and Reports Concerning the Blame of This World (Dhamm al-Dunyā)
6:12.anchors:
- Root: د ن ا (D-N-A)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The near, the lower, that which is immediate and proximate; the worldly abode as that which is "closest" in contrast to the Hereafter which is "farthest."
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الدنو: القرب بالذات، أو بالحكم" — proximity by essence or by judgment; the dunyā is so named for its temporal nearness, its inferior rank, and its being the "lesser" (adnā) in contrast to the greater and abiding.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): the nearest and lowest abode. Metaphorical (Majaz): the life of this world as a "dung-hill" (mazbalah) and a carcass — its worthlessness rendered sensibly perceptible.
- Root: ر س ل (R-S-L)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Sending forth with gentleness and ease; a messenger (rasūl) as one dispatched.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "أصل الرسل: الانبعاث على التؤدة" — the root is emission upon measured deliberation; the prophetic mission (risālah) as the sending of guidance to turn creation away from the dunyā toward the ākhirah.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: dispatch of a messenger with a message. Metaphorical: "أرسل الله عليهم العذاب" — the sending of punishment; here, the prophets were sent with the sole purpose of diverting hearts from the world.
- Root: ح د ث (H-D-TH)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Origination after non-existence; that which is new and temporal.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الحدوث: كون الشيء بعد أن لم يكن" — the world as muḥdath (originated/temporal), hence inherently perishable and contemptible before the Eternal.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: new occurrence. Metaphorical: "صاروا أحاديث" — becoming mere tales; the dunyā's ornaments become "rotten rags" and "withered bones."
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — The prophetic reports employ restrictive constructions (e.g., "The world is but a prison of the believer") to confine the dunyā's essence to a single defining attribute, negating all else.
6:12.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Condemnation of the World'

6:12.arabic: الخبر المشهور إن الله تعالى كتب على نفسه الرحمة قبل أن يخلق الخلق إن رحمتي تغلب غضبي (6) وعن معاذ بن جبل وأنس بن مالك أنه صلى الله عليه وسلم قال من قال لا إله إلا الله دخل الجنة (7) ومن كان آخر كلامه لا إله إلا الله لم تسمه النار (8) ومن لقي الله لا يشرك به شيئا حرمت عليه النار (9) ولا يدخلها من في قلبه مثقال ذرة من إيمان (10) وفي خبر آخر لو علم الكافر سعة رحمة الله ما آيس من جنته أحد (11) ولما تلا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قوله تعالى إن زلزلة الساعة شيء عظيم {قال} أتدرون أي يوم هذا هذا يوم يق
6:12.english: So it was said to him: "And what is in it of hope?" He said: "This world, all of it, is little, and a man's provision from it is little, and his religion is little in comparison to his provision. So look at how God Most High sent down in it the longest verse, to guide His servant to the path of caution in preserving his wealth — so how could He not preserve his religion, which has no substitute for him?"
6:12.section_title_en: The Book of Hope (Kitāb al-Rajā') — Section 1033: The Second Art — Surveying the Verses and Reports Concerning Hope
6:12.anchors:
- Root: وجود (w-j-d)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of "finding" and "existence"; here in the sense of what is present and available.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Existence as that which is found and realized; in theological context, the given order of creation.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) sense of "being found"; metaphorical (majāz) extension to the entirety of created things.
- Root: رجا (r-j-w)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To hope, to expect with desire; the opposite of despair (ya's).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Hope as a theological virtue — the heart's expectation of divine mercy, balanced against fear (khawf).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: expectation of a desired outcome; metaphorical: the soul's reliance on divine generosity.
- Root: غفر (gh-f-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To cover, to shield, to pardon; the root implies veiling the fault.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Divine forgiveness as the covering of sins and the effacing of their consequence.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: covering; metaphorical: God's remission of punishment.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — used to emphasize exclusive attributes of divine mercy and forgiveness.
6:12.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Fear and Hope'

6:75.arabic: قال الله تعالى ما كذب الفؤاد ما رأى وقال تعالى وكذلك نرى إبراهيم ملكوت السموات والأرض الآية وسمي ضده عمى فقال تعالى فإنها لا تعمى الأبصار ولكن تعمي القلوب التي في الصدور وقال تعالى ومن كان في هذه أعمى فهو في الآخرة أعمى وأضل سبيلا وهذه الأمور التي كشفت للأنبياء بعضها كان بالبصر وبعضها كان بالبصيرة وسمي الكل رؤية وبالجملة من لم تكن بصيرته الباطنة ثاقبة لم يعلق به من الدين إلا قشوره وأمثلته دون لبابه وحقائقه فهذه أقسام ما ينطلق اسم العقل عليها
6:75.english: I say: Know that the washing of the eye is forbidden — that is, the eye of insight (ʿayn al-baṣīrah) is not to be washed with the water of blind imitation and mere hearsay, for it is the organ by which the realities of the intellect are disclosed. And the divisions of what the name "intellect" (al-ʿaql) is applied to have become clear: it is said of the inborn faculty (al-gharīzah), and it is said of the knowledge that is acquired through that faculty, and it is said of the state of that knowledge when it governs the soul, and it is said of the very actions that proceed from that governance.
6:75.section_title_en: The Washing of the Eye is Forbidden — On the True Meaning of Intellect (ʿAql) and Its Divisions
6:75.anchors:
- Root: عقل (ʿAql)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The root denotes binding, restraining, and holding back — the intellect is that which restrains the soul from base desires and prevents it from straying.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "العقل يقال للقوة المتهيئة لقبول العلم، ويقال للعلم الذي يستفيده الإنسان بتلك القوة عقل" — al-ʿaql is said of the faculty prepared to receive knowledge, and it is also said of the knowledge acquired by that faculty. It is the instrument of divine discernment and the locus of taklīf (moral responsibility).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): the inborn faculty of discernment. Metaphorical (Majaz): "نخلة لا تعقل الإبار إذا لم تقبله" — a palm tree that does not accept pollination is said to be "not to ʿaqil" the pollen, extending the root to the sense of "accepting/receiving." Thus, knowledge is called ʿaql metaphorically as its fruit.
- Root: بصر (Baṣar)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Sight, perception — both of the eye and of the heart.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "البصر يقال للجارحة الناظرة... ويقال لقوة القلب المدركة: بصيرة وبصر" — baṣar is said of the seeing organ, and of the perceiving power of the heart: baṣīrah and baṣar. The inner sight (baṣīrah) perceives immaterial realities.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: ocular vision. Metaphorical: "هذه آية مبصرة" — this is an illuminating sign; "واجعلني بصيرة عليهم أي رقيبا وشاهدا" — make me a watcher over them. The inner eye perceives what the outer eye cannot.
- Root: فطر (Faṭara)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To split, cleave, originate, create — the primordial act of divine creation.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "أصل الفطر: الشق طولا... وفطر الله الخلق" — the root is splitting lengthwise; God's "fatr" of creation is His originating of things. "فطرة الله التي فطر الناس عليها" — the primordial disposition upon which God originated mankind.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "فطر الله الخلق، وهو فاطر السموات: مبتدعها" — God originated creation; He is the Originator of the heavens. "وكل مولود يولد على الفطرة" — every newborn is born upon the fiṭrah, i.e., the innate disposition receptive to the religion of truth.
- Root: نفس (Nafs)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Self, soul, spirit; the innermost reality of a thing.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "النفس: الروح... وقوله: تعلم ما في نفسي ولا أعلم ما في نفسك" — nafs is the spirit/soul; "You know what is in my nafs and I know not what is in Your nafs" — the nafs is the seat of inner assent and recognition.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the self. Metaphorical: "دفق نفسه أي دمه" — he poured out his nafs, i.e., his blood. The nafs is the locus of the primordial covenant (mīthāq).
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — The construction "إنما العاقل من آمن بالله" restricts the predicate: the intellect is not merely a faculty of cleverness but is defined by its fruit — faith and God-consciousness (taqwā).
6:75.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Contemplation'

6:88.arabic: ويهدي بها من يشاء فمن نظر في هذه الأمور من حيث إنها فعل الله تعالى وصنعه استفاد منه المعرفة بجلال الله تعالى وعظمته واهتدى به ومن نظر فيها قاصرا للنظر عليها من حيث تأثير بعضها فى بعض لا من حيث ارتباطها بمسبب الأسباب فقد شقى وارتدى فنعوذ بالله من الضلال ونسأله أن يجنبنا مزلة أقدام الجهال بمنه وكرمه وفضله وجوده ورحمته تم الكتاب التاسع من ربع المنجيات والحمد لله وحده وصلواته على محمد وآله وسلامه يتلوه كتاب ذكر الموت وما بعده وبه كمل جميع الديوان بحمد الله تعالى وكرم
6:88.english: To proceed: Worthy is one whose place of downfall is death, whose bed is the dust, whose companion is the worm, whose boon-companions are Munkar and Nakīr, whose abode is the grave, whose resting-place is the belly of the earth, whose appointed time is the Resurrection, and whose destination is Paradise or the Fire — that he should have no thought except of death, no remembrance except of it, no preparation except for it, no deliberation except concerning it, no aspiration except toward it, no lingering except upon it, no concern except with it, no power except around it, and no waiting or tarrying except for it. And it is fitting that he should count himself among the dead and see himself among the inhabitants of the graves, for everything that is coming is near, and the distant is only that which is not coming. The Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "The shrewd one (al-kayyis) is he who subdues his soul and works for what comes after death" (1). And preparation for a thing will not be facilitated except upon the renewal of its remembrance in the heart, and its remembrance is not renewed except through recollection by lending ear to those things that remind of it and by looking upon those things that alert to it.
6:88.section_title_en: The Book of the Remembrance of Death and What Follows It — Introduction and Opening Homily
6:88.anchors:
- Root: موت (m-w-t)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root denotes cessation of vital faculty; death as transition, not annihilation.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Death is the divinely ordained terminus of corporeal life, gateway to reckoning; "أماته فأقبره" {«عبس/ 21»} implies divine disposal of the deceased.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: bodily death and burial. Metaphorical: "أحيا الله البلد الميت" — revival of barren land; death of hearts through heedlessness.
- Root: قبر (q-b-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Grave as the resting place of the dead; "المقبرة" as the site of interment.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "حتى زرتم المقابر" {«التكاثر/ 2»} — metonymy for death itself; the grave as prelude to resurrection.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: burial of the deceased. Metaphorical: "رفع قبراه" — the haughty one who raises his nose like a grave-mound, signifying pride.
- Root: حمد (ḥ-m-d)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Praise predicated upon volitional excellence; gratitude for beneficence.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): True praise (ḥamd) is due solely to God, whose acts are pure beneficence; distinct from mere thanks (shukr) for favors received.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "أحمد الله بجميع محامده" — praising God with all praises. Metaphorical: "أحمدت صنيعه" — approving an act as praiseworthy.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The periodic opening "الحمد لله الذي..." employs a suspended genitive construction (جار ومجرور) with a relative clause (صلة الموصول) that permits extended expansion, governing the entire homiletic sequence that follows.
6:88.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Contemplation'

7:146.arabic: قد ذم الله الكبر في مواضع من كتابه وذم كل جبار متكبر فقال تعالى {سأصرف عن آياتي الذين يتكبرون في الأرض بغير الحق} وقال عز وجل {كذلك يطبع الله على كل قلب متكبر جبار} وقال تعالى {واستفتحوا وخاب كل جبار عنيد} وقال تعالى {إنه لا يحب المستكبرين} وقال تعالى {لقد استكبروا في أنفسهم وعتوا عتوا كبيرا} وقال تعالى {إن الذين يستكبرون عن عبادتي سيدخلون جهنم داخرين} وذم الكبر في القرآن كثير وقد قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لا يدخل الجنة من كان في قلبه مثقال حبة من خردل من كبر ولا يدخل الجنة من كان في قلبه مثقال حبة من خردل من إيمان (1) حديث أبي هريرة يقول ال
7:146.english: To proceed: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said — God, exalted be He, said: "Pride (al-kibriyāʾ) is My cloak, and greatness (al-ʿaẓamah) is My wrapper; whoever contends with Me over either of them, I crush him." {«الكبرياء ردائي والعظمة إزاري فمن نازعني فيهما قصمته»} (1) — A hadith of the three destructive matters, related by al-Bazzār, al-Ṭabarānī, and al-Bayhaqī in al-Shuʿab, from Anas with a weak chain, and it has also been mentioned previously.
7:146.section_title_en: The Book of Condemnation of Pride and Self-Admiration — Being the Ninth Book of the Quarter of Destructive Matters from The Revival of the Religious Sciences
7:146.anchors:
- Root: كبر (k-b-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root denotes magnitude, whether physical size, age, or rank; "al-kibriyā'" is the supreme majesty exclusive to God.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "al-kabīr wa al-ṣaghīr" are relative terms; used for quantity, quality, and dignity. "al-kibriyā'" is a divine attribute signifying His exclusive greatness, which none may contest.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): "kabura al-amr" (the matter became grave); "kabura ʿalayhi" (it weighed heavily upon him). Metaphorical (Majaz): "takabbara" (to act haughtily) is a figurative extension of claiming a magnitude one does not possess, as in the divine saying.
- Root: عجب (ʿ-j-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Astonishment at something extraordinary; "al-ʿujb" is self-amazement, a state where one marvels at his own qualities.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Astonishment arises from ignorance of the true cause; self-admiration (ʿujb) blinds one to one's own defects and to the divine origin of all good.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "ʿajiba minhu" (he marveled at it). Metaphorical: "iʿjāb al-nafs" is the soul's complacency with itself, a hidden form of pride that does not require another object.
- Root: هلك (h-l-k)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Perishing, destruction, ruin; "al-muhlikāt" are the things that cause perdition.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Destruction is of three kinds: loss, corruption, and death. Here it is spiritual perdition — the ruin of the soul's eternal felicity.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical ruin. Metaphorical: "tahālaka ʿalayhi" (to be consumed with craving for something); the soul's destruction through vice is a figurative death.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Apposition and Parenthetical Clauses (al-badal wa al-iʿtirāḍ) — The opening doxology employs extended appositional chains (badal) and parenthetical invocations that delay the main clause, requiring the translator to preserve the periodic structure without collapsing the theological weight of each divine epithet.
7:146.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'Condemnation of Pride and Conceit'

7:146.arabic: ومن لم يكن نظره اعتبارا فهو لهو وفي قوله تعالى سأصرف عن آياتي الذين يتكبرون في الأرض يغير الحق قال أمنع قلوبهم التفكر في أمرى وعن أبى سعيدى الخدري قال قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أعطوا أعينكم حظها من العبادة فقالوا يا رسول الله وما حظها من العبادة قال النظر في المصحف والتفكر فيه والاعتبار عند عجائبه (4) وعن امرأة كانت تسكن البادية قريبا من مكة أنها قالت لو تطالعت قلوب المتقين بفكرها إلى ما قد ادخر لها في حجب الغيب من خير الآخرة لم يصف لهم في الدنيا عيش ولم تقر لهم في الدنيا عين وكان لقمان يطيل الجلوس وحده فكان يمر به مولاه فيقول يا لقمان
7:146.english: And it is related from Ṭāwūs that he said: The disciples (al-Ḥawāriyyūn) said to Jesus son of Mary (ʿalayhi al-salām): "O Spirit of God, is there upon the earth today anyone like you?" He said: "Yes — whoever's speech is remembrance (dhikr), whose silence is reflection (fikr), and whose gaze is a lesson (ʿibrah) — then he is like me."
7:146.section_title_en: The Virtue of Reflection (Faḍīlat al-Tafakkur) — Section 1258
7:146.anchors:
- Root: فكر (F-K-R)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root denotes the power of intellective search; "الفكرة: قوة مطرقة للعلم إلى المعلوم" — a force driving knowledge toward the known.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "التفكر: جولان تلك القوة بحسب نظر العقل" — reflection is the circulation of that force according to rational consideration; exclusive to humans, not animals; only said of what can be imaged in the heart.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): "ما دار حوله فكري" — what revolves around one's reflection. Metaphorical (Majaz): "لفلان فكر، كلها فقر" — reflection likened to diving for pearls (مغاص الدرر).
- Root: جلس (J-L-S)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "ناقة جَلْس" — firm/robust she-camel; "الجُلْسان: ما حول الحدقة" — what surrounds the pupil (eye-socket).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "أصل الجلس: الغليظ من الأرض" — origin: elevated firm ground; then generalized to any sitting (قعود).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "هو حسن الجلسة" — good posture in sitting. Metaphorical: "فلان جليس نفسه" — one who is companion to himself (solitary by choice).
- Root: قلب (Q-L-B)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "قلب الشيء: تصريفه وصرفه عن وجه إلى وجه" — turning a thing from one face to another.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "قلب الإنسان: صرفه عن طريقته" — turning the heart from its course; "الانقلاب: الانصراف" — reversion.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "قلب رداءه" — turning one's garment. Metaphorical: "قلب المعلم الصبيان: صرفهم إلى بيوتهم" — the teacher turning the boys back home; "رجل قلب حول: يقلب الأمور ويحتال" — a man who turns matters over and devises.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — Permissibility of interposing elements between a governing word and its governed prepositional phrase when the interposed material is syntactically complete, as in "إن به" constructions; here governing the periodic structure of reported sayings (e.g., "قال الحسن: من لم يكن...") where the conditional clauses are interposed between the verb of saying and its content.
7:146.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Contemplation'

7:185.arabic: وفي أنفسهم حتى يتبين لهم أنه الحق} الآية وبقوله عز وجل أولم ينظروا في ملكوت السموات والأرض وبقوله تعالى قل انظروا ماذا في السموات والأرض وبقوله تعالى الذي خلق سبع سموات طباقا ما ترى في خلق الرحمن من تفاوت فارجع البصر هل ترى من فطور ثم ارجع البصر كرتين ينقلب إليك البصر خاسئا وهو حسير وهذا الطريق هو الأسهل على الأكثرين وهو الأوسع على السالكين وإليه أكثر دعوة القرآن عند الأمر بالتدبر والتفكر والاعتبار والنظر في آيات خارجة عن الحصر فإن قلت كلا الطريقين مشكل فأوضح لنا منهما ما يستعان به على تحصيل المعرفة والتوصل به إلى المحبة فاعلم أن الط
7:185.english: Those who arrive at this rank divide into two groups: the strong, whose first knowledge is of God, exalted be He, and then through Him they come to know other than Him; and the weak, whose first knowledge is of [His] acts, and then they ascend from them to the Agent. To the first points His saying, exalted be He: {أو لم يكف بربك أنه على كل شيء شهيد} [Is it not sufficient concerning your Lord that He is over all things a Witness], and His saying, exalted be He: {«شهد الله أنه لا إله إلا هو»} [God bears witness that there is no god but He]. And of this kind is the saying of one of them, when it was said to him: "By what have you known your Lord?" He said: "I have known my Lord — and were it not for my Lord, I would not have known my Lord."
7:185.section_title_en: The Two Paths to Knowledge and Love: The Higher Way of Witnessing the Truth and the Easier Way of Contemplating Creation
7:185.anchors:
- Root: طيب (ṭ-y-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Pure, good, wholesome; free from defilement
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): That which is pure and agreeable in both sensory and intellectual registers; the "good word" (al-kalim al-ṭayyib) is the declaration of divine unity
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal for sensory purity; metaphorical for spiritual purity of heart and speech
- Root: عرف (ʿ-r-f)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To know by reflection and discernment of traces/effects
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Maʿrifah is knowledge of God attained through contemplation of His effects, not through direct apprehension of His essence; it is more specific than ʿilm
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: to recognize someone; metaphorical: knowledge of God through His signs
- Root: شهد (sh-h-d)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To witness, testify, be present
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Bearing witness to the truth of something based on direct presence or evidence
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: ocular presence; metaphorical: intellectual certitude
- Root: نظر (n-ẓ-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To look, gaze, contemplate
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Contemplative reflection (naẓar) directed toward creation to derive knowledge of the Creator
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: visual perception; metaphorical: intellectual consideration and inference
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — used to restrict the purpose of works to purification of the heart, and to restrict the ultimate end to knowledge of unveiling
7:185.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Love, Longing, Intimacy and Contentment'

7:185.arabic: عظيم به حجب أكثر المتكلمين والمتعصبين للمذاهب بل أكثر الصالحين المتفكرين في ملكوت السموات والأرض لأنهم محجوبون باعتقادات تقليدية جمدت في نفوسهم ورسخت في قلوبهم وصارت حجابا بينهم وبين درك الحقائق الخامس الجهل بالجهة التي يقع منها العثور على المطلوب فإن طالب العلم ليس يمكنه أن يحصل العلم بالمجهول إلا بالتذكر للعلوم التي تناسب مطلوبه حتى إذا تذكرها ورتبها في نفسه ترتيبا مخصوصا يعرفه العلماء بطرق الاعتبار فعند ذلك يكون قد عثر على جهة المطلوب فتنجلى حقيقة المطلوب لقلبه فإن العلوم المطلوبة التي ليست فطرية لا تقتنص إلا بشبكة العلوم الحاصلة بل كل
7:185.english: The second is the turbidity of disobedience and the foulness that accumulates upon the face of the heart from the abundance of lusts. For that prevents the heart's purity and clarity, and thus the appearance of truth within it is prevented by its darkness and accumulation. To this points his saying, peace be upon him: "Whoever commits a sin departs from him an intellect that never returns to him" {«حديث»} — and his saying, peace be upon him: "Whoever acts upon what he knows, God bequeaths to him knowledge of what he does not know," narrated by Abū Nuʿaym in al-Ḥilyah from the hadith of Anas, and it has preceded in the Book of Knowledge.
7:185.section_title_en: The Heart as a Mirror: The Five Obstacles to Knowledge and the Path to Unveiling
7:185.anchors:
- Root: قلب (q-l-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To turn, overturn, transform from one state to another; the heart as that which constantly fluctuates and turns.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The heart is the subtle center of perception and understanding, that which turns toward matters and apprehends their realities.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: turning a thing over. Metaphorical: the heart as the seat of understanding that "turns over" matters to grasp their true nature.
- Root: علم (ʿ-l-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To know, to perceive a thing's reality; knowledge as the impression of the form of a thing.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Knowledge is the apprehension of a thing by its true reality (idrāk al-shayʾ bi-ḥaqīqatihi) — either the perception of the thing's essence or the judgment of its attributes.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: knowledge as direct perception. Metaphorical: knowledge as the "arrival" of the known's form in the heart.
- Root: صور (ṣ-w-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Form, shape, image; that by which a thing is distinguished.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Form is twofold: sensible (perceived by all) and intelligible (perceived by the discerning) — the latter being the form of the intellect and meanings.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical shape. Metaphorical: the "form" of a thing's reality that imprints upon the heart.
- Root: مرا (m-r-ʾ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: A person, a human being; also mirror (mirʾāh).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The mirror as that which reflects forms without itself being altered.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: mirror as reflective surface. Metaphorical: the heart as a mirror reflecting the realities of things.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — Used to establish precise definitions of knowledge, known, and knower through restrictive predication.
7:185.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Contemplation'

7:185.arabic: من الملائكة بعدد جميع ما خلق الله من شيء فقلت من أنتم فقالوا نحن المحبون لله عز وجل نعبده ههنا منذ ثلثمائة ألف سنة ما خطر على قلوبنا قط سواه ولا ذكرنا غيره قال فاستحييت من أعمالي فوهبتها لمن حق عليه الوعيد تخفيفا عنه في جهنم فإذن من عرف نفسه وعرف ربه واستحيا منه حق الحياء خرس لسانه عن التظاهر بالدعوى نعم يشهد على حبه حركاته وسكناته وإقدامه وإحجامه وتردداته كما حكي عن الجنيد أنه قال مرض أستاذنا السري رحمه الله فلم نعرف لعلته دواء ولا عرفنا لها سببا فوصف لنا طبيب حاذق فأخذ قارورة مائه ف
7:185.english: It is related that a man saw something from one of the madmen that made him deem him foolish, and he reported that to Maʿrūf al-Karkhī — may Allah have mercy on him. He smiled, then said: "O my brother, he has lovers, both young and old, both rational and mad. So this one you saw is among their madmen."
7:185.section_title_en: On the Concealment of Love and Its True Signs — Section 1183
7:185.anchors:
- Root: خفي (khafā)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To be hidden, concealed, imperceptible to the senses.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-Khafī is that which is not perceived by the senses; its theological nuance relates to Allah's knowledge of the unseen (ghayb) and the inner conscience (sirr).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (haqīqah) refers to physical concealment; metaphorical (majāz) applies to the heart's hidden states, as in "the secret" (al-sirr) which only Allah perceives.
- Root: حب (ḥubb)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to love, to be steadfast upon something; also a jar (ḥubb) that holds water — implying that love is a vessel containing the lover's entire being.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-Maḥabbah is the will directed toward what is perceived as agreeable; in theological terms, love of Allah is the soul's inclination toward Him due to His perfection, not due to benefit or harm.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: inclination of the heart. Metaphorical: the bodily movements and stillness that testify to an inward state, as the physician's diagnosis of the lover's urine.
- Root: وجد (wajd)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To find; also intense emotion, ecstasy, or passionate yearning that overwhelms the lover.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-Wajd is the arrival of a spiritual state (ḥāl) that dominates the heart, often leading to loss of self-control (ghashyah).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: finding something lost. Metaphorical: the overpowering of the heart by love, such that the lover falls unconscious — as related of al-Sarī.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Interposition (al-Faṣl bayna al-Jār wa al-Majrūr) — The syntactic principle that a clause may be interrupted by an explanatory parenthetical without breaking grammatical cohesion, as seen in the narrative digressions (e.g., the story of the madman and al-Karkhī) that serve as illustrative asides within the main argument.
7:185.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Love, Longing, Intimacy and Contentment'

10:55.arabic: وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم يستغفر للعالم ما في السموات والأرض (3) وأي منصب يزيد على منصب من تشتغل ملائكة السموات والأرض بالاستغفار له وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم إن الحكمة تزيد الشريف شرفا وترفع المملوك حتى يدرك مدارك الملوك (4) وقد نبه بهذا على ثمراته في الدنيا ومعلوم أن الآخرة خير وأبقى وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم خصلتان لا يكونان في منافق حسن سمت وفقه في الدين (5) ولا تشكن في الحديث لنفاق بعض فقهاء الزمان فإنه ما أراد به الفقه الذي ظننته وسيأتي معنى الفقه وأدنى درجات الفقيه أن يعلم أن الآخرة خير من الدنيا
10:55.english: How He, Glorified and Exalted, began with Himself, then seconded with the angels, and thirded with the people of knowledge — and sufficient for you is this as honor, excellence, splendor, and nobility. And God, Exalted, said: {«يرفع الله الذين آمنوا منكم والذين أوتوا العلم درجات»} — "God will raise those who have believed among you and those who have been given knowledge, in degrees." Ibn ʿAbbās, may God be pleased with them both, said: For the scholars there are degrees above the believers, seven hundred degrees, and between each two degrees is a distance of five hundred years' journey.
10:55.section_title_en: The Book of Knowledge — Section 4: The Excellence of Knowledge and the Scholars
10:55.anchors:
- Root: علم (ʿ-l-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root meaning of knowing, perceiving a thing in its true reality; the act of apprehension and judgment.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "العلم: إدراك الشيء بحقيقته" — knowledge is the apprehension of a thing in its true reality, divided into apprehension of the essence and judgment of existence or non-existence.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) usage denotes genuine knowing; metaphorical (majāz) usage extends to signs, landmarks, and traces that guide to knowledge.
- Root: درج (d-r-j)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Degrees, steps, ascending stations; the root denotes gradation and progressive elevation.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الدرجة نحو المنزلة، لكن يقال للمنزلة: درجة إذا اعتبرت بالصعود" — a degree is a station considered by ascent, not horizontal extension.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical steps of ascent. Metaphorical: "لفلان درجة رفيعة" — lofty rank; "امش في مدارج الحق" — walk in the paths of truth.
- Root: يوم (y-w-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: A day; a period of time from sunrise to sunset, or any duration whatsoever.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "اليوم يعبر به عن وقت طلوع الشمس إلى غروبها. وقد يعبر به عن مدة من الزمان أي مدة كانت" — the day denotes the time of the sun's rising to its setting, and may denote any period of time whatsoever.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the solar day. Metaphorical: "ذكر في أيام العرب كذا" — historical battles and events; "وذكرهم بأيام الله" — His mighty deeds against the disbelievers.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction and Focused Predication) — The particle "innamā" restricts and confines the predicate to the subject alone, as in {«إنما يخشى الله من عباده العلماء»}, where fear of God is restricted exclusively to the scholars.
10:55.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'Contemplation'

13:4.arabic: الأشكال والألوان والطعوم والصفات والأرابيح يفضل بعضها على بعض في الأكل تسقى بماء واحد وتخرج من أرض واحدة فإن قلت إن اختلافها باختلاف بذورها وأصولها فمتى كان فى النواة نخلة مطوقة لعناقيد الرطب ومتى كان فى حبة واحدة سمع سنابل فى كل سنبلة مائة ثم انظر إلى أرض البوادي وفتش ظاهرها وباطنها فتراها ترابا متشابها فإذا أنزل عليها الماء اهتزت وربت وأنبتت من كل زوج بهيج ألوانا مختلفة ونباتا متشابها وغير متشابه لكل واحد طعم وريح ولون وشكل يخالف الآخر فانظر إلى كثرتها واختلاف أصنافها وكثرة أشكالها ثم اختلاف طبائع النبات وكثرة م
13:4.english: For the beast has no power over that; but as for man, God created for him the power, then he disabled it and disbelieved in God's grace therein. So those are like cattle — nay, they are even further astray from the way {فَأُولَٰئِكَ كَالْأَنْعَامِ بَلْ هُمْ أَضَلُّ سَبِيلًا}.
13:4.section_title_en: On Contemplating the Earth, Its Rivers, Mountains, and Minerals — Section 1273
13:4.anchors:
- Root: فكر (f-k-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: التفكر: تأمل القلب وتدبر الشيء، والفكر: إعمال النظر في الشيء
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): الفكر: قوة العلم التي بها يدرك الإنسان، وقيل: هو ترتيب أمور معلومة للتأدي إلى مجهول
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): الفكر: تصرف القلب في النظر — literal: إعمال الروية؛ metaphorical: التفكر في ملكوت الله
- Root: ارض (arḍ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: الأرض: التي عليها الناس، وجمعها أرضون
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): الأرض: الجرم المقابل للسماء، ويعبر بها عن أسفل الشيء
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): literal: الأرض المهاد والفراش؛ metaphorical: تذلل الأرض وسكونها
- Root: دحا (d-ḥ-w) / مهد (m-h-d)
  * Lisan / Ayn: مهد: وطأ المكان وهيأه، والمهاد: الفراش الموطأ
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): المهد: الموضع المهيأ للصبي، والمهاد: الأرض الموطأة
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): literal: فرش الأرض وتمهيدها؛ metaphorical: جعلها قارة ساكنة لا تميد
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — the interposed clause "فانظر" after "إلى الأرض" maintains grammatical continuity while allowing rhetorical pause.
13:4.topic: Classical commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya Ulum al-Din, from 'Contemplation'

13:16.arabic: ومتعلقة بقدرته تصديقا له في قوله تعالى الله خالق كل شيء وفي قوله تعالى والله خلقكم وما تعملون وفي قوله تعالى وأسروا قولكم أو اجهروا به إنه عليم بذات الصدور ألا يعلم من خلق وهو اللطيف الخبير أمر العباد بالتحرز في أقوالهم وأفعالهم وإسرارهم وإضمارهم لعلمه بموارد أفعالهم واستدل على العلم بالخلق وكيف لا يكون خالقا لفعل العبد وقدرته تامة لا قصور فيها وهي متعلقة بحركة أبدان العباد والحركات متماثلة وتعلق القدرة بها لذاتها فما الذي يقصر تعلقها عن بعض الحركات دون البعض مع تماثلها أو كيف يكون الحيوان مستبدا با
13:16.english: Rather, the attribute of origination (ḥudūth) is established for bodies only by virtue of their being subject to change and the fluctuation of states. So how could their Creator share with them in the acceptance of change? And upon this is built [the doctrine] that His Speech (kalām) is eternal, subsisting in His Essence—only the sounds indicating it are originated. Just as one rationally apprehends the subsistence of a request for learning and the father's will for [his] child in the father's essence before the child is created—such that when the child is created, attains reason, and God creates for him a knowledge pertaining to what is in his father's heart of the request, the child becomes commanded by that very request which subsisted in his father's essence and whose existence endured until the time of his child's awareness of it—so let one rationally apprehend the subsistence of the command indicated by His words, Mighty and Majestic: {«اخلع نعليك»} "Take off your sandals" [Q 20:12], in God's Essence, and Moses—peace be upon him—becoming addressed by it after his existence, when God created for him a knowledge of that command and hearing of that eternal Speech.
13:16.section_title_en: The Revival of the Religious Sciences — Section 92: On the Divine Attributes of Eternity, Knowledge, Will, and the Third Pillar Concerning God's Acts
13:16.anchors:
- Root: قدم (q-d-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Primordial precedence; that which has no temporal beginning; eternal past (azal) and eternal future (abad).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Precedence either by time, by honor, or by ontological necessity—here, God's attributes are eternal in the sense that they are not subject to temporal origination.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "to precede." Metaphorical: that which cannot be conceived as non-existent posterior to its existence—applied to God's essence and attributes.
- Root: علم (ʿ-l-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Comprehension of a thing as it truly is; the indelible mark or trace by which one is guided.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Knowledge is the apprehension of a thing in its reality"—twofold: apprehension of the essence, and judgment concerning existence or non-existence. God's knowledge is eternal, encompassing all created things without renewal.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: perception and awareness. Metaphorical: the "signs" (maʿālim) of God's power—His knowledge is identical with His creative act, for "Does He who created not know?" {«ألا يعلم من خلق»}.
- Root: خلق (kh-l-q)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Measuring, proportioning, then bringing into existence upon a determined measure.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Origination from nothing without prior model—"He created the heavens and the earth" {«خلق السماوات والأرض»}—and also bringing forth from something, as man from a drop. All acts of creatures are God's creation.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the tailor's measuring before cutting. Metaphorical: God's bringing forth existence upon a measure dictated by wisdom—He is the sole Creator (al-Khāliq) of all acts, including those of His servants.
- Root: قتل (q-t-l)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Removal of the spirit from the body; also, intense subjugation.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The root meaning is the separation of soul from body, whether by an agent (qatl) or by natural death (mawt). Used here analogically: as "killer," "killed," and "killing" are mutually entailing, so are "knower," "known," and "knowledge."
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: slaying. Metaphorical: mutual entailment—just as no killer exists without a killing and a killed one, so no knower exists without knowledge and a known object.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب التلازم والتضايف (Mutual Entailment and Correlativity) — Terms like ʿālim/ʿilm/maʿlūm are correlatives (mutalāzimāt) that cannot be conceptually separated; the predicate necessitates the co-existence of its correlates in the intellect.
13:16.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Foundations of Belief'

13:16.arabic: عاجزون عن أنفسهم لا يملكون لأنفسهم نفعا ولا ضرا فكيف يملكون لغيرهم هذا في الدنيا فكيف في يوم لا يجزي والد عن ولده ولا مولود هو جاز عن والده شيئا بل تقول الأنبياء فيه نفسي نفسي فكيف يستبدل الجاهل عن ثواب الآخرة ونيل القرب عند الله ما يرتقبه بطمعه الكاذب في الدنيا من الناس فلا ينبغي أن نشك في أن المرائي بطاعة الله في سخط الله من حيث النقل والقياس جميعا هذا إذا لم يقصد الأجر فأما إذا قصد الأجر والحمد جميعا في صدقته أو صلاته فهو الشرك الذي يناقض الإخلاص وقد ذكرنا حكمه في كتاب الإخلاص ويدل على ما نقل
13:16.english: The Messenger of God, may God's peace and blessings be upon him, named it the lesser shirk (al-shirk al-aṣghar). The hadith naming riya' as the lesser shirk was transmitted by Ahmad from the hadith of Mahmud ibn Labid, and it has already preceded. Al-Tabarani also narrated it from the transmission of Mahmud ibn Labid from Rafi' ibn Khadij, making it part of Rafi's musnad, and it has also preceded recently. Al-Hakim recorded it and authenticated its chain from the hadith of Shaddad ibn Aws: "We used to count riya' on the day of the Messenger of God, may God's peace and blessings be upon him, as the lesser shirk."
13:16.anchors:
- Root: راءى (rā'ā)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of visual display, showing oneself; from الرؤية (seeing), implying making oneself seen.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Riya' is the seeking of station (manzilah) in hearts through acts of obedience — a subtle shirk because the actor's qasd (intention) is diverted from the Creator to creatures.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (haqiqah) = mutual seeing; metaphorical (majaz) = displaying deeds for the gaze of others, transferring the object of worship from God to His servants.
- Root: قصد (qaṣada)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To aim, intend, direct one's course toward a target; the straight path of intention.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Qasd is the straightness of a road; iqtisad (moderation) is praiseworthy between two extremes — here, the qasd of the actor is the very substance of the act's moral weight.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal = aiming at a physical target; metaphorical = the soul's inclination toward a goal, whether divine reward or human praise.
- Root: عظم (ʿaẓuma)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To be great, to magnify; ʿazamah = grandeur, majesty.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): ʿIẓam (magnification) is the heart's ascription of greatness to an object; when transferred from God to creatures, it constitutes the hidden kernel of shirk.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal = physical largeness; metaphorical = the heart's veneration (taʿẓīm) of a being, which is the true object of worship.
- Root: درج (daraja)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To ascend step by step; degrees of a ladder.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Darajah is a station considered by ascent; used for ranks of honor or degradation.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal = physical steps; metaphorical = graded levels of moral severity, as here: "degrees of riya'."
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين المبتدأ والخبر (Interposition between subject and predicate) — The periodic structure "اعلم أن بعض أبواب الرياء أشد وأغلظ من بعض" employs an embedded clause (أنّ + nominal sentence) requiring careful tracking of the governed accusative and its predicate to preserve the logical hierarchy of the author's taxonomy.
13:16.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Contemplation'

16:8.arabic: فيها وكم من الموجودات التى لا نعلمها كما قال الله تعالى ويخلق ما لا تعلمون سبحان الذي خلق الأزواج كلها مما تنبت الأرض ومن أنفسهم ومما لا يعلمون {وقال} وننشئكم فيما لا تعلمون {وإلى} ما يعرف أصلها وجملتها ولا يعرف تفصيلها فيمكننا أن نتفكر في تفصيلها وهي منقسمة إلى ما أدركناه بحس البصر وإلى ما لا ندركه بالبصر أما الذي لا ندركه بالبصر فكالملائكة والجن والشياطين والعرش والكرسي وغير ذلك ومجال الفكر في هذه الأشياء مما يضيق ويغمض فلنعدل إلى الأقرب إلى الأفهام وهي المدركات بحس البصر وذلك هو السموات السبع والأرض وما بينهما
16:8.english: We say: Created existents are divided into that whose origin is unknown to us, such that we cannot contemplate it—and how many are the existents we do not know! As God Most High said: {«وَيَخْلُقُ مَا لَا تَعْلَمُونَ»} (And He creates what you do not know — Q. 16:8), and {«سُبْحَانَ الَّذِي خَلَقَ الْأَزْوَاجَ كُلَّهَا مِمَّا تُنبِتُ الْأَرْضُ وَمِنْ أَنفُسِهِمْ وَمِمَّا لَا يَعْلَمُونَ»} (Glory be to Him who created all pairs, of what the earth grows, and of themselves, and of what they do not know — Q. 36:36), and He said: {«وَنُنشِئُكُمْ فِيمَا لَا تَعْلَمُونَ»} (And We raise you up in what you do not know — Q. 56:61). And [it is divided] into that whose origin and general nature are known, but whose detailed particulars are not known—so we are able to contemplate its details.
16:8.section_title_en: Exposition of the Method of Contemplation upon the Creation of God Most High
16:8.anchors:
- Root: فكر (f-k-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning is reflection, deliberation, and the movement of the mind over a matter to arrive at its reality.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In theological usage, *tafakkur* is the soul's journey through created things (al-makhlūqāt) to derive knowledge of the Creator—it is the bridge from the sensory to the intelligible.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) sense is mental consideration; metaphorical (majāz) extension applies it to the heart's "seeing" of divine wisdom latent in creation.
- Root: خلق (kh-l-q)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Root meaning is measuring, proportioning, and fashioning a thing with precise estimation.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): *Khalq* denotes origination from nothing (ibdāʿ) or creation of one thing from another, always upon a measure necessitated by wisdom.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the artisan's sizing of material before cutting; Metaphorical: God's bringing things into existence upon a measure that wisdom dictates—He is Rabb al-khalīqah.
- Root: بصر (b-ṣ-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning is sight, both ocular and perceptive.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): *Baṣar* applies to the eye's organ and its power, and to the heart's perceptive faculty (*baṣīrah*), as in {«فَكَشَفْنَا عَنكَ غِطَاءَكَ فَبَصَرُكَ الْيَوْمَ حَدِيدٌ»} (Q. 50:22).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical sight; Metaphorical: *ibṣār* as intellectual discernment—"هذه آية مبصرة" (this is an illuminating sign).
- Root: نفس (n-f-s)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning is the self, the soul, the vital principle.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): *Nafs* denotes the rational soul (al-rūḥ) and also the very essence (al-dhāt); in {«وَفِي أَنفُسِكُمْ أَفَلَا تُبْصِرُونَ»} (Q. 51:21) it refers to the human self as a microcosmic sign.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the self as animate entity; Metaphorical: the inner dimension of man as a locus of divine signs.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Specification and Restriction (Bāb al-Takhṣīṣ) — When a general term (like "everything in existence") is followed by a restrictive clause ("save God"), the syntax governs the scope of predication, ensuring the exception is precise and the universal claim is bounded.
16:8.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Contemplation'

16:52.arabic: الشكر فى السموات والأرض وله الحمد فى الأولى والآخرة والصلاة على محمد ذي المعجزات الظاهرة والآيات الباهرة وعلى آله وأصحابه وسلم تسليما كثيرا أما بعد فجدير بمن الموت مصرعه والتراب مضجعه والدود أنيسه ومنكر ونكير جليسه والقبر مقره وبطن الأرض مستقره والقيامة موعده والجنة أو النار مورده أن لا يكون له فكر إلا فى الموت ولا ذكر إلا له ولا استعداد إلا لأجله ولا تدبير إلا فيه ولا تطلع إلا إليه ولا تعريج إلا عليه ولا اهتمام إلا به ولا حول إلا حوله ولا انتظار وتربص إلا له وحقيق بأن يع
16:52.english: To proceed: Worthy is one whose place of downfall is death, whose bed is the dust, whose companion is the worm, whose boon-companions are Munkar and Nakīr, whose abode is the grave, whose resting-place is the belly of the earth, whose appointed time is the Resurrection, and whose destination is Paradise or the Fire — that he should have no thought except of death, no remembrance except of it, no preparation except for it, no deliberation except concerning it, no aspiration except toward it, no lingering except upon it, no concern except with it, no power except around it, and no waiting or tarrying except for it. And it is fitting that he should count himself among the dead and see himself among the inhabitants of the graves, for everything that is coming is near, and the distant is only that which is not coming. The Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "The shrewd one (al-kayyis) is he who subdues his soul and works for what comes after death" (1). And preparation for a thing will not be facilitated except upon the renewal of its remembrance in the heart, and its remembrance is not renewed except through recollection by lending ear to those things that remind of it and by looking upon those things that alert to it.
16:52.section_title_en: The Book of the Remembrance of Death and What Follows It — Introduction and Opening Homily
16:52.anchors:
- Root: موت (m-w-t)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root denotes cessation of vital faculty; death as transition, not annihilation.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Death is the divinely ordained terminus of corporeal life, gateway to reckoning; "أماته فأقبره" {«عبس/ 21»} implies divine disposal of the deceased.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: bodily death and burial. Metaphorical: "أحيا الله البلد الميت" — revival of barren land; death of hearts through heedlessness.
- Root: قبر (q-b-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Grave as the resting place of the dead; "المقبرة" as the site of interment.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "حتى زرتم المقابر" {«التكاثر/ 2»} — metonymy for death itself; the grave as prelude to resurrection.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: burial of the deceased. Metaphorical: "رفع قبراه" — the haughty one who raises his nose like a grave-mound, signifying pride.
- Root: حمد (ḥ-m-d)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Praise predicated upon volitional excellence; gratitude for beneficence.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): True praise (ḥamd) is due solely to God, whose acts are pure beneficence; distinct from mere thanks (shukr) for favors received.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "أحمد الله بجميع محامده" — praising God with all praises. Metaphorical: "أحمدت صنيعه" — approving an act as praiseworthy.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The periodic opening "الحمد لله الذي..." employs a suspended genitive construction (جار ومجرور) with a relative clause (صلة الموصول) that permits extended expansion, governing the entire homiletic sequence that follows.
16:52.topic: Al-Ghazali on the journey of the soul, death, and the Hereafter, from 'Remembrance of Death and Afterlife'

16:52.arabic: وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم يستغفر للعالم ما في السموات والأرض (3) وأي منصب يزيد على منصب من تشتغل ملائكة السموات والأرض بالاستغفار له وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم إن الحكمة تزيد الشريف شرفا وترفع المملوك حتى يدرك مدارك الملوك (4) وقد نبه بهذا على ثمراته في الدنيا ومعلوم أن الآخرة خير وأبقى وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم خصلتان لا يكونان في منافق حسن سمت وفقه في الدين (5) ولا تشكن في الحديث لنفاق بعض فقهاء الزمان فإنه ما أراد به الفقه الذي ظننته وسيأتي معنى الفقه وأدنى درجات الفقيه أن يعلم أن الآخرة خير من الدنيا
16:52.english: How He, Glorified and Exalted, began with Himself, then seconded with the angels, and thirded with the people of knowledge — and sufficient for you is this as honor, excellence, splendor, and nobility. And God, Exalted, said: {«يرفع الله الذين آمنوا منكم والذين أوتوا العلم درجات»} — "God will raise those who have believed among you and those who have been given knowledge, in degrees." Ibn ʿAbbās, may God be pleased with them both, said: For the scholars there are degrees above the believers, seven hundred degrees, and between each two degrees is a distance of five hundred years' journey.
16:52.section_title_en: The Book of Knowledge — Section 4: The Excellence of Knowledge and the Scholars
16:52.anchors:
- Root: علم (ʿ-l-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root meaning of knowing, perceiving a thing in its true reality; the act of apprehension and judgment.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "العلم: إدراك الشيء بحقيقته" — knowledge is the apprehension of a thing in its true reality, divided into apprehension of the essence and judgment of existence or non-existence.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) usage denotes genuine knowing; metaphorical (majāz) usage extends to signs, landmarks, and traces that guide to knowledge.
- Root: درج (d-r-j)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Degrees, steps, ascending stations; the root denotes gradation and progressive elevation.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الدرجة نحو المنزلة، لكن يقال للمنزلة: درجة إذا اعتبرت بالصعود" — a degree is a station considered by ascent, not horizontal extension.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical steps of ascent. Metaphorical: "لفلان درجة رفيعة" — lofty rank; "امش في مدارج الحق" — walk in the paths of truth.
- Root: يوم (y-w-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: A day; a period of time from sunrise to sunset, or any duration whatsoever.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "اليوم يعبر به عن وقت طلوع الشمس إلى غروبها. وقد يعبر به عن مدة من الزمان أي مدة كانت" — the day denotes the time of the sun's rising to its setting, and may denote any period of time whatsoever.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the solar day. Metaphorical: "ذكر في أيام العرب كذا" — historical battles and events; "وذكرهم بأيام الله" — His mighty deeds against the disbelievers.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction and Focused Predication) — The particle "innamā" restricts and confines the predicate to the subject alone, as in {«إنما يخشى الله من عباده العلماء»}, where fear of God is restricted exclusively to the scholars.
16:52.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'Contemplation'

17:85.arabic: وإنما هو أمر إلهي كما قال تعالى ويسئلونك عن الروح قل الروح من أمر ربي وكل المخلوقات منسوبة إلى الله تعالى ولكن نسبته أشرف من نسبة سائر أعضاء البدن فلله الخلق والأمر جميعا والأمر أعلى من الخلق وهذه الجوهرة النفيسة الحاملة لأمانة الله تعالى المتقدمة بهذه الرتبة على السموات والأرضين والجبال إذ أبين أن يحملنها وأشفقن منها من عالم الأمر ولا يفهم من هذا أنه تعريض بقدمها فإن القائل بقدم الأرواح مغرور جاهل لا يدري ما يقول فلنقبض عنان البيان عن هذا الفن فهو وراء ما نحن بصدده والمقصود أن هذه اللطيفة هي الساعية إلى قرب الرب
17:85.english: As for the attainment of happiness, none reaches it except the knowers of Allah the Exalted — and they are the brought-near (al-muqarrabūn), the blessed ones in the vicinity of Allah the Exalted, with repose and fragrance and the Garden of Delight. As for those who are barred below the summit of perfection, for them is deliverance and safety, as Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: {«فأما إن كان من المقربين فروح وريحان وجنة نعيم وأما إن كان من أصحاب اليمين فسلام لك من أصحاب اليمين»} (So if he is of those brought near, then repose and fragrance and a Garden of Delight. And if he is of the companions of the right, then peace to you from the companions of the right). And whoever does not set out toward the objective, nor rouses himself for it — or rouses himself toward it not with the intention of compliance and servitude, but rather for some immediate purpose — he is of the companions of the left and of the astray; for him is an entertainment of boiling water and a roasting in Hellfire.
17:85.section_title_en: The Science of the Path: On the Threefold Division of Knowledge and the Journey to God
17:85.anchors:
- Root: سلك (s-l-k)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To traverse, to pass through, to thread (as a needle through cloth); the path one takes through a terrain.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "السلوك: النفاذ في الطريق" — the penetrating passage through a road; used both literally (traversing a physical path) and metaphorically (the soul's passage through spiritual wayfaring).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "طريق مسلوك" (a trodden path); Metaphorical: "ذهب في مسلك خفي، وخذ في مسالك الحق" — going in a hidden course, taking the paths of truth. The term thus spans both physical travel and the interior journey of the soul.
- Root: قرب (q-r-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Nearness in place, time, or rank; kinship and proximity.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "القرب والبعد يتقابلان... ويستعمل ذلك في المكان، وفي الزمان، وفي النسبة، وفي الحظوة، والرعاية، والقدرة" — nearness and distance are opposites, used in place, time, relation, favor, care, and power. The theological sense here is nearness to God as station (ḥaẓwah) and favor.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "قرب منه وإليه" (he drew near to him); Metaphorical: "لقد قربت أمرا ما أدري ما هو" (you have brought near a matter I know not what it is) — indicating that proximity can be by rank and honor, not merely spatial.
- Root: علم (ʿ-l-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Knowledge, perception, cognition; the root from which ʿālim (knower) and ʿilm (knowledge) derive.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "العلم: إدراك الشيء بحقيقته" — knowledge is the apprehension of a thing in its true reality; two kinds: apprehension of the essence of a thing, and judgment upon a thing affirming or denying something of it.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "ما علمت بخبرك: ما شعرت به" (I did not know of your news: I was unaware of it); the term spans sensory awareness and intellectual certitude.
- Root: الي (a-l-y) [as in ألى/إلى]
  * Lisan / Ayn: The root of "إلى" (toward, unto) and "أولى" (more worthy); also related to "آل" (family, those who return to a head).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The root carries the sense of direction and destination — the "unto" of a journey's end.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): The prepositional force of "إلى" marks the terminus of motion, whether physical or spiritual.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب التشبيه والتقسيم الثلاثي (The Chapter of Analogy and Tripartite Division) — The author employs a structured analogy (tamthīl) dividing knowledge into three categories, each mapped to a stage of the pilgrimage journey (preparation, traversing the wilderness, and the rites themselves). The syntax moves from the concrete (physical journey) to the abstract (spiritual wayfaring), with each division governed by a parallel construction (qism... qism... qism).
17:85.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

17:85.arabic: سره للبشر فما أوتينا من العلم إلا قليلا ويكفينا في التصديق بذلك التجربة والمشاهدة فقد ورد الخبر به قال صلى الله عليه وسلم لو أن مؤمنا دخل إلى مجلس فيه مائة منافق واحد لجاء حتى يجلس إليه ولو أم منافقا دخل إلى مجلس فيه مائة ومؤمن ومنافق واحد لجاه حتى يجلس إليه وهذا يدل على أن شبه الشيء منجذب إليه بالطبع وإن كان هو لا يشعر به وكان مالك بن دينار يقول لا يتفق اثنان في عشرة إلا وفي أحدهما وصف من الآخر وإن أجناس الناس كأجناس الطير ولا يتفق نوعان من الطير في الطيران إلا وبينهما مناسبة قال فرأى ي
17:85.english: Nay, in the harmony of hearts there is a matter even more subtle than this. For affection may become firmly rooted between two persons without any comeliness of form, nor beauty of innate disposition or character, but solely due to a suitability that necessitates intimacy and concord. For the like of a thing is drawn to it by nature, and inward matters are hidden, having subtle causes that are not within human power to perceive. The Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, alluded to this when he said: {«الأرواح جنود مجندة فما تعارف منها ائتلف وما تناكر منها اختلف»} — "Spirits are conscripted soldiers; those that recognize one another unite, and those that reject one another diverge." Thus, mutual rejection is the result of disparity, and union is the result of the suitability that he expressed as "mutual recognition." In some wordings: {«الأرواح جنود مجندة تلتقي فتتشام في الهواء»} — "Spirits are conscripted soldiers; they meet and sniff one another in the air."
17:85.section_title_en: On Love for Allah's Sake and Hatred for Allah's Sake: The Subtle Realities of Spiritual Affinity
17:85.anchors:
- Root: ح ب ب (ḥ-b-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of love, affection, and endearment; the beloved (maḥbūb) is that toward which the heart inclines.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Love (maḥabbah) in the theological sense is the soul's inclination toward that which is pleasing — ultimately, the soul's attraction to Allah and His awliyā', distinguished from base desire (hawā).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): physical inclination and attachment. Metaphorical (majāz): the spiritual communion of souls and the intentional pursuit of companionship for religious ends.
- Root: ص ح ب (ṣ-ḥ-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Companionship (ṣuḥbah) — association, sitting together, and enduring presence with another.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Companionship as a voluntary act of association; in the religious context, brotherhood (ukhuwwah) in dīn is a deliberate covenant, not mere accident.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical proximity and sitting together. Metaphorical: the soul's affinity and harmonious union with another's character.
- Root: ن س ب (n-s-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Proportion, relation, and congruence; the basis of similarity.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Munāsabah — the spiritual correspondence between created souls, preordained in the divine decree.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: genealogical or categorical relation. Metaphorical: the hidden congruity of temperaments that draws souls together.
- Root: أ ل ف (ʾ-l-f)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Union, harmony, and the taming of what is disparate into concord.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): I'tilāf — the divinely ordained concord among souls, as opposed to tanāfur (mutual aversion).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: to unite or reconcile. Metaphorical: the spontaneous attraction of like souls, as expressed in the prophetic tradition of "spirits as conscripted soldiers."
- Sibawayh Rule: The Division of the Sentence into Conditional and Categorical Clauses (Bāb al-Sharṭ wa al-Jazāʾ) — governing the logical structure of "if... then..." constructions that articulate the causal relationship between love, companionship, and their objects.
17:85.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Duties of Brotherhood'

17:85.arabic: قال سبحانه ويسألونك عن الروح قل الروح من أمر ربي أو معنى كونه ربانيا أنه من أسرار علوم المكاشفة ولا رخصة في إظهاره إذا لم يظهره رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم // حديث أنه صلى الله عليه وسلم لم يظهر سر الروح أخرجه البخاري من حديث ابن مسعود وقد تقدم ولكنك قبل معرفة ذلك تعلم أن للقلب ميلا إلى صفات بهيمية كالأكل والوقاع وإلى صفات سبعية كالقتل والضرب والإيذاء وإلى صفات شيطانية كالمكر والخديعة والإغواء وإلى صفات ربوبية كالكبر والعز والتجبر وطلب الاستعلاء وذلك لأنه مركب من أصول مختلفة يطول شرحها وتفصيلها
17:85.english: As for the second cause — and it is the stronger one — it is because the spirit (al-rūḥ) is a divine command (amr rabbānī), by which God — exalted is He — described it, when He said, glorified and majestic: {«وَيَسْأَلُونَكَ عَنِ الرُّوحِ قُلِ الرُّوحُ مِنْ أَمْرِ رَبِّي»} ("And they ask you concerning the spirit; say: The spirit is of the command of my Lord") [Al-Isrā', 17:85]. The meaning of its being "divine" (rabbāniyyan) is that it belongs to the secrets of the sciences of unveiling (asrār ʿulūm al-mukāshafah), and there is no license to disclose it, since the Messenger of God — may God's peace and blessings be upon him — did not disclose it. [Regarding the hadith that he — peace be upon him — did not reveal the secret of the spirit, it is reported by Al-Bukhārī from the narration of Ibn Masʿūd, and it has preceded.]
17:85.section_title_en: The Second Cause of the Heart's Affinity for Sovereignty — The Divine Command and the Innate Love of Uniqueness in Existence
17:85.anchors:
- Root: روح (r-w-ḥ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core sense of breath, spirit, and that which animates; Al-Farahidi notes its usage for the vital principle.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الروح" is the divine subtlety (al-laṭīfah al-rabbāniyyah) that is the seat of knowledge and command, distinct from corporeal nature; its reality is from the unseen order of God.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) for the animating spirit; metaphorical (majāz) extension to "command" (amr) as a mode of divine origination without intermediary.
- Root: رب (r-b-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Lordship, nurturing, and ownership; the root implies mastery and independent governance.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الربوبية" (rubūbiyyah) denotes exclusive sovereignty and self-subsistence, entailing uniqueness (tafarruf) in essence and attributes.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal for lordship over a domain; metaphorical for the soul's innate aspiration to solitary perfection, as in the reported saying of Pharaoh.
- Root: كمل (k-m-l)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Completeness and perfection; the absence of deficiency or peer.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Perfection (kamāl) is the attribute of the divine essence; any participation in existence entails imperfection, for the unique alone is complete.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal for a thing's full realization; metaphorical for the soul's love of domination as a shadow of divine perfection.
- Root: ملك (m-l-k)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Possession, power, and dominion; the capacity to dispose of a thing.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الاستيلاء" (istīlā') is a form of mastery; knowledge is a mode of possession, for the known is encompassed by the knower.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal for physical control; metaphorical for intellectual apprehension as a type of conquest.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Restriction and Specification (al-ḥaṣr wa al-taqyīd bi-innamā) — The phrase "إنما الكمال بعد أن يسلم التفرد بالوجود" restricts perfection to the condition of secured uniqueness, governing the predicate's scope.
17:85.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'Condemnation of Status and Ostentation'

17:85.arabic: يعرفون منها إلا قدرا يسيرا بالإضافة إلى ما في علم الله تعالى {وما أوتيتم من العلم إلا قليلا} فإذن كل من استعمل شيئا في جهة غير الجهة التي خلق لها ولا على الوجه الذي أريد به فقد كفر فيه نعمة الله تعالى فمن ضرب غيره بيده فقد كفر نعمة اليد إذ خلقت له اليد ليدفع بها عن نفسه ما يهلكه ويأخذ ما ينفعه لا ليهلك بها غيره ومن نظر إلى وجه غير المحرم فقد كفر نعمة العين ونعمة الشمس إذ الإبصار يتم بهما وإنما خلقتا ليبصر بهما ما ينفعه في دينه ودنياه ويتقي بهما ما يضره فيهما فقد استعملها في غير ما اريد به وهذا لأن المراد من خلق الخلق وخلق الدنيا وأسباب
17:85.english: ...and there is no omnipotent one save the King, the Compeller. And when the covering is lifted from the eyes of the heedless, and they behold the matter to be thus, they will hear at that time the call of the Proclaimer: {«لِمَنِ الْمُلْكُ الْيَوْمَ لِلَّهِ الْوَاحِدِ الْقَهَّارِ»} — "To whom belongs the sovereignty this Day? To God, the One, the Compeller" {Q 40:16}. And indeed sovereignty belonged to God, the One, the Compeller, every single day — not exclusively on that day — but the heedless do not hear this proclamation save on that day. Thus it is tidings of what is renewed for the heedless of the unveiling of states, at a time when the unveiling will not benefit them. So we seek refuge in God, the Forbearing, the Generous, from ignorance and blindness, for it is the root cause of destruction.
17:85.section_title_en: The Unveiling of Sovereignty and the Discernment of What God Loves from What He Abhors
17:85.anchors:
- Root: كشف (kashafa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Removal of a covering; disclosure of what was hidden.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Unveiling of the unseen realities (mukāshafah) — the lifting of the veil from the heart's eye to perceive things as they truly are.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): removal of a physical covering. Metaphorical (majāz): the disclosure of intellectual or spiritual realities to the percipient.
- Root: ملك (malaka)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Possession, dominion, sovereignty; the one who possesses is malik (king).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): True sovereignty (mulk) belongs exclusively to God; all created dominion is borrowed and ephemeral.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: royal authority. Metaphorical: absolute, unshared dominion — as in the Qur'anic proclamation of sole kingship on the Day of Judgment.
- Root: شكر (shakara)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Gratitude; acknowledgment of beneficence.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Thankfulness is the recognition of the Benefactor and the employment of His blessings in that which pleases Him — not mere verbal praise.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: requital of favor. Metaphorical: the use of blessings in obedience to the Giver, which is the true meaning of gratitude.
- Root: كفر (kafara)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Covering, concealing; ingratitude that veils the recognition of favor.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Kufr is the covering of blessings by failing to employ them in the manner intended by the Giver, or by employing them in what He abhors.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: covering a seed in the earth. Metaphorical: the concealment of God's blessings through misuse or neglect.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Restriction and Focused Predication (al-ḥaṣr wa al-taqyīd bi-innamā) — restricting the means of gratitude to two exclusive cognitive faculties, and the restriction of creation's purpose to the sole end of attaining unto God.
17:85.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Contemplation'

18:109.arabic: لو كان البحر مدادا لكلمات ربي لنفد البحر قبل أن تنفد كلمات ربي ولو جئنا بمثله مددا ولذلك قال علي رضي الله عنه لو شئت لأوقرت سبعين بعيرا من تفسير فاتحة الكتاب فالغرض مما ذكرناه التنبيه على طريق التفهيم لينفتح بابه فأما الاستقصاء فلا مطمع فيه ومن لم يكن له فهم ما في القرآن ولو في أدنى الدرجات دخل في قوله تعالى ومنهم من يستمع إليك حتى إذا خرجوا من عندك قالوا للذين أوتوا العلم ماذا قال آنفا أولئك الذين طبع الله على قلوبهم والطابع هي الموانع التي سنذكرها في م
18:109.english: I say: These meanings are buried treasures that are not unveiled except to the divinely aided ones. To this 'Ali — may God be pleased with him — alluded by his saying: "The Messenger of God — may God's peace and blessings be upon him — did not confide to me anything that he concealed from the people, except that God — mighty and majestic — grants to a servant understanding (fahm) of His Book. So let one be eager in seeking that understanding." (1) And Ibn Mas'ud — may God be pleased with him — said: "Whoever desires the knowledge of the first and the last, let him stir up the Qur'an." And the greatest of the sciences of the Qur'an lie beneath the names of God — mighty and majestic — and His attributes, for most of creation have grasped from them only matters befitting their understandings and have not stumbled upon their depths.
18:109.section_title_en: The Revival of the Religious Sciences — Section 228: On the Inner Meanings of the Qur'an and the Removal of Obstacles to Understanding
18:109.anchors:
- Root: فهم (f-h-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Comprehension, discernment, the faculty by which one grasps meanings
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الفهم: هيئة للإنسان بها يتحقق معاني ما يحسن" — a disposition by which one verifies the realities of what is perceived; distinct from mere hearing or transmission
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: swift apprehension; Metaphorical: the divine gift of insight into hidden meanings, as in the verse {ففهمناها سليمان}
- Root: قلب (q-l-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Turning, overturning, transformation from one state to another
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "قلب الشيء: تصريفه وصرفه عن وجه إلى وجه" — the heart as that which is perpetually turned and overturned between states
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical turning; Metaphorical: the heart as the seat of understanding that is veiled or illuminated, rusted or polished
- Root: سمع (s-m-')
  * Lisan / Ayn: Hearing, the auditory faculty
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "السمع: قوة في الأذن به يدرك الأصوات" — extends metaphorically to comprehension and obedience; "أو ألقى السمع وهو شهيد" — one who casts his hearing while present
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: auditory perception; Metaphorical: attentive obedience and receptive understanding
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد (Restriction & Specification) — governing the precise delimitation of predicates such as "إنما يتذكر أولوا الألباب" where restriction confines the action to its proper subject
18:109.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Contemplation'

18:109.arabic: وقدرته وجلاله وعظمته وإحصاء ذلك غير ممكن لأنه لو كان البحر مدادا لذلك لنفد البحر قبل أن ينفد عشر عشيره ولكنا نشير إلى جمل منه ليكون ذلك كالمثال لماعداه فنقول الموجودات المخلوقة منقسمة الى مالا يعرف أصلها فلا يمكننا التفكر فيها وكم من الموجودات التى لا نعلمها كما قال الله تعالى ويخلق ما لا تعلمون سبحان الذي خلق الأزواج كلها مما تنبت الأرض ومن أنفسهم ومما لا يعلمون {وقال} وننشئكم فيما لا تعلمون {وإلى} ما يعرف أصلها وجملتها ولا يعرف تفصيلها فيمكننا أن نتفكر في تفصيلها وهي منقسمة إلى ما أدركناه بحس البصر وإلى ما لا ندركه بالبصر أما
18:109.english: We say: Created existents are divided into that whose origin is unknown to us, such that we cannot contemplate it—and how many are the existents we do not know! As God Most High said: {«وَيَخْلُقُ مَا لَا تَعْلَمُونَ»} (And He creates what you do not know — Q. 16:8), and {«سُبْحَانَ الَّذِي خَلَقَ الْأَزْوَاجَ كُلَّهَا مِمَّا تُنبِتُ الْأَرْضُ وَمِنْ أَنفُسِهِمْ وَمِمَّا لَا يَعْلَمُونَ»} (Glory be to Him who created all pairs, of what the earth grows, and of themselves, and of what they do not know — Q. 36:36), and He said: {«وَنُنشِئُكُمْ فِيمَا لَا تَعْلَمُونَ»} (And We raise you up in what you do not know — Q. 56:61). And [it is divided] into that whose origin and general nature are known, but whose detailed particulars are not known—so we are able to contemplate its details.
18:109.section_title_en: Exposition of the Method of Contemplation upon the Creation of God Most High
18:109.anchors:
- Root: فكر (f-k-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning is reflection, deliberation, and the movement of the mind over a matter to arrive at its reality.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In theological usage, *tafakkur* is the soul's journey through created things (al-makhlūqāt) to derive knowledge of the Creator—it is the bridge from the sensory to the intelligible.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) sense is mental consideration; metaphorical (majāz) extension applies it to the heart's "seeing" of divine wisdom latent in creation.
- Root: خلق (kh-l-q)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Root meaning is measuring, proportioning, and fashioning a thing with precise estimation.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): *Khalq* denotes origination from nothing (ibdāʿ) or creation of one thing from another, always upon a measure necessitated by wisdom.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the artisan's sizing of material before cutting; Metaphorical: God's bringing things into existence upon a measure that wisdom dictates—He is Rabb al-khalīqah.
- Root: بصر (b-ṣ-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning is sight, both ocular and perceptive.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): *Baṣar* applies to the eye's organ and its power, and to the heart's perceptive faculty (*baṣīrah*), as in {«فَكَشَفْنَا عَنكَ غِطَاءَكَ فَبَصَرُكَ الْيَوْمَ حَدِيدٌ»} (Q. 50:22).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical sight; Metaphorical: *ibṣār* as intellectual discernment—"هذه آية مبصرة" (this is an illuminating sign).
- Root: نفس (n-f-s)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning is the self, the soul, the vital principle.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): *Nafs* denotes the rational soul (al-rūḥ) and also the very essence (al-dhāt); in {«وَفِي أَنفُسِكُمْ أَفَلَا تُبْصِرُونَ»} (Q. 51:21) it refers to the human self as a microcosmic sign.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the self as animate entity; Metaphorical: the inner dimension of man as a locus of divine signs.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Specification and Restriction (Bāb al-Takhṣīṣ) — When a general term (like "everything in existence") is followed by a restrictive clause ("save God"), the syntax governs the scope of predication, ensuring the exception is precise and the universal claim is bounded.
18:109.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Contemplation'

20:113.arabic: والقناعة وقيل هو الذى يحدث مشاهدة وتقوى ولذلك قال تعالى {لعلهم يتقون أو يحدث لهم ذكرا} وإن أردت أن تفهم كيفية تغير الحال بالفكر فمثاله ما ذكرناه من أمر الآخرة فإن الفكر يعرفنا أن الآخرة أولى بالإيثار فإذا رسخت هذه المعرفة يقينا
20:113.english: Thus, thought is more excellent than the totality of works. For this reason it was said: "An hour of reflection is better than a year of worship" (tafakkur sāʿah khayr min ʿibādah sanah). And it was said [of the reflector] that he is the one who moves from detested things (al-makārih) to beloved things (al-maḥābb), and from desire (al-raghbah) and greed (al-ḥirṣ) to renunciation (al-zuhd) and contentment (al-qanāʿah). And it was said that he is the one who engenders witnessing (mushāhadah) and god-fearingness (taqwā). Therefore God Most High said: {«لعلهم يتقون أو يحدث لهم ذكرا»} — "That perhaps they may fear [God], or that it may produce for them a remembrance" (Q. 20:113). And if you wish to understand how the state is changed by thought, its example is what we have mentioned concerning the matter of the Hereafter: for thought makes us know that the Hereafter is more worthy of preference; and when this knowledge becomes firmly rooted as certainty (yaqīnan)...
20:113.section_title_en: On Reflection and Contemplation — The Fruits of Thought and the Hierarchy of Knowledge
20:113.anchors:
- Root: فكر (F-K-R)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of turning a matter over in the mind, deliberating.
