  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الفكرة: قوة مطرقة للعلم إلى المعلوم، والتفكر: جولان تلك القوة بحسب نظر العقل" — Thought is the power that drives knowledge toward the known; reflection is the circulation of that power according to rational consideration, unique to humans.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal sense of mental movement and circulation; metaphorically, "مازالت فكرتك مغاص الدرر" — one's thought as a diver's plunge for pearls.
- Root: عرف (ʿ-R-F)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To know by tracing the mark (ʿaraf) of a thing.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "المعرفة والعرفان: إدراك الشيء بتفكر وتدبر لأثره" — Knowledge (maʿrifah) is the apprehension of a thing through reflection and deliberation upon its trace/effect; it is more specific than ʿilm.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: to recognize; metaphorical: "لأعرفن لك ما صنعت" — to requite/reward one for one's deed.
- Root: ذكر (Dh-K-R)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To remember, to recall, to keep present in the mind.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Remembrance as the opposite of forgetfulness (nisyān); the heart's retention of what was previously apprehended.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: verbal mention; metaphorical: the heart's presence with what is remembered.
- Root: عبر (ʿ-B-R)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To cross over, to traverse from one side to another.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): ʿIʿtibār (consideration) is derived from ʿubūr (crossing) — passing from known things to unknown things.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: crossing a valley or river; metaphorical: interpreting a dream (ʿabara al-ruʾyā) — passing from the image to its meaning.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الترادف والتغاير (Synonymy and Distinction) — Terms may share a single referent (musammā) yet differ in semantic specification (takhṣīṣ), like al-ṣārim, al-muhannad, and al-sayf all denoting the sword but from different aspects.

21:32.arabic: ثم مسح بها سبلته (1) أى تجاوزها من غير فكر وذم المعرضين عنها فقال وجعلنا السماء سقفا محفوظا وهم عن آياتها معرضون فأى نسبة لجميع البحار والأرض إلى السماء وهى متغيرات على القرب والسموات صلاب شداد محفوظات عن التغير إلى أن يبلغ الكتاب أجله ولذلك سماه الله تعالى محفوظا فقال وجعلنا السماء سقفا محفوظا وقال سبحانه وبنينا فوقكم سبعا شدادا {وقال} أأنتم أشد خلقا أم السماء بناها رفع سمكها فسواها فانظر إلى الملكوت لترى عجائب العز والجبروت ولا تظنن أن معنى النظر إلى الملكوت بأن تمد البصر إليه فترى زرقة السماء وضوء الكواكب وتفرقها فإن البهائم تشاركك فى هذا النظر فإن كان
21:32.english: I say — and of the heaven with its woven structure, and the heaven and what built it; and His saying, may He be exalted: {«And the sun and its morning brightness, and the moon when it follows it»} (Q 91:1-2); and His saying, may He be exalted: {«Nay, I swear by the slinking stars, the runners, the sinkers»} (Q 81:15-16); and His saying, may He be exalted: {«And the star when it falls — nay, I swear by the positions of the stars, and verily it is a mighty oath, if you but knew»} (Q 56:75-76). You have thus come to know that the wonders of the filthy drop of semen — the first and last generations have fallen short of comprehending them. So if God swore by such things, what is your assumption concerning that by which God, may He be exalted, swore, and upon which He made provisions dependent, and to which He annexed them, saying, may He be exalted: {«And in the heaven is your provision and that which you are promised»} (Q 51:22)? And He praised those who reflect upon it, saying: {«And they reflect upon the creation of the heavens and the earth»} (Q 3:191). And the Messenger of God, may God's peace and blessing be upon him, said: "Woe to him who recites this verse and then wipes his moustache with it" — that is, passes over it without reflection. And He censured those who turn away from it, saying: {«And We made the heaven a protected roof, yet from its signs they turn away»} (Q 21:32). So what comparison is there between all the seas and the earth, on the one hand, and the heaven, on the other — given that the former are subject to rapid changes, while the heavens are solid, mighty, and preserved from change until the Book reaches its appointed term? For this reason God, may He be exalted, called it "protected," saying: {«And We made the heaven a protected roof»} (Q 21:32); and He said, glory be to Him: {«And We built above you seven mighty ones»} (Q 78:12); and He said: {«Are you stronger in creation or the heaven? He built it, He raised high its roof and fashioned it»} (Q 79:27-28).
21:32.section_title_en: On Contemplating the Kingdom of the Heavens (التفكر في ملكوت السموات)
21:32.anchors:
- Root: م ل ك (malaka)
  * Lisan / Ayn: الملك: القوة على التصرف، والملكوت: زيادة الميم للمبالغة كالرهبوت والرحموت
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): الملكوت: عالم الغيب الذي لا تدركه الحواس، والملك: عالم الشهادة المحسوس
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): الملكوت مجاز عن باطن الملك وسرّه، لا عن ظاهره المحسوس
- Root: س م و (sama)
  * Lisan / Ayn: السماء: كل ما علاك فأظلك، وأصلها السمو بمعنى الارتفاع
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): السماء: الجرم المقابل للأرض، وتستعمل بمعنى العلو والملكوت الأعلى
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "سقفا محفوظا" حقيقة في الحفظ عن التغير والاضمحلال
- Root: غ ي ب (ghayb)
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): الغيب: ما استتر عن الحواس، ويقال للشيء غيب باعتباره بالناس لا بالله تعالى، فإنه لا يغيب عنه شيء
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): الغيب والملكوت مترادفان في اصطلاح القرآن لما غاب عن الأبصار
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — جواز تقديم المعمول وتأخيره لمراعاة البلاغة والمقام

22:5.arabic: الله من أرذل الأشياء ثم من أقذرها إذ قد خلقه من تراب ثم من نطفة ثم من علقة ثم من مضغة ثم جعله عظما ثم كسا العظم لحما فقد كان هذا بداية وجوده حيث كان شيئا مذكورا فما صار شيئا مذكورا إلا وهو على أخس الأوصاف والنعوت إذ لم يخلق في ابتدائه كاملا بل خلقه جمادا ميتا لا يسمع ولا يبصر ولا يحس ولا يتحرك ولا ينطق ولا يبطش ولا يدرك ولا يعلم فبدأ بموته قبل حياته وبضعفه قبل قوته وبجهله قبل علمه وبعماه قبل بصره وبصممه قبل سمعه وببكمه قبل نطقه وبضلالته قبل هداه وبفقره قبل غناه وبعجزه قبل قدرته فهذا معنى قوله من أي شيء خلقه من نطفة خلقه فقدره و
22:5.english: As for his knowledge of his Lord, His greatness, and His glory — the discourse thereon is lengthy, and it is the ultimate end of the science of unveiling (ʿilm al-mukāshafah). As for his knowledge of himself, that too is lengthy; but we shall mention therefrom that which benefits in arousing humility and lowliness. And it suffices him to understand the meaning of a single verse in the Book of God — for in the Qurʾān is the knowledge of the first and the last, for him whose inner sight has been opened. God, may He be exalted, has said: {«قُتِلَ الْإِنْسَانُ مَا أَكْفَرَهُ ۝ مِنْ أَيِّ شَيْءٍ خَلَقَهُ ۝ مِنْ نُطْفَةٍ خَلَقَهُ فَقَدَّرَهُ ۝ ثُمَّ السَّبِيلَ يَسَّرَهُ ۝ ثُمَّ أَمَاتَهُ فَأَقْبَرَهُ ۝ ثُمَّ إِذَا شَاءَ أَنْشَرَهُ»} [ʿAbasa: 17–22] — "May man be killed! How ungrateful he is! From what thing did He create him? From a drop of fluid He created him and proportioned him. Then the path He made easy for him. Then He causes him to die and buries him. Then when He wills, He raises him." The verse has pointed to the first origin of man, to the last of his affair, and to his middle state. Let man, then, look upon that, in order to understand the meaning of this verse.
22:5.section_title_en: Exposition of the Character Traits of the Humble and the Sum Total of Wherein the Effect of Humility and Arrogance Appears — and the Exposition of the Method of Treating Arrogance and Acquiring Humility
22:5.anchors:
- Root: تواضع (tawāḍuʿ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Root و-ض-ع: to place down, lower, set in a low position; al-tawāḍuʿ is self-lowering, the voluntary assumption of lowness.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-waḍʿ is placing a thing in a station; tawāḍuʿ is the soul's self-abasement before truth and before the Creator, opposed to takabbur (self-elevation).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Haqīqah: physical lowering of position. Majāz: the soul's humility and abandonment of claims to eminence.
- Root: كبر (kibr)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Root ك-ب-ر: bigness, magnitude; al-kibriyāʾ is exclusive divine majesty; al-kibr (arrogance) is the creature's false claim to that majesty.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-kibr is the soul's self-magnification, a claim to a station of greatness that belongs to God alone; it is the root of all disobedience.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Haqīqah: physical greatness. Majāz: the heart's disdain of others and refusal of truth — the blameworthy kibr.
- Root: نطف (nuṭfah)
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-nuṭfah: pure water, used for the seminal fluid. {«ثُمَّ جَعَلْنَاهُ نُطْفَةً فِي قَرَارٍ مَكِينٍ»} [Al-Muʾminūn: 13].
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Haqīqah: clear water, little or much. Majāz: "laylah naṭūf" — a night raining until morning.
- Root: خلق (khalaqa)
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-khalq: measured estimation (taqdīr mustaqīm); used for bringing forth from nothing without model, and for producing a thing from another thing.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Haqīqah: the tailor's cutting cloth to measure. Majāz: God's origination of creatures upon a measure necessitated by wisdom.
- Sibawayh Rule: Bāb al-ʿaṭf ʿalā al-ḍamīr al-marfūʿ al-muttaṣil (Coordination upon the connected nominative pronoun) — permissible when preceded by an explicit subject, as in "خلقه من نطفة فقدره" where the sequence of verbs coordinates without repetition of the pronoun, each verb governing its own object in ordered succession.

22:5.arabic: فانظر إلى الأرض وهى ميتة فإذا أنزل عليها الماء اهتزت وربت واخضرت وأنبتت عجائب النبات وخرجت منها أصناف الحيوانات ثم انظر كيف أحكم جوانب الأرض بالجبال الراسيات الشوامخ الصم الصلاب وكيف أودع المياه تحتها ففجر العيون وأسال الأنهار تجري على وجهها وأخرج من الحجارة اليابسة ومن التراب الكدر ماء رقيقا عذبا صافيا زلالا وجعل به كل شيء حي فأخرج به فنون الأشجار والنبات من حب وعنب وقضب وزيتون ونخل ورمان وفواكه كثيرة لا تحصى مختلفة الأشكال والألوان والطعوم والصفات والأرابيح يفضل بعضها على بعض في الأكل تسقى بماء واحد وت
22:5.english: For the beast has no power over that; but as for man, God created for him the power, then he disabled it and disbelieved in God's grace therein. So those are like cattle — nay, they are even further astray from the way {فَأُولَٰئِكَ كَالْأَنْعَامِ بَلْ هُمْ أَضَلُّ سَبِيلًا}.
22:5.section_title_en: On Contemplating the Earth, Its Rivers, Mountains, and Minerals — Section 1273
22:5.anchors:
- Root: فكر (f-k-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: التفكر: تأمل القلب وتدبر الشيء، والفكر: إعمال النظر في الشيء
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): الفكر: قوة العلم التي بها يدرك الإنسان، وقيل: هو ترتيب أمور معلومة للتأدي إلى مجهول
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): الفكر: تصرف القلب في النظر — literal: إعمال الروية؛ metaphorical: التفكر في ملكوت الله
- Root: ارض (arḍ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: الأرض: التي عليها الناس، وجمعها أرضون
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): الأرض: الجرم المقابل للسماء، ويعبر بها عن أسفل الشيء
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): literal: الأرض المهاد والفراش؛ metaphorical: تذلل الأرض وسكونها
- Root: دحا (d-ḥ-w) / مهد (m-h-d)
  * Lisan / Ayn: مهد: وطأ المكان وهيأه، والمهاد: الفراش الموطأ
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): المهد: الموضع المهيأ للصبي، والمهاد: الأرض الموطأة
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): literal: فرش الأرض وتمهيدها؛ metaphorical: جعلها قارة ساكنة لا تميد
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — the interposed clause "فانظر" after "إلى الأرض" maintains grammatical continuity while allowing rhetorical pause.

22:5.arabic: انظر إلى أرض البوادي وفتش ظاهرها وباطنها فتراها ترابا متشابها فإذا أنزل عليها الماء اهتزت وربت وأنبتت من كل زوج بهيج ألوانا مختلفة ونباتا متشابها وغير متشابه لكل واحد طعم وريح ولون وشكل يخالف الآخر فانظر إلى كثرتها واختلاف أصنافها وكثرة أشكالها ثم اختلاف طبائع النبات وكثرة منافعه وكيف أودع الله تعالى العقاقير المنافع الغريبة فهذا النبات يغذي وهذا يقوي وهذا يحيي وهذا يقتل وهذا يبرد وهذا يسخن وهذا إذا حصل في المعدة قمع الصفراء من أعماق العروق وهذا يستحيل إلى الصفراء وهذا يقمع البلغم والسوداء وهذا يستحيل إليهما وهذا يصفى الدم وهذا يستحل دما وهذا يفرح وهذا ينوم و
22:5.english: For the beast has no power over that; but as for man, God created for him the power, then he disabled it and disbelieved in God's grace therein. So those are like cattle — nay, they are even further astray from the way {فَأُولَٰئِكَ كَالْأَنْعَامِ بَلْ هُمْ أَضَلُّ سَبِيلًا}.

23:12.arabic: ثم ذكر كيف جعل النطفة علقة والعلقة مضغة والمضغة عظاما فقال تعالى ولقد خلقنا الإنسان من سلالة من طين ثم جعلناه نطفة في قرار مكين ثم خلقنا النطفة علقة الآية فتكرير ذكر النطفة في الكتاب العزيز ليس ليسمع لفظه ويترك التفكر في معناه فانظر الآن إلى النطفة وهي قطرة من الماء قذرة لو تركت ساعة ليضربها الهواء فسدت وأنتنت كيف أخرجها رب الأرباب من الصلب والترائب وكيف جمع بين الذكر والأنثى وألقى الألفة والمحبة في قلوبهم وكيف قادهم بسلسلة المحبة والشهوة إلى الاجتماع وكيف استخرج النطفة من الرجل بحركة الوقاع وكيف استجلب دم الحيض من أعماق العروق وجمعه في الرحم ثم كيف خلق المولود من النطفة وسقاه بماء الحيض وغ
23:12.english: I say: The Exalted said: {أَلَمْ يَكُ نُطْفَةً مِنْ مَنِيٍّ يُمْنَىٰ ثُمَّ كَانَ عَلَقَةً فَخَلَقَ فَسَوَّىٰ} [Was he not a sperm-drop from semen emitted? Then he was a clinging clot, and He created and proportioned him] (Al-Qiyamah: 37-38). And the Exalted said: {أَلَمْ نَخْلُقْكُمْ مِنْ مَاءٍ مَهِينٍ فَجَعَلْنَاهُ فِي قَرَارٍ مَكِينٍ إِلَىٰ قَدَرٍ مَعْلُومٍ} [Did We not create you from a despicable fluid, then We placed it in a firm resting-place for a known term?] (Al-Mursalat: 20-22). And He said: {أَوَلَمْ يَرَ الْإِنْسَانُ أَنَّا خَلَقْنَاهُ مِنْ نُطْفَةٍ فَإِذَا هُوَ خَصِيمٌ مُبِينٌ} [Does man not see that We created him from a sperm-drop, yet behold, he is a manifest adversary?] (Ya-Sin: 77). And He said: {إِنَّا خَلَقْنَا الْإِنْسَانَ مِنْ نُطْفَةٍ أَمْشَاجٍ} [Indeed, We created man from a mixed sperm-drop] (Al-Insan: 2). Then He mentioned how He made the sperm-drop a clinging clot, the clot a chewed lump, and the lump bones, saying: {وَلَقَدْ خَلَقْنَا الْإِنْسَانَ مِنْ سُلَالَةٍ مِنْ طِينٍ ثُمَّ جَعَلْنَاهُ نُطْفَةً فِي قَرَارٍ مَكِينٍ ثُمَّ خَلَقْنَا النُّطْفَةَ عَلَقَةً} [And indeed We created man from an extract of clay, then We made him a sperm-drop in a firm resting-place, then We created the sperm-drop into a clinging clot] (Al-Mu'minun: 12-14), to the end of the verse.
23:12.section_title_en: The Wonders of Human Creation from a Sperm-Drop — Section 1269
23:12.anchors:
- Root: نطف (n-ṭ-f)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Pure, clear water; a drop of fluid; the seminal fluid; also pearl.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "النطفة: الماء الصافي" — the sperm-drop as pure water, used Quranically for the seminal fluid; a technical term for the initial stage of human embryological creation.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): "الماء الصافي قل أو كثر" — clear water, little or much. Metaphorical (Majaz): "ليلة نطوف: مطرت حتى الصباح" — a night of continuous rain, extending the root's sense of flowing/pouring.
- Root: خلق (kh-l-q)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Measuring, estimating, fashioning precisely; creating from nothing or from a prior substance.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الخلق أصله: التقدير المستقيم" — origination upon a straight measure; used for both creation ex nihilo (إبداع) and formation from an existing thing (إيجاد من الشيء).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "قدره قبل القطع" — measuring before cutting (craftsman's act). Metaphorical: "خلق الله الخلق: أوجده على تقدير أوجبته الحكمة" — God's creation as bringing into existence upon a measure necessitated by wisdom.
- Root: كيف (kayf)
  * Lisan / Ayn: An interrogative particle asking about state or condition; also used for manner.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "كيف: لفظ يسأل به عما يصح أن يقال فيه: شبيه وغير شبيه" — a word asking about what admits of likeness or unlikeness (qualities); not applicable to God's essence, but used here to provoke reflection on creaturely processes.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Interrogative of modality; in this context, a rhetorical summons to contemplate the "how" of divine craftsmanship.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The periodic structure here repeatedly employs "ثم كيف" (then how) as a coordinating interrogative chain, linking successive clauses without ellipsis, preserving the full syntactic weight of each stage of creation.

23:12.arabic: سبعة أطوار وتلا الآية الواردة في أطوار الخلقة وهي قوله تعالى ولقد خلقنا الإنسان من سلالة من طين ثم جعلناه نطفة في قرار مكين إلى قوله ثم أنشأناه خلقا آخر أي نفخنا فيه الروح ثم تلا قوله تعالى في الآية وإذا الموءودة سئلت وإذا نظرت إلى ما قدمناه في طريق القياس والاعتبار ظهر لك تفاوت منصب علي وابن عباس رضي الله عنهما في الغوص على المعاني ودرك العلوم كيف وفي المتفق عليه في الصحيحين على جابر أنه قال كنا نعزل على عهد رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم والقرآن ينزل وفي لفظ آخر كنا نعزل فبلغ ذلك نبي الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فلم ينهنا (1) وفيه أيضا عن جابر أنه قال إن رجلا أتى رسول الله صل
23:12.english: **The third:** Fear of excessive hardship (ḥaraj) due to the multitude of children, and guarding against the need for toil in earning a livelihood and entering into evil means of acquisition. This also is not prohibited, for the paucity of hardship assists one in religion. Indeed, perfection and excellence lie in trust in God (tawakkul) and confidence in God's guarantee, where He said: {«وما من دابة في الأرض إلا على الله رزقها»} "And there is no creature on earth but that upon Allah is its provision" [Hūd: 6]. Without doubt, in this [trust] there is a falling from the summit of perfection and an abandonment of what is more excellent — but looking to consequences and preserving wealth and storing it up, despite its contradicting tawakkul, we do not say it is prohibited.
23:12.section_title_en: ** On Coitus Interruptus ('Azl), Its Intentions, and the Etiquettes of Childbirth and Divorce
23:12.anchors:
**
- Root: عزل (ʿazl)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Separation, removal, setting aside
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Withdrawal to prevent conception
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical separation; Metaphorical: preventing pregnancy
- Root: وأد (waʾad)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Burying a female infant alive (pre-Islamic practice)
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The killing of daughters by burial
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: burial alive; Metaphorical: any prevention of life
- Root: طلق (ṭalaq)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Divorce; dissolution of marriage bond
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Legal dissolution of the marriage contract
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: releasing/loosing; Metaphorical: dissolution of marriage
- Sibawayh Rule: Conditional clauses with "فإن قلت" (objection-response dialectic structure)

23:12.arabic: التراب وأخرج ذريته من سلالة من طين ومن ماء دافق فأخرجهم من الأصلاب إلى الأرحام ومنها إلى الدنيا ثم إلى القبر ثم إلى العرض ثم إلى الجنة أو إلى النار فهذا مبدؤهم وهذا غايتهم وهذه منازلهم وخلق الدنيا زادا للمعاد ليتناول منها ما يصلح للتزود فلو تناولوها بالعدل لانقطعت الخصومات وتعطل الفقهاء ولكنهم تناولوها بالشهوات فتولدت منها الخصومات فمست الحاجة إلى سلطان يسوسهم واحتاج السلطان إلى قانون يسوسهم به فالفقيه هو العالم بقانون السياسة وطريق التوسط بين الخلق إذا تنازعوا بحكم الشهوات فكان
23:12.english: Know that the obligatory (al-farḍ) is not distinguished from other things except by mentioning the divisions of the sciences. The sciences, in relation to the purpose with which we are concerned, divide into religious (sharʿiyyah) and non-religious. By "religious" I mean that which is derived from the prophets — may the blessings of God be upon them and His peace — and to which the intellect does not guide, such as arithmetic (al-ḥisāb); nor does experience guide to it, such as medicine (al-ṭibb); nor does hearing/linguistic convention guide to it, such as language (al-lughah). For the sciences that are not religious divide into: that which is praiseworthy (maḥmūd), that which is blameworthy (madhmūm), and that which is permissible (mubāḥ).
23:12.section_title_en: Section 13 — The Distinction of Sciences: Religious and Non-Religious, Their Divisions and Rulings
23:12.anchors:
- Root: علم (ʿalima)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root meaning: "knowledge, perception, cognition of a thing by its true reality." Al-Farahidi: "العلم: إدراك الشيء بحقيقته" (knowledge is the apprehension of a thing by its true reality).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "العلم: إدراك الشيء بحقيقته" — knowledge is of two kinds: (1) apprehension of the essence of a thing, and (2) judgment upon a thing by the existence or negation of something pertaining to it. This is the theological (Kalam) sense: knowledge as veridical cognition of the real.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (haqiqah): "علمت الشيء: عرفته" — to know a thing is to recognize it. Metaphorical (majaz): "ما علمت بخبرك: ما شعرت به" — "I did not know of your news" means "I had no awareness of it," indicating that knowledge can be used for latent perception.
- Root: شرع (sharaʿa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Al-Farahidi: "الشرع: نهج الطريق الواضح" — the clear, open path. The root denotes making a path clear and accessible.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الشرع: نهج الطريق الواضح... ثم استعير ذلك للطريقة الإلهية" — the term is metaphorically transferred to the Divine Law (al-sharīʿah), the clear path laid down by God through His prophets.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "شرع في الماء شروعا" — to enter into water (immersion). Metaphorical: the religious law is that which one enters into and follows as a clear way, like entering a watering-place (al-mashraʿ).
- Root: دنا (danā)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Al-Farahidi: "دنا: قرب" — to be near, to approach. The root denotes proximity in place, time, or rank.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الدنو: القرب بالذات، أو بالحكم" — nearness by essence or by judgment. Used for spatial, temporal, and station proximity. The "nearer" (al-adnā) can mean the lesser or the meaner, as opposed to the greater or the better.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "دنا منه: قرب" — to draw near. The root is distinct from "danu'a" (دناءة) meaning baseness or lowness, though the two are sometimes confused by the masses.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The rule governing the permissibility of interposing elements between a governing word and its governed prepositional phrase, particularly when the interposed element is essential to the completion of meaning. This applies to the periodic sentence structure of the text, where long conditional and relative clauses are interposed between the subject (al-farḍ) and its predicate (lā yamtāzu).
23:12.topic: Al-Ghazali on the journey of the soul, death, and the Hereafter, from 'Book of Knowledge'

24:64.arabic: وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم يستغفر للعالم ما في السموات والأرض (3) وأي منصب يزيد على منصب من تشتغل ملائكة السموات والأرض بالاستغفار له وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم إن الحكمة تزيد الشريف شرفا وترفع المملوك حتى يدرك مدارك الملوك (4) وقد نبه بهذا على ثمراته في الدنيا ومعلوم أن الآخرة خير وأبقى وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم خصلتان لا يكونان في منافق حسن سمت وفقه في الدين (5) ولا تشكن في الحديث لنفاق بعض فقهاء الزمان فإنه ما أراد به الفقه الذي ظننته وسيأتي معنى الفقه وأدنى درجات الفقيه أن يعلم أن الآخرة خير من الدنيا
24:64.english: How He, Glorified and Exalted, began with Himself, then seconded with the angels, and thirded with the people of knowledge — and sufficient for you is this as honor, excellence, splendor, and nobility. And God, Exalted, said: {«يرفع الله الذين آمنوا منكم والذين أوتوا العلم درجات»} — "God will raise those who have believed among you and those who have been given knowledge, in degrees." Ibn ʿAbbās, may God be pleased with them both, said: For the scholars there are degrees above the believers, seven hundred degrees, and between each two degrees is a distance of five hundred years' journey.
24:64.section_title_en: The Book of Knowledge — Section 4: The Excellence of Knowledge and the Scholars
24:64.anchors:
- Root: علم (ʿ-l-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root meaning of knowing, perceiving a thing in its true reality; the act of apprehension and judgment.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "العلم: إدراك الشيء بحقيقته" — knowledge is the apprehension of a thing in its true reality, divided into apprehension of the essence and judgment of existence or non-existence.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) usage denotes genuine knowing; metaphorical (majāz) usage extends to signs, landmarks, and traces that guide to knowledge.
- Root: درج (d-r-j)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Degrees, steps, ascending stations; the root denotes gradation and progressive elevation.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الدرجة نحو المنزلة، لكن يقال للمنزلة: درجة إذا اعتبرت بالصعود" — a degree is a station considered by ascent, not horizontal extension.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical steps of ascent. Metaphorical: "لفلان درجة رفيعة" — lofty rank; "امش في مدارج الحق" — walk in the paths of truth.
- Root: يوم (y-w-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: A day; a period of time from sunrise to sunset, or any duration whatsoever.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "اليوم يعبر به عن وقت طلوع الشمس إلى غروبها. وقد يعبر به عن مدة من الزمان أي مدة كانت" — the day denotes the time of the sun's rising to its setting, and may denote any period of time whatsoever.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the solar day. Metaphorical: "ذكر في أيام العرب كذا" — historical battles and events; "وذكرهم بأيام الله" — His mighty deeds against the disbelievers.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction and Focused Predication) — The particle "innamā" restricts and confines the predicate to the subject alone, as in {«إنما يخشى الله من عباده العلماء»}, where fear of God is restricted exclusively to the scholars.
24:64.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'Contemplation'

25:3.arabic: عند الله فالعباد كلهم عجزة لا يملكون لأنفسهم ضرا ولا نفعا ولا يملكون موتا ولا حياتا ولا نشورا فإذا قرر في قلبه آفة هذه الأسباب وضررها فترت رغبته وأقبل على الله قلبه فإن العاقل لا يرغب فيما يكثر ضرره ويقل نفعه ويكفيه أن الناس لو علموا ما في باطنه من قصد الرياء وإظهار الإخلاص لمقتوه وسيكشف الله عن سره حتى يبغضه إلى الناس ويعرفهم أنه مراء وممقوت عند الله ولو أخلص لله لكشف الله لهم إخلاصه وحببه إليهم وسخرهم له وأطلق ألسنتهم بالمدح والثناء عليه مع أنه لا كمال في مدحهم ولا نقصان في ذمهم كما قال شاعر بني تميم إن مدحي زين وإن ذمي شين فقال له رسول الله ص
25:3.english: So when the harm and injury of these causes is firmly settled in his heart, his desire [for them] slackens, and his heart turns toward God. For the intelligent person does not covet that whose harm is abundant and whose benefit is scant. It suffices him that if people knew what is in his inner self—the intent of ostentation (riyā') and the display of sincerity—they would abhor him. And God will surely expose his secret until He makes him odious to the people and makes them know that he is a show-off, abhorrent to God. Had he been sincere to God, God would have unveiled his sincerity to them, made him beloved to them, subjected them to him, and loosened their tongues in praise and commendation of him—even though there is no perfection in their praise, nor deficiency in their blame. As the poet of Banī Tamīm said: "My praise is an adornment, and my blame is a disgrace." The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said to him: "You have lied—that belongs to God, there is no deity but Him." // [Hadith: A poet of Banī Tamīm said, "My praise is an adornment, and my blame is a disgrace." He (the Prophet) said: "You have lied—that belongs to God." Ahmad narrated it from the hadith of al-Aqra' ibn Ḥābis—who was the speaker of that verse, excluding the phrase "You have lied"—and its narrators are trustworthy, except that I do not know of Abū Salamah ibn 'Abd al-Raḥmān having heard [directly] from al-Aqra'. Al-Tirmidhī narrated it from the hadith of al-Barā' and deemed it sound (ḥasan), with the wording: "A man said, 'Indeed, my praise...'"]
25:3.section_title_en: The Revival of the Religious Sciences — Section 827: The Second Station: Repelling the Accidental Promptings of Ostentation During Worship
25:3.anchors:
- Root: كذب (kadhaba)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: falsehood, lying, saying what is contrary to reality; also used for "to declare someone a liar."
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In theological context, kadhb is the antithesis of sidq (truthfulness); it is a moral and epistemic vice, often linked to hypocrisy (nifāq) and false claims.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (haqīqah): to report what did not occur. Metaphorical (majāz): attributing to God what is unworthy of Him, as in the Prophet's rebuke of the poet's self-praise.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Predicate Emphasis (Bāb al-Tawkīd) — The Prophet's reply "كَذَبْتَ" (You have lied) functions as an emphatic categorical refutation, structured as a nominal sentence with implied subject, establishing a permanent verdict rather than a transient rebuke.
25:3.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Condemnation of Status and Ostentation'

25:3.arabic: بعض أشخاص الإنس في بعض الأمور وهو مع ذلك لا يملك لنفسه موتا ولا حياة ولا نشورا ولا ضرا ولا نفعا بل لا يقدر على حفظ عينه من العمى ولسانه من الخرس وأذنه من الصمم وبدنه من المرض ولا يحتاج إلى عد ما يعجز عنه في نفسه وغيره مما هو على الجملة متعلق قدرته فضلا عما لا تتعلق به قدرته من ملكوت السموات وأفلاكها وكواكبها والأرض وجبالها وبحارها ورياحها وصواعقها ومعادنها ونباتها وحيواناتها وجميع أجزائها فلا قدرة له على ذرة منها وما هو قادر عليه من نفسه وغيره فليست قدرته من نفسه وبنفسه بل الله خالقه وخالق قدرته وخالق أسبابه والممكن له من
25:3.english: As for knowledge — where is the knowledge of the first and the last among all creation compared to the knowledge of Allah, the Exalted, which encompasses all things with an encompassing that transcends all limit, so that not even the weight of an atom escapes Him in the heavens or on the earth? He has addressed all of creation, saying, the Mighty and Majestic: {«وَمَا أُوتِيتُم مِّنَ الْعِلْمِ إِلَّا قَلِيلًا»} (And you have not been given of knowledge except a little) (Q 17:85). Nay, even if all the inhabitants of the earth and the heavens were to gather together to encompass His knowledge and His wisdom in the detailed formation of a single ant or gnat, they would not attain to one-tenth of a tenth of that — {«وَلَا يُحِيطُونَ بِشَيْءٍ مِّنْ عِلْمِهِ إِلَّا بِمَا شَاءَ»} (And they do not encompass anything of His knowledge except what He wills) (Q 2:255). And the paltry measure that all creatures have learned, they have learned only through His teaching, as He, the Exalted, said: {«خَلَقَ الْإِنسَانَ عَلَّمَهُ الْبَيَانَ»} (He created man; He taught him eloquence) (Q 55:3-4). If, therefore, the beauty and nobility of knowledge is something beloved, and it is in itself an adornment and perfection for the one described by it, then it is not fitting that anyone be loved for this reason except Allah, the Exalted alone.
25:3.section_title_en: The Beauty of Divine Attributes and the Relative Nature of Human Perfection
25:3.anchors:
- Root: علم (ʿalima)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of perception, cognition, and certain apprehension of a thing's reality.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "العلم: إدراك الشيء بحقيقته" — knowledge is the apprehension of a thing in its true reality; it is twofold: apprehension of the essence, and judgment affirming or negating a predicate.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) usage denotes genuine cognition; metaphorical (majāz) usage extends to perception and awareness. Here, the comparative "أعلم/أجهل" (more knowing/ more ignorant) operates on a scale of relative apprehension.
- Root: قدر (qadara)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Root denotes measuring, determining, and the capacity to bring about an effect.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "القدرة إذا وصف بها الإنسان فاسم لهيئة له بها يتمكن من فعل شيء ما، وإذا وصف الله تعالى بها فهي نفي العجز عنه" — power in man is a disposition enabling specific acts; power in God is absolute negation of incapacity, unrestricted and infinite.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "هو قادر مقتدر ذو قدرة ومقدرة" — the possessor of power. Metaphorical: extended to strength and dominion. The text contrasts finite human power (maqdūr) with divine power that encompasses all things without limit.
- Root: نفس (nafs)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Self, soul, essence; the innermost reality of a thing.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "نفسه: ذاته" — God's "self" is His very essence. For man, nafs denotes the composite self that requires discipline and reform (iṣlāḥ).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the self as the seat of attributes; metaphorical: "دفق نفسه" — blood/life. Here, "سياسة نفسه" (governance of one's self) is the literal, ethical sense.
- Root: خلق (khalaqa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Root denotes measuring, smoothing, and fashioning; also moral character (khuluq).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الخلق أصله: التقدير المستقيم" — origination by precise measure; used for creation ex nihilo and for formation from existing matter.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "خلق الله الخلق: أوجده على تقدير أوجبته الحكمة" — God's creation is bringing into existence upon a measure required by wisdom. The text uses "الخبائث" (vices) as the corruption of this created nature.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — The phrase "فإنما غايته أن يقدر" restricts human power to a finite limit, emphasizing that the utmost reach of creaturely capacity is merely partial and derivative, never absolute.
25:3.topic: Al-Ghazali on the journey of the soul, death, and the Hereafter, from 'Contemplation'

25:12.arabic: وأنهم كلما أرادوا أن يخرجوا منها أعيدوا فيها وأنهم إذا رأوها من مكان بعيد سمعوا لها تغيظا وزفيرا وهلم جرا إلى جميع ما ورد في القرآن من شرحها وإذا أراد أن يستجلب حال الرجاء فلينظر إلى الجنة ونعيمها وأشجارها وأنهارها وحورها وولدانها ونعيمها المقيم وملكها الدائم
25:12.english: For example, if he observes in himself self-amazement (ʿujb) at his deeds, let him reflect and say: "I performed this only with my body and my limbs, and by my power and my will — yet all of that is neither from me nor unto me. Rather, it is from God's creation and His bounty upon me. For He it is who created me, created my limbs, created my power and my will, and He it is who moves my organs by His power — and likewise my power and my will. So how can I marvel at my deed or at myself, when I do not sustain myself by myself?"
25:12.section_title_en: On the Paths of Reflection for Cultivating the Traits of Salvation (Section 1264)
25:12.anchors:
- Root: ع-ج-ب (ʿajiba)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Self-amazement; the state of finding something wondrous, rooted in a perception of one's own act as extraordinary.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): ʿUjb (self-admiration) is a blameworthy trait that veils one from recognizing the divine origin of all power and action; it stems from ignorance (jahl) of God's sole agency.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (haqiqah) sense is wonder at something rare; metaphorical (majaz) usage here denotes moral corruption of the heart's intention (khabth al-dakhlah).
- Root: ك-ب-ر (kabura)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Bigness in stature or rank; arrogance (kibr) as a moral-spiritual inflation of the self against God's majesty.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Kabir and saghir are relative terms; kibr (pride) is the soul's claim to greatness that belongs only to God, making it a root of ruin (muhlik).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical or seniority-based greatness; metaphorical: the soul's false elevation, which is folly (hamaqah) since true greatness is measured by God's scale, unveiled only after death.
- Root: ش-ه-و (shahiya)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Appetitive desire; craving for food or copulation shared with beasts.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Shahwah is a lower faculty; when dominant, it distances one from angelic attributes (knowledge, power) and aligns one with animal nature.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: bodily craving; metaphorical: a sign of spiritual degradation, as perfection lies in divine attributes, not in bestial appetites.
- Root: ر-ج-و (rajā)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Hope; expectation of good.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Rajāʾ is a salvific state (munjī) that balances fear (khawf), drawing the heart toward God's mercy and the promise of Paradise.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: anticipation of a desired outcome; metaphorical: the soul's anchor against despair, cultivated by contemplating Paradise's eternal bliss.
- Sibawayh Rule: Bāb al-ḥaṣr wa-l-taqyīd bi-innamā (Restriction & Focused Predication): The particle innamā restricts the predicate to the subject alone, as in "إنما عمل ببدني وجارحتي" — affirming that the act's origin is solely through bodily instruments, not the self's independent power, thereby negating any ground for self-amazement.
25:12.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Contemplation'

25:44.arabic: هواه أفأنت تكون عليه وكيلا أم تحسب أن أكثرهم يسمعون أو يعقلون إن هم إلا كالأنعام بل هم أضل سبيلا وبقوله عز وجل لقد حق القول على أكثرهم فهم لا يؤمنون وبقوله سواء عليهم أأنذرتهم أم لم تنذرهم لا يؤمنون ورب قلب هذا حاله بالإضافة إلى بعض الشهوات كالذي يتورع عن بعض الأشياء ولكنه إذا رأى وجها حسنا لم يملك عينه وقلبه وطاش عقله وسقط مساك قلبه أو كالذي لا يملك نفسه فيما فيه الجاه والرياسة والكبر ولا يبقى معه مسكة للتثبت عند ظهور أسبابه أو كالذي لا يملك نفسه عند الغضب مهما استحقر وذكر عيب من عيوبه أو كالذي لا يملك نفسه عند القدرة على أخذ درهم أو د
25:44.english: Know that the heart, as we have mentioned, is surrounded by the attributes we have described, and the traces and states pour into it from the gateways we have set forth. It is as if it were a target perpetually struck from every side. When something afflicts it, it is affected by it; then it is struck from another side by that which opposes it, and so its state changes. If the devil descends upon it and calls it to passion (hawā), the angel descends upon it and turns it away from that. If one devil drags it toward evil, another devil drags it toward something else; and if one angel draws it toward good, another draws it toward something else. Thus at times it is contested between two angels, at times between two devils, and at times between an angel and a devil — it is never, ever left neglected. To this points the saying of the Exalted: {وَنُقَلِّبُ أَفْئِدَتَهُمْ وَأَبْصَارَهُمْ} (And We turn their hearts and their visions) {«الأنعام/110»}. And because the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) was privy to the wondrous handiwork of Allah the Exalted in the marvels of the heart and its overturning, he used to swear by it, saying: "No, by the Turner of the hearts." (1)
25:44.section_title_en: The Wonders of the Heart: Its States of Stability, Inclination, and Fluctuation Between the Two Attracting Forces
25:44.anchors:
- Root: قلب (q-l-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To turn a thing over, to revolve it, to divert it from one face to another; the heart is so named for its constant turning and fluctuation.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "قلب الشيء: تصريفه وصرفه عن وجه إلى وجه" — the heart's perpetual overturning is its very essence; its states are never fixed, and its rectitude or corruption follows its turning.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): "قلب الشيء قلبا: حوله عن وجهه" — physical overturning. Metaphorical (Majaz): "رجل قلب حول: يقلب الأمور ويحتال" — one who turns matters over and manages them; the heart's fluctuation between the two attractants is a real, continuous overturning.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The periodic structure of the opening sentence, with its cascading circumstantial clauses, requires careful tracking of the governing verb and its dependent states to preserve the causal sequence of the heart's affliction and response.

25:47.arabic: يتميز وقت المعاش عن وقت الاستراحة فانظر كيف جعل الله تعالى الليل لباسا والنوم سباتا والنهار معاشا وانظر إلى إيلاجه الليل في النهار والنهار في الليل وإدخاله الزيادة والنقصان عليهما على ترتيب مخصوص وانظر إلى إمالته مسير الشمس عن وسط السماء حتى اختلف بسببه الصيف والشتاء والربيع والخريف فإذا انخفضت الشمس من وسط السماء فى مسيرها برد الهواء وظهر الشتاء وإذا استوت فى وسط السماء اشتد القيظ وإذا كانت فيما بينهما اعتدل الزمان وعجائب السموات لا مطمع في إحصاء عشر عشير جزء من أجزائها وإنما هذا تنبيه على طريق الفكر واعتقد على طريق الجملة أنه
25:47.english: By another course [of motion] its Creator has subjugated it [the sun] to His service. Were it not for its rising and its setting, the night and the day would not alternate, the appointed times would not be known, and darkness would envelop all perpetually, or light would prevail forever — such that the time of livelihood would not be distinguished from the time of rest. So behold how God, the Exalted, made the night a garment {«وَجَعَلْنَا اللَّيْلَ لِبَاسًا»}, and sleep a repose, and the day a means of livelihood {«وَجَعَلْنَا النَّهَارَ مَعَاشًا»}. And behold His insertion of the night into the day and the day into the night, and His bringing of increase and decrease upon them both according to a precise ordering.
25:47.section_title_en: On Contemplating the Sun, the Heavens, and the Wisdom of Their Creator
25:47.anchors:
- Root: سير (s-y-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of movement, journeying, traversing a path.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Used for the celestial bodies' appointed courses (musayyarāt), indicating divine ordainment of motion.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal for physical traversal; metaphorical for the subjugation of celestial bodies to their Maker's command.
- Root: شمس (sh-m-s)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The celestial orb itself; also that which is restless, never settling.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Denotes both the solar disc and its diffused light; its rising and setting are signs of divine governance.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal for the sun's course; metaphorical (majāz) for manifest power and relentless motion.
- Root: خلق (kh-l-q)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Measuring, estimating, fashioning with precise proportion.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Origination from nothing (ījād min lā aṣl) and creation upon a measure determined by wisdom.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal for the artisan's sizing before cutting; metaphorical for God's bringing things into being upon an exact decree.
- Root: عجب (ʿ-j-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Astonishment at something whose cause is hidden or whose magnitude exceeds the ordinary.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The wondrous (ʿajab) is that which strikes the soul with amazement due to its surpassing of customary limits.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal for marvel; metaphorical for the overwhelming evidence of divine wisdom in creation.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Restriction and Specification (al-ḥaṣr wa al-taqyīd) — governing the use of "إنما" and conditional-command structures (fa-inẓur...), where the imperative to "look" functions as a focused directive restricting attention to the object of contemplation.
25:47.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Contemplation'

29:52.arabic: وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم يستغفر للعالم ما في السموات والأرض (3) وأي منصب يزيد على منصب من تشتغل ملائكة السموات والأرض بالاستغفار له وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم إن الحكمة تزيد الشريف شرفا وترفع المملوك حتى يدرك مدارك الملوك (4) وقد نبه بهذا على ثمراته في الدنيا ومعلوم أن الآخرة خير وأبقى وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم خصلتان لا يكونان في منافق حسن سمت وفقه في الدين (5) ولا تشكن في الحديث لنفاق بعض فقهاء الزمان فإنه ما أراد به الفقه الذي ظننته وسيأتي معنى الفقه وأدنى درجات الفقيه أن يعلم أن الآخرة خير من الدنيا
29:52.english: How He, Glorified and Exalted, began with Himself, then seconded with the angels, and thirded with the people of knowledge — and sufficient for you is this as honor, excellence, splendor, and nobility. And God, Exalted, said: {«يرفع الله الذين آمنوا منكم والذين أوتوا العلم درجات»} — "God will raise those who have believed among you and those who have been given knowledge, in degrees." Ibn ʿAbbās, may God be pleased with them both, said: For the scholars there are degrees above the believers, seven hundred degrees, and between each two degrees is a distance of five hundred years' journey.
29:52.section_title_en: The Book of Knowledge — Section 4: The Excellence of Knowledge and the Scholars
29:52.anchors:
- Root: علم (ʿ-l-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root meaning of knowing, perceiving a thing in its true reality; the act of apprehension and judgment.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "العلم: إدراك الشيء بحقيقته" — knowledge is the apprehension of a thing in its true reality, divided into apprehension of the essence and judgment of existence or non-existence.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) usage denotes genuine knowing; metaphorical (majāz) usage extends to signs, landmarks, and traces that guide to knowledge.
- Root: درج (d-r-j)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Degrees, steps, ascending stations; the root denotes gradation and progressive elevation.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الدرجة نحو المنزلة، لكن يقال للمنزلة: درجة إذا اعتبرت بالصعود" — a degree is a station considered by ascent, not horizontal extension.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical steps of ascent. Metaphorical: "لفلان درجة رفيعة" — lofty rank; "امش في مدارج الحق" — walk in the paths of truth.
- Root: يوم (y-w-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: A day; a period of time from sunrise to sunset, or any duration whatsoever.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "اليوم يعبر به عن وقت طلوع الشمس إلى غروبها. وقد يعبر به عن مدة من الزمان أي مدة كانت" — the day denotes the time of the sun's rising to its setting, and may denote any period of time whatsoever.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the solar day. Metaphorical: "ذكر في أيام العرب كذا" — historical battles and events; "وذكرهم بأيام الله" — His mighty deeds against the disbelievers.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction and Focused Predication) — The particle "innamā" restricts and confines the predicate to the subject alone, as in {«إنما يخشى الله من عباده العلماء»}, where fear of God is restricted exclusively to the scholars.
29:52.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'Contemplation'

30:20.arabic: ويخرج الميت من الحي ويحيي الأرض بعد موتها وكذلك تخرجون ومن آياته أن خلقكم من تراب ثم إذا أنتم بشر تنتشرون اللهم إني أسألك إيمانا دائما ويقينا صادقا وعلما نافعا وقلبا خاشعا ولسانا ذاكرا وأسألك العفو والعافية والمعافاة الدائمة في الدنيا والآخرة ويصلي على محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم ويدعو الله عز وجل بما شاء من حاجته عقيب هذا الدعاء ثم ينزل ويبتدىء السعي وهو يقول رب اغفر وارحم وتجاوز عما تعلم إنك أنت الأعز الأكرم اللهم آتنا في الدنيا حسنة وفي الآخرة حسنة وقنا عذاب النار ويمشي على هينة حتى ينتهي إلى الميل الأخضر وهو أول ما يلقاه إذا نزل من الصفا وهو على زا
30:20.english: Upon ascending al-Ṣafā, he should face the House (al-Bayt) and say: "God is Greater, God is Greater. Praise be to God for what He has guided us to. Praise be to God with all His praises, for all His graces, all of them. There is no god but God alone, with no partner. His is the dominion, and His is the praise. He gives life and causes death; in His hand is all good, and He is over all things competent. There is no god but God alone; He fulfilled His promise, aided His servant, and honored His soldiers; He alone defeated the confederates. There is no god but God, devoting religion sincerely to Him, even if the disbelievers detest it. There is no god but God, devoting religion sincerely to Him. Praise be to God, Lord of the worlds. So exalted is God when you reach the evening and when you reach the morning. And His is the praise in the heavens and the earth, and at nightfall and when you are at noon. He brings forth the living from the dead and brings forth the dead from the living, and He revives the earth after its death, and thus shall you be brought forth. And of His signs is that He created you from dust; then, behold, you are humans spreading out. O God, I ask You for enduring faith, sincere certainty, beneficial knowledge, a humble heart, and a tongue that remembers You. And I ask You for pardon, well-being, and perpetual immunity in this world and the Hereafter." Then he sends blessings upon Muḥammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and supplicates God, Mighty and Majestic, with whatever need he wishes, following this supplication.
30:20.section_title_en: The Yemeni Corner and the Stone — The Beginning of the Saʿy and Its Rites
30:20.anchors:
- Root: سعي (Saʿy)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The root denotes striving, running, or rapid walking; it is the exertion of effort in a matter, whether good or evil.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "السعي: المشي السريع، وهو دون العدو، ويستعمل للجد في الأمر" — Saʿy is swift walking, less than running, and is used for earnest exertion in a matter. In the sacred rite, it signifies the ritual traversing between al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah, an act of devotional striving.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Ḥaqīqah): "سعى إلى المسجد" — physical exertion toward a goal. Metaphorical (Majāz): "هو يسعى على عياله" — he strives to provide for his family. In the ritual context, the physical traversing is the literal embodiment of devotional striving.
- Root: حمد (Ḥamd)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The root denotes praise, commendation, and the acknowledgment of beneficence; it is the opposite of blame (dhamm).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Praise (ḥamd) is the acknowledgment of beneficence with reverence and love, and it is due to God alone in His absolute perfection.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "أحمد الله تعالى بجميع محامده" — praising God with all His praises. Metaphorical: "أحمدت صنيعه" — I approved of his deed. In the supplications of the saʿy, the pilgrim's praise is both literal acknowledgment and the metaphorical "approval" of God's decree.
- Root: رمل (Raml)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The root denotes rapid walking with a slight trotting motion, a form of hastening in movement.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Not a primary theological term, but in ritual context it signifies the prescribed hastening between the two green markers, emulating the Prophet's action.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical hastening. Metaphorical: The rapid pace is a visible emblem of spiritual earnestness and the rejection of the polytheists' claim that the Muslims were weakened by fever.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Restriction and Specification (al-Ḥaṣr wa al-Taqyīd) — The phrase "وإنما ذلك شرط في طواف الركن" employs restriction to delimit a condition exclusively to the circumambulation of the pillar (ṭawāf al-rukn), thereby negating its applicability to the saʿy.
30:20.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications, prayers, and their spiritual power, from 'Contemplation'

32:20.arabic: صالح فإني أجد غما فقرأت {كلما أرادوا أن يخرجوا منها أعيدوا فيها} فخر ميتا وروى أن زرارة بن أبي أوفى صلى بالناس الغداة فلما قرأ {فإذا نقر في الناقور} خر مغشيا عليه فحمل ميتا ودخل يزيد الرقاشي على عمر بن عبد العزيز فقال عظني يا يزيد فقال يا أمير المؤمنين اعلم أنك لست أول خليفة يموت فبكى ثم قال زدني قال يا أمير المومنين ليس بينك وبين آدم أب إلا ميت فبكى ثم قال زدني يا يزيد فقال يا أمير المؤمنين ليس بينك وبين الجنة والنار منزل فخر مغشيا عليه وقال ميمون بن مهران لما نزلت هذه الآية {وإن جهنم لموعدهم أجمعين} صاح
32:20.english: Al-Ḥasan [al-Baṣrī] passed by a young man who was completely absorbed in his laughter, sitting with a group of people in a gathering. Al-Ḥasan said to him: "O young man, have you crossed the Ṣirāṭ [the Bridge]?" He said: "No." He said: "Then do you know whether you will go to Paradise or to the Fire?" He said: "No." He said: "Then what is this laughter?" He said: "And that young man was never seen laughing after that."
32:20.section_title_en: The States of Fear and the Severity of Khawf — Accounts of the Early Pious (Section 1062)
32:20.anchors:
- Root: ضحك (Ḍaḥika)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning is laughter, arising from a state of heedlessness or joy; its opposite is weeping (bukā') which accompanies khashyah.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Laughter is a human accident (ʿaraḍ) indicating the heart's occupation with worldly pleasure, contra the state of the God-fearing whose hearts are preoccupied with divine threat.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) for audible laughter; metaphorical (majāz) for the soul's levity and forgetfulness of the reckoning.
- Root: خوف (Khawf)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Fear, dread, anxiety of anticipated harm; in the Kalam context, it is the soul's perturbation due to probable punishment.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Khawf is distinguished from khashyah — khashyah is specific to knowledge-based fear of Allah's majesty, while khawf is broader; here, the accounts blend both as the engine of righteous action.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal for fear of a known threat; metaphorical for the "fear" that severs the liver (qataʿa al-kabid), i.e., a spiritual state overwhelming the corporeal frame.
- Root: أمن (Amn)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Security, safety, freedom from fear; its root denotes tranquility of heart.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Amn is the cessation of fear, which in this world is only proper for the prophets and angels in specific contexts; for the sinner, it is a delusion (ghurūr).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal for physical safety; metaphorical for spiritual complacency, which is blameworthy — as in the saying of Ḥammād: "That is the sitting of the secure one."
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Restriction with إنما (Innamā) — as in "إنما جعل الله هذه الغفلة" and "إنما أغبط من لم يخلق" — where the predicate is restricted to the subject, emphasizing exclusive causation or exclusive object of envy, per the canonical pattern of ḥaṣr.
32:20.topic: Al-Ghazali on the journey of the soul, death, and the Hereafter, from 'Contemplation'

36:36.arabic: تعلمون سبحان الذي خلق الأزواج كلها مما تنبت الأرض ومن أنفسهم ومما لا يعلمون {وقال} وننشئكم فيما لا تعلمون {وإلى} ما يعرف أصلها وجملتها ولا يعرف تفصيلها فيمكننا أن نتفكر في تفصيلها وهي منقسمة إلى ما أدركناه بحس البصر وإلى ما لا ندركه بالبصر أما الذي لا ندركه بالبصر فكالملائكة والجن والشياطين والعرش والكرسي وغير ذلك ومجال الفكر في هذه الأشياء مما يضيق ويغمض فلنعدل إلى الأقرب إلى الأفهام وهي المدركات بحس البصر وذلك هو السموات السبع والأرض وما بينهما فالسموات مشاهدة بكواكبها وشمسها وقمرها وحركتها ودورانها في طلوعها وغ
36:36.english: We say: Created existents are divided into that whose origin is unknown to us, such that we cannot contemplate it—and how many are the existents we do not know! As God Most High said: {«وَيَخْلُقُ مَا لَا تَعْلَمُونَ»} (And He creates what you do not know — Q. 16:8), and {«سُبْحَانَ الَّذِي خَلَقَ الْأَزْوَاجَ كُلَّهَا مِمَّا تُنبِتُ الْأَرْضُ وَمِنْ أَنفُسِهِمْ وَمِمَّا لَا يَعْلَمُونَ»} (Glory be to Him who created all pairs, of what the earth grows, and of themselves, and of what they do not know — Q. 36:36), and He said: {«وَنُنشِئُكُمْ فِيمَا لَا تَعْلَمُونَ»} (And We raise you up in what you do not know — Q. 56:61). And [it is divided] into that whose origin and general nature are known, but whose detailed particulars are not known—so we are able to contemplate its details.
36:36.section_title_en: Exposition of the Method of Contemplation upon the Creation of God Most High
36:36.anchors:
- Root: فكر (f-k-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning is reflection, deliberation, and the movement of the mind over a matter to arrive at its reality.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In theological usage, *tafakkur* is the soul's journey through created things (al-makhlūqāt) to derive knowledge of the Creator—it is the bridge from the sensory to the intelligible.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) sense is mental consideration; metaphorical (majāz) extension applies it to the heart's "seeing" of divine wisdom latent in creation.
- Root: خلق (kh-l-q)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Root meaning is measuring, proportioning, and fashioning a thing with precise estimation.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): *Khalq* denotes origination from nothing (ibdāʿ) or creation of one thing from another, always upon a measure necessitated by wisdom.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the artisan's sizing of material before cutting; Metaphorical: God's bringing things into existence upon a measure that wisdom dictates—He is Rabb al-khalīqah.
- Root: بصر (b-ṣ-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning is sight, both ocular and perceptive.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): *Baṣar* applies to the eye's organ and its power, and to the heart's perceptive faculty (*baṣīrah*), as in {«فَكَشَفْنَا عَنكَ غِطَاءَكَ فَبَصَرُكَ الْيَوْمَ حَدِيدٌ»} (Q. 50:22).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical sight; Metaphorical: *ibṣār* as intellectual discernment—"هذه آية مبصرة" (this is an illuminating sign).
- Root: نفس (n-f-s)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning is the self, the soul, the vital principle.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): *Nafs* denotes the rational soul (al-rūḥ) and also the very essence (al-dhāt); in {«وَفِي أَنفُسِكُمْ أَفَلَا تُبْصِرُونَ»} (Q. 51:21) it refers to the human self as a microcosmic sign.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the self as animate entity; Metaphorical: the inner dimension of man as a locus of divine signs.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Specification and Restriction (Bāb al-Takhṣīṣ) — When a general term (like "everything in existence") is followed by a restrictive clause ("save God"), the syntax governs the scope of predication, ensuring the exception is precise and the universal claim is bounded.
36:36.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Contemplation'

36:77.arabic: والشهوة والكبر والجهل والتكذيب والمجادلة كما قال تعالى أولم ير الإنسان أنا خلقناه من نطفة فإذا هو خصيم مبين فليتأمل هذه العجائب ليترقى منها إلى عجب العجائب وهو الصفة التي منها صدرت هذه الأعاجيب فلا يزال ينظر إلى الصنعة فيرى الصانع وأما أحوال الأنبياء عليهم السلام فإذا سمع منها كيف كذبوا وضربوا وقتل بعضهم فليفهم منه صفة الاستغناء لله عز وجل عن الرسل والمرسل إليهم وأنه لو أهلك جميعهم لم يؤثر في ملكه شيئا وإذا سمع نصرتهم في آخر الأمر فليفهم قدرة الله عز وجل وإرادته لنصرة الحق وأما أحوال المكذبين كعاد وثمود وما جرى عليهم فليكن فهمه منه استشعار الخوف من سطوت
36:77.english: I say: These meanings are buried treasures that are not unveiled except to the divinely aided ones. To this 'Ali — may God be pleased with him — alluded by his saying: "The Messenger of God — may God's peace and blessings be upon him — did not confide to me anything that he concealed from the people, except that God — mighty and majestic — grants to a servant understanding (fahm) of His Book. So let one be eager in seeking that understanding." (1) And Ibn Mas'ud — may God be pleased with him — said: "Whoever desires the knowledge of the first and the last, let him stir up the Qur'an." And the greatest of the sciences of the Qur'an lie beneath the names of God — mighty and majestic — and His attributes, for most of creation have grasped from them only matters befitting their understandings and have not stumbled upon their depths.
36:77.section_title_en: The Revival of the Religious Sciences — Section 228: On the Inner Meanings of the Qur'an and the Removal of Obstacles to Understanding
36:77.anchors:
- Root: فهم (f-h-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Comprehension, discernment, the faculty by which one grasps meanings
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الفهم: هيئة للإنسان بها يتحقق معاني ما يحسن" — a disposition by which one verifies the realities of what is perceived; distinct from mere hearing or transmission
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: swift apprehension; Metaphorical: the divine gift of insight into hidden meanings, as in the verse {ففهمناها سليمان}
- Root: قلب (q-l-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Turning, overturning, transformation from one state to another
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "قلب الشيء: تصريفه وصرفه عن وجه إلى وجه" — the heart as that which is perpetually turned and overturned between states
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical turning; Metaphorical: the heart as the seat of understanding that is veiled or illuminated, rusted or polished
- Root: سمع (s-m-')
  * Lisan / Ayn: Hearing, the auditory faculty
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "السمع: قوة في الأذن به يدرك الأصوات" — extends metaphorically to comprehension and obedience; "أو ألقى السمع وهو شهيد" — one who casts his hearing while present
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: auditory perception; Metaphorical: attentive obedience and receptive understanding
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد (Restriction & Specification) — governing the precise delimitation of predicates such as "إنما يتذكر أولوا الألباب" where restriction confines the action to its proper subject
36:77.topic: Al-Ghazali on purifying the character, moral diseases, and spiritual remedies, from 'Contemplation'

41:39.arabic: فانظر إلى الأرض وهى ميتة فإذا أنزل عليها الماء اهتزت وربت واخضرت وأنبتت عجائب النبات وخرجت منها أصناف الحيوانات ثم انظر كيف أحكم جوانب الأرض بالجبال الراسيات الشوامخ الصم الصلاب وكيف أودع المياه تحتها ففجر العيون وأسال الأنهار تجري على وجهها وأخرج من الحجارة اليابسة ومن التراب الكدر ماء رقيقا عذبا صافيا زلالا وجعل به كل شيء حي فأخرج به فنون الأشجار والنبات من حب وعنب وقضب وزيتون ونخل ورمان وفواكه كثيرة لا تحصى مختلفة الأشكال والألوان والطعوم والصفات والأرابيح يفضل بعضها على بعض في الأكل تسقى بماء واحد وت
41:39.english: For the beast has no power over that; but as for man, God created for him the power, then he disabled it and disbelieved in God's grace therein. So those are like cattle — nay, they are even further astray from the way {فَأُولَٰئِكَ كَالْأَنْعَامِ بَلْ هُمْ أَضَلُّ سَبِيلًا}.
41:39.section_title_en: On Contemplating the Earth, Its Rivers, Mountains, and Minerals — Section 1273
41:39.anchors:
- Root: فكر (f-k-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: التفكر: تأمل القلب وتدبر الشيء، والفكر: إعمال النظر في الشيء
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): الفكر: قوة العلم التي بها يدرك الإنسان، وقيل: هو ترتيب أمور معلومة للتأدي إلى مجهول
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): الفكر: تصرف القلب في النظر — literal: إعمال الروية؛ metaphorical: التفكر في ملكوت الله
- Root: ارض (arḍ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: الأرض: التي عليها الناس، وجمعها أرضون
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): الأرض: الجرم المقابل للسماء، ويعبر بها عن أسفل الشيء
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): literal: الأرض المهاد والفراش؛ metaphorical: تذلل الأرض وسكونها
- Root: دحا (d-ḥ-w) / مهد (m-h-d)
  * Lisan / Ayn: مهد: وطأ المكان وهيأه، والمهاد: الفراش الموطأ
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): المهد: الموضع المهيأ للصبي، والمهاد: الأرض الموطأة
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): literal: فرش الأرض وتمهيدها؛ metaphorical: جعلها قارة ساكنة لا تميد
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — the interposed clause "فانظر" after "إلى الأرض" maintains grammatical continuity while allowing rhetorical pause.
41:39.topic: Al-Ghazali on the inner and outer dimensions of worship, from 'Contemplation'

44:38.arabic: فلنعدل إلى الأقرب إلى الأفهام وهي المدركات بحس البصر وذلك هو السموات السبع والأرض وما بينهما فالسموات مشاهدة بكواكبها وشمسها وقمرها وحركتها ودورانها في طلوعها وغروبها والأرض مشاهدة بما فيها من جبالها ومعادنها وأنهارها وبحارها وحيوانها ونباتها وما بين السماء والأرض وهو الجو مدرك بغيومها وأمطارها وثلوجها ورعدها وبرقها وصواعقها وشهبها وعواصف رياحها فهذه هي الأجناس المشاهدة من السموات والأرض وما بينهما وكل جنس منها ينقسم إلى أنواع وكل نوع ينقسم إلى أقسام ويتشعب كل قسم إلى أصناف ولا نهاية لانشعاب ذلك وانقسامه في اختلاف صفاته وهيآته ومعانيه الظاهرة والباطنة وجميع ذلك مجال الفكر فلا تتحرك ذرة في السموات والأرض من جماد ولا نبات ولا حيوان ولا فلك ولا كوكب إلا والله تعالى هو محركها وفي حركتها حكمة أو حكمتان أو عشر أو ألف حكمة كل ذلك شاهد لله تعالى بالوحدانية ودال على جلاله وكبريائه وهي الآيات الدالة عليه وقد ورد القرآن بالحث على التفكر في هذه الايات كما قال الله تعالى إن في خلق السموات والأرض واختلاف الليل والنهار لآيات لأولي الألباب وكما قال تعالى ومن آياته من أول القرآن إلى آخره فلنذكر كيفية الفكر في بعض الآيات فمن آياته الإنسان المخلوق من النطفة وأقرب شيء إليك نفسك وفيك من العجائب الدالة على عظمة الله تعالى ما تنقضي الأعمار في الوقوف على عشر عشيره وأنت غافل عنه فيامن هو غافل عن نفسه وجاهل بها كيف تطمع في معرفة غيرك وقد أمرك الله تعالى بالتدبر في نفسك في كتابه العزيز فقال وفي أنفسكم أفلا تبصرون وذكر أنك مخلوق من نطفة قذرة فقال قتل الإنسان ما أكفره من أي شئ خلقه من نطفة خلقه فقدره ثم السبيل يسره ثم أماته فأقبره ثم إذا شاء أنشره وقال تعالى ومن آياته أن خلقكم من تراب ثم إذا أنتم بشر تنتشرون وقال تعالى
