6:101.arabic: الأول والآخر والظاهر والباطن وهو بكل شيء عليم التنزيه وأنه ليس بجسم مصور ولا جوهر محدود مقدر وأنه لا يماثل والأجسام ولا في التقدير ولا في قبول الانقسام وأنه ليس بجوهر ولا تحله الجواهر ولا بعرض ولا تحله الأعراض بل لا يماثل موجودا ولا يماثله موجود ليس كمثله شيء ولا هو مثل شيء وأنه لا يحده المقدار ولا تحويه الأقطار ولا تحيط به الجهات ولا تكتنفه الأرضون ولا السموات وأنه مستو على العرش على الوجه الذي قاله وبالمعنى الذي أراده استواء منزها عن المماسة والاستقرار والتمكن والحلول والانتقال لا يحمله ال
6:101.english:
- **Root: خلق (khalaqa)**
  - *Lisan / Ayn:* Core meaning of measuring, proportioning, and fashioning; al-Khalil notes the root's application to the act of creation as bringing forth upon a measured determination.
  - *Al-Raghib (Mufradat):* "الخلق أصله: التقدير المستقيم" — Creation fundamentally signifies right/straight measurement; used for bringing into being from nothing (ibdāʿ) as in {خلق السماوات والأرض}, and for bringing forth from something as in {خلقكم من نفس واحدة}.
  - *Al-Zamakhshari (Asas):* Literal (ḥaqīqah): the craftsman's measuring before cutting. Metaphorical (majāz): "خلق الله الخلق: أوجده على تقدير أوجبته الحكمة" — God's creation is bringing into existence upon a measure necessitated by wisdom.
6:101.topic: Classical commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya Ulum al-Din, from 'Foundations of Belief'

6:103.arabic: لقوله عز وجل لا تدركه الأبصار وهو يدرك الأبصار ولقوله تعالى في خطاب موسى عليه السلام لن تراني وليت شعري كيف عرف المعتزل من صفات رب الأرباب ما جهله موسى عليه السلام وكيف سأل موسى عليه السلام الرؤية مع كونها محالا ولعل الجهل بذوي البدع والأهواء من الجهلة الأغبياء أولى من الجهل بالأنبياء صلوات الله عليهم وأما وجه إجراء آية الرؤية على الظاهر فهو أنه غير مؤد إلى المحال فإن الرؤية نوع كشف وعلم إلا أنه أتم وأوضح من العلم فإذا جاز تعلق العلم به وليس في جهة جاز تعلق الرؤية به وليس بجهة وكما يجوز أن ير
6:103.english: **The Eighth Principle: Knowledge that He, Exalted is He, is established upon His Throne (mustawin ʿalā ʿarshihi) in the sense that God, Exalted is He, intended by istiwāʾ — which is the sense that does not contradict the attribute of Majesty, nor does any mark of origination (ḥudūth) or passing away (fanāʾ) attach to it. And it is the sense intended by His saying — istiwāʾ toward the heaven — where He said in the Qur'an: {«ثُمَّ اسْتَوَىٰ إِلَى السَّمَاءِ وَهِيَ دُخَانٌ»} ("Then He directed Himself to the heaven, and it was smoke") [Fussilat 41:11]. And that is only by way of subjugation (qahr) and dominion (istīlāʾ), as the poet said:
6:103.section_title_en: The Revival of the Religious Sciences — Section 90: The Ten Principles Concerning Knowledge of the Divine Attributes
6:103.anchors:
- Root: ع ل م (ʿ-l-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root denoting the faculty of perception and comprehension; the mark or trace by which something is known.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "العلم: إدراك الشيء بحقيقته" — knowledge is the apprehension of a thing in its true reality, divided into apprehension of the essence and judgment upon it.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Distinguishes literal knowledge (ḥaqīqah) from awareness (shiʿr); here, it denotes certain, verified cognition of theological verities.
- Root: س و ي (s-w-y)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Root indicating straightness, equality, and levelness; from it derives istiwāʾ (establishing oneself upon, ascending to).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Istiwāʾ upon the Throne (al-ʿArsh) is a divine act of sovereign dominion, not corporeal settlement.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal sense of physical sitting is impossible for God; metaphorical sense (majāz) of qahr (overpowering) and istīlāʾ (dominion) is necessitated by reason and consensus.
- Root: ر أ ي (r-ʾ-y)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Visual perception; also opinion and discernment.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Ruʾyah (vision) of God in the Hereafter is a mode of disclosure (kashf) and knowledge (ʿilm), more complete than intellectual cognition, not conditioned by spatial direction.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal vision requires corporeality and direction; its application to God demands theological specification (takhṣīṣ) without nullifying the veracity of the scriptural promise.
- Root: ق د ر (q-d-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Power, measure, decree; the capacity to bring about an act.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Divine power (qudrah) is the negation of incapacity (ʿajz); absolute power belongs to God alone, while creatures possess limited capacity.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal power over an object; metaphorically, God's power encompasses all things without exertion or instrument.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Prepositional Interposition (باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور) — governing the permissible separation between the preposition and its object for rhetorical emphasis, applied here to the parsing of "إلى السماء" in the verse on istiwāʾ, where the prepositional phrase is delayed to highlight the divine act of sovereign direction toward the heavens.
6:103.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Foundations of Belief'

6:115.arabic: في قوله تعالى وتمت كلمات ربك صدقا وعدلا صدقا لمن مات على الإيمان وعدلا لمن مات على الشرك وقد قال تعالى {ولله عاقبة الأمور} فمهما كان الشك بهذه المثابة كان الاستثناء واجبا لأن الإيمان عبارة عما يفيد الجنة كما أن الصوم عبارة عما يبرىء الذمة وما فسد قبل الغروب لا يبرىء الذمة فيخرج عن كونه صوما فكذلك الإيمان بل لا يبعد أن يسأل عن الصوم الماضي الذي لا يشك فيه بعد الفراغ منه فيقال أصمت بالأمس فيقول نعم إن شاء الله تعالى إذ الصوم الحقيقي هو المقبول والمقبول غائب عنه لا يطلع عليه إلا الله تع
6:115.english: I say: The fear of an evil end (sū' al-khātimah) is so severe that one of the early scholars (salaf) said: "Were I to stand at the door of the Prophet's chamber — peace be upon him — and be given the choice between death and affirming God's Oneness (al-tawḥīd) at that very door, I would choose death over affirming His Oneness there, for I do not know what change might befall my heart, turning me from tawḥīd [to its opposite] by the time I reached the door of the house."
6:115.section_title_en: The Book of the Foundations of Belief — Section 105: The Justification of Exception (Istithnā') in Matters of Faith
6:115.anchors:
- Root: صوم (ṣ-w-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning is "abstention" (imsāk) from any act — food, speech, or movement.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الصوم في الأصل: الإمساك عن الفعل مطعما كان، أو كلاما، أو مشيا" — Abstention from any act, whether food, speech, or walking; the horse that refrains from movement is called ṣā'im.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): The month of fasting. Metaphorical (Majaz): "صام الفرس على آريه إذا لم يعتلف" — The horse "fasts" when it refuses its fodder.
- Root: حسن (ḥ-s-n)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Beauty, goodness, excellence in form and act.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الحسن: عبارة عن كل مبهج مرغوب فيه" — That which pleases and is desired, whether by intellect, passion, or sense.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: Physical beauty and adornment. Metaphorical: "فلان لا يحسن شيئا، وقيمة المرء ما يحسن" — "So-and-so does not do anything well; a man's worth is what he does well."
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The permissibility of interposing elements between a governing word and its governed prepositional phrase, contingent upon the semantic completeness of the intervening clause.
6:115.topic: Al-Ghazali on the journey of the soul, death, and the Hereafter, from 'Foundations of Belief'

6:149.arabic: هل عندكم من سلطان بهذا أي حجة وبرهان وقال تعالى قل فلله الحجة البالغة وقال تعالى ألم تر إلى الذي حاج إبراهيم في ربه إلى قوله فبهت الذي كفر إذ ذكر سبحانه احتجاج إبراهيم ومجادلته وإفحامه خصمه في معرض الثناء عليه وقال عز وجل وتلك حجتنا آتيناها إبراهيم على قومه وقال تعالى قالوا يا نوح قد جادلتنا فأكثرت جدالنا وقال تعالى في قصة فرعون وما رب العالمين إلى قوله أولوا جئتك بشيء مبين وعلى الجملة فالقرآن من أوله إلى آخره محاجة مع الكفار فعمدة أدلة المتكلمين في التوحيد قوله تعالى {لو كان فيهما آلهة إلا الله لفسدتا} وفي النبوة

7:8.arabic: القيامة وقال تعالى فمن ثقلت موازينه فأولئك هم المفلحون ومن خفت موازينه الآية ووجهها أن الله تعالى يحدث في صحائف الأعمال وزنا بحسب درجات الأعمال عند الله تعالى فتصير مقادير أعمال العباد معلومة للعباد حتى يظهر لهم العدل في العقاب أو الفضل في العفو وتضعيف الثواب الأصل الخامس الصراط وهو جسر ممدود على متن جهنم أرق من الشعرة وأحد من السيف قال الله تعالى فاهدوهم إلى صراط الجحيم وقفوهم إنهم مسئولون وهذا ممكن فيجب التصديق به فإن القادر على أن يطير الطير في الهواء قادر على أن يسير الإنسان على الصراط الأصل السا
7:8.english: For they, despite their distinction in eloquence and rhetorical perfection, aimed at reviling him, forbidding him, killing him, and expelling him — as God, Mighty and Majestic, informed us about them — yet they were unable to produce anything to rival the Qur'an. For it was not within the capacity of human beings to combine the grandeur of the Qur'an's diction with its harmonious order, especially given what it contains of the accounts of the ancients, while he was illiterate, never having practiced the study of books — and [given] its announcement of the unseen in matters whose truthfulness was verified in the future, such as His saying, Exalted is He: {«لَتَدْخُلُنَّ الْمَسْجِدَ الْحَرَامَ إِنْ شَاءَ اللَّهُ آمِنِينَ مُحَلِّقِينَ رُءُوسَكُمْ وَمُقَصِّرِينَ»} (You shall surely enter the Sacred Mosque, if God wills, secure, with your heads shaved and cut short) [Al-Fatḥ 48:27], and such as His saying: {«الم غُلِبَتِ الرُّومُ فِي أَدْنَى الْأَرْضِ وَهُمْ مِنْ بَعْدِ غَلَبِهِمْ سَيَغْلِبُونَ فِي بِضْعِ سِنِينَ»} (Alif Lām Mīm. The Romans have been defeated in the nearest land, and they, after their defeat, shall be victorious within a few years) [Al-Rūm 30:1-3].
7:8.section_title_en: The Fourth Pillar: On Matters of Hearing (al-Samʿiyyāt) and the Verification of the Prophet ﷺ in What He Reported — Comprising Ten Fundamental Principles
7:8.anchors:
- Root: حشر (ḥ-sh-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To gather, assemble, drive together; al-ḥashr is the gathering of creation on the Day of Resurrection.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-ḥashr is the bringing together of a people from their various places of dispersal; it is used specifically for the resurrection gathering.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) for driving cattle together; metaphorical (majāz) for the ingathering of souls for judgment.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Conditional Protasis (al-sharṭ) — "If you are truthful, then rise..." (fa-in kunta ṣādiqan fa-qum...) — the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) functions as the proof of the protasis, establishing necessary knowledge (ʿilm ḍarūrī).

- Root: نشر (n-sh-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To spread, unfold, revive after death; al-nushūr is the revivification of the dead.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-nashr is the spreading of the soul back into the body after death; it is the opposite of al-ṭayy (folding up).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal for unfolding a garment; metaphorical for the resurrection when the earth "spreads forth" what it contains.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Coordination (al-ʿaṭf) — "al-ḥashr wa-l-nashr" (the gathering and the spreading) — two coordinated nouns forming a single compound concept of resurrection.

- Root: مكن (m-k-n)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To establish, empower, give firm footing; makkana means to make something firm and stable.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-makān is the place that contains a thing; tamakkun is the firm establishment of a thing in its place.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal for physical placement; metaphorical for divine power — "God is able" (qādir) means He has full capacity and authority over all things.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Possibility (al-imkān) — "that is possible" (dhālika mumkin) — the predicate of possibility is established by the absence of logical contradiction, not by empirical observation.

- Root: عذب (ʿ-dh-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Sweet, pleasant (of water); al-ʿadhāb is the punishment that is "sweet" to the inflictor but bitter to the recipient — used predominantly for divine chastisement.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-ʿadhāb is the infliction of pain that deters; it is specifically the painful consequence of disobedience.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal for sweet water; metaphorical (majāz) for punishment that is "appointed" as a deterrent.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Exception (al-istithnāʾ) — "except as God wills" (illā mā shāʾa) — the exception clause restricts the scope of human perception, not divine action.
7:8.topic: Al-Ghazali on the journey of the soul, death, and the Hereafter, from 'Foundations of Belief'

7:42.arabic: دونه وادعى الإجماع فيه واستدل بأدلة تشعر بنقيض غرضه كقوله تعالى {الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات} إذ هذا يدل على أن العمل وراء الإيمان لا من نفس الإيمان وإلا فيكون العمل في حكم المعاد والعجب أنه ادعى الإجماع في هذا وهو مع ذلك ينقل قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم لا يكفر أحد إلا بعد جحوده لما أقر به (1) وينكر على المعتزلة قولهم بالتخليد في النار بسبب الكبائر والقائل بهذا قائل بنفس مذهب المعتزلة إذ يقال له من صدق بقلبه وشهد بلسانه ومات في الحال فهل هو في الجنة فلا بد أن يقول نعم وفيه حكم بوجود الإيمان دون العمل فنزيد ونقول لو بقي حيا حتى دخل عليه وقت
7:42.english: He was asked, "Which deed is most excellent?" The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Islam." It was then asked, "Which aspect of Islam is most excellent?" He (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Faith (Īmān)." This is evidence for both the distinction (ikhtilāf) between the two terms and their overlap (tadākhul). This usage is the most consistent with the conventions of the language, because faith is a deed among deeds, and it is the most excellent of them. Islam is submission (taslīm), whether by the heart, by the tongue, or by the limbs. The most excellent of these is that which is by the heart, which is the assent (taṣdīq) that is called faith. Using the two terms in a way that indicates distinction, overlap, or even complete synonymy (tarāduf) is all within the bounds of metaphorical usage (tajawwuz) in the language.
7:42.section_title_en: The Book of the Revival of the Religious Sciences — Section 99: On the Distinction, Overlap, and Synonymy of Faith (Īmān) and Submission (Islām), and Their Worldly and Otherworldly Judgments
7:42.anchors:
- Root: ايم (A-Y-M)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of remaining unmarried, or a state of being without a spouse; extended metaphorically to describe one who is solitary or without support.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الأيامى: جمع أيم، وهي المرأة التي لا بعل لها... والحرب مأيمة، أي: يفرق بين الزوج والزوجة." The root carries the sense of separation or a state of lacking union, which informs the theological discussion of what constitutes the essential bond of faith.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah) usage denotes the state of being unmarried; metaphorical (Majaz) usage extends to anything that separates or leaves one bereft. This distinction between literal and metaphorical application is central to the chapter's method.
- Root: قلب (Q-L-B)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To turn, overturn, or transform a thing from one state to another.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "قلب الشيء: تصريفه وصرفه عن وجه إلى وجه... والانقلاب: الانصراف." The heart (qalb) is so named for its constant fluctuation and turning. In theological terms, it is the seat of taṣdīq (assent), the immaterial faculty of cognition and conviction.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah) usage is physical turning; metaphorical (Majaz) usage is "قلب الأمور" — to deliberate, scrutinize, and manage affairs. This supports the distinction between the heart's internal act of assent and the external acts of the limbs.
- Root: عمل (ʿ-A-M-L)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Any deed or action performed with purpose and intent.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "العمل: كل فعل يكون من الحيوان بقصد، فهو أخص من الفعل." Work is more specific than mere action, as it implies deliberate, intentional agency. It is used for both righteous and sinful deeds, and is the external manifestation of internal conviction.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah) usage refers to physical labor or deeds. The chapter explores whether "work" is an integral part of the reality of faith or a separate, consequent requirement.
- Root: صدق (S-D-Q)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To be truthful, to speak the truth, to verify.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الصدق والكذب أصلهما في القول... ولا يكونان بالقصد الأول إلا في القول." Truth and falsehood are primarily properties of speech and reports. Taṣdīq (assent) is the heart's affirmation of the truth of a report, which is the core reality of Īmān.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah) usage is truthful speech; metaphorical (Majaz) usage is "صادق الحملة" — one who is true and firm in battle or resolve. This shows that taṣdīq is not merely verbal but a firm, internal resolution.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication). This rule governs how restriction (ḥaṣr) is achieved in Arabic, often through particles like "innamā" or through contextual specification (takhṣīṣ). The chapter's core argument hinges on how terms like Īmān and Islām are semantically restricted, expanded, or made synonymous through contextual usage (majāz), requiring precise parsing of the predicate and its scope.
7:42.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Foundations of Belief'

7:50.arabic: ونكير وفي الميزان والصراط والحساب ومناظرات أهل النار وأهل الجنة في قولهم أفيضوا علينا من الماء أو مما رزقكم الله زعموا أن ذلك كله بلسان الحال وغلا آخرون في حسم الباب منهم أحمد بن حنبل رضي الله عنه حتى منع تأويل قوله كن فيكون وزعموا أن ذلك خطاب بحرف وصوت يوجد من الله تعالى في كل لحظة بعدد كون مكون حتى سمعت بعض أصحابه يقول إنه حسم باب التأويل إلا لثلاثة ألفاظ قوله
7:50.english: The fifth [division] is that one expresses by the tongue of explicit statement (lisān al-maqāl) what belongs to the tongue of state (lisān al-ḥāl). The one of deficient understanding stops at the outward and believes it to be literal speech, while the one with insight into realities perceives the secret within it. This is like the saying of one who said: "The wall said to the peg: 'Why have you split me?' It replied: 'Ask the one who strikes me — he did not leave me behind the stone that is behind me.'" This is an expression of the tongue of state by the tongue of explicit statement.
7:50.section_title_en: The Fourth Division — Comprehension by Encounter and Taste (Al-Dhawq), and the Fifth Division — The Tongue of State (Lisān al-Ḥāl)
7:50.anchors:
- Root: علم (ʿalima)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root denotes the faculty of knowing, perceiving a thing's reality; encompasses both direct apprehension and judgment about existence.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "العلم: إدراك الشيء بحقيقته" — knowledge is the apprehension of a thing in its true reality, divided into apprehension of the essence itself and judgment concerning it.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Distinguishes literal knowledge (maʿrifah) from awareness (shuʿūr); here, the distinction between superficial knowledge (ẓāhir) and realized knowledge (bāṭin) is rhetorical-metaphorical, not contradictory.
- Root: ظهر (ẓahara)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root denotes outwardness, visibility, strength of back; the ẓāhir is what is manifest and apparent.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The ẓāhir is used metaphorically for the outward aspect of a thing, as opposed to its inner reality (bāṭin); the back (ẓahr) carries what is loaded upon it.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas - Majaz): "قلبت الأمر ظهرا لبطن" — turning a matter over, examining its outward and inward aspects; the ẓāhir is the shell (qishr) that contains and is completed by the inner kernel (lubb).
- Root: وقع (waqaʿa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root denotes falling, occurring, befalling; a thing's occurrence and realization.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الوقوع: ثبوت الشيء وسقوطه" — occurrence is the establishment and falling of a thing; in Quranic usage, often associated with calamities and inevitable events.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas - Majaz): "وقع الأمر حصل ووجد" — the matter occurred, i.e., it became realized and existent; here, the "occurrence" of a state (ḥāl) is its actual realization in the soul, as opposed to mere intellectual assent before its descent.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The syntactic structure allows for separation between the operative word and its object to achieve rhetorical emphasis, mirroring the semantic distinction between outward apprehension and inward realization.
7:50.topic: Al-Ghazali on the journey of the soul, death, and the Hereafter, from 'Foundations of Belief'

8:4.arabic: تعالى لقوم مخصوصين بأعيانهم أولئك هم المؤمنون حقا فانقسموا إلى قسمين ويرجع هذا إلى الشك في كمال الإيمان لا في أصله وكل إنسان شاك في كمال إيمانه وذلك ليس بكفر والشك في كمال الإيمان حق من وجهين أحدهما من حيث إن النفاق يزيل كمال الإيمان وهو خفي لا تتحقق البراءة منه والثاني أنه يكمل بأعمال الطاعات ولا يدري وجودها على الكمال أما العمل فقد قال الله تعالى إنما المؤمنون الذين آمنوا بالله ورسوله ثم لم يرتابوا وجاهدوا بأموالهم وأنفسهم في سبيل الله أولئك هم الصادقون {فيكون}
8:4.english: If you say: "What is the meaning of the Salaf's statement, 'I am a believer, if God wills' — given that the exception (istithnā') implies doubt, and doubt in faith is unbelief? Yet they all refrained from giving an unqualified answer affirming faith and were cautious about it."
8:4.section_title_en: On the Meaning of the Salaf's Statement "I am a Believer, If God Wills" — Section 102
8:4.anchors:
- Root: نفس (n-f-s)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The self, the soul; that which is breathed; the innermost reality of a person.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): النفس is used for the rūḥ (spirit), for the dhāt (essence/self), and for the seat of intention and knowledge. When one says "he knows in himself (nafsihi) that he is a believer," it denotes certitude residing in the very core of one's being, not a corporeal faculty.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) usage refers to the soul's reflexive self-awareness; metaphorical (majāz) usage extends to "blood" (dam) or "the eye" (ʿayn) of envy. Here, "in himself" (fī nafsihi) is literal self-knowledge, not mere outward profession.
- Root: وجه (w-j-h)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Face, countenance; the foremost part; a mode, aspect, or direction.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The face is the most noble apparent part of a thing; hence it is used for the "aspect" or "manner" (wajh) of an affair. "Four aspects" (wujūh) means four distinct modes of interpretation or rational grounds.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the face of a person or object. Metaphorical: "the face of the matter" (wajh al-amr) — its most salient and honorable dimension. Here, the "aspects" are hermeneutical angles, not physical parts.
- Root: ايم (a-y-m)
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The unmarried state (aym); one who has no spouse. Not applicable here directly, but the root's semantic field of "being alone/without attachment" contrasts with īmān's root (a-m-n) — security and trust — which is the operative term in this text.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Not directly relevant; the operative root is أمن (a-m-n), meaning security from fear, and by extension, faith (īmān) as the state of being secure in God's truth.
- Root: كان (k-w-n)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To be, to exist; the copula of predication.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Kāna denotes existence and becoming; in theological usage, it grounds the distinction between what is (mawjūd) and what is merely asserted. The question "Are you a believer?" (a-mu'min anta?) uses kāna implicitly to ask about actual, present state — not future contingency.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: existence. Metaphorical: the "being-so" of a predicate. The istithnā' (exception) with "in shā' Allāh" suspends the copula's certainty, shifting from assertive existence to contingent hope.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الاستثناء والتعليق بالمشيئة (The Chapter of Exception and Suspension by the Divine Will) — When an exception clause (istithnā') follows a positive assertion, it grammatically suspends the universality or certainty of the predication. In theological discourse, this suspension may be semantic (doubt) or pragmatic (deference, etiquette, or self-deprecation), and Sibawayh's parsing of conditional suspension (taʿlīq) shows that the apodosis need not be negated — only its absolute, unqualified force is tempered.
8:4.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Foundations of Belief'

8:42.arabic: برهانكم وقال عز وجل ليهلك من هلك عن بينة ويحيا من حي عن بينة وقال تعالى هل عندكم من سلطان بهذا أي حجة وبرهان وقال تعالى قل فلله الحجة البالغة وقال تعالى ألم تر إلى الذي حاج إبراهيم في ربه إلى قوله فبهت الذي كفر إذ ذكر سبحانه احتجاج إبراهيم ومجادلته وإفحامه خصمه في معرض الثناء عليه وقال عز وجل وتلك حجتنا آتيناها إبراهيم على قومه وقال تعالى قالوا يا نوح قد جادلتنا فأكثرت جدالنا وقال تعالى في قصة فرعون وما رب العالمين إلى قوله أولوا جئتك بشيء مبين وعلى الجملة فالقرآن من أوله إلى آخره محاجة مع الكفار فعمدة أدل
8:42.english: The mention of the proof (ḥujjah), the demand for it, and the search after it — how could these be prohibited, when God — may He be exalted — has said: {«قُلْ هَاتُوا بُرْهَانَكُمْ»} (Say: Bring forth your proof — Qur'an 2:111), and He — mighty and majestic — has said: {«لِيَهْلِكَ مَنْ هَلَكَ عَنْ بَيِّنَةٍ وَيَحْيَا مَنْ حَيَّ عَنْ بَيِّنَةٍ»} (So that he who perishes may perish upon clear evidence, and he who lives may live upon clear evidence — Qur'an 8:42), and He — may He be exalted — has said: {«هَلْ عِنْدَكُمْ مِنْ سُلْطَانٍ بِهَذَا»} (Have you any authority for this? — Qur'an 10:68), meaning a proof and demonstration, and He — may He be exalted — has said: {«قُلْ فَلِلَّهِ الْحُجَّةُ الْبَالِغَةُ»} (Say: To God belongs the conclusive proof — Qur'an 6:149), and He — may He be exalted — has said: {«أَلَمْ تَرَ إِلَى الَّذِي حَاجَّ إِبْرَاهِيمَ فِي رَبِّهِ»} (Have you not considered him who disputed with Abraham concerning his Lord? — Qur'an 2:258) up to His words: {«فَبُهِتَ الَّذِي كَفَرَ»} (So the one who disbelieved was confounded — Qur'an 2:258).
8:42.section_title_en: The Revival of the Religious Sciences — Section 77: On the Permissibility of Theological Discourse (Kalām) and Its Early Practice
8:42.anchors:
- Root: ح-د-ث (ḥ-d-th)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "Al-ḥudūth: the coming-to-be of a thing after it was not; al-ḥadath: the novel event; al-ḥīdāth: origination."
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Al-ḥudūth: a thing's becoming after it was not, whether accident or substance; iḥdāth: bringing it into existence. The origination of substances belongs to God alone."
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "Literal: 'He is a recent event among events.' Metaphorical: 'They became topics of conversation (aḥādīth).'"
- Root: ح-ا-ج (ḥ-ā-j)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "Al-ḥājah: need of a thing, with desire for it; its plural: ḥājāt and ḥawā'ij."
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Al-ḥājah ilā al-shay': poverty toward it with love of it. God said: {«إِلَّا حَاجَةً فِي نَفْسِ يَعْقُوبَ»} (except a need in Jacob's soul — Qur'an 12:68)."
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "Literal: need and want. The 'ḥājah' is that which one seeks to obtain."
- Root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "Kāna: to be, to exist; takwīn: bringing into being from non-existence."
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Al-kawn: existence after non-existence; the muḥdath (originated thing) is that brought forth after it was not."
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "Literal: being and becoming. Metaphorical: the continuous states of affairs."
- Sibawayh Rule: Al-Faṣl bayna al-Jār wa-al-Majrūr (Prepositional Interposition) — The permissibility of separating a preposition from its object when the intervening clause is complete in meaning, as in the verse's structure of argumentation where the proof (ḥujjah) stands independently before its conclusion.
8:42.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Foundations of Belief'

8:42.arabic: القلوب قلة إلى أن تقرب الساعة ويقضي الله أمرا كان مفعولا وإنما وجب أن يكون هذا نادرا لأنه مبادي ملك الآخرة والملك عزيز والملوك لا يكثرون فكما لا يكون الفائق في الملك والجمال إلا نادرا وأكثر الناس من دونهم فكذا في ملك الآخرة فإن الدنيا مرآة الآخرة فإنها عبارة عن عالم الشهادة والآخرة عبارة عن عالم الغيب وعالم الشهادة تابع لعالم الغيب كما أن الصورة في المرآة تابعة لصورة الناظر في المرآة والصورة في المرآة وإن كانت هي الثانية في رتبة الوجود فإنها أولى في حق رؤيتك فإنك لا ترى نفسك وترى صورتك في المرآة أولا فتعرف
8:42.english: As for the first: if it is possible in existence at all, it is at the utmost extreme of remoteness. As for the second: the lower world is overflowing with it. As for the third and fourth: they exist, but at the utmost extreme of rarity. And it is inconceivable that this [rarity] should itself be rare and anomalous — rather, even with its rarity, it varies in degree of fewness and abundance. Its abundance occurs only in ages proximate to the ages of the Prophets, peace be upon them. The longer the interval [from their time] grows, the scarcer such hearts become, until the Hour draws near and God accomplishes a matter already decreed ( {وكان أمرا مفعولا} ).
8:42.section_title_en: The Division of Hearts and the Rarity of the Heart Fit for the Kingdom of the Hereafter
8:42.anchors:
- Root: م ل ك (Malaka)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of possession, dominion, and sovereign control; al-Ayn notes the pattern shift in derived nouns.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الملك: هو المتصرف بالأمر والنهي في الجمهور" — kingship is governance over rational beings, divided into actual sovereignty (al-tamalluk) and capacity for it (al-quwwah).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "لله الملك والملكوت" — dominion over the visible and invisible realms. Metaphorical: "ملك نفسه عند الغضب" — self-mastery; here extended to the heart's sovereignty over the soul's appetites.
- Root: ق ل ب (Qalaba)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Turning and overturning a thing from one state to another.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "قلب الشيء: تصريفه وصرفه عن وجه إلى وجه" — the heart is so named for its constant fluctuation between states.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "قلب الشيء قلبا: حوله عن وجهه." Metaphorical: "رجل قلب حول: يقلب الأمور ويحتال" — one who turns matters over; here, hearts are classified by their dominant orientation.
- Root: ع ل م (ʿAlima)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Foundational knowing and perception.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "العلم: إدراك الشيء بحقيقته" — apprehension of a thing's true reality, of two kinds: grasping the essence, and judging its attributes.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "هو من أعلام العلم الخافقه" — knowledge as a raised banner. Here, "علم اليقين" (knowledge of certainty) vs. "عين اليقين" (eye of certainty) marks the literal-to-metaphorical ascent from inference to direct vision.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — The repeated use of "إنما" (only/indeed) throughout this passage serves to restrict predicates exclusively to their subjects, e.g., "وإنما تكون كثرته في الأعصار القريبة" — restricting abundance to specific eras, and "وإنما وجب أن يكون هذا نادرا" — restricting the cause of rarity.
8:42.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

8:74.arabic: كأنك حفي عنها أي يسألونك عنها كأنك حفي بها وقوله عز وجل لهم مغفرة ورزق كريم كما أخرجك ربك من بيتك بالحق فهذا الكلام غير متصل وإنما هو عائد إلى قوله السابق قل الأنفال لله والرسول كما أخرجك ربك من بيتك بالحق أي فصارت أنفال الغنائم لك إذ أنت راض بخروجك وهم كارهون فاعترض بين الكلام الأمر بالتقوى وغيره ومن هذا النوع قوله عز وجل حتى تؤمنوا بالله وحده إلا قول إبراهيم لأبيه الآية ومنها المبهم وهو اللفظ المشترك بين معن من كلمة أو حرف أما الكلمة فكالشيء والقرين والأمة والروح ونظائرها قال الله تعالى ضرب الله مثلا عبدا مملوكا لا ي
8:74.english: I say: The Prophet (peace be upon him) was asked about the means of deliverance from these trials, and he said: "The Book of Allah — act by what is in it, for it is that which delivers one from them." The questioner repeated this three times, and he (peace be upon him) said three times: "Learn the Book of Allah, Mighty and Glorious, and act by what is in it, for in it is deliverance."
8:74.section_title_en: The Book of the Etiquette of Recitation — Section 233: On Understanding the Meanings of the Qur'an and the Limits of Interpretation
8:74.anchors:
- Root: ف-ه-م (f-h-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الفهم: هيئة للإنسان بها يتحقق معاني ما يحسن" — comprehension as an inherent faculty by which one ascertains meanings
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الفهم: هيئة للإنسان بها يتحقق معاني ما يحسن... وأفهمته: إذا قلت له حتى تصوره" — comprehension is a cognitive disposition; distinction between understanding (fahm) and making understood (ifhām)
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "تقول: من لم يؤت من سوء الفهم أتى من سوء الإفهام" — literal usage; failure of understanding often stems from failure of communication
- Root: ف-س-ر (f-s-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "وكل شيء يعرف به تفسير الشيء ومعناه، فهو تَفْسِرَتُه" — that by which a thing's meaning is made known
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "التفسير قد يقال فيما يختص بمفردات الألفاظ وغريبها، وفيما يختص بالتأويل" — tafsīr concerns lexical surface; taʾwīl concerns deeper meaning
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "هذا كلام يحتاج إلى فسر وتفسير" — literal: exposition of what is obscure
- Root: و-ج-ل (w-j-l)
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الوجل: استشعار الخوف" — the sensing of fear; used of hearts trembling at divine mention
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "لو واجلت فلانا لوجلته: لغلبته في الوجل" — literal sense of fear; metaphorical extension to overpowering in fear
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — the particle innamā restricts predication, essential for parsing the Prophet's saying "innamā al-aʿmālu bi-l-niyyāt" and analogous restrictive formulations in the ḥadīth cited herein
8:74.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Etiquette of Quran Recitation'

8:74.arabic: تعالى لقوم مخصوصين بأعيانهم أولئك هم المؤمنون حقا فانقسموا إلى قسمين ويرجع هذا إلى الشك في كمال الإيمان لا في أصله وكل إنسان شاك في كمال إيمانه وذلك ليس بكفر والشك في كمال الإيمان حق من وجهين أحدهما من حيث إن النفاق يزيل كمال الإيمان وهو خفي لا تتحقق البراءة منه والثاني أنه يكمل بأعمال الطاعات ولا يدري وجودها على الكمال أما العمل فقد قال الله تعالى إنما المؤمنون الذين آمنوا بالله ورسوله ثم لم يرتابوا وجاهدوا بأموالهم وأنفسهم في سبيل الله أولئك هم الصادقون {فيكون}
8:74.english: If you say: "What is the meaning of the Salaf's statement, 'I am a believer, if God wills' — given that the exception (istithnā') implies doubt, and doubt in faith is unbelief? Yet they all refrained from giving an unqualified answer affirming faith and were cautious about it."
8:74.section_title_en: On the Meaning of the Salaf's Statement "I am a Believer, If God Wills" — Section 102
8:74.anchors:
- Root: نفس (n-f-s)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The self, the soul; that which is breathed; the innermost reality of a person.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): النفس is used for the rūḥ (spirit), for the dhāt (essence/self), and for the seat of intention and knowledge. When one says "he knows in himself (nafsihi) that he is a believer," it denotes certitude residing in the very core of one's being, not a corporeal faculty.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) usage refers to the soul's reflexive self-awareness; metaphorical (majāz) usage extends to "blood" (dam) or "the eye" (ʿayn) of envy. Here, "in himself" (fī nafsihi) is literal self-knowledge, not mere outward profession.
- Root: وجه (w-j-h)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Face, countenance; the foremost part; a mode, aspect, or direction.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The face is the most noble apparent part of a thing; hence it is used for the "aspect" or "manner" (wajh) of an affair. "Four aspects" (wujūh) means four distinct modes of interpretation or rational grounds.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the face of a person or object. Metaphorical: "the face of the matter" (wajh al-amr) — its most salient and honorable dimension. Here, the "aspects" are hermeneutical angles, not physical parts.
- Root: ايم (a-y-m)
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The unmarried state (aym); one who has no spouse. Not applicable here directly, but the root's semantic field of "being alone/without attachment" contrasts with īmān's root (a-m-n) — security and trust — which is the operative term in this text.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Not directly relevant; the operative root is أمن (a-m-n), meaning security from fear, and by extension, faith (īmān) as the state of being secure in God's truth.
- Root: كان (k-w-n)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To be, to exist; the copula of predication.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Kāna denotes existence and becoming; in theological usage, it grounds the distinction between what is (mawjūd) and what is merely asserted. The question "Are you a believer?" (a-mu'min anta?) uses kāna implicitly to ask about actual, present state — not future contingency.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: existence. Metaphorical: the "being-so" of a predicate. The istithnā' (exception) with "in shā' Allāh" suspends the copula's certainty, shifting from assertive existence to contingent hope.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الاستثناء والتعليق بالمشيئة (The Chapter of Exception and Suspension by the Divine Will) — When an exception clause (istithnā') follows a positive assertion, it grammatically suspends the universality or certainty of the predication. In theological discourse, this suspension may be semantic (doubt) or pragmatic (deference, etiquette, or self-deprecation), and Sibawayh's parsing of conditional suspension (taʿlīq) shows that the apodosis need not be negated — only its absolute, unqualified force is tempered.
8:74.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Foundations of Belief'

9:120.arabic: فتح الباب والله لا يضيع أجر المحسنين وإن تك حسنة يضاعفها ويؤت من لدنه أجرا عظيما المقام الثاني في دفع العارض منه في أثناء العبادة وذلك لا بد من تعلمه أيضا فإن من جاهد نفسه وقلع مغارس الرياء من قلبه بالقناعة وقطع الطمع وإسقاط نفسه من أعين المخلوقين واستحقار مدح المخلوقين وذمهم فالشيطان لا يتركه في أثناء العبادات بل يعارضه بخطرات الرياء ولا تنقطع عنه نزعاته وهوى النفس وميلها لا ينمحي بالكلية فلا بد وأن يتشمر لدفع ما يعرض من خاطر الرياء وخواطر الرياء ثلاثة قد تخطر دفعة واحدة كالخاطر ال
9:120.english: So when the harm and injury of these causes is firmly settled in his heart, his desire [for them] slackens, and his heart turns toward God. For the intelligent person does not covet that whose harm is abundant and whose benefit is scant. It suffices him that if people knew what is in his inner self—the intent of ostentation (riyā') and the display of sincerity—they would abhor him. And God will surely expose his secret until He makes him odious to the people and makes them know that he is a show-off, abhorrent to God. Had he been sincere to God, God would have unveiled his sincerity to them, made him beloved to them, subjected them to him, and loosened their tongues in praise and commendation of him—even though there is no perfection in their praise, nor deficiency in their blame. As the poet of Banī Tamīm said: "My praise is an adornment, and my blame is a disgrace." The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said to him: "You have lied—that belongs to God, there is no deity but Him." // [Hadith: A poet of Banī Tamīm said, "My praise is an adornment, and my blame is a disgrace." He (the Prophet) said: "You have lied—that belongs to God." Ahmad narrated it from the hadith of al-Aqra' ibn Ḥābis—who was the speaker of that verse, excluding the phrase "You have lied"—and its narrators are trustworthy, except that I do not know of Abū Salamah ibn 'Abd al-Raḥmān having heard [directly] from al-Aqra'. Al-Tirmidhī narrated it from the hadith of al-Barā' and deemed it sound (ḥasan), with the wording: "A man said, 'Indeed, my praise...'"]
9:120.section_title_en: The Revival of the Religious Sciences — Section 827: The Second Station: Repelling the Accidental Promptings of Ostentation During Worship
9:120.anchors:
- Root: كذب (kadhaba)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: falsehood, lying, saying what is contrary to reality; also used for "to declare someone a liar."
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In theological context, kadhb is the antithesis of sidq (truthfulness); it is a moral and epistemic vice, often linked to hypocrisy (nifāq) and false claims.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (haqīqah): to report what did not occur. Metaphorical (majāz): attributing to God what is unworthy of Him, as in the Prophet's rebuke of the poet's self-praise.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Predicate Emphasis (Bāb al-Tawkīd) — The Prophet's reply "كَذَبْتَ" (You have lied) functions as an emphatic categorical refutation, structured as a nominal sentence with implied subject, establishing a permanent verdict rather than a transient rebuke.
9:120.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Condemnation of Status and Ostentation'

9:120.arabic: من إيمان وقوله تعالى إنا لا نضيع أجر من أحسن عملا وقوله تعالى إن الله لا يضيع أجر المحسنين فكيف يضيع أجر أصل الإيمان وجميع الطاعات بمعصية واحدة وقوله تعالى ومن يقتل مؤمنا متعمدا أي لإيمانه وقد ورد على مثل هذا السبب فإن قلت فقد مال الاختيار إلى أن الإيمان حاصل دون العمل وقد اشتهر عن السلف قولهم الإيمان عقد وقول وعمل فما معناه قلنا لا يبعد أن يعد العمل من الإيمان لأنه مكمل له ومتمم كما يقال الرأس واليدان من الإنسان ومعلوم أنه يخرج عن كونه إنسانا بعدم الرأس ولا يخرج عنه بكونه مقطوع اليد وكذلك يقال التسبيحات والتكبيرات من الصلاة وإن كا
9:120.english: He was asked, "Which deed is most excellent?" The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Islam." It was then asked, "Which aspect of Islam is most excellent?" He (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Faith (Īmān)." This is evidence for both the distinction (ikhtilāf) between the two terms and their overlap (tadākhul). This usage is the most consistent with the conventions of the language, because faith is a deed among deeds, and it is the most excellent of them. Islam is submission (taslīm), whether by the heart, by the tongue, or by the limbs. The most excellent of these is that which is by the heart, which is the assent (taṣdīq) that is called faith. Using the two terms in a way that indicates distinction, overlap, or even complete synonymy (tarāduf) is all within the bounds of metaphorical usage (tajawwuz) in the language.
9:120.section_title_en: The Book of the Revival of the Religious Sciences — Section 99: On the Distinction, Overlap, and Synonymy of Faith (Īmān) and Submission (Islām), and Their Worldly and Otherworldly Judgments
9:120.anchors:
- Root: ايم (A-Y-M)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of remaining unmarried, or a state of being without a spouse; extended metaphorically to describe one who is solitary or without support.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الأيامى: جمع أيم، وهي المرأة التي لا بعل لها... والحرب مأيمة، أي: يفرق بين الزوج والزوجة." The root carries the sense of separation or a state of lacking union, which informs the theological discussion of what constitutes the essential bond of faith.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah) usage denotes the state of being unmarried; metaphorical (Majaz) usage extends to anything that separates or leaves one bereft. This distinction between literal and metaphorical application is central to the chapter's method.
- Root: قلب (Q-L-B)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To turn, overturn, or transform a thing from one state to another.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "قلب الشيء: تصريفه وصرفه عن وجه إلى وجه... والانقلاب: الانصراف." The heart (qalb) is so named for its constant fluctuation and turning. In theological terms, it is the seat of taṣdīq (assent), the immaterial faculty of cognition and conviction.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah) usage is physical turning; metaphorical (Majaz) usage is "قلب الأمور" — to deliberate, scrutinize, and manage affairs. This supports the distinction between the heart's internal act of assent and the external acts of the limbs.
- Root: عمل (ʿ-A-M-L)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Any deed or action performed with purpose and intent.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "العمل: كل فعل يكون من الحيوان بقصد، فهو أخص من الفعل." Work is more specific than mere action, as it implies deliberate, intentional agency. It is used for both righteous and sinful deeds, and is the external manifestation of internal conviction.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah) usage refers to physical labor or deeds. The chapter explores whether "work" is an integral part of the reality of faith or a separate, consequent requirement.
- Root: صدق (S-D-Q)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To be truthful, to speak the truth, to verify.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الصدق والكذب أصلهما في القول... ولا يكونان بالقصد الأول إلا في القول." Truth and falsehood are primarily properties of speech and reports. Taṣdīq (assent) is the heart's affirmation of the truth of a report, which is the core reality of Īmān.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah) usage is truthful speech; metaphorical (Majaz) usage is "صادق الحملة" — one who is true and firm in battle or resolve. This shows that taṣdīq is not merely verbal but a firm, internal resolution.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication). This rule governs how restriction (ḥaṣr) is achieved in Arabic, often through particles like "innamā" or through contextual specification (takhṣīṣ). The chapter's core argument hinges on how terms like Īmān and Islām are semantically restricted, expanded, or made synonymous through contextual usage (majāz), requiring precise parsing of the predicate and its scope.
9:120.topic: Al-Ghazali on constant remembrance of God and contemplative invocations, from 'Foundations of Belief'

10:61.arabic: السموات وأنه عالم لا يعزب عن علمه مثقال ذرة في الأرض ولا في السماء بل يعلم دبيب النملة السوداء على الصخرة الصماء في الليلة الظلماء ويدرك حركة الذر في جو الهواء ويعلم السر وأخفى ويطلع على هواجس الضمائر وحركات الخواطر وخفيات السرائر بعلم قديم أزلي لم يزل موصوفا به في أزل الآزال لا بعلم متجدد حاصل في ذاته بالحلول والانتقال الإرادة وأنه تعالى مريد للكائنات مدبر للحادثات فلا يجري في الملك والملكوت قليل أو كثير صغير أو كبير خير أو شر نفع أو ضر إيمان أو كفر عرفان أو نكر فوز أو خسران زيادة أو نقصان طاعة أو عصيان إلا بقضا
10:61.english:
- **Root: خلق (khalaqa)**
  - *Lisan / Ayn:* Core meaning of measuring, proportioning, and fashioning; al-Khalil notes the root's application to the act of creation as bringing forth upon a measured determination.
  - *Al-Raghib (Mufradat):* "الخلق أصله: التقدير المستقيم" — Creation fundamentally signifies right/straight measurement; used for bringing into being from nothing (ibdāʿ) as in {خلق السماوات والأرض}, and for bringing forth from something as in {خلقكم من نفس واحدة}.
  - *Al-Zamakhshari (Asas):* Literal (ḥaqīqah): the craftsman's measuring before cutting. Metaphorical (majāz): "خلق الله الخلق: أوجده على تقدير أوجبته الحكمة" — God's creation is bringing into existence upon a measure necessitated by wisdom.
10:61.topic: Classical commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya Ulum al-Din, from 'Foundations of Belief'

10:68.arabic: هل عندكم من سلطان بهذا أي حجة وبرهان وقال تعالى قل فلله الحجة البالغة وقال تعالى ألم تر إلى الذي حاج إبراهيم في ربه إلى قوله فبهت الذي كفر إذ ذكر سبحانه احتجاج إبراهيم ومجادلته وإفحامه خصمه في معرض الثناء عليه وقال عز وجل وتلك حجتنا آتيناها إبراهيم على قومه وقال تعالى قالوا يا نوح قد جادلتنا فأكثرت جدالنا وقال تعالى في قصة فرعون وما رب العالمين إلى قوله أولوا جئتك بشيء مبين وعلى الجملة فالقرآن من أوله إلى آخره محاجة مع الكفار فعمدة أدلة المتكلمين في التوحيد قوله تعالى {
10:68.english: The mention of the proof (ḥujjah), the demand for it, and the search after it — how could these be prohibited, when God — may He be exalted — has said: {«قُلْ هَاتُوا بُرْهَانَكُمْ»} (Say: Bring forth your proof — Qur'an 2:111), and He — mighty and majestic — has said: {«لِيَهْلِكَ مَنْ هَلَكَ عَنْ بَيِّنَةٍ وَيَحْيَا مَنْ حَيَّ عَنْ بَيِّنَةٍ»} (So that he who perishes may perish upon clear evidence, and he who lives may live upon clear evidence — Qur'an 8:42), and He — may He be exalted — has said: {«هَلْ عِنْدَكُمْ مِنْ سُلْطَانٍ بِهَذَا»} (Have you any authority for this? — Qur'an 10:68), meaning a proof and demonstration, and He — may He be exalted — has said: {«قُلْ فَلِلَّهِ الْحُجَّةُ الْبَالِغَةُ»} (Say: To God belongs the conclusive proof — Qur'an 6:149), and He — may He be exalted — has said: {«أَلَمْ تَرَ إِلَى الَّذِي حَاجَّ إِبْرَاهِيمَ فِي رَبِّهِ»} (Have you not considered him who disputed with Abraham concerning his Lord? — Qur'an 2:258) up to His words: {«فَبُهِتَ الَّذِي كَفَرَ»} (So the one who disbelieved was confounded — Qur'an 2:258).
10:68.section_title_en: The Revival of the Religious Sciences — Section 77: On the Permissibility of Theological Discourse (Kalām) and Its Early Practice
10:68.anchors:
- Root: ح-د-ث (ḥ-d-th)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "Al-ḥudūth: the coming-to-be of a thing after it was not; al-ḥadath: the novel event; al-ḥīdāth: origination."
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Al-ḥudūth: a thing's becoming after it was not, whether accident or substance; iḥdāth: bringing it into existence. The origination of substances belongs to God alone."
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "Literal: 'He is a recent event among events.' Metaphorical: 'They became topics of conversation (aḥādīth).'"
- Root: ح-ا-ج (ḥ-ā-j)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "Al-ḥājah: need of a thing, with desire for it; its plural: ḥājāt and ḥawā'ij."
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Al-ḥājah ilā al-shay': poverty toward it with love of it. God said: {«إِلَّا حَاجَةً فِي نَفْسِ يَعْقُوبَ»} (except a need in Jacob's soul — Qur'an 12:68)."
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "Literal: need and want. The 'ḥājah' is that which one seeks to obtain."
- Root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "Kāna: to be, to exist; takwīn: bringing into being from non-existence."
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Al-kawn: existence after non-existence; the muḥdath (originated thing) is that brought forth after it was not."
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "Literal: being and becoming. Metaphorical: the continuous states of affairs."
- Sibawayh Rule: Al-Faṣl bayna al-Jār wa-al-Majrūr (Prepositional Interposition) — The permissibility of separating a preposition from its object when the intervening clause is complete in meaning, as in the verse's structure of argumentation where the proof (ḥujjah) stands independently before its conclusion.
10:68.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Foundations of Belief'

10:84.arabic: بيت من المسلمين ولم يكن بالاتفاق إلا بيت واحد وقال تعالى يا قوم إن كنتم آمنتم بالله فعليه توكلوا إن كنتم مسلمين وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم بني الإسلام على خمس (1) وسئل رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم مرة عن الإيمان فأجاب بهذه الخمس (2) وأما الاختلاف فقوله تعالى {قالت الأعراب آمنا قل لم تؤمنوا ولكن قولوا أسلمنا} ومعناه استسلمنا في الظاهر فأراد بالإيمان ههنا التصديق بالقلب فقط وبالإسلام الاستسلام ظاهرا باللسان والجوارح وفي حديث جبرائيل عليه السلام لما سأله عن الإيمان فقال أن تؤمن بالله وملائكته وكتبه ورسله واليوم الآخر وبالبعث بعد الموت وبالحساب وبالقدر خيره وشره ف
10:84.english: The truth in this matter is that faith (iman) is an expression for assent (tasdiq). God, exalted be He, has said: {وَمَا أَنتَ بِمُؤْمِنٍ لِّنَا} [And you are not one to believe us] (Quran 12:17) — that is, not one to assent to us. And Islam is an expression for surrender (taslim) and self-abandonment (istislam) through acquiescence (idhan) and compliance (inqiyad), and the abandonment of recalcitrance, refusal, obstinacy, and stubbornness.
10:84.section_title_en: On Whether Islam and Faith (Iman) Are Identical or Distinct
10:84.anchors:
- Root: أمن (amana)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root denotes safety, security, and freedom from fear; the isti'man form yields 'belief' as an act of granting credence and trust.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الإيمان هو التصديق" — Faith (iman) is fundamentally assent (tasdiq), a conviction of the heart, not a mere verbal profession.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah) usage ties iman to tasdiq (verification/assent); metaphorical extension applies it to outward compliance only in a derived sense.
- Root: سلم (salima)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root denotes soundness, safety, and freedom from defect; the istislam form yields 'submission' as an act of yielding and surrendering.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الإسلام عبارة عن التسليم والاستسلام" — Islam is surrender (taslim) and self-abandonment (istislam) through compliance and obedience.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah) usage encompasses outward acts of the limbs; metaphorical (Majaz) usage can extend to inward assent, but the primary domain is the external.
- Root: صدق (sadaqa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root denotes truthfulness and veracity in speech and report.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الصدق والكذب أصلهما في القول" — Truth and falsehood originate in speech; tasdiq is the act of affirming a report as true.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah) usage is in verbal confirmation; metaphorical extension applies to 'true in resolve' or 'true in attack,' i.e., confirming through action.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Interposition (باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور) — Governing the permissible separation between a governing word and its governed prepositional phrase, relevant here for parsing the conditional and contrastive structures in the theological arguments.
10:84.topic: Al-Ghazali on the journey of the soul, death, and the Hereafter, from 'Foundations of Belief'

11:32.arabic: عز وجل وتلك حجتنا آتيناها إبراهيم على قومه وقال تعالى قالوا يا نوح قد جادلتنا فأكثرت جدالنا وقال تعالى في قصة فرعون وما رب العالمين إلى قوله أولوا جئتك بشيء مبين وعلى الجملة فالقرآن من أوله إلى آخره محاجة مع الكفار فعمدة أدلة المتكلمين في التوحيد قوله تعالى {لو كان فيهما آلهة إلا الله لفسدتا} وفي النبوة {وإن كنتم في ريب مما نزلنا على عبدنا فأتوا بسورة من مثله} وفي البعث {قل يحييها الذي أنشأها أول مرة} إلى غير ذلك من الآيات والأدلة ولم تزل الرسل صلوات الله عليهم يحاجون المنكرين ويجادلونهم قال تعالى {وجادلهم بالتي هي أحسن} فالصحابة رضي ال
11:32.english: The mention of the proof (ḥujjah), the demand for it, and the search after it — how could these be prohibited, when God — may He be exalted — has said: {«قُلْ هَاتُوا بُرْهَانَكُمْ»} (Say: Bring forth your proof — Qur'an 2:111), and He — mighty and majestic — has said: {«لِيَهْلِكَ مَنْ هَلَكَ عَنْ بَيِّنَةٍ وَيَحْيَا مَنْ حَيَّ عَنْ بَيِّنَةٍ»} (So that he who perishes may perish upon clear evidence, and he who lives may live upon clear evidence — Qur'an 8:42), and He — may He be exalted — has said: {«هَلْ عِنْدَكُمْ مِنْ سُلْطَانٍ بِهَذَا»} (Have you any authority for this? — Qur'an 10:68), meaning a proof and demonstration, and He — may He be exalted — has said: {«قُلْ فَلِلَّهِ الْحُجَّةُ الْبَالِغَةُ»} (Say: To God belongs the conclusive proof — Qur'an 6:149), and He — may He be exalted — has said: {«أَلَمْ تَرَ إِلَى الَّذِي حَاجَّ إِبْرَاهِيمَ فِي رَبِّهِ»} (Have you not considered him who disputed with Abraham concerning his Lord? — Qur'an 2:258) up to His words: {«فَبُهِتَ الَّذِي كَفَرَ»} (So the one who disbelieved was confounded — Qur'an 2:258).
11:32.section_title_en: The Revival of the Religious Sciences — Section 77: On the Permissibility of Theological Discourse (Kalām) and Its Early Practice
11:32.anchors:
- Root: ح-د-ث (ḥ-d-th)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "Al-ḥudūth: the coming-to-be of a thing after it was not; al-ḥadath: the novel event; al-ḥīdāth: origination."
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Al-ḥudūth: a thing's becoming after it was not, whether accident or substance; iḥdāth: bringing it into existence. The origination of substances belongs to God alone."
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "Literal: 'He is a recent event among events.' Metaphorical: 'They became topics of conversation (aḥādīth).'"
- Root: ح-ا-ج (ḥ-ā-j)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "Al-ḥājah: need of a thing, with desire for it; its plural: ḥājāt and ḥawā'ij."
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Al-ḥājah ilā al-shay': poverty toward it with love of it. God said: {«إِلَّا حَاجَةً فِي نَفْسِ يَعْقُوبَ»} (except a need in Jacob's soul — Qur'an 12:68)."
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "Literal: need and want. The 'ḥājah' is that which one seeks to obtain."
- Root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "Kāna: to be, to exist; takwīn: bringing into being from non-existence."
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Al-kawn: existence after non-existence; the muḥdath (originated thing) is that brought forth after it was not."
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "Literal: being and becoming. Metaphorical: the continuous states of affairs."
- Sibawayh Rule: Al-Faṣl bayna al-Jār wa-al-Majrūr (Prepositional Interposition) — The permissibility of separating a preposition from its object when the intervening clause is complete in meaning, as in the verse's structure of argumentation where the proof (ḥujjah) stands independently before its conclusion.
11:32.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'Foundations of Belief'

12:17.arabic: الله تعالى وما أنت بمؤمن لنا أي بمصدق والإسلام عبارة عن التسليم والاستسلام بالإذعان والانقياد وترك التمرد والإباء والعناد وللتصديق محل خاص وهو القلب واللسان ترجمان وأما التسليم فإنه عام في القلب واللسان والجوارح فإن كل تصديق بالقلب فهو تسليم وترك الإباء والجحود وكذلك الاعتراف باللسان وكذلك الطاعة والانقياد بالجوارح فموجب اللغة أن الإسلام أعم والإيمان أخص فكان الإيمان عبارة عن أشرف أجزاء الإسلام فإذن كل تصديق تسليم وليس كل تسليم تصديقا البحث الثاني عن إطلاق الشرع والحق
12:17.english: The truth in this matter is that faith (iman) is an expression for assent (tasdiq). God, exalted be He, has said: {وَمَا أَنتَ بِمُؤْمِنٍ لِّنَا} [And you are not one to believe us] (Quran 12:17) — that is, not one to assent to us. And Islam is an expression for surrender (taslim) and self-abandonment (istislam) through acquiescence (idhan) and compliance (inqiyad), and the abandonment of recalcitrance, refusal, obstinacy, and stubbornness.
12:17.section_title_en: On Whether Islam and Faith (Iman) Are Identical or Distinct
12:17.anchors:
- Root: أمن (amana)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root denotes safety, security, and freedom from fear; the isti'man form yields 'belief' as an act of granting credence and trust.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الإيمان هو التصديق" — Faith (iman) is fundamentally assent (tasdiq), a conviction of the heart, not a mere verbal profession.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah) usage ties iman to tasdiq (verification/assent); metaphorical extension applies it to outward compliance only in a derived sense.
- Root: سلم (salima)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root denotes soundness, safety, and freedom from defect; the istislam form yields 'submission' as an act of yielding and surrendering.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الإسلام عبارة عن التسليم والاستسلام" — Islam is surrender (taslim) and self-abandonment (istislam) through compliance and obedience.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah) usage encompasses outward acts of the limbs; metaphorical (Majaz) usage can extend to inward assent, but the primary domain is the external.
- Root: صدق (sadaqa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root denotes truthfulness and veracity in speech and report.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الصدق والكذب أصلهما في القول" — Truth and falsehood originate in speech; tasdiq is the act of affirming a report as true.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah) usage is in verbal confirmation; metaphorical extension applies to 'true in resolve' or 'true in attack,' i.e., confirming through action.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Interposition (باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور) — Governing the permissible separation between a governing word and its governed prepositional phrase, relevant here for parsing the conditional and contrastive structures in the theological arguments.
12:17.topic: Al-Ghazali on purifying the character, moral diseases, and spiritual remedies, from 'Foundations of Belief'

13:17.arabic: أنه أريد به غير الظاهر كما ورد في تفسير قوله تعالى أنزل من السماء ماء فسالت أودية بقدرها الآية وأن معنى الماء ههنا هو القرآن ومعنى الأودية هي القلوب وأن بعضها احتملت شيئا كثيرا وبعضها قليلا وبعضها لم يحتمل والزبد مثل الكفر والنفاق فإنه وإن ظهر وطفا على رأس الماء فإنه لا يثبت والهداية التي تنفع الناس تمكث وفي هذا القسم تعمق جماعة فأولوا ما ورد في الآخرة من الميزان والصراط وغيرهما وهو بدعة إذ لم ينقل ذلك بطريق الرواية وإجراؤه على الظاهر غير محال فيجب إجراؤه على الظاهر
13:17.english: The third category is when a thing is such that if it were mentioned explicitly it would be understood and there would be no harm in it, yet one alludes to it by way of metaphor (istiʿārah) and symbol (ramz), so that its impact upon the heart of the listener may be more powerful, and so that there may be a benefit in magnifying the matter's importance in his heart. For example, if someone said, "I saw so-and-so hanging pearls upon the necks of swine," he would be alluding thereby to the dissemination of knowledge and the scattering of wisdom among those unworthy of it. Now, the listener may have his understanding rush to the literal sense of the words; but the verifier (muḥaqqiq), when he reflects and knows that that man had no pearls with him, nor was there any swine in that place, becomes alert to the apprehension of the secret and the inner meaning. Thus people differ in this matter. Of this kind is the poet's saying:
13:17.section_title_en: The Third Category of Allusion: Metaphorical Expression for Deeper Impact
13:17.anchors:
- Root: كنو (K-N-W)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To use a metonymy or indirect expression; to refer to something by a name other than its direct designation
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The use of indirect expression to convey a meaning whose direct statement, while comprehensible, would lack the desired psychological impact
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Distinguishes between literal expression (haqīqah) and metaphorical indirection (kināyah) — here the latter is employed for rhetorical amplification
- Root: قلب (Q-L-B)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To turn over, to overturn, to transform from one state to another
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The heart as the seat of understanding and the organ of spiritual perception; the "turning" of meanings upon the heart
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: to flip a thing over. Metaphorical: the heart's reception and internalization of meaning — "وقع في قلبه" (its impact upon his heart)
- Root: مثل (M-TH-L)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Likeness, similitude, example, parable
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The expression of a meaning through an image that contains either the very essence of that meaning or its likeness
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: resemblance. Metaphorical: the parabolic mode where the image conveys the inner reality
- Root: ظهر (Z-H-R)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The back; the outward, apparent aspect of a thing
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The apparent sense (zāhir) versus the inner meaning (bāṭin); the exoteric versus the esoteric
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the visible surface. Metaphorical: "ظهرًا لبطن" — turning a matter over, examining both its outward and inward aspects
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد (Restriction and Specification) — The structure "إنما" in the Quranic citation restricts and focuses the predication, indicating that the creative command is exclusively and entirely Allah's, with no intermediary or temporal process.
13:17.topic: Al-Ghazali on the journey of the soul, death, and the Hereafter, from 'Foundations of Belief'

13:31.arabic: الله عز وجل أن لو يشاء الله لهدى الناس جميعا وقوله تعالى ولو شئنا لآتينا كل نفس هداها ويدل عليه من جهة العقل أن المعاصي والجرائم إن كان الله يكرهها ولا يريدها وإنما هي جارية على وفق إرادة العدو إبليس لعنه الله مع أنه عدو لله سبحانه والجاري على وفق إرادة العدو أكثر من الجاري على وفق إرادته تعالى فليت شعري كيف يستجيز المسلم أن يرد ملك الجبار ذي الجلال والإكرام إلى رتبة لو ردت إليها رياسة زعيم ضيعة لاستنكف منها إذ لو كان ما يستمر لعدو الزعيم في القرية أكثر مما يستقيم له لاستنكف من زعامته وتب
13:31.english: As for the movement, it is a creation of the Lord — exalted is He — an attribute of the servant, and an acquisition of his. For it was created as empowered (maqdūrah) by a power that is His attribute, and the movement has a relation to another attribute called power; thus, by virtue of that relation, it is termed "acquisition." And how could it be pure compulsion (jabr maḥḍ), when he necessarily perceives the distinction between the empowered movement and the involuntary tremor (al-raʿdah al-ḍarūriyyah)? Or how could it be a creation of the servant, when he does not encompass knowledge of the details of the parts of acquired movements nor their numbers? And when both extremes are refuted, nothing remains except moderation in belief (al-iqtiṣād fī al-iʿtiqād) — namely, that it is empowered by the power of God — exalted is He — by way of origination, and by the power of the servant in another mode of attachment (taʿlīq) expressed as acquisition.
13:31.section_title_en: The Second Foundation: God's Sole Creation of Servants' Movements Does Not Negate Their Being Acquired by Servants
13:31.anchors:
- Root: قدر (q-d-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of measuring, determining, and empowering; al-Farahidi notes its application to capacity and divine decree.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "القدرة" when attributed to humans denotes a state enabling one to perform an act; when attributed to God, it negates incapacity. Absolute power belongs solely to God; for others, it is always restricted and particularized.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "هو قادر مقتدر ذو قدرة ومقدرة" — one possessing power. Metaphorical: "فرس بعيد القدر" — a horse of far-reaching stride, extending the root to scope and reach.
- Root: كسب (k-s-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Acquisition, earning, and what one gains; al-Farahidi links it to amassing and profiting.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Acquisition (al-kasb) in theological terms denotes an act's relation to the servant whereby responsibility attaches, while its origination remains divine.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: earning and gaining. Metaphorical: the theological sense of acquired act (al-faʿl al-iktisābī) — a relational attribution distinct from creation.
- Root: خلق (kh-l-q)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Measuring and smoothing; al-Farahidi notes its application to fashioning and proportioning.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الخلق أصله: التقدير المستقيم" — origination from nothing (ibdāʿ) or from something, always upon a measured determination.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: measuring before cutting. Metaphorical: "خلق الله الخلق: أوجده على تقدير أوجبته الحكمة" — God's creation is bringing into existence upon a measure required by wisdom.
- Root: وجب (w-j-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Being due, necessary, or obligatory; al-Farahidi notes its legal and ontological senses.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الوجوب: الثبوت" — necessary being is that whose non-existence entails an impossibility; obligation is that whose omission warrants blame.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "وجب البيع" — the sale became binding. Metaphorical: "هو يأكل الوجبة" — eating once daily, extending to fixed determination.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد (Restriction and Specification) — The particle "إنما" restricts predication, as in "إنما هو إله واحد," confining the attribute to its subject and negating it from others. This governs the Ashʿarī restriction of creative power to God alone while affirming acquired power for servants through a distinct relational mode.
13:31.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'Foundations of Belief'

13:31.arabic: ولميله إليه وغير محبب إليه فهل يكون في زمرة المرائين فاعلم أن الله لم يكلف العباد إلا ما تطيق وليس في طاقة العبد منع الشيطان عن نزغاته ولا قمع الطبع حتى لا يميل إلى الشهوات ولا ينزع إليها وإنما غايته أن يقابل شهوته بكراهة استثمارها من معرفة العواقب وعلم الدين وأصول الإيمان بالله واليوم الآخر فإذا فعل ذلك فهو الغاية في أداء ما كلف به ويدل على ذلك من الأخبار ما روي أن أصحاب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم شكوا إليه وقالوا تعرض لقلوبنا أشياء لأن تخر من السماء فتخطفنا الطير أو تهوي بنا الريح في مكان سحيق أحب إلينا من أن نتكلم ب
13:31.english: If you say: "Whoever finds in himself a dislike of ostentation (riyā'), and this dislike compels him to refuse it, yet he is not entirely free from the soul's inclination toward it, its love for it, and its striving after it — except that he dislikes his own love and his own inclination, and it is not beloved to him — is he then among the ranks of the ostentatious?" — Know that God has not burdened His servants except with what they can bear. It is not within the servant's power to prevent the Devil from his incitements (nazaghāt), nor to suppress nature entirely so that it neither inclines to lusts nor strives after them. His utmost limit is only that he confront his lust with a dislike born of his knowledge of consequences, his understanding of religion, and his roots of faith in God and the Last Day. When he does this, he has reached the utmost limit of performing what he has been charged with.
13:31.section_title_en: On the Degrees of Resistance to Ostentation and the Devil's Wiles — Section 829
13:31.anchors:
- Root: شيط (Shayṭ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of burning, scorching, or spoiling by fire; the Devil as that which burns and destroys.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): الشيطان as the one who leads astray and incites; his "نزغات" (incitements) are his piercing stings of temptation.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "شاط اللحم" (meat scorched/ruined). Metaphorical: "أشاط دمه" (shed his blood vainly) — the Devil's aim is to ruin the soul's deeds.
- Root: كره (K-R-H)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Dislike, aversion, abhorrence; the opposite of love (ḥubb) and desire (mīl).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The moral faculty of repulsion against sin; a trait of faith (īmān) distinguishing the believer's higher self from the lower nature.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "كرهت الشيء" (I disliked it). Metaphorical: The heart's rejection of the soul's base inclinations as an act of worship.
- Root: نفس (Nafs)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The self, soul, or spirit; the seat of desires and passions.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): النفس as the lower commanding soul (النفس الأمارة) that inclines to lusts, distinct from the intellect (عقل) and faith.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "نفس سائلة" (flowing blood/life). Metaphorical: The inner self that must be opposed when it inclines to ostentation.
- Root: جهد (J-H-D) / مجادلة (Jadal)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Striving, exertion, argumentation; from جدل (twisting ropes tightly).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): المجادلة as disputation that can distract from divine remembrance (ذكر الله).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "جادله" (he argued with him). Metaphorical: The soul's engagement with the Devil's whispers as a subtle trap, diverting from sincere worship.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — Used to delimit the four ranks of resistance, each defined by what it exclusively does or omits.
13:31.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Condemnation of Status and Ostentation'

13:33.arabic: يراك (2) وقد قال تعالى أفمن هو قائم على كل نفس بما كسبت وقال تعالى ألم يعلم بأن الله يرى وقال الله تعالى إن الله كان عليكم رقيبا وقال تعالى والذين هم لأماناتهم وعهدهم راعون والذين هم بشهاداتهم قائمون وقال ابن المبارك لرجل راقب الله تعالى فسأله عن تفسيره فقال كن أبدا كأنك ترى الله عز وجل وقال عبد الواحد بن زيد إذا كان سيدي رقيبا على فلا أبالى بغيره وقال أبو عثمان المغربي أفضل ما يلزم الإنسان نفسه في هذه الطريقة المحاسبة والمراقبة وسياسة عمله بالعلم وقال ابن عطاء أفضل الطاعات مراقبة الحق ع
13:33.english: As for its excellence: Gabriel, peace be upon him, asked about iḥsān (perfection of worship), and he, peace be upon him, replied: "That you worship Allah as though you see Him." {«أن تعبد الله كأنك تراه»} And he, peace be upon him, also said: "Worship Allah as though you see Him; for if you do not see Him, verily He sees you." {«اعبد الله كأنك تراه فإن لم تكن تراه فإنه يراك»} And Allah, Exalted is He, has said: {«أفمن هو قائم على كل نفس بما كسبت»} — "Is He who stands over every soul with what it has earned [like any other]?" And He said: {«ألم يعلم بأن الله يرى»} — "Does he not know that Allah sees?" And Allah, Exalted is He, said: {«إن الله كان عليكم رقيبا»} — "Verily, Allah is ever a Watcher (raqīb) over you." And He said: {«والذين هم لأماناتهم وعهدهم راعون والذين هم بشهاداتهم قائمون»} — "And those who are keepers of their trusts and their covenant, and those who stand firm in their testimonies."
13:33.section_title_en: The Second Station of Vigilance: Murāqabah (Spiritual Watchfulness)
13:33.anchors:
- Root: رقب (R-Q-B)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To watch, guard, observe attentively; the neck (as that which turns to observe); a lookout post.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Murāqabah entails the heart's persistent awareness of divine proximity; it is the theological state wherein the servant knows Allah is witness over his secret and public acts.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Haqiqah (literal): physical watching/awaiting. Majaz (metaphorical): "This matter is upon your necks" (في رقابكم) — i.e., an inescapable obligation; likewise, murāqabah of Allah is the soul's standing under the watchful eye of the King, a transferred sense denoting reverent vigilance.
- Sibawayh Rule: Restriction & Focused Predication (باب الحصر والتقييد) — governing the conditional structures "إذا... فلا يبقى إلا..." and "إنها إن تركت طغت وفسدت," where the apodosis is restricted to a single remaining duty.
13:33.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Monitoring and Accounting'

13:33.arabic: قديما فنزه عن الالتفات إليه قلبك فلله سبحانه سر في إبعاد بعض العباد ومن يضلل الله فما له من هاد ومن استبعد أن يسمع موسى عليه السلام في الدنيا كلاما ليس بصوت ولا حرف فليستنكر أن يرى في الآخرة موجودا ليس بجسم ولا لون وإن عقل أن يرى ما ليس بلون ولا جسم ولا قدر ولا كمية وهو إلى الآن لم ير غيره فليعقل في حاسة السمع ما عقله في حاسة البصر وإن عقل على أن يكون له علم واحد هو علم بجميع الموجودات فليعقل صفة واحدة للذات هو كلام بجميع ما دل عليه من العبارات وإن عقل كون السموات السبع وكون الجنة والنار مكتوبة في ورقة صغيرة ومحفوظة في مقدار ذرة من القلب
13:33.english:
[Root: عقل]
  • Al-Raghib (Al-Mufradat): "العقل يقال للقوة المتهيئة لقبول العلم، ويقال للعلم الذي يستفيده الإنسان بتلك القوة عقل" — The intellect is the faculty prepared for receiving knowledge, and the knowledge acquired through that faculty is also called intellect. This dual sense is crucial for understanding Ghazali's argument that true intellection ('aql) grasps realities beyond sensory perception.
  • Al-Zamakhshari (Asas - Haqiqah/Literal): "عقل فلان بعد الصبا أي عرف الخطأ الذي كان عليه" — To exercise intellect means to recognize error. Ghazali employs this to demand intellectual consistency from his opponents.
  • Al-Zamakhshari (Asas - Majaz/Metaphorical): "نخلة لا تعقل الإبار إذا لم تقبله" — A palm tree that does not accept pollination is said metaphorically to "not comprehend." This illustrates that 'aql involves receptivity to what is appropriate.
13:33.topic: Al-Ghazali on the journey of the soul, death, and the Hereafter, from 'Foundations of Belief'

13:33.arabic: الثابت تحقيقا وهو القيوم الذي هو قائم بنفسه وقائم على كل نفس بما كسبت وكل قائم فقائم به ولم يقتصروا على هذا حتى أثبتوا أنفسهم ولو عرفوا لعلموا أنهم من حيث هم هم لا ثبات لهم ولا وجود لهم وإنما وجودهم من حيث أوجدوا لا من حيث وجدوا وفرق بين الموجود وبين الموجد وليس في الوجود إلا موجود واحد وموجد فالموجود حق والموجد باطل من حيث هو هو والموجود قائم وقيوم والموجد هالك وفان وإذا كان كل من عليها فان فلا يبقى إلا وجه ربك ذو الجلال والإكرام الفريق الثاني ليس بهم عمى ولكن بهم عور لأنهم يبصرون بإحدى العينين وجود الموجود الح
13:33.english: From this station did Ḥabīb ibn Abī Ḥabīb look when he recited {«إِنَّا وَجَدْنَاهُ صَابِرًا نِعْمَ الْعَبْدُ إِنَّهُ أَوَّابٌ»} [We found him patient — an excellent servant, indeed he was oft-returning] and then exclaimed: "How astonishing! He gave and He praised!" — signaling that when He praises His own giving, He praises Himself; so He is the Praiser and He is the Praised. And from this station did the Shaykh Abū Saʿīd al-Muhayyanī look when {«يُحِبُّهُمْ وَيُحِبُّونَهُ»} [He loves them and they love Him] was recited before him, and he said: "By my life, He loves them — leave Him to love them! By His right, He loves them — for He only loves Himself." He signaled thereby that He is the Loving and He is the Beloved.
13:33.section_title_en: The Two Visions: The Eye of Pure Unity and the Eye of Those Veiled from Self-Annihilation
13:33.anchors:
- Root: نظر (naẓar)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of "sight, gazing, contemplation" — both physical vision and intellectual perception.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: naẓar as "deliberative reflection" (ta'ammul) leading to knowledge of the divine — the inward eye of the heart.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) = ocular sight; Metaphorical (majāz) = intellectual insight and spiritual vision.
- Root: فنو (fanā')
  * Lisan / Ayn: Root meaning of "passing away, perishing, ceasing to be."
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: fanā' as the annihilation of the self's independent consideration — not physical extinction but the obliteration of the illusion of otherness beside God.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal = perishing of a thing; Metaphorical = the mystic's passing away from self-awareness into pure divine contemplation.
- Root: قوم (qawm)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of "standing, rising, being established."
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): al-Qayyūm (القيوم) — the Self-Subsisting One by whom all else stands; theologically distinct from al-Qā'im (the standing one).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal = physical standing; Metaphorical = self-subsistence and sustaining others.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Restriction and Focused Predication (باب الحصر والتقييد) — governing the exclusive predication in "He is the Thankful and the Thanked" (هو الشاكر وهو المشكور), where the definite predicate restricts the attribution solely to God.
13:33.topic: Al-Ghazali on constant remembrance of God and contemplative invocations, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

14:10.arabic: ولذلك قال الله تعالى أفي الله شك فاطر السموات والأرض ولهذا بعث الأنبياء صلوات الله عليهم لدعوة الخلق إلى التوحيد ليقولوا لا إله إلا الله وما أمروا أن يقولوا لنا إله وللعالم إله فإن ذلك كان مجبولا في فطرة عقولهم من مبدأ نشؤهم وفي عنفوان شبابهم ولذلك قال عز وجل ولئن سألتهم من خلق السموات والأرض ليقولن الله وقال تعالى فأقم وجهك للدين حنيفا فطرة الله التي
14:10.english: The First Principle: the knowledge of His existence, the Exalted. The first thing by which one is illuminated from among the lights, and the path of reflection (ṭarīq al-iʿtibār) by which one proceeds, is that to which the Qurʾān has guided. For after the explanation of God, glorified be He, there is no explanation. He, the Exalted, has said: {«أَلَمْ نَجْعَلِ الْأَرْضَ مِهَادًا وَالْجِبَالَ أَوْتَادًا وَخَلَقْنَاكُمْ أَزْوَاجًا وَجَعَلْنَا نَوْمَكُمْ سُبَاتًا وَجَعَلْنَا اللَّيْلَ لِبَاسًا وَجَعَلْنَا النَّهَارَ مَعَاشًا وَبَنَيْنَا فَوْقَكُمْ سَبْعًا شِدَادًا وَجَعَلْنَا سِرَاجًا وَهَّاجًا وَأَنزَلْنَا مِنَ الْمُعْصِرَاتِ مَاءً ثَجَّاجًا لِّنُخْرِجَ بِهِ حَبًّا وَنَبَاتًا وَجَنَّاتٍ أَلْفَافًا»} — "Have We not made the earth a resting place, and the mountains as pegs, and created you in pairs, and made your sleep a repose, and made the night a covering, and made the day for livelihood, and built above you seven strong heavens, and made a blazing lamp, and sent down from the rain-clouds pouring water, that We may bring forth thereby grain and vegetation, and gardens dense with foliage?" (Q 78:6–16).
