And He, the Exalted, has said: {«إِنَّ فِي خَلْقِ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَاخْتِلَافِ اللَّيْلِ وَالنَّهَارِ وَالْفُلْكِ الَّتِي تَجْرِي فِي الْبَحْرِ بِمَا يَنفَعُ النَّاسَ وَمَا أَنزَلَ اللَّهُ مِنَ السَّمَاءِ مِن مَّاءٍ فَأَحْيَا بِهِ الْأَرْضَ بَعْدَ مَوْتِهَا وَبَثَّ فِيهَا مِن كُلِّ دَابَّةٍ وَتَصْرِيفِ الرِّيَاحِ وَالسَّحَابِ الْمُسَخَّرِ بَيْنَ السَّمَاءِ وَالْأَرْضِ لَآيَاتٍ لِّقَوْمٍ يَعْقِلُونَ»} — "Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth, and the alternation of the night and the day, and the ships which sail through the sea with that which benefits people, and what God has sent down from the sky of water, thereby reviving the earth after its death, and dispersing therein every creature, and the directing of the winds, and the clouds subservient between the heaven and the earth — are signs for a people who reason" (Q 2:164). And He, the Exalted, has said: {«أَلَمْ تَرَوْا كَيْفَ خَلَقَ اللَّهُ سَبْعَ سَمَاوَاتٍ طِبَاقًا وَجَعَلَ الْقَمَرَ فِيهِنَّ نُورًا وَجَعَلَ الشَّمْسَ سِرَاجًا وَاللَّهُ أَنبَتَكُم مِّنَ الْأَرْضِ نَبَاتًا ثُمَّ يُعِيدُكُمْ فِيهَا وَيُخْرِجُكُمْ إِخْرَاجًا»} — "Have you not seen how God created seven heavens in layers, and made the moon therein a light, and made the sun a lamp? And God caused you to grow from the earth a growth; then He returns you into it, and brings you forth a bringing forth" (Q 71:15–18). And He, the Exalted, has said: {«أَفَرَأَيْتُم مَّا تُمْنُونَ أَأَنتُمْ تَخْلُقُونَهُ أَمْ نَحْنُ الْخَالِقُونَ»} — "Have you considered what you emit? Do you create it, or are We the Creator?" — up to His saying: {«لِلْمُقْوِينَ»} — "for the settlers" (Q 56:58–73).
14:10.section_title_en: The Pillars of Faith: Knowledge of God, His Attributes, His Acts, and the Audibles — Section 87
14:10.anchors:
- Root: وجود (w-j-d)
  * Lisan / Ayn: [Core linguistic root meaning: to find, to perceive, to be; existence as that which is found or discovered]
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): [Theological/Kalam semantic nuance: al-wujūd as necessary existence (wujūb) versus contingent existence (imkān); the self-evident reality of the Creator's being]
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): [Literal vs Metaphorical distinction: haqīqah — existence as affirmed reality; majāz — "finding" as in discovery, not applicable to God's necessary being]
- Root: خلق (kh-l-q)
  * Lisan / Ayn: [Core linguistic root meaning: measuring, proportioning, fashioning; origination of a thing upon a measure]
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الخلق أصله: التقدير المستقيم، ويستعمل في إبداع الشيء من غير أصل ولا احتذاء" — creation as origination from nothing without prior model
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): [Literal: خلق الله الخلق: أوجده على تقدير أوجبته الحكمة — brought into existence upon a measure necessitated by wisdom; Majaz: not applicable to God's act as pure origination]
- Root: فطر (f-t-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: [Core linguistic root meaning: to split, cleave, rend; to originate, to bring forth as a new creation]
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "فطر الله الخلق" — God's origination of creation as a primordial act; "الفطرة" as the innate disposition
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): [Literal: فطر الله الخلق، وهو فاطر السموات: مبتدعها — originator without precedent; Majaz: "رأيه فطير" — immature opinion, not applicable to divine]
- Root: ارض (ar-d)
  * Lisan / Ayn: [Core linguistic root meaning: the earth, the lower sphere; that which is beneath]
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الأرض: الجرم المقابل للسماء" — the body opposite the heaven
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): [Literal: the earth as a resting place (مهادا); Majaz: not applicable in this context of divine creation]
- Root: ركن (r-k-n)
  * Lisan / Ayn: [Core linguistic root meaning: corner, pillar, support; that to which one leans for strength]
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "ركن الشيء: جانبه الذي يسكن إليه" — the side of a thing to which one repairs; used metaphorically for strength
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): [Literal: physical pillar/corner; Majaz: "فلان يأوي من عز قومه إلى ركن شديد" — one who repairs to a mighty support; here, the "pillars" (أركان) of faith as structural supports]
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The syntactic structure "مداره على عشرة أصول" (its circuit revolves upon ten principles) employs a prepositional phrase governing the verbal noun, establishing the necessary grammatical dependency that mirrors the ontological dependency of the created upon the Creator.
14:10.topic: Al-Ghazali on the journey of the soul, death, and the Hereafter, from 'Foundations of Belief'

14:10.arabic: قولهم أنؤمن لبشرين مثلنا {وقولهم} إن أنتم إلا بشر مثلنا ولئن أطعتم بشرا مثلكم إنكم إذا لخاسرون وقال الذين لا يرجون لقاءنا لولا أنزل علينا الملائكة أو نرى ربنا لقد استكبروا في أنفسهم وعتوا عتوا كبيرا وقالوا لولا أنزل عليه ملك وقال فرعون فيما أخبر الله عنه {أو جاء معه الملائكة مقترنين} وقال الله تعالى {واستكبر هو وجنوده في الأرض بغير الحق} فتكبر هو على الله وعلى رسله جميعا قال وهب قال له موسى عليه السلام آمن ولك ملكك قال حتى أشاور هامان فشاور هامان فقال هامان بينما أنت رب يعبد إذ صرت عبد تعب
14:10.english: Know that the one against whom pride is directed is either God—mighty and majestic—or His messengers, or the rest of His creation. Man has been created unjust and ignorant {«وخلق الإنسان ظلوما جهولا»}, so at times he grows proud against the creation, and at times he grows proud against the Creator. Thus, pride, considered with respect to the one against whom it is directed, falls into three divisions.
14:10.section_title_en: Exposition of the One Against Whom Pride Is Directed, Its Degrees, Its Divisions, and the Fruits of Pride Within It
14:10.anchors:
- Root: كبر (k-b-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root denotes magnitude, whether physical size, age, or rank; "الكبرة" specifically marks the state of advanced age or an ingrained, chronic condition.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الكبير والصغير من الأسماء المتضايفة" — bigness and smallness are relative terms. In the theological context, pride (الكبر) is the soul's self-magnification against another, a relational vice that distorts the creature's standing before the Creator.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah) usage concerns physical or quantitative magnitude. Metaphorical (Majaz) usage transfers this to moral and spiritual stature, as in "كبر علي ذلك" (it weighed heavily upon him) — here, the soul's swelling against divine command is a metaphorical arrogation of greatness.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Prepositional Interposition (باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور) — Governing the syntactic tension between the agent of pride (المتكبر) and its object (المتكبر عليه), where the preposition "على" carries the full weight of opposition and elevation, structuring the periodic sentences that follow.
14:10.topic: Al-Ghazali on purifying the character, moral diseases, and spiritual remedies, from 'Condemnation of Pride and Conceit'

14:24.arabic: كالسقي والتربية له حتى ينمو ذلك البذر يقوى ويرتفع شجرة طيبة راسخة أصلها ثابت وفرعها في السماء وينبغي أن يحرس سمعه من الجدل والكلام غاية الحراسة فإن ما يشوشه الجدل أكثر مما يمهده وما يفسده أكثر مما يصلحه بل تقويته بالجدل تضاهي ضرب الشجرة بالمدقة من الحديد رجاء تقويتها بأن تكثر أجزاؤها وربما يفتتها ذلك ويفسدها وهو الأغلب والمشاهدة تكفيك في هذا بيانا فناهيك بالعيان برهانا فقس عقيدة أهل الصلاح والتقى من عوام الناس بعقيدة المتكلمين والمجادلين فترى اعتقاد العامي في الثبات كالطود الشامخ لا تحركه الدواهي والصواعق وعقيدة المتكلم الحارس اعتق
14:24.english: The way to strengthen and establish it is not by teaching the craft of disputation (jadal) and scholastic theology (kalām). Rather, one should occupy oneself with the recitation of the Qur'an and its interpretation, and with the reading of the hadith and its meanings. And one should occupy oneself with the duties of worship. Thus one's belief will not cease to increase in firmness by what strikes the ear of the proofs of the Qur'an and its arguments, by what comes upon one of the evidences of the hadiths and their benefits, by what shines upon one of the lights of worship and its functions, and by what permeates into one from the observation of the righteous and their companionship, their appearance, their speech, and their bearing in humility before God — mighty and majestic — in fear of Him and in submissiveness to Him. So the initial inculcation is like the casting of a seed into the breast, and these means are like the watering and nurturing of it, until that seed grows, strengthens, and rises as a goodly tree, firmly rooted, its branches reaching into the sky. {أَلَمْ تَرَ كَيْفَ ضَرَبَ اللَّهُ مَثَلًا كَلِمَةً طَيِّبَةً كَشَجَرَةٍ طَيِّبَةٍ أَصْلُهَا ثَابِتٌ وَفَرْعُهَا فِي السَّمَاءِ} (Q. 14:24).
14:24.section_title_en: Chapter Two: On the Method of Gradual Progression toward Guidance and the Ordering of the Degrees of Belief
14:24.anchors:
- Root: درج (daraja)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Gradual ascent by steps; to walk gently along a path; to pass away one generation after another.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Degree (darajah) denotes a station considered by ascent, not horizontal extension; used for rank and elevation.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: walking stepwise, folding a letter. Metaphorical: "walk in the paths (madārij) of truth," "degrees of rank."
- Root: عقد ('aqada)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To tie, bind, knot; to make firm a compact.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Literal tying of physical things, then metaphorically transferred to meanings: the contract of sale, covenant, and belief ('aqīdah) as that which is firmly bound in the heart.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: knotting a rope, constructing vaulted arches. Metaphorical: a firmly held conviction that is bound and secured.
- Root: جدل (jadala)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To twist or braid a rope tightly; to wrestle someone to the ground.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Disputation (jadal) is dialogue on a footing of contention and rivalry; its origin is twisting a rope firmly, as if each disputant twists the other away from his opinion.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: twisting a rope, throwing a man to hard ground. Metaphorical: a well-knit chainmail, firm resolve; "the affair of the people became ordered (istajāda) like a flowing stream."
- Root: صدق (ṣadaqa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To speak truthfully; firmness in speech and action.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Truth and falsehood are originally in speech, whether past or future; truth is only primarily in reports, and may be secondarily in other kinds of speech.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: verifying a report. Metaphorical: "a man truthful in attack," "a horse with truthfulness in racing" — i.e., firm, reliable, unwavering.
- Sibawayh Rule: The Interposition of Prepositional Phrases (باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور) — The periodic sentence may be extended by embedding causal clauses and prepositional phrases, provided the governing construction remains intact and the meaning is not suspended; this governs the long chains of causal explanation (fa-inna... bi-sabab...) in this passage.
14:24.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'Foundations of Belief'

14:24.arabic: {طيبة كشجرة طيبة أصلها ثابت وفرعها في السماء} وإليها الإشارة بقوله تعالى {إليه يصعد الكلم الطيب} أي المعرفة {والعمل الصالح يرفعه} فالعمل الصالح كالجمال لهذه المعرفة وكالخادم وإنما العمل الصالح كله في تطهير القلب أولا من الدنيا ثم إدامة طهارته فلا يراد العمل إلا لهذه المعرفة وأما العلم بكيفية العمل فيراد للعمل فالعلم هو الأول وهو الآخر وإنما الأول علم المعاملة وغرضه العمل وغرض المعاملة صفاء القلب وطهارته ليتضح فيه جلية الحق ويتزين بعلم المعرفة وهو علم المكاشفة ومهما حصلت هذه المعرفة تبعتها
14:24.english: Those who arrive at this rank divide into two groups: the strong, whose first knowledge is of God, exalted be He, and then through Him they come to know other than Him; and the weak, whose first knowledge is of [His] acts, and then they ascend from them to the Agent. To the first points His saying, exalted be He: {أو لم يكف بربك أنه على كل شيء شهيد} [Is it not sufficient concerning your Lord that He is over all things a Witness], and His saying, exalted be He: {«شهد الله أنه لا إله إلا هو»} [God bears witness that there is no god but He]. And of this kind is the saying of one of them, when it was said to him: "By what have you known your Lord?" He said: "I have known my Lord — and were it not for my Lord, I would not have known my Lord."
14:24.section_title_en: The Two Paths to Knowledge and Love: The Higher Way of Witnessing the Truth and the Easier Way of Contemplating Creation
14:24.anchors:
- Root: طيب (ṭ-y-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Pure, good, wholesome; free from defilement
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): That which is pure and agreeable in both sensory and intellectual registers; the "good word" (al-kalim al-ṭayyib) is the declaration of divine unity
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal for sensory purity; metaphorical for spiritual purity of heart and speech
- Root: عرف (ʿ-r-f)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To know by reflection and discernment of traces/effects
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Maʿrifah is knowledge of God attained through contemplation of His effects, not through direct apprehension of His essence; it is more specific than ʿilm
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: to recognize someone; metaphorical: knowledge of God through His signs
- Root: شهد (sh-h-d)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To witness, testify, be present
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Bearing witness to the truth of something based on direct presence or evidence
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: ocular presence; metaphorical: intellectual certitude
- Root: نظر (n-ẓ-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To look, gaze, contemplate
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Contemplative reflection (naẓar) directed toward creation to derive knowledge of the Creator
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: visual perception; metaphorical: intellectual consideration and inference
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — used to restrict the purpose of works to purification of the heart, and to restrict the ultimate end to knowledge of unveiling
14:24.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Love, Longing, Intimacy and Contentment'

14:24.arabic: الكلمة الطيبة التي ضرب الله بها مثلا حيث قال {ضرب الله مثلا كلمة}
14:24.english: The first: severing the attachments of this world and expelling love of other-than-God from the heart. For the heart is like a vessel: it cannot accommodate vinegar, for example, unless the water is first poured out of it. {God has not made for any man two hearts in his breast} [Al-Ahzab/4]. The perfection of love consists in loving God — mighty and majestic — with one's entire heart. As long as he turns toward other than Him, a corner of his heart is occupied with other than Him. To the extent that he is occupied with other than God, love of God diminishes from it; and to the extent that water remains in the vessel, the vinegar poured into it is diminished.
14:24.section_title_en: The Two Pillars of Love for God: Purification of the Heart and Strength of Knowledge
14:24.anchors:
- Root: ح ب ب (ḥ-b-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root denotes steadfastness and permanence; the heart's fixed attachment to its object.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Love (maḥabbah) is the soul's inclination toward what pleases it; its perfection is exclusive devotion, as in the verse {يحبهم ويحبونه} [Al-Ma'idah/54].
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) usage denotes the heart's clinging; metaphorical (majāz) usage extends to acts of obedience and yearning, culminating in 'ishq (intense passionate love) when it overwhelms the lover.
- Root: خ ل ص (kh-l-ṣ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Purity from admixture; the essence of a thing freed from foreign elements.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Ikhlāṣ is the purification of intention so that no share of creation remains in it; it is the condition for the validity of the shahādah.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: clear, unmixed honey or water; metaphorical: the heart emptied of all rivals so that God alone occupies it.
- Root: ز ه د (z-h-d)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Abstention from what is not essential; renunciation of the superfluous.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Asceticism (zuhd) is the heart's detachment from worldly goods, not merely the abandonment of possessions; it is a preparatory station (maqām) for love.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: disinterest in a thing; metaphorical: the soul's indifference to the ephemeral in favor of the eternal.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Restriction and Specification (Bāb al-Ḥaṣr wa al-Taqyīd bi-innamā) — The particle innamā restricts the predicate to the subject alone, as in "إنما يكتسب العبد حب الله" — affirming love's acquisition solely through specified means, negating all others.
14:24.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Love, Longing, Intimacy and Contentment'

16:40.arabic: ومن هذا القبيل في كنايته عن الاقتدار قوله تعالى إنما قولنا لشيء إذا أردناه أن نقول له كن فيكون فإن ظاهره ممتنع إذ قوله كن إن كان خطابا للشيء قبل وجوده فهو محال إذا المعدوم لا يفهم الخطاب حتى يمثل وإن كان بعد الوجود فهو مستغن عن التكوين ولكن لما كانت هذه الكناية أوقع في النفوس في تفهيم غاية الاقتدار عدل إليها وأما المدرك بالشرع فهو أن يكون إجراؤه على الظاهر ممكنا ولكنه يروى أنه أريد به غير الظاهر كما ورد في تفسير قوله تعالى أنزل من السماء ماء فسالت أودية بقدرها الآية وأن معنى الماء ههنا هو القرآن ومعنى الأودية هي القلوب وأن بعضها احتم
16:40.english: The third category is when a thing is such that if it were mentioned explicitly it would be understood and there would be no harm in it, yet one alludes to it by way of metaphor (istiʿārah) and symbol (ramz), so that its impact upon the heart of the listener may be more powerful, and so that there may be a benefit in magnifying the matter's importance in his heart. For example, if someone said, "I saw so-and-so hanging pearls upon the necks of swine," he would be alluding thereby to the dissemination of knowledge and the scattering of wisdom among those unworthy of it. Now, the listener may have his understanding rush to the literal sense of the words; but the verifier (muḥaqqiq), when he reflects and knows that that man had no pearls with him, nor was there any swine in that place, becomes alert to the apprehension of the secret and the inner meaning. Thus people differ in this matter. Of this kind is the poet's saying:
16:40.section_title_en: The Third Category of Allusion: Metaphorical Expression for Deeper Impact
16:40.anchors:
- Root: كنو (K-N-W)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To use a metonymy or indirect expression; to refer to something by a name other than its direct designation
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The use of indirect expression to convey a meaning whose direct statement, while comprehensible, would lack the desired psychological impact
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Distinguishes between literal expression (haqīqah) and metaphorical indirection (kināyah) — here the latter is employed for rhetorical amplification
- Root: قلب (Q-L-B)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To turn over, to overturn, to transform from one state to another
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The heart as the seat of understanding and the organ of spiritual perception; the "turning" of meanings upon the heart
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: to flip a thing over. Metaphorical: the heart's reception and internalization of meaning — "وقع في قلبه" (its impact upon his heart)
- Root: مثل (M-TH-L)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Likeness, similitude, example, parable
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The expression of a meaning through an image that contains either the very essence of that meaning or its likeness
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: resemblance. Metaphorical: the parabolic mode where the image conveys the inner reality
- Root: ظهر (Z-H-R)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The back; the outward, apparent aspect of a thing
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The apparent sense (zāhir) versus the inner meaning (bāṭin); the exoteric versus the esoteric
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the visible surface. Metaphorical: "ظهرًا لبطن" — turning a matter over, examining both its outward and inward aspects
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد (Restriction and Specification) — The structure "إنما" in the Quranic citation restricts and focuses the predication, indicating that the creative command is exclusively and entirely Allah's, with no intermediary or temporal process.
16:40.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Foundations of Belief'

16:75.arabic: ظاهرا من الحياة الدنيا وهم عن الآخرة هم غافلون الحمد لله بل أكثرهم لا يعلمون فالحب بهذا السبب أقوى من الحب بالإحسان لأن الإحسان يزيد وينقص ولذلك أوحى الله تعالى إلى داود عليه السلام إن أود الأوداء إلى من عبدني بغير نوال لكن ليعطي الربوبية حقها وفي الزبور من أظلم ممن عبدنى لجنة أونار لو لم أخلق جنة ولا نارا ألم أكن أهلا أن أطاع ومر عيسى عليه السلام على طائفة من العباد قد نحلوا فقالوا نخاف النار ونرجو الجنة فقال لهم مخلوقا خفتم ومخلوقا رجوتم ومر بقوم آخرين كذلك فقالوا نعبده حبا له وتعظيما لجلاله فقال أنتم أولياء الله حقا معكم أ
16:75.english: ...power except through the enabling of his Master, just as He said concerning the greatest of the kings of the earth, Dhul-Qarnayn, when He said: {«إنا مكنا له في الأرض»} — "Indeed, We established him firmly upon the earth" (Q. 18:84). For all his kingship and sovereignty was nothing but the enabling of God Most High granted to him over a portion of the earth — and the entire earth is but a speck of dust in relation to the bodies of the world. And all the dominions that people attain from the earth are but a mote from that speck of dust. Then that mote, too, is from the bounty of God Most High and His enabling. It is therefore impossible that a servant should love one of God's servants for his power, his governance, his enablement, his dominion, and the completeness of his strength, yet not love God Most High for that very reason. And there is no might and no power except through God, the Exalted, the Magnificent. For He is the Compeller (al-Jabbār), the Subduer (al-Qāhir), the All-Knowing (al-'Alīm), the All-Powerful (al-Qādir). The heavens are folded in His right hand, and the earth with its kingdom and all that is upon it is in His grasp. The forelock of all creatures is in the grip of His power. If He destroyed them all, from the first to the last, not a single atom would diminish from His sovereignty and kingdom; and if He created their like a thousand times, He would not be wearied by their creation, nor would fatigue or languor touch Him in inventing them. So there is no power and no powerful one except that it is a trace of the traces of His power. To Him belongs beauty (al-jamāl), splendor (al-bahā'), majesty (al-'azamah), grandeur (al-kibriyā'), subjugation (al-qahr), and dominion (al-istīlā'). If, then, it is conceivable that a powerful one be loved for the completeness of his power, then none whatsoever deserves love for completeness of power save Him alone.
16:75.section_title_en: The Fifth Cause of Love: Essential Beauty and Inner Affinity (Section 1156)
16:75.anchors:
- Root: قدر (q-d-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of measuring, determining, and enabling power; al-Farahidi notes its application to divine ordainment and human capacity.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Divine power (qudrah) is negation of incapacity ('ajz) in God; for humans, it is a contingent capacity granted by God's enabling (tamkīn), never absolute.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: measured capacity and enablement; Metaphorical: "far-reaching stride" (ba'īd al-qadr) — here, all creaturely power is but a trace of divine power.
- Root: قدس (q-d-s)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Purity and sanctity; being set apart from defilement.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Transcendence (taqdīs) as absolute purity from all deficiency — applicable in full only to God, the Holy (al-Quddūs).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical cleansing; Metaphorical: moral and ontological transcendence from every imperfection.
- Root: مثل (m-th-l)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Likeness, similarity, and representation.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Tamthīl (assimilation) and tashbīh (anthropomorphism) are impossible for God; munāsabah (affinity) is not likeness in form but in inner meaning.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: visual resemblance; Metaphorical: spiritual congruence (munāsabah) between the servant and God through acquired divine attributes.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — Used to confine absolute beauty, perfection, and lovability exclusively to God, e.g., "the Beautiful absolutely is the One who has no equal."
16:75.topic: Al-Ghazali on the journey of the soul, death, and the Hereafter, from 'Love, Longing, Intimacy and Contentment'

16:75.arabic: في استحقاق الجنة به وإن قال أردت به أن يعيش مدة طويلة ولا يصلي ولا يقدم على شيء من الأعمال الشرعية فنقول فما ضبط تلك المدة وما عدد تلك الطاعات التي بتركها يبطل الإيمان وما عدد الكبائر التي بارتكابها يبطل الإيمان وهذا لا يمكن التحكم بتقديره ولم يصر إليه صائر أصلا الدرجة الرابعة أن يوجد التصديق بالقلب قبل أن ينطق باللسان أو يشتغل بالأعمال ومات فهل نقول مات مؤمنا بينه وبين الله تعالى وهذا مما اختلف فيه ومن شرط القول لتمام الإيمان يقول هذا مات قبل الإيمان وهو فاسد إذ قال صلى الله عليه وسلم يخرج من النار من كان في قلبه مثقال ذرة من
16:75.english: He was asked, "Which deed is most excellent?" The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Islam." It was then asked, "Which aspect of Islam is most excellent?" He (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Faith (Īmān)." This is evidence for both the distinction (ikhtilāf) between the two terms and their overlap (tadākhul). This usage is the most consistent with the conventions of the language, because faith is a deed among deeds, and it is the most excellent of them. Islam is submission (taslīm), whether by the heart, by the tongue, or by the limbs. The most excellent of these is that which is by the heart, which is the assent (taṣdīq) that is called faith. Using the two terms in a way that indicates distinction, overlap, or even complete synonymy (tarāduf) is all within the bounds of metaphorical usage (tajawwuz) in the language.
16:75.section_title_en: The Book of the Revival of the Religious Sciences — Section 99: On the Distinction, Overlap, and Synonymy of Faith (Īmān) and Submission (Islām), and Their Worldly and Otherworldly Judgments
16:75.anchors:
- Root: ايم (A-Y-M)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of remaining unmarried, or a state of being without a spouse; extended metaphorically to describe one who is solitary or without support.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الأيامى: جمع أيم، وهي المرأة التي لا بعل لها... والحرب مأيمة، أي: يفرق بين الزوج والزوجة." The root carries the sense of separation or a state of lacking union, which informs the theological discussion of what constitutes the essential bond of faith.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah) usage denotes the state of being unmarried; metaphorical (Majaz) usage extends to anything that separates or leaves one bereft. This distinction between literal and metaphorical application is central to the chapter's method.
- Root: قلب (Q-L-B)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To turn, overturn, or transform a thing from one state to another.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "قلب الشيء: تصريفه وصرفه عن وجه إلى وجه... والانقلاب: الانصراف." The heart (qalb) is so named for its constant fluctuation and turning. In theological terms, it is the seat of taṣdīq (assent), the immaterial faculty of cognition and conviction.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah) usage is physical turning; metaphorical (Majaz) usage is "قلب الأمور" — to deliberate, scrutinize, and manage affairs. This supports the distinction between the heart's internal act of assent and the external acts of the limbs.
- Root: عمل (ʿ-A-M-L)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Any deed or action performed with purpose and intent.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "العمل: كل فعل يكون من الحيوان بقصد، فهو أخص من الفعل." Work is more specific than mere action, as it implies deliberate, intentional agency. It is used for both righteous and sinful deeds, and is the external manifestation of internal conviction.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah) usage refers to physical labor or deeds. The chapter explores whether "work" is an integral part of the reality of faith or a separate, consequent requirement.
- Root: صدق (S-D-Q)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To be truthful, to speak the truth, to verify.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الصدق والكذب أصلهما في القول... ولا يكونان بالقصد الأول إلا في القول." Truth and falsehood are primarily properties of speech and reports. Taṣdīq (assent) is the heart's affirmation of the truth of a report, which is the core reality of Īmān.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah) usage is truthful speech; metaphorical (Majaz) usage is "صادق الحملة" — one who is true and firm in battle or resolve. This shows that taṣdīq is not merely verbal but a firm, internal resolution.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication). This rule governs how restriction (ḥaṣr) is achieved in Arabic, often through particles like "innamā" or through contextual specification (takhṣīṣ). The chapter's core argument hinges on how terms like Īmān and Islām are semantically restricted, expanded, or made synonymous through contextual usage (majāz), requiring precise parsing of the predicate and its scope.
16:75.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Foundations of Belief'

16:75.arabic: كالملوك والأكابر ويضعف مهما كان المادح ممن لا يؤبه له ولا يقدر على شيء فإن القدرة عليه بملك قلبه قدرة على أمر حقير فلا يدل المدح إلا على قدرة قاصرة وبهذه العلة أيضا يكره الذم ويتألم به القلب وإذا كان من الأكابر كانت نكايته أعظم لأن الفائت به أعظم السبب الثالث أن ثناء المثني ومدح المادح سبب لاصطياد قلب كل من يسمعه لا سيما إذا كان ذلك ممن يلتفت إلى قوله ويعتد بثنائه وهذا مختص بثناء يقع على الملأ فلا جرم كلما كان الجمع أكثر والمثني أجدر بأن يلتفت إلى
16:75.english: This contains no dissimulation (talbīs); rather, it is a blocking of the path to knowledge of that in which there is no benefit in knowing — like one who conceals from the Sultan that he drinks wine, yet does not cast to him that he is pious. For his saying "I am pious" would be dissimulation, whereas his failure to confess to drinking does not necessitate the belief in his piety; rather, it merely prevents knowledge of his drinking.
16:75.section_title_en: Section 802 — On the Causes of the Love of Praise and the Soul's Delight in It, and Its Aversion to Blame
16:75.anchors:
- Root: مدح (m-d-ḥ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: مدح: الحسن الجميل في القول، والثناء على الرجل بما فيه من الخير.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): المدح: ذكر محاسن الغير، وهو ضرب من الثناء، ويقابله الذم، وكلاهما من أفعال القول الدالة على اعتقاد المتكلم.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Haqiqah: مدحه: أحسن الثناء عليه. Majaz: مدحه بوجهه: إذا أظهر السرور به، ومدحت الأرض: إذا أخصبت وحسنت.
- Root: ذم (dh-m-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: الذم: نقيض المدح، وهو ذكر المساوي والقبائح.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): الذم: إظهار نقائص الغير، وهو ضد المدح، وقد يكون بحق أو بباطل.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Haqiqah: ذمه: قبح فعله ووصفه بالقبيح. Majaz: ذم الماء: إذا كان غير عذب، وذم المكان: إذا كان وخيما.
- Root: ملك (m-l-k)
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): الملك: هو المتصرف بالأمر والنهي في الجمهور، والملك ضربان: ملك هو التملك والتولي، وملك هو القوة على ذلك.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Haqiqah: ملك الشيء وامتلكه وتملكه. Majaz: ملك قلبه: استولى عليه، وملكت فلانة أمرها: خليت وشأنها.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — Used to isolate the four causes of love of praise as exhaustive and ordered.
16:75.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Condemnation of Status and Ostentation'

16:75.arabic: الله مثلا عبدا مملوكا لا يقدر على شيء أراد به النفقة مما رزق وقوله عز وجل وضرب الله مثلا رجلين أحدهما أبكم لا يقدر على شيء أي الأمر بالعدل والاستقامة وقوله عز وجل فإن اتبعتني فلا تسألني عن شيء أراد به من صفات الربوبية وهو العلوم التي لا يحل السؤال عنها حتى يبتدئ بها العارف في أوان الاستحقاق وقوله عز وجل أم خلقوا من غير شي أم هم الخالقون أي من غير خالق فربما يتوهم به أنه يدل على أنه لا يخلق شيء إلا من شيء وأما القرين فكقوله عز وجل وقال قرينه هذا ما لدي عتيد ألقيا في جهنم كل كفار أر
16:75.english: I say: The Prophet (peace be upon him) was asked about the means of deliverance from these trials, and he said: "The Book of Allah — act by what is in it, for it is that which delivers one from them." The questioner repeated this three times, and he (peace be upon him) said three times: "Learn the Book of Allah, Mighty and Glorious, and act by what is in it, for in it is deliverance."
16:75.section_title_en: The Book of the Etiquette of Recitation — Section 233: On Understanding the Meanings of the Qur'an and the Limits of Interpretation
16:75.anchors:
- Root: ف-ه-م (f-h-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الفهم: هيئة للإنسان بها يتحقق معاني ما يحسن" — comprehension as an inherent faculty by which one ascertains meanings
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الفهم: هيئة للإنسان بها يتحقق معاني ما يحسن... وأفهمته: إذا قلت له حتى تصوره" — comprehension is a cognitive disposition; distinction between understanding (fahm) and making understood (ifhām)
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "تقول: من لم يؤت من سوء الفهم أتى من سوء الإفهام" — literal usage; failure of understanding often stems from failure of communication
- Root: ف-س-ر (f-s-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "وكل شيء يعرف به تفسير الشيء ومعناه، فهو تَفْسِرَتُه" — that by which a thing's meaning is made known
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "التفسير قد يقال فيما يختص بمفردات الألفاظ وغريبها، وفيما يختص بالتأويل" — tafsīr concerns lexical surface; taʾwīl concerns deeper meaning
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "هذا كلام يحتاج إلى فسر وتفسير" — literal: exposition of what is obscure
- Root: و-ج-ل (w-j-l)
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الوجل: استشعار الخوف" — the sensing of fear; used of hearts trembling at divine mention
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "لو واجلت فلانا لوجلته: لغلبته في الوجل" — literal sense of fear; metaphorical extension to overpowering in fear
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — the particle innamā restricts predication, essential for parsing the Prophet's saying "innamā al-aʿmālu bi-l-niyyāt" and analogous restrictive formulations in the ḥadīth cited herein
16:75.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

16:75.arabic: حرف أما الكلمة فكالشيء والقرين والأمة والروح ونظائرها قال الله تعالى ضرب الله مثلا عبدا مملوكا لا يقدر على شيء أراد به النفقة مما رزق وقوله عز وجل وضرب الله مثلا رجلين أحدهما أبكم لا يقدر على شيء أي الأمر بالعدل والاستقامة وقوله عز وجل فإن اتبعتني فلا تسألني عن شيء أراد به من صفات الربوبية وهو العلوم التي لا يحل السؤال عنها حتى يبتدئ بها العارف في أوان الاستحقاق وقوله عز وجل أم خلقوا من غير شي أم هم الخالقون أي من غير خالق فربما يتوهم به أنه يدل على أنه لا يخلق شيء إلا من شيء وأما القرين فكقوله عز وجل وقال قرينه هذا ما لدي عتيد ألقيا في جهنم كل كفار أراد
16:75.english: I say: The Prophet (peace be upon him) was asked about the means of deliverance from these trials, and he said: "The Book of Allah — act by what is in it, for it is that which delivers one from them." The questioner repeated this three times, and he (peace be upon him) said three times: "Learn the Book of Allah, Mighty and Glorious, and act by what is in it, for in it is deliverance."

16:76.arabic: في استحقاق الجنة به وإن قال أردت به أن يعيش مدة طويلة ولا يصلي ولا يقدم على شيء من الأعمال الشرعية فنقول فما ضبط تلك المدة وما عدد تلك الطاعات التي بتركها يبطل الإيمان وما عدد الكبائر التي بارتكابها يبطل الإيمان وهذا لا يمكن التحكم بتقديره ولم يصر إليه صائر أصلا الدرجة الرابعة أن يوجد التصديق بالقلب قبل أن ينطق باللسان أو يشتغل بالأعمال ومات فهل نقول مات مؤمنا بينه وبين الله تعالى وهذا مما اختلف فيه ومن شرط القول لتمام الإيمان يقول هذا مات قبل الإيمان وهو فاسد إذ قال صلى الله عليه وسلم يخرج من النار من كان في قلبه مثقال ذرة من
16:76.english: He was asked, "Which deed is most excellent?" The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Islam." It was then asked, "Which aspect of Islam is most excellent?" He (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Faith (Īmān)." This is evidence for both the distinction (ikhtilāf) between the two terms and their overlap (tadākhul). This usage is the most consistent with the conventions of the language, because faith is a deed among deeds, and it is the most excellent of them. Islam is submission (taslīm), whether by the heart, by the tongue, or by the limbs. The most excellent of these is that which is by the heart, which is the assent (taṣdīq) that is called faith. Using the two terms in a way that indicates distinction, overlap, or even complete synonymy (tarāduf) is all within the bounds of metaphorical usage (tajawwuz) in the language.
16:76.section_title_en: The Book of the Revival of the Religious Sciences — Section 99: On the Distinction, Overlap, and Synonymy of Faith (Īmān) and Submission (Islām), and Their Worldly and Otherworldly Judgments
16:76.anchors:
- Root: ايم (A-Y-M)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of remaining unmarried, or a state of being without a spouse; extended metaphorically to describe one who is solitary or without support.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الأيامى: جمع أيم، وهي المرأة التي لا بعل لها... والحرب مأيمة، أي: يفرق بين الزوج والزوجة." The root carries the sense of separation or a state of lacking union, which informs the theological discussion of what constitutes the essential bond of faith.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah) usage denotes the state of being unmarried; metaphorical (Majaz) usage extends to anything that separates or leaves one bereft. This distinction between literal and metaphorical application is central to the chapter's method.
- Root: قلب (Q-L-B)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To turn, overturn, or transform a thing from one state to another.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "قلب الشيء: تصريفه وصرفه عن وجه إلى وجه... والانقلاب: الانصراف." The heart (qalb) is so named for its constant fluctuation and turning. In theological terms, it is the seat of taṣdīq (assent), the immaterial faculty of cognition and conviction.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah) usage is physical turning; metaphorical (Majaz) usage is "قلب الأمور" — to deliberate, scrutinize, and manage affairs. This supports the distinction between the heart's internal act of assent and the external acts of the limbs.
- Root: عمل (ʿ-A-M-L)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Any deed or action performed with purpose and intent.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "العمل: كل فعل يكون من الحيوان بقصد، فهو أخص من الفعل." Work is more specific than mere action, as it implies deliberate, intentional agency. It is used for both righteous and sinful deeds, and is the external manifestation of internal conviction.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah) usage refers to physical labor or deeds. The chapter explores whether "work" is an integral part of the reality of faith or a separate, consequent requirement.
- Root: صدق (S-D-Q)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To be truthful, to speak the truth, to verify.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الصدق والكذب أصلهما في القول... ولا يكونان بالقصد الأول إلا في القول." Truth and falsehood are primarily properties of speech and reports. Taṣdīq (assent) is the heart's affirmation of the truth of a report, which is the core reality of Īmān.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah) usage is truthful speech; metaphorical (Majaz) usage is "صادق الحملة" — one who is true and firm in battle or resolve. This shows that taṣdīq is not merely verbal but a firm, internal resolution.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication). This rule governs how restriction (ḥaṣr) is achieved in Arabic, often through particles like "innamā" or through contextual specification (takhṣīṣ). The chapter's core argument hinges on how terms like Īmān and Islām are semantically restricted, expanded, or made synonymous through contextual usage (majāz), requiring precise parsing of the predicate and its scope.
16:76.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Foundations of Belief'

16:76.arabic: كالملوك والأكابر ويضعف مهما كان المادح ممن لا يؤبه له ولا يقدر على شيء فإن القدرة عليه بملك قلبه قدرة على أمر حقير فلا يدل المدح إلا على قدرة قاصرة وبهذه العلة أيضا يكره الذم ويتألم به القلب وإذا كان من الأكابر كانت نكايته أعظم لأن الفائت به أعظم السبب الثالث أن ثناء المثني ومدح المادح سبب لاصطياد قلب كل من يسمعه لا سيما إذا كان ذلك ممن يلتفت إلى قوله ويعتد بثنائه وهذا مختص بثناء يقع على الملأ فلا جرم كلما كان الجمع أكثر والمثني أجدر بأن يلتفت إلى
16:76.english: This contains no dissimulation (talbīs); rather, it is a blocking of the path to knowledge of that in which there is no benefit in knowing — like one who conceals from the Sultan that he drinks wine, yet does not cast to him that he is pious. For his saying "I am pious" would be dissimulation, whereas his failure to confess to drinking does not necessitate the belief in his piety; rather, it merely prevents knowledge of his drinking.
16:76.section_title_en: Section 802 — On the Causes of the Love of Praise and the Soul's Delight in It, and Its Aversion to Blame
16:76.anchors:
- Root: مدح (m-d-ḥ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: مدح: الحسن الجميل في القول، والثناء على الرجل بما فيه من الخير.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): المدح: ذكر محاسن الغير، وهو ضرب من الثناء، ويقابله الذم، وكلاهما من أفعال القول الدالة على اعتقاد المتكلم.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Haqiqah: مدحه: أحسن الثناء عليه. Majaz: مدحه بوجهه: إذا أظهر السرور به، ومدحت الأرض: إذا أخصبت وحسنت.
- Root: ذم (dh-m-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: الذم: نقيض المدح، وهو ذكر المساوي والقبائح.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): الذم: إظهار نقائص الغير، وهو ضد المدح، وقد يكون بحق أو بباطل.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Haqiqah: ذمه: قبح فعله ووصفه بالقبيح. Majaz: ذم الماء: إذا كان غير عذب، وذم المكان: إذا كان وخيما.
- Root: ملك (m-l-k)
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): الملك: هو المتصرف بالأمر والنهي في الجمهور، والملك ضربان: ملك هو التملك والتولي، وملك هو القوة على ذلك.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Haqiqah: ملك الشيء وامتلكه وتملكه. Majaz: ملك قلبه: استولى عليه، وملكت فلانة أمرها: خليت وشأنها.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — Used to isolate the four causes of love of praise as exhaustive and ordered.

16:76.arabic: الله مثلا عبدا مملوكا لا يقدر على شيء أراد به النفقة مما رزق وقوله عز وجل وضرب الله مثلا رجلين أحدهما أبكم لا يقدر على شيء أي الأمر بالعدل والاستقامة وقوله عز وجل فإن اتبعتني فلا تسألني عن شيء أراد به من صفات الربوبية وهو العلوم التي لا يحل السؤال عنها حتى يبتدئ بها العارف في أوان الاستحقاق وقوله عز وجل أم خلقوا من غير شي أم هم الخالقون أي من غير خالق فربما يتوهم به أنه يدل على أنه لا يخلق شيء إلا من شيء وأما القرين فكقوله عز وجل وقال قرينه هذا ما لدي عتيد ألقيا في جهنم كل كفار أر

16:76.arabic: وجل وضرب الله مثلا رجلين أحدهما أبكم لا يقدر على شيء أي الأمر بالعدل والاستقامة وقوله عز وجل فإن اتبعتني فلا تسألني عن شيء أراد به من صفات الربوبية وهو العلوم التي لا يحل السؤال عنها حتى يبتدئ بها العارف في أوان الاستحقاق وقوله عز وجل أم خلقوا من غير شي أم هم الخالقون أي من غير خالق فربما يتوهم به أنه يدل على أنه لا يخلق شيء إلا من شيء وأما القرين فكقوله عز وجل وقال قرينه هذا ما لدي عتيد ألقيا في جهنم كل كفار أراد به الملك الموكل به وقوله تعالى قال قرينه ربنا ما أطغيته ولكن كان أراد به الشيطان وأما
16:76.english: I say: The Prophet (peace be upon him) was asked about the means of deliverance from these trials, and he said: "The Book of Allah — act by what is in it, for it is that which delivers one from them." The questioner repeated this three times, and he (peace be upon him) said three times: "Learn the Book of Allah, Mighty and Glorious, and act by what is in it, for in it is deliverance."

16:76.arabic: مملوك لا تقدر على شيء ومن عرف ذلك لا بد وأن يزول كبره ومثاله أن يفتخر الغافل بقوته وجماله وماله وحريته واستقلاله وسعة منازله وكثرة خيوله وغلمانه إذ شهد عليه شاهدان عدلان عند حاكم منصف بأنه رقيق لفلان وأن أبويه كانا مملوكين له فعلم ذلك وحكم به الحاكم فجاء مالكه فأخذه وأخذ جميع ما في يده وهو مع ذلك يخشى أن يعاقبه وينكل به لتفريطه في أمواله وتقصيره في طلب مالكه ليعرف أن له مالكا ثم نظر العبد فرأى نفسه محبوسا في منزل قد أحدقت به الحيات والعقارب والهوام وهو في كل حال على
16:76.english: ...twice. Likewise, Ṭāwūs said to ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz — when he saw him strutting with arrogance, and that was before his caliphate — "This is not the gait of one in whose belly there is filth." And this is its beginning and its middle.
16:76.section_title_en: The Cure for Pride in Beauty, Strength, and Wealth — Section 867
16:76.anchors:
- Root: قبح (qubḥ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root meaning "ugliness, foulness, disgrace" — both moral and physical deformity.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: qubḥ is the contrary of ḥusn; in Kalam, it denotes what reason or revelation deems reprehensible, whether in act or attribute.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) usage applies to sensory ugliness; metaphorical (majāz) extends to moral baseness — here Ghazali pivots between both to shame the proud.
- Root: ذل (dhillah)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "Lowliness, abasement, submission" — opposite of ʿizzah (honor/might).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In Quranic usage, dhullah is the state of one stripped of all self-sufficiency, utterly dependent on another.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical humiliation before a conqueror; metaphorical: the soul's recognition of its ontological servitude before its true Owner.
- Root: ملك (milk)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "Possession, ownership, dominion" — from which malik (king) and mamlūk (slave) derive.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): True milk belongs to Allah alone; creaturely possession is borrowed, contingent, and revocable at any instant.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: legal ownership of property or persons; metaphorical: the illusion of self-ownership that pride presupposes — Ghazali shatters this illusion via the juridical parable.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The periodic sentence structure here repeatedly delays the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) to build rhetorical tension, as in "لو توجع عرق واحد... لصار أعجز" — the protasis and apodosis are separated by expanding clauses, mirroring the cumulative weight of evidence against pride.
16:76.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Condemnation of Pride and Conceit'

16:125.arabic: ولم تزل الرسل صلوات الله عليهم يحاجون المنكرين ويجادلونهم قال تعالى {وجادلهم بالتي هي أحسن} فالصحابة رضي الله عنهم أيضا كانوا يحاجون المنكرين ويجادلون ولكن عند الحاجة وكانت الحاجة إليه قليلة في زمانهم وأول من سن دعوة المبتدعة بالمجادلة إلى الحق علي ابن أبي طالب رضي الله عنه إذ بعث ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما إلى الخوارج فكلمهم فقال ما تنقمون على إمامكم قالوا قاتل ولم يسب ولم يغنم فقال ذلك في قتال الكفار أرأيتم لو سببت عائشة رضي الله عنها في سهم أحدكم أكنتم تستحلون منها ما تستحلون من ملككم وهي أمكم في نص الكتاب فقالوا لا فرجع منهم إلى
16:125.english: The mention of the proof (ḥujjah), the demand for it, and the search after it — how could these be prohibited, when God — may He be exalted — has said: {«قُلْ هَاتُوا بُرْهَانَكُمْ»} (Say: Bring forth your proof — Qur'an 2:111), and He — mighty and majestic — has said: {«لِيَهْلِكَ مَنْ هَلَكَ عَنْ بَيِّنَةٍ وَيَحْيَا مَنْ حَيَّ عَنْ بَيِّنَةٍ»} (So that he who perishes may perish upon clear evidence, and he who lives may live upon clear evidence — Qur'an 8:42), and He — may He be exalted — has said: {«هَلْ عِنْدَكُمْ مِنْ سُلْطَانٍ بِهَذَا»} (Have you any authority for this? — Qur'an 10:68), meaning a proof and demonstration, and He — may He be exalted — has said: {«قُلْ فَلِلَّهِ الْحُجَّةُ الْبَالِغَةُ»} (Say: To God belongs the conclusive proof — Qur'an 6:149), and He — may He be exalted — has said: {«أَلَمْ تَرَ إِلَى الَّذِي حَاجَّ إِبْرَاهِيمَ فِي رَبِّهِ»} (Have you not considered him who disputed with Abraham concerning his Lord? — Qur'an 2:258) up to His words: {«فَبُهِتَ الَّذِي كَفَرَ»} (So the one who disbelieved was confounded — Qur'an 2:258).
16:125.section_title_en: The Revival of the Religious Sciences — Section 77: On the Permissibility of Theological Discourse (Kalām) and Its Early Practice
16:125.anchors:
- Root: ح-د-ث (ḥ-d-th)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "Al-ḥudūth: the coming-to-be of a thing after it was not; al-ḥadath: the novel event; al-ḥīdāth: origination."
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Al-ḥudūth: a thing's becoming after it was not, whether accident or substance; iḥdāth: bringing it into existence. The origination of substances belongs to God alone."
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "Literal: 'He is a recent event among events.' Metaphorical: 'They became topics of conversation (aḥādīth).'"
- Root: ح-ا-ج (ḥ-ā-j)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "Al-ḥājah: need of a thing, with desire for it; its plural: ḥājāt and ḥawā'ij."
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Al-ḥājah ilā al-shay': poverty toward it with love of it. God said: {«إِلَّا حَاجَةً فِي نَفْسِ يَعْقُوبَ»} (except a need in Jacob's soul — Qur'an 12:68)."
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "Literal: need and want. The 'ḥājah' is that which one seeks to obtain."
- Root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "Kāna: to be, to exist; takwīn: bringing into being from non-existence."
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Al-kawn: existence after non-existence; the muḥdath (originated thing) is that brought forth after it was not."
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "Literal: being and becoming. Metaphorical: the continuous states of affairs."
- Sibawayh Rule: Al-Faṣl bayna al-Jār wa-al-Majrūr (Prepositional Interposition) — The permissibility of separating a preposition from its object when the intervening clause is complete in meaning, as in the verse's structure of argumentation where the proof (ḥujjah) stands independently before its conclusion.
16:125.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'Foundations of Belief'

16:125.arabic: الله وعمل صالحا} وقال تعالى {ادع إلى سبيل ربك بالحكمة والموعظة الحسنة} وقال تعالى {ويعلمهم الكتاب والحكمة} وأما الأخبار فقوله صلى الله عليه وسلم لما بعث معاذا رضي الله عنه إلى اليمن لأن يهدي الله بك رجلا واحدا خير لك من الدنيا وما فيها // حديث قال لمعاذ حين بعثه إلى اليمن لأن يهدي الله بك رجلا واحدا خير لك الحديث أخرجه أحمد من حديث معاذ وفي الصحيحين من حديث سهل ابن سعد أنه قال ذلك لعلي وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم من تعلم بابا من العلم ليعلم الناس أعطي ثواب سبعين صديقا (1) وقال عيسى صلى الله عليه وسلم
16:125.english: As for the Qur'anic verses: His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: {وَلِيُنذِرُوا قَوْمَهُمْ إِذَا رَجَعُوا إِلَيْهِمْ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَحْذَرُونَ} "That they may warn their people when they return to them, that perhaps they may be cautious" {«ولينذروا قومهم إذا رجعوا إليهم لعلهم يحذرون»} — and the intended meaning is teaching and guidance (al-taʿlīm wa-al-irshād).
16:125.anchors:
- Root: علم (ʿalima)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning is "to know, to perceive a thing by its reality"; the root also carries the sense of "marker, sign, banner" — that by which something is distinguished and recognized.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "العلم: إدراك الشيء بحقيقته" — knowledge is the apprehension of a thing by its true reality, divided into apprehension of the essence of a thing and judgment upon it. This is the attribute by which the scholar (ʿālim) is distinguished and by which he becomes a "sign" (ʿalam) pointing to truth.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): "هو من أعلام العلم الخافقه" — the scholar is among the lofty banners of knowledge. The teaching act makes the scholar a living signpost; the root's literal sense of "marking" or "branding" a thing carries into the metaphorical (majāz) register of "imprinting" knowledge upon hearts.
- Root: حدث (ḥadatha)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning is "to be new, to occur after not having been"; al-ḥadīth is speech that is new and conveyed.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الحدوث: كون الشيء بعد أن لم يكن" — origination after non-existence. The prophetic traditions (aḥādīth) cited here are "newly conveyed" reports that carry authority.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Metaphorical (majāz): "صاروا أحاديث" — they became subjects of discourse. The transmission of knowledge is an "event" (ḥadath) that occurs in the listener, renewing his state.
- Root: عهد (ʿahida)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning is "covenant, pact, charge"; al-ʿahd is a binding commission that one is obligated to fulfill.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The covenant (mīthāq) taken from the People of the Book and from the scholars is a divine charge (taklīf) that makes teaching an obligation, not a supererogatory act.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the covenant is a "charge entrusted" (waṣiyyah) that binds the one who receives knowledge to its dissemination.
- Root: كتم (katama)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning is "to conceal, to hide"; al-kitmān is the deliberate suppression of what ought to be revealed.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Concealment of knowledge is paired with concealment of testimony (shahādah) in the Qur'an — both are sins of the heart (ithm al-qalb) because they withhold what God has commanded to be made manifest.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal vs. metaphorical: the "bridle of fire" (lijām min nār) on the Day of Judgment is a metaphorical (majāz) embodiment of the inner restraint of truth — the concealed knowledge becomes a physical restraint in the afterlife.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد (Restriction & Specification) — The verse {وإن فريقا منهم ليكتمون الحق وهم يعلمون} employs the restrictive particle "inna" with the continuous verb form (yaktimūn) to specify an ongoing, willful concealment, distinguishing it from mere ignorance. The conditional structures in the ḥadīth "man taʿallama... man ʿallama... man katama" (whoever learns... whoever teaches... whoever conceals) follow the canonical pattern of protasis-apodosis (sharṭ/jazāʾ) that establishes a universal causal linkage between the act and its recompense.

17:44.arabic: ومن هذا قوله تعالى وإن من شيء إلا يسبح بحمده فالبليد يفتقر فيه إلى أن يقدر للجمادات حياة وعقلا ونطقا بصوت وحرف حتى يقول سبحان الله ليتحقق تسبيحه والبصير يعلم أنه ما أريد به نطق اللسان بل كونه مسبحا بوجوده ومقدسا بذاته وشاهدا بوحدانية الله سبحانه كما يقال وفي كل شيء له آية .
17:44.english: The fifth [division] is that one expresses by the tongue of explicit statement (lisān al-maqāl) what belongs to the tongue of state (lisān al-ḥāl). The one of deficient understanding stops at the outward and believes it to be literal speech, while the one with insight into realities perceives the secret within it. This is like the saying of one who said: "The wall said to the peg: 'Why have you split me?' It replied: 'Ask the one who strikes me — he did not leave me behind the stone that is behind me.'" This is an expression of the tongue of state by the tongue of explicit statement.
17:44.section_title_en: The Fourth Division — Comprehension by Encounter and Taste (Al-Dhawq), and the Fifth Division — The Tongue of State (Lisān al-Ḥāl)
17:44.anchors:
- Root: علم (ʿalima)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root denotes the faculty of knowing, perceiving a thing's reality; encompasses both direct apprehension and judgment about existence.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "العلم: إدراك الشيء بحقيقته" — knowledge is the apprehension of a thing in its true reality, divided into apprehension of the essence itself and judgment concerning it.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Distinguishes literal knowledge (maʿrifah) from awareness (shuʿūr); here, the distinction between superficial knowledge (ẓāhir) and realized knowledge (bāṭin) is rhetorical-metaphorical, not contradictory.
- Root: ظهر (ẓahara)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root denotes outwardness, visibility, strength of back; the ẓāhir is what is manifest and apparent.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The ẓāhir is used metaphorically for the outward aspect of a thing, as opposed to its inner reality (bāṭin); the back (ẓahr) carries what is loaded upon it.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas - Majaz): "قلبت الأمر ظهرا لبطن" — turning a matter over, examining its outward and inward aspects; the ẓāhir is the shell (qishr) that contains and is completed by the inner kernel (lubb).
- Root: وقع (waqaʿa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root denotes falling, occurring, befalling; a thing's occurrence and realization.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الوقوع: ثبوت الشيء وسقوطه" — occurrence is the establishment and falling of a thing; in Quranic usage, often associated with calamities and inevitable events.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas - Majaz): "وقع الأمر حصل ووجد" — the matter occurred, i.e., it became realized and existent; here, the "occurrence" of a state (ḥāl) is its actual realization in the soul, as opposed to mere intellectual assent before its descent.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The syntactic structure allows for separation between the operative word and its object to achieve rhetorical emphasis, mirroring the semantic distinction between outward apprehension and inward realization.
17:44.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications, prayers, and their spiritual power, from 'Foundations of Belief'

17:44.arabic: ولذلك قال تعالى ولكن لا تفقهون تسبيحهم وأما القاصرون فلا يفقهون أصلا وأما المقربون والعلماء الراسخون فلا يفقهون كنهه وكماله إذ لكل شيء شهادات شتى على تقديس الله سبحانه وتسبيحه ويدرك كل واحد بقدر عقله وبصيرته وتعداد تلك الشهادات لا يليق بعلم المعاملة فهذا الفن أيضا مما يتفاوت أرباب الظواهر وأرباب البصائر في علمه وتظهر به مفارقة الباطن للظاهر وفي هذا المقام لأرباب المقامات إسراف واقتصاد فمن مسرف في رفع الظواهر انتهى إلى تغيير جميع الظواهر والبراهين أو أكثرها حتى حملوا قوله تعالى وتكل
17:44.english: The fifth [division] is that one expresses by the tongue of explicit statement (lisān al-maqāl) what belongs to the tongue of state (lisān al-ḥāl). The one of deficient understanding stops at the outward and believes it to be literal speech, while the one with insight into realities perceives the secret within it. This is like the saying of one who said: "The wall said to the peg: 'Why have you split me?' It replied: 'Ask the one who strikes me — he did not leave me behind the stone that is behind me.'" This is an expression of the tongue of state by the tongue of explicit statement.

17:44.arabic: بالوحدانية هي توحيدها وأنواع شاهدات لصانعها بالتقدس هي تسبيحها ولكن لا يفقهون تسبيحها لأنهم لم يسافروا من مضيق سمع الظاهر إلى فضاء سمع الباطن ومن ركاكة لسان المقال إلى فصاحة لسان الحال ولو قدر كل عاجز على مثل هذا السير لما كان سليمان عليه السلام مختصا بفهم منطق الطير ولما كان موسى عليه السلام مختصا بسماع كلام الله تعالى الذي يجب تقديسه عن مشابهة الحروف والأصوات ومن يسافر ليستقرئ هذه الشهادات من الأسطر المكتوبة بالخطوط الإلهية على صفحات الجمادات لم يطل سفره بالبدن بل يستقر في موضع ويفرغ قلبه للتمتع بسماع نغمات التسبيحا
17:44.english: I say: As for the signs of God in His earth, in contemplating them there are benefits for the discerning seeker of insight. For in them are contiguous tracts, and in them are mountains, wildernesses, seas, and varieties of animals and plants. And there is not a single thing among them but that it bears witness to God of His Oneness and glorifies Him with an eloquent tongue (lisān dhalq) that none perceives save him who gives ear while being present as a witness {«وَأَلْقَى السَّمْعَ وَهُوَ شَهِيدٌ»} (And gives ear while he is a witness) [Q. 50:37].
17:44.section_title_en: The Book of Seclusion — The Benefits of Association and Travel: Association with Increased Occupation and Endurance of Hardships
17:44.anchors:
- Root: سمع (s-m-')
  * Lisan / Ayn: The faculty of hearing in the ear; also used for the ear itself, and metaphorically for understanding or obedience.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "السمع" denotes both the physical faculty and, in theological contexts, the inner hearing of the heart by which divine truths are apprehended — distinct from mere auditory perception.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): hearing sounds. Metaphorical (Majaz): "سمع الله لمن حمده" (God hears him who praises Him) means acceptance and response; "ألقى السمع" (gave ear) implies attentive presence of heart.
- Root: سفر (s-f-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To uncover, reveal, or travel; the traveler (musāfir) is one who uncovers new horizons.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "السفر: كشف الغطاء" — uncovering the veil; journeying as a means of unveiling hidden realities.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical travel. Metaphorical: "وجه مسفر" (a face radiant with joy); the inner journey from the narrow confines of outward perception to the expanse of inner vision.
- Root: ظهر (ẓ-h-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The back; outward or visible aspect.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Used metaphorically for the outward, apparent dimension of things, as opposed to the inner (bāṭin).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the back of a beast. Metaphorical: "قلبت الأمر ظهرا لبطن" (turned the matter over, back and belly) — examining all aspects; the visible world (ʿālam al-shahādah) as the outward face of reality.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — Used to distinguish the exclusive nature of inner hearing (al-samʿ al-bāṭin) as the sole means of apprehending the language of states (lisān al-ḥāl), in contrast to outward hearing shared with beasts.
17:44.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Etiquette of Travel'

18:23.arabic: ولا تقولن لشيء إني فاعل ذلك غدا إلا أن يشاء الله ثم لم يقتصر على ذلك فيما لا يشك فيه بل قال تعالى لتدخلن المسجد الحرام إن شاء الله آمنين محلقين رءؤسكم ومقصرين وكان الله سبحانه عالما بأنهم يدخلون لا محالة وأنه شاءه ولكن المقصود تعليمه ذلك فتأدب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في ما كان يخبر عنه معلوما كان أو مشكوكا حتى قال صلى الله عليه وسلم لما دخل المقابر السلام عليكم دار قوم مؤمنين وإنا إن شاء الله بكم لاحقون (1) واللحوق بهم غير مشكوك فيه ولكن مقتضى الأدب ذكر الله تعالى وربط الأمور به وهذه الصيغ
18:23.english: If you say: "What is the meaning of the Salaf's statement, 'I am a believer, if God wills' — given that the exception (istithnā') implies doubt, and doubt in faith is unbelief? Yet they all refrained from giving an unqualified answer affirming faith and were cautious about it."
18:23.section_title_en: On the Meaning of the Salaf's Statement "I am a Believer, If God Wills" — Section 102
18:23.anchors:
- Root: نفس (n-f-s)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The self, the soul; that which is breathed; the innermost reality of a person.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): النفس is used for the rūḥ (spirit), for the dhāt (essence/self), and for the seat of intention and knowledge. When one says "he knows in himself (nafsihi) that he is a believer," it denotes certitude residing in the very core of one's being, not a corporeal faculty.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) usage refers to the soul's reflexive self-awareness; metaphorical (majāz) usage extends to "blood" (dam) or "the eye" (ʿayn) of envy. Here, "in himself" (fī nafsihi) is literal self-knowledge, not mere outward profession.
- Root: وجه (w-j-h)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Face, countenance; the foremost part; a mode, aspect, or direction.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The face is the most noble apparent part of a thing; hence it is used for the "aspect" or "manner" (wajh) of an affair. "Four aspects" (wujūh) means four distinct modes of interpretation or rational grounds.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the face of a person or object. Metaphorical: "the face of the matter" (wajh al-amr) — its most salient and honorable dimension. Here, the "aspects" are hermeneutical angles, not physical parts.
- Root: ايم (a-y-m)
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The unmarried state (aym); one who has no spouse. Not applicable here directly, but the root's semantic field of "being alone/without attachment" contrasts with īmān's root (a-m-n) — security and trust — which is the operative term in this text.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Not directly relevant; the operative root is أمن (a-m-n), meaning security from fear, and by extension, faith (īmān) as the state of being secure in God's truth.
- Root: كان (k-w-n)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To be, to exist; the copula of predication.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Kāna denotes existence and becoming; in theological usage, it grounds the distinction between what is (mawjūd) and what is merely asserted. The question "Are you a believer?" (a-mu'min anta?) uses kāna implicitly to ask about actual, present state — not future contingency.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: existence. Metaphorical: the "being-so" of a predicate. The istithnā' (exception) with "in shā' Allāh" suspends the copula's certainty, shifting from assertive existence to contingent hope.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الاستثناء والتعليق بالمشيئة (The Chapter of Exception and Suspension by the Divine Will) — When an exception clause (istithnā') follows a positive assertion, it grammatically suspends the universality or certainty of the predication. In theological discourse, this suspension may be semantic (doubt) or pragmatic (deference, etiquette, or self-deprecation), and Sibawayh's parsing of conditional suspension (taʿlīq) shows that the apodosis need not be negated — only its absolute, unqualified force is tempered.

18:30.arabic: فالإيمان رأس الحسنات ولقوله تعالى {والله يحب المحسنين} وقال تعالى {إنا لا نضيع أجر من أحسن عملا} ولا حجة لهم في ذلك فإنه حيث ذكر الإيمان في هذه الآيات أريد به الإيمان مع العمل إذ بينا أن الإيمان قد يطلق ويراد به الإسلام وهو الموافقة بالقلب والقول والعمل ودليل هذا التأويل أخبار كثيرة في معاقبة العاصين ومقادير العقاب وقوله صلى الله عليه وسلم يخرج من النار من كان في قلبه مثقال ذرة من إيمان فكيف يخرج إذا لم يدخل ومن القرآن قوله تعالى {إن الله لا يغفر أن يشرك به ويغفر ما دون ذلك لمن يشاء} والاستثناء بالمشيئة يدل على الانقسام وقوله تعالى {ومن يعص ال
18:30.english: He was asked, "Which deed is most excellent?" The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Islam." It was then asked, "Which aspect of Islam is most excellent?" He (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Faith (Īmān)." This is evidence for both the distinction (ikhtilāf) between the two terms and their overlap (tadākhul). This usage is the most consistent with the conventions of the language, because faith is a deed among deeds, and it is the most excellent of them. Islam is submission (taslīm), whether by the heart, by the tongue, or by the limbs. The most excellent of these is that which is by the heart, which is the assent (taṣdīq) that is called faith. Using the two terms in a way that indicates distinction, overlap, or even complete synonymy (tarāduf) is all within the bounds of metaphorical usage (tajawwuz) in the language.

18:30.anchors:
- Root: ايم (A-Y-M)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of remaining unmarried, or a state of being without a spouse; extended metaphorically to describe one who is solitary or without support.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الأيامى: جمع أيم، وهي المرأة التي لا بعل لها... والحرب مأيمة، أي: يفرق بين الزوج والزوجة." The root carries the sense of separation or a state of lacking union, which informs the theological discussion of what constitutes the essential bond of faith.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah) usage denotes the state of being unmarried; metaphorical (Majaz) usage extends to anything that separates or leaves one bereft. This distinction between literal and metaphorical application is central to the chapter's method.
- Root: قلب (Q-L-B)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To turn, overturn, or transform a thing from one state to another.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "قلب الشيء: تصريفه وصرفه عن وجه إلى وجه... والانقلاب: الانصراف." The heart (qalb) is so named for its constant fluctuation and turning. In theological terms, it is the seat of taṣdīq (assent), the immaterial faculty of cognition and conviction.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah) usage is physical turning; metaphorical (Majaz) usage is "قلب الأمور" — to deliberate, scrutinize, and manage affairs. This supports the distinction between the heart's internal act of assent and the external acts of the limbs.
- Root: عمل (ʿ-A-M-L)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Any deed or action performed with purpose and intent.

  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah) usage refers to physical labor or deeds. The chapter explores whether "work" is an integral part of the reality of faith or a separate, consequent requirement.
- Root: صدق (S-D-Q)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To be truthful, to speak the truth, to verify.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الصدق والكذب أصلهما في القول... ولا يكونان بالقصد الأول إلا في القول." Truth and falsehood are primarily properties of speech and reports. Taṣdīq (assent) is the heart's affirmation of the truth of a report, which is the core reality of Īmān.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah) usage is truthful speech; metaphorical (Majaz) usage is "صادق الحملة" — one who is true and firm in battle or resolve. This shows that taṣdīq is not merely verbal but a firm, internal resolution.

19:42.arabic: الأصنام جهلا وغيا فقال له لم تعبد ما لا يسمع ولا يبصر ولا يغني عنك شيئا ولو انقلب ذلك عليه في معبوده لأضحت حجته داحضة ودلالته ساقطة ولم يصدق قوله تعالى وتلك حجتنا آتيناها إبراهيم على قومه وكما عقل كونه فاعلا بلا جارحة وعالما بلا قلب ودماغ فليعقل كونه بصيرا بلا حدقة وسميعا بلا اذن إذ لا فرق بينهما الأصل السادس أنه سبحانه وتعالى متكلم بكلام وهو وصف قائم بذاته ليس بصوت ولا حرف بل لا يشبه كلامه كلام غيره كما لا يشبه وجوده وجود غيره والكلام بالحقيقة كلام النفس وإنما الأصوات قطعت حروفا للدلالات كما يدل عليها تارة بالحركات
19:42.english:
[Root: عقل]
  • Al-Raghib (Al-Mufradat): "العقل يقال للقوة المتهيئة لقبول العلم، ويقال للعلم الذي يستفيده الإنسان بتلك القوة عقل" — The intellect is the faculty prepared for receiving knowledge, and the knowledge acquired through that faculty is also called intellect. This dual sense is crucial for understanding Ghazali's argument that true intellection ('aql) grasps realities beyond sensory perception.
  • Al-Zamakhshari (Asas - Haqiqah/Literal): "عقل فلان بعد الصبا أي عرف الخطأ الذي كان عليه" — To exercise intellect means to recognize error. Ghazali employs this to demand intellectual consistency from his opponents.
  • Al-Zamakhshari (Asas - Majaz/Metaphorical): "نخلة لا تعقل الإبار إذا لم تقبله" — A palm tree that does not accept pollination is said metaphorically to "not comprehend." This illustrates that 'aql involves receptivity to what is appropriate.

19:71.arabic: وإن منكم إلا واردها كان على ربك حتما مقضيا ثم ننجي الذين اتقوا ونذر الظالمين فيها جثيا ولذلك قال الخائفون من السلف إنما خوفنا لأنا تيقنا أنا على النار واردون وشككنا في النجاة ولما روى الحسن الخبر الوارد فيمن يخرج من النار بعد ألف عام وأنه ينادي يا حنان يا منان (1) قال الحسن يا ليتني كنت ذلك الرجل واعلم أن في الأخبار ما يدل على أن آخر من يخرج من النار بعد سبعة آلاف سنة وأن الاختلاف في المدة بين اللحظة وبين سبعة آلاف سنة حتى قد يجوز بعضهم على النار كبرق خاطف ولا يكون له فيها لبث وبين اللحظة وبين سبعة آلاف سنة درجات متفاوتة من اليوم والأسب
19:71.english: The fire of Hell is the coldest of fires [in comparison to the fire of separation]. And you should not deny this in the world of the Hereafter, for it has a witnessed parallel in the world of this world. Indeed, one has been seen who was overcome by ecstasy (wajd) and walked upon fire and upon the roots of cane, his feet being cut, yet he did not feel it, due to the extreme dominance of what was in his heart. And you see the angry man, when anger overcomes him in battle, receiving wounds and not feeling them at that moment, because anger is a fire in the heart. The Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, said: {«الغضب قطعة من النار»} "Anger is a piece of fire." The burning of the heart (iḥtirāq al-fu'ād) is more severe than the burning of bodies, and the more severe annuls the sensation of the weaker, as you observe. For destruction from fire and the sword is only inasmuch as they separate between two parts that are linked one to the other by the bond of composition (ta'līf) possible in bodies. So that which separates between the heart and its Beloved, to which it is linked by a bond of composition far more firm than the composition of bodies, is more intensely painful—if you are among the people of insight (abṣār) and the people of hearts. And it is not far-fetched that he who has no heart should not perceive the severity of this pain and should deem it trivial in comparison to bodily pain. For a boy, if he were given the choice between the pain of being deprived of a ball and a polo-stick, and the pain of being deprived of the rank of a Sultan, he would not feel the pain of deprivation from the Sultan's rank at all, nor would he count that as a pain. And the enemy in the field with the polo-stick is more beloved to him than a thousand thrones of the Sultan with sitting upon them. Nay, even one overcome by the lust of the belly, if given the choice between porridge (harīsah) and sweets (ḥalwā) and between a beautiful deed by which he conquers enemies and delights friends, he would prefer the porridge and sweets. All of this is due to the absence of the meaning (maʿnā) by whose existence rank becomes beloved, and the presence of the meaning by whose existence food becomes delicious. This is for one whom the attributes of beasts and predators have enslaved, and in whom the attributes of the angels have not appeared—those attributes which are not suited by, nor delight in, anything but proximity to the Lord of the Worlds, and which are pained only by distance and the veil (ḥijāb). And just as taste is only in the tongue and hearing only in the ears, so this attribute is only in the heart. So he who has no heart has no such sense, like he who has no hearing or sight has no pleasure in melodies or the beauty of forms and colors. And not every human has a heart; were it so, the saying of God, Most High, would not be sound: {«إن في ذلك لذكرى لمن كان له قلب»} "Indeed in that is a reminder for whoever has a heart" (Q. 50:37). Thus He made the one who does not heed the Quran devoid of a heart. And by "heart" I do not mean this [organ] which the ribs of the chest encompass. Rather, I mean the secret (sirr) which is of the world of the Command (ʿālam al-amr). The flesh which is of the world of Creation (ʿālam al-khalq) is its Throne (ʿarsh), the chest is its Footstool (kursī), and the rest of the limbs are its domain and kingdom. And to God belongs the Creation and the Command altogether. But that secret, concerning which God, Most High, said: {«قل الروح من أمر ربي»} "Say: The Spirit is of the Command of my Lord" (Q. 17:85), is the commander and the king, because between the world of the Command and the world of Creation there is an ordering, and the world of the Command is commander over the world of Creation. It is the subtle divine reality (al-laṭīfah) which, when it is sound, the rest of the body is sound for its sake. Whoever knows it has known his own self, and whoever knows his own self has known his Lord. At that point, the servant smells the beginnings of the fragrance of the meaning folded under his saying, peace and blessings be upon him: {«إن الله خلق آدم على صورته»} "God created Adam upon His image." He looks with the eye of mercy upon those who adhere to its literal wording and upon those who are obstinate in the path of its interpretation (ta'wīl). And even though His mercy for those adhering to the letter is greater than His mercy for the obstinate interpreters, because mercy is proportional to the affliction, and the affliction of those [literalists] is greater—even if they share in the affliction of being deprived of the reality of the matter—for the Reality (al-ḥaqīqah) is the bounty of God which He gives to whom He wills, and God is the Possessor of Great Bounty. And His Wisdom is singled out for whom He wills: {«ومن يؤت الحكمة فقد أوتي خيرا كثيرا»} "And whoever is given wisdom has been given much good" (Q. 2:269). Let us return to the purpose, for we have drawn out the length and lengthened the breath in a matter that is higher than the sciences of transactions (muʿāmalāt) which we intend in this book. It has become clear that the rank of destruction is only for the ignorant deniers. And the testimony of that from the Book of God and the Sunnah of His Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, is beyond enumeration, so we have not cited it.
19:71.section_title_en: The Ranks of the Hereafter: On the Distribution of Degrees and the States of the Saved, the Punished, and the Victorious
19:71.anchors:
- Root: ح ر ق (ḥ-r-q)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of burning, scorching, and the fire's consumption of its fuel.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The fire of the Hereafter (Nār) is a created reality, but its perception is tied to the spiritual state of the perceiver.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah) for physical burning; metaphorical (Majaz) for the burning of the heart (iḥtirāq al-fu'ād) by overwhelming love or anger.
- Root: ق ل ب (q-l-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To turn, overturn, or transform a thing from one state to another.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The heart (Qalb) is the seat of perception and understanding, distinct from the physical organ.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal for the physical heart; metaphorical for the spiritual subtlety (Laṭīfah) that is the locus of divine knowledge and love.
- Root: ع ل م (ʿ-l-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To know, to perceive a thing by its true nature.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Knowledge (ʿIlm) is the apprehension of a thing's reality, which is the basis for distinguishing the ranks of the believers.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal for acquired knowledge; metaphorical for the "unveiling" (Kashf) knowledge granted to the knowers (ʿĀrifūn).
- Sibawayh Rule: Restriction and Specification (Bāb al-Ḥaṣr wa al-Taqyīd bi-innamā) — Used to distinguish the specific referents of terms like "heart" (Qalb) and "faith" (Īmān), ensuring the precise meaning is not conflated with common usage.
