19:71.arabic: تعالى وإن منكم إلا واردها كان على ربك حتما مقضيا ثم ننجي الذين اتقوا أي الذين كان قربهم إلى الصراط المستقيم أكثر من بعدهم عنه ولأجل عسر الاستقامة وجب على كل عبد أن يدعو الله تعالى في كل يوم سبع عشرة مرة في قوله اهدنا الصراط المستقيم إذ وجب قراءة الفاتحة في كل ركعة فقد روي أن بعضهم رأى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في المنام فقال قد قلت يا رسول الله شيبتني هود فلم قلت ذلك فقال عليه السلام لقوله تعالى فاستقم كما أمرت فالاستقامة على سواء السبيل في غاية الغموض ولكن ينبغي أن يجتهد الإنسان في القرب من الاستقامة إن لم يقدر على
19:71.english: And for this reason, he is never free from a torment of some kind and a passage over the Fire, even if it be like the flash of lightning. God Almighty said: {«وَإِن مِّنكُمْ إِلَّا وَارِدُهَا ۚ كَانَ عَلَىٰ رَبِّكَ حَتْمًا مَّقْضِيًّا * ثُمَّ نُنَجِّي الَّذِينَ اتَّقَوا»} — "And there is none of you but will pass over it (the Fire): this is with your Lord a decree which must be accomplished. Then We shall save those who guarded against evil" (Q. 19:71-72) — that is, those whose nearness to the straight path was greater than their distance from it. And because of the difficulty of uprightness (al-istiqāmah), it became incumbent upon every servant to supplicate God Almighty seventeen times each day in His saying: {«اهْدِنَا الصِّرَاطَ الْمُسْتَقِيمَ»} — "Guide us to the straight path" (Q. 1:6) — since the recitation of the Opening Chapter (al-Fātiḥah) is obligatory in every unit of prayer (rakʿah).
19:71.section_title_en: The Revival of the Religious Sciences — Section 625: The Straight Path, Its Difficulty, and the Means of Knowing One's Own Faults
19:71.anchors:
- Root: ورد (warada)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To arrive at water, to come to a place of watering; to approach, to present oneself
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In the Quranic context of {«وَإِن مِّنكُمْ إِلَّا وَارِدُهَا»} (Q. 19:71), denotes the universal passage over the Fire — a necessary approach, not necessarily abiding therein
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (haqiqah) sense of arriving at water; here metaphorically (majaz) extended to the obligatory crossing over the Fire on the Day of Resurrection
- Root: قرب (qaruba)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Nearness in place, time, or rank; proximity
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Nearness to God is by virtue and knowledge, not by physical distance; al-qurb (nearness) is the opposite of al-buʿd (distance)
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal spatial proximity; metaphorical proximity in degree of obedience and alignment with the straight path
- Root: عيب (ʿayb)
  * Lisan / Ayn: A defect, blemish, imperfection; also curdled milk (al-ʿāʾib)
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Moral deficiency in character or action; that which renders one blameworthy
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: a blemish in a garment or vessel; metaphorical (majaz): "He is the repository (ʿaybah) of so-and-so's secrets" — i.e., the one entrusted with what is hidden; here, the inward faults of the soul
- Root: نفس (nafs)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The self, soul, spirit; breath; essence
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The soul as the locus of both blameworthy and praiseworthy traits; in {«وَنَفْسٍ وَمَا سَوَّاهَا»} (Q. 91:7), that which is inspired with its wickedness and its righteousness
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the self; metaphorical: "he poured out his nafs" meaning his blood; here, the inner self with its hidden defects
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — "فمن كانت بصيرته نافذة لم تخف عليه عيوبه" employs conditional restriction (al-sharṭ) to delimit the scope of insight; "إنما نكايتها على البدن" uses innamā for exclusive predication, restricting the harm of the scorpion's sting to the body alone

19:71.arabic: لأن الأخبار مصرحة بأن العصاة يعذبون (1) بل قوله تعالى وإن منكم إلا واردها كالصريح في أن ذلك لا بد منه للكل إذ لا يخلو مؤمن عن ذنب يرتكبه وقوله تعالى لا يصلاها إلا الأشقى الذي كذب وتولى أراد به من جماعة مخصوصين أو أراد بالأشقى شخصا معينا أيضا وقوله تعالى كلما ألقى فيها فوج سألهم خزنتها أي فوج من الكفار وتخصيص العمومات قريب ومن هذه الآية وقع للأشعري وطائفة من المتكلمين إنكار صيغ العموم وأن هذه الألفاظ يتوقف فيها إلى ظهور قرينة تدل على معناها وأما المعتزلة فشبهتهم قوله تعالى وإني لغفار لمن تاب وآمن وعمل صالحا ثم اهت
19:71.english: He was asked, "Which deed is most excellent?" The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Islam." It was then asked, "Which aspect of Islam is most excellent?" 21:22.arabic: الكفار فعمدة أدلة المتكلمين في التوحيد قوله تعالى {لو كان فيهما آلهة إلا الله لفسدتا} وفي النبوة {وإن كنتم في ريب مما نزلنا على عبدنا فأتوا بسورة من مثله} وفي البعث {قل يحييها الذي أنشأها أول مرة} إلى غير ذلك من الآيات والأدلة ولم تزل الرسل صلوات الله عليهم يحاجون المنكرين ويجادلونهم قال تعالى {وجادلهم بالتي هي أحسن} فالصحابة رضي الله عنهم أيضا كانوا يحاجون المنكرين ويجادلون ولكن عند الحاجة وكانت الحاجة إليه قليلة في زمانهم وأول من سن دعوة المبتدعة بالمجادلة إلى الحق علي ابن أبي طالب رضي الله عنه إذ بعث ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما إ
21:22.english: The mention of the proof (ḥujjah), the demand for it, and the search after it — how could these be prohibited, when God — may He be exalted — has said: {«قُلْ هَاتُوا بُرْهَانَكُمْ»} (Say: Bring forth your proof — Qur'an 2:111), and He — mighty and majestic — has said: {«لِيَهْلِكَ مَنْ هَلَكَ عَنْ بَيِّنَةٍ وَيَحْيَا مَنْ حَيَّ عَنْ بَيِّنَةٍ»} (So that he who perishes may perish upon clear evidence, and he who lives may live upon clear evidence — Qur'an 8:42), and He — may He be exalted — has said: {«هَلْ عِنْدَكُمْ مِنْ سُلْطَانٍ بِهَذَا»} (Have you any authority for this? — Qur'an 10:68), meaning a proof and demonstration, and He — may He be exalted — has said: {«قُلْ فَلِلَّهِ الْحُجَّةُ الْبَالِغَةُ»} (Say: To God belongs the conclusive proof — Qur'an 6:149), and He — may He be exalted — has said: {«أَلَمْ تَرَ إِلَى الَّذِي حَاجَّ إِبْرَاهِيمَ فِي رَبِّهِ»} (Have you not considered him who disputed with Abraham concerning his Lord? — Qur'an 2:258) up to His words: {«فَبُهِتَ الَّذِي كَفَرَ»} (So the one who disbelieved was confounded — Qur'an 2:258).
21:22.section_title_en: The Revival of the Religious Sciences — Section 77: On the Permissibility of Theological Discourse (Kalām) and Its Early Practice
21:22.anchors:
- Root: ح-د-ث (ḥ-d-th)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "Al-ḥudūth: the coming-to-be of a thing after it was not; al-ḥadath: the novel event; al-ḥīdāth: origination."
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Al-ḥudūth: a thing's becoming after it was not, whether accident or substance; iḥdāth: bringing it into existence. The origination of substances belongs to God alone."
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "Literal: 'He is a recent event among events.' Metaphorical: 'They became topics of conversation (aḥādīth).'"
- Root: ح-ا-ج (ḥ-ā-j)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "Al-ḥājah: need of a thing, with desire for it; its plural: ḥājāt and ḥawā'ij."
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Al-ḥājah ilā al-shay': poverty toward it with love of it. God said: {«إِلَّا حَاجَةً فِي نَفْسِ يَعْقُوبَ»} (except a need in Jacob's soul — Qur'an 12:68)."
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "Literal: need and want. The 'ḥājah' is that which one seeks to obtain."
- Root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "Kāna: to be, to exist; takwīn: bringing into being from non-existence."
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Al-kawn: existence after non-existence; the muḥdath (originated thing) is that brought forth after it was not."
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "Literal: being and becoming. Metaphorical: the continuous states of affairs."
- Sibawayh Rule: Al-Faṣl bayna al-Jār wa-al-Majrūr (Prepositional Interposition) — The permissibility of separating a preposition from its object when the intervening clause is complete in meaning, as in the verse's structure of argumentation where the proof (ḥujjah) stands independently before its conclusion.

21:23.arabic: العبودية مشتركون نوديت من سرادقات الجلال لا تجاوز حد الأدب فإنه لا يسئل عما يفعل وهم يسئلون ولعمري تأدب اللسان والظاهر مما يقدر عليه الأكثرون فأما تأدب السر عن إضمار الاستبعاد بهذا الاختلاف الظاهر في التقريب والإبعاد والإشقاء والإسعاد مع بقاء السعادة والشقاوة أبد الآباد فلا يقوى عليه إلا العلماء الراسخون في العلم ولهذا قال الخضر عليه السلام لما سئل عن السماع في المنام إنه الصفو الزلال الذي لا يثبت عليه إلا أقدام العلماء لأنه محرك لأسرار القلوب ومكامنها ومشوش لها تشويش السكر المدهش الذي يكاد يحل عقدة الأدب عن السر إلا ممن عصمه الله تعالى
21:23.english: Among the masters of ecstatic finding (arbāb al-wajd), there is one whom a state overwhelms like intoxicating drunkenness (sukr mudhish), so his tongue loosens with reproach (ʿitāb) toward God Almighty, and he finds objectionable (yastankiru) His overwhelming (iqtihār) of hearts and His apportioning of noble states differentially. For He is the One who elects (mustaṣfā) the hearts of the veracious (ṣiddīqīn) and distances the hearts of the deniers and the deluded (jāḥidīn wa-l-maghrūrīn). There is no preventer of what He gives, and no giver of what He withholds. He did not cut off divine success (tawfīq) from the disbelievers due to some prior transgression, nor did He extend to the Prophets, peace be upon them, His success and the light of His guidance due to some preceding means. Rather, He said: {«وَلَقَدْ سَبَقَتْ كَلِمَتُنَا لِعِبَادِنَا الْمُرْسَلِينَ»} "And Our word has already preceded for Our servants, the messengers" [Al-Ṣāffāt/171]. And He said, Mighty and Majestic: {«وَلَٰكِنْ حَقَّ الْقَوْلُ مِنِّي لَأَمْلَأَنَّ جَهَنَّمَ مِنَ الْجِنَّةِ وَالنَّاسِ أَجْمَعِينَ»} "But the word from Me has taken effect: I will surely fill Hell with jinn and people all together" [Al-Sajdah/13]. And He said, Exalted: {«إِنَّ الَّذِينَ سَبَقَتْ لَهُمْ مِنَّا الْحُسْنَىٰ أُولَٰئِكَ عَنْهَا مُبْعَدُونَ»} "Indeed, those for whom the best [reward] has preceded from Us — they are from it far removed" [Al-Anbiyāʾ/101].
21:23.section_title_en: The Peril of Listening (Samāʿ) for the Novice and the Reality of Divine Transcendence Beyond Change
21:23.anchors:
- Root: لون (L-W-N)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of color, hue, and physical appearance; also used for types and kinds.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "اللون معروف، وينطوي على الأبيض والأسود وما يركب منهما، ويقال: تلون: إذا اكتسى لوناً غير اللون الذي كان له" — indicating acquisition of a new state or attribute.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): physical coloring and change of hue. Metaphorical (Majaz): "عنده لون من الثياب: صنف منه" — a type, kind, or varying disposition; hence "mutalawwin" (متلون) as one who shifts between states and moods.
- Root: قلب (Q-L-B)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To turn over, overturn, transform, or redirect from one face to another.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "قلب الشيء: تصريفه وصرفه عن وجه إلى وجه" — the continuous turning and overturning of a thing; God as "Muqallib al-Qulūb" (Turner of hearts).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical overturning. Metaphorical: "رجل قلب حول: يقلب الأمور ويحتال" — one who manages and disposes affairs; divine action of disposing hearts.
- Root: حول (H-W-L)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Change, transformation, power, and capacity.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "أصل الحول تغير الشيء وانفصاله عن غيره" — change and separation from another state; "يحول بين المرء وقلبه" {«الأنفال/ 24»} — divine interposition between a man and his heart.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: passage of time, transformation. Metaphorical: "حال عليه الحول" — the changing of conditions; "حائل" as that which has altered.
- Root: قرب (Q-R-B)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Nearness in place, time, or rank.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "القرب والبعد يتقابلان... ويستعمل ذلك في المكان، وفي الزمان، وفي النسبة، وفي الحظوة، والرعاية، والقدرة" — including nearness in honor and station (zulfā).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical proximity. Metaphorical: "فلان يقرب أمراً لا يتسهل له" — drawing near in rank and favor; divine drawing near (taqrīb) and distancing (ibʿād).
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The permissibility of interposing elements between a preposition and its object when the meaning remains clear, paralleling how divine attributes may be qualified without compromising essential unity.
21:23.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

21:23.arabic: ولا معقب لحكمه يضل من يشاء ويهدي من يشاء لا يسئل عما يفعل وهم يسألون ويدل عليه من النقل قول الأمة قاطبة ما شاء كان وما لم يشأ لم يكن وقول الله عز وجل أن لو يشاء الله لهدى الناس جميعا وقوله تعالى ولو شئنا لآتينا كل نفس هداها ويدل عليه من جهة العقل أن المعاصي والجرائم إن كان الله يكرهها ولا يريدها وإنما هي جارية على وفق إرادة العدو إبليس لعنه الله مع أنه عدو لله سبحانه والجاري على وفق إرادة العدو أكثر من الجاري على وفق إرادته تعالى فليت شعري كيف يستجيز المسلم أن يرد ملك الجبار ذي الجلال والإكرام إلى رتبة لو ردت إل
21:23.english: As for the movement, it is a creation of the Lord — exalted is He — an attribute of the servant, and an acquisition of his. For it was created as empowered (maqdūrah) by a power that is His attribute, and the movement has a relation to another attribute called power; thus, by virtue of that relation, it is termed "acquisition." And how could it be pure compulsion (jabr maḥḍ), when he necessarily perceives the distinction between the empowered movement and the involuntary tremor (al-raʿdah al-ḍarūriyyah)? Or how could it be a creation of the servant, when he does not encompass knowledge of the details of the parts of acquired movements nor their numbers? And when both extremes are refuted, nothing remains except moderation in belief (al-iqtiṣād fī al-iʿtiqād) — namely, that it is empowered by the power of God — exalted is He — by way of origination, and by the power of the servant in another mode of attachment (taʿlīq) expressed as acquisition.
21:23.section_title_en: The Second Foundation: God's Sole Creation of Servants' Movements Does Not Negate Their Being Acquired by Servants
21:23.anchors:
- Root: قدر (q-d-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of measuring, determining, and empowering; al-Farahidi notes its application to capacity and divine decree.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "القدرة" when attributed to humans denotes a state enabling one to perform an act; when attributed to God, it negates incapacity. Absolute power belongs solely to God; for others, it is always restricted and particularized.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "هو قادر مقتدر ذو قدرة ومقدرة" — one possessing power. Metaphorical: "فرس بعيد القدر" — a horse of far-reaching stride, extending the root to scope and reach.
- Root: كسب (k-s-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Acquisition, earning, and what one gains; al-Farahidi links it to amassing and profiting.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Acquisition (al-kasb) in theological terms denotes an act's relation to the servant whereby responsibility attaches, while its origination remains divine.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: earning and gaining. Metaphorical: the theological sense of acquired act (al-faʿl al-iktisābī) — a relational attribution distinct from creation.
- Root: خلق (kh-l-q)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Measuring and smoothing; al-Farahidi notes its application to fashioning and proportioning.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الخلق أصله: التقدير المستقيم" — origination from nothing (ibdāʿ) or from something, always upon a measured determination.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: measuring before cutting. Metaphorical: "خلق الله الخلق: أوجده على تقدير أوجبته الحكمة" — God's creation is bringing into existence upon a measure required by wisdom.
- Root: وجب (w-j-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Being due, necessary, or obligatory; al-Farahidi notes its legal and ontological senses.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الوجوب: الثبوت" — necessary being is that whose non-existence entails an impossibility; obligation is that whose omission warrants blame.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "وجب البيع" — the sale became binding. Metaphorical: "هو يأكل الوجبة" — eating once daily, extending to fixed determination.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد (Restriction and Specification) — The particle "إنما" restricts predication, as in "إنما هو إله واحد," confining the attribute to its subject and negating it from others. This governs the Ashʿarī restriction of creative power to God alone while affirming acquired power for servants through a distinct relational mode.
21:23.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'Foundations of Belief'

21:23.arabic: فإنه لا يسأل عما يفعل وهم يسألون وليت شعري بما يجيب المعتزلي في قوله إن الأصلح واجب عليه في مسألة نعرضها عليه وهو أن يفرض مناظرة في الآخرة بين صبي وبين بالغ ماتا مسلمين فإن الله سبحانه يزيد في درجات البالغ ويفضله على الصبي لأنه تعب بالإيمان والطاعات بعد البلوغ ويجب عليه ذلك عند المعتزلي فلو قال الصبي يا رب لم رفعت منزلته علي فيقول لأنه بلغ واجتهد في الطاعات ويقول الصبي أنت أمتني في الصبا فكان يجب عليك أن تديم حياتي حتى أبلغ فأجتهد فقد عدلت عن العدل في التفضل عليه بطول العمر ل
21:23.english: **The Fifth Principle**: It is permissible for God—glorified be He—to charge His creatures with what they cannot bear (mā lā yuṭīqūnahu), contrary to the Muʿtazilites. For were that not permissible, then the petition to avert it would be impossible—yet they have petitioned it, saying: {«Rabbanā wa lā tuḥammilnā mā lā ṭāqata lanā bih»} "Our Lord, do not burden us with what we have no capacity for" {Q. 2:286}. And because God—exalted be He—informed His Prophet (peace be upon him) that Abū Jahl would not believe him, then commanded him to command Abū Jahl to believe him in all his statements. Now among Abū Jahl's statements was that he would not believe him—so how could he believe him in [the statement] that he would not believe him? Is this anything other than the impossible in its very existence?
21:23.section_title_en: The Fifth and Sixth Principles: On the Impossibility of Obligation Upon God and the Permissibility of What Reason Deems Impossible
21:23.anchors:
- Root: وجب (w-j-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of "being established, fixed, and necessary"; al-Kitab al-Ayn notes its application to ritual obligations (wujūb al-iḥrām).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Al-wujūb is thubūt (establishment). The wājib is said in two senses: (1) in contrast to the possible—that whose non-existence entails a contradiction; (2) that whose omission merits blame—either by reason (as knowing God's unity) or by revelation (as ritual duties)."
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "Wajaba lī ʿalayhi kadhā" (such is incumbent upon him); "awjabahu ʿalā nafsihi" (he made it incumbent upon himself). Metaphorical: "huwa ya'kulu al-wajbah" (he eats but once a day)—the root shifts from legal necessity to a single, fixed act.
- Root: ملك (m-l-k)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Sovereignty and possession; al-Kitab al-Ayn distinguishes mālik (owner) from malik (king), both deriving from absolute discretionary disposal.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Al-mulk: one who disposes by command and prohibition over a community—this pertains to governance of rational beings. Ownership (milk) is of two kinds: possession itself, and the power to dispose."
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "Malaktu al-shay'" (I possessed the thing). Metaphorical: "Malaktu nafsī ʿinda al-ghaḍab" (I mastered myself at anger)—dominion over one's own domain.
- Sibawayh Rule: Interposition of the conditional clause (al-sharṭ) between subject and predicate—governing the logical structure of "if X were permissible, then Y would follow," where the protasis restricts the apodosis.
21:23.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'Foundations of Belief'

21:47.arabic: ما بأنفسهم إن الله لا يظلم مثقال ذرة وإن تك حسنة يضاعفها وإن كان مثقال حبة من خردل أتينا بها وكفى بنا حاسبين فمن كان حبه في الدنيا رجاءه لنعيم الجنة والحور العين والقصور مكن من الجنة ليتبوأ منها حيث يشاء فيلعب مع الولدان ويتمتع بالنسوان فهناك تنتهي لذته في الآخرة لأنه إنما يعطى كل إنسان في المحبة ما تشتهيه نفسه وتلذ عينه ومن كان مقصده رب الدار ومالك الملك ولم يغلب عليه إلا حبه بالإخلاص والصدق أنزل في مقعد
21:47.english:
...twenty years.
And al-Junayd said: "The mark of the lover is the constancy of vigor and cheerfulness with a passion that wearies his body but does not weary his heart."
And some of them said: "Labor borne out of love — languor does not enter into it."
And one of the scholars said: "By God, no lover of God is ever fully quenched by His obedience, even if he were to attain to the most immense of means."
All of this and its like is found in observable experience, for the passionate lover does not find burdensome the pursuit of his beloved's desire, and he savors with his heart the service of the beloved even if it is arduous upon his body. And whenever his body falls short, the dearest of things to him is that his capacity should return to him and that incapacity should depart from him, so that he may occupy himself with it. Such, likewise, is the love of God the Exalted — for every love that becomes dominant inevitably subdues whatever is beneath it. So whoever's beloved is dearer to him than his sloth abandons sloth in serving him; and if the beloved is dearer to him than his wealth, he spends his wealth in his love.
And it was said to one of the lovers — who had expended his very self and his wealth until nothing remained to him — "What was the cause of your state in love?" He said: "One day I heard a lover who had secluded himself with his beloved, saying: 'By God, I love you with my whole heart, while you turn away from me with your whole face.' The beloved said to him: 'If you truly love me, what will you spend upon me?' He said: 'O my master, I put you in possession of all that I own, and then I spend upon you my very spirit until it is destroyed.'" So I said: "This is a creature loving a creature, and a slave loving a slave — how then with slaves loving the Worshipped One?" All of this is by His cause.
And among them is that he be compassionate toward all of God's servants, merciful to them, and severe against all of God's enemies — and against everyone who commits something of what God dislikes — as God the Exalted said: {«أشداء على الكفار رحماء بينهم»} "Harsh against the disbelievers, merciful among themselves." No reproach of any reproacher seizes him, and no diverting force turns him from wrath for God's sake. With this God described His friends, saying: "Those who are enamored with My love as a child is enamored with a thing, and who take refuge in My remembrance as the eagle takes refuge in its nest, and who rage for the sake of My sanctities as the leopard rages when provoked — for then he cares not whether the people are few or many."
So consider this example: the child, when enamored with a thing, does not part from it at all; if it is taken from him, he has no occupation but weeping and crying out until it is returned to him. If he sleeps, he takes it with him into his clothes; when he awakens, he returns and clings to it. Whenever he is parted from it, he weeps; whenever he finds it, he laughs. Whoever contends with him over it, he hates; whoever gives it to him, he loves. As for the leopard, he does not master himself at the moment of rage, until he reaches such a pitch of fury that he destroys himself. These, then, are the marks of love. Whoever's marks are perfected in him, his love is perfected and his affection is purified — so in the Hereafter his drink is clear and his draught is sweet.
But whoever's love is mingled with the love of other than God, he delights in the Hereafter in proportion to his love, for his drink is mingled with a measure of the drink of the Near Ones (al-muqarrabūn), as God the Exalted said concerning the righteous (al-abrār): {«إن الأبرار لفي نعيم»} "Verily the righteous are in bliss," {ثم قال} then He said: {«يسقون من رحيق مختوم * ختامه مسك وفي ذلك فليتنافس المتنافسون * ومزاجه من تسنيم * عينا يشرب بها المقربون»} "They are given to drink of sealed nectar, whose seal is musk — and in that let the competitors compete — and its mixture is of tasnīm, a spring from which the Near Ones drink." So when the drink of the righteous is sweetened by the admixture of the pure drink which belongs to the Near Ones...
And "drink" is an expression for the totality of the bliss of the Gardens, just as the Book expressed by it all deeds, for He said: {«إن كتاب الأبرار لفي عليين»} "Verily the book of the righteous is in 'Illiyyūn," {ثم قال} then He said: {«يشهده المقربون»} "The Near Ones bear witness to it." So it was a sign of the loftiness of their book that it ascended to where the Near Ones bear witness to it. And just as the righteous find increase in their state and their knowledge by their proximity to the Near Ones and their beholding of them, so likewise is their state in the Hereafter — {«ما خلقكم ولا بعثكم إلا كنفس واحدة»} "Your creation and your resurrection are but as a single soul," just as He said — as we began the first creation, We shall repeat it — and as the Exalted said: {«جزاء وفاقا»} "A recompense fully matching" — that is, the recompense matched their deeds. So the pure was met with the unmixed of the drink, and the mingled was met with the mingled.
And the admixture of every drink is in proportion to what preceded of admixture in his love and his deeds. For {«من يعمل مثقال ذرة خيرا يره * ومن يعمل مثقال ذرة شرا يره»} "Whoever does an atom's weight of good shall see it, and whoever does an atom's weight of evil shall see it." And {«إن الله لا يغير ما بقوم حتى يغيروا ما بأنفسهم * إن الله لا يظلم مثقال ذرة وإن تك حسنة يضاعفها وإن كان مثقال حبة من خردل أتينا بها وكفى بنا حاسبين»} "Verily God does not change what is in a people until they change what is in themselves. Verily God does not wrong an atom's weight; and if it be a good deed, He multiplies it, and if it be a grain of mustard-seed, We bring it — and sufficient are We as reckoners."
So whoever's love in this world was his hope for the bliss of the Garden, the wide-eyed houris, and the palaces — he is granted the Garden to settle therein wherever he wishes, to sport with the immortal youths and take pleasure with the women. There his delight in the Hereafter reaches its end, because every man is given in love only what his soul desires and his eye delights in.
But whoever's aim was the Lord of the Abode and the Owner of the Kingdom, and nothing overcame him save His love with sincerity and truthfulness — he is lodged in the seat...
21:47.section_title_en: The Marks of True Love and the Degrees of the Hereafter
21:47.anchors:
- Root: نشط (n-sh-ṭ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of vitality, energy, and alacrity in action.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Activity of the soul (nafs) in pursuing what it loves, unflagging in its ardor.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: bodily vigor; Metaphorical: the heart's persistent zeal that overrides physical exhaustion.
- Root: شرب (sh-r-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Drinking; the act of imbibing liquids.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In Quranic usage, a metaphor (majaz) for the soul's reception of spiritual bliss and states.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical quenching; Metaphorical: the tasting of paradisiacal delight, graded by purity (safā') versus admixture (shawb).
- Root: صفو (ṣ-f-w)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Purity, clarity, and freedom from turbidity or mixture.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The unalloyed state of sincere love (mahabbah) and its corresponding reward.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: clear liquid; Metaphorical: the soul's exclusive devotion to God, yielding unmixed bliss.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — Used to delimit the final reward strictly by the object and purity of one's love, as in "إنما يعطى كل إنسان في المحبة ما تشتهيه نفسه."
21:47.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Love, Longing, Intimacy and Contentment'

21:47.arabic: أما بعد فقد قال الله تعالى {ونضع الموازين القسط ليوم القيامة فلا تظلم نفس شيئا وإن كان مثقال حبة من خردل أتينا بها وكفى بنا حاسبين} وقال تعالى {ووضع الكتاب فترى المجرمين مشفقين مما فيه ويقولون يا ويلتنا ما لهذا الكتاب لا يغادر صغيرة ولا كبيرة إلا أحصاها ووجدوا ما عملوا حاضرا ولا يظلم ربك أحدا} وقال تعالى {يوم يبعثهم الله جميعا فينبئهم بما عملوا أحصاه الله ونسوه والله على كل شيء شهيد} وقال تعالى {يومئذ يصدر الناس أشتاتا ليروا أعمالهم فمن يعمل مثقال ذرة خيرا يره ومن يعمل مثقال ذرة شرا يره} وقال تعالى {ثم توفى كل نفس ما كسبت وهم لا يظلمون} وقال تعالى {يوم تجد كل نفس ما عملت من خي
21:47.english: To proceed: God Most High has said: {And We shall set up the scales of justice for the Day of Resurrection, so no soul shall be wronged in anything; and if it be the weight of a grain of mustard seed, We shall bring it forth, and sufficient are We as Reckoners} (21:47). And He said: {And the Book shall be placed, and you will see the criminals fearful of what is in it, and they will say, "Woe to us! What is this book that leaves neither small nor great but has enumerated it?" And they will find what they did present, and your Lord wrongs no one} (18:49). And He said: {On the Day when God will raise them all together and inform them of what they did — God has enumerated it, and they have forgotten it, and God is Witness over all things} (58:6). And He said: {On that Day, people will issue forth in scattered groups to be shown their deeds. So whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it, and whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it} (99:6-8). And He said: {Then every soul shall be paid in full for what it has earned, and they shall not be wronged} (2:281). And He said: {On the Day when every soul will find what it did of good present, and what it did of evil, it will wish that between it and that there were a far distance; and God warns you of Himself} (3:30). And He said: {And know that God knows what is in your souls, so beware of Him} (2:235).
21:47.section_title_en: Exposition of the Reality of Truthfulness (Al-Sidq), Its Meaning, and Its Grades — Book of Vigilance and Self-Reckoning, Being the Eighth Book of the Quarter of Deliverance from the Revival of the Religious Sciences
21:47.anchors:
- Root: رقب (Raqaba)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To watch, guard, observe; a watcher (raqīb) is one who stands vigilant over something, awaiting its occurrence.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Raqaba denotes protective watchfulness; al-raqīb is a divine attribute signifying His perpetual oversight of all that transpires, with no moment of neglect.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (haqīqah): physical watching/awaiting. Metaphorical (majāz): "This matter is upon your necks (fī riqābikum)" — i.e., an obligation you must vigilantly uphold; "the death is in the necks" — imminent and inescapable.
- Root: حسب (Hasaba)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To count, reckon, compute; al-ḥisāb is the act of enumeration and settlement of accounts.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-ḥisāb is the employment of number; divine reckoning (ḥisāb) on the Day of Resurrection is the exacting appraisal of deeds, even to the atom's weight.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: counting wealth or deeds. Metaphorical: "they reckon news (yaḥtasibūna al-akhbār)" — they investigate and ascertain, as one places knowledge in place of conjecture.
- Root: قلب (Qalaba)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To turn, overturn, transform; the heart (qalb) is so named for its constant fluctuation and turning of states.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Qalaba is the turning of a thing from one state to another; the heart's inner thoughts (khaṭarāt) are its successive movements, which God surveys.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: turning a garment or object. Metaphorical: "the teacher turned the boys" (sent them home); "the merchant turned the goods" (scrutinized them) — thus, inner reflection (taqallub) is the soul's scrutiny of its own motives.
- Sibawayh Rule: Restriction and Focused Predication (al-ḥaṣr wa al-taqyīd bi-innamā) — The particle innamā restricts the predicate to the subject alone, as in "إنما يحاسبهم لتعلم كل نفس" — the sole purpose of reckoning is specified, excluding all other ends.
21:47.topic: Al-Ghazali on the journey of the soul, death, and the Hereafter, from 'Monitoring and Accounting'

21:47.arabic: الأصل الرابع الميزان وهو حق قال الله تعالى ونضع الموازين القسط ليوم القيامة وقال تعالى فمن ثقلت موازينه فأولئك هم المفلحون ومن خفت موازينه الآية ووجهها أن الله تعالى يحدث في صحائف الأعمال وزنا بحسب درجات الأعمال عند الله تعالى فتصير مقادير أعمال العباد معلومة للعباد حتى يظهر لهم العدل في العقاب أو الفضل في العفو وتضعيف الثواب الأصل الخامس الصراط وهو جسر ممدود على متن جهنم أرق من الشعرة وأحد من السيف قال الله تعالى فاهدوهم إلى صراط الجحيم وقفوهم إنهم مسئولون وهذا ممكن فيجب التصديق به فإن القادر على أن يطي
21:47.english: For they, despite their distinction in eloquence and rhetorical perfection, aimed at reviling him, forbidding him, killing him, and expelling him — as God, Mighty and Majestic, informed us about them — yet they were unable to produce anything to rival the Qur'an. For it was not within the capacity of human beings to combine the grandeur of the Qur'an's diction with its harmonious order, especially given what it contains of the accounts of the ancients, while he was illiterate, never having practiced the study of books — and [given] its announcement of the unseen in matters whose truthfulness was verified in the future, such as His saying, Exalted is He: {«لَتَدْخُلُنَّ الْمَسْجِدَ الْحَرَامَ إِنْ شَاءَ اللَّهُ آمِنِينَ مُحَلِّقِينَ رُءُوسَكُمْ وَمُقَصِّرِينَ»} (You shall surely enter the Sacred Mosque, if God wills, secure, with your heads shaved and cut short) [Al-Fatḥ 48:27], and such as His saying: {«الم غُلِبَتِ الرُّومُ فِي أَدْنَى الْأَرْضِ وَهُمْ مِنْ بَعْدِ غَلَبِهِمْ سَيَغْلِبُونَ فِي بِضْعِ سِنِينَ»} (Alif Lām Mīm. The Romans have been defeated in the nearest land, and they, after their defeat, shall be victorious within a few years) [Al-Rūm 30:1-3].
21:47.section_title_en: The Fourth Pillar: On Matters of Hearing (al-Samʿiyyāt) and the Verification of the Prophet ﷺ in What He Reported — Comprising Ten Fundamental Principles
21:47.anchors:
- Root: حشر (ḥ-sh-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To gather, assemble, drive together; al-ḥashr is the gathering of creation on the Day of Resurrection.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-ḥashr is the bringing together of a people from their various places of dispersal; it is used specifically for the resurrection gathering.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) for driving cattle together; metaphorical (majāz) for the ingathering of souls for judgment.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Conditional Protasis (al-sharṭ) — "If you are truthful, then rise..." (fa-in kunta ṣādiqan fa-qum...) — the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) functions as the proof of the protasis, establishing necessary knowledge (ʿilm ḍarūrī).

- Root: نشر (n-sh-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To spread, unfold, revive after death; al-nushūr is the revivification of the dead.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-nashr is the spreading of the soul back into the body after death; it is the opposite of al-ṭayy (folding up).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal for unfolding a garment; metaphorical for the resurrection when the earth "spreads forth" what it contains.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Coordination (al-ʿaṭf) — "al-ḥashr wa-l-nashr" (the gathering and the spreading) — two coordinated nouns forming a single compound concept of resurrection.

- Root: مكن (m-k-n)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To establish, empower, give firm footing; makkana means to make something firm and stable.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-makān is the place that contains a thing; tamakkun is the firm establishment of a thing in its place.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal for physical placement; metaphorical for divine power — "God is able" (qādir) means He has full capacity and authority over all things.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Possibility (al-imkān) — "that is possible" (dhālika mumkin) — the predicate of possibility is established by the absence of logical contradiction, not by empirical observation.

- Root: عذب (ʿ-dh-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Sweet, pleasant (of water); al-ʿadhāb is the punishment that is "sweet" to the inflictor but bitter to the recipient — used predominantly for divine chastisement.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-ʿadhāb is the infliction of pain that deters; it is specifically the painful consequence of disobedience.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal for sweet water; metaphorical (majāz) for punishment that is "appointed" as a deterrent.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Exception (al-istithnāʾ) — "except as God wills" (illā mā shāʾa) — the exception clause restricts the scope of human perception, not divine action.
21:47.topic: Al-Ghazali on the journey of the soul, death, and the Hereafter, from 'Foundations of Belief'

21:47.arabic: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لا يدخل الجنة من كان في قلبه مثقال حبة من خردل من كبر ولا يدخل الجنة من كان في قلبه مثقال حبة من خردل من إيمان (1) حديث أبي هريرة يقول الله تعالى الكبرياء ردائي والعظمة إزاري فمن نازعني واحدا منهما ألقيته في جهنم أخرجه مسلم وأبو داود وابن ماجه واللفظ له وقال أبو داود قذفته في النار وقال مسلم عذبته وقال رداؤه وإزاره بالغيبة وزاد مع أبي هريرة أبا سعيد أيضا وعن أبي سلمة بن عبد الرحمن قال التقى عبد الله بن عمرو وعبد الله بن عمر على الصفا فتواقفا فمضى ابن عمرو وأقام ابن عمر يبكي فقالوا ما يب
21:47.english: To proceed: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said — God, exalted be He, said: "Pride (al-kibriyāʾ) is My cloak, and greatness (al-ʿaẓamah) is My wrapper; whoever contends with Me over either of them, I crush him." {«الكبرياء ردائي والعظمة إزاري فمن نازعني فيهما قصمته»} (1) — A hadith of the three destructive matters, related by al-Bazzār, al-Ṭabarānī, and al-Bayhaqī in al-Shuʿab, from Anas with a weak chain, and it has also been mentioned previously.
21:47.section_title_en: The Book of Condemnation of Pride and Self-Admiration — Being the Ninth Book of the Quarter of Destructive Matters from The Revival of the Religious Sciences
21:47.anchors:
- Root: كبر (k-b-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root denotes magnitude, whether physical size, age, or rank; "al-kibriyā'" is the supreme majesty exclusive to God.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "al-kabīr wa al-ṣaghīr" are relative terms; used for quantity, quality, and dignity. "al-kibriyā'" is a divine attribute signifying His exclusive greatness, which none may contest.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): "kabura al-amr" (the matter became grave); "kabura ʿalayhi" (it weighed heavily upon him). Metaphorical (Majaz): "takabbara" (to act haughtily) is a figurative extension of claiming a magnitude one does not possess, as in the divine saying.
- Root: عجب (ʿ-j-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Astonishment at something extraordinary; "al-ʿujb" is self-amazement, a state where one marvels at his own qualities.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Astonishment arises from ignorance of the true cause; self-admiration (ʿujb) blinds one to one's own defects and to the divine origin of all good.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "ʿajiba minhu" (he marveled at it). Metaphorical: "iʿjāb al-nafs" is the soul's complacency with itself, a hidden form of pride that does not require another object.
- Root: هلك (h-l-k)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Perishing, destruction, ruin; "al-muhlikāt" are the things that cause perdition.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Destruction is of three kinds: loss, corruption, and death. Here it is spiritual perdition — the ruin of the soul's eternal felicity.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical ruin. Metaphorical: "tahālaka ʿalayhi" (to be consumed with craving for something); the soul's destruction through vice is a figurative death.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Apposition and Parenthetical Clauses (al-badal wa al-iʿtirāḍ) — The opening doxology employs extended appositional chains (badal) and parenthetical invocations that delay the main clause, requiring the translator to preserve the periodic structure without collapsing the theological weight of each divine epithet.
21:47.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'Foundations of Belief'

21:101.arabic: جهنم من الجنة والناس أجمعين وقال تعالى إن الذين سبقت لهم منا الحسنى أولئك عنها مبعدون فإن خطر ببالك أنه لم اختلفت السابقة وهم في ربقه العبودية مشتركون نوديت من سرادقات الجلال لا تجاوز حد الأدب فإنه لا يسئل عما يفعل وهم يسئلون ولعمري تأدب اللسان والظاهر مما يقدر عليه الأكثرون فأما تأدب السر عن إضمار الاستبعاد بهذا الاختلاف الظاهر في التقريب والإبعاد والإشقاء والإسعاد مع بقاء السعادة والشقاوة أبد الآباد فلا يقوى عليه إلا العلماء الراسخون في العلم ولهذا قال الخضر عليه السلام لما سئل عن السماع في المنام إنه الصفو الزلال الذي لا يثبت عليه إ
21:101.english: Among the masters of ecstatic finding (arbāb al-wajd), there is one whom a state overwhelms like intoxicating drunkenness (sukr mudhish), so his tongue loosens with reproach (ʿitāb) toward God Almighty, and he finds objectionable (yastankiru) His overwhelming (iqtihār) of hearts and His apportioning of noble states differentially. For He is the One who elects (mustaṣfā) the hearts of the veracious (ṣiddīqīn) and distances the hearts of the deniers and the deluded (jāḥidīn wa-l-maghrūrīn). There is no preventer of what He gives, and no giver of what He withholds. He did not cut off divine success (tawfīq) from the disbelievers due to some prior transgression, nor did He extend to the Prophets, peace be upon them, His success and the light of His guidance due to some preceding means. Rather, He said: {«وَلَقَدْ سَبَقَتْ كَلِمَتُنَا لِعِبَادِنَا الْمُرْسَلِينَ»} "And Our word has already preceded for Our servants, the messengers" [Al-Ṣāffāt/171]. And He said, Mighty and Majestic: {«وَلَٰكِنْ حَقَّ الْقَوْلُ مِنِّي لَأَمْلَأَنَّ جَهَنَّمَ مِنَ الْجِنَّةِ وَالنَّاسِ أَجْمَعِينَ»} "But the word from Me has taken effect: I will surely fill Hell with jinn and people all together" [Al-Sajdah/13]. And He said, Exalted: {«إِنَّ الَّذِينَ سَبَقَتْ لَهُمْ مِنَّا الْحُسْنَىٰ أُولَٰئِكَ عَنْهَا مُبْعَدُونَ»} "Indeed, those for whom the best [reward] has preceded from Us — they are from it far removed" [Al-Anbiyāʾ/101].
21:101.section_title_en: The Peril of Listening (Samāʿ) for the Novice and the Reality of Divine Transcendence Beyond Change
21:101.anchors:
- Root: لون (L-W-N)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of color, hue, and physical appearance; also used for types and kinds.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "اللون معروف، وينطوي على الأبيض والأسود وما يركب منهما، ويقال: تلون: إذا اكتسى لوناً غير اللون الذي كان له" — indicating acquisition of a new state or attribute.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): physical coloring and change of hue. Metaphorical (Majaz): "عنده لون من الثياب: صنف منه" — a type, kind, or varying disposition; hence "mutalawwin" (متلون) as one who shifts between states and moods.
- Root: قلب (Q-L-B)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To turn over, overturn, transform, or redirect from one face to another.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "قلب الشيء: تصريفه وصرفه عن وجه إلى وجه" — the continuous turning and overturning of a thing; God as "Muqallib al-Qulūb" (Turner of hearts).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical overturning. Metaphorical: "رجل قلب حول: يقلب الأمور ويحتال" — one who manages and disposes affairs; divine action of disposing hearts.
- Root: حول (H-W-L)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Change, transformation, power, and capacity.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "أصل الحول تغير الشيء وانفصاله عن غيره" — change and separation from another state; "يحول بين المرء وقلبه" {«الأنفال/ 24»} — divine interposition between a man and his heart.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: passage of time, transformation. Metaphorical: "حال عليه الحول" — the changing of conditions; "حائل" as that which has altered.
- Root: قرب (Q-R-B)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Nearness in place, time, or rank.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "القرب والبعد يتقابلان... ويستعمل ذلك في المكان، وفي الزمان، وفي النسبة، وفي الحظوة، والرعاية، والقدرة" — including nearness in honor and station (zulfā).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical proximity. Metaphorical: "فلان يقرب أمراً لا يتسهل له" — drawing near in rank and favor; divine drawing near (taqrīb) and distancing (ibʿād).
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The permissibility of interposing elements between a preposition and its object when the meaning remains clear, paralleling how divine attributes may be qualified without compromising essential unity.
21:101.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'Audition and Ecstasy'

21:101.arabic: يدري أنه من الذين سبقت لهم من الله الحسنى وقيل في معنى قوله تعالى {وجاءت سكرة الموت بالحق} أي بالسابقة يعني أظهرتها وقال بعض السلف إنما يوزن من الأعمال خواتيمها وكان أبو الدرداء رضي الله عنه يحلف بالله ما من أحد يأمن أن يسلب إيمانه إلا سلبه وقيل من الذنوب ذنوب عقوبتها سوء الخاتمة نعوذ بالله من ذلك وقيل هي عقوبات دعوى الولاية والكرامة بالافتراء وقال بعض العارفين لو عرضت علي الشهادة عند باب الدار والموت على التوحيد
21:101.english: ...doubt concerning this truthfulness. Likewise, God Most High said: {«But righteousness is he who believes in God and the Last Day and the angels and the Book and the prophets»} (2:177) — thus He conditioned twenty attributes, such as faithfulness to covenant and patience under hardship. Then He said Most High: {«Those are the truthful ones»} (2:177). And God Most High said: {«God will raise those who have believed among you and those who have been given knowledge, by degrees»} (58:11). And He said Most High: {«Not equal among you are those who spent before the conquest and fought»} (57:10). And He said Most High: {«They are degrees before God»} (3:163). And the Prophet, peace be upon him, said: "Faith is naked, and its garment is God-consciousness (al-taqwā)." And the Prophet, peace be upon him, said: "Faith has seventy-some branches; the lowest of them is removing harm from the path." All this indicates the interconnection of the perfection of faith with works.
21:101.section_title_en: The Revival of the Religious Sciences — Book of the Secrets of Zakāh, Section 104: On the Degrees of Faith and Its Connection to Works, and the Hidden Hypocrisy (al-Nifāq al-Khafī) That Contradicts the Perfection of Faith
21:101.anchors:
- Root: ن ف ق (N-F-Q)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Root denotes passing away, depletion, and expenditure; also the underground burrow of the jerboa (nāfiqāʾ) with a concealed exit — the etymological basis for hypocrisy as a hidden exit from faith.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "نفق الشيء: مضى ونفد" — theological nuance: hypocrisy (nifāq) is that which causes faith to expire and pass away, whether by sale (worldly gain) or by death (spiritual ruin).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "نفقت الدراهم" (coins ran out). Metaphorical: "نفق روحه: خرج" (his soul expired and went forth) — hence the hypocrite's faith is one whose spirit has already departed.
- Root: أ ي م (A-Y-M)
  * Lisan / Ayn: A woman without a husband; a man long unmarried. Al-Raghib: "الحرب مأيمة" — war makes women widows.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "تركوا النساء أيامى" (they left women widowed). Metaphorical application: the one who feels secure from hypocrisy is like one who claims immunity from widowhood — a false security.
- Root: و ف ي (W-F-Y)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Fullness, completion, fulfillment of a measure or covenant.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الوافي: الذي بلغ التمام" — the one who has reached completion. "أوفى: إذا تمم العهد ولم ينقض حفظه" — to fulfill the covenant without breach.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "درهم واف" (a full-weight dirham). Metaphorical: "أوفى على المائة" (he surpassed a hundred) — faith's perfection (wafāʾ) is only attained by surpassing mere profession to include works and inward sincerity.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد (Restriction & Focused Predication) — governing the grammatical force of "إنما" constructions and conditional clauses (من كان...), where the predicate is restricted to the condition stated, as in the hadith "أربع من كن فيه فهو منافق خالص" — the four traits are exhaustive of the ruling.
21:101.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'Foundations of Belief'

21:101.arabic: اللهم إن أنت أمرضتني لتقبض روحي في مرضي هذا فاجعل روحي في أرواح من سبقت لهم منك الحسنى وباعدني من النار كما باعدت أولياءك الذين سبقت لهم منك الحسنى (1) وروي أنه قال صلى الله عليه وسلم عيادة المريض بعد ثلاث فواق ناقة (2) وقال طاوس أفضل العيادة أخفها وقال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما عيادة المريض مرة سنة فما ازدادت فنافلة وقال بعضهم عيادة المريض بعد ثلاث وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم أغبوا في العيادة وأربعوا فيها (3) وجملة أدب المريض حسن الصبر وقلة الشكوى والضجر والفزع إلى الدعاء والتوكل بعد الدواء على خالق الدواء ومنها أن
21:101.english: A man defended him, and the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: "Whoever defends the honor of his brother shall have it as a shield for him against the Fire." (1)
21:101.anchors:
- Root: رد (r-d-d)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To return, repel, defend, avert; al-radd ʿan al-ʿirḍ is to repel defamation from one's honor
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Defense against false accusation; the theological nuance of divine recompense (al-mukāfaʾah) for defending a brother's honor
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal repulsion of physical harm extended metaphorically to verbal defense of honor (ḥaqīqah vs. majāz)
- Root: عطس (ʿ-t-s)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Sneezing; al-tashmīt is the invocation of mercy upon the sneezer
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The sneeze is attributed to God (min Allāh) as a sign of divine favor, while yawning is attributed to Satan
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): The response "yarḥamukallāh" is a supplication, not an assertion — distinguishing literal invocation from mere congratulation
- Root: عاد (ʿ-w-d)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To visit repeatedly; al-ʿiyādah is the visitation of the sick
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Returning to someone in his affliction; the reward is measured by the intensity of compassion shown
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): The "return" (ʿawd) is literal in visitation, but the reward is spiritual — a metaphorical extension of recompense
- Root: شيع (sh-y-ʿ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To accompany, follow; al-tashyīʿ is the funeral procession
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Following the bier with the intention of honoring the deceased and taking admonition (al-iʿtibār)
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): The qīrāṭ is a measure of reward — metaphorical weight, not literal coin
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Conditional Protasis (Bāb al-sharṭ) — The construction "man ... fa-..." (whoever does X, then Y) establishes a causal nexus requiring the apodosis to be a new sentence, often carrying the force of divine decree.

21:101.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Duties of Brotherhood'

21:101.arabic: سبقت لهم منك الحسنى وباعدني من النار كما باعدت أولياءك الذين سبقت لهم منك الحسنى (1) وروي أنه قال صلى الله عليه وسلم عيادة المريض بعد ثلاث فواق ناقة (2) وقال طاوس أفضل العيادة أخفها وقال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما عيادة المريض مرة سنة فما ازدادت فنافلة وقال بعضهم عيادة المريض بعد ثلاث وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم أغبوا في العيادة وأربعوا فيها (3) وجملة أدب المريض حسن الصبر وقلة الشكوى والضجر والفزع إلى الدعاء والتوكل بعد الدواء على خالق الدواء ومنها أن يشيع جنائزهم قال صلى الله عليه وسلم من شيع جنازة فله قيراط
21:101.english: A man defended him, and the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: "Whoever defends the honor of his brother shall have it as a shield for him against the Fire." (1)

  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Defense against false accusation; the theological nuance of divine recompense (al-mukāfaʾah) for defending a brother's honor
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal repulsion of physical harm extended metaphorically to verbal defense of honor (ḥaqīqah vs. majāz)
- Root: عطس (ʿ-t-s)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Sneezing; al-tashmīt is the invocation of mercy upon the sneezer
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The sneeze is attributed to God (min Allāh) as a sign of divine favor, while yawning is attributed to Satan
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): The response "yarḥamukallāh" is a supplication, not an assertion — distinguishing literal invocation from mere congratulation
- Root: عاد (ʿ-w-d)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To visit repeatedly; al-ʿiyādah is the visitation of the sick
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Returning to someone in his affliction; the reward is measured by the intensity of compassion shown
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): The "return" (ʿawd) is literal in visitation, but the reward is spiritual — a metaphorical extension of recompense
- Root: شيع (sh-y-ʿ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To accompany, follow; al-tashyīʿ is the funeral procession
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Following the bier with the intention of honoring the deceased and taking admonition (al-iʿtibār)
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): The qīrāṭ is a measure of reward — metaphorical weight, not literal coin
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Conditional Protasis (Bāb al-sharṭ) — The construction "man ... fa-..." (whoever does X, then Y) establishes a causal nexus requiring the apodosis to be a new sentence, often carrying the force of divine decree.

23:102.arabic: القيامة وقال تعالى فمن ثقلت موازينه فأولئك هم المفلحون ومن خفت موازينه الآية ووجهها أن الله تعالى يحدث في صحائف الأعمال وزنا بحسب درجات الأعمال عند الله تعالى فتصير مقادير أعمال العباد معلومة للعباد حتى يظهر لهم العدل في العقاب أو الفضل في العفو وتضعيف الثواب الأصل الخامس الصراط وهو جسر ممدود على متن جهنم أرق من الشعرة وأحد من السيف قال الله تعالى فاهدوهم إلى صراط الجحيم وقفوهم إنهم مسئولون وهذا ممكن فيجب التصديق به فإن القادر على أن يطير الطير في الهواء قادر على أن يسير الإنسان على الصراط الأصل السا
23:102.english: For they, despite their distinction in eloquence and rhetorical perfection, aimed at reviling him, forbidding him, killing him, and expelling him — as God, Mighty and Majestic, informed us about them — yet they were unable to produce anything to rival the Qur'an. For it was not within the capacity of human beings to combine the grandeur of the Qur'an's diction with its harmonious order, especially given what it contains of the accounts of the ancients, while he was illiterate, never having practiced the study of books — and [given] its announcement of the unseen in matters whose truthfulness was verified in the future, such as His saying, Exalted is He: {«لَتَدْخُلُنَّ الْمَسْجِدَ الْحَرَامَ إِنْ شَاءَ اللَّهُ آمِنِينَ مُحَلِّقِينَ رُءُوسَكُمْ وَمُقَصِّرِينَ»} (You shall surely enter the Sacred Mosque, if God wills, secure, with your heads shaved and cut short) [Al-Fatḥ 48:27], and such as His saying: {«الم غُلِبَتِ الرُّومُ فِي أَدْنَى الْأَرْضِ وَهُمْ مِنْ بَعْدِ غَلَبِهِمْ سَيَغْلِبُونَ فِي بِضْعِ سِنِينَ»} (Alif Lām Mīm. The Romans have been defeated in the nearest land, and they, after their defeat, shall be victorious within a few years) [Al-Rūm 30:1-3].
23:102.section_title_en: The Fourth Pillar: On Matters of Hearing (al-Samʿiyyāt) and the Verification of the Prophet ﷺ in What He Reported — Comprising Ten Fundamental Principles
23:102.anchors:
- Root: حشر (ḥ-sh-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To gather, assemble, drive together; al-ḥashr is the gathering of creation on the Day of Resurrection.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-ḥashr is the bringing together of a people from their various places of dispersal; it is used specifically for the resurrection gathering.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) for driving cattle together; metaphorical (majāz) for the ingathering of souls for judgment.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Conditional Protasis (al-sharṭ) — "If you are truthful, then rise..." (fa-in kunta ṣādiqan fa-qum...) — the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) functions as the proof of the protasis, establishing necessary knowledge (ʿilm ḍarūrī).

- Root: نشر (n-sh-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To spread, unfold, revive after death; al-nushūr is the revivification of the dead.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-nashr is the spreading of the soul back into the body after death; it is the opposite of al-ṭayy (folding up).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal for unfolding a garment; metaphorical for the resurrection when the earth "spreads forth" what it contains.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Coordination (al-ʿaṭf) — "al-ḥashr wa-l-nashr" (the gathering and the spreading) — two coordinated nouns forming a single compound concept of resurrection.

- Root: مكن (m-k-n)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To establish, empower, give firm footing; makkana means to make something firm and stable.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-makān is the place that contains a thing; tamakkun is the firm establishment of a thing in its place.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal for physical placement; metaphorical for divine power — "God is able" (qādir) means He has full capacity and authority over all things.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Possibility (al-imkān) — "that is possible" (dhālika mumkin) — the predicate of possibility is established by the absence of logical contradiction, not by empirical observation.

- Root: عذب (ʿ-dh-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Sweet, pleasant (of water); al-ʿadhāb is the punishment that is "sweet" to the inflictor but bitter to the recipient — used predominantly for divine chastisement.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-ʿadhāb is the infliction of pain that deters; it is specifically the painful consequence of disobedience.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal for sweet water; metaphorical (majāz) for punishment that is "appointed" as a deterrent.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Exception (al-istithnāʾ) — "except as God wills" (illā mā shāʾa) — the exception clause restricts the scope of human perception, not divine action.

26:23.arabic: جادلتنا فأكثرت جدالنا وقال تعالى في قصة فرعون وما رب العالمين إلى قوله أولوا جئتك بشيء مبين وعلى الجملة فالقرآن من أوله إلى آخره محاجة مع الكفار فعمدة أدلة المتكلمين في التوحيد قوله تعالى {لو كان فيهما آلهة إلا الله لفسدتا} وفي النبوة {وإن كنتم في ريب مما نزلنا على عبدنا فأتوا بسورة من مثله} وفي البعث {قل يحييها الذي أنشأها أول مرة} إلى غير ذلك من الآيات والأدلة ولم تزل الرسل صلوات الله عليهم يحاجون المنكرين ويجادلونهم قال تعالى {وجادلهم بالتي هي أحسن} فالصحابة رضي الله عنهم أيضا كانوا يحاجون المنكرين ويجاد
26:23.english: The mention of the proof (ḥujjah), the demand for it, and the search after it — how could these be prohibited, when God — may He be exalted — has said: {«قُلْ هَاتُوا بُرْهَانَكُمْ»} (Say: Bring forth your proof — Qur'an 2:111), and He — mighty and majestic — has said: {«لِيَهْلِكَ مَنْ هَلَكَ عَنْ بَيِّنَةٍ وَيَحْيَا مَنْ حَيَّ عَنْ بَيِّنَةٍ»} (So that he who perishes may perish upon clear evidence, and he who lives may live upon clear evidence — Qur'an 8:42), and He — may He be exalted — has said: {«هَلْ عِنْدَكُمْ مِنْ سُلْطَانٍ بِهَذَا»} (Have you any authority for this? — Qur'an 10:68), meaning a proof and demonstration, and He — may He be exalted — has said: {«قُلْ فَلِلَّهِ الْحُجَّةُ الْبَالِغَةُ»} (Say: To God belongs the conclusive proof — Qur'an 6:149), and He — may He be exalted — has said: {«أَلَمْ تَرَ إِلَى الَّذِي حَاجَّ إِبْرَاهِيمَ فِي رَبِّهِ»} (Have you not considered him who disputed with Abraham concerning his Lord? — Qur'an 2:258) up to His words: {«فَبُهِتَ الَّذِي كَفَرَ»} (So the one who disbelieved was confounded — Qur'an 2:258).
26:23.section_title_en: The Revival of the Religious Sciences — Section 77: On the Permissibility of Theological Discourse (Kalām) and Its Early Practice
26:23.anchors:
- Root: ح-د-ث (ḥ-d-th)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "Al-ḥudūth: the coming-to-be of a thing after it was not; al-ḥadath: the novel event; al-ḥīdāth: origination."
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Al-ḥudūth: a thing's becoming after it was not, whether accident or substance; iḥdāth: bringing it into existence. The origination of substances belongs to God alone."
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "Literal: 'He is a recent event among events.' Metaphorical: 'They became topics of conversation (aḥādīth).'"
- Root: ح-ا-ج (ḥ-ā-j)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "Al-ḥājah: need of a thing, with desire for it; its plural: ḥājāt and ḥawā'ij."
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Al-ḥājah ilā al-shay': poverty toward it with love of it. God said: {«إِلَّا حَاجَةً فِي نَفْسِ يَعْقُوبَ»} (except a need in Jacob's soul — Qur'an 12:68)."
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "Literal: need and want. The 'ḥājah' is that which one seeks to obtain."
- Root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "Kāna: to be, to exist; takwīn: bringing into being from non-existence."
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Al-kawn: existence after non-existence; the muḥdath (originated thing) is that brought forth after it was not."
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "Literal: being and becoming. Metaphorical: the continuous states of affairs."
- Sibawayh Rule: Al-Faṣl bayna al-Jār wa-al-Majrūr (Prepositional Interposition) — The permissibility of separating a preposition from its object when the intervening clause is complete in meaning, as in the verse's structure of argumentation where the proof (ḥujjah) stands independently before its conclusion.

27:89.arabic: ونفي ولقوله تعالى {من جاء بالحسنة فله خير منها وهم من فزع يومئذ آمنون} فالإيمان رأس الحسنات ولقوله تعالى {والله يحب المحسنين} وقال تعالى {إنا لا نضيع أجر من أحسن عملا} ولا حجة لهم في ذلك فإنه حيث ذكر الإيمان في هذه الآيات أريد به الإيمان مع العمل إذ بينا أن الإيمان قد يطلق ويراد به الإسلام وهو الموافقة بالقلب والقول والعمل ودليل هذا التأويل أخبار كثيرة في معاقبة العاصين ومقادير العقاب وقوله صلى الله عليه وسلم يخرج من النار من كان في قلبه مثقال ذرة من إيمان فكيف يخرج إذا لم يدخل ومن القرآن قوله تعالى {إن الله لا يغفر أن ي
27:89.english: He was asked, "Which deed is most excellent?" The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Islam." It was then asked, "Which aspect of Islam is most excellent?" He (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Faith (Īmān)." This is evidence for both the distinction (ikhtilāf) between the two terms and their overlap (tadākhul). This usage is the most consistent with the conventions of the language, because faith is a deed among deeds, and it is the most excellent of them. Islam is submission (taslīm), whether by the heart, by the tongue, or by the limbs. The most excellent of these is that which is by the heart, which is the assent (taṣdīq) that is called faith. Using the two terms in a way that indicates distinction, overlap, or even complete synonymy (tarāduf) is all within the bounds of metaphorical usage (tajawwuz) in the language.
27:89.section_title_en: The Book of the Revival of the Religious Sciences — Section 99: On the Distinction, Overlap, and Synonymy of Faith (Īmān) and Submission (Islām), and Their Worldly and Otherworldly Judgments
27:89.anchors:
- Root: ايم (A-Y-M)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of remaining unmarried, or a state of being without a spouse; extended metaphorically to describe one who is solitary or without support.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الأيامى: جمع أيم، وهي المرأة التي لا بعل لها... والحرب مأيمة، أي: يفرق بين الزوج والزوجة." The root carries the sense of separation or a state of lacking union, which informs the theological discussion of what constitutes the essential bond of faith.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah) usage denotes the state of being unmarried; metaphorical (Majaz) usage extends to anything that separates or leaves one bereft. This distinction between literal and metaphorical application is central to the chapter's method.
- Root: قلب (Q-L-B)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To turn, overturn, or transform a thing from one state to another.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "قلب الشيء: تصريفه وصرفه عن وجه إلى وجه... والانقلاب: الانصراف." The heart (qalb) is so named for its constant fluctuation and turning. In theological terms, it is the seat of taṣdīq (assent), the immaterial faculty of cognition and conviction.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah) usage is physical turning; metaphorical (Majaz) usage is "قلب الأمور" — to deliberate, scrutinize, and manage affairs. This supports the distinction between the heart's internal act of assent and the external acts of the limbs.
- Root: عمل (ʿ-A-M-L)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Any deed or action performed with purpose and intent.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "العمل: كل فعل يكون من الحيوان بقصد، فهو أخص من الفعل." Work is more specific than mere action, as it implies deliberate, intentional agency. It is used for both righteous and sinful deeds, and is the external manifestation of internal conviction.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah) usage refers to physical labor or deeds. The chapter explores whether "work" is an integral part of the reality of faith or a separate, consequent requirement.
- Root: صدق (S-D-Q)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To be truthful, to speak the truth, to verify.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الصدق والكذب أصلهما في القول... ولا يكونان بالقصد الأول إلا في القول." Truth and falsehood are primarily properties of speech and reports. Taṣdīq (assent) is the heart's affirmation of the truth of a report, which is the core reality of Īmān.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah) usage is truthful speech; metaphorical (Majaz) usage is "صادق الحملة" — one who is true and firm in battle or resolve. This shows that taṣdīq is not merely verbal but a firm, internal resolution.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication). This rule governs how restriction (ḥaṣr) is achieved in Arabic, often through particles like "innamā" or through contextual specification (takhṣīṣ). The chapter's core argument hinges on how terms like Īmān and Islām are semantically restricted, expanded, or made synonymous through contextual usage (majāz), requiring precise parsing of the predicate and its scope.
27:89.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Foundations of Belief'

27:90.arabic: عذاب مقيم} وقال تعالى {ومن جاء بالسيئة فكبت وجوههم في النار} فهذه العمومات في معارضة عموماتهم ولا بد من تسليط التخصص والتأويل على الجانبين لأن الأخبار مصرحة بأن العصاة يعذبون (1) بل قوله تعالى وإن منكم إلا واردها كالصريح في أن ذلك لا بد منه للكل إذ لا يخلو مؤمن عن ذنب يرتكبه وقوله تعالى لا يصلاها إلا الأشقى الذي كذب وتولى أراد به من جماعة مخصوصين أو أراد بالأشقى شخصا معينا أيضا وقوله تعالى كلما ألقى فيها فوج سألهم خزنتها أي فوج من الكفار وتخصيص العمومات قريب ومن هذه الآية وقع للأشعري وطائفة من المتكلم

29:7.arabic: دونه وادعى الإجماع فيه واستدل بأدلة تشعر بنقيض غرضه كقوله تعالى {الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات} إذ هذا يدل على أن العمل وراء الإيمان لا من نفس الإيمان وإلا فيكون العمل في حكم المعاد والعجب أنه ادعى الإجماع في هذا وهو مع ذلك ينقل قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم لا يكفر أحد إلا بعد جحوده لما أقر به (1) وينكر على المعتزلة قولهم بالتخليد في النار بسبب الكبائر والقائل بهذا قائل بنفس مذهب المعتزلة إذ يقال له من صدق بقلبه وشهد بلسانه ومات في الحال فهل هو في الجنة فلا بد أن يقول نعم وفيه حكم بوجود الإيمان دون العمل فنزيد ونقول لو بقي حيا حتى دخل عليه وقت

29:9.english: He was asked, "Which deed is most excellent?" The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Islam." It was then asked, "Which aspect of Islam is most excellent?" 29:43.arabic: وقال تعالى {وتلك الأمثال نضربها للناس وما يعقلها إلا العالمون} وقال تعالى {ولو ردوه إلى الرسول وإلى أولي الأمر منهم لعلمه الذين يستنبطونه منهم} رد حكمه في الوقائع إلى استنباطهم وألحق رتبتهم برتبة الأنبياء في كشف حكم الله وقيل في قوله تعالى يا بني آدم قد أنزلنا عليكم لباسا يواري سوءاتكم يعني العلم وريشا يعني اليقين ولباس التقوى يعني الحياء وقال عز وجل {ولقد جئناهم بكتاب فصلناه على علم} وقال تعالى {فلنقصن عليهم بعلم} وقال عز وجل {بل هو آيات بينات في صدور الذين أوتوا العلم} وقال تعالى {خلق الإنسان علمه ال
29:43.english: How He, Glorified and Exalted, began with Himself, then seconded with the angels, and thirded with the people of knowledge — and sufficient for you is this as honor, excellence, splendor, and nobility. And God, Exalted, said: {«يرفع الله الذين آمنوا منكم والذين أوتوا العلم درجات»} — "God will raise those who have believed among you and those who have been given knowledge, in degrees." Ibn ʿAbbās, may God be pleased with them both, said: For the scholars there are degrees above the believers, seven hundred degrees, and between each two degrees is a distance of five hundred years' journey.
29:43.section_title_en: The Book of Knowledge — Section 4: The Excellence of Knowledge and the Scholars
29:43.anchors:
- Root: علم (ʿ-l-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root meaning of knowing, perceiving a thing in its true reality; the act of apprehension and judgment.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "العلم: إدراك الشيء بحقيقته" — knowledge is the apprehension of a thing in its true reality, divided into apprehension of the essence and judgment of existence or non-existence.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) usage denotes genuine knowing; metaphorical (majāz) usage extends to signs, landmarks, and traces that guide to knowledge.
- Root: درج (d-r-j)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Degrees, steps, ascending stations; the root denotes gradation and progressive elevation.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الدرجة نحو المنزلة، لكن يقال للمنزلة: درجة إذا اعتبرت بالصعود" — a degree is a station considered by ascent, not horizontal extension.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical steps of ascent. Metaphorical: "لفلان درجة رفيعة" — lofty rank; "امش في مدارج الحق" — walk in the paths of truth.
- Root: يوم (y-w-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: A day; a period of time from sunrise to sunset, or any duration whatsoever.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "اليوم يعبر به عن وقت طلوع الشمس إلى غروبها. وقد يعبر به عن مدة من الزمان أي مدة كانت" — the day denotes the time of the sun's rising to its setting, and may denote any period of time whatsoever.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the solar day. Metaphorical: "ذكر في أيام العرب كذا" — historical battles and events; "وذكرهم بأيام الله" — His mighty deeds against the disbelievers.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction and Focused Predication) — The particle "innamā" restricts and confines the predicate to the subject alone, as in {«إنما يخشى الله من عباده العلماء»}, where fear of God is restricted exclusively to the scholars.

29:69.arabic: بالمجاهدة التي جعلها الله سبحانه مقدمة للهداية حيث قال تعالى {والذين جاهدوا فينا لنهدينهم سبلنا وإن الله لمع المحسنين} فإن قلت فقد رددت حد المتكلم إلى حراسة عقيدة العوام عن تشويش المبتدعة كما أن حد البذرقة حراسة أقمشة الحجيج عن نهب العرب ورددت حد الفقيه إلى حفظ القانون الذي به يكف السلطان شر بعض أهل العدوان عن بعض وهاتان رتبتان نازلتان بالإضافة إلى علم الدين وعلماء الأمة المشهورون بالفضل هم الفقهاء والمتكلمون وهم أفضل الخلق عند الله تعالى فكيف تنزل درجاتهم إلى هذه المنزلة السافلة بالإضافة إلى علم الدين فاعلم أن من عرف الحق بالرجال حار في متاهات الضلال فاعرف الحق تع
29:69.english: And al-Junayd — may God have mercy on him — said: My shaykh al-Sarī said to me one day: "When you leave my presence, whom do you sit with?" I replied: "Al-Muḥāsibī." He said: "Yes. Take from his knowledge and his refinement, but leave aside his hair-splitting speech and his refutations against the theologians (mutakallimūn)." Then, when I turned away, I heard him say: "May God make you a traditionist who is a Sufi, and not a Sufi who is a traditionist." He pointed thereby to the fact that whoever first acquires the ḥadīth and knowledge, and then becomes a Sufi, succeeds; but whoever becomes a Sufi before knowledge imperils his own soul.
29:69.section_title_en: The Station of the Jurists and Theologians Relative to the Science of Religion — Section 17
29:69.anchors:
- Root: علم (ʿalima)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root denotes the faculty of perception and discernment; the act of grasping a thing's reality.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "العلم: إدراك الشيء بحقيقته" — knowledge is the apprehension of a thing in its true reality, divided into apprehension of essence and judgment of existence.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Distinguishes literal knowledge (maʿrifah) from the metaphorical "awareness" (shiʿr); here, the "science of the Hereafter" (ʿilm al-ākhirah) is the true knowledge of God, not mere discursive theology.
- Root: بدع (badaʿa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To originate something without prior model; innovation.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الإبداع: إنشاء صنعة بلا احتذاء واقتداء" — creation without precedent; when applied to God, it is bringing into being without instrument, matter, time, or place.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: to invent or initiate. Metaphorical: "أبدعت حجتك" — your argument became weak. Here, the "innovation" (bidʿah) that diverts from the Qur'an and Sunnah is the blameworthy innovation that necessitated the science of theology (kalām) as a defensive necessity.
- Root: طرق (ṭaraqa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To strike, to beat; a path beaten by feet.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الطريق: السبيل الذي يطرق بالأرجل" — the path trodden by feet; metaphorically, any course of action, praiseworthy or blameworthy.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: striking iron with a hammer. Metaphorical: "طرقني الخيال" — the phantom visited me at night. Here, the "way of the Hereafter" (ṭarīq al-ākhirah) is the path of spiritual striving (mujāhadah), not the beaten track of disputation.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — Used to confine the true rank of the jurist and theologian to the role of guardian, not the possessor of the science of the Hereafter.
