37:96.arabic: ومتعلقة بقدرته تصديقا له في قوله تعالى الله خالق كل شيء وفي قوله تعالى والله خلقكم وما تعملون وفي قوله تعالى وأسروا قولكم أو اجهروا به إنه عليم بذات الصدور ألا يعلم من خلق وهو اللطيف الخبير أمر العباد بالتحرز في أقوالهم وأفعالهم وإسرارهم وإضمارهم لعلمه بموارد أفعالهم واستدل على العلم بالخلق وكيف لا يكون خالقا لفعل العبد وقدرته تامة لا قصور فيها وهي متعلقة بحركة أبدان العباد والحركات متماثلة وتعلق القدرة بها لذاتها فما الذي يقصر تعلقها عن بعض الحركات دون البعض مع تماثلها أو كيف يكون الحيوان مستبدا بالاختراع ويصدر من العنكبوت والنحل وسا
37:96.english: Rather, the attribute of origination (ḥudūth) is established for bodies only by virtue of their being subject to change and the fluctuation of states. So how could their Creator share with them in the acceptance of change? And upon this is built [the doctrine] that His Speech (kalām) is eternal, subsisting in His Essence—only the sounds indicating it are originated. Just as one rationally apprehends the subsistence of a request for learning and the father's will for [his] child in the father's essence before the child is created—such that when the child is created, attains reason, and God creates for him a knowledge pertaining to what is in his father's heart of the request, the child becomes commanded by that very request which subsisted in his father's essence and whose existence endured until the time of his child's awareness of it—so let one rationally apprehend the subsistence of the command indicated by His words, Mighty and Majestic: {«اخلع نعليك»} "Take off your sandals" [Q 20:12], in God's Essence, and Moses—peace be upon him—becoming addressed by it after his existence, when God created for him a knowledge of that command and hearing of that eternal Speech.
37:96.section_title_en: The Revival of the Religious Sciences — Section 92: On the Divine Attributes of Eternity, Knowledge, Will, and the Third Pillar Concerning God's Acts
37:96.anchors:
- Root: قدم (q-d-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Primordial precedence; that which has no temporal beginning; eternal past (azal) and eternal future (abad).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Precedence either by time, by honor, or by ontological necessity—here, God's attributes are eternal in the sense that they are not subject to temporal origination.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "to precede." Metaphorical: that which cannot be conceived as non-existent posterior to its existence—applied to God's essence and attributes.
- Root: علم (ʿ-l-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Comprehension of a thing as it truly is; the indelible mark or trace by which one is guided.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Knowledge is the apprehension of a thing in its reality"—twofold: apprehension of the essence, and judgment concerning existence or non-existence. God's knowledge is eternal, encompassing all created things without renewal.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: perception and awareness. Metaphorical: the "signs" (maʿālim) of God's power—His knowledge is identical with His creative act, for "Does He who created not know?" {«ألا يعلم من خلق»}.
- Root: خلق (kh-l-q)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Measuring, proportioning, then bringing into existence upon a determined measure.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Origination from nothing without prior model—"He created the heavens and the earth" {«خلق السماوات والأرض»}—and also bringing forth from something, as man from a drop. All acts of creatures are God's creation.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the tailor's measuring before cutting. Metaphorical: God's bringing forth existence upon a measure dictated by wisdom—He is the sole Creator (al-Khāliq) of all acts, including those of His servants.
- Root: قتل (q-t-l)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Removal of the spirit from the body; also, intense subjugation.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The root meaning is the separation of soul from body, whether by an agent (qatl) or by natural death (mawt). Used here analogically: as "killer," "killed," and "killing" are mutually entailing, so are "knower," "known," and "knowledge."
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: slaying. Metaphorical: mutual entailment—just as no killer exists without a killing and a killed one, so no knower exists without knowledge and a known object.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب التلازم والتضايف (Mutual Entailment and Correlativity) — Terms like ʿālim/ʿilm/maʿlūm are correlatives (mutalāzimāt) that cannot be conceptually separated; the predicate necessitates the co-existence of its correlates in the intellect.
37:96.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Foundations of Belief'

39:36.arabic: يعذب ولا يبعد ولا يحجب وقال تعالى أليس الله بكاف عبده فطالب الكفاية من غيره والتارك للتوكل هو المكذب لهذه الآية فإنه سؤال في معرض استنطاق بالحق كقوله تعالى هل أتى على الإنسان حين من الدهر لم يكن شيئا مذكورا وقال عز وجل ومن يتوكل على الله فإن الله عزيز حكيم أي عزيز لا يذل من استجار به ولا يضيع من لاذ بجنا به والتجأ إلى
39:36.english: Praise be to God, the Disposer of the dominion (mulk) and the spiritual sovereignty (malakūt), the One alone in majesty (ʿizzah) and omnipotence (jabarūt), Who raised the heaven without any pillar, and apportioned therein the provisions of His servants; Who turned the eyes of those possessed of hearts and intellects away from the observation of intermediaries and causes (al-wasāʾiṭ wa-l-asbāb) toward the Causer of causes (musabbib al-asbāb); and Who lifted their concern from turning toward anything other than Him, and from relying upon any disposer besides Him. Thus they worshipped none but Him alone — in knowledge that He is the One, the Unique, the Eternal Refuge (al-ṣamad), the God — and in verification that all classes of creatures are servants like themselves, from whom no provision is sought, and that there is no atom but God created it, and no beast but upon God is its sustenance. When they verified that He is the Guarantor of His servants' provision and the Surety for it, they relied upon Him and said: {«حسبنا الله ونعم الوكيل»} — "God is sufficient for us, and what an excellent Guardian!" (Q. 3:173).
39:36.section_title_en: The Book of Divine Unity (Tawḥīd) and Reliance (Tawakkul) — Book Five of the Quarter of Deliverance from The Revival of the Religious Sciences
39:36.anchors:
- Root: وكل (w-k-l)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of delegating, entrusting, and appointing a deputy (wakīl) to manage one's affairs.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "التوكيل: أن تعتمد على غيرك وتجعله نائبا عنك" — Reliance (tawakkul) is the act of depending upon another and making him a deputy over your affair; its theological force is that God alone is the sufficient Guardian (wakīl), as in {«وكفى بالله وكيلا»}.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): appointing an agent; Metaphorical (majāz): the weak man who leans on others (وكل ووكلة تكلة). In the divine context, tawakkul is a real, not figurative, transfer of one's trust to God as the sole efficient cause.
- Root: سبب (s-b-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: A rope, cord, or means by which one ascends or reaches something; extended to any intermediary cause.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "سمي كل ما يتوصل به إلى شيء سببا" — Every means by which one reaches a goal is termed a cause (sabab); God is the "Musabbib al-Asbāb" (Causer of causes), transcending the causal ropes He suspends.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: a physical cord; Metaphorical: any linkage or connection. Here, the "gaze upon causes" (mulāḥaẓat al-asbāb) is a metaphorical veiling of the true Agent.
- Root: حسب (ḥ-s-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To count, reckon, suffice; derived: ḥasb (sufficiency), ḥasīb (one who suffices, or the Reckoner).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الحساب: استعمال العدد" — Counting; but in the divine attribute, "ḥasb" denotes God's all-sufficient guardianship, as in {«حسبنا الله ونعم الوكيل»}.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: reckoning by number; Metaphorical: "احتسبت ما عند فلان: اختبرته وسبرته" — to test and probe. God's being "Ḥasb" for the believer is a tested, verified sufficiency, not a mere claim.
- Root: غمض (gh-m-d)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To close the eye, to be obscure, low-lying, or hidden ground.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "يستعار للتغافل والتساهل" — closing the eye is metaphorically used for overlooking; here, the "ghumūḍ" (obscurity) of tawakkul is its conceptual hiddenness from the intellect.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: a low, concealed place; Metaphorical: "أمر غامض" — a subtle, difficult affair. The text uses it for the doctrinal opacity of tawakkul.
- Sibawayh Rule: Interposition of the prepositional phrase (باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور) — The periodic structure "فلم يعبدوا إلا إياه" and "فقالوا حسبنا الله" shows the separation of the operative verb from its object for rhetorical emphasis, permissible where the pause is complete and the meaning remains unbroken.
39:36.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Monotheism and Reliance'

39:36.arabic: قديما فنزه عن الالتفات إليه قلبك فلله سبحانه سر في إبعاد بعض العباد ومن يضلل الله فما له من هاد ومن استبعد أن يسمع موسى عليه السلام في الدنيا كلاما ليس بصوت ولا حرف فليستنكر أن يرى في الآخرة موجودا ليس بجسم ولا لون وإن عقل أن يرى ما ليس بلون ولا جسم ولا قدر ولا كمية وهو إلى الآن لم ير غيره فليعقل في حاسة السمع ما عقله في حاسة البصر وإن عقل على أن يكون له علم واحد هو علم بجميع الموجودات فليعقل صفة واحدة للذات هو كلام بجميع ما دل عليه من العبارات وإن عقل كون السموات السبع وكون الجنة والنار مكتوبة في ورقة صغيرة ومحفوظة في مقدار ذرة من القلب
39:36.english:
[Root: عقل]
  • Al-Raghib (Al-Mufradat): "العقل يقال للقوة المتهيئة لقبول العلم، ويقال للعلم الذي يستفيده الإنسان بتلك القوة عقل" — The intellect is the faculty prepared for receiving knowledge, and the knowledge acquired through that faculty is also called intellect. This dual sense is crucial for understanding Ghazali's argument that true intellection ('aql) grasps realities beyond sensory perception.
  • Al-Zamakhshari (Asas - Haqiqah/Literal): "عقل فلان بعد الصبا أي عرف الخطأ الذي كان عليه" — To exercise intellect means to recognize error. Ghazali employs this to demand intellectual consistency from his opponents.
  • Al-Zamakhshari (Asas - Majaz/Metaphorical): "نخلة لا تعقل الإبار إذا لم تقبله" — A palm tree that does not accept pollination is said metaphorically to "not comprehend." This illustrates that 'aql involves receptivity to what is appropriate.
39:36.topic: Al-Ghazali on the journey of the soul, death, and the Hereafter, from 'Foundations of Belief'

39:38.arabic: ولذلك قال عز وجل ولئن سألتهم من خلق السموات والأرض ليقولن الله وقال تعالى فأقم وجهك للدين حنيفا فطرة الله التي
39:38.english: The First Principle: the knowledge of His existence, the Exalted. The first thing by which one is illuminated from among the lights, and the path of reflection (ṭarīq al-iʿtibār) by which one proceeds, is that to which the Qurʾān has guided. For after the explanation of God, glorified be He, there is no explanation. He, the Exalted, has said: {«أَلَمْ نَجْعَلِ الْأَرْضَ مِهَادًا وَالْجِبَالَ أَوْتَادًا وَخَلَقْنَاكُمْ أَزْوَاجًا وَجَعَلْنَا نَوْمَكُمْ سُبَاتًا وَجَعَلْنَا اللَّيْلَ لِبَاسًا وَجَعَلْنَا النَّهَارَ مَعَاشًا وَبَنَيْنَا فَوْقَكُمْ سَبْعًا شِدَادًا وَجَعَلْنَا سِرَاجًا وَهَّاجًا وَأَنزَلْنَا مِنَ الْمُعْصِرَاتِ مَاءً ثَجَّاجًا لِّنُخْرِجَ بِهِ حَبًّا وَنَبَاتًا وَجَنَّاتٍ أَلْفَافًا»} — "Have We not made the earth a resting place, and the mountains as pegs, and created you in pairs, and made your sleep a repose, and made the night a covering, and made the day for livelihood, and built above you seven strong heavens, and made a blazing lamp, and sent down from the rain-clouds pouring water, that We may bring forth thereby grain and vegetation, and gardens dense with foliage?" (Q 78:6–16). And He, the Exalted, has said: {«إِنَّ فِي خَلْقِ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَاخْتِلَافِ اللَّيْلِ وَالنَّهَارِ وَالْفُلْكِ الَّتِي تَجْرِي فِي الْبَحْرِ بِمَا يَنفَعُ النَّاسَ وَمَا أَنزَلَ اللَّهُ مِنَ السَّمَاءِ مِن مَّاءٍ فَأَحْيَا بِهِ الْأَرْضَ بَعْدَ مَوْتِهَا وَبَثَّ فِيهَا مِن كُلِّ دَابَّةٍ وَتَصْرِيفِ الرِّيَاحِ وَالسَّحَابِ الْمُسَخَّرِ بَيْنَ السَّمَاءِ وَالْأَرْضِ لَآيَاتٍ لِّقَوْمٍ يَعْقِلُونَ»} — "Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth, and the alternation of the night and the day, and the ships which sail through the sea with that which benefits people, and what God has sent down from the sky of water, thereby reviving the earth after its death, and dispersing therein every creature, and the directing of the winds, and the clouds subservient between the heaven and the earth — are signs for a people who reason" (Q 2:164). And He, the Exalted, has said: {«أَلَمْ تَرَوْا كَيْفَ خَلَقَ اللَّهُ سَبْعَ سَمَاوَاتٍ طِبَاقًا وَجَعَلَ الْقَمَرَ فِيهِنَّ نُورًا وَجَعَلَ الشَّمْسَ سِرَاجًا وَاللَّهُ أَنبَتَكُم مِّنَ الْأَرْضِ نَبَاتًا ثُمَّ يُعِيدُكُمْ فِيهَا وَيُخْرِجُكُمْ إِخْرَاجًا»} — "Have you not seen how God created seven heavens in layers, and made the moon therein a light, and made the sun a lamp? And God caused you to grow from the earth a growth; then He returns you into it, and brings you forth a bringing forth" (Q 71:15–18). And He, the Exalted, has said: {«أَفَرَأَيْتُم مَّا تُمْنُونَ أَأَنتُمْ تَخْلُقُونَهُ أَمْ نَحْنُ الْخَالِقُونَ»} — "Have you considered what you emit? Do you create it, or are We the Creator?" — up to His saying: {«لِلْمُقْوِينَ»} — "for the settlers" (Q 56:58–73).
39:38.section_title_en: The Pillars of Faith: Knowledge of God, His Attributes, His Acts, and the Audibles — Section 87
39:38.anchors:
- Root: وجود (w-j-d)
  * Lisan / Ayn: [Core linguistic root meaning: to find, to perceive, to be; existence as that which is found or discovered]
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): [Theological/Kalam semantic nuance: al-wujūd as necessary existence (wujūb) versus contingent existence (imkān); the self-evident reality of the Creator's being]
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): [Literal vs Metaphorical distinction: haqīqah — existence as affirmed reality; majāz — "finding" as in discovery, not applicable to God's necessary being]
- Root: خلق (kh-l-q)
  * Lisan / Ayn: [Core linguistic root meaning: measuring, proportioning, fashioning; origination of a thing upon a measure]
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الخلق أصله: التقدير المستقيم، ويستعمل في إبداع الشيء من غير أصل ولا احتذاء" — creation as origination from nothing without prior model
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): [Literal: خلق الله الخلق: أوجده على تقدير أوجبته الحكمة — brought into existence upon a measure necessitated by wisdom; Majaz: not applicable to God's act as pure origination]
- Root: فطر (f-t-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: [Core linguistic root meaning: to split, cleave, rend; to originate, to bring forth as a new creation]
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "فطر الله الخلق" — God's origination of creation as a primordial act; "الفطرة" as the innate disposition
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): [Literal: فطر الله الخلق، وهو فاطر السموات: مبتدعها — originator without precedent; Majaz: "رأيه فطير" — immature opinion, not applicable to divine]
- Root: ارض (ar-d)
  * Lisan / Ayn: [Core linguistic root meaning: the earth, the lower sphere; that which is beneath]
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الأرض: الجرم المقابل للسماء" — the body opposite the heaven
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): [Literal: the earth as a resting place (مهادا); Majaz: not applicable in this context of divine creation]
- Root: ركن (r-k-n)
  * Lisan / Ayn: [Core linguistic root meaning: corner, pillar, support; that to which one leans for strength]
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "ركن الشيء: جانبه الذي يسكن إليه" — the side of a thing to which one repairs; used metaphorically for strength
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): [Literal: physical pillar/corner; Majaz: "فلان يأوي من عز قومه إلى ركن شديد" — one who repairs to a mighty support; here, the "pillars" (أركان) of faith as structural supports]
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The syntactic structure "مداره على عشرة أصول" (its circuit revolves upon ten principles) employs a prepositional phrase governing the verbal noun, establishing the necessary grammatical dependency that mirrors the ontological dependency of the created upon the Creator.
39:38.topic: Al-Ghazali on the journey of the soul, death, and the Hereafter, from 'Foundations of Belief'

39:47.arabic: والقلوب بين إصبعين من أصابع الرحمن يقلبها كيف يشاء وقد قال سبحانه {وبدا لهم من الله ما لم يكونوا يحتسبون} (2) قيل في التفسير عملوا أعمالا ظنوا أنها حسنات فكانت في كفة السيئات وقال سري السقطي لو أن إنسانا دخل بستانا فيه من جميع الأشجار عليها من جميع الطيور فخاطبه كل طير منها بلغة فقال السلام عليك يا ولي الله فسكنت نفسه إلى ذلك كان أسيرا في يديها فهذه الأخبار والآثار تعرفك خطر الأمر بسبب دقائق النفاق والشرك الخفي وأنه لا يؤمن منه حتى كان عمر بن الخطاب رضي الله عنه يسأل حذيفة عن نفسه وأنه هل ذكر في المنافقين وقال أبو سليمان الداراني سمعت
39:47.english: ...doubt concerning this truthfulness. Likewise, God Most High said: {«But righteousness is he who believes in God and the Last Day and the angels and the Book and the prophets»} (2:177) — thus He conditioned twenty attributes, such as faithfulness to covenant and patience under hardship. Then He said Most High: {«Those are the truthful ones»} (2:177). And God Most High said: {«God will raise those who have believed among you and those who have been given knowledge, by degrees»} (58:11). And He said Most High: {«Not equal among you are those who spent before the conquest and fought»} (57:10). And He said Most High: {«They are degrees before God»} (3:163). And the Prophet, peace be upon him, said: "Faith is naked, and its garment is God-consciousness (al-taqwā)." And the Prophet, peace be upon him, said: "Faith has seventy-some branches; the lowest of them is removing harm from the path." All this indicates the interconnection of the perfection of faith with works.
39:47.section_title_en: The Revival of the Religious Sciences — Book of the Secrets of Zakāh, Section 104: On the Degrees of Faith and Its Connection to Works, and the Hidden Hypocrisy (al-Nifāq al-Khafī) That Contradicts the Perfection of Faith
39:47.anchors:
- Root: ن ف ق (N-F-Q)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Root denotes passing away, depletion, and expenditure; also the underground burrow of the jerboa (nāfiqāʾ) with a concealed exit — the etymological basis for hypocrisy as a hidden exit from faith.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "نفق الشيء: مضى ونفد" — theological nuance: hypocrisy (nifāq) is that which causes faith to expire and pass away, whether by sale (worldly gain) or by death (spiritual ruin).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "نفقت الدراهم" (coins ran out). Metaphorical: "نفق روحه: خرج" (his soul expired and went forth) — hence the hypocrite's faith is one whose spirit has already departed.
- Root: أ ي م (A-Y-M)
  * Lisan / Ayn: A woman without a husband; a man long unmarried. Al-Raghib: "الحرب مأيمة" — war makes women widows.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "تركوا النساء أيامى" (they left women widowed). Metaphorical application: the one who feels secure from hypocrisy is like one who claims immunity from widowhood — a false security.
- Root: و ف ي (W-F-Y)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Fullness, completion, fulfillment of a measure or covenant.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الوافي: الذي بلغ التمام" — the one who has reached completion. "أوفى: إذا تمم العهد ولم ينقض حفظه" — to fulfill the covenant without breach.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "درهم واف" (a full-weight dirham). Metaphorical: "أوفى على المائة" (he surpassed a hundred) — faith's perfection (wafāʾ) is only attained by surpassing mere profession to include works and inward sincerity.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد (Restriction & Focused Predication) — governing the grammatical force of "إنما" constructions and conditional clauses (من كان...), where the predicate is restricted to the condition stated, as in the hadith "أربع من كن فيه فهو منافق خالص" — the four traits are exhaustive of the ruling.

40:33.arabic: قديما فنزه عن الالتفات إليه قلبك فلله سبحانه سر في إبعاد بعض العباد ومن يضلل الله فما له من هاد ومن استبعد أن يسمع موسى عليه السلام في الدنيا كلاما ليس بصوت ولا حرف فليستنكر أن يرى في الآخرة موجودا ليس بجسم ولا لون وإن عقل أن يرى ما ليس بلون ولا جسم ولا قدر ولا كمية وهو إلى الآن لم ير غيره فليعقل في حاسة السمع ما عقله في حاسة البصر وإن عقل على أن يكون له علم واحد هو علم بجميع الموجودات فليعقل صفة واحدة للذات هو كلام بجميع ما دل عليه من العبارات وإن عقل كون السموات السبع وكون الجنة والنار مكتوبة في ورقة صغيرة ومحفوظة في مقدار ذرة من القلب

[Root: عقل]
  • Al-Raghib (Al-Mufradat): "العقل يقال للقوة المتهيئة لقبول العلم، ويقال للعلم الذي يستفيده الإنسان بتلك القوة عقل" — The intellect is the faculty prepared for receiving knowledge, and the knowledge acquired through that faculty is also called intellect. This dual sense is crucial for understanding Ghazali's argument that true intellection ('aql) grasps realities beyond sensory perception.
  • Al-Zamakhshari (Asas - Haqiqah/Literal): "عقل فلان بعد الصبا أي عرف الخطأ الذي كان عليه" — To exercise intellect means to recognize error. Ghazali employs this to demand intellectual consistency from his opponents.
  • Al-Zamakhshari (Asas - Majaz/Metaphorical): "نخلة لا تعقل الإبار إذا لم تقبله" — A palm tree that does not accept pollination is said metaphorically to "not comprehend." This illustrates that 'aql involves receptivity to what is appropriate.

40:46.arabic: الأصل الثالث عذاب القبر وقد ورد الشرع به قال الله تعالى النار يعرضون عليها غدوا وعشيا ويوم تقوم الساعة أدخلوا آل فرعون أشد العذاب واشتهر عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم والسلف الصالح الاستعاذة من عذاب القبر (4) وهو ممكن فيجب التصديق به ولا يمنع من التصديق به تفرق أجزاء الميت في بطون السباع وحواصل الطيور فإن المدرك لألم العذاب من الحيوان أجزاء مخصوصة يقدر الله تعالى على إعادة الإدراك إليها الأصل الرابع الميزان وهو حق قال الله تعالى ونضع الموازين القسط ليوم القيامة وقال تعالى فمن ثقلت موازينه فأولئك هم المفلحون ومن خفت موازينه الآية ووجهها أن الله تعالى يحدث في صحائف ا
40:46.english: For they, despite their distinction in eloquence and rhetorical perfection, aimed at reviling him, forbidding him, killing him, and expelling him — as God, Mighty and Majestic, informed us about them — yet they were unable to produce anything to rival the Qur'an. For it was not within the capacity of human beings to combine the grandeur of the Qur'an's diction with its harmonious order, especially given what it contains of the accounts of the ancients, while he was illiterate, never having practiced the study of books — and [given] its announcement of the unseen in matters whose truthfulness was verified in the future, such as His saying, Exalted is He: {«لَتَدْخُلُنَّ الْمَسْجِدَ الْحَرَامَ إِنْ شَاءَ اللَّهُ آمِنِينَ مُحَلِّقِينَ رُءُوسَكُمْ وَمُقَصِّرِينَ»} (You shall surely enter the Sacred Mosque, if God wills, secure, with your heads shaved and cut short) [Al-Fatḥ 48:27], and such as His saying: {«الم غُلِبَتِ الرُّومُ فِي أَدْنَى الْأَرْضِ وَهُمْ مِنْ بَعْدِ غَلَبِهِمْ سَيَغْلِبُونَ فِي بِضْعِ سِنِينَ»} (Alif Lām Mīm. The Romans have been defeated in the nearest land, and they, after their defeat, shall be victorious within a few years) [Al-Rūm 30:1-3].
40:46.section_title_en: The Fourth Pillar: On Matters of Hearing (al-Samʿiyyāt) and the Verification of the Prophet ﷺ in What He Reported — Comprising Ten Fundamental Principles
40:46.anchors:
- Root: حشر (ḥ-sh-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To gather, assemble, drive together; al-ḥashr is the gathering of creation on the Day of Resurrection.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-ḥashr is the bringing together of a people from their various places of dispersal; it is used specifically for the resurrection gathering.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) for driving cattle together; metaphorical (majāz) for the ingathering of souls for judgment.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Conditional Protasis (al-sharṭ) — "If you are truthful, then rise..." (fa-in kunta ṣādiqan fa-qum...) — the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) functions as the proof of the protasis, establishing necessary knowledge (ʿilm ḍarūrī).

- Root: نشر (n-sh-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To spread, unfold, revive after death; al-nushūr is the revivification of the dead.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-nashr is the spreading of the soul back into the body after death; it is the opposite of al-ṭayy (folding up).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal for unfolding a garment; metaphorical for the resurrection when the earth "spreads forth" what it contains.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Coordination (al-ʿaṭf) — "al-ḥashr wa-l-nashr" (the gathering and the spreading) — two coordinated nouns forming a single compound concept of resurrection.

- Root: مكن (m-k-n)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To establish, empower, give firm footing; makkana means to make something firm and stable.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-makān is the place that contains a thing; tamakkun is the firm establishment of a thing in its place.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal for physical placement; metaphorical for divine power — "God is able" (qādir) means He has full capacity and authority over all things.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Possibility (al-imkān) — "that is possible" (dhālika mumkin) — the predicate of possibility is established by the absence of logical contradiction, not by empirical observation.

- Root: عذب (ʿ-dh-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Sweet, pleasant (of water); al-ʿadhāb is the punishment that is "sweet" to the inflictor but bitter to the recipient — used predominantly for divine chastisement.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-ʿadhāb is the infliction of pain that deters; it is specifically the painful consequence of disobedience.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal for sweet water; metaphorical (majāz) for punishment that is "appointed" as a deterrent.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Exception (al-istithnāʾ) — "except as God wills" (illā mā shāʾa) — the exception clause restricts the scope of human perception, not divine action.
40:46.topic: Al-Ghazali on the journey of the soul, death, and the Hereafter, from 'Foundations of Belief'

40:58.arabic: دونه وادعى الإجماع فيه واستدل بأدلة تشعر بنقيض غرضه كقوله تعالى {الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات} إذ هذا يدل على أن العمل وراء الإيمان لا من نفس الإيمان وإلا فيكون العمل في حكم المعاد والعجب أنه ادعى الإجماع في هذا وهو مع ذلك ينقل قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم لا يكفر أحد إلا بعد جحوده لما أقر به (1) وينكر على المعتزلة قولهم بالتخليد في النار بسبب الكبائر والقائل بهذا قائل بنفس مذهب المعتزلة إذ يقال له من صدق بقلبه وشهد بلسانه ومات في الحال فهل هو في الجنة فلا بد أن يقول نعم وفيه حكم بوجود الإيمان دون العمل فنزيد ونقول لو بقي حيا حتى دخل عليه وقت
40:58.english: He was asked, "Which deed is most excellent?" The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Islam." It was then asked, "Which aspect of Islam is most excellent?" He (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Faith (Īmān)." This is evidence for both the distinction (ikhtilāf) between the two terms and their overlap (tadākhul). This usage is the most consistent with the conventions of the language, because faith is a deed among deeds, and it is the most excellent of them. 40:62.arabic: وفي كل شيء له آية ... تدل على أنه الواحد وكما يقال هذه الصنعة المحكمة تشهد لصانعها بحسن التدبير وكمال العلم لا بمعنى أنها تقول أشهد بالقول ولكن بالذات والحال وكذلك ما من شيء إلا وهو محتاج في نفسه إلى موجد يوجده ويبقيه ويديم أوصافه ويردده في أطواره فهو بحاجته يشهد لخالقه بالتقديس يدرك شهادته ذوو البصائر دون الجامدين على الظواهر ولذلك قال تعالى ولكن لا تفقهون تسبيحهم وأما القاصرون فلا يفقهون أصلا وأما المقربون والعلماء الراسخون فلا يفقهون كنهه وكماله إذ لكل شيء شهاد
40:62.english: The fifth [division] is that one expresses by the tongue of explicit statement (lisān al-maqāl) what belongs to the tongue of state (lisān al-ḥāl). The one of deficient understanding stops at the outward and believes it to be literal speech, while the one with insight into realities perceives the secret within it. This is like the saying of one who said: "The wall said to the peg: 'Why have you split me?' It replied: 'Ask the one who strikes me — he did not leave me behind the stone that is behind me.'" This is an expression of the tongue of state by the tongue of explicit statement.

40:62.anchors:
- Root: علم (ʿalima)

  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Distinguishes literal knowledge (maʿrifah) from awareness (shuʿūr); here, the distinction between superficial knowledge (ẓāhir) and realized knowledge (bāṭin) is rhetorical-metaphorical, not contradictory.
- Root: ظهر (ẓahara)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root denotes outwardness, visibility, strength of back; the ẓāhir is what is manifest and apparent.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The ẓāhir is used metaphorically for the outward aspect of a thing, as opposed to its inner reality (bāṭin); the back (ẓahr) carries what is loaded upon it.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas - Majaz): "قلبت الأمر ظهرا لبطن" — turning a matter over, examining its outward and inward aspects; the ẓāhir is the shell (qishr) that contains and is completed by the inner kernel (lubb).

42:22.arabic: دونه وادعى الإجماع فيه واستدل بأدلة تشعر بنقيض غرضه كقوله تعالى {الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات} إذ هذا يدل على أن العمل وراء الإيمان لا من نفس الإيمان وإلا فيكون العمل في حكم المعاد والعجب أنه ادعى الإجماع في هذا وهو مع ذلك ينقل قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم لا يكفر أحد إلا بعد جحوده لما أقر به (1) وينكر على المعتزلة قولهم بالتخليد في النار بسبب الكبائر والقائل بهذا قائل بنفس مذهب المعتزلة إذ يقال له من صدق بقلبه وشهد بلسانه ومات في الحال فهل هو في الجنة فلا بد أن يقول نعم وفيه حكم بوجود الإيمان دون العمل فنزيد ونقول لو بقي حيا حتى دخل عليه وقت
42:22.english: He was asked, "Which deed is most excellent?" The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Islam." It was then asked, "Which aspect of Islam is most excellent?" 42:45.arabic: ثم زفرت الثالثة فتساقط الخلائق على وجوههم وشخصوا بأبصارهم ينظرون من طرف خفى خاشع وانهضمت عند ذلك قلوب الظالمين فبلغت الحناجر كاظمين وذهلت العقول من السعداء والأشقياء أجمعين وبعد ذلك اقبل الله تعالى على الرسل وقال ماذا أجبتم فإذا رأوا ما قد أقيم من السياسة على الأنبياء اشتد الفزع على العصاة ففر الوالد من ولده والأخ من أخيه والزوج من زوجته وبقى كل واحد منتظرا لأمره ثم يؤخذ واحد واحد فيسأله الله تعالى شفاها عن قليل عمله وكثيره وعن سره وعلانيته وعن جميع جوارحه وأعضائه قال أبو هريرة قالوا يا رسول الله هل نرى ربنا يوم القيامة
42:45.english: {«ماذا أجبتم قالوا لا علم لنا إنك أنت علام الغيوب»} — "What did you answer?" They will say: "We have no knowledge; indeed, You alone are the Knower of the unseen." {Quran 5:109} So woe betide the severity of a Day in which the intellects of the prophets are stupefied and their knowledges are effaced by the sheer intensity of the awe, when it is said to them: "What did you answer, when you were sent to the creatures?" — though they had known — yet their intellects are bewildered, and they know not with what to reply. So they say, from the intensity of the awe: "We have no knowledge; indeed, You alone are the Knower of the unseen." And they are, at that very moment, truthful, for the intellects have flown away from them and the knowledges have been effaced — until God Almighty strengthens them. Then Noah (peace be upon him) is summoned, and it is said to him: "Did you convey the message?" He says: "Yes." Then it is said to his community: "Did he convey to you?" They say: "No warner came to us."
42:45.section_title_en: The Day of Reckoning: The Questioning of the Prophets and the Exposure of the Servant Before the Lord of the Worlds
42:45.anchors:
- Root: رسل (R-S-L)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of "sending forth with ease and gentleness"; a messenger (rasūl) is one dispatched with a message.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الرسول" denotes one sent with a commission; the root conveys both the act of dispatch and the message borne. In the eschatological context, the prophets (rusul) are asked "ماذا أجبتم" — what answer did they give to those to whom they were sent.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (haqīqah): "أرسل الله في الأمم رسلا" — God sent messengers among the nations. Metaphorical (majāz): "أرسل الله عليهم العذاب" — God loosed chastisement upon them. Here, the sending of prophets is literal, but the terror of the Day is such that even their knowledge is effaced.
- Root: علم (ʿ-L-M)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Knowledge, perception, certainty; the opposite of ignorance.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "العلم: إدراك الشيء بحقيقته" — knowledge is the apprehension of a thing in its true reality. On the Day of Terror, the prophets' knowledge (ʿulūmuhum) is erased (tunmaḥū) by the sheer overwhelming majesty (haybah) of the Divine address, leaving them to answer: "لا علم لنا" — "We have no knowledge."
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "علمت الشيء أعلمه" — I knew the thing. Here, the effacement of knowledge is a literal event of the Hour, not metaphorical, for the prophets are truthful when they disavow knowledge in that state.
- Root: يوم (Y-W-M)
  * Lisan / Ayn: A day; a period of time, whether short or long.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "اليوم يعبر به عن وقت طلوع الشمس إلى غروبها. وقد يعبر به عن مدة من الزمان أي مدة كانت" — the day is the time from sunrise to sunset, but it may denote any span of time. The "Day" of Resurrection is a duration whose terrors are magnified beyond earthly measure.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "ما رأيته اليوم" — I did not see him today. Metaphorical: "ذكر في أيام العرب كذا أي في وقائعها" — "days" of the Arabs means their battles. The "Day" of Judgment is a real day, but its horrors are such that the prophets themselves are stupefied.
- Root: الم (ʾ-L-M)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Severe pain, anguish.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الألم الوجع الشديد" — pain is intense suffering. The "عذاب أليم" is a painful chastisement. In this passage, the terror of the Day is an "أليم" affliction upon the hearts of all creatures.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "مسه بضرب أليم" — he touched him with a painful blow. The anguish of the Day is literal and inescapable.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — The construction "إنك أنت علام الغيوب" employs the emphatic pronoun "أنت" as a focused predication, restricting the attribute of absolute knowledge of the unseen to God alone, even as the prophets disavow all knowledge before Him.
42:45.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications, prayers, and their spiritual power, from 'Remembrance of Death and Afterlife'

42:45.arabic: جهنم خالدين فيها} وتخصيصه بالكفر تحكم وقوله تعالى {ألا إن الظالمين في عذاب مقيم} وقال تعالى {ومن جاء بالسيئة فكبت وجوههم في النار} فهذه العمومات في معارضة عموماتهم ولا بد من تسليط التخصص والتأويل على الجانبين لأن الأخبار مصرحة بأن العصاة يعذبون (1) بل قوله تعالى وإن منكم إلا واردها كالصريح في أن ذلك لا بد منه للكل إذ لا يخلو مؤمن عن ذنب يرتكبه وقوله تعالى لا يصلاها إلا الأشقى الذي كذب وتولى أراد به من جماعة مخصوصين أو أراد بالأشقى شخصا معينا أيضا وقوله تعالى كلما ألقى فيها فوج سألهم خزنتها أي فوج من الكفار وتخصيص العمومات
42:45.english: He was asked, "Which deed is most excellent?" The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Islam." It was then asked, "Which aspect of Islam is most excellent?" He (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Faith (Īmān)." This is evidence for both the distinction (ikhtilāf) between the two terms and their overlap (tadākhul). This usage is the most consistent with the conventions of the language, because faith is a deed among deeds, and it is the most excellent of them. Islam is submission (taslīm), whether by the heart, by the tongue, or by the limbs. The most excellent of these is that which is by the heart, which is the assent (taṣdīq) that is called faith. Using the two terms in a way that indicates distinction, overlap, or even complete synonymy (tarāduf) is all within the bounds of metaphorical usage (tajawwuz) in the language.
42:45.section_title_en: The Book of the Revival of the Religious Sciences — Section 99: On the Distinction, Overlap, and Synonymy of Faith (Īmān) and Submission (Islām), and Their Worldly and Otherworldly Judgments
42:45.anchors:
- Root: ايم (A-Y-M)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of remaining unmarried, or a state of being without a spouse; extended metaphorically to describe one who is solitary or without support.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الأيامى: جمع أيم، وهي المرأة التي لا بعل لها... والحرب مأيمة، أي: يفرق بين الزوج والزوجة." The root carries the sense of separation or a state of lacking union, which informs the theological discussion of what constitutes the essential bond of faith.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah) usage denotes the state of being unmarried; metaphorical (Majaz) usage extends to anything that separates or leaves one bereft. This distinction between literal and metaphorical application is central to the chapter's method.
- Root: قلب (Q-L-B)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To turn, overturn, or transform a thing from one state to another.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "قلب الشيء: تصريفه وصرفه عن وجه إلى وجه... والانقلاب: الانصراف." The heart (qalb) is so named for its constant fluctuation and turning. In theological terms, it is the seat of taṣdīq (assent), the immaterial faculty of cognition and conviction.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah) usage is physical turning; metaphorical (Majaz) usage is "قلب الأمور" — to deliberate, scrutinize, and manage affairs. This supports the distinction between the heart's internal act of assent and the external acts of the limbs.
- Root: عمل (ʿ-A-M-L)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Any deed or action performed with purpose and intent.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "العمل: كل فعل يكون من الحيوان بقصد، فهو أخص من الفعل." Work is more specific than mere action, as it implies deliberate, intentional agency. It is used for both righteous and sinful deeds, and is the external manifestation of internal conviction.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah) usage refers to physical labor or deeds. The chapter explores whether "work" is an integral part of the reality of faith or a separate, consequent requirement.
- Root: صدق (S-D-Q)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To be truthful, to speak the truth, to verify.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الصدق والكذب أصلهما في القول... ولا يكونان بالقصد الأول إلا في القول." Truth and falsehood are primarily properties of speech and reports. Taṣdīq (assent) is the heart's affirmation of the truth of a report, which is the core reality of Īmān.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah) usage is truthful speech; metaphorical (Majaz) usage is "صادق الحملة" — one who is true and firm in battle or resolve. This shows that taṣdīq is not merely verbal but a firm, internal resolution.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication). This rule governs how restriction (ḥaṣr) is achieved in Arabic, often through particles like "innamā" or through contextual specification (takhṣīṣ). The chapter's core argument hinges on how terms like Īmān and Islām are semantically restricted, expanded, or made synonymous through contextual usage (majāz), requiring precise parsing of the predicate and its scope.
42:45.topic: Al-Ghazali on the journey of the soul, death, and the Hereafter, from 'Foundations of Belief'

47:2.arabic: دونه وادعى الإجماع فيه واستدل بأدلة تشعر بنقيض غرضه كقوله تعالى {الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات} إذ هذا يدل على أن العمل وراء الإيمان لا من نفس الإيمان وإلا فيكون العمل في حكم المعاد والعجب أنه ادعى الإجماع في هذا وهو مع ذلك ينقل قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم لا يكفر أحد إلا بعد جحوده لما أقر به (1) وينكر على المعتزلة قولهم بالتخليد في النار بسبب الكبائر والقائل بهذا قائل بنفس مذهب المعتزلة إذ يقال له من صدق بقلبه وشهد بلسانه ومات في الحال فهل هو في الجنة فلا بد أن يقول نعم وفيه حكم بوجود الإيمان دون العمل فنزيد ونقول لو بقي حيا حتى دخل عليه وقت
47:2.english: He was asked, "Which deed is most excellent?" The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Islam." It was then asked, "Which aspect of Islam is most excellent?" He (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Faith (Īmān)." This is evidence for both the distinction (ikhtilāf) between the two terms and their overlap (tadākhul). Using the two terms in a way that indicates distinction, overlap, or even complete synonymy (tarāduf) is all within the bounds of metaphorical usage (tajawwuz) in the language.

48:4.arabic: إيمانا وقال تعالى ليزدادوا إيمانا مع إيمانهم وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم فيما يروى في بعض الأخبار الإيمان يزيد وينقص (2) وذلك بتأثير الطاعات في القلب وهذا لا يدركه إلا من راقب أحوال نفسه في أوقات المواظبة على العبادة والتجرد لها بحضور القلب مع أوقات الفتور وإدراك التفاوت في السكون إلى عقائد الإيمان في هذه الأحوال حتى يزيد عقده استعصاء على من يريد حله بالتشكيك بل من يعتقد في اليتيم معنى الرحمة إذا عمل بموجب اعتقاده فمسح رأسه وتلطف به أدرك من باطنه تأكيد الرحمة وتضاعفها بسبب العمل وكذلك مع
48:4.english: And this exists in the true conviction as well. Works effect the growth of this resolve and its increase, just as the watering of trees effects their growth. For this reason God — exalted — said: {فزادتهم إيمانا} "And it increased them in faith" {«فزادتهم إيمانا»} and said: {ليزدادوا إيمانا مع إيمانهم} "That they might increase in faith upon their faith" {«ليزدادوا إيمانا مع إيمانهم»}. And the Prophet — peace be upon him — said, as narrated in some reports: "Faith increases and decreases" (2). That is by the effect of acts of obedience upon the heart. This is perceived only by one who watches over the states of his soul — in the times of persevering in worship and devoting oneself to it with presence of heart — as against the times of languor, and perceives the disparity in tranquility (sukūn) toward the tenets of faith in these states, until his knot increases in resistance to anyone who would undo it by casting doubt. Nay, consider one who holds the meaning of mercy toward an orphan: if he acts upon the requirement of his conviction — wiping the orphan's head and being kind to him — he perceives within his inner self the reinforcement of mercy and its multiplication by reason of the work. Likewise, one who holds the conviction of humility: if he acts upon its requirement — advancing or prostrating before another — he senses in his heart the humility when he undertakes the service.
48:4.section_title_en: On the Increase and Decrease of Faith (Al-Īmān) — Section 100
48:4.anchors:
- Root: زيد (z-y-d)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of increase in quantity, quality, or degree; augmentation upon a pre-existing base.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Increase (ziyādah) presupposes an existing essence (dhāt) that receives accretion; it is not constitutive of the thing's existence but an accident upon it.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) usage applies to corporeal growth (e.g., a man's height); metaphorical (majāz) usage extends to spiritual and moral states, where increase is by qualities, not by essence.
- Root: صدق (ṣ-d-q)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Firmness, veracity, and strength of conviction; the root implies solidity without fissure.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Taṣdīq (assent) is the heart's affirmation of a reported truth, distinguished from mere knowledge by its volitional and settled character.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: confirming a statement as true. Metaphorical: the heart's unwavering resolution (taṣmīm) that admits of degrees of intensity.
- Root: عقد (ʿ-q-d)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Tying, knotting, binding; a knot (ʿuqdah) that holds fast or loosens.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Contract or covenant; here extended to the heart's conviction as a binding knot that strengthens or weakens.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical knotting of a rope. Metaphorical: the firmness of belief as a knot in the heart, subject to tightening and loosening.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — Used to delimit the referent of "faith" (īmān) to taṣdīq alone, excluding works from its essence while affirming their augmentative role.
48:4.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Foundations of Belief'

48:5.arabic: نفسه وعلم ذلك كان كذلك عند الله وكذا من كان مسرورا أو حزينا أو سميعا أو بصيرا ولو قيل للإنسان هل أنت حيوان لم يحسن أن يقول أنا حيوان إن شاء الله ولما قال سفيان ذلك قيل له فماذا نقول قال قولوا آمنا بالله وما أنزل إلينا وأي فرق بين أن يقول آمنا بالله وما أنزل إلينا وبين أن يقول أنا مؤمن وقيل للحسن أمؤمن أنت فقال إن شاء الله فقيل له لم تستثني يا أبا سعيد في الإيمان فقال أخاف أن أقول نعم فيقول الله سبحانه كذبت يا حسن فتحق علي الكلمة وكان يقول ما يؤمنني أن يكون الله سب
48:5.english: If you say: "What is the meaning of the Salaf's statement, 'I am a believer, if God wills' — given that the exception (istithnā') implies doubt, and doubt in faith is unbelief? Yet they all refrained from giving an unqualified answer affirming faith and were cautious about it."
48:5.section_title_en: On the Meaning of the Salaf's Statement "I am a Believer, If God Wills" — Section 102
48:5.anchors:
- Root: نفس (n-f-s)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The self, the soul; that which is breathed; the innermost reality of a person.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): النفس is used for the rūḥ (spirit), for the dhāt (essence/self), and for the seat of intention and knowledge. When one says "he knows in himself (nafsihi) that he is a believer," it denotes certitude residing in the very core of one's being, not a corporeal faculty.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) usage refers to the soul's reflexive self-awareness; metaphorical (majāz) usage extends to "blood" (dam) or "the eye" (ʿayn) of envy. Here, "in himself" (fī nafsihi) is literal self-knowledge, not mere outward profession.
- Root: وجه (w-j-h)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Face, countenance; the foremost part; a mode, aspect, or direction.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The face is the most noble apparent part of a thing; hence it is used for the "aspect" or "manner" (wajh) of an affair. "Four aspects" (wujūh) means four distinct modes of interpretation or rational grounds.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the face of a person or object. Metaphorical: "the face of the matter" (wajh al-amr) — its most salient and honorable dimension. Here, the "aspects" are hermeneutical angles, not physical parts.
- Root: ايم (a-y-m)
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The unmarried state (aym); one who has no spouse. Not applicable here directly, but the root's semantic field of "being alone/without attachment" contrasts with īmān's root (a-m-n) — security and trust — which is the operative term in this text.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Not directly relevant; the operative root is أمن (a-m-n), meaning security from fear, and by extension, faith (īmān) as the state of being secure in God's truth.
- Root: كان (k-w-n)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To be, to exist; the copula of predication.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Kāna denotes existence and becoming; in theological usage, it grounds the distinction between what is (mawjūd) and what is merely asserted. The question "Are you a believer?" (a-mu'min anta?) uses kāna implicitly to ask about actual, present state — not future contingency.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: existence. Metaphorical: the "being-so" of a predicate. The istithnā' (exception) with "in shā' Allāh" suspends the copula's certainty, shifting from assertive existence to contingent hope.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الاستثناء والتعليق بالمشيئة (The Chapter of Exception and Suspension by the Divine Will) — When an exception clause (istithnā') follows a positive assertion, it grammatically suspends the universality or certainty of the predication. In theological discourse, this suspension may be semantic (doubt) or pragmatic (deference, etiquette, or self-deprecation), and Sibawayh's parsing of conditional suspension (taʿlīq) shows that the apodosis need not be negated — only its absolute, unqualified force is tempered.
48:5.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'Foundations of Belief'

48:27.arabic: صلى الله عليه وسلم في النوم حتى نزل قوله تعالى لقد صدق الله ورسوله الرؤيا بالحق (4) وقلما يخلوا الإنسان عن منامات دلت على أمور فوجدها صحيحة والرؤيا ومعرفة الغيب في النوم من عجائب صنع الله تعالى وبدائع فطرة الآدمي وهو من أوضح الأدلة على عالم الملكوت والخلق غافلون عنه كغفلتهم عن سائر عجائب القلب وعجائب العالم والقول في حقيقة الرؤيا من دقائق علوم المكاشفة فلا يمكن ذكره علاوة على علم المعاملة ولكن القدر الذي يمكن ذكره ههنا مثال يفهمك المقصود وهو أن تعلم أن القلب مثاله مثال مرآة تتراءى فيها الصور وحقائق الأمور وأن كل ما قدره
48:27.english: Know that the lights of inner insights (anwār al-baṣā'ir) derived from the Book of God—mighty and majestic is He—and from the Sunnah of His Messenger—may God's peace and blessings be upon him—and from the pathways of reflective consideration, make known to us the states of the dead in general and their division into the blessed and the wretched. But the specific case of Zayd and ʿAmr in particular is not disclosed at all. For if we rely upon the faith of Zayd and ʿAmr, we do not know upon what they died nor how their end was sealed for them. And if we rely upon their outward righteousness, then piety (taqwā) has its seat in the heart, and it is hidden—concealed even from the possessor of that piety himself—so how then from others? Thus there is no ruling for outward righteousness apart from inward piety. God—exalted is He—said: {«إنما يتقبل الله من المتقين»} ["God only accepts from the God-fearing"] (Al-Mā'idah 5:27). So the knowledge of the judgment concerning Zayd and ʿAmr is not possible except by witnessing them and witnessing what transpires upon them. And when one dies, he has transferred from the world of dominion and testimony (ʿālam al-mulk wa al-shahādah) to the world of the unseen and the kingdom (ʿālam al-ghayb wa al-malakūt), so he is not seen by the outward eye. Rather, he is seen only by another eye—that eye being created in the heart of every human being. But upon it has been placed a dense covering (ghishāwah) of his lusts and worldly preoccupations, so that he does not see with it, nor is it conceivable that he should see with it anything of the realm of the kingdom (malakūt) unless that covering is peeled away from the eye of his heart.
48:27.section_title_en: The Unveiling of the Veil: On the Vision of the Dead and the Reality of Dreams
48:27.anchors:
- Root: بصر (B-Ṣ-R)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Inner perception and discernment; the eye as an organ of sight versus the "insight" (baṣīrah) as the heart's eye.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Baṣīrah is the perception of the heart, a spiritual sight (ru'yah qalbiyyah) that penetrates to realities, distinct from mere ocular vision.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) sight is of the physical eye; metaphorical (majāz) sight is the heart's illumination by which hidden truths are disclosed.
- Root: كشف (K-Sh-F)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Removal of a covering; disclosure of what is concealed.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Kashf in the theological sense is the lifting of the veil (ghishāwah) from the heart so that the unseen realm (malakūt) becomes manifest.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: uncovering a physical object; metaphorical: revelation of meanings and hidden affairs to the inner eye.
- Root: لوح (L-W-Ḥ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: A tablet or board upon which writing appears; also the flat bones of the body.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The Preserved Tablet (al-Lawḥ al-Maḥfūẓ) is that upon which all destinies are inscribed; its modality is unknown to us save by report.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: a wooden plank; metaphorical: the divine register of all that was and will be, not corporeal but a subtle reality.
- Root: مثل (M-Th-L)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Likeness, similitude, example; to stand in representation of another.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Mathal is the analogical representation by which an absent or abstract reality is brought near to understanding through a present likeness.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: a resembling image; metaphorical: the parabolic example (mithāl) used to approximate what transcends sensory grasp.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Restriction and Specification (al-ḥaṣr wa al-taqyīd bi-innamā) — The particle "innamā" confines the predicate to the subject alone, as in "إنما يتقبل الله من المتقين," restricting divine acceptance exclusively to the God-fearing, a syntactic anchor for the theological point that outward piety without inward taqwā avails nothing.
48:27.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Remembrance of Death and Afterlife'

48:27.arabic: (5) وقوله تعالى {لقد جاءكم رسول من أنفسكم} إلى آخرها (6) وقوله تعالى {لقد صدق الله رسوله الرؤيا بالحق} إلى آخرها (7) وقوله سبحانه الحمد لله الذي لم يتخذ ولدا (8) الآية وخمس آيات من أول الحديد (9) وثلاثا من آخر سورة الحشر (10) وإن قرأ المسبعات العشر التي أهداها الخضر عليه السلام إلى إبراهيم التيمي رحمه الله ووصاه أن يقولها غدوة وعشية فقد استكمل الفضل وجمع له ذلك فضيلة جملة الأدعية المذكورة فقد روي عن كرز بن وبرة رحمه الله وكان من الأبدال قال أتاني أخ لي من أهل الشام فأهدى لي هدية وقال يا كرز اقبل مني هذه الهدية فإنها نع
48:27.english: Now, the first watch (al-wird al-awwal) is that which extends from the dawn prayer (ṣalāt al-ṣubḥ) until sunrise (ṭulūʿ al-shams). When the servant has completed his obligatory prayer, he should remain seated in his place of prayer, occupying himself with the remembrance of God most High, until the sun has risen. For it has been reported that the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "That I should sit in my assembly, remembering God most High therein, from the morning prayer until sunrise, is more beloved to me than freeing four slaves." {«لأن أقعد في مجلسي أذكر الله تعالى فيه من صلاة الغداة إلى طلوع الشمس أحب إلي من أن أعتق أربع رقاب»} And it is related that he, peace and blessings be upon him, when he had prayed the morning prayer, would sit in his place of prayer until the sun rose; and in some versions [it is added] that he would pray two rakʿahs—that is, after sunrise. Concerning the virtue of this [practice], an incalculable number of reports have come down. Al-Ḥasan related that the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, used to mention, among what he recounted of his Lord's mercy, that He said: "O son of Adam, remember Me for an hour after the dawn prayer and for an hour after the afternoon prayer, and I shall suffice you for what lies between them." {«يا ابن آدم اذكرني بعد صلاة الفجر ساعة وبعد صلاة العصر ساعة أكفك ما بينهما»}
48:27.section_title_en: The Daily Liturgy of the Devout Servant: The First Watch (After Dawn Prayer until Sunrise)
48:27.anchors:
- Root: ذكر (dhakara)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Remembrance, invocation, mention; the opposite of forgetfulness (nisyān).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Remembrance of God (dhikr) is the heart's presence with the Divine, ranging from the tongue's utterance to the heart's contemplation; it is the noblest act when accompanied by presence of heart.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): verbal mention. Metaphorical (majāz): the heart's steadfastness in knowledge of God, which is the reality of dhikr.
- Root: صلا (ṣallā)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Prayer (ṣalāh); root meaning of supplication and blessing; also "to kindle a fire" (as in ṣalā al-nār).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Ṣalāh is the servant's standing before God in humility and devotion, comprising praise, recitation, bowing, and prostration; its perfection lies in the heart's presence.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the ritual prayer with its pillars. Metaphorical: supplication (duʿā') and blessing (taṣliyah) upon the Prophet.
- Root: ورد (warada)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To arrive at water; a portion or share of something that comes regularly.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The daily portion (wird) of devotion—a set liturgy of prayers, recitations, and remembrances that the servant regularly performs at appointed times.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: arriving at a watering place. Metaphorical: the soul's regular approach to the fountain of divine grace through prescribed acts of worship.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Restriction and Specification (al-ḥaṣr wa al-taqyīd) — governing the precise enumeration of the four functions (adʿiyah, adhkār, qirā'ah, fikr) after the dawn prayer, each specified by its own governing verb and object.
48:27.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications, prayers, and their spiritual power, from 'Arrangement of Litanies'

48:27.arabic: الاستقبال كقوله تعالى لتدخلن المسجد الحرام إن شاء الله آمنين محلقين رؤوسكم ومقصرين وكقوله ألم غلبت الروم في أدنى الأرض وهم من بعد غلبهم سيغلبون في بضع سنين ووجه دلالة المعجزة على صدق الرسل أن كل ما عجز عنه البشر لم يكن إلا فعلا لله تعالى فمهما كان مقرونا بتحدي النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ينزل منزلة قوله صدقت وذلك مثل القائل بين يدي 2 الملك المدعي على رعيته أنه رسول الملك إليهم فإنه مهما قال لذلك إن كنت صادقا فقم على سريرك ثلاثا واقعد على خلاف عادتك ففعل الملك ذلك حصل للحاضرين علم ضروري بأن ذلك نازل منزلة قوله صدقت الركن ا
48:27.english: For they, despite their distinction in eloquence and rhetorical perfection, aimed at reviling him, forbidding him, killing him, and expelling him — as God, Mighty and Majestic, informed us about them — yet they were unable to produce anything to rival the Qur'an. For it was not within the capacity of human beings to combine the grandeur of the Qur'an's diction with its harmonious order, especially given what it contains of the accounts of the ancients, while he was illiterate, never having practiced the study of books — and [given] its announcement of the unseen in matters whose truthfulness was verified in the future, such as His saying, Exalted is He: {«لَتَدْخُلُنَّ الْمَسْجِدَ الْحَرَامَ إِنْ شَاءَ اللَّهُ آمِنِينَ مُحَلِّقِينَ رُءُوسَكُمْ وَمُقَصِّرِينَ»} (You shall surely enter the Sacred Mosque, if God wills, secure, with your heads shaved and cut short) [Al-Fatḥ 48:27], and such as His saying: {«الم غُلِبَتِ الرُّومُ فِي أَدْنَى الْأَرْضِ وَهُمْ مِنْ بَعْدِ غَلَبِهِمْ سَيَغْلِبُونَ فِي بِضْعِ سِنِينَ»} (Alif Lām Mīm. The Romans have been defeated in the nearest land, and they, after their defeat, shall be victorious within a few years) [Al-Rūm 30:1-3].
48:27.section_title_en: The Fourth Pillar: On Matters of Hearing (al-Samʿiyyāt) and the Verification of the Prophet ﷺ in What He Reported — Comprising Ten Fundamental Principles
48:27.anchors:
- Root: حشر (ḥ-sh-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To gather, assemble, drive together; al-ḥashr is the gathering of creation on the Day of Resurrection.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-ḥashr is the bringing together of a people from their various places of dispersal; it is used specifically for the resurrection gathering.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) for driving cattle together; metaphorical (majāz) for the ingathering of souls for judgment.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Conditional Protasis (al-sharṭ) — "If you are truthful, then rise..." (fa-in kunta ṣādiqan fa-qum...) — the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) functions as the proof of the protasis, establishing necessary knowledge (ʿilm ḍarūrī).

- Root: نشر (n-sh-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To spread, unfold, revive after death; al-nushūr is the revivification of the dead.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-nashr is the spreading of the soul back into the body after death; it is the opposite of al-ṭayy (folding up).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal for unfolding a garment; metaphorical for the resurrection when the earth "spreads forth" what it contains.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Coordination (al-ʿaṭf) — "al-ḥashr wa-l-nashr" (the gathering and the spreading) — two coordinated nouns forming a single compound concept of resurrection.

- Root: مكن (m-k-n)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To establish, empower, give firm footing; makkana means to make something firm and stable.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-makān is the place that contains a thing; tamakkun is the firm establishment of a thing in its place.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal for physical placement; metaphorical for divine power — "God is able" (qādir) means He has full capacity and authority over all things.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Possibility (al-imkān) — "that is possible" (dhālika mumkin) — the predicate of possibility is established by the absence of logical contradiction, not by empirical observation.

- Root: عذب (ʿ-dh-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Sweet, pleasant (of water); al-ʿadhāb is the punishment that is "sweet" to the inflictor but bitter to the recipient — used predominantly for divine chastisement.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-ʿadhāb is the infliction of pain that deters; it is specifically the painful consequence of disobedience.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal for sweet water; metaphorical (majāz) for punishment that is "appointed" as a deterrent.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Exception (al-istithnāʾ) — "except as God wills" (illā mā shāʾa) — the exception clause restricts the scope of human perception, not divine action.
48:27.topic: Classical commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya Ulum al-Din, from 'Foundations of Belief'

48:27.arabic: الاحتمال في كتاب الحلال والحرام إن شاء الله تعالى
48:27.english: The second: that he thank the giver, supplicate for him, and praise him; and his gratitude and supplication should be such that it does not remove him from being a mere intermediary, but rather he is a channel for the arrival of God's blessing to him. And the channel has a right, insofar as God made him a channel and an intermediary — and that does not negate seeing the blessing as from God, Glorified be He. For he, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "He who does not thank the people has not thanked God" {«من لم يشكر الناس لم يشكر الله»}. And God, Mighty and Majestic, has praised His servants in places for their deeds, while He is their Creator and the Originator of the capacity for them — such as His saying, Exalted is He: {«نعم العبد إنه أواب»} ["Excellent is the servant. Indeed, he is penitent."] — and other similar instances.
48:27.section_title_en: The Etiquette of the Recipient of Wealth: On the Virtue of Poverty and the Conduct of Taking from Others
48:27.anchors:
- Root: كرم (karuma)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root meaning: nobility, generosity, honorableness of origin and character.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: Divine Generosity (al-Karam) as an attribute of God entailing beneficence (al-Ifḍāl) that is pure grace, not obligation.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: nobility of lineage/character. Metaphorical: God's abundant giving without recompense.
- Root: فضل (faḍala)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root meaning: surplus, excess, superiority, that which remains beyond need.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: God's Bounty (al-Faḍl) as gratuitous favor exceeding what is merited; distinct from justice ('Adl).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: excess/surplus. Metaphorical: divine favor and grace.
- Root: نعم (ni'ma)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root meaning: well-being, bounty, benefaction; state of goodness.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-Ni'ma as the good state (al-ḥālah al-ḥasanah) bestowed by God; its genus encompasses both little and much.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: pleasant life and bounty. Metaphorical: "خفت نعامتهم" (their ostriches departed) — i.e., they went away, indicating the fleeting nature of worldly boons.
- Root: قدر (qadara)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root meaning: measure, extent, power, decree.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-Qudrah for God is the negation of incapacity; for man, a capacity for specific acts. Al-Qadr: the divine measure/decree.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: measure, amount, power. Metaphorical: "فرس بعيد القدر" (a horse of far-reaching stride) — extended reach.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — Governing the precise restriction of agency and causation in statements like "إنما المنكر أن يرى الواسطة أصلا" (The only objectionable thing is to regard the intermediary as the origin).
48:27.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications, prayers, and their spiritual power, from 'Mysteries of Zakat'

48:27.arabic: فيما لا يشك فيه بل قال تعالى لتدخلن المسجد الحرام إن شاء الله آمنين محلقين رءؤسكم ومقصرين وكان الله سبحانه عالما بأنهم يدخلون لا محالة وأنه شاءه ولكن المقصود تعليمه ذلك فتأدب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في ما كان يخبر عنه معلوما كان أو مشكوكا حتى قال صلى الله عليه وسلم لما دخل المقابر السلام عليكم دار قوم مؤمنين وإنا إن شاء الله بكم لاحقون (1) واللحوق بهم غير مشكوك فيه ولكن مقتضى الأدب ذكر الله تعالى وربط الأمور به وهذه الصيغة دالة عليه حتى صار بعرف الاستعمال عبارة عن إظهار الرغبة والتمني فإذا قيل لك إن فلانا يموت سريعا فتقول إن شاء الله
48:27.english: If you say: "What is the meaning of the Salaf's statement, 'I am a believer, if God wills' — given that the exception (istithnā') implies doubt, and doubt in faith is unbelief? Yet they all refrained from giving an unqualified answer affirming faith and were cautious about it."
48:27.section_title_en: On the Meaning of the Salaf's Statement "I am a Believer, If God Wills" — Section 102
48:27.anchors:
- Root: نفس (n-f-s)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The self, the soul; that which is breathed; the innermost reality of a person.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): النفس is used for the rūḥ (spirit), for the dhāt (essence/self), and for the seat of intention and knowledge. When one says "he knows in himself (nafsihi) that he is a believer," it denotes certitude residing in the very core of one's being, not a corporeal faculty.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) usage refers to the soul's reflexive self-awareness; metaphorical (majāz) usage extends to "blood" (dam) or "the eye" (ʿayn) of envy. Here, "in himself" (fī nafsihi) is literal self-knowledge, not mere outward profession.
- Root: وجه (w-j-h)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Face, countenance; the foremost part; a mode, aspect, or direction.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The face is the most noble apparent part of a thing; hence it is used for the "aspect" or "manner" (wajh) of an affair. "Four aspects" (wujūh) means four distinct modes of interpretation or rational grounds.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the face of a person or object. Metaphorical: "the face of the matter" (wajh al-amr) — its most salient and honorable dimension. Here, the "aspects" are hermeneutical angles, not physical parts.
- Root: ايم (a-y-m)
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The unmarried state (aym); one who has no spouse. Not applicable here directly, but the root's semantic field of "being alone/without attachment" contrasts with īmān's root (a-m-n) — security and trust — which is the operative term in this text.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Not directly relevant; the operative root is أمن (a-m-n), meaning security from fear, and by extension, faith (īmān) as the state of being secure in God's truth.
- Root: كان (k-w-n)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To be, to exist; the copula of predication.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Kāna denotes existence and becoming; in theological usage, it grounds the distinction between what is (mawjūd) and what is merely asserted. The question "Are you a believer?" (a-mu'min anta?) uses kāna implicitly to ask about actual, present state — not future contingency.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: existence. Metaphorical: the "being-so" of a predicate. The istithnā' (exception) with "in shā' Allāh" suspends the copula's certainty, shifting from assertive existence to contingent hope.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الاستثناء والتعليق بالمشيئة (The Chapter of Exception and Suspension by the Divine Will) — When an exception clause (istithnā') follows a positive assertion, it grammatically suspends the universality or certainty of the predication. In theological discourse, this suspension may be semantic (doubt) or pragmatic (deference, etiquette, or self-deprecation), and Sibawayh's parsing of conditional suspension (taʿlīq) shows that the apodosis need not be negated — only its absolute, unqualified force is tempered.
48:27.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Foundations of Belief'

49:14.arabic: وأما الاختلاف فقوله تعالى {قالت الأعراب آمنا قل لم تؤمنوا ولكن قولوا أسلمنا} ومعناه استسلمنا في الظاهر فأراد بالإيمان ههنا التصديق بالقلب فقط وبالإسلام الاستسلام ظاهرا باللسان والجوارح وفي حديث جبرائيل عليه السلام لما سأله عن الإيمان فقال أن تؤمن بالله وملائكته وكتبه ورسله واليوم الآخر وبالبعث بعد الموت وبالحساب وبالقدر خيره وشره فقال فما الإسلام فأجاب بذكر الخصال الخمس (3) فعبر بالإسلام عن تسليم الظاهر بالقول والعمل وفي الحديث عن سعد أنه صلى الله عليه وسلم أعطى رجلا عطاء ولم يعط الآخر فقال له سعد يا رسول الله تركت فلانا لم
49:14.english: The truth in this matter is that faith (iman) is an expression for assent (tasdiq). God, exalted be He, has said: {وَمَا أَنتَ بِمُؤْمِنٍ لِّنَا} [And you are not one to believe us] (Quran 12:17) — that is, not one to assent to us. And Islam is an expression for surrender (taslim) and self-abandonment (istislam) through acquiescence (idhan) and compliance (inqiyad), and the abandonment of recalcitrance, refusal, obstinacy, and stubbornness.
49:14.section_title_en: On Whether Islam and Faith (Iman) Are Identical or Distinct
49:14.anchors:
- Root: أمن (amana)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root denotes safety, security, and freedom from fear; the isti'man form yields 'belief' as an act of granting credence and trust.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الإيمان هو التصديق" — Faith (iman) is fundamentally assent (tasdiq), a conviction of the heart, not a mere verbal profession.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah) usage ties iman to tasdiq (verification/assent); metaphorical extension applies it to outward compliance only in a derived sense.
- Root: سلم (salima)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root denotes soundness, safety, and freedom from defect; the istislam form yields 'submission' as an act of yielding and surrendering.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الإسلام عبارة عن التسليم والاستسلام" — Islam is surrender (taslim) and self-abandonment (istislam) through compliance and obedience.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah) usage encompasses outward acts of the limbs; metaphorical (Majaz) usage can extend to inward assent, but the primary domain is the external.
- Root: صدق (sadaqa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root denotes truthfulness and veracity in speech and report.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الصدق والكذب أصلهما في القول" — Truth and falsehood originate in speech; tasdiq is the act of affirming a report as true.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah) usage is in verbal confirmation; metaphorical extension applies to 'true in resolve' or 'true in attack,' i.e., confirming through action.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Interposition (باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور) — Governing the permissible separation between a governing word and its governed prepositional phrase, relevant here for parsing the conditional and contrastive structures in the theological arguments.
49:14.topic: Al-Ghazali on the journey of the soul, death, and the Hereafter, from 'Foundations of Belief'

49:15.arabic: فقد قال الله تعالى إنما المؤمنون الذين آمنوا بالله ورسوله ثم لم يرتابوا وجاهدوا بأموالهم وأنفسهم في سبيل الله أولئك هم الصادقون {فيكون}
49:15.english: If you say: "What is the meaning of the Salaf's statement, 'I am a believer, if God wills' — given that the exception (istithnā') implies doubt, and doubt in faith is unbelief? Yet they all refrained from giving an unqualified answer affirming faith and were cautious about it."
49:15.section_title_en: On the Meaning of the Salaf's Statement "I am a Believer, If God Wills" — Section 102

  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Kāna denotes existence and becoming; in theological usage, it grounds the distinction between what is (mawjūd) and what is merely asserted. The question "Are you a believer?" (a-mu'min anta?) uses kāna implicitly to ask about actual, present state — not future contingency.
