- Sibawayh Rule: باب الاستثناء والتعليق بالمشيئة (The Chapter of Exception and Suspension by the Divine Will) — When an exception clause (istithnā') follows a positive assertion, it grammatically suspends the universality or certainty of the predication. In theological discourse, this suspension may be semantic (doubt) or pragmatic (deference, etiquette, or self-deprecation), and Sibawayh's parsing of conditional suspension (taʿlīq) shows that the apodosis need not be negated — only its absolute, unqualified force is tempered.
49:15.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Foundations of Belief'

50:19.arabic: يدري أنه من الذين سبقت لهم من الله الحسنى وقيل في معنى قوله تعالى {وجاءت سكرة الموت بالحق} أي بالسابقة يعني أظهرتها وقال بعض السلف إنما يوزن من الأعمال خواتيمها وكان أبو الدرداء رضي الله عنه يحلف بالله ما من أحد يأمن أن يسلب إيمانه إلا سلبه وقيل من الذنوب ذنوب عقوبتها سوء الخاتمة نعوذ بالله من ذلك وقيل هي عقوبات دعوى الولاية والكرامة بالافتراء وقال بعض العارفين لو عرضت علي الشهادة عند باب الدار والموت على التوحيد
50:19.english: ...doubt concerning this truthfulness. Likewise, God Most High said: {«But righteousness is he who believes in God and the Last Day and the angels and the Book and the prophets»} (2:177) — thus He conditioned twenty attributes, such as faithfulness to covenant and patience under hardship. Then He said Most High: {«Those are the truthful ones»} (2:177). And God Most High said: {«God will raise those who have believed among you and those who have been given knowledge, by degrees»} (58:11). And He said Most High: {«Not equal among you are those who spent before the conquest and fought»} (57:10). And He said Most High: {«They are degrees before God»} (3:163). And the Prophet, peace be upon him, said: "Faith is naked, and its garment is God-consciousness (al-taqwā)." And the Prophet, peace be upon him, said: "Faith has seventy-some branches; the lowest of them is removing harm from the path." All this indicates the interconnection of the perfection of faith with works.
50:19.section_title_en: The Revival of the Religious Sciences — Book of the Secrets of Zakāh, Section 104: On the Degrees of Faith and Its Connection to Works, and the Hidden Hypocrisy (al-Nifāq al-Khafī) That Contradicts the Perfection of Faith
50:19.anchors:
- Root: ن ف ق (N-F-Q)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Root denotes passing away, depletion, and expenditure; also the underground burrow of the jerboa (nāfiqāʾ) with a concealed exit — the etymological basis for hypocrisy as a hidden exit from faith.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "نفق الشيء: مضى ونفد" — theological nuance: hypocrisy (nifāq) is that which causes faith to expire and pass away, whether by sale (worldly gain) or by death (spiritual ruin).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "نفقت الدراهم" (coins ran out). Metaphorical: "نفق روحه: خرج" (his soul expired and went forth) — hence the hypocrite's faith is one whose spirit has already departed.
- Root: أ ي م (A-Y-M)
  * Lisan / Ayn: A woman without a husband; a man long unmarried. Al-Raghib: "الحرب مأيمة" — war makes women widows.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "تركوا النساء أيامى" (they left women widowed). Metaphorical application: the one who feels secure from hypocrisy is like one who claims immunity from widowhood — a false security.
- Root: و ف ي (W-F-Y)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Fullness, completion, fulfillment of a measure or covenant.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الوافي: الذي بلغ التمام" — the one who has reached completion. "أوفى: إذا تمم العهد ولم ينقض حفظه" — to fulfill the covenant without breach.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "درهم واف" (a full-weight dirham). Metaphorical: "أوفى على المائة" (he surpassed a hundred) — faith's perfection (wafāʾ) is only attained by surpassing mere profession to include works and inward sincerity.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد (Restriction & Focused Predication) — governing the grammatical force of "إنما" constructions and conditional clauses (من كان...), where the predicate is restricted to the condition stated, as in the hadith "أربع من كن فيه فهو منافق خالص" — the four traits are exhaustive of the ruling.
50:19.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'Foundations of Belief'

50:19.arabic: فكشف عن وجهه وقال ليس كذا ولكن قولي {وجاءت سكرة الموت بالحق ذلك ما كنت منه تحيد} انظروا ثوبي هذين فاغسلوهما وكفنوني فيهما فإن الحي إلى الجديد أحوج من الميت وقالت عائشة رضي الله عنها عند موته وأبيض يستسقى الغمام بوجهه .
50:19.english: When Abu Bakr (may Allah Most High be pleased with him) was in the throes of death, ʿĀʾishah (may Allah be pleased with her) came and recited this verse: "By your life, wealth avails not the youth... when the breath rattles in his chest one day, and the breast is straitened thereby."
50:19.section_title_en: The Death of Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (may Allah Most High be pleased with him)
50:19.anchors:
- Root: حشرج (ḥashraja)
  * Lisan / Ayn: [Core linguistic root meaning: The rattling, gurgling sound of the death-throe in the throat; the final breath struggling in the chest.]
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): [Theological/Kalam semantic nuance: The terminal state of the soul's separation from the body, the moment of overwhelming divine decree.]
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): [Literal vs Metaphorical distinction: Literal — the physical rattle of the dying; Metaphorical — the constriction of the breast as the soul is drawn forth.]
- Root: سكر (sakara)
  * Lisan / Ayn: [Core linguistic root meaning: The veiling of the intellect; intoxication; the stupor that overcomes one at the onset of death.]
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): [Theological/Kalam semantic nuance: The stupor of death (sakrat al-mawt) as the removal of all veils, wherein the truth of the Hereafter becomes undeniably present.]
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): [Literal vs Metaphorical distinction: Literal — intoxication from drink; Metaphorical — the overwhelming bewilderment of the soul at death's onset.]
- Root: ذمم (dhimam)
  * Lisan / Ayn: [Core linguistic root meaning: The covenant of protection; the bond of safe-conduct; that which one is obligated to honor and safeguard.]
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): [Theological/Kalam semantic nuance: The divine guarantee (dhimmat Allah) extended to the believer who prays the dawn prayer — a sacred pact not to be violated.]
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): [Literal vs Metaphorical distinction: Literal — a pledge of security between men; Metaphorical — the inviolable covenant between the servant and his Lord.]
- Root: وزن (wazana)
  * Lisan / Ayn: [Core linguistic root meaning: To weigh; the balance; the measure of equivalence between two things.]
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): [Theological/Kalam semantic nuance: The weighing of deeds on the Day of Resurrection as the manifestation of divine justice — the scales (mawāzīn) receiving only truth or falsehood.]
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): [Literal vs Metaphorical distinction: Literal — the physical act of weighing; Metaphorical — the spiritual weighing of deeds by their conformity to truth (ḥaqq) or falsehood (bāṭil).]
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — [The particle innamā restricts the predicate exclusively to its subject, as in Abu Bakr's dictum: "It is only that the scales of those whose scales are heavy on the Day of Resurrection are weighed down by their following the truth in this world."]
50:19.topic: Al-Ghazali on the journey of the soul, death, and the Hereafter, from 'Remembrance of Death and Afterlife'

50:37.arabic: لذكرى لمن كان له قلب أو ألقى السمع وهو شهيد} ومعنى كونه ذا قلب أن يكون قابلا للعلم فهما ثم لا تعينه القدرة على الفهم حتى يلقي السمع وهو شهيد حاضر القلب ليستقيل كل ما ألقى إليه بحسن الإصغاء والضراعة والشكر والفرح وقبول المنة فليكن المتعلم لمعلمه كأرض دمثة نالت مطرا غزيرا فتشربت جميع أجزائها وأذعنت بالكلية لقبوله ومهما أشار عليه المعلم بطريق في التعلم فليقلده وليدع رأيه فإن خطأ مرشده أنفع له من صوابه في نفسه إذ التجربة تطلع على دقائق يستغرب سماعها مع أنه يعظم نفعها فكم من مريض محرور يعالجة
50:37.english: I say: Knowledge is like a torrent that is hostile to the elevated place — it flows only to the low ground. Thus knowledge is not attained except through humility and the casting of one's hearing [in attentive submission]. God — exalted is He — said: {«Indeed in that is a reminder for whoever has a heart or casts his hearing while present as a witness»} (Q 50:37). And the meaning of his being "one having a heart" is that he should be receptive to knowledge, comprehending it. But then the capacity for understanding does not avail him until he casts his hearing while being a present witness — present of heart — so that he may receive everything that is cast to him with excellence of listening, supplication, gratitude, joy, and acceptance of the benefaction.
50:37.section_title_en: The Revival of the Religious Sciences — Book I, Section 42: On the Duties of the Student (Ādāb al-Mutaʿallim)
50:37.anchors:
- Root: ع ل م (ʿ-l-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of knowing, perceiving a thing in its reality; the mark, trace, or sign by which one is guided.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "العلم: إدراك الشيء بحقيقته" — knowledge is the apprehension of a thing in its true reality, divided into apprehension of the essence and judgment upon it.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): "هو من أعلام العلم الخافقه" — he is among the lofty banners of knowledge. Metaphorical (majāz): "خفيت معالم الطريق" — the waymarks of the road are hidden, i.e., the traces by which one is guided.
- Root: س م ع (s-m-ʿ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Hearing, listening; the ear; obedience and acceptance.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Hearing with attentive presence of heart, not merely the physical sensation of sound.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: auditory perception. Metaphorical: "ألقى السمع" — to cast one's hearing, i.e., to listen with full attentiveness and submission.
- Root: ق ل ب (q-l-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The heart; to turn, overturn, or transform a thing from one state to another.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "قلب الشيء: تصريفه وصرفه عن وجه إلى وجه" — the turning of a thing from one face to another; the heart as that which is ever-turning between states.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "قلب الشيء قلبا: حوله عن وجهه" — to turn a thing from its face. Metaphorical: "رجل قلب حول: يقلب الأمور ويحتال" — a man who turns matters over and devises means.
- Root: ب ح ر (b-ḥ-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The sea; vast expanse of water.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "أصل البحر: كل مكان واسع جامع للماء الكثير" — the sea is every vast place gathering much water; then metaphorically applied to one who expands deeply into a domain.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Metaphorical: "تبحر في العلم واستبحر فيه" — he plunged deep into knowledge and expanded therein like a sea.
- Sibawayh Rule: Bāb al-ḥaṣr wa-l-taqyīd bi-innamā (Restriction and Focused Predication) — the particle innamā restricts the predicate to the subject alone, negating all else; applied here to the exclusive path of the student's submission to the teacher's direction.

50:37.arabic: فلا ينال العلم إلا بالتواضع وإلقاء السمع قال الله تعالى {إن في ذلك لذكرى لمن كان له قلب أو ألقى السمع وهو شهيد} ومعنى كونه ذا قلب أن يكون قابلا للعلم فهما ثم لا تعينه القدرة على الفهم حتى يلقي السمع وهو شهيد حاضر القلب ليستقيل كل ما ألقى إليه بحسن الإصغاء والضراعة والشكر والفرح وقبول المنة فليكن المتعلم لمعلمه كأرض دمثة نالت مطرا غزيرا فتشربت جميع أجزائها وأذعنت بالكلية لقبوله ومهما أشار عليه المعلم بطريق في التعلم فليقلده وليدع رأيه فإن خطأ مرشده أنفع له من صوابه في نفسه إذ التجربة تطلع على دقائق يستغرب سماعها مع أنه يعظم نفعها فكم من مريض محرور يعالجة الطبي

51:35.arabic: الترادف ففيقوله تعالى فأخرجنا من كان فيها من المؤمنين فما وجدنا فيها غير بيت من المسلمين ولم يكن بالاتفاق إلا بيت واحد وقال تعالى يا قوم إن كنتم آمنتم بالله فعليه توكلوا إن كنتم مسلمين وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم بني الإسلام على خمس (1) وسئل رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم مرة عن الإيمان فأجاب بهذه الخمس (2) وأما الاختلاف فقوله تعالى {قالت الأعراب آمنا قل لم تؤمنوا ولكن قولوا أسلمنا} ومعناه استسلمنا في الظاهر فأراد بالإيمان ههنا التصديق بالقلب فقط وبالإسلام الاستسلام ظاهرا باللسان والجوارح وفي حديث جبرائيل عليه السلام لما سأله عن الإيمان فقال أ
51:35.english: The truth in this matter is that faith (iman) is an expression for assent (tasdiq). God, exalted be He, has said: {وَمَا أَنتَ بِمُؤْمِنٍ لِّنَا} [And you are not one to believe us] (Quran 12:17) — that is, not one to assent to us. And Islam is an expression for surrender (taslim) and self-abandonment (istislam) through acquiescence (idhan) and compliance (inqiyad), and the abandonment of recalcitrance, refusal, obstinacy, and stubbornness.
51:35.section_title_en: On Whether Islam and Faith (Iman) Are Identical or Distinct
51:35.anchors:
- Root: أمن (amana)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root denotes safety, security, and freedom from fear; the isti'man form yields 'belief' as an act of granting credence and trust.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الإيمان هو التصديق" — Faith (iman) is fundamentally assent (tasdiq), a conviction of the heart, not a mere verbal profession.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah) usage ties iman to tasdiq (verification/assent); metaphorical extension applies it to outward compliance only in a derived sense.
- Root: سلم (salima)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root denotes soundness, safety, and freedom from defect; the istislam form yields 'submission' as an act of yielding and surrendering.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الإسلام عبارة عن التسليم والاستسلام" — Islam is surrender (taslim) and self-abandonment (istislam) through compliance and obedience.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah) usage encompasses outward acts of the limbs; metaphorical (Majaz) usage can extend to inward assent, but the primary domain is the external.
- Root: صدق (sadaqa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root denotes truthfulness and veracity in speech and report.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الصدق والكذب أصلهما في القول" — Truth and falsehood originate in speech; tasdiq is the act of affirming a report as true.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah) usage is in verbal confirmation; metaphorical extension applies to 'true in resolve' or 'true in attack,' i.e., confirming through action.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Interposition (باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور) — Governing the permissible separation between a governing word and its governed prepositional phrase, relevant here for parsing the conditional and contrastive structures in the theological arguments.
51:35.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'Foundations of Belief'

56:58.arabic: من الأرض نباتا ثم يعيدكم فيها ويخرجكم إخراجا وقال تعالى أفرأيتم ما تمنون أأنتم تخلقونه أم نحن الخالقون إلى قوله للمقوين فليس يخفي على من معه أدنى مسكة من عقل إذا تأمل بأدنى فكرة مضمون هذه الآيات وأدار نظره على عجائب خلق الله في الأرض والسموات وبدائع فطرة الحيوان والنبات أن هذا الأمر العجيب والترتيب المحكم لا يستغني عن صانع يدبره وفاعل يحكمه ويقدره بل تكاد فطرة النفوس تشهد بكونها مقهورة تحت تسخيره ومصرفة بمقتضى تدبيره ولذلك قال الله تعالى أفي الله شك فاطر السموات والأرض ولهذا بعث الأنبياء صلوات الله عليهم لدعوة الخلق إلى التوحيد ليقولوا لا إله إلا
56:58.english: The First Principle: the knowledge of His existence, the Exalted. The first thing by which one is illuminated from among the lights, and the path of reflection (ṭarīq al-iʿtibār) by which one proceeds, is that to which the Qurʾān has guided. For after the explanation of God, glorified be He, there is no explanation. He, the Exalted, has said: {«أَلَمْ نَجْعَلِ الْأَرْضَ مِهَادًا وَالْجِبَالَ أَوْتَادًا وَخَلَقْنَاكُمْ أَزْوَاجًا وَجَعَلْنَا نَوْمَكُمْ سُبَاتًا وَجَعَلْنَا اللَّيْلَ لِبَاسًا وَجَعَلْنَا النَّهَارَ مَعَاشًا وَبَنَيْنَا فَوْقَكُمْ سَبْعًا شِدَادًا وَجَعَلْنَا سِرَاجًا وَهَّاجًا وَأَنزَلْنَا مِنَ الْمُعْصِرَاتِ مَاءً ثَجَّاجًا لِّنُخْرِجَ بِهِ حَبًّا وَنَبَاتًا وَجَنَّاتٍ أَلْفَافًا»} — "Have We not made the earth a resting place, and the mountains as pegs, and created you in pairs, and made your sleep a repose, and made the night a covering, and made the day for livelihood, and built above you seven strong heavens, and made a blazing lamp, and sent down from the rain-clouds pouring water, that We may bring forth thereby grain and vegetation, and gardens dense with foliage?" (Q 78:6–16). And He, the Exalted, has said: {«إِنَّ فِي خَلْقِ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَاخْتِلَافِ اللَّيْلِ وَالنَّهَارِ وَالْفُلْكِ الَّتِي تَجْرِي فِي الْبَحْرِ بِمَا يَنفَعُ النَّاسَ وَمَا أَنزَلَ اللَّهُ مِنَ السَّمَاءِ مِن مَّاءٍ فَأَحْيَا بِهِ الْأَرْضَ بَعْدَ مَوْتِهَا وَبَثَّ فِيهَا مِن كُلِّ دَابَّةٍ وَتَصْرِيفِ الرِّيَاحِ وَالسَّحَابِ الْمُسَخَّرِ بَيْنَ السَّمَاءِ وَالْأَرْضِ لَآيَاتٍ لِّقَوْمٍ يَعْقِلُونَ»} — "Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth, and the alternation of the night and the day, and the ships which sail through the sea with that which benefits people, and what God has sent down from the sky of water, thereby reviving the earth after its death, and dispersing therein every creature, and the directing of the winds, and the clouds subservient between the heaven and the earth — are signs for a people who reason" (Q 2:164). And He, the Exalted, has said: {«أَلَمْ تَرَوْا كَيْفَ خَلَقَ اللَّهُ سَبْعَ سَمَاوَاتٍ طِبَاقًا وَجَعَلَ الْقَمَرَ فِيهِنَّ نُورًا وَجَعَلَ الشَّمْسَ سِرَاجًا وَاللَّهُ أَنبَتَكُم مِّنَ الْأَرْضِ نَبَاتًا ثُمَّ يُعِيدُكُمْ فِيهَا وَيُخْرِجُكُمْ إِخْرَاجًا»} — "Have you not seen how God created seven heavens in layers, and made the moon therein a light, and made the sun a lamp? And God caused you to grow from the earth a growth; then He returns you into it, and brings you forth a bringing forth" (Q 71:15–18). And He, the Exalted, has said: {«أَفَرَأَيْتُم مَّا تُمْنُونَ أَأَنتُمْ تَخْلُقُونَهُ أَمْ نَحْنُ الْخَالِقُونَ»} — "Have you considered what you emit? Do you create it, or are We the Creator?" — up to His saying: {«لِلْمُقْوِينَ»} — "for the settlers" (Q 56:58–73).
56:58.section_title_en: The Pillars of Faith: Knowledge of God, His Attributes, His Acts, and the Audibles — Section 87
56:58.anchors:
- Root: وجود (w-j-d)
  * Lisan / Ayn: [Core linguistic root meaning: to find, to perceive, to be; existence as that which is found or discovered]
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): [Theological/Kalam semantic nuance: al-wujūd as necessary existence (wujūb) versus contingent existence (imkān); the self-evident reality of the Creator's being]
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): [Literal vs Metaphorical distinction: haqīqah — existence as affirmed reality; majāz — "finding" as in discovery, not applicable to God's necessary being]
- Root: خلق (kh-l-q)
  * Lisan / Ayn: [Core linguistic root meaning: measuring, proportioning, fashioning; origination of a thing upon a measure]
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الخلق أصله: التقدير المستقيم، ويستعمل في إبداع الشيء من غير أصل ولا احتذاء" — creation as origination from nothing without prior model
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): [Literal: خلق الله الخلق: أوجده على تقدير أوجبته الحكمة — brought into existence upon a measure necessitated by wisdom; Majaz: not applicable to God's act as pure origination]
- Root: فطر (f-t-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: [Core linguistic root meaning: to split, cleave, rend; to originate, to bring forth as a new creation]
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "فطر الله الخلق" — God's origination of creation as a primordial act; "الفطرة" as the innate disposition
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): [Literal: فطر الله الخلق، وهو فاطر السموات: مبتدعها — originator without precedent; Majaz: "رأيه فطير" — immature opinion, not applicable to divine]
- Root: ارض (ar-d)
  * Lisan / Ayn: [Core linguistic root meaning: the earth, the lower sphere; that which is beneath]
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الأرض: الجرم المقابل للسماء" — the body opposite the heaven
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): [Literal: the earth as a resting place (مهادا); Majaz: not applicable in this context of divine creation]
- Root: ركن (r-k-n)
  * Lisan / Ayn: [Core linguistic root meaning: corner, pillar, support; that to which one leans for strength]
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "ركن الشيء: جانبه الذي يسكن إليه" — the side of a thing to which one repairs; used metaphorically for strength
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): [Literal: physical pillar/corner; Majaz: "فلان يأوي من عز قومه إلى ركن شديد" — one who repairs to a mighty support; here, the "pillars" (أركان) of faith as structural supports]
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The syntactic structure "مداره على عشرة أصول" (its circuit revolves upon ten principles) employs a prepositional phrase governing the verbal noun, establishing the necessary grammatical dependency that mirrors the ontological dependency of the created upon the Creator.
56:58.topic: Al-Ghazali on the journey of the soul, death, and the Hereafter, from 'Foundations of Belief'

57:3.arabic: إلا مسخرون تحت قهره وقدرته مرددون في قبضته وهو الأول والآخر والظاهر والباطن فلما ذكر ذلك في عالم الشهادة استبعد منه ذلك وقيل له كيف يكون هو الأول والاخر وهما وصفان متناقضان وكيف يكون هو الظاهر والباطن فالأول ليس بآخر والظاهر ليس بباطن فقال هو الأول بالإضافة إلى الموجودات إذ صدر منه الكل على ترتيبه واحدا بعد واحد وهو الآخر بالإضافة إلى سير السائرين إليه فإنهم لا يزالون مترقين من منزل إلى منزل إلى أن يقع الانتهاء إلى تلك الحضرة فيكون ذلك آخر السفر فهو آخر في المشاهدة أول في الوجود وهو باطن بالإضافة إلى العاكفين في عالم ال
57:3.english: ...its mover is Power (al-qudrah) without any doubt. So the seeker (al-sālik) journeyed on to the world of Power, and there he beheld wonders before which all that had preceded seemed contemptible. He asked Power concerning the movement of the right hand, and it said: "I am but an attribute (innamā anā ṣifah) — ask the Powerful One (al-Qādir), for the reliance is upon the described substances (al-mawṣūfāt), not upon the attributes." At that point he almost deviated and unleashed the tongue of questioning with audacity, but he was steadied by the firm word (al-qawl al-thābit), and a caller cried out from behind the veils of the pavilions of the Divine Presence: "He is not asked about what He does, but they shall be asked" {«لَا يُسْأَلُ عَمَّا يَفْعَلُ وَهُمْ يُسْأَلُونَ»}. Then the awe of the Presence overwhelmed him, and he fell down stricken, convulsing in his swoon. When he regained consciousness, he said: "Glory be to You — how magnificent is Your majesty! I repent unto You, and I place my trust in You, and I believe that You are the Sovereign, the Compeller, the One, the Subduer. I fear none but You, I hope for none other than You, and I seek refuge only in Your pardon from Your punishment, and in Your good pleasure from Your wrath. I have nothing but to ask of You and to supplicate before You, and to plead humbly in Your presence, saying: 'Expand my breast that I may know You, and loosen the knot from my tongue that I may praise You.'"
57:3.section_title_en: The Unification of the Acts — The Journey of the Seekers to the Oneness of the Agent
57:3.anchors:
- Root: قدر (q-d-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of measuring, determining, and empowering; al-Qadir as the One whose power is absolute and unbounded.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Power (qudrah) when ascribed to God is the negation of incapacity ('ajz); when ascribed to man it is a contingent capacity limited by divine ordainment.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (haqiqah) — "He is Qadir, Muqtadir, possessor of power"; metaphorical (majaz) — "a far-reaching steed" (ba'id al-qadr), indicating extension of effect.
- Root: وحد (w-ḥ-d)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Oneness and singularity; al-Wahid as that which has no part whatsoever.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): True unity (wahdah) is absolute indivisibility; applied to God exclusively in the sense of unique sovereignty.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "He is one (wahid), and they are singular (wuhdan)"; literal unity versus numerical oneness.
- Root: علم (ʿ-l-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Knowledge as perception of a thing's reality; the mark or sign by which something is known.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Knowledge ('ilm) is the apprehension of a thing in its true reality — either grasping the essence or judging its attributes.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — "I knew not of your news" (ma 'alimtu bi-khabarika); the knower as one marked by discernment.
- Sibawayh Rule: Restriction and Focused Predication (al-ḥaṣr wa al-taqyīd bi-innamā) — "Innamā anā ṣifah" (I am but an attribute) restricts the speaker's essence to being a mere accident, redirecting inquiry to the substantive subject (al-mawṣūf).
57:3.topic: Al-Ghazali on constant remembrance of God and contemplative invocations, from 'Monotheism and Reliance'

57:3.arabic: لا يقضى عليه بالانقضاء والانفصال بتصرم الآباد وانقراض الآجال بن هو الأول والآخر والظاهر والباطن وهو بكل شيء عليم التنزيه وأنه ليس بجسم مصور ولا جوهر محدود مقدر وأنه لا يماثل والأجسام ولا في التقدير ولا في قبول الانقسام وأنه ليس بجوهر ولا تحله الجواهر ولا بعرض ولا تحله الأعراض بل لا يماثل موجودا ولا يماثله موجود ليس كمثله شيء ولا هو مثل شيء وأنه لا يحده المقدار ولا تحويه الأقطار ولا تحيط به الجهات ولا تكتنفه الأرضون ولا السموات وأنه مستو على العرش على الوجه الذي قاله وبالمعنى الذي أراده استواء منزها عن المماسة والاستقرار والتمكن والحلول والانتقال لا يحمله العرش ب
57:3.english:
- **Root: خلق (khalaqa)**
  - *Lisan / Ayn:* Core meaning of measuring, proportioning, and fashioning; al-Khalil notes the root's application to the act of creation as bringing forth upon a measured determination.
  - *Al-Raghib (Mufradat):* "الخلق أصله: التقدير المستقيم" — Creation fundamentally signifies right/straight measurement; used for bringing into being from nothing (ibdāʿ) as in {خلق السماوات والأرض}, and for bringing forth from something as in {خلقكم من نفس واحدة}.
  - *Al-Zamakhshari (Asas):* Literal (ḥaqīqah): the craftsman's measuring before cutting. Metaphorical (majāz): "خلق الله الخلق: أوجده على تقدير أوجبته الحكمة" — God's creation is bringing into existence upon a measure necessitated by wisdom.

57:3.arabic: الأول والآخر والظاهر والباطن وهو بكل شيء عليم التنزيه وأنه ليس بجسم مصور ولا جوهر محدود مقدر وأنه لا يماثل والأجسام ولا في التقدير ولا في قبول الانقسام وأنه ليس بجوهر ولا تحله الجواهر ولا بعرض ولا تحله الأعراض بل لا يماثل موجودا ولا يماثله موجود ليس كمثله شيء ولا هو مثل شيء وأنه لا يحده المقدار ولا تحويه الأقطار ولا تحيط به الجهات ولا تكتنفه الأرضون ولا السموات وأنه مستو على العرش على الوجه الذي قاله وبالمعنى الذي أراده استواء منزها عن المماسة والاستقرار والتمكن والحلول وال
57:3.english:
- **Root: خلق (khalaqa)**
  - *Lisan / Ayn:* Core meaning of measuring, proportioning, and fashioning; al-Khalil notes the root's application to the act of creation as bringing forth upon a measured determination.
  - *Al-Raghib (Mufradat):* "الخلق أصله: التقدير المستقيم" — Creation fundamentally signifies right/straight measurement; used for bringing into being from nothing (ibdāʿ) as in {خلق السماوات والأرض}, and for bringing forth from something as in {خلقكم من نفس واحدة}.
  - *Al-Zamakhshari (Asas):* Literal (ḥaqīqah): the craftsman's measuring before cutting. Metaphorical (majāz): "خلق الله الخلق: أوجده على تقدير أوجبته الحكمة" — God's creation is bringing into existence upon a measure necessitated by wisdom.

57:10.arabic: منكم والذين أوتوا العلم درجات وقال تعالى لا يستوي منكم من أنفق من قبل الفتح وقاتل الآية وقد قال تعالى هم درجات عند الله وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم الإيمان عريان ولباسه التقوى (1) الحديث وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم الإيمان بضع وسبعون بابا أدناها إماطة الأذى عن الطريق فهذا ما يدل على ارتباط كمال الإيمان بالأعمال وأما ارتباطه بالبراءة عن النفاق والشرك الخفي فقوله صلى الله عليه وسلم أربع من كن فيه فهو منافق خالص وإن صام وصلى وزعم أنه مؤمن من إذا حدث كذب وإذا وعد أخلف وإذا اؤتمن خان وإذا خاصم فجر (2) وفي بعض الروايات وإذا عاهد غدر وفي حدي
57:10.english: ...doubt concerning this truthfulness. Likewise, God Most High said: {«But righteousness is he who believes in God and the Last Day and the angels and the Book and the prophets»} (2:177) — thus He conditioned twenty attributes, such as faithfulness to covenant and patience under hardship. Then He said Most High: {«Those are the truthful ones»} (2:177). And God Most High said: {«God will raise those who have believed among you and those who have been given knowledge, by degrees»} (58:11). And He said Most High: {«Not equal among you are those who spent before the conquest and fought»} (57:10). And He said Most High: {«They are degrees before God»} (3:163). And the Prophet, peace be upon him, said: "Faith is naked, and its garment is God-consciousness (al-taqwā)." And the Prophet, peace be upon him, said: "Faith has seventy-some branches; the lowest of them is removing harm from the path." All this indicates the interconnection of the perfection of faith with works.
57:10.section_title_en: The Revival of the Religious Sciences — Book of the Secrets of Zakāh, Section 104: On the Degrees of Faith and Its Connection to Works, and the Hidden Hypocrisy (al-Nifāq al-Khafī) That Contradicts the Perfection of Faith
57:10.anchors:
- Root: ن ف ق (N-F-Q)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Root denotes passing away, depletion, and expenditure; also the underground burrow of the jerboa (nāfiqāʾ) with a concealed exit — the etymological basis for hypocrisy as a hidden exit from faith.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "نفق الشيء: مضى ونفد" — theological nuance: hypocrisy (nifāq) is that which causes faith to expire and pass away, whether by sale (worldly gain) or by death (spiritual ruin).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "نفقت الدراهم" (coins ran out). Metaphorical: "نفق روحه: خرج" (his soul expired and went forth) — hence the hypocrite's faith is one whose spirit has already departed.
- Root: أ ي م (A-Y-M)
  * Lisan / Ayn: A woman without a husband; a man long unmarried. Al-Raghib: "الحرب مأيمة" — war makes women widows.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "تركوا النساء أيامى" (they left women widowed). Metaphorical application: the one who feels secure from hypocrisy is like one who claims immunity from widowhood — a false security.
- Root: و ف ي (W-F-Y)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Fullness, completion, fulfillment of a measure or covenant.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الوافي: الذي بلغ التمام" — the one who has reached completion. "أوفى: إذا تمم العهد ولم ينقض حفظه" — to fulfill the covenant without breach.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "درهم واف" (a full-weight dirham). Metaphorical: "أوفى على المائة" (he surpassed a hundred) — faith's perfection (wafāʾ) is only attained by surpassing mere profession to include works and inward sincerity.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد (Restriction & Focused Predication) — governing the grammatical force of "إنما" constructions and conditional clauses (من كان...), where the predicate is restricted to the condition stated, as in the hadith "أربع من كن فيه فهو منافق خالص" — the four traits are exhaustive of the ruling.
57:10.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'Foundations of Belief'

57:10.arabic: من أعوان الشهوات فهو من الذين أوتوا العلم وكلا وعد الله الحسنى والذي يقتضي الإيمان بهذا الأمر في القرآن والسنة وأقاويل العلماء أكثر من أن يحصر قال الله تعالى ونهى النفس عن الهوى فإن الجنة هي المأوى وقال تعالى أولئك الذين امتحن الله قلوبهم للتقوى قيل نزع منها محبة الشهوات وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم المؤمن بين خمس شدائد مؤمن يحسده ومنافق يبغضه وكافر يقاتله وشيطان يضله ونفس تنازعه (1) فبين أن النفس عدو منازع يجب عليه مجاهدتها ويروى أن الله تعالى أوحى إلى داود عليه السلام يا داود حذر وأنذر أصحابك أكل الشهوات فإن ال
57:10.english: But if you are incapable of that, then it behooves you not to let slip the affirmation of truth (taṣdīq) and faith (īmān) by way of receptive acceptance (talqqī) and emulation (taqlīd) of one who deserves to be emulated. For faith has a degree, just as knowledge has a degree; and knowledge is attained after faith, and it lies beyond it. God, the Exalted, said: {«يرفع الله الذين آمنوا منكم والذين أوتوا العلم درجات»} — "God will raise those who have believed among you and those who have been given knowledge, by degrees." So whoever affirms as true that opposing the desires (mukhālafat al-shahawāt) is the road to God, the Mighty and Majestic, yet has not been apprised of its cause and its secret — he is among those who believe. And when he is apprised of what we have mentioned concerning the helpers of the desires, he is among those who have been given knowledge. And to both has God promised the goodly reward.
57:10.section_title_en: Section 627 — The Path of Opposition to the Desires: On the Consensus of the Scholars that There Is No Road to the Happiness of the Hereafter Save through Restraining the Soul from Caprice
57:10.anchors:
- Root: نفس (n-f-s)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The self, soul, spirit; that which breathes; the animating principle; also blood, and the "evil eye" (nafs sā'ilah)
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): النفس: الروح — the soul as the spiritual reality; in the verse {«ويحذركم الله نفسه»} it denotes the very Essence (al-dhāt); the soul is that which must be disciplined and opposed in its caprice (hawā)
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the self that desires and inclines; Metaphorical: "دفق نفسه" — he poured out his blood/life; the soul as the internal adversary that must be fought (jihād al-nafs)

  * Lisan / Ayn: The heart; to turn over, to transform, to fluctuate; the heart as that which is constantly turning between states
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): قلب الشيء: تصريفه وصرفه عن وجه إلى وجه — the heart is so named because of its constant turning and fluctuation between conditions; the seat of spiritual perception and disease
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: to turn something over; Metaphorical: the heart as the organ of spiritual understanding that can be veiled (maḥjūbah) from God by attachment to desires
- Root: دنا (d-n-w)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To be near, proximity; the world (al-dunyā) as that which is nearer/lower
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): الدنو: القرب بالذات أو بالحكم — proximity by essence or by judgment; the world as the nearer realm that veils from the distant (al-ākhirah)
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: closeness; Metaphorical: the lower world as that which is "near" and thus preoccupies the heart from what is higher
- Root: أكل (a-k-l)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To eat, consume; also to possess and enjoy
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Eating as the most fundamental desire; the restriction of food (qillat al-ṭa'ām) as the first pillar of spiritual discipline (riyāḍah)
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: consumption of food; Metaphorical: "أكل الشهوات" — the devouring of desires as that which veils the intellect from God

57:19.arabic: سبحانه وتعالى {والذين آمنوا بالله ورسله أولئك هم الصديقون} الآية ولقوله تعالى كلما ألقى فيها فوج سألهم خزنتها إلى قوله فكذبنا وقلنا ما نزل الله من شيء فقوله {كلما ألقى فيها فوج} عام فينبغي أن يكون من ألقي في النار مكذبا ولقوله تعالى {لا يصلاها إلا الأشقى الذي كذب وتولى} وهذا حصر وإثبات ونفي ولقوله تعالى {من جاء بالحسنة فله خير منها وهم من فزع يومئذ آمنون} فالإيمان رأس الحسنات ولقوله تعالى {والله يحب المحسنين} وقال تعالى {إنا لا نضيع أجر من أحسن عملا} ولا حجة لهم في ذلك فإنه حيث ذكر الإيمان في هذه الآيات أريد به ال
57:19.english: He was asked, "Which deed is most excellent?" The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Islam." It was then asked, "Which aspect of Islam is most excellent?" He (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Faith (Īmān)." This is evidence for both the distinction (ikhtilāf) between the two terms and their overlap (tadākhul). This usage is the most consistent with the conventions of the language, because faith is a deed among deeds, and it is the most excellent of them. Islam is submission (taslīm), whether by the heart, by the tongue, or by the limbs. The most excellent of these is that which is by the heart, which is the assent (taṣdīq) that is called faith. Using the two terms in a way that indicates distinction, overlap, or even complete synonymy (tarāduf) is all within the bounds of metaphorical usage (tajawwuz) in the language.
57:19.section_title_en: The Book of the Revival of the Religious Sciences — Section 99: On the Distinction, Overlap, and Synonymy of Faith (Īmān) and Submission (Islām), and Their Worldly and Otherworldly Judgments
57:19.anchors:
- Root: ايم (A-Y-M)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of remaining unmarried, or a state of being without a spouse; extended metaphorically to describe one who is solitary or without support.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الأيامى: جمع أيم، وهي المرأة التي لا بعل لها... والحرب مأيمة، أي: يفرق بين الزوج والزوجة." The root carries the sense of separation or a state of lacking union, which informs the theological discussion of what constitutes the essential bond of faith.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah) usage denotes the state of being unmarried; metaphorical (Majaz) usage extends to anything that separates or leaves one bereft. This distinction between literal and metaphorical application is central to the chapter's method.
- Root: قلب (Q-L-B)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To turn, overturn, or transform a thing from one state to another.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "قلب الشيء: تصريفه وصرفه عن وجه إلى وجه... والانقلاب: الانصراف." The heart (qalb) is so named for its constant fluctuation and turning. In theological terms, it is the seat of taṣdīq (assent), the immaterial faculty of cognition and conviction.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah) usage is physical turning; metaphorical (Majaz) usage is "قلب الأمور" — to deliberate, scrutinize, and manage affairs. This supports the distinction between the heart's internal act of assent and the external acts of the limbs.
- Root: عمل (ʿ-A-M-L)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Any deed or action performed with purpose and intent.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "العمل: كل فعل يكون من الحيوان بقصد، فهو أخص من الفعل." Work is more specific than mere action, as it implies deliberate, intentional agency. It is used for both righteous and sinful deeds, and is the external manifestation of internal conviction.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah) usage refers to physical labor or deeds. The chapter explores whether "work" is an integral part of the reality of faith or a separate, consequent requirement.
- Root: صدق (S-D-Q)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To be truthful, to speak the truth, to verify.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الصدق والكذب أصلهما في القول... ولا يكونان بالقصد الأول إلا في القول." Truth and falsehood are primarily properties of speech and reports. Taṣdīq (assent) is the heart's affirmation of the truth of a report, which is the core reality of Īmān.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah) usage is truthful speech; metaphorical (Majaz) usage is "صادق الحملة" — one who is true and firm in battle or resolve. This shows that taṣdīq is not merely verbal but a firm, internal resolution.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication). This rule governs how restriction (ḥaṣr) is achieved in Arabic, often through particles like "innamā" or through contextual specification (takhṣīṣ). The chapter's core argument hinges on how terms like Īmān and Islām are semantically restricted, expanded, or made synonymous through contextual usage (majāz), requiring precise parsing of the predicate and its scope.

58:11.arabic: وقد قال الله تعالى يا أيها الذين آمنوا أنفقوا من طيبات ما كسبتم ومما أخرجنا لكم من الأرض ولا تيمموا الخبيث منه تنفقون ولستم بآخذيه إلا أن تغمضوا فيه أي لا تأخذوه إلا مع كراهية وحياء وهو معنى الإغماض فلا تؤثروا به ربكم وفي الخبر سبق درهم مائة ألف درهم (3) وذلك بأن يخرجه الإنسان وهو من أحل ماله وأجوده فيصدر ذلك عن الرضا والفرح بالبذل وقد يخرج مائة ألف درهم مما يكره من ماله فيدل ذلك على أنه ليس يؤثر الله عز وجل بشيء مما يحبه وبذلك ذم الله تعالى قوما جعلوا لله ما يكرهون فقال تعال
58:11.english: The heart is not treated save with the compound electuary (maʿjūn) of knowledge and works. And this condition among the conditions of almsgiving runs in the same course as humility (al-khushūʿ) runs in the prayer. This is established by his saying — may Allah bless him and grant him peace: "A man has nothing of his prayer save that of which he was conscious." And this is like his saying — may Allah bless him and grant him peace: "Allah does not accept the charity of the one who bestows it with reproach (al-mannān)." And like His saying — Exalted is He: {«لا تبطلوا صدقاتكم بالمن والأذى»} ("Do not nullify your charities by reproach and injury"). As for the legal opinion (fatwā) of the jurist that the alms fall in their proper place and that one's liability is discharged without this condition — that is another discussion, and we have already pointed to its meaning in the Book of Prayer.
58:11.section_title_en: The Inner Conditions of Charity — Section 175 (From The Revival of the Religious Sciences, Book of the Mysteries of Almsgiving)
58:11.anchors:
- Root: قلب (q-l-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "To turn, overturn, transform a thing from one state to another; to rotate, to flip"
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "قلب الشيء: تصريفه وصرفه عن وجه إلى وجه" — the heart is so named because of its constant turning and transformation between states
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "قلب الشيء قلبا: حوله عن وجهه" (to turn a thing from its face). Metaphorical: "رجل قلب حول: يقلب الأمور ويحتال" — one who turns matters over and manages them; "قلبوا لك الأمور" (they turned matters against you)
- Root: وجل (w-j-l)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "Fear, dread, apprehension that strikes the heart"
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الوجل: استشعار الخوف" — the sensing of fear; cited in {«إنما المؤمنون الذين إذا ذكر الله وجلت قلوبهم»}
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "رجل وجل، وقوم وجال" — a fearful man, a fearful people; "وفي قلبه وجل" — in his heart is dread
- Root: عجب (ʿ-j-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "Wonder, amazement; self-admiration, vanity"
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Self-admiration (al-ʿujb) is a destructive spiritual ailment that nullifies deeds
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: wonder at something extraordinary. Metaphorical: self-conceit regarding one's own acts of obedience
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد (Restriction & Focused Predication) — governing the precise limitation of general categories (al-ṣifāt al-khāṣṣah within al-aṣnāf al-thamāniyyah) and the conditional structure of acceptance

58:11.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Duties of Brotherhood'

58:11.arabic: شرفا وفضلا وجلاء ونبلا وقال الله تعالى {يرفع الله الذين آمنوا منكم والذين أوتوا العلم درجات} قال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما للعلماء درجات فوق المؤمنين بسبعمائة درجة ما بين الدرجتين مسيرة خمسمائة عام وقال عز وجل {قل هل يستوي الذين يعلمون والذين لا يعلمون} وقال تعالى {إنما يخشى الله من عباده العلماء} وقال تعالى {قل كفى بالله شهيدا بيني وبينكم ومن عنده علم الكتاب} وقال تعالى {قال الذي عنده علم من الكتاب أنا آتيك به} تنبيها على أنه اقتدر بقوة العلم وقال عز وجل {وقال الذين أوتوا العلم ويلكم ثواب الله خير لمن آمن وعمل صالحا} بين أن عظم قدر الآخرة
58:11.english: How He, Glorified and Exalted, began with Himself, then seconded with the angels, and thirded with the people of knowledge — and sufficient for you is this as honor, excellence, splendor, and nobility. And God, Exalted, said: {«يرفع الله الذين آمنوا منكم والذين أوتوا العلم درجات»} — "God will raise those who have believed among you and those who have been given knowledge, in degrees." Ibn ʿAbbās, may God be pleased with them both, said: For the scholars there are degrees above the believers, seven hundred degrees, and between each two degrees is a distance of five hundred years' journey.
58:11.section_title_en: The Book of Knowledge — Section 4: The Excellence of Knowledge and the Scholars
58:11.anchors:
- Root: علم (ʿ-l-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root meaning of knowing, perceiving a thing in its true reality; the act of apprehension and judgment.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "العلم: إدراك الشيء بحقيقته" — knowledge is the apprehension of a thing in its true reality, divided into apprehension of the essence and judgment of existence or non-existence.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) usage denotes genuine knowing; metaphorical (majāz) usage extends to signs, landmarks, and traces that guide to knowledge.
- Root: درج (d-r-j)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Degrees, steps, ascending stations; the root denotes gradation and progressive elevation.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الدرجة نحو المنزلة، لكن يقال للمنزلة: درجة إذا اعتبرت بالصعود" — a degree is a station considered by ascent, not horizontal extension.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical steps of ascent. Metaphorical: "لفلان درجة رفيعة" — lofty rank; "امش في مدارج الحق" — walk in the paths of truth.
- Root: يوم (y-w-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: A day; a period of time from sunrise to sunset, or any duration whatsoever.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "اليوم يعبر به عن وقت طلوع الشمس إلى غروبها. وقد يعبر به عن مدة من الزمان أي مدة كانت" — the day denotes the time of the sun's rising to its setting, and may denote any period of time whatsoever.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the solar day. Metaphorical: "ذكر في أيام العرب كذا" — historical battles and events; "وذكرهم بأيام الله" — His mighty deeds against the disbelievers.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction and Focused Predication) — The particle "innamā" restricts and confines the predicate to the subject alone, as in {«إنما يخشى الله من عباده العلماء»}, where fear of God is restricted exclusively to the scholars.
58:11.topic: Al-Ghazali on the journey of the soul, death, and the Hereafter, from 'Foundations of Belief'

67:8.arabic: للإنسان إلا ما سعى وأن سعيه سوف يرى كلما ألقى فيها فوج سألهم خزنتها ألم يأتكم نذير قالوا بلى قد جاءنا نذير أي ألم نسمعكم سنة الله في عباده وأنه
67:8.english: I say: God—exalted is He—loves the obedient and hates the disobedient. So just as He does not hate the obedient father because of His hatred for the disobedient son, likewise He does not love the disobedient son because of His love for the obedient father. And if love were to flow from the father to the son, then hatred would likewise be bound to flow. Rather, the truth is: {«ولا تزر وازرة وزر أخرى»} — "And no bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another" {Quran 6:164, 17:15, 35:18, 39:7, 53:38}. And whoever supposes that he will be saved by his father's piety is like one who supposes he will be satiated by his father's eating, quenched by his father's drinking, become a scholar by his father's learning, and reach the Ka'bah and see it by his father's walking.
67:8.section_title_en: The Reality of Hope (Al-Rajā') and the Futility of Reliance on Another's Piety
67:8.anchors:
- Root: و ل د (walada)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Physical begetting and offspring; the father's generative act.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الولد: المولود" — offspring as a created entity; here used metaphorically for spiritual causation.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical birth. Metaphorical: "تولدت العصبية" — something generated or produced from another; Ghazali exploits this to refute the notion that a father's obedience "generates" salvation for the son.
- Root: ر ج و (rajā)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Expectation, hope, longing for a favorable outcome.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Hope tied to legitimate means; not mere wishful thinking (tamannī).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: awaiting rain. Metaphorical: "رجوت فلانا" — to expect from someone; Ghazali contrasts true hope (with action) vs. delusion (ghurūr).
- Root: غ ر ر (gharara)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Deception, heedlessness, being lured by a false appearance.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The state of one who is duped by Satan's plausible speech.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: a risky venture. Metaphorical: "اغتر بفلان" — to be deceived by outward charm while the inner reality is corrupt.
- Root: ك ي س (kays)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Intelligence, shrewdness, prudence.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The wise man who disciplines his soul and acts for the afterlife.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: alertness. Metaphorical: "الكيس من دان نفسه" — the prudent one who holds his soul to account; antonym of "الأحمق" (the fool).
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — "إنما يوفى الصابرون أجرهم بغير حساب" style; Ghazali uses "إنما" to restrict reward to personal action, and "ليس للإنسان إلا ما سعى" as a restrictive negative clause (nafy + illā) to deny any transfer of merit.
67:8.topic: Classical commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya Ulum al-Din, from 'Condemnation of Delusion'

67:9.arabic: تعالى كلما ألقى فيها فوج سألهم خزنتها إلى قوله فكذبنا وقلنا ما نزل الله من شيء فقوله {كلما ألقى فيها فوج} عام فينبغي أن يكون من ألقي في النار مكذبا ولقوله تعالى {لا يصلاها إلا الأشقى الذي كذب وتولى} وهذا حصر وإثبات ونفي ولقوله تعالى {من جاء بالحسنة فله خير منها وهم من فزع يومئذ آمنون} فالإيمان رأس الحسنات ولقوله تعالى {والله يحب المحسنين} وقال تعالى {إنا لا نضيع أجر من أحسن عملا} ولا حجة لهم في ذلك فإنه حيث ذكر الإيمان في هذه الآيات أريد به الإيمان مع العمل إذ بينا أن الإيمان قد يطلق ويراد به الإسلام وهو الموافقة بالقلب والقول والعمل
67:9.english: He was asked, "Which deed is most excellent?" The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Islam." It was then asked, "Which aspect of Islam is most excellent?" He (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Faith (Īmān)." This is evidence for both the distinction (ikhtilāf) between the two terms and their overlap (tadākhul). This usage is the most consistent with the conventions of the language, because faith is a deed among deeds, and it is the most excellent of them. Islam is submission (taslīm), whether by the heart, by the tongue, or by the limbs. The most excellent of these is that which is by the heart, which is the assent (taṣdīq) that is called faith. Using the two terms in a way that indicates distinction, overlap, or even complete synonymy (tarāduf) is all within the bounds of metaphorical usage (tajawwuz) in the language.
67:9.section_title_en: The Book of the Revival of the Religious Sciences — Section 99: On the Distinction, Overlap, and Synonymy of Faith (Īmān) and Submission (Islām), and Their Worldly and Otherworldly Judgments
67:9.anchors:
- Root: ايم (A-Y-M)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of remaining unmarried, or a state of being without a spouse; extended metaphorically to describe one who is solitary or without support.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الأيامى: جمع أيم، وهي المرأة التي لا بعل لها... والحرب مأيمة، أي: يفرق بين الزوج والزوجة." The root carries the sense of separation or a state of lacking union, which informs the theological discussion of what constitutes the essential bond of faith.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah) usage denotes the state of being unmarried; metaphorical (Majaz) usage extends to anything that separates or leaves one bereft. This distinction between literal and metaphorical application is central to the chapter's method.
- Root: قلب (Q-L-B)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To turn, overturn, or transform a thing from one state to another.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "قلب الشيء: تصريفه وصرفه عن وجه إلى وجه... والانقلاب: الانصراف." The heart (qalb) is so named for its constant fluctuation and turning. In theological terms, it is the seat of taṣdīq (assent), the immaterial faculty of cognition and conviction.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah) usage is physical turning; metaphorical (Majaz) usage is "قلب الأمور" — to deliberate, scrutinize, and manage affairs. This supports the distinction between the heart's internal act of assent and the external acts of the limbs.
- Root: عمل (ʿ-A-M-L)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Any deed or action performed with purpose and intent.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "العمل: كل فعل يكون من الحيوان بقصد، فهو أخص من الفعل." Work is more specific than mere action, as it implies deliberate, intentional agency. It is used for both righteous and sinful deeds, and is the external manifestation of internal conviction.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah) usage refers to physical labor or deeds. The chapter explores whether "work" is an integral part of the reality of faith or a separate, consequent requirement.
- Root: صدق (S-D-Q)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To be truthful, to speak the truth, to verify.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الصدق والكذب أصلهما في القول... ولا يكونان بالقصد الأول إلا في القول." Truth and falsehood are primarily properties of speech and reports. Taṣdīq (assent) is the heart's affirmation of the truth of a report, which is the core reality of Īmān.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah) usage is truthful speech; metaphorical (Majaz) usage is "صادق الحملة" — one who is true and firm in battle or resolve. This shows that taṣdīq is not merely verbal but a firm, internal resolution.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication). This rule governs how restriction (ḥaṣr) is achieved in Arabic, often through particles like "innamā" or through contextual specification (takhṣīṣ). The chapter's core argument hinges on how terms like Īmān and Islām are semantically restricted, expanded, or made synonymous through contextual usage (majāz), requiring precise parsing of the predicate and its scope.
67:9.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Foundations of Belief'

67:13.arabic: والله خلقكم وما تعملون وفي قوله تعالى وأسروا قولكم أو اجهروا به إنه عليم بذات الصدور ألا يعلم من خلق وهو اللطيف الخبير أمر العباد بالتحرز في أقوالهم وأفعالهم وإسرارهم وإضمارهم لعلمه بموارد أفعالهم واستدل على العلم بالخلق وكيف لا يكون خالقا لفعل العبد وقدرته تامة لا قصور فيها وهي متعلقة بحركة أبدان العباد والحركات متماثلة وتعلق القدرة بها لذاتها فما الذي يقصر تعلقها عن بعض الحركات دون البعض مع تماثلها أو كيف يكون الحيوان مستبدا بالاختراع ويصدر من العنكبوت والنحل وسائر الحيوانات من لطائف الصناعات ما يتحير فيه عقول ذوي الألباب فكيف انفردت هي باختراعها دون رب الأرب
67:13.english: Rather, the attribute of origination (ḥudūth) is established for bodies only by virtue of their being subject to change and the fluctuation of states. So how could their Creator share with them in the acceptance of change? And upon this is built [the doctrine] that His Speech (kalām) is eternal, subsisting in His Essence—only the sounds indicating it are originated. Just as one rationally apprehends the subsistence of a request for learning and the father's will for [his] child in the father's essence before the child is created—such that when the child is created, attains reason, and God creates for him a knowledge pertaining to what is in his father's heart of the request, the child becomes commanded by that very request which subsisted in his father's essence and whose existence endured until the time of his child's awareness of it—so let one rationally apprehend the subsistence of the command indicated by His words, Mighty and Majestic: {«اخلع نعليك»} "Take off your sandals" [Q 20:12], in God's Essence, and Moses—peace be upon him—becoming addressed by it after his existence, when God created for him a knowledge of that command and hearing of that eternal Speech.
67:13.section_title_en: The Revival of the Religious Sciences — Section 92: On the Divine Attributes of Eternity, Knowledge, Will, and the Third Pillar Concerning God's Acts
67:13.anchors:
- Root: قدم (q-d-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Primordial precedence; that which has no temporal beginning; eternal past (azal) and eternal future (abad).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Precedence either by time, by honor, or by ontological necessity—here, God's attributes are eternal in the sense that they are not subject to temporal origination.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "to precede." Metaphorical: that which cannot be conceived as non-existent posterior to its existence—applied to God's essence and attributes.
- Root: علم (ʿ-l-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Comprehension of a thing as it truly is; the indelible mark or trace by which one is guided.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Knowledge is the apprehension of a thing in its reality"—twofold: apprehension of the essence, and judgment concerning existence or non-existence. God's knowledge is eternal, encompassing all created things without renewal.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: perception and awareness. Metaphorical: the "signs" (maʿālim) of God's power—His knowledge is identical with His creative act, for "Does He who created not know?" {«ألا يعلم من خلق»}.
- Root: خلق (kh-l-q)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Measuring, proportioning, then bringing into existence upon a determined measure.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Origination from nothing without prior model—"He created the heavens and the earth" {«خلق السماوات والأرض»}—and also bringing forth from something, as man from a drop. All acts of creatures are God's creation.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the tailor's measuring before cutting. Metaphorical: God's bringing forth existence upon a measure dictated by wisdom—He is the sole Creator (al-Khāliq) of all acts, including those of His servants.
- Root: قتل (q-t-l)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Removal of the spirit from the body; also, intense subjugation.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The root meaning is the separation of soul from body, whether by an agent (qatl) or by natural death (mawt). Used here analogically: as "killer," "killed," and "killing" are mutually entailing, so are "knower," "known," and "knowledge."
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: slaying. Metaphorical: mutual entailment—just as no killer exists without a killing and a killed one, so no knower exists without knowledge and a known object.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب التلازم والتضايف (Mutual Entailment and Correlativity) — Terms like ʿālim/ʿilm/maʿlūm are correlatives (mutalāzimāt) that cannot be conceptually separated; the predicate necessitates the co-existence of its correlates in the intellect.
67:13.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Foundations of Belief'

67:14.arabic: شيء عليم ومرشد إلى صدقه بقوله تعالى ألا يعلم من خلق وهو اللطيف الخبير أرشدك إلى الاستدلال بالخلق على العلم بأنك لا تستريب في دلالة الخلق اللطيف والصنع المزين بالترتيب ولو في الشيء الحقير الضعيف على علم الصانع بكيفية الترتيب والترصيف فما ذكره الله سبحانه هو المنتهى في الهداية والتعريف الأصل الثالث العلم بكونه عز وجل حيا فإن من ثبت علمه وقدرته ثبت بالضرورة حياته ولو تصور قادر وعالم فاعل مدبر دون أن يكون حيا لجاز أن يشك في حياة الحيوانات عند ترددها في الحركات والسكنات بل في حياة أرباب الحرف والصناعات وذلك
67:14.english: **The Eighth Principle: Knowledge that He, Exalted is He, is established upon His Throne (mustawin ʿalā ʿarshihi) in the sense that God, Exalted is He, intended by istiwāʾ — which is the sense that does not contradict the attribute of Majesty, nor does any mark of origination (ḥudūth) or passing away (fanāʾ) attach to it. And it is the sense intended by His saying — istiwāʾ toward the heaven — where He said in the Qur'an: {«ثُمَّ اسْتَوَىٰ إِلَى السَّمَاءِ وَهِيَ دُخَانٌ»} ("Then He directed Himself to the heaven, and it was smoke") [Fussilat 41:11]. And that is only by way of subjugation (qahr) and dominion (istīlāʾ), as the poet said:
67:14.section_title_en: The Revival of the Religious Sciences — Section 90: The Ten Principles Concerning Knowledge of the Divine Attributes
67:14.anchors:
- Root: ع ل م (ʿ-l-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root denoting the faculty of perception and comprehension; the mark or trace by which something is known.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "العلم: إدراك الشيء بحقيقته" — knowledge is the apprehension of a thing in its true reality, divided into apprehension of the essence and judgment upon it.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Distinguishes literal knowledge (ḥaqīqah) from awareness (shiʿr); here, it denotes certain, verified cognition of theological verities.
- Root: س و ي (s-w-y)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Root indicating straightness, equality, and levelness; from it derives istiwāʾ (establishing oneself upon, ascending to).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Istiwāʾ upon the Throne (al-ʿArsh) is a divine act of sovereign dominion, not corporeal settlement.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal sense of physical sitting is impossible for God; metaphorical sense (majāz) of qahr (overpowering) and istīlāʾ (dominion) is necessitated by reason and consensus.
- Root: ر أ ي (r-ʾ-y)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Visual perception; also opinion and discernment.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Ruʾyah (vision) of God in the Hereafter is a mode of disclosure (kashf) and knowledge (ʿilm), more complete than intellectual cognition, not conditioned by spatial direction.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal vision requires corporeality and direction; its application to God demands theological specification (takhṣīṣ) without nullifying the veracity of the scriptural promise.
- Root: ق د ر (q-d-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Power, measure, decree; the capacity to bring about an act.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Divine power (qudrah) is the negation of incapacity (ʿajz); absolute power belongs to God alone, while creatures possess limited capacity.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal power over an object; metaphorically, God's power encompasses all things without exertion or instrument.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Prepositional Interposition (باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور) — governing the permissible separation between the preposition and its object for rhetorical emphasis, applied here to the parsing of "إلى السماء" in the verse on istiwāʾ, where the prepositional phrase is delayed to highlight the divine act of sovereign direction toward the heavens.
67:14.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'Foundations of Belief'

71:15.arabic: المسخر بين السماء والأرض لآيات لقوم يعقلون وقال تعالى ألم تروا كيف خلق الله سبع سموات طباقا وجعل القمر فيهن نورا وجعل الشمس سراجا والله أنبتكم من الأرض نباتا ثم يعيدكم فيها ويخرجكم إخراجا وقال تعالى أفرأيتم ما تمنون أأنتم تخلقونه أم نحن الخالقون إلى قوله للمقوين فليس يخفي على من معه أدنى مسكة من عقل إذا تأمل بأدنى فكرة مضمون هذه الآيات وأدار نظره على عجائب خلق الله في الأرض والسموات وبدائع فطرة الحيوان والنبات أن هذا الأمر العجيب والترتيب المحكم لا يستغني عن صانع يدبره وفاعل يحكمه ويقدره بل تكاد فطرة النفوس تشهد بكونها مقهورة تحت تسخيره ومصرفة بمقتضى تدبيره ولذلك قال الله تعالى أفي الله شك فاطر السموات والأرض ولهذا بعث الأنبياء صل
71:15.english: The First Principle: the knowledge of His existence, the Exalted. The first thing by which one is illuminated from among the lights, and the path of reflection (ṭarīq al-iʿtibār) by which one proceeds, is that to which the Qurʾān has guided. For after the explanation of God, glorified be He, there is no explanation. He, the Exalted, has said: {«أَلَمْ نَجْعَلِ الْأَرْضَ مِهَادًا وَالْجِبَالَ أَوْتَادًا وَخَلَقْنَاكُمْ أَزْوَاجًا وَجَعَلْنَا نَوْمَكُمْ سُبَاتًا وَجَعَلْنَا اللَّيْلَ لِبَاسًا وَجَعَلْنَا النَّهَارَ مَعَاشًا وَبَنَيْنَا فَوْقَكُمْ سَبْعًا شِدَادًا وَجَعَلْنَا سِرَاجًا وَهَّاجًا وَأَنزَلْنَا مِنَ الْمُعْصِرَاتِ مَاءً ثَجَّاجًا لِّنُخْرِجَ بِهِ حَبًّا وَنَبَاتًا وَجَنَّاتٍ أَلْفَافًا»} — "Have We not made the earth a resting place, and the mountains as pegs, and created you in pairs, and made your sleep a repose, and made the night a covering, and made the day for livelihood, and built above you seven strong heavens, and made a blazing lamp, and sent down from the rain-clouds pouring water, that We may bring forth thereby grain and vegetation, and gardens dense with foliage?" (Q 78:6–16). And He, the Exalted, has said: {«إِنَّ فِي خَلْقِ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَاخْتِلَافِ اللَّيْلِ وَالنَّهَارِ وَالْفُلْكِ الَّتِي تَجْرِي فِي الْبَحْرِ بِمَا يَنفَعُ النَّاسَ وَمَا أَنزَلَ اللَّهُ مِنَ السَّمَاءِ مِن مَّاءٍ فَأَحْيَا بِهِ الْأَرْضَ بَعْدَ مَوْتِهَا وَبَثَّ فِيهَا مِن كُلِّ دَابَّةٍ وَتَصْرِيفِ الرِّيَاحِ وَالسَّحَابِ الْمُسَخَّرِ بَيْنَ السَّمَاءِ وَالْأَرْضِ لَآيَاتٍ لِّقَوْمٍ يَعْقِلُونَ»} — "Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth, and the alternation of the night and the day, and the ships which sail through the sea with that which benefits people, and what God has sent down from the sky of water, thereby reviving the earth after its death, and dispersing therein every creature, and the directing of the winds, and the clouds subservient between the heaven and the earth — are signs for a people who reason" (Q 2:164). And He, the Exalted, has said: {«أَلَمْ تَرَوْا كَيْفَ خَلَقَ اللَّهُ سَبْعَ سَمَاوَاتٍ طِبَاقًا وَجَعَلَ الْقَمَرَ فِيهِنَّ نُورًا وَجَعَلَ الشَّمْسَ سِرَاجًا وَاللَّهُ أَنبَتَكُم مِّنَ الْأَرْضِ نَبَاتًا ثُمَّ يُعِيدُكُمْ فِيهَا وَيُخْرِجُكُمْ إِخْرَاجًا»} — "Have you not seen how God created seven heavens in layers, and made the moon therein a light, and made the sun a lamp? And God caused you to grow from the earth a growth; then He returns you into it, and brings you forth a bringing forth" (Q 71:15–18). And He, the Exalted, has said: {«أَفَرَأَيْتُم مَّا تُمْنُونَ أَأَنتُمْ تَخْلُقُونَهُ أَمْ نَحْنُ الْخَالِقُونَ»} — "Have you considered what you emit? Do you create it, or are We the Creator?" — up to His saying: {«لِلْمُقْوِينَ»} — "for the settlers" (Q 56:58–73).
71:15.section_title_en: The Pillars of Faith: Knowledge of God, His Attributes, His Acts, and the Audibles — Section 87
71:15.anchors:
- Root: وجود (w-j-d)
  * Lisan / Ayn: [Core linguistic root meaning: to find, to perceive, to be; existence as that which is found or discovered]
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): [Theological/Kalam semantic nuance: al-wujūd as necessary existence (wujūb) versus contingent existence (imkān); the self-evident reality of the Creator's being]
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): [Literal vs Metaphorical distinction: haqīqah — existence as affirmed reality; majāz — "finding" as in discovery, not applicable to God's necessary being]
- Root: خلق (kh-l-q)
  * Lisan / Ayn: [Core linguistic root meaning: measuring, proportioning, fashioning; origination of a thing upon a measure]
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الخلق أصله: التقدير المستقيم، ويستعمل في إبداع الشيء من غير أصل ولا احتذاء" — creation as origination from nothing without prior model
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): [Literal: خلق الله الخلق: أوجده على تقدير أوجبته الحكمة — brought into existence upon a measure necessitated by wisdom; Majaz: not applicable to God's act as pure origination]
- Root: فطر (f-t-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: [Core linguistic root meaning: to split, cleave, rend; to originate, to bring forth as a new creation]
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "فطر الله الخلق" — God's origination of creation as a primordial act; "الفطرة" as the innate disposition
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): [Literal: فطر الله الخلق، وهو فاطر السموات: مبتدعها — originator without precedent; Majaz: "رأيه فطير" — immature opinion, not applicable to divine]
- Root: ارض (ar-d)
  * Lisan / Ayn: [Core linguistic root meaning: the earth, the lower sphere; that which is beneath]
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الأرض: الجرم المقابل للسماء" — the body opposite the heaven
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): [Literal: the earth as a resting place (مهادا); Majaz: not applicable in this context of divine creation]
- Root: ركن (r-k-n)
  * Lisan / Ayn: [Core linguistic root meaning: corner, pillar, support; that to which one leans for strength]
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "ركن الشيء: جانبه الذي يسكن إليه" — the side of a thing to which one repairs; used metaphorically for strength
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): [Literal: physical pillar/corner; Majaz: "فلان يأوي من عز قومه إلى ركن شديد" — one who repairs to a mighty support; here, the "pillars" (أركان) of faith as structural supports]
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The syntactic structure "مداره على عشرة أصول" (its circuit revolves upon ten principles) employs a prepositional phrase governing the verbal noun, establishing the necessary grammatical dependency that mirrors the ontological dependency of the created upon the Creator.
71:15.topic: Al-Ghazali on the journey of the soul, death, and the Hereafter, from 'Foundations of Belief'

72:13.arabic: المعاصي لقوله عز وجل {فمن يؤمن بربه فلا يخاف بخسا ولا رهقا} ولقوله سبحانه وتعالى {والذين آمنوا بالله ورسله أولئك هم الصديقون} الآية ولقوله تعالى كلما ألقى فيها فوج سألهم خزنتها إلى قوله فكذبنا وقلنا ما نزل الله من شيء فقوله {كلما ألقى فيها فوج} عام فينبغي أن يكون من ألقي في النار مكذبا ولقوله تعالى {لا يصلاها إلا الأشقى الذي كذب وتولى} وهذا حصر وإثبات ونفي ولقوله تعالى {من جاء بالحسنة فله خير منها وهم من فزع يومئذ آمنون} فالإيمان رأس الحسنات ولقوله تعالى {والله يحب المحسنين} وقال تعالى {إنا لا نضيع أجر من أحسن عملا}
72:13.english: He was asked, "Which deed is most excellent?" The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Islam." It was then asked, "Which aspect of Islam is most excellent?" He (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Faith (Īmān)." This is evidence for both the distinction (ikhtilāf) between the two terms and their overlap (tadākhul). This usage is the most consistent with the conventions of the language, because faith is a deed among deeds, and it is the most excellent of them. Islam is submission (taslīm), whether by the heart, by the tongue, or by the limbs. The most excellent of these is that which is by the heart, which is the assent (taṣdīq) that is called faith. Using the two terms in a way that indicates distinction, overlap, or even complete synonymy (tarāduf) is all within the bounds of metaphorical usage (tajawwuz) in the language.
72:13.section_title_en: The Book of the Revival of the Religious Sciences — Section 99: On the Distinction, Overlap, and Synonymy of Faith (Īmān) and Submission (Islām), and Their Worldly and Otherworldly Judgments
72:13.anchors:
- Root: ايم (A-Y-M)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of remaining unmarried, or a state of being without a spouse; extended metaphorically to describe one who is solitary or without support.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الأيامى: جمع أيم، وهي المرأة التي لا بعل لها... والحرب مأيمة، أي: يفرق بين الزوج والزوجة." The root carries the sense of separation or a state of lacking union, which informs the theological discussion of what constitutes the essential bond of faith.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah) usage denotes the state of being unmarried; metaphorical (Majaz) usage extends to anything that separates or leaves one bereft. This distinction between literal and metaphorical application is central to the chapter's method.
- Root: قلب (Q-L-B)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To turn, overturn, or transform a thing from one state to another.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "قلب الشيء: تصريفه وصرفه عن وجه إلى وجه... والانقلاب: الانصراف." The heart (qalb) is so named for its constant fluctuation and turning. In theological terms, it is the seat of taṣdīq (assent), the immaterial faculty of cognition and conviction.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah) usage is physical turning; metaphorical (Majaz) usage is "قلب الأمور" — to deliberate, scrutinize, and manage affairs. This supports the distinction between the heart's internal act of assent and the external acts of the limbs.
- Root: عمل (ʿ-A-M-L)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Any deed or action performed with purpose and intent.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "العمل: كل فعل يكون من الحيوان بقصد، فهو أخص من الفعل." Work is more specific than mere action, as it implies deliberate, intentional agency. It is used for both righteous and sinful deeds, and is the external manifestation of internal conviction.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah) usage refers to physical labor or deeds. The chapter explores whether "work" is an integral part of the reality of faith or a separate, consequent requirement.
- Root: صدق (S-D-Q)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To be truthful, to speak the truth, to verify.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الصدق والكذب أصلهما في القول... ولا يكونان بالقصد الأول إلا في القول." Truth and falsehood are primarily properties of speech and reports. Taṣdīq (assent) is the heart's affirmation of the truth of a report, which is the core reality of Īmān.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah) usage is truthful speech; metaphorical (Majaz) usage is "صادق الحملة" — one who is true and firm in battle or resolve. This shows that taṣdīq is not merely verbal but a firm, internal resolution.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication). This rule governs how restriction (ḥaṣr) is achieved in Arabic, often through particles like "innamā" or through contextual specification (takhṣīṣ). The chapter's core argument hinges on how terms like Īmān and Islām are semantically restricted, expanded, or made synonymous through contextual usage (majāz), requiring precise parsing of the predicate and its scope.

72:23.arabic: بالمشيئة يدل على الانقسام وقوله تعالى {ومن يعص الله ورسوله فإن له نار جهنم خالدين فيها} وتخصيصه بالكفر تحكم وقوله تعالى {ألا إن الظالمين في عذاب مقيم} وقال تعالى {ومن جاء بالسيئة فكبت وجوههم في النار} فهذه العمومات في معارضة عموماتهم ولا بد من تسليط التخصص والتأويل على الجانبين لأن الأخبار مصرحة بأن العصاة يعذبون (1) بل قوله تعالى وإن منكم إلا واردها كالصريح في أن ذلك لا بد منه للكل إذ لا يخلو مؤمن عن ذنب يرتكبه وقوله تعالى لا يصلاها إلا الأشقى الذي كذب وتولى أراد به من جماعة مخصوصين أو أراد بالأشقى شخصا معينا أيضا وقوله تعال
72:23.english: He was asked, "Which deed is most excellent?" The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Islam." It was then asked, "Which aspect of Islam is most excellent?"
