2:25.arabic: والسلوى والعسل واللبن وأصناف كثيرة لا تحصى قال الله تعالى كلما رزقوا فيها من ثمرة رزقا قالوا هذا الذي رزقنا من قبل وأتوا به متشابها وذكر الله تعالى شراب أهل الجنة في مواضع كثيرة وقد قال ثوبان مولى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كنت قائما عند رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فجاءه حبر من أحبار اليهود فذكر أسئلة إلى أن قال فمن أول إجازة يعني على الصراط فقال فقراء المهاجرين قال اليهودي فما تحفتهم حين يدخلون الجنة قال زيادة كبد الحوت قال فما غداؤهم على أثرها قال ينحر لهم ثور الجنة الذي كان يأكل في أطرافها قال فما شرابهم عليه قال من عين فيها تسمى سلسبيلا فقال صدقت (7) وقال زيد
2:25.english: The description of the food of the people of Paradise is mentioned in the Qur'an: fruits, fattened birds, manna (al-mann) and quails (al-salwā), honey, milk, and countless other varieties. God Most High said: {«كُلَّمَا رُزِقُوا مِنْهَا مِنْ ثَمَرَةٍ رِزْقًا قَالُوا هَٰذَا الَّذِي رُزِقْنَا مِنْ قَبْلُ وَأُتُوا بِهِ مُتَشَابِهًا»} "Whenever they are given a fruit therefrom as provision, they will say: 'This is what we were provided with before,' and it is brought to them in resemblance." And God Most High mentioned the drink of the people of Paradise in many places.
2:25.section_title_en: The Description of the Food of the People of Paradise
2:25.anchors:
- Root: طعم (ṭaʿima)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning is tasting, eating, and by extension the substance of food itself; the act of ingestion and its object.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In theological context, the Quranic descriptions of food and drink in Paradise are not mere metaphors but designate real (ḥaqīqī) pleasures granted to the blessed, affirming the resurrection of the body alongside the soul.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) usage applies to physical consumption; metaphorical (majāz) usage is absent here, as the texts affirm actual eating and drinking in the Hereafter.
- Root: عرق (ʿirq)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Root denotes a vein, root, or channel; also sweat that exudes from the body.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The sweat of the people of Paradise is a subtle (laṭīf) bodily emission, purified of foulness, serving as a sign of the perfected corporeal state free from base needs.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: sweat from the skin. Metaphorical: its description as "like musk" (misk) transfers the sensory quality of fragrance to a spiritualized corporeal reality.
- Root: طير (ṭayr)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Birds; creatures with wings that fly in the air.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Birds in Paradise are real created beings, yet their instantaneous transformation into roasted meat upon desire demonstrates the omnipotence of God and the suspension of natural causality in the Hereafter.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: birds as animals. Metaphorical: the phrase "like Bactrian camels" (mithl al-bukhātī) is a simile (tashbīh) for size, not a claim of species identity.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Conditional Clauses (Bāb al-sharṭ) — The construction "if you desire it, it falls before you roasted" (tashtahīhi fa-yakhirru bayna yadayka mashwiyyan) uses a conditional protasis followed by an apodosis in the past tense to express immediate, certain consequence, a hallmark of Quranic and prophetic style for emphasizing divine responsiveness.
2:25.topic: Al-Ghazali on the journey of the soul, death, and the Hereafter, from 'Remembrance of Death and Afterlife'

2:48.arabic: ويوم لا تجزي نفس عن نفس شيئا ويوم تشخص فيه الأبصار ويوم لا يغنى مولى عن مولى شيئا ويوم لا تملك نفس لنفس شيئا ويوم يدعون إلى نار جهنم دعا ويوم يسحبون فى النار على وجوههم ويوم تقلب وجوههم فى النار ويوم لا يجزى والد عن ولده ويوم يفر المرء من أخيه وأمه وأبيه ويوم لا ينطقون ولا يؤذن لهم فيعتذرون يوم لا مرد له من الله يوم هم بارزون ويوم هم على النار يفتنون يوم لا ينفع مال ولا بنون يوم لا ينفع الظالمين معذرتهم ولهم اللعنة ولهم سوء الدار يوم ترد فيه المعاذير وتبلى الس
2:48.english: So prepare yourself, O wretched one, for this Day of immense magnitude, of prolonged duration, of overwhelming dominion, whose appointed time is near — a Day when you shall see the heaven split asunder, and the stars scattered in its terror, and the shining planets extinguished, and the sun folded up, and the mountains set in motion, and the pregnant camels neglected, and the wild beasts gathered together, and the seas set ablaze, and the souls paired with their bodies, and the Hellfire ignited, and Paradise brought near, and the mountains pulverized, and the earth stretched out — a Day when you shall see the earth shaken with its quaking, and the earth casts forth its burdens. On that Day shall people issue forth in scattered groups to be shown their deeds — a Day when the earth and the mountains are lifted and crushed with a single crushing. Then on that Day the Imminent Event shall come to pass, and the heaven shall split open, for on that Day it shall be frail, and the angels shall be at its edges, and eight shall bear the Throne of your Lord above them on that Day. On that Day you shall be presented — no secret of yours shall remain hidden. A Day when the mountains shall move and you shall see the earth laid bare — a Day when the earth shall be shaken with a violent shaking, and the mountains crumbled to dust, becoming scattered particles — a Day when people shall be like scattered moths, and the mountains like carded wool — a Day when every nursing mother shall forget what she nursed, and every pregnant female shall cast down her burden, and you shall see people drunk, yet they are not drunk, but the chastisement of God is severe — a Day when the earth shall be changed to other than this earth, and the heavens, and they shall appear before God, the One, the All-Compelling — a Day when the mountains shall be blown away as dust, leaving a level, bare plain, wherein you see no crookedness nor curve — a Day when you see the mountains and suppose them solid, yet they pass by like the passing of clouds — a Day when the heaven shall split open and become rosy like molten oil. Then on that Day no human nor jinn shall be asked about his sin. A Day when the disobedient shall be prevented from speech, and shall not be asked about their crimes, but shall be seized by their forelocks and their feet — a Day when every soul shall find what it did of good brought forth present, and what it did of evil, wishing that between it and that evil there were a far distance — a Day when every soul shall know what it has sent ahead, and shall witness what it has forwarded and what it has left behind — a Day when tongues shall be struck mute and the bodily members shall speak — a Day whose mention turned the hair of the Master of the Messengers white, when al-Ṣiddīq (may God be pleased with him) said to him: "I see that you have turned white-haired, O Messenger of God." He said: "Sūrat Hūd and its sisters have made me white-haired" — namely, al-Wāqiʿah, al-Mursalāt, ʿAmma Yatasāʾalūn, and Idhā al-Shamsu Kuwwirat.
2:48.section_title_en: The Names and Attributes of the Day of Resurrection — An Exhortation to the Negligent
2:48.anchors:
- Root: يوم (yawm)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "اليوم: وقت طلوع الشمس إلى غروبها، وقد يعبر به عن مدة من الزمان أي مدة كانت" — the day as a temporal span, extended metaphorically to any epoch or era.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "اليوم يعبر به عن وقت طلوع الشمس إلى غروبها. وقد يعبر به عن مدة من الزمان أي مدة كانت" — theological usage denotes the appointed time of reckoning, magnified by divine attribution (أيام الله).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): a measured solar period. Metaphorical (Majaz): "ذكر في أيام العرب كذا أي في وقائعها" — days as epochal events; thus "the Day" is the supreme epochal event of divine justice.
- Root: نفس (nafs)
  * Lisan / Ayn: النفس: الروح والذات — the self, soul, or very essence.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "النفس: الروح... وقوله: ويحذركم الله نفسه فنفسه: ذاته" — nafs as the innermost reality of a being; in the eschatological context, souls are "paired" (زوجت) with bodies for judgment.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the soul as life-principle. Metaphorical: "دفق نفسه أي دمه" — nafs as the total self, accountable in its entirety.
- Root: ارض (arḍ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: الأرض: الجرم المقابل للسماء — the earth as the corporeal substratum beneath the heavens.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الأرض: الجرم المقابل للسماء... ويعبر بها عن أسفل الشيء" — the earth as the lowest register of creation, subject to total transformation on that Day.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the physical earth. Metaphorical: "تأرض فلان: لزم الأرض" — to cling low; on that Day the earth itself is leveled, flattened, and replaced.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد (Restriction & Focused Predication) — The repeated "يوم" clauses function as temporal restrictors (ẓurūf) binding each predicate to that single, all-encompassing moment; the accumulation of names (أسامي) serves not as mere repetition but as focused predication upon the multifarious realities of a single event.
2:48.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Remembrance of Death and Afterlife'

2:90.arabic: الروح من أمره على من يشاء من عباده} وأحال الإغواء على إبليس فقال تعالى {ليضل عن سبيله} والإغواء هو استيقاف العباد دون بلوغ غاية الحكمة فانظر كيف نسبه إلى العبد الذي غضب عليه والإرشاد سياقه لهم إلى الغاية فانظر كيف نسبه إلى العبد الذي أحبه وعندك في العادة له مثال فالملك إذا كان محتاجا إلى من يسقيه الشراب وإلى من يحجمه وينظف فناء منزله عن القاذورات وكان له عبدان فلا يعين للحجامة والتنظيف إلا أقبحهما وأخسهما ولا يفوض حمل الشراب والطيب إلا إلى أحسنهما وأكملهما وأحبهما إليه ولا ينبغ
2:90.english: Thus was the beginning of this matter and its end. And do not understand it unless you are worthy of it. And if you are worthy of it, the eye is opened and you see, so you have no need of a leader to lead you. The blind man can indeed be led, but only to a limit. For when the path narrows and becomes sharper than a sword and finer than a hair, the bird is able to fly over it but is not able to drag a blind man behind it. And when the field becomes narrow and subtle — subtle as water, for example — and crossing is possible only by swimming, then the one skilled in the art of swimming may be able to cross by himself, and perhaps he is not able to drag another behind him. These matters bear the same relation to walking upon the way of the common masses of creatures as walking upon water bears to walking upon earth. Swimming can be learned; but as for walking upon water, it is not acquired by instruction, but rather is attained through the strength of certainty (yaqīn). For this reason it was said to the Prophet, peace be upon him, that Jesus, peace be upon him, was said to have walked upon water, and he, peace be upon him, said: "Had his certainty increased, he would have walked upon the air." {«حديث قيل له يقال إن عيسى مشى على الماء قال لو ازداد يقينا لمشي على الهواء»} — This hadith is rejected (munkar) and is not known in this form. What is known is what Ibn Abi al-Dunya narrated in the Book of Certainty from the saying of Bakr ibn Abd Allah al-Muzani, who said: The disciples lost their Prophet, and it was said to them: "He has headed toward the sea." So they set out seeking him, and when they reached the sea, behold, he was coming toward them walking upon the water. And he mentioned a hadith in which Jesus said: "If the son of Adam had a hair's breadth of certainty, he would walk upon the water." And Abu Mansur al-Daylami narrated in the Musnad al-Firdaws with a weak chain from the hadith of Muadh ibn Jabal: "If you knew God with true knowledge, you would walk upon the seas, and the mountains would be removed by your supplications." These are symbols and allusions to the meaning of aversion (karāhah) and love (maḥabbah), and good pleasure (riḍā) and wrath (ghaḍab), and gratitude (shukr) and ingratitude (kufrān) — more than this is not fitting for the science of practical conduct (ʿilm al-muʿāmalah). And God, exalted be He, struck an example of this to draw it near to the understanding of creatures, since He knew that He created the jinn and mankind only to worship Him, and their worship was the ultimate purpose of wisdom (ghāyat al-ḥikmah) with respect to them. Then He informed that He has two servants: one whom He loves, whose name is Gabriel — the Holy Spirit and the Trustworthy One — and he is with Him beloved, obeyed, trustworthy, and honored; and another whom He hates, whose name is Iblis — the accursed one, reprieved until the Day of Judgment. Then He delegated guidance (irshād) to Gabriel, saying, the Exalted: {«قل نزله روح القدس من ربك بالحق»} "Say: The Holy Spirit has brought it down from your Lord with truth" (16:102), and said, the Exalted: {«يلقي الروح من أمره على من يشاء من عباده»} "He casts the Spirit of His command upon whom He wills of His servants" (40:15). And He delegated misguidance (ighwāʾ) to Iblis, saying, the Exalted: {«ليضل عن سبيله»} "That he may lead astray from His path" (4:119). And ighwāʾ is the halting of servants short of attaining the ultimate purpose of wisdom. So observe how He attributed it to the servant with whom He was wrathful; and guidance (irshād) is the conduct of them toward the ultimate purpose — so observe how He attributed it to the servant whom He loves. And you have an example of this in custom: when a king is in need of one to give him drink and one to cup him and to clean the courtyard of his house of filth, and he has two servants, he does not appoint for cupping and cleaning except the ugliest and meanest of them, and he does not entrust the carrying of drink and perfume except to the best and most complete of them and the most beloved to him. And you should not say: "This is my act, and his act was not without my act" — for you have erred when you attributed that to yourself. Rather, He is the One who directed your motive (dāʿiyah) to the specification of the disliked act to the disliked person, and the beloved act to the beloved person, as a completion of justice (ʿadl). For His justice is sometimes completed through matters in which you have no entry, and sometimes it is completed in you — for you also are among His acts. So your motive, your power, your knowledge, your action, and all the other causes of your movements in expression — all of this is His act, which He arranged with justice in an arrangement from which moderate acts issue forth. Except that you see only yourself, and so you suppose that what appears through you in the world of witness (ʿālam al-shahādah) has no cause from the world of the unseen and the dominion (ʿālam al-ghayb wa al-malakūt). Therefore you attribute it to yourself. And you are only like the child who looks at night at the play of the juggler (mushʿabadh) who brings forth figures from behind a curtain that dance and scream and rise and sit, composed of rags that do not move by themselves — rather, they are moved by fine hair-like threads that do not appear in the darkness of night, their ends in the hand of the juggler, who is hidden from the eyes of the children. So they rejoice and marvel, supposing that those rags dance and play and rise and sit. As for the intelligent ones, they know that this is a moving (taḥrīk) and not a self-movement, but perhaps they do not know its detailed modality. And the one who knows some of its detail does not know it as the juggler knows it, to whom the command belongs and in whose hand is the pulling. Likewise, the children of the people of this world — and all creatures are children relative to the scholars — look at these persons (ashkhāṣ) and suppose that they are the movers, and so they attribute [action] to them. And the scholars know that they are moved, except that they do not know the modality of the moving — and they are the majority. Except the knowers (ʿārifūn), the scholars, and those firmly rooted in knowledge (al-rāsikhūn), for they have perceived, with the sharpness of their sight, fine spider-web threads — nay, much finer than these — suspended from heaven, their ends attached to the persons of the people of the earth. Those threads are not perceived, due to their fineness, by these outward eyes. Then they witnessed the heads of those threads in their suspension-points (manāṭāt) to which they are attached, and they witnessed for those suspension-points handles (maqābiḍ) that are in the hands of the angels who move the heavens. And they also witnessed the angels of the heavens directed toward the bearers of the Throne (ḥamalat al-ʿarsh), awaiting what descends upon them of the command from the presence of Lordship (ḥaḍrat al-rubūbiyyah) — "they do not disobey God in what He commands them, and they do what they are commanded" (66:6). And He expressed these witnessed realities in the Qur'an, and it was said: {«وفي السماء رزقكم وما توعدون»} "And in the heaven is your provision and what you are promised" (51:22). And He expressed the waiting of the angels of the heavens for what descends upon them of decree and command, and it was said: "He created seven heavens and of the earth the like of them; {«يتنزل الأمر بينهن لتعلموا أن الله على كل شيء قدير وأن الله قد أحاط بكل شيء علما»} 'the command descends between them, that you may know that God is powerful over all things and that God encompasses all things in knowledge'" (65:12). These are matters whose interpretation (taʾwīl) none knows except God and those firmly rooted in knowledge (al-rāsikhūn fī al-ʿilm). And Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, expressed the exclusivity of those firmly rooted in knowledge to sciences that the understandings of creatures cannot bear, when he recited the saying of the Exalted: {«يتنزل الأمر بينهن»} "The command descends between them," and said: "Were I to mention what I know of the meaning of this verse, you would stone me" — and in another wording: "You would say he is an unbeliever."
2:90.section_title_en: On the Degrees of Proximity to God and the Hierarchy of Those Who Perfect Divine Wisdom
2:90.anchors:
- Root: سير (s-y-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "السير: الذهاب والسفر، وسار يسير سيرا ومسيرا، والسيارة: الرفقة المسافرة"
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "السير: الانتقال من مكان إلى مكان، ويستعار للسلوك في الدين والطريقة"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): [Literal] "سار القوم: مشوا" — [Metaphorical] "سار فيه السير: مضى في الأمر، وسار ذكره: انتشر، ومنه: سيرة فلان: طريقته"
- Root: مشي (m-sh-y)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "المشي: تردد الأركان على الأرض، والماشية: الإبل والغنم لانتقالها في المرعى"
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "المشي: الانتقال من مكان إلى مكان بإرادة، ويكنى به عن النميمة، وعن شرب المسهل"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): [Literal] "مشيت وتمشيت، وهي حسنة المشية" — [Metaphorical] "مشى بطنه، وأمشاه الدواء، واستمشيت بالدواء، ومنه: مشت المرأة: كثرت أولادها"
- Root: خلق (kh-l-q)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الخلق: التقدير، والخلق: الناس، والخليقة: الطبيعة، والخلق: السجية"
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الخلق أصله: التقدير المستقيم، ويستعمل في إبداع الشيء من غير أصل ولا احتذاء"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): [Literal] "خلق الخراز الأديم: قدره قبل القطع" — [Metaphorical] "خلق الله الخلق: أوجده على تقدير أوجبته الحكمة"
- Root: نفس (n-f-s)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "النفس: الروح، والذات، والشيء النفيس"
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "النفس: الروح، وتطلق على الذات، قال تعالى: {ويحذركم الله نفسه} فنفسه: ذاته"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): [Literal] "شيء نفيس ومنفس" — [Metaphorical] "دفق نفسه أي دمه، وأصابته نفس: عين"
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — Used to distinguish exclusive attribution of actions to God versus creatures, as in "إنما أنت مثل الصبي" (You are only like a child), restricting the simile to the creature while preserving divine agency.
2:90.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'Remembrance of Death and Afterlife'

2:90.arabic: جاءهم ما عرفوا كفروا به} إلى قوله {أن يكفروا بما أنزل الله بغيا} أي حسدا وقالت صفية بنت حيي للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم جاء أبي وعمي من عندك يوما فقال أبي لعمي ما تقول فيه قال أقول أنه النبي الذي بشر به موسى قال فما ترى قال أرى معاداته أيام الحياة (2) فهذا حكم الحسد في التحريم وأما المنافسة فليست بحرام بل هي إما واجبة وإما مندوبة وإما مباحة وقد يستعمل لفظ الحسد بدل المنافسة والمنافسة بدل الحسد قال قثم بن العباس لما أراد هو والفضل أن يأتيا النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فيسألاه أن يؤمرهما على الصدقة قالا لعلي حين
2:90.english: The Prophet ﷺ said: «إن المؤمن يغبط والمنافق يحسد» — "The believer aspires emulously, and the hypocrite envies."
2:90.section_title_en: On the Reality of Envy (Ḥasad) and Its Degrees — Section 720
2:90.anchors:
- Root: نعم (n-ʿ-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root meaning of "bounty, benefaction, grace" — that state of goodness and well-being bestowed.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "النعمة: الحالة الحسنة" — bounty is the excellent state/condition; it is the genus term applying to both little and much, as in {«وإن تعدوا نعمة الله لا تحصوها»} [Ibrahim: 34].
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): "جلت نعمة الله ونعماؤه" — bounty as actual bestowed good. Metaphorical (majāz): "خفت نعامتهم" — departure/removal, relevant to the envier's wish for the bounty's removal.
- Root: حسد (ḥ-s-d)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Envy — the desire for removal of another's good.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الحسد: تمني زوال نعمة من مستحق لها" — envy is wishing the removal of bounty from one who deserves it, sometimes accompanied by striving to effect its removal. Cited: «المؤمن يغبط والمنافق يحسد».
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "حسده على نعمة الله" — envying someone for God's bounty. "إن الحسد يأكل الجسد" — envy consumes the body.
- Root: نفس (n-f-s)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The self; also value, preciousness.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): النفس: الروح — the soul/spirit; also الذات (essence/self).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "شيء نفيس ومنفس" — a precious thing. Metaphorical: "دفق نفسه أي دمه" — poured out his self, i.e., his blood. From this root derives المنافسة (emulative competition) — the striving for precious things.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد (Restriction & Specification) — The definition of ḥasad is given as a restricted predication (ḥadd), delimiting its essential meaning: "كراهة النعمة وحب زوالها عن المنعم عليه" — the hatred of bounty and love of its removal from the one upon whom it is bestowed. This is a formal definition (ḥadd), not merely a lexical gloss.
2:90.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'Condemnation of Envy'

2:96.arabic: الله تعالى يود أحدهم لو يعمر ألف سنة ومنهم من يأمل البقاء إلى الهرم وهو أقصى العمر الذي شاهده ورآه وهو الذي يحب الدنيا حبا شديدا قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم الشيخ شاب في حب طلب الدنيا وإن التفت ترقوتاه من الكبر إلا الذين اتقوا وقليل ما هم (1) ومنهم من يأمل إلى سنة فلا يشتغل بتدبير ما وراءها فلا يقدر لنفسه وجودا في عام قابل ولكن هذا يستعد في الصيف للشتاء وفي الشتاء للصيف فإذا جمع ما يكفيه لسنته اشتغل بالعبادة ومنهم من يأمل مدة الصيف أو الشتاء فلا يدخر في الصيف ثياب
2:96.english: I say: Know that people vary in this matter [of hope's length and brevity]. Among them is one who hopes for survival and desires it perpetually. Allah Most High said: {يَوَدُّ أَحَدُهُمْ لَوْ يُعَمَّرُ أَلْفَ سَنَةٍ} "One of them wishes he might live a thousand years" (Al-Baqarah 96). Among them is one who hopes for survival until senility — that being the farthest lifespan he has witnessed and seen — and he is the one who loves this world with intense love. The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "The old man is young in the love of seeking this world, even if his collarbones have bent from old age — except for the God-fearing, and few they are." Among them is one who hopes for a single year, so he does not occupy himself with managing what lies beyond it, and he does not grant himself existence in the coming year. But this one prepares in summer for winter and in winter for summer; when he has gathered what suffices him for his year, he occupies himself with worship. Among them is one whose hope reverts to the duration of summer or winter, so he does not store winter clothes in summer, nor summer clothes in winter. Among them is one whose hope returns to a day and a night, so he prepares only for his daytime, and as for tomorrow, he does not. Jesus, peace be upon him, said: "Do not worry about the provision of tomorrow; for if tomorrow is among your appointed terms, your provisions will come to you in it along with your terms, and if it is not among your terms, then do not worry about the terms of others." Among them is one whose hope does not exceed an hour, as our Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "O servant of Allah, when you enter the morning, do not speak to yourself of the evening, and when you enter the evening, do not speak to yourself of the morning." Among them is one who does not even grant himself survival for an hour — the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, used to perform dry ablution (tayammum) despite the availability of water before an hour passed, saying, "Perhaps I will not reach it." Among them is one who has death placed before his very eyes as if it has already befallen him, so he awaits it. This is the man who prays the prayer of a farewell. Concerning this, what is transmitted from Muʿādh ibn Jabal, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, is relevant: when the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, asked him about the reality of his faith, he said, "I have not taken a single step except that I thought I would not follow it with another." Likewise, what is transmitted from al-Aswad, an Abyssinian, that he used to pray at night and turn right and left, and a speaker said to him, "What is this?" He said, "I am looking to see from which direction the Angel of Death will come to me." These are the ranks of people, and for each are degrees with Allah. The one whose hope is confined to a month is not like the one whose hope is a month and a day; rather, between them is a difference in degree with Allah, for {إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَا يَظْلِمُ مِثْقَالَ ذَرَّةٍ وَمَنْ يَعْمَلْ مِثْقَالَ ذَرَّةٍ خَيْرًا يَرَهُ} "Indeed, Allah does not wrong even the weight of an atom, and whoever does an atom's weight of good shall see it" (Al-Zalzalah 7-8). Then the effect of shortened hope appears in hastening to action. Every person claims to be short of hope, yet he is a liar; this is only manifested by his deeds, for he attends to causes that perhaps he will not need for a year — and that indicates the length of his hope. The sole sign of divine success (tawfīq) is that death be placed before one's eyes, not neglected for an hour. So let him prepare for the death that will come upon him at any moment; for if he lives until evening, he thanks Allah Most High for his obedience and rejoices that he did not waste his day, but rather extracted his full share from it and stored it for himself. Then he resumes the like of it until morning, and likewise when he enters the morning. And this is not facilitated except for one whose heart is emptied of tomorrow and what it contains. Such a one, if he dies, has prospered and gained; and if he lives, he rejoices in the excellence of his preparation and the delight of intimate communion (munājāh). So death is for him a happiness, and life is for him an increase. Let death be on your mind, O wretched one, for the journey is hastening you onward while you are heedless of yourself — perhaps you have already neared the destination and traversed the distance. And you will not be so except by hastening to action, seizing the opportunity of every breath in which you are granted respite.
2:96.section_title_en: Exposition of the Ranks of People Regarding the Length and Shortness of Hope (Bayān Marātib al-Nās fī Ṭūl al-Amal wa Qiṣrih)
2:96.anchors:
- Root: أمل (amal)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning is "hope" or "expectation" — the soul's aspiration toward a future occurrence; its length or brevity determines one's orientation to worldly life versus the Hereafter.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: Amal is the psychological attachment to prolonged life in this world (Ṭūl al-Amal), which the Qur'an censures as a veil from preparation for death; its opposite is qaṣr al-amal (shortening of hope), a mark of true piety and vigilance.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): Amal as genuine expectation of future events. Metaphorical (Majaz): When coupled with deeds, it reveals the heart's true state — a man's claim of short hope is tested by his actual preparations, which betray hidden length of hope.
- Root: موت (mawt)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Death as the cessation of life; also "dead land" (mawāt) — that which is lifeless and awaiting revival.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Death is not annihilation but transition; the soul's separation from the body. In Kalam, it is an accident (ʿaraḍ) created by Allah, and the believer's constant awareness of it is the catalyst for righteous action.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: Physical death. Metaphorical: "Placing death before one's eyes" (al-mawt naṣb ʿaynayh) — a state of perpetual mindfulness where one acts as if death is imminent, transforming hope into urgent obedience.
- Root: نفس (nafs)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The self or soul; also breath — the animating principle.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Nafs as the locus of desire and aspiration; here, the self that must be disciplined against false hopes, for it naturally clings to worldly survival.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: The soul's innate longing. Metaphorical: "Do not speak to yourself" (lā tuḥaddith nafsaka) — restraining the inner dialogue that projects future plans, a discipline of the subtle reality (laṭīfah) within.
- Root: صيف (ṣayf)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Summer — a season of provision and preparation.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Summer and winter (Quraysh 2) symbolize cyclical worldly concerns; the wise prepare in one season for the next, but the truly awakened prepare only for the hour at hand.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: Seasonal preparation. Metaphorical: "Summer-born" (ṣayfiyyūn) — children born late in life, akin to those whose hope extends only to a season, yet even this is a form of worldly attachment.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — Used in the final clause "إنما علامة التوفيق" to restrict the sole sign of divine success to keeping death before one's eyes, excluding all other pretensions.
2:96.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Remembrance of Death and Afterlife'

2:123.arabic: ويوم لا تجزي نفس عن نفس شيئا ويوم تشخص فيه الأبصار ويوم لا يغنى مولى عن مولى شيئا ويوم لا تملك نفس لنفس شيئا ويوم يدعون إلى نار جهنم دعا ويوم يسحبون فى النار على وجوههم ويوم تقلب وجوههم فى النار ويوم لا يجزى والد عن ولده ويوم يفر المرء من أخيه وأمه وأبيه ويوم لا ينطقون ولا يؤذن لهم فيعتذرون يوم لا مرد له من الله يوم هم بارزون ويوم هم على النار يفتنون يوم لا ينفع مال ولا بنون يوم لا ينفع الظالمين معذرتهم ولهم اللعنة ولهم سوء الدار يوم ترد فيه المعاذير وتبلى الس
2:123.english: So prepare yourself, O wretched one, for this Day of immense magnitude, of prolonged duration, of overwhelming dominion, whose appointed time is near — a Day when you shall see the heaven split asunder, and the stars scattered in its terror, and the shining planets extinguished, and the sun folded up, and the mountains set in motion, and the pregnant camels neglected, and the wild beasts gathered together, and the seas set ablaze, and the souls paired with their bodies, and the Hellfire ignited, and Paradise brought near, and the mountains pulverized, and the earth stretched out — a Day when you shall see the earth shaken with its quaking, and the earth casts forth its burdens. On that Day shall people issue forth in scattered groups to be shown their deeds — a Day when the earth and the mountains are lifted and crushed with a single crushing. Then on that Day the Imminent Event shall come to pass, and the heaven shall split open, for on that Day it shall be frail, and the angels shall be at its edges, and eight shall bear the Throne of your Lord above them on that Day. On that Day you shall be presented — no secret of yours shall remain hidden. A Day when the mountains shall move and you shall see the earth laid bare — a Day when the earth shall be shaken with a violent shaking, and the mountains crumbled to dust, becoming scattered particles — a Day when people shall be like scattered moths, and the mountains like carded wool — a Day when every nursing mother shall forget what she nursed, and every pregnant female shall cast down her burden, and you shall see people drunk, yet they are not drunk, but the chastisement of God is severe — a Day when the earth shall be changed to other than this earth, and the heavens, and they shall appear before God, the One, the All-Compelling — a Day when the mountains shall be blown away as dust, leaving a level, bare plain, wherein you see no crookedness nor curve — a Day when you see the mountains and suppose them solid, yet they pass by like the passing of clouds — a Day when the heaven shall split open and become rosy like molten oil. Then on that Day no human nor jinn shall be asked about his sin. A Day when the disobedient shall be prevented from speech, and shall not be asked about their crimes, but shall be seized by their forelocks and their feet — a Day when every soul shall find what it did of good brought forth present, and what it did of evil, wishing that between it and that evil there were a far distance — a Day when every soul shall know what it has sent ahead, and shall witness what it has forwarded and what it has left behind — a Day when tongues shall be struck mute and the bodily members shall speak — a Day whose mention turned the hair of the Master of the Messengers white, when al-Ṣiddīq (may God be pleased with him) said to him: "I see that you have turned white-haired, O Messenger of God." He said: "Sūrat Hūd and its sisters have made me white-haired" — namely, al-Wāqiʿah, al-Mursalāt, ʿAmma Yatasāʾalūn, and Idhā al-Shamsu Kuwwirat.
2:123.section_title_en: The Names and Attributes of the Day of Resurrection — An Exhortation to the Negligent
2:123.anchors:
- Root: يوم (yawm)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "اليوم: وقت طلوع الشمس إلى غروبها، وقد يعبر به عن مدة من الزمان أي مدة كانت" — the day as a temporal span, extended metaphorically to any epoch or era.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "اليوم يعبر به عن وقت طلوع الشمس إلى غروبها. وقد يعبر به عن مدة من الزمان أي مدة كانت" — theological usage denotes the appointed time of reckoning, magnified by divine attribution (أيام الله).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): a measured solar period. Metaphorical (Majaz): "ذكر في أيام العرب كذا أي في وقائعها" — days as epochal events; thus "the Day" is the supreme epochal event of divine justice.
- Root: نفس (nafs)
  * Lisan / Ayn: النفس: الروح والذات — the self, soul, or very essence.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "النفس: الروح... وقوله: ويحذركم الله نفسه فنفسه: ذاته" — nafs as the innermost reality of a being; in the eschatological context, souls are "paired" (زوجت) with bodies for judgment.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the soul as life-principle. Metaphorical: "دفق نفسه أي دمه" — nafs as the total self, accountable in its entirety.
- Root: ارض (arḍ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: الأرض: الجرم المقابل للسماء — the earth as the corporeal substratum beneath the heavens.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الأرض: الجرم المقابل للسماء... ويعبر بها عن أسفل الشيء" — the earth as the lowest register of creation, subject to total transformation on that Day.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the physical earth. Metaphorical: "تأرض فلان: لزم الأرض" — to cling low; on that Day the earth itself is leveled, flattened, and replaced.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد (Restriction & Focused Predication) — The repeated "يوم" clauses function as temporal restrictors (ẓurūf) binding each predicate to that single, all-encompassing moment; the accumulation of names (أسامي) serves not as mere repetition but as focused predication upon the multifarious realities of a single event.
2:123.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Remembrance of Death and Afterlife'

2:197.arabic: بأحسن ما بحضرتكم من النقلة وتزودوا فإن خير الزاد التقوى إنما الدنيا كفىء ظلال قلص فذهب بينا ابن آدم في الدنيا ينافس وهو قدير العين إذ دعاه الله بقدره ورماه بيوم حتفه فسلبه آثاره ودنياه وصير لقوم آخرين مصانعه ومغناه إن الدنيا لا تسر بقدر ما تضر إنها تسر قليلا وتحزن طويلا وعن أبي بكر الصديق رضي الله تعالى عنه إنه كان يقول في خطبته أين الوضاء الحسنة وجوههم المعجبون بشبابهم أين الملوك الذين بنوا المدائن وحصنوها بالحيطان أين الذين كانوا يعطون الغلبة في مواطن الحرب قد تضعضع بهم الدهر فأصبحوا في ظلمات القبور
2:197.english: It is narrated that a man said: "He has cast off the means (al-ashāb) and parted from the beloved ones and confronted the reckoning." And by God, I utter this my saying, and I know not that any of you has more sins than what I know of myself. But these are just ordinances from God, equitable; therein I command His obedience and forbid His disobedience. I seek God's forgiveness." And he placed his sleeve over his face and began to weep until his tears wetted his beard, and he did not return to his gathering until he died.
2:197.section_title_en: The Virtue of Shortening Hope (Faḍīlat Qaṣr al-Amal) and the Explanation of the Cause of Long Hope and Its Remedy
2:197.anchors:
- Root: أمل (amal)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of "hope" or "expectation," often extended to "aspiration" or "wish" for future outcomes.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In theological terms, al-amal denotes the soul's inclination toward future possibilities, which, when excessive (ṭūl al-amal), becomes a blameworthy attachment to worldly continuance, distracting from death and the afterlife.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) usage refers to genuine expectation; metaphorical (majāz) usage applies to vain fancies (amānī) that deceive the self into postponing repentance.
- Root: قصر (qaṣr)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To shorten, confine, or restrict; opposite of prolonging.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Qaṣr al-amal is the virtuous discipline of limiting one's worldly expectations, aligning the soul with the reality of death's proximity.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Distinguishes literal shortening (of time or distance) from metaphorical restraint (of the heart's attachments).
- Root: سبب (sabab)
  * Lisan / Ayn: A cord or means by which one reaches something; extended to any cause or linkage.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Every means (sabab) leading to a goal; here, the causes of ṭūl al-amal are identified as ignorance (jahl) and love of the world (ḥubb al-dunyā).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: a physical rope; metaphorical: any instrumental cause, as in the chain of worldly preoccupations.
- Root: دنو (dunūw)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Proximity, nearness in place, time, or rank.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-dunūw is nearness by essence or by judgment; used for spatial, temporal, and status proximity—here, the nearness of death (qurb al-mawt) that the heedless ignore.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical closeness; metaphorical: the inescapable imminence of what is to come (kull mā huwa ātin qarīb).
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — Used to confine predicates to specific subjects, e.g., "إنما الدنيا كفىء ظلال" (The world is but the shade of a passing cloud), emphasizing exclusivity of meaning.
2:197.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'Remembrance of Death and Afterlife'

3:30.arabic: وقال تعالى {ثم توفى كل نفس ما كسبت وهم لا يظلمون} وقال تعالى {يوم تجد كل نفس ما عملت من خير محضرا وما عملت من سوء تود لو أن بينها وبينه أمدا بعيدا ويحذركم الله نفسه} وقال تعالى {واعلموا أن الله يعلم ما في أنفسكم فاحذروه} فعرف أرباب البصائر من جملة العباد أن الله تعالى لهم بالمرصاد وأنهم سيناقشون في الحساب ويطالبون بمثاقيل الذر من الخطرات واللحظات وتحققوا أنه لا ينجيهم من هذه الأخطار إلا لزوم المحاسبة وصدق المراقبة ومطالبة النفس في الأنفاس والحركات ومحاسبتها في الخطرات واللحظات فمن حاسب نفسه قبل أن يحاسب خف في القيامة حسابه وحضر عند السؤال جوابه وحسن منقلبه ومآبه ومن لم يحاس
3:30.english: To proceed: God Most High has said: {And We shall set up the scales of justice for the Day of Resurrection, so no soul shall be wronged in anything; and if it be the weight of a grain of mustard seed, We shall bring it forth, and sufficient are We as Reckoners} (21:47). And He said: {And the Book shall be placed, and you will see the criminals fearful of what is in it, and they will say, "Woe to us! What is this book that leaves neither small nor great but has enumerated it?" And they will find what they did present, and your Lord wrongs no one} (18:49). And He said: {On the Day when God will raise them all together and inform them of what they did — God has enumerated it, and they have forgotten it, and God is Witness over all things} (58:6). And He said: {On that Day, people will issue forth in scattered groups to be shown their deeds. So whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it, and whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it} (99:6-8). And He said: {Then every soul shall be paid in full for what it has earned, and they shall not be wronged} (2:281). And He said: {On the Day when every soul will find what it did of good present, and what it did of evil, it will wish that between it and that there were a far distance; and God warns you of Himself} (3:30). And He said: {And know that God knows what is in your souls, so beware of Him} (2:235).
3:30.section_title_en: Exposition of the Reality of Truthfulness (Al-Sidq), Its Meaning, and Its Grades — Book of Vigilance and Self-Reckoning, Being the Eighth Book of the Quarter of Deliverance from the Revival of the Religious Sciences
3:30.anchors:
- Root: رقب (Raqaba)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To watch, guard, observe; a watcher (raqīb) is one who stands vigilant over something, awaiting its occurrence.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Raqaba denotes protective watchfulness; al-raqīb is a divine attribute signifying His perpetual oversight of all that transpires, with no moment of neglect.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (haqīqah): physical watching/awaiting. Metaphorical (majāz): "This matter is upon your necks (fī riqābikum)" — i.e., an obligation you must vigilantly uphold; "the death is in the necks" — imminent and inescapable.
- Root: حسب (Hasaba)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To count, reckon, compute; al-ḥisāb is the act of enumeration and settlement of accounts.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-ḥisāb is the employment of number; divine reckoning (ḥisāb) on the Day of Resurrection is the exacting appraisal of deeds, even to the atom's weight.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: counting wealth or deeds. Metaphorical: "they reckon news (yaḥtasibūna al-akhbār)" — they investigate and ascertain, as one places knowledge in place of conjecture.
- Root: قلب (Qalaba)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To turn, overturn, transform; the heart (qalb) is so named for its constant fluctuation and turning of states.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Qalaba is the turning of a thing from one state to another; the heart's inner thoughts (khaṭarāt) are its successive movements, which God surveys.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: turning a garment or object. Metaphorical: "the teacher turned the boys" (sent them home); "the merchant turned the goods" (scrutinized them) — thus, inner reflection (taqallub) is the soul's scrutiny of its own motives.
- Sibawayh Rule: Restriction and Focused Predication (al-ḥaṣr wa al-taqyīd bi-innamā) — The particle innamā restricts the predicate to the subject alone, as in "إنما يحاسبهم لتعلم كل نفس" — the sole purpose of reckoning is specified, excluding all other ends.
3:30.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Remembrance of Death and Afterlife'

3:30.arabic: الهوى وستجد كل نفس ما عملت من سوء أو خير محضرا عند الله ولو في فلتة خاطر أو فلتة ناظر من غير ظلم وجور فما الله بظلام للعبيد وأما القسم الثاني وهو فوات الحاصل فهو مكروه ومعتبر في جواز السكوت في الأمور الأربعة إلا العلم فإن فواته غير مخوف إلا بتقصير منه وإلا فلا يقدر أحد على سلب العلم من غيره وإن قدر على سلب الصحة والسلامة والثروة والمال وهذا أحد أسباب شرف العلم فإنه يدوم في الدنيا ويدوم ثوابه في الآخرة فلا انقطاع له أبد الآباد وأما الصحة والسلامة ففواتهما بالضرب فكل من عل
3:30.english: All of this does not nullify the obligation of ḥisbah, because these are but increases (ziyādāt) whose attainment is prevented — and calling the mere prevention of attaining increases "harm" (ḍarar) is metaphorical (majāz). True harm (al-ḍarar al-ḥaqīqī) is only the loss of something already in hand (fawāt ḥāṣil). Nothing is excepted from this rule save that which necessity (ḥājah) calls for, and whose loss entails a danger (maḥdhūr) exceeding the danger of remaining silent over the wrong (al-sukūt ʿalā al-munkar) — as when one is in need of a physician for an acute illness, and the cure is anticipated from the physician's treatment, and he knows that in the physician's delay there is severe aggravation of his malady and prolongation of his sickness, which may even lead to death.
3:30.section_title_en: On the Conditions Permitting Abandonment of Enjoining Right — Section 532
3:30.anchors:
- Root: حسب (ḥ-s-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of counting, reckoning, and calculating; al-ḥisbah derives from the notion of taking account of another's deeds.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الحساب: استعمال العدد" — reckoning is the employment of number; the theological nuance connects to divine accounting and the duty of moral reckoning upon others.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): "حسب المال" — to count property. Metaphorical (majāz): "يَتَحَسَّبانِ الأخبار" — to seek out and investigate news, as one probes and tests; thus ḥisbah is the active seeking-out of wrongs to rectify them.
- Root: ضرر (ḍ-r-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of harm, injury, and detriment; al-ḍarar is that which opposes benefit (nafʿ).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Harm is of two kinds — that which is truly detrimental to one's religion or worldly welfare, and that which is merely imagined or anticipated.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: actual physical or material injury. Metaphorical: the mere loss of an anticipated increase (ziyādah), which is not true harm but is called so figuratively.
- Root: سكت (s-k-t)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of silence, refraining from speech.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "السكوت مختص بترك الكلام" — silence is specific to abstaining from speech; it is a form of rest (sukūn) and is used metaphorically for the subsiding of anger or other states.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "رجل سكوت" — a man habitually silent. Metaphorical: "سكت عنه الغضب" — anger subsided; thus al-sukūt ʿan al-munkar is the deliberate cessation of verbal objection.
- Root: علم (ʿ-l-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of knowledge, perception, and discernment.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "العلم: إدراك الشيء بحقيقته" — knowledge is the apprehension of a thing in its true reality; it is that which cannot be forcibly stripped from its possessor.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "ما علمت بخبرك" — I had no awareness of your news. Metaphorical: knowledge as an enduring mark (ʿalam) and signpost of guidance.
- Sibawayh Rule: Restriction and exception (al-ḥaṣr wa al-istithnāʾ) — the conditional framing of permissibility (al-tarkhīṣ) through specified exceptions (istithnāʾ) governed by the weighing of two harms (taʿāruḍ al-mafsadatayn), where the lesser is borne to avert the greater.
3:30.topic: Al-Ghazali on purifying the character, moral diseases, and spiritual remedies, from 'Enjoining Good and Forbidding Evil'

3:33.arabic: ورأى رجل من أصحاب الحسن البصري ليلة مات الحسن كأن مناديا ينادي إن الله اصطفى آدم ونوحا وآل إبراهيم وآل عمران على العالمين واصطفى الحسن البصري على أهل زمانه وقال أبو يعقوب القاري الدقيقي رأيت في منامي رجلا آدم طوالا والناس يتبعونه فقلت من هذا قالوا أويس القرني فأتيته فقلت أوصني رحمك الله فكلح في وجهي فقلت مسترشدا فأرشدني أرشدك الله فأقبل على وقال اتبع رحمة ربك عند محبته واحذر نقمته عند معصيته ولا تقطع رجاءك منه في خلال ذلك ثم ولى وتركني وقال أبو بكر بن أبي مريم رأيت ورقاء بن بشر الحضرمي فقلت ما فعلت يا ورقاء قال البكاء من خشية الله وقال يزيد بن نعامة هلكت جارية ف
3:33.english: Abu Sa'id al-Shahham said: I saw Sahl al-Sa'luki in a dream and said, "O Shaykh!" He said, "Leave off this addressing me as shaykh." I said, "Those spiritual states (aḥwāl) which you witnessed [in life]?" He said, "They availed us nothing." I said, "What did God do with you?" He said, "He forgave me on account of the questions about which the incapable ones used to ask."
3:33.section_title_en: Section 1333 — Visions of the Deceased and Their States After Death
3:33.anchors:
- Root: م و ت (m-w-t)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Death as the cessation of vital faculty; the state of the deceased (mayyit) contrasted with the living (ḥayy).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Death as separation of the soul from the body, a transition to the Barzakh; visions of the dead (ru'yā) reveal their post-mortem states.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal death (ḥaqīqah) vs. metaphorical "death" of the heart; here, actual death and its aftermath.
- Root: غ ف ر (gh-f-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Covering, protection from defilement; forgiveness as divine concealment of sin.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Divine forgiveness (maghfirah) as God's safeguarding the servant from punishment.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: covering a garment; metaphorical: God's pardon enveloping all sins, as in the vision of Ibn al-Mubarak.
- Root: ر أ ي (r-'-y)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Seeing, perceiving; in dreams (ru'yā), a mode of non-sensory perception.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Vision as a form of divine disclosure (mukāshafah) granted to the righteous.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal sight vs. dream-vision as a vehicle for veridical reports of the unseen.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The rule governing the placement of prepositional phrases and their objects, ensuring syntactic coherence in complex narrative chains, as applied here to the sequence of reported dream-visions.
3:33.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Remembrance of Death and Afterlife'

3:83.arabic: وهو أحد والآصال التي ذكرها الله تعالى إذ قال ولله يسجد من في السموات والأرض طوعا وكرها وظلالهم بالغدو والآصال وإذا سجد لله عز وجل الجمادات فكيف يجوز أن يغفل العبد العاقل عن أنواع العبادات الورد السادس إذا دخل وقت العصر دخل وقت الورد السادس وهو الذي أقسم الله تعالى به فقال تعالى {والعصر} هذا أحد معنيي الآية وهو المراد بالآصال في أحد التفسيرين وهو العشي المذكور في قوله {وعشيا} وفي قوله {بالعشي والإشراق} وليس في هذا الورد صلاة إلا أربع ركعات بين الأذان والإقامة كما سبق في الظهر ثم يصلي الفرض ويشتغل بالأقسام الأربعة المذكورة
3:83.english: I say: And just as knowledge and remembrance are the nourishment of the heart, which can never be cut off from it, so too the measure of moderation is this; and deficiency from it may lead to the disturbance of the body — except for one who accustoms himself to wakefulness gradually, for he may train himself upon it without disturbance. And this litany (wird) is among the longest of the litanies and the most delightful for the worshippers, and it is one of the "evenings and mornings" (al-āṣāl) which God Most High mentioned when He said: {«ولله يسجد من في السموات والأرض طوعا وكرها وظلالهم بالغدو والآصال»} "And to God prostrates whoever is in the heavens and the earth, willingly or unwillingly, and their shadows, in the mornings and the evenings" (Q. 13:15). And when inanimate objects prostrate to God, Mighty and Majestic, how then can the intelligent servant be heedless of the varieties of worship?
3:83.section_title_en: The Seventh Daily Litany (Al-Wird al-Sābiʿ): The Time of Sunset — The Completion of the Day's Litanies and Self-Accounting
3:83.anchors:
- Root: ورد (warada)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The root denotes arriving at water, seeking it, and drinking from it; also the portion or share of water allotted for drinking at a specific time.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الورود أصله: قصد الماء" — the core meaning is the intentional approach to water; the litany (wird) is the appointed portion of devotional recitation, likened to the daily share of water that a person must take to sustain life.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): the act of arriving at water. Metaphorical (Majaz): "ورد علي كتاب سرني مورده" — a book arrived upon me whose arrival pleased me; likewise, the wird is the arrival of the appointed time for worship, and the soul's approach to the fountain of divine remembrance.
- Root: عصر (ʿaṣr)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The root denotes pressing, squeezing, and extracting; also the time of afternoon, so called because it is the pressing of the day's end.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The ʿaṣr is the latter part of the day; God swore by it in {«والعصر»} (Q. 103:1), indicating its great merit.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the afternoon time. Metaphorical: the pressing of one's life — as the day is pressed at its end, so the life of man is pressed at its term.
- Root: غرب (gharaba)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The root denotes disappearance, absence, and setting; the sun's setting (ghurūb) is its concealment from the eye.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The setting of the sun marks the boundary between the day's works and the night's; it is the terminus of the visible world's diurnal cycle.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the sun's descent below the horizon. Metaphorical: the setting of the sun of life — the death of man, after which there is no rising.
- Root: حاسب (ḥāsaba)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The root denotes reckoning, counting, and taking account; muḥāsabah is the mutual reckoning between two parties.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Self-accounting (muḥāsabat al-nafs) is the soul's reckoning with itself over its deeds before the Day of Reckoning, for "one who reckons himself before he is reckoned" is among the wise.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the arithmetic counting of sums. Metaphorical: the soul's audit of its own works, weighing the day's deeds against the standard of the Sacred Law.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The rule governing the separation of the prepositional phrase from its governing verb, as in the construction "فسبحان الله حين تمسون" where the adverbial clause is interposed to emphasize the temporal specification of the act of glorification.
3:83.topic: Al-Ghazali on constant remembrance of God and contemplative invocations, from 'Remembrance of Death and Afterlife'

3:103.arabic: إخوانا} أي بالألفة ثم ذم التفرقة وزجر عنها فقال عز من قائل واعتصموا بحبل الله جميعا ولا تفرقوا إلى لعلكم تهتدون وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم إن أقربكم مني مجلسا أحاسنكم أخلاقا الموطئون أكنافا الذين يألفون ويؤلفون (2) وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم المؤمن آلف مألوف ولا خير فيمن لا يألف ولا يؤلف حديث والمؤمن آلف مألوف ولا خير فيمن لا يألف ولا يؤلف رواه أحمد والطبراني من حديث سهل بن سعد والحاكم من حديث أبي هريرة وصححه (3) حديث من أراد الله به خيرا رزقه أخا صالحا إن نسي ذكره وإن ذكر أعانه غريب بهذا اللفظ والمعروف أن ذلك في الأمير ورواه أبو دا
3:103.english: Know that affability (al-ulfah) is the fruit of excellent character (ḥusn al-khuluq), and estrangement (al-tafarruq) is the fruit of evil character. For excellent character necessitates mutual love, harmony, and concord, whereas evil character yields mutual hatred, envy, and turning away (al-tadābur). And whenever the source is praiseworthy, the fruit is likewise praiseworthy. The excellence of good character is not hidden in the religion; indeed, it is that with which God—glorified be He—praised His Prophet, peace be upon him, when He said: {وَإِنَّكَ لَعَلَىٰ خُلُقٍ عَظِيمٍ} «And indeed, you are upon an immense character» (Al-Qalam: 4). The Prophet, peace be upon him, said: "The thing which most causes people to enter Paradise is God-consciousness (taqwā) and excellent character." (1) Usāmah ibn Sharīk said: "We said, O Messenger of God, what is the best thing given to a person?" He said: "Excellent character." (2) He, peace be upon him, also said: "I was sent only to perfect the noble traits of character." (3) He, peace be upon him, said: "Nothing is heavier in the Balance than excellent character." (4) He, peace be upon him, said: "God does not beautify a person's outward form and his inward character, then feed him to the Fire." (5) He, peace be upon him, said: "O Abū Hurayrah, adhere to excellent character." (Page V02P157) Abū Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him, said: "What is excellent character, O Messenger of God?" He said: "That you join the one who cuts you off, forgive the one who wrongs you, and give to the one who deprives you." (1)
3:103.section_title_en: The Book of the Revival of the Religious Sciences — Section 402: On the Excellence of Affability (Al-Ulfah) and Brotherhood in God
3:103.anchors:
- Root: ألف (Alifa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of harmonizing, uniting, and reconciling; the removal of estrangement (al-waḥshah) and the establishment of concord.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance of ta'līf as the divine act of harmonizing hearts, a blessing bestowed by God alone, as in {لَوْ أَنفَقْتَ مَا فِي الْأَرْضِ جَمِيعًا مَّا أَلَّفْتَ بَيْنَ قُلُوبِهِمْ}.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) denotes physical joining; metaphorical (majāz) denotes the spiritual and moral concord of hearts, which is the fruit of excellent character (ḥusn al-khuluq).
- Root: خلق (Khalaqa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Root meaning of measuring, proportioning, and smoothing; hence, the inherent disposition and moral character of a person.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The origination of a thing upon a just measure; for character, it is the inward form (al-ṣūrah al-bāṭinah) of the soul, just as the physical form is its outward shape.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) is the physical creation and proportioning; metaphorical (majāz) is the moral and spiritual constitution, praised by God in {وَإِنَّكَ لَعَلَىٰ خُلُقٍ عَظِيمٍ}.
- Root: بغض (Bughḍ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The opposite of love (ḥubb); intense aversion and hatred.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In the Kalam context, al-bughḍ fī Allāh (hatred for God's sake) is a spiritual act of discernment and loyalty, not a mere emotional impulse; it is paired with al-ḥubb fī Allāh as the strongest bond of faith (awthaq ʿurā al-īmān).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) is personal animosity; metaphorical (majāz) is the righteous aversion to disobedience and the enemies of God, which is a form of devotion.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Prepositional Interposition (Bāb al-Faṣl bayna al-Jār wa al-Majrūr) — Governing the syntactic flow of conditional and relative clauses, ensuring the periodic structure of the author's argument remains coherent and unbroken.
3:103.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'Duties of Brotherhood'

3:103.arabic: ابن عباس يقرأ {وكنتم على شفا حفرة من النار فأنقذكم منها} فقال الأعرابي فوالله ما أنقذكم منها وهو يريد أن يوقعكم فيها فقال ابن عباس خذوها من غير فقيه وقال الصنابحي دخلت على عبادة بن الصامت وهو في مرض الموت فبكيت فقال مهلا لم تبكي فوالله ما من حديث سمعته من رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لكم فيه خير إلا حدثتكموه إلا حديثا واحدا وسوف أحدثكموه اليوم وقد أحيط بنفسي سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول من شهد أن لا إله إلا الله وأن محمدا رسول الله حرم الله النار عليه (5) وقال عبد الله ابن عمرو بن ا
3:103.english: He mentioned me one day, or feared me in a station (1). And the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: "When the people of the Fire are gathered in the Fire — and with them, whomsoever God wills of the people of the Qiblah — the disbelievers will say to the Muslims: 'Were you not Muslims?' They will reply: 'Yes.' Then they will say: 'What did your Islam avail you, seeing that you are with us in the Fire?' They will answer: 'We had sins, and we were seized for them.' Then God, Mighty and Glorious, will hear what they have said, and He will command that whoever was in the Fire of the people of the Qiblah be brought out, and they will be brought out. When the disbelievers see that, they will say: 'Would that we had been Muslims, so that we might be brought out as they were brought out.' Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited: {ربما يود الذين كفروا لو كانوا مسلمين} — "Perhaps those who disbelieve will wish that they had been Muslims" (Q. 15:2). (2)
3:103.section_title_en: On the Vastness of Divine Mercy and the Intercession for the Sinful — Section 1360
3:103.anchors:
- Root: ذكر (dhakara)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Remembrance, recollection; also mention, invocation.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-dhikr is the opposite of forgetfulness (nisyān); it denotes the heart's presence with what is recalled, and the tongue's utterance thereof.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): to recall in the heart or utter on the tongue. Metaphorical (majāz): "dhakartuhu bi-khayr" — to speak well of someone, i.e., to raise their mention in honor.
- Root: خرج (kharaja)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To exit, depart, emerge from an interior to an exterior.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-khurūj is the departure of a thing from its place or state; used of the soul leaving the body, and of the damned leaving the Fire.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: spatial egress. Metaphorical: "kharaja min al-amr" — to emerge from an affair, i.e., to be free of its obligation; and "akhrajahu Allāh min al-nār" — divine extraction by mercy, not by merit.
- Root: شفع (shafa'a)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To make even, pair; intercession is making one's supplication a pair with another's need.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-shafā'ah is the joining of one's intercession to another's request for aid; its reality is the elevation of the intercessor's rank and the remission of the offender's burden.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: pairing. Metaphorical: intercession before a king — the intercessor "pairs" his own honor with the petitioner's deficiency.
- Root: رحم (raḥima)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Tenderness of heart, compassion; al-Raḥmān is intensive — mercy as an essential attribute.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-raḥmah is tenderness that necessitates beneficence; when attributed to God, it is pure beneficence (tafaddul) without emotional change.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the mother's womb (raḥim) as the seat of compassion. Metaphorical: "arḥam al-rāḥimīn" — God's mercy as sheer gratuitous giving, exceeding any creaturely pity.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Restriction and Focused Predication (al-ḥaṣr wa al-taqyīd bi-innamā) — "Innamā shafā'atu Rasūlillāh…" restricts intercession to a specific class, namely those who have burdened themselves with sins, not the innocent.
3:103.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Remembrance of Death and Afterlife'

3:144.arabic: يعبد رب محمد فإنه حى لا يموت قال الله تعالى وما محمد إلا رسول قد خلت من قبله الرسل أفإن مات أو قتل أنقلبتم على أعقابكم الآية (1) فكأن الناس لم يسمعوا هذه الآية إلا يومئذ وفي رواية أن أبا بكر رضي الله تعالى عنه لما بلغه الخبر دخل بيت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وهو يصلي على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وعيناه تهملان وغصصه ترتفع كقصع الجرة وهو في ذلك جلد الفعل والمقال فأكب عليه فكشف عن وجهه وقبل جبينه وخديه ومسح وجهه وجعل يبكي ويقول بأبي أنت وأمي ونفسي وأهلي طبت حيا وميتا انقطع لموتك ما لم ينقطع لموت أحد من الأنبياء والنبوة فعظمت عن الصفة وجللت عن البكاء وخصصت حتى صرت
3:144.english: He said: "The prayer, the prayer!" (1) ʿĀʾishah (may Allah be pleased with her) said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) died between the rising of the forenoon (al-ḍuḥā) and the midpoint of the day, on Monday." (2) Fāṭimah (may Allah be pleased with her) said: "What have I suffered from Monday! By Allah, the community will never cease to be stricken through it with a tremendous calamity." Umm Kulthūm said, on the day ʿAlī (may Allah honor his face) was struck down in Kūfah, the like of what she had said: "What have I suffered from Monday! On it died the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), on it was killed ʿAlī (may Allah honor him), and on it was killed my father — so what have I suffered from Monday!"
3:144.section_title_en: The Death of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) — The Events of Monday, the Dispute over His Passing, and the Address of Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (may Allah be pleased with him)
3:144.anchors:
- Root: صلو (ṣ-l-w)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of supplication, blessing, and the act of prayer; al-salāh as the established ritual worship.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-salāh denotes invocation of mercy (al-rahmah) from Allah, and from angels and believers, supplication and seeking of forgiveness; its theological nuance here is the emphatic exhortation to preserve the prayer at the moment of death.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) usage for the ritual prayer; metaphorical (majāz) extension for blessing and mercy descending upon the Prophet (ﷺ).
- Root: موت (m-w-t)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Death as the cessation of life; the opposite of life (al-ḥayāh).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-mawt is the cessation of the rational soul's governance over the body, not its annihilation; theologically, the Prophet's death is a real tasting of death (dhawq al-mawt) yet his prophetic reality (al-nubuwwah) remains imperishable.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal for physical death; metaphorical in the sense that what is "cut off" by his death is only the worldly life, while the light of prophethood persists.
- Root: خلف (kh-l-f)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To succeed, to remain after; a successor (khalaf) and a substitute.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-khalaf denotes that which takes the place of another; in theodicy, Allah is the true Successor (al-Khalaf) from every loss — the One in Whom consolation is found for every affliction.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal for succession in time; metaphorical for Allah as the abiding Substitute after the passing of every created being.
- Sibawayh Rule: Bāb al-ḥaṣr wa al-taqyīd bi-innamā (Restriction and Focused Predication) — The construction "إنما واعده الله" restricts the promise of death to a single appointed term, negating any second death, and "إنما انقطع لموتك" restricts the severance to what pertains to worldly life alone, not to the eternal reality of prophethood.
3:144.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Remembrance of Death and Afterlife'

3:180.arabic: قال تعالى ولا يحسبن الذين يبخلون بما آتاهم الله من فضله هو خير لهم بل هو شر لهم سيطوقون ما بخلوا به يوم القيامة وقال تعالى الذين يبخلون ويأمرون الناس بالبخل ويكتمون ما آتاهم الله من فضله وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم إياكم والشح فإنه أهلك من كان قبلكم حملهم على أن سفكوا دماءهم واستحلوا محارمهم (1) وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم إياكم والشح فإنه دعا من كان قبلكم فسفكوا دماءهم ودعاهم فاستحلوا محارمهم ودعاهم فقطعوا أرحامهم (1) وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم لا يدخل الجنة بخيل ولا خب ولا خائن ولا سيء الملكة (2)
3:180.english: God the Exalted said: {«And whoever is saved from the covetousness of his own soul — those are the successful»} (al-Hashr 59:9). And He said the Exalted: {«And let not those who withhold stingily what God has given them of His bounty suppose that it is good for them. Rather, it is evil for them. They shall be collared with what they withheld on the Day of Resurrection»} (Al 'Imran 3:180). And He said the Exalted: {«Those who are stingy and command people to stinginess, and conceal what God has given them of His bounty»} (al-Nisa' 4:37).
3:180.section_title_en: The Book of the Revival of the Religious Sciences — Section 773: On the Condemnation of Stinginess (Al-Bukhl) and Covetousness (Al-Shuhh)
3:180.anchors:
- Root: بخل (B-Kh-L)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning is withholding or restraining that which one possesses from what does not rightfully permit its detention. Al-Khalil notes: "بَخِلَ بَخَلاً وبُخْلاً فهو بَخِيلٌ بَخَّالٌ مُبَخِّلٌ. والبَخْلَةُ: بُخْلُ مَرَّةٍ وَاحِدَةٍ."
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "البخل: إمساك المقتنيات عما لا يحق حبسها عنه، ويقابله الجود... والبخل ضربان: بخل بقنيات نفسه، وبخل بقنيات غيره، وهو أكثرها ذما." — Stinginess is of two kinds: withholding one's own possessions, and withholding what belongs to others (i.e., covetousness, shuhh), the latter being more blameworthy.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): "فلان لم يبخل ولم يبخل، وما كانت منه بخلة قط." Metaphorical (Majaz): "إذا السماء بخلت بالفطر" — the sky "withholding" rain is a metaphorical extension of the root.
- Root: شح (Sh-H-H)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The root denotes intense covetousness combined with avarice — a grasping desire for what others possess alongside a tight-fisted withholding of one's own.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The distinction between shuhh and bukhl: shuhh is the more severe — it is the inner disposition of craving that drives one to seize what is in others' hands and to cling to what is in one's own; bukhl is its outward manifestation in withholding.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): The rhetorical usage in the hadith "اتقوا الشح" employs the term in its comprehensive sense, encompassing both the inward vice and its outward acts.
- Root: ظلم (Z-L-M)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The root signifies placing something in other than its proper position; darkness (zulmah) is its sensory correlate.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الظلمة: عدم النور... ويعبر بها عن الجهل والشرك والفسق" — darkness is used metaphorically for ignorance, polytheism, and transgression.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "الظلم ظلمات يوم القيامة" — injustice is darknesses on the Day of Resurrection. Metaphorical: "أرض مظلومة: حفر فيها بئر" — a land "wronged" by being dug into for the first time.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The permissibility of interposing elements between a governing word and its governed prepositional phrase, as in the hadith "إياكم والشح فإنه أهلك من كان قبلكم," where the warning construction (إياكم) governs the subsequent clause with rhetorical emphasis.

3:182.arabic: يوم القيامة بإخراج رجلين من النار فيقول الله تبارك وتعالى ذلك بما قدمت أيديكما وما أنا بظلام للعبيد ويأمر بردهما إلى النار فيعدو أحدهما في سلاسله حتى يقتحمها ويتلكأ الآخر ويأمر بردهما ويسألهما عن فعلهما فيقول الذي عدا إلى النار قد حذرت من وبال المعصية فلم أكن لأتعرض لسخطك ثانية ويقول الذي تلكأ حسن ظني بك كان يشعرني أن لا تردني إليها بعد ما أخرجتني منها فيأمر بهما إلى الجنة وقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ينادي مناد من تحت العرش يوم القيامة يا أمة محمد أما ما كان لي قبلكم فقد وهبته لكم وبقيت التبعات فتواهبوها وادخلوا ال
