3:185.arabic: الله خير} وقوله {والآخرة خير وأبقى} وقوله {وما الحياة الدنيا إلا متاع الغرور} وقوله {فلا تغرنكم الحياة الدنيا} وقد أخبر رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بذلك طوائف من الكفار فقلدوه وصدقوه وآمنوا به ولم يطالبوه بالبرهان (1) حديث قول من قال له نشدتك الله أبعثك رسولا فيقول {نعم} فيصدق متفق عليه من حديث أنس في قصة ضمام ابن ثعلبة وقوله للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أرسلك للناس كلهم فقال اللهم نعم وفي آخره فقال الرجل آمنت بما جئت به وللطبراني من حديث ابن عباس في ضمام قال نشدتك به أهو أرسلك بما أتتنا كتبك وأتتنا رسلك أن نشهد أن لا إله إلا ا
3:185.english: Know that the saying of God Most High — {«fa-lā taghurrannakum al-ḥayātu al-dunyā wa-lā yaghurrannakum billāhi al-gharūr»} (So let not the life of this world deceive you, nor let the Deceiver deceive you concerning God) — and His saying — {«wa-lākinnakum fatantum anfusakum wa-tarabbastum wa-irtabtum wa-gharratkum al-amānī»} (But ye tempted your own souls, and ye waited, and ye doubted, and vain desires deceived you) — is sufficient for the blameworthiness of self-deception (al-ghurūr). And the Messenger of God, may God's peace and blessing be upon him, has said: "How excellent is the sleep of the intelligent and their breaking of the fast! How they outwit the wakefulness of the foolish and their striving! And verily a mustard-seed's weight [of faith] from a possessor of piety and certainty is better than the earth filled with the self-deceived." And the ḥadīth: "The intelligent man (al-kayyis) is he who takes account of his own soul and works for what is after death" — this ḥadīth was transmitted by al-Tirmidhī and Ibn Mājah from the ḥadīth of Shaddād ibn Aws.
3:185.section_title_en: Exposition of the Blameworthiness of Self-Deception (Al-Ghurūr), Its Reality, and Its Examples
3:185.anchors:
- Root: غرر (Gh-R-R)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The core meaning is "an apparent trace or mark of a thing" (al-athar al-ẓāhir), from which derives "the blaze of a horse" (ghurrat al-faras). To deceive (gharra) is to strike one's heedlessness (ghirrah) and attain one's sought desire from him, as if folding a garment upon its original crease (ṭawāhu ʿalā gharrihi).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Ghurrah is heedlessness in wakefulness, and ghirār is heedlessness with drowsiness." Theologically, it is the soul's repose upon a false semblance (shubhah) that pleases the caprice (hawā), rendering one oblivious to the true state of affairs—as in {«mā gharraka bi-rabbika al-karīm»} (What deceived thee concerning thy Generous Lord?).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): "A gazelle in a moonlit night is called agharr" because it ventures out thinking it is day and is devoured by beasts—heedlessness in perception. Metaphorical (majāz): "A day agharr muḥajjal" (a white-browed, white-legged day) for intense heat, transferring the blaze of a horse to the day's visible intensity.
- Root: جهل (J-H-L)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "Jahila bihi" — to be ignorant of it; "jāhala ʿalā qawmihi" — to act foolishly/insolently against one's people. The pre-Islamic era is "al-jāhiliyyah al-jahlā'" (the utterly ignorant age).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Ignorance (jahl) is of three kinds: (1) the soul's emptiness of knowledge (this is the root); (2) believing a thing contrary to what it is; (3) doing a thing contrary to what it ought to be, whether one's belief is sound or corrupt. Ghurūr is a species of the second kind—a false belief arising from a corrupt semblance.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "Kafā bil-shakki jahlā" (Sufficient is doubt as ignorance). Metaphorical: "Istajhalat al-rīḥ al-ghuṣn" (The wind made the branch sway violently) — transferred from mental foolishness to physical agitation.
- Root: حدث (Ḥ-D-TH)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "Al-ḥudūth: the coming-to-be of a thing after it was not." "Al-ḥadath: the novel event." "Ḥaddatha: to speak/communicate."
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Ḥudūth is the existence of a thing after non-existence, whether accident or substance. Iḥdāth is bringing it into existence. The iḥdāth of substances belongs to God alone." The "ḥadīth" (report/speech) is so-called for its temporal novelty.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "Nazalat bihi ḥawādith al-dahr" (The vicissitudes of time befell him). Metaphorical: "Kāna ʿUmar muḥaddathan" (Umar was one inspired with true discernment) — as if he were spoken to (ḥudditha) by what he conjectured.
- Root: دنا (D-N-W)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "Danā fa-huwa dānin" — he drew near. "Al-dunyā" (the lower world) is so named because it is nearer (danat) and precedes the Hereafter.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Al-dunūw: proximity by essence or by judgment, used of place, time, and station." The "adnā" (lower/nearer) is contrasted with the greater and with the better: {«a-tastabdilūna alladhī huwa adnā billadhī huwa khayr»} (Will ye take the lower in exchange for what is better?).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "Huwa danī' min al-adniyā'" (He is base, of the base ones) — but this is the homonym danu'a (baseness), distinct from danā (nearness). The dunyā's "nearness" is its temporal immediacy versus the Hereafter's deferral.
- Sibawayh Rule: Bab al-faṣl bayna al-jār wa-al-majrūr (Prepositional Interposition) — The particle "bi" in {«wa-lā yaghurrannakum billāhi al-gharūr»} governs the deceiver (al-gharūr) as the agent of deception, while "billāh" (concerning God) is the object of the deception. The syntactic structure permits the deceiver to be named after the prepositional phrase, indicating that the deception is *about* God's attributes (His forbearance, His respite) — a grammatical subtlety showing the ghurūr deceives *by means of* false notions of God, not that God Himself deceives.
3:185.topic: Al-Ghazali on the journey of the soul, death, and the Hereafter, from 'Condemnation of Delusion'

3:185.arabic: تعالى وإنما توفون أجوركم يوم القيامة أفترى أن من استؤجر على إصلاح أوان وشرط له أجرة عليها وكان الشارط كريما يفي بالوعد مهما وعد ولا يخلف بل يزيد فجاء الأجير وكسر الأواني وأفسد جميعها ثم جلس ينتظر الأجر ويزعم أن المستأجر كريم أفيراه العقلاء في انتظاره متمنيا مغرورا أو راجيا وهذا للجهل بالفرق بين الرجاء والغرة قيل للحسن قوم يقولون نرجو الله ويضيعون العمل فقال هيهات هيهات تلك أمانيهم يترجحون فيها من رجا شيئا طلبه ومن خاف شيئا هرب منه وقال مسلم بن يسار لقد سجدت البارحة حتى سقطت ثنيتاي فق
3:185.english: I say: God—exalted is He—loves the obedient and hates the disobedient. So just as He does not hate the obedient father because of His hatred for the disobedient son, likewise He does not love the disobedient son because of His love for the obedient father. And if love were to flow from the father to the son, then hatred would likewise be bound to flow. Rather, the truth is: {«ولا تزر وازرة وزر أخرى»} — "And no bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another" {Quran 6:164, 17:15, 35:18, 39:7, 53:38}. And whoever supposes that he will be saved by his father's piety is like one who supposes he will be satiated by his father's eating, quenched by his father's drinking, become a scholar by his father's learning, and reach the Ka'bah and see it by his father's walking.
3:185.section_title_en: The Reality of Hope (Al-Rajā') and the Futility of Reliance on Another's Piety
3:185.anchors:
- Root: و ل د (walada)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Physical begetting and offspring; the father's generative act.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الولد: المولود" — offspring as a created entity; here used metaphorically for spiritual causation.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical birth. Metaphorical: "تولدت العصبية" — something generated or produced from another; Ghazali exploits this to refute the notion that a father's obedience "generates" salvation for the son.
- Root: ر ج و (rajā)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Expectation, hope, longing for a favorable outcome.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Hope tied to legitimate means; not mere wishful thinking (tamannī).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: awaiting rain. Metaphorical: "رجوت فلانا" — to expect from someone; Ghazali contrasts true hope (with action) vs. delusion (ghurūr).
- Root: غ ر ر (gharara)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Deception, heedlessness, being lured by a false appearance.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The state of one who is duped by Satan's plausible speech.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: a risky venture. Metaphorical: "اغتر بفلان" — to be deceived by outward charm while the inner reality is corrupt.
- Root: ك ي س (kays)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Intelligence, shrewdness, prudence.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The wise man who disciplines his soul and acts for the afterlife.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: alertness. Metaphorical: "الكيس من دان نفسه" — the prudent one who holds his soul to account; antonym of "الأحمق" (the fool).
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — "إنما يوفى الصابرون أجرهم بغير حساب" style; Ghazali uses "إنما" to restrict reward to personal action, and "ليس للإنسان إلا ما سعى" as a restrictive negative clause (nafy + illā) to deny any transfer of merit.
3:185.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'Condemnation of Delusion'

3:185.arabic: وقال عليه السلام من سره أن يزحزح عن النار ويدخل الجنة فلتأته منيته وهو يشهد أن لا إله إلا الله وأن محمدا رسول الله وليؤت إلى الناس ما يحب أن يؤتى إليه (6) وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم يا أبا الدرداء أحسن مجاورة من جاورك تكن مؤمنا وأحب للناس ما تحب لنفسك تكن مسلما (7) قال الحسن أوحى الله تعالى إلى آدم صلى الله عليه وسلم بأربع خصال وقال فيهن جماع الأمر لك ولولدك واحدة لي وواحدة لك وواحدة بيني وبينك وواحدة بينك وبين الخلق فأما التي لي تعبدني ولا تشرك بي شيئا وأما التي لك فعملك أجزيك به أفقر ما
3:185.english: **First**: That you greet him with peace (*salām*) when you meet him, and respond to his invitation when he invites you, and say "may Allah have mercy on you" (*tashmīt*) when he sneezes, and visit him when he is ill, and attend his funeral procession when he dies, and fulfill his oath when he swears by you, and give him sincere counsel when he seeks your advice, and protect him in his absence when he is away from you, and love for him what you love for yourself, and dislike for him what you dislike for yourself. (1)
3:185.section_title_en: The Rights of Brotherhood — Section 433: The Duties of a Muslim Toward His Fellow Muslims
3:185.anchors:
- Root: سلم (s-l-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of safety, security, freedom from harm; the root from which *islām* (submission/surrender) and *salām* (peace) derive
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): *Salām* as the theological state of being secure from harm — both giving and receiving safety; *islām* as the total surrender of the heart to Allah
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (*ḥaqīqah*): physical safety from tongue and hand; Metaphorical (*majāz*): the comprehensive spiritual safety that defines true Muslim brotherhood
- Root: عون (ʿ-w-n)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Assistance, aid, helping another in need
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Mutual assistance as a divine ordinance among believers
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical aid; Metaphorical: intercession (*shafāʿah*) and advocacy on behalf of others
- Root: ستر (s-t-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Covering, concealing, veiling; protection from exposure
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): *Sitr* as the divine attribute of concealment — Allah's covering of sins in this world and the next
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: covering a physical defect; Metaphorical: concealing another's faults and sins — a cardinal virtue of brotherhood
- Root: عذر (ʿ-dh-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Excuse, pardon, acceptance of apology
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): *ʿAfw* (pardon) as the higher station of forgiveness that elevates the forgiver
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: releasing from obligation; Metaphorical: the noble trait of overlooking others' offenses
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد (Restriction & Focused Predication) — The repeated use of restrictive constructions (e.g., "المسلم من سلم المسلمون") establishes definitional boundaries through predicate restriction, indicating that the *ḥaqīqah* of faith is manifested through specific observable actions.

##
3:185.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'Duties of Brotherhood'

3:185.arabic: وقال بعض الصوفية كنت أقرأ ليلة هذه الآية {كل نفس ذائقة الموت} فجعلت أرددها فإذا هاتف يهتف بي كم تردد هذه الآية فقد قتلت أربعة من الجن ما رفعوا رءوسهم إلى السماء منذ خلقوا وقال أبو علي المغازلي للشبلي ربما تطرق سمعي آية من كتاب الله تعالى فتجذبني إلى الإعراض عن الدنيا ثم أرجع إلى أحوالي وإلى الناس فلا أبقى على ذلك فقال ما طرق سمعك من القرآن فاجتذبك به إليه فذلك عطف منه عليك ولطف منه بك وإذا ردك إلى نفسك فهو شفقة منه عليك فإنه لا يصلح لك إلا التبري من الحول والقوة في التوجه إليه وسمع رجل من أه
3:185.english: Some of the Sufis said: "One night I was reciting this verse: {كُلُّ نَفْسٍ ذَائِقَةُ الْمَوْتِ} «Every soul shall taste death» [Q. 3:185]. I kept repeating it, and lo, a caller cried out to me: 'How long will you repeat this verse? You have killed four of the jinn who have not raised their heads to the sky since they were created.'"
3:185.section_title_en: On the Ecstatic States (Wajd) Produced by Qur'anic Recitation and the Superiority of Song (Ghinā') in Stirring the Heart
3:185.anchors:
- Root: وجد (w-j-d)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of finding, attaining, and also denoting the emotional state of ecstasy or rapture that "finds" the heart.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In the theological context, 'wajd' is the state of spiritual finding—a direct, overwhelming apprehension of divine realities that bypasses discursive reasoning.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah) usage denotes "finding" a lost object; metaphorical (Majaz) usage denotes the heart "finding" its spiritual state, leading to agitation and ecstasy.
- Root: سمع (s-m-')
  * Lisan / Ayn: The faculty of hearing; also the ear itself.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Hearing can be literal (perception of sound) or figurative (understanding, obedience, acceptance). The heart's "hearing" is a deeper comprehension.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "سمعته" (I heard him). Metaphorical: "سمع الله لمن حمده" (God answers/he accepts the one who praises Him), indicating a responsive, transformative hearing.
- Root: موت (m-w-t)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Death; the opposite of life.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Death is the cessation of the soul's governance over the body, a separation. In the spiritual context, it can be a metaphorical death to worldly desires.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical death. Metaphorical: "أحيا الله البلد الميت" (God revives the dead land), indicating spiritual revival or the death of the ego.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — Used to emphasize that the stirring of the heart is exclusively through what is appropriate to its state, as in the phrase "إنما المحرك لما في القلب ما يناسبه" (The only thing that moves what is in the heart is that which is suitable to it).
3:185.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Remembrance of Death and Afterlife'

4:18.arabic: وذلك سوء الخاتمة ولمثل هذا يقال {وليست التوبة للذين يعملون السيئات حتى إذا حضر أحدهم الموت قال إني تبت الآن} وقوله {إنما التوبة على الله للذين يعملون السوء بجهالة ثم يتوبون من قريب} ومعناه عن قرب عهد بالخطيئة بأن يتندم عليها ويمحو أثرها بحسنة يردفها بها قبل أن يتراكم الرين على القلب فلا يقبل المحو ولذلك قال صلى الله عليه وسلم أتبع السيئة الحسنة تمحها ولذلك قال لقمان لابنه يا بني لا تؤخر التوبة فإن الموت يأتي بغتة ومن ترك المبادرة إلى التوبة بالتسويف كان بين خطرين عظيمين {أحدهما} أن تتراكم الظلمة على قلبه من المعاصي حتى يصير رينا وطبعا فلا يقبل المحو الثاني
4:18.english: I say: Every human being is never free from disobedience of the bodily members (jawāriḥ), for even the prophets were not free from it — as has come down in the Qurʾān and the reports concerning the sins of the prophets, their repentance, and their weeping over their misdeeds. And if one is free, in some states, from disobedience of the members, he is not free from the heart's inclination (hamm) toward sins. And if he is free, in some states, from the inclination, he is not free from the whispering of Satan (waswās al-shayṭān) by way of importing scattered thoughts that divert from the remembrance of God. And if he is free from that, he is not free from heedlessness (ghaflah) and deficiency in knowledge of God, His attributes, and His acts. All of that is deficiency (nuqṣān), and it has causes; and abandoning its causes by occupying oneself with their opposites is a reversion from one path to its contrary. The meaning of "repentance" (tawbah) is "returning" (rujūʿ), and it is inconceivable that a human being should be entirely free of this deficiency — rather, people differ only in degrees. As for the principle itself, it is unavoidable. For this reason, he (peace be upon him) said: "Truly, a veil is cast over my heart, so that I seek forgiveness from God seventy times a day and night" (1) — the hadith. And for this reason, God (exalted be He) honored him by saying: {«لِيَغْفِرَ لَكَ اللَّهُ مَا تَقَدَّمَ مِنْ ذَنْبِكَ وَمَا تَأَخَّرَ»} [That God may forgive you what has passed of your sin and what remains]. And if this was his state, how then is the state of anyone else?
4:18.section_title_en: On the Universality of Repentance (Tawbah) and Its Obligation in Every Breath
4:18.anchors:
- Root: توب (T-W-B)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of "returning" (rujūʿ) — turning back from a path to its opposite; the root denotes the act of revisiting and reversing a prior state.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Tawbah is "abandoning the sin in the most excellent manner" — the most complete form of excuse; in sacred law (sharʿ), it is abandoning the sin due to its ugliness, regretting what has passed, resolving not to return, and rectifying what can be rectified of past deeds through renewed acts.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): "He repented to God from his sin" (tāba al-ʿabdu ilā Allāhi min dhanbihi). Metaphorical (majāz): The extension of "repentance" to inner purification of the heart from accumulated rust (rayn), as the root's sense of "returning" is applied to the soul's reversion from negligence to vigilance.
- Root: قلب (Q-L-B)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The heart as the organ of turning and overturning (taqlīb) — its state fluctuates between illumination and darkness, purity and rust.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Turning a thing" is directing it from one face to another; the heart (qalb) is so named for its constant overturning between states — a key metaphysical anchor for Ghazali's doctrine of the heart's susceptibility to stains (akdār) and polish (ṣaqal).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "He turned the thing over" (qalaba al-shayʾ). Metaphorical: "The heart is rusted" (qalb wajīb) — the inner organ's receptivity to impressions, whether dark (from sins) or luminous (from obedience).
- Root: وجب (W-J-B)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Obligation as fixed establishment (thubūt); what is due and settled upon a person.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Wājib has two senses: (1) that whose non-existence entails a contradiction (metaphysical necessity), and (2) that whose neglect merits blame — subdivided into what reason deems obligatory (e.g., knowing divine unity) and what the Law deems obligatory (e.g., acts of worship). Ghazali here exploits this dual sense to distinguish legal obligation (fatwā) from the higher obligation of the path (ṭarīq).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "It became incumbent upon him" (wajaba ʿalayhi). Metaphorical: The extension to "the heart's palpitation" (wajīb) — the inner agitation of one who realizes the urgency of repentance before death.
- Sibawayh Rule: Restriction and Focused Predication (al-ḥaṣr wa al-taqyīd bi-innamā) — governing the Quranic citations {«إِنَّمَا التَّوْبَةُ عَلَى اللَّهِ»} and {«وَلَيْسَتِ التَّوْبَةُ لِلَّذِينَ»}, where innamā restricts the predicate to a specific subject, delimiting the scope of accepted repentance to those who turn before death's arrival and before the rust hardens into a seal.
4:18.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Remembrance of Death and Afterlife'

4:40.arabic: ما بأنفسهم إن الله لا يظلم مثقال ذرة وإن تك حسنة يضاعفها وإن كان مثقال حبة من خردل أتينا بها وكفى بنا حاسبين فمن كان حبه في الدنيا رجاءه لنعيم الجنة والحور العين والقصور مكن من الجنة ليتبوأ منها حيث يشاء فيلعب مع الولدان ويتمتع بالنسوان فهناك تنتهي لذته في الآخرة لأنه إنما يعطى كل إنسان في المحبة ما تشتهيه نفسه وتلذ عينه ومن كان مقصده رب الدار ومالك الملك ولم يغلب عليه إلا حبه بالإخلاص والصدق أنزل في مقعد
4:40.english:
...twenty years.
And al-Junayd said: "The mark of the lover is the constancy of vigor and cheerfulness with a passion that wearies his body but does not weary his heart."
And some of them said: "Labor borne out of love — languor does not enter into it."
And one of the scholars said: "By God, no lover of God is ever fully quenched by His obedience, even if he were to attain to the most immense of means."
All of this and its like is found in observable experience, for the passionate lover does not find burdensome the pursuit of his beloved's desire, and he savors with his heart the service of the beloved even if it is arduous upon his body. And whenever his body falls short, the dearest of things to him is that his capacity should return to him and that incapacity should depart from him, so that he may occupy himself with it. Such, likewise, is the love of God the Exalted — for every love that becomes dominant inevitably subdues whatever is beneath it. So whoever's beloved is dearer to him than his sloth abandons sloth in serving him; and if the beloved is dearer to him than his wealth, he spends his wealth in his love.
And it was said to one of the lovers — who had expended his very self and his wealth until nothing remained to him — "What was the cause of your state in love?" He said: "One day I heard a lover who had secluded himself with his beloved, saying: 'By God, I love you with my whole heart, while you turn away from me with your whole face.' The beloved said to him: 'If you truly love me, what will you spend upon me?' He said: 'O my master, I put you in possession of all that I own, and then I spend upon you my very spirit until it is destroyed.'" So I said: "This is a creature loving a creature, and a slave loving a slave — how then with slaves loving the Worshipped One?" All of this is by His cause.
And among them is that he be compassionate toward all of God's servants, merciful to them, and severe against all of God's enemies — and against everyone who commits something of what God dislikes — as God the Exalted said: {«أشداء على الكفار رحماء بينهم»} "Harsh against the disbelievers, merciful among themselves." No reproach of any reproacher seizes him, and no diverting force turns him from wrath for God's sake. With this God described His friends, saying: "Those who are enamored with My love as a child is enamored with a thing, and who take refuge in My remembrance as the eagle takes refuge in its nest, and who rage for the sake of My sanctities as the leopard rages when provoked — for then he cares not whether the people are few or many."
So consider this example: the child, when enamored with a thing, does not part from it at all; if it is taken from him, he has no occupation but weeping and crying out until it is returned to him. If he sleeps, he takes it with him into his clothes; when he awakens, he returns and clings to it. Whenever he is parted from it, he weeps; whenever he finds it, he laughs. Whoever contends with him over it, he hates; whoever gives it to him, he loves. As for the leopard, he does not master himself at the moment of rage, until he reaches such a pitch of fury that he destroys himself. These, then, are the marks of love. Whoever's marks are perfected in him, his love is perfected and his affection is purified — so in the Hereafter his drink is clear and his draught is sweet.
But whoever's love is mingled with the love of other than God, he delights in the Hereafter in proportion to his love, for his drink is mingled with a measure of the drink of the Near Ones (al-muqarrabūn), as God the Exalted said concerning the righteous (al-abrār): {«إن الأبرار لفي نعيم»} "Verily the righteous are in bliss," {ثم قال} then He said: {«يسقون من رحيق مختوم * ختامه مسك وفي ذلك فليتنافس المتنافسون * ومزاجه من تسنيم * عينا يشرب بها المقربون»} "They are given to drink of sealed nectar, whose seal is musk — and in that let the competitors compete — and its mixture is of tasnīm, a spring from which the Near Ones drink." So when the drink of the righteous is sweetened by the admixture of the pure drink which belongs to the Near Ones...
And "drink" is an expression for the totality of the bliss of the Gardens, just as the Book expressed by it all deeds, for He said: {«إن كتاب الأبرار لفي عليين»} "Verily the book of the righteous is in 'Illiyyūn," {ثم قال} then He said: {«يشهده المقربون»} "The Near Ones bear witness to it." So it was a sign of the loftiness of their book that it ascended to where the Near Ones bear witness to it. And just as the righteous find increase in their state and their knowledge by their proximity to the Near Ones and their beholding of them, so likewise is their state in the Hereafter — {«ما خلقكم ولا بعثكم إلا كنفس واحدة»} "Your creation and your resurrection are but as a single soul," just as He said — as we began the first creation, We shall repeat it — and as the Exalted said: {«جزاء وفاقا»} "A recompense fully matching" — that is, the recompense matched their deeds. So the pure was met with the unmixed of the drink, and the mingled was met with the mingled.
And the admixture of every drink is in proportion to what preceded of admixture in his love and his deeds. For {«من يعمل مثقال ذرة خيرا يره * ومن يعمل مثقال ذرة شرا يره»} "Whoever does an atom's weight of good shall see it, and whoever does an atom's weight of evil shall see it." And {«إن الله لا يغير ما بقوم حتى يغيروا ما بأنفسهم * إن الله لا يظلم مثقال ذرة وإن تك حسنة يضاعفها وإن كان مثقال حبة من خردل أتينا بها وكفى بنا حاسبين»} "Verily God does not change what is in a people until they change what is in themselves. Verily God does not wrong an atom's weight; and if it be a good deed, He multiplies it, and if it be a grain of mustard-seed, We bring it — and sufficient are We as reckoners."
So whoever's love in this world was his hope for the bliss of the Garden, the wide-eyed houris, and the palaces — he is granted the Garden to settle therein wherever he wishes, to sport with the immortal youths and take pleasure with the women. There his delight in the Hereafter reaches its end, because every man is given in love only what his soul desires and his eye delights in.
But whoever's aim was the Lord of the Abode and the Owner of the Kingdom, and nothing overcame him save His love with sincerity and truthfulness — he is lodged in the seat...
4:40.section_title_en: The Marks of True Love and the Degrees of the Hereafter
4:40.anchors:
- Root: نشط (n-sh-ṭ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of vitality, energy, and alacrity in action.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Activity of the soul (nafs) in pursuing what it loves, unflagging in its ardor.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: bodily vigor; Metaphorical: the heart's persistent zeal that overrides physical exhaustion.
- Root: شرب (sh-r-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Drinking; the act of imbibing liquids.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In Quranic usage, a metaphor (majaz) for the soul's reception of spiritual bliss and states.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical quenching; Metaphorical: the tasting of paradisiacal delight, graded by purity (safā') versus admixture (shawb).
- Root: صفو (ṣ-f-w)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Purity, clarity, and freedom from turbidity or mixture.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The unalloyed state of sincere love (mahabbah) and its corresponding reward.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: clear liquid; Metaphorical: the soul's exclusive devotion to God, yielding unmixed bliss.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — Used to delimit the final reward strictly by the object and purity of one's love, as in "إنما يعطى كل إنسان في المحبة ما تشتهيه نفسه."
4:40.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Love, Longing, Intimacy and Contentment'

4:40.arabic: قوله تعالى إن الله لا يظلم مثقال ذرة وكل ذلك صحيح فليس للإنسان إلا ما سعى وسعيه هو الذي يرى وكل نفس بما كسبت رهينه فلما زاغوا أزاغ الله قلوبهم ولما غيروا ما بانفسهم غير الله ما بهم تحقيقا لقوله تعالى إن الله لا يغير ما بقوم حتى يغيروا ما بأنفسهم وهذا كله قد انكشف لأرباب القلوب انكشافا اوضح من المشاهدة بالبصر إذ للبصر يمكن الغلط فيه إذ قد يرى البعيد قريبا والكبير صغيرا ومشاهدة القلب لا يمكن الغلط فيها وإنما الشأن في انفتاح بصيرة القلب وإلا فما يرى بها بعد الانفتاح فلا يتصور فيه الكذ
4:40.english: The fire of Hell is the coldest of fires [in comparison to the fire of separation]. And you should not deny this in the world of the Hereafter, for it has a witnessed parallel in the world of this world. Indeed, one has been seen who was overcome by ecstasy (wajd) and walked upon fire and upon the roots of cane, his feet being cut, yet he did not feel it, due to the extreme dominance of what was in his heart. And you see the angry man, when anger overcomes him in battle, receiving wounds and not feeling them at that moment, because anger is a fire in the heart. The Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, said: {«الغضب قطعة من النار»} "Anger is a piece of fire." The burning of the heart (iḥtirāq al-fu'ād) is more severe than the burning of bodies, and the more severe annuls the sensation of the weaker, as you observe. For destruction from fire and the sword is only inasmuch as they separate between two parts that are linked one to the other by the bond of composition (ta'līf) possible in bodies. So that which separates between the heart and its Beloved, to which it is linked by a bond of composition far more firm than the composition of bodies, is more intensely painful—if you are among the people of insight (abṣār) and the people of hearts. And it is not far-fetched that he who has no heart should not perceive the severity of this pain and should deem it trivial in comparison to bodily pain. For a boy, if he were given the choice between the pain of being deprived of a ball and a polo-stick, and the pain of being deprived of the rank of a Sultan, he would not feel the pain of deprivation from the Sultan's rank at all, nor would he count that as a pain. And the enemy in the field with the polo-stick is more beloved to him than a thousand thrones of the Sultan with sitting upon them. Nay, even one overcome by the lust of the belly, if given the choice between porridge (harīsah) and sweets (ḥalwā) and between a beautiful deed by which he conquers enemies and delights friends, he would prefer the porridge and sweets. All of this is due to the absence of the meaning (maʿnā) by whose existence rank becomes beloved, and the presence of the meaning by whose existence food becomes delicious. This is for one whom the attributes of beasts and predators have enslaved, and in whom the attributes of the angels have not appeared—those attributes which are not suited by, nor delight in, anything but proximity to the Lord of the Worlds, and which are pained only by distance and the veil (ḥijāb). And just as taste is only in the tongue and hearing only in the ears, so this attribute is only in the heart. So he who has no heart has no such sense, like he who has no hearing or sight has no pleasure in melodies or the beauty of forms and colors. And not every human has a heart; were it so, the saying of God, Most High, would not be sound: {«إن في ذلك لذكرى لمن كان له قلب»} "Indeed in that is a reminder for whoever has a heart" (Q. 50:37). Thus He made the one who does not heed the Quran devoid of a heart. And by "heart" I do not mean this [organ] which the ribs of the chest encompass. Rather, I mean the secret (sirr) which is of the world of the Command (ʿālam al-amr). The flesh which is of the world of Creation (ʿālam al-khalq) is its Throne (ʿarsh), the chest is its Footstool (kursī), and the rest of the limbs are its domain and kingdom. And to God belongs the Creation and the Command altogether. But that secret, concerning which God, Most High, said: {«قل الروح من أمر ربي»} "Say: The Spirit is of the Command of my Lord" (Q. 17:85), is the commander and the king, because between the world of the Command and the world of Creation there is an ordering, and the world of the Command is commander over the world of Creation. It is the subtle divine reality (al-laṭīfah) which, when it is sound, the rest of the body is sound for its sake. Whoever knows it has known his own self, and whoever knows his own self has known his Lord. At that point, the servant smells the beginnings of the fragrance of the meaning folded under his saying, peace and blessings be upon him: {«إن الله خلق آدم على صورته»} "God created Adam upon His image." He looks with the eye of mercy upon those who adhere to its literal wording and upon those who are obstinate in the path of its interpretation (ta'wīl). And even though His mercy for those adhering to the letter is greater than His mercy for the obstinate interpreters, because mercy is proportional to the affliction, and the affliction of those [literalists] is greater—even if they share in the affliction of being deprived of the reality of the matter—for the Reality (al-ḥaqīqah) is the bounty of God which He gives to whom He wills, and God is the Possessor of Great Bounty. And His Wisdom is singled out for whom He wills: {«ومن يؤت الحكمة فقد أوتي خيرا كثيرا»} "And whoever is given wisdom has been given much good" (Q. 2:269). Let us return to the purpose, for we have drawn out the length and lengthened the breath in a matter that is higher than the sciences of transactions (muʿāmalāt) which we intend in this book. It has become clear that the rank of destruction is only for the ignorant deniers. And the testimony of that from the Book of God and the Sunnah of His Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, is beyond enumeration, so we have not cited it.
4:40.section_title_en: The Ranks of the Hereafter: On the Distribution of Degrees and the States of the Saved, the Punished, and the Victorious
4:40.anchors:
- Root: ح ر ق (ḥ-r-q)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of burning, scorching, and the fire's consumption of its fuel.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The fire of the Hereafter (Nār) is a created reality, but its perception is tied to the spiritual state of the perceiver.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah) for physical burning; metaphorical (Majaz) for the burning of the heart (iḥtirāq al-fu'ād) by overwhelming love or anger.
- Root: ق ل ب (q-l-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To turn, overturn, or transform a thing from one state to another.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The heart (Qalb) is the seat of perception and understanding, distinct from the physical organ.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal for the physical heart; metaphorical for the spiritual subtlety (Laṭīfah) that is the locus of divine knowledge and love.
- Root: ع ل م (ʿ-l-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To know, to perceive a thing by its true nature.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Knowledge (ʿIlm) is the apprehension of a thing's reality, which is the basis for distinguishing the ranks of the believers.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal for acquired knowledge; metaphorical for the "unveiling" (Kashf) knowledge granted to the knowers (ʿĀrifūn).
- Sibawayh Rule: Restriction and Specification (Bāb al-Ḥaṣr wa al-Taqyīd bi-innamā) — Used to distinguish the specific referents of terms like "heart" (Qalb) and "faith" (Īmān), ensuring the precise meaning is not conflated with common usage.
4:40.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Remembrance of Death and Afterlife'

4:40.arabic: فتح الباب والله لا يضيع أجر المحسنين وإن تك حسنة يضاعفها ويؤت من لدنه أجرا عظيما المقام الثاني في دفع العارض منه في أثناء العبادة وذلك لا بد من تعلمه أيضا فإن من جاهد نفسه وقلع مغارس الرياء من قلبه بالقناعة وقطع الطمع وإسقاط نفسه من أعين المخلوقين واستحقار مدح المخلوقين وذمهم فالشيطان لا يتركه في أثناء العبادات بل يعارضه بخطرات الرياء ولا تنقطع عنه نزعاته وهوى النفس وميلها لا ينمحي بالكلية فلا بد وأن يتشمر لدفع ما يعرض من خاطر الرياء وخواطر الرياء ثلاثة قد تخطر دفعة واحدة كالخاطر الواحد وقد تترادف على التدريج فالأول العلم باطلاع الخ
4:40.english: So when the harm and injury of these causes is firmly settled in his heart, his desire [for them] slackens, and his heart turns toward God. For the intelligent person does not covet that whose harm is abundant and whose benefit is scant. It suffices him that if people knew what is in his inner self—the intent of ostentation (riyā') and the display of sincerity—they would abhor him. And God will surely expose his secret until He makes him odious to the people and makes them know that he is a show-off, abhorrent to God. Had he been sincere to God, God would have unveiled his sincerity to them, made him beloved to them, subjected them to him, and loosened their tongues in praise and commendation of him—even though there is no perfection in their praise, nor deficiency in their blame. As the poet of Banī Tamīm said: "My praise is an adornment, and my blame is a disgrace." The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said to him: "You have lied—that belongs to God, there is no deity but Him." // [Hadith: A poet of Banī Tamīm said, "My praise is an adornment, and my blame is a disgrace." He (the Prophet) said: "You have lied—that belongs to God." Ahmad narrated it from the hadith of al-Aqra' ibn Ḥābis—who was the speaker of that verse, excluding the phrase "You have lied"—and its narrators are trustworthy, except that I do not know of Abū Salamah ibn 'Abd al-Raḥmān having heard [directly] from al-Aqra'. Al-Tirmidhī narrated it from the hadith of al-Barā' and deemed it sound (ḥasan), with the wording: "A man said, 'Indeed, my praise...'"]
4:40.section_title_en: The Revival of the Religious Sciences — Section 827: The Second Station: Repelling the Accidental Promptings of Ostentation During Worship
4:40.anchors:
- Root: كذب (kadhaba)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: falsehood, lying, saying what is contrary to reality; also used for "to declare someone a liar."
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In theological context, kadhb is the antithesis of sidq (truthfulness); it is a moral and epistemic vice, often linked to hypocrisy (nifāq) and false claims.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (haqīqah): to report what did not occur. Metaphorical (majāz): attributing to God what is unworthy of Him, as in the Prophet's rebuke of the poet's self-praise.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Predicate Emphasis (Bāb al-Tawkīd) — The Prophet's reply "كَذَبْتَ" (You have lied) functions as an emphatic categorical refutation, structured as a nominal sentence with implied subject, establishing a permanent verdict rather than a transient rebuke.
4:40.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Condemnation of Status and Ostentation'

4:40.arabic: به فكان أبو سعيد يقول إن لم تصدقوني بهذا الحديث فاقرءوا إن شئتم إن الله لا يظلم مثقال ذرة وإن تك حسنة يضاعفها ويؤت من لدنه أجرا عظيما قال فيقول الله تعالى شفعت الملائكة وشفع النبيون وشفع المؤمنون ولم يبق إلا أرحم الراحمين فيقبض قبضة فيخرج منها قوما لم يعملوا خيرا قط قد عادوا حمما فيلقيهم في نهر في أفواه الجنة يقال له نهر الحياة فيخرجون منها كما تخرج الحبة في حميل السيل ألا ترونها تكون مما يلي الحجر والشجر ما يكون إلى الشمس أصفر وأخضر وما يكون منها إلى الظل أبيض قالوا يا رسول الله كأنك كنت ترعى بالبادية قال فيخرجون كاللؤلؤ في رقابهم الخواتيم يعرفهم أهل الجنة يقولون هؤلاء عتقاء الر
4:40.english: On that Day, a card will be brought forth bearing the testimony: "I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, and I bear witness that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah." He will say: "O Lord, what is this card alongside these records?" He will reply: "Indeed, you shall not be wronged." Then the records will be placed on one pan of the scale, and the card on the other. The records will prove light, and the card will prove heavy—for nothing weighs heavier than the Name of Allah. {«لا يثقل مع اسم الله شيء»} (Nothing weighs heavier alongside the Name of Allah.)
4:40.section_title_en: On the Vastness of Divine Mercy and the Intercession of the Angels, Prophets, and Believers
4:40.anchors:
- Root: وزن (w-z-n)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning is weighing, measuring, and balancing; al-wazn denotes the act of determining weight and, by extension, the scales of justice.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In theological context, al-mīzān (the Balance) on the Day of Judgment is a divine instrument of perfect equity; its "weighing" is not corporeal but a manifestation of absolute justice wherein no deed, even of atom-weight (mithqāl dharratin), is overlooked.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (haqīqah) usage refers to physical scales; metaphorical (majāz) usage extends to the moral and eschatological weighing of deeds, where the "card" (biṭāqah) of shahādah outweighs accumulated records—a rhetorical hyperbole of divine grace.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Conditional Clauses with Repeated Protasis (Bāb al-sharṭ wa-l-jawāb) — The recurring structure "fa-man wajadtum fī qalbihi... fa-akhrijūhu" employs iterative conditionals to emphasize progressive divine mercy, each protasis narrowing the measure of faith required for salvation.
4:40.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'Remembrance of Death and Afterlife'

4:56.arabic: مرات فتجدد جلودههم ولحومهم قال الحسن في قوله تعالى كلما نضجت جلودهم بدلناهم جلودا غيرها قال تأكلهم النار كل يوم سبعين ألف مرة كلما أكلتهم قيل لهم عودوا فيعودون كما كانوا ثم تفكر الآن في بكاء أهل النار وشهيقهم ودعاتهم بالويل والثبور فإن ذلك يسلط عليهم في أول إلقائهم في النار قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يؤتى بجهنم يومئذ لها سبعون ألف زمام مع كل زمام سبعون ألف ملك (7) وقال أنس قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يرسل على أهل النار البكاء فيبكون حتى تنقطع الدموع ثم يبكون الدم حتى يرى في وجوههم كهيئة الأخدود لو أرسلت فيها السفن ل
4:56.english: At that point they despair of every good, and at that point they take to sighing, regret, and wailing. Abu Umamah said: The Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, said concerning His words, "And he is given to drink of festering water, which he sips but can hardly swallow" {«وَيُسْقَىٰ مِن مَّاءٍ صَدِيدٍ يَتَجَرَّعُهُ وَلَا يَكَادُ يُسِيغُهُ»}: "It is brought near to him, and he loathes it. When it is drawn close to him, it scorches his face, and the skin of his scalp falls off. When he drinks it, it severs his intestines until it exits from his anus." God Almighty says: {«وَسُقُوا مَاءً حَمِيمًا فَقَطَّعَ أَمْعَاءَهُمْ»} "And they are given to drink boiling water, and it severs their intestines." And He says: {«وَإِن يَسْتَغِيثُوا يُغَاثُوا بِمَاءٍ كَالْمُهْلِ يَشْوِي الْوُجُوهَ»} "And if they cry for relief, they are relieved with water like molten brass, which scalds the faces." So this is their food and drink in their hunger and thirst.
4:56.section_title_en: The Torments of the Fire: Serpents, Scorpions, and the Anguish of the Damned
4:56.anchors:
- Root: حس (ḥ-s-s) — [AVOIDED per instruction]
- Root: نار (n-r) — Fire
  * Lisan al-Arab: "النار: معروفة، وهي نار جهنم، ذات لفح وحرّ."
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "النار: قد تطلق على نار الدنيا ونار الآخرة، وهي التي أعدها الله للكافرين، وفيها من أصناف العذاب ما لا يعلمه إلا الله."
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "نار: حقيقة في النار المحرقة، ومجاز في نار الحرب والحرب."
- Root: حي (ḥ-y) — Serpent
  * Lisan al-Arab: "الحية: من الهوام، وتجمع على حيات، وأعظمها ما كان كأعناق البخت."
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الحية: دابة مؤذية، وفي الآخرة تكون أعظم وأشد إيلامًا."
- Root: عقر (ʿ-q-r) — Scorpion
  * Lisan al-Arab: "العقرب: دويبة مؤذية تلدغ، وفي النار تكون كالبغال."
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — Used to specify that serpents and scorpions are only empowered over those who were dominated by miserliness and evil character in the world.
4:56.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Remembrance of Death and Afterlife'

4:74.arabic: مائة فارس كلهم يقاتل في سبيل الله (1) وإنما ذكر السقط تنبيها بالأدنى على الأعلى وإلا فالثواب على قدر محل الولد من القلب وقال زيد بن أسلم توفي ابن لداود عليك السلام فحزن عليه حزنا شديدا فقيل له ما كان عدله عندك قال ملء الأرض ذهبا قيل له فإن لك من الأجر في الآخرة مثل ذلك وقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لا يموت لأحد من المسلمين ثلاثة من الولد فيحتسبهم إلا كانوا له جنة من النار فقالت امرأة عند رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أو اثنان قال أو اثنان (2) وليخلص الوالد الدعاء لولد
4:74.english: And thus is death: its meaning is precedence to the homeland, until the one delayed catches up. And when one holds this conviction, his agitation and sorrow diminish—especially since there has come down regarding the death of a child such reward as consoles every afflicted one. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: "That I should be presented with a stillborn child is dearer to me than that I should leave behind a hundred horsemen, all of them fighting in the path of God" {«لأن أقدم سقطا أحب إلي من أن أخلف مائة فارس كلهم يقاتل في سبيل الله»}. He only mentioned the stillborn as an intimation from the lesser to the greater—for otherwise, the reward is according to the station of the child in the heart.
4:74.section_title_en: Exposition of Their Sayings at the Death of a Child
4:74.anchors:
- Root: ولد (w-l-d)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Offspring, child—applies to singular, plural, young, and old alike; also used for an adopted child.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Walad denotes the born one; in theological usage, it carries the sense of progeny as a trust and trial from God, with reward proportioned to the child's station in the parent's heart.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (haqiqah) for biological birth and kinship; metaphorical (majaz) for "newly generated" speech or emergent states—here, the literal sense governs the parent-child relation.
- Root: موت (m-w-t)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Death as the cessation of life; mawt is the common term for dying, whether of humans or beasts.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Death is departure from this abode to the next; in Kalam, it is an accident (ʿaraḍ) terminating the soul's tenure in the body, not annihilation.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal for physical death; metaphorical for "dead land" revived by rain—here, the literal sense of death as journey's end is extended by the author's simile of travel.
- Root: لهم (l-h-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Root meaning to swallow or devour; lahma is a morsel.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Ilham is God's casting of a meaning into the heart (al-rawʿ)—distinct from human instruction; relevant to the parent's inspired resignation and supplication.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal for physical swallowing; metaphorical for the heart's receptivity to divine inspiration—here, the parent's heart is opened to patience through ilham.
- Sibawayh Rule: Restriction and Focused Predication (al-ḥaṣr wa al-taqyīd bi-innamā) — governing the exclusive phrasing in "إنما ذكر السقط تنبيها بالأدنى على الأعلى" (he only mentioned the stillborn as an intimation from the lesser to the greater), where innamā restricts the mention to a specific purpose.
4:74.topic: Al-Ghazali on the journey of the soul, death, and the Hereafter, from 'Remembrance of Death and Afterlife'

4:74.arabic: الجنة اغزوا في سبيل الله فانه من قاتل في سبيل الله فواق ناقة أدخله الله الجنة (5) واحتجوا بما روى معاذ بن جبل أنه صلى الله عليه وسلم قال ان الشيطان ذئب الإنسان كذئب الغنم يأخذ القاصية والناحية والشاردة وإياكم والشعاب وعليكم بالعامة والجماعة والمساجد (6) وهذا إنما أراد به من اعتزل قبل تمام الغلم وسيأتي بيان ذلك وأن ذلك ينهى عنه إلا لضرورة
4:74.english: They (the advocates of total seclusion) argued by His saying, the Exalted: {«And be not like those who became divided and differed»} (3:105) — to the end of the verse. And by His saying, the Exalted: {«And He brought their hearts together»} (8:63) — He bestowed a favor upon mankind through the cause that unites. But this is weak, because what is meant thereby is the divergence of opinions and the disagreement of schools of thought concerning the meanings of the Book of God and the foundations of the Sacred Law. And what is meant by "bringing together" (al-ulfah) is the removal of rancors (al-ghawāʾil) from the breasts — those being the causes that provoke sedition and stir up contentions. And seclusion does not contradict that.
4:74.section_title_en: Section 444 — Refutation of the Isolationists' Proof-Texts from the Qur'an and Sunnah
4:74.anchors:
- Root: هجر (hajara)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To abandon, forsake, or sever relations — whether by body, tongue, or heart; the root carries the sense of definitive separation.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): الهجران is the separation of one from another — by body, by tongue, or by heart. The Quranic usages distinguish between physical abandonment (as in {«واهجروهن في المضاجع»}), verbal/mental rejection (as in {«اتخذوا هذا القرآن مهجورا»}), and the comprehensive sense in {«واهجرهم هجرا جميلا»} — a noble forsaking that avoids harm.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): physical separation and cutting off of contact. Metaphorical (Majaz): the she-camel that refuses the stallion (هجر الفحل) — a cessation of a natural function, applied here to the cessation of social intercourse.
- Root: عله (ʿaliha)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To be bewildered or distracted; related to being occupied away from something. (Contextual note: the root appears in the hadith materials concerning the Prophet's withdrawal from his wives.)
- Root: ضعف (ḍaʿufa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Weakness, feebleness — whether in body, intellect, or resolve.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): الضعف is the opposite of strength; it may be in the soul, the body, or one's condition. Al-Khalil distinguished: الضعف (with dammah) is bodily weakness, while الضعف (with fatḥah) is weakness in intellect and judgment.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical or moral weakness. Metaphorical: "in the folds of the book" (في أضعاف الكتاب) — hidden within the inner recesses, as the isolationists' arguments are weak in their inner structure.
- Root: خلط (khalata)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To mix, blend, or intermingle — whether liquids, solids, or persons in society.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): الخلط is the joining of parts of two or more things; it is more general than al-mazj (fusion). Applied to persons, it denotes social mixing, partnership, and companionship.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: mixing substances. Metaphorical: social intercourse and companionship (خالطت فلانا) — the very thing the isolationist abandons, yet which the believer of good character can undertake without harm.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد (Restriction and Specification) — When a general prohibition (like the hadith against hajr beyond three days) is followed by specific exceptions (the two cases of perceived benefit or safety), the general is carried (maḥmūl) upon the specific, per the established principle of takhṣīṣ al-ʿāmm.
4:74.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Etiquette of Seclusion'

4:74.arabic: وذلك لما سئل أبو موسى عن رجل قاتل في سبيل الله فقتل فقال هو في الجنة وكان أمير الكوفة فقام ابن مسعود فقال أعده على الأمير فلعله لم يفهم فأعادوا عليه فأعاد الجواب فقال ابن مسعود وأنا أقول إن قتل فأصاب الحق فهو في الجنة فقال أبو موسى الحق ما قال وهكذا يكون إنصاف طلب الحق ولو ذكر مثل هذا الآن لأقل فقيه لأنكره واستبعده وقال لا يحتاج إلى أن يقال أصاب الحق فإن ذلك معلوم لكل أحد فانظر إلى مناظري زمانك اليوم كيف يسود وجه أحدهم إذا اتضح الحق على لسان خصمه وكيف يخجل به وكيف يجهد في مجاحدته بأقصى قدرته وكي
4:74.english: The fourth [etiquette]: that he should not dispute except over a matter that has actually occurred, or that is likely to occur in most cases. For the Companions (may God be pleased with them) did not consult one another except over newly arising incidents or what was likely to occur, such as the laws of inheritance (farāʾiḍ). And we do not see the disputants concerning themselves with critiquing questions that are of general affliction (ʿumūm al-balawā) in issuing verdicts about them; rather, they seek out the "drum-beat" questions (ṭubūliyyāt)—those that make noise—so that the field of argumentation widens in them, however the matter may be. PageV01P043
4:74.section_title_en: Section 37 — On the Etiquette of Disputation and the Pursuit of Truth
4:74.anchors:
- Root: نظر (naẓara)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of gazing, examining, and deliberating with the eye of the intellect.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance of speculative reflection (naẓar) as the means to attain knowledge of the unseen and the divine.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) denotes physical sight; metaphorical (majāz) denotes intellectual consideration and weighing of evidence.
- Root: حق (ḥaqqa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The root denotes firmness, reality, and that which is established and undeniable.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance of truth (ḥaqq) as the eternal reality of God and His commands, opposed to falsehood (bāṭil).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal denotes the opposite of falsehood; metaphorical denotes the due right and the correct ruling in a given case.
- Root: خصم (khaṣama)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The root denotes the act of contending, disputing, and overcoming in argument.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance of the adversary (khaṣm) in debate, whose refutation is sought for the sake of truth, not vanity.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal denotes the opponent in a legal contest; metaphorical denotes the one who contends against the truth with fallacious reasoning.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Restriction and Focused Predication (al-ḥaṣr wa al-taqyīd bi-innamā) — Governing the exclusive emphasis on truth-seeking over partisan victory, as in the phrase "the object is truth alone."
4:74.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Book of Knowledge'

4:119.arabic: وأطاع الشيطان لما قال ولآمرنهم فليغيرن خلق الله إذ حق الرجل أن يكون متبوعا لا تابعا وقد سمى الله الرجال قوامين على النساء وسمى الزوج سيدا فقال تعالى وألفيا سيدها لدى الباب فإذا انقلب السيد مسخرا فقد بدل نعمة الله كفرا ونفس المرأة على مثال نفسك إن أرسلت عنانها قليلا جمحت بك طويلا وإن أرخيت عذارها فترا جذبتك ذراعا وإن كبحتها وشددت يدك عليها في محل الشدة ملكتها قال الشافعي رضي الله عنه ثلاثة إن أكرمتهم أهانوك وإن أهنتهم أكرموك المرأة والخادم والنبطي أراد به إن محضت الإكرام ولم تمزج غلظك
4:119.english: The first point of etiquette is the wedding feast (walīmah), and it is recommended (mustaḥabbah). Anas, may God be pleased with him, said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, saw upon ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf, may God be pleased with him, a trace of yellow dye, so he said: {«What is this?»} He replied: "I have married a woman for the weight of a date-stone in gold." He said: "May God bless you. Hold a wedding feast, even if with a single sheep." {«...»} And the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, held a wedding feast for Ṣafiyyah with dates and sawīq (barley porridge). {«...»} And he, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: "The food of the first day is an obligation (ḥaqq), the food of the second day is a Sunnah, and the food of the third day is for show (sumʿah); and whoever seeks to be heard, God will make his deeds heard." {«...»} None raised this hadith except Ziyād ibn ʿAbd Allāh, and it is anomalous (gharīb). It is recommended to offer congratulations to him, and the one who enters upon the husband should say: "May God bless you and shower blessings upon you, and may He bring you both together in goodness." {«...»} Abū Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him, reported that he, may God bless him and grant him peace, commanded this. It is also recommended to make the marriage public (iẓhār al-nikāḥ). He, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: "The distinction between the lawful and the unlawful is the drum and the voice." {«...»} The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: "Announce this marriage, hold it in the mosques, and beat drums for it." {«...»} And on the authority of al-Rubayyiʿ bint Muʿawwidh, she said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came and entered on the morning of my wedding night, and he sat upon my bedding, and we had young girls with us who were beating their drums and lamenting those of my forefathers who had been killed—until one of them said: "And among us is a Prophet who knows what will be tomorrow." He said to her: "Stop this, and say what you were saying before." {«...»}
4:119.section_title_en: On What is Incumbent Upon the Husband and What is Incumbent Upon the Wife
4:119.anchors:
- Root: و ل م (w-l-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The core meaning pertains to the wedding feast (walīmah), derived from the concept of gathering and union.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In theological usage, it signifies the communal meal marking the consummation of a marriage contract, a recommended act of public gratitude.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah) usage denotes the specific feast; metaphorical (Majaz) extension applies to any act of publicizing a joyous occasion.
- Root: ع ش ر (ʿ- sh-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The root denotes association, companionship, and intimacy; the tenth (ʿasharah) of a thing is related, but the primary social sense is cohabitation and mutual dealing.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In the Quranic context of {وَعَاشِرُوهُنَّ بِالْمَعْرُوفِ}, it signifies a sustained, equitable mode of social intercourse grounded in moral rectitude, not mere physical proximity.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah) usage is the act of living together; metaphorical (Majaz) usage elevates it to a standard of ethical conduct (maʿrūf) that defines the marital bond.
- Root: ق س م (q-s-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The root indicates division, apportionment, and distribution; in the marital context, it refers to the equitable division of time among co-wives.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theologically, it is tied to justice (ʿadl) as a divine attribute; for the husband, it is a legal obligation to maintain fairness in material and temporal allotments.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah) usage is the physical act of dividing; metaphorical (Majaz) usage applies to the moral duty of impartiality in affection and provision.
- Root: غ ي ر (gh-y-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The root conveys alteration and change, but in the moral register, it denotes protective jealousy (ghayrah), a state of aversion to the violation of honor.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In Kalam, ghayrah is a praiseworthy emotion when aligned with divine law—jealousy for the sanctity of the family—and blameworthy when it stems from unjust suspicion (sūʾ al-ẓann).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah) usage is the emotional state; metaphorical (Majaz) usage is attributed to God (al-Ghayyār) as a figure for His prohibition of indecencies, distinguishing human passion from divine will.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — Used to isolate specific obligations (e.g., "the third is that he should increase...") and to distinguish categories of jealousy and pride, ensuring precise legal and moral demarcation.
4:119.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Etiquette of Marriage'

4:119.arabic: أما من كان مستعدا فقد فاز فوزا عظيما وأما من كان مغرورا بطول الأمل فقد خسر خسرانا مبينا فلينظر الإنسان كل ساعة في أطرافه وأعضائه وليتدبر أنها كيف تأكلها الديدان لا محالة وكيف تتفتت عظامها وليتفكر أن الدود يبدأ بحدقته اليمنى أولا أو اليسرى فما على بدنه شيء إلا وهو طعمة الدود وما له من نفسه إلا العلم والعمل الخالص لوجه الله تعالى وكذلك يتفكر فيما سنورده من عذاب القبر وسؤال منكر ونكير ومن الحشر والنشر وأهوال القيامة وقرع النداء يوم العرض الأكبر فأمثال هذه الأفكار هي التي تجدد ذكر الموت على قلبه وتدعوه إلى الاستعداد له
4:119.english: He defers day after day, and one occupation passes him on to another — nay, to many occupations — until death snatches him away at a moment he does not anticipate. Then his regret becomes prolonged, and most of the people of the Fire — and their screaming — are from "I will" (sawfa). They say: "Woe to us for our 'I will'!" (wa-ḥazanāh min sawfa).
4:119.section_title_en: The True Nature of Procrastination (al-Taswīf): Its Causes and Cures — On the Deception of Extended Hope (ṭūl al-amal)
4:119.anchors:
- Root: سوف (s-w-f)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "سوف" is a particle of future tense (tanjīz al-waʿd), indicating postponement and delay; al-musawwif is one who defers action.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The root conveys "delay" (taʾkhīr) and is tied to the blameworthy trait of procrastination in religious duties, as opposed to immediate resolve (mubādarah).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "سوّفت به" (I delayed him). Metaphorical: "سوّف بنفسه" — he lulled himself with false promises of future time, a majāz for self-deception.
- Root: أمل (a-m-l)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Hope/expectation (rajāʾ); ṭūl al-amal is extended hope — the root cause of negligence (ghaflah) in preparing for death.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Amal is expectation of a desired outcome; blameworthy when it exceeds the appointed term (ajal), diverting from the Hereafter.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "أملت الشيء" (I hoped for it). Metaphorical: Extended hope is a veil (ḥijāb) over the certainty of death.
- Root: جهل (j-h-l)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Ignorance, the opposite of knowledge (ʿilm); also rashness acting without knowledge.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Jahl is the absence of knowledge about what one must know — here, ignorance of death's unpredictability.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: lack of knowledge. Metaphorical: acting as if death is distant despite its certainty — a practical ignorance.
- Root: حب (ḥ-b-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Love/attachment (wudd); ḥubb al-dunyā is the love of the lower world.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Love is the inclination of the heart toward what pleases it; love of the world (dunyā) is the root of all blameworthy traits.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: affection. Metaphorical: "ḥubb al-khaṭīr" (love of the momentous) erases "ḥubb al-ḥaqīr" (love of the trivial) — a majāz for spiritual reorientation.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — Used in "فإنما يزداد بطول المدة قوة ورسوخا" (it only increases in strength and rootedness with length of time), restricting the outcome to intensification alone.
4:119.topic: Al-Ghazali on the journey of the soul, death, and the Hereafter, from 'Remembrance of Death and Afterlife'

4:135.arabic: قليلا منهم كانوا ينهون عن الفساد وقال تعالى يا أيها الذين آمنوا كونوا قوامين بالقسط شهداء لله ولو على أنفسكم أو الوالدين والأقربين وذلك هو الأمر بالمعروف للوالدين والأقربين وقال تعالى لا خير في كثير من نجواهم إلا من أمر بصدقة أو معروف أو إصلاح بين الناس ومن يفعل ذلك ابتغاء مرضاة الله فسوف نؤتيه أجرا عظيما وقال تعالى وإن طائفتان من المؤمنين اقتتلوا فأصلحوا بينهما الآية والإصلاح نهي عن البغي وإعادة إلى الطاعة فإن لم يفعل فقد أمر الله تعالى بقتاله فقال فقاتلوا التي تبغي حتى تفيء إلى أمر الله وذلك هو النهي عن المنكر وأما الأخبار فمنها ما ر
4:135.english: Know that the verses indicating the obligation of commanding right and forbidding wrong are numerous. Among them is His saying, may He be exalted: {«Let there arise from among you a nation inviting to good, commanding right and forbidding wrong — and those are the successful»} (Āl ʿImrān 3:104). In this verse is the declaration of obligation, for His saying, may He be exalted, "Let there be" (wal-takun) is a command, and the apparent meaning of a command is obligation. In it also is the declaration that success (falāḥ) is contingent upon it, for He restricted it and said: {«And those are the successful»}. In it also is the declaration that it is a collective obligation (farḍ kifāyah), not an individual obligation (farḍ ʿayn), and that when a group undertakes it, the obligation falls from the rest — for He did not say, "Let all of you be commanders of right," but rather said: {«Let there arise from among you a nation»}. Thus, whenever one person or a group undertakes it, the burden falls from the others, and success is particularized to those who undertake it and directly perform it. But if all of creation were to hold back from it, the burden would encompass all those capable of it without exception.
4:135.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Remembrance of Death and Afterlife'

4:135.arabic: وقد قال الله تعالى يا أيها الذين آمنوا أنفقوا من طيبات ما كسبتم ومما أخرجنا لكم من الأرض ولا تيمموا الخبيث منه تنفقون ولستم بآخذيه إلا أن تغمضوا فيه أي لا تأخذوه إلا مع كراهية وحياء وهو معنى الإغماض فلا تؤثروا به ربكم وفي الخبر سبق درهم مائة ألف درهم (3) وذلك بأن يخرجه الإنسان وهو من أحل ماله وأجوده فيصدر ذلك عن الرضا والفرح بالبذل وقد يخرج مائة ألف درهم مما يكره من ماله فيدل ذلك على أنه ليس يؤثر الله عز وجل بشيء مما يحبه وبذلك ذم الله تعالى قوما جعلوا لله ما يكرهون فقال تعال
4:135.english: The heart is not treated save with the compound electuary (maʿjūn) of knowledge and works. And this condition among the conditions of almsgiving runs in the same course as humility (al-khushūʿ) runs in the prayer. This is established by his saying — may Allah bless him and grant him peace: "A man has nothing of his prayer save that of which he was conscious." And this is like his saying — may Allah bless him and grant him peace: "Allah does not accept the charity of the one who bestows it with reproach (al-mannān)." And like His saying — Exalted is He: {«لا تبطلوا صدقاتكم بالمن والأذى»} ("Do not nullify your charities by reproach and injury"). As for the legal opinion (fatwā) of the jurist that the alms fall in their proper place and that one's liability is discharged without this condition — that is another discussion, and we have already pointed to its meaning in the Book of Prayer.
4:135.section_title_en: The Inner Conditions of Charity — Section 175 (From The Revival of the Religious Sciences, Book of the Mysteries of Almsgiving)
4:135.anchors:
- Root: قلب (q-l-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "To turn, overturn, transform a thing from one state to another; to rotate, to flip"
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "قلب الشيء: تصريفه وصرفه عن وجه إلى وجه" — the heart is so named because of its constant turning and transformation between states
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "قلب الشيء قلبا: حوله عن وجهه" (to turn a thing from its face). Metaphorical: "رجل قلب حول: يقلب الأمور ويحتال" — one who turns matters over and manages them; "قلبوا لك الأمور" (they turned matters against you)
- Root: وجل (w-j-l)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "Fear, dread, apprehension that strikes the heart"
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الوجل: استشعار الخوف" — the sensing of fear; cited in {«إنما المؤمنون الذين إذا ذكر الله وجلت قلوبهم»}
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "رجل وجل، وقوم وجال" — a fearful man, a fearful people; "وفي قلبه وجل" — in his heart is dread
- Root: عجب (ʿ-j-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "Wonder, amazement; self-admiration, vanity"
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Self-admiration (al-ʿujb) is a destructive spiritual ailment that nullifies deeds
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: wonder at something extraordinary. Metaphorical: self-conceit regarding one's own acts of obedience
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد (Restriction & Focused Predication) — governing the precise limitation of general categories (al-ṣifāt al-khāṣṣah within al-aṣnāf al-thamāniyyah) and the conditional structure of acceptance

4:135.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Duties of Brotherhood'

4:171.arabic: السلام فيأتون عيسى فيقولون يا عيسى أنت رسول الله وكلمته ألقاها إلى مريم وروح منه وكلمت الناس في المهد اشفع لنا إلى ربك ألا ترى ما نحن فيه فيقول عيسى عليه السلام إن ربي غضب اليوم غضبا لم يغضب قبله مثله ولن يغضب بعده مثله ولم يذكر ذنبا نفسي نفسي اذهبوا إلى غيري اذهبوا إلى محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم فيأتون فيقولون يا محمد أنت رسول الله وخاتم النبيين وغفر الله لك ما تقدم من ذنبك وما تأخر اشفع لنا إلى ربك ألا ترى ما نحن فيه فأنطلق فآتي تحت العرش فأقع ساجدا لربي ثم يفتح الله لي من محامده وحسن الثناء عليه شيئا لم يفتحه على أحد قبلي ثم
4:171.english: The evidences for intercession in the Qurʾān and the reports (akhbār) are numerous. God—exalted be He—said: {«وَلَسَوْفَ يُعْطِيكَ رَبُّكَ فَتَرْضَىٰ»} [And verily thy Lord shall give thee, and thou shalt be well-pleased] (93:5). ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ narrated that the Messenger of God—peace and blessings be upon him—recited the saying of Abraham—peace be upon him—{«رَبِّ إِنَّهُنَّ أَضْلَلْنَ كَثِيرًا مِّنَ النَّاسِ ۖ فَمَن تَبِعَنِي فَإِنَّهُ مِنِّي ۖ وَمَنْ عَصَانِي فَإِنَّكَ غَفُورٌ رَّحِيمٌ»} [My Lord, verily they have led astray many of mankind; so whoso follows me, verily he is of me; and whoso disobeys me, verily Thou art Forgiving, Merciful] (14:36), and the saying of Jesus—peace be upon him—{«إِن تُعَذِّبْهُمْ فَإِنَّهُمْ عِبَادُكَ»} [If Thou chastise them, verily they are Thy servants] (5:118). Then he raised his hands and said: "My community, my community!" Then he wept. So God—mighty and majestic—said: "O Gabriel, go to Muhammad and ask him what makes him weep." Gabriel came to him and asked him, and he informed him—and God knows best concerning him. Then He said: "O Gabriel, go to Muhammad and say to him: 'Verily We shall please thee concerning thy community, and shall not cause thee grief.'"
4:171.section_title_en: On the Reality of Intercession (Shafāʿah) and the Means of Attaining It
4:171.anchors:
- Root: شفع (Sh-F-ʿ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root denotes pairing/joining (al-ḍamm), whence shafāʿah = the intercessor joining his own plea to the petitioner's, making it two (shafʿ) rather than one (watr).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance — intercession is a divinely granted honor (jāh) bestowed upon prophets and saints, not an independent power; its efficacy is wholly contingent upon divine will and pleasure.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) — "شفعت الشيء" (I made it even/pair). Metaphorical (majāz) — the intercessor "pairs" his rank with the sinner's need, elevating the latter through the former's proximity to God.
- Root: خبأ (Kh-B-ʾ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To conceal, hide, store away secretly (khabaʾa). Implies deliberate concealment of something precious or dangerous within a locus.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance — God's "hiding" (takhbiʾah) of His friendship (wilāyah), wrath (ghaḍab), and pleasure (riḍā) within creatures and acts respectively teaches epistemic humility: no outward judgment can access the hidden decree.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — physical concealment. Metaphorical — the inscrutability of divine judgment (ḥukm) regarding ultimate states (ʿawāqib), rendering contempt for any person or act a potential act of defiance against God's hidden will.
- Root: عله (not applicable here; avoided per instruction)
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — Governing the periodic suspension of meaning across lengthy narrative sequences (e.g., the extended ḥadīth of intercession), where the syntactic resolution (jawāb) is deferred to heighten rhetorical impact, yet remains grammatically anchored.
4:171.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Remembrance of Death and Afterlife'

4:171.arabic: الله عليه وسلم من جاءني زائرا لا يهمه إلا زيارتي كان حقا على الله سبحانه أن أكون له شفيعا (4) فمن قصد زيارة المدينة فليصل على رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في طريقه كثيرا فإذا وقع بصره على حيطان المدينة وأشجاره قال اللهم هذا حرم رسولك فاجعله لي وقاية من النار وأمانا من العذاب وسوء الحساب وليغتسل قبل الدخول من بئر الحرة وليتطيب وليلبس أنظف ثيابه فإذا دخلها فليدخلها متواضعا معظما وليقل بسم الله وعلى ملة رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم رب أدخلني مدخل صدق وأخرجني مخرج صدق واجعل لي من لدنك سلطانا نصيرا ثم يقصد المسجد وي
4:171.english: I say: The Prophet ﷺ said: "Whoever visits me after my death, it is as though he visited me during my life." {من زارني بعد وفاتي فكأنما زارني في حياتي}
4:171.section_title_en: Section 210 — The Etiquette of Visiting the Prophet's Mosque and Grave in Medina
4:171.anchors:
- Root: زور (z-w-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of inclining toward, visiting, or intending a place or person; the visitor (zā'ir) is one who turns away from his own affairs toward another.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In theological context, ziyārah (visitation) of the Prophet ﷺ after death is an act of spiritual devotion (taqarrub), not a mere physical journey; its reward is tied to the sincerity of intention (niyyah).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (haqīqah) usage denotes physical approach; metaphorical (majāz) usage extends to seeking intercession (shafā'ah) and spiritual connection with the visited.
- Root: سلم (s-l-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Root denotes safety, peace, and deliverance from harm; the greeting "al-salāmu ʿalaykum" is a prayer for the recipient's immunity from all deficiency.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The greeting upon the Prophet ﷺ is a form of supplication (duʿā') and acknowledgment of his rank; it is also a renewal of the covenant (mīthāq) of obedience.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal usage is the exchange of safety; metaphorical usage in the visitation context signifies the visitor's submission and the Prophet's reciprocal blessing.
- Root: شفع (sh-f-ʿ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Root denotes pairing or joining; shafā'ah (intercession) is the act of the intercessor joining his own plea to that of the petitioner.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In Kalam, shafā'ah is a divinely granted honor (karāmah) to the Prophet ﷺ, conditional upon divine will; it is not an independent power but a mediated mercy.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: making a number even by adding one; metaphorical: the intercessor's elevation of the petitioner's rank before the king.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Prepositional Interposition (al-faṣl bayna al-jār wa al-majrūr) — The text employs extended vocative and prepositional structures (e.g., "al-salāmu ʿalayka yā Rasūl Allāh") where the syntactic pause after each invocation is permissible and rhetorically deliberate, mirroring the classical allowance for separation between the governing particle and its object for emphasis.
4:171.topic: Al-Ghazali on the journey of the soul, death, and the Hereafter, from 'Mysteries of Hajj'

4:171.arabic: معناه أن لا يكونا له بل أن يكونا له ولا يشغلانه وهو إشارة إلى قول أبي سليمان الداراني ما شغلك عن الله من أهل ومال وولد فهو عليك مشئوم وبالجملة لم ينقل عن أحد الترغيب عن النكاح مطلقا إلا مقرونا بشرط وأما الترغيب في النكاح فقد ورد مطلقا ومقرونا بشرط فلنكشف الغطاء عنه بحصر آفات النكاح وفوائده آفات النكاح وفوائده وفيه فوائد خمسة الولد وكسر الشهوة وتدبير المنزل وكثرة العشيرة ومجاهدة النفس بالقيام بهن الفائدة الأولى الولد وهو الأصل وله وضع النكاح والمقصود إبقاء النسل وأن لا يخلو العالم عن
4:171.english: وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم: "لا يلقى الله أحد بذنب أعظم من جهالة أهله."
4:171.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Etiquette of Marriage'

5:27.arabic: ثم قرأ {واتل عليهم نبأ ابني آدم بالحق} الآيات وإذا ذكر أصحاب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فأمسك وإذا ذكر القدر فاسكت وإذا ذكرت النجوم فاسكت وقال بكر بن عبد الله كان رجل يغشى بعض الملوك فيقوم بحذاء الملك فيقول أحسن إلى المحسن بإحسانه فإن المسيء سيكفيكه إساءته فحسده رجل على ذلك المقام والكلام فسعى به إلى الملك فقال إن هذا الذي يقوم بحذائك ويقول ما يقول زعم أن الملك أبخر فقال له الملك وكيف يصح ذلك عندي قال تدعوه إليك فإنه إذا دنا منك وضع يده على أنفه لئلا يشم ريح البخر فقال له انص
5:27.english: Know that envy (ḥasad) is likewise among the fruits of rancor (ḥiqd), and rancor is among the fruits of anger (ghaḍab) — so envy is a branch of a branch, while anger is the root of the root. Then envy has, among its blameworthy branches, that which can scarcely be enumerated. And there have come down, specifically in condemnation of envy, many reports (akhbār). The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: {«Envy consumes good deeds just as fire consumes wood»} (1). The ḥadīth: {«Do not cut one another off, nor turn your backs on one another, nor hate one another»} — agreed upon (muttafaq ʿalayh), and it has already preceded. (2) The ḥadīth of Anas: "We were sitting one day with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, when he said: 'There will now come upon you from this mountain pass a man from among the people of Paradise'" — the ḥadīth in its entirety, and in it: that man said, "I do not find in myself any rancor toward any of the Muslims, nor envy of anyone for the good that God has given him." Narrated by Aḥmad with a sound chain (isnād) upon the condition of the two Shaykhs (al-Bukhārī and Muslim), and narrated by al-Bazzār, and the man was named in one of its narrations as Saʿd — though in it there is Ibn Lahīʿah. (3) The ḥadīth: {«Three things from which no one escapes: suspicion, slander, and envy»} — and in another narration: "And few are those who escape them." It was related by Ibn Abī al-Dunyā in his book "Dhamm al-Ḥasad" (The Condemnation of Envy) from the ḥadīth of Abū Hurayrah — though in its chain there are Yaʿqūb ibn Muḥammad al-Zuhrī and Mūsā ibn Yaʿqūb al-Zamaʿī, both of whom the majority of scholars have declared weak. The second narration was also related by Ibn Abī al-Dunyā from the narration of ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Muʿāwiyah, and it is mursal (broken chain) and weak. Al-Ṭabarānī has something similar from the ḥadīth of Ḥārithah ibn al-Nuʿmān, and it has already preceded in the section on the afflictions of the tongue. And in one narration: {«Three things from which no one escapes — and few are those who escape them»} — so this narration affirms the possibility of deliverance. And he, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: {«There has crept upon you the disease of the nations before you: envy and hatred. And hatred is the clipper — I do not say it clips the hair, but rather it clips the religion. By Him in whose hand is the soul of Muḥammad, you shall not enter Paradise until you believe, and you shall not believe until you love one another. Shall I not inform you of that which will establish this for you? Spread peace (salām) among you»} (4). And he, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: {«Poverty almost becomes unbelief, and envy almost overcomes destiny (qadar)»} (5). And he, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: {«Indeed, my community will be afflicted with the disease of the nations.» They said: "And what is the disease of the nations?" He said: {«Extravagance, arrogance, accumulation, rivalry in worldly things, mutual distance, and mutual envy — until transgression (baghy) comes, and then destruction (harj)»} (6). And he, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: {«Do not show gloating (shamātah) over your brother, lest God heal him and afflict you»} (7). And it is narrated that Moses, peace be upon him, when he hastened to his Lord, Exalted is He, saw a man in the shade of the Throne (ʿArsh) and envied him his station (ghabaṭahu), saying: "This one is honored before his Lord." So he asked his Lord, Exalted is He, to inform him of his name, but He did not inform him, and said: "I shall tell you of three of his deeds: he did not envy people for what God had given them of His bounty, he was not undutiful to his parents, and he did not go about with slander (namīmah)." And Zechariah, peace be upon him, said: God, Exalted is He, said: {«The envier is an enemy of My blessing, resentful of My decree, dissatisfied with My apportioning which I have apportioned among My servants»}.
