And he, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: {«The thing I most fear for my community is that wealth will increase among them, and they will envy one another and fight one another»} (1). And he, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: {«Seek help in fulfilling your needs by keeping them secret, for everyone who possesses a blessing is envied»} (2). And he, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: {«Indeed, the blessings of God have enemies.» It was said: "And who are they?" He said: {«Those who envy people for what God has given them of His bounty»} (3). The ḥadīth: {«Six will enter the Fire before the Reckoning by a year.» It was said: "O Messenger of God, who are they?" He said: {«The unjust rulers»} — the ḥadīth — and in it: {«And the scholars who envy»}. Narrated by Abū Manṣūr al-Daylamī from the ḥadīth of Ibn ʿUmar and Anas with two weak chains of transmission.
5:27.section_title_en: Section 718 — On Envy (Ḥasad): Its Roots, Branches, and Blameworthy Fruits
5:27.anchors:
- Root: حسد (Ḥ-S-D)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of wishing for removal of a blessing from its possessor, rooted in spite and resentment.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الحسد: تمني زوال نعمة من مستحق لها" — Envy is the desire for the removal of a blessing from one who rightly deserves it, sometimes accompanied by active striving to effect its removal. The believer envies not, but the hypocrite does.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): "حسده على نعمة الله" — to envy him for God's blessing. Metaphorical (majāz): "إن الحسد يأكل الجسد" — envy consumes the body, as fire consumes wood, indicating its destructive spiritual effect.
- Root: حدث (Ḥ-D-TH)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Origination after non-existence; bringing into being after nothingness.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الحدوث: كون الشيء بعد أن لم يكن" — origination is a thing's coming to be after it was not. The ḥadīth (report) is so-called for its temporal proximity to the event it narrates.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "هو حدث من الأحداث" — he is a youth among youths. Metaphorical: "صاروا أحاديث" — they became subjects of talk, indicating fame or infamy spread by tongues.
- Root: ملك (M-L-K)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Possession, dominion, sovereignty; the one who possesses and disposes.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الملك: هو المتصرف بالأمر والنهي" — dominion is disposal by command and prohibition. Two kinds: actual possession/sovereignty, and the power/capacity to exercise it.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "ملكت فلانة" — he married her (possessed her in wedlock). Metaphorical: "ملك نفسه عند الغضب" — he mastered himself at the moment of anger, i.e., self-restraint.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — When the Prophet (ﷺ) says "إنما قتل ابن آدم أخاه حين حسده" (It was only envy that led the son of Adam to kill his brother), the restrictive particle إنما confines the cause of the first murder to envy alone, isolating it as the sole efficient cause of that primordial transgression.
5:27.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Condemnation of Envy'

5:27.arabic: وجل {إنما يتقبل الله من المتقين} ودخل الحسن رضي الله عنه على رجل يجود بنفسه فقال إن أمرا هذا أوله لجدير أن يتقي آخره وإن أمرا هذا آخره لجدير أن يزهد في أوله وقال الجريري كنت عند الجنيد في حال نزعه وكان يوم الجمعة ويوم النيروز وهو يقرأ القرآن فختم فقلت له في الحالة يا أبا القاسم فقال ومن أولى بذلك مني وهو ذا تطوى صحيفتى وقال رويم حضرت وفاة أبي سعيد الخراز وهو يقول حنين قلوب العارفين إلى الذكر .
5:27.english: When death came to Mu'adh — may God be pleased with him — he said: "O God, I have indeed feared You, yet today I hope in You. O God, You know that I did not love this world nor long abiding in it for the flowing of rivers, nor for the planting of trees, but rather for the thirst of noonday heat, the endurance of the hours, and the jostling of scholars knee-to-knee at the circles of remembrance." And when the agony of death grew severe upon him — a throes such as no one else had endured — every time he regained consciousness from its overwhelming flood, he would open his eyes and then say: "O Lord, how constricting is Your strangling! By Your might, You know that my heart loves You."
5:27.section_title_en: The Deathbed Sayings of the Righteous — Yearning for the Beloved at the Final Hour
5:27.anchors:
- Root: موت (m-w-t)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of death as cessation of vital faculty; "مات ميتة سوء" — a death of evil kind; "أماته الله" — God causes death.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Death (al-mawt) is the cessation of the rational soul's attachment to the body — not annihilation; the state of the dying (naz') is the severing of that attachment.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (haqiqah) — bodily death; Metaphorical (majaz) — "أحيا الله البلد الميت" (reviving dead land), and the death of the heart through heedlessness.
- Root: بكي (b-k-y)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Weeping with tears; "بكاء" (with prolongation) — weeping with audible wailing; "بكى" (with shortening) — weeping where grief predominates over sound.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Weeping is the flow of tears from grief or lamentation; the plural "بكي" (bukiyy) describes those overcome by weeping, as in {خروا سجدا وبكيا} (Maryam: 58).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — weeping over the dead; Metaphorical — "بكت السماء والأرض" (the sky and earth wept) for the oppressed.
- Root: فتح (f-t-ḥ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Opening, removing closure; "فتح الباب" — opening a door.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Two kinds: (1) perceived by sight — opening a door; (2) perceived by inner vision (basirah) — opening of distress, i.e., removal of grief; also opening the eyes at death as a final glance toward the unseen.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — opening a door; Metaphorical — "فتح الله عليه: نصره" (God opened/granted him victory); the opening of the eyes of the dying as a spiritual unveiling.
- Root: قال (q-w-l)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Saying, uttering; a comprehensive term for speech, whether statement, question, or command.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — "إنما يتقبل الله من المتقين" (Al-Ma'idah: 27): the particle innama restricts acceptance exclusively to the God-fearing, negating any notion of acceptance based on outward deed alone.
5:27.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Remembrance of Death and Afterlife'

5:109.arabic: عما كانوا يعملون} فيبدأ سبحانه بالأنبياء {يوم يجمع الله الرسل فيقول}
5:109.english: Then reflect, O wretched one, after these states upon what is directed against you of the questioning — face to face, without any interpreter — and you shall be asked concerning the little and the much, the speck on a date-stone (al-naqīr) and the husk (al-qitmīr). For while you are amidst the distress of the Resurrection, its sweat, and the severity of its terrors, lo! the angels descend from the horizons of the heaven with immense bodies and gigantic forms — harsh, severe — commanded to seize the forelocks of the criminals and drag them to the standing-place of presentation (mawqif al-ʿarḍ) before the Omnipotent (al-Jabbār). The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: "Verily, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has an angel between whose two eyelids is a distance of a hundred years' journey." So what is your assumption concerning yourself when you behold the likes of these angels — dispatched unto you to seize you and bring you to the station of presentation — and you see them, despite the enormity of their forms, broken in humility before the severity of that Day, filled with dread at what has become manifest of the Omnipotent's wrath upon His servants? And at their descent, there remains no prophet, no veracious one (ṣiddīq), no righteous soul, save that they fall upon their chins in fear, lest they themselves be the seized ones. Such is the state of those brought near (al-muqarrabūn) — so what is your assumption concerning the disobedient criminals?
5:109.section_title_en: The Description of the Day of Resurrection, Its Calamities, and Its Names — The Description of the Questioning
5:109.anchors:
- Root: س-أ-ل (sa-ʾa-la)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root denotes seeking, demanding, or interrogating; al-suʾāl is the act of asking, and musāʾalah implies reciprocal or formal interrogation.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In theological context, al-suʾāl on the Day of Resurrection is a divine inquest (musāʾalah) demanding account of deeds, not for God's knowledge (as He is 'alīm) but for establishing proof (ḥujjah) against the creature.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) usage is verbal inquiry; metaphorical (majāz) extends to the juridical reckoning (muḥāsabah) where the tongue is made to testify without intermediary.
- Root: ن-ز-ل (na-za-la)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root signifies descent from a height; nuzūl is the act of alighting.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): When predicated of angels, it denotes their dispatch from the celestial realm to execute divine command — a descent of authority, not spatial movement in the divine essence.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical descent; metaphorical: the advent of divine decree or angelic execution of wrath.
- Root: ع-ر-ض (ʿa-ra-ḍa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root means to present, expose, or show; al-ʿarḍ is the exhibition of something before a viewer.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In eschatological usage, mawqif al-ʿarḍ is the standing-place of presentation before God for judgment — a public display of deeds.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: to show; metaphorical: the juridical tribunal of the Hereafter where all acts are exhibited.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Interrogative Scope (Bāb al-istifhām) — The rhetorical question "فما ظنك" (so what is your assumption?) functions as a periodic pause, redirecting the addressee's cognition from narrated events to self-projection, governed by the conditional-temporal particle "إذ" (when) that binds the apodosis to the protasis.
5:109.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'Remembrance of Death and Afterlife'

5:109.arabic: {ماذا أجبتم قالوا لا علم لنا إنك أنت علام الغيوب} فيا لشدة يوم تذهل فيه عقول الأنبياء وتنمحى علومهم من شدة الهيبة إذ يقال لهم ما أجبتم وقد أرسلتم إلى الخلائق وكانوا قد علموا فتدهش عقولهم فلا يدرون بماذا يجيبون فيقولون من شدة الهيبة لا علم لنا إنك أنت علام الغيوب وهم فى ذلك الوقت صادقون إذ طارت منهم العقول وانمحت العلوم إلى أن يقويهم الله تعالى فيدعى نوح عليه السلام فيقال له هل بلغت فيقول نعم فيقال لأمته هل بلغكم فيقولون ما أتانا من نذير ويؤتى بعيسى عليه السلام فيقول الله تعالى له {أأنت قلت للنا
5:109.english: {«ماذا أجبتم قالوا لا علم لنا إنك أنت علام الغيوب»} — "What did you answer?" They will say: "We have no knowledge; indeed, You alone are the Knower of the unseen." {Quran 5:109} So woe betide the severity of a Day in which the intellects of the prophets are stupefied and their knowledges are effaced by the sheer intensity of the awe, when it is said to them: "What did you answer, when you were sent to the creatures?" — though they had known — yet their intellects are bewildered, and they know not with what to reply. So they say, from the intensity of the awe: "We have no knowledge; indeed, You alone are the Knower of the unseen." And they are, at that very moment, truthful, for the intellects have flown away from them and the knowledges have been effaced — until God Almighty strengthens them. Then Noah (peace be upon him) is summoned, and it is said to him: "Did you convey the message?" He says: "Yes." Then it is said to his community: "Did he convey to you?" They say: "No warner came to us."
5:109.section_title_en: The Day of Reckoning: The Questioning of the Prophets and the Exposure of the Servant Before the Lord of the Worlds
5:109.anchors:
- Root: رسل (R-S-L)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of "sending forth with ease and gentleness"; a messenger (rasūl) is one dispatched with a message.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الرسول" denotes one sent with a commission; the root conveys both the act of dispatch and the message borne. In the eschatological context, the prophets (rusul) are asked "ماذا أجبتم" — what answer did they give to those to whom they were sent.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (haqīqah): "أرسل الله في الأمم رسلا" — God sent messengers among the nations. Metaphorical (majāz): "أرسل الله عليهم العذاب" — God loosed chastisement upon them. Here, the sending of prophets is literal, but the terror of the Day is such that even their knowledge is effaced.
- Root: علم (ʿ-L-M)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Knowledge, perception, certainty; the opposite of ignorance.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "العلم: إدراك الشيء بحقيقته" — knowledge is the apprehension of a thing in its true reality. On the Day of Terror, the prophets' knowledge (ʿulūmuhum) is erased (tunmaḥū) by the sheer overwhelming majesty (haybah) of the Divine address, leaving them to answer: "لا علم لنا" — "We have no knowledge."
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "علمت الشيء أعلمه" — I knew the thing. Here, the effacement of knowledge is a literal event of the Hour, not metaphorical, for the prophets are truthful when they disavow knowledge in that state.
- Root: يوم (Y-W-M)
  * Lisan / Ayn: A day; a period of time, whether short or long.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "اليوم يعبر به عن وقت طلوع الشمس إلى غروبها. وقد يعبر به عن مدة من الزمان أي مدة كانت" — the day is the time from sunrise to sunset, but it may denote any span of time. The "Day" of Resurrection is a duration whose terrors are magnified beyond earthly measure.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "ما رأيته اليوم" — I did not see him today. Metaphorical: "ذكر في أيام العرب كذا أي في وقائعها" — "days" of the Arabs means their battles. The "Day" of Judgment is a real day, but its horrors are such that the prophets themselves are stupefied.
- Root: الم (ʾ-L-M)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Severe pain, anguish.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الألم الوجع الشديد" — pain is intense suffering. The "عذاب أليم" is a painful chastisement. In this passage, the terror of the Day is an "أليم" affliction upon the hearts of all creatures.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "مسه بضرب أليم" — he touched him with a painful blow. The anguish of the Day is literal and inescapable.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — The construction "إنك أنت علام الغيوب" employs the emphatic pronoun "أنت" as a focused predication, restricting the attribute of absolute knowledge of the unseen to God alone, even as the prophets disavow all knowledge before Him.
5:109.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'Remembrance of Death and Afterlife'

5:118.arabic: يرددها وهي إن تعذبهم فإنهم عبادك وإن تغفر لهم (2) الآية وقام تميم الداري ليلة بهذه الآية {أم حسب الذين اجترحوا السيئات} الآية وقام سعيد بن جبير ليلة يردد هذه الآية وامتازوا اليوم أيها المجرمون وقال بعضهم إني لأفتتح السورة فيوقفني بعض ما أشهد فيها عن الفراغ منها حتى يطلع الفجر وكان بعضهم يقول آية لا أتفهمها ولا يكون قلبي فيها لا أعد لها ثوابا وحكي عن أبي سليمان الداراني أنه قال إني لأتلو الآية فأقيم فيها أربع ليال أو خمس ليال ولولا أني أقطع الفكر فيها ما جاوزتها إلى غيرها وعن
5:118.english: Ali, may God be pleased with him, said: "There is no good in worship that lacks understanding (fiqh), nor in recitation that lacks reflection."
5:118.section_title_en: The Third Book on the Inward Acts During Recitation — Ten in Number
5:118.anchors:
- Root: دبر (d-b-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The rear, the back part; what comes after; to turn one's back; the end or sequel of a thing.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): That which is opposite of "front" (qabal); used metaphorically for what follows or comes after; "adbar al-nahar" — the latter part of the day; "adbar al-sujud" — the concluding portions of prayers.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the back or hind part. Metaphorical: what comes at the end, the sequel, the consequence of an affair.
- Root: قلب (q-l-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To turn over, to overturn, to transform; the heart as that which is constantly turning and fluctuating between states.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The turning and directing of a thing from one face to another; al-taqallub — the constant changing and fluctuation; the heart (qalb) is so named for its perpetual turning about of resolutions and states.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: to turn a thing over from its face. Metaphorical: to ponder, to examine thoroughly, to turn a matter over in the mind — "qallaba al-amr" — he examined the affair from all sides.
- Root: ختم (kh-t-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To seal, to stamp, to imprint; the seal or stamp itself.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Sealing and stamping — used both for the act of impressing and the impression left; metaphorically employed for securing a thing and preventing access to it, as in {«ختم الله على قلوبهم»} (God sealed their hearts).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: placing a seal upon something. Metaphorical: to conclude, to finish, to bring to an end — "khatama al-Qur'an" — he completed the recitation of the Quran.
- Root: بقي (b-q-y)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To remain, to endure, to persist; the lasting and continuing of a thing.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The persistence of a thing upon its original state; that which remains (al-baqi) is of two kinds: that which remains by itself without limit — and that is the Creator, may He be exalted — and that which remains by another, which is everything other than Him.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: to remain, to stay. Metaphorical: "baqiya al-shay'" — the enduring of a thing; "ma baqiyat minhum baqiyah" — not one of them remained.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — When the construction "innama" is employed, it restricts the predicate to the subject alone, excluding all else. This is pertinent here as the author delimits the inward acts of recitation to precisely ten, no more and no less.
5:118.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Remembrance of Death and Afterlife'

6:38.arabic: وقال أبو هريرة في قوله عز وجل {وما من دابة في الأرض ولا طائر يطير بجناحيه إلا أمم أمثالكم} أنه يحشر الخلق كلهم يوم القيامة البهائم والدواب والطير وكل شىء فيبلغ من عدل الله تعالى أن يأخذ للجماء من القرناء ثم يقول كونى ترابا فذلك حين يقول الكافر يا ليتني كنت ترابا فكنت أنت يا مسكين فى يوم ترى صحيفتك خالية عن حسنات طال فيها تعبك فتقول أين حسناتى فيقال نقلت إلى صحيفة خصمائك وترى صحيفتك مشحونة بسيئات طال فى الصبر عنها نصبك واشتد بسبب الكف عنها عناؤك فتقول يا رب هذه سيئات ما قارفتها قط فيقال هذه سيئات القوم الذين اغتبتهم وشتمتهم وقصدتهم بالسو
6:38.english: Know that none is saved from the peril of the Scale except him who, in this world, called his own soul to account, and weighed therein — by the scale of the Sacred Law — his deeds, his words, his passing thoughts, and his glances, just as ʿUmar — may God be well pleased with him — said: "Call yourselves to account before you are called to account, and weigh yourselves before you are weighed." Indeed, his calling himself to account consists in his repenting, before death, from every act of disobedience with a sincere repentance (tawbah naṣūḥ), and in his making up for what was neglected of his shortcomings regarding the obligatory commands of God — may He be exalted — and in his restoring rights to those he wronged, grain by grain, and in his seeking absolution from everyone whom he harmed by his tongue, his hand, or his evil suspicion harbored in his heart — and this by winning their hearts' contentment — until he dies with no outstanding wrong against him, nor any neglected obligation.
6:38.section_title_en: The Perils of the Scale and the Reckoning of Wrongs Against Others
6:38.anchors:
- Root: وزن (w-z-n)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning is weighing, measuring, and balancing; al-mīzān (the Scale) is the instrument of equitable judgment.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In theological context, al-mīzān is the divine instrument of justice on the Day of Resurrection, weighing deeds to manifest equitable recompense, not a corporeal balance.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) usage denotes physical weighing; metaphorical (majāz) usage extends to moral and spiritual accounting, as in "weighing one's deeds by the scale of the Sacred Law."
- Sibawayh Rule: Conditional and Exceptive Constructions (الشّرط والاستثناء) — governing the protasis-apodosis structure in "whoever's scales are heavy... whoever's scales are light," and the exceptive force in "none is saved... except he who reckons."
6:38.topic: Al-Ghazali on the journey of the soul, death, and the Hereafter, from 'Remembrance of Death and Afterlife'

6:93.arabic: الله تعالى بين من افترى على الله كذبا وبين من كذب بالحق فقال تعالى ومن أظلم ممن افترى على الله كذبا أو كذب بالحق لما جاءه وقال تعالى فمن أظلم ممن كذب على الله وكذب بالصدق إذ جاءه ومنها الرياء وملاحظة الخلق والجهد في استمالة قلوبهم وصرف وجوههم والرياء هو الداء العضال الذي يدعو إلى أكبر الكبائر كما سيأتي في كتاب الرياء والمناظر لا يقصد إلا الظهور عند الخلق وانطلاق ألسنتهم بالثناء عليه فهذه عشر خصال من أمهات الفواحش الباطنة سوى ما يتفق لغير المتماسكين منهم من الخصام المؤدي إلى الضرب
6:93.english:
**QUAD_ANCHORS:**
- Root: نظر (naẓara)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to look, to examine, to consider; al-munāẓarah is mutual examination/argumentation between two parties.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: naẓar as intellectual contemplation (taʾammul bi-l-baṣīrah); munāẓarah as dialectical exchange.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: sitting face-to-face in debate; Metaphorical: disputation for victory.
- Root: غلب (ghalaba)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to overcome, to conquer, to prevail.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-ghalabah as seeking to dominate another in argument.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: victory in combat; Metaphorical: intellectual supremacy.
- Root: حسد (ḥasada)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to envy, to wish removal of blessings from another.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: envy as wishing deprivation of blessings from the deserving — among the basest traits.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: envy of another's blessing; Metaphorical: consuming fire of the soul.
- Root: كبر (kabura)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to be great, to be haughty.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-kibr as self-elevation above others; condemned by God.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: greatness; Metaphorical: arrogance and pride.
- Root: غيب (ghāba)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to be absent, to be hidden.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-ghībah as mentioning another with what he dislikes in his absence — likened to eating carrion.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: backbiting; Metaphorical: consuming the flesh of one's brother.
- Root: راءى (rāʾā)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to show off, to display.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-riyāʾ as performing acts for the sake of being seen — hidden shirk.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: showing good deeds; Metaphorical: seeking reputation.
- Root: نفس (nafs)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: self, soul, spirit.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: tazkiyat al-nafs as self-praise and self-purification — forbidden by God.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: self; Metaphorical: self-commendation.
- Root: حقd (ḥaqida)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to bear malice, to harbor resentment.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-ḥiqd as nursing enmity in the heart — negated from the believer.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: bearing grudge; Metaphorical: hidden rancor.
- Root: نفاق (nifāq)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: hypocrisy, showing contrary to what one conceals.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: hypocrisy in deeds — outward display contrary to inward state.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: hypocrisy in faith; Metaphorical: hypocrisy in character.
- Root: علم (ʿalima)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to know, to perceive.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: knowledge as apprehension of reality — its pursuit for other than God is destructive.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: knowledge; Metaphorical: the dangerous burden of the scholar.
- Root: جدل (jadala)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to argue, to dispute.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-jidāl as contention; al-mirāʾ as disputation with falsehood — condemned.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: argumentation; Metaphorical: obstinate disputation.
- Root: شرك (sharaka)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to associate, to share.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-riyāʾ as hidden shirk — associating others with God in intention.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: polytheism; Metaphorical: hidden association in deeds.
- Root: موت (māta)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to die.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: death as separation of soul from body; spiritual death as ruin of the soul.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical death; Metaphorical: spiritual destruction.
- Root: حيى (ḥayiya)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to live.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: life as the power of perception; eternal life as the reward of the righteous.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical life; Metaphorical: spiritual vitality.
- Root: هلك (halaka)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to perish, to be destroyed.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-halāk as ruin; eternal destruction as everlasting punishment.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: destruction; Metaphorical: eternal ruin.
- Root: رياء (riyāʾ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: showing off, ostentation.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: riyāʾ as the incurable disease calling to the greatest sins.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: ostentation; Metaphorical: spiritual disease.
- Root: جاه (jāh)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: rank, status, prestige.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: love of status (ḥubb al-jāh) among the destructive traits.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: position; Metaphorical: seeking prestige.
- Root: مباهاة (mubāhāh)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: mutual boasting, vying in splendor.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: mubāhāh as each seeking to display superiority over the other.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: mutual boasting; Metaphorical: rivalry in honor.
- Root: مماراة (mumārāh)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: disputation, wrangling.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-mirāʾ as contentious argument — condemned by the Prophet.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: disputation; Metaphorical: obstinate wrangling.
- Root: فخر (fakhara)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to boast, to pride oneself.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-fakhr as self-glorification — among the blameworthy traits.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: boasting; Metaphorical: vainglory.
- Root: عجب (ʿajiba)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to wonder, to be amazed.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-ʿujb as self-admiration — among the destructive traits.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: wonder; Metaphorical: self-conceit.
- Root: بغض (baghiḍa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to hate, to detest.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-baghdāʾ as mutual hatred — contrary to brotherhood.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: hatred; Metaphorical: mutual enmity.
- Root: غضب (ghaḍiba)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to be angry.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-ghaḍab as anger — among the blameworthy traits.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: anger; Metaphorical: rage.
- Root: طمع (ṭamiʿa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to covet, to desire.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-ṭamaʿ as covetousness — among the destructive traits.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: desire; Metaphorical: greed.
- Root: أشر (ashira)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to be exultant, to be insolent.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-ashar as excessive joy and insolence — blameworthy.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: exultation; Metaphorical: insolence.
- Root: بطر (baṭira)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to be arrogant, to be ungrateful.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-baṭar as arrogance in prosperity — among the destructive traits.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: arrogance; Metaphorical: ingratitude for blessings.
- Root: خيلاء (khuyalāʾ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: pride, haughtiness.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-khuyalāʾ as pride and conceit — blameworthy.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: pride; Metaphorical: haughty bearing.
- Root: خشية (khashyah)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: fear, awe.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-khashyah as reverential fear — among the traits of the believers.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: fear; Metaphorical: reverential awe.
- Root: رحمة (raḥmah)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: mercy, compassion.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-raḥmah as tenderness of heart — among the traits of the believers.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: mercy; Metaphorical: compassion.
- Root: غفلة (ghaflah)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: heedlessness, inattention.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-ghaflah as heedlessness — contrary to vigilance.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: inattention; Metaphorical: spiritual heedlessness.
- Root: خشوع (khushūʿ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: humility, submissiveness.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-khushūʿ as humility — among the traits of the believers.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: humility; Metaphorical: devotional submission.
- Root: تذكير (tadhkīr)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: reminding, admonishing.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-tadhkīr as reminding of God — a righteous act.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: reminding; Metaphorical: preaching.
- Root: وعظ (waʿaẓa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to admonish, to exhort.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-waʿẓ as exhortation to obedience and warning against disobedience.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: admonition; Metaphorical: sermonizing.
- Root: فتوى (fatwā)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: legal ruling, formal opinion.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-fatwā as clarification of legal rulings.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: legal opinion; Metaphorical: religious authority.
- Root: قضاء (qaḍāʾ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: judgment, decree.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-qaḍāʾ as judgment between people.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: judgment; Metaphorical: judicial authority.
- Root: وقف (waqafa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to stop, to stand.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-waqf as endowment of property for charitable purposes.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: standing; Metaphorical: religious endowment.
- Root: ثواب (thawāb)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: reward, recompense.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-thawāb as divine recompense for righteous deeds.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: reward; Metaphorical: divine recompense.
- Root: عذاب (ʿadhāb)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: punishment, torment.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-ʿadhāb as divine punishment for the disobedient.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: punishment; Metaphorical: divine chastisement.
- Root: ملك (malaka)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to possess, to rule.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-mulk as sovereignty; al-mulk al-muʾabbad as eternal sovereignty in Paradise.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: dominion; Metaphorical: eternal kingdom.
- Root: نعيم (naʿīm)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: bliss, delight.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-naʿīm as bliss; al-naʿīm al-sarmad as everlasting bliss.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: delight; Metaphorical: eternal bliss.
- Root: رخصة (rukhaṣah)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: concession, dispensation.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-rukhaṣah as legal concession.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: concession; Metaphorical: legal dispensation.
- Root: رياسة (riyāsah)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: leadership, headship.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: love of leadership among the destructive traits.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: leadership; Metaphorical: seeking authority.
- Root: اندراس (indirās)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: effacement, obliteration.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: indirās al-ʿulūm as the obliteration of the sciences.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: effacement; Metaphorical: extinction of knowledge.
- Root: صبيان (ṣibyān)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: boys, children.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: children's motivation for learning through play.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: boys; Metaphorical: pupils.
- Root: مكتب (maktab)
  * Lisan / Ayn- Root: مكتب (maktab)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: place of instruction, school for boys.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: the elementary school where children are taught.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: school; Metaphorical: place of elementary learning.
- Root: خلاق (khilāq)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: portion, share, lot.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: "no portion" (lā khilāq) in the Hereafter — utter deprivation of divine reward.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: share; Metaphorical: spiritual allotment in the afterlife.
- Root: فاجر (fājir)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: wicked, immoral, profligate.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: the dissolute one who commits sins openly.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: sinner; Metaphorical: one through whom God nonetheless supports religion.
- Root: شمع (shamʿ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: candle, wax taper.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: the candle as parable — consuming itself while giving light to others.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: candle; Metaphorical: one who destroys himself but benefits others.
- Root: نار (nār)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: fire.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: fire as parable — consuming itself and all around it.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: fire; Metaphorical: one who destroys himself and others.
- Root: سعد (saʿida)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to be fortunate, to prosper.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: saʿādah as felicity — success in the Hereafter.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: good fortune; Metaphorical: eternal felicity.
- Root: شقي (shaqiya)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to be wretched, to be miserable.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: shaqāwah as wretchedness — ruin in the Hereafter.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: misery; Metaphorical: eternal ruin.
- Root: أخلص (akhlaṣa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to purify, to be sincere.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: ikhlāṣ as purifying intention for God alone — the condition of acceptance.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: sincerity; Metaphorical: pure devotion.
- Root: ريب (rāba)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to doubt, to suspect.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-rayb as doubt and uncertainty — to be dispelled by evidence.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: doubt; Metaphorical: skepticism.
6:93.topic: Al-Ghazali on purifying the character, moral diseases, and spiritual remedies, from 'Book of Knowledge'

6:93.arabic: أيديهم إلى قوله وكنتم عن آياته تستكبرون {ثم قال} ادخلوا أبواب جنهنم خالدين فيها فبئس مثوى المتكبرين ثم أخبر أن أشد أهل النار عذابا أشدهم عتيا على الله تعالى فقال ثم لننزعن من كل شيعة أيهم أشد على الرحمن عتيا وقال تعالى فالذين لا يؤمنون بالآخرة قلوبهم منكرة وهم مستكبرون وقال عز وجل يقول الذين استضعفوا للذين استكبروا لولا أنتم لكنا مؤمنين وقال تعالى إن الذين يستكبرون عن عبادتي سيدخلون جهنم داخرين وقال تعالى سأصرف عن آياتي الذين يتكبرون في الأرض بغير الحق قيل في التفسير سأرفع فهم القرآن عن قل
6:93.english: When this [pride] appears upon the bodily limbs, it is called "behaving arrogantly" (takabbur); and when it does not appear [outwardly], it is said that in his soul there is pride (kibr). The root [of the matter] is the moral trait (khuluq) that resides in the soul — namely, the soul's taking comfort and repose in seeing itself as above the one over whom it acts proudly. For pride necessarily requires an object over whom one is proud and a quality by virtue of which one is proud; and by this [requirement], pride is distinguished from self-conceit ('ujb), as will come later. For self-conceit does not require an object other than the self-conceited one. Indeed, were a human being created alone, it is conceivable that he would be self-conceited, but it is not conceivable that he would be proud except when there is another alongside him, and he sees himself as above that other in the attributes of perfection. Only at that point does he become proud. Nor is it sufficient that he deem himself great in order to be proud — for a man may deem himself great yet see another as greater than himself or equal to himself, and so he does not act proudly toward him. Nor is it sufficient that he hold another in contempt — for even so, if he saw himself as more contemptible [than that other], he would not be proud; and if he saw the other as his equal, he would not be proud. Rather, he must assign to himself a rank and to the other a rank, then see his own rank as above the other's rank. Upon these three beliefs, the trait of pride comes to be in him. It is not that this perception alone negates pride; rather, this perception and this conviction blow into him [a wind of vanity], and there arises in his heart self-complacency, a thrill, joy, and repose in what he has come to believe, and a sense of vainglory in himself on account of that. That vainglory, that thrill, and that repose in the belief — that is the trait of pride. For this reason, the Prophet — God's peace and blessings be upon him — said: "I seek refuge in You from the puff of pride (nafkhat al-kibriyā')." And the hadith has preceded: "None shall enter Paradise who has in his heart the weight of a mustard seed of pride."
6:93.section_title_en: The Reality of Pride (Kibr) and Its Manifestation in the Soul and Limbs
6:93.anchors:
- Root: كبر (K-B-R)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of bigness, greatness, and seniority in age or rank; al-Farahidi notes its use for physical growth and maturity.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الكبير والصغير من الأسماء المتضايفة" — great and small are relative terms, applied by comparison; in Kalam, pride (kibr) is a state of the soul that esteems itself above another in perfection.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): "كبر الأمر، وخطب كبير" — to be great in magnitude. Metaphorical (Majaz): "كبر عليه" — to find something burdensome or grievous; the moral-spiritual sense of kibr is a metaphorical extension of physical magnitude to the soul's self-assessment.
- Root: نفس (N-F-S)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The self, soul, or spirit; that which animates and is the seat of inner states.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "النفس: الروح" — the soul; also the very essence (al-dhat), as in "ويحذركم الله نفسه" {آل عمران/ 30}, where His "self" is His essence.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "شيء نفيس" — precious thing. Metaphorical: "دفق نفسه أي دمه" — "his self" for "his blood"; here, the soul's inner disposition (khuluq) is the locus where pride takes root before it appears on the limbs.
- Root: وفي (W-F-Y)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Completeness, fulfillment, and reaching full measure.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الوافي: الذي بلغ التمام" — that which attains completion; "أوفى بعهده" — to fulfill one's covenant fully.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "درهم واف" — a full-weight dirham. Metaphorical: "أوفى على المائة" — to exceed a hundred; in this text, the "full measure of a mustard seed" (مثقال ذرة) of pride is the complete, realized quantity that bars one from Paradise.
- Root: خلق (Kh-L-Q)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Measuring, shaping, and fashioning; also innate disposition and moral character.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الخلق أصله: التقدير المستقيم" — its root is right measure and estimation; used for God's origination of things and for the moral constitution of the soul.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "خلق الخراز الأديم" — the leatherworker measures the hide before cutting. Metaphorical: "خلق الله الخلق" — God originated creation upon a measure dictated by wisdom; hence khuluq is the soul's fixed moral form.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction and Focused Predication) — used to delimit the precise definition of kibr as a specific soul-state distinct from 'ujb (self-conceit), and to restrict the cause of exclusion from Paradise to the presence of pride in the heart.
6:93.topic: Al-Ghazali on the journey of the soul, death, and the Hereafter, from 'Condemnation of Pride and Conceit'

6:93.arabic: التهلكة ولا يتمنى على الله غير الحق فإن حفظت وصيتي هذه فلا يكون غائب أحب إليك من الموت ولا بد لك منه وإن ضيعت وصيتي فلا يكون غائب أبغض إليك من الموت ولا بد لك منه ولست بمعجزه وقال سعيد بن المسيب لما احتضر أبو بكر رضي الله عنه أتاه ناس من الصحابة فقالوا يا خليفة رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم زودنا فإنا نراك لما بك فقالوا أبو بكر من قال هؤلاء الكلمات ثم مات جعل الله روحه في الأفق المبين قالوا وما الأفق المبين قال قاع بين يديالعرش فيه رياض الله وأنهار وأشجار يغشاه كل يوم ما
6:93.english: When Abu Bakr (may Allah Most High be pleased with him) was in the throes of death, ʿĀʾishah (may Allah be pleased with her) came and recited this verse: "By your life, wealth avails not the youth... when the breath rattles in his chest one day, and the breast is straitened thereby."
6:93.section_title_en: The Death of Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (may Allah Most High be pleased with him)
6:93.anchors:
- Root: حشرج (ḥashraja)
  * Lisan / Ayn: [Core linguistic root meaning: The rattling, gurgling sound of the death-throe in the throat; the final breath struggling in the chest.]
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): [Theological/Kalam semantic nuance: The terminal state of the soul's separation from the body, the moment of overwhelming divine decree.]
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): [Literal vs Metaphorical distinction: Literal — the physical rattle of the dying; Metaphorical — the constriction of the breast as the soul is drawn forth.]
- Root: سكر (sakara)
  * Lisan / Ayn: [Core linguistic root meaning: The veiling of the intellect; intoxication; the stupor that overcomes one at the onset of death.]
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): [Theological/Kalam semantic nuance: The stupor of death (sakrat al-mawt) as the removal of all veils, wherein the truth of the Hereafter becomes undeniably present.]
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): [Literal vs Metaphorical distinction: Literal — intoxication from drink; Metaphorical — the overwhelming bewilderment of the soul at death's onset.]
- Root: ذمم (dhimam)
  * Lisan / Ayn: [Core linguistic root meaning: The covenant of protection; the bond of safe-conduct; that which one is obligated to honor and safeguard.]
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): [Theological/Kalam semantic nuance: The divine guarantee (dhimmat Allah) extended to the believer who prays the dawn prayer — a sacred pact not to be violated.]
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): [Literal vs Metaphorical distinction: Literal — a pledge of security between men; Metaphorical — the inviolable covenant between the servant and his Lord.]
- Root: وزن (wazana)
  * Lisan / Ayn: [Core linguistic root meaning: To weigh; the balance; the measure of equivalence between two things.]
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): [Theological/Kalam semantic nuance: The weighing of deeds on the Day of Resurrection as the manifestation of divine justice — the scales (mawāzīn) receiving only truth or falsehood.]
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): [Literal vs Metaphorical distinction: Literal — the physical act of weighing; Metaphorical — the spiritual weighing of deeds by their conformity to truth (ḥaqq) or falsehood (bāṭil).]
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — [The particle innamā restricts the predicate exclusively to its subject, as in Abu Bakr's dictum: "It is only that the scales of those whose scales are heavy on the Day of Resurrection are weighed down by their following the truth in this world."]
6:93.topic: Al-Ghazali on the journey of the soul, death, and the Hereafter, from 'Remembrance of Death and Afterlife'

6:94.arabic: يقال ولقد جئتمونا فرادى كما خلقناكم أول مرة وفيها يقال كفى بنفسك اليوم عليك حسيبا أما في القيامة الكبرى الجامعة لكافة الخلائق فلا يكون وحده بل ربما يحاسب على ملأ من الخلق وفيها يساق المتقون إلى الجنة والمجرمون إلى النار زمرا لا آحادا والهول الأول هو هول القيامة الصغرى ولجميع أهوال القيامة الكبرى نظير في القيامة الصغرى مثل زلزلة الأرض مثلا فإن أرضك الخاصة بك تزلزل في الموت فإنك تعلم أن الزلزلة إذا نزلت ببلدة صدق أن يقال قد زلزلت أرضهم وإن لم تزلزل البلاد المحيطة بها بل لو زلزل مسكن الإنسا
6:94.english: As for the noble ones (al-kirām), it is because of the servant's benefit from their nobility, and because all the angels are noble and righteous (kirām bararah). As for the two writers (al-kātibān), it is for the recording of the good deeds and the evil deeds. They write only upon scrolls folded within the secret of the heart (sirr al-qalb) and folded away from the secret of the heart, so that no one may behold them in this world. For verily, they, their writings, their script, their pages, and the totality of what pertains to them belong to the unseen world and the dominion of sovereignty (ʿālam al-ghayb wa al-malakūt), not to the world of sensory witness (ʿālam al-shahādah). And everything belonging to the world of sovereignty (al-malakūt) is imperceptible to corporeal eyes in this world. Then these scrolls, folded away from him, are unfolded twice: once at the minor resurrection (al-qiyāmah al-ṣughrā) and once at the major resurrection (al-qiyāmah al-kubrā). By the minor resurrection I mean the state of death, for the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: "Whoever has died, his resurrection has indeed come to pass" {«من مات فقد قامت قيامته»}. In this resurrection, the servant is alone, and at that time it is said: {«وَلَقَدْ جِئْتُمُونَا فُرَادَىٰ كَمَا خَلَقْنَاكُمْ أَوَّلَ مَرَّةٍ»} ("And indeed you have come to Us alone, just as We created you the first time") — and in it, it is said: {«كَفَىٰ بِنَفْسِكَ الْيَوْمَ عَلَيْكَ حَسِيبًا»} ("Sufficient is your own soul this day as a reckoner against you"). As for the major resurrection, which gathers all of creation, he is not alone therein; rather, he may be reckoned before a multitude of creatures, and in it the God-fearing are driven to Paradise and the criminals to the Fire in groups (zumar), not as individuals. The first great terror is the terror of the minor resurrection, and for all the terrors of the major resurrection there is a counterpart in the minor resurrection — such as the earthquake of the earth, for example. For your own particular earth quakes at death, since you know that when an earthquake descends upon a town, it is truly said that "their earth has quaked," even if the surrounding lands have not quaked. Nay, even if only a man's dwelling quakes, the earthquake has occurred relative to him, because he is harmed by the quaking of the entire earth only through the quaking of his own dwelling, not through the quaking of another's dwelling. Thus his share of the earthquake has been fully realized without any diminution. Know that you are an earth created from dust, and your particular share of the dust is only your body. As for the body of another, it is not your share. The earth upon which you sit, in relation to your body, is but a vessel and a place. You fear its quaking only because your body might quake on account of it; otherwise, the air is perpetually in motion and you do not dread it, since your body does not quake because of it. So your share of the earthquake of the entire earth is only the quaking of your body — it is your earth and your particular dust. Your bones are the mountains of your earth; your head is the sky of your earth; your heart is the sun of your earth; your hearing, your sight, and the rest of your faculties are the stars of your sky; the outpouring of sweat from your body is the sea of your earth; your hair is the vegetation of your earth; your limbs are the trees of your earth; and so on to all of your parts. When the pillars of your body collapse through death, then the earth has quaked with its quaking {«إِذَا زُلْزِلَتِ الْأَرْضُ زِلْزَالَهَا»}. When the bones separate from the flesh, then the earth has borne its burdens and the mountains have been crushed to powder {«وَحُمِلَتِ الْأَرْضُ وَالْجِبَالُ فَدُكَّتَا دَكَّةً وَاحِدَةً»}. When the bones crumble, then the mountains have been blown away as dust {«وَنُسِفَتِ الْجِبَالُ نَسْفًا»}. When your heart darkens at death, then the sun has been folded up {«كُوِّرَتِ الشَّمْسُ تَكْوِيرًا»}. When your hearing, sight, and all your senses cease, then the stars have been scattered {«وَانْكَدَرَتِ النُّجُومُ انْكِدَارًا»}. When your brain splits, then the sky has been split asunder {«انْشَقَّتِ السَّمَاءُ انْشِقَاقًا»}. When the sweat of your brow bursts forth from the terror of death, then the seas have been caused to burst forth {«فُجِّرَتِ الْبِحَارُ تَفْجِيرًا»}. When one of your legs entwines with the other — and they are your two mounts — then the pregnant she-camels have been neglected {«عُطِّلَتِ الْعِشَارُ تَعْطِيلًا»}. When the soul departs from the body, then the earth has been lifted and stretched until it casts out what is within it and empties itself {«وَأَلْقَتْ مَا فِيهَا وَتَخَلَّتْ»}. I shall not prolong the enumeration of all the corresponding states and terrors, but I say: by mere death, this minor resurrection comes to pass over you, and nothing of the major resurrection that pertains specifically to you escapes you — rather, only what pertains to another escapes you. For what benefit is the survival of the stars to another, when your senses — through which you benefited by gazing at the stars — have been scattered? The blind man finds night and day equal, and the eclipse of the sun and its clearing likewise, for the sun has been eclipsed for him all at once — that being his share of it — while its clearing thereafter is the share of another. And he whose head has been split open has had his sky split, for the sky is but an expression for what lies in the direction of the head; so whoever has no head has no sky — whence, then, would the survival of the sky for another benefit him? This, then, is the minor resurrection; and the fear after it is greater, and the terror after it is deferred — that is when the Great Calamity arrives {«الطَّامَّةُ الْكُبْرَىٰ»}, particularity is lifted, the heavens and the earth are abolished, the mountains are blown away, and the terrors multiply.
6:94.section_title_en: The Minor Resurrection: The Microcosmic Earthquake of Death
6:94.anchors:
- Root: كرم (karuma)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root meaning of nobility, generosity, and honor; al-kirām are those distinguished by noble character and beneficence.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: karāmah denotes the honor bestowed by Allah upon His angels and righteous servants, entailing both dignity and generous bestowal.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): noble, generous in character; Metaphorical (Majaz): the angels described as kirām because of their exalted station and pure obedience, not corporeal nobility.
- Root: كتب (kataba)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To write, inscribe, decree; kitāb as a written record; kataba as the act of fixing something in a permanent form.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-kātibūn are the recording angels (ḥafaẓah) who inscribe deeds; writing here signifies divine preservation of acts in a register accessible to Allah alone.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical inscription on sheets; Metaphorical: the "writing" upon the heart's secret core is an immaterial imprinting (naqsh rūḥānī) imperceptible to corporeal sight.
- Root: موت (mawta)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Death as cessation of animal life; the separation of the soul from the body.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-mawt is not annihilation but a transition (intiqlāl) from one abode to another; the minor resurrection (al-qiyāmah al-ṣughrā) is the individual's death, as per the prophetic saying.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: biological death; Metaphorical: "whoever dies, his resurrection has come to pass" — the term qiyāmah is transferred (majāz) to the moment of death because the full unveiling of one's deeds begins then.
- Root: زلزل (zalzala)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Violent shaking, earthquake; intense agitation of the earth.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: the earthquake is a cosmic sign of divine power; in the microcosm, the death-throes of the body are the individual's own "earthquake."
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: seismic tremor of the earth; Metaphorical: the dissolution of one's own body is a true earthquake relative to that person, since only his own frame is his "earth" — the rest of the globe is another's concern.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب التشبيه والتمثيل (Analogy and Proportional Correspondence) — The syntactic structure equates parts of the human microcosm with the macrocosmic phenomena of the Hour, using fa- (consequence) clauses to map each bodily dissolution to its corresponding cosmic portent.
6:94.topic: Al-Ghazali on the journey of the soul, death, and the Hereafter, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

6:94.arabic: المؤمنين قال أجدني كما قال الله تعالى {ولقد جئتمونا فرادى كما خلقناكم أول مرة وتركتم ما خولناكم وراء ظهوركم} الآية ومات وقالت فاطمة بنت عبد الملك بن مروان امرأة عمر بن عبد العزيز كنت أسمع عمر في مرضه الذي مات فيه يقول اللهم أخف عليهم موتي ولو ساعة من نهار فلما كان اليوم الذي قبض فيه خرجت من عنده فجلست في بيت آخر بيني وبينه باب وهو في قبة له فسمعته يقول {تلك الدار الآخرة نجعلها للذين لا يريدون علوا في الأرض ولا فسادا والعاقبة للمتقين} ثم هدا فجعلت لا أسمع حركة ولا كلاما فقلت لوصيف له انظر أنائم هو فلما دخل صاح فوثبت فإذا هو ميت وقيل له لما حضره الموت أ
6:94.english: I say: Know that when death came to Muʿāwiyah ibn Abī Sufyān, he said, "Seat me upright." So they seated him, and he began to glorify God Almighty and remember Him. Then he wept and said, "Do you remember your Lord, O Muʿāwiyah, only after decrepitude and decline? Should this not have been while the branch of youth was fresh and verdant?" And he wept until his weeping grew loud, then said, "O Lord, have mercy on the sinful elder, the possessor of the hard heart. O Allah, overlook the misstep and forgive the slip, and repay with Your forbearance the one who hopes in none but You and trusts in none other than You."
6:94.section_title_en: The Fifth Chapter: On the Deathbed Utterances of the Caliphs, Princes, and the Righteous
6:94.anchors:
- Root: حضر (ḥaḍara)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of presence, attendance, or arrival at a place or time.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Often used for the arrival of an inevitable event, especially death (ḥuḍūr al-mawt), marking a temporal threshold.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal for physical presence; metaphorical for the onset of an inescapable decree.
- Root: عهد (ʿahida)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To covenant, to be charged with a trust, to make a bequest.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Implies a binding injunction, often divine or paternal, that outlasts the speaker.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal for a written pact; metaphorical for the final counsel of the dying.
- Root: وتر (watara)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To make single, to sever, to deprive; also odd-numbered.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In the passive (wutirat), signifies being left bereft or defrauded of one's due.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal for cutting off; metaphorical for the world's betrayal and stripping of its gifts.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — Governs the permissible separation of a preposition from its object for rhetorical emphasis, as seen in the dying men's abrupt, heartfelt exclamations.
6:94.topic: Al-Ghazali on the journey of the soul, death, and the Hereafter, from 'Remembrance of Death and Afterlife'

6:111.arabic: ولا تقولن لشيء إني فاعل ذلك غدا إلا أن يشاء الله ثم لم يقتصر على ذلك فيما لا يشك فيه بل قال تعالى لتدخلن المسجد الحرام إن شاء الله آمنين محلقين رءؤسكم ومقصرين وكان الله سبحانه عالما بأنهم يدخلون لا محالة وأنه شاءه ولكن المقصود تعليمه ذلك فتأدب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في ما كان يخبر عنه معلوما كان أو مشكوكا حتى قال صلى الله عليه وسلم لما دخل المقابر السلام عليكم دار قوم مؤمنين وإنا إن شاء الله بكم لاحقون (1) واللحوق بهم غير مشكوك فيه ولكن مقتضى الأدب ذكر الله تعالى وربط الأمور به وهذه الصيغ
6:111.english: If you say: "What is the meaning of the Salaf's statement, 'I am a believer, if God wills' — given that the exception (istithnā') implies doubt, and doubt in faith is unbelief? Yet they all refrained from giving an unqualified answer affirming faith and were cautious about it."
6:111.section_title_en: On the Meaning of the Salaf's Statement "I am a Believer, If God Wills" — Section 102
6:111.anchors:
- Root: نفس (n-f-s)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The self, the soul; that which is breathed; the innermost reality of a person.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): النفس is used for the rūḥ (spirit), for the dhāt (essence/self), and for the seat of intention and knowledge. When one says "he knows in himself (nafsihi) that he is a believer," it denotes certitude residing in the very core of one's being, not a corporeal faculty.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) usage refers to the soul's reflexive self-awareness; metaphorical (majāz) usage extends to "blood" (dam) or "the eye" (ʿayn) of envy. Here, "in himself" (fī nafsihi) is literal self-knowledge, not mere outward profession.
- Root: وجه (w-j-h)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Face, countenance; the foremost part; a mode, aspect, or direction.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The face is the most noble apparent part of a thing; hence it is used for the "aspect" or "manner" (wajh) of an affair. "Four aspects" (wujūh) means four distinct modes of interpretation or rational grounds.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the face of a person or object. Metaphorical: "the face of the matter" (wajh al-amr) — its most salient and honorable dimension. Here, the "aspects" are hermeneutical angles, not physical parts.
- Root: ايم (a-y-m)
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The unmarried state (aym); one who has no spouse. Not applicable here directly, but the root's semantic field of "being alone/without attachment" contrasts with īmān's root (a-m-n) — security and trust — which is the operative term in this text.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Not directly relevant; the operative root is أمن (a-m-n), meaning security from fear, and by extension, faith (īmān) as the state of being secure in God's truth.
- Root: كان (k-w-n)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To be, to exist; the copula of predication.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Kāna denotes existence and becoming; in theological usage, it grounds the distinction between what is (mawjūd) and what is merely asserted. The question "Are you a believer?" (a-mu'min anta?) uses kāna implicitly to ask about actual, present state — not future contingency.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: existence. Metaphorical: the "being-so" of a predicate. The istithnā' (exception) with "in shā' Allāh" suspends the copula's certainty, shifting from assertive existence to contingent hope.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الاستثناء والتعليق بالمشيئة (The Chapter of Exception and Suspension by the Divine Will) — When an exception clause (istithnā') follows a positive assertion, it grammatically suspends the universality or certainty of the predication. In theological discourse, this suspension may be semantic (doubt) or pragmatic (deference, etiquette, or self-deprecation), and Sibawayh's parsing of conditional suspension (taʿlīq) shows that the apodosis need not be negated — only its absolute, unqualified force is tempered.
6:111.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Remembrance of Death and Afterlife'

6:128.arabic: علامات المرض وبهذا يعرف أن القلوب كلها مريضة إلا ما شاء الله إلا أن من الأمراض ما لا يعرفها صاحبها ومرض القلب مما لا يعرفه صاحبه فلذلك يغفل عنه وإن عرفه صعب عليه الصبر على مرارة دوائه فإن دواءه مخالفة الشهوات وهو نزع الروح فإن وجد من نفسه قوة الصبر عليه لم يجد طبيبا حاذقا يعالجه فإن الأطباء هم العلماء وقد استولى عليهم المرض فالطبيب المريض قلما يلتفت إلى علاجه فلهذا صار الداء عضالا والمرض مزمنا واندرس هذا العلم وأنكر بالكلية طب القلوب وأنكر مرضها وأقبل الخلق على حب الدنيا وعلى أعمال ظاهرها عبادات وباطنها
6:128.english: I say: The soul (nafs) that belongs to the human being — that by which he is distinguished from the beasts — for he is not distinguished from them by the power of eating, copulation, sight, or any other such thing. Rather, he is distinguished by the knowledge of things as they truly are. And the Origin of all things, their Existentiator and their Inventor, is God, Mighty and Majestic — He who made them things. So if one knew everything but did not know God, Mighty and Majestic, it would be as though he knew nothing at all. And the sign of knowledge is love: whoever knows God Most High loves Him. And the sign of love is that one does not prefer over Him this world nor any other beloved thing. As God Most High said: {«Say: If your fathers, your sons, your brothers, your spouses, your clans — the wealth you have acquired, commerce whose decline you fear, and dwellings you find pleasing — are more beloved to you than God and His Messenger and striving in His cause, then wait until God brings about His command»} [Q 9:24]. So whoever possesses something more beloved to him than God — his heart is sick. Just as any stomach to which clay has become more beloved than bread and water, or whose appetite for bread and water has fallen away — it is sick. These are the signs of sickness. And by this it is known that all hearts are sick — except what God wills. Yet among sicknesses there are those the sufferer does not recognize; and the sickness of the heart is among those the sufferer does not recognize. For this reason he is heedless of it. And even if he recognized it, patience upon the bitterness of its medicine would be difficult for him — for its medicine is opposing the appetites, and that is the tearing out of the spirit (nafs). And if he found in himself the strength of patience upon it, he would not find a skillful physician to treat him — for the physicians are the scholars, and sickness has overcome them. So the sick physician rarely attends to his own cure. For this reason the malady has become chronic and the sickness chronic. This science has become effaced, and the medicine of hearts is denied entirely, and the sickness of the heart is denied. And creation has turned to the love of this world and to deeds whose outward form is acts of worship but whose inward reality is habit and ostentation. These are the signs of the roots of sicknesses.
6:128.section_title_en: The Soul's Distinction, the Sickness of the Heart, and the Path of Moderation
6:128.anchors:
- Root: نفس (n-f-s)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The self, soul, or spirit; that by which a thing is distinguished in its essential reality
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The soul (nafs) as the principle of rational discrimination and knowledge, distinguishing humans from beasts
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the self or person; Metaphorical: the rational soul as the seat of knowledge and moral responsibility
- Root: مرض (m-r-d)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Departure from the state of health and equilibrium
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Sickness of the heart as a metaphor for moral and spiritual vices — ignorance, cowardice, avarice, hypocrisy
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: bodily illness; Metaphorical: spiritual malady whereby the heart inclines toward what is harmful and away from what is beneficial
- Root: قلب (q-l-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The heart; that which is ever-turning and fluctuating between states
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The heart as the seat of understanding and moral perception; its "turning" (taqlīb) signifies its instability between soundness and sickness
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the physical organ; Metaphorical: the spiritual faculty of cognition and moral discernment
- Root: خلق (kh-l-q)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Measured, proportioned disposition; character and temperament
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Moral character as the inward form (ṣūrah bāṭinah) corresponding to the outward physical form
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: measuring and proportioning; Metaphorical: the ingrained disposition that governs action
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — The use of restrictive constructions to isolate the defining characteristic of the human soul as knowledge of God, not animal appetites
6:128.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Remembrance of Death and Afterlife'

6:129.arabic: أولياء وقال تعالى وكذلك نولي بعض الظالمين بعضا وفي الخبر إن الله تعالى أخذ الميثاق على كل مؤمن أن يبغض كل منافق وعلى كل منافق أن يبغض كل مؤمن (3) وقال عليه السلام المرء مع من أحب (4) وقال من أحب قوما ووالاهم حشر معهم يوم القيامة (5) وقال عليه السلام أوثق عرى الإيمان الحب في الله والبغض في الله (6) وشواهد هذا قد ذكرناها في بيان الحب والبغض في الله تعالى من كتاب آداب الصحبة وفي كتاب الأمر بالمعروف والنهي عن المنكر فلا نعيده فإن قلت فقد وردت الآيات والأخبار بالرضا بقضاء الله تعالى (7) فإن كانت المعاصي بغير
6:129.english: ...as a partner in his killing. And God—exalted be He—has commanded envy and competition in good things and the warding off of evils, for He said—exalted be He—{وَفِي ذَٰلِكَ فَلْيَتَنَافَسِ الْمُتَنَافِسُونَ} ["So for this let the competitors compete"] (Al-Muṭaffifīn 83:26). And the Prophet—peace be upon him—said: "There is no envy except in two: a man whom God has given wisdom, and he disseminates it among the people and teaches it; and a man whom God has given wealth, and he has been empowered over it to spend it in the truth." In another wording: "And a man whom God has given the Qur'an, and he stands with it through the hours of the night and the day; then a man says: 'If God had given me the like of what He gave this one, I would have done the like of what he does.'"
6:129.section_title_en: On the Reconciliation Between Hatred of Sinners and Satisfaction with Divine Decree — Section 1196
6:129.anchors:
- Root: بغض (b-gh-d)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root meaning of aversion, repugnance, and the soul's flight from what it disdains; al-baghḍā' as intense enmity.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "البغض: نفار النفس عن الشيء الذي ترغب عنه، وهو ضد الحب" — hatred is the soul's aversion from what it shuns, the exact opposite of love's attraction; used theologically for God's repudiation of the disobedient.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) usage denotes personal antipathy; metaphorical (majāz) extension applies to religiously mandated aversion (al-bughḍ fī Allāh) as an act of devotion, not private spite.
- Root: وجه (w-j-h)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The face as the foremost and noblest part; by extension, an aspect, direction, or respect under which a thing is considered.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "ولما كان الوجه أول ما يستقبلك، وأشرف ما في ظاهر البدن استعمل في مستقبل كل شيء" — the face is that which first confronts you, hence used for every aspect or angle of consideration.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the bodily face; metaphorical: "هذا وجه الثوب" (the face/right side of a garment) — i.e., a facet or dimension of a single act that may be evaluated differently.
- Root: كره (k-r-h)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Dislike, detestation, and unwillingness; karāhah as the soul's resistance to what befalls it.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Karāhah is the soul's repugnance toward something, distinguished from ridā (satisfaction) which is the soul's acquiescence and embrace.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): The rhetorical key here is that karāhah and ridā are contraries only when they "تواردا على شيء واحد من جهة واحدة" — converge on one thing from one single respect; from different respects, no contradiction arises.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — The resolution of the apparent contradiction hinges on precise restriction (taqyīd): the act is hated "من حيث إنه وصف العبد وكسبه" (insofar as it is the servant's attribute and acquisition) and loved "من حيث إنه مراد الله" (insofar as it is God's will and decree). The predicate is qualified by its aspect, eliminating the logical clash.
6:129.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Remembrance of Death and Afterlife'

6:134.arabic: بني آدم إن كنتم تعقلون فعدوا أنفسكم من الموتى والذي نفسي بيده إن ما توعدون لآت وما أنتم بمعجزين (3) وعن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما إن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كان يخرج يهريق الماء فيتمسح بالتراب فأقول له يا رسول الله إن الماء منك قريب فيقول ما يدريني لعلي لا أبلغه (4) والبزاز بسند ضعيف وروي أنه صلى الله عليه وسلم أخذ ثلاثة أعواد فغرز عودا بين يديه والآخر إلى جنبه وأما الثالث فأبعده فقال هل تدرون ما هذا قالوا الله ورسوله أعلم قال هذا الإنسان وهذا الأجل وذاك الأمل يتعاطاه ابن آدم ويختلجه الأجل دون الأمل (5) وقال عليه السلام مثل ابن آدم وإلى
6:134.english: The Messenger of God, may God's blessings and peace be upon him, said to ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar: "When you reach the morning, do not speak to yourself of the evening; and when you reach the evening, do not speak to yourself of the morning. Take from your life for your death, and from your health for your sickness. For you, O ʿAbd Allāh, do not know what your name will be tomorrow." {«إذا أصبحت فلا تحدث نفسك بالمساء وإذا أمسيت فلا تحدث نفسك بالصباح وخذ من حياتك لموتك ومن صحتك لسقمك فإنك يا عبد الله لا تدري ما اسمك غدا»}
6:134.section_title_en: The Cutting of Hope (Qaṣr al-Amal) — Section 1286
6:134.anchors:
- Root: أمل (amal)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الأمل: رجاء الشيء وتوقع حصوله، والأمل: امتداد النفس في طلب الخير المستقبل؛ ومنه قولهم: أَمَلَ يَأْمُلُ أَمْلاً، وهو تمديد النظر إلى ما يُستبعد حصوله."
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الأمل: توقع حصول الأمر المستقبل، وهو مذموم إذا جاوز الحد المشروع لأنه يلهي عن الاستعداد للآخرة؛ والأجل: غاية العمر المضروب، والفرق بينهما أن الأجل محتوم والأمل ممدود."
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "Literal (Haqiqah): الأمل تمديد النفس إلى بلوغ المراد. Metaphorical (Majaz): طول الأمل كناية عن الغفلة عن قرب الأجل والانكباب على الدنيا، وقصر الأمل عبارة عن الاستعداد للموت والزهد."
- Root: أجل (ajal)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الأجل: غاية الوقت في الموت وغيره، والأجل المسمى: الوقت المضروب لانقضاء العمر."
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الأجل: مدة الشيء المضروبة لانتهائه، وأجل الإنسان: الوقت الذي ينتهي فيه عمره، وهو بيد الله وحده."
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "Literal: الأجل نهاية العمر المحتومة. Metaphorical: جعل الأجل محيطًا بالإنسان كالخط المحيط بالمركز."
- Root: مني (munya)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "المنية: الموت، وأصلها من التمني لأن الموت يتمنى أو لأنه مقدر مكتوب."
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "المنية: الموت المحتوم، وجمعها منايا، وهي الآفات المهلكة التي تترصد الإنسان."
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — Used in the prophetic statement "إنما يلقاك غدا ندمك" to restrict the outcome exclusively to regret, and "إنما يكون الأمان غدا لمن خاف واتقى" to confine safety solely to the God-fearing.
6:134.topic: Al-Ghazali on the journey of the soul, death, and the Hereafter, from 'Remembrance of Death and Afterlife'

7:6.arabic: وعند ذلك يصدق الله تعالى قوله {فلنسألن الذين أرسل إليهم ولنسألن المرسلين فلنقصن عليهم بعلم وما كنا غائبين} وقوله {فوربك لنسألنهم أجمعين عما كانوا يعملون} فيبدأ سبحانه بالأنبياء {يوم يجمع الله الرسل فيقول}
7:6.english: Then reflect, O wretched one, after these states upon what is directed against you of the questioning — face to face, without any interpreter — and you shall be asked concerning the little and the much, the speck on a date-stone (al-naqīr) and the husk (al-qitmīr). For while you are amidst the distress of the Resurrection, its sweat, and the severity of its terrors, lo! the angels descend from the horizons of the heaven with immense bodies and gigantic forms — harsh, severe — commanded to seize the forelocks of the criminals and drag them to the standing-place of presentation (mawqif al-ʿarḍ) before the Omnipotent (al-Jabbār). The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: "Verily, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has an angel between whose two eyelids is a distance of a hundred years' journey." So what is your assumption concerning yourself when you behold the likes of these angels — dispatched unto you to seize you and bring you to the station of presentation — and you see them, despite the enormity of their forms, broken in humility before the severity of that Day, filled with dread at what has become manifest of the Omnipotent's wrath upon His servants? And at their descent, there remains no prophet, no veracious one (ṣiddīq), no righteous soul, save that they fall upon their chins in fear, lest they themselves be the seized ones. Such is the state of those brought near (al-muqarrabūn) — so what is your assumption concerning the disobedient criminals?
7:6.section_title_en: The Description of the Day of Resurrection, Its Calamities, and Its Names — The Description of the Questioning
7:6.anchors:
- Root: س-أ-ل (sa-ʾa-la)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root denotes seeking, demanding, or interrogating; al-suʾāl is the act of asking, and musāʾalah implies reciprocal or formal interrogation.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In theological context, al-suʾāl on the Day of Resurrection is a divine inquest (musāʾalah) demanding account of deeds, not for God's knowledge (as He is 'alīm) but for establishing proof (ḥujjah) against the creature.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) usage is verbal inquiry; metaphorical (majāz) extends to the juridical reckoning (muḥāsabah) where the tongue is made to testify without intermediary.
- Root: ن-ز-ل (na-za-la)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root signifies descent from a height; nuzūl is the act of alighting.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): When predicated of angels, it denotes their dispatch from the celestial realm to execute divine command — a descent of authority, not spatial movement in the divine essence.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical descent; metaphorical: the advent of divine decree or angelic execution of wrath.
- Root: ع-ر-ض (ʿa-ra-ḍa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root means to present, expose, or show; al-ʿarḍ is the exhibition of something before a viewer.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In eschatological usage, mawqif al-ʿarḍ is the standing-place of presentation before God for judgment — a public display of deeds.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: to show; metaphorical: the juridical tribunal of the Hereafter where all acts are exhibited.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Interrogative Scope (Bāb al-istifhām) — The rhetorical question "فما ظنك" (so what is your assumption?) functions as a periodic pause, redirecting the addressee's cognition from narrated events to self-projection, governed by the conditional-temporal particle "إذ" (when) that binds the apodosis to the protasis.
7:6.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'Remembrance of Death and Afterlife'

7:40.arabic: الدنس ثيابا الذين لا ينكحون المتنعمات ولا تفتح لهم أبواب السدد (5) فقال عمر بن عبد العزيز والله لقد نكحت المتنعمات فاطمة بنت عبد الملك وفتحت لي أبواب السدد إلا أن يرحمني الله لا جرم لا أدهن رأسي حتى يشعث ولا أغسل ثوبي الذي على جسدي حتى يتسخ وعن أبي ذر قال قلت يا رسول الله ما آنية الحوض قال والذي نفس محمد بيده لآنيته أكثر من عدد نجوم السماء وكواكبها في الليلة المظلمة المضحية من شرب منه لم يظمأ آخر ما عليه يشخب فيه ميزابان من الجنة عرضه مثل طوله ما بين عمان وأيلة ماؤه أشد بياضا من اللبن وأحلى م
7:40.english: Know that the Basin (al-Ḥawḍ) is a magnificent honor (mukramah ʿaẓīmah) which God—exalted is He—has singled out for our Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him. The reports (akhbār) have encompassed its description, and we—PageV04P528—hope that God—exalted is He—will grant us knowledge of it in this world and its tasting (dhawq) in the Hereafter. For among its attributes is that whoever drinks from it will never thirst again. Anas said: The Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, dozed a light slumber, then raised his head smiling. They said to him: "O Messenger of God, why did you laugh?" He said: "A verse was just revealed to me," and he recited {In the name of God, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate: {إِنَّا أَعْطَيْنَاكَ الْكَوْثَرَ} [Verily, We have given you the Abundance]} until he completed it. Then he said: "Do you know what al-Kawthar is?" They said: "God and His Messenger know best." He said: "It is a river which my Lord—mighty and majestic is He—has promised me in Paradise, upon which is abundant good. Upon it is a Basin (ḥawḍ) which my community will approach on the Day of Resurrection; its vessels (āniyah) are as numerous as the stars of the sky." (1) And Anas said: The Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "While I was walking in Paradise, behold, there was a river whose banks were domes of hollowed pearl. I said: 'What is this, O Gabriel?' He said: 'This is al-Kawthar which your Lord has given you.' Then the angel struck his hand, and lo, its clay was pure musk (misk adhfar)." (2) And he said: The Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, used to say: "The distance between the two banks of my Basin is like that between Medina and Ṣanʿāʾ, or like that between Medina and ʿAmmān." (3) And Ibn ʿUmar narrated that when the saying of God—exalted is He—{إِنَّا أَعْطَيْنَاكَ الْكَوْثَرَ} was revealed, the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "It is a river in Paradise; its two banks are of gold, its drink is whiter than milk, sweeter than honey, and more fragrant than musk; it flows over pebbles of pearl and ruby (marjān)." (4) And Thawbān, the freed slave of the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, said: The Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "My Basin extends from ʿAdan to ʿAmmān of al-Balqāʾ; its water is whiter than milk and sweeter than honey; its cups (akwāb) are as numerous as the stars of the sky. Whoever drinks from it a single drink will never thirst after it ever. The first people to arrive at it are the poor among the Emigrants (fuqarāʾ al-muhājirīn)." ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb said: "And who are they, O Messenger of God?" He said: "They are those with disheveled heads (shaʿth) and dusty garments, who do not marry the pampered beauties (al-mutannaʿimāt), nor are the doors of the great mansions (al-sudad) opened for them." (5) Then ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz said: "By God, I have married the pampered beauties—Fāṭimah bint ʿAbd al-Malik—and the doors of the great mansions have been opened for me, unless God has mercy on me. No doubt! I will not oil my head until it becomes disheveled, nor will I wash the garment upon my body until it becomes soiled." And on the authority of Abū Dharr, he said: I said: "O Messenger of God, what are the vessels of the Basin?" He said: "By Him in whose hand is the soul of Muḥammad, its vessels are more numerous than the number of the stars of the sky and its planets on a dark, moonless night (al-muḍḥiyah). Whoever drinks from it will never thirst at the end of his affair. Two spouts (mīzābān) pour into it from Paradise, each as wide as its length, between ʿAmmān and Aylah; its water is whiter than milk and sweeter than honey."
