(6) And on the authority of Samurah, he said: The Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Every prophet has a Basin, and they vie in glory over which of them has the most arrivals (wāridah). And I indeed hope that I will be the most numerous of them in arrivals." (7) This, then, is the hope (rajāʾ) of the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him. Let every servant hope to be among the number of those who arrive (al-wāridīn), and let him beware of being merely a wishful thinker (mutamanniyan) and self-deluded (mughtarran) while supposing himself to be a hopeful one (rājin). For the one who truly hopes for the harvest is he who sows the seed, clears the earth, and waters it, then sits hoping for God's bounty in causing it to sprout and in warding off calamities (ṣawāʿiq) until the time of harvest. As for the one who abandons tilling, sowing, clearing the earth, and watering it, and then takes to hoping for God's bounty to grow for him grain and fruit—this one is deluded (mughtarr) and a wishful thinker (mutamannin), PageV04P529—and is not among the hopeful in any way. And such is the hope of most creatures, and it is the delusion of fools (ghurūr al-ḥumaqāʾ). We seek refuge in God from delusion (al-ghurūr) and heedlessness (al-ghaflah). For self-delusion regarding God (al-ightirār billāh) is greater than self-delusion regarding this world. God—exalted is He—said: {فَلَا تَغُرَّنَّكُمُ الْحَيَاةُ الدُّنْيَا وَلَا يَغُرَّنَّكُمْ بِاللَّهِ الْغَرُورُ} [So let not the life of this world delude you, nor let the Deluder (al-Gharūr) delude you concerning God] {Luqmān: 33}.
7:40.section_title_en: The Description of the Intercession and the Description of the Basin (Ḥawḍ)
7:40.anchors:
- Root: حوض (Ḥ-W-Ḍ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The basin or cistern where water collects; a place of gathering for drinking.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In the eschatological context, it signifies the Prophet's (ﷺ) designated watering-place, a divine honor (mukramah) granted specifically to him, embodying spiritual sustenance.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) for a physical water-trough; here used literally as a corporeal reality of the Hereafter, yet its description transcends earthly analogies.
- Root: ورد (W-R-D)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To arrive at water; to come to a watering-place.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The act of approaching the Ḥawḍ denotes the believer's arrival at the source of spiritual quench, contrasting with thirst as deprivation.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal for seeking water; metaphorically, the "ward" (those arriving) are the faithful community seeking the Prophet's intercession.
- Root: غرر (Gh-R-R)
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الاغترار" is self-deception through heedlessness (ghiflah), as in {لَا يَغُرَّنَّكُمْ بِاللَّهِ الْغَرُورُ} — the delusion of assuming divine favor without due action.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: a state of being deceived by a mirage; metaphorical: the fool's reliance on hope (rajā') without labor, akin to a farmer who neglects sowing yet expects harvest.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The periodic structure in "عليه خير كثير" and "عليه حوض" allows fronting of the prepositional phrase for emphasis, highlighting the abundance and honor bestowed upon the Prophet (ﷺ).
7:40.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Remembrance of Death and Afterlife'

7:43.arabic: تنعموا فلا تبأسوا أبدا فذلك قوله عز وجل ونودوا أن تلكم الجنة أورثتموها بما كنتم تعلمون (1) ومهما أردت أن تعرف صفة الجنة فاقرأ القرآن فليس وراء بيان الله تعالى بيان واقرأ من قوله تعالى لمن خاف مقام ربه جنتان إلى آخر سورة الرحمن واقرأ سورة الواقعة وغيرها من السور وإن أردت أن تعرف تفصيل صفاتها من الأخبار فتأمل الآن تفصليها بعد أن اطلعت على جملتها وتأمل أولا عدد الجنان قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في قوله تعالى {ولمن خاف مقام ربه جنتان} قال جنتان من فضة آنيتهما وما فيهما وجنتان من ذهب آنيتهما وما فيهما وما بين القوم وبين أن ين
7:43.english: ...of death, hunger, thirst, and all other kinds of calamities, he would be worthy of abandoning this world because of them, and of not preferring it over that whose cutting-off and vexation are of its very necessity. How [could he prefer it], when its people — the kings — are secure, and in varieties of joy are delighting? For them therein is all they desire, and every day they attend at the courtyard of the Throne, and gaze upon the noble Face of Allah. They attain, through that gazing upon Allah, that which makes them not look, along with it, at the rest of the delights of the Gardens, nor do they turn aside. They are perpetually moving among these kinds of blessings, and they are secure from their passing away. Abu Hurayrah said: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "A herald will call out: 'O People of Paradise! Verily for you is that you be healthy and never be ill; and for you is that you live and never die; and for you is that you be young and never grow old; and for you is that you be in bliss and never suffer misery.'" That is the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: {«And they will be called: 'This is the Paradise which you have been made to inherit for what you used to do'»} (7:43).
7:43.section_title_en: The Description of Paradise: Its Gates, Rivers, and the Bliss of Its Inhabitants
7:43.anchors:
- Root: نعم (n-'-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root denotes ease, comfort, and the state of well-being; al-Ayn notes it is also a name for the leopard and panther, indicating swiftness and grace.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "النعمة: الحالة الحسنة" — the goodly state; "النعيم" is the enduring, perfect form of bliss, specifically tied to divine reward in the afterlife.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): "نعم عيشه" — a life of ease and pleasantness. Metaphorical (Majaz): "خفّت نعامتهم" — their prosperity departed, showing the root's extension to transient worldly goods, contrasted here with eternal Paradise.
- Root: اهل (a-h-l)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root signifies those united by kinship, dwelling, or faith; al-Ayn notes it also refers to the prominent part of a beast's back, implying a place of honor and rest.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "أهل الرجل: من يجمعه وإياهم نسب أو دين" — the people of a man are those joined by lineage or religion; "أهل الجنة" (the People of Paradise) are thus bound by the covenant of faith and divine favor.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "رجعوا إلى أهاليهم" — returning to one's family. Here, the "أهل الجنة" are the inhabitants of Paradise, addressed by the herald as a household of eternal blessedness.
- Root: باب (b-a-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root denotes a door or gateway; al-Ayn links it to "إبهام" (obscurity/concealment), as a door hides what lies within until opened.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الباب" is the means of access to a thing; in the Quranic context, the gates of Paradise are the entry points to divine mercy, each corresponding to a specific act of obedience.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical gates of a city or house. Metaphorical: "أبواب الجنة" are the spiritual avenues of righteous deeds (prayer, fasting, charity, jihad) through which the believer enters divine reward.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The rule permits separation between a preposition and its governed noun for rhetorical emphasis, as seen in "لهم فيها كل ما يشتهون" (for them therein is all they desire), where "لهم" is fronted for exclusivity and "فيها" interposed to stress the locus of bliss.
7:43.topic: Al-Ghazali on the journey of the soul, death, and the Hereafter, from 'Remembrance of Death and Afterlife'

7:43.arabic: إلا الله والله أكبر سبع مرات وقال الحمد لله الذي هدانا لهذا وما كنا لنهتدي لولا أن هدانا الله اللهم أنت الحامل على الظهر وأنت المستعان على الأمور السادسة في النزول والسنة أن لا ينزل حتى يحمى النهار ويكون أكثر سيره بالليل قال صلى الله عليه وسلم عليكم بالدلجة فإن الأرض تطوي بالليل ما لا تطوي بالنهار (3) وليقلل نومه بالليل حتى يكون عونا على السير ومهما أشرف على المنزل فليقل اللهم رب السموات السبع وما أظللن ورب الأرضين السبع وما أقللن ورب الشياطين وما أضللن ورب الرياح وما ذرين ورب البحار وما جرين أسالك خير هذا ا
7:43.english: He ought to seek out a righteous companion, one who loves goodness and assists in it: if he forgets, the companion reminds him; if he remembers, the companion aids him; if he fears, the companion emboldens him; if he weakens, the companion strengthens him; if his breast narrows, the companion enlarges his patience. He should bid farewell to his resident companions, his brothers, and his neighbors — taking leave of them and seeking their supplications, for God Most High places goodness in their prayers. The Sunnah of farewell is to say: «أستودع الله دينك وأمانتك وخواتيم عملك» — "I entrust to God your religion, your trustworthiness, and the seal of your deeds." And he, peace and blessings be upon him, used to say to one intending travel: "In God's protection and His care — may God provide you with piety, forgive your sin, and direct you toward goodness wherever you may be."
7:43.section_title_en: The Book of the Etiquette of Travel — Section 199: On the Comprehensive Etiquette of the Journey (From Provisioning to Guarding)
7:43.anchors:
- Root: س ف ر (S-F-R)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "السفر: كشف الغطاء" — unveiling, uncovering; the traveler is one who uncovers the veils of distant lands.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "السفر: كشف الغطاء، ويختص ذلك بالأعيان" — the journey is a literal uncovering of horizons, yet the spiritual journey unveils the soul's veils.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Haqiqah: "سافر سفرا بعيدا" (to travel far); Majaz: "وجه مسفر: مشرق سرورا" — a face radiant with joy, as the traveler's face brightens with divine trust.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — governing the permissible separation between the preposition and its object for rhetorical emphasis, as in the supplications' structural pauses.
7:43.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications, prayers, and their spiritual power, from 'Remembrance of Death and Afterlife'

7:89.arabic: ولا تقولن لشيء إني فاعل ذلك غدا إلا أن يشاء الله ثم لم يقتصر على ذلك فيما لا يشك فيه بل قال تعالى لتدخلن المسجد الحرام إن شاء الله آمنين محلقين رءؤسكم ومقصرين وكان الله سبحانه عالما بأنهم يدخلون لا محالة وأنه شاءه ولكن المقصود تعليمه ذلك فتأدب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في ما كان يخبر عنه معلوما كان أو مشكوكا حتى قال صلى الله عليه وسلم لما دخل المقابر السلام عليكم دار قوم مؤمنين وإنا إن شاء الله بكم لاحقون (1) واللحوق بهم غير مشكوك فيه ولكن مقتضى الأدب ذكر الله تعالى وربط الأمور به وهذه الصيغ
7:89.english: If you say: "What is the meaning of the Salaf's statement, 'I am a believer, if God wills' — given that the exception (istithnā') implies doubt, and doubt in faith is unbelief? Yet they all refrained from giving an unqualified answer affirming faith and were cautious about it."
7:89.section_title_en: On the Meaning of the Salaf's Statement "I am a Believer, If God Wills" — Section 102
7:89.anchors:
- Root: نفس (n-f-s)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The self, the soul; that which is breathed; the innermost reality of a person.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): النفس is used for the rūḥ (spirit), for the dhāt (essence/self), and for the seat of intention and knowledge. When one says "he knows in himself (nafsihi) that he is a believer," it denotes certitude residing in the very core of one's being, not a corporeal faculty.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) usage refers to the soul's reflexive self-awareness; metaphorical (majāz) usage extends to "blood" (dam) or "the eye" (ʿayn) of envy. Here, "in himself" (fī nafsihi) is literal self-knowledge, not mere outward profession.
- Root: وجه (w-j-h)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Face, countenance; the foremost part; a mode, aspect, or direction.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The face is the most noble apparent part of a thing; hence it is used for the "aspect" or "manner" (wajh) of an affair. "Four aspects" (wujūh) means four distinct modes of interpretation or rational grounds.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the face of a person or object. Metaphorical: "the face of the matter" (wajh al-amr) — its most salient and honorable dimension. Here, the "aspects" are hermeneutical angles, not physical parts.
- Root: ايم (a-y-m)
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The unmarried state (aym); one who has no spouse. Not applicable here directly, but the root's semantic field of "being alone/without attachment" contrasts with īmān's root (a-m-n) — security and trust — which is the operative term in this text.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Not directly relevant; the operative root is أمن (a-m-n), meaning security from fear, and by extension, faith (īmān) as the state of being secure in God's truth.
- Root: كان (k-w-n)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To be, to exist; the copula of predication.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Kāna denotes existence and becoming; in theological usage, it grounds the distinction between what is (mawjūd) and what is merely asserted. The question "Are you a believer?" (a-mu'min anta?) uses kāna implicitly to ask about actual, present state — not future contingency.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: existence. Metaphorical: the "being-so" of a predicate. The istithnā' (exception) with "in shā' Allāh" suspends the copula's certainty, shifting from assertive existence to contingent hope.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الاستثناء والتعليق بالمشيئة (The Chapter of Exception and Suspension by the Divine Will) — When an exception clause (istithnā') follows a positive assertion, it grammatically suspends the universality or certainty of the predication. In theological discourse, this suspension may be semantic (doubt) or pragmatic (deference, etiquette, or self-deprecation), and Sibawayh's parsing of conditional suspension (taʿlīq) shows that the apodosis need not be negated — only its absolute, unqualified force is tempered.
7:89.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Remembrance of Death and Afterlife'

7:188.arabic: علامات المرض وبهذا يعرف أن القلوب كلها مريضة إلا ما شاء الله إلا أن من الأمراض ما لا يعرفها صاحبها ومرض القلب مما لا يعرفه صاحبه فلذلك يغفل عنه وإن عرفه صعب عليه الصبر على مرارة دوائه فإن دواءه مخالفة الشهوات وهو نزع الروح فإن وجد من نفسه قوة الصبر عليه لم يجد طبيبا حاذقا يعالجه فإن الأطباء هم العلماء وقد استولى عليهم المرض فالطبيب المريض قلما يلتفت إلى علاجه فلهذا صار الداء عضالا والمرض مزمنا واندرس هذا العلم وأنكر بالكلية طب القلوب وأنكر مرضها وأقبل الخلق على حب الدنيا وعلى أعمال ظاهرها عبادات وباطنها
7:188.english: I say: The soul (nafs) that belongs to the human being — that by which he is distinguished from the beasts — for he is not distinguished from them by the power of eating, copulation, sight, or any other such thing. Rather, he is distinguished by the knowledge of things as they truly are. And the Origin of all things, their Existentiator and their Inventor, is God, Mighty and Majestic — He who made them things. So if one knew everything but did not know God, Mighty and Majestic, it would be as though he knew nothing at all. And the sign of knowledge is love: whoever knows God Most High loves Him. And the sign of love is that one does not prefer over Him this world nor any other beloved thing. As God Most High said: {«Say: If your fathers, your sons, your brothers, your spouses, your clans — the wealth you have acquired, commerce whose decline you fear, and dwellings you find pleasing — are more beloved to you than God and His Messenger and striving in His cause, then wait until God brings about His command»} [Q 9:24]. So whoever possesses something more beloved to him than God — his heart is sick. Just as any stomach to which clay has become more beloved than bread and water, or whose appetite for bread and water has fallen away — it is sick. These are the signs of sickness. And by this it is known that all hearts are sick — except what God wills. Yet among sicknesses there are those the sufferer does not recognize; and the sickness of the heart is among those the sufferer does not recognize. For this reason he is heedless of it. And even if he recognized it, patience upon the bitterness of its medicine would be difficult for him — for its medicine is opposing the appetites, and that is the tearing out of the spirit (nafs). And if he found in himself the strength of patience upon it, he would not find a skillful physician to treat him — for the physicians are the scholars, and sickness has overcome them. So the sick physician rarely attends to his own cure. For this reason the malady has become chronic and the sickness chronic. This science has become effaced, and the medicine of hearts is denied entirely, and the sickness of the heart is denied. And creation has turned to the love of this world and to deeds whose outward form is acts of worship but whose inward reality is habit and ostentation. These are the signs of the roots of sicknesses.
7:188.section_title_en: The Soul's Distinction, the Sickness of the Heart, and the Path of Moderation
7:188.anchors:
- Root: نفس (n-f-s)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The self, soul, or spirit; that by which a thing is distinguished in its essential reality
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The soul (nafs) as the principle of rational discrimination and knowledge, distinguishing humans from beasts
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the self or person; Metaphorical: the rational soul as the seat of knowledge and moral responsibility
- Root: مرض (m-r-d)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Departure from the state of health and equilibrium
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Sickness of the heart as a metaphor for moral and spiritual vices — ignorance, cowardice, avarice, hypocrisy
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: bodily illness; Metaphorical: spiritual malady whereby the heart inclines toward what is harmful and away from what is beneficial
- Root: قلب (q-l-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The heart; that which is ever-turning and fluctuating between states
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The heart as the seat of understanding and moral perception; its "turning" (taqlīb) signifies its instability between soundness and sickness
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the physical organ; Metaphorical: the spiritual faculty of cognition and moral discernment
- Root: خلق (kh-l-q)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Measured, proportioned disposition; character and temperament
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Moral character as the inward form (ṣūrah bāṭinah) corresponding to the outward physical form
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: measuring and proportioning; Metaphorical: the ingrained disposition that governs action
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — The use of restrictive constructions to isolate the defining characteristic of the human soul as knowledge of God, not animal appetites
7:188.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Remembrance of Death and Afterlife'

7:188.arabic: محمد بن إدريس قل اللهم إني لا أملك لنفسي نفعا ولا ضرا ولا موتا ولا حياة ولا نشورا ولا أستطيع أن آخذ إلا ما أعطيتني ولا أتقي إلا ما وقيتني اللهم فوفقني لما تحب وترضى من القول والعمل في عافية فلما أصبحت أعدت ذلك فلما ترحل النهار أعطاني الله عز وجل طلبتي وسهل لي الخلاص مما كنت فيه فعليكم بهذه الدعوات لا تغفلوا عنها فهذه جملة من المكاشفات تدل على أحوال الموتى وعلى الأعمال المقربة إلى الله زلفى فلنذكر بعدها ما بين يدى الموتى من ابتداء نفخة الصور إلى آخر القرار إما فى الجنة أو فى النار والحم
7:188.english: Abu Sa'id al-Shahham said: I saw Sahl al-Sa'luki in a dream and said, "O Shaykh!" He said, "Leave off this addressing me as shaykh." I said, "Those spiritual states (aḥwāl) which you witnessed [in life]?" He said, "They availed us nothing." I said, "What did God do with you?" He said, "He forgave me on account of the questions about which the incapable ones used to ask."
7:188.section_title_en: Section 1333 — Visions of the Deceased and Their States After Death
7:188.anchors:
- Root: م و ت (m-w-t)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Death as the cessation of vital faculty; the state of the deceased (mayyit) contrasted with the living (ḥayy).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Death as separation of the soul from the body, a transition to the Barzakh; visions of the dead (ru'yā) reveal their post-mortem states.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal death (ḥaqīqah) vs. metaphorical "death" of the heart; here, actual death and its aftermath.
- Root: غ ف ر (gh-f-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Covering, protection from defilement; forgiveness as divine concealment of sin.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Divine forgiveness (maghfirah) as God's safeguarding the servant from punishment.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: covering a garment; metaphorical: God's pardon enveloping all sins, as in the vision of Ibn al-Mubarak.
- Root: ر أ ي (r-'-y)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Seeing, perceiving; in dreams (ru'yā), a mode of non-sensory perception.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Vision as a form of divine disclosure (mukāshafah) granted to the righteous.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal sight vs. dream-vision as a vehicle for veridical reports of the unseen.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The rule governing the placement of prepositional phrases and their objects, ensuring syntactic coherence in complex narrative chains, as applied here to the sequence of reported dream-visions.
7:188.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Remembrance of Death and Afterlife'

8:1.arabic: الجنة ثم قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عند ذلك اتقوا الله وأصلحوا ذات بينكم فإن الله يصلح بين المؤمنين (1) وهذا تنبيه على أن ذلك إنما ينال بالتخلق بأخلاق الله وهو إصلاح ذات البين وسائر الأخلاق فتفكر الآن فى نفسك إن خلت صحيفتك عن المظالم أو تلطف لك حتى عفا عنك وأيقنت بسعادة الأبد كيف يكون سرورك فى منصرفك من مفصل الفضاء وقد خلع عليك خلعة الرضا وعدت بسعادة ليس بعدها شقاء وبنعيم لا يدور بحواشيه الفناء وعند ذلك طار قلبك سرورا وفرحا وابيض وجهك واستنار وأشرق كما يشرق القمر ليلة البدر فتوهم تبخترك بين الخلائق رافعا رأسك خالي
8:1.english: Know that none is saved from the peril of the Scale except him who, in this world, called his own soul to account, and weighed therein — by the scale of the Sacred Law — his deeds, his words, his passing thoughts, and his glances, just as ʿUmar — may God be well pleased with him — said: "Call yourselves to account before you are called to account, and weigh yourselves before you are weighed." Indeed, his calling himself to account consists in his repenting, before death, from every act of disobedience with a sincere repentance (tawbah naṣūḥ), and in his making up for what was neglected of his shortcomings regarding the obligatory commands of God — may He be exalted — and in his restoring rights to those he wronged, grain by grain, and in his seeking absolution from everyone whom he harmed by his tongue, his hand, or his evil suspicion harbored in his heart — and this by winning their hearts' contentment — until he dies with no outstanding wrong against him, nor any neglected obligation.
8:1.section_title_en: The Perils of the Scale and the Reckoning of Wrongs Against Others
8:1.anchors:
- Root: وزن (w-z-n)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning is weighing, measuring, and balancing; al-mīzān (the Scale) is the instrument of equitable judgment.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In theological context, al-mīzān is the divine instrument of justice on the Day of Resurrection, weighing deeds to manifest equitable recompense, not a corporeal balance.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) usage denotes physical weighing; metaphorical (majāz) usage extends to moral and spiritual accounting, as in "weighing one's deeds by the scale of the Sacred Law."
- Sibawayh Rule: Conditional and Exceptive Constructions (الشّرط والاستثناء) — governing the protasis-apodosis structure in "whoever's scales are heavy... whoever's scales are light," and the exceptive force in "none is saved... except he who reckons."
8:1.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Remembrance of Death and Afterlife'

8:1.arabic: قوله السابق قل الأنفال لله والرسول كما أخرجك ربك من بيتك بالحق أي فصارت أنفال الغنائم لك إذ أنت راض بخروجك وهم كارهون فاعترض بين الكلام الأمر بالتقوى وغيره ومن هذا النوع قوله عز وجل حتى تؤمنوا بالله وحده إلا قول إبراهيم لأبيه الآية ومنها المبهم وهو اللفظ المشترك بين معن من كلمة أو حرف أما الكلمة فكالشيء والقرين والأمة والروح ونظائرها قال الله تعالى ضرب الله مثلا عبدا مملوكا لا يقدر على شيء أراد به النفقة مما رزق وقوله عز وجل وضرب الله مثلا رجلين أحدهما أبكم لا يقدر على شيء أي الأم
8:1.english: I say: The Prophet (peace be upon him) was asked about the means of deliverance from these trials, and he said: "The Book of Allah — act by what is in it, for it is that which delivers one from them." The questioner repeated this three times, and he (peace be upon him) said three times: "Learn the Book of Allah, Mighty and Glorious, and act by what is in it, for in it is deliverance."
8:1.section_title_en: The Book of the Etiquette of Recitation — Section 233: On Understanding the Meanings of the Qur'an and the Limits of Interpretation
8:1.anchors:
- Root: ف-ه-م (f-h-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الفهم: هيئة للإنسان بها يتحقق معاني ما يحسن" — comprehension as an inherent faculty by which one ascertains meanings
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الفهم: هيئة للإنسان بها يتحقق معاني ما يحسن... وأفهمته: إذا قلت له حتى تصوره" — comprehension is a cognitive disposition; distinction between understanding (fahm) and making understood (ifhām)
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "تقول: من لم يؤت من سوء الفهم أتى من سوء الإفهام" — literal usage; failure of understanding often stems from failure of communication
- Root: ف-س-ر (f-s-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "وكل شيء يعرف به تفسير الشيء ومعناه، فهو تَفْسِرَتُه" — that by which a thing's meaning is made known
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "التفسير قد يقال فيما يختص بمفردات الألفاظ وغريبها، وفيما يختص بالتأويل" — tafsīr concerns lexical surface; taʾwīl concerns deeper meaning
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "هذا كلام يحتاج إلى فسر وتفسير" — literal: exposition of what is obscure
- Root: و-ج-ل (w-j-l)
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الوجل: استشعار الخوف" — the sensing of fear; used of hearts trembling at divine mention
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "لو واجلت فلانا لوجلته: لغلبته في الوجل" — literal sense of fear; metaphorical extension to overpowering in fear
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — the particle innamā restricts predication, essential for parsing the Prophet's saying "innamā al-aʿmālu bi-l-niyyāt" and analogous restrictive formulations in the ḥadīth cited herein
8:1.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Etiquette of Quran Recitation'

8:51.arabic: يوم القيامة بإخراج رجلين من النار فيقول الله تبارك وتعالى ذلك بما قدمت أيديكما وما أنا بظلام للعبيد ويأمر بردهما إلى النار فيعدو أحدهما في سلاسله حتى يقتحمها ويتلكأ الآخر ويأمر بردهما ويسألهما عن فعلهما فيقول الذي عدا إلى النار قد حذرت من وبال المعصية فلم أكن لأتعرض لسخطك ثانية ويقول الذي تلكأ حسن ظني بك كان يشعرني أن لا تردني إليها بعد ما أخرجتني منها فيأمر بهما إلى الجنة وقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ينادي مناد من تحت العرش يوم القيامة يا أمة محمد أما ما كان لي قبلكم فقد وهبته لكم وبقيت التبعات فتواهبوها وادخلوا ال
8:51.english: He mentioned me one day, or feared me in a station (1). And the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: "When the people of the Fire are gathered in the Fire — and with them, whomsoever God wills of the people of the Qiblah — the disbelievers will say to the Muslims: 'Were you not Muslims?' They will reply: 'Yes.' Then they will say: 'What did your Islam avail you, seeing that you are with us in the Fire?' They will answer: 'We had sins, and we were seized for them.' Then God, Mighty and Glorious, will hear what they have said, and He will command that whoever was in the Fire of the people of the Qiblah be brought out, and they will be brought out. When the disbelievers see that, they will say: 'Would that we had been Muslims, so that we might be brought out as they were brought out.' Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited: {ربما يود الذين كفروا لو كانوا مسلمين} — "Perhaps those who disbelieve will wish that they had been Muslims" (Q. 15:2). (2)
8:51.section_title_en: On the Vastness of Divine Mercy and the Intercession for the Sinful — Section 1360
8:51.anchors:
- Root: ذكر (dhakara)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Remembrance, recollection; also mention, invocation.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-dhikr is the opposite of forgetfulness (nisyān); it denotes the heart's presence with what is recalled, and the tongue's utterance thereof.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): to recall in the heart or utter on the tongue. Metaphorical (majāz): "dhakartuhu bi-khayr" — to speak well of someone, i.e., to raise their mention in honor.
- Root: خرج (kharaja)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To exit, depart, emerge from an interior to an exterior.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-khurūj is the departure of a thing from its place or state; used of the soul leaving the body, and of the damned leaving the Fire.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: spatial egress. Metaphorical: "kharaja min al-amr" — to emerge from an affair, i.e., to be free of its obligation; and "akhrajahu Allāh min al-nār" — divine extraction by mercy, not by merit.
- Root: شفع (shafa'a)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To make even, pair; intercession is making one's supplication a pair with another's need.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-shafā'ah is the joining of one's intercession to another's request for aid; its reality is the elevation of the intercessor's rank and the remission of the offender's burden.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: pairing. Metaphorical: intercession before a king — the intercessor "pairs" his own honor with the petitioner's deficiency.
- Root: رحم (raḥima)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Tenderness of heart, compassion; al-Raḥmān is intensive — mercy as an essential attribute.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-raḥmah is tenderness that necessitates beneficence; when attributed to God, it is pure beneficence (tafaddul) without emotional change.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the mother's womb (raḥim) as the seat of compassion. Metaphorical: "arḥam al-rāḥimīn" — God's mercy as sheer gratuitous giving, exceeding any creaturely pity.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Restriction and Focused Predication (al-ḥaṣr wa al-taqyīd bi-innamā) — "Innamā shafā'atu Rasūlillāh…" restricts intercession to a specific class, namely those who have burdened themselves with sins, not the innocent.
8:51.topic: Al-Ghazali on the journey of the soul, death, and the Hereafter, from 'Remembrance of Death and Afterlife'

9:72.arabic: وقال تعالى {ومساكن طيبة في جنات عدن ورضوان من الله أكبر} فقد رفع الله الرضا فوق جنات عدن كما رفع ذكره فوق الصلاة حيث قال {إن الصلاة تنهي عن الفحشاء والمنكر ولذكر الله أكبر} فكما أن مشاهدة المذكور في الصلاة أكبر من الصلاة فرضوان رب الجنة أعلى من الجنة بل هو غاية مطلب سكان الجنان وفي الحديث إن الله تعالى يتجلى للمؤمنين فيقول سلوني فيقولون رضاك (1) فسؤالهم الرضا بعد النظر نهاية التفضيل وأما رضا العبد فسنذكر حقيقته وأما رضوان الله تعالى عن العبد فهو بمعنى آخر يقرب مما ذكرناه في ح
9:72.english: I say: As for the verses [indicating the supremacy of divine pleasure], there is the saying of the Exalted: {رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمْ وَرَضُوا عَنْهُ} [Allah is well-pleased with them and they are well-pleased with Him] {«God is well-pleased with them and they are well-pleased with Him»}. And the Exalted has said: {هَلْ جَزَاءُ الْإِحْسَانِ إِلَّا الْإِحْسَانُ} [Is the reward of goodness aught but goodness?] {«Is the reward of goodness aught but goodness?»}. The ultimate end of goodness is God's pleasure with His servant, and that is the reward for the servant's pleasure in God the Exalted.
9:72.section_title_en: The Reality of Divine Pleasure (Riḍā) and the Servant's Contentment with the Decree — Section 1189
9:72.anchors:
- Root: رضي (raḍiya)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning is "to be content, to approve, to be pleased." Al-Farahidi notes its usage in mutual accord and satisfaction, with the form *tarāḍin* indicating reciprocal consent.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In theological usage, *riḍā* denotes the will's acquiescence to the divine decree without resistance. It is the apex of the servant's station, being the fruit of *maḥabbah* (love) and the key to perpetual vision (*nazar*).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (*ḥaqīqah*) sense is "satisfaction of the heart." Metaphorical (*majāz*) extension applies to God, where *riḍwān* is not an emotional state but a volitional attribute signifying the bestowal of grace and the removal of the veil.
- Root: نظر (naẓara)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "To look, to behold, to consider." In the lexicon, *naẓar* implies directed vision with the eye or the intellect.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Elevated to the highest beatific vision (*ru'yat Allāh*) in the afterlife, the ultimate reward and the supreme object of the inhabitants of Paradise.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical sight. Metaphorical: intellectual contemplation or the unveiled witnessing of the Divine in the Hereafter.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب التفضيل والتشبيه (The Chapter of Preference and Comparison) — Governing the syntactic structures of *afʿala* (elative) forms like *akbar* ("greater") to establish hierarchical supremacy between two entities, as in the verse {وَرِضْوَانٌ مِنَ اللَّهِ أَكْبَرُ}.
9:72.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Remembrance of Death and Afterlife'

9:102.arabic: هم الذين {خلطوا عملا صالحا وآخر سيئا عسى الله أن يتوب عليهم} هذا باعتبار القوة والضعف ويتطرق إليه أيضا ثلاثة أحوال باعتبار عدد ما يصبر عنه فإنه إما أن يغلب جميع الشهوات أو لا يغلب شيئا منها أو يغلب بعضها دون بعض وتنزيل قوله تعالى {خلطوا عملا صالحا وآخر سيئا} على من عجز عن بعض الشهوات دون بعض أولى والتاركون للمجاهدة مع الشهوات مطلقا يشبهون بالأنعام بل هم أضل سبيلا إذ البهيمة لم تخلق لها المعرفة والقدرة التي بها تجاهد مقتضى الشهوات وهذا قد خلق ذلك له وعطله فهو الناقص حقا المدبر يقينا ولذلك قيل ولم أر في عيوب ا
9:102.english: {وَلَمْ يُرِدْ إِلَّا الْحَيَاةَ الدُّنْيَا ذَلِكَ مَبْلَغُهُمْ مِنَ الْعِلْمِ} — "And they desire only the life of this world; that is the reach of their knowledge." {Quran 53:29} And the mark of this state is despair, dejection, and self-delusion with vain hopes — and that is the extreme of folly, just as he, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "The clever one is he who subjugates his own soul and works for what comes after death; and the foolish one is he who follows his soul's caprice and makes wishes upon God." {Hadith — al-Tirmidhi, Ibn Majah} And the possessor of this state, when admonished, says: "I long for repentance, but it has become impossible for me, so I have no aspiration for it." Or he is not longing for repentance at all, but says: "Indeed, God is Forgiving, Merciful, Generous — so there is no need for me to repent." And this wretched one — his intellect has become thin and subservient to his lust, so he does not employ his intellect except in extracting the subtle devices (daqāʾiq al-ḥiyal) by which he attains the satisfaction of his passion. Thus his intellect has come to be in the hand of his lusts like a Muslim captive in the hands of the infidels — they press him into service for tending swine, guarding wines, and carrying them. And his station with God Almighty is the station of one who subdues a Muslim and delivers him to the infidels, making him a captive among them — because by his obscene transgression, it is as though he has pressed into service that which had the right not to be pressed into service, and has given dominion over that which had the right not to be given dominion over it. For the Muslim only deserved to be dominant because of what is in him of knowledge of God and the impulsion of religion; and the infidel only deserved to be given dominion over him because of what is in him of ignorance of religion and the impulsion of the devils. And the right of the Muslim over his own soul is more obligatory than the right of another over him. So whenever the noble meaning (al-maʿnā al-sharīf) — which is of the party of God and the host of the angels — is pressed into service for the base meaning (al-maʿnā al-khasīs) — which is of the party of the devils banished from God Almighty — then he is like one who enslaves a Muslim to an infidel. Nay, he is like one who, intending to spite the king who has bestowed favors upon him, seizes the king's most beloved son and delivers him to his most hated enemy. Consider then how great is his ingratitude for the king's favor and his deservingness of the king's vengeance — because passion (al-hawā) is the most abominable deity worshipped on the face of the earth in the sight of God Almighty, and the intellect (al-ʿaql) is the most noble existing thing created upon the face of the earth.
9:102.section_title_en: The States of the Soul in the Struggle Against Passion — Section 961
9:102.anchors:
- Root: ي-أ-س (ya-sa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Despair, cessation of hope; al-ya's is the cutting off of expectation from a matter.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological despair (qunūṭ) is blameworthy as it negates divine mercy; linked to ignorance of God's attributes.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: loss of hope; metaphorical: the soul's surrender to worldly limitation, as in {ذَلِكَ مَبْلَغُهُمْ مِنَ الْعِلْمِ} — their knowledge reaches only the worldly.
- Root: ك-ي-س (kay-sa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Keenness, intelligence; al-kays is acuteness of mind and good management of affairs.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The "clever one" (al-kays) in prophetic idiom is he who subjugates his soul (dāna nafsahu) — a moral-intellectual virtue, not mere cunning.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: sharpness; metaphorical: prudence oriented to the afterlife, contrasted with ḥumq (folly) which follows caprice.
- Root: ع-ق-ل (ʿayn-qaf-lam)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The intellect; binding and restraining (al-ʿiqqāl) — that which prevents the soul from base acts.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): ʿAql is the faculty prepared for knowledge and the knowledge acquired thereby; its referent (musammā) is a divine subtlety (laṭīfah rabbāniyyah), not a corporeal substance.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the rope binding a camel's leg; metaphorical: the rational faculty that restrains passion — here, perverted into a captive serving lust.

  * Lisan / Ayn: The soul's inclination; hawan is the falling of the soul toward base desires.

9:102.arabic: وتنزيل قوله تعالى {خلطوا عملا صالحا وآخر سيئا} على من عجز عن بعض الشهوات دون بعض أولى والتاركون للمجاهدة مع الشهوات مطلقا يشبهون بالأنعام بل هم أضل سبيلا إذ البهيمة لم تخلق لها المعرفة والقدرة التي بها تجاهد مقتضى الشهوات وهذا قد خلق ذلك له وعطله فهو الناقص حقا المدبر يقينا ولذلك قيل ولم أر في عيوب الناس عيبا .
9:102.english: {وَلَمْ يُرِدْ إِلَّا الْحَيَاةَ الدُّنْيَا ذَلِكَ مَبْلَغُهُمْ مِنَ الْعِلْمِ} — "And they desire only the life of this world; that is the reach of their knowledge." {Quran 53:29} And the mark of this state is despair, dejection, and self-delusion with vain hopes — and that is the extreme of folly, just as he, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "The clever one is he who subjugates his own soul and works for what comes after death; and the foolish one is he who follows his soul's caprice and makes wishes upon God." {Hadith — al-Tirmidhi, Ibn Majah} And the possessor of this state, when admonished, says: "I long for repentance, but it has become impossible for me, so I have no aspiration for it." Or he is not longing for repentance at all, but says: "Indeed, God is Forgiving, Merciful, Generous — so there is no need for me to repent." And this wretched one — his intellect has become thin and subservient to his lust, so he does not employ his intellect except in extracting the subtle devices (daqāʾiq al-ḥiyal) by which he attains the satisfaction of his passion. Thus his intellect has come to be in the hand of his lusts like a Muslim captive in the hands of the infidels — they press him into service for tending swine, guarding wines, and carrying them. And his station with God Almighty is the station of one who subdues a Muslim and delivers him to the infidels, making him a captive among them — because by his obscene transgression, it is as though he has pressed into service that which had the right not to be pressed into service, and has given dominion over that which had the right not to be given dominion over it. For the Muslim only deserved to be dominant because of what is in him of knowledge of God and the impulsion of religion; and the infidel only deserved to be given dominion over him because of what is in him of ignorance of religion and the impulsion of the devils. And the right of the Muslim over his own soul is more obligatory than the right of another over him. So whenever the noble meaning (al-maʿnā al-sharīf) — which is of the party of God and the host of the angels — is pressed into service for the base meaning (al-maʿnā al-khasīs) — which is of the party of the devils banished from God Almighty — then he is like one who enslaves a Muslim to an infidel. Nay, he is like one who, intending to spite the king who has bestowed favors upon him, seizes the king's most beloved son and delivers him to his most hated enemy. Consider then how great is his ingratitude for the king's favor and his deservingness of the king's vengeance — because passion (al-hawā) is the most abominable deity worshipped on the face of the earth in the sight of God Almighty, and the intellect (al-ʿaql) is the most noble existing thing created upon the face of the earth.
9:102.section_title_en: The States of the Soul in the Struggle Against Passion — Section 961
9:102.anchors:
- Root: ي-أ-س (ya-sa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Despair, cessation of hope; al-ya's is the cutting off of expectation from a matter.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological despair (qunūṭ) is blameworthy as it negates divine mercy; linked to ignorance of God's attributes.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: loss of hope; metaphorical: the soul's surrender to worldly limitation, as in {ذَلِكَ مَبْلَغُهُمْ مِنَ الْعِلْمِ} — their knowledge reaches only the worldly.
- Root: ك-ي-س (kay-sa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Keenness, intelligence; al-kays is acuteness of mind and good management of affairs.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The "clever one" (al-kays) in prophetic idiom is he who subjugates his soul (dāna nafsahu) — a moral-intellectual virtue, not mere cunning.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: sharpness; metaphorical: prudence oriented to the afterlife, contrasted with ḥumq (folly) which follows caprice.
- Root: ع-ق-ل (ʿayn-qaf-lam)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The intellect; binding and restraining (al-ʿiqqāl) — that which prevents the soul from base acts.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): ʿAql is the faculty prepared for knowledge and the knowledge acquired thereby; its referent (musammā) is a divine subtlety (laṭīfah rabbāniyyah), not a corporeal substance.

9:102.arabic: وآخرون اعترفوا بذنوبهم خلطوا عملا صالحا وآخر سيئا فأمره من حيث مواظبته على الطاعات وكراهته لما تعاطاه مرجو فعسى الله أن يتوب عليه وعاقبته مخطرة من حيث تسويفه وتأخيره فربما بختطف قبل التوبة ويقع أمره في المشيئة فإن تداركه الله بفضله وجبر كسره وامتن عليه بالتوبة التحق بالسابقين وإن غلبته شقوته وقهرته شهوته فيخشى أن يحق عليه في الخاتمة ما سبق عليه من القول في الأزل لأنه مهما تعذر على المتفقه مثلا الاحتراز عن شواغل التعلم دل تعذره على أنه سبق له في الأزل أن يكون من الجاهلين فيضعف الرجاء في حقه
9:102.english: **The First Rank:** That the disobedient one repents and remains steadfast upon repentance until the end of his life, so that he makes up for what he let slip of his affair, and does not prompt himself to return to his sins — except for the slips (zallāt) from which human beings are not free in their habitual ways, so long as one is not at the rank of prophethood. This is steadfastness upon repentance, and its possessor is the one who races forward in good deeds, exchanging his evil deeds for good ones. The name of this repentance is "sincere repentance" (al-tawbah al-naṣūḥ), and the name of this soul is the "tranquil soul" (al-nafs al-muṭma'innah) which returns to its Lord, well-pleased and well-pleasing. These are those to whom the Prophet, peace be upon him, pointed when he said: {«سبق المفردون المستهترون بذكر الله تعالى وضع الذكر عنهم أوزارهم فوردوا القيامة خفافا»} — "The solitary ones have outstripped [all others] — those who are engrossed in the remembrance of God Almighty, for remembrance has lifted their burdens from them, and they arrive at the Resurrection light [of burden]." For in this there is an indication that they were beneath burdens which remembrance lifted from them.
9:102.section_title_en: The Four Ranks of the Repentant — On the Degrees of Tawbah and the States of the Soul
9:102.anchors:
- Root: توب (T-W-B)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Return, turning back; the verbal noun denotes the act of reverting from a state.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "التوب: ترك الذنب على أجمل الوجوه" — abandoning sin in the most beautiful manner; the most complete form of apology, comprising abandonment of the sin due to its ugliness, remorse for what passed, and resolve against return.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): "تاب العبد إلى الله من ذنبه" — the servant's turning to God from his sin. Metaphorical (Majaz): The mutual relation of divine acceptance (تاب الله على عبده) as a response to the servant's turning.
- Root: نفس (N-F-S)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The self, soul, spirit; that which animates and distinguishes.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The soul (النفس) as the locus of divine address and self-reproach; its states (mutma'innah, lawwāmah, ammārah) are graded by its orientation toward God or toward passions.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the self as animate entity. Metaphorical: "دفق نفسه" (his blood/life) — the soul as the seat of life and moral agency.
- Root: ذنب (Dh-N-B)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The tail; that which follows behind.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الذنب في الأصل: الأخذ بذنب الشيء" — sin as the act of seizing the consequence; the trailing fault that follows the agent.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the tail of an animal. Metaphorical: "هو من الأذناب" — one who follows; sin as the trailing mark of the soul's deviation.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — Used to delimit the four ranks precisely, ensuring each category is mutually exclusive and exhaustive in its defining condition.

9:102.arabic: على الطاعات وكراهته لما تعاطاه مرجو فعسى الله أن يتوب عليه وعاقبته مخطرة من حيث تسويفه وتأخيره فربما بختطف قبل التوبة ويقع أمره في المشيئة فإن تداركه الله بفضله وجبر كسره وامتن عليه بالتوبة التحق بالسابقين وإن غلبته شقوته وقهرته شهوته فيخشى أن يحق عليه في الخاتمة ما سبق عليه من القول في الأزل لأنه مهما تعذر على المتفقه مثلا الاحتراز عن شواغل التعلم دل تعذره على أنه سبق له في الأزل أن يكون من الجاهلين فيضعف الرجاء في حقه وإذا يسرت له أسباب المواظبة على التحصيل دل على أنه سبق له في الأزل أن يكون من جم
9:102.english: **The First Rank:** That the disobedient one repents and remains steadfast upon repentance until the end of his life, so that he makes up for what he let slip of his affair, and does not prompt himself to return to his sins — except for the slips (zallāt) from which human beings are not free in their habitual ways, so long as one is not at the rank of prophethood. This is steadfastness upon repentance, and its possessor is the one who races forward in good deeds, exchanging his evil deeds for good ones. The name of this repentance is "sincere repentance" (al-tawbah al-naṣūḥ), and the name of this soul is the "tranquil soul" (al-nafs al-muṭma'innah) which returns to its Lord, well-pleased and well-pleasing. These are those to whom the Prophet, peace be upon him, pointed when he said: {«سبق المفردون المستهترون بذكر الله تعالى وضع الذكر عنهم أوزارهم فوردوا القيامة خفافا»} — "The solitary ones have outstripped [all others] — those who are engrossed in the remembrance of God Almighty, for remembrance has lifted their burdens from them, and they arrive at the Resurrection light [of burden]." For in this there is an indication that they were beneath burdens which remembrance lifted from them.

9:102.arabic: عملا صالحا وآخر سيئا وعلى الجملة فهمة الدنيا وهمة الآخرة في القلب مثل الماء الذي يصب في قدح مملوء بخل فبقدر ما ندخل فيه من الماء يخرج منه من الخل لا محالة ولا يجتمعان
9:102.english: The Messenger of Allah — peace and blessings be upon him — said to ʿUthmān ibn Abī Shaybah: "I forgot to tell you to cover the cooking pot that is in the house, for it is not fitting that there be in the house anything that would occupy people away from their prayer." This, then, is the way of calming thoughts.
9:102.section_title_en: The Revival of the Religious Sciences — Section 137: On the Inward and Outward Causes of Distraction in Prayer and Their Remedies
9:102.anchors:
- Root: شغل (Sh-Gh-L)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The core meaning is occupation or engagement that diverts one's attention; al-Ayn notes it as that which preoccupies and distracts.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-Shughl is that which diverts the intellect and causes heedlessness; it is an accidental state that overtakes the heart, turning it away from its proper focus.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): being occupied with a task. Metaphorical (Majaz): "A preoccupied heart" — one entangled with worldly concerns that obstruct spiritual presence.
- Root: قلب (Q-L-B)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To turn, overturn, or redirect something from one state to another; the heart is so named for its constant fluctuation and turning.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The heart's turning between states; its transformation and redirection. In the Kalam context, the heart (qalb) is the seat of spiritual perception and intention.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical turning over. Metaphorical: the heart's oscillation between attentiveness and distraction, and the deliberate redirecting of one's focus.
- Root: شجر (Sh-J-R)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Trees and vegetation with trunks; also used for branching and spreading out.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The branching of a tree; used metaphorically for the ramification of desires and thoughts that spread and entangle.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: trees. Metaphorical: "The tree of desires" — when its branches spread, thoughts are drawn to it as birds are drawn to trees.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد (Restriction and Specification) — The conditional and restrictive constructions (e.g., "لا يطمعن," "لا يغني غيره") that establish exclusive causal relationships between spiritual states and their remedies.
