9:112.arabic: رضي الله عنه يا رسول الله ومن هم قال الآمرون بالمعروف والناهون عن المنكر والمحبون في الله والمبغضون في الله {ثم قال} والذي نفسي بيده إن العبد منهم ليكون في الغرفة فوق الغرفات فوق غرف الشهداء للغرفة منها ثلثمائة ألف
9:112.english: Know that the verses indicating the obligation of commanding right and forbidding wrong are numerous. Among them is His saying, may He be exalted: {«Let there arise from among you a nation inviting to good, commanding right and forbidding wrong — and those are the successful»} (Āl ʿImrān 3:104). In this verse is the declaration of obligation, for His saying, may He be exalted, "Let there be" (wal-takun) is a command, and the apparent meaning of a command is obligation. In it also is the declaration that success (falāḥ) is contingent upon it, for He restricted it and said: {«And those are the successful»}. In it also is the declaration that it is a collective obligation (farḍ kifāyah), not an individual obligation (farḍ ʿayn), and that when a group undertakes it, the obligation falls from the rest — for He did not say, "Let all of you be commanders of right," but rather said: {«Let there arise from among you a nation»}. Thus, whenever one person or a group undertakes it, the burden falls from the others, and success is particularized to those who undertake it and directly perform it. But if all of creation were to hold back from it, the burden would encompass all those capable of it without exception.
9:112.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Remembrance of Death and Afterlife'

10:48.arabic: على الكافرين غير يسير} وقال تعالى {ويقولون متى هذا الوعد إن كنتم صادقين ما ينظرون إلا صيحة واحدة تأخذهم وهم يخصمون فلا يستطيعون توصية ولا إلى أهلهم يرجعون ونفخ في الصور فإذا هم من الأجداث إلى ربهم ينسلون قالوا يا ويلنا من بعثنا من مرقدنا هذا ما وعد الرحمن وصدق المرسلون} فلو لم يكن بين يدي الموتى إلا هول تلك النفخة لكان ذلك جديرا بأن يتقى فإنها نفخة وصيحة يصعق بها من في السموات والأرض يعنى يموتون بها إلا من شاء الله وهو بعض الملائكة ولذلك قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كيف أنعم وصاحب الصور قد التقم القرن وحنى الجبهة
10:48.english: The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: Allah the Exalted said: "The son of Adam has reviled Me, and he had no right to revile Me; and he has denied Me, and he had no right to deny Me. As for his reviling of Me, it is his saying that I have a son. And as for his denial of Me, it is his saying: 'He will never bring me back as He created me at first.'" {«شتمني ابن آدم وما ينبغي له أن يشتمني وكذبني وما ينبغي له أن يكذبني...»}
10:48.section_title_en: On the Terrors of the Trumpet-Blast and the Awakening for the Resurrection
10:48.anchors:
- Root: نفخ (N-F-Kh)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To blow into a thing, to inflate; the breath of wind entering a vessel or body.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The divine act of breathing spirit into creation {«ونفخت فيه من روحي»}; here, the eschatological blast that annihilates and then revives all beings.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah) usage of blowing into the Trumpet (الصور); metaphorical extension to the "blast of spring" reviving the earth—here applied to the two cosmic blasts of death and resurrection.
- Root: صور (S-W-R)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Form, image, shape; also a horn or trumpet (the instrument of the blast).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The perceptible form of bodies and the intelligible form of souls; here, the Trumpet (الصور) as the instrument of divine command that re-forms and re-shapes creation.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the horn (القرن) held by Israfil; metaphorical: the "inclination" (صورة) of hearts toward terror and anticipation.
- Root: موت (M-W-T)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Death as the cessation of life; the state of the corpse.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Death as the separation of the soul from the body; the "first death" of the blast and the "second death" of the wicked.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical death; metaphorical: the "death" of the heart through heedlessness, and the reviving of dead lands by rain—here, the reviving of bodies by the second blast.
- Root: قبر (Q-B-R)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The grave as the abode of the dead; burial.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The grave as the intermediate state (barzakh) before resurrection; {«حتى زرتم المقابر»} as a metaphor for death.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the grave and its inhabitants; metaphorical: the "raising of the nose" (قبراه) of the proud—contrasted here with the humility of the dead rising from their graves.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — Used to emphasize that true faith is not mere verbal assent but heartfelt conviction, as in "إنما فتور البواطن... لقلة الفهم" (The languor of the inner selves is only due to the lack of understanding).
10:48.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'Remembrance of Death and Afterlife'

10:49.arabic: علامات المرض وبهذا يعرف أن القلوب كلها مريضة إلا ما شاء الله إلا أن من الأمراض ما لا يعرفها صاحبها ومرض القلب مما لا يعرفه صاحبه فلذلك يغفل عنه وإن عرفه صعب عليه الصبر على مرارة دوائه فإن دواءه مخالفة الشهوات وهو نزع الروح فإن وجد من نفسه قوة الصبر عليه لم يجد طبيبا حاذقا يعالجه فإن الأطباء هم العلماء وقد استولى عليهم المرض فالطبيب المريض قلما يلتفت إلى علاجه فلهذا صار الداء عضالا والمرض مزمنا واندرس هذا العلم وأنكر بالكلية طب القلوب وأنكر مرضها وأقبل الخلق على حب الدنيا وعلى أعمال ظاهرها عبادات وباطنها
10:49.english: I say: The soul (nafs) that belongs to the human being — that by which he is distinguished from the beasts — for he is not distinguished from them by the power of eating, copulation, sight, or any other such thing. Rather, he is distinguished by the knowledge of things as they truly are. And the Origin of all things, their Existentiator and their Inventor, is God, Mighty and Majestic — He who made them things. So if one knew everything but did not know God, Mighty and Majestic, it would be as though he knew nothing at all. And the sign of knowledge is love: whoever knows God Most High loves Him. And the sign of love is that one does not prefer over Him this world nor any other beloved thing. As God Most High said: {«Say: If your fathers, your sons, your brothers, your spouses, your clans — the wealth you have acquired, commerce whose decline you fear, and dwellings you find pleasing — are more beloved to you than God and His Messenger and striving in His cause, then wait until God brings about His command»} [Q 9:24]. So whoever possesses something more beloved to him than God — his heart is sick. Just as any stomach to which clay has become more beloved than bread and water, or whose appetite for bread and water has fallen away — it is sick. These are the signs of sickness. And by this it is known that all hearts are sick — except what God wills. Yet among sicknesses there are those the sufferer does not recognize; and the sickness of the heart is among those the sufferer does not recognize. For this reason he is heedless of it. And even if he recognized it, patience upon the bitterness of its medicine would be difficult for him — for its medicine is opposing the appetites, and that is the tearing out of the spirit (nafs). And if he found in himself the strength of patience upon it, he would not find a skillful physician to treat him — for the physicians are the scholars, and sickness has overcome them. So the sick physician rarely attends to his own cure. For this reason the malady has become chronic and the sickness chronic. This science has become effaced, and the medicine of hearts is denied entirely, and the sickness of the heart is denied. And creation has turned to the love of this world and to deeds whose outward form is acts of worship but whose inward reality is habit and ostentation. These are the signs of the roots of sicknesses.
10:49.section_title_en: The Soul's Distinction, the Sickness of the Heart, and the Path of Moderation
10:49.anchors:
- Root: نفس (n-f-s)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The self, soul, or spirit; that by which a thing is distinguished in its essential reality
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The soul (nafs) as the principle of rational discrimination and knowledge, distinguishing humans from beasts
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the self or person; Metaphorical: the rational soul as the seat of knowledge and moral responsibility
- Root: مرض (m-r-d)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Departure from the state of health and equilibrium
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Sickness of the heart as a metaphor for moral and spiritual vices — ignorance, cowardice, avarice, hypocrisy
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: bodily illness; Metaphorical: spiritual malady whereby the heart inclines toward what is harmful and away from what is beneficial
- Root: قلب (q-l-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The heart; that which is ever-turning and fluctuating between states
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The heart as the seat of understanding and moral perception; its "turning" (taqlīb) signifies its instability between soundness and sickness
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the physical organ; Metaphorical: the spiritual faculty of cognition and moral discernment
- Root: خلق (kh-l-q)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Measured, proportioned disposition; character and temperament
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Moral character as the inward form (ṣūrah bāṭinah) corresponding to the outward physical form
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: measuring and proportioning; Metaphorical: the ingrained disposition that governs action
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — The use of restrictive constructions to isolate the defining characteristic of the human soul as knowledge of God, not animal appetites
10:49.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Remembrance of Death and Afterlife'

12:76.arabic: كذا كذا فقال أصبت وأخطأت وفوق كل ذي علم عليم واستدرك ابن مسعود على أبي موسى الأشعري رضي الله عنهما فقال أبو موسى لا تسألوني عن شيء وهذا الحبر بين أظهركم وذلك لما سئل أبو موسى عن رجل قاتل في سبيل الله فقتل فقال هو في الجنة وكان أمير الكوفة فقام ابن مسعود فقال أعده على الأمير فلعله لم يفهم فأعادوا عليه فأعاد الجواب فقال ابن مسعود وأنا أقول إن قتل فأصاب الحق فهو في الجنة فقال أبو موسى الحق ما قال وهكذا يكون إنصاف طلب الحق ولو ذكر مثل هذا الآن لأقل فقيه لأنكره واستبعده وقال لا يحتاج إلى أن يقال
12:76.english: The fourth [etiquette]: that he should not dispute except over a matter that has actually occurred, or that is likely to occur in most cases. For the Companions (may God be pleased with them) did not consult one another except over newly arising incidents or what was likely to occur, such as the laws of inheritance (farāʾiḍ). And we do not see the disputants concerning themselves with critiquing questions that are of general affliction (ʿumūm al-balawā) in issuing verdicts about them; rather, they seek out the "drum-beat" questions (ṭubūliyyāt)—those that make noise—so that the field of argumentation widens in them, however the matter may be. PageV01P043
12:76.section_title_en: Section 37 — On the Etiquette of Disputation and the Pursuit of Truth
12:76.anchors:
- Root: نظر (naẓara)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of gazing, examining, and deliberating with the eye of the intellect.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance of speculative reflection (naẓar) as the means to attain knowledge of the unseen and the divine.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) denotes physical sight; metaphorical (majāz) denotes intellectual consideration and weighing of evidence.
- Root: حق (ḥaqqa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The root denotes firmness, reality, and that which is established and undeniable.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance of truth (ḥaqq) as the eternal reality of God and His commands, opposed to falsehood (bāṭil).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal denotes the opposite of falsehood; metaphorical denotes the due right and the correct ruling in a given case.
- Root: خصم (khaṣama)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The root denotes the act of contending, disputing, and overcoming in argument.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance of the adversary (khaṣm) in debate, whose refutation is sought for the sake of truth, not vanity.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal denotes the opponent in a legal contest; metaphorical denotes the one who contends against the truth with fallacious reasoning.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Restriction and Focused Predication (al-ḥaṣr wa al-taqyīd bi-innamā) — Governing the exclusive emphasis on truth-seeking over partisan victory, as in the phrase "the object is truth alone."
12:76.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Book of Knowledge'

12:76.arabic: ولا تقولن لشيء إني فاعل ذلك غدا إلا أن يشاء الله ثم لم يقتصر على ذلك فيما لا يشك فيه بل قال تعالى لتدخلن المسجد الحرام إن شاء الله آمنين محلقين رءؤسكم ومقصرين وكان الله سبحانه عالما بأنهم يدخلون لا محالة وأنه شاءه ولكن المقصود تعليمه ذلك فتأدب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في ما كان يخبر عنه معلوما كان أو مشكوكا حتى قال صلى الله عليه وسلم لما دخل المقابر السلام عليكم دار قوم مؤمنين وإنا إن شاء الله بكم لاحقون (1) واللحوق بهم غير مشكوك فيه ولكن مقتضى الأدب ذكر الله تعالى وربط الأمور به وهذه الصيغ
12:76.english: If you say: "What is the meaning of the Salaf's statement, 'I am a believer, if God wills' — given that the exception (istithnā') implies doubt, and doubt in faith is unbelief? Yet they all refrained from giving an unqualified answer affirming faith and were cautious about it."
12:76.section_title_en: On the Meaning of the Salaf's Statement "I am a Believer, If God Wills" — Section 102
12:76.anchors:
- Root: نفس (n-f-s)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The self, the soul; that which is breathed; the innermost reality of a person.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): النفس is used for the rūḥ (spirit), for the dhāt (essence/self), and for the seat of intention and knowledge. When one says "he knows in himself (nafsihi) that he is a believer," it denotes certitude residing in the very core of one's being, not a corporeal faculty.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) usage refers to the soul's reflexive self-awareness; metaphorical (majāz) usage extends to "blood" (dam) or "the eye" (ʿayn) of envy. Here, "in himself" (fī nafsihi) is literal self-knowledge, not mere outward profession.
- Root: وجه (w-j-h)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Face, countenance; the foremost part; a mode, aspect, or direction.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The face is the most noble apparent part of a thing; hence it is used for the "aspect" or "manner" (wajh) of an affair. "Four aspects" (wujūh) means four distinct modes of interpretation or rational grounds.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the face of a person or object. Metaphorical: "the face of the matter" (wajh al-amr) — its most salient and honorable dimension. Here, the "aspects" are hermeneutical angles, not physical parts.
- Root: ايم (a-y-m)
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The unmarried state (aym); one who has no spouse. Not applicable here directly, but the root's semantic field of "being alone/without attachment" contrasts with īmān's root (a-m-n) — security and trust — which is the operative term in this text.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Not directly relevant; the operative root is أمن (a-m-n), meaning security from fear, and by extension, faith (īmān) as the state of being secure in God's truth.
- Root: كان (k-w-n)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To be, to exist; the copula of predication.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Kāna denotes existence and becoming; in theological usage, it grounds the distinction between what is (mawjūd) and what is merely asserted. The question "Are you a believer?" (a-mu'min anta?) uses kāna implicitly to ask about actual, present state — not future contingency.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: existence. Metaphorical: the "being-so" of a predicate. The istithnā' (exception) with "in shā' Allāh" suspends the copula's certainty, shifting from assertive existence to contingent hope.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الاستثناء والتعليق بالمشيئة (The Chapter of Exception and Suspension by the Divine Will) — When an exception clause (istithnā') follows a positive assertion, it grammatically suspends the universality or certainty of the predication. In theological discourse, this suspension may be semantic (doubt) or pragmatic (deference, etiquette, or self-deprecation), and Sibawayh's parsing of conditional suspension (taʿlīq) shows that the apodosis need not be negated — only its absolute, unqualified force is tempered.
12:76.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Remembrance of Death and Afterlife'

13:15.arabic: وهو أحد والآصال التي ذكرها الله تعالى إذ قال ولله يسجد من في السموات والأرض طوعا وكرها وظلالهم بالغدو والآصال وإذا سجد لله عز وجل الجمادات فكيف يجوز أن يغفل العبد العاقل عن أنواع العبادات الورد السادس إذا دخل وقت العصر دخل وقت الورد السادس وهو الذي أقسم الله تعالى به فقال تعالى {والعصر} هذا أحد معنيي الآية وهو المراد بالآصال في أحد التفسيرين وهو العشي المذكور في قوله {وعشيا} وفي قوله {بالعشي والإشراق} وليس في هذا الورد صلاة إلا أربع ركعات بين الأذان والإقامة كما سبق في الظهر ثم يصلي الفرض ويشتغل بالأقسام الأربعة المذكورة
13:15.english: I say: And just as knowledge and remembrance are the nourishment of the heart, which can never be cut off from it, so too the measure of moderation is this; and deficiency from it may lead to the disturbance of the body — except for one who accustoms himself to wakefulness gradually, for he may train himself upon it without disturbance. And this litany (wird) is among the longest of the litanies and the most delightful for the worshippers, and it is one of the "evenings and mornings" (al-āṣāl) which God Most High mentioned when He said: {«ولله يسجد من في السموات والأرض طوعا وكرها وظلالهم بالغدو والآصال»} "And to God prostrates whoever is in the heavens and the earth, willingly or unwillingly, and their shadows, in the mornings and the evenings" (Q. 13:15). And when inanimate objects prostrate to God, Mighty and Majestic, how then can the intelligent servant be heedless of the varieties of worship?
13:15.section_title_en: The Seventh Daily Litany (Al-Wird al-Sābiʿ): The Time of Sunset — The Completion of the Day's Litanies and Self-Accounting
13:15.anchors:
- Root: ورد (warada)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The root denotes arriving at water, seeking it, and drinking from it; also the portion or share of water allotted for drinking at a specific time.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الورود أصله: قصد الماء" — the core meaning is the intentional approach to water; the litany (wird) is the appointed portion of devotional recitation, likened to the daily share of water that a person must take to sustain life.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): the act of arriving at water. Metaphorical (Majaz): "ورد علي كتاب سرني مورده" — a book arrived upon me whose arrival pleased me; likewise, the wird is the arrival of the appointed time for worship, and the soul's approach to the fountain of divine remembrance.
- Root: عصر (ʿaṣr)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The root denotes pressing, squeezing, and extracting; also the time of afternoon, so called because it is the pressing of the day's end.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The ʿaṣr is the latter part of the day; God swore by it in {«والعصر»} (Q. 103:1), indicating its great merit.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the afternoon time. Metaphorical: the pressing of one's life — as the day is pressed at its end, so the life of man is pressed at its term.
- Root: غرب (gharaba)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The root denotes disappearance, absence, and setting; the sun's setting (ghurūb) is its concealment from the eye.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The setting of the sun marks the boundary between the day's works and the night's; it is the terminus of the visible world's diurnal cycle.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the sun's descent below the horizon. Metaphorical: the setting of the sun of life — the death of man, after which there is no rising.
- Root: حاسب (ḥāsaba)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The root denotes reckoning, counting, and taking account; muḥāsabah is the mutual reckoning between two parties.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Self-accounting (muḥāsabat al-nafs) is the soul's reckoning with itself over its deeds before the Day of Reckoning, for "one who reckons himself before he is reckoned" is among the wise.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the arithmetic counting of sums. Metaphorical: the soul's audit of its own works, weighing the day's deeds against the standard of the Sacred Law.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The rule governing the separation of the prepositional phrase from its governing verb, as in the construction "فسبحان الله حين تمسون" where the adverbial clause is interposed to emphasize the temporal specification of the act of glorification.
13:15.topic: Al-Ghazali on constant remembrance of God and contemplative invocations, from 'Remembrance of Death and Afterlife'

13:42.arabic: اللهم إنك علمت ما تكسب كل نفس قبل أن تخلقها فلا محيص لها مما علمت فاجعلني ممن تستعمله بطاعتك اللهم إن أحدا لا يشاء حتى تشاء فاجعل مشيئتك أن أشاء ما يقربني إليك اللهم إنك قد قدرت حركات العباد فلا يتحرك شيء إلا بإذنك فاجعل حركاتي في تقواك اللهم إنك خلقت الخير والشر وجعلت لكل واحد منهما عاملا يعمل به فاجعلني من خير القسمين اللهم إنك خلقت الجنة والنار وجعلت لكل واحدة منهما أهلا فاجعلني من سكان جنتك اللهم إنك أردت بقوم الضلال وضيقت به صدورهم فاشرح صدري للإيمان وزينه في قلبي
13:42.english: When Abu Bakr (may Allah Most High be pleased with him) was in the throes of death, ʿĀʾishah (may Allah be pleased with her) came and recited this verse: "By your life, wealth avails not the youth... when the breath rattles in his chest one day, and the breast is straitened thereby."
13:42.section_title_en: The Death of Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (may Allah Most High be pleased with him)
13:42.anchors:
- Root: حشرج (ḥashraja)
  * Lisan / Ayn: [Core linguistic root meaning: The rattling, gurgling sound of the death-throe in the throat; the final breath struggling in the chest.]
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): [Theological/Kalam semantic nuance: The terminal state of the soul's separation from the body, the moment of overwhelming divine decree.]
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): [Literal vs Metaphorical distinction: Literal — the physical rattle of the dying; Metaphorical — the constriction of the breast as the soul is drawn forth.]
- Root: سكر (sakara)
  * Lisan / Ayn: [Core linguistic root meaning: The veiling of the intellect; intoxication; the stupor that overcomes one at the onset of death.]
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): [Theological/Kalam semantic nuance: The stupor of death (sakrat al-mawt) as the removal of all veils, wherein the truth of the Hereafter becomes undeniably present.]
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): [Literal vs Metaphorical distinction: Literal — intoxication from drink; Metaphorical — the overwhelming bewilderment of the soul at death's onset.]
- Root: ذمم (dhimam)
  * Lisan / Ayn: [Core linguistic root meaning: The covenant of protection; the bond of safe-conduct; that which one is obligated to honor and safeguard.]
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): [Theological/Kalam semantic nuance: The divine guarantee (dhimmat Allah) extended to the believer who prays the dawn prayer — a sacred pact not to be violated.]
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): [Literal vs Metaphorical distinction: Literal — a pledge of security between men; Metaphorical — the inviolable covenant between the servant and his Lord.]
- Root: وزن (wazana)
  * Lisan / Ayn: [Core linguistic root meaning: To weigh; the balance; the measure of equivalence between two things.]
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): [Theological/Kalam semantic nuance: The weighing of deeds on the Day of Resurrection as the manifestation of divine justice — the scales (mawāzīn) receiving only truth or falsehood.]
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): [Literal vs Metaphorical distinction: Literal — the physical act of weighing; Metaphorical — the spiritual weighing of deeds by their conformity to truth (ḥaqq) or falsehood (bāṭil).]
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — [The particle innamā restricts the predicate exclusively to its subject, as in Abu Bakr's dictum: "It is only that the scales of those whose scales are heavy on the Day of Resurrection are weighed down by their following the truth in this world."]
13:42.topic: Al-Ghazali on the journey of the soul, death, and the Hereafter, from 'Remembrance of Death and Afterlife'

14:11.arabic: الروح من أمره على من يشاء من عباده} وأحال الإغواء على إبليس فقال تعالى {ليضل عن سبيله} والإغواء هو استيقاف العباد دون بلوغ غاية الحكمة فانظر كيف نسبه إلى العبد الذي غضب عليه والإرشاد سياقه لهم إلى الغاية فانظر كيف نسبه إلى العبد الذي أحبه وعندك في العادة له مثال فالملك إذا كان محتاجا إلى من يسقيه الشراب وإلى من يحجمه وينظف فناء منزله عن القاذورات وكان له عبدان فلا يعين للحجامة والتنظيف إلا أقبحهما وأخسهما ولا يفوض حمل الشراب والطيب إلا إلى أحسنهما وأكملهما وأحبهما إليه ولا ينبغ
14:11.english: Thus was the beginning of this matter and its end. And do not understand it unless you are worthy of it. And if you are worthy of it, the eye is opened and you see, so you have no need of a leader to lead you. The blind man can indeed be led, but only to a limit. For when the path narrows and becomes sharper than a sword and finer than a hair, the bird is able to fly over it but is not able to drag a blind man behind it. And when the field becomes narrow and subtle — subtle as water, for example — and crossing is possible only by swimming, then the one skilled in the art of swimming may be able to cross by himself, and perhaps he is not able to drag another behind him. These matters bear the same relation to walking upon the way of the common masses of creatures as walking upon water bears to walking upon earth. Swimming can be learned; but as for walking upon water, it is not acquired by instruction, but rather is attained through the strength of certainty (yaqīn). For this reason it was said to the Prophet, peace be upon him, that Jesus, peace be upon him, was said to have walked upon water, and he, peace be upon him, said: "Had his certainty increased, he would have walked upon the air." {«حديث قيل له يقال إن عيسى مشى على الماء قال لو ازداد يقينا لمشي على الهواء»} — This hadith is rejected (munkar) and is not known in this form. What is known is what Ibn Abi al-Dunya narrated in the Book of Certainty from the saying of Bakr ibn Abd Allah al-Muzani, who said: The disciples lost their Prophet, and it was said to them: "He has headed toward the sea." So they set out seeking him, and when they reached the sea, behold, he was coming toward them walking upon the water. And he mentioned a hadith in which Jesus said: "If the son of Adam had a hair's breadth of certainty, he would walk upon the water." And Abu Mansur al-Daylami narrated in the Musnad al-Firdaws with a weak chain from the hadith of Muadh ibn Jabal: "If you knew God with true knowledge, you would walk upon the seas, and the mountains would be removed by your supplications." These are symbols and allusions to the meaning of aversion (karāhah) and love (maḥabbah), and good pleasure (riḍā) and wrath (ghaḍab), and gratitude (shukr) and ingratitude (kufrān) — more than this is not fitting for the science of practical conduct (ʿilm al-muʿāmalah). And God, exalted be He, struck an example of this to draw it near to the understanding of creatures, since He knew that He created the jinn and mankind only to worship Him, and their worship was the ultimate purpose of wisdom (ghāyat al-ḥikmah) with respect to them. Then He informed that He has two servants: one whom He loves, whose name is Gabriel — the Holy Spirit and the Trustworthy One — and he is with Him beloved, obeyed, trustworthy, and honored; and another whom He hates, whose name is Iblis — the accursed one, reprieved until the Day of Judgment. Then He delegated guidance (irshād) to Gabriel, saying, the Exalted: {«قل نزله روح القدس من ربك بالحق»} "Say: The Holy Spirit has brought it down from your Lord with truth" (16:102), and said, the Exalted: {«يلقي الروح من أمره على من يشاء من عباده»} "He casts the Spirit of His command upon whom He wills of His servants" (40:15). And He delegated misguidance (ighwāʾ) to Iblis, saying, the Exalted: {«ليضل عن سبيله»} "That he may lead astray from His path" (4:119). And ighwāʾ is the halting of servants short of attaining the ultimate purpose of wisdom. So observe how He attributed it to the servant with whom He was wrathful; and guidance (irshād) is the conduct of them toward the ultimate purpose — so observe how He attributed it to the servant whom He loves. And you have an example of this in custom: when a king is in need of one to give him drink and one to cup him and to clean the courtyard of his house of filth, and he has two servants, he does not appoint for cupping and cleaning except the ugliest and meanest of them, and he does not entrust the carrying of drink and perfume except to the best and most complete of them and the most beloved to him. And you should not say: "This is my act, and his act was not without my act" — for you have erred when you attributed that to yourself. Rather, He is the One who directed your motive (dāʿiyah) to the specification of the disliked act to the disliked person, and the beloved act to the beloved person, as a completion of justice (ʿadl). For His justice is sometimes completed through matters in which you have no entry, and sometimes it is completed in you — for you also are among His acts. So your motive, your power, your knowledge, your action, and all the other causes of your movements in expression — all of this is His act, which He arranged with justice in an arrangement from which moderate acts issue forth. Except that you see only yourself, and so you suppose that what appears through you in the world of witness (ʿālam al-shahādah) has no cause from the world of the unseen and the dominion (ʿālam al-ghayb wa al-malakūt). Therefore you attribute it to yourself. And you are only like the child who looks at night at the play of the juggler (mushʿabadh) who brings forth figures from behind a curtain that dance and scream and rise and sit, composed of rags that do not move by themselves — rather, they are moved by fine hair-like threads that do not appear in the darkness of night, their ends in the hand of the juggler, who is hidden from the eyes of the children. So they rejoice and marvel, supposing that those rags dance and play and rise and sit. As for the intelligent ones, they know that this is a moving (taḥrīk) and not a self-movement, but perhaps they do not know its detailed modality. And the one who knows some of its detail does not know it as the juggler knows it, to whom the command belongs and in whose hand is the pulling. Likewise, the children of the people of this world — and all creatures are children relative to the scholars — look at these persons (ashkhāṣ) and suppose that they are the movers, and so they attribute [action] to them. And the scholars know that they are moved, except that they do not know the modality of the moving — and they are the majority. Except the knowers (ʿārifūn), the scholars, and those firmly rooted in knowledge (al-rāsikhūn), for they have perceived, with the sharpness of their sight, fine spider-web threads — nay, much finer than these — suspended from heaven, their ends attached to the persons of the people of the earth. Those threads are not perceived, due to their fineness, by these outward eyes. Then they witnessed the heads of those threads in their suspension-points (manāṭāt) to which they are attached, and they witnessed for those suspension-points handles (maqābiḍ) that are in the hands of the angels who move the heavens. And they also witnessed the angels of the heavens directed toward the bearers of the Throne (ḥamalat al-ʿarsh), awaiting what descends upon them of the command from the presence of Lordship (ḥaḍrat al-rubūbiyyah) — "they do not disobey God in what He commands them, and they do what they are commanded" (66:6). And He expressed these witnessed realities in the Qur'an, and it was said: {«وفي السماء رزقكم وما توعدون»} "And in the heaven is your provision and what you are promised" (51:22). And He expressed the waiting of the angels of the heavens for what descends upon them of decree and command, and it was said: "He created seven heavens and of the earth the like of them; {«يتنزل الأمر بينهن لتعلموا أن الله على كل شيء قدير وأن الله قد أحاط بكل شيء علما»} 'the command descends between them, that you may know that God is powerful over all things and that God encompasses all things in knowledge'" (65:12). These are matters whose interpretation (taʾwīl) none knows except God and those firmly rooted in knowledge (al-rāsikhūn fī al-ʿilm). And Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, expressed the exclusivity of those firmly rooted in knowledge to sciences that the understandings of creatures cannot bear, when he recited the saying of the Exalted: {«يتنزل الأمر بينهن»} "The command descends between them," and said: "Were I to mention what I know of the meaning of this verse, you would stone me" — and in another wording: "You would say he is an unbeliever."
14:11.section_title_en: On the Degrees of Proximity to God and the Hierarchy of Those Who Perfect Divine Wisdom
14:11.anchors:
- Root: سير (s-y-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "السير: الذهاب والسفر، وسار يسير سيرا ومسيرا، والسيارة: الرفقة المسافرة"
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "السير: الانتقال من مكان إلى مكان، ويستعار للسلوك في الدين والطريقة"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): [Literal] "سار القوم: مشوا" — [Metaphorical] "سار فيه السير: مضى في الأمر، وسار ذكره: انتشر، ومنه: سيرة فلان: طريقته"
- Root: مشي (m-sh-y)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "المشي: تردد الأركان على الأرض، والماشية: الإبل والغنم لانتقالها في المرعى"
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "المشي: الانتقال من مكان إلى مكان بإرادة، ويكنى به عن النميمة، وعن شرب المسهل"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): [Literal] "مشيت وتمشيت، وهي حسنة المشية" — [Metaphorical] "مشى بطنه، وأمشاه الدواء، واستمشيت بالدواء، ومنه: مشت المرأة: كثرت أولادها"
- Root: خلق (kh-l-q)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الخلق: التقدير، والخلق: الناس، والخليقة: الطبيعة، والخلق: السجية"
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الخلق أصله: التقدير المستقيم، ويستعمل في إبداع الشيء من غير أصل ولا احتذاء"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): [Literal] "خلق الخراز الأديم: قدره قبل القطع" — [Metaphorical] "خلق الله الخلق: أوجده على تقدير أوجبته الحكمة"
- Root: نفس (n-f-s)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "النفس: الروح، والذات، والشيء النفيس"
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "النفس: الروح، وتطلق على الذات، قال تعالى: {ويحذركم الله نفسه} فنفسه: ذاته"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): [Literal] "شيء نفيس ومنفس" — [Metaphorical] "دفق نفسه أي دمه، وأصابته نفس: عين"
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — Used to distinguish exclusive attribution of actions to God versus creatures, as in "إنما أنت مثل الصبي" (You are only like a child), restricting the simile to the creature while preserving divine agency.
14:11.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'Remembrance of Death and Afterlife'

14:16.arabic: أبو أمامة قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في قوله تعالى ويسقى من ماء صديد يتجرعه ولا يكاد يسيغه {قال} يقرب إليه فيتكرهه فإذا أدني منه شوي وجهه فوقعت فروة رأسه فإذا شربه قطع أمعاءه حتى يخرج من دبره يقول الله تعالى {وسقوا ماء حميما فقطع أمعاءهم} وقال تعالى {وإن يستغيثوا يغاثوا بماء كالمهل يشوى الوجوه} فهذه طعامهم وشرابهم عند جوعهم وعطشهم (1) فانظر الآن إلى حيات جهنم وعقاربها وإلى شدة سمومها وعظم أشخاصها وفظاظة منظرها وقد سلطت على أهلها وأغريت بهم فهي لا تفتر عن النهش واللدغ ساعة واحدة قال أبو هريرة قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم من أتاه الله
14:16.english: At that point they despair of every good, and at that point they take to sighing, regret, and wailing. Abu Umamah said: The Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, said concerning His words, "And he is given to drink of festering water, which he sips but can hardly swallow" {«وَيُسْقَىٰ مِن مَّاءٍ صَدِيدٍ يَتَجَرَّعُهُ وَلَا يَكَادُ يُسِيغُهُ»}: "It is brought near to him, and he loathes it. When it is drawn close to him, it scorches his face, and the skin of his scalp falls off. When he drinks it, it severs his intestines until it exits from his anus." God Almighty says: {«وَسُقُوا مَاءً حَمِيمًا فَقَطَّعَ أَمْعَاءَهُمْ»} "And they are given to drink boiling water, and it severs their intestines." And He says: {«وَإِن يَسْتَغِيثُوا يُغَاثُوا بِمَاءٍ كَالْمُهْلِ يَشْوِي الْوُجُوهَ»} "And if they cry for relief, they are relieved with water like molten brass, which scalds the faces." So this is their food and drink in their hunger and thirst.
14:16.section_title_en: The Torments of the Fire: Serpents, Scorpions, and the Anguish of the Damned
14:16.anchors:
- Root: حس (ḥ-s-s) — [AVOIDED per instruction]
- Root: نار (n-r) — Fire
  * Lisan al-Arab: "النار: معروفة، وهي نار جهنم، ذات لفح وحرّ."
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "النار: قد تطلق على نار الدنيا ونار الآخرة، وهي التي أعدها الله للكافرين، وفيها من أصناف العذاب ما لا يعلمه إلا الله."
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "نار: حقيقة في النار المحرقة، ومجاز في نار الحرب والحرب."
- Root: حي (ḥ-y) — Serpent
  * Lisan al-Arab: "الحية: من الهوام، وتجمع على حيات، وأعظمها ما كان كأعناق البخت."
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الحية: دابة مؤذية، وفي الآخرة تكون أعظم وأشد إيلامًا."
- Root: عقر (ʿ-q-r) — Scorpion
  * Lisan al-Arab: "العقرب: دويبة مؤذية تلدغ، وفي النار تكون كالبغال."
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — Used to specify that serpents and scorpions are only empowered over those who were dominated by miserliness and evil character in the world.

14:16.arabic: من العطش فيسقى أحرهم من ماء صديد يتجرعه ولا يكاد يسيغه ويأتيه الموت من كل مكان وما هو يميت وإن يستغيثوا يغاثوا بماء كالمهل يشوي الوجوه بئس الشراب وساءت مرتفقا ثم انظر إلى طعامهم وهو الزقوم كما قال الله تعالى {ثم إنكم أيها الضالون المكذبون لآكلون من شجر من زقوم فمالئون منها البطون فشاربون عليه من الحميم فشاربون شرب الهيم} وقال تعالى {إنها شجرة تخرج في أصل الجحيم طلعها كأنه رؤوس الشياطين فإنهم لآكلون منها فمالئون منها البطون ثم إن لهم عليها لشوبا من حميم ثم إن مرجعهم لإلى الجحيم} وقال تعالى {تصلى نارا حامية تسقى من عين آنية} وقال تعالى {إن لدين
14:16.english: And ʿAlī, may God honor his face, said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: "Seek refuge in God from the Pit of Sorrow, or the Valley of Sorrow." It was said: "O Messenger of God, what is the Valley or Pit of Sorrow?" He said: "A valley in Hell from which Hell itself seeks refuge with God seventy times each day. God, the Exalted, has prepared it for the reciters who show off." (2)
14:16.section_title_en: The Vastness of Hellfire, Its Depths, and the Torments of Its Inhabitants
14:16.anchors:
- Root: و د ي (w-d-y)
  * Lisan / Ayn: A valley; a place where torrents flow. In the lexicon, it denotes a lowland or watercourse between mountains.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Used for the valleys of Hell as places of confinement and passage, each containing further branching ravines (شُعَب), indicating graded descent.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal for earthly valleys; here transferred (majāz) to the topographical reality of Hell, affirming its corporeal vastness.
- Root: ع م ق (ʿ-m-q)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Depth; the far bottom of a well or pit. Al-Farahidi: "العمق: قعر البئر ونحوها."
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Depth as a measure of descent; in the Hereafter, it is unbounded, paralleling the unbounded depth of worldly desire.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal for physical depth; here extended to show the infinite regress of punishment corresponding to infinite craving.
- Root: غ س ق (gh-s-q)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Stinking, foul pus or ichor that flows from the skin of the damned; also intense darkness.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-Ghassāq is the putrid effusion of Hell, a punishment for the senses, specifically for drinking when the damned cry out in thirst.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal for what is loathsome and fetid; in the Quranic context, it is the designated drink of the inhabitants.
- Root: ز ق م (z-q-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To swallow with difficulty; the tree of Zaqqūm, which grows in the depths of Hell.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): A specific tree in Hell whose fruit is like the heads of devils, eaten by the damned to fill their bellies, causing choking and agony.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal for a real tree; its description is sensory, not metaphorical, affirming the physical reality of punishment.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The periodic structure of "في جهنم سبعين ألف واد" allows the prepositional phrase to precede the subject for emphasis, establishing the spatial setting before detailing its contents.

14:21.arabic: غاية شدة العذاب قال مالك بن أنس رضي الله عنه قال زيد بن أسلم في قوله تعالى {سواء علينا أجزعنا أم صبرنا ما لنا من محيص} قال صبروا مائة سنة ثم جزعوا مائة سنة ثم صبروا مائة سنة ثم قالوا {سواء علينا أجزعنا أم صبرنا} وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم يؤتى بالموت يوم القيامة كأنه كبش أملح فيذبح بين الجنة والنار ويقال يا أهل الجنة خلود بلا موت ويا أهل النار خلود بلا موت (1) وعن الحسن قال يخرج من النار رجل بعد ألف عام وليتني كنت ذلك الرجل ورؤي الحسن رضي الله عنه جالسا في زاوية وهو يبكي فقيل له لم تبكي فقال أخشى أن يطرحني في النار ولا يبالي فهذه أصناف عذاب جهنم على الجمل
14:21.english: At that point they despair of every good, and at that point they take to sighing, regret, and wailing. Abu Umamah said: The Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, said concerning His words, "And he is given to drink of festering water, which he sips but can hardly swallow" {«وَيُسْقَىٰ مِن مَّاءٍ صَدِيدٍ يَتَجَرَّعُهُ وَلَا يَكَادُ يُسِيغُهُ»}: "It is brought near to him, and he loathes it. When it is drawn close to him, it scorches his face, and the skin of his scalp falls off. When he drinks it, it severs his intestines until it exits from his anus." God Almighty says: {«وَسُقُوا مَاءً حَمِيمًا فَقَطَّعَ أَمْعَاءَهُمْ»} "And they are given to drink boiling water, and it severs their intestines." And He says: {«وَإِن يَسْتَغِيثُوا يُغَاثُوا بِمَاءٍ كَالْمُهْلِ يَشْوِي الْوُجُوهَ»} "And if they cry for relief, they are relieved with water like molten brass, which scalds the faces." 14:36.arabic: إبراهيم عليه السلام {رب إنهن أضللن كثيرا من الناس فمن تبعني فإنه مني ومن عصاني فإنك غفور رحيم} وقول عيسى عليه السلام {إن تعذبهم فإنهم عبادك} ثم رفع يديه وقال أمتي أمتي ثم بكى فقال الله عز وجل يا جبريل اذهب إلى محمد فسله ما يبكيك فأتاه جبريل فسأله فأخبره والله أعلم به فقال يا جبريل اذهب إلى محمد فقل له إنا سنرضيك في أمتك ولا نسوءك (1) وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم أعطيت خمسا لم يعطهن أحد قبل نصرت بالرعب مسيرة شهر وأحلت لي الغنائم ولم تحل لأحد قبلي وجعلت لي الأرض مسجدا وترابها طهورا فأيما رجل من أمتي أدركته الصلاة فليصل وأعطيت الشفاعة وكل نبي بعث
14:36.english: The evidences for intercession in the Qurʾān and the reports (akhbār) are numerous. God—exalted be He—said: {«وَلَسَوْفَ يُعْطِيكَ رَبُّكَ فَتَرْضَىٰ»} [And verily thy Lord shall give thee, and thou shalt be well-pleased] (93:5). ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ narrated that the Messenger of God—peace and blessings be upon him—recited the saying of Abraham—peace be upon him—{«رَبِّ إِنَّهُنَّ أَضْلَلْنَ كَثِيرًا مِّنَ النَّاسِ ۖ فَمَن تَبِعَنِي فَإِنَّهُ مِنِّي ۖ وَمَنْ عَصَانِي فَإِنَّكَ غَفُورٌ رَّحِيمٌ»} [My Lord, verily they have led astray many of mankind; so whoso follows me, verily he is of me; and whoso disobeys me, verily Thou art Forgiving, Merciful] (14:36), and the saying of Jesus—peace be upon him—{«إِن تُعَذِّبْهُمْ فَإِنَّهُمْ عِبَادُكَ»} [If Thou chastise them, verily they are Thy servants] (5:118). Then he raised his hands and said: "My community, my community!" Then he wept. So God—mighty and majestic—said: "O Gabriel, go to Muhammad and ask him what makes him weep." Gabriel came to him and asked him, and he informed him—and God knows best concerning him. Then He said: "O Gabriel, go to Muhammad and say to him: 'Verily We shall please thee concerning thy community, and shall not cause thee grief.'"
14:36.section_title_en: On the Reality of Intercession (Shafāʿah) and the Means of Attaining It
14:36.anchors:
- Root: شفع (Sh-F-ʿ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root denotes pairing/joining (al-ḍamm), whence shafāʿah = the intercessor joining his own plea to the petitioner's, making it two (shafʿ) rather than one (watr).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance — intercession is a divinely granted honor (jāh) bestowed upon prophets and saints, not an independent power; its efficacy is wholly contingent upon divine will and pleasure.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) — "شفعت الشيء" (I made it even/pair). Metaphorical (majāz) — the intercessor "pairs" his rank with the sinner's need, elevating the latter through the former's proximity to God.
- Root: خبأ (Kh-B-ʾ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To conceal, hide, store away secretly (khabaʾa). Implies deliberate concealment of something precious or dangerous within a locus.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance — God's "hiding" (takhbiʾah) of His friendship (wilāyah), wrath (ghaḍab), and pleasure (riḍā) within creatures and acts respectively teaches epistemic humility: no outward judgment can access the hidden decree.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — physical concealment. Metaphorical — the inscrutability of divine judgment (ḥukm) regarding ultimate states (ʿawāqib), rendering contempt for any person or act a potential act of defiance against God's hidden will.
- Root: عله (not applicable here; avoided per instruction)
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — Governing the periodic suspension of meaning across lengthy narrative sequences (e.g., the extended ḥadīth of intercession), where the syntactic resolution (jawāb) is deferred to heighten rhetorical impact, yet remains grammatically anchored.
14:36.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'Remembrance of Death and Afterlife'

14:42.arabic: ويوم لا تجزي نفس عن نفس شيئا ويوم تشخص فيه الأبصار ويوم لا يغنى مولى عن مولى شيئا ويوم لا تملك نفس لنفس شيئا ويوم يدعون إلى نار جهنم دعا ويوم يسحبون فى النار على وجوههم ويوم تقلب وجوههم فى النار ويوم لا يجزى والد عن ولده ويوم يفر المرء من أخيه وأمه وأبيه ويوم لا ينطقون ولا يؤذن لهم فيعتذرون يوم لا مرد له من الله يوم هم بارزون ويوم هم على النار يفتنون يوم لا ينفع مال ولا بنون يوم لا ينفع الظالمين معذرتهم ولهم اللعنة ولهم سوء الدار يوم ترد فيه المعاذير وتبلى السرائر وتظهر الضمائر وتكشف الأستار يوم تخشع فيه الأبصار وتسكن الأصوات ويقل فيه الالتفات وتبرز الخفيات وتظهر الخطيئات يوم يساق العباد ومعهم الأشهاد ويشيب الصغير ويسكر الكبير فيومئذ وضعت الموازين ونشرت الدواوين وبرزت الجحيم وأغلى الحميم وزفرت النار ويئس الكفار وسعرت النيران وتغيرت الألوان وخرس اللسان ونطقت جوارح الإنسان فيا أيها الإنسان ما غرك بربك الكريم حيث أغلقت الأبواب وأرخيت الستور واستترت عن الخلائق فقارفت الفجور فماذا تفعل وقد شهدت عليك جوارحك فالويل كل الويل لنا معشر الغافلين يرسل الله لنا سيد المرسلين وينزل عليه الكتاب المبين ويخبرنا بهذه الصفات من نعوت يوم الدين ثم يعرفنا غفلتنا ويقول اقترب الناس حسابهم وهم في غفلة معرضون ما يأتيهم من ذكر من ربهم محدث إلا استمعوه وهم يلعبون لاهية قلوبهم ثم يعرفنا قرب القيامة فيقول اقتربت الساعة وانشق القمر إنهم يرونه بعيدا ونراه قريبا وما يدريك لعل الساعة تكون قريبا ثم يكون أحسن أحوالنا أن نتخذ دراسة هذا القرآن عملا فلا نتدبر معانيه ولا ننظر في كثرة أوصاف هذا اليوم وأساميه ولا نستعد للتخلص من دواهيه فنعوذ بالله من هذه الغفلة إن لم يداركنا الله بواسع رحمته
14:42.english: So prepare yourself, O wretched one, for this Day of immense magnitude, of prolonged duration, of overwhelming dominion, whose appointed time is near — a Day when you shall see the heaven split asunder, and the stars scattered in its terror, and the shining planets extinguished, and the sun folded up, and the mountains set in motion, and the pregnant camels neglected, and the wild beasts gathered together, and the seas set ablaze, and the souls paired with their bodies, and the Hellfire ignited, and Paradise brought near, and the mountains pulverized, and the earth stretched out — a Day when you shall see the earth shaken with its quaking, and the earth casts forth its burdens. On that Day shall people issue forth in scattered groups to be shown their deeds — a Day when the earth and the mountains are lifted and crushed with a single crushing. Then on that Day the Imminent Event shall come to pass, and the heaven shall split open, for on that Day it shall be frail, and the angels shall be at its edges, and eight shall bear the Throne of your Lord above them on that Day. On that Day you shall be presented — no secret of yours shall remain hidden. A Day when the mountains shall move and you shall see the earth laid bare — a Day when the earth shall be shaken with a violent shaking, and the mountains crumbled to dust, becoming scattered particles — a Day when people shall be like scattered moths, and the mountains like carded wool — a Day when every nursing mother shall forget what she nursed, and every pregnant female shall cast down her burden, and you shall see people drunk, yet they are not drunk, but the chastisement of God is severe — a Day when the earth shall be changed to other than this earth, and the heavens, and they shall appear before God, the One, the All-Compelling — a Day when the mountains shall be blown away as dust, leaving a level, bare plain, wherein you see no crookedness nor curve — a Day when you see the mountains and suppose them solid, yet they pass by like the passing of clouds — a Day when the heaven shall split open and become rosy like molten oil. Then on that Day no human nor jinn shall be asked about his sin. A Day when the disobedient shall be prevented from speech, and shall not be asked about their crimes, but shall be seized by their forelocks and their feet — a Day when every soul shall find what it did of good brought forth present, and what it did of evil, wishing that between it and that evil there were a far distance — a Day when every soul shall know what it has sent ahead, and shall witness what it has forwarded and what it has left behind — a Day when tongues shall be struck mute and the bodily members shall speak — a Day whose mention turned the hair of the Master of the Messengers white, when al-Ṣiddīq (may God be pleased with him) said to him: "I see that you have turned white-haired, O Messenger of God." He said: "Sūrat Hūd and its sisters have made me white-haired" — namely, al-Wāqiʿah, al-Mursalāt, ʿAmma Yatasāʾalūn, and Idhā al-Shamsu Kuwwirat.
14:42.section_title_en: The Names and Attributes of the Day of Resurrection — An Exhortation to the Negligent
14:42.anchors:
- Root: يوم (yawm)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "اليوم: وقت طلوع الشمس إلى غروبها، وقد يعبر به عن مدة من الزمان أي مدة كانت" — the day as a temporal span, extended metaphorically to any epoch or era.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "اليوم يعبر به عن وقت طلوع الشمس إلى غروبها. وقد يعبر به عن مدة من الزمان أي مدة كانت" — theological usage denotes the appointed time of reckoning, magnified by divine attribution (أيام الله).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): a measured solar period. Metaphorical (Majaz): "ذكر في أيام العرب كذا أي في وقائعها" — days as epochal events; thus "the Day" is the supreme epochal event of divine justice.
- Root: نفس (nafs)
  * Lisan / Ayn: النفس: الروح والذات — the self, soul, or very essence.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "النفس: الروح... وقوله: ويحذركم الله نفسه فنفسه: ذاته" — nafs as the innermost reality of a being; in the eschatological context, souls are "paired" (زوجت) with bodies for judgment.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the soul as life-principle. Metaphorical: "دفق نفسه أي دمه" — nafs as the total self, accountable in its entirety.
- Root: ارض (arḍ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: الأرض: الجرم المقابل للسماء — the earth as the corporeal substratum beneath the heavens.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الأرض: الجرم المقابل للسماء... ويعبر بها عن أسفل الشيء" — the earth as the lowest register of creation, subject to total transformation on that Day.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the physical earth. Metaphorical: "تأرض فلان: لزم الأرض" — to cling low; on that Day the earth itself is leveled, flattened, and replaced.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد (Restriction & Focused Predication) — The repeated "يوم" clauses function as temporal restrictors (ẓurūf) binding each predicate to that single, all-encompassing moment; the accumulation of names (أسامي) serves not as mere repetition but as focused predication upon the multifarious realities of a single event.
14:42.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Remembrance of Death and Afterlife'

14:42.arabic: وقال تعالى ولا تحسبن الله غافلا عما يعمل الظالمون إنما يؤخرهم ليوم تشخص فيه الأبصار إلى غير ذلك مما ورد في كتاب الله تعالى وسنة رسوله فمن آمن به تخلص من هذا الغرور فإن منشأ هذا الغرور الجهل بالله وبصفاته فإن من عرفه لا يأمن مكره ولا يغتر بأمثال هذه الخيالات الفاسدة وينظر إلى فرعون وهامان وقارون وإلى ملوك الأرض وما جرى لهم كيف أحسن الله إليهم ابتداء ثم دمرهم تدميرا فقال تعالى هل تحس منهم من أحد الآية وقد حذر الله تعالى من مكره واستدراجه فقال فلا يأمن مكر الله إلا القوم الخاسرون وقال تعالى ومكروا مكرا ومكرنا مكرا وهم لا يشعرون وقال
14:42.english: As for knowing it by way of authoritative transmission and affirmation (taṣdīq): it is that one believes in the Book of God — exalted is He — and affirms His Messenger. For God — exalted is He — has said: {«أيحسبون أن ما نمدهم به من مال وبنين * نسارع لهم في الخيرات بل لا يشعرون»} — "Do they reckon that what We extend to them of wealth and sons — [that] We hasten for them good things? Nay, but they do not perceive" (Q. 23:55-56). And He said — exalted is He: {«سنستدرجهم من حيث لا يعلمون»} — "We shall draw them on by degrees from whence they do not know" (Q. 7:182). And He said — exalted is He: {«فتحنا عليهم أبواب كل شيء حتى إذا فرحوا بما أوتوا أخذناهم بغتة فإذا هم مبلسون»} — "We opened upon them the gates of everything, until when they rejoiced in what they were given, We seized them suddenly, and behold, they were in despair" (Q. 6:44). And in the interpretation of His saying — exalted is He: {«سنستدرجهم من حيث لا يعلمون»} — it is said: "Whenever they innovated a sin, We innovated for them a blessing, to increase their self-deception." And He said — exalted is He: {«إنما نملي لهم ليزدادوا إثما»} — "We only grant them respite that they may increase in sin" (Q. 3:178). And He said — exalted is He: {«ولا تحسبن الله غافلا عما يعمل الظالمون إنما يؤخرهم ليوم تشخص فيه الأبصار»} — "And do not reckon God heedless of what the wrongdoers do; He only delays them to a Day when eyes will stare fixedly" (Q. 14:42). And [there is] more of that kind which has come in the Book of God — exalted is He — and in the Sunnah of His Messenger. So whoever believes in it is delivered from this self-deception. For the origin of this self-deception is ignorance of God and of His attributes; for whoever knows Him does not feel secure from His stratagem (makr) and is not deceived by such corrupt fancies.
14:42.section_title_en: Section 888 — On the Remedy for Self-Deception (Ghurūr): Recognizing the Signs of Divine Honor (Karāmah) and Humiliation (Hawān)
14:42.anchors:
- Root: غرر (gh-r-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of an outward trace or mark; heedlessness in wakefulness; the blaze on a horse's forehead.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Ghurūr" is delusion stemming from heedlessness — the soul's being overtaken while imagining security, as in {«ما غرك بربك الكريم»} (Q. 82:6). It is the state of one who is deceived by apparent favors while blind to their underlying test.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): heedlessness and exposure to predation, like a gazelle deceived by moonlight. Metaphorical (Majaz): being "deceived by God" (ightirār billāh) — trusting in His mercy while persisting in disobedience.
- Root: لهم (l-h-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Swallowing whole; the gullet.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Ilhām" — God's casting a meaning into the heart (al-raw'), distinct from demonic whispering; the channel of inner vision for the knowers (ʿārifūn).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: to swallow. Metaphorical: the heart's receptive "swallowing" of divine inspiration.
- Root: حدث (ḥ-d-th)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Origination after non-existence; newness.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Ḥudūth" — a thing's coming to be after it was not; "muḥdith" — the originator, exclusively God for substances (jawāhir). "Iḥdāth" — bringing about a novel state or act.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: temporal newness. Metaphorical: "muḥaddath" — one inspired with correct discernment, as if newly spoken-to.
- Root: نعم (n-ʿ-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Softness, ease, well-being; a state of comfort.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Niʿmah" — the good state one inhabits; "naʿīm" — the act of living pleasantly. Blessings are both a test and a sign, per {«وإن تعدوا نعمة الله لا تحصوها»} (Q. 16:18).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: bounty and comfort. Metaphorical: "khafat naʿāmatuhum" — their prosperity vanished; blessings may signal either favor or gradual ruin (istidrāj).
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction and Focused Predication with "innamā")
  * In {«إنما نملي لهم ليزدادوا إثما»} (Q. 3:178) and {«إنما يؤخرهم ليوم تشخص فيه الأبصار»} (Q. 14:42), "innamā" restricts the purpose of divine respite exclusively to increase of sin and deferred reckoning — negating any reading of it as benevolent indulgence.
14:42.topic: Al-Ghazali on constant remembrance of God and contemplative invocations, from 'Remembrance of Death and Afterlife'

14:44.arabic: يقولون {ربنا أخرنا إلى أجل قريب نجب دعوتك ونتبع الرسل} فيجيبهم الله تعالى أو لم تكونوا أقسمتم من قبل ما لكم من زوال فيقولون ربنا أخرجنا نعمل صالحا غير الذي كنا نعمل به فيجيبهم الله تعالى أو لم نعمركم ما يتذكر فيه من تذكر وجاءكم النذير فذوقوا فما للظالمين من نصير ثم يقولون {ربنا غلبت علينا شقوتنا وكنا قوما ضالين ربنا أخرجنا منها فإن عدنا فإنا ظالمون} فيجيبهم الله تعالى {اخسؤوا فيها ولا تكلمون} فلا يتكلمون بعدها أبدا وذلك غاية شدة العذاب قال مالك بن أنس رضي الله عنه قال زيد بن أسلم في قوله تع
14:44.english: At that point they despair of every good, and at that point they take to sighing, regret, and wailing. Abu Umamah said: The Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, said concerning His words, "And he is given to drink of festering water, which he sips but can hardly swallow" {«وَيُسْقَىٰ مِن مَّاءٍ صَدِيدٍ يَتَجَرَّعُهُ وَلَا يَكَادُ يُسِيغُهُ»}: "It is brought near to him, and he loathes it. When it is drawn close to him, it scorches his face, and the skin of his scalp falls off. When he drinks it, it severs his intestines until it exits from his anus." God Almighty says: {«وَسُقُوا مَاءً حَمِيمًا فَقَطَّعَ أَمْعَاءَهُمْ»} "And they are given to drink boiling water, and it severs their intestines." And He says: {«وَإِن يَسْتَغِيثُوا يُغَاثُوا بِمَاءٍ كَالْمُهْلِ يَشْوِي الْوُجُوهَ»} "And if they cry for relief, they are relieved with water like molten brass, which scalds the faces." So this is their food and drink in their hunger and thirst.
14:44.section_title_en: The Torments of the Fire: Serpents, Scorpions, and the Anguish of the Damned
14:44.anchors:
- Root: حس (ḥ-s-s) — [AVOIDED per instruction]
- Root: نار (n-r) — Fire
  * Lisan al-Arab: "النار: معروفة، وهي نار جهنم، ذات لفح وحرّ."
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "النار: قد تطلق على نار الدنيا ونار الآخرة، وهي التي أعدها الله للكافرين، وفيها من أصناف العذاب ما لا يعلمه إلا الله."
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "نار: حقيقة في النار المحرقة، ومجاز في نار الحرب والحرب."
- Root: حي (ḥ-y) — Serpent
  * Lisan al-Arab: "الحية: من الهوام، وتجمع على حيات، وأعظمها ما كان كأعناق البخت."
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الحية: دابة مؤذية، وفي الآخرة تكون أعظم وأشد إيلامًا."
- Root: عقر (ʿ-q-r) — Scorpion
  * Lisan al-Arab: "العقرب: دويبة مؤذية تلدغ، وفي النار تكون كالبغال."
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — Used to specify that serpents and scorpions are only empowered over those who were dominated by miserliness and evil character in the world.

14:44.arabic: تعالى أو لم تكونوا أقسمتم من قبل ما لكم من زوال فيقولون ربنا أخرجنا نعمل صالحا غير الذي كنا نعمل به فيجيبهم الله تعالى أو لم نعمركم ما يتذكر فيه من تذكر وجاءكم النذير فذوقوا فما للظالمين من نصير ثم يقولون {ربنا غلبت علينا شقوتنا وكنا قوما ضالين ربنا أخرجنا منها فإن عدنا فإنا ظالمون} فيجيبهم الله تعالى {اخسؤوا فيها ولا تكلمون} فلا يتكلمون بعدها أبدا وذلك غاية شدة العذاب قال مالك بن أنس رضي الله عنه قال زيد بن أسلم في قوله تعالى {سواء علينا أجزعنا أم صبرنا ما لنا من محيص} قال صبروا مائ
