14:48.arabic: وما هم بسكارى ولكن عذاب الله شديد يوم تبدل الأرض غير الأرض والسموات وبرزوا لله الواحد القهار يوم تنسف فيه الجبال نسفا فتترك قاعا صفصفا لا ترى فيها عوجا ولا أمتا يوم ترى الجبال تحسبها جامدة وهي تمر مر السحاب يوم تنشق فيه السماء فتكون وردة كالدهان فيومئذ لا يسئل عن ذنبه إنس ولا جان يوم يمنع فيه العاصى من الكلام ولا يسئل فيه عن الأجرام بل يؤخذ بالنواصى والأقدام يوم تجد كل نفس ما عملت من خير محضرا وما عملت من سوء تود لو أن بينها وبينه أمدا بعيدا يوم تعلم فيه كل نفس ما أحضرت وتشهد ما قدمت وأخرت يوم تخرس فيه الألسن وتنطق الجوارح يوم شيب ذكره س
14:48.english: So prepare yourself, O wretched one, for this Day of immense magnitude, of prolonged duration, of overwhelming dominion, whose appointed time is near — a Day when you shall see the heaven split asunder, and the stars scattered in its terror, and the shining planets extinguished, and the sun folded up, and the mountains set in motion, and the pregnant camels neglected, and the wild beasts gathered together, and the seas set ablaze, and the souls paired with their bodies, and the Hellfire ignited, and Paradise brought near, and the mountains pulverized, and the earth stretched out — a Day when you shall see the earth shaken with its quaking, and the earth casts forth its burdens. On that Day shall people issue forth in scattered groups to be shown their deeds — a Day when the earth and the mountains are lifted and crushed with a single crushing. Then on that Day the Imminent Event shall come to pass, and the heaven shall split open, for on that Day it shall be frail, and the angels shall be at its edges, and eight shall bear the Throne of your Lord above them on that Day. On that Day you shall be presented — no secret of yours shall remain hidden. A Day when the mountains shall move and you shall see the earth laid bare — a Day when the earth shall be shaken with a violent shaking, and the mountains crumbled to dust, becoming scattered particles — a Day when people shall be like scattered moths, and the mountains like carded wool — a Day when every nursing mother shall forget what she nursed, and every pregnant female shall cast down her burden, and you shall see people drunk, yet they are not drunk, but the chastisement of God is severe — a Day when the earth shall be changed to other than this earth, and the heavens, and they shall appear before God, the One, the All-Compelling — a Day when the mountains shall be blown away as dust, leaving a level, bare plain, wherein you see no crookedness nor curve — a Day when you see the mountains and suppose them solid, yet they pass by like the passing of clouds — a Day when the heaven shall split open and become rosy like molten oil. Then on that Day no human nor jinn shall be asked about his sin. A Day when the disobedient shall be prevented from speech, and shall not be asked about their crimes, but shall be seized by their forelocks and their feet — a Day when every soul shall find what it did of good brought forth present, and what it did of evil, wishing that between it and that evil there were a far distance — a Day when every soul shall know what it has sent ahead, and shall witness what it has forwarded and what it has left behind — a Day when tongues shall be struck mute and the bodily members shall speak — a Day whose mention turned the hair of the Master of the Messengers white, when al-Ṣiddīq (may God be pleased with him) said to him: "I see that you have turned white-haired, O Messenger of God." He said: "Sūrat Hūd and its sisters have made me white-haired" — namely, al-Wāqiʿah, al-Mursalāt, ʿAmma Yatasāʾalūn, and Idhā al-Shamsu Kuwwirat.
14:48.section_title_en: The Names and Attributes of the Day of Resurrection — An Exhortation to the Negligent
14:48.anchors:
- Root: يوم (yawm)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "اليوم: وقت طلوع الشمس إلى غروبها، وقد يعبر به عن مدة من الزمان أي مدة كانت" — the day as a temporal span, extended metaphorically to any epoch or era.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "اليوم يعبر به عن وقت طلوع الشمس إلى غروبها. وقد يعبر به عن مدة من الزمان أي مدة كانت" — theological usage denotes the appointed time of reckoning, magnified by divine attribution (أيام الله).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): a measured solar period. Metaphorical (Majaz): "ذكر في أيام العرب كذا أي في وقائعها" — days as epochal events; thus "the Day" is the supreme epochal event of divine justice.
- Root: نفس (nafs)
  * Lisan / Ayn: النفس: الروح والذات — the self, soul, or very essence.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "النفس: الروح... وقوله: ويحذركم الله نفسه فنفسه: ذاته" — nafs as the innermost reality of a being; in the eschatological context, souls are "paired" (زوجت) with bodies for judgment.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the soul as life-principle. Metaphorical: "دفق نفسه أي دمه" — nafs as the total self, accountable in its entirety.
- Root: ارض (arḍ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: الأرض: الجرم المقابل للسماء — the earth as the corporeal substratum beneath the heavens.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الأرض: الجرم المقابل للسماء... ويعبر بها عن أسفل الشيء" — the earth as the lowest register of creation, subject to total transformation on that Day.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the physical earth. Metaphorical: "تأرض فلان: لزم الأرض" — to cling low; on that Day the earth itself is leveled, flattened, and replaced.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد (Restriction & Focused Predication) — The repeated "يوم" clauses function as temporal restrictors (ẓurūf) binding each predicate to that single, all-encompassing moment; the accumulation of names (أسامي) serves not as mere repetition but as focused predication upon the multifarious realities of a single event.
14:48.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Remembrance of Death and Afterlife'

14:48.arabic: ولا تظنن أن تلك الأرض مثل أرض الدنيا بل لا تساويها إلا فى الاسم قال تعالى يوم تبدل الأرض غير الأرض والسموات قال ابن عباس يزداد فيها وينقص وتذهب أشجارها وجبالها وأوديتها وما فيها وتمد مد الأديم العكاظى أرض بيضاء مثل الفضة لم يسفك عليها دم ولم يعمل عليها خطيئة والسموات تذهب شمسها وقمرها ونجومها فانظر يا مسكين في هول ذلك اليوم وشدته فإنه إذا اجتمع الخلائق على هذا الصعيد تناثرت من فوقهم نجوم السماء وطمس الشمس والقمر وأظلمت الأرض لخمود سراجها فبينا هم كذلك إذ دارت السماء من فوق رءوسهم وانشقت مع غلظها وشدتها خمسمائة عام والملائكة قيام على حافات
14:48.english: Know, O seeker, that after the resurrection and the arising from the graves, consider how they are driven — barefoot, naked, uncircumcised — to the land of the Gathering. It is a white land, a level plain, smooth and even, wherein you see no crookedness nor any curve, and upon which you see no hillock behind which a person might hide, nor any hollow that would sink him from view. Rather, it is one single, simple expanse with no variation whatsoever, and to it they are driven in troops. Glory be to Him who gathered all creatures, despite their differing kinds, from the far quarters of the earth, when He drove them by the Rajīfah (the Trembling Blast) followed by the Rādifah (the Second Blast). The Rajīfah is the first trumpet-blast, and the Rādifah is the second. Rightly are those hearts on that day agitated, and rightly are those eyes humbled. The Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, said: «The people will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection upon a white, ʿafrāʾ earth, like a pure loaf of bread, upon which there is no marker for anyone.» The narrator said: "ʿAfrah is a whiteness that is not brilliant, and al-naqī is the bread purified of its bran and husk. 'No marker' means no building that conceals, and no unevenness that repels the eye."
14:48.section_title_en: The Description of the Trumpet-Blast and the Land of the Gathering
14:48.anchors:
- Root: صور (ṣ-w-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root denotes form/shape; the "trumpet" (ṣūr) is that which shapes and transforms states through its blast.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance — the ṣūr is the instrument of cosmic transformation, linking the two blasts (rajīfah and rādifah) to the divine command of resurrection.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — a horn/trumpet; metaphorical — the blast as the signal of universal upheaval, not a mere physical sound.
- Root: حشر (ḥ-sh-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to gather, drive, or assemble a multitude forcibly.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theologically, ḥashr is the divine gathering of all creatures to the plain of reckoning, distinct from ordinary aggregation by its comprehensiveness and compulsion.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — herding animals; metaphorical — the compelled assembly of humanity before God, stripped of all worldly coverings.
- Root: عفر (ʿ-f-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: ʿafrāʾ denotes a whitish hue tinged with redness or dust-color; the "white" earth of the gathering is not pure white but a dusty, pale expanse.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The earth's transformation (tabdīl al-arḍ) signifies a new creation, not mere alteration of accidents.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — color description; metaphorical — the earth's purity from sin and bloodshed, as the narrator glosses ʿafrāʾ as "whiteness not brilliant."
- Sibawayh Rule: Interposition of descriptive clauses (ṣifah) between subject and predicate — the extended adjectival chains (e.g., "arḍ bayḍāʾ qāʿ ṣafṣaf...") delay the main verb to build cumulative, awe-inducing imagery, permissible due to the semantic completeness of each descriptive unit.
14:48.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Remembrance of Death and Afterlife'

15:2.arabic: الله عليه وسلم {ربما يود الذين كفروا لو كانوا مسلمين} (2) وقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لله أرحم بعبده المؤمن من الوالدة الشفيقة بولدها (3) وقال جابر بن عبد الله من زادت حسناته على سيآته يوم القيامة فذلك الذي يدخل الجنة بغير حساب ومن استوت حسناته وسيآته فذلك الذي يحاسب حسابا يسيرا ثم يدخل الجنة وإنما شفاعة رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لمن أوبق نفسه وأثقل ظهره ويروى إن الله عز وجل قال لموسى عليه السلام يا موسى استغاث بك قارون فلم تغثه وعزتي وجلالي لو استغاث بي لأغثته وعفوت عنه وقال سعد ب
15:2.english: He mentioned me one day, or feared me in a station (1). And the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: "When the people of the Fire are gathered in the Fire — and with them, whomsoever God wills of the people of the Qiblah — the disbelievers will say to the Muslims: 'Were you not Muslims?' They will reply: 'Yes.' Then they will say: 'What did your Islam avail you, seeing that you are with us in the Fire?' They will answer: 'We had sins, and we were seized for them.' Then God, Mighty and Glorious, will hear what they have said, and He will command that whoever was in the Fire of the people of the Qiblah be brought out, and they will be brought out. When the disbelievers see that, they will say: 'Would that we had been Muslims, so that we might be brought out as they were brought out.' Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited: {ربما يود الذين كفروا لو كانوا مسلمين} — "Perhaps those who disbelieve will wish that they had been Muslims" (Q. 15:2). (2)
15:2.section_title_en: On the Vastness of Divine Mercy and the Intercession for the Sinful — Section 1360
15:2.anchors:
- Root: ذكر (dhakara)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Remembrance, recollection; also mention, invocation.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-dhikr is the opposite of forgetfulness (nisyān); it denotes the heart's presence with what is recalled, and the tongue's utterance thereof.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): to recall in the heart or utter on the tongue. Metaphorical (majāz): "dhakartuhu bi-khayr" — to speak well of someone, i.e., to raise their mention in honor.
- Root: خرج (kharaja)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To exit, depart, emerge from an interior to an exterior.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-khurūj is the departure of a thing from its place or state; used of the soul leaving the body, and of the damned leaving the Fire.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: spatial egress. Metaphorical: "kharaja min al-amr" — to emerge from an affair, i.e., to be free of its obligation; and "akhrajahu Allāh min al-nār" — divine extraction by mercy, not by merit.
- Root: شفع (shafa'a)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To make even, pair; intercession is making one's supplication a pair with another's need.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-shafā'ah is the joining of one's intercession to another's request for aid; its reality is the elevation of the intercessor's rank and the remission of the offender's burden.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: pairing. Metaphorical: intercession before a king — the intercessor "pairs" his own honor with the petitioner's deficiency.
- Root: رحم (raḥima)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Tenderness of heart, compassion; al-Raḥmān is intensive — mercy as an essential attribute.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-raḥmah is tenderness that necessitates beneficence; when attributed to God, it is pure beneficence (tafaddul) without emotional change.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the mother's womb (raḥim) as the seat of compassion. Metaphorical: "arḥam al-rāḥimīn" — God's mercy as sheer gratuitous giving, exceeding any creaturely pity.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Restriction and Focused Predication (al-ḥaṣr wa al-taqyīd bi-innamā) — "Innamā shafā'atu Rasūlillāh…" restricts intercession to a specific class, namely those who have burdened themselves with sins, not the innocent.
15:2.topic: Al-Ghazali on the journey of the soul, death, and the Hereafter, from 'Remembrance of Death and Afterlife'

15:92.arabic: المرسلين فلنقصن عليهم بعلم وما كنا غائبين} وقوله {فوربك لنسألنهم أجمعين عما كانوا يعملون} فيبدأ سبحانه بالأنبياء {يوم يجمع الله الرسل فيقول}
15:92.english: Then reflect, O wretched one, after these states upon what is directed against you of the questioning — face to face, without any interpreter — and you shall be asked concerning the little and the much, the speck on a date-stone (al-naqīr) and the husk (al-qitmīr). For while you are amidst the distress of the Resurrection, its sweat, and the severity of its terrors, lo! the angels descend from the horizons of the heaven with immense bodies and gigantic forms — harsh, severe — commanded to seize the forelocks of the criminals and drag them to the standing-place of presentation (mawqif al-ʿarḍ) before the Omnipotent (al-Jabbār). The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: "Verily, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has an angel between whose two eyelids is a distance of a hundred years' journey." So what is your assumption concerning yourself when you behold the likes of these angels — dispatched unto you to seize you and bring you to the station of presentation — and you see them, despite the enormity of their forms, broken in humility before the severity of that Day, filled with dread at what has become manifest of the Omnipotent's wrath upon His servants? And at their descent, there remains no prophet, no veracious one (ṣiddīq), no righteous soul, save that they fall upon their chins in fear, lest they themselves be the seized ones. Such is the state of those brought near (al-muqarrabūn) — so what is your assumption concerning the disobedient criminals?
15:92.section_title_en: The Description of the Day of Resurrection, Its Calamities, and Its Names — The Description of the Questioning
15:92.anchors:
- Root: س-أ-ل (sa-ʾa-la)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root denotes seeking, demanding, or interrogating; al-suʾāl is the act of asking, and musāʾalah implies reciprocal or formal interrogation.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In theological context, al-suʾāl on the Day of Resurrection is a divine inquest (musāʾalah) demanding account of deeds, not for God's knowledge (as He is 'alīm) but for establishing proof (ḥujjah) against the creature.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) usage is verbal inquiry; metaphorical (majāz) extends to the juridical reckoning (muḥāsabah) where the tongue is made to testify without intermediary.
- Root: ن-ز-ل (na-za-la)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root signifies descent from a height; nuzūl is the act of alighting.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): When predicated of angels, it denotes their dispatch from the celestial realm to execute divine command — a descent of authority, not spatial movement in the divine essence.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical descent; metaphorical: the advent of divine decree or angelic execution of wrath.
- Root: ع-ر-ض (ʿa-ra-ḍa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root means to present, expose, or show; al-ʿarḍ is the exhibition of something before a viewer.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In eschatological usage, mawqif al-ʿarḍ is the standing-place of presentation before God for judgment — a public display of deeds.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: to show; metaphorical: the juridical tribunal of the Hereafter where all acts are exhibited.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Interrogative Scope (Bāb al-istifhām) — The rhetorical question "فما ظنك" (so what is your assumption?) functions as a periodic pause, redirecting the addressee's cognition from narrated events to self-projection, governed by the conditional-temporal particle "إذ" (when) that binds the apodosis to the protasis.
15:92.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'Remembrance of Death and Afterlife'

16:107.arabic: وفضلا عما أعده الله تعالى للذين استحبوا الحياة الدنيا على الآخرة ورضوا بها واطمأنوا إليها من
16:107.english: The hadith was transmitted by Muslim, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah: "Verily, a man may work for a long stretch of time with the deeds of the people of Paradise, then his final deed is sealed with a deed of the people of the Fire." Al-Bazzar and al-Tabarani in al-Awsat [added]: "for seventy years," and its chain is sound. And from the Two Shaykhs [al-Bukhari and Muslim], within a hadith of Ibn Mas'ud: "Verily, one of you may work with the deeds of the people of Paradise until there remains between him and it [Paradise] only a cubit..." — this hadith contains no specification of a time period for the work of fifty years, nor any mention of a span [shibr], nor {nor} the interval of a she-camel's milking [fawaq nāqah]. And in another narration: "except the measure of the milking-interval of a she-camel," then the decree overtakes him, and he is sealed with a deed of the people of the Fire. Now, the measure of a she-camel's milking-interval cannot accommodate any deed performed by the bodily limbs; rather, it is [sufficient] only for the measure of a passing thought [khāṭir] that surges within the heart at the moment of death, thereby necessitating an evil final outcome. So how can one feel secure from that? Therefore, the utmost limit of the believer's aspiration is that his fear and his hope be balanced. Yet the predominance of hope in most people is grounded in self-delusion and deficiency of knowledge. For this reason, God Most High conjoined both [fear and hope] in describing those whom He praised, saying: {«يدعون ربهم خوفا وطمعا»} — "They call upon their Lord in fear and in hope" — and He, Mighty and Majestic, said: {«ويدعوننا رغبا ورهبا»} — "And they call upon Us in desire and in awe." And where is the like of Umar, may God be pleased with him? So the creatures existing in this age — all of them — the most salutary for them is the predominance of fear, on the condition that it does not cast them into despair, nor abandon them from work, nor cut off hope of forgiveness; for that would become a cause of indolence in action and a summons to plunging into disobedience. For that is despondency [qunūṭ], not fear. Rather, fear is that which spurs one to action, which clouds all appetites, which agitates the heart away from repose in this world, and which calls it to hold aloof from the Abode of Delusion. That is the praiseworthy fear — not the whisperings of the self that produce no effect in restraint or incitement, and not the despair that necessitates despondency.
16:107.section_title_en: The Balance of Fear and Hope at Death — Section 1046
16:107.anchors:
- Root: خوف (khawf)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core sense of dread and apprehension; the heart's agitation before an anticipated harm.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الخوف: توقع مكروه عن أمارة مظنونة، أو معلومة" — expectation of evil from a conjectured or known sign; antithesis of amn (security); applies to both worldly and otherworldly matters.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Haqiqah: "خفته على مالي خوفا وخيفة" — literal fear for what one possesses. Majaz: "تخوفه: تنقصه" — metaphorical sense of gradual diminution, as in Zuhayr's verse, implying fear that erodes resolve.
- Root: موت (mawt)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Death as the cessation of vital power; "مات ميتة سوء" — dying an evil death.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Death contrasted with life (ḥayāh); in Quranic usage, linked to the finality of deeds and the sealing of one's fate.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Haqiqah: "مات موتة لم يمتها أحد" — literal death. Majaz: "أحيا الله البلد الميت" — metaphorical revival of barren land, paralleling spiritual death and life.
- Root: قلب (qalb)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The heart as the seat of fluctuating states; "قلب الشيء: تصريفه وصرفه عن وجه إلى وجه" — turning and overturning.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "قلب الشيء: تصريفه وصرفه عن وجه إلى وجه، كقلب الثوب، وقلب الإنسان" — the heart's constant oscillation between states, here between fear and hope.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Haqiqah: "قلب الشيء قلبا: حوله عن وجهه" — literal overturning. Majaz: "رجل قلب حول: يقلب الأمور ويحتال" — metaphorical agility in discerning and managing affairs.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — Used to delimit the true nature of khawf (fear) as that which impels action, excluding mere whisperings of the self and despair.
16:107.topic: Al-Ghazali on the journey of the soul, death, and the Hereafter, from 'Remembrance of Death and Afterlife'

17:14.arabic: وعذاب القبر والصراط والميزان والحساب ومعنى قوله تعالى {اقرأ كتابك كفى بنفسك اليوم عليك حسيبا} ومعنى قوله تعالى {وإن الدار الآخرة لهي الحيوان لو كانوا يعلمون} ومعنى لقاء الله عز وجل والنظر إلى وجهه الكريم ومعنى القرب منه والنزول في جواره ومعنى حصول السعادة بمرافقة الملأ الأعلى ومقارنة الملائكة والنبيين ومعنى تفاوت درجات أهل الجنان حتى يرى بعضهم البعض كما يرى الكوكب الدري في جوف السماء إلى غير ذلك مما يطول تفصيله إذ للناس في معاني هذه الأمور بعد التصديق بأصولها مقامات شتى فبعضهم يرى أن جميع ذلك أمثلة وأن الذي أعده الله لعباده الصالحين ما ل
17:14.english: He, exalted, said: {«لهم قلوب لا يفقهون بها»} [They have hearts with which they do not understand] (Q 7:179), meaning thereby the realities of faith, not legal fatwas. By my life, jurisprudence and understanding (fahm) are in language two names with one meaning; the discussion concerns customary usage, both ancient and modern.
17:14.section_title_en: The Revival of the Religious Sciences — Section 16: The Science of Unveiling (ʿIlm al-Mukāshafah) and the Science of Practical Conduct (ʿIlm al-Muʿāmalah)
17:14.anchors:
- Root: كشف (kashafa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Removal of a covering; unveiling, disclosure.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The lifting of a veil (ghishāwah) from the heart such that the realities of things become manifest as if witnessed directly (muʿāyanah).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): removal of a physical covering. Metaphorical (majāz): the illumination of the heart with the light of certainty, dispelling the darkness of doubt and heedlessness.
- Root: عرف (ʿarafa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To know by reflection and trace; to recognize.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Maʿrifah" is the perception of a thing through reflection upon its effects; it is more specific than ʿilm and is the knowledge of God attained by the servants through His signs, not by grasping His essence.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: to recognize a person or thing. Metaphorical: the knowledge of God that necessitates reverential fear and love, as opposed to mere information.
- Root: عمل (ʿamila)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To do, to act, to perform.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The act (ʿamal) is the movement of the servant toward a goal; in religious usage, it is the movement of the heart and limbs in obedience or disobedience.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical action. Metaphorical: the actions of the heart (aʿmāl al-qulūb), which are the inward realities of faith.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد (Restriction & Specification) — The distinction between the two sciences is a restriction of the term "science" (ʿilm) to its two true referents: the science of unveiling (mukāshafah) and the science of practical conduct (muʿāmalah), excluding all else that is falsely named science.
17:14.topic: Al-Ghazali on the journey of the soul, death, and the Hereafter, from 'Remembrance of Death and Afterlife'

17:100.arabic: له ما فعل الله بك قال غفر لي وقال قل لأيوب قل لو أنتم تملكون خزائن رحمة ربي إذا لأمسكتم خشية الإنفاق وقال بعضهم رأيت في الليلة التي مات فيها
17:100.english: ...you would dwell. She said: "Every joyful, merry heart." He said: "Then I awoke and pledged myself that I would not laugh except when overcome [by it]."
17:100.section_title_en: The Visions of the Righteous After Death — Dreams of the Prophet's Companions, the Pious, and Iblis (Section 1332)
17:100.anchors:
- Root: نوم (n-w-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Sleep and dreaming; the state wherein the soul perceives unseen realities.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "النوم: فسر على أوجه كلها صحيح بنظرات مختلفة... وقيل: النوم موت خفيف، والموت نوم ثقيل" — Sleep is a light death; visions in sleep (ru'ya) are a channel for divine communication and post-mortem disclosures.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "رأى في المنام كذا" (he saw such-and-such in a dream). Metaphorical: "نامت السوق: كسدت" (the market slept = stagnated) — here, dreams are literal vehicles for veridical spiritual encounters.
- Root: غفر (gh-f-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Covering, shielding from defilement; forgiveness.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الغفران والمغفرة من الله هو أن يصون العبد من أن يمسه العذاب" — Divine forgiveness is God's shielding of the servant from touching chastisement.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "اللهم غفرا" (O God, forgiveness). Metaphorical: beasts "not forgiving" a lapse = devouring the young — here, God's forgiveness is literal, absolute, and gracious.
- Root: سعد (s-'-d)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Felicity, divine aid toward good.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "السعادة: معاونة الأمور الإلهية للإنسان على نيل الخير" — Happiness is the cooperation of divine matters with man to attain the good.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "أسعده الله" (God made him fortunate). Metaphorical: "ساعد الدهر" (time aided) — here, the blessed state of the deceased is literal divine favor.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — In the phrase "وإنما يخاف من نور يكون في القلب" ("but rather he fears only a light that resides in the heart"), إنما restricts fear exclusively to the spiritual light, negating all corporeal means.
17:100.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Remembrance of Death and Afterlife'

18:24.arabic: ولا تقولن لشيء إني فاعل ذلك غدا إلا أن يشاء الله ثم لم يقتصر على ذلك فيما لا يشك فيه بل قال تعالى لتدخلن المسجد الحرام إن شاء الله آمنين محلقين رءؤسكم ومقصرين وكان الله سبحانه عالما بأنهم يدخلون لا محالة وأنه شاءه ولكن المقصود تعليمه ذلك فتأدب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في ما كان يخبر عنه معلوما كان أو مشكوكا حتى قال صلى الله عليه وسلم لما دخل المقابر السلام عليكم دار قوم مؤمنين وإنا إن شاء الله بكم لاحقون (1) واللحوق بهم غير مشكوك فيه ولكن مقتضى الأدب ذكر الله تعالى وربط الأمور به وهذه الصيغ
18:24.english: If you say: "What is the meaning of the Salaf's statement, 'I am a believer, if God wills' — given that the exception (istithnā') implies doubt, and doubt in faith is unbelief? Yet they all refrained from giving an unqualified answer affirming faith and were cautious about it."
18:24.section_title_en: On the Meaning of the Salaf's Statement "I am a Believer, If God Wills" — Section 102
18:24.anchors:
- Root: نفس (n-f-s)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The self, the soul; that which is breathed; the innermost reality of a person.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): النفس is used for the rūḥ (spirit), for the dhāt (essence/self), and for the seat of intention and knowledge. When one says "he knows in himself (nafsihi) that he is a believer," it denotes certitude residing in the very core of one's being, not a corporeal faculty.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) usage refers to the soul's reflexive self-awareness; metaphorical (majāz) usage extends to "blood" (dam) or "the eye" (ʿayn) of envy. Here, "in himself" (fī nafsihi) is literal self-knowledge, not mere outward profession.
- Root: وجه (w-j-h)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Face, countenance; the foremost part; a mode, aspect, or direction.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The face is the most noble apparent part of a thing; hence it is used for the "aspect" or "manner" (wajh) of an affair. "Four aspects" (wujūh) means four distinct modes of interpretation or rational grounds.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the face of a person or object. Metaphorical: "the face of the matter" (wajh al-amr) — its most salient and honorable dimension. Here, the "aspects" are hermeneutical angles, not physical parts.
- Root: ايم (a-y-m)
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The unmarried state (aym); one who has no spouse. Not applicable here directly, but the root's semantic field of "being alone/without attachment" contrasts with īmān's root (a-m-n) — security and trust — which is the operative term in this text.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Not directly relevant; the operative root is أمن (a-m-n), meaning security from fear, and by extension, faith (īmān) as the state of being secure in God's truth.
- Root: كان (k-w-n)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To be, to exist; the copula of predication.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Kāna denotes existence and becoming; in theological usage, it grounds the distinction between what is (mawjūd) and what is merely asserted. The question "Are you a believer?" (a-mu'min anta?) uses kāna implicitly to ask about actual, present state — not future contingency.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: existence. Metaphorical: the "being-so" of a predicate. The istithnā' (exception) with "in shā' Allāh" suspends the copula's certainty, shifting from assertive existence to contingent hope.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الاستثناء والتعليق بالمشيئة (The Chapter of Exception and Suspension by the Divine Will) — When an exception clause (istithnā') follows a positive assertion, it grammatically suspends the universality or certainty of the predication. In theological discourse, this suspension may be semantic (doubt) or pragmatic (deference, etiquette, or self-deprecation), and Sibawayh's parsing of conditional suspension (taʿlīq) shows that the apodosis need not be negated — only its absolute, unqualified force is tempered.
18:24.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Remembrance of Death and Afterlife'

18:31.arabic: قال الله يحلون فيها من أساور من ذهب ولؤلؤا ولباسهم فيها حرير والآيات في ذلك كثيرة وإنما تفصيله في الأخبار فقد روى أبو هريرة أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال من يدخل الجنة ينعم لا يبأس لا تبلى ثيابه ولا يفنى شبابه في الجنة ما لا عين رأت ولا أذن سمعت ولا خطر عن قلب بشر (1) وقال رجل يا رسول الله أخبرنا عن ثياب أهل الجنة أخلق تخلق أم نسج تنسج فسكت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وضحك بعض القوم فقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم مم تضحكون من جاهل سأل عالما ثم قال رسول ا
18:31.english: Ponder the form of Paradise, and reflect upon the bliss of its inhabitants, and upon the remorse of him who is deprived of it for his contentment with this world as a substitute for it. For Abu Hurayrah said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: "Verily, the wall of Paradise is a brick of silver and a brick of gold; its soil is saffron, and its clay is musk." (1) And he was asked, may God bless him and grant him peace, about the earth of Paradise, and he said: "A white flour-like pure musk." (2) And Abu Hurayrah said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: "Whosoever would delight that God, Mighty and Majestic, should give him wine to drink in the Hereafter, let him abandon it in this world; and whosoever would delight that God should clothe him in silk in the Hereafter, let him abandon it in this world." (3) And he said: "The rivers of Paradise gush forth from beneath hills, or beneath mountains, of musk." (4) And were the least of the people of Paradise in adornment to be weighed against the adornment of all the people of this world together, that with which God, Mighty and Majestic, adorns him in the Hereafter would still be better than all the adornment of this world. (5) And Abu Hurayrah said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: "Verily, in Paradise there is a tree beneath whose shade a rider travels for a hundred years without crossing it. Recite, if you wish: {And a shade extended} (6) {«وَظِلٍّ مَمْدُودٍ»}." And Abu Umāmah said: The companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to say: "God, Mighty and Majestic, benefits us through the Bedouins and their questions." A Bedouin came forward and said: "O Messenger of God, God has mentioned in the Qur'an a harmful tree, and I did not know that in Paradise there is a tree that harms its companion." The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: "{What is it?} {«مَا هِيَ»}" He said: "The lote-tree (al-sidr), for it has thorns." He said: "God, Exalted is He, has said: {In a lote-tree that is thornless} {«فِي سِدْرٍ مَخْضُودٍ»} — God clips its thorns and places in the stead of every thorn a fruit; then the fruit splits open from it into seventy-two colors of food, no one color of which resembles another." (7) And Jarīr ibn ʿAbd Allāh said: We alighted at al-Ṣifāḥ, and there was a man sleeping beneath a tree, the sun having nearly reached him. I said to the youth: "Go with this leather sheet and shade him." So he went and shaded him. When he awoke, behold, it was Salmān. I came to him and greeted him, and he said: "O Jarīr, humble yourself before God, for whosoever humbles himself before God in this world, God raises him on the Day of Resurrection. Do you know what the darknesses are on the Day of Resurrection?" I said: "I do not know." He said: "The wronging of people, one another." Then he took a small twig that I could scarcely see due to its smallness, and said: "O Jarīr, were you to seek the like of this in Paradise, you would not find it." I said: "O Abu ʿAbd Allāh, where then are the date-palms and the trees?" He said: "Their roots are of pearl and gold, and their tops are the fruit."
18:31.section_title_en: The Description of the Wall of Paradise, Its Lands, Trees, and Rivers; and the Description of the Garments, Furnishings, Couches, Canopies, and Tents of Its Inhabitants
18:31.anchors:
- Root: حوط (ḥ-w-ṭ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The enclosing wall or boundary that surrounds and protects a garden; its core sense is preservation and encompassment.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In the eschatological context, the wall (ḥā'iṭ) is a corporeal boundary delineating the Garden, yet its materials (silver and gold bricks) signify a reality transcending earthly substance (jawhar), pointing to the immaterial bounty (faḍl) of the divine grant.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) for the physical wall; metaphorical (majāz) extension when the "wall" denotes the barrier of honor separating the blessed from deprivation.
- Root: خلد (kh-l-d)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Perpetuity and endless duration; the state of abiding without termination.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Eternal subsistence (khulūd) is an attribute of the abode of recompense, contrasting with the temporal accidents (aʿrāḍ) of worldly existence; it is a fixed, necessary concomitant of the divine promise.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal for unceasing time; metaphorical for the soul's permanent state of felicity, free from the vicissitudes of generation and corruption.
- Root: ثمر (th-m-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The fruit borne by trees; the yield of a plant at its culmination.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In the Garden, fruit (thamarah) is a designated reality (musammā) whose essence is transformed by divine power—each thorn replaced by fruit—demonstrating the absolute capacity of the Creator over nature.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal for edible produce; metaphorical for the "fruit" of deeds, whether reward or punishment, as an accrued outcome.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Restriction and Specification (al-ḥaṣr wa al-taqyīd) — Governing how predicates like "its soil is saffron" and "its clay is musk" are syntactically focused to affirm the exclusive, unprecedented nature of Paradise's attributes, distinguishing them from earthly analogues.
18:31.topic: Al-Ghazali on the journey of the soul, death, and the Hereafter, from 'Remembrance of Death and Afterlife'

18:47.arabic: ويحمل عرش ربك فوقهم يومئذ ثمانية يومئذ تعرضون لا تخفى منكم خافية يوم تسير الجبال وترى الأرض بارزة يوم ترج الأرض فيه رجا وتبس الجبال بسا فكانت هباء منبثا يوم يكون الناس كالفراش المبثوث وتكون الجبال كالعهن المنفوش يوم تذهل فيه كل مرضعة عما أرضعت وتضع كل ذات حمل حملها وترى الناس سكارى وما هم بسكارى ولكن عذاب الله شديد يوم تبدل الأرض غير الأرض والسموات وبرزوا لله الواحد القهار يوم تنسف فيه الجبال نسفا فتترك قاعا صفصفا لا ترى فيها عوجا ولا أمتا يوم ترى الجبال تحسبها جامدة وهي تمر مر السحاب يوم تنشق فيه السماء فتكون وردة كالدهان فيومئذ لا يسئل عن ذنبه
18:47.english: So prepare yourself, O wretched one, for this Day of immense magnitude, of prolonged duration, of overwhelming dominion, whose appointed time is near — a Day when you shall see the heaven split asunder, and the stars scattered in its terror, and the shining planets extinguished, and the sun folded up, and the mountains set in motion, and the pregnant camels neglected, and the wild beasts gathered together, and the seas set ablaze, and the souls paired with their bodies, and the Hellfire ignited, and Paradise brought near, and the mountains pulverized, and the earth stretched out — a Day when you shall see the earth shaken with its quaking, and the earth casts forth its burdens. On that Day shall people issue forth in scattered groups to be shown their deeds — a Day when the earth and the mountains are lifted and crushed with a single crushing. Then on that Day the Imminent Event shall come to pass, and the heaven shall split open, for on that Day it shall be frail, and the angels shall be at its edges, and eight shall bear the Throne of your Lord above them on that Day. On that Day you shall be presented — no secret of yours shall remain hidden. A Day when the mountains shall move and you shall see the earth laid bare — a Day when the earth shall be shaken with a violent shaking, and the mountains crumbled to dust, becoming scattered particles — a Day when people shall be like scattered moths, and the mountains like carded wool — a Day when every nursing mother shall forget what she nursed, and every pregnant female shall cast down her burden, and you shall see people drunk, yet they are not drunk, but the chastisement of God is severe — a Day when the earth shall be changed to other than this earth, and the heavens, and they shall appear before God, the One, the All-Compelling — a Day when the mountains shall be blown away as dust, leaving a level, bare plain, wherein you see no crookedness nor curve — a Day when you see the mountains and suppose them solid, yet they pass by like the passing of clouds — a Day when the heaven shall split open and become rosy like molten oil. Then on that Day no human nor jinn shall be asked about his sin. A Day when the disobedient shall be prevented from speech, and shall not be asked about their crimes, but shall be seized by their forelocks and their feet — a Day when every soul shall find what it did of good brought forth present, and what it did of evil, wishing that between it and that evil there were a far distance — a Day when every soul shall know what it has sent ahead, and shall witness what it has forwarded and what it has left behind — a Day when tongues shall be struck mute and the bodily members shall speak — a Day whose mention turned the hair of the Master of the Messengers white, when al-Ṣiddīq (may God be pleased with him) said to him: "I see that you have turned white-haired, O Messenger of God." He said: "Sūrat Hūd and its sisters have made me white-haired" — namely, al-Wāqiʿah, al-Mursalāt, ʿAmma Yatasāʾalūn, and Idhā al-Shamsu Kuwwirat.
18:47.section_title_en: The Names and Attributes of the Day of Resurrection — An Exhortation to the Negligent
18:47.anchors:
- Root: يوم (yawm)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "اليوم: وقت طلوع الشمس إلى غروبها، وقد يعبر به عن مدة من الزمان أي مدة كانت" — the day as a temporal span, extended metaphorically to any epoch or era.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "اليوم يعبر به عن وقت طلوع الشمس إلى غروبها. وقد يعبر به عن مدة من الزمان أي مدة كانت" — theological usage denotes the appointed time of reckoning, magnified by divine attribution (أيام الله).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): a measured solar period. Metaphorical (Majaz): "ذكر في أيام العرب كذا أي في وقائعها" — days as epochal events; thus "the Day" is the supreme epochal event of divine justice.
- Root: نفس (nafs)
  * Lisan / Ayn: النفس: الروح والذات — the self, soul, or very essence.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "النفس: الروح... وقوله: ويحذركم الله نفسه فنفسه: ذاته" — nafs as the innermost reality of a being; in the eschatological context, souls are "paired" (زوجت) with bodies for judgment.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the soul as life-principle. Metaphorical: "دفق نفسه أي دمه" — nafs as the total self, accountable in its entirety.
- Root: ارض (arḍ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: الأرض: الجرم المقابل للسماء — the earth as the corporeal substratum beneath the heavens.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الأرض: الجرم المقابل للسماء... ويعبر بها عن أسفل الشيء" — the earth as the lowest register of creation, subject to total transformation on that Day.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the physical earth. Metaphorical: "تأرض فلان: لزم الأرض" — to cling low; on that Day the earth itself is leveled, flattened, and replaced.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد (Restriction & Focused Predication) — The repeated "يوم" clauses function as temporal restrictors (ẓurūf) binding each predicate to that single, all-encompassing moment; the accumulation of names (أسامي) serves not as mere repetition but as focused predication upon the multifarious realities of a single event.
18:47.topic: Al-Ghazali on the journey of the soul, death, and the Hereafter, from 'Remembrance of Death and Afterlife'

18:49.arabic: نفس شيئا وإن كان مثقال حبة من خردل أتينا بها وكفى بنا حاسبين} وقال تعالى {ووضع الكتاب فترى المجرمين مشفقين مما فيه ويقولون يا ويلتنا ما لهذا الكتاب لا يغادر صغيرة ولا كبيرة إلا أحصاها ووجدوا ما عملوا حاضرا ولا يظلم ربك أحدا} وقال تعالى {يوم يبعثهم الله جميعا فينبئهم بما عملوا أحصاه الله ونسوه والله على كل شيء شهيد} وقال تعالى {يومئذ يصدر الناس أشتاتا ليروا أعمالهم فمن يعمل مثقال ذرة خيرا يره ومن يعمل مثقال ذرة شرا يره} وقال تعالى {ثم توفى كل نفس ما كسبت وهم لا يظلمون} وقال تعالى {يوم تجد كل نفس ما عملت من خير محضرا وما عملت من سوء تود لو أن بينها وبينه أمدا بعيدا ويحذركم الله نفسه} وقال تعالى {واعلموا أن الله يعلم ما في أنفسكم فاحذروه} فعرف أرباب البصائر من جملة الع
18:49.english: To proceed: God Most High has said: {And We shall set up the scales of justice for the Day of Resurrection, so no soul shall be wronged in anything; and if it be the weight of a grain of mustard seed, We shall bring it forth, and sufficient are We as Reckoners} (21:47). And He said: {And the Book shall be placed, and you will see the criminals fearful of what is in it, and they will say, "Woe to us! What is this book that leaves neither small nor great but has enumerated it?" And they will find what they did present, and your Lord wrongs no one} (18:49). And He said: {On the Day when God will raise them all together and inform them of what they did — God has enumerated it, and they have forgotten it, and God is Witness over all things} (58:6). And He said: {On that Day, people will issue forth in scattered groups to be shown their deeds. So whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it, and whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it} (99:6-8). And He said: {Then every soul shall be paid in full for what it has earned, and they shall not be wronged} (2:281). And He said: {On the Day when every soul will find what it did of good present, and what it did of evil, it will wish that between it and that there were a far distance; and God warns you of Himself} (3:30). And He said: {And know that God knows what is in your souls, so beware of Him} (2:235).
18:49.section_title_en: Exposition of the Reality of Truthfulness (Al-Sidq), Its Meaning, and Its Grades — Book of Vigilance and Self-Reckoning, Being the Eighth Book of the Quarter of Deliverance from the Revival of the Religious Sciences
18:49.anchors:
- Root: رقب (Raqaba)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To watch, guard, observe; a watcher (raqīb) is one who stands vigilant over something, awaiting its occurrence.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Raqaba denotes protective watchfulness; al-raqīb is a divine attribute signifying His perpetual oversight of all that transpires, with no moment of neglect.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (haqīqah): physical watching/awaiting. Metaphorical (majāz): "This matter is upon your necks (fī riqābikum)" — i.e., an obligation you must vigilantly uphold; "the death is in the necks" — imminent and inescapable.
- Root: حسب (Hasaba)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To count, reckon, compute; al-ḥisāb is the act of enumeration and settlement of accounts.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-ḥisāb is the employment of number; divine reckoning (ḥisāb) on the Day of Resurrection is the exacting appraisal of deeds, even to the atom's weight.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: counting wealth or deeds. Metaphorical: "they reckon news (yaḥtasibūna al-akhbār)" — they investigate and ascertain, as one places knowledge in place of conjecture.
- Root: قلب (Qalaba)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To turn, overturn, transform; the heart (qalb) is so named for its constant fluctuation and turning of states.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Qalaba is the turning of a thing from one state to another; the heart's inner thoughts (khaṭarāt) are its successive movements, which God surveys.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: turning a garment or object. Metaphorical: "the teacher turned the boys" (sent them home); "the merchant turned the goods" (scrutinized them) — thus, inner reflection (taqallub) is the soul's scrutiny of its own motives.
- Sibawayh Rule: Restriction and Focused Predication (al-ḥaṣr wa al-taqyīd bi-innamā) — The particle innamā restricts the predicate to the subject alone, as in "إنما يحاسبهم لتعلم كل نفس" — the sole purpose of reckoning is specified, excluding all other ends.
18:49.topic: Al-Ghazali on the journey of the soul, death, and the Hereafter, from 'Monitoring and Accounting'

18:49.arabic: الكتاب لا يغادر صغيرة ولا كبيرة إلا أحصاها} قال الصغيرة التبسم والكبيرة الضحك فكيف بما عملته الأيدي وحصدته الألسن يا أمير المؤمنين بلغني أن عمر بن الخطاب رضي الله عنه قال لو ماتت سخلة على شاطئ الفرات ضيعة لخشيت أن أسأل عنها فكيف بمن حرم عدلك وهو على بساطك يا أمير المؤمنين أتدري ما جاء في تأويل هذه الآية عن جدك {يا داود إنا جعلناك خليفة في الأرض فاحكم بين الناس بالحق ولا تتبع الهوى فيضلك عن سبيل الله} قال الله تعالى في الزبور يا داود إذا قعد الخصمان بين يديك فكان لك في أحدهما هوى فلا تتمني
18:49.english: He turned to al-Shaʿbī and said: "O Abā ʿAmr! I am the trustee of the Commander of the Faithful over Iraq and his governor over it, and a man commanded to obedience. I have been tried with the subjects, and their right has become incumbent upon me. So I love to preserve them and to attend to what sets them right, along with sincere counsel (naṣīḥah) to them. And reports may reach me about a band of people from the regions concerning a matter, and I find myself severe against them therein, so I withhold a portion of their stipends and place it in the treasury (bayt al-māl), with the intention in myself that I shall return it to them. Then it reaches the Commander of the Faithful that I have withheld it in that manner, so he writes to me that I must not return it. I cannot then countermand his order, nor can I execute his letter [against my better judgment]. I am but a man commanded to obedience. Is there any liability upon me in this, and in similar matters, where the intention is as I have described?"
18:49.section_title_en: The Upright Scholars Before the Tyrannical Rulers — Counsel and Fearless Truth-Telling
18:49.anchors:
- Root: نصح (naṣaḥa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning is sincerity, faithfulness, and pure counsel free from deceit; the root denotes the act of seeking the welfare of another with complete integrity.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In theological context, naṣīḥah is the obligation of the sincere advisor to guide the ruler toward divine truth, even at personal peril, as it is a form of worship (ʿibādah) and a trust (amānah).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) usage denotes pure honey (ʿasal naṣīḥ) free from admixture; metaphorical (majāz) usage applies to counsel that is untainted by flattery or self-interest.
- Root: سلط (sulṭ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Denotes authority, power, and dominion; the ruler (sulṭān) is one who has been given sway over affairs.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In Kalam, sulṭān is a trial (ibtilāʾ) and a trust (amānah) from God, whose exercise demands justice (ʿadl) and whose neglect invites divine wrath.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal usage refers to physical power or a governing authority; metaphorical usage extends to the authority of proof (sulṭān al-burhān) that compels assent.
- Root: عظ (waʿaẓa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Root denotes admonition, exhortation, and reminding of consequences; it implies softening the heart through remembrance of God and the Hereafter.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In theological terms, ʿiẓah is the act of turning the soul away from transgression through a blend of fear (tarhīb) and hope (targhīb), grounded in revealed truth.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal usage is the verbal admonition; metaphorical usage is the admonition of circumstance (ʿiẓah al-ḥāl) when events themselves teach a lesson.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Restriction and Focused Predication (bāb al-ḥaṣr wa al-taqyīd bi-innamā) — Governing the emphasis of exclusive predication in statements of counsel, such as "No obedience to a creature in disobedience of the Creator," where the restriction (ḥaṣr) is achieved through negation and exception (nafy wa istithnāʾ).

18:49.arabic: يا أمير المؤمنين أتدري ما جاء في تأويل هذه الآية عن جدك {ما لهذا الكتاب لا يغادر صغيرة ولا كبيرة إلا أحصاها} قال الصغيرة التبسم والكبيرة الضحك فكيف بما عملته الأيدي وحصدته الألسن يا أمير المؤمنين بلغني أن عمر بن الخطاب رضي الله عنه قال لو ماتت سخلة على شاطئ الفرات ضيعة لخشيت أن أسأل عنها فكيف بمن حرم عدلك وهو على بساطك يا أمير المؤمنين أتدري ما جاء في تأويل هذه الآية عن جدك {يا داود إنا جعلناك خليفة في الأرض فاحكم بين الناس بالحق ولا تتبع الهوى فيضلك عن سبيل الله} قال الله تعالى في الزبور يا داود إذا قعد الخصمان بين يديك فكان لك في أحدهما هوى فلا تتمني

I have been tried with the subjects, and their right has become incumbent upon me. So I love to preserve them and to attend to what sets them right, along with sincere counsel (naṣīḥah) to them. And reports may reach me about a band of people from the regions concerning a matter, and I find myself severe against them therein, so I withhold a portion of their stipends and place it in the treasury (bayt al-māl), with the intention in myself that I shall return it to them. Is there any liability upon me in this, and in similar matters, where the intention is as I have described?"
