18:49.arabic: يقول ليجزى الذي أساءوا بما عملوا ويجزى الذي أحسنوا بالحسنى وقال تعالى {ووضع الكتاب فترى المجرمين مشفقين مما فيه} الآية جعلنا الله وإياكم عاملين بكتابة متبعين لأوليائه حتى يحلنا وإياكم دار المقامة من فضله إنه حميد مجيد وقال بعض الحكماء الأيام سهام والناس أغراض والدهر يرميك كل يوم بسهامه ويخترمك بلياليه وأيامه حتى يستغرق جميع أجزائك فكيف بقاء سلامتك مع وقوع الأيام بك وسرعة الليالي في بدنك لو كشف لك عما أحدثت الأيام فيك من النقص لاستوحشت من كل يوم يأتي عليك واستثقلت ممر الساعة بك ولكن تدبير الله فوق تدبير الاعتبار وبالسلو عن غوائل الدنيا وجد طعم لذات
18:49.english: And indeed there has come the narration from him, from his Lord, Mighty and Glorious, that He said to Moses, peace be upon him: "When you see the rich man approaching, say: 'A sin whose punishment has been hastened.' And when you see the poor man approaching, say: 'Welcome to the badge of the righteous.'" And if you wish, you may follow the possessor of the Spirit and the Word, Jesus son of Mary, peace be upon him — for he used to say: "My condiment is hunger, my badge is fear, my garment is wool, my warmth in winter is the rising places of the sun, my lamp is the moon, my mount is my two feet, and my food and my fruit is what the earth brings forth. I pass the night and I possess nothing, and I rise in the morning and I possess nothing — and there is no one upon the earth richer than I."
18:49.section_title_en: The Revival of the Religious Sciences — Section 737: On the Censure of This World and the Description of Its Perils
18:49.anchors:
- Root: دنو (danuww)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "دنا فهو دانٍ" — proximity, nearness; the world (al-dunyā) is so named because it is nearer and lower, deferred from the Hereafter.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الدنو: القرب بالذات، أو بالحكم" — proximity by essence or by decree; used of place, time, and station. The "nearer" (al-adnā) is contrasted with the greater and the better.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical nearness. Metaphorical: the lower, contemptible station — "أهل الدناءة هم أهل الشناءة" (the people of baseness are the people of abhorrence).
- Root: يوم (yawm)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "اليوم" — a day; also any period of time.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "اليوم يعبر به عن وقت طلوع الشمس إلى غروبها. وقد يعبر به عن مدة من الزمان أي مدة كانت" — the day is the time from sunrise to sunset, or any duration whatsoever. "وذكرهم بأيام الله" — the days of God are His mighty deeds and calamities upon the disbelievers.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the solar day. Metaphorical: "أيام العرب" — their battles and vicissitudes; "أيام الله" — His punitive visitations.
- Root: وقد (waqada)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "وقدت النار تقد وقودا ووقدا" — the fire blazed; al-wuqūd is the fuel.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "وقودها الناس والحجارة" — the fuel of the Fire is men and stones; the one who kindles it for himself (istawqada) is he who seeks its light.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: kindling a fire. Metaphorical: "قلب وقاد" — a blazing, keen heart; "وقد الحصى" — the pebbles became scorching hot (i.e., the intensity of the sun's heat).
- Root: ألك (alaka)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "المألكة: الرسالة، لأنها تؤلك في الفم" — the message (risālah) is called ma'lakah because it is chewed/worked in the mouth.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الملائكة تقع على الواحد والجمع" — angels (malā'ikah) are so named as bearers of messages; "الله يصطفي من الملائكة رسلا" {«الله يصطفي من الملائكة رسلا»} — God chooses messengers from the angels.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: chewing (as a horse chews its bit). Metaphorical: delivering a message — the angel is the one who delivers the divine communication.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — "إنما" restricts the predicate to the subject alone, negating it of all else. Applied in the sermon: "إنما يتزين لي أوليائي بالذل والخوف" — My friends adorn themselves for Me ONLY with humility, fear, and submission — restricting their adornment to these alone, excluding all worldly ornament.
18:49.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Condemnation of the World'

18:49.arabic: تعالى يا ويلتنا ما لهذا الكتاب لا يغادر صغيرة ولا كبيرة إلا أحصاها إن الصغيرة التبسم بالاستهزاء بالمؤمن والكبيرة القهقهة بذلك وهذا إشارة إلى أن الضحك على الناس من جملة الذنوب والكبائر وعن عبد الله بن زمعة أنه قال سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وهو يخطب فوعظهم في ضحكهم من الضرطة فقال علام يضحك أحدكم مما يفعل (3) وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم إن المستهزئين بالناس يفتح لأحدهم باب من الجنة فيقال هلم هلم فيجيء بكربه وغمه فإذا أتاه أغلق دونه ثم يفتح له باب آخر فيقال هلم هلم فيجيء بكربه وغمه فإذا أتاه أغلق دونه فما يزال
18:49.english: This is forbidden whenever it is harmful, just as God—Exalted is He—has said: {«يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا يسخر قوم من قوم عسى أن يكونوا خيرا منهم ولا نساء من نساء عسى أن يكن خيرا منهن»} ["O you who believe, let not a people deride a people; perhaps they may be better than them. Nor let women deride women; perhaps they may be better than them"] (Q. 49:11). The meaning of mockery (al-sukhriyyah) is contempt, belittlement, and drawing attention to faults and defects in a manner that causes laughter at the person. This may occur through imitation in action and speech, and it may occur through gesture and indication. And if it occurs in the presence of the one being mocked, it is not called backbiting (ghībah), yet it contains the meaning of backbiting.
18:49.section_title_en: The Revival of the Religious Sciences — Section 673: The Eleventh Affliction: Mockery and Derision
18:49.anchors:
- Root: سخر (s-kh-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of subjugation and forced employment; also derision and making a mockery of someone.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "التسخير: سياقة إلى الغرض المختص قهرا" — driving toward a specific purpose by compulsion. The theological nuance here shifts to the passive form (سُخِرَ) and the verbal noun (سخرية) denoting the act of holding another in contempt and compelling them into a position of ridicule.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Haqiqah (Literal): "فلان سخرة سخرة: يضحك منه الناس" — one whom people laugh at. Majaz (Metaphorical): The root's use for subjugated service (as in "سخر الله لك") is distinct from this interpersonal derision, which is the literal sense intended here.
- Root: ضحك (ḍ-ḥ-k)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Physical laughter with the baring of teeth; the molars are called الضواحك.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الضحك: انبساط الوجه وتكشر الأسنان من سرور النفس" — expansion of the face and baring of teeth from delight of the soul. He explicitly notes: "واستعير الضحك للسخرية" — laughter is metaphorically extended to mockery, as in "ضحكت منه" (I laughed at him). This metaphorical extension is precisely the mechanism of the sin discussed here.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Haqiqah: "افتر عن ضاحكته" — smiling broadly. Majaz: "ضحكت الأرض عن النبات" — the earth "laughs" forth vegetation. The distinction is critical: the physical act of laughing (haqiqah) becomes blameworthy mockery (majaz) when directed at another's defects.
- Root: هلم (h-l-m)
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "هلم دعاء إلى الشيء" — a call toward something. Derived from "ها لم" (come, repair to) or "هل أم" (is there intent?). It is an imperative summons.
  * Lisan al-Arab: "لأَن الهاء زائدة، وأَصله هالُمّ" — the ha is augmentative; the root is l-m-m (to repair, to mend).
- Root: وقد (w-q-d)
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "وقدت النار تقد وقودا ووقدا" — the fire blazed. The verbal noun وقود refers both to fuel and to the resulting flame.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Haqiqah: "وقدت النار وقودا ووقدا، واتقدت وتوقدت" — the fire ignited and blazed. Majaz: "قلب وقاد" — a blazing heart (for intelligence). The imagery of a door opening to the scorner, who approaches "بكربه وغمه" (with his distress and grief), evokes this root's sense of burning anguish.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — The prohibition is restricted by the conditional clause "مهما كان مؤذيا" (whenever it is harmful), and the focus is sharpened by the Quranic address "يا أيها الذين آمنوا" which restricts the address to believers, making the prohibition binding upon them specifically.
18:49.topic: Al-Ghazali on the journey of the soul, death, and the Hereafter, from 'Condemnation of Anger and Hatred'

19:39.arabic: تعالى وأنذرهم يوم الحسرة إذ قضي الأمر وهم في غفلة وهم لا يؤمنون
19:39.english: At that point they despair of every good, and at that point they take to sighing, regret, and wailing. Abu Umamah said: The Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, said concerning His words, "And he is given to drink of festering water, which he sips but can hardly swallow" {«وَيُسْقَىٰ مِن مَّاءٍ صَدِيدٍ يَتَجَرَّعُهُ وَلَا يَكَادُ يُسِيغُهُ»}: "It is brought near to him, and he loathes it. When it is drawn close to him, it scorches his face, and the skin of his scalp falls off. When he drinks it, it severs his intestines until it exits from his anus." God Almighty says: {«وَسُقُوا مَاءً حَمِيمًا فَقَطَّعَ أَمْعَاءَهُمْ»} "And they are given to drink boiling water, and it severs their intestines." And He says: {«وَإِن يَسْتَغِيثُوا يُغَاثُوا بِمَاءٍ كَالْمُهْلِ يَشْوِي الْوُجُوهَ»} "And if they cry for relief, they are relieved with water like molten brass, which scalds the faces." So this is their food and drink in their hunger and thirst.
19:39.section_title_en: The Torments of the Fire: Serpents, Scorpions, and the Anguish of the Damned
19:39.anchors:
- Root: حس (ḥ-s-s) — [AVOIDED per instruction]
- Root: نار (n-r) — Fire
  * Lisan al-Arab: "النار: معروفة، وهي نار جهنم، ذات لفح وحرّ."
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "النار: قد تطلق على نار الدنيا ونار الآخرة، وهي التي أعدها الله للكافرين، وفيها من أصناف العذاب ما لا يعلمه إلا الله."
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "نار: حقيقة في النار المحرقة، ومجاز في نار الحرب والحرب."
- Root: حي (ḥ-y) — Serpent
  * Lisan al-Arab: "الحية: من الهوام، وتجمع على حيات، وأعظمها ما كان كأعناق البخت."
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الحية: دابة مؤذية، وفي الآخرة تكون أعظم وأشد إيلامًا."
- Root: عقر (ʿ-q-r) — Scorpion
  * Lisan al-Arab: "العقرب: دويبة مؤذية تلدغ، وفي النار تكون كالبغال."
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — Used to specify that serpents and scorpions are only empowered over those who were dominated by miserliness and evil character in the world.
19:39.topic: Classical commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya Ulum al-Din, from 'Remembrance of Death and Afterlife'

19:62.arabic: لهم رزقهم فيها بكرة وعشيا أما إنه ليس ليل يكر الغدو على الرواح والرواح على الغدو وإن آخر من يدخل الجنة وأدناهم منزلة ليمد له في بصره وملكه مسيرة مائة عام في قصور من الذهب والفضة وخيام اللؤلؤ ويفسح له في بصره حتى ينظر إلى أقصاه كما ينظر إلى أدناه يغدى عليهم بسبعين ألف صحفة من ذهب ويراح عليهم بمثلها في كل صحفة لون ليس في الأخرى مثله ويجد طعم آخره كما يجد طعم أوله وإن في الجنة لياقوتة فيها سبعون ألف دار في كل دار سبعون ألف بيت ليس فيها صدع ولا ثقب وقال مجاهد إن أدنى أهل الجن
19:62.english: And Mujāhid said: "The lowest of the people of Paradise in station is one who travels through his dominion for a thousand years, seeing its farthest as he sees its nearest. And the highest of them is the one who gazes upon his Lord morning and evening." And Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib said: "There is none among the people of Paradise except that in his hand are three bracelets: a bracelet of gold, a bracelet of pearl, and a bracelet of silver."
19:62.section_title_en: The Vision of Allah and the Gaze Upon His Face — The Supreme Bliss of the Hereafter
19:62.anchors:
- Root: حسن (ḥ-s-n)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of beauty, goodness, and excellence in form and act.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الحسنى" denotes the superlative good (al-ḥusnā), and "زيادة" (increase) is the added bounty beyond merit — a theological term for the beatific vision.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) for moral beauty; metaphorical (majāz) elevation when applied to divine reward, where "increase" transcends all corporeal delights.
- Root: رءي (r-'-y)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Visual perception (ru'yā) and sight (naẓar), both sensory and intellectual.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In Kalam, "ru'yat Allāh" is the vision of the divine essence — an immaterial perception granted to the blessed, not a corporeal sight of a spatial object.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal for physical sight; metaphorical transfer (naql) when applied to God, signifying direct, unveiled apprehension of His glory.
- Root: نعم (n-'-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "النعمة" is the state of well-being; "النعمى" is the superlative felicity.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "النعمة" as the good state (ḥālah ḥasanah), and "النعمى" as the ultimate bliss — here contrasted with the lesser delights of Paradise.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal for sensory comfort; metaphorical for the spiritual joy of divine proximity, which surpasses all bodily pleasures.
- Root: اهل ('-h-l)
  * Lisan / Ayn: People of a household or place; "أهل الجنة" — the inhabitants of Paradise.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "أهل الرجل" — those united by kinship, religion, or abode; here, the denizens of the Garden as a community of the blessed.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal for residents; metaphorical extension to those who merit a station by virtue of their deeds.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — Used in the closing exhortation to restrict the servant's aspiration solely to the vision of the Lord, excluding all lesser aims.
19:62.topic: Al-Ghazali on the journey of the soul, death, and the Hereafter, from 'Remembrance of Death and Afterlife'

19:68.arabic: العرض على الله تعالى تصديقا لقوله تعالى {فوربك لنحشرنهم والشياطين ثم لنحضرنهم حول جهنم جثيا} فتفكر فى حالك وحال قلبك هنالك
19:68.english: The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: Allah the Exalted said: "The son of Adam has reviled Me, and he had no right to revile Me; and he has denied Me, and he had no right to deny Me. As for his reviling of Me, it is his saying that I have a son. And as for his denial of Me, it is his saying: 'He will never bring me back as He created me at first.'" {«شتمني ابن آدم وما ينبغي له أن يشتمني وكذبني وما ينبغي له أن يكذبني...»}
19:68.section_title_en: On the Terrors of the Trumpet-Blast and the Awakening for the Resurrection
19:68.anchors:
- Root: نفخ (N-F-Kh)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To blow into a thing, to inflate; the breath of wind entering a vessel or body.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The divine act of breathing spirit into creation {«ونفخت فيه من روحي»}; here, the eschatological blast that annihilates and then revives all beings.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah) usage of blowing into the Trumpet (الصور); metaphorical extension to the "blast of spring" reviving the earth—here applied to the two cosmic blasts of death and resurrection.
- Root: صور (S-W-R)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Form, image, shape; also a horn or trumpet (the instrument of the blast).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The perceptible form of bodies and the intelligible form of souls; here, the Trumpet (الصور) as the instrument of divine command that re-forms and re-shapes creation.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the horn (القرن) held by Israfil; metaphorical: the "inclination" (صورة) of hearts toward terror and anticipation.
- Root: موت (M-W-T)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Death as the cessation of life; the state of the corpse.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Death as the separation of the soul from the body; the "first death" of the blast and the "second death" of the wicked.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical death; metaphorical: the "death" of the heart through heedlessness, and the reviving of dead lands by rain—here, the reviving of bodies by the second blast.
- Root: قبر (Q-B-R)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The grave as the abode of the dead; burial.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The grave as the intermediate state (barzakh) before resurrection; {«حتى زرتم المقابر»} as a metaphor for death.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the grave and its inhabitants; metaphorical: the "raising of the nose" (قبراه) of the proud—contrasted here with the humility of the dead rising from their graves.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — Used to emphasize that true faith is not mere verbal assent but heartfelt conviction, as in "إنما فتور البواطن... لقلة الفهم" (The languor of the inner selves is only due to the lack of understanding).
19:68.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Remembrance of Death and Afterlife'

19:84.arabic: إلى نفسه وبكى على عدد ذنوبه ثم قرأ هذه الآية إنما نعد لهم عدا يعني الأنفاس آخر العدد خروج نفسك آخر العدد فراق أهلك آخر العدد دخولك في قبرك واجتهد أبو موسى الأشعري قبل موته اجتهادا شديدا فقيل له لو أمسكت أو رفقت بنفسك بعض الرفق فقال إن الخيل إذا أرسلت فقاربت رأس مجراها أخرجت جميع ما عندها والذي بقي من أجلى أقل من ذلك قال فلم يزل على ذلك حتى مات وكان يقول لامرأته شدي رحلك فليس على جهنم معبرة وقال بعض الخلفاء على منبره عباد الله اتقوا الله ما استطعتم وكونوا قوما صيح بهم فانتبهوا وعلموا أن الدنيا ليست
19:84.english: I say: The hadith was transmitted by al-Tirmidhi and deemed sound (ḥasan) from the narration of Ubayy ibn Kaʿb (5): a hadith that when he (the Prophet, peace be upon him) sensed from his companions heedlessness or negligence, he would call out to them in a raised voice: "Death has come upon you." This hadith was transmitted by Ibn Abi al-Dunya in *Qaṣr al-Amal* from the narration of Zayd al-Sulaymi as a mursal report (6). The hadith of Abu Hurayrah: "I am the warner, death is the transformer, and the Hour is the appointed meeting" — transmitted by Ibn Abi al-Dunya in *Qaṣr al-Amal* and by Abu al-Qasim al-Baghawi with an isnad containing some weakness (7). The hadith of Ibn ʿUmar: "The Messenger of God, peace be upon him, went out while the sun was at the tips of the palm fronds and said: 'What remains of this world is but like what remains of this day of ours, relative to what has passed of it'" — transmitted by Ibn Abi al-Dunya therein with a sound isnad, and al-Tirmidhi transmitted something similar from the narration of Abu Saʿid and deemed it sound (8). The hadith: "The likeness of this world is like a garment torn from its beginning to its end" — transmitted by Ibn Abi al-Dunya therein from the narration of Anas, but it is not authentic (9). Ibn Masʿud, may God be pleased with him, said: The Messenger of God, peace be upon him, recited: {فمن يرد الله أن يهديه يشرح صدره للإسلام} "Whomsoever God wishes to guide, He expands his breast to Islam" {فقال} "Then he said: 'When the light enters the breast, it expands.' It was said: 'O Messenger of God, is there a sign of this that is recognized?' PageV04P459 {قال} He said: 'Yes: withdrawal from the abode of delusion, turning in repentance to the abode of permanence, and preparation for death before its descent.'" Al-Suddi said concerning His saying: {الذي خلق الموت والحياة ليبلوكم أيكم أحسن عملا} "He who created death and life to test you, which of you is best in deed" — meaning: which of you is most mindful of death, best prepared for it, and most fearful and cautious of it. Hudhayfah said: "There is no morning or evening except that a caller calls out: 'O people, the departure! The departure!'" The confirmation of that is His saying, the Exalted: {إنها لإحدى الكبر * نذيرا للبشر * لمن شاء منكم أن يتقدم أو يتأخر} "Indeed, it is one of the greatest calamities, a warning to mankind, for whoever among you wishes to advance or delay" — regarding death. Suhaym, the freed slave of Banu Tamim, said: I sat with ʿAmir ibn ʿAbd Allah while he was praying, and he shortened his prayer, then turned to me and said: "Relieve me of your need, for I am hastening." I said: "What are you hastening for?" He said: "The angel of death, may God have mercy on you." He said: So I rose from him, and he returned to his prayer. Dawud al-Ta'i passed by, and a man asked him about a hadith, so he said: "Leave me, for I am only hastening against the departure of my soul." ʿUmar, may God be pleased with him, said: "Deliberation is good in everything except in deeds of goodness for the Hereafter." Al-Mundhir said: I heard Malik ibn Dinar saying to himself: "Woe to you, hasten before the matter comes upon you. Woe to you, hasten before the matter comes upon you" — repeating that sixty times, while I heard him and he did not see me. Al-Hasan used to say in his exhortation: "Hasten, hasten! For it is but breaths — if they are held back, your deeds by which you draw near to God, the Mighty and Majestic, are cut off. May God have mercy on a man who looked to his own soul and wept over the number of his sins." Then he recited this verse: {إنما نعد لهم عدا} "We only count for them a counting" — meaning the breaths. The end of the counting is the departure of your soul; the end of the counting is the parting from your family; the end of the counting is your entry into your grave. Abu Musa al-Ashʿari strove with intense exertion before his death, and it was said to him: "Would you not hold back, or show yourself some gentleness?" He said: "When horses are released and approach the end of their course, they bring out all that they have. What remains of my term is less than that." He said: He continued in that state until he died. And he used to say to his wife: "Tighten your saddle, for there is no crossing over Hellfire." One of the caliphs said from his pulpit: "O servants of God, fear God as much as you are able, and be a people who were called out to, so they awoke, and knew that this world is not for them a permanent abode, so they exchanged it, and prepared for death, for it has overshadowed you. And depart, for the journey has become urgent for you. Indeed, a goal that the moment diminishes and the hour demolishes is worthy of a short duration. Indeed, an absent one whom the two new ones — night and day — hasten is deserving of a swift return. Indeed, an arrival that resolves in triumph or misery is worthy of the best provision. So let him meet his Lord — whoever advises his own soul, presents his repentance, and overcomes his desire — for his term is concealed from him, his hope deceives him, and Satan is entrusted to him, promising him repentance to postpone it, and beautifying disobedience to him to commit it, until his death descends upon him when he is most heedless of it. Indeed, between each of you and Paradise or Hellfire is nothing but death, that it should alight upon him. So what a regret for one who is heedless, or whose life is a proof against him, and whose days lead him to misery. May God make us and you among those whom prosperity does not make insolent, whom disobedience does not hold back from obedience to God, and upon whom regret does not alight after death. Indeed, He is Hearing of supplication, and in His hand is goodness always, and He does what He wills." Some of the exegetes said concerning His saying, the Exalted: {فتنتم أنفسكم} "You tried yourselves" — meaning: with desires and pleasures; {وتربصتم} "and you waited" — meaning: for repentance; {وارتبتم} "and you doubted" — meaning: you were skeptical, until the command of God came — meaning: death; {وغركم بالله الغرور} "and the deluder deluded you concerning God" — meaning: Satan. Al-Hasan said: "Be patient and be firm, for it is but a few days, and you are but a standing caravan — soon one of you will be called, and he will respond without turning back. So move on with the righteous deeds that are in your possession." Ibn Masʿud said: "There is none of you who wakes up except that he is a guest, and what he has is a loan. The guest departs, and the loan is returned." Abu ʿUbaydah al-Baji said: We entered upon al-Hasan in his illness from which he died, and he said: "Welcome to you, and greetings. May God greet you with peace, and settle us and you in the abode of permanence. This is a good outward sign if you are patient, truthful, and God-fearing. So let not your share of this report — may God have mercy on you — be merely that you hear it with this ear and let it out from this ear. For whoever has seen Muhammad, peace be upon him, has seen him going forth early."
19:84.section_title_en: The Haste for Death and Readiness for the Hereafter — Section 1291
19:84.anchors:
- Root: موت (m-w-t)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root denotes cessation of vital faculty; "مات موتة" as a singular event of death.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Death as transition from worldly life to the reckoning; linked to "أجل" (appointed term) and divine decree.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah) = biological death; Metaphorical (Majaz) = "إماتة" of the heart via heedlessness, and "الموت المغير" as the transformative destroyer of states.
- Root: بدر (b-d-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root denotes hastening, rushing to a task; "بادر" implies competing with time.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In Quranic usage, "المبادر" is the soul's urgency toward obedience before the term expires.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal = physical speed; Metaphorical = spiritual vigilance against procrastination (تسويف).
- Root: عرض (ʿ-r-ḍ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root denotes presenting, exposing; "العارية" (loan) as something transiently possessed.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Worldly life as "عارية" (borrowed thing) from God, to be returned at death.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal = loaned object; Metaphorical = the body and lifespan as a trust (أمانة) from the Creator.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب التوكيد بالتكرار (Emphatic Repetition) — Repetition of phrases like "ويحك بادري" and "المبادرة المبادرة" serves as syntactic emphasis (توكيد لفظي) to intensify the exhortation, a structure Sibawayh treats as permissible for rhetorical force without redundancy.
19:84.topic: Al-Ghazali on the journey of the soul, death, and the Hereafter, from 'Remembrance of Death and Afterlife'

19:85.arabic: خثعم فقرأ عليه {يوم نحشر المتقين إلى الرحمن وفدا ونسوق المجرمين إلى جهنم وردا} فقال أنا من المجرمين ولست من المتقين أعد على القول أيها القارئ فأعادها عليه فشهق شهقة فلحق بالآخرة وقرئ عند يحيى البكاء {ولو ترى إذ وقفوا على ربهم} فصاح صيحة مكث منها مريضا أربعة أشهر يعاد من أطراف البصرة وقال مالك بن دينار بينما أنا أطوف بالبيت إذا أنا بجويرة متعبدة متعلقة بأستار الكعبة وهي تقول يا رب كم شهوة ذهبت لذاتها وبقيت تبعاتها يا رب أما كان لك أدب وعقوبة إلا النار وتبكى فما زال ذلك مقامها حتى طلع الفجر قال مالك فلما رأيت ذلك وضعت يدي
19:85.english: One of them said: "Would that my mother had never given birth to me."
19:85.section_title_en: The States of the Fearful — Accounts of the Companions and Early Saints (Section 1061)
19:85.anchors:
- Root: خوف (kh-w-f)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of dread and apprehension; the heart's agitation before an anticipated harm.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الخوف: توقع مكروه عن أمارة مظنونة، أو معلومة" — fear is the expectation of misfortune based on a probable or certain sign; it is the opposite of security (amn) and pertains to both worldly and otherworldly matters.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): "خفته على مالي خوفا وخيفة" — to fear for something. Metaphorical (Majaz): "تخوفه: تنقصه وأخذ من أطرافه" — fear that consumes one gradually, as in the verse of Zuhayr where the journey "wears away" the camel's hump little by little, as if in dread of it.
- Root: يوم (y-w-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: A measure of time from sunrise to sunset, or any period whatsoever.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "اليوم يعبر به عن وقت طلوع الشمس إلى غروبها. وقد يعبر به عن مدة من الزمان أي مدة كانت" — the Day is a term for any span of time; when added to God (أيام الله), it signifies His mighty acts and visitations upon the nations.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: a single day. Metaphorical: "ذكر في أيام العرب كذا أي في وقائعها" — "days" denotes battles and momentous events; "أيام الله" are His punitive calamities upon the disbelievers.
- Root: حتي (ḥ-t-y)
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): A particle of end-point (ghāyah), signifying the terminal limit of an action or state, as in {ليسجننه حتى حين} and {حتى مطلع الفجر}.
  * Sibawayh Rule: Prepositional and particle interposition (الفصل بين الجار والمجرور) — the particle ḥattā governs what follows as the culminating limit of the preceding narrative, marking the climax of an emotional or physical state (e.g., "until he fell unconscious," "until he died").
- Root: بكى (b-k-y)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Weeping with tears; the physical manifestation of inner anguish.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Weeping is the outward expression of the heart's grief (ḥuzn); in the fearful, it is the release of the soul's dread before God's majesty.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: shedding tears. Metaphorical: "بكاء الثكلي" — the weeping of a bereaved mother, intensified by burning loss, used here to describe the saints' weeping on the Day of Arafah.
19:85.topic: Al-Ghazali on the journey of the soul, death, and the Hereafter, from 'Remembrance of Death and Afterlife'

19:93.arabic: وهو أحد والآصال التي ذكرها الله تعالى إذ قال ولله يسجد من في السموات والأرض طوعا وكرها وظلالهم بالغدو والآصال وإذا سجد لله عز وجل الجمادات فكيف يجوز أن يغفل العبد العاقل عن أنواع العبادات الورد السادس إذا دخل وقت العصر دخل وقت الورد السادس وهو الذي أقسم الله تعالى به فقال تعالى {والعصر} هذا أحد معنيي الآية وهو المراد بالآصال في أحد التفسيرين وهو العشي المذكور في قوله {وعشيا} وفي قوله {بالعشي والإشراق} وليس في هذا الورد صلاة إلا أربع ركعات بين الأذان والإقامة كما سبق في الظهر ثم يصلي الفرض ويشتغل بالأقسام الأربعة المذكورة
19:93.english: I say: And just as knowledge and remembrance are the nourishment of the heart, which can never be cut off from it, so too the measure of moderation is this; and deficiency from it may lead to the disturbance of the body — except for one who accustoms himself to wakefulness gradually, for he may train himself upon it without disturbance. And this litany (wird) is among the longest of the litanies and the most delightful for the worshippers, and it is one of the "evenings and mornings" (al-āṣāl) which God Most High mentioned when He said: {«ولله يسجد من في السموات والأرض طوعا وكرها وظلالهم بالغدو والآصال»} "And to God prostrates whoever is in the heavens and the earth, willingly or unwillingly, and their shadows, in the mornings and the evenings" (Q. 13:15). And when inanimate objects prostrate to God, Mighty and Majestic, how then can the intelligent servant be heedless of the varieties of worship?
19:93.section_title_en: The Seventh Daily Litany (Al-Wird al-Sābiʿ): The Time of Sunset — The Completion of the Day's Litanies and Self-Accounting
19:93.anchors:
- Root: ورد (warada)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The root denotes arriving at water, seeking it, and drinking from it; also the portion or share of water allotted for drinking at a specific time.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الورود أصله: قصد الماء" — the core meaning is the intentional approach to water; the litany (wird) is the appointed portion of devotional recitation, likened to the daily share of water that a person must take to sustain life.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): the act of arriving at water. Metaphorical (Majaz): "ورد علي كتاب سرني مورده" — a book arrived upon me whose arrival pleased me; likewise, the wird is the arrival of the appointed time for worship, and the soul's approach to the fountain of divine remembrance.
- Root: عصر (ʿaṣr)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The root denotes pressing, squeezing, and extracting; also the time of afternoon, so called because it is the pressing of the day's end.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The ʿaṣr is the latter part of the day; God swore by it in {«والعصر»} (Q. 103:1), indicating its great merit.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the afternoon time. Metaphorical: the pressing of one's life — as the day is pressed at its end, so the life of man is pressed at its term.
- Root: غرب (gharaba)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The root denotes disappearance, absence, and setting; the sun's setting (ghurūb) is its concealment from the eye.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The setting of the sun marks the boundary between the day's works and the night's; it is the terminus of the visible world's diurnal cycle.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the sun's descent below the horizon. Metaphorical: the setting of the sun of life — the death of man, after which there is no rising.
- Root: حاسب (ḥāsaba)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The root denotes reckoning, counting, and taking account; muḥāsabah is the mutual reckoning between two parties.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Self-accounting (muḥāsabat al-nafs) is the soul's reckoning with itself over its deeds before the Day of Reckoning, for "one who reckons himself before he is reckoned" is among the wise.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the arithmetic counting of sums. Metaphorical: the soul's audit of its own works, weighing the day's deeds against the standard of the Sacred Law.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The rule governing the separation of the prepositional phrase from its governing verb, as in the construction "فسبحان الله حين تمسون" where the adverbial clause is interposed to emphasize the temporal specification of the act of glorification.
19:93.topic: Al-Ghazali on constant remembrance of God and contemplative invocations, from 'Remembrance of Death and Afterlife'

19:93.arabic: ونمجده تمجيد من يصرح بأن كل شيء ما سوى الله باطل ولا يتحاشى وأن كل من في السموات والأرض لن يخلقوا ذبابا ولو اجتمعوا له ولا فراشا ونشكره إذ رفع السماء لعباده سقفا مبنيا ومهد الأرض بساطا لهم وفراشا وكور الليل على النهار فجعل الليل لباسا والنهار معاشا لينتشروا في إبتغاء فضله وينتعشوا به عن ضراعة الحاجات انتعاشا ونصلي على رسوله الذي يصدر المؤمنون عن حوضه رواء بعد ورودهم عليه عطاشا وعلى آله وأصحابه الذين لم يدعوا في نصرة دينه تشمرا وانكماشا وسلم تسليما كثيرا أما بعد فإن رب الأرباب ومسبب الأسباب جعل الآخرة دار الثواب والعقاب والدنيا
19:93.english: It is related from Muʿādh ibn Jabal, who said: The Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "No woman harms her husband in this world but that his wife from the ḥūr al-ʿīn says to her: 'May God slay you! Do not harm him — for he is only a sojourner (dakhīl) with you; soon he shall part from you and come to us.'"
19:93.section_title_en: The Book of the Etiquette of Earning and Livelihood — Introduction and Chapter Divisions
19:93.anchors:
- Root: زوج (z-w-j)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Pairing, coupling; each of the two members of a pair — whether male/female in animals, or two matched things like sandals; "زوجة" is a weak (radī'ah) dialectal form.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Every one of two paired things — in animals, the male and female; in other things, any two that are paired, similar or opposite. From this: the wife is called "zawj" for the husband, and he "zawj" for her.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (haqīqah): "He is her zawj and she is his zawj or zawjah; the two are zawjān." Metaphorical (majāz): "The two discourses paired (tazāwajā) and were coupled (izdawajā)."
- Root: رسل (r-s-l)
  * Lisan / Ayn: A small creature; "Umm risālah": the carrion kite. The root conveys sending forth with gentleness and ease.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The origin of "risl" is emission with leisurely ease — a she-camel that is "raslah" is easy-paced. From this, the messenger (rasūl) is one sent forth; and from the sense of gentleness comes "on your leisure" (alā rislik).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: sending a message, dispatching messengers, releasing a stallion among camels, loosing a dog or falcon upon game. Metaphorical: "God loosed (arsala) chastisement upon them"; "the arrows are the messengers (rusul) of deathly fates."
- Root: داب (d-'-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To persist and toil; "al-dābbatān" (the two toiling ones) is said of night and day in their ceaseless alternation.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Da'b" is the continuance of journeying — "and He subjected the sun and moon to you, both persisting (dā'ibayn)" {«وَسَخَّرَ لَكُمُ الشَّمْسَ وَالْقَمَرَ دَائِبَيْنِ»}; and "da'b" is the habitual custom one persists upon — "like the custom (ka-da'bi) of the house of Pharaoh."
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: to strive diligently in work, to toil in travel. Metaphorical: "This is your da'b" — i.e., your constant concern and occupation; "night and day toil (yad'abān) in their mutual succession."
- Root: الي ('-l-k)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "Al-alak" and "al-ālūk": the chewing and working of the bit in a horse's mouth.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-Khalīl said: "al-ma'lakah" (the message/angelic mission) is the conveying of a message, because it is "worked in the mouth" (tu'lak fī al-fam) — from their saying of a horse: "it works (ya'lik) the bit," i.e., chews it. The angels are called "malā'ikah" because they convey messages.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد (Restriction & Specification) — The particle "innamā" restricts the predicate to the subject alone, negating any extension beyond it. Applied here to the wife's mourning obligation: "she must not mourn (lā taḥidd) over any dead person more than three days — except over a husband, four months and ten days," where the exception clause (istithnā') delimits the general prohibition.
19:93.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Etiquette of Earning'

19:98.arabic: تدميرا فقال تعالى هل تحس منهم من أحد الآية وقد حذر الله تعالى من مكره واستدراجه فقال فلا يأمن مكر الله إلا القوم الخاسرون وقال تعالى ومكروا مكرا ومكرنا مكرا وهم لا يشعرون وقال عز وجل ومكروا ومكر الله والله خير الماكرين وقال تعالى إنهم يكيدون كيدا وأكيد كيدا فمهل الكافرين أمهلهم رويدا فكما لا يجوز للعبد المهمل أن يستدل بإهمال السيد إياه وتمكينه من النعم على حب السيد بل ينبغي أن يحذر أن يكون ذلك مكرا منه وكيدا مع أن السيد لم يحذره مكر نفسه فبأن يجب ذلك في حق الله تعالى مع تحذيره استدراج
19:98.english: As for knowing it by way of authoritative transmission and affirmation (taṣdīq): it is that one believes in the Book of God — exalted is He — and affirms His Messenger. For God — exalted is He — has said: {«أيحسبون أن ما نمدهم به من مال وبنين * نسارع لهم في الخيرات بل لا يشعرون»} — "Do they reckon that what We extend to them of wealth and sons — [that] We hasten for them good things? Nay, but they do not perceive" (Q. 23:55-56). And He said — exalted is He: {«سنستدرجهم من حيث لا يعلمون»} — "We shall draw them on by degrees from whence they do not know" (Q. 7:182). And He said — exalted is He: {«فتحنا عليهم أبواب كل شيء حتى إذا فرحوا بما أوتوا أخذناهم بغتة فإذا هم مبلسون»} — "We opened upon them the gates of everything, until when they rejoiced in what they were given, We seized them suddenly, and behold, they were in despair" (Q. 6:44). And in the interpretation of His saying — exalted is He: {«سنستدرجهم من حيث لا يعلمون»} — it is said: "Whenever they innovated a sin, We innovated for them a blessing, to increase their self-deception." And He said — exalted is He: {«إنما نملي لهم ليزدادوا إثما»} — "We only grant them respite that they may increase in sin" (Q. 3:178). And He said — exalted is He: {«ولا تحسبن الله غافلا عما يعمل الظالمون إنما يؤخرهم ليوم تشخص فيه الأبصار»} — "And do not reckon God heedless of what the wrongdoers do; He only delays them to a Day when eyes will stare fixedly" (Q. 14:42). And [there is] more of that kind which has come in the Book of God — exalted is He — and in the Sunnah of His Messenger. So whoever believes in it is delivered from this self-deception. For the origin of this self-deception is ignorance of God and of His attributes; for whoever knows Him does not feel secure from His stratagem (makr) and is not deceived by such corrupt fancies.
19:98.section_title_en: Section 888 — On the Remedy for Self-Deception (Ghurūr): Recognizing the Signs of Divine Honor (Karāmah) and Humiliation (Hawān)
19:98.anchors:
- Root: غرر (gh-r-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of an outward trace or mark; heedlessness in wakefulness; the blaze on a horse's forehead.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Ghurūr" is delusion stemming from heedlessness — the soul's being overtaken while imagining security, as in {«ما غرك بربك الكريم»} (Q. 82:6). It is the state of one who is deceived by apparent favors while blind to their underlying test.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): heedlessness and exposure to predation, like a gazelle deceived by moonlight. Metaphorical (Majaz): being "deceived by God" (ightirār billāh) — trusting in His mercy while persisting in disobedience.
- Root: لهم (l-h-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Swallowing whole; the gullet.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Ilhām" — God's casting a meaning into the heart (al-raw'), distinct from demonic whispering; the channel of inner vision for the knowers (ʿārifūn).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: to swallow. Metaphorical: the heart's receptive "swallowing" of divine inspiration.
- Root: حدث (ḥ-d-th)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Origination after non-existence; newness.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Ḥudūth" — a thing's coming to be after it was not; "muḥdith" — the originator, exclusively God for substances (jawāhir). "Iḥdāth" — bringing about a novel state or act.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: temporal newness. Metaphorical: "muḥaddath" — one inspired with correct discernment, as if newly spoken-to.
- Root: نعم (n-ʿ-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Softness, ease, well-being; a state of comfort.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Niʿmah" — the good state one inhabits; "naʿīm" — the act of living pleasantly. Blessings are both a test and a sign, per {«وإن تعدوا نعمة الله لا تحصوها»} (Q. 16:18).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: bounty and comfort. Metaphorical: "khafat naʿāmatuhum" — their prosperity vanished; blessings may signal either favor or gradual ruin (istidrāj).
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction and Focused Predication with "innamā")
  * In {«إنما نملي لهم ليزدادوا إثما»} (Q. 3:178) and {«إنما يؤخرهم ليوم تشخص فيه الأبصار»} (Q. 14:42), "innamā" restricts the purpose of divine respite exclusively to increase of sin and deferred reckoning — negating any reading of it as benevolent indulgence.
19:98.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Condemnation of Delusion'

19:98.arabic: ولا ذكر من ذكرك كما أتى على الملوك الذين كانوا من قبلك فهل تحس منهم من أحد أو تسمع لهم ركزا فكيف تبيعين يا نفس ما يبقى أبد الآباد بما لا يبقى أكثر من خمسين سنة إن بقى هذا إن كنت ملكا من ملوك الأرض سلم لك الشرق والغرب حتى أذعنت لك الرقاب وانتظمت لك الأسباب كيف ويأبى إدبارك وشقاوتك أن يسلم لك أمر محلتك بل أمر دارك فضلا عن محلتك فإن كنت يا نفس لا تتركين الدنيا رغبة في الآخرة لجهلك وعمى بصيرتك فما لك لا تتركينها ترفعا عن خسة شركائها وتنزها عن كثرة عنائها وتوقيا من سرعة فنائها أم ما لك لا تزهدين في قليلها بعد أن زهد فيك كثيرها وما لك تفرحين بد
19:98.english: ...from creation, but rather you attain your goal through every stratagem. And by this ignorance you deserve the title of foolishness from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, where he said: "The shrewd one is he who holds his soul to account and works for what comes after death, and the foolish one is he who follows his soul's whims and harbors vain hopes upon God." {«الكيس من دان نفسه وعمل لما بعد الموت والأحمق من أتبع نفسه هواها وتمنى على الله الأماني»}
19:98.section_title_en: Section 1253 — The Soul's Self-Reproach and the Awakening from Negligence
19:98.anchors:
- Root: نفس (n-f-s)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The self, soul, or spirit; that which animates and is addressed as an independent moral agent.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The soul as the locus of divine address and self-knowledge; its essence (dhāt) is the referent of God's "self" in revelation, yet here it is the reproaching subject.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (haqīqah) usage as the speaking, desiring self; metaphorical (majāz) extension to blame and counsel, as in "self-accusation" (lawwāmah).
- Root: موت (m-w-t)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Death as the cessation of life; the inevitable terminus of every soul.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Death as separation (furqah) from worldly attachments and the transition to reckoning; linked to the soul's journey.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal death of the body; metaphorical "death" of the heart through heedlessness, contrasted here with physical death as the ultimate wake-up call.
- Root: جهل (j-h-l)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Ignorance as the absence of knowledge; folly and rashness.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Ignorance as the soul's failure to perceive true realities, leading to misplaced desires and false hopes.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal ignorance of facts; metaphorical ignorance as moral stupidity, as when the soul follows whims despite clear signs.
- Root: دنا (d-n-w)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Nearness in place, time, or rank.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Drawing near (dunūw) to God through obedience, contrasted with the soul's clinging to the near (dunyā) world.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal proximity; metaphorical use for the "lower" world (dunyā) as that which is nearer and inferior.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — Used to emphasize exclusive causation, e.g., "God's generosity is only in guiding you to the path," restricting divine favor to guidance, not exemption from effort.
19:98.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Remembrance of Death and Afterlife'

20:55.arabic: منها خلقناكم وفيها نعيدكم ومنها نخرجكم تارة أخرى وإنه ليسمع خفق نعالهم إذا ولوا مدبرين حتى يقال يا هذا من ربك وما دينك وما نبيك فيقول ربي الله وديني الإسلام ونبي محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم قال فينتهرأنه انتهارا شديدا وهي آخر فرصة تعرض على الميت فإذا قال ذلك نادى مناد أن قد صدقت وهي معنى قوله تعالى {يثبت الله الذين آمنوا بالقول الثابت} ثم يأتيه آت حسن الوجه طيب الريح حسن الثياب فيقول أبشر برحمة ربك وجنات فيها نعيم مقيم فيقول وأنت فبشرك الله بخير من أنت فيقول أنا عملك الصالح والله ما علمت أن كنت لسريعا إ
20:55.english: Al-Barā' ibn ʿĀzib said: We went out with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the funeral procession of a man from the Anṣār. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sat at his grave with his head bowed, then said: "O God, I seek refuge in You from the torment of the grave" — three times. Then he said: "Verily, the believer, when he is in the final stage of the Hereafter and the severance from this world, God sends down to him angels whose faces are like the sun, bearing with them his embalming perfume and his shroud. They sit before him as far as his eye can reach. When his soul departs, every angel between heaven and earth prays for him, and every angel in heaven [prays for him], and the gates of heaven are opened — there is no gate but that it yearns for his soul to enter through it. When his soul ascends, it is said: 'O Lord, Your servant so-and-so.' He says: 'Return him, and show him what I have prepared for him of honor, for I promised him: {From it We created you, and into it We shall return you, and from it We shall bring you forth another time} [Ta-Ha/ 55].' And he indeed hears the shuffling of their sandals when they turn away departing, until it is said to him: 'O this one, who is your Lord, and what is your religion, and who is your Prophet?' He says: 'My Lord is God, my religion is Islam, and my Prophet is Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace.' He said: Then he is rebuked with a severe rebuke — and this is the last opportunity presented to the dead — and when he says that, a caller calls out: 'He has spoken the truth' — and this is the meaning of His saying, the Exalted: {God establishes those who believe with the firm word} [Ibrahim/ 27]. Then there comes to him a visitor of beautiful countenance, pleasant fragrance, and fine garments, who says: 'Rejoice in the mercy of your Lord and gardens of enduring delight.' He says: 'And you — may God give you good news of good. Who are you?' He says: 'I am your righteous deed. By God, I knew not but that you were swift to the obedience of God and slow to the disobedience of God — so may God reward you with good.' He said: Then a caller calls out: 'Spread for him from the carpets of Paradise, and open for him a gate to Paradise.' So carpets of Paradise are spread for him, and a gate to Paradise is opened for him. He says: 'O God, hasten the establishment of the Hour, so that I may return to my family and my wealth.' He said: And as for the disbeliever — when he is in the final stage of the Hereafter and the severance from this world, there descend to him angels, harsh and severe, bearing with them garments of fire and tunics of molten pitch. They surround him completely. When his soul departs, every angel between heaven and earth curses him, and every angel in heaven [curses him], and the gates of heaven are shut — there is no gate but that it abhors his soul to enter through it. When his soul ascends, it is cast away, and it is said: 'O Lord, Your servant so-and-so — neither heaven nor earth accepted him.' So God, Mighty and Majestic, says: 'Return him, and show him what I have prepared for him of evil, for I promised him: {From it We created you, and into it We shall return you, and from it We shall bring you forth another time}.' And he indeed hears the shuffling of their sandals when they turn away departing, until it is said to him: 'O this one, who is your Lord, and who is your Prophet, and what is your religion?' He says: 'I do not know.' It is said: 'You did not know!' Then there comes to him a visitor of ugly countenance, foul stench, and vile garments, who says: 'Rejoice in the wrath of God and a painful enduring torment.' He says: 'May God give you evil news. Who are you?' He says: 'I am your wicked deed. By God, I knew not but that you were swift in the disobedience of God and slow to the obedience of God — so may God reward you with evil.' He says: 'And you — may God reward you with evil.' Then there is appointed for him a blind, deaf, and mute one, bearing with him an iron mace — were the two heavy species (thaqalān, i.e., jinn and men) to gather upon it to lift it, they could not — and were he to strike a mountain with it, it would become dust. He strikes him with it a blow, and he becomes dust. Then the soul is returned to him, and he strikes him with it between his eyes a blow whose sound is heard by all upon the earths, save the two heavy species. He said: Then a caller calls out: 'Spread for him two planks of fire, and open for him a gate to the Fire.' So two planks of fire are spread for him, and a gate to the Fire is opened for him.
20:55.section_title_en: The Torments of the Grave and the Visions of the Soul at Death — Section 1323
20:55.anchors:
- Root: قبر (q-b-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The grave as the abode of the dead; the act of interment.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The grave is the place of repose for the dead, and the term extends metaphorically to the state of the barzakh (intermediate realm). The Quranic phrase {حتى زرتم المقابر} [التكاثر/ 2] is a metonymy for death itself.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah) — the physical grave. Metaphorical (Majaz) — the spiritual state of the soul after death, as in "رفع قبراه" (raising one's grave-mound), i.e., arrogance, indicating that the grave's true reality transcends mere earth.
- Root: ملك (m-l-k)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Dominion and authority; the angels as emissaries of divine command.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الملك: هو المتصرف بالأمر والنهي" — the one who disposes by command and prohibition. Angels are termed "رسل" (messengers) of God, as in {الله يصطفي من الملائكة رسلا} [الحج/ 75], and their acts are entirely subordinate to divine will.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — angels as corporeal agents of punishment or mercy. Metaphorical — their true nature is immaterial (laṭīfah rabbāniyyah), imperceptible to the physical senses of the living.
- Root: روح (r-w-ḥ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Breath, spirit, the animating principle.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The soul (rūḥ) is a subtle divine reality (laṭīfah rabbāniyyah) that departs the body at death; its extraction is described in degrees of ease or violence according to faith or disbelief.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — the breath of life. Metaphorical — the spiritual essence that perceives the malakūt (invisible dominion) after death, a realm beyond the reach of the corporeal eye.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The periodic structure of the hadith, e.g., "خرجنا مع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في جنازة رجل من الأنصار," demonstrates how prepositional phrases (مع، في، من) interlock to build a narrative sequence, each clause grammatically complete yet subordinate to the overarching report, mirroring the unbroken chain of transmission (isnād).
20:55.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'Remembrance of Death and Afterlife'

20:98.arabic: القلوب فوالله الذي لا إله إلا هو ما ذلك إلا لأن المعلمين علموا لغير الله تعالى والمتعلمين تعلموا لغير الله تعالى وفي التوراة والإنجيل مكتوب لا تطلبوا علم ما لم تعلموا حتى تعملوا بما علمتم وقال حذيفة رضي الله عنه إنكم في زمان من ترك فيه عشر ما يعلم هلك وسيأتي زمان من عمل فيه بعشر ما يعلم نجا وذلك لكثرة البطالين واعلم أن مثل العالم مثل القاضي وقد قال صلى الله عليه وسلم القضاة ثلاثة قاض قضى بالحق وهو يعلم فذلك في الجنة وقاض قضى بالجور وهو يعلم أو لا يعلم فهو في النار وقاض ق
20:98.english: Know that the scholar who does not act upon his knowledge is condemned by the Book, the Sunnah, and the sayings of the sages. God, exalted be He, said: {«يا أيها الذين آمنوا لم تقولون ما لا تفعلون * كبر مقتا عند الله أن تقولوا ما لا تفعلون»} ("O you who believe, why do you say what you do not do? Most hateful it is to God that you say what you do not do"). And He said: {«أتأمرون الناس بالبر وتنسون أنفسكم»} ("Do you command people to righteousness while you forget yourselves?"). And He said: {«ومن الناس من يعجبك قوله في الحياة الدنيا ويشهد الله على ما في قلبه وهو ألد الخصام»} ("And among people is he whose speech pleases you in the worldly life, and he calls God to witness what is in his heart, yet he is the fiercest of opponents").
20:98.topic: Al-Ghazali on the journey of the soul, death, and the Hereafter, from 'Remembrance of Death and Afterlife'

20:107.arabic: ثم انظر كيف يساقون بعد البعث والنشور حفاة عراة غرلا إلى أرض المحشر أرض بيضاء قاع صفصف لا ترى فيها عوجا ولا أمتا ولا ترى عليها ربوة يختفى الإنسان وراءها ولا وهدة ينخفض عن الأعين فيها بل هو صعيد واحد بسيط لا تفاوت فيه يساقون إليه زمرا فسبحان من جمع الخلائق على اختلاف أصنافهم من أقطار الأرض إذ ساقهم بالراجفة تتبعها الرادفة والراجفة هى النفخة الأولى والرادفة هى النفخة الثانية وحقيق لتلك القلوب أن تكون يومئذ واجفة ولتلك الأبصار أن تكون خاشعة قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يحشر الناس يوم القيامة على أرض بيضاء عفراء كقرص النقي ليس فيها معلم
20:107.english: Know, O seeker, that after the resurrection and the arising from the graves, consider how they are driven — barefoot, naked, uncircumcised — to the land of the Gathering. It is a white land, a level plain, smooth and even, wherein you see no crookedness nor any curve, and upon which you see no hillock behind which a person might hide, nor any hollow that would sink him from view. Rather, it is one single, simple expanse with no variation whatsoever, and to it they are driven in troops. Glory be to Him who gathered all creatures, despite their differing kinds, from the far quarters of the earth, when He drove them by the Rajīfah (the Trembling Blast) followed by the Rādifah (the Second Blast). The Rajīfah is the first trumpet-blast, and the Rādifah is the second. Rightly are those hearts on that day agitated, and rightly are those eyes humbled. The Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, said: «The people will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection upon a white, ʿafrāʾ earth, like a pure loaf of bread, upon which there is no marker for anyone.» The narrator said: "ʿAfrah is a whiteness that is not brilliant, and al-naqī is the bread purified of its bran and husk. 'No marker' means no building that conceals, and no unevenness that repels the eye."
20:107.section_title_en: The Description of the Trumpet-Blast and the Land of the Gathering
20:107.anchors:
- Root: صور (ṣ-w-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root denotes form/shape; the "trumpet" (ṣūr) is that which shapes and transforms states through its blast.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance — the ṣūr is the instrument of cosmic transformation, linking the two blasts (rajīfah and rādifah) to the divine command of resurrection.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — a horn/trumpet; metaphorical — the blast as the signal of universal upheaval, not a mere physical sound.
- Root: حشر (ḥ-sh-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to gather, drive, or assemble a multitude forcibly.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theologically, ḥashr is the divine gathering of all creatures to the plain of reckoning, distinct from ordinary aggregation by its comprehensiveness and compulsion.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — herding animals; metaphorical — the compelled assembly of humanity before God, stripped of all worldly coverings.
- Root: عفر (ʿ-f-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: ʿafrāʾ denotes a whitish hue tinged with redness or dust-color; the "white" earth of the gathering is not pure white but a dusty, pale expanse.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The earth's transformation (tabdīl al-arḍ) signifies a new creation, not mere alteration of accidents.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — color description; metaphorical — the earth's purity from sin and bloodshed, as the narrator glosses ʿafrāʾ as "whiteness not brilliant."
- Sibawayh Rule: Interposition of descriptive clauses (ṣifah) between subject and predicate — the extended adjectival chains (e.g., "arḍ bayḍāʾ qāʿ ṣafṣaf...") delay the main verb to build cumulative, awe-inducing imagery, permissible due to the semantic completeness of each descriptive unit.
20:107.topic: Al-Ghazali on the journey of the soul, death, and the Hereafter, from 'Remembrance of Death and Afterlife'

20:109.arabic: يملكون الشفاعة إلا من أذن له الرحمن ورضى له قولا فتأمل في طول هذا اليوم وشدة الانتظار فيه حتى يخف عليك انتظار الصبر عن المعاصى فى عمرك المختصر واعلم أن من طال انتظاره فى الدنيا للموت لشدة مقاساته للصبر عن الشهوات فإنه يقصر انتظاره فى ذلك اليوم خاصة قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لما سئل عن طول ذلك اليوم فقال والذي نفسي بيده إنه ليخفف على المؤمن حتى يكون أهون عليه من الصلاة المكتوبة يصليها فى الدنيا (2) فاجتهد أن تكون من أولئك المؤمنين فما دام يبقى لك نفس من عمرك فالأمر إليك والاستعداد ب
20:109.english: It is a Day on which all creatures stand, their eyes fixed in a stare, their hearts split asunder. They are not spoken to, and no one looks into their affairs. They stand for three hundred years, eating not therein a single eating, drinking not therein a single drink, and finding not therein the breath of any breeze. Ka'b and Qatadah said: "The Day when mankind shall stand before the Lord of the Worlds" {«يوم يقوم الناس لرب العالمين»} (Al-Mutaffifin: 6) — they stand for the measure of three hundred years. Nay — 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr said: The Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, recited this verse, then said: "How will it be with you when Allah gathers you as arrows are gathered in a quiver, for fifty thousand years, and He does not look upon you?" (1) And Al-Hasan said: What is your opinion of a Day on which they stand upon their feet for the measure of fifty thousand years, eating not therein a single eating, drinking not therein a single drink — until, when their necks are severed by thirst and their innards are burnt by hunger, they are turned away to the Fire and given to drink from a boiling spring whose heat has reached its peak and whose scorching blast has grown fierce. Then when the utmost exhaustion reaches them, beyond what they have strength to bear, they speak one to another, seeking one who is honored before his Lord to intercede on their behalf. They cling to no prophet but that he repels them, saying: "Leave me, leave me — my own self, my own self; my own affair has occupied me from the affair of another." And each one excuses himself by the severity of God's wrath, saying: "Today our Lord has become wrathful with a wrath the like of which He has never been wrathful before, nor will He be wrathful with its like after." — until our Prophet, peace be upon him, intercedes for those to whom permission is granted therein; they possess not intercession save for him whom the Merciful has permitted and with whose word He is pleased {«لا يملكون الشفاعة إلا من أذن له الرحمن ورضي له قولا»} (Ta-Ha: 109).
20:109.section_title_en: The Description of the Length of the Day of Resurrection
20:109.anchors:
- Root: يوم (yawm)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning is the period from sunrise to sunset; extended to any span of time, however long.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "اليوم يعبر به عن وقت طلوع الشمس إلى غروبها. وقد يعبر به عن مدة من الزمان أي مدة كانت" — the term denotes any duration whatsoever, as in {«وذكرهم بأيام الله»} (Ibrahim: 5), where "days" are attributed to God as an honorific for His mighty acts.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah) usage refers to the solar day; metaphorical (Majaz) usage extends to "days of the Arabs" meaning their battles and epochal events. Here, the "day" of fifty thousand years is a real duration, not a metaphor.
- Root: نفس (nafs)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The self, soul, or spirit; also breath.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "نفسه: ذاته" — God's "Self" is His very Essence. In the prophetic oath "والذي نفسي بيده" (By Him in Whose hand is my soul), the soul is the living self.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the soul/spirit; metaphorical: "دفق نفسه" (he poured out his soul = his blood). The Prophet's cry "نفسي نفسي" (myself, myself) is literal self-reference — each prophet is absorbed in his own deliverance.
- Root: اكل (akl)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Eating, consuming food.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الأكل: تناول المطعم" — partaking of nourishment; metaphorically extended to fire consuming fuel.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: eating; metaphorical: "أكل مالي وشربه" (he ate my wealth and drank it = he fed it to people). The negation "لا يأكلون فيه أكلة" (they eat not therein a single eating) is literal — total deprivation of food.
- Root: شرب (sharb)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Drinking; also a share or portion.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الشرب: تناول كل مائع" — partaking of any liquid; "الشرب: النصيب منه" — the share of it.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: drinking water, milk, medicine; metaphorical: "أشرب الثوب حمرة" (the garment was saturated with redness). "ولا يشربون فيه شربة" (nor drink therein a single drink) is literal — total deprivation of drink.
- Sibawayh Rule: Interposition of the subject between the conditional and its apodosis; also the construction of "حتى إذا" (until when) marking a temporal sequence where the subordinate clause (انقطعت أعناقهم) is completed before the main clause (انصرف بهم) — a periodic structure requiring careful temporal parsing.

20:124.arabic: جدير بأن يكون هو المراد بقوله تعالى {ومن أعرض عن ذكري فإن له معيشة ضنكا ونحشره يوم القيامة أعمى} وبقوله عز وجل {كذلك أتتك آياتنا فنسيتها وكذلك اليوم تنسى} أي تركتها ولم تنظر إليها ولم تعبأ بها فإن المقصر في الأمر يقال إنه نسي الأمر وتلاوة القرآن حق تلاوته هو أن يشترك فيه اللسان والعقل والقلب فحظ اللسان تصحيح الحروف بالترتيل وحظ العقل تفسير المعاني وحظ القلب الاتعاظ والتأثر بالانزجار والائتمار فاللسان يرتل والعقل يترجم والقلب يتعظ التاسع الترقي وأعني به أن يترقى إلى أن يسمع الكلام من الله عز وجل لا من نفسه فد
20:124.english: For this reason, Yūsuf ibn Asbāṭ said: "I intend to recite the Qur'an, but when I recall what is in it, I fear abhorrence (al-maqt), so I turn instead to glorification (al-tasbīḥ) and seeking forgiveness (al-istighfār)."
20:124.section_title_en: ** The Revival of the Religious Sciences — Section 231: On the Inward Conditions of Qur'anic Recitation (Continued)
20:124.anchors:
**
- Root: وجل (w-j-l)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الوجل: استشعار الخوف" — the stirring of fear/apprehension within
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الوجل: استشعار الخوف. يقال: وجل يوجل وجلا، فهو وجل. قال تعالى: {إنما المؤمنون الذين إذا ذكر الله وجلت قلوبهم}" — the theological state of the heart's trembling upon remembrance of God
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): "رجل وجل، وقوم وجال، وقد وجل وجلا" — the physical/emotional state of fear. Metaphorical (Majaz): The heart's trembling as the seat of spiritual perception
- Root: قلب (q-l-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "قلب الشيء: تصريفه وصرفه عن وجه إلى وجه" — turning and transforming
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "قلب الشيء: تصريفه وصرفه عن وجه إلى وجه، كقلب الثوب، وقلب الإنسان" — the heart as that which is constantly turning/transforming between states
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "قلب الشيء قلبا: حوله عن وجهه" — physical turning. Metaphorical: "قلب المعلم الصبيان: صرفهم إلى بيوتهم" — the heart's turning toward or away from spiritual realities
- Root: نفس (n-f-s)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The self, soul, spirit — that which is breathed
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "النفس: الروح" — the soul as the animating principle; also the self as the locus of blameworthy attributes
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "شيء نفيس ومنفس" — preciousness. Metaphorical: "دفق نفسه أي دمه" — the self as that which must be transcended in spiritual realization
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد (Restriction & Focused Predication) — governing the precise delimitation of spiritual states (أحوال) and their hierarchical gradation (درجات)

20:130.arabic: {إن ناشئة الليل هي أشد وطأ وأقوم قيلا} وقال تعالى {ومن آناء الليل فسبح وأطراف النهار لعلك ترضى} وقال عز وجل {وأقم الصلاة طرفي النهار وزلفا من الليل أن الحسنات يذهبن السيئات} ثم انظر كيف وصف الفائزين من عباده وبماذا وصفهم فقال تعالى {أم من هو قانت}
20:130.english: This is what has been unveiled to those who gaze with the light of inner vision. But if you are not among its people, then look to the address of God Most High to His Messenger and derive it by the light of faith. For God Most High said to the nearest of His servants to Him and the highest of them in rank before Him: {«Indeed, for you in the day is prolonged occupation and [in the night] long travail. And remember the name of your Lord and devote yourself to Him with [complete] devotion»} (73:7-8). And He said Most High: {«And remember the name of your Lord [in prayer] morning and evening. And from [part of] the night, prostrate to Him and exalt Him a long [part of the] night»} (76:25-26). And He said Most High: {«And exalt [Allah] with praise of your Lord before the rising of the sun and before its setting, and during periods of the night [exalt Him] and after the [performance of] prostrations»} (50:39-40). And He said, Glorified be He: {«And exalt [Allah] with praise of your Lord when you arise. And during part of the night exalt Him and after the stars»} (52:48-49). And He said Most High: {«Indeed, the rising by night is more potent for directing the soul and more suitable for the recitation [of the Qur'an]»} (73:6). And He said Most High: {«And from [part of] the night, exalt Him and after the setting of the stars»} (52:49). And He said Most High: {«And during parts of the night, exalt Him and at the ends of the day, that you may be satisfied»} (20:130). And He said, Mighty and Majestic: {«And establish prayer at the two ends of the day and at the approach of the night. Indeed, good deeds do away with misdeeds»} (11:114).
20:130.section_title_en: The Virtue of the Liturgies of Remembrance (Awrād) and the Elucidation That Perseverance Upon Them Is the Path to God Most High
20:130.anchors:
- Root: ورد (w-r-d)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The root denotes arriving at water, approaching a watering-place; the awrād (pl. of wird) are the appointed portions of devotional recitation assigned to fixed times, as one approaches the fountain of divine mercy.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The wird is the allocated share of worship apportioned to a specific hour; its theological nuance is the systematic distribution of remembrance (dhikr) and reflection (fikr) across the昼夜 cycle to combat the soul's innate restlessness.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the portion of water one drinks. Metaphorical: the fixed liturgical portion one "drinks" from the fountain of gnosis—the shift from physical quenching to spiritual saturation.
- Root: لطف (l-ṭ-f)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Gentleness, subtlety, graciousness; to treat with kindness and refinement.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The divine subtlety (al-luṭf) by which God gently draws His servant; here, the soul's need for gentle management (talṭīf) through variety in worship, lest it weary.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical gentleness of touch. Metaphorical: the strategic, compassionate variation of devotional acts to sustain the soul's momentum—a haqīqah of spiritual governance.
- Root: سأم (s-'-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Weariness, boredom, satiety that breeds aversion; the soul's constitutional fatigue with a single monotonous mode.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The psychological impediment to perseverance; overcome only by the divine mercy of variety, as the Prophet said: «إن الله لا يمل حتى تملوا» — God does not weary, but He has ordained that you may.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the nausea of over-satiation. Metaphorical: the spiritual listlessness that overtakes the heart when devotion becomes mechanical—requiring the "turn" (tanqul) between genres of worship.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب التنويع والتقسيم (The Chapter of Division and Distribution) — The periodic structure here distributes predicates across multiple conditional clauses (fa-in... fa-in...), each governing a distinct outcome, requiring the translator to preserve the balanced, correlative syntax of proportional reward.
