20:130.arabic: تمسون وحين تصبحون} وبقوله تعالى فسبح بحمد ربك قبل طلوع الشمس وقبل غروبها وقوله عز وجل {ومن آناء الليل فسبح وأطراف النهار لعلك ترضى} وقوله تعالى {واذكر اسم ربك بكرة وأصيلا} فأما ترتيبه فليأخذ من وقت انتباهه من النوم فإذا انتبه فينبغي أن يبتدىء بذكر الله تعالى فيقول الحمد لله الذي أحيانا بعد ما أماتنا وإليه النشور إلى آخر الأدعية والآيات التي ذكرناها في دعاء الاستيقاظ من كتاب الدعوات وليلبس ثوبه وهو في الدعاء وينوي به ستر عورته امتثالا لأمر الله تعالى واستعانة به على عبادته من غير قصد رياء ولا رعونة
20:130.english: {«آناء الليل ساجدا وقائما يحذر الآخرة ويرجو رحمة ربه قل هل يستوي الذين يعلمون والذين لا يعلمون»} — "During the hours of the night, prostrating and standing, fearing the Hereafter and hoping for the mercy of his Lord. Say: Are those who know equal to those who do not know?" (Q. 39:9). And God Most High said: {«تتجافى جنوبهم عن المضاجع يدعون ربهم خوفا وطمعا»} — "Their sides forsake their beds, calling upon their Lord in fear and hope" (Q. 32:16). And God, Mighty and Majestic, said: {«والذين يبيتون لربهم سجدا وقياما»} — "And those who pass the night prostrating and standing before their Lord" (Q. 25:64). And God, Mighty and Majestic, said: {«كانوا قليلا من الليل ما يهجعون وبالأسحار هم يستغفرون»} — "They used to sleep but little of the night, and in the dawn-hours they would seek forgiveness" (Q. 51:17-18). And God, Mighty and Majestic, said: {«فسبحان الله حين تمسون وحين تصبحون»} — "So glory be to God when you enter the evening and when you enter the morning" (Q. 30:17). And God Most High said: {«ولا تطرد الذين يدعون ربهم بالغداة والعشي يريدون وجهه»} — "And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord morning and evening, desiring His Face" (Q. 6:52). All of this makes clear to you that the path to God Most High is the watchfulness over the times (murāqabat al-awqāt) and the cultivation of them with the appointed devotions (al-awrād) in a perpetual manner.
20:130.section_title_en: The Revival of the Religious Sciences — Section 258: The Virtues of the Watches (Awrād) and Their Ordering
20:130.anchors:
- Root: ورد (w-r-d)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning is "to arrive at water" — the quenching of thirst at a watering place; al-Wird (pl. Awrād) denotes a set portion or appointed round of devotional recitation, by extension from the regular "arrival" at a source.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-Wurūd is originally "the intending of water," then used for other things. The theological nuance: the awrād are the appointed "watering places" of the soul — fixed times at which the servant presents himself before God to drink from the fountain of remembrance (dhikr).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): "warda al-mā'a" — to arrive at water. Metaphorical (Majāz): "warada ʿalayhi amrun lam yuṭiqhu" — an affair he could not bear arrived upon him; "waradat-hu al-ḥummā" — fever came upon him. Here, the awrād are the appointed times that "come upon" the servant, demanding their due of devotion.
- Root: طلع (ṭ-l-ʿ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To rise, to appear above the horizon (of the sun); to ascend; to come upon suddenly.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Ṭalaʿa al-shams ṭulūʿan wa-maṭlaʿan" — the sun rose. From this is borrowed: "ṭalaʿa ʿalaynā fulān" — so-and-so came upon us. The maṭlaʿ is the place of rising.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "ṭalaʿat al-shams" — the sun rose. Metaphorical: "ṭalaʿa ʿalaynā fulān" — he descended upon us suddenly. The "rising of the sun" is the boundary-marker of the first watch.
- Root: ليل (l-y-l)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The night — from the time of sunset to sunrise; its root suggests "enveloping" and "concealing."
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The night (al-layl) and the day (al-nahār) are two signs (āyatān) of God; the night is for stillness and the day for seeking provision.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the period of darkness. Metaphorical: "layl al-hamm" — the night of anxiety (a dark affair). The night is divided into watches for the one who stands in prayer.
- Sibawayh Rule: Bāb al-ḥaṣr wa-al-taqyīd bi-innamā (Restriction and Focused Predication) — The particle innamā restricts the predicate to the subject alone, negating all else. Applied here: "the purpose of the sun and moon's course is not for worldly matters, but only (innamā) for knowing the measures of the times."
20:130.topic: Al-Ghazali on constant remembrance of God and contemplative invocations, from 'Remembrance of Death and Afterlife'

20:130.arabic: فافعلوا ثم قرأ {وسبح بحمد ربك قبل طلوع الشمس وقبل غروبها} (1) وهو مخرج في الصحيحين وروى مسلم في الصحيح عن صهيب قال قرأ رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قوله تعالى للذين أحسنوا الحسنى وزيادة {قال} إذا دخل أهل الجنة الجنة وأهل النار النار نادى مناد يا أهل الجنة إن لكم عند الله موعدا يريد أن ينجزكموه قالوا ما هذا الموعد ألم يثقل موازيننا ويبيض وجوهنا ويدخلنا الجنة ويجرنا من النار قال فيرفع الحجاب وينظرون إلى وجه الله عز وجل فما أعطوا شيئا أحب إليهم من النظر إليه (2) وقد روى حديث الرؤيا جماعة من الصحابة وهذه
20:130.english: And Mujāhid said: "The lowest of the people of Paradise in station is one who travels through his dominion for a thousand years, seeing its farthest as he sees its nearest. And the highest of them is the one who gazes upon his Lord morning and evening." And Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib said: "There is none among the people of Paradise except that in his hand are three bracelets: a bracelet of gold, a bracelet of pearl, and a bracelet of silver."
20:130.section_title_en: The Vision of Allah and the Gaze Upon His Face — The Supreme Bliss of the Hereafter
20:130.anchors:
- Root: حسن (ḥ-s-n)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of beauty, goodness, and excellence in form and act.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الحسنى" denotes the superlative good (al-ḥusnā), and "زيادة" (increase) is the added bounty beyond merit — a theological term for the beatific vision.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) for moral beauty; metaphorical (majāz) elevation when applied to divine reward, where "increase" transcends all corporeal delights.
- Root: رءي (r-'-y)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Visual perception (ru'yā) and sight (naẓar), both sensory and intellectual.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In Kalam, "ru'yat Allāh" is the vision of the divine essence — an immaterial perception granted to the blessed, not a corporeal sight of a spatial object.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal for physical sight; metaphorical transfer (naql) when applied to God, signifying direct, unveiled apprehension of His glory.
- Root: نعم (n-'-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "النعمة" is the state of well-being; "النعمى" is the superlative felicity.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "النعمة" as the good state (ḥālah ḥasanah), and "النعمى" as the ultimate bliss — here contrasted with the lesser delights of Paradise.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal for sensory comfort; metaphorical for the spiritual joy of divine proximity, which surpasses all bodily pleasures.
- Root: اهل ('-h-l)
  * Lisan / Ayn: People of a household or place; "أهل الجنة" — the inhabitants of Paradise.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "أهل الرجل" — those united by kinship, religion, or abode; here, the denizens of the Garden as a community of the blessed.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal for residents; metaphorical extension to those who merit a station by virtue of their deeds.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — Used in the closing exhortation to restrict the servant's aspiration solely to the vision of the Lord, excluding all lesser aims.
20:130.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'Remembrance of Death and Afterlife'

21:1.arabic: تعالى اقترب للناس حسابهم وهم في غفلة معرضون ما يأتيهم من ذكر من ربهم محدث إلا استمعوه وهم يلعبون لاهية قلوبهم ويحك يا نفس إن كانت جراءتك على معصية الله لاعتقادك أن الله لا يراك فما أعظم كفرك وإن كان مع علمك باطلاعه عليك فما أشد وقاحتك وأقل حياءك ويحك يا نفس لو واجهك عبد من عبيدك بل أخ من إخوانك بما تكرهينه كيف كان غضبك عليه ومقتك له فبأي جسارة تتعرضين لمقت الله وغضبه وشديد عقابه أفتظنين أنك تطيقين عذابه هيهات هيهات جربي نفسك إن ألهاك البطر عن أليم عذابه فاحتبسي ساعة في الشمس أو في بيت الحمام أو قربي أصبعك من النار ليتبين قدر طاقتك أمتغترين بكرم الله وفضله واستغنائه عن طاعتك وعبادتك فما لك لا تعولين على كرم الله تعالى في مهمات دنياك فإذا قصدك عدو فلم تستنبطين الحيل في دفعه ولا تكلينه إلى كرم الله تعالى وإذا أرهقتك حاجة إلى شهوة من شهوات الدنيا مما لا ينقضي إلا بالدينار والدرهم فما لك تنزعين الروح في طلبها وتحصيلها من وجوه الحيل فلا تعولين على كرم الله تعالى حتى يعثر بك على كنز أو يسخر عبدا من عبيده فيحمل إليك حاجتك من غير سعي منك ولا طلب أفتحسبين أن الله كريم في الآخرة دون الدنيا وقد عرفت أن سنة الله لا تبديل لها وأن رب الآخرة والدنيا واحد وأن ليس للإنسان إلا ما سعى ويحك يا نفس ما أعجب نفاقك ودواعيك الباطلة فإنك تدعين الإيمان بلسانك وأثر النفاق ظاهر عليك ألم يقل لك سيدك ومولاك وما من دابة في الأرض إلا على الله رزقها وقال في أمر الآخرة وأن ليس للإنسان إلا ما سعى فقد تكفل لك بأمر الدنيا خاصة وصرفك عن السعى فيها فكذبته بأفعالك وأصبحت تتكالبين على طلبها تكالب المدهوش المستهتر ووكل أمر الآخرة إلى سعيك فأعرضت عنها إعراض المغرور المستحقر ما هذا من علامات الإيمان لو كان الإيمان باللسان فلم كان المنافقون في الدرك الأسفل من النار ويحك يا نفس كأنك لا تؤمنين بيوم الحساب وتظنين أنك إذا مت انفلت وتخلصت وهيهات أتحسبين أنك تتركين سدى ألم تكونى نطفة من مني يمنى ثم كنت علقة فخلق فسوى أليس ذلك بقادر على أن يحيى الموتى فإن كان هذا من إضمارك فما أكفرك وأجهلك أما تتفكرين أنه مماذا خلقك من نطفة خلقك فقدرك ثم السبيل يسرك ثم أماتك فأقبرك أفتكذبينه في قوله ثم إذا شاء أنشرك فإن لم تكونى مكذبة فما لك لا تأخذين حذرك ولو أن يهوديا أخبرك في ألذ أطعمتك بأنه يضرك في مرضك لصبرت عنه وتركته وجاهدت نفسك فيه أفكان قول الأنبياء المؤيدين بالمعجزات وقول الله تعالى في كتبه المنزلة أقل عندك تأثيرا من قول يهودى يخبرك عن حدس وتخمين وظن مع نقصان عقل وقصور علم والعجب أنه لو أخبرك طفل بأن في ثوبك عقربا لرميت ثوبك في الحال من غير مطالبة له بدليل وبرهان أفكان قول الأنبياء والعلماء والحكماء وكافة
21:1.english: ...and intelligence and acumen, while you are the most stupid and foolish of people? Do you not recognize what lies before you of the Garden and the Fire, and that you are hastening to one of the two imminently? So why do you rejoice and laugh and occupy yourself with frivolity while you are being sought for this tremendous calamity? Perhaps today you will be snatched away, or tomorrow. I see that you regard death as distant, but God regards it as near. Do you not know that everything that is coming is near, and that the distant is only that which is not coming? Do you not know that death comes suddenly, without a prior messenger, without prior appointment or covenant? It does not come in one thing rather than another, nor in winter rather than summer, nor in summer rather than winter, nor in day rather than night, nor in night rather than day. It does not come in youth rather than old age, nor in old age rather than youth. Rather, every single breath could be the moment of sudden death. And if death does not come suddenly, then illness comes suddenly, and then leads to death. So why do you not prepare for death, when it is nearer to you than anything near? Do you not ponder the saying of God Most High: {«اقترب للناس حسابهم وهم في غفلة معرضون * ما يأتيهم من ذكر من ربهم محدث إلا استمعوه وهم يلعبون * لاهية قلوبهم»} (The reckoning for mankind has drawn near, while they turn away in heedlessness. No fresh reminder comes to them from their Lord but they listen to it while they play—their hearts distracted). Woe to you, O soul! If your audacity toward disobeying God stems from your belief that God does not see you, then how immense is your disbelief! And if it is despite your knowledge of His awareness of you, then how severe is your shamelessness and how little your modesty! Woe to you, O soul! If a slave of your slaves—nay, a brother among your brothers—were to confront you with what you detest, how would your anger and hatred toward him be? So with what audacity do you expose yourself to God's hatred, His wrath, and His severe punishment? Do you think you can endure His chastisement? Far be it, far be it! Test yourself—if heedless pride has distracted you from His painful punishment, then restrain yourself for an hour in the sun, or in the bathhouse, or bring your finger near the fire, so that your capacity may become clear to you. Are you deluded by God's generosity, His bounty, and His independence from your obedience and worship? Then why do you not rely on God's generosity in the important matters of your worldly life? When an enemy approaches you, why do you devise stratagems to repel him, rather than entrusting him to God's generosity? And when you are pressed by a need for one of the worldly desires that cannot be fulfilled except through dinar and dirham, why do you strain your very soul in seeking and procuring it through various contrivances, without relying on God's generosity—so that He might lead you to a treasure, or subjugate one of His slaves to carry your need to you without any effort or seeking on your part? Do you suppose that God is generous in the Hereafter but not in this world, when you already know that the sunnah of God admits no change, and that the Lord of the Hereafter and this world is One, and that {«ليس للإنسان إلا ما سعى»} (man shall have nothing but what he strives for)?
21:1.section_title_en: Section 1251 — The Admonition of the Soul Concerning the Nearness of Death and the Duplicity of False Hopes
21:1.anchors:
- Root: قرب (q-r-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Proximity in place, time, or rank; nearness of relation or degree.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Used for spatial, temporal, and relational nearness; here, divine nearness of death and the Hour—a metaphysical proximity, not measurable distance.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) for physical closeness; metaphorical (majāz) for what is inevitable and imminent—"كل ما هو آت قريب" (all that is coming is near).
- Root: موت (m-w-t)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Death as the cessation of animal life; also used metaphorically for lifelessness.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Death as transition, not annihilation; linked to resurrection (baʿth) and divine power.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal for bodily death; metaphorical for the "death" of heedlessness or the dead heart.
- Root: نفس (n-f-s)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The self, soul, or spirit; that which desires and is accountable.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The soul as the locus of blameworthy traits (al-nafs al-ammārah) versus the rational, discerning faculty; here, self-address in reproach.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal for the animate self; metaphorical for the inner voice of conscience rebuking the lower soul.
- Root: طلب (ṭ-l-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Seeking, pursuing, demanding.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The active search for something, whether physical or conceptual; here, the soul's frantic pursuit of worldly desires versus its neglect of what is truly sought from it.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal for seeking provisions; metaphorical for the soul being "sought" by death—"وأنت مطلوبة" (you are being sought).
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The rhetorical separation between the preposition and its object to emphasize urgency, as in "على القرب" and "أقرب إليك من كل قريب," where proximity is stressed through syntactic placement.
21:1.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Remembrance of Death and Afterlife'

21:1.arabic: المبين ويخبرنا بهذه الصفات من نعوت يوم الدين ثم يعرفنا غفلتنا ويقول اقترب الناس حسابهم وهم في غفلة معرضون ما يأتيهم من ذكر من ربهم محدث إلا استمعوه وهم يلعبون لاهية قلوبهم ثم يعرفنا قرب القيامة فيقول اقتربت الساعة وانشق القمر إنهم يرونه بعيدا ونراه قريبا وما يدريك لعل الساعة تكون قريبا ثم يكون أحسن أحوالنا أن نتخذ دراسة هذا القرآن عملا فلا نتدبر معانيه ولا ننظر في كثرة أوصاف هذا اليوم وأساميه ولا نستعد للتخلص من دواهيه فنعوذ بالله من هذه الغفلة إن لم يداركنا الله بواسع رحمته
21:1.english: So prepare yourself, O wretched one, for this Day of immense magnitude, of prolonged duration, of overwhelming dominion, whose appointed time is near — a Day when you shall see the heaven split asunder, and the stars scattered in its terror, and the shining planets extinguished, and the sun folded up, and the mountains set in motion, and the pregnant camels neglected, and the wild beasts gathered together, and the seas set ablaze, and the souls paired with their bodies, and the Hellfire ignited, and Paradise brought near, and the mountains pulverized, and the earth stretched out — a Day when you shall see the earth shaken with its quaking, and the earth casts forth its burdens. On that Day shall people issue forth in scattered groups to be shown their deeds — a Day when the earth and the mountains are lifted and crushed with a single crushing. Then on that Day the Imminent Event shall come to pass, and the heaven shall split open, for on that Day it shall be frail, and the angels shall be at its edges, and eight shall bear the Throne of your Lord above them on that Day. On that Day you shall be presented — no secret of yours shall remain hidden. A Day when the mountains shall move and you shall see the earth laid bare — a Day when the earth shall be shaken with a violent shaking, and the mountains crumbled to dust, becoming scattered particles — a Day when people shall be like scattered moths, and the mountains like carded wool — a Day when every nursing mother shall forget what she nursed, and every pregnant female shall cast down her burden, and you shall see people drunk, yet they are not drunk, but the chastisement of God is severe — a Day when the earth shall be changed to other than this earth, and the heavens, and they shall appear before God, the One, the All-Compelling — a Day when the mountains shall be blown away as dust, leaving a level, bare plain, wherein you see no crookedness nor curve — a Day when you see the mountains and suppose them solid, yet they pass by like the passing of clouds — a Day when the heaven shall split open and become rosy like molten oil. Then on that Day no human nor jinn shall be asked about his sin. A Day when the disobedient shall be prevented from speech, and shall not be asked about their crimes, but shall be seized by their forelocks and their feet — a Day when every soul shall find what it did of good brought forth present, and what it did of evil, wishing that between it and that evil there were a far distance — a Day when every soul shall know what it has sent ahead, and shall witness what it has forwarded and what it has left behind — a Day when tongues shall be struck mute and the bodily members shall speak — a Day whose mention turned the hair of the Master of the Messengers white, when al-Ṣiddīq (may God be pleased with him) said to him: "I see that you have turned white-haired, O Messenger of God." He said: "Sūrat Hūd and its sisters have made me white-haired" — namely, al-Wāqiʿah, al-Mursalāt, ʿAmma Yatasāʾalūn, and Idhā al-Shamsu Kuwwirat.
21:1.section_title_en: The Names and Attributes of the Day of Resurrection — An Exhortation to the Negligent
21:1.anchors:
- Root: يوم (yawm)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "اليوم: وقت طلوع الشمس إلى غروبها، وقد يعبر به عن مدة من الزمان أي مدة كانت" — the day as a temporal span, extended metaphorically to any epoch or era.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "اليوم يعبر به عن وقت طلوع الشمس إلى غروبها. وقد يعبر به عن مدة من الزمان أي مدة كانت" — theological usage denotes the appointed time of reckoning, magnified by divine attribution (أيام الله).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): a measured solar period. Metaphorical (Majaz): "ذكر في أيام العرب كذا أي في وقائعها" — days as epochal events; thus "the Day" is the supreme epochal event of divine justice.
- Root: نفس (nafs)
  * Lisan / Ayn: النفس: الروح والذات — the self, soul, or very essence.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "النفس: الروح... وقوله: ويحذركم الله نفسه فنفسه: ذاته" — nafs as the innermost reality of a being; in the eschatological context, souls are "paired" (زوجت) with bodies for judgment.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the soul as life-principle. Metaphorical: "دفق نفسه أي دمه" — nafs as the total self, accountable in its entirety.
- Root: ارض (arḍ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: الأرض: الجرم المقابل للسماء — the earth as the corporeal substratum beneath the heavens.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الأرض: الجرم المقابل للسماء... ويعبر بها عن أسفل الشيء" — the earth as the lowest register of creation, subject to total transformation on that Day.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the physical earth. Metaphorical: "تأرض فلان: لزم الأرض" — to cling low; on that Day the earth itself is leveled, flattened, and replaced.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد (Restriction & Focused Predication) — The repeated "يوم" clauses function as temporal restrictors (ẓurūf) binding each predicate to that single, all-encompassing moment; the accumulation of names (أسامي) serves not as mere repetition but as focused predication upon the multifarious realities of a single event.
21:1.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Remembrance of Death and Afterlife'

21:1.arabic: قوله عز وجل وهم في غفلة معرضون وفي قوله فأعرض عمن تولى عن ذكرنا ولم يرد إلا الحياة الدنيا وفي قوله تعالى ومن لم يتب فأولئك هم الظالمون إلى غير ذلك من الآيات وكان داخلا في معنى قوله عز وجل ومنهم أميون لا يعلمون الكتاب إلا أماني يعني التلاوة المجردة وقوله عز وجل وكأين من آية في السموات والأرض يمرون عليها وهم عنها معرضون لأن القرآن هو المبين لتلك الآيات في السموات والأرض ومهما تجاوزها ولم يتأثر بها كان معرضا عنها ولذلك قيل إن من لم يكن متصفا بأخلاق القرآن فإذا قرأ القرآن ناداه
21:1.english: And at the mention of God, His attributes, and His names, he bows low in humility before His majesty and in apprehension of His greatness. And at the mention of the disbelievers' sayings — those things impossible for God, Mighty and Majestic, such as their attributing to Him a son or a consort — he lowers his voice and inwardly recoils in shame at the ugliness of their speech. And at the description of Paradise, his innermost being surges forth with longing for it. And at the description of the Fire, his limbs tremble in fear of it. For when the Messenger of God, peace be upon him, said to Ibn Mas'ud, "Recite to me," he said: "I began reciting Surah al-Nisa'. When I reached {فكيف إذا جئنا من كل أمة بشهيد وجئنا بك على هؤلاء شهيدا} [How then shall it be when We bring from every nation a witness, and We bring you as a witness against these?] (4:41), I saw his two eyes overflowing with tears. He then said to me: 'That is enough for you now.'" And this was because the witnessing of that very state had wholly overwhelmed his heart.
21:1.section_title_en: The States of the Heart During Qur'anic Recitation — The Condition of the True Recieter
21:1.anchors:
- Root: وجل (w-j-l)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root meaning of trembling fear, trepidation of the heart
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الوجل: استشعار الخوف" — the inward apprehension of fear; cited in {إنما المؤمنون الذين إذا ذكر الله وجلت قلوبهم}
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): "رجل وجل، وقوم وجال" — a man fearful, a people fearful; the state of the heart's trembling before divine majesty
- Root: وصف (w-ṣ-f)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Describing a thing by its attributes and qualities
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الوصف: ذكر الشيء بحليته ونعته" — description is the mention of a thing by its adornment and attribute; may be true or false
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal vs Metaphorical: "وجهها يصف الحسن" — metaphorical usage where the face itself "describes" beauty; likewise, the tongue may "describe" falsehood, as in {ولا تقولوا لما تصف ألسنتكم الكذب}
- Root: وفي (w-f-y)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Completeness, fulfillment, reaching full measure
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الوافي: الذي بلغ التمام" — that which attains completion; "أوفى: إذا تمم العهد ولم ينقض حفظه" — fulfilled the covenant without breach
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "درهم واف" — a full-weight dirham; Metaphorical: "أوفى على المائة إذا زاد عليها" — surpassed the hundred
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The separation between the governing preposition and its object by intervening clauses, as in "فلما بلغت {فكيف إذا جئنا...}" where the temporal clause governs the narrative sequence
21:1.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Etiquette of Quran Recitation'

21:19.arabic: وهو أحد والآصال التي ذكرها الله تعالى إذ قال ولله يسجد من في السموات والأرض طوعا وكرها وظلالهم بالغدو والآصال وإذا سجد لله عز وجل الجمادات فكيف يجوز أن يغفل العبد العاقل عن أنواع العبادات الورد السادس إذا دخل وقت العصر دخل وقت الورد السادس وهو الذي أقسم الله تعالى به فقال تعالى {والعصر} هذا أحد معنيي الآية وهو المراد بالآصال في أحد التفسيرين وهو العشي المذكور في قوله {وعشيا} وفي قوله {بالعشي والإشراق} وليس في هذا الورد صلاة إلا أربع ركعات بين الأذان والإقامة كما سبق في الظهر ثم يصلي الفرض ويشتغل بالأقسام الأربعة المذكورة
21:19.english: I say: And just as knowledge and remembrance are the nourishment of the heart, which can never be cut off from it, so too the measure of moderation is this; and deficiency from it may lead to the disturbance of the body — except for one who accustoms himself to wakefulness gradually, for he may train himself upon it without disturbance. And this litany (wird) is among the longest of the litanies and the most delightful for the worshippers, and it is one of the "evenings and mornings" (al-āṣāl) which God Most High mentioned when He said: {«ولله يسجد من في السموات والأرض طوعا وكرها وظلالهم بالغدو والآصال»} "And to God prostrates whoever is in the heavens and the earth, willingly or unwillingly, and their shadows, in the mornings and the evenings" (Q. 13:15). And when inanimate objects prostrate to God, Mighty and Majestic, how then can the intelligent servant be heedless of the varieties of worship?
21:19.section_title_en: The Seventh Daily Litany (Al-Wird al-Sābiʿ): The Time of Sunset — The Completion of the Day's Litanies and Self-Accounting
21:19.anchors:
- Root: ورد (warada)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The root denotes arriving at water, seeking it, and drinking from it; also the portion or share of water allotted for drinking at a specific time.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الورود أصله: قصد الماء" — the core meaning is the intentional approach to water; the litany (wird) is the appointed portion of devotional recitation, likened to the daily share of water that a person must take to sustain life.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): the act of arriving at water. Metaphorical (Majaz): "ورد علي كتاب سرني مورده" — a book arrived upon me whose arrival pleased me; likewise, the wird is the arrival of the appointed time for worship, and the soul's approach to the fountain of divine remembrance.
- Root: عصر (ʿaṣr)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The root denotes pressing, squeezing, and extracting; also the time of afternoon, so called because it is the pressing of the day's end.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The ʿaṣr is the latter part of the day; God swore by it in {«والعصر»} (Q. 103:1), indicating its great merit.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the afternoon time. Metaphorical: the pressing of one's life — as the day is pressed at its end, so the life of man is pressed at its term.
- Root: غرب (gharaba)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The root denotes disappearance, absence, and setting; the sun's setting (ghurūb) is its concealment from the eye.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The setting of the sun marks the boundary between the day's works and the night's; it is the terminus of the visible world's diurnal cycle.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the sun's descent below the horizon. Metaphorical: the setting of the sun of life — the death of man, after which there is no rising.
- Root: حاسب (ḥāsaba)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The root denotes reckoning, counting, and taking account; muḥāsabah is the mutual reckoning between two parties.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Self-accounting (muḥāsabat al-nafs) is the soul's reckoning with itself over its deeds before the Day of Reckoning, for "one who reckons himself before he is reckoned" is among the wise.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the arithmetic counting of sums. Metaphorical: the soul's audit of its own works, weighing the day's deeds against the standard of the Sacred Law.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The rule governing the separation of the prepositional phrase from its governing verb, as in the construction "فسبحان الله حين تمسون" where the adverbial clause is interposed to emphasize the temporal specification of the act of glorification.
21:19.topic: Al-Ghazali on constant remembrance of God and contemplative invocations, from 'Remembrance of Death and Afterlife'

21:19.arabic: وعبادته التي هو مشغول بها لا ينتقل إلى غيرها ولا يفتر عنها لا يستكبرون عن عبادته ولا يستحسرون يسبحون الليل والنهار لا يفترون ومفتاح مزيد الدرجات هي الصلوات قال الله عز وجل قد أفلح المؤمنون الذين هم في صلاتهم خاشعون فمدحهم بعد الإيمان بصلاة مخصوصة وهي المقرونة بالخشوع ثم ختم أوصاف المفلحين بالصلاة أيضا فقال تعالى والذين هم على صلواتهم يحافظون ثم قال تعالى في ثمرة تلك الصفات أولئك هم الوارثون الذين يرثون الفردوس هم فيها خالدون فوصفهم بالفلاح أولا وبوراثة الفردوس آخرا وما عندي أن هذرمة اللسان مع غفلة القلب تنتهي إلى هذا الحد ولذلك قال الله عز وجل في أضدادهم ما سلككم في س
21:19.english: For the friends of God (awliyāʾ Allāh) who are granted unveiling of the dominion of the heavens and the earth (malakūt al-samāwāt wa-al-arḍ) and the secrets of lordship (asrār al-rubūbiyyah) — they are unveiled only in prayer, especially in prostration (sujūd), for the servant draws near to his Lord (Mighty and Majestic) through prostration. For this reason, He said, Most High: {«And prostrate and draw near»} (Q 96:19). And the unveiling of each worshiper is only to the measure of his purity from the turbidities of this world. It varies in strength and weakness, in abundance and scarcity, and in clarity and obscurity — until some are unveiled the very thing itself (al-shayʾ bi-ʿaynihi), while others are unveiled its likeness (al-shayʾ bi-mithālihi), just as some were shown this world in the form of a corpse, and Satan in the form of a dog crouching upon it, calling people to it.
21:19.section_title_en: The Prayer of the Humble and the Unveiling of the Unveiled — Section 140
21:19.anchors:
- Root: خ ش ع (kh-sh-ʿ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of humility, submissiveness, and lowering oneself; the physical posture of one who is abased before a greater power.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In theological terms, khushūʿ is the state of the heart's stillness and trembling before divine majesty, manifesting in the body's composure during ritual prayer (ṣalāh).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) refers to the physical lowering of the gaze and voice; metaphorical (majāz) extends to the soul's inner quietude and awe before God.
- Root: ك ش ف (k-sh-f)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To remove a covering, unveil, disclose; the act of stripping away an obstruction to reveal what lies beneath.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In Quranic usage, kashf denotes divine removal of veils (kashf al-ḥijāb) — the uncovering of unseen realities (ghayb) to the heart, as in {«We have removed from you your covering»} (Q 50:22).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: uncovering a physical object; metaphorical: the disclosure of spiritual truths (mukāshafah) to the purified heart, a technical term in Sufi epistemology.
- Root: ص ل و (ṣ-l-w)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The root denotes supplication, blessing, and the act of ritual prayer; also the burning of fire (iṣlāʾ), suggesting the consuming fervor of devotion.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-ṣalāh is the act of turning toward God in worship, encompassing both the physical rites and the inner orientation of the soul; its perfection lies in the presence of the heart.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the performance of the prescribed ritual; metaphorical: the soul's "burning" with longing and its purification through the fire of sincere devotion.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — The use of restrictive particles to single out the specific quality (khushūʿ) as the defining attribute of the believers' prayer, distinguishing it from mere mechanical performance.
21:19.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Mysteries of Prayer'

21:35.arabic: وقال بعض الصوفية كنت أقرأ ليلة هذه الآية {كل نفس ذائقة الموت} فجعلت أرددها فإذا هاتف يهتف بي كم تردد هذه الآية فقد قتلت أربعة من الجن ما رفعوا رءوسهم إلى السماء منذ خلقوا وقال أبو علي المغازلي للشبلي ربما تطرق سمعي آية من كتاب الله تعالى فتجذبني إلى الإعراض عن الدنيا ثم أرجع إلى أحوالي وإلى الناس فلا أبقى على ذلك فقال ما طرق سمعك من القرآن فاجتذبك به إليه فذلك عطف منه عليك ولطف منه بك وإذا ردك إلى نفسك فهو شفقة منه عليك فإنه لا يصلح لك إلا التبري من الحول والقوة في التوجه إليه وسمع رجل من أه
21:35.english: Some of the Sufis said: "One night I was reciting this verse: {كُلُّ نَفْسٍ ذَائِقَةُ الْمَوْتِ} «Every soul shall taste death» [Q. 3:185]. I kept repeating it, and lo, a caller cried out to me: 'How long will you repeat this verse? You have killed four of the jinn who have not raised their heads to the sky since they were created.'"
21:35.section_title_en: On the Ecstatic States (Wajd) Produced by Qur'anic Recitation and the Superiority of Song (Ghinā') in Stirring the Heart
21:35.anchors:
- Root: وجد (w-j-d)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of finding, attaining, and also denoting the emotional state of ecstasy or rapture that "finds" the heart.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In the theological context, 'wajd' is the state of spiritual finding—a direct, overwhelming apprehension of divine realities that bypasses discursive reasoning.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah) usage denotes "finding" a lost object; metaphorical (Majaz) usage denotes the heart "finding" its spiritual state, leading to agitation and ecstasy.
- Root: سمع (s-m-')
  * Lisan / Ayn: The faculty of hearing; also the ear itself.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Hearing can be literal (perception of sound) or figurative (understanding, obedience, acceptance). The heart's "hearing" is a deeper comprehension.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "سمعته" (I heard him). Metaphorical: "سمع الله لمن حمده" (God answers/he accepts the one who praises Him), indicating a responsive, transformative hearing.
- Root: موت (m-w-t)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Death; the opposite of life.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Death is the cessation of the soul's governance over the body, a separation. In the spiritual context, it can be a metaphorical death to worldly desires.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical death. Metaphorical: "أحيا الله البلد الميت" (God revives the dead land), indicating spiritual revival or the death of the ego.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — Used to emphasize that the stirring of the heart is exclusively through what is appropriate to its state, as in the phrase "إنما المحرك لما في القلب ما يناسبه" (The only thing that moves what is in the heart is that which is suitable to it).
21:35.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Remembrance of Death and Afterlife'

21:38.arabic: على الكافرين غير يسير} وقال تعالى {ويقولون متى هذا الوعد إن كنتم صادقين ما ينظرون إلا صيحة واحدة تأخذهم وهم يخصمون فلا يستطيعون توصية ولا إلى أهلهم يرجعون ونفخ في الصور فإذا هم من الأجداث إلى ربهم ينسلون قالوا يا ويلنا من بعثنا من مرقدنا هذا ما وعد الرحمن وصدق المرسلون} فلو لم يكن بين يدي الموتى إلا هول تلك النفخة لكان ذلك جديرا بأن يتقى فإنها نفخة وصيحة يصعق بها من في السموات والأرض يعنى يموتون بها إلا من شاء الله وهو بعض الملائكة ولذلك قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كيف أنعم وصاحب الصور قد التقم القرن وحنى الجبهة
21:38.english: The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: Allah the Exalted said: "The son of Adam has reviled Me, and he had no right to revile Me; and he has denied Me, and he had no right to deny Me. As for his reviling of Me, it is his saying that I have a son. And as for his denial of Me, it is his saying: 'He will never bring me back as He created me at first.'" {«شتمني ابن آدم وما ينبغي له أن يشتمني وكذبني وما ينبغي له أن يكذبني...»}
21:38.section_title_en: On the Terrors of the Trumpet-Blast and the Awakening for the Resurrection
21:38.anchors:
- Root: نفخ (N-F-Kh)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To blow into a thing, to inflate; the breath of wind entering a vessel or body.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The divine act of breathing spirit into creation {«ونفخت فيه من روحي»}; here, the eschatological blast that annihilates and then revives all beings.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah) usage of blowing into the Trumpet (الصور); metaphorical extension to the "blast of spring" reviving the earth—here applied to the two cosmic blasts of death and resurrection.
- Root: صور (S-W-R)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Form, image, shape; also a horn or trumpet (the instrument of the blast).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The perceptible form of bodies and the intelligible form of souls; here, the Trumpet (الصور) as the instrument of divine command that re-forms and re-shapes creation.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the horn (القرن) held by Israfil; metaphorical: the "inclination" (صورة) of hearts toward terror and anticipation.
- Root: موت (M-W-T)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Death as the cessation of life; the state of the corpse.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Death as the separation of the soul from the body; the "first death" of the blast and the "second death" of the wicked.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical death; metaphorical: the "death" of the heart through heedlessness, and the reviving of dead lands by rain—here, the reviving of bodies by the second blast.
- Root: قبر (Q-B-R)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The grave as the abode of the dead; burial.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The grave as the intermediate state (barzakh) before resurrection; {«حتى زرتم المقابر»} as a metaphor for death.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the grave and its inhabitants; metaphorical: the "raising of the nose" (قبراه) of the proud—contrasted here with the humility of the dead rising from their graves.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — Used to emphasize that true faith is not mere verbal assent but heartfelt conviction, as in "إنما فتور البواطن... لقلة الفهم" (The languor of the inner selves is only due to the lack of understanding).
21:38.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'Remembrance of Death and Afterlife'

22:2.arabic: يوم تذهل فيه كل مرضعة عما أرضعت وتضع كل ذات حمل حملها وترى الناس سكارى وما هم بسكارى ولكن عذاب الله شديد يوم تبدل الأرض غير الأرض والسموات وبرزوا لله الواحد القهار يوم تنسف فيه الجبال نسفا فتترك قاعا صفصفا لا ترى فيها عوجا ولا أمتا يوم ترى الجبال تحسبها جامدة وهي تمر مر السحاب يوم تنشق فيه السماء فتكون وردة كالدهان فيومئذ لا يسئل عن ذنبه إنس ولا جان يوم يمنع فيه العاصى من الكلام ولا يسئل فيه عن الأجرام بل يؤخذ بالنواصى والأقدام يوم تجد كل نفس ما عملت من خير محضرا وما عملت من سوء تود لو أن بينها وبينه أمدا بعيدا يوم تعلم فيه كل نفس ما أحضرت وتشهد ما قدمت
22:2.english: So prepare yourself, O wretched one, for this Day of immense magnitude, of prolonged duration, of overwhelming dominion, whose appointed time is near — a Day when you shall see the heaven split asunder, and the stars scattered in its terror, and the shining planets extinguished, and the sun folded up, and the mountains set in motion, and the pregnant camels neglected, and the wild beasts gathered together, and the seas set ablaze, and the souls paired with their bodies, and the Hellfire ignited, and Paradise brought near, and the mountains pulverized, and the earth stretched out — a Day when you shall see the earth shaken with its quaking, and the earth casts forth its burdens. On that Day shall people issue forth in scattered groups to be shown their deeds — a Day when the earth and the mountains are lifted and crushed with a single crushing. Then on that Day the Imminent Event shall come to pass, and the heaven shall split open, for on that Day it shall be frail, and the angels shall be at its edges, and eight shall bear the Throne of your Lord above them on that Day. On that Day you shall be presented — no secret of yours shall remain hidden. A Day when the mountains shall move and you shall see the earth laid bare — a Day when the earth shall be shaken with a violent shaking, and the mountains crumbled to dust, becoming scattered particles — a Day when people shall be like scattered moths, and the mountains like carded wool — a Day when every nursing mother shall forget what she nursed, and every pregnant female shall cast down her burden, and you shall see people drunk, yet they are not drunk, but the chastisement of God is severe — a Day when the earth shall be changed to other than this earth, and the heavens, and they shall appear before God, the One, the All-Compelling — a Day when the mountains shall be blown away as dust, leaving a level, bare plain, wherein you see no crookedness nor curve — a Day when you see the mountains and suppose them solid, yet they pass by like the passing of clouds — a Day when the heaven shall split open and become rosy like molten oil. Then on that Day no human nor jinn shall be asked about his sin. A Day when the disobedient shall be prevented from speech, and shall not be asked about their crimes, but shall be seized by their forelocks and their feet — a Day when every soul shall find what it did of good brought forth present, and what it did of evil, wishing that between it and that evil there were a far distance — a Day when every soul shall know what it has sent ahead, and shall witness what it has forwarded and what it has left behind — a Day when tongues shall be struck mute and the bodily members shall speak — a Day whose mention turned the hair of the Master of the Messengers white, when al-Ṣiddīq (may God be pleased with him) said to him: "I see that you have turned white-haired, O Messenger of God." He said: "Sūrat Hūd and its sisters have made me white-haired" — namely, al-Wāqiʿah, al-Mursalāt, ʿAmma Yatasāʾalūn, and Idhā al-Shamsu Kuwwirat.
22:2.section_title_en: The Names and Attributes of the Day of Resurrection — An Exhortation to the Negligent
22:2.anchors:
- Root: يوم (yawm)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "اليوم: وقت طلوع الشمس إلى غروبها، وقد يعبر به عن مدة من الزمان أي مدة كانت" — the day as a temporal span, extended metaphorically to any epoch or era.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "اليوم يعبر به عن وقت طلوع الشمس إلى غروبها. وقد يعبر به عن مدة من الزمان أي مدة كانت" — theological usage denotes the appointed time of reckoning, magnified by divine attribution (أيام الله).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): a measured solar period. Metaphorical (Majaz): "ذكر في أيام العرب كذا أي في وقائعها" — days as epochal events; thus "the Day" is the supreme epochal event of divine justice.
- Root: نفس (nafs)
  * Lisan / Ayn: النفس: الروح والذات — the self, soul, or very essence.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "النفس: الروح... وقوله: ويحذركم الله نفسه فنفسه: ذاته" — nafs as the innermost reality of a being; in the eschatological context, souls are "paired" (زوجت) with bodies for judgment.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the soul as life-principle. Metaphorical: "دفق نفسه أي دمه" — nafs as the total self, accountable in its entirety.
- Root: ارض (arḍ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: الأرض: الجرم المقابل للسماء — the earth as the corporeal substratum beneath the heavens.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الأرض: الجرم المقابل للسماء... ويعبر بها عن أسفل الشيء" — the earth as the lowest register of creation, subject to total transformation on that Day.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the physical earth. Metaphorical: "تأرض فلان: لزم الأرض" — to cling low; on that Day the earth itself is leveled, flattened, and replaced.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد (Restriction & Focused Predication) — The repeated "يوم" clauses function as temporal restrictors (ẓurūf) binding each predicate to that single, all-encompassing moment; the accumulation of names (أسامي) serves not as mere repetition but as focused predication upon the multifarious realities of a single event.
22:2.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Remembrance of Death and Afterlife'

22:19.arabic: الدنيا نزلت إليه ملائكة غلاظ شداد معهم ثياب من نار وسرابيل من قطران فيحتوشونه فإذا خرجت نفسه لعنه كل ملك بين السماء والأرض وكل ملك في السماء وغلقت أبواب السماء فليس بها باب إلا يكره أن يدخل بروحه منه فإذا صعد بروحه نبذ وقيل أي ربعبدك فلان لم تقبله سماء ولا ارض فيقول الله عز وجل ارجعوه فأروه ما أعددت له من الشر إني وعدته {منها خلقناكم وفيها نعيدكم ومنها نخرجكم تارة أخرى} وأنه ليسمع خفق نعالهم إذا ولوا مدبرين حتى يقال له يا هذا من ربك ومن نبيك وما دينك فيقول لا أدرى فيقال لا دريت ثم يأتيه آت قبيح الوجه منتن الريح قبيح الثياب فيقول أبشر بسخط من الله وبعذاب أليم مقيم فيقول بشرك الله شرا من أنت فيقول أنا عملك الخبيث والله إن كنت لسريعا في معصية الله بطيئا عن طاعة الله فجزاك الله شرا فيقول وأنت فجزاك الله شرا ثم يقيض له أعمى أصم أبكم معه مرزبة من حديد لو اجتمع عليها الثقلان على أن يقلوها لم يستطيعوا لو ضرب بها جبل صار ترابا فيضربه بها ضربة فيصير ترابا ثم تعود فيه الروح فيضربه بها بين عينيه ضربة يسمعها من على الأرضين ليس الثقلين {قال} ثم ينادي مناد أن افرشوا له لوحين من النار وافتحوا له بابا إلى النار فيفرش له لوحان من نار ويفتح له باب إلى النار (2) وقال محمد بن علي ما من ميت يموت إلا مثل له عند الموت أعماله الحسنة وأعماله السيئة قال فيشخص إلى حسناته ويطرق عن سيئاته وقال أبو هريرة قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إن المؤمن إذا احتضر أتته الملائكة بحريرة فيها مسك وضبائر الريحان فتسل روحه كما تسل الشعرة من العجين ويقال أيتها النفس المطمئنة اخرجي راضية ومرضيا عنك إلى روح الله وكرامته فإذا أخرجت روحه وضعت على ذلك المسك والريحان وطويت عليها الحريرة وبعث بها إلى عليين وإن الكافر إذا احتضر أتته الملائكة بمسح فيه جمرة فتنزع روحه انتزاعا شديدا ويقال أيتها النفس الخبيثة أخرجي ساخطة ومسخوط عليك إلى هوان الله وعذابه فإذا أخرجت روحه وضعت على تلك الجمرة وأن لها نشيشا ويطوى عليها المسح ويذهب بها إلى سجين (1) وعن محمد بن كعب القرظي أنه كان يقرأ قوله تعالى حتى إذا جاء أحدهم الموت قال ربي أرجعون لعلي أعمل صالحا فيما تركت قال أي شيء تريد في أي شيء ترغب أتريد أن ترجع لتجمع المال وتغرس الغراس وتبني البنيان وتشق الأنهار قال لا لعلي أعمل صالحا فيما تركت قال فيقول الجبار {كلا إنها كلمة هو قائلها} أي ليقولنها عند الموت وقال أبو هريرة قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم المؤمن في قبره في روضة خضراء ويرحب له في قبره سبعون ذراعا ويضىء حتى يكون كالقمر ليلة البدر هل تدرون فيماذا أنزلت فإن له معيشة ضنكا قالوا الله ورسوله أعلم قال عذاب الكافر في قبره يسلط عليه تسعة وتسعون تنينا هل تدرون ما التنين تسعة وتسعون حية لكل حية تسعة رؤوس يخدشونه ويلحسونه وينفخون في جسمه إلى يوم يبعثون (2) ولا ينبغي أن يتعجب من هذا العدد على الخصوص فإن أعداد هذه الحيات والعقارب بعدد الأخلاق المذمومة من الكبر والرياء والحسد والغل والحقد وسائر الصفات فإن لها أصولا معدودة ثم تتشعب منها فروع معدودة ثم تنقسم فروعها إلى أقسام وتلك الصفات بأعيانها هي المهلكات وهي بأعيانها تنقلب عقارب وحيات فالقوي منها يلدغ لدغ التنين والضعيف يلدغ لدغ العقرب وما بينهما يؤذي إيذاء الحية وأرباب القلوب والبصائر يشاهدون بنور البصيرة هذه المهلكات والشعاب فروعها إلا أن مقدار عددها لا يوقف عليه إلا بنور النبوة فأمثال هذه الأخبار لها ظواهر صحيحة وأسرار خفية ولكنها عند أرباب البصائر واضحة فمن لم تنكشف له حقائقها فلا ينبغي أن ينكر ظواهرها بل أقل درجات الإيمان التصديق والتسليم فإن قلت فنحن نشاهد الكافر في قبره مدة ونراقبه ولا نشاهد شيئا من ذلك فما وجه التصديق على خلاف المشاهدة فأعلم أن لك ثلاث مقامات في التصديق بأمثال هذا إحداهما وهو الأظهر والأصح والأسلم أن تصدق بأنها موجودة وهي تلدغ الميت ولكنك لا تشاهد ذلك فإن هذه العين لا تصلح لمشاهدة الأمور الملكوتية وكل ما يتعلق بالآخرة فهو من علم الملكوت أما ترى الصحابة رضي الله عنهم كيف كانوا يؤمنون بنزول جبريل وما كانوا يشاهدونه ويؤمنون بأنه عليه السلام يشاهده فإن كنت لا تؤمن بهذا فتصحيح أصل الإيمان بالملائكة والوحي أهم عليك وإن كنت آمنت به وجوزت أن يشاهد النبي مالا تشاهده الأمة فكيف لا تجوز هذا في الميت وكما أن الملك لا يشبه الآدميين والحيوانات فالحيات والعقارب التي تلدغ في القبر ليست من جنس حيات عالمنا بل هي جنس آخر وتدرك بحاسة أخرى
22:19.english: Al-Barā' ibn ʿĀzib said: We went out with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the funeral procession of a man from the Anṣār. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sat at his grave with his head bowed, then said: "O God, I seek refuge in You from the torment of the grave" — three times. Then he said: "Verily, the believer, when he is in the final stage of the Hereafter and the severance from this world, God sends down to him angels whose faces are like the sun, bearing with them his embalming perfume and his shroud. They sit before him as far as his eye can reach. When his soul departs, every angel between heaven and earth prays for him, and every angel in heaven [prays for him], and the gates of heaven are opened — there is no gate but that it yearns for his soul to enter through it. When his soul ascends, it is said: 'O Lord, Your servant so-and-so.' He says: 'Return him, and show him what I have prepared for him of honor, for I promised him: {From it We created you, and into it We shall return you, and from it We shall bring you forth another time} [Ta-Ha/ 55].' And he indeed hears the shuffling of their sandals when they turn away departing, until it is said to him: 'O this one, who is your Lord, and what is your religion, and who is your Prophet?' He says: 'My Lord is God, my religion is Islam, and my Prophet is Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace.' He said: Then he is rebuked with a severe rebuke — and this is the last opportunity presented to the dead — and when he says that, a caller calls out: 'He has spoken the truth' — and this is the meaning of His saying, the Exalted: {God establishes those who believe with the firm word} [Ibrahim/ 27]. Then there comes to him a visitor of beautiful countenance, pleasant fragrance, and fine garments, who says: 'Rejoice in the mercy of your Lord and gardens of enduring delight.' He says: 'And you — may God give you good news of good. Who are you?' He says: 'I am your righteous deed. By God, I knew not but that you were swift to the obedience of God and slow to the disobedience of God — so may God reward you with good.' He said: Then a caller calls out: 'Spread for him from the carpets of Paradise, and open for him a gate to Paradise.' So carpets of Paradise are spread for him, and a gate to Paradise is opened for him. He says: 'O God, hasten the establishment of the Hour, so that I may return to my family and my wealth.' He said: And as for the disbeliever — when he is in the final stage of the Hereafter and the severance from this world, there descend to him angels, harsh and severe, bearing with them garments of fire and tunics of molten pitch. They surround him completely. When his soul departs, every angel between heaven and earth curses him, and every angel in heaven [curses him], and the gates of heaven are shut — there is no gate but that it abhors his soul to enter through it. When his soul ascends, it is cast away, and it is said: 'O Lord, Your servant so-and-so — neither heaven nor earth accepted him.' So God, Mighty and Majestic, says: 'Return him, and show him what I have prepared for him of evil, for I promised him: {From it We created you, and into it We shall return you, and from it We shall bring you forth another time}.' And he indeed hears the shuffling of their sandals when they turn away departing, until it is said to him: 'O this one, who is your Lord, and who is your Prophet, and what is your religion?' He says: 'I do not know.' It is said: 'You did not know!' Then there comes to him a visitor of ugly countenance, foul stench, and vile garments, who says: 'Rejoice in the wrath of God and a painful enduring torment.' He says: 'May God give you evil news. Who are you?' He says: 'I am your wicked deed. By God, I knew not but that you were swift in the disobedience of God and slow to the obedience of God — so may God reward you with evil.' He says: 'And you — may God reward you with evil.' Then there is appointed for him a blind, deaf, and mute one, bearing with him an iron mace — were the two heavy species (thaqalān, i.e., jinn and men) to gather upon it to lift it, they could not — and were he to strike a mountain with it, it would become dust. He strikes him with it a blow, and he becomes dust. Then the soul is returned to him, and he strikes him with it between his eyes a blow whose sound is heard by all upon the earths, save the two heavy species. He said: Then a caller calls out: 'Spread for him two planks of fire, and open for him a gate to the Fire.' So two planks of fire are spread for him, and a gate to the Fire is opened for him.
22:19.section_title_en: The Torments of the Grave and the Visions of the Soul at Death — Section 1323
22:19.anchors:
- Root: قبر (q-b-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The grave as the abode of the dead; the act of interment.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The grave is the place of repose for the dead, and the term extends metaphorically to the state of the barzakh (intermediate realm). The Quranic phrase {حتى زرتم المقابر} [التكاثر/ 2] is a metonymy for death itself.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah) — the physical grave. Metaphorical (Majaz) — the spiritual state of the soul after death, as in "رفع قبراه" (raising one's grave-mound), i.e., arrogance, indicating that the grave's true reality transcends mere earth.
- Root: ملك (m-l-k)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Dominion and authority; the angels as emissaries of divine command.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الملك: هو المتصرف بالأمر والنهي" — the one who disposes by command and prohibition. Angels are termed "رسل" (messengers) of God, as in {الله يصطفي من الملائكة رسلا} [الحج/ 75], and their acts are entirely subordinate to divine will.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — angels as corporeal agents of punishment or mercy. Metaphorical — their true nature is immaterial (laṭīfah rabbāniyyah), imperceptible to the physical senses of the living.
- Root: روح (r-w-ḥ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Breath, spirit, the animating principle.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The soul (rūḥ) is a subtle divine reality (laṭīfah rabbāniyyah) that departs the body at death; its extraction is described in degrees of ease or violence according to faith or disbelief.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — the breath of life. Metaphorical — the spiritual essence that perceives the malakūt (invisible dominion) after death, a realm beyond the reach of the corporeal eye.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The periodic structure of the hadith, e.g., "خرجنا مع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في جنازة رجل من الأنصار," demonstrates how prepositional phrases (مع، في، من) interlock to build a narrative sequence, each clause grammatically complete yet subordinate to the overarching report, mirroring the unbroken chain of transmission (isnād).
22:19.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Remembrance of Death and Afterlife'

22:19.arabic: ومهما دعوا بالثبور صب من فوق رءوسهم الحميم يصهر به ما في بطونهم والجلود ولهم مقامع من حديد تهشم بها جباههم فيتفجر الصديد من أفواههم وننقطع من العطش أكبادهم وتسيل على الخدود أحداقهم ويسقط من الوجنات لحومها ويتمعط من الأطراف شعورها بل جلودها وكلما نضجت جلودهم بدلوا جلودا غيرها قد عريت من اللحم عظامهم فبقيت الأرواح منوطة بالعروق وعلائق العصب وهي تنش في لفح تلك النيران وهم مع ذلك يتمنون الموت فلا يموتون فكيف بك لو نظرت إليهم وقد سودت وجوههم أشد سوادا من الحميم وأعميت أبصارهم وأبكمت ألسن
22:19.english: O you who are heedless of your own soul, deluded by what occupies you of the distractions of this world that is on the verge of passing away and perishing — abandon reflection upon that from which you are departing, and turn your thought to your place of arrival (mawrid), for you have been informed that the Fire is a place of arrival for all, since it was said: {«وإن منكم إلا واردها كان على ربك حتما مقضيا ثم ننجي الذين اتقوا ونذر الظالمين فيها جثيا»} [And there is none of you but shall arrive at it — an inevitability decreed upon your Lord. Then We shall save those who were God-fearing, and leave the wrongdoers in it, kneeling]. You are thus in certainty regarding the arrival (wurūd), and in doubt regarding deliverance. So instill within your heart the terror of that place of arrival — perhaps you will thereby prepare yourself for deliverance from it.
22:19.section_title_en: Discourse on the Attributes of Hellfire, Its Terrors, and Its Fetters
22:19.anchors:
- Root: ورد (w-r-d)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning is "to arrive at water" — the primordial act of approaching a watering-place; from this derives the sense of arriving at any destination, whether desired or dreaded.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الورود أصله: قصد الماء" — its origin is the intent to reach water; then applied generally, and used of the Fire "على سبيل الفظاعة" (by way of horrification), as in {وإن منكم إلا واردها} — the universal "arrival" at Hell is a divinely decreed certainty.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): ورد الماء — arriving at water to drink. Metaphorical (Majaz): وردت البلد — arriving at a land; ورد عليه أمر لم يطقه — an overwhelming matter descended upon him. Here, "al-wurūd" is majaz extended to the eschatological "arrival" at the Fire, a passage all must undergo.
- Root: جلد (j-l-d)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The skin or hide covering the body; جلد الكتاب — to cover a book with leather; جلدته بالسياط — to flog.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الجلد: قشر البدن" — the skin is the body's integument; in the Quranic verse {كلما نضجت جلودهم بدلناهم جلودا غيرها} [النساء/56], the renewal of skins is the renewal of the seat of pain, ensuring perpetual sensation.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: flaying, covering, stripping. Metaphorical: جلدته على هذا الأمر — compelled him. In this text, the literal sense governs: skins roasted, then replaced, so that torment never ceases.
- Root: ظلم (z-l-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Darkness, absence of light; also wrongdoing. The lexicographers note the moral-ontological link: injustice is a kind of darkness.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الظلمة: عدم النور" — darkness is the privation of light; used metaphorically for ignorance, polytheism, and transgression, as light is used for their opposites.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "الظلم ظلمات يوم القيامة" — wrongdoing is darknesses on the Day of Resurrection. Metaphorical: أرض مظلومة — land never before dug. Here, "zulumāt" (ظلمات) is used literally of Hell's physical darknesses, yet these are also the reified shadows of the inmates' own wrongs.
- Root: نار (n-w-r / n-w-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Fire; the root also yields نار — to kindle, to blaze up. The lexicons record the proverb: ورَيْتُ بك زنادي — "I struck fire from your flint," i.e., I perceived from you good counsel.
  * Al-Raghib (Al-Mufradat): Fire is the elemental reality of Hell, but its Quranic usage spans both physical flame and the "Fire of God kindled" which mounts over hearts [الهمزة/6-7] — the inward fire of heedlessness made outward.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: flame, burning. Metaphorical: نار الحرب — the fire of war. In this passage, the literal fire of Jahannam is described with maximal sensory concreteness, yet it remains the outward manifestation of the soul's own kindled crimes.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The rule governing the permissibility of interposing elements between a preposition and its object when the intervening phrase is semantically complete. Applied here in the periodic constructions where long descriptive clauses intervene between the initial vocative (يا أيها الغافل) and its eventual predicate, sustaining rhetorical tension across the entire passage.
22:19.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Remembrance of Death and Afterlife'

22:23.arabic: قال الله يحلون فيها من أساور من ذهب ولؤلؤا ولباسهم فيها حرير والآيات في ذلك كثيرة وإنما تفصيله في الأخبار فقد روى أبو هريرة أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال من يدخل الجنة ينعم لا يبأس لا تبلى ثيابه ولا يفنى شبابه في الجنة ما لا عين رأت ولا أذن سمعت ولا خطر عن قلب بشر (1) وقال رجل يا رسول الله أخبرنا عن ثياب أهل الجنة أخلق تخلق أم نسج تنسج فسكت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وضحك بعض القوم فقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم مم تضحكون من جاهل سأل عالما ثم قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ب
22:23.english: Ponder the form of Paradise, and reflect upon the bliss of its inhabitants, and upon the remorse of him who is deprived of it for his contentment with this world as a substitute for it. For Abu Hurayrah said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: "Verily, the wall of Paradise is a brick of silver and a brick of gold; its soil is saffron, and its clay is musk." (1) And he was asked, may God bless him and grant him peace, about the earth of Paradise, and he said: "A white flour-like pure musk." (2) And Abu Hurayrah said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: "Whosoever would delight that God, Mighty and Majestic, should give him wine to drink in the Hereafter, let him abandon it in this world; and whosoever would delight that God should clothe him in silk in the Hereafter, let him abandon it in this world." (3) And he said: "The rivers of Paradise gush forth from beneath hills, or beneath mountains, of musk." (4) And were the least of the people of Paradise in adornment to be weighed against the adornment of all the people of this world together, that with which God, Mighty and Majestic, adorns him in the Hereafter would still be better than all the adornment of this world. (5) And Abu Hurayrah said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: "Verily, in Paradise there is a tree beneath whose shade a rider travels for a hundred years without crossing it. Recite, if you wish: {And a shade extended} (6) {«وَظِلٍّ مَمْدُودٍ»}." And Abu Umāmah said: The companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to say: "God, Mighty and Majestic, benefits us through the Bedouins and their questions." A Bedouin came forward and said: "O Messenger of God, God has mentioned in the Qur'an a harmful tree, and I did not know that in Paradise there is a tree that harms its companion." The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: "{What is it?} {«مَا هِيَ»}" He said: "The lote-tree (al-sidr), for it has thorns." He said: "God, Exalted is He, has said: {In a lote-tree that is thornless} {«فِي سِدْرٍ مَخْضُودٍ»} — God clips its thorns and places in the stead of every thorn a fruit; then the fruit splits open from it into seventy-two colors of food, no one color of which resembles another." (7) And Jarīr ibn ʿAbd Allāh said: We alighted at al-Ṣifāḥ, and there was a man sleeping beneath a tree, the sun having nearly reached him. I said to the youth: "Go with this leather sheet and shade him." So he went and shaded him. When he awoke, behold, it was Salmān. I came to him and greeted him, and he said: "O Jarīr, humble yourself before God, for whosoever humbles himself before God in this world, God raises him on the Day of Resurrection. Do you know what the darknesses are on the Day of Resurrection?" I said: "I do not know." He said: "The wronging of people, one another." Then he took a small twig that I could scarcely see due to its smallness, and said: "O Jarīr, were you to seek the like of this in Paradise, you would not find it." I said: "O Abu ʿAbd Allāh, where then are the date-palms and the trees?" He said: "Their roots are of pearl and gold, and their tops are the fruit."
22:23.section_title_en: The Description of the Wall of Paradise, Its Lands, Trees, and Rivers; and the Description of the Garments, Furnishings, Couches, Canopies, and Tents of Its Inhabitants
22:23.anchors:
- Root: حوط (ḥ-w-ṭ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The enclosing wall or boundary that surrounds and protects a garden; its core sense is preservation and encompassment.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In the eschatological context, the wall (ḥā'iṭ) is a corporeal boundary delineating the Garden, yet its materials (silver and gold bricks) signify a reality transcending earthly substance (jawhar), pointing to the immaterial bounty (faḍl) of the divine grant.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) for the physical wall; metaphorical (majāz) extension when the "wall" denotes the barrier of honor separating the blessed from deprivation.
- Root: خلد (kh-l-d)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Perpetuity and endless duration; the state of abiding without termination.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Eternal subsistence (khulūd) is an attribute of the abode of recompense, contrasting with the temporal accidents (aʿrāḍ) of worldly existence; it is a fixed, necessary concomitant of the divine promise.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal for unceasing time; metaphorical for the soul's permanent state of felicity, free from the vicissitudes of generation and corruption.
- Root: ثمر (th-m-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The fruit borne by trees; the yield of a plant at its culmination.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In the Garden, fruit (thamarah) is a designated reality (musammā) whose essence is transformed by divine power—each thorn replaced by fruit—demonstrating the absolute capacity of the Creator over nature.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal for edible produce; metaphorical for the "fruit" of deeds, whether reward or punishment, as an accrued outcome.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Restriction and Specification (al-ḥaṣr wa al-taqyīd) — Governing how predicates like "its soil is saffron" and "its clay is musk" are syntactically focused to affirm the exclusive, unprecedented nature of Paradise's attributes, distinguishing them from earthly analogues.
22:23.topic: Al-Ghazali on the journey of the soul, death, and the Hereafter, from 'Remembrance of Death and Afterlife'

22:61.arabic: في النهار لا يقبله في الليل وأن لله حقا في الليل لا يقبله في النهار وأنه لا يقبل النافلة حتى تؤدى الفريضة وإنما ثقلت موازين من ثقلت موازينهم يوم القيامة باتباعهم الحق في الدنيا وثقله عليهم وحق لميزان لا يوضع فيه إلا الحق أن يثقل وإنما خفت موازين من خفت موزاينهم يوم القيامة باتباع الباطل وخفته عليهم وحق لميزان لا يوضع فيه إلاالباطل أن يخف وإن الله ذكر أهل الجنة بأحسن أعمالهم وتجاوز عن سيئاتهم فيقول القائل أنا دون هؤلاء ولا أبلغ مبلغ صالح الذي عملوا فيقول القائل أنا أ
22:61.english: When Abu Bakr (may Allah Most High be pleased with him) was in the throes of death, ʿĀʾishah (may Allah be pleased with her) came and recited this verse: "By your life, wealth avails not the youth... when the breath rattles in his chest one day, and the breast is straitened thereby."
22:61.section_title_en: The Death of Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (may Allah Most High be pleased with him)
22:61.anchors:
- Root: حشرج (ḥashraja)
  * Lisan / Ayn: [Core linguistic root meaning: The rattling, gurgling sound of the death-throe in the throat; the final breath struggling in the chest.]
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): [Theological/Kalam semantic nuance: The terminal state of the soul's separation from the body, the moment of overwhelming divine decree.]
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): [Literal vs Metaphorical distinction: Literal — the physical rattle of the dying; Metaphorical — the constriction of the breast as the soul is drawn forth.]
- Root: سكر (sakara)
  * Lisan / Ayn: [Core linguistic root meaning: The veiling of the intellect; intoxication; the stupor that overcomes one at the onset of death.]
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): [Theological/Kalam semantic nuance: The stupor of death (sakrat al-mawt) as the removal of all veils, wherein the truth of the Hereafter becomes undeniably present.]
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): [Literal vs Metaphorical distinction: Literal — intoxication from drink; Metaphorical — the overwhelming bewilderment of the soul at death's onset.]
- Root: ذمم (dhimam)
  * Lisan / Ayn: [Core linguistic root meaning: The covenant of protection; the bond of safe-conduct; that which one is obligated to honor and safeguard.]
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): [Theological/Kalam semantic nuance: The divine guarantee (dhimmat Allah) extended to the believer who prays the dawn prayer — a sacred pact not to be violated.]
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): [Literal vs Metaphorical distinction: Literal — a pledge of security between men; Metaphorical — the inviolable covenant between the servant and his Lord.]
- Root: وزن (wazana)
  * Lisan / Ayn: [Core linguistic root meaning: To weigh; the balance; the measure of equivalence between two things.]
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): [Theological/Kalam semantic nuance: The weighing of deeds on the Day of Resurrection as the manifestation of divine justice — the scales (mawāzīn) receiving only truth or falsehood.]
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): [Literal vs Metaphorical distinction: Literal — the physical act of weighing; Metaphorical — the spiritual weighing of deeds by their conformity to truth (ḥaqq) or falsehood (bāṭil).]
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — [The particle innamā restricts the predicate exclusively to its subject, as in Abu Bakr's dictum: "It is only that the scales of those whose scales are heavy on the Day of Resurrection are weighed down by their following the truth in this world."]
22:61.topic: Al-Ghazali on the journey of the soul, death, and the Hereafter, from 'Remembrance of Death and Afterlife'

23:99.arabic: القرظي أنه كان يقرأ قوله تعالى حتى إذا جاء أحدهم الموت قال ربي أرجعون لعلي أعمل صالحا فيما تركت قال أي شيء تريد في أي شيء ترغب أتريد أن ترجع لتجمع المال وتغرس الغراس وتبني البنيان وتشق الأنهار قال لا لعلي أعمل صالحا فيما تركت قال فيقول الجبار {كلا إنها كلمة هو قائلها} أي ليقولنها عند الموت وقال أبو هريرة قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم المؤمن في قبره في روضة خضراء ويرحب له في قبره سبعون ذراعا ويضىء حتى يكون كالقمر ليلة البدر هل تدرون فيماذا أنزلت فإن له معيشة ضنكا قالوا الله ورسوله أعلم قال عذاب الكافر في قبره يسلط عليه تسعة وتسعون تنينا هل
23:99.english: Al-Barā' ibn ʿĀzib said: We went out with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the funeral procession of a man from the Anṣār. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sat at his grave with his head bowed, then said: "O God, I seek refuge in You from the torment of the grave" — three times. Then he said: "Verily, the believer, when he is in the final stage of the Hereafter and the severance from this world, God sends down to him angels whose faces are like the sun, bearing with them his embalming perfume and his shroud. They sit before him as far as his eye can reach. When his soul departs, every angel between heaven and earth prays for him, and every angel in heaven [prays for him], and the gates of heaven are opened — there is no gate but that it yearns for his soul to enter through it. When his soul ascends, it is said: 'O Lord, Your servant so-and-so.' He says: 'Return him, and show him what I have prepared for him of honor, for I promised him: {From it We created you, and into it We shall return you, and from it We shall bring you forth another time} [Ta-Ha/ 55].' And he indeed hears the shuffling of their sandals when they turn away departing, until it is said to him: 'O this one, who is your Lord, and what is your religion, and who is your Prophet?' He says: 'My Lord is God, my religion is Islam, and my Prophet is Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace.' He said: Then he is rebuked with a severe rebuke — and this is the last opportunity presented to the dead — and when he says that, a caller calls out: 'He has spoken the truth' — and this is the meaning of His saying, the Exalted: {God establishes those who believe with the firm word} [Ibrahim/ 27]. Then there comes to him a visitor of beautiful countenance, pleasant fragrance, and fine garments, who says: 'Rejoice in the mercy of your Lord and gardens of enduring delight.' He says: 'And you — may God give you good news of good. Who are you?' He says: 'I am your righteous deed. By God, I knew not but that you were swift to the obedience of God and slow to the disobedience of God — so may God reward you with good.' He said: Then a caller calls out: 'Spread for him from the carpets of Paradise, and open for him a gate to Paradise.' So carpets of Paradise are spread for him, and a gate to Paradise is opened for him. He says: 'O God, hasten the establishment of the Hour, so that I may return to my family and my wealth.' He said: And as for the disbeliever — when he is in the final stage of the Hereafter and the severance from this world, there descend to him angels, harsh and severe, bearing with them garments of fire and tunics of molten pitch. They surround him completely. When his soul departs, every angel between heaven and earth curses him, and every angel in heaven [curses him], and the gates of heaven are shut — there is no gate but that it abhors his soul to enter through it. When his soul ascends, it is cast away, and it is said: 'O Lord, Your servant so-and-so — neither heaven nor earth accepted him.' So God, Mighty and Majestic, says: 'Return him, and show him what I have prepared for him of evil, for I promised him: {From it We created you, and into it We shall return you, and from it We shall bring you forth another time}.' And he indeed hears the shuffling of their sandals when they turn away departing, until it is said to him: 'O this one, who is your Lord, and who is your Prophet, and what is your religion?' He says: 'I do not know.' It is said: 'You did not know!' Then there comes to him a visitor of ugly countenance, foul stench, and vile garments, who says: 'Rejoice in the wrath of God and a painful enduring torment.' He says: 'May God give you evil news. Who are you?' He says: 'I am your wicked deed. By God, I knew not but that you were swift in the disobedience of God and slow to the obedience of God — so may God reward you with evil.' He says: 'And you — may God reward you with evil.' Then there is appointed for him a blind, deaf, and mute one, bearing with him an iron mace — were the two heavy species (thaqalān, i.e., jinn and men) to gather upon it to lift it, they could not — and were he to strike a mountain with it, it would become dust. He strikes him with it a blow, and he becomes dust. Then the soul is returned to him, and he strikes him with it between his eyes a blow whose sound is heard by all upon the earths, save the two heavy species. He said: Then a caller calls out: 'Spread for him two planks of fire, and open for him a gate to the Fire.' So two planks of fire are spread for him, and a gate to the Fire is opened for him.
23:99.section_title_en: The Torments of the Grave and the Visions of the Soul at Death — Section 1323
23:99.anchors:
- Root: قبر (q-b-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The grave as the abode of the dead; the act of interment.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The grave is the place of repose for the dead, and the term extends metaphorically to the state of the barzakh (intermediate realm). The Quranic phrase {حتى زرتم المقابر} [التكاثر/ 2] is a metonymy for death itself.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah) — the physical grave. Metaphorical (Majaz) — the spiritual state of the soul after death, as in "رفع قبراه" (raising one's grave-mound), i.e., arrogance, indicating that the grave's true reality transcends mere earth.
- Root: ملك (m-l-k)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Dominion and authority; the angels as emissaries of divine command.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الملك: هو المتصرف بالأمر والنهي" — the one who disposes by command and prohibition. Angels are termed "رسل" (messengers) of God, as in {الله يصطفي من الملائكة رسلا} [الحج/ 75], and their acts are entirely subordinate to divine will.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — angels as corporeal agents of punishment or mercy. Metaphorical — their true nature is immaterial (laṭīfah rabbāniyyah), imperceptible to the physical senses of the living.
- Root: روح (r-w-ḥ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Breath, spirit, the animating principle.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The soul (rūḥ) is a subtle divine reality (laṭīfah rabbāniyyah) that departs the body at death; its extraction is described in degrees of ease or violence according to faith or disbelief.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — the breath of life. Metaphorical — the spiritual essence that perceives the malakūt (invisible dominion) after death, a realm beyond the reach of the corporeal eye.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The periodic structure of the hadith, e.g., "خرجنا مع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في جنازة رجل من الأنصار," demonstrates how prepositional phrases (مع، في، من) interlock to build a narrative sequence, each clause grammatically complete yet subordinate to the overarching report, mirroring the unbroken chain of transmission (isnād).
23:99.topic: Al-Ghazali on the journey of the soul, death, and the Hereafter, from 'Remembrance of Death and Afterlife'

23:99.arabic: دخل فيه فاضطجع فيه ومكث ساعة ثم قال {رب أرجعون لعلي أعمل صالحا فيما تركت} ثم يقول يا ربيع قد أرجعت فاعمل الآن قبل أن لا ترجع وقال ميمون بن مهران خرجت مع عمر بن عبد العزيز إلى المقبرة فلما نظر إلى القبور بكى وقال يا ميمون هذه قبور آبائي بني أمية كأنهم لم يشاركوا أهل الدنيا في لذاتهم أما تراهم صرعى قد خلت بهم المثلات وأصاب الهوام من أبدانهم ثم بكى وقال والله ما أعلم أحدا أنعم ممن صار إلى هذه القبور وقد أمن من عذاب الله وآداب المعزي خفض الجناح وإظهار الحزن وقلة الحديث وترك التبسم وآداب تشييع الجنا
23:99.english: A man defended him, and the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: "Whoever defends the honor of his brother shall have it as a shield for him against the Fire." (1)
23:99.anchors:
- Root: رد (r-d-d)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To return, repel, defend, avert; al-radd ʿan al-ʿirḍ is to repel defamation from one's honor
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Defense against false accusation; the theological nuance of divine recompense (al-mukāfaʾah) for defending a brother's honor
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal repulsion of physical harm extended metaphorically to verbal defense of honor (ḥaqīqah vs. majāz)
- Root: عطس (ʿ-t-s)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Sneezing; al-tashmīt is the invocation of mercy upon the sneezer
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The sneeze is attributed to God (min Allāh) as a sign of divine favor, while yawning is attributed to Satan
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): The response "yarḥamukallāh" is a supplication, not an assertion — distinguishing literal invocation from mere congratulation
- Root: عاد (ʿ-w-d)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To visit repeatedly; al-ʿiyādah is the visitation of the sick
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Returning to someone in his affliction; the reward is measured by the intensity of compassion shown
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): The "return" (ʿawd) is literal in visitation, but the reward is spiritual — a metaphorical extension of recompense
- Root: شيع (sh-y-ʿ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To accompany, follow; al-tashyīʿ is the funeral procession
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Following the bier with the intention of honoring the deceased and taking admonition (al-iʿtibār)
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): The qīrāṭ is a measure of reward — metaphorical weight, not literal coin
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Conditional Protasis (Bāb al-sharṭ) — The construction "man ... fa-..." (whoever does X, then Y) establishes a causal nexus requiring the apodosis to be a new sentence, often carrying the force of divine decree.
