23:99.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'Duties of Brotherhood'

23:100.arabic: ظعنوا فليس لهم إياب هيهات هيهات {كلا إنها كلمة هو قائلها ومن ورائهم برزخ إلى يوم يبعثون} فكأن قد صرتم إلى ما صاروا إليه من البلاء والوحدة في دار المثوى وارتهنتم في ذلك المضجع وضمكم ذلك المستودع فكيف بكم لو عاينتم الأمور وبعثرت القبور وحصل ما في الصدور وأوقفتم للتحصيل بين يدي الملك الجليل فطارت القلوب لإشفاقها من سالف الذنوب وهتكت عنكم الحجب والأستار وظهرت منكم العيوب والأسرار هنالك تجزى كل نفس بما كسبت إن الله عز وجل يقول ليجزى الذي أساءوا بما عملوا ويجزى الذي أحسنوا بالحسنى وقال تعالى {ووضع الكتاب ف
23:100.english: And indeed there has come the narration from him, from his Lord, Mighty and Glorious, that He said to Moses, peace be upon him: "When you see the rich man approaching, say: 'A sin whose punishment has been hastened.' And when you see the poor man approaching, say: 'Welcome to the badge of the righteous.'" And if you wish, you may follow the possessor of the Spirit and the Word, Jesus son of Mary, peace be upon him — for he used to say: "My condiment is hunger, my badge is fear, my garment is wool, my warmth in winter is the rising places of the sun, my lamp is the moon, my mount is my two feet, and my food and my fruit is what the earth brings forth. I pass the night and I possess nothing, and I rise in the morning and I possess nothing — and there is no one upon the earth richer than I."
23:100.section_title_en: The Revival of the Religious Sciences — Section 737: On the Censure of This World and the Description of Its Perils
23:100.anchors:
- Root: دنو (danuww)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "دنا فهو دانٍ" — proximity, nearness; the world (al-dunyā) is so named because it is nearer and lower, deferred from the Hereafter.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الدنو: القرب بالذات، أو بالحكم" — proximity by essence or by decree; used of place, time, and station. The "nearer" (al-adnā) is contrasted with the greater and the better.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical nearness. Metaphorical: the lower, contemptible station — "أهل الدناءة هم أهل الشناءة" (the people of baseness are the people of abhorrence).
- Root: يوم (yawm)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "اليوم" — a day; also any period of time.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "اليوم يعبر به عن وقت طلوع الشمس إلى غروبها. وقد يعبر به عن مدة من الزمان أي مدة كانت" — the day is the time from sunrise to sunset, or any duration whatsoever. "وذكرهم بأيام الله" — the days of God are His mighty deeds and calamities upon the disbelievers.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the solar day. Metaphorical: "أيام العرب" — their battles and vicissitudes; "أيام الله" — His punitive visitations.
- Root: وقد (waqada)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "وقدت النار تقد وقودا ووقدا" — the fire blazed; al-wuqūd is the fuel.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "وقودها الناس والحجارة" — the fuel of the Fire is men and stones; the one who kindles it for himself (istawqada) is he who seeks its light.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: kindling a fire. Metaphorical: "قلب وقاد" — a blazing, keen heart; "وقد الحصى" — the pebbles became scorching hot (i.e., the intensity of the sun's heat).
- Root: ألك (alaka)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "المألكة: الرسالة، لأنها تؤلك في الفم" — the message (risālah) is called ma'lakah because it is chewed/worked in the mouth.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الملائكة تقع على الواحد والجمع" — angels (malā'ikah) are so named as bearers of messages; "الله يصطفي من الملائكة رسلا" {«الله يصطفي من الملائكة رسلا»} — God chooses messengers from the angels.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: chewing (as a horse chews its bit). Metaphorical: delivering a message — the angel is the one who delivers the divine communication.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — "إنما" restricts the predicate to the subject alone, negating it of all else. Applied in the sermon: "إنما يتزين لي أوليائي بالذل والخوف" — My friends adorn themselves for Me ONLY with humility, fear, and submission — restricting their adornment to these alone, excluding all worldly ornament.
23:100.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'Remembrance of Death and Afterlife'

23:100.arabic: قوله عز وجل رب أرجعون لعلي أعمل صالحا فيما تركت {قال}
23:100.english: And whoever dies without having performed Hajj despite affluence — his matter is severe with God — Exalted is He. ʿUmar — may God be pleased with him — said: "I nearly resolved to write to the provinces imposing the jizyah upon whoever did not perform Hajj among those who could find a way to it."
23:100.section_title_en: The Second Chapter on the Conditions for the Obligation of Hajj, the Validity of Its Pillars, Its Duties, and Its Prohibitions
23:100.anchors:
- Root: شرط (sh-r-t)
  * Lisan / Ayn: A mark, sign, or condition; that which is stipulated and by which something is bound.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): A condition (sharṭ) is that upon which the existence or validity of another thing depends, whether by divine decree or human stipulation.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): a sign or token; metaphorical (majāz): a stipulated prerequisite that renders an act contingent upon it.
- Root: أحرم (a-ḥ-r-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To enter into the sacred state (iḥrām); from ḥarām, that which is protected and forbidden during the pilgrimage.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Iḥrām is the intentional entry into a state wherein certain otherwise permissible acts become prohibited, marking the commencement of pilgrimage rites.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: to make something forbidden; metaphorical: the pilgrim's self-consecration by intention and talbiyah, rendering ordinary acts unlawful.
- Root: استطاع (i-s-t-ṭ-ʿ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To have power, capacity, or means over something; istiṭāʿah is the ability to accomplish an act.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Istiṭāʿah is of two kinds: capacity of the self (bodily ability) and capacity of one's wealth (financial means); both are requisite for the obligation of Hajj.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical or financial power; metaphorical: the legal capacity that renders worship obligatory, as in the verse {وَلِلَّهِ عَلَى النَّاسِ حِجُّ الْبَيْتِ مَنِ اسْتَطَاعَ إِلَيْهِ سَبِيلًا}.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Conditional Clauses (Bāb al-sharṭ) — The particle "fa" (then) in apodosis clauses marks the consequent as dependent upon the fulfillment of the protasis, as in "man istatāʿa lazimahu al-ḥajj" (whoever has the means, Hajj becomes obligatory upon him).
23:100.topic: Classical commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya Ulum al-Din, from 'Remembrance of Death and Afterlife'

23:106.arabic: من ربكم فيقولون ربنا غلبت علينا شقوتنا وكنا قوما ضالين ربنا أخرجنا منها فإن عدنا فإنا ظالمون قال فيجيبهم اخسئوا فيها ولا تكلمون {قال}
23:106.english: And ʿAlī, may God honor his face, said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: "Seek refuge in God from the Pit of Sorrow, or the Valley of Sorrow." It was said: "O Messenger of God, what is the Valley or Pit of Sorrow?" He said: "A valley in Hell from which Hell itself seeks refuge with God seventy times each day. God, the Exalted, has prepared it for the reciters who show off." (2)
23:106.section_title_en: The Vastness of Hellfire, Its Depths, and the Torments of Its Inhabitants
23:106.anchors:
- Root: و د ي (w-d-y)
  * Lisan / Ayn: A valley; a place where torrents flow. In the lexicon, it denotes a lowland or watercourse between mountains.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Used for the valleys of Hell as places of confinement and passage, each containing further branching ravines (شُعَب), indicating graded descent.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal for earthly valleys; here transferred (majāz) to the topographical reality of Hell, affirming its corporeal vastness.
- Root: ع م ق (ʿ-m-q)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Depth; the far bottom of a well or pit. Al-Farahidi: "العمق: قعر البئر ونحوها."
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Depth as a measure of descent; in the Hereafter, it is unbounded, paralleling the unbounded depth of worldly desire.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal for physical depth; here extended to show the infinite regress of punishment corresponding to infinite craving.
- Root: غ س ق (gh-s-q)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Stinking, foul pus or ichor that flows from the skin of the damned; also intense darkness.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-Ghassāq is the putrid effusion of Hell, a punishment for the senses, specifically for drinking when the damned cry out in thirst.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal for what is loathsome and fetid; in the Quranic context, it is the designated drink of the inhabitants.
- Root: ز ق م (z-q-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To swallow with difficulty; the tree of Zaqqūm, which grows in the depths of Hell.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): A specific tree in Hell whose fruit is like the heads of devils, eaten by the damned to fill their bellies, causing choking and agony.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal for a real tree; its description is sensory, not metaphorical, affirming the physical reality of punishment.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The periodic structure of "في جهنم سبعين ألف واد" allows the prepositional phrase to precede the subject for emphasis, establishing the spatial setting before detailing its contents.
23:106.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications, prayers, and their spiritual power, from 'Remembrance of Death and Afterlife'

23:108.arabic: ولا يغاثون بل يقال لهم اخسئوا فيها ولا تكلمون أولئك الذي اشتروا الحياة الدنيا بالآخرة فلا يخفف عنهم العذاب ولا هم ينصرون وإذا عظمت غوائل الدنيا وشرورها فلا بد أولا من معرفة حقيقة الدنيا وما هي وما الحكمة في خلقها مع عداوتها وما مدخل غرورها وشرورها فإن من لا يعرف الشر لا يتقيه ويوشك أن يقع فيه ونحن نذكر ذم الدنيا وأمثلتها وحقيقتها وتفصيل معانيها وأصناف الأشغال المتعلقة بها ووجه الحاجة إلى أصولها وسبب انصراف الخلق عن الله بسبب التشاغل بفضولها إن شاء الله تعالى وهو المعين على ما يرت
23:108.english: Praise be to God, who made His friends acquainted with the calamitous snares of this world and its afflictions, and uncovered for them its defects and its shameful parts, until they gazed upon its evidences and its signs, and weighed its evil deeds against its good deeds. Thus they came to know that its objectionable aspects exceed its commendable ones, that what is hoped from it does not fulfill what is feared from it, and that its rising is not safe from its eclipse. Yet it is in the likeness of a comely woman who draws people to herself by her beauty — while within her are hidden secrets of evil, ugly things that destroy those who yearn for union with her. Then she is a fleer from her seekers, niggardly in her turning toward them; and when she does turn, one is not secure from her evil and her pestilence. If she does good for an hour, she does evil for a year; and if she does evil once, she makes it her perpetual habit. So the cycles of her turning are ever more tightly drawn, and the commerce of her sons is losing and ruined, and her afflictions in succession strike the breasts of her seekers, and the courses of her states proclaim the humiliation of those who pursue her. Thus every one deluded by her is destined to abasement, and every one who waxes proud through her proceeds to regret. Her very nature is to flee from her seeker and to be sought by the one who flees from her. Whoever serves her, she eludes; whoever turns away from her, she comes to. Her clarity is never free of the admixture of turbidity, nor is her joy ever disentangled from what embitters it. Her soundness bequeaths sickness, her youth drives on to decrepitude, and her bliss bears no fruit but remorse and regret. She is deceitful, guileful, fleeting, evasive. She never ceases adorning herself for her seekers until, when they have become her lovers, she bares her fangs at them, disorders the ordered strands of their affairs, and uncovers for them the hidden store of her wonders — then she makes them taste the lethal poisons and strikes them with the piercing shafts of her arrows. While her companions are in joy and bounty from her, suddenly she turns away from them as though she were but scattered dreams; then she rushes upon them with her calamities, grinds them as grain is ground, and shrouds them in their winding-sheets beneath the dust. If she has possessed one of them with all that the sun has risen upon, she makes him as reaped harvest, as though he had not dwelt in plenty the day before. Her companions desire joy from her, and she promises them delusion — until they hope for much and build palaces, and then their palaces become graves, their gatherings become ruin, their striving becomes scattered dust, and their cry becomes "Woe and destruction!" Such is her description — and the command of God is a decree determined. And the prayer and peace be upon Muhammad, His servant and His Messenger, sent to the worlds as a bringer of glad tidings and a warner, and as an illuminating lamp; and upon those of his family and companions who were for him supporters in the religion, and against the wrongdoers helpers; and abundant peace.
23:108.section_title_en: The Book of Condemnation of This World — Being the Sixth Book of the Quarter of the Destructive Things from The Revival of the Religious Sciences
23:108.anchors:
- Root: لهم (l-h-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root meaning of swallowing, devouring, or ingesting wholly
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): الإلهام: casting something into the heart (al-rawʿ), specifically from God or the higher assembly; the root denotes the soul's complete reception, as one who swallows entirely
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: ألهمه الله الخير — God cast good into his heart. Metaphorical: جيش لهم — an army that engulfs and swallows whomever enters it
- Root: دنا (d-n-w)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Nearness in place, time, or rank; the world (al-dunyā) is so named because it is nearer and lower, deferred from the Hereafter
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): الدنو: proximity by essence or by judgment, used of place, time, and station; al-dunyā is the nearer, lower life
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: هو دانٍ — he is near. Metaphorical: الأدنى — the inferior, the baser, contrasted with what is better
- Root: حسر (ḥ-s-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Uncovering, stripping away a covering; exhaustion from exposure of one's strength
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): الحسر: uncovering what veils; al-ḥasīr: one whose strength is laid bare and spent; al-ḥāsir: the weary whose powers are uncovered as exhausted
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: حسر عن ذراعيه — he bared his forearms. Metaphorical: فلان كريم المحسر — so-and-so is noble when tested/examined (his hidden quality is uncovered)
- Root: سرر (s-r-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Concealment, the secret kept hidden in the breast; the innermost
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): الإسرار: opposite of declaration; al-sirr: the speech concealed in the soul
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: أسر الحديث — he concealed the speech. Metaphorical: أعطيتك سره — I gave you its choicest essence; هو في سر النسب — he is in the pure core of lineage
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The permissibility of interposing elements between a governing word and its governed prepositional phrase when the interposed element is complete in itself, as in the rhetorical suspensions of this oration
23:108.topic: Al-Ghazali on the journey of the soul, death, and the Hereafter, from 'Remembrance of Death and Afterlife'

23:108.arabic: الزبانية هيهات لات حين أمان ولا خروج لكم من دار الهوان فاخسئوا فيها ولا تكلمون ولو أخرجتم منها لكنتم إلى ما نهيتم عنه تعودون فعند ذلك يقنطون وعلى ما فرطوا في جنب الله يتأسفون ولا ينجيهم الندم ولا يغنيهم الأسف بل يكبون على وجوههم مغلولين النار من فوقهم والنار من تحتهم والنار عن أيمانهم والنار عن شمائلهم فهم غرقى في النار طعامهم نار وشرابهم نار ولباسهم نار ومهادهم نار فهم بين مقطعات النيران وسرابيل القطران وضرب المقامع وثقل السلاسل فهم يتجلجلون في مضايقها ويتحطمون في دركاتها ويضطربون بين غواشيها تغلى بهم النار كغلي ا
23:108.english: O you who are heedless of your own soul, deluded by what occupies you of the distractions of this world that is on the verge of passing away and perishing — abandon reflection upon that from which you are departing, and turn your thought to your place of arrival (mawrid), for you have been informed that the Fire is a place of arrival for all, since it was said: {«وإن منكم إلا واردها كان على ربك حتما مقضيا ثم ننجي الذين اتقوا ونذر الظالمين فيها جثيا»} [And there is none of you but shall arrive at it — an inevitability decreed upon your Lord. Then We shall save those who were God-fearing, and leave the wrongdoers in it, kneeling]. You are thus in certainty regarding the arrival (wurūd), and in doubt regarding deliverance. So instill within your heart the terror of that place of arrival — perhaps you will thereby prepare yourself for deliverance from it.
23:108.section_title_en: Discourse on the Attributes of Hellfire, Its Terrors, and Its Fetters
23:108.anchors:
- Root: ورد (w-r-d)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning is "to arrive at water" — the primordial act of approaching a watering-place; from this derives the sense of arriving at any destination, whether desired or dreaded.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الورود أصله: قصد الماء" — its origin is the intent to reach water; then applied generally, and used of the Fire "على سبيل الفظاعة" (by way of horrification), as in {وإن منكم إلا واردها} — the universal "arrival" at Hell is a divinely decreed certainty.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): ورد الماء — arriving at water to drink. Metaphorical (Majaz): وردت البلد — arriving at a land; ورد عليه أمر لم يطقه — an overwhelming matter descended upon him. Here, "al-wurūd" is majaz extended to the eschatological "arrival" at the Fire, a passage all must undergo.
- Root: جلد (j-l-d)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The skin or hide covering the body; جلد الكتاب — to cover a book with leather; جلدته بالسياط — to flog.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الجلد: قشر البدن" — the skin is the body's integument; in the Quranic verse {كلما نضجت جلودهم بدلناهم جلودا غيرها} [النساء/56], the renewal of skins is the renewal of the seat of pain, ensuring perpetual sensation.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: flaying, covering, stripping. Metaphorical: جلدته على هذا الأمر — compelled him. In this text, the literal sense governs: skins roasted, then replaced, so that torment never ceases.
- Root: ظلم (z-l-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Darkness, absence of light; also wrongdoing. The lexicographers note the moral-ontological link: injustice is a kind of darkness.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الظلمة: عدم النور" — darkness is the privation of light; used metaphorically for ignorance, polytheism, and transgression, as light is used for their opposites.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "الظلم ظلمات يوم القيامة" — wrongdoing is darknesses on the Day of Resurrection. Metaphorical: أرض مظلومة — land never before dug. Here, "zulumāt" (ظلمات) is used literally of Hell's physical darknesses, yet these are also the reified shadows of the inmates' own wrongs.
- Root: نار (n-w-r / n-w-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Fire; the root also yields نار — to kindle, to blaze up. The lexicons record the proverb: ورَيْتُ بك زنادي — "I struck fire from your flint," i.e., I perceived from you good counsel.
  * Al-Raghib (Al-Mufradat): Fire is the elemental reality of Hell, but its Quranic usage spans both physical flame and the "Fire of God kindled" which mounts over hearts [الهمزة/6-7] — the inward fire of heedlessness made outward.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: flame, burning. Metaphorical: نار الحرب — the fire of war. In this passage, the literal fire of Jahannam is described with maximal sensory concreteness, yet it remains the outward manifestation of the soul's own kindled crimes.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The rule governing the permissibility of interposing elements between a preposition and its object when the intervening phrase is semantically complete. Applied here in the periodic constructions where long descriptive clauses intervene between the initial vocative (يا أيها الغافل) and its eventual predicate, sustaining rhetorical tension across the entire passage.
23:108.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Remembrance of Death and Afterlife'

24:15.arabic: المعاصي بالجوارح ولذلك قال تعالى في مثله وتحسبونه هينا وهو عند الله عظيم فمن أين تعلم أن غيرك أعصى منك ثم لعله قد أخرت عقوبته إلى الآخرة وعجلت عقوبتك في الدنيا فلم لا تشكر الله تعالى على ذلك وهذا هو الوجه الثالث في الشكر وهو أنه ما من عقوبة إلا وكان يتصور أن تؤخر إلى الآخرة ومصائب الدنيا يتسلى عنها بأسباب أخر تهون المصيبة فيخف وقعها ومصيبة الآخرة تدوم وإن لم تدم فلا سبيل إلى تخفيفها بالتسلي إذ أسباب التسلي مقطوعة بالكلية في الآخرة عن المعذبين ومن عجلت عقوبته في الدنيا فلا يعاقب ثانيا إذ قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
24:15.english: You might say: "What you have mentioned concerning graces (niʿam) indicates that for God most high there is in every existing thing a grace — and this suggests that trial (balā') has no existence at all. So what then is the meaning of patience (ṣabr)? And if trial does exist, then what is the meaning of gratitude (shukr) for trial? For some claimants have asserted that we give thanks for trial, let alone for grace. So how is gratitude for trial conceivable? And how does one give thanks for that which one endures with patience? For patience in trial demands pain, while gratitude demands joy, and the two are mutually opposed. And what is the meaning of what you have mentioned — that for God most high there is in everything He has brought into existence a grace upon His servants?"
24:15.section_title_en: On the Reconciliation of Patience and Gratitude in the Face of Trial — Section 1018
24:15.anchors:
- Root: نعم (n-ʿ-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core sense of softness, ease, and well-being; al-Farahidi notes it as a name for the leopard and tiger, indicating inherent vigor in the state of grace.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "النعمة: الحالة الحسنة" — the goodly state; divided into absolute (mutlaqah) and restricted (muqayyadah), the former being felicity in the Hereafter (nearness to God) and faith in this world.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah) usage denotes the actual state of well-being; metaphorical (Majaz) extension applies to any beneficial circumstance, even apparent hardship, when considered relative to the recipient's ultimate good.
- Root: بلي (b-l-w)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Testing, affliction, and wear of the body; the root implies a state of being tried or proven.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Trial (balā') is that which tests one's state; its existence is affirmed alongside grace (niʿmah) as its contrary, for the absence of grace is a trial and the absence of trial is a grace.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal sense is calamity or hardship; metaphorical sense applies to any condition that, while painful in one respect, may be a vehicle for divine benefit in another.
- Root: صبر (ṣ-b-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Restraint and forbearance; al-Farahidi ties it to holding back the self from complaint.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Patience is the withholding of the soul from agitation and complaint; it is only commanded where the trial cannot be repelled by the servant's own effort.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal usage is enduring pain; metaphorical usage extends to steadfastness in obedience and abstention from sin, which are acts of patience toward the soul's base inclinations.
- Root: شكر (sh-k-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Gratitude as acknowledgment of benefit; al-Farahidi links it to fullness, as a full udder (shukrā).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الشكر: تصور النعمة وإظهارها" — gratitude is the conception of the grace and its manifestation; it is threefold: of the heart (perceiving the grace), of the tongue (praising the Benefactor), and of the limbs (rewarding the grace through obedience).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal sense is verbal and inward acknowledgment; metaphorical sense is the "grateful beast" (dābbah shakūr) that thrives on little fodder — so the servant thrives on little trial, seeing in it abundant divine favor.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — Used to delimit the scope of patience and gratitude: patience is restricted to unavoidable pain, while gratitude is focused on the relative good within that pain, preventing the logical contradiction of their simultaneous application.
24:15.topic: Al-Ghazali on purifying the character, moral diseases, and spiritual remedies, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

24:15.arabic: واحد كان يحسبه هينا وهو عند الله عظيم وقد مقته به وإذا كان هذا ممكنا كان على نفسه خائفا فإذا كان كل واحد من العابد والعالم خائفا على نفسه وقد كلف أمر نفسه لا أمر غيره فينبغي أن يكون الغالب عليه في حق نفسه الخوف وفي حق غيره الرجاء وذلك يمنعه من التكبر بكل حال فهذا العابد مع العالم فأما مع غير العالم فهم منقسمون في حقه إلى مستورين وإلى مكشوفين فينبغي أن لا يتكبر على المستور فلعله أقل عنه ذنوبا وأكثر منه عبادة وأشد منه حبا لله وأما المكشوف حاله إن لم يظهر لك من الذنوب إلا ما تزيد عليه
24:15.english: If the worshiper said that to a scholar who acts upon his knowledge — and this scholar is a wicked transgressor — then it is said to him: "Have you not known that good deeds erase evil deeds? And just as knowledge can be a proof against the scholar, so too can it be a means for him and an expiation for his sins. Each of the two is possible, and the reports (al-akhbār) have come attesting to that. And since this matter is hidden from him, it is not permissible for him to hold a scholar in contempt; rather, he must show humility toward him."
24:15.section_title_en: On the Humility of the Learned Toward the Open Sinner, and the Fear of the Final Outcome
24:15.anchors:
- Root: حسن (Ḥ-S-N)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of beauty and goodness, both in outward form and inward virtue; al-ḥasanāt are acts of beneficence and obedience.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-ḥasanah is that which brings joy to the soul and is praiseworthy in its consequence; its opposite is al-sayyi'ah (the evil deed). The verse {«إِنَّ الْحَسَنَاتِ يُذْهِبْنَ السَّيِّئَاتِ»} (Hūd 11:114) establishes the divinely ordained mechanism of expiation through good works.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) usage denotes intrinsic goodness; metaphorical (majāz) usage extends to acts that erase prior sins, as in the prophetic tradition cited here.
- Root: خطر (Kha-Ṭ-R)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To be in peril; khaṭar is the looming danger that makes one tremble for one's fate.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Khaṭar denotes the imminent threat of punishment; the one who is mushfiq (apprehensive) weighs the unseen consequences of his state.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: a spear's quivering threat; metaphorical: the soul's dread of the unknown decree (al-qaḍā' al-azalī).
- Root: ستر (S-T-R)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To cover, conceal; mastūr is one whose sins are veiled from public view.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-sitr is the divine concealment of faults, a mercy that prevents presumption of another's inferiority.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical covering; metaphorical: the hidden state of a person's moral condition, contrasted with makshūf (exposed).
- Sibawayh Rule: Bāb al-ḥaṣr wa-al-taqyīd bi-innamā (Restriction and Focused Predication) — The conditional structures (fa-in qāla... fa-in qulta...) and the restrictive phrasing (fa-lā yajūz... bal yajibu) govern the logical progression, binding each hypothetical objection to its necessary response.
24:15.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Remembrance of Death and Afterlife'

24:25.arabic: قال وأن الله هو الحق المبين اللهم فصل على محمد عبدك ورسولك ونبيك وحبيبك وأمينك وخيرتك وصفوتك بأفضل ما صليت به على أحد من خلقك اللهم واجعل صلواتك ومعافاتك ورحمتك على سيد المرسلين وخاتم النبيين وإمام المتقين محمد قائد الخير وإمام الخير ورسول الرحمة اللهم قرب زلفته وعظم برهانه وكرم مقامه وابعثه مقاما محمودا يغبطه به الأولون وألاخرون وانفعنا بمقامه المحمود يوم القيامة واخلفه فينا في الدنيا والآخرة وبلغه الدرجة والوسيلة في الجنة اللهم صلي على محمد وعلى آل محمد وبارك على محمد وع
24:25.english: O people! Whoever worshipped Muhammad — then Muhammad has died. And whoever worshipped God — then God is Living, He dies not. And God has already sent forward to you in His command — so do not call upon him out of anguish (jazaʿan). For God, Mighty and Majestic, has chosen for His Prophet ﷺ what is with Him over what is with you, and has taken him to His reward, and has left among you His Book and the Sunnah of His Prophet ﷺ. Whoever clings to both has recognized (ʿarafa), and whoever separates between them has denied (ankara). {«يا أيها الذين آمنوا كونوا قوامين بالقسط»} — "O you who believe, be steadfast in justice" {Q. 5:8}. Let not Satan distract you by the death of your Prophet, nor seduce you away from your religion. Combat Satan with goodness and you will overcome him; do not grant him respite, lest he overtake you and seduce you.
24:25.section_title_en: The Death of the Prophet ﷺ — Consolation and the Steadfastness of the Faithful
24:25.anchors:
- Root: حدث (ḥ-d-th)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To bring forth anew after non-existence; that which is newly originated (muḥdath).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Al-ḥudūth: the coming-to-be of a thing after it was not — whether accident or substance. Its creation (iḥdāth) belongs solely to God."
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "He is a youth of recent age (ḥadath)." Metaphorical: "ʿUmar was muḥaddath — one whose conjecture is true, as if things were spoken (ḥudditha) to him."
- Root: موت (m-w-t)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Death; the cessation of the vital faculty; contrasted with ḥayāt (life).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Death is the privation of life; for the Prophet ﷺ, it is the transition (intiqāl) to the highest companionship, not annihilation of his reality.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "He died." Metaphorical: "Death is the messenger (rasūl) of separation."
- Root: قدم (q-d-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To precede, to send forward; also "foot" — that by which one advances.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Qaddama" — to send forth (a deed) before one; God "sent forward" His Prophet to what is with Him, i.e., His reward.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "He advanced." Metaphorical: "He sent him ahead to honor (qāddama ilā karāmatihi)."
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Prepositional Interposition (Bāb al-faṣl bayna al-jār wa al-majrūr) — The periodic structure here (e.g., "وإن الله قد قدم إليكم في أمره") interposes the object of consolation between the verb and its complement, governing the listener's attention toward the divine decree rather than the human loss.
24:25.topic: Al-Ghazali on the journey of the soul, death, and the Hereafter, from 'Remembrance of Death and Afterlife'

24:41.arabic: وهو أحد والآصال التي ذكرها الله تعالى إذ قال ولله يسجد من في السموات والأرض طوعا وكرها وظلالهم بالغدو والآصال وإذا سجد لله عز وجل الجمادات فكيف يجوز أن يغفل العبد العاقل عن أنواع العبادات الورد السادس إذا دخل وقت العصر دخل وقت الورد السادس وهو الذي أقسم الله تعالى به فقال تعالى {والعصر} هذا أحد معنيي الآية وهو المراد بالآصال في أحد التفسيرين وهو العشي المذكور في قوله {وعشيا} وفي قوله {بالعشي والإشراق} وليس في هذا الورد صلاة إلا أربع ركعات بين الأذان والإقامة كما سبق في الظهر ثم يصلي الفرض ويشتغل بالأقسام الأربعة المذكورة
24:41.english: I say: And just as knowledge and remembrance are the nourishment of the heart, which can never be cut off from it, so too the measure of moderation is this; and deficiency from it may lead to the disturbance of the body — except for one who accustoms himself to wakefulness gradually, for he may train himself upon it without disturbance. And this litany (wird) is among the longest of the litanies and the most delightful for the worshippers, and it is one of the "evenings and mornings" (al-āṣāl) which God Most High mentioned when He said: {«ولله يسجد من في السموات والأرض طوعا وكرها وظلالهم بالغدو والآصال»} "And to God prostrates whoever is in the heavens and the earth, willingly or unwillingly, and their shadows, in the mornings and the evenings" (Q. 13:15). And when inanimate objects prostrate to God, Mighty and Majestic, how then can the intelligent servant be heedless of the varieties of worship?
24:41.section_title_en: The Seventh Daily Litany (Al-Wird al-Sābiʿ): The Time of Sunset — The Completion of the Day's Litanies and Self-Accounting
24:41.anchors:
- Root: ورد (warada)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The root denotes arriving at water, seeking it, and drinking from it; also the portion or share of water allotted for drinking at a specific time.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الورود أصله: قصد الماء" — the core meaning is the intentional approach to water; the litany (wird) is the appointed portion of devotional recitation, likened to the daily share of water that a person must take to sustain life.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): the act of arriving at water. Metaphorical (Majaz): "ورد علي كتاب سرني مورده" — a book arrived upon me whose arrival pleased me; likewise, the wird is the arrival of the appointed time for worship, and the soul's approach to the fountain of divine remembrance.
- Root: عصر (ʿaṣr)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The root denotes pressing, squeezing, and extracting; also the time of afternoon, so called because it is the pressing of the day's end.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The ʿaṣr is the latter part of the day; God swore by it in {«والعصر»} (Q. 103:1), indicating its great merit.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the afternoon time. Metaphorical: the pressing of one's life — as the day is pressed at its end, so the life of man is pressed at its term.
- Root: غرب (gharaba)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The root denotes disappearance, absence, and setting; the sun's setting (ghurūb) is its concealment from the eye.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The setting of the sun marks the boundary between the day's works and the night's; it is the terminus of the visible world's diurnal cycle.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the sun's descent below the horizon. Metaphorical: the setting of the sun of life — the death of man, after which there is no rising.
- Root: حاسب (ḥāsaba)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The root denotes reckoning, counting, and taking account; muḥāsabah is the mutual reckoning between two parties.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Self-accounting (muḥāsabat al-nafs) is the soul's reckoning with itself over its deeds before the Day of Reckoning, for "one who reckons himself before he is reckoned" is among the wise.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the arithmetic counting of sums. Metaphorical: the soul's audit of its own works, weighing the day's deeds against the standard of the Sacred Law.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The rule governing the separation of the prepositional phrase from its governing verb, as in the construction "فسبحان الله حين تمسون" where the adverbial clause is interposed to emphasize the temporal specification of the act of glorification.
24:41.topic: Al-Ghazali on constant remembrance of God and contemplative invocations, from 'Remembrance of Death and Afterlife'

25:27.arabic: قدمت لحياتي يا ليتني اتخذت مع الرسول سبيلا يا ويلتا ليتني لم أتخذ فلانا خليلا يا ليتني كنت ترابا يا ليتني كنت نسيا منسيا يا ليت أمي لم تلدني وعند ذلك تختطفك النيران والعياذ بالله وينادي المنادي {اخسؤوا فيها ولا تكلمون} فلا يبقى سبيل إلا الصياح والأنين والتنفس والاستغاثة فكيف ترى الآن عقلك وهذه الأخطار بين يديك فإن كنت غير مؤمن بذلك فما أطول مقامك مع الكفار في دركات جهنم وإن كنت به مؤمنا وعنه غافلا وبالاستعداد له متهاونا فما أعظم خسرانك وطغيانك وماذا ينفعك إيمانك إذا لم يبعثك ع
25:27.english: Then, after these terrors, reflect upon the saying of God Most High: {«On the Day We shall gather the righteous to the All-Merciful as a delegation, and drive the criminals to Hell as a thirsty herd»} and upon His saying: {«Then lead them to the path of Hellfire, and stop them, for they shall be questioned»}. For after these terrors, mankind is driven to the Bridge — and it is a bridge stretched across the surface of the Fire, sharper than a sword and finer than a hair. Whoever was upright in this world upon the straight path (al-ṣirāṭ al-mustaqīm) will pass lightly over the Bridge of the Hereafter and be saved. But whoever deviated from uprightness in this world, weighed down his back with heavy burdens (awzār) of sin, and disobeyed — he will stumble at the very first step of the Bridge and plummet down.
25:27.section_title_en: The Description of the Bridge (Ṣirāṭ) and the Redress of Grievances
25:27.anchors:
- Root: صرط (Ṣirāṭ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The root denotes the straight path, a road; lexically, al-ṣirāṭ is the clear, broad way.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In Quranic usage, al-ṣirāṭ al-mustaqīm is the path of truth and obedience leading to God, contrasted with the paths of error and perdition.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) for a physical bridge/road; metaphorical (majāz) for the moral and religious course of conduct in this world that determines one's passage in the hereafter.
- Root: زلل (Zalala)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To slip, stumble, or err; a foot slipping from its place.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Used both physically (slipping on a path) and morally (falling into sin and error); the Hereafter's slipping is the consequence of worldly deviation.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal for the foot's slip on the Bridge; metaphorical for deviation from the straight path in deeds and belief.
- Root: خطف (Khaṭafa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To snatch away swiftly and violently.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The angels of punishment snatch souls and bodies with hooks; denotes sudden seizure by divine decree.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal for the physical snatching by iron hooks (kalālīb); metaphorical for the sudden ruin caused by one's own works.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Interposition and Parenthetical Clauses (al-iʿtirāḍ) — The frequent vocative cries (e.g., "yā laytanī") and exclamatory interruptions (e.g., "fa-yā layta") are syntactically embedded as parenthetical invocations within the periodic narrative, preserving the rhetorical flow of lament without breaking the grammatical dependency of the surrounding clauses.
25:27.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Remembrance of Death and Afterlife'

25:43.arabic: تعالى ولا معبود غيره ومن اتخذ إلهه هواه فهو بعيد من الصدق في توحيده وأمره مخطر في نفسه فإن عجزت عن ذلك كله فكن محبا لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم حريصا على تعظيم سننه ومتشوقا إلى مراعاة قلوب الصالحين من أمته ومتبركا بأدعيتهم فعساك أن تنال من شفاعته أو شفاعتهم فتنجو بالشفاعة إن كنت قليل البضاعة
25:43.english: And on the authority of Ibn Masʿūd, may God be pleased with him, that the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "God will gather the first and the last for an appointed time on a known Day, standing for forty years, their eyes fixed heavenward, awaiting the verdict of judgment." And he mentioned the ḥadīth until he reached the time of the prostration of the believers. He said: "Then He will say to the believers: 'Raise your heads.' So they raise their heads, and they are given their light according to their deeds. Among them is one who is given his light like a great mountain, racing before him; among them is one who is given his light smaller than that; among them is one who is given his light like a palm tree; among them is one who is given his light smaller than that—until the last of them is a man who is given his light upon the toe of his foot. It shines once and dims once. When it shines, he steps forward with his foot and walks; when it darkens, he stands still." Then he mentioned their crossing over the Bridge (al-Ṣirāṭ) according to their light: among them is one who crosses like the blink of an eye; among them is one who crosses like lightning; among them is one who crosses like a cloud; among them is one who crosses like the shooting of stars; among them is one who crosses like the gallop of a horse; among them is one who crosses like the running of a man—until the one who was given his light upon the toe of his foot crosses, crawling on his face, hands, and feet. One hand is dragged while another clings; one foot is caught while another is dragged, and the fire touches his sides. He said: "He will not cease thus until he is delivered. When he is delivered, he stands over it (the fire), then says: 'Praise be to God! God has given me what He has not given anyone, for He saved me from it after I had seen it.' Then he is taken to a pool at the gate of Paradise and bathes therein." (2) And Anas ibn Mālik said: "I heard the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, say: 'The Bridge is like the edge of a sword or like the edge of a hair. The angels save the believing men and the believing women, and Gabriel, peace be upon him, takes hold of my waist, and I say: "O Lord, save, save!" The slipers and slippers among men and women on that Day are many.'" (3)
25:43.section_title_en: The Terrors of the Bridge (Ṣirāṭ) and the Reality of Fear
25:43.anchors:
- Root: نور (n-w-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of radiant light, illumination, and luminosity; the source of visibility.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Light is of two kinds: sensory (perceived by the eye) and intellectual/spiritual (perceived by the inner eye of insight). The light granted to the believers on the Day of Resurrection is a spiritual light (nūr maʿnawī) apportioned by divine justice according to their deeds, manifesting their degree of faith and works.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) usage refers to physical illumination; metaphorical (majāz) usage refers to clarity, guidance, and manifestation. Here, the "light" is a metaphorical extension of the believer's true faith and righteous action, made perceptible in the Hereafter.
- Root: خوف (kh-w-f)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Fear, dread, apprehension of a harmful or painful event.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Fear (khawf) is the anticipation of something disliked, based on a probable or certain sign. It is the opposite of security (amn). True fear is a cognitive and motivational state that drives one to avoid its object, not mere emotional softness.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) usage is the emotion of fear; metaphorical (majāz) usage, as in "a fearful road" (ṭarīq khāʾif), denotes a place or state that causes fear. Al-Ghazali here critiques the metaphorical "fear" of the foolish—mere verbal utterance without behavioral consequence.
- Root: قدم (q-d-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Foot; also precedence and advancement.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The foot (qadam) is the instrument of standing and walking; from it, concepts of precedence (taqaddum) and delay are derived. In the ḥadīth, the light placed on the toe (ibhām al-qadam) signifies the minimal degree of faith, barely sufficient for movement.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) usage is the physical foot; metaphorical (majāz) usage, as in "place it under your feet" (i.e., forgive it), indicates subjugation or minimal standing. Here, the toe's light is literal in the eschatological scene but symbolically denotes the weakest degree of saving faith.
- Root: حصن (ḥ-ṣ-n)
  * Lisan / Ayn: A fortress, an impregnable stronghold; that which protects its interior from penetration.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): A fortress (ḥiṣn) is a place of refuge; metaphorically, it applies to anything that provides protection, such as armor or a chaste woman. True protection from the terrors of the Hereafter is not a physical fortress but the sincere utterance of "lā ilāha illā Allāh."
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) usage is a fortified structure; metaphorical (majāz) usage, as in "he came carrying a fortress" (i.e., weapons), denotes any means of defense. Al-Ghazali employs this metaphorically: the only fortress against the terrors of the Hereafter is sincere monotheism.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The rule governing the separation of a preposition from its object by an intervening clause, as in "فأنى يغني عنه ذلك من السبع" (So how can that avail him against the lion?), where the syntactic structure emphasizes the futility of the verbal refuge.
25:43.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'Remembrance of Death and Afterlife'

25:43.arabic: قال الله تعالى {أفرأيت من اتخذ إلهه هواه} وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم أبغض إله عبد في الأرض
25:43.english: They have manipulated this term through specification (takhṣīṣ), not through transfer (naql) or conversion (taḥwīl), for they have restricted it to knowledge of obscure legal branches (furūʿ gharībah) in legal opinions (fatāwā), to grasping the subtleties of their underlying causes (ʿilal), to multiplying discourse concerning them, and to memorizing the doctrinal positions related to them. Whoever is more profound in this and more occupied with it is called "the most learned in fiqh" (al-afqah). Yet in the first era, the name fiqh was applied absolutely to knowledge of the path of the Hereafter, to knowing the subtleties of the maladies of the souls (āfāt al-nufūs), to the corrupters of deeds (mufsidāt al-aʿmāl), to the power of encompassing the pettiness of this world, to intense longing for the bliss of the Hereafter, and to the dominance of fear over the heart. What indicates this to you is His saying, Mighty and Majestic: {«ليتفقهوا في الدين ولينذروا قومهم إذا رجعوا إليهم»} [“That they may gain understanding in the religion and warn their people when they return to them”] (Q 9:122). What effects warning and intimidation is this very fiqh — not the subdivisions of divorce (ṭalāq), manumission (ʿitāq), imprecation (liʿān), salam contracts, and leases (ijārah). For that (latter) does not produce warning or intimidation; rather, total devotion to it perpetually hardens the heart and strips away godly fear (khashyah) from it, as we now observe in those wholly devoted to it.
25:43.section_title_en: The Revival of the Religious Sciences — Section 27: The Corruption of the Praiseworthy Names (Taḥrīf al-Asāmī al-Maḥmūdah)
25:43.anchors:
- Root: فقه (Fiqh)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core linguistic meaning of "understanding" (al-fahm) and "comprehension" (al-fahm ʿan al-shayʾ)
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Al-fiqh: attainment of knowledge of the unseen through a witnessed sign — it is more specific than ʿilm." Theological nuance: true fiqh is knowledge of the heart's maladies and the path to the Hereafter.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): "afqih ʿannī mā aqūl" — understand what I say. Metaphorical (majāz): technical restriction to legal rulings (furūʿ al-fatāwā) is a later convention, not the lexical or prophetic norm.
- Root: علم (ʿIlm)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Perception of a thing as it truly is; knowledge of the essence of a thing.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Two types: (1) perception of the essence of a thing; (2) judgment upon a thing affirming or negating something of it. The highest ʿilm is knowledge of God, His verses, and His acts.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "He is from the banners (aʿlām) of knowledge." Metaphorical: restriction of the title "scholar" (al-ʿālim) to the dialectician (al-munāẓir) is a corrupt specification (takhṣīṣ fāsid).
- Root: وحد (Waḥḥada)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To make one; to affirm unity.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Tawḥīd is affirming God's unity in essence, attributes, and acts — the highest degree being the vision that all things proceed from Him alone.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: utterance of "Lā ilāha illā Allāh." Metaphorical: the inner reality (al-lubāb) — seeing all affairs from God, cutting off attention from secondary causes.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب التخصيص والتقييد (Restriction and Specification) — The corruption of names occurs through takhṣīṣ (semantic restriction), not naql (lexical transfer). The grammarians' principle: a general term (al-ism al-ʿāmm) retains its full semantic range unless a valid sharʿī or linguistic evidence restricts it; arbitrary restriction by custom (ʿādat al-istimāl) is a rhetorical device of the devils among men and jinn.
25:43.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Mysteries of Prayer'

25:43.arabic: تعالى وقدره وإلى مثل هذا القلب الإشارة بقوله تعالى أرأيت من اتخذ إلهه هواه أفأنت تكون عليه وكيلا أم تحسب أن أكثرهم يسمعون أو يعقلون إن هم إلا كالأنعام بل هم أضل سبيلا وبقوله عز وجل لقد حق القول على أكثرهم فهم لا يؤمنون وبقوله سواء عليهم أأنذرتهم أم لم تنذرهم لا يؤمنون ورب قلب هذا حاله بالإضافة إلى بعض الشهوات كالذي يتورع عن بعض الأشياء ولكنه إذا رأى وجها حسنا لم يملك عينه وقلبه وطاش عقله وسقط مساك قلبه أو كالذي لا يملك نفسه فيما فيه الجاه والرياسة والكبر ولا يبقى معه مسكة للتثبت عند ظهور أسبابه أو كالذي لا يملك نفسه
25:43.english: Know that the heart, as we have mentioned, is surrounded by the attributes we have described, and the traces and states pour into it from the gateways we have set forth. It is as if it were a target perpetually struck from every side. When something afflicts it, it is affected by it; then it is struck from another side by that which opposes it, and so its state changes. If the devil descends upon it and calls it to passion (hawā), the angel descends upon it and turns it away from that. If one devil drags it toward evil, another devil drags it toward something else; and if one angel draws it toward good, another draws it toward something else. Thus at times it is contested between two angels, at times between two devils, and at times between an angel and a devil — it is never, ever left neglected. To this points the saying of the Exalted: {وَنُقَلِّبُ أَفْئِدَتَهُمْ وَأَبْصَارَهُمْ} (And We turn their hearts and their visions) {«الأنعام/110»}. And because the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) was privy to the wondrous handiwork of Allah the Exalted in the marvels of the heart and its overturning, he used to swear by it, saying: "No, by the Turner of the hearts." (1)
25:43.section_title_en: The Wonders of the Heart: Its States of Stability, Inclination, and Fluctuation Between the Two Attracting Forces
25:43.anchors:
- Root: قلب (q-l-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To turn a thing over, to revolve it, to divert it from one face to another; the heart is so named for its constant turning and fluctuation.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "قلب الشيء: تصريفه وصرفه عن وجه إلى وجه" — the heart's perpetual overturning is its very essence; its states are never fixed, and its rectitude or corruption follows its turning.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): "قلب الشيء قلبا: حوله عن وجهه" — physical overturning. Metaphorical (Majaz): "رجل قلب حول: يقلب الأمور ويحتال" — one who turns matters over and manages them; the heart's fluctuation between the two attractants is a real, continuous overturning.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The periodic structure of the opening sentence, with its cascading circumstantial clauses, requires careful tracking of the governing verb and its dependent states to preserve the causal sequence of the heart's affliction and response.
25:43.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Love, Longing, Intimacy and Contentment'

25:58.arabic: تحصنت بالله العظيم واستغثت بالحي الذي لا يموت اللهم احرسنا بعينك التي لا تنام واكنفنا بركنك الذي لا يرام اللهم ارحمنا بقدرتك علينا فلا نهلك وأنت ثقتنا ورجاؤنا اللهم أعطف علينا قلوب عبادك وإمائك برأفة ورحمة إنك أنت أرحم الراحمين الثامنة مهما علا نشزا من الأرض في الطريق فيستحب أن يكبر ثلاثا ثم يقول اللهم لك الشرف على كل شرف ولك الحمد على كل حال ومهما هبط سبح ومهما خاف الوحشة في سفره قال سبحان الله الملك القدوس رب الملائكة والروح جللت السموات بالعزة والجبروت
25:58.english: He ought to seek out a righteous companion, one who loves goodness and assists in it: if he forgets, the companion reminds him; if he remembers, the companion aids him; if he fears, the companion emboldens him; if he weakens, the companion strengthens him; if his breast narrows, the companion enlarges his patience. He should bid farewell to his resident companions, his brothers, and his neighbors — taking leave of them and seeking their supplications, for God Most High places goodness in their prayers. The Sunnah of farewell is to say: «أستودع الله دينك وأمانتك وخواتيم عملك» — "I entrust to God your religion, your trustworthiness, and the seal of your deeds." And he, peace and blessings be upon him, used to say to one intending travel: "In God's protection and His care — may God provide you with piety, forgive your sin, and direct you toward goodness wherever you may be."
25:58.section_title_en: The Book of the Etiquette of Travel — Section 199: On the Comprehensive Etiquette of the Journey (From Provisioning to Guarding)
25:58.anchors:
- Root: س ف ر (S-F-R)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "السفر: كشف الغطاء" — unveiling, uncovering; the traveler is one who uncovers the veils of distant lands.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "السفر: كشف الغطاء، ويختص ذلك بالأعيان" — the journey is a literal uncovering of horizons, yet the spiritual journey unveils the soul's veils.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Haqiqah: "سافر سفرا بعيدا" (to travel far); Majaz: "وجه مسفر: مشرق سرورا" — a face radiant with joy, as the traveler's face brightens with divine trust.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — governing the permissible separation between the preposition and its object for rhetorical emphasis, as in the supplications' structural pauses.
25:58.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications, prayers, and their spiritual power, from 'Remembrance of Death and Afterlife'

25:58.arabic: وقرأ الخواص قوله تعالى {وتوكل على الحي الذي لا يموت} إلى آخر فقال ما ينبغي للعبد بعدد هذه الآية أن يلجأ إلى أحد غير الله تعالى وقيل لبعض العلماء في منامه من وثق بالله تعالى فقد أحرز قوته وقال بعض العلماء لا يشغلك المضمون لك من الرزق عن المفروض عليك من العمل فتضيع أمر آخرتك ولا تنال من الدنيا إلا ما قد كتب الله لك وقال يحيى بن معاذ في وجود العبد الرزق من غير طلب دلالة على أن الرزق مأمور بطلب العبد وقال إبراهيم بن أدهم سألت بعض الرهبان من أين تأكل فقال لي ليس هذا العلم عندي ولكن سل ربي من أين يطعمني
25:58.english: His protection and His sanctuary, and He is a Wise One who does not fall short in managing the affairs of one who entrusts His management to Him. And He, exalted is He, said: {إِنَّ الَّذِينَ تَدْعُونَ مِن دُونِ اللَّهِ عِبَادٌ أَمْثَالُكُمْ} — "Indeed, those you call upon besides Allah are servants like yourselves" — thereby making clear that everything other than Allah, exalted is He, is a subjugated servant, whose need is like your need; so how then can one rely upon him?
25:58.section_title_en: Section 1103 — On the First Part Concerning Divine Unity (Tawḥīd) and the Perfection of Trust in Allah
25:58.anchors:
- Root: وكل (W-K-L)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of delegating, entrusting, and appointing another as a deputy or guardian over one's affairs.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "التوكيل: أن تعتمد على غيرك وتجعله نائبا عنك" — Trust (tawakkul) is to rely upon another and make him a deputy; the true Wakīl is Allah alone, as in {وَكَفَىٰ بِاللَّهِ وَكِيلًا}.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): "توكل على الله ولا تتكل على غيره" — reliance on Allah. Metaphorical (majāz): "وكل همه بكذا" — one who delegates his care to a thing, implying abandonment by Allah of those who turn to other than Him.
- Root: عبد (ʿ-B-D)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Servitude, submission, and humble obedience; the created being as subjugated servant.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "العبودية: إظهار التذلل، والعبادة أبلغ منها" — servitude is the display of humility; worship is its utmost degree, due only to Allah. All besides Allah are "عباد أمثالكم" — servants like yourselves, incapable of independent provision.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "عبد بين العبودية" — a slave bound in servitude. Metaphorical: "استعبده الطمع" — greed enslaves a man, just as reliance on creatures enslaves the heart.
- Root: رسل (R-S-L)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Sending forth with ease and gentleness; a messenger dispatched with a message.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "أصل الرسل: الانبعاث على التؤدة" — the root is gentle dispatch; the messenger is one sent, and the verse {وَأْمُرْ أَهْلَكَ بِالصَّلَاةِ} is a divine sending of command.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "أرسل الله في الأمم رسلا" — Allah sent messengers to nations. Metaphorical: "أرسل الله عليهم العذاب" — Allah loosed punishment upon them, showing His sole agency.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The rule governing the separation of the preposition from its object for rhetorical emphasis, as in "على ربهم يتوكلون" where the preposition "على" is fronted before its governed noun "ربهم" to highlight exclusive reliance, a construction permissible when the clause is semantically complete and the fronting serves emphasis (takhrīṣ).
25:58.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Monotheism and Reliance'

26:88.arabic: على النار يفتنون يوم لا ينفع مال ولا بنون يوم لا ينفع الظالمين معذرتهم ولهم اللعنة ولهم سوء الدار يوم ترد فيه المعاذير وتبلى السرائر وتظهر الضمائر وتكشف الأستار يوم تخشع فيه الأبصار وتسكن الأصوات ويقل فيه الالتفات وتبرز الخفيات وتظهر الخطيئات يوم يساق العباد ومعهم الأشهاد ويشيب الصغير ويسكر الكبير فيومئذ وضعت الموازين ونشرت الدواوين وبرزت الجحيم وأغلى الحميم وزفرت النار ويئس الكفار وسعرت النيران وتغيرت الألوان وخرس اللسان ونطقت جوارح الإنسان فيا أيها الإنسان ما غرك بربك الكريم حيث أغلق
26:88.english: So prepare yourself, O wretched one, for this Day of immense magnitude, of prolonged duration, of overwhelming dominion, whose appointed time is near — a Day when you shall see the heaven split asunder, and the stars scattered in its terror, and the shining planets extinguished, and the sun folded up, and the mountains set in motion, and the pregnant camels neglected, and the wild beasts gathered together, and the seas set ablaze, and the souls paired with their bodies, and the Hellfire ignited, and Paradise brought near, and the mountains pulverized, and the earth stretched out — a Day when you shall see the earth shaken with its quaking, and the earth casts forth its burdens. On that Day shall people issue forth in scattered groups to be shown their deeds — a Day when the earth and the mountains are lifted and crushed with a single crushing. Then on that Day the Imminent Event shall come to pass, and the heaven shall split open, for on that Day it shall be frail, and the angels shall be at its edges, and eight shall bear the Throne of your Lord above them on that Day. On that Day you shall be presented — no secret of yours shall remain hidden. A Day when the mountains shall move and you shall see the earth laid bare — a Day when the earth shall be shaken with a violent shaking, and the mountains crumbled to dust, becoming scattered particles — a Day when people shall be like scattered moths, and the mountains like carded wool — a Day when every nursing mother shall forget what she nursed, and every pregnant female shall cast down her burden, and you shall see people drunk, yet they are not drunk, but the chastisement of God is severe — a Day when the earth shall be changed to other than this earth, and the heavens, and they shall appear before God, the One, the All-Compelling — a Day when the mountains shall be blown away as dust, leaving a level, bare plain, wherein you see no crookedness nor curve — a Day when you see the mountains and suppose them solid, yet they pass by like the passing of clouds — a Day when the heaven shall split open and become rosy like molten oil. Then on that Day no human nor jinn shall be asked about his sin. A Day when the disobedient shall be prevented from speech, and shall not be asked about their crimes, but shall be seized by their forelocks and their feet — a Day when every soul shall find what it did of good brought forth present, and what it did of evil, wishing that between it and that evil there were a far distance — a Day when every soul shall know what it has sent ahead, and shall witness what it has forwarded and what it has left behind — a Day when tongues shall be struck mute and the bodily members shall speak — a Day whose mention turned the hair of the Master of the Messengers white, when al-Ṣiddīq (may God be pleased with him) said to him: "I see that you have turned white-haired, O Messenger of God." He said: "Sūrat Hūd and its sisters have made me white-haired" — namely, al-Wāqiʿah, al-Mursalāt, ʿAmma Yatasāʾalūn, and Idhā al-Shamsu Kuwwirat.
26:88.section_title_en: The Names and Attributes of the Day of Resurrection — An Exhortation to the Negligent
26:88.anchors:
- Root: يوم (yawm)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "اليوم: وقت طلوع الشمس إلى غروبها، وقد يعبر به عن مدة من الزمان أي مدة كانت" — the day as a temporal span, extended metaphorically to any epoch or era.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "اليوم يعبر به عن وقت طلوع الشمس إلى غروبها. وقد يعبر به عن مدة من الزمان أي مدة كانت" — theological usage denotes the appointed time of reckoning, magnified by divine attribution (أيام الله).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): a measured solar period. Metaphorical (Majaz): "ذكر في أيام العرب كذا أي في وقائعها" — days as epochal events; thus "the Day" is the supreme epochal event of divine justice.
- Root: نفس (nafs)
  * Lisan / Ayn: النفس: الروح والذات — the self, soul, or very essence.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "النفس: الروح... وقوله: ويحذركم الله نفسه فنفسه: ذاته" — nafs as the innermost reality of a being; in the eschatological context, souls are "paired" (زوجت) with bodies for judgment.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the soul as life-principle. Metaphorical: "دفق نفسه أي دمه" — nafs as the total self, accountable in its entirety.
- Root: ارض (arḍ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: الأرض: الجرم المقابل للسماء — the earth as the corporeal substratum beneath the heavens.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الأرض: الجرم المقابل للسماء... ويعبر بها عن أسفل الشيء" — the earth as the lowest register of creation, subject to total transformation on that Day.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the physical earth. Metaphorical: "تأرض فلان: لزم الأرض" — to cling low; on that Day the earth itself is leveled, flattened, and replaced.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد (Restriction & Focused Predication) — The repeated "يوم" clauses function as temporal restrictors (ẓurūf) binding each predicate to that single, all-encompassing moment; the accumulation of names (أسامي) serves not as mere repetition but as focused predication upon the multifarious realities of a single event.
26:88.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Remembrance of Death and Afterlife'

27:16.arabic: عليه وسلم فقال يا أيها الناس إن لكل شيء مطية ومطية المرء العقل وأحسنكم دلالة ومعرفة بالحجة أفضلكم عقلا (6) وعن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه قال لما رجع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم من غزوة أحد سمع الناس يقولون فلان أشجع من فلان وفلان أبلى ما لم يبل فلان ونحو هذا فقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أما هذا فلا علم لكم به قالوا وكيف ذلك يا رسول الله فقال صلى الله عليه وسلم إنهم قاتلوا على قدر ما قسم الله لهم من العقل وكانت نصرتهم ونيتهم على قدر عقولهم فأصيب منهم من أصيب على منازل شتى
27:16.english: It is narrated from Anas (may Allah be pleased with him) who said: A group of people praised a man before the Prophet (peace be upon him) until they exaggerated. The Prophet (peace be upon him) said: **"How is the man's intellect?"** They said: "We inform you of his diligence in worship and his various kinds of goodness, yet you ask us about his intellect?" The Prophet (peace be upon him) said: **"Indeed, the foolish man attains through his ignorance more corruption than the wickedness of the wicked man attains through his wickedness. And indeed, the servants will be raised on the Day of Resurrection in the degrees of nearness (al-zulfā) to their Lord only according to the measure of their intellects."**
27:16.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'Remembrance of Death and Afterlife'

27:65.arabic: وهو أحد والآصال التي ذكرها الله تعالى إذ قال ولله يسجد من في السموات والأرض طوعا وكرها وظلالهم بالغدو والآصال وإذا سجد لله عز وجل الجمادات فكيف يجوز أن يغفل العبد العاقل عن أنواع العبادات الورد السادس إذا دخل وقت العصر دخل وقت الورد السادس وهو الذي أقسم الله تعالى به فقال تعالى {والعصر} هذا أحد معنيي الآية وهو المراد بالآصال في أحد التفسيرين وهو العشي المذكور في قوله {وعشيا} وفي قوله {بالعشي والإشراق} وليس في هذا الورد صلاة إلا أربع ركعات بين الأذان والإقامة كما سبق في الظهر ثم يصلي الفرض ويشتغل بالأقسام الأربعة المذكورة
27:65.english: I say: And just as knowledge and remembrance are the nourishment of the heart, which can never be cut off from it, so too the measure of moderation is this; and deficiency from it may lead to the disturbance of the body — except for one who accustoms himself to wakefulness gradually, for he may train himself upon it without disturbance. And this litany (wird) is among the longest of the litanies and the most delightful for the worshippers, and it is one of the "evenings and mornings" (al-āṣāl) which God Most High mentioned when He said: {«ولله يسجد من في السموات والأرض طوعا وكرها وظلالهم بالغدو والآصال»} "And to God prostrates whoever is in the heavens and the earth, willingly or unwillingly, and their shadows, in the mornings and the evenings" (Q. 13:15). And when inanimate objects prostrate to God, Mighty and Majestic, how then can the intelligent servant be heedless of the varieties of worship?
27:65.section_title_en: The Seventh Daily Litany (Al-Wird al-Sābiʿ): The Time of Sunset — The Completion of the Day's Litanies and Self-Accounting
27:65.anchors:
- Root: ورد (warada)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The root denotes arriving at water, seeking it, and drinking from it; also the portion or share of water allotted for drinking at a specific time.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الورود أصله: قصد الماء" — the core meaning is the intentional approach to water; the litany (wird) is the appointed portion of devotional recitation, likened to the daily share of water that a person must take to sustain life.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): the act of arriving at water. Metaphorical (Majaz): "ورد علي كتاب سرني مورده" — a book arrived upon me whose arrival pleased me; likewise, the wird is the arrival of the appointed time for worship, and the soul's approach to the fountain of divine remembrance.
- Root: عصر (ʿaṣr)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The root denotes pressing, squeezing, and extracting; also the time of afternoon, so called because it is the pressing of the day's end.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The ʿaṣr is the latter part of the day; God swore by it in {«والعصر»} (Q. 103:1), indicating its great merit.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the afternoon time. Metaphorical: the pressing of one's life — as the day is pressed at its end, so the life of man is pressed at its term.
- Root: غرب (gharaba)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The root denotes disappearance, absence, and setting; the sun's setting (ghurūb) is its concealment from the eye.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The setting of the sun marks the boundary between the day's works and the night's; it is the terminus of the visible world's diurnal cycle.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the sun's descent below the horizon. Metaphorical: the setting of the sun of life — the death of man, after which there is no rising.
- Root: حاسب (ḥāsaba)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The root denotes reckoning, counting, and taking account; muḥāsabah is the mutual reckoning between two parties.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Self-accounting (muḥāsabat al-nafs) is the soul's reckoning with itself over its deeds before the Day of Reckoning, for "one who reckons himself before he is reckoned" is among the wise.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the arithmetic counting of sums. Metaphorical: the soul's audit of its own works, weighing the day's deeds against the standard of the Sacred Law.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The rule governing the separation of the prepositional phrase from its governing verb, as in the construction "فسبحان الله حين تمسون" where the adverbial clause is interposed to emphasize the temporal specification of the act of glorification.
27:65.topic: Al-Ghazali on constant remembrance of God and contemplative invocations, from 'Remembrance of Death and Afterlife'

27:71.arabic: على الكافرين غير يسير} وقال تعالى {ويقولون متى هذا الوعد إن كنتم صادقين ما ينظرون إلا صيحة واحدة تأخذهم وهم يخصمون فلا يستطيعون توصية ولا إلى أهلهم يرجعون ونفخ في الصور فإذا هم من الأجداث إلى ربهم ينسلون قالوا يا ويلنا من بعثنا من مرقدنا هذا ما وعد الرحمن وصدق المرسلون} فلو لم يكن بين يدي الموتى إلا هول تلك النفخة لكان ذلك جديرا بأن يتقى فإنها نفخة وصيحة يصعق بها من في السموات والأرض يعنى يموتون بها إلا من شاء الله وهو بعض الملائكة ولذلك قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كيف أنعم وصاحب الصور قد التقم القرن وحنى الجبهة
27:71.english: The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: Allah the Exalted said: "The son of Adam has reviled Me, and he had no right to revile Me; and he has denied Me, and he had no right to deny Me. As for his reviling of Me, it is his saying that I have a son. And as for his denial of Me, it is his saying: 'He will never bring me back as He created me at first.'" {«شتمني ابن آدم وما ينبغي له أن يشتمني وكذبني وما ينبغي له أن يكذبني...»}
27:71.section_title_en: On the Terrors of the Trumpet-Blast and the Awakening for the Resurrection
27:71.anchors:
- Root: نفخ (N-F-Kh)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To blow into a thing, to inflate; the breath of wind entering a vessel or body.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The divine act of breathing spirit into creation {«ونفخت فيه من روحي»}; here, the eschatological blast that annihilates and then revives all beings.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah) usage of blowing into the Trumpet (الصور); metaphorical extension to the "blast of spring" reviving the earth—here applied to the two cosmic blasts of death and resurrection.
- Root: صور (S-W-R)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Form, image, shape; also a horn or trumpet (the instrument of the blast).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The perceptible form of bodies and the intelligible form of souls; here, the Trumpet (الصور) as the instrument of divine command that re-forms and re-shapes creation.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the horn (القرن) held by Israfil; metaphorical: the "inclination" (صورة) of hearts toward terror and anticipation.
- Root: موت (M-W-T)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Death as the cessation of life; the state of the corpse.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Death as the separation of the soul from the body; the "first death" of the blast and the "second death" of the wicked.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical death; metaphorical: the "death" of the heart through heedlessness, and the reviving of dead lands by rain—here, the reviving of bodies by the second blast.
- Root: قبر (Q-B-R)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The grave as the abode of the dead; burial.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The grave as the intermediate state (barzakh) before resurrection; {«حتى زرتم المقابر»} as a metaphor for death.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the grave and its inhabitants; metaphorical: the "raising of the nose" (قبراه) of the proud—contrasted here with the humility of the dead rising from their graves.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — Used to emphasize that true faith is not mere verbal assent but heartfelt conviction, as in "إنما فتور البواطن... لقلة الفهم" (The languor of the inner selves is only due to the lack of understanding).
27:71.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'Remembrance of Death and Afterlife'

27:87.arabic: والبلاء إلا من شاء الله وقال اعلموا أن هذا زمان لا ينال أحد فيه النجاة إلا بذبح نفسه وقتلها بالجوع والسهر والجهد وقال ما مر على وجه الأرض أحد شرب من هذا الماء حتى روي فسلم من المعصية وإن شكر الله تعالى فكيف الشبع من الطعام وسئل حكيم بأي قيد أقيد نفسي قال قيدها بالجوع والعطش وذللها بإخمال الذكر وترك العز وصغرها بوضعها تحت أرجل أبناء الآخرة واكسرها بترك زي القراء عن ظاهرها وانج من آفاتها بدوام سوء الظن بها واصحبها بخلاف هواها وكان عبد الواحد بن زيد يقسم بالله تع
27:87.english: The Messenger of God, peace be upon him, said: "Strive against your souls with hunger and thirst, for the reward in that is like the reward of the warrior striving in the path of God. And there is no deed more beloved to God than hunger and thirst." (1) And Ibn 'Abbas said: The Prophet, peace be upon him, said: "He who fills his belly shall not enter the kingdom of heaven." (2) And it was said: O Messenger of God, which person is most excellent? He said: "He whose food is little, and whose laughter is little, and who is content with what covers his nakedness." (3) And the Prophet, peace be upon him, said: "The master of deeds is hunger, and the abasement of the soul, and the wearing of wool." (4) And Abu Sa'id al-Khudri said: The Messenger of God, peace be upon him, said: "Wear, eat, and drink in half of the belly, for that is a part of prophethood." (5) And al-Hasan said: The Prophet, peace be upon him, said: "Reflection is half of worship, and little food is the whole of worship." (6) And al-Hasan also said: The Messenger of God, peace be upon him, said: "The most excellent of you in station before God on the Day of Resurrection is the one among you who is longest in hunger and reflection upon God, Glorified be He. And the most hateful of you to God, Mighty and Majestic, on the Day of Resurrection is every sleepy, gluttonous, drink-loving person." (1)
27:87.section_title_en: The Book of the Revival of the Religious Sciences — Section 639: On the Excellence of Hunger and Thirst, and the Blameworthiness of Satiety
27:87.anchors:
- Root: جوع (J-W-')
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root meaning: hunger, emptiness of the stomach, famine (makhmasah); the state of one who abstains from food.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Hunger is the pain afflicting the living being from the emptiness of the stomach; it is a spiritual discipline that severs the soul's attachment to corporeal appetites, aligning with the laṭīfah's (subtle divine reality) purification from bodily preoccupations.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (haqiqah): physical hunger from lack of food. Metaphorical (majaz): "hunger of the heart" — the soul's yearning for God, as in "I hunger for my family"; here, the Prophet's voluntary hunger is a majaz for spiritual elevation, not mere deprivation.
- Root: عله (gh-dh-')
  * Lisan / Ayn: Root meaning: to feed, nourishment, provision (ghidhā'); the intake that sustains the body.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Sustenance is that which maintains the corporeal substance (jawhar) for obedience; excess nourishment (shib') dulls the heart's perception, while measured intake preserves the subtle reality (laṭīfah) for divine knowledge.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: food as physical sustenance. Metaphorical: "feeding the heart" with remembrance (dhikr) versus "killing the heart" with excess — the Prophet's simile of the heart as a crop (zar') drowned by excessive water.
- Root: رسل (R-S-L)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Root meaning: to send forth gently, to dispatch; a messenger (rasūl) sent with a mission.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The root implies gentle dispatch and measured movement; here, the "messengers" of the prophets (ulu al-'azm) who endured hunger as a sent discipline, and the believer's self-sending (irsāl) toward God through voluntary abstinence.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: sending a message. Metaphorical: "sending the soul" (irsāl al-nafs) on the path of hunger as a means of approach to God — the Prophet's statement that hunger is a "part of prophethood" (juz' min al-nubuwwah).
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — Governing the Prophet's statements like "Sayyid al-a'māl al-jū'" (The master of deeds is hunger), where the predicate is restricted to a single virtue, emphasizing its exclusive supremacy over other acts.
27:87.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Remembrance of Death and Afterlife'

27:88.arabic: ذلك فقال {وترى الجبال تحسبها جامدة وهي تمر مر السحاب صنع الله الذي أتقن كل شيء} إشارة إلى أن القلب مضطرب جائل في الملكوت والجوارح متأدبة في الظاهر ساكنة وقال أبو الحسن محمد بن أحمد وكان بالبصرة صحبت سهل بن عبد الله ستين سنة فما رأيته تغير عند شيء كان يسمعه من الذكر أو القرآن فلما كان في آخر عمره قرأ رجل بين يديه {فاليوم لا يؤخذ منكم فدية} الآية فرأيته قد ارتعد وكاد يسقط فلما عاد إلى حاله سألته عن ذلك فقال نعم يا حبيبي قد ضعفنا وكذلك سمع مرة قوله تعالى {الملك يومئذ الحق للرحمن} فاضطرب فسأله ابن سالم وك
27:88.english: And it is related that Moses — peace be upon him — was preaching among the Children of Israel, and one of them tore his garment or his shirt. So God — exalted be He — revealed to Moses — peace be upon him: "Say to him: Tear for Me your heart, and do not tear your garment."
27:88.section_title_en: The Revival of the Religious Sciences — Section 517: On the Steadfastness of the Strong in the Face of Ecstatic Samaʿ, and the Degrees of Manifestation and Restraint
27:88.anchors:
- Root: قلب (q-l-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To turn over, to overturn, to transform from one state to another; the heart as that which is perpetually fluctuating and being overturned between states.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "قلب الشيء: تصريفه وصرفه عن وجه إلى وجه" — the heart's turning and overturning is its being diverted from one disposition to another. The heart (qalb) is so named for its constant fluctuation (taqallub) between states.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): "قلب الشيء قلبا: حوله عن وجهه" — to turn a thing from its face. Metaphorical (Majaz): "قلب المعلم الصبيان: صرفهم إلى بيوتهم" — to turn pupils back to their homes; and "رجل قلب حول: يقلب الأمور ويحتال" — a man who turns matters over and manages them. Here, the heart's being "split" (inshaqqa) and its "turning" (taqallub) in the unseen realm (malakūt) are majaz for the soul's profound transformation.
- Root: ظهر (ẓ-h-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The back; the outward, visible surface as opposed to the hidden interior.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الظهر الجارحة" — the back as a bodily limb; used metaphorically for the outward aspect of the earth: "ظهر الأرض وبطنها" — its surface and its interior.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "رجل مظهر: قوي الظهر" — a man strong of back. Metaphorical: "قلبت الأمر ظهرا لبطن" — to turn the matter over, back and belly, i.e., to examine it thoroughly. In this section, the "outward" (zāhir) is the domain of the bodily members (jawāriḥ) which must be restrained, while the "inward" (bāṭin) is the domain of the heart's ecstasy (wajd).
- Root: حول (ḥ-w-l)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To change, to turn, to shift from one state to another; power and capacity to effect change.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "أصل الحول تغير الشيء وانفصاله عن غيره" — the root meaning is the changing of a thing and its separation from another. "حال بيني وبينك كذا" — something intervened between me and you.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "حال عليه الحول" — a year passed over it. Metaphorical: "لقحت الحرب عن حيال" — war conceived after a period of barrenness. Here, "ḥāl" (state/condition) and "taḥawwul" (transformation) denote the changing spiritual conditions that assail the heart, and the power (ḥawl) to restrain the outward members.
- Root: نفس (n-f-s)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The self, the soul; breath; that which is precious and valued.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "النفس: الروح" — the self is the spirit; "نفسه: ذاته" — His Self is His Essence. The soul is that which is breathed out and drawn in, and by extension, the living self.
