  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "شيء نفيس ومنفس" — a precious thing. Metaphorical: "دفق نفسه أي دمه" — he poured out his self, i.e., his blood. In this text, "nafsahu" (his self/soul) departs at death when the heart is split by suppressed ecstasy.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين المبتدأ والخبر (Interposition between Subject and Predicate) — The periodic structure of al-Ghazali's conditional sentences (fa-in qulta... fa-'lam) follows the classical pattern of protasis and apodosis, where the apodosis is introduced by the particle fa- to mark the resumption of the main clause after a lengthy conditional protasis, preserving syntactic cohesion across extended theological arguments.
27:88.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Remembrance of Death and Afterlife'

28:70.arabic: الشكر فى السموات والأرض وله الحمد فى الأولى والآخرة والصلاة على محمد ذي المعجزات الظاهرة والآيات الباهرة وعلى آله وأصحابه وسلم تسليما كثيرا أما بعد فجدير بمن الموت مصرعه والتراب مضجعه والدود أنيسه ومنكر ونكير جليسه والقبر مقره وبطن الأرض مستقره والقيامة موعده والجنة أو النار مورده أن لا يكون له فكر إلا فى الموت ولا ذكر إلا له ولا استعداد إلا لأجله ولا تدبير إلا فيه ولا تطلع إلا إليه ولا تعريج إلا عليه ولا اهتمام إلا به ولا حول إلا حوله ولا انتظار وتربص إلا له وحقيق بأن يعد نفسه من الموتى ويراها
28:70.english: To proceed: Worthy is one whose place of downfall is death, whose bed is the dust, whose companion is the worm, whose boon-companions are Munkar and Nakīr, whose abode is the grave, whose resting-place is the belly of the earth, whose appointed time is the Resurrection, and whose destination is Paradise or the Fire — that he should have no thought except of death, no remembrance except of it, no preparation except for it, no deliberation except concerning it, no aspiration except toward it, no lingering except upon it, no concern except with it, no power except around it, and no waiting or tarrying except for it. And it is fitting that he should count himself among the dead and see himself among the inhabitants of the graves, for everything that is coming is near, and the distant is only that which is not coming. The Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "The shrewd one (al-kayyis) is he who subdues his soul and works for what comes after death" (1). And preparation for a thing will not be facilitated except upon the renewal of its remembrance in the heart, and its remembrance is not renewed except through recollection by lending ear to those things that remind of it and by looking upon those things that alert to it.
28:70.section_title_en: The Book of the Remembrance of Death and What Follows It — Introduction and Opening Homily
28:70.anchors:
- Root: موت (m-w-t)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root denotes cessation of vital faculty; death as transition, not annihilation.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Death is the divinely ordained terminus of corporeal life, gateway to reckoning; "أماته فأقبره" {«عبس/ 21»} implies divine disposal of the deceased.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: bodily death and burial. Metaphorical: "أحيا الله البلد الميت" — revival of barren land; death of hearts through heedlessness.
- Root: قبر (q-b-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Grave as the resting place of the dead; "المقبرة" as the site of interment.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "حتى زرتم المقابر" {«التكاثر/ 2»} — metonymy for death itself; the grave as prelude to resurrection.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: burial of the deceased. Metaphorical: "رفع قبراه" — the haughty one who raises his nose like a grave-mound, signifying pride.
- Root: حمد (ḥ-m-d)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Praise predicated upon volitional excellence; gratitude for beneficence.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): True praise (ḥamd) is due solely to God, whose acts are pure beneficence; distinct from mere thanks (shukr) for favors received.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "أحمد الله بجميع محامده" — praising God with all praises. Metaphorical: "أحمدت صنيعه" — approving an act as praiseworthy.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The periodic opening "الحمد لله الذي..." employs a suspended genitive construction (جار ومجرور) with a relative clause (صلة الموصول) that permits extended expansion, governing the entire homiletic sequence that follows.
28:70.topic: Al-Ghazali on the journey of the soul, death, and the Hereafter, from 'Remembrance of Death and Afterlife'

29:57.arabic: وقال بعض الصوفية كنت أقرأ ليلة هذه الآية {كل نفس ذائقة الموت} فجعلت أرددها فإذا هاتف يهتف بي كم تردد هذه الآية فقد قتلت أربعة من الجن ما رفعوا رءوسهم إلى السماء منذ خلقوا وقال أبو علي المغازلي للشبلي ربما تطرق سمعي آية من كتاب الله تعالى فتجذبني إلى الإعراض عن الدنيا ثم أرجع إلى أحوالي وإلى الناس فلا أبقى على ذلك فقال ما طرق سمعك من القرآن فاجتذبك به إليه فذلك عطف منه عليك ولطف منه بك وإذا ردك إلى نفسك فهو شفقة منه عليك فإنه لا يصلح لك إلا التبري من الحول والقوة في التوجه إليه وسمع رجل من أه
29:57.english: Some of the Sufis said: "One night I was reciting this verse: {كُلُّ نَفْسٍ ذَائِقَةُ الْمَوْتِ} «Every soul shall taste death» [Q. 3:185]. I kept repeating it, and lo, a caller cried out to me: 'How long will you repeat this verse? You have killed four of the jinn who have not raised their heads to the sky since they were created.'"
29:57.section_title_en: On the Ecstatic States (Wajd) Produced by Qur'anic Recitation and the Superiority of Song (Ghinā') in Stirring the Heart
29:57.anchors:
- Root: وجد (w-j-d)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of finding, attaining, and also denoting the emotional state of ecstasy or rapture that "finds" the heart.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In the theological context, 'wajd' is the state of spiritual finding—a direct, overwhelming apprehension of divine realities that bypasses discursive reasoning.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah) usage denotes "finding" a lost object; metaphorical (Majaz) usage denotes the heart "finding" its spiritual state, leading to agitation and ecstasy.
- Root: سمع (s-m-')
  * Lisan / Ayn: The faculty of hearing; also the ear itself.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Hearing can be literal (perception of sound) or figurative (understanding, obedience, acceptance). The heart's "hearing" is a deeper comprehension.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "سمعته" (I heard him). Metaphorical: "سمع الله لمن حمده" (God answers/he accepts the one who praises Him), indicating a responsive, transformative hearing.
- Root: موت (m-w-t)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Death; the opposite of life.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Death is the cessation of the soul's governance over the body, a separation. In the spiritual context, it can be a metaphorical death to worldly desires.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical death. Metaphorical: "أحيا الله البلد الميت" (God revives the dead land), indicating spiritual revival or the death of the ego.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — Used to emphasize that the stirring of the heart is exclusively through what is appropriate to its state, as in the phrase "إنما المحرك لما في القلب ما يناسبه" (The only thing that moves what is in the heart is that which is suitable to it).
29:57.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Remembrance of Death and Afterlife'

29:61.arabic: ولذلك قال عز وجل ولئن سألتهم من خلق السموات والأرض ليقولن الله وقال تعالى فأقم وجهك للدين حنيفا فطرة الله التي
29:61.english: The First Principle: the knowledge of His existence, the Exalted. The first thing by which one is illuminated from among the lights, and the path of reflection (ṭarīq al-iʿtibār) by which one proceeds, is that to which the Qurʾān has guided. For after the explanation of God, glorified be He, there is no explanation. He, the Exalted, has said: {«أَلَمْ نَجْعَلِ الْأَرْضَ مِهَادًا وَالْجِبَالَ أَوْتَادًا وَخَلَقْنَاكُمْ أَزْوَاجًا وَجَعَلْنَا نَوْمَكُمْ سُبَاتًا وَجَعَلْنَا اللَّيْلَ لِبَاسًا وَجَعَلْنَا النَّهَارَ مَعَاشًا وَبَنَيْنَا فَوْقَكُمْ سَبْعًا شِدَادًا وَجَعَلْنَا سِرَاجًا وَهَّاجًا وَأَنزَلْنَا مِنَ الْمُعْصِرَاتِ مَاءً ثَجَّاجًا لِّنُخْرِجَ بِهِ حَبًّا وَنَبَاتًا وَجَنَّاتٍ أَلْفَافًا»} — "Have We not made the earth a resting place, and the mountains as pegs, and created you in pairs, and made your sleep a repose, and made the night a covering, and made the day for livelihood, and built above you seven strong heavens, and made a blazing lamp, and sent down from the rain-clouds pouring water, that We may bring forth thereby grain and vegetation, and gardens dense with foliage?" (Q 78:6–16). And He, the Exalted, has said: {«إِنَّ فِي خَلْقِ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَاخْتِلَافِ اللَّيْلِ وَالنَّهَارِ وَالْفُلْكِ الَّتِي تَجْرِي فِي الْبَحْرِ بِمَا يَنفَعُ النَّاسَ وَمَا أَنزَلَ اللَّهُ مِنَ السَّمَاءِ مِن مَّاءٍ فَأَحْيَا بِهِ الْأَرْضَ بَعْدَ مَوْتِهَا وَبَثَّ فِيهَا مِن كُلِّ دَابَّةٍ وَتَصْرِيفِ الرِّيَاحِ وَالسَّحَابِ الْمُسَخَّرِ بَيْنَ السَّمَاءِ وَالْأَرْضِ لَآيَاتٍ لِّقَوْمٍ يَعْقِلُونَ»} — "Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth, and the alternation of the night and the day, and the ships which sail through the sea with that which benefits people, and what God has sent down from the sky of water, thereby reviving the earth after its death, and dispersing therein every creature, and the directing of the winds, and the clouds subservient between the heaven and the earth — are signs for a people who reason" (Q 2:164). And He, the Exalted, has said: {«أَلَمْ تَرَوْا كَيْفَ خَلَقَ اللَّهُ سَبْعَ سَمَاوَاتٍ طِبَاقًا وَجَعَلَ الْقَمَرَ فِيهِنَّ نُورًا وَجَعَلَ الشَّمْسَ سِرَاجًا وَاللَّهُ أَنبَتَكُم مِّنَ الْأَرْضِ نَبَاتًا ثُمَّ يُعِيدُكُمْ فِيهَا وَيُخْرِجُكُمْ إِخْرَاجًا»} — "Have you not seen how God created seven heavens in layers, and made the moon therein a light, and made the sun a lamp? And God caused you to grow from the earth a growth; then He returns you into it, and brings you forth a bringing forth" (Q 71:15–18). And He, the Exalted, has said: {«أَفَرَأَيْتُم مَّا تُمْنُونَ أَأَنتُمْ تَخْلُقُونَهُ أَمْ نَحْنُ الْخَالِقُونَ»} — "Have you considered what you emit? Do you create it, or are We the Creator?" — up to His saying: {«لِلْمُقْوِينَ»} — "for the settlers" (Q 56:58–73).
29:61.section_title_en: The Pillars of Faith: Knowledge of God, His Attributes, His Acts, and the Audibles — Section 87
29:61.anchors:
- Root: وجود (w-j-d)
  * Lisan / Ayn: [Core linguistic root meaning: to find, to perceive, to be; existence as that which is found or discovered]
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): [Theological/Kalam semantic nuance: al-wujūd as necessary existence (wujūb) versus contingent existence (imkān); the self-evident reality of the Creator's being]
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): [Literal vs Metaphorical distinction: haqīqah — existence as affirmed reality; majāz — "finding" as in discovery, not applicable to God's necessary being]
- Root: خلق (kh-l-q)
  * Lisan / Ayn: [Core linguistic root meaning: measuring, proportioning, fashioning; origination of a thing upon a measure]
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الخلق أصله: التقدير المستقيم، ويستعمل في إبداع الشيء من غير أصل ولا احتذاء" — creation as origination from nothing without prior model
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): [Literal: خلق الله الخلق: أوجده على تقدير أوجبته الحكمة — brought into existence upon a measure necessitated by wisdom; Majaz: not applicable to God's act as pure origination]
- Root: فطر (f-t-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: [Core linguistic root meaning: to split, cleave, rend; to originate, to bring forth as a new creation]
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "فطر الله الخلق" — God's origination of creation as a primordial act; "الفطرة" as the innate disposition
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): [Literal: فطر الله الخلق، وهو فاطر السموات: مبتدعها — originator without precedent; Majaz: "رأيه فطير" — immature opinion, not applicable to divine]
- Root: ارض (ar-d)
  * Lisan / Ayn: [Core linguistic root meaning: the earth, the lower sphere; that which is beneath]
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الأرض: الجرم المقابل للسماء" — the body opposite the heaven
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): [Literal: the earth as a resting place (مهادا); Majaz: not applicable in this context of divine creation]
- Root: ركن (r-k-n)
  * Lisan / Ayn: [Core linguistic root meaning: corner, pillar, support; that to which one leans for strength]
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "ركن الشيء: جانبه الذي يسكن إليه" — the side of a thing to which one repairs; used metaphorically for strength
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): [Literal: physical pillar/corner; Majaz: "فلان يأوي من عز قومه إلى ركن شديد" — one who repairs to a mighty support; here, the "pillars" (أركان) of faith as structural supports]
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The syntactic structure "مداره على عشرة أصول" (its circuit revolves upon ten principles) employs a prepositional phrase governing the verbal noun, establishing the necessary grammatical dependency that mirrors the ontological dependency of the created upon the Creator.
29:61.topic: Al-Ghazali on the journey of the soul, death, and the Hereafter, from 'Remembrance of Death and Afterlife'

30:26.arabic: وهو أحد والآصال التي ذكرها الله تعالى إذ قال ولله يسجد من في السموات والأرض طوعا وكرها وظلالهم بالغدو والآصال وإذا سجد لله عز وجل الجمادات فكيف يجوز أن يغفل العبد العاقل عن أنواع العبادات الورد السادس إذا دخل وقت العصر دخل وقت الورد السادس وهو الذي أقسم الله تعالى به فقال تعالى {والعصر} هذا أحد معنيي الآية وهو المراد بالآصال في أحد التفسيرين وهو العشي المذكور في قوله {وعشيا} وفي قوله {بالعشي والإشراق} وليس في هذا الورد صلاة إلا أربع ركعات بين الأذان والإقامة كما سبق في الظهر ثم يصلي الفرض ويشتغل بالأقسام الأربعة المذكورة
30:26.english: I say: And just as knowledge and remembrance are the nourishment of the heart, which can never be cut off from it, so too the measure of moderation is this; and deficiency from it may lead to the disturbance of the body — except for one who accustoms himself to wakefulness gradually, for he may train himself upon it without disturbance. And this litany (wird) is among the longest of the litanies and the most delightful for the worshippers, and it is one of the "evenings and mornings" (al-āṣāl) which God Most High mentioned when He said: {«ولله يسجد من في السموات والأرض طوعا وكرها وظلالهم بالغدو والآصال»} "And to God prostrates whoever is in the heavens and the earth, willingly or unwillingly, and their shadows, in the mornings and the evenings" (Q. 13:15). And when inanimate objects prostrate to God, Mighty and Majestic, how then can the intelligent servant be heedless of the varieties of worship?
30:26.section_title_en: The Seventh Daily Litany (Al-Wird al-Sābiʿ): The Time of Sunset — The Completion of the Day's Litanies and Self-Accounting
30:26.anchors:
- Root: ورد (warada)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The root denotes arriving at water, seeking it, and drinking from it; also the portion or share of water allotted for drinking at a specific time.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الورود أصله: قصد الماء" — the core meaning is the intentional approach to water; the litany (wird) is the appointed portion of devotional recitation, likened to the daily share of water that a person must take to sustain life.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): the act of arriving at water. Metaphorical (Majaz): "ورد علي كتاب سرني مورده" — a book arrived upon me whose arrival pleased me; likewise, the wird is the arrival of the appointed time for worship, and the soul's approach to the fountain of divine remembrance.
- Root: عصر (ʿaṣr)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The root denotes pressing, squeezing, and extracting; also the time of afternoon, so called because it is the pressing of the day's end.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The ʿaṣr is the latter part of the day; God swore by it in {«والعصر»} (Q. 103:1), indicating its great merit.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the afternoon time. Metaphorical: the pressing of one's life — as the day is pressed at its end, so the life of man is pressed at its term.
- Root: غرب (gharaba)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The root denotes disappearance, absence, and setting; the sun's setting (ghurūb) is its concealment from the eye.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The setting of the sun marks the boundary between the day's works and the night's; it is the terminus of the visible world's diurnal cycle.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the sun's descent below the horizon. Metaphorical: the setting of the sun of life — the death of man, after which there is no rising.
- Root: حاسب (ḥāsaba)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The root denotes reckoning, counting, and taking account; muḥāsabah is the mutual reckoning between two parties.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Self-accounting (muḥāsabat al-nafs) is the soul's reckoning with itself over its deeds before the Day of Reckoning, for "one who reckons himself before he is reckoned" is among the wise.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the arithmetic counting of sums. Metaphorical: the soul's audit of its own works, weighing the day's deeds against the standard of the Sacred Law.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The rule governing the separation of the prepositional phrase from its governing verb, as in the construction "فسبحان الله حين تمسون" where the adverbial clause is interposed to emphasize the temporal specification of the act of glorification.
30:26.topic: Al-Ghazali on constant remembrance of God and contemplative invocations, from 'Remembrance of Death and Afterlife'

30:43.arabic: ينطقون ولا يؤذن لهم فيعتذرون يوم لا مرد له من الله يوم هم بارزون ويوم هم على النار يفتنون يوم لا ينفع مال ولا بنون يوم لا ينفع الظالمين معذرتهم ولهم اللعنة ولهم سوء الدار يوم ترد فيه المعاذير وتبلى السرائر وتظهر الضمائر وتكشف الأستار يوم تخشع فيه الأبصار وتسكن الأصوات ويقل فيه الالتفات وتبرز الخفيات وتظهر الخطيئات يوم يساق العباد ومعهم الأشهاد ويشيب الصغير ويسكر الكبير فيومئذ وضعت الموازين ونشرت الدواوين وبرزت الجحيم وأغلى الحميم وزفرت النار ويئس الكفار وسعرت النيران وتغيرت الألوان وخرس اللسان
30:43.english: So prepare yourself, O wretched one, for this Day of immense magnitude, of prolonged duration, of overwhelming dominion, whose appointed time is near — a Day when you shall see the heaven split asunder, and the stars scattered in its terror, and the shining planets extinguished, and the sun folded up, and the mountains set in motion, and the pregnant camels neglected, and the wild beasts gathered together, and the seas set ablaze, and the souls paired with their bodies, and the Hellfire ignited, and Paradise brought near, and the mountains pulverized, and the earth stretched out — a Day when you shall see the earth shaken with its quaking, and the earth casts forth its burdens. On that Day shall people issue forth in scattered groups to be shown their deeds — a Day when the earth and the mountains are lifted and crushed with a single crushing. Then on that Day the Imminent Event shall come to pass, and the heaven shall split open, for on that Day it shall be frail, and the angels shall be at its edges, and eight shall bear the Throne of your Lord above them on that Day. On that Day you shall be presented — no secret of yours shall remain hidden. A Day when the mountains shall move and you shall see the earth laid bare — a Day when the earth shall be shaken with a violent shaking, and the mountains crumbled to dust, becoming scattered particles — a Day when people shall be like scattered moths, and the mountains like carded wool — a Day when every nursing mother shall forget what she nursed, and every pregnant female shall cast down her burden, and you shall see people drunk, yet they are not drunk, but the chastisement of God is severe — a Day when the earth shall be changed to other than this earth, and the heavens, and they shall appear before God, the One, the All-Compelling — a Day when the mountains shall be blown away as dust, leaving a level, bare plain, wherein you see no crookedness nor curve — a Day when you see the mountains and suppose them solid, yet they pass by like the passing of clouds — a Day when the heaven shall split open and become rosy like molten oil. Then on that Day no human nor jinn shall be asked about his sin. A Day when the disobedient shall be prevented from speech, and shall not be asked about their crimes, but shall be seized by their forelocks and their feet — a Day when every soul shall find what it did of good brought forth present, and what it did of evil, wishing that between it and that evil there were a far distance — a Day when every soul shall know what it has sent ahead, and shall witness what it has forwarded and what it has left behind — a Day when tongues shall be struck mute and the bodily members shall speak — a Day whose mention turned the hair of the Master of the Messengers white, when al-Ṣiddīq (may God be pleased with him) said to him: "I see that you have turned white-haired, O Messenger of God." He said: "Sūrat Hūd and its sisters have made me white-haired" — namely, al-Wāqiʿah, al-Mursalāt, ʿAmma Yatasāʾalūn, and Idhā al-Shamsu Kuwwirat.
30:43.section_title_en: The Names and Attributes of the Day of Resurrection — An Exhortation to the Negligent
30:43.anchors:
- Root: يوم (yawm)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "اليوم: وقت طلوع الشمس إلى غروبها، وقد يعبر به عن مدة من الزمان أي مدة كانت" — the day as a temporal span, extended metaphorically to any epoch or era.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "اليوم يعبر به عن وقت طلوع الشمس إلى غروبها. وقد يعبر به عن مدة من الزمان أي مدة كانت" — theological usage denotes the appointed time of reckoning, magnified by divine attribution (أيام الله).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): a measured solar period. Metaphorical (Majaz): "ذكر في أيام العرب كذا أي في وقائعها" — days as epochal events; thus "the Day" is the supreme epochal event of divine justice.
- Root: نفس (nafs)
  * Lisan / Ayn: النفس: الروح والذات — the self, soul, or very essence.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "النفس: الروح... وقوله: ويحذركم الله نفسه فنفسه: ذاته" — nafs as the innermost reality of a being; in the eschatological context, souls are "paired" (زوجت) with bodies for judgment.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the soul as life-principle. Metaphorical: "دفق نفسه أي دمه" — nafs as the total self, accountable in its entirety.
- Root: ارض (arḍ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: الأرض: الجرم المقابل للسماء — the earth as the corporeal substratum beneath the heavens.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الأرض: الجرم المقابل للسماء... ويعبر بها عن أسفل الشيء" — the earth as the lowest register of creation, subject to total transformation on that Day.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the physical earth. Metaphorical: "تأرض فلان: لزم الأرض" — to cling low; on that Day the earth itself is leveled, flattened, and replaced.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد (Restriction & Focused Predication) — The repeated "يوم" clauses function as temporal restrictors (ẓurūf) binding each predicate to that single, all-encompassing moment; the accumulation of names (أسامي) serves not as mere repetition but as focused predication upon the multifarious realities of a single event.
30:43.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Remembrance of Death and Afterlife'

30:43.arabic: وسلم قال من كانت لأخيه عنده مظلمة في عرض أو مال فليستحللها منه من قبل أن يأتي يوم ليس هناك دينار ولا درهم إنما يؤخذ من حسناته فإن لم يكن له حسنات أخذ من سيئات صاحبه فزيدت على سيئاته (1) وقالت عائشة رضي الله عنها لامرأة قالت لأخرى أنها طويلة الذيل قد اغتبتيها فاستحليها فإذن لا بد من الاستحلال إن قدر عليه فإن كان غائبا أو ميتا فينبغي أن يكثر له الاستغفار والدعاء ويكثر من الحسنات فإن قلت فالتحليل هل يجب فأقول لا لأنه تبرع والتبرع فضل وليس بواجب ولكنه مستحسن وسبيل المعتذر أن يبالغ في الثناء عليه والتودد إليه
30:43.english:
- Root: غيب (gh-y-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "To be absent, hidden, concealed from sight; ghayb = that which is unseen/absent from perception"
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الغيب: مصدر غابت الشمس وغيرها: إذا استترت عن العين — used of everything absent from the senses and from human knowledge; applied to things as ghayb/ghā'ib relative to people, not relative to God, for nothing is absent from Him"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Haqiqah: "تكلم بذلك عن ظهر الغيب" (speaking of the unseen); Majaz: "أتونا في غابة" (metaphorical extension to dense/thick things)
- Root: حسن (ḥ-s-n)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "Beauty, goodness, excellence; to be fair, comely, good"
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الحسن: عبارة عن كل مبهج مرغوب فيه — three kinds: good by reason, good by desire, good by sense; ḥasanah = everything that delights one, whether in self, body, or circumstances"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Haqiqah: "أنظر إلى محاسن وجهه" (physical beauty); Majaz: "فلان لا يحسن شيئًا" (to do well/excel — transferred to action)
- Root: حرم (ḥ-r-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "To forbid, prohibit, make unlawful; ḥarām = that which is forbidden"
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الحرام: الممنوع منه إما بتسخير إلهي وإما بشري — prohibition by divine decree, by human law, by coercive prevention, by reason, or by revelation"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Haqiqah: "هتك رحمته" (violating sanctity); Majaz: "جلد محرم: لم يدبغ" (raw hide — metaphorical extension to "untreated/unlawful")
- Root: ظلم (ẓ-l-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "Wrongdoing, injustice, oppression; to place something in other than its proper place"
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الظلمة: عدم النور — darkness is absence of light; used metaphorically for ignorance, polytheism, and sin, just as light is used for their opposites"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Haqiqah: "فلان يظلم فيظلم" (to wrong and be wronged); Majaz: "أرض مظلومة" (land never dug — metaphorical: "wronged" land)
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — "إنما يؤخذ من حسناته" restricts the taking exclusively to good deeds, excluding any monetary compensation on that Day.
30:43.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'Condemnation of Anger and Hatred'

31:33.arabic: القيامة وأنه يوم لا ينفع فيه مال ولا بنون ولا يجزي والد عن ولده ويشتغل الصديقون بأنفسهم فيقول كل واحد نفسي نفسي فضلا عن غيرهم فكانوا كزوار بيت الله إذا توجهوا إلى مكة فإنهم يستصحبون مع أنفسهم الذهب المغربي الخالص لعلمهم أن أرباب البوادي لا يروج عندهم الزائف والبهرج والحاجة تشتد في البادية ولا وطن يفزع إليه ولا حميم يتمسك به فلا ينجي إلى الخالص من النقد فكذا يشاهد أرباب القلوب يوم القيامة والزاد الذي يتزودونه له من التقوى فإذن شوائب الرياء الخفي كثيرة لا تنحصر ومهما أدرك من نفسه تفرقة بين أن يطلع على عبادته
31:33.english: And that they should be energetic in fulfilling his needs, and that they should be lenient with him in buying and selling, and that they should make room for him in the gathering place. For if anyone falls short in this, that weighs heavily upon his heart, and he finds in himself a sense of astonishment at it—as though he were demanding respect in return for the obedience which he had kept hidden, even though no one had been made aware of it. And had that act of obedience not preceded from him, he would not have deemed people's falling short in his regard to be something astonishing. And whenever the existence of his worship is not equivalent to its non-existence in all that pertains to creatures, then he has not been content with God's knowledge [alone], nor has he been free of a hidden taint of ostentation more concealed than the creeping of ants. {Hadith on ostentation: traces more concealed than the creeping of ants, narrated by Ahmad and al-Ṭabarānī from Abū Mūsā al-Ashʿarī: "Beware of this shirk, for it is more concealed than the creeping of ants." Also narrated by Ibn Ḥibbān in al-Ḍuʿafāʾ from Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq, and he and al-Dāraquṭnī declared it weak.}
31:33.section_title_en: On the Hidden Traces of Ostentation (Riyāʾ) and the Striving of the Sincere (Mukhliṣūn) to Conceal Their Deeds
31:33.anchors:
- Root: خلص (khalasa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of purity after admixture—that which is sifted, refined, and cleared of alloy.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الخالص كالصافي إلا أن الخالص هو ما زال عنه شوبه بعد أن كان فيه" — the sincere (mukhliṣ) is one from whom the taint has been removed after it existed; pure gold (al-dhahab al-khāliṣ) as metaphor for accepted deeds.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Haqiqah: "خلص الشيء خلوصا فهو خالص، وخلصته: صفيته." Majaz: "أخلص لله دينه" — sincerity as metaphorical purification of religion from all foreign admixture.
- Root: راءى (rāʾā) / ريا (riyāʾ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Derived from رؤية (seeing); ostentation is performing acts to be seen by creatures rather than the Creator.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Riyāʾ is the seeking of station (manzilah) in the hearts of men through displaying acts of obedience—a hidden shirk (associationism).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Majaz: "راءى فلان الناس" — to show off; the root implies visual perception transferred to the seeking of social regard.
- Root: نفس (nafs)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The self, the soul; here denoting the inner seat of intention and hidden motives.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "نفسه: ذاته" — the self as the locus of divine knowledge; the sincere one is content with God's knowledge alone, not human witness.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Majaz: "دفق نفسه أي دمه" — the self as the whole person; here, the inner state of the heart that must be purified.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد (Restriction & Focused Predication) — The conditional structures (fa-in qaṣṣara... wa-law lam... wa-mahmā lam...) establish logical entailment: the absence of equanimity between public and private worship entails the persistence of hidden ostentation.
31:33.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Condemnation of Status and Ostentation'

31:33.arabic: اعلم أن قوله تعالى {فلا تغرنكم الحياة الدنيا ولا يغرنكم بالله الغرور} وقوله تعالى {ولكنكم فتنتم أنفسكم وتربصتم وارتبتم وغرتكم الأماني} الآية كاف في ذم الغرور وقد قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم حبذا نوم الأكياس وفطرهم كيف يغبنون سهر الحمقى واجتهادهم ولمثقال ذرة من صاحب تقوى ويقين أفضل من ملء الأرض من المغترين (1) حديث الكيس من دان نفسه وعمل لما بعد الموت الحديث أخرجه الترمذي وابن ماجه من حديث شداد بن أوس وكل ما ورد في فضل العلم وذم الجهل فهو دليل على ذم الغرور لأن الغرور عبارة عن بعض أنواع الجهل إذ الجهل
31:33.english: Know that the saying of God Most High — {«fa-lā taghurrannakum al-ḥayātu al-dunyā wa-lā yaghurrannakum billāhi al-gharūr»} (So let not the life of this world deceive you, nor let the Deceiver deceive you concerning God) — and His saying — {«wa-lākinnakum fatantum anfusakum wa-tarabbastum wa-irtabtum wa-gharratkum al-amānī»} (But ye tempted your own souls, and ye waited, and ye doubted, and vain desires deceived you) — is sufficient for the blameworthiness of self-deception (al-ghurūr). And the Messenger of God, may God's peace and blessing be upon him, has said: "How excellent is the sleep of the intelligent and their breaking of the fast! How they outwit the wakefulness of the foolish and their striving! And verily a mustard-seed's weight [of faith] from a possessor of piety and certainty is better than the earth filled with the self-deceived." And the ḥadīth: "The intelligent man (al-kayyis) is he who takes account of his own soul and works for what is after death" — this ḥadīth was transmitted by al-Tirmidhī and Ibn Mājah from the ḥadīth of Shaddād ibn Aws.
31:33.section_title_en: Exposition of the Blameworthiness of Self-Deception (Al-Ghurūr), Its Reality, and Its Examples
31:33.anchors:
- Root: غرر (Gh-R-R)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The core meaning is "an apparent trace or mark of a thing" (al-athar al-ẓāhir), from which derives "the blaze of a horse" (ghurrat al-faras). To deceive (gharra) is to strike one's heedlessness (ghirrah) and attain one's sought desire from him, as if folding a garment upon its original crease (ṭawāhu ʿalā gharrihi).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Ghurrah is heedlessness in wakefulness, and ghirār is heedlessness with drowsiness." Theologically, it is the soul's repose upon a false semblance (shubhah) that pleases the caprice (hawā), rendering one oblivious to the true state of affairs—as in {«mā gharraka bi-rabbika al-karīm»} (What deceived thee concerning thy Generous Lord?).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): "A gazelle in a moonlit night is called agharr" because it ventures out thinking it is day and is devoured by beasts—heedlessness in perception. Metaphorical (majāz): "A day agharr muḥajjal" (a white-browed, white-legged day) for intense heat, transferring the blaze of a horse to the day's visible intensity.
- Root: جهل (J-H-L)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "Jahila bihi" — to be ignorant of it; "jāhala ʿalā qawmihi" — to act foolishly/insolently against one's people. The pre-Islamic era is "al-jāhiliyyah al-jahlā'" (the utterly ignorant age).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Ignorance (jahl) is of three kinds: (1) the soul's emptiness of knowledge (this is the root); (2) believing a thing contrary to what it is; (3) doing a thing contrary to what it ought to be, whether one's belief is sound or corrupt. Ghurūr is a species of the second kind—a false belief arising from a corrupt semblance.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "Kafā bil-shakki jahlā" (Sufficient is doubt as ignorance). Metaphorical: "Istajhalat al-rīḥ al-ghuṣn" (The wind made the branch sway violently) — transferred from mental foolishness to physical agitation.
- Root: حدث (Ḥ-D-TH)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "Al-ḥudūth: the coming-to-be of a thing after it was not." "Al-ḥadath: the novel event." "Ḥaddatha: to speak/communicate."
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Ḥudūth is the existence of a thing after non-existence, whether accident or substance. Iḥdāth is bringing it into existence. The iḥdāth of substances belongs to God alone." The "ḥadīth" (report/speech) is so-called for its temporal novelty.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "Nazalat bihi ḥawādith al-dahr" (The vicissitudes of time befell him). Metaphorical: "Kāna ʿUmar muḥaddathan" (Umar was one inspired with true discernment) — as if he were spoken to (ḥudditha) by what he conjectured.
- Root: دنا (D-N-W)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "Danā fa-huwa dānin" — he drew near. "Al-dunyā" (the lower world) is so named because it is nearer (danat) and precedes the Hereafter.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Al-dunūw: proximity by essence or by judgment, used of place, time, and station." The "adnā" (lower/nearer) is contrasted with the greater and with the better: {«a-tastabdilūna alladhī huwa adnā billadhī huwa khayr»} (Will ye take the lower in exchange for what is better?).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "Huwa danī' min al-adniyā'" (He is base, of the base ones) — but this is the homonym danu'a (baseness), distinct from danā (nearness). The dunyā's "nearness" is its temporal immediacy versus the Hereafter's deferral.
- Sibawayh Rule: Bab al-faṣl bayna al-jār wa-al-majrūr (Prepositional Interposition) — The particle "bi" in {«wa-lā yaghurrannakum billāhi al-gharūr»} governs the deceiver (al-gharūr) as the agent of deception, while "billāh" (concerning God) is the object of the deception. The syntactic structure permits the deceiver to be named after the prepositional phrase, indicating that the deception is *about* God's attributes (His forbearance, His respite) — a grammatical subtlety showing the ghurūr deceives *by means of* false notions of God, not that God Himself deceives.
31:33.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Remembrance of Death and Afterlife'

31:33.arabic: في الدنيا فكيف في يوم لا يجزي والد عن ولده ولا مولود هو جاز عن والده شيئا بل تقول الأنبياء فيه نفسي نفسي فكيف يستبدل الجاهل عن ثواب الآخرة ونيل القرب عند الله ما يرتقبه بطمعه الكاذب في الدنيا من الناس فلا ينبغي أن نشك في أن المرائي بطاعة الله في سخط الله من حيث النقل والقياس جميعا هذا إذا لم يقصد الأجر فأما إذا قصد الأجر والحمد جميعا في صدقته أو صلاته فهو الشرك الذي يناقض الإخلاص وقد ذكرنا حكمه في كتاب الإخلاص ويدل على ما نقلناه من الآثار قول سعيد بن المسيب وعبادة بن الصامت إنه لا أجر له فيه أصلا بيان درجات الريا
31:33.english: The Messenger of God, may God's peace and blessings be upon him, named it the lesser shirk (al-shirk al-aṣghar). The hadith naming riya' as the lesser shirk was transmitted by Ahmad from the hadith of Mahmud ibn Labid, and it has already preceded. Al-Tabarani also narrated it from the transmission of Mahmud ibn Labid from Rafi' ibn Khadij, making it part of Rafi's musnad, and it has also preceded recently. Al-Hakim recorded it and authenticated its chain from the hadith of Shaddad ibn Aws: "We used to count riya' on the day of the Messenger of God, may God's peace and blessings be upon him, as the lesser shirk."
31:33.anchors:
- Root: راءى (rā'ā)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of visual display, showing oneself; from الرؤية (seeing), implying making oneself seen.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Riya' is the seeking of station (manzilah) in hearts through acts of obedience — a subtle shirk because the actor's qasd (intention) is diverted from the Creator to creatures.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (haqiqah) = mutual seeing; metaphorical (majaz) = displaying deeds for the gaze of others, transferring the object of worship from God to His servants.
- Root: قصد (qaṣada)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To aim, intend, direct one's course toward a target; the straight path of intention.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Qasd is the straightness of a road; iqtisad (moderation) is praiseworthy between two extremes — here, the qasd of the actor is the very substance of the act's moral weight.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal = aiming at a physical target; metaphorical = the soul's inclination toward a goal, whether divine reward or human praise.
- Root: عظم (ʿaẓuma)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To be great, to magnify; ʿazamah = grandeur, majesty.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): ʿIẓam (magnification) is the heart's ascription of greatness to an object; when transferred from God to creatures, it constitutes the hidden kernel of shirk.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal = physical largeness; metaphorical = the heart's veneration (taʿẓīm) of a being, which is the true object of worship.
- Root: درج (daraja)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To ascend step by step; degrees of a ladder.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Darajah is a station considered by ascent; used for ranks of honor or degradation.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal = physical steps; metaphorical = graded levels of moral severity, as here: "degrees of riya'."
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين المبتدأ والخبر (Interposition between subject and predicate) — The periodic structure "اعلم أن بعض أبواب الرياء أشد وأغلظ من بعض" employs an embedded clause (أنّ + nominal sentence) requiring careful tracking of the governed accusative and its predicate to preserve the logical hierarchy of the author's taxonomy.
31:33.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Condemnation of Status and Ostentation'

31:33.arabic: ويحك يا نفس لا ينبغى أن تغرك الحياة الدنيا ولا يغرنك بالله الغرور فانظرى لنفسك فما أمرك بمهم لغيرك ولا تضيعى أوقاتك فالأنفاس معدودة فإذا مضى منك نفس فقد ذهب بعضك فاغتنمى الصحة قبل السقم والفراغ قبل الشغل والغنى قبل الفقر والشباب قبل الهرم والحياة قبل الموت واستعدي للآخرة على قدر بقائك فيها يا نفس أما تستعدين للشتاء بقدر طول مدته فتجمعين له القوت والكسوة والحطب وجميع الأسباب ولا تتكلين في ذلك على فضل الله وكرمه حتى يدفع عنك البرد من غير جبة ولبد وحطب وغير ذلك فإنه قادر على ذلك أفتظنين أيتها النفس أن زمهرير جهنم
31:33.english: ...from creation, but rather you attain your goal through every stratagem. And by this ignorance you deserve the title of foolishness from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, where he said: "The shrewd one is he who holds his soul to account and works for what comes after death, and the foolish one is he who follows his soul's whims and harbors vain hopes upon God." {«الكيس من دان نفسه وعمل لما بعد الموت والأحمق من أتبع نفسه هواها وتمنى على الله الأماني»}
31:33.section_title_en: Section 1253 — The Soul's Self-Reproach and the Awakening from Negligence
31:33.anchors:
- Root: نفس (n-f-s)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The self, soul, or spirit; that which animates and is addressed as an independent moral agent.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The soul as the locus of divine address and self-knowledge; its essence (dhāt) is the referent of God's "self" in revelation, yet here it is the reproaching subject.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (haqīqah) usage as the speaking, desiring self; metaphorical (majāz) extension to blame and counsel, as in "self-accusation" (lawwāmah).
- Root: موت (m-w-t)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Death as the cessation of life; the inevitable terminus of every soul.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Death as separation (furqah) from worldly attachments and the transition to reckoning; linked to the soul's journey.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal death of the body; metaphorical "death" of the heart through heedlessness, contrasted here with physical death as the ultimate wake-up call.
- Root: جهل (j-h-l)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Ignorance as the absence of knowledge; folly and rashness.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Ignorance as the soul's failure to perceive true realities, leading to misplaced desires and false hopes.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal ignorance of facts; metaphorical ignorance as moral stupidity, as when the soul follows whims despite clear signs.
- Root: دنا (d-n-w)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Nearness in place, time, or rank.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Drawing near (dunūw) to God through obedience, contrasted with the soul's clinging to the near (dunyā) world.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal proximity; metaphorical use for the "lower" world (dunyā) as that which is nearer and inferior.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — Used to emphasize exclusive causation, e.g., "God's generosity is only in guiding you to the path," restricting divine favor to guidance, not exemption from effort.
31:33.topic: Al-Ghazali on the journey of the soul, death, and the Hereafter, from 'Monitoring and Accounting'

31:33.arabic: وقال الحسن بعد أن تلا قوله تعالى {فلا تغرنكم الحياة الدنيا} من قال ذا قاله من خلقها ومن هو أعلم بها إياكم وما شغل من الدنيا فإن الدنيا كثيرة الأشغال لا يفتح رجل على نفسه باب شغل إلا أوشك ذلك الباب أن يفتح عليه عشرة أبواب وقال أيضا مسكين ابن أدم رضي بدار حلالها حساب وحرامها عذاب إن أخذه من حله حوسب به وإن أخذه من حرام عذب به ابن آدم يستقل ماله ولا يستقل عمله يفرح بمصيبته في دينه ويجزع من مصيبته في دنياه وكتب الحسن إلى عمر بن عبد العزيز سلام عليك أما بعد فكأنك بآخر من كتب عليه الموت قد مات فأجابه عمر سلا
31:33.english: Al-Hasan said: "By Allah, I have known people for whom the world was more insignificant than the dust upon which you walk. They cared not whether the world rose or set, whether it went to this one or to that one."
31:33.topic: Al-Ghazali on the journey of the soul, death, and the Hereafter, from 'Condemnation of the World'

33:40.arabic: عليه وسلم فيأتون فيقولون يا محمد أنت رسول الله وخاتم النبيين وغفر الله لك ما تقدم من ذنبك وما تأخر اشفع لنا إلى ربك ألا ترى ما نحن فيه فأنطلق فآتي تحت العرش فأقع ساجدا لربي ثم يفتح الله لي من محامده وحسن الثناء عليه شيئا لم يفتحه على أحد قبلي ثم يقال يا محمد ارفع رأسك سل تعط واشفع تشفع فأرفع رأسي فأقول أمتي أمتى يا رب فقال يا محمد أدخل من أمتك من لا حساب عليهم من الباب الأيمن من أبواب الجنة وهم شركاء الناس فيما سوى ذلك من الأبواب ثم قال والذي نفسي بيده إن بين المصراعين من مصاريع الجنة كما بين مكة وحمير أو
33:40.english: The evidences for intercession in the Qurʾān and the reports (akhbār) are numerous. God—exalted be He—said: {«وَلَسَوْفَ يُعْطِيكَ رَبُّكَ فَتَرْضَىٰ»} [And verily thy Lord shall give thee, and thou shalt be well-pleased] (93:5). ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ narrated that the Messenger of God—peace and blessings be upon him—recited the saying of Abraham—peace be upon him—{«رَبِّ إِنَّهُنَّ أَضْلَلْنَ كَثِيرًا مِّنَ النَّاسِ ۖ فَمَن تَبِعَنِي فَإِنَّهُ مِنِّي ۖ وَمَنْ عَصَانِي فَإِنَّكَ غَفُورٌ رَّحِيمٌ»} [My Lord, verily they have led astray many of mankind; so whoso follows me, verily he is of me; and whoso disobeys me, verily Thou art Forgiving, Merciful] (14:36), and the saying of Jesus—peace be upon him—{«إِن تُعَذِّبْهُمْ فَإِنَّهُمْ عِبَادُكَ»} [If Thou chastise them, verily they are Thy servants] (5:118). Then he raised his hands and said: "My community, my community!" Then he wept. So God—mighty and majestic—said: "O Gabriel, go to Muhammad and ask him what makes him weep." Gabriel came to him and asked him, and he informed him—and God knows best concerning him. Then He said: "O Gabriel, go to Muhammad and say to him: 'Verily We shall please thee concerning thy community, and shall not cause thee grief.'"
33:40.section_title_en: On the Reality of Intercession (Shafāʿah) and the Means of Attaining It
33:40.anchors:
- Root: شفع (Sh-F-ʿ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root denotes pairing/joining (al-ḍamm), whence shafāʿah = the intercessor joining his own plea to the petitioner's, making it two (shafʿ) rather than one (watr).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance — intercession is a divinely granted honor (jāh) bestowed upon prophets and saints, not an independent power; its efficacy is wholly contingent upon divine will and pleasure.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) — "شفعت الشيء" (I made it even/pair). Metaphorical (majāz) — the intercessor "pairs" his rank with the sinner's need, elevating the latter through the former's proximity to God.
- Root: خبأ (Kh-B-ʾ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To conceal, hide, store away secretly (khabaʾa). Implies deliberate concealment of something precious or dangerous within a locus.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance — God's "hiding" (takhbiʾah) of His friendship (wilāyah), wrath (ghaḍab), and pleasure (riḍā) within creatures and acts respectively teaches epistemic humility: no outward judgment can access the hidden decree.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — physical concealment. Metaphorical — the inscrutability of divine judgment (ḥukm) regarding ultimate states (ʿawāqib), rendering contempt for any person or act a potential act of defiance against God's hidden will.
- Root: عله (not applicable here; avoided per instruction)
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — Governing the periodic suspension of meaning across lengthy narrative sequences (e.g., the extended ḥadīth of intercession), where the syntactic resolution (jawāb) is deferred to heighten rhetorical impact, yet remains grammatically anchored.
33:40.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'Remembrance of Death and Afterlife'

33:63.arabic: الساعة وانشق القمر إنهم يرونه بعيدا ونراه قريبا وما يدريك لعل الساعة تكون قريبا ثم يكون أحسن أحوالنا أن نتخذ دراسة هذا القرآن عملا فلا نتدبر معانيه ولا ننظر في كثرة أوصاف هذا اليوم وأساميه ولا نستعد للتخلص من دواهيه فنعوذ بالله من هذه الغفلة إن لم يداركنا الله بواسع رحمته
33:63.english: So prepare yourself, O wretched one, for this Day of immense magnitude, of prolonged duration, of overwhelming dominion, whose appointed time is near — a Day when you shall see the heaven split asunder, and the stars scattered in its terror, and the shining planets extinguished, and the sun folded up, and the mountains set in motion, and the pregnant camels neglected, and the wild beasts gathered together, and the seas set ablaze, and the souls paired with their bodies, and the Hellfire ignited, and Paradise brought near, and the mountains pulverized, and the earth stretched out — a Day when you shall see the earth shaken with its quaking, and the earth casts forth its burdens. On that Day shall people issue forth in scattered groups to be shown their deeds — a Day when the earth and the mountains are lifted and crushed with a single crushing. Then on that Day the Imminent Event shall come to pass, and the heaven shall split open, for on that Day it shall be frail, and the angels shall be at its edges, and eight shall bear the Throne of your Lord above them on that Day. On that Day you shall be presented — no secret of yours shall remain hidden. A Day when the mountains shall move and you shall see the earth laid bare — a Day when the earth shall be shaken with a violent shaking, and the mountains crumbled to dust, becoming scattered particles — a Day when people shall be like scattered moths, and the mountains like carded wool — a Day when every nursing mother shall forget what she nursed, and every pregnant female shall cast down her burden, and you shall see people drunk, yet they are not drunk, but the chastisement of God is severe — a Day when the earth shall be changed to other than this earth, and the heavens, and they shall appear before God, the One, the All-Compelling — a Day when the mountains shall be blown away as dust, leaving a level, bare plain, wherein you see no crookedness nor curve — a Day when you see the mountains and suppose them solid, yet they pass by like the passing of clouds — a Day when the heaven shall split open and become rosy like molten oil. Then on that Day no human nor jinn shall be asked about his sin. A Day when the disobedient shall be prevented from speech, and shall not be asked about their crimes, but shall be seized by their forelocks and their feet — a Day when every soul shall find what it did of good brought forth present, and what it did of evil, wishing that between it and that evil there were a far distance — a Day when every soul shall know what it has sent ahead, and shall witness what it has forwarded and what it has left behind — a Day when tongues shall be struck mute and the bodily members shall speak — a Day whose mention turned the hair of the Master of the Messengers white, when al-Ṣiddīq (may God be pleased with him) said to him: "I see that you have turned white-haired, O Messenger of God." He said: "Sūrat Hūd and its sisters have made me white-haired" — namely, al-Wāqiʿah, al-Mursalāt, ʿAmma Yatasāʾalūn, and Idhā al-Shamsu Kuwwirat.
33:63.section_title_en: The Names and Attributes of the Day of Resurrection — An Exhortation to the Negligent
33:63.anchors:
- Root: يوم (yawm)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "اليوم: وقت طلوع الشمس إلى غروبها، وقد يعبر به عن مدة من الزمان أي مدة كانت" — the day as a temporal span, extended metaphorically to any epoch or era.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "اليوم يعبر به عن وقت طلوع الشمس إلى غروبها. وقد يعبر به عن مدة من الزمان أي مدة كانت" — theological usage denotes the appointed time of reckoning, magnified by divine attribution (أيام الله).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): a measured solar period. Metaphorical (Majaz): "ذكر في أيام العرب كذا أي في وقائعها" — days as epochal events; thus "the Day" is the supreme epochal event of divine justice.
- Root: نفس (nafs)
  * Lisan / Ayn: النفس: الروح والذات — the self, soul, or very essence.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "النفس: الروح... وقوله: ويحذركم الله نفسه فنفسه: ذاته" — nafs as the innermost reality of a being; in the eschatological context, souls are "paired" (زوجت) with bodies for judgment.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the soul as life-principle. Metaphorical: "دفق نفسه أي دمه" — nafs as the total self, accountable in its entirety.
- Root: ارض (arḍ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: الأرض: الجرم المقابل للسماء — the earth as the corporeal substratum beneath the heavens.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الأرض: الجرم المقابل للسماء... ويعبر بها عن أسفل الشيء" — the earth as the lowest register of creation, subject to total transformation on that Day.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the physical earth. Metaphorical: "تأرض فلان: لزم الأرض" — to cling low; on that Day the earth itself is leveled, flattened, and replaced.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد (Restriction & Focused Predication) — The repeated "يوم" clauses function as temporal restrictors (ẓurūf) binding each predicate to that single, all-encompassing moment; the accumulation of names (أسامي) serves not as mere repetition but as focused predication upon the multifarious realities of a single event.
33:63.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Remembrance of Death and Afterlife'

33:63.arabic: غرورا وظن أن تزكية الناس له دليل على كونه مرضيا عند الله ولا يدري أن ذلك لجهل الناس بخبائث باطنه وفرقة أخرى حرصت على النوافل ولم يعظم اعتدادها بالفرائض ترى أحدهم يفرح بصلاة الضحى وبصلاة الليل وأمثال هذه النوافل ولا يجد للفريضة لذة ولا يشتد حرصه على المبادرة بها في أول الوقت وينسى قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم فيما يرويه عن ربه ما تقرب المتقربون إلي بمثل أداء ما افترضت عليهم (1) حديث من أبر قال أمك الحديث أخرجه الترمذي والحاكم وصححه من حديث زيد بن حكيم عن أبيه عن جده وقد تقدم في آداب الصحة فينبغي أن يبدأ في الصلة بال
33:63.english: Yes — and he may even abandon leadership and prefer seclusion and withdrawal, yet still be deluded, for he then shows favor toward the wealthy, speaks harshly to them, and looks upon them with an eye of contempt. He hopes for himself more than he hopes for them, marvels at his own deeds, and is characterized by a host of hidden vices of the heart while he does not perceive it. Perhaps he is offered wealth and refuses to take it, fearing that it will be said that his asceticism has been nullified — yet were it said to him: "It is lawful, so take it openly and return it secretly," his soul would not permit him, out of fear of people's blame. Thus he is desirous of people's praise — and that is among the most delicious of the doors of this world — while he sees himself as an ascetic in this world, and he is deluded. Moreover, he is not free from venerating the wealthy, giving them precedence over the poor, inclining toward those who seek him out and praise him, and recoiling from those who incline toward other ascetics besides him. All of that is deception and delusion from Satan — we seek refuge in God from him.
33:63.section_title_en: On the Deluded Ascetic Who Seeks Renown and Neglects the Inner Heart
33:63.anchors:
- Root: غرر (gh-r-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of an outward trace or mark; غرّة is heedlessness in wakefulness, and being deluded (مغرور) is one who is deceived by an outward appearance.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "غررت فلانا: أصبت غرته" — to strike one's heedless spot; the delusion is a heedlessness wherein one takes the apparent for the real, as in {«ما غرك بربك الكريم»} (Q. 82:6).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Haqiqah: غارّ = heedless/negligent. Majaz: The "white-blazed" day (يوم أغر) is one of intense heat — a metaphorical extension of a shining, deceptive surface.
- Root: خلق (kh-l-q)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Root of measuring and smoothing; خلق الثوب = worn-out garment (from being measured by use).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Originary creation by precise estimation (تقدير مستقيم); also character/disposition as the inward "measure" of the soul.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Haqiqah: tailoring/measuring before cutting. Majaz: God's creation as bringing into being upon a measure required by wisdom; خلق حسن = excellent moral character.
- Root: قلب (q-l-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Turning a thing over from one face to another.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): تصريف الشيء وصرفه عن وجه إلى وجه — the heart is so named for its constant turning (تقلب) between states.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Haqiqah: physical overturning. Majaz: "قلبت الأمر ظهرا لبطن" — to scrutinize a matter thoroughly, turning it over in examination.
- Root: ظهر (z-h-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The back; outward surface.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Used metaphorically for the outward aspect of the earth (ظهر الأرض) versus its inward (بطنها); also for the manifest versus the hidden.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Haqiqah: physical back. Majaz: "قلبت الأمر ظهرا لبطن" — exhaustive examination; ظاهر = outward deeds vs. باطن = inner states.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين المبتدأ والخبر (Interposition between subject and predicate) — allowing parenthetical clauses (e.g., "وهو لا يدري") to interrupt the main periodic sentence without breaking its grammatical cohesion, preserving the cumulative rhetorical force of the author's warning.
33:63.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'Condemnation of Delusion'

33:71.arabic: وخطب رجل عند رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال من يطع الله ورسوله فقد رشد ومن يعصهما فقد غوى فقال قل ومن يعص الله ورسوله فقد غوى (2) فكره رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قوله ومن يعصهما لأنه تسوية وجمع وكان إبراهيم يكره أن يقول الرجل أعوذ بالله وبك ويجوز أن يقول أعوذ بالله ثم بك وأن يقول لولا الله ثم فلان ولا يقول لولا الله وفلان وكره بعضهم أن يقال اللهم أعتقنا من النار وكان يقول العتق يكون بعد الورود وكانوا يستجيرون من النار ويتعوذون من النار وقال رجل اللهم اجعلني ممن تصيبه شفاعة محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم فق
33:71.english: An example of this is what Ḥudhayfah reported: The Prophet, peace be upon him, said: "Let none of you say: 'What Allah willed and you willed' — but rather let him say: 'What Allah willed, then you willed.'" (5) This is because in the absolute conjunction [with "and"] there is an association and an equalization, which is contrary to [the due measure of] reverence. And Ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: A man came to the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, speaking to him concerning some matter, and he said: "What Allah willed and you willed." The Prophet, peace be upon him, said: "Have you made me an equal to Allah? Rather, [say]: 'What Allah willed alone.'" (1)
33:71.section_title_en: The Revival of the Religious Sciences — Section 698: The Nineteenth Affliction — Heedlessness Regarding Subtle Errors in the Import of Speech
33:71.anchors:
- Root: غفل (ghafla)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of heedlessness, neglect, and inattention; the absence of vigilance over a matter.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Heedlessness (al-ghafla) is the soul's failure to attend to what it is obligated to know or consider; it is the opposite of mindfulness (al-tayaqquẓ) and remembrance (al-dhikr).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) usage denotes the absence of guarding; metaphorical (majāz) usage extends to the tongue's straying from precise expression in sacred matters.
- Root: عطف (ʿaṭf)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Inclination, turning, or joining one thing to another; grammatically, the conjunction that links two items in a shared ruling.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Joining (al-ʿaṭf) implies equal treatment of the conjoined items; in theological speech, absolute conjunction (al-ʿaṭf al-muṭlaq) with Allah entails an inadmissible association.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the bending of a staff or the inclining of a branch; metaphorical: the grammatical coupling that levels two referents under one predicate.
- Root: شرك (shirk)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Sharing, partnership, or association; the root of polytheism (al-shirk) as the ascription of a partner to Allah.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Association (al-shirk) is the equalization of two things in a shared ruling; in theology, it is the gravest form when applied to the Divine, whether in belief or in the mere wording of speech.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: co-participation in ownership; metaphorical: any verbal or creedal equalization of the creature with the Creator.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Conjunction (al-ʿaṭf) and Restriction (al-ḥaṣr) — The particle "thumma" (then) indicates sequential ordering and distinction of rank, whereas "wa" (and) denotes absolute conjunction and mutual equivalence; thus the Prophet's command to replace "wa" with "thumma" in "what Allah willed and you willed" is a syntactic correction to abolish the implication of equal partnership.
33:71.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications, prayers, and their spiritual power, from 'Condemnation of Anger and Hatred'

33:71.arabic: أما من كان مستعدا فقد فاز فوزا عظيما وأما من كان مغرورا بطول الأمل فقد خسر خسرانا مبينا فلينظر الإنسان كل ساعة في أطرافه وأعضائه وليتدبر أنها كيف تأكلها الديدان لا محالة وكيف تتفتت عظامها وليتفكر أن الدود يبدأ بحدقته اليمنى أولا أو اليسرى فما على بدنه شيء إلا وهو طعمة الدود وما له من نفسه إلا العلم والعمل الخالص لوجه الله تعالى وكذلك يتفكر فيما سنورده من عذاب القبر وسؤال منكر ونكير ومن الحشر والنشر وأهوال القيامة وقرع النداء يوم العرض الأكبر فأمثال هذه الأفكار هي التي
33:71.english: He defers day after day, and one occupation passes him on to another — nay, to many occupations — until death snatches him away at a moment he does not anticipate. Then his regret becomes prolonged, and most of the people of the Fire — and their screaming — are from "I will" (sawfa). They say: "Woe to us for our 'I will'!" (wa-ḥazanāh min sawfa).
33:71.section_title_en: The True Nature of Procrastination (al-Taswīf): Its Causes and Cures — On the Deception of Extended Hope (ṭūl al-amal)
33:71.anchors:
- Root: سوف (s-w-f)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "سوف" is a particle of future tense (tanjīz al-waʿd), indicating postponement and delay; al-musawwif is one who defers action.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The root conveys "delay" (taʾkhīr) and is tied to the blameworthy trait of procrastination in religious duties, as opposed to immediate resolve (mubādarah).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "سوّفت به" (I delayed him). Metaphorical: "سوّف بنفسه" — he lulled himself with false promises of future time, a majāz for self-deception.
- Root: أمل (a-m-l)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Hope/expectation (rajāʾ); ṭūl al-amal is extended hope — the root cause of negligence (ghaflah) in preparing for death.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Amal is expectation of a desired outcome; blameworthy when it exceeds the appointed term (ajal), diverting from the Hereafter.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "أملت الشيء" (I hoped for it). Metaphorical: Extended hope is a veil (ḥijāb) over the certainty of death.
- Root: جهل (j-h-l)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Ignorance, the opposite of knowledge (ʿilm); also rashness acting without knowledge.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Jahl is the absence of knowledge about what one must know — here, ignorance of death's unpredictability.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: lack of knowledge. Metaphorical: acting as if death is distant despite its certainty — a practical ignorance.
- Root: حب (ḥ-b-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Love/attachment (wudd); ḥubb al-dunyā is the love of the lower world.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Love is the inclination of the heart toward what pleases it; love of the world (dunyā) is the root of all blameworthy traits.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: affection. Metaphorical: "ḥubb al-khaṭīr" (love of the momentous) erases "ḥubb al-ḥaqīr" (love of the trivial) — a majāz for spiritual reorientation.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — Used in "فإنما يزداد بطول المدة قوة ورسوخا" (it only increases in strength and rootedness with length of time), restricting the outcome to intensification alone.
33:71.topic: Al-Ghazali on the journey of the soul, death, and the Hereafter, from 'Remembrance of Death and Afterlife'

34:29.arabic: على الكافرين غير يسير} وقال تعالى {ويقولون متى هذا الوعد إن كنتم صادقين ما ينظرون إلا صيحة واحدة تأخذهم وهم يخصمون فلا يستطيعون توصية ولا إلى أهلهم يرجعون ونفخ في الصور فإذا هم من الأجداث إلى ربهم ينسلون قالوا يا ويلنا من بعثنا من مرقدنا هذا ما وعد الرحمن وصدق المرسلون} فلو لم يكن بين يدي الموتى إلا هول تلك النفخة لكان ذلك جديرا بأن يتقى فإنها نفخة وصيحة يصعق بها من في السموات والأرض يعنى يموتون بها إلا من شاء الله وهو بعض الملائكة ولذلك قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كيف أنعم وصاحب الصور قد التقم القرن وحنى الجبهة
34:29.english: The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: Allah the Exalted said: "The son of Adam has reviled Me, and he had no right to revile Me; and he has denied Me, and he had no right to deny Me. As for his reviling of Me, it is his saying that I have a son. And as for his denial of Me, it is his saying: 'He will never bring me back as He created me at first.'" {«شتمني ابن آدم وما ينبغي له أن يشتمني وكذبني وما ينبغي له أن يكذبني...»}
34:29.section_title_en: On the Terrors of the Trumpet-Blast and the Awakening for the Resurrection
34:29.anchors:
- Root: نفخ (N-F-Kh)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To blow into a thing, to inflate; the breath of wind entering a vessel or body.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The divine act of breathing spirit into creation {«ونفخت فيه من روحي»}; here, the eschatological blast that annihilates and then revives all beings.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah) usage of blowing into the Trumpet (الصور); metaphorical extension to the "blast of spring" reviving the earth—here applied to the two cosmic blasts of death and resurrection.
- Root: صور (S-W-R)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Form, image, shape; also a horn or trumpet (the instrument of the blast).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The perceptible form of bodies and the intelligible form of souls; here, the Trumpet (الصور) as the instrument of divine command that re-forms and re-shapes creation.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the horn (القرن) held by Israfil; metaphorical: the "inclination" (صورة) of hearts toward terror and anticipation.
- Root: موت (M-W-T)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Death as the cessation of life; the state of the corpse.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Death as the separation of the soul from the body; the "first death" of the blast and the "second death" of the wicked.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical death; metaphorical: the "death" of the heart through heedlessness, and the reviving of dead lands by rain—here, the reviving of bodies by the second blast.
- Root: قبر (Q-B-R)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The grave as the abode of the dead; burial.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The grave as the intermediate state (barzakh) before resurrection; {«حتى زرتم المقابر»} as a metaphor for death.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the grave and its inhabitants; metaphorical: the "raising of the nose" (قبراه) of the proud—contrasted here with the humility of the dead rising from their graves.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — Used to emphasize that true faith is not mere verbal assent but heartfelt conviction, as in "إنما فتور البواطن... لقلة الفهم" (The languor of the inner selves is only due to the lack of understanding).
34:29.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'Remembrance of Death and Afterlife'

34:54.arabic: معاني قوله تعالى {وحيل بينهم وبين ما يشتهون} وإليه الإشارة بقوله تعالى من قبل أن يأتي أحدكم الموت فيقول رب لولا أخرتني إلى أجل قريب فأصدق وأكن من الصالحين ولن يؤخر الله نفسا إذا جاء أجلها فقيل الأجل القريب الذي يطلبه معناه أنه يقول عند كشف الغطاء للعبد يا ملك الموت أخرني يوما أعتذر فيه إلى ربي وأتوب وأتزود صالحا لنفسي فيقول فنيت الأيام فلا يوم فيقول فأخرني ساعة فيقول فنيت الساعات فلا ساعة فيغلق عليه باب التوبة فيتغرغر بروحه وتتردد أنفاسه في شراسفه ويتجرع غصة اليأس عن التدارك وحسرة الندامة على تضييع
34:54.english: I say: Every human being is never free from disobedience of the bodily members (jawāriḥ), for even the prophets were not free from it — as has come down in the Qurʾān and the reports concerning the sins of the prophets, their repentance, and their weeping over their misdeeds. And if one is free, in some states, from disobedience of the members, he is not free from the heart's inclination (hamm) toward sins. And if he is free, in some states, from the inclination, he is not free from the whispering of Satan (waswās al-shayṭān) by way of importing scattered thoughts that divert from the remembrance of God. And if he is free from that, he is not free from heedlessness (ghaflah) and deficiency in knowledge of God, His attributes, and His acts. All of that is deficiency (nuqṣān), and it has causes; and abandoning its causes by occupying oneself with their opposites is a reversion from one path to its contrary. The meaning of "repentance" (tawbah) is "returning" (rujūʿ), and it is inconceivable that a human being should be entirely free of this deficiency — rather, people differ only in degrees. As for the principle itself, it is unavoidable. For this reason, he (peace be upon him) said: "Truly, a veil is cast over my heart, so that I seek forgiveness from God seventy times a day and night" (1) — the hadith. And for this reason, God (exalted be He) honored him by saying: {«لِيَغْفِرَ لَكَ اللَّهُ مَا تَقَدَّمَ مِنْ ذَنْبِكَ وَمَا تَأَخَّرَ»} [That God may forgive you what has passed of your sin and what remains]. And if this was his state, how then is the state of anyone else?
34:54.section_title_en: On the Universality of Repentance (Tawbah) and Its Obligation in Every Breath
34:54.anchors:
- Root: توب (T-W-B)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of "returning" (rujūʿ) — turning back from a path to its opposite; the root denotes the act of revisiting and reversing a prior state.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Tawbah is "abandoning the sin in the most excellent manner" — the most complete form of excuse; in sacred law (sharʿ), it is abandoning the sin due to its ugliness, regretting what has passed, resolving not to return, and rectifying what can be rectified of past deeds through renewed acts.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): "He repented to God from his sin" (tāba al-ʿabdu ilā Allāhi min dhanbihi). Metaphorical (majāz): The extension of "repentance" to inner purification of the heart from accumulated rust (rayn), as the root's sense of "returning" is applied to the soul's reversion from negligence to vigilance.
- Root: قلب (Q-L-B)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The heart as the organ of turning and overturning (taqlīb) — its state fluctuates between illumination and darkness, purity and rust.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Turning a thing" is directing it from one face to another; the heart (qalb) is so named for its constant overturning between states — a key metaphysical anchor for Ghazali's doctrine of the heart's susceptibility to stains (akdār) and polish (ṣaqal).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "He turned the thing over" (qalaba al-shayʾ). Metaphorical: "The heart is rusted" (qalb wajīb) — the inner organ's receptivity to impressions, whether dark (from sins) or luminous (from obedience).
- Root: وجب (W-J-B)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Obligation as fixed establishment (thubūt); what is due and settled upon a person.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Wājib has two senses: (1) that whose non-existence entails a contradiction (metaphysical necessity), and (2) that whose neglect merits blame — subdivided into what reason deems obligatory (e.g., knowing divine unity) and what the Law deems obligatory (e.g., acts of worship). Ghazali here exploits this dual sense to distinguish legal obligation (fatwā) from the higher obligation of the path (ṭarīq).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "It became incumbent upon him" (wajaba ʿalayhi). Metaphorical: The extension to "the heart's palpitation" (wajīb) — the inner agitation of one who realizes the urgency of repentance before death.
- Sibawayh Rule: Restriction and Focused Predication (al-ḥaṣr wa al-taqyīd bi-innamā) — governing the Quranic citations {«إِنَّمَا التَّوْبَةُ عَلَى اللَّهِ»} and {«وَلَيْسَتِ التَّوْبَةُ لِلَّذِينَ»}, where innamā restricts the predicate to a specific subject, delimiting the scope of accepted repentance to those who turn before death's arrival and before the rust hardens into a seal.
34:54.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Remembrance of Death and Afterlife'

35:5.arabic: اعلم أن قوله تعالى {فلا تغرنكم الحياة الدنيا ولا يغرنكم بالله الغرور} وقوله تعالى {ولكنكم فتنتم أنفسكم وتربصتم وارتبتم وغرتكم الأماني} الآية كاف في ذم الغرور وقد قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم حبذا نوم الأكياس وفطرهم كيف يغبنون سهر الحمقى واجتهادهم ولمثقال ذرة من صاحب تقوى ويقين أفضل من ملء الأرض من المغترين (1) حديث الكيس من دان نفسه وعمل لما بعد الموت الحديث أخرجه الترمذي وابن ماجه من حديث شداد بن أوس وكل ما ورد في فضل العلم وذم الجهل فهو دليل على ذم الغرور لأن الغرور عبارة عن بعض أنواع الجهل إذ الجهل
35:5.english: Know that the saying of God Most High — {«fa-lā taghurrannakum al-ḥayātu al-dunyā wa-lā yaghurrannakum billāhi al-gharūr»} (So let not the life of this world deceive you, nor let the Deceiver deceive you concerning God) — and His saying — {«wa-lākinnakum fatantum anfusakum wa-tarabbastum wa-irtabtum wa-gharratkum al-amānī»} (But ye tempted your own souls, and ye waited, and ye doubted, and vain desires deceived you) — is sufficient for the blameworthiness of self-deception (al-ghurūr). And the Messenger of God, may God's peace and blessing be upon him, has said: "How excellent is the sleep of the intelligent and their breaking of the fast! How they outwit the wakefulness of the foolish and their striving! And verily a mustard-seed's weight [of faith] from a possessor of piety and certainty is better than the earth filled with the self-deceived." And the ḥadīth: "The intelligent man (al-kayyis) is he who takes account of his own soul and works for what is after death" — this ḥadīth was transmitted by al-Tirmidhī and Ibn Mājah from the ḥadīth of Shaddād ibn Aws.
35:5.section_title_en: Exposition of the Blameworthiness of Self-Deception (Al-Ghurūr), Its Reality, and Its Examples
35:5.anchors:
- Root: غرر (Gh-R-R)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The core meaning is "an apparent trace or mark of a thing" (al-athar al-ẓāhir), from which derives "the blaze of a horse" (ghurrat al-faras). To deceive (gharra) is to strike one's heedlessness (ghirrah) and attain one's sought desire from him, as if folding a garment upon its original crease (ṭawāhu ʿalā gharrihi).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Ghurrah is heedlessness in wakefulness, and ghirār is heedlessness with drowsiness." Theologically, it is the soul's repose upon a false semblance (shubhah) that pleases the caprice (hawā), rendering one oblivious to the true state of affairs—as in {«mā gharraka bi-rabbika al-karīm»} (What deceived thee concerning thy Generous Lord?).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): "A gazelle in a moonlit night is called agharr" because it ventures out thinking it is day and is devoured by beasts—heedlessness in perception. Metaphorical (majāz): "A day agharr muḥajjal" (a white-browed, white-legged day) for intense heat, transferring the blaze of a horse to the day's visible intensity.
- Root: جهل (J-H-L)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "Jahila bihi" — to be ignorant of it; "jāhala ʿalā qawmihi" — to act foolishly/insolently against one's people. The pre-Islamic era is "al-jāhiliyyah al-jahlā'" (the utterly ignorant age).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Ignorance (jahl) is of three kinds: (1) the soul's emptiness of knowledge (this is the root); (2) believing a thing contrary to what it is; (3) doing a thing contrary to what it ought to be, whether one's belief is sound or corrupt. Ghurūr is a species of the second kind—a false belief arising from a corrupt semblance.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "Kafā bil-shakki jahlā" (Sufficient is doubt as ignorance). Metaphorical: "Istajhalat al-rīḥ al-ghuṣn" (The wind made the branch sway violently) — transferred from mental foolishness to physical agitation.
- Root: حدث (Ḥ-D-TH)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "Al-ḥudūth: the coming-to-be of a thing after it was not." "Al-ḥadath: the novel event." "Ḥaddatha: to speak/communicate."
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Ḥudūth is the existence of a thing after non-existence, whether accident or substance. Iḥdāth is bringing it into existence. The iḥdāth of substances belongs to God alone." The "ḥadīth" (report/speech) is so-called for its temporal novelty.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "Nazalat bihi ḥawādith al-dahr" (The vicissitudes of time befell him). Metaphorical: "Kāna ʿUmar muḥaddathan" (Umar was one inspired with true discernment) — as if he were spoken to (ḥudditha) by what he conjectured.
- Root: دنا (D-N-W)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "Danā fa-huwa dānin" — he drew near. "Al-dunyā" (the lower world) is so named because it is nearer (danat) and precedes the Hereafter.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Al-dunūw: proximity by essence or by judgment, used of place, time, and station." The "adnā" (lower/nearer) is contrasted with the greater and with the better: {«a-tastabdilūna alladhī huwa adnā billadhī huwa khayr»} (Will ye take the lower in exchange for what is better?).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "Huwa danī' min al-adniyā'" (He is base, of the base ones) — but this is the homonym danu'a (baseness), distinct from danā (nearness). The dunyā's "nearness" is its temporal immediacy versus the Hereafter's deferral.
- Sibawayh Rule: Bab al-faṣl bayna al-jār wa-al-majrūr (Prepositional Interposition) — The particle "bi" in {«wa-lā yaghurrannakum billāhi al-gharūr»} governs the deceiver (al-gharūr) as the agent of deception, while "billāh" (concerning God) is the object of the deception. The syntactic structure permits the deceiver to be named after the prepositional phrase, indicating that the deception is *about* God's attributes (His forbearance, His respite) — a grammatical subtlety showing the ghurūr deceives *by means of* false notions of God, not that God Himself deceives.
35:5.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Remembrance of Death and Afterlife'

35:5.arabic: ويحك يا نفس لا ينبغى أن تغرك الحياة الدنيا ولا يغرنك بالله الغرور فانظرى لنفسك فما أمرك بمهم لغيرك ولا تضيعى أوقاتك فالأنفاس معدودة فإذا مضى منك نفس فقد ذهب بعضك فاغتنمى الصحة قبل السقم والفراغ قبل الشغل والغنى قبل الفقر والشباب قبل الهرم والحياة قبل الموت واستعدي للآخرة على قدر بقائك فيها يا نفس أما تستعدين للشتاء بقدر طول مدته فتجمعين له القوت والكسوة والحطب وجميع الأسباب ولا تتكلين في ذلك على فضل الله وكرمه حتى يدفع عنك البرد من غير جبة ولبد وحطب وغير ذلك فإنه قادر على ذلك أفتظنين أيتها النفس أن زمهرير جهنم
35:5.english: ...from creation, but rather you attain your goal through every stratagem. And by this ignorance you deserve the title of foolishness from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, where he said: "The shrewd one is he who holds his soul to account and works for what comes after death, and the foolish one is he who follows his soul's whims and harbors vain hopes upon God." {«الكيس من دان نفسه وعمل لما بعد الموت والأحمق من أتبع نفسه هواها وتمنى على الله الأماني»}
35:5.section_title_en: Section 1253 — The Soul's Self-Reproach and the Awakening from Negligence
35:5.anchors:
- Root: نفس (n-f-s)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The self, soul, or spirit; that which animates and is addressed as an independent moral agent.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The soul as the locus of divine address and self-knowledge; its essence (dhāt) is the referent of God's "self" in revelation, yet here it is the reproaching subject.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (haqīqah) usage as the speaking, desiring self; metaphorical (majāz) extension to blame and counsel, as in "self-accusation" (lawwāmah).
- Root: موت (m-w-t)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Death as the cessation of life; the inevitable terminus of every soul.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Death as separation (furqah) from worldly attachments and the transition to reckoning; linked to the soul's journey.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal death of the body; metaphorical "death" of the heart through heedlessness, contrasted here with physical death as the ultimate wake-up call.
- Root: جهل (j-h-l)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Ignorance as the absence of knowledge; folly and rashness.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Ignorance as the soul's failure to perceive true realities, leading to misplaced desires and false hopes.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal ignorance of facts; metaphorical ignorance as moral stupidity, as when the soul follows whims despite clear signs.
- Root: دنا (d-n-w)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Nearness in place, time, or rank.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Drawing near (dunūw) to God through obedience, contrasted with the soul's clinging to the near (dunyā) world.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal proximity; metaphorical use for the "lower" world (dunyā) as that which is nearer and inferior.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — Used to emphasize exclusive causation, e.g., "God's generosity is only in guiding you to the path," restricting divine favor to guidance, not exemption from effort.
