Swimming can be learned; but as for walking upon water, it is not acquired by instruction, but rather is attained through the strength of certainty (yaqīn). For this reason it was said to the Prophet, peace be upon him, that Jesus, peace be upon him, was said to have walked upon water, and he, peace be upon him, said: "Had his certainty increased, he would have walked upon the air." {«حديث قيل له يقال إن عيسى مشى على الماء قال لو ازداد يقينا لمشي على الهواء»} — This hadith is rejected (munkar) and is not known in this form. What is known is what Ibn Abi al-Dunya narrated in the Book of Certainty from the saying of Bakr ibn Abd Allah al-Muzani, who said: The disciples lost their Prophet, and it was said to them: "He has headed toward the sea." So they set out seeking him, and when they reached the sea, behold, he was coming toward them walking upon the water. And he mentioned a hadith in which Jesus said: "If the son of Adam had a hair's breadth of certainty, he would walk upon the water." And Abu Mansur al-Daylami narrated in the Musnad al-Firdaws with a weak chain from the hadith of Muadh ibn Jabal: "If you knew God with true knowledge, you would walk upon the seas, and the mountains would be removed by your supplications." These are symbols and allusions to the meaning of aversion (karāhah) and love (maḥabbah), and good pleasure (riḍā) and wrath (ghaḍab), and gratitude (shukr) and ingratitude (kufrān) — more than this is not fitting for the science of practical conduct (ʿilm al-muʿāmalah). And God, exalted be He, struck an example of this to draw it near to the understanding of creatures, since He knew that He created the jinn and mankind only to worship Him, and their worship was the ultimate purpose of wisdom (ghāyat al-ḥikmah) with respect to them. Then He informed that He has two servants: one whom He loves, whose name is Gabriel — the Holy Spirit and the Trustworthy One — and he is with Him beloved, obeyed, trustworthy, and honored; and another whom He hates, whose name is Iblis — the accursed one, reprieved until the Day of Judgment. Then He delegated guidance (irshād) to Gabriel, saying, the Exalted: {«قل نزله روح القدس من ربك بالحق»} "Say: The Holy Spirit has brought it down from your Lord with truth" (16:102), and said, the Exalted: {«يلقي الروح من أمره على من يشاء من عباده»} "He casts the Spirit of His command upon whom He wills of His servants" (40:15). And He delegated misguidance (ighwāʾ) to Iblis, saying, the Exalted: {«ليضل عن سبيله»} "That he may lead astray from His path" (4:119). And ighwāʾ is the halting of servants short of attaining the ultimate purpose of wisdom. So observe how He attributed it to the servant with whom He was wrathful; and guidance (irshād) is the conduct of them toward the ultimate purpose — so observe how He attributed it to the servant whom He loves. And you have an example of this in custom: when a king is in need of one to give him drink and one to cup him and to clean the courtyard of his house of filth, and he has two servants, he does not appoint for cupping and cleaning except the ugliest and meanest of them, and he does not entrust the carrying of drink and perfume except to the best and most complete of them and the most beloved to him. And you should not say: "This is my act, and his act was not without my act" — for you have erred when you attributed that to yourself. Rather, He is the One who directed your motive (dāʿiyah) to the specification of the disliked act to the disliked person, and the beloved act to the beloved person, as a completion of justice (ʿadl). For His justice is sometimes completed through matters in which you have no entry, and sometimes it is completed in you — for you also are among His acts. So your motive, your power, your knowledge, your action, and all the other causes of your movements in expression — all of this is His act, which He arranged with justice in an arrangement from which moderate acts issue forth. Except that you see only yourself, and so you suppose that what appears through you in the world of witness (ʿālam al-shahādah) has no cause from the world of the unseen and the dominion (ʿālam al-ghayb wa al-malakūt). Therefore you attribute it to yourself. And you are only like the child who looks at night at the play of the juggler (mushʿabadh) who brings forth figures from behind a curtain that dance and scream and rise and sit, composed of rags that do not move by themselves — rather, they are moved by fine hair-like threads that do not appear in the darkness of night, their ends in the hand of the juggler, who is hidden from the eyes of the children. So they rejoice and marvel, supposing that those rags dance and play and rise and sit. As for the intelligent ones, they know that this is a moving (taḥrīk) and not a self-movement, but perhaps they do not know its detailed modality. And the one who knows some of its detail does not know it as the juggler knows it, to whom the command belongs and in whose hand is the pulling. Likewise, the children of the people of this world — and all creatures are children relative to the scholars — look at these persons (ashkhāṣ) and suppose that they are the movers, and so they attribute [action] to them. And the scholars know that they are moved, except that they do not know the modality of the moving — and they are the majority. Except the knowers (ʿārifūn), the scholars, and those firmly rooted in knowledge (al-rāsikhūn), for they have perceived, with the sharpness of their sight, fine spider-web threads — nay, much finer than these — suspended from heaven, their ends attached to the persons of the people of the earth. Those threads are not perceived, due to their fineness, by these outward eyes. Then they witnessed the heads of those threads in their suspension-points (manāṭāt) to which they are attached, and they witnessed for those suspension-points handles (maqābiḍ) that are in the hands of the angels who move the heavens. And they also witnessed the angels of the heavens directed toward the bearers of the Throne (ḥamalat al-ʿarsh), awaiting what descends upon them of the command from the presence of Lordship (ḥaḍrat al-rubūbiyyah) — "they do not disobey God in what He commands them, and they do what they are commanded" (66:6). And He expressed these witnessed realities in the Qur'an, and it was said: {«وفي السماء رزقكم وما توعدون»} "And in the heaven is your provision and what you are promised" (51:22). And He expressed the waiting of the angels of the heavens for what descends upon them of decree and command, and it was said: "He created seven heavens and of the earth the like of them; {«يتنزل الأمر بينهن لتعلموا أن الله على كل شيء قدير وأن الله قد أحاط بكل شيء علما»} 'the command descends between them, that you may know that God is powerful over all things and that God encompasses all things in knowledge'" (65:12). These are matters whose interpretation (taʾwīl) none knows except God and those firmly rooted in knowledge (al-rāsikhūn fī al-ʿilm). And Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, expressed the exclusivity of those firmly rooted in knowledge to sciences that the understandings of creatures cannot bear, when he recited the saying of the Exalted: {«يتنزل الأمر بينهن»} "The command descends between them," and said: "Were I to mention what I know of the meaning of this verse, you would stone me" — and in another wording: "You would say he is an unbeliever."
40:15.section_title_en: On the Degrees of Proximity to God and the Hierarchy of Those Who Perfect Divine Wisdom
40:15.anchors:
- Root: سير (s-y-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "السير: الذهاب والسفر، وسار يسير سيرا ومسيرا، والسيارة: الرفقة المسافرة"
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "السير: الانتقال من مكان إلى مكان، ويستعار للسلوك في الدين والطريقة"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): [Literal] "سار القوم: مشوا" — [Metaphorical] "سار فيه السير: مضى في الأمر، وسار ذكره: انتشر، ومنه: سيرة فلان: طريقته"
- Root: مشي (m-sh-y)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "المشي: تردد الأركان على الأرض، والماشية: الإبل والغنم لانتقالها في المرعى"
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "المشي: الانتقال من مكان إلى مكان بإرادة، ويكنى به عن النميمة، وعن شرب المسهل"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): [Literal] "مشيت وتمشيت، وهي حسنة المشية" — [Metaphorical] "مشى بطنه، وأمشاه الدواء، واستمشيت بالدواء، ومنه: مشت المرأة: كثرت أولادها"
- Root: خلق (kh-l-q)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الخلق: التقدير، والخلق: الناس، والخليقة: الطبيعة، والخلق: السجية"
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الخلق أصله: التقدير المستقيم، ويستعمل في إبداع الشيء من غير أصل ولا احتذاء"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): [Literal] "خلق الخراز الأديم: قدره قبل القطع" — [Metaphorical] "خلق الله الخلق: أوجده على تقدير أوجبته الحكمة"
- Root: نفس (n-f-s)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "النفس: الروح، والذات، والشيء النفيس"
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "النفس: الروح، وتطلق على الذات، قال تعالى: {ويحذركم الله نفسه} فنفسه: ذاته"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): [Literal] "شيء نفيس ومنفس" — [Metaphorical] "دفق نفسه أي دمه، وأصابته نفس: عين"
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — Used to distinguish exclusive attribution of actions to God versus creatures, as in "إنما أنت مثل الصبي" (You are only like a child), restricting the simile to the creature while preserving divine agency.
40:15.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

40:16.arabic: عملا صالحا وآخر سيئا وقد يخفى عليهم ولا يخفى على الله تعالى أن الغالب حسناتهم أو سيئاتهم ولكن يأبى الله إلا أن يعرفهم ذلك ليبين فضله عند العفو وعدله عند العقاب فتتطاير الصحف والكتب منطوية على الحسنات والسيئات وينصب الميزان وتشخص الأبصار إلى الكتب أتقع فى اليمين أو فى الشمال ثم إلى لسان الميزان أيميل إلى جانب السيئات أو إلى جانب الحسنات وهذه حالة هائلة تطيش فيها عقول الخلائق وروى الحسن أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كان رأسه فى حجر عائشة رضي الله عنها فنعس فذكرت الآخرة فبكت حتى سال دمعها ف
40:16.english: Then do not neglect reflection upon the Balance (al-Mīzān) and the flying of the scrolls to the right hands and the left hands, for the people after the questioning are three groups: {a group} having no good deeds — so a black neck emerges from the Fire, snatching them up as a bird snatches seeds, folding over them, and casting them into the Fire; the Fire swallows them, and a proclamation is made over them: "Wretchedness, after which there is no felicity!" Another group has no evil deeds — so a herald calls out: "Let those who praised God in every circumstance stand forth!" They rise and are sped to Paradise. Then this is done for the people of night prayer (qiyām al-layl), then for those whom neither the commerce of the world nor trade distracted from the remembrance of God Almighty. A proclamation is made over them: "Felicity, after which there is no wretchedness!" A third group remains — and they are the majority — who mixed a righteous deed with another evil one. It may be hidden from them, but it is not hidden from God Almighty whether their good deeds or their evil deeds predominate. Yet God refuses except to make this known to them, to manifest His bounty at the time of pardon and His justice at the time of punishment. So the pages and scrolls fly, folded up with the good deeds and the evil deeds, and the Balance is erected, and the eyes strain toward the scrolls — will they fall to the right or to the left? — then toward the tongue of the Balance — does it incline toward the side of evil deeds or toward the side of good deeds? This is a stupendous state in which the intellects of creatures reel. Al-Ḥasan narrated that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had his head in the lap of ʿĀʾishah, may God be pleased with her, and he dozed off. She mentioned the Hereafter and wept until her tears flowed and dripped upon the cheek of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. He awoke and said: "What makes you weep, O ʿĀʾishah?" She said: "I mentioned the Hereafter — will you remember your families on the Day of Resurrection?" He said: "By Him in Whose hand is my soul, in three places no one will remember anyone but himself: when the Balances are set up and the deeds are weighed, until the son of Adam sees whether his Balance is light or heavy; and at the scrolls, until he sees whether he takes his book in his right hand or his left; and at the Bridge (al-Ṣirāṭ)." And on the authority of Anas: The son of Adam is brought on the Day of Resurrection until he is made to stand between the two pans of the Balance, and an angel is appointed over him. If his Balance is heavy, the angel calls out with a voice heard by all creatures: "So-and-so has prospered — a prosperity after which he will never be wretched!" And if his Balance is light, he calls out with a voice heard by all creatures: "So-and-so has been wretched — a wretchedness after which he will never prosper!" And when the pan of good deeds is light, the Zabāniyah (the keepers of Hell) advance, holding iron maces, wearing garments of fire, and they seize the portion of the Fire and drag them to the Fire. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: "On the Day of Resurrection — it is a day on which God Almighty calls to Adam, upon him peace, saying: 'Rise, O Adam, and send forth the contingent of the Fire!' He says: 'And how many is the contingent of the Fire?' He says: 'From every thousand, nine hundred and ninety-nine.'" When the Companions heard this, they were stricken dumb until they could not even smile. When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, saw what his Companions were experiencing, he said: "Work and rejoice! For by Him in Whose hand is the soul of Muḥammad, there are with you two creatures who have never been with any people except that they increased their number — among those who perished from the sons of Adam and the sons of Iblīs." They said: "And who are they, O Messenger of God?" He said: "Gog and Magog (Yaʾjūj and Maʾjūj)." He said: "Then the distress lifted from the people, and he said: 'Work and rejoice! For by Him in Whose hand is the soul of Muḥammad, you are among the people on the Day of Resurrection only like a mole on the flank of a camel, or like a small mark on the foreleg of a beast.'"
40:16.section_title_en: The Description of the Balance (Ṣifat al-Mīzān)
40:16.anchors:
- Root: ميز (m-y-z)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Separation and distinction between things; al-Farahidi notes its core sense of division and discernment.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الميز والتمييز: الفصل بين المتشابهات" — the act of distinguishing between similars; the Balance (Mīzān) is the instrument of divine discrimination between good and evil deeds.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): physical weighing and separation; Metaphorical (Majaz): "تكاد تميز من الغيظ" — near-bursting from rage, indicating the intense emotional state described here.
- Root: حسن (ḥ-s-n)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Beauty, goodness, excellence; what is pleasing and praiseworthy.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الحسن: عبارة عن كل مبهج مرغوب فيه" — that which delights and is desired, whether by intellect, inclination, or sense; "ḥasanah" (good deed) is what brings joy to the soul.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: visible beauty and virtue; Metaphorical: "فلان لا يحسن شيئا" — one who does nothing well; here, "ḥasanāt" are the meritorious acts weighed in the Balance.
- Root: رسل (r-s-l)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Sending forth with ease and gentleness; a messenger dispatched.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "أصل الرسل: الانبعاث على التؤدة" — originary sending with deliberation; "رسول" is one sent; here, the "ṣuḥuf" (scrolls) are dispatched to right and left.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: sending letters or envoys; Metaphorical: "السهام رسل المنايا" — arrows as messengers of fate; the flying scrolls are dispatched as divine missives.
- Root: يوم (y-w-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: A day, from sunrise to sunset; extended to any period of time.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "اليوم يعبر به عن وقت طلوع الشمس إلى غروبه... وقد يعبر به عن مدة من الزمان" — the Day of Resurrection is a prolonged epoch of reckoning.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: a measured span; Metaphorical: "أيام الله" — God's mighty deeds and calamities upon the wicked; here, the terrors of that Day.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — Allowing separation between a governing verb and its governed prepositional phrase for rhetorical emphasis, as in "يوقف بين كفتي الميزان" (he is made to stand between the two pans of the Balance), where the spatial imagery is foregrounded.
40:16.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Remembrance of Death and Afterlife'

40:16.arabic: الأمر كذلك سمعوا عند ذلك نداء المنادي {لمن الملك اليوم لله الواحد القهار} ولقد كان الملك لله الواحد القهار كل يوم لا ذلك على الخصوص ولكن الغافلين لا يسمعون هذا النداء إلا ذلك اليوم فهو نبأ عما يتجدد للغافلين من كشف الأحوال حيث لا ينفعهم الكشف فنعوذ بالله الحليم الكريم من الجهل والعمى فإنه أصل أسباب الهلاك بيان تمييز ما يحبه الله تعالى عما يكرهه اعلم إن فعل الشكر وترك الكفر لا يتم إلا بمعرفة ما يحبه الله تعالى عما يكرهه إذ معنى الشكر استعمال نعمه تعالى في محابه ومعنى الكفر نقيض ذلك إما بترك الاستعمال أو
40:16.english: ...and there is no omnipotent one save the King, the Compeller. And when the covering is lifted from the eyes of the heedless, and they behold the matter to be thus, they will hear at that time the call of the Proclaimer: {«لِمَنِ الْمُلْكُ الْيَوْمَ لِلَّهِ الْوَاحِدِ الْقَهَّارِ»} — "To whom belongs the sovereignty this Day? To God, the One, the Compeller" {Q 40:16}. And indeed sovereignty belonged to God, the One, the Compeller, every single day — not exclusively on that day — but the heedless do not hear this proclamation save on that day. Thus it is tidings of what is renewed for the heedless of the unveiling of states, at a time when the unveiling will not benefit them. So we seek refuge in God, the Forbearing, the Generous, from ignorance and blindness, for it is the root cause of destruction.
40:16.section_title_en: The Unveiling of Sovereignty and the Discernment of What God Loves from What He Abhors
40:16.anchors:
- Root: كشف (kashafa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Removal of a covering; disclosure of what was hidden.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Unveiling of the unseen realities (mukāshafah) — the lifting of the veil from the heart's eye to perceive things as they truly are.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): removal of a physical covering. Metaphorical (majāz): the disclosure of intellectual or spiritual realities to the percipient.
- Root: ملك (malaka)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Possession, dominion, sovereignty; the one who possesses is malik (king).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): True sovereignty (mulk) belongs exclusively to God; all created dominion is borrowed and ephemeral.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: royal authority. Metaphorical: absolute, unshared dominion — as in the Qur'anic proclamation of sole kingship on the Day of Judgment.
- Root: شكر (shakara)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Gratitude; acknowledgment of beneficence.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Thankfulness is the recognition of the Benefactor and the employment of His blessings in that which pleases Him — not mere verbal praise.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: requital of favor. Metaphorical: the use of blessings in obedience to the Giver, which is the true meaning of gratitude.
- Root: كفر (kafara)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Covering, concealing; ingratitude that veils the recognition of favor.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Kufr is the covering of blessings by failing to employ them in the manner intended by the Giver, or by employing them in what He abhors.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: covering a seed in the earth. Metaphorical: the concealment of God's blessings through misuse or neglect.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Restriction and Focused Predication (al-ḥaṣr wa al-taqyīd bi-innamā) — restricting the means of gratitude to two exclusive cognitive faculties, and the restriction of creation's purpose to the sole end of attaining unto God.
40:16.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

40:17.arabic: الجبار جل جلاله اليوم تجزى كل نفس بما كسبت لا ظلم اليوم فعند ذلك ينخلع قلبك من الهيبة وتوقن نفسك بالبوار وتتذكر ما أنذرك الله تعالى على لسان رسوله حيث قال ولا تحسبن الله غافلا عما يعمل الظالمون إنما يؤخرهم ليوم تشخص فيه الأبصار مهطعين مقنعي رءوسهم لا يرتد إليهم طرفهم وأفئدتهم هواء وأنذر الناس الآية فما أشد فرحك اليوم بتمضمضك باعراض الناس ويناولك أموالهم وما أشد حسراتك في ذلك اليوم إذا وقف ربك على بساط العدل وشوفهت بخطاب السياسة وأنت مفلس فقير عاجز مهين لا تقدر على أن ترد حقا أو تظهر عذرا فعند ذلك تؤخذ ح
40:17.english: Know that none is saved from the peril of the Scale except him who, in this world, called his own soul to account, and weighed therein — by the scale of the Sacred Law — his deeds, his words, his passing thoughts, and his glances, just as ʿUmar — may God be well pleased with him — said: "Call yourselves to account before you are called to account, and weigh yourselves before you are weighed." Indeed, his calling himself to account consists in his repenting, before death, from every act of disobedience with a sincere repentance (tawbah naṣūḥ), and in his making up for what was neglected of his shortcomings regarding the obligatory commands of God — may He be exalted — and in his restoring rights to those he wronged, grain by grain, and in his seeking absolution from everyone whom he harmed by his tongue, his hand, or his evil suspicion harbored in his heart — and this by winning their hearts' contentment — until he dies with no outstanding wrong against him, nor any neglected obligation.
40:17.section_title_en: The Perils of the Scale and the Reckoning of Wrongs Against Others
40:17.anchors:
- Root: وزن (w-z-n)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning is weighing, measuring, and balancing; al-mīzān (the Scale) is the instrument of equitable judgment.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In theological context, al-mīzān is the divine instrument of justice on the Day of Resurrection, weighing deeds to manifest equitable recompense, not a corporeal balance.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) usage denotes physical weighing; metaphorical (majāz) usage extends to moral and spiritual accounting, as in "weighing one's deeds by the scale of the Sacred Law."
- Sibawayh Rule: Conditional and Exceptive Constructions (الشّرط والاستثناء) — governing the protasis-apodosis structure in "whoever's scales are heavy... whoever's scales are light," and the exceptive force in "none is saved... except he who reckons."
40:17.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Remembrance of Death and Afterlife'

40:17.arabic: وظهرت منكم العيوب والأسرار هنالك تجزى كل نفس بما كسبت إن الله عز وجل يقول ليجزى الذي أساءوا بما عملوا ويجزى الذي أحسنوا بالحسنى وقال تعالى {ووضع الكتاب فترى المجرمين مشفقين مما فيه} الآية جعلنا الله وإياكم عاملين بكتابة متبعين لأوليائه حتى يحلنا وإياكم دار المقامة من فضله إنه حميد مجيد وقال بعض الحكماء الأيام سهام والناس أغراض والدهر يرميك كل يوم بسهامه ويخترمك بلياليه وأيامه حتى يستغرق جميع أجزائك فكيف بقاء سلامتك مع وقوع الأيام بك وسرعة الليالي في بدنك لو كشف لك عما أحدثت الأيام فيك من النقص لا
40:17.english: And indeed there has come the narration from him, from his Lord, Mighty and Glorious, that He said to Moses, peace be upon him: "When you see the rich man approaching, say: 'A sin whose punishment has been hastened.' And when you see the poor man approaching, say: 'Welcome to the badge of the righteous.'" And if you wish, you may follow the possessor of the Spirit and the Word, Jesus son of Mary, peace be upon him — for he used to say: "My condiment is hunger, my badge is fear, my garment is wool, my warmth in winter is the rising places of the sun, my lamp is the moon, my mount is my two feet, and my food and my fruit is what the earth brings forth. I pass the night and I possess nothing, and I rise in the morning and I possess nothing — and there is no one upon the earth richer than I."
40:17.section_title_en: The Revival of the Religious Sciences — Section 737: On the Censure of This World and the Description of Its Perils
40:17.anchors:
- Root: دنو (danuww)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "دنا فهو دانٍ" — proximity, nearness; the world (al-dunyā) is so named because it is nearer and lower, deferred from the Hereafter.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الدنو: القرب بالذات، أو بالحكم" — proximity by essence or by decree; used of place, time, and station. The "nearer" (al-adnā) is contrasted with the greater and the better.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical nearness. Metaphorical: the lower, contemptible station — "أهل الدناءة هم أهل الشناءة" (the people of baseness are the people of abhorrence).
- Root: يوم (yawm)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "اليوم" — a day; also any period of time.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "اليوم يعبر به عن وقت طلوع الشمس إلى غروبها. وقد يعبر به عن مدة من الزمان أي مدة كانت" — the day is the time from sunrise to sunset, or any duration whatsoever. "وذكرهم بأيام الله" — the days of God are His mighty deeds and calamities upon the disbelievers.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the solar day. Metaphorical: "أيام العرب" — their battles and vicissitudes; "أيام الله" — His punitive visitations.
- Root: وقد (waqada)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "وقدت النار تقد وقودا ووقدا" — the fire blazed; al-wuqūd is the fuel.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "وقودها الناس والحجارة" — the fuel of the Fire is men and stones; the one who kindles it for himself (istawqada) is he who seeks its light.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: kindling a fire. Metaphorical: "قلب وقاد" — a blazing, keen heart; "وقد الحصى" — the pebbles became scorching hot (i.e., the intensity of the sun's heat).
- Root: ألك (alaka)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "المألكة: الرسالة، لأنها تؤلك في الفم" — the message (risālah) is called ma'lakah because it is chewed/worked in the mouth.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الملائكة تقع على الواحد والجمع" — angels (malā'ikah) are so named as bearers of messages; "الله يصطفي من الملائكة رسلا" {«الله يصطفي من الملائكة رسلا»} — God chooses messengers from the angels.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: chewing (as a horse chews its bit). Metaphorical: delivering a message — the angel is the one who delivers the divine communication.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — "إنما" restricts the predicate to the subject alone, negating it of all else. Applied in the sermon: "إنما يتزين لي أوليائي بالذل والخوف" — My friends adorn themselves for Me ONLY with humility, fear, and submission — restricting their adornment to these alone, excluding all worldly ornament.

40:49.arabic: فيقولون ادعوا خزنة جهنم قال فيدعون خزنة جهنم أن ادعوا ربكم يخفف عنا يوما من العذاب فيقولون أو لم تك تأتيكم رسلكم بالبينات قالوا بلى قالوا فادعوا وما دعاء الكافرين إلا في ضلال قال فيقولون ادعوا مالكا فيدعون فيقولون يا مالك ليقض علينا ربك قال فيجيبهم إنكم ماكثون (4) قال الأعمش أنبئت أن بين دعائهم وبين إجابة مالك إياهم ألف عام قال فيقولون ادعوا ربكم فلا أحد خير من ربكم فيقولون ربنا غلبت علينا شقوتنا وكنا قوما ضالين ربنا أخرجنا منها فإن عدنا فإنا ظالمون قال فيجيبهم اخسئوا فيها ولا تكلمون {قال}
40:49.english: And ʿAlī, may God honor his face, said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: "Seek refuge in God from the Pit of Sorrow, or the Valley of Sorrow." It was said: "O Messenger of God, what is the Valley or Pit of Sorrow?" He said: "A valley in Hell from which Hell itself seeks refuge with God seventy times each day. God, the Exalted, has prepared it for the reciters who show off." (2)
40:49.section_title_en: The Vastness of Hellfire, Its Depths, and the Torments of Its Inhabitants
40:49.anchors:
- Root: و د ي (w-d-y)
  * Lisan / Ayn: A valley; a place where torrents flow. In the lexicon, it denotes a lowland or watercourse between mountains.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Used for the valleys of Hell as places of confinement and passage, each containing further branching ravines (شُعَب), indicating graded descent.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal for earthly valleys; here transferred (majāz) to the topographical reality of Hell, affirming its corporeal vastness.
- Root: ع م ق (ʿ-m-q)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Depth; the far bottom of a well or pit. Al-Farahidi: "العمق: قعر البئر ونحوها."
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Depth as a measure of descent; in the Hereafter, it is unbounded, paralleling the unbounded depth of worldly desire.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal for physical depth; here extended to show the infinite regress of punishment corresponding to infinite craving.
- Root: غ س ق (gh-s-q)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Stinking, foul pus or ichor that flows from the skin of the damned; also intense darkness.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-Ghassāq is the putrid effusion of Hell, a punishment for the senses, specifically for drinking when the damned cry out in thirst.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal for what is loathsome and fetid; in the Quranic context, it is the designated drink of the inhabitants.
- Root: ز ق م (z-q-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To swallow with difficulty; the tree of Zaqqūm, which grows in the depths of Hell.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): A specific tree in Hell whose fruit is like the heads of devils, eaten by the damned to fill their bellies, causing choking and agony.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal for a real tree; its description is sensory, not metaphorical, affirming the physical reality of punishment.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The periodic structure of "في جهنم سبعين ألف واد" allows the prepositional phrase to precede the subject for emphasis, establishing the spatial setting before detailing its contents.

40:52.arabic: على النار يفتنون يوم لا ينفع مال ولا بنون يوم لا ينفع الظالمين معذرتهم ولهم اللعنة ولهم سوء الدار يوم ترد فيه المعاذير وتبلى السرائر وتظهر الضمائر وتكشف الأستار يوم تخشع فيه الأبصار وتسكن الأصوات ويقل فيه الالتفات وتبرز الخفيات وتظهر الخطيئات يوم يساق العباد ومعهم الأشهاد ويشيب الصغير ويسكر الكبير فيومئذ وضعت الموازين ونشرت الدواوين وبرزت الجحيم وأغلى الحميم وزفرت النار ويئس الكفار وسعرت النيران وتغيرت الألوان وخرس اللسان ونطقت جوارح الإنسان فيا أيها الإنسان ما غرك بربك الكريم حيث أغلقت الأبواب وأرخيت الستور واستترت عن الخلائق فقارفت الفجور
40:52.english: So prepare yourself, O wretched one, for this Day of immense magnitude, of prolonged duration, of overwhelming dominion, whose appointed time is near — a Day when you shall see the heaven split asunder, and the stars scattered in its terror, and the shining planets extinguished, and the sun folded up, and the mountains set in motion, and the pregnant camels neglected, and the wild beasts gathered together, and the seas set ablaze, and the souls paired with their bodies, and the Hellfire ignited, and Paradise brought near, and the mountains pulverized, and the earth stretched out — a Day when you shall see the earth shaken with its quaking, and the earth casts forth its burdens. On that Day shall people issue forth in scattered groups to be shown their deeds — a Day when the earth and the mountains are lifted and crushed with a single crushing. Then on that Day the Imminent Event shall come to pass, and the heaven shall split open, for on that Day it shall be frail, and the angels shall be at its edges, and eight shall bear the Throne of your Lord above them on that Day. On that Day you shall be presented — no secret of yours shall remain hidden. A Day when the mountains shall move and you shall see the earth laid bare — a Day when the earth shall be shaken with a violent shaking, and the mountains crumbled to dust, becoming scattered particles — a Day when people shall be like scattered moths, and the mountains like carded wool — a Day when every nursing mother shall forget what she nursed, and every pregnant female shall cast down her burden, and you shall see people drunk, yet they are not drunk, but the chastisement of God is severe — a Day when the earth shall be changed to other than this earth, and the heavens, and they shall appear before God, the One, the All-Compelling — a Day when the mountains shall be blown away as dust, leaving a level, bare plain, wherein you see no crookedness nor curve — a Day when you see the mountains and suppose them solid, yet they pass by like the passing of clouds — a Day when the heaven shall split open and become rosy like molten oil. Then on that Day no human nor jinn shall be asked about his sin. A Day when the disobedient shall be prevented from speech, and shall not be asked about their crimes, but shall be seized by their forelocks and their feet — a Day when every soul shall find what it did of good brought forth present, and what it did of evil, wishing that between it and that evil there were a far distance — a Day when every soul shall know what it has sent ahead, and shall witness what it has forwarded and what it has left behind — a Day when tongues shall be struck mute and the bodily members shall speak — a Day whose mention turned the hair of the Master of the Messengers white, when al-Ṣiddīq (may God be pleased with him) said to him: "I see that you have turned white-haired, O Messenger of God." He said: "Sūrat Hūd and its sisters have made me white-haired" — namely, al-Wāqiʿah, al-Mursalāt, ʿAmma Yatasāʾalūn, and Idhā al-Shamsu Kuwwirat.
40:52.section_title_en: The Names and Attributes of the Day of Resurrection — An Exhortation to the Negligent
40:52.anchors:
- Root: يوم (yawm)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "اليوم: وقت طلوع الشمس إلى غروبها، وقد يعبر به عن مدة من الزمان أي مدة كانت" — the day as a temporal span, extended metaphorically to any epoch or era.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "اليوم يعبر به عن وقت طلوع الشمس إلى غروبها. وقد يعبر به عن مدة من الزمان أي مدة كانت" — theological usage denotes the appointed time of reckoning, magnified by divine attribution (أيام الله).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): a measured solar period. Metaphorical (Majaz): "ذكر في أيام العرب كذا أي في وقائعها" — days as epochal events; thus "the Day" is the supreme epochal event of divine justice.
- Root: نفس (nafs)
  * Lisan / Ayn: النفس: الروح والذات — the self, soul, or very essence.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "النفس: الروح... وقوله: ويحذركم الله نفسه فنفسه: ذاته" — nafs as the innermost reality of a being; in the eschatological context, souls are "paired" (زوجت) with bodies for judgment.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the soul as life-principle. Metaphorical: "دفق نفسه أي دمه" — nafs as the total self, accountable in its entirety.
- Root: ارض (arḍ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: الأرض: الجرم المقابل للسماء — the earth as the corporeal substratum beneath the heavens.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الأرض: الجرم المقابل للسماء... ويعبر بها عن أسفل الشيء" — the earth as the lowest register of creation, subject to total transformation on that Day.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the physical earth. Metaphorical: "تأرض فلان: لزم الأرض" — to cling low; on that Day the earth itself is leveled, flattened, and replaced.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد (Restriction & Focused Predication) — The repeated "يوم" clauses function as temporal restrictors (ẓurūf) binding each predicate to that single, all-encompassing moment; the accumulation of names (أسامي) serves not as mere repetition but as focused predication upon the multifarious realities of a single event.

42:47.arabic: ينطقون ولا يؤذن لهم فيعتذرون يوم لا مرد له من الله يوم هم بارزون ويوم هم على النار يفتنون يوم لا ينفع مال ولا بنون يوم لا ينفع الظالمين معذرتهم ولهم اللعنة ولهم سوء الدار يوم ترد فيه المعاذير وتبلى السرائر وتظهر الضمائر وتكشف الأستار يوم تخشع فيه الأبصار وتسكن الأصوات ويقل فيه الالتفات وتبرز الخفيات وتظهر الخطيئات يوم يساق العباد ومعهم الأشهاد ويشيب الصغير ويسكر الكبير فيومئذ وضعت الموازين ونشرت الدواوين وبرزت الجحيم وأغلى الحميم وزفرت النار ويئس الكفار وسعرت النيران وتغيرت الألوان وخرس اللسان

42:47.arabic: وسلم قال من كانت لأخيه عنده مظلمة في عرض أو مال فليستحللها منه من قبل أن يأتي يوم ليس هناك دينار ولا درهم إنما يؤخذ من حسناته فإن لم يكن له حسنات أخذ من سيئات صاحبه فزيدت على سيئاته (1) وقالت عائشة رضي الله عنها لامرأة قالت لأخرى أنها طويلة الذيل قد اغتبتيها فاستحليها فإذن لا بد من الاستحلال إن قدر عليه فإن كان غائبا أو ميتا فينبغي أن يكثر له الاستغفار والدعاء ويكثر من الحسنات فإن قلت فالتحليل هل يجب فأقول لا لأنه تبرع والتبرع فضل وليس بواجب ولكنه مستحسن وسبيل المعتذر أن يبالغ في الثناء عليه والتودد إليه
42:47.english:
- Root: غيب (gh-y-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "To be absent, hidden, concealed from sight; ghayb = that which is unseen/absent from perception"
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الغيب: مصدر غابت الشمس وغيرها: إذا استترت عن العين — used of everything absent from the senses and from human knowledge; applied to things as ghayb/ghā'ib relative to people, not relative to God, for nothing is absent from Him"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Haqiqah: "تكلم بذلك عن ظهر الغيب" (speaking of the unseen); Majaz: "أتونا في غابة" (metaphorical extension to dense/thick things)
- Root: حسن (ḥ-s-n)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "Beauty, goodness, excellence; to be fair, comely, good"
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الحسن: عبارة عن كل مبهج مرغوب فيه — three kinds: good by reason, good by desire, good by sense; ḥasanah = everything that delights one, whether in self, body, or circumstances"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Haqiqah: "أنظر إلى محاسن وجهه" (physical beauty); Majaz: "فلان لا يحسن شيئًا" (to do well/excel — transferred to action)
- Root: حرم (ḥ-r-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "To forbid, prohibit, make unlawful; ḥarām = that which is forbidden"
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الحرام: الممنوع منه إما بتسخير إلهي وإما بشري — prohibition by divine decree, by human law, by coercive prevention, by reason, or by revelation"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Haqiqah: "هتك رحمته" (violating sanctity); Majaz: "جلد محرم: لم يدبغ" (raw hide — metaphorical extension to "untreated/unlawful")
- Root: ظلم (ẓ-l-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "Wrongdoing, injustice, oppression; to place something in other than its proper place"
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الظلمة: عدم النور — darkness is absence of light; used metaphorically for ignorance, polytheism, and sin, just as light is used for their opposites"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Haqiqah: "فلان يظلم فيظلم" (to wrong and be wronged); Majaz: "أرض مظلومة" (land never dug — metaphorical: "wronged" land)
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — "إنما يؤخذ من حسناته" restricts the taking exclusively to good deeds, excluding any monetary compensation on that Day.
42:47.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'Condemnation of Anger and Hatred'

42:47.arabic: الأماني فأخذته الحسرة والندامة وبدا له من الله ما لم يكن يحتسب فما ذكرناه بيان لبعض آفات الغفلة عن التفكر وهذا القدر في التوبة كاف وإذا كان الصبر ركنا من أركان دوام التوبة فلا بد من بيان الصبر فنذكره في كتاب مفرد إن شاء الله تعالى كتاب الصبر والشكر وهو الكتاب الثاني من ربع المنجيات من كتاب إحياء علوم الدين بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم الحمد لله أهل الحمد والثناء المنفرد برداء الكبرياء المتوحد بصفات المجد والعلاء المؤيد صفوة الأولياء بقوة الصبر على السراء والضراء والشكر على البلاء والنعماء والصلاة على
42:47.english: It has been related in a lengthy hadith that ʿAmmār ibn Yāsir stood up and said to ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib—may God honor his face—"O Commander of the Believers, inform us: upon what is unbelief (kufr) founded?" ʿAlī—may God be pleased with him—replied: "It is founded upon four pillars: harshness (jafāʾ), blindness (ʿamā), heedlessness (ghaflah), and doubt (shakk). Whoever is harsh holds truth in contempt, proclaims falsehood openly, and detests the scholars. Whoever is blind forgets the remembrance (dhikr). Whoever is heedless veers away from right guidance (rushd). And whoever doubts is deceived by vain hopes (amānī), so remorse (ḥasrah) and regret (nadāmah) seize him, and there appears to him from God that which he had never reckoned with."
42:47.section_title_en: The Book of Patience and Gratitude — Being the Second Book of the Quarter of Deliverance from The Revival of the Religious Sciences
42:47.anchors:
- Root: صبر (Ṣ-B-R)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of restraint and withholding; "ṣabara al-dābbah" = to hold back an animal from fodder; "ṣabara fulānan" = to confine someone with no exit.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Patience is the withholding of the soul in constriction... it is a general term whose names vary by context: if withholding the soul over a calamity, it is called ṣabr (patience), opposed by jazʿ (panic); if in battle, it is called shajāʿah (courage), opposed by jubn (cowardice)."
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Ḥaqīqah): "I bore patiently what I dislike, and I refrained patiently from what I love." Metaphorical (Majāz): "His right hand was made to swear earnestly (ṣubirat yamīnuhu)" — i.e., bound by an oath; "This tree is patient against cold" — i.e., resistant.
- Root: شكر (Sh-K-R)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Root denotes fullness and manifestation; "shakirat al-ḥalūbah" = the milch camel's udder became full.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Gratitude is the perception of the blessing and its manifestation... it is the inverse of kufr (ingratitude), which is forgetting and concealing the blessing. It has three kinds: gratitude of the heart (perceiving the blessing), of the tongue (praising the Bestower), and of the limbs (rewarding the blessing with obedience)."
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "I thanked God for His blessing." Metaphorical: "A grateful beast (dābbah shakūr)" — one satisfied with little fodder yet thriving on it.
- Root: وصف (W-Ṣ-F)
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Description is the mention of a thing by its attribute and quality; the attribute (ṣifah) is the state upon which the thing is found."
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "I described him with a description." Metaphorical: "Her face describes beauty" — i.e., it manifests it visibly.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Interposition between the Preposition and its Object (باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور) — governing the periodic suspension of grammatical dependency to allow parenthetical theological qualifications, as in "فإن الإيمان نصفان" where the predicate is deferred for rhetorical emphasis.
42:47.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Fear and Hope'

43:9.arabic: ولذلك قال عز وجل ولئن سألتهم من خلق السموات والأرض ليقولن الله وقال تعالى فأقم وجهك للدين حنيفا فطرة الله التي
43:9.english: The First Principle: the knowledge of His existence, the Exalted. The first thing by which one is illuminated from among the lights, and the path of reflection (ṭarīq al-iʿtibār) by which one proceeds, is that to which the Qurʾān has guided. For after the explanation of God, glorified be He, there is no explanation. He, the Exalted, has said: {«أَلَمْ نَجْعَلِ الْأَرْضَ مِهَادًا وَالْجِبَالَ أَوْتَادًا وَخَلَقْنَاكُمْ أَزْوَاجًا وَجَعَلْنَا نَوْمَكُمْ سُبَاتًا وَجَعَلْنَا اللَّيْلَ لِبَاسًا وَجَعَلْنَا النَّهَارَ مَعَاشًا وَبَنَيْنَا فَوْقَكُمْ سَبْعًا شِدَادًا وَجَعَلْنَا سِرَاجًا وَهَّاجًا وَأَنزَلْنَا مِنَ الْمُعْصِرَاتِ مَاءً ثَجَّاجًا لِّنُخْرِجَ بِهِ حَبًّا وَنَبَاتًا وَجَنَّاتٍ أَلْفَافًا»} — "Have We not made the earth a resting place, and the mountains as pegs, and created you in pairs, and made your sleep a repose, and made the night a covering, and made the day for livelihood, and built above you seven strong heavens, and made a blazing lamp, and sent down from the rain-clouds pouring water, that We may bring forth thereby grain and vegetation, and gardens dense with foliage?" (Q 78:6–16). And He, the Exalted, has said: {«إِنَّ فِي خَلْقِ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَاخْتِلَافِ اللَّيْلِ وَالنَّهَارِ وَالْفُلْكِ الَّتِي تَجْرِي فِي الْبَحْرِ بِمَا يَنفَعُ النَّاسَ وَمَا أَنزَلَ اللَّهُ مِنَ السَّمَاءِ مِن مَّاءٍ فَأَحْيَا بِهِ الْأَرْضَ بَعْدَ مَوْتِهَا وَبَثَّ فِيهَا مِن كُلِّ دَابَّةٍ وَتَصْرِيفِ الرِّيَاحِ وَالسَّحَابِ الْمُسَخَّرِ بَيْنَ السَّمَاءِ وَالْأَرْضِ لَآيَاتٍ لِّقَوْمٍ يَعْقِلُونَ»} — "Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth, and the alternation of the night and the day, and the ships which sail through the sea with that which benefits people, and what God has sent down from the sky of water, thereby reviving the earth after its death, and dispersing therein every creature, and the directing of the winds, and the clouds subservient between the heaven and the earth — are signs for a people who reason" (Q 2:164). And He, the Exalted, has said: {«أَلَمْ تَرَوْا كَيْفَ خَلَقَ اللَّهُ سَبْعَ سَمَاوَاتٍ طِبَاقًا وَجَعَلَ الْقَمَرَ فِيهِنَّ نُورًا وَجَعَلَ الشَّمْسَ سِرَاجًا وَاللَّهُ أَنبَتَكُم مِّنَ الْأَرْضِ نَبَاتًا ثُمَّ يُعِيدُكُمْ فِيهَا وَيُخْرِجُكُمْ إِخْرَاجًا»} — "Have you not seen how God created seven heavens in layers, and made the moon therein a light, and made the sun a lamp? And God caused you to grow from the earth a growth; then He returns you into it, and brings you forth a bringing forth" (Q 71:15–18). And He, the Exalted, has said: {«أَفَرَأَيْتُم مَّا تُمْنُونَ أَأَنتُمْ تَخْلُقُونَهُ أَمْ نَحْنُ الْخَالِقُونَ»} — "Have you considered what you emit? Do you create it, or are We the Creator?" — up to His saying: {«لِلْمُقْوِينَ»} — "for the settlers" (Q 56:58–73).
43:9.section_title_en: The Pillars of Faith: Knowledge of God, His Attributes, His Acts, and the Audibles — Section 87
43:9.anchors:
- Root: وجود (w-j-d)
  * Lisan / Ayn: [Core linguistic root meaning: to find, to perceive, to be; existence as that which is found or discovered]
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): [Theological/Kalam semantic nuance: al-wujūd as necessary existence (wujūb) versus contingent existence (imkān); the self-evident reality of the Creator's being]
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): [Literal vs Metaphorical distinction: haqīqah — existence as affirmed reality; majāz — "finding" as in discovery, not applicable to God's necessary being]
- Root: خلق (kh-l-q)
  * Lisan / Ayn: [Core linguistic root meaning: measuring, proportioning, fashioning; origination of a thing upon a measure]
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الخلق أصله: التقدير المستقيم، ويستعمل في إبداع الشيء من غير أصل ولا احتذاء" — creation as origination from nothing without prior model
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): [Literal: خلق الله الخلق: أوجده على تقدير أوجبته الحكمة — brought into existence upon a measure necessitated by wisdom; Majaz: not applicable to God's act as pure origination]
- Root: فطر (f-t-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: [Core linguistic root meaning: to split, cleave, rend; to originate, to bring forth as a new creation]
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "فطر الله الخلق" — God's origination of creation as a primordial act; "الفطرة" as the innate disposition
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): [Literal: فطر الله الخلق، وهو فاطر السموات: مبتدعها — originator without precedent; Majaz: "رأيه فطير" — immature opinion, not applicable to divine]
- Root: ارض (ar-d)
  * Lisan / Ayn: [Core linguistic root meaning: the earth, the lower sphere; that which is beneath]
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الأرض: الجرم المقابل للسماء" — the body opposite the heaven
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): [Literal: the earth as a resting place (مهادا); Majaz: not applicable in this context of divine creation]
- Root: ركن (r-k-n)
  * Lisan / Ayn: [Core linguistic root meaning: corner, pillar, support; that to which one leans for strength]
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "ركن الشيء: جانبه الذي يسكن إليه" — the side of a thing to which one repairs; used metaphorically for strength
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): [Literal: physical pillar/corner; Majaz: "فلان يأوي من عز قومه إلى ركن شديد" — one who repairs to a mighty support; here, the "pillars" (أركان) of faith as structural supports]
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The syntactic structure "مداره على عشرة أصول" (its circuit revolves upon ten principles) employs a prepositional phrase governing the verbal noun, establishing the necessary grammatical dependency that mirrors the ontological dependency of the created upon the Creator.
43:9.topic: Al-Ghazali on the journey of the soul, death, and the Hereafter, from 'Remembrance of Death and Afterlife'

43:77.arabic: وما دعاء الكافرين إلا في ضلال قال فيقولون ادعوا مالكا فيدعون فيقولون يا مالك ليقض علينا ربك قال فيجيبهم إنكم ماكثون (4) قال الأعمش أنبئت أن بين دعائهم وبين إجابة مالك إياهم ألف عام قال فيقولون ادعوا ربكم فلا أحد خير من ربكم فيقولون ربنا غلبت علينا شقوتنا وكنا قوما ضالين ربنا أخرجنا منها فإن عدنا فإنا ظالمون قال فيجيبهم اخسئوا فيها ولا تكلمون {قال}
43:77.english: And ʿAlī, may God honor his face, said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: "Seek refuge in God from the Pit of Sorrow, or the Valley of Sorrow." It was said: "O Messenger of God, what is the Valley or Pit of Sorrow?" He said: "A valley in Hell from which Hell itself seeks refuge with God seventy times each day. God, the Exalted, has prepared it for the reciters who show off." (2)
43:77.section_title_en: The Vastness of Hellfire, Its Depths, and the Torments of Its Inhabitants
43:77.anchors:
- Root: و د ي (w-d-y)
  * Lisan / Ayn: A valley; a place where torrents flow. In the lexicon, it denotes a lowland or watercourse between mountains.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Used for the valleys of Hell as places of confinement and passage, each containing further branching ravines (شُعَب), indicating graded descent.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal for earthly valleys; here transferred (majāz) to the topographical reality of Hell, affirming its corporeal vastness.
- Root: ع م ق (ʿ-m-q)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Depth; the far bottom of a well or pit. Al-Farahidi: "العمق: قعر البئر ونحوها."
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Depth as a measure of descent; in the Hereafter, it is unbounded, paralleling the unbounded depth of worldly desire.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal for physical depth; here extended to show the infinite regress of punishment corresponding to infinite craving.
- Root: غ س ق (gh-s-q)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Stinking, foul pus or ichor that flows from the skin of the damned; also intense darkness.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-Ghassāq is the putrid effusion of Hell, a punishment for the senses, specifically for drinking when the damned cry out in thirst.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal for what is loathsome and fetid; in the Quranic context, it is the designated drink of the inhabitants.
- Root: ز ق م (z-q-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To swallow with difficulty; the tree of Zaqqūm, which grows in the depths of Hell.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): A specific tree in Hell whose fruit is like the heads of devils, eaten by the damned to fill their bellies, causing choking and agony.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal for a real tree; its description is sensory, not metaphorical, affirming the physical reality of punishment.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The periodic structure of "في جهنم سبعين ألف واد" allows the prepositional phrase to precede the subject for emphasis, establishing the spatial setting before detailing its contents.
43:77.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications, prayers, and their spiritual power, from 'Remembrance of Death and Afterlife'

44:49.arabic: العذاب الشديد وينكسونه في قعر الجحيم ويقولون له {ذق إنك أنت العزيز الكريم} فأسكنوا دارا ضيقة الأرجاء مظلمة المسالك مبهمة المهالك يخلد فيها الأسير ويوقد فيها السعير شرابهم فيها الحميم ومستقرهم الجحيم الزبانية تقمعهم والهاوية تجمعهم أمانيهم فيها الهلاك وما لهم منها فكاك قد شدت أقدامهم إلى النواصي واسودت وجوههم من ظلمة المعاصي ينادون من أكنافها ويصيحون في نواحيها وأطرافها يا مالك قد حق علينا الوعيد يا مالك قد أثقلنا الحديد يا مالك قد نضجت منا الجلود يا مالك أخرجنا منها فإنا لا نعود فتقول الزبانية هيهات لات حين أمان
44:49.english: O you who are heedless of your own soul, deluded by what occupies you of the distractions of this world that is on the verge of passing away and perishing — abandon reflection upon that from which you are departing, and turn your thought to your place of arrival (mawrid), for you have been informed that the Fire is a place of arrival for all, since it was said: {«وإن منكم إلا واردها كان على ربك حتما مقضيا ثم ننجي الذين اتقوا ونذر الظالمين فيها جثيا»} [And there is none of you but shall arrive at it — an inevitability decreed upon your Lord. Then We shall save those who were God-fearing, and leave the wrongdoers in it, kneeling]. You are thus in certainty regarding the arrival (wurūd), and in doubt regarding deliverance. So instill within your heart the terror of that place of arrival — perhaps you will thereby prepare yourself for deliverance from it.
44:49.section_title_en: Discourse on the Attributes of Hellfire, Its Terrors, and Its Fetters
44:49.anchors:
- Root: ورد (w-r-d)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning is "to arrive at water" — the primordial act of approaching a watering-place; from this derives the sense of arriving at any destination, whether desired or dreaded.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الورود أصله: قصد الماء" — its origin is the intent to reach water; then applied generally, and used of the Fire "على سبيل الفظاعة" (by way of horrification), as in {وإن منكم إلا واردها} — the universal "arrival" at Hell is a divinely decreed certainty.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): ورد الماء — arriving at water to drink. Metaphorical (Majaz): وردت البلد — arriving at a land; ورد عليه أمر لم يطقه — an overwhelming matter descended upon him. Here, "al-wurūd" is majaz extended to the eschatological "arrival" at the Fire, a passage all must undergo.
- Root: جلد (j-l-d)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The skin or hide covering the body; جلد الكتاب — to cover a book with leather; جلدته بالسياط — to flog.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الجلد: قشر البدن" — the skin is the body's integument; in the Quranic verse {كلما نضجت جلودهم بدلناهم جلودا غيرها} [النساء/56], the renewal of skins is the renewal of the seat of pain, ensuring perpetual sensation.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: flaying, covering, stripping. Metaphorical: جلدته على هذا الأمر — compelled him. In this text, the literal sense governs: skins roasted, then replaced, so that torment never ceases.
- Root: ظلم (z-l-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Darkness, absence of light; also wrongdoing. The lexicographers note the moral-ontological link: injustice is a kind of darkness.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الظلمة: عدم النور" — darkness is the privation of light; used metaphorically for ignorance, polytheism, and transgression, as light is used for their opposites.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "الظلم ظلمات يوم القيامة" — wrongdoing is darknesses on the Day of Resurrection. Metaphorical: أرض مظلومة — land never before dug. Here, "zulumāt" (ظلمات) is used literally of Hell's physical darknesses, yet these are also the reified shadows of the inmates' own wrongs.
- Root: نار (n-w-r / n-w-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Fire; the root also yields نار — to kindle, to blaze up. The lexicons record the proverb: ورَيْتُ بك زنادي — "I struck fire from your flint," i.e., I perceived from you good counsel.
  * Al-Raghib (Al-Mufradat): Fire is the elemental reality of Hell, but its Quranic usage spans both physical flame and the "Fire of God kindled" which mounts over hearts [الهمزة/6-7] — the inward fire of heedlessness made outward.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: flame, burning. Metaphorical: نار الحرب — the fire of war. In this passage, the literal fire of Jahannam is described with maximal sensory concreteness, yet it remains the outward manifestation of the soul's own kindled crimes.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The rule governing the permissibility of interposing elements between a preposition and its object when the intervening phrase is semantically complete. Applied here in the periodic constructions where long descriptive clauses intervene between the initial vocative (يا أيها الغافل) and its eventual predicate, sustaining rhetorical tension across the entire passage.
44:49.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Remembrance of Death and Afterlife'

44:51.arabic: كأمثال اللؤلؤ المكنون جزاء بما كانوا يعملون في مقام أمين في جنات وعيون في جنات ونهر في مقعد صدق عند مليك مقتدر ينظرون فيها إلى وجه الملك الكريم وقد أشرقت في وجوههم نضرة النعيم لا يرهقهم فتر ولا ذلة بل عباد مكرمون وبأنواع التحف من ربهم يتعاهدون فهم فيما اشتهيت أنفسهم خالدون لا يخافون فيها ولا يحزنون وهم من ريب المنون آمنون فهم فيها يتنعمون ويأكلون من أطعمتها ويشربون من أنهارها لبنا وخمرا وعسلا في أنهار أراضيها من فضة وحصباؤها مرجان وعلى أرض ترابها مسك أذفر ونباتها زعفران ويمطرون من سحاب فيها من ماء النسرين على كثب
44:51.english: For God Most High has said: {«إن الأبرار لفي نعيم وإن الفجار لفي جحيم»} — "Indeed the righteous are in bliss, and indeed the wicked are in Hellfire." So present yourself before these two verses, and you will have known your resting-place between the two abodes. And God knows best.
44:51.section_title_en: Section 1351 — On the Description of Paradise and the Varieties of Its Bliss
44:51.anchors:
- Root: نعم (n-ʿ-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root denotes softness, ease, and pleasant living; al-Ayn notes it among names of the leopard and tiger, while Lisan records "Nuʿm" as a proper name.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "النعمة: الحالة الحسنة" — niʿmah is the excellent state/condition one inhabits; niʿīm is the experience of delight. The verse {«إن الأبرار لفي نعيم»} designates the abiding state of bliss as a settled condition, not a transient act.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): "في النعمة والنعيم" — dwelling in bounty and bliss. Metaphorical (Majaz): "خفت نعامتهم: ذهبوا" — ostriches departing; here the root's literal sense of softness is transfigured into the theological state of perpetual ease, free from all harshness.
- Root: وجه (w-j-h)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root: face, front, direction; al-Ayn cites "وجه الصواب" — the face/course of correctness.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The face is the noblest part of the outward body, hence used for the essence (al-dhāt) of a thing; in {«ويبقى وجه ربك ذو الجلال والإكرام»} it signifies the Divine Essence. Here "وجه الملك الكريم" — the Face of the Generous King — denotes the Beatific Vision of God's Essence, not a corporeal organ.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical face. Metaphorical: "وجه القوم، وهؤلاء وجوه البلد" — the foremost, noblest of a people; thus the "face" of the King is His most august presence.
- Root: مرج (m-r-j)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root: mixing, confusion, letting loose; al-Ayn: "المرج: الشهد" — also pure honey; Lisan: "مرج أمرهم: اختلط" — their affair became disordered.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "أصل المرج: الخلط" — mixing; "أمر مريج" — a confused affair (Q. 50:5). In this text, the rivers of Paradise "مطردة" (flowing) are not "ممرجة" (mixed/confused) — rather they run pure and distinct, each in its channel.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "مرج الدواب: أرسلها في المرج" — releasing beasts into pasture. Metaphorical: "مرج الله البحرين" — God let the two seas flow freely; "مرجت عهودهم" — covenants became disordered. The contrast sharpens the purity of Paradise's rivers.
- Root: امن (a-m-n)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root: safety, freedom from fear; al-Ayn treats it under the hamzah chapter as the state of security.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "أصل الأمن: طمأنينة النفس وزوال الخوف" — tranquility of the soul and removal of fear. In the Hereafter, "آمنون" is not mere absence of threat but the positive, settled peace of the soul in the Divine presence.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "أمنته وآمننيه" — to grant safety. Metaphorical: "فرس أمين القوى" — a horse whose strength is trustworthy; here the blessed are "آمنون من ريب المنون" — secure from the vicissitudes of fate, a security that is trustworthy and unbreachable.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The rule permits separation between a preposition and its object by an element upon which speech may properly pause, as in "إن به لضرًا" — here "فهم فيما اشتهت أنفسهم خالدون" (in what their souls desire, abiding eternally) interposes the clause of desire between the prepositional phrase and its predicate, heightening rhetorical emphasis on the soul's fulfillment.
44:51.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Remembrance of Death and Afterlife'

45:23.arabic: تعالى ولا معبود غيره ومن اتخذ إلهه هواه فهو بعيد من الصدق في توحيده وأمره مخطر في نفسه فإن عجزت عن ذلك كله فكن محبا لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم حريصا على تعظيم سننه ومتشوقا إلى مراعاة قلوب الصالحين من أمته ومتبركا بأدعيتهم فعساك أن تنال من شفاعته أو شفاعتهم فتنجو بالشفاعة إن كنت قليل البضاعة
45:23.english: And on the authority of Ibn Masʿūd, may God be pleased with him, that the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "God will gather the first and the last for an appointed time on a known Day, standing for forty years, their eyes fixed heavenward, awaiting the verdict of judgment." And he mentioned the ḥadīth until he reached the time of the prostration of the believers. He said: "Then He will say to the believers: 'Raise your heads.' So they raise their heads, and they are given their light according to their deeds. Among them is one who is given his light like a great mountain, racing before him; among them is one who is given his light smaller than that; among them is one who is given his light like a palm tree; among them is one who is given his light smaller than that—until the last of them is a man who is given his light upon the toe of his foot. It shines once and dims once. When it shines, he steps forward with his foot and walks; when it darkens, he stands still." Then he mentioned their crossing over the Bridge (al-Ṣirāṭ) according to their light: among them is one who crosses like the blink of an eye; among them is one who crosses like lightning; among them is one who crosses like a cloud; among them is one who crosses like the shooting of stars; among them is one who crosses like the gallop of a horse; among them is one who crosses like the running of a man—until the one who was given his light upon the toe of his foot crosses, crawling on his face, hands, and feet. One hand is dragged while another clings; one foot is caught while another is dragged, and the fire touches his sides. He said: "He will not cease thus until he is delivered. When he is delivered, he stands over it (the fire), then says: 'Praise be to God! God has given me what He has not given anyone, for He saved me from it after I had seen it.' Then he is taken to a pool at the gate of Paradise and bathes therein." (2) And Anas ibn Mālik said: "I heard the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, say: 'The Bridge is like the edge of a sword or like the edge of a hair. The angels save the believing men and the believing women, and Gabriel, peace be upon him, takes hold of my waist, and I say: "O Lord, save, save!" The slipers and slippers among men and women on that Day are many.'" (3)
45:23.section_title_en: The Terrors of the Bridge (Ṣirāṭ) and the Reality of Fear
45:23.anchors:
- Root: نور (n-w-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of radiant light, illumination, and luminosity; the source of visibility.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Light is of two kinds: sensory (perceived by the eye) and intellectual/spiritual (perceived by the inner eye of insight). The light granted to the believers on the Day of Resurrection is a spiritual light (nūr maʿnawī) apportioned by divine justice according to their deeds, manifesting their degree of faith and works.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) usage refers to physical illumination; metaphorical (majāz) usage refers to clarity, guidance, and manifestation. Here, the "light" is a metaphorical extension of the believer's true faith and righteous action, made perceptible in the Hereafter.
- Root: خوف (kh-w-f)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Fear, dread, apprehension of a harmful or painful event.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Fear (khawf) is the anticipation of something disliked, based on a probable or certain sign. It is the opposite of security (amn). True fear is a cognitive and motivational state that drives one to avoid its object, not mere emotional softness.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) usage is the emotion of fear; metaphorical (majāz) usage, as in "a fearful road" (ṭarīq khāʾif), denotes a place or state that causes fear. Al-Ghazali here critiques the metaphorical "fear" of the foolish—mere verbal utterance without behavioral consequence.
- Root: قدم (q-d-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Foot; also precedence and advancement.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The foot (qadam) is the instrument of standing and walking; from it, concepts of precedence (taqaddum) and delay are derived. In the ḥadīth, the light placed on the toe (ibhām al-qadam) signifies the minimal degree of faith, barely sufficient for movement.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) usage is the physical foot; metaphorical (majāz) usage, as in "place it under your feet" (i.e., forgive it), indicates subjugation or minimal standing. Here, the toe's light is literal in the eschatological scene but symbolically denotes the weakest degree of saving faith.
- Root: حصن (ḥ-ṣ-n)
  * Lisan / Ayn: A fortress, an impregnable stronghold; that which protects its interior from penetration.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): A fortress (ḥiṣn) is a place of refuge; metaphorically, it applies to anything that provides protection, such as armor or a chaste woman. True protection from the terrors of the Hereafter is not a physical fortress but the sincere utterance of "lā ilāha illā Allāh."
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) usage is a fortified structure; metaphorical (majāz) usage, as in "he came carrying a fortress" (i.e., weapons), denotes any means of defense. Al-Ghazali employs this metaphorically: the only fortress against the terrors of the Hereafter is sincere monotheism.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The rule governing the separation of a preposition from its object by an intervening clause, as in "فأنى يغني عنه ذلك من السبع" (So how can that avail him against the lion?), where the syntactic structure emphasizes the futility of the verbal refuge.
45:23.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'Remembrance of Death and Afterlife'

45:23.arabic: قال الله تعالى {أفرأيت من اتخذ إلهه هواه} وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم أبغض إله عبد في الأرض
45:23.english: They have manipulated this term through specification (takhṣīṣ), not through transfer (naql) or conversion (taḥwīl), for they have restricted it to knowledge of obscure legal branches (furūʿ gharībah) in legal opinions (fatāwā), to grasping the subtleties of their underlying causes (ʿilal), to multiplying discourse concerning them, and to memorizing the doctrinal positions related to them. Whoever is more profound in this and more occupied with it is called "the most learned in fiqh" (al-afqah). Yet in the first era, the name fiqh was applied absolutely to knowledge of the path of the Hereafter, to knowing the subtleties of the maladies of the souls (āfāt al-nufūs), to the corrupters of deeds (mufsidāt al-aʿmāl), to the power of encompassing the pettiness of this world, to intense longing for the bliss of the Hereafter, and to the dominance of fear over the heart. What indicates this to you is His saying, Mighty and Majestic: {«ليتفقهوا في الدين ولينذروا قومهم إذا رجعوا إليهم»} [“That they may gain understanding in the religion and warn their people when they return to them”] (Q 9:122). What effects warning and intimidation is this very fiqh — not the subdivisions of divorce (ṭalāq), manumission (ʿitāq), imprecation (liʿān), salam contracts, and leases (ijārah). For that (latter) does not produce warning or intimidation; rather, total devotion to it perpetually hardens the heart and strips away godly fear (khashyah) from it, as we now observe in those wholly devoted to it.
45:23.section_title_en: The Revival of the Religious Sciences — Section 27: The Corruption of the Praiseworthy Names (Taḥrīf al-Asāmī al-Maḥmūdah)
45:23.anchors:
- Root: فقه (Fiqh)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core linguistic meaning of "understanding" (al-fahm) and "comprehension" (al-fahm ʿan al-shayʾ)
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Al-fiqh: attainment of knowledge of the unseen through a witnessed sign — it is more specific than ʿilm." Theological nuance: true fiqh is knowledge of the heart's maladies and the path to the Hereafter.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): "afqih ʿannī mā aqūl" — understand what I say. Metaphorical (majāz): technical restriction to legal rulings (furūʿ al-fatāwā) is a later convention, not the lexical or prophetic norm.
- Root: علم (ʿIlm)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Perception of a thing as it truly is; knowledge of the essence of a thing.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Two types: (1) perception of the essence of a thing; (2) judgment upon a thing affirming or negating something of it. The highest ʿilm is knowledge of God, His verses, and His acts.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "He is from the banners (aʿlām) of knowledge." Metaphorical: restriction of the title "scholar" (al-ʿālim) to the dialectician (al-munāẓir) is a corrupt specification (takhṣīṣ fāsid).
- Root: وحد (Waḥḥada)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To make one; to affirm unity.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Tawḥīd is affirming God's unity in essence, attributes, and acts — the highest degree being the vision that all things proceed from Him alone.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: utterance of "Lā ilāha illā Allāh." Metaphorical: the inner reality (al-lubāb) — seeing all affairs from God, cutting off attention from secondary causes.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب التخصيص والتقييد (Restriction and Specification) — The corruption of names occurs through takhṣīṣ (semantic restriction), not naql (lexical transfer). The grammarians' principle: a general term (al-ism al-ʿāmm) retains its full semantic range unless a valid sharʿī or linguistic evidence restricts it; arbitrary restriction by custom (ʿādat al-istimāl) is a rhetorical device of the devils among men and jinn.
45:23.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Book of Knowledge'

45:23.arabic: أخلاقها ومن عدل عن هذه الطريقة كان كمن قال الله تعالى فيه أفرأيت من اتخذ إلهه هواه وأضله الله على علم وقال تعالى واتبع هواه فمثله كمثل الكلب إن تحمل عليه يلهث أو تتركه يلهث وقال عز وجل فيمن نهى النفس عن الهوى وأما من خاف مقام ربه ونهى النفس عن الهوى فإن الجنة هي المأوى وسيأتي كيفية مجاهدة هذه الجنود وتسليط بعضها على بعض في كتاب رياضة النفس إن شاء الله تعالى المثال الثاني اعلم أن البدن كالمدينة والعقل أعني المدرك من الإنسان كملك مدبر لها وقواه المدركة من الحواس الظاهرة والباطنة كجنوده وأعوانه وأعضاؤه كرعيته والنفس الأمارة بالسوء التي هي الشهوة والغضب
45:23.english: But whoever turns away from this path is like the one of whom Allah, the Exalted, said: {أفرأيت من اتخذ إلهه هواه وأضله الله على علم} — "Have you seen the one who takes as his god his own desire, and Allah has led him astray out of knowledge?" (Q 45:23). And He, the Exalted, said: {واتبع هواه فمثله كمثل الكلب إن تحمل عليه يلهث أو تتركه يلهث} — "And he followed his desire, so his example is like the example of a dog: if you drive him away, he pants, or if you leave him, he pants" (Q 7:176). And He, the Exalted and Glorious, said concerning the one who restrains the soul from passion: {وأما من خاف مقام ربه ونهى النفس عن الهوى فإن الجنة هي المأوى} — "But as for he who feared the standing before his Lord and restrained the soul from passion, then indeed, Paradise will be the refuge" (Q 79:40-41).
45:23.section_title_en: ** The Body as Kingdom: The Governance of the Soul's Faculties — Section 577
45:23.anchors:
**
- Root: نفس (n-f-s)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The self, soul, breath; that which is breathed forth; the essence of a thing
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): النفس: الروح — the soul as the immaterial spiritual reality; when attributed to Allah, denotes His very essence (al-dhāt), not a separate entity
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the self/essence; Metaphorical: نفس سائلة — a "flowing self" (blood) as the criterion for ritual purity
- Root: عقل (ʿ-q-l)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Intellect, reason; that which restrains and binds
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): العقل يقال للقوة المتهيئة لقبول العلم — the faculty prepared for receiving knowledge; and the knowledge acquired through that faculty
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: intellectual apprehension; Metaphorical: نخلة لا تعقل الإبار — a palm that does not "accept" pollination (i.e., does not receive)
- Root: غضب (gh-d-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Anger, wrath; the boiling of the blood of the heart desiring vengeance
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): ثوران دم القلب إرادة الانتقام — when attributed to Allah, it means retribution alone, not an emotional state
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: anger toward the living (غضبت لفلان); Metaphorical: anger toward the dead (غضبت به) — the preposition shift marking the distinction
- Root: نصح (n-s-ḥ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Sincere counsel; to be pure and unadulterated; to sew (as a tailor)
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): تحري فعل أو قول فيه صلاح صاحبه — the earnest pursuit of action or speech containing the welfare of its recipient
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: sincere advice; Metaphorical: نصح الغيث البلاد — rain "counseling" the land (i.e., giving it its due generously)
- Sibawayh Rule: باب التشبيه التمثيلي (The Chapter of Illustrative Simile) — extended analogical comparisons (tamthīl) where multiple relations are mapped across domains, governed by the syntactic pattern of predicate assignment (isnād) to establish parallel structures
