45:23.topic: Al-Ghazali on purifying the character, moral diseases, and spiritual remedies, from 'Disciplining the Soul'

45:28.arabic: مدبرين يوم ترى كل أمة جاثية وسقط بعضهم على الوجوه منكبين وينادى العصاة والظالمون بالويل والثبور وينادى الصديقون نفسى نفسى فبينما هم كذلك إذ زفرت الناس زفرتها الثانية فتضاعف خوفهم وتخاذلت قواهم وظنوا أنهم مأخوذون ثم زفرت الثالثة فتساقط الخلائق على وجوههم وشخصوا بأبصارهم ينظرون من طرف خفى خاشع وانهضمت عند ذلك قلوب الظالمين فبلغت الحناجر كاظمين وذهلت العقول من السعداء والأشقياء أجمعين وبعد ذلك اقبل الله تعالى على الرسل وقال ماذا أجبتم فإذا رأوا ما قد أقيم من السياسة على الأ
45:28.english: {«ماذا أجبتم قالوا لا علم لنا إنك أنت علام الغيوب»} — "What did you answer?" They will say: "We have no knowledge; indeed, You alone are the Knower of the unseen." {Quran 5:109} So woe betide the severity of a Day in which the intellects of the prophets are stupefied and their knowledges are effaced by the sheer intensity of the awe, when it is said to them: "What did you answer, when you were sent to the creatures?" — though they had known — yet their intellects are bewildered, and they know not with what to reply. So they say, from the intensity of the awe: "We have no knowledge; indeed, You alone are the Knower of the unseen." And they are, at that very moment, truthful, for the intellects have flown away from them and the knowledges have been effaced — until God Almighty strengthens them. Then Noah (peace be upon him) is summoned, and it is said to him: "Did you convey the message?" He says: "Yes." Then it is said to his community: "Did he convey to you?" They say: "No warner came to us."
45:28.section_title_en: The Day of Reckoning: The Questioning of the Prophets and the Exposure of the Servant Before the Lord of the Worlds
45:28.anchors:
- Root: رسل (R-S-L)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of "sending forth with ease and gentleness"; a messenger (rasūl) is one dispatched with a message.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الرسول" denotes one sent with a commission; the root conveys both the act of dispatch and the message borne. In the eschatological context, the prophets (rusul) are asked "ماذا أجبتم" — what answer did they give to those to whom they were sent.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (haqīqah): "أرسل الله في الأمم رسلا" — God sent messengers among the nations. Metaphorical (majāz): "أرسل الله عليهم العذاب" — God loosed chastisement upon them. Here, the sending of prophets is literal, but the terror of the Day is such that even their knowledge is effaced.
- Root: علم (ʿ-L-M)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Knowledge, perception, certainty; the opposite of ignorance.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "العلم: إدراك الشيء بحقيقته" — knowledge is the apprehension of a thing in its true reality. On the Day of Terror, the prophets' knowledge (ʿulūmuhum) is erased (tunmaḥū) by the sheer overwhelming majesty (haybah) of the Divine address, leaving them to answer: "لا علم لنا" — "We have no knowledge."
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "علمت الشيء أعلمه" — I knew the thing. Here, the effacement of knowledge is a literal event of the Hour, not metaphorical, for the prophets are truthful when they disavow knowledge in that state.
- Root: يوم (Y-W-M)
  * Lisan / Ayn: A day; a period of time, whether short or long.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "اليوم يعبر به عن وقت طلوع الشمس إلى غروبها. وقد يعبر به عن مدة من الزمان أي مدة كانت" — the day is the time from sunrise to sunset, but it may denote any span of time. The "Day" of Resurrection is a duration whose terrors are magnified beyond earthly measure.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "ما رأيته اليوم" — I did not see him today. Metaphorical: "ذكر في أيام العرب كذا أي في وقائعها" — "days" of the Arabs means their battles. The "Day" of Judgment is a real day, but its horrors are such that the prophets themselves are stupefied.
- Root: الم (ʾ-L-M)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Severe pain, anguish.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الألم الوجع الشديد" — pain is intense suffering. The "عذاب أليم" is a painful chastisement. In this passage, the terror of the Day is an "أليم" affliction upon the hearts of all creatures.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "مسه بضرب أليم" — he touched him with a painful blow. The anguish of the Day is literal and inescapable.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — The construction "إنك أنت علام الغيوب" employs the emphatic pronoun "أنت" as a focused predication, restricting the attribute of absolute knowledge of the unseen to God alone, even as the prophets disavow all knowledge before Him.
45:28.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Remembrance of Death and Afterlife'

47:4.arabic: إليه لا ينافي ذكر الله عز وجل وقال تعالى ولا تحسبن الذين قتلوا في سبيل الله أمواتا بل أحياء عند ربهم يرزقون فرحين بما آتاهم الله من فضله ويستبشرون بالذين لم يلحقوا بهم من خلفهم الآية ولأجل شرف ذكر الله عز وجل عظمت رتبة الشهادة لأن المطلوب الخاتمة ونعني بالخاتمة وداع الدنيا والقدوم على الله والقلب مستغرق بالله عز وجل منقطع العلائق عن غيره فإن قدر عبد على أن يجعل همه مستغرقا بالله عز وجل فلا يقدر على أن يموت على تلك الحالة إلا في صف القتال فإنه قطع الطمع عن مهجته وأهله وماله وولده بل من الدنيا كلها فإنه يريدها ل
47:4.english: If, therefore, he had grown intimate with it, he delights in it and takes pleasure in the cessation of the impediments that had diverted him from it. For the pressing necessities of needs in this worldly life divert one from the remembrance of God, may He be mighty and majestic, and after death no impediment remains. It is as if he has been left alone with his Beloved, and so his joy is immense, and he is delivered from the prison in which he had been prevented from that which was his source of intimacy. For this reason, he, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "The Holy Spirit (Rūḥ al-Qudus) breathed into my heart: Love whom you will, for you shall surely part from him." {«أحبب من أحببت فإنك مفارقه»} By this he intended everything connected to this world, for that perishes with respect to him at death. For {«كل من عليها فان * ويبقى وجه ربك ذو الجلال والإكرام»} [Everything upon it is perishing, and there remains the Face of your Lord, Possessor of Majesty and Honor]. And this world only perishes with respect to him at death, until it perishes in itself when the Book reaches its appointed term.
47:4.section_title_en: Section 240 — The Station of Remembrance (Dhikr): On the Transformation of Habit into Nature, the Intimacy of Remembrance After Death, and the Excellence of Martyrdom as the Seal of One's State
47:4.anchors:
- Root: ألف (Alifa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of reconciliation, familiarity, and the formation of habit through repeated engagement.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The theological nuance of 'uns' (intimacy) as the soul's acquired disposition of comfort in the presence of its Beloved, contrasting with 'wahsha' (estrangement).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Distinguishes the literal sense of social familiarity from the metaphorical (majaz) sense of the heart's deep-seated repose in the remembrance of God, which becomes a 'second nature' (ṭabʿan ākhara).
- Root: ختم (Khatama)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To seal, stamp, or conclude; the final impression left upon a thing.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The theological sense of the 'seal' (khātima) of one's life—the terminal state upon which one departs from the world and which determines the nature of the afterlife.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): The literal act of sealing a document versus the metaphorical designation of one's final spiritual condition as the determining factor of one's eternal outcome.
- Root: شهد (Shahida)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To witness, to be present, to testify.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The specific theological elevation of 'shahāda' (martyrdom) as the ultimate act of witnessing the truth of God through the sacrifice of one's own life, rendering the martyr a living witness (shahīd).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): The literal sense of legal testimony versus the metaphorical reality of the martyr whose very being testifies to the sincerity of his devotion, being 'alive' with his Lord.
- Root: قطع (Qata'a)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To sever, cut off, or detach.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The essential spiritual operation of severing worldly attachments ('alā'iq) to achieve the unadulterated focus of the heart upon God.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): The literal cutting of a physical tie versus the metaphorical severance of all internal and external impediments that distract the soul from its sole Beloved.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Restriction and Specification (Bāb al-Ḥaṣr wa al-Taqyīd bi-innamā) — Governing how the exclusive focus of the martyr's intention is syntactically and logically restricted to God alone, as exemplified in the phrase "no god but God" (lā ilāha illā Allāh), which requires the complete negation of all other objects of intention before affirming the sole Divine Object.
47:4.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Remembrance of Death and Afterlife'

47:4.arabic: فوالذي نفسي بيده ليودن رجال قتلوا في سبيل الله شهداء أن يبعثهم الله علماء لما يرون من كرامتهم فإن أحدا لم يولد عالما وإنما العلم بالتعلم وقال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما تذاكر العلم بعض ليلة أحب إلي من إحيائها وكذلك عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه وأحمد بن حنبل رحمة الله وقال الحسن في قوله تعالى {ربنا آتنا في الدنيا حسنة وفي الآخرة حسنة} إن الحسنة في الدنيا هي العلم والعبادة وفي الآخرة هي الجنة وقيل لبعض الحكماء أي الأشياء تقتنى قال الأشياء التي إذا غرقت سفينتك سبحت معك يعني العلم وقيل أراد بغرق السف
47:4.english: And al-Ḥasan, may God have mercy on him, said: "The ink of the scholars will be weighed against the blood of the martyrs, and the ink of the scholars will outweigh the blood of the martyrs."
47:4.section_title_en: The Book of Knowledge — Section 6: On the Virtue of Teaching and Learning (Continued)
47:4.anchors:
- Root: شغل (sh-gh-l)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Occupation, preoccupation, that which engages one entirely
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Preoccupation that veils one from perception of other things
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — physical occupation; Metaphorical — absorption of the heart that blinds the senses
- Root: حسن (ḥ-s-n)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Beauty, goodness, excellence
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الحسن: عبارة عن كل مبهج مرغوب فيه" — that which is pleasing and desirable, of three kinds: rational, appetitive, sensory
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — beauty of form; Metaphorical — the ḥasanah in the Qur'anic supplication denotes knowledge and worship
- Root: علم (ʿ-l-m) — [Note: recently used, but required by text; applied per governing rule]
  * Lisan / Ayn: Knowledge, perception, cognition
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "العلم: إدراك الشيء بحقيقته" — apprehension of a thing in its true reality
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — direct perception; Metaphorical — knowledge as a garment of honor from God
- Root: موت (m-w-t)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Death, cessation of life
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Death as the lifting of the burdens of this world; awakening from the sleep of heedlessness
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — physical death; Metaphorical — "الناس نيام فإذا ماتوا انتبهوا" (people are asleep; when they die, they awaken)
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — applied in the ḥadīth "إنما العلم بالتعلم" (knowledge is only attained through learning), restricting the means of acquiring knowledge to learning alone.
47:4.topic: Al-Ghazali on the journey of the soul, death, and the Hereafter, from 'Book of Knowledge'

47:15.arabic: تعالى {وسقوا ماء حميما فقطع أمعاءهم} وقال تعالى {وإن يستغيثوا يغاثوا بماء كالمهل يشوى الوجوه} فهذه طعامهم وشرابهم عند جوعهم وعطشهم (1) فانظر الآن إلى حيات جهنم وعقاربها وإلى شدة سمومها وعظم أشخاصها وفظاظة منظرها وقد سلطت على أهلها وأغريت بهم فهي لا تفتر عن النهش واللدغ ساعة واحدة قال أبو هريرة قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم من أتاه الله مالا فلم يؤد زكاته مثل له يوم القيامة شجاعا له زييبتان يطوقه يوم القيامة ثم يأخذ بلهازمه يعنى أشدافه فيقول أنا مالك أنا كنزك ثم تلا قوله تعالى ولا
47:15.english: At that point they despair of every good, and at that point they take to sighing, regret, and wailing. Abu Umamah said: The Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, said concerning His words, "And he is given to drink of festering water, which he sips but can hardly swallow" {«وَيُسْقَىٰ مِن مَّاءٍ صَدِيدٍ يَتَجَرَّعُهُ وَلَا يَكَادُ يُسِيغُهُ»}: "It is brought near to him, and he loathes it. When it is drawn close to him, it scorches his face, and the skin of his scalp falls off. When he drinks it, it severs his intestines until it exits from his anus." God Almighty says: {«وَسُقُوا مَاءً حَمِيمًا فَقَطَّعَ أَمْعَاءَهُمْ»} "And they are given to drink boiling water, and it severs their intestines." And He says: {«وَإِن يَسْتَغِيثُوا يُغَاثُوا بِمَاءٍ كَالْمُهْلِ يَشْوِي الْوُجُوهَ»} "And if they cry for relief, they are relieved with water like molten brass, which scalds the faces." So this is their food and drink in their hunger and thirst.
47:15.section_title_en: The Torments of the Fire: Serpents, Scorpions, and the Anguish of the Damned
47:15.anchors:
- Root: حس (ḥ-s-s) — [AVOIDED per instruction]
- Root: نار (n-r) — Fire
  * Lisan al-Arab: "النار: معروفة، وهي نار جهنم، ذات لفح وحرّ."
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "النار: قد تطلق على نار الدنيا ونار الآخرة، وهي التي أعدها الله للكافرين، وفيها من أصناف العذاب ما لا يعلمه إلا الله."
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "نار: حقيقة في النار المحرقة، ومجاز في نار الحرب والحرب."
- Root: حي (ḥ-y) — Serpent
  * Lisan al-Arab: "الحية: من الهوام، وتجمع على حيات، وأعظمها ما كان كأعناق البخت."
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الحية: دابة مؤذية، وفي الآخرة تكون أعظم وأشد إيلامًا."
- Root: عقر (ʿ-q-r) — Scorpion
  * Lisan al-Arab: "العقرب: دويبة مؤذية تلدغ، وفي النار تكون كالبغال."
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — Used to specify that serpents and scorpions are only empowered over those who were dominated by miserliness and evil character in the world.
47:15.topic: Al-Ghazali on the journey of the soul, death, and the Hereafter, from 'Remembrance of Death and Afterlife'

47:15.arabic: أنهارها لمن ماء غير آسن وأنهار من لبن لم يتغير طعمه وأنهار من عسل مصفى لم يصفه الرجال وأنها من خمر لذة للشاربين لا تسفه الأحلام ولا تصدع منها الرءوس وإن فيها ما لا عين رأت ولا أذن سمعت ولا خطر على قلب بشر ملوك ناعمون أبناء ثلاث وثلاثون في سن واحد طولهم ستون ذراعا في السماء كحل جرد مرد قد أمنوا العذاب واطمأنت بهم الدار وإن أنهارها لتجري على رضراض من ياقوت وزبرجد وإن عروقها ونخلها وكرمها اللؤلؤ وثمارها لا يعلم علمها إلا الله تعالى وإن ريحها ليوجد من مسيرة خمسمائة سنة وإن لهم فيها خيلا وإبلا هفافة رحال
47:15.english: Usamah ibn Zayd narrated that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said to his companions: "Behold! Is there anyone striving eagerly for Paradise? For Paradise — no measure can encompass it, by the Lord of the Kaʿbah — it is light gleaming, and a fragrant basil swaying, and a lofty palace, and a flowing river, and abundant ripe fruit, and a wife — a beautiful, comely wife — in splendid raiment, and bliss in an everlasting abode, and radiance in a lofty, resplendent, secure dwelling." They said: "We are the eager strivers for it, O Messenger of Allah." He said: "Say: 'If Allah the Exalted wills.'" Then he mentioned jihad and its due right.
47:15.section_title_en: Exposition of Scattered Descriptions of the Inhabitants of Paradise as Reported in the Traditions
47:15.anchors:
- Root: جمل (j-m-l)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "جمل" denotes gathering and collecting scattered parts into a whole; "جملة" (totality/summary) is the aggregate as opposed to "تفصيل" (detailed enumeration).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الجمال: الحسن الكثير" — beauty in abundance; here the nominal form "جمل" (plural of "جملة") signals comprehensive, summarized statements, not ornamental beauty.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): "أجمل في الطلب" — to be moderate; Majaz (Metaphorical): "اتخذ الليل جملا" — to traverse the night as a whole. In this title, "جمل مفرقة" is literal: "dispersed summary statements" — a rhetorical oxymoron meaning concise reports scattered across various traditions.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الصفة والموصوف (Attributive Interposition) — The genitive construct "جمل مفرقة" (summary statements scattered) with the adjective "مفرقة" (dispersed) following the noun "جمل" (statements) requires agreement in definiteness, gender, and number, here feminine plural agreeing with the broken plural "جمل."

- Root: خطر (kh-t-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الخطر" is the stake in a wager; "ما خطر بباله" — what crosses the mind; "لا خطر لها" — of no worth or measure.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الخطر" denotes the estimation of a thing's value; "لا خطر لها" means it transcends all valuation — no comparison can measure it.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "خاطر بنفسه" — risked himself; Majaz: "لا خطر لها" — metaphorical negation of any comparable measure, i.e., infinite worth.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب النفي بلا (Negation with "lā") — "لا خطر لها" is a generic negation (lā li-nafy al-jins) rendering "خطر" in the accusative indefinite, here functioning as a predicate of worthlessness-turned-sublimity.

- Root: عين (ʿayn)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "العين" — the eye; also a spring of water; "قرت عينه" — his eye was cooled (contentment).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "العين الجارحة... وللمراعي للشيء عين، وفلان بعيني، أي: أحفظه وأراعيه" — the eye as organ and as metaphor for divine guardianship; "ولذت عيناك" — what your eyes delight in.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "فلان عيون وعيان" — a watchful spy; Majaz: "نظرت الأرض بعين" — the earth sprouted with early pasture; here "ولذت عيناك" is literal sensory pleasure of sight.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفعل اللازم والمتعدي (Transitive and Intransitive Verbs) — "لذت عيناك" (your eyes delighted) is intransitive with the subject "عيناك" (dual), the pleasure being an internal accident (ʿaraḍ) of perception.

47:15.arabic: لم يصفه الرجال وأنها من خمر لذة للشاربين لا تسفه الأحلام ولا تصدع منها الرءوس وإن فيها ما لا عين رأت ولا أذن سمعت ولا خطر على قلب بشر ملوك ناعمون أبناء ثلاث وثلاثون في سن واحد طولهم ستون ذراعا في السماء كحل جرد مرد قد أمنوا العذاب واطمأنت بهم الدار وإن أنهارها لتجري على رضراض من ياقوت وزبرجد وإن عروقها ونخلها وكرمها اللؤلؤ وثمارها لا يعلم علمها إلا الله تعالى وإن ريحها ليوجد من مسيرة خمسمائة سنة وإن لهم فيها خيلا وإبلا هفافة رحالها وأزمتها وسروجها من ياقوت يتزاورون فيها وأزواجهم ال
47:15.english: Usamah ibn Zayd narrated that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said to his companions: "Behold! Is there anyone striving eagerly for Paradise? For Paradise — no measure can encompass it, by the Lord of the Kaʿbah — it is light gleaming, and a fragrant basil swaying, and a lofty palace, and a flowing river, and abundant ripe fruit, and a wife — a beautiful, comely wife — in splendid raiment, and bliss in an everlasting abode, and radiance in a lofty, resplendent, secure dwelling." They said: "We are the eager strivers for it, O Messenger of Allah." He said: "Say: 'If Allah the Exalted wills.'" Then he mentioned jihad and its due right.

47:22.arabic: أحد ومن غالب الله غلبه ومن خادع الله خدعه فهل عسيتم إن توليتم أن تفسدوا في الأرض وتقطعوا أرحامكم وأوصيكم بالأنصار خيرا فإنهم الذين تبوءوا الدار والإيمان من قبلكم أن تحسنوا إليهم ألم يشاطروكم الثمار ألم يوسعوا عليكم في الديار ألم يؤثروكم على أنفسهم وبهم الخصاصة ألا فمن ولي أن يحكم بين رجلين فليقبل من محسنهم وليتجاوز عن مسيئهم ألا ولا تستأثروا عليهم ألا وإني فرط لكم وأنتم لاحقون بي ألا وإن موعدكم الحوض حوضي أعرض مما بين بصرى الشام وصنعاء اليمن يصب فيه ميزاب الكوثر ماؤه أشد بياضا من اللبن وألين من الزبد وأحلى من الشهد من شرب منه لم يظمأ أبدا
47:22.english: And a clarification for those who seek insight — for there was none more honored before God than him, for he was the Intimate Friend of God (khalīl Allāh), His Beloved (ḥabībuh), and His Confidant (najiyyuh); he was His Chosen One (ṣafiyyuh), His Messenger (rasūluh), and His Prophet (nabiyyuh). So consider: did He grant him respite for even an hour at the end of his term? Did He delay him for a single moment after his appointed death had arrived? No indeed — rather, He dispatched to him the noble angels entrusted with seizing the souls of all creation. They rushed upon his pure and generous spirit to extract it, and they wrestled with it to remove it from his pure body — unto mercy, good pleasure, and beautiful bounties; nay, unto a seat of truth in the vicinity of the All-Merciful. Yet despite all that, his distress (karbuh) intensified during the throes of death, his groaning became apparent, his restlessness followed in succession, his yearning rose high, his color changed, his brow sweated, and his left and right sides trembled in contraction and expansion — until those present wept over his fall, and those who witnessed his state sobbed at its severity. So have you seen any station of prophethood repelling what was decreed from him? Did the angel (of death) show regard for his kin and tribe? Did he grant him leniency because he was a supporter of the Truth and a bearer of glad tidings and warnings to creation? Far from it! Rather, he fulfilled what he was commanded, and he followed what he found inscribed on the Preserved Tablet. Such was his state — while he, before God, held the Praiseworthy Station (al-maqām al-maḥmūd) and the Pond of Abundance (al-ḥawḍ al-mawrūd); he is the first from whom the earth will split open, and he is the master of intercession on the Day of Presentation. So the wonder is that we do not take heed from him, nor are we certain of what we shall encounter. Nay, we are captives of lusts and companions of sins and misdeeds. Why then do we not draw a lesson from the death-fall of Muhammad, the Master of the Messengers, the Imam of the God-fearing, and the Beloved of the Lord of the Worlds? Perhaps we imagine that we shall be immortal, or we fancy that despite our evil deeds we are honored before God. Far from it! Far from it! Rather, we are certain that all of us shall enter the Fire — {«وإن منكم إلا واردها كان على ربك حتما مقضيا ثم ننجي الذين اتقوا ونذر الظالمين فيها جثيا»} (And there is none of you but will pass over it [the Fire]; this is with your Lord a decree firmly established. Then We shall save those who feared God and leave the wrongdoers therein on their knees) — and none shall be saved from it except the God-fearing. So we are certain of entering it, but merely deluded about emerging from it. Nay, we have wronged our own souls if, being as we are, we await with mere predominant conjecture. By God, we are not among the God-fearing! And God, Lord of the Worlds, has said: {«وإن منكم إلا واردها كان على ربك حتما مقضيا ثم ننجي الذين اتقوا ونذر الظالمين فيها جثيا»} (And there is none of you but will pass over it; it is with your Lord a decree firmly established. Then We shall save those who feared God and leave the wrongdoers therein on their knees). So let every servant look to himself — whether he is closer to the wrongdoers or to the God-fearing. And look to yourself after you have looked to the conduct of the righteous predecessors (al-salaf al-ṣāliḥīn), for they, despite all that they were granted of success, were among the fearful.
47:22.section_title_en: On the Death-Throes of the Prophet (Peace Be Upon Him) and the Lessons Therein — A Warning to the Negligent
47:22.anchors:
- Root: رسل (r-s-l)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of "sending forth with ease and gentleness"; a messenger (rasūl) is one dispatched with a message.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "أصل الرسل: الانبعاث على التؤدة" — the root denotes measured, deliberate dispatch; the angelic messengers (al-malā'ikah al-mursalūn) are sent on a precise, inexorable errand.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): "أرسل الله في الأمم رسلا" — sending prophets with tidings. Metaphorical (Majaz): "أرسل الله عليهم العذاب" — the inescapable descent of decree; here, the angels are dispatched to seize the Prophet's soul, showing that even the most honored cannot repel the divine command.
- Root: نفس (n-f-s)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The self, soul, or spirit; that which is breathed and animates; also "preciousness" (nufāsah).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The soul (nafs) as the immaterial reality (al-rūḥ) that is seized at death; in "ويحذركم الله نفسه" it denotes the very Essence (al-dhāt), underscoring that the soul's extraction is an act of divine sovereignty.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "نفس سائلة" — a flowing essence. Metaphorical: "دفق نفسه أي دمه" — the pouring out of life; here, the angels "عالجوها ليرحلوها" (wrestled with it to remove it), depicting the soul's reluctant departure from the body.
- Root: عله (ʿ-l-h) — [Note: Root avoided per constraints; substituted with relevant root for "suffering" — see كرب below]
- Root: كرب (k-r-b) — [Derived from context; not in avoidance list]
  * Lisan / Ayn: Grief, distress, agony that grips the chest (karb); the intensification of anguish at death's threshold.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The "sakarat al-mawt" (agonies of death) as a trial for the soul's detachment from the corporeal frame.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical constriction. Metaphorical: the spiritual weight of transition, as the Prophet's "karb" (distress) is magnified despite his rank.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — Used in "إنما أوصي بهذا الأمر قريشا" to restrict leadership to Quraysh, and "فإنما هو عمن أخبره" to limit chains of transmission; also applies to "لا بل" (nay, rather) constructions that negate a prior assumption and affirm a corrective truth, as in "لا بل ظلمنا أنفسنا".
47:22.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'Remembrance of Death and Afterlife'

50:22.arabic: يقال للأشقياء وقد انكشف الغطاء {لقد كنت في غفلة من هذا فكشفنا عنك غطاءك فبصرك اليوم حديد} ويقال أفسخر هذا أم أنتم لا تبصرون اصلوها فاصبروا أو لا تبصروا سواء عليكم إنما تجزون ما كنتم تعملون وإليهم الإشارة بقوله تعالى {وبدا لهم من الله ما لم يكونوا يحتسبون} فأعلم العلماء وأحكم الحكماء ينكشف له عقيب الموت من العجائب والآيات ما لم يخطر قط بباله ولا اختلج به ضميره فلو لم يكن للعاقل هم وغم إلا الفكرة في خطر تلك الحال أن الحجاب عماذا يرتفع وما الذي ينكشف عنه الغطاء من
50:22.english: Know that the lights of inner insights (anwār al-baṣā'ir) derived from the Book of God—mighty and majestic is He—and from the Sunnah of His Messenger—may God's peace and blessings be upon him—and from the pathways of reflective consideration, make known to us the states of the dead in general and their division into the blessed and the wretched. But the specific case of Zayd and ʿAmr in particular is not disclosed at all. For if we rely upon the faith of Zayd and ʿAmr, we do not know upon what they died nor how their end was sealed for them. And if we rely upon their outward righteousness, then piety (taqwā) has its seat in the heart, and it is hidden—concealed even from the possessor of that piety himself—so how then from others? Thus there is no ruling for outward righteousness apart from inward piety. God—exalted is He—said: {«إنما يتقبل الله من المتقين»} ["God only accepts from the God-fearing"] (Al-Mā'idah 5:27). So the knowledge of the judgment concerning Zayd and ʿAmr is not possible except by witnessing them and witnessing what transpires upon them. And when one dies, he has transferred from the world of dominion and testimony (ʿālam al-mulk wa al-shahādah) to the world of the unseen and the kingdom (ʿālam al-ghayb wa al-malakūt), so he is not seen by the outward eye. Rather, he is seen only by another eye—that eye being created in the heart of every human being. But upon it has been placed a dense covering (ghishāwah) of his lusts and worldly preoccupations, so that he does not see with it, nor is it conceivable that he should see with it anything of the realm of the kingdom (malakūt) unless that covering is peeled away from the eye of his heart.
50:22.section_title_en: The Unveiling of the Veil: On the Vision of the Dead and the Reality of Dreams
50:22.anchors:
- Root: بصر (B-Ṣ-R)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Inner perception and discernment; the eye as an organ of sight versus the "insight" (baṣīrah) as the heart's eye.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Baṣīrah is the perception of the heart, a spiritual sight (ru'yah qalbiyyah) that penetrates to realities, distinct from mere ocular vision.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) sight is of the physical eye; metaphorical (majāz) sight is the heart's illumination by which hidden truths are disclosed.
- Root: كشف (K-Sh-F)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Removal of a covering; disclosure of what is concealed.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Kashf in the theological sense is the lifting of the veil (ghishāwah) from the heart so that the unseen realm (malakūt) becomes manifest.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: uncovering a physical object; metaphorical: revelation of meanings and hidden affairs to the inner eye.
- Root: لوح (L-W-Ḥ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: A tablet or board upon which writing appears; also the flat bones of the body.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The Preserved Tablet (al-Lawḥ al-Maḥfūẓ) is that upon which all destinies are inscribed; its modality is unknown to us save by report.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: a wooden plank; metaphorical: the divine register of all that was and will be, not corporeal but a subtle reality.
- Root: مثل (M-Th-L)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Likeness, similitude, example; to stand in representation of another.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Mathal is the analogical representation by which an absent or abstract reality is brought near to understanding through a present likeness.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: a resembling image; metaphorical: the parabolic example (mithāl) used to approximate what transcends sensory grasp.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Restriction and Specification (al-ḥaṣr wa al-taqyīd bi-innamā) — The particle "innamā" confines the predicate to the subject alone, as in "إنما يتقبل الله من المتقين," restricting divine acceptance exclusively to the God-fearing, a syntactic anchor for the theological point that outward piety without inward taqwā avails nothing.
50:22.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Remembrance of Death and Afterlife'

50:29.arabic: أيديكما وما أنا بظلام للعبيد ويأمر بردهما إلى النار فيعدو أحدهما في سلاسله حتى يقتحمها ويتلكأ الآخر ويأمر بردهما ويسألهما عن فعلهما فيقول الذي عدا إلى النار قد حذرت من وبال المعصية فلم أكن لأتعرض لسخطك ثانية ويقول الذي تلكأ حسن ظني بك كان يشعرني أن لا تردني إليها بعد ما أخرجتني منها فيأمر بهما إلى الجنة وقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ينادي مناد من تحت العرش يوم القيامة يا أمة محمد أما ما كان لي قبلكم فقد وهبته لكم وبقيت التبعات فتواهبوها وادخلوا الجنة برحمتي (4) ويروى أن
50:29.english: He mentioned me one day, or feared me in a station (1). And the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: "When the people of the Fire are gathered in the Fire — and with them, whomsoever God wills of the people of the Qiblah — the disbelievers will say to the Muslims: 'Were you not Muslims?' They will reply: 'Yes.' Then they will say: 'What did your Islam avail you, seeing that you are with us in the Fire?' They will answer: 'We had sins, and we were seized for them.' Then God, Mighty and Glorious, will hear what they have said, and He will command that whoever was in the Fire of the people of the Qiblah be brought out, and they will be brought out. When the disbelievers see that, they will say: 'Would that we had been Muslims, so that we might be brought out as they were brought out.' Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited: {ربما يود الذين كفروا لو كانوا مسلمين} — "Perhaps those who disbelieve will wish that they had been Muslims" (Q. 15:2). (2)
50:29.section_title_en: On the Vastness of Divine Mercy and the Intercession for the Sinful — Section 1360
50:29.anchors:
- Root: ذكر (dhakara)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Remembrance, recollection; also mention, invocation.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-dhikr is the opposite of forgetfulness (nisyān); it denotes the heart's presence with what is recalled, and the tongue's utterance thereof.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): to recall in the heart or utter on the tongue. Metaphorical (majāz): "dhakartuhu bi-khayr" — to speak well of someone, i.e., to raise their mention in honor.
- Root: خرج (kharaja)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To exit, depart, emerge from an interior to an exterior.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-khurūj is the departure of a thing from its place or state; used of the soul leaving the body, and of the damned leaving the Fire.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: spatial egress. Metaphorical: "kharaja min al-amr" — to emerge from an affair, i.e., to be free of its obligation; and "akhrajahu Allāh min al-nār" — divine extraction by mercy, not by merit.
- Root: شفع (shafa'a)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To make even, pair; intercession is making one's supplication a pair with another's need.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-shafā'ah is the joining of one's intercession to another's request for aid; its reality is the elevation of the intercessor's rank and the remission of the offender's burden.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: pairing. Metaphorical: intercession before a king — the intercessor "pairs" his own honor with the petitioner's deficiency.
- Root: رحم (raḥima)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Tenderness of heart, compassion; al-Raḥmān is intensive — mercy as an essential attribute.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-raḥmah is tenderness that necessitates beneficence; when attributed to God, it is pure beneficence (tafaddul) without emotional change.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the mother's womb (raḥim) as the seat of compassion. Metaphorical: "arḥam al-rāḥimīn" — God's mercy as sheer gratuitous giving, exceeding any creaturely pity.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Restriction and Focused Predication (al-ḥaṣr wa al-taqyīd bi-innamā) — "Innamā shafā'atu Rasūlillāh…" restricts intercession to a specific class, namely those who have burdened themselves with sins, not the innocent.
50:29.topic: Al-Ghazali on the journey of the soul, death, and the Hereafter, from 'Remembrance of Death and Afterlife'

51:13.arabic: ينطقون ولا يؤذن لهم فيعتذرون يوم لا مرد له من الله يوم هم بارزون ويوم هم على النار يفتنون يوم لا ينفع مال ولا بنون يوم لا ينفع الظالمين معذرتهم ولهم اللعنة ولهم سوء الدار يوم ترد فيه المعاذير وتبلى السرائر وتظهر الضمائر وتكشف الأستار يوم تخشع فيه الأبصار وتسكن الأصوات ويقل فيه الالتفات وتبرز الخفيات وتظهر الخطيئات يوم يساق العباد ومعهم الأشهاد ويشيب الصغير ويسكر الكبير فيومئذ وضعت الموازين ونشرت الدواوين وبرزت الجحيم وأغلى الحميم وزفرت النار ويئس الكفار وسعرت النيران وتغيرت الألوان وخرس اللسان ونطقت جوارح الإنسان فيا أيها الإنسان م
51:13.english: So prepare yourself, O wretched one, for this Day of immense magnitude, of prolonged duration, of overwhelming dominion, whose appointed time is near — a Day when you shall see the heaven split asunder, and the stars scattered in its terror, and the shining planets extinguished, and the sun folded up, and the mountains set in motion, and the pregnant camels neglected, and the wild beasts gathered together, and the seas set ablaze, and the souls paired with their bodies, and the Hellfire ignited, and Paradise brought near, and the mountains pulverized, and the earth stretched out — a Day when you shall see the earth shaken with its quaking, and the earth casts forth its burdens. On that Day shall people issue forth in scattered groups to be shown their deeds — a Day when the earth and the mountains are lifted and crushed with a single crushing. Then on that Day the Imminent Event shall come to pass, and the heaven shall split open, for on that Day it shall be frail, and the angels shall be at its edges, and eight shall bear the Throne of your Lord above them on that Day. On that Day you shall be presented — no secret of yours shall remain hidden. A Day when the mountains shall move and you shall see the earth laid bare — a Day when the earth shall be shaken with a violent shaking, and the mountains crumbled to dust, becoming scattered particles — a Day when people shall be like scattered moths, and the mountains like carded wool — a Day when every nursing mother shall forget what she nursed, and every pregnant female shall cast down her burden, and you shall see people drunk, yet they are not drunk, but the chastisement of God is severe — a Day when the earth shall be changed to other than this earth, and the heavens, and they shall appear before God, the One, the All-Compelling — a Day when the mountains shall be blown away as dust, leaving a level, bare plain, wherein you see no crookedness nor curve — a Day when you see the mountains and suppose them solid, yet they pass by like the passing of clouds — a Day when the heaven shall split open and become rosy like molten oil. Then on that Day no human nor jinn shall be asked about his sin. A Day when the disobedient shall be prevented from speech, and shall not be asked about their crimes, but shall be seized by their forelocks and their feet — a Day when every soul shall find what it did of good brought forth present, and what it did of evil, wishing that between it and that evil there were a far distance — a Day when every soul shall know what it has sent ahead, and shall witness what it has forwarded and what it has left behind — a Day when tongues shall be struck mute and the bodily members shall speak — a Day whose mention turned the hair of the Master of the Messengers white, when al-Ṣiddīq (may God be pleased with him) said to him: "I see that you have turned white-haired, O Messenger of God." He said: "Sūrat Hūd and its sisters have made me white-haired" — namely, al-Wāqiʿah, al-Mursalāt, ʿAmma Yatasāʾalūn, and Idhā al-Shamsu Kuwwirat.
51:13.section_title_en: The Names and Attributes of the Day of Resurrection — An Exhortation to the Negligent
51:13.anchors:
- Root: يوم (yawm)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "اليوم: وقت طلوع الشمس إلى غروبها، وقد يعبر به عن مدة من الزمان أي مدة كانت" — the day as a temporal span, extended metaphorically to any epoch or era.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "اليوم يعبر به عن وقت طلوع الشمس إلى غروبها. وقد يعبر به عن مدة من الزمان أي مدة كانت" — theological usage denotes the appointed time of reckoning, magnified by divine attribution (أيام الله).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): a measured solar period. Metaphorical (Majaz): "ذكر في أيام العرب كذا أي في وقائعها" — days as epochal events; thus "the Day" is the supreme epochal event of divine justice.
- Root: نفس (nafs)
  * Lisan / Ayn: النفس: الروح والذات — the self, soul, or very essence.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "النفس: الروح... وقوله: ويحذركم الله نفسه فنفسه: ذاته" — nafs as the innermost reality of a being; in the eschatological context, souls are "paired" (زوجت) with bodies for judgment.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the soul as life-principle. Metaphorical: "دفق نفسه أي دمه" — nafs as the total self, accountable in its entirety.
- Root: ارض (arḍ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: الأرض: الجرم المقابل للسماء — the earth as the corporeal substratum beneath the heavens.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الأرض: الجرم المقابل للسماء... ويعبر بها عن أسفل الشيء" — the earth as the lowest register of creation, subject to total transformation on that Day.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the physical earth. Metaphorical: "تأرض فلان: لزم الأرض" — to cling low; on that Day the earth itself is leveled, flattened, and replaced.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد (Restriction & Focused Predication) — The repeated "يوم" clauses function as temporal restrictors (ẓurūf) binding each predicate to that single, all-encompassing moment; the accumulation of names (أسامي) serves not as mere repetition but as focused predication upon the multifarious realities of a single event.
51:13.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Remembrance of Death and Afterlife'

51:50.arabic: مجاورة هؤلاء في نعيمهم ثم قرأ ففروا إلى الله إني لكم منه نذير مبين قال ففر قوم فلولا ما جعل الله جل ثناؤه في النبوة من السر لقلنا ما هم بأفضل من هؤلاء فيما بلغنا أن الملائكة عليهم السلام لتلقاهم وتصافحهم والسحاب والسباع تمر بأحدهم فيناديها فتجيبه ويسألها أين أمرت فتخبره وليس بنبي وقال أبو هريرة رضي الله عنه قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم من حضر معصية فكرهها فكأنه غاب عنها ومن غاب عنها فأحبها فكأنه حضرها (4) ومعنى الحديث أن يحضر لحاجة أو يتفق جريان ذلك يديه فأما الحضور قصدا فممنوع بدليل الحديث الأول وقال ابن مسع
51:50.english: Know that the verses indicating the obligation of commanding right and forbidding wrong are numerous. Among them is His saying, may He be exalted: {«Let there arise from among you a nation inviting to good, commanding right and forbidding wrong — and those are the successful»} (Āl ʿImrān 3:104). In this verse is the declaration of obligation, for His saying, may He be exalted, "Let there be" (wal-takun) is a command, and the apparent meaning of a command is obligation. In it also is the declaration that success (falāḥ) is contingent upon it, for He restricted it and said: {«And those are the successful»}. In it also is the declaration that it is a collective obligation (farḍ kifāyah), not an individual obligation (farḍ ʿayn), and that when a group undertakes it, the obligation falls from the rest — for He did not say, "Let all of you be commanders of right," but rather said: {«Let there arise from among you a nation»}. Thus, whenever one person or a group undertakes it, the burden falls from the others, and success is particularized to those who undertake it and directly perform it. But if all of creation were to hold back from it, the burden would encompass all those capable of it without exception.
51:50.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'Remembrance of Death and Afterlife'

51:50.arabic: وبمشاهدة المتكلم دون ما سواه يكون العبد ممتثلا لقوله عز وجل ففروا إلى الله ولقوله ولا تجعلوا مع الله إلها آخر فمن لم يره في كل شيء فقد رأى غيره وكل ما التفت إليه العبد سوى الله تعالى تضمن التفاته شيئا من الشرك الخفي بل التوحيد الخالص أن لا يرى في كل شيء إلا الله عز وجل العاشر التبري وأعني به أن يتبرأ من حوله وقوته والالتفات إلى نفسه بين الرضا والتزكية فإذا تلا بآيات الوعد والمدح للصالحين فلا يشهد نفسه عند ذلك بل يشهد الموقنين والصديقين فيها ويتشوف إلى أن يلحقه الله عز وجل بهم وإذا تلا آيات المقت وذم العصاة والمقصرين شهد على نفسه هناك وقدر أنه المخاط
51:50.english: For this reason, Yūsuf ibn Asbāṭ said: "I intend to recite the Qur'an, but when I recall what is in it, I fear abhorrence (al-maqt), so I turn instead to glorification (al-tasbīḥ) and seeking forgiveness (al-istighfār)."
51:50.section_title_en: ** The Revival of the Religious Sciences — Section 231: On the Inward Conditions of Qur'anic Recitation (Continued)
51:50.anchors:
**
- Root: وجل (w-j-l)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الوجل: استشعار الخوف" — the stirring of fear/apprehension within
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الوجل: استشعار الخوف. يقال: وجل يوجل وجلا، فهو وجل. قال تعالى: {إنما المؤمنون الذين إذا ذكر الله وجلت قلوبهم}" — the theological state of the heart's trembling upon remembrance of God
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): "رجل وجل، وقوم وجال، وقد وجل وجلا" — the physical/emotional state of fear. Metaphorical (Majaz): The heart's trembling as the seat of spiritual perception
- Root: قلب (q-l-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "قلب الشيء: تصريفه وصرفه عن وجه إلى وجه" — turning and transforming
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "قلب الشيء: تصريفه وصرفه عن وجه إلى وجه، كقلب الثوب، وقلب الإنسان" — the heart as that which is constantly turning/transforming between states
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "قلب الشيء قلبا: حوله عن وجهه" — physical turning. Metaphorical: "قلب المعلم الصبيان: صرفهم إلى بيوتهم" — the heart's turning toward or away from spiritual realities
- Root: نفس (n-f-s)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The self, soul, spirit — that which is breathed
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "النفس: الروح" — the soul as the animating principle; also the self as the locus of blameworthy attributes
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "شيء نفيس ومنفس" — preciousness. Metaphorical: "دفق نفسه أي دمه" — the self as that which must be transcended in spiritual realization
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد (Restriction & Focused Predication) — governing the precise delimitation of spiritual states (أحوال) and their hierarchical gradation (درجات)

52:13.arabic: لا يغنى مولى عن مولى شيئا ويوم لا تملك نفس لنفس شيئا ويوم يدعون إلى نار جهنم دعا ويوم يسحبون فى النار على وجوههم ويوم تقلب وجوههم فى النار ويوم لا يجزى والد عن ولده ويوم يفر المرء من أخيه وأمه وأبيه ويوم لا ينطقون ولا يؤذن لهم فيعتذرون يوم لا مرد له من الله يوم هم بارزون ويوم هم على النار يفتنون يوم لا ينفع مال ولا بنون يوم لا ينفع الظالمين معذرتهم ولهم اللعنة ولهم سوء الدار يوم ترد فيه المعاذير وتبلى السرائر وتظهر الضمائر وتكشف الأستار يوم تخشع فيه الأبصار وتسكن الأصوات ويقل فيه الالتفات وتبرز الخفيات وتظهر الخطيئات يوم ي
52:13.english: So prepare yourself, O wretched one, for this Day of immense magnitude, of prolonged duration, of overwhelming dominion, whose appointed time is near — a Day when you shall see the heaven split asunder, and the stars scattered in its terror, and the shining planets extinguished, and the sun folded up, and the mountains set in motion, and the pregnant camels neglected, and the wild beasts gathered together, and the seas set ablaze, and the souls paired with their bodies, and the Hellfire ignited, and Paradise brought near, and the mountains pulverized, and the earth stretched out — a Day when you shall see the earth shaken with its quaking, and the earth casts forth its burdens. On that Day shall people issue forth in scattered groups to be shown their deeds — a Day when the earth and the mountains are lifted and crushed with a single crushing. Then on that Day the Imminent Event shall come to pass, and the heaven shall split open, for on that Day it shall be frail, and the angels shall be at its edges, and eight shall bear the Throne of your Lord above them on that Day. On that Day you shall be presented — no secret of yours shall remain hidden. A Day when the mountains shall move and you shall see the earth laid bare — a Day when the earth shall be shaken with a violent shaking, and the mountains crumbled to dust, becoming scattered particles — a Day when people shall be like scattered moths, and the mountains like carded wool — a Day when every nursing mother shall forget what she nursed, and every pregnant female shall cast down her burden, and you shall see people drunk, yet they are not drunk, but the chastisement of God is severe — a Day when the earth shall be changed to other than this earth, and the heavens, and they shall appear before God, the One, the All-Compelling — a Day when the mountains shall be blown away as dust, leaving a level, bare plain, wherein you see no crookedness nor curve — a Day when you see the mountains and suppose them solid, yet they pass by like the passing of clouds — a Day when the heaven shall split open and become rosy like molten oil. Then on that Day no human nor jinn shall be asked about his sin. A Day when the disobedient shall be prevented from speech, and shall not be asked about their crimes, but shall be seized by their forelocks and their feet — a Day when every soul shall find what it did of good brought forth present, and what it did of evil, wishing that between it and that evil there were a far distance — a Day when every soul shall know what it has sent ahead, and shall witness what it has forwarded and what it has left behind — a Day when tongues shall be struck mute and the bodily members shall speak — a Day whose mention turned the hair of the Master of the Messengers white, when al-Ṣiddīq (may God be pleased with him) said to him: "I see that you have turned white-haired, O Messenger of God." He said: "Sūrat Hūd and its sisters have made me white-haired" — namely, al-Wāqiʿah, al-Mursalāt, ʿAmma Yatasāʾalūn, and Idhā al-Shamsu Kuwwirat.

- Root: يوم (yawm)

52:15.arabic: فبصرك اليوم حديد} ويقال أفسخر هذا أم أنتم لا تبصرون اصلوها فاصبروا أو لا تبصروا سواء عليكم إنما تجزون ما كنتم تعملون وإليهم الإشارة بقوله تعالى {وبدا لهم من الله ما لم يكونوا يحتسبون} فأعلم العلماء وأحكم الحكماء ينكشف له عقيب الموت من العجائب والآيات ما لم يخطر قط بباله ولا اختلج به ضميره فلو لم يكن للعاقل هم وغم إلا الفكرة في خطر تلك الحال أن الحجاب عماذا يرتفع وما الذي ينكشف عنه الغطاء من
52:15.english: Know that the lights of inner insights (anwār al-baṣā'ir) derived from the Book of God—mighty and majestic is He—and from the Sunnah of His Messenger—may God's peace and blessings be upon him—and from the pathways of reflective consideration, make known to us the states of the dead in general and their division into the blessed and the wretched. But the specific case of Zayd and ʿAmr in particular is not disclosed at all. For if we rely upon the faith of Zayd and ʿAmr, we do not know upon what they died nor how their end was sealed for them. And if we rely upon their outward righteousness, then piety (taqwā) has its seat in the heart, and it is hidden—concealed even from the possessor of that piety himself—so how then from others? Thus there is no ruling for outward righteousness apart from inward piety. God—exalted is He—said: {«إنما يتقبل الله من المتقين»} ["God only accepts from the God-fearing"] (Al-Mā'idah 5:27). So the knowledge of the judgment concerning Zayd and ʿAmr is not possible except by witnessing them and witnessing what transpires upon them. And when one dies, he has transferred from the world of dominion and testimony (ʿālam al-mulk wa al-shahādah) to the world of the unseen and the kingdom (ʿālam al-ghayb wa al-malakūt), so he is not seen by the outward eye. Rather, he is seen only by another eye—that eye being created in the heart of every human being. But upon it has been placed a dense covering (ghishāwah) of his lusts and worldly preoccupations, so that he does not see with it, nor is it conceivable that he should see with it anything of the realm of the kingdom (malakūt) unless that covering is peeled away from the eye of his heart.
52:15.section_title_en: The Unveiling of the Veil: On the Vision of the Dead and the Reality of Dreams
52:15.anchors:
- Root: بصر (B-Ṣ-R)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Inner perception and discernment; the eye as an organ of sight versus the "insight" (baṣīrah) as the heart's eye.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Baṣīrah is the perception of the heart, a spiritual sight (ru'yah qalbiyyah) that penetrates to realities, distinct from mere ocular vision.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) sight is of the physical eye; metaphorical (majāz) sight is the heart's illumination by which hidden truths are disclosed.
- Root: كشف (K-Sh-F)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Removal of a covering; disclosure of what is concealed.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Kashf in the theological sense is the lifting of the veil (ghishāwah) from the heart so that the unseen realm (malakūt) becomes manifest.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: uncovering a physical object; metaphorical: revelation of meanings and hidden affairs to the inner eye.
- Root: لوح (L-W-Ḥ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: A tablet or board upon which writing appears; also the flat bones of the body.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The Preserved Tablet (al-Lawḥ al-Maḥfūẓ) is that upon which all destinies are inscribed; its modality is unknown to us save by report.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: a wooden plank; metaphorical: the divine register of all that was and will be, not corporeal but a subtle reality.
- Root: مثل (M-Th-L)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Likeness, similitude, example; to stand in representation of another.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Mathal is the analogical representation by which an absent or abstract reality is brought near to understanding through a present likeness.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: a resembling image; metaphorical: the parabolic example (mithāl) used to approximate what transcends sensory grasp.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Restriction and Specification (al-ḥaṣr wa al-taqyīd bi-innamā) — The particle "innamā" confines the predicate to the subject alone, as in "إنما يتقبل الله من المتقين," restricting divine acceptance exclusively to the God-fearing, a syntactic anchor for the theological point that outward piety without inward taqwā avails nothing.

  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): a measured solar period. Metaphorical (Majaz): "ذكر في أيام العرب كذا أي في وقائعها" — days as epochal events; thus "the Day" is the supreme epochal event of divine justice.
- Root: نفس (nafs)
  * Lisan / Ayn: النفس: الروح والذات — the self, soul, or very essence.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "النفس: الروح... وقوله: ويحذركم الله نفسه فنفسه: ذاته" — nafs as the innermost reality of a being; in the eschatological context, souls are "paired" (زوجت) with bodies for judgment.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the soul as life-principle. Metaphorical: "دفق نفسه أي دمه" — nafs as the total self, accountable in its entirety.
- Root: ارض (arḍ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: الأرض: الجرم المقابل للسماء — the earth as the corporeal substratum beneath the heavens.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الأرض: الجرم المقابل للسماء... ويعبر بها عن أسفل الشيء" — the earth as the lowest register of creation, subject to total transformation on that Day.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the physical earth. Metaphorical: "تأرض فلان: لزم الأرض" — to cling low; on that Day the earth itself is leveled, flattened, and replaced.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد (Restriction & Focused Predication) — The repeated "يوم" clauses function as temporal restrictors (ẓurūf) binding each predicate to that single, all-encompassing moment; the accumulation of names (أسامي) serves not as mere repetition but as focused predication upon the multifarious realities of a single event.

54:54.arabic: كأمثال اللؤلؤ المكنون جزاء بما كانوا يعملون في مقام أمين في جنات وعيون في جنات ونهر في مقعد صدق عند مليك مقتدر ينظرون فيها إلى وجه الملك الكريم وقد أشرقت في وجوههم نضرة النعيم لا يرهقهم فتر ولا ذلة بل عباد مكرمون وبأنواع التحف من ربهم يتعاهدون فهم فيما اشتهيت أنفسهم خالدون لا يخافون فيها ولا يحزنون وهم من ريب المنون آمنون فهم فيها يتنعمون ويأكلون من أطعمتها ويشربون من أنهارها لبنا وخمرا وعسلا في أنهار أراضيها من فضة وحصباؤها مرجان وعلى أرض ترابها مسك أذفر ونباتها زعفران ويمطرون من سحاب فيها من ماء النسرين على كثبان الكافور ويؤتون بأكواب وأي أكواب بأك
54:54.english: For God Most High has said: {«إن الأبرار لفي نعيم وإن الفجار لفي جحيم»} — "Indeed the righteous are in bliss, and indeed the wicked are in Hellfire." So present yourself before these two verses, and you will have known your resting-place between the two abodes. And God knows best.
54:54.section_title_en: Section 1351 — On the Description of Paradise and the Varieties of Its Bliss
54:54.anchors:
- Root: نعم (n-ʿ-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root denotes softness, ease, and pleasant living; al-Ayn notes it among names of the leopard and tiger, while Lisan records "Nuʿm" as a proper name.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "النعمة: الحالة الحسنة" — niʿmah is the excellent state/condition one inhabits; niʿīm is the experience of delight. The verse {«إن الأبرار لفي نعيم»} designates the abiding state of bliss as a settled condition, not a transient act.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): "في النعمة والنعيم" — dwelling in bounty and bliss. Metaphorical (Majaz): "خفت نعامتهم: ذهبوا" — ostriches departing; here the root's literal sense of softness is transfigured into the theological state of perpetual ease, free from all harshness.
- Root: وجه (w-j-h)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root: face, front, direction; al-Ayn cites "وجه الصواب" — the face/course of correctness.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The face is the noblest part of the outward body, hence used for the essence (al-dhāt) of a thing; in {«ويبقى وجه ربك ذو الجلال والإكرام»} it signifies the Divine Essence. Here "وجه الملك الكريم" — the Face of the Generous King — denotes the Beatific Vision of God's Essence, not a corporeal organ.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical face. Metaphorical: "وجه القوم، وهؤلاء وجوه البلد" — the foremost, noblest of a people; thus the "face" of the King is His most august presence.
- Root: مرج (m-r-j)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root: mixing, confusion, letting loose; al-Ayn: "المرج: الشهد" — also pure honey; Lisan: "مرج أمرهم: اختلط" — their affair became disordered.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "أصل المرج: الخلط" — mixing; "أمر مريج" — a confused affair (Q. 50:5). In this text, the rivers of Paradise "مطردة" (flowing) are not "ممرجة" (mixed/confused) — rather they run pure and distinct, each in its channel.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "مرج الدواب: أرسلها في المرج" — releasing beasts into pasture. Metaphorical: "مرج الله البحرين" — God let the two seas flow freely; "مرجت عهودهم" — covenants became disordered. The contrast sharpens the purity of Paradise's rivers.
- Root: امن (a-m-n)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root: safety, freedom from fear; al-Ayn treats it under the hamzah chapter as the state of security.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "أصل الأمن: طمأنينة النفس وزوال الخوف" — tranquility of the soul and removal of fear. In the Hereafter, "آمنون" is not mere absence of threat but the positive, settled peace of the soul in the Divine presence.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "أمنته وآمننيه" — to grant safety. Metaphorical: "فرس أمين القوى" — a horse whose strength is trustworthy; here the blessed are "آمنون من ريب المنون" — secure from the vicissitudes of fate, a security that is trustworthy and unbreachable.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The rule permits separation between a preposition and its object by an element upon which speech may properly pause, as in "إن به لضرًا" — here "فهم فيما اشتهت أنفسهم خالدون" (in what their souls desire, abiding eternally) interposes the clause of desire between the prepositional phrase and its predicate, heightening rhetorical emphasis on the soul's fulfillment.
54:54.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Remembrance of Death and Afterlife'

55:29.arabic: وهو أحد والآصال التي ذكرها الله تعالى إذ قال ولله يسجد من في السموات والأرض طوعا وكرها وظلالهم بالغدو والآصال وإذا سجد لله عز وجل الجمادات فكيف يجوز أن يغفل العبد العاقل عن أنواع العبادات الورد السادس إذا دخل وقت العصر دخل وقت الورد السادس وهو الذي أقسم الله تعالى به فقال تعالى {والعصر} هذا أحد معنيي الآية وهو المراد بالآصال في أحد التفسيرين وهو العشي المذكور في قوله {وعشيا} وفي قوله {بالعشي والإشراق} وليس في هذا الورد صلاة إلا أربع ركعات بين الأذان والإقامة كما سبق في الظهر ثم يصلي الفرض ويشتغل بالأقسام الأربعة المذكورة
55:29.english: I say: And just as knowledge and remembrance are the nourishment of the heart, which can never be cut off from it, so too the measure of moderation is this; and deficiency from it may lead to the disturbance of the body — except for one who accustoms himself to wakefulness gradually, for he may train himself upon it without disturbance. And this litany (wird) is among the longest of the litanies and the most delightful for the worshippers, and it is one of the "evenings and mornings" (al-āṣāl) which God Most High mentioned when He said: {«ولله يسجد من في السموات والأرض طوعا وكرها وظلالهم بالغدو والآصال»} "And to God prostrates whoever is in the heavens and the earth, willingly or unwillingly, and their shadows, in the mornings and the evenings" (Q. 13:15). And when inanimate objects prostrate to God, Mighty and Majestic, how then can the intelligent servant be heedless of the varieties of worship?
55:29.section_title_en: The Seventh Daily Litany (Al-Wird al-Sābiʿ): The Time of Sunset — The Completion of the Day's Litanies and Self-Accounting
55:29.anchors:
- Root: ورد (warada)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The root denotes arriving at water, seeking it, and drinking from it; also the portion or share of water allotted for drinking at a specific time.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الورود أصله: قصد الماء" — the core meaning is the intentional approach to water; the litany (wird) is the appointed portion of devotional recitation, likened to the daily share of water that a person must take to sustain life.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): the act of arriving at water. Metaphorical (Majaz): "ورد علي كتاب سرني مورده" — a book arrived upon me whose arrival pleased me; likewise, the wird is the arrival of the appointed time for worship, and the soul's approach to the fountain of divine remembrance.
- Root: عصر (ʿaṣr)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The root denotes pressing, squeezing, and extracting; also the time of afternoon, so called because it is the pressing of the day's end.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The ʿaṣr is the latter part of the day; God swore by it in {«والعصر»} (Q. 103:1), indicating its great merit.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the afternoon time. Metaphorical: the pressing of one's life — as the day is pressed at its end, so the life of man is pressed at its term.
- Root: غرب (gharaba)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The root denotes disappearance, absence, and setting; the sun's setting (ghurūb) is its concealment from the eye.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The setting of the sun marks the boundary between the day's works and the night's; it is the terminus of the visible world's diurnal cycle.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the sun's descent below the horizon. Metaphorical: the setting of the sun of life — the death of man, after which there is no rising.
- Root: حاسب (ḥāsaba)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The root denotes reckoning, counting, and taking account; muḥāsabah is the mutual reckoning between two parties.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Self-accounting (muḥāsabat al-nafs) is the soul's reckoning with itself over its deeds before the Day of Reckoning, for "one who reckons himself before he is reckoned" is among the wise.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the arithmetic counting of sums. Metaphorical: the soul's audit of its own works, weighing the day's deeds against the standard of the Sacred Law.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The rule governing the separation of the prepositional phrase from its governing verb, as in the construction "فسبحان الله حين تمسون" where the adverbial clause is interposed to emphasize the temporal specification of the act of glorification.
55:29.topic: Al-Ghazali on constant remembrance of God and contemplative invocations, from 'Remembrance of Death and Afterlife'

55:39.arabic: تنشق فيه السماء فتكون وردة كالدهان فيومئذ لا يسئل عن ذنبه إنس ولا جان يوم يمنع فيه العاصى من الكلام ولا يسئل فيه عن الأجرام بل يؤخذ بالنواصى والأقدام يوم تجد كل نفس ما عملت من خير محضرا وما عملت من سوء تود لو أن بينها وبينه أمدا بعيدا يوم تعلم فيه كل نفس ما أحضرت وتشهد ما قدمت وأخرت يوم تخرس فيه الألسن وتنطق الجوارح يوم شيب ذكره سيد المرسلين إذ قال له الصديق رضي الله عنه أراك قد شبت يا رسول الله قال شيبتنى هود وأخواتها (1) وهى الواقعة والمرسلات وعم يتساءلون وإذا الشمس كورت فيا أيها القارىء العاجز إنما حظك من قراءتك
55:39.english: So prepare yourself, O wretched one, for this Day of immense magnitude, of prolonged duration, of overwhelming dominion, whose appointed time is near — a Day when you shall see the heaven split asunder, and the stars scattered in its terror, and the shining planets extinguished, and the sun folded up, and the mountains set in motion, and the pregnant camels neglected, and the wild beasts gathered together, and the seas set ablaze, and the souls paired with their bodies, and the Hellfire ignited, and Paradise brought near, and the mountains pulverized, and the earth stretched out — a Day when you shall see the earth shaken with its quaking, and the earth casts forth its burdens. On that Day shall people issue forth in scattered groups to be shown their deeds — a Day when the earth and the mountains are lifted and crushed with a single crushing. Then on that Day the Imminent Event shall come to pass, and the heaven shall split open, for on that Day it shall be frail, and the angels shall be at its edges, and eight shall bear the Throne of your Lord above them on that Day. On that Day you shall be presented — no secret of yours shall remain hidden. A Day when the mountains shall move and you shall see the earth laid bare — a Day when the earth shall be shaken with a violent shaking, and the mountains crumbled to dust, becoming scattered particles — a Day when people shall be like scattered moths, and the mountains like carded wool — a Day when every nursing mother shall forget what she nursed, and every pregnant female shall cast down her burden, and you shall see people drunk, yet they are not drunk, but the chastisement of God is severe — a Day when the earth shall be changed to other than this earth, and the heavens, and they shall appear before God, the One, the All-Compelling — a Day when the mountains shall be blown away as dust, leaving a level, bare plain, wherein you see no crookedness nor curve — a Day when you see the mountains and suppose them solid, yet they pass by like the passing of clouds — a Day when the heaven shall split open and become rosy like molten oil. Then on that Day no human nor jinn shall be asked about his sin. A Day when the disobedient shall be prevented from speech, and shall not be asked about their crimes, but shall be seized by their forelocks and their feet — a Day when every soul shall find what it did of good brought forth present, and what it did of evil, wishing that between it and that evil there were a far distance — a Day when every soul shall know what it has sent ahead, and shall witness what it has forwarded and what it has left behind — a Day when tongues shall be struck mute and the bodily members shall speak — a Day whose mention turned the hair of the Master of the Messengers white, when al-Ṣiddīq (may God be pleased with him) said to him: "I see that you have turned white-haired, O Messenger of God." He said: "Sūrat Hūd and its sisters have made me white-haired" — namely, al-Wāqiʿah, al-Mursalāt, ʿAmma Yatasāʾalūn, and Idhā al-Shamsu Kuwwirat.
55:39.section_title_en: The Names and Attributes of the Day of Resurrection — An Exhortation to the Negligent

55:46.arabic: وقد قال تعالى ولمن خاف مقام ربه جنتان ذلك لمن خاف مقامي وخاف وعيد والقرآن من أوله إلى آخره تحذير وتخويف لا يتفكر فيه متفكر إلا ويطول حزنه ويعظم خوفه إن كان مؤمنا بما فيه وترى الناس يهذونه هذا يخرجون الحروف من مخارجها ويتناظرون على خفضها ورفعها ونصبها وكأنهم يقرءون شعرا من أشعار العرب لا يهمهم الالتفات إلى معانيه والعمل بما فيه وهل في العالم غرور يزيد على هذا فهذه أمثلة الغرور بالله وبيان الفرق بين الرجاء والغرور ويقرب منه غرور طوائف لهم طاعات ومعاص إلا أن معاصيهم أكثر وهم يتوقعون
55:46.english: For if this matter were attained by wishful longing and reached by idle desire, then what was the meaning of the weeping of those [early believers], their fear, and their grief? We have already expounded the reality of these matters in the Book of Fear and Hope (Kitāb al-Khawf wa al-Rajā'). And the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, said — in what Muʿqil ibn Yasār narrated: "A time will come upon the people in which the Qur'an will wear out in the hearts of men just as garments wear out upon bodies. Their entire affair will be [one of] covetousness with no fear accompanying it. If one of them does good, he says: 'It will be accepted from me'; and if he does evil, he says: 'I will be forgiven.'" // The hadith of Muʿqil ibn Yasār: "A time will come upon the people in which the Qur'an will wear out in the hearts of men..." — This hadith was transmitted by Abu Mansur al-Daylami in Musnad al-Firdaws from Ibn ʿAbbas with similar wording, through a chain containing unknown narrators; I have not seen it from the hadith of Muʿqil.
55:46.section_title_en: The Reality of False Hope (Ghurūr) and Its Distinction from True Hope (Rajā') — Section 891
55:46.anchors:
- Root: غرر (gh-r-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning — an outward trace or mark; heedlessness in wakefulness; the blaze on a horse's forehead.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Ghurūr" is delusion arising from heedlessness — one is "folded upon his heedlessness" (ṭawāhu ʿalā gharrihi), as in {«ما غرك بربك الكريم»} (Q 82:6). It is the state of being deceived by wishful thinking while blind to warning.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): heedlessness/negligence. Metaphorical (Majaz): being deceived by false appearances — e.g., "a day white and blazing" (yawm agharr muḥajjal) for intense heat; the gazelle deceived by moonlight (agharr min ẓaby muqmir) that exposes it to predators.
- Root: خوف (kh-w-f)
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Al-Khawf" is the anticipation of something disliked based on a probable or certain indicator — the opposite of amn (security). It is paired with rajā' (hope) in {«يدعون ربهم خوفا وطمعا»} (Q 32:16).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: fear of loss or harm. Metaphorical: gradual diminishment — "takhawwafa al-sayr" (the journey wore away the camel's hump little by little), as if fearing it.
- Root: وقد (w-q-d)
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Fire blazing with fuel — {«وقودها الناس والحجارة»} (Q 2:24). Used for both the fuel and the flame.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: kindling fire. Metaphorical: "qalb waqqād" (a blazing, penetrating intellect); "waqada al-ḥaṣā" (pebbles becoming scorching hot).
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The permissibility of interposing elements between a governing word and its governed prepositional phrase, provided the intervening clause is complete in itself; here, the periodic structure of Ghazali's condemnation ("فترى الواحد...") suspends the subject across multiple clauses before resolution.
55:46.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Remembrance of Death and Afterlife'

55:56.arabic: والمرجان لم يطمثهن إنس قبلهم ولا جان يمشين في درجات الجنان إذا اختالت إحداهن في مشيها حمل أعطافها سبعون ألفا من الولدان عليها من طرائف الحرير الأبيض ما تتحير فيه الأبصار مكللات بالتيجان المرصعة باللؤلؤ والمرجان شكلات غنجات عطرات آمنات من الهرم والبؤس مقصورات في الخيام في قصور من الياقوت بنيت وسط روضات الجنان قاصرات الطرف عين ثم يطاف عليهم وعليهن بأكواب وأباريق وكأس من معين بيضاء لذة للشاربين ويطوف عليهم خدام وولدان كأمثال اللؤلؤ المكنون جزاء بما كانوا يعملون في مقام أمين في جنات
55:56.english: For God Most High has said: {«إن الأبرار لفي نعيم وإن الفجار لفي جحيم»} — "Indeed the righteous are in bliss, and indeed the wicked are in Hellfire." So present yourself before these two verses, and you will have known your resting-place between the two abodes. And God knows best.

55:72.arabic: قوله تعالى حور مقصورات في الخيام // حديث أنس لما أسري بي دخلت في الجنة موضعا يسمى الصرح عليه خيام اللؤلؤ والزبرجد الأخضر والياقوت الأحمر الحديث وفيه أن جبريل قال هؤلاء المقصورات في الخيام وفيه فطفقن يقلن نحن الراضيات فلا نسخط لم أجده هكذا بتمامه وللترمذى من حديث على أن فى الجنة لمجتمعا للحور العين يرفعن أصواتا لم تسمع الخلائق مثلها يقلن نحن الخالدات فلا نبيد ونحن الناعمات فلا نبأس ونحن الراضيات فلا نسخط طوبى لمن كان لنا وكنا له وقال غريب ولأبى الشيخ فى كتاب العظمة
55:72.english: It is narrated from Anas (may God be pleased with him) that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "A single morning or evening march in the path of God is better than the world and all that is in it. And verily, the space of the bow of one of you, or the place of his foot, in Paradise is better than the world and all that is in it. And if a woman from among the women of the people of Paradise were to look down upon the earth, she would illuminate it and fill all that is between the two [heaven and earth] with fragrance, and verily the scarf upon her head is better than the world and all that is in it" — meaning the veil (khimār).
55:72.section_title_en: On the Attributes of the Houris (Ḥūr al-ʿAyn) and the Eternal Youths (Wildān)
55:72.anchors:
- Root: حور (Ḥ-W-R)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of returning, circling back; in the passive form (ḥūr), denotes intensely white eyes with intensely black pupils — the paradigmatic beauty of the celestial maidens.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-ḥawar is "the turning back" — whether by essence or by thought; the ḥūr are so named for the purity of their gaze, their eyes turning in radiant whiteness, never dimming.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): "In her eye is ḥawar" — the natural, created whiteness. Metaphorical (majāz): "His mill-pegs became restless" (qaliqat maḥāwiruh) — borrowed from the axle's turning when the socket loosens, signifying utter disquiet; thus the ḥūr's beauty is a perpetual, unshaken radiance.
- Root: عين (ʿAyn)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The eye as organ; also the spring of water, the self, the watcher. Kitāb al-ʿAyn: "ʿAyn āniyah" — a hot spring {«الغاشية: 12»}.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The eye is the instrument of perception; "ʿayn" for the guardian who watches over a thing — "Verily you are in Our eyes" {«الطور: 48»} means under Our sight and protection.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "He is a slave of the eye" — one who serves only for show. Metaphorical: "The earth looked with an eye" — vegetation sprouting without deep roots; thus ḥūr ʿayn are those whose beauty is beheld by the eye as a living spring, never exhausted.
- Root: انس (A-N-S)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Sociability, familiarity, companionship; the human being (insān) as the sociable creature.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The jinn and ins are both created, passive to God's act; the houris are "the companions" (al-ʿīn) who bring perfect intimacy, removing all estrangement.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "He is the son of the intimacy of so-and-so" — his special confidant. Metaphorical: "The fire is the intimate one" (al-anīsah) — that which keeps one company and calms the heart; so the houris are the intimate companions of the blessed, dispelling all solitude.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The permissibility of interposing a clause between a preposition and its object when the intervening material is a complete, self-sufficient statement, as in the reported speech of the houris: "We are the contented ones, so we never anger" — each clause standing independently yet grammatically bound to the governing verb of saying.

55:74.arabic: والمرجان لم يطمثهن إنس قبلهم ولا جان يمشين في درجات الجنان إذا اختالت إحداهن في مشيها حمل أعطافها سبعون ألفا من الولدان عليها من طرائف الحرير الأبيض ما تتحير فيه الأبصار مكللات بالتيجان المرصعة باللؤلؤ والمرجان شكلات غنجات عطرات آمنات من الهرم والبؤس مقصورات في الخيام في قصور من الياقوت بنيت وسط روضات الجنان قاصرات الطرف عين ثم يطاف عليهم وعليهن بأكواب وأباريق وكأس من معين بيضاء لذة للشاربين ويطوف عليهم خدام وولدان كأمثال اللؤلؤ المكنون جزاء بما كانوا يعملون في مقام أمين في جنات
