56:51.arabic: ثم انظر إلى طعامهم وهو الزقوم كما قال الله تعالى {ثم إنكم أيها الضالون المكذبون لآكلون من شجر من زقوم فمالئون منها البطون فشاربون عليه من الحميم فشاربون شرب الهيم} وقال تعالى {إنها شجرة تخرج في أصل الجحيم طلعها كأنه رؤوس الشياطين فإنهم لآكلون منها فمالئون منها البطون ثم إن لهم عليها لشوبا من حميم ثم إن مرجعهم لإلى الجحيم} وقال تعالى {تصلى نارا حامية تسقى من عين آنية} وقال تعالى {إن لدينا أنكالا وجحيما وطعاما ذا غصة وعذابا أليما} وقال ابن عباس قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لو أن قطرة من الزقوم قطرت في بحار الدنيا أفسدت على أهل الدنيا معايشهم (2) فكيف من يكون طعامه ذلك وقال أنس قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
56:51.english: And ʿAlī, may God honor his face, said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: "Seek refuge in God from the Pit of Sorrow, or the Valley of Sorrow." It was said: "O Messenger of God, what is the Valley or Pit of Sorrow?" He said: "A valley in Hell from which Hell itself seeks refuge with God seventy times each day. God, the Exalted, has prepared it for the reciters who show off." (2)
56:51.section_title_en: The Vastness of Hellfire, Its Depths, and the Torments of Its Inhabitants
56:51.anchors:
- Root: و د ي (w-d-y)
  * Lisan / Ayn: A valley; a place where torrents flow. In the lexicon, it denotes a lowland or watercourse between mountains.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Used for the valleys of Hell as places of confinement and passage, each containing further branching ravines (شُعَب), indicating graded descent.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal for earthly valleys; here transferred (majāz) to the topographical reality of Hell, affirming its corporeal vastness.
- Root: ع م ق (ʿ-m-q)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Depth; the far bottom of a well or pit. Al-Farahidi: "العمق: قعر البئر ونحوها."
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Depth as a measure of descent; in the Hereafter, it is unbounded, paralleling the unbounded depth of worldly desire.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal for physical depth; here extended to show the infinite regress of punishment corresponding to infinite craving.
- Root: غ س ق (gh-s-q)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Stinking, foul pus or ichor that flows from the skin of the damned; also intense darkness.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-Ghassāq is the putrid effusion of Hell, a punishment for the senses, specifically for drinking when the damned cry out in thirst.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal for what is loathsome and fetid; in the Quranic context, it is the designated drink of the inhabitants.
- Root: ز ق م (z-q-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To swallow with difficulty; the tree of Zaqqūm, which grows in the depths of Hell.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): A specific tree in Hell whose fruit is like the heads of devils, eaten by the damned to fill their bellies, causing choking and agony.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal for a real tree; its description is sensory, not metaphorical, affirming the physical reality of punishment.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The periodic structure of "في جهنم سبعين ألف واد" allows the prepositional phrase to precede the subject for emphasis, establishing the spatial setting before detailing its contents.
56:51.topic: Al-Ghazali on purifying the character, moral diseases, and spiritual remedies, from 'Remembrance of Death and Afterlife'

57:14.arabic: وتربصتم قال بالتوبة وارتبتم قال شككتم حتى جاء أمر الله قال الموت وغركم بالله الغرور قال الشيطان وقال الحسن تصبروا وتشددوا فإنما هي أيام قلائل وإنما أنتم ركب وقوف يوشك أن يدعى الرجل منكم فيجيب ولا يلتفت فانتقلوا بصالح ما بحضرتكم وقال ابن مسعود ما منكم من أحد أصبح إلا وهو ضيف وما له عارية والضيف مرتحل والعارية مؤداة وقال أبو عبيدة الباجي دخلنا على الحسن في مرضه الذي مات فيه فقال مرحبا بكم وأهلا حياكم الله بالسلام وأحلنا وإياكم دار المقام هذه علانية حسنة إن صبرتم وصدقتم واتقيتم فلا يكن حظكم من هذا ال
57:14.english: I say: The hadith was transmitted by al-Tirmidhi and deemed sound (ḥasan) from the narration of Ubayy ibn Kaʿb (5): a hadith that when he (the Prophet, peace be upon him) sensed from his companions heedlessness or negligence, he would call out to them in a raised voice: "Death has come upon you." This hadith was transmitted by Ibn Abi al-Dunya in *Qaṣr al-Amal* from the narration of Zayd al-Sulaymi as a mursal report (6). The hadith of Abu Hurayrah: "I am the warner, death is the transformer, and the Hour is the appointed meeting" — transmitted by Ibn Abi al-Dunya in *Qaṣr al-Amal* and by Abu al-Qasim al-Baghawi with an isnad containing some weakness (7). The hadith of Ibn ʿUmar: "The Messenger of God, peace be upon him, went out while the sun was at the tips of the palm fronds and said: 'What remains of this world is but like what remains of this day of ours, relative to what has passed of it'" — transmitted by Ibn Abi al-Dunya therein with a sound isnad, and al-Tirmidhi transmitted something similar from the narration of Abu Saʿid and deemed it sound (8). The hadith: "The likeness of this world is like a garment torn from its beginning to its end" — transmitted by Ibn Abi al-Dunya therein from the narration of Anas, but it is not authentic (9). Ibn Masʿud, may God be pleased with him, said: The Messenger of God, peace be upon him, recited: {فمن يرد الله أن يهديه يشرح صدره للإسلام} "Whomsoever God wishes to guide, He expands his breast to Islam" {فقال} "Then he said: 'When the light enters the breast, it expands.' It was said: 'O Messenger of God, is there a sign of this that is recognized?' PageV04P459 {قال} He said: 'Yes: withdrawal from the abode of delusion, turning in repentance to the abode of permanence, and preparation for death before its descent.'" Al-Suddi said concerning His saying: {الذي خلق الموت والحياة ليبلوكم أيكم أحسن عملا} "He who created death and life to test you, which of you is best in deed" — meaning: which of you is most mindful of death, best prepared for it, and most fearful and cautious of it. Hudhayfah said: "There is no morning or evening except that a caller calls out: 'O people, the departure! The departure!'" The confirmation of that is His saying, the Exalted: {إنها لإحدى الكبر * نذيرا للبشر * لمن شاء منكم أن يتقدم أو يتأخر} "Indeed, it is one of the greatest calamities, a warning to mankind, for whoever among you wishes to advance or delay" — regarding death. Suhaym, the freed slave of Banu Tamim, said: I sat with ʿAmir ibn ʿAbd Allah while he was praying, and he shortened his prayer, then turned to me and said: "Relieve me of your need, for I am hastening." I said: "What are you hastening for?" He said: "The angel of death, may God have mercy on you." He said: So I rose from him, and he returned to his prayer. Dawud al-Ta'i passed by, and a man asked him about a hadith, so he said: "Leave me, for I am only hastening against the departure of my soul." ʿUmar, may God be pleased with him, said: "Deliberation is good in everything except in deeds of goodness for the Hereafter." Al-Mundhir said: I heard Malik ibn Dinar saying to himself: "Woe to you, hasten before the matter comes upon you. Woe to you, hasten before the matter comes upon you" — repeating that sixty times, while I heard him and he did not see me. Al-Hasan used to say in his exhortation: "Hasten, hasten! For it is but breaths — if they are held back, your deeds by which you draw near to God, the Mighty and Majestic, are cut off. May God have mercy on a man who looked to his own soul and wept over the number of his sins." Then he recited this verse: {إنما نعد لهم عدا} "We only count for them a counting" — meaning the breaths. The end of the counting is the departure of your soul; the end of the counting is the parting from your family; the end of the counting is your entry into your grave. Abu Musa al-Ashʿari strove with intense exertion before his death, and it was said to him: "Would you not hold back, or show yourself some gentleness?" He said: "When horses are released and approach the end of their course, they bring out all that they have. What remains of my term is less than that." He said: He continued in that state until he died. And he used to say to his wife: "Tighten your saddle, for there is no crossing over Hellfire." One of the caliphs said from his pulpit: "O servants of God, fear God as much as you are able, and be a people who were called out to, so they awoke, and knew that this world is not for them a permanent abode, so they exchanged it, and prepared for death, for it has overshadowed you. And depart, for the journey has become urgent for you. Indeed, a goal that the moment diminishes and the hour demolishes is worthy of a short duration. Indeed, an absent one whom the two new ones — night and day — hasten is deserving of a swift return. Indeed, an arrival that resolves in triumph or misery is worthy of the best provision. So let him meet his Lord — whoever advises his own soul, presents his repentance, and overcomes his desire — for his term is concealed from him, his hope deceives him, and Satan is entrusted to him, promising him repentance to postpone it, and beautifying disobedience to him to commit it, until his death descends upon him when he is most heedless of it. Indeed, between each of you and Paradise or Hellfire is nothing but death, that it should alight upon him. So what a regret for one who is heedless, or whose life is a proof against him, and whose days lead him to misery. May God make us and you among those whom prosperity does not make insolent, whom disobedience does not hold back from obedience to God, and upon whom regret does not alight after death. Indeed, He is Hearing of supplication, and in His hand is goodness always, and He does what He wills." Some of the exegetes said concerning His saying, the Exalted: {فتنتم أنفسكم} "You tried yourselves" — meaning: with desires and pleasures; {وتربصتم} "and you waited" — meaning: for repentance; {وارتبتم} "and you doubted" — meaning: you were skeptical, until the command of God came — meaning: death; {وغركم بالله الغرور} "and the deluder deluded you concerning God" — meaning: Satan. Al-Hasan said: "Be patient and be firm, for it is but a few days, and you are but a standing caravan — soon one of you will be called, and he will respond without turning back. So move on with the righteous deeds that are in your possession." Ibn Masʿud said: "There is none of you who wakes up except that he is a guest, and what he has is a loan. The guest departs, and the loan is returned." Abu ʿUbaydah al-Baji said: We entered upon al-Hasan in his illness from which he died, and he said: "Welcome to you, and greetings. May God greet you with peace, and settle us and you in the abode of permanence. This is a good outward sign if you are patient, truthful, and God-fearing. So let not your share of this report — may God have mercy on you — be merely that you hear it with this ear and let it out from this ear. For whoever has seen Muhammad, peace be upon him, has seen him going forth early."
57:14.section_title_en: The Haste for Death and Readiness for the Hereafter — Section 1291
57:14.anchors:
- Root: موت (m-w-t)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root denotes cessation of vital faculty; "مات موتة" as a singular event of death.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Death as transition from worldly life to the reckoning; linked to "أجل" (appointed term) and divine decree.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah) = biological death; Metaphorical (Majaz) = "إماتة" of the heart via heedlessness, and "الموت المغير" as the transformative destroyer of states.
- Root: بدر (b-d-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root denotes hastening, rushing to a task; "بادر" implies competing with time.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In Quranic usage, "المبادر" is the soul's urgency toward obedience before the term expires.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal = physical speed; Metaphorical = spiritual vigilance against procrastination (تسويف).
- Root: عرض (ʿ-r-ḍ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root denotes presenting, exposing; "العارية" (loan) as something transiently possessed.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Worldly life as "عارية" (borrowed thing) from God, to be returned at death.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal = loaned object; Metaphorical = the body and lifespan as a trust (أمانة) from the Creator.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب التوكيد بالتكرار (Emphatic Repetition) — Repetition of phrases like "ويحك بادري" and "المبادرة المبادرة" serves as syntactic emphasis (توكيد لفظي) to intensify the exhortation, a structure Sibawayh treats as permissible for rhetorical force without redundancy.
57:14.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Remembrance of Death and Afterlife'

59:9.arabic: في الأرض وتقطعوا أرحامكم وأوصيكم بالأنصار خيرا فإنهم الذين تبوءوا الدار والإيمان من قبلكم أن تحسنوا إليهم ألم يشاطروكم الثمار ألم يوسعوا عليكم في الديار ألم يؤثروكم على أنفسهم وبهم الخصاصة ألا فمن ولي أن يحكم بين رجلين فليقبل من محسنهم وليتجاوز عن مسيئهم ألا ولا تستأثروا عليهم ألا وإني فرط لكم وأنتم لاحقون بي ألا وإن موعدكم الحوض حوضي أعرض مما بين بصرى الشام وصنعاء اليمن يصب فيه ميزاب الكوثر ماؤه أشد بياضا من اللبن وألين من الزبد وأحلى من الشهد من شرب منه لم يظمأ أبدا حصباؤه اللؤلؤ وبطحاؤه المسك من حرمه في الموقف غدا حرم الخير كله أ
59:9.english: And a clarification for those who seek insight — for there was none more honored before God than him, for he was the Intimate Friend of God (khalīl Allāh), His Beloved (ḥabībuh), and His Confidant (najiyyuh); he was His Chosen One (ṣafiyyuh), His Messenger (rasūluh), and His Prophet (nabiyyuh). So consider: did He grant him respite for even an hour at the end of his term? Did He delay him for a single moment after his appointed death had arrived? No indeed — rather, He dispatched to him the noble angels entrusted with seizing the souls of all creation. They rushed upon his pure and generous spirit to extract it, and they wrestled with it to remove it from his pure body — unto mercy, good pleasure, and beautiful bounties; nay, unto a seat of truth in the vicinity of the All-Merciful. Yet despite all that, his distress (karbuh) intensified during the throes of death, his groaning became apparent, his restlessness followed in succession, his yearning rose high, his color changed, his brow sweated, and his left and right sides trembled in contraction and expansion — until those present wept over his fall, and those who witnessed his state sobbed at its severity. So have you seen any station of prophethood repelling what was decreed from him? Did the angel (of death) show regard for his kin and tribe? Did he grant him leniency because he was a supporter of the Truth and a bearer of glad tidings and warnings to creation? Far from it! Rather, he fulfilled what he was commanded, and he followed what he found inscribed on the Preserved Tablet. Such was his state — while he, before God, held the Praiseworthy Station (al-maqām al-maḥmūd) and the Pond of Abundance (al-ḥawḍ al-mawrūd); he is the first from whom the earth will split open, and he is the master of intercession on the Day of Presentation. So the wonder is that we do not take heed from him, nor are we certain of what we shall encounter. Nay, we are captives of lusts and companions of sins and misdeeds. Why then do we not draw a lesson from the death-fall of Muhammad, the Master of the Messengers, the Imam of the God-fearing, and the Beloved of the Lord of the Worlds? Perhaps we imagine that we shall be immortal, or we fancy that despite our evil deeds we are honored before God. Far from it! Far from it! Rather, we are certain that all of us shall enter the Fire — {«وإن منكم إلا واردها كان على ربك حتما مقضيا ثم ننجي الذين اتقوا ونذر الظالمين فيها جثيا»} (And there is none of you but will pass over it [the Fire]; this is with your Lord a decree firmly established. Then We shall save those who feared God and leave the wrongdoers therein on their knees) — and none shall be saved from it except the God-fearing. So we are certain of entering it, but merely deluded about emerging from it. Nay, we have wronged our own souls if, being as we are, we await with mere predominant conjecture. By God, we are not among the God-fearing! And God, Lord of the Worlds, has said: {«وإن منكم إلا واردها كان على ربك حتما مقضيا ثم ننجي الذين اتقوا ونذر الظالمين فيها جثيا»} (And there is none of you but will pass over it; it is with your Lord a decree firmly established. Then We shall save those who feared God and leave the wrongdoers therein on their knees). So let every servant look to himself — whether he is closer to the wrongdoers or to the God-fearing. And look to yourself after you have looked to the conduct of the righteous predecessors (al-salaf al-ṣāliḥīn), for they, despite all that they were granted of success, were among the fearful.
59:9.section_title_en: On the Death-Throes of the Prophet (Peace Be Upon Him) and the Lessons Therein — A Warning to the Negligent
59:9.anchors:
- Root: رسل (r-s-l)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of "sending forth with ease and gentleness"; a messenger (rasūl) is one dispatched with a message.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "أصل الرسل: الانبعاث على التؤدة" — the root denotes measured, deliberate dispatch; the angelic messengers (al-malā'ikah al-mursalūn) are sent on a precise, inexorable errand.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): "أرسل الله في الأمم رسلا" — sending prophets with tidings. Metaphorical (Majaz): "أرسل الله عليهم العذاب" — the inescapable descent of decree; here, the angels are dispatched to seize the Prophet's soul, showing that even the most honored cannot repel the divine command.
- Root: نفس (n-f-s)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The self, soul, or spirit; that which is breathed and animates; also "preciousness" (nufāsah).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The soul (nafs) as the immaterial reality (al-rūḥ) that is seized at death; in "ويحذركم الله نفسه" it denotes the very Essence (al-dhāt), underscoring that the soul's extraction is an act of divine sovereignty.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "نفس سائلة" — a flowing essence. Metaphorical: "دفق نفسه أي دمه" — the pouring out of life; here, the angels "عالجوها ليرحلوها" (wrestled with it to remove it), depicting the soul's reluctant departure from the body.
- Root: عله (ʿ-l-h) — [Note: Root avoided per constraints; substituted with relevant root for "suffering" — see كرب below]
- Root: كرب (k-r-b) — [Derived from context; not in avoidance list]
  * Lisan / Ayn: Grief, distress, agony that grips the chest (karb); the intensification of anguish at death's threshold.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The "sakarat al-mawt" (agonies of death) as a trial for the soul's detachment from the corporeal frame.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical constriction. Metaphorical: the spiritual weight of transition, as the Prophet's "karb" (distress) is magnified despite his rank.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — Used in "إنما أوصي بهذا الأمر قريشا" to restrict leadership to Quraysh, and "فإنما هو عمن أخبره" to limit chains of transmission; also applies to "لا بل" (nay, rather) constructions that negate a prior assumption and affirm a corrective truth, as in "لا بل ظلمنا أنفسنا".
59:9.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'Remembrance of Death and Afterlife'

59:9.arabic: وسلم ثلاث مهلكات شح مطاع وهوى متبع وإعجاب المرء بنفسه (2) وقال تعالى ومن يوق شح نفسه فأولئك هم المفلحون وسيأتي في ربع المهلكات وجه كونه مهلكا وكيفية التقصي منه وإنما تزول صفة البخل بأن تتعود بذل المال فحب الشيء لا ينقطع إلا بقهر النفس على مفارقته حتى يصير ذلك اعتيادا فالزكاة بهذا المعنى طهرة أي تطهر صاحبها عن خبث البخل المهلك وإنما طهارته بقدر بذله وبقدر فرحه بإخراجه واستبشاره بصرفه إلى الله تعالى المعنى الثالث شكر النعمة فإن لله عز وجل على عبده نعمة في نفسه وفي ماله فالعبادات البدنية شكر لنعمة البدن والمالية شكر لنعمة المال وما أخس من ينظر إلى الفقير
59:9.english: A group of the Followers (tābiʿūn) held that there are rights in wealth beyond the zakat — among them al-Nakhaʿī, al-Shaʿbī, ʿAṭāʾ, and Mujāhid. Al-Shaʿbī said, after being asked, "Is there a right in wealth beyond the zakat?": "Yes. Have you not heard His saying — mighty and majestic is He: {«وَآتَى الْمَالَ عَلَىٰ حُبِّهِ ذَوِي الْقُرْبَىٰ»} 'And gives wealth, despite his love for it, to relatives' (2:177)?" They also adduced His saying — mighty and majestic is He: {«وَمِمَّا رَزَقْنَاهُمْ يُنفِقُونَ»} 'And from what We have provided them, they spend' (2:3), and His saying — exalted is He: {«وَأَنفِقُوا مِن مَّا رَزَقْنَاكُم»} 'And spend from what We have provided you' (2:254). They claimed that this is not abrogated by the verse of zakat; rather, it falls within the right of a Muslim upon a Muslim. Its meaning is that it is incumbent upon the affluent one, whenever he finds a needy person, to remove his need — over and above the zakat wealth.
59:9.section_title_en: The Second Division: Those Who Guard Their Wealth Awaiting Seasons of Need — On the Inner Meanings of Zakat (Section 173)
59:9.anchors:
- Root: ف-ق-ر (f-q-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of neediness, poverty; the hollow of the spine (faqār) — that which is structurally weak and dependent.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Poverty (faqr) has four senses: (1) essential neediness before Allah, universal to all creatures; (2) lack of possessions; (3) [the third and fourth senses as elaborated in the full lexicon entry].
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (haqīqah): one who lacks wealth. Metaphorical (majāz): "the poverty of speech" (fuqar al-kalām) — its subtle points, likened to ornaments shaped like vertebrae.
- Root: ص-د-ق (ṣ-d-q)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Truthfulness in speech; giving (ṣadaqah) as the outward verification of inward faith.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Ṣidq (truth) and kidhb (falsehood) are originally in speech — statement of what is, or what will be. By extension, ṣadaqah is that which verifies the truthfulness of one's claim to faith through expenditure.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: truthful speech. Metaphorical: "a horse with true running" (dhū miṣdaq fī al-jary) — that which verifies its excellence through action. Thus charity verifies the giver's sincerity.
- Root: م-ن-ن (m-n-n)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The bestowal of a favor; reproaching another by reminding them of one's gift (al-mann).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): [As elaborated in the full lexicon entry on the heart's self-perception of superiority over the recipient.]
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: a heavy weight; a favor. Metaphorical: the act of counting one's favors over another — a corrosion of the gift's value.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد (Restriction & Specification) — governing the precise scope of obligation (farḍ kifāyah) versus supererogatory merit (faḍl), and the restriction of "rights in wealth" (ḥuqūq fī al-māl) beyond the obligatory zakat.
59:9.topic: Al-Ghazali on purifying the character, moral diseases, and spiritual remedies, from 'Mysteries of Zakat'

59:9.arabic: فقال ولا يجدون في صدورهم حاجة مما أوتوا ويؤثرون على أنفسهم ووجود الحاجة هو الحسد ومن الوفاء أن لا يتغير حاله في التواضع مع أخيه وإن ارتفع شأنه واتسعت ولايته وعظم جاهه فالترفع على الإخوان بما يتجدد من الأحوال لؤم قال الشاعر إن الكرام إذا ما أيسروا ذكروا .
59:9.english: I say: The meaning of loyalty (al-wafāʾ) is steadfastness upon love and its continuation until death — with him, and after death with his children and his friends. For love is sought only for the Hereafter; if it is severed before death, the deed is rendered void and the striving is lost. For this reason, he ﷺ said concerning the seven whom God will shade in His shade: «ورجلان تحابا في الله اجتمعا على ذلك وتفرقا عليه» — "And two men who loved each other for God's sake, gathering upon that and parting upon that."
59:9.section_title_en: The Book of the Revival of the Religious Sciences — Section 427: On the Meaning of Loyalty (al-Wafāʾ) and Its Fruits
59:9.anchors:
- Root: وفي (W-F-Y)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Complete fulfillment, perfect performance of a covenant; to be true to one's bond.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Loyalty (wafāʾ) is the completion of a promise (ʿahd) and its preservation against dissolution; its opposite is betrayal (ghadr) and severance (qaṭīʿah).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "وفى بعهده" — he fulfilled his pact completely. Metaphorical: "وفى الكيل" — he gave full measure; loyalty in love is the full measure of brotherhood, for it is the perfection of the covenant of affection.
- Root: حبب (Ḥ-B-B)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core love, affection, steadfast amity.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): True love (maḥabbah) in the theological sense is the inclination of the heart toward what pleases the Beloved; when it is "for God" (fī Allāh), it is purely spiritual and enduring, not subject to the vicissitudes of worldly aims.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "حبه يحبه حبا" — he loved him. Metaphorical: "تحابا في الله" — they loved each other for God's sake, i.e., their love is bound by the divine bond, not by transient causes.
- Root: نزغ (N-Z-GH)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To incite, to provoke, to instigate discord.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Nazgh" is the insinuation of corruption and the stirring of strife by Satan; it is the subtle injection of rancor between two hearts united in good.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "نزغ بينهم" — he stirred up trouble between them. Metaphorical: Satan's "nazgh" is his secret whispering that ignites the fire of separation after the coolness of affection.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد (Restriction & Specification) — The conditional and restrictive particles (innamā, law, idhā) govern the periodic structure, binding the protasis of loyalty's test to its apodosis of reward or loss.
59:9.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Condemnation of Envy'

59:9.arabic: وقد أثنى الله على الصحابة رضي الله عنهم به فقال ويؤثرون على أنفسهم ولو كان بهم خصاصة وقال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أيما امرئ اشتهى شهوة فرد شهوته وآثر على نفسه غفر له (1) حديث عائشة ما شبع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ثلاثة أيام متواليات ولو شئنا لشبعنا ولكنا كنا نؤثر على أنفسنا أخرجه البيهقي في الشعب بلفظ ولكنه كان يؤثر على نفسه وأول الحديث عند مسلم بلفظ ما شبع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ثلاثة أيام تباعا من خبز بر حتى مضى لسبيله وللشيخين ما شبع آل محمد منذ قدم المدينة ثلاثة ليال تباعا حتى قبض زاد مسلم من طعام ونزل برسول الله ص
59:9.english: And one day he went out intending to visit the Caliph al-Mahdī, and a woman of his household said to him: "What do I get from you if you return with the gift?" He said: "If I am given one hundred thousand, I shall give you one dirham." So he was given sixty thousand, and he gave her four dānaqs (a fraction of a dirham).
59:9.book_title: Condemnation of Miserliness and Love of Wealth
59:9.section_title_en: The Explanation of Altruism (Īthār) and Its Excellence
59:9.anchors:
- Root: أ ث ر (Athara)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of precedence, choosing one thing over another; īthār is the act of preferring another over oneself.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance — īthār is the highest degree of generosity (sakhāʾ), the voluntary preference of another despite one's own need; it is the station of the Companions praised in the Qur'an.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) — giving precedence; metaphorical (majāz) — the soul's inclination away from self-interest toward the welfare of others, even at personal cost.
- Root: س خ و (Sakhuwa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of liberality, open-handedness; sakhaʾ is the disposition of giving freely.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Sakhāʾ is the mean between extravagance and miserliness; its perfection is īthār.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — expending what one does not need; metaphorical — expending what one needs, which is the peak of generosity.
- Root: ب خ ل (Bakhila)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of withholding, miserliness; bukhl is the vice opposed to sakhaʾ.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "البخل: إمساك المقتنيات عما لا يحق حبسها عنه" — withholding possessions from what it is not right to withhold them from; its extreme form is withholding from oneself despite need.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — withholding wealth; metaphorical — the miser's soul withholds even from itself, as in the anecdote of the sick miser who refuses medicine due to its price.
- Root: ض ي ف (Dayf)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of inclining, leaning toward; dayf is the guest who inclines toward a host.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "أصل الضيف الميل" — the guest is one who leans toward you, seeking hospitality; the root carries the sense of inclination and approach.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — one who inclines toward a place or person; metaphorical — the guest as one to whom hospitality is owed, and the host's act of turning toward the guest's need.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — used in the author's framing "إنما السخاء عبارة عن..." to restrict the definition of generosity to its precise scope, and in the hadith "ما شبع آل محمد..." to emphasize the continuous state of the Prophet's household.
59:9.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'Condemnation of Miserliness and Love of Wealth'

59:9.arabic: لهم حرمتهم وأوصيه بالأنصار خيرا الذين تبوءوا الدار والإيمان من قبلهم أن يقبل من محسنهم وأن يعفو عن مسيئهم وأوصيه بأهل الأمصار خيرا فإنهم ردء الإسلام وجباة الأموال وغيظ العدو وأن لا يأخذ منهم إلا فضلهم عن رضا منهم وأوصيه بالأعراب خيرا فإنهم أصل العرب ومادة الإسلام وأن يأخذ من حواشي أموالهم ويرد على فقرائهم وأوصيه بذمة الله عز وجل وذمة رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أن يوفى لهم بعهدهم وأن يقاتل لهم من وراءهم ولا يكلفهم إلا طاقتهم قال فلما قبض خرجنا به فانطلقنا نمشي فسلم عبد الله بن عمر وقال يستأذن عمر بن الخطاب فقالت أدخلوه
59:9.english: [ʿUmar (may Allah be pleased with him) said:] "ʿUmar conveys to you the greeting of peace, and do not say 'Commander of the Faithful,' for today I am not a commander over the believers. Rather, say: 'ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb seeks permission to be buried alongside his two companions.'"
59:9.section_title_en: The Death of ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb (May Allah Be Pleased with Him) — Section 1304
59:9.anchors:
- Root: عمر (ʿ-m-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of "living/peopling" a land; ʿumr = the duration of life that "peoples" the body.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): ʿUmr is the span of bodily vitality, distinct from eternal subsistence (baqāʾ); used here as the proper name ʿUmar.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) usage as a personal name; no metaphorical transfer in this context.
- Root: أذن (ʾ-dh-n)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Listening, then granting permission; istiʾdhān = seeking leave to enter.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Permission as a legal-religious act of authorization (idhn), tied to obedience.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal usage for entry permission; metaphorical extension to "permission to rule" in the succession narrative.
- Root: وصى (w-ṣ-y)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To enjoin, command, or bequeath; waṣiyyah = testamentary instruction.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In theological context, waṣiyyah denotes binding counsel regarding communal duties (rights of others, caliphal obligations).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal for "testament"; metaphorical for "moral charge" passed to the successor.
- Sibawayh Rule: Interposition of the subject between the verb and its object (al-faṣl bayn al-ʿāmil wa al-maʿmūl) — e.g., "قال يقرأ عليك عمر السلام" where the quoted speech is interposed for narrative clarity, permissible when the clause is self-sufficient.
59:9.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'Remembrance of Death and Afterlife'

61:12.arabic: وقال تعالى {ومساكن طيبة في جنات عدن ورضوان من الله أكبر} فقد رفع الله الرضا فوق جنات عدن كما رفع ذكره فوق الصلاة حيث قال {إن الصلاة تنهي عن الفحشاء والمنكر ولذكر الله أكبر} فكما أن مشاهدة المذكور في الصلاة أكبر من الصلاة فرضوان رب الجنة أعلى من الجنة بل هو غاية مطلب سكان الجنان وفي الحديث إن الله تعالى يتجلى للمؤمنين فيقول سلوني فيقولون رضاك (1) فسؤالهم الرضا بعد النظر نهاية التفضيل وأما رضا العبد فسنذكر حقيقته وأما رضوان الله تعالى عن العبد فهو بمعنى آخر يقرب مما ذكرناه في ح
61:12.english: I say: As for the verses [indicating the supremacy of divine pleasure], there is the saying of the Exalted: {رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمْ وَرَضُوا عَنْهُ} [Allah is well-pleased with them and they are well-pleased with Him] {«God is well-pleased with them and they are well-pleased with Him»}. And the Exalted has said: {هَلْ جَزَاءُ الْإِحْسَانِ إِلَّا الْإِحْسَانُ} [Is the reward of goodness aught but goodness?] {«Is the reward of goodness aught but goodness?»}. The ultimate end of goodness is God's pleasure with His servant, and that is the reward for the servant's pleasure in God the Exalted.
61:12.section_title_en: The Reality of Divine Pleasure (Riḍā) and the Servant's Contentment with the Decree — Section 1189
61:12.anchors:
- Root: رضي (raḍiya)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning is "to be content, to approve, to be pleased." Al-Farahidi notes its usage in mutual accord and satisfaction, with the form *tarāḍin* indicating reciprocal consent.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In theological usage, *riḍā* denotes the will's acquiescence to the divine decree without resistance. It is the apex of the servant's station, being the fruit of *maḥabbah* (love) and the key to perpetual vision (*nazar*).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (*ḥaqīqah*) sense is "satisfaction of the heart." Metaphorical (*majāz*) extension applies to God, where *riḍwān* is not an emotional state but a volitional attribute signifying the bestowal of grace and the removal of the veil.
- Root: نظر (naẓara)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "To look, to behold, to consider." In the lexicon, *naẓar* implies directed vision with the eye or the intellect.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Elevated to the highest beatific vision (*ru'yat Allāh*) in the afterlife, the ultimate reward and the supreme object of the inhabitants of Paradise.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical sight. Metaphorical: intellectual contemplation or the unveiled witnessing of the Divine in the Hereafter.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب التفضيل والتشبيه (The Chapter of Preference and Comparison) — Governing the syntactic structures of *afʿala* (elative) forms like *akbar* ("greater") to establish hierarchical supremacy between two entities, as in the verse {وَرِضْوَانٌ مِنَ اللَّهِ أَكْبَرُ}.
61:12.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Remembrance of Death and Afterlife'

67:2.arabic: للموت قبل نزوله وقال السدي الذي خلق الموت والحياة ليبلوكم أيكم احسن عملا أي أيكم أكثرللموت ذكرا وأحسن له استعدادا وأشد منه خوفا وحذرا وقال حذيفة ما من صباح ولا مساء إلا ومنادى ينادى أيها الناس الرحيل الرحيل وتصديق ذلك قوله تعالى إنها لإحدى الكبر نذيرا للبشر لمن شاء منكم أن يتقدم أو يتأخر في الموت وقال سحيم مولى بني تميم جلست إلى عامر بن عبد الله وهو يصلي فأوجز في صلاته ثم أقبل على فقال أرحني بحاجتك فإني أبادر قلت وما تبادر قال ملك الموت رحمك الله قال فقمت عنه وقام إلى صلاته ومر داود الطائي فسأله رجل عن حديث
67:2.english: I say: The hadith was transmitted by al-Tirmidhi and deemed sound (ḥasan) from the narration of Ubayy ibn Kaʿb (5): a hadith that when he (the Prophet, peace be upon him) sensed from his companions heedlessness or negligence, he would call out to them in a raised voice: "Death has come upon you." This hadith was transmitted by Ibn Abi al-Dunya in *Qaṣr al-Amal* from the narration of Zayd al-Sulaymi as a mursal report (6). The hadith of Abu Hurayrah: "I am the warner, death is the transformer, and the Hour is the appointed meeting" — transmitted by Ibn Abi al-Dunya in *Qaṣr al-Amal* and by Abu al-Qasim al-Baghawi with an isnad containing some weakness (7). The hadith of Ibn ʿUmar: "The Messenger of God, peace be upon him, went out while the sun was at the tips of the palm fronds and said: 'What remains of this world is but like what remains of this day of ours, relative to what has passed of it'" — transmitted by Ibn Abi al-Dunya therein with a sound isnad, and al-Tirmidhi transmitted something similar from the narration of Abu Saʿid and deemed it sound (8). The hadith: "The likeness of this world is like a garment torn from its beginning to its end" — transmitted by Ibn Abi al-Dunya therein from the narration of Anas, but it is not authentic (9). Ibn Masʿud, may God be pleased with him, said: The Messenger of God, peace be upon him, recited: {فمن يرد الله أن يهديه يشرح صدره للإسلام} "Whomsoever God wishes to guide, He expands his breast to Islam" {فقال} "Then he said: 'When the light enters the breast, it expands.' It was said: 'O Messenger of God, is there a sign of this that is recognized?' PageV04P459 {قال} He said: 'Yes: withdrawal from the abode of delusion, turning in repentance to the abode of permanence, and preparation for death before its descent.'" Al-Suddi said concerning His saying: {الذي خلق الموت والحياة ليبلوكم أيكم أحسن عملا} "He who created death and life to test you, which of you is best in deed" — meaning: which of you is most mindful of death, best prepared for it, and most fearful and cautious of it. Hudhayfah said: "There is no morning or evening except that a caller calls out: 'O people, the departure! The departure!'" The confirmation of that is His saying, the Exalted: {إنها لإحدى الكبر * نذيرا للبشر * لمن شاء منكم أن يتقدم أو يتأخر} "Indeed, it is one of the greatest calamities, a warning to mankind, for whoever among you wishes to advance or delay" — regarding death. Suhaym, the freed slave of Banu Tamim, said: I sat with ʿAmir ibn ʿAbd Allah while he was praying, and he shortened his prayer, then turned to me and said: "Relieve me of your need, for I am hastening." I said: "What are you hastening for?" He said: "The angel of death, may God have mercy on you." He said: So I rose from him, and he returned to his prayer. Dawud al-Ta'i passed by, and a man asked him about a hadith, so he said: "Leave me, for I am only hastening against the departure of my soul." ʿUmar, may God be pleased with him, said: "Deliberation is good in everything except in deeds of goodness for the Hereafter." Al-Mundhir said: I heard Malik ibn Dinar saying to himself: "Woe to you, hasten before the matter comes upon you. Woe to you, hasten before the matter comes upon you" — repeating that sixty times, while I heard him and he did not see me. Al-Hasan used to say in his exhortation: "Hasten, hasten! For it is but breaths — if they are held back, your deeds by which you draw near to God, the Mighty and Majestic, are cut off. May God have mercy on a man who looked to his own soul and wept over the number of his sins." Then he recited this verse: {إنما نعد لهم عدا} "We only count for them a counting" — meaning the breaths. The end of the counting is the departure of your soul; the end of the counting is the parting from your family; the end of the counting is your entry into your grave. Abu Musa al-Ashʿari strove with intense exertion before his death, and it was said to him: "Would you not hold back, or show yourself some gentleness?" He said: "When horses are released and approach the end of their course, they bring out all that they have. What remains of my term is less than that." He said: He continued in that state until he died. And he used to say to his wife: "Tighten your saddle, for there is no crossing over Hellfire." One of the caliphs said from his pulpit: "O servants of God, fear God as much as you are able, and be a people who were called out to, so they awoke, and knew that this world is not for them a permanent abode, so they exchanged it, and prepared for death, for it has overshadowed you. And depart, for the journey has become urgent for you. Indeed, a goal that the moment diminishes and the hour demolishes is worthy of a short duration. Indeed, an absent one whom the two new ones — night and day — hasten is deserving of a swift return. Indeed, an arrival that resolves in triumph or misery is worthy of the best provision. So let him meet his Lord — whoever advises his own soul, presents his repentance, and overcomes his desire — for his term is concealed from him, his hope deceives him, and Satan is entrusted to him, promising him repentance to postpone it, and beautifying disobedience to him to commit it, until his death descends upon him when he is most heedless of it. Indeed, between each of you and Paradise or Hellfire is nothing but death, that it should alight upon him. So what a regret for one who is heedless, or whose life is a proof against him, and whose days lead him to misery. May God make us and you among those whom prosperity does not make insolent, whom disobedience does not hold back from obedience to God, and upon whom regret does not alight after death. Indeed, He is Hearing of supplication, and in His hand is goodness always, and He does what He wills." Some of the exegetes said concerning His saying, the Exalted: {فتنتم أنفسكم} "You tried yourselves" — meaning: with desires and pleasures; {وتربصتم} "and you waited" — meaning: for repentance; {وارتبتم} "and you doubted" — meaning: you were skeptical, until the command of God came — meaning: death; {وغركم بالله الغرور} "and the deluder deluded you concerning God" — meaning: Satan. Al-Hasan said: "Be patient and be firm, for it is but a few days, and you are but a standing caravan — soon one of you will be called, and he will respond without turning back. So move on with the righteous deeds that are in your possession." Ibn Masʿud said: "There is none of you who wakes up except that he is a guest, and what he has is a loan. The guest departs, and the loan is returned." Abu ʿUbaydah al-Baji said: We entered upon al-Hasan in his illness from which he died, and he said: "Welcome to you, and greetings. May God greet you with peace, and settle us and you in the abode of permanence. This is a good outward sign if you are patient, truthful, and God-fearing. So let not your share of this report — may God have mercy on you — be merely that you hear it with this ear and let it out from this ear. For whoever has seen Muhammad, peace be upon him, has seen him going forth early."
67:2.section_title_en: The Haste for Death and Readiness for the Hereafter — Section 1291
67:2.anchors:
- Root: موت (m-w-t)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root denotes cessation of vital faculty; "مات موتة" as a singular event of death.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Death as transition from worldly life to the reckoning; linked to "أجل" (appointed term) and divine decree.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah) = biological death; Metaphorical (Majaz) = "إماتة" of the heart via heedlessness, and "الموت المغير" as the transformative destroyer of states.
- Root: بدر (b-d-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root denotes hastening, rushing to a task; "بادر" implies competing with time.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In Quranic usage, "المبادر" is the soul's urgency toward obedience before the term expires.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal = physical speed; Metaphorical = spiritual vigilance against procrastination (تسويف).
- Root: عرض (ʿ-r-ḍ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root denotes presenting, exposing; "العارية" (loan) as something transiently possessed.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Worldly life as "عارية" (borrowed thing) from God, to be returned at death.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal = loaned object; Metaphorical = the body and lifespan as a trust (أمانة) from the Creator.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب التوكيد بالتكرار (Emphatic Repetition) — Repetition of phrases like "ويحك بادري" and "المبادرة المبادرة" serves as syntactic emphasis (توكيد لفظي) to intensify the exhortation, a structure Sibawayh treats as permissible for rhetorical force without redundancy.
67:2.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'Remembrance of Death and Afterlife'

67:2.arabic: تعالى نحن قدرنا بينكم الموت وفي قوله تعالى الذي خلق الموت والحياة ولا مناقضة بين قوله تعالى نحن قدرنا بينكم الموت وبين قوله وأنا أكره مساءته ولكن إيضاح الحق في هذا يستدعي تحقيق معنى الإرادة والمحبة والكراهة وبيان حقائقها فإن السابق إلى الإفهام منها أمور تناسب إرادة الخلق ومحبتهم وكراهتهم وهيهات فبين صفات الله تعالى وصفات الخلق من البعد ما بين ذاته العزيز وذاتهم وكما أن ذوات الخلق جوهر وعرض وذات الله مقدس عنه ولا يناسب ما ليس بجوهر وعرض الجوهر والعرض فكذا صفاته لا تناسب صفات الخلق وهذه الحقائق داخلة في علم المكاشفة ووراء
67:2.english: وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم: "لا يلقى الله أحد بذنب أعظم من جهالة أهله."
67:2.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Etiquette of Marriage'

67:25.arabic: على الكافرين غير يسير} وقال تعالى {ويقولون متى هذا الوعد إن كنتم صادقين ما ينظرون إلا صيحة واحدة تأخذهم وهم يخصمون فلا يستطيعون توصية ولا إلى أهلهم يرجعون ونفخ في الصور فإذا هم من الأجداث إلى ربهم ينسلون قالوا يا ويلنا من بعثنا من مرقدنا هذا ما وعد الرحمن وصدق المرسلون} فلو لم يكن بين يدي الموتى إلا هول تلك النفخة لكان ذلك جديرا بأن يتقى فإنها نفخة وصيحة يصعق بها من في السموات والأرض يعنى يموتون بها إلا من شاء الله وهو بعض الملائكة ولذلك قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كيف أنعم وصاحب الصور قد التقم القرن وحنى الجبهة
67:25.english: The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: Allah the Exalted said: "The son of Adam has reviled Me, and he had no right to revile Me; and he has denied Me, and he had no right to deny Me. As for his reviling of Me, it is his saying that I have a son. And as for his denial of Me, it is his saying: 'He will never bring me back as He created me at first.'" {«شتمني ابن آدم وما ينبغي له أن يشتمني وكذبني وما ينبغي له أن يكذبني...»}
67:25.section_title_en: On the Terrors of the Trumpet-Blast and the Awakening for the Resurrection
67:25.anchors:
- Root: نفخ (N-F-Kh)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To blow into a thing, to inflate; the breath of wind entering a vessel or body.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The divine act of breathing spirit into creation {«ونفخت فيه من روحي»}; here, the eschatological blast that annihilates and then revives all beings.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah) usage of blowing into the Trumpet (الصور); metaphorical extension to the "blast of spring" reviving the earth—here applied to the two cosmic blasts of death and resurrection.
- Root: صور (S-W-R)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Form, image, shape; also a horn or trumpet (the instrument of the blast).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The perceptible form of bodies and the intelligible form of souls; here, the Trumpet (الصور) as the instrument of divine command that re-forms and re-shapes creation.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the horn (القرن) held by Israfil; metaphorical: the "inclination" (صورة) of hearts toward terror and anticipation.
- Root: موت (M-W-T)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Death as the cessation of life; the state of the corpse.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Death as the separation of the soul from the body; the "first death" of the blast and the "second death" of the wicked.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical death; metaphorical: the "death" of the heart through heedlessness, and the reviving of dead lands by rain—here, the reviving of bodies by the second blast.
- Root: قبر (Q-B-R)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The grave as the abode of the dead; burial.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The grave as the intermediate state (barzakh) before resurrection; {«حتى زرتم المقابر»} as a metaphor for death.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the grave and its inhabitants; metaphorical: the "raising of the nose" (قبراه) of the proud—contrasted here with the humility of the dead rising from their graves.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — Used to emphasize that true faith is not mere verbal assent but heartfelt conviction, as in "إنما فتور البواطن... لقلة الفهم" (The languor of the inner selves is only due to the lack of understanding).
67:25.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'Remembrance of Death and Afterlife'

68:35.arabic: أن تكون غدا من أمته وأتباعه وما أبعد ظنك وما أبرد طمعك {أفنجعل المسلمين كالمجرمين ما لكم كيف تحكمون} ولنرجع إلى ما كنا فيه وبصدده فقد امتد عنان الكلام إلى غير مقصده ولنذكر الآن من المنامات الكاشفة لأحوال الموتى ما يعظم الانتفاع به إذ ذهبت النبوة وبقيت المبشرات وليس ذلك إلا المنامات
68:35.english: If [the matter of death] were a lasting misery or an enduring felicity, that alone would suffice to consume the entirety of one's lifespan. And the wonder is at our heedlessness while these enormities lie before our very eyes; and more wondrous still is our rejoicing over our wealth, our families, our means, our offspring — nay, even over our limbs, our hearing, and our sight — despite our certain knowledge that we shall part from all of that. But where is the one who breathes the Spirit of Holiness (rūḥ al-quds) into his breast such that he utters what was said to the Master of the Prophets: "Love whom you will, for you shall part from him; live as you will, for you shall die; and do what you will, for you shall be recompensed for it" {«أحبب من أحببت فإنك مفارقه وعش ما شئت فإنك ميت واعمل ما شئت فإنك مجزي به»}? Without doubt, since that was unveiled to him with the eye of certainty (ʿayn al-yaqīn), he was in this world like a wayfarer passing through: he laid no brick upon brick, nor reed upon reed {«لم يضع لبنة على لبنة ولا قصبة على قصبة»}, he left behind no dinar nor dirham {«ولم يخلف دينارا ولا درهما»}, and he took no beloved nor intimate friend. Indeed, he said: "Had I taken an intimate friend (khalīl), I would have taken Abū Bakr as a friend; but your companion is the intimate friend of the Merciful" {«لو كنت متخذا خليلا لاتخذت أبا بكر خليلا ولكن صاحبكم خليل الرحمن»}. Thus he made clear that the intimacy of the Merciful (khullat al-Raḥmān) had permeated the innermost depth of his heart, and that his love had taken firm hold upon the very core of his heart, leaving therein no space for any friend or beloved. And he said to his community: {«إن كنتم تحبون الله فاتبعوني يحببكم الله»} — "If you love God, then follow me, and God will love you." For his community is only those who follow him; and none follows him save one who turns away from this world and turns toward the Hereafter. For he called only to God and the Last Day, and he turned away only from this world and its fleeting appetites. So to the extent that you turn away from this world and turn toward the Hereafter, to that extent you have trodden his path which he trod; and to the extent that you tread his path, to that extent you have followed him; and to the extent that you follow him, to that extent you have become of his community; and to the extent that you turn toward this world, to that extent you have deviated from his path, turned away from following him, and joined those of whom God the Exalted said: {«فأما من طغى وآثر الحياة الدنيا فإن الجحيم هي المأوى»} — "As for him who transgressed and preferred the life of this world, then indeed the Fire is the abode." So if you were to emerge from the hiding-place of delusion and deal justly with yourself — O man, and each of us is that man — you would know that from the moment you rise in the morning until the moment you retire at night, you strive only for fleeting appetites, and you move not nor rest save for something immediate in this world; then you aspire that tomorrow you shall be of his community and his followers. How far is your conjecture, and how cold is your hope! {«أفنجعل المسلمين كالمجرمين ما لكم كيف تحكمون»} — "Shall We make the Muslims like the criminals? What is the matter with you, how do you judge?" Let us now return to what we were upon and what was its purpose, for the reins of discourse have stretched far beyond its intended aim. Let us now mention, from among the dreams that unveil the states of the dead, that whose benefit is great — since prophethood has ceased while the glad tidings (mubashshirāt) remain, and that is none other than dreams.
68:35.section_title_en: The Eighth Book: On What Has Been Revealed of the States of the Dead through Unveiling (Mukāshafah) in Dreams
68:35.anchors:
- Root: سبل (s-b-l)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The path that is easy and trodden; the wayfarer (sābil) is one who traverses it.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-Sabīl is the road of ease; when used absolutely, it designates the path of truth (ṭarīq al-ḥaqq).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: a beaten road. Metaphorical: "asbala al-maṭar" — the rain poured forth as if letting down a veil (sitār).
- Sibawayh Rule: Restriction and Focused Predication (al-ḥaṣr wa al-taqyīd bi-innamā) — governing the exclusive linkage of following the Prophet to turning away from this world.

69:14.arabic: يصدر الناس أشتاتا ليروا أعمالهم يوم تحمل الأرض والجبال فدكتا دكة واحدة فيومئذ وقعت الواقعة وانشقت السماء فهى يومئذ واهية والملك على أرجائها ويحمل عرش ربك فوقهم يومئذ ثمانية يومئذ تعرضون لا تخفى منكم خافية يوم تسير الجبال وترى الأرض بارزة يوم ترج الأرض فيه رجا وتبس الجبال بسا فكانت هباء منبثا يوم يكون الناس كالفراش المبثوث وتكون الجبال كالعهن المنفوش يوم تذهل فيه كل مرضعة عما أرضعت وتضع كل ذات حمل حملها وترى الناس سكارى وما هم بسكارى ولكن عذاب الله شديد يوم تبدل الأرض غير الأرض والسموات وبرزوا لله الواحد القهار يوم تنسف فيه الجبال نسفا فتترك قاعا صفصفا لا ترى فيها عوجا ولا أمتا يوم ترى الجبال تحسبها جامدة وهي تمر مر السحاب يوم تنشق فيه السماء فتكون وردة كالده
69:14.english: So prepare yourself, O wretched one, for this Day of immense magnitude, of prolonged duration, of overwhelming dominion, whose appointed time is near — a Day when you shall see the heaven split asunder, and the stars scattered in its terror, and the shining planets extinguished, and the sun folded up, and the mountains set in motion, and the pregnant camels neglected, and the wild beasts gathered together, and the seas set ablaze, and the souls paired with their bodies, and the Hellfire ignited, and Paradise brought near, and the mountains pulverized, and the earth stretched out — a Day when you shall see the earth shaken with its quaking, and the earth casts forth its burdens. On that Day shall people issue forth in scattered groups to be shown their deeds — a Day when the earth and the mountains are lifted and crushed with a single crushing. Then on that Day the Imminent Event shall come to pass, and the heaven shall split open, for on that Day it shall be frail, and the angels shall be at its edges, and eight shall bear the Throne of your Lord above them on that Day. On that Day you shall be presented — no secret of yours shall remain hidden. A Day when the mountains shall move and you shall see the earth laid bare — a Day when the earth shall be shaken with a violent shaking, and the mountains crumbled to dust, becoming scattered particles — a Day when people shall be like scattered moths, and the mountains like carded wool — a Day when every nursing mother shall forget what she nursed, and every pregnant female shall cast down her burden, and you shall see people drunk, yet they are not drunk, but the chastisement of God is severe — a Day when the earth shall be changed to other than this earth, and the heavens, and they shall appear before God, the One, the All-Compelling — a Day when the mountains shall be blown away as dust, leaving a level, bare plain, wherein you see no crookedness nor curve — a Day when you see the mountains and suppose them solid, yet they pass by like the passing of clouds — a Day when the heaven shall split open and become rosy like molten oil. Then on that Day no human nor jinn shall be asked about his sin. A Day when the disobedient shall be prevented from speech, and shall not be asked about their crimes, but shall be seized by their forelocks and their feet — a Day when every soul shall find what it did of good brought forth present, and what it did of evil, wishing that between it and that evil there were a far distance — a Day when every soul shall know what it has sent ahead, and shall witness what it has forwarded and what it has left behind — a Day when tongues shall be struck mute and the bodily members shall speak — a Day whose mention turned the hair of the Master of the Messengers white, when al-Ṣiddīq (may God be pleased with him) said to him: "I see that you have turned white-haired, O Messenger of God." He said: "Sūrat Hūd and its sisters have made me white-haired" — namely, al-Wāqiʿah, al-Mursalāt, ʿAmma Yatasāʾalūn, and Idhā al-Shamsu Kuwwirat.
69:14.section_title_en: The Names and Attributes of the Day of Resurrection — An Exhortation to the Negligent
69:14.anchors:
- Root: يوم (yawm)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "اليوم: وقت طلوع الشمس إلى غروبها، وقد يعبر به عن مدة من الزمان أي مدة كانت" — the day as a temporal span, extended metaphorically to any epoch or era.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "اليوم يعبر به عن وقت طلوع الشمس إلى غروبها. وقد يعبر به عن مدة من الزمان أي مدة كانت" — theological usage denotes the appointed time of reckoning, magnified by divine attribution (أيام الله).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): a measured solar period. Metaphorical (Majaz): "ذكر في أيام العرب كذا أي في وقائعها" — days as epochal events; thus "the Day" is the supreme epochal event of divine justice.
- Root: نفس (nafs)
  * Lisan / Ayn: النفس: الروح والذات — the self, soul, or very essence.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "النفس: الروح... وقوله: ويحذركم الله نفسه فنفسه: ذاته" — nafs as the innermost reality of a being; in the eschatological context, souls are "paired" (زوجت) with bodies for judgment.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the soul as life-principle. Metaphorical: "دفق نفسه أي دمه" — nafs as the total self, accountable in its entirety.
- Root: ارض (arḍ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: الأرض: الجرم المقابل للسماء — the earth as the corporeal substratum beneath the heavens.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الأرض: الجرم المقابل للسماء... ويعبر بها عن أسفل الشيء" — the earth as the lowest register of creation, subject to total transformation on that Day.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the physical earth. Metaphorical: "تأرض فلان: لزم الأرض" — to cling low; on that Day the earth itself is leveled, flattened, and replaced.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد (Restriction & Focused Predication) — The repeated "يوم" clauses function as temporal restrictors (ẓurūf) binding each predicate to that single, all-encompassing moment; the accumulation of names (أسامي) serves not as mere repetition but as focused predication upon the multifarious realities of a single event.

69:28.arabic: ويقول {ما أغنى عني ماليه هلك عني سلطانيه} وفرش المأمون رمادا واضطجع عليه وكان يقول يا من لا يزول ملكه ارحم من قد زال ملكه وكان المعتصم يقول عند موته لو علمت ان عمري هكذا قصير ما فعلت وكان المنتصر يضطرب على نفسه عند موته فقيل له لا بأس عليك يا أمير المؤمنين فقال ليس إلا هذا لقد ذهبت الدنيا واقبلت الآخرة وقال عمرو بن العاص عند الوفاة وقد نظر إلى صناديق لبنيه من يأخذها بما فيها ليته كان بعرا وقال الحجاج عند موته اللهم أغفر لي فإن الناس يقولون إنك لا تغفر لي فكان عمر بن عبد العزيز تعجبه هذه ا
69:28.english: ...my hand had not been raised to my ear before I seized it. He said: "O God, choose for ʿUmar [the best] in meeting You." And he did not remain but a few days until he died. And it was said: when death came upon him, he wept. So it was said to him: "What makes you weep, O Commander of the Faithful? Rejoice, for God has revived through you the prophetic practices (sunan) and manifested through you justice." He wept, then said: "Will I not be made to stand and be questioned concerning the affair of these creatures? By God, were I to have been perfectly just among them, I would still fear for myself that I could not establish its full proof before God — unless God Himself were to prompt me with that proof. So how [shall I fare] with much of what we have neglected?" And his eyes overflowed, and he did not remain but a little while until he died. And when the time of his death drew near, he said: "Seat me." So they seated him, and he said: "I am the one whom You commanded, and I fell short; and You forbade me, and I disobeyed" — three times — "but there is no god but God." Then he raised his head and strained his gaze, and it was said to him concerning that, and he said: "I see a verdure — they are neither humans nor jinn." Then he was taken [in death], may God have mercy on him.
69:28.section_title_en: Section 1307 — The Deathbed Reflections of the Caliphs and the Verdict of the Righteous
69:28.anchors:
- Root: عمر (ʿ-m-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Prolonged sojourn, cultivation of life, the span of earthly existence.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): ʿUmr as the divinely allotted tenure of the soul in the body — its term (ajal) being the boundary set by God's decree.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the duration of life. Metaphorical: the flourishing of religion through a just ruler, as in "أحيا الله بك سننا" — where revival (iḥyāʾ) is the restoration of prophetic practice after its desuetude.
- Root: ملك (m-l-k)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Possession, dominion, sovereign authority.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Mul'k as the earthly sovereignty that is inherently transient, contrasted with the eternal dominion (malakūt) of God — the latter alone being imperishable.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: royal power. Metaphorical: the soul's governance over the body, which dissolves at death — hence al-Maʾmūn's plea: "Have mercy on him whose sovereignty has departed."
- Root: غني (gh-n-y)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Self-sufficiency, freedom from need, wealth.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Ghinā as the illusory self-sufficiency of the worldly man, unmasked at death when wealth yields no benefit — as in the Quranic verse cited by Hārūn al-Rashīd.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: riches. Metaphorical: the utter destitution (faqr) of the soul before God when all worldly means are stripped away.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The rhetorical pause between the prepositional phrase and its governing verb, as in "يا من لا يزول ملكه ارحم من قد زال ملكه," where the interposed vocative clause heightens the contrast between divine permanence and human evanescence.

70:6.arabic: الساعة وانشق القمر إنهم يرونه بعيدا ونراه قريبا وما يدريك لعل الساعة تكون قريبا ثم يكون أحسن أحوالنا أن نتخذ دراسة هذا القرآن عملا فلا نتدبر معانيه ولا ننظر في كثرة أوصاف هذا اليوم وأساميه ولا نستعد للتخلص من دواهيه فنعوذ بالله من هذه الغفلة إن لم يداركنا الله بواسع رحمته

On that Day shall people issue forth in scattered groups to be shown their deeds — a Day when the earth and the mountains are lifted and crushed with a single crushing. On that Day you shall be presented — no secret of yours shall remain hidden.
