73:12.arabic: وفي رواية أنه صلى الله عليه وسلم قرأ هذا الآية أو قرئ عنده {إن لدينا أنكالا وجحيما وطعاما ذا غصة وعذابا أليما} فصعق (4) وفي رواية أنه صلى الله عليه وسلم قرأ {إن تعذبهم فإنهم عبادك} فبكى (5) وكان صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا مر بآية رحمة دعا واستبشر (6) والاستبشار وجد وقد أثنى الله تعالى على أهل الوجد بالقرآن فقال تعالى {وإذا سمعوا ما أنزل إلى الرسول ترى أعينهم تفيض من الدمع مما عرفوا من الحق} وروي أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كان يصلي ولصدره أزيز كأزيز المرجل (7) وأما ما نقل من الوجد بالقرآن عن الصحابة رضي الله عنهم والتابعين فكثير فمنهم من صعق ومنهم من بكى ومنهم
73:12.english:
**QUAD_ANCHORS:**
- Root: وجد (Wajd)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The root وجد encompasses multiple senses: finding/attaining (إدراك), intense love (الحب الشديد), grief (الحزن), and wealth/sufficiency (الغنى). Al-Khalil notes the range: "الوجد: الحب. والوجد: الحزن. والوجد: الغنى. والوجد: إدراك الشيء"
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الوجد: إدراك الشيء على خلاف ما يطلب" — and in the technical terminology of the Sufis: "ما يصادف القلب من واردات الأحوال" (what the heart encounters of the influxes of spiritual states)
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal sense is finding/attaining; metaphorical extension (majāz) in devotional context: "وجد فلان في العبادة وجدا: إذا أتى بها على وجهها مع حضور القلب"
- Root: طبع (Tabʿ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الطبع: السجية التي جبل عليها الإنسان" — the innate disposition upon which one is created; also "الختم" (sealing)
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الطبع: السجية التي جبل عليها الإنسان" — the original constitution
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Distinguishes "مطبوع" (innate/natural) from "متكلف" (deliberately acquired) — "فلان مطبوع على الكرم، ومتكلف له"
- Root: كلف (Kulfah/Takalluf)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "التكلف: تجشم ما لا يلزمك" — undertaking what is not incumbent upon you with effort and hardship
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "التكلف: تجشم ما ليس من شأنه" — burdening oneself with what is not one's natural concern
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "تكلفت الأمر: تجشمته على مشقة" — deliberate self-imposition of effort
- Root: سمع (Samāʿ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Auditory perception; also what is heard — recitation, song, remembrance
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "السماع عند الصوفية: ما يهيج الوجد من الأصوات الموزونة" — that which stirs ecstatic finding from measured sounds
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "السماع عند القوم: حضور مجلس يهيج الأحوال الشريفة" — attending an assembly that stirs noble spiritual states
- Root: عشق (ʿIshq)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "العشق: فرط الحب" — excessive love; from "العشقة" — a plant that twines around another
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "العشق: فرط الحب، وأصله من عشقة النبات وهي ما التف منه على غيره"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "العشق مجاز في حق الله تعالى" — metaphorical when applied to God
- Root: بكى (Bukāʾ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Weeping, shedding tears
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "البكاء: إجراء الدمع من عين لحزن أو غيره"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "تباكى: تكلف البكاء" — deliberate self-induced weeping
- Root: صعق (Ṣaʿq)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الصعق: الغشي. والصعق: الموت" — swooning/loss of consciousness; death
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الصعق: غشية تعرض من صوت شديد أو هول"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "صعق من هول الأمر: إذا غشي عليه من شدة الخوف"
- Root: خشع (Khushūʿ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الخشوع: الخضوع والتذلل" — humility and submissiveness
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الخشوع: التذلل والخضوع، وقيل: الخشوع في الصوت والبصر، والخضوع في البدن"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "خشعت الأصوات: سكنت. وخشع البصر: انكسر"
- Root: أنس (Uns)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الأنس: نقيض الوحشة" — the opposite of loneliness/estrangement
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الأنس: حضور القلب مع المحبوب" — the heart's presence with the Beloved
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "الأنس بالله: سكون القلب إليه"
- Root: وجل (Wajal)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الوجل: الخوف مع اضطراب القلب" — fear accompanied by cardiac agitation
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الوجل: الخوف مع اضطراب القلب"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "الوجل: أشد من الخوف، فإنه مع اضطراب"
- Root: طمأن (Ṭumaʾnīnah)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الطمأنينة: السكون" — tranquility
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الطمأنينة: سكون القلب بعد اضطراب"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "اطمأن القلب: سكن بعد اضطراب"
- Root: قشعر (Iqshirʿār)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "القشعريرة: تقبض الجلد من الخوف" — contraction of the skin from fear
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الاقشعرار: انقباض الجلد وتقبضه من الخوف"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "اقشعر الجلد من الخوف: إذا تقبض"
- Root: لين (Līn)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "اللين: ضد الخشونة" — softness, opposite of hardness
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "اللين: نقيض الخشونة"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "لان قلبه: إذا سكن وخشع"
- Root: غشي (Ghashy)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الغشي: الإغماء" — loss of consciousness
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الغشية: ما يغشى القلب من شدة الوجد"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "غشي عليه: إذا أغمي عليه من شدة وجد أو خوف"
- Root: زعق (Zaʿq)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الزعق: الصياح الشديد" — violent screaming
  * Al-Raghib (Al-Mufradat): "الزعق: الصياح الشديد"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "زعق: صاح بأعلى صوته"
- Root: أزيز (Azīz)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الأزيز: صوت النار والمرجل" — the sound of fire and boiling pot
  * Al-Raghib (Al-Mufradat): "الأزيز: صوت النار والمرجل ونحوهما"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "أزيز الصدر: صوت يسمع من شدة البكاء والوجد"
- Root: شهق (Shahīq)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الشهيق: رد النفس إلى الداخل بصوت" — drawing breath inward with sound
  * Al-Raghib (Al-Mufradat): "الشهيق: رد النفس إلى الداخل بصوت"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "شهق الرجل: إذا خرجت نفسه بصوت من شدة الوجد"
- Root: حزن (Ḥuzn)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الحزن: ضد السرور" — grief, opposite of joy
  * Al-Raghib (Al-Mufradat): "الحزن: ألم النفس"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "الحزن: ألم النفس، وهو مجاز من حزن الأرض" (metaphorical extension from rough ground)
- Root: شيب (Shayb)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الشيب: بياض الشعر" — whitening of hair
  * Al-Raghib (Al-Mufradat): "الشيب: بياض الشعر"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "شيبتني هود: أي: كبرتني وأحزنتني حتى شاب شعري"
- Root: ذرف (Dharf)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الذرف: سيلان الدمع" — flowing of tears
  * Al-Raghib (Al-Mufradat): "ذرفت العين: سال دمعها"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "ذرفت عينه: إذا سال دمعها من حزن"
- Root: فيض (Fayḍ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الفيض: سيلان الماء" — overflowing of water
  * Al-Raghib (Al-Mufradat): "الفيض: جريان الماء بكثرة"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "فاضت العين بالدمع: سالت. وفاض القلب: امتلأ"
- Root: نقر (Naqr)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "النقر: الضرب على الشيء حتى يصوت" — striking something until it sounds
  * Al-Raghib (Al-Mufradat): "الناقور: الصور" — the Trumpet
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "الناقور: الصور الذي ينفخ فيه إسرافيل"
- Root: رعش (Riʿshah)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الرعدة: الاضطراب" — trembling
  * Al-Raghib (Al-Mufradat): "الارتعداد: الاضطراب"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "ارتعدت فرائصه: اضطربت من شدة الخوف"
- Root: فرص (Farīṣah)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الفريصة: لحمة بين الجنب والكتف ترعد عند الفزع" — the flesh between the side and shoulder blade that trembles at fright
  * Al-Raghib (Al-Mufradat): "الفريصة: لحمة بين الجنب والكتف ترعد عند الفزع"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "ارتعدت فرائصه: من شدة الخوف"
- Root: عما (ʿAmā)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "العمى: ذهاب البصر. والعمى: ذهاب البصيرة" — blindness of sight; blindness of insight
  * Al-Raghib (Al-Mufradat): "العمى: آفة في البصر، وقد يستعار لآفة البصيرة"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "عمي القلب: ذهبت بصيرته"
- Root: أبصر (Abṣara)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "البصر: حاسة الرؤية. والبصيرة: العلم" — sight; insight
  *Al-Raghib (Al-Mufradat): "الإبصار: إدراك البصر، وقد يستعار للبصيرة"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "أبصر الحق: علمه. ومنه: البصيرة"
- Root: كأس (Ka's)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الكأس: القدح إذا كان فيه شراب" — the cup when it contains drink
  * Al-Raghib (Al-Mufradat): "الكأس: الإناء المعروف، وقد يقال لما فيه"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "الكأس: القدح إذا كان فيه شراب"
73:12.topic: Al-Ghazali on the journey of the soul, death, and the Hereafter, from 'Remembrance of Death and Afterlife'

74:8.arabic: فإذا هم قيام ينظرون وقال تعالى {فإذا نقر في الناقور فذلك يومئذ يوم عسير على الكافرين غير يسير} وقال تعالى {ويقولون متى هذا الوعد إن كنتم صادقين ما ينظرون إلا صيحة واحدة تأخذهم وهم يخصمون فلا يستطيعون توصية ولا إلى أهلهم يرجعون ونفخ في الصور فإذا هم من الأجداث إلى ربهم ينسلون قالوا يا ويلنا من بعثنا من مرقدنا هذا ما وعد الرحمن وصدق المرسلون} فلو لم يكن بين يدي الموتى إلا هول تلك النفخة لكان ذلك جديرا بأن يتقى فإنها نفخة وصيحة يصعق بها من في السموات والأرض يعنى يموتون بها إلا من شاء الله وهو بعض الملائكة ولذلك قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ك
74:8.english: The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: Allah the Exalted said: "The son of Adam has reviled Me, and he had no right to revile Me; and he has denied Me, and he had no right to deny Me. As for his reviling of Me, it is his saying that I have a son. And as for his denial of Me, it is his saying: 'He will never bring me back as He created me at first.'" {«شتمني ابن آدم وما ينبغي له أن يشتمني وكذبني وما ينبغي له أن يكذبني...»}
74:8.section_title_en: On the Terrors of the Trumpet-Blast and the Awakening for the Resurrection
74:8.anchors:
- Root: نفخ (N-F-Kh)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To blow into a thing, to inflate; the breath of wind entering a vessel or body.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The divine act of breathing spirit into creation {«ونفخت فيه من روحي»}; here, the eschatological blast that annihilates and then revives all beings.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah) usage of blowing into the Trumpet (الصور); metaphorical extension to the "blast of spring" reviving the earth—here applied to the two cosmic blasts of death and resurrection.
- Root: صور (S-W-R)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Form, image, shape; also a horn or trumpet (the instrument of the blast).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The perceptible form of bodies and the intelligible form of souls; here, the Trumpet (الصور) as the instrument of divine command that re-forms and re-shapes creation.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the horn (القرن) held by Israfil; metaphorical: the "inclination" (صورة) of hearts toward terror and anticipation.
- Root: موت (M-W-T)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Death as the cessation of life; the state of the corpse.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Death as the separation of the soul from the body; the "first death" of the blast and the "second death" of the wicked.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical death; metaphorical: the "death" of the heart through heedlessness, and the reviving of dead lands by rain—here, the reviving of bodies by the second blast.
- Root: قبر (Q-B-R)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The grave as the abode of the dead; burial.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The grave as the intermediate state (barzakh) before resurrection; {«حتى زرتم المقابر»} as a metaphor for death.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the grave and its inhabitants; metaphorical: the "raising of the nose" (قبراه) of the proud—contrasted here with the humility of the dead rising from their graves.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — Used to emphasize that true faith is not mere verbal assent but heartfelt conviction, as in "إنما فتور البواطن... لقلة الفهم" (The languor of the inner selves is only due to the lack of understanding).
74:8.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'Remembrance of Death and Afterlife'

74:8.arabic: وروى أن زرارة بن أوفى لما انتهى إلى قوله تعالى {فإذا نقر في الناقور} خر ميتا وكان إبراهيم النخعي إذا سمع قوله تعالى {إذا السماء انشقت} اضطرب حتى تضطرب أوصاله وقال عبد الله بن واقد رأيت ابن عمر يصلي مغلوبا عليه وحق له أن يحترق قلبه بوعد سيده ووعيده فإنه عبد مذنب ذليل بين يدي جبار قاهر وتكون هذه المعاني بحسب درجات الفهم ويكون الفهم بحسب وفور العلم وصفاء القلب ودرجات ذلك لا تنحصر والصلاة مفتاح القلوب فيها تنكشف أسرار الكلمات فهذا حق القراءة وهو حق الأذكار والتسبيحات أيضا ثم يراعي الهيبة في القراءة فيرتل ولا يسرد فإن ذ
74:8.english: For this reason, he, peace be upon him, said: "Give us rest, O Bilāl" (1) — meaning, give us rest through it (the prayer) and through the call to it, for his delight, peace be upon him, was in it.
74:8.section_title_en: The Inner Works of Prayer: Unveiling the Heart's Secrets in the Ritual Prayer (Asrār al-Ṣalāh)
74:8.anchors:
- Root: قلب (Q-L-B)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To turn a thing over, to revolve it, to divert it from one state to another; the heart as that which is constantly turning and fluctuating.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "قلب الشيء: تصريفه وصرفه عن وجه إلى وجه" — The heart is that which is turned and diverted; its rectitude lies in its orientation towards God, its ruin in its turning towards other than Him.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): "قلب الشيء قلبا: حوله عن وجهه" (to turn a thing from its face). Metaphorical (Majaz): "قلب المعلم الصبيان: صرفهم إلى بيوتهم" (the teacher turned the boys towards their homes) — thus the heart's turning is its direction and intent.
- Root: وجه (W-J-H)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The face; the foremost, noblest, and most apparent part of a thing.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "ولما كان الوجه أول ما يستقبلك، وأشرف ما في ظاهر البدن استعمل في مستقبل كل شيء، وفي أشرفه ومبدئه" — The face is used metaphorically for the essence and the direction of a thing; the "face of the heart" is its intention and aspiration.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "واجهته مواجهة ووجاها" (to face one another). Metaphorical: "هذا وجه الثوب. ووجه القوم، وهؤلاء وجوه البلد" (the face of a garment, the chiefs of a people) — thus the "face" of the heart is its foremost orientation.
- Root: وجل (W-J-L)
  * Lisan / Ayn: A trembling of the heart from fear or awe.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الوجل: استشعار الخوف" — The sensing of fear; the heart's tremor before the majesty of the Divine.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "رجل وجل، وقوم وجال، وقد وجل وجلا" — A man trembling with fear.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — The particle "innamā" restricts and confines the predicate to the subject alone, negating it from all else. This is crucial for understanding "إنما هذه الظواهر تحريكات للبواطن" — the outward acts are *only* movements to stir the inward realities, nothing more.
74:8.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Mysteries of Prayer'

74:35.arabic: وتصديق ذلك قوله تعالى إنها لإحدى الكبر نذيرا للبشر لمن شاء منكم أن يتقدم أو يتأخر في الموت وقال سحيم مولى بني تميم جلست إلى عامر بن عبد الله وهو يصلي فأوجز في صلاته ثم أقبل على فقال أرحني بحاجتك فإني أبادر قلت وما تبادر قال ملك الموت رحمك الله قال فقمت عنه وقام إلى صلاته ومر داود الطائي فسأله رجل عن حديث فقال دعنى إنما أبادر خروج نفسي قال عمر رضي الله عنه التؤدة في كل شيء خير إلا في أعمال الخير للآخرة وقال المنذر سمعت مالك بن دينار يقول لنفسه ويحك بادرى قبل أن يأتيك الأمر ويحك بادرى قبل أن يأتيك الأمر حتى كرر ذلك ستي
74:35.english: I say: The hadith was transmitted by al-Tirmidhi and deemed sound (ḥasan) from the narration of Ubayy ibn Kaʿb (5): a hadith that when he (the Prophet, peace be upon him) sensed from his companions heedlessness or negligence, he would call out to them in a raised voice: "Death has come upon you." This hadith was transmitted by Ibn Abi al-Dunya in *Qaṣr al-Amal* from the narration of Zayd al-Sulaymi as a mursal report (6). The hadith of Abu Hurayrah: "I am the warner, death is the transformer, and the Hour is the appointed meeting" — transmitted by Ibn Abi al-Dunya in *Qaṣr al-Amal* and by Abu al-Qasim al-Baghawi with an isnad containing some weakness (7). The hadith of Ibn ʿUmar: "The Messenger of God, peace be upon him, went out while the sun was at the tips of the palm fronds and said: 'What remains of this world is but like what remains of this day of ours, relative to what has passed of it'" — transmitted by Ibn Abi al-Dunya therein with a sound isnad, and al-Tirmidhi transmitted something similar from the narration of Abu Saʿid and deemed it sound (8). The hadith: "The likeness of this world is like a garment torn from its beginning to its end" — transmitted by Ibn Abi al-Dunya therein from the narration of Anas, but it is not authentic (9). Ibn Masʿud, may God be pleased with him, said: The Messenger of God, peace be upon him, recited: {فمن يرد الله أن يهديه يشرح صدره للإسلام} "Whomsoever God wishes to guide, He expands his breast to Islam" {فقال} "Then he said: 'When the light enters the breast, it expands.' It was said: 'O Messenger of God, is there a sign of this that is recognized?' PageV04P459 {قال} He said: 'Yes: withdrawal from the abode of delusion, turning in repentance to the abode of permanence, and preparation for death before its descent.'" Al-Suddi said concerning His saying: {الذي خلق الموت والحياة ليبلوكم أيكم أحسن عملا} "He who created death and life to test you, which of you is best in deed" — meaning: which of you is most mindful of death, best prepared for it, and most fearful and cautious of it. Hudhayfah said: "There is no morning or evening except that a caller calls out: 'O people, the departure! The departure!'" The confirmation of that is His saying, the Exalted: {إنها لإحدى الكبر * نذيرا للبشر * لمن شاء منكم أن يتقدم أو يتأخر} "Indeed, it is one of the greatest calamities, a warning to mankind, for whoever among you wishes to advance or delay" — regarding death. Suhaym, the freed slave of Banu Tamim, said: I sat with ʿAmir ibn ʿAbd Allah while he was praying, and he shortened his prayer, then turned to me and said: "Relieve me of your need, for I am hastening." I said: "What are you hastening for?" He said: "The angel of death, may God have mercy on you." He said: So I rose from him, and he returned to his prayer. Dawud al-Ta'i passed by, and a man asked him about a hadith, so he said: "Leave me, for I am only hastening against the departure of my soul." ʿUmar, may God be pleased with him, said: "Deliberation is good in everything except in deeds of goodness for the Hereafter." Al-Mundhir said: I heard Malik ibn Dinar saying to himself: "Woe to you, hasten before the matter comes upon you. Woe to you, hasten before the matter comes upon you" — repeating that sixty times, while I heard him and he did not see me. Al-Hasan used to say in his exhortation: "Hasten, hasten! For it is but breaths — if they are held back, your deeds by which you draw near to God, the Mighty and Majestic, are cut off. May God have mercy on a man who looked to his own soul and wept over the number of his sins." Then he recited this verse: {إنما نعد لهم عدا} "We only count for them a counting" — meaning the breaths. The end of the counting is the departure of your soul; the end of the counting is the parting from your family; the end of the counting is your entry into your grave. Abu Musa al-Ashʿari strove with intense exertion before his death, and it was said to him: "Would you not hold back, or show yourself some gentleness?" He said: "When horses are released and approach the end of their course, they bring out all that they have. What remains of my term is less than that." He said: He continued in that state until he died. And he used to say to his wife: "Tighten your saddle, for there is no crossing over Hellfire." One of the caliphs said from his pulpit: "O servants of God, fear God as much as you are able, and be a people who were called out to, so they awoke, and knew that this world is not for them a permanent abode, so they exchanged it, and prepared for death, for it has overshadowed you. And depart, for the journey has become urgent for you. Indeed, a goal that the moment diminishes and the hour demolishes is worthy of a short duration. Indeed, an absent one whom the two new ones — night and day — hasten is deserving of a swift return. Indeed, an arrival that resolves in triumph or misery is worthy of the best provision. So let him meet his Lord — whoever advises his own soul, presents his repentance, and overcomes his desire — for his term is concealed from him, his hope deceives him, and Satan is entrusted to him, promising him repentance to postpone it, and beautifying disobedience to him to commit it, until his death descends upon him when he is most heedless of it. Indeed, between each of you and Paradise or Hellfire is nothing but death, that it should alight upon him. So what a regret for one who is heedless, or whose life is a proof against him, and whose days lead him to misery. May God make us and you among those whom prosperity does not make insolent, whom disobedience does not hold back from obedience to God, and upon whom regret does not alight after death. Indeed, He is Hearing of supplication, and in His hand is goodness always, and He does what He wills." Some of the exegetes said concerning His saying, the Exalted: {فتنتم أنفسكم} "You tried yourselves" — meaning: with desires and pleasures; {وتربصتم} "and you waited" — meaning: for repentance; {وارتبتم} "and you doubted" — meaning: you were skeptical, until the command of God came — meaning: death; {وغركم بالله الغرور} "and the deluder deluded you concerning God" — meaning: Satan. Al-Hasan said: "Be patient and be firm, for it is but a few days, and you are but a standing caravan — soon one of you will be called, and he will respond without turning back. So move on with the righteous deeds that are in your possession." Ibn Masʿud said: "There is none of you who wakes up except that he is a guest, and what he has is a loan. The guest departs, and the loan is returned." Abu ʿUbaydah al-Baji said: We entered upon al-Hasan in his illness from which he died, and he said: "Welcome to you, and greetings. May God greet you with peace, and settle us and you in the abode of permanence. This is a good outward sign if you are patient, truthful, and God-fearing. So let not your share of this report — may God have mercy on you — be merely that you hear it with this ear and let it out from this ear. For whoever has seen Muhammad, peace be upon him, has seen him going forth early."
74:35.section_title_en: The Haste for Death and Readiness for the Hereafter — Section 1291
74:35.anchors:
- Root: موت (m-w-t)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root denotes cessation of vital faculty; "مات موتة" as a singular event of death.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Death as transition from worldly life to the reckoning; linked to "أجل" (appointed term) and divine decree.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah) = biological death; Metaphorical (Majaz) = "إماتة" of the heart via heedlessness, and "الموت المغير" as the transformative destroyer of states.
- Root: بدر (b-d-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root denotes hastening, rushing to a task; "بادر" implies competing with time.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In Quranic usage, "المبادر" is the soul's urgency toward obedience before the term expires.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal = physical speed; Metaphorical = spiritual vigilance against procrastination (تسويف).
- Root: عرض (ʿ-r-ḍ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root denotes presenting, exposing; "العارية" (loan) as something transiently possessed.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Worldly life as "عارية" (borrowed thing) from God, to be returned at death.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal = loaned object; Metaphorical = the body and lifespan as a trust (أمانة) from the Creator.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب التوكيد بالتكرار (Emphatic Repetition) — Repetition of phrases like "ويحك بادري" and "المبادرة المبادرة" serves as syntactic emphasis (توكيد لفظي) to intensify the exhortation, a structure Sibawayh treats as permissible for rhetorical force without redundancy.
74:35.topic: Al-Ghazali on the journey of the soul, death, and the Hereafter, from 'Remembrance of Death and Afterlife'

74:56.arabic: ولا تقولن لشيء إني فاعل ذلك غدا إلا أن يشاء الله ثم لم يقتصر على ذلك فيما لا يشك فيه بل قال تعالى لتدخلن المسجد الحرام إن شاء الله آمنين محلقين رءؤسكم ومقصرين وكان الله سبحانه عالما بأنهم يدخلون لا محالة وأنه شاءه ولكن المقصود تعليمه ذلك فتأدب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في ما كان يخبر عنه معلوما كان أو مشكوكا حتى قال صلى الله عليه وسلم لما دخل المقابر السلام عليكم دار قوم مؤمنين وإنا إن شاء الله بكم لاحقون (1) واللحوق بهم غير مشكوك فيه ولكن مقتضى الأدب ذكر الله تعالى وربط الأمور به وهذه الصيغ
74:56.english: If you say: "What is the meaning of the Salaf's statement, 'I am a believer, if God wills' — given that the exception (istithnā') implies doubt, and doubt in faith is unbelief? Yet they all refrained from giving an unqualified answer affirming faith and were cautious about it."
74:56.section_title_en: On the Meaning of the Salaf's Statement "I am a Believer, If God Wills" — Section 102
74:56.anchors:
- Root: نفس (n-f-s)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The self, the soul; that which is breathed; the innermost reality of a person.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): النفس is used for the rūḥ (spirit), for the dhāt (essence/self), and for the seat of intention and knowledge. When one says "he knows in himself (nafsihi) that he is a believer," it denotes certitude residing in the very core of one's being, not a corporeal faculty.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) usage refers to the soul's reflexive self-awareness; metaphorical (majāz) usage extends to "blood" (dam) or "the eye" (ʿayn) of envy. Here, "in himself" (fī nafsihi) is literal self-knowledge, not mere outward profession.
- Root: وجه (w-j-h)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Face, countenance; the foremost part; a mode, aspect, or direction.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The face is the most noble apparent part of a thing; hence it is used for the "aspect" or "manner" (wajh) of an affair. "Four aspects" (wujūh) means four distinct modes of interpretation or rational grounds.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the face of a person or object. Metaphorical: "the face of the matter" (wajh al-amr) — its most salient and honorable dimension. Here, the "aspects" are hermeneutical angles, not physical parts.
- Root: ايم (a-y-m)
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The unmarried state (aym); one who has no spouse. Not applicable here directly, but the root's semantic field of "being alone/without attachment" contrasts with īmān's root (a-m-n) — security and trust — which is the operative term in this text.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Not directly relevant; the operative root is أمن (a-m-n), meaning security from fear, and by extension, faith (īmān) as the state of being secure in God's truth.
- Root: كان (k-w-n)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To be, to exist; the copula of predication.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Kāna denotes existence and becoming; in theological usage, it grounds the distinction between what is (mawjūd) and what is merely asserted. The question "Are you a believer?" (a-mu'min anta?) uses kāna implicitly to ask about actual, present state — not future contingency.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: existence. Metaphorical: the "being-so" of a predicate. The istithnā' (exception) with "in shā' Allāh" suspends the copula's certainty, shifting from assertive existence to contingent hope.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الاستثناء والتعليق بالمشيئة (The Chapter of Exception and Suspension by the Divine Will) — When an exception clause (istithnā') follows a positive assertion, it grammatically suspends the universality or certainty of the predication. In theological discourse, this suspension may be semantic (doubt) or pragmatic (deference, etiquette, or self-deprecation), and Sibawayh's parsing of conditional suspension (taʿlīq) shows that the apodosis need not be negated — only its absolute, unqualified force is tempered.
74:56.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Remembrance of Death and Afterlife'

75:36.arabic: نطفة فإذا هو خصيم مبين} وقال تعالى {أيحسب الإنسان أن يترك سدى ألم يك نطفة من مني يمنى ثم كان علقة فخلق فسوى فجعل منه الزوجين الذكر والأنثى} ففى خلق الآدمى مع كثرة عجائبه واختلاف تركيب أعضائه أعاجيب تزيد على الأعاجيب فى بعثه وإعادته فكيف ينكر ذلك من قدرة الله تعالى وحكمته من يشاهد ذلك فى صنعته وقدرته فإن كان فى إيمانك ضعف فقو الإيمان بالنظر فى النشأة الأولى فإن الثانية مثلها وأسهل منها وإن كنت قوى الإيمان بها فأشعر قلبك تلك المخاوف والأخطار وأكثر فيها التفكر والاعتبار لتسلب عن قلبك الراحة والقرار فتشتغل بالتشمر للعرض على الجبار وتفكر أولا فيما يقرع سمع سكان القبور من شدة ن
75:36.english: The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: Allah the Exalted said: "The son of Adam has reviled Me, and he had no right to revile Me; and he has denied Me, and he had no right to deny Me. As for his reviling of Me, it is his saying that I have a son. And as for his denial of Me, it is his saying: 'He will never bring me back as He created me at first.'" {«شتمني ابن آدم وما ينبغي له أن يشتمني وكذبني وما ينبغي له أن يكذبني...»}
75:36.section_title_en: On the Terrors of the Trumpet-Blast and the Awakening for the Resurrection
75:36.anchors:
- Root: نفخ (N-F-Kh)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To blow into a thing, to inflate; the breath of wind entering a vessel or body.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The divine act of breathing spirit into creation {«ونفخت فيه من روحي»}; here, the eschatological blast that annihilates and then revives all beings.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah) usage of blowing into the Trumpet (الصور); metaphorical extension to the "blast of spring" reviving the earth—here applied to the two cosmic blasts of death and resurrection.
- Root: صور (S-W-R)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Form, image, shape; also a horn or trumpet (the instrument of the blast).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The perceptible form of bodies and the intelligible form of souls; here, the Trumpet (الصور) as the instrument of divine command that re-forms and re-shapes creation.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the horn (القرن) held by Israfil; metaphorical: the "inclination" (صورة) of hearts toward terror and anticipation.
- Root: موت (M-W-T)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Death as the cessation of life; the state of the corpse.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Death as the separation of the soul from the body; the "first death" of the blast and the "second death" of the wicked.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical death; metaphorical: the "death" of the heart through heedlessness, and the reviving of dead lands by rain—here, the reviving of bodies by the second blast.
- Root: قبر (Q-B-R)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The grave as the abode of the dead; burial.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The grave as the intermediate state (barzakh) before resurrection; {«حتى زرتم المقابر»} as a metaphor for death.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the grave and its inhabitants; metaphorical: the "raising of the nose" (قبراه) of the proud—contrasted here with the humility of the dead rising from their graves.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — Used to emphasize that true faith is not mere verbal assent but heartfelt conviction, as in "إنما فتور البواطن... لقلة الفهم" (The languor of the inner selves is only due to the lack of understanding).
75:36.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Remembrance of Death and Afterlife'

77:35.arabic: ويوم لا يجزى والد عن ولده ويوم يفر المرء من أخيه وأمه وأبيه ويوم لا ينطقون ولا يؤذن لهم فيعتذرون يوم لا مرد له من الله يوم هم بارزون ويوم هم على النار يفتنون يوم لا ينفع مال ولا بنون يوم لا ينفع الظالمين معذرتهم ولهم اللعنة ولهم سوء الدار يوم ترد فيه المعاذير وتبلى السرائر وتظهر الضمائر وتكشف الأستار يوم تخشع فيه الأبصار وتسكن الأصوات ويقل فيه الالتفات وتبرز الخفيات وتظهر الخطيئات يوم يساق العباد ومعهم الأشهاد ويشيب الصغير ويسكر الكبير فيومئذ وضعت الموازين ونشرت الدواوين وبرزت الجحيم وأغلى الحميم وزفرت النار ويئس الكفار وسعرت النيران وتغي
77:35.english: So prepare yourself, O wretched one, for this Day of immense magnitude, of prolonged duration, of overwhelming dominion, whose appointed time is near — a Day when you shall see the heaven split asunder, and the stars scattered in its terror, and the shining planets extinguished, and the sun folded up, and the mountains set in motion, and the pregnant camels neglected, and the wild beasts gathered together, and the seas set ablaze, and the souls paired with their bodies, and the Hellfire ignited, and Paradise brought near, and the mountains pulverized, and the earth stretched out — a Day when you shall see the earth shaken with its quaking, and the earth casts forth its burdens. On that Day shall people issue forth in scattered groups to be shown their deeds — a Day when the earth and the mountains are lifted and crushed with a single crushing. Then on that Day the Imminent Event shall come to pass, and the heaven shall split open, for on that Day it shall be frail, and the angels shall be at its edges, and eight shall bear the Throne of your Lord above them on that Day. On that Day you shall be presented — no secret of yours shall remain hidden. A Day when the mountains shall move and you shall see the earth laid bare — a Day when the earth shall be shaken with a violent shaking, and the mountains crumbled to dust, becoming scattered particles — a Day when people shall be like scattered moths, and the mountains like carded wool — a Day when every nursing mother shall forget what she nursed, and every pregnant female shall cast down her burden, and you shall see people drunk, yet they are not drunk, but the chastisement of God is severe — a Day when the earth shall be changed to other than this earth, and the heavens, and they shall appear before God, the One, the All-Compelling — a Day when the mountains shall be blown away as dust, leaving a level, bare plain, wherein you see no crookedness nor curve — a Day when you see the mountains and suppose them solid, yet they pass by like the passing of clouds — a Day when the heaven shall split open and become rosy like molten oil. Then on that Day no human nor jinn shall be asked about his sin. A Day when the disobedient shall be prevented from speech, and shall not be asked about their crimes, but shall be seized by their forelocks and their feet — a Day when every soul shall find what it did of good brought forth present, and what it did of evil, wishing that between it and that evil there were a far distance — a Day when every soul shall know what it has sent ahead, and shall witness what it has forwarded and what it has left behind — a Day when tongues shall be struck mute and the bodily members shall speak — a Day whose mention turned the hair of the Master of the Messengers white, when al-Ṣiddīq (may God be pleased with him) said to him: "I see that you have turned white-haired, O Messenger of God." He said: "Sūrat Hūd and its sisters have made me white-haired" — namely, al-Wāqiʿah, al-Mursalāt, ʿAmma Yatasāʾalūn, and Idhā al-Shamsu Kuwwirat.
77:35.section_title_en: The Names and Attributes of the Day of Resurrection — An Exhortation to the Negligent
77:35.anchors:
- Root: يوم (yawm)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "اليوم: وقت طلوع الشمس إلى غروبها، وقد يعبر به عن مدة من الزمان أي مدة كانت" — the day as a temporal span, extended metaphorically to any epoch or era.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "اليوم يعبر به عن وقت طلوع الشمس إلى غروبها. وقد يعبر به عن مدة من الزمان أي مدة كانت" — theological usage denotes the appointed time of reckoning, magnified by divine attribution (أيام الله).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): a measured solar period. Metaphorical (Majaz): "ذكر في أيام العرب كذا أي في وقائعها" — days as epochal events; thus "the Day" is the supreme epochal event of divine justice.
- Root: نفس (nafs)
  * Lisan / Ayn: النفس: الروح والذات — the self, soul, or very essence.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "النفس: الروح... وقوله: ويحذركم الله نفسه فنفسه: ذاته" — nafs as the innermost reality of a being; in the eschatological context, souls are "paired" (زوجت) with bodies for judgment.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the soul as life-principle. Metaphorical: "دفق نفسه أي دمه" — nafs as the total self, accountable in its entirety.
- Root: ارض (arḍ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: الأرض: الجرم المقابل للسماء — the earth as the corporeal substratum beneath the heavens.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الأرض: الجرم المقابل للسماء... ويعبر بها عن أسفل الشيء" — the earth as the lowest register of creation, subject to total transformation on that Day.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the physical earth. Metaphorical: "تأرض فلان: لزم الأرض" — to cling low; on that Day the earth itself is leveled, flattened, and replaced.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد (Restriction & Focused Predication) — The repeated "يوم" clauses function as temporal restrictors (ẓurūf) binding each predicate to that single, all-encompassing moment; the accumulation of names (أسامي) serves not as mere repetition but as focused predication upon the multifarious realities of a single event.
77:35.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Remembrance of Death and Afterlife'

77:35.arabic: تلميذ الصالح المري فافتتح يقرأ وكان حسن الصوت فقرأ هذه الآية عليه {هذا يوم لا ينطقون ولا يؤذن لهم فيعتذرون} فرأيت الشافعي رحمه الله وقد تغير لونه واقشعر جلده واضطرب اضطرابا شديدا وخر مغشيا عليه فلما أفاق جعل يقول أعوذ بك من مقام الكاذبين وإعراض الغافلين اللهم لك خضعت قلوب العارفين وذلت لك رقاب المشتاقين إلهي هب لي جودك وجللني بسترك واعف عن تقصيري بكرم وجهك قال ثم مشى وانصرفنا فلما دخلت بغداد وكان هو بالعراق فقعدت على الشط أتوضأ للصلاة إذ مر بي رجل فقال لي يا غلام أحسن وضوءك أحسن الله إليك في الدنيا والآخرة فالتفت فإذا أنا برجل يتبعه جماعة فأسرعت في وضوئي وجع
77:35.english: Al-Shāfiʿī, may God be pleased with him, was asked a question and remained silent. It was said to him: "Will you not answer, may God have mercy on you?" He said: "Not until I know whether the excellence lies in my silence or in my answering." Consider then his watchfulness over his tongue — despite its being the member most imperious over the jurists and the most rebellious against restraint and subjugation — and by this it becomes evident that he neither spoke nor remained silent for the sake of attaining excellence or seeking reward.
77:35.section_title_en: The Revival of the Religious Sciences — Section 20: On the Reverence, Asceticism, and God-Consciousness of Imam al-Shāfiʿī
77:35.anchors:
- Root: حرم (ḥ-r-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Sacred inviolability; that which is protected and sanctified
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Reverence owed to that which possesses sacredness (ḥurmah)—here, the sanctity of knowledge and its bearer
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical sanctuary; Metaphorical: the inward sanctity of the scholar's station before God
- Root: زهد (z-h-d)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Abstemiousness; to regard something as little (ḥazr)
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الزاهد في الشيء: الراغب عنه والراضي منه بالزهيد، أي: القليل" — the ascetic is one who turns away from a thing and is content with little of it
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "زهد في الشيء: رغب عنه" (turning away from a thing); Metaphorical: "رجل زهيد: قليل الخير" and "اد زهيد: قليل الأخذ للماء" — a valley that takes little water, i.e., the soul that takes little from the world
- Root: خوف (kh-w-f)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Fear, dread, apprehension of harm
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): God-conscious fear (khashyah) — that fear which arises specifically from knowledge of God's majesty, as in {«إنما يخشى الله من عباده العلماء»}
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: fear of a known threat; Metaphorical: the awe that seizes the heart upon realization of divine grandeur
- Root: سفه (s-f-h)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Foolishness, levity, indecency of speech
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Moral and intellectual lightness; the opposite of ḥilm (forbearance)
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: foolish conduct; Metaphorical: the one who pours filth from his vessel into the vessels of others — the slanderer who seeks to empty his own corruption into pure hearts
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — used in the ḥadīth {«إنما يخشى الله من عباده العلماء»} to restrict true khashyah to the learned, and in al-Shāfiʿī's dictum restricting the claim of loving both world and Creator to falsehood
77:35.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications, prayers, and their spiritual power, from 'Book of Knowledge'

78:40.arabic: كونى ترابا فذلك حين يقول الكافر يا ليتني كنت ترابا فكنت أنت يا مسكين فى يوم ترى صحيفتك خالية عن حسنات طال فيها تعبك فتقول أين حسناتى فيقال نقلت إلى صحيفة خصمائك وترى صحيفتك مشحونة بسيئات طال فى الصبر عنها نصبك واشتد بسبب الكف عنها عناؤك فتقول يا رب هذه سيئات ما قارفتها قط فيقال هذه سيئات القوم الذين اغتبتهم وشتمتهم وقصدتهم بالسوء وظلمتهم فى المبايعة والمجاورة والمخاطبة والمناظرة والمذاكرة والمدارسة وسائر أصناف المعاملة قال ابن مسعود قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إن الشيطان قد يئس أن تعبد الأصنام
78:40.english: Know that none is saved from the peril of the Scale except him who, in this world, called his own soul to account, and weighed therein — by the scale of the Sacred Law — his deeds, his words, his passing thoughts, and his glances, just as ʿUmar — may God be well pleased with him — said: "Call yourselves to account before you are called to account, and weigh yourselves before you are weighed." Indeed, his calling himself to account consists in his repenting, before death, from every act of disobedience with a sincere repentance (tawbah naṣūḥ), and in his making up for what was neglected of his shortcomings regarding the obligatory commands of God — may He be exalted — and in his restoring rights to those he wronged, grain by grain, and in his seeking absolution from everyone whom he harmed by his tongue, his hand, or his evil suspicion harbored in his heart — and this by winning their hearts' contentment — until he dies with no outstanding wrong against him, nor any neglected obligation.
78:40.section_title_en: The Perils of the Scale and the Reckoning of Wrongs Against Others
78:40.anchors:
- Root: وزن (w-z-n)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning is weighing, measuring, and balancing; al-mīzān (the Scale) is the instrument of equitable judgment.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In theological context, al-mīzān is the divine instrument of justice on the Day of Resurrection, weighing deeds to manifest equitable recompense, not a corporeal balance.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) usage denotes physical weighing; metaphorical (majāz) usage extends to moral and spiritual accounting, as in "weighing one's deeds by the scale of the Sacred Law."
- Sibawayh Rule: Conditional and Exceptive Constructions (الشّرط والاستثناء) — governing the protasis-apodosis structure in "whoever's scales are heavy... whoever's scales are light," and the exceptive force in "none is saved... except he who reckons."
78:40.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Remembrance of Death and Afterlife'

79:37.arabic: عدلت عن سبيله ورغبت عن متابعته والتحقت بالذين قال الله تعالى فيهم {فأما من طغى وآثر الحياة الدنيا فإن الجحيم هي المأوى} فلو خرجت من مكمن الغرور وأنصفت نفسك يا رجل وكلنا ذلك الرجل لعلمت أنك من حين تصبح إلى حين تمسي لا تسعى إلا في الحظوظ العاجلة ولا تتحرك ولا تسكن إلا لعاجل الدنيا ثم تطمع أن تكون غدا من أمته وأتباعه وما أبعد ظنك وما أبرد طمعك {أفنجعل المسلمين كالمجرمين ما لكم كيف تحكمون} ولنرجع إلى ما كنا فيه وبصدده فقد امتد عنان الكلام إلى غير مقصده ولنذكر الآن من المنامات الكاشفة لأحوال الموتى ما يعظم الانتفاع به إذ ذهبت النبوة وبقيت المبشرات وليس ذلك إلا الم
79:37.english: If [the matter of death] were a lasting misery or an enduring felicity, that alone would suffice to consume the entirety of one's lifespan. And the wonder is at our heedlessness while these enormities lie before our very eyes; and more wondrous still is our rejoicing over our wealth, our families, our means, our offspring — nay, even over our limbs, our hearing, and our sight — despite our certain knowledge that we shall part from all of that. But where is the one who breathes the Spirit of Holiness (rūḥ al-quds) into his breast such that he utters what was said to the Master of the Prophets: "Love whom you will, for you shall part from him; live as you will, for you shall die; and do what you will, for you shall be recompensed for it" {«أحبب من أحببت فإنك مفارقه وعش ما شئت فإنك ميت واعمل ما شئت فإنك مجزي به»}? Without doubt, since that was unveiled to him with the eye of certainty (ʿayn al-yaqīn), he was in this world like a wayfarer passing through: he laid no brick upon brick, nor reed upon reed {«لم يضع لبنة على لبنة ولا قصبة على قصبة»}, he left behind no dinar nor dirham {«ولم يخلف دينارا ولا درهما»}, and he took no beloved nor intimate friend. Indeed, he said: "Had I taken an intimate friend (khalīl), I would have taken Abū Bakr as a friend; but your companion is the intimate friend of the Merciful" {«لو كنت متخذا خليلا لاتخذت أبا بكر خليلا ولكن صاحبكم خليل الرحمن»}. Thus he made clear that the intimacy of the Merciful (khullat al-Raḥmān) had permeated the innermost depth of his heart, and that his love had taken firm hold upon the very core of his heart, leaving therein no space for any friend or beloved. And he said to his community: {«إن كنتم تحبون الله فاتبعوني يحببكم الله»} — "If you love God, then follow me, and God will love you." For his community is only those who follow him; and none follows him save one who turns away from this world and turns toward the Hereafter. For he called only to God and the Last Day, and he turned away only from this world and its fleeting appetites. So to the extent that you turn away from this world and turn toward the Hereafter, to that extent you have trodden his path which he trod; and to the extent that you tread his path, to that extent you have followed him; and to the extent that you follow him, to that extent you have become of his community; and to the extent that you turn toward this world, to that extent you have deviated from his path, turned away from following him, and joined those of whom God the Exalted said: {«فأما من طغى وآثر الحياة الدنيا فإن الجحيم هي المأوى»} — "As for him who transgressed and preferred the life of this world, then indeed the Fire is the abode." So if you were to emerge from the hiding-place of delusion and deal justly with yourself — O man, and each of us is that man — you would know that from the moment you rise in the morning until the moment you retire at night, you strive only for fleeting appetites, and you move not nor rest save for something immediate in this world; then you aspire that tomorrow you shall be of his community and his followers. How far is your conjecture, and how cold is your hope! {«أفنجعل المسلمين كالمجرمين ما لكم كيف تحكمون»} — "Shall We make the Muslims like the criminals? What is the matter with you, how do you judge?" Let us now return to what we were upon and what was its purpose, for the reins of discourse have stretched far beyond its intended aim. Let us now mention, from among the dreams that unveil the states of the dead, that whose benefit is great — since prophethood has ceased while the glad tidings (mubashshirāt) remain, and that is none other than dreams.
79:37.section_title_en: The Eighth Book: On What Has Been Revealed of the States of the Dead through Unveiling (Mukāshafah) in Dreams
79:37.anchors:
- Root: سبل (s-b-l)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The path that is easy and trodden; the wayfarer (sābil) is one who traverses it.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-Sabīl is the road of ease; when used absolutely, it designates the path of truth (ṭarīq al-ḥaqq).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: a beaten road. Metaphorical: "asbala al-maṭar" — the rain poured forth as if letting down a veil (sitār).
- Sibawayh Rule: Restriction and Focused Predication (al-ḥaṣr wa al-taqyīd bi-innamā) — governing the exclusive linkage of following the Prophet to turning away from this world.
79:37.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Remembrance of Death and Afterlife'

80:34.arabic: ويوم لا يجزى والد عن ولده ويوم يفر المرء من أخيه وأمه وأبيه ويوم لا ينطقون ولا يؤذن لهم فيعتذرون يوم لا مرد له من الله يوم هم بارزون ويوم هم على النار يفتنون يوم لا ينفع مال ولا بنون يوم لا ينفع الظالمين معذرتهم ولهم اللعنة ولهم سوء الدار يوم ترد فيه المعاذير وتبلى السرائر وتظهر الضمائر وتكشف الأستار يوم تخشع فيه الأبصار وتسكن الأصوات ويقل فيه الالتفات وتبرز الخفيات وتظهر الخطيئات يوم يساق العباد ومعهم الأشهاد ويشيب الصغير ويسكر الكبير فيومئذ وضعت الموازين ونشرت الدواوين وبرزت الجحيم وأغلى الحميم وزفرت
80:34.english: So prepare yourself, O wretched one, for this Day of immense magnitude, of prolonged duration, of overwhelming dominion, whose appointed time is near — a Day when you shall see the heaven split asunder, and the stars scattered in its terror, and the shining planets extinguished, and the sun folded up, and the mountains set in motion, and the pregnant camels neglected, and the wild beasts gathered together, and the seas set ablaze, and the souls paired with their bodies, and the Hellfire ignited, and Paradise brought near, and the mountains pulverized, and the earth stretched out — a Day when you shall see the earth shaken with its quaking, and the earth casts forth its burdens. On that Day shall people issue forth in scattered groups to be shown their deeds — a Day when the earth and the mountains are lifted and crushed with a single crushing. Then on that Day the Imminent Event shall come to pass, and the heaven shall split open, for on that Day it shall be frail, and the angels shall be at its edges, and eight shall bear the Throne of your Lord above them on that Day. On that Day you shall be presented — no secret of yours shall remain hidden. A Day when the mountains shall move and you shall see the earth laid bare — a Day when the earth shall be shaken with a violent shaking, and the mountains crumbled to dust, becoming scattered particles — a Day when people shall be like scattered moths, and the mountains like carded wool — a Day when every nursing mother shall forget what she nursed, and every pregnant female shall cast down her burden, and you shall see people drunk, yet they are not drunk, but the chastisement of God is severe — a Day when the earth shall be changed to other than this earth, and the heavens, and they shall appear before God, the One, the All-Compelling — a Day when the mountains shall be blown away as dust, leaving a level, bare plain, wherein you see no crookedness nor curve — a Day when you see the mountains and suppose them solid, yet they pass by like the passing of clouds — a Day when the heaven shall split open and become rosy like molten oil. Then on that Day no human nor jinn shall be asked about his sin. A Day when the disobedient shall be prevented from speech, and shall not be asked about their crimes, but shall be seized by their forelocks and their feet — a Day when every soul shall find what it did of good brought forth present, and what it did of evil, wishing that between it and that evil there were a far distance — a Day when every soul shall know what it has sent ahead, and shall witness what it has forwarded and what it has left behind — a Day when tongues shall be struck mute and the bodily members shall speak — a Day whose mention turned the hair of the Master of the Messengers white, when al-Ṣiddīq (may God be pleased with him) said to him: "I see that you have turned white-haired, O Messenger of God." He said: "Sūrat Hūd and its sisters have made me white-haired" — namely, al-Wāqiʿah, al-Mursalāt, ʿAmma Yatasāʾalūn, and Idhā al-Shamsu Kuwwirat.
80:34.section_title_en: The Names and Attributes of the Day of Resurrection — An Exhortation to the Negligent
80:34.anchors:
- Root: يوم (yawm)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "اليوم: وقت طلوع الشمس إلى غروبها، وقد يعبر به عن مدة من الزمان أي مدة كانت" — the day as a temporal span, extended metaphorically to any epoch or era.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "اليوم يعبر به عن وقت طلوع الشمس إلى غروبها. وقد يعبر به عن مدة من الزمان أي مدة كانت" — theological usage denotes the appointed time of reckoning, magnified by divine attribution (أيام الله).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): a measured solar period. Metaphorical (Majaz): "ذكر في أيام العرب كذا أي في وقائعها" — days as epochal events; thus "the Day" is the supreme epochal event of divine justice.
- Root: نفس (nafs)
  * Lisan / Ayn: النفس: الروح والذات — the self, soul, or very essence.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "النفس: الروح... وقوله: ويحذركم الله نفسه فنفسه: ذاته" — nafs as the innermost reality of a being; in the eschatological context, souls are "paired" (زوجت) with bodies for judgment.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the soul as life-principle. Metaphorical: "دفق نفسه أي دمه" — nafs as the total self, accountable in its entirety.
- Root: ارض (arḍ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: الأرض: الجرم المقابل للسماء — the earth as the corporeal substratum beneath the heavens.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الأرض: الجرم المقابل للسماء... ويعبر بها عن أسفل الشيء" — the earth as the lowest register of creation, subject to total transformation on that Day.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the physical earth. Metaphorical: "تأرض فلان: لزم الأرض" — to cling low; on that Day the earth itself is leveled, flattened, and replaced.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد (Restriction & Focused Predication) — The repeated "يوم" clauses function as temporal restrictors (ẓurūf) binding each predicate to that single, all-encompassing moment; the accumulation of names (أسامي) serves not as mere repetition but as focused predication upon the multifarious realities of a single event.
80:34.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Remembrance of Death and Afterlife'

80:34.arabic: القيامة {يوم يفر المرء من أخيه وأمه وأبيه وصاحبته وبنيه} الآية فأي خير فيمن يفارقك في أشد أحوالك ويهرب منك وكيف تعجب به ولا ينفعك في القبر والقيامة وعلى الصراط إلا عملك وفضل الله تعالى فكيف تتكل على من لا ينفعك وتنسى نعم من يملك نفعك وضرك وموتك وحياتك السابع العجب بالمال كما قال تعالى إخبارا عن صاحب الجنتين إذ قال {أنا أكثر منك مالا وأعز نفرا} ورأى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم رجلا غنيا جلس بجنبه فقير فانقبض عنه وجمع ثيابه فقال صلى الله عليه وسلم أخشيت أن يعدو إليك فقره (1) حديث بينما
80:34.english: If you say: "He, peace and blessings be upon him, said after his words to Fāṭimah and Ṣafiyyah: 'I cannot avail you against God in anything, except that you have a tie of kinship which I will moisten with its moisture'" — a ḥadīth [reported as]: "Do you hope for my intercession, while the Banū ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib do not hope for it?" — narrated by al-Ṭabarānī in al-Awsaṭ from the narration of ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jaʿfar, and in it is Uṣayrim ibn Ḥawshab from Isḥāq ibn Wāṣil, and both are extremely weak — so that indicates that he will single out his relatives for intercession.
80:34.section_title_en: Section 882 — On the Limits of Intercession, the Vices of Pride in Lineage, Numbers, Wealth, and Opinion, and Their Treatment
80:34.anchors:
- Root: شفع (Sh-F-')
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning is pairing or joining; intercession (shafā'ah) is the joining of one's plea to another's cause.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Intercession is the seeking of benefit for another; its acceptance is contingent upon divine permission and good pleasure, as restricted by the Qur'anic qualifiers.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (haqīqah) is the act of making a number even (from watr, odd); metaphorical (majāz) is the mediator's plea before authority.
- Root: عجب (ʿ-J-B)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Astonishment arising from an unknown cause; self-admiration (ʿujb) is a blameworthy state of being pleased with oneself.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "العجب والتعجب: حالة تعرض للإنسان عند الجهل بسبب الشيء" — a state that overtakes a person due to ignorance of the cause; hence, it is impossible regarding God.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: a wondrous thing; metaphorical: the one who performs marvels (taʿjābah). Self-admiration is the root of every error and innovation.
- Root: رأي (R-'-Y)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Opinion, view, or judgment formed through reflection.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Ra'y is the considered opinion that may err or hit the mark; it is blameworthy when it becomes an object of ʿujb (self-admiration).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: sight/vision; metaphorical: intellectual insight. The ḥadīth "إعجاب كل ذي رأي برأيه" (the admiration of every man of opinion for his own view) is cited as a sign of the age's corruption.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد (Restriction and Qualification) — The conditional clauses (in-sharṭ) governing intercession, e.g., {إلا لمن ارتضى} and {إلا بإذنه}, impose necessary restrictions that negate any absolute reliance on intercession.
80:34.topic: Al-Ghazali on the journey of the soul, death, and the Hereafter, from 'Condemnation of Delusion'

81:29.arabic: ولا تقولن لشيء إني فاعل ذلك غدا إلا أن يشاء الله ثم لم يقتصر على ذلك فيما لا يشك فيه بل قال تعالى لتدخلن المسجد الحرام إن شاء الله آمنين محلقين رءؤسكم ومقصرين وكان الله سبحانه عالما بأنهم يدخلون لا محالة وأنه شاءه ولكن المقصود تعليمه ذلك فتأدب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في ما كان يخبر عنه معلوما كان أو مشكوكا حتى قال صلى الله عليه وسلم لما دخل المقابر السلام عليكم دار قوم مؤمنين وإنا إن شاء الله بكم لاحقون (1) واللحوق بهم غير مشكوك فيه ولكن مقتضى الأدب ذكر الله تعالى وربط الأمور به وهذه الصيغ
81:29.english: If you say: "What is the meaning of the Salaf's statement, 'I am a believer, if God wills' — given that the exception (istithnā') implies doubt, and doubt in faith is unbelief? Yet they all refrained from giving an unqualified answer affirming faith and were cautious about it."
81:29.section_title_en: On the Meaning of the Salaf's Statement "I am a Believer, If God Wills" — Section 102
81:29.anchors:
- Root: نفس (n-f-s)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The self, the soul; that which is breathed; the innermost reality of a person.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): النفس is used for the rūḥ (spirit), for the dhāt (essence/self), and for the seat of intention and knowledge. When one says "he knows in himself (nafsihi) that he is a believer," it denotes certitude residing in the very core of one's being, not a corporeal faculty.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) usage refers to the soul's reflexive self-awareness; metaphorical (majāz) usage extends to "blood" (dam) or "the eye" (ʿayn) of envy. Here, "in himself" (fī nafsihi) is literal self-knowledge, not mere outward profession.
- Root: وجه (w-j-h)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Face, countenance; the foremost part; a mode, aspect, or direction.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The face is the most noble apparent part of a thing; hence it is used for the "aspect" or "manner" (wajh) of an affair. "Four aspects" (wujūh) means four distinct modes of interpretation or rational grounds.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the face of a person or object. Metaphorical: "the face of the matter" (wajh al-amr) — its most salient and honorable dimension. Here, the "aspects" are hermeneutical angles, not physical parts.
- Root: ايم (a-y-m)
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The unmarried state (aym); one who has no spouse. Not applicable here directly, but the root's semantic field of "being alone/without attachment" contrasts with īmān's root (a-m-n) — security and trust — which is the operative term in this text.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Not directly relevant; the operative root is أمن (a-m-n), meaning security from fear, and by extension, faith (īmān) as the state of being secure in God's truth.
- Root: كان (k-w-n)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To be, to exist; the copula of predication.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Kāna denotes existence and becoming; in theological usage, it grounds the distinction between what is (mawjūd) and what is merely asserted. The question "Are you a believer?" (a-mu'min anta?) uses kāna implicitly to ask about actual, present state — not future contingency.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: existence. Metaphorical: the "being-so" of a predicate. The istithnā' (exception) with "in shā' Allāh" suspends the copula's certainty, shifting from assertive existence to contingent hope.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الاستثناء والتعليق بالمشيئة (The Chapter of Exception and Suspension by the Divine Will) — When an exception clause (istithnā') follows a positive assertion, it grammatically suspends the universality or certainty of the predication. In theological discourse, this suspension may be semantic (doubt) or pragmatic (deference, etiquette, or self-deprecation), and Sibawayh's parsing of conditional suspension (taʿlīq) shows that the apodosis need not be negated — only its absolute, unqualified force is tempered.
81:29.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Remembrance of Death and Afterlife'

82:6.arabic: فيا أيها الإنسان ما غرك بربك الكريم حيث أغلقت الأبواب وأرخيت الستور واستترت عن الخلائق فقارفت الفجور فماذا تفعل وقد شهدت عليك جوارحك فالويل كل الويل لنا معشر الغافلين يرسل الله لنا سيد المرسلين وينزل عليه الكتاب المبين ويخبرنا بهذه الصفات من نعوت يوم الدين ثم يعرفنا غفلتنا ويقول اقترب الناس حسابهم وهم في غفلة معرضون ما يأتيهم من ذكر من ربهم محدث إلا استمعوه وهم يلعبون لاهية قلوبهم ثم يعرفنا قرب القيامة فيقول اقتربت الساعة وانشق القمر إنهم يرونه بعيدا ونراه قريبا وما يدريك لعل السا
82:6.english: So prepare yourself, O wretched one, for this Day of immense magnitude, of prolonged duration, of overwhelming dominion, whose appointed time is near — a Day when you shall see the heaven split asunder, and the stars scattered in its terror, and the shining planets extinguished, and the sun folded up, and the mountains set in motion, and the pregnant camels neglected, and the wild beasts gathered together, and the seas set ablaze, and the souls paired with their bodies, and the Hellfire ignited, and Paradise brought near, and the mountains pulverized, and the earth stretched out — a Day when you shall see the earth shaken with its quaking, and the earth casts forth its burdens. On that Day shall people issue forth in scattered groups to be shown their deeds — a Day when the earth and the mountains are lifted and crushed with a single crushing. Then on that Day the Imminent Event shall come to pass, and the heaven shall split open, for on that Day it shall be frail, and the angels shall be at its edges, and eight shall bear the Throne of your Lord above them on that Day. On that Day you shall be presented — no secret of yours shall remain hidden. A Day when the mountains shall move and you shall see the earth laid bare — a Day when the earth shall be shaken with a violent shaking, and the mountains crumbled to dust, becoming scattered particles — a Day when people shall be like scattered moths, and the mountains like carded wool — a Day when every nursing mother shall forget what she nursed, and every pregnant female shall cast down her burden, and you shall see people drunk, yet they are not drunk, but the chastisement of God is severe — a Day when the earth shall be changed to other than this earth, and the heavens, and they shall appear before God, the One, the All-Compelling — a Day when the mountains shall be blown away as dust, leaving a level, bare plain, wherein you see no crookedness nor curve — a Day when you see the mountains and suppose them solid, yet they pass by like the passing of clouds — a Day when the heaven shall split open and become rosy like molten oil. Then on that Day no human nor jinn shall be asked about his sin. A Day when the disobedient shall be prevented from speech, and shall not be asked about their crimes, but shall be seized by their forelocks and their feet — a Day when every soul shall find what it did of good brought forth present, and what it did of evil, wishing that between it and that evil there were a far distance — a Day when every soul shall know what it has sent ahead, and shall witness what it has forwarded and what it has left behind — a Day when tongues shall be struck mute and the bodily members shall speak — a Day whose mention turned the hair of the Master of the Messengers white, when al-Ṣiddīq (may God be pleased with him) said to him: "I see that you have turned white-haired, O Messenger of God." He said: "Sūrat Hūd and its sisters have made me white-haired" — namely, al-Wāqiʿah, al-Mursalāt, ʿAmma Yatasāʾalūn, and Idhā al-Shamsu Kuwwirat.
82:6.section_title_en: The Names and Attributes of the Day of Resurrection — An Exhortation to the Negligent
82:6.anchors:
- Root: يوم (yawm)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "اليوم: وقت طلوع الشمس إلى غروبها، وقد يعبر به عن مدة من الزمان أي مدة كانت" — the day as a temporal span, extended metaphorically to any epoch or era.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "اليوم يعبر به عن وقت طلوع الشمس إلى غروبها. وقد يعبر به عن مدة من الزمان أي مدة كانت" — theological usage denotes the appointed time of reckoning, magnified by divine attribution (أيام الله).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): a measured solar period. Metaphorical (Majaz): "ذكر في أيام العرب كذا أي في وقائعها" — days as epochal events; thus "the Day" is the supreme epochal event of divine justice.
- Root: نفس (nafs)
  * Lisan / Ayn: النفس: الروح والذات — the self, soul, or very essence.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "النفس: الروح... وقوله: ويحذركم الله نفسه فنفسه: ذاته" — nafs as the innermost reality of a being; in the eschatological context, souls are "paired" (زوجت) with bodies for judgment.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the soul as life-principle. Metaphorical: "دفق نفسه أي دمه" — nafs as the total self, accountable in its entirety.
- Root: ارض (arḍ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: الأرض: الجرم المقابل للسماء — the earth as the corporeal substratum beneath the heavens.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الأرض: الجرم المقابل للسماء... ويعبر بها عن أسفل الشيء" — the earth as the lowest register of creation, subject to total transformation on that Day.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the physical earth. Metaphorical: "تأرض فلان: لزم الأرض" — to cling low; on that Day the earth itself is leveled, flattened, and replaced.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد (Restriction & Focused Predication) — The repeated "يوم" clauses function as temporal restrictors (ẓurūf) binding each predicate to that single, all-encompassing moment; the accumulation of names (أسامي) serves not as mere repetition but as focused predication upon the multifarious realities of a single event.

82:13.arabic: تعالى حيث قال {إن الأبرار لفي نعيم وإن الفجار لفي جحيم} قال فأين رحمة الله قال قريب من المحسنين ثم قال سليمان يا أبا حازم أي عباد الله أكرم قال أهل البر والتقوى قال فأي الأعمال أفضل قال أداء الفرائض مع اجتناب المحارم قال فأي الكلام أسمع قال قول الحق عند من تخاف وترجوا قال فأي المؤمنين أكيس قال رجل عمل بطاعة الله ودعا الناس إليها قال فأي المؤمنين أخسر قال رجل خطا في هوى أخيه وهو ظالم فباع آخرته بدنيا غيره قال سليمان ما تقول فيما نحن فيه قال أو تعفيني قال لا بد فإنها نصيحة تلقيها إلي قال يا أمير المؤم
82:13.english: ...my need, so I said: "I have only been placed in this station by the swords of the Muhājirūn and the Anṣār, while their sons are dying of hunger. So fear God, and deliver to them their rights." He lowered his head, then raised it and said: "Present your need to us." I said: "ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb—may God be pleased with him—performed the Pilgrimage." He said to his treasurer: "How much did he spend?" He replied: "A little over ten dirhams." And I see here wealth that the necks of camels cannot bear to carry. Then he left. Thus were their manner of entering upon the sultans when they were compelled [to do so], and they would risk their very souls to exact vengeance for God against their oppressors.
82:13.section_title_en: Section 392 — The Conduct of the Religious Scholars with Rulers, and the States that Arise from Mixing with Them
82:13.anchors:
- Root: قول (q-w-l)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Speech, utterance, saying; the act of articulating words with meaning.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological discourse; the content of what is said as binding or informative.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: articulated speech. Metaphorical: a statement of truth or counsel delivered with authority.
- Root: ملك (m-l-k)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Possession, dominion, sovereignty; to have power over something.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The king (malik) is one who disposes by command and prohibition over a people; kingship (mulk) is of two kinds: actual possession/authority and the capacity for it.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: ownership and rule. Metaphorical: mastery over oneself, or the seizure of control over affairs.
- Root: ولي (w-l-y)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Nearness, closeness; guardianship, governance; to be in charge of a matter.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The walī is the one who undertakes a matter; wilāyah is the office of governance or authority over others.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: proximity and friendship. Metaphorical: the assumption of authority (tawallī) over a public office.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Restriction and Focused Predication (باب الحصر والتقييد) — Constructions such as "إنما" and "ما ... إلا" restrict the predicate to a single referent, emphasizing exclusivity in the assertion.

82:19.arabic: لا يغنى مولى عن مولى شيئا ويوم لا تملك نفس لنفس شيئا ويوم يدعون إلى نار جهنم دعا ويوم يسحبون فى النار على وجوههم ويوم تقلب وجوههم فى النار ويوم لا يجزى والد عن ولده ويوم يفر المرء من أخيه وأمه وأبيه ويوم لا ينطقون ولا يؤذن لهم فيعتذرون يوم لا مرد له من الله يوم هم بارزون ويوم هم على النار يفتنون يوم لا ينفع مال ولا بنون يوم لا ينفع الظالمين معذرتهم ولهم اللعنة ولهم سوء الدار يوم ترد فيه المعاذير وتبلى السرائر وتظهر الضمائر وتكشف الأستار يوم تخشع فيه الأبصار وتسكن الأصوات ويقل فيه الالتفات وتبرز
