83:6.arabic: وسمع علي بن الفضيل قارئا يقرأ {يوم يقوم الناس لرب العالمين} فسقط مغشيا عليه فقال الفضيل شكر الله لك ما قد علمه منك وكذلك نقل عن جماعة منهم وكذلك الصوفية فقد كان الشبلي في مسجده ليلة من رمضان وهو يصلي خلف إمام له فقرأ الإمام {ولئن شئنا لنذهبن بالذي أوحينا إليك} فزعق الشبلي زعقة ظن الناس أنه قد طارت روحه وأحمر وجهه وارتعدت فرائصه وكان يقول بمثل هذا يخاطب الأحباب يردد ذلك مرارا وقال الجنيد دخلت على سرى السقطي فرأيت بين يديه رجلا قد غشي عليه فقال لي هذا رجل قد سمع آية من القرآن فغشي عليه فقلت اقرءوا عليه تل
83:6.english:
**QUAD_ANCHORS:**
- Root: وجد (Wajd)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The root وجد encompasses multiple senses: finding/attaining (إدراك), intense love (الحب الشديد), grief (الحزن), and wealth/sufficiency (الغنى). Al-Khalil notes the range: "الوجد: الحب. والوجد: الحزن. والوجد: الغنى. والوجد: إدراك الشيء"
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الوجد: إدراك الشيء على خلاف ما يطلب" — and in the technical terminology of the Sufis: "ما يصادف القلب من واردات الأحوال" (what the heart encounters of the influxes of spiritual states)
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal sense is finding/attaining; metaphorical extension (majāz) in devotional context: "وجد فلان في العبادة وجدا: إذا أتى بها على وجهها مع حضور القلب"
- Root: طبع (Tabʿ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الطبع: السجية التي جبل عليها الإنسان" — the innate disposition upon which one is created; also "الختم" (sealing)
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الطبع: السجية التي جبل عليها الإنسان" — the original constitution
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Distinguishes "مطبوع" (innate/natural) from "متكلف" (deliberately acquired) — "فلان مطبوع على الكرم، ومتكلف له"
- Root: كلف (Kulfah/Takalluf)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "التكلف: تجشم ما لا يلزمك" — undertaking what is not incumbent upon you with effort and hardship
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "التكلف: تجشم ما ليس من شأنه" — burdening oneself with what is not one's natural concern
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "تكلفت الأمر: تجشمته على مشقة" — deliberate self-imposition of effort
- Root: سمع (Samāʿ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Auditory perception; also what is heard — recitation, song, remembrance
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "السماع عند الصوفية: ما يهيج الوجد من الأصوات الموزونة" — that which stirs ecstatic finding from measured sounds
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "السماع عند القوم: حضور مجلس يهيج الأحوال الشريفة" — attending an assembly that stirs noble spiritual states
- Root: عشق (ʿIshq)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "العشق: فرط الحب" — excessive love; from "العشقة" — a plant that twines around another
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "العشق: فرط الحب، وأصله من عشقة النبات وهي ما التف منه على غيره"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "العشق مجاز في حق الله تعالى" — metaphorical when applied to God
- Root: بكى (Bukāʾ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Weeping, shedding tears
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "البكاء: إجراء الدمع من عين لحزن أو غيره"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "تباكى: تكلف البكاء" — deliberate self-induced weeping
- Root: صعق (Ṣaʿq)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الصعق: الغشي. والصعق: الموت" — swooning/loss of consciousness; death
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الصعق: غشية تعرض من صوت شديد أو هول"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "صعق من هول الأمر: إذا غشي عليه من شدة الخوف"
- Root: خشع (Khushūʿ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الخشوع: الخضوع والتذلل" — humility and submissiveness
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الخشوع: التذلل والخضوع، وقيل: الخشوع في الصوت والبصر، والخضوع في البدن"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "خشعت الأصوات: سكنت. وخشع البصر: انكسر"
- Root: أنس (Uns)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الأنس: نقيض الوحشة" — the opposite of loneliness/estrangement
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الأنس: حضور القلب مع المحبوب" — the heart's presence with the Beloved
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "الأنس بالله: سكون القلب إليه"
- Root: وجل (Wajal)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الوجل: الخوف مع اضطراب القلب" — fear accompanied by cardiac agitation
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الوجل: الخوف مع اضطراب القلب"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "الوجل: أشد من الخوف، فإنه مع اضطراب"
- Root: طمأن (Ṭumaʾnīnah)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الطمأنينة: السكون" — tranquility
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الطمأنينة: سكون القلب بعد اضطراب"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "اطمأن القلب: سكن بعد اضطراب"
- Root: قشعر (Iqshirʿār)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "القشعريرة: تقبض الجلد من الخوف" — contraction of the skin from fear
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الاقشعرار: انقباض الجلد وتقبضه من الخوف"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "اقشعر الجلد من الخوف: إذا تقبض"
- Root: لين (Līn)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "اللين: ضد الخشونة" — softness, opposite of hardness
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "اللين: نقيض الخشونة"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "لان قلبه: إذا سكن وخشع"
- Root: غشي (Ghashy)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الغشي: الإغماء" — loss of consciousness
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الغشية: ما يغشى القلب من شدة الوجد"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "غشي عليه: إذا أغمي عليه من شدة وجد أو خوف"
- Root: زعق (Zaʿq)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الزعق: الصياح الشديد" — violent screaming
  * Al-Raghib (Al-Mufradat): "الزعق: الصياح الشديد"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "زعق: صاح بأعلى صوته"
- Root: أزيز (Azīz)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الأزيز: صوت النار والمرجل" — the sound of fire and boiling pot
  * Al-Raghib (Al-Mufradat): "الأزيز: صوت النار والمرجل ونحوهما"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "أزيز الصدر: صوت يسمع من شدة البكاء والوجد"
- Root: شهق (Shahīq)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الشهيق: رد النفس إلى الداخل بصوت" — drawing breath inward with sound
  * Al-Raghib (Al-Mufradat): "الشهيق: رد النفس إلى الداخل بصوت"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "شهق الرجل: إذا خرجت نفسه بصوت من شدة الوجد"
- Root: حزن (Ḥuzn)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الحزن: ضد السرور" — grief, opposite of joy
  * Al-Raghib (Al-Mufradat): "الحزن: ألم النفس"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "الحزن: ألم النفس، وهو مجاز من حزن الأرض" (metaphorical extension from rough ground)
- Root: شيب (Shayb)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الشيب: بياض الشعر" — whitening of hair
  * Al-Raghib (Al-Mufradat): "الشيب: بياض الشعر"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "شيبتني هود: أي: كبرتني وأحزنتني حتى شاب شعري"
- Root: ذرف (Dharf)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الذرف: سيلان الدمع" — flowing of tears
  * Al-Raghib (Al-Mufradat): "ذرفت العين: سال دمعها"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "ذرفت عينه: إذا سال دمعها من حزن"
- Root: فيض (Fayḍ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الفيض: سيلان الماء" — overflowing of water
  * Al-Raghib (Al-Mufradat): "الفيض: جريان الماء بكثرة"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "فاضت العين بالدمع: سالت. وفاض القلب: امتلأ"
- Root: نقر (Naqr)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "النقر: الضرب على الشيء حتى يصوت" — striking something until it sounds
  * Al-Raghib (Al-Mufradat): "الناقور: الصور" — the Trumpet
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "الناقور: الصور الذي ينفخ فيه إسرافيل"
- Root: رعش (Riʿshah)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الرعدة: الاضطراب" — trembling
  * Al-Raghib (Al-Mufradat): "الارتعداد: الاضطراب"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "ارتعدت فرائصه: اضطربت من شدة الخوف"
- Root: فرص (Farīṣah)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الفريصة: لحمة بين الجنب والكتف ترعد عند الفزع" — the flesh between the side and shoulder blade that trembles at fright
  * Al-Raghib (Al-Mufradat): "الفريصة: لحمة بين الجنب والكتف ترعد عند الفزع"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "ارتعدت فرائصه: من شدة الخوف"
- Root: عما (ʿAmā)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "العمى: ذهاب البصر. والعمى: ذهاب البصيرة" — blindness of sight; blindness of insight
  * Al-Raghib (Al-Mufradat): "العمى: آفة في البصر، وقد يستعار لآفة البصيرة"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "عمي القلب: ذهبت بصيرته"
- Root: أبصر (Abṣara)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "البصر: حاسة الرؤية. والبصيرة: العلم" — sight; insight
  *Al-Raghib (Al-Mufradat): "الإبصار: إدراك البصر، وقد يستعار للبصيرة"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "أبصر الحق: علمه. ومنه: البصيرة"
- Root: كأس (Ka's)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الكأس: القدح إذا كان فيه شراب" — the cup when it contains drink
  * Al-Raghib (Al-Mufradat): "الكأس: الإناء المعروف، وقد يقال لما فيه"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "الكأس: القدح إذا كان فيه شراب"
83:6.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Remembrance of Death and Afterlife'

83:6.arabic: فيه روح نسيم قال كعب وقتادة يوم يقوم الناس لرب العلمين قال يقومون مقدار ثلثمائة عام بل قال عبد الله بن عمرو تلا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم هذه الآية ثم قال كيف بكم إنه جمعكم الله كما تجمع النبل فى الكنانة خمسين ألف سنة ولا ينظر إليكم (1) وقال الحسن ما ظنك بيوم قاموا فيه على أقدامهم مقدار خمسين ألف سنة لا يأكلون فيها أكلة ولا يشربون فيها شربة حتى إذا انقطعت أعناقهم عطشا واحترقت أجوافهم جوعا انصرف بهم إلى النار فسقوا من عين آنية قد آن حرها واشتد لفحها فلما بلغ المجهود منهم ما لا طاقة لهم ب
83:6.english: It is a Day on which all creatures stand, their eyes fixed in a stare, their hearts split asunder. They are not spoken to, and no one looks into their affairs. They stand for three hundred years, eating not therein a single eating, drinking not therein a single drink, and finding not therein the breath of any breeze. Ka'b and Qatadah said: "The Day when mankind shall stand before the Lord of the Worlds" {«يوم يقوم الناس لرب العالمين»} (Al-Mutaffifin: 6) — they stand for the measure of three hundred years. Nay — 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr said: The Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, recited this verse, then said: "How will it be with you when Allah gathers you as arrows are gathered in a quiver, for fifty thousand years, and He does not look upon you?" (1) And Al-Hasan said: What is your opinion of a Day on which they stand upon their feet for the measure of fifty thousand years, eating not therein a single eating, drinking not therein a single drink — until, when their necks are severed by thirst and their innards are burnt by hunger, they are turned away to the Fire and given to drink from a boiling spring whose heat has reached its peak and whose scorching blast has grown fierce. Then when the utmost exhaustion reaches them, beyond what they have strength to bear, they speak one to another, seeking one who is honored before his Lord to intercede on their behalf. They cling to no prophet but that he repels them, saying: "Leave me, leave me — my own self, my own self; my own affair has occupied me from the affair of another." And each one excuses himself by the severity of God's wrath, saying: "Today our Lord has become wrathful with a wrath the like of which He has never been wrathful before, nor will He be wrathful with its like after." — until our Prophet, peace be upon him, intercedes for those to whom permission is granted therein; they possess not intercession save for him whom the Merciful has permitted and with whose word He is pleased {«لا يملكون الشفاعة إلا من أذن له الرحمن ورضي له قولا»} (Ta-Ha: 109).
83:6.section_title_en: The Description of the Length of the Day of Resurrection
83:6.anchors:
- Root: يوم (yawm)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning is the period from sunrise to sunset; extended to any span of time, however long.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "اليوم يعبر به عن وقت طلوع الشمس إلى غروبها. وقد يعبر به عن مدة من الزمان أي مدة كانت" — the term denotes any duration whatsoever, as in {«وذكرهم بأيام الله»} (Ibrahim: 5), where "days" are attributed to God as an honorific for His mighty acts.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah) usage refers to the solar day; metaphorical (Majaz) usage extends to "days of the Arabs" meaning their battles and epochal events. Here, the "day" of fifty thousand years is a real duration, not a metaphor.
- Root: نفس (nafs)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The self, soul, or spirit; also breath.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "نفسه: ذاته" — God's "Self" is His very Essence. In the prophetic oath "والذي نفسي بيده" (By Him in Whose hand is my soul), the soul is the living self.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the soul/spirit; metaphorical: "دفق نفسه" (he poured out his soul = his blood). The Prophet's cry "نفسي نفسي" (myself, myself) is literal self-reference — each prophet is absorbed in his own deliverance.
- Root: اكل (akl)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Eating, consuming food.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الأكل: تناول المطعم" — partaking of nourishment; metaphorically extended to fire consuming fuel.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: eating; metaphorical: "أكل مالي وشربه" (he ate my wealth and drank it = he fed it to people). The negation "لا يأكلون فيه أكلة" (they eat not therein a single eating) is literal — total deprivation of food.
- Root: شرب (sharb)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Drinking; also a share or portion.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الشرب: تناول كل مائع" — partaking of any liquid; "الشرب: النصيب منه" — the share of it.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: drinking water, milk, medicine; metaphorical: "أشرب الثوب حمرة" (the garment was saturated with redness). "ولا يشربون فيه شربة" (nor drink therein a single drink) is literal — total deprivation of drink.
- Sibawayh Rule: Interposition of the subject between the conditional and its apodosis; also the construction of "حتى إذا" (until when) marking a temporal sequence where the subordinate clause (انقطعت أعناقهم) is completed before the main clause (انصرف بهم) — a periodic structure requiring careful temporal parsing.
83:6.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'Remembrance of Death and Afterlife'

83:22.arabic: تعالى حيث قال {إن الأبرار لفي نعيم وإن الفجار لفي جحيم} قال فأين رحمة الله قال قريب من المحسنين ثم قال سليمان يا أبا حازم أي عباد الله أكرم قال أهل البر والتقوى قال فأي الأعمال أفضل قال أداء الفرائض مع اجتناب المحارم قال فأي الكلام أسمع قال قول الحق عند من تخاف وترجوا قال فأي المؤمنين أكيس قال رجل عمل بطاعة الله ودعا الناس إليها قال فأي المؤمنين أخسر قال رجل خطا في هوى أخيه وهو ظالم فباع آخرته بدنيا غيره قال سليمان ما تقول فيما نحن فيه قال أو تعفيني قال لا بد فإنها نصيحة تلقيها إ
83:22.english: ...my need, so I said: "I have only been placed in this station by the swords of the Muhājirūn and the Anṣār, while their sons are dying of hunger. So fear God, and deliver to them their rights." He lowered his head, then raised it and said: "Present your need to us." I said: "ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb—may God be pleased with him—performed the Pilgrimage." He said to his treasurer: "How much did he spend?" He replied: "A little over ten dirhams." And I see here wealth that the necks of camels cannot bear to carry. Then he left. Thus were their manner of entering upon the sultans when they were compelled [to do so], and they would risk their very souls to exact vengeance for God against their oppressors.
83:22.section_title_en: Section 392 — The Conduct of the Religious Scholars with Rulers, and the States that Arise from Mixing with Them
83:22.anchors:
- Root: قول (q-w-l)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Speech, utterance, saying; the act of articulating words with meaning.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological discourse; the content of what is said as binding or informative.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: articulated speech. Metaphorical: a statement of truth or counsel delivered with authority.
- Root: ملك (m-l-k)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Possession, dominion, sovereignty; to have power over something.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The king (malik) is one who disposes by command and prohibition over a people; kingship (mulk) is of two kinds: actual possession/authority and the capacity for it.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: ownership and rule. Metaphorical: mastery over oneself, or the seizure of control over affairs.
- Root: ولي (w-l-y)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Nearness, closeness; guardianship, governance; to be in charge of a matter.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The walī is the one who undertakes a matter; wilāyah is the office of governance or authority over others.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: proximity and friendship. Metaphorical: the assumption of authority (tawallī) over a public office.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Restriction and Focused Predication (باب الحصر والتقييد) — Constructions such as "إنما" and "ما ... إلا" restrict the predicate to a single referent, emphasizing exclusivity in the assertion.
83:22.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Remembrance of Death and Afterlife'

83:24.arabic: في أهل الجنة وفي وجوههم نضرة النعيم يسقون من رحيق مختوم جالسين على منابر الياقوت الأحمر في خيام من اللؤلؤ الرطب الأبيض فيها بسط من العبقري الأخضر متكئين على أرائك منصوبة على أطراف أنهار مطردة بالخمر والعسل محفوفة بالغلمان والولدان مزينة بالحور العين من الخيرات الحسان كأنهن الياقوت والمرجان لم يطمثهن إنس قبلهم ولا جان يمشين في درجات الجنان إذا اختالت إحداهن في مشيها حمل أعطافها سبعون ألفا من الولدان عليها من طرائف الحرير الأبيض ما تتحير فيه الأبصار مكللات بالتيجان المرصعة باللؤلؤ والمرجان شكلا
83:24.english: For God Most High has said: {«إن الأبرار لفي نعيم وإن الفجار لفي جحيم»} — "Indeed the righteous are in bliss, and indeed the wicked are in Hellfire." So present yourself before these two verses, and you will have known your resting-place between the two abodes. And God knows best.
83:24.section_title_en: Section 1351 — On the Description of Paradise and the Varieties of Its Bliss
83:24.anchors:
- Root: نعم (n-ʿ-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root denotes softness, ease, and pleasant living; al-Ayn notes it among names of the leopard and tiger, while Lisan records "Nuʿm" as a proper name.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "النعمة: الحالة الحسنة" — niʿmah is the excellent state/condition one inhabits; niʿīm is the experience of delight. The verse {«إن الأبرار لفي نعيم»} designates the abiding state of bliss as a settled condition, not a transient act.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): "في النعمة والنعيم" — dwelling in bounty and bliss. Metaphorical (Majaz): "خفت نعامتهم: ذهبوا" — ostriches departing; here the root's literal sense of softness is transfigured into the theological state of perpetual ease, free from all harshness.
- Root: وجه (w-j-h)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root: face, front, direction; al-Ayn cites "وجه الصواب" — the face/course of correctness.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The face is the noblest part of the outward body, hence used for the essence (al-dhāt) of a thing; in {«ويبقى وجه ربك ذو الجلال والإكرام»} it signifies the Divine Essence. Here "وجه الملك الكريم" — the Face of the Generous King — denotes the Beatific Vision of God's Essence, not a corporeal organ.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical face. Metaphorical: "وجه القوم، وهؤلاء وجوه البلد" — the foremost, noblest of a people; thus the "face" of the King is His most august presence.
- Root: مرج (m-r-j)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root: mixing, confusion, letting loose; al-Ayn: "المرج: الشهد" — also pure honey; Lisan: "مرج أمرهم: اختلط" — their affair became disordered.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "أصل المرج: الخلط" — mixing; "أمر مريج" — a confused affair (Q. 50:5). In this text, the rivers of Paradise "مطردة" (flowing) are not "ممرجة" (mixed/confused) — rather they run pure and distinct, each in its channel.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "مرج الدواب: أرسلها في المرج" — releasing beasts into pasture. Metaphorical: "مرج الله البحرين" — God let the two seas flow freely; "مرجت عهودهم" — covenants became disordered. The contrast sharpens the purity of Paradise's rivers.
- Root: امن (a-m-n)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root: safety, freedom from fear; al-Ayn treats it under the hamzah chapter as the state of security.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "أصل الأمن: طمأنينة النفس وزوال الخوف" — tranquility of the soul and removal of fear. In the Hereafter, "آمنون" is not mere absence of threat but the positive, settled peace of the soul in the Divine presence.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "أمنته وآمننيه" — to grant safety. Metaphorical: "فرس أمين القوى" — a horse whose strength is trustworthy; here the blessed are "آمنون من ريب المنون" — secure from the vicissitudes of fate, a security that is trustworthy and unbreachable.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The rule permits separation between a preposition and its object by an element upon which speech may properly pause, as in "إن به لضرًا" — here "فهم فيما اشتهت أنفسهم خالدون" (in what their souls desire, abiding eternally) interposes the clause of desire between the prepositional phrase and its predicate, heightening rhetorical emphasis on the soul's fulfillment.
83:24.topic: Al-Ghazali on the journey of the soul, death, and the Hereafter, from 'Remembrance of Death and Afterlife'

83:26.arabic: والمنافسة في اللغة مشتقة من النفاسة والذي يدل على إباحة المنافسة قوله تعالى {وفي ذلك فليتنافس المتنافسون} وقال تعالى {سابقوا إلى مغفرة من ربكم} وإنما المسابقة عند خوف الفوت وهو كالعبدين ينسابقان إلى خدمة مولاهما إذ يجزع كل واحد أن يسبقه صاحبه فيحظى عند مولاه بمنزلة لا يحظى هو بها فكيف وقد صرح رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بذلك فقال لا حسد إلا في اثنتين رجل أتاه الله مالا فسلطه على هلكته في الحق ورجل آتاه الله تعالى علما فهو يعمل به ويعلمه الناس (1) حديث أبي كبشة مثل هذه الأمة مثل أربعة رجل أتاه الله مالا الحديث رواه ابن ماجه والت
83:26.english: The Prophet ﷺ said: «إن المؤمن يغبط والمنافق يحسد» — "The believer aspires emulously, and the hypocrite envies."
83:26.section_title_en: On the Reality of Envy (Ḥasad) and Its Degrees — Section 720
83:26.anchors:
- Root: نعم (n-ʿ-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root meaning of "bounty, benefaction, grace" — that state of goodness and well-being bestowed.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "النعمة: الحالة الحسنة" — bounty is the excellent state/condition; it is the genus term applying to both little and much, as in {«وإن تعدوا نعمة الله لا تحصوها»} [Ibrahim: 34].
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): "جلت نعمة الله ونعماؤه" — bounty as actual bestowed good. Metaphorical (majāz): "خفت نعامتهم" — departure/removal, relevant to the envier's wish for the bounty's removal.
- Root: حسد (ḥ-s-d)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Envy — the desire for removal of another's good.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الحسد: تمني زوال نعمة من مستحق لها" — envy is wishing the removal of bounty from one who deserves it, sometimes accompanied by striving to effect its removal. Cited: «المؤمن يغبط والمنافق يحسد».
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "حسده على نعمة الله" — envying someone for God's bounty. "إن الحسد يأكل الجسد" — envy consumes the body.
- Root: نفس (n-f-s)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The self; also value, preciousness.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): النفس: الروح — the soul/spirit; also الذات (essence/self).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "شيء نفيس ومنفس" — a precious thing. Metaphorical: "دفق نفسه أي دمه" — poured out his self, i.e., his blood. From this root derives المنافسة (emulative competition) — the striving for precious things.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد (Restriction & Specification) — The definition of ḥasad is given as a restricted predication (ḥadd), delimiting its essential meaning: "كراهة النعمة وحب زوالها عن المنعم عليه" — the hatred of bounty and love of its removal from the one upon whom it is bestowed. This is a formal definition (ḥadd), not merely a lexical gloss.
83:26.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'Remembrance of Death and Afterlife'

87:7.arabic: علامات المرض وبهذا يعرف أن القلوب كلها مريضة إلا ما شاء الله إلا أن من الأمراض ما لا يعرفها صاحبها ومرض القلب مما لا يعرفه صاحبه فلذلك يغفل عنه وإن عرفه صعب عليه الصبر على مرارة دوائه فإن دواءه مخالفة الشهوات وهو نزع الروح فإن وجد من نفسه قوة الصبر عليه لم يجد طبيبا حاذقا يعالجه فإن الأطباء هم العلماء وقد استولى عليهم المرض فالطبيب المريض قلما يلتفت إلى علاجه فلهذا صار الداء عضالا والمرض مزمنا واندرس هذا العلم وأنكر بالكلية طب القلوب وأنكر مرضها وأقبل الخلق على حب الدنيا وعلى أعمال ظاهرها عبادات وباطنها
87:7.english: I say: The soul (nafs) that belongs to the human being — that by which he is distinguished from the beasts — for he is not distinguished from them by the power of eating, copulation, sight, or any other such thing. Rather, he is distinguished by the knowledge of things as they truly are. And the Origin of all things, their Existentiator and their Inventor, is God, Mighty and Majestic — He who made them things. So if one knew everything but did not know God, Mighty and Majestic, it would be as though he knew nothing at all. And the sign of knowledge is love: whoever knows God Most High loves Him. And the sign of love is that one does not prefer over Him this world nor any other beloved thing. As God Most High said: {«Say: If your fathers, your sons, your brothers, your spouses, your clans — the wealth you have acquired, commerce whose decline you fear, and dwellings you find pleasing — are more beloved to you than God and His Messenger and striving in His cause, then wait until God brings about His command»} [Q 9:24]. So whoever possesses something more beloved to him than God — his heart is sick. Just as any stomach to which clay has become more beloved than bread and water, or whose appetite for bread and water has fallen away — it is sick. These are the signs of sickness. And by this it is known that all hearts are sick — except what God wills. Yet among sicknesses there are those the sufferer does not recognize; and the sickness of the heart is among those the sufferer does not recognize. For this reason he is heedless of it. And even if he recognized it, patience upon the bitterness of its medicine would be difficult for him — for its medicine is opposing the appetites, and that is the tearing out of the spirit (nafs). And if he found in himself the strength of patience upon it, he would not find a skillful physician to treat him — for the physicians are the scholars, and sickness has overcome them. So the sick physician rarely attends to his own cure. For this reason the malady has become chronic and the sickness chronic. This science has become effaced, and the medicine of hearts is denied entirely, and the sickness of the heart is denied. And creation has turned to the love of this world and to deeds whose outward form is acts of worship but whose inward reality is habit and ostentation. These are the signs of the roots of sicknesses.
87:7.section_title_en: The Soul's Distinction, the Sickness of the Heart, and the Path of Moderation
87:7.anchors:
- Root: نفس (n-f-s)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The self, soul, or spirit; that by which a thing is distinguished in its essential reality
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The soul (nafs) as the principle of rational discrimination and knowledge, distinguishing humans from beasts
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the self or person; Metaphorical: the rational soul as the seat of knowledge and moral responsibility
- Root: مرض (m-r-d)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Departure from the state of health and equilibrium
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Sickness of the heart as a metaphor for moral and spiritual vices — ignorance, cowardice, avarice, hypocrisy
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: bodily illness; Metaphorical: spiritual malady whereby the heart inclines toward what is harmful and away from what is beneficial
- Root: قلب (q-l-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The heart; that which is ever-turning and fluctuating between states
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The heart as the seat of understanding and moral perception; its "turning" (taqlīb) signifies its instability between soundness and sickness
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the physical organ; Metaphorical: the spiritual faculty of cognition and moral discernment
- Root: خلق (kh-l-q)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Measured, proportioned disposition; character and temperament
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Moral character as the inward form (ṣūrah bāṭinah) corresponding to the outward physical form
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: measuring and proportioning; Metaphorical: the ingrained disposition that governs action
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — The use of restrictive constructions to isolate the defining characteristic of the human soul as knowledge of God, not animal appetites
87:7.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Remembrance of Death and Afterlife'

88:4.arabic: لشوبا من حميم ثم إن مرجعهم لإلى الجحيم} وقال تعالى {تصلى نارا حامية تسقى من عين آنية} وقال تعالى {إن لدينا أنكالا وجحيما وطعاما ذا غصة وعذابا أليما} وقال ابن عباس قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لو أن قطرة من الزقوم قطرت في بحار الدنيا أفسدت على أهل الدنيا معايشهم (2) فكيف من يكون طعامه ذلك وقال أنس قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ارغبوا فيما رغبكم الله واحذروا وخافوا ما خوفكم اللهبه من عذابه وعقابه ومن جهنم فإنه لو كانت قطرة من الجنة معكم في دنياكم التي أنتم فيها طيبها لكم ولو كانت قطرة من النار معكم في دنياكم التي أنتم فيها خ
88:4.english: And ʿAlī, may God honor his face, said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: "Seek refuge in God from the Pit of Sorrow, or the Valley of Sorrow." It was said: "O Messenger of God, what is the Valley or Pit of Sorrow?" He said: "A valley in Hell from which Hell itself seeks refuge with God seventy times each day. God, the Exalted, has prepared it for the reciters who show off." (2)
88:4.section_title_en: The Vastness of Hellfire, Its Depths, and the Torments of Its Inhabitants
88:4.anchors:
- Root: و د ي (w-d-y)
  * Lisan / Ayn: A valley; a place where torrents flow. In the lexicon, it denotes a lowland or watercourse between mountains.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Used for the valleys of Hell as places of confinement and passage, each containing further branching ravines (شُعَب), indicating graded descent.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal for earthly valleys; here transferred (majāz) to the topographical reality of Hell, affirming its corporeal vastness.
- Root: ع م ق (ʿ-m-q)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Depth; the far bottom of a well or pit. Al-Farahidi: "العمق: قعر البئر ونحوها."
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Depth as a measure of descent; in the Hereafter, it is unbounded, paralleling the unbounded depth of worldly desire.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal for physical depth; here extended to show the infinite regress of punishment corresponding to infinite craving.
- Root: غ س ق (gh-s-q)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Stinking, foul pus or ichor that flows from the skin of the damned; also intense darkness.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-Ghassāq is the putrid effusion of Hell, a punishment for the senses, specifically for drinking when the damned cry out in thirst.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal for what is loathsome and fetid; in the Quranic context, it is the designated drink of the inhabitants.
- Root: ز ق م (z-q-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To swallow with difficulty; the tree of Zaqqūm, which grows in the depths of Hell.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): A specific tree in Hell whose fruit is like the heads of devils, eaten by the damned to fill their bellies, causing choking and agony.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal for a real tree; its description is sensory, not metaphorical, affirming the physical reality of punishment.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The periodic structure of "في جهنم سبعين ألف واد" allows the prepositional phrase to precede the subject for emphasis, establishing the spatial setting before detailing its contents.
88:4.topic: Al-Ghazali on the journey of the soul, death, and the Hereafter, from 'Remembrance of Death and Afterlife'

88:7.arabic: فيه من العذاب فيستغيثون بالطعام فيغاثون بطعام من ضريع لا يسمن ولا يغني من جوع ويستغيثون بالطعام فيغاثون بطعام ذي غصة فيذكرون كما كانوا يجيزون الغصص في الدنيا بشراب فيستغيثون بشراب فيرفع إليهم الحميم بكلاليب الحديد فإذا دنت من وجوههم شوت وجوههم فإذا دخل الشراب بطونهم قطع ما في بطونهم فيقولون ادعوا خزنة جهنم قال فيدعون خزنة جهنم أن ادعوا ربكم يخفف عنا يوما من العذاب فيقولون أو لم تك تأتيكم رسلكم بالبينات قالوا بلى قالوا فادعوا وما دعاء الكافرين إلا في ضلال قال فيقولون ادعوا مالكا فيدعون فيقولون يا مالك ليقض علينا ربك قال فيجي
88:7.english: And ʿAlī, may God honor his face, said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: "Seek refuge in God from the Pit of Sorrow, or the Valley of Sorrow." It was said: "O Messenger of God, what is the Valley or Pit of Sorrow?" He said: "A valley in Hell from which Hell itself seeks refuge with God seventy times each day. God, the Exalted, has prepared it for the reciters who show off." (2)
