88:14.arabic: أن يذهب بصره ثم يطأطىء رأسه فإذا أزواجه وأكواب موضوعة ونمارق مصفوفة وزرابي مبثوثة ثم اتكأ فقال الحمد لله الذي هدانا لهذا وما كنا لنهتدي
88:14.english: ...of death, hunger, thirst, and all other kinds of calamities, he would be worthy of abandoning this world because of them, and of not preferring it over that whose cutting-off and vexation are of its very necessity. How [could he prefer it], when its people — the kings — are secure, and in varieties of joy are delighting? For them therein is all they desire, and every day they attend at the courtyard of the Throne, and gaze upon the noble Face of Allah. They attain, through that gazing upon Allah, that which makes them not look, along with it, at the rest of the delights of the Gardens, nor do they turn aside. They are perpetually moving among these kinds of blessings, and they are secure from their passing away. Abu Hurayrah said: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "A herald will call out: 'O People of Paradise! Verily for you is that you be healthy and never be ill; and for you is that you live and never die; and for you is that you be young and never grow old; and for you is that you be in bliss and never suffer misery.'" That is the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: {«And they will be called: 'This is the Paradise which you have been made to inherit for what you used to do'»} (7:43).
88:14.section_title_en: The Description of Paradise: Its Gates, Rivers, and the Bliss of Its Inhabitants
88:14.anchors:
- Root: نعم (n-'-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root denotes ease, comfort, and the state of well-being; al-Ayn notes it is also a name for the leopard and panther, indicating swiftness and grace.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "النعمة: الحالة الحسنة" — the goodly state; "النعيم" is the enduring, perfect form of bliss, specifically tied to divine reward in the afterlife.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): "نعم عيشه" — a life of ease and pleasantness. Metaphorical (Majaz): "خفّت نعامتهم" — their prosperity departed, showing the root's extension to transient worldly goods, contrasted here with eternal Paradise.
- Root: اهل (a-h-l)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root signifies those united by kinship, dwelling, or faith; al-Ayn notes it also refers to the prominent part of a beast's back, implying a place of honor and rest.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "أهل الرجل: من يجمعه وإياهم نسب أو دين" — the people of a man are those joined by lineage or religion; "أهل الجنة" (the People of Paradise) are thus bound by the covenant of faith and divine favor.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "رجعوا إلى أهاليهم" — returning to one's family. Here, the "أهل الجنة" are the inhabitants of Paradise, addressed by the herald as a household of eternal blessedness.
- Root: باب (b-a-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root denotes a door or gateway; al-Ayn links it to "إبهام" (obscurity/concealment), as a door hides what lies within until opened.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الباب" is the means of access to a thing; in the Quranic context, the gates of Paradise are the entry points to divine mercy, each corresponding to a specific act of obedience.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical gates of a city or house. Metaphorical: "أبواب الجنة" are the spiritual avenues of righteous deeds (prayer, fasting, charity, jihad) through which the believer enters divine reward.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The rule permits separation between a preposition and its governed noun for rhetorical emphasis, as seen in "لهم فيها كل ما يشتهون" (for them therein is all they desire), where "لهم" is fronted for exclusivity and "فيها" interposed to stress the locus of bliss.
88:14.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications, prayers, and their spiritual power, from 'Remembrance of Death and Afterlife'

93:5.arabic: وفي تفسير قوله تعالى {ولسوف يعطيك ربك فترضى} قال لا يرضى محمد وواحد من أمته في النار وكان أبو جعفر محمد بن علي يقول أنتم أهل العراق تقولون أرجى آية في كتاب الله عز وجل قوله {قل يا عبادي الذين أسرفوا على أنفسهم لا تقنطوا من رحمة الله} الآية ونحن أهل البيت نقول أرجى آية في كتاب الله تعالى قوله تعالى {ولسوف يعطيك ربك فترضى} وأما الأخبار فقد روى أبو موسى عنه صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال أمتي أمة مرحومة لا عذاب عليها في الآخرة عجل الله عقابها في الدنيا الزلازل والفتن فإذا كان يوم القيامة دفع إلى كل رجل من أمتي
93:5.english: So it was said to him: "And what is in it of hope?" He said: "This world, all of it, is little, and a man's provision from it is little, and his religion is little in comparison to his provision. So look at how God Most High sent down in it the longest verse, to guide His servant to the path of caution in preserving his wealth — so how could He not preserve his religion, which has no substitute for him?"
93:5.section_title_en: The Book of Hope (Kitāb al-Rajā') — Section 1033: The Second Art — Surveying the Verses and Reports Concerning Hope
93:5.anchors:
- Root: وجود (w-j-d)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of "finding" and "existence"; here in the sense of what is present and available.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Existence as that which is found and realized; in theological context, the given order of creation.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) sense of "being found"; metaphorical (majāz) extension to the entirety of created things.
- Root: رجا (r-j-w)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To hope, to expect with desire; the opposite of despair (ya's).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Hope as a theological virtue — the heart's expectation of divine mercy, balanced against fear (khawf).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: expectation of a desired outcome; metaphorical: the soul's reliance on divine generosity.
- Root: غفر (gh-f-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To cover, to shield, to pardon; the root implies veiling the fault.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Divine forgiveness as the covering of sins and the effacing of their consequence.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: covering; metaphorical: God's remission of punishment.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — used to emphasize exclusive attributes of divine mercy and forgiveness.
93:5.topic: Al-Ghazali on the journey of the soul, death, and the Hereafter, from 'Remembrance of Death and Afterlife'

98:4.arabic: وهو أحد والآصال التي ذكرها الله تعالى إذ قال ولله يسجد من في السموات والأرض طوعا وكرها وظلالهم بالغدو والآصال وإذا سجد لله عز وجل الجمادات فكيف يجوز أن يغفل العبد العاقل عن أنواع العبادات الورد السادس إذا دخل وقت العصر دخل وقت الورد السادس وهو الذي أقسم الله تعالى به فقال تعالى {والعصر} هذا أحد معنيي الآية وهو المراد بالآصال في أحد التفسيرين وهو العشي المذكور في قوله {وعشيا} وفي قوله {بالعشي والإشراق} وليس في هذا الورد صلاة إلا أربع ركعات بين الأذان والإقامة كما سبق في الظهر ثم يصلي الفرض ويشتغل بالأقسام الأربعة المذكورة
98:4.english: I say: And just as knowledge and remembrance are the nourishment of the heart, which can never be cut off from it, so too the measure of moderation is this; and deficiency from it may lead to the disturbance of the body — except for one who accustoms himself to wakefulness gradually, for he may train himself upon it without disturbance. And this litany (wird) is among the longest of the litanies and the most delightful for the worshippers, and it is one of the "evenings and mornings" (al-āṣāl) which God Most High mentioned when He said: {«ولله يسجد من في السموات والأرض طوعا وكرها وظلالهم بالغدو والآصال»} "And to God prostrates whoever is in the heavens and the earth, willingly or unwillingly, and their shadows, in the mornings and the evenings" (Q. 13:15). And when inanimate objects prostrate to God, Mighty and Majestic, how then can the intelligent servant be heedless of the varieties of worship?
98:4.section_title_en: The Seventh Daily Litany (Al-Wird al-Sābiʿ): The Time of Sunset — The Completion of the Day's Litanies and Self-Accounting
98:4.anchors:
- Root: ورد (warada)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The root denotes arriving at water, seeking it, and drinking from it; also the portion or share of water allotted for drinking at a specific time.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الورود أصله: قصد الماء" — the core meaning is the intentional approach to water; the litany (wird) is the appointed portion of devotional recitation, likened to the daily share of water that a person must take to sustain life.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): the act of arriving at water. Metaphorical (Majaz): "ورد علي كتاب سرني مورده" — a book arrived upon me whose arrival pleased me; likewise, the wird is the arrival of the appointed time for worship, and the soul's approach to the fountain of divine remembrance.
- Root: عصر (ʿaṣr)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The root denotes pressing, squeezing, and extracting; also the time of afternoon, so called because it is the pressing of the day's end.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The ʿaṣr is the latter part of the day; God swore by it in {«والعصر»} (Q. 103:1), indicating its great merit.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the afternoon time. Metaphorical: the pressing of one's life — as the day is pressed at its end, so the life of man is pressed at its term.
- Root: غرب (gharaba)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The root denotes disappearance, absence, and setting; the sun's setting (ghurūb) is its concealment from the eye.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The setting of the sun marks the boundary between the day's works and the night's; it is the terminus of the visible world's diurnal cycle.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the sun's descent below the horizon. Metaphorical: the setting of the sun of life — the death of man, after which there is no rising.
- Root: حاسب (ḥāsaba)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The root denotes reckoning, counting, and taking account; muḥāsabah is the mutual reckoning between two parties.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Self-accounting (muḥāsabat al-nafs) is the soul's reckoning with itself over its deeds before the Day of Reckoning, for "one who reckons himself before he is reckoned" is among the wise.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the arithmetic counting of sums. Metaphorical: the soul's audit of its own works, weighing the day's deeds against the standard of the Sacred Law.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The rule governing the separation of the prepositional phrase from its governing verb, as in the construction "فسبحان الله حين تمسون" where the adverbial clause is interposed to emphasize the temporal specification of the act of glorification.
98:4.topic: Al-Ghazali on constant remembrance of God and contemplative invocations, from 'Remembrance of Death and Afterlife'

99:6.arabic: الله ونسوه والله على كل شيء شهيد} وقال تعالى {يومئذ يصدر الناس أشتاتا ليروا أعمالهم فمن يعمل مثقال ذرة خيرا يره ومن يعمل مثقال ذرة شرا يره} وقال تعالى {ثم توفى كل نفس ما كسبت وهم لا يظلمون} وقال تعالى {يوم تجد كل نفس ما عملت من خير محضرا وما عملت من سوء تود لو أن بينها وبينه أمدا بعيدا ويحذركم الله نفسه} وقال تعالى {واعلموا أن الله يعلم ما في أنفسكم فاحذروه} فعرف أرباب البصائر من جملة العباد أن الله تعالى لهم بالمرصاد وأنهم سيناقشون في الحساب ويطالبون بمثاقيل الذر من الخطرات واللحظات وتحققوا أنه لا ينجيهم من هذه
99:6.english: To proceed: God Most High has said: {And We shall set up the scales of justice for the Day of Resurrection, so no soul shall be wronged in anything; and if it be the weight of a grain of mustard seed, We shall bring it forth, and sufficient are We as Reckoners} (21:47). And He said: {And the Book shall be placed, and you will see the criminals fearful of what is in it, and they will say, "Woe to us! What is this book that leaves neither small nor great but has enumerated it?" And they will find what they did present, and your Lord wrongs no one} (18:49). And He said: {On the Day when God will raise them all together and inform them of what they did — God has enumerated it, and they have forgotten it, and God is Witness over all things} (58:6). And He said: {On that Day, people will issue forth in scattered groups to be shown their deeds. So whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it, and whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it} (99:6-8). And He said: {Then every soul shall be paid in full for what it has earned, and they shall not be wronged} (2:281). And He said: {On the Day when every soul will find what it did of good present, and what it did of evil, it will wish that between it and that there were a far distance; and God warns you of Himself} (3:30). And He said: {And know that God knows what is in your souls, so beware of Him} (2:235).
99:6.section_title_en: Exposition of the Reality of Truthfulness (Al-Sidq), Its Meaning, and Its Grades — Book of Vigilance and Self-Reckoning, Being the Eighth Book of the Quarter of Deliverance from the Revival of the Religious Sciences
99:6.anchors:
- Root: رقب (Raqaba)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To watch, guard, observe; a watcher (raqīb) is one who stands vigilant over something, awaiting its occurrence.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Raqaba denotes protective watchfulness; al-raqīb is a divine attribute signifying His perpetual oversight of all that transpires, with no moment of neglect.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (haqīqah): physical watching/awaiting. Metaphorical (majāz): "This matter is upon your necks (fī riqābikum)" — i.e., an obligation you must vigilantly uphold; "the death is in the necks" — imminent and inescapable.
- Root: حسب (Hasaba)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To count, reckon, compute; al-ḥisāb is the act of enumeration and settlement of accounts.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-ḥisāb is the employment of number; divine reckoning (ḥisāb) on the Day of Resurrection is the exacting appraisal of deeds, even to the atom's weight.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: counting wealth or deeds. Metaphorical: "they reckon news (yaḥtasibūna al-akhbār)" — they investigate and ascertain, as one places knowledge in place of conjecture.
- Root: قلب (Qalaba)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To turn, overturn, transform; the heart (qalb) is so named for its constant fluctuation and turning of states.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Qalaba is the turning of a thing from one state to another; the heart's inner thoughts (khaṭarāt) are its successive movements, which God surveys.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: turning a garment or object. Metaphorical: "the teacher turned the boys" (sent them home); "the merchant turned the goods" (scrutinized them) — thus, inner reflection (taqallub) is the soul's scrutiny of its own motives.
- Sibawayh Rule: Restriction and Focused Predication (al-ḥaṣr wa al-taqyīd bi-innamā) — The particle innamā restricts the predicate to the subject alone, as in "إنما يحاسبهم لتعلم كل نفس" — the sole purpose of reckoning is specified, excluding all other ends.
99:6.topic: Al-Ghazali on the journey of the soul, death, and the Hereafter, from 'Remembrance of Death and Afterlife'

99:8.arabic: درجاتهم وبالجملة {فمن يعمل مثقال ذرة خيرا يره ومن يعمل مثقال ذرة شرا يره} ومن قصد الله تعالى بالعلم أي علم كان نفعه ورفعه لا محالة الوظيفة العاشرة أن يعلم نسبة العلوم إلى المقصد كيما يؤثر الرفيع القريب على البعيد والمهم على غيره ومعنى المهم ما يهمك ولا يهمك إلا شأنك في الدنيا والآخرة وإذا لم يمكنك الجمع بين ملاذ الدنيا ونعيم الآخرة كما نطق به القرآن وشهد له من نور البصائر ما يجري مجرى العيان فالأهم ما يبقى أبد الآباد وعند ذلك تصير الدنيا منزلا والبدن مركبا والأعمال سعيا إلى المقصد ولا مقصد إلا لقاء الله تعالى
99:8.english: By this I do not mean the belief which the common man picks up by inheritance or by rote acquisition, nor the method of theological disputation and argumentation for fortifying one's creed against the evasions of opponents—as is the ultimate aim of the scholastic theologian (mutakallim). Rather, it is a kind of certainty which is the fruit of a light that God—may He be exalted—casts into the heart of a servant whose inward being has been purified by spiritual striving (mujāhadah) from all impurities, until he attains to the rank of the faith of Abū Bakr—may God be pleased with him—whose faith, were it weighed against the faith of all created beings, would outweigh them, as the Master of mankind—peace and blessings be upon him—bore witness for him. For in my view, what the common man believes and what the theologian arranges—who exceeds the common man only in the craft of speech (kalām), and for that very reason his craft is named "kalām"—is not that rank. Indeed, ʿUmar, ʿUthmān, ʿAlī, and the rest of the Companions—may God be pleased with them all—fell short of it, until Abū Bakr surpassed them by that secret which was deposited in his breast.
99:8.section_title_en: The Revival of the Religious Sciences — Section 43: On the Ordering of the Sciences and the Duties of the Seeker
99:8.anchors:
- Root: ذوق (dh-w-q)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Perceiving by taste; experiential apprehension
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Direct, unmediated perception—contrasted with mere cognition or hearsay
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal tasting vs. metaphorical "savoring" of knowledge
- Root: سلك (s-l-k)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Entering into a path; threading through
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The spiritual wayfaring (sulūk) toward God
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal road-taking vs. metaphorical spiritual journeying
- Root: كشف (k-sh-f) — AVOIDED per constraints; substituted with Root: غور (gh-w-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Depth, profundity; the deep bed of a sea
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The unfathomable depth of divine knowledge
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal deep water vs. metaphorical inaccessibility of ultimate truth
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — Governing the periodic suspension of meaning across clauses for rhetorical emphasis
99:8.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Remembrance of Death and Afterlife'

101:4.arabic: هباء منبثا يوم يكون الناس كالفراش المبثوث وتكون الجبال كالعهن المنفوش يوم تذهل فيه كل مرضعة عما أرضعت وتضع كل ذات حمل حملها وترى الناس سكارى وما هم بسكارى ولكن عذاب الله شديد يوم تبدل الأرض غير الأرض والسموات وبرزوا لله الواحد القهار يوم تنسف فيه الجبال نسفا فتترك قاعا صفصفا لا ترى فيها عوجا ولا أمتا يوم ترى الجبال تحسبها جامدة وهي تمر مر السحاب يوم تنشق فيه السماء فتكون وردة كالدهان فيومئذ لا يسئل عن ذنبه إنس ولا جان يوم يمنع فيه العاصى من الكلام ولا يسئل فيه عن الأجرام بل يؤخذ بالنواصى
101:4.english: So prepare yourself, O wretched one, for this Day of immense magnitude, of prolonged duration, of overwhelming dominion, whose appointed time is near — a Day when you shall see the heaven split asunder, and the stars scattered in its terror, and the shining planets extinguished, and the sun folded up, and the mountains set in motion, and the pregnant camels neglected, and the wild beasts gathered together, and the seas set ablaze, and the souls paired with their bodies, and the Hellfire ignited, and Paradise brought near, and the mountains pulverized, and the earth stretched out — a Day when you shall see the earth shaken with its quaking, and the earth casts forth its burdens. On that Day shall people issue forth in scattered groups to be shown their deeds — a Day when the earth and the mountains are lifted and crushed with a single crushing. Then on that Day the Imminent Event shall come to pass, and the heaven shall split open, for on that Day it shall be frail, and the angels shall be at its edges, and eight shall bear the Throne of your Lord above them on that Day. On that Day you shall be presented — no secret of yours shall remain hidden. A Day when the mountains shall move and you shall see the earth laid bare — a Day when the earth shall be shaken with a violent shaking, and the mountains crumbled to dust, becoming scattered particles — a Day when people shall be like scattered moths, and the mountains like carded wool — a Day when every nursing mother shall forget what she nursed, and every pregnant female shall cast down her burden, and you shall see people drunk, yet they are not drunk, but the chastisement of God is severe — a Day when the earth shall be changed to other than this earth, and the heavens, and they shall appear before God, the One, the All-Compelling — a Day when the mountains shall be blown away as dust, leaving a level, bare plain, wherein you see no crookedness nor curve — a Day when you see the mountains and suppose them solid, yet they pass by like the passing of clouds — a Day when the heaven shall split open and become rosy like molten oil. Then on that Day no human nor jinn shall be asked about his sin. A Day when the disobedient shall be prevented from speech, and shall not be asked about their crimes, but shall be seized by their forelocks and their feet — a Day when every soul shall find what it did of good brought forth present, and what it did of evil, wishing that between it and that evil there were a far distance — a Day when every soul shall know what it has sent ahead, and shall witness what it has forwarded and what it has left behind — a Day when tongues shall be struck mute and the bodily members shall speak — a Day whose mention turned the hair of the Master of the Messengers white, when al-Ṣiddīq (may God be pleased with him) said to him: "I see that you have turned white-haired, O Messenger of God." He said: "Sūrat Hūd and its sisters have made me white-haired" — namely, al-Wāqiʿah, al-Mursalāt, ʿAmma Yatasāʾalūn, and Idhā al-Shamsu Kuwwirat.
101:4.section_title_en: The Names and Attributes of the Day of Resurrection — An Exhortation to the Negligent
101:4.anchors:
- Root: يوم (yawm)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "اليوم: وقت طلوع الشمس إلى غروبها، وقد يعبر به عن مدة من الزمان أي مدة كانت" — the day as a temporal span, extended metaphorically to any epoch or era.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "اليوم يعبر به عن وقت طلوع الشمس إلى غروبها. وقد يعبر به عن مدة من الزمان أي مدة كانت" — theological usage denotes the appointed time of reckoning, magnified by divine attribution (أيام الله).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): a measured solar period. Metaphorical (Majaz): "ذكر في أيام العرب كذا أي في وقائعها" — days as epochal events; thus "the Day" is the supreme epochal event of divine justice.
- Root: نفس (nafs)
  * Lisan / Ayn: النفس: الروح والذات — the self, soul, or very essence.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "النفس: الروح... وقوله: ويحذركم الله نفسه فنفسه: ذاته" — nafs as the innermost reality of a being; in the eschatological context, souls are "paired" (زوجت) with bodies for judgment.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the soul as life-principle. Metaphorical: "دفق نفسه أي دمه" — nafs as the total self, accountable in its entirety.
- Root: ارض (arḍ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: الأرض: الجرم المقابل للسماء — the earth as the corporeal substratum beneath the heavens.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الأرض: الجرم المقابل للسماء... ويعبر بها عن أسفل الشيء" — the earth as the lowest register of creation, subject to total transformation on that Day.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the physical earth. Metaphorical: "تأرض فلان: لزم الأرض" — to cling low; on that Day the earth itself is leveled, flattened, and replaced.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد (Restriction & Focused Predication) — The repeated "يوم" clauses function as temporal restrictors (ẓurūf) binding each predicate to that single, all-encompassing moment; the accumulation of names (أسامي) serves not as mere repetition but as focused predication upon the multifarious realities of a single event.
101:4.topic: Al-Ghazali on the journey of the soul, death, and the Hereafter, from 'Remembrance of Death and Afterlife'

101:4.arabic: فصارت وردة كالدهان وصارت السماء كالمهل وصارت الجبال كالعهن واشتبك الناس كالفراش المبثوث وهم حفاة عراة مشاة قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يبعث الناس حفاة عراة غرلا قد ألجمهم العرق وبلغ شحوم الآذان قالت سودة زوج النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم راوية الحديث قلت يا رسول الله واسوأتاه ينظر بعضنا إلى بعض فقال شغل الناس عن ذلك بهم لكل امرىء يومئذ شأن يغنيه (2) فأعظم بيوم تنكشف فيه العورات ويؤمن فيه مع ذلك النظر والالتفات كيف وبعضهم يمشون على بطونهم ووجوههم فلا قدرة لهم على الالتفات إلى غيرهم قال أبو هريرة رضي الله عنه قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يحشر الناس يوم القيامة ثلاثة أصناف ركبانا ومشاة وعلى وجوههم فقال رجل يا رسول الله وكيف يمشون على وجوههم قال الذى أمشاهم على أقدامهم قادر على أن يمشيهم على وجوههم (1) فى طبع الآدمى إنكار كل ما لم يأنس به ولو لم يشاهد الإنسان الحية وهى تمشى على بطنها كالبرق الخاطف لأنكر تصور المشى على غير رجل والمشى بالرجل أيضا مستبعد عند من لم يشاهد ذلك فإياك أن تنكر شيئا من عجائب يوم القيامة لمخالفته قياس ما فى الدنيا فإنك لو لم تكن قد شاهدت عجائب الدنيا ثم عرضت عليك قبل المشاهدة لكنت أشد إنكارا لها فأحضر فى قلبك صورتك وأنت واقف عاريا مكشوفا ذليلا مدحورا متحيرا مبهوتا منتظرا لما يجرى عليك من القضاء بالسعادة أو بالشقاوة وأعظم هذه الحال فإنها عظيمة
101:4.english: Know, O seeker, that after the resurrection and the arising from the graves, consider how they are driven — barefoot, naked, uncircumcised — to the land of the Gathering. It is a white land, a level plain, smooth and even, wherein you see no crookedness nor any curve, and upon which you see no hillock behind which a person might hide, nor any hollow that would sink him from view. Rather, it is one single, simple expanse with no variation whatsoever, and to it they are driven in troops. Glory be to Him who gathered all creatures, despite their differing kinds, from the far quarters of the earth, when He drove them by the Rajīfah (the Trembling Blast) followed by the Rādifah (the Second Blast). The Rajīfah is the first trumpet-blast, and the Rādifah is the second. Rightly are those hearts on that day agitated, and rightly are those eyes humbled. The Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, said: «The people will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection upon a white, ʿafrāʾ earth, like a pure loaf of bread, upon which there is no marker for anyone.» The narrator said: "ʿAfrah is a whiteness that is not brilliant, and al-naqī is the bread purified of its bran and husk. 'No marker' means no building that conceals, and no unevenness that repels the eye."
101:4.section_title_en: The Description of the Trumpet-Blast and the Land of the Gathering
101:4.anchors:
- Root: صور (ṣ-w-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root denotes form/shape; the "trumpet" (ṣūr) is that which shapes and transforms states through its blast.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance — the ṣūr is the instrument of cosmic transformation, linking the two blasts (rajīfah and rādifah) to the divine command of resurrection.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — a horn/trumpet; metaphorical — the blast as the signal of universal upheaval, not a mere physical sound.
- Root: حشر (ḥ-sh-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to gather, drive, or assemble a multitude forcibly.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theologically, ḥashr is the divine gathering of all creatures to the plain of reckoning, distinct from ordinary aggregation by its comprehensiveness and compulsion.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — herding animals; metaphorical — the compelled assembly of humanity before God, stripped of all worldly coverings.
- Root: عفر (ʿ-f-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: ʿafrāʾ denotes a whitish hue tinged with redness or dust-color; the "white" earth of the gathering is not pure white but a dusty, pale expanse.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The earth's transformation (tabdīl al-arḍ) signifies a new creation, not mere alteration of accidents.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — color description; metaphorical — the earth's purity from sin and bloodshed, as the narrator glosses ʿafrāʾ as "whiteness not brilliant."
- Sibawayh Rule: Interposition of descriptive clauses (ṣifah) between subject and predicate — the extended adjectival chains (e.g., "arḍ bayḍāʾ qāʿ ṣafṣaf...") delay the main verb to build cumulative, awe-inducing imagery, permissible due to the semantic completeness of each descriptive unit.
101:4.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Remembrance of Death and Afterlife'

101:6.arabic: قد عرفت هول الميزان وخطره وأن الأعين شاخصة إلى لسان الميزان فأما من ثقلت موازينه فهو في عيشة راضية وأما من خفت موازينه فأمه هاوية وما أدراك ماهيه نار حامية واعلم أنه لا ينجو من خطر الميزان إلا من حاسب في الدنيا نفسه ووزن فيها بميزان الشرع أعماله وأقواله وخطراته ولحظاته كما قال عمر رضي الله عنه حاسبوا أنفسكم قبل أن تحاسبوا وزنوها قبل أن توزنوا وإنما حسابه لنفسه أن يتوب عن كل معصية قبل الموت توبة نصوحا ويتدارك ما فرط من تقصيره في فرائض الله تعالى ويرد المظالم حبة بعد حبة ويستحل كل من تعرض له بلسانه ويده وسوء ظنه بقلبه وبطيب قل
101:6.english: Know that none is saved from the peril of the Scale except him who, in this world, called his own soul to account, and weighed therein — by the scale of the Sacred Law — his deeds, his words, his passing thoughts, and his glances, just as ʿUmar — may God be well pleased with him — said: "Call yourselves to account before you are called to account, and weigh yourselves before you are weighed." Indeed, his calling himself to account consists in his repenting, before death, from every act of disobedience with a sincere repentance (tawbah naṣūḥ), and in his making up for what was neglected of his shortcomings regarding the obligatory commands of God — may He be exalted — and in his restoring rights to those he wronged, grain by grain, and in his seeking absolution from everyone whom he harmed by his tongue, his hand, or his evil suspicion harbored in his heart — and this by winning their hearts' contentment — until he dies with no outstanding wrong against him, nor any neglected obligation.
101:6.section_title_en: The Perils of the Scale and the Reckoning of Wrongs Against Others
101:6.anchors:
- Root: وزن (w-z-n)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning is weighing, measuring, and balancing; al-mīzān (the Scale) is the instrument of equitable judgment.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In theological context, al-mīzān is the divine instrument of justice on the Day of Resurrection, weighing deeds to manifest equitable recompense, not a corporeal balance.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) usage denotes physical weighing; metaphorical (majāz) usage extends to moral and spiritual accounting, as in "weighing one's deeds by the scale of the Sacred Law."
- Sibawayh Rule: Conditional and Exceptive Constructions (الشّرط والاستثناء) — governing the protasis-apodosis structure in "whoever's scales are heavy... whoever's scales are light," and the exceptive force in "none is saved... except he who reckons."
101:6.topic: Al-Ghazali on the journey of the soul, death, and the Hereafter, from 'Remembrance of Death and Afterlife'

101:6.arabic: لا يقبل النافلة حتى تؤدى الفريضة وإنما ثقلت موازين من ثقلت موازينهم يوم القيامة باتباعهم الحق في الدنيا وثقله عليهم وحق لميزان لا يوضع فيه إلا الحق أن يثقل وإنما خفت موازين من خفت موزاينهم يوم القيامة باتباع الباطل وخفته عليهم وحق لميزان لا يوضع فيه إلاالباطل أن يخف وإن الله ذكر أهل الجنة بأحسن أعمالهم وتجاوز عن سيئاتهم فيقول القائل أنا دون هؤلاء ولا أبلغ مبلغ صالح الذي عملوا فيقول القائل أنا أفضل من هؤلاء وإن الله ذكر آية الرحمة وآية العذاب ليكون المؤمن راغبا راهبا ولا يلقى بيديه إلى التهلكة ولا يتمنى على الله غير الحق فإن حفظت وصيتي هذه فلا يكون غائب أحب إليك من الموت ولا بد لك منه وإن ضيعت وصيتي فلا يكون غائب أبغض إليك من الموت ولا بد لك منه ولست بمعجزه وقال سعيد بن المسيب لما احتضر أبو بكر رضي الله عنه أتاه ناس من الصحابة فقالوا يا خليفة رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم زودنا فإنا نراك لما بك فقالوا أبو بكر من قال هؤلاء الكلمات ثم مات جعل الله روحه في الأفق المبين قالوا وما الأفق المبين قال قاع بين يديالعرش فيه رياض الله وأنهار وأشجار يغشاه كل يوم مائة رحمة فمن قال هذا القول جعل الله روحه في هذا المكان اللهم إنك ابتدأت الخلق من غير حاجة بك إليهم ثم جعلتهم فريقين فريقا للنعيم وفريقا للسعير فاجعلني للنعيم ولا تجعلني للسعير اللهم إنك خلقت الخلق فرقا وميزتهم قبل أن تخلقهم فجعلت منهم شقيا وسعيدا وغويا ورشيدا فلا تشقني بمعاصيك اللهم إنك علمت ما تكسب كل نفس قبل أن تخلقها فلا محيص لها مما علمت فاجعلني ممن تستعمله بطاعتك اللهم إن أحدا لا يشاء حتى تشاء فاجعل مشيئتك أن أشاء ما يقربني إليك اللهم إنك قد قدرت حركات العباد فلا يتحرك شيء إلا بإذنك فاجعل حركاتي في تقواك اللهم إنك خلقت الخير والشر وجعلت لكل واحد منهما عاملا يعمل به فاجعلني من خير القسمين اللهم إنك خلقت الجنة والنار وجعلت لكل واحدة منهما أهلا فاجعلني من سكان جنتك اللهم إنك أردت بقوم الضلال وضيقت به صدورهم فاشرح صدري للإيمان وزينه في قلبي اللهم إنك دبرت الأمور وجعلت مصيرها إليك فأحيني بعد الموت حياة طيبة وقربني إليك زلفى اللهم من أصبح وأمسى ثقته ورجاؤه غيرك فأنت ثقتي ورجائي ولا حول ولا قوة إلا بالله قال أبو بكر هذا كله في كتاب الله عز وجل
101:6.english: When Abu Bakr (may Allah Most High be pleased with him) was in the throes of death, ʿĀʾishah (may Allah be pleased with her) came and recited this verse: "By your life, wealth avails not the youth... when the breath rattles in his chest one day, and the breast is straitened thereby."
101:6.section_title_en: The Death of Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (may Allah Most High be pleased with him)
101:6.anchors:
- Root: حشرج (ḥashraja)
  * Lisan / Ayn: [Core linguistic root meaning: The rattling, gurgling sound of the death-throe in the throat; the final breath struggling in the chest.]
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): [Theological/Kalam semantic nuance: The terminal state of the soul's separation from the body, the moment of overwhelming divine decree.]
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): [Literal vs Metaphorical distinction: Literal — the physical rattle of the dying; Metaphorical — the constriction of the breast as the soul is drawn forth.]
- Root: سكر (sakara)
  * Lisan / Ayn: [Core linguistic root meaning: The veiling of the intellect; intoxication; the stupor that overcomes one at the onset of death.]
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): [Theological/Kalam semantic nuance: The stupor of death (sakrat al-mawt) as the removal of all veils, wherein the truth of the Hereafter becomes undeniably present.]
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): [Literal vs Metaphorical distinction: Literal — intoxication from drink; Metaphorical — the overwhelming bewilderment of the soul at death's onset.]
- Root: ذمم (dhimam)
  * Lisan / Ayn: [Core linguistic root meaning: The covenant of protection; the bond of safe-conduct; that which one is obligated to honor and safeguard.]
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): [Theological/Kalam semantic nuance: The divine guarantee (dhimmat Allah) extended to the believer who prays the dawn prayer — a sacred pact not to be violated.]
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): [Literal vs Metaphorical distinction: Literal — a pledge of security between men; Metaphorical — the inviolable covenant between the servant and his Lord.]
- Root: وزن (wazana)
  * Lisan / Ayn: [Core linguistic root meaning: To weigh; the balance; the measure of equivalence between two things.]
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): [Theological/Kalam semantic nuance: The weighing of deeds on the Day of Resurrection as the manifestation of divine justice — the scales (mawāzīn) receiving only truth or falsehood.]
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): [Literal vs Metaphorical distinction: Literal — the physical act of weighing; Metaphorical — the spiritual weighing of deeds by their conformity to truth (ḥaqq) or falsehood (bāṭil).]
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — [The particle innamā restricts the predicate exclusively to its subject, as in Abu Bakr's dictum: "It is only that the scales of those whose scales are heavy on the Day of Resurrection are weighed down by their following the truth in this world."]
101:6.topic: Al-Ghazali on the journey of the soul, death, and the Hereafter, from 'Remembrance of Death and Afterlife'

112:1.arabic: وفي الصبح في السفر قل يا أيها الكافرون وقل هو الله أحد وكذلك في ركعتي الفجر والطواف والتحية وهو في جميع ذلك مستديم للقيام ووضع اليدين كما وصفنا في أول الصلاة الركوع ولواحقه ثم يركع ويراعي فيه أمورا وهو أن يكبر للركوع وأن يرفع يديه مع تكبيرة الركوع وأن يمد التكبير مدا إلى الانتهاء إلى الركوع وأن يضع راحتيه على ركبتيه في الركوع وأصابعه منشورة موجهة نحو القبلة على طول الساق وأن ينصب ركبتيه ولا يثنيهما وأن يمد ظهره مستويا وأن يكون عنقه ورأسه مستويين مع ظهره كالصفيحة الواحدة لا يكون رأسه أخف
112:1.english: I say: Then the worshipper begins with the opening supplication (duʿāʾ al-istiftāḥ). It is excellent that he say, following his utterance of "Allāhu akbar, Allāhu akbar": "Kabīran wa-l-ḥamdu lillāhi kathīran wa-subḥāna Allāhi bukratan wa-aṣīlā" (Great indeed is Allah, and abundant praise be to Allah, and glory be to Allah morning and evening) {«الله أكبر كبيرا والحمد لله كثيرا وسبحان الله بكرة وأصيلا»} — then: "Wajjahtu wajhiya..." (I have turned my face...) up to his saying "...wa-anā min al-muslimīn" (and I am among those who submit) {«وجهت وجهي إلى قوله وأنا من المسلمين»}. Then he says: "Subḥānaka Allāhumma wa-bi-ḥamdika wa-tabāraka-smuka wa-taʿālā jadduka wa-jalla thanāʾuka wa-lā ilāha ghayruk" (Glory be to You, O Allah, and with Your praise; blessed is Your Name and exalted is Your majesty; glorious is Your praise and there is no god but You) {«سبحانك اللهم وبحمدك وتبارك اسمك وتعالى جدك وجل ثناؤك ولا إله غيرك»} — so that he may combine within himself the various dispersed reports transmitted in the traditions.
112:1.section_title_en: Section 127 — On the Recitation (Qirāʾah) and the Bowing (Rukūʿ) with Its Attendant Matters
112:1.anchors:
- Root: قرأ (Qaraʾa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of gathering and assembling letters into articulated speech; recitation as the oral articulation of written or memorized text.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In the Quranic and liturgical context, qirāʾah is the deliberate, worshipful utterance of the divine word, distinct from mere reading; it is an act of devotion requiring presence of heart.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) usage denotes the physical articulation of sounds; metaphorical (majāz) usage extends to the inward recitation of the heart in contemplation.
- Root: ركع (Rakaʿa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The physical act of bowing; the bending of the back in humility.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الركوع: الانحناء، فتارة يستعمل في الهيئة المخصوصة في الصلاة كما هي، وتارة في التواضع والتذلل" — The bowing is an inclination, used sometimes for the specific posture in prayer, and sometimes for humility and self-abasement.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): "شيخ راكع: منحن من الكبر" — an old man bowed with age. Metaphorical (majāz): "لغبت الإبل حتى ركعت" — camels fatigued until they lowered their heads, indicating the physical posture as the outward sign of inward submission.
- Root: صبح (Ṣabaḥa)
  * Al-Raghib (Al-Mufradat): "الصبح والصباح، أول النهار" — the dawn is the beginning of the day, the time when the horizon reddens.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas - Majaz/Metaphorical): "أصبح يا رجل: انتبه من غفلتك" — "become awake, O man: awaken from your heedlessness," showing the dawn prayer as the time of spiritual awakening.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Prepositional Interposition (باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور) — governing the permissible separation between governing and governed elements, applied here to the proper pausing (waqf) and connecting (waṣl) of Quranic phrases to preserve meaning.
112:1.topic: Al-Ghazali on constant remembrance of God and contemplative invocations, from 'Remembrance of Death and Afterlife'

112:1.arabic: فتارة يتعرف إليهم بالتقديس فيقول قل هو الله أحد الله الصمد لم يلد ولم يولد ولم يكن له كفوا أحد وتارة يتعرف إليهم بصفات جلاله فيقول الملك القدوس السلام المؤمن المهيمن العزيز الجبار المتكبر وتارة يتعرف إليهم في أفعاله المخوفة والمرجوة فيتلو عليهم سنته في أعدائه وفي أنبيائه فيقول ألم تر كيف فعل ربك بعاد إرم ذات العماد ألم تر كيف فعل ربك بأصحاب الفيل ولايعدو القرآن هذه الأقسام الثلاثة وهي الإرشاد إلى معرفة ذات الله وتقديسه أو معرفة صفاته وأسمائه أو معرفة أفعاله وسنته مع عباده ولما اشتملت سورة الإخلاص على أحد ه
112:1.english: And in the report [it is said]: Verily God—exalted is He—revealed to a servant whom He had taken by the hand after he had been on the brink of destruction: "How many a sin did you commit against Me, and I forgave it for you—sins for the sake of which I destroyed entire nations among the nations!" So this is the way (sunnah) of God—exalted is He—with His servants, by way of favor (tafḍīl), and bringing forward (taqdīm), and deferring (taʾkhīr), according to what the eternal will (al-mashīʾah al-azaliyyah) had previously decreed.
112:1.section_title_en: On the Meaning of Contentment with God's Decree (Al-Riḍā bi Qaḍāʾ Allāh), Its Reality, and What Has Been Reported Concerning Its Virtue
112:1.anchors:
- Root: رضي (Raḍā)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of being pleased, satisfied, consenting; the opposite of anger (sakhaṭ). Its object is that which is agreeable and harmonious with one's will.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Raḍā is a state of the heart (ḥāl min aḥwāl al-qalb) signifying the soul's inclination toward what is pleasing, and its cessation of opposition. In theological terms, it is the soul's acquiescence to the divine decree (qaḍāʾ) after the removal of inner resistance.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): "رَضِيَ عَنْهُ" — to be content with someone. Metaphorical (majāz): "رَضِيَ بِالكَوْنِ" — submission to what is, even when it opposes the appetites, which is the higher spiritual usage.
- Root: قضي (Qaḍā)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To decree, determine, execute, or finish a matter; the cutting off of a thing decisively.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Qaḍāʾ is the divine determination (taqdīr) and execution of affairs according to prior eternal knowledge; it encompasses both what is feared and what is hoped for.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the completion of a judgment. Metaphorical: the divine decree as the all-encompassing will of God, which the believer must embrace.
- Root: ولي (Waliya)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Nearness, guardianship, and governance; the one who manages affairs.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Walī is the one who is near to God through obedience, and God is the Walī of the believer through grace and protection.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: proximity. Metaphorical: friendship and divine patronage.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Predicate Emphasis (Bāb al-Taʾkīd bi al-Ḍamīr al-Munfaṣil) — The repetition of the pronoun for emphasis, as in "اللهُ هُوَ" structures, to affirm the exclusivity of divine attributes without ambiguity.
112:1.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Condemnation of Anger and Hatred'

2:26.arabic: {يضل به كثيرا ويهدي به كثيرا} فهؤلاء لما ظنوا أنهم استخدموا لأجل المساكين والفقراء أو جل الله تعالى ثم قالوا لا حظ لنا في المساكين ولا حظ لله فينا وفي أموالنا سواء أنفقنا أو أمسكنا هلكوا كما هلك الصبي لما ظن أن مقصود الوالد استخدامه لأجل
2:26.english: Likewise, if it were said: "Is oxymel (sikanjabīn) better, or the drink of the water-lily (sharāb al-līnūfar)?" — no unqualified answer could be correct at all. Indeed, if it were said to us: "Is oxymel better, or the absence of yellow bile?" — we would say: the absence of yellow bile, for oxymel is sought for the sake of something else, and that which is sought for its own sake is necessarily better than that which is sought for the sake of another.
2:26.section_title_en: The Superiority of Knowledge Over Action — The Parable of the Physician and the Child
2:26.anchors:
- Root: فضل (faḍl)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Excess or increase beyond what is required; superiority in degree.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الفضل: الزيادة عن الاقتصاد" — excess beyond moderation, divided into praiseworthy (like excess of knowledge) and blameworthy; comparative superiority of one thing over another by genus, species, or merit.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): "فاضلني فلان ففضلته" — to surpass in excellence. Here used comparatively: one act or state exceeds another in rank.
- Root: علم (ʿilm)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Knowledge as the apprehension of a thing's reality; the mark or sign by which something is known.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "العلم: إدراك الشيء بحقيقته" — apprehension of a thing's true reality, whether by direct perception of its essence or by judgment concerning it.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "هو من أعلام العلم الخافقه" — knowledge as a lofty, manifest sign; distinguished from mere action which is its instrument.
- Root: صدق (ṣidq)
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Truthfulness primarily in speech — correspondence of report with reality; may become blameworthy when it leads to ruin, as with the disbelievers who spoke truly about God's independence yet drew false conclusions.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "صدقته الحديث" — truthful in statement. Metaphorical (Majaz): "رجل صادق الحملة" — truthful in resolve. Here: the disbelievers were literally truthful in their words yet destroyed by that very truthfulness.
- Root: هلك (halak)
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Destruction on three levels: loss of something from one's possession, corruption and dissolution, and death. Used here for spiritual ruin through misapplied reasoning.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "وقعوا في المهلكة" — falling into destruction. Metaphorical: "تهالك على الشيء" — intense craving. Here: literal perdition of the soul through false inference.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The conditional structure "فإن قلت... فاعلم" (if you say... then know) governs the entire periodic sentence, requiring the apodosis to resolve the protasis with logical necessity, as in the physician analogy where praise of the medicine does not entail its intrinsic superiority.
2:26.topic: Classical commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya Ulum al-Din, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

2:32.arabic: الله عز وجل قال يا جبريل ما جزاء من سلبت كريمتيه قال سبحانك لا علم لنا إلا ما علمتنا قال الله تعالى جزاؤه الخلود في داري والنظر إلى وجهي // وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول الله عز وجل إذا ابتليت عبدي ببلاء فصبر ولم يشكني إلى عواده أبدلته لحما خيرا من لحمه ودما خيرا من دمه فإذا أبرأته أبرأته ولا ذنب له وإن توفيته فإلى رحمتي وقال داود عليه السلام يا رب ما جزاء الحزين الذي يصبر على المصائب ابتغاء مرضاتك قال جزاؤه أن ألبسه لباس الإيمان فلا أنزعه عنه أبدا وقال عمر بن عبد العزيز رحمه الله في خطبته ما أنعم الله على عبد نعمة فانتزعها منه
2:32.english: Ibn ʿAbbās, may God be pleased with them both, said: "Patience in the Qur'an is of three aspects: patience in performing the obligatory duties of God most High — for it has three hundred degrees; patience in refraining from the forbidden things of God most High — for it has six hundred degrees; and patience over calamity at the first shock — for it has nine hundred degrees." This rank, despite being among the virtuous acts, was only rendered superior to what precedes it — which belongs to the obligatory acts — because every believer is capable of patience in refraining from forbidden things.
2:32.section_title_en: The Third Division: Patience Regarding What Lies Beyond the Scope of Choice — Calamities, Its Supreme Stations, and the Warfare of the Heart Against the Whisperer
2:32.anchors:
- Root: صبر (ṣ-b-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "Al-Sabr: al-imsāk fī ḍīq" — restraint within constriction; to hold back, to bind, to detain.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Ṣabartu al-dābbah: ḥabastuhā bilā ʿalaf" — I held the beast back without fodder. "Al-ṣabr: ḥabs al-nafs ʿalā mā yaqtaḍīhi al-ʿaql wa-al-sharʿ" — Patience is the soul's self-restraint upon what reason and Law require, or from what they require it to be withheld. It is a generic term whose names vary by situation: over calamity it is *ṣabr* alone (opposed to *jazaʿ*); in battle, *shajāʿah* (courage); in affliction, forbearance.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Haqiqah (Literal): "Ṣabartu ʿalā mā akrah, wa-ṣabartu ʿammā uḥibb" — I bore patiently what I dislike and refrained from what I love. Majaz (Metaphorical): "Huwa aṣbaru ʿalā al-ḍarb min al-arḍ" — He is more enduring of blows than the earth; and "ṣabartu yamīnahu" — I bound him by an oath (holding him to a stringent vow).
- Root: قلب (q-l-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To turn over, to overturn, to flip from one face to another; the heart as that which is perpetually turning (taqallub).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Qalb al-shay': taṣrīfuhu wa-ṣarfuhu ʿan wajh ilā wajh" — The heart's essence is its constant overturning and veering between states; hence its name.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Haqiqah: "Qalaba al-shay' qalban: ḥawwalahu ʿan wajhihi" — to turn a thing from its face. Majaz: "Rajul qalb ḥawal: yuqallibu al-umūr wa-yaḥtāl" — a man who turns matters over and devises stratagems; "wa-qallabū laka al-umūr" — they turned the affairs over for you (scrutinized them).
- Root: عله (ʿ-l-h) — [Note: Root appears corrupted in source; likely intended ʿ-l-m or ʿ-l-q; context governs]
  * Lisan / Ayn: [Source entry unclear; context indicates occupation and preoccupation of the heart.]
- Root: نعم (n-ʿ-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Grace, bounty, well-being; the state of ease and delight.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Al-niʿmah: al-ḥālah al-ḥasanah" — the beautiful state; "al-naʿīm: al-tanaʿʿum" — the act of living pleasantly. "Wa-in taʿuddū niʿmata Allāhi lā tuḥṣūhā" {«وَإِن تَعُدُّوا نِعْمَةَ اللَّهِ لَا تُحْصُوهَا»} — the genus of grace encompasses both little and much.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Haqiqah: "Jallat niʿmat Allāh wa-naʿmā'uh" — God's grace and bounties are immense. Majaz: "Khafat naʿāmatuhum: dhahabū" — their ostriches departed (i.e., their prosperity fled).
- Sibawayh Rule: Bāb al-ḥaṣr wa-al-taqyīd bi-innamā (Restriction and Specification by *innamā*) — Governing the exclusive predication in "إنما يرحم الله من عباده الرحما" (God shows mercy only to the merciful among His servants), restricting mercy's object.
2:32.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

2:74.arabic: بكاء الشكر والسرور وقلب العبد كالحجارة أو أشد قسوة ولا تزول قسوته إلا بالبكاء في حال الخوف والشكر جميعا وروي عنه صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال ينادى يوم القيامة ليقم الحمادون فتقوم زمرة فينصب لهم لواء فيدخلون الجنة قيل ومن الحمادون قال الذين يشكرون الله تعالى على كل حال (2) حديث الحمد رداء الرحمن لم اجد له اصلا وفي الصحيح من حديث ابي هريرة الكبر رداؤه الحديث وتقدم في العلم وأوحى الله تعالى إلى أيوب عليه السلام إني رضيت بالشكر مكافأة من أوليائي في كلام طويل وأوحى الله تعالى إليه أيضا في صفة الصابرين
2:74.english: And as for the reports [concerning this], the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: "The eater who gives thanks is in the station of the faster who is patient." (1) The hadith of ʿAṭāʾ: I entered upon ʿĀʾishah and said to her: "Inform us of the most wondrous thing you saw of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace." She said: "What of his affair was not wondrous?" — the hadith concerning his weeping during the night prayer. It was transmitted by Abū al-Shaykh Ibn Ḥibbān in the Book of the Character of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and by way of him by Ibn al-Jawzī in al-Wafā. In its chain is Abū Jannāb, whose name is Yaḥyā ibn Abī Ḥabbah, whom the majority of scholars declared weak. Ibn Ḥibbān narrated it in his Ṣaḥīḥ from the narration of ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Abī Sulaymān from ʿAṭāʾ, without her saying "What of his affair was not wondrous?" — and it is found in Muslim from the narration of ʿUrwah from ʿĀʾishah, restricted to the end of the hadith. And this indicates that weeping ought never to cease. And to this secret points what has been narrated: that one of the prophets passed by a small stone from which abundant water issued forth, and he marvelled at it. Then God, exalted be He, gave it speech, and it said: "Ever since I heard the saying of God, exalted be祂: {وَقُودُهَا النَّاسُ وَالْحِجَارَةُ} — 'Its fuel is men and stones' — I weep from fear of Him." So he asked it to intercede for him against the Fire, and it was granted protection for him. Then he saw it after a time in the same state, and said: "Why do you weep now?" It said: "That was the weeping of fear, and this is the weeping of gratitude and joy." And the heart of the servant is like stones, or even harder in hardness, and its hardness is not removed except by weeping in the state of fear and gratitude both together. And it is narrated from him, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: "It will be called out on the Day of Resurrection: 'Let the praisers (al-ḥammādūn) arise!' So a group will arise, and a banner will be erected for them, and they will enter Paradise." It was said: "And who are the praisers?" He said: "Those who thank God, exalted be He, in every state." (2) The hadith "Praise is the cloak of the Merciful" — I found no basis for it. And in the Ṣaḥīḥ, from the hadith of Abū Hurayrah: "Pride is His cloak" — the hadith, and it has preceded in the Book of Knowledge. And God, exalted be He, revealed to Job (Ayyūb), peace be upon him: "I am well-pleased with gratitude as the recompense from My beloved ones" — in a lengthy discourse. And God, exalted be He, also revealed to him concerning the description of the patient ones: "Their abode is the Abode of Peace; when they enter it, I inspire them with gratitude, and it is the best of speech. And upon gratitude I increase them, and through [their] looking to Me I augment them." And when that which was revealed concerning treasures was revealed, ʿUmar, may God be pleased with him, said: "Which wealth shall we take for ourselves?" He, peace be upon him, said: "Let each of you take for himself a remembering tongue and a grateful heart." // The hadith of ʿUmar: "Let each of you take for himself a remembering tongue and a grateful heart" — the hadith has preceded in the Book of Marriage. So he commanded the acquisition of the grateful heart in place of wealth. And Ibn Masʿūd said: "Gratitude is half of faith."
2:74.section_title_en: On the Station of Gratitude (Shukr) — The Virtue of the Thankful Eater and the Ever-Weeping Heart
2:74.anchors:
- Root: شكر (Sh-K-R)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root denotes fullness, saturation, and the appearance of increase upon a beast of burden; the she-camel "shakūr" is one whose udder overflows with milk from scant fodder.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الشكر: تصور النعمة وإظهارها" — Gratitude is the conceptual apprehension of the blessing and its outward manifestation. It is the inverse of kufr (covering/forgetting). Three ranks: gratitude of the heart (perceiving the blessing), of the tongue (praise of the Bestower), and of the limbs (requital proportionate to the blessing).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (haqīqah): "شكرت لله تعالى نعمته" — thanking God for His grace. Metaphorical (majāz): "دابة شكور" — a beast that thrives on little fodder, its condition itself displaying gratitude; the overflowing udder (ضرّة شكرى) as embodied thanksgiving.
- Root: حدث (Ḥ-D-Th)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Origination after non-existence; the new, the recent.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الحدوث: كون الشيء بعد أن لم يكن" — coming-to-be after not having been; the muḥdath is that which is originated, whether accident or substance.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "نزلت به حوادث الدهر" — calamities of time befell him. Metaphorical: "كان عمر محدثا" — ʿUmar was one inspired with correct discernment, as if truth were spoken into his heart.
- Root: ابي (A-B-Y)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Refusal, stubborn refusal, haughtiness in declining.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الإباء: شدة الامتناع" — intense refusal; every ibāʾ is a refusal but not every refusal is ibāʾ. God's word: {وَيَأْبَى اللَّهُ إِلَّا أَنْ يُتِمَّ نُورَهُ} — God refuses but to perfect His light.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "أبى الله إلا أن يكون كذا" — God refused except that it be so. Metaphorical: "لا أبا لك" — an idiom of urging, not literal denial of paternity.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The permissibility of separating a preposition from its governed noun when the intervening clause is complete in itself, as in "إن به..." — governing the flow of periodic constructions where a full sentence intervenes between the particle and its object.
2:74.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

2:74.arabic: قلوب الغافلين مثل الحجارة أو أشد قسوة وإن من الحجارة لما يتفجر منه الأنهار وإن منها لما يشقق فيخرج منه الماء وإن منها لما يهبط من خشية الله وما الله بغافل عما تعملون الشطر الثاني في الخوف بيان أحوال الأنبياء والملائكة عليهم الصلاة والسلام في الخوف روت عائشة رضي الله عنها أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كان إذا تغير الهواء وهبت ريح عاصفة يتغير وجهه فيقول ويتردد في الحجرة ويدخل ويخرج كل ذلك خوفا من عذاب الله (1) وقرأ صلى الله عليه وسلم آية في سورة الواقعة فصعق (2) وقال تعالى وخر موسى صعقا ورأى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم صورة جبريل
2:74.english: And God — may He be exalted — said: {«وَخَرَّ مُوسَىٰ صَعِقًا»} — "And Moses fell down senseless" (al-Aʿrāf 143). And the Messenger of God — may God's peace and blessings be upon him — saw the form of Gabriel — upon him be peace — in a form that caused him to fall down senseless as well, overwhelmed by the awe of the divine manifestation.
2:74.section_title_en: On the Discipline of Eating, Dress, and Dwelling — and the Fear of the Prophets and Angels
2:74.anchors:
- Root: بطن (baṭana)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The belly as the corporeal cavity; the lower/hidden part of a thing, contrasted with ẓahr (back/surface).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The belly is the bodily organ; metaphorically, the "inner" aspect of any matter (baṭn al-amr). Here, it anchors the physiological necessity of ingestion and excretion as twin, involuntary dictates of nature (jibillah).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): "ألقت الدجاجة ذا بطنها" — the hen laid what was in her belly. Metaphorical (majāz): "في بطنان الشباب" — in the very midst of youth. In this text, al-Ghazali uses the literal sense to strip food of any spiritual prestige, equating intake with output.
- Root: قلب (qalaba)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To turn, overturn, or transform a thing from one state to another.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Taṣrīf al-shayʾ — the constant turning of a thing, as in {«إليه تقلبون»} (al-ʿAnkabūt 21). The heart (qalb) is so named for its perpetual fluctuation.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "قلب الثوب" — to turn a garment inside out. Metaphorical: "قلب التاجر السلعة" — the merchant scrutinizes his goods, examining their conditions. Here, the heart's occupation (ishtighāl) with food is a turning of one's inner attention toward the belly, a misdirection of the qalb from God.
- Root: خوف (khāfa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Fear, dread, apprehension of harm.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الخوف: توقع مكروه عن أمارة مظنونة أو معلومة" — the expectation of an undesirable event based on a probable or certain sign. It is the opposite of amn (security), and applies to both worldly and otherworldly matters, as in {«يدعون ربهم خوفا وطمعا»} (al-Sajdah 16).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "خفته على مالي" — I feared for my wealth. Metaphorical: "تخوفه: تنقصه" — to diminish something gradually, as in Zuhayr's verse. In this section, the fear of the prophets is literal and overwhelming — a genuine, annihilating dread of divine wrath, not a mere figure of speech.
- Sibawayh Rule: Bāb al-faṣl bayna al-jār wa-al-majrūr (Prepositional Interposition) — The permissibility of separating a prepositional phrase from its governed noun for rhetorical emphasis, as in "إن به" constructions. Here, the periodic sentences (e.g., "فإن غلبك حر أو برد فعليك بالمساجد") deploy conditional clauses (sharṭ/jazāʾ) to structure the argument: the protasis states the hypothetical excess, the apodosis delivers the normative command.
2:74.topic: Al-Ghazali on the inner and outer dimensions of worship, from 'Fear and Hope'

2:86.arabic: ولا يغاثون بل يقال لهم اخسئوا فيها ولا تكلمون أولئك الذي اشتروا الحياة الدنيا بالآخرة فلا يخفف عنهم العذاب ولا هم ينصرون وإذا عظمت غوائل الدنيا وشرورها فلا بد أولا من معرفة حقيقة الدنيا وما هي وما الحكمة في خلقها مع عداوتها وما مدخل غرورها وشرورها فإن من لا يعرف الشر لا يتقيه ويوشك أن يقع فيه ونحن نذكر ذم الدنيا وأمثلتها وحقيقتها وتفصيل معانيها وأصناف الأشغال المتعلقة بها ووجه الحاجة إلى أصولها وسبب انصراف الخلق عن الله بسبب التشاغل بفضولها إن شاء الله تعالى وهو المعين على ما يرتضيه
2:86.english: Praise be to God, who made His friends acquainted with the calamitous snares of this world and its afflictions, and uncovered for them its defects and its shameful parts, until they gazed upon its evidences and its signs, and weighed its evil deeds against its good deeds. Thus they came to know that its objectionable aspects exceed its commendable ones, that what is hoped from it does not fulfill what is feared from it, and that its rising is not safe from its eclipse. Yet it is in the likeness of a comely woman who draws people to herself by her beauty — while within her are hidden secrets of evil, ugly things that destroy those who yearn for union with her. Then she is a fleer from her seekers, niggardly in her turning toward them; and when she does turn, one is not secure from her evil and her pestilence. If she does good for an hour, she does evil for a year; and if she does evil once, she makes it her perpetual habit. So the cycles of her turning are ever more tightly drawn, and the commerce of her sons is losing and ruined, and her afflictions in succession strike the breasts of her seekers, and the courses of her states proclaim the humiliation of those who pursue her. Thus every one deluded by her is destined to abasement, and every one who waxes proud through her proceeds to regret. Her very nature is to flee from her seeker and to be sought by the one who flees from her. Whoever serves her, she eludes; whoever turns away from her, she comes to. Her clarity is never free of the admixture of turbidity, nor is her joy ever disentangled from what embitters it. Her soundness bequeaths sickness, her youth drives on to decrepitude, and her bliss bears no fruit but remorse and regret. She is deceitful, guileful, fleeting, evasive. She never ceases adorning herself for her seekers until, when they have become her lovers, she bares her fangs at them, disorders the ordered strands of their affairs, and uncovers for them the hidden store of her wonders — then she makes them taste the lethal poisons and strikes them with the piercing shafts of her arrows. While her companions are in joy and bounty from her, suddenly she turns away from them as though she were but scattered dreams; then she rushes upon them with her calamities, grinds them as grain is ground, and shrouds them in their winding-sheets beneath the dust. If she has possessed one of them with all that the sun has risen upon, she makes him as reaped harvest, as though he had not dwelt in plenty the day before. Her companions desire joy from her, and she promises them delusion — until they hope for much and build palaces, and then their palaces become graves, their gatherings become ruin, their striving becomes scattered dust, and their cry becomes "Woe and destruction!" Such is her description — and the command of God is a decree determined. And the prayer and peace be upon Muhammad, His servant and His Messenger, sent to the worlds as a bringer of glad tidings and a warner, and as an illuminating lamp; and upon those of his family and companions who were for him supporters in the religion, and against the wrongdoers helpers; and abundant peace.
2:86.section_title_en: The Book of Condemnation of This World — Being the Sixth Book of the Quarter of the Destructive Things from The Revival of the Religious Sciences
2:86.anchors:
- Root: لهم (l-h-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root meaning of swallowing, devouring, or ingesting wholly
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): الإلهام: casting something into the heart (al-rawʿ), specifically from God or the higher assembly; the root denotes the soul's complete reception, as one who swallows entirely
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: ألهمه الله الخير — God cast good into his heart. Metaphorical: جيش لهم — an army that engulfs and swallows whomever enters it
- Root: دنا (d-n-w)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Nearness in place, time, or rank; the world (al-dunyā) is so named because it is nearer and lower, deferred from the Hereafter
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): الدنو: proximity by essence or by judgment, used of place, time, and station; al-dunyā is the nearer, lower life
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: هو دانٍ — he is near. Metaphorical: الأدنى — the inferior, the baser, contrasted with what is better
- Root: حسر (ḥ-s-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Uncovering, stripping away a covering; exhaustion from exposure of one's strength
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): الحسر: uncovering what veils; al-ḥasīr: one whose strength is laid bare and spent; al-ḥāsir: the weary whose powers are uncovered as exhausted
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: حسر عن ذراعيه — he bared his forearms. Metaphorical: فلان كريم المحسر — so-and-so is noble when tested/examined (his hidden quality is uncovered)
- Root: سرر (s-r-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Concealment, the secret kept hidden in the breast; the innermost
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): الإسرار: opposite of declaration; al-sirr: the speech concealed in the soul
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: أسر الحديث — he concealed the speech. Metaphorical: أعطيتك سره — I gave you its choicest essence; هو في سر النسب — he is in the pure core of lineage
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The permissibility of interposing elements between a governing word and its governed prepositional phrase when the interposed element is complete in itself, as in the rhetorical suspensions of this oration
2:86.topic: Al-Ghazali on the journey of the soul, death, and the Hereafter, from 'Condemnation of Status and Ostentation'

2:86.arabic: وخلقته من طين} وإلى هؤلاء الإشارة بقوله تعالى {أولئك الذين اشتروا الحياة الدنيا بالآخرة فلا يخفف عنهم العذاب ولا هم ينصرون} وعلاج هذا الغرور إما بتصديق الإيمان وإما بالبرهان أما التصديق بمجرد الإيمان فهو أن يصدق الله تعالى في قوله ما عندكم ينفذ وما عند الله باق وفي قوله عز وجل {وما عند الله خير} وقوله {والآخرة خير وأبقى} وقوله {وما الحياة الدنيا إلا متاع الغرور} وقوله {فلا تغرنكم الحياة الدنيا} وقد أخبر رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بذلك طوائف من الكفار فقلدوه وصدقوه وآمنوا به ولم يطالبوه بالبرهان (1) حديث قول من قال له نشدتك الله أبعثك رسولا فيقول {نعم} فيصدق متفق عليه من
2:86.english: Know that the saying of God Most High — {«fa-lā taghurrannakum al-ḥayātu al-dunyā wa-lā yaghurrannakum billāhi al-gharūr»} (So let not the life of this world deceive you, nor let the Deceiver deceive you concerning God) — and His saying — {«wa-lākinnakum fatantum anfusakum wa-tarabbastum wa-irtabtum wa-gharratkum al-amānī»} (But ye tempted your own souls, and ye waited, and ye doubted, and vain desires deceived you) — is sufficient for the blameworthiness of self-deception (al-ghurūr). And the Messenger of God, may God's peace and blessing be upon him, has said: "How excellent is the sleep of the intelligent and their breaking of the fast! How they outwit the wakefulness of the foolish and their striving! And verily a mustard-seed's weight [of faith] from a possessor of piety and certainty is better than the earth filled with the self-deceived." And the ḥadīth: "The intelligent man (al-kayyis) is he who takes account of his own soul and works for what is after death" — this ḥadīth was transmitted by al-Tirmidhī and Ibn Mājah from the ḥadīth of Shaddād ibn Aws.
2:86.section_title_en: Exposition of the Blameworthiness of Self-Deception (Al-Ghurūr), Its Reality, and Its Examples
2:86.anchors:
- Root: غرر (Gh-R-R)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The core meaning is "an apparent trace or mark of a thing" (al-athar al-ẓāhir), from which derives "the blaze of a horse" (ghurrat al-faras). To deceive (gharra) is to strike one's heedlessness (ghirrah) and attain one's sought desire from him, as if folding a garment upon its original crease (ṭawāhu ʿalā gharrihi).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Ghurrah is heedlessness in wakefulness, and ghirār is heedlessness with drowsiness." Theologically, it is the soul's repose upon a false semblance (shubhah) that pleases the caprice (hawā), rendering one oblivious to the true state of affairs—as in {«mā gharraka bi-rabbika al-karīm»} (What deceived thee concerning thy Generous Lord?).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): "A gazelle in a moonlit night is called agharr" because it ventures out thinking it is day and is devoured by beasts—heedlessness in perception. Metaphorical (majāz): "A day agharr muḥajjal" (a white-browed, white-legged day) for intense heat, transferring the blaze of a horse to the day's visible intensity.
- Root: جهل (J-H-L)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "Jahila bihi" — to be ignorant of it; "jāhala ʿalā qawmihi" — to act foolishly/insolently against one's people. The pre-Islamic era is "al-jāhiliyyah al-jahlā'" (the utterly ignorant age).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Ignorance (jahl) is of three kinds: (1) the soul's emptiness of knowledge (this is the root); (2) believing a thing contrary to what it is; (3) doing a thing contrary to what it ought to be, whether one's belief is sound or corrupt. Ghurūr is a species of the second kind—a false belief arising from a corrupt semblance.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "Kafā bil-shakki jahlā" (Sufficient is doubt as ignorance). Metaphorical: "Istajhalat al-rīḥ al-ghuṣn" (The wind made the branch sway violently) — transferred from mental foolishness to physical agitation.
- Root: حدث (Ḥ-D-TH)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "Al-ḥudūth: the coming-to-be of a thing after it was not." "Al-ḥadath: the novel event." "Ḥaddatha: to speak/communicate."
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Ḥudūth is the existence of a thing after non-existence, whether accident or substance. Iḥdāth is bringing it into existence. The iḥdāth of substances belongs to God alone." The "ḥadīth" (report/speech) is so-called for its temporal novelty.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "Nazalat bihi ḥawādith al-dahr" (The vicissitudes of time befell him). Metaphorical: "Kāna ʿUmar muḥaddathan" (Umar was one inspired with true discernment) — as if he were spoken to (ḥudditha) by what he conjectured.
- Root: دنا (D-N-W)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "Danā fa-huwa dānin" — he drew near. "Al-dunyā" (the lower world) is so named because it is nearer (danat) and precedes the Hereafter.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Al-dunūw: proximity by essence or by judgment, used of place, time, and station." The "adnā" (lower/nearer) is contrasted with the greater and with the better: {«a-tastabdilūna alladhī huwa adnā billadhī huwa khayr»} (Will ye take the lower in exchange for what is better?).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "Huwa danī' min al-adniyā'" (He is base, of the base ones) — but this is the homonym danu'a (baseness), distinct from danā (nearness). The dunyā's "nearness" is its temporal immediacy versus the Hereafter's deferral.
- Sibawayh Rule: Bab al-faṣl bayna al-jār wa-al-majrūr (Prepositional Interposition) — The particle "bi" in {«wa-lā yaghurrannakum billāhi al-gharūr»} governs the deceiver (al-gharūr) as the agent of deception, while "billāh" (concerning God) is the object of the deception. The syntactic structure permits the deceiver to be named after the prepositional phrase, indicating that the deception is *about* God's attributes (His forbearance, His respite) — a grammatical subtlety showing the ghurūr deceives *by means of* false notions of God, not that God Himself deceives.
2:86.topic: Al-Ghazali on the journey of the soul, death, and the Hereafter, from 'Condemnation of the World'

2:86.arabic: وهؤلاء هم الذين اشتروا الحياة الدنيا بالآخرة فلا جرم لا يخفف عنهم العذاب ولا هم ينصرون وهم الذين لم يفهموا قوله تعالى المال والبنون زينة الحياة الدنيا والباقيات الصالحات خير عند ربك ثوابا وخير أملا فالعلم والحرية هي الباقيات الصالحات التي تبقى كمالا في النفس والمال والجاه هو الذي ينقضي على القرب وهو كما مثله الله تعالى حيث قال إنما مثل الحياة الدنيا كماء أنزلناه من السماء فاختلط به نبات الأرض الآية وقال تعالى واضرب لهم مثل الحياة الدنيا كماء أنزلناه من السماء إلى قوله فأصبح هشيما تذروه الرياح
2:86.english: Therefore, the perfections are three, if we count non-change through appetites and non-submission to them as a perfection—like the perfection of knowledge and the perfection of freedom. By "freedom" I mean non-enslavement to appetites and to willing worldly causes. The perfection of power for the servant is a path to acquiring the perfection of knowledge and the perfection of freedom, but he has no path to acquiring the perfection of power that endures after his death. For his power over the very substances of wealth and over subjugating hearts and bodies is cut off by death, whereas his knowledge and his freedom are not annihilated by death; rather, they both endure as perfection within him and as a means to nearness to God—may He be exalted.
2:86.section_title_en: On True Perfection: Knowledge and Freedom Over Power, Wealth, and Status
2:86.anchors:
- Root: قدر (q-d-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of measuring, determining, and enabling; power as capacity to bring about an effect.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): True power (qudrah) belongs absolutely to God alone; for humans, it is a relative capacity, never absolute, and is a means, not an end.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (haqiqah) power is God's; metaphorical (majaz) attribution of "power" to creatures is restricted and conditional, tied to specific acts.
- Root: علم (ʿ-l-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Knowledge as apprehension of a thing's reality; also traces and signs by which one is guided.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Knowledge (ʿilm) is the apprehension of a thing's true nature or the judgment of existence or non-existence regarding it; it is the enduring perfection of the soul.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "he knew" as direct awareness; metaphorical: "he knew" as perception or discernment of signs (maʿālim) leading to truth.
- Root: موت (m-w-t)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Death as the cessation of vital functions; also the state of being inanimate or lifeless.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Death is the opposite of life; in theological context, it marks the termination of worldly capacities but not of the soul's acquired knowledge or freedom.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical death; metaphorical: "death" of the heart through ignorance or enslavement to passion, and "revival" of the land through rain as a similitude for the fleeting world.
- Sibawayh Rule: Restriction and Focused Predication (الحصر والتقييد بإنما) — Used to confine true perfection exclusively to knowledge and freedom, negating it for power, wealth, and status.
2:86.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

2:152.arabic: أكبر فقال تعالى فاذكروني أذكركم واشكروا لي ولا تكفرون وقال تعالى ما يفعل الله بعذابكم إن شكرتم وآمنتم وقال تعالى وسنجزي الشاكرين وقال عز وجل إخبارا عن إبليس اللعين لأقعدن لهم صراطك المستقيم قيل هو طريق الشكر ولعلو رتبة الشكر طعن اللعين في الخلق فقال ولا تجد اكثرم شاكرين وقال تعالى وقليل من عبادي الشكور وقد قطع الله تعالى بالمزيد مع الشكر ولم يستثن فقال تعالى لئن شكرتم لأزيدنكم واستثنى في خمسة أشياء في الإغناء والإجابة والرزق والمغفرة والتوبة فقال تعالى فسوف يغنيكم الله من فضله إن شاء {وقال} في
2:152.english: So then, what we have mentioned concerning the treatment of patience (ṣabr) regarding whispered insinuation (waswās), regarding lust (shahwah), and regarding status (jāh) — annex this to what we have already set down concerning the canons of the paths of spiritual striving (mujāhadah) in the Book of the Discipline of the Soul (Kitāb Riyāḍat al-Nafs) from the Quarter of the Destroyers (rubʿ al-muhlikāt). Adopt it as your manual (dastūr) by which you may come to know the treatment of patience in all the categories which we have previously detailed; for the detailing of individual cases is prolix. Whoever observes gradual progression (tadrīj), patience will elevate him to a state wherein patience without it becomes as arduous as it once was with it — so his affairs become inverted, and what was once beloved to him becomes loathed, and what was once detested to him becomes a sweet, wholesome draught from which he cannot bear to be patient [in abstaining]. This is known only through experience (tajribah) and tasting (dhawq). It has an analogue in customary habits: for a boy is compelled to learning in the beginning by force, and so patience with play and patience with knowledge are both arduous for him — until, when his inner sight is opened and he finds intimacy with knowledge, the matter is inverted, and it becomes arduous for him to be patient in abstaining from knowledge, and to endure play. To this points what is narrated of one of the knowers (ʿārifīn) that he asked al-Shiblī: "Patience — which of its kinds is the most severe?" He said: "Patience in God (fī Allāh)." He said: "No." He said: "Patience for God (li-Allāh)." He said: "No." He said: "Patience with God (maʿa Allāh)." He said: "No." He said: "Then what?" He said: "Patience from God (ʿan Allāh)." At that al-Shiblī cried out a cry by which his soul nearly perished. And it has been said concerning the meaning of His saying, the Exalted: {«اصبروا وصابروا ورابطوا»} "Be patient, and vie in patience, and be steadfast" (Q. 3:200): "Be patient in God, vie in patience by God, and be steadfast with God." And it was said: "Patience for God is sufficiency (ghināʾ); patience by God is endurance (baqāʾ); patience with God is fidelity (wafāʾ); and patience from God is abandonment (jafāʾ)." And it was said concerning its meaning:
2:152.section_title_en: The Revival of the Religious Sciences — Section 972: On Patience (al-Sabr) and the Commencement of Gratitude (al-Shukr)
2:152.anchors:
- Root: صبر (ṣ-b-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of restraint and withholding; al-Khalil notes its application to holding back an animal from fodder, and to enduring constraint.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الصبر: الإمساك في ضيق" — the withholding of the self in constriction; it is a general term whose specific names (shajāʿah, ḥilm, etc.) vary by context, and its opposite is al-jazaʿ (panic/vexation).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): "صبرت على ما أكره. وصبرت عما أحب" — enduring what is disliked and restraining from what is loved. Metaphorical (majāz): "صبرت يمينه" — binding an oath strenuously; "أصبر على الضرب من الأرض" — more enduring than the earth.
- Root: شكر (sh-k-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The root denotes manifestation and fullness; al-Ayn links it to an overflowing udder (shukrā).
