2:157.arabic: أمور لم يجمعها لغيرهم فقال تعالى أولئك عليهم صلوات من ربهم ورحمة وأولئك هم المهتدون فالهدى والرحمة والصلوات مجموعة للصابرين واستقصاء جميع الآيات في مقام الصبر يطول وأما الأخبار فقد قال صلى الله عليه وسلم الصبر نصف الإيمان (1) على ما سيأتي وجه كونه نصفا وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم من أقل ما أوتيتم اليقين وعزيمة الصبر ومن أعطي حظه منهما لم يبال بما فاته من قيام الليل وصيام النهار ولأن تصبروا على ما أنتم عليه أحب إلي من أن يوافيني كل امرىء منكم بمثل عمل جميعكم ولكني أخاف أن تفتح عليكم الدنيا بعدي فينكر بعضكم بعضا وينكركم أهل السماء عند ذلك
2:157.english: Allah — exalted be He — has described the patient (al-ṣābirīn) with attributes, and He mentioned patience (al-ṣabr) in the Qur’an in upwards of seventy places. He attached most of the degrees and goods to patience, making them its fruit. For He said — majestic is His utterance: {«وَجَعَلْنَا مِنْهُمْ أَئِمَّةً يَهْدُونَ بِأَمْرِنَا لَمَّا صَبَرُوا»} — “And We made from among them imams guiding by Our command, when they were patient” (Q 32:24). And He said — exalted be He: {«وَتَمَّتْ كَلِمَتُ رَبِّكَ الْحُسْنَىٰ عَلَىٰ بَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ بِمَا صَبَرُوا»} — “And the good word of your Lord was fulfilled upon the Children of Israel, because they were patient” (Q 7:137). And He said — exalted be He: {«وَلَنَجْزِيَنَّ الَّذِينَ صَبَرُوا أَجْرَهُم بِأَحْسَنِ مَا كَانُوا يَعْمَلُونَ»} — “And We shall surely recompense those who were patient their wage according to the best of what they used to do” (Q 16:96). And He said — exalted be He: {«أُولَٰئِكَ يُؤْتَوْنَ أَجْرَهُم مَّرَّتَيْنِ بِمَا صَبَرُوا»} — “Those shall be given their wage twice, because they were patient” (Q 28:54). And He said — exalted be He: {«إِنَّمَا يُوَفَّى الصَّابِرُونَ أَجْرَهُم بِغَيْرِ حِسَابٍ»} — “Only the patient shall be paid their wage without reckoning” (Q 39:10). Thus there is no act of nearness (qurbah) whose wage is not meted out by measure and account — except patience. And because fasting (al-ṣawm) is of patience, and it is half of patience, Allah — exalted be He — said: “Fasting is Mine, and I recompense it” — so He attributed it to Himself, to the exclusion of all other acts of worship. And He promised the patient that He is with them, saying — exalted be He: {«وَاصْبِرُوا إِنَّ اللَّهَ مَعَ الصَّابِرِينَ»} — “And be patient; indeed Allah is with the patient” (Q 8:46). And He made victory contingent upon patience, saying — exalted be He: {«بَلَىٰ إِن تَصْبِرُوا وَتَتَّقُوا وَيَأْتُوكُم مِّن فَوْرِهِمْ هَٰذَا يُمْدِدْكُمْ رَبُّكُم بِخَمْسَةِ آلَافٍ مِّنَ الْمَلَائِكَةِ مُسَوِّمِينَ»} — “Yes, if you are patient and God-fearing, and they come upon you in their rush, your Lord will reinforce you with five thousand marked angels” (Q 3:125). And He gathered for the patient things He gathered for no others, saying — exalted be He: {«أُولَٰئِكَ عَلَيْهِمْ صَلَوَاتٌ مِّن رَّبِّهِمْ وَرَحْمَةٌ وَأُولَٰئِكَ هُمُ الْمُهْتَدُونَ»} — “Those — upon them are blessings from their Lord, and mercy; and those — they are the rightly guided” (Q 2:157). So guidance, mercy, and blessings are all gathered for the patient. And to exhaust all the verses concerning the station of patience would be lengthy.
2:157.section_title_en: The Virtue of Patience (Ṣabr) — Its Excellence in the Qur’an, Sunnah, and Reports of the Salaf
2:157.anchors:
- Root: صبر (Ṣ-B-R)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning is “to restrain, to hold back, to bind firmly” — as in holding an animal by its halter or confining someone against departure.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Patience is “the self’s restraint upon what reason and Sacred Law require, or from what they require it to abstain from.” It is a generic term whose specific names vary by context: in calamity it is ṣabr (opposed to jazaʿ); in battle it is courage (shajāʿah); in vexation it is forbearance.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): “I bore patiently what I disliked, and I refrained patiently from what I loved.” Metaphorical (majāz): “His right hand was made to swear patiently” (i.e., bound by an emphatic oath), and “this tree is patient against cold” (i.e., unaffected by it).
- Root: عله (ʿ-L-H) — [Noted as a rare root; no direct bearing on this passage’s core terms, but included per lexical apparatus.]
- Root: ايم (A-Y-M) — [Noted as a rare root; no direct bearing on this passage’s core terms, but included per lexical apparatus.]
- Root: نفس (N-F-S)
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The self (nafs) as the locus of volitional restraint — patience is an act of the nafs holding itself back, distinguishing it from mere physical endurance.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: “a precious thing” (nafīs). Metaphorical: “he poured out his soul” (i.e., his blood), and “everything that has no flowing soul does not defile water.”
- Sibawayh Rule: Restriction and Focused Predication (Bāb al-Ḥaṣr wa al-Taqyīd bi-innamā) — Governing the exclusive clause {«إِنَّمَا يُوَفَّى الصَّابِرُونَ أَجْرَهُم بِغَيْرِ حِسَابٍ»}, where innamā restricts the reward-without-account solely to the patient, and {«الصَّوْمُ لِي وَأَنَا أَجْزِي بِهِ»}, where the predicate is focused to Allah alone.

2:212.arabic: {وقال} فيكشف ما تدعون إليه إن شاء {وقال} يرزق من يشاء بغير حساب {وقال} ويغفر ما دون ذلك لمن يشاء {وقال} ويتوب الله على من يشاء وهو خلق من أخلاق الربوبية إذ قال تعالى والله شكور حليم وقد جعل الله الشكر مفتاح كلام أهل الجنة فقال تعالى وقالوا الحمد لله الذي صدقناه وعده {وقال} وآخر دعواهم أن الحمد لله رب العالمين
2:212.english: So then, what we have mentioned concerning the treatment of patience (ṣabr) regarding whispered insinuation (waswās), regarding lust (shahwah), and regarding status (jāh) — annex this to what we have already set down concerning the canons of the paths of spiritual striving (mujāhadah) in the Book of the Discipline of the Soul (Kitāb Riyāḍat al-Nafs) from the Quarter of the Destroyers (rubʿ al-muhlikāt). Adopt it as your manual (dastūr) by which you may come to know the treatment of patience in all the categories which we have previously detailed; for the detailing of individual cases is prolix. Whoever observes gradual progression (tadrīj), patience will elevate him to a state wherein patience without it becomes as arduous as it once was with it — so his affairs become inverted, and what was once beloved to him becomes loathed, and what was once detested to him becomes a sweet, wholesome draught from which he cannot bear to be patient [in abstaining]. This is known only through experience (tajribah) and tasting (dhawq). It has an analogue in customary habits: for a boy is compelled to learning in the beginning by force, and so patience with play and patience with knowledge are both arduous for him — until, when his inner sight is opened and he finds intimacy with knowledge, the matter is inverted, and it becomes arduous for him to be patient in abstaining from knowledge, and to endure play. To this points what is narrated of one of the knowers (ʿārifīn) that he asked al-Shiblī: "Patience — which of its kinds is the most severe?" He said: "Patience in God (fī Allāh)." He said: "No." He said: "Patience for God (li-Allāh)." He said: "No." He said: "Patience with God (maʿa Allāh)." He said: "No." He said: "Then what?" He said: "Patience from God (ʿan Allāh)." At that al-Shiblī cried out a cry by which his soul nearly perished. And it has been said concerning the meaning of His saying, the Exalted: {«اصبروا وصابروا ورابطوا»} "Be patient, and vie in patience, and be steadfast" (Q. 3:200): "Be patient in God, vie in patience by God, and be steadfast with God." And it was said: "Patience for God is sufficiency (ghināʾ); patience by God is endurance (baqāʾ); patience with God is fidelity (wafāʾ); and patience from God is abandonment (jafāʾ)." And it was said concerning its meaning:
2:212.section_title_en: The Revival of the Religious Sciences — Section 972: On Patience (al-Sabr) and the Commencement of Gratitude (al-Shukr)

2:245.arabic: بعبادة القرض فقال من ذا الذي يقرض الله قرضا حسنا فإن قلت قولك إن بقاء النسل والنفس محبوب يوهم أن فناءها مكروه عند الله وهو فرق بين الموت والحياة بالإضافة إلى إرادة الله تعالى ومعلوم أن الكل بمشيئة الله وأن الله غني عن العالمين فمن أين يتميز عنده موتهم عن حياتهم أو بقاؤهم عن فنائهم فأعلم أن هذه الكلمة حق أريد بها باطل فإن ما ذكرناه لا ينافي إضافة الكائنات كلها إلى إرادة الله خيرها وشرها ونفعها وضرها ولكن المحبة والكراهية يتضادان وكلاهما لا يضادان الإرادة فرب مراد مكروه ورب مراد محبوب فالمعاصي مكروهة و
2:245.english: وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم: "لا يلقى الله أحد بذنب أعظم من جهالة أهله."

2:247.arabic: ممتنا بذلك {وزاده بسطة في العلم والجسم} ولسنا نعني بالجمال ما يحرك الشهوة فإن ذلك أنوثة وإنما نعني به ارتفاع القامة على الاستقامة مع الاعتدال في اللحم وتناسب الأعضاء وتناصف خلقة الوجه بحيث لا تنبو الطباع عن النظر إليه فإن قلت فقد أدخلت المال والجاه والنسب والأهل والولد في حيز النعم وقد ذم الله تعالى المال والجاه وكذا رسول صلى الله عليه وسلم حديث ذم المال والجاه أخرجه الترمذي من حديث كعب بن مالك ما ذئبان جائعان أرسلا في غنم بأفسد لها من حب المال والشرف لدينه وقد تقدم في ذم المال وا
2:247.english: If you say: "Is the nobility of one's clan and the honor of one's family among the blessings (ni'am) or not?" — I say: Yes. For this reason, he, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "The leaders (a'immah) are from Quraysh" (1). And for this reason, he, peace and blessings be upon him, was of the most noble of people in root (arumah) within the lineage of Adam, upon him peace. Regarding the hadith "The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, was of the most noble of people in arumah" — al-arumah means the origin (asl); this is well known. Muslim narrated from the hadith of Wathilah ibn al-Asqa', raised to the Prophet (marfu'): "Indeed, Allah chose Kinanah from the descendants of Isma'il, and chose Quraysh from Kinanah, and chose from Quraysh the Banu Hashim, and chose me from the Banu Hashim." In the narration of al-Tirmidhi: "Indeed, Allah chose Isma'il from the descendants of Ibrahim." And from him (al-Tirmidhi) is the hadith of al-'Abbas — which he deemed good (hasan) — and of Ibn 'Abbas and al-Muttalib ibn Rabi'ah — which he authenticated (sahih) — and of al-Muttalib ibn Abi Wada'ah — which he deemed good — : "Indeed, Allah created the creation and made me from the best of them." In the hadith of Ibn 'Abbas: "What is the matter with people who debase their origin? By Allah, I am the most excellent of them in origin and the best of them in standing." And he, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Choose for your sperm the suitable (akfa') [women]" (2). The hadith "Seek good from those with beautiful faces" was narrated by Abu Ya'la from the narration of Isma'il ibn 'Ayyash, from Khayrah bint Muhammad ibn Thabit ibn Siba', from her mother 'A'ishah — but Khayrah and her mother, I do not know their condition (i.e., reliability). Ibn Hibban narrated it from another chain among the weak narrators, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Shu'ab from the hadith of Ibn 'Umar; it has chains, all of them weak. // And 'Umar, may Allah the Exalted be pleased with him, said: "When you send a messenger, seek him to be beautiful of face and beautiful of name." And the jurists (fuqaha') said: "When the ranks of those praying are equal, then the most beautiful of them in face is the most deserving of leading the prayer (imamah)." And Allah the Exalted said, bestowing this as a favor: {وَزَادَهُ بَسْطَةً فِي الْعِلْمِ وَالْجِسْمِ} [And increased him in abundance in knowledge and body] (Al-Baqarah: 247). And we do not mean by beauty that which stirs lust — for that is effeminacy (unuthah) — but rather we mean tallness of stature with uprightness, along with moderation of flesh, proportionality of limbs, and symmetry of the facial constitution, such that natural temperaments do not recoil from looking upon it.
2:247.section_title_en: On Nobility of Lineage, Beauty, Wealth, and Status as Divine Blessings — With the Parable of the Serpent and the Pearl-Diver
2:247.anchors:
- Root: كرم (karuma)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Generosity, honor, nobility of origin; "الكريم" as the noble one whose lineage is pure and whose character is exalted.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Nobility (karam) as an ontological elevation in rank, whether by lineage (hasab) or by virtue (hasanah), aligning with divine selection (istifa').
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical and moral nobility. Metaphorical: "كرم الله فلانا" — divine ennoblement through choice and favor.
- Root: نعم (ni'mah)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "النعمة: الحالة الحسنة" — a state of well-being; "النعماء" abundance; "أنعم" to bestow favor.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Ni'mah as the good state (al-halat al-hasanah), both sensory and intellectual; divine blessings are uncountable {وَإِن تَعُدُّوا نِعْمَتَ اللَّهِ لَا تُحْصُوهَا} [Ibrahim: 34].
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "جلت نعمة الله" — manifest favor. Metaphorical: "خفت نعامتهم" — their blessings departed, showing ni'mah as a dynamic, transferable reality.
- Root: مثل (mathala)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Likeness, similitude, example; "المثل" as the illustrative paradigm.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "المثل: القول السائر المشتمل على تشبيه" — a proverb or parable conveying a hidden truth through analogy.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical resemblance. Metaphorical: the parable (mathal) as a vehicle for abstract moral instruction, as in the Qur'anic "ضرب الله مثلا".
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — Used in the citation {إِنَّمَا أَمْوَالُكُمْ وَأَوْلَادُكُمْ فِتْنَةٌ} to restrict wealth and children to the category of trial, not absolute evil, requiring contextual specification (takhsis).

2:247.arabic: يهودي يخبرني عن التوراة فقدم علي اليهودي من سفر فقلت إن الله قد بعث فينا نبيا فدعانا إلى الإسلام فأسلمنا وقد أنزل علينا كتابا مصدقا للتوراة فقال اليهودي صدقت ولكنكم لا تستطيعون أن تقوموا بما جاءكم به إنا نجد نعته ونعت أمته في التوراة إنه لا يحل لامريء أن يخرج من عتبة بابه وفي قلبه سخيمة على أخيه المسلم ومن ذلك أن يسكت عن إفشاء سره الذي استودعه وله أن ينكره وإن كان كاذبا فليس الصدق واجبا في كل مقام فإنه كما يجوز للرجل أن يخفي عيوب نفسه وأسراره وإن احتاج إلى الكذب فله أن يفعل ذلك في حق أخيه فإن أخاه نازل منزلته وهما كشخص وا
2:247.english: Anas said: "The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) never confronted anyone with something he disliked." — The ḥadīth of Anas: "He never confronted anyone with something he disliked" — narrated by Abū Dāwūd, al-Tirmidhī in al-Shamāʾil, and al-Nasāʾī in al-Yawm wa al-Laylah with a weak chain.
2:247.section_title_en: On Silence Regarding the Faults of Brothers — The Rights of Brotherhood (Section 419)
2:247.anchors:
- Root: سكت (s-k-t)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of silence, refraining from speech; al-sukūt is the cessation of utterance, whether by tongue or by heart.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance — silence as a positive act of restraint (imsāk) that guards the tongue from what Allah has forbidden, paralleling the heart's silence from evil suspicion.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) — refraining from audible speech; Metaphorical (majāz) — the heart's silence, i.e., refraining from passing judgment on a brother's actions when a good interpretation is possible.
- Root: غيب (gh-y-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: That which is absent or hidden; ghībah (backbiting) is mentioning a brother in his absence with what he dislikes.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Ghībah is a violation of the unseen honor (ʿirḍ) of the Muslim, which the Law has rendered inviolable like blood and property.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — speaking of the absent; Metaphorical — the heart's backbiting (sūʾ al-ẓann), i.e., conceiving evil of a brother without certain knowledge.
- Root: ظن (ẓ-n-n)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Doubt, suspicion, or belief not founded on certainty; ẓann is the inclination of the soul toward one of two possibilities.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In the Qur'anic context, "avoid much suspicion" {«إِنَّ بَعْضَ الظَّنِّ إِثْمٌ»} — the blameworthy suspicion is that which attributes evil to a believer without a decisive sign (amārah).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — conjecture; Metaphorical — the heart's ghībah, for just as the tongue can wound, so too can the heart's presumption.
- Root: ستر (s-t-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To cover, conceal; sitr is the act of veiling a fault or defect.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Allah's attribute al-Sattār — He who veils the sins of His servants; the believer's emulation of this attribute is a mark of perfected faith.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — physical covering; Metaphorical — concealing another's moral faults, as the Prophet said: "Whoever conceals the fault of a brother, Allah conceals his fault in this world and the next."
- Sibawayh Rule: Restriction and specification (al-ḥaṣr wa al-taqyīd) — the conditional clauses (law, idhā) and exceptions (illā) governing when silence is obligatory versus when speech becomes mandatory (amr bi-l-maʿrūf).
2:247.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Duties of Brotherhood'

2:251.arabic: بإفساد شخص واحد وأشخاص ولولا دفع الله الناس بعضهم ببعض لفسدت الأرض وإن الله يؤيد هذا الدين بأقوام لا خلاق لهم
2:251.english: If you say: "When, then, is it sound for him to occupy himself with admonishing people?" — I say: When he has no aim except their guidance for the sake of God most high, and he would wish to find one who aids him, or that they should be guided by themselves; and his hope for their praise and their wealth is entirely cut off; and their praise and their blame become equal to him — so he does not care about their blame when God praises him, nor does he rejoice in their praise when it is not accompanied by the praise of God most high; and he looks upon them as he looks upon masters (sādāt) and upon beasts.
2:251.section_title_en: On the Hidden Corruption of the Preacher's Intention: The Love of Leadership and the Test of Sincerity
2:251.anchors:
- Root: نفس (n-f-s)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The self, soul, or spirit; that which breathes and desires; the seat of volition and inclination.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-nafs denotes the immaterial reality of the human being (al-rūḥ) and, in theological contexts, the self as the locus of blameworthy attributes (hawā) versus the tranquil soul; it is that which must be disciplined.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): the soul as animate essence; metaphorical (majāz): "he poured out his nafs" i.e., his blood, and "a nafs struck him" i.e., the evil eye — indicating the soul's susceptibility to hidden afflictions.
- Root: قلب (q-l-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To turn, overturn, or flip a thing from one state to another; the heart as that which is perpetually fluctuating between states.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Taqlīb is the constant turning and redirecting of a thing; the heart (qalb) is so named for its incessant oscillation — hence "O Turner of hearts, make my heart firm upon Your religion."
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: turning a garment or object over; metaphorical (majāz): "the teacher turned the boys" i.e., dismissed them, and "he turned the matter over" i.e., examined it — thus the heart's turning toward or away from sincerity.
- Root: دنا (d-n-w)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Nearness in place, time, or rank; the lower world (al-dunyā) as that which is nearer and lower.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-dunūw is proximity by essence or by judgment; used of spatial, temporal, and station-based closeness — as in {«ثُمَّ دَنَا فَتَدَلَّىٰ»} (Then he drew near and descended) [al-Najm 53:8].
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical closeness; metaphorical: closeness in honor or station — here, the preacher's craving for proximity to people's hearts (al-riyāsah).
- Sibawayh Rule: Bāb al-ḥaṣr wa al-taqyīd bi-innamā (Restriction and Specification with innamā) — used to isolate the true motive from the apparent one, e.g., "You only do this so that..." — a restrictive clause exposing the inward cause.
2:251.topic: Al-Ghazali on constant remembrance of God and contemplative invocations, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

2:251.arabic: وقال في قوله تعالى {ولولا دفع الله الناس بعضهم ببعض} قال بالرغبة والرهبة والحياء والمداراة وقالت عائشة رضي الله عنها استأذن رجل على رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال ائذنوا له فبئس رجل العشيرة هو فلما دخل ألان له القول حتى أن له عنده منزلة فلما خرج قلت له لما دخل قلت الذي قلت ثم ألنت له القول فقال يا عائشة إن شر الناس منزلة عند الله يوم القيامة من تركه الناس اتقاء فحشه (4) وفي الخبر ما وقى الرجل به عرضه فهو له صدقة (5) وفي الأثر خالطوا الناس بأعمالكم وزايلوهم بالقلوب وقال محمد بن الحن
2:251.english: A man defended him, and the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: "Whoever defends the honor of his brother shall have it as a shield for him against the Fire." (1)
2:251.anchors:
- Root: رد (r-d-d)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To return, repel, defend, avert; al-radd ʿan al-ʿirḍ is to repel defamation from one's honor
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Defense against false accusation; the theological nuance of divine recompense (al-mukāfaʾah) for defending a brother's honor
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal repulsion of physical harm extended metaphorically to verbal defense of honor (ḥaqīqah vs. majāz)
- Root: عطس (ʿ-t-s)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Sneezing; al-tashmīt is the invocation of mercy upon the sneezer
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The sneeze is attributed to God (min Allāh) as a sign of divine favor, while yawning is attributed to Satan
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): The response "yarḥamukallāh" is a supplication, not an assertion — distinguishing literal invocation from mere congratulation
- Root: عاد (ʿ-w-d)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To visit repeatedly; al-ʿiyādah is the visitation of the sick
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Returning to someone in his affliction; the reward is measured by the intensity of compassion shown
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): The "return" (ʿawd) is literal in visitation, but the reward is spiritual — a metaphorical extension of recompense
- Root: شيع (sh-y-ʿ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To accompany, follow; al-tashyīʿ is the funeral procession
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Following the bier with the intention of honoring the deceased and taking admonition (al-iʿtibār)
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): The qīrāṭ is a measure of reward — metaphorical weight, not literal coin
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Conditional Protasis (Bāb al-sharṭ) — The construction "man ... fa-..." (whoever does X, then Y) establishes a causal nexus requiring the apodosis to be a new sentence, often carrying the force of divine decree.

##
2:251.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'Duties of Brotherhood'

2:264.arabic: الوظيفة الخامسة أن لا يفسد صدقته بالمن والأذى قال الله تعالى لا تبطلوا صدقاتكم بالمن والأذى واختلفوا في حقيقة المن والأذى فقيل المن أن يذكرها والأذى أن يظهرها وقال سفيان من من فسدت صدقته فقيل له كيف المن فقال أن يذكره ويتحدث به وقيل المن أن يستخدمه بالعطاء والأذى أن يعيره بالفقر وقيل المن أن يتكبر عليه لأجل عطائه والأذى أن ينتهره أو يوبخه بالمسألة وقد قال صلى الله عليه وسلم لا يقبل الله صدقة منان (2) وعندي أن المن له أصل ومغرس وهو من أحوال القلب وصفاته ثم يتفرع عليه أحوال ظاهرة على اللسان والجوارح فأصله أن يرى نفسه محسنا إليه ومنعما عليه
2:264.english: A group of the Followers (tābiʿūn) held that there are rights in wealth beyond the zakat — among them al-Nakhaʿī, al-Shaʿbī, ʿAṭāʾ, and Mujāhid. Al-Shaʿbī said, after being asked, "Is there a right in wealth beyond the zakat?": "Yes. Have you not heard His saying — mighty and majestic is He: {«وَآتَى الْمَالَ عَلَىٰ حُبِّهِ ذَوِي الْقُرْبَىٰ»} 'And gives wealth, despite his love for it, to relatives' (2:177)?" They also adduced His saying — mighty and majestic is He: {«وَمِمَّا رَزَقْنَاهُمْ يُنفِقُونَ»} 'And from what We have provided them, they spend' (2:3), and His saying — exalted is He: {«وَأَنفِقُوا مِن مَّا رَزَقْنَاكُم»} 'And spend from what We have provided you' (2:254). They claimed that this is not abrogated by the verse of zakat; rather, it falls within the right of a Muslim upon a Muslim. Its meaning is that it is incumbent upon the affluent one, whenever he finds a needy person, to remove his need — over and above the zakat wealth.
2:264.section_title_en: The Second Division: Those Who Guard Their Wealth Awaiting Seasons of Need — On the Inner Meanings of Zakat (Section 173)
2:264.anchors:
- Root: ف-ق-ر (f-q-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of neediness, poverty; the hollow of the spine (faqār) — that which is structurally weak and dependent.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Poverty (faqr) has four senses: (1) essential neediness before Allah, universal to all creatures; (2) lack of possessions; (3) [the third and fourth senses as elaborated in the full lexicon entry].
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (haqīqah): one who lacks wealth. Metaphorical (majāz): "the poverty of speech" (fuqar al-kalām) — its subtle points, likened to ornaments shaped like vertebrae.
- Root: ص-د-ق (ṣ-d-q)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Truthfulness in speech; giving (ṣadaqah) as the outward verification of inward faith.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Ṣidq (truth) and kidhb (falsehood) are originally in speech — statement of what is, or what will be. By extension, ṣadaqah is that which verifies the truthfulness of one's claim to faith through expenditure.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: truthful speech. Metaphorical: "a horse with true running" (dhū miṣdaq fī al-jary) — that which verifies its excellence through action. Thus charity verifies the giver's sincerity.
- Root: م-ن-ن (m-n-n)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The bestowal of a favor; reproaching another by reminding them of one's gift (al-mann).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): [As elaborated in the full lexicon entry on the heart's self-perception of superiority over the recipient.]
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: a heavy weight; a favor. Metaphorical: the act of counting one's favors over another — a corrosion of the gift's value.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد (Restriction & Specification) — governing the precise scope of obligation (farḍ kifāyah) versus supererogatory merit (faḍl), and the restriction of "rights in wealth" (ḥuqūq fī al-māl) beyond the obligatory zakat.
2:264.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

2:264.arabic: وقد قال الله تعالى يا أيها الذين آمنوا أنفقوا من طيبات ما كسبتم ومما أخرجنا لكم من الأرض ولا تيمموا الخبيث منه تنفقون ولستم بآخذيه إلا أن تغمضوا فيه أي لا تأخذوه إلا مع كراهية وحياء وهو معنى الإغماض فلا تؤثروا به ربكم وفي الخبر سبق درهم مائة ألف درهم (3) وذلك بأن يخرجه الإنسان وهو من أحل ماله وأجوده فيصدر ذلك عن الرضا والفرح بالبذل وقد يخرج مائة ألف درهم مما يكره من ماله فيدل ذلك على أنه ليس يؤثر الله عز وجل بشيء مما يحبه وبذلك ذم الله تعالى قوما جعلوا لله ما يكرهون فقال تعال
2:264.english: The heart is not treated save with the compound electuary (maʿjūn) of knowledge and works. And this condition among the conditions of almsgiving runs in the same course as humility (al-khushūʿ) runs in the prayer. This is established by his saying — may Allah bless him and grant him peace: "A man has nothing of his prayer save that of which he was conscious." And this is like his saying — may Allah bless him and grant him peace: "Allah does not accept the charity of the one who bestows it with reproach (al-mannān)." And like His saying — Exalted is He: {«لا تبطلوا صدقاتكم بالمن والأذى»} ("Do not nullify your charities by reproach and injury"). As for the legal opinion (fatwā) of the jurist that the alms fall in their proper place and that one's liability is discharged without this condition — that is another discussion, and we have already pointed to its meaning in the Book of Prayer.
2:264.section_title_en: The Inner Conditions of Charity — Section 175 (From The Revival of the Religious Sciences, Book of the Mysteries of Almsgiving)
2:264.anchors:
- Root: قلب (q-l-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "To turn, overturn, transform a thing from one state to another; to rotate, to flip"
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "قلب الشيء: تصريفه وصرفه عن وجه إلى وجه" — the heart is so named because of its constant turning and transformation between states
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "قلب الشيء قلبا: حوله عن وجهه" (to turn a thing from its face). Metaphorical: "رجل قلب حول: يقلب الأمور ويحتال" — one who turns matters over and manages them; "قلبوا لك الأمور" (they turned matters against you)
- Root: وجل (w-j-l)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "Fear, dread, apprehension that strikes the heart"
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الوجل: استشعار الخوف" — the sensing of fear; cited in {«إنما المؤمنون الذين إذا ذكر الله وجلت قلوبهم»}
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "رجل وجل، وقوم وجال" — a fearful man, a fearful people; "وفي قلبه وجل" — in his heart is dread
- Root: عجب (ʿ-j-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "Wonder, amazement; self-admiration, vanity"
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Self-admiration (al-ʿujb) is a destructive spiritual ailment that nullifies deeds
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: wonder at something extraordinary. Metaphorical: self-conceit regarding one's own acts of obedience
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد (Restriction & Focused Predication) — governing the precise limitation of general categories (al-ṣifāt al-khāṣṣah within al-aṣnāf al-thamāniyyah) and the conditional structure of acceptance

##
2:264.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Duties of Brotherhood'

2:264.arabic: الأول تعجيل الطعام فذلك من إكرام الضيف وقد قال صلى الله عليه وسلم من كان يؤمن بالله واليوم الآخر فليكرم ضيفه (1) ومهما حضر الأكثرون وغاب واحد أو اثنان وتأخروا عن الوقت الموعود فحق الحاضر في التعجيل أولى من حق أولئك في التأخير إلا أن يكون المتأخر فقيرا أو ينكسر قلبه بذلك فلا بأس في التأخير وأحد المعنيين في قوله تعالى {هل أتاك حديث ضيف إبراهيم المكرمين} أنهم أكرموا بتعجيل الطعام إليهم دل عليه قوله تعالى {فما لبث أن جاء بعجل حنيذ} وقوله {فراغ إلى أهله فجاء بعجل سمين} والروغان الذهاب بسرعة وقيل في خفية وقيل جاء بفخذ من لحم وإنما سمي ع
2:264.english: The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Do not burden your guest so that you make him hate you, for whoever hates his guest has hated Allah, and whoever hates Allah, Allah hates him."
2:264.section_title_en: The Etiquettes of Hospitality: Invitation, Response, Attendance, and the Serving of Food — Section 290 of The Revival of the Religious Sciences
2:264.anchors:
- Root: ضيف (ḍ-y-f)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning is "to incline, to lean toward." The guest (al-ḍayf) is one who inclines toward you, alighting as a visitor; the root carries the sense of leaning or bending.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The guest is "one who inclines to you, alighting with you"; hospitality (al-ḍiyāfah) became customary in the sense of receiving such a one. The word is originally a verbal noun, hence one and many are equal in most usage.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): "ḍāfa ilayhi: he inclined toward him"; "ḍāfat al-shams: the sun inclined toward setting." Metaphorical (majāz): "aḍāfa ilayhi amran: he attributed a matter to him, leaning it upon him"; "al-muḍāf: the one constrained, hemmed in, in distress."
- Sibawayh Rule: Restriction and Focused Predication (al-ḥaṣr wa al-taqyīd bi-innamā) — governing the Prophet's statement "innamā hādhihi al-akhlāq bi-yad Allāh" (these morals are only in the hand of Allah), where innamā restricts the attribution of moral character exclusively to divine bestowal.
2:264.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'Mysteries of Prayer'

3:13.arabic: لما رأيت ابني يتعثر لم أملك نفسي أن أخذته ففي ذلك عبرة لأولي الأبصار فالرجل كل الرجل من يصبر على العافية ومعنى الصبر عليها أن لا يركن إليها ويعلم أن كل ذلك مستودع عنده وعسى أن يسترجع على القرب وأن لا يرسل نفسه في الفرح بها ولا ينهمك في التنعم واللذة واللهو واللعب وأن يرعى حقوق الله في ماله بالإنفاق وفي بدنه ببذل المعونة للخلق وفي لسانه ببذل الصدق وكذلك في سائر ما أنعم الله به عليه وهذا الصبر متصل بالشكر فلا يتم إلا بالقيام بحق الشكر كما سيأتي وإنما كان الصبر على السراء أشد لأنه مقرون بالقدرة ومن العص
3:13.english: The first kind is that which accords with caprice (al-hawā) — namely, sound health and well-being, wealth and status, the abundance of kinsfolk, the expanse of means, the multitude of followers and helpers, and all the pleasures of this world. How greatly the servant stands in need of patience over these very things! For if he does not restrain his soul (nafsahu) from letting loose toward them, from reposing in them, and from plunging into their permissible pleasures, that drives him to insolence (al-baṭar) and transgression (al-ṭughyān) — for indeed {verily man doth transgress when he sees himself self-sufficient} {«إن الإنسان ليطغى أن رآه استغنى»}. Hence one of the knowers of God (al-ʿārifīn) said: "Affliction — the believer can bear it; but well-being — none bears it save the veracious (al-ṣiddīq)." And Sahl said: "Patience over well-being is more severe than patience over affliction." When the doors of this world were opened upon the Companions — may God be well pleased with them — they said: "We were tried with the trial of adversity (fitnat al-ḍarrāʾ) and we bore it patiently; and we were tried with the trial of prosperity (fitnat al-sarrāʾ) and we did not bear it patiently." For this reason God — mighty and majestic — warned His servants against the trial of wealth, spouse, and child, saying — exalted is He: {O you who believe! Let not your wealth nor your children divert you from the remembrance of God} {«يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا تلهكم أموالكم ولا أولادكم عن ذكر الله»}. And He said — mighty and majestic: {Indeed, among your spouses and your children there is an enemy unto you, so beware of them} {«إن من أزواجكم وأولادكم عدوا لكم فاحذروهم»}. And the Prophet — peace be upon him — said: "The child is a cause of miserliness (mubakhkhilah), a cause of cowardice (mujabinah), a cause of grief (muḥzinah)." When he — peace be upon him — looked upon his son al-Ḥasan — may God be well pleased with him — stumbling in his shirt, he descended from the pulpit and embraced him, then said: {God has spoken truly} {«صدق الله»} — {Indeed, your wealth and your children are a trial} {«إنما أموالكم وأولادكم فتنة»} — "When I saw my son stumbling, I could not control myself (lam amlik nafsī) from taking him up." In that is a lesson for those of insight. So the man — the complete man — is he who bears patience over well-being. And the meaning of patience over it is that he does not repose in it, and knows that all of it is but a trust (mustawdaʿ) deposited with him, that it may well be reclaimed at any near moment; and that he does not release his soul to rejoice in it, nor plunge into comfort, pleasure, play, and amusement; and that he observes the rights of God in his wealth by spending, in his body by expending aid to creation, in his tongue by expending truthfulness (al-ṣidq) — and likewise in all the rest of what God has bestowed upon him.
3:13.section_title_en: On Patience in Prosperity and Adversity — Section 963
3:13.anchors:
- Root: صبر (ṣ-b-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of restraint and holding back; al-Farahidi notes "صبر على قليه" (endurance upon hardship).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الصبر: الإمساك في ضيق... حبس النفس على ما يقتضيه العقل والشرع، أو عما يقتضيان حبسها عنه" — Patience is the soul's restraint upon what reason and Law require, or from what they require restraining it; its names vary by context (shajāʿah in battle, etc.).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): "صبرت على ما أكره. وصبرت عما أحب" — patience over the disliked and patience away from the beloved. Metaphorical (majāz): "هو أصبر على الضرب من الأرض" — extreme endurance likened to earth's impassivity.
- Root: نفس (n-f-s)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The self, soul, or spirit; that which one guards and restrains.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "النفس: الروح" and in divine attribution, "نفسه: ذاته" — the self as the locus of volition and desire.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "نفس" as the animate self; metaphorical: "دفق نفسه أي دمه" — extended to blood/life.
- Root: ولد (w-l-d)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Offspring, child; al-Farahidi notes singular/plural usage.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الولد: المولود. يقال للواحد والجمع والصغير والكبير" — child, born one, applied to one or many, young or old.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: biological progeny; metaphorical (majāz): "ولدوا حديثا وكلاما: استحدثوه" — newly invented speech; here, children as a trial.
- Root: صدق (ṣ-d-q)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Truthfulness; al-Farahidi links it to earnestness in word and deed.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الصدق والكذب أصلهما في القول" — truth and falsehood originate in speech, but extend to action and intention.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: truthful speech; metaphorical: "رجل صادق الحملة" — one whose charge in battle is true/earnest.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — "إنما" restricts the predicate exclusively to the subject, as in the prophetic citation {إنما أموالكم وأولادكم فتنة}, affirming trial as the sole designated function of wealth and children.
3:13.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

3:37.arabic: {وقال} فيكشف ما تدعون إليه إن شاء {وقال} يرزق من يشاء بغير حساب {وقال} ويغفر ما دون ذلك لمن يشاء {وقال} ويتوب الله على من يشاء وهو خلق من أخلاق الربوبية إذ قال تعالى والله شكور حليم وقد جعل الله الشكر مفتاح كلام أهل الجنة فقال تعالى وقالوا الحمد لله الذي صدقناه وعده {وقال} وآخر دعواهم أن الحمد لله رب العالمين
3:37.english: So then, what we have mentioned concerning the treatment of patience (ṣabr) regarding whispered insinuation (waswās), regarding lust (shahwah), and regarding status (jāh) — annex this to what we have already set down concerning the canons of the paths of spiritual striving (mujāhadah) in the Book of the Discipline of the Soul (Kitāb Riyāḍat al-Nafs) from the Quarter of the Destroyers (rubʿ al-muhlikāt). Adopt it as your manual (dastūr) by which you may come to know the treatment of patience in all the categories which we have previously detailed; for the detailing of individual cases is prolix. Whoever observes gradual progression (tadrīj), patience will elevate him to a state wherein patience without it becomes as arduous as it once was with it — so his affairs become inverted, and what was once beloved to him becomes loathed, and what was once detested to him becomes a sweet, wholesome draught from which he cannot bear to be patient [in abstaining]. This is known only through experience (tajribah) and tasting (dhawq). It has an analogue in customary habits: for a boy is compelled to learning in the beginning by force, and so patience with play and patience with knowledge are both arduous for him — until, when his inner sight is opened and he finds intimacy with knowledge, the matter is inverted, and it becomes arduous for him to be patient in abstaining from knowledge, and to endure play. To this points what is narrated of one of the knowers (ʿārifīn) that he asked al-Shiblī: "Patience — which of its kinds is the most severe?" He said: "Patience in God (fī Allāh)." He said: "No." He said: "Patience for God (li-Allāh)." He said: "No." He said: "Patience with God (maʿa Allāh)." He said: "No." He said: "Then what?" He said: "Patience from God (ʿan Allāh)." At that al-Shiblī cried out a cry by which his soul nearly perished. And it has been said concerning the meaning of His saying, the Exalted: {«اصبروا وصابروا ورابطوا»} "Be patient, and vie in patience, and be steadfast" (Q. 3:200): "Be patient in God, vie in patience by God, and be steadfast with God." And it was said: "Patience for God is sufficiency (ghināʾ); patience by God is endurance (baqāʾ); patience with God is fidelity (wafāʾ); and patience from God is abandonment (jafāʾ)." And it was said concerning its meaning:
3:37.section_title_en: The Revival of the Religious Sciences — Section 972: On Patience (al-Sabr) and the Commencement of Gratitude (al-Shukr)
3:37.anchors:
- Root: صبر (ṣ-b-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of restraint and withholding; al-Khalil notes its application to holding back an animal from fodder, and to enduring constraint.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الصبر: الإمساك في ضيق" — the withholding of the self in constriction; it is a general term whose specific names (shajāʿah, ḥilm, etc.) vary by context, and its opposite is al-jazaʿ (panic/vexation).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): "صبرت على ما أكره. وصبرت عما أحب" — enduring what is disliked and restraining from what is loved. Metaphorical (majāz): "صبرت يمينه" — binding an oath strenuously; "أصبر على الضرب من الأرض" — more enduring than the earth.
- Root: شكر (sh-k-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The root denotes manifestation and fullness; al-Ayn links it to an overflowing udder (shukrā).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الشكر: تصور النعمة وإظهارها" — the perception of a blessing and its display; it is the opposite of kufr (covering/denial). It has three degrees: of the heart (perception), of the tongue (praise), and of the limbs (requital).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "شكرت لله تعالى نعمته" — thanking God for His grace. Metaphorical: "دابة شكور" — a beast that thrives on little fodder, displaying its owner's care through its fatness.
- Root: علم (ʿ-l-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Knowledge as the apprehension of a thing's reality; al-Ayn treats it under the entry of umm (source/origin), indicating that knowledge is the root to which all else is annexed.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "العلم: إدراك الشيء بحقيقته" — apprehension of a thing by its true reality, either by grasping its essence or by affirming/denying a predicate of it.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "ما علمت بخبرك: ما شعرت به" — to be aware/perceive. It is also used for the landmarks (maʿālim) of the road, i.e., traces by which one is guided.
- Root: وقد (w-q-d)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The kindling and blazing of fire; al-Ayn records it under the entry of w-q-d with the sense of fuel and flame.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "وقدت النار تقد وقودا ووقدا" — the fire blazed; al-wuqūd is both the fuel and the resulting flame, as in {«وقودها الناس والحجارة»} (Q. 2:24).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "وقدت النار وقودا ووقدا، واتقدت وتوقدت" — the fire blazed and blazed fiercely. Metaphorical: "قلب وقاد" — a blazing, keen heart; "وقدة الصيف" — the blazing heat of summer.
- Sibawayh Rule: Interposition between the operative word and its object (al-faṣl bayna al-ʿāmil wa al-maʿmūl fīhi) — governing the placement of circumstantial qualifiers (ḥāl) and prepositional phrases to preserve the intended semantic restriction, as in the verse "اصبروا وصابروا ورابطوا" where each imperative carries a distinct operative scope.
3:37.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

3:125.arabic: الصابرين وعلق النصرة على الصبر فقال تعالى بلى إن تصبروا وتتقوا ويأتوكم من فورهم هذا يمددكم ربكم بخمسة آلاف من الملائكة مسومين وجمع للصابرين بين أمور لم يجمعها لغيرهم فقال تعالى أولئك عليهم صلوات من ربهم ورحمة وأولئك هم المهتدون فالهدى والرحمة والصلوات مجموعة للصابرين واستقصاء جميع الآيات في مقام الصبر يطول وأما الأخبار فقد قال صلى الله عليه وسلم الصبر نصف الإيمان (1) على ما سيأتي وجه كونه نصفا وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم من أقل ما أوتيتم اليقين وعزيمة الصبر ومن أعطي حظه منهما لم يبال بما فاته من قيام الليل وصيام النهار ولأن تصبروا على ما أنتم عليه أحب إلي من أن يوافيني كل امرىء
3:125.english: Allah — exalted be He — has described the patient (al-ṣābirīn) with attributes, and He mentioned patience (al-ṣabr) in the Qur’an in upwards of seventy places. He attached most of the degrees and goods to patience, making them its fruit. For He said — majestic is His utterance: {«وَجَعَلْنَا مِنْهُمْ أَئِمَّةً يَهْدُونَ بِأَمْرِنَا لَمَّا صَبَرُوا»} — “And We made from among them imams guiding by Our command, when they were patient” (Q 32:24). And He said — exalted be He: {«وَتَمَّتْ كَلِمَتُ رَبِّكَ الْحُسْنَىٰ عَلَىٰ بَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ بِمَا صَبَرُوا»} — “And the good word of your Lord was fulfilled upon the Children of Israel, because they were patient” (Q 7:137). And He said — exalted be He: {«وَلَنَجْزِيَنَّ الَّذِينَ صَبَرُوا أَجْرَهُم بِأَحْسَنِ مَا كَانُوا يَعْمَلُونَ»} — “And We shall surely recompense those who were patient their wage according to the best of what they used to do” (Q 16:96). And He said — exalted be He: {«أُولَٰئِكَ يُؤْتَوْنَ أَجْرَهُم مَّرَّتَيْنِ بِمَا صَبَرُوا»} — “Those shall be given their wage twice, because they were patient” (Q 28:54). And He said — exalted be He: {«إِنَّمَا يُوَفَّى الصَّابِرُونَ أَجْرَهُم بِغَيْرِ حِسَابٍ»} — “Only the patient shall be paid their wage without reckoning” (Q 39:10). Thus there is no act of nearness (qurbah) whose wage is not meted out by measure and account — except patience. And because fasting (al-ṣawm) is of patience, and it is half of patience, Allah — exalted be He — said: “Fasting is Mine, and I recompense it” — so He attributed it to Himself, to the exclusion of all other acts of worship. And He promised the patient that He is with them, saying — exalted be He: {«وَاصْبِرُوا إِنَّ اللَّهَ مَعَ الصَّابِرِينَ»} — “And be patient; indeed Allah is with the patient” (Q 8:46). And He made victory contingent upon patience, saying — exalted be He: {«بَلَىٰ إِن تَصْبِرُوا وَتَتَّقُوا وَيَأْتُوكُم مِّن فَوْرِهِمْ هَٰذَا يُمْدِدْكُمْ رَبُّكُم بِخَمْسَةِ آلَافٍ مِّنَ الْمَلَائِكَةِ مُسَوِّمِينَ»} — “Yes, if you are patient and God-fearing, and they come upon you in their rush, your Lord will reinforce you with five thousand marked angels” (Q 3:125). And He gathered for the patient things He gathered for no others, saying — exalted be He: {«أُولَٰئِكَ عَلَيْهِمْ صَلَوَاتٌ مِّن رَّبِّهِمْ وَرَحْمَةٌ وَأُولَٰئِكَ هُمُ الْمُهْتَدُونَ»} — “Those — upon them are blessings from their Lord, and mercy; and those — they are the rightly guided” (Q 2:157). So guidance, mercy, and blessings are all gathered for the patient. And to exhaust all the verses concerning the station of patience would be lengthy.
3:125.section_title_en: The Virtue of Patience (Ṣabr) — Its Excellence in the Qur’an, Sunnah, and Reports of the Salaf
3:125.anchors:
- Root: صبر (Ṣ-B-R)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning is “to restrain, to hold back, to bind firmly” — as in holding an animal by its halter or confining someone against departure.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Patience is “the self’s restraint upon what reason and Sacred Law require, or from what they require it to abstain from.” It is a generic term whose specific names vary by context: in calamity it is ṣabr (opposed to jazaʿ); in battle it is courage (shajāʿah); in vexation it is forbearance.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): “I bore patiently what I disliked, and I refrained patiently from what I loved.” Metaphorical (majāz): “His right hand was made to swear patiently” (i.e., bound by an emphatic oath), and “this tree is patient against cold” (i.e., unaffected by it).
- Root: عله (ʿ-L-H) — [Noted as a rare root; no direct bearing on this passage’s core terms, but included per lexical apparatus.]
- Root: ايم (A-Y-M) — [Noted as a rare root; no direct bearing on this passage’s core terms, but included per lexical apparatus.]
- Root: نفس (N-F-S)
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The self (nafs) as the locus of volitional restraint — patience is an act of the nafs holding itself back, distinguishing it from mere physical endurance.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: “a precious thing” (nafīs). Metaphorical: “he poured out his soul” (i.e., his blood), and “everything that has no flowing soul does not defile water.”
- Sibawayh Rule: Restriction and Focused Predication (Bāb al-Ḥaṣr wa al-Taqyīd bi-innamā) — Governing the exclusive clause {«إِنَّمَا يُوَفَّى الصَّابِرُونَ أَجْرَهُم بِغَيْرِ حِسَابٍ»}, where innamā restricts the reward-without-account solely to the patient, and {«الصَّوْمُ لِي وَأَنَا أَجْزِي بِهِ»}, where the predicate is focused to Allah alone.
3:125.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

3:178.arabic: ذنبا أحدثنا لهم نعمة ليزيد غرورهم وقال تعالى إنما نملي لهم ليزدادوا إثما وقال تعالى ولا تحسبن الله غافلا عما يعمل الظالمون إنما يؤخرهم ليوم تشخص فيه الأبصار إلى غير ذلك مما ورد في كتاب الله تعالى وسنة رسوله فمن آمن به تخلص من هذا الغرور فإن منشأ هذا الغرور الجهل بالله وبصفاته فإن من عرفه لا يأمن مكره ولا يغتر بأمثال هذه الخيالات الفاسدة وينظر إلى فرعون وهامان وقارون وإلى ملوك الأرض وما جرى لهم كيف أحسن الله إليهم ابتداء ثم دمرهم تدميرا فقال تعالى هل تحس منهم من أحد الآية وقد حذر الله تعالى من مكره واستدراجه فقال فلا يأ
3:178.english: As for knowing it by way of authoritative transmission and affirmation (taṣdīq): it is that one believes in the Book of God — exalted is He — and affirms His Messenger. For God — exalted is He — has said: {«أيحسبون أن ما نمدهم به من مال وبنين * نسارع لهم في الخيرات بل لا يشعرون»} — "Do they reckon that what We extend to them of wealth and sons — [that] We hasten for them good things? Nay, but they do not perceive" (Q. 23:55-56). And He said — exalted is He: {«سنستدرجهم من حيث لا يعلمون»} — "We shall draw them on by degrees from whence they do not know" (Q. 7:182). And He said — exalted is He: {«فتحنا عليهم أبواب كل شيء حتى إذا فرحوا بما أوتوا أخذناهم بغتة فإذا هم مبلسون»} — "We opened upon them the gates of everything, until when they rejoiced in what they were given, We seized them suddenly, and behold, they were in despair" (Q. 6:44). And in the interpretation of His saying — exalted is He: {«سنستدرجهم من حيث لا يعلمون»} — it is said: "Whenever they innovated a sin, We innovated for them a blessing, to increase their self-deception." And He said — exalted is He: {«إنما نملي لهم ليزدادوا إثما»} — "We only grant them respite that they may increase in sin" (Q. 3:178). And He said — exalted is He: {«ولا تحسبن الله غافلا عما يعمل الظالمون إنما يؤخرهم ليوم تشخص فيه الأبصار»} — "And do not reckon God heedless of what the wrongdoers do; He only delays them to a Day when eyes will stare fixedly" (Q. 14:42). And [there is] more of that kind which has come in the Book of God — exalted is He — and in the Sunnah of His Messenger. So whoever believes in it is delivered from this self-deception. For the origin of this self-deception is ignorance of God and of His attributes; for whoever knows Him does not feel secure from His stratagem (makr) and is not deceived by such corrupt fancies.
3:178.section_title_en: Section 888 — On the Remedy for Self-Deception (Ghurūr): Recognizing the Signs of Divine Honor (Karāmah) and Humiliation (Hawān)
3:178.anchors:
- Root: غرر (gh-r-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of an outward trace or mark; heedlessness in wakefulness; the blaze on a horse's forehead.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Ghurūr" is delusion stemming from heedlessness — the soul's being overtaken while imagining security, as in {«ما غرك بربك الكريم»} (Q. 82:6). It is the state of one who is deceived by apparent favors while blind to their underlying test.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): heedlessness and exposure to predation, like a gazelle deceived by moonlight. Metaphorical (Majaz): being "deceived by God" (ightirār billāh) — trusting in His mercy while persisting in disobedience.
- Root: لهم (l-h-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Swallowing whole; the gullet.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Ilhām" — God's casting a meaning into the heart (al-raw'), distinct from demonic whispering; the channel of inner vision for the knowers (ʿārifūn).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: to swallow. Metaphorical: the heart's receptive "swallowing" of divine inspiration.
- Root: حدث (ḥ-d-th)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Origination after non-existence; newness.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Ḥudūth" — a thing's coming to be after it was not; "muḥdith" — the originator, exclusively God for substances (jawāhir). "Iḥdāth" — bringing about a novel state or act.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: temporal newness. Metaphorical: "muḥaddath" — one inspired with correct discernment, as if newly spoken-to.
- Root: نعم (n-ʿ-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Softness, ease, well-being; a state of comfort.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Niʿmah" — the good state one inhabits; "naʿīm" — the act of living pleasantly. Blessings are both a test and a sign, per {«وإن تعدوا نعمة الله لا تحصوها»} (Q. 16:18).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: bounty and comfort. Metaphorical: "khafat naʿāmatuhum" — their prosperity vanished; blessings may signal either favor or gradual ruin (istidrāj).
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction and Focused Predication with "innamā")
  * In {«إنما نملي لهم ليزدادوا إثما»} (Q. 3:178) and {«إنما يؤخرهم ليوم تشخص فيه الأبصار»} (Q. 14:42), "innamā" restricts the purpose of divine respite exclusively to increase of sin and deferred reckoning — negating any reading of it as benevolent indulgence.
3:178.topic: Al-Ghazali on constant remembrance of God and contemplative invocations, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

3:179.arabic: النهار ولأن تصبروا على ما أنتم عليه أحب إلي من أن يوافيني كل امرىء منكم بمثل عمل جميعكم ولكني أخاف أن تفتح عليكم الدنيا بعدي فينكر بعضكم بعضا وينكركم أهل السماء عند ذلك فمن صبر واحتسب ظفر بكمال ثوابه ثم قرأ قوله تعالى ما عندكم ينفد وما عنده الله باق ولنجزين الذين صبروا أجرهم الآية (2) الآية وروى جابر أنه سئل صلى الله عليه وسلم عن الإيمان فقال الصبر والسماحة (3) حديث الصبر كنز من كنوز الجنة غريب لم أجده وسئل مرة ما الإيمان فقال الصبر (4) حديث الحج عرفه تقدم في الحج معناه معظم الحج عرف

And He said — exalted be He: {«وَتَمَّتْ كَلِمَتُ رَبِّكَ الْحُسْنَىٰ عَلَىٰ بَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ بِمَا صَبَرُوا»} — “And the good word of your Lord was fulfilled upon the Children of Israel, because they were patient” (Q 7:137). And because fasting (al-ṣawm) is of patience, and it is half of patience, Allah — exalted be He — said: “Fasting is Mine, and I recompense it” — so He attributed it to Himself, to the exclusion of all other acts of worship. And He promised the patient that He is with them, saying — exalted be He: {«وَاصْبِرُوا إِنَّ اللَّهَ مَعَ الصَّابِرِينَ»} — “And be patient; indeed Allah is with the patient” (Q 8:46). And He made victory contingent upon patience, saying — exalted be He: {«بَلَىٰ إِن تَصْبِرُوا وَتَتَّقُوا وَيَأْتُوكُم مِّن فَوْرِهِمْ هَٰذَا يُمْدِدْكُمْ رَبُّكُم بِخَمْسَةِ آلَافٍ مِّنَ الْمَلَائِكَةِ مُسَوِّمِينَ»} — “Yes, if you are patient and God-fearing, and they come upon you in their rush, your Lord will reinforce you with five thousand marked angels” (Q 3:125). And He gathered for the patient things He gathered for no others, saying — exalted be He: {«أُولَٰئِكَ عَلَيْهِمْ صَلَوَاتٌ مِّن رَّبِّهِمْ وَرَحْمَةٌ وَأُولَٰئِكَ هُمُ الْمُهْتَدُونَ»} — “Those — upon them are blessings from their Lord, and mercy; and those — they are the rightly guided” (Q 2:157). So guidance, mercy, and blessings are all gathered for the patient. And to exhaust all the verses concerning the station of patience would be lengthy.
3:179.section_title_en: The Virtue of Patience (Ṣabr) — Its Excellence in the Qur’an, Sunnah, and Reports of the Salaf
3:179.anchors:
- Root: صبر (Ṣ-B-R)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning is “to restrain, to hold back, to bind firmly” — as in holding an animal by its halter or confining someone against departure.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Patience is “the self’s restraint upon what reason and Sacred Law require, or from what they require it to abstain from.” It is a generic term whose specific names vary by context: in calamity it is ṣabr (opposed to jazaʿ); in battle it is courage (shajāʿah); in vexation it is forbearance.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): “I bore patiently what I disliked, and I refrained patiently from what I loved.” Metaphorical (majāz): “His right hand was made to swear patiently” (i.e., bound by an emphatic oath), and “this tree is patient against cold” (i.e., unaffected by it).
- Root: عله (ʿ-L-H) — [Noted as a rare root; no direct bearing on this passage’s core terms, but included per lexical apparatus.]
- Root: ايم (A-Y-M) — [Noted as a rare root; no direct bearing on this passage’s core terms, but included per lexical apparatus.]
- Root: نفس (N-F-S)
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The self (nafs) as the locus of volitional restraint — patience is an act of the nafs holding itself back, distinguishing it from mere physical endurance.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: “a precious thing” (nafīs). Metaphorical: “he poured out his soul” (i.e., his blood), and “everything that has no flowing soul does not defile water.”
- Sibawayh Rule: Restriction and Focused Predication (Bāb al-Ḥaṣr wa al-Taqyīd bi-innamā) — Governing the exclusive clause {«إِنَّمَا يُوَفَّى الصَّابِرُونَ أَجْرَهُم بِغَيْرِ حِسَابٍ»}, where innamā restricts the reward-without-account solely to the patient, and {«الصَّوْمُ لِي وَأَنَا أَجْزِي بِهِ»}, where the predicate is focused to Allah alone.
3:179.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

3:186.arabic: صدرك بما يقولون فسبح بحمد ربك} الآية وقال تعالى {ولتسمعن من الذين أوتوا الكتاب من قبلكم ومن الذين أشركوا أذى كثيرا وإن تصبروا وتتقوا فإن ذلك من عزم الأمور} أي تصبروا عن المكافأة ولذلك مدح الله تعالى العافين عن حقوقهم في القصاص وغيره فقال تعالى {وإن عاقبتم فعاقبوا بمثل ما عوقبتم به ولئن صبرتم لهو} خير الصابرين {وقال} صلى الله عليه وسلم صل من قطعك وأعط من حرمك واعف عمن ظلمك // ورأيت في الإنجيل قال عيسى بن مريم عليه السلام لقد قيل لكم من قبل إن السن بالسن والأنف بالأنف وأنا أقول لكم لا تقاوموا بالشر بل من ضرب خدك الأيمن فحول إليه الخد الأيسر ومن أخذ رداءك فأعطه إزارك ومن سخرك لتسير معه ميلا فسر م
3:186.english: And acts of disobedience are the requisite of the impulse of caprice (bāʿith al-hawā). And the most severe kind of patience is patience in abstaining from those acts of disobedience that have become familiar through habit — for habit is a fifth nature. When habit is joined to lustful desire, two battalions from the battalions of Satan array themselves in concert against the battalion of God (jund Allāh) — may He be exalted — and the impulse of religion (bāʿith al-dīn) has no strength to suppress them. Then, if that act be one whose commission has been rendered easy (tayassara), patience in abstaining from it is heavier upon the soul — such as patience in abstaining from the sins of the tongue: backbiting (ghībah), falsehood, contentious disputation (mirāʾ), self-praise whether by insinuation (taʿrīḍ) or by explicit statement (taṣrīḥ), the varieties of jesting that wound hearts, the kinds of words by which one intends belittlement and contempt, and the mention of the dead with aspersion cast upon them, upon their sciences, their conduct, and their stations. For such mention is in its outward aspect (fī ẓāhirihi) backbiting, and in its inward aspect (fī bāṭinihi) self-praise. In it the soul has two lusts: one is the negation of the other [person], and the other is the affirmation of oneself. And by these two together there is completed for it that lordship (rubūbiyyah) which is innate in its disposition — and which is the very opposite of what it has been commanded regarding servanthood (ʿubūdiyyah). And because of the conjunction of the two lusts, and the ease of moving the tongue, and the fact that this becomes habitual in everyday converse, patience in abstaining from it becomes difficult. And it is among the greatest of the destructive enormities (al-mūbiqāt) — so much so that its disapproval and ugliness have been effaced from hearts by dint of its frequent repetition and the universality of familiarity with it. Thus you see a man who would, for example, wear silk and deem it utterly remote [of permissibility], yet he unleashes his tongue the whole day long against the reputations (aʿrāḍ) of people and does not deem that objectionable — notwithstanding what has come down in the report that backbiting is more severe than adultery (zinā). And God — may He be exalted — said: {«ودع أذاهم وتوكل على الله»} "And leave aside their harm and put thy trust in God" (Q. 33:48). And He said — may He be exalted: {«واصبر على ما يقولون واهجرهم هجرا جميلا»} "And be patient over what they say, and depart from them with a gracious departure" (Q. 73:10). And He said — may He be exalted: {«ولقد نعلم أنك يضيق صدرك بما يقولون فسبح بحمد ربك»} "And indeed We know that thy breast is straitened by what they say; so glorify with the praise of thy Lord" (Q. 15:97–98) — to the end of the verse. And He said — may He be exalted: {«ولتسمعن من الذين أوتوا الكتاب من قبلكم ومن الذين أشركوا أذى كثيرا وإن تصبروا وتتقوا فإن ذلك من عزم الأمور»} "And you shall surely hear from those who were given the Scripture before you and from those who associate [others with God] much harm. And if you are patient and God-fearing, indeed that is of the resolute affairs" (Q. 3:186) — that is, that you be patient in refraining from requital (mukāfaʾah). And for this reason God — may He be exalted — praised those who pardon others their due rights in retaliation (qiṣāṣ) and otherwise, saying — may He be exalted: {«وإن عاقبتم فعاقبوا بمثل ما عوقبتم به ولئن صبرتم لهو خير الصابرين»} "And if you punish, then punish with the like of that wherewith you were afflicted. And if you are patient, it is surely better for the patient" (Q. 16:126). And he — upon him be peace — said: "Maintain the bond with him who cuts you off, and give to him who withholds from you, and pardon him who wrongs you." And I have seen in the Gospel that ʿĪsā ibn Maryam — upon him be peace — said: "It was said to you of old: an eye for an eye and a nose for a nose. But I say to you: do not resist evil. Rather, whoever strikes your right cheek, turn to him PageV04P071 the left cheek; and whoever takes your cloak, give him your garment; and whoever compels you to walk with him one mile, walk with him two miles." And all of that is a command to be patient under harm. So patience under the harm of people is among the highest stations of patience, because in it the impulse of religion and the impulse of lustful desire and anger are all arrayed together [against the soul].
3:186.section_title_en: The Most Severe Forms of Patience: Abstaining from Habitual Sins and Enduring Harm
3:186.anchors:
- Root: صبر (ṣ-b-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of restraint and withholding; "ṣabara al-dābbah" = to hold back an animal without fodder; "ṣabartu nafsī" = I restrained my soul.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الصبر: حبس النفس على ما يقتضيه العقل والشرع، أو عما يقتضيان حبسها عنه" — Patience is the withholding of the soul upon what reason and Law require, or from what they require it to be withheld. When exercised against calamity it is called ṣabr alone (opposed to jazaʿ); in warfare, courage (shajāʿah); in vexing misfortune, forbearance.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): "صبرت على ما أكره. وصبرت عما أحب" — I bore patiently what I dislike, and I restrained myself from what I love. Metaphorical (majāz): "هو أصبر على الضرب من الأرض" — he is more enduring of beating than the earth.
- Root: عادة (ʿ-w-d)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Recurrence and return; habitual practice that becomes second nature through repetition.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Habit (ʿādah) as reiterated action that imprints upon the soul, rendering the act facile and its abandonment burdensome.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: return to a state or place. Metaphorical: the ingrained disposition that governs conduct.
- Root: غيب (gh-y-b)
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الغيب: مصدر غابت الشمس وغيرها: إذا استترت عن العين" — that which is concealed from the senses; applied to what is absent from human perception, though nothing is absent from God.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "تكلم بذلك عن ظهر الغيب" — he spoke of that behind the veil of the unseen. Metaphorical: "أتونا في غابة" — they came in a dense host (like tangled thickets).
- Sibawayh Rule: Prepositional Interposition (باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور) — governing the permissible separation between the preposition and its object for rhetorical emphasis, as in the periodic construction "فإن ذلك في ظاهره غيبة وفي باطنه ثناء على النفس" where the circumstantial qualifiers (ẓāhir/bāṭin) are interposed to contrast outward form with inward reality.
3:186.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

4:97.arabic: المحركة ومن لم يفعل هذا فقد كفر نعمة الله في سعة الأرض إذ قال تعالى ألم تكن أرض الله واسعة فتهاجروا فيها الثاني أن يكلف نفسه في أعماله أفعالا تخالف ما اعتاده فيبدل التكلف بالتبذل وزي الحشمة بزي التواضع وكذلك كل هيئة وحال وفعل في مسكن وملبس ومطعم وقيام وقعود كان يعتاده وفاء بمقتضى جاهه فينبغي أن يبدلها بنقائضها حتى يرسخ باعتياد ذلك ضد ما رسخ فيه من قبل باعتياد ضده فلا معنى للمعالجة إلا المضادة الثالث أن يراعى في ذلك التلطف والتدريج فلا ينتقل دفعة واحدة إلى الطرف الأقصى من التبذل فإن الطبع نفور ولا يمكن نقله عن أخلاقه إلا بالتدريج فيترك البعض ويسلي ن
4:97.english: ...anxieties in [worldly] administrations, and likewise all the other means to rank. Then, whenever the means are secured and completed, the lifespan expires — until, when the earth has taken on its ornament and is adorned, and its people suppose that they are able to master it, there comes to it Our command by night or by day, and We make it a harvested stubble as if it had not flourished the day before. Thus God — exalted be He — struck for it a parable, saying — exalted be He: {And strike for them the parable of the life of this world: like water which We send down from the sky, and the vegetation of the earth mingles with it, and then it becomes dry chaff which the winds scatter} {«وَاضْرِبْ لَهُمْ مَثَلَ الْحَيَاةِ الدُّنْيَا كَمَاءٍ أَنْزَلْنَاهُ مِنَ السَّمَاءِ فَاخْتَلَطَ بِهِ نَبَاتُ الْأَرْضِ فَأَصْبَحَ هَشِيمًا تَذْرُوهُ الرِّيَاحُ»} [Al-Kahf: 45]. And asceticism (al-zuhd) in this world — because it was a present sovereignty — Satan envied him for it and barred him from it.
4:97.section_title_en: On Renouncing Status and the True Meaning of Sovereignty — The Cure for the Love of Prestige
4:97.anchors:
- Root: ملك (malaka)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root denotes possession, dominion, and the power to command and forbid; al-Farahidi notes its application to kingship and ownership alike.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Distinguishes two modes: (1) actual possession/sovereignty (al-tamalluk wa al-tawallī) and (2) the capacity/power to exercise it (al-quwwah ʿalā dhālika), whether or not one actually rules. True sovereignty belongs to him who governs his own soul.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (haqīqah): ownership of property and dominion over subjects. Metaphorical (majāz): "he mastered his anger" (malaka nafsahu ʿinda al-ghadab) — self-mastery as the paradigmatic figurative extension of kingship.
- Root: عقد (ʿabada)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Servitude and worship; the slave (ʿabd) is one who is owned and subjugated.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): ʿUbūdiyyah is the state of being subjugated to another's command; true slavery to passion is the degradation of the rational soul.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: chattel slavery. Metaphorical: he who is led by his lusts is a slave in reality, even if free in legal form.
- Root: سخر (sakhkhara)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To subjugate, compel, and employ against one's will; used of beasts and forces pressed into service.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Taskhīr is the compelled employment of a thing for another's purpose — the opposite of free, rational agency.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: subjugation of animals. Metaphorical: the man ruled by appetite is musakhkhar — driven like a beast by its halter.
- Root: دنا (dānā)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Nearness in place, time, or rank.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-dunyā (the lower world) is so named for its nearness and lowness relative to the Hereafter; it is the realm of delusion when pursued for its own sake.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: proximity. Metaphorical: the "nearer" life as the inferior, contemptible portion.
- Sibawayh Rule: Bāb al-faṣl bayna al-jār wa al-majrūr (Prepositional Interposition) — The periodic sentence structure here interposes lengthy causal and conditional clauses between the governing verb and its complements, requiring the translator to preserve the logical sequence of protasis and apodosis without collapsing the rhetorical tension of the original.
4:97.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

4:97.arabic: قوله تعالى إن الذين توفاهم الملائكة ظالمي أنفسهم في قوم من المسلمين كانوا يكثرون جماعة المشركين بالمخالطة وقد روي أن الله تعالى أوحى إلى يوشع ابن نون إني مهلك من قومك أربعين ألفا من خيارهم وستين ألفا من شرارهم فقال ما بال الأخيار قال إنهم لا يغضبون لغضبي فكانوا يؤاكلونهم ويشاربونهم وبهذا يتبين أن بعض الظلمة والغضب لله عليهم واجب وروى ابن مسعود عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم إن الله لعن علماء بني إسرائيل إذ خالطوا الظالمين في معاشهم (6)
4:97.english: As for the servants and the retinue, most of their wealth comes from outright usurpation (al-ghaṣb al-ṣarīḥ). There falls into their hands no wealth from legitimate sources — no lawful gain, no inheritance, no poll-tax (jizyah), and no lawful means whatsoever — such that the suspicion might be weakened by the mixing of the lawful with their wealth. Ṭāwūs said: "I do not bear witness before them even if I am certain [of the truth of my testimony], because I fear their transgression against the one against whom I bear witness."
4:97.section_title_en: The Ruling on Dealing with Tyrannical Rulers, Their Judges, and Their Servants
4:97.anchors:
- Root: ظلم (Ẓ-L-M)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning is placing something in other than its proper place; darkness (ẓulmah) as its cognate.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Ẓulm is transgression against right order; its theological weight is that it is a violation of God's boundaries, and its ultimate consequence is darkness on the Day of Judgment.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) usage denotes wrongful harm and injustice; metaphorical (majāz) usage extends to any act of overstepping, even against oneself.
- Root: ملك (M-L-K)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Possession, dominion, and sovereign authority.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-Mulk is the power to command and forbid over a polity; its corruption spreads when those in authority are corrupt.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal usage denotes sovereign rule; metaphorical usage includes mastery over one's own soul or affairs.
- Root: وقد (W-Q-D)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Fire burning fiercely; fuel for fire.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Used for the fire of punishment and its fuel; metaphorically for intense divine wrath.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal usage is physical fire; metaphorical usage is the burning of divine anger against wrongdoers.
- Root: لعن (L-ʿ-N)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To curse, to drive away from mercy, to ostracize.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Divine curse is exclusion from mercy; prophetic curse is a declaration of that exclusion.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal usage is expulsion and distancing; metaphorical usage is the declaration of one's deserving punishment.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — Used to confine a ruling to a specific class, as in the restriction of severe avoidance to tyrants specifically, not to all sinners.
4:97.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'The Lawful and Prohibited'

4:104.arabic: الآخرة فليقرأ المعرض عن الدنيا على نفسه قوله تعالى ولا تهنوا في ابتغاء القوم إن تكونوا تألمون فإنهم يألمون كما تألمون وترجون من الله ما لا يرجون فإذن إنما انسد طريق الشكر على الخلق لجهلهم بضروب النعم الظاهرة والباطنة والخاصة والعامة فإن قلت فما علاج هذه القلوب الغافلة حتى تشعر بنعم الله تعالى فعساها تشكر فأقول أما القلوب البصيرة فعلاجها التأمل فيما رمزنا إليه من أصناف نعم الله تعالى العامة وأما القلوب البليدة التي لا تعد النعمة نعمة إلا إذا خصتها أو شعرت بالبلاء معها فسبيله أن ينظر أبدا إلى من دونه ويفعل ما كان يفعله بعض الصوفية إذ كان كل يوم يحضر دار المرضى والمقابر والمواضع التي تقام ف
4:104.english: So may sorrow never part from you. Nay, rather, the most eloquent of expressions and the most lucid of words is the speech of the most eloquent of all who uttered with the Ḍād, whereupon he — peace and blessings be upon him — conveyed this very meaning when he said: "Whosoever awakens secure in his private state, sound in his body, having the provision of his day, it is as though the entire world with all its fullness were gathered for him." {«من أصبح آمنا في سربه معافى في بدنه عنده قوت يومه فكأنما حيزت له الدنيا بحذافيرها»}
4:104.section_title_en: The Remedy for Hearts Unmindful of Divine Blessings — The Path to Gratitude
4:104.anchors:
- Root: حزن (ḥ-z-n)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Deep, entrenched sorrow that clings to the heart and does not depart.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Grief as a spiritual state opposed to the soul's tranquility; its removal is tied to recognizing divine beneficence.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: enduring sadness; Metaphorical: the "sorrow" of deprivation from ultimate felicity.
- Root: سرب (s-r-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The self in its private, secure state; safety of one's person and affairs.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Security (amn) as a comprehensive blessing encompassing faith and worldly safety.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical safety in one's abode; Metaphorical: spiritual security from divine wrath.
- Root: عوض (ʿ-w-ḍ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Exchange, substitution, recompense for loss.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The concept of barter between worldly pleasure and knowledge; knowledge's delight is imperishable, thus no exchange is equitable.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: giving something in return; Metaphorical: the soul's refusal to trade eternal gnosis for transient sensation.
- Root: غبن (gh-b-n)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Loss in a transaction; being cheated of one's due.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The Day of Mutual Loss (Yawm al-Taghābun) where the obedient see the vastness of missed opportunity and the disobedient see their ruin.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: commercial fraud; Metaphorical: the ultimate self-deception in squandering life's hours.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — "إنما انسد طريق الشكر" restricts the cause exclusively to ignorance, not to any deficiency in divine bounty.
4:104.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

4:123.arabic: وروي أنه لما نزل قوله تعالى من يعمل سوءا يجز به قال أبو بكر الصديق رضي الله تعالى عنه كيف الفرح بعد هذه الآية فقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم غفر الله لك يا أبا بكر ألست تمرض ألست يصيبك الأذى ألست تحزن فهذا مما تجزون به (2) يعني أن جميع ما يصيبك يكون كفارة لذنوبك وعن عقبة بن عامر عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال إذا رأيتم الرجل يعطيه الله ما يحب وهو مقيم على معصيته فاعلموا أن ذلك استدراج ثم قرأ قوله تعالى فلما نسوا ما
4:123.english: And God is better for you than al-ʿAbbās. Ibn ʿAbbās said: "No one consoled me more beautifully than his consolation."
4:123.section_title_en: On Patience in Calamities — The Virtue of the Afflicted and the Reward of the Patient
4:123.anchors:
- Root: صبر (ṣ-b-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning is restraint and retention — holding oneself back from complaint and panic; al-ṣabr is the opposite of al-jazaʿ (restless agitation).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In the theological register, ṣabr is the retention of the soul upon the dictates of revelation and the restraint of the lower self from objecting to divine decree — it is half of faith, paired with shukr (gratitude).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): endurance of physical hardship. Metaphorical (majāz): "ṣabara ʿanhu" — to withhold oneself from something forbidden; the patient one (al-ṣābir) is he who restrains his tongue from complaint and his heart from resentment.
- Root: بلا (b-l-w)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To test, to try, to afflict; ibtalā means to subject to trial for the purpose of manifesting the inner state.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Balā' in the Quran oscillates between tribulation (miḥnah) and favor (niʿmah) — both are divine tests; the believer is tried with what purifies, the disbeliever with what condemns.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the wearing away of a garment (ablā al-thawb). Metaphorical: divine trial that "wears away" sins as the garment wears with use.
- Root: أجر ('-j-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Reward, recompense; the wage given in exchange for labor.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In the eschatological sense, ajr is the recompense that God grants not as a debt of justice but as a bounty of grace — hence the verse {«إنما يوفى الصابرون أجرهم بغير حساب»} signals its measurelessness.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: hire for work. Metaphorical: the reward of the afterlife, since deeds are the "work" and paradise the "wage."
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Restriction by Innama (الحصر بإنما) — When the verse {«إنما يوفى الصابرون أجرهم بغير حساب»} employs innamā, it restricts the unmeasured reward exclusively to the patient, excluding all others from that specific bounty.
4:123.topic: Classical commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya Ulum al-Din, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

4:147.arabic: أكبر فقال تعالى فاذكروني أذكركم واشكروا لي ولا تكفرون وقال تعالى ما يفعل الله بعذابكم إن شكرتم وآمنتم وقال تعالى وسنجزي الشاكرين وقال عز وجل إخبارا عن إبليس اللعين لأقعدن لهم صراطك المستقيم قيل هو طريق الشكر ولعلو رتبة الشكر طعن اللعين في الخلق فقال ولا تجد اكثرم شاكرين وقال تعالى وقليل من عبادي الشكور وقد قطع الله تعالى بالمزيد مع الشكر ولم يستثن فقال تعالى لئن شكرتم لأزيدنكم واستثنى في خمسة أشياء في الإغناء والإجابة والرزق والمغفرة والتوبة فقال تعالى فسوف يغنيكم الله من فضله إن شاء {وقال} فيكشف ما تدعون إليه إن شاء {وقال} يرزق من يشاء بغ
4:147.english: So then, what we have mentioned concerning the treatment of patience (ṣabr) regarding whispered insinuation (waswās), regarding lust (shahwah), and regarding status (jāh) — annex this to what we have already set down concerning the canons of the paths of spiritual striving (mujāhadah) in the Book of the Discipline of the Soul (Kitāb Riyāḍat al-Nafs) from the Quarter of the Destroyers (rubʿ al-muhlikāt). Adopt it as your manual (dastūr) by which you may come to know the treatment of patience in all the categories which we have previously detailed; for the detailing of individual cases is prolix. Whoever observes gradual progression (tadrīj), patience will elevate him to a state wherein patience without it becomes as arduous as it once was with it — so his affairs become inverted, and what was once beloved to him becomes loathed, and what was once detested to him becomes a sweet, wholesome draught from which he cannot bear to be patient [in abstaining]. This is known only through experience (tajribah) and tasting (dhawq). It has an analogue in customary habits: for a boy is compelled to learning in the beginning by force, and so patience with play and patience with knowledge are both arduous for him — until, when his inner sight is opened and he finds intimacy with knowledge, the matter is inverted, and it becomes arduous for him to be patient in abstaining from knowledge, and to endure play. To this points what is narrated of one of the knowers (ʿārifīn) that he asked al-Shiblī: "Patience — which of its kinds is the most severe?" He said: "Patience in God (fī Allāh)." He said: "No." He said: "Patience for God (li-Allāh)." He said: "No." He said: "Patience with God (maʿa Allāh)." He said: "No." He said: "Then what?" He said: "Patience from God (ʿan Allāh)." At that al-Shiblī cried out a cry by which his soul nearly perished. And it has been said concerning the meaning of His saying, the Exalted: {«اصبروا وصابروا ورابطوا»} "Be patient, and vie in patience, and be steadfast" (Q. 3:200): "Be patient in God, vie in patience by God, and be steadfast with God." And it was said: "Patience for God is sufficiency (ghināʾ); patience by God is endurance (baqāʾ); patience with God is fidelity (wafāʾ); and patience from God is abandonment (jafāʾ)." And it was said concerning its meaning:
