4:147.section_title_en: The Revival of the Religious Sciences — Section 972: On Patience (al-Sabr) and the Commencement of Gratitude (al-Shukr)
4:147.anchors:
- Root: صبر (ṣ-b-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of restraint and withholding; al-Khalil notes its application to holding back an animal from fodder, and to enduring constraint.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الصبر: الإمساك في ضيق" — the withholding of the self in constriction; it is a general term whose specific names (shajāʿah, ḥilm, etc.) vary by context, and its opposite is al-jazaʿ (panic/vexation).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): "صبرت على ما أكره. وصبرت عما أحب" — enduring what is disliked and restraining from what is loved. Metaphorical (majāz): "صبرت يمينه" — binding an oath strenuously; "أصبر على الضرب من الأرض" — more enduring than the earth.
- Root: شكر (sh-k-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The root denotes manifestation and fullness; al-Ayn links it to an overflowing udder (shukrā).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الشكر: تصور النعمة وإظهارها" — the perception of a blessing and its display; it is the opposite of kufr (covering/denial). It has three degrees: of the heart (perception), of the tongue (praise), and of the limbs (requital).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "شكرت لله تعالى نعمته" — thanking God for His grace. Metaphorical: "دابة شكور" — a beast that thrives on little fodder, displaying its owner's care through its fatness.
- Root: علم (ʿ-l-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Knowledge as the apprehension of a thing's reality; al-Ayn treats it under the entry of umm (source/origin), indicating that knowledge is the root to which all else is annexed.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "العلم: إدراك الشيء بحقيقته" — apprehension of a thing by its true reality, either by grasping its essence or by affirming/denying a predicate of it.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "ما علمت بخبرك: ما شعرت به" — to be aware/perceive. It is also used for the landmarks (maʿālim) of the road, i.e., traces by which one is guided.
- Root: وقد (w-q-d)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The kindling and blazing of fire; al-Ayn records it under the entry of w-q-d with the sense of fuel and flame.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "وقدت النار تقد وقودا ووقدا" — the fire blazed; al-wuqūd is both the fuel and the resulting flame, as in {«وقودها الناس والحجارة»} (Q. 2:24).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "وقدت النار وقودا ووقدا، واتقدت وتوقدت" — the fire blazed and blazed fiercely. Metaphorical: "قلب وقاد" — a blazing, keen heart; "وقدة الصيف" — the blazing heat of summer.
- Sibawayh Rule: Interposition between the operative word and its object (al-faṣl bayna al-ʿāmil wa al-maʿmūl fīhi) — governing the placement of circumstantial qualifiers (ḥāl) and prepositional phrases to preserve the intended semantic restriction, as in the verse "اصبروا وصابروا ورابطوا" where each imperative carries a distinct operative scope.
4:147.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

5:110.arabic: خارج وهو المراد بقوله عز وجل {إذ أيدتك بروح القدس} وتقرب منه العصمة وهى
5:110.english:
PageV04P107
But if one does not know what constitutes the welfare of his hereafter—so that he even supposes corruption to be welfare—then from where would mere volition benefit him? There is no benefit in volition, power, and causes except after guidance (hidāyah). For this reason, God—exalted is He—said: {«ربنا الذي أعطى كل شيء خلقه ثم هدى»} "Our Lord who gave everything its creation, then guided." And He said—exalted is He—: {«ولولا فضل الله عليكم ورحمته ما زكى منكم أحد أبدا ولكن الله يزكي من يشاء»} "And were it not for God's bounty upon you and His mercy, not one of you would ever be purified; but God purifies whom He wills." And the Prophet—peace be upon him—said: "No one enters Paradise except by the mercy of God—exalted is He—," that is, by His guidance. So it was said: "Not even you, O Messenger of God?" He said: "Not even I" (1). And guidance (hidāyah) has three stations (manāzil):
5:110.section_title_en: The Degrees of Divine Guidance (Hidāyah), Righteous Discernment (Rushd), Straightening (Tasdīd), and Divine Support (Ta'yīd)
5:110.anchors:
- Root: هدي (H-D-Y)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of gentle, gracious direction (dalālah bi-luṭf); the root also yields "gift" (hadiyyah) and the leading beasts of prey (hawādī) that guide the herd.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Guidance is "directional indication with gentleness" (dalālah bi-luṭf), distinct from mere intellectual proof; it is a divine act that may be general (to all) or specific (to the elect), and its withholding is a form of abandonment.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): "He guided him to the path" (hadāhu lil-sabīl). Metaphorical (majāz): "He guided him" meaning "he preceded him" (taqaddamahu), as a leader precedes the caravan; hence guidance is not merely pointing but active leading.
- Root: رشد (R-SH-D)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The state of being rightly directed in one's affairs; integrity of judgment; names Rāshid, Rushayd derive from it.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Rushd is the opposite of ghayy (error/ruin); it is used like hidāyah but with a nuance of practical, executive discernment—knowing the good AND being moved to pursue it. Al-Raghib explicitly distinguishes the rushd of Abraham (given before, as a special gift) from the mere legal competence (rushd) of an orphan.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "A man is rāshid or rashīd" (possessing rightness in conduct). Metaphorical: "He is of sound lineage" (huwa li-rushdah), i.e., legitimate—showing the root's extension to ontological soundness.
- Root: سدد (S-D-D)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To aim correctly, to hit the mark; the arrow that flies straight (sadīd); the opposite of deviation (ighrāḍ).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): (Not in the retrieved scholia, but by extension from the root's usage in the Qur'an, e.g., {wa-saddidū}, "and be straight/aim rightly")—it denotes the divine facilitation of the creature's movements so they align with the intended good.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "He aimed the arrow and it went straight." Metaphorical: "He was granted success in speech and action" (sudda li-l-ṣawāb).
- Root: أيد (A-Y-D)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Strength, support, reinforcement; the "aid" (ayd) of God is His empowering of His servant.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): (By extension from {إذ أيدتك بروح القدس})—divine reinforcement through a holy spirit, i.e., an immaterial power that fortifies both inner perception (baṣīrah) and outer action.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "He strengthened him" (ayyadahu). Metaphorical: Used for the conferral of spiritual power that makes the servant invincible against error.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Gradation and Specification (Tartīb wa-Takhṣīṣ) — The author structures a sequence of terms (hidāyah → rushd → tasdīd → ta'yīd) where each subsequent term is syntactically and semantically superordinate, building a hierarchy of divine acts. The particle "wa-ammā" (وأما) marks a new topic with contrastive focus, and the anaphoric references (هو، وهي) bind the exposition into a single periodic argument.
5:110.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

5:114.arabic: حرمك واعف عمن ظلمك // ورأيت في الإنجيل قال عيسى بن مريم عليه السلام لقد قيل لكم من قبل إن السن بالسن والأنف بالأنف وأنا أقول لكم لا تقاوموا بالشر بل من ضرب خدك الأيمن فحول إليه الخد الأيسر ومن أخذ رداءك فأعطه إزارك ومن سخرك لتسير معه ميلا فسر معه ميلين وكل ذلك أمر بالصبر على الأذى فالصبر على أذى الناس من أعلى مراتب الصبر لأنه يتعاون فيه باعث الدين وباعث الشهوة والغضب جميعا
5:114.english: And acts of disobedience are the requisite of the impulse of caprice (bāʿith al-hawā). And the most severe kind of patience is patience in abstaining from those acts of disobedience that have become familiar through habit — for habit is a fifth nature. When habit is joined to lustful desire, two battalions from the battalions of Satan array themselves in concert against the battalion of God (jund Allāh) — may He be exalted — and the impulse of religion (bāʿith al-dīn) has no strength to suppress them. Then, if that act be one whose commission has been rendered easy (tayassara), patience in abstaining from it is heavier upon the soul — such as patience in abstaining from the sins of the tongue: backbiting (ghībah), falsehood, contentious disputation (mirāʾ), self-praise whether by insinuation (taʿrīḍ) or by explicit statement (taṣrīḥ), the varieties of jesting that wound hearts, the kinds of words by which one intends belittlement and contempt, and the mention of the dead with aspersion cast upon them, upon their sciences, their conduct, and their stations. For such mention is in its outward aspect (fī ẓāhirihi) backbiting, and in its inward aspect (fī bāṭinihi) self-praise. In it the soul has two lusts: one is the negation of the other [person], and the other is the affirmation of oneself. And by these two together there is completed for it that lordship (rubūbiyyah) which is innate in its disposition — and which is the very opposite of what it has been commanded regarding servanthood (ʿubūdiyyah). And because of the conjunction of the two lusts, and the ease of moving the tongue, and the fact that this becomes habitual in everyday converse, patience in abstaining from it becomes difficult. And it is among the greatest of the destructive enormities (al-mūbiqāt) — so much so that its disapproval and ugliness have been effaced from hearts by dint of its frequent repetition and the universality of familiarity with it. Thus you see a man who would, for example, wear silk and deem it utterly remote [of permissibility], yet he unleashes his tongue the whole day long against the reputations (aʿrāḍ) of people and does not deem that objectionable — notwithstanding what has come down in the report that backbiting is more severe than adultery (zinā). And God — may He be exalted — said: {«ودع أذاهم وتوكل على الله»} "And leave aside their harm and put thy trust in God" (Q. 33:48). And He said — may He be exalted: {«واصبر على ما يقولون واهجرهم هجرا جميلا»} "And be patient over what they say, and depart from them with a gracious departure" (Q. 73:10). And He said — may He be exalted: {«ولقد نعلم أنك يضيق صدرك بما يقولون فسبح بحمد ربك»} "And indeed We know that thy breast is straitened by what they say; so glorify with the praise of thy Lord" (Q. 15:97–98) — to the end of the verse. And He said — may He be exalted: {«ولتسمعن من الذين أوتوا الكتاب من قبلكم ومن الذين أشركوا أذى كثيرا وإن تصبروا وتتقوا فإن ذلك من عزم الأمور»} "And you shall surely hear from those who were given the Scripture before you and from those who associate [others with God] much harm. And if you are patient and God-fearing, indeed that is of the resolute affairs" (Q. 3:186) — that is, that you be patient in refraining from requital (mukāfaʾah). And for this reason God — may He be exalted — praised those who pardon others their due rights in retaliation (qiṣāṣ) and otherwise, saying — may He be exalted: {«وإن عاقبتم فعاقبوا بمثل ما عوقبتم به ولئن صبرتم لهو خير الصابرين»} "And if you punish, then punish with the like of that wherewith you were afflicted. And if you are patient, it is surely better for the patient" (Q. 16:126). And he — upon him be peace — said: "Maintain the bond with him who cuts you off, and give to him who withholds from you, and pardon him who wrongs you." And I have seen in the Gospel that ʿĪsā ibn Maryam — upon him be peace — said: "It was said to you of old: an eye for an eye and a nose for a nose. But I say to you: do not resist evil. Rather, whoever strikes your right cheek, turn to him PageV04P071 the left cheek; and whoever takes your cloak, give him your garment; and whoever compels you to walk with him one mile, walk with him two miles." And all of that is a command to be patient under harm. So patience under the harm of people is among the highest stations of patience, because in it the impulse of religion and the impulse of lustful desire and anger are all arrayed together [against the soul].
5:114.section_title_en: The Most Severe Forms of Patience: Abstaining from Habitual Sins and Enduring Harm
5:114.anchors:
- Root: صبر (ṣ-b-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of restraint and withholding; "ṣabara al-dābbah" = to hold back an animal without fodder; "ṣabartu nafsī" = I restrained my soul.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الصبر: حبس النفس على ما يقتضيه العقل والشرع، أو عما يقتضيان حبسها عنه" — Patience is the withholding of the soul upon what reason and Law require, or from what they require it to be withheld. When exercised against calamity it is called ṣabr alone (opposed to jazaʿ); in warfare, courage (shajāʿah); in vexing misfortune, forbearance.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): "صبرت على ما أكره. وصبرت عما أحب" — I bore patiently what I dislike, and I restrained myself from what I love. Metaphorical (majāz): "هو أصبر على الضرب من الأرض" — he is more enduring of beating than the earth.
- Root: عادة (ʿ-w-d)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Recurrence and return; habitual practice that becomes second nature through repetition.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Habit (ʿādah) as reiterated action that imprints upon the soul, rendering the act facile and its abandonment burdensome.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: return to a state or place. Metaphorical: the ingrained disposition that governs conduct.
- Root: غيب (gh-y-b)
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الغيب: مصدر غابت الشمس وغيرها: إذا استترت عن العين" — that which is concealed from the senses; applied to what is absent from human perception, though nothing is absent from God.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "تكلم بذلك عن ظهر الغيب" — he spoke of that behind the veil of the unseen. Metaphorical: "أتونا في غابة" — they came in a dense host (like tangled thickets).
- Sibawayh Rule: Prepositional Interposition (باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور) — governing the permissible separation between the preposition and its object for rhetorical emphasis, as in the periodic construction "فإن ذلك في ظاهره غيبة وفي باطنه ثناء على النفس" where the circumstantial qualifiers (ẓāhir/bāṭin) are interposed to contrast outward form with inward reality.
5:114.topic: Al-Ghazali on purifying the character, moral diseases, and spiritual remedies, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

5:114.arabic: ينادي أين الزهاد في الدنيا زوروا عرس الزاهد في الدنيا عيسى ابن مريم وقال عيسى ابن مريم عليه السلام ويل لصاحب الدنيا كيف يموت ويتركها وما فيها وتغره ويأمنها ويثق بها وتخذله وويل للمغترين كيف أرتهم ما يكرهون وفارقهم ما يحبون وجاءهم ما يوعدون وويل لمن الدنيا همه والخطايا عمله كيف يفتضح غدا بذنبه وقيل أوحى الله تعالى إلى موسى عليه السلام يا موسى مالك ولدار الظالمين إنها ليست لك بدار أخرج منها همك وفارقها بعقلك فبئست الدار هي إلا لعامل يعمل فيها فنعمت الدار هي يا موسى إني مرصد للظالم حتى آخذ منه للمظلوم وروي أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه و
5:114.english: And lightning appeared one day, and he began seeking something to which he might take refuge. His eye fell upon a tent from afar, so he approached it — and behold, there was a woman within it. So he turned aside from her, and then there was a cave in a mountain. He came to it — and behold, there was a lion within it. So he placed his hand upon it and said: "My God, Thou hast made for every thing a refuge, and Thou hast made for me no refuge." Then God — exalted be He — revealed to him: "Thy refuge is in the resting place of My mercy. I shall surely wed thee on the Day of Resurrection to a hundred houris whom I created with My own hand, and I shall surely feed thee at thy wedding-feast for four thousand years — each day of which is like the age of this world — and I shall surely command a herald to proclaim: 'Where are the ascetics of the world? Come visit the wedding-feast of the ascetic of the world, Jesus son of Mary.'"
5:114.section_title_en: The Revival of the Religious Sciences — Book on the Remembrance of Death: On the Merit of Renouncing the World (Section 732)
5:114.anchors:
- Root: برق (b-r-q)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of shining, flashing, and appearing suddenly — from which "al-barq" (lightning) derives; also used for that which startles and alarms.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Used for sudden manifestation; here, the lightning serves as a natural sign prompting reflection on transience.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (haqiqah) for lightning; metaphorical (majaz) for the fleeting illumination of worldly life that vanishes instantly.
- Root: زهد (z-h-d)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To abstain from, to disdain, to regard as little; al-zuhd is the renunciation of something while it remains within one's power.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The theological virtue of renouncing the world (al-zuhd fi al-dunya) — not the mere abandonment of wealth, but the emptying of the heart from attachment to it.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: to turn away from a thing with aversion; metaphorical: the soul's disengagement from worldly allurements while the body remains present.
- Root: عرس (ʿ-r-s)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Wedding feast; the celebration of union; also used for the bridal chamber.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In the eschatological context, the "wedding" of the ascetic (al-zāhid) is a divine metaphor for the honor bestowed upon the renunciant in the Hereafter.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: a human marriage celebration; metaphorical: the spiritual recompense of intimacy with the Divine.
- Root: سخط (s-kh-t)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Displeasure, wrath, indignation; the opposite of ridā (satisfaction).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Divine displeasure (sakhat) as the cause of destruction; death by "wrath" (sakhtah) signifies a punishment visited upon a people for their disobedience.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: anger; metaphorical: the withdrawal of divine mercy and the sending of chastisement.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The permissibility of separating a prepositional phrase from its governed noun when the intervening element is semantically complete, as in the narrative transitions between reported speech and action.
5:114.topic: Al-Ghazali on the journey of the soul, death, and the Hereafter, from 'Condemnation of the World'

6:4.arabic: معدمون كلا وإن كل لما جميع لدينا محضرون {ولكن} ما تأتيهم من آية من آيات ربهم إلا كانوا عنها معرضين وذلك لأنا جعلنا من بين أيديهم سدا ومن خلفهم سدا فأغشيناهم فهم لا يبصرون وسواء عليهم أأنذرتهم أم لم تنذرهم لا يؤمنون ولنرجع إلى الغرض فإن هذه تلويحات تشير إلى أمور هي أعلى من علوم المعاملة فنقول ظهر أن الصبر عبارة عن ثبات باعث الدين في مقاومة باعث الهوى وهذه المقاومة من خاصة الآدميين لما وكل بهم من الكرام الكاتبين ولا يكتبان شيئا عن الصبيان والمجانين إذ قد ذكرنا أن الحسنة في الإقبال على الاستفادة منهما والسيئة في الإعراض عنهما وما للصبيان والمج
6:4.english: How immense is your heedlessness, O wretched one—and all of us are that wretched one—while before you are these terrors! If you do not believe in the greater resurrection out of ignorance and error, does not the evidence of the lesser resurrection suffice you? Have you not heard the saying of the Master of the Prophets, peace be upon him: "Sufficient is death as a warner" (kafā bil-mawti wāʿiẓan)? Have you not heard of his weeping, peace be upon him, at death, until he said, may God's peace and blessing be upon him: "O God, ease for Muhammad the agonies of death" (allāhumma hawwin ʿalā Muḥammadin sakarāti al-mawt)? Are you not ashamed of your slowness in anticipating the onslaught of death, following the rabble of the heedless—those who look only for a single cry that seizes them while they are disputing, so they can neither make a bequest nor return to their families? Then illness comes to them as a warner of death, and they are not deterred; and gray hair comes to them as a messenger from it, and they do not take heed. {«يَا حَسْرَةً عَلَى الْعِبَادِ مَا يَأْتِيهِمْ مِنْ رَسُولٍ إِلَّا كَانُوا بِهِ يَسْتَهْزِئُونَ»} (O regret upon the servants! There comes not to them a messenger but they mock him) [Ya-Sin: 30]. Do they think that they are in this world immortal? {«أَوَلَمْ يَرَوْا كَمْ أَهْلَكْنَا قَبْلَهُمْ مِنَ الْقُرُونِ أَنَّهُمْ إِلَيْهِمْ لَا يَرْجِعُونَ»} (Have they not seen how many generations We destroyed before them—that they will not return to them?) [Ya-Sin: 31]. Or do they reckon that the dead have merely traveled away from them, and so they are annihilated? Nay! {«وَإِنْ كُلٌّ لَمَّا جَمِيعٌ لَدَيْنَا مُحْضَرُونَ»} (And indeed, all of them, without exception, will be brought before Us) [Ya-Sin: 32]. {«وَمَا تَأْتِيهِمْ مِنْ آيَةٍ مِنْ آيَاتِ رَبِّهِمْ إِلَّا كَانُوا عَنْهَا مُعْرِضِينَ»} (And there comes not to them a sign from the signs of their Lord but they turn away from it) [Ya-Sin: 46]. And that is because {«إِنَّا جَعَلْنَا مِنْ بَيْنِ أَيْدِيهِمْ سَدًّا وَمِنْ خَلْفِهِمْ سَدًّا فَأَغْشَيْنَاهُمْ فَهُمْ لَا يُبْصِرُونَ»} (We have placed before them a barrier and behind them a barrier, and We have covered them, so they do not see) [Ya-Sin: 9]. {«وَسَوَاءٌ عَلَيْهِمْ أَأَنْذَرْتَهُمْ أَمْ لَمْ تُنْذِرْهُمْ لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ»} (And it is alike to them whether you warn them or warn them not—they will not believe) [Ya-Sin: 10].
6:4.section_title_en: On the Lesser Resurrection as Proof of the Greater, and the Station of the Guardian over the Child
6:4.anchors:
- Root: صغر (ṣaghara)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Smallness in magnitude, rank, or time; the lesser as opposed to the greater (al-kabīr), each term relative to the other.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Ṣighar and kibar are relative opposites, applied variously to age, body, or station; here, the "lesser resurrection" (al-qiyāmah al-ṣughrā) is death, measured against the "greater" (al-kubrā), the final rising.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: diminution in size or status. Metaphorical: the lesser as a type or foreshadow of the greater—death as the microcosmic analogue of the macrocosmic resurrection.
- Root: موت (mawt)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Death as the cessation of animal life; the root also yields "amāta" (to cause death) and "mayyit" (the dead).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Death is the departure of the soul from the body, a transition between two abodes; it is the "lesser resurrection" in that it separates the spirit from the corporeal frame, prefiguring the greater separation and recompense.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: biological death. Metaphorical: "the dead land" revived by rain, and here, death as a "warner" (nadhīr) and "messenger" (rasūl)—personified agencies of admonition.
- Root: علم (ʿalima)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Knowledge as perception or cognition of a thing; "ʿallama" (to teach) and "ʿālim" (the knowing one).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): ʿIlm is apprehension of a thing's reality—either its essence or a judgment about it. Here, the "knowledge" of the two resurrections distinguishes the believer (muʾmin) from the ignorant (jāhil), who sees with a "blind eye" (al-ʿayn al-ʿawrāʾ).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: certain cognition. Metaphorical: "I knew not of your news" (mā ʿalimtu bi-khabarika) meaning "I perceived not"—thus ignorance is a failure of perception, not mere absence of data.
- Root: ولي (waliya)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Nearness, guardianship, or patronage; the walī is one who assumes charge of another's affairs, whether kin or protector.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Wilāyah denotes proximity and authority; the walī of a child acts as God's deputy in discipline, mirroring the angels' custodianship of the moral ledger.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical adjacency. Metaphorical: the guardian's "inheriting the character of the angels" (waritha akhlāq al-malāʾikah)—a moral, not genealogical, inheritance.
- Sibawayh Rule: Interposition of the conditional and its apodosis (al-faṣl bayna al-sharṭ wa al-jawāb)—the periodic structure in "fa-in kunta lā tuʾminu... afalā takfīka" (if you believe not... does not suffice you?) allows the protasis to govern the rhetorical question, binding the lesser sign to the greater inference.
6:4.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

6:41.arabic: {وقال} فيكشف ما تدعون إليه إن شاء {وقال} يرزق من يشاء بغير حساب {وقال} ويغفر ما دون ذلك لمن يشاء {وقال} ويتوب الله على من يشاء وهو خلق من أخلاق الربوبية إذ قال تعالى والله شكور حليم وقد جعل الله الشكر مفتاح كلام أهل الجنة فقال تعالى وقالوا الحمد لله الذي صدقناه وعده {وقال} وآخر دعواهم أن الحمد لله رب العالمين
6:41.english: So then, what we have mentioned concerning the treatment of patience (ṣabr) regarding whispered insinuation (waswās), regarding lust (shahwah), and regarding status (jāh) — annex this to what we have already set down concerning the canons of the paths of spiritual striving (mujāhadah) in the Book of the Discipline of the Soul (Kitāb Riyāḍat al-Nafs) from the Quarter of the Destroyers (rubʿ al-muhlikāt). Adopt it as your manual (dastūr) by which you may come to know the treatment of patience in all the categories which we have previously detailed; for the detailing of individual cases is prolix. Whoever observes gradual progression (tadrīj), patience will elevate him to a state wherein patience without it becomes as arduous as it once was with it — so his affairs become inverted, and what was once beloved to him becomes loathed, and what was once detested to him becomes a sweet, wholesome draught from which he cannot bear to be patient [in abstaining]. This is known only through experience (tajribah) and tasting (dhawq). It has an analogue in customary habits: for a boy is compelled to learning in the beginning by force, and so patience with play and patience with knowledge are both arduous for him — until, when his inner sight is opened and he finds intimacy with knowledge, the matter is inverted, and it becomes arduous for him to be patient in abstaining from knowledge, and to endure play. To this points what is narrated of one of the knowers (ʿārifīn) that he asked al-Shiblī: "Patience — which of its kinds is the most severe?" He said: "Patience in God (fī Allāh)." He said: "No." He said: "Patience for God (li-Allāh)." He said: "No." He said: "Patience with God (maʿa Allāh)." He said: "No." He said: "Then what?" He said: "Patience from God (ʿan Allāh)." At that al-Shiblī cried out a cry by which his soul nearly perished. And it has been said concerning the meaning of His saying, the Exalted: {«اصبروا وصابروا ورابطوا»} "Be patient, and vie in patience, and be steadfast" (Q. 3:200): "Be patient in God, vie in patience by God, and be steadfast with God." And it was said: "Patience for God is sufficiency (ghināʾ); patience by God is endurance (baqāʾ); patience with God is fidelity (wafāʾ); and patience from God is abandonment (jafāʾ)." And it was said concerning its meaning:
6:41.section_title_en: The Revival of the Religious Sciences — Section 972: On Patience (al-Sabr) and the Commencement of Gratitude (al-Shukr)
6:41.anchors:
- Root: صبر (ṣ-b-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of restraint and withholding; al-Khalil notes its application to holding back an animal from fodder, and to enduring constraint.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الصبر: الإمساك في ضيق" — the withholding of the self in constriction; it is a general term whose specific names (shajāʿah, ḥilm, etc.) vary by context, and its opposite is al-jazaʿ (panic/vexation).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): "صبرت على ما أكره. وصبرت عما أحب" — enduring what is disliked and restraining from what is loved. Metaphorical (majāz): "صبرت يمينه" — binding an oath strenuously; "أصبر على الضرب من الأرض" — more enduring than the earth.
- Root: شكر (sh-k-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The root denotes manifestation and fullness; al-Ayn links it to an overflowing udder (shukrā).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الشكر: تصور النعمة وإظهارها" — the perception of a blessing and its display; it is the opposite of kufr (covering/denial). It has three degrees: of the heart (perception), of the tongue (praise), and of the limbs (requital).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "شكرت لله تعالى نعمته" — thanking God for His grace. Metaphorical: "دابة شكور" — a beast that thrives on little fodder, displaying its owner's care through its fatness.
- Root: علم (ʿ-l-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Knowledge as the apprehension of a thing's reality; al-Ayn treats it under the entry of umm (source/origin), indicating that knowledge is the root to which all else is annexed.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "العلم: إدراك الشيء بحقيقته" — apprehension of a thing by its true reality, either by grasping its essence or by affirming/denying a predicate of it.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "ما علمت بخبرك: ما شعرت به" — to be aware/perceive. It is also used for the landmarks (maʿālim) of the road, i.e., traces by which one is guided.
- Root: وقد (w-q-d)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The kindling and blazing of fire; al-Ayn records it under the entry of w-q-d with the sense of fuel and flame.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "وقدت النار تقد وقودا ووقدا" — the fire blazed; al-wuqūd is both the fuel and the resulting flame, as in {«وقودها الناس والحجارة»} (Q. 2:24).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "وقدت النار وقودا ووقدا، واتقدت وتوقدت" — the fire blazed and blazed fiercely. Metaphorical: "قلب وقاد" — a blazing, keen heart; "وقدة الصيف" — the blazing heat of summer.
- Sibawayh Rule: Interposition between the operative word and its object (al-faṣl bayna al-ʿāmil wa al-maʿmūl fīhi) — governing the placement of circumstantial qualifiers (ḥāl) and prepositional phrases to preserve the intended semantic restriction, as in the verse "اصبروا وصابروا ورابطوا" where each imperative carries a distinct operative scope.
6:41.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

6:44.arabic: فتحنا عليهم أبواب كل شيء حتى إذا فرحوا بما أوتوا أخذناهم بغتة فإذا هم مبلسون وفي تفسير قوله تعالى سنستدرجهم من حيث لا يعلمون أنهم كلما أحدثوا ذنبا أحدثنا لهم نعمة ليزيد غرورهم وقال تعالى إنما نملي لهم ليزدادوا إثما وقال تعالى ولا تحسبن الله غافلا عما يعمل الظالمون إنما يؤخرهم ليوم تشخص فيه الأبصار إلى غير ذلك مما ورد في كتاب الله تعالى وسنة رسوله فمن آمن به تخلص من هذا الغرور فإن منشأ هذا الغرور الجهل بالله وبصفاته فإن من عرفه لا يأمن مكره ولا يغتر بأمثال هذه الخيالات الفاسدة وينظر إلى فرعون وها
6:44.english: As for knowing it by way of authoritative transmission and affirmation (taṣdīq): it is that one believes in the Book of God — exalted is He — and affirms His Messenger. For God — exalted is He — has said: {«أيحسبون أن ما نمدهم به من مال وبنين * نسارع لهم في الخيرات بل لا يشعرون»} — "Do they reckon that what We extend to them of wealth and sons — [that] We hasten for them good things? Nay, but they do not perceive" (Q. 23:55-56). And He said — exalted is He: {«سنستدرجهم من حيث لا يعلمون»} — "We shall draw them on by degrees from whence they do not know" (Q. 7:182). And He said — exalted is He: {«فتحنا عليهم أبواب كل شيء حتى إذا فرحوا بما أوتوا أخذناهم بغتة فإذا هم مبلسون»} — "We opened upon them the gates of everything, until when they rejoiced in what they were given, We seized them suddenly, and behold, they were in despair" (Q. 6:44). And in the interpretation of His saying — exalted is He: {«سنستدرجهم من حيث لا يعلمون»} — it is said: "Whenever they innovated a sin, We innovated for them a blessing, to increase their self-deception." And He said — exalted is He: {«إنما نملي لهم ليزدادوا إثما»} — "We only grant them respite that they may increase in sin" (Q. 3:178). And He said — exalted is He: {«ولا تحسبن الله غافلا عما يعمل الظالمون إنما يؤخرهم ليوم تشخص فيه الأبصار»} — "And do not reckon God heedless of what the wrongdoers do; He only delays them to a Day when eyes will stare fixedly" (Q. 14:42). And [there is] more of that kind which has come in the Book of God — exalted is He — and in the Sunnah of His Messenger. So whoever believes in it is delivered from this self-deception. For the origin of this self-deception is ignorance of God and of His attributes; for whoever knows Him does not feel secure from His stratagem (makr) and is not deceived by such corrupt fancies.
6:44.section_title_en: Section 888 — On the Remedy for Self-Deception (Ghurūr): Recognizing the Signs of Divine Honor (Karāmah) and Humiliation (Hawān)
6:44.anchors:
- Root: غرر (gh-r-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of an outward trace or mark; heedlessness in wakefulness; the blaze on a horse's forehead.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Ghurūr" is delusion stemming from heedlessness — the soul's being overtaken while imagining security, as in {«ما غرك بربك الكريم»} (Q. 82:6). It is the state of one who is deceived by apparent favors while blind to their underlying test.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): heedlessness and exposure to predation, like a gazelle deceived by moonlight. Metaphorical (Majaz): being "deceived by God" (ightirār billāh) — trusting in His mercy while persisting in disobedience.
- Root: لهم (l-h-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Swallowing whole; the gullet.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Ilhām" — God's casting a meaning into the heart (al-raw'), distinct from demonic whispering; the channel of inner vision for the knowers (ʿārifūn).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: to swallow. Metaphorical: the heart's receptive "swallowing" of divine inspiration.
- Root: حدث (ḥ-d-th)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Origination after non-existence; newness.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Ḥudūth" — a thing's coming to be after it was not; "muḥdith" — the originator, exclusively God for substances (jawāhir). "Iḥdāth" — bringing about a novel state or act.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: temporal newness. Metaphorical: "muḥaddath" — one inspired with correct discernment, as if newly spoken-to.
- Root: نعم (n-ʿ-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Softness, ease, well-being; a state of comfort.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Niʿmah" — the good state one inhabits; "naʿīm" — the act of living pleasantly. Blessings are both a test and a sign, per {«وإن تعدوا نعمة الله لا تحصوها»} (Q. 16:18).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: bounty and comfort. Metaphorical: "khafat naʿāmatuhum" — their prosperity vanished; blessings may signal either favor or gradual ruin (istidrāj).
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction and Focused Predication with "innamā")
  * In {«إنما نملي لهم ليزدادوا إثما»} (Q. 3:178) and {«إنما يؤخرهم ليوم تشخص فيه الأبصار»} (Q. 14:42), "innamā" restricts the purpose of divine respite exclusively to increase of sin and deferred reckoning — negating any reading of it as benevolent indulgence.
6:44.topic: Al-Ghazali on constant remembrance of God and contemplative invocations, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

6:44.arabic: فلما نسوا ما ذكروا به أنجينا الذين ينهون عن السوء وأخذنا الذين ظلموا بعذاب بئيس بما كانوا يفسقون فبين أنهم استفادوا النجاة بالنهي عن السوء ويدل ذلك على الوجوب أيضا وقال تعالى الذين إن مكناهم في الأرض أقاموا الصلاة وآتوا الزكاة وأمروا بالمعروف ونهوا عن المنكر فقرن ذلك بالصلاة والزكاة في نعت الصالحين والمؤمنين وقال تعالى وتعاونوا على البر والتقوى ولا تعاونوا على الإثم والعدوان وهو أمر جزم ومعنى التعاون الحث عليه وتسهيل طرق الخير وسد سبل الشر والعدوان بحسب الإمكان وقال تعالى لولا ينهاهم الربانيون و
6:44.english: Know that the verses indicating the obligation of commanding right and forbidding wrong are numerous. Among them is His saying, may He be exalted: {«Let there arise from among you a nation inviting to good, commanding right and forbidding wrong — and those are the successful»} (Āl ʿImrān 3:104). In this verse is the declaration of obligation, for His saying, may He be exalted, "Let there be" (wal-takun) is a command, and the apparent meaning of a command is obligation. In it also is the declaration that success (falāḥ) is contingent upon it, for He restricted it and said: {«And those are the successful»}. In it also is the declaration that it is a collective obligation (farḍ kifāyah), not an individual obligation (farḍ ʿayn), and that when a group undertakes it, the obligation falls from the rest — for He did not say, "Let all of you be commanders of right," but rather said: {«Let there arise from among you a nation»}. Thus, whenever one person or a group undertakes it, the burden falls from the others, and success is particularized to those who undertake it and directly perform it. But if all of creation were to hold back from it, the burden would encompass all those capable of it without exception.
6:44.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

6:44.arabic: ذكروا به فتحنا عليهم أبواب كل شيء (3) يعني لما تركوا ما أمروا به فتحنا عليهم أبواب الخير حتى إذا فرحوا بما أوتوا أي بما أعطوا من الخير أخذناهم بغتة وعن الحسن البصري رحمه الله أن رجلا من الصحابة رضي الله عنهم رأى امرأة كان يعرفها في الجاهلية فكلمها ثم تركها فجعل الرجل يلتفت إليها وهو يمشي فصدمه حائط فأثر في وجهه فأتى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فأخبره فقال صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا أراد الله بعبد خيرا عجل له عقوبة ذنبه في الدنيا (4) وقال علي كرم الله وجهه ألا أخبركم بأرجى آية في
6:44.english: And it is related from al-Hasan al-Basri (may God have mercy on him) that a man among the Companions (may God be pleased with them) saw a woman he had known in the pre-Islamic period of ignorance. He spoke to her, then left her, but kept turning his gaze back toward her as he walked, until a wall struck him and left a mark on his face. He came to the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) and informed him of this. The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "When God desires good for a servant, He hastens the punishment of his sin for him in this world."
6:44.section_title_en: On the Divine Wisdom of Trials and the Patience of the Prophets and Righteous
6:44.anchors:
- Root: فتح (f-t-ḥ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To open, to unlock, to grant access; also victory and judgment.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In Quranic usage, opening "the doors of all things" signifies God’s granting expansive worldly means as a test, not necessarily as honor.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) for physical opening; metaphorical (majāz) here for divine facilitation of blessings that lead to heedlessness.
- Sibawayh Rule: Interposition of circumstantial clauses (ḥāl) — the parenthetical "يعني" (meaning) functions as an explanatory aside, permissible between subject and predicate for clarity.
6:44.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

6:71.arabic: تعالى بتخصيص الإضافة إليه وإن كان الكل من جهته تعالى فقال تعالى {قل إن هدى الله هو الهدى} وهو المسمى حياة في قوله تعالى {أو من كان ميتا فأحييناه وجعلنا له نورا يمشي به في الناس} والمعنى بقوله تعالى {أفمن شرح الله صدره للإسلام فهو على نور من ربه} وأما الرشد فنعني به العناية الإلهية التي تعين الإنسان عند توجهه إلى مقاصده فتقوبه على ما فيه صلاحه وتفتره عما فيه فساده ويكون ذلك من الباطن كما قال تعالى {ولقد آتينا إبراهيم رشده من قبل وكنا به عالمين} فالرشد عبارة عن هداية باعثة إلى جهة السعادة محركة إليها فالصبي إذا بلغ خبيرا بحفظ الم
6:71.english:
PageV04P107
But if one does not know what constitutes the welfare of his hereafter—so that he even supposes corruption to be welfare—then from where would mere volition benefit him? There is no benefit in volition, power, and causes except after guidance (hidāyah). For this reason, God—exalted is He—said: {«ربنا الذي أعطى كل شيء خلقه ثم هدى»} "Our Lord who gave everything its creation, then guided." And He said—exalted is He—: {«ولولا فضل الله عليكم ورحمته ما زكى منكم أحد أبدا ولكن الله يزكي من يشاء»} "And were it not for God's bounty upon you and His mercy, not one of you would ever be purified; but God purifies whom He wills." And the Prophet—peace be upon him—said: "No one enters Paradise except by the mercy of God—exalted is He—," that is, by His guidance. So it was said: "Not even you, O Messenger of God?" He said: "Not even I" (1). And guidance (hidāyah) has three stations (manāzil):
6:71.section_title_en: The Degrees of Divine Guidance (Hidāyah), Righteous Discernment (Rushd), Straightening (Tasdīd), and Divine Support (Ta'yīd)
6:71.anchors:
- Root: هدي (H-D-Y)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of gentle, gracious direction (dalālah bi-luṭf); the root also yields "gift" (hadiyyah) and the leading beasts of prey (hawādī) that guide the herd.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Guidance is "directional indication with gentleness" (dalālah bi-luṭf), distinct from mere intellectual proof; it is a divine act that may be general (to all) or specific (to the elect), and its withholding is a form of abandonment.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): "He guided him to the path" (hadāhu lil-sabīl). Metaphorical (majāz): "He guided him" meaning "he preceded him" (taqaddamahu), as a leader precedes the caravan; hence guidance is not merely pointing but active leading.
- Root: رشد (R-SH-D)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The state of being rightly directed in one's affairs; integrity of judgment; names Rāshid, Rushayd derive from it.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Rushd is the opposite of ghayy (error/ruin); it is used like hidāyah but with a nuance of practical, executive discernment—knowing the good AND being moved to pursue it. Al-Raghib explicitly distinguishes the rushd of Abraham (given before, as a special gift) from the mere legal competence (rushd) of an orphan.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "A man is rāshid or rashīd" (possessing rightness in conduct). Metaphorical: "He is of sound lineage" (huwa li-rushdah), i.e., legitimate—showing the root's extension to ontological soundness.
- Root: سدد (S-D-D)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To aim correctly, to hit the mark; the arrow that flies straight (sadīd); the opposite of deviation (ighrāḍ).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): (Not in the retrieved scholia, but by extension from the root's usage in the Qur'an, e.g., {wa-saddidū}, "and be straight/aim rightly")—it denotes the divine facilitation of the creature's movements so they align with the intended good.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "He aimed the arrow and it went straight." Metaphorical: "He was granted success in speech and action" (sudda li-l-ṣawāb).
- Root: أيد (A-Y-D)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Strength, support, reinforcement; the "aid" (ayd) of God is His empowering of His servant.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): (By extension from {إذ أيدتك بروح القدس})—divine reinforcement through a holy spirit, i.e., an immaterial power that fortifies both inner perception (baṣīrah) and outer action.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "He strengthened him" (ayyadahu). Metaphorical: Used for the conferral of spiritual power that makes the servant invincible against error.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Gradation and Specification (Tartīb wa-Takhṣīṣ) — The author structures a sequence of terms (hidāyah → rushd → tasdīd → ta'yīd) where each subsequent term is syntactically and semantically superordinate, building a hierarchy of divine acts. The particle "wa-ammā" (وأما) marks a new topic with contrastive focus, and the anaphoric references (هو، وهي) bind the exposition into a single periodic argument.
6:71.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

6:120.arabic: ظاهرة وباطنة ثم قال وذروا ظاهر الإثم وباطنه فترك باطن الإثم مما لا يعرفه الخلق من الحسد وسوء الظن والبدعة وإضمار الشر للناس إلى غير ذلك من آثام القلوب هو الشكر للنعم الباطنة وترك الإثم الظاهر بالجوارح شكر للنعمة الظاهرة بل أقول كل من عصى الله تعالى ولو فى طريفة واحدة بأن فتح جفنه مثلا حيث يجب غض البصر فقد كفر كل نعمة لله تعالى عليه في السموات والأرض وما بينهما فإن كل ما خلقه الله تعالى حتى الملائكة والسموات والأرض والحيوانات والنبات بجملته نعمة على كل واحد من العباد قد نم به انتفاعه وإن ان
6:120.english: If you say: Why were these acts not delegated to a single angel, without my needing seven angels? — For the wheat also requires one to grind it first, then one to separate the bran from it and cast away the refuse second, then one to pour water upon it third, then one to knead it fourth, then one to cut it into round balls fifth, then one to roll it into broad flat loaves sixth, then one to affix it to the oven seventh — yet a single man may undertake all of that and suffice for it. So why were not the works of the angels inwardly like the works of men outwardly? — Know that the constitution (khilqah) of the angels differs from the constitution of men. There is not a single one of them but is singular in attribute (waḥdānī al-ṣifah), having in him no admixture or composition whatsoever; hence there cannot issue from each of them save a single act. And to this points His saying, the Exalted: {«وما منا إلا له مقام معلوم»} (And there is not one of us but has a known station) {Q. 37:164}. Therefore there is among them no rivalry and no combat. Rather, their example, in the determination of the rank of each one of them and his act, is the example of the five senses: for sight does not vie with hearing in the perception of sounds, nor does smell vie with them, nor do the two contend with smell over it. And it is not like the hand and the foot — for you may grasp feebly with the toes of your foot and thereby vie with the hand — nor like when you strike another with your head and thereby vie with the hand which is the instrument of striking. Nor is it like the single man who undertakes by himself the grinding, the kneading, and the baking, for this is a kind of crookedness and deviation from equity, whose cause is the diversity of man's attributes and the diversity of his impulses: for he is not singular in attribute, and therefore he is not singular in act. For this reason we see man obeying Allah at one time and disobeying Him at another, due to the diversity of his impulses and attributes. And that is not possible in the nature of the angels; rather, they are created disposed to obedience — there is no scope for disobedience in their case. Hence, necessarily: {«لا يعصون الله ما أمرهم ويفعلون ما يؤمرون»} (They do not disobey Allah in what He commands them, and they do what they are commanded) {Q. 66:6}, and {«يسبحون الليل والنهار لا يفترون»} (They glorify night and day without ceasing) {Q. 21:20}. The one who bows among them is bowing forever, the one who prostrates among them is prostrating forever, and the one who stands is standing forever — there is no variation in their acts and no weariness, and for each one is a known station (maqām maʿlūm) which he does not overstep. And their obedience to Allah the Exalted — inasmuch as there is no scope for opposition in them — may be likened to the obedience of your limbs to you: for whenever you have resolved with firm will upon opening the eyelids, the sound eyelid has no hesitation or variation — obeying you at one time and disobeying you at another — but rather it is as though it awaits your command and your prohibition, opening and closing continuously at your signal. This resembles it in one respect but differs from it in another: for the eyelid has no knowledge of what issues from it of movement, opening and shutting, whereas the angels are living beings, knowing what they do.
6:120.section_title_en: The Division and Distribution of Nutritive Substance — The Earthly Angels and the Hierarchy of Divine Bounty
6:120.anchors:
- Root: ملك (malaka)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الملك: هو المتصرف بالأمر والنهي" — the one who governs by command and prohibition; dominion and sovereign power.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الملك: هو المتصرف بالأمر والنهي في الجمهور" — the angel (malak) as a designated agent of divine governance, distinct from human composite agency.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): "لله الملك والملكوت" — absolute sovereignty. Metaphorical (Majaz): "ملك عليه أمره إذا استولى عليه" — not applicable here; the term is used in its literal theological sense of delegated divine administration.
- Root: وحد (waḥada)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الواحد: ما لا جزء له" — that which has no part; indivisible unity.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الواحد في الحقيقة هو الشيء الذي لا جزء له البتة" — the truly one is that which has no composition whatsoever; hence "وحداني الصفة" (singular in attribute) means uncompounded in nature.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "هو واحد، وهم وحدان" — numerical unity. Here applied analogically to angelic nature: absolute simplicity without admixture.
- Root: نعم (naʿima)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "النعمة: الحالة الحسنة" — the goodly state; benefaction.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "النعمة: الحالة الحسنة... والنعمة للجنس تقال للقليل والكثير" — bounty as a genus encompassing both apparent (ẓāhirah) and inward (bāṭinah) blessings.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "جلت نعمة الله ونعماؤه" — manifest divine beneficence. Metaphorical: "خفّت نعامتهم: ذهبوا" — not applicable; the term is literal throughout.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — governing the periodic suspension of clauses (e.g., "فإن قلت... فاعلم أن") where the protasis is held in suspense before the apodosis, requiring the reader to grasp the full syntactic arc before resolution.
6:120.topic: Al-Ghazali on purifying the character, moral diseases, and spiritual remedies, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

6:122.arabic: مطمع في هذا النور فيبقى كمن مثله في الظلمات ليس بخارج منها بل كظلمات في بحر لجى يغشاه موج من فوقه موج من فوقه سحاب ظلمات بعضها فوق بعض فإذن لا سعادة إلا في معرفة الله تعالى وأما ما عدا ذلك من المعارف فمنها ما لا فائدة له أصلا كمعرفة الشعر وأنساب العرب وغيرهما ومنها ما له منفعة في الإعانة على معرفة الله تعالى كمعرفة لغة العرب والتفسير والفقه والأخبار فإن معرفة لغة العرب تعين على معرفة تفسير القرآن ومعرفة التفسير تعين على معرفة ما في القرآن من كيفية العبادات والأعمال التي تفيد تزكية النفس ومعرفة طري
6:122.english: All of these divisions are comprised within knowledge of God — of what is necessary for Him, what is impossible in His attributes, and what is permissible in His acts. Thus, knowledge of God — exalted be He — of His attributes, His acts, His wisdom in the dominion (malakūt) of the heavens and the earth, the ordering of this world and the Hereafter, and what pertains to that — this is the true perfection that draws near to God — exalted be He — the one who is described by it, and it remains a perfection for the soul after death. And this knowledge becomes a light for the knowers after death: {their light running before them and on their right hands, they saying: "Our Lord, perfect for us our light"} {«ربنا أتمم لنا نورنا»} — that is, this knowledge is the capital that leads to the disclosure of what was not disclosed in this world. Just as one who carries a hidden lamp — it is possible that this becomes the cause of increased light by another lamp from which he kindles, so that the hidden light is completed by way of supplementation — while one who has no lamp at all has no hope of that. So too, one who has no root of knowledge of God — exalted be He — has no hope in that light; he remains like one whose similitude is in darkness, not emerging from it — nay, {like darknesses in a vast deep sea, covered by wave above wave, above which is cloud: darknesses, one above another} {«كظلمات في بحر لجي يغشاه موج من فوقه موج من فوقه سحاب ظلمات بعضها فوق بعض»}. Therefore, there is no happiness save in knowledge of God — exalted be He.
6:122.section_title_en: The True Perfection of Knowledge and Its Degrees of Proximity to God
6:122.anchors:
- Root: علم (ʿ-L-M)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core sense of "knowing" as the impression of a thing's reality upon the mind; the root also carries the sense of a "mark" or "sign" by which something is distinguished and recognized.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Knowledge (ʿilm) is "the apprehension of a thing by its true reality" — divided into apprehension of the essence of a thing, and judgment upon a thing regarding what is or is not predicated of it. It is the broadest epistemic term, applicable to God and creatures alike.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) usage: "He is a sign (ʿalam) of knowledge" — knowledge is that which marks and distinguishes. The metaphorical (majāz) extension: "I knew of your news" = "I perceived it" — indicating that knowledge as proximity to God is not mere information but a transformative mark upon the soul.
- Root: عرف (ʿ-R-F)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Recognition through traces and effects; the root denotes "coming to know by way of discernment of distinguishing features."
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Maʿrifah is "apprehension of a thing through reflection and deliberation upon its effect" — more specific than ʿilm. It is the term used for the creature's knowledge of God, since it proceeds from contemplating His works, not from grasping His essence.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "I will make you recognize (la-ʾuʿarrifanna-ka) what you did" = "I will requite you for it." This underscores that maʿrifah is knowledge that returns upon the knower as a state of recompense or illumination.
- Root: نور (N-W-R)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Light as that which renders visible; the root also yields "beacon" (manār) — a landmark set upon a path for guidance.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Light is the diffused radiance that aids vision" — of two kinds: the sensory (perceived by the eye) and the intellectual (perceived by the inner eye of insight), the latter being "the light of the intellect and the light of the Qur'an."
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Metaphorical (majāz): "The matter became luminous (nāra)" = "it became clear." Light is thus the very clarity of knowledge that guides the knower through the darkness of ignorance.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Restriction and Specification (al-ḥaṣr wa al-taqyīd) — governing the use of "إنما" (innamā) to restrict perfection exclusively to knowledge of God, and the conditional-connective structure (fa-innahu, fa-kullamā) that links degrees of knowledge to degrees of proximity.
6:122.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Condemnation of Status and Ostentation'

6:122.arabic: أوحينا إليك روحا من أمرنا} وقال سبحانه أومن كان ميتا فأحييناه وجعلنا له نورا يمشي به في الناس وحيث ذكر النور والظلمة أراد به العلم والجهل كقوله {يخرجهم من الظلمات إلى النور} وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم يا أيها الناس اعقلوا عن ربكم وتواصوا بالعقل تعرفوا ما أمرتم به وما نهيتم عنه واعلموا أنه ينجدكم عند ربكم واعلموا أن العاقل من أطاع الله وإن كان دميم المنظر حقير الخطر دنيء المنزلة رث الهيئة وأن الجاهل من عصى الله تعالى وإن كان جميل المنظر عظيم الخطر شريف المنزلة حسن الهيئة فصيحا نطوقا فالقردة والخنازير أعقل عند الله تعالى ممن عصاه ولا تغتر ب
6:122.english: The Book of Seclusion ('Uzlah) — its explanation, God Most High willing. For this reason, Yūsuf ibn Asbāṭ wrote to Ḥudhayfah al-Marʿashī: "What is your opinion of one who remains, finding no one with whom to remember God Most High except that he is either sinful, or his remembrance in company is itself an act of disobedience — and that because he finds no one of his own kind?" And indeed he spoke truly, for mixing with people is never free from backbiting (ghībah), or listening to backbiting, or remaining silent upon wrongdoing (munkar). And the best of his states is that he either imparts knowledge or acquires it. Yet were this poor wretch to reflect, and to know that his imparting of knowledge is never free from the taints of ostentation (riyā'), the seeking of followers, and the desire for leadership (ri'āsah), he would know that the one who acquires knowledge from him only seeks to make it an instrument for pursuing the world and a means toward evil — so that the teacher becomes his helper therein, his support and his backer, preparing its causes for him, like one who sells a sword to a highway robber. For knowledge is like the sword: its soundness for good is like the soundness of the sword for warfare. And for this reason, it is not permitted to sell it to one whom one knows, by the indications of his circumstances, intends to use it to aid in cutting off the road.
6:122.section_title_en: The Book of Seclusion ('Uzlah) — Section 65, and The Seventh Book: On the Intellect, Its Nobility, Its Reality, and Its Divisions
6:122.anchors:
- Root: عقل (ʿaql)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The root denotes binding, restraining, and holding back; the intellect is that which restrains the soul from base desires and prevents it from straying.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "العقل يقال للقوة المتهيئة لقبول العلم، ويقال للعلم الذي يستفيده الإنسان بتلك القوة عقل" — The intellect is said of the faculty prepared for the reception of knowledge, and it is also said of the knowledge which man acquires by means of that faculty.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): intellectual apprehension and understanding. Metaphorical (Majaz): "نخلة لا تعقل الإبار" — a palm tree that does not accept pollination, i.e., does not grasp or take in.
- Root: علم (ʿilm)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Knowledge as the mark or sign by which a thing is known; the trace or landmark that guides.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "العلم: إدراك الشيء بحقيقته" — Knowledge is the apprehension of a thing in its true reality; it is of two kinds: apprehension of the essence of a thing, and judgment upon a thing regarding what exists for it or is negated of it.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: certain awareness. Metaphorical: "هو من أعلام العلم الخافقه" — he is among the lofty banners of knowledge; knowledge as a guiding landmark (maʿlam).
- Root: نور (nūr)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Light; the first to set up beacons (manār) on his path in his campaigns to guide his return.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "النور: الضوء المنتشر الذي يعين على الإبصار" — Light is the diffused radiance that aids vision; it is of two kinds: that perceived by the eye of inner insight (baṣīrah) — such as the light of the intellect and the light of the Qur'an — and that perceived by the eye of the head, such as the celestial bodies.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: illumination. Metaphorical: "نور الأمر: بينه" — he illuminated the matter: he made it clear; "وهذا أنور من ذاك: أبين" — this is more luminous than that: more evident.
- Sibawayh Rule: Restriction and Focused Predication (al-ḥaṣr wa al-taqyīd bi-innamā) — governing the exclusive attribution of a predicate to a subject, as in the author's restriction of the scholar's condition to one of two men, and the exclusion of the third.
6:122.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

6:148.arabic: أيضا {لو شاء الله ما أشركنا ولا آباؤنا} فانظر كيف كانوا صادقين في كلامهم وكيف هلكوا بصدقهم فسبحان من إذا شاء أهلك بالصدق وإذا شاء أسعد بالجهل {يضل به كثيرا ويهدي به كثيرا} فهؤلاء لما ظنوا أنهم استخدموا لأجل المساكين والفقراء أو جل الله تعالى ثم قالوا لا حظ لنا في المساكين ولا حظ لله فينا وفي أموالنا سواء أنفقنا أو أمسكنا هلكوا كما هلك الصبي لما ظن أن مقصود الوالد استخدامه لأجل
6:148.english: Likewise, if it were said: "Is oxymel (sikanjabīn) better, or the drink of the water-lily (sharāb al-līnūfar)?" — no unqualified answer could be correct at all. Indeed, if it were said to us: "Is oxymel better, or the absence of yellow bile?" — we would say: the absence of yellow bile, for oxymel is sought for the sake of something else, and that which is sought for its own sake is necessarily better than that which is sought for the sake of another.
6:148.section_title_en: The Superiority of Knowledge Over Action — The Parable of the Physician and the Child
6:148.anchors:
- Root: فضل (faḍl)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Excess or increase beyond what is required; superiority in degree.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الفضل: الزيادة عن الاقتصاد" — excess beyond moderation, divided into praiseworthy (like excess of knowledge) and blameworthy; comparative superiority of one thing over another by genus, species, or merit.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): "فاضلني فلان ففضلته" — to surpass in excellence. Here used comparatively: one act or state exceeds another in rank.
- Root: علم (ʿilm)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Knowledge as the apprehension of a thing's reality; the mark or sign by which something is known.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "العلم: إدراك الشيء بحقيقته" — apprehension of a thing's true reality, whether by direct perception of its essence or by judgment concerning it.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "هو من أعلام العلم الخافقه" — knowledge as a lofty, manifest sign; distinguished from mere action which is its instrument.
- Root: صدق (ṣidq)
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Truthfulness primarily in speech — correspondence of report with reality; may become blameworthy when it leads to ruin, as with the disbelievers who spoke truly about God's independence yet drew false conclusions.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "صدقته الحديث" — truthful in statement. Metaphorical (Majaz): "رجل صادق الحملة" — truthful in resolve. Here: the disbelievers were literally truthful in their words yet destroyed by that very truthfulness.
- Root: هلك (halak)
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Destruction on three levels: loss of something from one's possession, corruption and dissolution, and death. Used here for spiritual ruin through misapplied reasoning.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "وقعوا في المهلكة" — falling into destruction. Metaphorical: "تهالك على الشيء" — intense craving. Here: literal perdition of the soul through false inference.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The conditional structure "فإن قلت... فاعلم" (if you say... then know) governs the entire periodic sentence, requiring the apodosis to resolve the protasis with logical necessity, as in the physician analogy where praise of the medicine does not entail its intrinsic superiority.
6:148.topic: Classical commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya Ulum al-Din, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

7:12.arabic: فمن استفزته نار الغضب فقد قويت فيه قرابة الشيطان حيث قال {خلقتني من نار وخلقته من طين} فإن شأن الطين السكون والوقار وشأن النار التلظي والاستعار والحركة والاضطراب ومن نتائج الغضب الحقد والحسد وبهما هلك من هلك وفسد من فسد ومفيضهما مضغة إذا صلحت صلح معها سائر الجسد وإذا كان الحقد والحسد والغضب مما يسوق العبد إلى مواطن العطب فما أحوجه إلى معرفة معاطبه ومساويه ليحذر ذلك ويتقيه ويميطه عن القلب إن كان وينفيه ويعالجه إن رسخ في قلبه ويداويه فإن من لا يعرف الشر يقع فيه ومن عرفه فالمعرفة لا تكفيه ما لم يعرف الطريق الذي به يدفع الشر ويقصيه و
7:12.english: In the name of God, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate. Praise be to God, upon whose pardon and mercy none rely except the hopeful, and from whose evil wrath and assault none fear except the fearful — He who gradually seizes His servants from whence they know not, and who has given dominion over them to their lusts, commanding them to abandon what they desire, and who has tried them with anger while charging them to swallow their rage in what provokes them. Then He surrounded them with hardships and pleasures, and granted them respite to see how they would act. He tested their love through them, to make known the truth of what they claim. He made known to them that nothing is hidden from Him of what they conceal or proclaim, and warned them lest He seize them suddenly while they are unaware. For He said: {«They await but a single blast which will seize them while they are disputing; so they will not be able to make a bequest, nor to their families will they return»} (Q. 36:49-50). And prayers and peace be upon Muhammad, His Messenger, beneath whose banner the prophets walk, and upon his family and companions — the rightly-guided imams and the pleasing masters — prayers whose number equals the number of what has been of God's creation and what will be, and by whose blessing the first and the last are favored — and abundant peace.
7:12.section_title_en: The Book of Condemnation of Anger, Spite, and Envy — Book Five of the Quarter of Destroyers from The Revival of the Religious Sciences
7:12.anchors:
- Root: غضب (ghadab)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root meaning of anger, rage, fury; the boiling and agitation of the blood
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance — when attributed to God, it means retribution (intiqām) alone, not emotional agitation; the Prophet described it as "a live coal kindled in the heart of the son of Adam"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal vs Metaphorical — literal anger is the boiling of the blood in living beings; metaphorical usage extends to inanimate things like fire and the reins of a mount
- Root: قلب (qalb)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The heart; also the turning, overturning, and transformation of a thing from one state to another
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance — the heart is so named for its constant turning (taqallub) and fluctuation between states; it is the seat of understanding and the locus of divine address
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal vs Metaphorical — literal is the physical organ; metaphorical is the subtle spiritual reality (laṭīfah rabbāniyyah) that is the locus of knowledge and will
- Root: حسد (hasad)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Envy; the wishing for removal of another's blessing
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance — envy is the desire for the removal of a blessing from one who deserves it, sometimes accompanied by striving to remove it; the believer envies (ghibṭah) while the hypocrite envies (hasad)
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal vs Metaphorical — "Envy consumes the body as fire consumes wood"; the envier is one who wishes evil upon the blessed
- Root: هلك (halak)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Perdition, destruction, ruin; death
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance — three senses: (1) loss of a thing from one's possession while it exists elsewhere, (2) corruption and dissolution of a thing, (3) death; the Quran uses it for all three
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal vs Metaphorical — literal is physical destruction; metaphorical is the ruin of one's religion and afterlife through spiritual corruption
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The permissibility of interposing elements between a preposition and its object when the intervening material constitutes a complete, meaningful unit, as in the Quranic pattern of extended periodic sentences that delay resolution for rhetorical effect.
7:12.topic: Al-Ghazali on purifying the character, moral diseases, and spiritual remedies, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

7:12.arabic: وهذه أقيسة فاسدة تشبه قياس إبليس حيث قال {أنا خير منه خلقتني من نار وخلقته من طين} وإلى هؤلاء الإشارة بقوله تعالى {أولئك الذين اشتروا الحياة الدنيا بالآخرة فلا يخفف عنهم العذاب ولا هم ينصرون} وعلاج هذا الغرور إما بتصديق الإيمان وإما بالبرهان أما التصديق بمجرد الإيمان فهو أن يصدق الله تعالى في قوله ما عندكم ينفذ وما عند الله باق وفي قوله عز وجل {وما عند الله خير} وقوله {والآخرة خير وأبقى} وقوله {وما الحياة الدنيا إلا متاع الغرور} وقوله {فلا تغرنكم الحياة الدنيا} وقد أخبر رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بذلك طوائف من الكفار فقلدوه وصدقوه
7:12.english: Know that the saying of God Most High — {«fa-lā taghurrannakum al-ḥayātu al-dunyā wa-lā yaghurrannakum billāhi al-gharūr»} (So let not the life of this world deceive you, nor let the Deceiver deceive you concerning God) — and His saying — {«wa-lākinnakum fatantum anfusakum wa-tarabbastum wa-irtabtum wa-gharratkum al-amānī»} (But ye tempted your own souls, and ye waited, and ye doubted, and vain desires deceived you) — is sufficient for the blameworthiness of self-deception (al-ghurūr). And the Messenger of God, may God's peace and blessing be upon him, has said: "How excellent is the sleep of the intelligent and their breaking of the fast! How they outwit the wakefulness of the foolish and their striving! And verily a mustard-seed's weight [of faith] from a possessor of piety and certainty is better than the earth filled with the self-deceived." And the ḥadīth: "The intelligent man (al-kayyis) is he who takes account of his own soul and works for what is after death" — this ḥadīth was transmitted by al-Tirmidhī and Ibn Mājah from the ḥadīth of Shaddād ibn Aws.
7:12.section_title_en: Exposition of the Blameworthiness of Self-Deception (Al-Ghurūr), Its Reality, and Its Examples
7:12.anchors:
- Root: غرر (Gh-R-R)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The core meaning is "an apparent trace or mark of a thing" (al-athar al-ẓāhir), from which derives "the blaze of a horse" (ghurrat al-faras). To deceive (gharra) is to strike one's heedlessness (ghirrah) and attain one's sought desire from him, as if folding a garment upon its original crease (ṭawāhu ʿalā gharrihi).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Ghurrah is heedlessness in wakefulness, and ghirār is heedlessness with drowsiness." Theologically, it is the soul's repose upon a false semblance (shubhah) that pleases the caprice (hawā), rendering one oblivious to the true state of affairs—as in {«mā gharraka bi-rabbika al-karīm»} (What deceived thee concerning thy Generous Lord?).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): "A gazelle in a moonlit night is called agharr" because it ventures out thinking it is day and is devoured by beasts—heedlessness in perception. Metaphorical (majāz): "A day agharr muḥajjal" (a white-browed, white-legged day) for intense heat, transferring the blaze of a horse to the day's visible intensity.
- Root: جهل (J-H-L)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "Jahila bihi" — to be ignorant of it; "jāhala ʿalā qawmihi" — to act foolishly/insolently against one's people. The pre-Islamic era is "al-jāhiliyyah al-jahlā'" (the utterly ignorant age).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Ignorance (jahl) is of three kinds: (1) the soul's emptiness of knowledge (this is the root); (2) believing a thing contrary to what it is; (3) doing a thing contrary to what it ought to be, whether one's belief is sound or corrupt. Ghurūr is a species of the second kind—a false belief arising from a corrupt semblance.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "Kafā bil-shakki jahlā" (Sufficient is doubt as ignorance). Metaphorical: "Istajhalat al-rīḥ al-ghuṣn" (The wind made the branch sway violently) — transferred from mental foolishness to physical agitation.
- Root: حدث (Ḥ-D-TH)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "Al-ḥudūth: the coming-to-be of a thing after it was not." "Al-ḥadath: the novel event." "Ḥaddatha: to speak/communicate."
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Ḥudūth is the existence of a thing after non-existence, whether accident or substance. Iḥdāth is bringing it into existence. The iḥdāth of substances belongs to God alone." The "ḥadīth" (report/speech) is so-called for its temporal novelty.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "Nazalat bihi ḥawādith al-dahr" (The vicissitudes of time befell him). Metaphorical: "Kāna ʿUmar muḥaddathan" (Umar was one inspired with true discernment) — as if he were spoken to (ḥudditha) by what he conjectured.
- Root: دنا (D-N-W)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "Danā fa-huwa dānin" — he drew near. "Al-dunyā" (the lower world) is so named because it is nearer (danat) and precedes the Hereafter.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Al-dunūw: proximity by essence or by judgment, used of place, time, and station." The "adnā" (lower/nearer) is contrasted with the greater and with the better: {«a-tastabdilūna alladhī huwa adnā billadhī huwa khayr»} (Will ye take the lower in exchange for what is better?).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "Huwa danī' min al-adniyā'" (He is base, of the base ones) — but this is the homonym danu'a (baseness), distinct from danā (nearness). The dunyā's "nearness" is its temporal immediacy versus the Hereafter's deferral.
- Sibawayh Rule: Bab al-faṣl bayna al-jār wa-al-majrūr (Prepositional Interposition) — The particle "bi" in {«wa-lā yaghurrannakum billāhi al-gharūr»} governs the deceiver (al-gharūr) as the agent of deception, while "billāh" (concerning God) is the object of the deception. The syntactic structure permits the deceiver to be named after the prepositional phrase, indicating that the deception is *about* God's attributes (His forbearance, His respite) — a grammatical subtlety showing the ghurūr deceives *by means of* false notions of God, not that God Himself deceives.
7:12.topic: Al-Ghazali on the journey of the soul, death, and the Hereafter, from 'Condemnation of Delusion'

7:16.arabic: الشهوات للقلب من جوانبه قال الله تعالى إخبارا عن إبليس لأقعدن لهم صراطك المستقيم ثم لآتينهم من بين أيديهم ومن خلفهم وعن أيمانهم وعن شمائلهم وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم إن الشيطان قعد لابن آدم بطرق فقعد له بطريق الإسلام فقال أتسلم وتترك دينك ودين آبائك فعصاه وأسلم ثم قعد له بطريق الهجرة فقال أتهاجر أتدع أرضك وسمائك فعصاه وهاجر هو قعد له بطريق الجهاد فقال أتجاهد وهو تلف النفس والمال فتقاتل فتقتل فتنكح نساؤك ويقسم مالك فعصاه وجاهد (2) حديث ما من أحد إلا له شيطان الحديث تقدم فقد اتضح بهذا النوع من الاستبصار معنى الوسوسة والإلهام والملك والشيطان والتوفيق والخذلان فبعد هذا نظر من ينظر في ذات ا
7:16.english: He said — and by my father, a face that will not prosper (1) — the hadith that Satan runs through the son of Adam like the running of blood has already been mentioned. That is because hunger breaks the appetite, and the course of Satan is through the appetites. And because the appetites surround the heart from all its sides, God—exalted is He—said, informing of Iblis: {«I will surely sit in wait for them on Your straight path. Then I will come to them from before them and from behind them and from their right and from their left»} (7:16-17). And he—peace and blessings be upon him—said: "Verily, Satan sat in wait for the son of Adam on his paths. He sat for him on the path of Islam and said: 'Will you submit and abandon your religion and the religion of your forefathers?' But he disobeyed him and submitted. Then he sat for him on the path of emigration (hijrah) and said: 'Will you emigrate and abandon your land and your sky?' But he disobeyed him and emigrated. Then he sat for him on the path of jihad and said: 'Will you strive? For it is the destruction of the soul and wealth — you will fight and be killed, your women will be married and your wealth divided.' But he disobeyed him and strove." (2) The hadith "There is no one among you except that he has a companion from the jinn" has already been mentioned.
7:16.section_title_en: The Revival of the Religious Sciences — Section 598: On the Whisperings of Satan, the Divine Subtleties, and the Means of Defense
7:16.anchors:
- Root: شيط (Shayṭ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of burning, scorching, or being consumed by fire; also one who is destroyed or perishes.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): الشيطان refers to the rebellious one among jinn and mankind who leads astray; the term denotes one distanced from divine mercy.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): burning or scorching of meat. Metaphorical (Majaz): "شاط دمه" — his blood was spilled in vain; "أشاط السلطان دمه" — the ruler declared his blood forfeit. Thus Satan is so named for his being consumed by divine wrath and for his causing others to perish.
- Root: لهم (Lahm)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Swallowing or devouring greedily; the larynx or throat (al-lahāt).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): الإلهام is the casting of something into the heart (al-rawʿ), specifically from God or the higher assembly (al-malaʾ al-aʿlā). It is akin to the "touch" (lamah) of the angel or the "breathing" (nafth) into the heart.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: to swallow or gulp down. Metaphorical: a horse that "swallows the ground" (i.e., devours distance with speed); a generous man who "swallows" the needs of others. Thus ilhām is the soul's swift reception of divine inspiration, like swallowing.
- Root: علم (ʿAlima)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Knowledge as the mark or trace by which something is known; a signpost (ʿalam).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): العلم is the apprehension of a thing in its true reality (idrāk al-shayʾ bi-ḥaqīqatihi), divided into apprehension of the essence and judgment upon it.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: knowledge as direct cognition. Metaphorical: "أعلام الدين" — the towering landmarks of the religion; "معالم الطريق" — the traces by which the road is recognized. Thus knowledge is the signpost illuminating the path of salvation.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد (Restriction and Specification) — The particle "إنما" restricts the predicate to the subject alone, excluding all else. This is crucial for understanding statements like "إنما يدعو حزبه" — Satan calls only his party, restricting his influence to those who follow him.
7:16.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Disciplining the Soul'

7:16.arabic: ولما سمع بعض السلف هذا قال غفر لهم ورب الكعبة وقيل في تفسير قوله عز وجل {لأقعدن لهم صراطك المستقيم} أي طريق مكة يقعد الشيطان عليها ليمنع الناس منها وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم من حج البيت فلم يرفث ولم يفسق خرج من ذنوبه كيوم ولدته أمه (2) وقال أيضا صلى الله عليه وسلم ما رؤي الشيطان في يوم أصغر ولا أدحر ولا أحقر ولا أغيظ منه يوم عرفة (1) وما ذلك إلا لما يرى من نزول الرحمة وتجاوز الله سبحانه عن الذنوب العظام إذ يقال إن من الذنوب ذنوبا لا يكفرها إلا الوقوف بعرفة (2) وقد أسنده جعفر بن محمد إلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وذكر بعض
7:16.english: I say: The first [matter] concerning the virtue of the pilgrimage — God Most High said: {«وَأَذِّن فِي النَّاسِ بِالْحَجِّ يَأْتُوكَ رِجَالًا وَعَلَىٰ كُلِّ ضَامِرٍ يَأْتِينَ مِن كُلِّ فَجٍّ عَمِيقٍ»} (And proclaim to the people the pilgrimage; they will come to you on foot and on every lean camel, coming from every deep and distant highway). Qatādah said: When God Most High commanded Ibrāhīm (peace be upon him — and upon our Prophet and upon every chosen servant) to proclaim the pilgrimage to the people, he called out: "O people! God Most High has built a House, so perform the pilgrimage to it." And He Most High said: {«لِيَشْهَدُوا مَنَافِعَ لَهُمْ»} (That they may witness benefits for them) — it is said [these benefits are] commerce during the season and reward in the Hereafter.
7:16.section_title_en: The Virtue of the Pilgrimage (Faḍīlat al-Ḥajj)
7:16.anchors:
- Root: ح ج ج (ḥ-j-j)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning is "to repair to a place repeatedly, to seek a thing, to overcome in argument." Al-Ayn: "الحج: القصد والتردد إلى الشيء."
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الحج: القصد إلى البيت الحرام للنسك، وأصله من قصدت الشيء وأقبلت عليه."
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "قصدت فلانا وحججت إليه." Metaphorical: "حاججته فحججته" — to overcome in disputation, from the idea of repeatedly pressing one's point.
- Root: غ ف ر (gh-f-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الغفر: الستر والتغطية." Al-Ayn: "غفرت الشيء: سترته."
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الغفران والمغفرة من الله هو أن يصون العبد من أن يمسه العذاب."
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "اغفر ثوبك في الوعاء" (cover/protect your garment). Metaphorical: Divine forgiveness as protective covering of sins.
- Root: و ف د (w-f-d)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الوفد: القوم يأتون السلطان أو الرئيس زائرين أو مستعطفين."
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الوفد: القوم المجتمعون القاصدون إلى رئيس."
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "وفد فلان على الأمير" — he came as a delegate. Metaphorical: The pilgrims as "delegation of God" (وفد الله) — those who come to Him seeking honor and bounty.
- Root: ر ح م (r-ḥ-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الرحمة: الرقة والتعطف." Al-Ayn: "الرحمة: رقة القلب."
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الرحمة: رقة تقتضي الإحسان إلى المرحوم."
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "رحمت فلانا" — I felt compassion. Metaphorical: Divine mercy as the descent of blessing and pardon upon creation.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The rule governing the placement of prepositional phrases and their objects, particularly relevant in the verse {«يأتين من كل فج عميق»} where the prepositional phrase "من كل فج" is interposed between the verb and its subject, demonstrating the rhetorical emphasis on the vastness of the routes of pilgrimage.
7:16.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'Patience and Gratitude'
