16:102.arabic: إلى جبريل فقال تعالى {قل نزله روح القدس من ربك بالحق} وقال تعالى {يلقي الروح من أمره على من يشاء من عباده} وأحال الإغواء على إبليس فقال تعالى {ليضل عن سبيله} والإغواء هو استيقاف العباد دون بلوغ غاية الحكمة فانظر كيف نسبه إلى العبد الذي غضب عليه والإرشاد سياقه لهم إلى الغاية فانظر كيف نسبه إلى العبد الذي أحبه وعندك في العادة له مثال فالملك إذا كان محتاجا إلى من يسقيه الشراب وإلى من يحجمه وينظف فناء منزله عن القاذورات وكان له عبدان فلا يعين للحجامة والتنظيف إلا أقبحهما وأخسهما ولا يفوض حمل الشراب و
16:102.english: Thus was the beginning of this matter and its end. And do not understand it unless you are worthy of it. And if you are worthy of it, the eye is opened and you see, so you have no need of a leader to lead you. The blind man can indeed be led, but only to a limit. For when the path narrows and becomes sharper than a sword and finer than a hair, the bird is able to fly over it but is not able to drag a blind man behind it. And when the field becomes narrow and subtle — subtle as water, for example — and crossing is possible only by swimming, then the one skilled in the art of swimming may be able to cross by himself, and perhaps he is not able to drag another behind him. These matters bear the same relation to walking upon the way of the common masses of creatures as walking upon water bears to walking upon earth. Swimming can be learned; but as for walking upon water, it is not acquired by instruction, but rather is attained through the strength of certainty (yaqīn). For this reason it was said to the Prophet, peace be upon him, that Jesus, peace be upon him, was said to have walked upon water, and he, peace be upon him, said: "Had his certainty increased, he would have walked upon the air." {«حديث قيل له يقال إن عيسى مشى على الماء قال لو ازداد يقينا لمشي على الهواء»} — This hadith is rejected (munkar) and is not known in this form. What is known is what Ibn Abi al-Dunya narrated in the Book of Certainty from the saying of Bakr ibn Abd Allah al-Muzani, who said: The disciples lost their Prophet, and it was said to them: "He has headed toward the sea." So they set out seeking him, and when they reached the sea, behold, he was coming toward them walking upon the water. And he mentioned a hadith in which Jesus said: "If the son of Adam had a hair's breadth of certainty, he would walk upon the water." And Abu Mansur al-Daylami narrated in the Musnad al-Firdaws with a weak chain from the hadith of Muadh ibn Jabal: "If you knew God with true knowledge, you would walk upon the seas, and the mountains would be removed by your supplications." These are symbols and allusions to the meaning of aversion (karāhah) and love (maḥabbah), and good pleasure (riḍā) and wrath (ghaḍab), and gratitude (shukr) and ingratitude (kufrān) — more than this is not fitting for the science of practical conduct (ʿilm al-muʿāmalah). And God, exalted be He, struck an example of this to draw it near to the understanding of creatures, since He knew that He created the jinn and mankind only to worship Him, and their worship was the ultimate purpose of wisdom (ghāyat al-ḥikmah) with respect to them. Then He informed that He has two servants: one whom He loves, whose name is Gabriel — the Holy Spirit and the Trustworthy One — and he is with Him beloved, obeyed, trustworthy, and honored; and another whom He hates, whose name is Iblis — the accursed one, reprieved until the Day of Judgment. Then He delegated guidance (irshād) to Gabriel, saying, the Exalted: {«قل نزله روح القدس من ربك بالحق»} "Say: The Holy Spirit has brought it down from your Lord with truth" (16:102), and said, the Exalted: {«يلقي الروح من أمره على من يشاء من عباده»} "He casts the Spirit of His command upon whom He wills of His servants" (40:15). And He delegated misguidance (ighwāʾ) to Iblis, saying, the Exalted: {«ليضل عن سبيله»} "That he may lead astray from His path" (4:119). And ighwāʾ is the halting of servants short of attaining the ultimate purpose of wisdom. So observe how He attributed it to the servant with whom He was wrathful; and guidance (irshād) is the conduct of them toward the ultimate purpose — so observe how He attributed it to the servant whom He loves. And you have an example of this in custom: when a king is in need of one to give him drink and one to cup him and to clean the courtyard of his house of filth, and he has two servants, he does not appoint for cupping and cleaning except the ugliest and meanest of them, and he does not entrust the carrying of drink and perfume except to the best and most complete of them and the most beloved to him. And you should not say: "This is my act, and his act was not without my act" — for you have erred when you attributed that to yourself. Rather, He is the One who directed your motive (dāʿiyah) to the specification of the disliked act to the disliked person, and the beloved act to the beloved person, as a completion of justice (ʿadl). For His justice is sometimes completed through matters in which you have no entry, and sometimes it is completed in you — for you also are among His acts. So your motive, your power, your knowledge, your action, and all the other causes of your movements in expression — all of this is His act, which He arranged with justice in an arrangement from which moderate acts issue forth. Except that you see only yourself, and so you suppose that what appears through you in the world of witness (ʿālam al-shahādah) has no cause from the world of the unseen and the dominion (ʿālam al-ghayb wa al-malakūt). Therefore you attribute it to yourself. And you are only like the child who looks at night at the play of the juggler (mushʿabadh) who brings forth figures from behind a curtain that dance and scream and rise and sit, composed of rags that do not move by themselves — rather, they are moved by fine hair-like threads that do not appear in the darkness of night, their ends in the hand of the juggler, who is hidden from the eyes of the children. So they rejoice and marvel, supposing that those rags dance and play and rise and sit. As for the intelligent ones, they know that this is a moving (taḥrīk) and not a self-movement, but perhaps they do not know its detailed modality. And the one who knows some of its detail does not know it as the juggler knows it, to whom the command belongs and in whose hand is the pulling. Likewise, the children of the people of this world — and all creatures are children relative to the scholars — look at these persons (ashkhāṣ) and suppose that they are the movers, and so they attribute [action] to them. And the scholars know that they are moved, except that they do not know the modality of the moving — and they are the majority. Except the knowers (ʿārifūn), the scholars, and those firmly rooted in knowledge (al-rāsikhūn), for they have perceived, with the sharpness of their sight, fine spider-web threads — nay, much finer than these — suspended from heaven, their ends attached to the persons of the people of the earth. Those threads are not perceived, due to their fineness, by these outward eyes. Then they witnessed the heads of those threads in their suspension-points (manāṭāt) to which they are attached, and they witnessed for those suspension-points handles (maqābiḍ) that are in the hands of the angels who move the heavens. And they also witnessed the angels of the heavens directed toward the bearers of the Throne (ḥamalat al-ʿarsh), awaiting what descends upon them of the command from the presence of Lordship (ḥaḍrat al-rubūbiyyah) — "they do not disobey God in what He commands them, and they do what they are commanded" (66:6). And He expressed these witnessed realities in the Qur'an, and it was said: {«وفي السماء رزقكم وما توعدون»} "And in the heaven is your provision and what you are promised" (51:22). And He expressed the waiting of the angels of the heavens for what descends upon them of decree and command, and it was said: "He created seven heavens and of the earth the like of them; {«يتنزل الأمر بينهن لتعلموا أن الله على كل شيء قدير وأن الله قد أحاط بكل شيء علما»} 'the command descends between them, that you may know that God is powerful over all things and that God encompasses all things in knowledge'" (65:12). These are matters whose interpretation (taʾwīl) none knows except God and those firmly rooted in knowledge (al-rāsikhūn fī al-ʿilm). And Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, expressed the exclusivity of those firmly rooted in knowledge to sciences that the understandings of creatures cannot bear, when he recited the saying of the Exalted: {«يتنزل الأمر بينهن»} "The command descends between them," and said: "Were I to mention what I know of the meaning of this verse, you would stone me" — and in another wording: "You would say he is an unbeliever."
16:102.section_title_en: On the Degrees of Proximity to God and the Hierarchy of Those Who Perfect Divine Wisdom
16:102.anchors:
- Root: سير (s-y-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "السير: الذهاب والسفر، وسار يسير سيرا ومسيرا، والسيارة: الرفقة المسافرة"
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "السير: الانتقال من مكان إلى مكان، ويستعار للسلوك في الدين والطريقة"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): [Literal] "سار القوم: مشوا" — [Metaphorical] "سار فيه السير: مضى في الأمر، وسار ذكره: انتشر، ومنه: سيرة فلان: طريقته"
- Root: مشي (m-sh-y)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "المشي: تردد الأركان على الأرض، والماشية: الإبل والغنم لانتقالها في المرعى"
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "المشي: الانتقال من مكان إلى مكان بإرادة، ويكنى به عن النميمة، وعن شرب المسهل"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): [Literal] "مشيت وتمشيت، وهي حسنة المشية" — [Metaphorical] "مشى بطنه، وأمشاه الدواء، واستمشيت بالدواء، ومنه: مشت المرأة: كثرت أولادها"
- Root: خلق (kh-l-q)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الخلق: التقدير، والخلق: الناس، والخليقة: الطبيعة، والخلق: السجية"
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الخلق أصله: التقدير المستقيم، ويستعمل في إبداع الشيء من غير أصل ولا احتذاء"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): [Literal] "خلق الخراز الأديم: قدره قبل القطع" — [Metaphorical] "خلق الله الخلق: أوجده على تقدير أوجبته الحكمة"
- Root: نفس (n-f-s)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "النفس: الروح، والذات، والشيء النفيس"
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "النفس: الروح، وتطلق على الذات، قال تعالى: {ويحذركم الله نفسه} فنفسه: ذاته"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): [Literal] "شيء نفيس ومنفس" — [Metaphorical] "دفق نفسه أي دمه، وأصابته نفس: عين"
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — Used to distinguish exclusive attribution of actions to God versus creatures, as in "إنما أنت مثل الصبي" (You are only like a child), restricting the simile to the creature while preserving divine agency.
16:102.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

16:126.arabic: في القصاص وغيره فقال تعالى {وإن عاقبتم فعاقبوا بمثل ما عوقبتم به ولئن صبرتم لهو} خير الصابرين {وقال} صلى الله عليه وسلم صل من قطعك وأعط من حرمك واعف عمن ظلمك // ورأيت في الإنجيل قال عيسى بن مريم عليه السلام لقد قيل لكم من قبل إن السن بالسن والأنف بالأنف وأنا أقول لكم لا تقاوموا بالشر بل من ضرب خدك الأيمن فحول إليه الخد الأيسر ومن أخذ رداءك فأعطه إزارك ومن سخرك لتسير معه ميلا فسر معه ميلين وكل ذلك أمر بالصبر على الأذى فالصبر على أذى الناس من أعلى مراتب الصبر لأنه يتعاون فيه باعث الدين وباعث الشهوة والغضب جميعا
16:126.english: And acts of disobedience are the requisite of the impulse of caprice (bāʿith al-hawā). And the most severe kind of patience is patience in abstaining from those acts of disobedience that have become familiar through habit — for habit is a fifth nature. When habit is joined to lustful desire, two battalions from the battalions of Satan array themselves in concert against the battalion of God (jund Allāh) — may He be exalted — and the impulse of religion (bāʿith al-dīn) has no strength to suppress them. Then, if that act be one whose commission has been rendered easy (tayassara), patience in abstaining from it is heavier upon the soul — such as patience in abstaining from the sins of the tongue: backbiting (ghībah), falsehood, contentious disputation (mirāʾ), self-praise whether by insinuation (taʿrīḍ) or by explicit statement (taṣrīḥ), the varieties of jesting that wound hearts, the kinds of words by which one intends belittlement and contempt, and the mention of the dead with aspersion cast upon them, upon their sciences, their conduct, and their stations. For such mention is in its outward aspect (fī ẓāhirihi) backbiting, and in its inward aspect (fī bāṭinihi) self-praise. In it the soul has two lusts: one is the negation of the other [person], and the other is the affirmation of oneself. And by these two together there is completed for it that lordship (rubūbiyyah) which is innate in its disposition — and which is the very opposite of what it has been commanded regarding servanthood (ʿubūdiyyah). And because of the conjunction of the two lusts, and the ease of moving the tongue, and the fact that this becomes habitual in everyday converse, patience in abstaining from it becomes difficult. And it is among the greatest of the destructive enormities (al-mūbiqāt) — so much so that its disapproval and ugliness have been effaced from hearts by dint of its frequent repetition and the universality of familiarity with it. Thus you see a man who would, for example, wear silk and deem it utterly remote [of permissibility], yet he unleashes his tongue the whole day long against the reputations (aʿrāḍ) of people and does not deem that objectionable — notwithstanding what has come down in the report that backbiting is more severe than adultery (zinā). And God — may He be exalted — said: {«ودع أذاهم وتوكل على الله»} "And leave aside their harm and put thy trust in God" (Q. 33:48). And He said — may He be exalted: {«واصبر على ما يقولون واهجرهم هجرا جميلا»} "And be patient over what they say, and depart from them with a gracious departure" (Q. 73:10). And He said — may He be exalted: {«ولقد نعلم أنك يضيق صدرك بما يقولون فسبح بحمد ربك»} "And indeed We know that thy breast is straitened by what they say; so glorify with the praise of thy Lord" (Q. 15:97–98) — to the end of the verse. And He said — may He be exalted: {«ولتسمعن من الذين أوتوا الكتاب من قبلكم ومن الذين أشركوا أذى كثيرا وإن تصبروا وتتقوا فإن ذلك من عزم الأمور»} "And you shall surely hear from those who were given the Scripture before you and from those who associate [others with God] much harm. And if you are patient and God-fearing, indeed that is of the resolute affairs" (Q. 3:186) — that is, that you be patient in refraining from requital (mukāfaʾah). And for this reason God — may He be exalted — praised those who pardon others their due rights in retaliation (qiṣāṣ) and otherwise, saying — may He be exalted: {«وإن عاقبتم فعاقبوا بمثل ما عوقبتم به ولئن صبرتم لهو خير الصابرين»} "And if you punish, then punish with the like of that wherewith you were afflicted. And if you are patient, it is surely better for the patient" (Q. 16:126). And he — upon him be peace — said: "Maintain the bond with him who cuts you off, and give to him who withholds from you, and pardon him who wrongs you." And I have seen in the Gospel that ʿĪsā ibn Maryam — upon him be peace — said: "It was said to you of old: an eye for an eye and a nose for a nose. But I say to you: do not resist evil. Rather, whoever strikes your right cheek, turn to him PageV04P071 the left cheek; and whoever takes your cloak, give him your garment; and whoever compels you to walk with him one mile, walk with him two miles." And all of that is a command to be patient under harm. So patience under the harm of people is among the highest stations of patience, because in it the impulse of religion and the impulse of lustful desire and anger are all arrayed together [against the soul].
16:126.section_title_en: The Most Severe Forms of Patience: Abstaining from Habitual Sins and Enduring Harm
16:126.anchors:
- Root: صبر (ṣ-b-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of restraint and withholding; "ṣabara al-dābbah" = to hold back an animal without fodder; "ṣabartu nafsī" = I restrained my soul.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الصبر: حبس النفس على ما يقتضيه العقل والشرع، أو عما يقتضيان حبسها عنه" — Patience is the withholding of the soul upon what reason and Law require, or from what they require it to be withheld. When exercised against calamity it is called ṣabr alone (opposed to jazaʿ); in warfare, courage (shajāʿah); in vexing misfortune, forbearance.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): "صبرت على ما أكره. وصبرت عما أحب" — I bore patiently what I dislike, and I restrained myself from what I love. Metaphorical (majāz): "هو أصبر على الضرب من الأرض" — he is more enduring of beating than the earth.
- Root: عادة (ʿ-w-d)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Recurrence and return; habitual practice that becomes second nature through repetition.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Habit (ʿādah) as reiterated action that imprints upon the soul, rendering the act facile and its abandonment burdensome.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: return to a state or place. Metaphorical: the ingrained disposition that governs conduct.
- Root: غيب (gh-y-b)
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الغيب: مصدر غابت الشمس وغيرها: إذا استترت عن العين" — that which is concealed from the senses; applied to what is absent from human perception, though nothing is absent from God.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "تكلم بذلك عن ظهر الغيب" — he spoke of that behind the veil of the unseen. Metaphorical: "أتونا في غابة" — they came in a dense host (like tangled thickets).
- Sibawayh Rule: Prepositional Interposition (باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور) — governing the permissible separation between the preposition and its object for rhetorical emphasis, as in the periodic construction "فإن ذلك في ظاهره غيبة وفي باطنه ثناء على النفس" where the circumstantial qualifiers (ẓāhir/bāṭin) are interposed to contrast outward form with inward reality.
16:126.topic: Al-Ghazali on purifying the character, moral diseases, and spiritual remedies, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

17:111.arabic: يألفه في الملأ ولا يكون حضور الغير هو السبب في حضور الخاطر كما لا يكون حضور البهيمة سببا فما دام يفرق في أحواله بين مشاهدة إنسان ومشاهدة بهيمة فهو بعد خارج عن صفو الإخلاص مدنس الباطن بالشرك الخفي من الرياء وهذا الشرك أخفي في قلب ابن آدم من دبيب النملة السوداء في الليلة الظلماء على الصخرة الصماء (1) كما ورد في الخبر ولا يسلم من الشيطان إلا من دق نظره وسعد بعصمة الله تعالى وتوفيقه وهدايته وإلا فالشيطان ملازم للمتشعرين لعبادة الله تعالى لا يغفل عنهم لحظة حتى يحملهم على ال
17:111.english: The fourth degree, which is finer and more hidden: That people look at him while he is in prayer, and the Devil is unable to say to him, "Be humble for their sake," for he knows that he has become alert to that. So the Devil says to him: "Reflect upon the majesty of Allah the Exalted and His glory, and upon Whose presence you stand. Feel shame that Allah looks upon your heart while it is heedless of Him." So by this he summons his heart [to presence] and his limbs become submissive, and he imagines that this is the very essence of sincerity — but it is the very essence of deceit and trickery (makr wa-khidāʿ). For if his humility were due to his contemplation of divine glory, this thought (khāṭir) would accompany him in seclusion, and its presence would not be restricted to the presence of others. The sign of safety from this defilement is that this thought be familiar to him in seclusion just as it is familiar in public, and that the presence of another not be the cause of the thought's presence, just as the presence of a beast is not a cause. So long as he distinguishes in his states between the sight of a human and the sight of a beast, he remains outside the purity of sincerity, his inner being defiled by the hidden polytheism (al-shirk al-khafī) of ostentation. This polytheism is more hidden in the heart of the son of Adam than the creeping of a black ant upon a solid rock in the pitch-dark night {«كما ورد في الخبر»} — as has come in the report. None is saved from the Devil except him whose insight is penetrating and who is blessed by Allah's protection (ʿiṣmah), success (tawfīq), and guidance (hidāyah). Otherwise, the Devil clings to those who adorn themselves for the worship of Allah the Exalted, never neglecting them for a single moment, until he drives them to ostentation in every movement — even in applying kohl to the eye, trimming the moustache, perfuming oneself on Friday, and wearing garments. For these are Sunnahs at specific times, yet the self has in them a hidden share (ḥaẓẓ khafiyy) due to the linkage of creatures' gaze to them and the soul's familiarity (istī'nās) with them. The Devil calls him to do them, saying: "This is a Sunnah; it should not be abandoned." But the heart's inner impulse toward them arises only for that hidden desire, or is mixed with it by an admixture that removes it from the bounds of sincerity. Whatever is not saved from all these defilements is not sincere. Rather, even one who secludes himself (iʿtikāf) in a mosque that is well-populated, clean, and beautiful in construction — to which the temperament feels drawn — the Devil makes it attractive to him and multiplies for him the virtues of seclusion, while the hidden motive in his secret heart is the comfort of the mosque's beautiful form and the soul's rest in it. This becomes evident in his inclination toward one of two mosques, or one of two places, when it is more beautiful than the other. All of this is a mingling with the impurities of temperament (shawā'ib al-ṭabʿ) and the turbidities of the self (kudūrāt al-nafs), and a nullifier of the reality of sincerity. By my life, the alloy (ghishsh) that is mixed with pure gold has varying degrees: some predominates, some is slight, but easy to perceive; and some is so subtle that none perceives it save the discerning assayer (al-nāqid al-baṣīr). The alloy of the heart, the deceit of the Devil, and the malice of the self are far more obscure and subtler than that.
17:111.section_title_en: On the Degrees of Hidden Defilements Corrupting Sincerity (Āfāt al-Ikhlāṣ)
17:111.anchors:
- Root: ر-ء-ي (r-y)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of "seeing" (ru'yā) and "showing" (murā'āt); riyā' is the act of displaying deeds for the gaze of others.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: riyā' is a form of shirk khafī (hidden polytheism) — the soul's inclination toward created beholders (khalq) as the motive for worship, displacing exclusive orientation toward Allah.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (haqīqah): visual perception; Metaphorical (majāz): seeking social standing (jāh) through ostentatious piety — the "eye" of the beholder becomes the qiblah of the heart.
- Root: خ-ل-ص (kh-l-ṣ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Purity from admixture; the clear essence after dross is removed.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Ikhlāṣ is the purification of intention (niyyah) from every motive other than Allah; it is the state of the deed being unalloyed (khāliṣ) as gold is freed from alloy.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical refinement (taṣfiyah); Metaphorical: "akhlāṣa al-dīna lillāh" — dedicating religion exclusively to Allah, with no trace of created purpose.
- Root: ش-ي-ط (sh-y-ṭ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Burning, scorching, or spoiling by fire; the one who is "burned" (shāṭ) — hence Shayṭān as the one consumed by divine wrath.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Shayṭān as the personification of insidious suggestion (waswasah) that infiltrates the heart's intent.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: meat scorched on the fire; Metaphorical: "ashāṭa damahu" — to nullify or waste blood (i.e., to destroy a life); likewise, Shayṭān "wastes" the deed's reward by corrupting its sincerity.
- Root: ن-ف-س (n-f-s)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The self, the soul; that which breathes and has desire.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The nafs as the seat of blameworthy inclination (hawā) — its hidden pleasures (shahawāt khafiyyah) are the raw material Shayṭān exploits.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the soul's essence; Metaphorical: "nafsu-hu lā tasmaḥu" — the soul's refusal to permit an act, revealing its covert attachment to created opinion.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Interposition (al-faṣl bayna al-jār wa al-majrūr) — the subtle insertion of a clause or motive between the agent and the act; syntactically, the "hidden" element (the beholder's gaze) interposes itself within the structure of the deed, altering its grammatical and moral valence.
17:111.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Intention, Sincerity and Truthfulness'

17:111.arabic: {لقد صدق الله رسوله الرؤيا بالحق} إلى آخرها (7) وقوله سبحانه الحمد لله الذي لم يتخذ ولدا (8) الآية وخمس آيات من أول الحديد (9) وثلاثا من آخر سورة الحشر (10) وإن قرأ المسبعات العشر التي أهداها الخضر عليه السلام إلى إبراهيم التيمي رحمه الله ووصاه أن يقولها غدوة وعشية فقد استكمل الفضل وجمع له ذلك فضيلة جملة الأدعية المذكورة فقد روي عن كرز بن وبرة رحمه الله وكان من الأبدال قال أتاني أخ لي من أهل الشام فأهدى لي هدية وقال يا كرز اقبل مني هذه الهدية فإنها نعمت الهدية فقلت يا أخي ومن أهدى لك هذه الهدية قال أعطاني
17:111.english: Now, the first watch (al-wird al-awwal) is that which extends from the dawn prayer (ṣalāt al-ṣubḥ) until sunrise (ṭulūʿ al-shams). When the servant has completed his obligatory prayer, he should remain seated in his place of prayer, occupying himself with the remembrance of God most High, until the sun has risen. For it has been reported that the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "That I should sit in my assembly, remembering God most High therein, from the morning prayer until sunrise, is more beloved to me than freeing four slaves." {«لأن أقعد في مجلسي أذكر الله تعالى فيه من صلاة الغداة إلى طلوع الشمس أحب إلي من أن أعتق أربع رقاب»} And it is related that he, peace and blessings be upon him, when he had prayed the morning prayer, would sit in his place of prayer until the sun rose; and in some versions [it is added] that he would pray two rakʿahs—that is, after sunrise. Concerning the virtue of this [practice], an incalculable number of reports have come down. Al-Ḥasan related that the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, used to mention, among what he recounted of his Lord's mercy, that He said: "O son of Adam, remember Me for an hour after the dawn prayer and for an hour after the afternoon prayer, and I shall suffice you for what lies between them." {«يا ابن آدم اذكرني بعد صلاة الفجر ساعة وبعد صلاة العصر ساعة أكفك ما بينهما»}
17:111.section_title_en: The Daily Liturgy of the Devout Servant: The First Watch (After Dawn Prayer until Sunrise)
17:111.anchors:
- Root: ذكر (dhakara)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Remembrance, invocation, mention; the opposite of forgetfulness (nisyān).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Remembrance of God (dhikr) is the heart's presence with the Divine, ranging from the tongue's utterance to the heart's contemplation; it is the noblest act when accompanied by presence of heart.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): verbal mention. Metaphorical (majāz): the heart's steadfastness in knowledge of God, which is the reality of dhikr.
- Root: صلا (ṣallā)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Prayer (ṣalāh); root meaning of supplication and blessing; also "to kindle a fire" (as in ṣalā al-nār).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Ṣalāh is the servant's standing before God in humility and devotion, comprising praise, recitation, bowing, and prostration; its perfection lies in the heart's presence.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the ritual prayer with its pillars. Metaphorical: supplication (duʿā') and blessing (taṣliyah) upon the Prophet.
- Root: ورد (warada)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To arrive at water; a portion or share of something that comes regularly.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The daily portion (wird) of devotion—a set liturgy of prayers, recitations, and remembrances that the servant regularly performs at appointed times.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: arriving at a watering place. Metaphorical: the soul's regular approach to the fountain of divine grace through prescribed acts of worship.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Restriction and Specification (al-ḥaṣr wa al-taqyīd) — governing the precise enumeration of the four functions (adʿiyah, adhkār, qirā'ah, fikr) after the dawn prayer, each specified by its own governing verb and object.
17:111.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications, prayers, and their spiritual power, from 'Arrangement of Litanies'

17:111.arabic: وميدان رحب وعلى أول الميدان عتبة هي مستقر ذلك الأمر الرباني فمن لم يكن له على هذه العتبة جواز ولا لحافظ العتبة مشاهدة واستحال أن يصل الميدان فكيف بالانتهاء إلى ما وراءه من المشاهدات العالية ولذلك قيل من لم يعرف نفسه لم يعرف ربه وأنى يصادف هذا خزانة الأطباء ومن أين للطبيب أن يلاحظه بل المعنى المسمى روحا عند الطبيب بالإضافة إلى هذا الأمر الرباني كالكرة التي يحركها صولجان الملك بالإضافة إلى الملك فمن عرف الروح الطبي فظن أنه أدرك الأمر الرباني كان كمن رأى الكرة التي يحركها صولجان الملك فظن أنه رأى الملك ولا يشك في أن خطأه فاحش
17:111.english: ...the entire body, and its lights which it used to derive from the spirit have departed from it — namely, the lights of the senses, the faculties of power and will, and all that the meaning of the word "life" encompasses. This too is a brief allusion to another world among the worlds of God's blessings and the wonders of His craftsmanship and wisdom, so that one may know that {«لو كان البحر مدادا لكلمات ربي لنفد البحر قبل أن تنفد كلمات ربي»} — "If the sea were ink for the words of my Lord, the sea would surely be exhausted before the words of my Lord were exhausted" — Glory be to Him, the Exalted. So perdition to him who disbelieves in God; perdition and ruin to him who denies His blessing.
17:111.section_title_en: On the Spirit as a Divine Command — The Limits of Reason in Comprehending the Soul
17:111.anchors:
- Root: روح (rūḥ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The root denotes breath, wind, and that which gives life; al-Khalil notes its application to both the physical breath and the animating principle.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الروح والروح في الأصل واحد، وجعل الروح اسما للنفس" — the spirit and the breath share one origin, with the spirit made a name for the soul/self (nafs), distinguishing the corporeal vehicle from its immaterial source.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): The literal sense (ḥaqīqah) applies to the physical subtle body; the metaphorical extension (majāz) points to the divine command (amr) which is not spatially extended nor corporeal.
- Root: عقل (ʿaql)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The root signifies binding, restraining, and comprehending; the intellect is that which restrains the soul from error.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "العقل يقال للقوة المتهيئة لقبول العلم" — the intellect is the faculty prepared to receive knowledge, and also the knowledge acquired thereby; it is a created, limited instrument.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal usage denotes rational apprehension; metaphorical usage shows its confinement — the intellect is "bound" within the categories of substance (jawhar) and accident (ʿaraḍ), unable to exceed its proper domain.
- Root: وصف (waṣf)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Description is the mention of a thing by its attributes and qualities.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الوصف: ذكر الشيء بحليته ونعته" — description may be true or false; the divine command (amr rabbānī) admits of no descriptive definition by created intellects.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: describing an object's attributes; metaphorical: "لسانه يصف الكذب" — a tongue that describes falsehood, showing that description is limited to what the describer can encompass.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — The verse {قُلِ الرُّوحُ مِنْ أَمْرِ رَبِّي} employs restrictive predication: the spirit is not defined by essence but only attributed to the divine command, confining the answer to relation (nisbah) rather than quiddity (māhiyyah).
17:111.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

18:45.arabic: تعالى لها مثلا فقال تعالى واضرب لهم مثل الحياة الدنيا كماء أنزلناه من السماء فاختلط به نبات الأرض فأصبح هشيما تذروه الرياح والزهد في الدنيا لما أن كان ملكا حاضرا حسده الشيطان عليه فصده عنه ومعنى الزهد أن يملك العبد شهوته وغضبه فينقادان لباعث الدين وإشارة الإيمان وهذا ملك بالاستحقاق إذ به يصير صاحبه حرا وباستيلاء الشهوة عليه يصير عبدا لفرجه وبطنه وسائر أغراضه فيكون مسخرا مثل البهيمة مملوكا يستجره زمام الشهوة آخذا بمختنقه إلى حيث يريد ويهوى فما أعظم اغترار الإنسان إذ ظن أنه ينال الملك بأنه يصير مملوكا وينال الربوبية بأن يصير عبدا ومثل هذا هل يكون إلا معكوسا في الدنيا من
18:45.english: ...anxieties in [worldly] administrations, and likewise all the other means to rank. Then, whenever the means are secured and completed, the lifespan expires — until, when the earth has taken on its ornament and is adorned, and its people suppose that they are able to master it, there comes to it Our command by night or by day, and We make it a harvested stubble as if it had not flourished the day before. Thus God — exalted be He — struck for it a parable, saying — exalted be He: {And strike for them the parable of the life of this world: like water which We send down from the sky, and the vegetation of the earth mingles with it, and then it becomes dry chaff which the winds scatter} {«وَاضْرِبْ لَهُمْ مَثَلَ الْحَيَاةِ الدُّنْيَا كَمَاءٍ أَنْزَلْنَاهُ مِنَ السَّمَاءِ فَاخْتَلَطَ بِهِ نَبَاتُ الْأَرْضِ فَأَصْبَحَ هَشِيمًا تَذْرُوهُ الرِّيَاحُ»} [Al-Kahf: 45]. And asceticism (al-zuhd) in this world — because it was a present sovereignty — Satan envied him for it and barred him from it.
18:45.section_title_en: On Renouncing Status and the True Meaning of Sovereignty — The Cure for the Love of Prestige
18:45.anchors:
- Root: ملك (malaka)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root denotes possession, dominion, and the power to command and forbid; al-Farahidi notes its application to kingship and ownership alike.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Distinguishes two modes: (1) actual possession/sovereignty (al-tamalluk wa al-tawallī) and (2) the capacity/power to exercise it (al-quwwah ʿalā dhālika), whether or not one actually rules. True sovereignty belongs to him who governs his own soul.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (haqīqah): ownership of property and dominion over subjects. Metaphorical (majāz): "he mastered his anger" (malaka nafsahu ʿinda al-ghadab) — self-mastery as the paradigmatic figurative extension of kingship.
- Root: عقد (ʿabada)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Servitude and worship; the slave (ʿabd) is one who is owned and subjugated.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): ʿUbūdiyyah is the state of being subjugated to another's command; true slavery to passion is the degradation of the rational soul.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: chattel slavery. Metaphorical: he who is led by his lusts is a slave in reality, even if free in legal form.
- Root: سخر (sakhkhara)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To subjugate, compel, and employ against one's will; used of beasts and forces pressed into service.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Taskhīr is the compelled employment of a thing for another's purpose — the opposite of free, rational agency.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: subjugation of animals. Metaphorical: the man ruled by appetite is musakhkhar — driven like a beast by its halter.
- Root: دنا (dānā)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Nearness in place, time, or rank.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-dunyā (the lower world) is so named for its nearness and lowness relative to the Hereafter; it is the realm of delusion when pursued for its own sake.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: proximity. Metaphorical: the "nearer" life as the inferior, contemptible portion.
- Sibawayh Rule: Bāb al-faṣl bayna al-jār wa al-majrūr (Prepositional Interposition) — The periodic sentence structure here interposes lengthy causal and conditional clauses between the governing verb and its complements, requiring the translator to preserve the logical sequence of protasis and apodosis without collapsing the rhetorical tension of the original.
18:45.topic: Al-Ghazali on purifying the character, moral diseases, and spiritual remedies, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

18:45.arabic: أنزلناه من السماء فاختلط به نبات الأرض الآية وقال تعالى واضرب لهم مثل الحياة الدنيا كماء أنزلناه من السماء إلى قوله فأصبح هشيما تذروه الرياح وكل ما تذروه رياح الموت فهو زهرة الحياة الدنيا وكل ما لا يقطعه الموت فهو الباقيات الصالحات فقد عرفت بهذا أن كمال القدرة بالمال والجاه كمال ظني لا أصل له وأن من قصر الوقت على طلبه وظنه مقصودا فهو جاهل وإليه أشار أبو الطيب بقوله ومن ينفق الساعات في جمع ماله .
18:45.english: Therefore, the perfections are three, if we count non-change through appetites and non-submission to them as a perfection—like the perfection of knowledge and the perfection of freedom. By "freedom" I mean non-enslavement to appetites and to willing worldly causes. The perfection of power for the servant is a path to acquiring the perfection of knowledge and the perfection of freedom, but he has no path to acquiring the perfection of power that endures after his death. For his power over the very substances of wealth and over subjugating hearts and bodies is cut off by death, whereas his knowledge and his freedom are not annihilated by death; rather, they both endure as perfection within him and as a means to nearness to God—may He be exalted.
18:45.section_title_en: On True Perfection: Knowledge and Freedom Over Power, Wealth, and Status
18:45.anchors:
- Root: قدر (q-d-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of measuring, determining, and enabling; power as capacity to bring about an effect.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): True power (qudrah) belongs absolutely to God alone; for humans, it is a relative capacity, never absolute, and is a means, not an end.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (haqiqah) power is God's; metaphorical (majaz) attribution of "power" to creatures is restricted and conditional, tied to specific acts.
- Root: علم (ʿ-l-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Knowledge as apprehension of a thing's reality; also traces and signs by which one is guided.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Knowledge (ʿilm) is the apprehension of a thing's true nature or the judgment of existence or non-existence regarding it; it is the enduring perfection of the soul.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "he knew" as direct awareness; metaphorical: "he knew" as perception or discernment of signs (maʿālim) leading to truth.
- Root: موت (m-w-t)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Death as the cessation of vital functions; also the state of being inanimate or lifeless.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Death is the opposite of life; in theological context, it marks the termination of worldly capacities but not of the soul's acquired knowledge or freedom.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical death; metaphorical: "death" of the heart through ignorance or enslavement to passion, and "revival" of the land through rain as a similitude for the fleeting world.
- Sibawayh Rule: Restriction and Focused Predication (الحصر والتقييد بإنما) — Used to confine true perfection exclusively to knowledge and freedom, negating it for power, wealth, and status.
18:45.topic: Al-Ghazali on the journey of the soul, death, and the Hereafter, from 'Condemnation of Status and Ostentation'

20:50.arabic: قال تعالى {ربنا الذي أعطى كل شيء خلقه ثم هدى} وقال تعالى ولولا فضل الله عليكم ورحمته ما زكى منكم أحد أبدا ولكن الله يزكي من يشاء وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم ما من أحد يدخل الجنة إلا برحمة الله تعالى أي بهدايته فقيل ولا أنت يا رسول الله قال ولا أنا (1) وللهداية ثلاث منازل {الأولى} معرفة طريق الخير والشر المشار إليه بقوله تعالى {وهديناه النجدين} وقد أنعم الله تعالى به على كافة عباده بعضه بالعقل وبعضه على لسان الرسل ولذلك قال تعالى {وأما ثمود فهديناهم فاستحبوا العمى على الهدى} فأسباب الهدى هي الكتاب
20:50.english:
PageV04P107
But if one does not know what constitutes the welfare of his hereafter—so that he even supposes corruption to be welfare—then from where would mere volition benefit him? There is no benefit in volition, power, and causes except after guidance (hidāyah). For this reason, God—exalted is He—said: {«ربنا الذي أعطى كل شيء خلقه ثم هدى»} "Our Lord who gave everything its creation, then guided." And He said—exalted is He—: {«ولولا فضل الله عليكم ورحمته ما زكى منكم أحد أبدا ولكن الله يزكي من يشاء»} "And were it not for God's bounty upon you and His mercy, not one of you would ever be purified; but God purifies whom He wills." And the Prophet—peace be upon him—said: "No one enters Paradise except by the mercy of God—exalted is He—," that is, by His guidance. So it was said: "Not even you, O Messenger of God?" He said: "Not even I" (1). And guidance (hidāyah) has three stations (manāzil):
20:50.section_title_en: The Degrees of Divine Guidance (Hidāyah), Righteous Discernment (Rushd), Straightening (Tasdīd), and Divine Support (Ta'yīd)
20:50.anchors:
- Root: هدي (H-D-Y)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of gentle, gracious direction (dalālah bi-luṭf); the root also yields "gift" (hadiyyah) and the leading beasts of prey (hawādī) that guide the herd.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Guidance is "directional indication with gentleness" (dalālah bi-luṭf), distinct from mere intellectual proof; it is a divine act that may be general (to all) or specific (to the elect), and its withholding is a form of abandonment.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): "He guided him to the path" (hadāhu lil-sabīl). Metaphorical (majāz): "He guided him" meaning "he preceded him" (taqaddamahu), as a leader precedes the caravan; hence guidance is not merely pointing but active leading.
- Root: رشد (R-SH-D)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The state of being rightly directed in one's affairs; integrity of judgment; names Rāshid, Rushayd derive from it.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Rushd is the opposite of ghayy (error/ruin); it is used like hidāyah but with a nuance of practical, executive discernment—knowing the good AND being moved to pursue it. Al-Raghib explicitly distinguishes the rushd of Abraham (given before, as a special gift) from the mere legal competence (rushd) of an orphan.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "A man is rāshid or rashīd" (possessing rightness in conduct). Metaphorical: "He is of sound lineage" (huwa li-rushdah), i.e., legitimate—showing the root's extension to ontological soundness.
- Root: سدد (S-D-D)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To aim correctly, to hit the mark; the arrow that flies straight (sadīd); the opposite of deviation (ighrāḍ).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): (Not in the retrieved scholia, but by extension from the root's usage in the Qur'an, e.g., {wa-saddidū}, "and be straight/aim rightly")—it denotes the divine facilitation of the creature's movements so they align with the intended good.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "He aimed the arrow and it went straight." Metaphorical: "He was granted success in speech and action" (sudda li-l-ṣawāb).
- Root: أيد (A-Y-D)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Strength, support, reinforcement; the "aid" (ayd) of God is His empowering of His servant.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): (By extension from {إذ أيدتك بروح القدس})—divine reinforcement through a holy spirit, i.e., an immaterial power that fortifies both inner perception (baṣīrah) and outer action.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "He strengthened him" (ayyadahu). Metaphorical: Used for the conferral of spiritual power that makes the servant invincible against error.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Gradation and Specification (Tartīb wa-Takhṣīṣ) — The author structures a sequence of terms (hidāyah → rushd → tasdīd → ta'yīd) where each subsequent term is syntactically and semantically superordinate, building a hierarchy of divine acts. The particle "wa-ammā" (وأما) marks a new topic with contrastive focus, and the anaphoric references (هو، وهي) bind the exposition into a single periodic argument.
20:50.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

21:20.arabic: يؤمرون ويسبحون الليل والنهار لا يفترون والراكع منهم راكع أبدا والساجد منهم ساجد أبدا والقائم قائم أبدا لا اختلاف في أفعالهم ولا فتور ولكل واحد مقام معلوم لا يتعداه وطاعتهم لله تعالى من حيث لا مجال للمخالفة فيهم يمكن أن تشبه بطاعة أطرافك لك فإنك مهما جزمت الإرادة بفتح الأجفان لم يكن للجفن الصحيح تردد واختلاف في طاعتك مرة ومعصيتك أخرى بل كأنه منتظر لأمرك ونهيك ينفتح وينطبق متصلا بإشارتك فهذا يشبهه من وجه ولكن يخالفه من وجه إذ الجفن لا علم له بما يصدر منه من الحركة فتحا وإطباقا والملائك
21:20.english: If you say: Why were these acts not delegated to a single angel, without my needing seven angels? — For the wheat also requires one to grind it first, then one to separate the bran from it and cast away the refuse second, then one to pour water upon it third, then one to knead it fourth, then one to cut it into round balls fifth, then one to roll it into broad flat loaves sixth, then one to affix it to the oven seventh — yet a single man may undertake all of that and suffice for it. So why were not the works of the angels inwardly like the works of men outwardly? — Know that the constitution (khilqah) of the angels differs from the constitution of men. There is not a single one of them but is singular in attribute (waḥdānī al-ṣifah), having in him no admixture or composition whatsoever; hence there cannot issue from each of them save a single act. And to this points His saying, the Exalted: {«وما منا إلا له مقام معلوم»} (And there is not one of us but has a known station) {Q. 37:164}. Therefore there is among them no rivalry and no combat. Rather, their example, in the determination of the rank of each one of them and his act, is the example of the five senses: for sight does not vie with hearing in the perception of sounds, nor does smell vie with them, nor do the two contend with smell over it. And it is not like the hand and the foot — for you may grasp feebly with the toes of your foot and thereby vie with the hand — nor like when you strike another with your head and thereby vie with the hand which is the instrument of striking. Nor is it like the single man who undertakes by himself the grinding, the kneading, and the baking, for this is a kind of crookedness and deviation from equity, whose cause is the diversity of man's attributes and the diversity of his impulses: for he is not singular in attribute, and therefore he is not singular in act. For this reason we see man obeying Allah at one time and disobeying Him at another, due to the diversity of his impulses and attributes. And that is not possible in the nature of the angels; rather, they are created disposed to obedience — there is no scope for disobedience in their case. Hence, necessarily: {«لا يعصون الله ما أمرهم ويفعلون ما يؤمرون»} (They do not disobey Allah in what He commands them, and they do what they are commanded) {Q. 66:6}, and {«يسبحون الليل والنهار لا يفترون»} (They glorify night and day without ceasing) {Q. 21:20}. The one who bows among them is bowing forever, the one who prostrates among them is prostrating forever, and the one who stands is standing forever — there is no variation in their acts and no weariness, and for each one is a known station (maqām maʿlūm) which he does not overstep. And their obedience to Allah the Exalted — inasmuch as there is no scope for opposition in them — may be likened to the obedience of your limbs to you: for whenever you have resolved with firm will upon opening the eyelids, the sound eyelid has no hesitation or variation — obeying you at one time and disobeying you at another — but rather it is as though it awaits your command and your prohibition, opening and closing continuously at your signal. This resembles it in one respect but differs from it in another: for the eyelid has no knowledge of what issues from it of movement, opening and shutting, whereas the angels are living beings, knowing what they do.
21:20.section_title_en: The Division and Distribution of Nutritive Substance — The Earthly Angels and the Hierarchy of Divine Bounty
21:20.anchors:
- Root: ملك (malaka)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الملك: هو المتصرف بالأمر والنهي" — the one who governs by command and prohibition; dominion and sovereign power.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الملك: هو المتصرف بالأمر والنهي في الجمهور" — the angel (malak) as a designated agent of divine governance, distinct from human composite agency.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): "لله الملك والملكوت" — absolute sovereignty. Metaphorical (Majaz): "ملك عليه أمره إذا استولى عليه" — not applicable here; the term is used in its literal theological sense of delegated divine administration.
- Root: وحد (waḥada)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الواحد: ما لا جزء له" — that which has no part; indivisible unity.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الواحد في الحقيقة هو الشيء الذي لا جزء له البتة" — the truly one is that which has no composition whatsoever; hence "وحداني الصفة" (singular in attribute) means uncompounded in nature.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "هو واحد، وهم وحدان" — numerical unity. Here applied analogically to angelic nature: absolute simplicity without admixture.
- Root: نعم (naʿima)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "النعمة: الحالة الحسنة" — the goodly state; benefaction.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "النعمة: الحالة الحسنة... والنعمة للجنس تقال للقليل والكثير" — bounty as a genus encompassing both apparent (ẓāhirah) and inward (bāṭinah) blessings.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "جلت نعمة الله ونعماؤه" — manifest divine beneficence. Metaphorical: "خفّت نعامتهم: ذهبوا" — not applicable; the term is literal throughout.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — governing the periodic suspension of clauses (e.g., "فإن قلت... فاعلم أن") where the protasis is held in suspense before the apodosis, requiring the reader to grasp the full syntactic arc before resolution.
21:20.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

21:20.arabic: عن عبادته ولا يستحسرون يسبحون الليل والنهار لا يفترون ومفتاح مزيد الدرجات هي الصلوات قال الله عز وجل قد أفلح المؤمنون الذين هم في صلاتهم خاشعون فمدحهم بعد الإيمان بصلاة مخصوصة وهي المقرونة بالخشوع ثم ختم أوصاف المفلحين بالصلاة أيضا فقال تعالى والذين هم على صلواتهم يحافظون ثم قال تعالى في ثمرة تلك الصفات أولئك هم الوارثون الذين يرثون الفردوس هم فيها خالدون فوصفهم بالفلاح أولا وبوراثة الفردوس آخرا وما عندي أن هذرمة اللسان مع غفلة القلب تنتهي إلى هذا الحد ولذلك قال الله عز وجل في أضدادهم ما سلككم في
21:20.english: For the friends of God (awliyāʾ Allāh) who are granted unveiling of the dominion of the heavens and the earth (malakūt al-samāwāt wa-al-arḍ) and the secrets of lordship (asrār al-rubūbiyyah) — they are unveiled only in prayer, especially in prostration (sujūd), for the servant draws near to his Lord (Mighty and Majestic) through prostration. For this reason, He said, Most High: {«And prostrate and draw near»} (Q 96:19). And the unveiling of each worshiper is only to the measure of his purity from the turbidities of this world. It varies in strength and weakness, in abundance and scarcity, and in clarity and obscurity — until some are unveiled the very thing itself (al-shayʾ bi-ʿaynihi), while others are unveiled its likeness (al-shayʾ bi-mithālihi), just as some were shown this world in the form of a corpse, and Satan in the form of a dog crouching upon it, calling people to it.
21:20.section_title_en: The Prayer of the Humble and the Unveiling of the Unveiled — Section 140
21:20.anchors:
- Root: خ ش ع (kh-sh-ʿ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of humility, submissiveness, and lowering oneself; the physical posture of one who is abased before a greater power.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In theological terms, khushūʿ is the state of the heart's stillness and trembling before divine majesty, manifesting in the body's composure during ritual prayer (ṣalāh).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) refers to the physical lowering of the gaze and voice; metaphorical (majāz) extends to the soul's inner quietude and awe before God.
- Root: ك ش ف (k-sh-f)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To remove a covering, unveil, disclose; the act of stripping away an obstruction to reveal what lies beneath.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In Quranic usage, kashf denotes divine removal of veils (kashf al-ḥijāb) — the uncovering of unseen realities (ghayb) to the heart, as in {«We have removed from you your covering»} (Q 50:22).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: uncovering a physical object; metaphorical: the disclosure of spiritual truths (mukāshafah) to the purified heart, a technical term in Sufi epistemology.
- Root: ص ل و (ṣ-l-w)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The root denotes supplication, blessing, and the act of ritual prayer; also the burning of fire (iṣlāʾ), suggesting the consuming fervor of devotion.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-ṣalāh is the act of turning toward God in worship, encompassing both the physical rites and the inner orientation of the soul; its perfection lies in the presence of the heart.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the performance of the prescribed ritual; metaphorical: the soul's "burning" with longing and its purification through the fire of sincere devotion.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — The use of restrictive particles to single out the specific quality (khushūʿ) as the defining attribute of the believers' prayer, distinguishing it from mere mechanical performance.
21:20.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Condemnation of Pride and Conceit'

21:51.arabic: وتفتره عما فيه فساده ويكون ذلك من الباطن كما قال تعالى {ولقد آتينا إبراهيم رشده من قبل وكنا به عالمين} فالرشد عبارة عن هداية باعثة إلى جهة السعادة محركة إليها فالصبي إذا بلغ خبيرا بحفظ المال وطرق التجارة والاستنماء ولكنه مع ذلك يبذر ولا يريد الاستنماء لا يسمى رشيدا لا لعدم هدايته بل لقصور هدايته عن تحريك داعيته فكم من شخص يقدم على ما يعلم أنه يضره فقد أعطي الهداية وميز بها عن الجاهل الذي لا يدري أنه يضره ولكن ما أعطى الرشد فالرشد بهذا الاعتبار أكمل من مجرد الهداية إلى وجوه الأعمال وهي نعمة عظيمة وأما التسديد فهو توجيه حركاته إلى صوب المطلوب
21:51.english:
PageV04P107
But if one does not know what constitutes the welfare of his hereafter—so that he even supposes corruption to be welfare—then from where would mere volition benefit him? There is no benefit in volition, power, and causes except after guidance (hidāyah). For this reason, God—exalted is He—said: {«ربنا الذي أعطى كل شيء خلقه ثم هدى»} "Our Lord who gave everything its creation, then guided." And He said—exalted is He—: {«ولولا فضل الله عليكم ورحمته ما زكى منكم أحد أبدا ولكن الله يزكي من يشاء»} "And were it not for God's bounty upon you and His mercy, not one of you would ever be purified; but God purifies whom He wills." And the Prophet—peace be upon him—said: "No one enters Paradise except by the mercy of God—exalted is He—," that is, by His guidance. So it was said: "Not even you, O Messenger of God?" He said: "Not even I" (1). And guidance (hidāyah) has three stations (manāzil):
21:51.section_title_en: The Degrees of Divine Guidance (Hidāyah), Righteous Discernment (Rushd), Straightening (Tasdīd), and Divine Support (Ta'yīd)
21:51.anchors:
- Root: هدي (H-D-Y)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of gentle, gracious direction (dalālah bi-luṭf); the root also yields "gift" (hadiyyah) and the leading beasts of prey (hawādī) that guide the herd.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Guidance is "directional indication with gentleness" (dalālah bi-luṭf), distinct from mere intellectual proof; it is a divine act that may be general (to all) or specific (to the elect), and its withholding is a form of abandonment.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): "He guided him to the path" (hadāhu lil-sabīl). Metaphorical (majāz): "He guided him" meaning "he preceded him" (taqaddamahu), as a leader precedes the caravan; hence guidance is not merely pointing but active leading.
- Root: رشد (R-SH-D)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The state of being rightly directed in one's affairs; integrity of judgment; names Rāshid, Rushayd derive from it.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Rushd is the opposite of ghayy (error/ruin); it is used like hidāyah but with a nuance of practical, executive discernment—knowing the good AND being moved to pursue it. Al-Raghib explicitly distinguishes the rushd of Abraham (given before, as a special gift) from the mere legal competence (rushd) of an orphan.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "A man is rāshid or rashīd" (possessing rightness in conduct). Metaphorical: "He is of sound lineage" (huwa li-rushdah), i.e., legitimate—showing the root's extension to ontological soundness.
- Root: سدد (S-D-D)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To aim correctly, to hit the mark; the arrow that flies straight (sadīd); the opposite of deviation (ighrāḍ).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): (Not in the retrieved scholia, but by extension from the root's usage in the Qur'an, e.g., {wa-saddidū}, "and be straight/aim rightly")—it denotes the divine facilitation of the creature's movements so they align with the intended good.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "He aimed the arrow and it went straight." Metaphorical: "He was granted success in speech and action" (sudda li-l-ṣawāb).
- Root: أيد (A-Y-D)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Strength, support, reinforcement; the "aid" (ayd) of God is His empowering of His servant.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): (By extension from {إذ أيدتك بروح القدس})—divine reinforcement through a holy spirit, i.e., an immaterial power that fortifies both inner perception (baṣīrah) and outer action.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "He strengthened him" (ayyadahu). Metaphorical: Used for the conferral of spiritual power that makes the servant invincible against error.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Gradation and Specification (Tartīb wa-Takhṣīṣ) — The author structures a sequence of terms (hidāyah → rushd → tasdīd → ta'yīd) where each subsequent term is syntactically and semantically superordinate, building a hierarchy of divine acts. The particle "wa-ammā" (وأما) marks a new topic with contrastive focus, and the anaphoric references (هو، وهي) bind the exposition into a single periodic argument.
21:51.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

22:46.arabic: السموات والأرض الآية وسمي ضده عمى فقال تعالى فإنها لا تعمى الأبصار ولكن تعمي القلوب التي في الصدور وقال تعالى ومن كان في هذه أعمى فهو في الآخرة أعمى وأضل سبيلا وهذه الأمور التي كشفت للأنبياء بعضها كان بالبصر وبعضها كان بالبصيرة وسمي الكل رؤية وبالجملة من لم تكن بصيرته الباطنة ثاقبة لم يعلق به من الدين إلا قشوره وأمثلته دون لبابه وحقائقه فهذه أقسام ما ينطلق اسم العقل عليها
22:46.english: I say: Know that the washing of the eye is forbidden — that is, the eye of insight (ʿayn al-baṣīrah) is not to be washed with the water of blind imitation and mere hearsay, for it is the organ by which the realities of the intellect are disclosed. And the divisions of what the name "intellect" (al-ʿaql) is applied to have become clear: it is said of the inborn faculty (al-gharīzah), and it is said of the knowledge that is acquired through that faculty, and it is said of the state of that knowledge when it governs the soul, and it is said of the very actions that proceed from that governance.
22:46.section_title_en: The Washing of the Eye is Forbidden — On the True Meaning of Intellect (ʿAql) and Its Divisions
22:46.anchors:
- Root: عقل (ʿAql)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The root denotes binding, restraining, and holding back — the intellect is that which restrains the soul from base desires and prevents it from straying.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "العقل يقال للقوة المتهيئة لقبول العلم، ويقال للعلم الذي يستفيده الإنسان بتلك القوة عقل" — al-ʿaql is said of the faculty prepared to receive knowledge, and it is also said of the knowledge acquired by that faculty. It is the instrument of divine discernment and the locus of taklīf (moral responsibility).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): the inborn faculty of discernment. Metaphorical (Majaz): "نخلة لا تعقل الإبار إذا لم تقبله" — a palm tree that does not accept pollination is said to be "not to ʿaqil" the pollen, extending the root to the sense of "accepting/receiving." Thus, knowledge is called ʿaql metaphorically as its fruit.
- Root: بصر (Baṣar)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Sight, perception — both of the eye and of the heart.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "البصر يقال للجارحة الناظرة... ويقال لقوة القلب المدركة: بصيرة وبصر" — baṣar is said of the seeing organ, and of the perceiving power of the heart: baṣīrah and baṣar. The inner sight (baṣīrah) perceives immaterial realities.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: ocular vision. Metaphorical: "هذه آية مبصرة" — this is an illuminating sign; "واجعلني بصيرة عليهم أي رقيبا وشاهدا" — make me a watcher over them. The inner eye perceives what the outer eye cannot.
- Root: فطر (Faṭara)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To split, cleave, originate, create — the primordial act of divine creation.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "أصل الفطر: الشق طولا... وفطر الله الخلق" — the root is splitting lengthwise; God's "fatr" of creation is His originating of things. "فطرة الله التي فطر الناس عليها" — the primordial disposition upon which God originated mankind.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "فطر الله الخلق، وهو فاطر السموات: مبتدعها" — God originated creation; He is the Originator of the heavens. "وكل مولود يولد على الفطرة" — every newborn is born upon the fiṭrah, i.e., the innate disposition receptive to the religion of truth.
- Root: نفس (Nafs)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Self, soul, spirit; the innermost reality of a thing.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "النفس: الروح... وقوله: تعلم ما في نفسي ولا أعلم ما في نفسك" — nafs is the spirit/soul; "You know what is in my nafs and I know not what is in Your nafs" — the nafs is the seat of inner assent and recognition.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the self. Metaphorical: "دفق نفسه أي دمه" — he poured out his nafs, i.e., his blood. The nafs is the locus of the primordial covenant (mīthāq).
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — The construction "إنما العاقل من آمن بالله" restricts the predicate: the intellect is not merely a faculty of cleverness but is defined by its fruit — faith and God-consciousness (taqwā).
22:46.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

24:21.arabic: قال تعالى {ربنا الذي أعطى كل شيء خلقه ثم هدى} وقال تعالى ولولا فضل الله عليكم ورحمته ما زكى منكم أحد أبدا ولكن الله يزكي من يشاء وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم ما من أحد يدخل الجنة إلا برحمة الله تعالى أي بهدايته فقيل ولا أنت يا رسول الله قال ولا أنا (1) وللهداية ثلاث منازل {الأولى} معرفة طريق الخير والشر المشار إليه بقوله تعالى {وهديناه النجدين} وقد أنعم الله تعالى به على كافة عباده بعضه بالعقل وبعضه على لسان الرسل ولذلك قال تعالى {وأما ثمود فهديناهم فاستحبوا العمى على الهدى} فأسباب الهدى هي الكتاب والرسل وبصائر العقول وهي مبذولة ولا يمنع منها إلا
24:21.english:
PageV04P107
But if one does not know what constitutes the welfare of his hereafter—so that he even supposes corruption to be welfare—then from where would mere volition benefit him? There is no benefit in volition, power, and causes except after guidance (hidāyah). For this reason, God—exalted is He—said: {«ربنا الذي أعطى كل شيء خلقه ثم هدى»} "Our Lord who gave everything its creation, then guided."   * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): (Not in the retrieved scholia, but by extension from the root's usage in the Qur'an, e.g., {wa-saddidū}, "and be straight/aim rightly")—it denotes the divine facilitation of the creature's movements so they align with the intended good.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "He aimed the arrow and it went straight." Metaphorical: "He was granted success in speech and action" (sudda li-l-ṣawāb).
- Root: أيد (A-Y-D)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Strength, support, reinforcement; the "aid" (ayd) of God is His empowering of His servant.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): (By extension from {إذ أيدتك بروح القدس})—divine reinforcement through a holy spirit, i.e., an immaterial power that fortifies both inner perception (baṣīrah) and outer action.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "He strengthened him" (ayyadahu). Metaphorical: Used for the conferral of spiritual power that makes the servant invincible against error.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Gradation and Specification (Tartīb wa-Takhṣīṣ) — The author structures a sequence of terms (hidāyah → rushd → tasdīd → ta'yīd) where each subsequent term is syntactically and semantically superordinate, building a hierarchy of divine acts. The particle "wa-ammā" (وأما) marks a new topic with contrastive focus, and the anaphoric references (هو، وهي) bind the exposition into a single periodic argument.
24:21.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

24:21.arabic: عليكم ورحمته ما زكى منكم أحد أبدا ولكن الله يزكي من يشاء وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم ما من أحد يدخل الجنة إلا برحمة الله تعالى أي بهدايته فقيل ولا أنت يا رسول الله قال ولا أنا (1) وللهداية ثلاث منازل {الأولى} معرفة طريق الخير والشر المشار إليه بقوله تعالى {وهديناه النجدين} وقد أنعم الله تعالى به على كافة عباده بعضه بالعقل وبعضه على لسان الرسل ولذلك قال تعالى {وأما ثمود فهديناهم فاستحبوا العمى على الهدى} فأسباب الهدى هي الكتاب والرسل وبصائر العقول وهي مبذولة ولا يمنع منها إلا الحسد والكبر وحب الدنيا والأسبا
24:21.english:
PageV04P107
But if one does not know what constitutes the welfare of his hereafter—so that he even supposes corruption to be welfare—then from where would mere volition benefit him? There is no benefit in volition, power, and causes except after guidance (hidāyah). For this reason, God—exalted is He—said: {«ربنا الذي أعطى كل شيء خلقه ثم هدى»} "Our Lord who gave everything its creation, then guided." And He said—exalted is He—: {«ولولا فضل الله عليكم ورحمته ما زكى منكم أحد أبدا ولكن الله يزكي من يشاء»} "And were it not for God's bounty upon you and His mercy, not one of you would ever be purified; but God purifies whom He wills." And the Prophet—peace be upon him—said: "No one enters Paradise except by the mercy of God—exalted is He—," that is, by His guidance. So it was said: "Not even you, O Messenger of God?" He said: "Not even I" (1). And guidance (hidāyah) has three stations (manāzil):
24:21.section_title_en: The Degrees of Divine Guidance (Hidāyah), Righteous Discernment (Rushd), Straightening (Tasdīd), and Divine Support (Ta'yīd)
24:21.anchors:
- Root: هدي (H-D-Y)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of gentle, gracious direction (dalālah bi-luṭf); the root also yields "gift" (hadiyyah) and the leading beasts of prey (hawādī) that guide the herd.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Guidance is "directional indication with gentleness" (dalālah bi-luṭf), distinct from mere intellectual proof; it is a divine act that may be general (to all) or specific (to the elect), and its withholding is a form of abandonment.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): "He guided him to the path" (hadāhu lil-sabīl). Metaphorical (majāz): "He guided him" meaning "he preceded him" (taqaddamahu), as a leader precedes the caravan; hence guidance is not merely pointing but active leading.
- Root: رشد (R-SH-D)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The state of being rightly directed in one's affairs; integrity of judgment; names Rāshid, Rushayd derive from it.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Rushd is the opposite of ghayy (error/ruin); it is used like hidāyah but with a nuance of practical, executive discernment—knowing the good AND being moved to pursue it. Al-Raghib explicitly distinguishes the rushd of Abraham (given before, as a special gift) from the mere legal competence (rushd) of an orphan.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "A man is rāshid or rashīd" (possessing rightness in conduct). Metaphorical: "He is of sound lineage" (huwa li-rushdah), i.e., legitimate—showing the root's extension to ontological soundness.
- Root: سدد (S-D-D)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To aim correctly, to hit the mark; the arrow that flies straight (sadīd); the opposite of deviation (ighrāḍ).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): (Not in the retrieved scholia, but by extension from the root's usage in the Qur'an, e.g., {wa-saddidū}, "and be straight/aim rightly")—it denotes the divine facilitation of the creature's movements so they align with the intended good.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "He aimed the arrow and it went straight." Metaphorical: "He was granted success in speech and action" (sudda li-l-ṣawāb).
- Root: أيد (A-Y-D)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Strength, support, reinforcement; the "aid" (ayd) of God is His empowering of His servant.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): (By extension from {إذ أيدتك بروح القدس})—divine reinforcement through a holy spirit, i.e., an immaterial power that fortifies both inner perception (baṣīrah) and outer action.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "He strengthened him" (ayyadahu). Metaphorical: Used for the conferral of spiritual power that makes the servant invincible against error.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Gradation and Specification (Tartīb wa-Takhṣīṣ) — The author structures a sequence of terms (hidāyah → rushd → tasdīd → ta'yīd) where each subsequent term is syntactically and semantically superordinate, building a hierarchy of divine acts. The particle "wa-ammā" (وأما) marks a new topic with contrastive focus, and the anaphoric references (هو، وهي) bind the exposition into a single periodic argument.
24:21.topic: Al-Ghazali on purifying the character, moral diseases, and spiritual remedies, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

24:21.arabic: وقد قال الله تعالى يا أيها الذين آمنوا أنفقوا من طيبات ما كسبتم ومما أخرجنا لكم من الأرض ولا تيمموا الخبيث منه تنفقون ولستم بآخذيه إلا أن تغمضوا فيه أي لا تأخذوه إلا مع كراهية وحياء وهو معنى الإغماض فلا تؤثروا به ربكم وفي الخبر سبق درهم مائة ألف درهم (3) وذلك بأن يخرجه الإنسان وهو من أحل ماله وأجوده فيصدر ذلك عن الرضا والفرح بالبذل وقد يخرج مائة ألف درهم مما يكره من ماله فيدل ذلك على أنه ليس يؤثر الله عز وجل بشيء مما يحبه وبذلك ذم الله تعالى قوما جعلوا لله ما يكرهون فقال تعال
24:21.english: The heart is not treated save with the compound electuary (maʿjūn) of knowledge and works. And this condition among the conditions of almsgiving runs in the same course as humility (al-khushūʿ) runs in the prayer. This is established by his saying — may Allah bless him and grant him peace: "A man has nothing of his prayer save that of which he was conscious." And this is like his saying — may Allah bless him and grant him peace: "Allah does not accept the charity of the one who bestows it with reproach (al-mannān)." And like His saying — Exalted is He: {«لا تبطلوا صدقاتكم بالمن والأذى»} ("Do not nullify your charities by reproach and injury"). As for the legal opinion (fatwā) of the jurist that the alms fall in their proper place and that one's liability is discharged without this condition — that is another discussion, and we have already pointed to its meaning in the Book of Prayer.
24:21.section_title_en: The Inner Conditions of Charity — Section 175 (From The Revival of the Religious Sciences, Book of the Mysteries of Almsgiving)
24:21.anchors:
- Root: قلب (q-l-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "To turn, overturn, transform a thing from one state to another; to rotate, to flip"
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "قلب الشيء: تصريفه وصرفه عن وجه إلى وجه" — the heart is so named because of its constant turning and transformation between states
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "قلب الشيء قلبا: حوله عن وجهه" (to turn a thing from its face). Metaphorical: "رجل قلب حول: يقلب الأمور ويحتال" — one who turns matters over and manages them; "قلبوا لك الأمور" (they turned matters against you)
- Root: وجل (w-j-l)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "Fear, dread, apprehension that strikes the heart"
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الوجل: استشعار الخوف" — the sensing of fear; cited in {«إنما المؤمنون الذين إذا ذكر الله وجلت قلوبهم»}
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "رجل وجل، وقوم وجال" — a fearful man, a fearful people; "وفي قلبه وجل" — in his heart is dread
- Root: عجب (ʿ-j-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "Wonder, amazement; self-admiration, vanity"
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Self-admiration (al-ʿujb) is a destructive spiritual ailment that nullifies deeds
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: wonder at something extraordinary. Metaphorical: self-conceit regarding one's own acts of obedience
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد (Restriction & Focused Predication) — governing the precise limitation of general categories (al-ṣifāt al-khāṣṣah within al-aṣnāf al-thamāniyyah) and the conditional structure of acceptance
