29:17.arabic: مع كونه عبدا مثله ذل قبيح قال الله تعالى {إن الذين تعبدون من دون الله لا يملكون لكم رزقا فابتغوا عند الله الرزق واعبدوه واشكروا له} وقال تعالى {إن الذين تدعون من دون الله عباد أمثالكم} فالشكر باللسان من جملة الشكر وقد روي أن وفدا قدموا على عمر بن عبد العزيز رحمه الله فقام شاب ليتكلم فقال عمر الكبر الكبر فقال يا أمير المؤمنين لو كان الأمر بالسن لكان في المسلمين من هو أسكن منك فقال تكلم فقال لسنا وفد الرغبة ولا وفد الرهبة أما الرغبة فقد أوصلها إلينا فضلك وأما الرهبة فقد آمننا منها عدلك وإنما نحن وقد الشكر جئناك نشكرك باللسان وننصرف فهذه هي أصول معاني الشكر المحيطة بمجموع حقيقته
29:17.english: ...not the vision of the blessing. And al-Khawwāṣ — God's mercy upon him — said: "The gratitude of the common folk is for food, clothing, and drink; the gratitude of the elite is for the arrivals upon the hearts [of divine gnosis]." This is a station that not everyone apprehends — those whose pleasures are confined to the belly, the loins, and the sensory perceptions of colors and sounds, and who are devoid of the heart's pleasure. For the heart, in a state of health, takes delight only in the remembrance of God — exalted is He — in knowledge of Him, and in the hope of meeting Him. It only delights in other than Him when it has fallen ill through evil habits — just as some people take pleasure in eating clay, and just as some of the sick find sweet things repugnant and bitter things sweet, as it was said:
29:17.section_title_en: The Reality of Gratitude (Shukr) — Its Three Pillars and the Degrees of the Thankful
29:17.anchors:
- Root: شكر (Sh-K-R)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning is "to open, reveal, or fill"; a beast that thrives on little fodder is called *shakūr* — its fullness of body manifests its owner's care.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Gratitude is "the conceptualization of the blessing and its manifestation" (*taṣawwur al-niʿmah wa-iẓhāruhā*). It is the inverse of *kufr* (disbelief/ingratitude), which is forgetting and concealing the blessing. It has three kinds: gratitude of the heart (perceiving the blessing), of the tongue (praising the Benefactor), and of the limbs (requiting the blessing through obedience).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (*ḥaqīqah*): "I thanked God for His blessing." Metaphorical (*majāz*): A beast is called *shakūr* when little fodder suffices it and it fattens — the gratitude is manifest in its condition, not uttered by a tongue.
- Root: نعم (N-ʿ-M)
  * Lisan / Ayn: *Niʿmah* denotes a state of well-being and ease; *naʿīm* is the felicitous life therein.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): *Niʿmah* is "the good state" (*al-ḥālah al-ḥasanah*), built on the pattern of states like sitting (*jilsah*) and riding (*rikbah*). It applies to both little and much, as in {«وَإِن تَعُدُّوا نِعْمَتَ اللَّهِ لَا تُحْصُوهَا»} (Ibrahim: 34).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "God's blessing and His bounties are immense." Metaphorical: "Their ostriches departed" (*khafat naʿāmatuhum*) — meaning they fled, a metaphor for the vanishing of comfort.
- Root: قلب (Q-L-B)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To turn a thing over, to rotate it from one face to another.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "The turning of a thing: directing it and moving it from one aspect to another." The heart is so named for its constant fluctuation (*taqallub*).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "I turned the thing over." Metaphorical: "A man *qalb ḥawal*" — one who turns matters over and devises stratagems; "they turned the matters over for you" (Quran 9:48), i.e., they examined and contrived.
- Sibawayh Rule: Restriction and Focused Predication (*al-ḥaṣr wa-al-taqyīd bi-innamā*) — The particle *innamā* restricts the predicate to the subject alone, as in the author's formulation "Gratitude is only the acknowledgment of the Benefactor's blessing in a posture of humility" — a definition that confines the reality to one part (the tongue with a state of the heart) rather than the whole.
29:17.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

29:65.arabic: الحواريون نبيهم فقيل لهم توجه نحو البحر فانطلقوا يطلبونه فلما انتهو إلى البحر إذا هو قد أقبل يمشى على الماء فذكر حديثا فيه أن عيسى قال لو أن لابن آدم من اليقين شعره مشى على الماء وروى أبو منصور الديلمى فى مسند الفردوس بسند ضعيف من حديث معاذ بن جبل لو عرفتم الله حق معرفته لمشيتم على البحور ولزالت بدعائكم الجبال فهذه رموز وإشارات إلى معنى الكراهة والمحبة والرضا والغضب والشكر والكفران لا يليق بعلم المعاملة أكثر منها وقد ضرب الله تعالى مثلا لذلك تقريبا إلى أفهام الخلق إذ عرف أنه ما خلق الجن والإنس إلا ليعبدوه فكانت عبادتهم غاية ال
29:65.english: Thus was the beginning of this matter and its end. And do not understand it unless you are worthy of it. And if you are worthy of it, the eye is opened and you see, so you have no need of a leader to lead you. The blind man can indeed be led, but only to a limit. For when the path narrows and becomes sharper than a sword and finer than a hair, the bird is able to fly over it but is not able to drag a blind man behind it. And when the field becomes narrow and subtle — subtle as water, for example — and crossing is possible only by swimming, then the one skilled in the art of swimming may be able to cross by himself, and perhaps he is not able to drag another behind him. These matters bear the same relation to walking upon the way of the common masses of creatures as walking upon water bears to walking upon earth. Swimming can be learned; but as for walking upon water, it is not acquired by instruction, but rather is attained through the strength of certainty (yaqīn). For this reason it was said to the Prophet, peace be upon him, that Jesus, peace be upon him, was said to have walked upon water, and he, peace be upon him, said: "Had his certainty increased, he would have walked upon the air." {«حديث قيل له يقال إن عيسى مشى على الماء قال لو ازداد يقينا لمشي على الهواء»} — This hadith is rejected (munkar) and is not known in this form. What is known is what Ibn Abi al-Dunya narrated in the Book of Certainty from the saying of Bakr ibn Abd Allah al-Muzani, who said: The disciples lost their Prophet, and it was said to them: "He has headed toward the sea." So they set out seeking him, and when they reached the sea, behold, he was coming toward them walking upon the water. And he mentioned a hadith in which Jesus said: "If the son of Adam had a hair's breadth of certainty, he would walk upon the water." And Abu Mansur al-Daylami narrated in the Musnad al-Firdaws with a weak chain from the hadith of Muadh ibn Jabal: "If you knew God with true knowledge, you would walk upon the seas, and the mountains would be removed by your supplications." These are symbols and allusions to the meaning of aversion (karāhah) and love (maḥabbah), and good pleasure (riḍā) and wrath (ghaḍab), and gratitude (shukr) and ingratitude (kufrān) — more than this is not fitting for the science of practical conduct (ʿilm al-muʿāmalah). And God, exalted be He, struck an example of this to draw it near to the understanding of creatures, since He knew that He created the jinn and mankind only to worship Him, and their worship was the ultimate purpose of wisdom (ghāyat al-ḥikmah) with respect to them. Then He informed that He has two servants: one whom He loves, whose name is Gabriel — the Holy Spirit and the Trustworthy One — and he is with Him beloved, obeyed, trustworthy, and honored; and another whom He hates, whose name is Iblis — the accursed one, reprieved until the Day of Judgment. Then He delegated guidance (irshād) to Gabriel, saying, the Exalted: {«قل نزله روح القدس من ربك بالحق»} "Say: The Holy Spirit has brought it down from your Lord with truth" (16:102), and said, the Exalted: {«يلقي الروح من أمره على من يشاء من عباده»} "He casts the Spirit of His command upon whom He wills of His servants" (40:15). And He delegated misguidance (ighwāʾ) to Iblis, saying, the Exalted: {«ليضل عن سبيله»} "That he may lead astray from His path" (4:119). And ighwāʾ is the halting of servants short of attaining the ultimate purpose of wisdom. So observe how He attributed it to the servant with whom He was wrathful; and guidance (irshād) is the conduct of them toward the ultimate purpose — so observe how He attributed it to the servant whom He loves. And you have an example of this in custom: when a king is in need of one to give him drink and one to cup him and to clean the courtyard of his house of filth, and he has two servants, he does not appoint for cupping and cleaning except the ugliest and meanest of them, and he does not entrust the carrying of drink and perfume except to the best and most complete of them and the most beloved to him. And you should not say: "This is my act, and his act was not without my act" — for you have erred when you attributed that to yourself. Rather, He is the One who directed your motive (dāʿiyah) to the specification of the disliked act to the disliked person, and the beloved act to the beloved person, as a completion of justice (ʿadl). For His justice is sometimes completed through matters in which you have no entry, and sometimes it is completed in you — for you also are among His acts. So your motive, your power, your knowledge, your action, and all the other causes of your movements in expression — all of this is His act, which He arranged with justice in an arrangement from which moderate acts issue forth. Except that you see only yourself, and so you suppose that what appears through you in the world of witness (ʿālam al-shahādah) has no cause from the world of the unseen and the dominion (ʿālam al-ghayb wa al-malakūt). Therefore you attribute it to yourself. And you are only like the child who looks at night at the play of the juggler (mushʿabadh) who brings forth figures from behind a curtain that dance and scream and rise and sit, composed of rags that do not move by themselves — rather, they are moved by fine hair-like threads that do not appear in the darkness of night, their ends in the hand of the juggler, who is hidden from the eyes of the children. So they rejoice and marvel, supposing that those rags dance and play and rise and sit. As for the intelligent ones, they know that this is a moving (taḥrīk) and not a self-movement, but perhaps they do not know its detailed modality. And the one who knows some of its detail does not know it as the juggler knows it, to whom the command belongs and in whose hand is the pulling. Likewise, the children of the people of this world — and all creatures are children relative to the scholars — look at these persons (ashkhāṣ) and suppose that they are the movers, and so they attribute [action] to them. And the scholars know that they are moved, except that they do not know the modality of the moving — and they are the majority. Except the knowers (ʿārifūn), the scholars, and those firmly rooted in knowledge (al-rāsikhūn), for they have perceived, with the sharpness of their sight, fine spider-web threads — nay, much finer than these — suspended from heaven, their ends attached to the persons of the people of the earth. Those threads are not perceived, due to their fineness, by these outward eyes. Then they witnessed the heads of those threads in their suspension-points (manāṭāt) to which they are attached, and they witnessed for those suspension-points handles (maqābiḍ) that are in the hands of the angels who move the heavens. And they also witnessed the angels of the heavens directed toward the bearers of the Throne (ḥamalat al-ʿarsh), awaiting what descends upon them of the command from the presence of Lordship (ḥaḍrat al-rubūbiyyah) — "they do not disobey God in what He commands them, and they do what they are commanded" (66:6). And He expressed these witnessed realities in the Qur'an, and it was said: {«وفي السماء رزقكم وما توعدون»} "And in the heaven is your provision and what you are promised" (51:22). And He expressed the waiting of the angels of the heavens for what descends upon them of decree and command, and it was said: "He created seven heavens and of the earth the like of them; {«يتنزل الأمر بينهن لتعلموا أن الله على كل شيء قدير وأن الله قد أحاط بكل شيء علما»} 'the command descends between them, that you may know that God is powerful over all things and that God encompasses all things in knowledge'" (65:12). These are matters whose interpretation (taʾwīl) none knows except God and those firmly rooted in knowledge (al-rāsikhūn fī al-ʿilm). And Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, expressed the exclusivity of those firmly rooted in knowledge to sciences that the understandings of creatures cannot bear, when he recited the saying of the Exalted: {«يتنزل الأمر بينهن»} "The command descends between them," and said: "Were I to mention what I know of the meaning of this verse, you would stone me" — and in another wording: "You would say he is an unbeliever."
29:65.section_title_en: On the Degrees of Proximity to God and the Hierarchy of Those Who Perfect Divine Wisdom
29:65.anchors:
- Root: سير (s-y-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "السير: الذهاب والسفر، وسار يسير سيرا ومسيرا، والسيارة: الرفقة المسافرة"
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "السير: الانتقال من مكان إلى مكان، ويستعار للسلوك في الدين والطريقة"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): [Literal] "سار القوم: مشوا" — [Metaphorical] "سار فيه السير: مضى في الأمر، وسار ذكره: انتشر، ومنه: سيرة فلان: طريقته"
- Root: مشي (m-sh-y)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "المشي: تردد الأركان على الأرض، والماشية: الإبل والغنم لانتقالها في المرعى"
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "المشي: الانتقال من مكان إلى مكان بإرادة، ويكنى به عن النميمة، وعن شرب المسهل"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): [Literal] "مشيت وتمشيت، وهي حسنة المشية" — [Metaphorical] "مشى بطنه، وأمشاه الدواء، واستمشيت بالدواء، ومنه: مشت المرأة: كثرت أولادها"
- Root: خلق (kh-l-q)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الخلق: التقدير، والخلق: الناس، والخليقة: الطبيعة، والخلق: السجية"
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الخلق أصله: التقدير المستقيم، ويستعمل في إبداع الشيء من غير أصل ولا احتذاء"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): [Literal] "خلق الخراز الأديم: قدره قبل القطع" — [Metaphorical] "خلق الله الخلق: أوجده على تقدير أوجبته الحكمة"
- Root: نفس (n-f-s)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "النفس: الروح، والذات، والشيء النفيس"
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "النفس: الروح، وتطلق على الذات، قال تعالى: {ويحذركم الله نفسه} فنفسه: ذاته"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): [Literal] "شيء نفيس ومنفس" — [Metaphorical] "دفق نفسه أي دمه، وأصابته نفس: عين"
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — Used to distinguish exclusive attribution of actions to God versus creatures, as in "إنما أنت مثل الصبي" (You are only like a child), restricting the simile to the creature while preserving divine agency.
29:65.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

29:65.arabic: وجهل بحقائق الأمور ولذلك قال تعالى {فإذا ركبوا في الفلك دعوا الله مخلصين له الدين فلما نجاهم إلى البر إذا هم يشركون} قيل معناه أنهم يقولون لولا استواء الريح لما نجونا ومن انكشف له أمر العالم كما هو عليه علم أن الريح هو الهواء والهواء لا يتحرك بنفسه مالم يحركه محرك وكذلك محركه وهكذا إلى أن ينتهي إلى المحرك الأول الذي لا محرك له ولا هو متحرك في نفسه عز وجل فالتفات العبد في النجاة إلى الريح يضاهي التفات من أخذ لتحزرقبته كتب الملك توقيعا بالعفو عنه وتخليته فأخذ يشتغل بذكر الحبر والكاغد والقلم الذي به يكتب التوقيع يقول لولا القلم لما تخلصت فيرى نجاته من القلم لا م
29:65.english: This witnessing (mushāhadah), in which nothing appears but the One Real (al-Wāḥid al-Ḥaqq), sometimes endures and sometimes flashes suddenly like a lightning bolt — and the latter is the more frequent. Perpetuity is rare and precious. To this alluded al-Ḥusayn ibn Manṣūr al-Ḥallāj when he saw al-Khawwāṣ journeying through the lands and said to him: "In what are you engaged?" He replied: "I journey through the lands to rectify my state in trust in God (tawakkul)" — and he had been among those who trust [in God]. Al-Ḥusayn said: "You have spent your life in cultivating your outward self — so where is annihilation (fanāʾ) in unity (tawḥīd)?" It was as though al-Khawwāṣ had been engaged in rectifying the third station in unity, and so he demanded of him the fourth station. These, then, are the stations of the monotheists (muwaḥḥidūn) in unity, in summary fashion.
29:65.section_title_en: The Stations of the Monotheists (Maqāmāt al-Muwaḥḥidīn) — On the Unfolding of Unity and Its Bearing on Trust in God
29:65.anchors:
- Root: وحد (w-ḥ-d)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core sense of singularity and indivisibility; al-wāḥid as that which has no part whatsoever.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-waḥdah is "al-infirād" (exclusive solitude); the One in truth is that which admits no composition, used across six nuanced senses from generic unity to existential uniqueness.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) usage denotes numerical and essential oneness; metaphorical (majāz) extension applies to acts of exclusive agency, as in "He alone is the Agent."
- Root: وكل (w-k-l)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Entrusting, deputizing; al-tawakkul as reliance upon another as deputy.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Al-tawkīl: that you depend upon another and make him your representative"; al-Wakīl is the One who undertakes your affair — God alone, without peer.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: delegation of authority; metaphorical: the soul's utter dependence, as in "tawakkala ʿalā Allāh" — contrasted with weak "takkala" (leaning on creatures).
- Root: قلم (q-l-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Trimming/cutting of a hard substance; then the writing reed; also the arrow shaft.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The pen as instrument of inscription; in Quranic usage {«عَلَّمَ بِالْقَلَمِ»} it signals divine teaching through means — yet the means has no independent power.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the reed; metaphorical: the pen as a mere tool, utterly subjugated to the writer's hand — a paradigm for all creatures under divine power.
- Sibawayh Rule: Restriction and exclusive predication (al-ḥaṣr wa-l-taqyīd bi-innamā) — governing the assertion that agency belongs to God alone, negating it from all others, as in "lā fāʿila illā Allāh."
29:65.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Monotheism and Reliance'

32:24.arabic: وجعلها ثمرة له فقال عز من قائل وجعلنا منهم أئمة يهدون بأمرنا لما صبروا وقال تعالى وتمت كلمة ربك الحسنى على بني إسرائيل بما صبروا وقال تعالى ولنجزين الذين صبروا أجرهم بأحسن ما كانوا يعملون وقال تعالى أولئك يؤتون أجرهم مرتين بما صبروا وقال تعالى إنما يوفى الصابرون أجرهم بغير حساب فما من قربة إلا وأجرها بتقدير وحساب إلا الصبر ولأجل كون الصوم من الصبر وأنه نصف الصبر قال الله تعالى الصوم لي وأنا أجزي به فأضافه إلى نفسه من بين سائر العبادات ووعد الصابرين بأنه معهم فقال تعالى واصبروا إن الله مع الصابرين وعلق النصرة على ال
32:24.english: Allah — exalted be He — has described the patient (al-ṣābirīn) with attributes, and He mentioned patience (al-ṣabr) in the Qur’an in upwards of seventy places. He attached most of the degrees and goods to patience, making them its fruit. For He said — majestic is His utterance: {«وَجَعَلْنَا مِنْهُمْ أَئِمَّةً يَهْدُونَ بِأَمْرِنَا لَمَّا صَبَرُوا»} — “And We made from among them imams guiding by Our command, when they were patient” (Q 32:24). And He said — exalted be He: {«وَتَمَّتْ كَلِمَتُ رَبِّكَ الْحُسْنَىٰ عَلَىٰ بَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ بِمَا صَبَرُوا»} — “And the good word of your Lord was fulfilled upon the Children of Israel, because they were patient” (Q 7:137). And He said — exalted be He: {«وَلَنَجْزِيَنَّ الَّذِينَ صَبَرُوا أَجْرَهُم بِأَحْسَنِ مَا كَانُوا يَعْمَلُونَ»} — “And We shall surely recompense those who were patient their wage according to the best of what they used to do” (Q 16:96). And He said — exalted be He: {«أُولَٰئِكَ يُؤْتَوْنَ أَجْرَهُم مَّرَّتَيْنِ بِمَا صَبَرُوا»} — “Those shall be given their wage twice, because they were patient” (Q 28:54). And He said — exalted be He: {«إِنَّمَا يُوَفَّى الصَّابِرُونَ أَجْرَهُم بِغَيْرِ حِسَابٍ»} — “Only the patient shall be paid their wage without reckoning” (Q 39:10). Thus there is no act of nearness (qurbah) whose wage is not meted out by measure and account — except patience. And because fasting (al-ṣawm) is of patience, and it is half of patience, Allah — exalted be He — said: “Fasting is Mine, and I recompense it” — so He attributed it to Himself, to the exclusion of all other acts of worship. And He promised the patient that He is with them, saying — exalted be He: {«وَاصْبِرُوا إِنَّ اللَّهَ مَعَ الصَّابِرِينَ»} — “And be patient; indeed Allah is with the patient” (Q 8:46). And He made victory contingent upon patience, saying — exalted be He: {«بَلَىٰ إِن تَصْبِرُوا وَتَتَّقُوا وَيَأْتُوكُم مِّن فَوْرِهِمْ هَٰذَا يُمْدِدْكُمْ رَبُّكُم بِخَمْسَةِ آلَافٍ مِّنَ الْمَلَائِكَةِ مُسَوِّمِينَ»} — “Yes, if you are patient and God-fearing, and they come upon you in their rush, your Lord will reinforce you with five thousand marked angels” (Q 3:125). And He gathered for the patient things He gathered for no others, saying — exalted be He: {«أُولَٰئِكَ عَلَيْهِمْ صَلَوَاتٌ مِّن رَّبِّهِمْ وَرَحْمَةٌ وَأُولَٰئِكَ هُمُ الْمُهْتَدُونَ»} — “Those — upon them are blessings from their Lord, and mercy; and those — they are the rightly guided” (Q 2:157). So guidance, mercy, and blessings are all gathered for the patient. And to exhaust all the verses concerning the station of patience would be lengthy.
32:24.section_title_en: The Virtue of Patience (Ṣabr) — Its Excellence in the Qur’an, Sunnah, and Reports of the Salaf
32:24.anchors:
- Root: صبر (Ṣ-B-R)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning is “to restrain, to hold back, to bind firmly” — as in holding an animal by its halter or confining someone against departure.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Patience is “the self’s restraint upon what reason and Sacred Law require, or from what they require it to abstain from.” It is a generic term whose specific names vary by context: in calamity it is ṣabr (opposed to jazaʿ); in battle it is courage (shajāʿah); in vexation it is forbearance.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): “I bore patiently what I disliked, and I refrained patiently from what I loved.” Metaphorical (majāz): “His right hand was made to swear patiently” (i.e., bound by an emphatic oath), and “this tree is patient against cold” (i.e., unaffected by it).
- Root: عله (ʿ-L-H) — [Noted as a rare root; no direct bearing on this passage’s core terms, but included per lexical apparatus.]
- Root: ايم (A-Y-M) — [Noted as a rare root; no direct bearing on this passage’s core terms, but included per lexical apparatus.]
- Root: نفس (N-F-S)
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The self (nafs) as the locus of volitional restraint — patience is an act of the nafs holding itself back, distinguishing it from mere physical endurance.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: “a precious thing” (nafīs). Metaphorical: “he poured out his soul” (i.e., his blood), and “everything that has no flowing soul does not defile water.”
- Sibawayh Rule: Restriction and Focused Predication (Bāb al-Ḥaṣr wa al-Taqyīd bi-innamā) — Governing the exclusive clause {«إِنَّمَا يُوَفَّى الصَّابِرُونَ أَجْرَهُم بِغَيْرِ حِسَابٍ»}, where innamā restricts the reward-without-account solely to the patient, and {«الصَّوْمُ لِي وَأَنَا أَجْزِي بِهِ»}, where the predicate is focused to Allah alone.
32:24.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

33:48.arabic: الغيبة أشد من الزنا (1) وقال تعالى {ودع أذاهم وتوكل على الله} وقال تعالى {واصبر على ما يقولون واهجرهم هجرا جميلا} وقال تعالى {ولقد نعلم أنك يضيق صدرك بما يقولون فسبح بحمد ربك} الآية وقال تعالى {ولتسمعن من الذين أوتوا الكتاب من قبلكم ومن الذين أشركوا أذى كثيرا وإن تصبروا وتتقوا فإن ذلك من عزم الأمور} أي تصبروا عن المكافأة ولذلك مدح الله تعالى العافين عن حقوقهم في القصاص وغيره فقال تعالى {وإن عاقبتم فعاقبوا بمثل ما عوقبتم به ولئن صبرتم لهو} خير الصابرين {وقال} صلى الله عليه وسلم صل من قطعك وأعط من حرمك واعف عمن ظل
33:48.english: And acts of disobedience are the requisite of the impulse of caprice (bāʿith al-hawā). And the most severe kind of patience is patience in abstaining from those acts of disobedience that have become familiar through habit — for habit is a fifth nature. When habit is joined to lustful desire, two battalions from the battalions of Satan array themselves in concert against the battalion of God (jund Allāh) — may He be exalted — and the impulse of religion (bāʿith al-dīn) has no strength to suppress them. Then, if that act be one whose commission has been rendered easy (tayassara), patience in abstaining from it is heavier upon the soul — such as patience in abstaining from the sins of the tongue: backbiting (ghībah), falsehood, contentious disputation (mirāʾ), self-praise whether by insinuation (taʿrīḍ) or by explicit statement (taṣrīḥ), the varieties of jesting that wound hearts, the kinds of words by which one intends belittlement and contempt, and the mention of the dead with aspersion cast upon them, upon their sciences, their conduct, and their stations. For such mention is in its outward aspect (fī ẓāhirihi) backbiting, and in its inward aspect (fī bāṭinihi) self-praise. In it the soul has two lusts: one is the negation of the other [person], and the other is the affirmation of oneself. And by these two together there is completed for it that lordship (rubūbiyyah) which is innate in its disposition — and which is the very opposite of what it has been commanded regarding servanthood (ʿubūdiyyah). And because of the conjunction of the two lusts, and the ease of moving the tongue, and the fact that this becomes habitual in everyday converse, patience in abstaining from it becomes difficult. And it is among the greatest of the destructive enormities (al-mūbiqāt) — so much so that its disapproval and ugliness have been effaced from hearts by dint of its frequent repetition and the universality of familiarity with it. Thus you see a man who would, for example, wear silk and deem it utterly remote [of permissibility], yet he unleashes his tongue the whole day long against the reputations (aʿrāḍ) of people and does not deem that objectionable — notwithstanding what has come down in the report that backbiting is more severe than adultery (zinā). And God — may He be exalted — said: {«ودع أذاهم وتوكل على الله»} "And leave aside their harm and put thy trust in God" (Q. 33:48). And He said — may He be exalted: {«واصبر على ما يقولون واهجرهم هجرا جميلا»} "And be patient over what they say, and depart from them with a gracious departure" (Q. 73:10). And He said — may He be exalted: {«ولقد نعلم أنك يضيق صدرك بما يقولون فسبح بحمد ربك»} "And indeed We know that thy breast is straitened by what they say; so glorify with the praise of thy Lord" (Q. 15:97–98) — to the end of the verse. And He said — may He be exalted: {«ولتسمعن من الذين أوتوا الكتاب من قبلكم ومن الذين أشركوا أذى كثيرا وإن تصبروا وتتقوا فإن ذلك من عزم الأمور»} "And you shall surely hear from those who were given the Scripture before you and from those who associate [others with God] much harm. And if you are patient and God-fearing, indeed that is of the resolute affairs" (Q. 3:186) — that is, that you be patient in refraining from requital (mukāfaʾah). And for this reason God — may He be exalted — praised those who pardon others their due rights in retaliation (qiṣāṣ) and otherwise, saying — may He be exalted: {«وإن عاقبتم فعاقبوا بمثل ما عوقبتم به ولئن صبرتم لهو خير الصابرين»} "And if you punish, then punish with the like of that wherewith you were afflicted. And if you are patient, it is surely better for the patient" (Q. 16:126). And he — upon him be peace — said: "Maintain the bond with him who cuts you off, and give to him who withholds from you, and pardon him who wrongs you." And I have seen in the Gospel that ʿĪsā ibn Maryam — upon him be peace — said: "It was said to you of old: an eye for an eye and a nose for a nose. But I say to you: do not resist evil. Rather, whoever strikes your right cheek, turn to him PageV04P071 the left cheek; and whoever takes your cloak, give him your garment; and whoever compels you to walk with him one mile, walk with him two miles." And all of that is a command to be patient under harm. So patience under the harm of people is among the highest stations of patience, because in it the impulse of religion and the impulse of lustful desire and anger are all arrayed together [against the soul].
33:48.section_title_en: The Most Severe Forms of Patience: Abstaining from Habitual Sins and Enduring Harm
33:48.anchors:
- Root: صبر (ṣ-b-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of restraint and withholding; "ṣabara al-dābbah" = to hold back an animal without fodder; "ṣabartu nafsī" = I restrained my soul.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الصبر: حبس النفس على ما يقتضيه العقل والشرع، أو عما يقتضيان حبسها عنه" — Patience is the withholding of the soul upon what reason and Law require, or from what they require it to be withheld. When exercised against calamity it is called ṣabr alone (opposed to jazaʿ); in warfare, courage (shajāʿah); in vexing misfortune, forbearance.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): "صبرت على ما أكره. وصبرت عما أحب" — I bore patiently what I dislike, and I restrained myself from what I love. Metaphorical (majāz): "هو أصبر على الضرب من الأرض" — he is more enduring of beating than the earth.
- Root: عادة (ʿ-w-d)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Recurrence and return; habitual practice that becomes second nature through repetition.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Habit (ʿādah) as reiterated action that imprints upon the soul, rendering the act facile and its abandonment burdensome.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: return to a state or place. Metaphorical: the ingrained disposition that governs conduct.
- Root: غيب (gh-y-b)
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الغيب: مصدر غابت الشمس وغيرها: إذا استترت عن العين" — that which is concealed from the senses; applied to what is absent from human perception, though nothing is absent from God.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "تكلم بذلك عن ظهر الغيب" — he spoke of that behind the veil of the unseen. Metaphorical: "أتونا في غابة" — they came in a dense host (like tangled thickets).
- Sibawayh Rule: Prepositional Interposition (باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور) — governing the permissible separation between the preposition and its object for rhetorical emphasis, as in the periodic construction "فإن ذلك في ظاهره غيبة وفي باطنه ثناء على النفس" where the circumstantial qualifiers (ẓāhir/bāṭin) are interposed to contrast outward form with inward reality.
33:48.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

34:1.arabic: عن هذا الترجيح بالملك وهو مجاز محض إذ لا ملك إلا لملك الملوك الذي له ما في السموات والأرض وكيف يكون العبد مالكا وهو في نفسه ليس يملك نفسه بل هو ملك غيره نعم الخلق عباد الله والأرض مائدة الله وقد أذن لهم في الأكل من مائدته بقدر حاجتهم كالملك ينصب مائدة لعبيده فمن أخذ لقمة بيمينه واحتوت عليها براجمه فجاء عبد آخر وأراد انتزاعها
34:1.english: ...to your heart, so that your heart becomes bound by it, and thus your body becomes bound in that direction in a posture of stillness and solemnity when you worship your Lord. Likewise, your actions are divided into those that are noble — such as acts of obedience — and those that are base — such as relieving oneself or spitting. So when you spit toward the direction of the Qiblah, you have indeed wronged it (ẓalamtahā) and shown ingratitude for the blessing (niʿmah) of Allah Most High upon you, by virtue of His placing the Qiblah, through whose placement the perfection of your worship is achieved. Similarly, when you put on your leather sock (khuff) and begin with the left foot, you have wronged (ẓalamta), because the sock is a protection for the foot; the foot has a share in it, and in matters of shares and portions, one ought to begin with the nobler — that is justice (al-ʿadl) and fidelity to wisdom, while its opposite is injustice (ẓulm) and ingratitude for the blessing of the sock and the foot. And this, in the eyes of the knowers (al-ʿārifīn), is a grave offense (kabīrah), even if the jurist (al-faqīh) labels it merely "disliked" (makrūh) — to the extent that one of them (the righteous predecessors) had gathered many measures of wheat and was giving them in charity, and when asked about the reason, he said: "I once put on a sandal and began with the left foot inadvertently, so I wish to expiate that (kufr) through charity." Yes, the jurist is unable to magnify the matter in these affairs, because he is constrained — rather, he is occupied with reforming the common folk (al-ʿawāmm), whose rank approaches the rank of the beasts (al-anʿām), and they are plunged into darknesses (ẓulumāt) far greater and more immense than that such minor darknesses should appear in comparison to them. For it would be ugly to say of one who drank wine and took the cup with his left hand that he transgressed in two respects — one being the drinking, and the other the taking with the left — and of one who sold wine at the time of the call to prayer on Friday, it would be ugly to say he betrayed in two respects — {one} the selling of wine, and the other the selling at the time of the call. And of one who relieved himself in the prayer niche (miḥrāb) of a mosque with his back to the Qiblah, it would be ugly to mention his abandonment of propriety in relieving himself, in that he did not place the Qiblah to his right. For all sins are darknesses, some piled atop others, such that one is eclipsed beside another. A master may punish his slave if he uses his knife without his permission — but if he killed his most beloved son with that very knife, the unauthorized use of the knife would retain no weight or sting in itself. Thus, all the etiquettes (ādāb) that the Prophets and the Saints (al-awliyāʾ) observed, and which we have treated leniently in jurisprudence (fiqh) concerning the common folk, have as their cause this very necessity. Otherwise, all these disliked acts are deviations from justice (al-ʿadl), ingratitude for blessing (kufrān al-niʿmah), and a deficiency in the rank that conveys the servant to the degrees of proximity (darajāt al-qurb) — some of them affect the servant by diminishing proximity and lowering station, while others expel him entirely from the bounds of proximity into the realm of distance (ʿālam al-buʿd), which is the abode of the devils. Likewise, whoever breaks a branch from a tree without an urgent pressing need, and without a sound purpose, has shown ingratitude for the blessing of Allah Most High in the creation of trees and the creation of the hand. As for the hand, it was not created for frivolity, but for obedience and for deeds that aid in obedience. As for the tree, Allah Most High created it, and created for it roots, and conveyed water to it, and placed within it the power of nourishment and growth, so that it might reach the culmination of its development (munthā nashwihi), and His servants might benefit from it. So breaking it before its culmination, not in a manner by which His servants benefit, is a violation of the purpose of wisdom and a deviation from justice. But if he has a sound purpose, then that is permissible for him — for trees and animals have been made a ransom (fidāʾ) for the purposes of human beings, since both are perishable and doomed. Thus, annihilating the baser (al-akhass) for the preservation of the nobler (al-ashraf) for a time is closer to justice than squandering both. And to this points His saying, Most High: {«وَسَخَّرَ لَكُم مَّا فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَمَا فِي الْأَرْضِ جَمِيعًا مِّنْهُ»} — "And He subjected to you whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth — all from Him" [Al-Jāthiyah: 13]. Yes — if he breaks a tree belonging to someone else, he is also a wrongdoer (ẓālim), even if he is in need, because every specific tree does not suffice for the needs of all the servants of Allah; rather, it suffices for a single need. And if one single person were to be singled out for it without preponderance (tarjīḥ) and specification (ikhtiṣāṣ), that would be injustice. So the one entitled to specification is he who obtained the seed, placed it in the ground, conveyed water to it, and undertook its care — he is more worthy of it than others, and his side is thereby established. But if it grew in dead land (mawāt al-arḍ) without any human effort, then one must seek another specification — namely, precedence in taking it (sabq ilā akhdhihi). For the one who precedes has the special property of precedence (khāṣṣiyyat al-sabq). Justice, then, is that he be most worthy of it. And the poor (al-fuqarāʾ) have expressed this preponderance by the term "ownership" (al-milk) — but it is pure metaphor (majāz maḥḍ), for there is no owner except the King of Kings (Malik al-Mulūk), to Whom belongs what is in the heavens and the earth. And how could a servant be an owner, when he himself does not own his own self — rather, he is the property of Another? Yes — the creatures are the servants of Allah, and the earth is the table (māʾidah) of Allah, and He has permitted them to eat from His table to the measure of their need — like a king who sets a table for his slaves. So if one takes a morsel with his right hand, and his fingers close over it, and another slave comes and seeks to snatch it away...
34:1.section_title_en: The Etiquette of the Heart and the Hidden Dimensions of Violating Sacred Directions and Blessings
34:1.anchors:
- Root: ظلم (ẓ-l-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning is "darkness" (ẓulmah) — absence of light; also "to place something in other than its proper place" (waḍʿ al-shayʾ fī ghayr mawḍiʿihi).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Ẓulm is expressed via "darknesses" (ẓulumāt) as ignorance, polytheism, and transgression — the opposite of nūr (light/justice).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): "الظلم ظلمات يوم القيامة" — injustice is darknesses on the Day of Judgment. Metaphorical (majāz): "أرض مظلومة" — land never dug, i.e., violated by first use; "ظلم البعير" — slaughtering an animal without cause (ʿabṭ).
- Root: نعم (n-ʿ-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Niʿmah is a state of well-being; also "softness" and "delicacy."
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Niʿmah is the good condition bestowed; its plural (niʿam) covers both little and much — "وَإِن تَعُدُّوا نِعْمَةَ اللَّهِ لَا تُحْصُوهَا" {And if you count the blessings of Allah, you cannot enumerate them} [Ibrahim: 34].
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "جلت نعمة الله" — the blessing of Allah is immense. Metaphorical: "خفت نعامتهم" — their ostriches departed (i.e., they fled), showing how blessing can be "kicked away" (kufrān al-niʿmah).
- Root: ملك (m-l-k)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Ownership and dominion; the possessor (mālik) who disposes freely.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الملك: هو المتصرف بالأمر والنهي" — the king is one who commands and forbids; true ownership belongs only to Allah, "لَهُ مَا فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَمَا فِي الْأَرْضِ" {To Him belongs what is in the heavens and the earth}.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "ملك يده" — what one's hand owns. Metaphorical: "ملكت فلانة أمرها" — she controlled her own affair; here, human "ownership" (milk) is pure metaphor (majāz maḥḍ), since real dominion is Allah's alone.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The rule governs how qualifying clauses (e.g., "التي بوضعها كمال عبادتك") attach to antecedents, preserving syntactic cohesion even when embedded phrases lengthen the sentence, ensuring no semantic break occurs between the act and its moral consequence.
34:1.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

34:13.arabic: رتبة الشكر طعن اللعين في الخلق فقال ولا تجد اكثرم شاكرين وقال تعالى وقليل من عبادي الشكور وقد قطع الله تعالى بالمزيد مع الشكر ولم يستثن فقال تعالى لئن شكرتم لأزيدنكم واستثنى في خمسة أشياء في الإغناء والإجابة والرزق والمغفرة والتوبة فقال تعالى فسوف يغنيكم الله من فضله إن شاء {وقال} فيكشف ما تدعون إليه إن شاء {وقال} يرزق من يشاء بغير حساب {وقال} ويغفر ما دون ذلك لمن يشاء {وقال} ويتوب الله على من يشاء وهو خلق من أخلاق الربوبية إذ قال تعالى والله شكور حليم وقد جعل الله الشكر مفتاح كلام أهل الجنة فقال تعالى وقالوا الحمد لله الذي صدقناه
34:13.english: So then, what we have mentioned concerning the treatment of patience (ṣabr) regarding whispered insinuation (waswās), regarding lust (shahwah), and regarding status (jāh) — annex this to what we have already set down concerning the canons of the paths of spiritual striving (mujāhadah) in the Book of the Discipline of the Soul (Kitāb Riyāḍat al-Nafs) from the Quarter of the Destroyers (rubʿ al-muhlikāt). Adopt it as your manual (dastūr) by which you may come to know the treatment of patience in all the categories which we have previously detailed; for the detailing of individual cases is prolix. Whoever observes gradual progression (tadrīj), patience will elevate him to a state wherein patience without it becomes as arduous as it once was with it — so his affairs become inverted, and what was once beloved to him becomes loathed, and what was once detested to him becomes a sweet, wholesome draught from which he cannot bear to be patient [in abstaining]. This is known only through experience (tajribah) and tasting (dhawq). It has an analogue in customary habits: for a boy is compelled to learning in the beginning by force, and so patience with play and patience with knowledge are both arduous for him — until, when his inner sight is opened and he finds intimacy with knowledge, the matter is inverted, and it becomes arduous for him to be patient in abstaining from knowledge, and to endure play. To this points what is narrated of one of the knowers (ʿārifīn) that he asked al-Shiblī: "Patience — which of its kinds is the most severe?" He said: "Patience in God (fī Allāh)." He said: "No." He said: "Patience for God (li-Allāh)." He said: "No." He said: "Patience with God (maʿa Allāh)." He said: "No." He said: "Then what?" He said: "Patience from God (ʿan Allāh)." At that al-Shiblī cried out a cry by which his soul nearly perished. And it has been said concerning the meaning of His saying, the Exalted: {«اصبروا وصابروا ورابطوا»} "Be patient, and vie in patience, and be steadfast" (Q. 3:200): "Be patient in God, vie in patience by God, and be steadfast with God." And it was said: "Patience for God is sufficiency (ghināʾ); patience by God is endurance (baqāʾ); patience with God is fidelity (wafāʾ); and patience from God is abandonment (jafāʾ)." And it was said concerning its meaning:
34:13.section_title_en: The Revival of the Religious Sciences — Section 972: On Patience (al-Sabr) and the Commencement of Gratitude (al-Shukr)
34:13.anchors:
- Root: صبر (ṣ-b-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of restraint and withholding; al-Khalil notes its application to holding back an animal from fodder, and to enduring constraint.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الصبر: الإمساك في ضيق" — the withholding of the self in constriction; it is a general term whose specific names (shajāʿah, ḥilm, etc.) vary by context, and its opposite is al-jazaʿ (panic/vexation).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): "صبرت على ما أكره. وصبرت عما أحب" — enduring what is disliked and restraining from what is loved. Metaphorical (majāz): "صبرت يمينه" — binding an oath strenuously; "أصبر على الضرب من الأرض" — more enduring than the earth.
- Root: شكر (sh-k-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The root denotes manifestation and fullness; al-Ayn links it to an overflowing udder (shukrā).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الشكر: تصور النعمة وإظهارها" — the perception of a blessing and its display; it is the opposite of kufr (covering/denial). It has three degrees: of the heart (perception), of the tongue (praise), and of the limbs (requital).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "شكرت لله تعالى نعمته" — thanking God for His grace. Metaphorical: "دابة شكور" — a beast that thrives on little fodder, displaying its owner's care through its fatness.
- Root: علم (ʿ-l-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Knowledge as the apprehension of a thing's reality; al-Ayn treats it under the entry of umm (source/origin), indicating that knowledge is the root to which all else is annexed.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "العلم: إدراك الشيء بحقيقته" — apprehension of a thing by its true reality, either by grasping its essence or by affirming/denying a predicate of it.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "ما علمت بخبرك: ما شعرت به" — to be aware/perceive. It is also used for the landmarks (maʿālim) of the road, i.e., traces by which one is guided.
- Root: وقد (w-q-d)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The kindling and blazing of fire; al-Ayn records it under the entry of w-q-d with the sense of fuel and flame.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "وقدت النار تقد وقودا ووقدا" — the fire blazed; al-wuqūd is both the fuel and the resulting flame, as in {«وقودها الناس والحجارة»} (Q. 2:24).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "وقدت النار وقودا ووقدا، واتقدت وتوقدت" — the fire blazed and blazed fiercely. Metaphorical: "قلب وقاد" — a blazing, keen heart; "وقدة الصيف" — the blazing heat of summer.
- Sibawayh Rule: Interposition between the operative word and its object (al-faṣl bayna al-ʿāmil wa al-maʿmūl fīhi) — governing the placement of circumstantial qualifiers (ḥāl) and prepositional phrases to preserve the intended semantic restriction, as in the verse "اصبروا وصابروا ورابطوا" where each imperative carries a distinct operative scope.
34:13.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

36:9.arabic: مقمحون وجعلنا من بين أيديهم سدا ومن خلفهم سدا فأغشيناهم فهم لا يبصرون وسواء عليهم أأنذرتهم أم لم تنذرهم لا يؤمنون} ولا يغرنك لفظ الإيمان فنقول المراد بالآية الكافر إذ بين لك أن الإيمان بضع وسبعون بابا وأن الزاني لا يزني حين يزني وهو مؤمن فالمحجوب عن الإيمان الذي هو شعب وفروع سيحجب في الخاتمة عن الإيمان الذي هو أصل كما أن الشخص الفاقد لجميع الأطراف التي هي حروف وفروع سيساق إلى الموت المعدم للروح التي هي أصل فلا بقاء للأصل دون الفرع بيان أن وجوب التوبة على الفور ولا وجود للفرع دون الأصل ولا فرق بين الأصل والفرع إلا في شيء واحد وهو أن وجود الفرع و
36:9.english: So haste, haste (al-bidār al-bidār) to repentance, before the poisons of sins work upon the spirit of faith a work that surpasses the physicians' art and their choice, after which no abstention (iḥtimāʾ) avails. After that, the counsel of counselors and the exhortation of exhorters will not succeed. And the Word will be fulfilled against him, that he is among the perished, and he falls under the general import of His saying — exalted be He: {«إنا جعلنا في أعناقهم أغلالا فهي إلى الأذقان فهم مقمحون وجعلنا من بين أيديهم سدا ومن خلفهم سدا فأغشيناهم فهم لا يبصرون وسواء عليهم أأنذرتهم أم لم تنذرهم لا يؤمنون»} (Ya-Sin: 8–10). And let not the mere utterance of faith (īmān) deceive you, such that we say: The verse refers only to the disbeliever — for it has been made clear to you that faith has seventy-some branches, and that the fornicator does not fornicate at the moment of fornication while he is a believer. Thus, the one veiled from faith — which is its branches and offshoots — will be veiled at the final seal from faith — which is its root. Just as a person who has lost all his limbs — which are, as it were, letters and branches — will inevitably be driven to death, which annihilates the spirit — which is the root. For the root has no endurance without the branch.
36:9.section_title_en: The Obligation of Immediate Repentance — The Poison of Sins and the Severing of the Artery of the Knowers
36:9.anchors:
- Root: نياط (nīāṭ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The aorta or vital artery; that which, if severed, causes death.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The vital thread connecting soul to body; metaphorically, the spiritual lifeline.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the jugular vein. Metaphorical: the point of no return; "انقطع نياطه" = his life-thread was cut.
- Root: ختم (khatama)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To seal, stamp, or impress a mark.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Sealing of the heart as divine restriction and veiling from guidance.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: affixing a seal. Metaphorical: final sealing of one's fate at death (khatimat al-ʿamal).
- Root: أصل (aṣl) / فرع (farʿ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Root/base vs. branch/twig.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The root is the foundation; the branch is that which grows from it. Quranic: {أصلها ثابت وفرعها في السماء} (Ibrahim: 24).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: tree root and branch. Metaphorical: the root (aṣl) of faith vs. its branches (furūʿ); the root of life (spirit) vs. its branches (limbs).
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — Used to emphasize that the obligation of repentance is immediate and unrestricted, as in "فالبدار البدار" (haste, haste!) — an emphatic accusative of exhortation (ikhtiṣāṣ).
36:9.topic: Al-Ghazali on the journey of the soul, death, and the Hereafter, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

36:9.arabic: الطريق قال الله تعالى {وجعلنا من بين أيديهم سدا ومن خلفهم سدا فأغشيناهم فهم لا يبصرون} والسد بين المريد وبين الحق أربعة المال والجاه والتقليد والمعصية وإنما يرفع حجاب المال بخروجه عن ملكه حتى لا يبقى له إلا قدر الضرورة فما دام يبقى له درهم يلتفت إليه فهو مقيد به محجوب عن الله عز وجل وإنما يرتفع حجاب الجاه بالبعد عن موضع الجاه بالتواضع وإيثار الخمول والهرب من أسباب الذكر وتعاطي أعمال تنفر قلوب الخلق عنه وإنما يرتفع حجاب التقليد بأن يترك التعصب للمذاهب وأن يصدق بمعنى قوله لا إله إلا الله محمد رسول الله تصديق إيمان ويحرض في تحقيق صدقه بأن ير
36:9.english: As for the conditions that must be set forth in the resolve: they are the lifting of the barrier and the veil that lies between him and the Truth. For the deprivation of creation from the Truth is caused by the accumulation of veils and the placing of a barrier upon the road. God Most High said: {«وجعلنا من بين أيديهم سدا ومن خلفهم سدا فأغشيناهم فهم لا يبصرون»} ("And We have placed before them a barrier and behind them a barrier, and We have covered them, so they do not see").
36:9.section_title_en: On the Sale of the Pearl to the Jewel — The Conditions of the Seeker's Beginning
36:9.anchors:
- Root: سلك (salaka)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To penetrate, pass through, traverse a path; threading a thread through a needle.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "السلوك: النفاذ في الطريق" — spiritual-moral passage through the path; used of one's course of action, whether praiseworthy or blameworthy.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "طريق مسلوك" (a trodden path). Metaphorical: "كلام دقيق السلك: خفي المسلك" — subtle speech whose passage is hidden; here, the path to God is a spiritual traversal requiring a guide.
- Root: صدق (ṣadaqa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Truthfulness in speech and resolve; sincerity of intention.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الصدق والكذب أصلهما في القول" — truth and falsehood are rooted in utterance, but true faith (taṣdīq) is the heart's verification, not mere verbal assent.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "صدقته الحديث" (I affirmed his speech). Metaphorical: "رجل صادق الحملة" — one truthful in his charge/assault; here, the one who "affirms" the pearl but knows only its name lacks true verification.
- Root: طرق (ṭaraqa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Striking, beating; a path beaten by feet.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الطريق: السبيل الذي يطرق بالأرجل" — the way is that which is trodden; metaphorically extended to every course one pursues in action.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "طرق الباب: قرعه" (to knock at a door). Metaphorical: "طرقني الخيال" (the phantom visited me by night); "طرقه الزمان بنوائبه" (time struck him with calamities) — here, the "blockers of the road" (قطاع الطريق) are spiritual bandits.
- Sibawayh Rule: Restriction and qualification (الحصر والتقييد) — the conditional clauses (إذا/فإن) structure the periodic sentence, linking protasis (condition) to apodosis (result) to establish causal necessity in the spiritual path.
36:9.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications, prayers, and their spiritual power, from 'Breaking the Two Desires'

36:9.arabic: المراد بقوله تعالى وجعلنا من بين أيديهم سدا ومن خلفهم سدا الآية ولذلك قال رضي الله تعالى عنه إن الإيمان ليبدو في القلب نكتة بيضاء كلما ازداد الإيمان ازداد ذلك البياض فإذا استكمل العبد الإيمان أبيض القلب كله وإن النفاق ليبدو في القلب نكتة سوداء كلما ازداد النفاق ازداد ذلك السواد فإذا استكمل النفاق أسود القلب كله فإذا عرفت أن الأخلاق الحسنة تارة تكون بالطبع والفطرة وتارة تكون باعتياد الأفعال الجميلة وتارة بمشاهدة أرباب الفعال الجميلة ومصاحبتهم وهم قرناء الخير وإخوان الصلاح إذ الطبع يسرق من الطبع الشر والخير جميعا فمن
36:9.english: For this reason, may God be well pleased with him, said: "Faith indeed appears in the heart as a white spot; whenever faith increases, that whiteness increases, until when the servant perfects faith, the whole heart becomes white. And hypocrisy indeed appears in the heart as a black spot; whenever hypocrisy increases, that blackness increases, until when hypocrisy is perfected, the whole heart becomes black."
36:9.section_title_en: The Gradual Acquisition of Moral Character and the Detailed Exposition of the Path to Refining Ethics
36:9.anchors:
- Root: فقه (Fiqh)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Comprehension and understanding of a matter's inward reality; deep penetration into meaning.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الفقه: هو التوصل إلى علم غائب بعلم شاهد" — Fiqh is attaining knowledge of the unseen through the witnessed; it is more specific than mere knowledge ('ilm), denoting a settled, abiding comprehension.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): "افقه عني ما أقول لك" — grasp what I say to you. The term denotes active, engaged understanding, not passive reception.
- Root: نفس (Nafs)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The self, the soul; that which desires proximity and discourse; the principle of life and animation.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The soul as the seat of both blameworthy and praiseworthy traits; its purification (tazkiyah) is the goal of moral discipline.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal vs. Metaphorical: "نفس" as blood (the life-fluid) versus the immaterial self; here, "فقيه النفس" denotes one whose very soul has become imbued with the habit of deep understanding — a settled disposition, not a transient state.
- Root: قلب (Qalb)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The heart; that which turns and is turned (taqlib), the organ of fluctuating states.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "قلب الشيء: تصريفه وصرفه عن وجه إلى وجه" — the heart is so named for its constant turning and overturning between states; it is the seat of both faith and hypocrisy, whiteness and blackness.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Metaphorical (Majaz): "قلب المعلم الصبيان: صرفهم إلى بيوتهم" — to turn something about, to manage and dispose; the heart is that which is turned by habits until it becomes fixed in one direction.
- Root: جمل (Jaml)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Beauty and comeliness; the sum total of a thing; that which is gathered and collected.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الجمال: الحسن الكثير" — beauty in abundance; both inward (character) and outward (action).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "فلان يعامل الناس بالجميل" — dealing with people beautifully; here, "الأفعال الجميلة" are the beautiful, virtuous actions whose repetition forms character.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد (Restriction & Specification) — The construction "لا طريق له إلا أن" (there is no path for him except that) effects complete restriction (hasr), confining the means of moral transformation to a single, specified avenue: the repetition of acts until they become nature.

36:30.arabic: رسولا منه فما يعتبرون فيا حسرة على العباد ما يأتيهم من رسول إلا كانوا به يستهزئون أفيظنون أنهم في الدنيا خالدون أو لم يروا كم أهلكنا قبلهم من القرون أنهم إليهم لا يرجعون أم يحسبون أن الموتى سافروا من عندهم فهم معدمون كلا وإن كل لما جميع لدينا محضرون {ولكن} ما تأتيهم من آية من آيات ربهم إلا كانوا عنها معرضين وذلك لأنا جعلنا من بين أيديهم سدا ومن خلفهم سدا فأغشيناهم فهم لا يبصرون وسواء عليهم أأنذرتهم أم لم تنذرهم لا يؤمنون ولنرجع إلى الغرض فإن هذه تلويحات تشير إلى أمور هي أعلى من علوم المعاملة فنقول ظهر أن الصبر عبارة عن ثبات
36:30.english: How immense is your heedlessness, O wretched one—and all of us are that wretched one—while before you are these terrors! If you do not believe in the greater resurrection out of ignorance and error, does not the evidence of the lesser resurrection suffice you? Have you not heard the saying of the Master of the Prophets, peace be upon him: "Sufficient is death as a warner" (kafā bil-mawti wāʿiẓan)? Have you not heard of his weeping, peace be upon him, at death, until he said, may God's peace and blessing be upon him: "O God, ease for Muhammad the agonies of death" (allāhumma hawwin ʿalā Muḥammadin sakarāti al-mawt)? Are you not ashamed of your slowness in anticipating the onslaught of death, following the rabble of the heedless—those who look only for a single cry that seizes them while they are disputing, so they can neither make a bequest nor return to their families? Then illness comes to them as a warner of death, and they are not deterred; and gray hair comes to them as a messenger from it, and they do not take heed. {«يَا حَسْرَةً عَلَى الْعِبَادِ مَا يَأْتِيهِمْ مِنْ رَسُولٍ إِلَّا كَانُوا بِهِ يَسْتَهْزِئُونَ»} (O regret upon the servants! There comes not to them a messenger but they mock him) [Ya-Sin: 30]. Do they think that they are in this world immortal? {«أَوَلَمْ يَرَوْا كَمْ أَهْلَكْنَا قَبْلَهُمْ مِنَ الْقُرُونِ أَنَّهُمْ إِلَيْهِمْ لَا يَرْجِعُونَ»} (Have they not seen how many generations We destroyed before them—that they will not return to them?) Then illness comes to them as a warner of death, and they are not deterred; and gray hair comes to them as a messenger from it, and they do not take heed. {«يَا حَسْرَةً عَلَى الْعِبَادِ مَا يَأْتِيهِمْ مِنْ رَسُولٍ إِلَّا كَانُوا بِهِ يَسْتَهْزِئُونَ»} (O regret upon the servants! There comes not to them a messenger but they mock him) [Ya-Sin: 30]. Do they think that they are in this world immortal? {«أَوَلَمْ يَرَوْا كَمْ أَهْلَكْنَا قَبْلَهُمْ مِنَ الْقُرُونِ أَنَّهُمْ إِلَيْهِمْ لَا يَرْجِعُونَ»} (Have they not seen how many generations We destroyed before them—that they will not return to them?) [Ya-Sin: 31]. Or do they reckon that the dead have merely traveled away from them, and so they are annihilated? Nay! {«وَإِنْ كُلٌّ لَمَّا جَمِيعٌ لَدَيْنَا مُحْضَرُونَ»} (And indeed, all of them, without exception, will be brought before Us) [Ya-Sin: 32]. {«وَمَا تَأْتِيهِمْ مِنْ آيَةٍ مِنْ آيَاتِ رَبِّهِمْ إِلَّا كَانُوا عَنْهَا مُعْرِضِينَ»} (And there comes not to them a sign from the signs of their Lord but they turn away from it) [Ya-Sin: 46]. And that is because {«إِنَّا جَعَلْنَا مِنْ بَيْنِ أَيْدِيهِمْ سَدًّا وَمِنْ خَلْفِهِمْ سَدًّا فَأَغْشَيْنَاهُمْ فَهُمْ لَا يُبْصِرُونَ»} (We have placed before them a barrier and behind them a barrier, and We have covered them, so they do not see) [Ya-Sin: 9]. {«وَسَوَاءٌ عَلَيْهِمْ أَأَنْذَرْتَهُمْ أَمْ لَمْ تُنْذِرْهُمْ لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ»} (And it is alike to them whether you warn them or warn them not—they will not believe) [Ya-Sin: 10].
36:46.section_title_en: On the Lesser Resurrection as Proof of the Greater, and the Station of the Guardian over the Child
36:46.anchors:
- Root: صغر (ṣaghara)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Smallness in magnitude, rank, or time; the lesser as opposed to the greater (al-kabīr), each term relative to the other.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Ṣighar and kibar are relative opposites, applied variously to age, body, or station; here, the "lesser resurrection" (al-qiyāmah al-ṣughrā) is death, measured against the "greater" (al-kubrā), the final rising.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: diminution in size or status. Metaphorical: the lesser as a type or foreshadow of the greater—death as the microcosmic analogue of the macrocosmic resurrection.
- Root: موت (mawt)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Death as the cessation of animal life; the root also yields "amāta" (to cause death) and "mayyit" (the dead).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Death is the departure of the soul from the body, a transition between two abodes; it is the "lesser resurrection" in that it separates the spirit from the corporeal frame, prefiguring the greater separation and recompense.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: biological death. Metaphorical: "the dead land" revived by rain, and here, death as a "warner" (nadhīr) and "messenger" (rasūl)—personified agencies of admonition.
- Root: علم (ʿalima)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Knowledge as perception or cognition of a thing; "ʿallama" (to teach) and "ʿālim" (the knowing one).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): ʿIlm is apprehension of a thing's reality—either its essence or a judgment about it. Here, the "knowledge" of the two resurrections distinguishes the believer (muʾmin) from the ignorant (jāhil), who sees with a "blind eye" (al-ʿayn al-ʿawrāʾ).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: certain cognition. Metaphorical: "I knew not of your news" (mā ʿalimtu bi-khabarika) meaning "I perceived not"—thus ignorance is a failure of perception, not mere absence of data.
- Root: ولي (waliya)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Nearness, guardianship, or patronage; the walī is one who assumes charge of another's affairs, whether kin or protector.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Wilāyah denotes proximity and authority; the walī of a child acts as God's deputy in discipline, mirroring the angels' custodianship of the moral ledger.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical adjacency. Metaphorical: the guardian's "inheriting the character of the angels" (waritha akhlāq al-malāʾikah)—a moral, not genealogical, inheritance.
- Sibawayh Rule: Interposition of the conditional and its apodosis (al-faṣl bayna al-sharṭ wa al-jawāb)—the periodic structure in "fa-in kunta lā tuʾminu... afalā takfīka" (if you believe not... does not suffice you?) allows the protasis to govern the rhetorical question, binding the lesser sign to the greater inference.
36:46.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

36:47.arabic: إليهم كما قال تعالى حكاية عن الكفار {وإذا قيل لهم أنفقوا من ما رزقكم الله قال الذين كفروا للذين آمنوا أنطعم من لو يشاء الله أطعمه} وقالوا أيضا {لو شاء الله ما أشركنا ولا آباؤنا} فانظر كيف كانوا صادقين في كلامهم وكيف هلكوا بصدقهم فسبحان من إذا شاء أهلك بالصدق وإذا شاء أسعد بالجهل {يضل به كثيرا ويهدي به كثيرا} فهؤلاء لما ظنوا أنهم استخدموا لأجل المساكين والفقراء أو جل الله تعالى ثم قالوا لا حظ لنا في المساكين ولا حظ لله فينا وفي أموالنا سواء أنفقنا أو أمسكنا هلكوا كما هلك الصبي لما ظن أن مقصود الوالد استخدامه لأجل
36:47.english: Likewise, if it were said: "Is oxymel (sikanjabīn) better, or the drink of the water-lily (sharāb al-līnūfar)?" — no unqualified answer could be correct at all. Indeed, if it were said to us: "Is oxymel better, or the absence of yellow bile?" — we would say: the absence of yellow bile, for oxymel is sought for the sake of something else, and that which is sought for its own sake is necessarily better than that which is sought for the sake of another.
36:47.section_title_en: The Superiority of Knowledge Over Action — The Parable of the Physician and the Child
36:47.anchors:
- Root: فضل (faḍl)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Excess or increase beyond what is required; superiority in degree.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الفضل: الزيادة عن الاقتصاد" — excess beyond moderation, divided into praiseworthy (like excess of knowledge) and blameworthy; comparative superiority of one thing over another by genus, species, or merit.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): "فاضلني فلان ففضلته" — to surpass in excellence. Here used comparatively: one act or state exceeds another in rank.
- Root: علم (ʿilm)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Knowledge as the apprehension of a thing's reality; the mark or sign by which something is known.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "العلم: إدراك الشيء بحقيقته" — apprehension of a thing's true reality, whether by direct perception of its essence or by judgment concerning it.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "هو من أعلام العلم الخافقه" — knowledge as a lofty, manifest sign; distinguished from mere action which is its instrument.
- Root: صدق (ṣidq)
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Truthfulness primarily in speech — correspondence of report with reality; may become blameworthy when it leads to ruin, as with the disbelievers who spoke truly about God's independence yet drew false conclusions.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "صدقته الحديث" — truthful in statement. Metaphorical (Majaz): "رجل صادق الحملة" — truthful in resolve. Here: the disbelievers were literally truthful in their words yet destroyed by that very truthfulness.
- Root: هلك (halak)
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Destruction on three levels: loss of something from one's possession, corruption and dissolution, and death. Used here for spiritual ruin through misapplied reasoning.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "وقعوا في المهلكة" — falling into destruction. Metaphorical: "تهالك على الشيء" — intense craving. Here: literal perdition of the soul through false inference.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The conditional structure "فإن قلت... فاعلم" (if you say... then know) governs the entire periodic sentence, requiring the apodosis to resolve the protasis with logical necessity, as in the physician analogy where praise of the medicine does not entail its intrinsic superiority.
36:47.topic: Classical commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya Ulum al-Din, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

36:49.arabic: {ما ينظرون إلا صيحة واحدة تأخذهم وهم يخصمون فلا يستطيعون توصية ولا إلى أهلهم يرجعون} والصلاة والسلام على محمد رسوله الذي يسير تحت لوائه النبيون وعلى آله وأصحابه الأئمة المهديين والسادة المرضيين صلاة يوازي عددها عدد ما كان من خلق الله وما سيكون ويحظى ببركتها الأولون والآخرون وسلم تسليما كثيرا أما بعد فإن الغضب شعلة نار اقتبست من نار الله الموقدة التي تطلع على الأفئدة وإنها لمستكنة في طي الفؤاد استكنان الجمر تحت الرماد ويستخرجه الكبر الدفين في قلب كل جبار عنيد كاستخراج الحجر النار من الحديد وقد انكشف للناظرين بنور اليقين أن ا
36:49.english: In the name of God, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate. Praise be to God, upon whose pardon and mercy none rely except the hopeful, and from whose evil wrath and assault none fear except the fearful — He who gradually seizes His servants from whence they know not, and who has given dominion over them to their lusts, commanding them to abandon what they desire, and who has tried them with anger while charging them to swallow their rage in what provokes them. Then He surrounded them with hardships and pleasures, and granted them respite to see how they would act. He tested their love through them, to make known the truth of what they claim. He made known to them that nothing is hidden from Him of what they conceal or proclaim, and warned them lest He seize them suddenly while they are unaware. For He said: {«They await but a single blast which will seize them while they are disputing; so they will not be able to make a bequest, nor to their families will they return»} (Q. 36:49-50). And prayers and peace be upon Muhammad, His Messenger, beneath whose banner the prophets walk, and upon his family and companions — the rightly-guided imams and the pleasing masters — prayers whose number equals the number of what has been of God's creation and what will be, and by whose blessing the first and the last are favored — and abundant peace.
36:49.section_title_en: The Book of Condemnation of Anger, Spite, and Envy — Book Five of the Quarter of Destroyers from The Revival of the Religious Sciences
36:49.anchors:
- Root: غضب (ghadab)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root meaning of anger, rage, fury; the boiling and agitation of the blood
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance — when attributed to God, it means retribution (intiqām) alone, not emotional agitation; the Prophet described it as "a live coal kindled in the heart of the son of Adam"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal vs Metaphorical — literal anger is the boiling of the blood in living beings; metaphorical usage extends to inanimate things like fire and the reins of a mount
- Root: قلب (qalb)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The heart; also the turning, overturning, and transformation of a thing from one state to another
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance — the heart is so named for its constant turning (taqallub) and fluctuation between states; it is the seat of understanding and the locus of divine address
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal vs Metaphorical — literal is the physical organ; metaphorical is the subtle spiritual reality (laṭīfah rabbāniyyah) that is the locus of knowledge and will
- Root: حسد (hasad)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Envy; the wishing for removal of another's blessing
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance — envy is the desire for the removal of a blessing from one who deserves it, sometimes accompanied by striving to remove it; the believer envies (ghibṭah) while the hypocrite envies (hasad)
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal vs Metaphorical — "Envy consumes the body as fire consumes wood"; the envier is one who wishes evil upon the blessed
- Root: هلك (halak)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Perdition, destruction, ruin; death
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance — three senses: (1) loss of a thing from one's possession while it exists elsewhere, (2) corruption and dissolution of a thing, (3) death; the Quran uses it for all three
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal vs Metaphorical — literal is physical destruction; metaphorical is the ruin of one's religion and afterlife through spiritual corruption
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The permissibility of interposing elements between a preposition and its object when the intervening material constitutes a complete, meaningful unit, as in the Quranic pattern of extended periodic sentences that delay resolution for rhetorical effect.

36:49.arabic: عليه شيء مما يسرون وما يعلنون وحذرهم أن يأخذهم بغتة وهم لا يشعرون فقال {ما ينظرون إلا صيحة واحدة تأخذهم وهم يخصمون فلا يستطيعون توصية ولا إلى أهلهم يرجعون} والصلاة والسلام على محمد رسوله الذي يسير تحت لوائه النبيون وعلى آله وأصحابه الأئمة المهديين والسادة المرضيين صلاة يوازي عددها عدد ما كان من خلق الله وما سيكون ويحظى ببركتها الأولون والآخرون وسلم تسليما كثيرا أما بعد فإن الغضب شعلة نار اقتبست من نار الله الموقدة التي تطلع على الأفئدة وإنها لمستكنة في طي الفؤاد استكنان الجمر تحت الرماد ويستخرجه الكبر الدفين في قلب كل جبار عنيد كاستخراج الحجر النار من الحديد وقد انكشف للناظرين بنور اليقين أن الإنسان
36:49.english: In the name of God, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate. Praise be to God, upon whose pardon and mercy none rely except the hopeful, and from whose evil wrath and assault none fear except the fearful — He who gradually seizes His servants from whence they know not, and who has given dominion over them to their lusts, commanding them to abandon what they desire, and who has tried them with anger while charging them to swallow their rage in what provokes them. Then He surrounded them with hardships and pleasures, and granted them respite to see how they would act. He tested their love through them, to make known the truth of what they claim. He made known to them that nothing is hidden from Him of what they conceal or proclaim, and warned them lest He seize them suddenly while they are unaware. For He said: {«They await but a single blast which will seize them while they are disputing; so they will not be able to make a bequest, nor to their families will they return»} (Q. 36:49-50). And prayers and peace be upon Muhammad, His Messenger, beneath whose banner the prophets walk, and upon his family and companions — the rightly-guided imams and the pleasing masters — prayers whose number equals the number of what has been of God's creation and what will be, and by whose blessing the first and the last are favored — and abundant peace.
