36:70.arabic: مرض} إشارة إلى مرض العقول وقوله عز وجل {لينذر من كان حيا} إشارة إلى من لم يحى حياة باطنة وكل حي بالبدن ميت بالقلب فهو عند الله من الموتى وإن كان عند الجهال من الأحياء ولذلك كان الشهداء أحياء عند ربهم يرزقون فرحين وإن كانوا موتى بالأبدان الثانية لذة يشارك الإنسان فيها بعض الحيوانات كلذة الرياسة والغلبة والاستيلاء وذلك موجود في الأسد والنمر وبعض الحيوانات الثالثة ما يشارك فيها سائر الحيوانات كلذة البطن والفرج وهذه أكثرها وجودا وهي أخسها ولذلك اشترك فيها كل ودرج حتى الديدان والحشرات ومن جاوز هذه الرتبة ت
36:70.english: The second type is the restricted one — he who has gathered some of these attributes but not others. For there may be a benefit that is painful, like the cutting off of a gangrenous finger or a tumor protruding from the body. And there may be a benefit that is ugly, like foolishness — for in relation to certain circumstances it is beneficial, as it has been said: "He who has no intellect is at rest," for he is not accused of foresight, so he rests in the present moment until the time of his destruction arrives. And there may be that which is beneficial in one respect and harmful in another, like casting wealth into the sea when fearing drowning — for it is harmful to the wealth, beneficial to the soul in its deliverance.
36:70.section_title_en: The Divisions of Benefit and the Hierarchy of Pleasures — Section 993
36:70.anchors:
- Root: كبر (k-b-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core sense of magnitude, greatness, and by extension pride/arrogance (istikbār) as a moral ailment.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-kibr is the state of self-amplification that blinds one to truth and disparages others — here coupled with the humiliation (dhull) of learning, forming a psychological contradiction.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) = physical largeness; metaphorical (majāz) = spiritual arrogance that prevents receptivity.
- Root: نفع (n-f-ʿ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Benefit, utility, that which yields good outcome.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "النفع: ما يستعان به في الوصول إلى الخيرات" — benefit is that by which one reaches goods; its opposite is ḍarar (harm). Benefit divides into the necessary (ḍarūrī) and the replaceable.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "فيه نفع ومنفعة ومنافع" — literal usage for tangible utility; extended to spiritual advantage.
- Root: لذ (l-dh-dh)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Pleasure, sweetness of perception; root denotes finding something agreeable to one's nature.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Pleasure (ladhdhah) is the perception of what suits one's constitution; its ranks follow the nobility of the perceiving faculty.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Distinguishes bodily pleasure shared with beasts from intellectual pleasure unique to the heart.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب التقسيم والترتيب (Division and Ordination) — periodic sentences structured by fa- (sequential) and ammā...fa- (as for...then) to mark categorical hierarchies.
36:70.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

37:6.arabic: تعالى {إنا زينا السماء الدنيا بزينة الكواكب} فجميع أجزاء العالم سماؤه وكواكبه ورياحه وبحاره وجباله ومعادنه ونباته وحيواناته وأعظاء حيواناته لا تخلو ذرة من ذراته عن حكم كثيرة من حكمه واحدة إلى عشرة إلى ألف إلى عشرة آلاف وكذا أعضاء الحيوان تنقسم إلا ما يعرف حكمتها كالعلم بأن العين للإبصار لا للبطش واليد للبطش لا للمشي والرجل للمشي لا للشم فأما الأعضاء الباطنة من الأمعاء والمرارة والكبد والكلية وآحاد العروق والأعصاب والعضلات وما فيها من التجاويف والالتفاف والاشتباك والانحراف والدقة وال
37:6.english: ...and there is no omnipotent one save the King, the Compeller. And when the covering is lifted from the eyes of the heedless, and they behold the matter to be thus, they will hear at that time the call of the Proclaimer: {«لِمَنِ الْمُلْكُ الْيَوْمَ لِلَّهِ الْوَاحِدِ الْقَهَّارِ»} — "To whom belongs the sovereignty this Day? To God, the One, the Compeller" {Q 40:16}. And indeed sovereignty belonged to God, the One, the Compeller, every single day — not exclusively on that day — but the heedless do not hear this proclamation save on that day. Thus it is tidings of what is renewed for the heedless of the unveiling of states, at a time when the unveiling will not benefit them. So we seek refuge in God, the Forbearing, the Generous, from ignorance and blindness, for it is the root cause of destruction.
37:6.section_title_en: The Unveiling of Sovereignty and the Discernment of What God Loves from What He Abhors
37:6.anchors:
- Root: كشف (kashafa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Removal of a covering; disclosure of what was hidden.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Unveiling of the unseen realities (mukāshafah) — the lifting of the veil from the heart's eye to perceive things as they truly are.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): removal of a physical covering. Metaphorical (majāz): the disclosure of intellectual or spiritual realities to the percipient.
- Root: ملك (malaka)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Possession, dominion, sovereignty; the one who possesses is malik (king).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): True sovereignty (mulk) belongs exclusively to God; all created dominion is borrowed and ephemeral.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: royal authority. Metaphorical: absolute, unshared dominion — as in the Qur'anic proclamation of sole kingship on the Day of Judgment.
- Root: شكر (shakara)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Gratitude; acknowledgment of beneficence.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Thankfulness is the recognition of the Benefactor and the employment of His blessings in that which pleases Him — not mere verbal praise.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: requital of favor. Metaphorical: the use of blessings in obedience to the Giver, which is the true meaning of gratitude.
- Root: كفر (kafara)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Covering, concealing; ingratitude that veils the recognition of favor.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Kufr is the covering of blessings by failing to employ them in the manner intended by the Giver, or by employing them in what He abhors.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: covering a seed in the earth. Metaphorical: the concealment of God's blessings through misuse or neglect.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Restriction and Focused Predication (al-ḥaṣr wa al-taqyīd bi-innamā) — restricting the means of gratitude to two exclusive cognitive faculties, and the restriction of creation's purpose to the sole end of attaining unto God.
37:6.topic: Al-Ghazali on purifying the character, moral diseases, and spiritual remedies, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

37:164.arabic: البتة فلا يكون لكل واحد منهم إلا فعل واحد وإليه الإشارة بقوله تعالى وما منا إلا وله مقام معلوم فلذلك ليس بينهم تنافس وتقاتل بل مثالهم في تعين مرتبة كل واحد منهم وفعله مثال الحواس الخمس فإن البصر لا يزاحم السمع في إدراك الأصوات ولا الشم يزاحمها ولا هما يتنازعان الشم وليس كاليد والرجل فإنك قد تبطش بأصابع الرجل بطشا ضعيفا فتزاحم به اليد وقد تضرب غيرك برأسك فتزاحم اليد التي هي آلة الضرب ولا كالإنسان الواحد الذي يتولى بنفسه الطحن والعجن والخبز فإن هذا نوع من الاعوجاج والعدول عن العدل سببه اختلاف صفات الإنسان واختلاف دواعيه فإنه ليس وحداني الصفة
37:164.english: If you say: Why were these acts not delegated to a single angel, without my needing seven angels? — For the wheat also requires one to grind it first, then one to separate the bran from it and cast away the refuse second, then one to pour water upon it third, then one to knead it fourth, then one to cut it into round balls fifth, then one to roll it into broad flat loaves sixth, then one to affix it to the oven seventh — yet a single man may undertake all of that and suffice for it. So why were not the works of the angels inwardly like the works of men outwardly? — Know that the constitution (khilqah) of the angels differs from the constitution of men. There is not a single one of them but is singular in attribute (waḥdānī al-ṣifah), having in him no admixture or composition whatsoever; hence there cannot issue from each of them save a single act. And to this points His saying, the Exalted: {«وما منا إلا له مقام معلوم»} (And there is not one of us but has a known station) {Q. 37:164}. Therefore there is among them no rivalry and no combat. Rather, their example, in the determination of the rank of each one of them and his act, is the example of the five senses: for sight does not vie with hearing in the perception of sounds, nor does smell vie with them, nor do the two contend with smell over it. And it is not like the hand and the foot — for you may grasp feebly with the toes of your foot and thereby vie with the hand — nor like when you strike another with your head and thereby vie with the hand which is the instrument of striking. Nor is it like the single man who undertakes by himself the grinding, the kneading, and the baking, for this is a kind of crookedness and deviation from equity, whose cause is the diversity of man's attributes and the diversity of his impulses: for he is not singular in attribute, and therefore he is not singular in act. For this reason we see man obeying Allah at one time and disobeying Him at another, due to the diversity of his impulses and attributes. And that is not possible in the nature of the angels; rather, they are created disposed to obedience — there is no scope for disobedience in their case. Hence, necessarily: {«لا يعصون الله ما أمرهم ويفعلون ما يؤمرون»} (They do not disobey Allah in what He commands them, and they do what they are commanded) {Q. 66:6}, and {«يسبحون الليل والنهار لا يفترون»} (They glorify night and day without ceasing) {Q. 21:20}. The one who bows among them is bowing forever, the one who prostrates among them is prostrating forever, and the one who stands is standing forever — there is no variation in their acts and no weariness, and for each one is a known station (maqām maʿlūm) which he does not overstep. And their obedience to Allah the Exalted — inasmuch as there is no scope for opposition in them — may be likened to the obedience of your limbs to you: for whenever you have resolved with firm will upon opening the eyelids, the sound eyelid has no hesitation or variation — obeying you at one time and disobeying you at another — but rather it is as though it awaits your command and your prohibition, opening and closing continuously at your signal. This resembles it in one respect but differs from it in another: for the eyelid has no knowledge of what issues from it of movement, opening and shutting, whereas the angels are living beings, knowing what they do.
37:164.section_title_en: The Division and Distribution of Nutritive Substance — The Earthly Angels and the Hierarchy of Divine Bounty
37:164.anchors:
- Root: ملك (malaka)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الملك: هو المتصرف بالأمر والنهي" — the one who governs by command and prohibition; dominion and sovereign power.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الملك: هو المتصرف بالأمر والنهي في الجمهور" — the angel (malak) as a designated agent of divine governance, distinct from human composite agency.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): "لله الملك والملكوت" — absolute sovereignty. Metaphorical (Majaz): "ملك عليه أمره إذا استولى عليه" — not applicable here; the term is used in its literal theological sense of delegated divine administration.
- Root: وحد (waḥada)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الواحد: ما لا جزء له" — that which has no part; indivisible unity.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الواحد في الحقيقة هو الشيء الذي لا جزء له البتة" — the truly one is that which has no composition whatsoever; hence "وحداني الصفة" (singular in attribute) means uncompounded in nature.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "هو واحد، وهم وحدان" — numerical unity. Here applied analogically to angelic nature: absolute simplicity without admixture.
- Root: نعم (naʿima)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "النعمة: الحالة الحسنة" — the goodly state; benefaction.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "النعمة: الحالة الحسنة... والنعمة للجنس تقال للقليل والكثير" — bounty as a genus encompassing both apparent (ẓāhirah) and inward (bāṭinah) blessings.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "جلت نعمة الله ونعماؤه" — manifest divine beneficence. Metaphorical: "خفّت نعامتهم: ذهبوا" — not applicable; the term is literal throughout.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — governing the periodic suspension of clauses (e.g., "فإن قلت... فاعلم أن") where the protasis is held in suspense before the apodosis, requiring the reader to grasp the full syntactic arc before resolution.
37:164.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

37:164.arabic: على حال واحد لا يزيد ولا ينقص لذلك أخبر الله عنهم أنهم قالوا وما منا إلا له مقام معلوم وفارق الإنسان الملائكة في الترقي من درجة إلى درجة فإنه لا يزال يتقرب إلى الله تعالى فيستفيد مزيد قربه وباب المزيد مسدود على الملائكة عليهم السلام وليس لكل واحد إلا رتبته التي هي وقف عليه وعبادته التي هو مشغول بها لا ينتقل إلى غيرها ولا يفتر عنها لا يستكبرون عن عبادته ولا يستحسرون يسبحون الليل والنهار لا يفترون ومفتاح مزيد الدرجات هي الصلوات قال الله عز وجل قد أفلح المؤمنون الذين هم في صلاتهم خاشعون فمدحهم بعد الإيمان بصلاة مخصوصة وهي المقرونة بالخش
37:164.english: For the friends of God (awliyāʾ Allāh) who are granted unveiling of the dominion of the heavens and the earth (malakūt al-samāwāt wa-al-arḍ) and the secrets of lordship (asrār al-rubūbiyyah) — they are unveiled only in prayer, especially in prostration (sujūd), for the servant draws near to his Lord (Mighty and Majestic) through prostration. For this reason, He said, Most High: {«And prostrate and draw near»} (Q 96:19). And the unveiling of each worshiper is only to the measure of his purity from the turbidities of this world. It varies in strength and weakness, in abundance and scarcity, and in clarity and obscurity — until some are unveiled the very thing itself (al-shayʾ bi-ʿaynihi), while others are unveiled its likeness (al-shayʾ bi-mithālihi), just as some were shown this world in the form of a corpse, and Satan in the form of a dog crouching upon it, calling people to it.
37:164.section_title_en: The Prayer of the Humble and the Unveiling of the Unveiled — Section 140
37:164.anchors:
- Root: خ ش ع (kh-sh-ʿ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of humility, submissiveness, and lowering oneself; the physical posture of one who is abased before a greater power.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In theological terms, khushūʿ is the state of the heart's stillness and trembling before divine majesty, manifesting in the body's composure during ritual prayer (ṣalāh).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) refers to the physical lowering of the gaze and voice; metaphorical (majāz) extends to the soul's inner quietude and awe before God.
- Root: ك ش ف (k-sh-f)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To remove a covering, unveil, disclose; the act of stripping away an obstruction to reveal what lies beneath.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In Quranic usage, kashf denotes divine removal of veils (kashf al-ḥijāb) — the uncovering of unseen realities (ghayb) to the heart, as in {«We have removed from you your covering»} (Q 50:22).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: uncovering a physical object; metaphorical: the disclosure of spiritual truths (mukāshafah) to the purified heart, a technical term in Sufi epistemology.
- Root: ص ل و (ṣ-l-w)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The root denotes supplication, blessing, and the act of ritual prayer; also the burning of fire (iṣlāʾ), suggesting the consuming fervor of devotion.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-ṣalāh is the act of turning toward God in worship, encompassing both the physical rites and the inner orientation of the soul; its perfection lies in the presence of the heart.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the performance of the prescribed ritual; metaphorical: the soul's "burning" with longing and its purification through the fire of sincere devotion.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — The use of restrictive particles to single out the specific quality (khushūʿ) as the defining attribute of the believers' prayer, distinguishing it from mere mechanical performance.
37:164.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Mysteries of Prayer'

38:44.arabic: ورحمة وأولئك هم المهتدون} وكان حبيب بن أبي حبيب إذا قرأ هذه الآية إنا وجدناه صابرا نعم العبد إنه أواب بكى وقال واعجباه أعطى وأثنى أي هو المعطي للصبر وهو المثني وقال أبو الدرداء ذروة الإيمان الصبر للحكم والرضا بالقدر هذا بيان فضيلة الصبر من حيث النقل وأما من حيث النظر بعين الاعتبار فلا تفهمه إلا بعد فهم حقيقة الصبر ومعناه إذ معرفة الفضيلة والرتبة معرفة صفة فلا تحصل قبل معرفة الموصوف فلنذكر حقيقته ومعناه وبالله التوفيق
38:44.english: Allah — exalted be He — has described the patient (al-ṣābirīn) with attributes, and He mentioned patience (al-ṣabr) in the Qur’an in upwards of seventy places. He attached most of the degrees and goods to patience, making them its fruit. For He said — majestic is His utterance: {«وَجَعَلْنَا مِنْهُمْ أَئِمَّةً يَهْدُونَ بِأَمْرِنَا لَمَّا صَبَرُوا»} — “And We made from among them imams guiding by Our command, when they were patient” (Q 32:24). And He said — exalted be He: {«وَتَمَّتْ كَلِمَتُ رَبِّكَ الْحُسْنَىٰ عَلَىٰ بَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ بِمَا صَبَرُوا»} — “And the good word of your Lord was fulfilled upon the Children of Israel, because they were patient” (Q 7:137). And He said — exalted be He: {«وَلَنَجْزِيَنَّ الَّذِينَ صَبَرُوا أَجْرَهُم بِأَحْسَنِ مَا كَانُوا يَعْمَلُونَ»} — “And We shall surely recompense those who were patient their wage according to the best of what they used to do” (Q 16:96). And He said — exalted be He: {«أُولَٰئِكَ يُؤْتَوْنَ أَجْرَهُم مَّرَّتَيْنِ بِمَا صَبَرُوا»} — “Those shall be given their wage twice, because they were patient” (Q 28:54). And He said — exalted be He: {«إِنَّمَا يُوَفَّى الصَّابِرُونَ أَجْرَهُم بِغَيْرِ حِسَابٍ»} — “Only the patient shall be paid their wage without reckoning” (Q 39:10). Thus there is no act of nearness (qurbah) whose wage is not meted out by measure and account — except patience. And because fasting (al-ṣawm) is of patience, and it is half of patience, Allah — exalted be He — said: “Fasting is Mine, and I recompense it” — so He attributed it to Himself, to the exclusion of all other acts of worship. And He promised the patient that He is with them, saying — exalted be He: {«وَاصْبِرُوا إِنَّ اللَّهَ مَعَ الصَّابِرِينَ»} — “And be patient; indeed Allah is with the patient” (Q 8:46). And He made victory contingent upon patience, saying — exalted be He: {«بَلَىٰ إِن تَصْبِرُوا وَتَتَّقُوا وَيَأْتُوكُم مِّن فَوْرِهِمْ هَٰذَا يُمْدِدْكُمْ رَبُّكُم بِخَمْسَةِ آلَافٍ مِّنَ الْمَلَائِكَةِ مُسَوِّمِينَ»} — “Yes, if you are patient and God-fearing, and they come upon you in their rush, your Lord will reinforce you with five thousand marked angels” (Q 3:125). And He gathered for the patient things He gathered for no others, saying — exalted be He: {«أُولَٰئِكَ عَلَيْهِمْ صَلَوَاتٌ مِّن رَّبِّهِمْ وَرَحْمَةٌ وَأُولَٰئِكَ هُمُ الْمُهْتَدُونَ»} — “Those — upon them are blessings from their Lord, and mercy; and those — they are the rightly guided” (Q 2:157). So guidance, mercy, and blessings are all gathered for the patient. And to exhaust all the verses concerning the station of patience would be lengthy.
38:44.section_title_en: The Virtue of Patience (Ṣabr) — Its Excellence in the Qur’an, Sunnah, and Reports of the Salaf
38:44.anchors:
- Root: صبر (Ṣ-B-R)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning is “to restrain, to hold back, to bind firmly” — as in holding an animal by its halter or confining someone against departure.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Patience is “the self’s restraint upon what reason and Sacred Law require, or from what they require it to abstain from.” It is a generic term whose specific names vary by context: in calamity it is ṣabr (opposed to jazaʿ); in battle it is courage (shajāʿah); in vexation it is forbearance.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): “I bore patiently what I disliked, and I refrained patiently from what I loved.” Metaphorical (majāz): “His right hand was made to swear patiently” (i.e., bound by an emphatic oath), and “this tree is patient against cold” (i.e., unaffected by it).
- Root: عله (ʿ-L-H) — [Noted as a rare root; no direct bearing on this passage’s core terms, but included per lexical apparatus.]
- Root: ايم (A-Y-M) — [Noted as a rare root; no direct bearing on this passage’s core terms, but included per lexical apparatus.]
- Root: نفس (N-F-S)
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The self (nafs) as the locus of volitional restraint — patience is an act of the nafs holding itself back, distinguishing it from mere physical endurance.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: “a precious thing” (nafīs). Metaphorical: “he poured out his soul” (i.e., his blood), and “everything that has no flowing soul does not defile water.”
- Sibawayh Rule: Restriction and Focused Predication (Bāb al-Ḥaṣr wa al-Taqyīd bi-innamā) — Governing the exclusive clause {«إِنَّمَا يُوَفَّى الصَّابِرُونَ أَجْرَهُم بِغَيْرِ حِسَابٍ»}, where innamā restricts the reward-without-account solely to the patient, and {«الصَّوْمُ لِي وَأَنَا أَجْزِي بِهِ»}, where the predicate is focused to Allah alone.
38:44.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

38:44.arabic: قوله تعالى {نعم العبد إنه أواب} إلى غير ذلك وليقل القابض في دعائه طهر الله قلبك في قلوب الأبرار وزكى عملك في عمل الأخيار وصلى على روحك في أرواح الشهداء وقد قال صلى الله عليه وسلم من أسدى إليكم معروفا فكافئوه فإن لم تستطيعوا فادعوا له حتى تعلموا أنكم قد كافأتموه (2) ومن تمام الشكر أن يستر عيوب العطاء إن كان فيه عيب ولا يحقره ولا يذمه ولا يعيره بالمنع إذا منع ويفخم عند نفسه وعند الناس صنيعه فوظيفة المعطي الاستصغار ووظيفة القابض تقلد المنة والاستعظام وعلى كل عبد القيام بحقه وذلك ل
38:44.english: The second: that he thank the giver, supplicate for him, and praise him; and his gratitude and supplication should be such that it does not remove him from being a mere intermediary, but rather he is a channel for the arrival of God's blessing to him. And the channel has a right, insofar as God made him a channel and an intermediary — and that does not negate seeing the blessing as from God, Glorified be He. For he, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "He who does not thank the people has not thanked God" {«من لم يشكر الناس لم يشكر الله»}. And God, Mighty and Majestic, has praised His servants in places for their deeds, while He is their Creator and the Originator of the capacity for them — such as His saying, Exalted is He: {«نعم العبد إنه أواب»} ["Excellent is the servant. Indeed, he is penitent."] — and other similar instances.
38:44.section_title_en: The Etiquette of the Recipient of Wealth: On the Virtue of Poverty and the Conduct of Taking from Others
38:44.anchors:
- Root: كرم (karuma)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root meaning: nobility, generosity, honorableness of origin and character.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: Divine Generosity (al-Karam) as an attribute of God entailing beneficence (al-Ifḍāl) that is pure grace, not obligation.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: nobility of lineage/character. Metaphorical: God's abundant giving without recompense.
- Root: فضل (faḍala)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root meaning: surplus, excess, superiority, that which remains beyond need.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: God's Bounty (al-Faḍl) as gratuitous favor exceeding what is merited; distinct from justice ('Adl).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: excess/surplus. Metaphorical: divine favor and grace.
- Root: نعم (ni'ma)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root meaning: well-being, bounty, benefaction; state of goodness.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-Ni'ma as the good state (al-ḥālah al-ḥasanah) bestowed by God; its genus encompasses both little and much.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: pleasant life and bounty. Metaphorical: "خفت نعامتهم" (their ostriches departed) — i.e., they went away, indicating the fleeting nature of worldly boons.
- Root: قدر (qadara)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root meaning: measure, extent, power, decree.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-Qudrah for God is the negation of incapacity; for man, a capacity for specific acts. Al-Qadr: the divine measure/decree.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: measure, amount, power. Metaphorical: "فرس بعيد القدر" (a horse of far-reaching stride) — extended reach.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — Governing the precise restriction of agency and causation in statements like "إنما المنكر أن يرى الواسطة أصلا" (The only objectionable thing is to regard the intermediary as the origin).
38:44.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Mysteries of Zakat'

38:65.arabic: يقوله رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لا إله إلا الله الواحد القهار رب السموات والأرض وما بينهما العزيز الغفار (3) وليجتهد أن يكون آخر ما يجري على قلبه عند النوم ذكر الله تعالى وأول ما يرد على قلبه عند التيقظ ذكر الله تعالى فهو علامة الحب ولا يلازم القلب في هاتين الحالتين إلا ما هو الغالب عليه فليجرب قلبه به فهو علامة الحب فإنها علامة تكشف من باطن القلب وإنما استحبت هذه الأذكار لتستجر القلب إلى ذكر الله تعالى فإذا استيقظ ليقوم قال الحمد لله الذي أحيانا بعد ما أماتنا وإليه النشور إلى آخر ما أوردناه من أدعية التيق
38:65.english: Then it is recommended, after the salutation of the witr, that he say: "Glory be to the King, the Most Holy, the Lord of the angels and the Spirit. You have enveloped the heavens and the earth with majesty and dominion. You have manifested Your might through power, and You have subdued the servants through death." It is related that he (peace and blessings be upon him) — until he died — most of his prayer was seated, except for the obligatory prayers (1). And he said to the one who prays seated: "Half the reward of the one who prays standing," and to the one who sleeps: "Half the reward of the one who prays seated" (2). This indicates the validity of the supererogatory prayer in all states.
38:65.section_title_en: The Fourth and Fifth Wirds (Portions of Night Devotion): On Sleep and the Final Sixth of the Night
38:65.anchors:
- Root: ليل (Layl)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Night; the period of darkness from sunset to dawn; its plural forms include layālī and layalāt.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Night is a divinely ordained sign (āyah) of Allah's power; sleep is described as a form of death (tawaffā) in the Qur'an, linking the nightly cycle to resurrection.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (haqīqah) for the astronomical night; metaphorical (majāz) for spiritual darkness or heedlessness.
- Root: نوم (Nawm)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Sleep; slumber; a state of rest.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Sleep is "death in a light form" (al-mawt al-khafīf), and death is "sleep in a heavy form" (al-nawm al-thaqīl). Allah says: {«Allah takes the souls at the time of their death, and those that die not during their sleep»} (Q. 39:42).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: bodily rest. Metaphorical: heedlessness (ghaflah) or spiritual inertia; "the market slept" means it stagnated.
- Root: عله (Alaha/Ilah)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To worship; to seek refuge; the root for ilāh (deity) and Allāh (the Supreme Deity).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The root denotes the act of devotion and the object of ultimate veneration; al-ulūhiyyah is the state of being worshipped.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: deity. Metaphorical: that which one is utterly devoted to or enslaved by (e.g., one's desires).
- Root: الي (Alā/Yalū)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To be occupied with; to manage; related to al-ālah (instrument) and ma'ālah (consequence).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The root conveys the idea of returning to a state or being entrusted with a matter; al-ālah is that by which one accomplishes an affair.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: instrumentality. Metaphorical: the means by which one draws near to Allah.
- Sibawayh Rule: Restriction and Focused Predication (al-Ḥaṣr wa al-Taqyīd bi-innamā) — Used to distinguish the specific legal scope of actions (e.g., the witr prayer's status) and to restrict general statements to their precise conditions.
38:65.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications, prayers, and their spiritual power, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

38:76.arabic: فمن استفزته نار الغضب فقد قويت فيه قرابة الشيطان حيث قال {خلقتني من نار وخلقته من طين} فإن شأن الطين السكون والوقار وشأن النار التلظي والاستعار والحركة والاضطراب ومن نتائج الغضب الحقد والحسد وبهما هلك من هلك وفسد من فسد ومفيضهما مضغة إذا صلحت صلح معها سائر الجسد وإذا كان الحقد والحسد والغضب مما يسوق العبد إلى مواطن العطب فما أحوجه إلى معرفة معاطبه ومساويه ليحذر ذلك ويتقيه ويميطه عن القلب إن كان وينفيه ويعالجه إن رسخ في قلبه ويداويه فإن من لا يعرف الشر يقع فيه ومن عرفه فالمعرفة لا تكفيه ما لم يعرف الطريق الذي به يدفع الشر ويقصيه و
38:76.english: In the name of God, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate. Praise be to God, upon whose pardon and mercy none rely except the hopeful, and from whose evil wrath and assault none fear except the fearful — He who gradually seizes His servants from whence they know not, and who has given dominion over them to their lusts, commanding them to abandon what they desire, and who has tried them with anger while charging them to swallow their rage in what provokes them. Then He surrounded them with hardships and pleasures, and granted them respite to see how they would act. He tested their love through them, to make known the truth of what they claim. He made known to them that nothing is hidden from Him of what they conceal or proclaim, and warned them lest He seize them suddenly while they are unaware. For He said: {«They await but a single blast which will seize them while they are disputing; so they will not be able to make a bequest, nor to their families will they return»} (Q. 36:49-50). And prayers and peace be upon Muhammad, His Messenger, beneath whose banner the prophets walk, and upon his family and companions — the rightly-guided imams and the pleasing masters — prayers whose number equals the number of what has been of God's creation and what will be, and by whose blessing the first and the last are favored — and abundant peace.
38:76.section_title_en: The Book of Condemnation of Anger, Spite, and Envy — Book Five of the Quarter of Destroyers from The Revival of the Religious Sciences
38:76.anchors:
- Root: غضب (ghadab)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root meaning of anger, rage, fury; the boiling and agitation of the blood
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance — when attributed to God, it means retribution (intiqām) alone, not emotional agitation; the Prophet described it as "a live coal kindled in the heart of the son of Adam"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal vs Metaphorical — literal anger is the boiling of the blood in living beings; metaphorical usage extends to inanimate things like fire and the reins of a mount
- Root: قلب (qalb)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The heart; also the turning, overturning, and transformation of a thing from one state to another
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance — the heart is so named for its constant turning (taqallub) and fluctuation between states; it is the seat of understanding and the locus of divine address
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal vs Metaphorical — literal is the physical organ; metaphorical is the subtle spiritual reality (laṭīfah rabbāniyyah) that is the locus of knowledge and will
- Root: حسد (hasad)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Envy; the wishing for removal of another's blessing
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance — envy is the desire for the removal of a blessing from one who deserves it, sometimes accompanied by striving to remove it; the believer envies (ghibṭah) while the hypocrite envies (hasad)
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal vs Metaphorical — "Envy consumes the body as fire consumes wood"; the envier is one who wishes evil upon the blessed
- Root: هلك (halak)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Perdition, destruction, ruin; death
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance — three senses: (1) loss of a thing from one's possession while it exists elsewhere, (2) corruption and dissolution of a thing, (3) death; the Quran uses it for all three
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal vs Metaphorical — literal is physical destruction; metaphorical is the ruin of one's religion and afterlife through spiritual corruption
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The permissibility of interposing elements between a preposition and its object when the intervening material constitutes a complete, meaningful unit, as in the Quranic pattern of extended periodic sentences that delay resolution for rhetorical effect.
38:76.topic: Al-Ghazali on purifying the character, moral diseases, and spiritual remedies, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

38:76.arabic: وهذه أقيسة فاسدة تشبه قياس إبليس حيث قال {أنا خير منه خلقتني من نار وخلقته من طين} وإلى هؤلاء الإشارة بقوله تعالى {أولئك الذين اشتروا الحياة الدنيا بالآخرة فلا يخفف عنهم العذاب ولا هم ينصرون} وعلاج هذا الغرور إما بتصديق الإيمان وإما بالبرهان أما التصديق بمجرد الإيمان فهو أن يصدق الله تعالى في قوله ما عندكم ينفذ وما عند الله باق وفي قوله عز وجل {وما عند الله خير} وقوله {والآخرة خير وأبقى} وقوله {وما الحياة الدنيا إلا متاع الغرور} وقوله {فلا تغرنكم الحياة الدنيا} وقد أخبر رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بذلك طوائف من الكفار فقلدوه وصدقوه
38:76.english: Know that the saying of God Most High — {«fa-lā taghurrannakum al-ḥayātu al-dunyā wa-lā yaghurrannakum billāhi al-gharūr»} (So let not the life of this world deceive you, nor let the Deceiver deceive you concerning God) — and His saying — {«wa-lākinnakum fatantum anfusakum wa-tarabbastum wa-irtabtum wa-gharratkum al-amānī»} (But ye tempted your own souls, and ye waited, and ye doubted, and vain desires deceived you) — is sufficient for the blameworthiness of self-deception (al-ghurūr). And the Messenger of God, may God's peace and blessing be upon him, has said: "How excellent is the sleep of the intelligent and their breaking of the fast! How they outwit the wakefulness of the foolish and their striving! And verily a mustard-seed's weight [of faith] from a possessor of piety and certainty is better than the earth filled with the self-deceived." And the ḥadīth: "The intelligent man (al-kayyis) is he who takes account of his own soul and works for what is after death" — this ḥadīth was transmitted by al-Tirmidhī and Ibn Mājah from the ḥadīth of Shaddād ibn Aws.
38:76.section_title_en: Exposition of the Blameworthiness of Self-Deception (Al-Ghurūr), Its Reality, and Its Examples
38:76.anchors:
- Root: غرر (Gh-R-R)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The core meaning is "an apparent trace or mark of a thing" (al-athar al-ẓāhir), from which derives "the blaze of a horse" (ghurrat al-faras). To deceive (gharra) is to strike one's heedlessness (ghirrah) and attain one's sought desire from him, as if folding a garment upon its original crease (ṭawāhu ʿalā gharrihi).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Ghurrah is heedlessness in wakefulness, and ghirār is heedlessness with drowsiness." Theologically, it is the soul's repose upon a false semblance (shubhah) that pleases the caprice (hawā), rendering one oblivious to the true state of affairs—as in {«mā gharraka bi-rabbika al-karīm»} (What deceived thee concerning thy Generous Lord?).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): "A gazelle in a moonlit night is called agharr" because it ventures out thinking it is day and is devoured by beasts—heedlessness in perception. Metaphorical (majāz): "A day agharr muḥajjal" (a white-browed, white-legged day) for intense heat, transferring the blaze of a horse to the day's visible intensity.
- Root: جهل (J-H-L)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "Jahila bihi" — to be ignorant of it; "jāhala ʿalā qawmihi" — to act foolishly/insolently against one's people. The pre-Islamic era is "al-jāhiliyyah al-jahlā'" (the utterly ignorant age).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Ignorance (jahl) is of three kinds: (1) the soul's emptiness of knowledge (this is the root); (2) believing a thing contrary to what it is; (3) doing a thing contrary to what it ought to be, whether one's belief is sound or corrupt. Ghurūr is a species of the second kind—a false belief arising from a corrupt semblance.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "Kafā bil-shakki jahlā" (Sufficient is doubt as ignorance). Metaphorical: "Istajhalat al-rīḥ al-ghuṣn" (The wind made the branch sway violently) — transferred from mental foolishness to physical agitation.
- Root: حدث (Ḥ-D-TH)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "Al-ḥudūth: the coming-to-be of a thing after it was not." "Al-ḥadath: the novel event." "Ḥaddatha: to speak/communicate."
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Ḥudūth is the existence of a thing after non-existence, whether accident or substance. Iḥdāth is bringing it into existence. The iḥdāth of substances belongs to God alone." The "ḥadīth" (report/speech) is so-called for its temporal novelty.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "Nazalat bihi ḥawādith al-dahr" (The vicissitudes of time befell him). Metaphorical: "Kāna ʿUmar muḥaddathan" (Umar was one inspired with true discernment) — as if he were spoken to (ḥudditha) by what he conjectured.
- Root: دنا (D-N-W)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "Danā fa-huwa dānin" — he drew near. "Al-dunyā" (the lower world) is so named because it is nearer (danat) and precedes the Hereafter.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Al-dunūw: proximity by essence or by judgment, used of place, time, and station." The "adnā" (lower/nearer) is contrasted with the greater and with the better: {«a-tastabdilūna alladhī huwa adnā billadhī huwa khayr»} (Will ye take the lower in exchange for what is better?).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "Huwa danī' min al-adniyā'" (He is base, of the base ones) — but this is the homonym danu'a (baseness), distinct from danā (nearness). The dunyā's "nearness" is its temporal immediacy versus the Hereafter's deferral.
- Sibawayh Rule: Bab al-faṣl bayna al-jār wa-al-majrūr (Prepositional Interposition) — The particle "bi" in {«wa-lā yaghurrannakum billāhi al-gharūr»} governs the deceiver (al-gharūr) as the agent of deception, while "billāh" (concerning God) is the object of the deception. The syntactic structure permits the deceiver to be named after the prepositional phrase, indicating that the deception is *about* God's attributes (His forbearance, His respite) — a grammatical subtlety showing the ghurūr deceives *by means of* false notions of God, not that God Himself deceives.
38:76.topic: Al-Ghazali on the journey of the soul, death, and the Hereafter, from 'Condemnation of Delusion'

39:3.arabic: قال الله تعالى وما أمروا إلا ليعبدوا الله مخلصين له الدين {وقال} ألا لله الدين الخالص وقال تعالى إلا الذين تابوا وأصلحوا واعتصموا بالله وأخلصوا دينهم لله وقال تعالى فمن كان يرجو لقاء ربه فليعمل عملا صالحا ولا يشرك بعبادة ربه أحدا نزلت فيمن يعمل لله ويحب أن يحمد عليه وقال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ثلاث لا يغل عليهن قلب رجل مسلم إخلاص العمل لله (1) وعن مصعب بن سعد عن أبيه قال ظن أبي أن له فضلا على من هو دونه من أصحاب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم إنما نصر الله عز وجل هذه الأمة بضعفائها ودعوتهم وإخلاصهم
39:3.english: God Most High said: {وما أمروا إلا ليعبدوا الله مخلصين له الدين} "And they were not commanded except to worship God, devoting their religion purely to Him." And He said: {ألا لله الدين الخالص} "Verily, to God belongs the pure religion." And He, Most High, said: {إلا الذين تابوا وأصلحوا واعتصموا بالله وأخلصوا دينهم لله} "Except those who repent, and make amends, and hold fast to God, and make their religion pure for God." And He, Most High, said: {فمن كان يرجو لقاء ربه فليعمل عملا صالحا ولا يشرك بعبادة ربه أحدا} "So whoever hopes for the meeting with his Lord, let him do righteous work, and not associate anyone in the worship of his Lord." This was revealed concerning the one who works for God but loves to be praised for it.
39:3.section_title_en: The Book of the Revival of the Religious Sciences — Section on Sincerity (Ikhlas): Its Virtue and the Peril of Ostentation (Riya')
39:3.anchors:
- Root: أخلَصَ (akhlaṣa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning is purity and clarity; khāliṣ is that which is unmixed and free from adulteration—pure gold, pure milk, pure friendship.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In theological usage, ikhlāṣ is the purification of one's act and intention (niyyah) exclusively for God, stripping away every other motive or partner. It is the essential condition for the acceptance of worship.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah) usage refers to the physical purity of a substance; metaphorical (Majaz) usage transfers this to the heart and deed, signifying the purification of intention from all that is not God.
- Root: دين (dīn)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning includes obedience, recompense, judgment, and the established way or custom.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The "religion" (dīn) of God is the way of obedience and submission to Him; "pure religion" (al-dīn al-khāliṣ) is that which is free from shirk (associationism) and hypocrisy.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the debt or obligation one owes; Metaphorical: the total submission and worship owed exclusively to the Creator.
- Root: راءى (rā'ā)
  * Lisan / Ayn: From the root رأى (ra'ā), to see. The third form implies showing off, making one's deeds seen by others.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Riya' is the seeking of status and praise from creatures, which nullifies the sincerity of the act directed to the Creator.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: to make something visible to the eye; Metaphorical: to perform an act of worship not for God, but so that people may see it and praise the doer.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Restriction and Focused Predication (باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما) — The particle "innamā" (إنما) restricts the predicate to the subject alone, negating all else. This is critical in the opening verse: "وما أمروا إلا ليعبدوا الله" — the restriction (hasr) via "illā" (except) confines their command solely to the worship of God with pure sincerity.
39:3.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Monitoring and Accounting'

39:3.arabic: والذين اتخذوا من دونه أولياء ما نعبدهم إلا ليقربونا إلى الله زلفى أي يقولون ما نعبدهم وقوله عز وجل فمال هؤلاء القوم لا يكادون يفقهون حديثا ما أصابك من حسنة فمن الله وما أصابك من سيئة فمن نفسك معناه لا يفقهون حديثا يقولون ما أصابك من حسنة فمن الله فإن لم يرد هذا كان مناقضا لقوله قل كل من عند الله وسبق إلى الفهم منه مذهب القدرية ومنها المنقول المنقلب كقوله تعالى وطور سينين أي طور سيناء سلام على آل ياسين أي على الياس وقيل إدريس لأن في حرف ابن مسعود سلام على إدراسين ومنها المكرر القاطع لوصل الكلام
39:3.english: I say: The Prophet (peace be upon him) was asked about the means of deliverance from these trials, and he said: "The Book of Allah — act by what is in it, for it is that which delivers one from them." The questioner repeated this three times, and he (peace be upon him) said three times: "Learn the Book of Allah, Mighty and Glorious, and act by what is in it, for in it is deliverance."
39:3.section_title_en: The Book of the Etiquette of Recitation — Section 233: On Understanding the Meanings of the Qur'an and the Limits of Interpretation
39:3.anchors:
- Root: ف-ه-م (f-h-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الفهم: هيئة للإنسان بها يتحقق معاني ما يحسن" — comprehension as an inherent faculty by which one ascertains meanings
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الفهم: هيئة للإنسان بها يتحقق معاني ما يحسن... وأفهمته: إذا قلت له حتى تصوره" — comprehension is a cognitive disposition; distinction between understanding (fahm) and making understood (ifhām)
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "تقول: من لم يؤت من سوء الفهم أتى من سوء الإفهام" — literal usage; failure of understanding often stems from failure of communication
- Root: ف-س-ر (f-s-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "وكل شيء يعرف به تفسير الشيء ومعناه، فهو تَفْسِرَتُه" — that by which a thing's meaning is made known
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "التفسير قد يقال فيما يختص بمفردات الألفاظ وغريبها، وفيما يختص بالتأويل" — tafsīr concerns lexical surface; taʾwīl concerns deeper meaning
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "هذا كلام يحتاج إلى فسر وتفسير" — literal: exposition of what is obscure
- Root: و-ج-ل (w-j-l)
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الوجل: استشعار الخوف" — the sensing of fear; used of hearts trembling at divine mention
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "لو واجلت فلانا لوجلته: لغلبته في الوجل" — literal sense of fear; metaphorical extension to overpowering in fear
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — the particle innamā restricts predication, essential for parsing the Prophet's saying "innamā al-aʿmālu bi-l-niyyāt" and analogous restrictive formulations in the ḥadīth cited herein
39:3.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

39:3.arabic: وقال عز وجل حتى توارت الحجاب أراد الشمس وما سبق لها ذكر وقوله تعالى والذين اتخذوا من دونه أولياء ما نعبدهم إلا ليقربونا إلى الله زلفى أي يقولون ما نعبدهم وقوله عز وجل فمال هؤلاء القوم لا يكادون يفقهون حديثا ما أصابك من حسنة فمن الله وما أصابك من سيئة فمن نفسك معناه لا يفقهون حديثا يقولون ما أصابك من حسنة فمن الله فإن لم يرد هذا كان مناقضا لقوله قل كل من عند الله وسبق إلى الفهم منه مذهب القدرية ومنها المنقول المنقلب كقوله تعالى وطور سينين أي طور سيناء سلام على آل ياسين أي على الياس وقيل إدريس لأن في حرف ابن مسعود سلام على إدراسين ومنها المكرر القاطع لوصل الكلام ف
39:3.english: I say: The Prophet (peace be upon him) was asked about the means of deliverance from these trials, and he said: "The Book of Allah — act by what is in it, for it is that which delivers one from them." The questioner repeated this three times, and he (peace be upon him) said three times: "Learn the Book of Allah, Mighty and Glorious, and act by what is in it, for in it is deliverance."

  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "لو واجلت فلانا لوجلته: لغلبته في الوجل" — literal sense of fear; metaphorical extension to overpowering in fear

39:3.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Etiquette of Quran Recitation'

39:10.arabic: الله تعالى {إنما يوفى الصابرون أجرهم بغير حساب} والصوم نصف الصبر فقد جاوز ثوابه قانون التقدير والحساب وناهيك في معرفة فضله قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم والذي نفسي بيده لخلوف فم الصائم أطيب عند الله من ريح المسك يقول الله عز وجل إنما يذر شهوته وطعامه وشرابه لأجلي فالصوم لي وأنا أجزي به (3) وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم للجنة باب يقال له الريال لا يدخله إلا الصائمون وهو موعود بلقاء الله تعالى في جزء صومه (4) وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم للصائم فرحتان فرحة عند إفطاره وفرحة عند لقاء ربه (5) وقال صلى الله عليه وس
39:10.english: To proceed: Fasting is one quarter of faith, by virtue of his saying, peace and blessings be upon him: "Fasting is half of patience" — and by virtue of his saying, peace and blessings be upon him: "Patience is half of faith" {«الإيمان»}. Then it is distinguished by a particular characteristic of its attribution to Allah the Exalted, above all the other pillars — for Allah the Exalted said, in what His Prophet narrated from Him, peace and blessings be upon him: "Every good deed is multiplied tenfold up to seven hundred times, except fasting, for it is Mine, and I shall reward it." And Allah the Exalted has said: {«Only the patient shall be paid their reward in full without reckoning»} (Q 39:10). And fasting is half of patience — so its reward has surpassed the law of measure and reckoning. And sufficient for you in knowing its excellence is his saying, peace and blessings be upon him: "By Him in whose hand is my soul, the change in the breath of the mouth of the fasting person is more fragrant to Allah than the scent of musk. Allah the Exalted says: 'He only abandons his appetite, his food, and his drink for My sake — so fasting is for Me, and I shall reward it.'" And he said, peace and blessings be upon him: "Paradise has a gate called al-Rayyān, through which none shall enter except the fasting ones." And the fasting person is promised the meeting with Allah the Exalted as a portion of his fasting. And he said, peace and blessings be upon him: "For the fasting person there are two joys: a joy when he breaks his fast, and a joy when he meets his Lord." And he said, peace and blessings be upon him: "Everything has a gate, and the gate of worship is fasting." And he said, peace and blessings be upon him: "The sleep of the fasting person is worship." And Abū Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, narrated that he, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "When the month of Ramaḍān enters, the gates of Paradise are opened, the gates of the Fire are closed, the devils are chained, and a caller calls out: 'O seeker of good, come forth! O seeker of evil, desist!'" And Wakīʿ said concerning His saying, the Exalted: {«Eat and drink in satisfaction for what you sent forth in the days past»} (Q 69:24) — these are the days of fasting, for in them they abandoned eating and drinking. And the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, gathered in the rank of divine boasting (mubāhāh) between renunciation of the world and fasting, saying: "Allah the Exalted boasts to His angels of the young worshiper, saying: 'O young man who abandons his appetite for My sake, who devotes his youth to Me — you are to Me as some of My angels.'" And he said, peace and blessings be upon him, concerning the fasting person: "Allah the Exalted says: 'Look, O My angels, at My servant — he has abandoned his appetite, his pleasure, his food, and his drink for My sake.'" And it was said concerning His saying, the Exalted: {«No soul knows what comfort has been concealed for them, as a reward for what they used to do»} (Q 32:17) — it was said: their deed was fasting, because He said: {«Only the patient shall be paid their reward in full without reckoning»} — so the reward of the fasting person is poured out upon him without measure, and is dealt out to him in bulk, not falling under any imagination or estimation.
39:10.section_title_en: The Book of the Secrets of Fasting — Section 185: On the Excellence of Fasting and Its Distinction Among the Acts of Worship
39:10.anchors:
- Root: صوم (ṣ-w-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core linguistic root meaning — abstention from any act, whether eating, speaking, or walking; a horse that refrains from movement or fodder is called ṣā'im.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological/Kalam semantic nuance — "الصوم في الأصل: الإمساك عن الفعل" — fasting is fundamentally the restraint of the self from action; it is an inward act of the heart, invisible to creation.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal vs Metaphorical distinction — Haqiqah: the month of fasting, "فمن شهد منكم الشهر فليصمه" (Q 2:185); Majaz: "صام الفرس على آريه" — a horse standing still at its tether, refusing fodder, metaphorically "fasting."
- Root: عله (ʿ-l-h)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core linguistic root meaning — to feed or pasture; related to cultivation and nourishment.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological/Kalam semantic nuance — not directly attested in Mufradat for this root; the root pertains to the means by which the body is sustained, which is precisely what the fasting person abstains from.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal vs Metaphorical distinction — literal feeding and satiation; the fasting person's abstention from these becomes the very means of spiritual nourishment.
- Root: الي (a-l-y)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core linguistic root meaning — to convey a message; the angel (malak) is so named because the message is "chewed" (yu'lak) in the mouth, as a horse chews its bit.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological/Kalam semantic nuance — "المألكة: الرسالة" — the angelic function is the conveyance of divine communication; the fasting person's hunger narrows the channels through which the devil (who runs like blood through the veins) reaches the heart.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal vs Metaphorical distinction — literal conveyance of a message versus the metaphorical "message" of the devil's insinuation (waswās) through the pathways of the body.
- Root: صبر (ṣ-b-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core linguistic root meaning — to restrain, to hold back in constriction; "صبرت الدابة: حبستها بلا علف" — to hold an animal back without fodder.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological/Kalam semantic nuance — "الصبر: الإمساك في ضيق" — patience is restraint within constriction; it is the holding of the soul upon what reason and law require, or from what they require it to abstain. Its names vary by context: in battle it is courage, in calamity it is patience proper.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal vs Metaphorical distinction — Haqiqah: "صبرت على ما أكره وصبرت عما أحب" — patience upon the disliked and patience from the beloved; Majaz: "صبرت يمينه" — to bind one's oath severely, and "هو أصبر على الضرب من الأرض" — more enduring of striking than the earth.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — The particle innamā restricts and confines the predicate exclusively to its subject, as in the divine saying {«إنما يوفى الصابرون أجرهم بغير حساب»} and {«إنما يذر شهوته وطعامه وشرابه لأجلي»}, where the restriction elevates the restricted matter to a rank beyond all quantitative measure.
39:10.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

39:22.arabic: بشري وفي لحمي ودمي وعظامي (1) متفق عليه (2) حديث سئل عن قوله تعالى أفمن شرح الله صدر للإسلام الحديث وفي المستدرك من حديث ابن مسعود وقد تقدم في العلم وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم لابن عباس اللهم فقهه في الدين وعلمه التأويل (3) (4) حديث علي ما عندنا شيء أسره إلينا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إلا إن يؤتي الله عبدا فهما في كتابه تقدم في آداب تلاوة القرآن وقيل في تفسير قوله تعالى {يؤتى الحكمة من يشاء} إنه الفهم في كتاب الله وقال تعالى {ففهمناها سليمان} خص ما انكشف باسم الفهم وكان أبو الدرداء يقول المؤمن من ينظر بنور الله من وراء ستر رقي
39:22.english: As for the evidences of the Sacred Law, there is His saying (Exalted is He): {«وَالَّذِينَ جَاهَدُوا فِينَا لَنَهْدِيَنَّهُمْ سُبُلَنَا»} ("And those who strive in Us, We shall surely guide them to Our paths") (Q. 29:69). So every wisdom that appears from the heart through persevering devotion to worship, without learning, is by way of unveiling and inspiration. And he (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Whoever acts upon what he knows, God bequeaths to him knowledge of what he does not know, and grants him success in what he does" — until he becomes deserving of Paradise. And whoever does not act upon what he knows wanders astray in what he knows and is not granted success in what he does, until he becomes deserving of the Fire. [The hadith "Whoever acts upon what he knows" has preceded in the Book of Knowledge, without his saying "and grants him success in what he does" — I have not found it with that addition.] And God (Exalted is He) said: {«وَمَنْ يَتَّقِ اللَّهَ يَجْعَلْ لَهُ مَخْرَجًا»} ("And whoever fears God, He makes for him a way out") (Q. 65:2) — from perplexities and doubts — {«وَيَرْزُقْهُ مِنْ حَيْثُ لَا يَحْتَسِبُ»} ("and provides for him from whence he does not reckon") (Q. 65:3) — teaching him knowledge without learning and granting him discernment without experience. And God (Exalted is He) said: {«يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا إِنْ تَتَّقُوا اللَّهَ يَجْعَلْ لَكُمْ فُرْقَانًا»} ("O you who believe, if you fear God, He will make for you a criterion") (Q. 8:29) — it is said: a light by which one distinguishes between truth and falsehood and by which one emerges from doubts. For this reason, he (peace and blessings be upon him) was abundant in his supplication in asking for light, saying (peace and blessings be upon him): "O God, grant me light, and increase me in light, and make for me light in my heart, and light in my grave, and light in my hearing, and light in my sight" — until he said: "and light in my hair, and in my skin, and in my flesh, and in my blood, and in my bones." [Agreed upon (by al-Bukhari and Muslim).] [The hadith concerning his being asked about His saying {«أَفَمَنْ شَرَحَ اللَّهُ صَدْرَهُ لِلْإِسْلَامِ»} ("Is he whose breast God has expanded for Islam") (Q. 39:22) — and in al-Mustadrak from the hadith of Ibn Masʿūd — has preceded in the Book of Knowledge.] And he (peace and blessings be upon him) said concerning Ibn ʿAbbās: "O God, grant him understanding in religion and teach him the interpretation (taʾwīl)." [The hadith of ʿAlī: "We have nothing with us that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) confided to us except that God grants a servant understanding in His Book" — has preceded in the Etiquettes of Qurʾanic Recitation.] And it is said in the interpretation of His saying (Exalted is He): {«يُؤْتِي الْحِكْمَةَ مَنْ يَشَاءُ»} ("He grants wisdom to whom He wills") (Q. 2:269) that it is understanding in the Book of God. And He (Exalted is He) said: {«فَفَهَّمْنَاهَا سُلَيْمَانَ»} ("And We made Solomon understand it") (Q. 21:79) — singling out what was unveiled with the name of understanding (fahm). And Abū al-Dardāʾ used to say: "The believer is one who sees by the light of God from behind a thin veil. By God, it is the truth that God casts into their hearts and causes to flow upon their tongues." And some of the Salaf said: "The believer's conjecture is like soothsaying."
39:22.section_title_en: The Unveiling of Knowledge Through Divine Inspiration and the Evidences of the Unseen
39:22.anchors:
- Root: علم (ʿalima)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning encompasses both perception of a thing's essence and judgment upon it—knowledge as direct apprehension or discursive ruling.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "العلم: إدراك الشيء بحقيقته" — knowledge is the apprehension of a thing in its true reality, divided into apprehension of the essence (transitive to one object) and judgment upon existence or non-existence (transitive to two objects).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal usage denotes certainty and awareness ("ما علمت بخبرك: ما شعرت به"); metaphorical extension applies to marks, signs, and beacons of guidance (معالم الطريق) — here, the inspired knowledge is a "mark" of the path.
- Root: كشف (kashafa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To remove a covering, unveil, disclose what was hidden.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Unveiling (kashf) in theological terms is the removal of the veil (ghishāwah) from the heart such that the realities of things become directly witnessed, not merely inferred.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: to lift a covering from a thing; metaphorical: the disclosure of inward states and hidden matters — the heart's eye perceives what the outward senses cannot.
- Root: فرس (farasa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To prey upon, devour; farāsah — the lion's pouncing upon its prey.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Discernment (farāsah) is a spiritual perception by which the believer penetrates into the inner states of others, a light cast by God into the heart.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the beast of prey seizing its quarry; metaphorical: the believer's insight seizing the truth of a matter or the hidden state of a person — "اتقوا فراسة المؤمن فإنه ينظر بنور الله."
- Root: حدث (ḥadatha)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To be new, originate after non-existence; muḥaddath — one who is spoken to, inspired with true speech from the unseen.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الحدوث: كون الشيء بعد أن لم يكن" — origination after non-existence; the muḥaddath is one to whom divine inspiration comes as a new, immediate occurrence without acquired means.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: newness of a thing; metaphorical: "كان عمر رضي الله عنه محدثا أي صادق الحدس، كأنما حدث بما ظن" — one whose intuition is so true it is as if he were directly spoken to.
- Sibawayh Rule: Restriction and specification (الحصر والتقييد) — the particle "إنما" and conditional clauses (إن/إذا) restrict predicates to their subjects, as in "إنما العالم الذي يأخذ علمه من ربه" — the true scholar is exclusively the one who takes knowledge from his Lord.
39:22.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'Disciplining the Soul'

39:22.arabic: المعرفة وهو المراد بقوله تعالى فمن يرد الله أن يهديه يشرح صدره للإسلام أفمن شرح الله صدره للإسلام فهو على نور من ربه نعم هذا التجلي وهذا الإيمان له ثلاث مراتب المرتبة الأولى إيمان العوام وهو إيمان التقليد المحض والثانية إيمان المتكلمين وهو ممزوج بنوع استدلال ودرجته قريبة من درجة إيمان العوام والثالثة إيمان العارفين وهو المشاهد بنور اليقين ونبين لك هذه المراتب بمثال وهو أن تصديقك بكون زيد مثلا في الدار له ثلاث درجات الأولى أن يخبرك من جربته بالصدق ولم تعرفه بالكذب ولا اتهمته في القول فإن قلبك يسكن إليه ويطمئن بخبره بمجرد السماع وهذا الإيمان بمجرد التقليد وه
39:22.english: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: "Were it not that the devils hover about the hearts of the children of Adam, they would look upon the kingdom of the heavens." (1) [Hadith of Ibn ʿUmar: "Where is God?" — "In the hearts of His believing servants." I have not found it in this wording. Al-Ṭabarānī narrated from Abū ʿUtbah al-Khawlānī, raised to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: "God has vessels from among the people of the earth, and the vessels of your Lord are the hearts of His righteous servants." In it is Baqiyyah ibn al-Walīd, who is a mudallis (one who conceals), but he explicitly stated hearing (al-taḥdīth) in it.] (2) [Hadith: God said: "My earth and My heavens do not contain Me, but the heart of My believing servant, the soft and tender one, contains Me." I have found no basis for it. In the hadith of Abū ʿUtbah before it, according to al-Ṭabarānī, after his saying "and the vessels of your Lord are the hearts of His righteous servants": "and the most beloved of them to Him are the softest and most tender of them."]
39:22.anchors:
- Root: قلب (q-l-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To turn, overturn, transform from one state to another; the heart as that which is constantly turning and fluctuating between states
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "قلب الشيء: تصريفه وصرفه عن وجه إلى وجه" — the heart is so named because of its constant turning and transformation; the spiritual heart (qalb) is that subtle divine reality (laṭīfah rabbāniyyah) which is the locus of perception and knowledge
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: turning a thing over; Metaphorical: "قلب المعلم الصبيان" — the teacher turns the boys toward their homes; thus the heart is that which turns toward the spiritual world (malakūt) when purified
- Root: ملك (m-l-k)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Possession, dominion, sovereignty; the kingdom
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): الملك: possession and dominion; الملكوت: the spiritual dominion — the unseen world of divine sovereignty
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): الملك: that which is under one's dominion; الملكوت: intensive form indicating the absolute and perfect dominion of God over all things
- Root: ايم (a-y-m)
  * Al-Raghib (Al-Mufradat): "الأيامى: جمع أيم، وهي المرأة التي لا بعل لها" — one without a spouse; extended metaphorically
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas - Haqiqah/Literal): "الحرب مأيمة ميتمة" — war makes women widows and children orphans
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد (Restriction & Focused Predication) — governing the precise scope of statements about what the heart perceives and the degrees of faith

39:74.arabic: الجنة فقال تعالى وقالوا الحمد لله الذي صدقناه وعده {وقال} وآخر دعواهم أن الحمد لله رب العالمين
39:74.english: So then, what we have mentioned concerning the treatment of patience (ṣabr) regarding whispered insinuation (waswās), regarding lust (shahwah), and regarding status (jāh) — annex this to what we have already set down concerning the canons of the paths of spiritual striving (mujāhadah) in the Book of the Discipline of the Soul (Kitāb Riyāḍat al-Nafs) from the Quarter of the Destroyers (rubʿ al-muhlikāt). Adopt it as your manual (dastūr) by which you may come to know the treatment of patience in all the categories which we have previously detailed; for the detailing of individual cases is prolix. Whoever observes gradual progression (tadrīj), patience will elevate him to a state wherein patience without it becomes as arduous as it once was with it — so his affairs become inverted, and what was once beloved to him becomes loathed, and what was once detested to him becomes a sweet, wholesome draught from which he cannot bear to be patient [in abstaining]. This is known only through experience (tajribah) and tasting (dhawq). It has an analogue in customary habits: for a boy is compelled to learning in the beginning by force, and so patience with play and patience with knowledge are both arduous for him — until, when his inner sight is opened and he finds intimacy with knowledge, the matter is inverted, and it becomes arduous for him to be patient in abstaining from knowledge, and to endure play. To this points what is narrated of one of the knowers (ʿārifīn) that he asked al-Shiblī: "Patience — which of its kinds is the most severe?" He said: "Patience in God (fī Allāh)." He said: "No." He said: "Patience for God (li-Allāh)." He said: "No." He said: "Patience with God (maʿa Allāh)." He said: "No." He said: "Then what?" He said: "Patience from God (ʿan Allāh)." At that al-Shiblī cried out a cry by which his soul nearly perished. And it has been said concerning the meaning of His saying, the Exalted: {«اصبروا وصابروا ورابطوا»} "Be patient, and vie in patience, and be steadfast" (Q. 3:200): "Be patient in God, vie in patience by God, and be steadfast with God." And it was said: "Patience for God is sufficiency (ghināʾ); patience by God is endurance (baqāʾ); patience with God is fidelity (wafāʾ); and patience from God is abandonment (jafāʾ)." And it was said concerning its meaning:
39:74.section_title_en: The Revival of the Religious Sciences — Section 972: On Patience (al-Sabr) and the Commencement of Gratitude (al-Shukr)
39:74.anchors:
- Root: صبر (ṣ-b-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of restraint and withholding; al-Khalil notes its application to holding back an animal from fodder, and to enduring constraint.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الصبر: الإمساك في ضيق" — the withholding of the self in constriction; it is a general term whose specific names (shajāʿah, ḥilm, etc.) vary by context, and its opposite is al-jazaʿ (panic/vexation).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): "صبرت على ما أكره. وصبرت عما أحب" — enduring what is disliked and restraining from what is loved. Metaphorical (majāz): "صبرت يمينه" — binding an oath strenuously; "أصبر على الضرب من الأرض" — more enduring than the earth.
- Root: شكر (sh-k-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The root denotes manifestation and fullness; al-Ayn links it to an overflowing udder (shukrā).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الشكر: تصور النعمة وإظهارها" — the perception of a blessing and its display; it is the opposite of kufr (covering/denial). It has three degrees: of the heart (perception), of the tongue (praise), and of the limbs (requital).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "شكرت لله تعالى نعمته" — thanking God for His grace. Metaphorical: "دابة شكور" — a beast that thrives on little fodder, displaying its owner's care through its fatness.
- Root: علم (ʿ-l-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Knowledge as the apprehension of a thing's reality; al-Ayn treats it under the entry of umm (source/origin), indicating that knowledge is the root to which all else is annexed.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "العلم: إدراك الشيء بحقيقته" — apprehension of a thing by its true reality, either by grasping its essence or by affirming/denying a predicate of it.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "ما علمت بخبرك: ما شعرت به" — to be aware/perceive. It is also used for the landmarks (maʿālim) of the road, i.e., traces by which one is guided.
- Root: وقد (w-q-d)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The kindling and blazing of fire; al-Ayn records it under the entry of w-q-d with the sense of fuel and flame.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "وقدت النار تقد وقودا ووقدا" — the fire blazed; al-wuqūd is both the fuel and the resulting flame, as in {«وقودها الناس والحجارة»} (Q. 2:24).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "وقدت النار وقودا ووقدا، واتقدت وتوقدت" — the fire blazed and blazed fiercely. Metaphorical: "قلب وقاد" — a blazing, keen heart; "وقدة الصيف" — the blazing heat of summer.
- Sibawayh Rule: Interposition between the operative word and its object (al-faṣl bayna al-ʿāmil wa al-maʿmūl fīhi) — governing the placement of circumstantial qualifiers (ḥāl) and prepositional phrases to preserve the intended semantic restriction, as in the verse "اصبروا وصابروا ورابطوا" where each imperative carries a distinct operative scope.
39:74.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications, prayers, and their spiritual power, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

40:28.arabic: رضي الله عنه دونه يقول وهو يبكي ويلكم أتقتلون رجلا أن يقول ربي الله ثم انصرفوا عنه وإن ذلك لأشد ما رأيت قريشا بلغت منه (1) وفي رواية أخرى عن عبد الله بن عمرو رضي الله عنهما قال بينا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بفناء الكعبة إذ أقبل عقبة بن أبي معيط فأخذ بمنكب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فلف ثوبه في عنقه فخنقه خنقا شديدا فجاء أبو بكر فأخذ بمنكبه ودفعه عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وقال أتقتلون رجلا أن يقول ربي الله وقد جاءكم بالبينات من ربكم (2) وروي أن معاوية رضي الله عنه حبس العطاء فقام إليه أبو مسلم الخولاني فقال له يا معاوية إنه ليس من كدك ولا م

40:28.arabic: فأخذ بمنكبه ودفعه عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وقال أتقتلون رجلا أن يقول ربي الله وقد جاءكم بالبينات من ربكم (2) وروي أن معاوية رضي الله عنه حبس العطاء فقام إليه أبو مسلم الخولاني فقال له يا معاوية إنه ليس من كدك ولا من كد أبيك ولا من كد أمك قال فغضب معاوية ونزل عن المنبر وقال لهم مكانكم وغاب عن أعينهم ساعة ثم خرج عليهم وقد اغتسل فقال إن أبا مسلم كلمني بكلام أغضبني وإني سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول الغضب من الشيطان والشيطان خلق من النار وإنما تطفأ النار بالماء فإذا غضب أحدكم فليغتسل (3) وإني دخلت فاغتسلت وصدق أبو مسلم أنه ليس من كدي ولا من كد أ

40:43.arabic: حاصل وإن كانا غائبين عنه بحيث يعلم إنه لا يصيبه منهما خير ولا شر في الدنيا ولا في الآخرة فذلك الميل هو حب في الله ولله من غير حظ فإنه إنما يحبه لأن الله يحبه ولأنه مرضي عند الله تعالى ولأنه يحب الله تعالى ولأنه مشغول بعبادة الله تعالى إلا أنه إذا ضعف لم يظهر أثر ولا يظهر به ثواب ولا أجر فإذا قوي حمل على الموالاة والنصرة والذب بالنفس والمال واللسان وتتفاوت الناس فيه بحسب تفاوتهم في حب الله عز وجل ولو كان الحب مقصورا على حظ ينال من المحبوب في الحال أو المآل لما تصور حب الموتى من العلماء والعباد ومن الصحابة والتابعين بل من الأنبياء الم
40:43.english: So from all this it is established that whoever loves a scholar or a worshiper, or loves a person who is eager in knowledge or in goodness, loves him only in God and for God; and he has therein of reward and recompense according to the measure of the strength of his love. This, then, is the explanation of love in God and its degrees. And by this, hatred in God is also made clear — but we shall add further clarification to it."
40:43.section_title_en: On Loving in God and Its Degrees — The Fruits of Love for God
40:43.anchors:
- Root: بكر (Bakara)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The core meaning is "the beginning of the day" (al-bukrah), from which is derived the sense of hastening to the first part of a matter.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): From the temporal sense of "first part," the root conveys the meaning of al-taʿjīl (hastening) — proceeding to a thing at its earliest and most virtuous time.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): "to go out at dawn." Metaphorical (Majaz): "to hasten to prayer at its first time" — as in the hadith, "The people will not cease to be in goodness as long as they hasten (bakkariū) the sunset prayer." Thus, the root signifies seizing the first and most excellent portion of a thing.
- Root: نفس (Nafs)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The self, the soul, the spirit; that which is most precious and dear to a man.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-nafs is the rūḥ (spirit); in God's speech {«And know that God knows what is in your souls»} (Q 2:235), it denotes the inner reality of man. When applied to God, as in {«and He warns you of Himself (nafsahu)»} (Q 3:28), it means His very essence (dhāt) — the expression being a grammatical annexation that implies distinction in wording but not in meaning.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "a precious thing (nafīs)." Metaphorical: "he poured out his soul (nafsahu)" i.e., his blood; "a soul with flowing blood" — that which distinguishes living from dead matter. The "share of the self" (ḥaẓẓ al-nafs) is thus the portion of base, worldly, or selfish desire.
- Root: ميل (Mayl)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Inclination, leaning, deviation from the middle toward one side.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Al-mayl is the deviation from the middle toward one of the two sides." It is used of inclination in affection and support: "I inclined (miltu) to so-and-so" — i.e., I aided him. It is also used of injustice, as in {«Do not incline with total inclination»} (Q 4:129).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "a horse with an inclining neck." Metaphorical: "He inclined away from the truth" (māla ʿan al-ḥaqq); "he sought to win him over" (istamālahu) — i.e., he sought to draw his affection. Thus, mayl al-ṭabʿ is the natural, spontaneous leaning of the heart.
- Root: ضعف (Ḍuʿf)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Weakness, the opposite of strength.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Al-ḍuʿf is the opposite of al-quwwah." It occurs in the soul, the body, and the condition. Al-Khalīl said: al-ḍuʿf (with ḍammah) is weakness of the body; al-ḍaʿf (with fatḥah) is weakness of intellect and opinion.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "In him is weakness (ḍuʿf/ḍaʿf)." Metaphorical: "It is in the folds (aḍʿāf) of the book" — i.e., in its midst and interstices. Thus, the strength or weakness of love is measured by its penetration into the hidden folds of the heart.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction and Specification with Innamā) — The particle innamā restricts the predicate to the subject alone, negating it for all else. This governs the crucial statement: "he loves him only because God loves him" — restricting the cause of love to divine pleasure alone, excluding all selfish shares (ḥuẓūẓ).
40:43.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

41:17.arabic: تعالى به على كافة عباده بعضه بالعقل وبعضه على لسان الرسل ولذلك قال تعالى {وأما ثمود فهديناهم فاستحبوا العمى على الهدى} فأسباب الهدى هي الكتاب والرسل وبصائر العقول وهي مبذولة ولا يمنع منها إلا الحسد والكبر وحب الدنيا والأسباب التي تعمي القلوب وإن كانت لا تعمى الأبصار قال تعالى {فإنها لا تعمى الأبصار ولكن تعمى القلوب التي في الصدور} ومن جملة المعميات الإلف والعادة وحب استصحابهما وعنه العبارة بقوله تعالى {إنا وجدنا آباءنا على أمة} الآية وعن الكبر والحسد العبارة بقوله تعالى {وقالوا لولا نزل هذا القرآن على رجل من القريتين عظيم} وقوله تعالى {أبشرا منا واحدا نتبعه}
41:17.english:
PageV04P107
But if one does not know what constitutes the welfare of his hereafter—so that he even supposes corruption to be welfare—then from where would mere volition benefit him? There is no benefit in volition, power, and causes except after guidance (hidāyah). For this reason, God—exalted is He—said: {«ربنا الذي أعطى كل شيء خلقه ثم هدى»} "Our Lord who gave everything its creation, then guided." And He said—exalted is He—: {«ولولا فضل الله عليكم ورحمته ما زكى منكم أحد أبدا ولكن الله يزكي من يشاء»} "And were it not for God's bounty upon you and His mercy, not one of you would ever be purified; but God purifies whom He wills." And the Prophet—peace be upon him—said: "No one enters Paradise except by the mercy of God—exalted is He—," that is, by His guidance. So it was said: "Not even you, O Messenger of God?" He said: "Not even I" (1). And guidance (hidāyah) has three stations (manāzil):
41:17.section_title_en: The Degrees of Divine Guidance (Hidāyah), Righteous Discernment (Rushd), Straightening (Tasdīd), and Divine Support (Ta'yīd)
41:17.anchors:
- Root: هدي (H-D-Y)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of gentle, gracious direction (dalālah bi-luṭf); the root also yields "gift" (hadiyyah) and the leading beasts of prey (hawādī) that guide the herd.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Guidance is "directional indication with gentleness" (dalālah bi-luṭf), distinct from mere intellectual proof; it is a divine act that may be general (to all) or specific (to the elect), and its withholding is a form of abandonment.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): "He guided him to the path" (hadāhu lil-sabīl). Metaphorical (majāz): "He guided him" meaning "he preceded him" (taqaddamahu), as a leader precedes the caravan; hence guidance is not merely pointing but active leading.
- Root: رشد (R-SH-D)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The state of being rightly directed in one's affairs; integrity of judgment; names Rāshid, Rushayd derive from it.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Rushd is the opposite of ghayy (error/ruin); it is used like hidāyah but with a nuance of practical, executive discernment—knowing the good AND being moved to pursue it. Al-Raghib explicitly distinguishes the rushd of Abraham (given before, as a special gift) from the mere legal competence (rushd) of an orphan.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "A man is rāshid or rashīd" (possessing rightness in conduct). Metaphorical: "He is of sound lineage" (huwa li-rushdah), i.e., legitimate—showing the root's extension to ontological soundness.
- Root: سدد (S-D-D)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To aim correctly, to hit the mark; the arrow that flies straight (sadīd); the opposite of deviation (ighrāḍ).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): (Not in the retrieved scholia, but by extension from the root's usage in the Qur'an, e.g., {wa-saddidū}, "and be straight/aim rightly")—it denotes the divine facilitation of the creature's movements so they align with the intended good.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "He aimed the arrow and it went straight." Metaphorical: "He was granted success in speech and action" (sudda li-l-ṣawāb).
- Root: أيد (A-Y-D)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Strength, support, reinforcement; the "aid" (ayd) of God is His empowering of His servant.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): (By extension from {إذ أيدتك بروح القدس})—divine reinforcement through a holy spirit, i.e., an immaterial power that fortifies both inner perception (baṣīrah) and outer action.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "He strengthened him" (ayyadahu). Metaphorical: Used for the conferral of spiritual power that makes the servant invincible against error.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Gradation and Specification (Tartīb wa-Takhṣīṣ) — The author structures a sequence of terms (hidāyah → rushd → tasdīd → ta'yīd) where each subsequent term is syntactically and semantically superordinate, building a hierarchy of divine acts. The particle "wa-ammā" (وأما) marks a new topic with contrastive focus, and the anaphoric references (هو، وهي) bind the exposition into a single periodic argument.
41:17.topic: Al-Ghazali on purifying the character, moral diseases, and spiritual remedies, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

41:30.arabic: في بالكلية غير الله ومعنى قوله تعالى الذين قالوا ربنا الله ثم استقاموا ولما كان الصراط المستقيم الذي لا يكمل التوحيد إلا بالاستقامة عليه أدق من الشعر وأخذ من السيف مثل الصراط الموصوف في الآخرة فلا ينفك بشر عن ميل عن الاستقامة ولو في أمر يسير إذ لا يخلو عن اتباع الهوى ولو في فعل قليل وذلك قادح في كمال التوحيد بقدر ميله عن الصراط المستقيم فذلك يقتضي لا محالة نقصانا في درجات القرب ومع كل نقصان ناران نار الفراق لذلك الكمال الفائت بالنقصان ونار جهنم كما وصفها القرآن فيكون كل مائل عن الصراط المستقيم معذبا مرتين من وجهين
41:30.english: The fire of Hell is the coldest of fires [in comparison to the fire of separation]. And you should not deny this in the world of the Hereafter, for it has a witnessed parallel in the world of this world. Indeed, one has been seen who was overcome by ecstasy (wajd) and walked upon fire and upon the roots of cane, his feet being cut, yet he did not feel it, due to the extreme dominance of what was in his heart. And you see the angry man, when anger overcomes him in battle, receiving wounds and not feeling them at that moment, because anger is a fire in the heart. The Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, said: {«الغضب قطعة من النار»} "Anger is a piece of fire."
