The burning of the heart (iḥtirāq al-fu'ād) is more severe than the burning of bodies, and the more severe annuls the sensation of the weaker, as you observe. For destruction from fire and the sword is only inasmuch as they separate between two parts that are linked one to the other by the bond of composition (ta'līf) possible in bodies. So that which separates between the heart and its Beloved, to which it is linked by a bond of composition far more firm than the composition of bodies, is more intensely painful—if you are among the people of insight (abṣār) and the people of hearts. And it is not far-fetched that he who has no heart should not perceive the severity of this pain and should deem it trivial in comparison to bodily pain. For a boy, if he were given the choice between the pain of being deprived of a ball and a polo-stick, and the pain of being deprived of the rank of a Sultan, he would not feel the pain of deprivation from the Sultan's rank at all, nor would he count that as a pain. And the enemy in the field with the polo-stick is more beloved to him than a thousand thrones of the Sultan with sitting upon them. Nay, even one overcome by the lust of the belly, if given the choice between porridge (harīsah) and sweets (ḥalwā) and between a beautiful deed by which he conquers enemies and delights friends, he would prefer the porridge and sweets. All of this is due to the absence of the meaning (maʿnā) by whose existence rank becomes beloved, and the presence of the meaning by whose existence food becomes delicious. This is for one whom the attributes of beasts and predators have enslaved, and in whom the attributes of the angels have not appeared—those attributes which are not suited by, nor delight in, anything but proximity to the Lord of the Worlds, and which are pained only by distance and the veil (ḥijāb). And just as taste is only in the tongue and hearing only in the ears, so this attribute is only in the heart. So he who has no heart has no such sense, like he who has no hearing or sight has no pleasure in melodies or the beauty of forms and colors. And not every human has a heart; were it so, the saying of God, Most High, would not be sound: {«إن في ذلك لذكرى لمن كان له قلب»} "Indeed in that is a reminder for whoever has a heart" (Q. 50:37). Thus He made the one who does not heed the Quran devoid of a heart. And by "heart" I do not mean this [organ] which the ribs of the chest encompass. Rather, I mean the secret (sirr) which is of the world of the Command (ʿālam al-amr). The flesh which is of the world of Creation (ʿālam al-khalq) is its Throne (ʿarsh), the chest is its Footstool (kursī), and the rest of the limbs are its domain and kingdom. And to God belongs the Creation and the Command altogether. But that secret, concerning which God, Most High, said: {«قل الروح من أمر ربي»} "Say: The Spirit is of the Command of my Lord" (Q. 17:85), is the commander and the king, because between the world of the Command and the world of Creation there is an ordering, and the world of the Command is commander over the world of Creation. It is the subtle divine reality (al-laṭīfah) which, when it is sound, the rest of the body is sound for its sake. Whoever knows it has known his own self, and whoever knows his own self has known his Lord. At that point, the servant smells the beginnings of the fragrance of the meaning folded under his saying, peace and blessings be upon him: {«إن الله خلق آدم على صورته»} "God created Adam upon His image." He looks with the eye of mercy upon those who adhere to its literal wording and upon those who are obstinate in the path of its interpretation (ta'wīl). And even though His mercy for those adhering to the letter is greater than His mercy for the obstinate interpreters, because mercy is proportional to the affliction, and the affliction of those [literalists] is greater—even if they share in the affliction of being deprived of the reality of the matter—for the Reality (al-ḥaqīqah) is the bounty of God which He gives to whom He wills, and God is the Possessor of Great Bounty. And His Wisdom is singled out for whom He wills: {«ومن يؤت الحكمة فقد أوتي خيرا كثيرا»} "And whoever is given wisdom has been given much good" (Q. 2:269). Let us return to the purpose, for we have drawn out the length and lengthened the breath in a matter that is higher than the sciences of transactions (muʿāmalāt) which we intend in this book. It has become clear that the rank of destruction is only for the ignorant deniers. And the testimony of that from the Book of God and the Sunnah of His Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, is beyond enumeration, so we have not cited it.
41:30.section_title_en: The Ranks of the Hereafter: On the Distribution of Degrees and the States of the Saved, the Punished, and the Victorious
41:30.anchors:
- Root: ح ر ق (ḥ-r-q)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of burning, scorching, and the fire's consumption of its fuel.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The fire of the Hereafter (Nār) is a created reality, but its perception is tied to the spiritual state of the perceiver.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah) for physical burning; metaphorical (Majaz) for the burning of the heart (iḥtirāq al-fu'ād) by overwhelming love or anger.
- Root: ق ل ب (q-l-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To turn, overturn, or transform a thing from one state to another.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The heart (Qalb) is the seat of perception and understanding, distinct from the physical organ.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal for the physical heart; metaphorical for the spiritual subtlety (Laṭīfah) that is the locus of divine knowledge and love.
- Root: ع ل م (ʿ-l-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To know, to perceive a thing by its true nature.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Knowledge (ʿIlm) is the apprehension of a thing's reality, which is the basis for distinguishing the ranks of the believers.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal for acquired knowledge; metaphorical for the "unveiling" (Kashf) knowledge granted to the knowers (ʿĀrifūn).
- Sibawayh Rule: Restriction and Specification (Bāb al-Ḥaṣr wa al-Taqyīd bi-innamā) — Used to distinguish the specific referents of terms like "heart" (Qalb) and "faith" (Īmān), ensuring the precise meaning is not conflated with common usage.
41:30.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

41:30.arabic: وبقوله تعالى إن الذين قالوا ربنا الله ثم استقاموا بل هو معنى قولك لا إله إلا الله أى لا معبود ولا محبوب سواه فكل محبوب فإنه معبود فإن العبد هو المقيد والمعبود هو المقيد به وكل محب فهو مقيد بما يحبه ولذلك قال الله تعالى أرأيت من اتخذ إلهه هواه وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم أبغض إله عبد في الأرض الهوى ولذلك قال عليه السلام من قال لا إله إلا الله مخلصا دخل الجنة ومعنى الإخلاص أن يخلص قلبه لله فلا يبقى فيه شرك لغير الله فيكون الله محبوب قلبه ومعبود قلبه ومقصود قلبه فقط ومن هذا حاله فالدنيا سجنه لأنها مانع
41:30.english: The first: severing the attachments of this world and expelling love of other-than-God from the heart. For the heart is like a vessel: it cannot accommodate vinegar, for example, unless the water is first poured out of it. {God has not made for any man two hearts in his breast} [Al-Ahzab/4]. The perfection of love consists in loving God — mighty and majestic — with one's entire heart. As long as he turns toward other than Him, a corner of his heart is occupied with other than Him. To the extent that he is occupied with other than God, love of God diminishes from it; and to the extent that water remains in the vessel, the vinegar poured into it is diminished.
41:30.section_title_en: The Two Pillars of Love for God: Purification of the Heart and Strength of Knowledge
41:30.anchors:
- Root: ح ب ب (ḥ-b-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root denotes steadfastness and permanence; the heart's fixed attachment to its object.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Love (maḥabbah) is the soul's inclination toward what pleases it; its perfection is exclusive devotion, as in the verse {يحبهم ويحبونه} [Al-Ma'idah/54].
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) usage denotes the heart's clinging; metaphorical (majāz) usage extends to acts of obedience and yearning, culminating in 'ishq (intense passionate love) when it overwhelms the lover.
- Root: خ ل ص (kh-l-ṣ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Purity from admixture; the essence of a thing freed from foreign elements.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Ikhlāṣ is the purification of intention so that no share of creation remains in it; it is the condition for the validity of the shahādah.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: clear, unmixed honey or water; metaphorical: the heart emptied of all rivals so that God alone occupies it.
- Root: ز ه د (z-h-d)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Abstention from what is not essential; renunciation of the superfluous.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Asceticism (zuhd) is the heart's detachment from worldly goods, not merely the abandonment of possessions; it is a preparatory station (maqām) for love.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: disinterest in a thing; metaphorical: the soul's indifference to the ephemeral in favor of the eternal.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Restriction and Specification (Bāb al-Ḥaṣr wa al-Taqyīd bi-innamā) — The particle innamā restricts the predicate to the subject alone, as in "إنما يكتسب العبد حب الله" — affirming love's acquisition solely through specified means, negating all others.
41:30.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Love, Longing, Intimacy and Contentment'

42:27.arabic: وبغى قال الله تعالى ولو بسط الله الرزق لعباده لبغوا في الأرض وقال تعالى كلا إن الإنسان ليطغى أن رآه استغنى وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم إن الله ليحمي عبده المؤمن من الدنيا وهو يحبه كما يحمي أحدكم مريضه (1) وكذلك الزوجة والولد والقريب وكل ما ذكرناه في الأقسام الستة عشر من النعم سوى الإيمان وحسن الخلق فإنها يتصور أن تكون بلاء في حق بعض الناس فتكون أضدادها إذن نعما في حقهم إذ سبق أن المعرفة كمال ونعمة فإنها صفة من صفات الله تعالى ولكن قد تكون على العبد في بعض الأمور بلاء ويكون فقدها نعمة مثاله جهل الإنسان بأجله فإ
42:27.english: You might say: "What you have mentioned concerning graces (niʿam) indicates that for God most high there is in every existing thing a grace — and this suggests that trial (balā') has no existence at all. So what then is the meaning of patience (ṣabr)? And if trial does exist, then what is the meaning of gratitude (shukr) for trial? For some claimants have asserted that we give thanks for trial, let alone for grace. So how is gratitude for trial conceivable? And how does one give thanks for that which one endures with patience? For patience in trial demands pain, while gratitude demands joy, and the two are mutually opposed. And what is the meaning of what you have mentioned — that for God most high there is in everything He has brought into existence a grace upon His servants?"
42:27.section_title_en: On the Reconciliation of Patience and Gratitude in the Face of Trial — Section 1018
42:27.anchors:
- Root: نعم (n-ʿ-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core sense of softness, ease, and well-being; al-Farahidi notes it as a name for the leopard and tiger, indicating inherent vigor in the state of grace.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "النعمة: الحالة الحسنة" — the goodly state; divided into absolute (mutlaqah) and restricted (muqayyadah), the former being felicity in the Hereafter (nearness to God) and faith in this world.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah) usage denotes the actual state of well-being; metaphorical (Majaz) extension applies to any beneficial circumstance, even apparent hardship, when considered relative to the recipient's ultimate good.
- Root: بلي (b-l-w)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Testing, affliction, and wear of the body; the root implies a state of being tried or proven.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Trial (balā') is that which tests one's state; its existence is affirmed alongside grace (niʿmah) as its contrary, for the absence of grace is a trial and the absence of trial is a grace.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal sense is calamity or hardship; metaphorical sense applies to any condition that, while painful in one respect, may be a vehicle for divine benefit in another.
- Root: صبر (ṣ-b-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Restraint and forbearance; al-Farahidi ties it to holding back the self from complaint.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Patience is the withholding of the soul from agitation and complaint; it is only commanded where the trial cannot be repelled by the servant's own effort.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal usage is enduring pain; metaphorical usage extends to steadfastness in obedience and abstention from sin, which are acts of patience toward the soul's base inclinations.
- Root: شكر (sh-k-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Gratitude as acknowledgment of benefit; al-Farahidi links it to fullness, as a full udder (shukrā).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الشكر: تصور النعمة وإظهارها" — gratitude is the conception of the grace and its manifestation; it is threefold: of the heart (perceiving the grace), of the tongue (praising the Benefactor), and of the limbs (rewarding the grace through obedience).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal sense is verbal and inward acknowledgment; metaphorical sense is the "grateful beast" (dābbah shakūr) that thrives on little fodder — so the servant thrives on little trial, seeing in it abundant divine favor.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — Used to delimit the scope of patience and gratitude: patience is restricted to unavoidable pain, while gratitude is focused on the relative good within that pain, preventing the logical contradiction of their simultaneous application.
42:27.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

42:30.arabic: عليهم {وما أصابكم من مصيبة فبما كسبت أيديكم ويعفو عن كثير} فالمصائب في الدنيا بكسب الأوزار فإذا عاقبه الله في الدنيا فالله أكرم من أن يعذبه ثانيا وإن عفا عنه في الدنيا فالله أكرم من أن يعذبه يوم القيامة وعن أنس رضي الله تعالى منه عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال ما تجرع عبد قط جرعتين أحب إلى الله من جرعة غيظ ردها بحلم وجرعة مصيبة يصبر الرجل لها ولا قطرت قطرة أحب إلى الله من قطرة دم أهريقت في سبيل الله أو قطرة دمع في سواد الليل وهو ساجد ولا يراه إلا الله وما خطا عبد خطوتين أحب إلى الله تعالى
42:30.english: And it is related from al-Hasan al-Basri (may God have mercy on him) that a man among the Companions (may God be pleased with them) saw a woman he had known in the pre-Islamic period of ignorance. He spoke to her, then left her, but kept turning his gaze back toward her as he walked, until a wall struck him and left a mark on his face. He came to the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) and informed him of this. The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "When God desires good for a servant, He hastens the punishment of his sin for him in this world."
42:30.section_title_en: On the Divine Wisdom of Trials and the Patience of the Prophets and Righteous
42:30.anchors:
- Root: فتح (f-t-ḥ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To open, to unlock, to grant access; also victory and judgment.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In Quranic usage, opening "the doors of all things" signifies God’s granting expansive worldly means as a test, not necessarily as honor.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) for physical opening; metaphorical (majāz) here for divine facilitation of blessings that lead to heedlessness.
- Sibawayh Rule: Interposition of circumstantial clauses (ḥāl) — the parenthetical "يعني" (meaning) functions as an explanatory aside, permissible between subject and predicate for clarity.
42:30.topic: Al-Ghazali on purifying the character, moral diseases, and spiritual remedies, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

42:53.arabic: عن هذا الترجيح بالملك وهو مجاز محض إذ لا ملك إلا لملك الملوك الذي له ما في السموات والأرض وكيف يكون العبد مالكا وهو في نفسه ليس يملك نفسه بل هو ملك غيره نعم الخلق عباد الله والأرض مائدة الله وقد أذن لهم في الأكل من مائدته بقدر حاجتهم كالملك ينصب مائدة لعبيده فمن أخذ لقمة بيمينه واحتوت عليها براجمه فجاء عبد آخر وأراد انتزاعها
42:53.english: ...to your heart, so that your heart becomes bound by it, and thus your body becomes bound in that direction in a posture of stillness and solemnity when you worship your Lord. Likewise, your actions are divided into those that are noble — such as acts of obedience — and those that are base — such as relieving oneself or spitting. So when you spit toward the direction of the Qiblah, you have indeed wronged it (ẓalamtahā) and shown ingratitude for the blessing (niʿmah) of Allah Most High upon you, by virtue of His placing the Qiblah, through whose placement the perfection of your worship is achieved. Similarly, when you put on your leather sock (khuff) and begin with the left foot, you have wronged (ẓalamta), because the sock is a protection for the foot; the foot has a share in it, and in matters of shares and portions, one ought to begin with the nobler — that is justice (al-ʿadl) and fidelity to wisdom, while its opposite is injustice (ẓulm) and ingratitude for the blessing of the sock and the foot. And this, in the eyes of the knowers (al-ʿārifīn), is a grave offense (kabīrah), even if the jurist (al-faqīh) labels it merely "disliked" (makrūh) — to the extent that one of them (the righteous predecessors) had gathered many measures of wheat and was giving them in charity, and when asked about the reason, he said: "I once put on a sandal and began with the left foot inadvertently, so I wish to expiate that (kufr) through charity." Yes, the jurist is unable to magnify the matter in these affairs, because he is constrained — rather, he is occupied with reforming the common folk (al-ʿawāmm), whose rank approaches the rank of the beasts (al-anʿām), and they are plunged into darknesses (ẓulumāt) far greater and more immense than that such minor darknesses should appear in comparison to them. For it would be ugly to say of one who drank wine and took the cup with his left hand that he transgressed in two respects — one being the drinking, and the other the taking with the left — and of one who sold wine at the time of the call to prayer on Friday, it would be ugly to say he betrayed in two respects — {one} the selling of wine, and the other the selling at the time of the call. And of one who relieved himself in the prayer niche (miḥrāb) of a mosque with his back to the Qiblah, it would be ugly to mention his abandonment of propriety in relieving himself, in that he did not place the Qiblah to his right. For all sins are darknesses, some piled atop others, such that one is eclipsed beside another. A master may punish his slave if he uses his knife without his permission — but if he killed his most beloved son with that very knife, the unauthorized use of the knife would retain no weight or sting in itself. Thus, all the etiquettes (ādāb) that the Prophets and the Saints (al-awliyāʾ) observed, and which we have treated leniently in jurisprudence (fiqh) concerning the common folk, have as their cause this very necessity. Otherwise, all these disliked acts are deviations from justice (al-ʿadl), ingratitude for blessing (kufrān al-niʿmah), and a deficiency in the rank that conveys the servant to the degrees of proximity (darajāt al-qurb) — some of them affect the servant by diminishing proximity and lowering station, while others expel him entirely from the bounds of proximity into the realm of distance (ʿālam al-buʿd), which is the abode of the devils. Likewise, whoever breaks a branch from a tree without an urgent pressing need, and without a sound purpose, has shown ingratitude for the blessing of Allah Most High in the creation of trees and the creation of the hand. As for the hand, it was not created for frivolity, but for obedience and for deeds that aid in obedience. As for the tree, Allah Most High created it, and created for it roots, and conveyed water to it, and placed within it the power of nourishment and growth, so that it might reach the culmination of its development (munthā nashwihi), and His servants might benefit from it. So breaking it before its culmination, not in a manner by which His servants benefit, is a violation of the purpose of wisdom and a deviation from justice. But if he has a sound purpose, then that is permissible for him — for trees and animals have been made a ransom (fidāʾ) for the purposes of human beings, since both are perishable and doomed. Thus, annihilating the baser (al-akhass) for the preservation of the nobler (al-ashraf) for a time is closer to justice than squandering both. And to this points His saying, Most High: {«وَسَخَّرَ لَكُم مَّا فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَمَا فِي الْأَرْضِ جَمِيعًا مِّنْهُ»} — "And He subjected to you whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth — all from Him" [Al-Jāthiyah: 13]. Yes — if he breaks a tree belonging to someone else, he is also a wrongdoer (ẓālim), even if he is in need, because every specific tree does not suffice for the needs of all the servants of Allah; rather, it suffices for a single need. And if one single person were to be singled out for it without preponderance (tarjīḥ) and specification (ikhtiṣāṣ), that would be injustice. So the one entitled to specification is he who obtained the seed, placed it in the ground, conveyed water to it, and undertook its care — he is more worthy of it than others, and his side is thereby established. But if it grew in dead land (mawāt al-arḍ) without any human effort, then one must seek another specification — namely, precedence in taking it (sabq ilā akhdhihi). For the one who precedes has the special property of precedence (khāṣṣiyyat al-sabq). Justice, then, is that he be most worthy of it. And the poor (al-fuqarāʾ) have expressed this preponderance by the term "ownership" (al-milk) — but it is pure metaphor (majāz maḥḍ), for there is no owner except the King of Kings (Malik al-Mulūk), to Whom belongs what is in the heavens and the earth. And how could a servant be an owner, when he himself does not own his own self — rather, he is the property of Another? Yes — the creatures are the servants of Allah, and the earth is the table (māʾidah) of Allah, and He has permitted them to eat from His table to the measure of their need — like a king who sets a table for his slaves. So if one takes a morsel with his right hand, and his fingers close over it, and another slave comes and seeks to snatch it away...
42:53.section_title_en: The Etiquette of the Heart and the Hidden Dimensions of Violating Sacred Directions and Blessings
42:53.anchors:
- Root: ظلم (ẓ-l-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning is "darkness" (ẓulmah) — absence of light; also "to place something in other than its proper place" (waḍʿ al-shayʾ fī ghayr mawḍiʿihi).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Ẓulm is expressed via "darknesses" (ẓulumāt) as ignorance, polytheism, and transgression — the opposite of nūr (light/justice).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): "الظلم ظلمات يوم القيامة" — injustice is darknesses on the Day of Judgment. Metaphorical (majāz): "أرض مظلومة" — land never dug, i.e., violated by first use; "ظلم البعير" — slaughtering an animal without cause (ʿabṭ).
- Root: نعم (n-ʿ-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Niʿmah is a state of well-being; also "softness" and "delicacy."
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Niʿmah is the good condition bestowed; its plural (niʿam) covers both little and much — "وَإِن تَعُدُّوا نِعْمَةَ اللَّهِ لَا تُحْصُوهَا" {And if you count the blessings of Allah, you cannot enumerate them} [Ibrahim: 34].
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "جلت نعمة الله" — the blessing of Allah is immense. Metaphorical: "خفت نعامتهم" — their ostriches departed (i.e., they fled), showing how blessing can be "kicked away" (kufrān al-niʿmah).
- Root: ملك (m-l-k)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Ownership and dominion; the possessor (mālik) who disposes freely.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الملك: هو المتصرف بالأمر والنهي" — the king is one who commands and forbids; true ownership belongs only to Allah, "لَهُ مَا فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَمَا فِي الْأَرْضِ" {To Him belongs what is in the heavens and the earth}.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "ملك يده" — what one's hand owns. Metaphorical: "ملكت فلانة أمرها" — she controlled her own affair; here, human "ownership" (milk) is pure metaphor (majāz maḥḍ), since real dominion is Allah's alone.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The rule governs how qualifying clauses (e.g., "التي بوضعها كمال عبادتك") attach to antecedents, preserving syntactic cohesion even when embedded phrases lengthen the sentence, ensuring no semantic break occurs between the act and its moral consequence.
42:53.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

42:53.arabic: طويل والعمر قصير وإلى الله تصير الأمور وخطب عمر بن عبد العزيز رحمه الله عليه فقال يا أيها الناس إنكم خلقتم لأمر إن كنتم تصدقون به فإنكم حمقى وإن كنتم تكذبون به فإنكم هلكى إنما خلقتم للأبد ولكنكم من دار إلى دار تنقلون عباد الله إنكم في دار لكم فيها من طعامكم غصص ومن شرابكم شرق لا تصفو لكم نعمة تسرون بها إلا بفراق أخرى تكرهون فراقها فاعملوا لما أنتم صائرون إليه وخالدون فيه ثم غلبه البكاء ونزل قال علي كرم الله وجهه في خطبته أوصيكم بتقوى الله والترك للدنيا التاركة لكم وإن كنتم لا تحبون
42:53.english: And indeed there has come the narration from him, from his Lord, Mighty and Glorious, that He said to Moses, peace be upon him: "When you see the rich man approaching, say: 'A sin whose punishment has been hastened.' And when you see the poor man approaching, say: 'Welcome to the badge of the righteous.'" And if you wish, you may follow the possessor of the Spirit and the Word, Jesus son of Mary, peace be upon him — for he used to say: "My condiment is hunger, my badge is fear, my garment is wool, my warmth in winter is the rising places of the sun, my lamp is the moon, my mount is my two feet, and my food and my fruit is what the earth brings forth. I pass the night and I possess nothing, and I rise in the morning and I possess nothing — and there is no one upon the earth richer than I."
42:53.section_title_en: The Revival of the Religious Sciences — Section 737: On the Censure of This World and the Description of Its Perils
42:53.anchors:
- Root: دنو (danuww)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "دنا فهو دانٍ" — proximity, nearness; the world (al-dunyā) is so named because it is nearer and lower, deferred from the Hereafter.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الدنو: القرب بالذات، أو بالحكم" — proximity by essence or by decree; used of place, time, and station. The "nearer" (al-adnā) is contrasted with the greater and the better.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical nearness. Metaphorical: the lower, contemptible station — "أهل الدناءة هم أهل الشناءة" (the people of baseness are the people of abhorrence).
- Root: يوم (yawm)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "اليوم" — a day; also any period of time.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "اليوم يعبر به عن وقت طلوع الشمس إلى غروبها. وقد يعبر به عن مدة من الزمان أي مدة كانت" — the day is the time from sunrise to sunset, or any duration whatsoever. "وذكرهم بأيام الله" — the days of God are His mighty deeds and calamities upon the disbelievers.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the solar day. Metaphorical: "أيام العرب" — their battles and vicissitudes; "أيام الله" — His punitive visitations.
- Root: وقد (waqada)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "وقدت النار تقد وقودا ووقدا" — the fire blazed; al-wuqūd is the fuel.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "وقودها الناس والحجارة" — the fuel of the Fire is men and stones; the one who kindles it for himself (istawqada) is he who seeks its light.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: kindling a fire. Metaphorical: "قلب وقاد" — a blazing, keen heart; "وقد الحصى" — the pebbles became scorching hot (i.e., the intensity of the sun's heat).
- Root: ألك (alaka)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "المألكة: الرسالة، لأنها تؤلك في الفم" — the message (risālah) is called ma'lakah because it is chewed/worked in the mouth.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الملائكة تقع على الواحد والجمع" — angels (malā'ikah) are so named as bearers of messages; "الله يصطفي من الملائكة رسلا" {«الله يصطفي من الملائكة رسلا»} — God chooses messengers from the angels.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: chewing (as a horse chews its bit). Metaphorical: delivering a message — the angel is the one who delivers the divine communication.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — "إنما" restricts the predicate to the subject alone, negating it of all else. Applied in the sermon: "إنما يتزين لي أوليائي بالذل والخوف" — My friends adorn themselves for Me ONLY with humility, fear, and submission — restricting their adornment to these alone, excluding all worldly ornament.
42:53.topic: Al-Ghazali on purifying the character, moral diseases, and spiritual remedies, from 'Condemnation of the World'

43:22.arabic: الدين كقوله عز وجل إنا وجدنا آباءنا على أمة والأمة الحين والزمان كقوله عز وجل إلى أمة معدودة وقوله عز وجل وادكر بعد أمة والأمة القامة يقال فلان حسن الأمة أي القامة وأمة رجل منفرد بدين لا يشركه فيه أحد قال صلى الله عليه وسلم يبعث زيد بن عمرو بن نفيل أمة وحده (1) والأمة يقال هذه أمة زيد أي أم زيد والروح أيضا ورد في القرآن على معان كثيرة فلا نطول بإيرادها وكذلك قد يقع الإبهام في الحروف مثل قوله عز وجل قأثرن به نقعا فوسطن به جمعا فالهاء الأولى كناية عن الحوافر وهي الموريات أي أثرن بالحوافر ن
43:22.english: I say: The Prophet (peace be upon him) was asked about the means of deliverance from these trials, and he said: "The Book of Allah — act by what is in it, for it is that which delivers one from them." The questioner repeated this three times, and he (peace be upon him) said three times: "Learn the Book of Allah, Mighty and Glorious, and act by what is in it, for in it is deliverance."
43:22.section_title_en: The Book of the Etiquette of Recitation — Section 233: On Understanding the Meanings of the Qur'an and the Limits of Interpretation
43:22.anchors:
- Root: ف-ه-م (f-h-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الفهم: هيئة للإنسان بها يتحقق معاني ما يحسن" — comprehension as an inherent faculty by which one ascertains meanings
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الفهم: هيئة للإنسان بها يتحقق معاني ما يحسن... وأفهمته: إذا قلت له حتى تصوره" — comprehension is a cognitive disposition; distinction between understanding (fahm) and making understood (ifhām)
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "تقول: من لم يؤت من سوء الفهم أتى من سوء الإفهام" — literal usage; failure of understanding often stems from failure of communication
- Root: ف-س-ر (f-s-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "وكل شيء يعرف به تفسير الشيء ومعناه، فهو تَفْسِرَتُه" — that by which a thing's meaning is made known
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "التفسير قد يقال فيما يختص بمفردات الألفاظ وغريبها، وفيما يختص بالتأويل" — tafsīr concerns lexical surface; taʾwīl concerns deeper meaning
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "هذا كلام يحتاج إلى فسر وتفسير" — literal: exposition of what is obscure
- Root: و-ج-ل (w-j-l)
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الوجل: استشعار الخوف" — the sensing of fear; used of hearts trembling at divine mention
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "لو واجلت فلانا لوجلته: لغلبته في الوجل" — literal sense of fear; metaphorical extension to overpowering in fear
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — the particle innamā restricts predication, essential for parsing the Prophet's saying "innamā al-aʿmālu bi-l-niyyāt" and analogous restrictive formulations in the ḥadīth cited herein
43:22.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

43:23.arabic: زمانهم حيث قالو إنا وجدنا آباءنا على أمة وإنا على آثارهم مقتدون فعليك إذا اشتغلت بمعاتبة نفسك وحملها على الاجتهاد فاستعصت أن لا تترك معاتبتها وتوبيخها وتعريفها سوء نظرها لنفسها فعساها تنزجر عن طغيانها المرابطة السادسة في توبيخ النفس ومعاتبتها اعلم أن أعدى عدوك نفسك التي بين جنبيك وقد خلقت أمارة بالسوء ميالة إلى الشر فرارة من الخير وأمرت بتزكيتها وتقويمها وقودها بسلاسل القهر إلى عبادة ربها وخالقها ومنعها عن شهواتها وفطامها عن لذاتها فإن أهملتها جمحت وشردت ولم تظفر بها بعد ذلك وإن لازمتها بالتوبيخ والمعاتب
43:23.english: So upon you — if you are among those who stand watch, those who keep vigil over their own souls (al-murāqibīn li-nafsik) — to scrutinize the states of the men and women among the strivers (al-mujtahidīn), that your zeal may be stirred and your eagerness increased. And beware of looking to the people of your own age, for if you obey most of those on earth, they will lead you astray from the path of God {«وإن تطع أكثر من في الأرض يضلوك عن سبيل الله»}.
43:23.section_title_en: Section 1250 — The Sixth Vigil: The Rebuke and Admonishment of the Soul
43:23.anchors:
- Root: نفس (n-f-s)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The self, soul, spirit; that which animates and is the seat of desire and volition.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-nafs denotes the immaterial reality of the human (al-rūḥ), the locus of divine address and moral accountability; its states range from al-ammārah (inciting to evil) to al-lawwāmah (self-reproaching) to al-muṭmaʾinnah (tranquil).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) usage refers to the soul itself; metaphorical (majāz) usage extends to blood (nafs sāʾilah) or the eye of envy — but here it is the true essence of man.
- Root: جهل (j-h-l)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Ignorance as the absence of knowledge; also foolish conduct contrary to right action.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Jahl is threefold: (1) the soul's emptiness of knowledge (the root), (2) belief contrary to reality, (3) acting contrary to what is due — whether with correct or corrupt belief.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: ignorance and folly; metaphorical: the wind "ignoring" the branch (i.e., agitating it violently) — here, the soul's self-deception is exposed as true ignorance.
- Root: اهل (a-h-l)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Those united by kinship, religion, or dwelling; one who is worthy or fit for something.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Ahl al-rajul: those joined by lineage, faith, or craft; Ahl al-Bayt in the Qurʾān {«إنما يريد الله ليذهب عنكم الرجس أهل البيت»} — and by extension, what one merits.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: family or inhabitants; metaphorical: "he is ahl (worthy) for such-and-such" — i.e., deserving of it, as in the supplication "tawallā min amrī mā anta ahluh" (undertake my affair as befits Thee).
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — "إنما" restricts the predicate exclusively to the subject, as in the soul's whisper "إنما تيسر الخير في ذلك الزمان لكثرة الأعوان" — a false restriction used to delude, and the divine reply "وذكر فإن الذكرى تنفع المؤمنين" — where the command is unrestricted.
43:23.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Monitoring and Accounting'

43:23.arabic: الدين كقوله عز وجل إنا وجدنا آباءنا على أمة والأمة الحين والزمان كقوله عز وجل إلى أمة معدودة وقوله عز وجل وادكر بعد أمة والأمة القامة يقال فلان حسن الأمة أي القامة وأمة رجل منفرد بدين لا يشركه فيه أحد قال صلى الله عليه وسلم يبعث زيد بن عمرو بن نفيل أمة وحده (1) والأمة يقال هذه أمة زيد أي أم زيد والروح أيضا ورد في القرآن على معان كثيرة فلا نطول بإيرادها وكذلك قد يقع الإبهام في الحروف مثل قوله عز وجل قأثرن به نقعا فوسطن به جمعا فالهاء الأولى كناية عن الحوافر وهي الموريات أي أثرن بالحوافر ن
43:23.english: I say: The Prophet (peace be upon him) was asked about the means of deliverance from these trials, and he said: "The Book of Allah — act by what is in it, for it is that which delivers one from them." The questioner repeated this three times, and he (peace be upon him) said three times: "Learn the Book of Allah, Mighty and Glorious, and act by what is in it, for in it is deliverance."
43:23.section_title_en: The Book of the Etiquette of Recitation — Section 233: On Understanding the Meanings of the Qur'an and the Limits of Interpretation
43:23.anchors:
- Root: ف-ه-م (f-h-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الفهم: هيئة للإنسان بها يتحقق معاني ما يحسن" — comprehension as an inherent faculty by which one ascertains meanings
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الفهم: هيئة للإنسان بها يتحقق معاني ما يحسن... وأفهمته: إذا قلت له حتى تصوره" — comprehension is a cognitive disposition; distinction between understanding (fahm) and making understood (ifhām)
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "تقول: من لم يؤت من سوء الفهم أتى من سوء الإفهام" — literal usage; failure of understanding often stems from failure of communication
- Root: ف-س-ر (f-s-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "وكل شيء يعرف به تفسير الشيء ومعناه، فهو تَفْسِرَتُه" — that by which a thing's meaning is made known
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "التفسير قد يقال فيما يختص بمفردات الألفاظ وغريبها، وفيما يختص بالتأويل" — tafsīr concerns lexical surface; taʾwīl concerns deeper meaning
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "هذا كلام يحتاج إلى فسر وتفسير" — literal: exposition of what is obscure
- Root: و-ج-ل (w-j-l)
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الوجل: استشعار الخوف" — the sensing of fear; used of hearts trembling at divine mention
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "لو واجلت فلانا لوجلته: لغلبته في الوجل" — literal sense of fear; metaphorical extension to overpowering in fear
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — the particle innamā restricts predication, essential for parsing the Prophet's saying "innamā al-aʿmālu bi-l-niyyāt" and analogous restrictive formulations in the ḥadīth cited herein
43:23.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

43:31.arabic: وجدنا آباءنا على أمة} الآية وعن الكبر والحسد العبارة بقوله تعالى {وقالوا لولا نزل هذا القرآن على رجل من القريتين عظيم} وقوله تعالى {أبشرا منا واحدا نتبعه} فهذه المعميات هي التي منعت الاهتداء والهداية الثانية وراء هذه الهداية العامة وهي التي يمد الله تعالى بها العبد حالا بعد حال وهي ثمرة المجاهدة حيث قال تعالى {والذين جاهدوا فينا لنهدينهم سبلنا} وهو المراد بقوله تعالى {والذين اهتدوا زادهم هدى} والهداية الثالثة وراء الثانية وهو النور الذي يشرق في عالم النبوة والولاية بعد كمال المجاهدة فيهتدي بها إلا ما لا يهتدى إليه بالعقل الذي يحصل به التكليف وإمكان تعلم ال
43:31.english:
PageV04P107
But if one does not know what constitutes the welfare of his hereafter—so that he even supposes corruption to be welfare—then from where would mere volition benefit him? There is no benefit in volition, power, and causes except after guidance (hidāyah). For this reason, God—exalted is He—said: {«ربنا الذي أعطى كل شيء خلقه ثم هدى»} "Our Lord who gave everything its creation, then guided." And He said—exalted is He—: {«ولولا فضل الله عليكم ورحمته ما زكى منكم أحد أبدا ولكن الله يزكي من يشاء»} "And were it not for God's bounty upon you and His mercy, not one of you would ever be purified; but God purifies whom He wills." And the Prophet—peace be upon him—said: "No one enters Paradise except by the mercy of God—exalted is He—," that is, by His guidance. So it was said: "Not even you, O Messenger of God?" He said: "Not even I" (1). And guidance (hidāyah) has three stations (manāzil):
43:31.section_title_en: The Degrees of Divine Guidance (Hidāyah), Righteous Discernment (Rushd), Straightening (Tasdīd), and Divine Support (Ta'yīd)
43:31.anchors:
- Root: هدي (H-D-Y)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of gentle, gracious direction (dalālah bi-luṭf); the root also yields "gift" (hadiyyah) and the leading beasts of prey (hawādī) that guide the herd.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Guidance is "directional indication with gentleness" (dalālah bi-luṭf), distinct from mere intellectual proof; it is a divine act that may be general (to all) or specific (to the elect), and its withholding is a form of abandonment.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): "He guided him to the path" (hadāhu lil-sabīl). Metaphorical (majāz): "He guided him" meaning "he preceded him" (taqaddamahu), as a leader precedes the caravan; hence guidance is not merely pointing but active leading.
- Root: رشد (R-SH-D)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The state of being rightly directed in one's affairs; integrity of judgment; names Rāshid, Rushayd derive from it.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Rushd is the opposite of ghayy (error/ruin); it is used like hidāyah but with a nuance of practical, executive discernment—knowing the good AND being moved to pursue it. Al-Raghib explicitly distinguishes the rushd of Abraham (given before, as a special gift) from the mere legal competence (rushd) of an orphan.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "A man is rāshid or rashīd" (possessing rightness in conduct). Metaphorical: "He is of sound lineage" (huwa li-rushdah), i.e., legitimate—showing the root's extension to ontological soundness.
- Root: سدد (S-D-D)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To aim correctly, to hit the mark; the arrow that flies straight (sadīd); the opposite of deviation (ighrāḍ).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): (Not in the retrieved scholia, but by extension from the root's usage in the Qur'an, e.g., {wa-saddidū}, "and be straight/aim rightly")—it denotes the divine facilitation of the creature's movements so they align with the intended good.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "He aimed the arrow and it went straight." Metaphorical: "He was granted success in speech and action" (sudda li-l-ṣawāb).
- Root: أيد (A-Y-D)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Strength, support, reinforcement; the "aid" (ayd) of God is His empowering of His servant.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): (By extension from {إذ أيدتك بروح القدس})—divine reinforcement through a holy spirit, i.e., an immaterial power that fortifies both inner perception (baṣīrah) and outer action.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "He strengthened him" (ayyadahu). Metaphorical: Used for the conferral of spiritual power that makes the servant invincible against error.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Gradation and Specification (Tartīb wa-Takhṣīṣ) — The author structures a sequence of terms (hidāyah → rushd → tasdīd → ta'yīd) where each subsequent term is syntactically and semantically superordinate, building a hierarchy of divine acts. The particle "wa-ammā" (وأما) marks a new topic with contrastive focus, and the anaphoric references (هو، وهي) bind the exposition into a single periodic argument.
43:31.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

43:31.arabic: وكيف نطأطيء رءوسنا فقالوا لولا نزل هذا القرآن على رجل من القريتين عظيم (1) أي كان لا يثقل علينا أن نتواضع له ونتبعه إذا كان عظيما وقال تعالى يصف قول قريش أهؤلاء من الله عليهم من بيننا كالاستحقار لهم والأنفة منهم السبب الرابع التعجب كما أخبر الله تعالى عن الأمم السالفة إذ قالوا ما أنتم إلا بشر مثلنا وقالوا أنؤمن لبشرين مثلنا ولئن أطعتم بشرا مثلكم إنكم إذا لخاسرون فتعجبوا من أن يفوز برتبة الرسالة والوحي والقرب من الله تعالى بشر مثلهم فحسدوهم وأحبوا زوال النبوة عنهم جزعا أن يفضل عليهم من هو مثلهم في الخلقة لا عن قص
43:31.english: I say: God is Knower of what is in the breasts. {«إِنْ تَمْسَسْكُمْ حَسَنَةٌ تَسُؤْهُمْ»} — "If good touches you, it grieves them" {«وَدُّوا مَا عَنِتُّمْ قَدْ بَدَتِ الْبَغْضَاءُ مِنْ أَفْوَاهِهِمْ وَمَا تُخْفِي صُدُورُهُمْ أَكْبَرُ»} — "They wish for your hardship; hatred has already appeared from their mouths, and what their breasts conceal is greater." And envy (ḥasad), arising from hatred, may lead to contention, mutual fighting, and the spending of one's entire life in removing another's blessing through stratagems, slander, the tearing of veils, and whatever runs in that course.
43:31.section_title_en: The Revival of the Religious Sciences — Book on the Rebuke of the Self: The Seven Causes of Envy (Section 722)
43:31.anchors:
- Root: سبب (sabab)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The rope by which one climbs; every means by which one reaches a thing.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Every means by which one arrives at something is called a sabab" — thus the causes enumerated here are the psychological "ropes" by which envy ascends in the soul.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: a physical cord. Metaphorical: any linkage or occasion — here, the inward occasions (asbāb) that give rise to ḥasad.
- Root: بغض (bughḍ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Hatred, aversion of the heart.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The opposite of love (maḥabbah); a disposition of the heart toward another's harm.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: inner aversion. Metaphorical: its "appearance from the mouths" (Quranic) as outward speech betraying the concealed hatred.
- Root: كبر (kibr)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Greatness; pride; disdain.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Al-kabīr and al-ṣaghīr are relative terms" — pride is the claim to greatness relative to another, deeming oneself above him.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: bigness in stature or age. Metaphorical: "takabbara 'alayhi" — to deem oneself greater than another and refuse submission to him.
- Root: قصد (qaṣd)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Straightness of path; intending a goal.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Al-qaṣd: istiqāmat al-ṭarīq" — the straight road; also moderation between extremes.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: to head toward a place. Metaphorical: "maqāṣid" — the aims and objectives toward which one directs oneself; here, the worldly goals whose pursuit breeds rivalry and envy.
- Root: نزل (nazal)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To descend from a height; to alight.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Al-nuzūl fī al-aṣl huwa inḥiṭāṭ min 'uluww" — descent from above; the sending down of revelation.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: descending from a high place. Metaphorical: "anzala Allāhu al-kitāb" — God's sending down of the Quran; and "mā unzila" — what was revealed, as in the Quranic citation regarding the Qurashites' objection to revelation upon a mere human.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Causal Coordination (al-'aṭf al-sababī) — The enumeration of the seven causes proceeds by coordinated clauses (fa-... thumma ...), each introduced as an independent proposition linked by causation (sabab), requiring the translator to preserve the logical sequence of psychological motivations without collapsing them into one another.
43:31.topic: Al-Ghazali on purifying the character, moral diseases, and spiritual remedies, from 'Condemnation of Envy'

43:36.arabic: يدرك بقي مع المحرومين في أسفل السافلين ومن يعش عن ذكر الرحمن نقيض له شيطانا فهو له قرين بيان الدواء الذي ينفي مرض الحسد عن القلب اعلم أن الحسد من الأمراض العظيمة للقلوب ولا تداوى أمراض القلوب إلا بالعلم والعمل والعلم النافع لمرض الحسد هو أن تعرف تحقيقا أن الحسد ضرر عليك في الدنيا والدين وأنه لا ضرر فيه على المحسود في الدنيا والدين بل ينتفع به فيهما ومهما عرفت هذا عن بصيرة ولم تكن عدو نفسك وصديق عدوك فارقت الحسد لا محالة أما كونه ضررا عليك في الدين فهو أنك بالحسد سخطت قضاء الله تعالى وكرهت نعمته التي قسمها بين عباده وعدله الذي
43:36.english: As for its being a harm upon the envied one in his religion and his worldly life — it is clear that the blessing does not depart from him through your envy. Rather, whatever Allah — exalted be He — has decreed of prosperity and blessing, it must endure until an appointed term unknown to us, which Allah — glorified be He — has measured. There is no stratagem to repel it, for everything with Him is by measure (miqdār), and for every term there is a book (kitāb). {«لكل أجل كتاب»} "For every term there is a decree."
43:36.section_title_en: The Remedy That Expels the Disease of Envy from the Heart — Section 725
43:36.anchors:
- Root: حسد (ḥ-s-d)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning — wishing for removal of a blessing from its possessor; the root also carries the sense of "grudging malice" that consumes the envier himself.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الحسد: تمني زوال نعمة من مستحق لها" — Envy is the wish for the removal of a blessing from one who deserves it, sometimes accompanied by striving to effect its removal. The believer envies not but rather admires (ghibṭah); the hypocrite envies.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) — envy is directed at another's blessing; metaphorically (majāz), envy "eats the body" as fire eats wood, indicating its self-destructive spiritual physiology.
- Root: قلب (q-l-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The heart as that which is ever-turning, overturning, and fluctuating between states.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "قلب الشيء: تصريفه وصرفه عن وجه إلى وجه" — To turn a thing from one face to another; the heart's diseases are its deviations from its original sound disposition (fiṭrah).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — turning a thing over; metaphorical — "رجل قلب" (a man who turns matters over) i.e., one who examines affairs with penetrating insight, as the physician of hearts must do.
- Root: نعم (n-ʿ-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Blessing, well-being, graciousness; the state of being in a condition of good.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "النعمة: الحالة الحسنة" — Blessing is the good state; it is a genus term applying to both little and much. Divine blessings are distributed by divine decree (qadar), and envy is resentment against that distribution.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — the act of bestowing; metaphorical — "خفت نعامتهم" (their ostriches departed) i.e., their blessings vanished, illustrating that blessings flee from the envier while remaining with the envied.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The periodic sentence structure here employs extended conditional and causal chains (law-lā, fa-in, fa-innaka) where the apodosis is delayed by embedded justificatory clauses, requiring the translator to preserve the logical subordination without collapsing the rhetorical tension.
43:36.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

45:13.arabic: وسخر لكم ما في السموات وما في الأرض جميعا منه نعم إذا كسر ذلك من ملك غيره فهو ظالم أيضا وإن كان محتاجا لأن كل شجرة بعينها لاتفى بحاجات عباد الله كلهم بل تفي بحاجة واحدة ولو خصص واحد بها من غير رجحان واختصاص كان ظلما فصاحب الاختصاص هو الذي حصل البذر ووضعه في الأرض وساق إليه الماء وقام بالتعهد فهو أولى به من غيره فيرجع جانبه بذلك فإن نبت ذلك في موات الأرض لا بسعي آدمي اختص بمغرسه أو بغرسه فلا بد من طلب اختصاص آخر وهو السبق إلى أخذه فللسابقخاصية السبق فالعدل هو أن يكون أولى به وعبر الفقراء عن هذا ا
45:13.english: ...to your heart, so that your heart becomes bound by it, and thus your body becomes bound in that direction in a posture of stillness and solemnity when you worship your Lord. Likewise, your actions are divided into those that are noble — such as acts of obedience — and those that are base — such as relieving oneself or spitting. So when you spit toward the direction of the Qiblah, you have indeed wronged it (ẓalamtahā) and shown ingratitude for the blessing (niʿmah) of Allah Most High upon you, by virtue of His placing the Qiblah, through whose placement the perfection of your worship is achieved. Similarly, when you put on your leather sock (khuff) and begin with the left foot, you have wronged (ẓalamta), because the sock is a protection for the foot; the foot has a share in it, and in matters of shares and portions, one ought to begin with the nobler — that is justice (al-ʿadl) and fidelity to wisdom, while its opposite is injustice (ẓulm) and ingratitude for the blessing of the sock and the foot. And this, in the eyes of the knowers (al-ʿārifīn), is a grave offense (kabīrah), even if the jurist (al-faqīh) labels it merely "disliked" (makrūh) — to the extent that one of them (the righteous predecessors) had gathered many measures of wheat and was giving them in charity, and when asked about the reason, he said: "I once put on a sandal and began with the left foot inadvertently, so I wish to expiate that (kufr) through charity." Yes, the jurist is unable to magnify the matter in these affairs, because he is constrained — rather, he is occupied with reforming the common folk (al-ʿawāmm), whose rank approaches the rank of the beasts (al-anʿām), and they are plunged into darknesses (ẓulumāt) far greater and more immense than that such minor darknesses should appear in comparison to them. For it would be ugly to say of one who drank wine and took the cup with his left hand that he transgressed in two respects — one being the drinking, and the other the taking with the left — and of one who sold wine at the time of the call to prayer on Friday, it would be ugly to say he betrayed in two respects — {one} the selling of wine, and the other the selling at the time of the call. And of one who relieved himself in the prayer niche (miḥrāb) of a mosque with his back to the Qiblah, it would be ugly to mention his abandonment of propriety in relieving himself, in that he did not place the Qiblah to his right. For all sins are darknesses, some piled atop others, such that one is eclipsed beside another. A master may punish his slave if he uses his knife without his permission — but if he killed his most beloved son with that very knife, the unauthorized use of the knife would retain no weight or sting in itself. Thus, all the etiquettes (ādāb) that the Prophets and the Saints (al-awliyāʾ) observed, and which we have treated leniently in jurisprudence (fiqh) concerning the common folk, have as their cause this very necessity. Otherwise, all these disliked acts are deviations from justice (al-ʿadl), ingratitude for blessing (kufrān al-niʿmah), and a deficiency in the rank that conveys the servant to the degrees of proximity (darajāt al-qurb) — some of them affect the servant by diminishing proximity and lowering station, while others expel him entirely from the bounds of proximity into the realm of distance (ʿālam al-buʿd), which is the abode of the devils. Likewise, whoever breaks a branch from a tree without an urgent pressing need, and without a sound purpose, has shown ingratitude for the blessing of Allah Most High in the creation of trees and the creation of the hand. As for the hand, it was not created for frivolity, but for obedience and for deeds that aid in obedience. As for the tree, Allah Most High created it, and created for it roots, and conveyed water to it, and placed within it the power of nourishment and growth, so that it might reach the culmination of its development (munthā nashwihi), and His servants might benefit from it. So breaking it before its culmination, not in a manner by which His servants benefit, is a violation of the purpose of wisdom and a deviation from justice. But if he has a sound purpose, then that is permissible for him — for trees and animals have been made a ransom (fidāʾ) for the purposes of human beings, since both are perishable and doomed. Thus, annihilating the baser (al-akhass) for the preservation of the nobler (al-ashraf) for a time is closer to justice than squandering both. And to this points His saying, Most High: {«وَسَخَّرَ لَكُم مَّا فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَمَا فِي الْأَرْضِ جَمِيعًا مِّنْهُ»} — "And He subjected to you whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth — all from Him" [Al-Jāthiyah: 13]. Yes — if he breaks a tree belonging to someone else, he is also a wrongdoer (ẓālim), even if he is in need, because every specific tree does not suffice for the needs of all the servants of Allah; rather, it suffices for a single need. And if one single person were to be singled out for it without preponderance (tarjīḥ) and specification (ikhtiṣāṣ), that would be injustice. So the one entitled to specification is he who obtained the seed, placed it in the ground, conveyed water to it, and undertook its care — he is more worthy of it than others, and his side is thereby established. But if it grew in dead land (mawāt al-arḍ) without any human effort, then one must seek another specification — namely, precedence in taking it (sabq ilā akhdhihi). For the one who precedes has the special property of precedence (khāṣṣiyyat al-sabq). Justice, then, is that he be most worthy of it. And the poor (al-fuqarāʾ) have expressed this preponderance by the term "ownership" (al-milk) — but it is pure metaphor (majāz maḥḍ), for there is no owner except the King of Kings (Malik al-Mulūk), to Whom belongs what is in the heavens and the earth. And how could a servant be an owner, when he himself does not own his own self — rather, he is the property of Another? Yes — the creatures are the servants of Allah, and the earth is the table (māʾidah) of Allah, and He has permitted them to eat from His table to the measure of their need — like a king who sets a table for his slaves. So if one takes a morsel with his right hand, and his fingers close over it, and another slave comes and seeks to snatch it away...
45:13.section_title_en: The Etiquette of the Heart and the Hidden Dimensions of Violating Sacred Directions and Blessings
45:13.anchors:
- Root: ظلم (ẓ-l-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning is "darkness" (ẓulmah) — absence of light; also "to place something in other than its proper place" (waḍʿ al-shayʾ fī ghayr mawḍiʿihi).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Ẓulm is expressed via "darknesses" (ẓulumāt) as ignorance, polytheism, and transgression — the opposite of nūr (light/justice).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): "الظلم ظلمات يوم القيامة" — injustice is darknesses on the Day of Judgment. Metaphorical (majāz): "أرض مظلومة" — land never dug, i.e., violated by first use; "ظلم البعير" — slaughtering an animal without cause (ʿabṭ).
- Root: نعم (n-ʿ-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Niʿmah is a state of well-being; also "softness" and "delicacy."
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Niʿmah is the good condition bestowed; its plural (niʿam) covers both little and much — "وَإِن تَعُدُّوا نِعْمَةَ اللَّهِ لَا تُحْصُوهَا" {And if you count the blessings of Allah, you cannot enumerate them} [Ibrahim: 34].
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "جلت نعمة الله" — the blessing of Allah is immense. Metaphorical: "خفت نعامتهم" — their ostriches departed (i.e., they fled), showing how blessing can be "kicked away" (kufrān al-niʿmah).
- Root: ملك (m-l-k)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Ownership and dominion; the possessor (mālik) who disposes freely.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الملك: هو المتصرف بالأمر والنهي" — the king is one who commands and forbids; true ownership belongs only to Allah, "لَهُ مَا فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَمَا فِي الْأَرْضِ" {To Him belongs what is in the heavens and the earth}.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "ملك يده" — what one's hand owns. Metaphorical: "ملكت فلانة أمرها" — she controlled her own affair; here, human "ownership" (milk) is pure metaphor (majāz maḥḍ), since real dominion is Allah's alone.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The rule governs how qualifying clauses (e.g., "التي بوضعها كمال عبادتك") attach to antecedents, preserving syntactic cohesion even when embedded phrases lengthen the sentence, ensuring no semantic break occurs between the act and its moral consequence.
45:13.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications, prayers, and their spiritual power, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

46:13.arabic: في بالكلية غير الله ومعنى قوله تعالى الذين قالوا ربنا الله ثم استقاموا ولما كان الصراط المستقيم الذي لا يكمل التوحيد إلا بالاستقامة عليه أدق من الشعر وأخذ من السيف مثل الصراط الموصوف في الآخرة فلا ينفك بشر عن ميل عن الاستقامة ولو في أمر يسير إذ لا يخلو عن اتباع الهوى ولو في فعل قليل وذلك قادح في كمال التوحيد بقدر ميله عن الصراط المستقيم فذلك يقتضي لا محالة نقصانا في درجات القرب ومع كل نقصان ناران نار الفراق لذلك الكمال الفائت بالنقصان ونار جهنم كما وصفها القرآن فيكون كل مائل عن الصراط المستقيم معذبا مرتين من وجهين
46:13.english: The fire of Hell is the coldest of fires [in comparison to the fire of separation]. And you should not deny this in the world of the Hereafter, for it has a witnessed parallel in the world of this world. Indeed, one has been seen who was overcome by ecstasy (wajd) and walked upon fire and upon the roots of cane, his feet being cut, yet he did not feel it, due to the extreme dominance of what was in his heart. And you see the angry man, when anger overcomes him in battle, receiving wounds and not feeling them at that moment, because anger is a fire in the heart. The Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, said: {«الغضب قطعة من النار»} "Anger is a piece of fire." The burning of the heart (iḥtirāq al-fu'ād) is more severe than the burning of bodies, and the more severe annuls the sensation of the weaker, as you observe. For destruction from fire and the sword is only inasmuch as they separate between two parts that are linked one to the other by the bond of composition (ta'līf) possible in bodies. So that which separates between the heart and its Beloved, to which it is linked by a bond of composition far more firm than the composition of bodies, is more intensely painful—if you are among the people of insight (abṣār) and the people of hearts. And it is not far-fetched that he who has no heart should not perceive the severity of this pain and should deem it trivial in comparison to bodily pain. For a boy, if he were given the choice between the pain of being deprived of a ball and a polo-stick, and the pain of being deprived of the rank of a Sultan, he would not feel the pain of deprivation from the Sultan's rank at all, nor would he count that as a pain. And the enemy in the field with the polo-stick is more beloved to him than a thousand thrones of the Sultan with sitting upon them. Nay, even one overcome by the lust of the belly, if given the choice between porridge (harīsah) and sweets (ḥalwā) and between a beautiful deed by which he conquers enemies and delights friends, he would prefer the porridge and sweets. All of this is due to the absence of the meaning (maʿnā) by whose existence rank becomes beloved, and the presence of the meaning by whose existence food becomes delicious. This is for one whom the attributes of beasts and predators have enslaved, and in whom the attributes of the angels have not appeared—those attributes which are not suited by, nor delight in, anything but proximity to the Lord of the Worlds, and which are pained only by distance and the veil (ḥijāb). And just as taste is only in the tongue and hearing only in the ears, so this attribute is only in the heart. So he who has no heart has no such sense, like he who has no hearing or sight has no pleasure in melodies or the beauty of forms and colors. And not every human has a heart; were it so, the saying of God, Most High, would not be sound: {«إن في ذلك لذكرى لمن كان له قلب»} "Indeed in that is a reminder for whoever has a heart" (Q. 50:37). Thus He made the one who does not heed the Quran devoid of a heart. And by "heart" I do not mean this [organ] which the ribs of the chest encompass. Rather, I mean the secret (sirr) which is of the world of the Command (ʿālam al-amr). The flesh which is of the world of Creation (ʿālam al-khalq) is its Throne (ʿarsh), the chest is its Footstool (kursī), and the rest of the limbs are its domain and kingdom. And to God belongs the Creation and the Command altogether. But that secret, concerning which God, Most High, said: {«قل الروح من أمر ربي»} "Say: The Spirit is of the Command of my Lord" (Q. 17:85), is the commander and the king, because between the world of the Command and the world of Creation there is an ordering, and the world of the Command is commander over the world of Creation. It is the subtle divine reality (al-laṭīfah) which, when it is sound, the rest of the body is sound for its sake. Whoever knows it has known his own self, and whoever knows his own self has known his Lord. At that point, the servant smells the beginnings of the fragrance of the meaning folded under his saying, peace and blessings be upon him: {«إن الله خلق آدم على صورته»} "God created Adam upon His image." He looks with the eye of mercy upon those who adhere to its literal wording and upon those who are obstinate in the path of its interpretation (ta'wīl). And even though His mercy for those adhering to the letter is greater than His mercy for the obstinate interpreters, because mercy is proportional to the affliction, and the affliction of those [literalists] is greater—even if they share in the affliction of being deprived of the reality of the matter—for the Reality (al-ḥaqīqah) is the bounty of God which He gives to whom He wills, and God is the Possessor of Great Bounty. And His Wisdom is singled out for whom He wills: {«ومن يؤت الحكمة فقد أوتي خيرا كثيرا»} "And whoever is given wisdom has been given much good" (Q. 2:269). Let us return to the purpose, for we have drawn out the length and lengthened the breath in a matter that is higher than the sciences of transactions (muʿāmalāt) which we intend in this book. It has become clear that the rank of destruction is only for the ignorant deniers. And the testimony of that from the Book of God and the Sunnah of His Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, is beyond enumeration, so we have not cited it.
46:13.section_title_en: The Ranks of the Hereafter: On the Distribution of Degrees and the States of the Saved, the Punished, and the Victorious
46:13.anchors:
- Root: ح ر ق (ḥ-r-q)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of burning, scorching, and the fire's consumption of its fuel.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The fire of the Hereafter (Nār) is a created reality, but its perception is tied to the spiritual state of the perceiver.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah) for physical burning; metaphorical (Majaz) for the burning of the heart (iḥtirāq al-fu'ād) by overwhelming love or anger.
- Root: ق ل ب (q-l-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To turn, overturn, or transform a thing from one state to another.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The heart (Qalb) is the seat of perception and understanding, distinct from the physical organ.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal for the physical heart; metaphorical for the spiritual subtlety (Laṭīfah) that is the locus of divine knowledge and love.
- Root: ع ل م (ʿ-l-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To know, to perceive a thing by its true nature.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Knowledge (ʿIlm) is the apprehension of a thing's reality, which is the basis for distinguishing the ranks of the believers.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal for acquired knowledge; metaphorical for the "unveiling" (Kashf) knowledge granted to the knowers (ʿĀrifūn).
- Sibawayh Rule: Restriction and Specification (Bāb al-Ḥaṣr wa al-Taqyīd bi-innamā) — Used to distinguish the specific referents of terms like "heart" (Qalb) and "faith" (Īmān), ensuring the precise meaning is not conflated with common usage.
46:13.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

46:13.arabic: وبقوله تعالى إن الذين قالوا ربنا الله ثم استقاموا بل هو معنى قولك لا إله إلا الله أى لا معبود ولا محبوب سواه فكل محبوب فإنه معبود فإن العبد هو المقيد والمعبود هو المقيد به وكل محب فهو مقيد بما يحبه ولذلك قال الله تعالى أرأيت من اتخذ إلهه هواه وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم أبغض إله عبد في الأرض الهوى ولذلك قال عليه السلام من قال لا إله إلا الله مخلصا دخل الجنة ومعنى الإخلاص أن يخلص قلبه لله فلا يبقى فيه شرك لغير الله فيكون الله محبوب قلبه ومعبود قلبه ومقصود قلبه فقط ومن هذا حاله فالدنيا سجنه لأنها مانع
46:13.english: The first: severing the attachments of this world and expelling love of other-than-God from the heart. For the heart is like a vessel: it cannot accommodate vinegar, for example, unless the water is first poured out of it. {God has not made for any man two hearts in his breast} [Al-Ahzab/4]. The perfection of love consists in loving God — mighty and majestic — with one's entire heart. As long as he turns toward other than Him, a corner of his heart is occupied with other than Him. To the extent that he is occupied with other than God, love of God diminishes from it; and to the extent that water remains in the vessel, the vinegar poured into it is diminished.
46:13.section_title_en: The Two Pillars of Love for God: Purification of the Heart and Strength of Knowledge
46:13.anchors:
- Root: ح ب ب (ḥ-b-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root denotes steadfastness and permanence; the heart's fixed attachment to its object.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Love (maḥabbah) is the soul's inclination toward what pleases it; its perfection is exclusive devotion, as in the verse {يحبهم ويحبونه} [Al-Ma'idah/54].
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) usage denotes the heart's clinging; metaphorical (majāz) usage extends to acts of obedience and yearning, culminating in 'ishq (intense passionate love) when it overwhelms the lover.
- Root: خ ل ص (kh-l-ṣ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Purity from admixture; the essence of a thing freed from foreign elements.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Ikhlāṣ is the purification of intention so that no share of creation remains in it; it is the condition for the validity of the shahādah.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: clear, unmixed honey or water; metaphorical: the heart emptied of all rivals so that God alone occupies it.
- Root: ز ه د (z-h-d)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Abstention from what is not essential; renunciation of the superfluous.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Asceticism (zuhd) is the heart's detachment from worldly goods, not merely the abandonment of possessions; it is a preparatory station (maqām) for love.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: disinterest in a thing; metaphorical: the soul's indifference to the ephemeral in favor of the eternal.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Restriction and Specification (Bāb al-Ḥaṣr wa al-Taqyīd bi-innamā) — The particle innamā restricts the predicate to the subject alone, as in "إنما يكتسب العبد حب الله" — affirming love's acquisition solely through specified means, negating all others.
46:13.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Love, Longing, Intimacy and Contentment'

47:17.arabic: المراد بقوله تعالى {والذين اهتدوا زادهم هدى} والهداية الثالثة وراء الثانية وهو النور الذي يشرق في عالم النبوة والولاية بعد كمال المجاهدة فيهتدي بها إلا ما لا يهتدى إليه بالعقل الذي يحصل به التكليف وإمكان تعلم العلوم وهو الهوى المطلق وما عداه حجاب له ومقدمات وهو الذي شرفه الله تعالى بتخصيص الإضافة إليه وإن كان الكل من جهته تعالى فقال تعالى {قل إن هدى الله هو الهدى} وهو المسمى حياة في قوله تعالى {أو من كان ميتا فأحييناه وجعلنا له نورا يمشي به في الناس} والمعنى بقوله تعالى {أفمن شرح
47:17.english:
PageV04P107
But if one does not know what constitutes the welfare of his hereafter—so that he even supposes corruption to be welfare—then from where would mere volition benefit him? There is no benefit in volition, power, and causes except after guidance (hidāyah). For this reason, God—exalted is He—said: {«ربنا الذي أعطى كل شيء خلقه ثم هدى»} "Our Lord who gave everything its creation, then guided." And He said—exalted is He—: {«ولولا فضل الله عليكم ورحمته ما زكى منكم أحد أبدا ولكن الله يزكي من يشاء»} "And were it not for God's bounty upon you and His mercy, not one of you would ever be purified; but God purifies whom He wills." And the Prophet—peace be upon him—said: "No one enters Paradise except by the mercy of God—exalted is He—," that is, by His guidance. So it was said: "Not even you, O Messenger of God?" He said: "Not even I" (1). And guidance (hidāyah) has three stations (manāzil):
47:17.section_title_en: The Degrees of Divine Guidance (Hidāyah), Righteous Discernment (Rushd), Straightening (Tasdīd), and Divine Support (Ta'yīd)
47:17.anchors:
- Root: هدي (H-D-Y)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of gentle, gracious direction (dalālah bi-luṭf); the root also yields "gift" (hadiyyah) and the leading beasts of prey (hawādī) that guide the herd.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Guidance is "directional indication with gentleness" (dalālah bi-luṭf), distinct from mere intellectual proof; it is a divine act that may be general (to all) or specific (to the elect), and its withholding is a form of abandonment.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): "He guided him to the path" (hadāhu lil-sabīl). Metaphorical (majāz): "He guided him" meaning "he preceded him" (taqaddamahu), as a leader precedes the caravan; hence guidance is not merely pointing but active leading.
- Root: رشد (R-SH-D)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The state of being rightly directed in one's affairs; integrity of judgment; names Rāshid, Rushayd derive from it.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Rushd is the opposite of ghayy (error/ruin); it is used like hidāyah but with a nuance of practical, executive discernment—knowing the good AND being moved to pursue it. Al-Raghib explicitly distinguishes the rushd of Abraham (given before, as a special gift) from the mere legal competence (rushd) of an orphan.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "A man is rāshid or rashīd" (possessing rightness in conduct). Metaphorical: "He is of sound lineage" (huwa li-rushdah), i.e., legitimate—showing the root's extension to ontological soundness.
- Root: سدد (S-D-D)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To aim correctly, to hit the mark; the arrow that flies straight (sadīd); the opposite of deviation (ighrāḍ).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): (Not in the retrieved scholia, but by extension from the root's usage in the Qur'an, e.g., {wa-saddidū}, "and be straight/aim rightly")—it denotes the divine facilitation of the creature's movements so they align with the intended good.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "He aimed the arrow and it went straight." Metaphorical: "He was granted success in speech and action" (sudda li-l-ṣawāb).
- Root: أيد (A-Y-D)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Strength, support, reinforcement; the "aid" (ayd) of God is His empowering of His servant.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): (By extension from {إذ أيدتك بروح القدس})—divine reinforcement through a holy spirit, i.e., an immaterial power that fortifies both inner perception (baṣīrah) and outer action.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "He strengthened him" (ayyadahu). Metaphorical: Used for the conferral of spiritual power that makes the servant invincible against error.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Gradation and Specification (Tartīb wa-Takhṣīṣ) — The author structures a sequence of terms (hidāyah → rushd → tasdīd → ta'yīd) where each subsequent term is syntactically and semantically superordinate, building a hierarchy of divine acts. The particle "wa-ammā" (وأما) marks a new topic with contrastive focus, and the anaphoric references (هو، وهي) bind the exposition into a single periodic argument.
47:17.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

47:37.arabic: وقال الله عز وجل أن يسئلكموها فيحفكم تبخلوا أي يستقصى عليكم وأما الحلق فلم يرد والإحفاء القريب من الحلق نقل عن الصحابة نظر بعض التابعين إلى رجل أحفى شاربه فقال ذكرتني أصحاب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وقال المغيرة بن شعبة نظر إلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وقد طال شاربي فقال تعال فقصه لي على سواك (5) ولا بأس بترك سباليه وهما طرفا الشارب فعل ذلك عمر وغيره لأن ذلك لا يستر الفم ولا يبقى فيه غمر الطعام إذ لا يصل إليه وقوله صلى الله عليه وسلم اعفوا اللحى أي كثروها وفي الخبر إن اليهود يعف
47:37.english: **The second: The hair of the moustache.** The Prophet, peace be upon him, said: "Trim the moustache" {«قصوا الشارب»}. In another wording: "Clip the moustaches" {«جزوا الشوارب»}. In yet another wording: "Remove the moustaches thoroughly (ḥuffū al-shawārib) and leave the beards to grow (aʿfū al-liḥā)" {«حفوا الشوارب وأعفوا اللحى»} — meaning: make them at the edge (ḥifāf) of the lip, that is, around it; and the edge (ḥifāf) of a thing is its surrounding. From this is the saying of God Almighty: {«وترى الملائكة حافين من حول العرش»} — "And you see the angels encircling around the Throne." In another wording: "Remove them thoroughly (aḥfū)" — and this suggests complete eradication. His saying "ḥuffū" indicates something less than that. And God Almighty said: {«أن يسألكموها فيحفكم تبخلوا»} — "If He asks you for them and presses you, you would be miserly" — meaning: He would exact from you completely. As for shaving (al-ḥalq) entirely, no command has come regarding it.
47:37.section_title_en: Section 117 — On the Sunnahs of Fitrah: Hair, Nails, and Related Matters
47:37.topic: Al-Ghazali on purifying the character, moral diseases, and spiritual remedies, from 'Mysteries of Purity'

47:37.arabic: يسألكموها فيحفكم تبخلوا يحفكم أي يستقص عليكم فكم بين عبد اشترى منه ماله ونفسه بأن له الجنة وبين عبد لا يستقصي عليه لبخله فهذا أحد معاني أمر الله سبحانه عباده ببذل الأموال المعنى الثاني التطهير من صفة البخل فإنه من المهلكات قال صلى الله عليه وسلم ثلاث مهلكات شح مطاع وهوى متبع وإعجاب المرء بنفسه (2) وقال تعالى ومن يوق شح نفسه فأولئك هم المفلحون وسيأتي في ربع المهلكات وجه كونه مهلكا وكيفية التقصي منه وإنما تزول صفة البخل بأن تتعود بذل المال فحب الشيء لا ينقطع إلا بقهر النفس ع
47:37.english: A group of the Followers (tābiʿūn) held that there are rights in wealth beyond the zakat — among them al-Nakhaʿī, al-Shaʿbī, ʿAṭāʾ, and Mujāhid. Al-Shaʿbī said, after being asked, "Is there a right in wealth beyond the zakat?": "Yes. Have you not heard His saying — mighty and majestic is He: {«وَآتَى الْمَالَ عَلَىٰ حُبِّهِ ذَوِي الْقُرْبَىٰ»} 'And gives wealth, despite his love for it, to relatives' (2:177)?" They also adduced His saying — mighty and majestic is He: {«وَمِمَّا رَزَقْنَاهُمْ يُنفِقُونَ»} 'And from what We have provided them, they spend' (2:3), and His saying — exalted is He: {«وَأَنفِقُوا مِن مَّا رَزَقْنَاكُم»} 'And spend from what We have provided you' (2:254). They claimed that this is not abrogated by the verse of zakat; rather, it falls within the right of a Muslim upon a Muslim. Its meaning is that it is incumbent upon the affluent one, whenever he finds a needy person, to remove his need — over and above the zakat wealth.
47:37.section_title_en: The Second Division: Those Who Guard Their Wealth Awaiting Seasons of Need — On the Inner Meanings of Zakat (Section 173)
47:37.anchors:
- Root: ف-ق-ر (f-q-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of neediness, poverty; the hollow of the spine (faqār) — that which is structurally weak and dependent.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Poverty (faqr) has four senses: (1) essential neediness before Allah, universal to all creatures; (2) lack of possessions; (3) [the third and fourth senses as elaborated in the full lexicon entry].
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (haqīqah): one who lacks wealth. Metaphorical (majāz): "the poverty of speech" (fuqar al-kalām) — its subtle points, likened to ornaments shaped like vertebrae.
- Root: ص-د-ق (ṣ-d-q)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Truthfulness in speech; giving (ṣadaqah) as the outward verification of inward faith.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Ṣidq (truth) and kidhb (falsehood) are originally in speech — statement of what is, or what will be. By extension, ṣadaqah is that which verifies the truthfulness of one's claim to faith through expenditure.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: truthful speech. Metaphorical: "a horse with true running" (dhū miṣdaq fī al-jary) — that which verifies its excellence through action. Thus charity verifies the giver's sincerity.
- Root: م-ن-ن (m-n-n)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The bestowal of a favor; reproaching another by reminding them of one's gift (al-mann).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): [As elaborated in the full lexicon entry on the heart's self-perception of superiority over the recipient.]
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: a heavy weight; a favor. Metaphorical: the act of counting one's favors over another — a corrosion of the gift's value.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد (Restriction & Specification) — governing the precise scope of obligation (farḍ kifāyah) versus supererogatory merit (faḍl), and the restriction of "rights in wealth" (ḥuqūq fī al-māl) beyond the obligatory zakat.
47:37.topic: Al-Ghazali on purifying the character, moral diseases, and spiritual remedies, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

51:56.arabic: الله تعالى مثلا لذلك تقريبا إلى أفهام الخلق إذ عرف أنه ما خلق الجن والإنس إلا ليعبدوه فكانت عبادتهم غاية الحكمة في حقهم ثم أخبر أن له عبدين يحب أحدهما واسمه جبريل وروح القدس والأمين وهو عنده محبوب مطاع أمين مكين ويبغض الآخر واسمه إبليس وهو اللعين المنظر إلى يوم الدين ثم أحال الإرشاد إلى جبريل فقال تعالى {قل نزله روح القدس من ربك بالحق} وقال تعالى {يلقي الروح من أمره على من يشاء من عباده} وأحال الإغواء على إبليس فقال تعالى {ليضل عن سبيله} والإغواء هو استيقاف العباد دون بلوغ غاية الحكمة فانظر كيف نسبه إلى العبد الذي غضب عليه والإرش
51:56.english: Thus was the beginning of this matter and its end. And do not understand it unless you are worthy of it.
