And if you are worthy of it, the eye is opened and you see, so you have no need of a leader to lead you. The blind man can indeed be led, but only to a limit. For when the path narrows and becomes sharper than a sword and finer than a hair, the bird is able to fly over it but is not able to drag a blind man behind it. And when the field becomes narrow and subtle — subtle as water, for example — and crossing is possible only by swimming, then the one skilled in the art of swimming may be able to cross by himself, and perhaps he is not able to drag another behind him. These matters bear the same relation to walking upon the way of the common masses of creatures as walking upon water bears to walking upon earth. Swimming can be learned; but as for walking upon water, it is not acquired by instruction, but rather is attained through the strength of certainty (yaqīn). For this reason it was said to the Prophet, peace be upon him, that Jesus, peace be upon him, was said to have walked upon water, and he, peace be upon him, said: "Had his certainty increased, he would have walked upon the air." {«حديث قيل له يقال إن عيسى مشى على الماء قال لو ازداد يقينا لمشي على الهواء»} — This hadith is rejected (munkar) and is not known in this form. What is known is what Ibn Abi al-Dunya narrated in the Book of Certainty from the saying of Bakr ibn Abd Allah al-Muzani, who said: The disciples lost their Prophet, and it was said to them: "He has headed toward the sea." So they set out seeking him, and when they reached the sea, behold, he was coming toward them walking upon the water. And he mentioned a hadith in which Jesus said: "If the son of Adam had a hair's breadth of certainty, he would walk upon the water." And Abu Mansur al-Daylami narrated in the Musnad al-Firdaws with a weak chain from the hadith of Muadh ibn Jabal: "If you knew God with true knowledge, you would walk upon the seas, and the mountains would be removed by your supplications." These are symbols and allusions to the meaning of aversion (karāhah) and love (maḥabbah), and good pleasure (riḍā) and wrath (ghaḍab), and gratitude (shukr) and ingratitude (kufrān) — more than this is not fitting for the science of practical conduct (ʿilm al-muʿāmalah). And God, exalted be He, struck an example of this to draw it near to the understanding of creatures, since He knew that He created the jinn and mankind only to worship Him, and their worship was the ultimate purpose of wisdom (ghāyat al-ḥikmah) with respect to them. Then He informed that He has two servants: one whom He loves, whose name is Gabriel — the Holy Spirit and the Trustworthy One — and he is with Him beloved, obeyed, trustworthy, and honored; and another whom He hates, whose name is Iblis — the accursed one, reprieved until the Day of Judgment. Then He delegated guidance (irshād) to Gabriel, saying, the Exalted: {«قل نزله روح القدس من ربك بالحق»} "Say: The Holy Spirit has brought it down from your Lord with truth" (16:102), and said, the Exalted: {«يلقي الروح من أمره على من يشاء من عباده»} "He casts the Spirit of His command upon whom He wills of His servants" (40:15). And He delegated misguidance (ighwāʾ) to Iblis, saying, the Exalted: {«ليضل عن سبيله»} "That he may lead astray from His path" (4:119). And ighwāʾ is the halting of servants short of attaining the ultimate purpose of wisdom. So observe how He attributed it to the servant with whom He was wrathful; and guidance (irshād) is the conduct of them toward the ultimate purpose — so observe how He attributed it to the servant whom He loves. And you have an example of this in custom: when a king is in need of one to give him drink and one to cup him and to clean the courtyard of his house of filth, and he has two servants, he does not appoint for cupping and cleaning except the ugliest and meanest of them, and he does not entrust the carrying of drink and perfume except to the best and most complete of them and the most beloved to him. And you should not say: "This is my act, and his act was not without my act" — for you have erred when you attributed that to yourself. Rather, He is the One who directed your motive (dāʿiyah) to the specification of the disliked act to the disliked person, and the beloved act to the beloved person, as a completion of justice (ʿadl). For His justice is sometimes completed through matters in which you have no entry, and sometimes it is completed in you — for you also are among His acts. So your motive, your power, your knowledge, your action, and all the other causes of your movements in expression — all of this is His act, which He arranged with justice in an arrangement from which moderate acts issue forth. Except that you see only yourself, and so you suppose that what appears through you in the world of witness (ʿālam al-shahādah) has no cause from the world of the unseen and the dominion (ʿālam al-ghayb wa al-malakūt). Therefore you attribute it to yourself. And you are only like the child who looks at night at the play of the juggler (mushʿabadh) who brings forth figures from behind a curtain that dance and scream and rise and sit, composed of rags that do not move by themselves — rather, they are moved by fine hair-like threads that do not appear in the darkness of night, their ends in the hand of the juggler, who is hidden from the eyes of the children. So they rejoice and marvel, supposing that those rags dance and play and rise and sit. As for the intelligent ones, they know that this is a moving (taḥrīk) and not a self-movement, but perhaps they do not know its detailed modality. And the one who knows some of its detail does not know it as the juggler knows it, to whom the command belongs and in whose hand is the pulling. Likewise, the children of the people of this world — and all creatures are children relative to the scholars — look at these persons (ashkhāṣ) and suppose that they are the movers, and so they attribute [action] to them. And the scholars know that they are moved, except that they do not know the modality of the moving — and they are the majority. Except the knowers (ʿārifūn), the scholars, and those firmly rooted in knowledge (al-rāsikhūn), for they have perceived, with the sharpness of their sight, fine spider-web threads — nay, much finer than these — suspended from heaven, their ends attached to the persons of the people of the earth. Those threads are not perceived, due to their fineness, by these outward eyes. Then they witnessed the heads of those threads in their suspension-points (manāṭāt) to which they are attached, and they witnessed for those suspension-points handles (maqābiḍ) that are in the hands of the angels who move the heavens. And they also witnessed the angels of the heavens directed toward the bearers of the Throne (ḥamalat al-ʿarsh), awaiting what descends upon them of the command from the presence of Lordship (ḥaḍrat al-rubūbiyyah) — "they do not disobey God in what He commands them, and they do what they are commanded" (66:6). And He expressed these witnessed realities in the Qur'an, and it was said: {«وفي السماء رزقكم وما توعدون»} "And in the heaven is your provision and what you are promised" (51:22). And He expressed the waiting of the angels of the heavens for what descends upon them of decree and command, and it was said: "He created seven heavens and of the earth the like of them; {«يتنزل الأمر بينهن لتعلموا أن الله على كل شيء قدير وأن الله قد أحاط بكل شيء علما»} 'the command descends between them, that you may know that God is powerful over all things and that God encompasses all things in knowledge'" (65:12). These are matters whose interpretation (taʾwīl) none knows except God and those firmly rooted in knowledge (al-rāsikhūn fī al-ʿilm). And Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, expressed the exclusivity of those firmly rooted in knowledge to sciences that the understandings of creatures cannot bear, when he recited the saying of the Exalted: {«يتنزل الأمر بينهن»} "The command descends between them," and said: "Were I to mention what I know of the meaning of this verse, you would stone me" — and in another wording: "You would say he is an unbeliever."
51:56.section_title_en: On the Degrees of Proximity to God and the Hierarchy of Those Who Perfect Divine Wisdom
51:56.anchors:
- Root: سير (s-y-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "السير: الذهاب والسفر، وسار يسير سيرا ومسيرا، والسيارة: الرفقة المسافرة"
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "السير: الانتقال من مكان إلى مكان، ويستعار للسلوك في الدين والطريقة"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): [Literal] "سار القوم: مشوا" — [Metaphorical] "سار فيه السير: مضى في الأمر، وسار ذكره: انتشر، ومنه: سيرة فلان: طريقته"
- Root: مشي (m-sh-y)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "المشي: تردد الأركان على الأرض، والماشية: الإبل والغنم لانتقالها في المرعى"
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "المشي: الانتقال من مكان إلى مكان بإرادة، ويكنى به عن النميمة، وعن شرب المسهل"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): [Literal] "مشيت وتمشيت، وهي حسنة المشية" — [Metaphorical] "مشى بطنه، وأمشاه الدواء، واستمشيت بالدواء، ومنه: مشت المرأة: كثرت أولادها"
- Root: خلق (kh-l-q)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الخلق: التقدير، والخلق: الناس، والخليقة: الطبيعة، والخلق: السجية"
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الخلق أصله: التقدير المستقيم، ويستعمل في إبداع الشيء من غير أصل ولا احتذاء"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): [Literal] "خلق الخراز الأديم: قدره قبل القطع" — [Metaphorical] "خلق الله الخلق: أوجده على تقدير أوجبته الحكمة"
- Root: نفس (n-f-s)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "النفس: الروح، والذات، والشيء النفيس"
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "النفس: الروح، وتطلق على الذات، قال تعالى: {ويحذركم الله نفسه} فنفسه: ذاته"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): [Literal] "شيء نفيس ومنفس" — [Metaphorical] "دفق نفسه أي دمه، وأصابته نفس: عين"
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — Used to distinguish exclusive attribution of actions to God versus creatures, as in "إنما أنت مثل الصبي" (You are only like a child), restricting the simile to the creature while preserving divine agency.
51:56.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

51:56.arabic: تعالى {وما خلقت الجن والإنس إلا ليعبدون ما أريد منهم من رزق} الآية فكل من استعمل شيئا في غير طاعة الله فقد كفر نعمة الله في جميع الأسباب التي لا بد منها لإقدامه على تلك المعصية ولتذكر مثالا واحدا للحكم الخفية التي ليست في غاية الخفاء حتى تعتبر بها وتعلم طريقة الشكر والكفران على النعم فنقول من نعم الله تعالى خلق الدراهم والدنانير وبهما قوام الدنيا وهما حجران لا منفعة في أعيانهما ولكن يضطر الخلق إليهما من حيث إن كل إنسان محتاج إلى أعيان كثيرة في مطعمه وملبسه وسائر حاجاته وقد يعجز عما يحتاج إليه ويملك ما يس
51:56.english: ...except through the permanence of remembrance (*dhikr*), and there is no love except through the knowledge (*maʿrifah*) attained by the permanence of reflection (*fikr*). And the permanence of remembrance and reflection is not possible except through the permanence of the body, and the body does not endure except through nourishment, and nourishment is not completed except through earth, water, and air, and that is not accomplished except through the creation of the heavens and the earth and the creation of all the other limbs, outwardly and inwardly. So all of that exists for the sake of the body, and the body is the mount (*maṭiyyah*) of the soul. And the one who returns to God Most High is the soul at peace (*al-nafs al-muṭmaʾinnah*) through prolonged worship and knowledge. Therefore He Most High said: {«وما خلقت الجن والإنس إلا ليعبدون ما أريد منهم من رزق»} [I created the jinn and mankind only that they might worship Me. I desire of them no provision] (Q. 51:56–57). So whoever uses anything for other than obedience to God has indeed disbelieved in the blessing (*niʿmah*) of God in all the causes that are indispensable for his committing that act of disobedience.
51:56.section_title_en: On the Hidden Wisdom of Gold and Silver Coinage and the Comprehensive Gratitude for Divine Provision
51:56.anchors:
- Root: غرض (gharaḍ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: a target aimed at in shooting; then generalized to any goal sought after.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Distinguishes two types of *gharaḍ*: the deficient goal (which is sought for the sake of something beyond it, e.g., wealth or status) and the complete goal (which is sought for its own sake, e.g., Paradise). Here, the term is used in the deficient sense—money has no intrinsic *gharaḍ* in its physical substance (*ʿayn*).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (*ḥaqīqah*): the physical object of aiming. Metaphorical (*majāz*): any intended purpose. In this text, the absence of *gharaḍ* in the coin's substance is the precise reason for its function as a just mediator.
- Root: حكم (ḥakama)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Root meaning: to restrain for the purpose of reform; hence the bridle (*ḥikmah*) of an animal.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): *Ḥukm* is the prevention of corruption and the establishment of justice. The coin is described as a *ḥākim* (judge/arbiter) between goods—it restrains excess and establishes equitable exchange.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: to place a bridle. Metaphorical: to adjudicate. The coin "bridles" disparate commodities, forcing them into a just relation.
- Root: جمل (jamala)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To collect, gather together; also beauty (*jamāl*) as a gathering of perfections.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): *Jamāl* is abundant goodness, either in oneself or in what flows from one to another. Here, the *jamal* (camel) is cited as an example of a commodity with a specific utility, contrasting with the universal utility of coinage.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the camel as a physical beast of burden. Metaphorical: "to take the night as a camel" (i.e., to traverse it). The text uses the literal camel to illustrate the problem of barter between incommensurate goods.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication). The repeated use of *innamā* ("only") throughout the passage—e.g., «وما خلقت الجن والإنس إلا ليعبدون» and «وإنما أمكن التعديل بالنقدين»—serves to restrict the purpose of creation and the mechanism of exchange to a single, precise cause, excluding all others.
51:56.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

51:56.arabic: سبحانه واليوم الآخر وهو المعني بقوله تعالى {وما خلقت الجن والإنس إلا ليعبدون} ولكن لما اقتضت الحكمة أن يسلط على العبد الشهوات والحاجات وهي تفرق همه
51:56.english: **The First:** That he know that God — mighty and majestic — has made obligatory the disbursement of zakat to him, in order to suffice his concern (hamm) and to make his concerns a single concern. For God — exalted be He — has bound His creatures in worship such that their concern should be one — namely, God — glorified be He — and the Last Day. This is the meaning of His saying — exalted be He: {«وما خلقت الجن والإنس إلا ليعبدون»} ("And I did not create the jinn and mankind except to worship Me") [Al-Dhāriyāt: 56]. But when wisdom required that the servant be subjected to appetites (al-shahawāt) and needs (al-ḥājāt) — and these scatter his concern (tufarriq hammahu) — so that his concern might be unified upon Him alone, and his needs might be gathered into a single need — the need for His worship and obedience.
51:56.section_title_en: ** Section 178: On the Causes of Worthiness (Bayān Asbāb al-Istihqāq) — The Functions of the Recipient of Zakat (Wazā'if al-Qābiḍ), Being Five
51:56.anchors:
**

- Root: سبب (s-b-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The rope by which one climbs a palm tree; every means by which one reaches something.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "السبب: الحبل الذي يصعد به النخل... وسمي كل ما يتوصل به إلى شيء سببا" — every means of access to a thing is called a sabab. Here, "causes of worthiness" (asbāb al-istihqāq) are the means by which the recipient becomes deserving of zakat.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: a rope or cord. Metaphorical: any means, connection, or cause that leads to an end. The title employs the metaphorical extension — the "ropes" that bind the recipient to divine grace.

- Root: وجب (w-j-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To be due, obligatory, established; to fall down dead.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الوجوب: الثبوت" — obligation is rooted in fixedness and establishment. The obligatory (wājib) is that whose non-existence entails impossibility or blameworthiness. Here: "أوجب الله" — God has made it a fixed, established duty.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "وجب البيع" — the sale is confirmed. Metaphorical: "أوجبه على نفسه" — he made it incumbent upon himself. God's "ījāb" is the divine act of rendering something firmly due.

- Root: وهي (w-h-y)
  * Lisan / Ayn: A crack or fissure in leather or cloth; loosening of a binding.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "كل شيء استرخى رباطه فقد وهي" — whatever has its binding loosened has "wahā." God says: {«وانشقت السماء فهي يومئذ واهية»} [Al-Hāqqah: 16].
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "وهى الحائط" — the wall cracked. Metaphorical: "واهي العزالي" — a cloud whose water-skins burst forth with rain. Here, the "هموم" (cares) are the "عزالي" (water-skins) that, when they burst, scatter the heart's attention.

- Root: قبض (q-b-d)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To take with the whole hand; to grasp, seize, contract.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "القبض: تناول الشيء بجميع الكف" — taking hold of a thing with the entire palm. The "qābiḍ" (recipient) is the one who takes hold of the zakat.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "قبض المتاع" — he took the goods. Metaphorical: "قبض على غريمه" — he seized his debtor; "الملك قابض الأرواح" — the Angel of Death is the "Seizer of souls." The recipient (al-qābiḍ) is the one who grasps what is given.

- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The construction "أوجب صرف الزكاة إليه" (He made the disbursement of zakat obligatory to him) shows the prepositional phrase (إليه) interposed between the verb and its direct object, indicating the purpose and direction of the divine command — the zakat flows toward the recipient for a specific end.

52:48.arabic: سبحانه {وسبح بحمد ربك حين تقوم ومن الليل فسبحه وإدبار النجوم} وقال تعالى {إن ناشئة الليل هي أشد وطأ وأقوم قيلا} وقال تعالى {ومن آناء الليل فسبح وأطراف النهار لعلك ترضى} وقال عز وجل {وأقم الصلاة طرفي النهار وزلفا من الليل أن الحسنات يذهبن السيئات} ثم انظر كيف وصف الفائزين من عباده وبماذا وصفهم فقال تعالى {أم من هو قانت}
52:48.english: This is what has been unveiled to those who gaze with the light of inner vision. But if you are not among its people, then look to the address of God Most High to His Messenger and derive it by the light of faith. For God Most High said to the nearest of His servants to Him and the highest of them in rank before Him: {«Indeed, for you in the day is prolonged occupation and [in the night] long travail. And remember the name of your Lord and devote yourself to Him with [complete] devotion»} (73:7-8). And He said Most High: {«And remember the name of your Lord [in prayer] morning and evening. And from [part of] the night, prostrate to Him and exalt Him a long [part of the] night»} (76:25-26). And He said Most High: {«And exalt [Allah] with praise of your Lord before the rising of the sun and before its setting, and during periods of the night [exalt Him] and after the [performance of] prostrations»} (50:39-40). And He said, Glorified be He: {«And exalt [Allah] with praise of your Lord when you arise. And during part of the night exalt Him and after the stars»} (52:48-49). And He said Most High: {«Indeed, the rising by night is more potent for directing the soul and more suitable for the recitation [of the Qur'an]»} (73:6). And He said Most High: {«And from [part of] the night, exalt Him and after the setting of the stars»} (52:49). And He said Most High: {«And during parts of the night, exalt Him and at the ends of the day, that you may be satisfied»} (20:130). And He said, Mighty and Majestic: {«And establish prayer at the two ends of the day and at the approach of the night. Indeed, good deeds do away with misdeeds»} (11:114).
52:48.section_title_en: The Virtue of the Liturgies of Remembrance (Awrād) and the Elucidation That Perseverance Upon Them Is the Path to God Most High
52:48.anchors:
- Root: ورد (w-r-d)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The root denotes arriving at water, approaching a watering-place; the awrād (pl. of wird) are the appointed portions of devotional recitation assigned to fixed times, as one approaches the fountain of divine mercy.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The wird is the allocated share of worship apportioned to a specific hour; its theological nuance is the systematic distribution of remembrance (dhikr) and reflection (fikr) across the昼夜 cycle to combat the soul's innate restlessness.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the portion of water one drinks. Metaphorical: the fixed liturgical portion one "drinks" from the fountain of gnosis—the shift from physical quenching to spiritual saturation.
- Root: لطف (l-ṭ-f)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Gentleness, subtlety, graciousness; to treat with kindness and refinement.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The divine subtlety (al-luṭf) by which God gently draws His servant; here, the soul's need for gentle management (talṭīf) through variety in worship, lest it weary.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical gentleness of touch. Metaphorical: the strategic, compassionate variation of devotional acts to sustain the soul's momentum—a haqīqah of spiritual governance.
- Root: سأم (s-'-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Weariness, boredom, satiety that breeds aversion; the soul's constitutional fatigue with a single monotonous mode.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The psychological impediment to perseverance; overcome only by the divine mercy of variety, as the Prophet said: «إن الله لا يمل حتى تملوا» — God does not weary, but He has ordained that you may.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the nausea of over-satiation. Metaphorical: the spiritual listlessness that overtakes the heart when devotion becomes mechanical—requiring the "turn" (tanqul) between genres of worship.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب التنويع والتقسيم (The Chapter of Division and Distribution) — The periodic structure here distributes predicates across multiple conditional clauses (fa-in... fa-in...), each governing a distinct outcome, requiring the translator to preserve the balanced, correlative syntax of proportional reward.
52:48.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications, prayers, and their spiritual power, from 'Arrangement of Litanies'

52:48.arabic: وكان فيها {واصبر لحكم ربك فإنك بأعيننا} ويقال أن امرأة فتح الموصلي عثرت فانقطع ظفرها فضحكت فقيل لها أما تجدين الوجع فقالت إن لذة ثوابه أزالت عن قلبي مرارة وجعه وقال داود لسليمان عليهما السلام يستدل على تقوى المؤمن بثلاث حسن التوكل فيما لم ينل وحسن الرضا فيما قد نال وحسن الصبر فيما قد فات وقال نبينا صلى الله عليه وسلم من إجلال الله ومعرفة حقه أن لا تشكو وجعك ولا تذكر مصيبتك (1) قال الراوي فلقد رأيت لهم بعد ذلك في المسجد سبعة كلهم قد قرءوا القرآن وروى جابر أنه عليه السلام قال رأيت
52:48.english: Ibn ʿAbbās, may God be pleased with them both, said: "Patience in the Qur'an is of three aspects: patience in performing the obligatory duties of God most High — for it has three hundred degrees; patience in refraining from the forbidden things of God most High — for it has six hundred degrees; and patience over calamity at the first shock — for it has nine hundred degrees." This rank, despite being among the virtuous acts, was only rendered superior to what precedes it — which belongs to the obligatory acts — because every believer is capable of patience in refraining from forbidden things.
52:48.section_title_en: The Third Division: Patience Regarding What Lies Beyond the Scope of Choice — Calamities, Its Supreme Stations, and the Warfare of the Heart Against the Whisperer
52:48.anchors:
- Root: صبر (ṣ-b-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "Al-Sabr: al-imsāk fī ḍīq" — restraint within constriction; to hold back, to bind, to detain.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Ṣabartu al-dābbah: ḥabastuhā bilā ʿalaf" — I held the beast back without fodder. "Al-ṣabr: ḥabs al-nafs ʿalā mā yaqtaḍīhi al-ʿaql wa-al-sharʿ" — Patience is the soul's self-restraint upon what reason and Law require, or from what they require it to be withheld. It is a generic term whose names vary by situation: over calamity it is *ṣabr* alone (opposed to *jazaʿ*); in battle, *shajāʿah* (courage); in affliction, forbearance.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Haqiqah (Literal): "Ṣabartu ʿalā mā akrah, wa-ṣabartu ʿammā uḥibb" — I bore patiently what I dislike and refrained from what I love. Majaz (Metaphorical): "Huwa aṣbaru ʿalā al-ḍarb min al-arḍ" — He is more enduring of blows than the earth; and "ṣabartu yamīnahu" — I bound him by an oath (holding him to a stringent vow).
- Root: قلب (q-l-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To turn over, to overturn, to flip from one face to another; the heart as that which is perpetually turning (taqallub).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Qalb al-shay': taṣrīfuhu wa-ṣarfuhu ʿan wajh ilā wajh" — The heart's essence is its constant overturning and veering between states; hence its name.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Haqiqah: "Qalaba al-shay' qalban: ḥawwalahu ʿan wajhihi" — to turn a thing from its face. Majaz: "Rajul qalb ḥawal: yuqallibu al-umūr wa-yaḥtāl" — a man who turns matters over and devises stratagems; "wa-qallabū laka al-umūr" — they turned the affairs over for you (scrutinized them).
- Root: عله (ʿ-l-h) — [Note: Root appears corrupted in source; likely intended ʿ-l-m or ʿ-l-q; context governs]
  * Lisan / Ayn: [Source entry unclear; context indicates occupation and preoccupation of the heart.]
- Root: نعم (n-ʿ-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Grace, bounty, well-being; the state of ease and delight.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Al-niʿmah: al-ḥālah al-ḥasanah" — the beautiful state; "al-naʿīm: al-tanaʿʿum" — the act of living pleasantly. "Wa-in taʿuddū niʿmata Allāhi lā tuḥṣūhā" {«وَإِن تَعُدُّوا نِعْمَةَ اللَّهِ لَا تُحْصُوهَا»} — the genus of grace encompasses both little and much.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Haqiqah: "Jallat niʿmat Allāh wa-naʿmā'uh" — God's grace and bounties are immense. Majaz: "Khafat naʿāmatuhum: dhahabū" — their ostriches departed (i.e., their prosperity fled).
- Sibawayh Rule: Bāb al-ḥaṣr wa-al-taqyīd bi-innamā (Restriction and Specification by *innamā*) — Governing the exclusive predication in "إنما يرحم الله من عباده الرحما" (God shows mercy only to the merciful among His servants), restricting mercy's object.
52:48.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

53:39.arabic: إلا بعمل صالح فارجعنا نعمل صالحا فقد علمنا الآن صدقك في قولك وأن ليس للإنسان إلا ما سعى وأن سعيه سوف يرى كلما ألقى فيها فوج سألهم خزنتها ألم يأتكم نذير قالوا بلى قد جاءنا نذير أي ألم نسمعكم سنة الله في عباده وأنه
53:39.english: I say: God—exalted is He—loves the obedient and hates the disobedient. So just as He does not hate the obedient father because of His hatred for the disobedient son, likewise He does not love the disobedient son because of His love for the obedient father. And if love were to flow from the father to the son, then hatred would likewise be bound to flow. Rather, the truth is: {«ولا تزر وازرة وزر أخرى»} — "And no bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another" {Quran 6:164, 17:15, 35:18, 39:7, 53:38}. And whoever supposes that he will be saved by his father's piety is like one who supposes he will be satiated by his father's eating, quenched by his father's drinking, become a scholar by his father's learning, and reach the Ka'bah and see it by his father's walking.
53:39.section_title_en: The Reality of Hope (Al-Rajā') and the Futility of Reliance on Another's Piety
53:39.anchors:
- Root: و ل د (walada)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Physical begetting and offspring; the father's generative act.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الولد: المولود" — offspring as a created entity; here used metaphorically for spiritual causation.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical birth. Metaphorical: "تولدت العصبية" — something generated or produced from another; Ghazali exploits this to refute the notion that a father's obedience "generates" salvation for the son.
- Root: ر ج و (rajā)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Expectation, hope, longing for a favorable outcome.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Hope tied to legitimate means; not mere wishful thinking (tamannī).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: awaiting rain. Metaphorical: "رجوت فلانا" — to expect from someone; Ghazali contrasts true hope (with action) vs. delusion (ghurūr).
- Root: غ ر ر (gharara)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Deception, heedlessness, being lured by a false appearance.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The state of one who is duped by Satan's plausible speech.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: a risky venture. Metaphorical: "اغتر بفلان" — to be deceived by outward charm while the inner reality is corrupt.
- Root: ك ي س (kays)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Intelligence, shrewdness, prudence.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The wise man who disciplines his soul and acts for the afterlife.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: alertness. Metaphorical: "الكيس من دان نفسه" — the prudent one who holds his soul to account; antonym of "الأحمق" (the fool).
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — "إنما يوفى الصابرون أجرهم بغير حساب" style; Ghazali uses "إنما" to restrict reward to personal action, and "ليس للإنسان إلا ما سعى" as a restrictive negative clause (nafy + illā) to deny any transfer of merit.
53:39.topic: Classical commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya Ulum al-Din, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

54:17.arabic: عليكم وميثاقه الذي واثقكم به ولقد يسرنا القرآن للذكر فهل من مدكر وتسمية هذا النمط تذكرا ليس ببعيد فكأن التذكر ضربان أحدهما أن يذكر صورة كانت حاضرة الوجود في قلبه لكن غابت بعد الوجود الآخر والآخر أن يذكر صورة كانت مضمنة فيه بالفطرة وهذه حقائق ظاهرة للناظر بنور البصيرة ثقيلة على من يستروجه (1) السماع والتقليد دون الكشف والعيان ولذلك تراه يتخبط في مثل هذه الآيات ويتعسف وفي تأويل التذكر بإقرار النفوس أنواعا من التعسفات ويتخايل إليه في الأخبار والآيات ضروب من المناقضات وربما يغلب ذلك عليه حتى ينظر إليها بعين ا
54:17.english: I say: Know that the washing of the eye is forbidden — that is, the eye of insight (ʿayn al-baṣīrah) is not to be washed with the water of blind imitation and mere hearsay, for it is the organ by which the realities of the intellect are disclosed. And the divisions of what the name "intellect" (al-ʿaql) is applied to have become clear: it is said of the inborn faculty (al-gharīzah), and it is said of the knowledge that is acquired through that faculty, and it is said of the state of that knowledge when it governs the soul, and it is said of the very actions that proceed from that governance.
54:17.section_title_en: The Washing of the Eye is Forbidden — On the True Meaning of Intellect (ʿAql) and Its Divisions
54:17.anchors:
- Root: عقل (ʿAql)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The root denotes binding, restraining, and holding back — the intellect is that which restrains the soul from base desires and prevents it from straying.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "العقل يقال للقوة المتهيئة لقبول العلم، ويقال للعلم الذي يستفيده الإنسان بتلك القوة عقل" — al-ʿaql is said of the faculty prepared to receive knowledge, and it is also said of the knowledge acquired by that faculty. It is the instrument of divine discernment and the locus of taklīf (moral responsibility).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): the inborn faculty of discernment. Metaphorical (Majaz): "نخلة لا تعقل الإبار إذا لم تقبله" — a palm tree that does not accept pollination is said to be "not to ʿaqil" the pollen, extending the root to the sense of "accepting/receiving." Thus, knowledge is called ʿaql metaphorically as its fruit.
- Root: بصر (Baṣar)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Sight, perception — both of the eye and of the heart.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "البصر يقال للجارحة الناظرة... ويقال لقوة القلب المدركة: بصيرة وبصر" — baṣar is said of the seeing organ, and of the perceiving power of the heart: baṣīrah and baṣar. The inner sight (baṣīrah) perceives immaterial realities.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: ocular vision. Metaphorical: "هذه آية مبصرة" — this is an illuminating sign; "واجعلني بصيرة عليهم أي رقيبا وشاهدا" — make me a watcher over them. The inner eye perceives what the outer eye cannot.
- Root: فطر (Faṭara)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To split, cleave, originate, create — the primordial act of divine creation.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "أصل الفطر: الشق طولا... وفطر الله الخلق" — the root is splitting lengthwise; God's "fatr" of creation is His originating of things. "فطرة الله التي فطر الناس عليها" — the primordial disposition upon which God originated mankind.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "فطر الله الخلق، وهو فاطر السموات: مبتدعها" — God originated creation; He is the Originator of the heavens. "وكل مولود يولد على الفطرة" — every newborn is born upon the fiṭrah, i.e., the innate disposition receptive to the religion of truth.
- Root: نفس (Nafs)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Self, soul, spirit; the innermost reality of a thing.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "النفس: الروح... وقوله: تعلم ما في نفسي ولا أعلم ما في نفسك" — nafs is the spirit/soul; "You know what is in my nafs and I know not what is in Your nafs" — the nafs is the seat of inner assent and recognition.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the self. Metaphorical: "دفق نفسه أي دمه" — he poured out his nafs, i.e., his blood. The nafs is the locus of the primordial covenant (mīthāq).
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — The construction "إنما العاقل من آمن بالله" restricts the predicate: the intellect is not merely a faculty of cleverness but is defined by its fruit — faith and God-consciousness (taqwā).
54:17.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

54:24.arabic: لولا نزل هذا القرآن على رجل من القريتين عظيم} وقوله تعالى {أبشرا منا واحدا نتبعه} فهذه المعميات هي التي منعت الاهتداء والهداية الثانية وراء هذه الهداية العامة وهي التي يمد الله تعالى بها العبد حالا بعد حال وهي ثمرة المجاهدة حيث قال تعالى {والذين جاهدوا فينا لنهدينهم سبلنا} وهو المراد بقوله تعالى {والذين اهتدوا زادهم هدى} والهداية الثالثة وراء الثانية وهو النور الذي يشرق في عالم النبوة والولاية بعد كمال المجاهدة فيهتدي بها إلا ما لا يهتدى إليه بالعقل الذي يحصل به التكليف وإمكان تعلم العلوم وهو الهوى المطلق وما عداه حجاب
54:24.english:
PageV04P107
But if one does not know what constitutes the welfare of his hereafter—so that he even supposes corruption to be welfare—then from where would mere volition benefit him? There is no benefit in volition, power, and causes except after guidance (hidāyah). For this reason, God—exalted is He—said: {«ربنا الذي أعطى كل شيء خلقه ثم هدى»} "Our Lord who gave everything its creation, then guided." And He said—exalted is He—: {«ولولا فضل الله عليكم ورحمته ما زكى منكم أحد أبدا ولكن الله يزكي من يشاء»} "And were it not for God's bounty upon you and His mercy, not one of you would ever be purified; but God purifies whom He wills." And the Prophet—peace be upon him—said: "No one enters Paradise except by the mercy of God—exalted is He—," that is, by His guidance. So it was said: "Not even you, O Messenger of God?" He said: "Not even I" (1). And guidance (hidāyah) has three stations (manāzil):
54:24.section_title_en: The Degrees of Divine Guidance (Hidāyah), Righteous Discernment (Rushd), Straightening (Tasdīd), and Divine Support (Ta'yīd)
54:24.anchors:
- Root: هدي (H-D-Y)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of gentle, gracious direction (dalālah bi-luṭf); the root also yields "gift" (hadiyyah) and the leading beasts of prey (hawādī) that guide the herd.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Guidance is "directional indication with gentleness" (dalālah bi-luṭf), distinct from mere intellectual proof; it is a divine act that may be general (to all) or specific (to the elect), and its withholding is a form of abandonment.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): "He guided him to the path" (hadāhu lil-sabīl). Metaphorical (majāz): "He guided him" meaning "he preceded him" (taqaddamahu), as a leader precedes the caravan; hence guidance is not merely pointing but active leading.
- Root: رشد (R-SH-D)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The state of being rightly directed in one's affairs; integrity of judgment; names Rāshid, Rushayd derive from it.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Rushd is the opposite of ghayy (error/ruin); it is used like hidāyah but with a nuance of practical, executive discernment—knowing the good AND being moved to pursue it. Al-Raghib explicitly distinguishes the rushd of Abraham (given before, as a special gift) from the mere legal competence (rushd) of an orphan.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "A man is rāshid or rashīd" (possessing rightness in conduct). Metaphorical: "He is of sound lineage" (huwa li-rushdah), i.e., legitimate—showing the root's extension to ontological soundness.
- Root: سدد (S-D-D)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To aim correctly, to hit the mark; the arrow that flies straight (sadīd); the opposite of deviation (ighrāḍ).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): (Not in the retrieved scholia, but by extension from the root's usage in the Qur'an, e.g., {wa-saddidū}, "and be straight/aim rightly")—it denotes the divine facilitation of the creature's movements so they align with the intended good.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "He aimed the arrow and it went straight." Metaphorical: "He was granted success in speech and action" (sudda li-l-ṣawāb).
- Root: أيد (A-Y-D)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Strength, support, reinforcement; the "aid" (ayd) of God is His empowering of His servant.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): (By extension from {إذ أيدتك بروح القدس})—divine reinforcement through a holy spirit, i.e., an immaterial power that fortifies both inner perception (baṣīrah) and outer action.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "He strengthened him" (ayyadahu). Metaphorical: Used for the conferral of spiritual power that makes the servant invincible against error.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Gradation and Specification (Tartīb wa-Takhṣīṣ) — The author structures a sequence of terms (hidāyah → rushd → tasdīd → ta'yīd) where each subsequent term is syntactically and semantically superordinate, building a hierarchy of divine acts. The particle "wa-ammā" (وأما) marks a new topic with contrastive focus, and the anaphoric references (هو، وهي) bind the exposition into a single periodic argument.

54:32.arabic: عليكم وميثاقه الذي واثقكم به ولقد يسرنا القرآن للذكر فهل من مدكر وتسمية هذا النمط تذكرا ليس ببعيد فكأن التذكر ضربان أحدهما أن يذكر صورة كانت حاضرة الوجود في قلبه لكن غابت بعد الوجود الآخر والآخر أن يذكر صورة كانت مضمنة فيه بالفطرة وهذه حقائق ظاهرة للناظر بنور البصيرة ثقيلة على من يستروجه (1) السماع والتقليد دون الكشف والعيان ولذلك تراه يتخبط في مثل هذه الآيات ويتعسف وفي تأويل التذكر بإقرار النفوس أنواعا من التعسفات ويتخايل إليه في الأخبار والآيات ضروب من المناقضات وربما يغلب ذلك عليه حتى ينظر إليها بعين ا
54:32.english: I say: Know that the washing of the eye is forbidden — that is, the eye of insight (ʿayn al-baṣīrah) is not to be washed with the water of blind imitation and mere hearsay, for it is the organ by which the realities of the intellect are disclosed. And the divisions of what the name "intellect" (al-ʿaql) is applied to have become clear: it is said of the inborn faculty (al-gharīzah), and it is said of the knowledge that is acquired through that faculty, and it is said of the state of that knowledge when it governs the soul, and it is said of the very actions that proceed from that governance.
54:32.section_title_en: The Washing of the Eye is Forbidden — On the True Meaning of Intellect (ʿAql) and Its Divisions
54:32.anchors:
- Root: عقل (ʿAql)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The root denotes binding, restraining, and holding back — the intellect is that which restrains the soul from base desires and prevents it from straying.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "العقل يقال للقوة المتهيئة لقبول العلم، ويقال للعلم الذي يستفيده الإنسان بتلك القوة عقل" — al-ʿaql is said of the faculty prepared to receive knowledge, and it is also said of the knowledge acquired by that faculty. It is the instrument of divine discernment and the locus of taklīf (moral responsibility).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): the inborn faculty of discernment. Metaphorical (Majaz): "نخلة لا تعقل الإبار إذا لم تقبله" — a palm tree that does not accept pollination is said to be "not to ʿaqil" the pollen, extending the root to the sense of "accepting/receiving." Thus, knowledge is called ʿaql metaphorically as its fruit.
- Root: بصر (Baṣar)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Sight, perception — both of the eye and of the heart.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "البصر يقال للجارحة الناظرة... ويقال لقوة القلب المدركة: بصيرة وبصر" — baṣar is said of the seeing organ, and of the perceiving power of the heart: baṣīrah and baṣar. The inner sight (baṣīrah) perceives immaterial realities.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: ocular vision. Metaphorical: "هذه آية مبصرة" — this is an illuminating sign; "واجعلني بصيرة عليهم أي رقيبا وشاهدا" — make me a watcher over them. The inner eye perceives what the outer eye cannot.
- Root: فطر (Faṭara)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To split, cleave, originate, create — the primordial act of divine creation.

- Root: نفس (Nafs)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Self, soul, spirit; the innermost reality of a thing.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "النفس: الروح... وقوله: تعلم ما في نفسي ولا أعلم ما في نفسك" — nafs is the spirit/soul; "You know what is in my nafs and I know not what is in Your nafs" — the nafs is the seat of inner assent and recognition.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the self. Metaphorical: "دفق نفسه أي دمه" — he poured out his nafs, i.e., his blood. The nafs is the locus of the primordial covenant (mīthāq).
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — The construction "إنما العاقل من آمن بالله" restricts the predicate: the intellect is not merely a faculty of cleverness but is defined by its fruit — faith and God-consciousness (taqwā).

55:8.arabic: تعالى إن لا تطغوا في الميزان وأقيموا الوزن بالقسط ولا تخسروا الميزان فمن خصي نفسه ليزيل شهوة النكاح أو ترك النكاح مع القدرة والأمن من الآفات أو ترك الأكل حتى ضعف عن العبادة والذكر والفكر فقد أخسر الميزان ومن انهمك في شهوة البطن والفرج فقد طغى في الميزان وإنما العدل أن يخلو وزنه وتقديره عن الطغيان والخسران فتعتدل به كفتا الميزان فإذن الفضائل الخاصة بالنفس المقربة إلى الله تعالى أربعة علم مكاشفة وعلم معاملة وعفة وعدالة ولا يتم هذا في غالب الأمر إلا بالنوع الثاني وهو الفضائل البدنية وهي أربعة الصحة والقوة والجمال و
55:8.english: The ultimate goal — nay, the ultimate goal — is the felicity of the Hereafter, and its total content reduces to four matters: a permanence with no annihilation, a joy with no grief therein, a knowledge with no ignorance accompanying it, and a wealth with no poverty after it. These constitute the true blessing (al-niʿmah al-ḥaqīqiyyah). For this reason, the Messenger of God — may God bless him and grant him peace — said: {«لَا عَيْشَ إِلَّا عَيْشُ الْآخِرَةِ»} ("There is no life save the life of the Hereafter"). He said this amid hardship as a consolation to the soul — and that was at the time of digging the trench (al-khandaq) in severe distress — and he said it once amid joy as a deterrent to the soul from leaning toward the pleasures of this world — and that was when the people crowded around him during the Farewell Pilgrimage. The report of his saying during the Farewell Pilgrimage, {«لَا عَيْشَ إِلَّا عَيْشَةُ الْآخِرَةِ»} ("There is no life save the life of the Hereafter"), was transmitted by al-Shāfiʿī as a disconnected (mursal) tradition and by al-Ḥākim as a connected (muttaṣil) one, and he declared it sound (ṣaḥīḥ); it has already been mentioned in the Book of Pilgrimage. And a man said: "O God, I ask You for the completion of blessing (tamām al-niʿmah)." The Prophet — may God bless him and grant him peace — said: "And do you know what the completion of blessing is?" He said: "No." He said: "The completion of blessing is the entering of Paradise." This is the hadith of the man who said: "O God, I ask You for the completion of blessing" — the full report.
55:8.section_title_en: The Ultimate Goal and Its Means — The Fourfold Division of True Blessedness and the Necessity of External Goods for the Path to the Hereafter
55:8.anchors:
- Root: غ ي ا (gh-y-a)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The extreme limit, endpoint, or terminal aim toward which something strives; the farthest reach of a matter.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The final purpose (al-ghāyah) contrasted with the means (al-wasīlah); in theological terms, the ultimate end of human striving is the felicity of the Hereafter (saʿādat al-ākhirah), not transient worldly states.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) usage denotes a spatial or temporal terminus; metaphorical (majāz) extension applies it to the teleological end of moral and spiritual endeavor.
- Root: ن ع م (n-ʿ-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Softness, ease, and well-being; also the state of living pleasantly and abundantly.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-Niʿmah is the "goodly state" (al-ḥālah al-ḥasanah) — a condition of being, not merely a discrete object; true niʿmah is that which endures without cessation, hence the Hereafter's bliss is the real blessing, while worldly goods are only instrumental.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "jallat niʿmatu-llāh" (God's blessing is immense); metaphorical: "khafat naʿāmatuhum" (their prosperity vanished) — indicating that apparent goods may be stripped of true value when severed from the ultimate end.
- Root: ر ب ع (r-b-ʿ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Fourfoldness; the root of quartile division and dwelling in a place (rubʿ).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The numerical base for systematic classification; here, the exhaustive partitioning of blessings into four genera, each subdivided into four species, yielding sixteen total — a structural device for comprehensive enumeration.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "rabiʿa al-makān" (he dwelt in the place); metaphorical: "rabbaʿahu Allāh" (God raised him up) — suggesting that the fourfold scheme is not arbitrary but a divinely ordered taxonomy of means that "raise up" the seeker toward the end.
- Root: ن ف س (n-f-s)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The self, soul, or spirit; that which is most interior and precious to a person.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-Nafs denotes the rational soul (al-rūḥ) in its capacity for knowledge and virtue; its "virtues" (faḍāʾil) are the immaterial perfections that draw one near to God, distinct from bodily or external accidents.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "shayʾ nafīs" (a precious thing); metaphorical: "aṣābat-hu nafs" (an evil eye struck him) — showing that the soul's true preciousness lies in its inward purity, not outward display.
- Sibawayh Rule: Bāb al-ḥaṣr wa-l-taqyīd bi-innamā (Restriction and Focused Predication) — The particle innamā restricts the predicate to the subject alone, as in "the true blessing is only the Hereafter's felicity," excluding all else from the category of genuine, ultimate good.
55:8.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

55:14.arabic: الطيار والشهوة عبارة عن حركة جنده السيار وهذا لأن الشيطان خلق من النار وخلق الإنسان من صلصال كالفخار والفخار قد اجتمع فيه مع النار الطين والطين طبيعته السكون والنار طبيعتها الحركة فلا يتصور نار مشتعلة لا تتحرك بل لا تزال تتحرك بطبعها وقد كلف الملعون المخلوق من النار أن يطمئن عن حركته ساجدا لما خلق الله من الطين فأبى واستكبر واستعصى وعبر عن سبب استعصائه بأن قال {خلقتني من نار وخلقته من طين} فإذن حيث لم يسجد الملعون لأبينا آدم صلوات الله عليه وسلامه فلا ينبغي أن يطمع في سجوده لأولاده ومهما كف عن القلب وسواسه وعدوانه وطيرانه وجولانه فقد أظهر انق
55:14.english: Ibn ʿAbbās, may God be pleased with them both, said: "Patience in the Qur'an is of three aspects: patience in performing the obligatory duties of God most High — for it has three hundred degrees; patience in refraining from the forbidden things of God most High — for it has six hundred degrees; and patience over calamity at the first shock — for it has nine hundred degrees." This rank, despite being among the virtuous acts, was only rendered superior to what precedes it — which belongs to the obligatory acts — because every believer is capable of patience in refraining from forbidden things.
55:14.section_title_en: The Third Division: Patience Regarding What Lies Beyond the Scope of Choice — Calamities, Its Supreme Stations, and the Warfare of the Heart Against the Whisperer
55:14.anchors:
- Root: صبر (ṣ-b-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "Al-Sabr: al-imsāk fī ḍīq" — restraint within constriction; to hold back, to bind, to detain.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Ṣabartu al-dābbah: ḥabastuhā bilā ʿalaf" — I held the beast back without fodder. "Al-ṣabr: ḥabs al-nafs ʿalā mā yaqtaḍīhi al-ʿaql wa-al-sharʿ" — Patience is the soul's self-restraint upon what reason and Law require, or from what they require it to be withheld. It is a generic term whose names vary by situation: over calamity it is *ṣabr* alone (opposed to *jazaʿ*); in battle, *shajāʿah* (courage); in affliction, forbearance.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Haqiqah (Literal): "Ṣabartu ʿalā mā akrah, wa-ṣabartu ʿammā uḥibb" — I bore patiently what I dislike and refrained from what I love. Majaz (Metaphorical): "Huwa aṣbaru ʿalā al-ḍarb min al-arḍ" — He is more enduring of blows than the earth; and "ṣabartu yamīnahu" — I bound him by an oath (holding him to a stringent vow).
- Root: قلب (q-l-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To turn over, to overturn, to flip from one face to another; the heart as that which is perpetually turning (taqallub).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Qalb al-shay': taṣrīfuhu wa-ṣarfuhu ʿan wajh ilā wajh" — The heart's essence is its constant overturning and veering between states; hence its name.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Haqiqah: "Qalaba al-shay' qalban: ḥawwalahu ʿan wajhihi" — to turn a thing from its face. Majaz: "Rajul qalb ḥawal: yuqallibu al-umūr wa-yaḥtāl" — a man who turns matters over and devises stratagems; "wa-qallabū laka al-umūr" — they turned the affairs over for you (scrutinized them).
- Root: عله (ʿ-l-h) — [Note: Root appears corrupted in source; likely intended ʿ-l-m or ʿ-l-q; context governs]
  * Lisan / Ayn: [Source entry unclear; context indicates occupation and preoccupation of the heart.]
- Root: نعم (n-ʿ-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Grace, bounty, well-being; the state of ease and delight.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Al-niʿmah: al-ḥālah al-ḥasanah" — the beautiful state; "al-naʿīm: al-tanaʿʿum" — the act of living pleasantly. "Wa-in taʿuddū niʿmata Allāhi lā tuḥṣūhā" {«وَإِن تَعُدُّوا نِعْمَةَ اللَّهِ لَا تُحْصُوهَا»} — the genus of grace encompasses both little and much.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Haqiqah: "Jallat niʿmat Allāh wa-naʿmā'uh" — God's grace and bounties are immense. Majaz: "Khafat naʿāmatuhum: dhahabū" — their ostriches departed (i.e., their prosperity fled).
- Sibawayh Rule: Bāb al-ḥaṣr wa-al-taqyīd bi-innamā (Restriction and Specification by *innamā*) — Governing the exclusive predication in "إنما يرحم الله من عباده الرحما" (God shows mercy only to the merciful among His servants), restricting mercy's object.
55:14.topic: Al-Ghazali on purifying the character, moral diseases, and spiritual remedies, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

55:27.arabic: في حقه بالموت ف كل من عليها فان ويبقى وجه ربك ذو الجلال والإكرام وإنما تفنى الدنيا بالموت في حقه إلى أن تفنى في نفسها عند بلوغ الكتاب أجله وهذا الأنس يتلذذ به العبد بعد موته إلى أن ينزل في جوار الله عز وجل ويترقى من الذكر إلى اللقاء وذلك بعد أن يبعثر ما في القبور ويحصل ما في الصدور ولا ينكر بقاء ذكر الله عز وجل معه الموت فيقول إنه أعدم فكيف يبقى معه ذكر الله عز وجل فإنه لم يعدم عدما يمنع الذكر بل عدما من الدنيا وعالم الملك والشهادة لا من عالم الملكوت وإلى ما ذكرناه الإشارة بقوله صلى الله عليه وسلم القبر إما حفر
55:27.english: If, therefore, he had grown intimate with it, he delights in it and takes pleasure in the cessation of the impediments that had diverted him from it. For the pressing necessities of needs in this worldly life divert one from the remembrance of God, may He be mighty and majestic, and after death no impediment remains. It is as if he has been left alone with his Beloved, and so his joy is immense, and he is delivered from the prison in which he had been prevented from that which was his source of intimacy. For this reason, he, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "The Holy Spirit (Rūḥ al-Qudus) breathed into my heart: Love whom you will, for you shall surely part from him." {«أحبب من أحببت فإنك مفارقه»} By this he intended everything connected to this world, for that perishes with respect to him at death. For {«كل من عليها فان * ويبقى وجه ربك ذو الجلال والإكرام»} [Everything upon it is perishing, and there remains the Face of your Lord, Possessor of Majesty and Honor]. And this world only perishes with respect to him at death, until it perishes in itself when the Book reaches its appointed term.
55:27.section_title_en: Section 240 — The Station of Remembrance (Dhikr): On the Transformation of Habit into Nature, the Intimacy of Remembrance After Death, and the Excellence of Martyrdom as the Seal of One's State
55:27.anchors:
- Root: ألف (Alifa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of reconciliation, familiarity, and the formation of habit through repeated engagement.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The theological nuance of 'uns' (intimacy) as the soul's acquired disposition of comfort in the presence of its Beloved, contrasting with 'wahsha' (estrangement).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Distinguishes the literal sense of social familiarity from the metaphorical (majaz) sense of the heart's deep-seated repose in the remembrance of God, which becomes a 'second nature' (ṭabʿan ākhara).
- Root: ختم (Khatama)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To seal, stamp, or conclude; the final impression left upon a thing.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The theological sense of the 'seal' (khātima) of one's life—the terminal state upon which one departs from the world and which determines the nature of the afterlife.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): The literal act of sealing a document versus the metaphorical designation of one's final spiritual condition as the determining factor of one's eternal outcome.
- Root: شهد (Shahida)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To witness, to be present, to testify.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The specific theological elevation of 'shahāda' (martyrdom) as the ultimate act of witnessing the truth of God through the sacrifice of one's own life, rendering the martyr a living witness (shahīd).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): The literal sense of legal testimony versus the metaphorical reality of the martyr whose very being testifies to the sincerity of his devotion, being 'alive' with his Lord.
- Root: قطع (Qata'a)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To sever, cut off, or detach.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The essential spiritual operation of severing worldly attachments ('alā'iq) to achieve the unadulterated focus of the heart upon God.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): The literal cutting of a physical tie versus the metaphorical severance of all internal and external impediments that distract the soul from its sole Beloved.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Restriction and Specification (Bāb al-Ḥaṣr wa al-Taqyīd bi-innamā) — Governing how the exclusive focus of the martyr's intention is syntactically and logically restricted to God alone, as exemplified in the phrase "no god but God" (lā ilāha illā Allāh), which requires the complete negation of all other objects of intention before affirming the sole Divine Object.
55:27.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

57:11.arabic: بعبادة القرض فقال من ذا الذي يقرض الله قرضا حسنا فإن قلت قولك إن بقاء النسل والنفس محبوب يوهم أن فناءها مكروه عند الله وهو فرق بين الموت والحياة بالإضافة إلى إرادة الله تعالى ومعلوم أن الكل بمشيئة الله وأن الله غني عن العالمين فمن أين يتميز عنده موتهم عن حياتهم أو بقاؤهم عن فنائهم فأعلم أن هذه الكلمة حق أريد بها باطل فإن ما ذكرناه لا ينافي إضافة الكائنات كلها إلى إرادة الله خيرها وشرها ونفعها وضرها ولكن المحبة والكراهية يتضادان وكلاهما لا يضادان الإرادة فرب مراد مكروه ورب مراد محبوب فالمعاصي مكروهة و
57:11.english: وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم: "لا يلقى الله أحد بذنب أعظم من جهالة أهله."
57:11.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

59:2.arabic: في معرض الإنكار وقال عز وجل {وظنوا أنهم مانعتهم حصونهم من الله فأتاهم الله من حيث لم يحتسبوا} فرد على الكفار في إعجابهم بحصونهم وشوكتهم وقال تعالى {وهم يحسبون أنهم يحسنون صنعا} وهذا أيضا يرجع إلى العجب بالعمل وقد يعجب الإنسان بالعمل هو مخطئ فيه كما يعجب بعمل هو مصيب فيه وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم ثلاث مهلكات شح مطاع وهوى متبع وإعجاب المرء بنفسه (1) حديث أبي ثعلبة إذا رأيت شحا مطاعا وهوى متبعا وإعجاب كل ذي رأي برأيه فعليك نفسك أخرجه أبو داود والترمذي وحسنه وابن ماجه وقد تقدم وقال ابن مسعود الهالك في اثنتين القنوط والعجب وإنما جمع بينه
59:2.english: Know that self-admiration (al-ʿujb) is blameworthy in the Book of God Most High and the Sunnah of His Messenger, peace be upon him. God Most High said: {«وَيَوْمَ حُنَيْنٍ إِذْ أَعْجَبَتْكُمْ كَثْرَتُكُمْ فَلَمْ تُغْنِ عَنكُمْ شَيْئًا»} (And on the day of Hunayn, when your great number pleased you—but it availed you nothing) — He mentioned this in the context of censure. And He, Mighty and Majestic, said: {«وَظَنُّوا أَنَّهُم مَّانِعَتُهُمْ حُصُونُهُم مِّنَ اللهِ فَأَتَاهُمُ اللهُ مِنْ حَيْثُ لَمْ يَحْتَسِبُوا»} (And they thought that their fortresses would protect them from God; but God came upon them from where they did not expect) — thus He rebuked the disbelievers for their self-admiration in their fortresses and their might. And He Most High said: {«وَهُمْ يَحْسَبُونَ أَنَّهُمْ يُحْسِنُونَ صُنْعًا»} (While they think that they are doing good work) — and this too reverts to self-admiration in one's deed. And a man may admire himself for a deed in which he is mistaken, just as he may admire himself for a deed in which he is correct.
59:2.section_title_en: Exposition of the Blameworthiness of Self-Admiration (Al-ʿUjb) and Its Afflictions
59:2.anchors:
- Root: عجب (ʿ-j-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: astonishment, wonder, or a state that seizes one due to an unrecognized cause; al-Ayn notes "العاجب" as one who marvels, and "أعجبه" as something pleasing or admirable.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): ʿUjb is a condition arising from ignorance of a thing's cause; hence, it is impermissible regarding God, the Knower of all unseen. It denotes self-conceit when one is pleased with one's own state or deed.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): wonder/astonishment; Metaphorical (Majaz): self-admiration (iʿjāb al-marʾ bi-nafsihi), where one deems his deed or self praiseworthy, leading to arrogance.
- Root: حدث (ḥ-d-th)
  * Lisan / Ayn: New occurrence after non-existence; al-Ayn: "الحدّث: الإبداء" (origination/manifestation).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Ḥudūth is coming-to-be after not being; for God, creation is iḥdāth; for man, it implies temporal novelty.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: recent event; Metaphorical: "مُحَدَّث" as one inspired with truth, as if spoken to by unseen—here, not applicable; rather, the root underscores the temporal, contingent nature of deeds that invite ʿujb.
- Root: وقد (w-q-d)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Fire blazing; al-Ayn: "وقدت النار" (fire kindled).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Used for fuel and flame; metaphorically, intense burning—here, linked to the "fire" of destruction caused by ʿujb, as in the hadith on destructive traits.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: kindling; Metaphorical: "وقدة الصيف" (summer's heat)—intensity of affliction, paralleling ʿujb's consuming harm.
- Root: طلح (ṭ-l-ḥ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Banana tree or acacia; al-Ayn: "الطلح: شجر" (a tree).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Ṭalḥ is a tree; ṭalīḥ means exhausted/emaciated from toil—here, the name Ṭalḥah (companion) appears, whose deed was nearly spoiled by ʿujb.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: tree; Metaphorical: "طلح على غريمه" (pressed a debtor until weary)—exertion; also "طالح" (corrupt), contrasting with ṣalāḥ (righteousness), hinting at ʿujb's corrupting effect.
- Sibawayh Rule: Restriction and Focused Predication (باب الحصر والتقييد) — Used in phrases like "إنما جمع بينهما" (He only paired them) and "فالموجود لا يطلب والمحال لا يطلب" (the existent is not sought, and the impossible is not sought), where the predicate is restricted to a specific cause, clarifying logical necessity.
59:2.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'Condemnation of Pride and Conceit'

59:2.arabic: فيسمى عبوره عبرة وقد أمر الحق به فقال {فاعتبروا يا أولي الأبصار} ومنهم من عميت بصيرته فلم يعتبر فاحتبس في عالم الملك والشهادة وستنفتح إلى حبسه أبواب جهنم وهذا الحبس مملوء نارا من شأنها أن تطلع على الأفئدة إلا أن بينه وبين إدراك المها حجابا فإذا رفع ذلك الحجاب بالموت أدرك وعن هذا أظهر الله تعالى الحق على لسان قوم استنطقهم بالحق فقالوا الجنة والنار مخلوقتان ولكن الجحيم تدرك مرة بإدراك يسمى علم اليقين ومرة بإدراك آخر يسمى عين اليقين وعين اليقين لا يكون إلا في الآخرة وعلم اليقين قد يكون في الدنيا ولكن للذين قد وفو
59:2.english: As for the first: if it is possible in existence at all, it is at the utmost extreme of remoteness. As for the second: the lower world is overflowing with it. As for the third and fourth: they exist, but at the utmost extreme of rarity. And it is inconceivable that this [rarity] should itself be rare and anomalous — rather, even with its rarity, it varies in degree of fewness and abundance. Its abundance occurs only in ages proximate to the ages of the Prophets, peace be upon them. The longer the interval [from their time] grows, the scarcer such hearts become, until the Hour draws near and God accomplishes a matter already decreed ( {وكان أمرا مفعولا} ).
59:2.section_title_en: The Division of Hearts and the Rarity of the Heart Fit for the Kingdom of the Hereafter
59:2.anchors:
- Root: م ل ك (Malaka)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of possession, dominion, and sovereign control; al-Ayn notes the pattern shift in derived nouns.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الملك: هو المتصرف بالأمر والنهي في الجمهور" — kingship is governance over rational beings, divided into actual sovereignty (al-tamalluk) and capacity for it (al-quwwah).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "لله الملك والملكوت" — dominion over the visible and invisible realms. Metaphorical: "ملك نفسه عند الغضب" — self-mastery; here extended to the heart's sovereignty over the soul's appetites.
- Root: ق ل ب (Qalaba)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Turning and overturning a thing from one state to another.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "قلب الشيء: تصريفه وصرفه عن وجه إلى وجه" — the heart is so named for its constant fluctuation between states.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "قلب الشيء قلبا: حوله عن وجهه." Metaphorical: "رجل قلب حول: يقلب الأمور ويحتال" — one who turns matters over; here, hearts are classified by their dominant orientation.
- Root: ع ل م (ʿAlima)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Foundational knowing and perception.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "العلم: إدراك الشيء بحقيقته" — apprehension of a thing's true reality, of two kinds: grasping the essence, and judging its attributes.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "هو من أعلام العلم الخافقه" — knowledge as a raised banner. Here, "علم اليقين" (knowledge of certainty) vs. "عين اليقين" (eye of certainty) marks the literal-to-metaphorical ascent from inference to direct vision.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — The repeated use of "إنما" (only/indeed) throughout this passage serves to restrict predicates exclusively to their subjects, e.g., "وإنما تكون كثرته في الأعصار القريبة" — restricting abundance to specific eras, and "وإنما وجب أن يكون هذا نادرا" — restricting the cause of rarity.
59:2.topic: Al-Ghazali on the journey of the soul, death, and the Hereafter, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

61:6.arabic: حرمك واعف عمن ظلمك // ورأيت في الإنجيل قال عيسى بن مريم عليه السلام لقد قيل لكم من قبل إن السن بالسن والأنف بالأنف وأنا أقول لكم لا تقاوموا بالشر بل من ضرب خدك الأيمن فحول إليه الخد الأيسر ومن أخذ رداءك فأعطه إزارك ومن سخرك لتسير معه ميلا فسر معه ميلين وكل ذلك أمر بالصبر على الأذى فالصبر على أذى الناس من أعلى مراتب الصبر لأنه يتعاون فيه باعث الدين وباعث الشهوة والغضب جميعا
61:6.english: And acts of disobedience are the requisite of the impulse of caprice (bāʿith al-hawā). And the most severe kind of patience is patience in abstaining from those acts of disobedience that have become familiar through habit — for habit is a fifth nature. When habit is joined to lustful desire, two battalions from the battalions of Satan array themselves in concert against the battalion of God (jund Allāh) — may He be exalted — and the impulse of religion (bāʿith al-dīn) has no strength to suppress them. Then, if that act be one whose commission has been rendered easy (tayassara), patience in abstaining from it is heavier upon the soul — such as patience in abstaining from the sins of the tongue: backbiting (ghībah), falsehood, contentious disputation (mirāʾ), self-praise whether by insinuation (taʿrīḍ) or by explicit statement (taṣrīḥ), the varieties of jesting that wound hearts, the kinds of words by which one intends belittlement and contempt, and the mention of the dead with aspersion cast upon them, upon their sciences, their conduct, and their stations. For such mention is in its outward aspect (fī ẓāhirihi) backbiting, and in its inward aspect (fī bāṭinihi) self-praise. In it the soul has two lusts: one is the negation of the other [person], and the other is the affirmation of oneself. And by these two together there is completed for it that lordship (rubūbiyyah) which is innate in its disposition — and which is the very opposite of what it has been commanded regarding servanthood (ʿubūdiyyah). And because of the conjunction of the two lusts, and the ease of moving the tongue, and the fact that this becomes habitual in everyday converse, patience in abstaining from it becomes difficult. And it is among the greatest of the destructive enormities (al-mūbiqāt) — so much so that its disapproval and ugliness have been effaced from hearts by dint of its frequent repetition and the universality of familiarity with it. Thus you see a man who would, for example, wear silk and deem it utterly remote [of permissibility], yet he unleashes his tongue the whole day long against the reputations (aʿrāḍ) of people and does not deem that objectionable — notwithstanding what has come down in the report that backbiting is more severe than adultery (zinā). And God — may He be exalted — said: {«ودع أذاهم وتوكل على الله»} "And leave aside their harm and put thy trust in God" (Q. 33:48). And He said — may He be exalted: {«واصبر على ما يقولون واهجرهم هجرا جميلا»} "And be patient over what they say, and depart from them with a gracious departure" (Q. 73:10). And He said — may He be exalted: {«ولقد نعلم أنك يضيق صدرك بما يقولون فسبح بحمد ربك»} "And indeed We know that thy breast is straitened by what they say; so glorify with the praise of thy Lord" (Q. 15:97–98) — to the end of the verse. And He said — may He be exalted: {«ولتسمعن من الذين أوتوا الكتاب من قبلكم ومن الذين أشركوا أذى كثيرا وإن تصبروا وتتقوا فإن ذلك من عزم الأمور»} "And you shall surely hear from those who were given the Scripture before you and from those who associate [others with God] much harm. And if you are patient and God-fearing, indeed that is of the resolute affairs" (Q. 3:186) — that is, that you be patient in refraining from requital (mukāfaʾah). And for this reason God — may He be exalted — praised those who pardon others their due rights in retaliation (qiṣāṣ) and otherwise, saying — may He be exalted: {«وإن عاقبتم فعاقبوا بمثل ما عوقبتم به ولئن صبرتم لهو خير الصابرين»} "And if you punish, then punish with the like of that wherewith you were afflicted. And if you are patient, it is surely better for the patient" (Q. 16:126). And he — upon him be peace — said: "Maintain the bond with him who cuts you off, and give to him who withholds from you, and pardon him who wrongs you." And I have seen in the Gospel that ʿĪsā ibn Maryam — upon him be peace — said: "It was said to you of old: an eye for an eye and a nose for a nose. But I say to you: do not resist evil. Rather, whoever strikes your right cheek, turn to him PageV04P071 the left cheek; and whoever takes your cloak, give him your garment; and whoever compels you to walk with him one mile, walk with him two miles." And all of that is a command to be patient under harm. So patience under the harm of people is among the highest stations of patience, because in it the impulse of religion and the impulse of lustful desire and anger are all arrayed together [against the soul].
61:6.section_title_en: The Most Severe Forms of Patience: Abstaining from Habitual Sins and Enduring Harm
61:6.anchors:
- Root: صبر (ṣ-b-r)

61:6.arabic: عز وجل فلما نظروا إلى داود عليه السلام نهضوا ليتفرقوا عنه فقال داود إني رسول الله إليكم جئتكم لأبلغكم رسالة ربكم فأقبلوا نحوه وألقوا أسماعهم نحو قوله وألقوا أبصارهم إلى الأرض فقال داود إني رسول الله إليكم يقرئكم السلام ويقول لكم ألا تسألون حاجة ألا تنادوني أسمع صوتكم وكلامكم فإنكم أحبائي وأصفيائي وأوليائي أفرح لفرحكم وأسارع إلى محبتكم وأنظر إليكم في كل ساعة نظر الوالدة الشفيقة الرفيقة قال فجرت الدموع على خدودهم فقال شيخهم سبحانك سبحانك نحن عبيدك وبنو عبيدك فاغفر لنا ما قطع قلوبنا عن ذكرك فيما مضى من أعمارنا وقال الآخر سبحانك سبح
61:6.english: And His saying, Glorified and Exalted is He: {نُورُهُمْ يَسْعَىٰ بَيْنَ أَيْدِيهِمْ وَبِأَيْمَانِهِمْ يَقُولُونَ رَبَّنَا أَتْمِمْ لَنَا نُورَنَا} ["Their light will run before them and on their right hands; they will say, 'Our Lord, perfect for us our light'"] (Q 66:8) — this is susceptible to the meaning that He bestows upon them the perfection of light whenever they had provisioned from the world the origin of light. And it is also susceptible that the intended meaning is the perfection of light in what was not illuminated in this world with an illumination that stands in need of further completion and radiance — so that this is what is meant by its perfection. And His saying, Exalted is He: {انْظُرُونَا نَقْتَبِسْ مِنْ نُورِكُمْ قِيلَ ارْجِعُوا وَرَاءَكُمْ فَالْتَمِسُوا نُورًا} ["Look upon us so we may borrow from your light. It will be said, 'Return behind you and seek light'"] (Q 57:13) — this indicates that the lights must have their origin provisioned in this world, then in the Hereafter they increase in radiance. But as for a light being newly generated [there without prior origin] — no. And the judgment in this matter is a venture of conjecture, perilous, and there has not been unveiled to us therein anything trustworthy. So we ask God, Exalted is He, to increase us in knowledge and right guidance, and to show us the truth as truth.
61:6.section_title_en: On the Ever-Replenished Delights of the Hereafter and the Yearning (Shawq) for the Divine Vision
61:6.anchors:
- Root: لذذ (Ladhdhah — Pleasure/Delight)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root denotes the sweetness of taste and the experience of sensory gratification; its verbal form (ladhdha) implies direct apprehension of what is agreeable.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In theological usage, true pleasure (al-ladhdhah al-ʿuẓmā) is the soul's perception of what is conformable to its nature — the highest being the vision of God (ru'yat Allāh) and the bliss of proximity to Him.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) for sensory delight; metaphorical (majāz) for intellectual and spiritual joys, where the "taste" is of gnosis (maʿrifah), not of the palate.

- Root: شوق (Shawq — Yearning/Longing)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The root signifies the soul's restless inclination toward a beloved; the "spurring on" of the heart toward reunion.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Shawq is the movement of the heart toward its ultimate Beloved (al-maḥbūb al-aʿlā) — a yearning that persists even in bliss, for the unveiling (kashf) of ever-greater divine self-disclosure.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal for human longing; metaphorical for the divine "yearning" attributed to God (as in the sacred reports), which is an expression of His loving acceptance and bestowal of grace, not an emotional lack.

- Root: نور (Nūr — Light)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root denotes illumination, radiance, and that by which one sees and is seen.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Twofold: sensory light (of the sun, stars) and intellectual/spiritual light (of reason, faith, and the Qur'an). The "light of the believers" on the Day of Resurrection is the latter — the radiance of their faith and works in the world.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal for physical luminosity; metaphorical (majāz) for guidance, clarity, and the illuminating power of divine truth in the heart.

- Root: قلب (Qalb — Heart)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root means to turn over, to flip, to transform — hence the heart is so-named for its constant fluctuation (taqallub) of states.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The heart is the seat of perception and understanding (al-ʿaql wa al-fahm); it is the subtle divine reality (al-laṭīfah al-rabbāniyyah) that apprehends God, not the physical organ.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal for the physical organ; metaphorical for the spiritual faculty of cognition and volition that turns toward or away from God.

- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — Governing the precise scope of statements like "the pleasure of what is renewed is only a distraction from the ache of yearning," ensuring the predicate is confined to the subject without overextension.

61:6.arabic: ينادي أين الزهاد في الدنيا زوروا عرس الزاهد في الدنيا عيسى ابن مريم وقال عيسى ابن مريم عليه السلام ويل لصاحب الدنيا كيف يموت ويتركها وما فيها وتغره ويأمنها ويثق بها وتخذله وويل للمغترين كيف أرتهم ما يكرهون وفارقهم ما يحبون وجاءهم ما يوعدون وويل لمن الدنيا همه والخطايا عمله كيف يفتضح غدا بذنبه وقيل أوحى الله تعالى إلى موسى عليه السلام يا موسى مالك ولدار الظالمين إنها ليست لك بدار أخرج منها همك وفارقها بعقلك فبئست الدار هي إلا لعامل يعمل فيها فنعمت الدار هي يا موسى إني مرصد للظالم حتى آخذ منه للمظلوم وروي أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه و
61:6.english: And lightning appeared one day, and he began seeking something to which he might take refuge. His eye fell upon a tent from afar, so he approached it — and behold, there was a woman within it. So he turned aside from her, and then there was a cave in a mountain. He came to it — and behold, there was a lion within it. So he placed his hand upon it and said: "My God, Thou hast made for every thing a refuge, and Thou hast made for me no refuge." Then God — exalted be He — revealed to him: "Thy refuge is in the resting place of My mercy. I shall surely wed thee on the Day of Resurrection to a hundred houris whom I created with My own hand, and I shall surely feed thee at thy wedding-feast for four thousand years — each day of which is like the age of this world — and I shall surely command a herald to proclaim: 'Where are the ascetics of the world? Come visit the wedding-feast of the ascetic of the world, Jesus son of Mary.'"
61:6.section_title_en: The Revival of the Religious Sciences — Book on the Remembrance of Death: On the Merit of Renouncing the World (Section 732)

- Root: برق (b-r-q)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of shining, flashing, and appearing suddenly — from which "al-barq" (lightning) derives; also used for that which startles and alarms.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Used for sudden manifestation; here, the lightning serves as a natural sign prompting reflection on transience.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (haqiqah) for lightning; metaphorical (majaz) for the fleeting illumination of worldly life that vanishes instantly.
- Root: زهد (z-h-d)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To abstain from, to disdain, to regard as little; al-zuhd is the renunciation of something while it remains within one's power.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The theological virtue of renouncing the world (al-zuhd fi al-dunya) — not the mere abandonment of wealth, but the emptying of the heart from attachment to it.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: to turn away from a thing with aversion; metaphorical: the soul's disengagement from worldly allurements while the body remains present.
- Root: عرس (ʿ-r-s)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Wedding feast; the celebration of union; also used for the bridal chamber.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In the eschatological context, the "wedding" of the ascetic (al-zāhid) is a divine metaphor for the honor bestowed upon the renunciant in the Hereafter.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: a human marriage celebration; metaphorical: the spiritual recompense of intimacy with the Divine.
- Root: سخط (s-kh-t)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Displeasure, wrath, indignation; the opposite of ridā (satisfaction).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Divine displeasure (sakhat) as the cause of destruction; death by "wrath" (sakhtah) signifies a punishment visited upon a people for their disobedience.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: anger; metaphorical: the withdrawal of divine mercy and the sending of chastisement.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The permissibility of separating a prepositional phrase from its governed noun when the intervening element is semantically complete, as in the narrative transitions between reported speech and action.
