61:14.arabic: حرمك واعف عمن ظلمك // ورأيت في الإنجيل قال عيسى بن مريم عليه السلام لقد قيل لكم من قبل إن السن بالسن والأنف بالأنف وأنا أقول لكم لا تقاوموا بالشر بل من ضرب خدك الأيمن فحول إليه الخد الأيسر ومن أخذ رداءك فأعطه إزارك ومن سخرك لتسير معه ميلا فسر معه ميلين وكل ذلك أمر بالصبر على الأذى فالصبر على أذى الناس من أعلى مراتب الصبر لأنه يتعاون فيه باعث الدين وباعث الشهوة والغضب جميعا
61:14.english: And acts of disobedience are the requisite of the impulse of caprice (bāʿith al-hawā). And the most severe kind of patience is patience in abstaining from those acts of disobedience that have become familiar through habit — for habit is a fifth nature. When habit is joined to lustful desire, two battalions from the battalions of Satan array themselves in concert against the battalion of God (jund Allāh) — may He be exalted — and the impulse of religion (bāʿith al-dīn) has no strength to suppress them. Then, if that act be one whose commission has been rendered easy (tayassara), patience in abstaining from it is heavier upon the soul — such as patience in abstaining from the sins of the tongue: backbiting (ghībah), falsehood, contentious disputation (mirāʾ), self-praise whether by insinuation (taʿrīḍ) or by explicit statement (taṣrīḥ), the varieties of jesting that wound hearts, the kinds of words by which one intends belittlement and contempt, and the mention of the dead with aspersion cast upon them, upon their sciences, their conduct, and their stations. For such mention is in its outward aspect (fī ẓāhirihi) backbiting, and in its inward aspect (fī bāṭinihi) self-praise. In it the soul has two lusts: one is the negation of the other [person], and the other is the affirmation of oneself. And by these two together there is completed for it that lordship (rubūbiyyah) which is innate in its disposition — and which is the very opposite of what it has been commanded regarding servanthood (ʿubūdiyyah). And because of the conjunction of the two lusts, and the ease of moving the tongue, and the fact that this becomes habitual in everyday converse, patience in abstaining from it becomes difficult. And it is among the greatest of the destructive enormities (al-mūbiqāt) — so much so that its disapproval and ugliness have been effaced from hearts by dint of its frequent repetition and the universality of familiarity with it. Thus you see a man who would, for example, wear silk and deem it utterly remote [of permissibility], yet he unleashes his tongue the whole day long against the reputations (aʿrāḍ) of people and does not deem that objectionable — notwithstanding what has come down in the report that backbiting is more severe than adultery (zinā). And God — may He be exalted — said: {«ودع أذاهم وتوكل على الله»} "And leave aside their harm and put thy trust in God" (Q. 33:48). And He said — may He be exalted: {«واصبر على ما يقولون واهجرهم هجرا جميلا»} "And be patient over what they say, and depart from them with a gracious departure" (Q. 73:10). And He said — may He be exalted: {«ولقد نعلم أنك يضيق صدرك بما يقولون فسبح بحمد ربك»} "And indeed We know that thy breast is straitened by what they say; so glorify with the praise of thy Lord" (Q. 15:97–98) — to the end of the verse. And He said — may He be exalted: {«ولتسمعن من الذين أوتوا الكتاب من قبلكم ومن الذين أشركوا أذى كثيرا وإن تصبروا وتتقوا فإن ذلك من عزم الأمور»} "And you shall surely hear from those who were given the Scripture before you and from those who associate [others with God] much harm. And if you are patient and God-fearing, indeed that is of the resolute affairs" (Q. 3:186) — that is, that you be patient in refraining from requital (mukāfaʾah). And for this reason God — may He be exalted — praised those who pardon others their due rights in retaliation (qiṣāṣ) and otherwise, saying — may He be exalted: {«وإن عاقبتم فعاقبوا بمثل ما عوقبتم به ولئن صبرتم لهو خير الصابرين»} "And if you punish, then punish with the like of that wherewith you were afflicted. And if you are patient, it is surely better for the patient" (Q. 16:126). And he — upon him be peace — said: "Maintain the bond with him who cuts you off, and give to him who withholds from you, and pardon him who wrongs you." And I have seen in the Gospel that ʿĪsā ibn Maryam — upon him be peace — said: "It was said to you of old: an eye for an eye and a nose for a nose. But I say to you: do not resist evil. Rather, whoever strikes your right cheek, turn to him PageV04P071 the left cheek; and whoever takes your cloak, give him your garment; and whoever compels you to walk with him one mile, walk with him two miles." And all of that is a command to be patient under harm. So patience under the harm of people is among the highest stations of patience, because in it the impulse of religion and the impulse of lustful desire and anger are all arrayed together [against the soul].

61:14.arabic: وقد قال الله تعالى يا أيها الذين آمنوا أنفقوا من طيبات ما كسبتم ومما أخرجنا لكم من الأرض ولا تيمموا الخبيث منه تنفقون ولستم بآخذيه إلا أن تغمضوا فيه أي لا تأخذوه إلا مع كراهية وحياء وهو معنى الإغماض فلا تؤثروا به ربكم وفي الخبر سبق درهم مائة ألف درهم (3) وذلك بأن يخرجه الإنسان وهو من أحل ماله وأجوده فيصدر ذلك عن الرضا والفرح بالبذل وقد يخرج مائة ألف درهم مما يكره من ماله فيدل ذلك على أنه ليس يؤثر الله عز وجل بشيء مما يحبه وبذلك ذم الله تعالى قوما جعلوا لله ما يكرهون فقال تعال

And this condition among the conditions of almsgiving runs in the same course as humility (al-khushūʿ) runs in the prayer. There is no might and no power except through Allah, the Exalted, the Magnificent. And He said Most High: {«ألهاكم التكاثر»} — "Vying in increase diverts you."

  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: play/amusement. Metaphorical: any engrossing worldly pursuit that veils one from the Hereafter.
- Root: كثر (k-th-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Abundance, multitude, increase in number or quantity.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): *Takāthur* (vying in increase) is censured as the competitive accumulation of worldly goods for pride, not need.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: seeking more. Metaphorical: the obsessive race toward worldly accumulation that hardens the heart.
- Root: غبن (gh-b-n)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To cheat, defraud, or suffer loss in a transaction; to be outwitted.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In the Hereafter, *ghubn* is the ultimate loss — exchanging eternal bliss for fleeting worldly gain.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: commercial deception. Metaphorical: the soul's self-deception in preferring the ephemeral over the everlasting.
- Root: فتن (f-t-n)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Trial, tribulation, test; that which sifts the sincere from the insincere.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): *Fitnah* is a divine test through which the heart's attachment to worldly goods is exposed.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: burning in fire (as gold is refined). Metaphorical: wealth as a crucible for faith.

64:14.arabic: لا تلهكم أموالكم ولا أولادكم عن ذكر الله} وقال عز وجل {إن من أزواجكم وأولادكم عدوا لكم فاحذروهم} وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم الولد مبخلة مجبنة محزنة ولما نظر عليه السلام إلى ولده الحسن رضي الله عنه يتعثر في قميصه نزل عن المنبر واحتضنه ثم قال {صدق الله} إنما أموالكم وأولادكم فتنة إني لما رأيت ابني يتعثر لم أملك نفسي أن أخذته ففي ذلك عبرة لأولي الأبصار فالرجل كل الرجل من يصبر على العافية ومعنى الصبر عليها أن لا يركن إليها ويعلم أن كل ذلك مستودع عنده وعسى أن يسترجع على القرب وأن لا يرسل نفسه في الفرح بها ولا ينهمك في التنعم واللذة واللهو واللعب وأن
64:14.english: The first kind is that which accords with caprice (al-hawā) — namely, sound health and well-being, wealth and status, the abundance of kinsfolk, the expanse of means, the multitude of followers and helpers, and all the pleasures of this world. How greatly the servant stands in need of patience over these very things! For if he does not restrain his soul (nafsahu) from letting loose toward them, from reposing in them, and from plunging into their permissible pleasures, that drives him to insolence (al-baṭar) and transgression (al-ṭughyān) — for indeed {verily man doth transgress when he sees himself self-sufficient} {«إن الإنسان ليطغى أن رآه استغنى»}. Hence one of the knowers of God (al-ʿārifīn) said: "Affliction — the believer can bear it; but well-being — none bears it save the veracious (al-ṣiddīq)." And Sahl said: "Patience over well-being is more severe than patience over affliction." When the doors of this world were opened upon the Companions — may God be well pleased with them — they said: "We were tried with the trial of adversity (fitnat al-ḍarrāʾ) and we bore it patiently; and we were tried with the trial of prosperity (fitnat al-sarrāʾ) and we did not bear it patiently." For this reason God — mighty and majestic — warned His servants against the trial of wealth, spouse, and child, saying — exalted is He: {O you who believe! Let not your wealth nor your children divert you from the remembrance of God} {«يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا تلهكم أموالكم ولا أولادكم عن ذكر الله»}. And He said — mighty and majestic: {Indeed, among your spouses and your children there is an enemy unto you, so beware of them} {«إن من أزواجكم وأولادكم عدوا لكم فاحذروهم»}. And the Prophet — peace be upon him — said: "The child is a cause of miserliness (mubakhkhilah), a cause of cowardice (mujabinah), a cause of grief (muḥzinah)." When he — peace be upon him — looked upon his son al-Ḥasan — may God be well pleased with him — stumbling in his shirt, he descended from the pulpit and embraced him, then said: {God has spoken truly} {«صدق الله»} — {Indeed, your wealth and your children are a trial} {«إنما أموالكم وأولادكم فتنة»} — "When I saw my son stumbling, I could not control myself (lam amlik nafsī) from taking him up." In that is a lesson for those of insight. So the man — the complete man — is he who bears patience over well-being. And the meaning of patience over it is that he does not repose in it, and knows that all of it is but a trust (mustawdaʿ) deposited with him, that it may well be reclaimed at any near moment; and that he does not release his soul to rejoice in it, nor plunge into comfort, pleasure, play, and amusement; and that he observes the rights of God in his wealth by spending, in his body by expending aid to creation, in his tongue by expending truthfulness (al-ṣidq) — and likewise in all the rest of what God has bestowed upon him.
64:14.section_title_en: On Patience in Prosperity and Adversity — Section 963
64:14.anchors:
- Root: صبر (ṣ-b-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of restraint and holding back; al-Farahidi notes "صبر على قليه" (endurance upon hardship).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الصبر: الإمساك في ضيق... حبس النفس على ما يقتضيه العقل والشرع، أو عما يقتضيان حبسها عنه" — Patience is the soul's restraint upon what reason and Law require, or from what they require restraining it; its names vary by context (shajāʿah in battle, etc.).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): "صبرت على ما أكره. وصبرت عما أحب" — patience over the disliked and patience away from the beloved. Metaphorical (majāz): "هو أصبر على الضرب من الأرض" — extreme endurance likened to earth's impassivity.
- Root: نفس (n-f-s)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The self, soul, or spirit; that which one guards and restrains.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "النفس: الروح" and in divine attribution, "نفسه: ذاته" — the self as the locus of volition and desire.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "نفس" as the animate self; metaphorical: "دفق نفسه أي دمه" — extended to blood/life.
- Root: ولد (w-l-d)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Offspring, child; al-Farahidi notes singular/plural usage.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الولد: المولود. يقال للواحد والجمع والصغير والكبير" — child, born one, applied to one or many, young or old.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: biological progeny; metaphorical (majāz): "ولدوا حديثا وكلاما: استحدثوه" — newly invented speech; here, children as a trial.
- Root: صدق (ṣ-d-q)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Truthfulness; al-Farahidi links it to earnestness in word and deed.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الصدق والكذب أصلهما في القول" — truth and falsehood originate in speech, but extend to action and intention.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: truthful speech; metaphorical: "رجل صادق الحملة" — one whose charge in battle is true/earnest.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — "إنما" restricts the predicate exclusively to the subject, as in the prophetic citation {إنما أموالكم وأولادكم فتنة}, affirming trial as the sole designated function of wealth and children.

  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): *Takāthur* (vying in increase) is censured as the competitive accumulation of worldly goods for pride, not need.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: seeking more. Metaphorical: the obsessive race toward worldly accumulation that hardens the heart.
- Root: غبن (gh-b-n)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To cheat, defraud, or suffer loss in a transaction; to be outwitted.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In the Hereafter, *ghubn* is the ultimate loss — exchanging eternal bliss for fleeting worldly gain.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: commercial deception. Metaphorical: the soul's self-deception in preferring the ephemeral over the everlasting.
- Root: فتن (f-t-n)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Trial, tribulation, test; that which sifts the sincere from the insincere.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): *Fitnah* is a divine test through which the heart's attachment to worldly goods is exposed.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: burning in fire (as gold is refined). Metaphorical: wealth as a crucible for faith.
- Sibawayh Rule: Restriction and Focused Predication (*Bāb al-Ḥaṣr wa al-Taqyīd bi-innamā*) — The particle *innamā* in {«إنما أموالكم وأولادكم فتنة»} restricts the predicate, affirming that wealth and children are solely a trial, not an end in themselves.
64:15.topic: Al-Ghazali on purifying the character, moral diseases, and spiritual remedies, from 'Condemnation of Miserliness and Love of Wealth'

64:15.arabic: وتعثر الحسن والنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم على منبره فنزل فحمله وقرأ قوله {إنما أموالكم وأولادكم فتنة} (3) وقال عبد الله بن شداد بينما رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يصلي بالناس إذ جاءه الحسين فركب عنقه وهو ساجد فأطال السجود بالناس حتى ظنوا أنه قد حدث أمر فلما قضى صلاته قالوا قد أطلت السجود يا رسول الله حتى ظننا أنه قد حدث أمر فقال إن ابني قد ارتحلني فكرهت أن أعجله حتى يقضي حاجته (4) وفي ذلك فوائد إحداها القرب من الله تعالى فإن العبد أقرب ما يكون من الله تعالى إذا كان ساجدا وفيه الرفق بالولد والبر وتعليم لأمته وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم ريح الو
64:15.english: The Prophet, peace be upon him, said: "A child will never repay his father until he finds him a slave, buys him, and sets him free."
64:15.section_title_en: The Book of the Revival of the Religious Sciences — Section 439: On the Rights of Parents and Children
64:15.anchors:
- Root: ولد (w-l-d)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To give birth, beget, produce; offspring, child, progeny.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-walad denotes the begotten, singular or plural, young or old; also used for an adopted child. The root signifies the direct causal link of generation.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) for physical birth and kinship. Metaphorical (majāz) for "newly invented speech" (kalām muwallad) — but here, strictly literal.
- Root: بر (b-r-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Piety, dutifulness, kindness, gentleness; antonym of ʿuqūq (disobedience, severance).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Birr is expansive goodness that connects the servant to God and creation; its opposite is ʿuqūq, the cutting of what God has commanded to be joined.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal for filial piety and charitable excellence.
- Root: رحم (r-ḥ-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The womb; kinship, blood-tie; mercy, compassion.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Raḥim is the organ of gestation, and raḥmah is the mercy that God apportions; the kin-tie (raḥim) is so named because it demands mutual mercy.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal for the womb and blood-relations; metaphorical for mercy as its spiritual fruit.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Restriction and Focused Predication (Bāb al-Ḥaṣr wa al-Taqyīd bi-innamā) — governing the exclusive force of statements like {«إنما أموالكم وأولادكم فتنة»}, where the predicate is restricted to the subject alone.
64:15.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

65:1.arabic: باختلاف الأحوال والأشخاص فيكون الحد ضروريا فلذلك قال الله تعالى {ومن يتعد حدود الله فقد ظلم نفسه} ولأن أصول هذه المعاني لا تختلف فيها الشرائع وإنما تختلف في وجوه التحديد كما يحد شرع عيسى ابن مريم عليه السلام تحريم الخمر بالسكر وقد حده شرعنا بكونه من جنس المسكر لأن قليله يدعو إلى كثير والداخل في الحدود داخل في التحريم بحكم الجنس كما دخل أصل المعنى بالجملة الأصلية فهذا مثال واحد لحكمة خفية من حكم النقدين فينبغي أن يعتبر شكر النعمة وكفرانها بهذا المثال فكل ما خلق لحكمة فينبغي أن يصرف عنها ولا يعرف هذا إلا من قد عرف الحكمة {ومن يؤت الحكمة فقد أوتى
65:1.english: He does not eat it if he is in need, nor does he make it a commodity of trade. But if he makes it a commodity of trade, let him sell it to one who seeks it in exchange for something other than food, being in need of that other thing. As for one who seeks it in exchange for that very same food, he too is independent of it. For this reason, the curse upon the hoarder (muḥtakir) has come down in the Sacred Law, and therein are the severities we have mentioned in the Book of the Etiquettes of Earning. Yes, the seller of wheat for dates is excused, for neither one of them takes the place of the other in the intended purpose. But the seller of a ṣāʿ of wheat for a ṣāʿ of the same wheat is not excused; rather, he is a trifler, and thus needs no prohibition, for souls do not permit it except when there is disparity in quality—and the owner of the good quality will not be satisfied with matching his good [grain] with its like of the inferior. As for good [grain] in exchange for two inferior ones, that may indeed be intended. But since foods are among the necessities, and the good equals the inferior in the fundamental benefit while differing from it in aspects of luxury, the Sacred Law dropped the aim of luxury in what is the very staff of life. Such is the wisdom of the Sacred Law in prohibiting usury (ribā). And this has become unveiled to us after turning away from the art of jurisprudence (fiqh). Let us, then, annex this to the art of juristic matters, for it is more fitting than all that we have adduced in the controversial questions. And by this, the preponderance of the school of al-Shāfiʿī—may Allah have mercy on him—becomes clear in specifying foods rather than measured commodities (makīlāt); for were gypsum (jiss) to enter into it, then garments and beasts would be even more deserving of entry. And were it not for salt, the school of Mālik—may Allah have mercy on him—would be the most upright of schools therein, for he specified it by the staple foods (aqwāt). But every meaning that the Sacred Law observes must be delimited by a boundary and a definition. This was possible by the staple food (qūt) and possible by the edible (maṭʿūm). So the Sacred Law deemed the specification by the genus of the edible more fitting for everything that is the necessity of survival. And the specifications of the Sacred Law may encompass peripheral edges where the root meaning impelling the ruling has no force, yet the specification occurs thus by necessity. For were it not delimited, creation would be bewildered in following the very essence of the meaning, given its variation with circumstances and persons. For the meaning, in the fullness of its force, varies with circumstances and persons, and thus the limit becomes necessary. Therefore, Allah—exalted is He—said: {«And whosoever transgresses the limits of Allah has indeed wronged his own soul»} (Q 65:1). And because the roots of these meanings do not differ across the Sacred Laws; they differ only in the modes of specification. Just as the law of Jesus son of Mary—peace be upon him—delimited the prohibition of wine by intoxication, while our law has delimited it by being of the genus of the intoxicant, because its small amount invites to its large amount. And what enters within the limits enters into the prohibition by virtue of the genus, just as the root meaning entered by the primary totality. This, then, is a single example of a hidden wisdom among the wisdoms of the two precious metals (naqdayn). One ought to weigh gratitude for the blessing and ingratitude against it by this example. For everything created for a wisdom ought not to be diverted from it—and none knows this save one who has known the wisdom. {«And whosoever is given wisdom has indeed been given abundant good»} (Q 2:269). But the jewels of wisdom do not alight upon hearts that are dunghills of lusts and playgrounds of devils. Rather, none remembers save those possessed of minds. Therefore, he—peace and blessings be upon him—said: "Were it not that the devils hover about the hearts of the sons of Adam, they would behold the kingdom of the heavens." And when you have known this example, then measure upon it your movement and your stillness, your speech and your silence, and every act issuing from you—for it is either gratitude or ingratitude, since it is inconceivable that it be free of both. Some of that we describe in the tongue of jurisprudence, which the common folk articulate, as "disliked" (makrūh), and some as "perilous" (khaṭar). But all of that, with the people of hearts, is described as perilous. So I say, for instance: If you cleansed yourself with the right hand, you have been ungrateful for the blessing of the two hands. For Allah created for you the two hands and made one of them stronger than the other. The stronger one, by its greater preponderance in most cases, deserves honor and preference. And preferring the deficient is a deviation from justice—and Allah does not command injustice. Then He who gave you the hands made you needful of acts, some of which are noble, like taking the Muṣḥaf, and some base, like removing filth. So if you take the Muṣḥaf with the left hand and remove filth with the right, you have singled out the noble for what is base, thereby diminishing its due, wronging it, and deviating from justice. Likewise, if you spat, for instance, toward the direction of the Qiblah, or faced it in relieving yourself, you have been ungrateful for the blessing of Allah—exalted is He—in the creation of the directions and the creation of the world's expanse. For He created the directions to be your expanse in movement, and He divided the directions into those He did not honor and those He honored, by placing therein a House He attributed to Himself, as an inclination [toward His servants].
65:1.section_title_en: The Wisdom Behind the Prohibition of Usury (Ribā) and the Principle of Proportional Gratitude for Divine Blessings
65:1.anchors:
- Root: طعم (ṭaʿima)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning pertains to tasting, flavor, and by extension that which is eaten—food as sustenance.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In theological usage, al-ṭaʿām denotes the essential nutriment preserving life (qūt), distinguished from mere luxury; the Sharīʿah's specification by "food" (ṭaʿām) rather than "measured commodities" (makīlāt) reflects a divine intent tied to necessity, not convention.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) sense is edible substance; metaphorical (majāz) extension applies to what "nourishes" a purpose, e.g., a legal cause (ʿillah) sustaining a ruling.
- Root: حدد (ḥaddada)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To set a boundary, define a limit, or fix a precise measure; al-ḥadd is the terminal edge separating one thing from another.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In Kalam, ḥudūd are the formal definitions and boundaries set by divine command; they may encompass peripheral cases where the underlying rationale (maʿnā) alone cannot determine the judgment, necessitating a fixed limit for practical guidance.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical demarcation (e.g., land boundaries); metaphorical: legal specification (takhṣīṣ) by the Lawgiver, where the limit is a divine convention (tawqīf) beyond pure rational analogy.
- Root: كفر (kafara)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To cover, conceal, or deny; also to be ungrateful for a benefit.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Kufrān (ingratitude) is the antithesis of shukr (gratitude); it entails misusing a blessing against its intended purpose, thereby "covering" the divine beneficence.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: covering a seed with earth; metaphorical: veiling the soul from recognizing and honoring the Giver by diverting His gifts from their ordained ends.
- Root: شكر (shakara)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To acknowledge a favor and respond with praise or appropriate action.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): True gratitude (shukr) is the soul's recognition of the blessing, the heart's delight in the Giver, and the bodily members' employment of the gift in obedience to its purpose.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: praise for a benefit; metaphorical: the actual "spending" of a blessing in its rightful place, as the tongue's thanks is but a token of the limb's due.
- Sibawayh Rule: Bāb al-Ḥaṣr wa al-Taqyīd bi-innamā (Restriction and Specification with "innamā") — Used to confine a predicate to a subject, here restricting the legal cause of ribā to foodstuffs, and the principle of gratitude to every act, whether motion or stillness.
65:1.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

65:1.arabic: قال ابن مسعود في قوله تعالى {ولا يخرجن إلا أن يأتين بفاحشة مبينة} مهما بذت على أهله وآذت زوجها فهو فاحشة وهذا أريد به في العدة ولكنه تنبيه على المقصود وإن كان الأذى من الزوج فلها أن تفتدي ببذل مال يكره للرجل أن يأخذ منها أكثر مما أعطى فإن ذلك إجحاف بها وتحامل عليها وتجارة على البضع قال تعالى {فلا جناح عليهما فيما افتدت به} فرد ما أخذته فما دونه لائق بالفداء فإن سألت الطلاق بغير ما بأس فهي آثمة قال صلى الله عليه وسلم أيما امرأة سألت زوجها طلاقها من غير ما بأس لم ترح رائحة الجنة (3) وفي لفظ آخر فالجنة عليها
65:1.english: **The third:** Fear of excessive hardship (ḥaraj) due to the multitude of children, and guarding against the need for toil in earning a livelihood and entering into evil means of acquisition. This also is not prohibited, for the paucity of hardship assists one in religion. Indeed, perfection and excellence lie in trust in God (tawakkul) and confidence in God's guarantee, where He said: {«وما من دابة في الأرض إلا على الله رزقها»} "And there is no creature on earth but that upon Allah is its provision" [Hūd: 6]. Without doubt, in this [trust] there is a falling from the summit of perfection and an abandonment of what is more excellent — but looking to consequences and preserving wealth and storing it up, despite its contradicting tawakkul, we do not say it is prohibited.

- Root: عزل (ʿazl)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Separation, removal, setting aside
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Withdrawal to prevent conception
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical separation; Metaphorical: preventing pregnancy

66:6.arabic: حملة العرش ينتظرون منهم ما ينزل عليهم من الأمر من حضرة الربوبية كي لا يعصوا الله ما أمرهم ويفعلون ما يؤمرون وعبر عن هذه المشاهدات في القرآن وقيل {وفي السماء رزقكم وما توعدون} وعبر عن انتظار ملائكة السموات لما ينزل إليهم من القدر والأمر فقيل خلق سبع سموات ومن الأرض مثلهن يتنزل الأمر بينهن لتعلموا أن الله على كل شيء قدير وأن الله قد أحاط بكل شيء علما وهذه أمور لا يعلم تأويلها إلا الله والراسخون في العلم وعبر ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما عن اختصاص الراسخين في العلم بعلوم لا تحتملها أفهام الخلق حيث قرأ قوله تعالى {يتنزل الأمر بينهن} فقال لو ذكرت ما أعرفه من مع
66:6.english: Thus was the beginning of this matter and its end. And do not understand it unless you are worthy of it. And if you are worthy of it, the eye is opened and you see, so you have no need of a leader to lead you. The blind man can indeed be led, but only to a limit. For when the path narrows and becomes sharper than a sword and finer than a hair, the bird is able to fly over it but is not able to drag a blind man behind it. And when the field becomes narrow and subtle — subtle as water, for example — and crossing is possible only by swimming, then the one skilled in the art of swimming may be able to cross by himself, and perhaps he is not able to drag another behind him. These matters bear the same relation to walking upon the way of the common masses of creatures as walking upon water bears to walking upon earth. Swimming can be learned; but as for walking upon water, it is not acquired by instruction, but rather is attained through the strength of certainty (yaqīn). For this reason it was said to the Prophet, peace be upon him, that Jesus, peace be upon him, was said to have walked upon water, and he, peace be upon him, said: "Had his certainty increased, he would have walked upon the air." {«حديث قيل له يقال إن عيسى مشى على الماء قال لو ازداد يقينا لمشي على الهواء»} — This hadith is rejected (munkar) and is not known in this form. What is known is what Ibn Abi al-Dunya narrated in the Book of Certainty from the saying of Bakr ibn Abd Allah al-Muzani, who said: The disciples lost their Prophet, and it was said to them: "He has headed toward the sea." So they set out seeking him, and when they reached the sea, behold, he was coming toward them walking upon the water. And he mentioned a hadith in which Jesus said: "If the son of Adam had a hair's breadth of certainty, he would walk upon the water." And Abu Mansur al-Daylami narrated in the Musnad al-Firdaws with a weak chain from the hadith of Muadh ibn Jabal: "If you knew God with true knowledge, you would walk upon the seas, and the mountains would be removed by your supplications." These are symbols and allusions to the meaning of aversion (karāhah) and love (maḥabbah), and good pleasure (riḍā) and wrath (ghaḍab), and gratitude (shukr) and ingratitude (kufrān) — more than this is not fitting for the science of practical conduct (ʿilm al-muʿāmalah). And God, exalted be He, struck an example of this to draw it near to the understanding of creatures, since He knew that He created the jinn and mankind only to worship Him, and their worship was the ultimate purpose of wisdom (ghāyat al-ḥikmah) with respect to them. Then He informed that He has two servants: one whom He loves, whose name is Gabriel — the Holy Spirit and the Trustworthy One — and he is with Him beloved, obeyed, trustworthy, and honored; and another whom He hates, whose name is Iblis — the accursed one, reprieved until the Day of Judgment. Then He delegated guidance (irshād) to Gabriel, saying, the Exalted: {«قل نزله روح القدس من ربك بالحق»} "Say: The Holy Spirit has brought it down from your Lord with truth" (16:102), and said, the Exalted: {«يلقي الروح من أمره على من يشاء من عباده»} "He casts the Spirit of His command upon whom He wills of His servants" (40:15). And He delegated misguidance (ighwāʾ) to Iblis, saying, the Exalted: {«ليضل عن سبيله»} "That he may lead astray from His path" (4:119). And ighwāʾ is the halting of servants short of attaining the ultimate purpose of wisdom. So observe how He attributed it to the servant with whom He was wrathful; and guidance (irshād) is the conduct of them toward the ultimate purpose — so observe how He attributed it to the servant whom He loves. And you have an example of this in custom: when a king is in need of one to give him drink and one to cup him and to clean the courtyard of his house of filth, and he has two servants, he does not appoint for cupping and cleaning except the ugliest and meanest of them, and he does not entrust the carrying of drink and perfume except to the best and most complete of them and the most beloved to him. And you should not say: "This is my act, and his act was not without my act" — for you have erred when you attributed that to yourself. Rather, He is the One who directed your motive (dāʿiyah) to the specification of the disliked act to the disliked person, and the beloved act to the beloved person, as a completion of justice (ʿadl). For His justice is sometimes completed through matters in which you have no entry, and sometimes it is completed in you — for you also are among His acts. So your motive, your power, your knowledge, your action, and all the other causes of your movements in expression — all of this is His act, which He arranged with justice in an arrangement from which moderate acts issue forth. Except that you see only yourself, and so you suppose that what appears through you in the world of witness (ʿālam al-shahādah) has no cause from the world of the unseen and the dominion (ʿālam al-ghayb wa al-malakūt). Therefore you attribute it to yourself. And you are only like the child who looks at night at the play of the juggler (mushʿabadh) who brings forth figures from behind a curtain that dance and scream and rise and sit, composed of rags that do not move by themselves — rather, they are moved by fine hair-like threads that do not appear in the darkness of night, their ends in the hand of the juggler, who is hidden from the eyes of the children. So they rejoice and marvel, supposing that those rags dance and play and rise and sit. As for the intelligent ones, they know that this is a moving (taḥrīk) and not a self-movement, but perhaps they do not know its detailed modality. And the one who knows some of its detail does not know it as the juggler knows it, to whom the command belongs and in whose hand is the pulling. Likewise, the children of the people of this world — and all creatures are children relative to the scholars — look at these persons (ashkhāṣ) and suppose that they are the movers, and so they attribute [action] to them. And the scholars know that they are moved, except that they do not know the modality of the moving — and they are the majority. Except the knowers (ʿārifūn), the scholars, and those firmly rooted in knowledge (al-rāsikhūn), for they have perceived, with the sharpness of their sight, fine spider-web threads — nay, much finer than these — suspended from heaven, their ends attached to the persons of the people of the earth. Those threads are not perceived, due to their fineness, by these outward eyes. Then they witnessed the heads of those threads in their suspension-points (manāṭāt) to which they are attached, and they witnessed for those suspension-points handles (maqābiḍ) that are in the hands of the angels who move the heavens. And they also witnessed the angels of the heavens directed toward the bearers of the Throne (ḥamalat al-ʿarsh), awaiting what descends upon them of the command from the presence of Lordship (ḥaḍrat al-rubūbiyyah) — "they do not disobey God in what He commands them, and they do what they are commanded" (66:6). And He expressed these witnessed realities in the Qur'an, and it was said: {«وفي السماء رزقكم وما توعدون»} "And in the heaven is your provision and what you are promised" (51:22). And He expressed the waiting of the angels of the heavens for what descends upon them of decree and command, and it was said: "He created seven heavens and of the earth the like of them; {«يتنزل الأمر بينهن لتعلموا أن الله على كل شيء قدير وأن الله قد أحاط بكل شيء علما»} 'the command descends between them, that you may know that God is powerful over all things and that God encompasses all things in knowledge'" (65:12). These are matters whose interpretation (taʾwīl) none knows except God and those firmly rooted in knowledge (al-rāsikhūn fī al-ʿilm). And Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, expressed the exclusivity of those firmly rooted in knowledge to sciences that the understandings of creatures cannot bear, when he recited the saying of the Exalted: {«يتنزل الأمر بينهن»} "The command descends between them," and said: "Were I to mention what I know of the meaning of this verse, you would stone me" — and in another wording: "You would say he is an unbeliever."
66:6.section_title_en: On the Degrees of Proximity to God and the Hierarchy of Those Who Perfect Divine Wisdom
66:6.anchors:
- Root: سير (s-y-r)

- Root: مشي (m-sh-y)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "المشي: تردد الأركان على الأرض، والماشية: الإبل والغنم لانتقالها في المرعى"
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "المشي: الانتقال من مكان إلى مكان بإرادة، ويكنى به عن النميمة، وعن شرب المسهل"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): [Literal] "مشيت وتمشيت، وهي حسنة المشية" — [Metaphorical] "مشى بطنه، وأمشاه الدواء، واستمشيت بالدواء، ومنه: مشت المرأة: كثرت أولادها"
- Root: خلق (kh-l-q)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الخلق: التقدير، والخلق: الناس، والخليقة: الطبيعة، والخلق: السجية"
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الخلق أصله: التقدير المستقيم، ويستعمل في إبداع الشيء من غير أصل ولا احتذاء"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): [Literal] "خلق الخراز الأديم: قدره قبل القطع" — [Metaphorical] "خلق الله الخلق: أوجده على تقدير أوجبته الحكمة"
- Root: نفس (n-f-s)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "النفس: الروح، والذات، والشيء النفيس"
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "النفس: الروح، وتطلق على الذات، قال تعالى: {ويحذركم الله نفسه} فنفسه: ذاته"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): [Literal] "شيء نفيس ومنفس" — [Metaphorical] "دفق نفسه أي دمه، وأصابته نفس: عين"
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — Used to distinguish exclusive attribution of actions to God versus creatures, as in "إنما أنت مثل الصبي" (You are only like a child), restricting the simile to the creature while preserving divine agency.
66:6.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications, prayers, and their spiritual power, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

66:6.arabic: هارب فقد قال تعالى {قوا أنفسكم وأهليكم نارا} أمرنا أن نقيهم النار كما نقي أنفسنا والإنسان قد يعجز عن القيام بحق نفسه وإذا تزوج تضاعف عليه الحق وانضافت إلى نفسه نفس أخرى والنفس أمارة بالسوء إن كثرت عليها الحقوق كثر الأمر بالسوء غالبا ولذلك اعتذر بعضهم من التزويج وقال أنا مبتلي بنفسي وكيف أضيف إليها نفسا أخرى كما قيل لن يسع الفأرة جحرها .
66:6.english: It is related that one who flees from his dependents (ʿiyāl) is in the station of the runaway slave (al-ʿabd al-ābiq) — no prayer of his is accepted, nor any fasting, until he returns to them. And one who falls short in fulfilling their rights (ḥuqūq) — even while remaining present among them — is in the station of the fugitive. For God Most High has said: {«قوا أنفسكم وأهليكم نارا»} "Guard yourselves and your families from a Fire" [Q. 66:6]. We are commanded to shield them from the Fire just as we shield ourselves. Yet a man may well be incapable of fulfilling the right due upon him toward his own self — and when he marries, the obligation upon him is doubled, and to his own self (nafs) is joined another self. Now the self is ever commanding toward evil (al-nafs ammāratun bi'l-sūʾ) [Q. 12:53] — when rights multiply upon it, the command toward evil multiplies in like measure, generally speaking. For this reason, some among them excused themselves from marriage, saying: "I am already afflicted with my own self — how then shall I add to it another self?" As was said:
66:6.section_title_en: The Third Impediment to Marriage: Occupation of Heart by Family and Children, and the Weighing of Benefits Against Harms
66:6.anchors:
- Root: ع-ي-ل (ʿ-y-l)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of dependence, those whom one must support (family/dependents); "عَالَ" signifies to burden oneself with maintenance of others.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In theological context, ʿiyāl denotes those entrusted to one's care, whose maintenance is a religious obligation (nafaqah), linking worldly provision to eschatological accountability.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) usage refers to actual dependents requiring material support; metaphorical (majāz) extension applies to spiritual "dependents" — the soul's inclinations that require governance.
- Root: ش-غ-ل (sh-gh-l)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To occupy, engross, divert; core sense of something that fills attention and prevents other concerns.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In Kalam, shughl (occupation) is contrasted with tafarrugh (being free/unoccupied) — the latter being prerequisite for contemplation (tafakkur) and preparation for the afterlife.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical occupation with tasks; Metaphorical: the heart's engrossment (ishtighāl al-qalb) with worldly concerns, which is the true impediment to spiritual devotion.
- Root: ز-و-ج (z-w-j)
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Each of a pair; in marriage, the coupling of two souls multiplies obligations — the husband's self (nafs) is joined by another self requiring rights (ḥuqūq).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the marital pair; Metaphorical: tazāwuj of concerns — how worldly cares "pair" and multiply upon the heart through marriage.
- Root: و-ز-ن (w-z-n)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To weigh, measure, balance; the act of determining preponderance.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In ethical judgment, mīzān (balance) is the instrument of equitable assessment — weighing spiritual benefit (manfaʿah dīniyyah) against harm (mafsadah).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical weighing; Metaphorical: al-mīzān al-qisṭ (the just balance) — the rational faculty's discernment in weighing competing religious considerations.
- Sibawayh Rule: Bāb al-ʿaṭf ʿalā al-sabab (Coordination on Causal Grounds) — The construction "فإن انتفت في حقه الآفات واجتمعت الفوائد" employs conditional coordination where the protasis (condition) governs multiple apodoses, requiring precise parsing of the logical relationship between the conditions and their consequent judgments.
66:6.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications, prayers, and their spiritual power, from 'Etiquette of Marriage'

66:6.arabic: وقد قال الله تعالى يا أيها الذين آمنوا أنفقوا من طيبات ما كسبتم ومما أخرجنا لكم من الأرض ولا تيمموا الخبيث منه تنفقون ولستم بآخذيه إلا أن تغمضوا فيه أي لا تأخذوه إلا مع كراهية وحياء وهو معنى الإغماض فلا تؤثروا به ربكم وفي الخبر سبق درهم مائة ألف درهم (3) وذلك بأن يخرجه الإنسان وهو من أحل ماله وأجوده فيصدر ذلك عن الرضا والفرح بالبذل وقد يخرج مائة ألف درهم مما يكره من ماله فيدل ذلك على أنه ليس يؤثر الله عز وجل بشيء مما يحبه وبذلك ذم الله تعالى قوما جعلوا لله ما يكرهون فقال تعال
66:6.english: The heart is not treated save with the compound electuary (maʿjūn) of knowledge and works. And this condition among the conditions of almsgiving runs in the same course as humility (al-khushūʿ) runs in the prayer. This is established by his saying — may Allah bless him and grant him peace: "A man has nothing of his prayer save that of which he was conscious." And this is like his saying — may Allah bless him and grant him peace: "Allah does not accept the charity of the one who bestows it with reproach (al-mannān)." And like His saying — Exalted is He: {«لا تبطلوا صدقاتكم بالمن والأذى»} ("Do not nullify your charities by reproach and injury"). As for the legal opinion (fatwā) of the jurist that the alms fall in their proper place and that one's liability is discharged without this condition — that is another discussion, and we have already pointed to its meaning in the Book of Prayer.
66:6.section_title_en: The Inner Conditions of Charity — Section 175 (From The Revival of the Religious Sciences, Book of the Mysteries of Almsgiving)
66:6.anchors:
- Root: قلب (q-l-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "To turn, overturn, transform a thing from one state to another; to rotate, to flip"
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "قلب الشيء: تصريفه وصرفه عن وجه إلى وجه" — the heart is so named because of its constant turning and transformation between states
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "قلب الشيء قلبا: حوله عن وجهه" (to turn a thing from its face). Metaphorical: "رجل قلب حول: يقلب الأمور ويحتال" — one who turns matters over and manages them; "قلبوا لك الأمور" (they turned matters against you)
- Root: وجل (w-j-l)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "Fear, dread, apprehension that strikes the heart"
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الوجل: استشعار الخوف" — the sensing of fear; cited in {«إنما المؤمنون الذين إذا ذكر الله وجلت قلوبهم»}
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "رجل وجل، وقوم وجال" — a fearful man, a fearful people; "وفي قلبه وجل" — in his heart is dread
- Root: عجب (ʿ-j-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "Wonder, amazement; self-admiration, vanity"
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Self-admiration (al-ʿujb) is a destructive spiritual ailment that nullifies deeds
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: wonder at something extraordinary. Metaphorical: self-conceit regarding one's own acts of obedience
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد (Restriction & Focused Predication) — governing the precise limitation of general categories (al-ṣifāt al-khāṣṣah within al-aṣnāf al-thamāniyyah) and the conditional structure of acceptance

##
66:6.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Duties of Brotherhood'

66:6.arabic: فإنهم مجبولون على الطاعة لا يستطيعون له خلافا بل لا يعصون الله ما أمرهم ويفعلون ما يؤمرون وإنما يفترقان في شيء وهو أن الملائكة عليهم السلام عالمة بطاعتها وامتثالها والأجفان تطيع القلب في الانفتاح والإنطباق على سبيل التسخير ولا خبر لها من نفسها ومن طاعتها للقلب وإنما افتقر القلب إلى هذه الجنود من حيث افتقاره إلى المركب والزاد لسفره الذي لأجله خلق وهو السفر إلى الله سبحانه وقطع المنازل إلى لقائه فلأجله خلقت القلوب قال الله تعالى وما خلقت الجن والإنس إلا ليعبدون وإنما مركبه البدن وزاده العلم وإنما الأسباب التي توصله إلى الزاد وتمكن
66:6.english: God — Exalted is He — said: {«وَمَا يَعْلَمُ جُنُودَ رَبِّكَ إِلَّا هُوَ»} (Q 74:31) — "And none knows the armies of your Lord except Him." Thus, for God — Glorified is He — within hearts, spirits, and other realms, there are marshaled armies (junūd mujannadah) whose true reality and detailed enumeration none knows except Him alone. And we now shall indicate some of the armies of the heart — for it is that which pertains to our purpose.
66:6.section_title_en: Exposition of the Armies of the Heart
66:6.anchors:
- Root: جند (j-n-d)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "جند: العسكر، والأرض الغليظة التي فيها حجارة" — the core meaning denotes both a gathered military host and rough, stony ground, implying hardness, strength, and collective force.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "يقال للعسكر الجند اعتبارا بالغلظة، من الجند، أي: الأرض الغليظة التي فيها حجارة ثم يقال لكل مجتمع جند" — the term extends from physical ruggedness to any gathered collective serving a purpose, including spiritual hosts.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "الأرواح جنود مجندة، والريح من جنود الله تعالى" — used both literally (military hosts) and metaphorically (spiritual forces, natural phenomena as divine armies).
- Root: قلب (q-l-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "قلب الشيء: تصريفه وصرفه عن وجه إلى وجه" — the heart is so named for its constant turning, flipping, and oscillation between states.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "قلب الشيء: تصريفه وصرفه عن وجه إلى وجه، كقلب الثوب، وقلب الإنسان" — the heart's essence is its capacity for transformation and redirection.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas - Majaz): "رجل قلب حول: يقلب الأمور ويحتال" — metaphorically, the heart is the seat of deliberation, discernment, and spiritual governance.
- Root: نزل (n-z-l)
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "النزول في الأصل هو انحطاط من علو" — descent from a height; used for divine sending down of revelation and spiritual realities.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas - Majaz): "نزل به مكروه، وأصابته نازلة من نوازل الدهر" — metaphorically, events "descend" upon one; the heart is a station where divine armies "descend" or are stationed.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد (Restriction & Focused Predication) — governing the exclusive attribution of knowledge of the divine armies to God alone through the restrictive particle "إلا" (except), establishing that full comprehension of these hosts belongs solely to the Creator.
