##
66:6.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

66:6.arabic: في حبهم الدائم وشوقهم اللازم الذي به يسبحون الليل والنهار لا يفترون ولا يعصون الله ما أمرهم ويفعلون ما يؤمرون لاستنكف من نفسه ومن إظهار حبه وعلم قطعا أنه من أخس المحبين في مملكته وأن حبه أنقص من حب كل محب لله قال بعض الكاشفين من المحبين عبدت الله تعالى ثلاثين سنة بأعمال القلوب والجوارح على بذل المجهود واستفراغ الطاقة حتى ظننت أن لي عند الله شيئا فذكر أشياء من مكاشفات آيات السموات في قصة طويلة قال في آخرها فبلغت صفا من الملائكة بعدد جميع ما خلق الله من شيء فقلت من أنتم فقالوا نحن المحبون لله عز وجل نعبده ههنا منذ ثلثمائة ألف سنة ما خطر على قلوبنا قط سواه
66:6.english: It is related that a man saw something from one of the madmen that made him deem him foolish, and he reported that to Maʿrūf al-Karkhī — may Allah have mercy on him. He smiled, then said: "O my brother, he has lovers, both young and old, both rational and mad. So this one you saw is among their madmen."
66:6.section_title_en: On the Concealment of Love and Its True Signs — Section 1183
66:6.anchors:
- Root: خفي (khafā)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To be hidden, concealed, imperceptible to the senses.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-Khafī is that which is not perceived by the senses; its theological nuance relates to Allah's knowledge of the unseen (ghayb) and the inner conscience (sirr).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (haqīqah) refers to physical concealment; metaphorical (majāz) applies to the heart's hidden states, as in "the secret" (al-sirr) which only Allah perceives.
- Root: حب (ḥubb)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to love, to be steadfast upon something; also a jar (ḥubb) that holds water — implying that love is a vessel containing the lover's entire being.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-Maḥabbah is the will directed toward what is perceived as agreeable; in theological terms, love of Allah is the soul's inclination toward Him due to His perfection, not due to benefit or harm.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: inclination of the heart. Metaphorical: the bodily movements and stillness that testify to an inward state, as the physician's diagnosis of the lover's urine.
- Root: وجد (wajd)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To find; also intense emotion, ecstasy, or passionate yearning that overwhelms the lover.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-Wajd is the arrival of a spiritual state (ḥāl) that dominates the heart, often leading to loss of self-control (ghashyah).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: finding something lost. Metaphorical: the overpowering of the heart by love, such that the lover falls unconscious — as related of al-Sarī.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Interposition (al-Faṣl bayna al-Jār wa al-Majrūr) — The syntactic principle that a clause may be interrupted by an explanatory parenthetical without breaking grammatical cohesion, as seen in the narrative digressions (e.g., the story of the madman and al-Karkhī) that serve as illustrative asides within the main argument.
66:6.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Love, Longing, Intimacy and Contentment'

67:22.arabic: الفريقين الإشارة بقوله تعالى {أفمن يمشي مكبا على وجهه أهدى أم من يمشي سويا على صراط مستقيم} فإن الكفار لم يغلطوا فيما غلطوا فيه إلا بمثل هذه الانعكاسات نسأل الله حسن التوفيق بكرمه ولطفه بيان أقسام الصبر بحسب اختلاف القوة والضعف اعلم إن باعث الدين بالإضافة إلى باعث الهوى له ثلاثة أحوال أحدها أن يقهر داعي الهوى فلا تبقى له قوة المنازعة ويتوصل إليه بدوام الصبر وعند هذا يقال من صبر ظفر والواصلون إلى هذه الرتبة هم الأقلون فلا جرم هم الصديقون المقربون {الذين قالوا ربنا الله ثم استقاموا} فهؤلاء لازموا الطريق المستقيم واستووا على الصراط
67:22.english: Thus most of the moral traits of faith (akhlāq al-īmān) are subsumed under patience. For this reason, when the Prophet — peace be upon him — was once asked about faith, he said: "It is patience" — because it is the most abundant and most precious of its works, just as he said: "The Pilgrimage is ʿArafah." And God — exalted be He — has gathered together all of these divisions and called the whole of them "patience," saying — exalted be He: {And the patient in adversity (al-ba'sā') — i.e., calamity — and in hardship (al-ḍarrā') — i.e., poverty — and at the time of peril (ḥīna al-ba's) — i.e., warfare — {those are the ones who have been truthful, and those are the ones who are God-fearing} «أولئك الذين صدقوا وأولئك هم المتقون». So these, then, are the divisions of patience according to the difference of its objects of relation (mutaʿallaqātihā).
67:22.section_title_en: The Names That Accrue to Patience (Ṣabr) in Relation to Its Object, and the Divisions of Patience According to Strength and Weakness
67:22.anchors:
- Root: صبر (Ṣ-B-R)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core sense of "holding back" or "restraining" (al-imsāk), as in holding a beast without fodder or confining someone; endurance of hardship.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Patience is the restraint of the self (ḥabs al-nafs) upon what reason and Law require, or from what they require it to abstain." It is a generic term (laẓf ʿāmm) whose specific names vary by context: in calamity it is "patience" (ṣabr) against "panic" (jazaʿ); in battle, "courage" (shajāʿah) against "cowardice" (jubn); in affliction, "breadth of breast" (saʿat al-ṣadr) against "vexation" (ḍajar).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): "I bore patiently what I dislike, and I held back from what I love." Metaphorical (majāz): "His hand does not endure the cold" — i.e., is not patient against it; "he is more patient of beating than the ground."
- Root: نفس (N-F-S)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The self or soul; that which is breathed; also blood (nafs sā'ilah).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Al-Nafs: the spirit (al-rūḥ)… and in God's saying {He warns you of Himself} (nafsihi) it denotes His very essence (dhāt)."
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "a precious thing (nafīs)"; Metaphorical: "he poured out his nafs (i.e., his blood)."
- Root: ضرب (Ḍ-R-B)
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Used for striking and for coercion; also for "types" or "kinds" (ḍarb min kadhā) — as in the section heading "two types" (ḍarbān).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "he struck him with the sword"; Metaphorical: "he struck his hand" (i.e., prevented him from an affair); "the vicissitudes of time struck them."
- Sibawayh Rule: Interposition and Specification (Bāb al-Faṣl bayn al-Jār wa-al-Majrūr) — The syntactic structure "bi-al-iḍāfah ilā mā ʿanhu al-ṣabr" (in relation to that from which one exercises patience) shows how prepositional phrases govern semantic specification, distinguishing the act of patience from its object (al-mutaʿallaq).
67:22.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

73:10.arabic: {واصبر على ما يقولون واهجرهم هجرا جميلا} وقال تعالى {ولقد نعلم أنك يضيق صدرك بما يقولون فسبح بحمد ربك} الآية وقال تعالى {ولتسمعن من الذين أوتوا الكتاب من قبلكم ومن الذين أشركوا أذى كثيرا وإن تصبروا وتتقوا فإن ذلك من عزم الأمور} أي تصبروا عن المكافأة ولذلك مدح الله تعالى العافين عن حقوقهم في القصاص وغيره فقال تعالى {وإن عاقبتم فعاقبوا بمثل ما عوقبتم به ولئن صبرتم لهو} خير الصابرين {وقال} صلى الله عليه وسلم صل من قطعك وأعط من حرمك واعف عمن ظلمك // ورأيت في الإنجيل قال عيسى بن مريم عليه السل
73:10.english: And acts of disobedience are the requisite of the impulse of caprice (bāʿith al-hawā). And the most severe kind of patience is patience in abstaining from those acts of disobedience that have become familiar through habit — for habit is a fifth nature. When habit is joined to lustful desire, two battalions from the battalions of Satan array themselves in concert against the battalion of God (jund Allāh) — may He be exalted — and the impulse of religion (bāʿith al-dīn) has no strength to suppress them. Then, if that act be one whose commission has been rendered easy (tayassara), patience in abstaining from it is heavier upon the soul — such as patience in abstaining from the sins of the tongue: backbiting (ghībah), falsehood, contentious disputation (mirāʾ), self-praise whether by insinuation (taʿrīḍ) or by explicit statement (taṣrīḥ), the varieties of jesting that wound hearts, the kinds of words by which one intends belittlement and contempt, and the mention of the dead with aspersion cast upon them, upon their sciences, their conduct, and their stations. For such mention is in its outward aspect (fī ẓāhirihi) backbiting, and in its inward aspect (fī bāṭinihi) self-praise. In it the soul has two lusts: one is the negation of the other [person], and the other is the affirmation of oneself. And by these two together there is completed for it that lordship (rubūbiyyah) which is innate in its disposition — and which is the very opposite of what it has been commanded regarding servanthood (ʿubūdiyyah). And because of the conjunction of the two lusts, and the ease of moving the tongue, and the fact that this becomes habitual in everyday converse, patience in abstaining from it becomes difficult. And it is among the greatest of the destructive enormities (al-mūbiqāt) — so much so that its disapproval and ugliness have been effaced from hearts by dint of its frequent repetition and the universality of familiarity with it. Thus you see a man who would, for example, wear silk and deem it utterly remote [of permissibility], yet he unleashes his tongue the whole day long against the reputations (aʿrāḍ) of people and does not deem that objectionable — notwithstanding what has come down in the report that backbiting is more severe than adultery (zinā). And God — may He be exalted — said: {«ودع أذاهم وتوكل على الله»} "And leave aside their harm and put thy trust in God" (Q. 33:48). And He said — may He be exalted: {«واصبر على ما يقولون واهجرهم هجرا جميلا»} "And be patient over what they say, and depart from them with a gracious departure" (Q. 73:10). And He said — may He be exalted: {«ولقد نعلم أنك يضيق صدرك بما يقولون فسبح بحمد ربك»} "And indeed We know that thy breast is straitened by what they say; so glorify with the praise of thy Lord" (Q. 15:97–98) — to the end of the verse. And He said — may He be exalted: {«ولتسمعن من الذين أوتوا الكتاب من قبلكم ومن الذين أشركوا أذى كثيرا وإن تصبروا وتتقوا فإن ذلك من عزم الأمور»} "And you shall surely hear from those who were given the Scripture before you and from those who associate [others with God] much harm. And if you are patient and God-fearing, indeed that is of the resolute affairs" (Q. 3:186) — that is, that you be patient in refraining from requital (mukāfaʾah). And for this reason God — may He be exalted — praised those who pardon others their due rights in retaliation (qiṣāṣ) and otherwise, saying — may He be exalted: {«وإن عاقبتم فعاقبوا بمثل ما عوقبتم به ولئن صبرتم لهو خير الصابرين»} "And if you punish, then punish with the like of that wherewith you were afflicted. And if you are patient, it is surely better for the patient" (Q. 16:126). And he — upon him be peace — said: "Maintain the bond with him who cuts you off, and give to him who withholds from you, and pardon him who wrongs you." And I have seen in the Gospel that ʿĪsā ibn Maryam — upon him be peace — said: "It was said to you of old: an eye for an eye and a nose for a nose. But I say to you: do not resist evil. Rather, whoever strikes your right cheek, turn to him PageV04P071 the left cheek; and whoever takes your cloak, give him your garment; and whoever compels you to walk with him one mile, walk with him two miles." And all of that is a command to be patient under harm. So patience under the harm of people is among the highest stations of patience, because in it the impulse of religion and the impulse of lustful desire and anger are all arrayed together [against the soul].
73:10.section_title_en: The Most Severe Forms of Patience: Abstaining from Habitual Sins and Enduring Harm
73:10.anchors:
- Root: صبر (ṣ-b-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of restraint and withholding; "ṣabara al-dābbah" = to hold back an animal without fodder; "ṣabartu nafsī" = I restrained my soul.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الصبر: حبس النفس على ما يقتضيه العقل والشرع، أو عما يقتضيان حبسها عنه" — Patience is the withholding of the soul upon what reason and Law require, or from what they require it to be withheld. When exercised against calamity it is called ṣabr alone (opposed to jazaʿ); in warfare, courage (shajāʿah); in vexing misfortune, forbearance.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): "صبرت على ما أكره. وصبرت عما أحب" — I bore patiently what I dislike, and I restrained myself from what I love. Metaphorical (majāz): "هو أصبر على الضرب من الأرض" — he is more enduring of beating than the earth.
- Root: عادة (ʿ-w-d)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Recurrence and return; habitual practice that becomes second nature through repetition.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Habit (ʿādah) as reiterated action that imprints upon the soul, rendering the act facile and its abandonment burdensome.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: return to a state or place. Metaphorical: the ingrained disposition that governs conduct.
- Root: غيب (gh-y-b)
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الغيب: مصدر غابت الشمس وغيرها: إذا استترت عن العين" — that which is concealed from the senses; applied to what is absent from human perception, though nothing is absent from God.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "تكلم بذلك عن ظهر الغيب" — he spoke of that behind the veil of the unseen. Metaphorical: "أتونا في غابة" — they came in a dense host (like tangled thickets).
- Sibawayh Rule: Prepositional Interposition (باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور) — governing the permissible separation between the preposition and its object for rhetorical emphasis, as in the periodic construction "فإن ذلك في ظاهره غيبة وفي باطنه ثناء على النفس" where the circumstantial qualifiers (ẓāhir/bāṭin) are interposed to contrast outward form with inward reality.
73:10.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

75:20.arabic: وقال عز وجل كلا بل تحبون العاجلة وتذرون الآخرة فمن هذا حده فينبغي أن يعالج قلبه من حب الجاه بالعلم بالآفات العاجلة وهو أن يتفكر في الأخطار التي يستهدف لها أرباب الجاه في الدنيا فإن كل ذي جاه محسود ومقصود بالإيذاء وخائف على الدوام على جاهه ومحترز من أن تتغير منزلته في القلوب والقلوب أشد تغيرا من القدر في غليانها وهي مترددة بين الإقبال والإعراض فكل ما يبنى على قلوب الخلق يضاهي ما يبنى على أمواج البحر فإنه لا ثبات له والاشتغال بمراعاة القلوب وحفظ الجاه ودفع كيد الحساد ومنع أذى الأعداء كل ذلك غ
75:20.english: And it is as though you had never ceased to be in the Hereafter — for these people, their attention was turned to the final outcome, and so their deeds were performed for its sake, through godfearingness (taqwā), since they knew that the final outcome belongs to the godfearing. Thus they held in contempt rank and wealth in this world. But the sight of most creatures is weak, confined to the immediate (al-ʿājilah), whose light does not extend to the witnessing of final outcomes. For this reason, Allah Most High said: {«بل تؤثرون الحياة الدنيا والآخرة خير وأبقى»} ("Nay, you prefer the life of this world, while the Hereafter is better and more enduring") [Al-Aʿlā 87:16–17]. And He, Mighty and Majestic, said: {«كلا بل تحبون العاجلة وتذرون الآخرة»} ("Nay, but you love the immediate and forsake the Hereafter") [Al-Qiyāmah 75:20–21].
75:20.section_title_en: The Cure for Love of Status — Section 804 of The Revival of the Religious Sciences
75:20.anchors:
- Root: جاه (jāh)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الجاه: القدر والمنزلة، وجاه عند الناس: وقع وعظم" — rank, standing, and elevation in the eyes of others.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: jāh is a social accident (ʿaraḍ) attached to the estimations of hearts, not a real attribute of the self; its pursuit is a veiling distraction from the Hereafter.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): "جاه عند السلطان: منزلته ووجهته." Metaphorical (majāz): the "face" (wajh) one presents to people — i.e., honor is but a reflected image in fluctuating hearts, like a building upon waves.
- Root: خطر (khaṭar)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الخطر: الإشراف على الهلاك، والخطر: السبق الذي يراهن عليه" — peril and stakes.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The "danger" (khaṭar) of status is that its possessor becomes a target (gharaḍ) for envy and harm — a Quranic motif of the world's transient allure versus the abiding Hereafter.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "خاطر بنفسه: ألقاها في المهلكة." Metaphorical: the aspirant to jāh "stakes" his own peace as wager in a game he cannot win.
- Root: خمل (khamūl)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الخمول: خفاء الذكر وعدم الشهرة، وخمل الرجل: سقط ولم يُعرف" — obscurity and anonymity.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Obscurity (khamūl) is the therapeutic counterweight to jāh; it severs the heart's attachment to created estimations.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "خمل الثوب: ما خفي من نسجه." Metaphorical: the soul's "hidden weave" — its true worth lies unseen, like the inner thread of cloth.
- Root: قنع (qanāʿah)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "قنع: رضي بالكفاف واكتفى باليسير" — contentment with sufficiency.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Qanāʿah is the root that severs ṭamaʿ (covetous expectation) from creatures, redirecting hope solely to the Creator.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "قنع الصائد: نصب القنوع" (the hunter's blind). Metaphorical: the contented man "blinds" himself to people's opinions, as one hides in a blind to escape prey's notice.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — governing the contrastive structure "إنما يعالج بالعلم... وأما من حيث العمل" where the particle ḥaṣr restricts each cure to its proper domain (knowledge vs. practice), and "فإن" clauses provide causal grounding for periodic sentences.
75:20.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

76:27.arabic: كلا بل تحبون العاجلة وتذرون الآخرة وقال تعالى إن هؤلاء يحبون العاجله ويذرون وراءهم يوما ثقيلا وقال تعالى فأعرض عمن تولى عن ذكرنا ولم يرد إلا الحياة الدنيا ذلك مبلغهم من العلم ولما استطار مكر الشيطان في كافة الخلق أرسل الله الملائكة إلى الرسل وأوحوا إليهم ما تم على الخلق من إهلاك العدو وإغوائه فاشتغلوا بدعوة الخلق إلى الملك الحقيقي عن الملك المجازى الذي لا أصل له إن سلم ولا دوام له أصلا فنادوا فيهم يا أيها الذين آمنوا ما لكم إذا قيل لكم انفروا في سبيل الله اثاقلتم إلى الأرض أرضيتم بالحياة الدنيا من الآخرة فما متاع الحياة الدنيا في الآخرة
76:27.english: Al-Junayd — may Allah have mercy on him — said: "The journey from this world to the Hereafter is easy for the believer, but abandoning creation out of love for the Truth is severe. The journey from the self to Allah — exalted is He — is difficult and severe, and patience *with* Allah is even more severe." So he mentioned the severity of patience regarding the distractions of the heart, then the severity of abandoning creation.
76:27.section_title_en: The Cure for Patience Regarding Whispers and Distractions — The Final Station of Patience
76:27.anchors:
- Root: ملك (malaka)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of possession, dominion, and sovereign authority; al-mulk is that which is grasped and held under one's control.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-Mulk is of two kinds: (1) possession and assumption of authority (al-tamalluk wa al-tawallī), and (2) the inherent capacity/power for it (al-quwwah ʿalā dhālika), whether or not one actually assumes it. True sovereignty belongs to Allah alone; human "kingship" is a shadow or metaphor of divine rubūbiyyah.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): "Li-llāh al-mulk wa al-malakūt" — dominion is real for God. Metaphorical (majāz): "malaka nafsahu ʿinda al-ghaḍab" (he mastered himself in anger) — self-possession as figurative rule; "malaka ʿalayhi amruhu" (his affair overcame him) — being dominated by external circumstance.
- Root: دنا (danā)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Proximity, nearness; al-dunyā (the lower/ nearer world) is so named because it is nearer to us and temporally prior, while the ākhirah is deferred.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-dunūw is nearness by essence or by judgment, used of place, time, and station. The "nearer" (al-adnā) is sometimes contrasted with the greater, sometimes with the better — as in {«أَتَسْتَبْدِلُونَ الَّذِي هُوَ أَدْنَى بِالَّذِي هُوَ خَيْرٌ»} (Do you exchange that which is lower for that which is better?).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical proximity. Metaphorical: preference for the immediate over the deferred — the dunyā as the "present" that seduces the impatient.
- Root: خلق (khalaqa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Originary measuring and fashioning; estimation before cutting; creation as bringing into being upon a determined measure.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-khalq is origination from no prior model (ibdāʿ), as in {«خَلَقَ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضَ»} — He originated them. Also used for bringing forth from something, as man from a drop. The "command" (amr) belongs to a different order than the "creation" (khalq).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the tailor's measuring of cloth before cutting. Metaphorical: Allah's creation of beings upon a measure necessitated by wisdom; "khalq" as the fashioned body vs. "amr" as the commanding, immaterial reality.
- Root: الي (aliha / risālah)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The root of mal'akah (messengership) — that which is "chewed" in the mouth, i.e., conveyed by utterance; the angel as one who delivers a message.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-malā'ikah (angels) are so named from al-mal'akah (the message), because they deliver what is "masticated" in speech — from "faras ya'luku al-lijām" (a horse chewing the bit). The spirit (al-rūḥ) is from the "command" (amr) of the Lord — a subtle, immaterial reality.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical chewing. Metaphorical: the conveyance of divine communication through angelic intermediaries.
- Sibawayh Rule: Bāb al-ḥaṣr wa al-taqyīd bi-innamā (Restriction and Focused Predication) — "Innamā" restricts the predicate exclusively to the subject, as in {«إِنَّمَا مَتَاعُ الْحَيَاةِ الدُّنْيَا فِي الْآخِرَةِ إِلَّا قَلِيلٌ»} — the restriction here nullifies any comparison between the two realms, affirming the utter insignificance of worldly goods against the Hereafter.
76:27.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

77:21.arabic: فهو في الرحم في قرار مكين إلى قدر معلوم وله في سلوكه إلى الكمال منازل وأطوار من نطفة وعلقة ومضغة وغيرها إلى أن يخرج من مضيق الرحم إلى فضاء العالم فنسبة عموم القيامة الكبرى إلى خصوص القيامة الصغرى كنسبة سعة فضاء العالم إلى سعة فضاء الرحم ونسبة سعة العالم الذي يقدم عليه العبد بالموت إلى سعة فضاء الدنيا كنسبة فضاء الدنيا أيضا إلى الرحم بل أوسع وأعظم فقس الآخرة بالأولى فما خلقكم ولا بعثكم إلا كنفس واحدة وما النشأة الثانية إلا على قياس النشأة الأولى بل أعداد النشآت ليست محصورة في اثنتين وإلي
77:21.english: How immense is your heedlessness, O wretched one—and all of us are that wretched one—while before you are these terrors! If you do not believe in the greater resurrection out of ignorance and error, does not the evidence of the lesser resurrection suffice you? Have you not heard the saying of the Master of the Prophets, peace be upon him: "Sufficient is death as a warner" (kafā bil-mawti wāʿiẓan)? Have you not heard of his weeping, peace be upon him, at death, until he said, may God's peace and blessing be upon him: "O God, ease for Muhammad the agonies of death" (allāhumma hawwin ʿalā Muḥammadin sakarāti al-mawt)? Are you not ashamed of your slowness in anticipating the onslaught of death, following the rabble of the heedless—those who look only for a single cry that seizes them while they are disputing, so they can neither make a bequest nor return to their families? Then illness comes to them as a warner of death, and they are not deterred; and gray hair comes to them as a messenger from it, and they do not take heed. {«يَا حَسْرَةً عَلَى الْعِبَادِ مَا يَأْتِيهِمْ مِنْ رَسُولٍ إِلَّا كَانُوا بِهِ يَسْتَهْزِئُونَ»} (O regret upon the servants! There comes not to them a messenger but they mock him) [Ya-Sin: 30]. Do they think that they are in this world immortal? {«أَوَلَمْ يَرَوْا كَمْ أَهْلَكْنَا قَبْلَهُمْ مِنَ الْقُرُونِ أَنَّهُمْ إِلَيْهِمْ لَا يَرْجِعُونَ»} (Have they not seen how many generations We destroyed before them—that they will not return to them?) [Ya-Sin: 31]. Or do they reckon that the dead have merely traveled away from them, and so they are annihilated? Nay! {«وَإِنْ كُلٌّ لَمَّا جَمِيعٌ لَدَيْنَا مُحْضَرُونَ»} (And indeed, all of them, without exception, will be brought before Us) [Ya-Sin: 32]. {«وَمَا تَأْتِيهِمْ مِنْ آيَةٍ مِنْ آيَاتِ رَبِّهِمْ إِلَّا كَانُوا عَنْهَا مُعْرِضِينَ»} (And there comes not to them a sign from the signs of their Lord but they turn away from it) [Ya-Sin: 46]. And that is because {«إِنَّا جَعَلْنَا مِنْ بَيْنِ أَيْدِيهِمْ سَدًّا وَمِنْ خَلْفِهِمْ سَدًّا فَأَغْشَيْنَاهُمْ فَهُمْ لَا يُبْصِرُونَ»} (We have placed before them a barrier and behind them a barrier, and We have covered them, so they do not see) [Ya-Sin: 9]. {«وَسَوَاءٌ عَلَيْهِمْ أَأَنْذَرْتَهُمْ أَمْ لَمْ تُنْذِرْهُمْ لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ»} (And it is alike to them whether you warn them or warn them not—they will not believe) [Ya-Sin: 10].
77:21.section_title_en: On the Lesser Resurrection as Proof of the Greater, and the Station of the Guardian over the Child
77:21.anchors:
- Root: صغر (ṣaghara)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Smallness in magnitude, rank, or time; the lesser as opposed to the greater (al-kabīr), each term relative to the other.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Ṣighar and kibar are relative opposites, applied variously to age, body, or station; here, the "lesser resurrection" (al-qiyāmah al-ṣughrā) is death, measured against the "greater" (al-kubrā), the final rising.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: diminution in size or status. Metaphorical: the lesser as a type or foreshadow of the greater—death as the microcosmic analogue of the macrocosmic resurrection.
- Root: موت (mawt)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Death as the cessation of animal life; the root also yields "amāta" (to cause death) and "mayyit" (the dead).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Death is the departure of the soul from the body, a transition between two abodes; it is the "lesser resurrection" in that it separates the spirit from the corporeal frame, prefiguring the greater separation and recompense.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: biological death. Metaphorical: "the dead land" revived by rain, and here, death as a "warner" (nadhīr) and "messenger" (rasūl)—personified agencies of admonition.
- Root: علم (ʿalima)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Knowledge as perception or cognition of a thing; "ʿallama" (to teach) and "ʿālim" (the knowing one).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): ʿIlm is apprehension of a thing's reality—either its essence or a judgment about it. Here, the "knowledge" of the two resurrections distinguishes the believer (muʾmin) from the ignorant (jāhil), who sees with a "blind eye" (al-ʿayn al-ʿawrāʾ).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: certain cognition. Metaphorical: "I knew not of your news" (mā ʿalimtu bi-khabarika) meaning "I perceived not"—thus ignorance is a failure of perception, not mere absence of data.
- Root: ولي (waliya)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Nearness, guardianship, or patronage; the walī is one who assumes charge of another's affairs, whether kin or protector.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Wilāyah denotes proximity and authority; the walī of a child acts as God's deputy in discipline, mirroring the angels' custodianship of the moral ledger.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical adjacency. Metaphorical: the guardian's "inheriting the character of the angels" (waritha akhlāq al-malāʾikah)—a moral, not genealogical, inheritance.
- Sibawayh Rule: Interposition of the conditional and its apodosis (al-faṣl bayna al-sharṭ wa al-jawāb)—the periodic structure in "fa-in kunta lā tuʾminu... afalā takfīka" (if you believe not... does not suffice you?) allows the protasis to govern the rhetorical question, binding the lesser sign to the greater inference.
77:21.topic: Al-Ghazali on the journey of the soul, death, and the Hereafter, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

80:24.arabic: يمتزج ماؤها بالأرض فيصير طينا وإليه الإشارة بقوله تعالى {فلينظر الإنسان إلى طعامه أنا صببنا الماء صبا ثم شققنا الأرض شقا فأنبتنا فيها حبا وعنبا وقضبا وزيتونا ونخلا} الآية ثم لا يكفي الماء والتراب إذ لو تركت في أرض ندية صلبة متراكمة لم تنبت لفقد الهواء فيحتاج إلى تركها في أرض رجوة متخلخلة يتغلغل الهواء إليها ثم الهواء لا يتحرك إليها بنفسه فيحتاج إلى ريح تحرك الهواء وتضربه بقهر وعنف على الأرض حتى ينفذ فيها وإليه الإشارة بقوله تعالى {وأرسلنا الرياح لواقح} وإنما إلقاحها في إيقاع الازدواج بين الهواء والماء والأرض ثم كل ذلك لا يغنيك لو كان في برد مفرط وشتاء شات فتحتاج إلى حرارة الربيع
80:24.english: Know that foods are many, and for God Most High in their creation there are many wonders beyond enumeration and successive causes without end. To mention this regarding every food would be lengthy, for foods are either medicines, or fruits, or nourishments. Let us take the nourishments, for they are the foundation, and from among them let us take a single grain of wheat, setting aside all other nourishments. We say: when a grain or grains are found, if you were to eat them, they would perish and you would remain hungry. So how necessary it is for you that the grain should grow in itself, increase, and multiply until it suffices for your complete need! Thus God Most High created in the grain of wheat powers by which it is nourished, just as He created in you. For the plant differs from you only in sensation and movement; it does not differ from you in nutrition, because it is nourished by water and draws it into its interior by means of roots, just as you are nourished and draw [food]. We shall not elaborate at length on the instruments of the plant in drawing nourishment to itself, but we shall point to its nourishment and say: just as wood and earth do not nourish you, but rather you need specific food, so too the grain is not nourished by everything, but rather needs something specific. The proof is that if you left it in the house, it would not increase, because nothing surrounds it but air, and mere air is not suitable for its nourishment. If you left it in water, it would not increase. If you left it in earth without water, it would not increase. Rather, there must be earth containing water, its water mingling with the earth until it becomes clay. To this points the saying of God Most High: {«فَلْيَنْظُرِ الْإِنْسَانُ إِلَىٰ طَعَامِهِ أَنَّا صَبَبْنَا الْمَاءَ صَبًّا ثُمَّ شَقَقْنَا الْأَرْضَ شَقًّا فَأَنْبَتْنَا فِيهَا حَبًّا وَعِنَبًا وَقَضْبًا وَزَيْتُونًا وَنَخْلًا»} — "Then let man look at his food: how We poured down water in torrents, then cleft the earth in clefts, and caused to grow therein grain, and grapes, and green fodder, and olives, and palms" — to the end of the verse. Then water and earth alone do not suffice, for if you left it in moist, hard, compacted earth, it would not sprout for lack of air. Thus it needs to be left in loose, crumbly earth through which air can penetrate. Then the air does not move to it by itself, so there is need for a wind that moves the air and strikes it with force and violence upon the earth until it penetrates therein. To this points His saying, Most High: {«وَأَرْسَلْنَا الرِّيَاحَ لَوَاقِحَ»} — "And We sent the winds as fertilizers." Its fertilization consists only in effecting the union between air, water, and earth. Then all that would not avail you if it were in excessive cold and a wintry winter, so you need the heat of spring and summer. Thus it has become clear that its nourishment requires these four [elements]. So consider what each one requires: for water must flow to the cultivated land from seas, springs, rivers, and channels. Consider how God created the seas, caused the springs to gush forth, and made the rivers flow from them. Then the land may be elevated, and waters do not rise to it. So consider how God Most High created the clouds, and how He subjected the winds to them, to drive them by His leave to the regions of the earth — they being heavy clouds bearing water. Then consider how He sends it down in copious showers upon the lands at the time of spring and autumn, according to need. And consider how He created the mountains as reservoirs for water, from which springs burst forth gradually — for were it to issue all at once, the lands would be flooded, and the crops and livestock would perish. The graces of God in the mountains, clouds, seas, and rains cannot be enumerated. As for heat, it cannot be obtained between water and earth, for both are cold. So consider how He subjected the sun, and how He created it — despite its distance from the earth — as a heater for the earth at one time and not another, so that cold is obtained when cold is needed, and heat when heat is needed. This is one of the wisdoms of the sun, and its wisdoms are more than can be counted. Then when the plant rises above the earth, there is in the fruits a hardening and solidity, so they need a moisture to ripen them. Consider how He created the moon and made its property to be moistening, just as He made the sun's property to be heating. Thus it ripens the fruits and colors them by the ordainment of the All-Wise Fashioner. For this reason, were the trees in a shade that blocked the rising of the sun and the moon and the rest of the stars, the fruits would not ripen nor attain their colors and flavors.
80:24.section_title_en: The Fourth Branch: On the Graces of God Most High in the Origins from Which Foods Are Produced and Become Suitable for Man to Thereafter Prepare by His Craft
80:24.anchors:
- Root: ن-ب-ت (n-b-t)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Emergence and growth from the earth; vegetation springing forth.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The act of causing growth attributed to God as Creator of the seed's inherent power; distinct from mere mechanical causation.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal for botanical sprouting; metaphorical for the divine origination of life from dead earth.
- Root: غ-ذ-و (gh-dh-w)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Nourishment; the intake by which a living body sustains and increases itself.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The principle of nutrition shared between animal and plant, differing only in sensory faculties and locomotion.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal for feeding; used analogically to show the plant's passive reception of water via roots as man's active ingestion.
- Root: م-ز-ج (m-z-j)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Blending and intermingling of two substances into a unified third.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The providential mixing of water with earth to form clay, a precondition for vegetative growth.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal for physical mixture; here signifying the divine ordination of elemental harmony.
- Root: ل-ق-ح (l-q-ḥ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Fertilization; impregnation of the date-palm by wind-borne pollen.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The winds as "fertilizers" (lawāqiḥ) — their function being to effect union between air, water, and earth.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal for pollination; metaphorical in the Quranic verse for the winds' role in driving rain-bearing clouds.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — Used to isolate the essential conditions for growth (e.g., "it is but air and mere air does not suffice"), emphasizing exclusive causal requirements.

80:24.arabic: وقد قال الله عز وجل فلينظر الإنسان إلى طعامه قال ابن عباس إلى رجيعه وقال رجل لابن عمر إني أريد أن أسألك وأستحي قال فلا تستحي واسأل قال إذا قضى أحدنا حاجته فقام ينظر إلى ذلك منه قال نعم إن الملك يقول له انظر إلى ما بخلت به انظر إلى ماذا صار وكان بشر بن كعب يقول انطلقوا حتى أريكم الدنيا فيذهب بهم إلى مزبلة فيقول انظروا إلى ثمارهم ودجاجهم وعسلهم وسمنهم مثال آخر في نسبة الدنيا إلى الآخرة قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ما الدنيا في الآخرة إلا كمثل ما يجعل أحدكم إصبعه في اليم فلينظر أحدكم بم
80:24.english: It resembles the phantasms of sleep and the confused dreams of slumber. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: "The world is a dream, and its people are upon it — held to account and punished." {«الدنيا حلم وأهلها عليها مجازون ومعاقبون»}
80:24.topic: Al-Ghazali on purifying the character, moral diseases, and spiritual remedies, from 'Condemnation of the World'

80:25.arabic: الدقيق الذي يقصرون عن فهمه إذ قال تعالى {أنا صببنا الماء صبا ثم شققنا الأرض شقا فأنبتنا فيها حبا وعنبا} الآية وأما الحكمة في سائر الكواكب السيارة منها والثوابت فخفية لا يطلع عليها كافة الخلق والقدر الذي يحتمله فهم الخلق أنها زينة للسماء لتستلذ العين بالنظر إليها وأشار إليه قوله تعالى {إنا زينا السماء الدنيا بزينة الكواكب} فجميع أجزاء العالم سماؤه وكواكبه ورياحه وبحاره وجباله ومعادنه ونباته وحيواناته وأعظاء حيواناته لا تخلو ذرة من ذراته عن حكم كثيرة من حكمه واحدة إلى عشرة إلى ألف إلى عشرة آلاف وكذا أعضاء الحيوان تنقسم إلا ما يعرف حكمتها كالعلم بأن العين للإبصار لا للبطش واليد للبطش لا للمشي والرجل للمشي لا للشم فأما الأعضاء الباطنة من الأمعاء والمرارة والكبد والكلية وآحاد العروق والأعصاب والعضلات وما فيها من التجاويف والالتفاف والاشتباك والانحراف والدقة والغلظ وسائر الصفات فلا يعرف الحكمة فيها سائر الناس والذين يعرفونها لا يعرفون منها إلا قدرا يسيرا بالإضافة إلى ما في علم الله تعالى {وما أوتيتم من العلم إلا قليلا} فإذن كل من استعمل شيئا في جهة غير الجهة التي خلق لها ولا على الوجه الذي أريد به فقد كفر فيه نعمة الله تعالى فمن ضرب غيره بيده فقد كفر نعمة اليد إذ خلقت له اليد ليدفع بها عن نفسه ما يهلكه ويأخذ ما ينفعه لا ليهلك بها غيره ومن نظر إلى وجه غير المحرم فقد كفر نعمة العين ونعمة الشمس إذ الإبصار يتم بهما وإنما خلقتا ليبصر بهما ما ينفعه في دينه ودنياه ويتقي بهما ما يضره فيهما فقد استعملها في غير ما اريد به وهذا لأن المراد من خلق الخلق وخلق الدنيا وأسبابها أن يستعين الخلق بهما على الوصول إلى الله تعالى ولا وصول إليه إلا بمحبته والأنس به في الدنيا والتجافي عن غرور الدنيا ولا أنس
80:25.english: ...and there is no omnipotent one save the King, the Compeller. And when the covering is lifted from the eyes of the heedless, and they behold the matter to be thus, they will hear at that time the call of the Proclaimer: {«لِمَنِ الْمُلْكُ الْيَوْمَ لِلَّهِ الْوَاحِدِ الْقَهَّارِ»} — "To whom belongs the sovereignty this Day? To God, the One, the Compeller" {Q 40:16}. And indeed sovereignty belonged to God, the One, the Compeller, every single day — not exclusively on that day — but the heedless do not hear this proclamation save on that day. Thus it is tidings of what is renewed for the heedless of the unveiling of states, at a time when the unveiling will not benefit them. So we seek refuge in God, the Forbearing, the Generous, from ignorance and blindness, for it is the root cause of destruction.
80:25.section_title_en: The Unveiling of Sovereignty and the Discernment of What God Loves from What He Abhors
80:25.anchors:
- Root: كشف (kashafa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Removal of a covering; disclosure of what was hidden.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Unveiling of the unseen realities (mukāshafah) — the lifting of the veil from the heart's eye to perceive things as they truly are.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): removal of a physical covering. Metaphorical (majāz): the disclosure of intellectual or spiritual realities to the percipient.
- Root: ملك (malaka)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Possession, dominion, sovereignty; the one who possesses is malik (king).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): True sovereignty (mulk) belongs exclusively to God; all created dominion is borrowed and ephemeral.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: royal authority. Metaphorical: absolute, unshared dominion — as in the Qur'anic proclamation of sole kingship on the Day of Judgment.
- Root: شكر (shakara)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Gratitude; acknowledgment of beneficence.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Thankfulness is the recognition of the Benefactor and the employment of His blessings in that which pleases Him — not mere verbal praise.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: requital of favor. Metaphorical: the use of blessings in obedience to the Giver, which is the true meaning of gratitude.
- Root: كفر (kafara)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Covering, concealing; ingratitude that veils the recognition of favor.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Kufr is the covering of blessings by failing to employ them in the manner intended by the Giver, or by employing them in what He abhors.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: covering a seed in the earth. Metaphorical: the concealment of God's blessings through misuse or neglect.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Restriction and Focused Predication (al-ḥaṣr wa al-taqyīd bi-innamā) — restricting the means of gratitude to two exclusive cognitive faculties, and the restriction of creation's purpose to the sole end of attaining unto God.
80:25.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

83:29.arabic: يكونوا ضحكة للجاهلين وإليه الإشارة بقوله تعالى إن الذين أجرموا كانوا من الذين آمنوا يضحكون وإذا مروا بهم يتغامزون وإذا انقلبوا إلى أهلهم انقلبوا فكهين وإذ رأوهم قالوا إن هؤلاء لضالون وما أرسلوا عليهم حافظين ثم بين أن ضحك العارفين عليهم غدا أعظم إذ قال تعالى {فاليوم الذين آمنوا من الكفار يضحكون على الأرائك ينظرون} وكذلك أمة نوح عليه السلام كانوا يضحكون عليه عند اشتغاله بعمل السفينة قال {إن تسخروا منا فإنا نسخر منكم كما تسخرون} فهذا أحد النظرين النظر الثاني نظر من لم يبلغ إلى مقام الفناء عن نفسه وهؤلاء قسمان قسم لم يثبتوا إلا وجود أنفسهم وأنكروا أن يكون لهم رب يعبد وهؤلاء هم العميان المنكوسون وع
83:29.english: From this station did Ḥabīb ibn Abī Ḥabīb look when he recited {«إِنَّا وَجَدْنَاهُ صَابِرًا نِعْمَ الْعَبْدُ إِنَّهُ أَوَّابٌ»} [We found him patient — an excellent servant, indeed he was oft-returning] and then exclaimed: "How astonishing! He gave and He praised!" — signaling that when He praises His own giving, He praises Himself; so He is the Praiser and He is the Praised. And from this station did the Shaykh Abū Saʿīd al-Muhayyanī look when {«يُحِبُّهُمْ وَيُحِبُّونَهُ»} [He loves them and they love Him] was recited before him, and he said: "By my life, He loves them — leave Him to love them! By His right, He loves them — for He only loves Himself." He signaled thereby that He is the Loving and He is the Beloved.
83:29.section_title_en: The Two Visions: The Eye of Pure Unity and the Eye of Those Veiled from Self-Annihilation
83:29.anchors:
- Root: نظر (naẓar)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of "sight, gazing, contemplation" — both physical vision and intellectual perception.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: naẓar as "deliberative reflection" (ta'ammul) leading to knowledge of the divine — the inward eye of the heart.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) = ocular sight; Metaphorical (majāz) = intellectual insight and spiritual vision.
- Root: فنو (fanā')
  * Lisan / Ayn: Root meaning of "passing away, perishing, ceasing to be."
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: fanā' as the annihilation of the self's independent consideration — not physical extinction but the obliteration of the illusion of otherness beside God.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal = perishing of a thing; Metaphorical = the mystic's passing away from self-awareness into pure divine contemplation.
- Root: قوم (qawm)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of "standing, rising, being established."
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): al-Qayyūm (القيوم) — the Self-Subsisting One by whom all else stands; theologically distinct from al-Qā'im (the standing one).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal = physical standing; Metaphorical = self-subsistence and sustaining others.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Restriction and Focused Predication (باب الحصر والتقييد) — governing the exclusive predication in "He is the Thankful and the Thanked" (هو الشاكر وهو المشكور), where the definite predicate restricts the attribution solely to God.

83:32.arabic: فكهين وإذ رأوهم قالوا إن هؤلاء لضالون وما أرسلوا عليهم حافظين ثم بين أن ضحك العارفين عليهم غدا أعظم إذ قال تعالى {فاليوم الذين آمنوا من الكفار يضحكون على الأرائك ينظرون} وكذلك أمة نوح عليه السلام كانوا يضحكون عليه عند اشتغاله بعمل السفينة قال {إن تسخروا منا فإنا نسخر منكم كما تسخرون} فهذا أحد النظرين النظر الثاني نظر من لم يبلغ إلى مقام الفناء عن نفسه وهؤلاء قسمان قسم لم يثبتوا إلا وجود أنفسهم وأنكروا أن يكون لهم رب يعبد وهؤلاء هم العميان المنكوسون وعماهم في كلتا العينين لأنهم نفوا ما هو الثابت تحقيقا وهو القي

83:34.arabic: ضحك العارفين عليهم غدا أعظم إذ قال تعالى {فاليوم الذين آمنوا من الكفار يضحكون على الأرائك ينظرون} وكذلك أمة نوح عليه السلام كانوا يضحكون عليه عند اشتغاله بعمل السفينة قال {إن تسخروا منا فإنا نسخر منكم كما تسخرون} فهذا أحد النظرين النظر الثاني نظر من لم يبلغ إلى مقام الفناء عن نفسه وهؤلاء قسمان قسم لم يثبتوا إلا وجود أنفسهم وأنكروا أن يكون لهم رب يعبد وهؤلاء هم العميان المنكوسون وعماهم في كلتا العينين لأنهم نفوا ما هو الثابت تحقيقا وهو القيوم الذي هو قائم بنفسه وقائم على كل نفس بما كسبت وكل قائم فقائم به ولم يقتصروا على هذا حتى أثبتوا أنفسه

84:4.arabic: فارقت الروح الجسد فقد حملت الأرض فمدت حتى ألقت ما فيها وتخلت ولست أطول بجميع موازنة الأحوال والأهوال ولكني أقول بمجرد الموت تقوم عليك هذه القيامة الصغرى ولا يفوتك من القيامة الكبرى شيء مما يخصك بل ما يخص غيرك فإن بقاء الكواكب في حق غيرك ماذا ينفعك وقد انتثرت حواسك التي بها تنتفع بالنظر إلى الكواكب والأعمى يستوى عنده الليل والنهار وكسوف الشمس وانجلاؤها لأنها قد كسفت في حقه دفعة واحدة وهو حصته منها فالانجلاء بعد ذلك حصة غيره ومن انشق رأسه فقد انشقت سماؤه إذ السماء عبارة عما يلي جهة الرأس فمن لا رأس له لا س
84:4.english: As for the noble ones (al-kirām), it is because of the servant's benefit from their nobility, and because all the angels are noble and righteous (kirām bararah). As for the two writers (al-kātibān), it is for the recording of the good deeds and the evil deeds. They write only upon scrolls folded within the secret of the heart (sirr al-qalb) and folded away from the secret of the heart, so that no one may behold them in this world. For verily, they, their writings, their script, their pages, and the totality of what pertains to them belong to the unseen world and the dominion of sovereignty (ʿālam al-ghayb wa al-malakūt), not to the world of sensory witness (ʿālam al-shahādah). And everything belonging to the world of sovereignty (al-malakūt) is imperceptible to corporeal eyes in this world. Then these scrolls, folded away from him, are unfolded twice: once at the minor resurrection (al-qiyāmah al-ṣughrā) and once at the major resurrection (al-qiyāmah al-kubrā). By the minor resurrection I mean the state of death, for the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: "Whoever has died, his resurrection has indeed come to pass" {«من مات فقد قامت قيامته»}. In this resurrection, the servant is alone, and at that time it is said: {«وَلَقَدْ جِئْتُمُونَا فُرَادَىٰ كَمَا خَلَقْنَاكُمْ أَوَّلَ مَرَّةٍ»} ("And indeed you have come to Us alone, just as We created you the first time") — and in it, it is said: {«كَفَىٰ بِنَفْسِكَ الْيَوْمَ عَلَيْكَ حَسِيبًا»} ("Sufficient is your own soul this day as a reckoner against you"). As for the major resurrection, which gathers all of creation, he is not alone therein; rather, he may be reckoned before a multitude of creatures, and in it the God-fearing are driven to Paradise and the criminals to the Fire in groups (zumar), not as individuals. The first great terror is the terror of the minor resurrection, and for all the terrors of the major resurrection there is a counterpart in the minor resurrection — such as the earthquake of the earth, for example. For your own particular earth quakes at death, since you know that when an earthquake descends upon a town, it is truly said that "their earth has quaked," even if the surrounding lands have not quaked. Nay, even if only a man's dwelling quakes, the earthquake has occurred relative to him, because he is harmed by the quaking of the entire earth only through the quaking of his own dwelling, not through the quaking of another's dwelling. Thus his share of the earthquake has been fully realized without any diminution. Know that you are an earth created from dust, and your particular share of the dust is only your body. As for the body of another, it is not your share. The earth upon which you sit, in relation to your body, is but a vessel and a place. You fear its quaking only because your body might quake on account of it; otherwise, the air is perpetually in motion and you do not dread it, since your body does not quake because of it. So your share of the earthquake of the entire earth is only the quaking of your body — it is your earth and your particular dust. Your bones are the mountains of your earth; your head is the sky of your earth; your heart is the sun of your earth; your hearing, your sight, and the rest of your faculties are the stars of your sky; the outpouring of sweat from your body is the sea of your earth; your hair is the vegetation of your earth; your limbs are the trees of your earth; and so on to all of your parts. When the pillars of your body collapse through death, then the earth has quaked with its quaking {«إِذَا زُلْزِلَتِ الْأَرْضُ زِلْزَالَهَا»}. When the bones separate from the flesh, then the earth has borne its burdens and the mountains have been crushed to powder {«وَحُمِلَتِ الْأَرْضُ وَالْجِبَالُ فَدُكَّتَا دَكَّةً وَاحِدَةً»}. When the bones crumble, then the mountains have been blown away as dust {«وَنُسِفَتِ الْجِبَالُ نَسْفًا»}. When your heart darkens at death, then the sun has been folded up {«كُوِّرَتِ الشَّمْسُ تَكْوِيرًا»}. When your hearing, sight, and all your senses cease, then the stars have been scattered {«وَانْكَدَرَتِ النُّجُومُ انْكِدَارًا»}. When your brain splits, then the sky has been split asunder {«انْشَقَّتِ السَّمَاءُ انْشِقَاقًا»}. When the sweat of your brow bursts forth from the terror of death, then the seas have been caused to burst forth {«فُجِّرَتِ الْبِحَارُ تَفْجِيرًا»}. When one of your legs entwines with the other — and they are your two mounts — then the pregnant she-camels have been neglected {«عُطِّلَتِ الْعِشَارُ تَعْطِيلًا»}. When the soul departs from the body, then the earth has been lifted and stretched until it casts out what is within it and empties itself {«وَأَلْقَتْ مَا فِيهَا وَتَخَلَّتْ»}. I shall not prolong the enumeration of all the corresponding states and terrors, but I say: by mere death, this minor resurrection comes to pass over you, and nothing of the major resurrection that pertains specifically to you escapes you — rather, only what pertains to another escapes you. For what benefit is the survival of the stars to another, when your senses — through which you benefited by gazing at the stars — have been scattered? The blind man finds night and day equal, and the eclipse of the sun and its clearing likewise, for the sun has been eclipsed for him all at once — that being his share of it — while its clearing thereafter is the share of another. And he whose head has been split open has had his sky split, for the sky is but an expression for what lies in the direction of the head; so whoever has no head has no sky — whence, then, would the survival of the sky for another benefit him? This, then, is the minor resurrection; and the fear after it is greater, and the terror after it is deferred — that is when the Great Calamity arrives {«الطَّامَّةُ الْكُبْرَىٰ»}, particularity is lifted, the heavens and the earth are abolished, the mountains are blown away, and the terrors multiply.
84:4.section_title_en: The Minor Resurrection: The Microcosmic Earthquake of Death
84:4.anchors:
- Root: كرم (karuma)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root meaning of nobility, generosity, and honor; al-kirām are those distinguished by noble character and beneficence.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: karāmah denotes the honor bestowed by Allah upon His angels and righteous servants, entailing both dignity and generous bestowal.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): noble, generous in character; Metaphorical (Majaz): the angels described as kirām because of their exalted station and pure obedience, not corporeal nobility.
- Root: كتب (kataba)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To write, inscribe, decree; kitāb as a written record; kataba as the act of fixing something in a permanent form.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-kātibūn are the recording angels (ḥafaẓah) who inscribe deeds; writing here signifies divine preservation of acts in a register accessible to Allah alone.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical inscription on sheets; Metaphorical: the "writing" upon the heart's secret core is an immaterial imprinting (naqsh rūḥānī) imperceptible to corporeal sight.
- Root: موت (mawta)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Death as cessation of animal life; the separation of the soul from the body.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-mawt is not annihilation but a transition (intiqlāl) from one abode to another; the minor resurrection (al-qiyāmah al-ṣughrā) is the individual's death, as per the prophetic saying.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: biological death; Metaphorical: "whoever dies, his resurrection has come to pass" — the term qiyāmah is transferred (majāz) to the moment of death because the full unveiling of one's deeds begins then.
- Root: زلزل (zalzala)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Violent shaking, earthquake; intense agitation of the earth.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: the earthquake is a cosmic sign of divine power; in the microcosm, the death-throes of the body are the individual's own "earthquake."
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: seismic tremor of the earth; Metaphorical: the dissolution of one's own body is a true earthquake relative to that person, since only his own frame is his "earth" — the rest of the globe is another's concern.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب التشبيه والتمثيل (Analogy and Proportional Correspondence) — The syntactic structure equates parts of the human microcosm with the macrocosmic phenomena of the Hour, using fa- (consequence) clauses to map each bodily dissolution to its corresponding cosmic portent.
84:4.topic: Al-Ghazali on the journey of the soul, death, and the Hereafter, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

89:27.arabic: وسمع رجل من أهل التصوف قارئا يقرأ {يا أيتها النفس المطمئنة ارجعي إلى ربك راضية مرضية} فاستعادها من القارىء وقال كم أقول لها ارجعي وليست ترجع وتواجد وزعق زعقة فخرجت روحه وسمع بكر بن معاذ قارئا يقرأ {وأنذرهم يوم الآزفة} الآية فاضطرب ثم صاح ارحم من أنذرته ولم يقبل إليك بعد الإنذار بطاعتك ثم غشى عليه وكان إبراهيم ابن أدهم رحمه الله إذا سمع أحدا يقرأ {إذا السماء انشقت} اضطربت أوصاله حتى كان يرتعد وعن محمد بن صبيح قال كان رجل يغتسل في الفرات فمر به رجل على الشاطىء يقرأ {وامتازوا اليوم أيها المجرمون} فلم يزل الرجل يضطرب حتى غرق ومات وذكر أن سلمان الفارسي أبصر شابا يقرأ فأتى على آية فاقشعر جلده فأحبه سلمان وفقده فسأل عنه فقيل له إنه مريض فأتاه يعوده فإذا هو في الموت فقال يا عبد الله أرأيت تلك القشعريرة التي كانت بي فإنها أتتني في أحسن صورة فأخبرتني أن الله قد غفر لي بها كل ذنب وبالجملة لا يخلو صاحب القلب عن وجد عند سماع القرآن فإن كان القرآن لا يؤثر فيه أصلا ف مثله كمثل الذي ينعق بما لا يسمع إلا دعاء ونداء صم بكم عمي فهم لا يعقلون بل صاحب القلب تؤثر فيه الكلمة من الحكمة يسمعها قال جعفر الخلدي دخل رجل من أهل خراسان على الجنيد وعنده جماعة فقال للجنيد متى يستوي عند العبد حامده وذامه فقال بعض الشيوخ إذا دخل البيمارستان وقيد بقيدين فقال الجنيد ليس هذا من شأنك ثم أقبل على الرجل وقال إذا تحقق أنه مخلوق فشهق الرجل شهقة ومات فإن قلت فإن كان سماع القرآن مفيدا للوجد فما بالهم يجتمعون على سماع الغناء من القوالين دون القارئين فكان ينبغي أن يكون اجتماعهم وتواجدهم في حلق القراء لا حلق المغنين وكان ينبغي أن يطلب عند كل اجتماع في كل دعوة قارىء لأقوال فإن كلام الله تعالى أفضل من الغناء لا محالة فاعلم أن الغناء أشد تهييجا للوجد من القرآن من سبعة أوجه الوجه الأول أن جميع آيات القرآن لا تناسب حال المستمع ولا تصلح لفهمه وتنزيله على ما هو ملابس له فمن استولى عليه حزن أو شوق أو ندم فمن أين يناسب حاله قوله تعالى {يوصيكم الله في أولادكم للذكر مثل حظ الأنثيين} وقوله تعالى {والذين يرمون المحصنات} وكذلك جميع الآيات التي فيها بيان أحكام الميراث والطلاق والحدود وغيرها وإنما المحرك لما في القلب ما يناسبه والأبيات إنما يضعها الشعراء إعرابا بها عن أحوال القلب فلا يحتاج في فهم الحال منها إلى تكلف نعم من يستولي عليه حالة غالبة قاهرة لم تبق فيه متسعا لغيرها ومعه تيقظ وذكاء ثاقب يتفطن به للمعاني البعيدة من الألفاظ فقد يخرج وجده على كل مسموع كمن يخطر له عند ذكر قوله تعالى {يوصيكم الله في أولادكم} حالة الموت المحوج إلى الوصية وأن كل إنسان لا بد أن يخلف ماله وولده وهما محبوباه من الدنيا فيترك أحد المحبوبين للثاني ويهجرهما جميعا فيغلب عليه الخوف والجزع أو يسمع ذكر الله في قوله {يوصيكم الله في أولادكم} فيدهش بمجرد الاسم عما قبله وبعده أو يخطر له رحمة الله على عباده وشفقته بأن تولى قسم مواريثهم بنفسه نظرا لهم في حياتهم وموتهم فيقول إذا نظر لأولادنا بعد موتنا فلا نشك بأنه ينظر لنا فيهيج
89:27.english: Some of the Sufis said: "One night I was reciting this verse: {كُلُّ نَفْسٍ ذَائِقَةُ الْمَوْتِ} «Every soul shall taste death» [Q. 3:185]. I kept repeating it, and lo, a caller cried out to me: 'How long will you repeat this verse? You have killed four of the jinn who have not raised their heads to the sky since they were created.'"
89:27.section_title_en: On the Ecstatic States (Wajd) Produced by Qur'anic Recitation and the Superiority of Song (Ghinā') in Stirring the Heart
89:27.anchors:
- Root: وجد (w-j-d)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of finding, attaining, and also denoting the emotional state of ecstasy or rapture that "finds" the heart.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In the theological context, 'wajd' is the state of spiritual finding—a direct, overwhelming apprehension of divine realities that bypasses discursive reasoning.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah) usage denotes "finding" a lost object; metaphorical (Majaz) usage denotes the heart "finding" its spiritual state, leading to agitation and ecstasy.
- Root: سمع (s-m-')
  * Lisan / Ayn: The faculty of hearing; also the ear itself.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Hearing can be literal (perception of sound) or figurative (understanding, obedience, acceptance). The heart's "hearing" is a deeper comprehension.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "سمعته" (I heard him). Metaphorical: "سمع الله لمن حمده" (God answers/he accepts the one who praises Him), indicating a responsive, transformative hearing.
- Root: موت (m-w-t)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Death; the opposite of life.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Death is the cessation of the soul's governance over the body, a separation. In the spiritual context, it can be a metaphorical death to worldly desires.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical death. Metaphorical: "أحيا الله البلد الميت" (God revives the dead land), indicating spiritual revival or the death of the ego.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — Used to emphasize that the stirring of the heart is exclusively through what is appropriate to its state, as in the phrase "إنما المحرك لما في القلب ما يناسبه" (The only thing that moves what is in the heart is that which is suitable to it).
89:27.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Patience and Gratitude'
