92:5.arabic: بالترغيب بالخير وتيسير الأمر عليه وإليه الإشارة بقوله تعالى فأما من أعطى واتقى وصدق بالحسنى فسنيسره لليسرى وفي مثل هذا القلب يشرق نور المصباح من مكشاة الربوبية حتى لا يخفي فيه الشرك الخفي الذي هو أخفى من دبيب النملة السوداء في الليلة الظلماء فلا يخفى على هذا النور خافية ولا يروج عليه شيء من مكايد الشيطان بل يقف الشيطان ويوحي زخرف القول غرورا فلا يلتفت إليه وهذا القلب بعد طهارته من المهلكات يصير على القرب معمورا بالمنجيات التي سنذكرها من الشكر والصبر والخوف والرجاء والفقر والزهد والمحبة والرضا والشوق والتوكل والتفكر والمحاسبة وغير ذلك وهو القلب
92:5.english: Know that the heart, as we have mentioned, is surrounded by the attributes we have described, and the traces and states pour into it from the gateways we have set forth. It is as if it were a target perpetually struck from every side. When something afflicts it, it is affected by it; then it is struck from another side by that which opposes it, and so its state changes. If the devil descends upon it and calls it to passion (hawā), the angel descends upon it and turns it away from that. If one devil drags it toward evil, another devil drags it toward something else; and if one angel draws it toward good, another draws it toward something else. Thus at times it is contested between two angels, at times between two devils, and at times between an angel and a devil — it is never, ever left neglected. To this points the saying of the Exalted: {وَنُقَلِّبُ أَفْئِدَتَهُمْ وَأَبْصَارَهُمْ} (And We turn their hearts and their visions) {«الأنعام/110»}. And because the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) was privy to the wondrous handiwork of Allah the Exalted in the marvels of the heart and its overturning, he used to swear by it, saying: "No, by the Turner of the hearts." (1)
92:5.section_title_en: The Wonders of the Heart: Its States of Stability, Inclination, and Fluctuation Between the Two Attracting Forces
92:5.anchors:
- Root: قلب (q-l-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To turn a thing over, to revolve it, to divert it from one face to another; the heart is so named for its constant turning and fluctuation.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "قلب الشيء: تصريفه وصرفه عن وجه إلى وجه" — the heart's perpetual overturning is its very essence; its states are never fixed, and its rectitude or corruption follows its turning.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): "قلب الشيء قلبا: حوله عن وجهه" — physical overturning. Metaphorical (Majaz): "رجل قلب حول: يقلب الأمور ويحتال" — one who turns matters over and manages them; the heart's fluctuation between the two attractants is a real, continuous overturning.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The periodic structure of the opening sentence, with its cascading circumstantial clauses, requires careful tracking of the governing verb and its dependent states to preserve the causal sequence of the heart's affliction and response.
92:5.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

95:4.arabic: استعماله في نيل درجة القرب وعن بعدهم وقربهم عبر الله تعالى إذ قال {لقد خلقنا الإنسان في أحسن تقويم ثم رددناه أسفل سافلين إلا الذين آمنوا} الآية فإذن نعم الله تعالى آلات يترقى العبد بها عن أسفل السافلين خلقها الله تعالى لأجل العبد حتى ينال بها سعادة القرب والله تعالى غني عنه قرب أم بعد والعبد فيها بين أن يستعملها في الطاعة فيكون قد شكر لموافقة محبة مولاه وبين أن يستعملها في معصيته فقد كفر لاقتحامه ما يكرهه مولاه ولا يرضاه له فإن الله لا يرضى لعباده الكفر والمعصية وإن عطلها ولم يستعملها في طاعة ولا معصية فهو أيضا كفر كفران إن للنعمة بالتضييع وكل ما خلق في الدنيا إنما خلق آلة للعبد ل
95:4.english: The hadith has already been presented in the Book of Repentance, and before that in the Book of Supplications. That was because of his ascent to seventy stations, some of which are above others. Its beginning — even though it surpassed the utmost limits of [all] creatures — was nevertheless a deficiency relative to its end. Thus his seeking forgiveness was for that [deficiency]. And when ʿĀʾishah, may God be pleased with her, said: "Has God not forgiven you what preceded of your sin and what came after? Then what is this weeping in prostration, and what is this severe exertion?" — PageV04P087 — he {said}: "Shall I not then be a grateful servant?" // The hadith of ʿĀʾishah, when she said to him: "God has forgiven you what preceded of your sin and what came after — so what is this weeping?" — the hadith was narrated by Abū al-Shaykh, and it is the remainder of the hadith of ʿAṭāʾ from her, which preceded this by nine hadiths. It is also in Muslim from the narration of ʿUrwah from her, in abbreviated form. Likewise it is in the Two Ṣaḥīḥs, abbreviated, from the hadith of al-Mughīrah ibn Shuʿbah. Its meaning is: "Shall I not be a seeker of increase in the stations?" — for gratitude is the cause of increase, as God Most High said: {«لئن شكرتم لأزيدنكم»} ["If you are grateful, I will surely increase you"].
95:4.section_title_en: The Reality of Gratitude and Ingratitude — The Parable of the King and the Servant
95:4.anchors:
- Root: شكر (sh-k-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of "opening/disclosing" (kashf) — the opposite of kufr, which is "covering/concealing"; also linked to a full udder (shukrā), i.e., abundance and fullness.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Gratitude is "the conceptualization of the blessing and its manifestation" — threefold: gratitude of the heart (perceiving the blessing), of the tongue (praising the Bestower), and of the limbs (rewarding the blessing through obedience).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (haqīqah): "I thanked God for His blessing." Metaphorical (majāz): A beast that suffices on little fodder yet fattens — gratitude as efficient use of provision for its intended purpose.
- Root: عبد (ʿ-b-d)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Servitude as manifest humility; ʿibādah is the utmost degree of self-abasement before the One deserving ultimate beneficence.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): ʿUbūdiyyah is "displaying humility," while ʿibādah is its extreme — and is of two kinds: by compulsion (all creatures) and by choice (the rational, who are commanded to worship).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "He is a servant (ʿabd) between servitude." Metaphorical: "So-and-so has enslaved me (taʿabbadanī)" — making one like a servant.
- Root: خلق (kh-l-q)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Originary estimation and measuring out (taqdīr) — creation as precise ordainment.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Creation is originally: precise estimation (al-taqdīr al-mustaqīm)" — used for bringing forth from nothing (ibdāʿ) and for fashioning from existing matter.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: The leatherworker "estimates" (khalq) the hide before cutting. Metaphorical: "God created the creation" — brought them into being upon an estimation necessitated by wisdom.
- Root: قرب (q-r-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Nearness in place or station; the opposite of buʿd (distance).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Nearness to God is not spatial but by rank, honor, and obedience — the soul's proximity to the divine presence through virtuous acts.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical proximity. Metaphorical: "nearness to the King" — honor and favor, not spatial contiguity.
- Sibawayh Rule: Restriction and Focused Predication (al-ḥaṣr wa al-taqyīd bi-innamā) — "إنما الشرع كله تعريف طريق" restricts the entire purpose of the Sacred Law to one function: defining the path. Also, conditional and bipartite clauses (al-sharṭ wa al-jawāb) governing "مهما لبس العبد الثوب... فقد شكر" — the protasis-apodosis structure establishing a causal equivalence between action and its moral verdict.
95:4.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

96:6.arabic: كلا إن الإنسان ليطغى أن رآه استغنى وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم إن الله ليحمي عبده المؤمن من الدنيا وهو يحبه كما يحمي أحدكم مريضه (1) وكذلك الزوجة والولد والقريب وكل ما ذكرناه في الأقسام الستة عشر من النعم سوى الإيمان وحسن الخلق فإنها يتصور أن تكون بلاء في حق بعض الناس فتكون أضدادها إذن نعما في حقهم إذ سبق أن المعرفة كمال ونعمة فإنها صفة من صفات الله تعالى ولكن قد تكون على العبد في بعض الأمور بلاء ويكون فقدها نعمة مثاله جهل الإنسان بأجله فإنه نعمة عليه إذ لو عرفه ربما تنغص عليه العيش و
96:6.english: You might say: "What you have mentioned concerning graces (niʿam) indicates that for God most high there is in every existing thing a grace — and this suggests that trial (balā') has no existence at all. So what then is the meaning of patience (ṣabr)? And if trial does exist, then what is the meaning of gratitude (shukr) for trial? For some claimants have asserted that we give thanks for trial, let alone for grace. So how is gratitude for trial conceivable? And how does one give thanks for that which one endures with patience? For patience in trial demands pain, while gratitude demands joy, and the two are mutually opposed. And what is the meaning of what you have mentioned — that for God most high there is in everything He has brought into existence a grace upon His servants?"
96:6.section_title_en: On the Reconciliation of Patience and Gratitude in the Face of Trial — Section 1018
96:6.anchors:
- Root: نعم (n-ʿ-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core sense of softness, ease, and well-being; al-Farahidi notes it as a name for the leopard and tiger, indicating inherent vigor in the state of grace.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "النعمة: الحالة الحسنة" — the goodly state; divided into absolute (mutlaqah) and restricted (muqayyadah), the former being felicity in the Hereafter (nearness to God) and faith in this world.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah) usage denotes the actual state of well-being; metaphorical (Majaz) extension applies to any beneficial circumstance, even apparent hardship, when considered relative to the recipient's ultimate good.
- Root: بلي (b-l-w)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Testing, affliction, and wear of the body; the root implies a state of being tried or proven.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Trial (balā') is that which tests one's state; its existence is affirmed alongside grace (niʿmah) as its contrary, for the absence of grace is a trial and the absence of trial is a grace.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal sense is calamity or hardship; metaphorical sense applies to any condition that, while painful in one respect, may be a vehicle for divine benefit in another.
- Root: صبر (ṣ-b-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Restraint and forbearance; al-Farahidi ties it to holding back the self from complaint.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Patience is the withholding of the soul from agitation and complaint; it is only commanded where the trial cannot be repelled by the servant's own effort.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal usage is enduring pain; metaphorical usage extends to steadfastness in obedience and abstention from sin, which are acts of patience toward the soul's base inclinations.
- Root: شكر (sh-k-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Gratitude as acknowledgment of benefit; al-Farahidi links it to fullness, as a full udder (shukrā).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الشكر: تصور النعمة وإظهارها" — gratitude is the conception of the grace and its manifestation; it is threefold: of the heart (perceiving the grace), of the tongue (praising the Benefactor), and of the limbs (rewarding the grace through obedience).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal sense is verbal and inward acknowledgment; metaphorical sense is the "grateful beast" (dābbah shakūr) that thrives on little fodder — so the servant thrives on little trial, seeing in it abundant divine favor.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — Used to delimit the scope of patience and gratitude: patience is restricted to unavoidable pain, while gratitude is focused on the relative good within that pain, preventing the logical contradiction of their simultaneous application.
96:6.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

96:6.arabic: إلى الله عز وجل ويمنع من نسيانه وأما الغنى فسبب للبطر في غالب الأمور فإن الإنسان ليطغى أن رآه استغنى فهذا ما أردنا أن نورده من جملة الأذكار والدعوات والله الموفق للخير وأما بقية الدعوات في الأكل والسفر وعيادة المريض وغيرها فستأتي في مواضعها إن شاء الله تعالى وعلى الله التكلان نجز كتاب الأذكار والدعوات بكماله يتلوه إن شاء الله تعالى كتاب الأوراد والحمد لله رب العالمين وصلى الله على سيدنا محمد وعلى آله وصحبه وسلم
96:6.english: "O God, whatever blessing has come to me this morning, or to any of Your creatures, it is from You alone, with no partner to You; to You is praise and to You is thanksgiving."
96:6.topic: Al-Ghazali on constant remembrance of God and contemplative invocations, from 'Monotheism and Reliance'

98:5.arabic: الله عليه وسلم إنما الأعمال بالنيات وإنما لكل امرىء ما نوى // وقال تعالى وما أمروا إلا ليعبدوا الله مخلصين له الدين ولهذا قدم الله تعالى الصبر على العمل فقال تعالى إلا الذين صبروا وعملوا الصالحات الحالة الثانية حالة العمل كي لا يغفل عن الله في أثناء عمله ولا يتكاسل عن تحقيق آدابه وسننه ويدوم على شرط الأدب إلى آخر العمل الأخير فيلازم الصبر عن دواعي الفتور إلى الفراغ وهذا أيضا من شدائد الصبر ولعله المراد بقوله تعالى نعم أجر العاملين الذين صبروا أي صبروا إلى تمام العمل الحالة الثالثة بعد الفراغ من العمل إذ يحتاج إلى الصبر عن إفشائه والتظاهر به للسمعة والرياء و
98:5.english: The first kind is obedience. The servant stands in need of patience in performing it, for patience in obedience is severe. This is because the soul (al-nafs) is by its very nature (bi-ṭabʿihā) averse to servitude (al-ʿubūdiyyah) and covets lordship (al-rubūbiyyah). For this reason, one of the knowers of God (al-ʿārifīn) said: "There is no soul but that it conceals within itself what Pharaoh displayed when he said, 'I am your lord most high' {أنا ربكم الأعلى} — but Pharaoh found for it a scope and an acceptance, so he manifested it when he vilified his people and they obeyed him. And there is no one but that he claims this [very thing] with respect to his slave, his servant, his followers, and every one who is under his subjugation and obedience — even if he refrains from manifesting it. For his fury and rage at their shortcomings in serving him, and his enslaving them [in that rage], issues only from an inner concealment of pride (al-kibr) and a contesting of lordship (munāzaʿat al-rubūbiyyah) within the mantle of majesty (ridāʾ al-kibriyāʾ)."
98:5.section_title_en: On Patience in Obedience and Abstinence from Disobedience — The Two Categories of Volitional Acts
98:5.anchors:
- Root: صبر (ṣ-b-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of restraint and retention under constraint; al-Farahidi notes its application to holding back.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الصبر: الإمساك في ضيق" — restraint within hardship; the soul's confinement to what reason and Law require, or its abstention from what they require it to abstain from. It is a generic term whose specific names vary by context: in tribulation it is patience (ṣabr) against despair (jazaʿ); in battle it is courage (shajāʿah) against cowardice.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): "صبرت على ما أكره" (I bore patiently what I dislike) and "صبرت عما أحب" (I held back from what I love). Metaphorical (majāz): "صبرت يمينه" (I bound him by a stringent oath) — extended to any firm constraining.
- Root: ع م ل (ʿ-m-l)
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "العمل: كل فعل يكون من الحيوان بقصد" — every purposeful act of a living being; more specific than mere "act" (fiʿl), and applies to both righteous and wicked deeds.
- Root: ن ف س (n-f-s)
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The soul (nafs) as the seat of volition and desire; its innate inclination (ṭabʿ) is central to Ghazali's argument here.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "نفس" as the self; metaphorical: "دفق نفسه" (he poured out his blood/life).
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction and Focused Predication with innamā) — governing the Prophet's dictum «إنما الأعمال بالنيات» where the predicate is restricted exclusively to intention.
98:5.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

102:5.arabic: ولكن للذين قد وفوا حظهم من نور اليقين فلذلك قال الله تعالى {كلا لو تعلمون علم اليقين لترون الجحيم} أي في الدنيا {ثم لترونها عين اليقين} أي في الآخرة فإذن قد ظهر أن القلب الصالح لملك الآخرة لا يكون إلا عزيزا كالشخص الصالح لملك الدنيا قسمة سادسة حاوية لمجامع النعم اعلم أن النعم تنقسم إلى ما هي غاية مطلوبة لذاتها وإلى ما هي مطلوبة لأجل
102:5.english: As for the first: if it is possible in existence at all, it is at the utmost extreme of remoteness. As for the second: the lower world is overflowing with it. As for the third and fourth: they exist, but at the utmost extreme of rarity. And it is inconceivable that this [rarity] should itself be rare and anomalous — rather, even with its rarity, it varies in degree of fewness and abundance. Its abundance occurs only in ages proximate to the ages of the Prophets, peace be upon them. The longer the interval [from their time] grows, the scarcer such hearts become, until the Hour draws near and God accomplishes a matter already decreed ( {وكان أمرا مفعولا} ).
102:5.section_title_en: The Division of Hearts and the Rarity of the Heart Fit for the Kingdom of the Hereafter
102:5.anchors:
- Root: م ل ك (Malaka)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of possession, dominion, and sovereign control; al-Ayn notes the pattern shift in derived nouns.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الملك: هو المتصرف بالأمر والنهي في الجمهور" — kingship is governance over rational beings, divided into actual sovereignty (al-tamalluk) and capacity for it (al-quwwah).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "لله الملك والملكوت" — dominion over the visible and invisible realms. Metaphorical: "ملك نفسه عند الغضب" — self-mastery; here extended to the heart's sovereignty over the soul's appetites.
- Root: ق ل ب (Qalaba)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Turning and overturning a thing from one state to another.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "قلب الشيء: تصريفه وصرفه عن وجه إلى وجه" — the heart is so named for its constant fluctuation between states.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "قلب الشيء قلبا: حوله عن وجهه." Metaphorical: "رجل قلب حول: يقلب الأمور ويحتال" — one who turns matters over; here, hearts are classified by their dominant orientation.
- Root: ع ل م (ʿAlima)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Foundational knowing and perception.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "العلم: إدراك الشيء بحقيقته" — apprehension of a thing's true reality, of two kinds: grasping the essence, and judging its attributes.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "هو من أعلام العلم الخافقه" — knowledge as a raised banner. Here, "علم اليقين" (knowledge of certainty) vs. "عين اليقين" (eye of certainty) marks the literal-to-metaphorical ascent from inference to direct vision.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — The repeated use of "إنما" (only/indeed) throughout this passage serves to restrict predicates exclusively to their subjects, e.g., "وإنما تكون كثرته في الأعصار القريبة" — restricting abundance to specific eras, and "وإنما وجب أن يكون هذا نادرا" — restricting the cause of rarity.
102:5.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

2:27.arabic: فهو في النار وقاض قضى بغير ما أمر الله به فهو في النار (2) وقال كعب رحمه الله يكون في آخر الزمان علماء يزهدون الناس في الدنيا ولا يزهدون ويخوفون الناس ولا يخافون وينهون عن غشيان الولاة ويأتونهم ويؤثرون الدنيا على الآخرة يأكلون بألسنتهم يقربون الأغنياء دون الفقراء يتغايرون على العلم كما تتغاير النساء على الرجال يغضب أحدهم على جليسه إذا جالس غيره أولئك الجبارون أعداء الرحمن وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم إن الشيطان ربما يسوفكم بالعلم فقيل يا رسول الله وكيف ذلك قال صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول اطلب الع
2:27.english: Know that the scholar who does not act upon his knowledge is condemned by the Book, the Sunnah, and the sayings of the sages. God, exalted be He, said: {«يا أيها الذين آمنوا لم تقولون ما لا تفعلون * كبر مقتا عند الله أن تقولوا ما لا تفعلون»} ("O you who believe, why do you say what you do not do? Most hateful it is to God that you say what you do not do"). And He said: {«أتأمرون الناس بالبر وتنسون أنفسكم»} ("Do you command people to righteousness while you forget yourselves?"). And He said: {«ومن الناس من يعجبك قوله في الحياة الدنيا ويشهد الله على ما في قلبه وهو ألد الخصام»} ("And among people is he whose speech pleases you in the worldly life, and he calls God to witness what is in his heart, yet he is the fiercest of opponents").
2:27.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Book of Knowledge'

2:27.arabic: يسعون في قطع ما أمر الله به أن يوصل ويفسدون في الأرض وقال تعالى {إنما السبيل على الذين يظلمون الناس ويبغون في الأرض بغير الحق} والنمام منهم وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم إن من شرار الناس
2:27.english: And whoever is the recipient of tale-bearing — it being said to him: "So-and-so said such-and-such about you," or "He did such-and-such against you," or "He is scheming to corrupt your affair," or "He is conspiring with your enemy," or "He is disparaging your condition," or whatever runs in that course — then six matters are incumbent upon him:
2:27.section_title_en: Section 692 — On the Duties of the One to Whom Tale-Bearing (Namīmah) Is Conveyed
2:27.anchors:
- Root: ن-م-م (N-M-M)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning — to stir up, incite, or carry tales; the one who transmits speech to cause discord.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance — namīmah is a species of corrupt speech that severs what God has commanded to be joined; it is aligned with fāsiq (transgressor) status, rendering the bearer's testimony rejected.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal vs Metaphorical — literally, the act of carrying and dropping seeds (naml) to cause sprouting; metaphorically, the dropping of speech into hearts to sow enmity.
- Root: غ-ي-ب (Gh-Y-B)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning — that which is concealed from the senses.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance — ghaybah (backbiting) is the mention of a person in his absence with what he dislikes; it is a violation of the unseen honor of the brother.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal vs Metaphorical — literal absence from sight; metaphorical — the absence of the subject from the gathering while his reputation is being torn.
- Root: ف-س-ق (F-S-Q)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning — to depart, to deviate from the straight path.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance — fisq is the breaking of the command of God; the fāsiq's report is not to be trusted without verification, per {إِن جَاءَكُمْ فَاسِقٌ بِنَبَإٍ فَتَبَيَّنُوا}.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal vs Metaphorical — literal: the date that peels from its husk; metaphorical: the soul that peels from obedience.
- Sibawayh Rule: Bāb al-Ḥaṣr wa al-Taqyīd bi-innamā (Restriction & Focused Predication) — The verse {إِنَّمَا السَّبِيلُ عَلَى الَّذِينَ يَظْلِمُونَ النَّاسَ} restricts the path of blame exclusively to the oppressors, thereby excluding the tale-bearer's victim from any culpability and affirming the tale-bearer's full liability.
2:27.topic: Classical commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya Ulum al-Din, from 'Condemnation of Anger and Hatred'

2:174.arabic: حديث عبد الرحمن بن شبل وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم ثلاثة نفر لا يكلمهم الله يوم القيامة ولا ينظر إليهم المنان بعطيته والمنفق سلعته بالحلف الفاجر والمسبل إزاره (7) وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم من حلف حالف بالله فأدخل فيها مثل جناح بعوضة إلا كانت نكتة في قلبه إلى يوم القيامة (8) حديث أبي ذر ثلاثة يحبهم الله
2:174.english: I say: Now we turn to the fourteenth affliction—lying in speech and in oaths. This is among the most abominable of sins and the most heinous of faults. Isma'il ibn Wasit said: I heard Abu Bakr al-Siddiq—may God be pleased with him—delivering a sermon after the death of the Messenger of God—peace be upon him—and he said: The Messenger of God—peace be upon him—stood among us in this very place of mine one year ago. Then he wept—Page V03P133—and said: Beware of lying, for it is coupled with wickedness (fujur), and the two are in the Fire. (1)
2:174.section_title_en: The Fourteenth Affliction: Lying in Speech and in Oaths
2:174.anchors:
- Root: كذب (Kadhaba)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root denotes the contrivance of falsehood in speech or action; the Kitab al-Ayn treats it as the antithesis of truthfulness (sidq), encompassing both verbal assertion and behavioral deception.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Lying (kadhib) applies to both speech (maqal) and deed (fi'l), as in the Quranic verse {«وَاللَّهُ يَشْهَدُ إِنَّ الْمُنَافِقِينَ لَكَاذِبُونَ»} where the hypocrites' claim of faith is false in their conviction, not necessarily in their utterance—thus lying is a corruption of the inner reality manifesting outwardly.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (haqiqah) usage is the utterance of falsehood; metaphorical (majaz) usage includes "kadhaba al-nāqah" (the she-camel's milk dried up, i.e., her promise of milk proved false) and "kadhaba al-rajul" (he turned coward after boasting), where the action itself is described as lying—indicating that lying encompasses any breach of what is expected or claimed.
- Root: حلف (Halafa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The root denotes swearing an oath (yamin), and in the Kitab al-Ayn, al-hilf is the covenant or compact between parties, with al-halif being one bound by such an oath.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-hilf is the covenant ('ahd) between people, and al-muhalafah is mutual pact-making; it is also used metaphorically for enduring attachment, as in "hulayf al-karam" (the ally of generosity), signifying a binding commitment.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal usage is swearing by God; metaphorical usage extends to any firm alliance or inseparable bond, as in "hulayf al-sahar" (the companion of sleeplessness), showing the root's semantic range from oath to lifelong adherence.
- Sibawayh Rule: Bab al-'Atf 'ala al-Mawdi' (Coordination on Syntactic Position) — When multiple clauses are coordinated, the second element may be parsed according to the governing context of the first, allowing for elision of repeated verbs or prepositions, as in the hadith structure where "wa huma fi al-nar" is coordinated with the preceding clause's implied judgment.
2:174.topic: Al-Ghazali on the journey of the soul, death, and the Hereafter, from 'Condemnation of Anger and Hatred'

2:174.arabic: وسلم ثلاثة لا يكلمهم الله ولا ينظر إليهم ولا يزكيهم ولهم عذاب أليم شيخ زان وملك كذاب وعائل مستكبر (4) حديث عبد الله بن عامر جاء رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إلى بيتنا وأنا صبي صغير فذهبت لألعب فقالت أمي يا عبد الله تعال أعطيك فقال وما أردت أن تعطيه قالت تمرا فقال إن لم تفعلي كتبت عليك كذبة رواه أبو داود وفيه من لم يسم وقال الحاكم أن عبد الله بن عامر ولد في حياته صلى الله عليه وسلم ولم يسمع منه قلت وله شاهد من حديث أبي هريرة وابن مسعود ورجالهما ثقات إلا أن الزهري لم يسمع من أبي هريرة وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم لو أف
2:174.english: Among them is the hadith: "And three whom God hates: the trader or seller who swears much." Ahmad narrated it, and the wording is his. In its chain is Ibn al-Aḥmaṣ, whose condition is unknown. Both Ahmad and al-Nasā'ī narrated it with another wording through a sound chain. And al-Nasā'ī has, from the hadith of Abū Hurayrah: "Four whom God abhors: the seller who swears much" — the hadith — and its chain is sound.
2:174.section_title_en: The Book of the Revival of the Religious Sciences — Section 676: On Lying (al-Kadhib) — Hadith Reports and Traditions (Āthār)
2:174.anchors:
- Root: كذب (Kadhaba)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to report a falsehood, to utter what is contrary to reality; al-Kadhdhābah: a variegated cloth that deceives the eye into thinking it is part of the ceiling — indicating the deceptive semblance of truth.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Kadhib applies to both speech and action. God says: {«Only they forge falsehood who do not believe in God's signs»} (Q 16:105) — the hypocrites' speech was true, but their inward conviction was false, so God called them liars (kādhibūn) regarding their belief.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqīqah): "He is kadhib, kadhūb, kadhāb, kaydhabān" — one who lies habitually. Metaphorical (Majāz): "He carried [the burden] then lied" — i.e., he cowardly retreated, making his charge a false one; "the she-camel lied" — her pregnancy proved false.
- Root: حدث (Ḥadatha)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to originate, to bring into being after non-existence; al-ḥadīth: speech that is new/recently originated.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Al-Ḥudūth: a thing's coming to be after it was not — whether accident or substance. Its creation (iḥdāth) belongs solely to God. Al-muḥdath: what is brought into existence after non-existence." God says: {«There comes not to them a fresh reminder (dhikr muḥdath) from their Lord»} (Q 21:2).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "He spoke a ḥadīth; fresh in age." Metaphorical: "They became aḥādīth (topics of talk)"; ʿUmar was called muḥaddath — one whose intuition is divinely inspired, as if truth were spoken into him.
- Root: ويل (Wayl)
  * Lisan / Ayn: An expression of intense woe, destruction, and chastisement; a word of threat and condemnation.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Wayl denotes severe affliction and ruin; it is a declaration of impending punishment.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "Woe to him" — a cry of ruin. Used in threats: "Waylun lahu" — destruction is his due.
- Root: شنأ (Shana'a)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Intense hatred and abhorrence.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-Shan'ān: intense hatred that drives one to shun the object.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "He hated him with shan'an" — vehement hatred.
- Sibawayh Rule: Bāb al-Ḥaṣr wa al-Taqyīd bi-innamā (Restriction and Focused Predication) — The particle innamā restricts the predicate to the subject alone, negating it for all else. Applied in the verse: {«Only they forge falsehood who do not believe»} — restricting fabrication to the disbelievers, affirming that the believer does not lie.
2:174.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'Condemnation of Anger and Hatred'

2:190.arabic: وسلم فقال نعم إن الله لا يحب المستكبرين فنزل وقعد معهم على الأرض وأكل ثم سلم عليهم وركب وقال قد أجبتكم فأجيبوني قالوا نعم فوعدهم وقتا معلوما فحضروا فقدم إليهم فاخر الطعام وجلس يأكل معهم وأما قول القائل إن من وضعت يدي في قصعته فقد ذلت له رقبتي فقد قال بعضهم هذا خلاف السنة وليس كذلك فإنه ذل إذا كان الداعي لا يفرح بالإجابة ولا يتقلد منة وكان يرى ذلك يدا له على المدعو ورسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كان يحضر لعلمه أن الداعي له يتقلد منة ويرى ذلك شرفا وذخرا لنفسه في الدنيا
2:190.english: The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Do not burden your guest so that you make him hate you, for whoever hates his guest has hated Allah, and whoever hates Allah, Allah hates him."
2:190.section_title_en: The Etiquettes of Hospitality: Invitation, Response, Attendance, and the Serving of Food — Section 290 of The Revival of the Religious Sciences
2:190.anchors:
- Root: ضيف (ḍ-y-f)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning is "to incline, to lean toward." The guest (al-ḍayf) is one who inclines toward you, alighting as a visitor; the root carries the sense of leaning or bending.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The guest is "one who inclines to you, alighting with you"; hospitality (al-ḍiyāfah) became customary in the sense of receiving such a one. The word is originally a verbal noun, hence one and many are equal in most usage.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): "ḍāfa ilayhi: he inclined toward him"; "ḍāfat al-shams: the sun inclined toward setting." Metaphorical (majāz): "aḍāfa ilayhi amran: he attributed a matter to him, leaning it upon him"; "al-muḍāf: the one constrained, hemmed in, in distress."
- Sibawayh Rule: Restriction and Focused Predication (al-ḥaṣr wa al-taqyīd bi-innamā) — governing the Prophet's statement "innamā hādhihi al-akhlāq bi-yad Allāh" (these morals are only in the hand of Allah), where innamā restricts the attribution of moral character exclusively to divine bestowal.
2:190.topic: Al-Ghazali on purifying the character, moral diseases, and spiritual remedies, from 'Condemnation of Anger and Hatred'

2:254.arabic: وسلم قال من كانت لأخيه عنده مظلمة في عرض أو مال فليستحللها منه من قبل أن يأتي يوم ليس هناك دينار ولا درهم إنما يؤخذ من حسناته فإن لم يكن له حسنات أخذ من سيئات صاحبه فزيدت على سيئاته (1) وقالت عائشة رضي الله عنها لامرأة قالت لأخرى أنها طويلة الذيل قد اغتبتيها فاستحليها فإذن لا بد من الاستحلال إن قدر عليه فإن كان غائبا أو ميتا فينبغي أن يكثر له الاستغفار والدعاء ويكثر من الحسنات فإن قلت فالتحليل هل يجب فأقول لا لأنه تبرع والتبرع فضل وليس بواجب ولكنه مستحسن وسبيل المعتذر أن يبالغ في الثناء عليه والتودد إليه
2:254.english:
- Root: غيب (gh-y-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "To be absent, hidden, concealed from sight; ghayb = that which is unseen/absent from perception"
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الغيب: مصدر غابت الشمس وغيرها: إذا استترت عن العين — used of everything absent from the senses and from human knowledge; applied to things as ghayb/ghā'ib relative to people, not relative to God, for nothing is absent from Him"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Haqiqah: "تكلم بذلك عن ظهر الغيب" (speaking of the unseen); Majaz: "أتونا في غابة" (metaphorical extension to dense/thick things)
- Root: حسن (ḥ-s-n)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "Beauty, goodness, excellence; to be fair, comely, good"
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الحسن: عبارة عن كل مبهج مرغوب فيه — three kinds: good by reason, good by desire, good by sense; ḥasanah = everything that delights one, whether in self, body, or circumstances"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Haqiqah: "أنظر إلى محاسن وجهه" (physical beauty); Majaz: "فلان لا يحسن شيئًا" (to do well/excel — transferred to action)
- Root: حرم (ḥ-r-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "To forbid, prohibit, make unlawful; ḥarām = that which is forbidden"
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الحرام: الممنوع منه إما بتسخير إلهي وإما بشري — prohibition by divine decree, by human law, by coercive prevention, by reason, or by revelation"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Haqiqah: "هتك رحمته" (violating sanctity); Majaz: "جلد محرم: لم يدبغ" (raw hide — metaphorical extension to "untreated/unlawful")
- Root: ظلم (ẓ-l-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "Wrongdoing, injustice, oppression; to place something in other than its proper place"
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الظلمة: عدم النور — darkness is absence of light; used metaphorically for ignorance, polytheism, and sin, just as light is used for their opposites"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Haqiqah: "فلان يظلم فيظلم" (to wrong and be wronged); Majaz: "أرض مظلومة" (land never dug — metaphorical: "wronged" land)
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — "إنما يؤخذ من حسناته" restricts the taking exclusively to good deeds, excluding any monetary compensation on that Day.
2:254.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'Condemnation of Anger and Hatred'

2:254.arabic: وقد قال الله تعالى يا أيها الذين آمنوا أنفقوا من طيبات ما كسبتم ومما أخرجنا لكم من الأرض ولا تيمموا الخبيث منه تنفقون ولستم بآخذيه إلا أن تغمضوا فيه أي لا تأخذوه إلا مع كراهية وحياء وهو معنى الإغماض فلا تؤثروا به ربكم وفي الخبر سبق درهم مائة ألف درهم (3) وذلك بأن يخرجه الإنسان وهو من أحل ماله وأجوده فيصدر ذلك عن الرضا والفرح بالبذل وقد يخرج مائة ألف درهم مما يكره من ماله فيدل ذلك على أنه ليس يؤثر الله عز وجل بشيء مما يحبه وبذلك ذم الله تعالى قوما جعلوا لله ما يكرهون فقال تعال
2:254.english: The heart is not treated save with the compound electuary (maʿjūn) of knowledge and works. And this condition among the conditions of almsgiving runs in the same course as humility (al-khushūʿ) runs in the prayer. This is established by his saying — may Allah bless him and grant him peace: "A man has nothing of his prayer save that of which he was conscious." And this is like his saying — may Allah bless him and grant him peace: "Allah does not accept the charity of the one who bestows it with reproach (al-mannān)." And like His saying — Exalted is He: {«لا تبطلوا صدقاتكم بالمن والأذى»} ("Do not nullify your charities by reproach and injury"). As for the legal opinion (fatwā) of the jurist that the alms fall in their proper place and that one's liability is discharged without this condition — that is another discussion, and we have already pointed to its meaning in the Book of Prayer.
2:254.section_title_en: The Inner Conditions of Charity — Section 175 (From The Revival of the Religious Sciences, Book of the Mysteries of Almsgiving)
2:254.anchors:
- Root: قلب (q-l-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "To turn, overturn, transform a thing from one state to another; to rotate, to flip"
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "قلب الشيء: تصريفه وصرفه عن وجه إلى وجه" — the heart is so named because of its constant turning and transformation between states
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "قلب الشيء قلبا: حوله عن وجهه" (to turn a thing from its face). Metaphorical: "رجل قلب حول: يقلب الأمور ويحتال" — one who turns matters over and manages them; "قلبوا لك الأمور" (they turned matters against you)
- Root: وجل (w-j-l)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "Fear, dread, apprehension that strikes the heart"
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الوجل: استشعار الخوف" — the sensing of fear; cited in {«إنما المؤمنون الذين إذا ذكر الله وجلت قلوبهم»}
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "رجل وجل، وقوم وجال" — a fearful man, a fearful people; "وفي قلبه وجل" — in his heart is dread
- Root: عجب (ʿ-j-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "Wonder, amazement; self-admiration, vanity"
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Self-admiration (al-ʿujb) is a destructive spiritual ailment that nullifies deeds
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: wonder at something extraordinary. Metaphorical: self-conceit regarding one's own acts of obedience
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد (Restriction & Focused Predication) — governing the precise limitation of general categories (al-ṣifāt al-khāṣṣah within al-aṣnāf al-thamāniyyah) and the conditional structure of acceptance

3:128.arabic: قنوته شهرا فنزل قوله تعالى ليس لك من الأمر شيء أو يتوب عليهم أو يعذبهم فإنهم ظالمون (2) يعني أنهم ربما يسلمون فمن أين تعلم أنهم ملعونون وكذلك من بان لنا موته على الكفر جاز لعنه وجاز ذمه إن لم يكن فيه أذى على مسلم فإن كان لم يجز كما روي أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم سأل أبا بكر رضي الله عنه عن قبر مر به وهو يريد الطائف فقال هذا قبر رجل كان عاتيا على الله ورسوله وهو سعيد بن العاص فغضب ابنه عمرو بن سعيد وقال يا رسول الله هذا قبر رجل كان أطعم للطعام وأضرب للهام من أبي قحافة فقال أبو بكر يكلمني هذا يا رسول الله بمثل هذا الكل
3:128.english: Know that cursing (al-laʿn) is an expression denoting expulsion and distancing (al-ṭard wa-al-ibʿād) from God, the Exalted. This is not permissible except upon one who is characterized by an attribute that distances him from God, the Mighty and Majestic — namely, unbelief (al-kufr) and wrongdoing (al-ẓulm) — such that one says: "May the curse of God be upon the wrongdoers" and "upon the unbelievers." One ought to follow therein the wording of the Sacred Law (al-sharʿ), for in cursing there is danger, because it is a judgment upon God, the Mighty and Majestic, that He has indeed distanced the cursed one — and that is an unseen matter (ghayb) which none can perceive save God, the Exalted, and His Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, when God discloses it to him.
3:128.section_title_en: On the Prohibition of Cursing (Laʿn) and Its Degrees of Permissibility
3:128.anchors:
- Root: لعن (la-ʿa-n)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of expulsion, driving away, and casting out with vehemence.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance — cursing as divine exclusion (ṭard wa-ibʿād) from mercy, a judgment upon the spiritual state of the cursed.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah) — "طرده وأبعده" (to drive out and distance); Metaphorical (Majaz) — "أبيت اللعن" as a pre-Islamic royal acclamation meaning "I have not done what would merit cursing," showing the term's extension to moral desert.
- Root: رسل (r-s-l)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Sending forth with ease and gentleness; a messenger (rasūl) as one dispatched.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The prophetic dispatch (baʿth) as the origin of the term; the Messenger as the one sent with a message.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — "أرسل الله في الأمم رسلا" (God sent messengers among the nations); Metaphorical — "السهام رسل المنايا" (arrows are the messengers of death), showing the extension of sending to divine decree.
- Root: حدث (ḥ-d-th)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Origination after non-existence; a new event (ḥādith).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الحدوث: كون الشيء بعد أن لم يكن" — the coming-to-be of a thing after it was not; divine origination (ījād) as exclusive to God.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — "نزلت به حوادث الدهر" (the vicissitudes of time befell him); Metaphorical — "كان عمر محدثا" (ʿUmar was one inspired with true discernment), as if spoken to by unseen reality.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The permissibility of interposing elements between a governing word and its governed prepositional phrase, provided the intervening clause is complete in itself, as in the conditional structures governing the permissibility of cursing specific individuals.
3:128.topic: Al-Ghazali on purifying the character, moral diseases, and spiritual remedies, from 'Condemnation of Anger and Hatred'

3:128.arabic: ويقول كيف يفلح قوم خضبوا وجه نبيهم بالدم وهو يدعوهم إلى ربهم (4) فأنزل الله تعالى {ليس لك من الأمر شيء} تأديبا له على ذلك وأمثال هذه التأديبات في القرآن لا تحصر وهو صلى الله عليه وسلم المقصود الأول بالتأديب والتهذيب ثم منه يشرق النور على كافة الخلق فإنه أدب بالقرآن وأدب الخلق به ولذلك قال صلى الله عليه وسلم بعثت لأتمم مكارم الأخلاق (5) ثم رغب الخلق في محاسن الأخلاق بما أوردناه في كتاب رياضة النفس وتهذيب الأخلاق فلا نعيده ثم لما أكمل الله تعالى خلقه أثنى عليه فقال تعالى {وإنك لعلى خلق عظيم} فسبحانه ما أعظم شأنه وأتم امتنانه ثم انظر
3:128.english: The Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, was abundant in supplication and earnest entreaty, perpetually asking God Most High to adorn him with the beauties of refined conduct and the noble traits of character. Thus he would say in his supplication: "O God, beautify my outward form and my inward character (khuluqī wa-khalqī)" (1), and he would say: "O God, protect me from the reprehensible traits of character" (2). God Most High answered his supplication, fulfilling His word, Exalted is He: {«ادعوني أستجب لكم»} ["Call upon Me, I will answer you"] (Ghafir 40:60). So He sent down upon him the Qur'an and disciplined him through it, and his character became the Qur'an.
3:128.section_title_en: The Prophet's Discipline Through the Qur'an and the Invitation to Noble Moral Traits
3:128.anchors:
- Root: خلق (khalaqa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of measuring, fashioning, and creating upon a precise estimation; also used for innate disposition and character.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الخلق أصله: التقدير المستقيم" — the root denotes straight/right estimation; used for bringing something into being from nothing (ibdāʿ) and for the moral constitution of the soul.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): "خلق الخراز الأديم" — the leather-worker measures before cutting. Metaphorical (Majaz): "خلق الله الخلق: أوجده على تقدير أوجبته الحكمة" — God's creation is bringing into existence upon a measure required by wisdom; and "له خلق حسن" — he has beautiful character.
- Root: كرم (karuma)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Generosity, nobility, honor; the root of karīm (noble/generous) and makārim (noble traits).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الكرم إذا وصف الله تعالى به فهو اسم لإحسانه وإنعامه المتظاهر" — when attributed to God, it denotes His manifest beneficence; when attributed to man, it denotes praiseworthy morals and deeds that appear from him.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "كرم علينا فلان كرامة" — he showed generosity. Metaphorical: "قوم كرم" — a noble people; "كرم السحاب تكريما: جاد بمطره" — the cloud was generous with its rain.
- Root: أدب (adaba)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Refinement, discipline, cultivation of character; calling to a gathering (ma'dabah) — the root implies assembling and summoning toward excellence.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Discipline (ta'dīb) is the cultivation of the soul through praiseworthy traits and the restraint from blameworthy ones.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "أدبته تأديبا" — I disciplined him. Metaphorical: "أدبه الله" — God disciplined him, i.e., refined his character through divine instruction.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — "إنما أدبه القرآن" restricts the means of the Prophet's discipline exclusively to the Qur'an, affirming that the Qur'an alone was the sufficient and complete instrument of his moral formation.
3:128.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications, prayers, and their spiritual power, from 'Condemnation of Anger and Hatred'

4:11.arabic: يوم القيامة إلى من اغتابه بدلا عما استباحه من عرضه فإن لم تكن له حسنات نقل إليه من سيئات خصمه وهو مع ذلك متعرض لمقت الله عز وجل ومشبه عنده بآكل الميتة بل العبد يدخل النار بأن تترجح كفة سيئاته على كفة حسناته وربما تنقل إليه سيئة واحدة ممن اغتابه فيحصل بها الرجحان ويدخل بها النار وإنما أقل الدرجات أن تنقص من ثواب أعماله وذلك بعد المخاصمة والمطالبة والسؤال والجواب والحساب قال صلى الله عليه وسلم ما النار في اليبس بأسرع من الغيبة في حسنات العبد (2) وروي أن رجلا قال للحسن بلغني أنك تغتابني فقال ما بلغ من قدرك عندي أ
4:11.english: As for the summary: it is that he know that by his backbiting he exposes himself to the wrath of God — exalted is He — according to these reports which we have related; and that he know that backbiting obliterates his good deeds on the Day of Resurrection, for it transfers his good deeds on the Day of Resurrection to the one he backbit, in exchange for what he unlawfully took of his honor. And if he has no good deeds, then there is transferred to him from the evil deeds of his adversary. And he is, moreover, exposed to the wrath of God — mighty and majestic is He — and is likened in His sight to an eater of carrion. Nay, the servant enters the Fire because the scale of his evil deeds outweighs the scale of his good deeds; and perhaps a single evil deed is transferred to him from the one he backbit, and by it the outweighing occurs, and by it he enters the Fire. And the least of the degrees is that it diminishes the reward of his works — and that after the dispute, the demand, the question, the answer, and the reckoning. He said — peace be upon him: {«ما النار في اليبس بأسرع من الغيبة في حسنات العبد»} "Fire is not swifter in dry wood than backbiting is in the good deeds of a servant." And it is related that a man said to al-Hasan: "It has reached me that you backbite me." He said: "It has not reached the extent of your worth in my sight that I should make you the arbiter over my good deeds." So when the servant believes in what has come down of the reports concerning backbiting, he will not unleash his tongue upon it, out of fear of that. And it also benefits him to reflect upon himself: for if he finds in himself a fault, he occupies himself with his own fault and recalls his saying — peace be upon him: {«طوبى لمن شغله عيبه عن عيوب الناس»} "Blessed is he whose own fault occupies him from the faults of people."
4:11.section_title_en: The Cure of the Tongue from Backbiting: General and Specific Remedies
4:11.anchors:
- Root: غيب (ghayb)
  * Lisan / Ayn: That which is hidden from the senses; absence from sight.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Used of what is absent from human perception, though nothing is absent from God.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: concealment from the eye. Metaphorical: speaking of one in his absence (ghībah).
- Root: عيب (ʿayb)
  * Lisan / Ayn: A flaw, defect, or blemish; to find fault with another.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Moral deficiency that diminishes one's perfection before God.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: a mark of deficiency. Metaphorical: moral failing that warrants self-reproach rather than blame of others.
- Root: غضب (ghaḍab)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Anger; violent displeasure.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Divine wrath as the consequence of transgression against divine commands.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: agitation of the soul. Metaphorical: God's punitive will against the disobedient.
- Sibawayh Rule: Conditional and Exceptive Constructions (Bāb al-sharṭ wa-l-istithnāʾ) — Governing the logical structure of remedies conditioned upon causes.
4:11.topic: Al-Ghazali on the journey of the soul, death, and the Hereafter, from 'Condemnation of Anger and Hatred'

4:11.arabic: محصورا على مصلاه الذي يصلي عليه فإن لم يكن له مصلى فليقرب من جدار الحائط أو ليخط خطا فإن ذلك يقصر مسافة البصر ويمنع تفوق الفكر وليحجر على بصره أن يجاوز أطراف المصلى وحدود الخط وليدم على هذا القيام كذلك إلى الركوع من غير التفات هذا أدب القيام فإذا استوى قيامه واستقباله وإطراقه كذلك فليقرأ {قل أعوذ برب الناس} تحصنا به من الشيطان ثم ليأت بالإقامة وإن كان يرجو حضور من يقتدي به فليؤذن أولا ثم ليحضر النية وهو أن ينوي في الظهر مثلا ويقول بقلبه أؤدي فريضة الظهر لله ليميزها بقول
4:11.english: This is the etiquette of standing. When his standing, his facing, and his lowering of the head are even, let him recite {«قُلْ أَعُوذُ بِرَبِّ النَّاسِ»} (Say: I seek refuge in the Lord of mankind), seeking protection thereby from the devil. Then let him perform the iqāmah. And if he hopes for the presence of one who will follow him in prayer, let him give the adhān first. Then let him bring forth the intention (niyyah), which is that he intends, for example, in the ẓuhr prayer, saying in his heart: "I perform the obligatory ẓuhr prayer for Allah," distinguishing it by his utterance: "I perform it as an obligation (adāʾan)" from the make-up prayer (qaḍāʾ), and by "obligatory" from the supererogatory (nafl), and by "ẓuhr" from the ʿaṣr and others. Let the meanings of these words be present in his heart, for that [presence] is the intention itself, while the words are reminders and causes for its presence. Let him strive to sustain this [intention] until the end of the takbīr, so that it does not slip away.
4:11.section_title_en: Section 126 — The Second Book on the Manner of the Outward Acts of Prayer, Beginning with the Takbīr and What Precedes It
4:11.anchors:
- Root: صفن (ṣafana)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To draw up one leg and sit upon it; also used of a horse standing on three legs, raising the fourth.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The posture of drawing up one foot, as in the description of the swift horses {«الصَّافِنَاتُ الْجِيَادُ»} (the standing steeds, the swift).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the physical posture of raising one leg. Metaphorical: not applicable here; used strictly in its corporeal sense.
- Root: صفد (ṣafada)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To fetter, bind, or chain together; al-ṣafad is the iron shackle.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Binding in chains, as in {«مُقَرَّنِينَ فِي الْأَصْفَادِ»} (bound together in fetters).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical binding of the feet together. The Prophet (peace be upon him) prohibited both postures in prayer as they mimic the bound or the beast.
- Root: قصد (qaṣada)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To intend, aim, or direct oneself toward something; also moderation and evenness.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The intention (niyyah) that directs the heart toward the act, distinguishing one act from another.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: to stand upright and face a direction. Metaphorical: the heart's orientation toward the divine command.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The syntactic principle that governs the placement of prepositional phrases, here applied to the physical orientation of the body toward the qiblah as a grammatical parallel to the soul's orientation toward Allah.
4:11.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Condemnation of Anger and Hatred'

4:11.arabic: بالولود الودود (1) فإن لم يكن لها زوج ولم يعرف حالها فيراعي صحتها وشبابها فإنها تكون ولودا في الغالب مع هذين الوصفين السادسة أن تكون بكرا قال صلى الله عليه وسلم لجابر وقد نكح ثيبا هلا بكرا تلاعبها وتلاعبك (2) في البكارة ثلاث فوائد إحداها أن تحب الزوج وتألفه فيؤثر في معنى الود وقد قال صلى الله عليه وسلم عليكم بالودود والطباع مجبولة على الأنس بأول مألوف وأما التي اختبرت الرجال ومارست الأحوال فربما لا ترضى بعض الأوصاف التي تخالف ما ألفته فتقلي الزوج الثانية أن ذلك أكمل في مودته
4:11.english: ...one of you sees a woman, let him look at her, for that is more likely to bring about harmony (iʾtilāf) between them — that is, to unite them — than the mere occurrence of the inner skin (al-adamah) upon the outer skin (al-basharah). He only mentioned that for emphasis on the union. And he, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Verily, in the eyes of the Ansar there is something, so when one of you wishes to marry from among them, let him look at them." It was said that there was a weakness of the eyes (ʿamash) in them, and it was said it was smallness of the eyes. And some of the scrupulous (al-warʿīn) would not marry their noble women except after looking, as a precaution against deception (al-ghurūr).
4:11.section_title_en: The Revival of the Religious Sciences — Book on the Etiquettes of Marriage: Section 301 — On the Recommended Attributes of the Wife (Continued)
4:11.anchors:
- Root: أدم (ʾ-d-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of harmony, concord, and the inner skin (al-adamah) beneath the outer skin (al-basharah); also used for the reconciliation between two parties.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance of ʾulfah (intimate familiarity) as a divinely ordained bond between spouses, achieved through mutual sight and attraction.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (haqiqah) usage refers to the physical inner skin; metaphorical (majaz) usage denotes the spiritual and emotional union (iʾtilāf) between husband and wife.
- Root: عقر (ʿ-q-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Barrenness (ʿuqr) in women; also the root for cutting off, as in severing lineage or progeny.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): A state of incapacity to bear children, which in the context of marriage contracts negates a primary purpose of the union (procreation).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical barrenness; metaphorical: the severance of the hoped-for continuity of offspring.
- Root: ودد (w-d-d)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Love, affection, and steadfast amity (wudd).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): A specific, enduring form of love (mahabbah) that is active and volitional, distinct from mere inclination.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the affection of the heart; metaphorical: the outward expression of that affection through service and companionship.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — Used to isolate the exclusive purpose of a clause, e.g., "إنما ذكر ذلك للمبالغة في الائتلاف" (He only mentioned that for emphasis on union), restricting the reason to a single, specific cause.
4:11.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Etiquette of Marriage'

4:11.arabic: يناسب حاله قوله تعالى {يوصيكم الله في أولادكم للذكر مثل حظ الأنثيين} وقوله تعالى {والذين يرمون المحصنات} وكذلك جميع الآيات التي فيها بيان أحكام الميراث والطلاق والحدود وغيرها وإنما المحرك لما في القلب ما يناسبه والأبيات إنما يضعها الشعراء إعرابا بها عن أحوال القلب فلا يحتاج في فهم الحال منها إلى تكلف نعم من يستولي عليه حالة غالبة قاهرة لم تبق فيه متسعا لغيرها ومعه تيقظ وذكاء ثاقب يتفطن به للمعاني البعيدة من الألفاظ فقد يخرج وجده على كل مسموع كمن يخطر له عند ذكر قوله تعالى {يوصيكم الله في أولادكم} حالة الموت المحوج
4:11.english: Some of the Sufis said: "One night I was reciting this verse: {كُلُّ نَفْسٍ ذَائِقَةُ الْمَوْتِ} «Every soul shall taste death» [Q. 3:185]. I kept repeating it, and lo, a caller cried out to me: 'How long will you repeat this verse? You have killed four of the jinn who have not raised their heads to the sky since they were created.'"
4:11.section_title_en: On the Ecstatic States (Wajd) Produced by Qur'anic Recitation and the Superiority of Song (Ghinā') in Stirring the Heart
4:11.anchors:
- Root: وجد (w-j-d)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of finding, attaining, and also denoting the emotional state of ecstasy or rapture that "finds" the heart.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In the theological context, 'wajd' is the state of spiritual finding—a direct, overwhelming apprehension of divine realities that bypasses discursive reasoning.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah) usage denotes "finding" a lost object; metaphorical (Majaz) usage denotes the heart "finding" its spiritual state, leading to agitation and ecstasy.
- Root: سمع (s-m-')
  * Lisan / Ayn: The faculty of hearing; also the ear itself.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Hearing can be literal (perception of sound) or figurative (understanding, obedience, acceptance). The heart's "hearing" is a deeper comprehension.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "سمعته" (I heard him). Metaphorical: "سمع الله لمن حمده" (God answers/he accepts the one who praises Him), indicating a responsive, transformative hearing.
- Root: موت (m-w-t)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Death; the opposite of life.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Death is the cessation of the soul's governance over the body, a separation. In the spiritual context, it can be a metaphorical death to worldly desires.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical death. Metaphorical: "أحيا الله البلد الميت" (God revives the dead land), indicating spiritual revival or the death of the ego.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — Used to emphasize that the stirring of the heart is exclusively through what is appropriate to its state, as in the phrase "إنما المحرك لما في القلب ما يناسبه" (The only thing that moves what is in the heart is that which is suitable to it).
4:11.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Audition and Ecstasy'

4:13.arabic: وخطب رجل عند رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال من يطع الله ورسوله فقد رشد ومن يعصهما فقد غوى فقال قل ومن يعص الله ورسوله فقد غوى (2) فكره رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قوله ومن يعصهما لأنه تسوية وجمع وكان إبراهيم يكره أن يقول الرجل أعوذ بالله وبك ويجوز أن يقول أعوذ بالله ثم بك وأن يقول لولا الله ثم فلان ولا يقول لولا الله وفلان وكره بعضهم أن يقال اللهم أعتقنا من النار وكان يقول العتق يكون بعد الورود وكانوا يستجيرون من النار ويتعوذون من النار وقال رجل اللهم اجعلني ممن تصيبه شفاعة محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم فق
4:13.english: An example of this is what Ḥudhayfah reported: The Prophet, peace be upon him, said: "Let none of you say: 'What Allah willed and you willed' — but rather let him say: 'What Allah willed, then you willed.'" (5) This is because in the absolute conjunction [with "and"] there is an association and an equalization, which is contrary to [the due measure of] reverence. And Ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: A man came to the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, speaking to him concerning some matter, and he said: "What Allah willed and you willed." The Prophet, peace be upon him, said: "Have you made me an equal to Allah? Rather, [say]: 'What Allah willed alone.'" (1)
4:13.section_title_en: The Revival of the Religious Sciences — Section 698: The Nineteenth Affliction — Heedlessness Regarding Subtle Errors in the Import of Speech
4:13.anchors:
- Root: غفل (ghafla)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of heedlessness, neglect, and inattention; the absence of vigilance over a matter.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Heedlessness (al-ghafla) is the soul's failure to attend to what it is obligated to know or consider; it is the opposite of mindfulness (al-tayaqquẓ) and remembrance (al-dhikr).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) usage denotes the absence of guarding; metaphorical (majāz) usage extends to the tongue's straying from precise expression in sacred matters.
- Root: عطف (ʿaṭf)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Inclination, turning, or joining one thing to another; grammatically, the conjunction that links two items in a shared ruling.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Joining (al-ʿaṭf) implies equal treatment of the conjoined items; in theological speech, absolute conjunction (al-ʿaṭf al-muṭlaq) with Allah entails an inadmissible association.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the bending of a staff or the inclining of a branch; metaphorical: the grammatical coupling that levels two referents under one predicate.
- Root: شرك (shirk)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Sharing, partnership, or association; the root of polytheism (al-shirk) as the ascription of a partner to Allah.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Association (al-shirk) is the equalization of two things in a shared ruling; in theology, it is the gravest form when applied to the Divine, whether in belief or in the mere wording of speech.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: co-participation in ownership; metaphorical: any verbal or creedal equalization of the creature with the Creator.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Conjunction (al-ʿaṭf) and Restriction (al-ḥaṣr) — The particle "thumma" (then) indicates sequential ordering and distinction of rank, whereas "wa" (and) denotes absolute conjunction and mutual equivalence; thus the Prophet's command to replace "wa" with "thumma" in "what Allah willed and you willed" is a syntactic correction to abolish the implication of equal partnership.
4:13.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications, prayers, and their spiritual power, from 'Condemnation of Anger and Hatred'

4:14.arabic: بالمشيئة يدل على الانقسام وقوله تعالى {ومن يعص الله ورسوله فإن له نار جهنم خالدين فيها} وتخصيصه بالكفر تحكم وقوله تعالى {ألا إن الظالمين في عذاب مقيم} وقال تعالى {ومن جاء بالسيئة فكبت وجوههم في النار} فهذه العمومات في معارضة عموماتهم ولا بد من تسليط التخصص والتأويل على الجانبين لأن الأخبار مصرحة بأن العصاة يعذبون (1) بل قوله تعالى وإن منكم إلا واردها كالصريح في أن ذلك لا بد منه للكل إذ لا يخلو مؤمن عن ذنب يرتكبه وقوله تعالى لا يصلاها إلا الأشقى الذي كذب وتولى أراد به من جماعة مخصوصين أو أراد بالأشقى شخصا
4:14.english: He was asked, "Which deed is most excellent?" The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Islam." It was then asked, "Which aspect of Islam is most excellent?" He (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Faith (Īmān)." This is evidence for both the distinction (ikhtilāf) between the two terms and their overlap (tadākhul). This usage is the most consistent with the conventions of the language, because faith is a deed among deeds, and it is the most excellent of them. Islam is submission (taslīm), whether by the heart, by the tongue, or by the limbs. The most excellent of these is that which is by the heart, which is the assent (taṣdīq) that is called faith. Using the two terms in a way that indicates distinction, overlap, or even complete synonymy (tarāduf) is all within the bounds of metaphorical usage (tajawwuz) in the language.
4:14.section_title_en: The Book of the Revival of the Religious Sciences — Section 99: On the Distinction, Overlap, and Synonymy of Faith (Īmān) and Submission (Islām), and Their Worldly and Otherworldly Judgments
4:14.anchors:
- Root: ايم (A-Y-M)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of remaining unmarried, or a state of being without a spouse; extended metaphorically to describe one who is solitary or without support.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الأيامى: جمع أيم، وهي المرأة التي لا بعل لها... والحرب مأيمة، أي: يفرق بين الزوج والزوجة." The root carries the sense of separation or a state of lacking union, which informs the theological discussion of what constitutes the essential bond of faith.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah) usage denotes the state of being unmarried; metaphorical (Majaz) usage extends to anything that separates or leaves one bereft. This distinction between literal and metaphorical application is central to the chapter's method.
- Root: قلب (Q-L-B)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To turn, overturn, or transform a thing from one state to another.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "قلب الشيء: تصريفه وصرفه عن وجه إلى وجه... والانقلاب: الانصراف." The heart (qalb) is so named for its constant fluctuation and turning. In theological terms, it is the seat of taṣdīq (assent), the immaterial faculty of cognition and conviction.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah) usage is physical turning; metaphorical (Majaz) usage is "قلب الأمور" — to deliberate, scrutinize, and manage affairs. This supports the distinction between the heart's internal act of assent and the external acts of the limbs.
- Root: عمل (ʿ-A-M-L)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Any deed or action performed with purpose and intent.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "العمل: كل فعل يكون من الحيوان بقصد، فهو أخص من الفعل." Work is more specific than mere action, as it implies deliberate, intentional agency. It is used for both righteous and sinful deeds, and is the external manifestation of internal conviction.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah) usage refers to physical labor or deeds. The chapter explores whether "work" is an integral part of the reality of faith or a separate, consequent requirement.
- Root: صدق (S-D-Q)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To be truthful, to speak the truth, to verify.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الصدق والكذب أصلهما في القول... ولا يكونان بالقصد الأول إلا في القول." Truth and falsehood are primarily properties of speech and reports. Taṣdīq (assent) is the heart's affirmation of the truth of a report, which is the core reality of Īmān.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah) usage is truthful speech; metaphorical (Majaz) usage is "صادق الحملة" — one who is true and firm in battle or resolve. This shows that taṣdīq is not merely verbal but a firm, internal resolution.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication). This rule governs how restriction (ḥaṣr) is achieved in Arabic, often through particles like "innamā" or through contextual specification (takhṣīṣ). The chapter's core argument hinges on how terms like Īmān and Islām are semantically restricted, expanded, or made synonymous through contextual usage (majāz), requiring precise parsing of the predicate and its scope.
4:14.topic: Al-Ghazali on the journey of the soul, death, and the Hereafter, from 'Condemnation of Anger and Hatred'

4:36.arabic: قد بايعناك فعلى ماذا نبايعك قال أن تعبدوا الله ولا تشركوا به شيئا وتصلوا الخمس وأن تسمعوا وتطيعوا وأسر كلمة خفية ولا تسألوا الناس شيئا (2) قال فلقد كان بعض أولئك النفر يسقط سوطه فلا يسأل أحدا أن يناوله إياه الآثار قال عمر رضي الله عنه إن الطمع فقر وإن اليأس غنى وإنه من ييأس عما في أيدي الناس استغنى عنهم وقيل لبعض الحكماء ما الغنى قال قلة تمنيك ورضاك بما يكفيك وفي ذلك قيل العيش ساعات تمر .
4:36.english: Now the human being (al-ādamī) has been naturally disposed (jubila) to greed, covetousness, and scant contentment. The Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, said: "Were the son of Adam to possess two valleys of gold, he would seek for them a third; and nothing fills the belly of the son of Adam but dust — and Allah relents toward whoever repents." {«لو كان لابن آدم واديان من ذهب لابتغى لهما ثالثا ولا يملأ جوف ابن آدم إلا التراب ويتوب الله على من تاب»} (1)
4:36.book_title: Condemnation of Miserliness and Love of Wealth
4:36.section_title_en: Exposition of the Blameworthiness of Greed and Covetousness, and the Praiseworthiness of Contentment and Despairing of What Is in People's Hands
4:36.anchors:
- Root: طمع (ṭamaʿ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of craving, yearning of the soul toward a thing with eager desire; the root carries the sense of an appetite that, when unrestrained, becomes a defining trait.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الطمع: نزوع النفس إلى الشيء شهوة له" — the soul's inclination toward a thing out of lustful desire. Al-Raghib notes that because most covetousness stems from caprice, it is said: "الطمع طبع" (covetousness is an innate disposition), and "الطمع يدنس الإهاب" (covetousness defiles the hide).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): "طمع في كذا وبه" — to covet something. Metaphorical (Majaz): "أخذ الجند أطماعهم: أرزاقهم" — the soldiers took their portions/rations, showing the extension of the root from craving to the very object of allotment.
- Root: قنع (qaniʿa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of being content, satisfied with one's portion; the root also carries the sense of asking humbly (qaniʿa = sa'ala) — a semantic tension resolved by context: the contented one does not ask.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Contentment (qanāʿah) is the soul's satisfaction with what suffices, restraining it from craving excess; it is the mean between avarice and prodigality.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "قنع يقنع قنوعا وقناعة" — to be content. The rhetorical force in Ghazali's usage is the pairing with "اليأس" (despairing of what others hold), making contentment an active renunciation rather than passive acceptance.
- Root: غني (ghaniya)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of being free from need, wealthy; the opposite of faqr (poverty).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الغنى يقال على ضروب: أحدها: عدم الحاجات، وليس ذلك إلا لله تعالى" — true wealth as absence of needs belongs to Allah alone; the second kind is fewness of needs, which is the wealth of the soul referenced in the hadith "الغنى غنى النفس."
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "لي عن هذا غنية. وأنا عنه غني" — I have no need of this. Metaphorical: "تغنته القيود" — the fetters made him independent (of movement), showing the root's extension to self-sufficiency in any state.
- Root: حرص (ḥaraṣa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of intense eager desire, avarice; the root implies a striving that exceeds due measure.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Greed (ḥirṣ) is the soul's excessive craving for something, exceeding what is needed; it is blameworthy when directed at worldly increase.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "حرص على الشيء" — to be greedily eager for a thing. The rhetorical contrast in this section is between ḥirṣ as an innate vice and qanāʿah as an acquired virtue.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — governing the hadith "ليس الغنى عن كثرة العرض إنما الغنى غنى النفس" (Wealth is not abundance of goods; rather, wealth is the wealth of the soul), where إنما restricts the predicate to the soul's sufficiency, negating any other sense of true wealth.
4:36.topic: Al-Ghazali on purifying the character, moral diseases, and spiritual remedies, from 'Condemnation of Miserliness and Love of Wealth'

4:36.arabic: وسلم فقال نعم إن الله لا يحب المستكبرين فنزل وقعد معهم على الأرض وأكل ثم سلم عليهم وركب وقال قد أجبتكم فأجيبوني قالوا نعم فوعدهم وقتا معلوما فحضروا فقدم إليهم فاخر الطعام وجلس يأكل معهم وأما قول القائل إن من وضعت يدي في قصعته فقد ذلت له رقبتي فقد قال بعضهم هذا خلاف السنة وليس كذلك فإنه ذل إذا كان الداعي لا يفرح بالإجابة ولا يتقلد منة وكان يرى ذلك يدا له على المدعو ورسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كان يحضر لعلمه أن الداعي له يتقلد منة ويرى ذلك شرفا وذخرا لنفسه في الدنيا
4:36.english: The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Do not burden your guest so that you make him hate you, for whoever hates his guest has hated Allah, and whoever hates Allah, Allah hates him."
4:36.section_title_en: The Etiquettes of Hospitality: Invitation, Response, Attendance, and the Serving of Food — Section 290 of The Revival of the Religious Sciences
4:36.anchors:
- Root: ضيف (ḍ-y-f)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning is "to incline, to lean toward." The guest (al-ḍayf) is one who inclines toward you, alighting as a visitor; the root carries the sense of leaning or bending.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The guest is "one who inclines to you, alighting with you"; hospitality (al-ḍiyāfah) became customary in the sense of receiving such a one. The word is originally a verbal noun, hence one and many are equal in most usage.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): "ḍāfa ilayhi: he inclined toward him"; "ḍāfat al-shams: the sun inclined toward setting." Metaphorical (majāz): "aḍāfa ilayhi amran: he attributed a matter to him, leaning it upon him"; "al-muḍāf: the one constrained, hemmed in, in distress."
- Sibawayh Rule: Restriction and Focused Predication (al-ḥaṣr wa al-taqyīd bi-innamā) — governing the Prophet's statement "innamā hādhihi al-akhlāq bi-yad Allāh" (these morals are only in the hand of Allah), where innamā restricts the attribution of moral character exclusively to divine bestowal.
4:36.topic: Al-Ghazali on purifying the character, moral diseases, and spiritual remedies, from 'Condemnation of Anger and Hatred'

4:86.arabic: بتحية فحيوا بأحسن منها أو ردوها} وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم والذي نفسي بيده لا تدخلوا الجنة حتى تؤمنوا ولا تؤمنوا حتى تحابوا أفلا أدلكم على عمل إذا عملتموه تحاببتم قالوا بلى يا رسول الله قال أفشوا السلام بينكم (1) وقال أيضا إذا سلم المسلم على المسلم فرد عليه صلت عليه الملائكة سبعين مرة (2) وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم إن الملائكة تعجب من المسلم يمر على المسلم ولا يسلم عليه (3) حديث يسلم الراكب على الماشي وإذا سلم من القوم أحد أجزأ عنهم رواه مالك في الموطأ عن زيد بن أسلم مرسلا ولأبي داود من حديث عل
4:86.english: **First**: That you greet him with peace (*salām*) when you meet him, and respond to his invitation when he invites you, and say "may Allah have mercy on you" (*tashmīt*) when he sneezes, and visit him when he is ill, and attend his funeral procession when he dies, and fulfill his oath when he swears by you, and give him sincere counsel when he seeks your advice, and protect him in his absence when he is away from you, and love for him what you love for yourself, and dislike for him what you dislike for yourself. (1)
4:86.section_title_en: The Rights of Brotherhood — Section 433: The Duties of a Muslim Toward His Fellow Muslims
4:86.anchors:
- Root: سلم (s-l-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of safety, security, freedom from harm; the root from which *islām* (submission/surrender) and *salām* (peace) derive
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): *Salām* as the theological state of being secure from harm — both giving and receiving safety; *islām* as the total surrender of the heart to Allah
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (*ḥaqīqah*): physical safety from tongue and hand; Metaphorical (*majāz*): the comprehensive spiritual safety that defines true Muslim brotherhood
- Root: عون (ʿ-w-n)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Assistance, aid, helping another in need
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Mutual assistance as a divine ordinance among believers
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical aid; Metaphorical: intercession (*shafāʿah*) and advocacy on behalf of others
- Root: ستر (s-t-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Covering, concealing, veiling; protection from exposure
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): *Sitr* as the divine attribute of concealment — Allah's covering of sins in this world and the next
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: covering a physical defect; Metaphorical: concealing another's faults and sins — a cardinal virtue of brotherhood
- Root: عذر (ʿ-dh-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Excuse, pardon, acceptance of apology
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): *ʿAfw* (pardon) as the higher station of forgiveness that elevates the forgiver
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: releasing from obligation; Metaphorical: the noble trait of overlooking others' offenses
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد (Restriction & Focused Predication) — The repeated use of restrictive constructions (e.g., "المسلم من سلم المسلمون") establishes definitional boundaries through predicate restriction, indicating that the *ḥaqīqah* of faith is manifested through specific observable actions.

4:107.arabic: وسلم فقال نعم إن الله لا يحب المستكبرين فنزل وقعد معهم على الأرض وأكل ثم سلم عليهم وركب وقال قد أجبتكم فأجيبوني قالوا نعم فوعدهم وقتا معلوما فحضروا فقدم إليهم فاخر الطعام وجلس يأكل معهم وأما قول القائل إن من وضعت يدي في قصعته فقد ذلت له رقبتي فقد قال بعضهم هذا خلاف السنة وليس كذلك فإنه ذل إذا كان الداعي لا يفرح بالإجابة ولا يتقلد منة وكان يرى ذلك يدا له على المدعو ورسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كان يحضر لعلمه أن الداعي له يتقلد منة ويرى ذلك شرفا وذخرا لنفسه في الدنيا
