4:114.arabic: الأمر بالمعروف للوالدين والأقربين وقال تعالى لا خير في كثير من نجواهم إلا من أمر بصدقة أو معروف أو إصلاح بين الناس ومن يفعل ذلك ابتغاء مرضاة الله فسوف نؤتيه أجرا عظيما وقال تعالى وإن طائفتان من المؤمنين اقتتلوا فأصلحوا بينهما الآية والإصلاح نهي عن البغي وإعادة إلى الطاعة فإن لم يفعل فقد أمر الله تعالى بقتاله فقال فقاتلوا التي تبغي حتى تفيء إلى أمر الله وذلك هو النهي عن المنكر وأما الأخبار فمنها ما روي عن أبي بكر الصديق رضي الله عنه أنه قال في خطبة خطبها أيها الناس إنكم تقرءون هذه الآية وتؤولونها على خلاف تأويلها يا أيها الذين آمنوا عليكم أنفسكم لا يضركم من ضل إذا اهتديتم (1) وإني سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
4:114.english: Know that the verses indicating the obligation of commanding right and forbidding wrong are numerous. Among them is His saying, may He be exalted: {«Let there arise from among you a nation inviting to good, commanding right and forbidding wrong — and those are the successful»} (Āl ʿImrān 3:104). In this verse is the declaration of obligation, for His saying, may He be exalted, "Let there be" (wal-takun) is a command, and the apparent meaning of a command is obligation. In it also is the declaration that success (falāḥ) is contingent upon it, for He restricted it and said: {«And those are the successful»}. In it also is the declaration that it is a collective obligation (farḍ kifāyah), not an individual obligation (farḍ ʿayn), and that when a group undertakes it, the obligation falls from the rest — for He did not say, "Let all of you be commanders of right," but rather said: {«Let there arise from among you a nation»}. Thus, whenever one person or a group undertakes it, the burden falls from the others, and success is particularized to those who undertake it and directly perform it. But if all of creation were to hold back from it, the burden would encompass all those capable of it without exception.
4:114.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Enjoining Good and Forbidding Evil'

4:114.arabic: أمر بمعروف أو نهي عن منكر أو ذكر الله تعالى (3) وقال تعالى لا خير في كثير من نجواهم إلا من أمر بصدقة أو معروف أو إصلاح بين الناس الآية ورأى بعض العلماء بعض أصحاب الرأي من أهل الكوفة في المنام فقال ما رأيت فيما كنت عليه من الفتيا والرأي فكره وجهه وأعرض عنه وقال ما وجدناه شيئا وما حمدنا عافيته وقال ابن حصين إن أحدهم ليفتي في مسئلة لو وردت على عمر بن الخطاب رضي الله عنه لجمع لها أهل بدر فلم يزل السكوت دأب أهل العلم إلا عند الضرورة وفي الحديث إذا رأيتم الرجل قد أوتي صمتا وزهدا فاقتربوا منه فإنه يلقن الحكمة (4) وقيل العالم إما عالم عامة وهو المفتي وهم أصحاب السلاطين أو ع
4:114.english: And in sum, mixing with them is a key to evils, and the scholars of the Hereafter — their way is caution (iḥtiyāṭ). And he, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Whoever dwells in the desert becomes coarse" — meaning whoever dwells in the desert becomes coarse — "and whoever follows the hunt becomes heedless, and whoever attends upon the sultan is tempted" (1). And he, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "There will be over you rulers whom you will recognize and denounce. Whoever denounces has absolved himself, and whoever disapproves has been saved. But whoever is pleased and follows — God, exalted is He, will distance him." It was said: "Shall we not fight them?" He, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "No, so long as they pray" (2). And Sufyān said: "In Hell there is a valley that none inhabits except the Qurʾān-readers who visit the kings."
4:114.section_title_en: The Revival of the Religious Sciences — Section 56: On the Etiquette of Scholars and the Perils of Worldly Attachment
4:114.anchors:
- Root: ع ل م (ʿ-l-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root denotes the mark or trace by which a thing is known; knowledge as the impression of reality upon the mind.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "العلم: إدراك الشيء بحقيقته" — knowledge is the apprehension of a thing in its true reality, divided into apprehension of the essence and judgment upon the thing.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Distinguishes literal knowledge (ḥaqīqah) from the metaphorical "sensing" (shaʿara); scholars as "علامة" — living landmarks of guidance.
- Root: ي ق ن (y-q-n)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Certainty as the settled state of the heart; the opposite of doubt.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "اليقين من صفة العلم فوق المعرفة والدراية" — certainty is an attribute of knowledge above mere cognition; it is "سكون الفهم مع ثبات الحكم" — the stillness of understanding with the firmness of judgment.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Used literally for that which is verified and settled, as opposed to conjecture (ẓann).
- Root: خ ش ي (kh-sh-y)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Fear that carries reverence and awe; the fear of one who knows the majesty of what he fears.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Khashyah is the fear that arises from knowledge of the greatness of the feared one — hence "إنما يخشى الله من عباده العلماء" (Only the learned among His servants fear God).
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد (Restriction & Specification) — The use of restrictive constructions (innamā, laysa...illā) to delimit predicates, as in "العلم ثلاثة" and the enumeration of the categories of those who issue legal rulings.
4:114.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Condemnation of Anger and Hatred'

4:140.arabic: تعالى فلا تقعدوا معهم حتى يخوضوا في حديث غيره إنكم إذا مثلهم وقال سلمان أكثر الناس ذنوبا يوم القيامة أكثرهم كلاما في معصية الله وقال ابن سيرين كان رجل من الأنصار يمر بمجلس لهم فيقول لهم توضئوا فإن بعض ما تقولون شر من الحدث فهذا هو الخوض في الباطل وهو وراء ما سيأتي من الغيبة والنميمة والفحش وغيرها بل هو الخوض في ذكر محظورات سبق وجودها أو تدبر للتوصل إليها من غير حاجة دينية إلى ذكرها ويدخل فيه أيضا الخوض في حكاية البدع والمذاهب الفاسدة وحكاية ما جرى من قتال الصحابة على وجه يوهم الطعن في بعضهم وكل ذلك باطل
4:140.english: For Bilāl ibn al-Ḥārith has related that the Messenger of God — may God's blessings and peace be upon him — said: "Indeed, a man speaks a word of God's good pleasure, not imagining that it reaches what it reaches, and God writes for him thereby His good pleasure until the Day of Resurrection. And indeed, a man speaks a word of God's wrath, not imagining that it reaches what it reaches, and God writes against him thereby His wrath until the Day of Resurrection." [The hadith of Bilāl ibn al-Ḥārith — "Indeed, a man speaks a word of God's good pleasure" — was transmitted by Ibn Mājah and al-Tirmidhī, who said it is ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ.] And ʿAlqamah used to say: "How much speech has the hadith of Bilāl ibn al-Ḥārith prevented me from [uttering]!"
4:140.section_title_en: The Third Affliction: Wading into Falsehood (al-Khawḍ fī al-Bāṭil)
4:140.anchors:
- Root: خوض (Kha-Wa-D)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning is wading or plunging into water, passing through it; the Kitab al-Ayn records it as "الشروع في الماء والمرور فيه" (entering into water and passing through it).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In theological usage, it is predominantly employed in the Quranic context of blameworthy engagement — as in {«وخضتم كالذي خاضوا»} (And you waded as those before you waded) and {«ذرهم في خوضهم يلعبون»} (Leave them in their wading, playing). It denotes immersion in that which is vain or false.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah) — physical wading in water. Metaphorical (Majaz) — "خاضوا في الحديث وتخاوضوا فيه" (they waded into speech and waded together in it), i.e., plunging into discourse; "وهو يخوض مع الخائضين أي يبطل مع المبطلين" (he wades with the waders, i.e., he engages in falsehood with those who engage in falsehood).
- Root: بطل (Ba-Ta-La)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The Kitab al-Ayn situates it within the semantic field of that which is null, void, or futile.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الباطل: نقيض الحق، وهو ما لا ثبات له عند الفحص عنه" (Al-Bāṭil is the opposite of truth, and it is that which has no stability upon examination). It applies to both speech and deed.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — "هو باطل بين البطلان" (it is false, clearly false). Metaphorical — the verbal form "بطل" (to become null) and "أبطله غيره" (another nullified it), as in {«وبطل ما كانوا يعملون»} (And nullified is what they used to do).
- Root: كلم (Ka-La-Ma)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The Kitab al-Ayn treats it under the root of speech and utterance.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الكلم: التأثير المدرك بإحدى الحاستين" (Speech: the effect perceived by one of the two senses) — indicating that speech is that which produces an impression.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — "سمعته يتكلم بكذا" (I heard him speaking such-and-such). Metaphorical — "وهذه كلمة شاعرة" (this is a penetrating word) and "وهذا مما يكلم العرض والدين" (this is something that wounds honor and religion) — speech that injures.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The rule governing the permissibility of interposing elements between a preposition and its object, relevant here to the syntactic structure of "الخوض في الباطل" where the verbal noun governs its prepositional complement, and to the periodic constructions of the hadith citations where the conditional clauses ("إن الرجل ليتكلم بالكلمة...") require careful parsing of the apodosis.
4:140.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'Condemnation of Anger and Hatred'

5:1.arabic: وقد قال الله تعالى يا أيها الذين آمنوا أنفقوا من طيبات ما كسبتم ومما أخرجنا لكم من الأرض ولا تيمموا الخبيث منه تنفقون ولستم بآخذيه إلا أن تغمضوا فيه أي لا تأخذوه إلا مع كراهية وحياء وهو معنى الإغماض فلا تؤثروا به ربكم وفي الخبر سبق درهم مائة ألف درهم (3) وذلك بأن يخرجه الإنسان وهو من أحل ماله وأجوده فيصدر ذلك عن الرضا والفرح بالبذل وقد يخرج مائة ألف درهم مما يكره من ماله فيدل ذلك على أنه ليس يؤثر الله عز وجل بشيء مما يحبه وبذلك ذم الله تعالى قوما جعلوا لله ما يكرهون فقال تعالى ويجعلون لله ما يكر
5:1.english: The heart is not treated save with the compound electuary (maʿjūn) of knowledge and works. And this condition among the conditions of almsgiving runs in the same course as humility (al-khushūʿ) runs in the prayer. This is established by his saying — may Allah bless him and grant him peace: "A man has nothing of his prayer save that of which he was conscious." And this is like his saying — may Allah bless him and grant him peace: "Allah does not accept the charity of the one who bestows it with reproach (al-mannān)." And like His saying — Exalted is He: {«لا تبطلوا صدقاتكم بالمن والأذى»} ("Do not nullify your charities by reproach and injury"). As for the legal opinion (fatwā) of the jurist that the alms fall in their proper place and that one's liability is discharged without this condition — that is another discussion, and we have already pointed to its meaning in the Book of Prayer.
5:1.section_title_en: The Inner Conditions of Charity — Section 175 (From The Revival of the Religious Sciences, Book of the Mysteries of Almsgiving)
5:1.anchors:
- Root: قلب (q-l-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "To turn, overturn, transform a thing from one state to another; to rotate, to flip"
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "قلب الشيء: تصريفه وصرفه عن وجه إلى وجه" — the heart is so named because of its constant turning and transformation between states
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "قلب الشيء قلبا: حوله عن وجهه" (to turn a thing from its face). Metaphorical: "رجل قلب حول: يقلب الأمور ويحتال" — one who turns matters over and manages them; "قلبوا لك الأمور" (they turned matters against you)
- Root: وجل (w-j-l)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "Fear, dread, apprehension that strikes the heart"
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الوجل: استشعار الخوف" — the sensing of fear; cited in {«إنما المؤمنون الذين إذا ذكر الله وجلت قلوبهم»}
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "رجل وجل، وقوم وجال" — a fearful man, a fearful people; "وفي قلبه وجل" — in his heart is dread
- Root: عجب (ʿ-j-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "Wonder, amazement; self-admiration, vanity"
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Self-admiration (al-ʿujb) is a destructive spiritual ailment that nullifies deeds
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: wonder at something extraordinary. Metaphorical: self-conceit regarding one's own acts of obedience
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد (Restriction & Focused Predication) — governing the precise limitation of general categories (al-ṣifāt al-khāṣṣah within al-aṣnāf al-thamāniyyah) and the conditional structure of acceptance

5:87.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Duties of Brotherhood'

5:87.arabic: وسلم فقال نعم إن الله لا يحب المستكبرين فنزل وقعد معهم على الأرض وأكل ثم سلم عليهم وركب وقال قد أجبتكم فأجيبوني قالوا نعم فوعدهم وقتا معلوما فحضروا فقدم إليهم فاخر الطعام وجلس يأكل معهم وأما قول القائل إن من وضعت يدي في قصعته فقد ذلت له رقبتي فقد قال بعضهم هذا خلاف السنة وليس كذلك فإنه ذل إذا كان الداعي لا يفرح بالإجابة ولا يتقلد منة وكان يرى ذلك يدا له على المدعو ورسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كان يحضر لعلمه أن الداعي له يتقلد منة ويرى ذلك شرفا وذخرا لنفسه في الدنيا
5:87.english: The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Do not burden your guest so that you make him hate you, for whoever hates his guest has hated Allah, and whoever hates Allah, Allah hates him."
5:87.section_title_en: The Etiquettes of Hospitality: Invitation, Response, Attendance, and the Serving of Food — Section 290 of The Revival of the Religious Sciences
5:87.anchors:
- Root: ضيف (ḍ-y-f)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning is "to incline, to lean toward." The guest (al-ḍayf) is one who inclines toward you, alighting as a visitor; the root carries the sense of leaning or bending.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The guest is "one who inclines to you, alighting with you"; hospitality (al-ḍiyāfah) became customary in the sense of receiving such a one. The word is originally a verbal noun, hence one and many are equal in most usage.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): "ḍāfa ilayhi: he inclined toward him"; "ḍāfat al-shams: the sun inclined toward setting." Metaphorical (majāz): "aḍāfa ilayhi amran: he attributed a matter to him, leaning it upon him"; "al-muḍāf: the one constrained, hemmed in, in distress."
- Sibawayh Rule: Restriction and Focused Predication (al-ḥaṣr wa al-taqyīd bi-innamā) — governing the Prophet's statement "innamā hādhihi al-akhlāq bi-yad Allāh" (these morals are only in the hand of Allah), where innamā restricts the attribution of moral character exclusively to divine bestowal.
5:87.topic: Al-Ghazali on purifying the character, moral diseases, and spiritual remedies, from 'Condemnation of Anger and Hatred'

7:87.arabic: والقيامة تجمعنا والله تعالى يحكم بيننا وهو خير الحاكمين ورفع بعض السعاة إلى الصاحب بن عباد رقعة نبه فيها على مال يتيم يحمله على أخذه لكثرته فوقع على ظهرها السعاية قبيحة وإن كانت صحيحة فإن كنت أجريتها مجرى النصح فخسرانك فيها افضل من الربح ومعاذ الله أن نقبل مهتوكا في مستور ولولا أنك في خفارة شيبتك لقابلناك بما يقتضيه فعلك في مثلك فتوق يا ملعون العيب فإن الله أعلم بالغيب الميت رحمه الله واليتيم جبره الله والمال ثمره الله والساعي لعنه الله وقال لقمان لابنه يا بني أوصيك بخلال إن تمسكت بهن لم تزل
7:87.english: A man said to ʿAmr ibn ʿUbayd: "The teacher (al-Uswārī) continues to mention you in his discourses with evil." So ʿAmr said to him: "O this man, you have not observed the right of companionship with the man, for you have transmitted his speech to me; nor have you fulfilled my right, for you have informed me of what I dislike concerning my brother. But I shall inform him that death encompasses us all, the grave gathers us, the Resurrection assembles us, and Allah — Most High — shall judge between us, and He is the Best of Judges."
7:87.section_title_en: On the Gravity of Slander (Namīmah) and Its Consequences
7:87.anchors:
- Root: ن م م (N-M-M)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of "to carry tales, to slander, to stir up enmity through speech" — the carrier of tales (nammām) is one who transmits speech to cause discord.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The theological nuance — namīmah is a moral corruption rooted in the intention to sever bonds of brotherhood, which the Sacred Law (Sharʿ) universally condemns.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) — the act of carrying speech from one party to another with corruptive intent; metaphorical (majāz) — the "slanderer" is one whose very presence breeds division, even if his report is factually true.
- Root: خ و ن (Kh-W-N)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Betrayal of trust (khiyānah) — the antithesis of amānah (fidelity); to act treacherously in what has been entrusted.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Khiyānah is the violation of a covenant or trust, whether overt or concealed; its opposite is amānah, which is the foundation of social contracts.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — breach of trust in material or moral matters; metaphorical — the slanderer betrays the trust of both the speaker and the subject of speech.
- Root: ي ت م (Y-T-M)
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Orphanhood — the severance of a child from his father before maturity; metaphorically, any isolated or defenseless entity (e.g., a "unique pearl").
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — a minor bereft of his father; metaphorical — the orphan's vulnerability as a test of the guardian's integrity, where betrayal is magnified.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The periodic structure of the narrative (e.g., the tale of the slave and the two spouses) demonstrates how clauses are interposed to build suspense and moral consequence, each element grammatically dependent on the governing verb of intention or action.
7:87.topic: Al-Ghazali on the journey of the soul, death, and the Hereafter, from 'Condemnation of Anger and Hatred'

7:199.arabic: ثم إن تفاخر عليه غيره فليحتمل قال الله تعالى لنبيه صلى الله عليه وسلم {خذ العفو وأمر بالعرف وأعرض عن الجاهلين} وعن ابن أبي أوفى كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يتواضع لكل مسلم ولا يأنف ولا يتكبر أن يمشي مع الأرملة والمسكين فيقضي حاجته (7) ومنها أن لا يسمع بلاغات الناس بعضهم على بعض ولا يبلغ بعضهم ما يسمع من بعض قال صلى الله عليه وسلم لا يدخل الجنة قتات (8) وقال الخليل بن أحمد من نم لك نم عليك ومن أخبرك بخير غيرك أخبر غيرك بخبرك ومنها أن لا يزيد في الهجر لمن يعرفه على ثلاثة أيام مهما غضب عليه قال أبو أيوب الأنصاري قال صلى الله عليه وسلم لا يحل لمسلم
7:199.english: **First**: That you greet him with peace (*salām*) when you meet him, and respond to his invitation when he invites you, and say "may Allah have mercy on you" (*tashmīt*) when he sneezes, and visit him when he is ill, and attend his funeral procession when he dies, and fulfill his oath when he swears by you, and give him sincere counsel when he seeks your advice, and protect him in his absence when he is away from you, and love for him what you love for yourself, and dislike for him what you dislike for yourself. (1)
7:199.section_title_en: The Rights of Brotherhood — Section 433: The Duties of a Muslim Toward His Fellow Muslims
7:199.anchors:
- Root: سلم (s-l-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of safety, security, freedom from harm; the root from which *islām* (submission/surrender) and *salām* (peace) derive
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): *Salām* as the theological state of being secure from harm — both giving and receiving safety; *islām* as the total surrender of the heart to Allah
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (*ḥaqīqah*): physical safety from tongue and hand; Metaphorical (*majāz*): the comprehensive spiritual safety that defines true Muslim brotherhood
- Root: عون (ʿ-w-n)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Assistance, aid, helping another in need
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Mutual assistance as a divine ordinance among believers
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical aid; Metaphorical: intercession (*shafāʿah*) and advocacy on behalf of others
- Root: ستر (s-t-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Covering, concealing, veiling; protection from exposure
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): *Sitr* as the divine attribute of concealment — Allah's covering of sins in this world and the next
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: covering a physical defect; Metaphorical: concealing another's faults and sins — a cardinal virtue of brotherhood
- Root: عذر (ʿ-dh-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Excuse, pardon, acceptance of apology
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): *ʿAfw* (pardon) as the higher station of forgiveness that elevates the forgiver
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: releasing from obligation; Metaphorical: the noble trait of overlooking others' offenses
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد (Restriction & Focused Predication) — The repeated use of restrictive constructions (e.g., "المسلم من سلم المسلمون") establishes definitional boundaries through predicate restriction, indicating that the *ḥaqīqah* of faith is manifested through specific observable actions.

- Root: ضيف (ḍ-y-f)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning is "to incline, to lean toward." The guest (al-ḍayf) is one who inclines toward you, alighting as a visitor; the root carries the sense of leaning or bending.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The guest is "one who inclines to you, alighting with you"; hospitality (al-ḍiyāfah) became customary in the sense of receiving such a one. The word is originally a verbal noun, hence one and many are equal in most usage.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): "ḍāfa ilayhi: he inclined toward him"; "ḍāfat al-shams: the sun inclined toward setting." Metaphorical (majāz): "aḍāfa ilayhi amran: he attributed a matter to him, leaning it upon him"; "al-muḍāf: the one constrained, hemmed in, in distress."
- Sibawayh Rule: Restriction and Focused Predication (al-ḥaṣr wa al-taqyīd bi-innamā) — governing the Prophet's statement "innamā hādhihi al-akhlāq bi-yad Allāh" (these morals are only in the hand of Allah), where innamā restricts the attribution of moral character exclusively to divine bestowal.
8:58.topic: Al-Ghazali on purifying the character, moral diseases, and spiritual remedies, from 'Condemnation of Anger and Hatred'

11:18.arabic: الله تعالى بين من افترى على الله كذبا وبين من كذب بالحق فقال تعالى ومن أظلم ممن افترى على الله كذبا أو كذب بالحق لما جاءه وقال تعالى فمن أظلم ممن كذب على الله وكذب بالصدق إذ جاءه ومنها الرياء وملاحظة الخلق والجهد في استمالة قلوبهم وصرف وجوههم والرياء هو الداء العضال الذي يدعو إلى أكبر الكبائر كما سيأتي في كتاب الرياء والمناظر لا يقصد إلا الظهور عند الخلق وانطلاق ألسنتهم بالثناء عليه فهذه عشر خصال من أمهات الفواحش الباطنة سوى ما يتفق لغير المتماسكين منهم من الخصام المؤدي إلى الضرب
11:18.english:
**QUAD_ANCHORS:**
- Root: نظر (naẓara)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to look, to examine, to consider; al-munāẓarah is mutual examination/argumentation between two parties.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: naẓar as intellectual contemplation (taʾammul bi-l-baṣīrah); munāẓarah as dialectical exchange.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: sitting face-to-face in debate; Metaphorical: disputation for victory.
- Root: غلب (ghalaba)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to overcome, to conquer, to prevail.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-ghalabah as seeking to dominate another in argument.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: victory in combat; Metaphorical: intellectual supremacy.
- Root: حسد (ḥasada)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to envy, to wish removal of blessings from another.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: envy as wishing deprivation of blessings from the deserving — among the basest traits.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: envy of another's blessing; Metaphorical: consuming fire of the soul.
- Root: كبر (kabura)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to be great, to be haughty.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-kibr as self-elevation above others; condemned by God.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: greatness; Metaphorical: arrogance and pride.
- Root: غيب (ghāba)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to be absent, to be hidden.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-ghībah as mentioning another with what he dislikes in his absence — likened to eating carrion.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: backbiting; Metaphorical: consuming the flesh of one's brother.
- Root: راءى (rāʾā)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to show off, to display.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-riyāʾ as performing acts for the sake of being seen — hidden shirk.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: showing good deeds; Metaphorical: seeking reputation.
- Root: نفس (nafs)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: self, soul, spirit.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: tazkiyat al-nafs as self-praise and self-purification — forbidden by God.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: self; Metaphorical: self-commendation.
- Root: حقd (ḥaqida)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to bear malice, to harbor resentment.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-ḥiqd as nursing enmity in the heart — negated from the believer.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: bearing grudge; Metaphorical: hidden rancor.
- Root: نفاق (nifāq)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: hypocrisy, showing contrary to what one conceals.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: hypocrisy in deeds — outward display contrary to inward state.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: hypocrisy in faith; Metaphorical: hypocrisy in character.
- Root: علم (ʿalima)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to know, to perceive.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: knowledge as apprehension of reality — its pursuit for other than God is destructive.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: knowledge; Metaphorical: the dangerous burden of the scholar.
- Root: جدل (jadala)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to argue, to dispute.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-jidāl as contention; al-mirāʾ as disputation with falsehood — condemned.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: argumentation; Metaphorical: obstinate disputation.
- Root: شرك (sharaka)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to associate, to share.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-riyāʾ as hidden shirk — associating others with God in intention.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: polytheism; Metaphorical: hidden association in deeds.
- Root: موت (māta)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to die.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: death as separation of soul from body; spiritual death as ruin of the soul.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical death; Metaphorical: spiritual destruction.
- Root: حيى (ḥayiya)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to live.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: life as the power of perception; eternal life as the reward of the righteous.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical life; Metaphorical: spiritual vitality.
- Root: هلك (halaka)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to perish, to be destroyed.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-halāk as ruin; eternal destruction as everlasting punishment.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: destruction; Metaphorical: eternal ruin.
- Root: رياء (riyāʾ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: showing off, ostentation.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: riyāʾ as the incurable disease calling to the greatest sins.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: ostentation; Metaphorical: spiritual disease.
- Root: جاه (jāh)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: rank, status, prestige.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: love of status (ḥubb al-jāh) among the destructive traits.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: position; Metaphorical: seeking prestige.
- Root: مباهاة (mubāhāh)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: mutual boasting, vying in splendor.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: mubāhāh as each seeking to display superiority over the other.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: mutual boasting; Metaphorical: rivalry in honor.
- Root: مماراة (mumārāh)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: disputation, wrangling.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-mirāʾ as contentious argument — condemned by the Prophet.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: disputation; Metaphorical: obstinate wrangling.
- Root: فخر (fakhara)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to boast, to pride oneself.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-fakhr as self-glorification — among the blameworthy traits.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: boasting; Metaphorical: vainglory.
- Root: عجب (ʿajiba)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to wonder, to be amazed.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-ʿujb as self-admiration — among the destructive traits.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: wonder; Metaphorical: self-conceit.
- Root: بغض (baghiḍa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to hate, to detest.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-baghdāʾ as mutual hatred — contrary to brotherhood.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: hatred; Metaphorical: mutual enmity.
- Root: غضب (ghaḍiba)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to be angry.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-ghaḍab as anger — among the blameworthy traits.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: anger; Metaphorical: rage.
- Root: طمع (ṭamiʿa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to covet, to desire.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-ṭamaʿ as covetousness — among the destructive traits.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: desire; Metaphorical: greed.
- Root: أشر (ashira)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to be exultant, to be insolent.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-ashar as excessive joy and insolence — blameworthy.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: exultation; Metaphorical: insolence.
- Root: بطر (baṭira)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to be arrogant, to be ungrateful.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-baṭar as arrogance in prosperity — among the destructive traits.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: arrogance; Metaphorical: ingratitude for blessings.
- Root: خيلاء (khuyalāʾ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: pride, haughtiness.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-khuyalāʾ as pride and conceit — blameworthy.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: pride; Metaphorical: haughty bearing.
- Root: خشية (khashyah)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: fear, awe.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-khashyah as reverential fear — among the traits of the believers.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: fear; Metaphorical: reverential awe.
- Root: رحمة (raḥmah)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: mercy, compassion.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-raḥmah as tenderness of heart — among the traits of the believers.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: mercy; Metaphorical: compassion.
- Root: غفلة (ghaflah)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: heedlessness, inattention.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-ghaflah as heedlessness — contrary to vigilance.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: inattention; Metaphorical: spiritual heedlessness.
- Root: خشوع (khushūʿ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: humility, submissiveness.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-khushūʿ as humility — among the traits of the believers.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: humility; Metaphorical: devotional submission.
- Root: تذكير (tadhkīr)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: reminding, admonishing.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-tadhkīr as reminding of God — a righteous act.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: reminding; Metaphorical: preaching.
- Root: وعظ (waʿaẓa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to admonish, to exhort.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-waʿẓ as exhortation to obedience and warning against disobedience.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: admonition; Metaphorical: sermonizing.
- Root: فتوى (fatwā)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: legal ruling, formal opinion.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-fatwā as clarification of legal rulings.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: legal opinion; Metaphorical: religious authority.
- Root: قضاء (qaḍāʾ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: judgment, decree.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-qaḍāʾ as judgment between people.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: judgment; Metaphorical: judicial authority.
- Root: وقف (waqafa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to stop, to stand.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-waqf as endowment of property for charitable purposes.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: standing; Metaphorical: religious endowment.
- Root: ثواب (thawāb)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: reward, recompense.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-thawāb as divine recompense for righteous deeds.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: reward; Metaphorical: divine recompense.
- Root: عذاب (ʿadhāb)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: punishment, torment.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-ʿadhāb as divine punishment for the disobedient.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: punishment; Metaphorical: divine chastisement.
- Root: ملك (malaka)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to possess, to rule.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-mulk as sovereignty; al-mulk al-muʾabbad as eternal sovereignty in Paradise.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: dominion; Metaphorical: eternal kingdom.
- Root: نعيم (naʿīm)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: bliss, delight.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-naʿīm as bliss; al-naʿīm al-sarmad as everlasting bliss.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: delight; Metaphorical: eternal bliss.
- Root: رخصة (rukhaṣah)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: concession, dispensation.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-rukhaṣah as legal concession.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: concession; Metaphorical: legal dispensation.
- Root: رياسة (riyāsah)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: leadership, headship.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: love of leadership among the destructive traits.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: leadership; Metaphorical: seeking authority.
- Root: اندراس (indirās)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: effacement, obliteration.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: indirās al-ʿulūm as the obliteration of the sciences.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: effacement; Metaphorical: extinction of knowledge.
- Root: صبيان (ṣibyān)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: boys, children.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: children's motivation for learning through play.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: boys; Metaphorical: pupils.
- Root: مكتب (maktab)
  * Lisan / Ayn- Root: مكتب (maktab)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: place of instruction, school for boys.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: the elementary school where children are taught.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: school; Metaphorical: place of elementary learning.
- Root: خلاق (khilāq)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: portion, share, lot.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: "no portion" (lā khilāq) in the Hereafter — utter deprivation of divine reward.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: share; Metaphorical: spiritual allotment in the afterlife.
- Root: فاجر (fājir)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: wicked, immoral, profligate.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: the dissolute one who commits sins openly.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: sinner; Metaphorical: one through whom God nonetheless supports religion.
- Root: شمع (shamʿ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: candle, wax taper.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: the candle as parable — consuming itself while giving light to others.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: candle; Metaphorical: one who destroys himself but benefits others.
- Root: نار (nār)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: fire.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: fire as parable — consuming itself and all around it.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: fire; Metaphorical: one who destroys himself and others.
- Root: سعد (saʿida)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to be fortunate, to prosper.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: saʿādah as felicity — success in the Hereafter.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: good fortune; Metaphorical: eternal felicity.
- Root: شقي (shaqiya)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to be wretched, to be miserable.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: shaqāwah as wretchedness — ruin in the Hereafter.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: misery; Metaphorical: eternal ruin.
- Root: أخلص (akhlaṣa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to purify, to be sincere.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: ikhlāṣ as purifying intention for God alone — the condition of acceptance.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: sincerity; Metaphorical: pure devotion.
- Root: ريب (rāba)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to doubt, to suspect.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-rayb as doubt and uncertainty — to be dispelled by evidence.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: doubt; Metaphorical: skepticism.
11:18.topic: Al-Ghazali on purifying the character, moral diseases, and spiritual remedies, from 'Book of Knowledge'

11:18.arabic: وأما الكافرون والمنافقون فتقول الأشهاد هؤلاء الذين كذبوا على ربهم ألا لعنة الله على الظالمين (2) وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم كل أمتي معافى إلا المجاهرين (3) وإن من المجاهرة أن يعمل الرجل السوء سرا ثم يخبر به وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم من استمع خبر قوم وهم له كارهون صب في أذنه الآنك يوم القيامة (4) ومنها أن يتقي مواضع التهم صيانة لقلوب الناس عن سوء الظن ولألسنتهم عن العيبة فإنهم إذا عصوا الله بذكره وكان هو السبب فيه كان شريكا قال الله تعالى ولا تسبوا الذي يدعون من دون الله فيسبوا الله عدوا بغير علم وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم كيف ترون من يسب أبويه فقالوا وهل من أحد يسب أبويه فق
11:18.english: **First**: That you greet him with peace (*salām*) when you meet him, and respond to his invitation when he invites you, and say "may Allah have mercy on you" (*tashmīt*) when he sneezes, and visit him when he is ill, and attend his funeral procession when he dies, and fulfill his oath when he swears by you, and give him sincere counsel when he seeks your advice, and protect him in his absence when he is away from you, and love for him what you love for yourself, and dislike for him what you dislike for yourself. (1)
11:18.section_title_en: The Rights of Brotherhood — Section 433: The Duties of a Muslim Toward His Fellow Muslims
11:18.anchors:
- Root: سلم (s-l-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of safety, security, freedom from harm; the root from which *islām* (submission/surrender) and *salām* (peace) derive
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): *Salām* as the theological state of being secure from harm — both giving and receiving safety; *islām* as the total surrender of the heart to Allah
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (*ḥaqīqah*): physical safety from tongue and hand; Metaphorical (*majāz*): the comprehensive spiritual safety that defines true Muslim brotherhood
- Root: عون (ʿ-w-n)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Assistance, aid, helping another in need
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Mutual assistance as a divine ordinance among believers
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical aid; Metaphorical: intercession (*shafāʿah*) and advocacy on behalf of others
- Root: ستر (s-t-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Covering, concealing, veiling; protection from exposure
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): *Sitr* as the divine attribute of concealment — Allah's covering of sins in this world and the next
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: covering a physical defect; Metaphorical: concealing another's faults and sins — a cardinal virtue of brotherhood
- Root: عذر (ʿ-dh-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Excuse, pardon, acceptance of apology
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): *ʿAfw* (pardon) as the higher station of forgiveness that elevates the forgiver
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: releasing from obligation; Metaphorical: the noble trait of overlooking others' offenses
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد (Restriction & Focused Predication) — The repeated use of restrictive constructions (e.g., "المسلم من سلم المسلمون") establishes definitional boundaries through predicate restriction, indicating that the *ḥaqīqah* of faith is manifested through specific observable actions.

##
11:18.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Duties of Brotherhood'

11:18.arabic: وقال بعض العلماء إن العبد ليتلو القرآن فيلعن نفسه وهو لا يعلم يقول {ألا لعنة الله على الظالمين} وهو ظالم نفسه ألا لعنة الله على الكاذبين وهو منهم وقال الحسن إنكم اتخذتم قراءة القرآن مراحل وجعلتم الليل جملا فأنتم تركبونه فتقطعون به مراحله وإن من كان قبلكم رأوه رسائل من ربهم فكانوا يتدبرونها بالليل وينفذونها بالنهار وقال ابن مسعود أنزل القرآن عليهم ليعملوا به فاتخذوا دراسته عملا إن أحدكم ليقرأ القرآن من فاتحته إلى خاتمته ما يسقط منه حرفا وقد أسقط العمل به وفي حديث ابن عمر وحديث جندب رضي الله عنهما لقد عشنا دهرا طويلا وأحدنا يؤتى الإي
11:18.english: Anas ibn Mālik said: "How many a reciter of the Qur'an there is, while the Qur'an curses him!" And Maysarah al-Gharīb said: "It is the Qur'an in the belly of the wicked one." And Abū Sulaymān al-Dārānī said: "The Zabāniyah (the stern keepers of Hell) are swifter to seize the carriers of the Qur'an who disobey God — Mighty and Majestic is He — than they are to seize the worshippers of idols, when they disobey God — Glorified is He — after having received the Qur'an."
11:18.section_title_en: Section 222 — On the Condemnation of the Recitation of the Negligent
11:18.anchors:
- Root: تلا (t-l-w)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of following in sequence, tracing footsteps; recitation as sequential articulation of words.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Tilāwah implies following with obedience — the reciter who does not follow the recited command is not truly a tālī.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: to follow behind. Metaphorical: the Qur'an "follows" or "pursues" its reciter — either blessing him or cursing him on the Day of Judgment.
- Root: لعل (l-ʿ-n)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To curse, to drive away from mercy, to banish.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Laʿnah is expulsion from divine mercy; the Qur'an itself "cursing" its reciter is a metaphorical (majāz) attribution of the act to the Book, the actual agent being God.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: imprecation. Metaphorical: the Qur'an's letters and verses standing as witnesses against the negligent reciter.
- Root: حمل (ḥ-m-l)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To carry, to bear; ḥāmil al-Qurʾān is one who bears the Qur'an by memorization.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Carrying implies bearing its obligations, not merely its letters — the true carrier is he who carries its commands into action.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical carrying. Metaphorical: bearing its legal responsibilities (takālīf).
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The rhetorical structure of "the Qur'an curses him" employs an implied agentive construction where the grammatical subject is the Book itself, requiring the reader to parse the metaphorical agency without literal attribution.
11:18.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'Condemnation of Anger and Hatred'

13:25.arabic: فهو في النار وقاض قضى بغير ما أمر الله به فهو في النار (2) وقال كعب رحمه الله يكون في آخر الزمان علماء يزهدون الناس في الدنيا ولا يزهدون ويخوفون الناس ولا يخافون وينهون عن غشيان الولاة ويأتونهم ويؤثرون الدنيا على الآخرة يأكلون بألسنتهم يقربون الأغنياء دون الفقراء يتغايرون على العلم كما تتغاير النساء على الرجال يغضب أحدهم على جليسه إذا جالس غيره أولئك الجبارون أعداء الرحمن وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم إن الشيطان ربما يسوفكم بالعلم فقيل يا رسول الله وكيف ذلك قال صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول اطلب الع
13:25.english: Know that the scholar who does not act upon his knowledge is condemned by the Book, the Sunnah, and the sayings of the sages. God, exalted be He, said: {«يا أيها الذين آمنوا لم تقولون ما لا تفعلون * كبر مقتا عند الله أن تقولوا ما لا تفعلون»} ("O you who believe, why do you say what you do not do? Most hateful it is to God that you say what you do not do"). And He said: {«أتأمرون الناس بالبر وتنسون أنفسكم»} ("Do you command people to righteousness while you forget yourselves?"). And He said: {«ومن الناس من يعجبك قوله في الحياة الدنيا ويشهد الله على ما في قلبه وهو ألد الخصام»} ("And among people is he whose speech pleases you in the worldly life, and he calls God to witness what is in his heart, yet he is the fiercest of opponents").
13:25.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Book of Knowledge'

13:25.arabic: يسعون في قطع ما أمر الله به أن يوصل ويفسدون في الأرض وقال تعالى {إنما السبيل على الذين يظلمون الناس ويبغون في الأرض بغير الحق} والنمام منهم وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم إن من شرار الناس
13:25.english: And whoever is the recipient of tale-bearing — it being said to him: "So-and-so said such-and-such about you," or "He did such-and-such against you," or "He is scheming to corrupt your affair," or "He is conspiring with your enemy," or "He is disparaging your condition," or whatever runs in that course — then six matters are incumbent upon him:
13:25.section_title_en: Section 692 — On the Duties of the One to Whom Tale-Bearing (Namīmah) Is Conveyed
13:25.anchors:
- Root: ن-م-م (N-M-M)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning — to stir up, incite, or carry tales; the one who transmits speech to cause discord.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance — namīmah is a species of corrupt speech that severs what God has commanded to be joined; it is aligned with fāsiq (transgressor) status, rendering the bearer's testimony rejected.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal vs Metaphorical — literally, the act of carrying and dropping seeds (naml) to cause sprouting; metaphorically, the dropping of speech into hearts to sow enmity.
- Root: غ-ي-ب (Gh-Y-B)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning — that which is concealed from the senses.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance — ghaybah (backbiting) is the mention of a person in his absence with what he dislikes; it is a violation of the unseen honor of the brother.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal vs Metaphorical — literal absence from sight; metaphorical — the absence of the subject from the gathering while his reputation is being torn.
- Root: ف-س-ق (F-S-Q)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning — to depart, to deviate from the straight path.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance — fisq is the breaking of the command of God; the fāsiq's report is not to be trusted without verification, per {إِن جَاءَكُمْ فَاسِقٌ بِنَبَإٍ فَتَبَيَّنُوا}.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal vs Metaphorical — literal: the date that peels from its husk; metaphorical: the soul that peels from obedience.
- Sibawayh Rule: Bāb al-Ḥaṣr wa al-Taqyīd bi-innamā (Restriction & Focused Predication) — The verse {إِنَّمَا السَّبِيلُ عَلَى الَّذِينَ يَظْلِمُونَ النَّاسَ} restricts the path of blame exclusively to the oppressors, thereby excluding the tale-bearer's victim from any culpability and affirming the tale-bearer's full liability.
13:25.topic: Classical commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya Ulum al-Din, from 'Condemnation of Anger and Hatred'

14:31.arabic: وسلم قال من كانت لأخيه عنده مظلمة في عرض أو مال فليستحللها منه من قبل أن يأتي يوم ليس هناك دينار ولا درهم إنما يؤخذ من حسناته فإن لم يكن له حسنات أخذ من سيئات صاحبه فزيدت على سيئاته (1) وقالت عائشة رضي الله عنها لامرأة قالت لأخرى أنها طويلة الذيل قد اغتبتيها فاستحليها فإذن لا بد من الاستحلال إن قدر عليه فإن كان غائبا أو ميتا فينبغي أن يكثر له الاستغفار والدعاء ويكثر من الحسنات فإن قلت فالتحليل هل يجب فأقول لا لأنه تبرع والتبرع فضل وليس بواجب ولكنه مستحسن وسبيل المعتذر أن يبالغ في الثناء عليه والتودد إليه
14:31.english:
- Root: غيب (gh-y-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "To be absent, hidden, concealed from sight; ghayb = that which is unseen/absent from perception"
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الغيب: مصدر غابت الشمس وغيرها: إذا استترت عن العين — used of everything absent from the senses and from human knowledge; applied to things as ghayb/ghā'ib relative to people, not relative to God, for nothing is absent from Him"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Haqiqah: "تكلم بذلك عن ظهر الغيب" (speaking of the unseen); Majaz: "أتونا في غابة" (metaphorical extension to dense/thick things)
- Root: حسن (ḥ-s-n)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "Beauty, goodness, excellence; to be fair, comely, good"
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الحسن: عبارة عن كل مبهج مرغوب فيه — three kinds: good by reason, good by desire, good by sense; ḥasanah = everything that delights one, whether in self, body, or circumstances"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Haqiqah: "أنظر إلى محاسن وجهه" (physical beauty); Majaz: "فلان لا يحسن شيئًا" (to do well/excel — transferred to action)
- Root: حرم (ḥ-r-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "To forbid, prohibit, make unlawful; ḥarām = that which is forbidden"
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الحرام: الممنوع منه إما بتسخير إلهي وإما بشري — prohibition by divine decree, by human law, by coercive prevention, by reason, or by revelation"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Haqiqah: "هتك رحمته" (violating sanctity); Majaz: "جلد محرم: لم يدبغ" (raw hide — metaphorical extension to "untreated/unlawful")
- Root: ظلم (ẓ-l-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "Wrongdoing, injustice, oppression; to place something in other than its proper place"
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الظلمة: عدم النور — darkness is absence of light; used metaphorically for ignorance, polytheism, and sin, just as light is used for their opposites"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Haqiqah: "فلان يظلم فيظلم" (to wrong and be wronged); Majaz: "أرض مظلومة" (land never dug — metaphorical: "wronged" land)
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — "إنما يؤخذ من حسناته" restricts the taking exclusively to good deeds, excluding any monetary compensation on that Day.
14:31.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'Condemnation of Anger and Hatred'

16:105.arabic: تعالى {إنما يفتري الكذب الذين لا يؤمنون بآيات الله} (2) وقال أبو سعيد الخدري سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يدعو فيقول في دعائه اللهم طهر قلبي من النفاق وفرجي من الزنا ولساني من الكذب (3) وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم ثلاثة لا يكلمهم الله ولا ينظر إليهم ولا يزكيهم ولهم عذاب أليم شيخ زان وملك كذاب وعائل مستكبر (4) حديث عبد الله بن عامر جاء رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إلى بيتنا وأنا صبي صغير فذهبت لألعب فقالت أمي يا عبد الله تعال أعطيك فقال وما أردت أن تعطيه قالت تمرا فقال إن لم تفعلي كتبت عليك كذ
16:105.english: Among them is the hadith: "And three whom God hates: the trader or seller who swears much." Ahmad narrated it, and the wording is his. In its chain is Ibn al-Aḥmaṣ, whose condition is unknown. Both Ahmad and al-Nasā'ī narrated it with another wording through a sound chain. And al-Nasā'ī has, from the hadith of Abū Hurayrah: "Four whom God abhors: the seller who swears much" — the hadith — and its chain is sound.
16:105.section_title_en: The Book of the Revival of the Religious Sciences — Section 676: On Lying (al-Kadhib) — Hadith Reports and Traditions (Āthār)
16:105.anchors:
- Root: كذب (Kadhaba)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to report a falsehood, to utter what is contrary to reality; al-Kadhdhābah: a variegated cloth that deceives the eye into thinking it is part of the ceiling — indicating the deceptive semblance of truth.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Kadhib applies to both speech and action. God says: {«Only they forge falsehood who do not believe in God's signs»} (Q 16:105) — the hypocrites' speech was true, but their inward conviction was false, so God called them liars (kādhibūn) regarding their belief.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqīqah): "He is kadhib, kadhūb, kadhāb, kaydhabān" — one who lies habitually. Metaphorical (Majāz): "He carried [the burden] then lied" — i.e., he cowardly retreated, making his charge a false one; "the she-camel lied" — her pregnancy proved false.
- Root: حدث (Ḥadatha)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to originate, to bring into being after non-existence; al-ḥadīth: speech that is new/recently originated.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Al-Ḥudūth: a thing's coming to be after it was not — whether accident or substance. Its creation (iḥdāth) belongs solely to God. Al-muḥdath: what is brought into existence after non-existence." God says: {«There comes not to them a fresh reminder (dhikr muḥdath) from their Lord»} (Q 21:2).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "He spoke a ḥadīth; fresh in age." Metaphorical: "They became aḥādīth (topics of talk)"; ʿUmar was called muḥaddath — one whose intuition is divinely inspired, as if truth were spoken into him.
- Root: ويل (Wayl)
  * Lisan / Ayn: An expression of intense woe, destruction, and chastisement; a word of threat and condemnation.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Wayl denotes severe affliction and ruin; it is a declaration of impending punishment.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "Woe to him" — a cry of ruin. Used in threats: "Waylun lahu" — destruction is his due.
- Root: شنأ (Shana'a)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Intense hatred and abhorrence.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-Shan'ān: intense hatred that drives one to shun the object.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "He hated him with shan'an" — vehement hatred.
- Sibawayh Rule: Bāb al-Ḥaṣr wa al-Taqyīd bi-innamā (Restriction and Focused Predication) — The particle innamā restricts the predicate to the subject alone, negating it for all else. Applied in the verse: {«Only they forge falsehood who do not believe»} — restricting fabrication to the disbelievers, affirming that the believer does not lie.
16:105.topic: Al-Ghazali on purifying the character, moral diseases, and spiritual remedies, from 'Condemnation of Anger and Hatred'

18:70.arabic: والتسليم فقال {فإن اتبعتني فلا تسألني عن شيء حتى أحدث لك منه ذكرا} ثم لم يصبر ولم يزل في مراودته إلى أن كان ذلك سبب الفراق بينهما وبالجملة كل متعلم استبقى لنفسه رأيا واختيارا دون اختيار المعلم فاحكم عليه بالإخفاق والخسران فإن قلت فقد قال الله تعالى {فاسألوا أهل الذكر إن كنتم لا تعلمون} فالسؤال مأمور به فاعلم أنه كذلك ولكن فيما يأذن المعلم في السؤال عنه فإن السؤال عما لم تبلغ مرتبتك إلى فهمه مذموم ولذلك منع الخضر موسى عليه السلام من السؤال أي دع السؤال قبل أوانه فالمعلم أعلم بما أنت أهل له وبأوان الك
18:70.english: I say: Knowledge is like a torrent that is hostile to the elevated place — it flows only to the low ground. Thus knowledge is not attained except through humility and the casting of one's hearing [in attentive submission]. God — exalted is He — said: {«Indeed in that is a reminder for whoever has a heart or casts his hearing while present as a witness»} (Q 50:37). And the meaning of his being "one having a heart" is that he should be receptive to knowledge, comprehending it. But then the capacity for understanding does not avail him until he casts his hearing while being a present witness — present of heart — so that he may receive everything that is cast to him with excellence of listening, supplication, gratitude, joy, and acceptance of the benefaction.
18:70.section_title_en: The Revival of the Religious Sciences — Book I, Section 42: On the Duties of the Student (Ādāb al-Mutaʿallim)
18:70.anchors:
- Root: ع ل م (ʿ-l-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of knowing, perceiving a thing in its reality; the mark, trace, or sign by which one is guided.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "العلم: إدراك الشيء بحقيقته" — knowledge is the apprehension of a thing in its true reality, divided into apprehension of the essence and judgment upon it.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): "هو من أعلام العلم الخافقه" — he is among the lofty banners of knowledge. Metaphorical (majāz): "خفيت معالم الطريق" — the waymarks of the road are hidden, i.e., the traces by which one is guided.
- Root: س م ع (s-m-ʿ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Hearing, listening; the ear; obedience and acceptance.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Hearing with attentive presence of heart, not merely the physical sensation of sound.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: auditory perception. Metaphorical: "ألقى السمع" — to cast one's hearing, i.e., to listen with full attentiveness and submission.
- Root: ق ل ب (q-l-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The heart; to turn, overturn, or transform a thing from one state to another.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "قلب الشيء: تصريفه وصرفه عن وجه إلى وجه" — the turning of a thing from one face to another; the heart as that which is ever-turning between states.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "قلب الشيء قلبا: حوله عن وجهه" — to turn a thing from its face. Metaphorical: "رجل قلب حول: يقلب الأمور ويحتال" — a man who turns matters over and devises means.
- Root: ب ح ر (b-ḥ-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The sea; vast expanse of water.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "أصل البحر: كل مكان واسع جامع للماء الكثير" — the sea is every vast place gathering much water; then metaphorically applied to one who expands deeply into a domain.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Metaphorical: "تبحر في العلم واستبحر فيه" — he plunged deep into knowledge and expanded therein like a sea.
- Sibawayh Rule: Bāb al-ḥaṣr wa-l-taqyīd bi-innamā (Restriction and Focused Predication) — the particle innamā restricts the predicate to the subject alone, negating all else; applied here to the exclusive path of the student's submission to the teacher's direction.
18:70.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Condemnation of Anger and Hatred'

18:73.arabic: فلما سأل عن السفينة أنكر عليه حتى اعتذر وقال {لا تؤاخذني بما نسيت ولا ترهقني من أمري عسرا} فلم يصبر حتى سأل ثلاثا قال {هذا فراق بيني وبينك} وفارقه فسؤال العوام عن غوامض الدين من أعظم الآفات وهو من المثيرات للفتن فيجب قمعهم ومنعهم من ذلك وخوضهم في حروف القرآن يضاهي حال من كتب الملك إليه كتابا ورسم له فيه أمورا فلم يشتغل بشيء منها وضيع زمانه في أن قرطاس الكتاب عتيق أم حديث فاستحق بذلك العقوبة لا محالة فكذلك تضييع العامي حدود القرآن واشتغاله بحروفه أهي قديمة أم حديثة وكذلك سائر صفات الله سبحانه وتعالى والله تعالى أعلم
18:73.english: Whoever asks concerning an obscure science (ʿilm ghāmiḍ) while his understanding has not reached that degree is blameworthy, for relative to that [science] he is a common man. For this reason, the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Leave me as I have left you, for those before you were destroyed only by their excessive questioning and their differing with their prophets. What I have forbidden you, avoid; and what I have commanded you, do of it what you are able." {«ذروني ما تركتكم فإنما هلك من كان قبلكم بكثرة سؤالهم واختلافهم على أنبيائهم ما نهيتكم عنه فاجتنبوه وما أمرتكم به فأتوا منه ما استطعتم»} (1)
18:73.section_title_en: The Twentieth Affliction: The Questioning of the Common Folk Concerning the Attributes of God and His Speech
18:73.anchors:
- Root: س-أ-ل (sa-ʾa-la)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The act of asking, inquiring, or seeking information; its core sense involves a request directed toward another.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In theological discourse, questioning (suʾāl) about divine matters without proper preparation or station is blameworthy, as it exceeds the bounds of what the questioner is obligated to know and ventures into what is not his concern.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) questioning seeks permissible knowledge; metaphorical (majāz) usage extends to the "questioning" of fate or the soul's improper probing into hidden matters, which is censured.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — The Prophet's command {«ذروني ما تركتكم»} uses restriction to delimit the sphere of permissible inquiry, confining it to what the Lawgiver has addressed.
18:73.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'Condemnation of Anger and Hatred'

18:78.arabic: ترهقني من أمري عسرا} فلم يصبر حتى سأل ثلاثا قال {هذا فراق بيني وبينك} وفارقه فسؤال العوام عن غوامض الدين من أعظم الآفات وهو من المثيرات للفتن فيجب قمعهم ومنعهم من ذلك وخوضهم في حروف القرآن يضاهي حال من كتب الملك إليه كتابا ورسم له فيه أمورا فلم يشتغل بشيء منها وضيع زمانه في أن قرطاس الكتاب عتيق أم حديث فاستحق بذلك العقوبة لا محالة فكذلك تضييع العامي حدود القرآن واشتغاله بحروفه أهي قديمة أم حديثة وكذلك سائر صفات الله سبحانه وتعالى والله تعالى أعلم

- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — The Prophet's command {«ذروني ما تركتكم»} uses restriction to delimit the sphere of permissible inquiry, confining it to what the Lawgiver has addressed.
