19:54.arabic: {واذكر في الكتاب إبراهيم إنه كان صديقا نبيا} وقال واذكر في الكتاب إسمعيل إنه كان صادق الوعد وكان رسولا نبيا وقال تعالى {واذكر في الكتاب إدريس إنه كان صديقا نبيا} وقال ابن عباس أربع من كن فيه فقد ربح الصدق والحياء وحسن الخلق والشكر وقال بشر ابن الحارث من عامل الله بالصدق استوحش من الناس وقال أبو عبد الله الرملي رأيت منصور الدينوري في المنام فقلت له ما فعل الله بك قال غفر لي ورحمني وأعطاني ما لم أؤمل فقلت له أحسن ما توجه العبد به إلى الله ماذا قال الصدق وأقبح ما توجه به الكذب وقال أبو سليمان اجعل الصدق مطيتك والح
19:54.english: God Most High has said: {«رجال صدقوا ما عاهدوا الله عليه»} — "Among the believers are men who have been true to the covenant they made with God" (Al-Aḥzāb 33:23). And the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Verily, truthfulness leads to righteousness (al-birr), and righteousness leads to Paradise. And verily, a man continues to speak truthfully until he is written with God as a supremely veracious one (ṣiddīq). And verily, falsehood leads to wickedness (al-fujūr), and wickedness leads to the Fire. And verily, a man continues to lie until he is written with God as a liar (kadhdhāb)." (1)
19:54.section_title_en: The Book of Truthfulness (Ṣidq): Its Virtue and Reality — Section on the Virtue of Truthfulness
19:54.anchors:
- Root: صدق (Ṣ-D-Q)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root denotes the firmness and soundness of a thing; a spear termed "ṣadq" is straight and rigid; truthfulness is speech that is firm, sound, and free of crookedness.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الصدق والكذب أصلهما في القول" — truthfulness and falsehood originate in speech, whether past or future, promise or otherwise; they occur by primary intent only in informative statements (khabar), not in other speech categories. Al-Raghib further notes the derived degrees: ṣidq (truthfulness), ṣiddīq (the supremely veracious — one whose truthfulness has become his very character), and ṣādiq al-waʿd (truthful in promise).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Haqiqah (literal): "صدقته الحديث" — to affirm someone's report as true. Majaz (metaphorical): "رجل صادق الحملة" — a man truthful in his charge (i.e., steadfast and unfaltering in battle), and "فرس ذو مصدق في الجري" — a horse with genuine exertion in running. Thus ṣidq extends metaphorically to any state of firmness, steadfastness, and correspondence between inner conviction and outward action.
- Root: بر (B-R-R)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Al-Birr: expansive goodness, piety, and obedience; the "barr" (land) is so named for its expanse. It encompasses all acts of righteousness and kindness.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-birr is the breadth of obedience to God through sincere intention and righteous action; it is the comprehensive term for all that God loves and approves.
- Root: فجر (F-J-R)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Al-Fujūr: the breaking forth and bursting open — the wickedness that breaks through the barrier of piety; the "fājir" is one who bursts out of obedience into transgression.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Fujūr is the violation of the covenant of obedience, the breaking open of the seal of God-consciousness; it is the opposite of birr.
- Root: كذب (K-DH-B)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Al-Kidhb: falsehood — informing of a thing contrary to its reality; the root also carries the sense of deficiency and weakness (as in "kadhaba" — to fall short).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Falsehood is the counterpart of ṣidq — it is reporting what does not correspond to reality, whether in past, present, or future tense.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The grammatical structure "يكتب عند الله صديقا" (he is written with God as a ṣiddīq) involves the prepositional phrase "عند الله" interposed between the verb and its predicate accusative, a construction permissible when the interposed element is semantically integral to the judgment, as here where divine decree is the ground of the designation.
19:54.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'Condemnation of Anger and Hatred'

22:38.arabic: وسلم فقال نعم إن الله لا يحب المستكبرين فنزل وقعد معهم على الأرض وأكل ثم سلم عليهم وركب وقال قد أجبتكم فأجيبوني قالوا نعم فوعدهم وقتا معلوما فحضروا فقدم إليهم فاخر الطعام وجلس يأكل معهم وأما قول القائل إن من وضعت يدي في قصعته فقد ذلت له رقبتي فقد قال بعضهم هذا خلاف السنة وليس كذلك فإنه ذل إذا كان الداعي لا يفرح بالإجابة ولا يتقلد منة وكان يرى ذلك يدا له على المدعو ورسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كان يحضر لعلمه أن الداعي له يتقلد منة ويرى ذلك شرفا وذخرا لنفسه في الدنيا
22:38.english: The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Do not burden your guest so that you make him hate you, for whoever hates his guest has hated Allah, and whoever hates Allah, Allah hates him."
22:38.section_title_en: The Etiquettes of Hospitality: Invitation, Response, Attendance, and the Serving of Food — Section 290 of The Revival of the Religious Sciences
22:38.anchors:
- Root: ضيف (ḍ-y-f)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning is "to incline, to lean toward." The guest (al-ḍayf) is one who inclines toward you, alighting as a visitor; the root carries the sense of leaning or bending.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The guest is "one who inclines to you, alighting with you"; hospitality (al-ḍiyāfah) became customary in the sense of receiving such a one. The word is originally a verbal noun, hence one and many are equal in most usage.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): "ḍāfa ilayhi: he inclined toward him"; "ḍāfat al-shams: the sun inclined toward setting." Metaphorical (majāz): "aḍāfa ilayhi amran: he attributed a matter to him, leaning it upon him"; "al-muḍāf: the one constrained, hemmed in, in distress."
- Sibawayh Rule: Restriction and Focused Predication (al-ḥaṣr wa al-taqyīd bi-innamā) — governing the Prophet's statement "innamā hādhihi al-akhlāq bi-yad Allāh" (these morals are only in the hand of Allah), where innamā restricts the attribution of moral character exclusively to divine bestowal.
22:38.topic: Al-Ghazali on purifying the character, moral diseases, and spiritual remedies, from 'Condemnation of Anger and Hatred'

24:48.arabic: والذين يكثرون البغضاء لإخوانهم في صدورهم فإذا لقوهم تملقوا لهم والذين إذا دعوا إلى الله ورسوله كانوا بطاء وإذا دعوا إلى الشيطان وأمره كانوا سراعا (3) وقال ابن مسعود لا يكونن أحدكم إمعة قالوا وما الإمعة قال الذي يجري مع كل ريح واتفقوا على أن ملاقاة الاثنين بوجهين نفاق وللنفاق علامات كثيرة وهذه من جملتها وقد روي أن رجلا من أصحاب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم مات فلم يصل عليه حذيفة فقال له عمر يموت رجل من أصحاب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ولم تصل عليه فقال يا أمير المؤمنين إنه منهم فقال نشدتك الله أنا منهم أم لا قال اللهم لا ولا أؤمن منها
24:48.english: ʿAmmār ibn Yāsir said: The Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Whoever has two faces in this world shall have two tongues of fire on the Day of Resurrection." {«من كان له وجهان في الدنيا كان له لسانان من نار يوم القيامة»} (1)
24:48.section_title_en: On the Two-Tongued Man (Dhū Lisānayn): The Marks of Hypocrisy in Dealing with Opposing Parties
24:48.anchors:
- Root: لسن (L-S-N)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The tongue (al-lisān); by extension, speech, language, and mode of expression. "Dhū lisānayn" (possessor of two tongues) is a metaphorical construction denoting one who speaks differently to different parties.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Speech is the instrument of disclosure (kashf) of what lies in the heart. Two tongues signify a duplicity of inward disposition manifesting as contradictory outward utterances — a rupture between the inner reality (sirr) and outward expression.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): the physical tongue. Metaphorical (majāz): "dhū lisānayn" as one who flatters each faction with agreeable speech, regardless of truth — the rhetorical figure of metonymy where the instrument of speech stands for the moral character of the speaker.
- Root: وجه (W-J-H)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The face; front; aspect; direction. "Dhū wajhayn" (possessor of two faces) — one who presents a different countenance to each party.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The face is the locus of human dignity and the mirror of inner states. Two faces signify a分裂 of the self between outward display and inward reality — a form of spiritual duplicity.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the physical face. Metaphorical: "coming to these with a face and to those with a face" — i.e., showing amity and honor to each while harboring enmity or contempt — a majāz for hypocrisy (nifāq).
- Root: وفق (W-F-Q)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To agree, to be suitable, to conform. "Yuwāfiq" — he speaks in a manner that accords with the listener's disposition.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): True agreement (tawfīq) is from God and aligns with truth; false agreement is mere accommodation to passion and self-interest.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: concordance. Metaphorical: the hypocrite's "agreement" is a simulation of concord while the heart is estranged — a majāz for flattery (mudāhanah).
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Predication with Dual Subjects (Bāb al-ʿAṭf ʿalā al-Mubtadaʾ) — The construction "man kāna lahu wajhān... kāna lahu lisānān" employs a conditional-relative clause where the apodosis mirrors the protasis in grammatical form, emphasizing the moral correspondence between outward duplicity and its eschatological recompense.
24:48.topic: Al-Ghazali on the journey of the soul, death, and the Hereafter, from 'Condemnation of Anger and Hatred'

24:52.arabic: وخطب رجل عند رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال من يطع الله ورسوله فقد رشد ومن يعصهما فقد غوى فقال قل ومن يعص الله ورسوله فقد غوى (2) فكره رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قوله ومن يعصهما لأنه تسوية وجمع وكان إبراهيم يكره أن يقول الرجل أعوذ بالله وبك ويجوز أن يقول أعوذ بالله ثم بك وأن يقول لولا الله ثم فلان ولا يقول لولا الله وفلان وكره بعضهم أن يقال اللهم أعتقنا من النار وكان يقول العتق يكون بعد الورود وكانوا يستجيرون من النار ويتعوذون من النار وقال رجل اللهم اجعلني ممن تصيبه شفاعة محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم فق
24:52.english: An example of this is what Ḥudhayfah reported: The Prophet, peace be upon him, said: "Let none of you say: 'What Allah willed and you willed' — but rather let him say: 'What Allah willed, then you willed.'" (5) This is because in the absolute conjunction [with "and"] there is an association and an equalization, which is contrary to [the due measure of] reverence. And Ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: A man came to the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, speaking to him concerning some matter, and he said: "What Allah willed and you willed." The Prophet, peace be upon him, said: "Have you made me an equal to Allah? Rather, [say]: 'What Allah willed alone.'" (1)
24:52.section_title_en: The Revival of the Religious Sciences — Section 698: The Nineteenth Affliction — Heedlessness Regarding Subtle Errors in the Import of Speech
24:52.anchors:
- Root: غفل (ghafla)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of heedlessness, neglect, and inattention; the absence of vigilance over a matter.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Heedlessness (al-ghafla) is the soul's failure to attend to what it is obligated to know or consider; it is the opposite of mindfulness (al-tayaqquẓ) and remembrance (al-dhikr).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) usage denotes the absence of guarding; metaphorical (majāz) usage extends to the tongue's straying from precise expression in sacred matters.
- Root: عطف (ʿaṭf)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Inclination, turning, or joining one thing to another; grammatically, the conjunction that links two items in a shared ruling.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Joining (al-ʿaṭf) implies equal treatment of the conjoined items; in theological speech, absolute conjunction (al-ʿaṭf al-muṭlaq) with Allah entails an inadmissible association.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the bending of a staff or the inclining of a branch; metaphorical: the grammatical coupling that levels two referents under one predicate.
- Root: شرك (shirk)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Sharing, partnership, or association; the root of polytheism (al-shirk) as the ascription of a partner to Allah.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Association (al-shirk) is the equalization of two things in a shared ruling; in theology, it is the gravest form when applied to the Divine, whether in belief or in the mere wording of speech.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: co-participation in ownership; metaphorical: any verbal or creedal equalization of the creature with the Creator.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Conjunction (al-ʿaṭf) and Restriction (al-ḥaṣr) — The particle "thumma" (then) indicates sequential ordering and distinction of rank, whereas "wa" (and) denotes absolute conjunction and mutual equivalence; thus the Prophet's command to replace "wa" with "thumma" in "what Allah willed and you willed" is a syntactic correction to abolish the implication of equal partnership.
24:52.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications, prayers, and their spiritual power, from 'Condemnation of Anger and Hatred'

28:76.arabic: وسلم فقال نعم إن الله لا يحب المستكبرين فنزل وقعد معهم على الأرض وأكل ثم سلم عليهم وركب وقال قد أجبتكم فأجيبوني قالوا نعم فوعدهم وقتا معلوما فحضروا فقدم إليهم فاخر الطعام وجلس يأكل معهم وأما قول القائل إن من وضعت يدي في قصعته فقد ذلت له رقبتي فقد قال بعضهم هذا خلاف السنة وليس كذلك فإنه ذل إذا كان الداعي لا يفرح بالإجابة ولا يتقلد منة وكان يرى ذلك يدا له على المدعو ورسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كان يحضر لعلمه أن الداعي له يتقلد منة ويرى ذلك شرفا وذخرا لنفسه في الدنيا
28:76.english: The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Do not burden your guest so that you make him hate you, for whoever hates his guest has hated Allah, and whoever hates Allah, Allah hates him."
28:76.section_title_en: The Etiquettes of Hospitality: Invitation, Response, Attendance, and the Serving of Food — Section 290 of The Revival of the Religious Sciences
28:76.anchors:
- Root: ضيف (ḍ-y-f)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning is "to incline, to lean toward." The guest (al-ḍayf) is one who inclines toward you, alighting as a visitor; the root carries the sense of leaning or bending.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The guest is "one who inclines to you, alighting with you"; hospitality (al-ḍiyāfah) became customary in the sense of receiving such a one. The word is originally a verbal noun, hence one and many are equal in most usage.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): "ḍāfa ilayhi: he inclined toward him"; "ḍāfat al-shams: the sun inclined toward setting." Metaphorical (majāz): "aḍāfa ilayhi amran: he attributed a matter to him, leaning it upon him"; "al-muḍāf: the one constrained, hemmed in, in distress."
- Sibawayh Rule: Restriction and Focused Predication (al-ḥaṣr wa al-taqyīd bi-innamā) — governing the Prophet's statement "innamā hādhihi al-akhlāq bi-yad Allāh" (these morals are only in the hand of Allah), where innamā restricts the attribution of moral character exclusively to divine bestowal.
28:76.topic: Al-Ghazali on purifying the character, moral diseases, and spiritual remedies, from 'Condemnation of Anger and Hatred'

28:77.arabic: قال الله وأحسن كما أحسن الله إليك وقال عز وجل إن الله يأمر بالعدل والإحسان وقال سبحانه إن رحمت الله قريب من المحسنين ونعني بالإحسان فعل ما ينتفع به المعامل وهو غير واجب عليه ولكنه تفضل منه فإن الواجب يدخل في باب العدل وترك الظلم وقد ذكرناه وتنال رتبة الإحسان بواحد من ستة أمور الأول في المغابنة فينبغي أن لا يغبن صاحبه بما لا يتغابن به في العادة فأما أصل المغابنة فمأذون فيه لأن البيع للربح ولا يمكن ذلك إلا بغبن ما ولكن يراعي فيه التقريب فإن بذل المشتري زيادة على الربح المعت
28:77.english: God (Exalted is He) has commanded both justice (al-ʿadl) and excellence (al-iḥsān) together. Justice is only the cause of deliverance (al-najāh), and it runs in trade as the course of capital (raʾs al-māl). Excellence is the cause of triumph (al-fawz) and the attainment of felicity (al-saʿādah), and it runs in trade as the course of profit (al-ribḥ). None is counted among the heedless who is content in his worldly transactions with merely his capital — and so likewise in the transactions of the Hereafter. Thus it behooves the religious person not to restrict himself to justice and the avoidance of wrongdoing (ẓulm), abandoning the doors of excellence. God has said: {«وَأَحْسِنْ كَمَا أَحْسَنَ اللَّهُ إِلَيْكَ»} ("And do good as God has done good to you") {«إِنَّ اللَّهَ يَأْمُرُ بِالْعَدْلِ وَالْإِحْسَانِ»} ("Indeed, God commands justice and excellence"), and He (Exalted is He) has said: {«إِنَّ رَحْمَتَ اللَّهِ قَرِيبٌ مِنَ الْمُحْسِنِينَ»} ("Indeed, the mercy of God is near to the doers of excellence").
28:77.section_title_en: Chapter Four: On Excellence (Iḥsān) in Transactional Dealings
28:77.anchors:
- Root: ع د ل (ʿadala)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of equality, straightness, and balance; the root denotes that which is level and even, without crookedness or deviation.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "العدالة والمعادلة: لفظ يقتضي معنى المساواة" — justice is that which is perceived by inner insight (al-baṣīrah), pertaining to judgments and rulings; it is the equitable apportioning of things on an even scale.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) usage pertains to physical evenness and moderation (e.g., a horse with an even blaze); metaphorical (majāz) extension applies to moral and legal equity.
- Root: ر ب ح (rabiḥa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Gain, profit, increase in trade; the root signifies surplus and augmentation.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الربح: الزيادة الحاصلة في المبايعة، ثم يتجوز به في كل ما يعود من ثمرة عمل" — profit is the increase occurring in exchange, then metaphorically extended to every fruit that returns from a deed.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal usage in commerce; metaphorical usage: "تجارة رابحة" — a profitable transaction, extended to spiritual commerce.
- Root: و ق د (waqada)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Fire blazing and burning fiercely; kindling.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Fire that burns; used in the Qur'an for the fuel of Hellfire.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: fire blazing; Metaphorical: "قلب وقاد" — a blazing, keen intellect; "وقدة الصيف" — the intense heat of summer.
- Sibawayh Rule: Chapter on the Interposition between the Preposition and its Object (Bāb al-Faṣl bayn al-Jār wa al-Majrūr) — governing the permissible separation between grammatical operators and their operands for rhetorical emphasis, as in the periodic construction of conditional and exceptive clauses.
28:77.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'Etiquette of Earning'

28:77.arabic: قال الله تعالى ولا تنس نصيبك من الدنيا أي لا تنس في الدنيا نصيبك منها للآخرة فإنها مزرعة الآخرة وفيها تكتسب الحسنات وإنما تتم شفقة التاجر على دينه بمراعاة سبعة أمور الأول حسن النية والعقيدة في ابتداء التجارة فلينو بها الاستعفاف عن السؤال وكف الطمع عن الناس استغناء بالحلال عنهم واستعانة بما يكسبه على الدين وقياما بكفاية العيال ليكون من جملة المجاهدين به ولينو النصح للمسلمين وأن يحب لسائر الخلق ما يحب لنفسه ولينو اتباع طريق العدل والإحسان في معاملته كما ذكرناه ولينو الأمر بالمعروف والن
28:77.english: Some of the Salaf (may God be pleased with them) said: "The thing most worthy of the intelligent man is that which he most needs in the immediate term; and the thing he most needs in the immediate term is that whose consequence is most praiseworthy in the long term."
28:77.section_title_en: On the Merchant's Vigilance Over His Religion: Seven Matters of Concern in Trade
28:77.anchors:
- Root: دنا (d-n-w)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Proximity, nearness in place, time, or rank; the nearer (adnā) as opposed to the farther.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الدنو: القرب بالذات، أو بالحكم" — nearness by essence or by judgment; used of place, time, and station. The "nearer life" (al-ḥayāh al-dunyā) is the proximate, lower life.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical nearness. Metaphorical: the worldly life (al-dunyā) as that which is "nearer" and lower, contrasted with the Hereafter (al-ākhirah) which is "farther" but enduring.
- Root: سوق (s-w-q)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To drive, to impel, to lead; a market (sūq) where goods are driven and circulated.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The driving of one's self toward a goal; the market as the arena of exchange and transaction.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "ساق النعم فانساقت" — he drove the cattle and they were driven. Metaphorical: "ساق الله إليه خيرا" — God drove good to him; "ساق إليها المهر" — he sent the dowry to her. The "market of the Hereafter" (sūq al-ākhirah) is the mosque, where one trades deeds for the next life.
- Root: جار (j-w-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To deviate from the right path, to wrong, to oppress; also a neighbor (jār) whose rights are sacred.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الجار: من يقرب مسكنه منك" — the neighbor is one whose dwelling is near yours; a reciprocal term. God's right and the neighbor's right are conjoined in the Qur'anic verse {والجار ذي القربى والجار الجنب} (Al-Nisā': 36).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: oppression and transgression. Metaphorical: the "oppressive oath" (yamīn fājirah) — an oath that swerves from truth and justice.
- Root: الي (a-l-w)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To fall short, to fail; also related to رسالة (message) via مألكة.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The root conveys the idea of commission and conveyance of a message; "المألكة: الرسالة" — the message, because it is "chewed" in the mouth (from ألك, to masticate).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: to chew. Metaphorical: the angelic conveyance of revelation as a "message" delivered.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — When the author says "وإنما تتم شفقة التاجر على دينه بمراعاة سبعة أمور" ("The merchant's compassion for his religion is only completed by observing seven matters"), the particle إنما restricts and confines the predicate to the subject, establishing that these seven matters are the exclusive and exhaustive means to the end.
28:77.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'Etiquette of Earning'

28:77.arabic: وسلم فقال نعم إن الله لا يحب المستكبرين فنزل وقعد معهم على الأرض وأكل ثم سلم عليهم وركب وقال قد أجبتكم فأجيبوني قالوا نعم فوعدهم وقتا معلوما فحضروا فقدم إليهم فاخر الطعام وجلس يأكل معهم وأما قول القائل إن من وضعت يدي في قصعته فقد ذلت له رقبتي فقد قال بعضهم هذا خلاف السنة وليس كذلك فإنه ذل إذا كان الداعي لا يفرح بالإجابة ولا يتقلد منة وكان يرى ذلك يدا له على المدعو ورسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كان يحضر لعلمه أن الداعي له يتقلد منة ويرى ذلك شرفا وذخرا لنفسه في الدنيا
28:77.english: The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Do not burden your guest so that you make him hate you, for whoever hates his guest has hated Allah, and whoever hates Allah, Allah hates him."
28:77.section_title_en: The Etiquettes of Hospitality: Invitation, Response, Attendance, and the Serving of Food — Section 290 of The Revival of the Religious Sciences
28:77.anchors:
- Root: ضيف (ḍ-y-f)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning is "to incline, to lean toward." The guest (al-ḍayf) is one who inclines toward you, alighting as a visitor; the root carries the sense of leaning or bending.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The guest is "one who inclines to you, alighting with you"; hospitality (al-ḍiyāfah) became customary in the sense of receiving such a one. The word is originally a verbal noun, hence one and many are equal in most usage.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): "ḍāfa ilayhi: he inclined toward him"; "ḍāfat al-shams: the sun inclined toward setting." Metaphorical (majāz): "aḍāfa ilayhi amran: he attributed a matter to him, leaning it upon him"; "al-muḍāf: the one constrained, hemmed in, in distress."
- Sibawayh Rule: Restriction and Focused Predication (al-ḥaṣr wa al-taqyīd bi-innamā) — governing the Prophet's statement "innamā hādhihi al-akhlāq bi-yad Allāh" (these morals are only in the hand of Allah), where innamā restricts the attribution of moral character exclusively to divine bestowal.

31:17.arabic: فقال يا أبا ثعلبة مر بالمعروف وأنه عن المنكر فإذا رأيت شحا مطاعا وهوى متبعا ودنيا مؤثرة وإعجاب كل ذي رأي برأيه فعليك بنفسك ودع عنك العوام إن من ورائكم فتنا كقطع الليل المظلم للمتمسك فيها بمثل الذي أنتم عليه أجر خمسين منكم قيل بل منهم يا رسول الله قال لا بل منكم لأنكم تجدون على الخير أعوانا ولا يجدون عليه أعوانا وسئل ابن مسعود رضي الله عنه عن تفسير هذه الآية فقال إن هذا ليس زمانها إنها اليوم مقبولة ولكن قد أوشك أن يأتي زمانها تأمرون بالمعروف فيصنع بكم كذا وكذا وتقولون فلا يقبل منكم فحينئذ عليكم أنف
31:17.english: Know that the verses indicating the obligation of commanding right and forbidding wrong are numerous. Among them is His saying, may He be exalted: {«Let there arise from among you a nation inviting to good, commanding right and forbidding wrong — and those are the successful»} (Āl ʿImrān 3:104). In this verse is the declaration of obligation, for His saying, may He be exalted, "Let there be" (wal-takun) is a command, and the apparent meaning of a command is obligation. In it also is the declaration that success (falāḥ) is contingent upon it, for He restricted it and said: {«And those are the successful»}. In it also is the declaration that it is a collective obligation (farḍ kifāyah), not an individual obligation (farḍ ʿayn), and that when a group undertakes it, the obligation falls from the rest — for He did not say, "Let all of you be commanders of right," but rather said: {«Let there arise from among you a nation»}. Thus, whenever one person or a group undertakes it, the burden falls from the others, and success is particularized to those who undertake it and directly perform it. But if all of creation were to hold back from it, the burden would encompass all those capable of it without exception.
31:17.topic: Al-Ghazali on purifying the character, moral diseases, and spiritual remedies, from 'Enjoining Good and Forbidding Evil'

31:17.arabic: الفحشاء والمنكر والبغي} وقوله {واصبر على ما أصابك إن ذلك من عزم الأمور} وقوله {ولمن صبر وغفر إن ذلك لمن عزم الأمور} وقوله {فاعف عنهم واصفح إن الله يحب المحسنين} وقوله {وليعفوا وليصفحوا ألا تحبون أن يغفر الله لكم} وقوله {ادفع بالتي هي أحسن فإذا الذي بينك وبينه عداوة كأنه ولي حميم} وقوله {والكاظمين الغيظ والعافين عن الناس والله يحب المحسنين} وقوله {اجتنبوا كثيرا من الظن إن بعض الظن إثم ولا تجسسوا ولا يغتب بعضكم بعضا} ولما كسرت رباعيته وشج يوم أحد فجعل الدم يسيل على وجهه وهو يمسح الدم ويقول كيف يفلح قوم خضبوا وجه
31:17.english: The Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, was abundant in supplication and earnest entreaty, perpetually asking God Most High to adorn him with the beauties of refined conduct and the noble traits of character. Thus he would say in his supplication: "O God, beautify my outward form and my inward character (khuluqī wa-khalqī)" (1), and he would say: "O God, protect me from the reprehensible traits of character" (2). God Most High answered his supplication, fulfilling His word, Exalted is He: {«ادعوني أستجب لكم»} ["Call upon Me, I will answer you"] (Ghafir 40:60). So He sent down upon him the Qur'an and disciplined him through it, and his character became the Qur'an.
31:17.book_title: Etiquette of Living and Prophetic Character
31:17.section_title_en: The Prophet's Discipline Through the Qur'an and the Invitation to Noble Moral Traits
31:17.anchors:
- Root: خلق (khalaqa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of measuring, fashioning, and creating upon a precise estimation; also used for innate disposition and character.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الخلق أصله: التقدير المستقيم" — the root denotes straight/right estimation; used for bringing something into being from nothing (ibdāʿ) and for the moral constitution of the soul.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): "خلق الخراز الأديم" — the leather-worker measures before cutting. Metaphorical (Majaz): "خلق الله الخلق: أوجده على تقدير أوجبته الحكمة" — God's creation is bringing into existence upon a measure required by wisdom; and "له خلق حسن" — he has beautiful character.
- Root: كرم (karuma)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Generosity, nobility, honor; the root of karīm (noble/generous) and makārim (noble traits).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الكرم إذا وصف الله تعالى به فهو اسم لإحسانه وإنعامه المتظاهر" — when attributed to God, it denotes His manifest beneficence; when attributed to man, it denotes praiseworthy morals and deeds that appear from him.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "كرم علينا فلان كرامة" — he showed generosity. Metaphorical: "قوم كرم" — a noble people; "كرم السحاب تكريما: جاد بمطره" — the cloud was generous with its rain.
- Root: أدب (adaba)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Refinement, discipline, cultivation of character; calling to a gathering (ma'dabah) — the root implies assembling and summoning toward excellence.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Discipline (ta'dīb) is the cultivation of the soul through praiseworthy traits and the restraint from blameworthy ones.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "أدبته تأديبا" — I disciplined him. Metaphorical: "أدبه الله" — God disciplined him, i.e., refined his character through divine instruction.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — "إنما أدبه القرآن" restricts the means of the Prophet's discipline exclusively to the Qur'an, affirming that the Qur'an alone was the sufficient and complete instrument of his moral formation.
31:17.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications, prayers, and their spiritual power, from 'Etiquette of Living and Prophetic Character'

31:17.arabic: فقال حاكيا عن لقمان يا بني أقم الصلاة وأمر بالمعروف وانه عن المنكر واصبر على ما أصابك ومن الآداب تقليل العلائق حتى لا يكثر خوفه وقطع الطمع عن الخلائق حتى تزول عنه المداهنة فقد روي عن بعض المشايخ أنه كان له سنور وكان يأخذ من قصاب في جواره كل يوم شيئا من الغدد لسنوره فرأى على القصاب منكرا فدخل الدار أولا وأخرج السنور ثم جاء واحتسب على القصاب فقال له القصاب لا أعطينك بعد هذا شيئا لسنورك فقال ما احتسبت عليك إلا بعد إخراج السنور وقطع الطمع منك وهو كما قال فمن لم يقطع الطمع من الخلق لم يقدر على الحسبة ومن طمع في أن
31:17.english: We do not mean by this that commanding right becomes prohibited by reason of one's sinfulness — rather, its effect upon hearts falls away by the manifestation of his sinfulness to the people. For it has been related from Anas, may God be pleased with him, who said: "We said, 'O Messenger of God, shall we not command right until we have acted upon it entirely, and shall we not forbid wrong until we have shunned it entirely?' He said, may God's peace and blessings be upon him: 'Rather, command right even if you do not act upon it entirely, and forbid wrong even if you do not shun it entirely.'"
31:17.section_title_en: On Gentleness in Commanding Right and Forbidding Wrong — The Etiquette of the Muḥtasib
31:17.anchors:
- Root: عيب (ʿayb)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root meaning — defect, blemish, reproach; to find fault with something.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance — the reproach of intellect (ʿaql) is the severest form of deficiency, for it touches the very faculty by which one is distinguished from beasts.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal vs Metaphorical — here used metaphorically: the reproach falls upon his intellect, i.e., the deficiency of his discernment becomes manifest.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Restriction (Bāb al-Ḥaṣr) — "فإنما يزرى على عقله" restricts the object of reproach to the intellect alone, excluding the person's faith or status.
31:17.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Condemnation of Anger and Hatred'

31:18.arabic: ومنها أن يتواضع لكل مسلم ولا يتكبر عليه فإن الله لا يحب كل مختال فخور قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إن الله تعالى أوحى إلي أن تواضعوا حتى لا يفخر أحد على أحد (6) ثم إن تفاخر عليه غيره فليحتمل قال الله تعالى لنبيه صلى الله عليه وسلم {خذ العفو وأمر بالعرف وأعرض عن الجاهلين} وعن ابن أبي أوفى كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يتواضع لكل مسلم ولا يأنف ولا يتكبر أن يمشي مع الأرملة والمسكين فيقضي حاجته (7) ومنها أن لا يسمع بلاغات الناس بعضهم على بعض ولا يبلغ بعضهم ما يسمع من بعض قال صلى الله عليه وسلم لا يدخل الجنة
31:18.english: **First**: That you greet him with peace (*salām*) when you meet him, and respond to his invitation when he invites you, and say "may Allah have mercy on you" (*tashmīt*) when he sneezes, and visit him when he is ill, and attend his funeral procession when he dies, and fulfill his oath when he swears by you, and give him sincere counsel when he seeks your advice, and protect him in his absence when he is away from you, and love for him what you love for yourself, and dislike for him what you dislike for yourself. (1)
31:18.section_title_en: The Rights of Brotherhood — Section 433: The Duties of a Muslim Toward His Fellow Muslims
31:18.anchors:
- Root: سلم (s-l-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of safety, security, freedom from harm; the root from which *islām* (submission/surrender) and *salām* (peace) derive
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): *Salām* as the theological state of being secure from harm — both giving and receiving safety; *islām* as the total surrender of the heart to Allah
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (*ḥaqīqah*): physical safety from tongue and hand; Metaphorical (*majāz*): the comprehensive spiritual safety that defines true Muslim brotherhood
- Root: عون (ʿ-w-n)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Assistance, aid, helping another in need
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Mutual assistance as a divine ordinance among believers
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical aid; Metaphorical: intercession (*shafāʿah*) and advocacy on behalf of others
- Root: ستر (s-t-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Covering, concealing, veiling; protection from exposure
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): *Sitr* as the divine attribute of concealment — Allah's covering of sins in this world and the next
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: covering a physical defect; Metaphorical: concealing another's faults and sins — a cardinal virtue of brotherhood
- Root: عذر (ʿ-dh-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Excuse, pardon, acceptance of apology
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): *ʿAfw* (pardon) as the higher station of forgiveness that elevates the forgiver
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: releasing from obligation; Metaphorical: the noble trait of overlooking others' offenses
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد (Restriction & Focused Predication) — The repeated use of restrictive constructions (e.g., "المسلم من سلم المسلمون") establishes definitional boundaries through predicate restriction, indicating that the *ḥaqīqah* of faith is manifested through specific observable actions.

  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The guest is "one who inclines to you, alighting with you"; hospitality (al-ḍiyāfah) became customary in the sense of receiving such a one. The word is originally a verbal noun, hence one and many are equal in most usage.

33:36.arabic: بالمشيئة يدل على الانقسام وقوله تعالى {ومن يعص الله ورسوله فإن له نار جهنم خالدين فيها} وتخصيصه بالكفر تحكم وقوله تعالى {ألا إن الظالمين في عذاب مقيم} وقال تعالى {ومن جاء بالسيئة فكبت وجوههم في النار} فهذه العمومات في معارضة عموماتهم ولا بد من تسليط التخصص والتأويل على الجانبين لأن الأخبار مصرحة بأن العصاة يعذبون (1) بل قوله تعالى وإن منكم إلا واردها كالصريح في أن ذلك لا بد منه للكل إذ لا يخلو مؤمن عن ذنب يرتكبه وقوله تعالى لا يصلاها إلا الأشقى الذي كذب وتولى أراد به من جماعة مخصوصين أو أراد بالأشقى شخصا
33:36.english: He was asked, "Which deed is most excellent?" The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Islam." It was then asked, "Which aspect of Islam is most excellent?" He (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Faith (Īmān)." This is evidence for both the distinction (ikhtilāf) between the two terms and their overlap (tadākhul). This usage is the most consistent with the conventions of the language, because faith is a deed among deeds, and it is the most excellent of them. Islam is submission (taslīm), whether by the heart, by the tongue, or by the limbs. The most excellent of these is that which is by the heart, which is the assent (taṣdīq) that is called faith. Using the two terms in a way that indicates distinction, overlap, or even complete synonymy (tarāduf) is all within the bounds of metaphorical usage (tajawwuz) in the language.
33:36.section_title_en: The Book of the Revival of the Religious Sciences — Section 99: On the Distinction, Overlap, and Synonymy of Faith (Īmān) and Submission (Islām), and Their Worldly and Otherworldly Judgments
33:36.anchors:
- Root: ايم (A-Y-M)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of remaining unmarried, or a state of being without a spouse; extended metaphorically to describe one who is solitary or without support.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الأيامى: جمع أيم، وهي المرأة التي لا بعل لها... والحرب مأيمة، أي: يفرق بين الزوج والزوجة." The root carries the sense of separation or a state of lacking union, which informs the theological discussion of what constitutes the essential bond of faith.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah) usage denotes the state of being unmarried; metaphorical (Majaz) usage extends to anything that separates or leaves one bereft. This distinction between literal and metaphorical application is central to the chapter's method.
- Root: قلب (Q-L-B)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To turn, overturn, or transform a thing from one state to another.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "قلب الشيء: تصريفه وصرفه عن وجه إلى وجه... والانقلاب: الانصراف." The heart (qalb) is so named for its constant fluctuation and turning. In theological terms, it is the seat of taṣdīq (assent), the immaterial faculty of cognition and conviction.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah) usage is physical turning; metaphorical (Majaz) usage is "قلب الأمور" — to deliberate, scrutinize, and manage affairs. This supports the distinction between the heart's internal act of assent and the external acts of the limbs.
- Root: عمل (ʿ-A-M-L)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Any deed or action performed with purpose and intent.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "العمل: كل فعل يكون من الحيوان بقصد، فهو أخص من الفعل." Work is more specific than mere action, as it implies deliberate, intentional agency. It is used for both righteous and sinful deeds, and is the external manifestation of internal conviction.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah) usage refers to physical labor or deeds. The chapter explores whether "work" is an integral part of the reality of faith or a separate, consequent requirement.
- Root: صدق (S-D-Q)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To be truthful, to speak the truth, to verify.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الصدق والكذب أصلهما في القول... ولا يكونان بالقصد الأول إلا في القول." Truth and falsehood are primarily properties of speech and reports. Taṣdīq (assent) is the heart's affirmation of the truth of a report, which is the core reality of Īmān.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah) usage is truthful speech; metaphorical (Majaz) usage is "صادق الحملة" — one who is true and firm in battle or resolve. This shows that taṣdīq is not merely verbal but a firm, internal resolution.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication). This rule governs how restriction (ḥaṣr) is achieved in Arabic, often through particles like "innamā" or through contextual specification (takhṣīṣ). The chapter's core argument hinges on how terms like Īmān and Islām are semantically restricted, expanded, or made synonymous through contextual usage (majāz), requiring precise parsing of the predicate and its scope.
33:36.topic: Al-Ghazali on the journey of the soul, death, and the Hereafter, from 'Condemnation of Anger and Hatred'

40:1.arabic: قال إذا أردت الخروج فآذني فكتب عند خروجه إليه بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم {حم تنزيل الكتاب من الله العزيز العليم غافر الذنب وقابل التوب شديد العقاب} الآية ثم عاتبه تحت ذلك وعذله فلما قرأ الكتاب بكى وقال صدق الله ونصح لي عمر فتاب ورجع وحكي أن أخوين ابتلى أحدهما بهوى فأظهر عليه أخاه وقال إني قد اعتللت فإن شئت أن لا تعقد على صحبتي لله فافعل فقال ما كنت لأحل عقد أخوتك لأجل خطيئتك أبدا ثم عقد أخوه بينه وبين الله بأن لا يأكل ولا يشرب حتى يعافى الله أخاه من هواه فطوى أربعين يوما في كلها يسأله عن هواه فكان يقول القلب مقيم على حاله وما زال هو ينحل من الغم والجوع حتى زال الهوى عن قلب أخيه بعد الأربعين
40:1.english: Abu Dharr (may Allah be pleased with him) held the view of severance, saying: "When your brother turns away from what he once was, then hate him from the very perspective from which you loved him." He considered this to be a requirement of loving for Allah's sake and hating for Allah's sake.
40:1.section_title_en: On the Error of a Friend: Between Severance and Gentleness in Brotherhood
40:1.anchors:
- Root: لطف (luṭf)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Gentleness, subtlety, refinement; the opposite of harshness and coarseness.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The subtle divine reality (laṭīfah) that perceives the finest nuances of affairs; also gentleness (rifq) in dealing.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: that which is not coarse. Metaphorical: "I was gentle with him" (laṭaftu bihi) — showing affection and gentleness in dealing, and "he is gentle with this matter" — skillful in managing it.
- Root: دين (dīn)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Religion, creed, judgment, recompense; the comprehensive term for one's obligatory practices and beliefs.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The root denotes indebtedness and obedience; the religion (dīn) is that by which one is bound to the Divine command.
- Root: عقد (ʿaqd)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To tie, bind, contract; the knot of brotherhood (ʿaqd al-ukhuwwah) as a binding covenant.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): A firm resolution or covenant that obligates its fulfillment.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — Used to distinguish the precise scope of a ruling, e.g., "I only hate his deed" (innamā ubghiḍu ʿamalahu), restricting hatred to the act, not the person.
40:1.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Condemnation of Anger and Hatred'

42:42.arabic: يسعون في قطع ما أمر الله به أن يوصل ويفسدون في الأرض وقال تعالى {إنما السبيل على الذين يظلمون الناس ويبغون في الأرض بغير الحق} والنمام منهم وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم إن من شرار الناس
42:42.english: And whoever is the recipient of tale-bearing — it being said to him: "So-and-so said such-and-such about you," or "He did such-and-such against you," or "He is scheming to corrupt your affair," or "He is conspiring with your enemy," or "He is disparaging your condition," or whatever runs in that course — then six matters are incumbent upon him:
42:42.section_title_en: Section 692 — On the Duties of the One to Whom Tale-Bearing (Namīmah) Is Conveyed
42:42.anchors:
- Root: ن-م-م (N-M-M)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning — to stir up, incite, or carry tales; the one who transmits speech to cause discord.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance — namīmah is a species of corrupt speech that severs what God has commanded to be joined; it is aligned with fāsiq (transgressor) status, rendering the bearer's testimony rejected.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal vs Metaphorical — literally, the act of carrying and dropping seeds (naml) to cause sprouting; metaphorically, the dropping of speech into hearts to sow enmity.
- Root: غ-ي-ب (Gh-Y-B)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning — that which is concealed from the senses.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance — ghaybah (backbiting) is the mention of a person in his absence with what he dislikes; it is a violation of the unseen honor of the brother.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal vs Metaphorical — literal absence from sight; metaphorical — the absence of the subject from the gathering while his reputation is being torn.
- Root: ف-س-ق (F-S-Q)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning — to depart, to deviate from the straight path.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance — fisq is the breaking of the command of God; the fāsiq's report is not to be trusted without verification, per {إِن جَاءَكُمْ فَاسِقٌ بِنَبَإٍ فَتَبَيَّنُوا}.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal vs Metaphorical — literal: the date that peels from its husk; metaphorical: the soul that peels from obedience.
- Sibawayh Rule: Bāb al-Ḥaṣr wa al-Taqyīd bi-innamā (Restriction & Focused Predication) — The verse {إِنَّمَا السَّبِيلُ عَلَى الَّذِينَ يَظْلِمُونَ النَّاسَ} restricts the path of blame exclusively to the oppressors, thereby excluding the tale-bearer's victim from any culpability and affirming the tale-bearer's full liability.
42:42.topic: Classical commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya Ulum al-Din, from 'Condemnation of Anger and Hatred'

45:19.arabic: فاخفض صوتك وإن كنت تريد الناس فإنهم لن يغنوا عنك من الله شيئا فسكت عمر بن عبد العزيز وخفف ركعته فلما سلم أخذ نعليه وانصرف وهو يومئذ أمير المدينة ويدل على استحباب الجهر ما روي أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم سمع جماعة من أصحابه يجهرون في صلاة الليل فصوب ذلك (7) وقد قال صلى الله عليه وسلم
45:19.english: If he recites without ritual purity, reclining upon his bed, he also has merit, but it is below that [of the one who is pure and seated properly]. Allah Most High said: {الَّذِينَ يَذْكُرُونَ اللَّهَ قِيَامًا وَقُعُودًا وَعَلَىٰ جُنُوبِهِمْ وَيَتَفَكَّرُونَ فِي خَلْقِ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ} ("Those who remember Allah standing, sitting, and upon their sides, and reflect upon the creation of the heavens and the earth") — and He praised all of them, but He mentioned standing first, then sitting, then remembrance while reclining.
45:19.section_title_en: The Book of the Etiquette of Qur'an Recitation — Section 223: On the Manners of the Reciter, the Measure of Recitation, Division into Portions, Orthography, Tartīl, Weeping, Rights of the Verses, Invocations, and Vocalization
45:19.anchors:
- Root: قرا (Q-R-A)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To read, recite, gather together; the core act of assembling letters into articulated speech.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Recitation (tilāwah) is the following of the Qur'an in obedience and belief; qirā'ah is the articulation of the letters. The term carries both the physical act of vocalization and the spiritual act of devotion.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (haqīqah): to read from a written text or from memory. Metaphorical (majāz): "qara'a al-rajul" — to become religious, devoted, as the reciter is characterized by the state of worship.
- Root: سجد (S-J-D)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To bow, prostrate, lower oneself; the physical posture of placing the forehead on the ground.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Prostration is of two kinds: voluntary (ikhtiyārī) — exclusive to humans, by which reward is deserved; and subjugated (taskhīrī) — universal to all creation, as in {وَلِلَّهِ يَسْجُدُ مَنْ فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ}.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the physical act of prostration. Metaphorical: "shajarah sājidah" — a tree bending over; "ʿayn sājidah" — a languid, drooping eye. The prostration of recitation is the literal act performed in obedience to the command of the verse.
- Root: تلو (T-L-W)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To follow, to recite; the reciter "follows" the letters in sequence and "follows" the commands contained therein.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Tilāwah is following the Qur'an in deed as well as in word; the true reciter is he whose recitation is a following of the divine command.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد (Restriction & Focused Predication) — The conditional and restrictive structures in the prophetic sayings (e.g., "من قرأ القرآن في أقل من ثلاث لم يفقهه") establish a causal link between the act and its consequence, requiring precise parsing of the conditional clause to extract the legal ruling.
45:19.topic: Al-Ghazali on constant remembrance of God and contemplative invocations, from 'Condemnation of Anger and Hatred'

48:17.arabic: وخطب رجل عند رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال من يطع الله ورسوله فقد رشد ومن يعصهما فقد غوى فقال قل ومن يعص الله ورسوله فقد غوى (2) فكره رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قوله ومن يعصهما لأنه تسوية وجمع وكان إبراهيم يكره أن يقول الرجل أعوذ بالله وبك ويجوز أن يقول أعوذ بالله ثم بك وأن يقول لولا الله ثم فلان ولا يقول لولا الله وفلان وكره بعضهم أن يقال اللهم أعتقنا من النار وكان يقول العتق يكون بعد الورود وكانوا يستجيرون من النار ويتعوذون من النار وقال رجل اللهم اجعلني ممن تصيبه شفاعة محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم فق
48:17.english: An example of this is what Ḥudhayfah reported: The Prophet, peace be upon him, said: "Let none of you say: 'What Allah willed and you willed' — but rather let him say: 'What Allah willed, then you willed.'" (5) This is because in the absolute conjunction [with "and"] there is an association and an equalization, which is contrary to [the due measure of] reverence. And Ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: A man came to the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, speaking to him concerning some matter, and he said: "What Allah willed and you willed." The Prophet, peace be upon him, said: "Have you made me an equal to Allah? Rather, [say]: 'What Allah willed alone.'" (1)
48:17.section_title_en: The Revival of the Religious Sciences — Section 698: The Nineteenth Affliction — Heedlessness Regarding Subtle Errors in the Import of Speech
48:17.anchors:
- Root: غفل (ghafla)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of heedlessness, neglect, and inattention; the absence of vigilance over a matter.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Heedlessness (al-ghafla) is the soul's failure to attend to what it is obligated to know or consider; it is the opposite of mindfulness (al-tayaqquẓ) and remembrance (al-dhikr).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) usage denotes the absence of guarding; metaphorical (majāz) usage extends to the tongue's straying from precise expression in sacred matters.
- Root: عطف (ʿaṭf)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Inclination, turning, or joining one thing to another; grammatically, the conjunction that links two items in a shared ruling.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Joining (al-ʿaṭf) implies equal treatment of the conjoined items; in theological speech, absolute conjunction (al-ʿaṭf al-muṭlaq) with Allah entails an inadmissible association.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the bending of a staff or the inclining of a branch; metaphorical: the grammatical coupling that levels two referents under one predicate.
- Root: شرك (shirk)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Sharing, partnership, or association; the root of polytheism (al-shirk) as the ascription of a partner to Allah.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Association (al-shirk) is the equalization of two things in a shared ruling; in theology, it is the gravest form when applied to the Divine, whether in belief or in the mere wording of speech.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: co-participation in ownership; metaphorical: any verbal or creedal equalization of the creature with the Creator.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Conjunction (al-ʿaṭf) and Restriction (al-ḥaṣr) — The particle "thumma" (then) indicates sequential ordering and distinction of rank, whereas "wa" (and) denotes absolute conjunction and mutual equivalence; thus the Prophet's command to replace "wa" with "thumma" in "what Allah willed and you willed" is a syntactic correction to abolish the implication of equal partnership.
48:17.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications, prayers, and their spiritual power, from 'Condemnation of Anger and Hatred'

49:6.arabic: وقد قال الله تعالى يا أيها الذين آمنوا إن جاءكم فاسق بنبأ فتبينوا أن تصيبوا قوما بجهالة فلا يجوز تصديق إبليس وإن كان ثم مخيلة تدل على فساد واحتمل خلافه لم يجز أن تصدق به لأن الفاسق يتصور أن بصدق في خيره ولكن لا يجوز لك أن تصدق به حتى إن من استنكه فوجد منه رائحة الخمر لا يجوز أن يحد إذ يقال يمكن أن يكون قد تمضمض بالخمر ومجها وما شربها أو حمل عليه قهرا فكل ذلك لا محالة دلالة محتملة فلا يجوز تصديقها بالقلب
49:6.english: For God Most High has said: {«يا أيها الذين آمنوا اجتنبوا كثيرا من الظن إن بعض الظن إثم»} — "O you who believe, avoid much suspicion; indeed, some suspicion is sin." The reason for its prohibition is that the secrets of hearts are known only to the Knower of the Unseen (ʿAllām al-Ghuyūb). You have no right to believe evil of another unless it is disclosed to you with certain sight (ʿiyān) that admits no interpretation. At that point you cannot but believe what you have known and witnessed. But what you have not witnessed with your eye nor heard with your ear, and then falls into your heart — it is Satan who casts it to you, and you ought to deny him, for he is the most wicked of the wicked. God Most High has said: {«يا أيها الذين آمنوا إن جاءكم فاسق بنبأ فتبينوا أن تصيبوا قوما بجهالة»} — "O you who believe, if a wicked one brings you news, then verify, lest you harm a people in ignorance." It is not permissible to believe Satan, even if there is some indication suggesting corruption. As long as the opposite remains possible, it is not permissible to believe it. Thus, even if one detects upon another the odor of wine, it is not permissible to impose the prescribed punishment (ḥadd) upon him — for it is said: perhaps he rinsed his mouth with wine and spat it out without drinking it, or he was compelled to carry it under duress. All of this is, inevitably, a possible indication, and it is not permissible to believe it in the heart.
49:6.section_title_en: The Cure That Restrains the Tongue from Backbiting, and the Prohibition of Backbiting in the Heart
49:6.anchors:
- Root: غيب (ghayb)
  * Lisan / Ayn: That which is hidden from the eye; absence from sensory perception.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-ghaybah (backbiting) is rooted in speaking of one who is absent (ghāʾib) — the unseen referent is absent from the listener's sight, yet present in the speaker's malice.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "speaking from behind the veil of absence" (takallama bihi ʿan ẓahri al-ghayb). Metaphorical: the tongue's slander reaches the absent one as if traversing a hidden realm.
- Root: نفس (nafs)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The self; the vital spirit; that which breathes and desires.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The nafs is the locus of blameworthy traits (hawā) and the battlefield between angelic and satanic promptings; its thoughts (khaṭarāt) are distinct from settled convictions (ʿaqd al-qalb).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "self-speaking" (ḥadīth al-nafs) as internal discourse. Metaphorical: the nafs "inclines" (tamīlu) toward suspicion — a leaning of the heart, not a mere passing thought.
- Root: قلب (qalb)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The heart; the organ of understanding and intention.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Taqlīb — the heart's constant turning between states; its "settling" (ʿaqd) upon a judgment constitutes belief (iʿtiqād), which is the object of divine prohibition in suspicion.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: turning a thing over. Metaphorical: the heart "turns over" a matter until it rests upon a conviction — this resting (sukūn) is what renders suspicion sinful, unlike the fleeting whisper.
- Sibawayh Rule: Restriction and specification (bāb al-ḥaṣr wa al-taqyīd bi-innamā) — the phrase "ولست أعني به إلا عقد القلب" restricts the referent of "suspicion" exclusively to the heart's settled judgment, excluding passing thoughts (khaṭarāt) and doubt (shakk), which are pardoned.
49:6.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Condemnation of Anger and Hatred'

49:6.arabic: وقد قال الله تعالى يا أيها الذين آمنوا أنفقوا من طيبات ما كسبتم ومما أخرجنا لكم من الأرض ولا تيمموا الخبيث منه تنفقون ولستم بآخذيه إلا أن تغمضوا فيه أي لا تأخذوه إلا مع كراهية وحياء وهو معنى الإغماض فلا تؤثروا به ربكم وفي الخبر سبق درهم مائة ألف درهم (3) وذلك بأن يخرجه الإنسان وهو من أحل ماله وأجوده فيصدر ذلك عن الرضا والفرح بالبذل وقد يخرج مائة ألف درهم مما يكره من ماله فيدل ذلك على أنه ليس يؤثر الله عز وجل بشيء مما يحبه وبذلك ذم الله تعالى قوما جعلوا لله ما يكرهون فقال تعال
49:6.english: The heart is not treated save with the compound electuary (maʿjūn) of knowledge and works. And this condition among the conditions of almsgiving runs in the same course as humility (al-khushūʿ) runs in the prayer. This is established by his saying — may Allah bless him and grant him peace: "A man has nothing of his prayer save that of which he was conscious." And this is like his saying — may Allah bless him and grant him peace: "Allah does not accept the charity of the one who bestows it with reproach (al-mannān)." And like His saying — Exalted is He: {«لا تبطلوا صدقاتكم بالمن والأذى»} ("Do not nullify your charities by reproach and injury"). As for the legal opinion (fatwā) of the jurist that the alms fall in their proper place and that one's liability is discharged without this condition — that is another discussion, and we have already pointed to its meaning in the Book of Prayer.
49:6.section_title_en: The Inner Conditions of Charity — Section 175 (From The Revival of the Religious Sciences, Book of the Mysteries of Almsgiving)
49:6.anchors:
- Root: قلب (q-l-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "To turn, overturn, transform a thing from one state to another; to rotate, to flip"
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "قلب الشيء: تصريفه وصرفه عن وجه إلى وجه" — the heart is so named because of its constant turning and transformation between states
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "قلب الشيء قلبا: حوله عن وجهه" (to turn a thing from its face). Metaphorical: "رجل قلب حول: يقلب الأمور ويحتال" — one who turns matters over and manages them; "قلبوا لك الأمور" (they turned matters against you)
- Root: وجل (w-j-l)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "Fear, dread, apprehension that strikes the heart"
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الوجل: استشعار الخوف" — the sensing of fear; cited in {«إنما المؤمنون الذين إذا ذكر الله وجلت قلوبهم»}
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "رجل وجل، وقوم وجال" — a fearful man, a fearful people; "وفي قلبه وجل" — in his heart is dread
- Root: عجب (ʿ-j-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "Wonder, amazement; self-admiration, vanity"
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Self-admiration (al-ʿujb) is a destructive spiritual ailment that nullifies deeds
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: wonder at something extraordinary. Metaphorical: self-conceit regarding one's own acts of obedience
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد (Restriction & Focused Predication) — governing the precise limitation of general categories (al-ṣifāt al-khāṣṣah within al-aṣnāf al-thamāniyyah) and the conditional structure of acceptance

##
49:6.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Duties of Brotherhood'

49:11.arabic: إلا الحياة الدنيا وفي قوله تعالى ومن لم يتب فأولئك هم الظالمون إلى غير ذلك من الآيات وكان داخلا في معنى قوله عز وجل ومنهم أميون لا يعلمون الكتاب إلا أماني يعني التلاوة المجردة وقوله عز وجل وكأين من آية في السموات والأرض يمرون عليها وهم عنها معرضون لأن القرآن هو المبين لتلك الآيات في السموات والأرض ومهما تجاوزها ولم يتأثر بها كان معرضا عنها ولذلك قيل إن من لم يكن متصفا بأخلاق القرآن فإذا قرأ القرآن ناداه الله تعالى مالك ولكلامي وأنت معرض عني دع عنك كلامي إن لم تتب إلي ومثال العاصي إذا قرأ القرآن وكرره مثال
49:11.english: And at the mention of God, His attributes, and His names, he bows low in humility before His majesty and in apprehension of His greatness. And at the mention of the disbelievers' sayings — those things impossible for God, Mighty and Majestic, such as their attributing to Him a son or a consort — he lowers his voice and inwardly recoils in shame at the ugliness of their speech. And at the description of Paradise, his innermost being surges forth with longing for it. And at the description of the Fire, his limbs tremble in fear of it. For when the Messenger of God, peace be upon him, said to Ibn Mas'ud, "Recite to me," he said: "I began reciting Surah al-Nisa'. When I reached {فكيف إذا جئنا من كل أمة بشهيد وجئنا بك على هؤلاء شهيدا} [How then shall it be when We bring from every nation a witness, and We bring you as a witness against these?] (4:41), I saw his two eyes overflowing with tears. He then said to me: 'That is enough for you now.'" And this was because the witnessing of that very state had wholly overwhelmed his heart.
49:11.section_title_en: The States of the Heart During Qur'anic Recitation — The Condition of the True Recieter
49:11.anchors:
- Root: وجل (w-j-l)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root meaning of trembling fear, trepidation of the heart
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الوجل: استشعار الخوف" — the inward apprehension of fear; cited in {إنما المؤمنون الذين إذا ذكر الله وجلت قلوبهم}
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): "رجل وجل، وقوم وجال" — a man fearful, a people fearful; the state of the heart's trembling before divine majesty
- Root: وصف (w-ṣ-f)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Describing a thing by its attributes and qualities
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الوصف: ذكر الشيء بحليته ونعته" — description is the mention of a thing by its adornment and attribute; may be true or false
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal vs Metaphorical: "وجهها يصف الحسن" — metaphorical usage where the face itself "describes" beauty; likewise, the tongue may "describe" falsehood, as in {ولا تقولوا لما تصف ألسنتكم الكذب}
- Root: وفي (w-f-y)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Completeness, fulfillment, reaching full measure
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الوافي: الذي بلغ التمام" — that which attains completion; "أوفى: إذا تمم العهد ولم ينقض حفظه" — fulfilled the covenant without breach
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "درهم واف" — a full-weight dirham; Metaphorical: "أوفى على المائة إذا زاد عليها" — surpassed the hundred
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The separation between the governing preposition and its object by intervening clauses, as in "فلما بلغت {فكيف إذا جئنا...}" where the temporal clause governs the narrative sequence
49:11.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Etiquette of Quran Recitation'

49:11.arabic: وقد قال الله تعالى يا أيها الذين آمنوا أنفقوا من طيبات ما كسبتم ومما أخرجنا لكم من الأرض ولا تيمموا الخبيث منه تنفقون ولستم بآخذيه إلا أن تغمضوا فيه أي لا تأخذوه إلا مع كراهية وحياء وهو معنى الإغماض فلا تؤثروا به ربكم وفي الخبر سبق درهم مائة ألف درهم (3) وذلك بأن يخرجه الإنسان وهو من أحل ماله وأجوده فيصدر ذلك عن الرضا والفرح بالبذل وقد يخرج مائة ألف درهم مما يكره من ماله فيدل ذلك على أنه ليس يؤثر الله عز وجل بشيء مما يحبه وبذلك ذم الله تعالى قوما جعلوا لله ما يكرهون فقال تعال
49:11.english: The heart is not treated save with the compound electuary (maʿjūn) of knowledge and works. And this condition among the conditions of almsgiving runs in the same course as humility (al-khushūʿ) runs in the prayer. This is established by his saying — may Allah bless him and grant him peace: "A man has nothing of his prayer save that of which he was conscious." And this is like his saying — may Allah bless him and grant him peace: "Allah does not accept the charity of the one who bestows it with reproach (al-mannān)." And like His saying — Exalted is He: {«لا تبطلوا صدقاتكم بالمن والأذى»} ("Do not nullify your charities by reproach and injury"). As for the legal opinion (fatwā) of the jurist that the alms fall in their proper place and that one's liability is discharged without this condition — that is another discussion, and we have already pointed to its meaning in the Book of Prayer.
49:11.section_title_en: The Inner Conditions of Charity — Section 175 (From The Revival of the Religious Sciences, Book of the Mysteries of Almsgiving)
49:11.anchors:
- Root: قلب (q-l-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "To turn, overturn, transform a thing from one state to another; to rotate, to flip"
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "قلب الشيء: تصريفه وصرفه عن وجه إلى وجه" — the heart is so named because of its constant turning and transformation between states
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "قلب الشيء قلبا: حوله عن وجهه" (to turn a thing from its face). Metaphorical: "رجل قلب حول: يقلب الأمور ويحتال" — one who turns matters over and manages them; "قلبوا لك الأمور" (they turned matters against you)
- Root: وجل (w-j-l)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "Fear, dread, apprehension that strikes the heart"
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الوجل: استشعار الخوف" — the sensing of fear; cited in {«إنما المؤمنون الذين إذا ذكر الله وجلت قلوبهم»}
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "رجل وجل، وقوم وجال" — a fearful man, a fearful people; "وفي قلبه وجل" — in his heart is dread
- Root: عجب (ʿ-j-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "Wonder, amazement; self-admiration, vanity"
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Self-admiration (al-ʿujb) is a destructive spiritual ailment that nullifies deeds
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: wonder at something extraordinary. Metaphorical: self-conceit regarding one's own acts of obedience
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد (Restriction & Focused Predication) — governing the precise limitation of general categories (al-ṣifāt al-khāṣṣah within al-aṣnāf al-thamāniyyah) and the conditional structure of acceptance

49:11.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Duties of Brotherhood'

49:11.arabic: وهذا محرم مهما كان مؤذيا كما قال تعالى يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا يسخر قوم من قوم عسى أن يكونوا خيرا منهم ولا نساء من نساء عسى أن يكن خيرا منهن ومعنى السخرية الاستهانة والتحقير والتنبيه على العيوب والنقائص على وجه يضحك منه وقد يكون ذلك بالمحاكاة في الفعل والقول وقد يكون بالإشارة والإيماء وإذا كان بحضرة المستهزأ به لم يسم ذلك غيبة وفيه معنى الغيبة قالت عائشة رضي الله عنها حاكيت إنسانا فقال لي النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم والله ما أحب أني حاكيت إنسانا ولي كذا وكذا (2) وقال ابن عباس في قوله تعالى يا ويلتنا ما لهذا الكتاب لا يغادر صغيرة ولا كبيرة إلا أحصاها إن الصغيرة التبسم بالاستهزاء بالمؤمن
49:11.english: This is forbidden whenever it is harmful, just as God—Exalted is He—has said: {«يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا يسخر قوم من قوم عسى أن يكونوا خيرا منهم ولا نساء من نساء عسى أن يكن خيرا منهن»} ["O you who believe, let not a people deride a people; perhaps they may be better than them. Nor let women deride women; perhaps they may be better than them"] (Q. 49:11). The meaning of mockery (al-sukhriyyah) is contempt, belittlement, and drawing attention to faults and defects in a manner that causes laughter at the person. This may occur through imitation in action and speech, and it may occur through gesture and indication. And if it occurs in the presence of the one being mocked, it is not called backbiting (ghībah), yet it contains the meaning of backbiting.
49:11.section_title_en: The Revival of the Religious Sciences — Section 673: The Eleventh Affliction: Mockery and Derision
49:11.anchors:
- Root: سخر (s-kh-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of subjugation and forced employment; also derision and making a mockery of someone.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "التسخير: سياقة إلى الغرض المختص قهرا" — driving toward a specific purpose by compulsion. The theological nuance here shifts to the passive form (سُخِرَ) and the verbal noun (سخرية) denoting the act of holding another in contempt and compelling them into a position of ridicule.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Haqiqah (Literal): "فلان سخرة سخرة: يضحك منه الناس" — one whom people laugh at. Majaz (Metaphorical): The root's use for subjugated service (as in "سخر الله لك") is distinct from this interpersonal derision, which is the literal sense intended here.
- Root: ضحك (ḍ-ḥ-k)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Physical laughter with the baring of teeth; the molars are called الضواحك.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الضحك: انبساط الوجه وتكشر الأسنان من سرور النفس" — expansion of the face and baring of teeth from delight of the soul. He explicitly notes: "واستعير الضحك للسخرية" — laughter is metaphorically extended to mockery, as in "ضحكت منه" (I laughed at him). This metaphorical extension is precisely the mechanism of the sin discussed here.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Haqiqah: "افتر عن ضاحكته" — smiling broadly. Majaz: "ضحكت الأرض عن النبات" — the earth "laughs" forth vegetation. The distinction is critical: the physical act of laughing (haqiqah) becomes blameworthy mockery (majaz) when directed at another's defects.
- Root: هلم (h-l-m)
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "هلم دعاء إلى الشيء" — a call toward something. Derived from "ها لم" (come, repair to) or "هل أم" (is there intent?). It is an imperative summons.
  * Lisan al-Arab: "لأَن الهاء زائدة، وأَصله هالُمّ" — the ha is augmentative; the root is l-m-m (to repair, to mend).
- Root: وقد (w-q-d)
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "وقدت النار تقد وقودا ووقدا" — the fire blazed. The verbal noun وقود refers both to fuel and to the resulting flame.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Haqiqah: "وقدت النار وقودا ووقدا، واتقدت وتوقدت" — the fire ignited and blazed. Majaz: "قلب وقاد" — a blazing heart (for intelligence). The imagery of a door opening to the scorner, who approaches "بكربه وغمه" (with his distress and grief), evokes this root's sense of burning anguish.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — The prohibition is restricted by the conditional clause "مهما كان مؤذيا" (whenever it is harmful), and the focus is sharpened by the Quranic address "يا أيها الذين آمنوا" which restricts the address to believers, making the prohibition binding upon them specifically.
49:11.topic: Al-Ghazali on purifying the character, moral diseases, and spiritual remedies, from 'Condemnation of Anger and Hatred'
