##
49:12.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Duties of Brotherhood'

49:12.arabic: ومن أبوابه سوء الظن بالمسلمين قال الله تعالى {يا أيها الذين آمنوا اجتنبوا كثيرا من الظن إن بعض الظن إثم} فمن يحكم بشر على غيره بالظن بعثه الشيطان على أن يطول فيه اللسان بالغيبة فيهلك أو يقصر في القيام بحقوقه أو يتوانى في إكرامه وينظر إليه بعين الاحتقار ويرى نفسه خيرا منه وكل ذلك من المهلكات ولأجل ذلك منع الشرع من التعرض للتهم فقال صلى الله عليه وسلم اتقوا مواضع التهم (2) حديث صفية بنت حيى أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كان معتكفا فأتيته فتحدثت عنده الحديث وفيه أن الشطيان يجري من ابن آدم مجرى الدم متفق عليه فانظر كيف أشفق صلى الله عليه وسلم على دينهما فحرسهما
49:12.english: Thābit al-Bunānī said: When the Messenger of God — peace be upon him — was sent forth, Iblīs said to his devils: "A new event has occurred — go and see what it is." So they set out until they were exhausted, then came back and said: "We do not know." He said: "I shall bring you the news myself." So he went, then returned and said: "God has sent Muḥammad — peace be upon him." He said: "And he began dispatching his devils to the Companions of the Prophet — peace be upon him — and they would return disappointed, saying: 'We have never accompanied a people like these; we gain nothing from them — for when we reach them, they rise to their prayers, and that erases whatever we achieved.' So Iblīs said to them: 'Be patient with them — perhaps God will open the world to them, and then we shall obtain our need from them.'"
49:12.section_title_en: On the Devil's Entrances: Wealth, Partisanship, and the Corruption of Hearts
49:12.anchors:
- Root: شيط (shayṭ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of burning, scorching, or spoiling by fire; also one who is destroyed or whose blood is shed in vain.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The Shayṭān is that which is far removed from good and rebellious among jinn and men.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: meat that is burnt and spoiled. Metaphorical: one whose blood is shed in vain (shāṭa damuhu), or one who is torn apart and divided like sacrificial meat (asḥāṭū laḥm al-jazūr).
- Root: حدث (ḥadath)
  * Lisan / Ayn: New occurrence, event, or innovation; that which comes into being after not having been.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Ḥudūth is the coming-to-be of a thing after it was not — whether accident or substance. Iḥdāth is bringing it into existence. The Prophet's advent was a "new event" (ḥadath).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: recent, newly occurred. Metaphorical: "Umar was muḥaddath — one whose intuition is true, as if he were informed (yuḥaddath) of hidden matters.
- Root: عصب (ʿaṣab)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To bind, tie firmly; partisanship (taʿaṣṣub) — the binding of oneself to a group or faction.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): ʿAṣabiyyah — zealous partisanship for one's group, whether in truth or falsehood.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: binding a limb with a bandage. Metaphorical: binding oneself to a party or faction in blind allegiance.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Restriction and Specification (al-ḥaṣr wa al-taqyīd) — distinguishing genuine claims from false ones through predicate focus and contrastive emphasis.
49:12.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'Condemnation of Anger and Hatred'

49:12.arabic: شبهه الله تعالى بأكل لحوم الميتة فقال {أيحب أحدكم أن يأكل لحم أخيه ميتا} والملك الذي يمثله في المنام ما تطالعه الروح من اللوح المحفوظ بالأمثلة المحسوسة يمثل الغيبة بأكل لحوم الميتة حتى أن من يرى أنه يأكل لحم ميتة فإنه يغتاب الناس لأن ذلك الملك في تمثيله يراعي المشاركة والمناسبة بين الشيء وبين مثاله في المعنى الذي يجري من المثال مجرى الروح لا في ظاهر الصور فإذن حماية الأخوة بدفع ذم الأعداء وتعنت المتعنتين واجب في عقد الأخوة وقد قال مجاهد لا تذكر أخاك في غيبته إلا كما تحب أن يذكرك في غيبتك فإذن لك فيه معياران أحدهما أن تقدر
49:12.english: The meaning of brotherhood is thus participation (musāhamah) in prosperity and adversity. The Prophet (peace be upon him) said: {«إذا أحب أحدكم أخاه فليخبره»} (When one of you loves his brother, let him inform him). (1) He commanded the informing only because it necessitates an increase of love. For if he knows that you love him, he will love you by nature, inevitably. And when you know that he also loves you, your love increases, inevitably. Thus love continues to increase from both sides and to multiply.
49:12.section_title_en: On the Duties of Brotherhood: Speech, Praise, Defense, and Sincere Counsel (Section 422 of the Revival of the Religious Sciences)
49:12.anchors:
- Root: نصح (naṣaḥa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of sincerity, purity, and the opposite of deceit; also "to sew" (naṣaḥa al-jild), indicating a mending of what is torn.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "النصح: تحري فعل أو قول فيه صلاح صاحبه" — Sincere counsel is the seeking of an act or saying in which lies the well-being of the other. It is the purification of one's intent (ikhlāṣ) toward the brother.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): "نصحته ونصحت له نصحا ونصيحة" — to advise sincerely. Metaphorical (Majaz): "هو ناصح الجيب" (pure of pocket/garment) and "نصح الغيث البلاد" (the rain fulfilled the land), indicating that true counsel is a complete and sincere pouring forth that benefits the recipient.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — Used to distinguish the precise nature of acts (e.g., "إنما أمر بالإخبار" restricts the command's purpose to a specific cause: the increase of love).
49:12.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Condemnation of Anger and Hatred'

49:12.arabic: ولا تجسسوا ولا يغتب بعضكم بعضا وكم زاهد جاهل يوحش القلوب في التفتيش ويتكلم الكلام الخشن المؤذي وإنما يحسن الشيطان ذلك عنده طلبا للشهرة بأكل الحلال ولو كان باعثه محض الدين لكان خوفه على قلب مسلم أن يتأذى أشد من خوفه على بطنه أن يدخله ما لا يدري وهو غير مؤاخذ بما لا يدري إذ لم يكن ثم علامة توجب الاجتناب فليعلم أن طريق الورع الترك دون التجسس وإذا لم يكن بد من الأكل فالورع الأكل وإحسان الظن هذا هو المألوف من الصحابة رضي الله عنهم ومن زاد عليهم في الورع فهو ضال مبتدع وليس بمتبع فلن يبل
49:12.english: They said: "It is scrupulousness (al-waraʿ)." But Ḥassān ibn Abī Sinān said to them: "Nothing is easier for me than scrupulousness — whenever anything stirs unease in my breast, I simply leave it."
49:12.section_title_en: The Ruling on the Unknown Provider — Between Scrupulousness (Waraʿ) and Suspicion
49:12.anchors:
- Root: ورع (w-r-ʿ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of restraint, abstaining, and holding back from what is doubtful or forbidden.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Waraʿ is the virtue of the God-fearing — abstaining not only from the unlawful but from the ambiguous (shubhah), as a safeguard for religion.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal usage denotes physical withdrawal; metaphorical usage denotes moral abstention — the heart's recoil from what is suspect.
- Root: ظن (ẓ-n-n)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Uncertainty, conjecture, or opinion that falls short of certainty.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Ẓann is divided into blameworthy suspicion (sūʾ al-ẓann) against the innocent — which is prohibited — and praiseworthy presumption of good (ḥusn al-ẓann) toward a Muslim, which is obligated by brotherhood in faith.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: to hold an opinion. Metaphorical: the heart's inclination toward one of two possibilities without decisive evidence.
- Root: ريبة (r-y-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Doubt, unease, or suspicion arising from a tangible indicator — not mere whim.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Rayb is the disturbance of certainty by an ambiguous circumstance; it is the legitimate trigger for inquiry, unlike baseless suspicion.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: uncertainty. Metaphorical: the inward disquiet that prompts a man to investigate before acting.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد (Restriction & Focused Predication) — The conditional and exceptive structures here (e.g., "لا يلزمك السؤال" and "إلا عن ريبة") restrict the obligation of inquiry to the presence of a genuine ground for doubt, not to mere possibility.
49:12.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Condemnation of Anger and Hatred'

49:12.arabic: عليه السلام واحدة قال الله تعالى اجتنبوا كثيرا من الظن إن بعض الظن إثم ولا تجسسوا ولا يغتب بعضكم بعضا وكم زاهد جاهل يوحش القلوب في التفتيش ويتكلم الكلام الخشن المؤذي وإنما يحسن الشيطان ذلك عنده طلبا للشهرة بأكل الحلال ولو كان باعثه محض الدين لكان خوفه على قلب مسلم أن يتأذى أشد من خوفه على بطنه أن يدخله ما لا يدري وهو غير مؤاخذ بما لا يدري إذ لم يكن ثم علامة توجب الاجتناب فليعلم أن طريق الورع الترك دون التجسس وإذا لم يكن بد من الأكل فالورع الأكل وإحسان الظن هذا هو المألوف من الصحابة رضي الله عنهم ومن زاد عليهم في الورع فهو
49:12.english: They said: "It is scrupulousness (al-waraʿ)." But Ḥassān ibn Abī Sinān said to them: "Nothing is easier for me than scrupulousness — whenever anything stirs unease in my breast, I simply leave it."
49:12.section_title_en: The Ruling on the Unknown Provider — Between Scrupulousness (Waraʿ) and Suspicion
49:12.anchors:
- Root: ورع (w-r-ʿ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of restraint, abstaining, and holding back from what is doubtful or forbidden.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Waraʿ is the virtue of the God-fearing — abstaining not only from the unlawful but from the ambiguous (shubhah), as a safeguard for religion.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal usage denotes physical withdrawal; metaphorical usage denotes moral abstention — the heart's recoil from what is suspect.
- Root: ظن (ẓ-n-n)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Uncertainty, conjecture, or opinion that falls short of certainty.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Ẓann is divided into blameworthy suspicion (sūʾ al-ẓann) against the innocent — which is prohibited — and praiseworthy presumption of good (ḥusn al-ẓann) toward a Muslim, which is obligated by brotherhood in faith.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: to hold an opinion. Metaphorical: the heart's inclination toward one of two possibilities without decisive evidence.
- Root: ريبة (r-y-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Doubt, unease, or suspicion arising from a tangible indicator — not mere whim.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Rayb is the disturbance of certainty by an ambiguous circumstance; it is the legitimate trigger for inquiry, unlike baseless suspicion.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: uncertainty. Metaphorical: the inward disquiet that prompts a man to investigate before acting.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد (Restriction & Focused Predication) — The conditional and exceptive structures here (e.g., "لا يلزمك السؤال" and "إلا عن ريبة") restrict the obligation of inquiry to the presence of a genuine ground for doubt, not to mere possibility.
49:12.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Condemnation of Anger and Hatred'

50:17.arabic: أتنكرون أن عليكم حافظين كراما كاتبين عن اليمين وعن الشمال قعيد ما يلفظ من قول إلا لديه رقيب عتيد أما يستحي أحدكم إذا نشرت صحيفته التي أملاها صدر نهاره كان أكثر ما فيها ليس من أمر دينه ولا دنياه وعن بعض الصحابة قال إن الرجل ليكلمني بالكلام لجوابه أشهى إلي من الماء البارد إلى الظمآن فأترك جوابه خيفة أن يكون فضولا وقال مطرف ليعظم جلال الله في قلوبكم فلا تذكروه عند مثل قول أحدكم للكلب والحمار اللهم اخزه وما أشبه ذلك واعلم أن فضول الكلام لا ينحصر بل المهم محصور في كتاب الله تعالى قال الله عز وجل لا خير في كثير من نجواهم إلا من أمر بصدقة
50:17.english: ʿAṭāʾ ibn Abī Rabāḥ said: "Those before you used to detest excess of speech, and they counted as excess of speech everything beyond the Book of God, Mighty and Majestic, and the Sunnah of His Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him—or a command to what is right, or a prohibition of what is wrong, or your uttering your need concerning your livelihood which you cannot do without. Do you deny that {«عَلَيْكُمْ حَافِظِينَ كِرَامًا كَاتِبِينَ، يَعْلَمُونَ مَا تَفْعَلُونَ»} (over you are watchers, noble scribes, knowing what you do)? {«مَا يَلْفِظُ مِنْ قَوْلٍ إِلَّا لَدَيْهِ رَقِيبٌ عَتِيدٌ»} (He utters not a word but that there is with him a watcher, ready.) Is not one of you ashamed that when his scroll is unfolded—which he dictated through the early part of his day—most of what is in it pertains neither to his religion nor to his worldly affairs?"
50:17.section_title_en: The Book of the Etiquette of Speech — Section 660: The Second Affliction — Excess of Speech (Faḍl al-Kalām)
50:17.anchors:
- Root: فضل (Faḍl)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Excess, surplus, that which remains beyond need; the superfluous portion.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الفضل: الزيادة عن الاقتصاد" — increase beyond moderation; blameworthy when it exceeds the due measure, as in speech surpassing the need.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): "مال فاضل: كثير يفضل عن القوت" — wealth exceeding sustenance. Here applied to speech: that which exceeds the necessary portion is "faḍl" (excess), blameworthy by analogy.
- Root: ابي (Abā)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Refusal, strong aversion, stubborn rejection.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الإباء: شدة الامتناع" — intense refusal; not every refusal is abā', but abā' is the emphatic form.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "أبى الله إلا أن يكون كذا" — God refuses but that a thing be so; used of divine will overriding human inclination.
- Root: حدث (Ḥadath)
  * Lisan / Ayn: New occurrence, event; that which comes to be after not being.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الحدوث: كون الشيء بعد أن لم يكن" — origination after non-existence; al-muḥdath: that which is originated.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "نزلت به حوادث الدهر" — calamities of time befall one. Metaphorical (Majaz): "كان عمر محدثا" — one whose inner discernment is inspired, as if spoken to.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين العامل والمعمول (Interposition between Operator and Operand) — The periodic structure here interposes explanatory clauses between the governing verb and its object, as in "واعلم أن فضول الكلام لا ينحصر بل المهم محصور" — the scope of the first clause is restricted by the exceptive particle "بل" (nay), requiring the reader to hold the initial assertion in suspension until the qualification arrives.
50:17.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications, prayers, and their spiritual power, from 'Condemnation of Anger and Hatred'

50:18.arabic: قال الله تعالى {ما يلفظ من قول إلا لديه رقيب عتيد} إلا أن يثني على السلعة بما فيها مما لا يعرفه المشتري ما لم يذكره كما يصفه من خفى أخلاق العبيد والجواري والدواب فلا بأس بذكر القدر الموجود منه من غير مبالغة وإطناب وليكن قصده منه أن يعرفه أخوه المسلم فيرغب فيه وتنقضي بسببه حاجته ولا ينبغي أن يحلف عليه البتة فإنه إن كان كاذبا فقد جاء باليمين الغموس وهي من الكبائر التي تذر الديار بلاقع وإن كان صادقا فقد جعل الله تعالى عرضة لأيمانه وقد أساء فيه إذ الدنيا أخس من أن يقصد ترويجها بذكر اسم الله من غير ضرورة و
50:18.english: One of the scholars said: "Whoever sells his brother a commodity for a dirham, while it would not be suitable for him, had he purchased it for himself, except for five dānaqs (six-tenths of a dirham) — then he has abandoned the sincere counsel (al-nuṣḥ) commanded in transactions, and has not loved for his brother what he loves for himself."
50:18.topic: Al-Ghazali on purifying the character, moral diseases, and spiritual remedies, from 'Condemnation of Anger and Hatred'

65:2.arabic: الثالثة أن ينظر فيما يأخذه فإن لم يكن من حل تورع عنه {ومن يتق الله يجعل له مخرجا ويرزقه من حيث لا يحتسب} ولن يعدم المتورع عن الحرام فتوحا من الحلال فلا يأخذ من أموال الأتراك والجنود وعمال السلاطين ومن أكثر كسبه من الحرام إلا إذا ضاق الأمر عليه وكان ما يسلم إليه لا يعرف له مالكا معينا فله أن يأخذ بقدر الحاجة فإن فتوى الشرع في مثل هذا أن يتصدق به على ما سيأتي بيانه في كتاب الحلال والحرام وذلك إذا عجز عن الحلال فإذا أخذ لم يكن أخذه أخذ زكاة إذ لا يقع زكاة عن مؤديه وهو حرام الرابعة أن يتوقى مواقع الريبة والاشتباه في مقدار ما يأخذه فلا يأخذ إلا المقدار
65:2.english: The second: that he thank the giver, supplicate for him, and praise him; and his gratitude and supplication should be such that it does not remove him from being a mere intermediary, but rather he is a channel for the arrival of God's blessing to him. And the channel has a right, insofar as God made him a channel and an intermediary — and that does not negate seeing the blessing as from God, Glorified be He. For he, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "He who does not thank the people has not thanked God" {«من لم يشكر الناس لم يشكر الله»}. And God, Mighty and Majestic, has praised His servants in places for their deeds, while He is their Creator and the Originator of the capacity for them — such as His saying, Exalted is He: {«نعم العبد إنه أواب»} ["Excellent is the servant. Indeed, he is penitent."] — and other similar instances.
65:2.section_title_en: The Etiquette of the Recipient of Wealth: On the Virtue of Poverty and the Conduct of Taking from Others
65:2.anchors:
- Root: كرم (karuma)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root meaning: nobility, generosity, honorableness of origin and character.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: Divine Generosity (al-Karam) as an attribute of God entailing beneficence (al-Ifḍāl) that is pure grace, not obligation.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: nobility of lineage/character. Metaphorical: God's abundant giving without recompense.
- Root: فضل (faḍala)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root meaning: surplus, excess, superiority, that which remains beyond need.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: God's Bounty (al-Faḍl) as gratuitous favor exceeding what is merited; distinct from justice ('Adl).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: excess/surplus. Metaphorical: divine favor and grace.
- Root: نعم (ni'ma)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root meaning: well-being, bounty, benefaction; state of goodness.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-Ni'ma as the good state (al-ḥālah al-ḥasanah) bestowed by God; its genus encompasses both little and much.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: pleasant life and bounty. Metaphorical: "خفت نعامتهم" (their ostriches departed) — i.e., they went away, indicating the fleeting nature of worldly boons.
- Root: قدر (qadara)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root meaning: measure, extent, power, decree.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-Qudrah for God is the negation of incapacity; for man, a capacity for specific acts. Al-Qadr: the divine measure/decree.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: measure, amount, power. Metaphorical: "فرس بعيد القدر" (a horse of far-reaching stride) — extended reach.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — Governing the precise restriction of agency and causation in statements like "إنما المنكر أن يرى الواسطة أصلا" (The only objectionable thing is to regard the intermediary as the origin).
65:2.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications, prayers, and their spiritual power, from 'Mysteries of Zakat'

65:2.arabic: الأول تعجيل الطعام فذلك من إكرام الضيف وقد قال صلى الله عليه وسلم من كان يؤمن بالله واليوم الآخر فليكرم ضيفه (1) ومهما حضر الأكثرون وغاب واحد أو اثنان وتأخروا عن الوقت الموعود فحق الحاضر في التعجيل أولى من حق أولئك في التأخير إلا أن يكون المتأخر فقيرا أو ينكسر قلبه بذلك فلا بأس في التأخير وأحد المعنيين في قوله تعالى {هل أتاك حديث ضيف إبراهيم المكرمين} أنهم أكرموا بتعجيل الطعام إليهم دل عليه قوله تعالى {فما لبث أن جاء بعجل حنيذ} وقوله {فراغ إلى أهله فجاء بعجل سمين} والروغان الذهاب بسرعة وقيل في خفية وقيل جاء بفخذ من لحم وإنما سمي ع
65:2.english: The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Do not burden your guest so that you make him hate you, for whoever hates his guest has hated Allah, and whoever hates Allah, Allah hates him."
65:2.section_title_en: The Etiquettes of Hospitality: Invitation, Response, Attendance, and the Serving of Food — Section 290 of The Revival of the Religious Sciences
65:2.anchors:
- Root: ضيف (ḍ-y-f)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning is "to incline, to lean toward." The guest (al-ḍayf) is one who inclines toward you, alighting as a visitor; the root carries the sense of leaning or bending.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The guest is "one who inclines to you, alighting with you"; hospitality (al-ḍiyāfah) became customary in the sense of receiving such a one. The word is originally a verbal noun, hence one and many are equal in most usage.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): "ḍāfa ilayhi: he inclined toward him"; "ḍāfat al-shams: the sun inclined toward setting." Metaphorical (majāz): "aḍāfa ilayhi amran: he attributed a matter to him, leaning it upon him"; "al-muḍāf: the one constrained, hemmed in, in distress."
- Sibawayh Rule: Restriction and Focused Predication (al-ḥaṣr wa al-taqyīd bi-innamā) — governing the Prophet's statement "innamā hādhihi al-akhlāq bi-yad Allāh" (these morals are only in the hand of Allah), where innamā restricts the attribution of moral character exclusively to divine bestowal.
65:2.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'Condemnation of Anger and Hatred'

66:10.arabic: وقال تعالى {حمالة الحطب} قيل إنها كانت نمامة حمالة للحديث وقال تعالى {فخانتاهما فلم يغنيا عنهما من الله شيئا} قيل كانت امرأة لوط تخبر بالضيفان وامرأة نوح تخبر أنه مجنون وقد قال صلى الله عليه وسلم لا يدخل الجنة نمام (1) وفي حديث آخر لا يدخل الجنة قتات والقتات هو النمام وقال أبو هريرة قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أحبكم إلى الله أحاسنكم أخلاقا الموطئون أكنافا الذين يألفون ويؤلفون وإن أبغضكم إلى الله المشاءون بالنميمة المفرقون بين الإخوان الملتمسون للبرءاء العثرات (2) وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم إلا أخبركم بشراركم قالوا بلى قال المشاءون بالنميمة المف
66:10.english: Allah Most High has said: {«هَمَّازٍ مَشَّاءٍ بِنَمِيمٍ»} [“A slanderer, a walker with talebearing”] (Al-Qalam: 11). Then He said: {«عُتُلٍّ بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ زَنِيمٍ»} [“Cruel, moreover, and an intruder (zanīm)”] (Al-Qalam: 13). ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Mubārak said: “Al-zanīm is the child of fornication (walad al-zinā) who does not conceal speech.” He indicated by this that whoever does not conceal speech and walks with talebearing is evidence that he is a child of fornication — this being deduced (istinbāṭan) from the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: {«عُتُلٍّ بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ زَنِيمٍ»}. And al-zanīm is the intruder (al-daʿīy) [one falsely attached to a lineage].
66:10.anchors:
- Root: نمم (n-m-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of "to spread a report," "to carry tales," "to divulge what should remain concealed." Al-Ayn notes the root's connection to intensification and penetration of heat, implying the corrosive, penetrating effect of talebearing.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: The talebearer (namūm) is one who transmits speech with the intent to corrupt and sever bonds of brotherhood, aligning with the Quranic condemnation of the "mushā' bi-namīm" (walker with slander).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): "He is a talebearer (namūm) between people, walking with slanders (namā'im)." Metaphorical (Majaz): "The scent spread over musk (namat 'alā al-misk rā'iḥatuhā)" — indicating that namīmah is the "spreading" of that which harms, just as fragrance spreads beneficially; the metaphor underscores the talebearer's deliberate dissemination of destructive words.
- Root: زنم (z-n-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: an extra, superfluous appendage, like the wattle (zanamatān) hanging from a goat's ear or throat — something attached but not truly part of the whole.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Al-Zanīm and al-muzannam: the one who is superfluous to a people, not being of them, likened to the two wattles of a sheep... i.e., one who claims affiliation to a people while being detached from them." Applied to the bastard (walad zinā) who is "attached" to a lineage not his own.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "He has a goat with wattles (muzannamah)." Metaphorical: "In so-and-so is a zanamah of good and a zanamah of evil: a mark/sign. And so-and-so is zanīm and muzannam: an intruder (da'īy) attached to those not of him."
- Root: قتت (q-t-t)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to seek out and gather information stealthily, to eavesdrop and then carry reports — the "qattāt" is one who listens to others' private speech and transmits it to cause harm.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The qattāt is synonymous with the namūm in the prophetic hadith; both denote the one who carries destructive speech between parties.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: The qattāt is the one who "tracks" (yaquttu) news, i.e., investigates and then spreads it. Metaphorical: The term extends to any medium of harmful disclosure — speech, writing, gesture, or sign.
- Sibawayh Rule: Restriction and Focused Predication (Bāb al-Ḥaṣr wa al-Taqyīd bi-innamā) — Governing the definitional statement "innamā yuṭlaqu...": the restriction confines the common application of namīmah to a specific case while the subsequent expansion (wa-laysat al-namīmah mukhtaṣṣah bihi) negates restriction, establishing the full technical definition through contrastive predication.
66:10.topic: Al-Ghazali on purifying the character, moral diseases, and spiritual remedies, from 'Condemnation of Anger and Hatred'

68:13.arabic: قال الله تعالى {هماز مشاء بنميم} ثم قال {عتل بعد ذلك زنيم} قال عبد الله بن المبارك الزنيم ولد الزنا الذي لا يكتم الحديث وأشار به إلى أن كل من لم يكتم الحديث ومشى بالنميمة دل على أنه ولد زنا استنباطا من قوله عز وجل {عتل بعد ذلك زنيم} والزنيم هو الدعى وقال تعالى {ويل لكل همزة لمزة} قيل الهمزة النمام وقال تعالى {حمالة الحطب} قيل إنها كانت نمامة حمالة للحديث وقال تعالى {فخانتاهما فلم يغنيا عنهما من الله شيئا} قيل كانت امرأة لوط تخبر بالضيفان وامرأة نوح تخبر أنه مجنون وقد قال صلى الله ع

  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "He has a goat with wattles (muzannamah)." Metaphorical: "In so-and-so is a zanamah of good and a zanamah of evil: a mark/sign. And so-and-so is zanīm and muzannam: an intruder (da'īy) attached to those not of him."
- Root: قتت (q-t-t)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to seek out and gather information stealthily, to eavesdrop and then carry reports — the "qattāt" is one who listens to others' private speech and transmits it to cause harm.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The qattāt is synonymous with the namūm in the prophetic hadith; both denote the one who carries destructive speech between parties.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: The qattāt is the one who "tracks" (yaquttu) news, i.e., investigates and then spreads it. Metaphorical: The term extends to any medium of harmful disclosure — speech, writing, gesture, or sign.
- Sibawayh Rule: Restriction and Focused Predication (Bāb al-Ḥaṣr wa al-Taqyīd bi-innamā) — Governing the definitional statement "innamā yuṭlaqu...": the restriction confines the common application of namīmah to a specific case while the subsequent expansion (wa-laysat al-namīmah mukhtaṣṣah bihi) negates restriction, establishing the full technical definition through contrastive predication.
68:13.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'Condemnation of Anger and Hatred'

74:45.arabic: مسعود بسند صحيح + وإليه الإشارة بقوله تعالى وكنا نخوض مع الخائضين وبقوله تعالى فلا تقعدوا معهم حتى يخوضوا في حديث غيره إنكم إذا مثلهم وقال سلمان أكثر الناس ذنوبا يوم القيامة أكثرهم كلاما في معصية الله وقال ابن سيرين كان رجل من الأنصار يمر بمجلس لهم فيقول لهم توضئوا فإن بعض ما تقولون شر من الحدث فهذا هو الخوض في الباطل وهو وراء ما سيأتي من الغيبة والنميمة والفحش وغيرها بل هو الخوض في ذكر محظورات سبق وجودها أو تدبر للتوصل إليها من غير حاجة دينية إلى ذكرها ويدخل فيه أيضا الخوض في حكاية البدع والمذاهب الفاسدة
74:45.english: For Bilāl ibn al-Ḥārith has related that the Messenger of God — may God's blessings and peace be upon him — said: "Indeed, a man speaks a word of God's good pleasure, not imagining that it reaches what it reaches, and God writes for him thereby His good pleasure until the Day of Resurrection. And indeed, a man speaks a word of God's wrath, not imagining that it reaches what it reaches, and God writes against him thereby His wrath until the Day of Resurrection." [The hadith of Bilāl ibn al-Ḥārith — "Indeed, a man speaks a word of God's good pleasure" — was transmitted by Ibn Mājah and al-Tirmidhī, who said it is ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ.] And ʿAlqamah used to say: "How much speech has the hadith of Bilāl ibn al-Ḥārith prevented me from [uttering]!"
74:45.section_title_en: The Third Affliction: Wading into Falsehood (al-Khawḍ fī al-Bāṭil)
74:45.anchors:
- Root: خوض (Kha-Wa-D)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning is wading or plunging into water, passing through it; the Kitab al-Ayn records it as "الشروع في الماء والمرور فيه" (entering into water and passing through it).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In theological usage, it is predominantly employed in the Quranic context of blameworthy engagement — as in {«وخضتم كالذي خاضوا»} (And you waded as those before you waded) and {«ذرهم في خوضهم يلعبون»} (Leave them in their wading, playing). It denotes immersion in that which is vain or false.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah) — physical wading in water. Metaphorical (Majaz) — "خاضوا في الحديث وتخاوضوا فيه" (they waded into speech and waded together in it), i.e., plunging into discourse; "وهو يخوض مع الخائضين أي يبطل مع المبطلين" (he wades with the waders, i.e., he engages in falsehood with those who engage in falsehood).
- Root: بطل (Ba-Ta-La)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The Kitab al-Ayn situates it within the semantic field of that which is null, void, or futile.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الباطل: نقيض الحق، وهو ما لا ثبات له عند الفحص عنه" (Al-Bāṭil is the opposite of truth, and it is that which has no stability upon examination). It applies to both speech and deed.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — "هو باطل بين البطلان" (it is false, clearly false). Metaphorical — the verbal form "بطل" (to become null) and "أبطله غيره" (another nullified it), as in {«وبطل ما كانوا يعملون»} (And nullified is what they used to do).
- Root: كلم (Ka-La-Ma)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The Kitab al-Ayn treats it under the root of speech and utterance.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الكلم: التأثير المدرك بإحدى الحاستين" (Speech: the effect perceived by one of the two senses) — indicating that speech is that which produces an impression.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — "سمعته يتكلم بكذا" (I heard him speaking such-and-such). Metaphorical — "وهذه كلمة شاعرة" (this is a penetrating word) and "وهذا مما يكلم العرض والدين" (this is something that wounds honor and religion) — speech that injures.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The rule governing the permissibility of interposing elements between a preposition and its object, relevant here to the syntactic structure of "الخوض في الباطل" where the verbal noun governs its prepositional complement, and to the periodic constructions of the hadith citations where the conditional clauses ("إن الرجل ليتكلم بالكلمة...") require careful parsing of the apodosis.
74:45.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'Condemnation of Anger and Hatred'

82:10.arabic: بمعروف أو نهيا عن منكر أو أن تنطق بحاجتك في معيشتك التي لا بد لك منها أتنكرون أن عليكم حافظين كراما كاتبين عن اليمين وعن الشمال قعيد ما يلفظ من قول إلا لديه رقيب عتيد أما يستحي أحدكم إذا نشرت صحيفته التي أملاها صدر نهاره كان أكثر ما فيها ليس من أمر دينه ولا دنياه وعن بعض الصحابة قال إن الرجل ليكلمني بالكلام لجوابه أشهى إلي من الماء البارد إلى الظمآن فأترك جوابه خيفة أن يكون فضولا وقال مطرف ليعظم جلال الله في قلوبكم فلا تذكروه عند مثل قول أحدكم للكلب والحمار اللهم اخزه وما أشبه ذلك واعلم أن فضول الكلام لا ينحصر بل المهم محصور في كتاب الله تع
82:10.english: ʿAṭāʾ ibn Abī Rabāḥ said: "Those before you used to detest excess of speech, and they counted as excess of speech everything beyond the Book of God, Mighty and Majestic, and the Sunnah of His Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him—or a command to what is right, or a prohibition of what is wrong, or your uttering your need concerning your livelihood which you cannot do without. Do you deny that {«عَلَيْكُمْ حَافِظِينَ كِرَامًا كَاتِبِينَ، يَعْلَمُونَ مَا تَفْعَلُونَ»} (over you are watchers, noble scribes, knowing what you do)? {«مَا يَلْفِظُ مِنْ قَوْلٍ إِلَّا لَدَيْهِ رَقِيبٌ عَتِيدٌ»} (He utters not a word but that there is with him a watcher, ready.) Is not one of you ashamed that when his scroll is unfolded—which he dictated through the early part of his day—most of what is in it pertains neither to his religion nor to his worldly affairs?"
82:10.section_title_en: The Book of the Etiquette of Speech — Section 660: The Second Affliction — Excess of Speech (Faḍl al-Kalām)
82:10.anchors:
- Root: فضل (Faḍl)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Excess, surplus, that which remains beyond need; the superfluous portion.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الفضل: الزيادة عن الاقتصاد" — increase beyond moderation; blameworthy when it exceeds the due measure, as in speech surpassing the need.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): "مال فاضل: كثير يفضل عن القوت" — wealth exceeding sustenance. Here applied to speech: that which exceeds the necessary portion is "faḍl" (excess), blameworthy by analogy.
- Root: ابي (Abā)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Refusal, strong aversion, stubborn rejection.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الإباء: شدة الامتناع" — intense refusal; not every refusal is abā', but abā' is the emphatic form.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "أبى الله إلا أن يكون كذا" — God refuses but that a thing be so; used of divine will overriding human inclination.
- Root: حدث (Ḥadath)
  * Lisan / Ayn: New occurrence, event; that which comes to be after not being.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الحدوث: كون الشيء بعد أن لم يكن" — origination after non-existence; al-muḥdath: that which is originated.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "نزلت به حوادث الدهر" — calamities of time befall one. Metaphorical (Majaz): "كان عمر محدثا" — one whose inner discernment is inspired, as if spoken to.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين العامل والمعمول (Interposition between Operator and Operand) — The periodic structure here interposes explanatory clauses between the governing verb and its object, as in "واعلم أن فضول الكلام لا ينحصر بل المهم محصور" — the scope of the first clause is restricted by the exceptive particle "بل" (nay), requiring the reader to hold the initial assertion in suspension until the qualification arrives.
82:10.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications, prayers, and their spiritual power, from 'Condemnation of Anger and Hatred'

104:1.arabic: الصيام إن كانا صائمين وعن مجاهد أنه قال في ويل لكل همزة لمزة الهمزة الطعان في الناس واللمزة الذي يأكل لحوم الناس وقال قيادة ذكر لنا أن عذاب القبر ثلاثة أثلاث ثلث من الغيبة وثلث من النميمة وثلث من البول وقال الحسن والله للغيبة أسرع في دين الرجل المؤمن من الأكله في الجسد وقال بعضهم أدركنا السلف وهم لا يرون العبادة في الصوم ولا في الصلاة ولكن في الكف عن أعراض الناس وقال ابن عباس إذا أردت أن تذكر عيوب صاحبك فاذكر عيوبك وقال أبو هريرة يبصر أحدكم القذى في عين أخيه ولا يبصر الجذع في عين نفسه وكان الحسن يقول
104:1.english: Salim ibn Jabir said: "I came to the Prophet, peace be upon him, and said: 'Teach me something beneficial by which I may profit.' He said: 'Do not belittle anything of goodness, even if it be that you pour from your bucket into the vessel of one who seeks water, and that you meet your brother with a cheerful face. And if he turns away, do not backbite him.'"
104:1.section_title_en: The Book of the Revival of the Religious Sciences — Section 681: On Backbiting (Ghibah) — Its Severe Prohibition and the Narrations Concerning It
104:1.anchors:
- Root: غيب (ghayb)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of being hidden, concealed, absent from sight.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الغيب: مصدر غابت الشمس وغيرها: إذا استترت عن العين" — used for what is absent from the senses; the backbiter (mughtab) speaks of the absent person in a way that defames him.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): "تكلم بذلك عن ظهر الغيب" — speaking about one who is absent. Metaphorical (Majaz): The term "ghibah" is transferred to the act of mentioning a person's fault in his absence, as established by the Hadith.
- Root: لحم (lahm)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Flesh, meat; "لحمت العظم: أخذت ما عليه من اللحم" — to strip flesh from bone.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "اللحم جمعه: لحام، ولحوم" — and the Quranic prohibition {أيحب أحدكم أن يأكل لحم أخيه ميتا} [Al-Hujurat: 12] employs the metaphor of eating a dead brother's flesh for backbiting.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "معه لحمان كثير ولحام" — having much meat. Metaphorical (Majaz): "رجل لحيم: قتيل، وقد لحم ومعناه قطع لحمه" — and "أكل لحوم الناس" is the classical rhetorical expression for backbiting, as in the Hadith of the two women who "ate the flesh of people."
- Root: عور (awr)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The private parts, a blemish, a weak point; "عورة" — that which one conceals.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Related to "عور" — exposing what is hidden and shameful.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "عورة" — the exposed, vulnerable part. Metaphorical: "تتبع عورات المسلمين" — seeking out their hidden faults and sins, as in the Hadith: "من تتبع عورة أخيه تتبع الله عورته."
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The Hadith "حتى أسمع العوانق في بيوتهن" demonstrates the periodic structure where the prepositional phrase "في بيوتهن" is interposed after the verb "أسمع" to emphasize the far-reaching effect of the Prophet's voice, showing the permissibility of such interposition when the meaning remains clear and the sentence is well-formed.
104:1.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Condemnation of Anger and Hatred'

2:44.arabic: وقال الله تعالى {أتأمرون الناس بالبر وتنسون أنفسكم} ولذلك كان وزر العالم في معاصيه أكثر من وزر الجاهل إذ يزل بزلته عالم كثير ويقتدون به ومن سن سنة سيئة فعليه وزرها ووزر من عمل بها ولذلك قال علي رضي الله عنه قصم ظهري رجلان عالم متهتك وجاهل متنسك فالجاهل يغر الناس بتنسكه والعالم يغرهم بتهتكه والله أعلم الباب السادس في آفات العلم وبيان علامات علما الآخرة والعلماء السوء قد ذكرنا ما ورد من فضائل العلم والعلماء وقد ورد في العلماء السوء تشديدات عظيمة دلت على أنهم أشد الخلق عذابا يوم القيامة فمن ال
2:44.english: I say: Leave the reins and go. For if one comes who comprehends, and you have concealed it from him, then let him bridle me — for God Most High has said: {«ولا تؤتوا السفهاء أموالكم»} — "And do not give the foolish your wealth" — as an indication that preserving knowledge from one who would corrupt it and harm it is even more incumbent. And wrongdoing in giving to one who is not deserving is no less than wrongdoing in withholding from one who is deserving.
2:44.section_title_en: The Book of the Revival of the Religious Sciences — Section 48: On the Etiquette of the Teacher and the Learner (Continued), and the Exposition of the Marks Distinguishing the Scholars of the Hereafter from the Evil Scholars
2:44.anchors:
- Root: علم (ʿalima)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Knowledge as the apprehension of a thing in its true reality; the root also carries the sense of a mark or sign (ʿalam) by which something is known.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Knowledge is of two kinds: apprehension of the essence of a thing, and judgment upon a thing affirming or denying something of it. The first is transitive to one object; the second to two.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal usage: "He is a sign (ʿalam) of knowledge" — i.e., a distinguished landmark. Metaphorical: "The traces (maʿālim) of the road" — the vestiges by which one is guided.
- Root: ظلم (ẓalama)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To place something in other than its proper place; darkness (ẓulmah) as the privation of light.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Darkness is the absence of light; figuratively used for ignorance, polytheism, and wickedness, just as light is used for their opposites.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "He wronged and was wronged" — to suffer injustice. Metaphorical: "Wrongdoing is darkness, just as justice is light" — for the wrongdoer acts in the darkness of his own soul.
- Root: منع (manaʿa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To withhold, to prevent, to protect; a fortress (manīʿah) is that which defends.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Used in opposition to giving; also used for protection, as in "a fortified place" (makān manīʿ).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "He prevented him from the thing." Metaphorical: "He protects the neighbor" — i.e., defends him from harm.
- Root: عقل (ʿaqala)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The intellect; originally to bind or restrain (as a camel is hobbled), hence the faculty that restrains the soul from base desires.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The intellect is the faculty prepared for the reception of knowledge, and also the knowledge acquired by that faculty.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "I have not done so since I attained reason." Metaphorical: "A palm tree that does not accept pollination" — i.e., does not receive what is offered to it.
- Sibawayh Rule: The Interposition of the Prepositional Phrase (al-faṣl bayna al-jār wa al-majrūr) — governing the permissible separation between a governing word and its governed prepositional phrase where the intervening element is syntactically complete, as in the construction "Leave the reins and go" (itruk al-lijām wa-idhhab), where the imperative governs two successive clauses without ellipsis.
2:44.topic: Al-Ghazali on the journey of the soul, death, and the Hereafter, from 'Book of Knowledge'

2:89.arabic: يعرفونه كما يعرفون أبناءهم وقال تعالى فلما جاءهم ما عرفوا كفروا به فلعنة الله على الكافرين وقال تعالى في قصة بلعام بن باعوراء واتل عليهم نبأ الذي آتيناه آياتنا فانسلخ منها فأتبعه الشيطان فكان من الغاوين حتى قال فمثله كمثل الكلب إن تحمل عليه يلهث أو تتركه يلهث فكذلك العالم الفاجر فإن بلعام أوتي كتاب الله تعالى فأخلد إلى الشهوات فشبه بالكلب أي سواء أوتي الحكمة أو لم يؤت فهو يلهث إلى الشهوات وقال عيسى عليه السلام مثل علماء السوء كمثل صخرة وقعت على فم النهر لا هي تشرب الماء ولا هي تترك الماء يخلص إلى الزرع ومثل علماء السوء مثل قناة الحش ظ
2:89.english: I say: The Prophet — peace and blessings be upon him — said: "The scholar will indeed be tormented with a torment at which the inhabitants of the Fire will circle around, marveling at the severity of his punishment." By it he meant the wicked scholar.
2:89.section_title_en: The Worldly Scholar's Punishment and the Marks of the Hereafter-Scholars
2:89.anchors:
- Root: فجر (fajara)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To split, cleave, or rend something widely; to break open
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The splitting of something with wide rupture — from which the dawn (al-fajr) is named, as it splits the night; used for both physical and moral rupture
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the cleaving of water or the breaking of dawn. Metaphorical: the eruption of punishment upon one suddenly and overwhelmingly
- Root: علم (ʿalima)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Knowledge; the faculty of apprehending a thing as it truly is
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Twofold: (1) apprehension of a thing's essence; (2) judgment upon a thing affirming or denying something of it. The scholar (al-ʿālim) is one who possesses such apprehension
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: knowledge as certain apprehension. Metaphorical: the "signs" (maʿālim) of the path — that by which one is guided; the scholar is a "sign" pointing either to guidance or to ruin
- Root: دنا (dana)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To be near, to draw close; al-dunyā (the nearer world) as that which is immediate and low
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Proximity by essence or by judgment; used of place, time, and station. The "nearer" (al-adnā) is contrasted with the greater and the better
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: nearness. Metaphorical: baseness and lowness — the dunyā as the inferior, the contemptible
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — The particle innamā restricts the predicate exclusively to its subject, as in "the winners and the brought-near are only the scholars of the Hereafter," effecting complete exclusion of all else.
2:89.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'Book of Knowledge'

2:89.arabic: بعد معرفتهم إياه فقال تعالى {وكانوا من قبل يستفتحون على الذين كفروا فلما جاءهم ما عرفوا كفروا به} إلى قوله {أن يكفروا بما أنزل الله بغيا} أي حسدا وقالت صفية بنت حيي للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم جاء أبي وعمي من عندك يوما فقال أبي لعمي ما تقول فيه قال أقول أنه النبي الذي بشر به موسى قال فما ترى قال أرى معاداته أيام الحياة (2) فهذا حكم الحسد في التحريم وأما المنافسة فليست بحرام بل هي إما واجبة وإما مندوبة وإما مباحة وقد يستعمل لفظ الحسد بدل المنافسة والمنافسة بدل الحسد قال قثم بن العباس لما أراد هو والفضل أن يأتيا النب
2:89.english: The Prophet ﷺ said: «إن المؤمن يغبط والمنافق يحسد» — "The believer aspires emulously, and the hypocrite envies."
2:89.section_title_en: On the Reality of Envy (Ḥasad) and Its Degrees — Section 720
2:89.anchors:
- Root: نعم (n-ʿ-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root meaning of "bounty, benefaction, grace" — that state of goodness and well-being bestowed.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "النعمة: الحالة الحسنة" — bounty is the excellent state/condition; it is the genus term applying to both little and much, as in {«وإن تعدوا نعمة الله لا تحصوها»} [Ibrahim: 34].
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): "جلت نعمة الله ونعماؤه" — bounty as actual bestowed good. Metaphorical (majāz): "خفت نعامتهم" — departure/removal, relevant to the envier's wish for the bounty's removal.
- Root: حسد (ḥ-s-d)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Envy — the desire for removal of another's good.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الحسد: تمني زوال نعمة من مستحق لها" — envy is wishing the removal of bounty from one who deserves it, sometimes accompanied by striving to effect its removal. Cited: «المؤمن يغبط والمنافق يحسد».
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "حسده على نعمة الله" — envying someone for God's bounty. "إن الحسد يأكل الجسد" — envy consumes the body.
- Root: نفس (n-f-s)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The self; also value, preciousness.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): النفس: الروح — the soul/spirit; also الذات (essence/self).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "شيء نفيس ومنفس" — a precious thing. Metaphorical: "دفق نفسه أي دمه" — poured out his self, i.e., his blood. From this root derives المنافسة (emulative competition) — the striving for precious things.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد (Restriction & Specification) — The definition of ḥasad is given as a restricted predication (ḥadd), delimiting its essential meaning: "كراهة النعمة وحب زوالها عن المنعم عليه" — the hatred of bounty and love of its removal from the one upon whom it is bestowed. This is a formal definition (ḥadd), not merely a lexical gloss.
2:89.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'Condemnation of Envy'

2:121.arabic: قال الله تعالى {الذين آتيناهم الكتاب يتلونه حق تلاوته} أي لا يجاوزون فنا حتى يحكموه علما وعملا وليكن قصده في كل علم يتحراه الترقي إلى ما هو فوقه فينبغي ألا يحكم على علم بالفساد لوقوع الخلف بين أصحابه فيه ولا بخطأ واحد أو آحاد فيه ولا بمخالفتهم موجب علمهم بالعمل فترى جماعة تركوا النظر في العقليات والفقهيات متعللين فيها بأنها لو كان لها أصل لأدركه أربابها وقد مضى كشف هذه الشبه في كتاب معيار العلم وترى طائفة يعتقدون بطلان الطب لخطأ شاهدوه من طبيب وطائفة اعتقدوا صحة النجوم لصواب اتفق لواحد وطائفة اعتقدوا بطلانه
2:121.english: By this I do not mean the belief which the common man picks up by inheritance or by rote acquisition, nor the method of theological disputation and argumentation for fortifying one's creed against the evasions of opponents—as is the ultimate aim of the scholastic theologian (mutakallim). Rather, it is a kind of certainty which is the fruit of a light that God—may He be exalted—casts into the heart of a servant whose inward being has been purified by spiritual striving (mujāhadah) from all impurities, until he attains to the rank of the faith of Abū Bakr—may God be pleased with him—whose faith, were it weighed against the faith of all created beings, would outweigh them, as the Master of mankind—peace and blessings be upon him—bore witness for him. For in my view, what the common man believes and what the theologian arranges—who exceeds the common man only in the craft of speech (kalām), and for that very reason his craft is named "kalām"—is not that rank. Indeed, ʿUmar, ʿUthmān, ʿAlī, and the rest of the Companions—may God be pleased with them all—fell short of it, until Abū Bakr surpassed them by that secret which was deposited in his breast.
2:121.section_title_en: The Revival of the Religious Sciences — Section 43: On the Ordering of the Sciences and the Duties of the Seeker
2:121.anchors:
- Root: ذوق (dh-w-q)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Perceiving by taste; experiential apprehension
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Direct, unmediated perception—contrasted with mere cognition or hearsay
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal tasting vs. metaphorical "savoring" of knowledge
- Root: سلك (s-l-k)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Entering into a path; threading through
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The spiritual wayfaring (sulūk) toward God
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal road-taking vs. metaphorical spiritual journeying
- Root: كشف (k-sh-f) — AVOIDED per constraints; substituted with Root: غور (gh-w-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Depth, profundity; the deep bed of a sea
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The unfathomable depth of divine knowledge
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal deep water vs. metaphorical inaccessibility of ultimate truth
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — Governing the periodic suspension of meaning across clauses for rhetorical emphasis
2:121.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Book of Knowledge'

2:146.arabic: وقوله تعالى {وإن فريقا منهم ليكتمون الحق وهم يعلمون} وهو تحريم للكتمان كما قال تعالى في الشهادة {ومن يكتمها فإنه آثم قلبه} وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم ما آتى الله عالما علما إلا وأخذ عليه من الميثاق ما أخذ على النبيين أن يبينوه للناس ولا يكتموه (6) وقال تعالى {ومن أحسن قولا ممن دعا إلى الله وعمل صالحا} وقال تعالى {ادع إلى سبيل ربك بالحكمة والموعظة الحسنة} وقال تعالى {ويعلمهم الكتاب والحكمة} وأما الأخبار فقوله صلى الله عليه وسلم لما بعث معاذا رضي الله عنه إلى اليمن لأن يهدي الله بك رجلا واحدا خير
2:146.english: As for the Qur'anic verses: His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: {وَلِيُنذِرُوا قَوْمَهُمْ إِذَا رَجَعُوا إِلَيْهِمْ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَحْذَرُونَ} "That they may warn their people when they return to them, that perhaps they may be cautious" {«ولينذروا قومهم إذا رجعوا إليهم لعلهم يحذرون»} — and the intended meaning is teaching and guidance (al-taʿlīm wa-al-irshād).
2:146.anchors:
- Root: علم (ʿalima)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning is "to know, to perceive a thing by its reality"; the root also carries the sense of "marker, sign, banner" — that by which something is distinguished and recognized.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "العلم: إدراك الشيء بحقيقته" — knowledge is the apprehension of a thing by its true reality, divided into apprehension of the essence of a thing and judgment upon it. This is the attribute by which the scholar (ʿālim) is distinguished and by which he becomes a "sign" (ʿalam) pointing to truth.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): "هو من أعلام العلم الخافقه" — the scholar is among the lofty banners of knowledge. The teaching act makes the scholar a living signpost; the root's literal sense of "marking" or "branding" a thing carries into the metaphorical (majāz) register of "imprinting" knowledge upon hearts.
- Root: حدث (ḥadatha)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning is "to be new, to occur after not having been"; al-ḥadīth is speech that is new and conveyed.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الحدوث: كون الشيء بعد أن لم يكن" — origination after non-existence. The prophetic traditions (aḥādīth) cited here are "newly conveyed" reports that carry authority.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Metaphorical (majāz): "صاروا أحاديث" — they became subjects of discourse. The transmission of knowledge is an "event" (ḥadath) that occurs in the listener, renewing his state.
- Root: عهد (ʿahida)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning is "covenant, pact, charge"; al-ʿahd is a binding commission that one is obligated to fulfill.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The covenant (mīthāq) taken from the People of the Book and from the scholars is a divine charge (taklīf) that makes teaching an obligation, not a supererogatory act.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the covenant is a "charge entrusted" (waṣiyyah) that binds the one who receives knowledge to its dissemination.
- Root: كتم (katama)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning is "to conceal, to hide"; al-kitmān is the deliberate suppression of what ought to be revealed.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Concealment of knowledge is paired with concealment of testimony (shahādah) in the Qur'an — both are sins of the heart (ithm al-qalb) because they withhold what God has commanded to be made manifest.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal vs. metaphorical: the "bridle of fire" (lijām min nār) on the Day of Judgment is a metaphorical (majāz) embodiment of the inner restraint of truth — the concealed knowledge becomes a physical restraint in the afterlife.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد (Restriction & Specification) — The verse {وإن فريقا منهم ليكتمون الحق وهم يعلمون} employs the restrictive particle "inna" with the continuous verb form (yaktimūn) to specify an ongoing, willful concealment, distinguishing it from mere ignorance. The conditional structures in the ḥadīth "man taʿallama... man ʿallama... man katama" (whoever learns... whoever teaches... whoever conceals) follow the canonical pattern of protasis-apodosis (sharṭ/jazāʾ) that establishes a universal causal linkage between the act and its recompense.
2:146.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'Book of Knowledge'

2:146.arabic: ولدا ولا قالوا إنه ثالث ثلاثة إلا أنهم أنكروا بعد المعرفة إذ قال الله يعرفونه كما يعرفون أبناءهم وقال تعالى فلما جاءهم ما عرفوا كفروا به فلعنة الله على الكافرين وقال تعالى في قصة بلعام بن باعوراء واتل عليهم نبأ الذي آتيناه آياتنا فانسلخ منها فأتبعه الشيطان فكان من الغاوين حتى قال فمثله كمثل الكلب إن تحمل عليه يلهث أو تتركه يلهث فكذلك العالم الفاجر فإن بلعام أوتي كتاب الله تعالى فأخلد إلى الشهوات فشبه بالكلب أي سواء أوتي الحكمة أو لم يؤت فهو يلهث إلى الشهوات وقال عيسى عليه السلام مثل علماء السوء كمثل صخرة وقعت على فم النهر لا هي تشرب الماء و
2:146.english: I say: The Prophet — peace and blessings be upon him — said: "The scholar will indeed be tormented with a torment at which the inhabitants of the Fire will circle around, marveling at the severity of his punishment." By it he meant the wicked scholar.
2:146.section_title_en: The Worldly Scholar's Punishment and the Marks of the Hereafter-Scholars
2:146.anchors:
- Root: فجر (fajara)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To split, cleave, or rend something widely; to break open
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The splitting of something with wide rupture — from which the dawn (al-fajr) is named, as it splits the night; used for both physical and moral rupture
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the cleaving of water or the breaking of dawn. Metaphorical: the eruption of punishment upon one suddenly and overwhelmingly
- Root: علم (ʿalima)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Knowledge; the faculty of apprehending a thing as it truly is
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Twofold: (1) apprehension of a thing's essence; (2) judgment upon a thing affirming or denying something of it. The scholar (al-ʿālim) is one who possesses such apprehension
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: knowledge as certain apprehension. Metaphorical: the "signs" (maʿālim) of the path — that by which one is guided; the scholar is a "sign" pointing either to guidance or to ruin
- Root: دنا (dana)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To be near, to draw close; al-dunyā (the nearer world) as that which is immediate and low
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Proximity by essence or by judgment; used of place, time, and station. The "nearer" (al-adnā) is contrasted with the greater and the better
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: nearness. Metaphorical: baseness and lowness — the dunyā as the inferior, the contemptible
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — The particle innamā restricts the predicate exclusively to its subject, as in "the winners and the brought-near are only the scholars of the Hereafter," effecting complete exclusion of all else.
2:146.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'Book of Knowledge'

2:161.arabic: في ديننا ما ليس منه فهو رد (2) وفي خبر آخر من غش أمتي فعليه لعنة الله والملائكة والناس أجمعين قيل يا رسول الله وما غش أمتك قال أن يبتدع بدعة يحمل الناس عليها (3) وقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إن لله عز وجل ملكا ينادي كل يوم من خالف سنة رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لم تنله شفاعته (4) ومثال الجاني على الدين بإبداع ما يخالف السنة بالنسبة إلى من يذنب ذنبا مثال من عصى الملك في قلب دولته بالنسبة إلى من خالف أمره في خدمة معينة وذلك قد يغفر له فأما في قلب الدولة فلا وقال بعض العلماء ما تكلم فيه السلف فالسكوت عنه جفاء وما سكت عنه السلف فالكلام في
2:161.english: For this reason ʿAlī, may God be pleased with him, said — when it was said to him, "You have opposed so-and-so" — "The best of us is the most following of us of this religion." So one ought not to be perturbed by opposing the people of one's own age when one is thereby conforming to the people of the age of the Messenger of God ﷺ. For the people have adopted an opinion (raʾy) concerning their present situation, due to the inclination of their natures toward it, and their souls have not permitted them to acknowledge that this is a cause of deprivation from Paradise — so they have claimed that there is no path to Paradise other than it.
2:161.section_title_en: ** Section 64 — On the Sciences of the Inner Life: The Obligation to Follow the Salaf and the Condemnation of Innovation (Bidʿah)
2:161.anchors:
**
- Root: علم (ʿalima)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning — perception of a thing by its true nature; knowledge as the apprehension of reality.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "العلم: إدراك الشيء بحقيقته" — knowledge is the apprehension of a thing in its true reality, divided into apprehension of the essence and judgment upon the thing.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal usage — "ما علمت بخبرك: ما شعرت به" (I did not know of your news: I had no awareness of it). The scholar (ʿālim) is one whose knowledge is manifest in action.
- Root: بدع (badaʿa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning — to originate, to create something new without prior example.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الإبداع: إنشاء صنعة بلا احتذاء واقتداء" — origination of a thing without model or precedent. When used of God, it is bringing into existence without instrument, matter, time, or place.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — "أبدع الشيء وابتدعه: اخترعه" (he originated it and innovated it: he invented it). Metaphorical — "أبدعت حجتك إذا ضعفت" (your argument became weak/innovative in the bad sense).
- Root: حدث (ḥadatha)
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الحدوث: كون الشيء بعد أن لم يكن" — coming-to-be of a thing after it was not. "المحدث: ما أوجد بعد أن لم يكن" — the originated thing.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — "هو حدث من الأحداث" (he is a youth among youths). Metaphorical — "صاروا أحاديث" (they became [mere] tales). In religious terminology: muḥdathāt = newly-invented matters in religion.
- Root: هدى (hadā)
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Guidance — directing to the path with gentleness; al-hudā is the guidance of the Prophet ﷺ in matters of religion.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "حسن الهدى" — excellent guidance, the prophetic way (sunnah) as opposed to innovation.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — "إنما هما اثنتان: الكلام والهدى" restricts the two matters exclusively to speech and guidance, excluding all else.

#
2:161.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Book of Knowledge'

2:282.arabic: وقد قال الله تعالى يا أيها الذين آمنوا أنفقوا من طيبات ما كسبتم ومما أخرجنا لكم من الأرض ولا تيمموا الخبيث منه تنفقون ولستم بآخذيه إلا أن تغمضوا فيه أي لا تأخذوه إلا مع كراهية وحياء وهو معنى الإغماض فلا تؤثروا به ربكم وفي الخبر سبق درهم مائة ألف درهم (3) وذلك بأن يخرجه الإنسان وهو من أحل ماله وأجوده فيصدر ذلك عن الرضا والفرح بالبذل وقد يخرج مائة ألف درهم مما يكره من ماله فيدل ذلك على أنه ليس يؤثر الله عز وجل بشيء مما يحبه وبذلك ذم الله تعالى قوما جعلوا لله ما يكرهون فقال تعال
2:282.english: The heart is not treated save with the compound electuary (maʿjūn) of knowledge and works. And this condition among the conditions of almsgiving runs in the same course as humility (al-khushūʿ) runs in the prayer. This is established by his saying — may Allah bless him and grant him peace: "A man has nothing of his prayer save that of which he was conscious." And this is like his saying — may Allah bless him and grant him peace: "Allah does not accept the charity of the one who bestows it with reproach (al-mannān)." And like His saying — Exalted is He: {«لا تبطلوا صدقاتكم بالمن والأذى»} ("Do not nullify your charities by reproach and injury"). As for the legal opinion (fatwā) of the jurist that the alms fall in their proper place and that one's liability is discharged without this condition — that is another discussion, and we have already pointed to its meaning in the Book of Prayer.
2:282.section_title_en: The Inner Conditions of Charity — Section 175 (From The Revival of the Religious Sciences, Book of the Mysteries of Almsgiving)
2:282.anchors:
- Root: قلب (q-l-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "To turn, overturn, transform a thing from one state to another; to rotate, to flip"
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "قلب الشيء: تصريفه وصرفه عن وجه إلى وجه" — the heart is so named because of its constant turning and transformation between states
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "قلب الشيء قلبا: حوله عن وجهه" (to turn a thing from its face). Metaphorical: "رجل قلب حول: يقلب الأمور ويحتال" — one who turns matters over and manages them; "قلبوا لك الأمور" (they turned matters against you)
- Root: وجل (w-j-l)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "Fear, dread, apprehension that strikes the heart"
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الوجل: استشعار الخوف" — the sensing of fear; cited in {«إنما المؤمنون الذين إذا ذكر الله وجلت قلوبهم»}
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "رجل وجل، وقوم وجال" — a fearful man, a fearful people; "وفي قلبه وجل" — in his heart is dread
- Root: عجب (ʿ-j-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "Wonder, amazement; self-admiration, vanity"
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Self-admiration (al-ʿujb) is a destructive spiritual ailment that nullifies deeds
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: wonder at something extraordinary. Metaphorical: self-conceit regarding one's own acts of obedience
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد (Restriction & Focused Predication) — governing the precise limitation of general categories (al-ṣifāt al-khāṣṣah within al-aṣnāf al-thamāniyyah) and the conditional structure of acceptance
