##
2:282.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Duties of Brotherhood'

2:282.arabic: إلى ما أنهاكم عنه وقال تعالى واتقوا الله ويعلمكم الله وقال تعالى واتقوا الله واعلموا واتقوا الله واسمعوا وقال تعالى لعيسى عليه السلام يا ابن مريم عظ نفسك فإن اتعظت فعظ الناس وإلا فاستحي مني وقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم مررت ليلة أسري بي بأقوام تقرض شفاههم بمقاريض من نار فقلت من أنتم فقالوا كنا نأمر بالخير ولا نأتيه وننهى عن الشر ونأتيه (2) وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم هلاك أمتي عالم فاجر وعابد جاهل وشر الشرار شرار العلماء وخير الخيار خيار العلماء (3) وقال الأوزاعي رحمه الله شكت النواويس ما تجد من نتن جي
2:282.english:
[Root: ملح]
  • Lisan al-Arab: "الملح: ما يصلح الطعام، وجمعه ملوح وأملاح. والمليح: الحسن. والملاحة: الحسن. وملح الرجل يملح ملاحة: حسن. وتملح: تزين."
  • Al-Raghib (Al-Mufradat): "الملح: ما يحفظ الطعام ويمنع فساده، ويستعار لما يحفظ الإيمان والعلم من الفساد."
  • Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "ملح الماء: إذا كان فيه ملوحة. وملح الطعام: جعل فيه الملح. وهذا على الحقيقة، ويستعار الملح لما يصلح به الأمر."
  • Kitab al-Ayn: "الملح: معروف، والمليح: الحسن من كل شيء."
2:282.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Book of Knowledge'

2:283.arabic: عمل الفؤاد كعمل السمع والبصر فلا يعفى عنه وقوله تعالى {ولا تكتموا الشهادة ومن يكتمها فإنه آثم قلبه} وقوله تعالى {لا يؤاخذكم الله باللغو في أيمانكم ولكن يؤاخذكم بما كسبت قلوبكم} والحق عندنا في هذه المسألة لا يوقف عليه ما لم تقع الإحاطة بتفصيل أعمال القلوب من مبدأ ظهورها إلى أن يظهر العمل على الجوارح فنقول أول ما يرد على القلب الخاطر كما لو خطر له مثلا صورة امرأة وأنها وراء ظهره في الطريق لو التفت إليها لرآها والثاني هيجان الرغبة إلى النظر وهو حركة الشهوة في الطبع وهذا يتولد من الخاطر الأول ونسميه ميل الطبع ويسمى الأول حديث النفس والثالث حكم ا
2:283.english: Know that this is a subtle matter, and there have come down concerning it verses and reports that are mutually conflicting, such that the way of reconciling between them becomes obscure — save for the master-brokers of the scholars of the Sacred Law. For it has been related from the Prophet — peace and blessings be upon him — that he said: "God has pardoned my community for what their souls whisper to them, so long as they do not speak of it or act upon it." (1) And Abū Hurayrah said: The Messenger of God — peace and blessings be upon him — said: "God — exalted is He — says to the guardian angels: When My servant intends a sin, do not write it against him; but if he commits it, then write it as one sin. And when he intends a good deed and does not perform it, write it for him as one good deed; but if he performs it, write it for him as ten." (2) This has been recorded by al-Bukhārī and Muslim in the two Ṣaḥīḥs, and it is evidence for the pardon of the heart's act and its intending of a sin. And in another wording: "Whoever intends a good deed and does not perform it, it is written for him as a good deed; and whoever intends a good deed and performs it, it is written for him as up to seven hundred multiples. And whoever intends a sin and does not perform it, it is not written against him; but if he performs it, it is written." And in yet another wording: "When My servant speaks within himself of committing a sin, I forgive him for it so long as he does not commit it." And all of this indicates the pardon.
2:283.section_title_en: The Heart's Whisperings and the Divine Pardon — On the Four Stages of Inner Acts
2:283.anchors:
- Root: نفس (n-f-s)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The self, soul, or inner being; that which breathes and harbors concealed thoughts.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-nafs denotes the soul or self (al-rūḥ), and in divine address, "what your souls whisper" (mā ḥaddathat bihi nufūsuhā) refers to the inner promptings that arise without deliberate volition.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) usage pertains to the soul's essence; metaphorical (majāz) usage extends to inner speech and inclination, as in "ḥadīth al-nafs" (self-talk), which is not yet resolved action.
- Root: حدث (ḥ-d-th)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To originate or bring forth something new; an event or occurrence that comes to be after non-existence.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-ḥudūth is the coming-to-be of a thing after it was not; "ḥadīth al-nafs" is the newly arising thought that occurs to the heart without prior acquisition.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: a recent matter or speech; metaphorical: the inner utterance of the soul, as in the prophetic report, "God has pardoned my community for what their souls whisper to them."
- Root: هم (h-m-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To intend, resolve, or purpose; the stirring of the will toward an act before its execution.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-hamm is the resolved intention (al-ʿazm) that precedes the deed; it is distinguished from mere inclination (mayl) and passing thought (khāṭir).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the soul's determination; metaphorical: the initial resolve that, when strengthened, becomes a firm will (irādah jazīmah).
- Root: قلب (q-l-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The heart; to turn or overturn, signifying its fluctuating nature between states.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The heart is the seat of cognition and volition; its "acts" (aʿmāl al-qulūb) include thought, belief, and resolve, which are subject to divine reckoning.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the physical organ; metaphorical: the spiritual faculty that perceives, believes, and intends, as in "the heart's sin" (ithm al-qalb).
- Sibawayh Rule: Restriction and Focused Predication (al-ḥaṣr wa al-taqyīd bi-innamā) — The prophetic and Quranic statements employ restriction to delineate the boundary between what is pardoned (the passing thought) and what is reckoned (the resolved intention), requiring precise parsing of the conditional clauses (law, idhā, man) to distinguish the stages of inner acts.
2:283.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Disciplining the Soul'

2:283.arabic: كما قال تعالى في الشهادة {ومن يكتمها فإنه آثم قلبه} وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم ما آتى الله عالما علما إلا وأخذ عليه من الميثاق ما أخذ على النبيين أن يبينوه للناس ولا يكتموه (6) وقال تعالى {ومن أحسن قولا ممن دعا إلى الله وعمل صالحا} وقال تعالى {ادع إلى سبيل ربك بالحكمة والموعظة الحسنة} وقال تعالى {ويعلمهم الكتاب والحكمة} وأما الأخبار فقوله صلى الله عليه وسلم لما بعث معاذا رضي الله عنه إلى اليمن لأن يهدي الله بك رجلا واحدا خير لك من الدنيا وما فيها // حديث قال لمعاذ حين بعثه إلى اليمن لأن يهدي
2:283.english: As for the Qur'anic verses: His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: {وَلِيُنذِرُوا قَوْمَهُمْ إِذَا رَجَعُوا إِلَيْهِمْ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَحْذَرُونَ} "That they may warn their people when they return to them, that perhaps they may be cautious" {«ولينذروا قومهم إذا رجعوا إليهم لعلهم يحذرون»} — and the intended meaning is teaching and guidance (al-taʿlīm wa-al-irshād).
2:283.anchors:
- Root: علم (ʿalima)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning is "to know, to perceive a thing by its reality"; the root also carries the sense of "marker, sign, banner" — that by which something is distinguished and recognized.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "العلم: إدراك الشيء بحقيقته" — knowledge is the apprehension of a thing by its true reality, divided into apprehension of the essence of a thing and judgment upon it. This is the attribute by which the scholar (ʿālim) is distinguished and by which he becomes a "sign" (ʿalam) pointing to truth.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): "هو من أعلام العلم الخافقه" — the scholar is among the lofty banners of knowledge. The teaching act makes the scholar a living signpost; the root's literal sense of "marking" or "branding" a thing carries into the metaphorical (majāz) register of "imprinting" knowledge upon hearts.
- Root: حدث (ḥadatha)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning is "to be new, to occur after not having been"; al-ḥadīth is speech that is new and conveyed.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الحدوث: كون الشيء بعد أن لم يكن" — origination after non-existence. The prophetic traditions (aḥādīth) cited here are "newly conveyed" reports that carry authority.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Metaphorical (majāz): "صاروا أحاديث" — they became subjects of discourse. The transmission of knowledge is an "event" (ḥadath) that occurs in the listener, renewing his state.
- Root: عهد (ʿahida)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning is "covenant, pact, charge"; al-ʿahd is a binding commission that one is obligated to fulfill.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The covenant (mīthāq) taken from the People of the Book and from the scholars is a divine charge (taklīf) that makes teaching an obligation, not a supererogatory act.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the covenant is a "charge entrusted" (waṣiyyah) that binds the one who receives knowledge to its dissemination.
- Root: كتم (katama)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning is "to conceal, to hide"; al-kitmān is the deliberate suppression of what ought to be revealed.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Concealment of knowledge is paired with concealment of testimony (shahādah) in the Qur'an — both are sins of the heart (ithm al-qalb) because they withhold what God has commanded to be made manifest.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal vs. metaphorical: the "bridle of fire" (lijām min nār) on the Day of Judgment is a metaphorical (majāz) embodiment of the inner restraint of truth — the concealed knowledge becomes a physical restraint in the afterlife.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد (Restriction & Specification) — The verse {وإن فريقا منهم ليكتمون الحق وهم يعلمون} employs the restrictive particle "inna" with the continuous verb form (yaktimūn) to specify an ongoing, willful concealment, distinguishing it from mere ignorance. The conditional structures in the ḥadīth "man taʿallama... man ʿallama... man katama" (whoever learns... whoever teaches... whoever conceals) follow the canonical pattern of protasis-apodosis (sharṭ/jazāʾ) that establishes a universal causal linkage between the act and its recompense.
2:283.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'Book of Knowledge'

3:18.arabic: شواهدها من القرآن قوله عز وجل شهد الله أنه لا إله إلا هو والملائكة وأولو العلم قائما بالقسط فانظر
3:18.english: That I have seen the desire of the students of knowledge to be sincere concerning jurisprudence (fiqh) — that [jurisprudence] which has become serviceable for those who fear not God (glorified and exalted be He), who arm themselves with it for vainglory and for seeking advantage through its prestige and station in rivalries. It is arranged in four quarters (arbāʿ). And one who clothes himself in the garb of the Beloved is beloved. So I did not deem it far-fetched that fashioning this book in the form of jurisprudence might be a gentle stratagem (talṭuf) for drawing hearts along by degrees. For this reason, one who sought to incline the hearts of princes to medicine gently devised it by setting it in the form of an astronomical almanac, arranged in tables and figures, and named it "The Almanac of Health" (taqwīm al-ṣiḥḥah) — so that their familiarity with that genre might draw them to perusal. And gentleness in drawing hearts to the knowledge that yields the life of eternity is more important than gentleness in drawing them to medicine, which yields only the health of the body. For the fruit of this knowledge is the healing of hearts and spirits, by which one attains to a life that endures for ever and ever (abad al-ābād). Where, then, is medicine — which treats bodies that are, by necessity, exposed to corruption in the nearest of times — in comparison to it?
3:18.section_title_en: The Book of Knowledge — Chapter One: On the Excellence of Knowledge, Teaching, and Learning
3:18.anchors:
- Root: كشف (kashafa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To unveil, disclose, remove a covering; كشف الغماء (removing distress); the uncovering of a thing from its covering.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-Mukāshafah (unveiling) in the theological sense is the direct apprehension of the unseen realities (ghayb) — the disclosure of the meaning of a thing as it truly is, without the intermediary of sensory perception or discursive reasoning.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): removing a physical covering. Metaphorical (majāz): the soul's attainment of spiritual realities by the lifting of the veil of sensory distraction.
- Root: عقل (ʿaql)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The intellect; originally, the rope by which a camel is tethered (ʿiqāl) — that which restrains and holds back; hence, the faculty that restrains the soul from base desires.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-ʿAql is that by which the rational soul (al-nafs al-nāṭiqah) apprehends the realities of things; it is the principle of discernment (tamyīz) and the ground of moral responsibility (taklīf).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the tethering of the camel. Metaphorical: the restraining of the soul from ignorance and passion; "He is one who possesses ʿaql" means he is restrained from error.
- Root: قلب (qalb)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The heart; the organ that fluctuates (yataqallab) between states; its very name derives from its constant turning over (taqlīb) of intentions and resolutions.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The heart is that subtle divine reality (al-laṭīfah al-rabbāniyyah) which is the seat of understanding (fahm) and knowledge (ʿilm); it is called qalb because of its rapid fluctuation (taqallub) between states of perception and heedlessness.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the physical organ. Metaphorical: the spiritual faculty of cognition and moral discernment — "the hearts of the knowers are the repositories of the secrets of God."
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Specification (Takhṣīṣ) via Conditional Partitioning (Taqsīm)
  * The author's division of knowledge into four parts follows the syntactic pattern of exhaustive binary partition (taqsīm thunāʾī), where each branch is specified by its defining predicate, yielding a complete and non-overlapping taxonomy — a structure Sibawayh recognizes as the rhetorical culmination of connected discourse (faṣl al-khiṭāb).
3:18.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications, prayers, and their spiritual power, from 'Book of Knowledge'

3:87.arabic: في ديننا ما ليس منه فهو رد (2) وفي خبر آخر من غش أمتي فعليه لعنة الله والملائكة والناس أجمعين قيل يا رسول الله وما غش أمتك قال أن يبتدع بدعة يحمل الناس عليها (3) وقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إن لله عز وجل ملكا ينادي كل يوم من خالف سنة رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لم تنله شفاعته (4) ومثال الجاني على الدين بإبداع ما يخالف السنة بالنسبة إلى من يذنب ذنبا مثال من عصى الملك في قلب دولته بالنسبة إلى من خالف أمره في خدمة معينة وذلك قد يغفر له فأما في قلب الدولة فلا وقال بعض العلماء ما تكلم فيه السلف فالسكوت عنه جفاء وما سكت عنه السلف فالكلام في
3:87.english: For this reason ʿAlī, may God be pleased with him, said — when it was said to him, "You have opposed so-and-so" — "The best of us is the most following of us of this religion." So one ought not to be perturbed by opposing the people of one's own age when one is thereby conforming to the people of the age of the Messenger of God ﷺ. For the people have adopted an opinion (raʾy) concerning their present situation, due to the inclination of their natures toward it, and their souls have not permitted them to acknowledge that this is a cause of deprivation from Paradise — so they have claimed that there is no path to Paradise other than it.
3:87.section_title_en: ** Section 64 — On the Sciences of the Inner Life: The Obligation to Follow the Salaf and the Condemnation of Innovation (Bidʿah)
3:87.anchors:
**
- Root: علم (ʿalima)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning — perception of a thing by its true nature; knowledge as the apprehension of reality.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "العلم: إدراك الشيء بحقيقته" — knowledge is the apprehension of a thing in its true reality, divided into apprehension of the essence and judgment upon the thing.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal usage — "ما علمت بخبرك: ما شعرت به" (I did not know of your news: I had no awareness of it). The scholar (ʿālim) is one whose knowledge is manifest in action.
- Root: بدع (badaʿa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning — to originate, to create something new without prior example.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الإبداع: إنشاء صنعة بلا احتذاء واقتداء" — origination of a thing without model or precedent. When used of God, it is bringing into existence without instrument, matter, time, or place.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — "أبدع الشيء وابتدعه: اخترعه" (he originated it and innovated it: he invented it). Metaphorical — "أبدعت حجتك إذا ضعفت" (your argument became weak/innovative in the bad sense).
- Root: حدث (ḥadatha)
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الحدوث: كون الشيء بعد أن لم يكن" — coming-to-be of a thing after it was not. "المحدث: ما أوجد بعد أن لم يكن" — the originated thing.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — "هو حدث من الأحداث" (he is a youth among youths). Metaphorical — "صاروا أحاديث" (they became [mere] tales). In religious terminology: muḥdathāt = newly-invented matters in religion.
- Root: هدى (hadā)
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Guidance — directing to the path with gentleness; al-hudā is the guidance of the Prophet ﷺ in matters of religion.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "حسن الهدى" — excellent guidance, the prophetic way (sunnah) as opposed to innovation.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — "إنما هما اثنتان: الكلام والهدى" restricts the two matters exclusively to speech and guidance, excluding all else.

3:159.arabic: لنت لهم ولو كنت فظا غليظ القلب لانفضوا من حولك ولقد كان يدعو أصحابه بكناهم إكراما لهم واستمالة لقلوبهم (9) ويكني من لم تكن له كنية فكان يدعى بما كناه به (10) ويكني أيضا النساء اللاتي لهن الأولاد واللاتي لم يلدن يبتدئ لهن الكنى (11) ويكني الصبيان فيستلين به قلوبهم (1) وكان أبعد الناس غضبا وأسرعهم رضا (2) وكان أرأف الناس بالناس وخير الناس للناس وأنفع الناس للناس (3) ولم تكن ترفع في مجلسه الأصوات (4) وكان إذا قام من مجلسه قال سبحانك اللهم وبحمدك أشهد أن لا إله إلا أنت أستغفرك وأتوب إليك {ثم ي
3:159.english: I say: Know that the perfection of repentance (tawbah) is not attained merely by the inward acts of regret and resolve, but by their manifestation in the character (khuluq) that the Prophet (peace be upon him) embodied — for he was the most perfect in repentance, the most complete in turning to God, and the most excellent in conduct toward creation. His very nature was a living repentance, for he was sent as a mercy, not as a curse. The Prophet (peace be upon him) said: "I was sent only as a mercy, and I was not sent as a curser." When he was asked to supplicate against a person — whether Muslim or disbeliever, general or specific — he would turn from supplicating against him to supplicating for him. He never struck anyone with his hand — neither a servant nor a woman — except when striving in the path of God, the Exalted. He never took revenge for anything done to him personally, except when a sanctity of God was violated — then his vengeance was for God's sake. He was never given a choice between two matters except that he chose the easier of them, unless it involved sin or the severing of kinship — then he was the most distant of people from it. Whenever anyone came to him — whether free, slave, or bondmaid — he would stand with him in his need. Anas (may God be pleased with him) said: "By Him who sent him with the truth, he never said to me regarding anything I did that he disliked, 'Why did you do that?' Nor did his wives rebuke me except that he would say: 'Leave him; this was only by a Book and a decree.'" They said: "The Messenger of God (peace be upon him) never found fault with a resting place — if they spread something for him, he lay upon it, and if they did not spread anything, he lay upon the bare earth." God, the Exalted, described him in the Torah before His sending him, in the first line, saying: "Muhammad is My Messenger, My chosen servant — neither harsh nor coarse, nor clamorous in the marketplaces; he does not repay evil with evil, but rather pardons and forgives. His birth is in Mecca, his emigration is in Ṭābah (Medina), and his dominion is in Syria. He and those with him gird themselves at the waist, callers to the Qur'an and knowledge; they perform ablution upon their extremities." Likewise, He described him in the Gospel.
3:159.section_title_en: The Book of Repentance — Section 562: The Prophet's Character as the Model of Repentance and Forbearance
3:159.anchors:
- Root: جلس (jalasa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning is "to sit," but the root extends to "a rugged, elevated land" (jals) — the place where one establishes one's seat; also "a sturdy, firm she-camel" (jals), indicating firmness of posture and resolve.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "The origin of jalsa is the rugged ground, and the elevated plateau was called jals for that reason... Then sitting (julūs) was made for every act of remaining seated, and majlis is every place where a person sits."
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): "He has a good posture of sitting (jilsah)." Metaphorical (Majaz): "He is the companion of his own self (jalis nafsihi)" — i.e., one who is given to solitude and withdrawal, a state befitting the penitent.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Restriction and Focused Predication (al-ḥaṣr wa al-taqyīd bi-innamā) — governing the Prophet's exclusive attributes, e.g., "he was not sent but as a mercy," restricting the purpose of his mission.

3:159.arabic: يتوكل على الله فهو حسبه وقال سبحانه وتعالى إن الله يحب المتوكلين وأعظم بمقام موسوم بمحبة الله تعالى صاحبه ومضمون كفاية الله تعالى ملابسه فمن الله تعالى حسبه وكافيه ومحبه ومراعيه فقد فاز الفوز العظيم فإن المحبوب لا يعذب ولا يبعد ولا يحجب وقال تعالى أليس الله بكاف عبده فطالب الكفاية من غيره والتارك للتوكل هو المكذب لهذه الآية فإنه سؤال في معرض استنطاق بالحق كقوله تعالى هل أتى على الإنسان حين من الدهر لم يكن شيئا مذكورا وقال عز وجل ومن يتوكل على الله فإن الله عزيز حكيم أي عزيز لا يذل من استجار به ولا يضيع م
3:159.english: Praise be to God, the Disposer of the dominion (mulk) and the spiritual sovereignty (malakūt), the One alone in majesty (ʿizzah) and omnipotence (jabarūt), Who raised the heaven without any pillar, and apportioned therein the provisions of His servants; Who turned the eyes of those possessed of hearts and intellects away from the observation of intermediaries and causes (al-wasāʾiṭ wa-l-asbāb) toward the Causer of causes (musabbib al-asbāb); and Who lifted their concern from turning toward anything other than Him, and from relying upon any disposer besides Him. Thus they worshipped none but Him alone — in knowledge that He is the One, the Unique, the Eternal Refuge (al-ṣamad), the God — and in verification that all classes of creatures are servants like themselves, from whom no provision is sought, and that there is no atom but God created it, and no beast but upon God is its sustenance. When they verified that He is the Guarantor of His servants' provision and the Surety for it, they relied upon Him and said: {«حسبنا الله ونعم الوكيل»} — "God is sufficient for us, and what an excellent Guardian!" (Q. 3:173).
3:159.section_title_en: The Book of Divine Unity (Tawḥīd) and Reliance (Tawakkul) — Book Five of the Quarter of Deliverance from The Revival of the Religious Sciences
3:159.anchors:
- Root: وكل (w-k-l)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of delegating, entrusting, and appointing a deputy (wakīl) to manage one's affairs.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "التوكيل: أن تعتمد على غيرك وتجعله نائبا عنك" — Reliance (tawakkul) is the act of depending upon another and making him a deputy over your affair; its theological force is that God alone is the sufficient Guardian (wakīl), as in {«وكفى بالله وكيلا»}.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): appointing an agent; Metaphorical (majāz): the weak man who leans on others (وكل ووكلة تكلة). In the divine context, tawakkul is a real, not figurative, transfer of one's trust to God as the sole efficient cause.
- Root: سبب (s-b-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: A rope, cord, or means by which one ascends or reaches something; extended to any intermediary cause.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "سمي كل ما يتوصل به إلى شيء سببا" — Every means by which one reaches a goal is termed a cause (sabab); God is the "Musabbib al-Asbāb" (Causer of causes), transcending the causal ropes He suspends.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: a physical cord; Metaphorical: any linkage or connection. Here, the "gaze upon causes" (mulāḥaẓat al-asbāb) is a metaphorical veiling of the true Agent.
- Root: حسب (ḥ-s-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To count, reckon, suffice; derived: ḥasb (sufficiency), ḥasīb (one who suffices, or the Reckoner).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الحساب: استعمال العدد" — Counting; but in the divine attribute, "ḥasb" denotes God's all-sufficient guardianship, as in {«حسبنا الله ونعم الوكيل»}.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: reckoning by number; Metaphorical: "احتسبت ما عند فلان: اختبرته وسبرته" — to test and probe. God's being "Ḥasb" for the believer is a tested, verified sufficiency, not a mere claim.
- Root: غمض (gh-m-d)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To close the eye, to be obscure, low-lying, or hidden ground.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "يستعار للتغافل والتساهل" — closing the eye is metaphorically used for overlooking; here, the "ghumūḍ" (obscurity) of tawakkul is its conceptual hiddenness from the intellect.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: a low, concealed place; Metaphorical: "أمر غامض" — a subtle, difficult affair. The text uses it for the doctrinal opacity of tawakkul.
- Sibawayh Rule: Interposition of the prepositional phrase (باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور) — The periodic structure "فلم يعبدوا إلا إياه" and "فقالوا حسبنا الله" shows the separation of the operative verb from its object for rhetorical emphasis, permissible where the pause is complete and the meaning remains unbroken.
3:159.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Monotheism and Reliance'

3:159.arabic: فمن قوله تعالى فبما رحمة من الله لنت لهم وأما الزهد فمن قوله تعالى وقال الذين أوتوا العلم ويلكم ثواب الله خير لمن آمن وعمل صالحا ولما تلا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قوله تعالى فمن يرد الله أن يهديه يشرح صدره للإسلام فقيل له ما هذا الشرح فقال إن النور إذا قذف في القلب انشرح له الصدر وانفسح قيل فهل لذلك من علامة قال صلى الله عليه وسلم نعم التجافي عن دار الغرور والإنابة إلى دار الخلود والاستعداد للموت قبل نزوله (2) ومنها أن يكون أكثر بحثه عن علم الأعمال وعما يفسدها ويشوش القلوب ويهيج الو
3:159.english: As for the fear (al-khashyah), it is from His saying, the Exalted: {«إِنَّمَا يَخْشَى اللَّهَ مِنْ عِبَادِهِ الْعُلَمَاءُ»} — "Only those of His servants who possess knowledge fear Allah" (Fāṭir 35:28). For khashyah is a fear suffused with veneration, and it arises only from knowledge of the Mighty and Majestic — for whoever knows Him fears Him, and whoever does not know Him does not fear Him.
3:159.section_title_en: The Book of God's Book — Fear, Humility, and the Preference for the Hereafter
3:159.anchors:
- Root: خشع (Khasha'a)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of lowliness, submissiveness, and being lowered to the ground.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الخشوع: الضراعة" — Khushū' is a state of supplication and humility; most often used for what appears on the limbs, while ḍarā'ah is for the heart. When the heart humbles, the limbs follow.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): "خشع له وتخشع: ذل وتطامن" — to be lowly and submissive. Metaphorical (Majaz): "أرض خاشعة" — a land that is low-lying; "خشعت الأصوات" — voices lowered in awe.
- Root: خشي (Khashiya)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Fear mixed with awe and reverence.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الخشية: خوف يشوبه تعظيم" — Khashyah is fear suffused with veneration, and it most often arises from knowledge of what is feared.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Distinguished from mere fear (khawf) by its component of reverential awe.
- Root: خلق (Khuluq)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Inherent disposition, character, nature.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الخلق أصله: التقدير المستقيم" — Its root is right measure and proportion; used for the creation of things and for the moral constitution of the soul.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "خلق الخراز الأديم" — the leather-worker cutting and measuring hide before cutting. Metaphorical: "خلق الله الخلق" — God originated creation upon a measure required by wisdom; "وله خلق حسن" — he has beautiful character.
- Root: زهد (Zuhd)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Abstinence, renunciation, disinclination.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الزاهد في الشيء: الراغب عنه والراضي منه بالزهيد" — The ascetic is one who turns away from a thing and is content with little of it.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "زهد في الشيء: رغب عنه" — to turn away from something. Metaphorical: "واد زهيد" — a valley that takes little water; "رجل زهيد" — a man of little good.
- Sibawayh Rule: Restriction and Focused Predication (باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما) — The particle "innamā" restricts the predicate to the subject alone, establishing a definitive causal linkage between knowledge and reverential fear.
3:159.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Book of Knowledge'

3:187.arabic: علماء الآخرة بالخشوع والزهد فقال عز وجل في علماء الدنيا وإذ أخذ الله ميثاق الذين أوتوا الكتاب لتبيننه للناس ولا تكتمونه فنبذوه وراء ظهورهم واشتروا به ثمنا قليلا وقال تعالى في علماء الآخرة وإن من أهل الكتاب لمن يؤمن بالله وما أنزل إليكم وما أنزل إليهم خاشعين لله لا يشترون بآيات الله ثمنا قليلا أولئك لهم أجرهم عند ربهم وقال بعض السلف العلماء يحشرون في زمرة الأنبياء والقضاة يحشرون في زمرة السلاطين وفي معنى القضاة كل فقيه قصده طلب الدنيا بعلمه وروى أبو الدرداء رضي الله عنه عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال أوحى الله عز وجل إلى بعض الأنبياء قل للذين يتفقهون لغير الدين ويتعلمون لغير العمل ويطلبون الدنيا بع
3:187.english:
[Root: ملح]
  • Lisan al-Arab: "الملح: ما يصلح الطعام، وجمعه ملوح وأملاح. والمليح: الحسن. والملاحة: الحسن. وملح الرجل يملح ملاحة: حسن. وتملح: تزين."
  • Al-Raghib (Al-Mufradat): "الملح: ما يحفظ الطعام ويمنع فساده، ويستعار لما يحفظ الإيمان والعلم من الفساد."
  • Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "ملح الماء: إذا كان فيه ملوحة. وملح الطعام: جعل فيه الملح. وهذا على الحقيقة، ويستعار الملح لما يصلح به الأمر."
  • Kitab al-Ayn: "الملح: معروف، والمليح: الحسن من كل شيء."
3:187.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Book of Knowledge'

3:187.arabic: ميثاق الذين أوتوا الكتاب لتبيننه للناس ولا تكتمونه فنبذوه وراء ظهورهم واشتروا به ثمنا قليلا وقال تعالى في علماء الآخرة وإن من أهل الكتاب لمن يؤمن بالله وما أنزل إليكم وما أنزل إليهم خاشعين لله لا يشترون بآيات الله ثمنا قليلا أولئك لهم أجرهم عند ربهم وقال بعض السلف العلماء يحشرون في زمرة الأنبياء والقضاة يحشرون في زمرة السلاطين وفي معنى القضاة كل فقيه قصده طلب الدنيا بعلمه وروى أبو الدرداء رضي الله عنه عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال أوحى الله عز وجل إلى بعض الأنبياء قل للذين يتفقهو
3:187.english:
[Root: ملح]
  • Lisan al-Arab: "الملح: ما يصلح الطعام، وجمعه ملوح وأملاح. والمليح: الحسن. والملاحة: الحسن. وملح الرجل يملح ملاحة: حسن. وتملح: تزين."
  • Al-Raghib (Al-Mufradat): "الملح: ما يحفظ الطعام ويمنع فساده، ويستعار لما يحفظ الإيمان والعلم من الفساد."
  • Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "ملح الماء: إذا كان فيه ملوحة. وملح الطعام: جعل فيه الملح. وهذا على الحقيقة، ويستعار الملح لما يصلح به الأمر."
  • Kitab al-Ayn: "الملح: معروف، والمليح: الحسن من كل شيء."
3:187.topic: Al-Ghazali on the journey of the soul, death, and the Hereafter, from 'The Lawful and Prohibited'

3:187.arabic: وقوله تعالى وإذ أخذ الله ميثاق الذين أوتوا الكتاب ليبيننه للناس ولا يكتمونه وهو إيجاب للتعليم وقوله تعالى {وإن فريقا منهم ليكتمون الحق وهم يعلمون} وهو تحريم للكتمان كما قال تعالى في الشهادة {ومن يكتمها فإنه آثم قلبه} وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم ما آتى الله عالما علما إلا وأخذ عليه من الميثاق ما أخذ على النبيين أن يبينوه للناس ولا يكتموه (6) وقال تعالى {ومن أحسن قولا ممن دعا إلى الله وعمل صالحا} وقال تعالى {ادع إلى سبيل ربك بالحكمة والموعظة الحسنة} وقال تعالى {ويعلمهم الكتاب والحكمة} وأما الأخبار فقوله صلى الله عليه و
3:187.english: As for the Qur'anic verses: His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: {وَلِيُنذِرُوا قَوْمَهُمْ إِذَا رَجَعُوا إِلَيْهِمْ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَحْذَرُونَ} "That they may warn their people when they return to them, that perhaps they may be cautious" {«ولينذروا قومهم إذا رجعوا إليهم لعلهم يحذرون»} — and the intended meaning is teaching and guidance (al-taʿlīm wa-al-irshād).
3:187.anchors:
- Root: علم (ʿalima)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning is "to know, to perceive a thing by its reality"; the root also carries the sense of "marker, sign, banner" — that by which something is distinguished and recognized.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "العلم: إدراك الشيء بحقيقته" — knowledge is the apprehension of a thing by its true reality, divided into apprehension of the essence of a thing and judgment upon it. This is the attribute by which the scholar (ʿālim) is distinguished and by which he becomes a "sign" (ʿalam) pointing to truth.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): "هو من أعلام العلم الخافقه" — the scholar is among the lofty banners of knowledge. The teaching act makes the scholar a living signpost; the root's literal sense of "marking" or "branding" a thing carries into the metaphorical (majāz) register of "imprinting" knowledge upon hearts.
- Root: حدث (ḥadatha)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning is "to be new, to occur after not having been"; al-ḥadīth is speech that is new and conveyed.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الحدوث: كون الشيء بعد أن لم يكن" — origination after non-existence. The prophetic traditions (aḥādīth) cited here are "newly conveyed" reports that carry authority.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Metaphorical (majāz): "صاروا أحاديث" — they became subjects of discourse. The transmission of knowledge is an "event" (ḥadath) that occurs in the listener, renewing his state.
- Root: عهد (ʿahida)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning is "covenant, pact, charge"; al-ʿahd is a binding commission that one is obligated to fulfill.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The covenant (mīthāq) taken from the People of the Book and from the scholars is a divine charge (taklīf) that makes teaching an obligation, not a supererogatory act.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the covenant is a "charge entrusted" (waṣiyyah) that binds the one who receives knowledge to its dissemination.
- Root: كتم (katama)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning is "to conceal, to hide"; al-kitmān is the deliberate suppression of what ought to be revealed.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Concealment of knowledge is paired with concealment of testimony (shahādah) in the Qur'an — both are sins of the heart (ithm al-qalb) because they withhold what God has commanded to be made manifest.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal vs. metaphorical: the "bridle of fire" (lijām min nār) on the Day of Judgment is a metaphorical (majāz) embodiment of the inner restraint of truth — the concealed knowledge becomes a physical restraint in the afterlife.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد (Restriction & Specification) — The verse {وإن فريقا منهم ليكتمون الحق وهم يعلمون} employs the restrictive particle "inna" with the continuous verb form (yaktimūn) to specify an ongoing, willful concealment, distinguishing it from mere ignorance. The conditional structures in the ḥadīth "man taʿallama... man ʿallama... man katama" (whoever learns... whoever teaches... whoever conceals) follow the canonical pattern of protasis-apodosis (sharṭ/jazāʾ) that establishes a universal causal linkage between the act and its recompense.
3:187.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'Book of Knowledge'

3:187.arabic: والمعرض عن العمل به أريد بقوله عز وجل فنبذوه وراء ظهورهم واشتروا به ثمنا قليلا فبئس ما يشترون ولذلك قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم اقرءوا القرآن ما ائتلفت عليه قلوبكم ولانت له جلودكم فإذا اختلفتم فلستم تقرءونه وفي بعضها فإذا اختلفتم فقوموا عنه (2) قال الله تعالى الذين إذا ذكر الله وجلت قلوبهم وإذا تليت عليهم آياته زادتهم إيمانا وعلى ربهم يتوكلون وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم إن أحسن الناس صوتا بالقرآن الذي إذا سمعته يقرأ رأيت أنه يخشى الله تعالى (3) وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم لا يسمع القرآن من أحد أشهى ممن يخشى الله عز وجل (4) يراد لاستجلاب هذه ا
3:187.english: For this reason, Yūsuf ibn Asbāṭ said: "I intend to recite the Qur'an, but when I recall what is in it, I fear abhorrence (al-maqt), so I turn instead to glorification (al-tasbīḥ) and seeking forgiveness (al-istighfār)."
3:187.section_title_en: ** The Revival of the Religious Sciences — Section 231: On the Inward Conditions of Qur'anic Recitation (Continued)
3:187.anchors:
**
- Root: وجل (w-j-l)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الوجل: استشعار الخوف" — the stirring of fear/apprehension within
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الوجل: استشعار الخوف. يقال: وجل يوجل وجلا، فهو وجل. قال تعالى: {إنما المؤمنون الذين إذا ذكر الله وجلت قلوبهم}" — the theological state of the heart's trembling upon remembrance of God
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): "رجل وجل، وقوم وجال، وقد وجل وجلا" — the physical/emotional state of fear. Metaphorical (Majaz): The heart's trembling as the seat of spiritual perception
- Root: قلب (q-l-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "قلب الشيء: تصريفه وصرفه عن وجه إلى وجه" — turning and transforming
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "قلب الشيء: تصريفه وصرفه عن وجه إلى وجه، كقلب الثوب، وقلب الإنسان" — the heart as that which is constantly turning/transforming between states
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "قلب الشيء قلبا: حوله عن وجهه" — physical turning. Metaphorical: "قلب المعلم الصبيان: صرفهم إلى بيوتهم" — the heart's turning toward or away from spiritual realities
- Root: نفس (n-f-s)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The self, soul, spirit — that which is breathed
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "النفس: الروح" — the soul as the animating principle; also the self as the locus of blameworthy attributes
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "شيء نفيس ومنفس" — preciousness. Metaphorical: "دفق نفسه أي دمه" — the self as that which must be transcended in spiritual realization
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد (Restriction & Focused Predication) — governing the precise delimitation of spiritual states (أحوال) and their hierarchical gradation (درجات)

3:199.arabic: واشتروا به ثمنا قليلا وقال تعالى في علماء الآخرة وإن من أهل الكتاب لمن يؤمن بالله وما أنزل إليكم وما أنزل إليهم خاشعين لله لا يشترون بآيات الله ثمنا قليلا أولئك لهم أجرهم عند ربهم وقال بعض السلف العلماء يحشرون في زمرة الأنبياء والقضاة يحشرون في زمرة السلاطين وفي معنى القضاة كل فقيه قصده طلب الدنيا بعلمه وروى أبو الدرداء رضي الله عنه عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال أوحى الله عز وجل إلى بعض الأنبياء قل للذين يتفقهون لغير الدين ويتعلمون لغير العمل ويطلبون الدنيا بعمل الآخرة يلبسون للناس مسوك الكباش وقلوبهم كقلوب الذئاب ألسنتهم أحلى من العسل وقلوبهم أمر من الصبر إياي يخادعون وبي يستهزئون لأفتحن لهم فتنة تذر الحليم حيران
3:199.english:
[Root: ملح]
  • Lisan al-Arab: "الملح: ما يصلح الطعام، وجمعه ملوح وأملاح. والمليح: الحسن. والملاحة: الحسن. وملح الرجل يملح ملاحة: حسن. وتملح: تزين."
  • Al-Raghib (Al-Mufradat): "الملح: ما يحفظ الطعام ويمنع فساده، ويستعار لما يحفظ الإيمان والعلم من الفساد."
  • Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "ملح الماء: إذا كان فيه ملوحة. وملح الطعام: جعل فيه الملح. وهذا على الحقيقة، ويستعار الملح لما يصلح به الأمر."
  • Kitab al-Ayn: "الملح: معروف، والمليح: الحسن من كل شيء."
3:199.topic: Al-Ghazali on purifying the character, moral diseases, and spiritual remedies, from 'Book of Knowledge'

3:199.arabic: يؤمن بالله وما أنزل إليكم وما أنزل إليهم خاشعين لله لا يشترون بآيات الله ثمنا قليلا أولئك لهم أجرهم عند ربهم وقال بعض السلف العلماء يحشرون في زمرة الأنبياء والقضاة يحشرون في زمرة السلاطين وفي معنى القضاة كل فقيه قصده طلب الدنيا بعلمه وروى أبو الدرداء رضي الله عنه عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال أوحى الله عز وجل إلى بعض الأنبياء قل للذين يتفقهون لغير الدين ويتعلمون لغير العمل ويطلبون الدنيا بعمل الآخرة يلبسون للناس مسوك الكباش وقلوبهم كقلوب الذئاب ألسنتهم أحلى من العسل وقلوبهم أمر من الصبر إياي يخادعون وبي يستهزئون لأفتحن
3:199.english:
[Root: ملح]
  • Lisan al-Arab: "الملح: ما يصلح الطعام، وجمعه ملوح وأملاح. والمليح: الحسن. والملاحة: الحسن. وملح الرجل يملح ملاحة: حسن. وتملح: تزين."
  • Al-Raghib (Al-Mufradat): "الملح: ما يحفظ الطعام ويمنع فساده، ويستعار لما يحفظ الإيمان والعلم من الفساد."
  • Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "ملح الماء: إذا كان فيه ملوحة. وملح الطعام: جعل فيه الملح. وهذا على الحقيقة، ويستعار الملح لما يصلح به الأمر."
  • Kitab al-Ayn: "الملح: معروف، والمليح: الحسن من كل شيء."

4:5.arabic: {ولا تؤتوا السفهاء أموالكم} تنبيها على أن حفظ العلم ممن يفسده ويضره أولى وليس الظلم في إعطاء غير المستحق بأقل من الظلم في منع المستحق أأنثر درا بين سارحة النعم .
4:5.english: I say: Leave the reins and go. For if one comes who comprehends, and you have concealed it from him, then let him bridle me — for God Most High has said: {«ولا تؤتوا السفهاء أموالكم»} — "And do not give the foolish your wealth" — as an indication that preserving knowledge from one who would corrupt it and harm it is even more incumbent. And wrongdoing in giving to one who is not deserving is no less than wrongdoing in withholding from one who is deserving.
4:5.section_title_en: The Book of the Revival of the Religious Sciences — Section 48: On the Etiquette of the Teacher and the Learner (Continued), and the Exposition of the Marks Distinguishing the Scholars of the Hereafter from the Evil Scholars
4:5.anchors:
- Root: علم (ʿalima)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Knowledge as the apprehension of a thing in its true reality; the root also carries the sense of a mark or sign (ʿalam) by which something is known.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Knowledge is of two kinds: apprehension of the essence of a thing, and judgment upon a thing affirming or denying something of it. The first is transitive to one object; the second to two.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal usage: "He is a sign (ʿalam) of knowledge" — i.e., a distinguished landmark. Metaphorical: "The traces (maʿālim) of the road" — the vestiges by which one is guided.
- Root: ظلم (ẓalama)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To place something in other than its proper place; darkness (ẓulmah) as the privation of light.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Darkness is the absence of light; figuratively used for ignorance, polytheism, and wickedness, just as light is used for their opposites.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "He wronged and was wronged" — to suffer injustice. Metaphorical: "Wrongdoing is darkness, just as justice is light" — for the wrongdoer acts in the darkness of his own soul.
- Root: منع (manaʿa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To withhold, to prevent, to protect; a fortress (manīʿah) is that which defends.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Used in opposition to giving; also used for protection, as in "a fortified place" (makān manīʿ).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "He prevented him from the thing." Metaphorical: "He protects the neighbor" — i.e., defends him from harm.
- Root: عقل (ʿaqala)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The intellect; originally to bind or restrain (as a camel is hobbled), hence the faculty that restrains the soul from base desires.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The intellect is the faculty prepared for the reception of knowledge, and also the knowledge acquired by that faculty.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "I have not done so since I attained reason." Metaphorical: "A palm tree that does not accept pollination" — i.e., does not receive what is offered to it.
- Sibawayh Rule: The Interposition of the Prepositional Phrase (al-faṣl bayna al-jār wa al-majrūr) — governing the permissible separation between a governing word and its governed prepositional phrase where the intervening element is syntactically complete, as in the construction "Leave the reins and go" (itruk al-lijām wa-idhhab), where the imperative governs two successive clauses without ellipsis.
4:5.topic: Classical commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya Ulum al-Din, from 'Book of Knowledge'

4:83.arabic: تعالى {ولو ردوه إلى الرسول وإلى أولي الأمر منهم لعلمه الذين يستنبطونه منهم} رد حكمه في الوقائع إلى استنباطهم وألحق رتبتهم برتبة الأنبياء في كشف حكم الله وقيل في قوله تعالى يا بني آدم قد أنزلنا عليكم لباسا يواري سوءاتكم يعني العلم وريشا يعني اليقين ولباس التقوى يعني الحياء وقال عز وجل {ولقد جئناهم بكتاب فصلناه على علم} وقال تعالى {فلنقصن عليهم بعلم} وقال عز وجل {بل هو آيات بينات في صدور الذين أوتوا العلم} وقال تعالى {خلق الإنسان علمه البيان} وإنما ذكر ذلك في معرض الامتنان وأما الأخبار فقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
4:83.english: How He, Glorified and Exalted, began with Himself, then seconded with the angels, and thirded with the people of knowledge — and sufficient for you is this as honor, excellence, splendor, and nobility. And God, Exalted, said: {«يرفع الله الذين آمنوا منكم والذين أوتوا العلم درجات»} — "God will raise those who have believed among you and those who have been given knowledge, in degrees." Ibn ʿAbbās, may God be pleased with them both, said: For the scholars there are degrees above the believers, seven hundred degrees, and between each two degrees is a distance of five hundred years' journey.
4:83.section_title_en: The Book of Knowledge — Section 4: The Excellence of Knowledge and the Scholars
4:83.anchors:
- Root: علم (ʿ-l-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root meaning of knowing, perceiving a thing in its true reality; the act of apprehension and judgment.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "العلم: إدراك الشيء بحقيقته" — knowledge is the apprehension of a thing in its true reality, divided into apprehension of the essence and judgment of existence or non-existence.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) usage denotes genuine knowing; metaphorical (majāz) usage extends to signs, landmarks, and traces that guide to knowledge.
- Root: درج (d-r-j)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Degrees, steps, ascending stations; the root denotes gradation and progressive elevation.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الدرجة نحو المنزلة، لكن يقال للمنزلة: درجة إذا اعتبرت بالصعود" — a degree is a station considered by ascent, not horizontal extension.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical steps of ascent. Metaphorical: "لفلان درجة رفيعة" — lofty rank; "امش في مدارج الحق" — walk in the paths of truth.
- Root: يوم (y-w-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: A day; a period of time from sunrise to sunset, or any duration whatsoever.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "اليوم يعبر به عن وقت طلوع الشمس إلى غروبها. وقد يعبر به عن مدة من الزمان أي مدة كانت" — the day denotes the time of the sun's rising to its setting, and may denote any period of time whatsoever.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the solar day. Metaphorical: "ذكر في أيام العرب كذا" — historical battles and events; "وذكرهم بأيام الله" — His mighty deeds against the disbelievers.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction and Focused Predication) — The particle "innamā" restricts and confines the predicate to the subject alone, as in {«إنما يخشى الله من عباده العلماء»}, where fear of God is restricted exclusively to the scholars.
4:83.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Book of Knowledge'

4:83.arabic: والرابع أنه قال عز وجل لعلمه الذي يستنبطونه منهم فأثبت لأهل العلم استنباطا ومعلوم أنه وراء السماع وجملة ما نقلناه من الآثار في فهم القرآن يناقض هذا الخيال فبطل أن يشترط السماع في التأويل وجاز لكل واحد أن يستنبط من القرآن بقدر فهمه وحد عقله وأما النهي فإنه ينزل على أحد وجهين أحدهما أن يكون له في الشيء رأي وإليه ميل من طبعه وهواه فيتأول القرآن على وفق رأيه وهواه وليحتج على تصحيح غرضه ولو لم يكن له ذلك الرأي والهوى لكان لا يلوح له من القرآن ذلك المعنى وهذا تارة يكون مع العلم كالذي يحتج ببعض آ
4:83.english: I say: The Prophet (peace be upon him) was asked about the means of deliverance from these trials, and he said: "The Book of Allah — act by what is in it, for it is that which delivers one from them." The questioner repeated this three times, and he (peace be upon him) said three times: "Learn the Book of Allah, Mighty and Glorious, and act by what is in it, for in it is deliverance."
4:83.section_title_en: The Book of the Etiquette of Recitation — Section 233: On Understanding the Meanings of the Qur'an and the Limits of Interpretation
4:83.anchors:
- Root: ف-ه-م (f-h-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الفهم: هيئة للإنسان بها يتحقق معاني ما يحسن" — comprehension as an inherent faculty by which one ascertains meanings
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الفهم: هيئة للإنسان بها يتحقق معاني ما يحسن... وأفهمته: إذا قلت له حتى تصوره" — comprehension is a cognitive disposition; distinction between understanding (fahm) and making understood (ifhām)
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "تقول: من لم يؤت من سوء الفهم أتى من سوء الإفهام" — literal usage; failure of understanding often stems from failure of communication
- Root: ف-س-ر (f-s-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "وكل شيء يعرف به تفسير الشيء ومعناه، فهو تَفْسِرَتُه" — that by which a thing's meaning is made known
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "التفسير قد يقال فيما يختص بمفردات الألفاظ وغريبها، وفيما يختص بالتأويل" — tafsīr concerns lexical surface; taʾwīl concerns deeper meaning
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "هذا كلام يحتاج إلى فسر وتفسير" — literal: exposition of what is obscure
- Root: و-ج-ل (w-j-l)
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الوجل: استشعار الخوف" — the sensing of fear; used of hearts trembling at divine mention
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "لو واجلت فلانا لوجلته: لغلبته في الوجل" — literal sense of fear; metaphorical extension to overpowering in fear
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — the particle innamā restricts predication, essential for parsing the Prophet's saying "innamā al-aʿmālu bi-l-niyyāt" and analogous restrictive formulations in the ḥadīth cited herein
4:83.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'Etiquette of Quran Recitation'

4:145.arabic: علم ولذلك قال الله عز وجل إن المنافقين في الدرك الأسفل من النار لأنهم جحدوا بعد العلم وجعل اليهود شرا من النصارى مع أنهم ما جعلوا لله سبحانه ولدا ولا قالوا إنه ثالث ثلاثة إلا أنهم أنكروا بعد المعرفة إذ قال الله يعرفونه كما يعرفون أبناءهم وقال تعالى فلما جاءهم ما عرفوا كفروا به فلعنة الله على الكافرين وقال تعالى في قصة بلعام بن باعوراء واتل عليهم نبأ الذي آتيناه آياتنا فانسلخ منها فأتبعه الشيطان فكان من الغاوين حتى قال فمثله كمثل الكلب إن تحمل عليه يلهث أو تتركه يلهث فكذلك العالم الفاجر فإن بلعام أوتي كتاب
4:145.english: I say: The Prophet — peace and blessings be upon him — said: "The scholar will indeed be tormented with a torment at which the inhabitants of the Fire will circle around, marveling at the severity of his punishment." By it he meant the wicked scholar.
4:145.section_title_en: The Worldly Scholar's Punishment and the Marks of the Hereafter-Scholars
4:145.anchors:
- Root: فجر (fajara)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To split, cleave, or rend something widely; to break open
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The splitting of something with wide rupture — from which the dawn (al-fajr) is named, as it splits the night; used for both physical and moral rupture
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the cleaving of water or the breaking of dawn. Metaphorical: the eruption of punishment upon one suddenly and overwhelmingly
- Root: علم (ʿalima)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Knowledge; the faculty of apprehending a thing as it truly is
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Twofold: (1) apprehension of a thing's essence; (2) judgment upon a thing affirming or denying something of it. The scholar (al-ʿālim) is one who possesses such apprehension
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: knowledge as certain apprehension. Metaphorical: the "signs" (maʿālim) of the path — that by which one is guided; the scholar is a "sign" pointing either to guidance or to ruin
- Root: دنا (dana)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To be near, to draw close; al-dunyā (the nearer world) as that which is immediate and low
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Proximity by essence or by judgment; used of place, time, and station. The "nearer" (al-adnā) is contrasted with the greater and the better
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: nearness. Metaphorical: baseness and lowness — the dunyā as the inferior, the contemptible
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — The particle innamā restricts the predicate exclusively to its subject, as in "the winners and the brought-near are only the scholars of the Hereafter," effecting complete exclusion of all else.
4:145.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'Book of Knowledge'

5:7.arabic: ولذلك قال عز وجل لعلهم يتذكرون وليتذكر أولوا الألباب واذكروا نعمة الله عليكم وميثاقه الذي واثقكم به ولقد يسرنا القرآن للذكر فهل من مدكر وتسمية هذا النمط تذكرا ليس ببعيد فكأن التذكر ضربان أحدهما أن يذكر صورة كانت حاضرة الوجود في قلبه لكن غابت بعد الوجود الآخر والآخر أن يذكر صورة كانت مضمنة فيه بالفطرة وهذه حقائق ظاهرة للناظر بنور البصيرة ثقيلة على من يستروجه (1) السماع والتقليد دون الكشف والعيان ولذلك تراه يتخبط في مثل هذه الآيات ويتعسف وفي تأويل التذكر بإقرار النفوس أنواعا من التعسفات ويتخايل إليه في الأخبار والآيات ضروب من المناقضات وربما يغل
5:7.english: I say: Know that the washing of the eye is forbidden — that is, the eye of insight (ʿayn al-baṣīrah) is not to be washed with the water of blind imitation and mere hearsay, for it is the organ by which the realities of the intellect are disclosed. And the divisions of what the name "intellect" (al-ʿaql) is applied to have become clear: it is said of the inborn faculty (al-gharīzah), and it is said of the knowledge that is acquired through that faculty, and it is said of the state of that knowledge when it governs the soul, and it is said of the very actions that proceed from that governance.
5:7.section_title_en: The Washing of the Eye is Forbidden — On the True Meaning of Intellect (ʿAql) and Its Divisions
5:7.anchors:
- Root: عقل (ʿAql)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The root denotes binding, restraining, and holding back — the intellect is that which restrains the soul from base desires and prevents it from straying.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "العقل يقال للقوة المتهيئة لقبول العلم، ويقال للعلم الذي يستفيده الإنسان بتلك القوة عقل" — al-ʿaql is said of the faculty prepared to receive knowledge, and it is also said of the knowledge acquired by that faculty. It is the instrument of divine discernment and the locus of taklīf (moral responsibility).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): the inborn faculty of discernment. Metaphorical (Majaz): "نخلة لا تعقل الإبار إذا لم تقبله" — a palm tree that does not accept pollination is said to be "not to ʿaqil" the pollen, extending the root to the sense of "accepting/receiving." Thus, knowledge is called ʿaql metaphorically as its fruit.
- Root: بصر (Baṣar)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Sight, perception — both of the eye and of the heart.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "البصر يقال للجارحة الناظرة... ويقال لقوة القلب المدركة: بصيرة وبصر" — baṣar is said of the seeing organ, and of the perceiving power of the heart: baṣīrah and baṣar. The inner sight (baṣīrah) perceives immaterial realities.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: ocular vision. Metaphorical: "هذه آية مبصرة" — this is an illuminating sign; "واجعلني بصيرة عليهم أي رقيبا وشاهدا" — make me a watcher over them. The inner eye perceives what the outer eye cannot.
- Root: فطر (Faṭara)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To split, cleave, originate, create — the primordial act of divine creation.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "أصل الفطر: الشق طولا... وفطر الله الخلق" — the root is splitting lengthwise; God's "fatr" of creation is His originating of things. "فطرة الله التي فطر الناس عليها" — the primordial disposition upon which God originated mankind.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "فطر الله الخلق، وهو فاطر السموات: مبتدعها" — God originated creation; He is the Originator of the heavens. "وكل مولود يولد على الفطرة" — every newborn is born upon the fiṭrah, i.e., the innate disposition receptive to the religion of truth.
- Root: نفس (Nafs)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Self, soul, spirit; the innermost reality of a thing.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "النفس: الروح... وقوله: تعلم ما في نفسي ولا أعلم ما في نفسك" — nafs is the spirit/soul; "You know what is in my nafs and I know not what is in Your nafs" — the nafs is the seat of inner assent and recognition.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the self. Metaphorical: "دفق نفسه أي دمه" — he poured out his nafs, i.e., his blood. The nafs is the locus of the primordial covenant (mīthāq).
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — The construction "إنما العاقل من آمن بالله" restricts the predicate: the intellect is not merely a faculty of cleverness but is defined by its fruit — faith and God-consciousness (taqwā).
5:7.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Book of Knowledge'

5:16.arabic: نورا يمشي به في الناس وحيث ذكر النور والظلمة أراد به العلم والجهل كقوله {يخرجهم من الظلمات إلى النور} وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم يا أيها الناس اعقلوا عن ربكم وتواصوا بالعقل تعرفوا ما أمرتم به وما نهيتم عنه واعلموا أنه ينجدكم عند ربكم واعلموا أن العاقل من أطاع الله وإن كان دميم المنظر حقير الخطر دنيء المنزلة رث الهيئة وأن الجاهل من عصى الله تعالى وإن كان جميل المنظر عظيم الخطر شريف المنزلة حسن الهيئة فصيحا نطوقا فالقردة والخنازير أعقل عند الله تعالى ممن عصاه ولا تغتر بتعظيم أهل الدنيا إياهم فإنهم من الخاسرين (2) وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم أول ما خلق
5:16.english: The Book of Seclusion ('Uzlah) — its explanation, God Most High willing. For this reason, Yūsuf ibn Asbāṭ wrote to Ḥudhayfah al-Marʿashī: "What is your opinion of one who remains, finding no one with whom to remember God Most High except that he is either sinful, or his remembrance in company is itself an act of disobedience — and that because he finds no one of his own kind?" And indeed he spoke truly, for mixing with people is never free from backbiting (ghībah), or listening to backbiting, or remaining silent upon wrongdoing (munkar). And the best of his states is that he either imparts knowledge or acquires it. Yet were this poor wretch to reflect, and to know that his imparting of knowledge is never free from the taints of ostentation (riyā'), the seeking of followers, and the desire for leadership (ri'āsah), he would know that the one who acquires knowledge from him only seeks to make it an instrument for pursuing the world and a means toward evil — so that the teacher becomes his helper therein, his support and his backer, preparing its causes for him, like one who sells a sword to a highway robber. For knowledge is like the sword: its soundness for good is like the soundness of the sword for warfare. And for this reason, it is not permitted to sell it to one whom one knows, by the indications of his circumstances, intends to use it to aid in cutting off the road.
5:16.section_title_en: The Book of Seclusion ('Uzlah) — Section 65, and The Seventh Book: On the Intellect, Its Nobility, Its Reality, and Its Divisions
5:16.anchors:
- Root: عقل (ʿaql)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The root denotes binding, restraining, and holding back; the intellect is that which restrains the soul from base desires and prevents it from straying.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "العقل يقال للقوة المتهيئة لقبول العلم، ويقال للعلم الذي يستفيده الإنسان بتلك القوة عقل" — The intellect is said of the faculty prepared for the reception of knowledge, and it is also said of the knowledge which man acquires by means of that faculty.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): intellectual apprehension and understanding. Metaphorical (Majaz): "نخلة لا تعقل الإبار" — a palm tree that does not accept pollination, i.e., does not grasp or take in.
- Root: علم (ʿilm)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Knowledge as the mark or sign by which a thing is known; the trace or landmark that guides.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "العلم: إدراك الشيء بحقيقته" — Knowledge is the apprehension of a thing in its true reality; it is of two kinds: apprehension of the essence of a thing, and judgment upon a thing regarding what exists for it or is negated of it.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: certain awareness. Metaphorical: "هو من أعلام العلم الخافقه" — he is among the lofty banners of knowledge; knowledge as a guiding landmark (maʿlam).
- Root: نور (nūr)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Light; the first to set up beacons (manār) on his path in his campaigns to guide his return.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "النور: الضوء المنتشر الذي يعين على الإبصار" — Light is the diffused radiance that aids vision; it is of two kinds: that perceived by the eye of inner insight (baṣīrah) — such as the light of the intellect and the light of the Qur'an — and that perceived by the eye of the head, such as the celestial bodies.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: illumination. Metaphorical: "نور الأمر: بينه" — he illuminated the matter: he made it clear; "وهذا أنور من ذاك: أبين" — this is more luminous than that: more evident.
- Sibawayh Rule: Restriction and Focused Predication (al-ḥaṣr wa al-taqyīd bi-innamā) — governing the exclusive attribution of a predicate to a subject, as in the author's restriction of the scholar's condition to one of two men, and the exclusion of the third.

5:16.arabic: {يخرجهم من الظلمات إلى النور} وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم يا أيها الناس اعقلوا عن ربكم وتواصوا بالعقل تعرفوا ما أمرتم به وما نهيتم عنه واعلموا أنه ينجدكم عند ربكم واعلموا أن العاقل من أطاع الله وإن كان دميم المنظر حقير الخطر دنيء المنزلة رث الهيئة وأن الجاهل من عصى الله تعالى وإن كان جميل المنظر عظيم الخطر شريف المنزلة حسن الهيئة فصيحا نطوقا فالقردة والخنازير أعقل عند الله تعالى ممن عصاه ولا تغتر بتعظيم أهل الدنيا إياهم فإنهم من الخاسرين (2) وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم أول ما خل
5:16.english: The Book of Seclusion ('Uzlah) — its explanation, God Most High willing. For this reason, Yūsuf ibn Asbāṭ wrote to Ḥudhayfah al-Marʿashī: "What is your opinion of one who remains, finding no one with whom to remember God Most High except that he is either sinful, or his remembrance in company is itself an act of disobedience — and that because he finds no one of his own kind?" And indeed he spoke truly, for mixing with people is never free from backbiting (ghībah), or listening to backbiting, or remaining silent upon wrongdoing (munkar). And the best of his states is that he either imparts knowledge or acquires it. Yet were this poor wretch to reflect, and to know that his imparting of knowledge is never free from the taints of ostentation (riyā'), the seeking of followers, and the desire for leadership (ri'āsah), he would know that the one who acquires knowledge from him only seeks to make it an instrument for pursuing the world and a means toward evil — so that the teacher becomes his helper therein, his support and his backer, preparing its causes for him, like one who sells a sword to a highway robber. For knowledge is like the sword: its soundness for good is like the soundness of the sword for warfare. And for this reason, it is not permitted to sell it to one whom one knows, by the indications of his circumstances, intends to use it to aid in cutting off the road.
