7:176.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Disciplining the Soul'

7:176.arabic: آتيناه آياتنا فانسلخ منها فأتبعه الشيطان فكان من الغاوين حتى قال فمثله كمثل الكلب إن تحمل عليه يلهث أو تتركه يلهث فكذلك العالم الفاجر فإن بلعام أوتي كتاب الله تعالى فأخلد إلى الشهوات فشبه بالكلب أي سواء أوتي الحكمة أو لم يؤت فهو يلهث إلى الشهوات وقال عيسى عليه السلام مثل علماء السوء كمثل صخرة وقعت على فم النهر لا هي تشرب الماء ولا هي تترك الماء يخلص إلى الزرع ومثل علماء السوء مثل قناة الحش ظاهرها جص وباطنها نتن ومثل القبور ظاهرها عامر وباطنها عظام الموتى فهذه الأخبار والآثار تبين أن العالم الذي هو من أبناء الدنيا أخس حالا وأشد عذابا من الجاهل وأن الفائزين المقربين هم عل
7:176.english: I say: The Prophet — peace and blessings be upon him — said: "The scholar will indeed be tormented with a torment at which the inhabitants of the Fire will circle around, marveling at the severity of his punishment." By it he meant the wicked scholar.
7:176.section_title_en: The Worldly Scholar's Punishment and the Marks of the Hereafter-Scholars
7:176.anchors:
- Root: فجر (fajara)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To split, cleave, or rend something widely; to break open
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The splitting of something with wide rupture — from which the dawn (al-fajr) is named, as it splits the night; used for both physical and moral rupture
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the cleaving of water or the breaking of dawn. Metaphorical: the eruption of punishment upon one suddenly and overwhelmingly
- Root: علم (ʿalima)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Knowledge; the faculty of apprehending a thing as it truly is
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Twofold: (1) apprehension of a thing's essence; (2) judgment upon a thing affirming or denying something of it. The scholar (al-ʿālim) is one who possesses such apprehension
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: knowledge as certain apprehension. Metaphorical: the "signs" (maʿālim) of the path — that by which one is guided; the scholar is a "sign" pointing either to guidance or to ruin
- Root: دنا (dana)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To be near, to draw close; al-dunyā (the nearer world) as that which is immediate and low
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Proximity by essence or by judgment; used of place, time, and station. The "nearer" (al-adnā) is contrasted with the greater and the better
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: nearness. Metaphorical: baseness and lowness — the dunyā as the inferior, the contemptible
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — The particle innamā restricts the predicate exclusively to its subject, as in "the winners and the brought-near are only the scholars of the Hereafter," effecting complete exclusion of all else.
7:176.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Book of Knowledge'

7:179.arabic: وقال تعالى {لهم قلوب لا يفقهون بها} وأراد به معاني الإيمان دون الفتاوى ولعمري إن الفقه والفهم في اللغة اسمان بمعنى واحد وإنما يتكلم في عادة الاستعمال به قديما وحديثا قال تعالى {لأنتم أشد رهبة في صدورهم من الله} الآية فأحال قلة خوفهم من الله واستعظامهم سطوة الخلق على قلة الفقه فانظر إن كان ذلك نتيجة عدم الحفظ لتفريعات الفتاوى أو هو نتيجة عدم ما ذكرناه من العلوم وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم علماء فقهاء (1) للذين وفدوا عليه وسئل سعد بن إبراهيم الزهري رحمه الله أي أهل المدينة أفقه فقال أتقا
7:179.english: They have manipulated this term through specification (takhṣīṣ), not through transfer (naql) or conversion (taḥwīl), for they have restricted it to knowledge of obscure legal branches (furūʿ gharībah) in legal opinions (fatāwā), to grasping the subtleties of their underlying causes (ʿilal), to multiplying discourse concerning them, and to memorizing the doctrinal positions related to them. Whoever is more profound in this and more occupied with it is called "the most learned in fiqh" (al-afqah). Yet in the first era, the name fiqh was applied absolutely to knowledge of the path of the Hereafter, to knowing the subtleties of the maladies of the souls (āfāt al-nufūs), to the corrupters of deeds (mufsidāt al-aʿmāl), to the power of encompassing the pettiness of this world, to intense longing for the bliss of the Hereafter, and to the dominance of fear over the heart. What indicates this to you is His saying, Mighty and Majestic: {«ليتفقهوا في الدين ولينذروا قومهم إذا رجعوا إليهم»} [“That they may gain understanding in the religion and warn their people when they return to them”] (Q 9:122). What effects warning and intimidation is this very fiqh — not the subdivisions of divorce (ṭalāq), manumission (ʿitāq), imprecation (liʿān), salam contracts, and leases (ijārah). For that (latter) does not produce warning or intimidation; rather, total devotion to it perpetually hardens the heart and strips away godly fear (khashyah) from it, as we now observe in those wholly devoted to it.
7:179.section_title_en: The Revival of the Religious Sciences — Section 27: The Corruption of the Praiseworthy Names (Taḥrīf al-Asāmī al-Maḥmūdah)
7:179.anchors:
- Root: فقه (Fiqh)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core linguistic meaning of "understanding" (al-fahm) and "comprehension" (al-fahm ʿan al-shayʾ)
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Al-fiqh: attainment of knowledge of the unseen through a witnessed sign — it is more specific than ʿilm." Theological nuance: true fiqh is knowledge of the heart's maladies and the path to the Hereafter.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): "afqih ʿannī mā aqūl" — understand what I say. Metaphorical (majāz): technical restriction to legal rulings (furūʿ al-fatāwā) is a later convention, not the lexical or prophetic norm.
- Root: علم (ʿIlm)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Perception of a thing as it truly is; knowledge of the essence of a thing.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Two types: (1) perception of the essence of a thing; (2) judgment upon a thing affirming or negating something of it. The highest ʿilm is knowledge of God, His verses, and His acts.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "He is from the banners (aʿlām) of knowledge." Metaphorical: restriction of the title "scholar" (al-ʿālim) to the dialectician (al-munāẓir) is a corrupt specification (takhṣīṣ fāsid).
- Root: وحد (Waḥḥada)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To make one; to affirm unity.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Tawḥīd is affirming God's unity in essence, attributes, and acts — the highest degree being the vision that all things proceed from Him alone.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: utterance of "Lā ilāha illā Allāh." Metaphorical: the inner reality (al-lubāb) — seeing all affairs from God, cutting off attention from secondary causes.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب التخصيص والتقييد (Restriction and Specification) — The corruption of names occurs through takhṣīṣ (semantic restriction), not naql (lexical transfer). The grammarians' principle: a general term (al-ism al-ʿāmm) retains its full semantic range unless a valid sharʿī or linguistic evidence restricts it; arbitrary restriction by custom (ʿādat al-istimāl) is a rhetorical device of the devils among men and jinn.
7:179.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Book of Knowledge'

7:179.arabic: يقال فيهم {أولئك كالأنعام بل هم أضل} وإنما كانوا أضل لأن الأنعام ليس في قوتها طلب درجة الملائكة فتركها الطلب للعجز وأما الإنسان ففي قوته ذلك والقادر على نيل الكمال أحرى بالذم وأجدر بالنسبة إلى الضلال مهما تقاعد عن طلب الكمال وإذا كان هذا كلاما معترضا فلنرجع إلى المقصود فقد بينا معنى قول {لا إله إلا الله} ومعنى قول لا حول ولا قوة إلا بالله وإن من ليس قائلا بهما عن مشاهدة فلا يتصور منه حال التوكل فإن قلت ليس في قولك لا حول ولا قوة إلا بالله إلا نسبة شيئين إلى الله فلو قال قائل السم
7:179.english: If you say: "Does there remain with the servant any management (tadbir) or attachment to causes (asbab) in these states?" — Know that the third station negates management entirely (rafʿan li-l-tadbir), so long as the state persists; rather, its possessor becomes like one stupefied (mabhut). The second station negates every management except that which pertains to fleeing unto Allah through supplication (duʿa) and earnest entreaty (ibtihal) — like the management of an infant in clinging to its mother alone. The first station does not negate the root of management and choice (ikhtiyar), but negates certain managements — like one who relies on his deputy (wakil) in a lawsuit: he abandons his own management with respect to what is not the deputy's concern, but he does not abandon the management which his deputy has indicated to him, nor the management which he knows from the deputy's custom and established practice (sunnah), apart from his explicit indication.
7:179.section_title_en: The Reality of Reliance (Haqiqat al-Tawakkul) — Degrees of Trust and the Station of Witnessing
7:179.anchors:
- Root: دبر (d-b-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "دبر الشيء: خلاف القبل" — the rear, the back; by extension, the management of affairs as one turns away from one thing toward another (tadbir: to manage, to deliberate over outcomes).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "دبر الشيء: خلاف القبل، وكني بهما عن العضوين المخصوصين" — used literally for spatial orientation; metaphorically for the ordering of one's own affairs (tadbir al-amr), which is the very faculty that tawakkul suspends or redirects.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "أدبر النهار ودبر دبورا" (the day passed away). Metaphorical: "ما يعرف قبيلا من دبير" — one who cannot distinguish front from back, i.e., total loss of self-direction; relevant to the state of the "bewildered" (mabhut) one.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — applies to the phrase "لا حول ولا قوة إلا بالله" where the restriction (hasr) confines all power (hawl) and strength (quwwah) exclusively to Allah, negating any independent creaturely agency.
7:179.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications, prayers, and their spiritual power, from 'Monotheism and Reliance'

7:182.arabic: الخيرات بل لا يشعرون وقال تعالى سنستدرجهم من حيث لا يعلمون وقال تعالى فتحنا عليهم أبواب كل شيء حتى إذا فرحوا بما أوتوا أخذناهم بغتة فإذا هم مبلسون وفي تفسير قوله تعالى سنستدرجهم من حيث لا يعلمون أنهم كلما أحدثوا ذنبا أحدثنا لهم نعمة ليزيد غرورهم وقال تعالى إنما نملي لهم ليزدادوا إثما وقال تعالى ولا تحسبن الله غافلا عما يعمل الظالمون إنما يؤخرهم ليوم تشخص فيه الأبصار إلى غير ذلك مما ورد في كتاب الله تعالى وسنة رسوله فمن آمن به تخلص من هذا الغرور فإن منشأ هذا الغرور الجهل بالله وبصفاته فإن من عرفه لا يأمن م
7:182.english: As for knowing it by way of authoritative transmission and affirmation (taṣdīq): it is that one believes in the Book of God — exalted is He — and affirms His Messenger. For God — exalted is He — has said: {«أيحسبون أن ما نمدهم به من مال وبنين * نسارع لهم في الخيرات بل لا يشعرون»} — "Do they reckon that what We extend to them of wealth and sons — [that] We hasten for them good things? Nay, but they do not perceive" (Q. 23:55-56). And He said — exalted is He: {«سنستدرجهم من حيث لا يعلمون»} — "We shall draw them on by degrees from whence they do not know" (Q. 7:182). And He said — exalted is He: {«فتحنا عليهم أبواب كل شيء حتى إذا فرحوا بما أوتوا أخذناهم بغتة فإذا هم مبلسون»} — "We opened upon them the gates of everything, until when they rejoiced in what they were given, We seized them suddenly, and behold, they were in despair" (Q. 6:44). And in the interpretation of His saying — exalted is He: {«سنستدرجهم من حيث لا يعلمون»} — it is said: "Whenever they innovated a sin, We innovated for them a blessing, to increase their self-deception." And He said — exalted is He: {«إنما نملي لهم ليزدادوا إثما»} — "We only grant them respite that they may increase in sin" (Q. 3:178). And He said — exalted is He: {«ولا تحسبن الله غافلا عما يعمل الظالمون إنما يؤخرهم ليوم تشخص فيه الأبصار»} — "And do not reckon God heedless of what the wrongdoers do; He only delays them to a Day when eyes will stare fixedly" (Q. 14:42). And [there is] more of that kind which has come in the Book of God — exalted is He — and in the Sunnah of His Messenger. So whoever believes in it is delivered from this self-deception. For the origin of this self-deception is ignorance of God and of His attributes; for whoever knows Him does not feel secure from His stratagem (makr) and is not deceived by such corrupt fancies.
7:182.section_title_en: Section 888 — On the Remedy for Self-Deception (Ghurūr): Recognizing the Signs of Divine Honor (Karāmah) and Humiliation (Hawān)
7:182.anchors:
- Root: غرر (gh-r-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of an outward trace or mark; heedlessness in wakefulness; the blaze on a horse's forehead.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Ghurūr" is delusion stemming from heedlessness — the soul's being overtaken while imagining security, as in {«ما غرك بربك الكريم»} (Q. 82:6). It is the state of one who is deceived by apparent favors while blind to their underlying test.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): heedlessness and exposure to predation, like a gazelle deceived by moonlight. Metaphorical (Majaz): being "deceived by God" (ightirār billāh) — trusting in His mercy while persisting in disobedience.
- Root: لهم (l-h-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Swallowing whole; the gullet.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Ilhām" — God's casting a meaning into the heart (al-raw'), distinct from demonic whispering; the channel of inner vision for the knowers (ʿārifūn).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: to swallow. Metaphorical: the heart's receptive "swallowing" of divine inspiration.
- Root: حدث (ḥ-d-th)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Origination after non-existence; newness.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Ḥudūth" — a thing's coming to be after it was not; "muḥdith" — the originator, exclusively God for substances (jawāhir). "Iḥdāth" — bringing about a novel state or act.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: temporal newness. Metaphorical: "muḥaddath" — one inspired with correct discernment, as if newly spoken-to.
- Root: نعم (n-ʿ-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Softness, ease, well-being; a state of comfort.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Niʿmah" — the good state one inhabits; "naʿīm" — the act of living pleasantly. Blessings are both a test and a sign, per {«وإن تعدوا نعمة الله لا تحصوها»} (Q. 16:18).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: bounty and comfort. Metaphorical: "khafat naʿāmatuhum" — their prosperity vanished; blessings may signal either favor or gradual ruin (istidrāj).
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction and Focused Predication with "innamā")
  * In {«إنما نملي لهم ليزدادوا إثما»} (Q. 3:178) and {«إنما يؤخرهم ليوم تشخص فيه الأبصار»} (Q. 14:42), "innamā" restricts the purpose of divine respite exclusively to increase of sin and deferred reckoning — negating any reading of it as benevolent indulgence.
7:182.topic: Al-Ghazali on constant remembrance of God and contemplative invocations, from 'Condemnation of Delusion'

7:182.arabic: بأن يخطر لهم على سبيل الورود عليهم من حيث لا يعلمون وتارة على سبيل الرؤيا الصادقة وتارة في اليقظة على سبيل كشف المعاني بمشاهدة الأمثلة كما يكون في المنام وهذا أعلى الدرجات وهي من درجات النبوة العالية كما أن الرؤيا الصادقة جزء من ستة وأربعين جزءا من النبوة فإياك أن يكون حظك من هذا العلم إنكار ما جاوز حد قصورك ففيه هلك المتحذلقون من العلماء الزاعمون أنهم أحاطوا بعلوم العقول فالجهل خير من عقل يدعو إلى إنكار مثل هذه الأمور لأولياء الله تعالى ومن أنكر ذلك للأولياء لزمه إنكار الأنبياء وكان خارجا عن
7:182.english: For this reason ʿAlī, may God be pleased with him, said — when it was said to him, "You have opposed so-and-so" — "The best of us is the most following of us of this religion." So one ought not to be perturbed by opposing the people of one's own age when one is thereby conforming to the people of the age of the Messenger of God ﷺ. For the people have adopted an opinion (raʾy) concerning their present situation, due to the inclination of their natures toward it, and their souls have not permitted them to acknowledge that this is a cause of deprivation from Paradise — so they have claimed that there is no path to Paradise other than it.
7:182.section_title_en: ** Section 64 — On the Sciences of the Inner Life: The Obligation to Follow the Salaf and the Condemnation of Innovation (Bidʿah)
7:182.anchors:
**
- Root: علم (ʿalima)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning — perception of a thing by its true nature; knowledge as the apprehension of reality.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "العلم: إدراك الشيء بحقيقته" — knowledge is the apprehension of a thing in its true reality, divided into apprehension of the essence and judgment upon the thing.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal usage — "ما علمت بخبرك: ما شعرت به" (I did not know of your news: I had no awareness of it). The scholar (ʿālim) is one whose knowledge is manifest in action.
- Root: بدع (badaʿa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning — to originate, to create something new without prior example.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الإبداع: إنشاء صنعة بلا احتذاء واقتداء" — origination of a thing without model or precedent. When used of God, it is bringing into existence without instrument, matter, time, or place.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — "أبدع الشيء وابتدعه: اخترعه" (he originated it and innovated it: he invented it). Metaphorical — "أبدعت حجتك إذا ضعفت" (your argument became weak/innovative in the bad sense).
- Root: حدث (ḥadatha)
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الحدوث: كون الشيء بعد أن لم يكن" — coming-to-be of a thing after it was not. "المحدث: ما أوجد بعد أن لم يكن" — the originated thing.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — "هو حدث من الأحداث" (he is a youth among youths). Metaphorical — "صاروا أحاديث" (they became [mere] tales). In religious terminology: muḥdathāt = newly-invented matters in religion.
- Root: هدى (hadā)
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Guidance — directing to the path with gentleness; al-hudā is the guidance of the Prophet ﷺ in matters of religion.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "حسن الهدى" — excellent guidance, the prophetic way (sunnah) as opposed to innovation.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — "إنما هما اثنتان: الكلام والهدى" restricts the two matters exclusively to speech and guidance, excluding all else.

  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): "afqih ʿannī mā aqūl" — understand what I say. Metaphorical (majāz): technical restriction to legal rulings (furūʿ al-fatāwā) is a later convention, not the lexical or prophetic norm.
- Root: علم (ʿIlm)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Perception of a thing as it truly is; knowledge of the essence of a thing.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Two types: (1) perception of the essence of a thing; (2) judgment upon a thing affirming or negating something of it. The highest ʿilm is knowledge of God, His verses, and His acts.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "He is from the banners (aʿlām) of knowledge." Metaphorical: restriction of the title "scholar" (al-ʿālim) to the dialectician (al-munāẓir) is a corrupt specification (takhṣīṣ fāsid).
- Root: وحد (Waḥḥada)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To make one; to affirm unity.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Tawḥīd is affirming God's unity in essence, attributes, and acts — the highest degree being the vision that all things proceed from Him alone.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: utterance of "Lā ilāha illā Allāh." Metaphorical: the inner reality (al-lubāb) — seeing all affairs from God, cutting off attention from secondary causes.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب التخصيص والتقييد (Restriction and Specification) — The corruption of names occurs through takhṣīṣ (semantic restriction), not naql (lexical transfer). The grammarians' principle: a general term (al-ism al-ʿāmm) retains its full semantic range unless a valid sharʿī or linguistic evidence restricts it; arbitrary restriction by custom (ʿādat al-istimāl) is a rhetorical device of the devils among men and jinn.
9:122.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Book of Knowledge'

9:122.arabic: أما الآيات فقوله تعالى {فلولا نفر من كل فرقة منهم طائفة ليتفقهوا في الدين} وقوله عز وجل {فاسألوا أهل الذكر إن كنتم لا تعلمون} وأما الأخبار فقوله صلى الله عليه وسلم من سلك طريقا يطلب فيه علما سلك الله به طريقا إلى الجنة (1) وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم إن الملائكة لتضع أجنحتها لطالب العلم رضاء بما يصنع (2) وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم لأن تغدو فتتعلم بابا من العلم خير من أن تصلي مائة ركعة (3) وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم باب من العلم يتعلمه الرجل خير له من الدنيا وما فيها (4) وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم اطلبوا العلم
9:122.english: As for the Quranic verses, there is the saying of God Most High: {«فلولا نفر من كل فرقة منهم طائفة ليتفقهوا في الدين»} — "Why then did not a party from every section of them go forth, that they might gain deep comprehension in the religion?" — and His saying, Mighty and Majestic: {«فاسألوا أهل الذكر إن كنتم لا تعلمون»} — "So ask the people of remembrance if you do not know."
9:122.section_title_en: The Virtue of Seeking Knowledge (Faḍīlat al-Taʿallum)
9:122.anchors:
- Root: فقه (Fiqh)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning is "comprehension" and "understanding" — the penetration into the inner meaning of speech, distinguished from mere hearing (samāʿ).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In the theological register, *tafaqquh* (تفقه) is the deep, exhaustive comprehension of the religious sciences — not mere memorization but the attainment of the realities of juridico-theological matters.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) usage denotes intellectual penetration; metaphorical (majāz) usage extends to any deep discernment of subtle meanings.
- Root: سأل (Saʾala)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To ask, to inquire, to seek information — the root act of petitioning for knowledge from its possessor.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Asking (*suʾāl*) is the divinely mandated means for the ignorant to access knowledge, as per {«فاسألوا أهل الذكر»} — it is the key that unlocks the treasuries of knowledge.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal usage is the verbal request; the Prophet's statement "العلم خزائن مفاتيحها السؤال" employs a metaphor (majāz) likening knowledge to locked treasuries and questioning to their keys.
- Root: طلب (Ṭalab)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To seek, to pursue, to search out a thing — whether a physical object or a meaning.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الطلب: الفحص عن وجود الشيء، عينا كان أو معنى" — the earnest investigation into the existence of a thing, whether concrete or conceptual. In the religious context, *ṭalab al-ʿilm* is the pursuit of that which revives the religion.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal usage is the physical pursuit of a quarry; the ḥadīth "من سلك طريقا يطلب فيه علما" employs the metaphor of the *path* (ṭarīq) as the means of pursuit, and the divine recompense as the *path to Paradise*.
- Root: غدو (Ghadā)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To go out early in the morning, to set forth at dawn — the time of vigorous, purposeful departure.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal usage denotes the morning journey; in the saying of Abū al-Dardāʾ, "الغدو إلى طلب العلم" is metaphorically elevated to the rank of *jihād* — the early morning departure for knowledge is a martial expedition of the soul.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Interposition (al-Faṣl bayna al-Jār wa-al-Majrūr) — The syntactic principle governing the separation of the prepositional phrase from its governing verb, as in "سلك الله به طريقا إلى الجنة," where the divine agency is interposed between the act and its recompense, indicating the causal nexus.
9:122.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Book of Knowledge'

9:122.arabic: أما الآيات فقوله عز وجل {ولينذروا قومهم إذا رجعوا إليهم لعلهم يحذرون} والمراد هو التعليم والإرشاد وقوله تعالى وإذ أخذ الله ميثاق الذين أوتوا الكتاب ليبيننه للناس ولا يكتمونه وهو إيجاب للتعليم وقوله تعالى {وإن فريقا منهم ليكتمون الحق وهم يعلمون} وهو تحريم للكتمان كما قال تعالى في الشهادة {ومن يكتمها فإنه آثم قلبه} وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم ما آتى الله عالما علما إلا وأخذ عليه من الميثاق ما أخذ على النبيين أن يبينوه للناس ولا يكتموه (6) وقال تعالى {ومن أحسن قولا ممن دعا إلى الله وعمل صالحا} وقال تعالى {ادع إلى
9:122.english: As for the Qur'anic verses: His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: {وَلِيُنذِرُوا قَوْمَهُمْ إِذَا رَجَعُوا إِلَيْهِمْ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَحْذَرُونَ} "That they may warn their people when they return to them, that perhaps they may be cautious" {«ولينذروا قومهم إذا رجعوا إليهم لعلهم يحذرون»} — and the intended meaning is teaching and guidance (al-taʿlīm wa-al-irshād).
9:122.anchors:
- Root: علم (ʿalima)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning is "to know, to perceive a thing by its reality"; the root also carries the sense of "marker, sign, banner" — that by which something is distinguished and recognized.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "العلم: إدراك الشيء بحقيقته" — knowledge is the apprehension of a thing by its true reality, divided into apprehension of the essence of a thing and judgment upon it. This is the attribute by which the scholar (ʿālim) is distinguished and by which he becomes a "sign" (ʿalam) pointing to truth.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): "هو من أعلام العلم الخافقه" — the scholar is among the lofty banners of knowledge. The teaching act makes the scholar a living signpost; the root's literal sense of "marking" or "branding" a thing carries into the metaphorical (majāz) register of "imprinting" knowledge upon hearts.
- Root: حدث (ḥadatha)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning is "to be new, to occur after not having been"; al-ḥadīth is speech that is new and conveyed.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الحدوث: كون الشيء بعد أن لم يكن" — origination after non-existence. The prophetic traditions (aḥādīth) cited here are "newly conveyed" reports that carry authority.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Metaphorical (majāz): "صاروا أحاديث" — they became subjects of discourse. The transmission of knowledge is an "event" (ḥadath) that occurs in the listener, renewing his state.
- Root: عهد (ʿahida)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning is "covenant, pact, charge"; al-ʿahd is a binding commission that one is obligated to fulfill.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The covenant (mīthāq) taken from the People of the Book and from the scholars is a divine charge (taklīf) that makes teaching an obligation, not a supererogatory act.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the covenant is a "charge entrusted" (waṣiyyah) that binds the one who receives knowledge to its dissemination.
- Root: كتم (katama)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning is "to conceal, to hide"; al-kitmān is the deliberate suppression of what ought to be revealed.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Concealment of knowledge is paired with concealment of testimony (shahādah) in the Qur'an — both are sins of the heart (ithm al-qalb) because they withhold what God has commanded to be made manifest.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal vs. metaphorical: the "bridle of fire" (lijām min nār) on the Day of Judgment is a metaphorical (majāz) embodiment of the inner restraint of truth — the concealed knowledge becomes a physical restraint in the afterlife.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد (Restriction & Specification) — The verse {وإن فريقا منهم ليكتمون الحق وهم يعلمون} employs the restrictive particle "inna" with the continuous verb form (yaktimūn) to specify an ongoing, willful concealment, distinguishing it from mere ignorance. The conditional structures in the ḥadīth "man taʿallama... man ʿallama... man katama" (whoever learns... whoever teaches... whoever conceals) follow the canonical pattern of protasis-apodosis (sharṭ/jazāʾ) that establishes a universal causal linkage between the act and its recompense.
9:122.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'Book of Knowledge'

10:17.arabic: الله تعالى بين من افترى على الله كذبا وبين من كذب بالحق فقال تعالى ومن أظلم ممن افترى على الله كذبا أو كذب بالحق لما جاءه وقال تعالى فمن أظلم ممن كذب على الله وكذب بالصدق إذ جاءه ومنها الرياء وملاحظة الخلق والجهد في استمالة قلوبهم وصرف وجوههم والرياء هو الداء العضال الذي يدعو إلى أكبر الكبائر كما سيأتي في كتاب الرياء والمناظر لا يقصد إلا الظهور عند الخلق وانطلاق ألسنتهم بالثناء عليه فهذه عشر خصال من أمهات الفواحش الباطنة سوى ما يتفق لغير المتماسكين منهم من الخصام المؤدي إلى الضرب
10:17.english:
**QUAD_ANCHORS:**
- Root: نظر (naẓara)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to look, to examine, to consider; al-munāẓarah is mutual examination/argumentation between two parties.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: naẓar as intellectual contemplation (taʾammul bi-l-baṣīrah); munāẓarah as dialectical exchange.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: sitting face-to-face in debate; Metaphorical: disputation for victory.
- Root: غلب (ghalaba)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to overcome, to conquer, to prevail.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-ghalabah as seeking to dominate another in argument.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: victory in combat; Metaphorical: intellectual supremacy.
- Root: حسد (ḥasada)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to envy, to wish removal of blessings from another.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: envy as wishing deprivation of blessings from the deserving — among the basest traits.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: envy of another's blessing; Metaphorical: consuming fire of the soul.
- Root: كبر (kabura)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to be great, to be haughty.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-kibr as self-elevation above others; condemned by God.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: greatness; Metaphorical: arrogance and pride.
- Root: غيب (ghāba)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to be absent, to be hidden.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-ghībah as mentioning another with what he dislikes in his absence — likened to eating carrion.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: backbiting; Metaphorical: consuming the flesh of one's brother.
- Root: راءى (rāʾā)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to show off, to display.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-riyāʾ as performing acts for the sake of being seen — hidden shirk.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: showing good deeds; Metaphorical: seeking reputation.
- Root: نفس (nafs)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: self, soul, spirit.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: tazkiyat al-nafs as self-praise and self-purification — forbidden by God.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: self; Metaphorical: self-commendation.
- Root: حقd (ḥaqida)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to bear malice, to harbor resentment.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-ḥiqd as nursing enmity in the heart — negated from the believer.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: bearing grudge; Metaphorical: hidden rancor.
- Root: نفاق (nifāq)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: hypocrisy, showing contrary to what one conceals.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: hypocrisy in deeds — outward display contrary to inward state.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: hypocrisy in faith; Metaphorical: hypocrisy in character.
- Root: علم (ʿalima)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to know, to perceive.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: knowledge as apprehension of reality — its pursuit for other than God is destructive.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: knowledge; Metaphorical: the dangerous burden of the scholar.
- Root: جدل (jadala)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to argue, to dispute.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-jidāl as contention; al-mirāʾ as disputation with falsehood — condemned.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: argumentation; Metaphorical: obstinate disputation.
- Root: شرك (sharaka)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to associate, to share.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-riyāʾ as hidden shirk — associating others with God in intention.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: polytheism; Metaphorical: hidden association in deeds.
- Root: موت (māta)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to die.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: death as separation of soul from body; spiritual death as ruin of the soul.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical death; Metaphorical: spiritual destruction.
- Root: حيى (ḥayiya)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to live.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: life as the power of perception; eternal life as the reward of the righteous.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical life; Metaphorical: spiritual vitality.
- Root: هلك (halaka)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to perish, to be destroyed.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-halāk as ruin; eternal destruction as everlasting punishment.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: destruction; Metaphorical: eternal ruin.
- Root: رياء (riyāʾ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: showing off, ostentation.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: riyāʾ as the incurable disease calling to the greatest sins.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: ostentation; Metaphorical: spiritual disease.
- Root: جاه (jāh)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: rank, status, prestige.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: love of status (ḥubb al-jāh) among the destructive traits.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: position; Metaphorical: seeking prestige.
- Root: مباهاة (mubāhāh)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: mutual boasting, vying in splendor.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: mubāhāh as each seeking to display superiority over the other.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: mutual boasting; Metaphorical: rivalry in honor.
- Root: مماراة (mumārāh)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: disputation, wrangling.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-mirāʾ as contentious argument — condemned by the Prophet.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: disputation; Metaphorical: obstinate wrangling.
- Root: فخر (fakhara)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to boast, to pride oneself.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-fakhr as self-glorification — among the blameworthy traits.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: boasting; Metaphorical: vainglory.
- Root: عجب (ʿajiba)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to wonder, to be amazed.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-ʿujb as self-admiration — among the destructive traits.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: wonder; Metaphorical: self-conceit.
- Root: بغض (baghiḍa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to hate, to detest.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-baghdāʾ as mutual hatred — contrary to brotherhood.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: hatred; Metaphorical: mutual enmity.
- Root: غضب (ghaḍiba)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to be angry.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-ghaḍab as anger — among the blameworthy traits.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: anger; Metaphorical: rage.
- Root: طمع (ṭamiʿa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to covet, to desire.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-ṭamaʿ as covetousness — among the destructive traits.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: desire; Metaphorical: greed.
- Root: أشر (ashira)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to be exultant, to be insolent.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-ashar as excessive joy and insolence — blameworthy.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: exultation; Metaphorical: insolence.
- Root: بطر (baṭira)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to be arrogant, to be ungrateful.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-baṭar as arrogance in prosperity — among the destructive traits.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: arrogance; Metaphorical: ingratitude for blessings.
- Root: خيلاء (khuyalāʾ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: pride, haughtiness.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-khuyalāʾ as pride and conceit — blameworthy.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: pride; Metaphorical: haughty bearing.
- Root: خشية (khashyah)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: fear, awe.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-khashyah as reverential fear — among the traits of the believers.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: fear; Metaphorical: reverential awe.
- Root: رحمة (raḥmah)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: mercy, compassion.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-raḥmah as tenderness of heart — among the traits of the believers.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: mercy; Metaphorical: compassion.
- Root: غفلة (ghaflah)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: heedlessness, inattention.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-ghaflah as heedlessness — contrary to vigilance.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: inattention; Metaphorical: spiritual heedlessness.
- Root: خشوع (khushūʿ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: humility, submissiveness.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-khushūʿ as humility — among the traits of the believers.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: humility; Metaphorical: devotional submission.
- Root: تذكير (tadhkīr)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: reminding, admonishing.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-tadhkīr as reminding of God — a righteous act.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: reminding; Metaphorical: preaching.
- Root: وعظ (waʿaẓa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to admonish, to exhort.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-waʿẓ as exhortation to obedience and warning against disobedience.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: admonition; Metaphorical: sermonizing.
- Root: فتوى (fatwā)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: legal ruling, formal opinion.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-fatwā as clarification of legal rulings.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: legal opinion; Metaphorical: religious authority.
- Root: قضاء (qaḍāʾ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: judgment, decree.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-qaḍāʾ as judgment between people.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: judgment; Metaphorical: judicial authority.
- Root: وقف (waqafa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to stop, to stand.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-waqf as endowment of property for charitable purposes.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: standing; Metaphorical: religious endowment.
- Root: ثواب (thawāb)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: reward, recompense.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-thawāb as divine recompense for righteous deeds.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: reward; Metaphorical: divine recompense.
- Root: عذاب (ʿadhāb)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: punishment, torment.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-ʿadhāb as divine punishment for the disobedient.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: punishment; Metaphorical: divine chastisement.
- Root: ملك (malaka)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to possess, to rule.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-mulk as sovereignty; al-mulk al-muʾabbad as eternal sovereignty in Paradise.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: dominion; Metaphorical: eternal kingdom.
- Root: نعيم (naʿīm)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: bliss, delight.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-naʿīm as bliss; al-naʿīm al-sarmad as everlasting bliss.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: delight; Metaphorical: eternal bliss.
- Root: رخصة (rukhaṣah)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: concession, dispensation.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-rukhaṣah as legal concession.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: concession; Metaphorical: legal dispensation.
- Root: رياسة (riyāsah)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: leadership, headship.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: love of leadership among the destructive traits.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: leadership; Metaphorical: seeking authority.
- Root: اندراس (indirās)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: effacement, obliteration.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: indirās al-ʿulūm as the obliteration of the sciences.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: effacement; Metaphorical: extinction of knowledge.
- Root: صبيان (ṣibyān)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: boys, children.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: children's motivation for learning through play.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: boys; Metaphorical: pupils.
- Root: مكتب (maktab)
  * Lisan / Ayn- Root: مكتب (maktab)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: place of instruction, school for boys.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: the elementary school where children are taught.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: school; Metaphorical: place of elementary learning.
- Root: خلاق (khilāq)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: portion, share, lot.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: "no portion" (lā khilāq) in the Hereafter — utter deprivation of divine reward.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: share; Metaphorical: spiritual allotment in the afterlife.
- Root: فاجر (fājir)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: wicked, immoral, profligate.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: the dissolute one who commits sins openly.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: sinner; Metaphorical: one through whom God nonetheless supports religion.
- Root: شمع (shamʿ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: candle, wax taper.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: the candle as parable — consuming itself while giving light to others.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: candle; Metaphorical: one who destroys himself but benefits others.
- Root: نار (nār)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: fire.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: fire as parable — consuming itself and all around it.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: fire; Metaphorical: one who destroys himself and others.
- Root: سعد (saʿida)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to be fortunate, to prosper.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: saʿādah as felicity — success in the Hereafter.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: good fortune; Metaphorical: eternal felicity.
- Root: شقي (shaqiya)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to be wretched, to be miserable.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: shaqāwah as wretchedness — ruin in the Hereafter.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: misery; Metaphorical: eternal ruin.
- Root: أخلص (akhlaṣa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to purify, to be sincere.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: ikhlāṣ as purifying intention for God alone — the condition of acceptance.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: sincerity; Metaphorical: pure devotion.
- Root: ريب (rāba)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to doubt, to suspect.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-rayb as doubt and uncertainty — to be dispelled by evidence.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: doubt; Metaphorical: skepticism.
10:17.topic: Al-Ghazali on purifying the character, moral diseases, and spiritual remedies, from 'Book of Knowledge'

11:6.arabic: فيها نفسه ويدخل فيما لا يحل له ثم نظرت إلى قوله تعالى وما من دابة في الأرض إلا على الله رزقها فعلمت أني واحد من هذه الدواب التي على الله رزقها فاشتغلت بما لله تعالى علي وتركت ما لي عنده الثامنة نظرت إلى هذا الخلق فرأيتهم كلهم متوكلين على مخلوق هذا على ضيعته وهذا على تجارته وهذا على صناعته وهذا على صحة بدنه وكل مخلوق متوكل على مخلوق مثله فرجعت إلى قوله تعالى ومن يتوكل على الله فهو حسبه فتوكلت على الله عز وجل فهو حسبي قال شقيق يا حاتم وفقك الله تعالى فإني نظرت في علوم التوراة والإنجيل والزبور والفرقان العظيم فوجدت جميع أنواع ا
11:6.english: Know that the scholar who does not act upon his knowledge is condemned by the Book, the Sunnah, and the sayings of the sages. God, exalted be He, said: {«يا أيها الذين آمنوا لم تقولون ما لا تفعلون * كبر مقتا عند الله أن تقولوا ما لا تفعلون»} ("O you who believe, why do you say what you do not do? Most hateful it is to God that you say what you do not do"). And He said: {«أتأمرون الناس بالبر وتنسون أنفسكم»} ("Do you command people to righteousness while you forget yourselves?"). And He said: {«ومن الناس من يعجبك قوله في الحياة الدنيا ويشهد الله على ما في قلبه وهو ألد الخصام»} ("And among people is he whose speech pleases you in the worldly life, and he calls God to witness what is in his heart, yet he is the fiercest of opponents").
11:6.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Book of Knowledge'

11:6.arabic: الأرض إلا على الله رزقها فعلمت أني واحد من هذه الدواب التي على الله رزقها فاشتغلت بما لله تعالى علي وتركت ما لي عنده الثامنة نظرت إلى هذا الخلق فرأيتهم كلهم متوكلين على مخلوق هذا على ضيعته وهذا على تجارته وهذا على صناعته وهذا على صحة بدنه وكل مخلوق متوكل على مخلوق مثله فرجعت إلى قوله تعالى ومن يتوكل على الله فهو حسبه فتوكلت على الله عز وجل فهو حسبي قال شقيق يا حاتم وفقك الله تعالى فإني نظرت في علوم التوراة والإنجيل والزبور والفرقان العظيم فوجدت جميع أنواع ال
11:6.english: Know that the scholar who does not act upon his knowledge is condemned by the Book, the Sunnah, and the sayings of the sages. God, exalted be He, said: {«يا أيها الذين آمنوا لم تقولون ما لا تفعلون * كبر مقتا عند الله أن تقولوا ما لا تفعلون»} ("O you who believe, why do you say what you do not do? Most hateful it is to God that you say what you do not do"). And He said: {«أتأمرون الناس بالبر وتنسون أنفسكم»} ("Do you command people to righteousness while you forget yourselves?"). And He said: {«ومن الناس من يعجبك قوله في الحياة الدنيا ويشهد الله على ما في قلبه وهو ألد الخصام»} ("And among people is he whose speech pleases you in the worldly life, and he calls God to witness what is in his heart, yet he is the fiercest of opponents").
11:6.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Monotheism and Reliance'

11:29.arabic: إلا من الله تعالى كما قال عز وجل {ويا قوم لا أسألكم عليه مالا إن أجري إلا على الله} فإن المال وما في الدنيا خادم البدن والبدن مركب النفس ومطيتها والمخدوم هو العلم إذ به شرف النفس فمن طلب بالعلم المال كان كمن مسح أسفل مداسه بوجهه لينظفه فجعل المخدوم خادما والخادم مخدوما وذلك هو الانتكاس على أم الرأس ومثله هو الذي يقوم في العرض الأكبر مع المجرمين ناكسي رءوسهم عند ربهم وعلى الجملة فالفضل والمنة للمعلم فانظر كيف انتهى أمر الدين إلى قوم يزعمون أن مقصودهم التقرب إلى الله تعالى بما هم فيه من علم الفقه والكلام والتدريس فيهما وفي غير
11:29.english: And those who turn aside to seek leadership (al-riyāsah) through the sciences have departed from the requirement of His saying, Exalted: {«The believers are but brothers»} (al-Ḥujurāt 49:10), and have entered into the implication of His saying, Exalted: {«Intimate friends on that Day will be enemies to one another, except the God-fearing»} (al-Zukhruf 43:67).
11:29.section_title_en: The Duties of the Teacher — Section 46: On the Teacher's Sincerity, His Conduct Toward Students, and the Signs of Those Who Seek the World Through Knowledge
11:29.anchors:
- Root: قصد (qaṣada)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of "intending, aiming toward, taking the straight path to a goal"; al-Ayn notes its use in aiming at a target.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Al-Qaṣd: the straightness of the path... al-iqtiṣād (moderation) is praiseworthy absolutely, as in generosity between extravagance and miserliness."
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "I intended him and intended for him" (physical direction). Metaphorical: "He was moderate in his livelihood... he who does not exceed the limit in a matter and is content with the middle way."
- Root: علم (ʿalima)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Knowledge as the perception of a thing's reality; al-Ayn traces its verbal forms across perception and knowing.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Al-ʿIlm: the apprehension of a thing by its true reality... two kinds: apprehension of the essence of a thing, and judgment upon a thing."
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "He was a sign (ʿalam) of knowledge." Metaphorical: "The landmarks (maʿālim) of the road" — the traces by which one is guided.
- Root: أخل (akhala)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "Al-Akhillāʾ: intimate friends (pl. of khalīl)." Al-Ayn: "Al-Maʾlaka: the message, because it is chewed (yuʾlak) in the mouth."
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Al-Khullāh: sincere friendship... {«Intimate friends on that Day will be enemies to one another, except the God-fearing»} (al-Zukhruf 43:67)."
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — "Innamā" restricts the predicate to the subject alone, excluding all else; used here to delimit the brotherhood of believers and the enmity of the wicked on the Day of Judgment.
11:29.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Book of Knowledge'

11:88.arabic: والله المعين لا رب غيره وما توفيقي إلا بالله وحسبنا الله ونعم الوكيل
11:88.english: As for what occurs in the year, after the days of Ramadan: the Day of 'Arafah, the Day of 'Āshūrā', the first ten days of Dhū al-Ḥijjah, and the first ten days of al-Muḥarram. All of the Sacred Months are occasions for fasting, and they are virtuous times. The Messenger of God, peace be upon him, used to fast much in Sha'bān, until it was thought that he was in Ramadan. (1) And in the report: "The best of fasting after the month of Ramadan is the month of God, al-Muḥarram" (2) — because it is the beginning of the year, and that its foundation be laid upon good is more beloved and more hopeful for the continuance of its blessing.
11:88.section_title_en: The Book of the Secrets of Fasting — Section 190: On the Virtuous Days and the Ranks of Voluntary Fasting
11:88.anchors:
- Root: صوم (ṣ-w-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning is "abstention" (imsāk) from any act—food, speech, or movement—as al-Raghib notes; a horse that refrains from fodder is called ṣā'im.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الصوم في الأصل: الإمساك عن الفعل" — fasting in its root is abstention from action, whether food, speech, or walking; hence the horse that refrains from movement or fodder is called ṣā'im.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): the month of fasting, "فمن شهد منكم الشهر فليصمه" — "so whoever witnesses the month, let him fast it." Metaphorical (majāz): "صام الفرس على آريه إذا لم يعتلف" — the horse "fasts" at its stall when it does not eat.
- Root: شهر (sh-h-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The month (al-shahr) is a well-known measure of time, marked by the appearance of the crescent or by a twelfth part of the solar circuit.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الشهر: مدة مشهورة بإهلال الهلال" — the month is a duration made known by the crescent's sighting; God says: {«شهر رمضان الذي أنزل فيه القرآن»} — "The month of Ramadan in which the Qur'an was sent down."
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "طلع الشهر: الهلال" — the month rises with the crescent. Metaphorical: "اشتهرت فلانا: استخففت به وفضحته" — to make one a "month-famous" is to expose and disgrace him.
- Root: رمض (r-m-ḍ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: From the intense heat of the sun-baked ground (al-ramḍā'); one whose feet are burned by it is ramiḍ.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "شهر رمضان هو من الرمض، أي: شدة وقع الشمس" — Ramadan derives from ramaḍ, the severity of the sun's heat; "أرمضته فرمض" — the heat burned him.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "مشى على الرمضاء وهي الحجارة التي اشتد عليها وقع الشمس فحميت" — walking on the ramḍā', stones heated by the sun's force. Metaphorical: "تداخلني من هذا الأمر رمض" — anxiety from an affair enters one, as if burning.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد (Restriction and Specification) — The phrase "إنما يكره لشيئين" (it is only disliked for two reasons) employs restriction (ḥaṣr) to delimit the scope of the ruling, a construction governed by the principles of focused predication in Al-Kitāb.
11:88.topic: Classical commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya Ulum al-Din, from 'Mysteries of Fasting'

11:88.arabic: الله أن تقولوا ما لا تفعلون وقال تعالى في قصة شعيب وما أريد أن أخالفكم إلى ما أنهاكم عنه وقال تعالى واتقوا الله ويعلمكم الله وقال تعالى واتقوا الله واعلموا واتقوا الله واسمعوا وقال تعالى لعيسى عليه السلام يا ابن مريم عظ نفسك فإن اتعظت فعظ الناس وإلا فاستحي مني وقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم مررت ليلة أسري بي بأقوام تقرض شفاههم بمقاريض من نار فقلت من أنتم فقالوا كنا نأمر بالخير ولا نأتيه وننهى عن الشر ونأتيه (2) وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم هلاك أمتي عالم فاجر وعابد جاهل وشر الشرار شرار العلماء وخير الخيار خيار العلماء (3) وقال الأوزاعي رحم
11:88.english:
[Root: ملح]
  • Lisan al-Arab: "الملح: ما يصلح الطعام، وجمعه ملوح وأملاح. والمليح: الحسن. والملاحة: الحسن. وملح الرجل يملح ملاحة: حسن. وتملح: تزين."
  • Al-Raghib (Al-Mufradat): "الملح: ما يحفظ الطعام ويمنع فساده، ويستعار لما يحفظ الإيمان والعلم من الفساد."
  • Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "ملح الماء: إذا كان فيه ملوحة. وملح الطعام: جعل فيه الملح. وهذا على الحقيقة، ويستعار الملح لما يصلح به الأمر."
  • Kitab al-Ayn: "الملح: معروف، والمليح: الحسن من كل شيء."
11:88.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Book of Knowledge'

11:88.arabic: مصطفى من أهل الأرض والسماء وما توفيقي إلا بالله عليه توكلت وإليه أنيب كتاب كسر الشهوتين وهو الكتاب الثالث من ربع المهلكات بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم الحمد لله المنفرد بالجلال في كبريائه وتعاليه المستحق للتحميد والتقديس والتسبيح والتنزيه القائم بالعدل فيما يبرمه ويقضيه المتطول بالفضل فيما ينعم به ويسديه المتكفل بحفظ عبده في جميع موارده ومجاريه المنعم عليه بما يزيد على مهمات مقاصده بل بما يفي بأمانيه فهو الذي يرشده ويهديه وهو الذي يميته ويحييه وإذا مرض فهو يشفيه وإذا ضعف فهو يقويه وهو الذي يوفقه للطاعة ويرتضيه وهو
11:88.english: And praise belongs to God alone, and blessings upon our master Muḥammad, upon his Family, his Companions, and upon every chosen servant from among the people of the earth and the heavens. And my success is only through God; upon Him I rely and unto Him I turn in repentance.
11:88.topic: Al-Ghazali on constant remembrance of God and contemplative invocations, from 'Breaking the Two Desires'

12:21.arabic: الدرجات قال الله عز وجل {وكذلك مكنا ليوسف في الأرض} وأيوب عليه السلام بعد المحنة العظيمة مكن قال الله تعالى وآتيناه أهله ومثلهم معهم الآية فهذا الكلام من الشافعي رحمه الله يدل على تبحره في أسرار القرآن واطلاعه على مقامات السائرين إلى الله تعالى من الأنبياء والأولياء وكل ذلك من علوم الآخرة وقيل للشافعي رحمه الله متى يكون الرجل عالما قال إذا تحقق في علم الدين فعلمه وتعرض لسائر العلوم فنظر فيما فاته فعند ذلك يكون عالما فإنه قيل لجالينوس إنك تأمر للداء الواحد بالأدوية الكثيرة المجمعة فقال إنما المقصود م
12:21.english: And al-Shafi'i, may God Most High have mercy upon him, said: "If you fear for your deed the blight of self-admiration (al-ʿujb), then consider: whose pleasure do you seek? Toward what reward do you yearn? From what punishment do you flee? What well-being do you thank? And what affliction do you recall? For if you reflect upon even one of these five qualities, your deed will appear small in your eyes." Observe how he mentioned the reality of ostentation and the remedy for self-admiration—both being among the gravest maladies of the heart.
12:21.section_title_en: The Revival of the Religious Sciences — Section 21: The Sciences of the Hereafter and the Signs of Sincere Intention in Knowledge
12:21.anchors:
- Root: مكن (m-k-n)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of establishing, empowering, and granting firm footing in a place or station.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "المكان عند أهل اللغة: الموضع الحاوي للشيء" — the place that encompasses a thing; theological nuance: divine empowerment (tamkīn) as a station granted after trial.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): "مكنته من الشيء وأمكنته منه، فتمكن منه واستمكن" — physical enabling. Metaphorical (Majaz): "الناس على مكناتهم: على مقارهم" — people upon their settled abodes/stations; here, the spiritual station of the prophets after tribulation.
- Root: محن (m-ḥ-n)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Testing, refining, and proving; a worn garment (mamḥūn) that has been stretched and expanded by use.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "المحن والامتحان نحو الابتلاء" — trial and testing akin to affliction; Quranic: {فامتحنوهن} (Al-Mumtahanah: 10) — the testing of hearts for sincerity.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "وقع في محنة ومحن" — falling into trial. Metaphorical: "محن الأديم: مدده حتى وسعه" — stretching hide until it widens; thus {امتحن الله قلوبهم} — God expands and purifies the heart through trial.
- Root: علم (ʿ-l-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Knowledge as the apprehension of a thing's reality; the mark (ʿalam) by which one is guided.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "العلم: إدراك الشيء بحقيقته" — knowledge is the perception of a thing in its true reality; two types: apprehension of essence, and judgment of existence or negation.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "ما علمت بخبرك: ما شعرت به" — to be aware. Metaphorical: "خفيت معالم الطريق" — the traces of the path that guide the seeker; here, the signs (ʿalāmāt) of sincere intention.
- Root: قلب (q-l-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Turning, overturning, and transforming a thing from one state to another.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "قلب الشيء: تصريفه وصرفه عن وجه إلى وجه" — the heart as that which is constantly turned and transformed; the seat of spiritual perception.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "قلب الشيء قلبا: حوله عن وجهه" — physical overturning. Metaphorical: "قلب التاجر السلعة" — the merchant scrutinizing his goods; "رجل قلب حول: يقلب الأمور" — one who turns matters over; here, the heart's gaze upon its own intentions.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — Used to confine a predicate to a single subject, as in "إنما المقصود منها واحد" (the intended aim is but one), emphasizing exclusive focus.
12:21.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Book of Knowledge'

12:56.arabic: فإذن جميع أقطار ملكوت السموات والأرض ميدان العارف يتبوأ منه حيث يشاء من غير حاجة إلى أن يتحرك إليها بجسمه وشخصه فهو من مطالعة جمال الملكوت في جنة عرضها السموات والأرض وكل عارف فله مثلها من غير أن يضيق بعضهم على بعض أصلا إلا أنهم يتفاوتون في سعة منتزهاتهم بقدر تفاوتهم في اتساع نظرهم
12:56.english: And just as the pleasure of leadership and honor is the most dominant of pleasures over the one who has surpassed the deficiency of childhood and imbecility, so too the pleasure of knowing Allah Most High, contemplating the beauty of the Presence of Lordship, and gazing upon the secrets of divine matters is more pleasurable than leadership — which is itself the highest of the pleasures that dominate creation. The utmost expression of it is to say: {«فَلَا تَعْلَمُ نَفْسٌ مَا أُخْفِيَ لَهُمْ مِنْ قُرَّةِ أَعْيُنٍ»} — "No soul knows what is hidden for them of comfort of the eyes" — and that He has prepared for them {«مَا لَا عَيْنٌ رَأَتْ وَلَا أُذُنٌ سَمِعَتْ وَلَا خَطَرَ عَلَى قَلْبِ بَشَرٍ»} — "what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and has never occurred to the heart of any human being."
12:56.section_title_en: Exposition that the Most Sublime and Highest of Pleasures is Knowledge of Allah Most High and the Contemplation of His Noble Countenance, and that No Other Pleasure Can Be Conceived to Outweigh It Save for One Who Has Been Deprived of This Very Pleasure
12:56.anchors:
- Root: لذذ (Ladhdh)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core sensory delight, sweetness, and gratification experienced through the faculties.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Pleasure (al-ladhdhah) as the perception of what is agreeable and harmonious with one's nature; its highest form is intellectual and spiritual, not merely corporeal.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah) for sensory delights; Metaphorical (Majaz) extension to intellectual and spiritual joys, such as dominance (al-ghalabah) and knowledge (al-ʿilm).
- Root: عرف (ʿArf)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To know by tracing effects and signs; cognizance through reflection.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Maʿrifah is the perception of a thing through reflection and contemplation of its trace; it is more specific than ʿilm and is the mode by which creatures know Allah—through His effects, not His essence.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal sense of recognition; here applied to the highest theological act of contemplative knowledge of the Divine.
- Root: غلب (Ghalab)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To overcome, conquer, or dominate.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-Ghalabah is qahr (compelling subjugation); victory of one over another.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical conquest; Metaphorical: the pleasure of intellectual and spiritual supremacy (riyāsah) over others.
- Root: صور (Ṣūr)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Form, shape, image.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Two types of form: sensible (perceived by the senses) and intelligible (perceived by the intellect alone); the latter is the higher, pertaining to spiritual realities.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical form; Metaphorical: inclination and turning of the heart toward a beloved object.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Restriction and Focused Predication (al-Ḥaṣr wa al-Taqyīd bi-innamā) — Used to delimit the exclusive superiority of divine knowledge over all other pleasures, and to structure conditional contrasts (law khuyyira... fa-in) for logical demonstration.
12:56.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Love, Longing, Intimacy and Contentment'

12:56.arabic: الدرجات قال الله عز وجل {وكذلك مكنا ليوسف في الأرض} وأيوب عليه السلام بعد المحنة العظيمة مكن قال الله تعالى وآتيناه أهله ومثلهم معهم الآية فهذا الكلام من الشافعي رحمه الله يدل على تبحره في أسرار القرآن واطلاعه على مقامات السائرين إلى الله تعالى من الأنبياء والأولياء وكل ذلك من علوم الآخرة وقيل للشافعي رحمه الله متى يكون الرجل عالما قال إذا تحقق في علم الدين فعلمه وتعرض لسائر العلوم فنظر فيما فاته فعند ذلك يكون عالما فإنه قيل لجالينوس إنك تأمر للداء الواحد بالأدوية الكثيرة المجمعة فقال إنما المقصود م
12:56.english: And al-Shafi'i, may God Most High have mercy upon him, said: "If you fear for your deed the blight of self-admiration (al-ʿujb), then consider: whose pleasure do you seek? Toward what reward do you yearn? From what punishment do you flee? What well-being do you thank? And what affliction do you recall? For if you reflect upon even one of these five qualities, your deed will appear small in your eyes." Observe how he mentioned the reality of ostentation and the remedy for self-admiration—both being among the gravest maladies of the heart.
12:56.section_title_en: The Revival of the Religious Sciences — Section 21: The Sciences of the Hereafter and the Signs of Sincere Intention in Knowledge
12:56.anchors:
- Root: مكن (m-k-n)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of establishing, empowering, and granting firm footing in a place or station.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "المكان عند أهل اللغة: الموضع الحاوي للشيء" — the place that encompasses a thing; theological nuance: divine empowerment (tamkīn) as a station granted after trial.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): "مكنته من الشيء وأمكنته منه، فتمكن منه واستمكن" — physical enabling. Metaphorical (Majaz): "الناس على مكناتهم: على مقارهم" — people upon their settled abodes/stations; here, the spiritual station of the prophets after tribulation.
- Root: محن (m-ḥ-n)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Testing, refining, and proving; a worn garment (mamḥūn) that has been stretched and expanded by use.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "المحن والامتحان نحو الابتلاء" — trial and testing akin to affliction; Quranic: {فامتحنوهن} (Al-Mumtahanah: 10) — the testing of hearts for sincerity.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "وقع في محنة ومحن" — falling into trial. Metaphorical: "محن الأديم: مدده حتى وسعه" — stretching hide until it widens; thus {امتحن الله قلوبهم} — God expands and purifies the heart through trial.
- Root: علم (ʿ-l-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Knowledge as the apprehension of a thing's reality; the mark (ʿalam) by which one is guided.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "العلم: إدراك الشيء بحقيقته" — knowledge is the perception of a thing in its true reality; two types: apprehension of essence, and judgment of existence or negation.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "ما علمت بخبرك: ما شعرت به" — to be aware. Metaphorical: "خفيت معالم الطريق" — the traces of the path that guide the seeker; here, the signs (ʿalāmāt) of sincere intention.
- Root: قلب (q-l-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Turning, overturning, and transforming a thing from one state to another.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "قلب الشيء: تصريفه وصرفه عن وجه إلى وجه" — the heart as that which is constantly turned and transformed; the seat of spiritual perception.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "قلب الشيء قلبا: حوله عن وجهه" — physical overturning. Metaphorical: "قلب التاجر السلعة" — the merchant scrutinizing his goods; "رجل قلب حول: يقلب الأمور" — one who turns matters over; here, the heart's gaze upon its own intentions.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — Used to confine a predicate to a single subject, as in "إنما المقصود منها واحد" (the intended aim is but one), emphasizing exclusive focus.
12:56.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Book of Knowledge'

13:21.arabic: فهو في النار وقاض قضى بغير ما أمر الله به فهو في النار (2) وقال كعب رحمه الله يكون في آخر الزمان علماء يزهدون الناس في الدنيا ولا يزهدون ويخوفون الناس ولا يخافون وينهون عن غشيان الولاة ويأتونهم ويؤثرون الدنيا على الآخرة يأكلون بألسنتهم يقربون الأغنياء دون الفقراء يتغايرون على العلم كما تتغاير النساء على الرجال يغضب أحدهم على جليسه إذا جالس غيره أولئك الجبارون أعداء الرحمن وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم إن الشيطان ربما يسوفكم بالعلم فقيل يا رسول الله وكيف ذلك قال صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول اطلب الع
13:21.english: Know that the scholar who does not act upon his knowledge is condemned by the Book, the Sunnah, and the sayings of the sages. God, exalted be He, said: {«يا أيها الذين آمنوا لم تقولون ما لا تفعلون * كبر مقتا عند الله أن تقولوا ما لا تفعلون»} ("O you who believe, why do you say what you do not do? Most hateful it is to God that you say what you do not do"). And He said: {«أتأمرون الناس بالبر وتنسون أنفسكم»} ("Do you command people to righteousness while you forget yourselves?"). And He said: {«ومن الناس من يعجبك قوله في الحياة الدنيا ويشهد الله على ما في قلبه وهو ألد الخصام»} ("And among people is he whose speech pleases you in the worldly life, and he calls God to witness what is in his heart, yet he is the fiercest of opponents").
13:21.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Book of Knowledge'

13:34.arabic: والحسد نار محرقة فمن بلي به فهو في العذاب في الدنيا ولعذاب الآخرة أشد وأعظم ولذلك قال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما خذوا العلم حيث وجدتموه ولا تقبلوا قول الفقهاء بعضهم على بعض فإنهم يتغايرون كما تتغاير التيوس في الزريبة ومنها التكبر والترفع على الناس فقد قال صلى الله عليه وسلم من تكبر وضعه الله ومن تواضع رفعه الله (2) وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم حكاية عن الله تعالى العظمة إزاري والكبرياء ردائي فمن نازعني فيهما قصمته (3) ولا ينفك المناظر عن التكبر على الأقران والأمثال والترفع إلى فوق قدره حتى إنهم ليتقاتلون على
13:34.english:
**QUAD_ANCHORS:**
- Root: نظر (naẓara)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to look, to examine, to consider; al-munāẓarah is mutual examination/argumentation between two parties.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: naẓar as intellectual contemplation (taʾammul bi-l-baṣīrah); munāẓarah as dialectical exchange.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: sitting face-to-face in debate; Metaphorical: disputation for victory.
- Root: غلب (ghalaba)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to overcome, to conquer, to prevail.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-ghalabah as seeking to dominate another in argument.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: victory in combat; Metaphorical: intellectual supremacy.
- Root: حسد (ḥasada)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to envy, to wish removal of blessings from another.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: envy as wishing deprivation of blessings from the deserving — among the basest traits.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: envy of another's blessing; Metaphorical: consuming fire of the soul.
- Root: كبر (kabura)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to be great, to be haughty.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-kibr as self-elevation above others; condemned by God.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: greatness; Metaphorical: arrogance and pride.
- Root: غيب (ghāba)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to be absent, to be hidden.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-ghībah as mentioning another with what he dislikes in his absence — likened to eating carrion.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: backbiting; Metaphorical: consuming the flesh of one's brother.
- Root: راءى (rāʾā)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to show off, to display.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-riyāʾ as performing acts for the sake of being seen — hidden shirk.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: showing good deeds; Metaphorical: seeking reputation.
- Root: نفس (nafs)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: self, soul, spirit.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: tazkiyat al-nafs as self-praise and self-purification — forbidden by God.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: self; Metaphorical: self-commendation.
- Root: حقd (ḥaqida)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to bear malice, to harbor resentment.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-ḥiqd as nursing enmity in the heart — negated from the believer.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: bearing grudge; Metaphorical: hidden rancor.
- Root: نفاق (nifāq)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: hypocrisy, showing contrary to what one conceals.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: hypocrisy in deeds — outward display contrary to inward state.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: hypocrisy in faith; Metaphorical: hypocrisy in character.
- Root: علم (ʿalima)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to know, to perceive.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: knowledge as apprehension of reality — its pursuit for other than God is destructive.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: knowledge; Metaphorical: the dangerous burden of the scholar.
- Root: جدل (jadala)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to argue, to dispute.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-jidāl as contention; al-mirāʾ as disputation with falsehood — condemned.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: argumentation; Metaphorical: obstinate disputation.
- Root: شرك (sharaka)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to associate, to share.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-riyāʾ as hidden shirk — associating others with God in intention.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: polytheism; Metaphorical: hidden association in deeds.
- Root: موت (māta)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to die.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: death as separation of soul from body; spiritual death as ruin of the soul.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical death; Metaphorical: spiritual destruction.
- Root: حيى (ḥayiya)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to live.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: life as the power of perception; eternal life as the reward of the righteous.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical life; Metaphorical: spiritual vitality.
- Root: هلك (halaka)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to perish, to be destroyed.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-halāk as ruin; eternal destruction as everlasting punishment.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: destruction; Metaphorical: eternal ruin.
- Root: رياء (riyāʾ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: showing off, ostentation.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: riyāʾ as the incurable disease calling to the greatest sins.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: ostentation; Metaphorical: spiritual disease.
- Root: جاه (jāh)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: rank, status, prestige.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: love of status (ḥubb al-jāh) among the destructive traits.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: position; Metaphorical: seeking prestige.
- Root: مباهاة (mubāhāh)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: mutual boasting, vying in splendor.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: mubāhāh as each seeking to display superiority over the other.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: mutual boasting; Metaphorical: rivalry in honor.
- Root: مماراة (mumārāh)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: disputation, wrangling.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-mirāʾ as contentious argument — condemned by the Prophet.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: disputation; Metaphorical: obstinate wrangling.
- Root: فخر (fakhara)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to boast, to pride oneself.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-fakhr as self-glorification — among the blameworthy traits.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: boasting; Metaphorical: vainglory.
- Root: عجب (ʿajiba)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to wonder, to be amazed.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-ʿujb as self-admiration — among the destructive traits.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: wonder; Metaphorical: self-conceit.
- Root: بغض (baghiḍa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to hate, to detest.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-baghdāʾ as mutual hatred — contrary to brotherhood.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: hatred; Metaphorical: mutual enmity.
- Root: غضب (ghaḍiba)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to be angry.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-ghaḍab as anger — among the blameworthy traits.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: anger; Metaphorical: rage.
- Root: طمع (ṭamiʿa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to covet, to desire.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-ṭamaʿ as covetousness — among the destructive traits.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: desire; Metaphorical: greed.
- Root: أشر (ashira)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to be exultant, to be insolent.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-ashar as excessive joy and insolence — blameworthy.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: exultation; Metaphorical: insolence.
- Root: بطر (baṭira)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to be arrogant, to be ungrateful.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-baṭar as arrogance in prosperity — among the destructive traits.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: arrogance; Metaphorical: ingratitude for blessings.
- Root: خيلاء (khuyalāʾ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: pride, haughtiness.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-khuyalāʾ as pride and conceit — blameworthy.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: pride; Metaphorical: haughty bearing.
- Root: خشية (khashyah)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: fear, awe.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-khashyah as reverential fear — among the traits of the believers.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: fear; Metaphorical: reverential awe.
- Root: رحمة (raḥmah)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: mercy, compassion.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-raḥmah as tenderness of heart — among the traits of the believers.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: mercy; Metaphorical: compassion.
- Root: غفلة (ghaflah)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: heedlessness, inattention.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-ghaflah as heedlessness — contrary to vigilance.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: inattention; Metaphorical: spiritual heedlessness.
- Root: خشوع (khushūʿ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: humility, submissiveness.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-khushūʿ as humility — among the traits of the believers.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: humility; Metaphorical: devotional submission.
- Root: تذكير (tadhkīr)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: reminding, admonishing.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-tadhkīr as reminding of God — a righteous act.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: reminding; Metaphorical: preaching.
- Root: وعظ (waʿaẓa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to admonish, to exhort.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-waʿẓ as exhortation to obedience and warning against disobedience.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: admonition; Metaphorical: sermonizing.
- Root: فتوى (fatwā)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: legal ruling, formal opinion.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-fatwā as clarification of legal rulings.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: legal opinion; Metaphorical: religious authority.
- Root: قضاء (qaḍāʾ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: judgment, decree.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-qaḍāʾ as judgment between people.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: judgment; Metaphorical: judicial authority.
- Root: وقف (waqafa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to stop, to stand.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-waqf as endowment of property for charitable purposes.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: standing; Metaphorical: religious endowment.
- Root: ثواب (thawāb)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: reward, recompense.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-thawāb as divine recompense for righteous deeds.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: reward; Metaphorical: divine recompense.
- Root: عذاب (ʿadhāb)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: punishment, torment.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-ʿadhāb as divine punishment for the disobedient.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: punishment; Metaphorical: divine chastisement.
- Root: ملك (malaka)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to possess, to rule.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-mulk as sovereignty; al-mulk al-muʾabbad as eternal sovereignty in Paradise.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: dominion; Metaphorical: eternal kingdom.
- Root: نعيم (naʿīm)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: bliss, delight.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-naʿīm as bliss; al-naʿīm al-sarmad as everlasting bliss.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: delight; Metaphorical: eternal bliss.
- Root: رخصة (rukhaṣah)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: concession, dispensation.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-rukhaṣah as legal concession.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: concession; Metaphorical: legal dispensation.
- Root: رياسة (riyāsah)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: leadership, headship.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: love of leadership among the destructive traits.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: leadership; Metaphorical: seeking authority.
- Root: اندراس (indirās)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: effacement, obliteration.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: indirās al-ʿulūm as the obliteration of the sciences.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: effacement; Metaphorical: extinction of knowledge.
- Root: صبيان (ṣibyān)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: boys, children.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: children's motivation for learning through play.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: boys; Metaphorical: pupils.
- Root: مكتب (maktab)
  * Lisan / Ayn- Root: مكتب (maktab)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: place of instruction, school for boys.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: the elementary school where children are taught.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: school; Metaphorical: place of elementary learning.
- Root: خلاق (khilāq)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: portion, share, lot.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: "no portion" (lā khilāq) in the Hereafter — utter deprivation of divine reward.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: share; Metaphorical: spiritual allotment in the afterlife.
- Root: فاجر (fājir)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: wicked, immoral, profligate.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: the dissolute one who commits sins openly.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: sinner; Metaphorical: one through whom God nonetheless supports religion.
- Root: شمع (shamʿ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: candle, wax taper.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: the candle as parable — consuming itself while giving light to others.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: candle; Metaphorical: one who destroys himself but benefits others.
- Root: نار (nār)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: fire.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: fire as parable — consuming itself and all around it.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: fire; Metaphorical: one who destroys himself and others.
- Root: سعد (saʿida)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to be fortunate, to prosper.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: saʿādah as felicity — success in the Hereafter.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: good fortune; Metaphorical: eternal felicity.
- Root: شقي (shaqiya)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to be wretched, to be miserable.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: shaqāwah as wretchedness — ruin in the Hereafter.
