  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: misery; Metaphorical: eternal ruin.
- Root: أخلص (akhlaṣa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to purify, to be sincere.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: ikhlāṣ as purifying intention for God alone — the condition of acceptance.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: sincerity; Metaphorical: pure devotion.
- Root: ريب (rāba)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to doubt, to suspect.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-rayb as doubt and uncertainty — to be dispelled by evidence.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: doubt; Metaphorical: skepticism.
13:34.topic: Al-Ghazali on purifying the character, moral diseases, and spiritual remedies, from 'Book of Knowledge'

13:34.arabic: أن يأمر بالمعروف فليوطن نفسه على الصبر وليثق بالثواب من الله فمن وثق بالثواب من الله لم يجد مس الأذى فإذن من آداب الحسبة توطين النفس على الصبر ولذلك قرن الله تعالى الصبر بالأمر بالمعروف فقال حاكيا عن لقمان يا بني أقم الصلاة وأمر بالمعروف وانه عن المنكر واصبر على ما أصابك ومن الآداب تقليل العلائق حتى لا يكثر خوفه وقطع الطمع عن الخلائق حتى تزول عنه المداهنة فقد روي عن بعض المشايخ أنه كان له سنور وكان يأخذ من قصاب في جواره كل يوم شيئا من الغدد لسنوره فرأى على القصاب منكرا فدخل الدار أولا وأخرج السنور ثم جاء واحتسب
13:34.english: We do not mean by this that commanding right becomes prohibited by reason of one's sinfulness — rather, its effect upon hearts falls away by the manifestation of his sinfulness to the people. For it has been related from Anas, may God be pleased with him, who said: "We said, 'O Messenger of God, shall we not command right until we have acted upon it entirely, and shall we not forbid wrong until we have shunned it entirely?' He said, may God's peace and blessings be upon him: 'Rather, command right even if you do not act upon it entirely, and forbid wrong even if you do not shun it entirely.'"
13:34.section_title_en: On Gentleness in Commanding Right and Forbidding Wrong — The Etiquette of the Muḥtasib
13:34.anchors:
- Root: عيب (ʿayb)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root meaning — defect, blemish, reproach; to find fault with something.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance — the reproach of intellect (ʿaql) is the severest form of deficiency, for it touches the very faculty by which one is distinguished from beasts.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal vs Metaphorical — here used metaphorically: the reproach falls upon his intellect, i.e., the deficiency of his discernment becomes manifest.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Restriction (Bāb al-Ḥaṣr) — "فإنما يزرى على عقله" restricts the object of reproach to the intellect alone, excluding the person's faith or status.
13:34.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Enjoining Good and Forbidding Evil'

13:43.arabic: {إنما يخشى الله من عباده العلماء} وقال تعالى {قل كفى بالله شهيدا بيني وبينكم ومن عنده علم الكتاب} وقال تعالى {قال الذي عنده علم من الكتاب أنا آتيك به} تنبيها على أنه اقتدر بقوة العلم وقال عز وجل {وقال الذين أوتوا العلم ويلكم ثواب الله خير لمن آمن وعمل صالحا} بين أن عظم قدر الآخرة يعلم بالعلم وقال تعالى {وتلك الأمثال نضربها للناس وما يعقلها إلا العالمون} وقال تعالى {ولو ردوه إلى الرسول وإلى أولي الأمر منهم لعلمه الذين يستنبطونه منهم} رد حكمه في الوقائع إلى استنباطهم وألحق رتبتهم برتبة الأنبياء في كشف حكم الله وقيل في قوله تعالى يا بني آدم قد
13:43.english: How He, Glorified and Exalted, began with Himself, then seconded with the angels, and thirded with the people of knowledge — and sufficient for you is this as honor, excellence, splendor, and nobility. And God, Exalted, said: {«يرفع الله الذين آمنوا منكم والذين أوتوا العلم درجات»} — "God will raise those who have believed among you and those who have been given knowledge, in degrees." Ibn ʿAbbās, may God be pleased with them both, said: For the scholars there are degrees above the believers, seven hundred degrees, and between each two degrees is a distance of five hundred years' journey.
13:43.section_title_en: The Book of Knowledge — Section 4: The Excellence of Knowledge and the Scholars
13:43.anchors:
- Root: علم (ʿ-l-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root meaning of knowing, perceiving a thing in its true reality; the act of apprehension and judgment.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "العلم: إدراك الشيء بحقيقته" — knowledge is the apprehension of a thing in its true reality, divided into apprehension of the essence and judgment of existence or non-existence.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) usage denotes genuine knowing; metaphorical (majāz) usage extends to signs, landmarks, and traces that guide to knowledge.
- Root: درج (d-r-j)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Degrees, steps, ascending stations; the root denotes gradation and progressive elevation.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الدرجة نحو المنزلة، لكن يقال للمنزلة: درجة إذا اعتبرت بالصعود" — a degree is a station considered by ascent, not horizontal extension.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical steps of ascent. Metaphorical: "لفلان درجة رفيعة" — lofty rank; "امش في مدارج الحق" — walk in the paths of truth.
- Root: يوم (y-w-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: A day; a period of time from sunrise to sunset, or any duration whatsoever.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "اليوم يعبر به عن وقت طلوع الشمس إلى غروبها. وقد يعبر به عن مدة من الزمان أي مدة كانت" — the day denotes the time of the sun's rising to its setting, and may denote any period of time whatsoever.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the solar day. Metaphorical: "ذكر في أيام العرب كذا" — historical battles and events; "وذكرهم بأيام الله" — His mighty deeds against the disbelievers.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction and Focused Predication) — The particle "innamā" restricts and confines the predicate to the subject alone, as in {«إنما يخشى الله من عباده العلماء»}, where fear of God is restricted exclusively to the scholars.
13:43.topic: Al-Ghazali on the journey of the soul, death, and the Hereafter, from 'Book of Knowledge'

16:12.arabic: والعالم الراسخ هو الذي يطلع على أن الشمس والقمر والنجوم مسخرات بأمره سبحانه وتعالى ومثال نظر الضعيف إلى حصول ضوء الشمس عقيب طلوع الشمس مثال النملة لو خلق لها عقل وكانت على سطح قرطاس وهي تنظر إلى سواد الخط يتجدد فتعتقد أنه فعل القلم ولا تترقى في نظرها إلى مشاهدة الأصابع ثم منها إلى اليد ثم منها إلى الإرادة المحركة اليد ثم منها إلى الكاتب القادر المريد ثم منه إلى خالق اليد والقدرة والإرادة فأكثر نظر الخلق مقصور على الأسباب القريبة السافلة مقطوع من الترقي إلى مسبب الأسباب فهذا أحد أسباب النهي عن النجوم وثانيها
16:12.english: You may say: "Knowledge is the apprehension of a thing as it is, and it is among the attributes of God, exalted be He. How then can a thing be knowledge, and while being knowledge, be blameworthy?"
16:12.section_title_en: Section 25 — On the Exposition of the Manner in Which Some Sciences May Be Blameworthy, and the Exposition of the Alteration of the Names of the Sciences — Namely Jurisprudence (Fiqh), Knowledge (ʿIlm), Divine Unity (Tawḥīd), Reminder (Tadhkīr), and Wisdom (Ḥikmah) — and the Exposition of the Praiseworthy Measure of the Religious Sciences and the Blameworthy Measure Thereof
16:12.anchors:
- Root: ع ل م (ʿ-l-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root denotes the trace or mark by which a thing is known; ʿilm is the apprehension of a thing as it is (idrāk al-shayʾ ʿalā mā huwa bihi), encompassing both the perception of the thing's essence and the judgment of its attributes.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): ʿIlm is "the apprehension of a thing by its reality" (إدراك الشيء بحقيقته), divided into the apprehension of the thing's essence and the judgment upon it. As a divine attribute, it is not blameworthy in itself; blame attaches only to its relation to human subjects.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Distinguishes literal knowledge (ḥaqīqah) from the metaphorical extension whereby a "learned" man may be called ignorant when his knowledge harms him — the term ʿilm is transferred (manqūl) in blame contexts to denote what is not truly beneficial knowledge.
- Root: س ب ب (s-b-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The rope by which one climbs to the palm-tree; extended to any means by which one reaches a thing.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Every means by which one arrives at a thing is called a sabab" — thus the science of the properties of substances and stellar computations is a "cause" (sabab) that may lead to harm, and the means to evil is evil.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal usage denotes a physical cord or tie; metaphorical usage (majāz) extends to any instrumental cause, whether beneficial or harmful.
- Root: ع ق ل (ʿ-q-l)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The intellect as that which binds and restrains; its root sense is of a fetter or halter that prevents the soul from straying.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The intellect is that by which one apprehends realities; its proper function is to lead one to the truth of prophecy, after which it must be restrained from independent speculation in matters beyond its scope.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal usage denotes the binding of the camel; metaphorical usage denotes the restraint of the soul from error.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Restriction and Focused Predication (باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما) — When the author states "knowledge is not blamed for its essence but only in relation to servants for one of three causes," the restriction (ḥaṣr) via "innamā" confines blame to the relational aspect, not the essence, requiring the translator to preserve this precise logical scope.
16:12.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'Book of Knowledge'

16:43.arabic: الدين} وقوله عز وجل {فاسألوا أهل الذكر إن كنتم لا تعلمون} وأما الأخبار فقوله صلى الله عليه وسلم من سلك طريقا يطلب فيه علما سلك الله به طريقا إلى الجنة (1) وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم إن الملائكة لتضع أجنحتها لطالب العلم رضاء بما يصنع (2) وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم لأن تغدو فتتعلم بابا من العلم خير من أن تصلي مائة ركعة (3) وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم باب من العلم يتعلمه الرجل خير له من الدنيا وما فيها (4) وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم اطلبوا العلم ولو بالصين (1) وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم طلب العلم ف
16:43.english: As for the Quranic verses, there is the saying of God Most High: {«فلولا نفر من كل فرقة منهم طائفة ليتفقهوا في الدين»} — "Why then did not a party from every section of them go forth, that they might gain deep comprehension in the religion?" — and His saying, Mighty and Majestic: {«فاسألوا أهل الذكر إن كنتم لا تعلمون»} — "So ask the people of remembrance if you do not know."
16:43.section_title_en: The Virtue of Seeking Knowledge (Faḍīlat al-Taʿallum)
16:43.anchors:
- Root: فقه (Fiqh)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning is "comprehension" and "understanding" — the penetration into the inner meaning of speech, distinguished from mere hearing (samāʿ).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In the theological register, *tafaqquh* (تفقه) is the deep, exhaustive comprehension of the religious sciences — not mere memorization but the attainment of the realities of juridico-theological matters.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) usage denotes intellectual penetration; metaphorical (majāz) usage extends to any deep discernment of subtle meanings.
- Root: سأل (Saʾala)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To ask, to inquire, to seek information — the root act of petitioning for knowledge from its possessor.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Asking (*suʾāl*) is the divinely mandated means for the ignorant to access knowledge, as per {«فاسألوا أهل الذكر»} — it is the key that unlocks the treasuries of knowledge.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal usage is the verbal request; the Prophet's statement "العلم خزائن مفاتيحها السؤال" employs a metaphor (majāz) likening knowledge to locked treasuries and questioning to their keys.
- Root: طلب (Ṭalab)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To seek, to pursue, to search out a thing — whether a physical object or a meaning.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الطلب: الفحص عن وجود الشيء، عينا كان أو معنى" — the earnest investigation into the existence of a thing, whether concrete or conceptual. In the religious context, *ṭalab al-ʿilm* is the pursuit of that which revives the religion.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal usage is the physical pursuit of a quarry; the ḥadīth "من سلك طريقا يطلب فيه علما" employs the metaphor of the *path* (ṭarīq) as the means of pursuit, and the divine recompense as the *path to Paradise*.
- Root: غدو (Ghadā)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To go out early in the morning, to set forth at dawn — the time of vigorous, purposeful departure.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal usage denotes the morning journey; in the saying of Abū al-Dardāʾ, "الغدو إلى طلب العلم" is metaphorically elevated to the rank of *jihād* — the early morning departure for knowledge is a martial expedition of the soul.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Interposition (al-Faṣl bayna al-Jār wa-al-Majrūr) — The syntactic principle governing the separation of the prepositional phrase from its governing verb, as in "سلك الله به طريقا إلى الجنة," where the divine agency is interposed between the act and its recompense, indicating the causal nexus.
16:43.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Book of Knowledge'

17:72.arabic: تعمي القلوب التي في الصدور وقال تعالى ومن كان في هذه أعمى فهو في الآخرة أعمى وأضل سبيلا وهذه الأمور التي كشفت للأنبياء بعضها كان بالبصر وبعضها كان بالبصيرة وسمي الكل رؤية وبالجملة من لم تكن بصيرته الباطنة ثاقبة لم يعلق به من الدين إلا قشوره وأمثلته دون لبابه وحقائقه فهذه أقسام ما ينطلق اسم العقل عليها
17:72.english: I say: Know that the washing of the eye is forbidden — that is, the eye of insight (ʿayn al-baṣīrah) is not to be washed with the water of blind imitation and mere hearsay, for it is the organ by which the realities of the intellect are disclosed. And the divisions of what the name "intellect" (al-ʿaql) is applied to have become clear: it is said of the inborn faculty (al-gharīzah), and it is said of the knowledge that is acquired through that faculty, and it is said of the state of that knowledge when it governs the soul, and it is said of the very actions that proceed from that governance.
17:72.section_title_en: The Washing of the Eye is Forbidden — On the True Meaning of Intellect (ʿAql) and Its Divisions
17:72.anchors:
- Root: عقل (ʿAql)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The root denotes binding, restraining, and holding back — the intellect is that which restrains the soul from base desires and prevents it from straying.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "العقل يقال للقوة المتهيئة لقبول العلم، ويقال للعلم الذي يستفيده الإنسان بتلك القوة عقل" — al-ʿaql is said of the faculty prepared to receive knowledge, and it is also said of the knowledge acquired by that faculty. It is the instrument of divine discernment and the locus of taklīf (moral responsibility).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): the inborn faculty of discernment. Metaphorical (Majaz): "نخلة لا تعقل الإبار إذا لم تقبله" — a palm tree that does not accept pollination is said to be "not to ʿaqil" the pollen, extending the root to the sense of "accepting/receiving." Thus, knowledge is called ʿaql metaphorically as its fruit.
- Root: بصر (Baṣar)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Sight, perception — both of the eye and of the heart.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "البصر يقال للجارحة الناظرة... ويقال لقوة القلب المدركة: بصيرة وبصر" — baṣar is said of the seeing organ, and of the perceiving power of the heart: baṣīrah and baṣar. The inner sight (baṣīrah) perceives immaterial realities.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: ocular vision. Metaphorical: "هذه آية مبصرة" — this is an illuminating sign; "واجعلني بصيرة عليهم أي رقيبا وشاهدا" — make me a watcher over them. The inner eye perceives what the outer eye cannot.
- Root: فطر (Faṭara)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To split, cleave, originate, create — the primordial act of divine creation.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "أصل الفطر: الشق طولا... وفطر الله الخلق" — the root is splitting lengthwise; God's "fatr" of creation is His originating of things. "فطرة الله التي فطر الناس عليها" — the primordial disposition upon which God originated mankind.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "فطر الله الخلق، وهو فاطر السموات: مبتدعها" — God originated creation; He is the Originator of the heavens. "وكل مولود يولد على الفطرة" — every newborn is born upon the fiṭrah, i.e., the innate disposition receptive to the religion of truth.
- Root: نفس (Nafs)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Self, soul, spirit; the innermost reality of a thing.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "النفس: الروح... وقوله: تعلم ما في نفسي ولا أعلم ما في نفسك" — nafs is the spirit/soul; "You know what is in my nafs and I know not what is in Your nafs" — the nafs is the seat of inner assent and recognition.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the self. Metaphorical: "دفق نفسه أي دمه" — he poured out his nafs, i.e., his blood. The nafs is the locus of the primordial covenant (mīthāq).
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — The construction "إنما العاقل من آمن بالله" restricts the predicate: the intellect is not merely a faculty of cleverness but is defined by its fruit — faith and God-consciousness (taqwā).
17:72.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Book of Knowledge'

17:74.arabic: تخاف فتنته وقد قيل لسيد المرسلين صلى الله عليه وسلم ولولا أن ثبتناك لقد كدت تركن إليهم شيئا قليلا وقال سهل رحمه الله العلم كله دنيا والآخرة منه العمل به والعمل كله هباء إلا الإخلاص وقال الناس كلهم موتى إلا العلماء والعلماء سكارى إلا العاملين والعاملون كلهم مغرورون إلا المخلصين والمخلص على وجل حتى يدري ماذا يختم له به وقال أبو سليمان الداراني رحمه الله إذا طلب الرجل الحديث أو تزوج أو سافر في طلب المعاش فقد ركن إلى الدنيا وإنما أراد به طلب الأسانيد العالية أو طلب الحديث الذي لا يحتاج إليه في طلب الآخرة وقال عيسى عليه السلام كيف يكون من أهل العلم
17:74.english:
[Root: ملح]
  • Lisan al-Arab: "الملح: ما يصلح الطعام، وجمعه ملوح وأملاح. والمليح: الحسن. والملاحة: الحسن. وملح الرجل يملح ملاحة: حسن. وتملح: تزين."
  • Al-Raghib (Al-Mufradat): "الملح: ما يحفظ الطعام ويمنع فساده، ويستعار لما يحفظ الإيمان والعلم من الفساد."
  • Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "ملح الماء: إذا كان فيه ملوحة. وملح الطعام: جعل فيه الملح. وهذا على الحقيقة، ويستعار الملح لما يصلح به الأمر."
  • Kitab al-Ayn: "الملح: معروف، والمليح: الحسن من كل شيء."
17:74.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'Book of Knowledge'

18:15.arabic: الله تعالى بين من افترى على الله كذبا وبين من كذب بالحق فقال تعالى ومن أظلم ممن افترى على الله كذبا أو كذب بالحق لما جاءه وقال تعالى فمن أظلم ممن كذب على الله وكذب بالصدق إذ جاءه ومنها الرياء وملاحظة الخلق والجهد في استمالة قلوبهم وصرف وجوههم والرياء هو الداء العضال الذي يدعو إلى أكبر الكبائر كما سيأتي في كتاب الرياء والمناظر لا يقصد إلا الظهور عند الخلق وانطلاق ألسنتهم بالثناء عليه فهذه عشر خصال من أمهات الفواحش الباطنة سوى ما يتفق لغير المتماسكين منهم من الخصام المؤدي إلى الضرب

18:67.arabic: نبه الله تعالى بقصة الخضر وموسى عليهما السلام حيث قال الخضر {إنك لن تستطيع معي صبرا وكيف تصبر على ما لم تحط به خبرا} ثم شرط عليه السكوت والتسليم فقال {فإن اتبعتني فلا تسألني عن شيء حتى أحدث لك منه ذكرا} ثم لم يصبر ولم يزل في مراودته إلى أن كان ذلك سبب الفراق بينهما وبالجملة كل متعلم استبقى لنفسه رأيا واختيارا دون اختيار المعلم فاحكم عليه بالإخفاق والخسران فإن قلت فقد قال الله تعالى {فاسألوا أهل الذكر إن كنتم لا تعلمون} فالسؤال مأمور به فاعلم أنه كذلك ولكن فيما يأذن المعلم في السؤال عنه فإن السؤال عما لم تبلغ مرتبتك إل
18:67.english: I say: Knowledge is like a torrent that is hostile to the elevated place — it flows only to the low ground. Thus knowledge is not attained except through humility and the casting of one's hearing [in attentive submission]. God — exalted is He — said: {«Indeed in that is a reminder for whoever has a heart or casts his hearing while present as a witness»} (Q 50:37). And the meaning of his being "one having a heart" is that he should be receptive to knowledge, comprehending it. But then the capacity for understanding does not avail him until he casts his hearing while being a present witness — present of heart — so that he may receive everything that is cast to him with excellence of listening, supplication, gratitude, joy, and acceptance of the benefaction.
18:67.section_title_en: The Revival of the Religious Sciences — Book I, Section 42: On the Duties of the Student (Ādāb al-Mutaʿallim)
18:67.anchors:
- Root: ع ل م (ʿ-l-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of knowing, perceiving a thing in its reality; the mark, trace, or sign by which one is guided.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "العلم: إدراك الشيء بحقيقته" — knowledge is the apprehension of a thing in its true reality, divided into apprehension of the essence and judgment upon it.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): "هو من أعلام العلم الخافقه" — he is among the lofty banners of knowledge. Metaphorical (majāz): "خفيت معالم الطريق" — the waymarks of the road are hidden, i.e., the traces by which one is guided.
- Root: س م ع (s-m-ʿ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Hearing, listening; the ear; obedience and acceptance.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Hearing with attentive presence of heart, not merely the physical sensation of sound.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: auditory perception. Metaphorical: "ألقى السمع" — to cast one's hearing, i.e., to listen with full attentiveness and submission.
- Root: ق ل ب (q-l-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The heart; to turn, overturn, or transform a thing from one state to another.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "قلب الشيء: تصريفه وصرفه عن وجه إلى وجه" — the turning of a thing from one face to another; the heart as that which is ever-turning between states.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "قلب الشيء قلبا: حوله عن وجهه" — to turn a thing from its face. Metaphorical: "رجل قلب حول: يقلب الأمور ويحتال" — a man who turns matters over and devises means.
- Root: ب ح ر (b-ḥ-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The sea; vast expanse of water.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "أصل البحر: كل مكان واسع جامع للماء الكثير" — the sea is every vast place gathering much water; then metaphorically applied to one who expands deeply into a domain.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Metaphorical: "تبحر في العلم واستبحر فيه" — he plunged deep into knowledge and expanded therein like a sea.
- Sibawayh Rule: Bāb al-ḥaṣr wa-l-taqyīd bi-innamā (Restriction and Focused Predication) — the particle innamā restricts the predicate to the subject alone, negating all else; applied here to the exclusive path of the student's submission to the teacher's direction.

18:75.arabic: قصدني سبع فخرج وصاح به وقال ألم أقل لك لا تتعرض لضيفاني فتنحى الأسد فتطهرت فلما رجعت قال لي اشتغلتم بتقويم الظاهر فخفتم الأسد واشتغلنا بتقويم البواطن فخافنا الأسد وما حكي من تفرس المشايخ وإخبارهم عن اعتقادات الناس وضمائرهم يخرج عن الحصر بل ما حكي عنهم من مشاهدة الخضر عليه السلام والسؤال منه ومن سماع صوت الهاتف ومن فنون الكرامات خارج عن الحصر والحكاية لا تنفع الجاحد ما لم يشاهد ذلك من نفسه ومن أنكر الأصل أنكر التفصيل والدليل القاطع الذي لا يقدر أحد على جحده أمران أحدهما عجائب الرؤي
18:75.english: As for the evidences of the Sacred Law, there is His saying (Exalted is He): {«وَالَّذِينَ جَاهَدُوا فِينَا لَنَهْدِيَنَّهُمْ سُبُلَنَا»} ("And those who strive in Us, We shall surely guide them to Our paths") (Q. 29:69). So every wisdom that appears from the heart through persevering devotion to worship, without learning, is by way of unveiling and inspiration. And he (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Whoever acts upon what he knows, God bequeaths to him knowledge of what he does not know, and grants him success in what he does" — until he becomes deserving of Paradise. And whoever does not act upon what he knows wanders astray in what he knows and is not granted success in what he does, until he becomes deserving of the Fire. [The hadith "Whoever acts upon what he knows" has preceded in the Book of Knowledge, without his saying "and grants him success in what he does" — I have not found it with that addition.] And God (Exalted is He) said: {«وَمَنْ يَتَّقِ اللَّهَ يَجْعَلْ لَهُ مَخْرَجًا»} ("And whoever fears God, He makes for him a way out") (Q. 65:2) — from perplexities and doubts — {«وَيَرْزُقْهُ مِنْ حَيْثُ لَا يَحْتَسِبُ»} ("and provides for him from whence he does not reckon") (Q. 65:3) — teaching him knowledge without learning and granting him discernment without experience. And God (Exalted is He) said: {«يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا إِنْ تَتَّقُوا اللَّهَ يَجْعَلْ لَكُمْ فُرْقَانًا»} ("O you who believe, if you fear God, He will make for you a criterion") (Q. 8:29) — it is said: a light by which one distinguishes between truth and falsehood and by which one emerges from doubts. For this reason, he (peace and blessings be upon him) was abundant in his supplication in asking for light, saying (peace and blessings be upon him): "O God, grant me light, and increase me in light, and make for me light in my heart, and light in my grave, and light in my hearing, and light in my sight" — until he said: "and light in my hair, and in my skin, and in my flesh, and in my blood, and in my bones." [Agreed upon (by al-Bukhari and Muslim).] [The hadith concerning his being asked about His saying {«أَفَمَنْ شَرَحَ اللَّهُ صَدْرَهُ لِلْإِسْلَامِ»} ("Is he whose breast God has expanded for Islam") (Q. 39:22) — and in al-Mustadrak from the hadith of Ibn Masʿūd — has preceded in the Book of Knowledge.] And he (peace and blessings be upon him) said concerning Ibn ʿAbbās: "O God, grant him understanding in religion and teach him the interpretation (taʾwīl)." [The hadith of ʿAlī: "We have nothing with us that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) confided to us except that God grants a servant understanding in His Book" — has preceded in the Etiquettes of Qurʾanic Recitation.] And it is said in the interpretation of His saying (Exalted is He): {«يُؤْتِي الْحِكْمَةَ مَنْ يَشَاءُ»} ("He grants wisdom to whom He wills") (Q. 2:269) that it is understanding in the Book of God. And He (Exalted is He) said: {«فَفَهَّمْنَاهَا سُلَيْمَانَ»} ("And We made Solomon understand it") (Q. 21:79) — singling out what was unveiled with the name of understanding (fahm). And Abū al-Dardāʾ used to say: "The believer is one who sees by the light of God from behind a thin veil. By God, it is the truth that God casts into their hearts and causes to flow upon their tongues." And some of the Salaf said: "The believer's conjecture is like soothsaying."
18:75.section_title_en: The Unveiling of Knowledge Through Divine Inspiration and the Evidences of the Unseen
18:75.anchors:
- Root: علم (ʿalima)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning encompasses both perception of a thing's essence and judgment upon it—knowledge as direct apprehension or discursive ruling.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "العلم: إدراك الشيء بحقيقته" — knowledge is the apprehension of a thing in its true reality, divided into apprehension of the essence (transitive to one object) and judgment upon existence or non-existence (transitive to two objects).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal usage denotes certainty and awareness ("ما علمت بخبرك: ما شعرت به"); metaphorical extension applies to marks, signs, and beacons of guidance (معالم الطريق) — here, the inspired knowledge is a "mark" of the path.
- Root: كشف (kashafa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To remove a covering, unveil, disclose what was hidden.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Unveiling (kashf) in theological terms is the removal of the veil (ghishāwah) from the heart such that the realities of things become directly witnessed, not merely inferred.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: to lift a covering from a thing; metaphorical: the disclosure of inward states and hidden matters — the heart's eye perceives what the outward senses cannot.
- Root: فرس (farasa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To prey upon, devour; farāsah — the lion's pouncing upon its prey.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Discernment (farāsah) is a spiritual perception by which the believer penetrates into the inner states of others, a light cast by God into the heart.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the beast of prey seizing its quarry; metaphorical: the believer's insight seizing the truth of a matter or the hidden state of a person — "اتقوا فراسة المؤمن فإنه ينظر بنور الله."
- Root: حدث (ḥadatha)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To be new, originate after non-existence; muḥaddath — one who is spoken to, inspired with true speech from the unseen.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الحدوث: كون الشيء بعد أن لم يكن" — origination after non-existence; the muḥaddath is one to whom divine inspiration comes as a new, immediate occurrence without acquired means.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: newness of a thing; metaphorical: "كان عمر رضي الله عنه محدثا أي صادق الحدس، كأنما حدث بما ظن" — one whose intuition is so true it is as if he were directly spoken to.
- Sibawayh Rule: Restriction and specification (الحصر والتقييد) — the particle "إنما" and conditional clauses (إن/إذا) restrict predicates to their subjects, as in "إنما العالم الذي يأخذ علمه من ربه" — the true scholar is exclusively the one who takes knowledge from his Lord.
18:75.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Disciplining the Soul'

20:24.arabic: ومثال تأويل أهل الطامات قول بعضهم في تأويل قوله تعالى {اذهب إلى فرعون إنه طغى} أنه إشارة إلى قلبه وقال هو المراد بفرعون وهو الطاغي على كل إنسان وفي قوله تعالى {وأن ألق عصاك} أي ما يتوكأ عليه ويعتمده مما سوى الله عز وجل فينبغي أن يلقيه وفي قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم تسحروا فإن في السحور بركة (1) أراد به الاستغفار في الأسحار وأمثال ذلك حتى يحرفون القرآن من أوله إلى آخره عن ظاهره وعن تفسيره المنقول عن ابن عباس وسائر العلماء وبعض هذه التأويلات يعلم بطلانها قطعا كتنزيل فرعون على القلب فإن فرعون شخص محسوس تواتر إلينا النقل بوجوده ودعوة موس
20:24.english: Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ, may God be pleased with him, said to his son ʿUmar — having heard him composing sajʿ — "This is what makes me dislike you. I will never fulfill your need until you repent." This was said when his son had come to him seeking a favor. And the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to ʿAbd Allāh ibn Rawāḥah when he spoke in sajʿ of three words: "Beware of sajʿ, O Ibn Rawāḥah." Thus, the forbidden sajʿ is the artificially contrived kind that exceeds two words. For this reason, when a man spoke concerning the blood-money for a fetus — saying, "How shall we pay blood-money for one who neither drank, nor ate, nor cried out, nor wailed? Such a one's blood is void" — the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, replied: "Sajʿ like the sajʿ of the bedouins!"
20:24.section_title_en: On the Etiquette of Preaching: The Condemnation of Artificial Sajʿ, Excessive Poetry, and the Perils of Shataḥ and Taʿwīl
20:24.anchors:
- Root: سجع (sajʿa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Rhymed prose; from the root meaning "to coo" (as a dove), indicating a measured, melodious cadence in speech.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In theological discourse, sajʿ is permissible when natural but blameworthy when artificially cultivated (takalluf), as it shifts focus from meaning to ornamentation.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) — natural rhythmic speech; Metaphorical (majāz) — the "sajʿ of the bedouins" (sajʿ al-aʿrāb) as a pejorative for empty, affected eloquence.
- Root: شعر (shiʿr)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Poetry; from the root denoting perception and fine discernment (shuʿūr), as the poet grasps subtle meanings.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Poetry is blameworthy when it stirs base appetites, but praiseworthy when it conveys wisdom (ḥikmah), as in the prophetic saying "Indeed from poetry there is wisdom."
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — metered, rhymed speech; Metaphorical — the "poetry" of the heart's inclination, where listeners project their own passions onto what they hear.
- Root: شطح (shaṭaḥa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To overflow, to gush forth; originally of a water-skin bursting, then applied to ecstatic utterances that overflow the bounds of conventional discourse.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In Sufi terminology, shataḥ refers to utterances arising from overwhelming spiritual states (ḥāl) that, when voiced to the unworthy, cause corruption.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — physical overflowing; Metaphorical — the soul's overflow in speech that exceeds the speaker's intentional control.
- Root: أول (taʿwīl)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To return something to its origin or end; interpretation that traces a word back to its intended meaning.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Taʿwīl is legitimate only when supported by textual (naqlī) or rational (ʿaqlī) evidence; arbitrary taʿwīl that severs words from their established senses destroys religious trust.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — the apparent sense (ẓāhir); Metaphorical — the inner sense (bāṭin), which is only valid when the literal sense is impossible or when transmitted authority sanctions it.
- Sibawayh Rule: Bāb al-Ḥaṣr wa al-Taqyīd bi-innamā (Restriction and Focused Predication) — The text repeatedly uses restrictive constructions (innamā, laysa...illā) to delimit permissible preaching, poetry, and interpretation, distinguishing the praiseworthy from the blameworthy with syntactic precision.
20:24.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'Book of Knowledge'

21:7.arabic: الدين} وقوله عز وجل {فاسألوا أهل الذكر إن كنتم لا تعلمون} وأما الأخبار فقوله صلى الله عليه وسلم من سلك طريقا يطلب فيه علما سلك الله به طريقا إلى الجنة (1) وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم إن الملائكة لتضع أجنحتها لطالب العلم رضاء بما يصنع (2) وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم لأن تغدو فتتعلم بابا من العلم خير من أن تصلي مائة ركعة (3) وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم باب من العلم يتعلمه الرجل خير له من الدنيا وما فيها (4) وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم اطلبوا العلم ولو بالصين (1) وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم طلب العلم ف
21:7.english: As for the Quranic verses, there is the saying of God Most High: {«فلولا نفر من كل فرقة منهم طائفة ليتفقهوا في الدين»} — "Why then did not a party from every section of them go forth, that they might gain deep comprehension in the religion?" — and His saying, Mighty and Majestic: {«فاسألوا أهل الذكر إن كنتم لا تعلمون»} — "So ask the people of remembrance if you do not know."
21:7.section_title_en: The Virtue of Seeking Knowledge (Faḍīlat al-Taʿallum)
21:7.anchors:
- Root: فقه (Fiqh)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning is "comprehension" and "understanding" — the penetration into the inner meaning of speech, distinguished from mere hearing (samāʿ).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In the theological register, *tafaqquh* (تفقه) is the deep, exhaustive comprehension of the religious sciences — not mere memorization but the attainment of the realities of juridico-theological matters.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) usage denotes intellectual penetration; metaphorical (majāz) usage extends to any deep discernment of subtle meanings.
- Root: سأل (Saʾala)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To ask, to inquire, to seek information — the root act of petitioning for knowledge from its possessor.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Asking (*suʾāl*) is the divinely mandated means for the ignorant to access knowledge, as per {«فاسألوا أهل الذكر»} — it is the key that unlocks the treasuries of knowledge.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal usage is the verbal request; the Prophet's statement "العلم خزائن مفاتيحها السؤال" employs a metaphor (majāz) likening knowledge to locked treasuries and questioning to their keys.
- Root: طلب (Ṭalab)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To seek, to pursue, to search out a thing — whether a physical object or a meaning.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الطلب: الفحص عن وجود الشيء، عينا كان أو معنى" — the earnest investigation into the existence of a thing, whether concrete or conceptual. In the religious context, *ṭalab al-ʿilm* is the pursuit of that which revives the religion.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal usage is the physical pursuit of a quarry; the ḥadīth "من سلك طريقا يطلب فيه علما" employs the metaphor of the *path* (ṭarīq) as the means of pursuit, and the divine recompense as the *path to Paradise*.
- Root: غدو (Ghadā)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To go out early in the morning, to set forth at dawn — the time of vigorous, purposeful departure.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal usage denotes the morning journey; in the saying of Abū al-Dardāʾ, "الغدو إلى طلب العلم" is metaphorically elevated to the rank of *jihād* — the early morning departure for knowledge is a martial expedition of the soul.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Interposition (al-Faṣl bayna al-Jār wa-al-Majrūr) — The syntactic principle governing the separation of the prepositional phrase from its governing verb, as in "سلك الله به طريقا إلى الجنة," where the divine agency is interposed between the act and its recompense, indicating the causal nexus.
21:7.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Book of Knowledge'

21:18.arabic: وفي مثله قوله تعالى ولكم الويل مما تصفون وفي الخبر إنما أخاف على أمتي زلة عالم وجدال منافق في القرآن (1) ومنها أن تكون عنايته بتحصيل العلم النافع في الآخرة المرغب في الطاعات مجتنبا للعلوم التي يقل نفعها ويكثر فيها الجدال والقيل والقال فمثال من يعرض عن علم الأعمال ويشتغل بالجدال مثل رجل مريض به علل كثيرة وقد صادف طبيبا حاذقا في وقت ضيق يخشى فواته فاشتغل بالسؤال عن خاصية العقاقير والأدوية وغرائب الطب وترك مهمه الذي هو مؤاخذ به وذلك محض السفه وقد روي أن رجلا جاء رسول الله صلى
21:18.english: Know that the scholar who does not act upon his knowledge is condemned by the Book, the Sunnah, and the sayings of the sages. God, exalted be He, said: {«يا أيها الذين آمنوا لم تقولون ما لا تفعلون * كبر مقتا عند الله أن تقولوا ما لا تفعلون»} ("O you who believe, why do you say what you do not do? Most hateful it is to God that you say what you do not do"). And He said: {«أتأمرون الناس بالبر وتنسون أنفسكم»} ("Do you command people to righteousness while you forget yourselves?"). And He said: {«ومن الناس من يعجبك قوله في الحياة الدنيا ويشهد الله على ما في قلبه وهو ألد الخصام»} ("And among people is he whose speech pleases you in the worldly life, and he calls God to witness what is in his heart, yet he is the fiercest of opponents").
21:18.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Book of Knowledge'

21:84.arabic: بعد المحنة العظيمة مكن قال الله تعالى وآتيناه أهله ومثلهم معهم الآية فهذا الكلام من الشافعي رحمه الله يدل على تبحره في أسرار القرآن واطلاعه على مقامات السائرين إلى الله تعالى من الأنبياء والأولياء وكل ذلك من علوم الآخرة وقيل للشافعي رحمه الله متى يكون الرجل عالما قال إذا تحقق في علم الدين فعلمه وتعرض لسائر العلوم فنظر فيما فاته فعند ذلك يكون عالما فإنه قيل لجالينوس إنك تأمر للداء الواحد بالأدوية الكثيرة المجمعة فقال إنما المقصود منها واحد وإنما يجعل معه غيره لتسكن حدته لأن الإفراد قاتل فهذا وأمثاله مما لا يح
21:84.english: And al-Shafi'i, may God Most High have mercy upon him, said: "If you fear for your deed the blight of self-admiration (al-ʿujb), then consider: whose pleasure do you seek? Toward what reward do you yearn? From what punishment do you flee? What well-being do you thank? And what affliction do you recall? For if you reflect upon even one of these five qualities, your deed will appear small in your eyes." Observe how he mentioned the reality of ostentation and the remedy for self-admiration—both being among the gravest maladies of the heart.
21:84.section_title_en: The Revival of the Religious Sciences — Section 21: The Sciences of the Hereafter and the Signs of Sincere Intention in Knowledge
21:84.anchors:
- Root: مكن (m-k-n)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of establishing, empowering, and granting firm footing in a place or station.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "المكان عند أهل اللغة: الموضع الحاوي للشيء" — the place that encompasses a thing; theological nuance: divine empowerment (tamkīn) as a station granted after trial.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): "مكنته من الشيء وأمكنته منه، فتمكن منه واستمكن" — physical enabling. Metaphorical (Majaz): "الناس على مكناتهم: على مقارهم" — people upon their settled abodes/stations; here, the spiritual station of the prophets after tribulation.
- Root: محن (m-ḥ-n)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Testing, refining, and proving; a worn garment (mamḥūn) that has been stretched and expanded by use.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "المحن والامتحان نحو الابتلاء" — trial and testing akin to affliction; Quranic: {فامتحنوهن} (Al-Mumtahanah: 10) — the testing of hearts for sincerity.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "وقع في محنة ومحن" — falling into trial. Metaphorical: "محن الأديم: مدده حتى وسعه" — stretching hide until it widens; thus {امتحن الله قلوبهم} — God expands and purifies the heart through trial.
- Root: علم (ʿ-l-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Knowledge as the apprehension of a thing's reality; the mark (ʿalam) by which one is guided.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "العلم: إدراك الشيء بحقيقته" — knowledge is the perception of a thing in its true reality; two types: apprehension of essence, and judgment of existence or negation.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "ما علمت بخبرك: ما شعرت به" — to be aware. Metaphorical: "خفيت معالم الطريق" — the traces of the path that guide the seeker; here, the signs (ʿalāmāt) of sincere intention.
- Root: قلب (q-l-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Turning, overturning, and transforming a thing from one state to another.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "قلب الشيء: تصريفه وصرفه عن وجه إلى وجه" — the heart as that which is constantly turned and transformed; the seat of spiritual perception.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "قلب الشيء قلبا: حوله عن وجهه" — physical overturning. Metaphorical: "قلب التاجر السلعة" — the merchant scrutinizing his goods; "رجل قلب حول: يقلب الأمور" — one who turns matters over; here, the heart's gaze upon its own intentions.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — Used to confine a predicate to a single subject, as in "إنما المقصود منها واحد" (the intended aim is but one), emphasizing exclusive focus.
21:84.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Book of Knowledge'

22:11.arabic: وفوز المقربين وذلك هو الخسران المبين ولقد كان الحسن البصري رحمه الله أشبه الناس كلاما بكلام الأنبياء عليهم الصلاة والسلام وأقربهم هديا من الصحابة رضي الله عنهم اتفقت الكلمة في حقه على ذلك وكان أكثر كلامه في خواطر القلوب وفساد الأعمال ووساس النفوس والصفات الخفية الغامضة من شهوات النفس وقد قيل له يا أبا سعيد إنك تتكلم بكلام لا يسمع من غيرك فمن أين أخذته قال من حذيفة بن اليمان وقيل لحذيفة نراك تتكلم بكلام لا يسمع من غيرك من الصحابة فمن أين أخذته قال خصني به رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كان
22:11.english: Indeed, al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī (may God have mercy on him) was the most similar of people in speech to the speech of the prophets (upon them be prayer and peace) and the closest of them in guidance to the Companions (may God be pleased with them). The consensus of opinion agreed upon this concerning him. And most of his speech concerned the thoughts that pass through the hearts, the corruption of deeds, the whisperings of the souls, and the hidden, obscure attributes of the soul's appetites. It was said to him: "O Abū Saʿīd, you speak words that are not heard from anyone other than you—so from where did you take them?" He said: "From Ḥudhayfah ibn al-Yamān."
22:11.section_title_en: The Science of the Heart's Subtleties and the Corruption of Deeds — Section 62
22:11.anchors:
- Root: قرب (q-r-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root meaning of proximity, nearness in place, time, and rank; the verbal noun *qurbān* denotes drawing near through devotional acts.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "القرب والبعد يتقابلان" — proximity and distance are opposites; used in place, time, relation, favor, care, and power. Theologically, *al-taqarrub ilā Allāh* is the soul's approach to God through knowledge and worship, not spatial movement.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (*ḥaqīqah*): physical nearness. Metaphorical (*majāz*): "فلان يقرب أمرا لا يتسهل له" — one who undertakes a difficult matter; and "حياك الله وقرب دارك" — a greeting of honor. Here, *al-taqarrub* from creation vs. from God marks the contrast between seeking favor of men and seeking nearness to God.
- Root: قلب (q-l-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Turning, overturning, transformation of a thing from one state to another.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "قلب الشيء: تصريفه وصرفه عن وجه إلى وجه" — the heart is so named for its constant fluctuation (*taqallub*) between states; it is the seat of intention and the organ by which one turns toward or away from God.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical turning. Metaphorical: "رجل قلب حول: يقلب الأمور ويحتال" — one who turns matters over and discerns their realities. In this text, *khaṭarāt al-qulūb* (thoughts that pass through hearts) are the subtle movements of the inner faculty that determine the soundness or corruption of deeds.
- Root: نفس (n-f-s)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The self, soul, breath; that by which a thing is valued.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "النفس: الروح" — the soul; also the essence (*al-dhāt*), as in "ويحذركم الله نفسه" where *nafsahu* means His very Self. In moral psychology, *al-nafs* is the lower self with its appetites (*shahawāt*), the source of *waswās* (whispering temptations).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the self or person. Metaphorical: "دفق نفسه أي دمه" — "he poured out his self," i.e., his blood; and "أصابته نفس: عين" — "a self struck him," i.e., the evil eye. Here, *wasāwis al-nufūs* refers to the insinuating promptings that arise from the soul's lower impulses.
- Root: عمل (ʿ-m-l)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Deed, action performed with purpose and intent.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "العمل: كل فعل يكون من الحيوان بقصد" — work is every act done by a living being with intention; it is more specific than *fiʿl* (mere act). Deeds are either righteous (*ṣāliḥāt*) or evil (*sayyiʾāt*), and their value depends on the heart's state.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical labor. Metaphorical: "فلان ابن عمل إذا كان قويا عليه" — one who is master of his work. In this passage, *āfāt al-aʿmāl* (corruptions of deeds) are the hidden defects that nullify works, which the scholars of the Hereafter investigate.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — When *innamā* introduces a clause, it restricts the predicate to the subject alone, excluding all else. In "وإنما الشأن في معرفة ما يفسدها ويشوشها" ("the only concern is knowing what corrupts and disturbs them"), the restriction emphasizes that the sole essential matter is knowledge of the inward corrupters of deeds, not outward elaboration.
22:11.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Book of Knowledge'

22:11.arabic: فلم تبق له دنياه ولم يسلم له دينه {خسر الدنيا والآخرة ذلك هو الخسران المبين} فيا لها من مصيبة ما أفظعها ورزية ما أجلها ألا فراقبوا الله إخواني ولا يغرنكم الشيطان وأولياؤه من الآنسين بالحجج الداحضة عند الله فإنهم يتكالبون على الدنيا ثم يطلبون لأنفسهم المعاذير والحجج ويزعمون أن أصحاب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كانت لهم أموال فيتزين المغرورون بذكر الصحابة ليعذرهم الناس على جمع المال ولقد دهاهم الشيطان وما يشعرون ويحك أيها المفتون إن احتجاجك بمال عبد الرحمن بن عوف مكيدة من الشيطان ينطق بها على لسانك فتهلك لأنك متى زعمت أن أخي
22:11.english: Then al-Ḥārith, may God have mercy on him, said: "My brothers! These are the scholars of evil — the devils of mankind and a trial upon the people. They coveted the goods of this world and its elevation, preferred it over the Hereafter, and interpreted religion for the sake of this world. So in the immediate term they are disgrace and shame, and in the Hereafter they are the losers — unless the Generous One pardons through His bounty."
22:11.book_title: Condemnation of Miserliness and Love of Wealth
22:11.section_title_en: The Condemnation of the Worldly Scholars — The Admonition of al-Ḥārith al-Muḥāsibī
22:11.anchors:
- Root: خرج (kharaja)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To extract, draw forth, or expel something from its place of containment.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Used for the emergence of something from its potential state into actuality, or from the inward to the outward.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Here used metaphorically (Majaz) for "uttering" — extracting wisdom from the mouth while the heart remains sealed against it.
- Root: غل (ghalla)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Concealed rancor, malice, or treachery harbored within the breast.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): A hidden corruption of the heart's disposition toward another, often linked to betrayal of trust.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal sense is "thirst" or "hidden enmity"; here it denotes the inward state of hypocrisy where outward speech contradicts inward conviction.
- Root: خسر (khasira)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To lose, to suffer diminution of capital or principal.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الخسر والخسران: انتقاص رأس المال" — loss of one's true capital (faith and the Hereafter), which is the "manifest loss" (الخسران المبين).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal for commercial loss; metaphorical (Majaz) for the one who disobeys God — "ومن لم يطع الله فهو خاسر" (Whoever does not obey God is a loser).
- Root: دحض (dahaḍa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To slip, slide, or become void; a false argument that has no firm footing.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): An argument that is invalidated and rendered null, having no grounding in truth.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal for a foot slipping on slippery ground; metaphorical for specious reasoning that collapses under scrutiny.
- Root: دها (dahā)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To befall with calamity, to deceive cunningly, to afflict with a great matter.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): A profound and overwhelming affliction or cunning deception that strikes unaware.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal for a sudden calamity; here metaphorical for Satan's subtle deception that overcomes the heedless.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The rule governing the separation of the prepositional phrase from its governing verb, allowing for rhetorical emphasis and dramatic effect in periodic sentences, as seen in the extended condemnations and rhetorical questions of this admonition.
22:11.topic: Al-Ghazali on purifying the character, moral diseases, and spiritual remedies, from 'Condemnation of Miserliness and Love of Wealth'

23:38.arabic: الله تعالى بين من افترى على الله كذبا وبين من كذب بالحق فقال تعالى ومن أظلم ممن افترى على الله كذبا أو كذب بالحق لما جاءه وقال تعالى فمن أظلم ممن كذب على الله وكذب بالصدق إذ جاءه ومنها الرياء وملاحظة الخلق والجهد في استمالة قلوبهم وصرف وجوههم والرياء هو الداء العضال الذي يدعو إلى أكبر الكبائر كما سيأتي في كتاب الرياء والمناظر لا يقصد إلا الظهور عند الخلق وانطلاق ألسنتهم بالثناء عليه فهذه عشر خصال من أمهات الفواحش الباطنة سوى ما يتفق لغير المتماسكين منهم من الخصام المؤدي إلى الضرب
23:38.english:
**QUAD_ANCHORS:**
- Root: نظر (naẓara)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to look, to examine, to consider; al-munāẓarah is mutual examination/argumentation between two parties.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: naẓar as intellectual contemplation (taʾammul bi-l-baṣīrah); munāẓarah as dialectical exchange.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: sitting face-to-face in debate; Metaphorical: disputation for victory.
- Root: غلب (ghalaba)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to overcome, to conquer, to prevail.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-ghalabah as seeking to dominate another in argument.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: victory in combat; Metaphorical: intellectual supremacy.
- Root: حسد (ḥasada)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to envy, to wish removal of blessings from another.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: envy as wishing deprivation of blessings from the deserving — among the basest traits.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: envy of another's blessing; Metaphorical: consuming fire of the soul.
- Root: كبر (kabura)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to be great, to be haughty.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-kibr as self-elevation above others; condemned by God.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: greatness; Metaphorical: arrogance and pride.
- Root: غيب (ghāba)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to be absent, to be hidden.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-ghībah as mentioning another with what he dislikes in his absence — likened to eating carrion.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: backbiting; Metaphorical: consuming the flesh of one's brother.
- Root: راءى (rāʾā)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to show off, to display.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-riyāʾ as performing acts for the sake of being seen — hidden shirk.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: showing good deeds; Metaphorical: seeking reputation.
- Root: نفس (nafs)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: self, soul, spirit.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: tazkiyat al-nafs as self-praise and self-purification — forbidden by God.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: self; Metaphorical: self-commendation.
- Root: حقd (ḥaqida)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to bear malice, to harbor resentment.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-ḥiqd as nursing enmity in the heart — negated from the believer.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: bearing grudge; Metaphorical: hidden rancor.
- Root: نفاق (nifāq)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: hypocrisy, showing contrary to what one conceals.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: hypocrisy in deeds — outward display contrary to inward state.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: hypocrisy in faith; Metaphorical: hypocrisy in character.
- Root: علم (ʿalima)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to know, to perceive.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: knowledge as apprehension of reality — its pursuit for other than God is destructive.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: knowledge; Metaphorical: the dangerous burden of the scholar.
- Root: جدل (jadala)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to argue, to dispute.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-jidāl as contention; al-mirāʾ as disputation with falsehood — condemned.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: argumentation; Metaphorical: obstinate disputation.
- Root: شرك (sharaka)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to associate, to share.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-riyāʾ as hidden shirk — associating others with God in intention.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: polytheism; Metaphorical: hidden association in deeds.
- Root: موت (māta)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to die.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: death as separation of soul from body; spiritual death as ruin of the soul.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical death; Metaphorical: spiritual destruction.
- Root: حيى (ḥayiya)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to live.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: life as the power of perception; eternal life as the reward of the righteous.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical life; Metaphorical: spiritual vitality.
- Root: هلك (halaka)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to perish, to be destroyed.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-halāk as ruin; eternal destruction as everlasting punishment.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: destruction; Metaphorical: eternal ruin.
- Root: رياء (riyāʾ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: showing off, ostentation.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: riyāʾ as the incurable disease calling to the greatest sins.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: ostentation; Metaphorical: spiritual disease.
- Root: جاه (jāh)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: rank, status, prestige.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: love of status (ḥubb al-jāh) among the destructive traits.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: position; Metaphorical: seeking prestige.
- Root: مباهاة (mubāhāh)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: mutual boasting, vying in splendor.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: mubāhāh as each seeking to display superiority over the other.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: mutual boasting; Metaphorical: rivalry in honor.
- Root: مماراة (mumārāh)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: disputation, wrangling.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-mirāʾ as contentious argument — condemned by the Prophet.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: disputation; Metaphorical: obstinate wrangling.
- Root: فخر (fakhara)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to boast, to pride oneself.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-fakhr as self-glorification — among the blameworthy traits.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: boasting; Metaphorical: vainglory.
- Root: عجب (ʿajiba)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to wonder, to be amazed.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-ʿujb as self-admiration — among the destructive traits.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: wonder; Metaphorical: self-conceit.
- Root: بغض (baghiḍa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to hate, to detest.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-baghdāʾ as mutual hatred — contrary to brotherhood.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: hatred; Metaphorical: mutual enmity.
- Root: غضب (ghaḍiba)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to be angry.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-ghaḍab as anger — among the blameworthy traits.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: anger; Metaphorical: rage.
- Root: طمع (ṭamiʿa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to covet, to desire.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-ṭamaʿ as covetousness — among the destructive traits.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: desire; Metaphorical: greed.
- Root: أشر (ashira)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to be exultant, to be insolent.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-ashar as excessive joy and insolence — blameworthy.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: exultation; Metaphorical: insolence.
- Root: بطر (baṭira)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to be arrogant, to be ungrateful.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-baṭar as arrogance in prosperity — among the destructive traits.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: arrogance; Metaphorical: ingratitude for blessings.
- Root: خيلاء (khuyalāʾ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: pride, haughtiness.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-khuyalāʾ as pride and conceit — blameworthy.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: pride; Metaphorical: haughty bearing.
- Root: خشية (khashyah)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: fear, awe.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-khashyah as reverential fear — among the traits of the believers.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: fear; Metaphorical: reverential awe.
- Root: رحمة (raḥmah)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: mercy, compassion.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-raḥmah as tenderness of heart — among the traits of the believers.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: mercy; Metaphorical: compassion.
- Root: غفلة (ghaflah)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: heedlessness, inattention.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-ghaflah as heedlessness — contrary to vigilance.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: inattention; Metaphorical: spiritual heedlessness.
- Root: خشوع (khushūʿ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: humility, submissiveness.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-khushūʿ as humility — among the traits of the believers.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: humility; Metaphorical: devotional submission.
- Root: تذكير (tadhkīr)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: reminding, admonishing.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-tadhkīr as reminding of God — a righteous act.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: reminding; Metaphorical: preaching.
- Root: وعظ (waʿaẓa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to admonish, to exhort.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-waʿẓ as exhortation to obedience and warning against disobedience.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: admonition; Metaphorical: sermonizing.
- Root: فتوى (fatwā)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: legal ruling, formal opinion.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-fatwā as clarification of legal rulings.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: legal opinion; Metaphorical: religious authority.
- Root: قضاء (qaḍāʾ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: judgment, decree.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-qaḍāʾ as judgment between people.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: judgment; Metaphorical: judicial authority.
- Root: وقف (waqafa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to stop, to stand.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-waqf as endowment of property for charitable purposes.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: standing; Metaphorical: religious endowment.
- Root: ثواب (thawāb)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: reward, recompense.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-thawāb as divine recompense for righteous deeds.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: reward; Metaphorical: divine recompense.
- Root: عذاب (ʿadhāb)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: punishment, torment.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-ʿadhāb as divine punishment for the disobedient.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: punishment; Metaphorical: divine chastisement.
- Root: ملك (malaka)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to possess, to rule.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-mulk as sovereignty; al-mulk al-muʾabbad as eternal sovereignty in Paradise.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: dominion; Metaphorical: eternal kingdom.
- Root: نعيم (naʿīm)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: bliss, delight.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-naʿīm as bliss; al-naʿīm al-sarmad as everlasting bliss.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: delight; Metaphorical: eternal bliss.
- Root: رخصة (rukhaṣah)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: concession, dispensation.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-rukhaṣah as legal concession.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: concession; Metaphorical: legal dispensation.
- Root: رياسة (riyāsah)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: leadership, headship.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: love of leadership among the destructive traits.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: leadership; Metaphorical: seeking authority.
- Root: اندراس (indirās)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: effacement, obliteration.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: indirās al-ʿulūm as the obliteration of the sciences.

  * Lisan / Ayn- Root: مكتب (maktab)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: place of instruction, school for boys.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: the elementary school where children are taught.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: school; Metaphorical: place of elementary learning.
- Root: خلاق (khilāq)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: portion, share, lot.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: "no portion" (lā khilāq) in the Hereafter — utter deprivation of divine reward.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: share; Metaphorical: spiritual allotment in the afterlife.
- Root: فاجر (fājir)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: wicked, immoral, profligate.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: the dissolute one who commits sins openly.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: sinner; Metaphorical: one through whom God nonetheless supports religion.
- Root: شمع (shamʿ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: candle, wax taper.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: the candle as parable — consuming itself while giving light to others.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: candle; Metaphorical: one who destroys himself but benefits others.
- Root: نار (nār)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: fire.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: fire as parable — consuming itself and all around it.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: fire; Metaphorical: one who destroys himself and others.
- Root: سعد (saʿida)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to be fortunate, to prosper.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: saʿādah as felicity — success in the Hereafter.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: good fortune; Metaphorical: eternal felicity.
- Root: شقي (shaqiya)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to be wretched, to be miserable.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: shaqāwah as wretchedness — ruin in the Hereafter.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: misery; Metaphorical: eternal ruin.
- Root: أخلص (akhlaṣa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to purify, to be sincere.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: ikhlāṣ as purifying intention for God alone — the condition of acceptance.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: sincerity; Metaphorical: pure devotion.
- Root: ريب (rāba)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to doubt, to suspect.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-rayb as doubt and uncertainty — to be dispelled by evidence.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: doubt; Metaphorical: skepticism.

26:224.arabic: قال الله تعالى {والشعراء يتبعهم الغاوون ألم تر أنهم في كل واد يهيمون} وقال تعالى {وما علمناه الشعر وما ينبغي له} وأكثر ما اعتاده الوعاظ من الأشعار ما يتعلق بالتواصف في العشق وجمال المعشوق وروح الوصال وألم الفراق والمجلس لا يحوي إلا أجلاف العوام وبواطنهم مشحونة بالشهوات وقلوبهم غير منفكة عن الالتفات إلى الصور المليحة فلا تحرك الأشعار من قلوبهم إلا ما هو مستكن فيها فتشتعل فيها نيران الشهوات فيزعقون ويتواجدون وأكثر ذلك أو كله يرجع إلى نوع فساد فلا ينبغي أن يستعمل من الشعر إلا ما فيه موعظة أو حكمة على سب
26:224.english: Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ, may God be pleased with him, said to his son ʿUmar — having heard him composing sajʿ — "This is what makes me dislike you. I will never fulfill your need until you repent." This was said when his son had come to him seeking a favor. And the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to ʿAbd Allāh ibn Rawāḥah when he spoke in sajʿ of three words: "Beware of sajʿ, O Ibn Rawāḥah." Thus, the forbidden sajʿ is the artificially contrived kind that exceeds two words. For this reason, when a man spoke concerning the blood-money for a fetus — saying, "How shall we pay blood-money for one who neither drank, nor ate, nor cried out, nor wailed? Such a one's blood is void" — the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, replied: "Sajʿ like the sajʿ of the bedouins!"
26:224.section_title_en: On the Etiquette of Preaching: The Condemnation of Artificial Sajʿ, Excessive Poetry, and the Perils of Shataḥ and Taʿwīl
26:224.anchors:
- Root: سجع (sajʿa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Rhymed prose; from the root meaning "to coo" (as a dove), indicating a measured, melodious cadence in speech.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In theological discourse, sajʿ is permissible when natural but blameworthy when artificially cultivated (takalluf), as it shifts focus from meaning to ornamentation.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) — natural rhythmic speech; Metaphorical (majāz) — the "sajʿ of the bedouins" (sajʿ al-aʿrāb) as a pejorative for empty, affected eloquence.
- Root: شعر (shiʿr)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Poetry; from the root denoting perception and fine discernment (shuʿūr), as the poet grasps subtle meanings.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Poetry is blameworthy when it stirs base appetites, but praiseworthy when it conveys wisdom (ḥikmah), as in the prophetic saying "Indeed from poetry there is wisdom."
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — metered, rhymed speech; Metaphorical — the "poetry" of the heart's inclination, where listeners project their own passions onto what they hear.
- Root: شطح (shaṭaḥa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To overflow, to gush forth; originally of a water-skin bursting, then applied to ecstatic utterances that overflow the bounds of conventional discourse.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In Sufi terminology, shataḥ refers to utterances arising from overwhelming spiritual states (ḥāl) that, when voiced to the unworthy, cause corruption.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — physical overflowing; Metaphorical — the soul's overflow in speech that exceeds the speaker's intentional control.
- Root: أول (taʿwīl)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To return something to its origin or end; interpretation that traces a word back to its intended meaning.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Taʿwīl is legitimate only when supported by textual (naqlī) or rational (ʿaqlī) evidence; arbitrary taʿwīl that severs words from their established senses destroys religious trust.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — the apparent sense (ẓāhir); Metaphorical — the inner sense (bāṭin), which is only valid when the literal sense is impossible or when transmitted authority sanctions it.
- Sibawayh Rule: Bāb al-Ḥaṣr wa al-Taqyīd bi-innamā (Restriction and Focused Predication) — The text repeatedly uses restrictive constructions (innamā, laysa...illā) to delimit permissible preaching, poetry, and interpretation, distinguishing the praiseworthy from the blameworthy with syntactic precision.
26:224.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'Book of Knowledge'

27:40.arabic: وبينكم ومن عنده علم الكتاب} وقال تعالى {قال الذي عنده علم من الكتاب أنا آتيك به} تنبيها على أنه اقتدر بقوة العلم وقال عز وجل {وقال الذين أوتوا العلم ويلكم ثواب الله خير لمن آمن وعمل صالحا} بين أن عظم قدر الآخرة يعلم بالعلم وقال تعالى {وتلك الأمثال نضربها للناس وما يعقلها إلا العالمون} وقال تعالى {ولو ردوه إلى الرسول وإلى أولي الأمر منهم لعلمه الذين يستنبطونه منهم} رد حكمه في الوقائع إلى استنباطهم وألحق رتبتهم برتبة الأنبياء في كشف حكم الله وقيل في قوله تعالى يا بني آدم قد أنزلنا عليكم لباسا يواري سوءاتكم يعني العلم وريشا يع
27:40.english: How He, Glorified and Exalted, began with Himself, then seconded with the angels, and thirded with the people of knowledge — and sufficient for you is this as honor, excellence, splendor, and nobility. And God, Exalted, said: {«يرفع الله الذين آمنوا منكم والذين أوتوا العلم درجات»} — "God will raise those who have believed among you and those who have been given knowledge, in degrees." Ibn ʿAbbās, may God be pleased with them both, said: For the scholars there are degrees above the believers, seven hundred degrees, and between each two degrees is a distance of five hundred years' journey.
27:40.section_title_en: The Book of Knowledge — Section 4: The Excellence of Knowledge and the Scholars
27:40.anchors:
- Root: علم (ʿ-l-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root meaning of knowing, perceiving a thing in its true reality; the act of apprehension and judgment.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "العلم: إدراك الشيء بحقيقته" — knowledge is the apprehension of a thing in its true reality, divided into apprehension of the essence and judgment of existence or non-existence.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) usage denotes genuine knowing; metaphorical (majāz) usage extends to signs, landmarks, and traces that guide to knowledge.
- Root: درج (d-r-j)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Degrees, steps, ascending stations; the root denotes gradation and progressive elevation.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الدرجة نحو المنزلة، لكن يقال للمنزلة: درجة إذا اعتبرت بالصعود" — a degree is a station considered by ascent, not horizontal extension.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical steps of ascent. Metaphorical: "لفلان درجة رفيعة" — lofty rank; "امش في مدارج الحق" — walk in the paths of truth.
- Root: يوم (y-w-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: A day; a period of time from sunrise to sunset, or any duration whatsoever.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "اليوم يعبر به عن وقت طلوع الشمس إلى غروبها. وقد يعبر به عن مدة من الزمان أي مدة كانت" — the day denotes the time of the sun's rising to its setting, and may denote any period of time whatsoever.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the solar day. Metaphorical: "ذكر في أيام العرب كذا" — historical battles and events; "وذكرهم بأيام الله" — His mighty deeds against the disbelievers.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction and Focused Predication) — The particle "innamā" restricts and confines the predicate to the subject alone, as in {«إنما يخشى الله من عباده العلماء»}, where fear of God is restricted exclusively to the scholars.
27:40.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Book of Knowledge'

29:49.arabic: عليهم بعلم} وقال عز وجل {بل هو آيات بينات في صدور الذين أوتوا العلم} وقال تعالى {خلق الإنسان علمه البيان} وإنما ذكر ذلك في معرض الامتنان وأما الأخبار فقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم من يرد الله به خيرا يفقهه في الدين ويلهمه رشده (1) وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم العلماء ورثة الأنبياء (2) ومعلوم أنه لا رتبة فوق النبوة ولا شرف فوق شرف الوراثة لتلك الرتبة وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم يستغفر للعالم ما في السموات والأرض (3) وأي منصب يزيد على منصب من تشتغل ملائكة السموات والأرض بالاستغفار له وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم إن الحكمة تزيد
29:49.english: How He, Glorified and Exalted, began with Himself, then seconded with the angels, and thirded with the people of knowledge — and sufficient for you is this as honor, excellence, splendor, and nobility. And God, Exalted, said: {«يرفع الله الذين آمنوا منكم والذين أوتوا العلم درجات»} — "God will raise those who have believed among you and those who have been given knowledge, in degrees." Ibn ʿAbbās, may God be pleased with them both, said: For the scholars there are degrees above the believers, seven hundred degrees, and between each two degrees is a distance of five hundred years' journey.
