  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: backbiting; Metaphorical: consuming the flesh of one's brother.
- Root: راءى (rāʾā)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to show off, to display.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-riyāʾ as performing acts for the sake of being seen — hidden shirk.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: showing good deeds; Metaphorical: seeking reputation.
- Root: نفس (nafs)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: self, soul, spirit.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: tazkiyat al-nafs as self-praise and self-purification — forbidden by God.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: self; Metaphorical: self-commendation.
- Root: حقd (ḥaqida)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to bear malice, to harbor resentment.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-ḥiqd as nursing enmity in the heart — negated from the believer.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: bearing grudge; Metaphorical: hidden rancor.
- Root: نفاق (nifāq)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: hypocrisy, showing contrary to what one conceals.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: hypocrisy in deeds — outward display contrary to inward state.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: hypocrisy in faith; Metaphorical: hypocrisy in character.
- Root: علم (ʿalima)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to know, to perceive.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: knowledge as apprehension of reality — its pursuit for other than God is destructive.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: knowledge; Metaphorical: the dangerous burden of the scholar.
- Root: جدل (jadala)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to argue, to dispute.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-jidāl as contention; al-mirāʾ as disputation with falsehood — condemned.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: argumentation; Metaphorical: obstinate disputation.
- Root: شرك (sharaka)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to associate, to share.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-riyāʾ as hidden shirk — associating others with God in intention.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: polytheism; Metaphorical: hidden association in deeds.
- Root: موت (māta)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to die.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: death as separation of soul from body; spiritual death as ruin of the soul.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical death; Metaphorical: spiritual destruction.
- Root: حيى (ḥayiya)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to live.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: life as the power of perception; eternal life as the reward of the righteous.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical life; Metaphorical: spiritual vitality.
- Root: هلك (halaka)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to perish, to be destroyed.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-halāk as ruin; eternal destruction as everlasting punishment.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: destruction; Metaphorical: eternal ruin.
- Root: رياء (riyāʾ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: showing off, ostentation.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: riyāʾ as the incurable disease calling to the greatest sins.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: ostentation; Metaphorical: spiritual disease.
- Root: جاه (jāh)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: rank, status, prestige.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: love of status (ḥubb al-jāh) among the destructive traits.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: position; Metaphorical: seeking prestige.
- Root: مباهاة (mubāhāh)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: mutual boasting, vying in splendor.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: mubāhāh as each seeking to display superiority over the other.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: mutual boasting; Metaphorical: rivalry in honor.
- Root: مماراة (mumārāh)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: disputation, wrangling.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-mirāʾ as contentious argument — condemned by the Prophet.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: disputation; Metaphorical: obstinate wrangling.
- Root: فخر (fakhara)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to boast, to pride oneself.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-fakhr as self-glorification — among the blameworthy traits.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: boasting; Metaphorical: vainglory.
- Root: عجب (ʿajiba)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to wonder, to be amazed.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-ʿujb as self-admiration — among the destructive traits.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: wonder; Metaphorical: self-conceit.
- Root: بغض (baghiḍa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to hate, to detest.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-baghdāʾ as mutual hatred — contrary to brotherhood.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: hatred; Metaphorical: mutual enmity.
- Root: غضب (ghaḍiba)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to be angry.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-ghaḍab as anger — among the blameworthy traits.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: anger; Metaphorical: rage.
- Root: طمع (ṭamiʿa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to covet, to desire.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-ṭamaʿ as covetousness — among the destructive traits.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: desire; Metaphorical: greed.
- Root: أشر (ashira)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to be exultant, to be insolent.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-ashar as excessive joy and insolence — blameworthy.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: exultation; Metaphorical: insolence.
- Root: بطر (baṭira)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to be arrogant, to be ungrateful.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-baṭar as arrogance in prosperity — among the destructive traits.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: arrogance; Metaphorical: ingratitude for blessings.
- Root: خيلاء (khuyalāʾ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: pride, haughtiness.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-khuyalāʾ as pride and conceit — blameworthy.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: pride; Metaphorical: haughty bearing.
- Root: خشية (khashyah)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: fear, awe.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-khashyah as reverential fear — among the traits of the believers.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: fear; Metaphorical: reverential awe.
- Root: رحمة (raḥmah)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: mercy, compassion.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-raḥmah as tenderness of heart — among the traits of the believers.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: mercy; Metaphorical: compassion.
- Root: غفلة (ghaflah)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: heedlessness, inattention.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-ghaflah as heedlessness — contrary to vigilance.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: inattention; Metaphorical: spiritual heedlessness.
- Root: خشوع (khushūʿ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: humility, submissiveness.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-khushūʿ as humility — among the traits of the believers.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: humility; Metaphorical: devotional submission.
- Root: تذكير (tadhkīr)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: reminding, admonishing.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-tadhkīr as reminding of God — a righteous act.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: reminding; Metaphorical: preaching.
- Root: وعظ (waʿaẓa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to admonish, to exhort.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-waʿẓ as exhortation to obedience and warning against disobedience.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: admonition; Metaphorical: sermonizing.
- Root: فتوى (fatwā)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: legal ruling, formal opinion.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-fatwā as clarification of legal rulings.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: legal opinion; Metaphorical: religious authority.
- Root: قضاء (qaḍāʾ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: judgment, decree.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-qaḍāʾ as judgment between people.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: judgment; Metaphorical: judicial authority.
- Root: وقف (waqafa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to stop, to stand.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-waqf as endowment of property for charitable purposes.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: standing; Metaphorical: religious endowment.
- Root: ثواب (thawāb)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: reward, recompense.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-thawāb as divine recompense for righteous deeds.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: reward; Metaphorical: divine recompense.
- Root: عذاب (ʿadhāb)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: punishment, torment.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-ʿadhāb as divine punishment for the disobedient.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: punishment; Metaphorical: divine chastisement.
- Root: ملك (malaka)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to possess, to rule.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-mulk as sovereignty; al-mulk al-muʾabbad as eternal sovereignty in Paradise.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: dominion; Metaphorical: eternal kingdom.
- Root: نعيم (naʿīm)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: bliss, delight.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-naʿīm as bliss; al-naʿīm al-sarmad as everlasting bliss.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: delight; Metaphorical: eternal bliss.
- Root: رخصة (rukhaṣah)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: concession, dispensation.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-rukhaṣah as legal concession.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: concession; Metaphorical: legal dispensation.
- Root: رياسة (riyāsah)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: leadership, headship.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: love of leadership among the destructive traits.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: leadership; Metaphorical: seeking authority.
- Root: اندراس (indirās)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: effacement, obliteration.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: indirās al-ʿulūm as the obliteration of the sciences.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: effacement; Metaphorical: extinction of knowledge.
- Root: صبيان (ṣibyān)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: boys, children.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: children's motivation for learning through play.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: boys; Metaphorical: pupils.
- Root: مكتب (maktab)
  * Lisan / Ayn- Root: مكتب (maktab)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: place of instruction, school for boys.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: the elementary school where children are taught.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: school; Metaphorical: place of elementary learning.
- Root: خلاق (khilāq)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: portion, share, lot.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: "no portion" (lā khilāq) in the Hereafter — utter deprivation of divine reward.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: share; Metaphorical: spiritual allotment in the afterlife.
- Root: فاجر (fājir)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: wicked, immoral, profligate.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: the dissolute one who commits sins openly.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: sinner; Metaphorical: one through whom God nonetheless supports religion.
- Root: شمع (shamʿ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: candle, wax taper.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: the candle as parable — consuming itself while giving light to others.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: candle; Metaphorical: one who destroys himself but benefits others.
- Root: نار (nār)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: fire.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: fire as parable — consuming itself and all around it.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: fire; Metaphorical: one who destroys himself and others.
- Root: سعد (saʿida)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to be fortunate, to prosper.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: saʿādah as felicity — success in the Hereafter.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: good fortune; Metaphorical: eternal felicity.
- Root: شقي (shaqiya)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to be wretched, to be miserable.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: shaqāwah as wretchedness — ruin in the Hereafter.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: misery; Metaphorical: eternal ruin.
- Root: أخلص (akhlaṣa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to purify, to be sincere.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: ikhlāṣ as purifying intention for God alone — the condition of acceptance.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: sincerity; Metaphorical: pure devotion.
- Root: ريب (rāba)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to doubt, to suspect.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-rayb as doubt and uncertainty — to be dispelled by evidence.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: doubt; Metaphorical: skepticism.
42:24.topic: Al-Ghazali on purifying the character, moral diseases, and spiritual remedies, from 'Book of Knowledge'

42:51.arabic: إلا بواسطة الملائكة وما كان لبشر أن يكلمه الله إلا وحيا أو من وراء حجاب أو يرسل رسولا فيوحي بإذنه ما يشاء وهكذا ما يرسل من رحمة العلوم إلى القلوب إنما تتولاها الملائكة الموكلون بها وهم المقدسون المطهرون المبرءون عن الصفات المذمومات فلا يلاحظون إلا طيبا ولا يعمرون بما عندهم من خزائن رحمة الله إلا طيبا طاهرا ولست أقول المراد بلفظ البيت هو القلب وبالكلب هو الغضب والصفات المذمومة ولكني أقول هو تنبيه عليه وفرق بين تعبير الظواهر إلى البواطن وبين التنبيه للبواطن من ذكر الظواهر مع تقرير الظواهر ففارق الباطنية بهذه الدقيقة فإن هذه طريق الاعتبار وهو مسلك
42:51.english: The Prophet, peace be upon him, said: "Religion is built upon cleanliness" — and it is so, both inwardly and outwardly. God, exalted, has said: {«إِنَّمَا الْمُشْرِكُونَ نَجَسٌ»} (Indeed, the polytheists are impure) — as an alert to the intellects that purity and impurity are not confined to the outward things perceived by the senses. For the polytheist may have a clean garment and a washed body, yet he is impure in his essence (jawhar) — that is, his inner being is stained with filths.
42:51.section_title_en: The Book of the Revival of the Religious Sciences — Section 40: Exposition of the Harms of Disputation and the Destructive Traits of Character Generated Therefrom; Chapter Five: On the Etiquettes of the Learner and the Teacher
42:51.anchors:
- Root: طهر (ṭahara)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of cleanliness, purity, and freedom from filth — both physical and spiritual.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: purification (taṭhīr) is the prerequisite for any act of worship (ʿibādah); inner purification from blameworthy traits parallels outer purification from ritual impurities (aḥdāth) for the validity of prayer.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) refers to physical cleanliness; metaphorical (majāz) extends to purity of the soul and heart from moral vices.
- Root: قلب (qalb)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The heart as the physical organ and center of the self.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The heart is that which is turned about (taqlīb) — its states fluctuate; it is the seat of understanding and the locus of divine knowledge.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the physical heart; Metaphorical: the inner spiritual reality (laṭīfah rabbāniyyah) that perceives and knows, the "house" of the angels.
- Root: نجس (najasa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Ritual impurity, filth, that which is avoided and shunned.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Impurity is not restricted to the sensory/physical; the polytheist (mushrik) is impure in essence (jawhar) — i.e., his inner being — even if his body is clean.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical uncleanliness; Metaphorical: moral and spiritual defilement that bars the angels and divine illumination from the heart.
- Root: عبر (ʿabara)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To cross over, to traverse from one side to another; to interpret.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Iʿtibār (reflection/consideration) is the crossing from the sensory/visible (shāhid) to the unseen/absent (ghāʾib) — drawing lessons from the apparent to the hidden.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: crossing a river or valley; Metaphorical: the intellectual passage from outward forms (ẓawāhir) to inner meanings (bawāṭin), distinguishing true allegorical interpretation from the invalid taʾwīl of the Bāṭiniyyah.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Restriction and Specification (al-ḥaṣr wa al-taqyīd bi-innamā) — governing the exclusive predication in the Prophet's statement "Prayer is built upon cleanliness" and the restriction of impurity to the polytheists, requiring precise parsing of what is affirmed and negated.
42:51.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Book of Knowledge'

42:52.arabic: نوره كمشكاة وسمى العلم المستفاد منه روحا ووحيا وحياة فقال تعالى {وكذلك أوحينا إليك روحا من أمرنا} وقال سبحانه أومن كان ميتا فأحييناه وجعلنا له نورا يمشي به في الناس وحيث ذكر النور والظلمة أراد به العلم والجهل كقوله {يخرجهم من الظلمات إلى النور} وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم يا أيها الناس اعقلوا عن ربكم وتواصوا بالعقل تعرفوا ما أمرتم به وما نهيتم عنه واعلموا أنه ينجدكم عند ربكم واعلموا أن العاقل من أطاع الله وإن كان دميم المنظر حقير الخطر دنيء المنزلة رث الهيئة وأن الجاهل من عصى الله تعالى وإن كان جميل المنظر عظيم الخطر شريف المنزلة حسن الهيئة فص
42:52.english: The Book of Seclusion ('Uzlah) — its explanation, God Most High willing. For this reason, Yūsuf ibn Asbāṭ wrote to Ḥudhayfah al-Marʿashī: "What is your opinion of one who remains, finding no one with whom to remember God Most High except that he is either sinful, or his remembrance in company is itself an act of disobedience — and that because he finds no one of his own kind?" And indeed he spoke truly, for mixing with people is never free from backbiting (ghībah), or listening to backbiting, or remaining silent upon wrongdoing (munkar). And the best of his states is that he either imparts knowledge or acquires it. Yet were this poor wretch to reflect, and to know that his imparting of knowledge is never free from the taints of ostentation (riyā'), the seeking of followers, and the desire for leadership (ri'āsah), he would know that the one who acquires knowledge from him only seeks to make it an instrument for pursuing the world and a means toward evil — so that the teacher becomes his helper therein, his support and his backer, preparing its causes for him, like one who sells a sword to a highway robber. For knowledge is like the sword: its soundness for good is like the soundness of the sword for warfare. And for this reason, it is not permitted to sell it to one whom one knows, by the indications of his circumstances, intends to use it to aid in cutting off the road.
42:52.section_title_en: The Book of Seclusion ('Uzlah) — Section 65, and The Seventh Book: On the Intellect, Its Nobility, Its Reality, and Its Divisions
42:52.anchors:
- Root: عقل (ʿaql)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The root denotes binding, restraining, and holding back; the intellect is that which restrains the soul from base desires and prevents it from straying.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "العقل يقال للقوة المتهيئة لقبول العلم، ويقال للعلم الذي يستفيده الإنسان بتلك القوة عقل" — The intellect is said of the faculty prepared for the reception of knowledge, and it is also said of the knowledge which man acquires by means of that faculty.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): intellectual apprehension and understanding. Metaphorical (Majaz): "نخلة لا تعقل الإبار" — a palm tree that does not accept pollination, i.e., does not grasp or take in.
- Root: علم (ʿilm)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Knowledge as the mark or sign by which a thing is known; the trace or landmark that guides.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "العلم: إدراك الشيء بحقيقته" — Knowledge is the apprehension of a thing in its true reality; it is of two kinds: apprehension of the essence of a thing, and judgment upon a thing regarding what exists for it or is negated of it.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: certain awareness. Metaphorical: "هو من أعلام العلم الخافقه" — he is among the lofty banners of knowledge; knowledge as a guiding landmark (maʿlam).
- Root: نور (nūr)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Light; the first to set up beacons (manār) on his path in his campaigns to guide his return.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "النور: الضوء المنتشر الذي يعين على الإبصار" — Light is the diffused radiance that aids vision; it is of two kinds: that perceived by the eye of inner insight (baṣīrah) — such as the light of the intellect and the light of the Qur'an — and that perceived by the eye of the head, such as the celestial bodies.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: illumination. Metaphorical: "نور الأمر: بينه" — he illuminated the matter: he made it clear; "وهذا أنور من ذاك: أبين" — this is more luminous than that: more evident.
- Sibawayh Rule: Restriction and Focused Predication (al-ḥaṣr wa al-taqyīd bi-innamā) — governing the exclusive attribution of a predicate to a subject, as in the author's restriction of the scholar's condition to one of two men, and the exclusion of the third.
42:52.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Book of Knowledge'

43:32.arabic: بقوله تعالى: {نحن قسمنا بينهم معيشتهم في الحياة الدنيا ورفعنا بعضهم فوق بعض درجات ليتخذ بعضهم بعضا سخريا} فإن قيل: لا حاجة إلى تقدير عموم التحريم حتى لا يبقى حلال فإن ذلك غير واقع وهو معلوم ولا شك في أن البعض حرام وذلك البعض هو الأقل أو الأكثر فيه نظر وما ذكرتموه من أنه الأقل بالإضافة إلى الكل جلي ولكن لا بد من دليل محصل على تجويزه ليس من المصالح المرسلة وما ذكرتموه من التقسيمات كلها مصالح مرسلة فلا بد لها من شاهد معين تقاس عليه حتى يكون الدليل مقبولا بالاتفاق فإن بعض العلماء لا يقبل المصالح المرسلة فأقول: إن سلم أن الحرام هو الأقل فيكفينا برهانا عصر
43:32.english: For the craftsmen are only subjugated so that the kingdom may be ordered for the kings. Likewise, those who turn toward the worldly life are subjugated so that the path of religion may be secured for the people of religion — and it is the kingdom of the Hereafter. And were it not for them, the religion of the people of religion would not be secured either. Thus the condition for the soundness of their religion is that the majority turn away from their path and occupy themselves with the affairs of the world. And that is a division preceded by the eternal will (al-mashīʾah al-azaliyyah). And to it points His saying, exalted: {«نَحْنُ قَسَمْنَا بَيْنَهُم مَّعِيشَتَهُمْ فِي الْحَيَاةِ الدُّنْيَا وَرَفَعْنَا بَعْضَهُمْ فَوْقَ بَعْضٍ دَرَجَاتٍ لِّيَتَّخِذَ بَعْضُهُم بَعْضًا سُخْرِيًّا»} ("We have apportioned among them their livelihood in the life of this world, and raised some of them above others in degrees, that some of them may take others in service") [al-Zukhruf 43:32].
43:32.section_title_en: On the Permissibility of Dealing with Unlawful Wealth in Times of General Corruption — Section 355
43:32.anchors:
- Root: رسل (R-S-L)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of sending forth gently, dispatch with ease; a messenger (rasūl) is one sent forth.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Root denotes being sent forth with deliberation and ease; from it derives the concept of the messenger, and metaphorically gentleness (rifq) — "upon your gentleness" (ʿalā rislika).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: sending a message or messenger. Metaphorical: "God sent upon them punishment" — the unleashing of divine decree; "the arrows are the messengers of death" — the instrumentality of created causes in executing ordained ends.
- Root: صلح (S-L-Ḥ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Rightness, soundness, the opposite of corruption (fasād).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Ṣalāḥ is the opposite of fasād, applied predominantly to acts; the Quran contrasts it with corruption and with evil deeds. The term ṣulḥ specifically concerns removing discord between people.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "his condition became sound"; "I repaired the sandal." Metaphorical: "this leather is suitable for the sandal" — fitness for a purpose; "he did good to his beast" — beneficence and care.
- Root: ملك (M-L-K)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Possession, dominion, sovereignty; to have power over something.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-Mulk is one who disposes by command and prohibition over a people — specifically governance of rational beings. Two types: possession/assumption of authority, and the power/capacity for it whether or not exercised.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "he possessed the thing and owned it"; "to God belongs the Kingdom and the Dominion." Metaphorical: "he married the woman" (malaka al-mar'ah); "he mastered himself at the moment of anger" — self-possession as dominion over one's own faculties.
- Root: دنا (D-N-W)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Nearness, proximity; the lower world (dunyā) named for its nearness to us.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-Dunūw is proximity by essence or by judgment, used of place, time, and station. The "nearer" (adnā) sometimes means the lesser, contrasted with the greater.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: proximity in space or rank. Metaphorical: the dunyā as that which is low and base (danīʾ) — the world as the inferior realm contrasted with the Hereafter.

- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication)
  * Governing Rule: When the particle innamā precedes a clause, it restricts the predicate to the subject alone, negating any extension beyond it. This is operative in the author's argument that the way of complete scrupulousness (al-waraʿ) is restricted to the fifth probability alone, and that the fourth probability is the one determined for legal ruling (fatwā) — each restricted to its proper domain.
43:32.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'The Lawful and Prohibited'

43:32.arabic: وأصل هذا كله الحسد ثم نظرت إلى قول الله عز وجل نحن قسمنا بينهم معيشتهم في الحياة الدنيا فتركت الحسد واجتنبت الخلق وعلمت أن القسمة من عند الله سبحانه وتعالى فتركت عداوة الخلق عني السادسة نظرت إلى هذا الخلق يبغي بعضهم على بعض ويقاتل بعضهم بعضا فرجعت إلى قول الله عز وجل إن الشيطان لكم عدو فاتخذوه عدوا فعاديته وحده واجتهدت في أخذ حذري منه لأن الله تعالى شهد عليه أنه عدو لي فتركت عداوة الخلق غيره السابعة نظرت إلى هذا الخلق فرأيت كل واحد منهم يطلب هذه الكسرة فيذل فيها نفسه ويدخل فيما لا يحل له ثم نظرت إلى قوله تعالى وما من دابة في الأرض إل
43:32.english: Know that the scholar who does not act upon his knowledge is condemned by the Book, the Sunnah, and the sayings of the sages. God, exalted be He, said: {«يا أيها الذين آمنوا لم تقولون ما لا تفعلون * كبر مقتا عند الله أن تقولوا ما لا تفعلون»} ("O you who believe, why do you say what you do not do? Most hateful it is to God that you say what you do not do"). And He said: {«أتأمرون الناس بالبر وتنسون أنفسكم»} ("Do you command people to righteousness while you forget yourselves?"). And He said: {«ومن الناس من يعجبك قوله في الحياة الدنيا ويشهد الله على ما في قلبه وهو ألد الخصام»} ("And among people is he whose speech pleases you in the worldly life, and he calls God to witness what is in his heart, yet he is the fiercest of opponents").
43:32.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Book of Knowledge'

43:32.arabic: يتيم كيف بعثه الله إلينا فقال تعالى {أهم يقسمون رحمة ربك} وقال الله تعالى {ليقولوا أهؤلاء من الله عليهم من بيننا} أي استحقارا لهم واستبعادا لتقدمهم وقالت قريش لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كيف نجلس إليك وعندك هؤلاء وأشاروا إلى فقراء المسلمين فازدروهم بأعينهم لفقرهم وتكبروا عن مجالستهم فأنزل الله تعالى {ولا تطرد الذين يدعون ربهم بالغداة والعشي} إلى قوله {ما عليك من حسابهم} وقال تعالى {واصبر نفسك مع الذين يدعون ربهم بالغداة والعشي يريدون وجهه ولا تعد عيناك عنهم تريد زينة الحياة الدنيا} // حديث قالت قريش لرسول
43:32.english: Know that the one against whom pride is directed is either God—mighty and majestic—or His messengers, or the rest of His creation. Man has been created unjust and ignorant {«وخلق الإنسان ظلوما جهولا»}, so at times he grows proud against the creation, and at times he grows proud against the Creator. Thus, pride, considered with respect to the one against whom it is directed, falls into three divisions.
43:32.section_title_en: Exposition of the One Against Whom Pride Is Directed, Its Degrees, Its Divisions, and the Fruits of Pride Within It
43:32.anchors:
- Root: كبر (k-b-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root denotes magnitude, whether physical size, age, or rank; "الكبرة" specifically marks the state of advanced age or an ingrained, chronic condition.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الكبير والصغير من الأسماء المتضايفة" — bigness and smallness are relative terms. In the theological context, pride (الكبر) is the soul's self-magnification against another, a relational vice that distorts the creature's standing before the Creator.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah) usage concerns physical or quantitative magnitude. Metaphorical (Majaz) usage transfers this to moral and spiritual stature, as in "كبر علي ذلك" (it weighed heavily upon him) — here, the soul's swelling against divine command is a metaphorical arrogation of greatness.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Prepositional Interposition (باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور) — Governing the syntactic tension between the agent of pride (المتكبر) and its object (المتكبر عليه), where the preposition "على" carries the full weight of opposition and elevation, structuring the periodic sentences that follow.
43:32.topic: Al-Ghazali on purifying the character, moral diseases, and spiritual remedies, from 'Condemnation of Pride and Conceit'

43:35.arabic: وعظمت منزلته فقال صلى الله عليه وسلم {وإن كل ذلك لما متاع الحياة الدنيا والآخرة عند ربك للمتقين} إن العاقل هو المتقي وإن كان في الدنيا خسيسا ذليلا (4) قال صلى الله عليه وسلم في حديث آخر إنما العاقل من آمن بالله وصدق رسله وعمل بطاعته (5) ويشبه أن يكون أصل الاسم في أصل اللغة لتلك الغريزة وكذلك في الاستعمال وإنما أطلق على العلوم من حيث إنها ثمرتها كما يعرف الشيء بثمرته فيقال العلم هو الخشية والعالم من يخشى الله تعالى فإن الخشية ثمرة العلم فتكون كالمجاز لغير تلك الغريزة ولكن ليس الغرض البحث عن اللغة والمقصود أن هذه الأقسام الأربعة موجودة وال
43:35.english: I say: Know that the washing of the eye is forbidden — that is, the eye of insight (ʿayn al-baṣīrah) is not to be washed with the water of blind imitation and mere hearsay, for it is the organ by which the realities of the intellect are disclosed. And the divisions of what the name "intellect" (al-ʿaql) is applied to have become clear: it is said of the inborn faculty (al-gharīzah), and it is said of the knowledge that is acquired through that faculty, and it is said of the state of that knowledge when it governs the soul, and it is said of the very actions that proceed from that governance.
43:35.section_title_en: The Washing of the Eye is Forbidden — On the True Meaning of Intellect (ʿAql) and Its Divisions
43:35.anchors:
- Root: عقل (ʿAql)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The root denotes binding, restraining, and holding back — the intellect is that which restrains the soul from base desires and prevents it from straying.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "العقل يقال للقوة المتهيئة لقبول العلم، ويقال للعلم الذي يستفيده الإنسان بتلك القوة عقل" — al-ʿaql is said of the faculty prepared to receive knowledge, and it is also said of the knowledge acquired by that faculty. It is the instrument of divine discernment and the locus of taklīf (moral responsibility).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): the inborn faculty of discernment. Metaphorical (Majaz): "نخلة لا تعقل الإبار إذا لم تقبله" — a palm tree that does not accept pollination is said to be "not to ʿaqil" the pollen, extending the root to the sense of "accepting/receiving." Thus, knowledge is called ʿaql metaphorically as its fruit.
- Root: بصر (Baṣar)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Sight, perception — both of the eye and of the heart.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "البصر يقال للجارحة الناظرة... ويقال لقوة القلب المدركة: بصيرة وبصر" — baṣar is said of the seeing organ, and of the perceiving power of the heart: baṣīrah and baṣar. The inner sight (baṣīrah) perceives immaterial realities.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: ocular vision. Metaphorical: "هذه آية مبصرة" — this is an illuminating sign; "واجعلني بصيرة عليهم أي رقيبا وشاهدا" — make me a watcher over them. The inner eye perceives what the outer eye cannot.
- Root: فطر (Faṭara)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To split, cleave, originate, create — the primordial act of divine creation.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "أصل الفطر: الشق طولا... وفطر الله الخلق" — the root is splitting lengthwise; God's "fatr" of creation is His originating of things. "فطرة الله التي فطر الناس عليها" — the primordial disposition upon which God originated mankind.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "فطر الله الخلق، وهو فاطر السموات: مبتدعها" — God originated creation; He is the Originator of the heavens. "وكل مولود يولد على الفطرة" — every newborn is born upon the fiṭrah, i.e., the innate disposition receptive to the religion of truth.
- Root: نفس (Nafs)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Self, soul, spirit; the innermost reality of a thing.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "النفس: الروح... وقوله: تعلم ما في نفسي ولا أعلم ما في نفسك" — nafs is the spirit/soul; "You know what is in my nafs and I know not what is in Your nafs" — the nafs is the seat of inner assent and recognition.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the self. Metaphorical: "دفق نفسه أي دمه" — he poured out his nafs, i.e., his blood. The nafs is the locus of the primordial covenant (mīthāq).
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — The construction "إنما العاقل من آمن بالله" restricts the predicate: the intellect is not merely a faculty of cleverness but is defined by its fruit — faith and God-consciousness (taqwā).
43:35.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Book of Knowledge'

43:58.arabic: ضربوه لك إلا جدلا بل هم قوم خصمون وفي الحديث في معنى قوله تعالى {فأما الذين في قلوبهم زيغ} الآية هم أهل الجدل الذين عناهم الله بقوله تعالى فاحذرهم (2) وقال بعض السلف يكون في آخر الزمان قوم يغلق عليهم باب العمل ويفتح لهم باب الجدل وفي بعض الأخبار إنكم في زمان ألهمتم فيه العمل وسيأتي قوم يلهمون الجدل (3) وفي الخبر المشهور أبغض الخلق إلى الله تعالى الألد الخصم (4) وفي الخبر ما أتى قوم المنطق إلا منعوا العمل (5) والله أعلم
43:58.english: This speech, perhaps, when heard from its speaker, prompts the saying: "People are enemies of what they do not know." So do not think that [of me] — for you have fallen upon one who is an expert (khabīr). Accept this counsel from one who wasted his life upon it for a time, and exceeded the earlier ones in composing, verifying, disputing, and elucidating — then God inspired him with his right course and showed him its defect, so he abandoned it and occupied himself with his own soul. Let not the saying of him who says, "The legal opinion (al-fatwā) is the pillar of the Sacred Law, and its rationales (ʿilal) are not known except through the science of disputation (ʿilm al-khilāf)," deceive you. For the rationales of the [established] school (al-madhhab) are mentioned within the school itself; and what is added upon them are disputations that the earlier ones — nor even the Companions — ever knew, and they were more knowledgeable of the rationales of legal opinions than others. Rather, these [disputations], besides being useless for the science of the school, are harmful and corrupting of the very taste (dhawq) of jurisprudence. For that which the intuition (hads) of the muftī testifies to — when his taste in jurisprudence is sound — cannot, in most cases, be made to conform to the conditions of formal disputation (shurūṭ al-jadal). Whoever accustoms his nature to the formalities of disputation, his mind submits to the requirements of disputation and shrinks from submitting to the taste of jurisprudence.
43:58.section_title_en: On the Soul — A Warning Against the Newly-Invented Disputations (Section 34)
43:58.anchors:
- Root: جدل (j-d-l)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To twist or braid a rope tightly; to throw someone down upon hard ground (al-jadālah).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Disputation (jadal) is a mutual exchange aimed at overcoming and prevailing — as if each disputant twists the other away from his opinion; from jadala al-ḥabl, to braid tightly.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: twisting/braiding; Metaphorical: a woman "majdūlah al-khalq" (well-knit in frame), and "disputation" as a wrestling-down of the opponent's view.
- Root: خبر (kh-b-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Knowledge of a thing; to be acquainted with the inner state of an affair.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Khabar is knowledge of things via report; khibrah is knowledge of the inner realities of a matter.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: to test/try a man; Metaphorical: "his mirror reports of his unknown state" — knowledge of hidden conditions.
- Root: وفي (w-f-y)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To fulfill completely, to reach full measure.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-Wāfī: one who has reached completion; awfā bi-ʿahdihi: to fulfill one's covenant entirely.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: full-weight coin, full measure; Metaphorical: awfā ʿalā al-miʾah — to exceed a hundred; tawaffāhu Allāh — God takes in full.
- Root: علم (ʿ-l-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: A mark/trace by which a thing is known; knowledge as the apprehension of a thing's reality.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): ʿIlm is the apprehension of a thing in its true reality — either grasping its essence or judging its existence/non-existence.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: to perceive/know; Metaphorical: "he is among the lofty banners (aʿlām) of knowledge" — a distinguished signpost of learning.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Restriction and Focused Predication (al-ḥaṣr wa-l-taqyīd bi-innamā) — used to confine the blame of disputation to those who seek fame, and to restrict true benefit to sincere works.
43:58.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Book of Knowledge'

43:67.arabic: المؤمنون إخوة} وداخلون في مقتضى قوله تعالى {الأخلاء يومئذ بعضهم لبعض عدو إلا المتقين} الوظيفة الثانية أن يقتدى بصاحب الشرع صلوات الله عليه وسلامه فلا يطلب على إفادة العلم أجرا ولا يقصد به جزاء ولا شكرا بل يعلم لوجه الله تعالى وطلبا للتقرب إليه ولا يرى لنفسه منة عليهم وإن كانت المنة لازمة عليهم بل يرى الفضل لهم إذ هذبوا قلوبهم لأن تتقرب إلى الله تعالى بزراعة العلوم فيها كالذي يعيرك الأرض لتزرع فيها لنفسك زراعة فمنفعتك بها تزيد على منفعة صاحب الأرض فكيف تقلده منه وثوابك في التعليم أكثر من ثواب المتعلم عند الله تعالى ولولا المتعلم
43:67.english: And those who turn aside to seek leadership (al-riyāsah) through the sciences have departed from the requirement of His saying, Exalted: {«The believers are but brothers»} (al-Ḥujurāt 49:10), and have entered into the implication of His saying, Exalted: {«Intimate friends on that Day will be enemies to one another, except the God-fearing»} (al-Zukhruf 43:67).
43:67.section_title_en: The Duties of the Teacher — Section 46: On the Teacher's Sincerity, His Conduct Toward Students, and the Signs of Those Who Seek the World Through Knowledge
43:67.anchors:
- Root: قصد (qaṣada)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of "intending, aiming toward, taking the straight path to a goal"; al-Ayn notes its use in aiming at a target.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Al-Qaṣd: the straightness of the path... al-iqtiṣād (moderation) is praiseworthy absolutely, as in generosity between extravagance and miserliness."
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "I intended him and intended for him" (physical direction). Metaphorical: "He was moderate in his livelihood... he who does not exceed the limit in a matter and is content with the middle way."
- Root: علم (ʿalima)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Knowledge as the perception of a thing's reality; al-Ayn traces its verbal forms across perception and knowing.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Al-ʿIlm: the apprehension of a thing by its true reality... two kinds: apprehension of the essence of a thing, and judgment upon a thing."
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "He was a sign (ʿalam) of knowledge." Metaphorical: "The landmarks (maʿālim) of the road" — the traces by which one is guided.
- Root: أخل (akhala)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "Al-Akhillāʾ: intimate friends (pl. of khalīl)." Al-Ayn: "Al-Maʾlaka: the message, because it is chewed (yuʾlak) in the mouth."
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Al-Khullāh: sincere friendship... {«Intimate friends on that Day will be enemies to one another, except the God-fearing»} (al-Zukhruf 43:67)."
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — "Innamā" restricts the predicate to the subject alone, excluding all else; used here to delimit the brotherhood of believers and the enmity of the wicked on the Day of Judgment.
43:67.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Book of Knowledge'

43:87.arabic: ولذلك قال تعالى ولئن سألتهم من خلقهم ليقولن الله معناه إن اعتبرت أحوالهم شهدت بذلك نفوسهم وبواطنهم فطرة الله التي فطر الناس عليها أي كل آدمي فطر على الإيمان بالله عز وجل بل على معرفة الأشياء على ما هي عليه أعني أنها كالمضمنة فيها لقرب استعدادها للإدراك ثم لما كان الإيمان مركوزا في النفوس بالفطرة انقسم الناس إلى قسمين إلى من أعرض فنسي وهم الكفار وإلى من أجال خاطره فتذكر فكان كمن حمل شهادة فنسيها بغفلة ثم تذكرها ولذلك قال عز وجل لعلهم يتذكرون وليتذكر أولوا الألباب واذكروا نعمة الله عليكم وميثاقه

  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "أصل الفطر: الشق طولا... وفطر الله الخلق" — the root is splitting lengthwise; God's "fatr" of creation is His originating of things. "فطرة الله التي فطر الناس عليها" — the primordial disposition upon which God originated mankind.

- Root: نفس (Nafs)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Self, soul, spirit; the innermost reality of a thing.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "النفس: الروح... وقوله: تعلم ما في نفسي ولا أعلم ما في نفسك" — nafs is the spirit/soul; "You know what is in my nafs and I know not what is in Your nafs" — the nafs is the seat of inner assent and recognition.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the self. Metaphorical: "دفق نفسه أي دمه" — he poured out his nafs, i.e., his blood. The nafs is the locus of the primordial covenant (mīthāq).
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — The construction "إنما العاقل من آمن بالله" restricts the predicate: the intellect is not merely a faculty of cleverness but is defined by its fruit — faith and God-consciousness (taqwā).
43:87.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Book of Knowledge'

46:11.arabic: جهله فإن الناس أعداء ما جهلوا قال تعالى وإذا لم يهتدوا به فسيقولون هذا إفك قديم قال الشاعر ومن يك ذا فم مر مريض ...
46:11.english: I say: Knowledge is like a torrent that is hostile to the elevated place — it flows only to the low ground. Thus knowledge is not attained except through humility and the casting of one's hearing [in attentive submission]. God — exalted is He — said: {«Indeed in that is a reminder for whoever has a heart or casts his hearing while present as a witness»} (Q 50:37). And the meaning of his being "one having a heart" is that he should be receptive to knowledge, comprehending it. But then the capacity for understanding does not avail him until he casts his hearing while being a present witness — present of heart — so that he may receive everything that is cast to him with excellence of listening, supplication, gratitude, joy, and acceptance of the benefaction.
46:11.section_title_en: The Revival of the Religious Sciences — Book I, Section 42: On the Duties of the Student (Ādāb al-Mutaʿallim)
46:11.anchors:
- Root: ع ل م (ʿ-l-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of knowing, perceiving a thing in its reality; the mark, trace, or sign by which one is guided.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "العلم: إدراك الشيء بحقيقته" — knowledge is the apprehension of a thing in its true reality, divided into apprehension of the essence and judgment upon it.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): "هو من أعلام العلم الخافقه" — he is among the lofty banners of knowledge. Metaphorical (majāz): "خفيت معالم الطريق" — the waymarks of the road are hidden, i.e., the traces by which one is guided.
- Root: س م ع (s-m-ʿ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Hearing, listening; the ear; obedience and acceptance.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Hearing with attentive presence of heart, not merely the physical sensation of sound.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: auditory perception. Metaphorical: "ألقى السمع" — to cast one's hearing, i.e., to listen with full attentiveness and submission.
- Root: ق ل ب (q-l-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The heart; to turn, overturn, or transform a thing from one state to another.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "قلب الشيء: تصريفه وصرفه عن وجه إلى وجه" — the turning of a thing from one face to another; the heart as that which is ever-turning between states.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "قلب الشيء قلبا: حوله عن وجهه" — to turn a thing from its face. Metaphorical: "رجل قلب حول: يقلب الأمور ويحتال" — a man who turns matters over and devises means.
- Root: ب ح ر (b-ḥ-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The sea; vast expanse of water.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "أصل البحر: كل مكان واسع جامع للماء الكثير" — the sea is every vast place gathering much water; then metaphorically applied to one who expands deeply into a domain.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Metaphorical: "تبحر في العلم واستبحر فيه" — he plunged deep into knowledge and expanded therein like a sea.
- Sibawayh Rule: Bāb al-ḥaṣr wa-l-taqyīd bi-innamā (Restriction and Focused Predication) — the particle innamā restricts the predicate to the subject alone, negating all else; applied here to the exclusive path of the student's submission to the teacher's direction.
46:11.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications, prayers, and their spiritual power, from 'Book of Knowledge'

49:13.arabic: من الخنازير ولذلك قال تعالى {يا أيها الناس إنا خلقناكم من ذكر وأنثى} أي لا تفاوت في أنسابكم لاجتماعكم في أصل واحد ثم ذكر فائدة النسب فقال {وجعلناكم شعوبا وقبائل لتعارفوا} ثم بين أن الشرف بالتقوى لا بالنسب فقال {إن أكرمكم عند الله أتقاكم} ولما قيل لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم من أكرم الناس من أكيس الناس لم يقل من ينتمي إلى نسبي ولكن قال أكرمهم أكثرهم للموت ذكرا وأشدهم له استعدادا (1) حديث إن الله قد أذهب عنكم عيبة الجاهلية الحديث أخرجه أبو داود والترمذي وحسنه من حديث أبي هريرة ورواه الترمذي أيضا من حديث ابن عمر وقال غريب
49:13.english: The fourth: pride in noble lineage, like the pride of the Hashimite, to the point that some of them imagine that they will be saved by the nobility of their lineage and the salvation of their forefathers, and that they are forgiven; and some of them fancy that all of creation are their clients and slaves. Its remedy is that he should know that whenever he contradicts his forefathers in their deeds and their moral traits, yet imagines himself to be joined with them, he has indeed been ignorant. And if he emulates his forefathers, then their moral traits were not pride, but rather fear, self-contempt, magnifying others, and self-blame. For they were ennobled by obedience, knowledge, and praiseworthy qualities — not by lineage. So let him seek honor through that by which they were honored. For those who shared their lineage and participated with them in their tribes, yet did not believe in God and the Last Day, were in God's sight worse than dogs and viler than swine. For this reason God (Exalted is He) said: {«يا أيها الناس إنا خلقناكم من ذكر وأنثى»} — "O mankind, indeed We have created you from a male and a female" — that is, there is no disparity in your lineages because you all share a single origin. Then He mentioned the benefit of lineage, saying: {«وجعلناكم شعوبا وقبائل لتعارفوا»} — "And We made you peoples and tribes that you may know one another." Then He clarified that honor is by piety, not by lineage, saying: {«إن أكرمكم عند الله أتقاكم»} — "Indeed, the most noble of you in the sight of God is the most righteous of you." And when it was said to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him), "Who is the most noble of people?" — he did not say, "Whoever traces himself to my lineage," but rather he said, "The most noble of them is the one most mindful of death and the most prepared for it." (1) A hadith: "Indeed, God has removed from you the pride of the Age of Ignorance" — this hadith was transmitted by Abu Dawud and al-Tirmidhi, who deemed it sound (ḥasan), from the narration of Abu Hurayrah; al-Tirmidhi also narrated it from the narration of Ibn ʿUmar and said it is gharīb (uncommon).
49:13.section_title_en: The Book of the Revival of the Religious Sciences — Section 881: On the Wonders of Pride in Strength, Intellect, and Lineage, and Their Remedies
49:13.anchors:
- Root: عقل (ʿaql)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The faculty of restraint and comprehension; the intellect as that which binds one from error.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "العقل يقال للقوة المتهيئة لقبول العلم، ويقال للعلم الذي يستفيده الإنسان بتلك القوة عقل" — the power prepared for receiving knowledge, and the knowledge acquired thereby.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: sound judgment after folly; Metaphorical: "نخلة لا تعقل الإبار" — a palm that does not accept pollination, i.e., lacks receptivity.
- Root: نسب (nasab)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Lineage and kinship through forebears.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "النسب والنسبة: اشتراك من جهة أحد الأبوين" — participation through one of the two parents; two types: vertical (through ancestors) and horizontal (through collaterals).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "فلان حسيب نسيب" — noble in deed and lineage; Metaphorical: "بين الشيئين مناسبة" — proportionality or correspondence between things.
- Root: حدث (ḥadath)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Origination after non-existence; newness.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الحدوث: كون الشيء بعد أن لم يكن" — a thing's coming to be after it was not; "المحدث: ما أوجد بعد أن لم يكن" — the originated.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: recent events; Metaphorical: "كان عمر رضي الله عنه محدثا" — one inspired with true discernment.
- Root: نفس (nafs)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The self, soul, or spirit; that which animates.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "النفس: الروح" — the spirit; also the very essence (dhāt) when attributed to God.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: preciousness; Metaphorical: "دفق نفسه" — poured out his blood, i.e., his life.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Interposition (الفصل بين الجار والمجرور) — governing the permissible separation between a governing word and its governed prepositional phrase, applied here to parse the conditional and relative clauses conveying causal relations between pride and its consequences.
49:13.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'Condemnation of Pride and Conceit'

49:13.arabic: الحسب والشرف والنسب فنظرت فيها فإذا هي لا شيء ثم نظرت إلى قول الله تعالى إن أكرمكم عند الله أتقاكم فعملت في التقوى حتى أكون عند الله كريما الخامسة أني نظرت إلى هذا الخلق وهم يطعن بعضهم في بعض ويلعن بعضهم بعضا وأصل هذا كله الحسد ثم نظرت إلى قول الله عز وجل نحن قسمنا بينهم معيشتهم في الحياة الدنيا فتركت الحسد واجتنبت الخلق وعلمت أن القسمة من عند الله سبحانه وتعالى فتركت عداوة الخلق عني السادسة نظرت إلى هذا الخلق يبغي بعضهم على بعض ويقاتل بعضهم بعضا فرجعت إلى قول الله عز وجل إن الشيطان لكم عدو فاتخذوه عدوا فعاديته وحده واجتهدت في أخذ حذري منه
49:13.english: Know that the scholar who does not act upon his knowledge is condemned by the Book, the Sunnah, and the sayings of the sages. God, exalted be He, said: {«يا أيها الذين آمنوا لم تقولون ما لا تفعلون * كبر مقتا عند الله أن تقولوا ما لا تفعلون»} ("O you who believe, why do you say what you do not do? Most hateful it is to God that you say what you do not do"). And He said: {«أتأمرون الناس بالبر وتنسون أنفسكم»} ("Do you command people to righteousness while you forget yourselves?"). And He said: {«ومن الناس من يعجبك قوله في الحياة الدنيا ويشهد الله على ما في قلبه وهو ألد الخصام»} ("And among people is he whose speech pleases you in the worldly life, and he calls God to witness what is in his heart, yet he is the fiercest of opponents").
49:13.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Book of Knowledge'

51:55.arabic: اللفظ الرابع الذكر والتذكير فقد قال الله تعالى {وذكر فإن الذكرى تنفع المؤمنين} وقد ورد في الثناء على مجالس الذكر أخبار كثيرة كقوله صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا مررتم برياض الجنة فارتعوا قيل وما رياض الجنة قال مجالس الذكر (2) وفي الحديث إن لله تعالى ملائكة سياحين في الدنيا سوى ملائكة الخلق إذا رأوا مجالس الذكر ينادي بعضهم بعضا ألا هلموا إلى بغيتكم فيأتونهم ويحفون بهم ويستمعون ألا فاذكروا الله وذكروا أنفسكم (3) فنقل ذلك إلى ما ترى أكثر الوعاظ في هذا الزمان يواظبون عليه وهو القصص والأشعار والشطح والطامات أما القصص فهي بدعة وقد ورد نهي ا
51:55.english: This [bankruptcy] is like the bankruptcy of one who rises at dawn, turns toward the qiblah, and says: "I have turned my face toward Him Who originated the heavens and the earth, as a ḥanīf" {«وجهت وجهي للذي فطر السموات والأرض حنيفا»} — and this is the very first lie with which he opens his address to God each day, unless the face of his heart is turned toward God — Exalted is He — exclusively and specifically. For if by "face" he means the outward, physical face, then his face is turned only toward the Kaʿbah, and he has merely diverted it from the other cardinal directions. But the Kaʿbah is not a direction (jihah) for the One Who originated the heavens and the earth, such that one who turns toward it would thereby be turning toward Him — far exalted is He above being bounded by directions and regions (aqṭār).
51:55.section_title_en: The Revival of the Religious Sciences — Section 29: On True Monotheism (Tawḥīd) and the Remembrance of God (Dhikr)
51:55.anchors:
- Root: هوي (h-w-y)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الهوى: سقوط الشيء من علو إلى أسفل؛ ثم استعمل في ميل النفس إلى ما تلتذ به من غير داعية العقل"
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الهوى: ميل النفس إلى ما تميل إليه من الشهوات، وقد ذم الله اتباعه في غير موضع من كتابه"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "هويته: أحببته" — Metaphorical: "فلان يهوي في الدين: يذهب فيه بغير بصيرة"
- Root: وجه (w-j-h)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الوجه: ما يستقبل به الشيء، وأول ما يبدو من الإنسان"
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "ولما كان الوجه أول ما يستقبلك وأشرف ما في ظاهر البدن استعمل في مستقبل كل شيء، وعبر عن الذات بالوجه في قوله: {ويبقى وجه ربك ذو الجلال والإكرام}"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "وجه الثوب: ما استقبلك منه" — Metaphorical: "وجه القلب: توجهه وإخلاصه لله"
- Root: ذكر (dh-k-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الذكر: نقيض النسيان، والذكر: الثناء والقول المتردد على اللسان"
  * Al-Raghib (Al-Mufradat): "الذكر: حضور المعنى في النفس، ويستعمل في القول الدال على ذلك، وفي الحفظ"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "ذكرت الشيء: استحضرته" — Metaphorical: "مجالس الذكر: المجالس التي يذكر فيها الله تعالى"
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — "إنما" restricts the predicate to the subject alone, negating all else; applied here to confine true tawḥīd to the heart's orientation, not the tongue's utterance.
51:55.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Book of Knowledge'

53:11.arabic: قال الله تعالى ما كذب الفؤاد ما رأى وقال تعالى وكذلك نرى إبراهيم ملكوت السموات والأرض الآية وسمي ضده عمى فقال تعالى فإنها لا تعمى الأبصار ولكن تعمي القلوب التي في الصدور وقال تعالى ومن كان في هذه أعمى فهو في الآخرة أعمى وأضل سبيلا وهذه الأمور التي كشفت للأنبياء بعضها كان بالبصر وبعضها كان بالبصيرة وسمي الكل رؤية وبالجملة من لم تكن بصيرته الباطنة ثاقبة لم يعلق به من الدين إلا قشوره وأمثلته دون لبابه وحقائقه فهذه أقسام ما ينطلق اسم العقل عليها
53:11.english: I say: Know that the washing of the eye is forbidden — that is, the eye of insight (ʿayn al-baṣīrah) is not to be washed with the water of blind imitation and mere hearsay, for it is the organ by which the realities of the intellect are disclosed. And the divisions of what the name "intellect" (al-ʿaql) is applied to have become clear: it is said of the inborn faculty (al-gharīzah), and it is said of the knowledge that is acquired through that faculty, and it is said of the state of that knowledge when it governs the soul, and it is said of the very actions that proceed from that governance.
53:11.section_title_en: The Washing of the Eye is Forbidden — On the True Meaning of Intellect (ʿAql) and Its Divisions
53:11.anchors:
- Root: عقل (ʿAql)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The root denotes binding, restraining, and holding back — the intellect is that which restrains the soul from base desires and prevents it from straying.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "العقل يقال للقوة المتهيئة لقبول العلم، ويقال للعلم الذي يستفيده الإنسان بتلك القوة عقل" — al-ʿaql is said of the faculty prepared to receive knowledge, and it is also said of the knowledge acquired by that faculty. It is the instrument of divine discernment and the locus of taklīf (moral responsibility).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): the inborn faculty of discernment. Metaphorical (Majaz): "نخلة لا تعقل الإبار إذا لم تقبله" — a palm tree that does not accept pollination is said to be "not to ʿaqil" the pollen, extending the root to the sense of "accepting/receiving." Thus, knowledge is called ʿaql metaphorically as its fruit.
- Root: بصر (Baṣar)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Sight, perception — both of the eye and of the heart.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "البصر يقال للجارحة الناظرة... ويقال لقوة القلب المدركة: بصيرة وبصر" — baṣar is said of the seeing organ, and of the perceiving power of the heart: baṣīrah and baṣar. The inner sight (baṣīrah) perceives immaterial realities.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: ocular vision. Metaphorical: "هذه آية مبصرة" — this is an illuminating sign; "واجعلني بصيرة عليهم أي رقيبا وشاهدا" — make me a watcher over them. The inner eye perceives what the outer eye cannot.
- Root: فطر (Faṭara)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To split, cleave, originate, create — the primordial act of divine creation.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "أصل الفطر: الشق طولا... وفطر الله الخلق" — the root is splitting lengthwise; God's "fatr" of creation is His originating of things. "فطرة الله التي فطر الناس عليها" — the primordial disposition upon which God originated mankind.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "فطر الله الخلق، وهو فاطر السموات: مبتدعها" — God originated creation; He is the Originator of the heavens. "وكل مولود يولد على الفطرة" — every newborn is born upon the fiṭrah, i.e., the innate disposition receptive to the religion of truth.
- Root: نفس (Nafs)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Self, soul, spirit; the innermost reality of a thing.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "النفس: الروح... وقوله: تعلم ما في نفسي ولا أعلم ما في نفسك" — nafs is the spirit/soul; "You know what is in my nafs and I know not what is in Your nafs" — the nafs is the seat of inner assent and recognition.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the self. Metaphorical: "دفق نفسه أي دمه" — he poured out his nafs, i.e., his blood. The nafs is the locus of the primordial covenant (mīthāq).
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — The construction "إنما العاقل من آمن بالله" restricts the predicate: the intellect is not merely a faculty of cleverness but is defined by its fruit — faith and God-consciousness (taqwā).
53:11.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Book of Knowledge'

53:32.arabic: ومنها تزكية النفس قال الله سبحانه وتعالى فلا تزكوا أنفسكم هو أعلم بمن اتقى وقيل لحكيم ما الصدق القبيح فقال ثناء المرء على نفسه ولا يخلو المناظر من الثناء على نفسه بالقوة والغلبة والتقدم على الأقران ولا ينفك في أثناء المناظرة عن قوله لست ممن يخفى عليه أمثال هذه الأمور وأنا المتفنن في العلوم والمستقل بالأصول وحفظ الأحاديث وغير ذلك مما يتمدح به تارة على سبيل الصلف وتارة للحاجة إلى ترويج كلامه ومعلوم أن الصلف والتمدح مذمومان شرعا وعقلا ومنها التجسس وتتبع عورات الناس وقد قال تعالى ولا تجسسوا والمناظر لا ينفك عن طلب عثرات أقرا
53:32.english:
**QUAD_ANCHORS:**
- Root: نظر (naẓara)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to look, to examine, to consider; al-munāẓarah is mutual examination/argumentation between two parties.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: naẓar as intellectual contemplation (taʾammul bi-l-baṣīrah); munāẓarah as dialectical exchange.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: sitting face-to-face in debate; Metaphorical: disputation for victory.
- Root: غلب (ghalaba)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to overcome, to conquer, to prevail.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-ghalabah as seeking to dominate another in argument.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: victory in combat; Metaphorical: intellectual supremacy.
- Root: حسد (ḥasada)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to envy, to wish removal of blessings from another.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: envy as wishing deprivation of blessings from the deserving — among the basest traits.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: envy of another's blessing; Metaphorical: consuming fire of the soul.
- Root: كبر (kabura)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to be great, to be haughty.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-kibr as self-elevation above others; condemned by God.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: greatness; Metaphorical: arrogance and pride.
- Root: غيب (ghāba)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to be absent, to be hidden.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-ghībah as mentioning another with what he dislikes in his absence — likened to eating carrion.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: backbiting; Metaphorical: consuming the flesh of one's brother.
- Root: راءى (rāʾā)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to show off, to display.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-riyāʾ as performing acts for the sake of being seen — hidden shirk.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: showing good deeds; Metaphorical: seeking reputation.
- Root: نفس (nafs)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: self, soul, spirit.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: tazkiyat al-nafs as self-praise and self-purification — forbidden by God.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: self; Metaphorical: self-commendation.
- Root: حقd (ḥaqida)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to bear malice, to harbor resentment.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-ḥiqd as nursing enmity in the heart — negated from the believer.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: bearing grudge; Metaphorical: hidden rancor.
- Root: نفاق (nifāq)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: hypocrisy, showing contrary to what one conceals.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: hypocrisy in deeds — outward display contrary to inward state.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: hypocrisy in faith; Metaphorical: hypocrisy in character.
- Root: علم (ʿalima)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to know, to perceive.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: knowledge as apprehension of reality — its pursuit for other than God is destructive.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: knowledge; Metaphorical: the dangerous burden of the scholar.
- Root: جدل (jadala)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to argue, to dispute.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-jidāl as contention; al-mirāʾ as disputation with falsehood — condemned.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: argumentation; Metaphorical: obstinate disputation.
- Root: شرك (sharaka)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to associate, to share.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-riyāʾ as hidden shirk — associating others with God in intention.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: polytheism; Metaphorical: hidden association in deeds.
- Root: موت (māta)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to die.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: death as separation of soul from body; spiritual death as ruin of the soul.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical death; Metaphorical: spiritual destruction.
- Root: حيى (ḥayiya)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to live.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: life as the power of perception; eternal life as the reward of the righteous.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical life; Metaphorical: spiritual vitality.
- Root: هلك (halaka)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to perish, to be destroyed.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-halāk as ruin; eternal destruction as everlasting punishment.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: destruction; Metaphorical: eternal ruin.
- Root: رياء (riyāʾ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: showing off, ostentation.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: riyāʾ as the incurable disease calling to the greatest sins.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: ostentation; Metaphorical: spiritual disease.
- Root: جاه (jāh)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: rank, status, prestige.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: love of status (ḥubb al-jāh) among the destructive traits.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: position; Metaphorical: seeking prestige.
- Root: مباهاة (mubāhāh)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: mutual boasting, vying in splendor.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: mubāhāh as each seeking to display superiority over the other.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: mutual boasting; Metaphorical: rivalry in honor.
- Root: مماراة (mumārāh)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: disputation, wrangling.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-mirāʾ as contentious argument — condemned by the Prophet.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: disputation; Metaphorical: obstinate wrangling.
- Root: فخر (fakhara)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to boast, to pride oneself.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-fakhr as self-glorification — among the blameworthy traits.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: boasting; Metaphorical: vainglory.
- Root: عجب (ʿajiba)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to wonder, to be amazed.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-ʿujb as self-admiration — among the destructive traits.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: wonder; Metaphorical: self-conceit.
- Root: بغض (baghiḍa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to hate, to detest.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-baghdāʾ as mutual hatred — contrary to brotherhood.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: hatred; Metaphorical: mutual enmity.
- Root: غضب (ghaḍiba)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to be angry.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-ghaḍab as anger — among the blameworthy traits.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: anger; Metaphorical: rage.
- Root: طمع (ṭamiʿa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to covet, to desire.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-ṭamaʿ as covetousness — among the destructive traits.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: desire; Metaphorical: greed.
- Root: أشر (ashira)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to be exultant, to be insolent.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-ashar as excessive joy and insolence — blameworthy.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: exultation; Metaphorical: insolence.
- Root: بطر (baṭira)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to be arrogant, to be ungrateful.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-baṭar as arrogance in prosperity — among the destructive traits.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: arrogance; Metaphorical: ingratitude for blessings.
- Root: خيلاء (khuyalāʾ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: pride, haughtiness.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-khuyalāʾ as pride and conceit — blameworthy.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: pride; Metaphorical: haughty bearing.
- Root: خشية (khashyah)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: fear, awe.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-khashyah as reverential fear — among the traits of the believers.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: fear; Metaphorical: reverential awe.
- Root: رحمة (raḥmah)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: mercy, compassion.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-raḥmah as tenderness of heart — among the traits of the believers.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: mercy; Metaphorical: compassion.
- Root: غفلة (ghaflah)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: heedlessness, inattention.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-ghaflah as heedlessness — contrary to vigilance.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: inattention; Metaphorical: spiritual heedlessness.
- Root: خشوع (khushūʿ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: humility, submissiveness.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-khushūʿ as humility — among the traits of the believers.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: humility; Metaphorical: devotional submission.
- Root: تذكير (tadhkīr)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: reminding, admonishing.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-tadhkīr as reminding of God — a righteous act.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: reminding; Metaphorical: preaching.
- Root: وعظ (waʿaẓa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to admonish, to exhort.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-waʿẓ as exhortation to obedience and warning against disobedience.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: admonition; Metaphorical: sermonizing.
- Root: فتوى (fatwā)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: legal ruling, formal opinion.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-fatwā as clarification of legal rulings.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: legal opinion; Metaphorical: religious authority.
- Root: قضاء (qaḍāʾ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: judgment, decree.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-qaḍāʾ as judgment between people.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: judgment; Metaphorical: judicial authority.
- Root: وقف (waqafa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to stop, to stand.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-waqf as endowment of property for charitable purposes.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: standing; Metaphorical: religious endowment.
- Root: ثواب (thawāb)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: reward, recompense.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-thawāb as divine recompense for righteous deeds.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: reward; Metaphorical: divine recompense.
- Root: عذاب (ʿadhāb)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: punishment, torment.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-ʿadhāb as divine punishment for the disobedient.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: punishment; Metaphorical: divine chastisement.
- Root: ملك (malaka)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to possess, to rule.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-mulk as sovereignty; al-mulk al-muʾabbad as eternal sovereignty in Paradise.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: dominion; Metaphorical: eternal kingdom.
- Root: نعيم (naʿīm)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: bliss, delight.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-naʿīm as bliss; al-naʿīm al-sarmad as everlasting bliss.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: delight; Metaphorical: eternal bliss.
- Root: رخصة (rukhaṣah)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: concession, dispensation.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-rukhaṣah as legal concession.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: concession; Metaphorical: legal dispensation.
- Root: رياسة (riyāsah)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: leadership, headship.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: love of leadership among the destructive traits.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: leadership; Metaphorical: seeking authority.
- Root: اندراس (indirās)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: effacement, obliteration.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: indirās al-ʿulūm as the obliteration of the sciences.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: effacement; Metaphorical: extinction of knowledge.
- Root: صبيان (ṣibyān)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: boys, children.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: children's motivation for learning through play.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: boys; Metaphorical: pupils.
- Root: مكتب (maktab)
  * Lisan / Ayn- Root: مكتب (maktab)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: place of instruction, school for boys.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: the elementary school where children are taught.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: school; Metaphorical: place of elementary learning.
- Root: خلاق (khilāq)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: portion, share, lot.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: "no portion" (lā khilāq) in the Hereafter — utter deprivation of divine reward.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: share; Metaphorical: spiritual allotment in the afterlife.
- Root: فاجر (fājir)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: wicked, immoral, profligate.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: the dissolute one who commits sins openly.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: sinner; Metaphorical: one through whom God nonetheless supports religion.
- Root: شمع (shamʿ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: candle, wax taper.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: the candle as parable — consuming itself while giving light to others.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: candle; Metaphorical: one who destroys himself but benefits others.
- Root: نار (nār)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: fire.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: fire as parable — consuming itself and all around it.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: fire; Metaphorical: one who destroys himself and others.
- Root: سعد (saʿida)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to be fortunate, to prosper.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: saʿādah as felicity — success in the Hereafter.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: good fortune; Metaphorical: eternal felicity.
- Root: شقي (shaqiya)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to be wretched, to be miserable.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: shaqāwah as wretchedness — ruin in the Hereafter.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: misery; Metaphorical: eternal ruin.
- Root: أخلص (akhlaṣa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to purify, to be sincere.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: ikhlāṣ as purifying intention for God alone — the condition of acceptance.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: sincerity; Metaphorical: pure devotion.
- Root: ريب (rāba)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to doubt, to suspect.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-rayb as doubt and uncertainty — to be dispelled by evidence.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: doubt; Metaphorical: skepticism.
