3:118.arabic: الله عليم بذات الصدور إن تمسسكم حسنة تسؤهم الآية وكذلك قال ودوا ما عنتم قد بدت البغضاء من أفواههم وما تخفي صدورهم أكبر والحسد بسبب البغض ربما يفضي إلى التنازع والتقاتل واستغراق العمر في إزالة النعمة بالحيل والسعاية وهتك الستر وما يجري مجراه السبب الثاني التعزز وهو أن يثقل عليه أن يترفع عليه غيره فإذا أصاب بعض أمثاله ولاية أو علما أو مالا خاف أن يتكبر عليه وهو لا يطيق تكبره ولا تسمح نفسه باحتمال صلفه وتفاخره عليه وليس من غرضه أن يتكبر بل غرضه أن يدفع كبره فإنه قد رضي بمساواته مثلا ولكن لا يرضى بالترفع عليه السبب الثالث الكبر وهو أن يكون في طبعه أن يتكبر عليه ويستصغر
3:118.english: I say: God is Knower of what is in the breasts. {«إِنْ تَمْسَسْكُمْ حَسَنَةٌ تَسُؤْهُمْ»} — "If good touches you, it grieves them" {«وَدُّوا مَا عَنِتُّمْ قَدْ بَدَتِ الْبَغْضَاءُ مِنْ أَفْوَاهِهِمْ وَمَا تُخْفِي صُدُورُهُمْ أَكْبَرُ»} — "They wish for your hardship; hatred has already appeared from their mouths, and what their breasts conceal is greater." And envy (ḥasad), arising from hatred, may lead to contention, mutual fighting, and the spending of one's entire life in removing another's blessing through stratagems, slander, the tearing of veils, and whatever runs in that course.
3:118.section_title_en: The Revival of the Religious Sciences — Book on the Rebuke of the Self: The Seven Causes of Envy (Section 722)
3:118.anchors:
- Root: سبب (sabab)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The rope by which one climbs; every means by which one reaches a thing.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Every means by which one arrives at something is called a sabab" — thus the causes enumerated here are the psychological "ropes" by which envy ascends in the soul.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: a physical cord. Metaphorical: any linkage or occasion — here, the inward occasions (asbāb) that give rise to ḥasad.
- Root: بغض (bughḍ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Hatred, aversion of the heart.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The opposite of love (maḥabbah); a disposition of the heart toward another's harm.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: inner aversion. Metaphorical: its "appearance from the mouths" (Quranic) as outward speech betraying the concealed hatred.
- Root: كبر (kibr)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Greatness; pride; disdain.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Al-kabīr and al-ṣaghīr are relative terms" — pride is the claim to greatness relative to another, deeming oneself above him.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: bigness in stature or age. Metaphorical: "takabbara 'alayhi" — to deem oneself greater than another and refuse submission to him.
- Root: قصد (qaṣd)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Straightness of path; intending a goal.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Al-qaṣd: istiqāmat al-ṭarīq" — the straight road; also moderation between extremes.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: to head toward a place. Metaphorical: "maqāṣid" — the aims and objectives toward which one directs oneself; here, the worldly goals whose pursuit breeds rivalry and envy.
- Root: نزل (nazal)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To descend from a height; to alight.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Al-nuzūl fī al-aṣl huwa inḥiṭāṭ min 'uluww" — descent from above; the sending down of revelation.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: descending from a high place. Metaphorical: "anzala Allāhu al-kitāb" — God's sending down of the Quran; and "mā unzila" — what was revealed, as in the Quranic citation regarding the Qurashites' objection to revelation upon a mere human.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Causal Coordination (al-'aṭf al-sababī) — The enumeration of the seven causes proceeds by coordinated clauses (fa-... thumma ...), each introduced as an independent proposition linked by causation (sabab), requiring the translator to preserve the logical sequence of psychological motivations without collapsing them into one another.
3:118.topic: Al-Ghazali on purifying the character, moral diseases, and spiritual remedies, from 'Condemnation of Envy'

3:119.arabic: بالعداوة إذ قال الله تعالى وإذا لقوكم قالوا آمنا وإذا خلو عضوا عليكم الأنامل من الغيظ قل موتوا بغيظكم إن
3:119.english: **The First Cause: Enmity and Hatred.** This is the most intense of the causes of envy. For when a person harms another by some cause, or opposes him in some aim in any manner, his heart comes to hate him and is angered against him, and rancor (ḥiqd) becomes firmly rooted in his soul. And rancor demands vindication (tashaffī) and revenge. If the hater is unable to vindicate himself, he loves that time itself should vindicate him. Perhaps he even attributes that to the honor of his own soul before God Almighty. So whenever a calamity befalls his enemy, he rejoices at it and supposes it to be a recompense from God for his hatred — that it was for his sake. And whenever a blessing befalls him, it grieves him, because it is contrary to his desire. Perhaps it even occurs to him that the other has no station with God, since God did not take vengeance for him against his enemy who harmed him, but rather bestowed blessing upon him. In sum, envy is inseparable from hatred and enmity; it never parts from them. The utmost limit of piety (al-tuqā) is only that one should not act unjustly and that one should dislike this [envy] in himself. But that a man should hate another, and then his joy and his grief at his state should become equal — this is simply not possible. And it is with this — namely, envy arising from enmity — that God Almighty described the disbelievers, for God Almighty said: {«وإذا لقوكم قالوا آمنا وإذا خلوا عضوا عليكم الأنامل من الغيظ قل موتوا بغيظكم»} ("And when they meet you, they say, 'We believe'; but when they are alone, they bite their fingertips at you in rage. Say: 'Die in your rage'" — Q. 3:119).
3:119.section_title_en: Section 721 — The Reality of Envy, Its Ruling, Its Divisions, and Its Degrees; The Causes of Envy and Rivalry
3:119.anchors:
- Root: حسد (ḥ-s-d)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of wishing for removal of a blessing from its possessor; the root carries the sense of spiteful resentment.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الحسد: تمني زوال نعمة من مستحق لها، وربما كان مع ذلك سعي في إزالتها" — Envy is the desire for the removal of a blessing from one who deserves it, and sometimes accompanied by striving to remove it. He cites {«ومن شر حاسد إذا حسد»} (Q. 113:5).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): "حسده على نعمة الله، وحسده نعمة الله" — to envy him for God's blessing. Metaphorical (majāz): The proverb "إن الحسد يأكل الجسد" (envy consumes the body) extends the root to describe the inner corrosion of the envier.
- Root: سبب (s-b-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: A rope, cord, or means by which one ascends or reaches something; any cause or connection.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "سمي كل ما يتوصل به إلى شيء سببا" — Everything by which one reaches something is called a cause (sabab). He cites {«وآتيناه من كل شيء سببا فأتبع سببا»} (Q. 18:84-85).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: a physical rope or cord. Metaphorical: any means, link, or occasion — as in the seven "doors" (abwāb) of entry for envy enumerated here.
- Root: عدو (ʿ-d-w)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To transgress, exceed bounds, or act with hostility; the enemy (ʿadūw) is one who oversteps against another.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Enmity (ʿadāwah) is the soul's disposition toward harming another; it is the opposite of friendship (wilāyah).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical transgression. Metaphorical: the inner state of hostility that drives one to wish harm upon another.
- Root: كبر (k-b-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To be great, large, or advanced; arrogance (kibr) is the soul's self-magnification.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الكبر: أن يرى الإنسان نفسه أكبر من غيره" — Arrogance is when one sees himself as greater than another, refusing to acknowledge the other's due.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical greatness. Metaphorical: the soul's haughtiness that refuses to accept another's superiority or blessing.
- Root: عجب (ʿ-j-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Astonishment or wonder at something extraordinary.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Self-amazement (ʿujb) is when one marvels at his own state or at another's, leading to disdain or disbelief at their worth.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: wonder at a marvel. Metaphorical: the envier's astonishment that a lesser person attained a great blessing.
- Root: خبث (kh-b-th)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Corruption, wickedness, or vileness of character.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الخبث: ما يستقبح من الأقوال والأفعال" — That which is repugnant in speech and deed; inner malice.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: that which is foul or impure. Metaphorical: the soul's innate wickedness that begrudges good to others.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد (Restriction & Specification) — The phrase "إنما نظرنا الآن في الحسد المذموم" restricts the present inquiry exclusively to blameworthy envy, distinguishing it from rivalry (munāfasah) which may be praiseworthy. The conditional clauses ("إما أن يكون...") enumerate exhaustive divisions (taqsīm) of causes, each introduced as a discrete possibility.
3:119.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Condemnation of Envy'

3:119.arabic: ألد الخصام وإذا تولى سعى في الأرض ليفسد فيها} الآية وقال تعالى {وإذا لقوكم قالوا آمنا وإذا خلوا عضوا عليكم الأنامل من الغيظ} وقال تعالى {يراؤون الناس ولا يذكرون الله إلا قليلا مذبذبين بين ذلك} والآيات فيهم كثيرة وكان النفاق يكثر في ابتداء الإسلام ممن يدخل في ظاهر الإسلام ابتداء لغرض وذلك مما يقل في زماننا ولكن يكثر نفاق من ينسل عن الدين باطنا فيجحد الجنة والنار والدار الآخرة ميلا إلى قول الملحدة أو يعتقد على بساط الشرع والأحكام ميلا إلى أهل الإباحة أو يعتقد كفرا أو بدعة وهو يظهر خلافه فهؤلاء من المنافقين والمرائين المخلدين في النار وليس وراء هذا الرياء رياء وحال هؤلاء
3:119.english: The fourth [case]: that the people's seeing him should be a weighty factor (murajjihan) and a strengthener of his vigor, such that were it not for that, he would not abandon the act of worship; and were the intention of ostentation alone [present], he would not have ventured upon it. So what we hold — and knowledge is with God — is that it does not annul the root of the reward, but rather it diminishes it; or he is punished to the measure of his intention of ostentation and rewarded to the measure of his intention of reward. As for his saying — may God's peace and blessings be upon him — that God the Exalted says: "I am the most Self-Sufficient of the self-sufficient, free of all need for partnership (shirk)" — that is carried upon the case when the two intentions are equal, or when the intention of ostentation is the weightier.
3:119.section_title_en: On the Degrees of Ostentation in Worship — The Second Pillar: That by Which One Ostentatiously Displays (Al-Riya' bi al-Ta'at)
3:119.anchors:
- Root: قصد (Qasada)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of "intending, aiming toward a goal, directing one's purpose."
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "القصد: استقامة الطريق" — intention as the straight path of the soul toward its object; in moral theology, it denotes the deliberate orientation of the will that determines the moral value of an act.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): "قصدته وقصدت له" — direct aiming. Metaphorical (Majaz): "قصد في الأمر إذا لم يجاوز فيه الحد" — moderation; here, the "intention" (qasd) is the precise measure by which an act is weighed between reward and punishment.
- Root: راءى (Ra'a) — from Root: رأى (Ra'a)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الرياء: إظهار العمل ليراه الناس" — showing one's deed so that people may see it; derived from الرؤية (sight/seeing).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Riya' is a branch of shirk (associating partners with God), for the actor directs his deed not to God alone but to the gaze of creatures, thus dividing his intention between the Creator and creation.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: seeing with the eye. Metaphorical: "راءى فلان" — to perform an act for the sake of being seen, i.e., seeking the approval of onlookers rather than the sight of God.
- Root: خلق (Khalaqa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الخلق: التقدير المستقيم" — measuring and proportioning; also "خلق الثوب" — wearing out a garment until it is threadbare.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الخلق أصله: التقدير المستقيم" — creation as precise estimation; in moral context, the "خلق" (character) is the inward measure by which a soul is formed.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "خلق الخراز الأديم" — the leather-worker cutting and measuring hide. Metaphorical: "خلق الله الخلق: أوجده على تقدير أوجبته الحكمة" — God's creation of creatures upon a measure required by wisdom; here, the "creatures" (الخلق) whose blame (المقت) is feared by the ostentatious worshipper.
- Root: نفق (Nafaqa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "نفق الشيء: مضى ونفد" — to pass away, to be spent, to perish.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "نفق الشيء: مضى ونفد، ينفق، إما بالبيع نحو: نفق البيع نفاقا" — to find a ready market; "ومنها نفاق الأيم" — hypocrisy as the "passing" of a false coin in the market of religion.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "نفقت الدراهم" — coins circulating and being spent. Metaphorical: "نافق" — the hypocrite (munafiq) whose outward faith circulates among people while his inward disbelief is void; the ostentatious man "spends" his deeds on the market of human praise.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The syntactic separation between a governing preposition and its object, as in "له من الثواب مثل ما عليه من العقاب," where the prepositional phrases are interposed to balance two opposing clauses, mirroring the theological weighing of reward against punishment.
3:119.topic: Al-Ghazali on the journey of the soul, death, and the Hereafter, from 'Condemnation of Status and Ostentation'

3:120.arabic: تمسسكم حسنة تسؤهم وإن تصبكم سيئة يفرحوا بها} وهذا الفرح شماتة والحسد والشماتة يتلازمان وقال تعالى {ود كثير من أهل الكتاب لو يردونكم من بعد إيمانكم كفارا حسدا من عند أنفسهم} فأخبر تعالى أن حبهم زوال نعمة الإيمان حسد وقال عز وجل {ودوا لو تكفرون كما كفروا فتكونون سواء} وذكر الله تعالى حسد إخوة يوسف عليه السلام وعبر عما في قلوبهم بقوله تعالى {إذ قالوا ليوسف وأخوه أحب إلى أبينا منا ونحن عصبة إن أبانا لفي ضلال مبين اقتلوا يوسف أو اطرحوه أرضا يخل لكم وجه أبيكم} فلما كرهوا حب أبيهم له وساءهم ذلك وأحبو
3:120.english: The Prophet ﷺ said: «إن المؤمن يغبط والمنافق يحسد» — "The believer aspires emulously, and the hypocrite envies."
3:120.section_title_en: On the Reality of Envy (Ḥasad) and Its Degrees — Section 720
3:120.anchors:
- Root: نعم (n-ʿ-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root meaning of "bounty, benefaction, grace" — that state of goodness and well-being bestowed.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "النعمة: الحالة الحسنة" — bounty is the excellent state/condition; it is the genus term applying to both little and much, as in {«وإن تعدوا نعمة الله لا تحصوها»} [Ibrahim: 34].
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): "جلت نعمة الله ونعماؤه" — bounty as actual bestowed good. Metaphorical (majāz): "خفت نعامتهم" — departure/removal, relevant to the envier's wish for the bounty's removal.
- Root: حسد (ḥ-s-d)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Envy — the desire for removal of another's good.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الحسد: تمني زوال نعمة من مستحق لها" — envy is wishing the removal of bounty from one who deserves it, sometimes accompanied by striving to effect its removal. Cited: «المؤمن يغبط والمنافق يحسد».
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "حسده على نعمة الله" — envying someone for God's bounty. "إن الحسد يأكل الجسد" — envy consumes the body.
- Root: نفس (n-f-s)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The self; also value, preciousness.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): النفس: الروح — the soul/spirit; also الذات (essence/self).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "شيء نفيس ومنفس" — a precious thing. Metaphorical: "دفق نفسه أي دمه" — poured out his self, i.e., his blood. From this root derives المنافسة (emulative competition) — the striving for precious things.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد (Restriction & Specification) — The definition of ḥasad is given as a restricted predication (ḥadd), delimiting its essential meaning: "كراهة النعمة وحب زوالها عن المنعم عليه" — the hatred of bounty and love of its removal from the one upon whom it is bestowed. This is a formal definition (ḥadd), not merely a lexical gloss.
3:120.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Condemnation of Envy'

4:54.arabic: تعالى أن يخبره باسمه فلم يخبره وقال أحدثك من عمله بثلاث كان لا يحسد الناس على ما آتاهم الله من فضله وكان لا يعق والديه ولا يمشي بالنميمة وقال زكريا عليه السلام قال الله تعالى الحاسد عدو لنعمتي متسخط لقضائي غير راض بقسمتي التي قسمت بين عبادي وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم أخوف ما أخاف على أمتي أن يكثر فيهم المال فيتحاسدون ويقتتلون (1) وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم استعينوا على قضاء الحوائج بالكتمان فإن كل ذي نعمة محسود (2) وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم إن لنعم الله أعداء فقيل ومن هم فقال الذين يحسدون الناس على ما آتاهم الله من فضله (3) حديث ستة يدخلون النار قبل
4:54.english: Know that envy (ḥasad) is likewise among the fruits of rancor (ḥiqd), and rancor is among the fruits of anger (ghaḍab) — so envy is a branch of a branch, while anger is the root of the root. Then envy has, among its blameworthy branches, that which can scarcely be enumerated. And there have come down, specifically in condemnation of envy, many reports (akhbār). The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: {«Envy consumes good deeds just as fire consumes wood»} (1). The ḥadīth: {«Do not cut one another off, nor turn your backs on one another, nor hate one another»} — agreed upon (muttafaq ʿalayh), and it has already preceded. (2) The ḥadīth of Anas: "We were sitting one day with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, when he said: 'There will now come upon you from this mountain pass a man from among the people of Paradise'" — the ḥadīth in its entirety, and in it: that man said, "I do not find in myself any rancor toward any of the Muslims, nor envy of anyone for the good that God has given him." Narrated by Aḥmad with a sound chain (isnād) upon the condition of the two Shaykhs (al-Bukhārī and Muslim), and narrated by al-Bazzār, and the man was named in one of its narrations as Saʿd — though in it there is Ibn Lahīʿah. (3) The ḥadīth: {«Three things from which no one escapes: suspicion, slander, and envy»} — and in another narration: "And few are those who escape them." It was related by Ibn Abī al-Dunyā in his book "Dhamm al-Ḥasad" (The Condemnation of Envy) from the ḥadīth of Abū Hurayrah — though in its chain there are Yaʿqūb ibn Muḥammad al-Zuhrī and Mūsā ibn Yaʿqūb al-Zamaʿī, both of whom the majority of scholars have declared weak. The second narration was also related by Ibn Abī al-Dunyā from the narration of ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Muʿāwiyah, and it is mursal (broken chain) and weak. Al-Ṭabarānī has something similar from the ḥadīth of Ḥārithah ibn al-Nuʿmān, and it has already preceded in the section on the afflictions of the tongue. And in one narration: {«Three things from which no one escapes — and few are those who escape them»} — so this narration affirms the possibility of deliverance. And he, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: {«There has crept upon you the disease of the nations before you: envy and hatred. And hatred is the clipper — I do not say it clips the hair, but rather it clips the religion. By Him in whose hand is the soul of Muḥammad, you shall not enter Paradise until you believe, and you shall not believe until you love one another. Shall I not inform you of that which will establish this for you? Spread peace (salām) among you»} (4). And he, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: {«Poverty almost becomes unbelief, and envy almost overcomes destiny (qadar)»} (5). And he, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: {«Indeed, my community will be afflicted with the disease of the nations.» They said: "And what is the disease of the nations?" He said: {«Extravagance, arrogance, accumulation, rivalry in worldly things, mutual distance, and mutual envy — until transgression (baghy) comes, and then destruction (harj)»} (6). And he, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: {«Do not show gloating (shamātah) over your brother, lest God heal him and afflict you»} (7). And it is narrated that Moses, peace be upon him, when he hastened to his Lord, Exalted is He, saw a man in the shade of the Throne (ʿArsh) and envied him his station (ghabaṭahu), saying: "This one is honored before his Lord." So he asked his Lord, Exalted is He, to inform him of his name, but He did not inform him, and said: "I shall tell you of three of his deeds: he did not envy people for what God had given them of His bounty, he was not undutiful to his parents, and he did not go about with slander (namīmah)." And Zechariah, peace be upon him, said: God, Exalted is He, said: {«The envier is an enemy of My blessing, resentful of My decree, dissatisfied with My apportioning which I have apportioned among My servants»}. And he, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: {«The thing I most fear for my community is that wealth will increase among them, and they will envy one another and fight one another»} (1). And he, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: {«Seek help in fulfilling your needs by keeping them secret, for everyone who possesses a blessing is envied»} (2). And he, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: {«Indeed, the blessings of God have enemies.» It was said: "And who are they?" He said: {«Those who envy people for what God has given them of His bounty»} (3). The ḥadīth: {«Six will enter the Fire before the Reckoning by a year.» It was said: "O Messenger of God, who are they?" He said: {«The unjust rulers»} — the ḥadīth — and in it: {«And the scholars who envy»}. Narrated by Abū Manṣūr al-Daylamī from the ḥadīth of Ibn ʿUmar and Anas with two weak chains of transmission.
4:54.section_title_en: Section 718 — On Envy (Ḥasad): Its Roots, Branches, and Blameworthy Fruits
4:54.anchors:
- Root: حسد (Ḥ-S-D)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of wishing for removal of a blessing from its possessor, rooted in spite and resentment.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الحسد: تمني زوال نعمة من مستحق لها" — Envy is the desire for the removal of a blessing from one who rightly deserves it, sometimes accompanied by active striving to effect its removal. The believer envies not, but the hypocrite does.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): "حسده على نعمة الله" — to envy him for God's blessing. Metaphorical (majāz): "إن الحسد يأكل الجسد" — envy consumes the body, as fire consumes wood, indicating its destructive spiritual effect.
- Root: حدث (Ḥ-D-TH)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Origination after non-existence; bringing into being after nothingness.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الحدوث: كون الشيء بعد أن لم يكن" — origination is a thing's coming to be after it was not. The ḥadīth (report) is so-called for its temporal proximity to the event it narrates.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "هو حدث من الأحداث" — he is a youth among youths. Metaphorical: "صاروا أحاديث" — they became subjects of talk, indicating fame or infamy spread by tongues.
- Root: ملك (M-L-K)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Possession, dominion, sovereignty; the one who possesses and disposes.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الملك: هو المتصرف بالأمر والنهي" — dominion is disposal by command and prohibition. Two kinds: actual possession/sovereignty, and the power/capacity to exercise it.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "ملكت فلانة" — he married her (possessed her in wedlock). Metaphorical: "ملك نفسه عند الغضب" — he mastered himself at the moment of anger, i.e., self-restraint.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — When the Prophet (ﷺ) says "إنما قتل ابن آدم أخاه حين حسده" (It was only envy that led the son of Adam to kill his brother), the restrictive particle إنما confines the cause of the first murder to envy alone, isolating it as the sole efficient cause of that primordial transgression.
4:54.topic: Al-Ghazali on purifying the character, moral diseases, and spiritual remedies, from 'Condemnation of Envy'

4:54.arabic: الله عليه وسلم إن لنعم الله أعداء فقيل ومن هم فقال الذين يحسدون الناس على ما آتاهم الله من فضله (3) حديث ستة يدخلون النار قبل الحساب بسنة قيل يا رسول الله ومن هم قال الأمراء بالجور الحديث وفيه والعلماء بالحسد أخرجه أبو منصور الديلمي من حديث ابن عمر وأنس بسندين ضعيفين // الآثار قال بعض السلف أول خطيئة هي الحسد حسد إبليس آدم عليه السلام على رتبته فأبى أن يسجد له فحمله على الحسد والمعصية وحكي أن عون بن عبد الله دخل على الفضل بن المهلب وكان يومئذ على واسط فقال إني أريد أن أعظك بشيء فقال وما هو قال إياك والكبر فإنه أول ذنب عصي الله
4:54.english: Know that envy (ḥasad) is likewise among the fruits of rancor (ḥiqd), and rancor is among the fruits of anger (ghaḍab) — so envy is a branch of a branch, while anger is the root of the root. Then envy has, among its blameworthy branches, that which can scarcely be enumerated. And there have come down, specifically in condemnation of envy, many reports (akhbār). The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: {«Envy consumes good deeds just as fire consumes wood»} (1). The ḥadīth: {«Do not cut one another off, nor turn your backs on one another, nor hate one another»} — agreed upon (muttafaq ʿalayh), and it has already preceded. (2) The ḥadīth of Anas: "We were sitting one day with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, when he said: 'There will now come upon you from this mountain pass a man from among the people of Paradise'" — the ḥadīth in its entirety, and in it: that man said, "I do not find in myself any rancor toward any of the Muslims, nor envy of anyone for the good that God has given him." Narrated by Aḥmad with a sound chain (isnād) upon the condition of the two Shaykhs (al-Bukhārī and Muslim), and narrated by al-Bazzār, and the man was named in one of its narrations as Saʿd — though in it there is Ibn Lahīʿah. (3) The ḥadīth: {«Three things from which no one escapes: suspicion, slander, and envy»} — and in another narration: "And few are those who escape them." It was related by Ibn Abī al-Dunyā in his book "Dhamm al-Ḥasad" (The Condemnation of Envy) from the ḥadīth of Abū Hurayrah — though in its chain there are Yaʿqūb ibn Muḥammad al-Zuhrī and Mūsā ibn Yaʿqūb al-Zamaʿī, both of whom the majority of scholars have declared weak. The second narration was also related by Ibn Abī al-Dunyā from the narration of ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Muʿāwiyah, and it is mursal (broken chain) and weak. Al-Ṭabarānī has something similar from the ḥadīth of Ḥārithah ibn al-Nuʿmān, and it has already preceded in the section on the afflictions of the tongue. And in one narration: {«Three things from which no one escapes — and few are those who escape them»} — so this narration affirms the possibility of deliverance. And he, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: {«There has crept upon you the disease of the nations before you: envy and hatred. And hatred is the clipper — I do not say it clips the hair, but rather it clips the religion. By Him in whose hand is the soul of Muḥammad, you shall not enter Paradise until you believe, and you shall not believe until you love one another. Shall I not inform you of that which will establish this for you? Spread peace (salām) among you»} (4). And he, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: {«Poverty almost becomes unbelief, and envy almost overcomes destiny (qadar)»} (5). And he, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: {«Indeed, my community will be afflicted with the disease of the nations.» They said: "And what is the disease of the nations?" He said: {«Extravagance, arrogance, accumulation, rivalry in worldly things, mutual distance, and mutual envy — until transgression (baghy) comes, and then destruction (harj)»} (6). And he, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: {«Do not show gloating (shamātah) over your brother, lest God heal him and afflict you»} (7). And it is narrated that Moses, peace be upon him, when he hastened to his Lord, Exalted is He, saw a man in the shade of the Throne (ʿArsh) and envied him his station (ghabaṭahu), saying: "This one is honored before his Lord." So he asked his Lord, Exalted is He, to inform him of his name, but He did not inform him, and said: "I shall tell you of three of his deeds: he did not envy people for what God had given them of His bounty, he was not undutiful to his parents, and he did not go about with slander (namīmah)." And Zechariah, peace be upon him, said: God, Exalted is He, said: {«The envier is an enemy of My blessing, resentful of My decree, dissatisfied with My apportioning which I have apportioned among My servants»}. And he, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: {«The thing I most fear for my community is that wealth will increase among them, and they will envy one another and fight one another»} (1). And he, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: {«Seek help in fulfilling your needs by keeping them secret, for everyone who possesses a blessing is envied»} (2). And he, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: {«Indeed, the blessings of God have enemies.» It was said: "And who are they?" He said: {«Those who envy people for what God has given them of His bounty»} (3). The ḥadīth: {«Six will enter the Fire before the Reckoning by a year.» It was said: "O Messenger of God, who are they?" He said: {«The unjust rulers»} — the ḥadīth — and in it: {«And the scholars who envy»}. Narrated by Abū Manṣūr al-Daylamī from the ḥadīth of Ibn ʿUmar and Anas with two weak chains of transmission.
4:54.section_title_en: Section 718 — On Envy (Ḥasad): Its Roots, Branches, and Blameworthy Fruits
4:54.anchors:
- Root: حسد (Ḥ-S-D)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of wishing for removal of a blessing from its possessor, rooted in spite and resentment.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الحسد: تمني زوال نعمة من مستحق لها" — Envy is the desire for the removal of a blessing from one who rightly deserves it, sometimes accompanied by active striving to effect its removal. The believer envies not, but the hypocrite does.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): "حسده على نعمة الله" — to envy him for God's blessing. Metaphorical (majāz): "إن الحسد يأكل الجسد" — envy consumes the body, as fire consumes wood, indicating its destructive spiritual effect.
- Root: حدث (Ḥ-D-TH)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Origination after non-existence; bringing into being after nothingness.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الحدوث: كون الشيء بعد أن لم يكن" — origination is a thing's coming to be after it was not. The ḥadīth (report) is so-called for its temporal proximity to the event it narrates.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "هو حدث من الأحداث" — he is a youth among youths. Metaphorical: "صاروا أحاديث" — they became subjects of talk, indicating fame or infamy spread by tongues.
- Root: ملك (M-L-K)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Possession, dominion, sovereignty; the one who possesses and disposes.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الملك: هو المتصرف بالأمر والنهي" — dominion is disposal by command and prohibition. Two kinds: actual possession/sovereignty, and the power/capacity to exercise it.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "ملكت فلانة" — he married her (possessed her in wedlock). Metaphorical: "ملك نفسه عند الغضب" — he mastered himself at the moment of anger, i.e., self-restraint.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — When the Prophet (ﷺ) says "إنما قتل ابن آدم أخاه حين حسده" (It was only envy that led the son of Adam to kill his brother), the restrictive particle إنما confines the cause of the first murder to envy alone, isolating it as the sole efficient cause of that primordial transgression.

4:54.arabic: الإنكار {أم يحسدون الناس على ما آتاهم الله من فضله} وقال تعالى {كان الناس أمة واحدة} إلى قوله {إلا الذين أوتوه من بعد ما جاءتهم البينات بغيا بينهم} قيل في التفسير حسدا وقال تعالى {وما تفرقوا إلا من بعد ما جاءهم العلم بغيا بينهم} فأنزل الله العلم ليجمعهم ويؤلف بينهم على طاعته وأمرهم أن يتألفوا بالعلم فتحاسدوا واختلفوا إذ أراد كل واحد منهم أن ينفرد بالرياسة وقبول القول فرد بعضهم على بعض قال ابن عباس كانت اليهود قبل أن يبعث النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا قاتلوا قوما قالوا نسألك بالنبي الذي وعدتنا أن ت
4:54.english: The Prophet ﷺ said: «إن المؤمن يغبط والمنافق يحسد» — "The believer aspires emulously, and the hypocrite envies."
4:54.section_title_en: On the Reality of Envy (Ḥasad) and Its Degrees — Section 720
4:54.anchors:
- Root: نعم (n-ʿ-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root meaning of "bounty, benefaction, grace" — that state of goodness and well-being bestowed.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "النعمة: الحالة الحسنة" — bounty is the excellent state/condition; it is the genus term applying to both little and much, as in {«وإن تعدوا نعمة الله لا تحصوها»} [Ibrahim: 34].
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): "جلت نعمة الله ونعماؤه" — bounty as actual bestowed good. Metaphorical (majāz): "خفت نعامتهم" — departure/removal, relevant to the envier's wish for the bounty's removal.
- Root: حسد (ḥ-s-d)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Envy — the desire for removal of another's good.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الحسد: تمني زوال نعمة من مستحق لها" — envy is wishing the removal of bounty from one who deserves it, sometimes accompanied by striving to effect its removal. Cited: «المؤمن يغبط والمنافق يحسد».
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "حسده على نعمة الله" — envying someone for God's bounty. "إن الحسد يأكل الجسد" — envy consumes the body.
- Root: نفس (n-f-s)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The self; also value, preciousness.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): النفس: الروح — the soul/spirit; also الذات (essence/self).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "شيء نفيس ومنفس" — a precious thing. Metaphorical: "دفق نفسه أي دمه" — poured out his self, i.e., his blood. From this root derives المنافسة (emulative competition) — the striving for precious things.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد (Restriction & Specification) — The definition of ḥasad is given as a restricted predication (ḥadd), delimiting its essential meaning: "كراهة النعمة وحب زوالها عن المنعم عليه" — the hatred of bounty and love of its removal from the one upon whom it is bestowed. This is a formal definition (ḥadd), not merely a lexical gloss.
4:54.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'Condemnation of Envy'

4:89.arabic: حسد وقال عز وجل {ودوا لو تكفرون كما كفروا فتكونون سواء} وذكر الله تعالى حسد إخوة يوسف عليه السلام وعبر عما في قلوبهم بقوله تعالى {إذ قالوا ليوسف وأخوه أحب إلى أبينا منا ونحن عصبة إن أبانا لفي ضلال مبين اقتلوا يوسف أو اطرحوه أرضا يخل لكم وجه أبيكم} فلما كرهوا حب أبيهم له وساءهم ذلك وأحبوا زواله عنه غيبوه عنه وقال تعالى {ولا يجدون في صدورهم حاجة مما أوتوا} أي لا تضيق صدورهم به ولا يغتمون فأثنى عليهم بعدم الحسد وقال تعالى في معرض الإنكار {أم يحسدون الناس على ما آتاهم الله من فضله} وقال تعالى {كان الناس أمة
4:89.english: The Prophet ﷺ said: «إن المؤمن يغبط والمنافق يحسد» — "The believer aspires emulously, and the hypocrite envies."
4:89.section_title_en: On the Reality of Envy (Ḥasad) and Its Degrees — Section 720

4:129.arabic: قال تعالى {ولن تستطيعوا أن تعدلوا بين النساء ولو حرصتم فلا تميلوا كل الميل فتذروها كالمعلقة} فليس كل من عجز عن الإتيان بالخير كله ينبغي أن يأتي بالشر كله ولكن بعض الشر أهون من بعض وبعض الخير أرفع من بعض فهذه حقيقة الغضب ودرجاته نسأله الله حسن التوفيق لما يرضيه إنه على ما يشاء قدير
4:129.english: As for deficiency: it is the loss of this power or its weakness. This is blameworthy, and it is of such a one that it is said: "He has no protective zeal (ḥamiyyah)." For this reason al-Shāfiʿī — may God have mercy on him — said: "Whoever is provoked to anger and does not become angry is a donkey." Whoever loses the power of anger and protective zeal entirely is utterly deficient. God — exalted be He — described the Companions of the Prophet — peace be upon him — with severity and protective zeal, saying: {«أشداء على الكفار رحماء بينهم»} "Severe against the disbelievers, merciful among themselves" (Q 48:29). And He said to His Prophet — peace be upon him: {«جاهد الكفار والمنافقين واغلظ عليهم»} "Strive against the disbelievers and the hypocrites and be harsh with them" (Q 9:73) — the verse. Harshness and severity are but effects of the power of protective zeal, which is anger.
4:129.section_title_en: The Reality of Anger (Ghaḍab) and Its Degrees — Book 21, Section 703
4:129.anchors:
- Root: غضب (Ghaḍab)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root denotes anger, rage, fury; the surge of blood in the heart seeking vengeance.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الغضب: ثوران دم القلب إرادة الانتقام" — when attributed to God, it means solely His retribution, not an emotional state.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): "غضبت لفلان" (anger for the living); Metaphorical (majāz): "غضبت به" (anger over the dead), and the poetic extension to inanimate objects like fire or reins.
- Root: نفس (Nafs)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Self, soul, spirit; the vital principle.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The soul as the seat of blameworthy traits when unrestrained; its purification is the goal of spiritual struggle.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the self; Metaphorical: "دفق نفسه" (spilled his blood/life).
- Root: قلب (Qalb)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The heart; to turn over, to flip.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "قلب الشيء: تصريفه وصرفه عن وجه إلى وجه" — the heart is so named for its constant fluctuation and turning.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical turning; Metaphorical: the heart as the seat of intellect and spiritual perception, which anger overturns and blinds.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد (Restriction & Focused Predication) — Used to distinguish the three degrees of anger (deficiency, excess, moderation) as mutually exclusive categories.
4:129.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'Condemnation of Envy'

4:129.arabic: قال الله تعالى {ولن تستطيعوا أن تعدلوا بين النساء ولو حرصتم} أي أن تعدلوا في شهوة القلب وميل النفس ويتبع ذلك التفاوت في الوقاع وكان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يعدل بينهن في العطاء والبيتوتة في الليالي ويقول اللهم هذا جهدي فيما أملك ولا طاقة لي فيما تملك ولا أملك (3) يعني الحب وقد كانت عائشة رضي الله عنها أحب نسائه إليه (4) وسائر نسائه يعرفن ذلك وكان يطاف به محمولا في مرضه في كل يوم وكل ليلة فيبيت عند كل واحدة منهن ويقول أين أنا غدا ففطنت لذلك امرأة منهن فقالت إنما يسأل عن يوم عائشة فقلن يا رسول الله قد
4:129.english: I say: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, has said: «من كان له امرأتان فمال إلى إحداهما دون الأخرى» — "Whoever has two wives and inclines toward one of them to the exclusion of the other" — and in another wording: «ولم يعدل بينهما جاء يوم القيامة وأحد شقيه مائل» — "and does not act equitably between them, he shall come on the Day of Resurrection with one of his sides leaning."
4:129.section_title_en: The Revival of the Religious Sciences — Book on the Etiquette of Marriage: Section 305 (On Justice Between Co-Wives, Nushuz, and the Etiquette of Intercourse)
4:129.anchors:
- Root: عدل (ʿadl)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning is "to be equal, to balance, to straighten" — the root denotes equity and even-handedness in distribution.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In theological usage, ʿadl is the mean of justice, opposed to jawr (tyranny) — it is the act of placing things in their proper stations.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah) usage pertains to measurable distribution (ʿatāʾ, mabīt); metaphorical (Majāz) usage extends to that which is not under voluntary control, such as love (maḥabbah) and inclination of the heart.
- Root: نشز (nushūz)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The root denotes "rising up" or "elevation"; in marital context it signifies a rising of one spouse against the other in discord or recalcitrance.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Nushūz is the rebellion of one spouse against the bond of obedience and harmony, a moral elevation against the other.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal usage is the physical rising from a place; metaphorical usage is the spiritual/moral rising in defiance.
- Root: وقع (waqʿ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The root denotes "falling" or "occurrence"; in the marital context, it is a euphemism for sexual intercourse.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The term is used in the Quran for the "falling" of an event; here it is a euphemistic transfer (naql) for coitus.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal usage is physical falling; metaphorical usage is the act of intercourse, as in the hadith "لا يقعن أحدكم على امرأته" (Let none of you fall upon his wife like a beast).
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — The particle innamā restricts the predicate to the subject alone, as in the hadith "إنما عليه العدل في العطاء والمبيت" (Upon him is only justice in expenditure and overnight stays), confining the obligation to what is within human capacity.
4:129.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Etiquette of Marriage'

6:53.arabic: قول قريش أهؤلاء من الله عليهم من بيننا كالاستحقار لهم والأنفة منهم السبب الرابع التعجب كما أخبر الله تعالى عن الأمم السالفة إذ قالوا ما أنتم إلا بشر مثلنا وقالوا أنؤمن لبشرين مثلنا ولئن أطعتم بشرا مثلكم إنكم إذا لخاسرون فتعجبوا من أن يفوز برتبة الرسالة والوحي والقرب من الله تعالى بشر مثلهم فحسدوهم وأحبوا زوال النبوة عنهم جزعا أن يفضل عليهم من هو مثلهم في الخلقة لا عن قصد تكبر وطلب رياسة وتقدم عداوة أو سبب آخر من سائر الأسباب وقالوا متعجبين أبعث الله بشرا رسولا {وقالوا} لولا أنزل علينا ا
6:53.english: I say: God is Knower of what is in the breasts. {«إِنْ تَمْسَسْكُمْ حَسَنَةٌ تَسُؤْهُمْ»} — "If good touches you, it grieves them" {«وَدُّوا مَا عَنِتُّمْ قَدْ بَدَتِ الْبَغْضَاءُ مِنْ أَفْوَاهِهِمْ وَمَا تُخْفِي صُدُورُهُمْ أَكْبَرُ»} — "They wish for your hardship; hatred has already appeared from their mouths, and what their breasts conceal is greater." And envy (ḥasad), arising from hatred, may lead to contention, mutual fighting, and the spending of one's entire life in removing another's blessing through stratagems, slander, the tearing of veils, and whatever runs in that course.
6:53.section_title_en: The Revival of the Religious Sciences — Book on the Rebuke of the Self: The Seven Causes of Envy (Section 722)
6:53.anchors:
- Root: سبب (sabab)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The rope by which one climbs; every means by which one reaches a thing.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Every means by which one arrives at something is called a sabab" — thus the causes enumerated here are the psychological "ropes" by which envy ascends in the soul.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: a physical cord. Metaphorical: any linkage or occasion — here, the inward occasions (asbāb) that give rise to ḥasad.
- Root: بغض (bughḍ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Hatred, aversion of the heart.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The opposite of love (maḥabbah); a disposition of the heart toward another's harm.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: inner aversion. Metaphorical: its "appearance from the mouths" (Quranic) as outward speech betraying the concealed hatred.
- Root: كبر (kibr)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Greatness; pride; disdain.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Al-kabīr and al-ṣaghīr are relative terms" — pride is the claim to greatness relative to another, deeming oneself above him.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: bigness in stature or age. Metaphorical: "takabbara 'alayhi" — to deem oneself greater than another and refuse submission to him.
- Root: قصد (qaṣd)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Straightness of path; intending a goal.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Al-qaṣd: istiqāmat al-ṭarīq" — the straight road; also moderation between extremes.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: to head toward a place. Metaphorical: "maqāṣid" — the aims and objectives toward which one directs oneself; here, the worldly goals whose pursuit breeds rivalry and envy.

  * Lisan / Ayn: To descend from a height; to alight.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Al-nuzūl fī al-aṣl huwa inḥiṭāṭ min 'uluww" — descent from above; the sending down of revelation.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: descending from a high place. Metaphorical: "anzala Allāhu al-kitāb" — God's sending down of the Quran; and "mā unzila" — what was revealed, as in the Quranic citation regarding the Qurashites' objection to revelation upon a mere human.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Causal Coordination (al-'aṭf al-sababī) — The enumeration of the seven causes proceeds by coordinated clauses (fa-... thumma ...), each introduced as an independent proposition linked by causation (sabab), requiring the translator to preserve the logical sequence of psychological motivations without collapsing them into one another.

6:53.arabic: تعالى {ليقولوا أهؤلاء من الله عليهم من بيننا} أي استحقارا لهم واستبعادا لتقدمهم وقالت قريش لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كيف نجلس إليك وعندك هؤلاء وأشاروا إلى فقراء المسلمين فازدروهم بأعينهم لفقرهم وتكبروا عن مجالستهم فأنزل الله تعالى {ولا تطرد الذين يدعون ربهم بالغداة والعشي} إلى قوله {ما عليك من حسابهم} وقال تعالى {واصبر نفسك مع الذين يدعون ربهم بالغداة والعشي يريدون وجهه ولا تعد عيناك عنهم تريد زينة الحياة الدنيا} // حديث قالت قريش لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كيف نجلس إليك وعندك هؤلاء الحد
6:53.english: Know that the one against whom pride is directed is either God—mighty and majestic—or His messengers, or the rest of His creation. Man has been created unjust and ignorant {«وخلق الإنسان ظلوما جهولا»}, so at times he grows proud against the creation, and at times he grows proud against the Creator. Thus, pride, considered with respect to the one against whom it is directed, falls into three divisions.
6:53.section_title_en: Exposition of the One Against Whom Pride Is Directed, Its Degrees, Its Divisions, and the Fruits of Pride Within It
6:53.anchors:
- Root: كبر (k-b-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root denotes magnitude, whether physical size, age, or rank; "الكبرة" specifically marks the state of advanced age or an ingrained, chronic condition.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الكبير والصغير من الأسماء المتضايفة" — bigness and smallness are relative terms. In the theological context, pride (الكبر) is the soul's self-magnification against another, a relational vice that distorts the creature's standing before the Creator.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah) usage concerns physical or quantitative magnitude. Metaphorical (Majaz) usage transfers this to moral and spiritual stature, as in "كبر علي ذلك" (it weighed heavily upon him) — here, the soul's swelling against divine command is a metaphorical arrogation of greatness.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Prepositional Interposition (باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور) — Governing the syntactic tension between the agent of pride (المتكبر) and its object (المتكبر عليه), where the preposition "على" carries the full weight of opposition and elevation, structuring the periodic sentences that follow.
6:53.topic: Al-Ghazali on purifying the character, moral diseases, and spiritual remedies, from 'Condemnation of Pride and Conceit'

6:164.arabic: وحسناته فإنه من كسبه وغير مؤاخذ بسيئاته فإنه لا تزر وازرة وزر أخرى ولذلك قال تعالى ألحقنا بهم ذرياتهم وما ألتناهم من عملهم من شيء أي ما نقصناهم من أعمالهم وجعلنا أولادهم مزيدا في إحسانهم الوجه الرابع أن يموت الولد قبله فيكون له شفيعا فقد روي عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال إن الطفل يجر بأبويه إلى الجنة (5) وفي بعض الأخبار يأخذ بثوبه كما أنا الآن آخذ بثوبك (6) وقال أيضا صلى الله عليه وسلم إن المولود يقال ادخل الجنة فيقف على باب الجنة فيظل محبنطئا أي ممتلئا غيظا وغضبا ويقول لا أدخل الجنة إلا وأبواي معي فيقال أدخلوا
6:164.english: وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم: "لا يلقى الله أحد بذنب أعظم من جهالة أهله."
6:164.topic: Al-Ghazali on the journey of the soul, death, and the Hereafter, from 'Condemnation of Envy'

7:95.arabic: عليه شيء مما يسرون وما يعلنون وحذرهم أن يأخذهم بغتة وهم لا يشعرون فقال {ما ينظرون إلا صيحة واحدة تأخذهم وهم يخصمون فلا يستطيعون توصية ولا إلى أهلهم يرجعون} والصلاة والسلام على محمد رسوله الذي يسير تحت لوائه النبيون وعلى آله وأصحابه الأئمة المهديين والسادة المرضيين صلاة يوازي عددها عدد ما كان من خلق الله وما سيكون ويحظى ببركتها الأولون والآخرون وسلم تسليما كثيرا أما بعد فإن الغضب شعلة نار اقتبست من نار الله الموقدة التي تطلع على الأفئدة وإنها لمستكنة في طي الفؤاد استكنان الجمر تحت الرماد ويستخرجه الكبر الدفي
7:95.english: In the name of God, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate. Praise be to God, upon whose pardon and mercy none rely except the hopeful, and from whose evil wrath and assault none fear except the fearful — He who gradually seizes His servants from whence they know not, and who has given dominion over them to their lusts, commanding them to abandon what they desire, and who has tried them with anger while charging them to swallow their rage in what provokes them. Then He surrounded them with hardships and pleasures, and granted them respite to see how they would act. He tested their love through them, to make known the truth of what they claim. He made known to them that nothing is hidden from Him of what they conceal or proclaim, and warned them lest He seize them suddenly while they are unaware. For He said: {«They await but a single blast which will seize them while they are disputing; so they will not be able to make a bequest, nor to their families will they return»} (Q. 36:49-50). And prayers and peace be upon Muhammad, His Messenger, beneath whose banner the prophets walk, and upon his family and companions — the rightly-guided imams and the pleasing masters — prayers whose number equals the number of what has been of God's creation and what will be, and by whose blessing the first and the last are favored — and abundant peace.
7:95.section_title_en: The Book of Condemnation of Anger, Spite, and Envy — Book Five of the Quarter of Destroyers from The Revival of the Religious Sciences
7:95.anchors:
- Root: غضب (ghadab)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root meaning of anger, rage, fury; the boiling and agitation of the blood
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance — when attributed to God, it means retribution (intiqām) alone, not emotional agitation; the Prophet described it as "a live coal kindled in the heart of the son of Adam"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal vs Metaphorical — literal anger is the boiling of the blood in living beings; metaphorical usage extends to inanimate things like fire and the reins of a mount
- Root: قلب (qalb)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The heart; also the turning, overturning, and transformation of a thing from one state to another
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance — the heart is so named for its constant turning (taqallub) and fluctuation between states; it is the seat of understanding and the locus of divine address
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal vs Metaphorical — literal is the physical organ; metaphorical is the subtle spiritual reality (laṭīfah rabbāniyyah) that is the locus of knowledge and will
- Root: حسد (hasad)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Envy; the wishing for removal of another's blessing
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance — envy is the desire for the removal of a blessing from one who deserves it, sometimes accompanied by striving to remove it; the believer envies (ghibṭah) while the hypocrite envies (hasad)
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal vs Metaphorical — "Envy consumes the body as fire consumes wood"; the envier is one who wishes evil upon the blessed
- Root: هلك (halak)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Perdition, destruction, ruin; death
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance — three senses: (1) loss of a thing from one's possession while it exists elsewhere, (2) corruption and dissolution of a thing, (3) death; the Quran uses it for all three
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal vs Metaphorical — literal is physical destruction; metaphorical is the ruin of one's religion and afterlife through spiritual corruption
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The permissibility of interposing elements between a preposition and its object when the intervening material constitutes a complete, meaningful unit, as in the Quranic pattern of extended periodic sentences that delay resolution for rhetorical effect.
7:95.topic: Al-Ghazali on purifying the character, moral diseases, and spiritual remedies, from 'Condemnation of Envy'

9:73.arabic: وقال لنبيه صلى الله عليه وسلم {جاهد الكفار والمنافقين واغلظ عليهم} الآية وإنما الغلظة والشدة من آثار قوة الحمية وهو الغضب وأما الإفراط فهو أن تغلب هذه الصفة حتى تخرج عن سياسة العقل والدين وطاعته ولا يبقى للمرء معها بصيرة ونظر وفكرة ولا اختيار بل يصير في صورة المضطر وسبب غلبته أمور غريزية وأمور اعتيادية فرب إنسان هو بالفطرة مستعد لسرعة الغضب حتى كأن صورته في الفطرة صورة غضبان ويعين على ذلك حرارة مزاج القلب لأن الغضب من النار (1) كما قال صلى الله عليه وسلم وإنما برودة المزاج تطفئه وتكسر سورته وأما الأسباب الاعتياد
9:73.english: As for deficiency: it is the loss of this power or its weakness. This is blameworthy, and it is of such a one that it is said: "He has no protective zeal (ḥamiyyah)." For this reason al-Shāfiʿī — may God have mercy on him — said: "Whoever is provoked to anger and does not become angry is a donkey." Whoever loses the power of anger and protective zeal entirely is utterly deficient. God — exalted be He — described the Companions of the Prophet — peace be upon him — with severity and protective zeal, saying: {«أشداء على الكفار رحماء بينهم»} "Severe against the disbelievers, merciful among themselves" (Q 48:29). And He said to His Prophet — peace be upon him: {«جاهد الكفار والمنافقين واغلظ عليهم»} "Strive against the disbelievers and the hypocrites and be harsh with them" (Q 9:73) — the verse. Harshness and severity are but effects of the power of protective zeal, which is anger.
9:73.section_title_en: The Reality of Anger (Ghaḍab) and Its Degrees — Book 21, Section 703
9:73.anchors:
- Root: غضب (Ghaḍab)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root denotes anger, rage, fury; the surge of blood in the heart seeking vengeance.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الغضب: ثوران دم القلب إرادة الانتقام" — when attributed to God, it means solely His retribution, not an emotional state.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): "غضبت لفلان" (anger for the living); Metaphorical (majāz): "غضبت به" (anger over the dead), and the poetic extension to inanimate objects like fire or reins.
- Root: نفس (Nafs)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Self, soul, spirit; the vital principle.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The soul as the seat of blameworthy traits when unrestrained; its purification is the goal of spiritual struggle.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the self; Metaphorical: "دفق نفسه" (spilled his blood/life).
- Root: قلب (Qalb)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The heart; to turn over, to flip.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "قلب الشيء: تصريفه وصرفه عن وجه إلى وجه" — the heart is so named for its constant fluctuation and turning.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical turning; Metaphorical: the heart as the seat of intellect and spiritual perception, which anger overturns and blinds.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد (Restriction & Focused Predication) — Used to distinguish the three degrees of anger (deficiency, excess, moderation) as mutually exclusive categories.
9:73.topic: Al-Ghazali on purifying the character, moral diseases, and spiritual remedies, from 'Condemnation of Envy'

12:92.arabic: عليه وسلم أقول كما قال يوسف {لا تثريب عليكم اليوم يغفر الله لكم وهو أرحم} {الراحمين} (1) قال فخرجوا كأنما نشروا من القبور فدخلوا في الإسلام وعن سهيل بن عمرو قال لما قدم رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم مكة وضع يديه على باب الكعبة والناس حوله فقال لا إله إلا الله وحده لا شريك له صدق وعده ونصر عبده وهزم الأحزاب وحده {ثم قال} يا معشر قريش ما تقولون وما تظنون قال قلت يا رسول الله نقول خيرا ونظن خيرا أخ كريم وابن عم رحيم وقد قدرت فقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أقول كما قال أخي يوسف {لا تثريب عليكم اليوم يغفر الله لكم}
12:92.english: Know that the Prophet (peace be upon him) said, as related by Anas (may God be pleased with him) in a tradition transmitted by Abū Ṣāliḥ al-Ḥanafī as a suspended (mursal) report: "When God—mighty and majestic—gathers the creatures on the Day of Resurrection, a herald will call out from beneath the Throne with three calls: 'O company of monotheists! Verily God has pardoned you, so let some of you pardon others.'" This was transmitted by Abū Saʿīd Aḥmad ibn Ibrāhīm al-Muqrī in his book *al-Tabṣirah wa al-Tadhkirah* with the wording: "A herald will call out from the innermost depths of the Throne on the Day of Resurrection: 'O community of Muḥammad! Verily God Most High says: Whatever was due to Me from you, I have bestowed it upon you as a gift. But the claims of one another remain—so forgive one another mutually, and enter Paradise through My mercy.'" Its chain of transmission is weak. Al-Ṭabarānī related it in *al-Awsaṭ* with the wording: "A herald will call out: 'O people of the Gathering! Mutually acknowledge the wrongs among yourselves, and your reward is upon Me.'" And he related from the ḥadīth of Umm Hāniʾ: "A herald will call out: 'O people of monotheism! Let some of you pardon others, and the reward is upon Me.'"
12:92.section_title_en: The Book of Pardon (Kitāb al-ʿAfw) — Section 714
12:92.anchors:
- Root: ع ف و (ʿ-f-w)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "عفا: ترك الذنب وأعرض عنه؛ والعفو: التجاوز عن الذنب، وأصله المحو والطمس"
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "العفو: التجافي عن الذنب، وهو أبلغ من الغفران لأنه يقتضي ترك المؤاخذة مع زوال أثر الذنب"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "Literal: عفا عن ذنبه: تجاوز عنه. Metaphorical: عفا الأثر: درَس وامّحى — فالعفو محو الذنب كأنه لم يكن"
- Root: ث ل ب (th-l-b) — as in "لا تثريب"
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الثرب: الشحم الرقيق الذي يغشى الكرش؛ والتثريب: التعيير والتوبيخ على الذنب"
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "التثريب: أشد اللوم والتعنيف، ومنه قوله تعالى {لا تثريب عليكم اليوم} أي لا تعيير ولا توبيخ"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "Literal: ثرّبه: وبّخه وعيّره. Metaphorical: لا تثريب: إزالة أثر الذنب بالكلية كإزالة الشحم الرقيق"
- Root: م ظ ل م (ẓ-l-m)
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "المظلمة: حق الغير الذي ظُلم صاحبه فيه، وجمعها مظالم"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "Literal: ظلمه: نقصه حقه. Metaphorical: المظالم: الحقوق التي غُصبت، وتناكُر المظالم: معرفة كل واحد مظلمته ليتحلل منها"
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The permissibility of interposing elements between the preposition and its object when the meaning remains clear, as in "من تحت العرش" where the spatial specification follows the prepositional phrase.
12:92.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications, prayers, and their spiritual power, from 'Condemnation of Envy'

12:92.arabic: لا تثريب عليكم اليوم يغفر الله لكم وهو أرحم الراحمين يعرض للحكم بالعفو عن أصحابه قال الحكم فأنا أقول لا تثريب عليكم اليوم ولو لم أجد إلا ثوبي هذا لواريتكم تحته وكتب ابن المقفع إلى صديق له يسأله العفو عن بعض إخوانه فلان هارب من زلته إلى عفوك لائذ منك بك واعلم أنه لن يزداد الذنب عظما إلا ازداد العفو فضلا وأتى عبد الملك بن مروان بأسارى ابن الأشعث فقال لرجاء بن حيوة ما ترى قال إن الله تعالى قد أعطاك ما تحب من الظفر فأعط الله ما يحب من العفو فعفا عنهم وروي أن زياد أخذ رجلا من الخوارج فأفلت منه فأخذ أخا له فقال ل
12:92.english: A man was brought to Hishām concerning whom word had reached him. When he was made to stand before him, he began to speak in his own defense. Hishām said to him: You speak as well? The man said: O Commander of the Faithful, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: {«يَوْمَ تَأْتِي كُلُّ نَفْسٍ تُجَادِلُ عَنْ نَفْسِهَا»} — "The Day when every soul will come disputing on its own behalf." Shall we dispute before Allah the Exalted, and not speak a word before you? Hishām said: Yes, woe to you — speak.
12:92.section_title_en: ** Section 715 — On the Virtue of Forbearance (al-Ḥilm) and Gentleness (al-Rifq)
12:92.anchors:
**

- **Root: عفو (ʿ-F-W)**
  - *Lisan / Ayn:* Al-ʿAfw is the effacing and obliteration of the trace of a thing; to pardon is to efface the trace of the offense entirely.
  - *Al-Raghib (Mufradat):* Al-ʿAfw is the erasure of the sin such that no consequence remains — it is the highest form of forgiveness, surpassing al-ghufrān which veils but does not necessarily efface.
  - *Al-Zamakhshari (Asas):* Literal: "عفا الأثر" — the trace was effaced. Metaphorical: pardon as the effacing of the offense's consequence, as in "عفا عن ذنبه."

- **Root: حلم (Ḥ-L-M)**
  - *Lisan / Ayn:* Al-Ḥilm is forbearance, clemency, and the restraint of the soul from agitation upon provocation.
  - *Al-Raghib (Mufradat):* Al-Ḥilm is the soul's composure and its withholding from haste; it is a virtue opposed to al-ṭaysh (levity) and al-jahl (foolishness) — not ignorance, but the deliberate restraint of passion.
  - *Al-Zamakhshari (Asas):* Literal: dreams (aḥlām) share the root — the state of being unmoved. Metaphorical: the forbearing man (ḥalīm) whose soul does not stir toward vengeance when provoked.

- **Root: رفق (R-F-Q)**
  - *Lisan / Ayn:* Al-Rifq is gentleness, lenity, and the opposite of violence (al-ʿunf).
  - *Al-Raghib (Mufradat):* Al-Rifq is the disposition toward ease and gentleness in all affairs; it is praised by the Law and is a quality of the prophets.
  - *Al-Zamakhshari (Asas):* Literal: "رفق به" — he was gentle with him. Metaphorical: gentleness in conduct as a mode of spiritual excellence.

- **Root: صفح (Ṣ-F-Ḥ)**
  - *Lisan / Ayn:* Al-Ṣafḥ is turning away from an offense and meeting it with a generous countenance; from ṣafḥah (cheek/face) — to turn one's face away from the wrong.
  - *Al-Raghib (Mufradat):* Al-Ṣafḥ is the overlooking of the offense combined with graciousness — it is more than mere pardon, for it includes magnanimity (al-Ifḍāl).
  - *Al-Zamakhshari (Asas):* Literal: "صفح عنه" — he turned his face away from him. Metaphorical: to turn away from requital and instead bestow favor.

- **Sibawayh Rule:** *Bāb al-Ḥaṣr wa al-Taqyīd bi-innamā* (Restriction & Focused Predication) — "إنما أعطى ما أعطى بأربع خصال" employs innamā to restrict the cause of the gift to four qualities, and "ليس الحليم من ظلم فحلم حتى إذا قدر انتقم" uses laysa to negate the predicate entirely before affirming the true definition.

---
