12:92.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Condemnation of Envy'

12:107.arabic: عليه شيء مما يسرون وما يعلنون وحذرهم أن يأخذهم بغتة وهم لا يشعرون فقال {ما ينظرون إلا صيحة واحدة تأخذهم وهم يخصمون فلا يستطيعون توصية ولا إلى أهلهم يرجعون} والصلاة والسلام على محمد رسوله الذي يسير تحت لوائه النبيون وعلى آله وأصحابه الأئمة المهديين والسادة المرضيين صلاة يوازي عددها عدد ما كان من خلق الله وما سيكون ويحظى ببركتها الأولون والآخرون وسلم تسليما كثيرا أما بعد فإن الغضب شعلة نار اقتبست من نار الله الموقدة التي تطلع على الأفئدة وإنها لمستكنة في طي الفؤاد استكنان الجمر تحت الرماد ويستخرجه الكبر الدفي
12:107.english: In the name of God, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate. Praise be to God, upon whose pardon and mercy none rely except the hopeful, and from whose evil wrath and assault none fear except the fearful — He who gradually seizes His servants from whence they know not, and who has given dominion over them to their lusts, commanding them to abandon what they desire, and who has tried them with anger while charging them to swallow their rage in what provokes them. Then He surrounded them with hardships and pleasures, and granted them respite to see how they would act. He tested their love through them, to make known the truth of what they claim. He made known to them that nothing is hidden from Him of what they conceal or proclaim, and warned them lest He seize them suddenly while they are unaware. For He said: {«They await but a single blast which will seize them while they are disputing; so they will not be able to make a bequest, nor to their families will they return»} (Q. 36:49-50). And prayers and peace be upon Muhammad, His Messenger, beneath whose banner the prophets walk, and upon his family and companions — the rightly-guided imams and the pleasing masters — prayers whose number equals the number of what has been of God's creation and what will be, and by whose blessing the first and the last are favored — and abundant peace.
12:107.section_title_en: The Book of Condemnation of Anger, Spite, and Envy — Book Five of the Quarter of Destroyers from The Revival of the Religious Sciences
12:107.anchors:
- Root: غضب (ghadab)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root meaning of anger, rage, fury; the boiling and agitation of the blood
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance — when attributed to God, it means retribution (intiqām) alone, not emotional agitation; the Prophet described it as "a live coal kindled in the heart of the son of Adam"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal vs Metaphorical — literal anger is the boiling of the blood in living beings; metaphorical usage extends to inanimate things like fire and the reins of a mount
- Root: قلب (qalb)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The heart; also the turning, overturning, and transformation of a thing from one state to another
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance — the heart is so named for its constant turning (taqallub) and fluctuation between states; it is the seat of understanding and the locus of divine address
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal vs Metaphorical — literal is the physical organ; metaphorical is the subtle spiritual reality (laṭīfah rabbāniyyah) that is the locus of knowledge and will
- Root: حسد (hasad)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Envy; the wishing for removal of another's blessing
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance — envy is the desire for the removal of a blessing from one who deserves it, sometimes accompanied by striving to remove it; the believer envies (ghibṭah) while the hypocrite envies (hasad)
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal vs Metaphorical — "Envy consumes the body as fire consumes wood"; the envier is one who wishes evil upon the blessed
- Root: هلك (halak)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Perdition, destruction, ruin; death
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance — three senses: (1) loss of a thing from one's possession while it exists elsewhere, (2) corruption and dissolution of a thing, (3) death; the Quran uses it for all three
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal vs Metaphorical — literal is physical destruction; metaphorical is the ruin of one's religion and afterlife through spiritual corruption
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The permissibility of interposing elements between a preposition and its object when the intervening material constitutes a complete, meaningful unit, as in the Quranic pattern of extended periodic sentences that delay resolution for rhetorical effect.
12:107.topic: Al-Ghazali on purifying the character, moral diseases, and spiritual remedies, from 'Condemnation of Envy'

13:8.arabic: غير معلوم قدره الله سبحانه فلا حيلة في دفعه بل كل شيء عنده بمقدار ولكل أجل كتاب ولذلك شكا نبي من الأنبياء من امرأة ظالمة مستولية على الخلق فأوحى الله إليه فر من قدامها حتى تنقضي أيامها أي ما قدرناه في الأزل لا سبيل إلى تغييره فاصبر حتى تنقضي المدة التي سبق القضاء بدوام إقبالها فيها ومهما
13:8.english: As for its being a harm upon the envied one in his religion and his worldly life — it is clear that the blessing does not depart from him through your envy. Rather, whatever Allah — exalted be He — has decreed of prosperity and blessing, it must endure until an appointed term unknown to us, which Allah — glorified be He — has measured. There is no stratagem to repel it, for everything with Him is by measure (miqdār), and for every term there is a book (kitāb). {«لكل أجل كتاب»} "For every term there is a decree."
13:8.section_title_en: The Remedy That Expels the Disease of Envy from the Heart — Section 725
13:8.anchors:
- Root: حسد (ḥ-s-d)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning — wishing for removal of a blessing from its possessor; the root also carries the sense of "grudging malice" that consumes the envier himself.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الحسد: تمني زوال نعمة من مستحق لها" — Envy is the wish for the removal of a blessing from one who deserves it, sometimes accompanied by striving to effect its removal. The believer envies not but rather admires (ghibṭah); the hypocrite envies.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) — envy is directed at another's blessing; metaphorically (majāz), envy "eats the body" as fire eats wood, indicating its self-destructive spiritual physiology.
- Root: قلب (q-l-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The heart as that which is ever-turning, overturning, and fluctuating between states.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "قلب الشيء: تصريفه وصرفه عن وجه إلى وجه" — To turn a thing from one face to another; the heart's diseases are its deviations from its original sound disposition (fiṭrah).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — turning a thing over; metaphorical — "رجل قلب" (a man who turns matters over) i.e., one who examines affairs with penetrating insight, as the physician of hearts must do.
- Root: نعم (n-ʿ-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Blessing, well-being, graciousness; the state of being in a condition of good.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "النعمة: الحالة الحسنة" — Blessing is the good state; it is a genus term applying to both little and much. Divine blessings are distributed by divine decree (qadar), and envy is resentment against that distribution.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — the act of bestowing; metaphorical — "خفت نعامتهم" (their ostriches departed) i.e., their blessings vanished, illustrating that blessings flee from the envier while remaining with the envied.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The periodic sentence structure here employs extended conditional and causal chains (law-lā, fa-in, fa-innaka) where the apodosis is delayed by embedded justificatory clauses, requiring the translator to preserve the logical subordination without collapsing the rhetorical tension.
13:8.topic: Al-Ghazali on purifying the character, moral diseases, and spiritual remedies, from 'Condemnation of Envy'

15:47.arabic: فيهم رب العالمين ونزعنا ما في صدورهم من غل إخوانا على سرر متقابلين فهذا حالهم وهم بعد في الدنيا فماذا يظن بهم عند انكشاف الغطاء ومشاهدة المحبوب في العقبى فإذن لا يتصور أن يكون في الجنة محاسدة ولا أن يكون بين أهل الدنيا في الجنة محاسدة لأن الجنة لا مضايقة فيها ولا مزاحمة ولا تنال إلا بمعرفة الله تعالى التي لا مزاحمة فيها في الدنيا أيضا فأهل الجنة بالضرورة برءاء من الحسد في الدنيا والآخرة جميعا بل الحسد من صفات المبعدين عن سعة عليين إلى مضيق سجين ولذلك وسم به الشيطان اللعين وذكر من صفاته أنه حسد آدم عليه السلام على م
15:47.english: The cobbler — nay, rather the cloth-merchant — and then the jostling of the cloth-merchant against his immediate neighbor is greater than his jostling against one farther from him toward the end of the market. Unavoidably, therefore, his envy of his neighbor is greater. Likewise, the brave man envies the brave man and does not envy the scholar, because his aim is to be mentioned for bravery, to become famous for it, and to be uniquely distinguished by this trait — and the scholar does not compete with him for this purpose. Similarly, the scholar envies the scholar and does not envy the brave man. Then the envy of the preacher for the preacher is greater than his envy for the jurist or the physician, because the competition between them is over a single, more specific aim. So the root of all these envies is enmity, and the root of enmity is the competition between two parties over a single purpose. And a single purpose does not unite two distant parties but rather two proportionate ones; therefore envy abounds between them. Yes — whoever's craving for prestige intensifies, and who loves fame throughout all the regions of the world in that which he pursues, he will envy everyone in the world, however distant, who shares with him in the trait by which he boasts. And the origin of all of that is love of this world, for it is only this world that straitens the competitors. As for the Hereafter, there is no constriction in it. The likeness of the Hereafter is the blessing of knowledge. Unavoidably, therefore, whoever loves knowledge of Allah Most High, and knowledge of His attributes, His angels, His prophets, and the dominion (malakūt) of His heavens and His earth, does not envy another when he too comes to know that — because knowledge does not straiten the knowers. Rather, the single known object is learned by a thousand thousand knowers, and each rejoices in knowing it and takes delight in it, and the delight of one is not diminished by another. Rather, through the multiplicity of knowers there accrues an increase of intimacy and the fruit of mutual learning and teaching. For this reason, there is no envy among the scholars of religion, because their aim is knowledge of Allah Most High — and He is a vast sea in which there is no constriction. And their purpose is rank with Allah — and there is no constriction either in what is with Allah Most High, because the most sublime of what is with Allah — glory be to Him — of bliss is the delight of beholding Him, and in that there is no hindrance and no competition, nor does one beholder straiten another. Rather, intimacy increases through their multiplicity. Yes — when scholars seek by their knowledge wealth and prestige, they envy one another, because wealth consists of concrete entities and bodies: when it falls into one hand, the other hand is emptied of it. And the meaning of prestige is the possession of hearts; and whenever a person's heart is filled with veneration of one scholar, it turns away from veneration of another, or diminishes toward him unavoidably — and this becomes a cause for mutual envy. But when a heart is filled with joy in knowledge of Allah Most High, that does not prevent another's heart from being filled with it as well and rejoicing in it. And the difference between knowledge and wealth is that wealth does not settle in one hand unless it departs from the other hand, whereas knowledge resides in the scholar's heart and settles in another's heart through his teaching it without departing from his own heart. And wealth consists of bodies and concrete entities, and they have an end — so if a man possessed all that is on the earth, no wealth would remain after him for another to possess. But knowledge has no end, nor can its exhaustive comprehension be conceived. So whoever accustoms his soul to reflection upon the majesty of Allah and His greatness and the dominion (malakūt) of His earth and His heavens — that becomes more delightful to him than every bliss, and he is neither barred from it nor competed with in it. Thus there is no envy in his heart toward any of creation, because if another came to know just as he knows, that would not diminish his delight — rather, his delight would increase through his companionship. So the delight of these people in contemplating the wonders of the dominion (malakūt) perpetually is greater than the delight of one who gazes upon the trees of Paradise and its gardens with the outward eye. For the bliss of the knower (al-ʿārif) and his Paradise is his knowledge, which is an attribute of his own essence — secure from perishing — and he perpetually harvests its fruits. So he, by his spirit and his heart, feeds upon the fruit of his knowledge — a fruit neither cut off nor forbidden, but whose clusters are within reach. And even if he closes the outward eye, his spirit perpetually pastures in a lofty Paradise and blooming meadows. And if one supposes a multitude among the knowers, they would not be envious of one another, but rather would be as the Lord of the Worlds said of them: {«ونزعنا ما في صدورهم من غل إخوانا على سرر متقابلين»} — "And We shall strip away whatever rancor is in their breasts, as brothers, upon couches, face to face." This is their state while still in this world — so what must be supposed of them when the veil is lifted and the Beloved is beheld in the Hereafter? Thus it is inconceivable that there be envy in Paradise, nor that there be envy among the people of this world in Paradise, because Paradise has no straitness in it and no competition, and it is attained only through knowledge of Allah Most High — in which there is no competition even in this world. So the people of Paradise are necessarily free of envy in this world and the Hereafter alike. Rather, envy is among the attributes of those banished from the spaciousness of ʿIlliyyīn to the narrows of Sijjīn. For this reason, the accursed Satan was branded with it, and it is mentioned among his attributes that he envied Adam — peace be upon him — for the special distinction of election (ijtibāʾ) conferred upon him; and when he was called to prostrate, he grew arrogant, refused, rebelled, and disobeyed. So you have come to know that there is no envy except from the converging of two parties upon a single sought aim.
15:47.section_title_en: On Envy Arising from Competition for Worldly Aims, and the Absence of Envy Among Seekers of Knowledge
15:47.anchors:
- Root: حسد (ḥ-s-d)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of wishing removal of another's blessing; the root carries the sense of ill-will toward another's good fortune.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الحسد: تمني زوال نعمة من مستحق لها" — envy is the desire for the removal of a blessing from one who rightfully possesses it, sometimes accompanied by striving to effect its removal.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) usage denotes this spiteful wishing; metaphorically (majāz), it is said "الحسد يأكل الجسد" — envy consumes the body, likening its inner corrosion to physical devouring.
- Root: ضيق (ḍ-y-q)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Narrowness, constriction, the opposite of spaciousness (saʿah).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الضيق: ضد السعة" — used literally for spatial tightness, and extended to distress, poverty, and constriction of the breast.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal for physical narrowness; metaphorical (majāz) in "ضاقت عليه الحيلة" (stratagem became straitened for him) and "وقع في مضيق من أمره" (he fell into a strait in his affair) — indicating incapacity and restriction of means.
- Root: علم (ʿ-l-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Knowledge, perception, cognition; the root denotes grasping a thing's reality.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "العلم: إدراك الشيء بحقيقته" — knowledge is the apprehension of a thing in its true reality, either by grasping its essence or by judging its attributes.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal for certain awareness; metaphorically, "أعلام العلم الخافقه" — the fluttering banners of knowledge — where knowledge is likened to a lofty standard guiding seekers.
- Root: قلب (q-l-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Turning, overturning, transforming a thing from one state to another.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "قلب الشيء: تصريفه وصرفه عن وجه إلى وجه" — the heart is so named for its constant turning and fluctuation.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal for physical overturning; metaphorical (majāz) in "قلب المعلم الصبيان" (the teacher turned the boys back) and "رجل قلب حول" (a man who turns matters over and devises stratagems) — indicating mental deliberation and management of affairs.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — The particle "إنما" restricts the predicate to the subject alone, negating it for all else. In the phrase "إنما الدنيا هي التي تضيق على المتزاحمين" (it is only this world that straitens the competitors), the restriction emphasizes that constriction belongs exclusively to worldly aims, not to the Hereafter.
15:47.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Condemnation of Envy'

16:98.arabic: تعالى {فاستعذ بالله من الشيطان الرجيم} وسائر الأخبار والآيات الواردة في الذكر قال أبو هريرة التقى شيطان المؤمن وشيطان الكافر فإذا شيطان الكافر دهين سمين كاس وشيطان المؤمن مهزول أشعث أغبر عار فقال شيطان الكافر لشيطان المؤمن مالك مهزول قال أنا مع رجل إذا أكل سمى الله فأظل جائعا وإذا شرب سمى الله فأظل عطشانا وإذا لبس سمى الله فأظل عريانا وإذا ادهن سمى الله فأظل شعثا فقال لكني مع رجل لا يفعل شيئا من ذلك فأنا أشاركه في طعامه وشرابه ولباسه وكان محمد بن واسع يقول كل يوم بعد صلاة الصبح اللهم إ
16:98.english: If you say: "What then is the remedy for repelling Satan, and is the remembrance of God—exalted is He—and one's saying 'There is no might and no power except through God' (lā ḥawla wa lā quwwata illā billāh) sufficient for that?" — Know that the remedy of the heart in this matter is to seal these entry points by purifying the heart of these blameworthy traits. And that is something whose full exposition would be lengthy; our purpose in this quarter of the book is to explain the remedy for the destructive traits (al-ṣifāt al-muhlikāt), and each trait requires a separate book, as will be explained later. Yes — when the roots of these traits are severed from the heart, Satan may still make incursions (ijtiyāzāt) and pass through it with fleeting thoughts (khaṭarāt), but he has no stability therein. And what prevents him from passing through is the remembrance of God—exalted is He—because the reality of dhikr cannot take firm hold of the heart except after the heart is built up with God-consciousness (taqwā) and purified of blameworthy traits. Otherwise, the dhikr is but the whisper of the self (ḥadīth nafs), having no authority over the heart, and so it does not repel the dominion of Satan. For this reason, God—exalted is He—said: {إِنَّ الَّذِينَ اتَّقَوْا إِذَا مَسَّهُمْ طَائِفٌ مِنَ الشَّيْطَانِ تَذَكَّرُوا فَإِذَا هُمْ مُبْصِرُونَ} "Indeed, those who fear God — when an impulse touches them from Satan, they remember [Him], and at once they are insightful" (Q 7:201). He specified thereby the God-fearing (muttaqī).
16:98.section_title_en: The Revival of the Religious Sciences — Section 603: On the Remedy for Evil Presumption and the Repelling of Satan
16:98.anchors:
- Root: شيط (Shayṭ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of burning, scorching, or being consumed by fire; also used for one who is destroyed or whose blood is shed in vain.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): الشيطان (Satan) — the one who is far removed from divine mercy, derived from the root indicating his being burned or destroyed.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): "شاط اللحم" — meat that is burnt or spoiled by fire. Metaphorical (Majaz): "شاط دمه" — his blood was shed in vain (i.e., destroyed); "أشاط السلطان دمه" — the ruler declared his blood lawful to shed. Thus, Satan is so named for his being "burned" or "destroyed" by divine curse, and for his causing others to be destroyed.
- Root: قلب (Qalb)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The heart; also the act of turning, overturning, or revolving a thing from one state to another.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "قلب الشيء: تصريفه وصرفه عن وجه إلى وجه" — the turning and directing of a thing from one aspect to another. The heart (qalb) is so named for its constant fluctuation and turning between states.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "قلب الشيء قلبا: حوله عن وجهه" — to turn a thing from its face. Metaphorical: "رجل قلب حول: يقلب الأمور ويحتال" — a man who turns matters over and devises stratagems. The heart's "suwaydāʾ" (core/blackness) is its innermost center where Satan seeks to establish his seat.
- Root: ذكر (Dhikr)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Remembrance, mention, recollection; the opposite of forgetfulness (nisyān).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): الذكر is the presence of a thing in the mind, whether by utterance or by heart; true dhikr is that which takes root in the heart, not mere speech of the tongue.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: uttering with the tongue. Metaphorical: the heart's presence with God, which alone has authority over the soul and repels Satan's incursions.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — The verse {إِنَّ الَّذِينَ اتَّقَوْا إِذَا مَسَّهُمْ طَائِفٌ مِنَ الشَّيْطَانِ تَذَكَّرُوا} restricts the efficacy of dhikr in repelling Satan to the God-fearing (muttaqūn), whose hearts are emptied of passions, thereby specifying the condition for its effectiveness.
16:98.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Disciplining the Soul'

16:98.arabic: وإن كان خلف الإمام اختصر إن لم يكن للإمام سكتة طويلة يقرأ فيها ثم يقول أعوذ بالله من الشيطان الرجيم ثم يقرأ الفاتحة يبتدىء فيها ب بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم بتمام تشديداتها وحروفها ويجتهد في الفرق بين الضاد والظاء ويقول آمين في آخر الفاتحة ويمدها مدا ولا يصل آمين بقوله ولا الضالين وصلا ويجهر بالقراءة في الصبح والمغرب والعشاء إلا أن يكون مأموما ويجهر بالتأمين ثم يقرأ السورة أو قدر ثلاث آيات من القرآن فما فوقها ولا يصل آخر السورة بتكبير الهوى بأن يفصل بينهما بقدر قوله سبحان الله ويقرأ في الصبح من السور الطوال من المفضل وفي المغرب من قصاره
16:98.english: I say: Then the worshipper begins with the opening supplication (duʿāʾ al-istiftāḥ). It is excellent that he say, following his utterance of "Allāhu akbar, Allāhu akbar": "Kabīran wa-l-ḥamdu lillāhi kathīran wa-subḥāna Allāhi bukratan wa-aṣīlā" (Great indeed is Allah, and abundant praise be to Allah, and glory be to Allah morning and evening) {«الله أكبر كبيرا والحمد لله كثيرا وسبحان الله بكرة وأصيلا»} — then: "Wajjahtu wajhiya..." (I have turned my face...) up to his saying "...wa-anā min al-muslimīn" (and I am among those who submit) {«وجهت وجهي إلى قوله وأنا من المسلمين»}. Then he says: "Subḥānaka Allāhumma wa-bi-ḥamdika wa-tabāraka-smuka wa-taʿālā jadduka wa-jalla thanāʾuka wa-lā ilāha ghayruk" (Glory be to You, O Allah, and with Your praise; blessed is Your Name and exalted is Your majesty; glorious is Your praise and there is no god but You) {«سبحانك اللهم وبحمدك وتبارك اسمك وتعالى جدك وجل ثناؤك ولا إله غيرك»} — so that he may combine within himself the various dispersed reports transmitted in the traditions.
16:98.section_title_en: Section 127 — On the Recitation (Qirāʾah) and the Bowing (Rukūʿ) with Its Attendant Matters
16:98.anchors:
- Root: قرأ (Qaraʾa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of gathering and assembling letters into articulated speech; recitation as the oral articulation of written or memorized text.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In the Quranic and liturgical context, qirāʾah is the deliberate, worshipful utterance of the divine word, distinct from mere reading; it is an act of devotion requiring presence of heart.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) usage denotes the physical articulation of sounds; metaphorical (majāz) usage extends to the inward recitation of the heart in contemplation.
- Root: ركع (Rakaʿa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The physical act of bowing; the bending of the back in humility.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الركوع: الانحناء، فتارة يستعمل في الهيئة المخصوصة في الصلاة كما هي، وتارة في التواضع والتذلل" — The bowing is an inclination, used sometimes for the specific posture in prayer, and sometimes for humility and self-abasement.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): "شيخ راكع: منحن من الكبر" — an old man bowed with age. Metaphorical (majāz): "لغبت الإبل حتى ركعت" — camels fatigued until they lowered their heads, indicating the physical posture as the outward sign of inward submission.
- Root: صبح (Ṣabaḥa)
  * Al-Raghib (Al-Mufradat): "الصبح والصباح، أول النهار" — the dawn is the beginning of the day, the time when the horizon reddens.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas - Majaz/Metaphorical): "أصبح يا رجل: انتبه من غفلتك" — "become awake, O man: awaken from your heedlessness," showing the dawn prayer as the time of spiritual awakening.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Prepositional Interposition (باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور) — governing the permissible separation between governing and governed elements, applied here to the proper pausing (waqf) and connecting (waṣl) of Quranic phrases to preserve meaning.
16:98.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications, prayers, and their spiritual power, from 'Condemnation of Envy'

16:111.arabic: الهوى وستجد كل نفس ما عملت من سوء أو خير محضرا عند الله ولو في فلتة خاطر أو فلتة ناظر من غير ظلم وجور فما الله بظلام للعبيد وأما القسم الثاني وهو فوات الحاصل فهو مكروه ومعتبر في جواز السكوت في الأمور الأربعة إلا العلم فإن فواته غير مخوف إلا بتقصير منه وإلا فلا يقدر أحد على سلب العلم من غيره وإن قدر على سلب الصحة والسلامة والثروة والمال وهذا أحد أسباب شرف العلم فإنه يدوم في الدنيا ويدوم ثوابه في الآخرة فلا انقطاع له أبد الآباد وأما الصحة والسلامة ففواتهما بالضرب فكل من عل
16:111.english: All of this does not nullify the obligation of ḥisbah, because these are but increases (ziyādāt) whose attainment is prevented — and calling the mere prevention of attaining increases "harm" (ḍarar) is metaphorical (majāz). True harm (al-ḍarar al-ḥaqīqī) is only the loss of something already in hand (fawāt ḥāṣil). Nothing is excepted from this rule save that which necessity (ḥājah) calls for, and whose loss entails a danger (maḥdhūr) exceeding the danger of remaining silent over the wrong (al-sukūt ʿalā al-munkar) — as when one is in need of a physician for an acute illness, and the cure is anticipated from the physician's treatment, and he knows that in the physician's delay there is severe aggravation of his malady and prolongation of his sickness, which may even lead to death.
16:111.section_title_en: On the Conditions Permitting Abandonment of Enjoining Right — Section 532
16:111.anchors:
- Root: حسب (ḥ-s-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of counting, reckoning, and calculating; al-ḥisbah derives from the notion of taking account of another's deeds.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الحساب: استعمال العدد" — reckoning is the employment of number; the theological nuance connects to divine accounting and the duty of moral reckoning upon others.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): "حسب المال" — to count property. Metaphorical (majāz): "يَتَحَسَّبانِ الأخبار" — to seek out and investigate news, as one probes and tests; thus ḥisbah is the active seeking-out of wrongs to rectify them.
- Root: ضرر (ḍ-r-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of harm, injury, and detriment; al-ḍarar is that which opposes benefit (nafʿ).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Harm is of two kinds — that which is truly detrimental to one's religion or worldly welfare, and that which is merely imagined or anticipated.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: actual physical or material injury. Metaphorical: the mere loss of an anticipated increase (ziyādah), which is not true harm but is called so figuratively.
- Root: سكت (s-k-t)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of silence, refraining from speech.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "السكوت مختص بترك الكلام" — silence is specific to abstaining from speech; it is a form of rest (sukūn) and is used metaphorically for the subsiding of anger or other states.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "رجل سكوت" — a man habitually silent. Metaphorical: "سكت عنه الغضب" — anger subsided; thus al-sukūt ʿan al-munkar is the deliberate cessation of verbal objection.
- Root: علم (ʿ-l-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of knowledge, perception, and discernment.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "العلم: إدراك الشيء بحقيقته" — knowledge is the apprehension of a thing in its true reality; it is that which cannot be forcibly stripped from its possessor.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "ما علمت بخبرك" — I had no awareness of your news. Metaphorical: knowledge as an enduring mark (ʿalam) and signpost of guidance.
- Sibawayh Rule: Restriction and exception (al-ḥaṣr wa al-istithnāʾ) — the conditional framing of permissibility (al-tarkhīṣ) through specified exceptions (istithnāʾ) governed by the weighing of two harms (taʿāruḍ al-mafsadatayn), where the lesser is borne to avert the greater.
16:111.topic: Al-Ghazali on purifying the character, moral diseases, and spiritual remedies, from 'Enjoining Good and Forbidding Evil'

16:111.arabic: الرجل يا أمير المؤمنين قال الله عز وجل يوم تأتي كل نفس تجادل عن نفسها أفنجادل الله تعالى ولا نتكلم بين يديك كلاما قال هشام بلى ويحك تكلم وروي أن سارقا دخل خباء عمار بن ياسر بصفين فقيل له اقطعه فإنه من أعدائنا فقال بل أستر عليه لعل الله يستر علي يوم القيامة وجلس ابن مسعود في السوق يبتاع طعاما فابتاع ثم طلب الدراهم وكانت في عمامته فوجدتها قد حلت فقال لقد جلست وإنها لمعي فجعلوا يدعون على من أخذها ويقولون اللهم اقطع يد السارق الذي أخذها اللهم افعل به كذا فقال عبد الله اللهم إن كان حمله على أخذها حاجة فبارك له فيها وإن كان
16:111.english: A man was brought to Hishām concerning whom word had reached him. When he was made to stand before him, he began to speak in his own defense. Hishām said to him: You speak as well? The man said: O Commander of the Faithful, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: {«يَوْمَ تَأْتِي كُلُّ نَفْسٍ تُجَادِلُ عَنْ نَفْسِهَا»} — "The Day when every soul will come disputing on its own behalf." Shall we dispute before Allah the Exalted, and not speak a word before you? Hishām said: Yes, woe to you — speak.
16:111.section_title_en: ** Section 715 — On the Virtue of Forbearance (al-Ḥilm) and Gentleness (al-Rifq)
16:111.anchors:
**

- **Root: عفو (ʿ-F-W)**
  - *Lisan / Ayn:* Al-ʿAfw is the effacing and obliteration of the trace of a thing; to pardon is to efface the trace of the offense entirely.
  - *Al-Raghib (Mufradat):* Al-ʿAfw is the erasure of the sin such that no consequence remains — it is the highest form of forgiveness, surpassing al-ghufrān which veils but does not necessarily efface.
  - *Al-Zamakhshari (Asas):* Literal: "عفا الأثر" — the trace was effaced. Metaphorical: pardon as the effacing of the offense's consequence, as in "عفا عن ذنبه."

- **Root: حلم (Ḥ-L-M)**
  - *Lisan / Ayn:* Al-Ḥilm is forbearance, clemency, and the restraint of the soul from agitation upon provocation.
  - *Al-Raghib (Mufradat):* Al-Ḥilm is the soul's composure and its withholding from haste; it is a virtue opposed to al-ṭaysh (levity) and al-jahl (foolishness) — not ignorance, but the deliberate restraint of passion.
  - *Al-Zamakhshari (Asas):* Literal: dreams (aḥlām) share the root — the state of being unmoved. Metaphorical: the forbearing man (ḥalīm) whose soul does not stir toward vengeance when provoked.

- **Root: رفق (R-F-Q)**
  - *Lisan / Ayn:* Al-Rifq is gentleness, lenity, and the opposite of violence (al-ʿunf).
  - *Al-Raghib (Mufradat):* Al-Rifq is the disposition toward ease and gentleness in all affairs; it is praised by the Law and is a quality of the prophets.
  - *Al-Zamakhshari (Asas):* Literal: "رفق به" — he was gentle with him. Metaphorical: gentleness in conduct as a mode of spiritual excellence.

- **Root: صفح (Ṣ-F-Ḥ)**
  - *Lisan / Ayn:* Al-Ṣafḥ is turning away from an offense and meeting it with a generous countenance; from ṣafḥah (cheek/face) — to turn one's face away from the wrong.
  - *Al-Raghib (Mufradat):* Al-Ṣafḥ is the overlooking of the offense combined with graciousness — it is more than mere pardon, for it includes magnanimity (al-Ifḍāl).
  - *Al-Zamakhshari (Asas):* Literal: "صفح عنه" — he turned his face away from him. Metaphorical: to turn away from requital and instead bestow favor.

- **Sibawayh Rule:** *Bāb al-Ḥaṣr wa al-Taqyīd bi-innamā* (Restriction & Focused Predication) — "إنما أعطى ما أعطى بأربع خصال" employs innamā to restrict the cause of the gift to four qualities, and "ليس الحليم من ظلم فحلم حتى إذا قدر انتقم" uses laysa to negate the predicate entirely before affirming the true definition.

---

**
16:111.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Condemnation of Envy'

17:15.arabic: وحسناته فإنه من كسبه وغير مؤاخذ بسيئاته فإنه لا تزر وازرة وزر أخرى ولذلك قال تعالى ألحقنا بهم ذرياتهم وما ألتناهم من عملهم من شيء أي ما نقصناهم من أعمالهم وجعلنا أولادهم مزيدا في إحسانهم الوجه الرابع أن يموت الولد قبله فيكون له شفيعا فقد روي عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال إن الطفل يجر بأبويه إلى الجنة (5) وفي بعض الأخبار يأخذ بثوبه كما أنا الآن آخذ بثوبك (6) وقال أيضا صلى الله عليه وسلم إن المولود يقال ادخل الجنة فيقف على باب الجنة فيظل محبنطئا أي ممتلئا غيظا وغضبا ويقول لا أدخل الجنة إلا وأبواي معي فيقال أدخلوا
17:15.english: وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم: "لا يلقى الله أحد بذنب أعظم من جهالة أهله."
17:15.topic: Al-Ghazali on the journey of the soul, death, and the Hereafter, from 'Condemnation of Envy'

17:61.arabic: فقال وما هو قال إياك والكبر فإنه أول ذنب عصي الله به ثم قرأ {وإذ قلنا للملائكة اسجدوا لآدم فسجدوا إلا إبليس} الآية وإياك والحرص فإنه أخرج آدم من الجنة أمكنه الله سبحانه من جنة عرضها السموات والأرض يأكل منها إلا شجرة واحدة نهاه الله عنها فأكل منها فأخرجه الله تعالى منها ثم قال {اهبطوا منها} إلى آخر الآية وإياك والحسد فإنما قتل ابن آدم أخاه حين حسده ثم قرأ {واتل عليهم نبأ ابني آدم بالحق} الآيات وإذا ذكر أصحاب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فأمسك وإذا ذكر القدر فاسكت وإذا ذكرت النجوم فاسكت وقال بكر بن عبد الله كان رجل يغشى بعض الملوك فيقوم بحذاء الملك ف
17:61.english: Know that envy (ḥasad) is likewise among the fruits of rancor (ḥiqd), and rancor is among the fruits of anger (ghaḍab) — so envy is a branch of a branch, while anger is the root of the root. Then envy has, among its blameworthy branches, that which can scarcely be enumerated. And there have come down, specifically in condemnation of envy, many reports (akhbār). - Root: حسد (Ḥ-S-D)

- Root: حدث (Ḥ-D-TH)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Origination after non-existence; bringing into being after nothingness.

17:94.arabic: الأسباب وقالوا متعجبين أبعث الله بشرا رسولا {وقالوا} لولا أنزل علينا الملائكة وقال تعالى أو عجبتم أن جاءكم ذكر من ربكم على رجل منكم الآية السبب الخامس الخوف من فوت المقاصد وذلك يختص بمتزاحمين على مقصود واحد فإن كان واحد يحسد صاحبه في كل نعمة تكون عونا له في الانفراد بمقصوده ومن هذا الجنس تحاسد الضرات في التزاحم على مقاصد الزوجية وتحاسد الأخوة في التزاحم على نيل المنزلة في قلب الأبوين للتوصل به إلى مقاصد الكرامة والمال وكذلك تحاسد التلميذين لأستاذ واحد على نيل المرتبة من قلب الأستاذ وتحاسد ندما
17:94.english: I say: God is Knower of what is in the breasts. {«إِنْ تَمْسَسْكُمْ حَسَنَةٌ تَسُؤْهُمْ»} — "If good touches you, it grieves them" {«وَدُّوا مَا عَنِتُّمْ قَدْ بَدَتِ الْبَغْضَاءُ مِنْ أَفْوَاهِهِمْ وَمَا تُخْفِي صُدُورُهُمْ أَكْبَرُ»} — "They wish for your hardship; hatred has already appeared from their mouths, and what their breasts conceal is greater." And envy (ḥasad), arising from hatred, may lead to contention, mutual fighting, and the spending of one's entire life in removing another's blessing through stratagems, slander, the tearing of veils, and whatever runs in that course.
17:94.section_title_en: The Revival of the Religious Sciences — Book on the Rebuke of the Self: The Seven Causes of Envy (Section 722)
17:94.anchors:
- Root: سبب (sabab)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The rope by which one climbs; every means by which one reaches a thing.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Every means by which one arrives at something is called a sabab" — thus the causes enumerated here are the psychological "ropes" by which envy ascends in the soul.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: a physical cord. Metaphorical: any linkage or occasion — here, the inward occasions (asbāb) that give rise to ḥasad.
- Root: بغض (bughḍ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Hatred, aversion of the heart.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The opposite of love (maḥabbah); a disposition of the heart toward another's harm.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: inner aversion. Metaphorical: its "appearance from the mouths" (Quranic) as outward speech betraying the concealed hatred.
- Root: كبر (kibr)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Greatness; pride; disdain.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Al-kabīr and al-ṣaghīr are relative terms" — pride is the claim to greatness relative to another, deeming oneself above him.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: bigness in stature or age. Metaphorical: "takabbara 'alayhi" — to deem oneself greater than another and refuse submission to him.
- Root: قصد (qaṣd)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Straightness of path; intending a goal.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Al-qaṣd: istiqāmat al-ṭarīq" — the straight road; also moderation between extremes.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: to head toward a place. Metaphorical: "maqāṣid" — the aims and objectives toward which one directs oneself; here, the worldly goals whose pursuit breeds rivalry and envy.
- Root: نزل (nazal)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To descend from a height; to alight.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Al-nuzūl fī al-aṣl huwa inḥiṭāṭ min 'uluww" — descent from above; the sending down of revelation.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: descending from a high place. Metaphorical: "anzala Allāhu al-kitāb" — God's sending down of the Quran; and "mā unzila" — what was revealed, as in the Quranic citation regarding the Qurashites' objection to revelation upon a mere human.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Causal Coordination (al-'aṭf al-sababī) — The enumeration of the seven causes proceeds by coordinated clauses (fa-... thumma ...), each introduced as an independent proposition linked by causation (sabab), requiring the translator to preserve the logical sequence of psychological motivations without collapsing them into one another.

And he, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: {«The thing I most fear for my community is that wealth will increase among them, and they will envy one another and fight one another»} (1). And he, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: {«Seek help in fulfilling your needs by keeping them secret, for everyone who possesses a blessing is envied»} (2). And he, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: {«Indeed, the blessings of God have enemies.» It was said: "And who are they?" He said: {«Those who envy people for what God has given them of His bounty»} (3). The ḥadīth: {«Six will enter the Fire before the Reckoning by a year.» It was said: "O Messenger of God, who are they?" He said: {«The unjust rulers»} — the ḥadīth — and in it: {«And the scholars who envy»}. Narrated by Abū Manṣūr al-Daylamī from the ḥadīth of Ibn ʿUmar and Anas with two weak chains of transmission.
20:116.section_title_en: Section 718 — On Envy (Ḥasad): Its Roots, Branches, and Blameworthy Fruits
20:116.anchors:
- Root: حسد (Ḥ-S-D)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of wishing for removal of a blessing from its possessor, rooted in spite and resentment.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الحسد: تمني زوال نعمة من مستحق لها" — Envy is the desire for the removal of a blessing from one who rightly deserves it, sometimes accompanied by active striving to effect its removal. The believer envies not, but the hypocrite does.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): "حسده على نعمة الله" — to envy him for God's blessing. Metaphorical (majāz): "إن الحسد يأكل الجسد" — envy consumes the body, as fire consumes wood, indicating its destructive spiritual effect.
- Root: حدث (Ḥ-D-TH)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Origination after non-existence; bringing into being after nothingness.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الحدوث: كون الشيء بعد أن لم يكن" — origination is a thing's coming to be after it was not. The ḥadīth (report) is so-called for its temporal proximity to the event it narrates.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "هو حدث من الأحداث" — he is a youth among youths. Metaphorical: "صاروا أحاديث" — they became subjects of talk, indicating fame or infamy spread by tongues.
- Root: ملك (M-L-K)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Possession, dominion, sovereignty; the one who possesses and disposes.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الملك: هو المتصرف بالأمر والنهي" — dominion is disposal by command and prohibition. Two kinds: actual possession/sovereignty, and the power/capacity to exercise it.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "ملكت فلانة" — he married her (possessed her in wedlock). Metaphorical: "ملك نفسه عند الغضب" — he mastered himself at the moment of anger, i.e., self-restraint.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — When the Prophet (ﷺ) says "إنما قتل ابن آدم أخاه حين حسده" (It was only envy that led the son of Adam to kill his brother), the restrictive particle إنما confines the cause of the first murder to envy alone, isolating it as the sole efficient cause of that primordial transgression.
20:116.topic: Al-Ghazali on purifying the character, moral diseases, and spiritual remedies, from 'Condemnation of Envy'

22:6.arabic: دفعه نسأل الله حسن التوفيق بلطفه وكرمه أنه على كل شيء قدير والحمد لله وحده
22:6.english: Rather, the necessary love is that which the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, pointed to in his saying: «من أصبح آمنا في سربه معافى في بدنه وله قوت يومه فكأنما حيزت له الدنيا بحذافيرها» — "Whoever wakes up secure in his person, healthy in his body, and having the sustenance of his day, it is as if the whole world had been gathered for him." (1)
22:6.section_title_en: The Third Category: What Is Necessary for Some People but Not Others — The Discipline of Anger
22:6.anchors:
- Root: غضب (ghaḍab)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: anger, wrath, fury — the boiling of the blood of the heart desiring vengeance.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): When attributed to God, it means retribution (intiqām) alone, not an emotional state. For humans, it is the surge of blood in the heart seeking revenge.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): anger toward the living (ghaḍibtu lahu). Metaphorical (majāz): anger toward the dead (ghaḍibtu bihi), and the kindling of anger like fire catching flame.
- Root: حب (ḥubb)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Love, affection, attachment — the inclination of the heart toward what pleases it.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Love is the heart's yearning for what it deems agreeable; it is the root from which anger branches, for one only becomes angry over what he loves.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: enduring affection. Metaphorical: love as the driving force behind action and reaction.
- Root: رياضة (riyāḍah)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Training, discipline, exercise — the breaking and subduing of the self through repeated practice.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Spiritual discipline: habituating the soul to virtuous acts until they become ingrained character (khuluq rāsikh).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: training an animal. Metaphorical: disciplining the soul's faculties.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب التقسيم والتفصيل (Division and Detailing) — The periodic structure here divides anger into three categories (qism), then treats each sequentially with conditional and causal clauses (fa-inna, fa-idhā, wa-ammā), requiring precise tracking of antecedents and consequents.
22:6.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications, prayers, and their spiritual power, from 'Condemnation of Envy'

23:34.arabic: أنتم إلا بشر مثلنا وقالوا أنؤمن لبشرين مثلنا ولئن أطعتم بشرا مثلكم إنكم إذا لخاسرون فتعجبوا من أن يفوز برتبة الرسالة والوحي والقرب من الله تعالى بشر مثلهم فحسدوهم وأحبوا زوال النبوة عنهم جزعا أن يفضل عليهم من هو مثلهم في الخلقة لا عن قصد تكبر وطلب رياسة وتقدم عداوة أو سبب آخر من سائر الأسباب وقالوا متعجبين أبعث الله بشرا رسولا {وقالوا} لولا أنزل علينا الملائكة وقال تعالى أو عجبتم أن جاءكم ذكر من ربكم على رجل منكم الآية السبب الخامس الخوف من فوت المقاصد وذلك يختص بمتزاحمين على مقصود واحد فإن كان واحد يحسد صاحبه في كل نعمة تكون عونا
23:34.english: I say: God is Knower of what is in the breasts. {«إِنْ تَمْسَسْكُمْ حَسَنَةٌ تَسُؤْهُمْ»} — "If good touches you, it grieves them" {«وَدُّوا مَا عَنِتُّمْ قَدْ بَدَتِ الْبَغْضَاءُ مِنْ أَفْوَاهِهِمْ وَمَا تُخْفِي صُدُورُهُمْ أَكْبَرُ»} — "They wish for your hardship; hatred has already appeared from their mouths, and what their breasts conceal is greater." And envy (ḥasad), arising from hatred, may lead to contention, mutual fighting, and the spending of one's entire life in removing another's blessing through stratagems, slander, the tearing of veils, and whatever runs in that course.
23:34.section_title_en: The Revival of the Religious Sciences — Book on the Rebuke of the Self: The Seven Causes of Envy (Section 722)
23:34.anchors:
- Root: سبب (sabab)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The rope by which one climbs; every means by which one reaches a thing.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Every means by which one arrives at something is called a sabab" — thus the causes enumerated here are the psychological "ropes" by which envy ascends in the soul.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: a physical cord. Metaphorical: any linkage or occasion — here, the inward occasions (asbāb) that give rise to ḥasad.
- Root: بغض (bughḍ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Hatred, aversion of the heart.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The opposite of love (maḥabbah); a disposition of the heart toward another's harm.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: inner aversion. Metaphorical: its "appearance from the mouths" (Quranic) as outward speech betraying the concealed hatred.
- Root: كبر (kibr)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Greatness; pride; disdain.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Al-kabīr and al-ṣaghīr are relative terms" — pride is the claim to greatness relative to another, deeming oneself above him.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: bigness in stature or age. Metaphorical: "takabbara 'alayhi" — to deem oneself greater than another and refuse submission to him.
- Root: قصد (qaṣd)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Straightness of path; intending a goal.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Al-qaṣd: istiqāmat al-ṭarīq" — the straight road; also moderation between extremes.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: to head toward a place. Metaphorical: "maqāṣid" — the aims and objectives toward which one directs oneself; here, the worldly goals whose pursuit breeds rivalry and envy.
- Root: نزل (nazal)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To descend from a height; to alight.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Al-nuzūl fī al-aṣl huwa inḥiṭāṭ min 'uluww" — descent from above; the sending down of revelation.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: descending from a high place. Metaphorical: "anzala Allāhu al-kitāb" — God's sending down of the Quran; and "mā unzila" — what was revealed, as in the Quranic citation regarding the Qurashites' objection to revelation upon a mere human.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Causal Coordination (al-'aṭf al-sababī) — The enumeration of the seven causes proceeds by coordinated clauses (fa-... thumma ...), each introduced as an independent proposition linked by causation (sabab), requiring the translator to preserve the logical sequence of psychological motivations without collapsing them into one another.
23:34.topic: Al-Ghazali on purifying the character, moral diseases, and spiritual remedies, from 'Condemnation of Envy'

24:2.arabic: يعني في الدين وقال تعالى {ولا تأخذكم بهما رأفة في دين الله} بل من فقد الغضب عجز عن رياضة نفسه إذ لا تتم الرياضة إلا بتسليط الغضب على الشهوة حتى يغضب على نفسه عند الميل إلى الشهوات الخسيسة ففقد الغضب مذموم وإنما المحمود غضب ينتظر إشارة العقل والدين فينبعث حيث تجب الحمية وينطفيء حيث يحسن الحلم وحفظه على حد الاعتدال هو الاستقامة التي كلف الله بها عباده وهو الوسط الذي وصفه رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم حيث قال خير الأمور أوساطها (1) فمن مال غضبه إلى الفتور حتى أحس من نفسه بضعف الغيرة وخسة النفس في ا
24:2.english: As for deficiency: it is the loss of this power or its weakness. This is blameworthy, and it is of such a one that it is said: "He has no protective zeal (ḥamiyyah)." For this reason al-Shāfiʿī — may God have mercy on him — said: "Whoever is provoked to anger and does not become angry is a donkey." Whoever loses the power of anger and protective zeal entirely is utterly deficient. God — exalted be He — described the Companions of the Prophet — peace be upon him — with severity and protective zeal, saying: {«أشداء على الكفار رحماء بينهم»} "Severe against the disbelievers, merciful among themselves" (Q 48:29). And He said to His Prophet — peace be upon him: {«جاهد الكفار والمنافقين واغلظ عليهم»} "Strive against the disbelievers and the hypocrites and be harsh with them" (Q 9:73) — the verse. Harshness and severity are but effects of the power of protective zeal, which is anger.
24:2.section_title_en: The Reality of Anger (Ghaḍab) and Its Degrees — Book 21, Section 703
24:2.anchors:
- Root: غضب (Ghaḍab)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root denotes anger, rage, fury; the surge of blood in the heart seeking vengeance.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الغضب: ثوران دم القلب إرادة الانتقام" — when attributed to God, it means solely His retribution, not an emotional state.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): "غضبت لفلان" (anger for the living); Metaphorical (majāz): "غضبت به" (anger over the dead), and the poetic extension to inanimate objects like fire or reins.
- Root: نفس (Nafs)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Self, soul, spirit; the vital principle.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The soul as the seat of blameworthy traits when unrestrained; its purification is the goal of spiritual struggle.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the self; Metaphorical: "دفق نفسه" (spilled his blood/life).
- Root: قلب (Qalb)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The heart; to turn over, to flip.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "قلب الشيء: تصريفه وصرفه عن وجه إلى وجه" — the heart is so named for its constant fluctuation and turning.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical turning; Metaphorical: the heart as the seat of intellect and spiritual perception, which anger overturns and blinds.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد (Restriction & Focused Predication) — Used to distinguish the three degrees of anger (deficiency, excess, moderation) as mutually exclusive categories.
24:2.topic: Al-Ghazali on purifying the character, moral diseases, and spiritual remedies, from 'Condemnation of Envy'

24:22.arabic: وفيه نزل قوله تعالى ولا يأتل أولوا الفضل منكم والسعة إلى قوله تعالى {ألا تحبون أن يغفر الله لكم} إذ تكلم مسطح بن أثاثة في واقعة الإفك (1) فحلف أبو بكر أن يقطع عنه رفقه وقد كان يواسيه بالمال فنزلت الآية مع عظم معصية مسطح وأية معصية تزيد على التعرض لحرم رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وإطالة اللسان في مثل عائشة رضي الله عنها إلا أن الصديق رضي الله عنه كان كالمجني عليه في نفسه بتلك الواقعة والعفو عمن ظلم والإحسان إلى من أساء من أخلاق الصديقين وإنما يحسن الإحسان إلى من ظلمك فأما من ظلم غيرك وعصى الله به
24:22.english:
**QUAD_ANCHORS:**
- Root: ط-و-ع (ṭ-w-ʿ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of obedience, submission, compliance; ṭāʿah is the act of conforming to command
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In theological usage, ṭāʿah is specifically obedience to Allah's commands as distinguished from maʿṣiyah (disobedience); the root carries the sense of voluntary compliance versus coerced submission
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal sense is yielding and complying; in religious context it denotes conformity to divine law as opposed to transgression (maʿṣiyah)
- Root: ب-غ-ض (b-gh-ḍ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Hatred, aversion, detestation; the opposite of ḥubb (love)
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In theological ethics, bughḍ is the soul's aversion to something; religiously it must be directed toward disobedience while preserving love for the believer's faith
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: intense dislike; metaphorical: the heart's turning away from what displeases Allah
- Root: ج-ن-ي (j-n-y)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To commit a crime or offense; picking fruit (jināyah as reaping what one has sown)
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Jināyah is any act that harms another; in legal-theological usage, it denotes transgression against rights — whether Allah's rights (ḥuqūq Allāh) or human rights (ḥuqūq al-ʿibād)
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: reaping/cutting fruit; metaphorical: committing an offense whose consequences one "reaps"
- Root: ع-ف-و (ʿ-f-w)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To pardon, forgive, efface; the root also carries the sense of leaving something and desisting from it
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): ʿAfw is to relinquish retaliation and erase the trace of the offense; it is the highest form of forgiveness, coupled with iḥsān (beneficence)
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: obliteration and effacement; metaphorical: the soul's effacement of resentment toward the offender
- Root: م-د-ه-ن (m-d-h-n)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Flattery, hypocrisy, dissimulation; from the sense of softening and pliability
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Mudāhanah is to show outward friendliness while concealing enmity, or to overlook sins out of worldly motive rather than genuine mercy
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: to be soft and pliant like oil (duhn); metaphorical: hypocritical leniency in religious matters
- Sibawayh Rule: باب التقسيم والتفصيل (Division and Specification) — The text employs systematic bipartite and tripartite divisions (taqsīm) to enumerate degrees and categories, each with its own governing rule, requiring the translator to preserve the structural parallelism of conditional clauses (sharṭ/jazā') and their apodoses.
24:22.topic: Al-Ghazali on purifying the character, moral diseases, and spiritual remedies, from 'Condemnation of Envy'

24:22.arabic: {ألا تحبون أن يغفر الله لكم} إذ تكلم مسطح بن أثاثة في واقعة الإفك (1) فحلف أبو بكر أن يقطع عنه رفقه وقد كان يواسيه بالمال فنزلت الآية مع عظم معصية مسطح وأية معصية تزيد على التعرض لحرم رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وإطالة اللسان في مثل عائشة رضي الله عنها إلا أن الصديق رضي الله عنه كان كالمجني عليه في نفسه بتلك الواقعة والعفو عمن ظلم والإحسان إلى من أساء من أخلاق الصديقين وإنما يحسن الإحسان إلى من ظلمك فأما من ظلم غيرك وعصى الله به فلا يحسن إحسانك إليه لأن في الإحسان إلى الظالم إ

24:22.arabic: وقرأ {وليعفوا وليصفحوا ألا تحبون أن يغفر الله لكم والله غفور رحيم} (1) وفي رواية فكأنما سفي في وجه رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم رماد لشدة تغيره وروى أن عمر رضي الله عنه كان يعس بالمدينة من الليل فسمع صوت رجل في بيت يتغنى فتسور عليه فوجده عنده امرأة وعنده خمر فقال يا عدو الله أظننت أن الله يسترك وأنت على معصيته فقال وأنت يا أمير المؤمنين فلا تعجل فإن كنت قد عصيت الله واحدة فقد عصيت الله في ثلاثا قال الله تعالى {ولا تجسسوا} وقد تجسست وقال الله تعالى {وليس البر بأن تأتوا البيوت من ظهورها} وقد تسورت علي وقد قال الله تعالى {لا تدخلوا بي
24:22.english: **First**: That you greet him with peace (*salām*) when you meet him, and respond to his invitation when he invites you, and say "may Allah have mercy on you" (*tashmīt*) when he sneezes, and visit him when he is ill, and attend his funeral procession when he dies, and fulfill his oath when he swears by you, and give him sincere counsel when he seeks your advice, and protect him in his absence when he is away from you, and love for him what you love for yourself, and dislike for him what you dislike for yourself. (1)
24:22.section_title_en: The Rights of Brotherhood — Section 433: The Duties of a Muslim Toward His Fellow Muslims
24:22.anchors:
- Root: سلم (s-l-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of safety, security, freedom from harm; the root from which *islām* (submission/surrender) and *salām* (peace) derive
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): *Salām* as the theological state of being secure from harm — both giving and receiving safety; *islām* as the total surrender of the heart to Allah
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (*ḥaqīqah*): physical safety from tongue and hand; Metaphorical (*majāz*): the comprehensive spiritual safety that defines true Muslim brotherhood
- Root: عون (ʿ-w-n)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Assistance, aid, helping another in need
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Mutual assistance as a divine ordinance among believers
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical aid; Metaphorical: intercession (*shafāʿah*) and advocacy on behalf of others
- Root: ستر (s-t-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Covering, concealing, veiling; protection from exposure
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): *Sitr* as the divine attribute of concealment — Allah's covering of sins in this world and the next
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: covering a physical defect; Metaphorical: concealing another's faults and sins — a cardinal virtue of brotherhood
- Root: عذر (ʿ-dh-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Excuse, pardon, acceptance of apology
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): *ʿAfw* (pardon) as the higher station of forgiveness that elevates the forgiver
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: releasing from obligation; Metaphorical: the noble trait of overlooking others' offenses
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد (Restriction & Focused Predication) — The repeated use of restrictive constructions (e.g., "المسلم من سلم المسلمون") establishes definitional boundaries through predicate restriction, indicating that the *ḥaqīqah* of faith is manifested through specific observable actions.

24:37.arabic: قال الله تعالى رجال لا تلهيهم تجارة ولا بيع عن ذكر الله وإقام الصلاة وإيتاء الزكاة وقال الله تعالى في بيوت أذن الله أن ترفع ويذكر فيها اسمه فينبغي أن يجعل أول النهار إلى وقت دخول السوق لآخرته فيلازم المسجد ويواظب على الأوراد كان عمر رضي الله عنه يقول للتجار اجعلوا أول نهاركم لآخرتكم وما بعده لدنياكم وكان صالحو السلف يجعلون أول النهار وآخره للآخرة والوسط للتجارة ولم يكن يبيع الهريسة والرءوس بكرة إلا الصبيان وأهل الذمة لأنهم كانوا في المساجد بعد وفي الخبر إن الملائكة إذا صعدت بصحيفة العبد وفيها في
24:37.english: Some of the Salaf (may God be pleased with them) said: "The thing most worthy of the intelligent man is that which he most needs in the immediate term; and the thing he most needs in the immediate term is that whose consequence is most praiseworthy in the long term."
24:37.section_title_en: On the Merchant's Vigilance Over His Religion: Seven Matters of Concern in Trade
24:37.anchors:
- Root: دنا (d-n-w)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Proximity, nearness in place, time, or rank; the nearer (adnā) as opposed to the farther.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الدنو: القرب بالذات، أو بالحكم" — nearness by essence or by judgment; used of place, time, and station. The "nearer life" (al-ḥayāh al-dunyā) is the proximate, lower life.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical nearness. Metaphorical: the worldly life (al-dunyā) as that which is "nearer" and lower, contrasted with the Hereafter (al-ākhirah) which is "farther" but enduring.
- Root: سوق (s-w-q)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To drive, to impel, to lead; a market (sūq) where goods are driven and circulated.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The driving of one's self toward a goal; the market as the arena of exchange and transaction.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "ساق النعم فانساقت" — he drove the cattle and they were driven. Metaphorical: "ساق الله إليه خيرا" — God drove good to him; "ساق إليها المهر" — he sent the dowry to her. The "market of the Hereafter" (sūq al-ākhirah) is the mosque, where one trades deeds for the next life.
- Root: جار (j-w-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To deviate from the right path, to wrong, to oppress; also a neighbor (jār) whose rights are sacred.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الجار: من يقرب مسكنه منك" — the neighbor is one whose dwelling is near yours; a reciprocal term. God's right and the neighbor's right are conjoined in the Qur'anic verse {والجار ذي القربى والجار الجنب} (Al-Nisā': 36).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: oppression and transgression. Metaphorical: the "oppressive oath" (yamīn fājirah) — an oath that swerves from truth and justice.
- Root: الي (a-l-w)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To fall short, to fail; also related to رسالة (message) via مألكة.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The root conveys the idea of commission and conveyance of a message; "المألكة: الرسالة" — the message, because it is "chewed" in the mouth (from ألك, to masticate).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: to chew. Metaphorical: the angelic conveyance of revelation as a "message" delivered.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — When the author says "وإنما تتم شفقة التاجر على دينه بمراعاة سبعة أمور" ("The merchant's compassion for his religion is only completed by observing seven matters"), the particle إنما restricts and confines the predicate to the subject, establishing that these seven matters are the exclusive and exhaustive means to the end.
24:37.topic: Al-Ghazali on constant remembrance of God and contemplative invocations, from 'Condemnation of Envy'

25:63.arabic: تعالى {وعباد الرحمن الذين يمشون على الأرض هونا وإذا خاطبهم الجاهلون قالوا سلاما} إلى آخر السورة من أشكل عليه حاله فليعرض نفسه على هذه الآيات فوجود جميع هذه الصفات علامة حسن الخلق وفقد جميعها علامة سوء الخلق ووجود بعضها دون بعض يدل على البعض دون البعض فليشتغل بتحصيل ما فقده وحفظ ما وجده وقد وصف رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم المؤمن بصفات كثيرة وأشار بجميعها إلى محاسن الأخلاق فقال المؤمن يحب لأخيه ما يحب لنفسه (1) وقال عليه السلام من كان يؤمن بالله واليوم الآخر فليكرم ضيفه (2) وقال صلى الله عليه وس
25:63.english: The foundational principle in this matter is that each person should abandon that which brings him joy from among the causes of this world. So whoever delights in wealth, or in status, or in acceptance during preaching, or in honor through judgeship and governance, or in the abundance of followers in teaching and benefitting others—he should first abandon that which brings him joy. For if he is prevented from something of that sort, and it is said to him: "Your reward is in the Hereafter," and his reward is not diminished by the prevention, yet he dislikes that and is pained by it—then he is among those who rejoice in the life of this world and are content with it, and that is destructive for him. Then, when he has abandoned the causes of joy, let him withdraw from people, let him seclude himself with his own soul, and let him watch over his heart so that it is occupied with nothing but the remembrance of Allah, the Exalted, and reflection upon Him. And let him lie in wait for whatever desire or whisper (shahwah wa waswās) appears in his soul, so that he may crush its substance whenever it emerges. For every whisper has a cause, and it does not vanish except by severing that cause and attachment. And let him persist in this for the remainder of his life, for striving has no end except death.
25:63.section_title_en: The Revival of the Religious Sciences — Section 630: The Signs of Good Character and the Path of Spiritual Striving
25:63.anchors:
- Root: جهد (j-h-d)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Exertion of one's utmost capacity; enduring hardship in pursuit of a goal.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-jihād is the soul's taking itself to the limit of its capacity while bearing difficulty; it is the means by which the lower self is subdued.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical toil and strain. Metaphorical: the striving of the soul against its passions, as in "ijtahada ra'yahu" (he exerted his judgment).
- Root: حسن (ḥ-s-n)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Beauty, goodness, and excellence in form and conduct.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): That which is desirable and pleasing—whether by reason, inclination, or sense; ḥusn al-khuluq is the beauty of the soul's inward disposition.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical beauty and adornment. Metaphorical: moral excellence, as in "ḥasuna khuluquhu" (his character became good).
- Root: خلق (kh-l-q)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Measuring, fashioning, and forming; also innate disposition and character.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Origination upon a just measure; for character, it denotes the soul's settled form and inward constitution.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: shaping and smoothing. Metaphorical: the created nature and moral temperament of a person.
- Sibawayh Rule: Restriction and Specification (al-ḥaṣr wa al-taqyīd bi-innamā) — The particle "innamā" restricts the predicate to the subject alone, as in the verse {«...»} "Innamā al-muʾminūna..." (The believers are only those...), which confines true faith to those possessing the enumerated attributes.
25:63.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Condemnation of Envy'

25:63.arabic: قال الله تعالى {وإذا خاطبهم الجاهلون قالوا سلاما} أي سلامة والألف بدل من الهاء ومعناه إنا سلمنا من إثمكم وأنتم سلمتم من شرنا فهذا ما أردنا أن نذكره من معاني الأخوة وشروطها وفوائدها فلنرجع في ذكر حقوقها ولوازمها وطرق القيام بحقها وأما الحريص على الدنيا فصحبته سم قاتل لأن الطباع مجبولة على التشبه والاقتداء بل الطبع يسرق من الطبع من حيث لا يدري صاحبه فمجالسة الحريص على الدنيا تحرك الحرص ومجالسة الزاهد تزهد في الدنيا فلذلك تكره صحبة طلاب الدنيا ويستحب صحبة الراغبين في الآخرة قال علي عليه السلام أحيو
25:63.english: I say: What we have mentioned regarding the observation of purposes and the observance of conditions with respect to them — that which is stipulated for companionship in the aims of this world is not what is stipulated for companionship in the Hereafter and brotherhood. For as Bishr said: "Brothers are three: a brother for your Hereafter, a brother for your worldly life, and a brother for your enjoyment of his company." And rarely do these purposes unite in a single person; rather, they are dispersed among a group, and so the conditions are necessarily dispersed among them as well.
25:63.section_title_en: The Revival of the Religious Sciences — Book on the Etiquette of Brotherhood: Section 416 — The Conditions of Brotherhood and Its Rights
25:63.anchors:
- Root: دنا (d-n-w)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Proximity in place, time, or rank; the near and the nearer.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الدنو: القرب بالذات، أو بالحكم" — proximity by essence or by judgment; used of spatial, temporal, and station-based nearness.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah) for physical nearness; metaphorical (Majaz) for nearness in rank, honor, or moral standing.
- Root: صحب (ṣ-ḥ-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The companion (al-ṣāḥib) is the one who accompanies another — whether a person, animal, place, or time; companionship by body is the origin and most frequent.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الصاحب: الملازم إنسانا كان أو حيوانا، أو مكانا، أو زمانا" — the companion is the constant attendant, whether by body or by care and concern.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah) for physical accompaniment; metaphorical (Majaz) for ownership or mastery — "هو صاحب مال وعلم" (he is a possessor of wealth and knowledge) — and for divine guardianship: "وصحبك الله تعالى" (may Allah accompany you).
- Root: ثمر (th-m-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Fruit of trees; the produce that is eaten.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الثمر اسم لكل ما يتطعم من أحمال الشجر" — fruit is the name for all that is savored from the burdens of trees; used metaphorically for benefit and outcome.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah) for botanical fruit; metaphorical (Majaz) for the knot at the tip of a whip — "سوط عظيم الثمرة" — and by extension, for any beneficial result or yield.
- Root: قصد (q-ṣ-d)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To intend, to aim, to head toward; the straight and middle path.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "القصد: استقامة الطريق" — moderation is the straightness of the way; commendable mean between two blameworthy extremes (extravagance and stinginess, recklessness and cowardice).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah) for physical direction and aiming; metaphorical (Majaz) for moral moderation — "قصد في الأمر إذا لم يجاوز فيه الحد" — and for the right path: "على قصد السبيل" (upon the straight way).
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — When the text employs restrictive particles or contrastive structures (e.g., "ليس ما يشترط... مشروطا"), the predicate is confined to the subject alone, demanding precise scoping of conditions across distinct categories.
25:63.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Condemnation of Envy'

26:202.arabic: عليه شيء مما يسرون وما يعلنون وحذرهم أن يأخذهم بغتة وهم لا يشعرون فقال {ما ينظرون إلا صيحة واحدة تأخذهم وهم يخصمون فلا يستطيعون توصية ولا إلى أهلهم يرجعون} والصلاة والسلام على محمد رسوله الذي يسير تحت لوائه النبيون وعلى آله وأصحابه الأئمة المهديين والسادة المرضيين صلاة يوازي عددها عدد ما كان من خلق الله وما سيكون ويحظى ببركتها الأولون والآخرون وسلم تسليما كثيرا أما بعد فإن الغضب شعلة نار اقتبست من نار الله الموقدة التي تطلع على الأفئدة وإنها لمستكنة في طي الفؤاد استكنان الجمر تحت الرماد ويستخرجه الكبر الدفي
26:202.english: In the name of God, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate. Praise be to God, upon whose pardon and mercy none rely except the hopeful, and from whose evil wrath and assault none fear except the fearful — He who gradually seizes His servants from whence they know not, and who has given dominion over them to their lusts, commanding them to abandon what they desire, and who has tried them with anger while charging them to swallow their rage in what provokes them. Then He surrounded them with hardships and pleasures, and granted them respite to see how they would act. He tested their love through them, to make known the truth of what they claim. He made known to them that nothing is hidden from Him of what they conceal or proclaim, and warned them lest He seize them suddenly while they are unaware. For He said: {«They await but a single blast which will seize them while they are disputing; so they will not be able to make a bequest, nor to their families will they return»} (Q. 36:49-50). And prayers and peace be upon Muhammad, His Messenger, beneath whose banner the prophets walk, and upon his family and companions — the rightly-guided imams and the pleasing masters — prayers whose number equals the number of what has been of God's creation and what will be, and by whose blessing the first and the last are favored — and abundant peace.
26:202.section_title_en: The Book of Condemnation of Anger, Spite, and Envy — Book Five of the Quarter of Destroyers from The Revival of the Religious Sciences
26:202.anchors:
- Root: غضب (ghadab)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root meaning of anger, rage, fury; the boiling and agitation of the blood
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance — when attributed to God, it means retribution (intiqām) alone, not emotional agitation; the Prophet described it as "a live coal kindled in the heart of the son of Adam"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal vs Metaphorical — literal anger is the boiling of the blood in living beings; metaphorical usage extends to inanimate things like fire and the reins of a mount
- Root: قلب (qalb)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The heart; also the turning, overturning, and transformation of a thing from one state to another
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance — the heart is so named for its constant turning (taqallub) and fluctuation between states; it is the seat of understanding and the locus of divine address
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal vs Metaphorical — literal is the physical organ; metaphorical is the subtle spiritual reality (laṭīfah rabbāniyyah) that is the locus of knowledge and will
- Root: حسد (hasad)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Envy; the wishing for removal of another's blessing
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance — envy is the desire for the removal of a blessing from one who deserves it, sometimes accompanied by striving to remove it; the believer envies (ghibṭah) while the hypocrite envies (hasad)
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal vs Metaphorical — "Envy consumes the body as fire consumes wood"; the envier is one who wishes evil upon the blessed
- Root: هلك (halak)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Perdition, destruction, ruin; death
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance — three senses: (1) loss of a thing from one's possession while it exists elsewhere, (2) corruption and dissolution of a thing, (3) death; the Quran uses it for all three
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal vs Metaphorical — literal is physical destruction; metaphorical is the ruin of one's religion and afterlife through spiritual corruption
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The permissibility of interposing elements between a preposition and its object when the intervening material constitutes a complete, meaningful unit, as in the Quranic pattern of extended periodic sentences that delay resolution for rhetorical effect.
26:202.topic: Al-Ghazali on purifying the character, moral diseases, and spiritual remedies, from 'Condemnation of Envy'

35:18.arabic: وحسناته فإنه من كسبه وغير مؤاخذ بسيئاته فإنه لا تزر وازرة وزر أخرى ولذلك قال تعالى ألحقنا بهم ذرياتهم وما ألتناهم من عملهم من شيء أي ما نقصناهم من أعمالهم وجعلنا أولادهم مزيدا في إحسانهم الوجه الرابع أن يموت الولد قبله فيكون له شفيعا فقد روي عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال إن الطفل يجر بأبويه إلى الجنة (5) وفي بعض الأخبار يأخذ بثوبه كما أنا الآن آخذ بثوبك (6) وقال أيضا صلى الله عليه وسلم إن المولود يقال ادخل الجنة فيقف على باب الجنة فيظل محبنطئا أي ممتلئا غيظا وغضبا ويقول لا أدخل الجنة إلا وأبواي معي فيقال أدخلوا
35:18.english: وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم: "لا يلقى الله أحد بذنب أعظم من جهالة أهله."
35:18.topic: Al-Ghazali on the journey of the soul, death, and the Hereafter, from 'Condemnation of Envy'

36:15.arabic: السبب الرابع التعجب كما أخبر الله تعالى عن الأمم السالفة إذ قالوا ما أنتم إلا بشر مثلنا وقالوا أنؤمن لبشرين مثلنا ولئن أطعتم بشرا مثلكم إنكم إذا لخاسرون فتعجبوا من أن يفوز برتبة الرسالة والوحي والقرب من الله تعالى بشر مثلهم فحسدوهم وأحبوا زوال النبوة عنهم جزعا أن يفضل عليهم من هو مثلهم في الخلقة لا عن قصد تكبر وطلب رياسة وتقدم عداوة أو سبب آخر من سائر الأسباب وقالوا متعجبين أبعث الله بشرا رسولا {وقالوا} لولا أنزل علينا الملائكة وقال تعالى أو عجبتم أن جاءكم ذكر من ربكم على رجل منكم الآية السبب الخامس الخوف من فوت المقاصد وذلك يختص بم
36:15.english: I say: God is Knower of what is in the breasts. {«إِنْ تَمْسَسْكُمْ حَسَنَةٌ تَسُؤْهُمْ»} — "If good touches you, it grieves them" {«وَدُّوا مَا عَنِتُّمْ قَدْ بَدَتِ الْبَغْضَاءُ مِنْ أَفْوَاهِهِمْ وَمَا تُخْفِي صُدُورُهُمْ أَكْبَرُ»} — "They wish for your hardship; hatred has already appeared from their mouths, and what their breasts conceal is greater." And envy (ḥasad), arising from hatred, may lead to contention, mutual fighting, and the spending of one's entire life in removing another's blessing through stratagems, slander, the tearing of veils, and whatever runs in that course.
36:15.section_title_en: The Revival of the Religious Sciences — Book on the Rebuke of the Self: The Seven Causes of Envy (Section 722)
36:15.anchors:
- Root: سبب (sabab)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The rope by which one climbs; every means by which one reaches a thing.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Every means by which one arrives at something is called a sabab" — thus the causes enumerated here are the psychological "ropes" by which envy ascends in the soul.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: a physical cord. Metaphorical: any linkage or occasion — here, the inward occasions (asbāb) that give rise to ḥasad.
- Root: بغض (bughḍ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Hatred, aversion of the heart.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The opposite of love (maḥabbah); a disposition of the heart toward another's harm.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: inner aversion. Metaphorical: its "appearance from the mouths" (Quranic) as outward speech betraying the concealed hatred.
- Root: كبر (kibr)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Greatness; pride; disdain.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Al-kabīr and al-ṣaghīr are relative terms" — pride is the claim to greatness relative to another, deeming oneself above him.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: bigness in stature or age. Metaphorical: "takabbara 'alayhi" — to deem oneself greater than another and refuse submission to him.
- Root: قصد (qaṣd)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Straightness of path; intending a goal.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Al-qaṣd: istiqāmat al-ṭarīq" — the straight road; also moderation between extremes.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: to head toward a place. Metaphorical: "maqāṣid" — the aims and objectives toward which one directs oneself; here, the worldly goals whose pursuit breeds rivalry and envy.
- Root: نزل (nazal)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To descend from a height; to alight.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Al-nuzūl fī al-aṣl huwa inḥiṭāṭ min 'uluww" — descent from above; the sending down of revelation.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: descending from a high place. Metaphorical: "anzala Allāhu al-kitāb" — God's sending down of the Quran; and "mā unzila" — what was revealed, as in the Quranic citation regarding the Qurashites' objection to revelation upon a mere human.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Causal Coordination (al-'aṭf al-sababī) — The enumeration of the seven causes proceeds by coordinated clauses (fa-... thumma ...), each introduced as an independent proposition linked by causation (sabab), requiring the translator to preserve the logical sequence of psychological motivations without collapsing them into one another.
