39:7.arabic: وحسناته فإنه من كسبه وغير مؤاخذ بسيئاته فإنه لا تزر وازرة وزر أخرى ولذلك قال تعالى ألحقنا بهم ذرياتهم وما ألتناهم من عملهم من شيء أي ما نقصناهم من أعمالهم وجعلنا أولادهم مزيدا في إحسانهم الوجه الرابع أن يموت الولد قبله فيكون له شفيعا فقد روي عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال إن الطفل يجر بأبويه إلى الجنة (5) وفي بعض الأخبار يأخذ بثوبه كما أنا الآن آخذ بثوبك (6) وقال أيضا صلى الله عليه وسلم إن المولود يقال ادخل الجنة فيقف على باب الجنة فيظل محبنطئا أي ممتلئا غيظا وغضبا ويقول لا أدخل الجنة إلا وأبواي معي فيقال أدخلوا
39:7.english: وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم: "لا يلقى الله أحد بذنب أعظم من جهالة أهله."
39:7.topic: Al-Ghazali on the journey of the soul, death, and the Hereafter, from 'Condemnation of Envy'

39:7.arabic: وقد قال الله تعالى ولا يرضى لعباده الكفر فكيف يكون الفناء بالإضافة إلى محبة الله وكراهته كالبقاء فإنه تعالى يقول ما ترددت في شيء كترددي في قبض روح عبدي المسلم هو يكره الموت وأنا أكره مساءته ولا بد له من الموت (1) فقوله لا بد له من الموت إشارة إلى سبق الإرادة والتقدير المذكور في قوله تعالى نحن قدرنا بينكم الموت وفي قوله تعالى الذي خلق الموت والحياة ولا مناقضة بين قوله تعالى نحن قدرنا بينكم الموت وبين قوله وأنا أكره مساءته ولكن إيضاح الحق في هذا يستدعي تحقيق معنى الإرادة والمحبة والكراهة وبيان حق
39:7.english: وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم: "لا يلقى الله أحد بذنب أعظم من جهالة أهله."
39:7.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Etiquette of Marriage'

41:34.arabic: وقوله {ادفع بالتي هي أحسن فإذا الذي بينك وبينه عداوة كأنه ولي حميم} وقوله {والكاظمين الغيظ والعافين عن الناس والله يحب المحسنين} وقوله {اجتنبوا كثيرا من الظن إن بعض الظن إثم ولا تجسسوا ولا يغتب بعضكم بعضا} ولما كسرت رباعيته وشج يوم أحد فجعل الدم يسيل على وجهه وهو يمسح الدم ويقول كيف يفلح قوم خضبوا وجه نبيهم بالدم وهو يدعوهم إلى ربهم (4) فأنزل الله تعالى {ليس لك من الأمر شيء} تأديبا له على ذلك وأمثال هذه التأديبات في القرآن لا تحصر وهو صلى الله عليه وسلم المقصود الأول بالتأديب والتهذيب ثم منه يشرق النور ع
41:34.english: The Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, was abundant in supplication and earnest entreaty, perpetually asking God Most High to adorn him with the beauties of refined conduct and the noble traits of character. Thus he would say in his supplication: "O God, beautify my outward form and my inward character (khuluqī wa-khalqī)" (1), and he would say: "O God, protect me from the reprehensible traits of character" (2). God Most High answered his supplication, fulfilling His word, Exalted is He: {«ادعوني أستجب لكم»} ["Call upon Me, I will answer you"] (Ghafir 40:60). So He sent down upon him the Qur'an and disciplined him through it, and his character became the Qur'an.
41:34.section_title_en: The Prophet's Discipline Through the Qur'an and the Invitation to Noble Moral Traits
41:34.anchors:
- Root: خلق (khalaqa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of measuring, fashioning, and creating upon a precise estimation; also used for innate disposition and character.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الخلق أصله: التقدير المستقيم" — the root denotes straight/right estimation; used for bringing something into being from nothing (ibdāʿ) and for the moral constitution of the soul.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): "خلق الخراز الأديم" — the leather-worker measures before cutting. Metaphorical (Majaz): "خلق الله الخلق: أوجده على تقدير أوجبته الحكمة" — God's creation is bringing into existence upon a measure required by wisdom; and "له خلق حسن" — he has beautiful character.
- Root: كرم (karuma)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Generosity, nobility, honor; the root of karīm (noble/generous) and makārim (noble traits).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الكرم إذا وصف الله تعالى به فهو اسم لإحسانه وإنعامه المتظاهر" — when attributed to God, it denotes His manifest beneficence; when attributed to man, it denotes praiseworthy morals and deeds that appear from him.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "كرم علينا فلان كرامة" — he showed generosity. Metaphorical: "قوم كرم" — a noble people; "كرم السحاب تكريما: جاد بمطره" — the cloud was generous with its rain.
- Root: أدب (adaba)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Refinement, discipline, cultivation of character; calling to a gathering (ma'dabah) — the root implies assembling and summoning toward excellence.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Discipline (ta'dīb) is the cultivation of the soul through praiseworthy traits and the restraint from blameworthy ones.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "أدبته تأديبا" — I disciplined him. Metaphorical: "أدبه الله" — God disciplined him, i.e., refined his character through divine instruction.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — "إنما أدبه القرآن" restricts the means of the Prophet's discipline exclusively to the Qur'an, affirming that the Qur'an alone was the sufficient and complete instrument of his moral formation.
41:34.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications, prayers, and their spiritual power, from 'Condemnation of Envy'

41:34.arabic: الله يحب المحسنين} وقوله {وليعفوا وليصفحوا ألا تحبون أن يغفر الله لكم} وقوله {ادفع بالتي هي أحسن فإذا الذي بينك وبينه عداوة كأنه ولي حميم} وقوله {والكاظمين الغيظ والعافين عن الناس والله يحب المحسنين} وقوله {اجتنبوا كثيرا من الظن إن بعض الظن إثم ولا تجسسوا ولا يغتب بعضكم بعضا} ولما كسرت رباعيته وشج يوم أحد فجعل الدم يسيل على وجهه وهو يمسح الدم ويقول كيف يفلح قوم خضبوا وجه نبيهم بالدم وهو يدعوهم إلى ربهم (4) فأنزل الله تعالى {ليس لك من الأمر شيء} تأديبا له على ذلك وأمثال هذه التأديبات في القرآن لا تحصر وهو صلى الله عليه وسلم المقصود الأول بالتأديب والتهذيب ثم منه يشرق النور
41:34.english: The Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, was abundant in supplication and earnest entreaty, perpetually asking God Most High to adorn him with the beauties of refined conduct and the noble traits of character. Thus he would say in his supplication: "O God, beautify my outward form and my inward character (khuluqī wa-khalqī)" (1), and he would say: "O God, protect me from the reprehensible traits of character" (2). God Most High answered his supplication, fulfilling His word, Exalted is He: {«ادعوني أستجب لكم»} ["Call upon Me, I will answer you"] (Ghafir 40:60). So He sent down upon him the Qur'an and disciplined him through it, and his character became the Qur'an.

42:14.arabic: بينهم} قيل في التفسير حسدا وقال تعالى {وما تفرقوا إلا من بعد ما جاءهم العلم بغيا بينهم} فأنزل الله العلم ليجمعهم ويؤلف بينهم على طاعته وأمرهم أن يتألفوا بالعلم فتحاسدوا واختلفوا إذ أراد كل واحد منهم أن ينفرد بالرياسة وقبول القول فرد بعضهم على بعض قال ابن عباس كانت اليهود قبل أن يبعث النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا قاتلوا قوما قالوا نسألك بالنبي الذي وعدتنا أن ترسله وبالكتاب الذي تنزله إلا ما نصرتنا (1) فكانوا ينصرون فلما جاء النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم من ولد إسماعيل عليه السلام عرفوه وكفروا به بعد معرفتهم إياه فقال تعالى {وكانوا من قبل ي
42:14.english: The Prophet ﷺ said: «إن المؤمن يغبط والمنافق يحسد» — "The believer aspires emulously, and the hypocrite envies."
42:14.section_title_en: On the Reality of Envy (Ḥasad) and Its Degrees — Section 720
42:14.anchors:
- Root: نعم (n-ʿ-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root meaning of "bounty, benefaction, grace" — that state of goodness and well-being bestowed.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "النعمة: الحالة الحسنة" — bounty is the excellent state/condition; it is the genus term applying to both little and much, as in {«وإن تعدوا نعمة الله لا تحصوها»} [Ibrahim: 34].
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): "جلت نعمة الله ونعماؤه" — bounty as actual bestowed good. Metaphorical (majāz): "خفت نعامتهم" — departure/removal, relevant to the envier's wish for the bounty's removal.
- Root: حسد (ḥ-s-d)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Envy — the desire for removal of another's good.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الحسد: تمني زوال نعمة من مستحق لها" — envy is wishing the removal of bounty from one who deserves it, sometimes accompanied by striving to effect its removal. Cited: «المؤمن يغبط والمنافق يحسد».
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "حسده على نعمة الله" — envying someone for God's bounty. "إن الحسد يأكل الجسد" — envy consumes the body.
- Root: نفس (n-f-s)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The self; also value, preciousness.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): النفس: الروح — the soul/spirit; also الذات (essence/self).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "شيء نفيس ومنفس" — a precious thing. Metaphorical: "دفق نفسه أي دمه" — poured out his self, i.e., his blood. From this root derives المنافسة (emulative competition) — the striving for precious things.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد (Restriction & Specification) — The definition of ḥasad is given as a restricted predication (ḥadd), delimiting its essential meaning: "كراهة النعمة وحب زوالها عن المنعم عليه" — the hatred of bounty and love of its removal from the one upon whom it is bestowed. This is a formal definition (ḥadd), not merely a lexical gloss.
42:14.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'Condemnation of Envy'

43:66.arabic: عليه شيء مما يسرون وما يعلنون وحذرهم أن يأخذهم بغتة وهم لا يشعرون فقال {ما ينظرون إلا صيحة واحدة تأخذهم وهم يخصمون فلا يستطيعون توصية ولا إلى أهلهم يرجعون} والصلاة والسلام على محمد رسوله الذي يسير تحت لوائه النبيون وعلى آله وأصحابه الأئمة المهديين والسادة المرضيين صلاة يوازي عددها عدد ما كان من خلق الله وما سيكون ويحظى ببركتها الأولون والآخرون وسلم تسليما كثيرا أما بعد فإن الغضب شعلة نار اقتبست من نار الله الموقدة التي تطلع على الأفئدة وإنها لمستكنة في طي الفؤاد استكنان الجمر تحت الرماد ويستخرجه الكبر الدفي
43:66.english: In the name of God, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate. Praise be to God, upon whose pardon and mercy none rely except the hopeful, and from whose evil wrath and assault none fear except the fearful — He who gradually seizes His servants from whence they know not, and who has given dominion over them to their lusts, commanding them to abandon what they desire, and who has tried them with anger while charging them to swallow their rage in what provokes them. Then He surrounded them with hardships and pleasures, and granted them respite to see how they would act. He tested their love through them, to make known the truth of what they claim. He made known to them that nothing is hidden from Him of what they conceal or proclaim, and warned them lest He seize them suddenly while they are unaware. For He said: {«They await but a single blast which will seize them while they are disputing; so they will not be able to make a bequest, nor to their families will they return»} (Q. 36:49-50). And prayers and peace be upon Muhammad, His Messenger, beneath whose banner the prophets walk, and upon his family and companions — the rightly-guided imams and the pleasing masters — prayers whose number equals the number of what has been of God's creation and what will be, and by whose blessing the first and the last are favored — and abundant peace.
43:66.section_title_en: The Book of Condemnation of Anger, Spite, and Envy — Book Five of the Quarter of Destroyers from The Revival of the Religious Sciences
43:66.anchors:
- Root: غضب (ghadab)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root meaning of anger, rage, fury; the boiling and agitation of the blood
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance — when attributed to God, it means retribution (intiqām) alone, not emotional agitation; the Prophet described it as "a live coal kindled in the heart of the son of Adam"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal vs Metaphorical — literal anger is the boiling of the blood in living beings; metaphorical usage extends to inanimate things like fire and the reins of a mount
- Root: قلب (qalb)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The heart; also the turning, overturning, and transformation of a thing from one state to another
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance — the heart is so named for its constant turning (taqallub) and fluctuation between states; it is the seat of understanding and the locus of divine address
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal vs Metaphorical — literal is the physical organ; metaphorical is the subtle spiritual reality (laṭīfah rabbāniyyah) that is the locus of knowledge and will
- Root: حسد (hasad)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Envy; the wishing for removal of another's blessing
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance — envy is the desire for the removal of a blessing from one who deserves it, sometimes accompanied by striving to remove it; the believer envies (ghibṭah) while the hypocrite envies (hasad)
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal vs Metaphorical — "Envy consumes the body as fire consumes wood"; the envier is one who wishes evil upon the blessed
- Root: هلك (halak)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Perdition, destruction, ruin; death
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance — three senses: (1) loss of a thing from one's possession while it exists elsewhere, (2) corruption and dissolution of a thing, (3) death; the Quran uses it for all three
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal vs Metaphorical — literal is physical destruction; metaphorical is the ruin of one's religion and afterlife through spiritual corruption
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The permissibility of interposing elements between a preposition and its object when the intervening material constitutes a complete, meaningful unit, as in the Quranic pattern of extended periodic sentences that delay resolution for rhetorical effect.
43:66.topic: Al-Ghazali on purifying the character, moral diseases, and spiritual remedies, from 'Condemnation of Envy'

48:26.arabic: قال الله تعالى {إذ جعل الذين كفروا في قلوبهم الحمية حمية الجاهلية فأنزل الله سكينته على رسوله وعلى}
48:26.english: In the name of God, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate. Praise be to God, upon whose pardon and mercy none rely except the hopeful, and from whose evil wrath and assault none fear except the fearful — He who gradually seizes His servants from whence they know not, and who has given dominion over them to their lusts, commanding them to abandon what they desire, and who has tried them with anger while charging them to swallow their rage in what provokes them. Then He surrounded them with hardships and pleasures, and granted them respite to see how they would act. He tested their love through them, to make known the truth of what they claim. He made known to them that nothing is hidden from Him of what they conceal or proclaim, and warned them lest He seize them suddenly while they are unaware. For He said: {«They await but a single blast which will seize them while they are disputing; so they will not be able to make a bequest, nor to their families will they return»} (Q. 36:49-50). And prayers and peace be upon Muhammad, His Messenger, beneath whose banner the prophets walk, and upon his family and companions — the rightly-guided imams and the pleasing masters — prayers whose number equals the number of what has been of God's creation and what will be, and by whose blessing the first and the last are favored — and abundant peace.
48:26.section_title_en: The Book of Condemnation of Anger, Spite, and Envy — Book Five of the Quarter of Destroyers from The Revival of the Religious Sciences
48:26.anchors:
- Root: غضب (ghadab)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root meaning of anger, rage, fury; the boiling and agitation of the blood
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance — when attributed to God, it means retribution (intiqām) alone, not emotional agitation; the Prophet described it as "a live coal kindled in the heart of the son of Adam"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal vs Metaphorical — literal anger is the boiling of the blood in living beings; metaphorical usage extends to inanimate things like fire and the reins of a mount
- Root: قلب (qalb)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The heart; also the turning, overturning, and transformation of a thing from one state to another
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance — the heart is so named for its constant turning (taqallub) and fluctuation between states; it is the seat of understanding and the locus of divine address
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal vs Metaphorical — literal is the physical organ; metaphorical is the subtle spiritual reality (laṭīfah rabbāniyyah) that is the locus of knowledge and will
- Root: حسد (hasad)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Envy; the wishing for removal of another's blessing
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance — envy is the desire for the removal of a blessing from one who deserves it, sometimes accompanied by striving to remove it; the believer envies (ghibṭah) while the hypocrite envies (hasad)
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal vs Metaphorical — "Envy consumes the body as fire consumes wood"; the envier is one who wishes evil upon the blessed
- Root: هلك (halak)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Perdition, destruction, ruin; death
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance — three senses: (1) loss of a thing from one's possession while it exists elsewhere, (2) corruption and dissolution of a thing, (3) death; the Quran uses it for all three
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal vs Metaphorical — literal is physical destruction; metaphorical is the ruin of one's religion and afterlife through spiritual corruption
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The permissibility of interposing elements between a preposition and its object when the intervening material constitutes a complete, meaningful unit, as in the Quranic pattern of extended periodic sentences that delay resolution for rhetorical effect.
48:26.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications, prayers, and their spiritual power, from 'Condemnation of Envy'

48:29.arabic: واقترب وقال عز وجل سيماهم في وجوههم من أثر السجود فقيل هو ما يلتصق بوجوههم من الأرض عند السجود وقيل هو نور الخشوع فإنه يشرق من الباطن على الظاهر وهو الأصح وقيل هي الغرر التي تكون في وجوههم يوم القيامة من أثر الوضوء وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا قرأ ابن آدم السجدة فسجد اعتزل الشيطان يبكي ويقول يا ويلاه أمر هذا بالسجود فسجد فله الجنة وأمرت أنا بالسجود فعصيت فلي النار (6) ويروى عن علي بن عبد الله بن عباس أنه كان يسجد في كل يوم ألف سجدة وكانوا يسمونه السجاد ويروى أن عمر بن عبد العزيز رضي ا
48:29.english: The Messenger of God — peace be upon him — said: "The servant draws near to God through nothing better than a hidden prostration." (2) And the Messenger of God — peace be upon him — said: "No Muslim prostrates to God with a single prostration, except that God raises him by it a degree and removes from him by it a sin." (3) And it is related that a man said to the Messenger of God — peace be upon him: "Supplicate God to make me among the people of your intercession and to grant me your companionship in Paradise." He — peace be upon him — said: "Help me by multiplying prostration." (4) And it was said: "The closest that the servant is to God — Mighty and Majestic — is when he is prostrating." (5) And this is the meaning of His saying — Glorified and Exalted: {«واسجد واقترب»} ("Prostrate and draw near") (Q. 96:19). And He — Glorified and Exalted — said: {«سيماهم في وجوههم من أثر السجود»} ("Their mark is on their faces from the trace of prostration") (Q. 48:29). It was said: "It is the dust that clings to their faces during prostration." And it was said: "It is the light of reverence (nūr al-khushūʿ), for it radiates from the inward to the outward" — and this is the most sound opinion. And it was said: "It is the radiant whiteness (al-ghurrah) that will be on their faces on the Day of Resurrection from the trace of ablution." And he — peace be upon him — said: "When the son of Adam recites the verse of prostration and then prostrates, Satan withdraws, weeping and saying: 'Woe to me! This one was commanded to prostrate, and he prostrated, so Paradise is his. And I was commanded to prostrate, but I disobeyed, so the Fire is mine.'" (6)
48:29.anchors:
- Root: سجد (S-J-D)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root denotes bowing, lowering oneself, and touching the ground in humility.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Prostration (sujūd) is of two types: voluntary (ikhtiyārī), exclusive to humans and meriting reward, and compelled (taskhīrī), shared by all creation. The Prophet's statement "a hidden prostration" (sujūd khafī) points to the voluntary type performed in secret, maximizing sincerity and divine proximity.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) usage is the physical act of placing the forehead on the ground in worship. Metaphorical (majāz) usage extends to any act of humble submission, such as a tree leaning or a ship yielding to the wind. Here, the term is literal, but its virtue is tied to the spiritual state of khushūʿ (reverent humility).
- Root: عبد (ʿ-B-D)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Root denotes servitude, obedience, and worship.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): ʿIbādah is the utmost degree of self-abasement (tadhallul), rendered exclusively to God due to His ultimate beneficence. The ḥadīth "the servant draws near to God" (yataqarrab al-ʿabd) frames prostration as the servant's act of voluntary worship (ʿibādah ikhtiyāriyyah), distinct from compelled submission.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal usage is the state of being a slave (ʿabd). Metaphorically, it implies total devotion and self-surrender, as in "he enslaved me" (taʿabbadanī). In this context, the servant (al-ʿabd) is the believing human who freely chooses worship.
- Root: قرب (Q-R-B)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Root denotes proximity, nearness, and approach.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Proximity (qurb) applies to place, time, relation, and — crucially here — to divine favor and honor (al-ḥaẓwah wa al-riʿāyah). The verse {«واسجد واقترب»} ("Prostrate and draw near") (Q. 96:19) indicates that prostration is the means to spiritual nearness to God, not physical closeness.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal usage is spatial nearness. Metaphorical usage is drawing near in rank or favor, as in "he approached a matter" (qarraba amran). Here, the servant's proximity to God is metaphorical — a station of honor and divine acceptance achieved through the act of prostration.
- Root: وجل (W-J-L)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Root denotes fear, trembling, and apprehension.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Wajal is the inward sensation of fear, as in {«الذين إذا ذكر الله وجلت قلوبهم»} ("those whose hearts tremble when God is mentioned") (Q. 8:2). The "light of khushūʿ" (nūr al-khushūʿ) mentioned in the exegesis of the prostration mark is an outward manifestation of this inward awe.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal usage is the feeling of fear. Metaphorically, it can denote a profound reverence that transforms the believer's demeanor. The "mark on the face" (sīmā) is interpreted as this radiant awe shining from within.
- Sibawayh Rule: Prepositional Interposition (al-faṣl bayna al-jār wa al-majrūr) — The construction "أقرب ما يكون العبد من الله تعالى أن يكون ساجدا" (the closest the servant is to God is when he is prostrating) employs a nominal sentence with an implied temporal clause, where the predicate (an yakūna sājidan) is delayed for rhetorical emphasis, highlighting the state of prostration as the pinnacle of proximity.
48:29.topic: Al-Ghazali on the journey of the soul, death, and the Hereafter, from 'Mysteries of Prayer'

48:29.arabic: الدين وأصفاها في اليقين وأرقها على الإخوان وهو إشارة إلى قوله تعالى أشداء على الكفار رحماء بينهم وقوله تعالى مثل نوره كمشكاة فيها مصباح قال أبي بن كعب رضي الله عنه معناه مثل نور المؤمن وقلبه وقوله تعالى أو كظلمات في بحر لجى مثل قلب المنافق وقال زيد بن أسلم في قوله تعالى في لوح محفوظ وهو قلب المؤمن وقال سهل مثل القلب والصدر مثل العرش والكرسي فهذه أمثلة القلب
48:29.english: Know that just as the rational person does not know the necessary sciences (al-ʿulūm al-ḍarūriyyah) nor what distinguishes the state of the rational one from what he has acquired of the theoretical sciences, so too does the rational person not know what Allah has opened for His friends (awliyāʾ) and His prophets of the prerogatives of His gentleness (luṭf) and mercy. Whatever mercy Allah opens to people, none can withhold it. This mercy is dispensed by the decree of bounty and generosity from Allah, Glorified and Exalted, not grudged to anyone. But it only appears in hearts that expose themselves to the wafts of the mercy of Allah, Exalted — as he, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Indeed, your Lord has, in the days of your time, wafts of mercy — so expose yourselves to them." (1) Hadith: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: "Long has been the yearning of the righteous for My meeting" — the hadith. I found no source for it except that the author of al-Firdaws transmitted it from the hadith of Abū al-Dardāʾ, and his son did not mention for it in the Musnad of al-Firdaws an isnād.
48:29.section_title_en: The Revival of the Religious Sciences — Section 579: The Human's Distinguishing Property is Knowledge and Wisdom; The Heart as the Seat of the King
48:29.anchors:
- Root: قلب (q-l-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of turning over, revolving, and transformation from one state to another; the heart as that which is constantly turning and fluctuating.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The heart (qalb) is so named for its constant turning (taqallub) between states; it is the seat of perception and understanding, the faculty by which one grasps realities.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: turning a thing over. Metaphorical: the heart as the seat of understanding and the center of the human kingdom, that which governs and directs the faculties.
- Root: علم (ʿ-l-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Knowledge, perception, and certainty; the mark or trace by which a thing is known.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Knowledge is the apprehension of a thing as it truly is; it is the distinguishing property of the human being and the purpose of his creation.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: knowing. Metaphorical: the light by which the heart perceives realities, the noblest of which is knowledge of God.
- Root: ملك (m-l-k)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Possession, sovereignty, and dominion; a king who rules over a domain.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The king is one who possesses authority and commands; the heart is the king of the human body, ruling over its faculties.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: a king. Metaphorical: the heart as the sovereign of the human kingdom, with the faculties as its subjects, messengers, and servants.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب التشبيه والتمثيل (The Chapter of Simile and Analogy) — The use of extended analogies (tamthīl) to clarify abstract realities through concrete images, where the comparison is drawn between the relations of parts, not merely individual attributes.
48:29.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Condemnation of Envy'

53:36.arabic: عليه شاهدين إبراهيم وموسى ثم تلا أم لم ينبأ بما في صحف موسى وإبراهيم الذي وفى أن لا تزر وازرة وزر أخرى فقال زياد خلوا سبيله هذا رجل قد لقن حجته وقيل مكتوب في الإنجيل من استغفر لمن ظلمه فقد هزم الشيطان فضيلة الرفق اعلم أن الرفق محمود ويضاده العنف والحدة والعنف نتيجة الغضب والفظاظة والرفق واللين نتيجة حسن
53:36.english: A man was brought to Hishām concerning whom word had reached him. When he was made to stand before him, he began to speak in his own defense. Hishām said to him: You speak as well? The man said: O Commander of the Faithful, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: {«يَوْمَ تَأْتِي كُلُّ نَفْسٍ تُجَادِلُ عَنْ نَفْسِهَا»} — "The Day when every soul will come disputing on its own behalf." Shall we dispute before Allah the Exalted, and not speak a word before you? Hishām said: Yes, woe to you — speak.
53:36.section_title_en: ** Section 715 — On the Virtue of Forbearance (al-Ḥilm) and Gentleness (al-Rifq)
53:36.anchors:
**

- **Root: عفو (ʿ-F-W)**
  - *Lisan / Ayn:* Al-ʿAfw is the effacing and obliteration of the trace of a thing; to pardon is to efface the trace of the offense entirely.
  - *Al-Raghib (Mufradat):* Al-ʿAfw is the erasure of the sin such that no consequence remains — it is the highest form of forgiveness, surpassing al-ghufrān which veils but does not necessarily efface.
  - *Al-Zamakhshari (Asas):* Literal: "عفا الأثر" — the trace was effaced. Metaphorical: pardon as the effacing of the offense's consequence, as in "عفا عن ذنبه."

- **Root: حلم (Ḥ-L-M)**
  - *Lisan / Ayn:* Al-Ḥilm is forbearance, clemency, and the restraint of the soul from agitation upon provocation.
  - *Al-Raghib (Mufradat):* Al-Ḥilm is the soul's composure and its withholding from haste; it is a virtue opposed to al-ṭaysh (levity) and al-jahl (foolishness) — not ignorance, but the deliberate restraint of passion.
  - *Al-Zamakhshari (Asas):* Literal: dreams (aḥlām) share the root — the state of being unmoved. Metaphorical: the forbearing man (ḥalīm) whose soul does not stir toward vengeance when provoked.

- **Root: رفق (R-F-Q)**
  - *Lisan / Ayn:* Al-Rifq is gentleness, lenity, and the opposite of violence (al-ʿunf).
  - *Al-Raghib (Mufradat):* Al-Rifq is the disposition toward ease and gentleness in all affairs; it is praised by the Law and is a quality of the prophets.
  - *Al-Zamakhshari (Asas):* Literal: "رفق به" — he was gentle with him. Metaphorical: gentleness in conduct as a mode of spiritual excellence.

- **Root: صفح (Ṣ-F-Ḥ)**
  - *Lisan / Ayn:* Al-Ṣafḥ is turning away from an offense and meeting it with a generous countenance; from ṣafḥah (cheek/face) — to turn one's face away from the wrong.
  - *Al-Raghib (Mufradat):* Al-Ṣafḥ is the overlooking of the offense combined with graciousness — it is more than mere pardon, for it includes magnanimity (al-Ifḍāl).
  - *Al-Zamakhshari (Asas):* Literal: "صفح عنه" — he turned his face away from him. Metaphorical: to turn away from requital and instead bestow favor.

- **Sibawayh Rule:** *Bāb al-Ḥaṣr wa al-Taqyīd bi-innamā* (Restriction & Focused Predication) — "إنما أعطى ما أعطى بأربع خصال" employs innamā to restrict the cause of the gift to four qualities, and "ليس الحليم من ظلم فحلم حتى إذا قدر انتقم" uses laysa to negate the predicate entirely before affirming the true definition.

66:9.arabic: وقال لنبيه صلى الله عليه وسلم {جاهد الكفار والمنافقين واغلظ عليهم} الآية وإنما الغلظة والشدة من آثار قوة الحمية وهو الغضب وأما الإفراط فهو أن تغلب هذه الصفة حتى تخرج عن سياسة العقل والدين وطاعته ولا يبقى للمرء معها بصيرة ونظر وفكرة ولا اختيار بل يصير في صورة المضطر وسبب غلبته أمور غريزية وأمور اعتيادية فرب إنسان هو بالفطرة مستعد لسرعة الغضب حتى كأن صورته في الفطرة صورة غضبان ويعين على ذلك حرارة مزاج القلب لأن الغضب من النار (1) كما قال صلى الله عليه وسلم وإنما برودة المزاج تطفئه وتكسر سورته وأما الأسباب الاعتياد
66:9.english: As for deficiency: it is the loss of this power or its weakness. This is blameworthy, and it is of such a one that it is said: "He has no protective zeal (ḥamiyyah)." For this reason al-Shāfiʿī — may God have mercy on him — said: "Whoever is provoked to anger and does not become angry is a donkey." Whoever loses the power of anger and protective zeal entirely is utterly deficient. God — exalted be He — described the Companions of the Prophet — peace be upon him — with severity and protective zeal, saying: {«أشداء على الكفار رحماء بينهم»} "Severe against the disbelievers, merciful among themselves" (Q 48:29). And He said to His Prophet — peace be upon him: {«جاهد الكفار والمنافقين واغلظ عليهم»} "Strive against the disbelievers and the hypocrites and be harsh with them" (Q 9:73) — the verse. Harshness and severity are but effects of the power of protective zeal, which is anger.
66:9.section_title_en: The Reality of Anger (Ghaḍab) and Its Degrees — Book 21, Section 703
66:9.anchors:
- Root: غضب (Ghaḍab)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root denotes anger, rage, fury; the surge of blood in the heart seeking vengeance.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الغضب: ثوران دم القلب إرادة الانتقام" — when attributed to God, it means solely His retribution, not an emotional state.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): "غضبت لفلان" (anger for the living); Metaphorical (majāz): "غضبت به" (anger over the dead), and the poetic extension to inanimate objects like fire or reins.
- Root: نفس (Nafs)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Self, soul, spirit; the vital principle.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The soul as the seat of blameworthy traits when unrestrained; its purification is the goal of spiritual struggle.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the self; Metaphorical: "دفق نفسه" (spilled his blood/life).
- Root: قلب (Qalb)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The heart; to turn over, to flip.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "قلب الشيء: تصريفه وصرفه عن وجه إلى وجه" — the heart is so named for its constant fluctuation and turning.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical turning; Metaphorical: the heart as the seat of intellect and spiritual perception, which anger overturns and blinds.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد (Restriction & Focused Predication) — Used to distinguish the three degrees of anger (deficiency, excess, moderation) as mutually exclusive categories.
66:9.topic: Al-Ghazali on purifying the character, moral diseases, and spiritual remedies, from 'Condemnation of Envy'

104:6.arabic: أما بعد فإن الغضب شعلة نار اقتبست من نار الله الموقدة التي تطلع على الأفئدة وإنها لمستكنة في طي الفؤاد استكنان الجمر تحت الرماد ويستخرجه الكبر الدفين في قلب كل جبار عنيد كاستخراج الحجر النار من الحديد وقد انكشف للناظرين بنور اليقين أن الإنسان ينزع منه عرق إلى الشيطان اللعين فمن استفزته نار الغضب فقد قويت فيه قرابة الشيطان حيث قال {خلقتني من نار وخلقته من طين} فإن شأن الطين السكون والوقار وشأن النار التلظي والاستعار والحركة والاضطراب ومن نتائج الغضب الحقد والحسد وبهما هلك من هلك وفسد من فسد ومفيضهما مضغة إذا صلحت صلح معها س
104:6.english: In the name of God, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate. Praise be to God, upon whose pardon and mercy none rely except the hopeful, and from whose evil wrath and assault none fear except the fearful — He who gradually seizes His servants from whence they know not, and who has given dominion over them to their lusts, commanding them to abandon what they desire, and who has tried them with anger while charging them to swallow their rage in what provokes them. Then He surrounded them with hardships and pleasures, and granted them respite to see how they would act. He tested their love through them, to make known the truth of what they claim. He made known to them that nothing is hidden from Him of what they conceal or proclaim, and warned them lest He seize them suddenly while they are unaware. For He said: {«They await but a single blast which will seize them while they are disputing; so they will not be able to make a bequest, nor to their families will they return»} (Q. 36:49-50). And prayers and peace be upon Muhammad, His Messenger, beneath whose banner the prophets walk, and upon his family and companions — the rightly-guided imams and the pleasing masters — prayers whose number equals the number of what has been of God's creation and what will be, and by whose blessing the first and the last are favored — and abundant peace.
104:6.section_title_en: The Book of Condemnation of Anger, Spite, and Envy — Book Five of the Quarter of Destroyers from The Revival of the Religious Sciences
104:6.anchors:
- Root: غضب (ghadab)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root meaning of anger, rage, fury; the boiling and agitation of the blood
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance — when attributed to God, it means retribution (intiqām) alone, not emotional agitation; the Prophet described it as "a live coal kindled in the heart of the son of Adam"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal vs Metaphorical — literal anger is the boiling of the blood in living beings; metaphorical usage extends to inanimate things like fire and the reins of a mount
- Root: قلب (qalb)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The heart; also the turning, overturning, and transformation of a thing from one state to another
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance — the heart is so named for its constant turning (taqallub) and fluctuation between states; it is the seat of understanding and the locus of divine address
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal vs Metaphorical — literal is the physical organ; metaphorical is the subtle spiritual reality (laṭīfah rabbāniyyah) that is the locus of knowledge and will
- Root: حسد (hasad)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Envy; the wishing for removal of another's blessing
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance — envy is the desire for the removal of a blessing from one who deserves it, sometimes accompanied by striving to remove it; the believer envies (ghibṭah) while the hypocrite envies (hasad)
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal vs Metaphorical — "Envy consumes the body as fire consumes wood"; the envier is one who wishes evil upon the blessed
- Root: هلك (halak)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Perdition, destruction, ruin; death
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance — three senses: (1) loss of a thing from one's possession while it exists elsewhere, (2) corruption and dissolution of a thing, (3) death; the Quran uses it for all three
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal vs Metaphorical — literal is physical destruction; metaphorical is the ruin of one's religion and afterlife through spiritual corruption
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The permissibility of interposing elements between a preposition and its object when the intervening material constitutes a complete, meaningful unit, as in the Quranic pattern of extended periodic sentences that delay resolution for rhetorical effect.

2:267.arabic: وقد قال الله تعالى يا أيها الذين آمنوا أنفقوا من طيبات ما كسبتم ومما أخرجنا لكم من الأرض ولا تيمموا الخبيث منه تنفقون ولستم بآخذيه إلا أن تغمضوا فيه أي لا تأخذوه إلا مع كراهية وحياء وهو معنى الإغماض فلا تؤثروا به ربكم وفي الخبر سبق درهم مائة ألف درهم (3) وذلك بأن يخرجه الإنسان وهو من أحل ماله وأجوده فيصدر ذلك عن الرضا والفرح بالبذل وقد يخرج مائة ألف درهم مما يكره من ماله فيدل ذلك على أنه ليس يؤثر الله عز وجل بشيء مما يحبه وبذلك ذم الله تعالى قوما جعلوا لله ما يكرهون فقال تعالى ويجعلون لله ما يكرهون وتصف ألسنتهم الكذب أن لهم الحسنى لا وقف بعض القراء على النفي تكذيبا لهم ثم ابتدأ وقا
2:267.english: The heart is not treated save with the compound electuary (maʿjūn) of knowledge and works. And this condition among the conditions of almsgiving runs in the same course as humility (al-khushūʿ) runs in the prayer. This is established by his saying — may Allah bless him and grant him peace: "A man has nothing of his prayer save that of which he was conscious." And this is like his saying — may Allah bless him and grant him peace: "Allah does not accept the charity of the one who bestows it with reproach (al-mannān)." And like His saying — Exalted is He: {«لا تبطلوا صدقاتكم بالمن والأذى»} ("Do not nullify your charities by reproach and injury"). As for the legal opinion (fatwā) of the jurist that the alms fall in their proper place and that one's liability is discharged without this condition — that is another discussion, and we have already pointed to its meaning in the Book of Prayer.
2:267.section_title_en: The Inner Conditions of Charity — Section 175 (From The Revival of the Religious Sciences, Book of the Mysteries of Almsgiving)
2:267.anchors:
- Root: قلب (q-l-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "To turn, overturn, transform a thing from one state to another; to rotate, to flip"
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "قلب الشيء: تصريفه وصرفه عن وجه إلى وجه" — the heart is so named because of its constant turning and transformation between states
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "قلب الشيء قلبا: حوله عن وجهه" (to turn a thing from its face). Metaphorical: "رجل قلب حول: يقلب الأمور ويحتال" — one who turns matters over and manages them; "قلبوا لك الأمور" (they turned matters against you)
- Root: وجل (w-j-l)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "Fear, dread, apprehension that strikes the heart"
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الوجل: استشعار الخوف" — the sensing of fear; cited in {«إنما المؤمنون الذين إذا ذكر الله وجلت قلوبهم»}
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "رجل وجل، وقوم وجال" — a fearful man, a fearful people; "وفي قلبه وجل" — in his heart is dread
- Root: عجب (ʿ-j-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "Wonder, amazement; self-admiration, vanity"
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Self-admiration (al-ʿujb) is a destructive spiritual ailment that nullifies deeds
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: wonder at something extraordinary. Metaphorical: self-conceit regarding one's own acts of obedience
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد (Restriction & Focused Predication) — governing the precise limitation of general categories (al-ṣifāt al-khāṣṣah within al-aṣnāf al-thamāniyyah) and the conditional structure of acceptance

2:271.arabic: تطفىء غضب الرب (6) وقال تعالى وإن تخفوها وتؤتوها الفقراء فهو خير لكم وفائدة الإخفاء الخلاص من آفات الرياء والسمعة فقد قال صلى الله عليه وسلم لا يقبل الله من مسمع ولا مراء ولا منان والمتحدث بصدقته يطلب السمعة والمعطي في ملأ من الناس يبغي الرياء والإخفاء والسكوت هو المخلص منه (7) وقد بالغ في فضل الإخفاء جماعة حتى اجتهدوا أن لا يعرف القابض المعطي فكان بعضهم يلقيه في يد أعمى وبعضهم يلقيه في طريق الفقير وفي موضع جلوسه حيث يراه ولا يرى المعطي وبعضهم كان يصره في ثوب الفقير وهو نائم وبعضهم كان يوصل إلى يد الفقير على يد
2:271.english: A group of the Followers (tābiʿūn) held that there are rights in wealth beyond the zakat — among them al-Nakhaʿī, al-Shaʿbī, ʿAṭāʾ, and Mujāhid. Al-Shaʿbī said, after being asked, "Is there a right in wealth beyond the zakat?": "Yes. Have you not heard His saying — mighty and majestic is He: {«وَآتَى الْمَالَ عَلَىٰ حُبِّهِ ذَوِي الْقُرْبَىٰ»} 'And gives wealth, despite his love for it, to relatives' (2:177)?" They also adduced His saying — mighty and majestic is He: {«وَمِمَّا رَزَقْنَاهُمْ يُنفِقُونَ»} 'And from what We have provided them, they spend' (2:3), and His saying — exalted is He: {«وَأَنفِقُوا مِن مَّا رَزَقْنَاكُم»} 'And spend from what We have provided you' (2:254). They claimed that this is not abrogated by the verse of zakat; rather, it falls within the right of a Muslim upon a Muslim. Its meaning is that it is incumbent upon the affluent one, whenever he finds a needy person, to remove his need — over and above the zakat wealth.
2:271.section_title_en: The Second Division: Those Who Guard Their Wealth Awaiting Seasons of Need — On the Inner Meanings of Zakat (Section 173)
2:271.anchors:
- Root: ف-ق-ر (f-q-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of neediness, poverty; the hollow of the spine (faqār) — that which is structurally weak and dependent.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Poverty (faqr) has four senses: (1) essential neediness before Allah, universal to all creatures; (2) lack of possessions; (3) [the third and fourth senses as elaborated in the full lexicon entry].
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (haqīqah): one who lacks wealth. Metaphorical (majāz): "the poverty of speech" (fuqar al-kalām) — its subtle points, likened to ornaments shaped like vertebrae.
- Root: ص-د-ق (ṣ-d-q)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Truthfulness in speech; giving (ṣadaqah) as the outward verification of inward faith.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Ṣidq (truth) and kidhb (falsehood) are originally in speech — statement of what is, or what will be. By extension, ṣadaqah is that which verifies the truthfulness of one's claim to faith through expenditure.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: truthful speech. Metaphorical: "a horse with true running" (dhū miṣdaq fī al-jary) — that which verifies its excellence through action. Thus charity verifies the giver's sincerity.
- Root: م-ن-ن (m-n-n)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The bestowal of a favor; reproaching another by reminding them of one's gift (al-mann).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): [As elaborated in the full lexicon entry on the heart's self-perception of superiority over the recipient.]
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: a heavy weight; a favor. Metaphorical: the act of counting one's favors over another — a corrosion of the gift's value.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد (Restriction & Specification) — governing the precise scope of obligation (farḍ kifāyah) versus supererogatory merit (faḍl), and the restriction of "rights in wealth" (ḥuqūq fī al-māl) beyond the obligatory zakat.

2:271.arabic: الرياء فقد قال الله عز وجل إن تبدوا الصدقات فنعما هي وذلك حيث يقتضي الحال الإبداء إما للاقتداء وإما لأن السائل إنما سأل على ملأ من الناس فلا ينبغي أن يترك التصدق خيفة من الرياء في الإظهار بل ينبغي أن يتصدق ويحفظ سره عن الرياء بقدر الإمكان وهذا لأن في الإظهار محذورا ثالثا سوى المن والرياء وهو هتك ستر الفقير فإنه ربما يتأذى بأن يرى في صورة المحتاج فمن أظهر السؤال فهو الذي هتك ستر نفسه فلا يحذر هذا المعنى في إظهاره وهو كإظهار الفسق على من تستر به فإنه محظور والتجسس فيه والاعتياد بذكره منهي عنه فأم
2:271.english: A group of the Followers (tābiʿūn) held that there are rights in wealth beyond the zakat — among them al-Nakhaʿī, al-Shaʿbī, ʿAṭāʾ, and Mujāhid. Al-Shaʿbī said, after being asked, "Is there a right in wealth beyond the zakat?": "Yes. Have you not heard His saying — mighty and majestic is He: {«وَآتَى الْمَالَ عَلَىٰ حُبِّهِ ذَوِي الْقُرْبَىٰ»} 'And gives wealth, despite his love for it, to relatives' (2:177)?" They also adduced His saying — mighty and majestic is He: {«وَمِمَّا رَزَقْنَاهُمْ يُنفِقُونَ»} 'And from what We have provided them, they spend' (2:3), and His saying — exalted is He: {«وَأَنفِقُوا مِن مَّا رَزَقْنَاكُم»} 'And spend from what We have provided you' (2:254). They claimed that this is not abrogated by the verse of zakat; rather, it falls within the right of a Muslim upon a Muslim. Its meaning is that it is incumbent upon the affluent one, whenever he finds a needy person, to remove his need — over and above the zakat wealth.
2:271.section_title_en: The Second Division: Those Who Guard Their Wealth Awaiting Seasons of Need — On the Inner Meanings of Zakat (Section 173)
2:271.anchors:
- Root: ف-ق-ر (f-q-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of neediness, poverty; the hollow of the spine (faqār) — that which is structurally weak and dependent.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Poverty (faqr) has four senses: (1) essential neediness before Allah, universal to all creatures; (2) lack of possessions; (3) [the third and fourth senses as elaborated in the full lexicon entry].
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (haqīqah): one who lacks wealth. Metaphorical (majāz): "the poverty of speech" (fuqar al-kalām) — its subtle points, likened to ornaments shaped like vertebrae.
- Root: ص-د-ق (ṣ-d-q)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Truthfulness in speech; giving (ṣadaqah) as the outward verification of inward faith.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Ṣidq (truth) and kidhb (falsehood) are originally in speech — statement of what is, or what will be. By extension, ṣadaqah is that which verifies the truthfulness of one's claim to faith through expenditure.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: truthful speech. Metaphorical: "a horse with true running" (dhū miṣdaq fī al-jary) — that which verifies its excellence through action. Thus charity verifies the giver's sincerity.
- Root: م-ن-ن (m-n-n)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The bestowal of a favor; reproaching another by reminding them of one's gift (al-mann).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): [As elaborated in the full lexicon entry on the heart's self-perception of superiority over the recipient.]
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: a heavy weight; a favor. Metaphorical: the act of counting one's favors over another — a corrosion of the gift's value.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد (Restriction & Specification) — governing the precise scope of obligation (farḍ kifāyah) versus supererogatory merit (faḍl), and the restriction of "rights in wealth" (ḥuqūq fī al-māl) beyond the obligatory zakat.
2:271.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Mysteries of Zakat'

2:271.arabic: الله تعالى على السر والعلانية فقال إن تبدوا الصدقات فنعما هي وإن تخفوها وتؤتوها الفقراء فهو خير لكم والإظهار قسمان أحدهما في نفس العمل والآخر التحدث بما عمل القسم الأول إظهار نفس العمل كالصدقة في الملأ لترغيب الناس فيها كما روي عن الأنصاري الذي جاء بالصرة فتتابع الناس بالعطية لما رأوه فقال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم من سن سنة حسنة فعمل بها كان له أجرها وأجر من اتبعه // حديث من سن سنة حسنة فعمل بها كان له أجرها وأجر من اتبعه وفي أوله قصة مسلم من حديث جرير بن عبد الله البيهقي وتجري سائر الأعمال هذا المجرى من الصلاة والصيام والحج والغزو وغيرها ول
2:271.english: Know that in the secrecy of deeds there is the benefit of sincerity (ikhlāṣ) and deliverance from ostentation (riyā'), while in their public display there is the benefit of emulation (iqtidā') and the incitement of people toward goodness — but in it also lies the affliction of ostentation. Al-Hasan said: "The Muslims have known that secrecy is the more protective of the two deeds." Yet in public display there is also a benefit, and for this reason Allah the Exalted praised both secrecy and openness, saying: {«إِن تُبْدُوا الصَّدَقَاتِ فَنِعِمَّا هِيَ وَإِن تُخْفُوهَا وَتُؤْتُوهَا الْفُقَرَاءَ فَهُوَ خَيْرٌ لَّكُمْ»} [If you disclose your charitable expenditures, they are good; but if you conceal them and give them to the poor, it is better for you] (Al-Baqarah: 271).
2:271.section_title_en: On the Permissibility of Intending the Public Display of Acts of Obedience
2:271.anchors:
- Root: نزغ (n-z-gh)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "النزغ: الدخول في الأمر بإفساد، والنزغ من الشيطان: الوسوسة والطعن"
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "النزغ: إفساد الشيء بالطعن فيه، ونزغ الشيطان: إلقاء الخواطر الفاسدة في القلب"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "نزغ بينهم: أفسد. ونزغ الشيطان: وسوس. وهو حقيقي في الإفساد، مجازي في الوسوسة"
- Root: سكر (s-k-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "السكر: ما سدد به النهر وغيره، والجمع سكور"
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "السكر: ما يرد به الماء، ويستعار لكل ما يمنع من الشيء"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "سكر النهر: سده. والسكر: الحاجز. وهو حقيقة في السد، مجاز في المنع"
- Root: أسر (s-r-r)
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "السر: ما يكتم، وهو ضد الإعلان. والسريرة: ما أسرّه الإنسان في نفسه"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "أسررت الشيء: خفيته. وساررته: كلمته سراً. والسر: حقيقة في الخفاء"
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The periodic sentence structure here employs interposed clauses to distinguish between the two opposing states (sleep and wakefulness) within a single governing verbal frame.
2:271.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'Condemnation of Status and Ostentation'

3:92.arabic: وكان عبد الله بن عمر يتصدق بالسكر ويقول سمعت الله يقول لن تنالوا البر حتى تنفقوا مما تحبون والله يعلم أني أحب السكر وقال النخعي إذا كان الشيء لله عز وجل لا يسرني أن يكون فيه عيب وقال عبيد بن عمير يحشر الناس يوم القيامة أجوع ما كانوا قط وأعطش ما كانووا قط وأعرى ما كانوا قط فمن أطعم لله عز وجل أشبعه الله ومن سقى لله عز وجل سقاه الله ومن كسا لله عز وجل كساه الله وقال الحسن لو شاء الله لجعلكم أغنياء لا فقير فيكم ولكنه ابتلى بعضكم ببعض وقال الشعبي من لم ير نفسه إلى ثواب الصدقة أحوج من الفقير إلى صدقته فقد أبطل صدقته وضرب بها وجهه وق
3:92.english: Among the reports [concerning charity], his saying (peace and blessings be upon him): "Give charity, even if with a single date-fruit, for it stays the hunger of the hungry and extinguishes sin just as water extinguishes fire." (1) And he said (peace and blessings be upon him): "Guard yourselves against the Fire, even if with half a date-fruit; and if you find not even that, then with a kind word." (2) And he said (peace and blessings be upon him): "There is no Muslim servant who gives charity from lawful earnings — and God accepts only what is lawful — but that God takes it in His Right Hand and nurtures it just as one of you nurtures his foal, until the single date-fruit grows to be like Mount Uḥud." (3) And he said (peace and blessings be upon him) to Abū al-Dardāʾ: "When you cook a broth, increase its water, then look to a household among your neighbors and bestow upon them from it with kindness." (4) And he said (peace and blessings be upon him): "No servant does well in charity but that God (mighty and majestic) does well for him in the stewardship of what he leaves behind." (5) And he said (peace and blessings be upon him): "Every person is in the shade of his charity until judgment is rendered between the people." (6) And he said (peace and blessings be upon him): "Charity closes seventy doors of evil." (7) And he said (peace and blessings be upon him): "Secret charity extinguishes the wrath of the Lord (mighty and majestic)." And the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "The one who gives from abundance is not more excellent in reward than the one who accepts from need." (8) Perhaps what is meant thereby is the one who intends, by the repelling of his need, to free himself for religion — so that he becomes equal to the giver who intends, by his giving, the flourishing of his religion.
3:92.section_title_en: The Book of the Etiquettes of Eating — Section on the Merits of Charity (Ṣadaqah) and Its Etiquettes
3:92.anchors:
- Root: صدق (ṣ-d-q)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of truthfulness, veracity in speech and action; al-Raghib notes its origin is in speech (al-qawl), whether past or future, promise or otherwise.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الصدق والكذب أصلهما في القول" — truth and falsehood originate in utterance; charity (ṣadaqah) is so named because it is the truthful verification of one's faith through material sacrifice.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): "صدقته الحديث" — to affirm someone's statement as true. Metaphorical (majāz): "رجل صادق الحملة" — a man truthful in his charge (i.e., steadfast in battle). Charity is thus the "truthing" of one's claim to faith by action.
- Root: عله (ʿ-l-h) — [Note: This root appears in the scholia but is not directly relevant to the present text; the governing root for "feeding" is أ-ك-ل and for "giving" is ع-ط-ي]
- Root: وجل (w-j-l)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الوجل: استشعار الخوف" — the sensing of fear within oneself.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الوجل: استشعار الخوف. يقال: وجل يوجل وجلا، فهو وجل. قال تعالى: {«إِنَّمَا الْمُؤْمِنُونَ الَّذِينَ إِذَا ذُكِرَ اللَّهُ وَجِلَتْ قُلُوبُهُمْ»}" — the believers are those whose hearts tremble when God is mentioned.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "رجل وجل، وقوم وجال" — a fearful man, a people fearful. The root conveys the inner trepidation of the heart before divine majesty.
- Root: سبع (s-b-ʿ)
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "أصل السبع العدد" — the root origin is the number seven; used for the seven heavens, seven earths, and in the present context, the seventy (seventy being a multiple of seven) doors of evil.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "هو سابع سبعة" — he is the seventh of seven. Metaphorical (majāz): "أخذه أخذ سبعة" — "he seized with the seizure of seven," a proverb for intense, overwhelming force. The number seventy thus signifies multiplicity and completeness in repelling evil.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — The particle "innamā" (إنما) restricts and confines the predicate to the subject alone, negating it for all others. This is crucial in the ḥadīth: "إنما هي أوساخ الناس" — charity is exclusively the filth of people, restricted to them and forbidden for the Prophet's family.
3:92.topic: Al-Ghazali on the journey of the soul, death, and the Hereafter, from 'Mysteries of Zakat'

4:37.arabic: وقرنه بالبخل فقال تعالى الذين يبخلون ويأمرون الناس بالبخل ويكتمون ما آتاهم الله من فضله وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا أنعم الله علي عبد نعمة أحب أن ترى نعمته عليه (1) وأعطى رجل بعض الصالحين شيئا في السر فرفع به يده وقال هذا من الدنيا والعلانية فيها أفضل والسر في أمور الآخرة أفضل ولذلك قال بعضهم إذا أعطيت في الملأ فخذ ثم اردد في السر والشكر فيه محثوث عليه قال صلى الله عليه وسلم من لم يشكر الناس لم يشكر الله عز وجل (2) والشكر قائم مقام المكافأة حتى قال صلى الله عليه وسلم من أسدى إليكم معروفا فكافئوه فإن لم تستطيعوا فأثنوا عليه به خيرا وادعوا
4:37.english: Abū Ayyūb al-Sakhtiyānī said: "I indeed abandon wearing a new garment, fearing that it might engender envy in my neighbors." And one of the ascetics said: "Perhaps I abandon the use of a thing for the sake of my brothers, lest they say: 'From where does he have this?'" It is related of Ibrāhīm al-Taymī that a new shirt was seen upon him, and one of his brothers said: "From where did you get this?" He replied: "My brother Khaythamah clothed me with it. Had I known that his family knew of it, I would not have accepted it."
4:37.section_title_en: On Sincerity (Ikhlas): The Ethics of Giving and Receiving — Concealment versus Disclosure
4:37.anchors:
- Root: س ت ر (s-t-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Covering, veiling, concealing; the act of screening something from view.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Concealment (sitr) preserves inviolability and prevents exposure of need, aligning with the Quranic description of the poor who "restrain themselves" so that the ignorant think them wealthy.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (haqiqah) — physical covering; Metaphorical (majaz) — concealing one's state of need or one's charitable act from the eyes of others.
- Root: ظ ه ر (ẓ-h-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To become apparent, visible, manifest; the opposite of concealment.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Openness and manifestation; used for both physical visibility and the public disclosure of an act.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — making something perceptible to the senses; Metaphorical — publicizing one's good deeds, which carries both the virtue of gratitude and the peril of ostentation.
- Root: ش ك ر (sh-k-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The core root denotes acknowledgment and increase; a beast "shakur" is one that thrives on little fodder.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "The perception of the blessing and its manifestation." It is the opposite of kufr (disbelief/ingratitude), which is the forgetting and covering of the blessing. It is of three types: of the heart (perceiving the blessing), of the tongue (praising the Benefactor), and of the limbs (rewarding the blessing with obedience).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — verbal praise of the benefactor; Metaphorical — the act of the one who, upon receiving a gift, openly expresses gratitude, which is a Sunnah, as in {«وَأَمَّا بِنِعْمَةِ رَبِّكَ فَحَدِّثْ»}.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The rule governing the separation of a preposition from its object for rhetorical emphasis, here applied to the nuanced interposition of intention (niyyah) between the outward act and its inward reality.
4:37.topic: Al-Ghazali on purifying the character, moral diseases, and spiritual remedies, from 'Mysteries of Zakat'

5:48.arabic: عز وجل سقاه الله ومن كسا لله عز وجل كساه الله وقال الحسن لو شاء الله لجعلكم أغنياء لا فقير فيكم ولكنه ابتلى بعضكم ببعض وقال الشعبي من لم ير نفسه إلى ثواب الصدقة أحوج من الفقير إلى صدقته فقد أبطل صدقته وضرب بها وجهه وقال مالك لا نرى بأسا بشرب المؤمن من الماء الذي يتصدق به ويسقى في المسجد لأنه إنما جعل للعطشان من كان ولم يرد به أهل الحاجة والمسكنة على الخصوص ويقال إن الحسن مر به نخاس ومعه جارية فقال للنخاس أترضى في ثمنها الدرهم والدرهمين قال لا قال فاذهب فإن الله عز وجل رضي في الحور العين بالفلس واللقمة

9:25.arabic: قال الله تعالى {ويوم حنين إذ أعجبتكم كثرتكم فلم تغن عنكم شيئا} ذكر ذلك في معرض الإنكار وقال عز وجل {وظنوا أنهم مانعتهم حصونهم من الله فأتاهم الله من حيث لم يحتسبوا} فرد على الكفار في إعجابهم بحصونهم وشوكتهم وقال تعالى {وهم يحسبون أنهم يحسنون صنعا} وهذا أيضا يرجع إلى العجب بالعمل وقد يعجب الإنسان بالعمل هو مخطئ فيه كما يعجب بعمل هو مصيب فيه وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم ثلاث مهلكات شح مطاع وهوى متبع وإعجاب المرء بنفسه (1) حديث أبي ثعلبة إذا رأيت شحا مطاعا وهوى متبعا وإعجاب كل ذي رأي برأيه فعليك نفسك أخرجه أبو
9:25.english: Know that self-admiration (al-ʿujb) is blameworthy in the Book of God Most High and the Sunnah of His Messenger, peace be upon him. God Most High said: {«وَيَوْمَ حُنَيْنٍ إِذْ أَعْجَبَتْكُمْ كَثْرَتُكُمْ فَلَمْ تُغْنِ عَنكُمْ شَيْئًا»} (And on the day of Hunayn, when your great number pleased you—but it availed you nothing) — He mentioned this in the context of censure. And He, Mighty and Majestic, said: {«وَظَنُّوا أَنَّهُم مَّانِعَتُهُمْ حُصُونُهُم مِّنَ اللهِ فَأَتَاهُمُ اللهُ مِنْ حَيْثُ لَمْ يَحْتَسِبُوا»} (And they thought that their fortresses would protect them from God; but God came upon them from where they did not expect) — thus He rebuked the disbelievers for their self-admiration in their fortresses and their might. And He Most High said: {«وَهُمْ يَحْسَبُونَ أَنَّهُمْ يُحْسِنُونَ صُنْعًا»} (While they think that they are doing good work) — and this too reverts to self-admiration in one's deed. And a man may admire himself for a deed in which he is mistaken, just as he may admire himself for a deed in which he is correct.
9:25.section_title_en: Exposition of the Blameworthiness of Self-Admiration (Al-ʿUjb) and Its Afflictions
9:25.anchors:
- Root: عجب (ʿ-j-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: astonishment, wonder, or a state that seizes one due to an unrecognized cause; al-Ayn notes "العاجب" as one who marvels, and "أعجبه" as something pleasing or admirable.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): ʿUjb is a condition arising from ignorance of a thing's cause; hence, it is impermissible regarding God, the Knower of all unseen. It denotes self-conceit when one is pleased with one's own state or deed.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): wonder/astonishment; Metaphorical (Majaz): self-admiration (iʿjāb al-marʾ bi-nafsihi), where one deems his deed or self praiseworthy, leading to arrogance.
- Root: حدث (ḥ-d-th)
  * Lisan / Ayn: New occurrence after non-existence; al-Ayn: "الحدّث: الإبداء" (origination/manifestation).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Ḥudūth is coming-to-be after not being; for God, creation is iḥdāth; for man, it implies temporal novelty.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: recent event; Metaphorical: "مُحَدَّث" as one inspired with truth, as if spoken to by unseen—here, not applicable; rather, the root underscores the temporal, contingent nature of deeds that invite ʿujb.
- Root: وقد (w-q-d)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Fire blazing; al-Ayn: "وقدت النار" (fire kindled).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Used for fuel and flame; metaphorically, intense burning—here, linked to the "fire" of destruction caused by ʿujb, as in the hadith on destructive traits.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: kindling; Metaphorical: "وقدة الصيف" (summer's heat)—intensity of affliction, paralleling ʿujb's consuming harm.
- Root: طلح (ṭ-l-ḥ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Banana tree or acacia; al-Ayn: "الطلح: شجر" (a tree).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Ṭalḥ is a tree; ṭalīḥ means exhausted/emaciated from toil—here, the name Ṭalḥah (companion) appears, whose deed was nearly spoiled by ʿujb.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: tree; Metaphorical: "طلح على غريمه" (pressed a debtor until weary)—exertion; also "طالح" (corrupt), contrasting with ṣalāḥ (righteousness), hinting at ʿujb's corrupting effect.
- Sibawayh Rule: Restriction and Focused Predication (باب الحصر والتقييد) — Used in phrases like "إنما جمع بينهما" (He only paired them) and "فالموجود لا يطلب والمحال لا يطلب" (the existent is not sought, and the impossible is not sought), where the predicate is restricted to a specific cause, clarifying logical necessity.

9:25.arabic: المهلكات وهو محبط للأعمال قال تعالى ويوم حنين إذا أعجبتكم كثرتكم فلم تغن عنكم شيئا ويقال إن الطاعة كلما استصغرت عظمت عند الله عز وجل والمعصية كلما استعظمت صغرت عند الله عز وجل وقيل لا يتم المعروف إلا بثلاثة أمور تصغيره وتعجيله وستره وليس الاستعظام هو المن والأذى فإنه لو صرف ماله إلى عمارة مسجد أو رباط أمكن فيه الاستعظام ولا يمكن فيه المن والأذى بل العجب والاستعظام يجري في جميع العبادات ودواؤه علم وعمل امام العلم فهو أن يعلم أن العشر أو ربع العشر قليل من كثير وأنه قد قنع لنفسه بأخس درجات البذل كما ذكرنا في فهم الوجوب فهو جدير ب
9:25.english: The heart is not treated save with the compound electuary (maʿjūn) of knowledge and works. And this condition among the conditions of almsgiving runs in the same course as humility (al-khushūʿ) runs in the prayer. This is established by his saying — may Allah bless him and grant him peace: "A man has nothing of his prayer save that of which he was conscious." And this is like his saying — may Allah bless him and grant him peace: "Allah does not accept the charity of the one who bestows it with reproach (al-mannān)." And like His saying — Exalted is He: {«لا تبطلوا صدقاتكم بالمن والأذى»} ("Do not nullify your charities by reproach and injury"). As for the legal opinion (fatwā) of the jurist that the alms fall in their proper place and that one's liability is discharged without this condition — that is another discussion, and we have already pointed to its meaning in the Book of Prayer.
9:25.section_title_en: The Inner Conditions of Charity — Section 175 (From The Revival of the Religious Sciences, Book of the Mysteries of Almsgiving)
9:25.anchors:
- Root: قلب (q-l-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "To turn, overturn, transform a thing from one state to another; to rotate, to flip"
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "قلب الشيء: تصريفه وصرفه عن وجه إلى وجه" — the heart is so named because of its constant turning and transformation between states
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "قلب الشيء قلبا: حوله عن وجهه" (to turn a thing from its face). Metaphorical: "رجل قلب حول: يقلب الأمور ويحتال" — one who turns matters over and manages them; "قلبوا لك الأمور" (they turned matters against you)
- Root: وجل (w-j-l)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "Fear, dread, apprehension that strikes the heart"
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الوجل: استشعار الخوف" — the sensing of fear; cited in {«إنما المؤمنون الذين إذا ذكر الله وجلت قلوبهم»}
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "رجل وجل، وقوم وجال" — a fearful man, a fearful people; "وفي قلبه وجل" — in his heart is dread
- Root: عجب (ʿ-j-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "Wonder, amazement; self-admiration, vanity"
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Self-admiration (al-ʿujb) is a destructive spiritual ailment that nullifies deeds
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: wonder at something extraordinary. Metaphorical: self-conceit regarding one's own acts of obedience

9:60.arabic: واجب وعليه يدل ظاهر قوله تعالى إنما الصدقات للفقراء والمساكين الآية فإنه يشبه قول المريض إنما ثلث مال للفقراء والمساكين وذلك يقتضي التشريك في التمليك والعبادات ينبغي أن يتوقى عن الهجوم فيها على الظواهر وقد عدم من الثمانية صنفان في أكثر البلاد وهم المؤلفة قلوبهم والعاملون على الزكاة ويوجد في جميع البلاد أربعة أصناف الفقراء والمساكين والغارمون والمسافرون أعني أبناء السبيل وصنفان يوجدان في بعض البلاد دون البعض وهم الغزاة والمكاتبون فإن وجد خمسة أصناف مثلا قسم بينهم زكاة ماله بخمسة أقسام متساوية أو متقاربة وعي
9:60.english: The fifth: that he divide his wealth according to the number of the categories (aṣnāf) present in his town. For covering all the categories is obligatory, and upon this the apparent meaning of His saying — exalted be He — indicates: {«Innamā al-ṣadaqātu lil-fuqarā'i wa al-masākīn»} (Charities are only for the poor and the needy) — the verse. For it resembles the saying of a sick person: "Only a third of my wealth is for the poor and the needy," and that entails sharing (tashrīk) in the ownership.
9:60.section_title_en: The Second Category of Legal Obligations: The Composite of Worship and Worldly Benefit — On Zakat
9:60.anchors:
- Root: قسم (q-s-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Division, apportionment, allotment of shares
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "القسم: إفراز النصيب" — the separation and allocation of portions; used for dividing inheritance, spoils, and designated shares
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: dividing property among parties. Metaphorical: "قلبه متقسم" — a heart divided by cares; "وجه مقسم" — a face given each portion of beauty, thus well-proportioned
- Root: وجب (w-j-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To be due, incumbent, necessary; to fall (as a duty)
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الوجوب: الثبوت" — obligation as established fixity; two types: obligatory by reason (as knowing divine unity) and obligatory by Law (as worship)
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "وجب البيع" — the sale is confirmed/binding. Metaphorical: "وجب" — to fall dead; the obligatory falling upon one
- Root: شرع (sh-r-ʿ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: A comprehensive name for what God has legislated; the clear path
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الشرع: نهج الطريق الواضح" — the clear path; then applied to the divine law (sharīʿah) as the way of religion
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "شرع الله الدين" — God legislated the religion. Metaphorical: "مد البعير شراعه" — the camel extended its neck like a ship's sail, then applied to the revealed Law as the path to water (life)
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — "إنما الصدقات للفقراء" restricts the recipients of charity to the eight specified categories, functioning as exclusive predication

9:60.arabic: المسئلة ويغنيها عن الناس فهو في سبيل الله وإن كان يسعى على أبوين ضعيفين أو ذرية ضعاف ليغنيهم ويكفيهم فهو في سبيل الله وإن كان يسعى تفاخرا وتكاثرا فهو في سبيل الشيطان (4) وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم إن الله يحب العبد يتخذ المهنة ليستغني بها عن الناس ويبغض العبد يتعلم العلم يتخذه مهنة (5) وفي الخبر إن الله تعالى يحب المؤمن المحترف (6) وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم أحل ما أكل الرجل من كسبه وكل بيع مبرور (7) وفي خبر آخر أحل ما أكل العبد كسب يد الصانع إذا نصح (1) وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم عل
9:60.english: As for what is [cited] from the Book [i.e., the Qur'an], there is His saying, the Exalted: «{وَجَعَلْنَا النَّهَارَ مَعَاشًا}» ("And We have made the day a means of livelihood" [al-Naba' 78:11]) — and He mentioned it in the context of bestowing favor (imtinān).
9:60.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'Etiquette of Earning'

13:22.arabic: قال الله تعالى وأنفقوا مما رزقناهم سرا وعلانية ندب إلى العلانية أيضا لما فيها من فائدة الترغيب فليكن العبد دقيق التأمل في وزن هذه الفائدة بالمحذور الذي فيه فإن ذلك يختلف بالأحوال والأشخاص فقد يكون الإعلان في بعض الأحوال لبعض الأشخاص أفضل ومن عرف الفوائد والغوائل ولم ينظر بعين الشهوة اتضح له الأولى والأليق بكل حال الوظيفة الخامسة أن لا يفسد صدقته بالمن والأذى قال الله تعالى لا تبطلوا صدقاتكم بالمن والأذى واختلفوا في حقيقة المن والأذى فقيل المن أن يذكرها والأذى أن يظهرها وقال سفيان من من فسدت
13:22.english: A group of the Followers (tābiʿūn) held that there are rights in wealth beyond the zakat — among them al-Nakhaʿī, al-Shaʿbī, ʿAṭāʾ, and Mujāhid. Al-Shaʿbī said, after being asked, "Is there a right in wealth beyond the zakat?": "Yes. Have you not heard His saying — mighty and majestic is He: {«وَآتَى الْمَالَ عَلَىٰ حُبِّهِ ذَوِي الْقُرْبَىٰ»} 'And gives wealth, despite his love for it, to relatives' (2:177)?" They also adduced His saying — mighty and majestic is He: {«وَمِمَّا رَزَقْنَاهُمْ يُنفِقُونَ»} 'And from what We have provided them, they spend' (2:3), and His saying — exalted is He: {«وَأَنفِقُوا مِن مَّا رَزَقْنَاكُم»} 'And spend from what We have provided you' (2:254). They claimed that this is not abrogated by the verse of zakat; rather, it falls within the right of a Muslim upon a Muslim. Its meaning is that it is incumbent upon the affluent one, whenever he finds a needy person, to remove his need — over and above the zakat wealth.
13:22.section_title_en: The Second Division: Those Who Guard Their Wealth Awaiting Seasons of Need — On the Inner Meanings of Zakat (Section 173)
13:22.anchors:
- Root: ف-ق-ر (f-q-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of neediness, poverty; the hollow of the spine (faqār) — that which is structurally weak and dependent.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Poverty (faqr) has four senses: (1) essential neediness before Allah, universal to all creatures; (2) lack of possessions; (3) [the third and fourth senses as elaborated in the full lexicon entry].
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (haqīqah): one who lacks wealth. Metaphorical (majāz): "the poverty of speech" (fuqar al-kalām) — its subtle points, likened to ornaments shaped like vertebrae.
- Root: ص-د-ق (ṣ-d-q)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Truthfulness in speech; giving (ṣadaqah) as the outward verification of inward faith.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Ṣidq (truth) and kidhb (falsehood) are originally in speech — statement of what is, or what will be. By extension, ṣadaqah is that which verifies the truthfulness of one's claim to faith through expenditure.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: truthful speech. Metaphorical: "a horse with true running" (dhū miṣdaq fī al-jary) — that which verifies its excellence through action. Thus charity verifies the giver's sincerity.
- Root: م-ن-ن (m-n-n)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The bestowal of a favor; reproaching another by reminding them of one's gift (al-mann).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): [As elaborated in the full lexicon entry on the heart's self-perception of superiority over the recipient.]
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: a heavy weight; a favor. Metaphorical: the act of counting one's favors over another — a corrosion of the gift's value.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد (Restriction & Specification) — governing the precise scope of obligation (farḍ kifāyah) versus supererogatory merit (faḍl), and the restriction of "rights in wealth" (ḥuqūq fī al-māl) beyond the obligatory zakat.

16:62.arabic: تكذيبا لهم ثم ابتدأ وقال جرم أن لهم النار أي كسب لهم جعلهم لله ما يكرهون النار الوظيفة الثامنة أن يطلب لصدقته من تزكو به الصدقة ولا يكتفي بأن يكون من عموم الأصناف الثمانية فإن في عمومهم خصوص صفات فليراع خصوص تلك الصفات وهي ستة الأولى أن يطلب الأتقياء المعرضين عن الدينا المتجردين لتجارة الآخرة قال صلى الله عليه وسلم لا تأكل إلا طعام تقي ولا يأكل طعامك إلا تقي (1) وهذا لأن التقي يستعين به على التقوى فتكون شريكا في طاعته بإعانتك إياه وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم أطعموا طعامكم الأتقياء وأولوا معروف

This is established by his saying — may Allah bless him and grant him peace: "A man has nothing of his prayer save that of which he was conscious." And this is like his saying — may Allah bless him and grant him peace: "Allah does not accept the charity of the one who bestows it with reproach (al-mannān)." And like His saying — Exalted is He: {«لا تبطلوا صدقاتكم بالمن والأذى»} ("Do not nullify your charities by reproach and injury"). As for the legal opinion (fatwā) of the jurist that the alms fall in their proper place and that one's liability is discharged without this condition — that is another discussion, and we have already pointed to its meaning in the Book of Prayer.
16:62.section_title_en: The Inner Conditions of Charity — Section 175 (From The Revival of the Religious Sciences, Book of the Mysteries of Almsgiving)
16:62.anchors:
- Root: قلب (q-l-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "To turn, overturn, transform a thing from one state to another; to rotate, to flip"
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "قلب الشيء: تصريفه وصرفه عن وجه إلى وجه" — the heart is so named because of its constant turning and transformation between states
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "قلب الشيء قلبا: حوله عن وجهه" (to turn a thing from its face). Metaphorical: "رجل قلب حول: يقلب الأمور ويحتال" — one who turns matters over and manages them; "قلبوا لك الأمور" (they turned matters against you)
- Root: وجل (w-j-l)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "Fear, dread, apprehension that strikes the heart"
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الوجل: استشعار الخوف" — the sensing of fear; cited in {«إنما المؤمنون الذين إذا ذكر الله وجلت قلوبهم»}
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "رجل وجل، وقوم وجال" — a fearful man, a fearful people; "وفي قلبه وجل" — in his heart is dread
- Root: عجب (ʿ-j-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "Wonder, amazement; self-admiration, vanity"
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Self-admiration (al-ʿujb) is a destructive spiritual ailment that nullifies deeds
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: wonder at something extraordinary. Metaphorical: self-conceit regarding one's own acts of obedience
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد (Restriction & Focused Predication) — governing the precise limitation of general categories (al-ṣifāt al-khāṣṣah within al-aṣnāf al-thamāniyyah) and the conditional structure of acceptance
