4:95.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'Disciplining the Soul'

4:95.arabic: بغير رضاهم هل رضي بفعلك المؤلفة قلوبهم والعاملون عليها في أرض الله تعالى والمجاهدون في سبيل الله وابن السبيل أم رضي بذلك حملة القرآن وأهل العلم والآرامل والأيتام أم هل رضي بذلك خلق من رعيتك فشد يا هرون مئزرك وأعد للمسألة جوابا وللبلاء جلبابا واعلم أنك ستقف بين يدي الحكم العدل فقد رزئت في نفسك إذ سلبت حلاوة العلم والزهد ولذيذ القرآن ومجالسة الأخيار ورضيت لنفسك أن تكون ظالما وللظالمين إماما يا هرون قعدت على السرير ولبست الحرير وأسبلت سترا دون بابك وتشبهت بالحجبة برب العالمين ثم أقعدت أجنادك الظلمة دون بابك وسترك يظلمون الناس ولا ينصفون يشربون
4:95.english: I extended my eyes toward them and said, "The one praying is Sufyān." So I threw the book to him.
4:95.section_title_en: The Revival of the Religious Sciences — Section 556: The Epistle of Sufyān al-Thawrī to Hārūn al-Rashīd
4:95.anchors:
- Root: ظ-ل-م (Ẓ-L-M)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning is placing something in other than its proper place; darkness (ẓulmah) as its cognate.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Ẓulm is the absence of light (nūr), used metaphorically for ignorance, polytheism, and transgression against others' rights.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) — acting unjustly; metaphorical (majāz) — "a land that has been wronged" (arḍ maẓlūmah), i.e., never dug or cultivated, indicating the severity of the injustice as a novel and unprecedented act.
- Root: ك-ت-ب (K-T-B)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To write, to prescribe, to assemble; a book (kitāb) as a gathered compilation.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Writing as the inscription of knowledge; the "Book of God" as His speech and decree.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — inscribing letters; metaphorical — the "writing" of a decree or obligation.
- Root: م-س-س (M-S-S)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To touch, to feel, to handle physically.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Physical contact; also used for the touch of harm or madness (mimsah).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — physical touch; metaphorical — the "touch" of a calamity or an evil consequence.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Interposition (al-Faṣl bayna al-Jār wa al-Majrūr) — The narrative structure here employs periodic sentences where the subject's actions are sequentially interposed with their objects, creating a dramatic and cumulative effect, as in the description of Sufyān's handling of the letter.
4:95.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Enjoining Good and Forbidding Evil'

4:100.arabic: الله عز وجل وافدا إليه إذ قال جل جلاله {ومن يخرج من بيته مهاجرا إلى الله ورسوله ثم يدركه الموت فقد وقع أجره على الله} وأما دخول البادية إلى الميقات ومشاهدة تلك العقبات فليتذكر فيها ما بين الخروج من الدنيا بالموت إلى ميقات يوم القيامة وما بينهما من الأهوال والمطالبات وليتذكر من هول قطاع الطريق هول سؤال منكر ونكير ومن سباع البوادي عقارب القبر وديدانه وما فيه من الأفاعي والحيات ومن انفراده من أهله وأقاربه وحشة القبر وكربته ووحدته وليكن في هذه المخاوف في أعماله وأقواله متزودا لمخاوف القبر وأما الإحرام والتلبية من الميقات فليعلم أن معناه إجابة نداء الله عز وجل فارج
4:100.english: As for leaving the town, let him know at that moment that he has parted from his family and homeland, heading towards God, Mighty and Majestic, in a journey that bears no resemblance to the journeys of this world. So let him bring to his heart: what does he intend, and where is he heading, and the visitation of whom does he seek? And that he is heading towards the King of Kings (Malik al-Mulūk) in the company of His visitors — those who were called and responded, who were made to yearn and so yearned, who were roused and so rose up, who cut off attachments and parted from creatures, and advanced towards the House of God, Mighty and Majestic — He who magnified its command, exalted its affair, and raised its standing — seeking consolation through the encounter with the House from the encounter with the Lord of the House, until they are granted the utmost of their hopes and are blessed with the vision of their Master. And let him bring to his heart the hope of arrival and acceptance — not boasting of his deeds in departing and parting from family and wealth — but rather trusting in the bounty of God, Mighty and Majestic, and hoping for the fulfillment of His promise to whoever visits His House. And let him hope that if he does not reach it and death overtakes him on the road, he will meet God, Mighty and Majestic, as one arriving as a visitor (wāfid) to Him. For He, Glorious is His majesty, said: {«وَمَنْ يَخْرُجْ مِنْ بَيْتِهِ مُهَاجِرًا إِلَى اللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ ثُمَّ يُدْرِكْهُ الْمَوْتُ فَقَدْ وَقَعَ أَجْرُهُ عَلَى اللَّهِ»} — "And whoever leaves his house as an emigrant to God and His Messenger, and then death overtakes him, his reward has already fallen due upon God" {Quran 4:100}.
4:100.section_title_en: Section 217 — The Explanation of Inward Acts, the Manner of Sincerity (Ikhlāṣ) in Intention, and the Path of Reflection upon the Witnessed Scenes (of the Pilgrimage)
4:100.anchors:
- Root: سفر (s-f-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "السفر: كشف الغطاء" — uncovering; the journey as a means of uncovering lands and states; "أسفر الصبح" — the dawn shone forth.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): السفر is the uncovering of a cover, and is applied to travel as it unveils new horizons and conditions of the soul.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas - Haqiqah/Literal): "سافر سفرا بعيدا" — to travel a far journey; "مسافر" — one who travels.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas - Majaz/Metaphorical): "سافرت عنه الحمى" — the fever departed from him; "أسفرت الحرب" — the war intensified. Here, the journey to God is a metaphorical "unveiling" of the soul's attachment to worldly causes.
- Root: حرم (ḥ-r-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "المُحِلَّةُ" — that which makes lawful; "حرم" — to forbid, to make sacred.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): الحرام is that which is prohibited, whether by divine decree or by human law; the state of iḥrām is a sacred prohibition of worldly adornments.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas - Haqiqah/Literal): "وهي له محرم" — a woman forbidden to him for marriage (a close relative); "جلد محرم" — undressed leather.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas - Majaz/Metaphorical): "سرى في محارم الليل" — he traveled in the sacred/forbidding darkness of the night, i.e., its perils. The iḥrām garments are a metaphorical "prohibition" of worldly dress, prefiguring the shroud.
- Root: ورد (w-r-d) [implied in "وافدا" and "الوفود"]
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): الورود is arriving at water; metaphorically, arriving before a king or lord as a visitor (wāfid).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas - Majaz/Metaphorical): "وفد على الأمير" — he came as a delegate to the governor. The pilgrim is a "wāfid" (visitor/delegate) to God, arriving at the water of His mercy.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The separation of the prepositional phrase from its governing verb for rhetorical emphasis, as in "فكيف يحتاط في أسباب السفر المشكوك فيه ويستظهر في زاده وراحلته ويهمل أمر السفر المستيقن" — the interposition of clauses to contrast the certain journey (death) with the uncertain one (travel).
4:100.topic: Al-Ghazali on the journey of the soul, death, and the Hereafter, from 'Mysteries of Hajj'

4:100.arabic: وقال الأمراء أربعة فأمير قوي ظلف نفسه وعماله فذلك كالمجاهد في سبيل الله يد الله باسطة عليه بالرحمة وأمير فيه ضعف ظلف نفسه وأرتع عماله لضعفه فهو على شفا هلاك إلا أن يرحمه الله وأمير ظلف عماله وأرتع نفسه فذلك الحطمة الذي قال فيه رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم شر الرعاة الحطمة فهو الهالك وحده (4) وأمير أرتع نفسه وعماله فهلكوا جميعا وقد بلغني يا أمير المؤمنين أن جبرائيل عليه السلام أتى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال أتيتك حين أمر الله بمنافخ النار فوضعت على النار تسعر ليوم القيامة فقال له يا جبريل صف لي النار فقال إن
4:100.english: He turned to al-Shaʿbī and said: "O Abā ʿAmr! I am the trustee of the Commander of the Faithful over Iraq and his governor over it, and a man commanded to obedience. I have been tried with the subjects, and their right has become incumbent upon me. So I love to preserve them and to attend to what sets them right, along with sincere counsel (naṣīḥah) to them. And reports may reach me about a band of people from the regions concerning a matter, and I find myself severe against them therein, so I withhold a portion of their stipends and place it in the treasury (bayt al-māl), with the intention in myself that I shall return it to them. Then it reaches the Commander of the Faithful that I have withheld it in that manner, so he writes to me that I must not return it. I cannot then countermand his order, nor can I execute his letter [against my better judgment]. I am but a man commanded to obedience. Is there any liability upon me in this, and in similar matters, where the intention is as I have described?"
4:100.section_title_en: The Upright Scholars Before the Tyrannical Rulers — Counsel and Fearless Truth-Telling
4:100.anchors:
- Root: نصح (naṣaḥa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning is sincerity, faithfulness, and pure counsel free from deceit; the root denotes the act of seeking the welfare of another with complete integrity.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In theological context, naṣīḥah is the obligation of the sincere advisor to guide the ruler toward divine truth, even at personal peril, as it is a form of worship (ʿibādah) and a trust (amānah).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) usage denotes pure honey (ʿasal naṣīḥ) free from admixture; metaphorical (majāz) usage applies to counsel that is untainted by flattery or self-interest.
- Root: سلط (sulṭ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Denotes authority, power, and dominion; the ruler (sulṭān) is one who has been given sway over affairs.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In Kalam, sulṭān is a trial (ibtilāʾ) and a trust (amānah) from God, whose exercise demands justice (ʿadl) and whose neglect invites divine wrath.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal usage refers to physical power or a governing authority; metaphorical usage extends to the authority of proof (sulṭān al-burhān) that compels assent.
- Root: عظ (waʿaẓa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Root denotes admonition, exhortation, and reminding of consequences; it implies softening the heart through remembrance of God and the Hereafter.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In theological terms, ʿiẓah is the act of turning the soul away from transgression through a blend of fear (tarhīb) and hope (targhīb), grounded in revealed truth.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal usage is the verbal admonition; metaphorical usage is the admonition of circumstance (ʿiẓah al-ḥāl) when events themselves teach a lesson.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Restriction and Focused Predication (bāb al-ḥaṣr wa al-taqyīd bi-innamā) — Governing the emphasis of exclusive predication in statements of counsel, such as "No obedience to a creature in disobedience of the Creator," where the restriction (ḥaṣr) is achieved through negation and exception (nafy wa istithnāʾ).
4:100.topic: Al-Ghazali on the journey of the soul, death, and the Hereafter, from 'Enjoining Good and Forbidding Evil'

4:100.arabic: أخاف أن يكون قد فطن وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم من خرج من بيته حاجا أو معتمرا فمات أجري له أجر الحاج المعتمر إلى يوم القيامة ومن مات في أحد الحرمين لم يعرض ولم يحاسب وقيل له ادخل الجنة (3) وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم حجة مبرورة خير من الدنيا وما فيها وحجة مبرورة ليس لها جزاء إلا الجنة (4) وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم الحجاج والعمار وفد الله عز وجل وزواره إن سألوه أعطاهم وإن استغفروه غفر لهم وإن دعوا استجيب لهم وإن شفعوا شفعوا (5) وفي حديث مسند من طريق أهل البيت عليهم السلام أعظم الناس ذنبا من وقف بعرفة فظن أن الله
4:100.english: I say: The first [matter] concerning the virtue of the pilgrimage — God Most High said: {«وَأَذِّن فِي النَّاسِ بِالْحَجِّ يَأْتُوكَ رِجَالًا وَعَلَىٰ كُلِّ ضَامِرٍ يَأْتِينَ مِن كُلِّ فَجٍّ عَمِيقٍ»} (And proclaim to the people the pilgrimage; they will come to you on foot and on every lean camel, coming from every deep and distant highway). Qatādah said: When God Most High commanded Ibrāhīm (peace be upon him — and upon our Prophet and upon every chosen servant) to proclaim the pilgrimage to the people, he called out: "O people! God Most High has built a House, so perform the pilgrimage to it." And He Most High said: {«لِيَشْهَدُوا مَنَافِعَ لَهُمْ»} (That they may witness benefits for them) — it is said [these benefits are] commerce during the season and reward in the Hereafter.
4:100.section_title_en: The Virtue of the Pilgrimage (Faḍīlat al-Ḥajj)
4:100.anchors:
- Root: ح ج ج (ḥ-j-j)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning is "to repair to a place repeatedly, to seek a thing, to overcome in argument." Al-Ayn: "الحج: القصد والتردد إلى الشيء."
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الحج: القصد إلى البيت الحرام للنسك، وأصله من قصدت الشيء وأقبلت عليه."
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "قصدت فلانا وحججت إليه." Metaphorical: "حاججته فحججته" — to overcome in disputation, from the idea of repeatedly pressing one's point.
- Root: غ ف ر (gh-f-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الغفر: الستر والتغطية." Al-Ayn: "غفرت الشيء: سترته."
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الغفران والمغفرة من الله هو أن يصون العبد من أن يمسه العذاب."
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "اغفر ثوبك في الوعاء" (cover/protect your garment). Metaphorical: Divine forgiveness as protective covering of sins.
- Root: و ف د (w-f-d)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الوفد: القوم يأتون السلطان أو الرئيس زائرين أو مستعطفين."
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الوفد: القوم المجتمعون القاصدون إلى رئيس."
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "وفد فلان على الأمير" — he came as a delegate. Metaphorical: The pilgrims as "delegation of God" (وفد الله) — those who come to Him seeking honor and bounty.
- Root: ر ح م (r-ḥ-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الرحمة: الرقة والتعطف." Al-Ayn: "الرحمة: رقة القلب."
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الرحمة: رقة تقتضي الإحسان إلى المرحوم."
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "رحمت فلانا" — I felt compassion. Metaphorical: Divine mercy as the descent of blessing and pardon upon creation.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The rule governing the placement of prepositional phrases and their objects, particularly relevant in the verse {«يأتين من كل فج عميق»} where the prepositional phrase "من كل فج" is interposed between the verb and its subject, demonstrating the rhetorical emphasis on the vastness of the routes of pilgrimage.
4:100.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'Mysteries of Hajj'

4:141.arabic: وما جعل الله للكافرين على المؤمنين سبيلا وأما مجرد قوله لا تزن فليس بمحرم عليه من حيث إنه نهى عن الزنا ولكن من حيث إنه إظهار دالة الاحتكام على المسلم وفيه إذلال للمحتكم عليه والفاسق يستحق الإذلال ولكن لا من الكافر الذي هو أولى بالذل منه فهذا وجه منعنا إياه من الحسبة وإلا فلسنا نقول إن الكافر يعاقب بسبب قوله لا تزن من حيث إنه نهى بل نقول إنه إذا لم يقل لا تزن يعاقب عليه إن رأينا خطاب الكافر بفروع الدين وفيه نظر استوفيناه في الفقهيات ولا يليق بغرضنا الآن
4:141.english: If it is said: "Then let the unbelieving dhimmī (protected non-Muslim subject) be permitted to enjoin right upon a Muslim if he sees him committing fornication — for his saying 'Do not fornicate' is true in itself, so it is impossible that it be unlawful for him; rather, it ought to be permissible or even obligatory."
4:141.section_title_en: The Revival of the Religious Sciences — Book of Blame of Status-Seeking and Hypocrisy: Section 525 — The First Pillar: The One Who Enjoins Right (Al-Muḥtasib)
4:141.anchors:
- Root: حسب (ḥ-s-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To count, reckon, compute; to hold an opinion or estimation.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الحساب: استعمال العدد" — the act of employing number; the reckoning of deeds. The muḥtasib is one who "reckons" or "takes account" of others' actions, demanding the right and forbidding the wrong.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Haqiqah (Literal): "حسب المال" — he counted the wealth. Majaz (Metaphorical): "يَتَحَسَّبانِ الأَخبار" — they seek out and ascertain news, as one places assumption in the position of knowledge. The "ḥisbah" is the act of account-taking, extended metaphorically to the duty of commanding right and forbidding wrong.
- Root: قهر (q-h-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To overcome, subdue, dominate; to force against one's will.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "القهر: الغلبة والتذليل معا" — overpowering and subjugation together. It is used of God's absolute dominance over His creation.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Haqiqah: "أخذتهم قهرة: من غير رضاهم" — he seized them by force, without their consent. Majaz: "جبال قواهر: شوامخ" — towering, overbearing mountains. The "qahr" in ḥisbah is the coercive enforcement of the right, distinct from mere verbal admonition.
- Root: فسق (f-s-q)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To emerge, exit, depart; of a date, to split from its skin.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "فسق فلان: خرج عن حجر الشرع" — he went out from the enclosure of the Sacred Law. It is more general than unbelief (kufr), applying to the one who commits to the Law's rulings then violates them, in whole or in part.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Haqiqah: "فسق عن أمر الله: خرج" — he departed from God's command. Majaz: "وفسقت الرطبة عن قشرها" — the ripe date burst from its skin. The fāsiq is one who has "burst out" of obedience.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The permissibility of interposing elements between a governing word and its dependent, provided the intervening clause is complete in itself, as in "إن به..." — governing the syntactic flow of conditional and exceptive constructions in the argumentation.

5:2.arabic: والزكاة في نعت الصالحين والمؤمنين وقال تعالى وتعاونوا على البر والتقوى ولا تعاونوا على الإثم والعدوان وهو أمر جزم ومعنى التعاون الحث عليه وتسهيل طرق الخير وسد سبل الشر والعدوان بحسب الإمكان وقال تعالى لولا ينهاهم الربانيون والأحبار عن قولهم الإثم وأكلهم السحت لبئس ما كانوا يصنعون فبين أنهم أثموا بترك النهي وقال تعالى فلولا كان من القرون من قبلكم أولوا بقية ينهون عن الفساد في الأرض الآية فبين أنه أهلك جميعهم إلا قليلا منهم كانوا ينهون عن الفساد وقال تعالى يا أيها الذين آمنوا كونوا قوامين بالقسط شهداء لله ولو على أنفسكم أو الوالدين والأقربين وذلك هو الأ
5:2.english: Know that the verses indicating the obligation of commanding right and forbidding wrong are numerous. Among them is His saying, may He be exalted: {«Let there arise from among you a nation inviting to good, commanding right and forbidding wrong — and those are the successful»} (Āl ʿImrān 3:104). In this verse is the declaration of obligation, for His saying, may He be exalted, "Let there be" (wal-takun) is a command, and the apparent meaning of a command is obligation. In it also is the declaration that success (falāḥ) is contingent upon it, for He restricted it and said: {«And those are the successful»}. In it also is the declaration that it is a collective obligation (farḍ kifāyah), not an individual obligation (farḍ ʿayn), and that when a group undertakes it, the obligation falls from the rest — for He did not say, "Let all of you be commanders of right," but rather said: {«Let there arise from among you a nation»}. Thus, whenever one person or a group undertakes it, the burden falls from the others, and success is particularized to those who undertake it and directly perform it. But if all of creation were to hold back from it, the burden would encompass all those capable of it without exception.
5:2.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Enjoining Good and Forbidding Evil'

5:2.arabic: وقد قال الله تعالى يا أيها الذين آمنوا أنفقوا من طيبات ما كسبتم ومما أخرجنا لكم من الأرض ولا تيمموا الخبيث منه تنفقون ولستم بآخذيه إلا أن تغمضوا فيه أي لا تأخذوه إلا مع كراهية وحياء وهو معنى الإغماض فلا تؤثروا به ربكم وفي الخبر سبق درهم مائة ألف درهم (3) وذلك بأن يخرجه الإنسان وهو من أحل ماله وأجوده فيصدر ذلك عن الرضا والفرح بالبذل وقد يخرج مائة ألف درهم مما يكره من ماله فيدل ذلك على أنه ليس يؤثر الله عز وجل بشيء مما يحبه وبذلك ذم الله تعالى قوما جعلوا لله ما يكرهون فقال تعال
5:2.english: The heart is not treated save with the compound electuary (maʿjūn) of knowledge and works. And this condition among the conditions of almsgiving runs in the same course as humility (al-khushūʿ) runs in the prayer. This is established by his saying — may Allah bless him and grant him peace: "A man has nothing of his prayer save that of which he was conscious." And this is like his saying — may Allah bless him and grant him peace: "Allah does not accept the charity of the one who bestows it with reproach (al-mannān)." And like His saying — Exalted is He: {«لا تبطلوا صدقاتكم بالمن والأذى»} ("Do not nullify your charities by reproach and injury"). As for the legal opinion (fatwā) of the jurist that the alms fall in their proper place and that one's liability is discharged without this condition — that is another discussion, and we have already pointed to its meaning in the Book of Prayer.
5:2.section_title_en: The Inner Conditions of Charity — Section 175 (From The Revival of the Religious Sciences, Book of the Mysteries of Almsgiving)
5:2.anchors:
- Root: قلب (q-l-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "To turn, overturn, transform a thing from one state to another; to rotate, to flip"
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "قلب الشيء: تصريفه وصرفه عن وجه إلى وجه" — the heart is so named because of its constant turning and transformation between states
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "قلب الشيء قلبا: حوله عن وجهه" (to turn a thing from its face). Metaphorical: "رجل قلب حول: يقلب الأمور ويحتال" — one who turns matters over and manages them; "قلبوا لك الأمور" (they turned matters against you)
- Root: وجل (w-j-l)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "Fear, dread, apprehension that strikes the heart"
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الوجل: استشعار الخوف" — the sensing of fear; cited in {«إنما المؤمنون الذين إذا ذكر الله وجلت قلوبهم»}
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "رجل وجل، وقوم وجال" — a fearful man, a fearful people; "وفي قلبه وجل" — in his heart is dread
- Root: عجب (ʿ-j-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "Wonder, amazement; self-admiration, vanity"
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Self-admiration (al-ʿujb) is a destructive spiritual ailment that nullifies deeds
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: wonder at something extraordinary. Metaphorical: self-conceit regarding one's own acts of obedience
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد (Restriction & Focused Predication) — governing the precise limitation of general categories (al-ṣifāt al-khāṣṣah within al-aṣnāf al-thamāniyyah) and the conditional structure of acceptance

5:63.arabic: للكذب أكالون للسحت وقال عز وجل لولا ينهاهم الربانيون والأحبار عن قولهم الإثم وأكلهم السحت فالسكوت على الغيبة حرام وقال تعالى إنكم إذا مثلهم ولذلك قال صلى الله عليه وسلم المغتاب والمستمع شريكان في لإثم (2) الرابع كف بقية الجوارح عن الآثام من اليد والرجل عن المكاره وكف البطن عن الشبهات وقت الإفطار فلا معنى للصوم وهو الكف عن الطعام الحلال ثم الإفطار على الحرام فمثال هذا الصائم مثال من يبني قصرا ويهدم مصرا فإن الطعام الحلال إنما يضر بكثرته لا بنوعه فالصوم لتقليله وتارك الاستكثار من الدواء خوفا من ضرره إذا عدل إلى تناول السم كان سفيها و
5:63.english: As for the fast of the elite of the elite, it is the fasting of the heart from base concerns (al-himam al-daniyyah) and worldly thoughts (al-afkār al-dunyawiyyah), and its complete restraint from everything other than God, Mighty and Majestic. The breaking of the fast in this degree occurs through thinking upon other than God, Mighty and Majestic, and the Last Day, and through thinking upon this world — except a worldly matter intended for the sake of religion, for that is of the provisions of the Hereafter and is not of this world. Indeed, the masters of hearts have said: "Whosoever's aspiration stirs him to act during his day to arrange what he will break his fast upon, a sin is recorded against him" — for that stems from lack of trust in the bounty of God, Mighty and Majestic, and lack of certainty in His promised provision. This is the station of the prophets, the veracious (al-ṣiddīqīn), and those brought near (al-muqarrabīn). There is no need to prolong the discussion of its details in speech, but rather in actualizing it in deed — for it is the turning of one's whole aspiration toward God, Mighty and Majestic, and the turning away from other than God, Glorified be He, and the clothing of oneself with the meaning of His saying, Mighty and Majestic: {«Say: God — then leave them in their vain play»} (Q. 6:91).
5:63.section_title_en: The Three Degrees of Fasting: The Fast of the Common People, the Fast of the Elite, and the Fast of the Elite of the Elite
5:63.anchors:
- Root: صوم (ṣ-w-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core linguistic root meaning — "abstention from action, whether from food, speech, or walking; the horse that refrains from moving or feeding is called ṣā'im"
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الصوم في الأصل: الإمساك عن الفعل مطعما كان، أو كلاما، أو مشيا" — fasting in origin is abstention from any act, whether food, speech, or movement; theological nuance extends to abstention of the heart from all save God
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah) — "شهر الصوم والصيام" the month of fasting; Metaphorical (Majaz) — "صام الفرس على آريه إذا لم يعتلف" the horse fasting upon its stable when it refrains from fodder; hence the heart's fasting from worldly concerns is a metaphorical extension of the same root abstention
- Root: وجل (w-j-l)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core linguistic root meaning — "fear, trepidation, the stirring of dread within the breast"
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الوجل: استشعار الخوف" — wajal is the inward sensing of fear; cited in {«إنما المؤمنون الذين إذا ذكر الله وجلت قلوبهم»} (Q. 8:2) — the believers are those whose hearts tremble when God is mentioned
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — "رجل وجل، وقوم وجال" a fearful man, a fearful people; the heart suspended between fear and hope after the fast partakes of this root's semantic field
- Root: عله (ʿ-l-h)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core linguistic root meaning — "to occupy, to divert, to preoccupy; the one preoccupied is mashghūl"
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The heart's occupation with other than God is the very breaking of the fast of the elite of the elite
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal vs Metaphorical — the heart's being "occupied" (mushtaghil) with worldly concerns is the metaphorical breaking of the spiritual fast, just as the stomach's occupation with food breaks the literal fast
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — the tripartite division of fasting (صوم العموم، صوم الخصوص، صوم خصوص الخصوص) employs graded specification, each level restricting and elevating the prior, moving from the corporeal (al-jawāhir) to the immaterial spiritual realities (al-laṭā'if)

5:63.arabic: ينهاهم الربانيون والأحبار عن قولهم الإثم وأكلهم السحت لبئس ما كانوا يصنعون فبين أنهم أثموا بترك النهي وقال تعالى فلولا كان من القرون من قبلكم أولوا بقية ينهون عن الفساد في الأرض الآية فبين أنه أهلك جميعهم إلا قليلا منهم كانوا ينهون عن الفساد وقال تعالى يا أيها الذين آمنوا كونوا قوامين بالقسط شهداء لله ولو على أنفسكم أو الوالدين والأقربين وذلك هو الأمر بالمعروف للوالدين والأقربين وقال تعالى لا خير في كثير من نجواهم إلا من أمر بصدقة أو معروف أو إصلاح بين الناس ومن يفعل ذلك ابتغاء مرضاة الله فسوف نؤتيه أجرا عظيما وقال تعالى وإن طائف

5:72.arabic: فلم يحطها بالنصيحة حرم الله عليه الجنة (1) ويقول إني ربما قبضت من عطائهم إرادة صلاحهم واستصلاحهم وأن يرجعوا إلى طاعتهم فيبلغ أمير المؤمنين أني قبضتها على ذلك النحو فيكتب إلى أن لا ترده فلا أستطيع رد أمره ولا أستطيع إنفاذ كتابه وحق الله ألزم من حق أمير المؤمنين والله أحق أن يطاع ولا طاعة لمخلوق في معصية الخالق فأعرض كتاب أمير المؤمنين على كتاب الله عز وجل فإن وجدته موافقا لكتاب الله فخذ به وإن وجدته مخالفا لكتاب الله فانبذه يا ابن هبيرة اتق الله فإنه يوشك أن يأتيك رسول من رب العالمين يزيلك
5:72.english: He turned to al-Shaʿbī and said: "O Abā ʿAmr! I am the trustee of the Commander of the Faithful over Iraq and his governor over it, and a man commanded to obedience. I have been tried with the subjects, and their right has become incumbent upon me. So I love to preserve them and to attend to what sets them right, along with sincere counsel (naṣīḥah) to them. And reports may reach me about a band of people from the regions concerning a matter, and I find myself severe against them therein, so I withhold a portion of their stipends and place it in the treasury (bayt al-māl), with the intention in myself that I shall return it to them. Then it reaches the Commander of the Faithful that I have withheld it in that manner, so he writes to me that I must not return it. I cannot then countermand his order, nor can I execute his letter [against my better judgment]. I am but a man commanded to obedience. Is there any liability upon me in this, and in similar matters, where the intention is as I have described?"
5:72.section_title_en: The Upright Scholars Before the Tyrannical Rulers — Counsel and Fearless Truth-Telling
5:72.anchors:
- Root: نصح (naṣaḥa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning is sincerity, faithfulness, and pure counsel free from deceit; the root denotes the act of seeking the welfare of another with complete integrity.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In theological context, naṣīḥah is the obligation of the sincere advisor to guide the ruler toward divine truth, even at personal peril, as it is a form of worship (ʿibādah) and a trust (amānah).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) usage denotes pure honey (ʿasal naṣīḥ) free from admixture; metaphorical (majāz) usage applies to counsel that is untainted by flattery or self-interest.
- Root: سلط (sulṭ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Denotes authority, power, and dominion; the ruler (sulṭān) is one who has been given sway over affairs.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In Kalam, sulṭān is a trial (ibtilāʾ) and a trust (amānah) from God, whose exercise demands justice (ʿadl) and whose neglect invites divine wrath.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal usage refers to physical power or a governing authority; metaphorical usage extends to the authority of proof (sulṭān al-burhān) that compels assent.
- Root: عظ (waʿaẓa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Root denotes admonition, exhortation, and reminding of consequences; it implies softening the heart through remembrance of God and the Hereafter.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In theological terms, ʿiẓah is the act of turning the soul away from transgression through a blend of fear (tarhīb) and hope (targhīb), grounded in revealed truth.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal usage is the verbal admonition; metaphorical usage is the admonition of circumstance (ʿiẓah al-ḥāl) when events themselves teach a lesson.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Restriction and Focused Predication (bāb al-ḥaṣr wa al-taqyīd bi-innamā) — Governing the emphasis of exclusive predication in statements of counsel, such as "No obedience to a creature in disobedience of the Creator," where the restriction (ḥaṣr) is achieved through negation and exception (nafy wa istithnāʾ).
5:72.topic: Al-Ghazali on the journey of the soul, death, and the Hereafter, from 'Enjoining Good and Forbidding Evil'

5:78.arabic: المؤمنين المنعوتين في هذه الآية وقال تعالى لعن الذين كفروا من بني إسرائيل على لسان داود وعيسى ابن مريم ذلك بما عصوا وكانوا يعتدون كانوا لا يتناهون عن منكر فعلوه لبئس ما كانوا يفعلون وهذا غاية التشديد إذ علل استحقاقهم للعنة بتركهم النهي عن المنكر وقال عز وجل كنتم خير أمة أخرجت للناس تأمرون بالمعروف وتنهون عن المنكر وهذا يدل على فضيلة الأمر بالمعروف والنهي عن المنكر إذ بين أنهم كانوا به خير أمة أخرجت للناس وقال تعالى فلما نسوا ما ذكروا به أنجينا الذين ينهون عن السوء وأخذنا الذين ظلموا بعذاب بئيس بما كانوا يفسقون فبين أنهم استفادوا النجاة بالنهي عن السوء ويدل ذلك على الوجوب أيضا وقال تعالى الذين إن مكناهم في الأرض أقاموا الصلاة وآتوا

But if all of creation were to hold back from it, the burden would encompass all those capable of it without exception.

5:78.arabic: إسرائيل على لسان داود وعيسى ابن مريم ذلك بما عصوا وكانوا يعتدون كانوا لا يتناهون عن منكر فعلوه لبئس ما كانوا يفعلون وهذا غاية التشديد إذ علل استحقاقهم للعنة بتركهم النهي عن المنكر وقال عز وجل كنتم خير أمة أخرجت للناس تأمرون بالمعروف وتنهون عن المنكر وهذا يدل على فضيلة الأمر بالمعروف والنهي عن المنكر إذ بين أنهم كانوا به خير أمة أخرجت للناس وقال تعالى فلما نسوا ما ذكروا به أنجينا الذين ينهون عن السوء وأخذنا الذين ظلموا بعذاب بئيس بما كانوا يفسقون فبين أنهم استفادوا النجاة بالنهي عن السو
5:78.english: Know that the verses indicating the obligation of commanding right and forbidding wrong are numerous. Among them is His saying, may He be exalted: {«Let there arise from among you a nation inviting to good, commanding right and forbidding wrong — and those are the successful»} (Āl ʿImrān 3:104). In this verse is the declaration of obligation, for His saying, may He be exalted, "Let there be" (wal-takun) is a command, and the apparent meaning of a command is obligation. In it also is the declaration that success (falāḥ) is contingent upon it, for He restricted it and said: {«And those are the successful»}. In it also is the declaration that it is a collective obligation (farḍ kifāyah), not an individual obligation (farḍ ʿayn), and that when a group undertakes it, the obligation falls from the rest — for He did not say, "Let all of you be commanders of right," but rather said: {«Let there arise from among you a nation»}. Thus, whenever one person or a group undertakes it, the burden falls from the others, and success is particularized to those who undertake it and directly perform it. But if all of creation were to hold back from it, the burden would encompass all those capable of it without exception.
5:78.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'The Lawful and Prohibited'

5:105.arabic: وقد قال الله تعالى يا أيها الذين آمنوا أنفقوا من طيبات ما كسبتم ومما أخرجنا لكم من الأرض ولا تيمموا الخبيث منه تنفقون ولستم بآخذيه إلا أن تغمضوا فيه أي لا تأخذوه إلا مع كراهية وحياء وهو معنى الإغماض فلا تؤثروا به ربكم وفي الخبر سبق درهم مائة ألف درهم (3) وذلك بأن يخرجه الإنسان وهو من أحل ماله وأجوده فيصدر ذلك عن الرضا والفرح بالبذل وقد يخرج مائة ألف درهم مما يكره من ماله فيدل ذلك على أنه ليس يؤثر الله عز وجل بشيء مما يحبه وبذلك ذم الله تعالى قوما جعلوا لله ما يكرهون فقال تعال
5:105.english: The heart is not treated save with the compound electuary (maʿjūn) of knowledge and works. And this condition among the conditions of almsgiving runs in the same course as humility (al-khushūʿ) runs in the prayer. This is established by his saying — may Allah bless him and grant him peace: "A man has nothing of his prayer save that of which he was conscious." And this is like his saying — may Allah bless him and grant him peace: "Allah does not accept the charity of the one who bestows it with reproach (al-mannān)." And like His saying — Exalted is He: {«لا تبطلوا صدقاتكم بالمن والأذى»} ("Do not nullify your charities by reproach and injury"). As for the legal opinion (fatwā) of the jurist that the alms fall in their proper place and that one's liability is discharged without this condition — that is another discussion, and we have already pointed to its meaning in the Book of Prayer.
5:105.section_title_en: The Inner Conditions of Charity — Section 175 (From The Revival of the Religious Sciences, Book of the Mysteries of Almsgiving)
5:105.anchors:
- Root: قلب (q-l-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "To turn, overturn, transform a thing from one state to another; to rotate, to flip"
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "قلب الشيء: تصريفه وصرفه عن وجه إلى وجه" — the heart is so named because of its constant turning and transformation between states
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "قلب الشيء قلبا: حوله عن وجهه" (to turn a thing from its face). Metaphorical: "رجل قلب حول: يقلب الأمور ويحتال" — one who turns matters over and manages them; "قلبوا لك الأمور" (they turned matters against you)
- Root: وجل (w-j-l)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "Fear, dread, apprehension that strikes the heart"
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الوجل: استشعار الخوف" — the sensing of fear; cited in {«إنما المؤمنون الذين إذا ذكر الله وجلت قلوبهم»}
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "رجل وجل، وقوم وجال" — a fearful man, a fearful people; "وفي قلبه وجل" — in his heart is dread
- Root: عجب (ʿ-j-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "Wonder, amazement; self-admiration, vanity"
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Self-admiration (al-ʿujb) is a destructive spiritual ailment that nullifies deeds
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: wonder at something extraordinary. Metaphorical: self-conceit regarding one's own acts of obedience
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد (Restriction & Focused Predication) — governing the precise limitation of general categories (al-ṣifāt al-khāṣṣah within al-aṣnāf al-thamāniyyah) and the conditional structure of acceptance

5:105.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Duties of Brotherhood'

5:105.arabic: {يا أيها الذين آمنوا عليكم أنفسكم لا يضركم من ضل إذا اهتديتم} وإنكم تضعونها في غير موضعها وإني سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول إذا رأى الناس المنكر فلم يغيروه أوشك أن يعمهم الله بعقاب (1) وقد قال صلى الله عليه وسلم إن الله ليسأل العبد حتى يقول له ما منعك إذا رأيت المنكر أن تنكره فإذا لقن الله لعبد حجته قال يا رب رجوتك وخفت الناس (2) وهذا إذا خاف من ضرب أو أمر لا يطاق ومعرفة حدود ذلك مشكلة وفيه خطر وفي العزلة خلاص وفي الأمر بالمعروف والنهي عن المنكر إثارة للخصومات وتحريك لغوائل الصدور كما قيل وكم سقت في
5:105.english: And for this reason one of the sages said: Man is only estranged from himself (innamā yastaʾnisu al-insān min nafsihi) because his essence is empty of virtue. So then he multiplies his meetings with people and drives away his loneliness by being with them. But when his essence is virtuous, he seeks solitude to aid himself in reflection (al-fikrah) and to extract knowledge and wisdom. And it has been said: "Sociability (al-istīʾnās) is among the signs of bankruptcy." So this is a great benefit — but only for certain elite individuals (al-khawāṣṣ) and for one to whom is facilitated, through perpetual remembrance (dawām al-dhikr), intimacy with God (al-uns bi-Allāh), or through perpetual reflection (dawām al-fikr), verification in the knowledge of God. For such a one, total detachment is better than everything connected with social mixing (al-mukhālaṭah).
5:105.section_title_en: The Book of the Revival of the Religious Sciences — Section 449: On the Benefits of Seclusion (Fawāʾid al-ʿUzlah)
5:105.anchors:
- Root: انس (ʾ-n-s)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of sociability, familiarity, and the dispelling of loneliness through company; the opposite of waḥshah (wilderness-like solitude).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-ʿuns is the heart's repose through the presence of what is beloved; its highest form is al-uns bi-Allāh — the soul's intimate familiarity with God achieved through perpetual remembrance (dhikr).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): human companionship. Metaphorical (majāz): "He is the son of the intimacy of so-and-so" — i.e., his special confidant; and the fire is called al-ʾanīsah because it dispels the night's loneliness.
- Root: خلط (kh-l-ṭ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The mixing or blending of two or more things; a companion, neighbor, or partner is called khalīṭ.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-khalṭ is the union of parts of two or more things — broader than mazj (fusion). From it derives khalīṭān (two partners) in jurisprudence.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: mixing water with wine. Metaphorical: "I mixed with so-and-so" — meaning intimate social intercourse; "he is my khalīṭ in trade" — i.e., my partner. The verse {«وَإِنَّ كَثِيرًا مِنَ الْخُلَطَاءِ لَيَبْغِي بَعْضُهُمْ عَلَى بَعْضٍ»} (Ṣād: 24) — "And indeed many partners oppress one another."
- Root: غيب (gh-y-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: That which is hidden from the eye; absence.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-ghayb is what is concealed from the senses and from human knowledge — but nothing is ghayb with respect to God, for nothing is hidden from Him.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "I met him at the setting of the sun" (ghaybūbat al-shams). Metaphorical: "They came in a ghābah" — i.e., amidst dense spears like tangled trees.
- Root: نكر (n-k-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Disapproval, rejection, or failure to recognize.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-inkār is the opposite of recognition (ʿirfān); the heart's rejection of what it does not conceive. It is also used for verbal disapproval — and the command to disapprove evil (al-nahy ʿan al-munkar) is a pillar of religion.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "I disapproved of the thing" (ankartu al-shayʾ). Metaphorical: the tongue may deny what the heart affirms — thus hypocrisy enters.
- Sibawayh Rule: Bāb al-ḥaṣr wa-al-taqyīd bi-innamā (Restriction and Focused Predication) — The particle innamā restricts the predicate to the subject alone, as in the sage's saying: "إنما يستوحش الإنسان من نفسه" — restricting the cause of spiritual loneliness to the soul's emptiness of virtue, not to the absence of companions.
5:105.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Enjoining Good and Forbidding Evil'

6:68.arabic: قال الله تعالى لنبيه {فاعرض عنهم حتى يخوضوا في حديث غيره} ومهما كان كلامه مائلا إلى الإرجاء وتجرئة الناس على المعاصي وكان الناس يزدادون بكلامه جراءة وبعفو الله وبرحمته وثوقا يزيد بسببه رجاؤهم على خوفهم فهو منكر ويجب منعه عنه لأن فساد ذلك عظيم بل لو رجح خوفهم على رجائهم فذلك أليق وأقرب بطباع الخلق فإنهم إلى الخوف أحوج وإنما العدل تعديل الخوف والرجاء كما قال عمر رضي الله عنه لو نادى مناد يوم القيامة ليدخل النار كل الناس إلا رجلا واحدا لرجوت أن أكون أنا ذلك الرجل ولو نادى مناد ليدخل الجنة كل الناس إلا رج
6:68.english: God the Exalted said to His Prophet: {«So turn away from them until they engage in a discourse other than that»} (6:68). And whenever his speech inclines toward irjāʾ (deferring judgment, i.e., the doctrine that sins do not harm faith) and emboldening people toward acts of disobedience, and the people increase through his speech in audacity and in trust in God's pardon and His mercy, such that their hope (rajāʾ) is increased by it over their fear (khawf) — then this is a reprehensible evil (munkar), and he must be prevented from it, for the corruption of that is immense. Rather, even if their fear outweighs their hope, that is more fitting and nearer to the natural constitution of creatures, for they are in greater need of fear. Justice is only the balancing of fear and hope, as ʿUmar (may God be pleased with him) said: "If a crier were to call out on the Day of Resurrection, 'Let every person enter the Fire except one man,' I would hope that I were that man. And if a crier were to call out, 'Let every person enter Paradise except one man,' I would fear that I were that man."
6:68.section_title_en: The Revival of the Religious Sciences — Section 545: On the Preacher, the Storyteller, and the Reciter; and the Regulations of the Mosque
6:68.anchors:
- Root: قصص (qaṣaṣa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The root denotes the tracing of a matter, following its traces and narrating its account; al-qaṣaṣ is the narration of reports and tales.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-qaṣaṣ is the seeking of a matter's trace and its exposition; the qāṣṣ (storyteller) is one who narrates accounts to admonish and remind.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: qaṣaṣa atharah — he followed his trace. Metaphorical: qaṣṣa ʿalayhi al-khabar — he narrated the report to him, as if tracing its unfolding.
- Root: وعظ (waʿaẓa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Al-waʿẓ is admonition and exhortation, combining reminder of good with the softening of the heart through warning and counsel.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-waʿẓ is the reminder of hearts through speech that softens, whether by way of enticement (targhīb) or intimidation (tarhīb).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: waʿaẓahu — he admonished him. Metaphorical: it is the speech that penetrates the heart and leaves its effect upon it, as if branding it with counsel.
- Root: بدع (badaʿa)
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-bidʿah is a novel matter (muḥdath) introduced into religion after the prophetic era, not sanctioned by the Book, the Sunnah, or consensus.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: badaʿa al-shayʾ — he originated it without precedent. Metaphorical: the innovator (mubtadiʿ) is one who introduces into the religion what is not from it.
- Root: خوف (khāfa)
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-khawf is the anticipation of something disliked based on a probable or certain indication; it is opposed by amn (security). The balanced servant alternates between khawf and rajāʾ (hope), for each alone is blameworthy.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: khiftuhu — I feared him. Metaphorical: takhawwufahu — to diminish it gradually, as if taking from its edges out of caution.
- Root: حضر (ḥaḍara)
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-ḥaḍar is the opposite of badw (nomadism); then it was made a term for the presence of a place, a person, or an affair.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: ḥaḍartu al-majlis — I attended the session. Metaphorical: aḥḍir dhihnaka — be attentive and present of mind.
- Sibawayh Rule: Bāb al-ḥaṣr wa-al-taqyīd bi-innamā (Restriction and Specification by innamā) — When the predicate is restricted to the subject by innamā, it negates the attribute from all others and affirms it solely for the restricted one, as in "innamā al-ʿadl taʿdīl al-khawf wa-al-rajāʾ" (justice is only the balancing of fear and hope).
6:68.topic: Al-Ghazali on the journey of the soul, death, and the Hereafter, from 'Enjoining Good and Forbidding Evil'

6:68.arabic: سلام عليكم وأمره بالإعراض عن غيرهم فقال وإذا رأيت الذين يخوضون في آياتنا فأعرض عنهم حتى قال فلا تقعد بعد الذكرى مع القوم الظالمبن وقال تعالى واصبر نفسك مع الذين يدعون ربهم بالغداة والعشي فكذلك الانبساط والإدلال يحتمل من بعض العباد دون بعض فمن انبساط الأنس قول موسى عليه السلام إن هي إلا فتنتك تضل بها من تشاء وتهدي من تشاء وقوله في التعليل والاعتذار لما قيل له اذهب إلى فرعون {فقال} ولهم على ذنب وقوله إني أخاف أن يكذبون ويضيق صدري ولا ينطلق لساني وقوله إننا نخاف أن يفرط علينا أو أن يطغى وهذا من غير موسى عليه السلام من سوء الأدب لأن الذ
6:68.english: As for Adam (peace be upon him), it was said concerning him: {«وعصى آدم ربه فغوى»} "And Adam disobeyed his Lord, so he went astray" (Q. 20:121), then {«اجتباه ربه فتاب عليه وهدى»} "his Lord chose him, and turned to him in forgiveness, and guided him" (Q. 20:122).
6:68.section_title_en: On the Varieties of Divine Proximity (Al-Inbisāṭ) and Awe (Al-Haybah) in the States of the Prophets and Saints
6:68.anchors:
- Root: بسط (B-S-T)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning is "to spread out, extend, expand" — both physically (basting a garment) and metaphorically.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: "بسط الشيء: نشره وتوسيعه" — used for expansion of mercy, favor, and the soul's comfort. In Kalam, it contrasts with *qabḍ* (contraction/withholding).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): "بسط الثوب والفراش إذا نشره." Metaphorical (Majaz): "بسطني ما بسطك" (what pleases you pleases me) — hence *inbisāṭ* here denotes the soul's expansive intimacy with God, a spiritual state, not a physical act.
- Root: أبلس (B-L-S)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "أبلس: انقطعت حجته ويئس" — to be reduced to silence, to despair.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الإبلاس: الحزن المعترض من شدة اليأس" — the despair of Iblis is a theological state of being cut off from mercy.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: despair/silence. Metaphorical: Iblis (the proper name) is derived from this root — he is the one "despairing" of divine mercy.
- Root: عله (not used; avoided per instruction) — *Note: The text's key term "الإدلال" (al-idlāl) is from root دلو (D-L-W).*
- Root: دلو (D-L-W)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "دلا الدلو: أخرجها من البئر" — to draw water from a well; hence *iddalā'a* (إدلال) means to advance boldly, relying on a familiar bond.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Not a primary Quranic term, but lexically implies confident approach based on prior intimacy.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: lowering the bucket. Metaphorical: "أدلّ عليه" — to act with bold familiarity toward someone who loves you, trusting in their affection.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — Applied in the phrase "فإنما هي عند ذوي الاعتبار من الأسماء" (they are but names to those who reflect), restricting the ontological status of stories to mere signifiers for the discerning.
6:68.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Love, Longing, Intimacy and Contentment'

6:68.arabic: فأعرض عنهم حتى قال فلا تقعد بعد الذكرى مع القوم الظالمبن وقال تعالى واصبر نفسك مع الذين يدعون ربهم بالغداة والعشي فكذلك الانبساط والإدلال يحتمل من بعض العباد دون بعض فمن انبساط الأنس قول موسى عليه السلام إن هي إلا فتنتك تضل بها من تشاء وتهدي من تشاء وقوله في التعليل والاعتذار لما قيل له اذهب إلى فرعون {فقال} ولهم على ذنب وقوله إني أخاف أن يكذبون ويضيق صدري ولا ينطلق لساني وقوله إننا نخاف أن يفرط علينا أو أن يطغى وهذا من غير موسى عليه السلام من سوء الأدب لأن الذي أقيم مقام الأنس يلاطف ويحتمل ولم يحتمل ل

7:61.arabic: هبيرة اتق الله فإنه يوشك أن يأتيك رسول من رب العالمين يزيلك عن سريرك ويخرجك من سعة قصرك إلى ضيق قبرك فتدع سلطانك ودنياك خلف ظهرك وتقدم على ربك وتنزل على عملك يا ابن هبيرة إن الله ليمنعك من يزيد ولا يمنعك يزيد من الله وإن أمر الله فوق كل أمر وإنه لا طاعة في معصية الله وإني أحذرك بأسه الذي لا يرد عن القوم المجرمين فقال ابن هبيرة أربع على ظلعك أيها الشيخ وأعرض عن ذكر أمير المؤمنين فإن أمير المؤمنين صاحب العلم وصاحب الحكم وصاحب الفضل وإنما ولاه الله تعالى ما ولاه من أمر هذه الأمة لعلمه به وما يعلمه من ف
7:61.english: He turned to al-Shaʿbī and said: "O Abā ʿAmr! I am the trustee of the Commander of the Faithful over Iraq and his governor over it, and a man commanded to obedience. I have been tried with the subjects, and their right has become incumbent upon me. So I love to preserve them and to attend to what sets them right, along with sincere counsel (naṣīḥah) to them. And reports may reach me about a band of people from the regions concerning a matter, and I find myself severe against them therein, so I withhold a portion of their stipends and place it in the treasury (bayt al-māl), with the intention in myself that I shall return it to them. Then it reaches the Commander of the Faithful that I have withheld it in that manner, so he writes to me that I must not return it. I cannot then countermand his order, nor can I execute his letter [against my better judgment]. I am but a man commanded to obedience. Is there any liability upon me in this, and in similar matters, where the intention is as I have described?"
7:61.section_title_en: The Upright Scholars Before the Tyrannical Rulers — Counsel and Fearless Truth-Telling
7:61.anchors:
- Root: نصح (naṣaḥa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning is sincerity, faithfulness, and pure counsel free from deceit; the root denotes the act of seeking the welfare of another with complete integrity.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In theological context, naṣīḥah is the obligation of the sincere advisor to guide the ruler toward divine truth, even at personal peril, as it is a form of worship (ʿibādah) and a trust (amānah).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) usage denotes pure honey (ʿasal naṣīḥ) free from admixture; metaphorical (majāz) usage applies to counsel that is untainted by flattery or self-interest.
- Root: سلط (sulṭ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Denotes authority, power, and dominion; the ruler (sulṭān) is one who has been given sway over affairs.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In Kalam, sulṭān is a trial (ibtilāʾ) and a trust (amānah) from God, whose exercise demands justice (ʿadl) and whose neglect invites divine wrath.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal usage refers to physical power or a governing authority; metaphorical usage extends to the authority of proof (sulṭān al-burhān) that compels assent.
- Root: عظ (waʿaẓa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Root denotes admonition, exhortation, and reminding of consequences; it implies softening the heart through remembrance of God and the Hereafter.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In theological terms, ʿiẓah is the act of turning the soul away from transgression through a blend of fear (tarhīb) and hope (targhīb), grounded in revealed truth.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal usage is the verbal admonition; metaphorical usage is the admonition of circumstance (ʿiẓah al-ḥāl) when events themselves teach a lesson.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Restriction and Focused Predication (bāb al-ḥaṣr wa al-taqyīd bi-innamā) — Governing the emphasis of exclusive predication in statements of counsel, such as "No obedience to a creature in disobedience of the Creator," where the restriction (ḥaṣr) is achieved through negation and exception (nafy wa istithnāʾ).

7:157.arabic: في الناس يأمرهم بالمعروف وينهاهم عن المنكر ولم يكن مأمورا من عنده بذلك فأمر بأن يدل عليه فلما صار بين يديه قال له إنني بلغني أنك رأيت نفسك أهلا للأمر بالمعروف والنهي عن المنكر من غير أن نأمرك وكان المأمون جالسا على كرسي ينظر في
7:157.english: Allah has condemned pride in numerous places of His Book, and has condemned every tyrant (jabbār) and arrogant one. He, exalted, said: {«سأصرف عن آياتي الذين يتكبرون في الأرض بغير الحق»} — "I shall turn away from My signs those who behave arrogantly upon the earth without right." And He, mighty and majestic, said: {«كذلك يطبع الله على كل قلب متكبر جبار»} — "Thus does Allah seal the heart of every arrogant tyrant." And He said: {«واستفتحوا وخاب كل جبار عنيد»} — "And they sought victory, and every obstinate tyrant was disappointed." And He said: {«إنه لا يحب المستكبرين»} — "Truly He does not love the arrogant." And He said: {«لقد استكبروا في أنفسهم وعتوا عتوا كبيرا»} — "They were arrogant within themselves and transgressed with great transgression." And He said: {«إن الذين يستكبرون عن عبادتي سيدخلون جهنم داخرين»} — "Those who are too proud to worship Me shall enter Hell, humiliated." The condemnation of pride in the Qur'an is abundant.
7:157.section_title_en: Section 527 — On the Condemnation of Pride: Narrations of the Pious Predecessors and Enjoining Good Before Rulers
7:157.anchors:
- Root: كرم (karuma)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of nobility, generosity, and honor; the root denotes the quality of being noble in character and action.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): When attributed to Allah, it signifies His manifest beneficence and grace; when attributed to humans, it denotes praiseworthy character traits and deeds that appear from them — one is not called "noble" (karīm) until such virtue manifests.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): "كرم علينا فلان كرامة" — he showed us honor. Metaphorical (Majaz): "كرم السحاب تكريما: جاد بمطره" — the cloud was generous with its rain; the term extends to any abundant giving.
- Root: حسن (ḥasuna)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Beauty, goodness, and excellence in form and character.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الحسن: عبارة عن كل مبهج مرغوب فيه" — that which is pleasing and desirable, divided into what is deemed good by intellect, by desire, and by sense-perception.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "أنظر إلى محاسن وجهه" — behold the beauties of his face. Metaphorical: "فلان لا يحسن شيئا" — he does not do anything well; "قيمة المرء ما يحسن" — a man's worth is what he does well.
- Root: وجه (wajaha)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The face; the foremost and most honored part of a thing.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The face is the first thing one encounters and the noblest of the outward body; hence it is used for the essence and the foremost aspect of every matter.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "واجهته مواجهة" — I faced him directly. Metaphorical: "هؤلاء وجوه البلد" — these are the notables of the land; "رجل وجيه" — a man of standing and honor.
- Root: نصر (naṣara)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Aid, assistance, and victory.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "النصر والنصرة: العون" — help and support; used of Allah's aid to His prophets and believers.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "نصره الله تعالى على عدوه" — Allah aided him against his enemy. Metaphorical: "أرض منصورة: مغيثة" — a land watered by rain; rain itself is called "نصر" (aid) as it brings life to the earth.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The permissibility of interposing elements between a preposition and its object when the intervening phrase is complete and the meaning remains clear, as in the rhetorical constructions of admonition and rebuke found in these narrations.
7:157.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Enjoining Good and Forbidding Evil'

7:157.arabic: الله تعالى للمؤمنين في قولهم {ولا تحمل علينا إصرا} وقال تعالى {ويضع عنهم إصرهم والأغلال التي كانت عليهم} وروى محمد بن الحنفية عن علي رضي الله تعالى عنهما أنه قال لما نزل قوله تعالى {فاصفح الصفح الجميل} قال يا جبريل وما الصفح الجميل قال عليه السلام إذا عفوت عمن ظلمك فلا تعاتبه فقال يا جبريل فالله تعالى أكرم من أن يعاتب من عفا عنه فبكى جبريل وبكى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فبعث الله تعالى إليهما ميكائيل عليه السلام وقال إن ربكما يقرئكما السلام ويقول كيف أعاتب من عفوت عنه هذا ما لا يشبه كرمي (1) والأخبار الواردة في أسباب ال
7:157.english: In the report (khabar): "Were you not to sin, God would create a creation who would sin, and He would forgive them." (1) In another wording: "He would take you away and bring a creation who would sin, and He would forgive them — verily, He is the Forgiving, the Merciful." And in the report: "Were you not to sin, I would fear for you what is worse than sins." It was said: "And what is that?" He said: "Self-amazement (al-ʿujb)." (2)
7:157.section_title_en: The Completion of the Matter — On the Preacher's Gentleness in Employing Reports of Fear and Hope
7:157.anchors:
- Root: لطف (luṭf)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Gentleness, subtlety, kindness in approach; to be gracious and delicate in manner.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Divine gentleness (luṭf) as an attribute of God's subtle providence; here, the preacher's emulation of prophetic gentleness in spiritual counsel.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) — physical softness; metaphorical (majāz) — refinement of speech and manner suited to the spiritual state of the listener.
- Root: رجا (rajā')
  * Lisan / Ayn: Hope, expectation of good; the opposite of despair (ya's).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Hope in God's mercy as a theological virtue balancing fear (khawf); the state of the believer who relies on divine generosity over personal merit.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — anticipation of a future good; metaphorical — the soul's reliance on God's pardon despite sin.
- Root: عجب (ʿajab)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Self-amazement, vanity, wonder at oneself.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Spiritual pride (ʿujb) — a hidden sin worse than overt transgression, as it nullifies deeds.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — astonishment; metaphorical — the heart's complacency in its own obedience, leading to ruin.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد (Restriction and Specification) — The conditional and exceptive structures (law lā... la-khalaqa, illā an yataghammadani) govern the precise scope of divine mercy and human agency.
7:157.topic: Al-Ghazali on purifying the character, moral diseases, and spiritual remedies, from 'Fear and Hope'

7:157.arabic: لله وأوصلهم لرحمه وآمرهم بالمعروف وأنهاهم عن المنكر (4) وقال أبو ذر رضي الله عنه أوصاني خليلي عليه السلام بصلة الرحم وإن أدبرت وأمرني أن أقول الحق وإن كان مرا (5) وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم إن الرحم معلقة بالعرش وليس الواصل بالمكافئ ولكن الواصل الذي إذا انقطعت رحمه وصلها (6) وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم إن أعجل الطاعة ثوابا صلة الرحم حتى إن أهل البيت ليكونون فجارا فتنموا أموالهم ويكثر عددهم إذا وصلوا أرحامهم (7) وقال زيد بن أسلم لما خرج رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إلى مكة عرض له رجل فقال إن كنت تر
7:157.english: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said — Allah Most High declares: "I am al-Raḥmān (the Merciful), and this is the raḥim (womb-relationship). I have split for it a name from My name. Whoever joins it, I join him; and whoever cuts it, I cut him off." (1)
7:157.section_title_en: The Rights of Kinsfolk and the Womb-Relationship (Ḥuqūq al-Aqārib wa al-Raḥim)
7:157.anchors:
- Root: رحم (Ra-Ḥa-Mīm)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The womb, the organ of gestation; by extension, the bond of kinship that issues from shared uterine origin. Al-Farahidi notes its derivation from mercy (raḥmah), as the womb is the locus of compassion's first manifestation.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Raḥim denotes both the physical womb and the relational bond of consanguinity. Allah's attribute al-Raḥmān is that mercy which encompasses all creation, while the raḥim is that specific bond which He has named from His own name, indicating a divinely instituted correspondence between human kinship-ties and divine mercy.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): the womb as physical organ. Metaphorical (majāz): the kinship-bond itself, as in "waṣala raḥimahu" (he joined his womb-relation), meaning he maintained the ties of kinship. The prophetic ḥadīth "al-raḥim muʿallaqah bi-al-ʿarsh" employs personification as rhetorical emphasis of its cosmic significance.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الإضافة والمعنى الإسنادي (Construct Phrase & Predicative Meaning) — The phrase "ḥuqūq al-aqārib" is an annexation (iḍāfah) where the first term (ḥuqūq) is unspecified in definiteness by the second (al-aqārib), yielding "rights of the kinsfolk" — a genitive construction indicating that these rights inhere in the very nature of the kinship relation itself.
7:157.topic: Classical commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya Ulum al-Din, from 'Duties of Brotherhood'

7:157.arabic: وقيل لداود الطائي رحمه الله أرأيت رجلا دخل على هؤلاء الأمراء فأمرهم بالمعروف ونهاهم عن المنكر فقال أخاف عليه السوط قال إنه يقوى عليه قال أخاف عليه السيف قال إنه يقوى عليه قال أخاف عليه الداء الدفين وهو العجب الدرجة الرابعة السب والتعنيف بالقول الغليظ الخشن وذلك يعدل إليه عند العجز عن المنع باللطف وظهور مبادىء الإصرار والاستهزاء بالوعظ والنصح وذلك مثل قول إبراهيم عليه السلام أف لكم ولما تعبدون من دون الله أفلا تعقلون ولسنا نعني بالسب والفحش بما فيه نسبة إلى الزنا ومقدماته ولا الكذب بل أن يخاطبه بما فيه مما لا يعد من جملة الفحش كقوله يا ف
7:157.english: And at this point it is said to him what was said to Jesus, peace be upon him: "O son of Mary, exhort yourself; if you are admonished, then exhort the people — and if not, then be ashamed before Me."
7:157.section_title_en: The Revival of the Religious Sciences — Section 540: On Gentleness in Forbidding Wrong and the Hidden Diseases of the Enjoiner
7:157.anchors:
- Root: لطف (luṭf)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Gentleness, subtlety, refinement; the opposite of harshness and roughness
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Divine gentleness (luṭf) as that which draws the servant toward obedience through kindness rather than compulsion
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical softness/delicacy; Metaphorical: kindness of manner and speech in dealing with others
- Root: عجب (ʿujb)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Self-admiration; the soul's being pleased with itself and its own states
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): A hidden disease of the heart wherein one admires his own qualities, forgetting that they are divine gifts
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: wonder/astonishment; Metaphorical: the soul's complacent delight in its own excellence
- Root: حسب (ḥasaba)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To reckon, count, account; the one who enjoins right and forbids wrong (muḥtasib)
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The act of calling to account; the muḥtasib as one who holds himself and others to divine standards
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: numerical reckoning; Metaphorical: moral accountability and the office of the public censor
- Sibawayh Rule: باب التدرج في الأحكام (Graduated Progression of Rulings) — The text moves through ascending degrees of severity in forbidding wrong, each stage conditional upon the failure of the preceding, requiring precise syntactic parsing of conditional and concessive clauses.

7:165.arabic: فلما نسوا ما ذكروا به أنجينا الذين ينهون عن السوء وأخذنا الذين ظلموا بعذاب بئيس بما كانوا يفسقون فبين أنهم استفادوا النجاة بالنهي عن السوء ويدل ذلك على الوجوب أيضا وقال تعالى الذين إن مكناهم في الأرض أقاموا الصلاة وآتوا الزكاة وأمروا بالمعروف ونهوا عن المنكر فقرن ذلك بالصلاة والزكاة في نعت الصالحين والمؤمنين وقال تعالى وتعاونوا على البر والتقوى ولا تعاونوا على الإثم والعدوان وهو أمر جزم ومعنى التعاون الحث عليه وتسهيل طرق الخير وسد سبل الشر والعدوان بحسب الإمكان وقال تعالى لولا ينهاهم الربانيون والأحبار عن قولهم الإثم وأكلهم السحت لبئس ما كانوا يصنعون ف
7:165.english: Know that the verses indicating the obligation of commanding right and forbidding wrong are numerous. Among them is His saying, may He be exalted: {«Let there arise from among you a nation inviting to good, commanding right and forbidding wrong — and those are the successful»} (Āl ʿImrān 3:104). In this verse is the declaration of obligation, for His saying, may He be exalted, "Let there be" (wal-takun) is a command, and the apparent meaning of a command is obligation. In it also is the declaration that success (falāḥ) is contingent upon it, for He restricted it and said: {«And those are the successful»}. In it also is the declaration that it is a collective obligation (farḍ kifāyah), not an individual obligation (farḍ ʿayn), and that when a group undertakes it, the obligation falls from the rest — for He did not say, "Let all of you be commanders of right," but rather said: {«Let there arise from among you a nation»}. Thus, whenever one person or a group undertakes it, the burden falls from the others, and success is particularized to those who undertake it and directly perform it. But if all of creation were to hold back from it, the burden would encompass all those capable of it without exception.

10:41.arabic: أغني عنكم من الله شيئا إن لي عملي ولكم عملكم (3) وقد قال عمر بن الخطاب رضي الله عنه لا يقيم أمر الناس إلا حصيف العقل أريب العقد لا يطلع منه على عورة ولا يخاف منه على حرة ولا تأخذه في الله لومة لائم وقال الأمراء أربعة فأمير قوي ظلف نفسه وعماله فذلك كالمجاهد في سبيل الله يد الله باسطة عليه بالرحمة وأمير فيه ضعف ظلف نفسه وأرتع عماله لضعفه فهو على شفا هلاك إلا أن يرحمه الله وأمير ظلف عماله وأرتع نفسه فذلك الحطمة الذي قال فيه رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم شر الرعاة الحطمة فهو الهالك وحده (
10:41.english: He turned to al-Shaʿbī and said: "O Abā ʿAmr! I am the trustee of the Commander of the Faithful over Iraq and his governor over it, and a man commanded to obedience. I have been tried with the subjects, and their right has become incumbent upon me. So I love to preserve them and to attend to what sets them right, along with sincere counsel (naṣīḥah) to them. And reports may reach me about a band of people from the regions concerning a matter, and I find myself severe against them therein, so I withhold a portion of their stipends and place it in the treasury (bayt al-māl), with the intention in myself that I shall return it to them. Then it reaches the Commander of the Faithful that I have withheld it in that manner, so he writes to me that I must not return it. I cannot then countermand his order, nor can I execute his letter [against my better judgment]. I am but a man commanded to obedience. Is there any liability upon me in this, and in similar matters, where the intention is as I have described?"
10:41.section_title_en: The Upright Scholars Before the Tyrannical Rulers — Counsel and Fearless Truth-Telling
10:41.anchors:
- Root: نصح (naṣaḥa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning is sincerity, faithfulness, and pure counsel free from deceit; the root denotes the act of seeking the welfare of another with complete integrity.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In theological context, naṣīḥah is the obligation of the sincere advisor to guide the ruler toward divine truth, even at personal peril, as it is a form of worship (ʿibādah) and a trust (amānah).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) usage denotes pure honey (ʿasal naṣīḥ) free from admixture; metaphorical (majāz) usage applies to counsel that is untainted by flattery or self-interest.
- Root: سلط (sulṭ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Denotes authority, power, and dominion; the ruler (sulṭān) is one who has been given sway over affairs.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In Kalam, sulṭān is a trial (ibtilāʾ) and a trust (amānah) from God, whose exercise demands justice (ʿadl) and whose neglect invites divine wrath.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal usage refers to physical power or a governing authority; metaphorical usage extends to the authority of proof (sulṭān al-burhān) that compels assent.
- Root: عظ (waʿaẓa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Root denotes admonition, exhortation, and reminding of consequences; it implies softening the heart through remembrance of God and the Hereafter.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In theological terms, ʿiẓah is the act of turning the soul away from transgression through a blend of fear (tarhīb) and hope (targhīb), grounded in revealed truth.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal usage is the verbal admonition; metaphorical usage is the admonition of circumstance (ʿiẓah al-ḥāl) when events themselves teach a lesson.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Restriction and Focused Predication (bāb al-ḥaṣr wa al-taqyīd bi-innamā) — Governing the emphasis of exclusive predication in statements of counsel, such as "No obedience to a creature in disobedience of the Creator," where the restriction (ḥaṣr) is achieved through negation and exception (nafy wa istithnāʾ).
10:41.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Enjoining Good and Forbidding Evil'

12:67.arabic: فإن قلت فقد قال صلى الله عليه وسلم بعد قوله لفاطمة وصفية إني لا أغني عنكما من الله شيئا إلا أن لكم رحما سأبلها ببلالها (1) حديث أترجو سليم شفاعتي ولا ترجوها بنو عبد المطلب أخرجه الطبراني في الأوسط من حديث عبد الله بن جعفر وفيه أصيرم بن حوشب عن إسحاق بن واصل وكلاهما ضعيف جدا فذلك يدل على أنه سيخصص قرابته بالشفاعة فاعلم أن كل مسلم فهو منتظر شفاعة رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم والنسيب أيضا جدير بأن يرجوها لكن بشرط أن يتقي الله أن يغضب عليه فإنه إن يغضب عليه فلا يأذن لأحد في شفاعته لأن الذنوب منقسمة إلى ما يوجب المقت فلا يؤذن في ال
12:67.english: If you say: "He, peace and blessings be upon him, said after his words to Fāṭimah and Ṣafiyyah: 'I cannot avail you against God in anything, except that you have a tie of kinship which I will moisten with its moisture'" — a ḥadīth [reported as]: "Do you hope for my intercession, while the Banū ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib do not hope for it?" — narrated by al-Ṭabarānī in al-Awsaṭ from the narration of ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jaʿfar, and in it is Uṣayrim ibn Ḥawshab from Isḥāq ibn Wāṣil, and both are extremely weak — so that indicates that he will single out his relatives for intercession.
12:67.section_title_en: Section 882 — On the Limits of Intercession, the Vices of Pride in Lineage, Numbers, Wealth, and Opinion, and Their Treatment
12:67.anchors:
- Root: شفع (Sh-F-')
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning is pairing or joining; intercession (shafā'ah) is the joining of one's plea to another's cause.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Intercession is the seeking of benefit for another; its acceptance is contingent upon divine permission and good pleasure, as restricted by the Qur'anic qualifiers.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (haqīqah) is the act of making a number even (from watr, odd); metaphorical (majāz) is the mediator's plea before authority.
- Root: عجب (ʿ-J-B)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Astonishment arising from an unknown cause; self-admiration (ʿujb) is a blameworthy state of being pleased with oneself.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "العجب والتعجب: حالة تعرض للإنسان عند الجهل بسبب الشيء" — a state that overtakes a person due to ignorance of the cause; hence, it is impossible regarding God.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: a wondrous thing; metaphorical: the one who performs marvels (taʿjābah). Self-admiration is the root of every error and innovation.
- Root: رأي (R-'-Y)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Opinion, view, or judgment formed through reflection.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Ra'y is the considered opinion that may err or hit the mark; it is blameworthy when it becomes an object of ʿujb (self-admiration).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: sight/vision; metaphorical: intellectual insight. The ḥadīth "إعجاب كل ذي رأي برأيه" (the admiration of every man of opinion for his own view) is cited as a sign of the age's corruption.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد (Restriction and Qualification) — The conditional clauses (in-sharṭ) governing intercession, e.g., {إلا لمن ارتضى} and {إلا بإذنه}, impose necessary restrictions that negate any absolute reliance on intercession.
12:67.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'Condemnation of Pride and Conceit'

17:26.arabic: على شيء وقال تعالى ولا تبذر تبذيرا إن المبذرين كانوا إخوان الشياطين وكذلك قال عز وجل والذين إذا أنفقوا لم يسرفوا ولم يقتروا فمن يسرف هذا الإسراف ينكر عليه ويجب على القاضي أن يحجر عليه إلا إذا كان الرجل وحده وكان له قوة في التوكل صادقة فله أن ينفق جميع ماله في أبواب البر ومن له عيال أو كان عاجزا عن التوكل فليس له أن يتصدق بجميع ماله وكذلك لو صرف جميع ماله إلى نقوش حيطانه وتزيين بنيانه فهو أيضا إسراف محرم وفعل ذلك ممن له مال كثير ليس بحرام لأن التزيين من الأغراض الصحيحة ولم تزل المساجد تزين وتنقش أبواب
17:26.english: And excess varies according to circumstances. Thus we say: whoever possesses only one hundred dinars, for example, and has with him his dependents and children, and they have no means of livelihood other than it, and he spends all of it upon a banquet — he is an extravagant one who must be prevented. God, exalted be He, said: «ولا تبسطها كل البسط فتقعد ملوما محسورا» — "And do not spread it forth with all spreading, lest you sit down blamed and exhausted" — and this was revealed concerning a man in Medina who divided all his wealth and left nothing for his dependents; he was then demanded for maintenance and could not produce anything. And God, exalted be He, said: «ولا تبذر تبذيرا إن المبذرين كانوا إخوان الشياطين» — "And do not squander with squandering; indeed, the squanderers are brothers of the devils." And likewise He, mighty and majestic, said: «والذين إذا أنفقوا لم يسرفوا ولم يقتروا» — "And those who, when they spend, are neither extravagant nor niggardly." So whoever commits this extravagance is to be denounced, and it is obligatory upon the judge to place him under legal interdiction (ḥajr) — except if the man be alone [without dependents] and possess true strength in trust in God (tawakkul), then he may spend all his wealth upon the gates of righteousness. But whoever has dependents, or is incapable of [true] trust in God, it is not for him to give in charity all his wealth.
17:26.section_title_en: Section 549 — On Sitting with a Sinner Without Necessity, and Related Rulings on Silk, Gold, Extravagance, and Permissible Merriment

  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Extravagance (isrāf) is transgressing the bound in every deed a person performs, whether in expenditure or otherwise; it is considered with regard to both quantity and quality — spending in disobedience to God is extravagance even if little.

  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Falsehood is said of both utterance and action; the hypocrites' claim of faith was true in words but false in conviction — hence God declared them liars regarding their belief, not their speech.
