17:29.arabic: قال تعالى {وكلوا واشربوا ولا تسرفوا} وقال تعالى {ولا تجعل يدك مغلولة إلى عنقك ولا تبسطها كل البسط} وقد قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم خيركم خيركم لأهله (5) وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم دينار أنفقته في سبيل الله ودينار أنفقته في رقبة ودينار تصدقت به على مسكين ودينار أنفقته على أهلك أعظمها أجرا الذي أنفقته على أهلك (6) وقيل كان لعلي رضي الله عنه أربع نسوة فكان يشتري لكل واحدة في كل أربعة أيام لحما بدرهم وقال الحسن رضي الله عنه كانوا في الرجال مخاصيب والإناث والثياب مجاديب وقال ابن سيرين يستحب للرجل أن يعمل لأهله في كل جمعة فالوذجة وكأن الحلاوة وإن
17:29.english: The first point of etiquette is the wedding feast (walīmah), and it is recommended (mustaḥabbah). Anas, may God be pleased with him, said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, saw upon ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf, may God be pleased with him, a trace of yellow dye, so he said: {«What is this?»} He replied: "I have married a woman for the weight of a date-stone in gold." He said: "May God bless you. Hold a wedding feast, even if with a single sheep." {«...»} And the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, held a wedding feast for Ṣafiyyah with dates and sawīq (barley porridge). {«...»} And he, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: "The food of the first day is an obligation (ḥaqq), the food of the second day is a Sunnah, and the food of the third day is for show (sumʿah); and whoever seeks to be heard, God will make his deeds heard." {«...»} None raised this hadith except Ziyād ibn ʿAbd Allāh, and it is anomalous (gharīb). It is recommended to offer congratulations to him, and the one who enters upon the husband should say: "May God bless you and shower blessings upon you, and may He bring you both together in goodness." {«...»} Abū Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him, reported that he, may God bless him and grant him peace, commanded this. It is also recommended to make the marriage public (iẓhār al-nikāḥ). He, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: "The distinction between the lawful and the unlawful is the drum and the voice." {«...»} The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: "Announce this marriage, hold it in the mosques, and beat drums for it." {«...»} And on the authority of al-Rubayyiʿ bint Muʿawwidh, she said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came and entered on the morning of my wedding night, and he sat upon my bedding, and we had young girls with us who were beating their drums and lamenting those of my forefathers who had been killed—until one of them said: "And among us is a Prophet who knows what will be tomorrow." He said to her: "Stop this, and say what you were saying before." {«...»}
17:29.section_title_en: On What is Incumbent Upon the Husband and What is Incumbent Upon the Wife
17:29.anchors:
- Root: و ل م (w-l-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The core meaning pertains to the wedding feast (walīmah), derived from the concept of gathering and union.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In theological usage, it signifies the communal meal marking the consummation of a marriage contract, a recommended act of public gratitude.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah) usage denotes the specific feast; metaphorical (Majaz) extension applies to any act of publicizing a joyous occasion.
- Root: ع ش ر (ʿ- sh-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The root denotes association, companionship, and intimacy; the tenth (ʿasharah) of a thing is related, but the primary social sense is cohabitation and mutual dealing.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In the Quranic context of {وَعَاشِرُوهُنَّ بِالْمَعْرُوفِ}, it signifies a sustained, equitable mode of social intercourse grounded in moral rectitude, not mere physical proximity.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah) usage is the act of living together; metaphorical (Majaz) usage elevates it to a standard of ethical conduct (maʿrūf) that defines the marital bond.
- Root: ق س م (q-s-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The root indicates division, apportionment, and distribution; in the marital context, it refers to the equitable division of time among co-wives.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theologically, it is tied to justice (ʿadl) as a divine attribute; for the husband, it is a legal obligation to maintain fairness in material and temporal allotments.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah) usage is the physical act of dividing; metaphorical (Majaz) usage applies to the moral duty of impartiality in affection and provision.
- Root: غ ي ر (gh-y-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The root conveys alteration and change, but in the moral register, it denotes protective jealousy (ghayrah), a state of aversion to the violation of honor.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In Kalam, ghayrah is a praiseworthy emotion when aligned with divine law—jealousy for the sanctity of the family—and blameworthy when it stems from unjust suspicion (sūʾ al-ẓann).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah) usage is the emotional state; metaphorical (Majaz) usage is attributed to God (al-Ghayyār) as a figure for His prohibition of indecencies, distinguishing human passion from divine will.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — Used to isolate specific obligations (e.g., "the third is that he should increase...") and to distinguish categories of jealousy and pride, ensuring precise legal and moral demarcation.
17:29.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'Breaking the Two Desires'

17:29.arabic: مسرف يجب منعه قال تعالى ولا تبسطها كل البسط فتقعد ملوما محسورا نزل هذا في رجل بالمدينة قسم جميع ماله ولم يبق شيئا لعياله فطولب بالنفقة فلم يقدر على شيء وقال تعالى ولا تبذر تبذيرا إن المبذرين كانوا إخوان الشياطين وكذلك قال عز وجل والذين إذا أنفقوا لم يسرفوا ولم يقتروا فمن يسرف هذا الإسراف ينكر عليه ويجب على القاضي أن يحجر عليه إلا إذا كان الرجل وحده وكان له قوة في التوكل صادقة فله أن ينفق جميع ماله في أبواب البر ومن له عيال أو كان عاجزا عن التوكل فليس له أن يتصدق بجميع ماله وكذلك لو صرف جميع ماله إ
17:29.english: And excess varies according to circumstances. Thus we say: whoever possesses only one hundred dinars, for example, and has with him his dependents and children, and they have no means of livelihood other than it, and he spends all of it upon a banquet — he is an extravagant one who must be prevented. God, exalted be He, said: «ولا تبسطها كل البسط فتقعد ملوما محسورا» — "And do not spread it forth with all spreading, lest you sit down blamed and exhausted" — and this was revealed concerning a man in Medina who divided all his wealth and left nothing for his dependents; he was then demanded for maintenance and could not produce anything. And God, exalted be He, said: «ولا تبذر تبذيرا إن المبذرين كانوا إخوان الشياطين» — "And do not squander with squandering; indeed, the squanderers are brothers of the devils." And likewise He, mighty and majestic, said: «والذين إذا أنفقوا لم يسرفوا ولم يقتروا» — "And those who, when they spend, are neither extravagant nor niggardly." So whoever commits this extravagance is to be denounced, and it is obligatory upon the judge to place him under legal interdiction (ḥajr) — except if the man be alone [without dependents] and possess true strength in trust in God (tawakkul), then he may spend all his wealth upon the gates of righteousness. But whoever has dependents, or is incapable of [true] trust in God, it is not for him to give in charity all his wealth.

20:44.arabic: فقال تعالى فقولا له قولا لينا لعله يتذكر أو يخشى فليكن اقتداء المحتسب في الرفق بالأنبياء صلوات الله عليهم فقد روى أبو إمامة أن غلاما شابا أتى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال يا نبي الله تأذن لي في الزنا فصاح الناس به فقال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قربوه أدن فدنا حتى جلس بين يديه فقال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أتحبه لأمك فقال لا جعلني الله فداك قال كذلك الناس لا يحبونه لأمهاتهم أتحبه لابنتك قال لا جعلني الله فداك قال كذلك الناس لا يحبونه لبناتهم أتحبه لأختك (3) وزاد ابن عوف حتى ذكر العمة والخالة وه
20:44.english: We do not mean by this that commanding right becomes prohibited by reason of one's sinfulness — rather, its effect upon hearts falls away by the manifestation of his sinfulness to the people. For it has been related from Anas, may God be pleased with him, who said: "We said, 'O Messenger of God, shall we not command right until we have acted upon it entirely, and shall we not forbid wrong until we have shunned it entirely?' He said, may God's peace and blessings be upon him: 'Rather, command right even if you do not act upon it entirely, and forbid wrong even if you do not shun it entirely.'"
20:44.section_title_en: On Gentleness in Commanding Right and Forbidding Wrong — The Etiquette of the Muḥtasib
20:44.anchors:
- Root: عيب (ʿayb)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root meaning — defect, blemish, reproach; to find fault with something.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance — the reproach of intellect (ʿaql) is the severest form of deficiency, for it touches the very faculty by which one is distinguished from beasts.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal vs Metaphorical — here used metaphorically: the reproach falls upon his intellect, i.e., the deficiency of his discernment becomes manifest.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Restriction (Bāb al-Ḥaṣr) — "فإنما يزرى على عقله" restricts the object of reproach to the intellect alone, excluding the person's faith or status.
20:44.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Enjoining Good and Forbidding Evil'

21:67.arabic: مثل قول إبراهيم عليه السلام أف لكم ولما تعبدون من دون الله أفلا تعقلون ولسنا نعني بالسب والفحش بما فيه نسبة إلى الزنا ومقدماته ولا الكذب بل أن يخاطبه بما فيه مما لا يعد من جملة الفحش كقوله يا فاسق يا أحمق يا جاهل ألا تخاف الله وكقوله يا سوادى يا غبي وما يجري هذا المجرى فإن كل فاسق فهو أحمق وجاهل ولولا حمقه لما عصى الله تعالى بل كل من ليس
21:67.english: And at this point it is said to him what was said to Jesus, peace be upon him: "O son of Mary, exhort yourself; if you are admonished, then exhort the people — and if not, then be ashamed before Me."
21:67.section_title_en: The Revival of the Religious Sciences — Section 540: On Gentleness in Forbidding Wrong and the Hidden Diseases of the Enjoiner
21:67.anchors:
- Root: لطف (luṭf)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Gentleness, subtlety, refinement; the opposite of harshness and roughness
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Divine gentleness (luṭf) as that which draws the servant toward obedience through kindness rather than compulsion
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical softness/delicacy; Metaphorical: kindness of manner and speech in dealing with others
- Root: عجب (ʿujb)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Self-admiration; the soul's being pleased with itself and its own states
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): A hidden disease of the heart wherein one admires his own qualities, forgetting that they are divine gifts
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: wonder/astonishment; Metaphorical: the soul's complacent delight in its own excellence
- Root: حسب (ḥasaba)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To reckon, count, account; the one who enjoins right and forbids wrong (muḥtasib)
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The act of calling to account; the muḥtasib as one who holds himself and others to divine standards
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: numerical reckoning; Metaphorical: moral accountability and the office of the public censor
- Sibawayh Rule: باب التدرج في الأحكام (Graduated Progression of Rulings) — The text moves through ascending degrees of severity in forbidding wrong, each stage conditional upon the failure of the preceding, requiring precise syntactic parsing of conditional and concessive clauses.
21:67.topic: Al-Ghazali on purifying the character, moral diseases, and spiritual remedies, from 'Enjoining Good and Forbidding Evil'

22:25.arabic: حلت بينه وبينه وقد قال الله تعالى سواء العاكف فيه والباد من جعل لك هذا فنظر في وجهه وكان بعرفه لأنه من مواليهم فقال أعبد الله ابن مرزوق قال نعم فأخذ فجىء به إلى بغداد فكره أن يعاقبه عقوبة يشنع بها عليه في العامة فجعله في اصطبل الدواب ليسوس الدواب وضموا إليه فرسا عضوضا سيىء الخلق ليعقره الفرس فلين الله تعالى له الفرس قال ثم صيروه إلى بيت وأغلق عليه وأخذ المهدي المفتاح عنده فإذا هو قد خرج بعد ثلاث إلى البستان يأكل البقل فأوذن به المهدي فقال له من أخرجك فقال الذي حبسني فضج المهدي وصاح وقال ما تخاف أن أقتلك
22:25.english: And it is astonishing that the Rāfiḍah went beyond this and said: "It is not permissible to enjoin the good as long as the infallible Imam — who, in their view, is the true Imam — has not come forth." These are too base in rank to be addressed; rather, their answer is to say to them: When they come to a judge seeking their rights concerning their blood and their wealth, [one says to them:] "If I aided you, that would be enjoining the good, and extracting your rights from the hands of those who wronged you would be forbidding the munkar — and your seeking your right is part of the good. But this is not the time for forbidding injustice and seeking rights, because the true Imam has not yet come forth."
22:25.section_title_en: The Fourth Condition: Authorization from the Imam and Governor — Its Invalidity, and the Five Ranks of Ḥisbah
22:25.anchors:
- Root: أ ذ ن (ʾ-dh-n)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning is "permission" or "license" — to grant leave for an act; also "ear" (udhun), the instrument of hearing command.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In theological usage, ʾidhn denotes divine or authoritative sanction that legitimizes an action; its absence renders the act transgressive (muʿtadā).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) sense is "to permit"; metaphorical (majāz) extension applies to the Imam's delegation of authority, which is a contingent, not essential, condition.
- Root: ن ك ر (n-k-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Nakirah denotes the unrecognized or the objectionable; munkar is that which the sound intellect and divine law repudiate.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Inkār is the heart's rejection of what it does not conceive as right; it opposes maʿrifah (recognition). The tongue's inkār may be true or feigned.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Nakira is stronger than ankara — the former is the heart's denial, the latter the eye's; here, munkar is the objective evil that the enjoiner must repel.
- Root: ع ر ف (ʿ-r-f)
  * Lisan / Ayn: ʿArafa means to know by trace or sign; maʿrūf is that which is well-known and approved by revelation and custom.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Maʿrifah is knowledge attained through reflection on effects — more specific than ʿilm; hence, al-amr bi-l-maʿrūf is commanding what is recognized as good by divine attestation.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal sense is "to know"; here, maʿrūf is the established good, and its enjoining is a communal obligation independent of temporal authorization.
- Sibawayh Rule: Bāb al-ḥaṣr wa-l-taqyīd bi-innamā (Restriction and Specification) — The conditional clause "sharaṭa hādhā al-sharṭ" is a restrictive predication that the author refutes by universalizing the command (ʿalā al-ʿumūm), a syntactic move that nullifies the exception.
22:25.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Enjoining Good and Forbidding Evil'

22:25.arabic: وأما هؤلاء فإنهم يصدون عن سبيل الله ويجرون الخلق إلى الغرور بالله بلفظ الرجاء فيزيدهم كلامهم جراءة على المعاصي ورغبة في الدنيا لا سيما إذا كان الواعظ متزينا بالثياب والخيل والمراكب فإنه تشهد هيئته من فرقه إلى قدمه بشدة حرصه على الدنيا فما يفسده هذا المغرور أكثر مما يصلحه بل لا يصلح أصلا ويضل خلقا كثيرا ولا يخفى وجه كونه مغرورا وفرقة أخرى منهم قنعوا بحفظ كلام الزهاد وأحاديثهم في ذم الدنيا فهم يحفظون الكلمات على وجهها ويؤدونها من غير إحاطة بمعانيها فبعضهم يفعل ذلك على المنابر وبعضهم
22:25.english: But as for these [deluded ones], they turn others away from the path of God and drag creation into self-deception concerning God (al-ghurūr billāh) by means of the word "hope" (al-rajāʾ). Thus their speech increases them in audacity toward sins and desire for this world — especially when the preacher is adorned with fine garments, horses, and mounts, for his very appearance bears witness from his hair to his feet to his intense greed for this world. So what this deluded one corrupts is more than what he reforms — nay, he reforms nothing at all, and he leads many people astray. Nor is the aspect of his being deluded hidden.
22:25.section_title_en: The Categories of the Deluded Among Preachers and Hadith Transmitters
22:25.anchors:
- Root: أ-ص-ل (ʾ-ṣ-l)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of foundation, root, and origin; to set right what is corrupt.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): اصلاح (iṣlāḥ) as the act of bringing something from a state of corruption (fasād) to soundness (ṣalāḥ), whether in belief, action, or speech.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) usage denotes rectifying a physical object; metaphorical (majāz) usage applies to moral and spiritual correction of others.
- Root: غ-ر-ر (gh-r-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: غرور (ghurūr) — deception, delusion, vanity; from غرّ (gharra), to be heedless or deceived by appearances.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): الغرور (al-ghurūr) is the delusion that leads one to rely on false hopes, particularly regarding God's mercy while persisting in sin; the state of one who is deceived by Satan or by his own vain fancies.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: a thing that deceives by its outward show; Metaphorical: the soul's self-deception through false reliance on divine forgiveness without repentance.
- Root: س-م-ع (s-m-ʿ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: السمع (al-samʿ) — hearing; the auditory faculty and its act.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Hearing as the means of acquiring transmitted knowledge (samāʿ); in hadith terminology, the formal act of hearing a tradition from a shaykh, which is the first stage of transmission.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the physical act of hearing; Metaphorical: attentive listening with the heart, as in "ألقى السمع وهو شهيد" {«وَأَلْقَى السَّمْعَ وَهُوَ شَهِيدٌ»} [Q. 50:37] — one who listens with full presence of mind.
- Root: ح-ف-ظ (ḥ-f-ẓ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: الحفظ (al-ḥifẓ) — preservation, guarding, memorization; keeping something safe from loss or alteration.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): الحفظ is the faculty of the soul by which what is understood is retained; its opposite is forgetfulness (nisyān). It also denotes vigilant care and protection.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: guarding a physical object; Metaphorical: committing knowledge to memory such that it is preserved from distortion.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The rule governing the separation of a preposition from its object by intervening clauses, as in the periodic structure "فإذا لم تحفظ لا بالقلب ولا بالكتاب وجرى على سمعك صوت غفل" where the conditional clause (فإذا) governs a sequence of coordinated conditions, each requiring its own apodosis, demonstrating the classical pattern of layered conditional sentences.
22:25.topic: Al-Ghazali on purifying the character, moral diseases, and spiritual remedies, from 'Condemnation of Delusion'

22:25.arabic: إلا مكة وتلا قوله تعالى ومن يرد فيه بإلحاد بظلم نذقه من عذاب أليم أي أنه على مجرد الإرادة ويقال إن السيئات تضاعف بها كما تضاعف الحسنات وكان ابن عباس رضي الله عنه يقول الاحتكار بمكة من الإلحاد في الحرم وقيل الكذب أيضا وقال ابن عباس لأن أذنب سبعين ذنبا بركية أحب إلي من أن أذنب ذنبا واحدا بمكة وركية منزل بين مكة والطائف والخوف ذلك انتهى بعض المقيمين إلى أن لم يقض حاجته في الحرم بل كان يخرج إلى الحل عند قضاء الحاجة وبعضهم أقام شهرا وما وضع جنبه على الأرض وللمنع من الإقامة كره بعض العلماء أجور دور مكة ولا تظنن أن كراهة
22:25.english: The first is the fear of becoming weary and familiar with the House, for that might perhaps effect a calming of the heart's burning in veneration. Thus it was that 'Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) used to strike the pilgrims when they performed the Hajj and say: "O people of Yemen, to your Yemen! O people of Syria, to your Syria! O people of Iraq, to your Iraq!" For this reason, 'Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) resolved to prevent people from excessive circumambulation and said: "I fear that the people may become familiar with this House."
22:25.section_title_en: The Virtue of Residing in Mecca (May Allah Protect It) and the Disapproval of Doing So
22:25.anchors:
- Root: خوف (kh-w-f)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of apprehension and dread of a feared outcome
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الخوف: توقع مكروه عن أمارة مظنونة، أو معلومة" — the expectation of something disliked based on a probable or known indication
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): fear of a tangible threat; Metaphorical (Majaz): "تخوفه: تنقصه" — to diminish gradually, as in "تخوف السير منها" (the journey wore it down little by little)
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — governing the permissible separation between a preposition and its object for rhetorical emphasis

- Root: بيت (b-y-t)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The place of overnight dwelling; the Ka'bah as the sacred house
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "أصل البيت: مأوى الإنسان بالليل" — the origin is man's shelter by night; then applied to any dwelling, with "البيوت" more specific to residences
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the physical structure of the Ka'bah; Metaphorical: the heart's attachment and longing toward it
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Contextual Specification — the term "البيت" (the House) in sacred context refers specifically to the Ka'bah by customary designation
22:25.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Mysteries of Hajj'

22:41.arabic: ويدل ذلك على الوجوب أيضا وقال تعالى الذين إن مكناهم في الأرض أقاموا الصلاة وآتوا الزكاة وأمروا بالمعروف ونهوا عن المنكر فقرن ذلك بالصلاة والزكاة في نعت الصالحين والمؤمنين وقال تعالى وتعاونوا على البر والتقوى ولا تعاونوا على الإثم والعدوان وهو أمر جزم ومعنى التعاون الحث عليه وتسهيل طرق الخير وسد سبل الشر والعدوان بحسب الإمكان وقال تعالى لولا ينهاهم الربانيون والأحبار عن قولهم الإثم وأكلهم السحت لبئس ما كانوا يصنعون فبين أنهم أثموا بترك النهي وقال تعالى فلولا كان من القرون من قبلكم أولوا بقية ينهون عن الفساد في الأرض الآية فبين أنه أهلك جميعهم إلا قليلا منهم كانوا ينهون ع
22:41.english: Know that the verses indicating the obligation of commanding right and forbidding wrong are numerous. Among them is His saying, may He be exalted: {«Let there arise from among you a nation inviting to good, commanding right and forbidding wrong — and those are the successful»} (Āl ʿImrān 3:104). In this verse is the declaration of obligation, for His saying, may He be exalted, "Let there be" (wal-takun) is a command, and the apparent meaning of a command is obligation. In it also is the declaration that success (falāḥ) is contingent upon it, for He restricted it and said: {«And those are the successful»}. In it also is the declaration that it is a collective obligation (farḍ kifāyah), not an individual obligation (farḍ ʿayn), and that when a group undertakes it, the obligation falls from the rest — for He did not say, "Let all of you be commanders of right," but rather said: {«Let there arise from among you a nation»}. Thus, whenever one person or a group undertakes it, the burden falls from the others, and success is particularized to those who undertake it and directly perform it. But if all of creation were to hold back from it, the burden would encompass all those capable of it without exception.
22:41.topic: Al-Ghazali on the inner and outer dimensions of worship, from 'Enjoining Good and Forbidding Evil'

24:27.arabic: البيوت من أبوابها وقد تسورت من السطح وقال لا تدخلوا بيوتا غير بيوتكم حتى تستأنسوا وتسلموا على أهلها وما سلمت فتركه عمر وشرط عليه التوبة ولذلك شاور عمر الصحابة رضي الله عنهم وهو على المنبر وسألهم عن الإمام إذا شاهد بنفسه منكرا فهل له إقامة الحد فيه فأشار علي رضي الله عنه بأن ذلك منوط بعدلين فلا يكفي فيه واحد وقد أوردنا هذه الأخبار في بيان حق المسلم من كتاب آداب الصحبة فلا نعيدها فإن قلت فما حد الظهور والاستتار فاعلم أن من أغلق باب داره وتستر بحيطانه فلا يجوز الدخول عليه بغير إذنه لنعرف المعصية إلا أن يظهر في الدار ظهورا يعرفه من هو خارج الدار كأ
24:27.english: The Book of the Etiquettes of Companionship. And likewise, it is narrated that ʿUmar, may God be pleased with him, climbed onto the roof of a man's house and saw him in a reprehensible state, so he rebuked him. The man said: "O Commander of the Believers, if I have disobeyed God in one respect, you have disobeyed Him in three respects." ʿUmar said: "And what are they?" He said: "God, exalted is He, has said: {وَلَا تَجَسَّسُوا} ('And do not spy.') [Q. 49:12] — and you have spied. And He has said: {وَأْتُوا الْبُيُوتَ مِنْ أَبْوَابِهَا} ('And enter houses from their doors.') [Q. 2:189] — and you have climbed over from the roof. And He has said: {لَا تَدْخُلُوا بُيُوتًا غَيْرَ بُيُوتِكُمْ حَتَّىٰ تَسْتَأْنِسُوا وَتُسَلِّمُوا عَلَىٰ أَهْلِهَا} ('Do not enter houses other than your own until you have sought permission and greeted their inhabitants.') [Q. 24:27] — and you did not greet." So ʿUmar left him, but stipulated upon him repentance.
24:27.section_title_en: The Book of the Etiquettes of Companionship — Section 535: On the Limits of Openness (Ẓuhūr) and Concealment (Istitār) in Enjoining Good and Forbidding Evil
24:27.anchors:
- Root: ظهر (ẓ-h-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning is "to become visible, apparent, or manifest"; the opposite of concealment (khabā').
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In theological discourse, ẓuhūr denotes the state of a matter becoming perceptible or known through sensory or evidentiary means, moving it from the realm of the hidden (ghayb) to the witnessed (shahādah).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) usage refers to physical visibility (e.g., "ظهر على السطح" — he appeared on the roof). Metaphorical (majāz) usage extends to intellectual or auditory manifestation, as in "ظهرت الحجة" (the proof became manifest). Here, it is applied to sounds and smells that "emerge" beyond physical barriers.
- Root: ستر (s-t-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning is "to cover, conceal, or screen" something from perception.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-Sitr is the covering of a thing; al-istitār is self-concealment. In the Kalam context, God's attribute of al-Sattār (the Concealer) establishes the normative principle of covering faults.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) usage is physical covering (e.g., "استترت بالثوب" — she covered herself with a garment). Metaphorical (majāz) usage is the concealment of moral faults, as in "هتك الله سترك" (God exposed your secrets). The text navigates between these: physical concealment (walls, sleeves) and the moral obligation to respect it unless a clear sign (amārah) indicates a public violation.
- Root: حسب (ḥ-s-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning is "to count, reckon, or calculate."
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-Ḥisbah is the act of seeking reward (iḥtisāb) from God by performing a commanded act. Technically, it becomes the institution of enjoining good and forbidding evil.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) usage is arithmetic reckoning. Metaphorical (majāz) usage is "to reckon or consider" a matter as sufficient or binding, as in "احْتَسَبَ عَلَيْهِ" (he acted against him by way of correction). The text uses "الحسبة" (al-ḥisbah) as the technical term for this institutional duty.
- Sibawayh Rule: Bāb al-Ḥaṣr wa al-Taqyīd bi-innamā (Restriction and Focused Predication). The phrase "فَإِنَّمَا يُدْرَكُ مَعَ تَخَلُّلِ الْحِيطَانِ صَوْتٌ أَوْ رَائِحَةٌ" (For it is only perceived through the interpenetration of walls as a sound or a smell) uses innamā to restrict the means of legitimate perception to sensory evidence that breaches the barrier of concealment, thereby specifying the legal trigger for intervention.
24:27.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Enjoining Good and Forbidding Evil'

24:27.arabic: وقد قال الله تعالى يا أيها الذين آمنوا أنفقوا من طيبات ما كسبتم ومما أخرجنا لكم من الأرض ولا تيمموا الخبيث منه تنفقون ولستم بآخذيه إلا أن تغمضوا فيه أي لا تأخذوه إلا مع كراهية وحياء وهو معنى الإغماض فلا تؤثروا به ربكم وفي الخبر سبق درهم مائة ألف درهم (3) وذلك بأن يخرجه الإنسان وهو من أحل ماله وأجوده فيصدر ذلك عن الرضا والفرح بالبذل وقد يخرج مائة ألف درهم مما يكره من ماله فيدل ذلك على أنه ليس يؤثر الله عز وجل بشيء مما يحبه وبذلك ذم الله تعالى قوما جعلوا لله ما يكرهون فقال تعال
24:27.english: The heart is not treated save with the compound electuary (maʿjūn) of knowledge and works. And this condition among the conditions of almsgiving runs in the same course as humility (al-khushūʿ) runs in the prayer. This is established by his saying — may Allah bless him and grant him peace: "A man has nothing of his prayer save that of which he was conscious." And this is like his saying — may Allah bless him and grant him peace: "Allah does not accept the charity of the one who bestows it with reproach (al-mannān)." And like His saying — Exalted is He: {«لا تبطلوا صدقاتكم بالمن والأذى»} ("Do not nullify your charities by reproach and injury"). As for the legal opinion (fatwā) of the jurist that the alms fall in their proper place and that one's liability is discharged without this condition — that is another discussion, and we have already pointed to its meaning in the Book of Prayer.
24:27.section_title_en: The Inner Conditions of Charity — Section 175 (From The Revival of the Religious Sciences, Book of the Mysteries of Almsgiving)
24:27.anchors:
- Root: قلب (q-l-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "To turn, overturn, transform a thing from one state to another; to rotate, to flip"
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "قلب الشيء: تصريفه وصرفه عن وجه إلى وجه" — the heart is so named because of its constant turning and transformation between states
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "قلب الشيء قلبا: حوله عن وجهه" (to turn a thing from its face). Metaphorical: "رجل قلب حول: يقلب الأمور ويحتال" — one who turns matters over and manages them; "قلبوا لك الأمور" (they turned matters against you)
- Root: وجل (w-j-l)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "Fear, dread, apprehension that strikes the heart"
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الوجل: استشعار الخوف" — the sensing of fear; cited in {«إنما المؤمنون الذين إذا ذكر الله وجلت قلوبهم»}
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "رجل وجل، وقوم وجال" — a fearful man, a fearful people; "وفي قلبه وجل" — in his heart is dread
- Root: عجب (ʿ-j-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "Wonder, amazement; self-admiration, vanity"
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Self-admiration (al-ʿujb) is a destructive spiritual ailment that nullifies deeds
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: wonder at something extraordinary. Metaphorical: self-conceit regarding one's own acts of obedience
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد (Restriction & Focused Predication) — governing the precise limitation of general categories (al-ṣifāt al-khāṣṣah within al-aṣnāf al-thamāniyyah) and the conditional structure of acceptance

##
24:27.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Duties of Brotherhood'

24:27.arabic: وقد تسورت علي وقد قال الله تعالى {لا تدخلوا بيوتا غير بيوتكم} الآية وقد دخلت بيتي بغير إذن ولا سلام فقال عمر رضي الله عنه هل عندك من خير إن عفوت عنك قال نعم والله يا أمير المؤمنين لئن عفوت عني لا أعود إلى مثلها أبدا فعفا عنه وخرج وتركه وقال رجل لعبد الله بن عمر يا أبا عبد الرحمن كيف سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول في النجوى يوم القيامة قال سمعته يقول إن الله ليدني منه المؤمن فيضع عليه كنفه ويستره من الناس فيقول أتعرف ذنب كذا أتعرف ذنب كذا فيقول نعم يارب حتى إذا قرره بذنوبه فرأى في نفسه أنه قد هلك قال له يا عبدي إني
24:27.english: **First**: That you greet him with peace (*salām*) when you meet him, and respond to his invitation when he invites you, and say "may Allah have mercy on you" (*tashmīt*) when he sneezes, and visit him when he is ill, and attend his funeral procession when he dies, and fulfill his oath when he swears by you, and give him sincere counsel when he seeks your advice, and protect him in his absence when he is away from you, and love for him what you love for yourself, and dislike for him what you dislike for yourself. (1)
24:27.section_title_en: The Rights of Brotherhood — Section 433: The Duties of a Muslim Toward His Fellow Muslims
24:27.anchors:
- Root: سلم (s-l-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of safety, security, freedom from harm; the root from which *islām* (submission/surrender) and *salām* (peace) derive
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): *Salām* as the theological state of being secure from harm — both giving and receiving safety; *islām* as the total surrender of the heart to Allah
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (*ḥaqīqah*): physical safety from tongue and hand; Metaphorical (*majāz*): the comprehensive spiritual safety that defines true Muslim brotherhood
- Root: عون (ʿ-w-n)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Assistance, aid, helping another in need
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Mutual assistance as a divine ordinance among believers
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical aid; Metaphorical: intercession (*shafāʿah*) and advocacy on behalf of others
- Root: ستر (s-t-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Covering, concealing, veiling; protection from exposure
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): *Sitr* as the divine attribute of concealment — Allah's covering of sins in this world and the next
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: covering a physical defect; Metaphorical: concealing another's faults and sins — a cardinal virtue of brotherhood
- Root: عذر (ʿ-dh-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Excuse, pardon, acceptance of apology
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): *ʿAfw* (pardon) as the higher station of forgiveness that elevates the forgiver
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: releasing from obligation; Metaphorical: the noble trait of overlooking others' offenses
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد (Restriction & Focused Predication) — The repeated use of restrictive constructions (e.g., "المسلم من سلم المسلمون") establishes definitional boundaries through predicate restriction, indicating that the *ḥaqīqah* of faith is manifested through specific observable actions.

##
24:27.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Duties of Brotherhood'

25:67.arabic: وكذلك قال عز وجل والذين إذا أنفقوا لم يسرفوا ولم يقتروا فمن يسرف هذا الإسراف ينكر عليه ويجب على القاضي أن يحجر عليه إلا إذا كان الرجل وحده وكان له قوة في التوكل صادقة فله أن ينفق جميع ماله في أبواب البر ومن له عيال أو كان عاجزا عن التوكل فليس له أن يتصدق بجميع ماله وكذلك لو صرف جميع ماله إلى نقوش حيطانه وتزيين بنيانه فهو أيضا إسراف محرم وفعل ذلك ممن له مال كثير ليس بحرام لأن التزيين من الأغراض الصحيحة ولم تزل المساجد تزين وتنقش أبوابها وسقوفها مع أن نقش الباب والسقف لا
25:67.english: And excess varies according to circumstances. Thus we say: whoever possesses only one hundred dinars, for example, and has with him his dependents and children, and they have no means of livelihood other than it, and he spends all of it upon a banquet — he is an extravagant one who must be prevented. God, exalted be He, said: «ولا تبسطها كل البسط فتقعد ملوما محسورا» — "And do not spread it forth with all spreading, lest you sit down blamed and exhausted" — and this was revealed concerning a man in Medina who divided all his wealth and left nothing for his dependents; he was then demanded for maintenance and could not produce anything. And God, exalted be He, said: «ولا تبذر تبذيرا إن المبذرين كانوا إخوان الشياطين» — "And do not squander with squandering; indeed, the squanderers are brothers of the devils." And likewise He, mighty and majestic, said: «والذين إذا أنفقوا لم يسرفوا ولم يقتروا» — "And those who, when they spend, are neither extravagant nor niggardly." So whoever commits this extravagance is to be denounced, and it is obligatory upon the judge to place him under legal interdiction (ḥajr) — except if the man be alone [without dependents] and possess true strength in trust in God (tawakkul), then he may spend all his wealth upon the gates of righteousness. But whoever has dependents, or is incapable of [true] trust in God, it is not for him to give in charity all his wealth.
25:67.section_title_en: Section 549 — On Sitting with a Sinner Without Necessity, and Related Rulings on Silk, Gold, Extravagance, and Permissible Merriment
25:67.anchors:
- Root: زين (z-y-n)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of adornment, ornamentation, and beautification — that which renders something attractive or comely.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): True adornment (al-zīnah al-ḥaqīqiyyah) is that which never disgraces its bearer in any state, neither in this world nor the next; bodily and external adornments are only partial, being a disgrace in one respect while an ornament in another.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) usage denotes physical beautification (e.g., adorning the earth with vegetation); metaphorical (majāz) usage extends to moral and spiritual adornment, as in faith being made beloved and adorned in the heart.
- Root: سرف (s-r-f)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Exceeding the proper limit in any act; the woodworm (surafah) that consumes timber utterly, leaving it hollow and ruined.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Extravagance (isrāf) is transgressing the bound in every deed a person performs, whether in expenditure or otherwise; it is considered with regard to both quantity and quality — spending in disobedience to God is extravagance even if little.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: a garment eaten by moths; Metaphorical: one whose intellect is consumed and corrupted, as the worm consumes wood — extravagance ruins wealth just as the insect ruins timber.
- Root: كذب (k-dh-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Falsehood in speech or deed; that which contradicts reality or intent.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Falsehood is said of both utterance and action; the hypocrites' claim of faith was true in words but false in conviction — hence God declared them liars regarding their belief, not their speech.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: to utter what is contrary to fact; Metaphorical: "he carried then lied" — meaning he attacked then retreated, making his charge false; likewise milk that fails to flow is called "lying."
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The permissibility of interposing elements between a governing word and its governed complement when the intervening clause is independently meaningful, just as conditional qualifications may be interposed without corrupting the syntactic bond.
25:67.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'Enjoining Good and Forbidding Evil'

25:67.arabic: مغلولة إلى عنقك ولا تبسطها كل البسط وقال تعالى والذين إذا أنفقوا لم يسرفوا ولم يقتروا وكان بين ذلك قواما فالجود وسط بين الإسراف والإقتار وبين البسط والقبض وهو أن يقدر بذله وإمساكه بقدر الواجب ولا يكفي أن يفعل ذلك بجوارحه ما لم يكن قلبه طيبا به غير منازع له فيه فإن بذل في محل وجوب البذل ونفسه تنازعه وهو يصابرها فهو متسخ وليس بسخي بل ينبغي أن لا يكون لقلبه علاقة مع المال إلا من حيث يراد المال له وهو صرفه إلى ما يجب صرفه إليه
25:67.english: We say: Some have said that the definition of miserliness is "the refusal of what is obligatory (wājib)." Thus, whoever fulfills what is obligatory upon him is not a miser. But this is not sufficient — for a man who returns meat to the butcher, or bread to the baker, short by a grain or half a grain, is counted a miser by unanimous agreement. Likewise, one who hands over to his family the amount that the judge would apportion to them, but then tightens upon them regarding a morsel they have added beyond that, or a date they have eaten from his wealth, is counted a miser. And a man who has a loaf before him, and someone arrives whom he thinks will eat with him, and he hides it from him — he is counted a miser.
25:67.section_title_en: The Revival of the Religious Sciences — Book on the Affirmation of Generosity and Miserliness: Their Definitions and Realities
25:67.anchors:
- Root: بخل (b-kh-l)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning is withholding/restraining (imsāk) what one possesses from that which it is not right to withhold. Al-Khalil notes the intensive form "bakhīl" denotes one in whom miserliness is a dominant trait, as opposed to the simple agent noun "bākhil."
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Miserliness (al-bukhl) is "the withholding of possessions from that which it is not right to withhold them," and it is of two kinds: withholding one's own possessions, and withholding what belongs to others (i.e., commanding others to withhold) — the latter being the more blameworthy, as in {«Those who are miserly and command people to miserliness»} (al-Nisā' 4:37).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (haqīqah): "So-and-so did not show miserliness (lam yabkhal)," and the noun "bukhleh" denotes a single act of miserliness. Metaphorical (majāz): The heavens "withholding" rain — {«When the sky withheld its rain»} — extending the root to natural phenomena.
- Root: جود (j-w-d)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning is the bountiful giving of what one possesses, whether wealth or knowledge. The intensive form "jawād" (pl. ajyād, ajāwīd) is applied to the generous man and the swift horse alike.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Generosity (al-jūd) is "the expending of possessions — whether wealth or knowledge — in the manner that is due." God is described as al-Jawād (the Generous). The term is also applied to abundant rain.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "So-and-so was generous (jāda) with generosity (jūdan); the sky poured generously; the horse was swift (jādat)." Metaphorical: "I am yearning (jād) toward meeting you" — derived from thirst (jūd), as a favorable omen, just as the desert wasteland is called "mafāzah" (place of salvation) though it is a place of perdition.
- Root: سرف (s-r-f)
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Extravagance (al-isrāf) is "exceeding the proper measure in expenditure," and it is the opposite of miserliness. It is blameworthy in all cases, as in {«And do not be extravagant; indeed, He does not love the extravagant»} (al-An'ām 6:141).
- Root: قتر (q-t-r)
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Frugality/penuriousness (al-iqtār) is "the tightening of expenditure below the proper measure," and it is the opposite of extravagance. The middle path between the two is praised in {«And those who, when they spend, are neither extravagant nor penurious, but hold a just balance between the two»} (al-Furqān 25:67).
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Semantic Specification (Takhṣīṣ) — The definition of a term (ḥadd) must specify its referent (musammā) exhaustively and exclusively. A definition that fails to include all instances of the defined term (like "withholding the obligatory") or that includes what is not part of it (like "finding giving difficult") is defective. The true definition must capture the formal boundary (ḥadd) of the reality itself, not merely a concomitant or a partial description.
25:67.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Breaking the Two Desires'

33:72.arabic: تعالى إنا عرضنا الأمانة على السموات والأرض والجبال فأبين أن يحملنها وأشفقن منها وحملها الإنسان إنه كان ظلوما جهولا قال عرضها على السموات السبع الطباق والطرائق التي زينها بالنجوم وحملة العرش العظيم فقال لها سبحانه وتعالى هل تحملين الأمانة بما فيها قالت وما فيها قال إن أحسنت جوزيت وإن أسأت عوقبت فقالت لا ثم عرضها كذلك على الأرض فأبت ثم عرضها على الجبال الشوامخ الصلاب الصعاب فقال لها هل تحملين الأمانة بما فيها قالت وما فيها فذكر الجزاء والعقوبة فقالت لا ثم عرضها على الإنسان فحملها إنه كان ظلوما لنفسه جهولا بأمر ربه فقد رأيناهم والله اشتروا الأمانة بأموالهم فأصابوا آل
33:72.english: It is related that al-Rashid gathered four physicians — an Indian, a Roman, an Iraqi, and a Sudanese — and said: "Let each of you describe the medicine that has no disease in it." The Indian said: "The medicine that has no disease in it, in my view, is black myrobalan (al-ihlīlaj al-aswad)." The Iraqi said: "It is white garden cress seeds (ḥabb al-rashād al-abyaḍ)." The Roman said: "In my view, it is hot water." The Sudanese — and he was the most learned of them — said: "Myrobalan constricts the stomach, and this is a disease; garden cress loosens the stomach, and this is a disease; hot water relaxes the stomach, and this is a disease." They said: "Then what is your view?" He said: "The medicine that has no disease with it, in my view, is that you do not eat food until you desire it, and that you raise your hand from it while you still desire it." They said: "You have spoken truthfully." And it was mentioned to one of the philosophers among the physicians of the People of the Book the saying of the Prophet, peace be upon him: "One third for food, one third for drink, and one third for breath." (1) The hadith "Gluttony is the root of disease, and diet is the root of cure, and accustom every body to what it has become accustomed" — I have not found for it a source. (2) The hadith "Fast, and you will be healthy" — narrated by al-Tabarani in al-Awsat and Abu Nuʿaym in al-Tibb al-Nabawi from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah with a weak chain. For in fasting, hunger, and the reduction of food is the health of bodies and the health of hearts from the sickness of tyranny, arrogance, and other than them.
33:72.section_title_en: The Book of Fasting — Section 643: Ten Benefits of Hunger and Fasting
33:72.anchors:
- Root: اكل (akl)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root meaning "to eat, consume, ingest"; Kitab al-Ayn notes the verbal noun for the act of eating and its derivatives for food, morsels, and prey.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الأكل: تناول المطعم" — eating is the taking of nourishment; metaphorically extended to fire consuming wood, and to the daily portion of provision.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah) usage denotes physical ingestion; metaphorical (Majaz) usage extends to consuming wealth unjustly, as in "أكل مال الشعب" (devouring people's wealth), and to the body's wasting away.
- Root: جوع (jaw')
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root meaning "hunger, famine"; Kitab al-Ayn: "الجوع: اسم جامع للمخمصة" — hunger is the comprehensive term for emptiness of the stomach.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الجوع: الألم الذي ينال الحيوان من خلو المعدة من الطعام" — hunger is the pain that befalls the living being from the emptiness of the stomach of food; al-majā'ah denotes a time of drought and scarcity.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal usage refers to bodily hunger; metaphorical usage extends to longing and yearning, as in "جائع إلى لقائك" (hungering for your meeting).
- Root: بطن (baṭn)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root meaning "belly, abdomen, interior"; Kitab al-Ayn: "البطن معروف" — the belly is well-known; its plural is buṭūn.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "أصل البطن الجارحة" — the root meaning is the bodily organ; metaphorically applied to the interior of things, the underside, and the hidden aspect of affairs.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal usage denotes the physical belly; metaphorical usage extends to the middle of youth, the interior of a valley, and the hidden dimension of a matter.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — When the author states "وإنما يستحقرها الغافلون" (only the heedless belittle them), the particle innamā restricts the predicate to the subject, affirming that belittlement proceeds exclusively from the heedless and negating it from the knowing.
33:72.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Harms of the Tongue'

33:72.arabic: يا أمير المؤمنين إنك قد بليت بأمر لو عرض على السموات والأرض والجبال لأبين أن يحملنه وأشفقن منه يا أمير المؤمنين حدثني يزيد بن جابر عن عبد الرحمن بن عمرة الأنصاري أن عمر بن الخطاب رضي الله عنه استعمل رجلا من الأنصار على الصدقة فرآه بعد أيام مقيما فقال له ما منعك من الخروج إلى عملك أما علمت أن لك مثل أجر المجاهد في سبيل الله قال لا قال وكيف ذلك قال إنه بلغني أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال ما من وال يلي شيئا من أمور الناس إلا أتى به يوم القيامة مغلولة يده إلى عنقه لا يفكها إلا عدله فيوقف على جسر من النار ينتفض به ذلك الجسر انتفاضة ت
33:72.english: He turned to al-Shaʿbī and said: "O Abā ʿAmr! I am the trustee of the Commander of the Faithful over Iraq and his governor over it, and a man commanded to obedience. I have been tried with the subjects, and their right has become incumbent upon me. So I love to preserve them and to attend to what sets them right, along with sincere counsel (naṣīḥah) to them. And reports may reach me about a band of people from the regions concerning a matter, and I find myself severe against them therein, so I withhold a portion of their stipends and place it in the treasury (bayt al-māl), with the intention in myself that I shall return it to them. Then it reaches the Commander of the Faithful that I have withheld it in that manner, so he writes to me that I must not return it. I cannot then countermand his order, nor can I execute his letter [against my better judgment]. I am but a man commanded to obedience. Is there any liability upon me in this, and in similar matters, where the intention is as I have described?"
33:72.section_title_en: The Upright Scholars Before the Tyrannical Rulers — Counsel and Fearless Truth-Telling
33:72.anchors:
- Root: نصح (naṣaḥa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning is sincerity, faithfulness, and pure counsel free from deceit; the root denotes the act of seeking the welfare of another with complete integrity.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In theological context, naṣīḥah is the obligation of the sincere advisor to guide the ruler toward divine truth, even at personal peril, as it is a form of worship (ʿibādah) and a trust (amānah).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) usage denotes pure honey (ʿasal naṣīḥ) free from admixture; metaphorical (majāz) usage applies to counsel that is untainted by flattery or self-interest.
- Root: سلط (sulṭ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Denotes authority, power, and dominion; the ruler (sulṭān) is one who has been given sway over affairs.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In Kalam, sulṭān is a trial (ibtilāʾ) and a trust (amānah) from God, whose exercise demands justice (ʿadl) and whose neglect invites divine wrath.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal usage refers to physical power or a governing authority; metaphorical usage extends to the authority of proof (sulṭān al-burhān) that compels assent.
- Root: عظ (waʿaẓa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Root denotes admonition, exhortation, and reminding of consequences; it implies softening the heart through remembrance of God and the Hereafter.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In theological terms, ʿiẓah is the act of turning the soul away from transgression through a blend of fear (tarhīb) and hope (targhīb), grounded in revealed truth.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal usage is the verbal admonition; metaphorical usage is the admonition of circumstance (ʿiẓah al-ḥāl) when events themselves teach a lesson.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Restriction and Focused Predication (bāb al-ḥaṣr wa al-taqyīd bi-innamā) — Governing the emphasis of exclusive predication in statements of counsel, such as "No obedience to a creature in disobedience of the Creator," where the restriction (ḥaṣr) is achieved through negation and exception (nafy wa istithnāʾ).
33:72.topic: Al-Ghazali on the journey of the soul, death, and the Hereafter, from 'Enjoining Good and Forbidding Evil'

33:72.arabic: وإليه الإشارة بقوله عز وجل إنا عرضنا الأمانة على السموات والأرض والجبال فأبين أن يحملنها وأشفقن منها وحملها الإنسان إشارة إلى أن له خاصية تميز بها عن السموات والأرض والجبال بها صار مطيقا لحمل أمانة الله تعالى وتلك الأمانة هي المعرفة والتوحيد وقلب كل آدمي مستعد لحمل الأمانة ومطيق لها في الأصل ولكن يثبطه عن النهوض بأعبائها والوصول إلى تحقيقها الأسباب التي ذكرناها ولذلك قال صلى الله عليه وسلم كل مولود يولد على الفطرة وإنما أبواه يهودانه وينصرانه ويمجسانه // حديث كل مولود يولد على الفطرة الحديث متفق عليه من حديث أبي هريرة وقول رسول الله
33:72.english: And to this points His saying, mighty and majestic: {«Indeed, We offered the Trust to the heavens and the earth and the mountains, and they refused to bear it and shrank from it, but man bore it»} (al-Aḥzāb 33:72) — an indication that he possesses a distinctive property by which he is set apart from the heavens, the earth, and the mountains, and by which he became capable of bearing the Trust of God, exalted.
33:72.section_title_en: The Exposition of the Heart's Relation to the Sciences Specifically
33:72.anchors:
- Root: قلب (q-l-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of turning, overturning, and transformation from one state to another; the heart as that which is perpetually subject to reversal and fluctuation.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The heart (qalb) is so named for its constant turning (taqlīb) and fluctuation between states; it is the seat of cognition and the instrument by which the soul apprehends realities.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (haqīqah): the physical organ that turns over. Metaphorical (majāz): the subtle spiritual faculty (laṭīfah rabbāniyyah) that apprehends knowledge — the true referent here.
- Root: فطر (f-ṭ-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Splitting lengthwise; origination and initial creation.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Fiṭrah is the primordial constitution upon which God originates creation — the innate disposition receptive to truth.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: God's act of originating creation. Metaphorical: "Every newborn is born upon the fiṭrah" — i.e., the innate disposition capable of accepting the religion of truth.
- Root: حدث (ḥ-d-th)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Origination after non-existence; newness.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Ḥudūth is the coming-to-be of a thing after it was not; the created order is entirely contingent and originated.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: temporal origination. Metaphorical: "Umar was muḥaddath" — one whose discernment is divinely inspired, as if truth were spoken into him.
- Root: سبب (s-b-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: A rope by which one ascends; a means of access.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Every means by which one reaches something is called a sabab; the impediments to knowledge are "causes" (asbāb) that veil the heart.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: a cord or tie. Metaphorical: any intermediary, cause, or hindering factor.
- Sibawayh Rule: Restriction and specification (al-ḥaṣr wa al-taqyīd) — the particle "innamā" (إِنَّمَا) confines and restricts predication, as in "every heart is by fiṭrah fit for knowledge" — a universal affirmative qualified by its cause.
33:72.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Disciplining the Soul'

33:72.arabic: ويتلون وجهه فقيل له مالك يا أمير المؤمنين فيقول جاء وقت أمانة عرضها الله على السموات والأرض والجبال فأبين أن يحملنها وأشفقن منها وحملتها ويروى عن علي بن الحسين أنه كان إذا توضأ اصفر لونه فيقول له أهله ما هذا الذي يعتريك عند الوضوء فيقول أتدرون بين يدي من أريد أن أقوم ويروى عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما أنه قال قال داود عليه السلام في مناجاته إلهي من يسكن بيتك وممن تتقبل الصلاة فأوحى الله إليه يا داود إنما يسكن بيتي وأقبل الصلاة منه من تواضع لعظمتي وقطع نهاره بذكري وكف نفسه عن الشهوات من أجلي يطعم الجائع ويؤوي الغريب ويرحم المصاب فذلك الذي يضيء نوره في السموات كالشمس إن دعاني لبي
33:72.english: God—Exalted is He—said: {«And establish prayer for My remembrance»} (Q 20:14). And He—Exalted is He—said: {«And be not among the heedless»} (Q 7:205). And He—Mighty and Majestic—said: {«Do not approach prayer while you are intoxicated until you know what you are saying»} (Q 4:43). It was said: "intoxicated" from the excess of worldly concern (al-hamm), and it was said: from love of this world.
33:72.section_title_en: The Virtue of Humble Devotion (Khusḥūʿ) in Prayer
33:72.anchors:
- Root: خشع (Khashaʿa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الخشوع: التواضع والسكون، وخشع بصره: غضه وأطرقه، وخشعت الأصوات: سكنت وخفضت"
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الخشوع: الضراعة والاستكانة، وأصله الانخفاض والتطامن، ويقال للصوت الخفيض والطرف المنكسر"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "Literal: خشع الرجل: خفض رأسه وتواضع. Metaphorical: خشع القلب: خضع وذل وسكن لله"
- Root: سكر (Sukr)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "السكر: نقيض الصحو، والسكران: الذي غطى عقله، وكل شيء غطى فقد سكر"
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "السكر: حالة تعرض بين العقل وبين إدراكه، ويستعار لما يغطي العقل من الهم وحب الدنيا"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "Literal: سكر من الشراب. Metaphorical: سكر الهم وحب الدنيا — ما يغطي العقل عن إدراك المقام"
- Root: ندم (Nadama)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الندم: التحسر على ما فات، والندامة: التوبة، والنادم: المتحسر"
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الندم: انكسار النفس لما فرط، وهو من لوازم التوبة"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "Literal: ندم على الشيء: تحسر. Metaphorical: تنادم في الصلاة: استحضار التقصير والانكسار بين يدي الله"
- Root: وجب (Wajaba)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "وجب القلب: اضطرب وخفق، ووجب الشيء: ثبت ولزم، والوجيب: صوت خفقان القلب"
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الوجيب: اضطراب القلب من هيبة الأمر وعظمته"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "Literal: وجب الباب: أغلقه. Metaphorical: وجيب القلب: خفقانه من الخوف والهيبة"
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — "إنما الصلاة تمسكن" restricts prayer's essence to humility, excluding distraction and heedlessness.
33:72.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Mysteries of Prayer'

38:26.arabic: في تأويل هذه الآية عن جدك {يا داود إنا جعلناك خليفة في الأرض فاحكم بين الناس بالحق ولا تتبع الهوى فيضلك عن سبيل الله} قال الله تعالى في الزبور يا داود إذا قعد الخصمان بين يديك فكان لك في أحدهما هوى فلا تتمنين في نفسك أن يكون الحق له فيفلح على صاحبه فأمحوك عن نبوتي ثم لا تكون خلفتي ولا كرامة يا داود إنما جعلت رسلي إلى عبادي رعاء كرعاء الإبل لعلمهم بالرعاية ورفقهم بالسياسة ليجبروا الكسير ويدلوا الهزيل على الكلأ والماء يا أمير المؤمنين إنك قد بليت بأمر لو عرض على السموات والأرض والجبال لأبين أن يحملنه وأشفقن منه يا أمير المؤمنين حدثني يزيد بن جابر عن عبد الرحمن بن
38:26.english: He turned to al-Shaʿbī and said: "O Abā ʿAmr! I am the trustee of the Commander of the Faithful over Iraq and his governor over it, and a man commanded to obedience. I have been tried with the subjects, and their right has become incumbent upon me. So I love to preserve them and to attend to what sets them right, along with sincere counsel (naṣīḥah) to them. And reports may reach me about a band of people from the regions concerning a matter, and I find myself severe against them therein, so I withhold a portion of their stipends and place it in the treasury (bayt al-māl), with the intention in myself that I shall return it to them. Then it reaches the Commander of the Faithful that I have withheld it in that manner, so he writes to me that I must not return it. I cannot then countermand his order, nor can I execute his letter [against my better judgment]. I am but a man commanded to obedience. Is there any liability upon me in this, and in similar matters, where the intention is as I have described?"
38:26.section_title_en: The Upright Scholars Before the Tyrannical Rulers — Counsel and Fearless Truth-Telling

- Root: نصح (naṣaḥa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning is sincerity, faithfulness, and pure counsel free from deceit; the root denotes the act of seeking the welfare of another with complete integrity.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In theological context, naṣīḥah is the obligation of the sincere advisor to guide the ruler toward divine truth, even at personal peril, as it is a form of worship (ʿibādah) and a trust (amānah).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) usage denotes pure honey (ʿasal naṣīḥ) free from admixture; metaphorical (majāz) usage applies to counsel that is untainted by flattery or self-interest.
- Root: سلط (sulṭ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Denotes authority, power, and dominion; the ruler (sulṭān) is one who has been given sway over affairs.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In Kalam, sulṭān is a trial (ibtilāʾ) and a trust (amānah) from God, whose exercise demands justice (ʿadl) and whose neglect invites divine wrath.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal usage refers to physical power or a governing authority; metaphorical usage extends to the authority of proof (sulṭān al-burhān) that compels assent.
- Root: عظ (waʿaẓa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Root denotes admonition, exhortation, and reminding of consequences; it implies softening the heart through remembrance of God and the Hereafter.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In theological terms, ʿiẓah is the act of turning the soul away from transgression through a blend of fear (tarhīb) and hope (targhīb), grounded in revealed truth.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal usage is the verbal admonition; metaphorical usage is the admonition of circumstance (ʿiẓah al-ḥāl) when events themselves teach a lesson.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Restriction and Focused Predication (bāb al-ḥaṣr wa al-taqyīd bi-innamā) — Governing the emphasis of exclusive predication in statements of counsel, such as "No obedience to a creature in disobedience of the Creator," where the restriction (ḥaṣr) is achieved through negation and exception (nafy wa istithnāʾ).
38:26.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Enjoining Good and Forbidding Evil'

39:70.arabic: الهوى وستجد كل نفس ما عملت من سوء أو خير محضرا عند الله ولو في فلتة خاطر أو فلتة ناظر من غير ظلم وجور فما الله بظلام للعبيد وأما القسم الثاني وهو فوات الحاصل فهو مكروه ومعتبر في جواز السكوت في الأمور الأربعة إلا العلم فإن فواته غير مخوف إلا بتقصير منه وإلا فلا يقدر أحد على سلب العلم من غيره وإن قدر على سلب الصحة والسلامة والثروة والمال وهذا أحد أسباب شرف العلم فإنه يدوم في الدنيا ويدوم ثوابه في الآخرة فلا انقطاع له أبد الآباد وأما الصحة والسلامة ففواتهما بالضرب فكل من عل
39:70.english: All of this does not nullify the obligation of ḥisbah, because these are but increases (ziyādāt) whose attainment is prevented — and calling the mere prevention of attaining increases "harm" (ḍarar) is metaphorical (majāz). True harm (al-ḍarar al-ḥaqīqī) is only the loss of something already in hand (fawāt ḥāṣil). Nothing is excepted from this rule save that which necessity (ḥājah) calls for, and whose loss entails a danger (maḥdhūr) exceeding the danger of remaining silent over the wrong (al-sukūt ʿalā al-munkar) — as when one is in need of a physician for an acute illness, and the cure is anticipated from the physician's treatment, and he knows that in the physician's delay there is severe aggravation of his malady and prolongation of his sickness, which may even lead to death.
39:70.section_title_en: On the Conditions Permitting Abandonment of Enjoining Right — Section 532
39:70.anchors:
- Root: حسب (ḥ-s-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of counting, reckoning, and calculating; al-ḥisbah derives from the notion of taking account of another's deeds.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الحساب: استعمال العدد" — reckoning is the employment of number; the theological nuance connects to divine accounting and the duty of moral reckoning upon others.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): "حسب المال" — to count property. Metaphorical (majāz): "يَتَحَسَّبانِ الأخبار" — to seek out and investigate news, as one probes and tests; thus ḥisbah is the active seeking-out of wrongs to rectify them.
- Root: ضرر (ḍ-r-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of harm, injury, and detriment; al-ḍarar is that which opposes benefit (nafʿ).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Harm is of two kinds — that which is truly detrimental to one's religion or worldly welfare, and that which is merely imagined or anticipated.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: actual physical or material injury. Metaphorical: the mere loss of an anticipated increase (ziyādah), which is not true harm but is called so figuratively.
- Root: سكت (s-k-t)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of silence, refraining from speech.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "السكوت مختص بترك الكلام" — silence is specific to abstaining from speech; it is a form of rest (sukūn) and is used metaphorically for the subsiding of anger or other states.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "رجل سكوت" — a man habitually silent. Metaphorical: "سكت عنه الغضب" — anger subsided; thus al-sukūt ʿan al-munkar is the deliberate cessation of verbal objection.
- Root: علم (ʿ-l-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of knowledge, perception, and discernment.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "العلم: إدراك الشيء بحقيقته" — knowledge is the apprehension of a thing in its true reality; it is that which cannot be forcibly stripped from its possessor.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "ما علمت بخبرك" — I had no awareness of your news. Metaphorical: knowledge as an enduring mark (ʿalam) and signpost of guidance.
- Sibawayh Rule: Restriction and exception (al-ḥaṣr wa al-istithnāʾ) — the conditional framing of permissibility (al-tarkhīṣ) through specified exceptions (istithnāʾ) governed by the weighing of two harms (taʿāruḍ al-mafsadatayn), where the lesser is borne to avert the greater.
39:70.topic: Al-Ghazali on purifying the character, moral diseases, and spiritual remedies, from 'Enjoining Good and Forbidding Evil'

40:21.arabic: أن يأمر بالمعروف فليوطن نفسه على الصبر وليثق بالثواب من الله فمن وثق بالثواب من الله لم يجد مس الأذى فإذن من آداب الحسبة توطين النفس على الصبر ولذلك قرن الله تعالى الصبر بالأمر بالمعروف فقال حاكيا عن لقمان يا بني أقم الصلاة وأمر بالمعروف وانه عن المنكر واصبر على ما أصابك ومن الآداب تقليل العلائق حتى لا يكثر خوفه وقطع الطمع عن الخلائق حتى تزول عنه المداهنة فقد روي عن بعض المشايخ أنه كان له سنور وكان يأخذ من قصاب في جواره كل يوم شيئا من الغدد لسنوره فرأى على القصاب منكرا فدخل الدار أولا وأخرج السنور ثم جاء واحتسب
40:21.english: We do not mean by this that commanding right becomes prohibited by reason of one's sinfulness — rather, its effect upon hearts falls away by the manifestation of his sinfulness to the people. For it has been related from Anas, may God be pleased with him, who said: "We said, 'O Messenger of God, shall we not command right until we have acted upon it entirely, and shall we not forbid wrong until we have shunned it entirely?' He said, may God's peace and blessings be upon him: 'Rather, command right even if you do not act upon it entirely, and forbid wrong even if you do not shun it entirely.'"
40:21.section_title_en: On Gentleness in Commanding Right and Forbidding Wrong — The Etiquette of the Muḥtasib
40:21.anchors:
- Root: عيب (ʿayb)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root meaning — defect, blemish, reproach; to find fault with something.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance — the reproach of intellect (ʿaql) is the severest form of deficiency, for it touches the very faculty by which one is distinguished from beasts.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal vs Metaphorical — here used metaphorically: the reproach falls upon his intellect, i.e., the deficiency of his discernment becomes manifest.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Restriction (Bāb al-Ḥaṣr) — "فإنما يزرى على عقله" restricts the object of reproach to the intellect alone, excluding the person's faith or status.
40:21.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Enjoining Good and Forbidding Evil'

49:9.arabic: الله فسوف نؤتيه أجرا عظيما وقال تعالى وإن طائفتان من المؤمنين اقتتلوا فأصلحوا بينهما الآية والإصلاح نهي عن البغي وإعادة إلى الطاعة فإن لم يفعل فقد أمر الله تعالى بقتاله فقال فقاتلوا التي تبغي حتى تفيء إلى أمر الله وذلك هو النهي عن المنكر وأما الأخبار فمنها ما روي عن أبي بكر الصديق رضي الله عنه أنه قال في خطبة خطبها أيها الناس إنكم تقرءون هذه الآية وتؤولونها على خلاف تأويلها يا أيها الذين آمنوا عليكم أنفسكم لا يضركم من ضل إذا اهتديتم (1) وإني سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول ما من قوم عملوا بالمعاصي وفيهم من يقدر أن ينكر علي
49:9.english: Know that the verses indicating the obligation of commanding right and forbidding wrong are numerous. Among them is His saying, may He be exalted: {«Let there arise from among you a nation inviting to good, commanding right and forbidding wrong — and those are the successful»} (Āl ʿImrān 3:104). In this verse is the declaration of obligation, for His saying, may He be exalted, "Let there be" (wal-takun) is a command, and the apparent meaning of a command is obligation. In it also is the declaration that success (falāḥ) is contingent upon it, for He restricted it and said: {«And those are the successful»}. In it also is the declaration that it is a collective obligation (farḍ kifāyah), not an individual obligation (farḍ ʿayn), and that when a group undertakes it, the obligation falls from the rest — for He did not say, "Let all of you be commanders of right," but rather said: {«Let there arise from among you a nation»}. Thus, whenever one person or a group undertakes it, the burden falls from the others, and success is particularized to those who undertake it and directly perform it. But if all of creation were to hold back from it, the burden would encompass all those capable of it without exception.
49:9.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Enjoining Good and Forbidding Evil'

49:9.arabic: فقد أمر الله تعالى بقتاله فقال فقاتلوا التي تبغي حتى تفيء إلى أمر الله وذلك هو النهي عن المنكر وأما الأخبار فمنها ما روي عن أبي بكر الصديق رضي الله عنه أنه قال في خطبة خطبها أيها الناس إنكم تقرءون هذه الآية وتؤولونها على خلاف تأويلها يا أيها الذين آمنوا عليكم أنفسكم لا يضركم من ضل إذا اهتديتم (1) وإني سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول ما من قوم عملوا بالمعاصي وفيهم من يقدر أن ينكر عليهم فلم يفعل إلا يوشك أن يعمهم الله بعذاب من عنده وروى عن أبي ثعلبة الخشني أنه سأل رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عن تفسير قوله تعال
49:9.english: Know that the verses indicating the obligation of commanding right and forbidding wrong are numerous. Among them is His saying, may He be exalted: {«Let there arise from among you a nation inviting to good, commanding right and forbidding wrong — and those are the successful»} (Āl ʿImrān 3:104). In this verse is the declaration of obligation, for His saying, may He be exalted, "Let there be" (wal-takun) is a command, and the apparent meaning of a command is obligation. In it also is the declaration that success (falāḥ) is contingent upon it, for He restricted it and said: {«And those are the successful»}. In it also is the declaration that it is a collective obligation (farḍ kifāyah), not an individual obligation (farḍ ʿayn), and that when a group undertakes it, the obligation falls from the rest — for He did not say, "Let all of you be commanders of right," but rather said: {«Let there arise from among you a nation»}. Thus, whenever one person or a group undertakes it, the burden falls from the others, and success is particularized to those who undertake it and directly perform it. But if all of creation were to hold back from it, the burden would encompass all those capable of it without exception.
49:9.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Enjoining Good and Forbidding Evil'

61:2.arabic: وقد قال الله تعالى يا أيها الذين آمنوا أنفقوا من طيبات ما كسبتم ومما أخرجنا لكم من الأرض ولا تيمموا الخبيث منه تنفقون ولستم بآخذيه إلا أن تغمضوا فيه أي لا تأخذوه إلا مع كراهية وحياء وهو معنى الإغماض فلا تؤثروا به ربكم وفي الخبر سبق درهم مائة ألف درهم (3) وذلك بأن يخرجه الإنسان وهو من أحل ماله وأجوده فيصدر ذلك عن الرضا والفرح بالبذل وقد يخرج مائة ألف درهم مما يكره من ماله فيدل ذلك على أنه ليس يؤثر الله عز وجل بشيء مما يحبه وبذلك ذم الله تعالى قوما جعلوا لله ما يكرهون فقال تعال
61:2.english: The heart is not treated save with the compound electuary (maʿjūn) of knowledge and works. And this condition among the conditions of almsgiving runs in the same course as humility (al-khushūʿ) runs in the prayer. This is established by his saying — may Allah bless him and grant him peace: "A man has nothing of his prayer save that of which he was conscious." And this is like his saying — may Allah bless him and grant him peace: "Allah does not accept the charity of the one who bestows it with reproach (al-mannān)." And like His saying — Exalted is He: {«لا تبطلوا صدقاتكم بالمن والأذى»} ("Do not nullify your charities by reproach and injury"). As for the legal opinion (fatwā) of the jurist that the alms fall in their proper place and that one's liability is discharged without this condition — that is another discussion, and we have already pointed to its meaning in the Book of Prayer.
61:2.section_title_en: The Inner Conditions of Charity — Section 175 (From The Revival of the Religious Sciences, Book of the Mysteries of Almsgiving)
61:2.anchors:
- Root: قلب (q-l-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "To turn, overturn, transform a thing from one state to another; to rotate, to flip"
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "قلب الشيء: تصريفه وصرفه عن وجه إلى وجه" — the heart is so named because of its constant turning and transformation between states
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "قلب الشيء قلبا: حوله عن وجهه" (to turn a thing from its face). Metaphorical: "رجل قلب حول: يقلب الأمور ويحتال" — one who turns matters over and manages them; "قلبوا لك الأمور" (they turned matters against you)
- Root: وجل (w-j-l)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "Fear, dread, apprehension that strikes the heart"
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الوجل: استشعار الخوف" — the sensing of fear; cited in {«إنما المؤمنون الذين إذا ذكر الله وجلت قلوبهم»}
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "رجل وجل، وقوم وجال" — a fearful man, a fearful people; "وفي قلبه وجل" — in his heart is dread
- Root: عجب (ʿ-j-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "Wonder, amazement; self-admiration, vanity"
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Self-admiration (al-ʿujb) is a destructive spiritual ailment that nullifies deeds
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: wonder at something extraordinary. Metaphorical: self-conceit regarding one's own acts of obedience
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد (Restriction & Focused Predication) — governing the precise limitation of general categories (al-ṣifāt al-khāṣṣah within al-aṣnāf al-thamāniyyah) and the conditional structure of acceptance
