61:2.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Duties of Brotherhood'

61:2.arabic: علمه وقوله تعالى لم تقولون ما لا تفعلون المراد به الوعد الكاذب وقوله عز وجل وتنسون أنفسكم إنكار من حيث إنهم نسوا أنفسهم لا من حيث إنهم أمروا غيرهم ولكن ذكر أمر الغير استدلالا به على علمهم وتأكيدا للحجة عليهم وقوله يا ابن مريم عظ نفسك الحديث هو في الحسبة بالوعظ وقد سلمنا أن وعظ الفاسق ساقط الجدوى عند من يعرف فسقه ثم قوله فاستحى مني لا يدل على تحريم وعظ الغير بل معناه استحى مني فلا تترك الأهم وتشتغل بالمهم كما يقال احفظ أباك ثم جارك وإلا فاستحي فإن قيل فليجز للكافر الذمي أن يحتسب عل
61:2.english: If it is said: "Then let the unbelieving dhimmī (protected non-Muslim subject) be permitted to enjoin right upon a Muslim if he sees him committing fornication — for his saying 'Do not fornicate' is true in itself, so it is impossible that it be unlawful for him; rather, it ought to be permissible or even obligatory."
61:2.section_title_en: The Revival of the Religious Sciences — Book of Blame of Status-Seeking and Hypocrisy: Section 525 — The First Pillar: The One Who Enjoins Right (Al-Muḥtasib)
61:2.anchors:
- Root: حسب (ḥ-s-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To count, reckon, compute; to hold an opinion or estimation.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الحساب: استعمال العدد" — the act of employing number; the reckoning of deeds. The muḥtasib is one who "reckons" or "takes account" of others' actions, demanding the right and forbidding the wrong.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Haqiqah (Literal): "حسب المال" — he counted the wealth. Majaz (Metaphorical): "يَتَحَسَّبانِ الأَخبار" — they seek out and ascertain news, as one places assumption in the position of knowledge. The "ḥisbah" is the act of account-taking, extended metaphorically to the duty of commanding right and forbidding wrong.
- Root: قهر (q-h-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To overcome, subdue, dominate; to force against one's will.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "القهر: الغلبة والتذليل معا" — overpowering and subjugation together. It is used of God's absolute dominance over His creation.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Haqiqah: "أخذتهم قهرة: من غير رضاهم" — he seized them by force, without their consent. Majaz: "جبال قواهر: شوامخ" — towering, overbearing mountains. The "qahr" in ḥisbah is the coercive enforcement of the right, distinct from mere verbal admonition.
- Root: فسق (f-s-q)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To emerge, exit, depart; of a date, to split from its skin.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "فسق فلان: خرج عن حجر الشرع" — he went out from the enclosure of the Sacred Law. It is more general than unbelief (kufr), applying to the one who commits to the Law's rulings then violates them, in whole or in part.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Haqiqah: "فسق عن أمر الله: خرج" — he departed from God's command. Majaz: "وفسقت الرطبة عن قشرها" — the ripe date burst from its skin. The fāsiq is one who has "burst out" of obedience.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The permissibility of interposing elements between a governing word and its dependent, provided the intervening clause is complete in itself, as in "إن به..." — governing the syntactic flow of conditional and exceptive constructions in the argumentation.
61:2.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Enjoining Good and Forbidding Evil'

2:45.arabic: تعالى وإنها لكبيرة إلا على الخاشعين وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم اعبد الله في الرضا فإن لم تستطع ففي الصبر على ما تكره خير كثير (2) ثم لا يكن في نيل السعادة الموعودة على حسن الخلق استلذاذ الطاعة واستكراه المعصية في زمان دون زمان بل ينبغي أن يكون ذلك على الدوام وفي جملة العمر وكلما كان العمر أطول كانت الفضيلة ارسخ وأكمل ولذلك لما سئل صلى الله عليه وسلم عن السعادة فقال طول العمر في طاعة الله تعالى (3) ولذلك كره الأنبياء والأولياء الموت فإن الدنيا مزرعة الآخرة وكلما كانت العبادات أكثر بط
2:45.english: And all the morally praiseworthy traits sanctioned by the Sacred Law are attained through this path. Its ultimate goal is that the act issuing from one becomes pleasurable (ladhīdh). For the generous person is the one who takes pleasure in expending the wealth he gives, not the one who gives it out of aversion. And the humble person is the one who takes pleasure in humility. The religious moral traits will never become firmly rooted in the soul so long as the soul has not habituated itself to all virtuous practices, has not abandoned all vicious acts, and has not persisted therein with the persistence of one who yearns for beautiful deeds and delights in them, and who detests ugly deeds and suffers pain from them — as he (peace and blessings be upon him) said: «وجعلت قرة عيني في الصلاة» ("And the coolness of my eye was placed in the prayer"). And whenever acts of worship and the abandonment of forbidden things are performed with aversion and reluctance, that is deficiency, and the perfection of felicity is not attained thereby. Indeed, persisting in them through striving is better — but better relative to abandoning them entirely, not relative to performing them willingly. For this reason God (Exalted is He) said: {وَإِنَّهَا لَكَبِيرَةٌ إِلَّا عَلَى الْخَاشِعِينَ} ("And indeed it is grievous, save upon the humble" — {Al-Baqarah: 45}), and he (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Worship God in a state of contentment; but if you are not able, then in patience upon what you dislike there is abundant good."
2:45.section_title_en: The Explanation of the Acceptability of Moral Character to Change through Discipline
2:45.anchors:
- Root: خلق (khalaqa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning is "to measure/estimate rightly" (taqdīr mustaqīm); al-khuluq is the inward disposition, the "measure" of the soul's constitution.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Creation (khalq) is bringing into being upon a right measure; moral character (khuluq) is the soul's settled form (ṣūrah) — either its natural constitution or one acquired through discipline.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) — the craftsman's precise measuring before cutting; Metaphorical (majāz) — God's bringing things into existence upon a measure required by wisdom, and the soul's acquired disposition.
- Root: وسط (wasaṭ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The middle, the center, that which is equally distant from two extremes.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The mean (iʿtidāl) is the praiseworthy station between two blameworthy extremes; the intellect's governance requires steering between excess and neglect.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — the physical center of a thing; Metaphorical — the balanced state of the soul's faculties.
- Root: رياضة (riyāḍah)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Training, disciplining, breaking in (as a horse); repeated exercise until obedience becomes natural.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The soul's training (riyāḍat al-nafs) through imposing upon it acts contrary to its habitual vice until the virtue becomes ingrained.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — physical exercise; Metaphorical — the soul's moral training through sustained self-imposed practice.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب التمييز بين الحال المؤسسة والحال المؤكدة (Distinguishing establishing from confirming circumstantial clauses) — the clause "فكأنه خال عن الوصفين" establishes a new state rather than confirming an existing one, marking the conceptual middle as devoid of both extreme attributes.
2:45.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Breaking the Two Desires'

3:134.arabic: وقوله {ادفع بالتي هي أحسن فإذا الذي بينك وبينه عداوة كأنه ولي حميم} وقوله {والكاظمين الغيظ والعافين عن الناس والله يحب المحسنين} وقوله {اجتنبوا كثيرا من الظن إن بعض الظن إثم ولا تجسسوا ولا يغتب بعضكم بعضا} ولما كسرت رباعيته وشج يوم أحد فجعل الدم يسيل على وجهه وهو يمسح الدم ويقول كيف يفلح قوم خضبوا وجه نبيهم بالدم وهو يدعوهم إلى ربهم (4) فأنزل الله تعالى {ليس لك من الأمر شيء} تأديبا له على ذلك وأمثال هذه التأديبات في القرآن لا تحصر وهو صلى الله عليه وسلم المقصود الأول بالتأديب والتهذيب ثم منه يشرق النور على كافة الخلق فإنه أدب بالقرآن وأدب الخ
3:134.english: The Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, was abundant in supplication and earnest entreaty, perpetually asking God Most High to adorn him with the beauties of refined conduct and the noble traits of character. Thus he would say in his supplication: "O God, beautify my outward form and my inward character (khuluqī wa-khalqī)" (1), and he would say: "O God, protect me from the reprehensible traits of character" (2). God Most High answered his supplication, fulfilling His word, Exalted is He: {«ادعوني أستجب لكم»} ["Call upon Me, I will answer you"] (Ghafir 40:60). So He sent down upon him the Qur'an and disciplined him through it, and his character became the Qur'an.
3:134.section_title_en: The Prophet's Discipline Through the Qur'an and the Invitation to Noble Moral Traits
3:134.anchors:
- Root: خلق (khalaqa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of measuring, fashioning, and creating upon a precise estimation; also used for innate disposition and character.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الخلق أصله: التقدير المستقيم" — the root denotes straight/right estimation; used for bringing something into being from nothing (ibdāʿ) and for the moral constitution of the soul.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): "خلق الخراز الأديم" — the leather-worker measures before cutting. Metaphorical (Majaz): "خلق الله الخلق: أوجده على تقدير أوجبته الحكمة" — God's creation is bringing into existence upon a measure required by wisdom; and "له خلق حسن" — he has beautiful character.
- Root: كرم (karuma)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Generosity, nobility, honor; the root of karīm (noble/generous) and makārim (noble traits).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الكرم إذا وصف الله تعالى به فهو اسم لإحسانه وإنعامه المتظاهر" — when attributed to God, it denotes His manifest beneficence; when attributed to man, it denotes praiseworthy morals and deeds that appear from him.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "كرم علينا فلان كرامة" — he showed generosity. Metaphorical: "قوم كرم" — a noble people; "كرم السحاب تكريما: جاد بمطره" — the cloud was generous with its rain.
- Root: أدب (adaba)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Refinement, discipline, cultivation of character; calling to a gathering (ma'dabah) — the root implies assembling and summoning toward excellence.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Discipline (ta'dīb) is the cultivation of the soul through praiseworthy traits and the restraint from blameworthy ones.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "أدبته تأديبا" — I disciplined him. Metaphorical: "أدبه الله" — God disciplined him, i.e., refined his character through divine instruction.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — "إنما أدبه القرآن" restricts the means of the Prophet's discipline exclusively to the Qur'an, affirming that the Qur'an alone was the sufficient and complete instrument of his moral formation.
3:134.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications, prayers, and their spiritual power, from 'Breaking the Two Desires'

7:31.arabic: قال تعالى {وكلوا واشربوا ولا تسرفوا} وقال تعالى {ولا تجعل يدك مغلولة إلى عنقك ولا تبسطها كل البسط} وقد قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم خيركم خيركم لأهله (5) وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم دينار أنفقته في سبيل الله ودينار أنفقته في رقبة ودينار تصدقت به على مسكين ودينار أنفقته على أهلك أعظمها أجرا الذي أنفقته على أهلك (6) وقيل كان لعلي رضي الله عنه أربع نسوة فكان يشتري لكل واحدة في كل أربعة أيام لحما بدرهم وقال الحسن رضي الله عنه كانوا في الرجال مخاصيب والإناث والثياب مجاديب وقال ابن سيرين يستحب للرجل أن ي
7:31.english: The first point of etiquette is the wedding feast (walīmah), and it is recommended (mustaḥabbah). Anas, may God be pleased with him, said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, saw upon ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf, may God be pleased with him, a trace of yellow dye, so he said: {«What is this?»} He replied: "I have married a woman for the weight of a date-stone in gold." He said: "May God bless you. Hold a wedding feast, even if with a single sheep." {«...»} And the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, held a wedding feast for Ṣafiyyah with dates and sawīq (barley porridge). {«...»} And he, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: "The food of the first day is an obligation (ḥaqq), the food of the second day is a Sunnah, and the food of the third day is for show (sumʿah); and whoever seeks to be heard, God will make his deeds heard." {«...»} None raised this hadith except Ziyād ibn ʿAbd Allāh, and it is anomalous (gharīb). It is recommended to offer congratulations to him, and the one who enters upon the husband should say: "May God bless you and shower blessings upon you, and may He bring you both together in goodness." {«...»} Abū Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him, reported that he, may God bless him and grant him peace, commanded this. It is also recommended to make the marriage public (iẓhār al-nikāḥ). He, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: "The distinction between the lawful and the unlawful is the drum and the voice." {«...»} The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: "Announce this marriage, hold it in the mosques, and beat drums for it." {«...»} And on the authority of al-Rubayyiʿ bint Muʿawwidh, she said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came and entered on the morning of my wedding night, and he sat upon my bedding, and we had young girls with us who were beating their drums and lamenting those of my forefathers who had been killed—until one of them said: "And among us is a Prophet who knows what will be tomorrow." He said to her: "Stop this, and say what you were saying before." {«...»}
7:31.section_title_en: On What is Incumbent Upon the Husband and What is Incumbent Upon the Wife
7:31.anchors:
- Root: و ل م (w-l-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The core meaning pertains to the wedding feast (walīmah), derived from the concept of gathering and union.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In theological usage, it signifies the communal meal marking the consummation of a marriage contract, a recommended act of public gratitude.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah) usage denotes the specific feast; metaphorical (Majaz) extension applies to any act of publicizing a joyous occasion.
- Root: ع ش ر (ʿ- sh-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The root denotes association, companionship, and intimacy; the tenth (ʿasharah) of a thing is related, but the primary social sense is cohabitation and mutual dealing.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In the Quranic context of {وَعَاشِرُوهُنَّ بِالْمَعْرُوفِ}, it signifies a sustained, equitable mode of social intercourse grounded in moral rectitude, not mere physical proximity.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah) usage is the act of living together; metaphorical (Majaz) usage elevates it to a standard of ethical conduct (maʿrūf) that defines the marital bond.
- Root: ق س م (q-s-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The root indicates division, apportionment, and distribution; in the marital context, it refers to the equitable division of time among co-wives.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theologically, it is tied to justice (ʿadl) as a divine attribute; for the husband, it is a legal obligation to maintain fairness in material and temporal allotments.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah) usage is the physical act of dividing; metaphorical (Majaz) usage applies to the moral duty of impartiality in affection and provision.
- Root: غ ي ر (gh-y-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The root conveys alteration and change, but in the moral register, it denotes protective jealousy (ghayrah), a state of aversion to the violation of honor.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In Kalam, ghayrah is a praiseworthy emotion when aligned with divine law—jealousy for the sanctity of the family—and blameworthy when it stems from unjust suspicion (sūʾ al-ẓann).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah) usage is the emotional state; metaphorical (Majaz) usage is attributed to God (al-Ghayyār) as a figure for His prohibition of indecencies, distinguishing human passion from divine will.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — Used to isolate specific obligations (e.g., "the third is that he should increase...") and to distinguish categories of jealousy and pride, ensuring precise legal and moral demarcation.
7:31.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'Breaking the Two Desires'

7:200.arabic: إليه ليدفعه عنه كما قال الله تعالى {وإما ينزغنك من الشيطان نزغ فاستعذ بالله إنه سميع عليم} وقال تعالى {إن الذين اتقوا إذا مسهم طائف من الشيطان تذكروا فإذا هم مبصرون} وإلى ما يشك فيه فينبغي أن يعرض ذلك على شيخه بل كل ما يجد في قلبه من الأحوال من فترة أو نشاط أو التفات إلى علقة أو صدق في إرادة فينبغي أن يظهر ذلك لشيخه وأن يستره عن غيره فلا يطلع عليه أحدا ثم إن شيخه ينظر في حاله ويتأمل في ذكائه وكياسته فلو علم أنه لو تركه وأمره بالفكر تنبه من نفسه على حقيقة الحق فينبغي أن يحيله على الفكر ويأمره بملازمته حتى يقذف في قلبه من النور ما يكشف له حق
7:200.english: As for hunger — it diminishes the blood of the heart and whitens it, and in its whiteness is its light; it melts the fat of the heart (shahm al-fuʾād), and in its melting is its tenderness; and its tenderness is the key to unveiling (mukāshafah), just as its hardness is the cause of the veil. And whenever the blood of the heart diminishes, the passage of the enemy narrows, for his channels are the veins filled with desires. Jesus, peace be upon him, said: "O company of disciples, hunger your bellies, that perhaps your hearts may see your Lord." And Sahl ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Tustarī said: "The substitutes (abdāl) became substitutes only through four qualities: emptying the bellies, vigil, silence, and withdrawal from people." The benefit of hunger in illuminating the heart is a manifest matter to which experience bears witness, and the explanation of the gradual method in it will come in the Book of Breaking the Two Desires.
7:200.section_title_en: The Path of the Seeker: On the Four Fortresses of Solitude, Silence, Hunger, and Vigilance
7:200.anchors:
- Root: قلب (q-l-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To turn over, to revolve, to transform from one state to another; the heart as that which constantly fluctuates and turns.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): تصريفه وصرفه عن وجه إلى وجه — the heart's perpetual turning and overturning; its rectification (إصلاح) is the seeker's sole aim, that it might witness its Lord.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Haqiqah: turning a thing over; Majaz: the heart's disposition and its being veiled or illumined.
- Root: طرق (t-r-q)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To strike, to beat upon; the road (طريق) that is beaten by feet.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The path trodden; metaphorically, every course a man pursues, whether praiseworthy or blameworthy.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Haqiqah: striking iron with a hammer; Majaz: the "strikers of the road" (قواطع الطريق) — the highway robbers who cut off the seeker's passage.
- Root: كان (k-w-n)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To be, to come into existence; the copula of being.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Existence and becoming; the states (أحوال) that befall the heart.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Haqiqah: being; Majaz: the continuous state of the servant before his Lord.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد (Restriction & Focused Predication) — The conditional and restrictive constructions (إنما، لا...إلا) governing the exclusive means of spiritual purification.
7:200.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Breaking the Two Desires'

7:201.arabic: قال الله تعالى إن الذين اتقوا إذا مسهم طائف من الشيطان تذكروا فإذا هم مبصرون فأخبر أن جلاء القلب وإبصاره يحصل بالذكر وأنه لا يتمكن منه إلا الذين اتقوا فالتقوى باب الذكر والذكر باب الكشف والكشف باب الفوز الأكبر وهو الفوز بلقاء الله تعالى
7:201.english: As for the praiseworthy effects that we have mentioned, they increase the mirror of the heart in clarity (jalā'), radiance (ishrāq), light (nūr), and brilliance (ḍiyā'), until the clear truth (jalīyat al-ḥaqq) gleams within it and the reality of the sought-after matter in religion is unveiled in it. And it is to such a heart that the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, pointed when he said: "When God desires good for a servant, He appoints for him an admonisher from his own heart." (1) The hadith: "Whoever has from his heart an admonisher, upon him is from God a protector" — I have not found for it a source (aṣl).
7:201.section_title_en: The Heart as a Mirror: The Effects of Virtues and Vices upon Spiritual Perception
7:201.anchors:
- Root: قلب (q-l-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To turn over, to overturn, to transform from one state to another; the heart as that which is constantly fluctuating and turning between states.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "قلب الشيء: تصريفه وصرفه عن وجه إلى وجه" — The heart is that which is perpetually turned about, and its rectitude or corruption depends upon the direction of its turning.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): physical turning over. Metaphorical (Majaz): "قلب المعلم الصبيان: صرفهم إلى بيوتهم" — the turning of a thing toward its proper end. Here, the heart is a mirror (مرآة) turned toward either the light of truth or the darkness of sin.
- Root: رين (r-y-n)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Rust, tarnish, or filth that overcomes a polished surface, veiling its original brightness.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The covering of the heart by accumulated sin, such that it becomes rusted over and incapable of receiving the light of truth.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the tarnishing of a blade or mirror. Metaphorical: the veiling of the heart's perceptive faculty by the accumulation of transgressions, as in {«كلا بل ران على قلوبهم ما كانوا يكسبون»} (The Mutaffifin: 14).
- Root: طبع (t-b-')
  * Lisan / Ayn: To stamp, to seal, to impress upon; the imprinting of a seal that renders the surface impermeable to further impression.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The sealing of the heart by God as a consequence of persistent sin, rendering it deaf to admonition and blind to truth.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the physical stamping of a seal. Metaphorical: the divine sealing of the heart as a just consequence of willful persistence in transgression.
- Root: ذكر (dh-k-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Remembrance, recollection, mindfulness; the opposite of forgetfulness (نسيان).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The presence of the thing remembered in the mind; the highest form being the remembrance of God which brings tranquility to the heart.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: verbal invocation. Metaphorical: the state of spiritual presence and awareness that polishes the heart's mirror and unveils the reality of truth.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The syntactic connection between cause and effect, as in the verse {«واتقوا الله واسمعوا»}, where hearing (spiritual perception) is grammatically and semantically linked to piety (تقوى), just as the sealing of the heart (طبع) is linked to the accumulation of sins (ذنوب).
7:201.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Breaking the Two Desires'

8:2.arabic: وقد قال الله تعالى {إنما المؤمنون الذين إذا ذكر الله وجلت قلوبهم} وقال تعالى {لو أنزلنا هذا القرآن على جبل لرأيته خاشعا متصدعا من خشية الله} فالوجل والخشوع وجد من قبيل الأحوال وإن لم يكن من قبيل المكاشفات ولكن قد يصير سببا للمكاشفات والتنبيهات ولهذا قال صلى الله عليه وسلم زينوا القرآن بأصواتكم (3) وقال لأبي موسى الأشعري لقد أوتى مزمارا من مزامير آل داود عليه السلام (1) وأما الحكايات الدالة على أن أرباب القلوب ظهر عليهم الوجد عند سماع القرآن فكثيرة فقوله صلى الله عليه وسلم شيبتني هود وأخواتها (2) خبر عن الوجد فإن الشي
8:2.english:
**QUAD_ANCHORS:**
- Root: وجد (Wajd)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The root وجد encompasses multiple senses: finding/attaining (إدراك), intense love (الحب الشديد), grief (الحزن), and wealth/sufficiency (الغنى). Al-Khalil notes the range: "الوجد: الحب. والوجد: الحزن. والوجد: الغنى. والوجد: إدراك الشيء"
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الوجد: إدراك الشيء على خلاف ما يطلب" — and in the technical terminology of the Sufis: "ما يصادف القلب من واردات الأحوال" (what the heart encounters of the influxes of spiritual states)
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal sense is finding/attaining; metaphorical extension (majāz) in devotional context: "وجد فلان في العبادة وجدا: إذا أتى بها على وجهها مع حضور القلب"
- Root: طبع (Tabʿ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الطبع: السجية التي جبل عليها الإنسان" — the innate disposition upon which one is created; also "الختم" (sealing)
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الطبع: السجية التي جبل عليها الإنسان" — the original constitution
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Distinguishes "مطبوع" (innate/natural) from "متكلف" (deliberately acquired) — "فلان مطبوع على الكرم، ومتكلف له"
- Root: كلف (Kulfah/Takalluf)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "التكلف: تجشم ما لا يلزمك" — undertaking what is not incumbent upon you with effort and hardship
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "التكلف: تجشم ما ليس من شأنه" — burdening oneself with what is not one's natural concern
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "تكلفت الأمر: تجشمته على مشقة" — deliberate self-imposition of effort
- Root: سمع (Samāʿ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Auditory perception; also what is heard — recitation, song, remembrance
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "السماع عند الصوفية: ما يهيج الوجد من الأصوات الموزونة" — that which stirs ecstatic finding from measured sounds
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "السماع عند القوم: حضور مجلس يهيج الأحوال الشريفة" — attending an assembly that stirs noble spiritual states
- Root: عشق (ʿIshq)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "العشق: فرط الحب" — excessive love; from "العشقة" — a plant that twines around another
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "العشق: فرط الحب، وأصله من عشقة النبات وهي ما التف منه على غيره"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "العشق مجاز في حق الله تعالى" — metaphorical when applied to God
- Root: بكى (Bukāʾ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Weeping, shedding tears
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "البكاء: إجراء الدمع من عين لحزن أو غيره"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "تباكى: تكلف البكاء" — deliberate self-induced weeping
- Root: صعق (Ṣaʿq)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الصعق: الغشي. والصعق: الموت" — swooning/loss of consciousness; death
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الصعق: غشية تعرض من صوت شديد أو هول"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "صعق من هول الأمر: إذا غشي عليه من شدة الخوف"
- Root: خشع (Khushūʿ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الخشوع: الخضوع والتذلل" — humility and submissiveness
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الخشوع: التذلل والخضوع، وقيل: الخشوع في الصوت والبصر، والخضوع في البدن"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "خشعت الأصوات: سكنت. وخشع البصر: انكسر"
- Root: أنس (Uns)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الأنس: نقيض الوحشة" — the opposite of loneliness/estrangement
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الأنس: حضور القلب مع المحبوب" — the heart's presence with the Beloved
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "الأنس بالله: سكون القلب إليه"
- Root: وجل (Wajal)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الوجل: الخوف مع اضطراب القلب" — fear accompanied by cardiac agitation
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الوجل: الخوف مع اضطراب القلب"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "الوجل: أشد من الخوف، فإنه مع اضطراب"
- Root: طمأن (Ṭumaʾnīnah)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الطمأنينة: السكون" — tranquility
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الطمأنينة: سكون القلب بعد اضطراب"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "اطمأن القلب: سكن بعد اضطراب"
- Root: قشعر (Iqshirʿār)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "القشعريرة: تقبض الجلد من الخوف" — contraction of the skin from fear
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الاقشعرار: انقباض الجلد وتقبضه من الخوف"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "اقشعر الجلد من الخوف: إذا تقبض"
- Root: لين (Līn)

8:2.english: For this reason, Yūsuf ibn Asbāṭ said: "I intend to recite the Qur'an, but when I recall what is in it, I fear abhorrence (al-maqt), so I turn instead to glorification (al-tasbīḥ) and seeking forgiveness (al-istighfār)."

9:24.arabic: المحبوبات كما قال الله تعالى قل إن كان آباؤكم وأبناؤكم وإخوانكم وأزواجكم إلى قوله أحب إليكم من الله ورسوله وجهاد في سبيله فتربصوا حتى يأتي الله بأمره فمن عنده شيء أحب إليه من الله فقلبه مريض كما أن كل معدة صار الطين أحب إليها من الخبز والماء أو سقطت شهوتها عن الخبز والماء فهي مريضة فهذه علامات المرض وبهذا يعرف أن القلوب كلها مريضة إلا ما شاء الله إلا أن من الأمراض ما لا يعرفها صاحبها ومرض القلب مما لا يعرفه صاحبه فلذلك يغفل عنه وإن عرفه صعب عليه الصبر على مرارة دوائه فإن دواءه مخالفة الشهوات وهو نزع الروح فإن وجد من نفسه
9:24.english: I say: The soul (nafs) that belongs to the human being — that by which he is distinguished from the beasts — for he is not distinguished from them by the power of eating, copulation, sight, or any other such thing. Rather, he is distinguished by the knowledge of things as they truly are. And the Origin of all things, their Existentiator and their Inventor, is God, Mighty and Majestic — He who made them things. So if one knew everything but did not know God, Mighty and Majestic, it would be as though he knew nothing at all. And the sign of knowledge is love: whoever knows God Most High loves Him. And the sign of love is that one does not prefer over Him this world nor any other beloved thing. As God Most High said: {«Say: If your fathers, your sons, your brothers, your spouses, your clans — the wealth you have acquired, commerce whose decline you fear, and dwellings you find pleasing — are more beloved to you than God and His Messenger and striving in His cause, then wait until God brings about His command»} [Q 9:24]. So whoever possesses something more beloved to him than God — his heart is sick. Just as any stomach to which clay has become more beloved than bread and water, or whose appetite for bread and water has fallen away — it is sick. These are the signs of sickness. And by this it is known that all hearts are sick — except what God wills. Yet among sicknesses there are those the sufferer does not recognize; and the sickness of the heart is among those the sufferer does not recognize. For this reason he is heedless of it. And even if he recognized it, patience upon the bitterness of its medicine would be difficult for him — for its medicine is opposing the appetites, and that is the tearing out of the spirit (nafs). And if he found in himself the strength of patience upon it, he would not find a skillful physician to treat him — for the physicians are the scholars, and sickness has overcome them. So the sick physician rarely attends to his own cure. For this reason the malady has become chronic and the sickness chronic. This science has become effaced, and the medicine of hearts is denied entirely, and the sickness of the heart is denied. And creation has turned to the love of this world and to deeds whose outward form is acts of worship but whose inward reality is habit and ostentation. These are the signs of the roots of sicknesses.
9:24.section_title_en: The Soul's Distinction, the Sickness of the Heart, and the Path of Moderation

  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: bodily illness; Metaphorical: spiritual malady whereby the heart inclines toward what is harmful and away from what is beneficial
- Root: قلب (q-l-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The heart; that which is ever-turning and fluctuating between states
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The heart as the seat of understanding and moral perception; its "turning" (taqlīb) signifies its instability between soundness and sickness
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the physical organ; Metaphorical: the spiritual faculty of cognition and moral discernment
- Root: خلق (kh-l-q)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Measured, proportioned disposition; character and temperament
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Moral character as the inward form (ṣūrah bāṭinah) corresponding to the outward physical form
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: measuring and proportioning; Metaphorical: the ingrained disposition that governs action
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — The use of restrictive constructions to isolate the defining characteristic of the human soul as knowledge of God, not animal appetites

9:24.arabic: تعالى إذ لا يحبه إلا من عرفه ولهذا قال تعالى قل إن كان آباؤكم وأبناؤكم وإخوانكم وأزواجكم وعشيرتكم وأموال اقترفتموها وتجارة تخشون كسادها ومساكن ترضونها أحب إليكم من الله ورسوله وجهاد في سبيله فتربصوا حتى يأتي الله بأمره فإذن كل من فارقته روحه في حالة خطرة الإنكار على الله تعالى بباله وظهر بغض فعل الله بقلبه في تفريقه بينه وبين أهله وماله وسائر محابه فيكون موته قدوما على ما أبغضه وفراقا بيان معنى سوء الخاتمة
9:24.english: And the cause which leads to such an end is the domination of love of this world, and reposing upon it, and rejoicing in its means — along with the weakness of faith which necessitates the weakness of love of God — exalted. Whoever finds in his heart the love of God more dominant than the love of this world — even if he also loves this world — is farther from this peril. And love of this world is the head of every sin (raʾs kull khaṭīʾah), and it is the chronic disease (al-dāʾ al-ʿuḍāl), and it has pervaded all classes of creatures. And all of that is due to the paucity of knowledge of God — exalted — for none loves Him except one who knows Him. For this reason, God — exalted — said: {Say: If your fathers, your sons, your brothers, your spouses, your clan, wealth which you have acquired, commerce whose decline you fear, and dwellings which please you are more beloved to you than God, His Messenger, and striving in His cause, then wait until God brings about His command} {«قُلْ إِن كَانَ آبَاؤُكُمْ وَأَبْنَاؤُكُمْ وَإِخْوَانُكُمْ وَأَزْوَاجُكُمْ وَعَشِيرَتُكُمْ وَأَمْوَالٌ اقْتَرَفْتُمُوهَا وَتِجَارَةٌ تَخْشَوْنَ كَسَادَهَا وَمَسَاكِنُ تَرْضَوْنَهَا أَحَبَّ إِلَيْكُم مِّنَ اللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ وَجِهَادٍ فِي سَبِيلِهِ فَتَرَبَّصُوا حَتَّىٰ يَأْتِيَ اللَّهُ بِأَمْرِهِ»} [Quran 9:24]. Therefore, whoever's soul departs from him in a state of perilous denial of God — exalted — in his mind, and hatred of God's act appears in his heart regarding His separating him from his family, wealth, and all his beloved things — then his death becomes an advance toward what he abhorred and a parting from what he loved.
9:24.section_title_en: The Meaning of an Evil End (Bayān Maʿnā Sūʾ al-Khātimah)
9:24.anchors:
- Root: غرر (gh-r-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of delusion, heedlessness, and being deceived by that which appears favorable while concealing harm.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-Ghurūr is a false hope that leads one to rely on transient things; theologically, it is reliance on other than God.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah) — deception by glittering appearance; Metaphorical (Majāz) — the soul's trust in the "safety of nights" as if immune to fate's vicissitudes.
- Root: خطر (kh-t-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To be in peril; a dangerous undertaking where outcome is uncertain; "khaṭar" as grave risk.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The state of exposure to destruction, particularly of the soul's final state (al-ʿāqibah).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — a threatening precipice; Metaphorical — the spiritual peril of theological speculation without divine illumination.
- Root: كدر (k-d-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Turbidity, clouding, and disturbance of clarity; opposite of ṣafāʾ (purity).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Moral and spiritual obscuration of the heart's perception.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — murky water; Metaphorical — the onset of calamity after ease, as in the cited verse.
- Root: كبريت (k-b-r-y-t)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Sulfur; "al-kibrīt al-aḥmar" (red sulfur) — the legendary elixir, unattainable by ordinary means.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Symbol of the rarest and most precious reality — here, the illuminative knowledge (al-mukāshafah) granted to prophets and saints.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Metaphorical usage denoting that which is exceedingly scarce and beyond conventional acquisition.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Restriction and Focused Predication (al-Ḥaṣr wa al-Taqyīd bi-innamā) — "إِنَّمَا يَسْلَمُ" restricts salvation exclusively to the simple faithful or those preoccupied by fear of Hell, excluding the speculative theologians.
9:24.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Fear and Hope'

12:4.arabic: الآثار قال ابن لقمان الحكيم لأبيه يا أبت أي الخصال من الإنسان خير قال الدين قال فإذا كانت اثنتين قال الدين والمال قال فإذا كانت ثلاثا قال الدين والمال والحياء قال فإذا كانت أربعا قال الدين والمال والحياء وحسن الخلق قال فإذا كانت خمسا قال الدين والمال والحياء وحسن الخلق والسخاء قال فإذا كانت ستا قال يا بني إذا اجتمعت فيه الخمس خصال فهو نقي تقي والله ولي ومن الشيطان يري وقال الحسن من ساء خلقه عذب نفسه وقال أنس بن مالك إن العبد ليبلغ بحسن خلقه أعلى درجة في الجنة وهو غير عابد ويبلغ
12:4.english: The Book of Etiquette — and in it [are reports] — and from al-Barāʾ ibn ʿĀzib, who said: "The Messenger of God — peace and blessings be upon him — was the most beautiful of people in face and the best of them in character." (1) And from Abū Masʿūd al-Badrī, who said: "The Messenger of God — peace and blessings be upon him — used to say in his supplication: 'O God, just as You have made beautiful my creation (khalqī), so make beautiful my character (khuluqī).'" (2) And from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar — may God be pleased with them both — who said: "The Messenger of God — peace and blessings be upon him — used to supplicate frequently, saying: 'O God, I ask You for [Page V03P050] soundness, well-being, and good character.'" (3)
12:4.section_title_en: The Book of Etiquette (Kitāb al-Ādāb) — Section 614: On Good Character (Ḥusn al-Khulq)
12:4.anchors:
- Root: خلق (Kh-L-Q)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning is "to measure, proportion, or fashion precisely" — as the leather-worker measures and cuts hide, or the tailor measures cloth before cutting. Also denotes smoothness (ṣakhrah khalqāʾ: a smooth rock) and worn-out garment (thawb khaliq).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الخلق أصله: التقدير المستقيم" — its origin is "straight/right measure." Used for bringing something into being from nothing (ibdāʿ) without prior model, as in {«He created the heavens and the earth»} (al-Anʿām 6:1), and for bringing something forth from another thing, as in {«He created you from a single soul»} (al-Nisāʾ 4:1). When applied to human character (khuluq), it denotes the inward constitution and disposition — the "measure" or "form" of the soul.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): "خلق الخراز الأديم" — the leather-worker measured the hide; "خلق الله الخلق" — God brought creation into being upon a measure necessitated by wisdom. Metaphorical (majāz): "وله خلق حسن" — he has beautiful character, i.e., the inward form of the soul measured upon praiseworthy traits. The term khuluq (character) is a metaphorical extension of khalq (creation/form), referring to the soul's stable constitution just as khalq refers to the body's outward form.
- Root: حسن (Ḥ-S-N)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Beauty, goodness, excellence — both in outward appearance and inward quality.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الحسن: عبارة عن كل مبهج مرغوب فيه" — goodness/beauty is an expression of everything delightful and desirable. It is of three kinds: what is deemed good by the intellect, by desire (hawā), and by the senses. "الحسنة" (a good deed) is everything that brings joy through a blessing reaching a person.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "أنظر إلى محاسن وجهه" — look at the beauties of his face (physical beauty). Metaphorical: "فلان لا يحسن شيئا" — so-and-so does not do anything well (competence); "قيمة المرء ما يحسن" — a man's worth is what he does well. When coupled with khuluq (character), ḥusn al-khuluq denotes the beauty of the soul's inward form — its praiseworthy measure and proportion.
- Root: حدث (Ḥ-D-Th)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Newness, origination, occurrence. "الحديث" — speech that is new/recently originated.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الحدوث: كون الشيء بعد أن لم يكن" — origination is a thing's coming to be after it was not. "المحدث: ما أوجد بعد أن لم يكن" — the originated is what is brought into existence after non-existence. In ḥadīth terminology, it refers to the transmitted sayings of the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) — reports that convey his words and deeds.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "هو حدث من الأحداث" — he is young (recent in age). Metaphorical: "صاروا أحاديث" — they became subjects of talk. In the context of this section, the term "ḥadīth" (pl. aḥādīth) refers to the prophetic traditions being cited as evidence for the virtue of good character.
- Root: قال (Q-W-L)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To say, to speak, to utter. In scholarly context, "qāla" (he said) introduces transmitted statements — whether prophetic, companion, or scholar sayings.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "قال" is the verb of direct speech, used to transmit authoritative statements. In this section, it introduces the chain of transmission for prophetic ḥadīths and the sayings of the Companions and early scholars (āthār).
- Sibawayh Rule: Prepositional Interposition and Apposition (al-ʿAṭf wa al-Badl) — The text employs extensive appositional structures (badl) and coordinated attributions (ʿaṭf bayān) to identify the sources of transmitted reports, e.g., "أخرجه الخرايطي في مكارم الأخلاق بإسناد ضعيف" — the verb "akhrajahu" (he recorded it) governs a chain of transmitters and works, each in apposition to the other, requiring precise tracking of who recorded what from whom.
12:4.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Breaking the Two Desires'

12:90.arabic: فتح الباب والله لا يضيع أجر المحسنين وإن تك حسنة يضاعفها ويؤت من لدنه أجرا عظيما المقام الثاني في دفع العارض منه في أثناء العبادة وذلك لا بد من تعلمه أيضا فإن من جاهد نفسه وقلع مغارس الرياء من قلبه بالقناعة وقطع الطمع وإسقاط نفسه من أعين المخلوقين واستحقار مدح المخلوقين وذمهم فالشيطان لا يتركه في أثناء العبادات بل يعارضه بخطرات الرياء ولا تنقطع عنه نزعاته وهوى النفس وميلها لا ينمحي بالكلية فلا بد وأن يتشمر لدفع ما يعرض من خاطر الرياء وخواطر الرياء ثلاثة قد تخطر دفعة واحدة كالخاطر ال
12:90.english: So when the harm and injury of these causes is firmly settled in his heart, his desire [for them] slackens, and his heart turns toward God. For the intelligent person does not covet that whose harm is abundant and whose benefit is scant. It suffices him that if people knew what is in his inner self—the intent of ostentation (riyā') and the display of sincerity—they would abhor him. And God will surely expose his secret until He makes him odious to the people and makes them know that he is a show-off, abhorrent to God. Had he been sincere to God, God would have unveiled his sincerity to them, made him beloved to them, subjected them to him, and loosened their tongues in praise and commendation of him—even though there is no perfection in their praise, nor deficiency in their blame. As the poet of Banī Tamīm said: "My praise is an adornment, and my blame is a disgrace." The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said to him: "You have lied—that belongs to God, there is no deity but Him." // [Hadith: A poet of Banī Tamīm said, "My praise is an adornment, and my blame is a disgrace." He (the Prophet) said: "You have lied—that belongs to God." Ahmad narrated it from the hadith of al-Aqra' ibn Ḥābis—who was the speaker of that verse, excluding the phrase "You have lied"—and its narrators are trustworthy, except that I do not know of Abū Salamah ibn 'Abd al-Raḥmān having heard [directly] from al-Aqra'. Al-Tirmidhī narrated it from the hadith of al-Barā' and deemed it sound (ḥasan), with the wording: "A man said, 'Indeed, my praise...'"]
12:90.section_title_en: The Revival of the Religious Sciences — Section 827: The Second Station: Repelling the Accidental Promptings of Ostentation During Worship
12:90.anchors:
- Root: كذب (kadhaba)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: falsehood, lying, saying what is contrary to reality; also used for "to declare someone a liar."
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In theological context, kadhb is the antithesis of sidq (truthfulness); it is a moral and epistemic vice, often linked to hypocrisy (nifāq) and false claims.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (haqīqah): to report what did not occur. Metaphorical (majāz): attributing to God what is unworthy of Him, as in the Prophet's rebuke of the poet's self-praise.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Predicate Emphasis (Bāb al-Tawkīd) — The Prophet's reply "كَذَبْتَ" (You have lied) functions as an emphatic categorical refutation, structured as a nominal sentence with implied subject, establishing a permanent verdict rather than a transient rebuke.
12:90.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Condemnation of Status and Ostentation'

12:90.arabic: الصبر والتقوى صيرا العبيد ملوكا فقال يوسف كما أخبر الله تعالى عنه {إنه من يتق ويصبر فإن الله لا يضيع أجر المحسنين} وقال الجنيد أرقت ليلة فقمت إلى وردي فلم أجد الحلاوة التي كنت أجدها فأردت أن أنام فلم أقدر فجلست فلم أطق الجلوس فخرجت فإذا رجل ملتف في عباءة مطروح على الطريق فلما أحس بي قال يا أبا القاسم إلى الساعة فقلت يا سيدي من غير موعد قال بلى سألت الله عز وجل إن يحرك لي قلبك فقلت قد فعل فما حاجتك قال فمتى يصير داء النفس دواءها فقلت إذا خالفت النفس هواها فأقبل على نفسه فقال اسمعي فقد أجبتك بهذا سبع مرات فأبيت أن تسمعيه إلا من الجنيدها قد سمعتيه ث
12:90.english: But if you are incapable of that, then it behooves you not to let slip the affirmation of truth (taṣdīq) and faith (īmān) by way of receptive acceptance (talqqī) and emulation (taqlīd) of one who deserves to be emulated. For faith has a degree, just as knowledge has a degree; and knowledge is attained after faith, and it lies beyond it. God, the Exalted, said: {«يرفع الله الذين آمنوا منكم والذين أوتوا العلم درجات»} — "God will raise those who have believed among you and those who have been given knowledge, by degrees." So whoever affirms as true that opposing the desires (mukhālafat al-shahawāt) is the road to God, the Mighty and Majestic, yet has not been apprised of its cause and its secret — he is among those who believe. And when he is apprised of what we have mentioned concerning the helpers of the desires, he is among those who have been given knowledge. And to both has God promised the goodly reward.
12:90.section_title_en: Section 627 — The Path of Opposition to the Desires: On the Consensus of the Scholars that There Is No Road to the Happiness of the Hereafter Save through Restraining the Soul from Caprice
12:90.anchors:
- Root: نفس (n-f-s)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The self, soul, spirit; that which breathes; the animating principle; also blood, and the "evil eye" (nafs sā'ilah)
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): النفس: الروح — the soul as the spiritual reality; in the verse {«ويحذركم الله نفسه»} it denotes the very Essence (al-dhāt); the soul is that which must be disciplined and opposed in its caprice (hawā)
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the self that desires and inclines; Metaphorical: "دفق نفسه" — he poured out his blood/life; the soul as the internal adversary that must be fought (jihād al-nafs)
- Root: قلب (q-l-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The heart; to turn over, to transform, to fluctuate; the heart as that which is constantly turning between states
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): قلب الشيء: تصريفه وصرفه عن وجه إلى وجه — the heart is so named because of its constant turning and fluctuation between conditions; the seat of spiritual perception and disease
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: to turn something over; Metaphorical: the heart as the organ of spiritual understanding that can be veiled (maḥjūbah) from God by attachment to desires
- Root: دنا (d-n-w)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To be near, proximity; the world (al-dunyā) as that which is nearer/lower
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): الدنو: القرب بالذات أو بالحكم — proximity by essence or by judgment; the world as the nearer realm that veils from the distant (al-ākhirah)
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: closeness; Metaphorical: the lower world as that which is "near" and thus preoccupies the heart from what is higher
- Root: أكل (a-k-l)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To eat, consume; also to possess and enjoy
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Eating as the most fundamental desire; the restriction of food (qillat al-ṭa'ām) as the first pillar of spiritual discipline (riyāḍah)
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: consumption of food; Metaphorical: "أكل الشهوات" — the devouring of desires as that which veils the intellect from God
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The periodic sentence structure in which the author interposes explanatory clauses between the subject and its predicate, as in "فإنه لو تمتع بشيء منه أنس به وألفه" where the conditional clause governs the entire following apodosis, requiring careful tracking of the protasis-apodosis relationship through extended digressions.

13:26.arabic: {ورضوا بالحياة الدنيا واطمأنوا بها} وقال تعالى {وما الحياة الدنيا في الآخرة إلا متاع} وقال تعالى {اعلموا أنما الحياة الدنيا لعب ولهو وزينة وتفاخر بينكم وتكاثر في الأموال والأولاد} الآية وكل ذلك ذم لها فنسأل الله السلامة فأولو الحزم من أرباب القلوب جربوا قلوبهم في حال الفرح بمؤاتاة الدنيا فوجدوها قاسية نفرة بعيدة التأثر عن ذكر الله واليوم الآخر وجربوها في حالة الحزن فوجدوها لينة رقيقة صافية قابلة لأثر الذكر فعلموا أن النجاة في الحزن الدائم والتباعد من أسباب الفرح والبطر ففطموها عن ملاذها وعودوها الصبر عن شهواتها حلالها وحرامها وعل
13:26.english: And beyond it lie afflictions greater than this—namely, that the soul rejoices in comfort within this world, leans toward it, and becomes tranquil in it with insolence (asharan) and pride (baṭaran), until it becomes intoxicated like a drunkard who does not awaken from his intoxication. And that joy in this world is a deadly poison that courses through the veins, expelling from the heart the fear (khawf) of God, sorrow (ḥuzn), the remembrance of death, and the terrors of the Day of Resurrection. This is the death of the heart. God, Exalted is He, said: {وَرَضُوا بِالْحَيَاةِ الدُّنْيَا وَاطْمَأَنُّوا بِهَا} ("And they were pleased with the life of this world and felt secure in it") (Q 10:7). And He, Exalted is He, said: {وَمَا الْحَيَاةُ الدُّنْيَا فِي الْآخِرَةِ إِلَّا مَتَاعٌ} ("And the life of this world, compared to the Hereafter, is but a [passing] enjoyment") (Q 13:26). And He, Exalted is He, said: {اعْلَمُوا أَنَّمَا الْحَيَاةُ الدُّنْيَا لَعِبٌ وَلَهْوٌ وَزِينَةٌ وَتَفَاخُرٌ بَيْنَكُمْ وَتَكَاثُرٌ فِي الْأَمْوَالِ وَالْأَوْلَادِ} ("Know that the life of this world is but amusement and diversion and adornment and boasting among you and competition in increase of wealth and children") (Q 57:20)—to the end of the verse. All of this is censure of it. So we ask God for safety (salāmah).
13:26.section_title_en: On the Afflictions of Permissible Things and the Discipline of the Soul
13:26.anchors:
- Root: س ك ت (s-k-t)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root meaning: silence, stillness, cessation of speech.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: silence (sukūt) as a positive act of worship when it restrains the tongue from falsehood and excess, aligning with the Quranic command to guard one's speech.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal vs Metaphorical: Literal silence (ḥaqīqah) is the absence of audible speech; metaphorical (majāz) silence is the restraint of the heart from vain desires and the tongue from all but the remembrance of God.
- Root: ش ه و (sh-h-w)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root meaning: desire, longing, appetite; the inclination of the soul toward what pleases it.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: shahwah (appetite/desire) is a neutral faculty; its blameworthiness lies in its direction toward the forbidden (ḥarām) or in its excess beyond the measure of necessity (ḍarūrah), which enslaves the heart.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal vs Metaphorical: Literal desire is the physical craving for food, drink, or sensual pleasure; metaphorical desire is the soul's craving for status, comfort, and the fleeting adornments of this world (dunyā), which is the root of spiritual ruin.
- Root: ف ط م (f-ṭ-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root meaning: to wean, to cut off from suckling; to abstain from a habit.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: fiṭām (weaning) is used analogically for the discipline of the soul—cutting it off from worldly pleasures (shahawāt) to accustom it to the remembrance of God, just as a child is weaned from the breast.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal vs Metaphorical: Literal weaning is the physical act of separating an infant from milk; metaphorical weaning is the soul's training (riyāḍah) to abandon the "milk" of worldly comfort for the "food" of spiritual devotion.
- Root: أ ن س ('-n-s)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root meaning: to be sociable, familiar, at ease; to find comfort in company.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: uns (intimacy/familiarity) with God is the highest station of the heart, achieved only after severing intimacy with the world; it is the soul's true home, contrasted with the alienation (waḥshah) of worldly attachment.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal vs Metaphorical: Literal intimacy is human companionship; metaphorical intimacy is the heart's tranquil repose (ṭuma'nīnah) in the remembrance of God, as cited in the Quranic verse {أَلَا بِذِكْرِ اللَّهِ تَطْمَئِنُّ الْقُلُوبُ}.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The rule governing the separation of a preposition from its object for rhetorical emphasis, as in the periodic structure of the author's conditional clauses (e.g., "فمن أراد... فحقه أن يلزمه"), where the protasis is extended to clarify the subject's intent before the apodosis delivers the ruling.
13:26.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Breaking the Two Desires'

16:33.arabic: ومن يعمل مثقال ذرة شرا يره وما ظلمهم الله ولكن كانوا أنفسهم يظلمون بيان تفصيل الطريق إلى تهذيب الأخلاق قد عرفت من قبل أن الاعتدال في الأخلاق هو صحة النفس والميل عن الاعتدال سقم ومرض فيها كما أن الاعتدال في مزاج البدن هو صحة له والميل عن الاعتدال مرض فيه فلنتخذ البدن مثالا فنقول مثال النفس في علاجها بمحو الرذائل والأخلاق الرديئة عنها وجلب الفضائل والأخلاق الجميلة إليها مثال البدن في علاجه بمحو العلل عنه وكسب الصحة له وجلبها إليه وكما أن الغالب على أصل المزاج الاعتدال وإنما تعتري المعدة المضرة بعوارض الأغذية والأهو
16:33.english: For this reason, may God be well pleased with him, said: "Faith indeed appears in the heart as a white spot; whenever faith increases, that whiteness increases, until when the servant perfects faith, the whole heart becomes white. And hypocrisy indeed appears in the heart as a black spot; whenever hypocrisy increases, that blackness increases, until when hypocrisy is perfected, the whole heart becomes black."
16:33.section_title_en: The Gradual Acquisition of Moral Character and the Detailed Exposition of the Path to Refining Ethics
16:33.anchors:
- Root: فقه (Fiqh)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Comprehension and understanding of a matter's inward reality; deep penetration into meaning.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الفقه: هو التوصل إلى علم غائب بعلم شاهد" — Fiqh is attaining knowledge of the unseen through the witnessed; it is more specific than mere knowledge ('ilm), denoting a settled, abiding comprehension.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): "افقه عني ما أقول لك" — grasp what I say to you. The term denotes active, engaged understanding, not passive reception.
- Root: نفس (Nafs)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The self, the soul; that which desires proximity and discourse; the principle of life and animation.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The soul as the seat of both blameworthy and praiseworthy traits; its purification (tazkiyah) is the goal of moral discipline.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal vs. Metaphorical: "نفس" as blood (the life-fluid) versus the immaterial self; here, "فقيه النفس" denotes one whose very soul has become imbued with the habit of deep understanding — a settled disposition, not a transient state.
- Root: قلب (Qalb)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The heart; that which turns and is turned (taqlib), the organ of fluctuating states.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "قلب الشيء: تصريفه وصرفه عن وجه إلى وجه" — the heart is so named for its constant turning and overturning between states; it is the seat of both faith and hypocrisy, whiteness and blackness.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Metaphorical (Majaz): "قلب المعلم الصبيان: صرفهم إلى بيوتهم" — to turn something about, to manage and dispose; the heart is that which is turned by habits until it becomes fixed in one direction.
- Root: جمل (Jaml)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Beauty and comeliness; the sum total of a thing; that which is gathered and collected.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الجمال: الحسن الكثير" — beauty in abundance; both inward (character) and outward (action).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "فلان يعامل الناس بالجميل" — dealing with people beautifully; here, "الأفعال الجميلة" are the beautiful, virtuous actions whose repetition forms character.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد (Restriction & Specification) — The construction "لا طريق له إلا أن" (there is no path for him except that) effects complete restriction (hasr), confining the means of moral transformation to a single, specified avenue: the repetition of acts until they become nature.
16:33.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Breaking the Two Desires'

23:1.arabic: الله تعالى {قد أفلح المؤمنون الذين هم في صلاتهم خاشعون والذين هم عن اللغو معرضون} إلى قوله {أولئك هم الوارثون} وقال عز وجل {التائبون العابدون الحامدون} إلى قوله {وبشر المؤمنين} وقال عز وجل {إنما المؤمنون الذين إذا ذكر الله وجلت قلوبهم} إلى قوله {أولئك هم المؤمنون حقا} وقال تعالى {وعباد الرحمن الذين يمشون على الأرض هونا وإذا خاطبهم الجاهلون قالوا سلاما} إلى آخر السورة من أشكل عليه حاله فليعرض نفسه على هذه الآيات فوجود جميع هذه الصفات علامة حسن الخلق وفقد جميعها علامة سوء الخلق ووجود بعضها دون بعض يدل على البعض دون البعض فليشتغل بتحصيل
23:1.english: The foundational principle in this matter is that each person should abandon that which brings him joy from among the causes of this world. So whoever delights in wealth, or in status, or in acceptance during preaching, or in honor through judgeship and governance, or in the abundance of followers in teaching and benefitting others—he should first abandon that which brings him joy. For if he is prevented from something of that sort, and it is said to him: "Your reward is in the Hereafter," and his reward is not diminished by the prevention, yet he dislikes that and is pained by it—then he is among those who rejoice in the life of this world and are content with it, and that is destructive for him. Then, when he has abandoned the causes of joy, let him withdraw from people, let him seclude himself with his own soul, and let him watch over his heart so that it is occupied with nothing but the remembrance of Allah, the Exalted, and reflection upon Him. And let him lie in wait for whatever desire or whisper (shahwah wa waswās) appears in his soul, so that he may crush its substance whenever it emerges. For every whisper has a cause, and it does not vanish except by severing that cause and attachment. And let him persist in this for the remainder of his life, for striving has no end except death.
23:1.section_title_en: The Revival of the Religious Sciences — Section 630: The Signs of Good Character and the Path of Spiritual Striving
23:1.anchors:
- Root: جهد (j-h-d)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Exertion of one's utmost capacity; enduring hardship in pursuit of a goal.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-jihād is the soul's taking itself to the limit of its capacity while bearing difficulty; it is the means by which the lower self is subdued.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical toil and strain. Metaphorical: the striving of the soul against its passions, as in "ijtahada ra'yahu" (he exerted his judgment).
- Root: حسن (ḥ-s-n)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Beauty, goodness, and excellence in form and conduct.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): That which is desirable and pleasing—whether by reason, inclination, or sense; ḥusn al-khuluq is the beauty of the soul's inward disposition.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical beauty and adornment. Metaphorical: moral excellence, as in "ḥasuna khuluquhu" (his character became good).
- Root: خلق (kh-l-q)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Measuring, fashioning, and forming; also innate disposition and character.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Origination upon a just measure; for character, it denotes the soul's settled form and inward constitution.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: shaping and smoothing. Metaphorical: the created nature and moral temperament of a person.
- Sibawayh Rule: Restriction and Specification (al-ḥaṣr wa al-taqyīd bi-innamā) — The particle "innamā" restricts the predicate to the subject alone, as in the verse {«...»} "Innamā al-muʾminūna..." (The believers are only those...), which confines true faith to those possessing the enumerated attributes.
23:1.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Breaking the Two Desires'

23:1.arabic: قال الله عز وجل قد أفلح المؤمنون الذين هم في صلاتهم خاشعون فمدحهم بعد الإيمان بصلاة مخصوصة وهي المقرونة بالخشوع ثم ختم أوصاف المفلحين بالصلاة أيضا فقال تعالى والذين هم على صلواتهم يحافظون ثم قال تعالى في ثمرة تلك الصفات أولئك هم الوارثون الذين يرثون الفردوس هم فيها خالدون فوصفهم بالفلاح أولا وبوراثة الفردوس آخرا وما عندي أن هذرمة اللسان مع غفلة القلب تنتهي إلى هذا الحد ولذلك قال الله عز وجل في أضدادهم ما سلككم في سقر قالوا لم نك من المصلين فالمصلون هم ورثة الفردوس وهم المشاهدون لنور الله تعالى والمتمتعو
23:1.english: For the friends of God (awliyāʾ Allāh) who are granted unveiling of the dominion of the heavens and the earth (malakūt al-samāwāt wa-al-arḍ) and the secrets of lordship (asrār al-rubūbiyyah) — they are unveiled only in prayer, especially in prostration (sujūd), for the servant draws near to his Lord (Mighty and Majestic) through prostration. For this reason, He said, Most High: {«And prostrate and draw near»} (Q 96:19). And the unveiling of each worshiper is only to the measure of his purity from the turbidities of this world. It varies in strength and weakness, in abundance and scarcity, and in clarity and obscurity — until some are unveiled the very thing itself (al-shayʾ bi-ʿaynihi), while others are unveiled its likeness (al-shayʾ bi-mithālihi), just as some were shown this world in the form of a corpse, and Satan in the form of a dog crouching upon it, calling people to it.
23:1.section_title_en: The Prayer of the Humble and the Unveiling of the Unveiled — Section 140
23:1.anchors:
- Root: خ ش ع (kh-sh-ʿ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of humility, submissiveness, and lowering oneself; the physical posture of one who is abased before a greater power.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In theological terms, khushūʿ is the state of the heart's stillness and trembling before divine majesty, manifesting in the body's composure during ritual prayer (ṣalāh).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) refers to the physical lowering of the gaze and voice; metaphorical (majāz) extends to the soul's inner quietude and awe before God.
- Root: ك ش ف (k-sh-f)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To remove a covering, unveil, disclose; the act of stripping away an obstruction to reveal what lies beneath.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In Quranic usage, kashf denotes divine removal of veils (kashf al-ḥijāb) — the uncovering of unseen realities (ghayb) to the heart, as in {«We have removed from you your covering»} (Q 50:22).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: uncovering a physical object; metaphorical: the disclosure of spiritual truths (mukāshafah) to the purified heart, a technical term in Sufi epistemology.
- Root: ص ل و (ṣ-l-w)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The root denotes supplication, blessing, and the act of ritual prayer; also the burning of fire (iṣlāʾ), suggesting the consuming fervor of devotion.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-ṣalāh is the act of turning toward God in worship, encompassing both the physical rites and the inner orientation of the soul; its perfection lies in the presence of the heart.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the performance of the prescribed ritual; metaphorical: the soul's "burning" with longing and its purification through the fire of sincere devotion.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — The use of restrictive particles to single out the specific quality (khushūʿ) as the defining attribute of the believers' prayer, distinguishing it from mere mechanical performance.
23:1.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Mysteries of Prayer'

38:71.arabic: أمره بإضافته إليه إذ قال تعالى إني خالق بشرا من طين فإذا سويته ونفخت فيه من روحي فقعوا له ساجدين فنبه على أن الجسد منسوب إلى الطين والروح إلى رب العالمين والمراد بالروح والنفس في هذا المقام واحد فالخلق عبارة عن هيئة في النفس راسخة عنها تصدر الأفعال بسهولة ويسر من غير حاجة إلى فكر وروية فإن كانت الهيئة بحيث تصدر عنها الأفعال الجميلة المحمودة عقلا وشرعا سميت تلك الهيئة خلقا حسنا وإن كان الصادر عنها الأفعال القبيحة سميت الهيئة التي هي المصدر خلقا سيئا وإنما قلنا إنها هيئة راسخة لأن من يصدر منه بذل المال على الندور لحاجة عارضة لا يقال خلقه السخاء ما
38:71.english: I say: Know that people have spoken concerning the reality of good character (ḥusn al-khulq) — what it is — yet they have not addressed its true nature; rather, they have addressed its fruits. Then they did not even exhaust all of its fruits, but each one mentioned only those fruits that occurred to him and were present in his mind. They did not direct their attention to mentioning its definition (ḥadd) and its reality (ḥaqīqah) that encompasses all its fruits in detail and with completeness. This is like the saying of al-Ḥasan: "Good character is a cheerful face, the giving of bounty, and the withholding of harm." Al-Wāsiṭī said: "It is that one neither disputes nor is disputed with, by virtue of his intense knowledge of God most high." Shāh al-Kirmānī said: "It is the withholding of harm and the bearing of burdens." Some said: "It is that one be near to people, yet a stranger among them." Al-Wāsiṭī said on another occasion: "It is the pleasing of creation in prosperity and adversity." Abū ʿUthmān said: "It is satisfaction with God most high." Sahl al-Tustarī was asked about good character, and he said: "Its lowest degree is forbearance, the abandonment of retaliation, mercy toward the oppressor, seeking forgiveness for him, and compassion toward him." He said on another occasion: "It is that one does not accuse the Truth concerning provision, but trusts in Him, and reposes in His faithfulness to what He has guaranteed, so that he obeys Him and does not disobey Him in all matters — both in what is between him and his Lord, and in what is between him and people." ʿAlī, may God be pleased with him, said: "Good character consists in three qualities: avoiding forbidden things, seeking what is lawful, and enlarging one's provision upon one's dependents." Al-Ḥusayn ibn Manṣūr said: "It is that the harshness of creation does not affect you after your contemplation of the Truth." Abū Saʿīd al-Kharrāz said: "It is that you have no concern other than God most high." This and the like of it is abundant — and it is an addressing of the fruits of good character, not of its very self. Nor is it even encompassing of all the fruits.
38:71.section_title_en: The Reality of Good Character (Ḥusn al-Khulq) — Its True Nature and the Four Pillars of the Soul
38:71.anchors:
- Root: خلق (Kh-L-Q)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "التقدير المستقيم" — precise measurement and fashioning; the outward form (khalq) and inward disposition (khuluq) as twin designations of the same root.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "إبداع الشيء من غير أصل ولا احتذاء" — origination without precedent; here extended to the soul's innate constitution, which God alone originates and proportions.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Haqiqah: "خلق الخراز الأديم" — the tanner measures the hide before cutting. Majaz: "خلق الله الخلق: أوجده على تقدير أوجبته الحكمة" — God's creation as measured origination. Thus khuluq is the soul's measured inward form, as khalq is the body's measured outward form.
- Root: حسن (Ḥ-S-N)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Beauty and comeliness in both visible and invisible orders.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الحسن: عبارة عن كل مبهج مرغوب فيه" — that which delights and is desired; three kinds: rational, appetitive, sensory. The good character is that which reason and revelation (ʿaqlan wa sharʿan) deem beautiful.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Haqiqah: "أنظر إلى محاسن وجهه" — visible beauties. Majaz: "فلان لا يحسن شيئا" — competence and virtue as moral beauty. The "beautiful" act is the metaphorical extension of visible comeliness to inward excellence.
- Root: نفس (N-F-S)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The self, soul, spirit; that which is valued and precious.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "النفس: الروح" — the soul as spirit; in the verse {«ونفخت فيه من روحي»} the soul is that which is divinely breathed, distinguished from the clay body.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Haqiqah: "شيء نفيس" — precious thing. Majaz: "دفق نفسه أي دمه" — the self as the whole living person. Here, the soul (nafs) perceived by inner vision (baṣīrah) is of greater rank than the body perceived by sight (baṣar).
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — The author's repeated "إنما قلنا" and "ليس الخلق عبارة عن..." employ restrictive predication to delimit the definition of khuluq against rival candidates (act, power, knowledge), each negated in turn before the fourth meaning is affirmed.
38:71.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Breaking the Two Desires'

47:14.arabic: {أفمن زين له سوء عمله فرآه حسنا} فكل ما أحدث بعد الصحابة رضي الله عنهم مما جاوز قدر الضرورة والحاجة فهو من اللعب واللهو وحكي عن إبليس لعنه الله أنه بث جنوده في وقت الصحابة رضي الله عنهم فرجعوا إليه محسورين فقال ما شأنكم قالوا ما رأينا مثل هؤلاء ما نصيب منهم شيئا وقد أتعبونا فقال إنكم لا تقدرون عليهم قد صحبوا نبيهم وشهدوا تنزيل ربهم ولكن سيأتي بعدهم قوم تنالون منهم حاجتكم فلما جاء التابعون بث جنوده فرجعوا إليه منكسين فقالوا ما رأينا أعجب من هؤلاء نصبب منهم الشيء
47:14.english: For this reason ʿAlī, may God be pleased with him, said — when it was said to him, "You have opposed so-and-so" — "The best of us is the most following of us of this religion." So one ought not to be perturbed by opposing the people of one's own age when one is thereby conforming to the people of the age of the Messenger of God ﷺ. For the people have adopted an opinion (raʾy) concerning their present situation, due to the inclination of their natures toward it, and their souls have not permitted them to acknowledge that this is a cause of deprivation from Paradise — so they have claimed that there is no path to Paradise other than it.
47:14.section_title_en: ** Section 64 — On the Sciences of the Inner Life: The Obligation to Follow the Salaf and the Condemnation of Innovation (Bidʿah)
47:14.anchors:
**
- Root: علم (ʿalima)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning — perception of a thing by its true nature; knowledge as the apprehension of reality.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "العلم: إدراك الشيء بحقيقته" — knowledge is the apprehension of a thing in its true reality, divided into apprehension of the essence and judgment upon the thing.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal usage — "ما علمت بخبرك: ما شعرت به" (I did not know of your news: I had no awareness of it). The scholar (ʿālim) is one whose knowledge is manifest in action.
- Root: بدع (badaʿa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning — to originate, to create something new without prior example.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الإبداع: إنشاء صنعة بلا احتذاء واقتداء" — origination of a thing without model or precedent. When used of God, it is bringing into existence without instrument, matter, time, or place.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — "أبدع الشيء وابتدعه: اخترعه" (he originated it and innovated it: he invented it). Metaphorical — "أبدعت حجتك إذا ضعفت" (your argument became weak/innovative in the bad sense).
- Root: حدث (ḥadatha)
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الحدوث: كون الشيء بعد أن لم يكن" — coming-to-be of a thing after it was not. "المحدث: ما أوجد بعد أن لم يكن" — the originated thing.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — "هو حدث من الأحداث" (he is a youth among youths). Metaphorical — "صاروا أحاديث" (they became [mere] tales). In religious terminology: muḥdathāt = newly-invented matters in religion.
- Root: هدى (hadā)
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Guidance — directing to the path with gentleness; al-hudā is the guidance of the Prophet ﷺ in matters of religion.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "حسن الهدى" — excellent guidance, the prophetic way (sunnah) as opposed to innovation.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — "إنما هما اثنتان: الكلام والهدى" restricts the two matters exclusively to speech and guidance, excluding all else.

49:3.arabic: تعالى أولئك الذين امتحن الله قلوبهم للتقوى قيل نزع منها محبة الشهوات وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم المؤمن بين خمس شدائد مؤمن يحسده ومنافق يبغضه وكافر يقاتله وشيطان يضله ونفس تنازعه (1) فبين أن النفس عدو منازع يجب عليه مجاهدتها ويروى أن الله تعالى أوحى إلى داود عليه السلام يا داود حذر وأنذر أصحابك أكل الشهوات فإن القلوب المتعلقة بشهوات الدنيا عقولها عني محجوبة وقال عيسى عليه السلام طوبى لمن ترك شهوة حاضرة لموعود غائب لم يره وقال نبينا صلى الله عليه وسلم لقوم قدموا من الجهاد مرحبا بكم
49:3.english: But if you are incapable of that, then it behooves you not to let slip the affirmation of truth (taṣdīq) and faith (īmān) by way of receptive acceptance (talqqī) and emulation (taqlīd) of one who deserves to be emulated. For faith has a degree, just as knowledge has a degree; and knowledge is attained after faith, and it lies beyond it. God, the Exalted, said: {«يرفع الله الذين آمنوا منكم والذين أوتوا العلم درجات»} — "God will raise those who have believed among you and those who have been given knowledge, by degrees." So whoever affirms as true that opposing the desires (mukhālafat al-shahawāt) is the road to God, the Mighty and Majestic, yet has not been apprised of its cause and its secret — he is among those who believe. And when he is apprised of what we have mentioned concerning the helpers of the desires, he is among those who have been given knowledge. And to both has God promised the goodly reward.
49:3.section_title_en: Section 627 — The Path of Opposition to the Desires: On the Consensus of the Scholars that There Is No Road to the Happiness of the Hereafter Save through Restraining the Soul from Caprice
49:3.anchors:
- Root: نفس (n-f-s)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The self, soul, spirit; that which breathes; the animating principle; also blood, and the "evil eye" (nafs sā'ilah)
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): النفس: الروح — the soul as the spiritual reality; in the verse {«ويحذركم الله نفسه»} it denotes the very Essence (al-dhāt); the soul is that which must be disciplined and opposed in its caprice (hawā)
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the self that desires and inclines; Metaphorical: "دفق نفسه" — he poured out his blood/life; the soul as the internal adversary that must be fought (jihād al-nafs)
- Root: قلب (q-l-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The heart; to turn over, to transform, to fluctuate; the heart as that which is constantly turning between states
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): قلب الشيء: تصريفه وصرفه عن وجه إلى وجه — the heart is so named because of its constant turning and fluctuation between conditions; the seat of spiritual perception and disease
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: to turn something over; Metaphorical: the heart as the organ of spiritual understanding that can be veiled (maḥjūbah) from God by attachment to desires
- Root: دنا (d-n-w)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To be near, proximity; the world (al-dunyā) as that which is nearer/lower
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): الدنو: القرب بالذات أو بالحكم — proximity by essence or by judgment; the world as the nearer realm that veils from the distant (al-ākhirah)
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: closeness; Metaphorical: the lower world as that which is "near" and thus preoccupies the heart from what is higher
- Root: أكل (a-k-l)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To eat, consume; also to possess and enjoy
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Eating as the most fundamental desire; the restriction of food (qillat al-ṭa'ām) as the first pillar of spiritual discipline (riyāḍah)
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: consumption of food; Metaphorical: "أكل الشهوات" — the devouring of desires as that which veils the intellect from God
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The periodic sentence structure in which the author interposes explanatory clauses between the subject and its predicate, as in "فإنه لو تمتع بشيء منه أنس به وألفه" where the conditional clause governs the entire following apodosis, requiring careful tracking of the protasis-apodosis relationship through extended digressions.
