68:4.arabic: وهو الذي مدح الله سبحانه به نبيه عليه السلام إذ قال {وإنك لعلى خلق عظيم} وقال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أكثر ما يدخل الناس الجنة تقوى الله وحسن الخلق (1) وقال أسامة بن شريك قلنا يا رسول الله ما خير ما أعطى الإنسان فقال خلق حسن (2) وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم بعثت لأتمم محاسن الأخلاق (3) وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم أثقل ما يوضع في الميزان خلق حسن (4) وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم ما حسن الله خلق امريء وخلقه فيطعمه النار (5) وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم يا أبا هريرة عليك بحسن الخلق قال أبو هريرة رضي الله عنه وما حسن الخلق يا رسو
68:4.english: Know that affability (al-ulfah) is the fruit of excellent character (ḥusn al-khuluq), and estrangement (al-tafarruq) is the fruit of evil character. For excellent character necessitates mutual love, harmony, and concord, whereas evil character yields mutual hatred, envy, and turning away (al-tadābur). And whenever the source is praiseworthy, the fruit is likewise praiseworthy. The excellence of good character is not hidden in the religion; indeed, it is that with which God—glorified be He—praised His Prophet, peace be upon him, when He said: {وَإِنَّكَ لَعَلَىٰ خُلُقٍ عَظِيمٍ} «And indeed, you are upon an immense character» (Al-Qalam: 4). The Prophet, peace be upon him, said: "The thing which most causes people to enter Paradise is God-consciousness (taqwā) and excellent character." (1) Usāmah ibn Sharīk said: "We said, O Messenger of God, what is the best thing given to a person?" He said: "Excellent character." (2) He, peace be upon him, also said: "I was sent only to perfect the noble traits of character." (3) He, peace be upon him, said: "Nothing is heavier in the Balance than excellent character." (4) He, peace be upon him, said: "God does not beautify a person's outward form and his inward character, then feed him to the Fire." (5) He, peace be upon him, said: "O Abū Hurayrah, adhere to excellent character." (Page V02P157) Abū Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him, said: "What is excellent character, O Messenger of God?" He said: "That you join the one who cuts you off, forgive the one who wrongs you, and give to the one who deprives you." (1)
68:4.section_title_en: The Book of the Revival of the Religious Sciences — Section 402: On the Excellence of Affability (Al-Ulfah) and Brotherhood in God
68:4.anchors:
- Root: ألف (Alifa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of harmonizing, uniting, and reconciling; the removal of estrangement (al-waḥshah) and the establishment of concord.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance of ta'līf as the divine act of harmonizing hearts, a blessing bestowed by God alone, as in {لَوْ أَنفَقْتَ مَا فِي الْأَرْضِ جَمِيعًا مَّا أَلَّفْتَ بَيْنَ قُلُوبِهِمْ}.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) denotes physical joining; metaphorical (majāz) denotes the spiritual and moral concord of hearts, which is the fruit of excellent character (ḥusn al-khuluq).
- Root: خلق (Khalaqa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Root meaning of measuring, proportioning, and smoothing; hence, the inherent disposition and moral character of a person.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The origination of a thing upon a just measure; for character, it is the inward form (al-ṣūrah al-bāṭinah) of the soul, just as the physical form is its outward shape.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) is the physical creation and proportioning; metaphorical (majāz) is the moral and spiritual constitution, praised by God in {وَإِنَّكَ لَعَلَىٰ خُلُقٍ عَظِيمٍ}.
- Root: بغض (Bughḍ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The opposite of love (ḥubb); intense aversion and hatred.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In the Kalam context, al-bughḍ fī Allāh (hatred for God's sake) is a spiritual act of discernment and loyalty, not a mere emotional impulse; it is paired with al-ḥubb fī Allāh as the strongest bond of faith (awthaq ʿurā al-īmān).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) is personal animosity; metaphorical (majāz) is the righteous aversion to disobedience and the enemies of God, which is a form of devotion.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Prepositional Interposition (Bāb al-Faṣl bayna al-Jār wa al-Majrūr) — Governing the syntactic flow of conditional and relative clauses, ensuring the periodic structure of the author's argument remains coherent and unbroken.
68:4.topic: Al-Ghazali on the journey of the soul, death, and the Hereafter, from 'Breaking the Two Desires'

87:16.arabic: مشاهدة العواقب ولذلك قال تعالى بل تؤثرون الحياة الدنيا والآخرة خير وأبقى وقال عز وجل كلا بل تحبون العاجلة وتذرون الآخرة فمن هذا حده فينبغي أن يعالج قلبه من حب الجاه بالعلم بالآفات العاجلة وهو أن يتفكر في الأخطار التي يستهدف لها أرباب الجاه في الدنيا فإن كل ذي جاه محسود ومقصود بالإيذاء وخائف على الدوام على جاهه ومحترز من أن تتغير منزلته في القلوب والقلوب أشد تغيرا من القدر في غليانها وهي مترددة بين الإقبال والإعراض فكل ما يبنى على قلوب الخلق يضاهي ما يبنى على أمواج البحر فإنه لا ثبات له والاشتغال بمراعاة القلوب وحفظ ال
87:16.english: And it is as though you had never ceased to be in the Hereafter — for these people, their attention was turned to the final outcome, and so their deeds were performed for its sake, through godfearingness (taqwā), since they knew that the final outcome belongs to the godfearing. Thus they held in contempt rank and wealth in this world. But the sight of most creatures is weak, confined to the immediate (al-ʿājilah), whose light does not extend to the witnessing of final outcomes. For this reason, Allah Most High said: {«بل تؤثرون الحياة الدنيا والآخرة خير وأبقى»} ("Nay, you prefer the life of this world, while the Hereafter is better and more enduring") [Al-Aʿlā 87:16–17]. And He, Mighty and Majestic, said: {«كلا بل تحبون العاجلة وتذرون الآخرة»} ("Nay, but you love the immediate and forsake the Hereafter") [Al-Qiyāmah 75:20–21].
87:16.section_title_en: The Cure for Love of Status — Section 804 of The Revival of the Religious Sciences
87:16.anchors:
- Root: جاه (jāh)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الجاه: القدر والمنزلة، وجاه عند الناس: وقع وعظم" — rank, standing, and elevation in the eyes of others.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: jāh is a social accident (ʿaraḍ) attached to the estimations of hearts, not a real attribute of the self; its pursuit is a veiling distraction from the Hereafter.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): "جاه عند السلطان: منزلته ووجهته." Metaphorical (majāz): the "face" (wajh) one presents to people — i.e., honor is but a reflected image in fluctuating hearts, like a building upon waves.
- Root: خطر (khaṭar)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الخطر: الإشراف على الهلاك، والخطر: السبق الذي يراهن عليه" — peril and stakes.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The "danger" (khaṭar) of status is that its possessor becomes a target (gharaḍ) for envy and harm — a Quranic motif of the world's transient allure versus the abiding Hereafter.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "خاطر بنفسه: ألقاها في المهلكة." Metaphorical: the aspirant to jāh "stakes" his own peace as wager in a game he cannot win.
- Root: خمل (khamūl)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الخمول: خفاء الذكر وعدم الشهرة، وخمل الرجل: سقط ولم يُعرف" — obscurity and anonymity.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Obscurity (khamūl) is the therapeutic counterweight to jāh; it severs the heart's attachment to created estimations.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "خمل الثوب: ما خفي من نسجه." Metaphorical: the soul's "hidden weave" — its true worth lies unseen, like the inner thread of cloth.
- Root: قنع (qanāʿah)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "قنع: رضي بالكفاف واكتفى باليسير" — contentment with sufficiency.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Qanāʿah is the root that severs ṭamaʿ (covetous expectation) from creatures, redirecting hope solely to the Creator.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "قنع الصائد: نصب القنوع" (the hunter's blind). Metaphorical: the contented man "blinds" himself to people's opinions, as one hides in a blind to escape prey's notice.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — governing the contrastive structure "إنما يعالج بالعلم... وأما من حيث العمل" where the particle ḥaṣr restricts each cure to its proper domain (knowledge vs. practice), and "فإن" clauses provide causal grounding for periodic sentences.
87:16.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Condemnation of Status and Ostentation'

87:16.arabic: {بل تؤثرون الحياة الدنيا} ثم بين أن الشر قديم في الطباع وأن ذلك مذكور في الكتب السالفة فقال {إن هذا لفي الصحف الأولى صحف إبراهيم وموسى} فهذا منهاج رياضة المريد وتربيته في التدريج إلى لقاء الله تعالى فأما تفصيل الرياضة في كل صفة فسيأتي فإن أغلب الصفات على الإنسان بطنه وفرجه ولسانه أعني به الشهوات المتعلقة بها ثم الغضب الذي هو كالجند لحماية الشهوات ثم مهما أحب الإنسان شهوة البطن والفرج وأنس بهما أحب الدنيا ولم يتمكن منها إلا بالمال والجاه وإذا طلب المال والجاه حدث فيه الكبر
87:16.english: Whoever devotes himself exclusively to remembrance (dhikr) and casts off the distracting attachments from his heart will not be free of such thoughts, for he has embarked upon a ship of peril. If he is saved, he becomes one of the kings of religion; if he errs, he becomes one of the perished. For this reason the Prophet (peace and blessing be upon him) said: "Upon you is the religion of the old women" {«عليكم بدين العجائز»}—that is, receiving the foundation of faith and the outward creed by way of blind acceptance (taqlīd), and occupying oneself with works of goodness. For the peril in deviating from that is great.
87:16.section_title_en: The Way of Spiritual Discipline: On the Perils of the Path and the Training of the Seeker (Section 637)
87:16.anchors:
- Root: طرق (ṭ-r-q)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الطريق: السبيل الذي يطرق بالأرجل" — the path beaten by feet; striking, knocking (as of a door at night).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الطريق: السبيل الذي يطرق بالأرجل... وعنه استعير كل مسلك يسلكه الإنسان في فعل" — every course a man pursues, whether praiseworthy or blameworthy.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: striking iron with a hammer, knocking at a door. Metaphorical: "طرقنا فلان طروقا... وطرقني الخيال" — a visitor coming by night; "أصابته طارقة من الطوارق" — calamities that strike suddenly. Here, the "مهالك الطريق" are the perilous passes of the spiritual path that strike the seeker unawares.
- Root: هلك (h-l-k)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Perishing, destruction, ruin.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الهلاك على ثلاثة أوجه" — three modes: (1) loss of a thing from one's possession while it exists elsewhere {هلك عني سلطانيه}; (2) corruption and dissolution {ويهلك الحرث والنسل}; (3) death {إن امرؤ هلك}. The "هلاك عظيم" here is the third sense compounded with the second—spiritual death through corruption of one's state.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: falling into destruction (المهالك). Metaphorical: "مفازة تهلك فيها الأرواح" — a desert waste wherein souls perish; "تهالك على الشيء" — to be consumed with craving for a thing. The text's warning against "السكون إليهم هلكة" (settling into ease with creation is perdition) employs the metaphorical register of the soul's ruin.
- Root: قلب (q-l-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Turning, overturning, transforming a thing from one state to another.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "قلب الشيء: تصريفه وصرفه عن وجه إلى وجه" — to turn a thing about, to divert it from one aspect to another. The heart (قلب) is so named for its constant turning and fluctuation.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: turning a garment, overturning a vessel. Metaphorical: "رجل قلب حول: يقلب الأمور ويحتال" — a man who turns matters over and devises stratagems. In this text, the heart's turning (تقلب) between states is the very arena of the seeker's trial—whether it settles upon God or is overturned by vain imaginings.
- Root: الي (a-l-h / ألَهَ)
  * Kitab al-Ayn: "المألكة: الرسالة، لأنها تؤلك في الفم" — the message is "chewed" in the mouth, i.e., delivered. The root carries the sense of bearing a message between parties.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الملائكة تقع على الواحد والجمع... الله يصطفي من الملائكة رسلا" — angels as messengers. In this text, the preacher's self-conception as "واسطة بين الله تعالى وبين الخلق" (an intermediary between God and creation) is precisely the angelic office—yet the seeker is warned against mistaking satanic suggestion for genuine prophetic mission.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد (Restriction & Focused Predication) — The repeated conditional constructions "فإن لم يكن... بل يرده" and "لا يمكن ذلك إلا بأن يخلو... ولا يخلو إلا بطول المجاهدة" employ restrictive exception (الاستثناء) to delimit the sole means of achieving the goal, and conditional protasis-apodosis (الشروط) to map the branching perils of the path.
87:16.topic: Al-Ghazali on purifying the character, moral diseases, and spiritual remedies, from 'Breaking the Two Desires'

91:9.arabic: فجورها وتقواها قد أفلح من زكاها وقد خاب من دساها فمهما وقع العبد في ذنب فصار الذنب نقدا والتوبة نسيئة كان هذا من علامات الخذلان قال صلى الله عليه وسلم إن العبد ليعمل بعمل أهل الجنة سبعين سنة حتى يقول الناس إنه من أهلها ولا يبقى بينه وبين الجنة إلا شبر فيسبق عليه الكتاب فيعمل بعمل أهل النار فيدخلها (1) فإذن الخوف من الخاتمة قبل التوبة وكل نفس فهو خاتمة ما قبله إذ يمكن أن يكون الموت متصلا به فليراقب الأنفاس وإلا وقع في المحذور ودامت الحسرات حين لا ينفع التحسر الطبقة الرابعة أن يتوب ويجري مدة على ا
91:9.english: **The First Rank:** That the disobedient one repents and remains steadfast upon repentance until the end of his life, so that he makes up for what he let slip of his affair, and does not prompt himself to return to his sins — except for the slips (zallāt) from which human beings are not free in their habitual ways, so long as one is not at the rank of prophethood. This is steadfastness upon repentance, and its possessor is the one who races forward in good deeds, exchanging his evil deeds for good ones. The name of this repentance is "sincere repentance" (al-tawbah al-naṣūḥ), and the name of this soul is the "tranquil soul" (al-nafs al-muṭma'innah) which returns to its Lord, well-pleased and well-pleasing. These are those to whom the Prophet, peace be upon him, pointed when he said: {«سبق المفردون المستهترون بذكر الله تعالى وضع الذكر عنهم أوزارهم فوردوا القيامة خفافا»} — "The solitary ones have outstripped [all others] — those who are engrossed in the remembrance of God Almighty, for remembrance has lifted their burdens from them, and they arrive at the Resurrection light [of burden]." For in this there is an indication that they were beneath burdens which remembrance lifted from them.
91:9.section_title_en: The Four Ranks of the Repentant — On the Degrees of Tawbah and the States of the Soul
91:9.anchors:
- Root: توب (T-W-B)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Return, turning back; the verbal noun denotes the act of reverting from a state.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "التوب: ترك الذنب على أجمل الوجوه" — abandoning sin in the most beautiful manner; the most complete form of apology, comprising abandonment of the sin due to its ugliness, remorse for what passed, and resolve against return.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): "تاب العبد إلى الله من ذنبه" — the servant's turning to God from his sin. Metaphorical (Majaz): The mutual relation of divine acceptance (تاب الله على عبده) as a response to the servant's turning.
- Root: نفس (N-F-S)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The self, soul, spirit; that which animates and distinguishes.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The soul (النفس) as the locus of divine address and self-reproach; its states (mutma'innah, lawwāmah, ammārah) are graded by its orientation toward God or toward passions.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the self as animate entity. Metaphorical: "دفق نفسه" (his blood/life) — the soul as the seat of life and moral agency.
- Root: ذنب (Dh-N-B)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The tail; that which follows behind.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الذنب في الأصل: الأخذ بذنب الشيء" — sin as the act of seizing the consequence; the trailing fault that follows the agent.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the tail of an animal. Metaphorical: "هو من الأذناب" — one who follows; sin as the trailing mark of the soul's deviation.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — Used to delimit the four ranks precisely, ensuring each category is mutually exclusive and exhaustive in its defining condition.
91:9.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Monitoring and Accounting'

91:9.arabic: وإنما مراد الطاعات وأعمال الجوارح كلها تصفية القلب وتزكيته وجلاؤه {قد أفلح من زكاها} ومراد تزكيته حصول أنوار الإيمان فيه أعني إشراق نور المعرفة وهو المراد بقوله تعالى فمن يرد الله أن يهديه يشرح صدره للإسلام أفمن شرح الله صدره للإسلام فهو على نور من ربه نعم هذا التجلي وهذا الإيمان له ثلاث مراتب المرتبة الأولى إيمان العوام وهو إيمان التقليد المحض والثانية إيمان المتكلمين وهو ممزوج بنوع استدلال ودرجته قريبة من درجة إيمان العوام والثالثة إيمان العارفين وهو المشاهد بنور اليقين ونبين لك هذه المراتب بمثال وهو أن تصديقك بكون زيد مثلا
91:9.english: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: "Were it not that the devils hover about the hearts of the children of Adam, they would look upon the kingdom of the heavens." (1) [Hadith of Ibn ʿUmar: "Where is God?" — "In the hearts of His believing servants." I have not found it in this wording. Al-Ṭabarānī narrated from Abū ʿUtbah al-Khawlānī, raised to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: "God has vessels from among the people of the earth, and the vessels of your Lord are the hearts of His righteous servants." In it is Baqiyyah ibn al-Walīd, who is a mudallis (one who conceals), but he explicitly stated hearing (al-taḥdīth) in it.] (2) [Hadith: God said: "My earth and My heavens do not contain Me, but the heart of My believing servant, the soft and tender one, contains Me." I have found no basis for it. In the hadith of Abū ʿUtbah before it, according to al-Ṭabarānī, after his saying "and the vessels of your Lord are the hearts of His righteous servants": "and the most beloved of them to Him are the softest and most tender of them."]
91:9.anchors:
- Root: قلب (q-l-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To turn, overturn, transform from one state to another; the heart as that which is constantly turning and fluctuating between states
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "قلب الشيء: تصريفه وصرفه عن وجه إلى وجه" — the heart is so named because of its constant turning and transformation; the spiritual heart (qalb) is that subtle divine reality (laṭīfah rabbāniyyah) which is the locus of perception and knowledge
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: turning a thing over; Metaphorical: "قلب المعلم الصبيان" — the teacher turns the boys toward their homes; thus the heart is that which turns toward the spiritual world (malakūt) when purified
- Root: ملك (m-l-k)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Possession, dominion, sovereignty; the kingdom
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): الملك: possession and dominion; الملكوت: the spiritual dominion — the unseen world of divine sovereignty
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): الملك: that which is under one's dominion; الملكوت: intensive form indicating the absolute and perfect dominion of God over all things
- Root: ايم (a-y-m)
  * Al-Raghib (Al-Mufradat): "الأيامى: جمع أيم، وهي المرأة التي لا بعل لها" — one without a spouse; extended metaphorically
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas - Haqiqah/Literal): "الحرب مأيمة ميتمة" — war makes women widows and children orphans

91:9.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Breaking the Two Desires'

91:10.arabic: هو المراد بقوله تعالى قد أفلح من زكاها وإهمالها هو المراد بقوله وقد خاب من دساها ونحن نشير في هذا الكتاب إلى جمل من أمراض القلوب وكيفية القول في معالجتها على الجملة من غير تفصيل لعلاج خصوص الأمراض فإن ذلك يأتي في بقية الكتب من هذا الربع وغرضنا الآن النظر الكلي في تهذيب الأخلاق وتمهيد منهاجها ونحن نذكر ذلك ونجعل علاج البدن مثالا له ليقرب من الأفهام دركه ويتضح ذلك ببيان فضيلة حسن الخلق ثم بيان حقيقة حسن الخلق ثم بيان قبول الأخلاق للتغير بالرياضة ثم بيان السبب الذي به ينال حسن الخلق ثم بيان الطرق التي بها يعرف تفصيل الطرق إلى
91:10.english: To proceed: Good character (al-khuluq al-ḥasan) is the attribute of the Master of the Messengers and the most excellent of the works of the Truthful Ones (al-ṣiddīqīn). It is, in truth, half of religion and the fruit of the striving (mujāhadah) of the God-fearing and the discipline (riyāḍah) of the devout worshippers. Evil character traits are the deadly poisons, the destructive ruinous things, the disgraceful shames, the manifest vices, and the foul impurities that distance one from the proximity of the Lord of the Worlds and that string their possessor into the ranks of the devils. They are the open doors leading to the Fire of God Almighty, the kindled one {«الَّتِي تَطَّلِعُ عَلَى الْأَفْئِدَةِ»} — "which rises over the hearts" — just as beautiful character traits are the open doors from the heart to the bliss of the Gardens and the proximity of the Most Merciful.
91:10.section_title_en: The Book of Training the Soul, Refining Character, and Treating the Maladies of the Heart — Being the Second Book of the Quarter of the Destroyers
91:10.anchors:
- Root: خلق (khalaqa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of measuring, proportioning, and fashioning; also the innate disposition and character (khuluq) that is the form of the soul.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الخلق أصله: التقدير المستقيم" — the original sense is sound estimation/proportioning; used for bringing something into being from nothing (ibdāʿ) and for the inward character that is the soul's stable form.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): "خلق الخراز الأديم" — the leather-worker measures the hide before cutting. Metaphorical (majāz): "خلق الله الخلق: أوجده على تقدير أوجبته الحكمة" — God created creation upon a measure necessitated by wisdom. Thus "khuluq" (character) is the soul's measured, stable form.
- Root: مرض (mariḍa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Sickness, departure from the body's balanced temperament.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "المرض: الخروج عن الاعتدال الخاص بالإنسان" — sickness is departure from the equilibrium specific to the human. Two kinds: bodily sickness, and "عبارة عن الرذائل كالجهل، والجبن، والبخل، والنفاق" — an expression for vices such as ignorance, cowardice, miserliness, and hypocrisy.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: bodily illness. Metaphorical: "مرض في الأمر: ضجع فيه" — to be weak/lax in a matter; and "تمارض" — to feign illness. Thus heart-sickness is the soul's departure from its proper spiritual equilibrium.
- Root: قلب (qalaba)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To turn, overturn, transform from one state to another.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "قلب الشيء: تصريفه وصرفه عن وجه إلى وجه" — turning a thing and diverting it from one face to another. The heart (qalb) is so named for its constant turning and fluctuation between states.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "قلب الشيء قلبا: حوله عن وجهه" — turned it from its face. Metaphorical: "قلب التاجر السلعة" — the merchant examined the merchandise, scrutinizing its conditions. Thus the heart is the seat of moral scrutiny and transformation.
- Root: حسن (ḥasuna)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Beauty, goodness, excellence.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الحسن: عبارة عن كل مبهج مرغوب فيه" — goodness is an expression for everything delightful and desirable. Three kinds: good by reason, good by desire (passion), good by sense.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "أنظر إلى محاسن وجهه" — behold the beauties of his face. Metaphorical: "فلان لا يحسن شيئا" — so-and-so does not do anything well; "وقيمة المرء ما يحسن" — a man's value is what he does well. Thus ḥusn al-khuluq (good character) is the soul's excellence in its measured form.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The rule governing the permissibility of interposing elements between a governing word and its governed prepositional phrase, as in "كقبح رب فيها رجل" — demonstrating that what may be separated in eloquent speech follows the pattern of what is grammatically sound and rhetorically effective.

104:7.arabic: وهي الأبواب المفتوحة إلى نار الله تعالى الموقدة التي تطلع على الأفئدة كما أن الأخلاق الجميلة هي الأبواب المفتوحة من القلب إلى نعيم الجنان وجوار الرحمن والأخلاق الخبيثة أمراض القلوب وأسقام النفوس إلا أنه مرض يفوت حياة الأبد وأين منه المرض الذي لا يفوت إلا حياة الجسد ومهما اشتدت عناية الأطباء بضبط قوانين العلاج للأبدان وليس في مرضها إلا فوت الحياة الفانية فالعناية بضبط قوانين العلاج لأمراض القلوب وفي مرضها فوت حياة باقية أولى وهذا النوع من الطب واجب تعلمه على كل ذي لب إذ لا يخلو قلب من القلوب عن أسقام لو أهملت

2:57.arabic: وقال تعالى في وصف الطيبات وأنزلنا عليكم المن والسلوى المن العسل والسلوى اللحم سمي سلوى لأنه يتسلى به عن جميع الإدام ولا يقوم غيره مقامه ولذلك قال صلى الله عليه وسلم سيد الإدام اللحم ثم قال بعد ذكر المن والسلوى كلوا من طيبات ما رزقناكم فاللحم والحلاوة من الطيبات قال أبو سليمان الداراني رضي الله عنه أكل الطيبات يورث الرضا عن الله وتتم هذه الطيبات بشرب الماء البارد وصب الماء الفاتر على اليد عند الغسل قال المأمون شرب الماء بثلج يخلص الشكر وقال بعض الأدباء إذا دعوت إخوانك فأطعمتهم حصرم
2:57.english: The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Do not burden your guest so that you make him hate you, for whoever hates his guest has hated Allah, and whoever hates Allah, Allah hates him."
2:57.section_title_en: The Etiquettes of Hospitality: Invitation, Response, Attendance, and the Serving of Food — Section 290 of The Revival of the Religious Sciences
2:57.anchors:
- Root: ضيف (ḍ-y-f)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning is "to incline, to lean toward." The guest (al-ḍayf) is one who inclines toward you, alighting as a visitor; the root carries the sense of leaning or bending.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The guest is "one who inclines to you, alighting with you"; hospitality (al-ḍiyāfah) became customary in the sense of receiving such a one. The word is originally a verbal noun, hence one and many are equal in most usage.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): "ḍāfa ilayhi: he inclined toward him"; "ḍāfat al-shams: the sun inclined toward setting." Metaphorical (majāz): "aḍāfa ilayhi amran: he attributed a matter to him, leaning it upon him"; "al-muḍāf: the one constrained, hemmed in, in distress."
- Sibawayh Rule: Restriction and Focused Predication (al-ḥaṣr wa al-taqyīd bi-innamā) — governing the Prophet's statement "innamā hādhihi al-akhlāq bi-yad Allāh" (these morals are only in the hand of Allah), where innamā restricts the attribution of moral character exclusively to divine bestowal.
2:57.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Manners of Eating'

2:57.arabic: ولذلك قال صلى الله عليه وسلم سيد الإدام اللحم ثم قال بعد ذكر المن والسلوى كلوا من طيبات ما رزقناكم فاللحم والحلاوة من الطيبات قال أبو سليمان الداراني رضي الله عنه أكل الطيبات يورث الرضا عن الله وتتم هذه الطيبات بشرب الماء البارد وصب الماء الفاتر على اليد عند الغسل قال المأمون شرب الماء بثلج يخلص الشكر وقال بعض الأدباء إذا دعوت إخوانك فأطعمتهم حصرمية وبورانية وسقيتهم ماء باردا فقد أكملت الضيافة وأنفق بعضهم دراهم في ضيافة فقال بعض الحكماء لم نكن نحتاج إلى هذا إذا كان خبزك جيدا وماؤك باردا وخلك حامضا فهو كفاية وقال بعضهم الحلاوة ب

2:172.arabic: وقد قال الله تعالى يا أيها الذين آمنوا أنفقوا من طيبات ما كسبتم ومما أخرجنا لكم من الأرض ولا تيمموا الخبيث منه تنفقون ولستم بآخذيه إلا أن تغمضوا فيه أي لا تأخذوه إلا مع كراهية وحياء وهو معنى الإغماض فلا تؤثروا به ربكم وفي الخبر سبق درهم مائة ألف درهم (3) وذلك بأن يخرجه الإنسان وهو من أحل ماله وأجوده فيصدر ذلك عن الرضا والفرح بالبذل وقد يخرج مائة ألف درهم مما يكره من ماله فيدل ذلك على أنه ليس يؤثر الله عز وجل بشيء مما يحبه وبذلك ذم الله تعالى قوما جعلوا لله ما يكرهون فقال تعال
2:172.english: The heart is not treated save with the compound electuary (maʿjūn) of knowledge and works. And this condition among the conditions of almsgiving runs in the same course as humility (al-khushūʿ) runs in the prayer. This is established by his saying — may Allah bless him and grant him peace: "A man has nothing of his prayer save that of which he was conscious." And this is like his saying — may Allah bless him and grant him peace: "Allah does not accept the charity of the one who bestows it with reproach (al-mannān)." And like His saying — Exalted is He: {«لا تبطلوا صدقاتكم بالمن والأذى»} ("Do not nullify your charities by reproach and injury"). As for the legal opinion (fatwā) of the jurist that the alms fall in their proper place and that one's liability is discharged without this condition — that is another discussion, and we have already pointed to its meaning in the Book of Prayer.
2:172.section_title_en: The Inner Conditions of Charity — Section 175 (From The Revival of the Religious Sciences, Book of the Mysteries of Almsgiving)
2:172.anchors:
- Root: قلب (q-l-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "To turn, overturn, transform a thing from one state to another; to rotate, to flip"
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "قلب الشيء: تصريفه وصرفه عن وجه إلى وجه" — the heart is so named because of its constant turning and transformation between states
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "قلب الشيء قلبا: حوله عن وجهه" (to turn a thing from its face). Metaphorical: "رجل قلب حول: يقلب الأمور ويحتال" — one who turns matters over and manages them; "قلبوا لك الأمور" (they turned matters against you)
- Root: وجل (w-j-l)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "Fear, dread, apprehension that strikes the heart"
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الوجل: استشعار الخوف" — the sensing of fear; cited in {«إنما المؤمنون الذين إذا ذكر الله وجلت قلوبهم»}
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "رجل وجل، وقوم وجال" — a fearful man, a fearful people; "وفي قلبه وجل" — in his heart is dread
- Root: عجب (ʿ-j-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "Wonder, amazement; self-admiration, vanity"
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Self-admiration (al-ʿujb) is a destructive spiritual ailment that nullifies deeds
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: wonder at something extraordinary. Metaphorical: self-conceit regarding one's own acts of obedience
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد (Restriction & Focused Predication) — governing the precise limitation of general categories (al-ṣifāt al-khāṣṣah within al-aṣnāf al-thamāniyyah) and the conditional structure of acceptance

2:172.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Duties of Brotherhood'

2:172.arabic: أطعمه فيرى الطعام نعمة منه قال الله تعالى كلوا من طيبات ما رزقناكم واشكروا لله ومهما أكل حلالا قال الحمد لله الذي بنعمته تتم الصالحات وتنزل البركات اللهم أطعمنا طيبا واستعملنا صالحا وإن أكل شبهة فليقل الحمد لله على كل حال اللهم لا تجعله قوة لنا على معصيتك ويقرأ بعد الطعام قل هو الله أحد ولإيلاف قريش ولا يقوم عن المائدة حتى ترفع أولا فإن أكل طعام الغير فليدع له وليقل اللهم أكثر خيره وبارك له فيما رزقته ويسر له أن يفعل فيه خيرا وقنعه بما أعطيته واجعلنا وإياه من الشاكرين وإن أفطر عند قوم فليقل أفطر عندكم الصائمون وأكل
2:172.english: It is that one should refrain from eating before complete satiety, and lick his fingers, then wipe them with a napkin, then wash them, and pick up the crumbs of food that have fallen. The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Whoever eats what falls from the table will live in abundance and his offspring will be protected." (5)
2:172.section_title_en: The Third Division: What is Recommended After Eating
2:172.anchors:
- Root: اكل (akl)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning is the act of eating/consuming food; also used for the action of fire upon wood, and metaphorically for devouring.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Distinguishes الأكل (eating) as the intake of nourishment; the theological nuance extends to the spiritual consequence of what is consumed — lawful (halal) versus unlawful (haram) food affecting the soul's disposition.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah) refers to physical ingestion; Metaphorical (Majaz) extends to "devouring" wealth or property unjustly. Here, the literal sense governs the etiquettes of eating, while the metaphorical sense underlies the warning against consuming what is unlawful.
- Root: لهم (lahm)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Root relates to swallowing/ingesting; also the flesh (lahm) of the body.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The root for إلهام (inspiration) is distinct, but the physical flesh (لحم) is the corporeal substance nourished by food. The Prophetic warning "every flesh that grows from the unlawful" connects the physical body to its spiritual source.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: flesh as bodily substance. Metaphorical: the moral state of the body as a direct consequence of its nourishment.
- Root: حمد (hamd)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Praise, commendation; the act of extolling virtues.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Praise (حمد) is the acknowledgment of beneficence with reverence; it is the verbal expression of gratitude for divine provision, distinct from mere thanks (شكر) which can be by action.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: to praise God for His favors. Metaphorical: "I praised his conduct" — extending to approving of an act. Here, the literal sense of praising God after eating is the prescribed liturgical response.
- Root: برك (barak)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The chest of a camel; to kneel down; blessing (بركة) as a derived concept of divine goodness descending.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Blessing (بركة) is the increase of good from God; it is invoked upon food, upon a person, or upon an action.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "God blessed him" — to confer goodness. Metaphorical: "War laid its chest upon them" — to press down heavily. In the supplications, the literal sense of invoking divine blessing upon food and the provider is intended.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The rule governing the placement of prepositional phrases and the flow of supplications, ensuring the syntactic structure of the du'a remains coherent and grammatically sound.
2:172.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications, prayers, and their spiritual power, from 'Manners of Eating'

2:172.arabic: وقال إن الله تعالى أمر المؤمنين بما أمر به المرسلين فقال {يا أيها الذين آمنوا كلوا من طيبات ما رزقناكم} (4) أخرجه مسلم من حديث أبي هريرة (5) حديث كان لا يسأل عن كل ما يحمل إليه رواه أحمد من حديث جابر أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وأصحابه مروا بامرأة فذبحت لهم شاة الحديث فأخذ رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لقمة فلم يستطع أن يسيغها فقال هذه شاة ذبحت بغير إذن أهلهاالحديث وله من حديث أبي هريرة كان إذا أتى بطعام من غير أهله سأل عنهالحديث وإسنادهما جيد وفي هذا أنه كان لا يسأل عما أتي به من عند أهله والله أعلم // وإنما الواجب أن ينظر التاجر إلى من يعامله
2:172.english: The fifth [etiquette] is that he should not be intensely eager for the marketplace and trade — that is, he should not be the first to enter nor the last to leave, nor should he voyage by sea for trade, for both of these are disliked (makrūh). It is said: "Whoever voyages by sea has been excessive in seeking provision."
2:172.section_title_en: The Book of Earning and Livelihood — Section 334: On the Etiquettes of the Trader (Continued)
2:172.anchors:
- Root: حرص (ḥaraṣa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: [Core linguistic root meaning] — Intense, covetous desire; eager clinging to something.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): [Theological/Kalam semantic nuance] — Blameworthy eagerness that distracts the heart from God; opposed to qanāʿah (contentment).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): [Literal vs Metaphorical distinction] — Literal: physical greed for provision. Metaphorical: the soul's excessive attachment to worldly gain.
- Root: شبه (shub'hah)
  * Lisan / Ayn: [Core linguistic root meaning] — Ambiguity; resemblance between truth and falsehood.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): [Theological/Kalam semantic nuance] — Matters whose legal status is uncertain; the pious abstain from them to safeguard their religion.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): [Literal vs Metaphorical distinction] — Literal: visual resemblance. Metaphorical: doubtful matters that resemble the permissible but are tainted with the forbidden.
- Root: عون (ʿawn)
  * Lisan / Ayn: [Core linguistic root meaning] — Assistance; aid in carrying a burden.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): [Theological/Kalam semantic nuance] — Complicity in sin; assisting the oppressor is itself an act of oppression.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): [Literal vs Metaphorical distinction] — Literal: physical help. Metaphorical: any act that enables or emboldens wrongdoing.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — The text uses restrictive constructions to emphasize that the trader's obligation is limited to dealing with the just, and that the pious are fewer in number than those to be avoided.
2:172.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'Etiquette of Earning'

4:29.arabic: لأمر الحرام وتعظيما لبركة الحلال فقال تعالى يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا تأكلوا أموالكم بينكم بالباطل إلى قوله ولا تقتلوا أنفسكم الآية فالأصل في الطعام كونه طيبا وهو من الفرائض وأصول الدين الثاني غسل اليد قال صلى الله عليه وسلم الوضوء قبل الطعام ينفي الفقر وبعده ينفي اللمم (1) وفي رواية ينفي الفقر قبل الطعام وبعده ولأن اليد لا تخلو عن لوث في تعاطي الأعمال فغسلها أقرب إلى النظافة والنزاهة ولأن الأكل لقصد الاستعانة على الدين عبادة فهو جدير بأن يقدم عليه ما يجري منه مجرى الطهارة من الصلاة الثالث أن يوضع الطعام على السفرة الموضوعة على الأرض فهو
4:29.english: The first [etiquette] is that the food, after being lawful in itself, should be pure (tayyib) with respect to the manner of its acquisition, conforming to the Sunnah and to scrupulous piety (al-waraʿ), not having been earned through anything disapproved in the Sacred Law, nor through the dictates of caprice and dissimulation in religion, as will be detailed concerning the meaning of absolute purity in the Book of the Lawful and the Unlawful. God—may He be exalted—has commanded the eating of what is pure, which is the lawful, and He placed the prohibition of consuming wealth unjustly before the prohibition of killing, as a magnification of the matter of the unlawful and an ennoblement of the blessing of the lawful. For He—may He be exalted—said: {«Yā ayyuhā alladhīna āmanū lā ta'kulū amwālakum baynakum bil-bāṭil»} ("O you who believe, do not consume your wealth among yourselves unjustly") up to His saying: {«wa lā taqtulū anfusakum»} ("and do not kill yourselves") — the verse. Thus the foundational principle concerning food is that it be pure, and this is among the obligatory duties and foundational principles of religion.
4:29.section_title_en: Section 282 — On the Etiquette Preceding Eating, Being the First Division of the Etiquettes of Eating
4:29.anchors:
- Root: اكل (akl)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning is the taking of nourishment; Al-Farahidi notes its extension to consumption generally.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الأكل: تناول المطعم" — eating is the taking of food; used metaphorically for fire consuming wood, and in the Quranic sense of consuming wealth unlawfully.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah) refers to physical ingestion; metaphorical (Majaz) extends to consuming property unjustly, as in the Quranic prohibition.
- Root: طيب (tayyib)
  * Lisan / Ayn: That which is pure, good, lawful, and pleasant.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theologically denotes what is lawful (halal) and pure, as opposed to what is defiled or prohibited.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Distinguishes literal purity from the legal-moral sense of lawfulness.
- Root: بدع (bada'a)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To originate something new without prior example.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الإبداع: إنشاء صنعة بلا احتذاء واقتداء" — innovation is the creation of something without imitating a prior model; when applied to God, it is creation ex nihilo.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal sense is inventing; metaphorical sense includes weakening in argument or failing expectations. In religious law, innovation (bid'ah) is only blameworthy when it contradicts an established Sunnah.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد (Restriction and Specification) — The phrase "ليس كل ما أبدع منهيا" employs negation of universal quantification to distinguish between types of innovation, requiring careful parsing of the exception clause.
4:29.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Manners of Eating'

4:29.arabic: وقد قال الله تعالى يا أيها الذين آمنوا أنفقوا من طيبات ما كسبتم ومما أخرجنا لكم من الأرض ولا تيمموا الخبيث منه تنفقون ولستم بآخذيه إلا أن تغمضوا فيه أي لا تأخذوه إلا مع كراهية وحياء وهو معنى الإغماض فلا تؤثروا به ربكم وفي الخبر سبق درهم مائة ألف درهم (3) وذلك بأن يخرجه الإنسان وهو من أحل ماله وأجوده فيصدر ذلك عن الرضا والفرح بالبذل وقد يخرج مائة ألف درهم مما يكره من ماله فيدل ذلك على أنه ليس يؤثر الله عز وجل بشيء مما يحبه وبذلك ذم الله تعالى قوما جعلوا لله ما يكرهون فقال تعال
4:29.english: The heart is not treated save with the compound electuary (maʿjūn) of knowledge and works. And this condition among the conditions of almsgiving runs in the same course as humility (al-khushūʿ) runs in the prayer. This is established by his saying — may Allah bless him and grant him peace: "A man has nothing of his prayer save that of which he was conscious." And this is like his saying — may Allah bless him and grant him peace: "Allah does not accept the charity of the one who bestows it with reproach (al-mannān)." And like His saying — Exalted is He: {«لا تبطلوا صدقاتكم بالمن والأذى»} ("Do not nullify your charities by reproach and injury"). As for the legal opinion (fatwā) of the jurist that the alms fall in their proper place and that one's liability is discharged without this condition — that is another discussion, and we have already pointed to its meaning in the Book of Prayer.
4:29.section_title_en: The Inner Conditions of Charity — Section 175 (From The Revival of the Religious Sciences, Book of the Mysteries of Almsgiving)
4:29.anchors:
- Root: قلب (q-l-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "To turn, overturn, transform a thing from one state to another; to rotate, to flip"
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "قلب الشيء: تصريفه وصرفه عن وجه إلى وجه" — the heart is so named because of its constant turning and transformation between states
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "قلب الشيء قلبا: حوله عن وجهه" (to turn a thing from its face). Metaphorical: "رجل قلب حول: يقلب الأمور ويحتال" — one who turns matters over and manages them; "قلبوا لك الأمور" (they turned matters against you)
- Root: وجل (w-j-l)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "Fear, dread, apprehension that strikes the heart"
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الوجل: استشعار الخوف" — the sensing of fear; cited in {«إنما المؤمنون الذين إذا ذكر الله وجلت قلوبهم»}
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "رجل وجل، وقوم وجال" — a fearful man, a fearful people; "وفي قلبه وجل" — in his heart is dread
- Root: عجب (ʿ-j-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "Wonder, amazement; self-admiration, vanity"
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Self-admiration (al-ʿujb) is a destructive spiritual ailment that nullifies deeds
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: wonder at something extraordinary. Metaphorical: self-conceit regarding one's own acts of obedience
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد (Restriction & Focused Predication) — governing the precise limitation of general categories (al-ṣifāt al-khāṣṣah within al-aṣnāf al-thamāniyyah) and the conditional structure of acceptance

7:160.arabic: ولذلك قال صلى الله عليه وسلم سيد الإدام اللحم ثم قال بعد ذكر المن والسلوى كلوا من طيبات ما رزقناكم فاللحم والحلاوة من الطيبات قال أبو سليمان الداراني رضي الله عنه أكل الطيبات يورث الرضا عن الله وتتم هذه الطيبات بشرب الماء البارد وصب الماء الفاتر على اليد عند الغسل قال المأمون شرب الماء بثلج يخلص الشكر وقال بعض الأدباء إذا دعوت إخوانك فأطعمتهم حصرمية وبورانية وسقيتهم ماء باردا فقد أكملت الضيافة وأنفق بعضهم دراهم في ضيافة فقال بعض الحكماء لم نكن نحتاج إلى هذا إذا كان خبزك جيدا وماؤك باردا وخلك حامضا فهو كفاية وقال بعضهم الحلاوة ب
7:160.english: The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Do not burden your guest so that you make him hate you, for whoever hates his guest has hated Allah, and whoever hates Allah, Allah hates him."
7:160.section_title_en: The Etiquettes of Hospitality: Invitation, Response, Attendance, and the Serving of Food — Section 290 of The Revival of the Religious Sciences
7:160.anchors:
- Root: ضيف (ḍ-y-f)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning is "to incline, to lean toward." The guest (al-ḍayf) is one who inclines toward you, alighting as a visitor; the root carries the sense of leaning or bending.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The guest is "one who inclines to you, alighting with you"; hospitality (al-ḍiyāfah) became customary in the sense of receiving such a one. The word is originally a verbal noun, hence one and many are equal in most usage.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): "ḍāfa ilayhi: he inclined toward him"; "ḍāfat al-shams: the sun inclined toward setting." Metaphorical (majāz): "aḍāfa ilayhi amran: he attributed a matter to him, leaning it upon him"; "al-muḍāf: the one constrained, hemmed in, in distress."
- Sibawayh Rule: Restriction and Focused Predication (al-ḥaṣr wa al-taqyīd bi-innamā) — governing the Prophet's statement "innamā hādhihi al-akhlāq bi-yad Allāh" (these morals are only in the hand of Allah), where innamā restricts the attribution of moral character exclusively to divine bestowal.
7:160.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Manners of Eating'

11:69.arabic: أتاك حديث ضيف إبراهيم المكرمين} أنهم أكرموا بتعجيل الطعام إليهم دل عليه قوله تعالى {فما لبث أن جاء بعجل حنيذ} وقوله {فراغ إلى أهله فجاء بعجل سمين} والروغان الذهاب بسرعة وقيل في خفية وقيل جاء بفخذ من لحم وإنما سمي عجلا لأنه عجله ولم يلبث قال حاتم الأصم العجلة من الشيطان إلا في خمسة فإنها من سنة رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إطعام الضيف وتجهيز الميت وتزويج البكر وقضاء الدين والتوبة من الذنب (2) ويستحب التعجيل في الوليمة قيل الوليمة في أول يوم سنة وفي الثاني معروف وفي الثالث رياء الثاني ترتيب الأطعمة بتقديم الفاكهة أولا إن كانت فذلك أوفق في ا
11:69.english: The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Do not burden your guest so that you make him hate you, for whoever hates his guest has hated Allah, and whoever hates Allah, Allah hates him."
11:69.section_title_en: The Etiquettes of Hospitality: Invitation, Response, Attendance, and the Serving of Food — Section 290 of The Revival of the Religious Sciences

23:51.arabic: الأكل من الدين وعليه نبه رب العالمين بقوله وهو أصدق القائلين كلوا من الطيبات واعملوا صالحا فمن يقدم على الأكل ليستعين به على العلم والعمل ويقوي به على التقوى فلا ينبغي أن يترك نفسه مهملا سدى يسترسل في الأكل استرسال البهائم في المرعى فإن ما هو ذريعة إلى الدين ووسيلة إليه ينبغي أن تظهر أنوار الدين عليه وإنما أنوار الدين آدابه وسننه التي يزم العبد بزمامها ويلجم المتقي بلجامها حتى يتزن بميزان الشرع شهوة الطعام في إقدامها وإحجامها فيصير بسببها مدفعة للوزر ومجلبة للأجر وإن كان فيها أوفى حظ للنفس قال صلى الله عليه وسلم إن الرجل ليؤجر حتى في ا
23:51.english: To proceed: The aspiration of those possessed of intellects (ulū al-albāb) is the meeting with Allah, the Exalted, in the Abode of Recompense. And there is no path to reaching the meeting with Allah except through knowledge (ʿilm) and action (ʿamal). Nor is perseverance upon both of them possible except through the soundness of the body; nor is the soundness of the body unclouded except through foods and provisions, partaking of them according to the measure of need, repeated over the succession of times. It is from this aspect that some of the righteous predecessors (al-salaf al-ṣāliḥīn) said: "Eating is part of the religion." Upon this the Lord of the Worlds alerted us by His saying — and He is the most truthful of speakers: {«كلوا من الطيبات واعملوا صالحا»} (Eat of the wholesome things and work righteousness) {«المؤمنون/51»}. So whoever undertakes eating in order to seek aid thereby upon knowledge and action, and to strengthen himself thereby upon godfearingness (taqwā), then he ought not to leave his soul neglected and aimless, letting himself loose in eating as cattle loose themselves in the pasture. For that which is a means to the religion and a pathway unto it — it is fitting that the lights of the religion shine upon it.
23:51.section_title_en: The Book of the Etiquettes of Eating — The First Book of the Quarter of Customs from The Revival of the Religious Sciences
23:51.anchors:
- Root: اكل (akl)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root meaning of eating, consuming, and taking nourishment; the act of ingesting food.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الأكل: تناول المطعم" — eating is the taking of nourishment; used metaphorically for fire consuming wood, and for the daily sustenance (rizq) provided by Allah.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (haqiqah) refers to physical ingestion; metaphorical (majaz) extends to consuming wealth, property, or even the effects of time upon objects.
- Root: دين (din)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of debt, obligation, and recompense; the structured way of obedience owed to Allah.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "دنت الرجل: أخذت منه دينا" — the root carries the sense of indebtedness and reciprocal obligation, framing religion as the binding covenant of servitude.
- Root: ربع (rubʿ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of four, a quarter, and a dwelling place.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "أربعة، وأربعون، وربع، ورباع كلها من أصل واحد" — all derived from one origin; the quarter (rubʿ) as a structural division.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "ربع بالمكان: أقام به" — to dwell in a place; metaphorical: "اللهم اربعني من دين علي أي انعشني" — to raise up, to revive, as the quarter of the book revives the religion.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — governing the exclusive framing of purpose statements, as in "إنما أنوار الدين آدابه" (the lights of religion are only its etiquettes).
23:51.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Manners of Eating'

27:23.arabic: سيدنا ومولانا يا كافي من كل شيء ولا يكفى منه شيء أطعمت من جوع وآمنت من خوف فلك الحمد آويت من يتم وهديت من ضلالة وأغنيت من عيلة فلك الحمد حمدا كثيرا دائما طيبا نافعا مباركا فيه كما أنت أهله ومستحقه اللهم أطعمتنا طيبا فاستعملنا صالحا واجعله عونا لنا عن طاعتك ونعوذ بك أن نستعين به على معصيتك وأما غسل اليدين بالأشنان فكيفيته أن يجعل الأشنان في كفه اليسرى ويغسل الأصابع الثلاث من اليد اليمنى أولا ويضرب أصابعه على الأشنان اليابس فيمسح به شفتيه ثم ينعم غسل الفم بإصبعه ويدلك ظاهر أسنان
27:23.english: It is that one should refrain from eating before complete satiety, and lick his fingers, then wipe them with a napkin, then wash them, and pick up the crumbs of food that have fallen. The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Whoever eats what falls from the table will live in abundance and his offspring will be protected." (5)
27:23.section_title_en: The Third Division: What is Recommended After Eating
27:23.anchors:
- Root: اكل (akl)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning is the act of eating/consuming food; also used for the action of fire upon wood, and metaphorically for devouring.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Distinguishes الأكل (eating) as the intake of nourishment; the theological nuance extends to the spiritual consequence of what is consumed — lawful (halal) versus unlawful (haram) food affecting the soul's disposition.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah) refers to physical ingestion; Metaphorical (Majaz) extends to "devouring" wealth or property unjustly. Here, the literal sense governs the etiquettes of eating, while the metaphorical sense underlies the warning against consuming what is unlawful.
- Root: لهم (lahm)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Root relates to swallowing/ingesting; also the flesh (lahm) of the body.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The root for إلهام (inspiration) is distinct, but the physical flesh (لحم) is the corporeal substance nourished by food. The Prophetic warning "every flesh that grows from the unlawful" connects the physical body to its spiritual source.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: flesh as bodily substance. Metaphorical: the moral state of the body as a direct consequence of its nourishment.
- Root: حمد (hamd)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Praise, commendation; the act of extolling virtues.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Praise (حمد) is the acknowledgment of beneficence with reverence; it is the verbal expression of gratitude for divine provision, distinct from mere thanks (شكر) which can be by action.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: to praise God for His favors. Metaphorical: "I praised his conduct" — extending to approving of an act. Here, the literal sense of praising God after eating is the prescribed liturgical response.
- Root: برك (barak)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The chest of a camel; to kneel down; blessing (بركة) as a derived concept of divine goodness descending.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Blessing (بركة) is the increase of good from God; it is invoked upon food, upon a person, or upon an action.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "God blessed him" — to confer goodness. Metaphorical: "War laid its chest upon them" — to press down heavily. In the supplications, the literal sense of invoking divine blessing upon food and the provider is intended.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The rule governing the placement of prepositional phrases and the flow of supplications, ensuring the syntactic structure of the du'a remains coherent and grammatically sound.
27:23.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications, prayers, and their spiritual power, from 'Manners of Eating'

33:53.arabic: وقد قال الله تعالى يا أيها الذين آمنوا أنفقوا من طيبات ما كسبتم ومما أخرجنا لكم من الأرض ولا تيمموا الخبيث منه تنفقون ولستم بآخذيه إلا أن تغمضوا فيه أي لا تأخذوه إلا مع كراهية وحياء وهو معنى الإغماض فلا تؤثروا به ربكم وفي الخبر سبق درهم مائة ألف درهم (3) وذلك بأن يخرجه الإنسان وهو من أحل ماله وأجوده فيصدر ذلك عن الرضا والفرح بالبذل وقد يخرج مائة ألف درهم مما يكره من ماله فيدل ذلك على أنه ليس يؤثر الله عز وجل بشيء مما يحبه وبذلك ذم الله تعالى قوما جعلوا لله ما يكرهون فقال تعال
33:53.english: The heart is not treated save with the compound electuary (maʿjūn) of knowledge and works. And this condition among the conditions of almsgiving runs in the same course as humility (al-khushūʿ) runs in the prayer. This is established by his saying — may Allah bless him and grant him peace: "A man has nothing of his prayer save that of which he was conscious." And this is like his saying — may Allah bless him and grant him peace: "Allah does not accept the charity of the one who bestows it with reproach (al-mannān)." And like His saying — Exalted is He: {«لا تبطلوا صدقاتكم بالمن والأذى»} ("Do not nullify your charities by reproach and injury"). As for the legal opinion (fatwā) of the jurist that the alms fall in their proper place and that one's liability is discharged without this condition — that is another discussion, and we have already pointed to its meaning in the Book of Prayer.
33:53.section_title_en: The Inner Conditions of Charity — Section 175 (From The Revival of the Religious Sciences, Book of the Mysteries of Almsgiving)
33:53.anchors:
- Root: قلب (q-l-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "To turn, overturn, transform a thing from one state to another; to rotate, to flip"
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "قلب الشيء: تصريفه وصرفه عن وجه إلى وجه" — the heart is so named because of its constant turning and transformation between states
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "قلب الشيء قلبا: حوله عن وجهه" (to turn a thing from its face). Metaphorical: "رجل قلب حول: يقلب الأمور ويحتال" — one who turns matters over and manages them; "قلبوا لك الأمور" (they turned matters against you)
- Root: وجل (w-j-l)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "Fear, dread, apprehension that strikes the heart"
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الوجل: استشعار الخوف" — the sensing of fear; cited in {«إنما المؤمنون الذين إذا ذكر الله وجلت قلوبهم»}
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "رجل وجل، وقوم وجال" — a fearful man, a fearful people; "وفي قلبه وجل" — in his heart is dread
- Root: عجب (ʿ-j-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "Wonder, amazement; self-admiration, vanity"
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Self-admiration (al-ʿujb) is a destructive spiritual ailment that nullifies deeds
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: wonder at something extraordinary. Metaphorical: self-conceit regarding one's own acts of obedience
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد (Restriction & Focused Predication) — governing the precise limitation of general categories (al-ṣifāt al-khāṣṣah within al-aṣnāf al-thamāniyyah) and the conditional structure of acceptance

33:53.arabic: وقت الأكل فإن ذلك من المفاجأة وقد نهي عنه قال الله تعالى {لا تدخلوا بيوت النبي إلا أن يؤذن لكم إلى طعام غير ناظرين إناه} يعني منتظرين حينه ونضجه وفي الخبر من مشى إلى طعام لم يدع إليه مشى فاسقا وأكل حراما (10) ولكن حق الداخل إذا لم يتربص وأتفق أن صادفهم على طعام أن لا يأكل ما لم يؤذن له فإذا قيل له كل نظر فإن علم أنهم يقولونه على محبة لمساعدته فليساعد وإن كانوا يقولونه حياء منه فلا ينبغي أن يأكل بل ينبغي أن يتعلل أما إذا كان جائعا فقصد بعض إخوانه ليطعمه ولم يتربص به وقت أكله فلا بأس به قصد رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وأبو بكر وعمر رضي الله عنه
33:53.english: Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad (may God be pleased with him and his father) said: "When you sit with your brothers at the table, prolong the sitting — for that hour is not reckoned against you from your lifespans."
33:53.section_title_en: On Presenting Food to Brothers — Its Excellence and Etiquettes
33:53.anchors:
- Root: ق-د-م (q-d-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "To present, offer, bring forward; to advance. Taqdīm (تقديم) is the act of setting something before another, whether physically or in rank."
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Al-Qudum (القدوم) is arrival; taqdīm is causing something to arrive before another. In the context of hospitality, it signifies the voluntary offering of provision (rizq) to a guest as an act of drawing near (taqarrub) to God."
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "Literal (haqīqah): placing food before a person. Metaphorical (majāz): preferring or advancing someone in honor — as in 'qaddamahu' meaning he honored him."
- Root: أ-ك-ل (a-k-l)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "To eat, to consume. Al-Akl (الأكل) is the taking of nourishment. Al-Aklah (الأكلة) is a single morsel or bite."
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Al-Akl: partaking of food. By way of metaphor, it is said 'the fire ate the wood.' The root carries the sense of receiving what sustains — and in the Hereafter, the reckoning (hisāb) is lifted from what one eats with brothers, for it partakes of the character of worship."
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "Literal: consuming food. Metaphorical: 'he ate my wealth' meaning he spent it among people. Here, the eating with brothers is elevated beyond mere consumption to an act of spiritual communion."
- Root: ك-ل-ف (k-l-f)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "Takalluf (تكلف) is burdening oneself with what is beyond one's capacity or custom — affectation, straining to exceed the ordinary."
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Al-Kulfah (الكلفة) is the hardship one undertakes. Takalluf is assuming a burden unnecessarily — and in hospitality, it is condemned because it introduces pretense (riyā') and disrupts the naturalness of brotherly love."
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "Literal: imposing upon oneself. Metaphorical: the affectation that severs the bonds of friendship, for when a man strains for his guest, the guest feels the weight and ceases to return."
- Root: ض-ي-ف (d-y-f)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "Al-Dayf (الضيف) is the guest; the root conveys inclination and leaning toward — the guest leans upon the host's generosity."
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Iḍāfah (الإضافة) is inclining toward another for refuge. The guest (dayf) is so named because he inclines toward the host's table. True hospitality (diyāfah) is rendering honor without ostentation."
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "Literal: the one who arrives seeking shelter. Metaphorical: the soul's inclination toward what is offered — and the host's soul should incline toward the guest with sincerity, not show."
- Sibawayh Rule: Bāb al-Ḥaṣr wa-l-Taqyīd bi-Innamā (Restriction & Focused Predication) — The conditional and restrictive constructions in the ḥadīth reports (e.g., "lā yuḥāsabu al-ʿabdu ʿalā mā ya'kulu maʿa ikhwānihi") employ the negative restriction to single out the act of brotherly eating from the general reckoning, requiring the translator to preserve the exclusivity of the predicate.

36:82.arabic: الرابع أن لا يحوج رفيقه إلى أن يقول له كل قال بعض الأدباء أحسن الآكلين أكلا من لا يحوج صاحبه إلى أن يتفقده في الأكل وحمل عن أخيه مؤنة القول ولا ينبغي أن يدع شيئا مما يشتهيه لأجل نظر الغير إليه فإن ذلك تصنع بل يجري على المعتاد ولا ينقص من عادته شيئا في الوحدة ولكن يعود نفسه حسن الأدب في الوحدة حتى لا يحتاج إلى التصنع عند الاجتماع نعم لو قلل من أكله إيثارا لإخوانه ونظرا لهم عند الحاجة إلى ذلك فهو حسن وإن زاد في الأكل على نية المساعدة وتحريك نشاط القوم في الأكل فلا بأس به بل هو حسن وكا
36:82.english: If his companion eats little, he should energize him, make eating desirable to him, and say to him: "Eat!" — but he should not exceed three repetitions of the word "Eat!", for that is importunity (ilḥāḥ) and excess. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, when addressed concerning a matter three times, did not return to it after the third. {«كان إذا خوطب في شيء ثلاثا لم يراجع بعد ثلاث»} — narrated by Aḥmad from the ḥadīth of Jābir in a long report, and also from the ḥadīth of Abū Ḥadrad; their chains are sound. {«كان يكرر الكلمة ثلاثا»} — narrated by al-Bukhārī from the ḥadīth of Anas: "He would repeat the word three times." Thus, exceeding this is not of the etiquette (al-adab).
36:82.section_title_en: The Revival of the Religious Sciences — Section 286: On the Etiquette of Eating in Company
36:82.anchors:
- Root: أكل (akl)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning is "to eat, to consume food"; Al-Farahidi notes the verbal noun for the act of eating, distinct from the morsel (uklah) and the meal (aklah).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الأكل: تناول المطعم" — eating is the taking of nourishment; metaphorically extended to fire consuming wood. In company, the act carries social and ethical weight, not mere physical intake.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah) usage denotes physical consumption; metaphorical (Majaz) usage appears in phrases like "فلان أكل غنمي" (he consumed my sheep) meaning he fed others at my expense — relevant to the prohibition on taking more than one's share.
- Root: حدث (ḥadath)
  * Lisan / Ayn: New occurrence, event, or speech; Al-Farahidi links it to bringing forth something new.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الحدوث: كون الشيء بعد أن لم يكن" — origination after non-existence; for speech, it denotes fresh, edifying discourse.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: recent events or sayings; Metaphorical: "صاروا أحاديث" (they became topics of talk). Here, "يتحدثون" (they converse) is literal — engaging in wholesome narrative.
- Root: حسن (ḥusn)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Beauty, goodness, excellence in form and conduct.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الحسن: عبارة عن كل مبهج مرغوب فيه" — that which pleases and is desired, whether by intellect, inclination, or sense. In etiquette, it is the morally and rationally commendable.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical beauty; Metaphorical: "فلان لا يحسن شيئا" (he does not do anything well) — skill and propriety in action, as in "حسن الأدب" (good manners).
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد (Restriction & Specification) — The conditional structures (إن كان، إذا كان) and prohibitions (لا يبتدئ، لا يسكتوا) function as restrictive predicates, delimiting permissible conduct from blameworthy action with precise syntactic boundaries.

42:21.arabic: ولكن حق الداخل إذا لم يتربص وأتفق أن صادفهم على طعام أن لا يأكل ما لم يؤذن له فإذا قيل له كل نظر فإن علم أنهم يقولونه على محبة لمساعدته فليساعد وإن كانوا يقولونه حياء منه فلا ينبغي أن يأكل بل ينبغي أن يتعلل أما إذا كان جائعا فقصد بعض إخوانه ليطعمه ولم يتربص به وقت أكله فلا بأس به قصد رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وأبو بكر وعمر رضي الله عنهما منزل أبي الهيثم بن التيهان وأبي أيوب الأنصاري لأجل طعام يأكلونه وكانوا جياعا (1) والدخول على مثل هذه الحالة إعانة لذلك المسلم على حيازة ثواب الإطعام وهي عادة الس
42:21.english: Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad (may God be pleased with him and his father) said: "When you sit with your brothers at the table, prolong the sitting — for that hour is not reckoned against you from your lifespans."

51:24.arabic: أو ينكسر قلبه بذلك فلا بأس في التأخير وأحد المعنيين في قوله تعالى {هل أتاك حديث ضيف إبراهيم المكرمين} أنهم أكرموا بتعجيل الطعام إليهم دل عليه قوله تعالى {فما لبث أن جاء بعجل حنيذ} وقوله {فراغ إلى أهله فجاء بعجل سمين} والروغان الذهاب بسرعة وقيل في خفية وقيل جاء بفخذ من لحم وإنما سمي عجلا لأنه عجله ولم يلبث قال حاتم الأصم العجلة من الشيطان إلا في خمسة فإنها من سنة رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إطعام الضيف وتجهيز الميت وتزويج البكر وقضاء الدين والتوبة من الذنب (2) ويستحب التعجيل في الوليمة قيل الوليمة في أول يوم سنة وفي الثاني معروف وفي
51:24.english: The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Do not burden your guest so that you make him hate you, for whoever hates his guest has hated Allah, and whoever hates Allah, Allah hates him."
51:24.section_title_en: The Etiquettes of Hospitality: Invitation, Response, Attendance, and the Serving of Food — Section 290 of The Revival of the Religious Sciences
51:24.anchors:
- Root: ضيف (ḍ-y-f)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning is "to incline, to lean toward." The guest (al-ḍayf) is one who inclines toward you, alighting as a visitor; the root carries the sense of leaning or bending.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The guest is "one who inclines to you, alighting with you"; hospitality (al-ḍiyāfah) became customary in the sense of receiving such a one. The word is originally a verbal noun, hence one and many are equal in most usage.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): "ḍāfa ilayhi: he inclined toward him"; "ḍāfat al-shams: the sun inclined toward setting." Metaphorical (majāz): "aḍāfa ilayhi amran: he attributed a matter to him, leaning it upon him"; "al-muḍāf: the one constrained, hemmed in, in distress."
- Sibawayh Rule: Restriction and Focused Predication (al-ḥaṣr wa al-taqyīd bi-innamā) — governing the Prophet's statement "innamā hādhihi al-akhlāq bi-yad Allāh" (these morals are only in the hand of Allah), where innamā restricts the attribution of moral character exclusively to divine bestowal.
51:24.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'Manners of Eating'

51:26.arabic: قوله تعالى {فما لبث أن جاء بعجل حنيذ} وقوله {فراغ إلى أهله فجاء بعجل سمين} والروغان الذهاب بسرعة وقيل في خفية وقيل جاء بفخذ من لحم وإنما سمي عجلا لأنه عجله ولم يلبث قال حاتم الأصم العجلة من الشيطان إلا في خمسة فإنها من سنة رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إطعام الضيف وتجهيز الميت وتزويج البكر وقضاء الدين والتوبة من الذنب (2) ويستحب التعجيل في الوليمة قيل الوليمة في أول يوم سنة وفي الثاني معروف وفي الثالث رياء الثاني ترتيب الأطعمة بتقديم الفاكهة أولا إن كانت فذلك أوفق في الطب فإنها أسرع استحالة فينبغي أن تقع
51:26.english: The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Do not burden your guest so that you make him hate you, for whoever hates his guest has hated Allah, and whoever hates Allah, Allah hates him."

56:21.arabic: وفي القرآن تنبيه على تقديم الفاكهة في قوله تعالى وفاكهة مما يتخيرون {ثم قال} ولحم طير مما يشتهون ثم أفضل ما يقدم بعد الفاكهة اللحم والثريد فقد قال صلى الله عليه وسلم فضل عائشة على النساء كفضل الثريد على سائر الطعام فإن جمع إليه حلاوة بعده فقد جمع الطيبات ودل على حصول الإكرام باللحم قوله تعالى في ضيف إبراهيم إذ أحضر العجل الحنيذ أي المحنوذ وهو الذي أجيد نضجه وهو أحد معنى الإكرام أعني تقديم اللحم وقال تعالى في وصف الطيبات وأنزلنا عليكم المن والسلوى المن العسل والسلوى اللحم سمي سلوى لأنه يتسلى به عن جميع الإدام ولا يقوم غيره مق
56:21.english: The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Do not burden your guest so that you make him hate you, for whoever hates his guest has hated Allah, and whoever hates Allah, Allah hates him."
