  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning is "to incline, to lean toward." The guest (al-ḍayf) is one who inclines toward you, alighting as a visitor; the root carries the sense of leaning or bending.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The guest is "one who inclines to you, alighting with you"; hospitality (al-ḍiyāfah) became customary in the sense of receiving such a one. The word is originally a verbal noun, hence one and many are equal in most usage.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): "ḍāfa ilayhi: he inclined toward him"; "ḍāfat al-shams: the sun inclined toward setting." Metaphorical (majāz): "aḍāfa ilayhi amran: he attributed a matter to him, leaning it upon him"; "al-muḍāf: the one constrained, hemmed in, in distress."
- Sibawayh Rule: Restriction and Focused Predication (al-ḥaṣr wa al-taqyīd bi-innamā) — governing the Prophet's statement "innamā hādhihi al-akhlāq bi-yad Allāh" (these morals are only in the hand of Allah), where innamā restricts the attribution of moral character exclusively to divine bestowal.
56:21.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'Manners of Eating'

75:33.arabic: وفي معناه قول العرب تغد تمد تعش تمش يعني تمدد كما قال الله تعال ثم ذهب إلى أهله يتمطى أي يتمطط ويقال إن حبس البول يفسد الجسد كما يفسد النهر ما حوله إذا سد مجراه الرابع في الخبر قطع العروق مسقمة وترك العشاء مهرمة (2) والعرب تقول ترك الغداء يذهب بشحم الكاذة يعني الآلية وقال بعض الحكماء لابنه يا بني لا تخرج من منزلك حتى تأخذ حلمك أي تتغذى إذ به يبقى الحلم ويزول الطيش وهو أيضا أقل لشهوته لما يرى في السوق وقال حكيم لسمين أرى عليك قطيفة من نسج أضراسك فمم هي قال من أكل لباب البر وصغار المعز وأدهن بجام بنفسج وألبس الكتان الخامس الحمية تضر
75:33.english: **The First [Matter]:** It is related of Ibrāhīm al-Nakhaʿī that he said: "Eating in the marketplace is baseness." He attributed this to the Messenger of God (peace be upon him), and its chain of transmission is sound and close. Yet the opposite has been transmitted from Ibn ʿUmar (may God be pleased with them both), who said: "We used to eat during the era of the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) while walking, and we would drink while standing." And some of the well-known shaykhs of the Sufis was seen eating in the marketplace, and it was said to him regarding that. He replied: "Woe to you! I become hungry in the marketplace, so shall I eat in the house?" It was said: "Then do you enter the mosque?" He said: "I am too ashamed to enter His house merely to eat therein."
75:33.section_title_en: On the Etiquette of Eating: The First Discourse on the Manners of Nourishment
75:33.anchors:
- Root: اكل (akl)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning is the physical act of consuming food; also used for the action of fire upon fuel, and for usury (ribā) in juridical metaphor.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Distinguishes al-akl (the act of eating) from al-ukl (that which is eaten, sustenance). The term carries a metaphorical extension to any form of consumption or acquisition.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (haqīqah) for mastication and swallowing; metaphorical (majāz) for consuming wealth unjustly, for the action of fire, and for the "eating" of one's reputation through slander.
- Root: رسل (rasl)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To send forth gently, to dispatch with ease; a messenger (rasūl) is one sent with a message.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The root implies gentle, measured dispatch; from it derives the concept of the divine message and the angelic emissary.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal for sending a person or animal; metaphorical for the sending of divine chastisement or the "messengers of death" (arrows).
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد (Restriction & Specification) — Governing how general statements about eating are restricted by the specific circumstances of the person, place, and intention, as exemplified in the first point's reconciliation of contradictory reports.
75:33.topic: Al-Ghazali on purifying the character, moral diseases, and spiritual remedies, from 'Manners of Eating'

2:125.arabic: الثاني تهييج الشوق بالمفارقة لتنبعث داعية العودة فإن الله تعالى جعل البيت مثابة للناس وأمنا أي يثوبون ويعودون إليه مرة بعد أخرى ولا يقضون منه وطرا وقال بعضهم تكون في بلد وقلبك مشتاق إلى مكة متعلق بهذا البيت خير لك من أن تكون فيه وأنت متبرم بالمقام وقلبك في بلد آخر وقال بعض السلف كم من رجل بخراسان هو أقرب إلى هذا البيت ممن يطوف به ويقال إن لله تعالى عبادا تطوف بهم الكعبة تقربا إلى الله عز وجل الثالث الخوف من ركوب الخطايا والذنوب بها فإن ذلك مخطر وبالحري أن يورث مقت الله عز وجل لشرف الموضع وروي عن وهيب بن الورد المكي قال كنت ذات ليلة
2:125.english: The first is the fear of becoming weary and familiar with the House, for that might perhaps effect a calming of the heart's burning in veneration. Thus it was that 'Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) used to strike the pilgrims when they performed the Hajj and say: "O people of Yemen, to your Yemen! O people of Syria, to your Syria! O people of Iraq, to your Iraq!" For this reason, 'Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) resolved to prevent people from excessive circumambulation and said: "I fear that the people may become familiar with this House."
2:125.section_title_en: The Virtue of Residing in Mecca (May Allah Protect It) and the Disapproval of Doing So
2:125.anchors:
- Root: خوف (kh-w-f)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of apprehension and dread of a feared outcome
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الخوف: توقع مكروه عن أمارة مظنونة، أو معلومة" — the expectation of something disliked based on a probable or known indication
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): fear of a tangible threat; Metaphorical (Majaz): "تخوفه: تنقصه" — to diminish gradually, as in "تخوف السير منها" (the journey wore it down little by little)
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — governing the permissible separation between a preposition and its object for rhetorical emphasis

- Root: بيت (b-y-t)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The place of overnight dwelling; the Ka'bah as the sacred house
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "أصل البيت: مأوى الإنسان بالليل" — the origin is man's shelter by night; then applied to any dwelling, with "البيوت" more specific to residences
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the physical structure of the Ka'bah; Metaphorical: the heart's attachment and longing toward it
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Contextual Specification — the term "البيت" (the House) in sacred context refers specifically to the Ka'bah by customary designation
2:125.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Mysteries of Hajj'

2:196.arabic: ولزمه دم شاة فإن لم يجد فصيام ثلاثة أيام في الحج قبل يوم النحر متفرقة أو متتابعة وسبعة إذا رجع إلى الوطن وإن لم يصم الثلاثة حتى رجع إلى الوطن صام العشرة تتابعا أو متفرقا وبدل دم القران والتمتع سواء والأفضل الإفراد ثم التمتع ثم القرن وأما محظورات الحج والعمرة فستة الأول اللبس للقميص والسراويل والخف والعمامة بل ينبغي أن يلبس إزارا ورداء ونعلين فإن لم يجد نعلين فمكعبين فإن لم يجد إزارا فسراويل ولا بأس بالمنطقة والاستظلال في المحمل ولكن لا ينبغي أن يغطي رأسه فإن إحرامه في الرأس وللمرأة أن تلبس كل مخيط بعد
2:196.english: **The Second: Qirān (Combined Pilgrimage)** — which is that one combines, saying: "Here I am, O God, for a Pilgrimage and an ʿUmrah together," thus becoming in a state of iḥrām for both. The rites of the Pilgrimage suffice him, and the ʿUmrah is subsumed under the Pilgrimage, just as the ablution (wuḍūʾ) is subsumed under the full bath (ghusl). However, if he circumambulates and runs before the standing at ʿArafāt, his running is counted for both rites, but his circumambulation is not counted, because the condition of the obligatory circumambulation in the Pilgrimage is that it occur after the standing. Upon the one performing Qirān is due a sheep's blood, unless he is a Meccan, in which case nothing is due upon him, because he has not abandoned his mīqāt, since his mīqāt is Mecca.
2:196.section_title_en: The Book of Pilgrimage — Section 198: The Pillars, Obligations, and Modes of Hajj and ʿUmrah, and the Commencement of the Journey's Visible Rites
2:196.anchors:
- Root: ح ج ج (Ḥ-J-J)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The intent (qaṣd) toward a venerated object; the annual pilgrimage to the Sacred House.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The religiously legislated intent to visit the Sacred House to perform the rites.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: repairing repeatedly to a place of veneration. Metaphorical: the pilgrim's repeated approach to God through ritual acts.
- Sibawayh Rule: The conditional clause (al-sharṭ) with its apodosis (jawāb), governing the legal hypotheticals ("if he does X, then Y is due").
2:196.topic: Al-Ghazali on the inner and outer dimensions of worship, from 'Mysteries of Hajj'

2:196.arabic: قاله عمر وعلي وابن مسعود رضي الله عنهم في معنى قوله عز وجل وأتموا الحج والعمرة لله وقال بعض العلماء الركوب أفضل لما فيه من الإنفاق والمؤنة ولأنه أبعد عن ضجر النفس وأقل لأذاه وأقرب إلى سلامته وتمام حجه وهذا عند التحقيق ليس مخالفا للأول بل ينبغي أن يفصل ويقال من سهل عليه المشي فهو أفضل فإن كان يضعف ويؤدي به ذلك إلى سوء الخلق وقصور عن عمل فالركوب له أفضل كما أن الصوم للمسافر أفضل وللمريض ما لم يفض إلى ضعف وسوء خلق وسئل بعض العلماء عن العمرة أيمشي فيها أو يكتري حمارا بدرهم فقال إن كان وزن الدرهم أشد عليه فالكراء أفضل من المشي وإن كان
2:196.english: For at that point, his intention should be the visitation of the House of God, Mighty and Majestic, and the assistance of his Muslim brother by discharging the obligation from him. And it is concerning the like of this that the saying of the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, descends: "God, Glorified be He, will enter three persons into Paradise by means of a single Pilgrimage: the one who bequeathed it, the one who executed it, and the one who performed the Pilgrimage on behalf of his brother."
2:196.section_title_en: The Book of the Revival of the Religious Sciences — Section 213: The Inward Conditions of the Pilgrimage (Continued)
2:196.anchors:
- Root: ن-ف-ق (n-f-q)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of expenditure, spending, and outlay; al-nifāq (hypocrisy) is derived from the same root, as the hypocrite burrows into faith and exits from it — thus expenditure is the outward flow of wealth.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-Nafaqah is the expenditure by which one seeks the means of nearness to God; it is praised when directed toward obedience and blamed when directed toward disobedience.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): spending wealth. Metaphorical (Majaz): spending of the self and effort in the path of God.
- Root: ر-ف-ث (r-f-th)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Al-Rafath: obscene, lewd, and indecent speech; also covers conjugal relations and their preliminaries.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In the Quranic context of pilgrimage, al-rafath is the comprehensive term for all that excites sexual desire and leads to what is forbidden during iḥrām.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: lewdness in speech. Metaphorical: any discourse that stirs the appetite toward the forbidden.
- Root: ج-د-ل (j-d-l)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Al-Jidāl: intense disputation and argumentation; the root denotes the twisting and plaiting of ropes — thus the twisting of truth through contention.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-Jidāl is the disputation that seeks to overcome the opponent; it is blameworthy when it proceeds from obstinacy and produces rancor.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the braiding of strands. Metaphorical: the interweaving of arguments in contentious debate.
- Root: ش-ع-ث (sh-ʿ-th)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Al-Shaʿath: dishevelment, dustiness, and the neglect of personal grooming; the state of one whose hair is disordered and whose appearance is unkempt.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The Prophet's command to appear disheveled and dusty (al-shaʿath wa al-ightibār) in pilgrimage is a mark of humility and the abandonment of worldly adornment.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical dishevelment. Metaphorical: the outward sign of inward humility and the renunciation of pomp.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The separation of the prepositional phrase from its governing verb is permissible when the intervening element is semantically complete, as in the construction "فإن تسليم المال إليهم إعانة على الظلم" where the prepositional phrase "إليهم" is interposed between the verbal noun and its complement for rhetorical emphasis.
2:196.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Mysteries of Hajj'

3:26.arabic: فاصرفني عنه واصرفه عني واقدر لي الخير أينما كان إنك على كل شيء قدير (6) رواه جابر بن عبد الله قال كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يعلمنا الاستخارة في الأمور كلها كما يعلمنا السورة من القرآن وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا هم أحدكم بأمر فليصل ركعتين ثم ليسم الأمر ويدعو بما ذكرناه وقال بعض الحكماء من أعطي أربعا لم يمنع أربعا من أعطي الشكر لم يمنع المزيد ومن أعطي التوبة لم يمنع القبول ومن أعطي الاستخارة لم يمنع الخيرة ومن أعطي المشورة لم يمنع الصواب الثامنة صلاة الحاجة (7) فمن ضاق عليه الأمر ومسته حاجة في صلاح دينه ودن
3:26.english:
**QUAD_ANCHORS:**
- Root: خسف (kha-sa-fa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: [Core linguistic root meaning] To swallow up, to cause to sink into the earth; the darkening of the sun or moon (khusūf for the moon, kusūf for the sun, though both are used interchangeably)
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): [Theological/Kalam semantic nuance] The eclipse as a divine sign (āyah) — not a natural phenomenon merely, but a portent summoning the servant to remembrance of God
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): [Literal vs Metaphorical distinction] Literal: the celestial bodies being veiled/obscured; Metaphorical: the veiling of hearts from divine remembrance
- Root: سقى (sa-qa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: [Core linguistic root meaning] To give to drink, to water; istisqā' — the act of seeking rain/water from God
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): [Theological/Kalam semantic nuance] The prayer for rain as a communal acknowledgment of absolute dependence upon divine providence
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): [Literal vs Metaphorical distinction] Literal: requesting water; Metaphorical: seeking divine mercy and abundance
- Root: جنز (ja-na-za)
  * Lisan / Ayn: [Core linguistic root meaning] The bier/corpse; janāzah — the funeral
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): [Theological/Kalam semantic nuance] The funeral prayer as a collective obligation (farḍ kifāyah) — the living standing as intercessors for the dead
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): [Literal vs Metaphorical distinction] Literal: the bier upon which the dead is carried; Metaphorical: the entire funeral rite as a reminder of one's own mortality
- Root: حيي (ḥa-ya)
  * Lisan / Ayn: [Core linguistic root meaning] To live; taḥiyyah — greeting, salutation; the "greeting of the mosque" (taḥiyyat al-masjid)
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): [Theological/Kalam semantic nuance] The greeting of the mosque as an act of reverence for the sacred space — a spiritual courtesy toward the house of God
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): [Literal vs Metaphorical distinction] Literal: greeting a person; Metaphorical: greeting the mosque through prayer as one greets a host upon entering his abode
- Root: خير (kha-ya-ra)
  * Lisan / Ayn: [Core linguistic root meaning] To choose; istikhārah — seeking divine choice/guidance
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): [Theological/Kalam semantic nuance] The prayer of seeking guidance as the servant's acknowledgment that only God knows the unseen consequences of affairs
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): [Literal vs Metaphorical distinction] Literal: asking someone to choose for you; Metaphorical: delegating one's affairs to divine providence while abandoning personal preference
- Root: ركع (ra-ka-ʿa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: [Core linguistic root meaning] To bow; rukūʿ — the bowing posture in prayer
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): [Theological/Kalam semantic nuance] Bowing as physical expression of humility and submission before divine majesty
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): [Literal vs Metaphorical distinction] Literal: the bodily posture of inclination; Metaphorical: the spiritual posture of humble submission — "Sheikhs bowing with age" and "camels bowing with exhaustion"
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد (Restriction & Focused Predication) — The conditional constructions (idhā... fa...) governing the temporal and circumstantial clauses for when these prayers become incumbent or recommended
3:26.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Mysteries of Hajj'

3:26.arabic: البقرة (3) من قوله آمن الرسول وشهد الله (4) وقل اللهم مالك الملك الآيتين (5) وقوله تعالى {لقد جاءكم رسول من أنفسكم} إلى آخرها (6) وقوله تعالى {لقد صدق الله رسوله الرؤيا بالحق} إلى آخرها (7) وقوله سبحانه الحمد لله الذي لم يتخذ ولدا (8) الآية وخمس آيات من أول الحديد (9) وثلاثا من آخر سورة الحشر (10) وإن قرأ المسبعات العشر التي أهداها الخضر عليه السلام إلى إبراهيم التيمي رحمه الله ووصاه أن يقولها غدوة وعشية فقد استكمل الفضل وجمع له ذلك فضيلة جملة الأدعية المذكورة فقد روي عن كرز بن وبرة رحمه ال
3:26.english: Now, the first watch (al-wird al-awwal) is that which extends from the dawn prayer (ṣalāt al-ṣubḥ) until sunrise (ṭulūʿ al-shams). When the servant has completed his obligatory prayer, he should remain seated in his place of prayer, occupying himself with the remembrance of God most High, until the sun has risen. For it has been reported that the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "That I should sit in my assembly, remembering God most High therein, from the morning prayer until sunrise, is more beloved to me than freeing four slaves." {«لأن أقعد في مجلسي أذكر الله تعالى فيه من صلاة الغداة إلى طلوع الشمس أحب إلي من أن أعتق أربع رقاب»} And it is related that he, peace and blessings be upon him, when he had prayed the morning prayer, would sit in his place of prayer until the sun rose; and in some versions [it is added] that he would pray two rakʿahs—that is, after sunrise. Concerning the virtue of this [practice], an incalculable number of reports have come down. Al-Ḥasan related that the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, used to mention, among what he recounted of his Lord's mercy, that He said: "O son of Adam, remember Me for an hour after the dawn prayer and for an hour after the afternoon prayer, and I shall suffice you for what lies between them." {«يا ابن آدم اذكرني بعد صلاة الفجر ساعة وبعد صلاة العصر ساعة أكفك ما بينهما»}
3:26.section_title_en: The Daily Liturgy of the Devout Servant: The First Watch (After Dawn Prayer until Sunrise)
3:26.anchors:
- Root: ذكر (dhakara)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Remembrance, invocation, mention; the opposite of forgetfulness (nisyān).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Remembrance of God (dhikr) is the heart's presence with the Divine, ranging from the tongue's utterance to the heart's contemplation; it is the noblest act when accompanied by presence of heart.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): verbal mention. Metaphorical (majāz): the heart's steadfastness in knowledge of God, which is the reality of dhikr.
- Root: صلا (ṣallā)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Prayer (ṣalāh); root meaning of supplication and blessing; also "to kindle a fire" (as in ṣalā al-nār).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Ṣalāh is the servant's standing before God in humility and devotion, comprising praise, recitation, bowing, and prostration; its perfection lies in the heart's presence.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the ritual prayer with its pillars. Metaphorical: supplication (duʿā') and blessing (taṣliyah) upon the Prophet.
- Root: ورد (warada)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To arrive at water; a portion or share of something that comes regularly.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The daily portion (wird) of devotion—a set liturgy of prayers, recitations, and remembrances that the servant regularly performs at appointed times.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: arriving at a watering place. Metaphorical: the soul's regular approach to the fountain of divine grace through prescribed acts of worship.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Restriction and Specification (al-ḥaṣr wa al-taqyīd) — governing the precise enumeration of the four functions (adʿiyah, adhkār, qirā'ah, fikr) after the dawn prayer, each specified by its own governing verb and object.
3:26.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications, prayers, and their spiritual power, from 'Arrangement of Litanies'

3:26.arabic: قرأ في ركعة بعد الفاتحة قل اللهم مالك الملك إلى آخر الآية فإذا فرغ من صلاته يقول جزى الله محمدا عنا ما هو أهله غفر له ذنوب سبعين سنة وكتب له براءة من النار (2) ليلة الخميس قال أبو هريرة رضي الله عنه قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم من صلى ليلة الخميس ما بين المغرب والعشاء ركعتين يقرأ في كل ركعة فاتحة الكتاب وآية الكرسي خمس مرات وقل هو الله أحد خمس مرات والمعوذتين خمس مرات فإذا فرغ من صلاته استغفر الله تعالى خمس عشرة مرة وجعل ثوابه لوالديه فقد أدى حق والديه عليه وإن كان عاقا لهما وأعطاه الله تعال
3:26.english: And in another ḥadīth: sixteen units [of prayer] — he recites after the Opening Chapter of the Book whatever God wills, and he recites in the last two units the Throne Verse thirty times, and in the first two units thirty times {قُلْ هُوَ اللَّهُ أَحَدٌ} (Say: He is God, the One). He will intercede for ten of his household, all of whom have had the Fire made obligatory upon them.
3:26.section_title_en: The Revival of the Religious Sciences — Section 161: Voluntary Prayers for Specific Nights and the Third Division: Prayers Recurring with the Recurrence of Years
3:26.anchors:
- Root: سلم (s-l-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Root denotes safety, security, and freedom from defect; the verbal form "sallama" (to greet/peace) and "aslama" (to surrender) both derive from the core notion of being secure and whole.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In the theological context, "salām" is both a divine attribute and the greeting of the people of Paradise; "taslīm" (the act of greeting) is an act of worship and supplication.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): the verbal greeting of peace. Metaphorical (Majaz): the act of seeking safety and security through submission.
- Root: صلو (s-l-w)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The root denotes supplication, blessing, and the act of prayer; "al-salāh" is the ritual prayer, while "al-salāt" upon the Prophet is a request for divine mercy and elevation of his rank.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Al-salāh" upon the Prophet from God is His mercy and His praise of him before the angels; from the angels it is their supplication for him; from the believers it is their request for mercy and their veneration of his station.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the ritual prayer with its specific postures. Metaphorical: the act of invoking blessings and mercy upon the Prophet, which is a form of devotional supplication.
- Root: شفع (sh-f-')
  * Lisan / Ayn: The root denotes pairing, joining, and making even; "al-shafā'ah" is the act of intercession — one joins one's own request to that of another to strengthen it.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Intercession is of two kinds: that which is sought from God for the removal of harm or attainment of benefit, and that which is sought from created beings. The former is exclusively God's to grant, and the latter is only effective by His permission.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: making a number even by adding one to it. Metaphorical: the intercessor's act of adding his own plea to the plea of the one for whom he intercedes.
- Root: عقر ('-q-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The root denotes barrenness, cutting off, and being unable to produce; "al-'āq" (the undutiful child) is one who cuts off the bond of filial piety and obedience to parents.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Uqūq" (undutifulness) is the severing of the bond of obedience and kindness that is due to parents, and it is a grave sin.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: cutting and severing. Metaphorical: the child who severs the tie of obedience and compassion to his parents.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Conditional Clauses (Bāb al-sharṭ) — The protasis (condition) introduced by "man" (whoever) is followed by an apodosis (result) that is the grammatical equivalent of the condition's answer, often introduced by "fa-" (then) when the apodosis is a nominal sentence or a verb preceded by "qad" or "sawfa," indicating the guaranteed consequence of the stipulated act.
3:26.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications, prayers, and their spiritual power, from 'Arrangement of Litanies'

4:64.arabic: الله عليه وسلم ثم يقول اللهم إنك قد قلت وقولك الحق ولو أنهم إذ ظلموا أنفسهم جاءوك فاستغفروا الله واستغفر لهم الرسول لوجدوا الله توابا رحيما اللهم إنا قد سمعنا قولك وأطعنا أمرك وقصدنا نبيك متشفعين به إليك في ذنوبنا وما أثقل ظهورنا من أوزارنا تائبين من زللنا معترفين بخطايانا وتقصيرنا فتب اللهم علينا وشفع نبيك هذا فينا وارفعنا بمنزلته عندك وحقه عليك اللهم اغفر للمهاجرين والأنصار واغفر لنا ولإخواننا الذين سبقونا بالإيمان اللهم لا تجعله آخر العهد من قبر نبيك ومن حرمك يا أرحم الراحمين ثم يأتي الروضة فيصلي فيها ركعتين ويكثر من الدعاء ما استطاع لقوله صلى الله عليه وسلم
4:64.english: I say: The Prophet ﷺ said: "Whoever visits me after my death, it is as though he visited me during my life." {من زارني بعد وفاتي فكأنما زارني في حياتي}
4:64.section_title_en: Section 210 — The Etiquette of Visiting the Prophet's Mosque and Grave in Medina
4:64.anchors:
- Root: زور (z-w-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of inclining toward, visiting, or intending a place or person; the visitor (zā'ir) is one who turns away from his own affairs toward another.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In theological context, ziyārah (visitation) of the Prophet ﷺ after death is an act of spiritual devotion (taqarrub), not a mere physical journey; its reward is tied to the sincerity of intention (niyyah).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (haqīqah) usage denotes physical approach; metaphorical (majāz) usage extends to seeking intercession (shafā'ah) and spiritual connection with the visited.
- Root: سلم (s-l-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Root denotes safety, peace, and deliverance from harm; the greeting "al-salāmu ʿalaykum" is a prayer for the recipient's immunity from all deficiency.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The greeting upon the Prophet ﷺ is a form of supplication (duʿā') and acknowledgment of his rank; it is also a renewal of the covenant (mīthāq) of obedience.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal usage is the exchange of safety; metaphorical usage in the visitation context signifies the visitor's submission and the Prophet's reciprocal blessing.
- Root: شفع (sh-f-ʿ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Root denotes pairing or joining; shafā'ah (intercession) is the act of the intercessor joining his own plea to that of the petitioner.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In Kalam, shafā'ah is a divinely granted honor (karāmah) to the Prophet ﷺ, conditional upon divine will; it is not an independent power but a mediated mercy.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: making a number even by adding one; metaphorical: the intercessor's elevation of the petitioner's rank before the king.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Prepositional Interposition (al-faṣl bayna al-jār wa al-majrūr) — The text employs extended vocative and prepositional structures (e.g., "al-salāmu ʿalayka yā Rasūl Allāh") where the syntactic pause after each invocation is permissible and rhetorically deliberate, mirroring the classical allowance for separation between the governing particle and its object for emphasis.
4:64.topic: Al-Ghazali on the journey of the soul, death, and the Hereafter, from 'Mysteries of Hajj'

5:3.arabic: وتمام الإسلام وكمال الدين فيه أنزل الله عز وجل {اليوم أكملت لكم دينكم وأتممت عليكم نعمتي ورضيت لكم الإسلام دينا} وفيه قال صلى الله عليه وسلم من مات ولم يحج فليمت إن شاء يهوديا وإن شاء نصرانيا (1) فأعظم بعبادة يعدم الدين بفقدها الكمال ويساوي تاركها اليهود والنصارى في الضلال وأجدر بها أن تصرف العناية إلى شرحها وتفصيل أركانها وسننها وآدابها وفضائلها وأسرارها وجملة ذلك ينكشف بتوفيق الله عز وجل في ثلاثة أبواب الباب الأول في فضائلها وفضائل مكة والبيت العتيق وجمل أركان وشرائط وجوبها الباب الثاني في أعمالها الظاهرة على الترتيب من مبدأ السفر إلى الرجوع الباب الثال
5:3.english: To proceed: Know that the Pilgrimage (ḥajj), among the pillars of Islam and its foundational supports, is the worship of a lifetime, the seal of one's affairs, the completion of Islam, and the perfection of the religion. Concerning it, God — Mighty and Majestic — revealed: {«اليوم أكملت لكم دينكم وأتممت عليكم نعمتي ورضيت لكم الإسلام دينا»} ("This day I have perfected for you your religion, and completed upon you My favor, and have chosen for you Islam as your religion") {Q. 5:3}. And concerning it, the Prophet — peace and blessings be upon him — said: "Whoever dies without having performed the Pilgrimage, let him die, if he wishes, as a Jew, and if he wishes, as a Christian." How great is a worship whose loss deprives the religion of its perfection, and whose abandoner is equated with Jews and Christians in error! And it is all the more fitting that careful attention be devoted to its exposition, the detailing of its pillars (arkān), its normative practices (sunan), its etiquettes (ādāb), its virtues (faḍā'il), and its inner secrets (asrār).
5:3.section_title_en: The Third Chapter on Voluntary Fasting and the Arrangement of Daily Liturgies (Awrād) Therein
5:3.anchors:
- Root: حمد (Ḥ-M-D)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of praise, commendation, and grateful acknowledgment of beneficence.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance — ḥamd is the conscious, deliberate act of praising God for His attributes and acts, distinct from mere shukr (thankfulness for benefits received).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Ḥaqīqah) — "أحمد الله تعالى بجميع محامده" (I praise God with all His praiseworthy attributes); Metaphorical (Majāz) — "أحمدت صنيعه" (I found his deed praiseworthy), extending to approval of conduct.
- Root: وفي (W-F-Y)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Completeness, fulfillment, reaching full measure.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance — wafā' signifies the perfect completion of a covenant or obligation; God's "completion" of His religion denotes its absolute finality and perfection.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — "درهم واف" (a full-weight dirham); Metaphorical — "أوفى على المائة" (he exceeded a hundred), indicating supererogatory completion beyond the obligatory.
- Root: فصل (F-Ṣ-L)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Separation, distinction, decisive division between two things.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance — faṣl is the act of distinguishing truth from falsehood, as in "Yawm al-Faṣl" (the Day of Decision); here, it denotes the structural division of a book into chapters.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — "فصلت الشاة" (I severed the joints of the sheep); Metaphorical — "هذا الأمر فيصل" (this matter is decisive, cutting through disputes).
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The structural division of discourse into clearly demarcated sections (fuṣūl) mirrors the syntactic principle of separating elements for clarity, ensuring each unit stands complete and unambiguous.
5:3.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Mysteries of Hajj'

5:82.arabic: الشاقة طمعا في الآخرة وأثنى الله عز وجل عليهم في كتابه فقال {ذلك بأن منهم قسيسين ورهبانا وأنهم لا يستكبرون} فلما اندرس ذلك وأقبل الخلق على اتباع الشهوات وهجروا التجرد لعبادة الله عز وجل وفتروا عنه بعث الله عز وجل نبيه محمدا صلى الله عليه وسلم لإحياء طريق الآخرة وتجديد سنة المرسلين في سلوكها فسأله أهل الملل عن الرهبانية والسياحة في دينه فقال صلى الله عليه وسلم أبدلنا الله بها الجهاد والتكبير على كل شرف (1) يعني الحج وسئل صلى الله عليه وسلم عن السائحين فقال هم الصائمون (2) فأنعم الله عز وجل على هذه الأمة بأن جعل الحج رهبانية لهم فشرف البيت العتيق بالإض
5:82.english: For this reason, the monastics (al-ruhbāniyyūn) in the past religions separated themselves from creation and withdrew to the peaks of mountains, preferring wild solitude away from people in pursuit of intimacy (uns) with God — mighty and majestic is He. They abandoned for God's sake the pleasures of the present and imposed upon themselves arduous spiritual exertions (mujāhidāt), hoping for the Hereafter. God — glorified and exalted is He — praised them in His Book, saying: {«ذلك بأن منهم قسيسين ورهبانا وأنهم لا يستكبرون»} — "That is because among them are priests and monks and because they do not behave arrogantly." Then when that [way] became effaced, and creation turned to following appetites, abandoned devotion to the worship of God — glorified and exalted is He — and grew languid in it, God — glorified and exalted is He — sent His Prophet Muhammad — may God's peace and blessings be upon him — to revive the path of the Hereafter and renew the way of the messengers in traversing it.
5:82.section_title_en: The Noble Stations of Pilgrimage and the Manner of Contemplation Upon Them — From the Beginning of Hajj to Its End
5:82.anchors:
- Root: فهم (f-h-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Comprehension, understanding, grasping the reality of a thing
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Intellectual apprehension that penetrates to the essential meaning, not mere surface awareness
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — understanding speech; Metaphorical — understanding the inner reality and wisdom of sacred acts
- Root: سفر (s-f-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Journey; also uncovering/disclosure — the traveler is one who uncovers distant horizons
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "السفر: كشف الغطاء" — uncovering the veil; the journey of hajj is both physical travel and spiritual unveiling
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — journeying across land; Metaphorical — "سفر عن وجهك الشر" (uncovering evil from your face), i.e., the hajj journey unveils the secrets of servitude
- Root: رهب (r-h-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To fear, to be awed; monastic withdrawal (rahbāniyyah) from worldly attachments
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Fear that drives one to solitary devotion; the monastic impulse redirected by Islamic law
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — fear; Metaphorical — the disciplined retreat from worldly pleasures for divine communion
- Root: بيت (b-y-t)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Place of nightly habitation; the Ka'bah as the primordial house
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "أصل البيت: مأوى الإنسان بالليل" — the house is where one dwells at night; the Sacred House is where hearts find nocturnal rest in God
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — physical structure; Metaphorical — the locus of divine presence and the object of spiritual yearning
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — "إنما" restricts the predicate exclusively to the subject, as in "إنما بعث الله نبيه لإحياء طريق الآخرة" — the sole purpose of prophetic mission is specified with exclusive focus.
5:82.topic: Al-Ghazali on constant remembrance of God and contemplative invocations, from 'Mysteries of Hajj'

6:13.arabic: البلد ووالد وما ولد وله ما سكن في الليل والنهار وهو السميع العليم السابعة في الحراسة ينبغي أن يحتاط بالنهار فلا يمشي منفردا خارج القافلة لأنه ربما يغتال أو ينقطع ويكون بالليل متحفظا عند النوم فإن نام في ابتداء الليل افترش ذراعه وإن نام في آخر الليل نصب ذراعه نصبا وجعل رأسه في كفه هكذا كان ينام رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في سفره (1) لأنه ربما استثقل النوم فتطلع الشمس وهو لا يدري فيكون ما يفوته من الصلاة أفضل مما يناله من الحج والأحب في الليل أن يتناوب الرفيقان في الحراسة فإن نام أحدهما حرس الآخر (2) فهو السنة فإن
6:13.english: He ought to seek out a righteous companion, one who loves goodness and assists in it: if he forgets, the companion reminds him; if he remembers, the companion aids him; if he fears, the companion emboldens him; if he weakens, the companion strengthens him; if his breast narrows, the companion enlarges his patience. He should bid farewell to his resident companions, his brothers, and his neighbors — taking leave of them and seeking their supplications, for God Most High places goodness in their prayers. The Sunnah of farewell is to say: «أستودع الله دينك وأمانتك وخواتيم عملك» — "I entrust to God your religion, your trustworthiness, and the seal of your deeds." And he, peace and blessings be upon him, used to say to one intending travel: "In God's protection and His care — may God provide you with piety, forgive your sin, and direct you toward goodness wherever you may be."
6:13.section_title_en: The Book of the Etiquette of Travel — Section 199: On the Comprehensive Etiquette of the Journey (From Provisioning to Guarding)
6:13.anchors:
- Root: س ف ر (S-F-R)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "السفر: كشف الغطاء" — unveiling, uncovering; the traveler is one who uncovers the veils of distant lands.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "السفر: كشف الغطاء، ويختص ذلك بالأعيان" — the journey is a literal uncovering of horizons, yet the spiritual journey unveils the soul's veils.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Haqiqah: "سافر سفرا بعيدا" (to travel far); Majaz: "وجه مسفر: مشرق سرورا" — a face radiant with joy, as the traveler's face brightens with divine trust.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — governing the permissible separation between the preposition and its object for rhetorical emphasis, as in the supplications' structural pauses.
6:13.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications, prayers, and their spiritual power, from 'Mysteries of Hajj'

6:162.arabic: اللهم رب الحمد لك الحمد كما تقول وخيرا مما نقول لك صلاتي ونسكي ومحياي ومماتي وإليك مآبي وإليك ثوابي اللهم إني أعوذ بك من وساوس الصدر وشتات الأمر وعذاب القبر اللهم إني أعوذ بك من شر ما يلج في الليل ومن شر ما يلج في النهار ومن شر ما تهب به الرياح ومن شر بوائق الدهر اللهم إني أعوذ بك من تحول عافيتك وفجأة نقمتك وجميع سخطك اللهم اهدني بالهدى واغفر لي في الآخرة والأولى يا خير مقصود وأسنى منزول به وأكرم مسئول ما لديه أعطني العشية أفضل ما أعطيت أحدا من خلقك وحجاج بيتك يا أرحم الراحمين اللهم يا رفيع الدرجات ومنزل البركات ويا فاط
6:162.english: On the Day of 'Arafah, the first thing with which one supplicates, let him say: There is no god but God alone, with no partner; His is the sovereignty and His is the praise; He gives life and causes death, and He is Living, He does not die; in His hand is all good, and He is over all things Omnipotent. O God, place in my heart a light, and in my hearing a light, and in my sight a light, and in my tongue a light. O God, expand for me my breast and make easy for me my affair. And let him say: O God, Lord of the praise, to You is the praise as You say, and better than what we say. To You is my prayer, my sacrifice, my living, and my dying; to You is my return, and to You is my recompense. O God, I seek refuge in You from the whisperings of the breast, the scattering of affairs, and the torment of the grave. O God, I seek refuge in You from the evil of what enters in the night, and from the evil of what enters in the day, and from the evil of what the winds bring, and from the evil of the calamities of time. O God, I seek refuge in You from the withdrawal of Your well-being, the suddenness of Your retribution, and all of Your wrath. O God, guide me with guidance, and forgive me in the Hereafter and the First. O Best of all sought goals, and Most Exalted of all that is alighted upon, and Most Generous of all who are asked — whatever is with You — grant me this evening the best of what You have given to any of Your creatures and pilgrims of Your Sacred House, O Most Merciful of the merciful. O God, O Raiser of degrees and Sender of blessings, O Originator of the earths and the heavens, voices have clamored to You in diverse languages, asking You their needs. And my need of You is that You not forget me in the abode of trial when the people of this world have forgotten me. O God, You hear my speech and see my place and know my secret and my public, and nothing of my affair is hidden from You. I am the wretched one, the poor one, the seeker of aid, the seeker of refuge, the fearful, the apprehensive, the confessor of his sin. I ask You with the asking of the destitute, and I supplicate to You with the supplication of the abased sinner, and I call upon You with the call of the fearful and distressed — the call of one whose neck has bowed to You, whose tears have flowed for You, whose body has humbled before You, and whose nose has been rubbed in the dust for You. O God, do not make me, by my supplication to You, O Lord, wretched, and be to me kind and merciful, O Best of those who are asked and Most Generous of those who give. My God, whoever has praised his own soul to You — for I am one who blames his own soul. My God, sins have silenced my tongue, so I have no means of intercession other than deeds, and no intercessor other than hope. My God, I know that my sins have left me no standing with You, nor any face for excuse — but You are the Most Generous of the generous. My God, if I am not worthy to attain Your mercy, then Your mercy is worthy to attain me, for Your mercy encompasses all things, and I am a thing. My God, though my sins be great, yet they are small beside Your pardon, so forgive them for me, O Generous One. My God, You are You, and I am I. I am the one who returns to sins, and You are the One who returns to forgiveness. My God, if You show mercy only to the people of obedience, then to whom shall the sinners flee? My God, I turned away from Your obedience deliberately, and I headed toward Your disobedience intentionally. Glory be to You — how great is Your proof against me, and how generous is Your pardon toward me! By the necessity of Your proof against me, and the severance of my excuse from You, and my poverty toward You, and Your richness from me — forgive me, O Best of those whom a caller has called, and Most Excellent of those whom a hope has hoped in. By the sanctity of Islam and by the covenant of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, I seek intercession with You, so forgive me all my sins, and turn me away from this standing place of mine with my needs fulfilled, and grant me what I have asked, and realize my hope in what I have wished. My God, I have called upon You with the supplication that You taught me, so do not deprive me of the hope that You made known to me. My God, what will You do this evening with a servant who confesses to You his sin, who is humble before You in his abasement, who is submissive in his offense, who pleads to You concerning his deed, who repents to You from his transgression, who seeks Your forgiveness for his wrong, who supplicates to You for pardon of him, who asks of You the success of his needs, who hopes in You at his standing place — despite the abundance of his sins? O Refuge of every living thing, and Protector of every believer — whoever does well, it is by Your mercy that he triumphs, and whoever errs, it is by his error that he perishes. O God, to You we have come forth, and in Your courtyard we have alighted, and You alone we hope, and what is with You we seek, and to Your beneficence we expose ourselves, and Your mercy we hope for, and from Your chastisement we are fearful, and to You with the heavy burdens of sins we have fled, and to Your Sacred House we have performed the pilgrimage. O You who owns the needs of those who ask, and knows the consciences of the silent — O You who has no lord with Him who is invoked, and no creator above Him who is feared, and no minister to whom one comes, and no chamberlain who is bribed — O You who increases not by the abundance of asking except in bounty and generosity, nor by the abundance of needs except in favor and beneficence. O God, You have made for every guest a hospitality, and we are Your guests, so make Your hospitality to us Paradise. O God, for every delegation there is a gift, and for every visitor there is an honor, and for every asker there is a giving, and for every one who hopes there is a reward, and for every seeker there is with You a recompense, and for every...
6:162.section_title_en: The Supplications of the Day of 'Arafah — Section 206
6:162.anchors:
- Root: دعو (d-'-w)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to call, summon, invoke; du'a is the act of calling upon God with humble petition.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In theological usage, du'a is the essence of worship ('ibadah), the creature's acknowledgment of need (iftiqar) before the Creator, and a means of drawing near (taqarrub).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (haqiqah): vocal calling. Metaphorical (majaz): the soul's inward turning to God, even without utterance.
- Root: نور (n-w-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Light; that by which one sees physically and, by extension, that by which the heart perceives truth.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Light (nur) is of two kinds: sensory (hissi) and intellectual ('aqli). The prophetic prayer for light in heart, hearing, sight, and tongue seeks the illumination of all faculties for obedience and gnosis (ma'rifah).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical luminosity. Metaphorical: guidance (huda) and clarity of perception in religious and moral matters.
- Root: عفو ('-f-w)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To pardon, to efface, to leave unpunished; to exceed in generosity.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): 'Afw is the erasure of sin and the lifting of its consequence; it is an attribute of God's mercy (rahmah) that supersedes His justice when the servant repents.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: to obliterate a trace. Metaphorical: God's complete remission of sin, leaving no mark of accountability.
- Root: رجا (r-j-w)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Hope, expectation of good; the opposite of despair (ya's).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Raja' is the heart's confident expectation of God's bounty, paired with fear (khawf); it is a station (maqam) of the sincere.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: to await. Metaphorical: the soul's reliance on divine mercy despite unworthiness.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Conjunction and Apposition (al-'Atf wa al-Badal) — The repeated vocatives "Ilahi" (My God) and "Allahumma" (O God) function as independent invocations, each followed by coordinated clauses that build a cumulative structure of petition, confession, and praise, requiring faithful preservation of each unit without conflation.
6:162.topic: Al-Ghazali on the journey of the soul, death, and the Hereafter, from 'Mysteries of Hajj'

8:38.arabic: إلهنا إنك قلت في كتابك المبين لمحمد خاتم النبيين {قل للذين كفروا إن ينتهوا يغفر لهم ما قد سلف} فأرضاك عنهم بالإقرار بكلمة التوحيد بعد الجحود وإنا نشهد لك بالتوحيد مخبتين ولمحمد بالرسالة مخلصين فاغفر لنا بهذه الشهادة سوالف الإجرام ولا تجعل حظنا فيه أنقص من حظ من دخل في الإسلام إلهنا إنك أحببت التقرب إليك بعتق ما ملكت أيماننا ونحن عبيدك وأنت أولى بالتفضل فأعتقنا وإنك أمرتنا أن نتصدق على فقرائنا ونحن فقراؤك وأنت أحق بالتطول فتصدق علينا ووصيتنا بالعفو عمن ظلمنا وقد ظلمنا أنفسنا وأنت أحق بالكرم فاعف عنا ربنا اغفر لنا وارحمنا أنت مولانا ربنا
8:38.english: "My God, every sinner has turned to You seeking mercy, and every aspirant to You seeks nearness (zulfā), and every one who beseeches You seeks pardon. We have arrived at Your Sacred House and stood at these mighty rites and witnessed these noble stations, hoping for what is with You — so do not disappoint our hope.
8:38.section_title_en: The Supplications of the Standing at 'Arafat and the Sacred Sites
8:38.anchors:
- Root: رحم (r-ḥ-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of tenderness, compassion, and mercy that issues in beneficent action toward the object of mercy.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Rahmah is that which necessitates beneficence (iḥsān) toward the one shown mercy; it is an attribute of God that is not mere feeling but a will to bestow.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) usage pertains to genuine compassion; metaphorical (majāz) usage is excluded for God, for His mercy is an eternal attribute, not a passing emotion.
- Root: عفو (ʿ-f-w)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To erase, obliterate, and leave something without trace; to pardon by removing the consequence of sin.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-ʿafw is to forgo the punishment due for an offense, and it is coupled with maghfirah (covering) — the former removes the requital, the latter veils the sin itself.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: to efface a trace (as wind effaces footprints). Metaphorical: God's pardon that wipes away the record of transgression.
- Root: زلفى (zulfā)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Nearness, proximity, and a means of approach.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Zulfā denotes a station of closeness to God attained through obedience and supplication; it is a degree of honor granted by Him.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical nearness. Metaphorical: spiritual rank and favor (darajah) before God.
- Root: سمع (s-m-ʿ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Hearing; perception of sound.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): God's hearing (samʿ) is not by ear or vibration but is His eternal attribute of encompassing all audible things without instrument.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: auditory perception. Metaphorical (for God): His knowledge of all supplications, without organ or multiplicity.
- Root: لهج (l-h-j)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To persist and cling to something; to be devotedly absorbed in it.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Ilḥāḥ (importunity) in supplication is the servant's persistent clinging to the door of God, which is beloved to Him, for it manifests need and dependence.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: to adhere stubbornly. Metaphorical: earnest, repeated petitioning of God, which is praised in the context of duʿā'.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب العطف على الضمير المرفوع المتصل (Coordination upon a connected nominative pronoun) — When coordinating upon a pronoun like "we" (naḥnu) with a new clause, the conjunction (wa) permits a fresh independent sentence, as in "We are Your servants and You are more worthy of bounty," where the second clause is not governed by the first but stands as a new assertion.
8:38.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Mysteries of Hajj'

17:80.arabic: متواضعا معظما وليقل بسم الله وعلى ملة رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم رب أدخلني مدخل صدق وأخرجني مخرج صدق واجعل لي من لدنك سلطانا نصيرا ثم يقصد المسجد ويدخله ويصلي بجنب المنبر ركعتين ويجعل عمود المنبر حذاء منكبه الأيمن ويستقبل السارية التي إلى جانبها الصندوق وتكون الدائرة التي في قبلة المسجد بين عينيه فذلك موقف رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قبل أن يغير المسجد وليجتهد أن يصلي في المسجد الأول قبل أن يزاد فيه ثم يأتي قبر النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فيقف عند وجهه وذلك بأن يستدبر القبلة ويستقبل جدار القبر على نحو من أربعة أذرع من السارية التي في زاوية جدار القبر ويجعل القنديل على رأس
17:80.english: I say: The Prophet ﷺ said: "Whoever visits me after my death, it is as though he visited me during my life." {من زارني بعد وفاتي فكأنما زارني في حياتي}
17:80.section_title_en: Section 210 — The Etiquette of Visiting the Prophet's Mosque and Grave in Medina
17:80.anchors:
- Root: زور (z-w-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of inclining toward, visiting, or intending a place or person; the visitor (zā'ir) is one who turns away from his own affairs toward another.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In theological context, ziyārah (visitation) of the Prophet ﷺ after death is an act of spiritual devotion (taqarrub), not a mere physical journey; its reward is tied to the sincerity of intention (niyyah).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (haqīqah) usage denotes physical approach; metaphorical (majāz) usage extends to seeking intercession (shafā'ah) and spiritual connection with the visited.
- Root: سلم (s-l-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Root denotes safety, peace, and deliverance from harm; the greeting "al-salāmu ʿalaykum" is a prayer for the recipient's immunity from all deficiency.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The greeting upon the Prophet ﷺ is a form of supplication (duʿā') and acknowledgment of his rank; it is also a renewal of the covenant (mīthāq) of obedience.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal usage is the exchange of safety; metaphorical usage in the visitation context signifies the visitor's submission and the Prophet's reciprocal blessing.
- Root: شفع (sh-f-ʿ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Root denotes pairing or joining; shafā'ah (intercession) is the act of the intercessor joining his own plea to that of the petitioner.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In Kalam, shafā'ah is a divinely granted honor (karāmah) to the Prophet ﷺ, conditional upon divine will; it is not an independent power but a mediated mercy.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: making a number even by adding one; metaphorical: the intercessor's elevation of the petitioner's rank before the king.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Prepositional Interposition (al-faṣl bayna al-jār wa al-majrūr) — The text employs extended vocative and prepositional structures (e.g., "al-salāmu ʿalayka yā Rasūl Allāh") where the syntactic pause after each invocation is permissible and rhetorically deliberate, mirroring the classical allowance for separation between the governing particle and its object for emphasis.
17:80.topic: Al-Ghazali on the journey of the soul, death, and the Hereafter, from 'Mysteries of Hajj'

22:27.arabic: قال الله عز وجل {وأذن في الناس بالحج يأتوك رجالا وعلى كل ضامر يأتين من كل فج عميق} وقال قتادة لما أمر الله عز وجل إبراهيم صلى الله عليه وسلم وعلى نبينا وعلى كل عبد مصطفى أن يؤذن في الناس بالحج نادى يا أيها الناس إن الله عز وجل بنى بيتا فحجوه وقال تعالى {ليشهدوا منافع لهم} قيل التجارة في الموسم والأجر في الآخرة ولما سمع بعض السلف هذا قال غفر لهم ورب الكعبة وقيل في تفسير قوله عز وجل {لأقعدن لهم صراطك المستقيم} أي طريق مكة يقعد الشيطان عليها ليمنع الناس منها وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم من حج البيت فلم يرفث ولم يفسق خرج م
22:27.english: I say: The first [matter] concerning the virtue of the pilgrimage — God Most High said: {«وَأَذِّن فِي النَّاسِ بِالْحَجِّ يَأْتُوكَ رِجَالًا وَعَلَىٰ كُلِّ ضَامِرٍ يَأْتِينَ مِن كُلِّ فَجٍّ عَمِيقٍ»} (And proclaim to the people the pilgrimage; they will come to you on foot and on every lean camel, coming from every deep and distant highway). Qatādah said: When God Most High commanded Ibrāhīm (peace be upon him — and upon our Prophet and upon every chosen servant) to proclaim the pilgrimage to the people, he called out: "O people! God Most High has built a House, so perform the pilgrimage to it." And He Most High said: {«لِيَشْهَدُوا مَنَافِعَ لَهُمْ»} (That they may witness benefits for them) — it is said [these benefits are] commerce during the season and reward in the Hereafter.
22:27.section_title_en: The Virtue of the Pilgrimage (Faḍīlat al-Ḥajj)
22:27.anchors:
- Root: ح ج ج (ḥ-j-j)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning is "to repair to a place repeatedly, to seek a thing, to overcome in argument." Al-Ayn: "الحج: القصد والتردد إلى الشيء."
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الحج: القصد إلى البيت الحرام للنسك، وأصله من قصدت الشيء وأقبلت عليه."
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "قصدت فلانا وحججت إليه." Metaphorical: "حاججته فحججته" — to overcome in disputation, from the idea of repeatedly pressing one's point.
- Root: غ ف ر (gh-f-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الغفر: الستر والتغطية." Al-Ayn: "غفرت الشيء: سترته."
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الغفران والمغفرة من الله هو أن يصون العبد من أن يمسه العذاب."
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "اغفر ثوبك في الوعاء" (cover/protect your garment). Metaphorical: Divine forgiveness as protective covering of sins.
- Root: و ف د (w-f-d)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الوفد: القوم يأتون السلطان أو الرئيس زائرين أو مستعطفين."
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الوفد: القوم المجتمعون القاصدون إلى رئيس."
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "وفد فلان على الأمير" — he came as a delegate. Metaphorical: The pilgrims as "delegation of God" (وفد الله) — those who come to Him seeking honor and bounty.
- Root: ر ح م (r-ḥ-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الرحمة: الرقة والتعطف." Al-Ayn: "الرحمة: رقة القلب."
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الرحمة: رقة تقتضي الإحسان إلى المرحوم."
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "رحمت فلانا" — I felt compassion. Metaphorical: Divine mercy as the descent of blessing and pardon upon creation.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The rule governing the placement of prepositional phrases and their objects, particularly relevant in the verse {«يأتين من كل فج عميق»} where the prepositional phrase "من كل فج" is interposed between the verb and its subject, demonstrating the rhetorical emphasis on the vastness of the routes of pilgrimage.
22:27.topic: Al-Ghazali on the journey of the soul, death, and the Hereafter, from 'Mysteries of Hajj'

22:32.arabic: تفسير قوله تعالى ذلك ومن يعظم شعائر الله إنه تحسينه وتسمينه وسوق الهدي من الميقات أفضل إن كان لا يجهده ولا يكده وليترك المكاس في شرائه فقد كانوا يغالون في ثلاث ويكرهون المكاس فيهن الهدي والأضحية والرقبة فإن أفضل ذلك أغلاه ثمنا وأنفسه عند أهله وروى ابن عمر أن عمر رضي الله عنهما أهدى بختية فطلبت منه بثلثمائة دينار فسأل رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أن يبيعها ويشتري بثمنها بدنا فنهاه عن ذلك وقال بل أهدها (1) وذلك لأن القليل الجيد خير من الكثير الدون وفي ثلثمائة دينار قيمة ثلاث
22:32.english: The ḥadīth states: "The pilgrim is only the disheveled and dust-covered one" (1). And God Most High says: "Look at the visitors of My House—they have come to Me disheveled and dust-covered from every deep valley" (2). And He Most High said: {«Then let them complete their rites (qadāʾ tafathihim)»} (al-Ḥajj 22:29). Al-tafath is the dishevelment and dust-covering, and its completion (qadāʾ) is by shaving the head, trimming the moustache, and clipping the nails.
22:32.section_title_en: The Book of the Secrets of Pilgrimage — Section 215: On the Etiquette of Pilgrimage (Ādāb al-Ḥajj)
22:32.anchors:
- Root: ش ع ث (sha-ʿ-th)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Dishevelment, dust-covered hair, unkempt appearance; the state of one who has abandoned grooming and adornment.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The outward state of humility and abandonment of worldly ornament—the physical correlative of spiritual self-abasement before God.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: unkempt hair and dust. Metaphorical: the visible sign of the pilgrim's total absorption in the sacred journey, forsaking all vanity.
- Root: ن ف ث (n-f-th)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To blow or spit; in the ḥadīth, the disheveled and dust-covered pilgrim who blows dust from himself.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The pilgrim who has completed the rites and blows away the dust of the journey—a state of completion and purification.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: expelling breath. Metaphorical: the final act of shedding the pilgrim state's physical residue.
- Root: ث ج (th-j)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The pouring forth of blood; the flowing of the sacrificial animal's blood at slaughter.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The ritual shedding of blood (nahr/dhabḥ) as an act of drawing near (qurbah) to God—the outward pouring of blood signifying the inward pouring forth of the soul in submission.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: copious flowing. Metaphorical: the complete and generous offering of the sacrificial animal.
- Root: ع ج (ʿ-j)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To raise the voice; the loud utterance of the talbiyah.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The vocal proclamation of God's oneness and presence at the pilgrimage—the audible counterpart to the silent intention.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: loud crying out. Metaphorical: the pilgrim's public declaration of submission, contrasting with the silent bloodshedding.
- Root: ق ض ي (q-ḍ-y)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To fulfill, complete, or discharge an obligation.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The completion of the rites of pilgrimage—specifically, the removal of the state of iḥrām's prohibitions through shaving, trimming, and cleansing.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: to settle a debt. Metaphorical: the discharge of the ritual obligations incumbent upon the pilgrim.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — The Prophet's statement "إنما الحاج الشعث النفث" restricts the true essence of the pilgrim to the disheveled and dust-covered state, negating the essence for others.
22:32.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Mysteries of Hajj'

22:37.arabic: والقرابين التي هي مجاهدة للنفس بتنقيص المال قال الله تعالى لن ينال الله لحومها ولا دماؤها ولكن يناله التقوى منكم أي الصفة التي استولت على القلب حتى حملته على امتثال الأوامر هي المطلوبة فكيف الأمر في الصلاة ولا أرب في أفعالها فهذا ما يدل من حيث المعنى على اشتراط حضور القلب فإن قلت إن حكمت ببطلان الصلاة وجعلت حضور القلب شرطا في صحتها خالفت إجماع الفقهاء فإنهم لم يشترطوا إلا حضور القلب عند التكبير فاعلم أنه قد تقدم في كتاب العلم أن الفقهاء لا يتصرفون في الباطن ولا يشقون عن القلوب ولا في طريق الآخرة بل يبنون أحكام الدين على ظاهر أعمال الجوارح وظاهر الأعمال كاف لسق
22:37.english: I do not see that all this grandeur belongs to the prayer by virtue of its outward actions alone — unless there be added to it the purpose of intimate converse (munājāh). For that takes precedence over fasting, alms-giving, pilgrimage, and other acts. Nay, even over the sacrificial animals and offerings (qarābīn), which are a striving of the soul through the diminution of wealth. Allah—exalted be He—said: {«لَن يَنَالَ اللَّهَ لُحُومُهَا وَلَا دِمَاؤُهَا وَلَكِن يَنَالُهُ التَّقْوَى مِنكُمْ»} ("Neither their flesh nor their blood reaches Allah, but the piety from you reaches Him") — that is, the attribute that has taken possession of the heart, such that it compels it to obey the commands, is what is sought. So how then with the prayer, in whose actions there is no doubt? This is what indicates, from the standpoint of meaning, the condition of heart-presence (ḥuḍūr al-qalb).
22:37.section_title_en: On the Remembrance, Recitation, Bowing, and Prostration — The Inner Reality of Prayer and the Condition of Heart-Presence
22:37.anchors:
- Root: ذكر (dhakara)
  * Lisan / Ayn: الذكر: نقيض النسيان، والذكر: الحفظ للشيء، والذكر باللسان والقلب. والذكر: الصوت الذي يذكر به، والذكر: الشرف والصيت.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الذكر: حضور معنى الشيء في النفس، إما بنطق اللسان أو بخطور القلب. والذكر ضربان: أحدهما ذكر باللسان، والآخر ذكر بالقلب. والذكر بالقلب أبلغ من الذكر باللسان، لأن الذكر باللسان قد يكون مع غفلة القلب، والذكر بالقلب لا يكون إلا مع التيقظ."
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Haqiqah: "ذكرت الشيء: نطقت به أو استحضرته في قلبك." Majaz: "ذكرت فلانا بخير: أثنيت عليه، وذكرت له نعمة: عددتها عليه. والذكر: الثناء الجميل، والذكر: الصلاة لله."
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The syntactic structure "فأما أن يكون المقصود منه كونه خطابا ومحاورة أو المقصود منه الحروف والأصوات" employs the disjunctive particle (أما) to establish a bipartite division, followed by the accusative of specification (التمييز) in "امتحانا للسان" to clarify the nature of the action.
22:37.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Mysteries of Hajj'

27:59.arabic: فإذا قرب من البيت قال الحمد لله وسلام على عباده الذين اصطفى اللهم صل على محمد عبدك ورسولك وعلى إبراهيم خليلك وعلى جميع أنبيائك ورسلك وليرفع يديه وليقل اللهم إني أسألك في مقامي هذا في أول مناسكي أن تتقبل توبتي وأن تتجاوز عن خطيئتي وتضع عني وزري الحمد لله الذي بلغني بيته الحرام الذي جعله مثابة للناس وأمنا وجعله مباركا وهدى للعالمين اللهم إني عبدك والبلد بلدك والحرم حرمك والبيت بيتك جئتك أطلب رحمتك وأسألك مسألة المضطر الخائف من عقوبتك الراجي لرحمتك الطالب مرضاتك السادس أن تقصد الحجر الأسود بعد ذل
27:59.english: The second [etiquette]: that he say, upon entering the first boundary of the Sacred Precinct (al-ḥaram), while still outside Mecca: "O Allah, this is Your Sanctuary (ḥaramuka) and Your Place of Security (amnuka); so make my flesh, my blood, my hair, and my skin forbidden to the Fire, and grant me security from Your punishment on the Day You resurrect Your servants, and make me among Your friends (awliyāʾ) and the people of Your obedience."
27:59.section_title_en: Section 201 — On the Etiquettes of Entering Mecca and the Sacred Mosque
27:59.anchors:
- Root: حرم (ḥ-r-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "Al-ḥaram" denotes that which is rendered inviolable and protected; the Sacred Precinct (al-ḥaram) is the sanctuary whose sanctity Allah has established, making its game, trees, and bloodshed forbidden.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Al-ḥarām: that which is prohibited—whether by divine decree, by legal command, or by coercive prevention." The ḥaram of Mecca is that which Allah has rendered sacrosanct, and His sanctuary (amn) is its correlate—security from fear and punishment.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): "He protects the sanctuary (ḥimā) and guards the inviolable precinct (ḥarīm)." Metaphorical (majāz): "A man of inviolable sanctity (muḥarram)"—one whose honor is protected; "the terrors of the night (maḥārim al-layl)"—its perils which make travel unlawful in safety.
- Root: ثني (th-n-y)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "Ath-thaniyyah" (pl. thanāyā): a mountain pass or defile in the road, so named because the path folds and doubles back upon itself through the heights.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Ath-thanā' and ithnān: a root for its derivatives, used by virtue of number or repetition." The two passes of Mecca—Thaniyyat Kadā' (upper) and Thaniyyat Kudā (lower)—are so named for their winding, doubled course.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "Every thing folded one part upon another in layers—each layer is a thanī." Metaphorical: "I turned him back (thanaytuhu) upon his face"—I returned him whence he came. The pilgrim's entry and exit through these passes enacts a turning toward and away from the Sacred House.
- Root: بيت (b-y-t)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "Al-bayt": the place of abode by night (al-baytūtah); the Kaaba is "al-Bayt al-Ḥarām"—the Inviolable House—because it is the primordial dwelling of worship.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "The origin of bayt: man's shelter by night... then applied to any dwelling." Allah says: {وَإِذْ جَعَلْنَا الْبَيْتَ مَثَابَةً لِلنَّاسِ وَأَمْنًا} [Al-Baqarah: 125]—a place of return and security.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the physical structure of the Kaaba. Metaphorical: "Bayt Allāh" as the locus of divine mercy and the qiblah of invocation—its corner (al-rukn) and its wall (al-multazam) are stations of answered supplication.
- Root: لهم (l-h-m) [as in ilhām, though not in this text, the root's semantic field of "swallowing/engulfing" informs the pilgrim's total absorption in the rites]
  * Lisan / Ayn: "Ilhām": to cast something into the heart (al-raw'); from lahima—to swallow entirely, leaving nothing.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Al-ilhām: the casting of a thing into the inner self (al-raw'), and it is specific to what comes from Allah." The pilgrim's supplications at the threshold of the House are an act of receptive swallowing of divine grace.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "He swallowed the thing—he gulped it down." Metaphorical: "A horse that swallows the ground (yaltahim al-arḍ)"—one that devours distance. The pilgrim's entry into the ḥaram is a devouring of the path of return to Allah.
- Sibawayh Rule: Al-ʿAṭf ʿalā al-Maʿnā (Coordination by Meaning) — When the Prophet ﷺ is reported to have entered from one pass and exited from another, the coordination of the two verbs (dakhala/kharaja) with their respective prepositions (min) governs the syntactic parallelism, each clause standing complete in its own semantic field, as in Sibawayh's treatment of coordinated sentences where the second member need not repeat the first's verb but carries its full force by ellipsis (ḥadhf).

30:17.arabic: الله مخلصين له الدين الحمد لله رب العالمين فسبحان الله حين تمسون وحين تصبحون وله الحمد في السموات والأرض وعشيا وحين تظهرون يخرج الحي من الميت ويخرج الميت من الحي ويحيي الأرض بعد موتها وكذلك تخرجون ومن آياته أن خلقكم من تراب ثم إذا أنتم بشر تنتشرون اللهم إني أسألك إيمانا دائما ويقينا صادقا وعلما نافعا وقلبا خاشعا ولسانا ذاكرا وأسألك العفو والعافية والمعافاة الدائمة في الدنيا والآخرة ويصلي على محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم ويدعو الله عز وجل بما شاء من حاجته عقيب هذا الدعاء ثم ينزل ويبتدىء السعي وهو يقول رب اغفر وارحم وتجاوز عما تعلم إنك أنت الأعز الأكرم اللهم آتنا في الدنيا حسنة وفي الآخرة حسنة وقنا عذاب النار ويمشي على هينة حتى ينتهي إلى الميل الأخضر وهو أول ما يلقاه إذا نزل من الصفا وهو على زاوية الم
30:17.english: Upon ascending al-Ṣafā, he should face the House (al-Bayt) and say: "God is Greater, God is Greater. Praise be to God for what He has guided us to. Praise be to God with all His praises, for all His graces, all of them. There is no god but God alone, with no partner. His is the dominion, and His is the praise. He gives life and causes death; in His hand is all good, and He is over all things competent. There is no god but God alone; He fulfilled His promise, aided His servant, and honored His soldiers; He alone defeated the confederates. There is no god but God, devoting religion sincerely to Him, even if the disbelievers detest it. There is no god but God, devoting religion sincerely to Him. Praise be to God, Lord of the worlds. So exalted is God when you reach the evening and when you reach the morning. And His is the praise in the heavens and the earth, and at nightfall and when you are at noon. He brings forth the living from the dead and brings forth the dead from the living, and He revives the earth after its death, and thus shall you be brought forth. And of His signs is that He created you from dust; then, behold, you are humans spreading out. O God, I ask You for enduring faith, sincere certainty, beneficial knowledge, a humble heart, and a tongue that remembers You. And I ask You for pardon, well-being, and perpetual immunity in this world and the Hereafter." Then he sends blessings upon Muḥammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and supplicates God, Mighty and Majestic, with whatever need he wishes, following this supplication.
30:17.section_title_en: The Yemeni Corner and the Stone — The Beginning of the Saʿy and Its Rites
30:17.anchors:
- Root: سعي (Saʿy)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The root denotes striving, running, or rapid walking; it is the exertion of effort in a matter, whether good or evil.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "السعي: المشي السريع، وهو دون العدو، ويستعمل للجد في الأمر" — Saʿy is swift walking, less than running, and is used for earnest exertion in a matter. In the sacred rite, it signifies the ritual traversing between al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah, an act of devotional striving.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Ḥaqīqah): "سعى إلى المسجد" — physical exertion toward a goal. Metaphorical (Majāz): "هو يسعى على عياله" — he strives to provide for his family. In the ritual context, the physical traversing is the literal embodiment of devotional striving.
- Root: حمد (Ḥamd)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The root denotes praise, commendation, and the acknowledgment of beneficence; it is the opposite of blame (dhamm).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Praise (ḥamd) is the acknowledgment of beneficence with reverence and love, and it is due to God alone in His absolute perfection.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "أحمد الله تعالى بجميع محامده" — praising God with all His praises. Metaphorical: "أحمدت صنيعه" — I approved of his deed. In the supplications of the saʿy, the pilgrim's praise is both literal acknowledgment and the metaphorical "approval" of God's decree.
- Root: رمل (Raml)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The root denotes rapid walking with a slight trotting motion, a form of hastening in movement.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Not a primary theological term, but in ritual context it signifies the prescribed hastening between the two green markers, emulating the Prophet's action.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical hastening. Metaphorical: The rapid pace is a visible emblem of spiritual earnestness and the rejection of the polytheists' claim that the Muslims were weakened by fever.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Restriction and Specification (al-Ḥaṣr wa al-Taqyīd) — The phrase "وإنما ذلك شرط في طواف الركن" employs restriction to delimit a condition exclusively to the circumambulation of the pillar (ṭawāf al-rukn), thereby negating its applicability to the saʿy.

40:14.arabic: الله وحده لا شريك له مخلصين له الدين ولو كره الكافرون يفتتح بالتكبير ليلة الفطر إلى الشروع في صلاة العيد وفي العيد الثاني يفتتح التكبير عقيب الصبح يوم عرفة إلى آخر النهار يوم الثالث عشر وهذا أكمل الأقاويل ويكبر عقيب الصلوات المفروضة وعقيب النوافل وهو عقيب الفرائض آكد الثاني إذا أصبح يوم العيد يغتسل ويتزين ويتطيب كما ذكرناه في الجمعة والرداء والعمامة هو الأفضل للرجال وليجنب الصبيان الحرير والعجائز التزين عند الخروج الثالث أن يخرج من طريق ويرجع من طريق آخر (1) هكذا فعل رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وك
40:14.english: **The First:** The takbīr (declaration of Allah's Greatness). Its beginning is established by the saying of Allah, the Exalted: {«وَتُكْمِلُوا الْعِدَّةَ وَلِتُكَبِّرُوا اللَّهَ عَلَى مَا هَدَاكُمْ»} ("And that you complete the number and magnify Allah for having guided you") {Al-Baqarah: 185}. Its form is that one says: "Allāhu akbar, Allāhu akbar, lā ilāha illā Allāhu wa-Allāhu akbar, Allāhu akbar wa-li-Llāhi al-ḥamd" (Allah is Greater, Allah is Greater, there is no deity except Allah, and Allah is Greater, Allah is Greater, and to Allah belongs all praise). And it is said: "Allāhu akbar kabīran, wa-al-ḥamdu li-Llāhi kathīran, wa-subḥāna Allāhi bukratan wa-aṣīlā, lā ilāha illā Allāhu waḥdahu lā sharīka lah, mukhlisīna lahu al-dīn wa-law kariha al-kāfirūn" (Allah is Greater, abundantly great, and praise be to Allah, abundantly much, and glory be to Allah morning and evening. There is no deity except Allah alone, with no partner, sincere to Him in religion, even though the disbelievers detest it). One begins the takbīr on the night of Fiṭr until the commencement of the Eid prayer. In the second Eid (al-Aḍḥā), one begins the takbīr immediately after the dawn prayer on the Day of ʿArafah until the end of the day of the thirteenth [of Dhū al-Ḥijjah]. This is the most complete of the sayings. One pronounces the takbīr after the obligatory prayers and after the supererogatory prayers, though it is more emphatic after the obligatory ones.
40:14.section_title_en: The Book of the Revival of the Religious Sciences — Section on the Two Festivals (Eid), the Supererogatory Prayers of Rajab and Shaʿbān
40:14.anchors:
- Root: كبر (k-b-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of greatness in magnitude, age, or rank; al-takbīr is the utterance "Allāhu akbar" (Allah is Greater).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-kabīr and al-ṣaghīr are relative terms; takbīr in worship signifies declaring Allah's transcendence above all comparison, used in quantity (connected/disconnected) and in dignity.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): "Allāhu akbar" as magnification of Allah's majesty. Metaphorical (majāz): "takabbara" for prideful self-aggrandizement (blameworthy), distinct from the liturgical takbīr.
- Root: صلا (ṣ-l-w)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Root denotes supplication (duʿā'), blessing, and the ritual prayer; al-ṣalāh as worship with bowing and prostration.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-ṣalāh is fundamentally supplication and seeking forgiveness; in the Law it is the specific acts of worship comprising standing, bowing, and prostration, with the heart present in humility.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the prescribed prayer (al-ṣalāh al-maktūbah). Metaphorical: "ṣallā ʿalā" for invoking blessings (on the Prophet), and "muṣallīn" for those who pray or supplicate.
- Root: سجد (s-j-d)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Prostration; placing the forehead on the ground in worship.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-sujūd is fundamentally humility and self-abasement; it is made a term for humbling oneself before Allah in worship — two kinds: voluntary (for humans, deserving reward) and compelled/subjugated (for all creation).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: prostration in prayer. Metaphorical: "sajadat al-safīnah lil-riyāḥ" (the ship yields to the winds), and "ʿayn sājidah" (a languid eye) — indicating submission or stillness.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Restriction and Focused Predication (al-ḥaṣr wa al-taqyīd bi-innamā) — Used in the text's argumentation (e.g., "إنما أوردناها في هذا القسم لأنها تتكرر") to restrict the reason for inclusion, and in preference statements ("والمختار أن الجماعة أفضل") to assert a focused judgment.
40:14.topic: Al-Ghazali on constant remembrance of God and contemplative invocations, from 'Mysteries of Hajj'

43:13.arabic: وما لم يشأ لم يكن سبحان الذي سخر لنا هذا وما كنا له مقرنين وإنا إلى ربنا لمنقلبون اللهم إني وجهت وجهي إليك وفوضت أمري كله إليك وتوكلت في جميع أموري عليك أنت حسبي ونعم الوكيل فإذا استوى على الراحلة واستوت تحته قال سبحان الله والحمد لله ولا إله إلا الله والله أكبر سبع مرات وقال الحمد لله الذي هدانا لهذا وما كنا لنهتدي لولا أن هدانا الله اللهم أنت الحامل على الظهر وأنت المستعان على الأمور السادسة في النزول والسنة أن لا ينزل حتى يحمى النهار ويكون أكثر سيره بالليل قال صلى الله عليه وسلم عليكم بالدلجة فإن الأرض تطوي بالليل ما لا تطوي با
43:13.english: He ought to seek out a righteous companion, one who loves goodness and assists in it: if he forgets, the companion reminds him; if he remembers, the companion aids him; if he fears, the companion emboldens him; if he weakens, the companion strengthens him; if his breast narrows, the companion enlarges his patience. He should bid farewell to his resident companions, his brothers, and his neighbors — taking leave of them and seeking their supplications, for God Most High places goodness in their prayers. The Sunnah of farewell is to say: «أستودع الله دينك وأمانتك وخواتيم عملك» — "I entrust to God your religion, your trustworthiness, and the seal of your deeds." And he, peace and blessings be upon him, used to say to one intending travel: "In God's protection and His care — may God provide you with piety, forgive your sin, and direct you toward goodness wherever you may be."
43:13.section_title_en: The Book of the Etiquette of Travel — Section 199: On the Comprehensive Etiquette of the Journey (From Provisioning to Guarding)
43:13.anchors:
- Root: س ف ر (S-F-R)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "السفر: كشف الغطاء" — unveiling, uncovering; the traveler is one who uncovers the veils of distant lands.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "السفر: كشف الغطاء، ويختص ذلك بالأعيان" — the journey is a literal uncovering of horizons, yet the spiritual journey unveils the soul's veils.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Haqiqah: "سافر سفرا بعيدا" (to travel far); Majaz: "وجه مسفر: مشرق سرورا" — a face radiant with joy, as the traveler's face brightens with divine trust.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — governing the permissible separation between the preposition and its object for rhetorical emphasis, as in the supplications' structural pauses.

58:21.arabic: الله منتهى ولا دون الله ملجأ كتب الله لأغلبن أنا ورسلي إن الله قوي عزيز تحصنت بالله العظيم واستغثت بالحي الذي لا يموت اللهم احرسنا بعينك التي لا تنام واكنفنا بركنك الذي لا يرام اللهم ارحمنا بقدرتك علينا فلا نهلك وأنت ثقتنا ورجاؤنا اللهم أعطف علينا قلوب عبادك وإمائك برأفة ورحمة إنك أنت أرحم الراحمين الثامنة مهما علا نشزا من الأرض في الطريق فيستحب أن يكبر ثلاثا ثم يقول اللهم لك الشرف على كل شرف ولك الحمد على كل حال ومهما هبط سبح ومهما خاف الوحشة في سفره قال سبحان الله الملك القدوس رب الملائكة والروح جللت السموات بالعزة و
