66:8.arabic: فاصرفني عنه واصرفه عني واقدر لي الخير أينما كان إنك على كل شيء قدير (6) رواه جابر بن عبد الله قال كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يعلمنا الاستخارة في الأمور كلها كما يعلمنا السورة من القرآن وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا هم أحدكم بأمر فليصل ركعتين ثم ليسم الأمر ويدعو بما ذكرناه وقال بعض الحكماء من أعطي أربعا لم يمنع أربعا من أعطي الشكر لم يمنع المزيد ومن أعطي التوبة لم يمنع القبول ومن أعطي الاستخارة لم يمنع الخيرة ومن أعطي المشورة لم يمنع الصواب الثامنة صلاة الحاجة (7) فمن ضاق عليه الأمر ومسته حاجة في صلاح دينه ودن
66:8.english:
**QUAD_ANCHORS:**
- Root: خسف (kha-sa-fa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: [Core linguistic root meaning] To swallow up, to cause to sink into the earth; the darkening of the sun or moon (khusūf for the moon, kusūf for the sun, though both are used interchangeably)
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): [Theological/Kalam semantic nuance] The eclipse as a divine sign (āyah) — not a natural phenomenon merely, but a portent summoning the servant to remembrance of God
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): [Literal vs Metaphorical distinction] Literal: the celestial bodies being veiled/obscured; Metaphorical: the veiling of hearts from divine remembrance
- Root: سقى (sa-qa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: [Core linguistic root meaning] To give to drink, to water; istisqā' — the act of seeking rain/water from God
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): [Theological/Kalam semantic nuance] The prayer for rain as a communal acknowledgment of absolute dependence upon divine providence
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): [Literal vs Metaphorical distinction] Literal: requesting water; Metaphorical: seeking divine mercy and abundance
- Root: جنز (ja-na-za)
  * Lisan / Ayn: [Core linguistic root meaning] The bier/corpse; janāzah — the funeral
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): [Theological/Kalam semantic nuance] The funeral prayer as a collective obligation (farḍ kifāyah) — the living standing as intercessors for the dead
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): [Literal vs Metaphorical distinction] Literal: the bier upon which the dead is carried; Metaphorical: the entire funeral rite as a reminder of one's own mortality
- Root: حيي (ḥa-ya)
  * Lisan / Ayn: [Core linguistic root meaning] To live; taḥiyyah — greeting, salutation; the "greeting of the mosque" (taḥiyyat al-masjid)
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): [Theological/Kalam semantic nuance] The greeting of the mosque as an act of reverence for the sacred space — a spiritual courtesy toward the house of God
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): [Literal vs Metaphorical distinction] Literal: greeting a person; Metaphorical: greeting the mosque through prayer as one greets a host upon entering his abode
- Root: خير (kha-ya-ra)
  * Lisan / Ayn: [Core linguistic root meaning] To choose; istikhārah — seeking divine choice/guidance
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): [Theological/Kalam semantic nuance] The prayer of seeking guidance as the servant's acknowledgment that only God knows the unseen consequences of affairs
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): [Literal vs Metaphorical distinction] Literal: asking someone to choose for you; Metaphorical: delegating one's affairs to divine providence while abandoning personal preference
- Root: ركع (ra-ka-ʿa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: [Core linguistic root meaning] To bow; rukūʿ — the bowing posture in prayer
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): [Theological/Kalam semantic nuance] Bowing as physical expression of humility and submission before divine majesty
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): [Literal vs Metaphorical distinction] Literal: the bodily posture of inclination; Metaphorical: the spiritual posture of humble submission — "Sheikhs bowing with age" and "camels bowing with exhaustion"

66:8.arabic: المعرفة نور للعارفين بعد الموت يسعى نورهم بين أيديهم وبأيمانهم يقولون ربنا أتمم لنا نورنا أي تكون هذه المعرفة رأس مال يوصل إلى كشف ما لم ينكشف في الدنيا كما أن من معه سراج خفي فإنه يجوز أن يصير ذلك سببا لزيادة النور بسراج آخر يقتبس منه فيكمل النور الخفي على سبيل الاستتمام ومن ليس معه أصل السراج فلا مطمع له في ذلك فمن ليس معه أصل معرفة الله تعالى لم يكن له مطمع في هذا النور فيبقى كمن مثله في الظلمات ليس بخارج منها بل كظلمات في بحر لجى يغشاه موج من فوقه موج من فوقه سحاب ظلمات بعضها فوق بعض فإذن لا سعادة إلا في معرفة الله تعالى وأما ما
66:8.english: All of these divisions are comprised within knowledge of God — of what is necessary for Him, what is impossible in His attributes, and what is permissible in His acts. Thus, knowledge of God — exalted be He — of His attributes, His acts, His wisdom in the dominion (malakūt) of the heavens and the earth, the ordering of this world and the Hereafter, and what pertains to that — this is the true perfection that draws near to God — exalted be He — the one who is described by it, and it remains a perfection for the soul after death. And this knowledge becomes a light for the knowers after death: {their light running before them and on their right hands, they saying: "Our Lord, perfect for us our light"} {«ربنا أتمم لنا نورنا»} — that is, this knowledge is the capital that leads to the disclosure of what was not disclosed in this world. Just as one who carries a hidden lamp — it is possible that this becomes the cause of increased light by another lamp from which he kindles, so that the hidden light is completed by way of supplementation — while one who has no lamp at all has no hope of that. So too, one who has no root of knowledge of God — exalted be He — has no hope in that light; he remains like one whose similitude is in darkness, not emerging from it — nay, {like darknesses in a vast deep sea, covered by wave above wave, above which is cloud: darknesses, one above another} {«كظلمات في بحر لجي يغشاه موج من فوقه موج من فوقه سحاب ظلمات بعضها فوق بعض»}. Therefore, there is no happiness save in knowledge of God — exalted be He.
66:8.section_title_en: The True Perfection of Knowledge and Its Degrees of Proximity to God
66:8.anchors:
- Root: علم (ʿ-L-M)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core sense of "knowing" as the impression of a thing's reality upon the mind; the root also carries the sense of a "mark" or "sign" by which something is distinguished and recognized.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Knowledge (ʿilm) is "the apprehension of a thing by its true reality" — divided into apprehension of the essence of a thing, and judgment upon a thing regarding what is or is not predicated of it. It is the broadest epistemic term, applicable to God and creatures alike.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) usage: "He is a sign (ʿalam) of knowledge" — knowledge is that which marks and distinguishes. The metaphorical (majāz) extension: "I knew of your news" = "I perceived it" — indicating that knowledge as proximity to God is not mere information but a transformative mark upon the soul.
- Root: عرف (ʿ-R-F)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Recognition through traces and effects; the root denotes "coming to know by way of discernment of distinguishing features."
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Maʿrifah is "apprehension of a thing through reflection and deliberation upon its effect" — more specific than ʿilm. It is the term used for the creature's knowledge of God, since it proceeds from contemplating His works, not from grasping His essence.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "I will make you recognize (la-ʾuʿarrifanna-ka) what you did" = "I will requite you for it." This underscores that maʿrifah is knowledge that returns upon the knower as a state of recompense or illumination.
- Root: نور (N-W-R)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Light as that which renders visible; the root also yields "beacon" (manār) — a landmark set upon a path for guidance.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Light is the diffused radiance that aids vision" — of two kinds: the sensory (perceived by the eye) and the intellectual (perceived by the inner eye of insight), the latter being "the light of the intellect and the light of the Qur'an."
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Metaphorical (majāz): "The matter became luminous (nāra)" = "it became clear." Light is thus the very clarity of knowledge that guides the knower through the darkness of ignorance.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Restriction and Specification (al-ḥaṣr wa al-taqyīd) — governing the use of "إنما" (innamā) to restrict perfection exclusively to knowledge of God, and the conditional-connective structure (fa-innahu, fa-kullamā) that links degrees of knowledge to degrees of proximity.

66:8.arabic: وقوله سبحانه وتعالى {نورهم يسعى بين أيديهم وبأيمانهم يقولون ربنا أتمم لنا نورنا} محتمل لهذا المعنى وهو أن ينعم عليه بإتمام النور مهما تزود من الدنيا أصل النور ويحتمل أن يكون المراد به إتمام النور في غير ما استنار في الدنيا استنارة محتاجة إلى مزيد الاستكمال والإشراق فيكون هو المراد بتمامه وقوله تعالى {انظرونا نقتبس من نوركم قيل ارجعوا وراءكم فالتمسوا نورا} يدل على أن الأنوار لابد وأن يتزود أصلها في الدنيا ثم يزداد في الآخرة إشراقا فأما أن يتجدد نور فلا والحكم في هذا برجم الظنون مخطر ولم ينكشف لنا فيه بعد ما يوثق به فنسأل الله ت
66:8.english: And His saying, Glorified and Exalted is He: {نُورُهُمْ يَسْعَىٰ بَيْنَ أَيْدِيهِمْ وَبِأَيْمَانِهِمْ يَقُولُونَ رَبَّنَا أَتْمِمْ لَنَا نُورَنَا} ["Their light will run before them and on their right hands; they will say, 'Our Lord, perfect for us our light'"] (Q 66:8) — this is susceptible to the meaning that He bestows upon them the perfection of light whenever they had provisioned from the world the origin of light. And it is also susceptible that the intended meaning is the perfection of light in what was not illuminated in this world with an illumination that stands in need of further completion and radiance — so that this is what is meant by its perfection. And His saying, Exalted is He: {انْظُرُونَا نَقْتَبِسْ مِنْ نُورِكُمْ قِيلَ ارْجِعُوا وَرَاءَكُمْ فَالْتَمِسُوا نُورًا} ["Look upon us so we may borrow from your light. It will be said, 'Return behind you and seek light'"] (Q 57:13) — this indicates that the lights must have their origin provisioned in this world, then in the Hereafter they increase in radiance. But as for a light being newly generated [there without prior origin] — no. And the judgment in this matter is a venture of conjecture, perilous, and there has not been unveiled to us therein anything trustworthy. So we ask God, Exalted is He, to increase us in knowledge and right guidance, and to show us the truth as truth.
66:8.section_title_en: On the Ever-Replenished Delights of the Hereafter and the Yearning (Shawq) for the Divine Vision
66:8.anchors:
- Root: لذذ (Ladhdhah — Pleasure/Delight)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root denotes the sweetness of taste and the experience of sensory gratification; its verbal form (ladhdha) implies direct apprehension of what is agreeable.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In theological usage, true pleasure (al-ladhdhah al-ʿuẓmā) is the soul's perception of what is conformable to its nature — the highest being the vision of God (ru'yat Allāh) and the bliss of proximity to Him.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) for sensory delight; metaphorical (majāz) for intellectual and spiritual joys, where the "taste" is of gnosis (maʿrifah), not of the palate.

- Root: شوق (Shawq — Yearning/Longing)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The root signifies the soul's restless inclination toward a beloved; the "spurring on" of the heart toward reunion.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Shawq is the movement of the heart toward its ultimate Beloved (al-maḥbūb al-aʿlā) — a yearning that persists even in bliss, for the unveiling (kashf) of ever-greater divine self-disclosure.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal for human longing; metaphorical for the divine "yearning" attributed to God (as in the sacred reports), which is an expression of His loving acceptance and bestowal of grace, not an emotional lack.

- Root: نور (Nūr — Light)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root denotes illumination, radiance, and that by which one sees and is seen.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Twofold: sensory light (of the sun, stars) and intellectual/spiritual light (of reason, faith, and the Qur'an). The "light of the believers" on the Day of Resurrection is the latter — the radiance of their faith and works in the world.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal for physical luminosity; metaphorical (majāz) for guidance, clarity, and the illuminating power of divine truth in the heart.

- Root: قلب (Qalb — Heart)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root means to turn over, to flip, to transform — hence the heart is so-named for its constant fluctuation (taqallub) of states.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The heart is the seat of perception and understanding (al-ʿaql wa al-fahm); it is the subtle divine reality (al-laṭīfah al-rabbāniyyah) that apprehends God, not the physical organ.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal for the physical organ; metaphorical for the spiritual faculty of cognition and volition that turns toward or away from God.

- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — Governing the precise scope of statements like "the pleasure of what is renewed is only a distraction from the ache of yearning," ensuring the predicate is confined to the subject without overextension.
66:8.topic: Al-Ghazali on the journey of the soul, death, and the Hereafter, from 'Love, Longing, Intimacy and Contentment'

66:8.arabic: وقد قال الله تعالى يا أيها الذين آمنوا أنفقوا من طيبات ما كسبتم ومما أخرجنا لكم من الأرض ولا تيمموا الخبيث منه تنفقون ولستم بآخذيه إلا أن تغمضوا فيه أي لا تأخذوه إلا مع كراهية وحياء وهو معنى الإغماض فلا تؤثروا به ربكم وفي الخبر سبق درهم مائة ألف درهم (3) وذلك بأن يخرجه الإنسان وهو من أحل ماله وأجوده فيصدر ذلك عن الرضا والفرح بالبذل وقد يخرج مائة ألف درهم مما يكره من ماله فيدل ذلك على أنه ليس يؤثر الله عز وجل بشيء مما يحبه وبذلك ذم الله تعالى قوما جعلوا لله ما يكرهون فقال تعال
66:8.english: The heart is not treated save with the compound electuary (maʿjūn) of knowledge and works. And this condition among the conditions of almsgiving runs in the same course as humility (al-khushūʿ) runs in the prayer. This is established by his saying — may Allah bless him and grant him peace: "A man has nothing of his prayer save that of which he was conscious." And this is like his saying — may Allah bless him and grant him peace: "Allah does not accept the charity of the one who bestows it with reproach (al-mannān)." And like His saying — Exalted is He: {«لا تبطلوا صدقاتكم بالمن والأذى»} ("Do not nullify your charities by reproach and injury"). As for the legal opinion (fatwā) of the jurist that the alms fall in their proper place and that one's liability is discharged without this condition — that is another discussion, and we have already pointed to its meaning in the Book of Prayer.
66:8.section_title_en: The Inner Conditions of Charity — Section 175 (From The Revival of the Religious Sciences, Book of the Mysteries of Almsgiving)
66:8.anchors:
- Root: قلب (q-l-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "To turn, overturn, transform a thing from one state to another; to rotate, to flip"
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "قلب الشيء: تصريفه وصرفه عن وجه إلى وجه" — the heart is so named because of its constant turning and transformation between states
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "قلب الشيء قلبا: حوله عن وجهه" (to turn a thing from its face). Metaphorical: "رجل قلب حول: يقلب الأمور ويحتال" — one who turns matters over and manages them; "قلبوا لك الأمور" (they turned matters against you)
- Root: وجل (w-j-l)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "Fear, dread, apprehension that strikes the heart"
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الوجل: استشعار الخوف" — the sensing of fear; cited in {«إنما المؤمنون الذين إذا ذكر الله وجلت قلوبهم»}
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "رجل وجل، وقوم وجال" — a fearful man, a fearful people; "وفي قلبه وجل" — in his heart is dread
- Root: عجب (ʿ-j-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "Wonder, amazement; self-admiration, vanity"
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Self-admiration (al-ʿujb) is a destructive spiritual ailment that nullifies deeds
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: wonder at something extraordinary. Metaphorical: self-conceit regarding one's own acts of obedience
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد (Restriction & Focused Predication) — governing the precise limitation of general categories (al-ṣifāt al-khāṣṣah within al-aṣnāf al-thamāniyyah) and the conditional structure of acceptance

66:8.arabic: جهنم وهي حظ المؤمن من النار (2) وروي في تفسير قوله تعالى {يوم لا يخزي الله النبي والذين آمنوا معه} أن الله تعالى أوحى إلى نبيه صلى الله عليه وسلم إني أجعل حساب أمتك إليك قال لا يارب أنت أرحم بهم مني فقال إذن لا نخزيك فيهم (3) وروي عن أنس إن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم سأل ربه في ذنوب أمته فقال يا رب اجعل حسابهم إلي لئلا يطلع على مساويهم غيري فأوحى الله تعالى إليه هم أمتك وهم عبادي وأنا أرحم بهم منك ولا أجعل حسابهم إلى غيري لئلا تنظر إلى مساويهم أنت ولا غيرك (4) وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم حياتي خير لكم وموتي خيرك لكم أما حياتي فأسن لكم السنن وأشرع لكم الشرائ
66:8.english: So it was said to him: "And what is in it of hope?" He said: "This world, all of it, is little, and a man's provision from it is little, and his religion is little in comparison to his provision. So look at how God Most High sent down in it the longest verse, to guide His servant to the path of caution in preserving his wealth — so how could He not preserve his religion, which has no substitute for him?"
66:8.section_title_en: The Book of Hope (Kitāb al-Rajā') — Section 1033: The Second Art — Surveying the Verses and Reports Concerning Hope
66:8.anchors:
- Root: وجود (w-j-d)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of "finding" and "existence"; here in the sense of what is present and available.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Existence as that which is found and realized; in theological context, the given order of creation.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) sense of "being found"; metaphorical (majāz) extension to the entirety of created things.
- Root: رجا (r-j-w)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To hope, to expect with desire; the opposite of despair (ya's).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Hope as a theological virtue — the heart's expectation of divine mercy, balanced against fear (khawf).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: expectation of a desired outcome; metaphorical: the soul's reliance on divine generosity.
- Root: غفر (gh-f-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To cover, to shield, to pardon; the root implies veiling the fault.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Divine forgiveness as the covering of sins and the effacing of their consequence.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: covering; metaphorical: God's remission of punishment.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — used to emphasize exclusive attributes of divine mercy and forgiveness.
66:8.topic: Al-Ghazali on the journey of the soul, death, and the Hereafter, from 'Fear and Hope'

109:1.arabic: بأن يصلي ركعتين يقرأ في الأولى فاتحة الكتاب وقل يا أيها الكافرون وفي الثانية الفاتحة وقل هو الله أحد فإذا فرغ دعا وقال اللهم إني أستخيرك بعلمك وأستقدرك بقدرتك وأسألك من فضلك العظيم فإنك تقدر ولا أقدر وتعلم ولا أعلم وأنت علام الغيوب اللهم إن كنت تعلم أن هذا الأمر خير لي في ديني ودنياي وعاقبة أمري وعاجله وآجله فاقدره لي وبارك لي فيه ثم يسره لي وإن كنت تعلم أن هذا الأمر شر لي في ديني ودنياي وعاقبة أمري وعاجله وآجله فاصرفني عنه واصرفه عني واقدر لي الخير أينما كان إنك على كل شيء قدير (6) رواه جابر بن عبد الله قال ك

- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد (Restriction & Focused Predication) — The conditional constructions (idhā... fa...) governing the temporal and circumstantial clauses for when these prayers become incumbent or recommended

109:1.arabic: وفي الصبح في السفر قل يا أيها الكافرون وقل هو الله أحد وكذلك في ركعتي الفجر والطواف والتحية وهو في جميع ذلك مستديم للقيام ووضع اليدين كما وصفنا في أول الصلاة الركوع ولواحقه ثم يركع ويراعي فيه أمورا وهو أن يكبر للركوع وأن يرفع يديه مع تكبيرة الركوع وأن يمد التكبير مدا إلى الانتهاء إلى الركوع وأن يضع راحتيه على ركبتيه في الركوع وأصابعه منشورة موجهة نحو القبلة على طول الساق وأن ينصب ركبتيه ولا يثنيهما وأن يمد ظهره مستويا وأن يكون عنقه ورأسه مستويين مع ظهره كالصفيحة الواحدة ل
109:1.english: I say: Then the worshipper begins with the opening supplication (duʿāʾ al-istiftāḥ). It is excellent that he say, following his utterance of "Allāhu akbar, Allāhu akbar": "Kabīran wa-l-ḥamdu lillāhi kathīran wa-subḥāna Allāhi bukratan wa-aṣīlā" (Great indeed is Allah, and abundant praise be to Allah, and glory be to Allah morning and evening) {«الله أكبر كبيرا والحمد لله كثيرا وسبحان الله بكرة وأصيلا»} — then: "Wajjahtu wajhiya..." (I have turned my face...) up to his saying "...wa-anā min al-muslimīn" (and I am among those who submit) {«وجهت وجهي إلى قوله وأنا من المسلمين»}. Then he says: "Subḥānaka Allāhumma wa-bi-ḥamdika wa-tabāraka-smuka wa-taʿālā jadduka wa-jalla thanāʾuka wa-lā ilāha ghayruk" (Glory be to You, O Allah, and with Your praise; blessed is Your Name and exalted is Your majesty; glorious is Your praise and there is no god but You) {«سبحانك اللهم وبحمدك وتبارك اسمك وتعالى جدك وجل ثناؤك ولا إله غيرك»} — so that he may combine within himself the various dispersed reports transmitted in the traditions.
109:1.section_title_en: Section 127 — On the Recitation (Qirāʾah) and the Bowing (Rukūʿ) with Its Attendant Matters
109:1.anchors:
- Root: قرأ (Qaraʾa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of gathering and assembling letters into articulated speech; recitation as the oral articulation of written or memorized text.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In the Quranic and liturgical context, qirāʾah is the deliberate, worshipful utterance of the divine word, distinct from mere reading; it is an act of devotion requiring presence of heart.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) usage denotes the physical articulation of sounds; metaphorical (majāz) usage extends to the inward recitation of the heart in contemplation.
- Root: ركع (Rakaʿa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The physical act of bowing; the bending of the back in humility.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الركوع: الانحناء، فتارة يستعمل في الهيئة المخصوصة في الصلاة كما هي، وتارة في التواضع والتذلل" — The bowing is an inclination, used sometimes for the specific posture in prayer, and sometimes for humility and self-abasement.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): "شيخ راكع: منحن من الكبر" — an old man bowed with age. Metaphorical (majāz): "لغبت الإبل حتى ركعت" — camels fatigued until they lowered their heads, indicating the physical posture as the outward sign of inward submission.
- Root: صبح (Ṣabaḥa)
  * Al-Raghib (Al-Mufradat): "الصبح والصباح، أول النهار" — the dawn is the beginning of the day, the time when the horizon reddens.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas - Majaz/Metaphorical): "أصبح يا رجل: انتبه من غفلتك" — "become awake, O man: awaken from your heedlessness," showing the dawn prayer as the time of spiritual awakening.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Prepositional Interposition (باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور) — governing the permissible separation between governing and governed elements, applied here to the proper pausing (waqf) and connecting (waṣl) of Quranic phrases to preserve meaning.
109:1.topic: Al-Ghazali on constant remembrance of God and contemplative invocations, from 'Mysteries of Hajj'

3:195.arabic: سأل عنهالحديث وإسنادهما جيد وفي هذا أنه كان لا يسأل عما أتي به من عند أهله والله أعلم // وإنما الواجب أن ينظر التاجر إلى من يعامله فكل منسوب إلى ظلم أو خيانة أو سرقة أو ربا فلا يعامله وكذا الأجناد والظلمة لا يعاملهم البتة ولا يعامل أصحابهم وأعوانهم لأنه معين بذلك على الظلم وحكي عن رجل أنه تولى عمارة سور لثغر من الثغور قال فوقع في نفسي من ذلك شيء وإن كان ذلك العمل من الخيرات بل من فرائض الإسلام ولكن كان الأمير الذي تولى في محلته من الظلمة قال فسألت سفيان رضي الله عنه فقال لا تكن عونا لهم على قليل ولا كثير فقلت ه
3:195.english: The fifth [etiquette] is that he should not be intensely eager for the marketplace and trade — that is, he should not be the first to enter nor the last to leave, nor should he voyage by sea for trade, for both of these are disliked (makrūh). It is said: "Whoever voyages by sea has been excessive in seeking provision."
3:195.section_title_en: The Book of Earning and Livelihood — Section 334: On the Etiquettes of the Trader (Continued)
3:195.anchors:
- Root: حرص (ḥaraṣa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: [Core linguistic root meaning] — Intense, covetous desire; eager clinging to something.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): [Theological/Kalam semantic nuance] — Blameworthy eagerness that distracts the heart from God; opposed to qanāʿah (contentment).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): [Literal vs Metaphorical distinction] — Literal: physical greed for provision. Metaphorical: the soul's excessive attachment to worldly gain.
- Root: شبه (shub'hah)
  * Lisan / Ayn: [Core linguistic root meaning] — Ambiguity; resemblance between truth and falsehood.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): [Theological/Kalam semantic nuance] — Matters whose legal status is uncertain; the pious abstain from them to safeguard their religion.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): [Literal vs Metaphorical distinction] — Literal: visual resemblance. Metaphorical: doubtful matters that resemble the permissible but are tainted with the forbidden.
- Root: عون (ʿawn)
  * Lisan / Ayn: [Core linguistic root meaning] — Assistance; aid in carrying a burden.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): [Theological/Kalam semantic nuance] — Complicity in sin; assisting the oppressor is itself an act of oppression.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): [Literal vs Metaphorical distinction] — Literal: physical help. Metaphorical: any act that enables or emboldens wrongdoing.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — The text uses restrictive constructions to emphasize that the trader's obligation is limited to dealing with the just, and that the pious are fewer in number than those to be avoided.
3:195.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'Etiquette of Earning'

5:32.arabic: وقيل فكأنما قتل الناس جميعا وعن علي رضي الله عنه من احتكر الطعام أربعين يوما قسا قلبه وعنه أيضا أنه أحرق طعام محتكر بالنار وروي في فضل ترك الاحتكار عنه صلى الله عليه وسلم من جلب طعاما فباعه بسعر يومه فكأنما تصدق به وفي لفظ آخر فكأنما أعتق رقبة (1) وقيل في قوله تعالى {ومن يرد فيه بإلحاد بظلم نذقه من عذاب أليم} إن الاحتكار من الظلم وداخل تحته في الوعيد وعن بعض السلف أنه كان بواسط فجهز سفينة حنطة إلى البصرة وكتب إلى وكيله بع هذا الطعام يوم يدخل البصرة ولا تؤخره
5:32.english: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: «من احتكر الطعام أربعين يوما ثم تصدق به لم تكن صدقته كفارة لاحتكاره» — "Whoever hoards food for forty days and then gives it in charity, his charity shall not be an expiation for his hoarding."
5:32.section_title_en: The First Type: Hoarding (Iḥtikār) — Its Prohibition, Degrees, and Juristic Nuances
5:32.anchors:
- Root: حكر (ḥ-k-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of withholding, storing, and monopolizing goods awaiting price inflation.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance — hoarding is an act of harm (ḍarar) against the community, tied to greed and distrust of divine provision.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) — physical retention of foodstuffs; Metaphorical (majāz) — hoarding as a spiritual disease of the heart, as in the report of ʿAlī that the hoarder's heart hardens.
- Root: ضرر (ḍ-r-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Harm, injury, distress — both physical and moral.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Ḍarar as the operative criterion (ʿillah) for prohibition; its absence or presence determines the ruling's gradation.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — tangible injury to others; Metaphorical — the anticipation of harm (intiẓār mabādiʾ al-ḍarar) treated as equivalent in moral weight to the harm itself.
- Root: قوت (q-w-t)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Sustenance, staple food — that which maintains life.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Qūt as the fundamental necessity (qiwām) for which creation was sustained; trading in it is disfavored because it seeks profit in essentials.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — grains and staples; Metaphorical — anything that "stands in the place" (yasuddu masaddan) of sustenance, extending the ruling analogically.
- Sibawayh Rule: Taʿlīq al-ḥukm bi-al-ʿillah (Attribution of Ruling to Cause) — The prohibition is anchored to the presence of ḍarar, not to the mere act of storage, allowing graded application across time and genus.
5:32.topic: Al-Ghazali on the journey of the soul, death, and the Hereafter, from 'Etiquette of Earning'

7:10.arabic: وقال تعالى وجعلنا لكم فيها معايش قليلا ما تشكرون فجعلها ربك نعمة وطلب الشكر عليها وقال تعالى ليس عليكم جناح أن تبتغوا فضلا من ربكم وقال تعالى وآخرون يضربون في الأرض يبتغون من فضل الله وقال تعالى فانتشروا في الأرض وابتغوا من فضل الله وأما الأخبار فقد قال صلى الله عليه وسلم من الذنوب ذنوب لا يكفرها إلا الهم في طلب المعيشة (1) وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم التاجر الصدوق يحشر يوم القيامة مع الصديقين والشهداء (2) وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم من طلب الدنيا حلالا وتعففا عن المسئلة وسعيا على عياله وتعطفا
7:10.english: As for what is [cited] from the Book [i.e., the Qur'an], there is His saying, the Exalted: «{وَجَعَلْنَا النَّهَارَ مَعَاشًا}» ("And We have made the day a means of livelihood" [al-Naba' 78:11]) — and He mentioned it in the context of bestowing favor (imtinān).
7:10.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Etiquette of Earning'

7:56.arabic: والإحسان وقال سبحانه إن رحمت الله قريب من المحسنين ونعني بالإحسان فعل ما ينتفع به المعامل وهو غير واجب عليه ولكنه تفضل منه فإن الواجب يدخل في باب العدل وترك الظلم وقد ذكرناه وتنال رتبة الإحسان بواحد من ستة أمور الأول في المغابنة فينبغي أن لا يغبن صاحبه بما لا يتغابن به في العادة فأما أصل المغابنة فمأذون فيه لأن البيع للربح ولا يمكن ذلك إلا بغبن ما ولكن يراعي فيه التقريب فإن بذل المشتري زيادة على الربح المعتاد إما لشدة رغبته أو لشدة حاجته في الحال إليه فينبغي أن يمتنع من قبوله فذلك من الإح
7:56.english: God (Exalted is He) has commanded both justice (al-ʿadl) and excellence (al-iḥsān) together. Justice is only the cause of deliverance (al-najāh), and it runs in trade as the course of capital (raʾs al-māl). Excellence is the cause of triumph (al-fawz) and the attainment of felicity (al-saʿādah), and it runs in trade as the course of profit (al-ribḥ). None is counted among the heedless who is content in his worldly transactions with merely his capital — and so likewise in the transactions of the Hereafter. Thus it behooves the religious person not to restrict himself to justice and the avoidance of wrongdoing (ẓulm), abandoning the doors of excellence. God has said: {«وَأَحْسِنْ كَمَا أَحْسَنَ اللَّهُ إِلَيْكَ»} ("And do good as God has done good to you") {«إِنَّ اللَّهَ يَأْمُرُ بِالْعَدْلِ وَالْإِحْسَانِ»} ("Indeed, God commands justice and excellence"), and He (Exalted is He) has said: {«إِنَّ رَحْمَتَ اللَّهِ قَرِيبٌ مِنَ الْمُحْسِنِينَ»} ("Indeed, the mercy of God is near to the doers of excellence").
7:56.section_title_en: Chapter Four: On Excellence (Iḥsān) in Transactional Dealings
7:56.anchors:
- Root: ع د ل (ʿadala)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of equality, straightness, and balance; the root denotes that which is level and even, without crookedness or deviation.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "العدالة والمعادلة: لفظ يقتضي معنى المساواة" — justice is that which is perceived by inner insight (al-baṣīrah), pertaining to judgments and rulings; it is the equitable apportioning of things on an even scale.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) usage pertains to physical evenness and moderation (e.g., a horse with an even blaze); metaphorical (majāz) extension applies to moral and legal equity.
- Root: ر ب ح (rabiḥa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Gain, profit, increase in trade; the root signifies surplus and augmentation.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الربح: الزيادة الحاصلة في المبايعة، ثم يتجوز به في كل ما يعود من ثمرة عمل" — profit is the increase occurring in exchange, then metaphorically extended to every fruit that returns from a deed.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal usage in commerce; metaphorical usage: "تجارة رابحة" — a profitable transaction, extended to spiritual commerce.
- Root: و ق د (waqada)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Fire blazing and burning fiercely; kindling.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Fire that burns; used in the Qur'an for the fuel of Hellfire.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: fire blazing; Metaphorical: "قلب وقاد" — a blazing, keen intellect; "وقدة الصيف" — the intense heat of summer.
- Sibawayh Rule: Chapter on the Interposition between the Preposition and its Object (Bāb al-Faṣl bayn al-Jār wa al-Majrūr) — governing the permissible separation between grammatical operators and their operands for rhetorical emphasis, as in the periodic construction of conditional and exceptive clauses.
7:56.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Etiquette of Earning'

7:56.arabic: اقتصر ذكر شرطا جامعا فقال تعالى إن رحمة الله قريب من المحسنين فالإحسان يجمع الكل وهكذا من يتصفح القرآن من أوله إلى آخره ومن فهم ذلك فجدير بأن يكون حاله الخشية والحزن ولذلك قال الحسن والله ما أصبح اليوم عبد يتلو القرآن يؤمن به إلا كثر حزنه وقل فرحه وكثر بكاؤه وقل ضحكه وكثر نصبه وشغله وقلت راحته وبطالته وقال وهيب بن الورد نظرنا في هذه الأحاديث والمواعظ فلم نجد شيئا أرق للقلوب ولا أشد استجلابا للحزن من قراءة القرآن وتفهمه وتدبره فتأثر العبد بالتلاوة أن يصير بصفة الآية المتلوة فعند الوعيد وتقييد المغفرة بالشر
7:56.english:
[Root: ذكر]
  • Al-Raghib (Al-Mufradat): "الذكر: حضور الشيء القلب أو القول، ويكون تارة بالقلب وتارة باللسان، والذكر باللسان تارة يكون حضور المعنى وبعده، وقد يقال: ذكرته إذا جرى على لسانه وإن لم يحضره قلبه، والذكر بالقلب هو حضور المعنى، قال تعالى: ولا تطع من أغفلنا قلبه عن ذكرنا [الكهف/ 28]"
  • Al-Zamakhshari (Asas - Haqiqah/Literal): "ذكرت الشيء: نطقت به أو استحضرته بقلبك. وذكرت فلانا بخير وشر. واذكروا الله ذكرا كثيرا. والذكر: الشرف والصيت، قال تعالى: وإنه لذكر لك ولقومك [الزخرف/ 44]"
  • Al-Zamakhshari (Asas - Majaz/Metaphorical): "الذكر: الكتاب الذي فيه تذكير الناس، قال تعالى: وأنزلنا إليك الذكر لتبين للناس ما نزل إليهم [النحل/ 44]، والذكر: القرآن، قال تعالى: إنا نحن نزلنا الذكر وإنا له لحافظون [الحجر/ 9]"
7:56.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Etiquette of Quran Recitation'

15:98.arabic: التاجرين ولكن أوحي إلي أن سبح بحمد ربك وكن من الساجدين واعبد ربك حتى يأتيك اليقين (3) وقيل لسلمان الفارسي أوصنا فقال من استطاع منكم أن يموت حاجا أو غازيا أو عامرا لمسجد ربه فليفعل ولا يموتن تاجرا ولا خائنا فالجواب أن وجه الجمع بين هذه الأخبار تفصيل الأحوال فنقول لسنا نقول التجارة أفضل مطلقا من كل شيء ولكن التجارة إما أن تطلب بها الكفاية أو الثروة أو الزيادة على الكفاية فإن طلب منها الزيادة على الكفاية لاستكثار المال وادخاره لا ليصرف إلى الخيرات والصدقات فهي مذمومة لأنه إقبال على الدنيا التي حبها رأس كل خطيئة فإن كان مع ذلك
15:98.english: Ibn Masʿūd, may God be pleased with him, said: "Truly I dislike seeing a man idle, neither in the affair of his worldly life nor in the affair of his Hereafter."
15:98.section_title_en: The Virtue of Earning and Trade — Section 313 of the Revival of the Religious Sciences
15:98.anchors:
- Root: كسب (Kasaba)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الكسب: طلب الرزق" — earning is the seeking of provision; the root denotes acquisition through effort and endeavor.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الكسب: ما يتحراه الإنسان مما فيه اجتلاب نفع" — earning is what a man pursues in order to draw benefit; distinguished from iktisāb, which is specifically what one acquires for oneself alone.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): "رجل كسوب للمال وكساب" — a man habitually earning wealth. Metaphorical (Majaz): "كسبت خيرا واكتسبت شرا" — earning good (for oneself and others) vs. acquiring evil (for oneself alone), per the Quranic distinction {«لها ما كسبت وعليها ما اكتسبت»}.
- Root: طلب (Talaba)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Seeking, searching out; "الطلب: الفحص عن وجود الشيء" — the examination and pursuit of a thing's existence.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الطلب: الفحص عن وجود الشيء، عينا كان أو معنى" — seeking applies to both corporeal and meaningful objects; "أطلبت فلانا: إذا أسعفته لما طلب" — to satisfy another's request.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "طلب الشيء طلبا ومطلبا وطلابا" — to seek with intensity. Metaphorical: "السراج يطلب أن ينطفيء" — the lamp "seeks" to go out, i.e., is disposed toward it; thus the bird "seeks" provision by divine disposition.
- Root: تجر (Tajara)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Commerce, trade; "سُوقاً ذاتَ رِبْحٍ" — a market of profit.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "التجارة: التصرف في رأس المال طلبا للربح" — the management of capital seeking profit; Quranically extended to faith: {«هل أدلكم على تجارة تنجيكم من عذاب أليم»}.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "فلان يتجر في البز" — trading in cloth. Metaphorical: "عليكم بتجارة الآخرة" — the commerce of the Hereafter; "ناقة تاجرة: حسنة نافقة" — a camel that is marketable and in demand, applied metaphorically to that which has currency and value.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction and Focused Predication) — The particle innamā restricts the predicate to the subject alone, negating all else. Applied here to the Prophet's statement {«وكن من الساجدين»} — the command to worship is restricted to him as a unique station, not a universal negation of trade; likewise, the conditional structure (law/fa-in) governs the nuanced rulings on when earning is praiseworthy versus blameworthy.
15:98.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Etiquette of Earning'

22:73.arabic: وأن كل من في السموات والأرض لن يخلقوا ذبابا ولو اجتمعوا له ولا فراشا ونشكره إذ رفع السماء لعباده سقفا مبنيا ومهد الأرض بساطا لهم وفراشا وكور الليل على النهار فجعل الليل لباسا والنهار معاشا لينتشروا في إبتغاء فضله وينتعشوا به عن ضراعة الحاجات انتعاشا ونصلي على رسوله الذي يصدر المؤمنون عن حوضه رواء بعد ورودهم عليه عطاشا وعلى آله وأصحابه الذين لم يدعوا في نصرة دينه تشمرا وانكماشا وسلم تسليما كثيرا أما بعد فإن رب الأرباب ومسبب الأسباب جعل الآخرة دار الثواب والعقاب والدنيا دار التمحل والاضطراب والتشمر
22:73.english: It is related from Muʿādh ibn Jabal, who said: The Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "No woman harms her husband in this world but that his wife from the ḥūr al-ʿīn says to her: 'May God slay you! Do not harm him — for he is only a sojourner (dakhīl) with you; soon he shall part from you and come to us.'"
22:73.section_title_en: The Book of the Etiquette of Earning and Livelihood — Introduction and Chapter Divisions
22:73.anchors:
- Root: زوج (z-w-j)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Pairing, coupling; each of the two members of a pair — whether male/female in animals, or two matched things like sandals; "زوجة" is a weak (radī'ah) dialectal form.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Every one of two paired things — in animals, the male and female; in other things, any two that are paired, similar or opposite. From this: the wife is called "zawj" for the husband, and he "zawj" for her.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (haqīqah): "He is her zawj and she is his zawj or zawjah; the two are zawjān." Metaphorical (majāz): "The two discourses paired (tazāwajā) and were coupled (izdawajā)."
- Root: رسل (r-s-l)
  * Lisan / Ayn: A small creature; "Umm risālah": the carrion kite. The root conveys sending forth with gentleness and ease.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The origin of "risl" is emission with leisurely ease — a she-camel that is "raslah" is easy-paced. From this, the messenger (rasūl) is one sent forth; and from the sense of gentleness comes "on your leisure" (alā rislik).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: sending a message, dispatching messengers, releasing a stallion among camels, loosing a dog or falcon upon game. Metaphorical: "God loosed (arsala) chastisement upon them"; "the arrows are the messengers (rusul) of deathly fates."
- Root: داب (d-'-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To persist and toil; "al-dābbatān" (the two toiling ones) is said of night and day in their ceaseless alternation.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Da'b" is the continuance of journeying — "and He subjected the sun and moon to you, both persisting (dā'ibayn)" {«وَسَخَّرَ لَكُمُ الشَّمْسَ وَالْقَمَرَ دَائِبَيْنِ»}; and "da'b" is the habitual custom one persists upon — "like the custom (ka-da'bi) of the house of Pharaoh."
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: to strive diligently in work, to toil in travel. Metaphorical: "This is your da'b" — i.e., your constant concern and occupation; "night and day toil (yad'abān) in their mutual succession."
- Root: الي ('-l-k)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "Al-alak" and "al-ālūk": the chewing and working of the bit in a horse's mouth.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-Khalīl said: "al-ma'lakah" (the message/angelic mission) is the conveying of a message, because it is "worked in the mouth" (tu'lak fī al-fam) — from their saying of a horse: "it works (ya'lik) the bit," i.e., chews it. The angels are called "malā'ikah" because they convey messages.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد (Restriction & Specification) — The particle "innamā" restricts the predicate to the subject alone, negating any extension beyond it. Applied here to the wife's mourning obligation: "she must not mourn (lā taḥidd) over any dead person more than three days — except over a husband, four months and ten days," where the exception clause (istithnā') delimits the general prohibition.

24:36.arabic: وإيتاء الزكاة وقال الله تعالى في بيوت أذن الله أن ترفع ويذكر فيها اسمه فينبغي أن يجعل أول النهار إلى وقت دخول السوق لآخرته فيلازم المسجد ويواظب على الأوراد كان عمر رضي الله عنه يقول للتجار اجعلوا أول نهاركم لآخرتكم وما بعده لدنياكم وكان صالحو السلف يجعلون أول النهار وآخره للآخرة والوسط للتجارة ولم يكن يبيع الهريسة والرءوس بكرة إلا الصبيان وأهل الذمة لأنهم كانوا في المساجد بعد وفي الخبر إن الملائكة إذا صعدت بصحيفة العبد وفيها في أول النهار وفي آخره ذكر الله وخير كفر الله عنهما ما بينهما من سيئ الأعمال (1) و
24:36.english: Some of the Salaf (may God be pleased with them) said: "The thing most worthy of the intelligent man is that which he most needs in the immediate term; and the thing he most needs in the immediate term is that whose consequence is most praiseworthy in the long term."
24:36.section_title_en: On the Merchant's Vigilance Over His Religion: Seven Matters of Concern in Trade
24:36.anchors:
- Root: دنا (d-n-w)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Proximity, nearness in place, time, or rank; the nearer (adnā) as opposed to the farther.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الدنو: القرب بالذات، أو بالحكم" — nearness by essence or by judgment; used of place, time, and station. The "nearer life" (al-ḥayāh al-dunyā) is the proximate, lower life.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical nearness. Metaphorical: the worldly life (al-dunyā) as that which is "nearer" and lower, contrasted with the Hereafter (al-ākhirah) which is "farther" but enduring.
- Root: سوق (s-w-q)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To drive, to impel, to lead; a market (sūq) where goods are driven and circulated.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The driving of one's self toward a goal; the market as the arena of exchange and transaction.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "ساق النعم فانساقت" — he drove the cattle and they were driven. Metaphorical: "ساق الله إليه خيرا" — God drove good to him; "ساق إليها المهر" — he sent the dowry to her. The "market of the Hereafter" (sūq al-ākhirah) is the mosque, where one trades deeds for the next life.
- Root: جار (j-w-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To deviate from the right path, to wrong, to oppress; also a neighbor (jār) whose rights are sacred.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الجار: من يقرب مسكنه منك" — the neighbor is one whose dwelling is near yours; a reciprocal term. God's right and the neighbor's right are conjoined in the Qur'anic verse {والجار ذي القربى والجار الجنب} (Al-Nisā': 36).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: oppression and transgression. Metaphorical: the "oppressive oath" (yamīn fājirah) — an oath that swerves from truth and justice.
- Root: الي (a-l-w)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To fall short, to fail; also related to رسالة (message) via مألكة.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The root conveys the idea of commission and conveyance of a message; "المألكة: الرسالة" — the message, because it is "chewed" in the mouth (from ألك, to masticate).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: to chew. Metaphorical: the angelic conveyance of revelation as a "message" delivered.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — When the author says "وإنما تتم شفقة التاجر على دينه بمراعاة سبعة أمور" ("The merchant's compassion for his religion is only completed by observing seven matters"), the particle إنما restricts and confines the predicate to the subject, establishing that these seven matters are the exclusive and exhaustive means to the end.
24:36.topic: Al-Ghazali on constant remembrance of God and contemplative invocations, from 'Etiquette of Earning'

36:12.arabic: ويسئل عنها إلى آخر انقراضها وقال تعالى {ونكتب ما قدموا وآثارهم} أي نكتب أيضا ما أخروه من آثار أعمالهم كما نكتب ما قدموه وفي مثله قوله تعالى {ينبأ الإنسان يومئذ بما قدم وأخر} وإنما أخر آثار أعماله من سنة سيئة عمل بها غيره وليعلم أن في الزيف خمسة أمور الأول أنه إذا رد عليه شيء منه فينبغي أن يطرحه في بئر بحيث لا تمتد إليه اليد وإياه أن يروجه في بيع آخر وإن أفسده بحيث لا يمكن التعامل به جاز الثاني أنه يجب على التاجر تعلم النقد لا ليستقصي لنفسه ولكن لئلا يسلم إلى مسلم زيفا وهو لا يدري فيكون آثما بتقصيره في تعل
36:12.english: Know that the circulation of counterfeit coinage (*al-zuyūf*) during the course of payment is an injustice (*ẓulm*), for the one who transacts with it is harmed thereby — if he does not recognize it [as counterfeit], he is injured; and if he does recognize it, he will circulate it to another. And so likewise with the third and the fourth [recipient]. It continues to pass from hand to hand, the harm becomes general, the corruption spreads widely, and the burden (*wizr*) of all of it and its evil consequence reverts upon him [the originator] — for he it is who opened this door. The Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, said: {«مَنْ سَنَّ سُنَّةً سَيِّئَةً فَعُمِلَ بِهَا مِنْ بَعْدِهِ كَانَ عَلَيْهِ وِزْرُهَا وَمِثْلُ وِزْرِ مَنْ عَمِلَ بِهَا لَا يَنْقُصُ مِنْ أَوْزَارِهِمْ شَيْئًا»} ("Whoever institutes an evil practice and it is acted upon after him, upon him is its burden and the like of the burden of those who act upon it, without diminishing anything from their burdens.")
36:12.section_title_en: Section 324 — On the Circulation of Counterfeit Coinage and Its Grave Consequences
36:12.anchors:
- **Root: زيف (z-y-f)**
  * *Lisan / Ayn*: Core meaning of falsification, adulteration, and counterfeiting — that which is false in its substance, not merely in its claim.
  * *Al-Raghib (Mufradat)*: The theological dimension concerns the *spreading of corruption* (ifsād) through deceptive transactions — a form of *ẓulm* (injustice) that multiplies as the counterfeit passes from hand to hand.
  * *Al-Zamakhshari (Asas)*: Literal (*ḥaqīqah*): false coinage. Metaphorical (*majāz*): the *sunnah sayyiʾah* (evil precedent) — the one who originates it bears its burden and the burden of those who follow it.

- **Root: وزر (w-z-r)**
  * *Lisan / Ayn*: The heavy burden (*al-wizr*), the load one carries; also the mountain refuge. The *wāzir* is the bearer of the burden.
  * *Al-Raghib (Mufradat)*: Used for sin (*ithm*) as a heavy burden upon the soul. The one who originates an evil practice carries his own burden and the burdens of those who follow him — as in {«وَلَيَحْمِلُنَّ أَثْقَالَهُمْ وَأَثْقَالًا مَّعَ أَثْقَالِهِمْ»} (Al-ʿAnkabūt: 13).
  * *Al-Zamakhshari (Asas)*: Literal: carrying a physical load. Metaphorical: bearing the weight of sin — "he is *mawzūr*, not *maʾjūr*" (burdened with sin, not rewarded).

- **Root: سنن (s-n-n)**
  * *Lisan / Ayn*: The path or way (*al-ṭarīqah*); to institute a practice or precedent.
  * *Al-Raghib (Mufradat)*: *Sunnah* as the established pattern — whether good or evil. The Prophet ﷺ said: "Whoever institutes a good sunnah..." and "Whoever institutes an evil sunnah..."
  * *Al-Zamakhshari (Asas)*: Literal: the beaten path. Metaphorical: the moral precedent that others follow — its originator is accountable for all who walk it after him.

- **Sibawayh Rule**: *Bāb al-ḥaṣr wa al-taqyīd bi-innamā* (Restriction and Focused Predication) — used in the phrase "إنما يتخلص من إثم الضرر الذي يخص معامله فقط" to restrict the scope of absolution to the specific harm done to one's immediate transactor, not the general harm propagated through subsequent circulation.

62:10.arabic: قال أنس بن مالك في قوله تعالى فإذا قضيت الصلاة فانتشروا في الأرض وابتغوا من فضل الله أما إنه ليس بطلب دنيا لكن عيادة مريض وشهود جنازة وتعلم علم وزيارة أخ في الله عز وجل وقد سمى الله عز وجل العلم فضلا في مواضع قال تعالى وعلمك ما لم تكن تعلم وكان فضل الله عليك عظيما وقال تعالى ولقد آتينا داود منا فضلا يعني العلم فتعلم العلم في هذا اليوم وتعليمه من أفضل القربات والصلاة أفضل من مجالس القصاص إذ كانوا يرونه بدعة ويخرجون القصاص من الجامع بكر ابن عمر رضي الله عنهما إلى مجلسه في المسجد الجامع فإذا قاص في موضعه فقال قم عن مجلسي فقال لا
62:10.english: Know that the one who attends the Friday prayer should remain in the mosque until he prays the afternoon prayer (al-ʿaṣr); and if he remains until the sunset prayer (al-maghrib), that is even more excellent. It is said: "Whoever prays the afternoon prayer in the congregational mosque (al-jāmiʿ) shall have the reward of the Pilgrimage (ḥajj); and whoever prays the sunset prayer therein shall have the reward of a Pilgrimage and an ʿUmra." However, if he does not feel secure from ostentation (al-taṣabbuʿ) and from harm befalling him through the gaze of people upon his seclusion (iʿtikāf), or he fears plunging into what does not concern him, then it is more excellent that he return to his house, remembering Allah (mighty and majestic), reflecting upon His graces (ālāʾihi), thanking Allah the Exalted for His granting of success (tawfīq), fearing his own shortcoming, and watching over his heart and his tongue until the setting of the sun — so that the noble hour (al-sāʿa al-sharīfa) does not pass him by. Nor should he speak in the congregational mosque or in other mosques about the affairs of this world. The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) said: {«يَأْتِي عَلَى النَّاسِ زَمَانٌ يَكُونُ حَدِيثُهُمْ فِي مَسَاجِدِهِمْ أَمْرَ دُنْيَاهُمْ لَيْسَ لِلَّهِ تَعَالَى فِيهِمْ حَاجَةٌ فَلَا تُجَالِسُوهُمْ»} — "A time will come upon people when their conversation in their mosques will be about their worldly affairs; Allah the Exalted has no need of them, so do not sit with them." (1)

83:1.arabic: الكيل فينبغي أن يكيل كما يكتال قال الله تعالى ويل للمطففين الذين إذا اكتالوا على الناس يستوفون وإذا كالوهم أو وزنوهم يخسرون ولا يخلص من هذا إلا بأن يرجع إذا أعطى وينقص إذا أخذ إذ العدل الحقيقي قلما يتصور فليستظهر بظهور الزيادة والنقصان فإن من استقصى حقه بكماله يوشك أن يتعداه وكان بعضهم يقول لا أشتري الويل من الله بحبة فكان إذا أخذ نقص نصف حبة وإذا أعطى زاد حبة وكان يقول ويل لمن باع بحبة جنة عرضها السموات والأرض وما أخسر من باع طوبى بويل وإنما بالغوا في الاحتراز من هذا وشبهه لأنها مظالم لا يمكن التوبة منها إذ لا يعرف أصحاب الحبات حتى يجمعهم ويؤدى حقوقهم ولذلك لما اشت
83:1.english: One of the scholars said: "Whoever sells his brother a commodity for a dirham, while it would not be suitable for him, had he purchased it for himself, except for five dānaqs (six-tenths of a dirham) — then he has abandoned the sincere counsel (al-nuṣḥ) commanded in transactions, and has not loved for his brother what he loves for himself."
83:1.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Etiquette of Earning'

2:62.arabic: يفزع الناس يوم القيامة ولا يفزعون وهم أولياء الله الذين لا خوف عليهم ولا هم يحزنون وفيه شهر بن حوشب مختلف فيه // ورواه أبو هريرة رضي الله عنه وقال فيه إن حول العرش منابر من نور عليها قوم لباسهم نور ووجوههم نورا ليسوا بأنبياء ولا شهداء يغبطهم النبيون والشهداء فقالوا يا رسول الله صفهم لنا فقال هم المتحابون في الله والمتجالسون في الله والمتزاورون في الله (1) وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم ما تحاب اثنان في الله إلا كان أحبهما إلى الله أشدهما حبا لصاحبه (2) ويقال إن الأخوين في الله إذا كان أحدهما أعلى مقاما من الآخر
2:62.english: Know that affability (al-ulfah) is the fruit of excellent character (ḥusn al-khuluq), and estrangement (al-tafarruq) is the fruit of evil character. For excellent character necessitates mutual love, harmony, and concord, whereas evil character yields mutual hatred, envy, and turning away (al-tadābur). And whenever the source is praiseworthy, the fruit is likewise praiseworthy. The excellence of good character is not hidden in the religion; indeed, it is that with which God—glorified be He—praised His Prophet, peace be upon him, when He said: {وَإِنَّكَ لَعَلَىٰ خُلُقٍ عَظِيمٍ} «And indeed, you are upon an immense character» (Al-Qalam: 4). The Prophet, peace be upon him, said: "The thing which most causes people to enter Paradise is God-consciousness (taqwā) and excellent character." (1) Usāmah ibn Sharīk said: "We said, O Messenger of God, what is the best thing given to a person?" He said: "Excellent character." (2) He, peace be upon him, also said: "I was sent only to perfect the noble traits of character." (3) He, peace be upon him, said: "Nothing is heavier in the Balance than excellent character." (4) He, peace be upon him, said: "God does not beautify a person's outward form and his inward character, then feed him to the Fire." (5) He, peace be upon him, said: "O Abū Hurayrah, adhere to excellent character." (Page V02P157) Abū Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him, said: "What is excellent character, O Messenger of God?" He said: "That you join the one who cuts you off, forgive the one who wrongs you, and give to the one who deprives you." (1)

  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) denotes physical joining; metaphorical (majāz) denotes the spiritual and moral concord of hearts, which is the fruit of excellent character (ḥusn al-khuluq).
- Root: خلق (Khalaqa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Root meaning of measuring, proportioning, and smoothing; hence, the inherent disposition and moral character of a person.

2:62.arabic: الشك في هذا الصدق وكذلك قال الله تعالى ولكن البر من آمن بالله واليوم الآخر والملائكة والكتاب والنبيين فشرط عشرين وصفا كالوفاء بالعهد والصبر على الشدائد ثم قال تعالى أولئك الذين صدقوا وقد قال تعالى يرفع الله الذين آمنوا منكم والذين أوتوا العلم درجات وقال تعالى لا يستوي منكم من أنفق من قبل الفتح وقاتل الآية وقد قال تعالى هم درجات عند الله وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم الإيمان عريان ولباسه التقوى (1) الحديث وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم الإيمان بضع وسبعون بابا أدناها إماطة الأذى عن الطريق فهذا ما يدل على ارتباط كمال الإيمان بالأعمال وأ
2:62.english: ...doubt concerning this truthfulness. Likewise, God Most High said: {«But righteousness is he who believes in God and the Last Day and the angels and the Book and the prophets»} (2:177) — thus He conditioned twenty attributes, such as faithfulness to covenant and patience under hardship. Then He said Most High: {«Those are the truthful ones»} (2:177). And God Most High said: {«God will raise those who have believed among you and those who have been given knowledge, by degrees»} (58:11). And He said Most High: {«Not equal among you are those who spent before the conquest and fought»} (57:10). And He said Most High: {«They are degrees before God»} (3:163). And the Prophet, peace be upon him, said: "Faith is naked, and its garment is God-consciousness (al-taqwā)." And the Prophet, peace be upon him, said: "Faith has seventy-some branches; the lowest of them is removing harm from the path." All this indicates the interconnection of the perfection of faith with works.
2:62.section_title_en: The Revival of the Religious Sciences — Book of the Secrets of Zakāh, Section 104: On the Degrees of Faith and Its Connection to Works, and the Hidden Hypocrisy (al-Nifāq al-Khafī) That Contradicts the Perfection of Faith
2:62.anchors:
- Root: ن ف ق (N-F-Q)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Root denotes passing away, depletion, and expenditure; also the underground burrow of the jerboa (nāfiqāʾ) with a concealed exit — the etymological basis for hypocrisy as a hidden exit from faith.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "نفق الشيء: مضى ونفد" — theological nuance: hypocrisy (nifāq) is that which causes faith to expire and pass away, whether by sale (worldly gain) or by death (spiritual ruin).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "نفقت الدراهم" (coins ran out). Metaphorical: "نفق روحه: خرج" (his soul expired and went forth) — hence the hypocrite's faith is one whose spirit has already departed.
- Root: أ ي م (A-Y-M)
  * Lisan / Ayn: A woman without a husband; a man long unmarried. Al-Raghib: "الحرب مأيمة" — war makes women widows.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "تركوا النساء أيامى" (they left women widowed). Metaphorical application: the one who feels secure from hypocrisy is like one who claims immunity from widowhood — a false security.
- Root: و ف ي (W-F-Y)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Fullness, completion, fulfillment of a measure or covenant.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الوافي: الذي بلغ التمام" — the one who has reached completion. "أوفى: إذا تمم العهد ولم ينقض حفظه" — to fulfill the covenant without breach.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "درهم واف" (a full-weight dirham). Metaphorical: "أوفى على المائة" (he surpassed a hundred) — faith's perfection (wafāʾ) is only attained by surpassing mere profession to include works and inward sincerity.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد (Restriction & Focused Predication) — governing the grammatical force of "إنما" constructions and conditional clauses (من كان...), where the predicate is restricted to the condition stated, as in the hadith "أربع من كن فيه فهو منافق خالص" — the four traits are exhaustive of the ruling.
2:62.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'Monitoring and Accounting'

2:104.arabic: وقد قال الله تعالى يا أيها الذين آمنوا أنفقوا من طيبات ما كسبتم ومما أخرجنا لكم من الأرض ولا تيمموا الخبيث منه تنفقون ولستم بآخذيه إلا أن تغمضوا فيه أي لا تأخذوه إلا مع كراهية وحياء وهو معنى الإغماض فلا تؤثروا به ربكم وفي الخبر سبق درهم مائة ألف درهم (3) وذلك بأن يخرجه الإنسان وهو من أحل ماله وأجوده فيصدر ذلك عن الرضا والفرح بالبذل وقد يخرج مائة ألف درهم مما يكره من ماله فيدل ذلك على أنه ليس يؤثر الله عز وجل بشيء مما يحبه وبذلك ذم الله تعالى قوما جعلوا لله ما يكرهون فقال تعال
2:104.english: The heart is not treated save with the compound electuary (maʿjūn) of knowledge and works. And this condition among the conditions of almsgiving runs in the same course as humility (al-khushūʿ) runs in the prayer. This is established by his saying — may Allah bless him and grant him peace: "A man has nothing of his prayer save that of which he was conscious." And this is like his saying — may Allah bless him and grant him peace: "Allah does not accept the charity of the one who bestows it with reproach (al-mannān)." And like His saying — Exalted is He: {«لا تبطلوا صدقاتكم بالمن والأذى»} ("Do not nullify your charities by reproach and injury"). As for the legal opinion (fatwā) of the jurist that the alms fall in their proper place and that one's liability is discharged without this condition — that is another discussion, and we have already pointed to its meaning in the Book of Prayer.
2:104.section_title_en: The Inner Conditions of Charity — Section 175 (From The Revival of the Religious Sciences, Book of the Mysteries of Almsgiving)
2:104.anchors:
- Root: قلب (q-l-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "To turn, overturn, transform a thing from one state to another; to rotate, to flip"
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "قلب الشيء: تصريفه وصرفه عن وجه إلى وجه" — the heart is so named because of its constant turning and transformation between states
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "قلب الشيء قلبا: حوله عن وجهه" (to turn a thing from its face). Metaphorical: "رجل قلب حول: يقلب الأمور ويحتال" — one who turns matters over and manages them; "قلبوا لك الأمور" (they turned matters against you)
- Root: وجل (w-j-l)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "Fear, dread, apprehension that strikes the heart"
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الوجل: استشعار الخوف" — the sensing of fear; cited in {«إنما المؤمنون الذين إذا ذكر الله وجلت قلوبهم»}
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "رجل وجل، وقوم وجال" — a fearful man, a fearful people; "وفي قلبه وجل" — in his heart is dread
- Root: عجب (ʿ-j-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "Wonder, amazement; self-admiration, vanity"
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Self-admiration (al-ʿujb) is a destructive spiritual ailment that nullifies deeds
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: wonder at something extraordinary. Metaphorical: self-conceit regarding one's own acts of obedience
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد (Restriction & Focused Predication) — governing the precise limitation of general categories (al-ṣifāt al-khāṣṣah within al-aṣnāf al-thamāniyyah) and the conditional structure of acceptance

  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) denotes physical joining; metaphorical (majāz) denotes the spiritual and moral concord of hearts, which is the fruit of excellent character (ḥusn al-khuluq).

  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The origination of a thing upon a just measure; for character, it is the inward form (al-ṣūrah al-bāṭinah) of the soul, just as the physical form is its outward shape.

2:178.arabic: وقد قال الله تعالى يا أيها الذين آمنوا أنفقوا من طيبات ما كسبتم ومما أخرجنا لكم من الأرض ولا تيمموا الخبيث منه تنفقون ولستم بآخذيه إلا أن تغمضوا فيه أي لا تأخذوه إلا مع كراهية وحياء وهو معنى الإغماض فلا تؤثروا به ربكم وفي الخبر سبق درهم مائة ألف درهم (3) وذلك بأن يخرجه الإنسان وهو من أحل ماله وأجوده فيصدر ذلك عن الرضا والفرح بالبذل وقد يخرج مائة ألف درهم مما يكره من ماله فيدل ذلك على أنه ليس يؤثر الله عز وجل بشيء مما يحبه وبذلك ذم الله تعالى قوما جعلوا لله ما يكرهون فقال تعال
2:178.english: The heart is not treated save with the compound electuary (maʿjūn) of knowledge and works. And this condition among the conditions of almsgiving runs in the same course as humility (al-khushūʿ) runs in the prayer. This is established by his saying — may Allah bless him and grant him peace: "A man has nothing of his prayer save that of which he was conscious." And this is like his saying — may Allah bless him and grant him peace: "Allah does not accept the charity of the one who bestows it with reproach (al-mannān)." And like His saying — Exalted is He: {«لا تبطلوا صدقاتكم بالمن والأذى»} ("Do not nullify your charities by reproach and injury"). As for the legal opinion (fatwā) of the jurist that the alms fall in their proper place and that one's liability is discharged without this condition — that is another discussion, and we have already pointed to its meaning in the Book of Prayer.
2:178.section_title_en: The Inner Conditions of Charity — Section 175 (From The Revival of the Religious Sciences, Book of the Mysteries of Almsgiving)
2:178.anchors:
- Root: قلب (q-l-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "To turn, overturn, transform a thing from one state to another; to rotate, to flip"
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "قلب الشيء: تصريفه وصرفه عن وجه إلى وجه" — the heart is so named because of its constant turning and transformation between states
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "قلب الشيء قلبا: حوله عن وجهه" (to turn a thing from its face). Metaphorical: "رجل قلب حول: يقلب الأمور ويحتال" — one who turns matters over and manages them; "قلبوا لك الأمور" (they turned matters against you)
- Root: وجل (w-j-l)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "Fear, dread, apprehension that strikes the heart"
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الوجل: استشعار الخوف" — the sensing of fear; cited in {«إنما المؤمنون الذين إذا ذكر الله وجلت قلوبهم»}
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "رجل وجل، وقوم وجال" — a fearful man, a fearful people; "وفي قلبه وجل" — in his heart is dread
- Root: عجب (ʿ-j-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "Wonder, amazement; self-admiration, vanity"
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Self-admiration (al-ʿujb) is a destructive spiritual ailment that nullifies deeds
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: wonder at something extraordinary. Metaphorical: self-conceit regarding one's own acts of obedience
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد (Restriction & Focused Predication) — governing the precise limitation of general categories (al-ṣifāt al-khāṣṣah within al-aṣnāf al-thamāniyyah) and the conditional structure of acceptance

2:262.arabic: أمضى السبيل فقلت وما إمضاء السبيل فقيل لي كنت تقول للشيء إنه في سبيل الله ثم ترجع فيه فلو كنت أمضيت السبيل لأمضينا لك وحكي عن بعض العباد بمكة أنه كان نائما إلى جنب رجل معه هميانه فانتبه الرجل ففقد هميانه فاتهمه به فقال له كم كان في هميانك فذكر له فحمله من البيت ووزنه من عنده ثم بعد ذلك أعلمه أصحابه أنهم كانوا أخذوا الهميان مزحا معه فجاء هو وأصحابه معه وردوا الذهب فأبى وقال خذه حلالا طيبا فما كنت لأعود في مال أخرجته في سبيل الله عز وجل فلم يقبل فألحوا عليه فدعا ابنه وجعل يصره صررا ويبعث به إلى الفقراء حتى لم يبق منه شيء فهكذا ك
2:262.english: ...his wealth being for him a deterrent from sin — for perhaps he would become independent by means of it and thus grow lax about theft afterward, while his disobedience had already ceased by his consuming the unlawful, since [the owner] had made it lawful for him. The second [intention] is that he not wrong another Muslim, such that his wealth becomes a ransom for the wealth of another Muslim. And whenever he intends thereby to protect another's wealth with his own wealth, or intends to repel sin from the thief or to lighten it upon him, then he has indeed advised the Muslims sincerely and has complied with his saying, peace and blessings be upon him: {«انصر أخاك ظالما أو مظلوما»} — "Help your brother whether he is the wrongdoer or the wronged." And helping the wrongdoer is that you prevent him from wrongdoing. His pardoning of him is an annihilation of the wrongdoing and a prevention of it. And let him be certain that this intention does not harm him in any way whatsoever, for there is nothing in it that empowers the thief or alters the eternal decree. Rather, let him verify his intention by means of renunciation (zuhd). For if his wealth is taken, he shall have for every dirham seven hundred dirhams, because he intended it and aimed at it. And if it is not taken, he still obtains the reward — as it was related from the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, concerning one who abstained from coitus interruptus and thus left the drop of semen in its place, that he would have the reward of a boy born to him from that intercourse who lived and was then killed in the path of Allah, the Exalted — even if no boy was actually born to him. For the matter of the child is nothing but the intercourse itself; as for the creation, the life, the provision, and the survival, these are not up to him. So had the child been created, his reward would have been upon his own act, and his act was not annihilated. Likewise is the matter of theft.
2:262.section_title_en: On the Etiquettes of Reliance (Adab al-Tawakkul) — Section 1134: Concerning One Whose Wealth is Stolen
2:262.anchors:
- Root: ظلم (Ẓ-L-M)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning is "to place something in other than its proper place"; darkness (ẓulmah) as its physical correlate.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Ẓulm is "transgression against right" and is expressed as darkness (ẓulumāt) versus light (nūr) — ignorance, shirk, and fisq.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): "He wrongs and is wronged." Metaphorical (majāz): "A land ẓalīm" — one never dug; the wrongdoer's darkness is like the darkness of the grave.
- Root: سبل (S-B-L)
  * Lisan / Ayn: A clear, easy path (sabīl); its plural subul.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "The way in which there is ease"; when used absolutely, it designates the path of truth (ṭarīq al-ḥaqq).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "Take this path, for it is the most even of paths." Metaphorical: "He let down (asbala) the rain" — as if lowering a curtain; "he let flow tears."
- Root: سرق (S-R-Q)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Taking what is not one's own covertly.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Theft is the taking of what one has no right to take, in secret"; legally specified by place and amount.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "A thief between thefts." Metaphorical: "He stole the hearing" (listened secretly); "a stolen voice" (hoarse).
- Sibawayh Rule: Bāb al-Ḥaṣr wa al-Taqyīd bi-innamā (Restriction and Specification with innamā) — Used to confine a predicate to a subject, as in the dream narrative: "It is only for him who carried the path through (amḍā al-sabīl)."

2:262.arabic: يفزع الناس يوم القيامة ولا يفزعون وهم أولياء الله الذين لا خوف عليهم ولا هم يحزنون وفيه شهر بن حوشب مختلف فيه // ورواه أبو هريرة رضي الله عنه وقال فيه إن حول العرش منابر من نور عليها قوم لباسهم نور ووجوههم نورا ليسوا بأنبياء ولا شهداء يغبطهم النبيون والشهداء فقالوا يا رسول الله صفهم لنا فقال هم المتحابون في الله والمتجالسون في الله والمتزاورون في الله (1) وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم ما تحاب اثنان في الله إلا كان أحبهما إلى الله أشدهما حبا لصاحبه (2) ويقال إن الأخوين في الله إذا كان أحدهما أعلى مقاما من الآخر
2:262.english: Know that affability (al-ulfah) is the fruit of excellent character (ḥusn al-khuluq), and estrangement (al-tafarruq) is the fruit of evil character. For excellent character necessitates mutual love, harmony, and concord, whereas evil character yields mutual hatred, envy, and turning away (al-tadābur). And whenever the source is praiseworthy, the fruit is likewise praiseworthy. The excellence of good character is not hidden in the religion; indeed, it is that with which God—glorified be He—praised His Prophet, peace be upon him, when He said: {وَإِنَّكَ لَعَلَىٰ خُلُقٍ عَظِيمٍ} «And indeed, you are upon an immense character» (Al-Qalam: 4). The Prophet, peace be upon him, said: "The thing which most causes people to enter Paradise is God-consciousness (taqwā) and excellent character." (1) Usāmah ibn Sharīk said: "We said, O Messenger of God, what is the best thing given to a person?" He said: "Excellent character." (2) He, peace be upon him, also said: "I was sent only to perfect the noble traits of character." (3) He, peace be upon him, said: "Nothing is heavier in the Balance than excellent character." (4) He, peace be upon him, said: "God does not beautify a person's outward form and his inward character, then feed him to the Fire." (5) He, peace be upon him, said: "O Abū Hurayrah, adhere to excellent character." (Page V02P157) Abū Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him, said: "What is excellent character, O Messenger of God?" He said: "That you join the one who cuts you off, forgive the one who wrongs you, and give to the one who deprives you." (1)

The excellence of good character is not hidden in the religion; indeed, it is that with which God—glorified be He—praised His Prophet, peace be upon him, when He said: {وَإِنَّكَ لَعَلَىٰ خُلُقٍ عَظِيمٍ} «And indeed, you are upon an immense character» (Al-Qalam: 4). The Prophet, peace be upon him, said: "The thing which most causes people to enter Paradise is God-consciousness (taqwā) and excellent character." (1) Usāmah ibn Sharīk said: "We said, O Messenger of God, what is the best thing given to a person?" He said: "Excellent character." (2) He, peace be upon him, also said: "I was sent only to perfect the noble traits of character." (3) He, peace be upon him, said: "Nothing is heavier in the Balance than excellent character." (4) He, peace be upon him, said: "God does not beautify a person's outward form and his inward character, then feed him to the Fire." (5) He, peace be upon him, said: "O Abū Hurayrah, adhere to excellent character." (Page V02P157) Abū Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him, said: "What is excellent character, O Messenger of God?" He said: "That you join the one who cuts you off, forgive the one who wrongs you, and give to the one who deprives you." (1)

2:277.arabic: يفزع الناس يوم القيامة ولا يفزعون وهم أولياء الله الذين لا خوف عليهم ولا هم يحزنون وفيه شهر بن حوشب مختلف فيه // ورواه أبو هريرة رضي الله عنه وقال فيه إن حول العرش منابر من نور عليها قوم لباسهم نور ووجوههم نورا ليسوا بأنبياء ولا شهداء يغبطهم النبيون والشهداء فقالوا يا رسول الله صفهم لنا فقال هم المتحابون في الله والمتجالسون في الله والمتزاورون في الله (1) وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم ما تحاب اثنان في الله إلا كان أحبهما إلى الله أشدهما حبا لصاحبه (2) ويقال إن الأخوين في الله إذا كان أحدهما أعلى مقاما من الآخر

(4) He, peace be upon him, said: "God does not beautify a person's outward form and his inward character, then feed him to the Fire." (5) He, peace be upon him, said: "O Abū Hurayrah, adhere to excellent character." (Page V02P157) Abū Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him, said: "What is excellent character, O Messenger of God?" He said: "That you join the one who cuts you off, forgive the one who wrongs you, and give to the one who deprives you." (1)

2:278.arabic: وقد قال الله تعالى يا أيها الذين آمنوا أنفقوا من طيبات ما كسبتم ومما أخرجنا لكم من الأرض ولا تيمموا الخبيث منه تنفقون ولستم بآخذيه إلا أن تغمضوا فيه أي لا تأخذوه إلا مع كراهية وحياء وهو معنى الإغماض فلا تؤثروا به ربكم وفي الخبر سبق درهم مائة ألف درهم (3) وذلك بأن يخرجه الإنسان وهو من أحل ماله وأجوده فيصدر ذلك عن الرضا والفرح بالبذل وقد يخرج مائة ألف درهم مما يكره من ماله فيدل ذلك على أنه ليس يؤثر الله عز وجل بشيء مما يحبه وبذلك ذم الله تعالى قوما جعلوا لله ما يكرهون فقال تعال
2:278.english: The heart is not treated save with the compound electuary (maʿjūn) of knowledge and works. And this condition among the conditions of almsgiving runs in the same course as humility (al-khushūʿ) runs in the prayer. This is established by his saying — may Allah bless him and grant him peace: "A man has nothing of his prayer save that of which he was conscious." And this is like his saying — may Allah bless him and grant him peace: "Allah does not accept the charity of the one who bestows it with reproach (al-mannān)." And like His saying — Exalted is He: {«لا تبطلوا صدقاتكم بالمن والأذى»} ("Do not nullify your charities by reproach and injury"). As for the legal opinion (fatwā) of the jurist that the alms fall in their proper place and that one's liability is discharged without this condition — that is another discussion, and we have already pointed to its meaning in the Book of Prayer.
2:278.section_title_en: The Inner Conditions of Charity — Section 175 (From The Revival of the Religious Sciences, Book of the Mysteries of Almsgiving)
2:278.anchors:
- Root: قلب (q-l-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "To turn, overturn, transform a thing from one state to another; to rotate, to flip"
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "قلب الشيء: تصريفه وصرفه عن وجه إلى وجه" — the heart is so named because of its constant turning and transformation between states
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "قلب الشيء قلبا: حوله عن وجهه" (to turn a thing from its face). Metaphorical: "رجل قلب حول: يقلب الأمور ويحتال" — one who turns matters over and manages them; "قلبوا لك الأمور" (they turned matters against you)
- Root: وجل (w-j-l)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "Fear, dread, apprehension that strikes the heart"
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الوجل: استشعار الخوف" — the sensing of fear; cited in {«إنما المؤمنون الذين إذا ذكر الله وجلت قلوبهم»}
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "رجل وجل، وقوم وجال" — a fearful man, a fearful people; "وفي قلبه وجل" — in his heart is dread
- Root: عجب (ʿ-j-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "Wonder, amazement; self-admiration, vanity"
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Self-admiration (al-ʿujb) is a destructive spiritual ailment that nullifies deeds
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: wonder at something extraordinary. Metaphorical: self-conceit regarding one's own acts of obedience
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد (Restriction & Focused Predication) — governing the precise limitation of general categories (al-ṣifāt al-khāṣṣah within al-aṣnāf al-thamāniyyah) and the conditional structure of acceptance

2:278.arabic: وقال تعالى يا أيها الذين آمنوا اتقوا الله وذروا ما بقي من الربا إن كنتم مؤمنين {ثم قال} فإن لم تفعلوا فأذنوا بحرب من الله ورسوله {ثم قال} وإن تبتم فلكم رءوس أموالكم {ثم قال} ومن عاد فأولئك أصحاب النار هم فيها خالدون جعل آكل الربا أول الأمر مؤذنا بمحاربة الله وفي آخره متعرضا للنار والآيات الواردة في الحلال والحرام لا تحصى وروى ابن مسعود رضي الله عنه عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال طلب الحلال فريضة على كل مسلم ولما قال صلى الله عليه وسلم طلب العلم فريضة على كل مسلم (1) قال بعض العلماء أراد به طلب علم الحلال والحرام وجعل المر
2:278.english: God Most High has said: {«كلوا من الطيبات واعملوا صالحا»} — "Eat of the good things and do righteous deeds." (Q. 23:51) He commanded eating from the good things before [commanding] righteous deeds. And it is said that what is meant by "the good things" is the lawful (al-ḥalāl).
2:278.section_title_en: The Revival of the Religious Sciences — Book of the Etiquette of Eating: Section 336 — The Virtue of Lawful Sustenance and the Blameworthiness of the Forbidden
2:278.anchors:
- Root: اكل (akl)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root meaning of eating, consuming, and tasting food; the act of taking nourishment into the body.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الأكل: تناول المطعم" — eating is the taking of food; used metaphorically for fire consuming wood, and extended to mean lawful provision (ḥalāl) as the sustenance of the soul's soundness.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) for physical ingestion; metaphorical (majāz) for consuming wealth unlawfully, as in "أكل مال اليتيم" (devouring the orphan's wealth).
- Root: طعم (tuʿm)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Food, sustenance, and the act of tasting; also used for bait and that which is eaten.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Sustenance as that which nourishes the body; in the Kalam context, the lawful (ḥalāl) is that which purifies the heart, while the forbidden (ḥarām) corrupts it.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal for food; metaphorical for the moral state of the soul — "طعمه حرام" (his food is forbidden) signifies the corruption of one's entire being.
- Root: ورق (waraʿ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Abstinence, scrupulousness, and piety; refraining from doubtful matters.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The theological virtue of cautious avoidance of all that is suspect, as the foundation of true worship and the key to answered supplication.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal for refraining; metaphorical for the heart's purity achieved through guarding the limbs from the unlawful.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The syntactic structure of conditional and consequential clauses, where the protasis (e.g., "من أكل حراما") governs the apodosis ("لم يقبل منه صرف ولا عدل"), demonstrating the causal nexus between action and divine recompense.
