33:69.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Duties of Brotherhood'

33:70.arabic: وقد قال الله تعالى يا أيها الذين آمنوا أنفقوا من طيبات ما كسبتم ومما أخرجنا لكم من الأرض ولا تيمموا الخبيث منه تنفقون ولستم بآخذيه إلا أن تغمضوا فيه أي لا تأخذوه إلا مع كراهية وحياء وهو معنى الإغماض فلا تؤثروا به ربكم وفي الخبر سبق درهم مائة ألف درهم (3) وذلك بأن يخرجه الإنسان وهو من أحل ماله وأجوده فيصدر ذلك عن الرضا والفرح بالبذل وقد يخرج مائة ألف درهم مما يكره من ماله فيدل ذلك على أنه ليس يؤثر الله عز وجل بشيء مما يحبه وبذلك ذم الله تعالى قوما جعلوا لله ما يكرهون فقال تعال
33:70.english: The heart is not treated save with the compound electuary (maʿjūn) of knowledge and works. And this condition among the conditions of almsgiving runs in the same course as humility (al-khushūʿ) runs in the prayer. This is established by his saying — may Allah bless him and grant him peace: "A man has nothing of his prayer save that of which he was conscious." And this is like his saying — may Allah bless him and grant him peace: "Allah does not accept the charity of the one who bestows it with reproach (al-mannān)." And like His saying — Exalted is He: {«لا تبطلوا صدقاتكم بالمن والأذى»} ("Do not nullify your charities by reproach and injury"). As for the legal opinion (fatwā) of the jurist that the alms fall in their proper place and that one's liability is discharged without this condition — that is another discussion, and we have already pointed to its meaning in the Book of Prayer.
33:70.section_title_en: The Inner Conditions of Charity — Section 175 (From The Revival of the Religious Sciences, Book of the Mysteries of Almsgiving)
33:70.anchors:
- Root: قلب (q-l-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "To turn, overturn, transform a thing from one state to another; to rotate, to flip"
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "قلب الشيء: تصريفه وصرفه عن وجه إلى وجه" — the heart is so named because of its constant turning and transformation between states
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "قلب الشيء قلبا: حوله عن وجهه" (to turn a thing from its face). Metaphorical: "رجل قلب حول: يقلب الأمور ويحتال" — one who turns matters over and manages them; "قلبوا لك الأمور" (they turned matters against you)
- Root: وجل (w-j-l)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "Fear, dread, apprehension that strikes the heart"
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الوجل: استشعار الخوف" — the sensing of fear; cited in {«إنما المؤمنون الذين إذا ذكر الله وجلت قلوبهم»}
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "رجل وجل، وقوم وجال" — a fearful man, a fearful people; "وفي قلبه وجل" — in his heart is dread
- Root: عجب (ʿ-j-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "Wonder, amazement; self-admiration, vanity"
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Self-admiration (al-ʿujb) is a destructive spiritual ailment that nullifies deeds
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: wonder at something extraordinary. Metaphorical: self-conceit regarding one's own acts of obedience
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد (Restriction & Focused Predication) — governing the precise limitation of general categories (al-ṣifāt al-khāṣṣah within al-aṣnāf al-thamāniyyah) and the conditional structure of acceptance

40:48.arabic: إذ قال صلى الله عليه وسلم إن الله قد حرم على المؤمن من المؤمن دمه وماله وعرضه وأن يظن به ظن السوء (4) وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم إياكم والظن فإن الظن أكذب الحديث (5) وسوء الظن يدعو إلى التحسس والتحسن وقد قال صلى الله عليه وسلم لا تحسسوا ولا تجسسوا ولا تقاطعوا ولاتدابروا وكونوا عباد الله إخوانا (1) والتجسس في تطلع الأخبار والتحسس بالمراقبة بالعين فستر العيوب والتجاهل والتغافل عنها شيمة أهل الدين ويكفيك تنبيها على كمال الرتبة في ستر القبيح وإظهار الجميل أن الله تعالى وصف به في الدعا
40:48.english: Anas said: "The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) never confronted anyone with something he disliked." — The ḥadīth of Anas: "He never confronted anyone with something he disliked" — narrated by Abū Dāwūd, al-Tirmidhī in al-Shamāʾil, and al-Nasāʾī in al-Yawm wa al-Laylah with a weak chain.
40:48.section_title_en: On Silence Regarding the Faults of Brothers — The Rights of Brotherhood (Section 419)
40:48.anchors:
- Root: سكت (s-k-t)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of silence, refraining from speech; al-sukūt is the cessation of utterance, whether by tongue or by heart.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance — silence as a positive act of restraint (imsāk) that guards the tongue from what Allah has forbidden, paralleling the heart's silence from evil suspicion.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) — refraining from audible speech; Metaphorical (majāz) — the heart's silence, i.e., refraining from passing judgment on a brother's actions when a good interpretation is possible.
- Root: غيب (gh-y-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: That which is absent or hidden; ghībah (backbiting) is mentioning a brother in his absence with what he dislikes.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Ghībah is a violation of the unseen honor (ʿirḍ) of the Muslim, which the Law has rendered inviolable like blood and property.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — speaking of the absent; Metaphorical — the heart's backbiting (sūʾ al-ẓann), i.e., conceiving evil of a brother without certain knowledge.
- Root: ظن (ẓ-n-n)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Doubt, suspicion, or belief not founded on certainty; ẓann is the inclination of the soul toward one of two possibilities.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In the Qur'anic context, "avoid much suspicion" {«إِنَّ بَعْضَ الظَّنِّ إِثْمٌ»} — the blameworthy suspicion is that which attributes evil to a believer without a decisive sign (amārah).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — conjecture; Metaphorical — the heart's ghībah, for just as the tongue can wound, so too can the heart's presumption.
- Root: ستر (s-t-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To cover, conceal; sitr is the act of veiling a fault or defect.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Allah's attribute al-Sattār — He who veils the sins of His servants; the believer's emulation of this attribute is a mark of perfected faith.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — physical covering; Metaphorical — concealing another's moral faults, as the Prophet said: "Whoever conceals the fault of a brother, Allah conceals his fault in this world and the next."
- Sibawayh Rule: Restriction and specification (al-ḥaṣr wa al-taqyīd) — the conditional clauses (law, idhā) and exceptions (illā) governing when silence is obligatory versus when speech becomes mandatory (amr bi-l-maʿrūf).

42:26.arabic: وروي في غريب التفسير في قوله تعالى {ويستجيب الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات ويزيدهم من فضله} قال يشفعهم في إخوانهم فيدخلهم الجنة معهم ويقال إذا غفر الله للعبد شفع في إخوانه ولذلك حث جماعة من السلف على الصحبة والألفة والمخالطة وكرهوا العزلة والانفراد فهذه فوائد تستدعي كل فائدة شروطا لا تحصل إلا بها ونحن نفصلها أما على الجملة فينبغي أن يكون فيمن تؤثر صحبته خمس خصال أن يكون عاقلا حسن الخلق غير فاسق ولا مبتدع ولا حريص على الدنيا أما العقل فهو رأس المال وهو الأصل فلا خير في صحبة الأحمق فإلى الوحشة والقطيعة ترجع عاقبتها وإن طالت قال علي رضي ا
42:26.english: Know that not every person is fit for companionship. The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: {«A man follows the religion of his intimate friend; so let each of you consider whom he takes as an intimate friend»}. One must therefore be distinguished by traits and qualities on account of which his companionship is desired, and those qualities are stipulated according to the benefits sought from companionship — for the meaning of a condition (sharṭ) is that without which the attainment of the intended object is impossible. Thus, in relation to the intended object, the conditions become manifest.
42:26.section_title_en: Exposition of the Qualities Required in One Whose Companionship Is Chosen
42:26.anchors:
- Root: صحب (ṣ-ḥ-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Companionship, association, intimacy of attachment — whether by body, place, or time; the companion is the one who is constantly attendant upon another.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Companionship (ṣuḥbah) may be physical — which is the original and most common sense — or by care and concern; the term extends to every thing that is attached to another as its possessor or associate.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): bodily association and fellowship. Metaphorical (majāz): "companion of wealth or knowledge" — i.e., one who is attached to it in concern; "companion of the sword and spear" for the warrior.
- Root: عقل (ʿ-q-l)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Intellect; that which restrains and binds one from error; the faculty of understanding and discernment.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): ʿAql is said of the faculty disposed to receive knowledge, and also of the knowledge acquired by that faculty; it is the instrument by which one apprehends things as they are.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: understanding and discernment after ignorance. Metaphorical: "a palm tree that does not accept pollination" — i.e., does not take in what would benefit it.
- Root: غرض (gh-r-ḍ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Target, aim, purpose; that at which one shoots; then applied to every goal one seeks to attain.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The object aimed at; divided into deficient aims (those pursued for the sake of something beyond them) and complete aims (those sought for their own sake, like Paradise).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the target of archery. Metaphorical: any sought-after end or purpose.
- Root: قلب (q-l-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To turn, overturn, transform a thing from one state to another; the heart — so named for its constant fluctuation and turning.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Taqlīb: the turning of a thing from one face to another; the heart is so named because of its perpetual turning between states.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: to turn a thing over. Metaphorical: "to turn matters over" — i.e., to examine and deliberate; the heart's turning between states.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The conditional structure "لا بد أن يتميز" (it is necessary that he be distinguished) governs the subsequent specification of qualities, where the conditions (shurūṭ) are semantically dependent upon the ends (aghrāḍ) sought, requiring careful parsing of the periodic sentence to preserve the logical priority of purpose over condition.

42:38.arabic: {وأمرهم شورى بينهم ومما رزقناهم ينفقون} أي كانوا خلطاء في الأموال لا يميز بعضهم رحله عن بعض وكان منهم من لا يصحب من قال نعلي لأنه أضافه إلى نفسه وجاء فتح الموصلي إلى منزل لأخ له وكان غائبا فأمر أهله فأخرجت صندوقه ففتحه وأخذ حاجته فأخبرت الجارية مولاها فقال إن صدقت فأنت حرة لوجه الله سرورا بما فعل وجاء رجل إلى أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه وقال إني أريد أن أواخيك في الله فقال أتدري ما حق الإخاء قال عرفني قال أن لا تكون أحق بدينارك ودرهمك مني قال لم أبلغ هذه المنزلة بعد قال فاذهب عني وقال علي بن ا
42:38.english: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: "The likeness of two brothers is like the likeness of two hands — one washes the other." {«مثل الأخوين مثل اليدين تغسل إحداهما الأخرى»}
42:38.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Duties of Brotherhood'

47:7.arabic: سبحانه وناصر الله تعالى موقوف على النصرة له قال الله تعالى {إن تنصروا الله ينصركم ويثبت أقدامكم} فالبداية بالجهد من العبد والجزاء بالهداية من الله عز وجل ولذلك قال تعالى {والذين جاهدوا فينا لنهدينهم سبلنا} وقال تعالى {إن الله لا يغير ما بقوم حتى يغيروا ما بأنفسهم} وإنما التغير تكثير الشهوات فهي مرتع الشياطين ومرعاهم فما دامت مخصبة لم ينقطع ترددهم وما داموا يترددون لم ينكشف للعبد جلال الله سبحانه وكان محجوبا عن لقائه وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم لولا أن الشياطين يحومون على قلوب بني آدم لنظروا إلى ملكوت السموات (3) فمن هذا الوجه صار الصوم باب ال
47:7.english: To proceed: Fasting is one quarter of faith, by virtue of his saying, peace and blessings be upon him: "Fasting is half of patience" — and by virtue of his saying, peace and blessings be upon him: "Patience is half of faith" {«الإيمان»}. Then it is distinguished by a particular characteristic of its attribution to Allah the Exalted, above all the other pillars — for Allah the Exalted said, in what His Prophet narrated from Him, peace and blessings be upon him: "Every good deed is multiplied tenfold up to seven hundred times, except fasting, for it is Mine, and I shall reward it." And Allah the Exalted has said: {«Only the patient shall be paid their reward in full without reckoning»} (Q 39:10). And fasting is half of patience — so its reward has surpassed the law of measure and reckoning. And sufficient for you in knowing its excellence is his saying, peace and blessings be upon him: "By Him in whose hand is my soul, the change in the breath of the mouth of the fasting person is more fragrant to Allah than the scent of musk. Allah the Exalted says: 'He only abandons his appetite, his food, and his drink for My sake — so fasting is for Me, and I shall reward it.'" And he said, peace and blessings be upon him: "Paradise has a gate called al-Rayyān, through which none shall enter except the fasting ones." And the fasting person is promised the meeting with Allah the Exalted as a portion of his fasting. And he said, peace and blessings be upon him: "For the fasting person there are two joys: a joy when he breaks his fast, and a joy when he meets his Lord." And he said, peace and blessings be upon him: "Everything has a gate, and the gate of worship is fasting." And he said, peace and blessings be upon him: "The sleep of the fasting person is worship." And Abū Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, narrated that he, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "When the month of Ramaḍān enters, the gates of Paradise are opened, the gates of the Fire are closed, the devils are chained, and a caller calls out: 'O seeker of good, come forth! O seeker of evil, desist!'" And Wakīʿ said concerning His saying, the Exalted: {«Eat and drink in satisfaction for what you sent forth in the days past»} (Q 69:24) — these are the days of fasting, for in them they abandoned eating and drinking. And the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, gathered in the rank of divine boasting (mubāhāh) between renunciation of the world and fasting, saying: "Allah the Exalted boasts to His angels of the young worshiper, saying: 'O young man who abandons his appetite for My sake, who devotes his youth to Me — you are to Me as some of My angels.'" And he said, peace and blessings be upon him, concerning the fasting person: "Allah the Exalted says: 'Look, O My angels, at My servant — he has abandoned his appetite, his pleasure, his food, and his drink for My sake.'" And it was said concerning His saying, the Exalted: {«No soul knows what comfort has been concealed for them, as a reward for what they used to do»} (Q 32:17) — it was said: their deed was fasting, because He said: {«Only the patient shall be paid their reward in full without reckoning»} — so the reward of the fasting person is poured out upon him without measure, and is dealt out to him in bulk, not falling under any imagination or estimation.
47:7.section_title_en: The Book of the Secrets of Fasting — Section 185: On the Excellence of Fasting and Its Distinction Among the Acts of Worship
47:7.anchors:
- Root: صوم (ṣ-w-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core linguistic root meaning — abstention from any act, whether eating, speaking, or walking; a horse that refrains from movement or fodder is called ṣā'im.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological/Kalam semantic nuance — "الصوم في الأصل: الإمساك عن الفعل" — fasting is fundamentally the restraint of the self from action; it is an inward act of the heart, invisible to creation.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal vs Metaphorical distinction — Haqiqah: the month of fasting, "فمن شهد منكم الشهر فليصمه" (Q 2:185); Majaz: "صام الفرس على آريه" — a horse standing still at its tether, refusing fodder, metaphorically "fasting."
- Root: عله (ʿ-l-h)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core linguistic root meaning — to feed or pasture; related to cultivation and nourishment.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological/Kalam semantic nuance — not directly attested in Mufradat for this root; the root pertains to the means by which the body is sustained, which is precisely what the fasting person abstains from.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal vs Metaphorical distinction — literal feeding and satiation; the fasting person's abstention from these becomes the very means of spiritual nourishment.
- Root: الي (a-l-y)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core linguistic root meaning — to convey a message; the angel (malak) is so named because the message is "chewed" (yu'lak) in the mouth, as a horse chews its bit.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological/Kalam semantic nuance — "المألكة: الرسالة" — the angelic function is the conveyance of divine communication; the fasting person's hunger narrows the channels through which the devil (who runs like blood through the veins) reaches the heart.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal vs Metaphorical distinction — literal conveyance of a message versus the metaphorical "message" of the devil's insinuation (waswās) through the pathways of the body.
- Root: صبر (ṣ-b-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core linguistic root meaning — to restrain, to hold back in constriction; "صبرت الدابة: حبستها بلا علف" — to hold an animal back without fodder.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological/Kalam semantic nuance — "الصبر: الإمساك في ضيق" — patience is restraint within constriction; it is the holding of the soul upon what reason and law require, or from what they require it to abstain. Its names vary by context: in battle it is courage, in calamity it is patience proper.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal vs Metaphorical distinction — Haqiqah: "صبرت على ما أكره وصبرت عما أحب" — patience upon the disliked and patience from the beloved; Majaz: "صبرت يمينه" — to bind one's oath severely, and "هو أصبر على الضرب من الأرض" — more enduring of striking than the earth.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — The particle innamā restricts and confines the predicate exclusively to its subject, as in the divine saying {«إنما يوفى الصابرون أجرهم بغير حساب»} and {«إنما يذر شهوته وطعامه وشرابه لأجلي»}, where the restriction elevates the restricted matter to a rank beyond all quantitative measure.

47:7.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Duties of Brotherhood'

52:21.arabic: قال تعالى ألحقنا بهم ذرياتهم وما ألتناهم من عملهم من شيء أي ما نقصناهم من أعمالهم وجعلنا أولادهم مزيدا في إحسانهم الوجه الرابع أن يموت الولد قبله فيكون له شفيعا فقد روي عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال إن الطفل يجر بأبويه إلى الجنة (5) وفي بعض الأخبار يأخذ بثوبه كما أنا الآن آخذ بثوبك (6) وقال أيضا صلى الله عليه وسلم إن المولود يقال ادخل الجنة فيقف على باب الجنة فيظل محبنطئا أي ممتلئا غيظا وغضبا ويقول لا أدخل الجنة إلا وأبواي معي فيقال أدخلوا أبويه معه الجنة (7) وفي خبر آخر إن الأطفال يجتمعون في
52:21.english: وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم: "لا يلقى الله أحد بذنب أعظم من جهالة أهله."
52:21.topic: Al-Ghazali on the journey of the soul, death, and the Hereafter, from 'Duties of Brotherhood'

58:12.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Duties of Brotherhood'

58:22.arabic: وقال عز وجل {رضي الله عنهم ورضوا عنه ذلك لمن خشي ربه} وكل ما دل على فضيلة العلم دل على فضيلة الخوف لأن الخوف ثمرة العلم ولذلك جاء في خبر موسى عليه أفضل الصلاة والسلام وأما الخائفون
58:22.english: As for the path of derivation (iqtibās) from the verses and reports, what has been transmitted concerning the virtue of fear is beyond enumeration. And sufficient as an indication of its virtue is that God—may He be exalted—has gathered together for the fearful (khāʾifūn) guidance (hudā), mercy (raḥmah), knowledge (ʿilm), and good pleasure (riḍwān)—and these are the sum total of the stations of the people of Paradise. God—may He be exalted—said: {وهدى ورحمة للذين هم لربهم يرهبون} "And guidance and mercy for those who of their Lord are fearful" [Al-Aʿrāf: 154]. And He—exalted is He—said: {إنما يخشى الله من عباده العلماء} "Only those of His servants who possess knowledge fear God" [Fāṭir: 28]—describing them with knowledge on account of their fear [of Him].
58:22.section_title_en: Exposition of the Virtue of Fear (Khawf) and Encouragement Thereof
58:22.anchors:
- Root: خوف (Khawf)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root denotes trepidation, apprehension, and the state of being overtaken by dread of a feared outcome.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الخوف: توقع مكروه عن أمارة مظنونة، أو معلومة" — the anticipation of something detestable based on a probable or certain indication; it is the direct opposite of amn (security) and applies to both worldly and otherworldly matters.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): "خفته على مالي خوفا وخيفة" — fearing for something. Metaphorical (Majaz): "تخوفه: تنقصه" — to diminish gradually, as fear consumes the soul piecemeal.
- Root: فضل (Fadl)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Excess, superiority, or merit beyond the baseline of sufficiency.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الفضل: الزيادة عن الاقتصاد" — increase beyond moderation; the praiseworthy type is like the surplus of knowledge and forbearance, and it is measured by its end (ghāyah).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "مال فلان فاضل: كثير يفضل عن القوت" — surplus wealth exceeding necessity. The virtue of a thing is gauged by its instrumental efficacy toward a noble goal.
- Root: علم (ʿIlm)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Certain cognition and apprehension of a thing as it truly is.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "العلم: إدراك الشيء بحقيقته" — apprehension of a thing's reality; it is the root from which khawf branches as its fruit.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "ما علمت بخبرك: ما شعرت به" — to have cognizance. The scholars (ʿulamāʾ) are so named for their knowledge, which necessarily engenders fear of God.
- Sibawayh Rule: Restriction and Focused Predication (باب الحصر والتقييد) — governing the exclusive attribution in {إنما يخشى الله من عباده العلماء}, where the predicate restricts fear to the knowledgeable, and the syntactic fronting of "whom they fear" (لربهم يرهبون) emphasizes the object of reverential dread.
58:22.topic: Al-Ghazali on the journey of the soul, death, and the Hereafter, from 'Love, Longing, Intimacy and Contentment'

58:22.arabic: منها إلى حد التحريم قال تعالى {لا تجد قوما يؤمنون بالله واليوم الآخر يوادون من حاد الله ورسوله ولو كانوا آباءهم أو أبناءهم} الآية وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم المسلم والمشرك لا تتراءى ناراهما (1) وقال عز وجل {يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا تتخذوا عدوي وعدوكم أولياء} الآية الثاني المبتدع الذي يدعو إلى بدعته فإن كانت البدعة بحيث يكفر بها فأمره أشد من الذمي لأنه لا يقر بجزية ولا يسامح بعقد ذمة وإن كان ممن لا يكفر به فأمره بينه وبين الله أخف من أمر الكافر لا محالة ولكن الأمر في الإنكار عليه أشد منه على الكافر لأن شر الكافر غير متعد فإن المسلمين اعتقدوا كفره فلا يلتفتون إلى قوله إذ ل
58:22.english: If you say: "The manifestation of hatred and enmity by deed, even if not obligatory, is undoubtedly commendable (mandūb); yet the disobedient and the flagrant sinners are of varying ranks — so how is excellence attained by dealing with them, and is a single course pursued with all of them or not?" — Know that the one who opposes the command of God, may He be exalted, is either one who opposes in his creed (ʿaqd) or in his deed (ʿamal). The one who opposes in creed is either an innovator (mubtadiʿ) or a disbeliever (kāfir). The innovator is either one who calls to his innovation (dāʿī) or one who remains silent — and the silent one is either so by incapacity or by choice. The divisions of corruption in belief are thus three:
58:22.section_title_en: Exposition of the Ranks of Those Who Are Hated for God's Sake and the Manner of Dealing with Them
58:22.anchors:
- Root: ب غ ض (b-gh-d)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of hatred and aversion, the opposite of love (al-ḥubb); al-baghḍāʾ is intense hatred.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance — hatred for God's sake (al-bughḍ fī Allāh) is a spiritual act of the heart (laṭīfah rabbāniyyah) distinguishing sincere faith from hypocrisy.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) — aversion of the heart; metaphorical (majāz) — manifesting aversion through outward acts of avoidance and censure.
- Root: ع ص و (ʿ-ṣ-w)
  * Lisan / Ayn: ʿiṣyān — disobedience and rebellion against a command; the ʿāṣī is one who transgresses the bound.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance — fisq (flagrant sin) is the departure from the straight path (khurūj ʿan al-ṭarīqah al-mustaqīmah) through willful transgression.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — breaking a command; metaphorical — persistence in sin without repentance.
- Root: ب د ع (b-d-ʿ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: bidʿah — an innovation, a newly invented matter in religion without precedent.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance — al-ibdāʿ is creation without model; for God it is bringing into being without instrument, matter, time, or place. For man, bidʿah is introducing into religion what is not from it.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — inventing something new; metaphorical — a weak argument (abdaʿat ḥujjatuka) or failing expectation.
- Root: ك ف ر (k-f-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: kufr — covering, concealing; the night is called kāfir for covering persons; the farmer (kāfir) covers the seed.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance — kufr is disbelief, the covering of truth; the kāfir is one who veils the truth of God's unity.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — covering (satar); metaphorical — ingratitude and rejection of divine blessings.
- Root: ق ل ب (q-l-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: qalb — the heart; taqallub — turning and changing from one state to another.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance — the heart's fluctuation (taqallub al-qulūb) between states of faith and heedlessness; the hearts of the common folk are quick to turn.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — turning a thing over; metaphorical — the instability of opinion and disposition.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Conditional Partitioning (Taqsīm al-Sharṭ) — the division of a genus into exhaustive species governed by conditional clauses (in kāna... fa-), each branch receiving its own ruling without conflation.
58:22.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Duties of Brotherhood'

58:22.arabic: إلى الله واشتياقا إليه وقدما في استباق الخيرات أولئك حزب الله ألا إن حزب الله هم المفلحون قال الراوي فقلت يا أبا الدرداء ما سمعت بصفة أشد علي من تلك الصفة وكيف لي أن أبلغها فقال ما بينك وبين أن تكون في أوسعها إلا أن تكون تبغض الدنيا فإنك إذا بغضت الدنيا أقبلت على حب الآخرة وبقدر حبك للآخرة تزهد في الدنيا وبقدر ذلك تبصر ما ينفعك وإذا علم الله من عبد حسن الطلب أفرغ عليه السداد واكتنفه بالعصمة واعلم يا ابن أخي أن ذلك في كتاب الله تعالى المنزل إن الله مع الذين اتقوا والذين هم محسنون قال يحيى بن كثير فنظرنا
58:22.english: Among these manifestations is pride in loving that people stand up for him, or rise before him. ʿAlī — may God honor his face — said: "Whoever wishes to look upon a man of the Fire, let him look at a man seated while people stand before him."
58:22.section_title_en: The Book of Pride and Self-Conceit — Section 862: Manifestations of Pride (Takabbur) in Bearing, Speech, and Conduct, and the Prophetic Model of Humility (Tawāḍuʿ)
58:22.anchors:
- Root: كبر (k-b-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of greatness, magnitude, and elevation in rank or stature; takabbur (تَكَبُّر) is the assumption of greatness over others, the comportment of one who deems himself above his fellow creatures.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-istikbār is the soul's refusal of truth out of disdain for its bearer, and its haughty rejection of what is right; it is the root of every blameworthy trait, for Iblis's fall was his refusal to prostrate out of pride.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): physical height and elevation. Metaphorical (majāz): the heart's self-elevation above others, manifesting in bodily postures — the "ṣaʿar" (turning the cheek away) being its visible sign.
- Root: وضع (w-ḍ-ʿ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To place down low, to lower, to set something down; tawāḍuʿ (تَوَاضُع) is the lowering of oneself, the opposite of elevation and haughtiness.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-tawāḍuʿ is humility before God and His creatures — the soul's recognition of its true station and its refusal to claim what it does not deserve; it is the root of every praiseworthy trait.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical lowering. Metaphorical: the soul's self-abasement in conduct — sitting where one is bid, serving oneself, and accepting invitation from the poor.
- Root: شمل (sh-m-l)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To encompass, to include all parts; shamāʾil (شَمَائِل) are the innate dispositions and outward traits that encompass a man's character.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The outward marks and habitual bearing through which inner moral states become visible to observers.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Used here in its literal sense of comprehensive outward features — the face, gait, voice, and gestures that betray the inner state.
- Root: بذذ (b-dh-dh)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Al-badhādha (البَذَاذَة) is the roughness and plainness of dress and appearance, the state of one who does not adorn himself.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In the prophetic tradition {البَذَاذَةُ مِنَ الإِيمَانِ}, it signifies the believer's indifference to worldly finery — a mean and unadorned appearance that reflects the heart's detachment.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: shabbiness of garment. Metaphorical: the soul's refusal to seek honor through dress, distinguishing genuine humility from affected squalor.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Restriction and Focused Predication (باب الحصر والتقييد) — governing the author's use of "إنما" and restrictive clauses to delimit the precise scope of pride's manifestations and humility's counter-examples, ensuring each trait is specified without overgeneralization.
58:22.topic: Al-Ghazali on purifying the character, moral diseases, and spiritual remedies, from 'Condemnation of Pride and Conceit'

59:18.arabic: أما الفضيلة فقد قال الله تعالى {يا أيها الذين آمنوا اتقوا الله ولتنظر نفس ما قدمت لغد} وهذه إشارة إلى المحاسبة على ما مضى من الأعمال ولذلك قال عمر رضي الله تعالى عنه حاسبوا أنفسكم قبل أن تحاسبوا وزنوها قبل أن توزنوا وفي الخبر انه عليه السلام جاءه رجل فقال يا رسول الله أوصنى فقال أمستوص أنت فقال نعم قال إذا هممت بأمر فتدبر عاقبته فإن كان رشدا فامضه وإن كان غيا فانته عنه وفي الخبر وينبغى للعاقل أن يكون له أربع ساعات ساعة يحاسب فيها نفسه وقال تعالى {وتوبوا إلى الله جميعا أيها المؤمنون لعلكم تفلحون} والتوبة نظر في الفعل بعد
59:18.english: As for its virtue, God most high has said: {«يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا اتَّقُوا اللَّهَ وَلْتَنْظُرْ نَفْسٌ مَا قَدَّمَتْ لِغَدٍ»} (O you who believe, fear God, and let every soul look to what it has sent forward for the morrow) — and this is an allusion to reckoning over past deeds. For this reason, ʿUmar — may God most high be pleased with him — said: "Call yourselves to account before you are called to account, and weigh yourselves before you are weighed." And in the report, a man came to him — peace be upon him — and said: "O Messenger of God, counsel me." He said: "Are you asking for counsel?" He replied: "Yes." He said: "When you resolve upon a matter, then ponder its consequence: if it be right guidance, proceed with it; and if it be error, desist from it." And in the report: "It behooves the intelligent man to have four hours: an hour in which he calls himself to account." And God most high said: {«وَتُوبُوا إِلَى اللَّهِ جَمِيعًا أَيُّهَا الْمُؤْمِنُونَ لَعَلَّكُمْ تُفْلِحُونَ»} (And turn in repentance to God all together, O believers, that you might succeed) — and repentance is a scrutiny of the deed after its completion, through regret over it. And he — peace be upon him — said: "Verily I seek forgiveness from God most high and turn to Him in repentance a hundred times a day." And God most high said: {«إِنَّ الَّذِينَ اتَّقَوْا إِذَا مَسَّهُمْ طَائِفٌ مِنَ الشَّيْطَانِ تَذَكَّرُوا فَإِذَا هُمْ مُبْصِرُونَ»} (Verily those who fear God, when a whisper from Satan touches them, they remember — and behold, they are seeing clearly). And it is related of ʿUmar — may God be pleased with him — that he would strike his own feet with a whip when night fell upon him, saying to himself: "What have you done today?" And it is related of Maymūn ibn Mihrān that he said: "A servant does not become one of the God-fearing until he calls himself to account more severely than he would his partner — and two partners reckon with each other after the work." And it is narrated from ʿĀʾishah — may God most high be pleased with her — that Abū Bakr — God's good pleasure be upon him — said to her at death: "There is no one among mankind more beloved to me than ʿUmar." Then he said to her: "How did I put it?" So she repeated to him what he had said, whereupon he said: "There is no one more honored by me than ʿUmar."
59:18.section_title_en: The Third Watch: Self-Reckoning After Deeds — Its Virtue and Its Reality
59:18.anchors:
- Root: ح س ب (ḥ-s-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of counting, reckoning, and sufficient estimation; al-ḥisāb is the act of numbering and settling accounts.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: muḥāsabah is the soul's voluntary audit of its deeds against divine command, prefiguring the eschatological reckoning (ḥisāb) by God.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): arithmetic counting; Metaphorical (majāz): self-interrogation and weighing of one's actions, as in "ḥāsaba nafsahu" (he called his soul to account).
- Root: ن ظ ر (n-ẓ-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To look, consider, reflect; naẓar implies deliberate examination with the eye or intellect.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: taḍabbur (deep reflection) on consequences of actions, aligning sight with insight (baṣīrah).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical gazing; Metaphorical: intellectual deliberation and foresight, as in "tadabbar al-amr" (he pondered the matter).
- Root: ن ف س (n-f-s)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The self, soul, or spirit; that which breathes and possesses volition.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-nafs al-lawwāmah (the blaming soul) is the conscience that reproaches its owner for misdeeds, distinct from the corporeal body.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the animate self; Metaphorical: the inner tribunal where the soul is both accused and judge.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Restriction and Focused Predication (باب الحصر والتقييد) — Constructions like "إنما" and conditional clauses (idhā... fa-) establish causal sequencing, as in "if a whim touches them, they remember" — the protasis governs the apodosis, binding reflection to action.
59:18.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Monitoring and Accounting'

59:18.arabic: وقد قال الله تعالى يا أيها الذين آمنوا أنفقوا من طيبات ما كسبتم ومما أخرجنا لكم من الأرض ولا تيمموا الخبيث منه تنفقون ولستم بآخذيه إلا أن تغمضوا فيه أي لا تأخذوه إلا مع كراهية وحياء وهو معنى الإغماض فلا تؤثروا به ربكم وفي الخبر سبق درهم مائة ألف درهم (3) وذلك بأن يخرجه الإنسان وهو من أحل ماله وأجوده فيصدر ذلك عن الرضا والفرح بالبذل وقد يخرج مائة ألف درهم مما يكره من ماله فيدل ذلك على أنه ليس يؤثر الله عز وجل بشيء مما يحبه وبذلك ذم الله تعالى قوما جعلوا لله ما يكرهون فقال تعال
59:18.english: The heart is not treated save with the compound electuary (maʿjūn) of knowledge and works. And this condition among the conditions of almsgiving runs in the same course as humility (al-khushūʿ) runs in the prayer. This is established by his saying — may Allah bless him and grant him peace: "A man has nothing of his prayer save that of which he was conscious." And this is like his saying — may Allah bless him and grant him peace: "Allah does not accept the charity of the one who bestows it with reproach (al-mannān)." And like His saying — Exalted is He: {«لا تبطلوا صدقاتكم بالمن والأذى»} ("Do not nullify your charities by reproach and injury"). As for the legal opinion (fatwā) of the jurist that the alms fall in their proper place and that one's liability is discharged without this condition — that is another discussion, and we have already pointed to its meaning in the Book of Prayer.
59:18.section_title_en: The Inner Conditions of Charity — Section 175 (From The Revival of the Religious Sciences, Book of the Mysteries of Almsgiving)
59:18.anchors:
- Root: قلب (q-l-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "To turn, overturn, transform a thing from one state to another; to rotate, to flip"
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "قلب الشيء: تصريفه وصرفه عن وجه إلى وجه" — the heart is so named because of its constant turning and transformation between states
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "قلب الشيء قلبا: حوله عن وجهه" (to turn a thing from its face). Metaphorical: "رجل قلب حول: يقلب الأمور ويحتال" — one who turns matters over and manages them; "قلبوا لك الأمور" (they turned matters against you)
- Root: وجل (w-j-l)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "Fear, dread, apprehension that strikes the heart"
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الوجل: استشعار الخوف" — the sensing of fear; cited in {«إنما المؤمنون الذين إذا ذكر الله وجلت قلوبهم»}
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "رجل وجل، وقوم وجال" — a fearful man, a fearful people; "وفي قلبه وجل" — in his heart is dread
- Root: عجب (ʿ-j-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "Wonder, amazement; self-admiration, vanity"
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Self-admiration (al-ʿujb) is a destructive spiritual ailment that nullifies deeds
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: wonder at something extraordinary. Metaphorical: self-conceit regarding one's own acts of obedience
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد (Restriction & Focused Predication) — governing the precise limitation of general categories (al-ṣifāt al-khāṣṣah within al-aṣnāf al-thamāniyyah) and the conditional structure of acceptance

60:1.arabic: وقال عز وجل {يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا تتخذوا عدوي وعدوكم أولياء} الآية الثاني المبتدع الذي يدعو إلى بدعته فإن كانت البدعة بحيث يكفر بها فأمره أشد من الذمي لأنه لا يقر بجزية ولا يسامح بعقد ذمة وإن كان ممن لا يكفر به فأمره بينه وبين الله أخف من أمر الكافر لا محالة ولكن الأمر في الإنكار عليه أشد منه على الكافر لأن شر الكافر غير متعد فإن المسلمين اعتقدوا كفره فلا يلتفتون إلى قوله إذ لا يدعي لنفسه الإسلام واعتقاد الحق أما المبتدع الذي يدعوا إلا البدعة ويزعم أن ما يدعو إليه حق فهو سبب لغواية الخلق فشره متعد فال
60:1.english: If you say: "The manifestation of hatred and enmity by deed, even if not obligatory, is undoubtedly commendable (mandūb); yet the disobedient and the flagrant sinners are of varying ranks — so how is excellence attained by dealing with them, and is a single course pursued with all of them or not?" — Know that the one who opposes the command of God, may He be exalted, is either one who opposes in his creed (ʿaqd) or in his deed (ʿamal). The one who opposes in creed is either an innovator (mubtadiʿ) or a disbeliever (kāfir). The innovator is either one who calls to his innovation (dāʿī) or one who remains silent — and the silent one is either so by incapacity or by choice. The divisions of corruption in belief are thus three:
60:1.section_title_en: Exposition of the Ranks of Those Who Are Hated for God's Sake and the Manner of Dealing with Them
60:1.anchors:
- Root: ب غ ض (b-gh-d)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of hatred and aversion, the opposite of love (al-ḥubb); al-baghḍāʾ is intense hatred.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance — hatred for God's sake (al-bughḍ fī Allāh) is a spiritual act of the heart (laṭīfah rabbāniyyah) distinguishing sincere faith from hypocrisy.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) — aversion of the heart; metaphorical (majāz) — manifesting aversion through outward acts of avoidance and censure.
- Root: ع ص و (ʿ-ṣ-w)
  * Lisan / Ayn: ʿiṣyān — disobedience and rebellion against a command; the ʿāṣī is one who transgresses the bound.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance — fisq (flagrant sin) is the departure from the straight path (khurūj ʿan al-ṭarīqah al-mustaqīmah) through willful transgression.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — breaking a command; metaphorical — persistence in sin without repentance.
- Root: ب د ع (b-d-ʿ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: bidʿah — an innovation, a newly invented matter in religion without precedent.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance — al-ibdāʿ is creation without model; for God it is bringing into being without instrument, matter, time, or place. For man, bidʿah is introducing into religion what is not from it.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — inventing something new; metaphorical — a weak argument (abdaʿat ḥujjatuka) or failing expectation.
- Root: ك ف ر (k-f-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: kufr — covering, concealing; the night is called kāfir for covering persons; the farmer (kāfir) covers the seed.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance — kufr is disbelief, the covering of truth; the kāfir is one who veils the truth of God's unity.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — covering (satar); metaphorical — ingratitude and rejection of divine blessings.
- Root: ق ل ب (q-l-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: qalb — the heart; taqallub — turning and changing from one state to another.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance — the heart's fluctuation (taqallub al-qulūb) between states of faith and heedlessness; the hearts of the common folk are quick to turn.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — turning a thing over; metaphorical — the instability of opinion and disposition.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Conditional Partitioning (Taqsīm al-Sharṭ) — the division of a genus into exhaustive species governed by conditional clauses (in kāna... fa-), each branch receiving its own ruling without conflation.

60:7.arabic: قال الله تعالى {عسى الله أن يجعل بينكم وبين الذين عاديتم منهم مودة} وقال عليه السلام أحبب حبيبك هونا ما عسى أن يكون بغيضك يوما ما وأبغض بغيضك هونا ما عسى أن يكون حبيبك يوما ما (1) وقال عمر رضي الله عنه لا يكن حبك كلفا ولا بغضك تلفا وهو أن تحب تلف صاحبك مع هلاكك الحق السادس الدعاء للأخ في حياته وبعد مماته بكل ما يحبه لنفسه ولأهله وكل متعلق به فتدعو له كما تدعو لنفسك ولا تفرق بين نفسك وبينه فإن دعاءك له دعاء لنفسك على التحقيق فقد قال صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا دعا الرجل لأخيه في ظهر الغيب قال الملك ولك مثل ذل
60:7.english: Abū Sulaymān al-Dārānī said to Aḥmad ibn Abī al-Ḥawārī: "If you take a brother in this age, do not reproach him for what you dislike, for you cannot be secure from seeing in his response to you something worse than the first [offense]." He said: "So I tried it, and I found it to be so."
60:7.section_title_en: Section 426 — On the Rights of Brotherhood: Forbearance, Moderation in Love and Hate, and Supplication for the Brother in Life and After Death
60:7.anchors:
- Root: شعث (sha-ʿatha)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Dishevelment, disorder of the hair; a state of being unkempt and scattered.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The condition of being disheveled or disordered, used metaphorically for the scattered, imperfect state of human affairs.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal for unkempt hair; metaphorical for the flawed, rough edges of a person's character that require forbearance.
- Root: وقع (wa-qa-ʿa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To fall, to occur, to befall; a falling into calamity.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-Wāqiʿah is not said except of severity and misfortune; most Quranic occurrences of "waqaʿa" pertain to chastisement and hardships.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: to fall to the ground. Metaphorical: to fall into slander or backbiting (al-waqīʿah), i.e., the utterance of evil against another.
- Root: وفي (wa-fā)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To fulfill, to complete, to be complete and whole.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-Wāfī: that which has reached completion. Awfā bi-ʿahdihi: to complete the covenant and not break its observance.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: a full dirham, a full measure. Metaphorical: to complete one's life term; al-wafāʾ as the perfection of loyalty.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The permissibility of interposing elements between a preposition and its object when the intervening phrase is semantically complete, allowing for rhetorical emphasis and rhythmic balance in periodic constructions.

60:10.arabic: وقد قال الله تعالى يا أيها الذين آمنوا أنفقوا من طيبات ما كسبتم ومما أخرجنا لكم من الأرض ولا تيمموا الخبيث منه تنفقون ولستم بآخذيه إلا أن تغمضوا فيه أي لا تأخذوه إلا مع كراهية وحياء وهو معنى الإغماض فلا تؤثروا به ربكم وفي الخبر سبق درهم مائة ألف درهم (3) وذلك بأن يخرجه الإنسان وهو من أحل ماله وأجوده فيصدر ذلك عن الرضا والفرح بالبذل وقد يخرج مائة ألف درهم مما يكره من ماله فيدل ذلك على أنه ليس يؤثر الله عز وجل بشيء مما يحبه وبذلك ذم الله تعالى قوما جعلوا لله ما يكرهون فقال تعال
60:10.english: The heart is not treated save with the compound electuary (maʿjūn) of knowledge and works. And this condition among the conditions of almsgiving runs in the same course as humility (al-khushūʿ) runs in the prayer. This is established by his saying — may Allah bless him and grant him peace: "A man has nothing of his prayer save that of which he was conscious." And this is like his saying — may Allah bless him and grant him peace: "Allah does not accept the charity of the one who bestows it with reproach (al-mannān)." And like His saying — Exalted is He: {«لا تبطلوا صدقاتكم بالمن والأذى»} ("Do not nullify your charities by reproach and injury"). As for the legal opinion (fatwā) of the jurist that the alms fall in their proper place and that one's liability is discharged without this condition — that is another discussion, and we have already pointed to its meaning in the Book of Prayer.

60:13.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Duties of Brotherhood'

60:13.arabic: ولم يستقر في القلب ولم يحركه إلى التوبة والتدارك أولئك يئسوا من الآخرة كما يئس الكفار من أصحاب القبور وهذا هو معنى اسوداد القلب بالذنوب كما نطق به القرآن والسنة قال ميمون بن مهران إذا أذنب العبد ذنبا نكت في قلبه نكته سوداء فإذا هو نزع وتاب صقل وإن عاد زيد فيها حتى يعلو قلبه فهو الران وقد قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قلب المؤمن أجرد فيه سراج يزهر وقلب الكافر أسود منكوس (2) حديث القلوب أربعة قلب أجرد فيه سراج يزهر الحديث أخرجه أحمد والطبراني في الصغير من حديث أبي سعيد الخدري وقد تقدم فمثل الإيمان فيه كمثل البقلة يمدها الماء الطيب ومثل النفاق فيه ك
60:13.english: As for the praiseworthy effects that we have mentioned, they increase the mirror of the heart in clarity (jalā'), radiance (ishrāq), light (nūr), and brilliance (ḍiyā'), until the clear truth (jalīyat al-ḥaqq) gleams within it and the reality of the sought-after matter in religion is unveiled in it. And it is to such a heart that the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, pointed when he said: "When God desires good for a servant, He appoints for him an admonisher from his own heart." (1) The hadith: "Whoever has from his heart an admonisher, upon him is from God a protector" — I have not found for it a source (aṣl).
60:13.section_title_en: The Heart as a Mirror: The Effects of Virtues and Vices upon Spiritual Perception
60:13.anchors:
- Root: قلب (q-l-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To turn over, to overturn, to transform from one state to another; the heart as that which is constantly fluctuating and turning between states.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "قلب الشيء: تصريفه وصرفه عن وجه إلى وجه" — The heart is that which is perpetually turned about, and its rectitude or corruption depends upon the direction of its turning.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): physical turning over. Metaphorical (Majaz): "قلب المعلم الصبيان: صرفهم إلى بيوتهم" — the turning of a thing toward its proper end. Here, the heart is a mirror (مرآة) turned toward either the light of truth or the darkness of sin.
- Root: رين (r-y-n)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Rust, tarnish, or filth that overcomes a polished surface, veiling its original brightness.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The covering of the heart by accumulated sin, such that it becomes rusted over and incapable of receiving the light of truth.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the tarnishing of a blade or mirror. Metaphorical: the veiling of the heart's perceptive faculty by the accumulation of transgressions, as in {«كلا بل ران على قلوبهم ما كانوا يكسبون»} (The Mutaffifin: 14).
- Root: طبع (t-b-')
  * Lisan / Ayn: To stamp, to seal, to impress upon; the imprinting of a seal that renders the surface impermeable to further impression.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The sealing of the heart by God as a consequence of persistent sin, rendering it deaf to admonition and blind to truth.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the physical stamping of a seal. Metaphorical: the divine sealing of the heart as a just consequence of willful persistence in transgression.
- Root: ذكر (dh-k-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Remembrance, recollection, mindfulness; the opposite of forgetfulness (نسيان).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The presence of the thing remembered in the mind; the highest form being the remembrance of God which brings tranquility to the heart.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: verbal invocation. Metaphorical: the state of spiritual presence and awareness that polishes the heart's mirror and unveils the reality of truth.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The syntactic connection between cause and effect, as in the verse {«واتقوا الله واسمعوا»}, where hearing (spiritual perception) is grammatically and semantically linked to piety (تقوى), just as the sealing of the heart (طبع) is linked to the accumulation of sins (ذنوب).

62:9.arabic: وقد قال الله تعالى يا أيها الذين آمنوا أنفقوا من طيبات ما كسبتم ومما أخرجنا لكم من الأرض ولا تيمموا الخبيث منه تنفقون ولستم بآخذيه إلا أن تغمضوا فيه أي لا تأخذوه إلا مع كراهية وحياء وهو معنى الإغماض فلا تؤثروا به ربكم وفي الخبر سبق درهم مائة ألف درهم (3) وذلك بأن يخرجه الإنسان وهو من أحل ماله وأجوده فيصدر ذلك عن الرضا والفرح بالبذل وقد يخرج مائة ألف درهم مما يكره من ماله فيدل ذلك على أنه ليس يؤثر الله عز وجل بشيء مما يحبه وبذلك ذم الله تعالى قوما جعلوا لله ما يكرهون فقال تعال
62:9.english: The heart is not treated save with the compound electuary (maʿjūn) of knowledge and works. And this condition among the conditions of almsgiving runs in the same course as humility (al-khushūʿ) runs in the prayer. This is established by his saying — may Allah bless him and grant him peace: "A man has nothing of his prayer save that of which he was conscious." And this is like his saying — may Allah bless him and grant him peace: "Allah does not accept the charity of the one who bestows it with reproach (al-mannān)." And like His saying — Exalted is He: {«لا تبطلوا صدقاتكم بالمن والأذى»} ("Do not nullify your charities by reproach and injury"). As for the legal opinion (fatwā) of the jurist that the alms fall in their proper place and that one's liability is discharged without this condition — that is another discussion, and we have already pointed to its meaning in the Book of Prayer.
62:9.section_title_en: The Inner Conditions of Charity — Section 175 (From The Revival of the Religious Sciences, Book of the Mysteries of Almsgiving)
62:9.anchors:
- Root: قلب (q-l-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "To turn, overturn, transform a thing from one state to another; to rotate, to flip"
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "قلب الشيء: تصريفه وصرفه عن وجه إلى وجه" — the heart is so named because of its constant turning and transformation between states
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "قلب الشيء قلبا: حوله عن وجهه" (to turn a thing from its face). Metaphorical: "رجل قلب حول: يقلب الأمور ويحتال" — one who turns matters over and manages them; "قلبوا لك الأمور" (they turned matters against you)
- Root: وجل (w-j-l)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "Fear, dread, apprehension that strikes the heart"
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الوجل: استشعار الخوف" — the sensing of fear; cited in {«إنما المؤمنون الذين إذا ذكر الله وجلت قلوبهم»}
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "رجل وجل، وقوم وجال" — a fearful man, a fearful people; "وفي قلبه وجل" — in his heart is dread
- Root: عجب (ʿ-j-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "Wonder, amazement; self-admiration, vanity"
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Self-admiration (al-ʿujb) is a destructive spiritual ailment that nullifies deeds
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: wonder at something extraordinary. Metaphorical: self-conceit regarding one's own acts of obedience

62:9.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Duties of Brotherhood'

62:9.arabic: قال الله تعالى {إذا نودي للصلاة من يوم الجمعة فاسعوا إلى ذكر الله وذروا البيع} فحرم الاشتغال بأمور الدنيا وبكل صارف عن السعي إلى الجمعة وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم إن الله عز وجل فرض عليكم الجمعة في يومي هذا في مقامي هذا (1) وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم من ترك الجمعة ثلاثا من غير عذر طبع الله على قلبه (2) وفي لفظ آخر فقد نبذ الإسلام وراء ظهره (3) واختلف رجل إلى ابن عباس يسأله عن رجل مات لم يكن يشهد جمعة ولا جماعة فقال في النار فلم يزل يتردد إليه شهرا يسأله عن ذلك وهو يقول في النار وفي الخبر إن أهل الكتابين أعطوا يوم
62:9.english: Know that this is a momentous day, by which Allah magnified Islam and singled out the Muslims exclusively. Allah, the Exalted, said: {«O you who believe! When the call is proclaimed for the prayer on Friday, hasten earnestly to the remembrance of Allah and leave off business»} (al-Jumuʿah 62:9). Thus, He prohibited engagement in worldly affairs and every distraction that turns one away from hastening to the Friday [prayer].
62:9.section_title_en: The Revival of the Religious Sciences — Book on the Etiquettes of Recitation, Section 145 (Continuation) & Chapter V: On the Excellence, Etiquettes, and Conditions of Friday (Jumuʿah)
62:9.anchors:
- Root: رفع (rafʿ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To raise, elevate, lift up; also to remove or abolish.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Elevation in rank or physical lifting; in ritual context, the raising of hands (rafʿ al-yadayn) as a physical gesture signifying supplication and humility before the Divine.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) physical lifting of the hands; metaphorical (majāz) elevation of one's station or the removal of a burden.
- Root: سعى (saʿy)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To walk quickly, to strive, to exert oneself; to run toward a goal.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Striving and hastening toward an objective; in the Quranic context of Friday, it denotes the earnest, purposeful movement toward the remembrance of Allah, leaving aside worldly transactions.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal physical hastening; metaphorical striving in obedience and abandoning distractions.
- Root: عيد (ʿīd)
  * Lisan / Ayn: A recurring festival or celebration; from the root meaning to return (ʿāda), signifying a day that returns annually or weekly.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): A day of gathering and joy appointed by Allah; for the Muslims, Friday is designated as a weekly festival (ʿīd) of communal worship and divine bounty.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal recurring day of celebration; metaphorical reference to the eternal "Day of Increase" (Yawm al-Mazīd) in the Hereafter, a festival of divine vision.
- Root: تجلى (tajallā)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To manifest, reveal, disclose oneself; to appear clearly.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The self-disclosure of the Divine to the blessed in Paradise; a theophany of grace, not of corporeal essence.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal unveiling or appearing; metaphorical for the beatific vision (ruʾyah) granted to the believers, a reality beyond spatial or material limitation.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Interposition (al-Faṣl bayna al-Jār wa al-Majrūr) — The separation of the prepositional phrase from its governing verb is permissible when the intervening clause is complete and meaningful, as in the structure of the ḥadīth, preserving clarity of syntax without ambiguity.

2:235.arabic: فقيرا عليه خرقتان فقلت في نفسي هذا وأشباهه كل على الناس فناداني وقال والله يعلم ما في أنفسكم فاحذروه فاستغفرت الله في سري فناداني وقال {وهو الذي يقبل التوبة عن عباده} ثم غاب عني ولم أره وقال زكريا بن داود دخل أبو العباس بن مسروق على أبي الفضل الهاشمي وهو عليل وكان ذا عيال ولم يعرف له سبب يعيش به قال فلما قمت قلت في نفسي من أين يأكل هذا الرجل قال فصاح بي يا أبا العباس رد هذه الهمة الدنية فإن لله تعالى ألطافا خفية وقال أحمد النقيب دخلت على الشبلي فقال مفتونا يا أحمد فقلت ما الخبر قال كنت جالسا فجرى بخاطري أنك بخيل فقلت ما أنا بخيل فعاد
2:235.english: As for the evidences of the Sacred Law, there is His saying (Exalted is He): {«وَالَّذِينَ جَاهَدُوا فِينَا لَنَهْدِيَنَّهُمْ سُبُلَنَا»} ("And those who strive in Us, We shall surely guide them to Our paths") (Q. 29:69). So every wisdom that appears from the heart through persevering devotion to worship, without learning, is by way of unveiling and inspiration. And he (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Whoever acts upon what he knows, God bequeaths to him knowledge of what he does not know, and grants him success in what he does" — until he becomes deserving of Paradise. And whoever does not act upon what he knows wanders astray in what he knows and is not granted success in what he does, until he becomes deserving of the Fire. [The hadith "Whoever acts upon what he knows" has preceded in the Book of Knowledge, without his saying "and grants him success in what he does" — I have not found it with that addition.] And God (Exalted is He) said: {«وَمَنْ يَتَّقِ اللَّهَ يَجْعَلْ لَهُ مَخْرَجًا»} ("And whoever fears God, He makes for him a way out") (Q. 65:2) — from perplexities and doubts — {«وَيَرْزُقْهُ مِنْ حَيْثُ لَا يَحْتَسِبُ»} ("and provides for him from whence he does not reckon") (Q. 65:3) — teaching him knowledge without learning and granting him discernment without experience. And God (Exalted is He) said: {«يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا إِنْ تَتَّقُوا اللَّهَ يَجْعَلْ لَكُمْ فُرْقَانًا»} ("O you who believe, if you fear God, He will make for you a criterion") (Q. 8:29) — it is said: a light by which one distinguishes between truth and falsehood and by which one emerges from doubts. For this reason, he (peace and blessings be upon him) was abundant in his supplication in asking for light, saying (peace and blessings be upon him): "O God, grant me light, and increase me in light, and make for me light in my heart, and light in my grave, and light in my hearing, and light in my sight" — until he said: "and light in my hair, and in my skin, and in my flesh, and in my blood, and in my bones." [Agreed upon (by al-Bukhari and Muslim).] [The hadith concerning his being asked about His saying {«أَفَمَنْ شَرَحَ اللَّهُ صَدْرَهُ لِلْإِسْلَامِ»} ("Is he whose breast God has expanded for Islam") (Q. 39:22) — and in al-Mustadrak from the hadith of Ibn Masʿūd — has preceded in the Book of Knowledge.] And he (peace and blessings be upon him) said concerning Ibn ʿAbbās: "O God, grant him understanding in religion and teach him the interpretation (taʾwīl)." [The hadith of ʿAlī: "We have nothing with us that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) confided to us except that God grants a servant understanding in His Book" — has preceded in the Etiquettes of Qurʾanic Recitation.] And it is said in the interpretation of His saying (Exalted is He): {«يُؤْتِي الْحِكْمَةَ مَنْ يَشَاءُ»} ("He grants wisdom to whom He wills") (Q. 2:269) that it is understanding in the Book of God. And He (Exalted is He) said: {«فَفَهَّمْنَاهَا سُلَيْمَانَ»} ("And We made Solomon understand it") (Q. 21:79) — singling out what was unveiled with the name of understanding (fahm). And Abū al-Dardāʾ used to say: "The believer is one who sees by the light of God from behind a thin veil. By God, it is the truth that God casts into their hearts and causes to flow upon their tongues." And some of the Salaf said: "The believer's conjecture is like soothsaying."
2:235.section_title_en: The Unveiling of Knowledge Through Divine Inspiration and the Evidences of the Unseen
2:235.anchors:
- Root: علم (ʿalima)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning encompasses both perception of a thing's essence and judgment upon it—knowledge as direct apprehension or discursive ruling.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "العلم: إدراك الشيء بحقيقته" — knowledge is the apprehension of a thing in its true reality, divided into apprehension of the essence (transitive to one object) and judgment upon existence or non-existence (transitive to two objects).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal usage denotes certainty and awareness ("ما علمت بخبرك: ما شعرت به"); metaphorical extension applies to marks, signs, and beacons of guidance (معالم الطريق) — here, the inspired knowledge is a "mark" of the path.
- Root: كشف (kashafa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To remove a covering, unveil, disclose what was hidden.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Unveiling (kashf) in theological terms is the removal of the veil (ghishāwah) from the heart such that the realities of things become directly witnessed, not merely inferred.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: to lift a covering from a thing; metaphorical: the disclosure of inward states and hidden matters — the heart's eye perceives what the outward senses cannot.
- Root: فرس (farasa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To prey upon, devour; farāsah — the lion's pouncing upon its prey.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Discernment (farāsah) is a spiritual perception by which the believer penetrates into the inner states of others, a light cast by God into the heart.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the beast of prey seizing its quarry; metaphorical: the believer's insight seizing the truth of a matter or the hidden state of a person — "اتقوا فراسة المؤمن فإنه ينظر بنور الله."
- Root: حدث (ḥadatha)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To be new, originate after non-existence; muḥaddath — one who is spoken to, inspired with true speech from the unseen.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الحدوث: كون الشيء بعد أن لم يكن" — origination after non-existence; the muḥaddath is one to whom divine inspiration comes as a new, immediate occurrence without acquired means.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: newness of a thing; metaphorical: "كان عمر رضي الله عنه محدثا أي صادق الحدس، كأنما حدث بما ظن" — one whose intuition is so true it is as if he were directly spoken to.
- Sibawayh Rule: Restriction and specification (الحصر والتقييد) — the particle "إنما" and conditional clauses (إن/إذا) restrict predicates to their subjects, as in "إنما العالم الذي يأخذ علمه من ربه" — the true scholar is exclusively the one who takes knowledge from his Lord.

2:235.arabic: بعيدا ويحذركم الله نفسه} وقال تعالى {واعلموا أن الله يعلم ما في أنفسكم فاحذروه} فعرف أرباب البصائر من جملة العباد أن الله تعالى لهم بالمرصاد وأنهم سيناقشون في الحساب ويطالبون بمثاقيل الذر من الخطرات واللحظات وتحققوا أنه لا ينجيهم من هذه الأخطار إلا لزوم المحاسبة وصدق المراقبة ومطالبة النفس في الأنفاس والحركات ومحاسبتها في الخطرات واللحظات فمن حاسب نفسه قبل أن يحاسب خف في القيامة حسابه وحضر عند السؤال جوابه وحسن منقلبه ومآبه ومن لم يحاسب نفسه دامت حسراته وطالت في عرصات القيامة وقفاته وقادته إلى الخزي والمقت
2:235.english: To proceed: God Most High has said: {And We shall set up the scales of justice for the Day of Resurrection, so no soul shall be wronged in anything; and if it be the weight of a grain of mustard seed, We shall bring it forth, and sufficient are We as Reckoners} (21:47). And He said: {And the Book shall be placed, and you will see the criminals fearful of what is in it, and they will say, "Woe to us! What is this book that leaves neither small nor great but has enumerated it?" And they will find what they did present, and your Lord wrongs no one} (18:49). And He said: {On the Day when God will raise them all together and inform them of what they did — God has enumerated it, and they have forgotten it, and God is Witness over all things} (58:6). And He said: {On that Day, people will issue forth in scattered groups to be shown their deeds. So whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it, and whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it} (99:6-8). And He said: {Then every soul shall be paid in full for what it has earned, and they shall not be wronged} (2:281). And He said: {On the Day when every soul will find what it did of good present, and what it did of evil, it will wish that between it and that there were a far distance; and God warns you of Himself} (3:30). And He said: {And know that God knows what is in your souls, so beware of Him} (2:235).
2:235.section_title_en: Exposition of the Reality of Truthfulness (Al-Sidq), Its Meaning, and Its Grades — Book of Vigilance and Self-Reckoning, Being the Eighth Book of the Quarter of Deliverance from the Revival of the Religious Sciences
2:235.anchors:
- Root: رقب (Raqaba)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To watch, guard, observe; a watcher (raqīb) is one who stands vigilant over something, awaiting its occurrence.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Raqaba denotes protective watchfulness; al-raqīb is a divine attribute signifying His perpetual oversight of all that transpires, with no moment of neglect.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (haqīqah): physical watching/awaiting. Metaphorical (majāz): "This matter is upon your necks (fī riqābikum)" — i.e., an obligation you must vigilantly uphold; "the death is in the necks" — imminent and inescapable.
- Root: حسب (Hasaba)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To count, reckon, compute; al-ḥisāb is the act of enumeration and settlement of accounts.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-ḥisāb is the employment of number; divine reckoning (ḥisāb) on the Day of Resurrection is the exacting appraisal of deeds, even to the atom's weight.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: counting wealth or deeds. Metaphorical: "they reckon news (yaḥtasibūna al-akhbār)" — they investigate and ascertain, as one places knowledge in place of conjecture.
- Root: قلب (Qalaba)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To turn, overturn, transform; the heart (qalb) is so named for its constant fluctuation and turning of states.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Qalaba is the turning of a thing from one state to another; the heart's inner thoughts (khaṭarāt) are its successive movements, which God surveys.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: turning a garment or object. Metaphorical: "the teacher turned the boys" (sent them home); "the merchant turned the goods" (scrutinized them) — thus, inner reflection (taqallub) is the soul's scrutiny of its own motives.
- Sibawayh Rule: Restriction and Focused Predication (al-ḥaṣr wa al-taqyīd bi-innamā) — The particle innamā restricts the predicate to the subject alone, as in "إنما يحاسبهم لتعلم كل نفس" — the sole purpose of reckoning is specified, excluding all other ends.

2:281.arabic: توفي كل نفس ما كسبت {وأن} كل نفس بما كسبت رهينة فما الذي غركم بالله بعد أن سمعتم وعقلتم قالوا لو كنا نسمع أو نعقل ما كنا في أصحاب السعير فاعترفوا بذنبهم فسحقا لأصحاب السعير فإن قلت فأين مظنة الرجاء وموضعه المحمود فاعلم أنه محمود في موضعين أحدهما في حق العاصي المنهمك إذا خطرت له التوبة فقال له الشيطان وأنى تقبل توبتك فيقنطه من رحمة الله تعالى فيجب عند هذا أن يقمع القنوط بالرجاء ويتذكر أن الله يغفر الذنوب جميعا وأن الله كريم يقبل التوبة عن عباده وأن التوبة طاعة تكفر الذنو
2:281.english: Every soul shall taste what it has earned. And {«وَأَنَّ كُلَّ نَفْسٍ بِمَا كَسَبَتْ رَهِينَةٌ»} — "And that every soul is a pledge for what it has earned." So what has deluded you concerning God, after you have heard and comprehended? They will say: "Had we but listened or reasoned, we would not be among the companions of the Blaze." Thus they will confess their sin. So away with the companions of the Blaze!
2:281.section_title_en: The Anatomy of Hope (Rajā') and Delusion (Ghurūr): A Kalamic Dissection of the Soul's Two States
2:281.anchors:
- Root: نفس (Nafs)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The self, soul, or spirit; that which desires proximity and discourse; the locus of breath and life.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Nafs denotes the rūḥ (spirit) and, in divine attribution, the very Dhāt (Essence) of God—as in {«وَيُحَذِّرُكُمُ اللَّهُ نَفْسَهُ»}—entailing no real multiplicity despite grammatical annexation.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah) usage refers to the living, breathing self; metaphorical (Majaz) usage extends to "blood" (nafs sā'ilah) and the "evil eye" (nafs as 'ayn). Here, it signifies the moral agent bearing responsibility.
- Root: توب (Tawb)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Return, repentance; the act of turning back from error.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Tawbah is abandoning the sin in the most excellent manner—the third and highest form of excuse (after denial and pretext). In Sacred Law: forsaking the sin due to its ugliness, remorse for the past, resolve against recurrence, and restitution of what can be restored.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "The servant repents to God from his sin; God turns in mercy to the servant." The reciprocal dynamic—God's acceptance (tawbah) meeting the servant's return (inābah)—is operative in this text.
- Root: ذنب (Dhanb)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The tail of an animal; what trails behind; by extension, a fault or crime as the "consequence" one drags after oneself.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In origin, "taking hold of a thing's tail"—i.e., seizing the outcome. Sin is that which trails the soul and binds it as a pledge (rahīnah).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Metaphorical: "He is among the tails (adhnāb) of the people"—the laggards. The sinner is one who follows his lower tail, and the verse {«كُلُّ نَفْسٍ بِمَا كَسَبَتْ رَهِينَةٌ»} makes the soul a hostage to its own trailing deeds.
- Root: غفر (Ghafr)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To cover, shield, or protect; the Ghifār tribe's name; a helmet (mighfar) that shields the head.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Ghufrān from God is His shielding the servant from the touch of chastisement—a protective covering, not mere erasure. It may also mean outward forbearance.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "O God, forgive (ghufrānan)!"—a covering over the stain. Metaphorical: Zuhayr's beasts "did not forgive" their negligence—i.e., did not shield the offspring from destruction. Hope of forgiveness without repentance is thus not ghufrān but ghurūr (delusion).
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين العامل والمعمول (Interposition between Operator and Operand) — The periodic structure of verses like {«إِنَّ اللَّهَ يَغْفِرُ الذُّنُوبَ جَمِيعًا»} delays the predicate to heighten rhetorical impact; the conditional "if you say... know that" (fa-in qulta... fa-'lam) governs the entire dialectical sequence, requiring the apodosis to resolve the protasis with logical necessity.
