##
9:18.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications, prayers, and their spiritual power, from 'Mysteries of Prayer'

9:19.arabic: الشك في هذا الصدق وكذلك قال الله تعالى ولكن البر من آمن بالله واليوم الآخر والملائكة والكتاب والنبيين فشرط عشرين وصفا كالوفاء بالعهد والصبر على الشدائد ثم قال تعالى أولئك الذين صدقوا وقد قال تعالى يرفع الله الذين آمنوا منكم والذين أوتوا العلم درجات وقال تعالى لا يستوي منكم من أنفق من قبل الفتح وقاتل الآية وقد قال تعالى هم درجات عند الله وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم الإيمان عريان ولباسه التقوى (1) الحديث وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم الإيمان بضع وسبعون بابا أدناها إماطة الأذى عن الطريق فهذا ما يدل على ارتباط كمال الإيمان بالأعمال وأ
9:19.english: ...doubt concerning this truthfulness. Likewise, God Most High said: {«But righteousness is he who believes in God and the Last Day and the angels and the Book and the prophets»} (2:177) — thus He conditioned twenty attributes, such as faithfulness to covenant and patience under hardship. Then He said Most High: {«Those are the truthful ones»} (2:177). And God Most High said: {«God will raise those who have believed among you and those who have been given knowledge, by degrees»} (58:11). And He said Most High: {«Not equal among you are those who spent before the conquest and fought»} (57:10). And He said Most High: {«They are degrees before God»} (3:163). And the Prophet, peace be upon him, said: "Faith is naked, and its garment is God-consciousness (al-taqwā)." And the Prophet, peace be upon him, said: "Faith has seventy-some branches; the lowest of them is removing harm from the path." All this indicates the interconnection of the perfection of faith with works.
9:19.section_title_en: The Revival of the Religious Sciences — Book of the Secrets of Zakāh, Section 104: On the Degrees of Faith and Its Connection to Works, and the Hidden Hypocrisy (al-Nifāq al-Khafī) That Contradicts the Perfection of Faith
9:19.anchors:
- Root: ن ف ق (N-F-Q)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Root denotes passing away, depletion, and expenditure; also the underground burrow of the jerboa (nāfiqāʾ) with a concealed exit — the etymological basis for hypocrisy as a hidden exit from faith.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "نفق الشيء: مضى ونفد" — theological nuance: hypocrisy (nifāq) is that which causes faith to expire and pass away, whether by sale (worldly gain) or by death (spiritual ruin).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "نفقت الدراهم" (coins ran out). Metaphorical: "نفق روحه: خرج" (his soul expired and went forth) — hence the hypocrite's faith is one whose spirit has already departed.
- Root: أ ي م (A-Y-M)
  * Lisan / Ayn: A woman without a husband; a man long unmarried. Al-Raghib: "الحرب مأيمة" — war makes women widows.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "تركوا النساء أيامى" (they left women widowed). Metaphorical application: the one who feels secure from hypocrisy is like one who claims immunity from widowhood — a false security.
- Root: و ف ي (W-F-Y)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Fullness, completion, fulfillment of a measure or covenant.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الوافي: الذي بلغ التمام" — the one who has reached completion. "أوفى: إذا تمم العهد ولم ينقض حفظه" — to fulfill the covenant without breach.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "درهم واف" (a full-weight dirham). Metaphorical: "أوفى على المائة" (he surpassed a hundred) — faith's perfection (wafāʾ) is only attained by surpassing mere profession to include works and inward sincerity.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد (Restriction & Focused Predication) — governing the grammatical force of "إنما" constructions and conditional clauses (من كان...), where the predicate is restricted to the condition stated, as in the hadith "أربع من كن فيه فهو منافق خالص" — the four traits are exhaustive of the ruling.
9:19.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'Monitoring and Accounting'

9:19.arabic: وتصدق بماله وجاهد في سبيل الله واجتنب محارم الله غير أنه يؤتى به يوم القيامة فيقال إن هذا عظم في عينه ما صغره الله وصغر في عينه ما عظمه الله كيف ترى يكون حاله فمن منا ليس هكذا الدنيا عظيمة عنده مع ما اقترفنا من الذنوب والخطايا وقال أبو حازم اشتدت مؤنة الدنيا والآخرة فأما مؤنة الآخرة فإنك لا تجد عليها أعوانا وأما مؤنة الدنيا فإنك لا تضرب بيدك إلى شيء منها إلا وجدت فاجرا قد سبقك إليه وقال أبو هريرة الدنيا موقوفة بين السماء والأرض كالشن البالي تنادي ربها منذ خلقها إلى يوم يفني
9:19.english: Al-Hasan said: "By Allah, I have known people for whom the world was more insignificant than the dust upon which you walk. They cared not whether the world rose or set, whether it went to this one or to that one."
9:19.topic: Al-Ghazali on the journey of the soul, death, and the Hereafter, from 'Condemnation of the World'

9:81.arabic: الرمضاء فكان يقول لنفسه ذوقى ونار جهنم أشد حرا أجيفة بالليل بطالة بالنهار فبينما هو كذلك إذ أبصر النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في ظل شجرة فأتاه فقال غلبتني نفسي فقال له النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ألم يكن لك بد من الذي صنعت أما لقد فتحت لك أبواب السماء ولقد باهى الله بك الملائكة ثم قال لأصحابه تزودوا من أخيكم فجعل الرجل يقول له يا فلان أدع لي يا فلان ادع لى فقال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم عمهم فقال اللهم أجعل التقوى زادهم واجمع على الهدى أمرهم فجعل النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول اللهم سدده فقال الرجل الله
9:81.english: A woman said: "You speak of what you do not know. Indeed, God has a covenant upon me which I shall never break: I shall not lay you upon the earth in sleep for a full year, except due to an obstructing illness or a departing intellect. Shame upon you! Do you not feel ashamed? How often you rebuke, yet from your error you do not desist." He said: And he began to weep, unaware of my presence. When I saw that, I departed and left him.
9:81.section_title_en: The Discipline of the Self: Accounts of the Pious in Reckoning and Punishing Their Souls
9:81.anchors:
- Root: نفس (n-f-s)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The self, soul, spirit; that which breathes and desires; the locus of blameworthy and praiseworthy traits.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-nafs denotes the soul as the principle of life and moral responsibility; its reckoning (muḥāsabah) is the essence of religious discipline.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the self as animate entity. Metaphorical: "دفق نفسه" (he poured out his self, i.e., his blood) — here, the self is addressed as a distinct interlocutor, a rhetorical personification of the lower impulses.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب النداء والتوبيخ (The Chapter of Direct Address and Rebuke) — The self is vocatively addressed (يا نفسي) as a second party, establishing the grammatical frame of moral confrontation.
9:81.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Monitoring and Accounting'

15:29.arabic: أمره بإضافته إليه إذ قال تعالى إني خالق بشرا من طين فإذا سويته ونفخت فيه من روحي فقعوا له ساجدين فنبه على أن الجسد منسوب إلى الطين والروح إلى رب العالمين والمراد بالروح والنفس في هذا المقام واحد فالخلق عبارة عن هيئة في النفس راسخة عنها تصدر الأفعال بسهولة ويسر من غير حاجة إلى فكر وروية فإن كانت الهيئة بحيث تصدر عنها الأفعال الجميلة المحمودة عقلا وشرعا سميت تلك الهيئة خلقا حسنا وإن كان الصادر عنها الأفعال القبيحة سميت الهيئة التي هي المصدر خلقا سيئا وإنما قلنا إنها هيئة راسخة لأن من يصدر منه بذل المال على الندور لحاجة عارضة
15:29.english: I say: Know that people have spoken concerning the reality of good character (ḥusn al-khulq) — what it is — yet they have not addressed its true nature; rather, they have addressed its fruits. Then they did not even exhaust all of its fruits, but each one mentioned only those fruits that occurred to him and were present in his mind. They did not direct their attention to mentioning its definition (ḥadd) and its reality (ḥaqīqah) that encompasses all its fruits in detail and with completeness. This is like the saying of al-Ḥasan: "Good character is a cheerful face, the giving of bounty, and the withholding of harm." Al-Wāsiṭī said: "It is that one neither disputes nor is disputed with, by virtue of his intense knowledge of God most high." Shāh al-Kirmānī said: "It is the withholding of harm and the bearing of burdens." Some said: "It is that one be near to people, yet a stranger among them." Al-Wāsiṭī said on another occasion: "It is the pleasing of creation in prosperity and adversity." Abū ʿUthmān said: "It is satisfaction with God most high." Sahl al-Tustarī was asked about good character, and he said: "Its lowest degree is forbearance, the abandonment of retaliation, mercy toward the oppressor, seeking forgiveness for him, and compassion toward him." He said on another occasion: "It is that one does not accuse the Truth concerning provision, but trusts in Him, and reposes in His faithfulness to what He has guaranteed, so that he obeys Him and does not disobey Him in all matters — both in what is between him and his Lord, and in what is between him and people." ʿAlī, may God be pleased with him, said: "Good character consists in three qualities: avoiding forbidden things, seeking what is lawful, and enlarging one's provision upon one's dependents." Al-Ḥusayn ibn Manṣūr said: "It is that the harshness of creation does not affect you after your contemplation of the Truth." Abū Saʿīd al-Kharrāz said: "It is that you have no concern other than God most high." This and the like of it is abundant — and it is an addressing of the fruits of good character, not of its very self. Nor is it even encompassing of all the fruits.
15:29.section_title_en: The Reality of Good Character (Ḥusn al-Khulq) — Its True Nature and the Four Pillars of the Soul
15:29.anchors:
- Root: خلق (Kh-L-Q)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "التقدير المستقيم" — precise measurement and fashioning; the outward form (khalq) and inward disposition (khuluq) as twin designations of the same root.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "إبداع الشيء من غير أصل ولا احتذاء" — origination without precedent; here extended to the soul's innate constitution, which God alone originates and proportions.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Haqiqah: "خلق الخراز الأديم" — the tanner measures the hide before cutting. Majaz: "خلق الله الخلق: أوجده على تقدير أوجبته الحكمة" — God's creation as measured origination. Thus khuluq is the soul's measured inward form, as khalq is the body's measured outward form.
- Root: حسن (Ḥ-S-N)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Beauty and comeliness in both visible and invisible orders.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الحسن: عبارة عن كل مبهج مرغوب فيه" — that which delights and is desired; three kinds: rational, appetitive, sensory. The good character is that which reason and revelation (ʿaqlan wa sharʿan) deem beautiful.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Haqiqah: "أنظر إلى محاسن وجهه" — visible beauties. Majaz: "فلان لا يحسن شيئا" — competence and virtue as moral beauty. The "beautiful" act is the metaphorical extension of visible comeliness to inward excellence.
- Root: نفس (N-F-S)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The self, soul, spirit; that which is valued and precious.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "النفس: الروح" — the soul as spirit; in the verse {«ونفخت فيه من روحي»} the soul is that which is divinely breathed, distinguished from the clay body.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Haqiqah: "شيء نفيس" — precious thing. Majaz: "دفق نفسه أي دمه" — the self as the whole living person. Here, the soul (nafs) perceived by inner vision (baṣīrah) is of greater rank than the body perceived by sight (baṣar).
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — The author's repeated "إنما قلنا" and "ليس الخلق عبارة عن..." employ restrictive predication to delimit the definition of khuluq against rival candidates (act, power, knowledge), each negated in turn before the fourth meaning is affirmed.
15:29.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Fear and Hope'

15:29.arabic: وحذرتك سخطى ألم أخلقك بيدى ونفخت فيك من روحى وأسجدت لك ملائكتى فعصيت أمرى ونسيت عهدى وتعرضت لسخطى فو عزتى وجلالى لو ملأت الأرض رجالا كلهم مثلك يعبدونني ويسبحونني ثم عصونى لأنزلتهم منازل العاصين فبكى آدم عليه السلام عند ذلك ثلثمائة عام وكان عبيد الله البجلى كثير البكاء يقول في بكائه طول ليله إلهى أنا الذى كلما طال عمرى زادت ذنوبى أنا الذى كلما هممت بترك خطيئة عرضت لى شهوة أخرى واعبيداه خطيئة لم تبل وصاحبها في طلب أخرى واعبيداه إن كانت النار لك مقيلا ومأوى واعبيداه إن كانت المقامع برأسك تهيأ
15:29.english: Following the example of your father Adam (upon him be peace). For Wahb ibn Munabbih related: When God caused Adam to descend from Paradise to the earth, he remained in a state where his tears would not dry. Then God—mighty and majestic is He—looked upon him on the seventh day, and he was sorrowful, dejected, and choked with grief, his head bowed low. So God—exalted is He—revealed to him: "O Adam, what is this anguish I see in you?" He said: "O my Lord, my calamity has become immense, my sin has encompassed me, and I have been expelled from the dominion of my Lord. I have come to dwell in the abode of humiliation after honor, in the abode of misery after happiness, in the abode of toil after rest, in the abode of tribulation after well-being, in the abode of transience after permanence, and in the abode of death and annihilation after immortality and endurance. How should I not weep over my sin?" So God—exalted is He—revealed to him: "O Adam, did I not choose you for Myself, settle you in My abode, single you out with My honor, and warn you of My wrath? Did I not create you with My hand, breathe into you of My spirit, and cause My angels to prostrate before you? Yet you disobeyed My command, forgot My covenant, and exposed yourself to My wrath. By My might and My majesty, were I to fill the earth with men, all of them like you, worshipping Me and glorifying Me, and then they disobeyed Me, I would cast them down to the stations of the disobedient." At that, Adam (upon him be peace) wept for three hundred years.
15:29.section_title_en: Section 1255 — The Supplication of the Distressed and the Path of the Devout in Private Confession
15:29.anchors:
- Root: ضرر (ḍ-r-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of hardship, harm, and dire necessity; al-muḍṭarr is one compelled by overwhelming distress.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance of existential neediness before God, where the creature’s incapacity meets divine sufficiency.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) sense of physical/compelling necessity; metaphorical (majāz) extension to spiritual desperation and supplication.
- Root: كرم (k-r-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Nobility and generosity as intrinsic qualities of character and divine action.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): When ascribed to God, denotes His manifest, overflowing beneficence; when to humans, praiseworthy acts and virtues.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: abundant giving; metaphorical: the "generosity" of rain-laden clouds or a land rich in bounty.
- Root: عفو (ʿ-f-w)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Erasure, pardon, and remission of a fault; to leave something unpunished.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Divine pardon as the effacement of sin and the restoration of the sinner to a state of grace.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: blotting out; metaphorical: comprehensive mercy that "covers" (shāmil) all transgressions.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب النداء والتضرع (The Chapter of Vocative Appeal and Supplication) — Governing the syntactic patterns of direct address (yā) with epithets of divine mercy, and the anaphoric repetition of "anā" (I am...) for emphatic self-abasement.
15:29.topic: Al-Ghazali on the journey of the soul, death, and the Hereafter, from 'Monitoring and Accounting'

15:44.arabic: التجارة وبها تتم أعمال هذه التجارة وإن لجهنم سبعة أبواب لكل باب منهم جزء مقسوم وإنما تتعين تلك الأبواب لمن عصى الله تعالى بهذه الأعضاء فيوصيها بحفظها عن معاصيها أما العين فيحفظها عن النظر إلى وجه من ليس له بمحرم أو إلى عورة مسلم أو النظر إلى مسلم بعين الاحتقار بل عن كل فضول مستغنى عنه فإن الله تعالى يسأل عبده عن فضول النظر كما يسأله عن فضول الكلام ثم إذا صرفها عن هذا لم تقنع به حتى يشغلها بما فيه تجارتها وربحها وهو ما خلقت له من النظر إلى عجائب صنع الله بعين الاعتبار والنظر إلى أعمال الخير للاقتداء والنظر في كتاب الله وسنة ر
15:44.english: And some have said: "Grant that the wrongdoer has been pardoned—has he not still missed the reward of the righteous?"—pointing thereby to the loss and regret. And God Most High says: {«يَوْمَ يَجْمَعُكُمْ لِيَوْمِ الْجَمْعِ ذَٰلِكَ يَوْمُ التَّغَابُنِ»} ("The Day He will gather you for the Day of Gathering—that is the Day of Mutual Loss") (Al-Taghābun 64:9). So this is his counsel to his soul concerning his hours.
15:44.section_title_en: The Revival of the Religious Sciences — Section 1232: The Soul's Covenant with Itself and Reckoning Before Deeds
15:44.anchors:
- Root: نفس (n-f-s)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The self, soul, or spirit; that which breathes and animates; the essence of a thing.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-nafs denotes the rūḥ (spirit) and, in theological contexts, the very dhāt (essence/self) of a being—as in {«وَيُحَذِّرُكُمُ اللَّهُ نَفْسَهُ»} (Āl ʿImrān 3:28), where "His self" means His essence, not a separate entity.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): the soul as the seat of desire and action. Metaphorical (majāz): "دفق نفسه" (he poured out his self = his blood); the soul as a recalcitrant entity requiring discipline.
- Root: يوم (y-w-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: A day, from sunrise to sunset; also any span of time, especially the Day of Reckoning.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Yawm signifies the period of the sun's course, but metaphorically extends to any era—most critically "the Day of Gathering" (yawm al-jamʿ) and "the Day of Mutual Loss" (yawm al-taghābun), where God's attribution of the day to Himself signals its supreme gravity.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: a 24-hour cycle. Metaphorical: "أيام الله" (the days of God) = His punitive acts against the disbelievers, as in {«وَذَكِّرْهُمْ بِأَيَّامِ اللَّهِ»} (Ibrāhīm 14:5).
- Root: حسب (ḥ-s-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To count, reckon, or compute; also to suffice.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Ḥisāb is the employment of number; the Day of Judgment is the day of reckoning where deeds are weighed. The "ḥusbān" (computation) of the sun and moon (Al-Anʿām 6:96) marks time for human accountability.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: counting wealth or deeds. Metaphorical: "احتسبت ما عند فلان" (I probed what so-and-so possesses) = testing and examining, as the soul must examine its own intentions and acts before God's scrutiny.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — The text uses conditional and imperative constructions (e.g., "فإياك ثم إياك" and "ليشترط على نفسه") to impose binding covenants, where the predicate restricts the soul's scope of action, demanding a precise, self-imposed legal obligation.
15:44.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Monitoring and Accounting'

16:9.arabic: {ثم إن علينا بيانه} وقال {وعلى الله قصد السبيل} وقال علي كرم الله وجهه الهوى شريك العمى ومن التوفيق التوقف عند الحيرة ونعم طارد الهم اليقين وعاقبة الكذب الندم وفي الصدق السلامة رب بعيد أقرب من قريب وغريب من لم يكن له حبيب والصديق من صدق غيبه ولا يعدمك من حبيب سوء ظن نعم الخلق التكرم والحياء سبب إلى كل جميل وأوثق العرا التقوى واوثق سبب أخذت به سبب بينك وبين الله تعالى إنما لك من دنياك ما أصلحت به مثواك والرزق رزقان رزق تطلبه ورزق يطلبك فان لم تأته أتاك وإن كنت جازعا على ما أصيب مما في يدي
16:9.english: This pausing at the beginnings of matters, up to the point of clarity, is an obligatory and inescapable duty (wājib maḥtūm) from which no one has any evasion. For it is related in the report (khabar) that for every movement of the servant — however small — three registers (dawāwīn) are unfolded: the first register [asks] "Why?" (lim), the second "How?" (kayfa), and the third "For whom?" (liman). The meaning of "Why?" is: Why did you do this? Was it incumbent upon you to do it for your Master, or did you incline toward it out of your lust and caprice? If he is delivered from this — because it was incumbent upon him to do it for his Master — he is asked about the second register, and it is said to him: "How did you do this?" For God has in every deed a condition and a ruling whose measure, time, and description cannot be grasped except through knowledge. So it is said to him: "How did you act — with verified knowledge, or with ignorance and conjecture?" If he is delivered from this, the third register is unfolded, which is the summons to sincerity (ikhlāṣ). It is said to him: "For whom did you act? Was it for the Face of God, purely, in fulfillment of your utterance 'There is no god but God' — so that your reward is with God? Or was it for the show of creatures like yourself — then take your reward from them? Or did you do it to attain the immediate [goods] of your worldly life — then we have paid you in full your share of this world? Or did you do it in heedlessness and forgetfulness — then your reward has fallen away, your deed is void, and your striving has failed. And if you acted for other than Me, then you have incurred My wrath and My punishment — for you were a servant of Mine, eating My provision and enjoying My bounty, yet you act for other than Me! Have you not heard Me say: {Those whom you call upon besides God are servants like yourselves} and {Those you worship besides God possess no provision for you, so seek provision from God and worship Him}? Woe to you! Have you not heard Me say: {Surely, to God belongs the pure religion}?"
16:9.section_title_en: The Twofold Vigilance: Examining the Intention Before Action and Perfecting the Action Itself
16:9.anchors:
- Root: رقب (Raqaba)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To watch, observe, await, and guard; the watcher (raqīb) is one who is on the lookout, not heedless.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Moral vigilance (murāqabah) is the soul's persistent awareness that God is ever-watchful over its secret thoughts and open deeds, necessitating reverence (ḥayā') and self-accounting.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) sense is physical watching; here it is metaphorical (majāz) for the heart's state of reverent awe and continuous self-scrutiny before the Divine.
- Sibawayh Rule: Restriction & Focused Predication (al-ḥaṣr wa al-taqyīd bi-innamā) — Used to isolate the exclusive motive for action (for God alone vs. for caprice), as in the interrogation "for whom did you act?"
16:9.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Monitoring and Accounting'

17:36.arabic: يحاسبكم به الله فيغفر لمن يشاء ويعذب من يشاء وقوله تعالى {ولا تقف ما ليس لك به علم إن السمع والبصر والفؤاد كل أولئك كان عنه مسؤولا} فدل على أن عمل الفؤاد كعمل السمع والبصر فلا يعفى عنه وقوله تعالى {ولا تكتموا الشهادة ومن يكتمها فإنه آثم قلبه} وقوله تعالى {لا يؤاخذكم الله باللغو في أيمانكم ولكن يؤاخذكم بما كسبت قلوبكم} والحق عندنا في هذه المسألة لا يوقف عليه ما لم تقع الإحاطة بتفصيل أعمال القلوب من مبدأ ظهورها إلى أن يظهر العمل على الجوارح فنقول أول ما يرد على القلب الخاطر كما لو خطر له مثلا صورة امرأة وأنها وراء ظهره في الطريق
17:36.english: Know that this is a subtle matter, and there have come down concerning it verses and reports that are mutually conflicting, such that the way of reconciling between them becomes obscure — save for the master-brokers of the scholars of the Sacred Law. For it has been related from the Prophet — peace and blessings be upon him — that he said: "God has pardoned my community for what their souls whisper to them, so long as they do not speak of it or act upon it." (1) And Abū Hurayrah said: The Messenger of God — peace and blessings be upon him — said: "God — exalted is He — says to the guardian angels: When My servant intends a sin, do not write it against him; but if he commits it, then write it as one sin. And when he intends a good deed and does not perform it, write it for him as one good deed; but if he performs it, write it for him as ten." (2) This has been recorded by al-Bukhārī and Muslim in the two Ṣaḥīḥs, and it is evidence for the pardon of the heart's act and its intending of a sin. And in another wording: "Whoever intends a good deed and does not perform it, it is written for him as a good deed; and whoever intends a good deed and performs it, it is written for him as up to seven hundred multiples. And whoever intends a sin and does not perform it, it is not written against him; but if he performs it, it is written." And in yet another wording: "When My servant speaks within himself of committing a sin, I forgive him for it so long as he does not commit it." And all of this indicates the pardon.
17:36.section_title_en: The Heart's Whisperings and the Divine Pardon — On the Four Stages of Inner Acts
17:36.anchors:
- Root: نفس (n-f-s)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The self, soul, or inner being; that which breathes and harbors concealed thoughts.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-nafs denotes the soul or self (al-rūḥ), and in divine address, "what your souls whisper" (mā ḥaddathat bihi nufūsuhā) refers to the inner promptings that arise without deliberate volition.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) usage pertains to the soul's essence; metaphorical (majāz) usage extends to inner speech and inclination, as in "ḥadīth al-nafs" (self-talk), which is not yet resolved action.
- Root: حدث (ḥ-d-th)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To originate or bring forth something new; an event or occurrence that comes to be after non-existence.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-ḥudūth is the coming-to-be of a thing after it was not; "ḥadīth al-nafs" is the newly arising thought that occurs to the heart without prior acquisition.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: a recent matter or speech; metaphorical: the inner utterance of the soul, as in the prophetic report, "God has pardoned my community for what their souls whisper to them."
- Root: هم (h-m-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To intend, resolve, or purpose; the stirring of the will toward an act before its execution.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-hamm is the resolved intention (al-ʿazm) that precedes the deed; it is distinguished from mere inclination (mayl) and passing thought (khāṭir).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the soul's determination; metaphorical: the initial resolve that, when strengthened, becomes a firm will (irādah jazīmah).
- Root: قلب (q-l-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The heart; to turn or overturn, signifying its fluctuating nature between states.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The heart is the seat of cognition and volition; its "acts" (aʿmāl al-qulūb) include thought, belief, and resolve, which are subject to divine reckoning.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the physical organ; metaphorical: the spiritual faculty that perceives, believes, and intends, as in "the heart's sin" (ithm al-qalb).
- Sibawayh Rule: Restriction and Focused Predication (al-ḥaṣr wa al-taqyīd bi-innamā) — The prophetic and Quranic statements employ restriction to delineate the boundary between what is pardoned (the passing thought) and what is reckoned (the resolved intention), requiring precise parsing of the conditional clauses (law, idhā, man) to distinguish the stages of inner acts.
17:36.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Monitoring and Accounting'

17:36.arabic: والعجب والرياء والنفاق والحسد وجملة الخبائث من أعمال القلب بل السمع والبصر والفؤاد كل أولئك كان عنه مسئولا أي ما يدخل تحت الاختيار فلو وقع البصر بغير اختيار على غير ذي محرم لم يؤاخذ به فإن أتبعها نظرة ثانية كان مؤاخذا به لأنه مختار فكذا خواطر القلب تجري هذا المجرى بل القلب أولى بمؤاخذته لأنه الأصل قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم التقوى ههنا وأشار إلى القلب (2) وقال الله تعالى {لن ينال الله لحومها ولا دماؤها ولكن يناله التقوى منكم} وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم الإثم حواز القلوب (3) وقال البر ما اطمأن إليه القلب وإن أفتوك وأفتوك (4) حتى إنا نقول إذا حكم القلب
17:36.english: The proof that the mere thought and the initial inclination are not held against the servant is that which is firmly established from the Messenger of God — peace be upon him — that he said: "God has pardoned my community for what their souls whisper to them, so long as they do not speak of it or act upon it." And he said — peace be upon him: "When two Muslims meet with their swords, then the killer and the killed are both in the Fire." It was said: "O Messenger of God, this is the killer — but what of the killed?" He said: "Because he intended to kill his companion." {«التقى المسلمان بسيفيهما فالقاتل والمقتول في النار»} — and his being held accountable was solely for his intention (niyyah) and his resolution, not for the mere thought that crossed his heart, for the thought of killing is not within one's capacity to prevent, while the resolution to kill is.
17:36.section_title_en: Exposition of What the Servant is Held Accountable For from the Whispers of the Hearts, Their Anxieties, Their Thoughts, and Their Intentions — and What is Pardoned and Not Held Against Him
17:36.anchors:
- Root: وسوس (w-s-w-s)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The faint, concealed sound; the subtle, indistinct voice that inclines one toward something
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The insinuation that enters the heart covertly, whether from Satan or from the self's inclination
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — the faint jingling of an ornament; Metaphorical — the secret prompting that stirs within the breast
- Root: خطر (kh-t-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To come to mind; the passing of a thought across the heart without deliberate pursuit
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The sudden occurrence of a notion in the mind, whether invited or uninvited
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — something that presents itself; Metaphorical — the fleeting thought that crosses the heart like a passing traveler
- Root: هم (h-m-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The intention that inclines one toward an act before resolution is firmly settled
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The initial stirring of the will toward an action, preceding the firm resolve ('azm)
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — to intend; Metaphorical — the heart's leaning that, if unchecked, hardens into determination
- Root: قصد (q-s-d)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The deliberate aiming toward a goal; the firm resolution that governs the limbs
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The settled intention that directs action and for which one is justly held accountable
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — to walk a straight path to a destination; Metaphorical — the will's firm orientation that constitutes the essence of moral agency
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين المبتدأ والخبر (The Interposition Between Subject and Predicate) — governing the periodic structure of conditional accountability clauses where the protasis (condition) and apodosis (result) are separated by explanatory parentheticals, preserving the logical dependency of moral judgment upon the specification of the act's nature.
17:36.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Disciplining the Soul'

18:104.arabic: الذي ضل سعيهم في الحياة الدنيا وهم يحسبون أنهم يحسنون صنعا وبالجملة لا ينبغي للإنسان أن يشتغل بدقائق الورع إلا بحضرة عالم متقن فإنه إذا جاوز ما رسم وتصرف بذهنه من غير سماع كان ما يفسده أكثر مما يصلحه وقد روي عن سعد بن أبي وقاص رضي الله عنه أنه أحرق كرمه خوفا من أن يباع العنب ممن يتخذه خمرا وهذا لا أعرف له وجها إن لم يعرف هو سببا خاصا يوجب الإحراق إذا ما أحرق كرمه ونخله من كان أرفع قدرامنه من الصحابة ولو جاز هذا لجاز قطع الذكر خيفة من الزنا وقطع اللسان خيفة من الكذب إلى غير ذلك من الإتلافات وأما المقدمات: فلت
18:104.english: Next is that which is an exaggeration and nearly attaches to obsessive scrupulosity (al-waswās)—namely, the saying of a group that one may not transact with farmers over the tools of tillage, because they use them to aid in plowing and sell food to oppressors; nor may one buy from them cattle, land, and plowing implements. This is the abstinence of obsession, for it leads to not selling food to the farmer because he gains strength thereby for plowing, nor watering [his land] from the public water for that reason. This reaches the limit of excessive affectation (al-tanaṭṭuʿ) that is prohibited. For everyone who directs himself toward something with the intention of good cannot but exceed [proper bounds] unless verified knowledge (al-ʿilm al-muḥaqqiq) censures him. Perhaps he may embark upon something that becomes an innovation in religion (bidʿah), by which people are harmed afterward, while he supposes himself occupied with good. For this reason, he said—peace and blessings be upon him: "The superiority of the scholar over the worshiper is like my superiority over the lowest man among my companions." And the excessive affectationists (al-mutanaṭṭiʿūn) are those feared to be among those of whom it was said: {«الَّذِينَ ضَلَّ سَعْيُهُمْ فِي الْحَيَاةِ الدُّنْيَا وَهُمْ يَحْسَبُونَ أَنَّهُمْ يُحْسِنُونَ صُنْعًا»} (Q. 18:104) — "Those whose effort is lost in the life of this world while they suppose that they are doing well in work."
18:104.section_title_en: On the Degrees of Abstinence (Al-Waraʿ) Concerning Transactions That Facilitate Sin
18:104.anchors:
- Root: كرم (karuma)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of nobility, generosity, and honor; also used for the grapevine (karm) as a noble plant.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): When ascribed to God, denotes His manifest beneficence; when ascribed to man, denotes praiseworthy character and acts that appear from him. It is not said "he is noble" until that becomes manifest.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "He was generous to us" (karma ʿalaynā). Metaphorical: "This land is but a grapevine and a date-palm" (karmah wa-nakhlah) when these abound therein—likewise, the sale of grapes (karm) is the very subject of this discourse.
- Root: شطر (shaṭara)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To halve, to divide into two parts; a half or portion.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "The half and middle of a thing." Used in {«فَوَلِّ وَجْهَكَ شَطْرَ الْمَسْجِدِ الْحَرَامِ»} (Q. 2:144) meaning its direction.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "He took his half" (shaṭrahu). "I divided the thing into two halves." Also: "He shared with him his wealth" (shāṭarahu mālī). This anchors the account of ʿUmar dividing the camels with his sons by halves (shāṭarahumā).
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Interposition and Continuity in Conditional Sentences (al-sharṭ wa-l-jawāb)—governing the balanced periodic structure of "If it is said... we say..." (fa-in qīla... qulnā...) where the protasis and apodosis maintain syntactic parallelism without ellipsis of the governing particle.
18:104.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Monitoring and Accounting'

18:104.arabic: بأنفسهم خيرا ويحسبون أنهم يحسنون صنعا ويعتقدون أن كل سوداء تمرة ويتوهمون أن المشاركة في الظاهر توجب المساهمة في الحقائق وهيهات فما أغزر حماقة من لا يميز بين الشحم والورم فهؤلاء بغضاء الله فإن الله تعالى يبغض الشاب الفارغ ولم يحملهم على السياحة إلا الشباب والفراغ إلا من سافر لحج أو عمرة في غير رياء ولا سمعة أو سافر لمشاهدة شيخ يقتدي به في علمه وسيرته وقد خلت البلاد عنه الآن والأمور الدينية كلها قد فسدت وضعفت إلا التصوف فإنه قد انمحق بالكلية وبطل لأن العلوم لم تندرس بعد والعالم وإن كان
18:104.english: And the most excellent in this matter is whatever is most helpful to one's religion. The ultimate fruit of religion in this world is the attainment of knowledge of God — may He be exalted — and the attainment of intimacy (uns) with the remembrance of God — may He be exalted. Intimacy is attained through the constancy of remembrance (dhikr), and knowledge is attained through the constancy of reflection (fikr).
18:104.section_title_en: The Book of Seclusion (Kitāb al-ʿUzlah) — Section 470: On Travel and Its Relation to the Seeker's Path
18:104.anchors:
- Root: سفر (s-f-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: "to uncover, to remove a covering"; al-Ayn: "al-safar: a people journeying"; the journey as that which unveils states and conditions.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "al-safar: the uncovering of a veil... al-isfār is specific to color/brightness" — travel as that which exposes the heart's true constitution.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Haqiqah: physical journeying; Majaz: "a face bright with joy" — here, the literal journey as a means that may either illuminate or agitate the heart.
- Root: قلب (q-l-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "to turn over, to transform, to flip from one state to another."
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "taṣrīf al-shayʾ wa ṣarfuhu ʿan wajh ilā wajh" — the heart's constant overturning between states.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Majaz: "a man who turns matters over [in his mind]" — the heart's agitation through travel's distractions.
- Root: صوف (ṣ-w-f)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "wool"; al-Raghib: "al-Ṣūfī: one who wears wool, or one attributed to the Ṣūfah who served the Kaʿbah."
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Majaz: "a clumsy woman who found wool [and wasted it]" — one who finds a treasure but lacks the knowledge to use it; the false Sufi who dons the garb without the reality.
- Sibawayh Rule: Restriction and Specification (al-ḥaṣr wa al-taqyīd bi-innamā) — the text's repeated use of "إنما" to delimit the true nature of Sufism (heart's purification) against its counterfeit forms.
18:104.topic: Al-Ghazali on purifying the character, moral diseases, and spiritual remedies, from 'Etiquette of Travel'

20:94.arabic: إنه قال يا ابن آدم اذكرني بعد صلاة الفجر ساعة وبعد صلاة العصر ساعة أكفك ما بينهما (3) وإذا ظهر فضل ذلك فليقعد ولا يتكلم إلى طلوع الشمس بل ينبغي أن تكون وظيفته إلى الطلوع أربعة أنواع أدعية وأذكار ويكررها في سبحة وقراءة قرآن وتفكر أما الأدعية فكلما يفرغ من صلاته فليبدأ وليقل اللهم صلي على محمد وعلى آل محمد وسلم اللهم أنت السلام ومنك السلام وإليك يعود السلام حينا ربنا بالسلام وأدخلنا دار السلام تباركت يا ذا الجلال والإكرام ثم يفتتح الدعاء بما كان يفتتح به رسول الله صل
20:94.english: Now, the first watch (al-wird al-awwal) is that which extends from the dawn prayer (ṣalāt al-ṣubḥ) until sunrise (ṭulūʿ al-shams). When the servant has completed his obligatory prayer, he should remain seated in his place of prayer, occupying himself with the remembrance of God most High, until the sun has risen. For it has been reported that the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "That I should sit in my assembly, remembering God most High therein, from the morning prayer until sunrise, is more beloved to me than freeing four slaves." {«لأن أقعد في مجلسي أذكر الله تعالى فيه من صلاة الغداة إلى طلوع الشمس أحب إلي من أن أعتق أربع رقاب»} And it is related that he, peace and blessings be upon him, when he had prayed the morning prayer, would sit in his place of prayer until the sun rose; and in some versions [it is added] that he would pray two rakʿahs—that is, after sunrise. Concerning the virtue of this [practice], an incalculable number of reports have come down. Al-Ḥasan related that the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, used to mention, among what he recounted of his Lord's mercy, that He said: "O son of Adam, remember Me for an hour after the dawn prayer and for an hour after the afternoon prayer, and I shall suffice you for what lies between them." {«يا ابن آدم اذكرني بعد صلاة الفجر ساعة وبعد صلاة العصر ساعة أكفك ما بينهما»}
20:94.section_title_en: The Daily Liturgy of the Devout Servant: The First Watch (After Dawn Prayer until Sunrise)
20:94.anchors:
- Root: ذكر (dhakara)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Remembrance, invocation, mention; the opposite of forgetfulness (nisyān).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Remembrance of God (dhikr) is the heart's presence with the Divine, ranging from the tongue's utterance to the heart's contemplation; it is the noblest act when accompanied by presence of heart.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): verbal mention. Metaphorical (majāz): the heart's steadfastness in knowledge of God, which is the reality of dhikr.
- Root: صلا (ṣallā)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Prayer (ṣalāh); root meaning of supplication and blessing; also "to kindle a fire" (as in ṣalā al-nār).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Ṣalāh is the servant's standing before God in humility and devotion, comprising praise, recitation, bowing, and prostration; its perfection lies in the heart's presence.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the ritual prayer with its pillars. Metaphorical: supplication (duʿā') and blessing (taṣliyah) upon the Prophet.
- Root: ورد (warada)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To arrive at water; a portion or share of something that comes regularly.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The daily portion (wird) of devotion—a set liturgy of prayers, recitations, and remembrances that the servant regularly performs at appointed times.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: arriving at a watering place. Metaphorical: the soul's regular approach to the fountain of divine grace through prescribed acts of worship.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Restriction and Specification (al-ḥaṣr wa al-taqyīd) — governing the precise enumeration of the four functions (adʿiyah, adhkār, qirā'ah, fikr) after the dawn prayer, each specified by its own governing verb and object.
20:94.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications, prayers, and their spiritual power, from 'Arrangement of Litanies'

20:94.arabic: نفسه وقال منك أتيت لو كان فيك خير لأعطيت حاجتك فنزل إليه ملك وقال يا ابن آدم ساعتك هذه خير من عبادتك التي مضت وقد قضى الله حاجتك وقال عبد الله بن قيس كنا في غزاة لنا فحضر العدو فصيح في الناس فقاموا إلى المصاف في يوم شديد الريح وإذا رجل أمامي وهو يخاطب نفسه ويقول أي نفسي ألم أشهد مشهد كذا فقلت لي أهلك وعيالك فأطعتك ورجعت ألم أشهد مشهد كذا وكذا فقلت لي أهلك وعيالك فأطعتك ورجعت والله لأعرضنك اليوم على الله أخذك أو تركك فقلت لأرمقنه اليوم فرمقته فحمل الناس على عدوهم فكان في أوائلهم ثم أن العدو حمل على الناس فانكشفوا فكان
20:94.english: A woman said: "You speak of what you do not know. Indeed, God has a covenant upon me which I shall never break: I shall not lay you upon the earth in sleep for a full year, except due to an obstructing illness or a departing intellect. Shame upon you! Do you not feel ashamed? How often you rebuke, yet from your error you do not desist." He said: And he began to weep, unaware of my presence. When I saw that, I departed and left him.
20:94.section_title_en: The Discipline of the Self: Accounts of the Pious in Reckoning and Punishing Their Souls
20:94.anchors:
- Root: نفس (n-f-s)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The self, soul, spirit; that which breathes and desires; the locus of blameworthy and praiseworthy traits.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-nafs denotes the soul as the principle of life and moral responsibility; its reckoning (muḥāsabah) is the essence of religious discipline.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the self as animate entity. Metaphorical: "دفق نفسه" (he poured out his self, i.e., his blood) — here, the self is addressed as a distinct interlocutor, a rhetorical personification of the lower impulses.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب النداء والتوبيخ (The Chapter of Direct Address and Rebuke) — The self is vocatively addressed (يا نفسي) as a second party, establishing the grammatical frame of moral confrontation.
20:94.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Monitoring and Accounting'

21:104.arabic: الآخرة ما خلقكم ولا بعثكم إلا كنفس واحدة كما بدأنا أول خلق نعيده وكما قال تعالى جزاء وفاقا أي وافق الجزاء أعمالهم فقوبل الخالص بالصرف من الشراب وقوبل المشوب بالمشوب وشوب كل شراب على قدر ما سبق من الشوب في حبه وأعماله فمن يعمل مثقال ذرة خيرا يره ومن يعمل مثقال ذرة شرا يره وإن الله لا يغير ما بقوم حتى يغيروا ما بأنفسهم إن الله لا يظلم مثقال ذرة وإن تك حسنة يضاعفها وإن كان مثقال حبة من خردل أتينا بها وكفى بنا حاسبين فمن كان حبه في الدنيا رجاءه لنعيم الجنة والحور العين والقصور مكن من الجنة ليتبوأ منها حيث يشاء
21:104.english:
...twenty years.
And al-Junayd said: "The mark of the lover is the constancy of vigor and cheerfulness with a passion that wearies his body but does not weary his heart."
And some of them said: "Labor borne out of love — languor does not enter into it."
And one of the scholars said: "By God, no lover of God is ever fully quenched by His obedience, even if he were to attain to the most immense of means."
All of this and its like is found in observable experience, for the passionate lover does not find burdensome the pursuit of his beloved's desire, and he savors with his heart the service of the beloved even if it is arduous upon his body. And whenever his body falls short, the dearest of things to him is that his capacity should return to him and that incapacity should depart from him, so that he may occupy himself with it. Such, likewise, is the love of God the Exalted — for every love that becomes dominant inevitably subdues whatever is beneath it. So whoever's beloved is dearer to him than his sloth abandons sloth in serving him; and if the beloved is dearer to him than his wealth, he spends his wealth in his love.
And it was said to one of the lovers — who had expended his very self and his wealth until nothing remained to him — "What was the cause of your state in love?" He said: "One day I heard a lover who had secluded himself with his beloved, saying: 'By God, I love you with my whole heart, while you turn away from me with your whole face.' The beloved said to him: 'If you truly love me, what will you spend upon me?' He said: 'O my master, I put you in possession of all that I own, and then I spend upon you my very spirit until it is destroyed.'" So I said: "This is a creature loving a creature, and a slave loving a slave — how then with slaves loving the Worshipped One?" All of this is by His cause.
And among them is that he be compassionate toward all of God's servants, merciful to them, and severe against all of God's enemies — and against everyone who commits something of what God dislikes — as God the Exalted said: {«أشداء على الكفار رحماء بينهم»} "Harsh against the disbelievers, merciful among themselves." No reproach of any reproacher seizes him, and no diverting force turns him from wrath for God's sake. With this God described His friends, saying: "Those who are enamored with My love as a child is enamored with a thing, and who take refuge in My remembrance as the eagle takes refuge in its nest, and who rage for the sake of My sanctities as the leopard rages when provoked — for then he cares not whether the people are few or many."
So consider this example: the child, when enamored with a thing, does not part from it at all; if it is taken from him, he has no occupation but weeping and crying out until it is returned to him. If he sleeps, he takes it with him into his clothes; when he awakens, he returns and clings to it. Whenever he is parted from it, he weeps; whenever he finds it, he laughs. Whoever contends with him over it, he hates; whoever gives it to him, he loves. As for the leopard, he does not master himself at the moment of rage, until he reaches such a pitch of fury that he destroys himself. These, then, are the marks of love. Whoever's marks are perfected in him, his love is perfected and his affection is purified — so in the Hereafter his drink is clear and his draught is sweet.
But whoever's love is mingled with the love of other than God, he delights in the Hereafter in proportion to his love, for his drink is mingled with a measure of the drink of the Near Ones (al-muqarrabūn), as God the Exalted said concerning the righteous (al-abrār): {«إن الأبرار لفي نعيم»} "Verily the righteous are in bliss," {ثم قال} then He said: {«يسقون من رحيق مختوم * ختامه مسك وفي ذلك فليتنافس المتنافسون * ومزاجه من تسنيم * عينا يشرب بها المقربون»} "They are given to drink of sealed nectar, whose seal is musk — and in that let the competitors compete — and its mixture is of tasnīm, a spring from which the Near Ones drink." So when the drink of the righteous is sweetened by the admixture of the pure drink which belongs to the Near Ones...
And "drink" is an expression for the totality of the bliss of the Gardens, just as the Book expressed by it all deeds, for He said: {«إن كتاب الأبرار لفي عليين»} "Verily the book of the righteous is in 'Illiyyūn," {ثم قال} then He said: {«يشهده المقربون»} "The Near Ones bear witness to it." So it was a sign of the loftiness of their book that it ascended to where the Near Ones bear witness to it. And just as the righteous find increase in their state and their knowledge by their proximity to the Near Ones and their beholding of them, so likewise is their state in the Hereafter — {«ما خلقكم ولا بعثكم إلا كنفس واحدة»} "Your creation and your resurrection are but as a single soul," just as He said — as we began the first creation, We shall repeat it — and as the Exalted said: {«جزاء وفاقا»} "A recompense fully matching" — that is, the recompense matched their deeds. So the pure was met with the unmixed of the drink, and the mingled was met with the mingled.
And the admixture of every drink is in proportion to what preceded of admixture in his love and his deeds. For {«من يعمل مثقال ذرة خيرا يره * ومن يعمل مثقال ذرة شرا يره»} "Whoever does an atom's weight of good shall see it, and whoever does an atom's weight of evil shall see it." And {«إن الله لا يغير ما بقوم حتى يغيروا ما بأنفسهم * إن الله لا يظلم مثقال ذرة وإن تك حسنة يضاعفها وإن كان مثقال حبة من خردل أتينا بها وكفى بنا حاسبين»} "Verily God does not change what is in a people until they change what is in themselves. Verily God does not wrong an atom's weight; and if it be a good deed, He multiplies it, and if it be a grain of mustard-seed, We bring it — and sufficient are We as reckoners."
So whoever's love in this world was his hope for the bliss of the Garden, the wide-eyed houris, and the palaces — he is granted the Garden to settle therein wherever he wishes, to sport with the immortal youths and take pleasure with the women. There his delight in the Hereafter reaches its end, because every man is given in love only what his soul desires and his eye delights in.
But whoever's aim was the Lord of the Abode and the Owner of the Kingdom, and nothing overcame him save His love with sincerity and truthfulness — he is lodged in the seat...
21:104.section_title_en: The Marks of True Love and the Degrees of the Hereafter
21:104.anchors:
- Root: نشط (n-sh-ṭ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of vitality, energy, and alacrity in action.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Activity of the soul (nafs) in pursuing what it loves, unflagging in its ardor.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: bodily vigor; Metaphorical: the heart's persistent zeal that overrides physical exhaustion.
- Root: شرب (sh-r-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Drinking; the act of imbibing liquids.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In Quranic usage, a metaphor (majaz) for the soul's reception of spiritual bliss and states.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical quenching; Metaphorical: the tasting of paradisiacal delight, graded by purity (safā') versus admixture (shawb).
- Root: صفو (ṣ-f-w)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Purity, clarity, and freedom from turbidity or mixture.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The unalloyed state of sincere love (mahabbah) and its corresponding reward.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: clear liquid; Metaphorical: the soul's exclusive devotion to God, yielding unmixed bliss.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — Used to delimit the final reward strictly by the object and purity of one's love, as in "إنما يعطى كل إنسان في المحبة ما تشتهيه نفسه."
21:104.topic: Al-Ghazali on the journey of the soul, death, and the Hereafter, from 'Monitoring and Accounting'

23:8.arabic: وبقوله تعالى {والذين هم لأماناتهم وعهدهم راعون}
23:8.english: I say: Every human being is never free from disobedience of the bodily members (jawāriḥ), for even the prophets were not free from it — as has come down in the Qurʾān and the reports concerning the sins of the prophets, their repentance, and their weeping over their misdeeds. And if one is free, in some states, from disobedience of the members, he is not free from the heart's inclination (hamm) toward sins. And if he is free, in some states, from the inclination, he is not free from the whispering of Satan (waswās al-shayṭān) by way of importing scattered thoughts that divert from the remembrance of God. And if he is free from that, he is not free from heedlessness (ghaflah) and deficiency in knowledge of God, His attributes, and His acts. All of that is deficiency (nuqṣān), and it has causes; and abandoning its causes by occupying oneself with their opposites is a reversion from one path to its contrary. The meaning of "repentance" (tawbah) is "returning" (rujūʿ), and it is inconceivable that a human being should be entirely free of this deficiency — rather, people differ only in degrees. As for the principle itself, it is unavoidable. For this reason, he (peace be upon him) said: "Truly, a veil is cast over my heart, so that I seek forgiveness from God seventy times a day and night" (1) — the hadith. And for this reason, God (exalted be He) honored him by saying: {«لِيَغْفِرَ لَكَ اللَّهُ مَا تَقَدَّمَ مِنْ ذَنْبِكَ وَمَا تَأَخَّرَ»} [That God may forgive you what has passed of your sin and what remains]. And if this was his state, how then is the state of anyone else?
23:8.section_title_en: On the Universality of Repentance (Tawbah) and Its Obligation in Every Breath
23:8.anchors:
- Root: توب (T-W-B)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of "returning" (rujūʿ) — turning back from a path to its opposite; the root denotes the act of revisiting and reversing a prior state.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Tawbah is "abandoning the sin in the most excellent manner" — the most complete form of excuse; in sacred law (sharʿ), it is abandoning the sin due to its ugliness, regretting what has passed, resolving not to return, and rectifying what can be rectified of past deeds through renewed acts.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): "He repented to God from his sin" (tāba al-ʿabdu ilā Allāhi min dhanbihi). Metaphorical (majāz): The extension of "repentance" to inner purification of the heart from accumulated rust (rayn), as the root's sense of "returning" is applied to the soul's reversion from negligence to vigilance.
- Root: قلب (Q-L-B)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The heart as the organ of turning and overturning (taqlīb) — its state fluctuates between illumination and darkness, purity and rust.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Turning a thing" is directing it from one face to another; the heart (qalb) is so named for its constant overturning between states — a key metaphysical anchor for Ghazali's doctrine of the heart's susceptibility to stains (akdār) and polish (ṣaqal).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "He turned the thing over" (qalaba al-shayʾ). Metaphorical: "The heart is rusted" (qalb wajīb) — the inner organ's receptivity to impressions, whether dark (from sins) or luminous (from obedience).
- Root: وجب (W-J-B)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Obligation as fixed establishment (thubūt); what is due and settled upon a person.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Wājib has two senses: (1) that whose non-existence entails a contradiction (metaphysical necessity), and (2) that whose neglect merits blame — subdivided into what reason deems obligatory (e.g., knowing divine unity) and what the Law deems obligatory (e.g., acts of worship). Ghazali here exploits this dual sense to distinguish legal obligation (fatwā) from the higher obligation of the path (ṭarīq).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "It became incumbent upon him" (wajaba ʿalayhi). Metaphorical: The extension to "the heart's palpitation" (wajīb) — the inner agitation of one who realizes the urgency of repentance before death.
- Sibawayh Rule: Restriction and Focused Predication (al-ḥaṣr wa al-taqyīd bi-innamā) — governing the Quranic citations {«إِنَّمَا التَّوْبَةُ عَلَى اللَّهِ»} and {«وَلَيْسَتِ التَّوْبَةُ لِلَّذِينَ»}, where innamā restricts the predicate to a specific subject, delimiting the scope of accepted repentance to those who turn before death's arrival and before the rust hardens into a seal.
23:8.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'Monitoring and Accounting'

24:31.arabic: فيها نفسه وقال تعالى {وتوبوا إلى الله جميعا أيها المؤمنون لعلكم تفلحون} والتوبة نظر في الفعل بعد الفراغ منه بالندم عليه وقد قال صلى الله عليه وسلم إني لأستغفر الله تعالى وأتوب إليه في اليوم مائة مرة (2) وقال تعالى {إن الذين اتقوا إذا مسهم طائف من الشيطان تذكروا فإذا هم مبصرون} وعن عمر رضي الله عنه انه كان يضرب قدميه بالدره إذا جنه الليل ويقول لنفسه ماذا عملت اليوم وعن ميمون ابن مهران أنه قال لا يكون العبد من المتقين حتى يحاسب نفسه أشد من محاسبة شريكه والشريكان يتحاسبان بعد العمل وروى عن عائشة رضي الله تعالى
24:31.english: As for its virtue, God most high has said: {«يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا اتَّقُوا اللَّهَ وَلْتَنْظُرْ نَفْسٌ مَا قَدَّمَتْ لِغَدٍ»} (O you who believe, fear God, and let every soul look to what it has sent forward for the morrow) — and this is an allusion to reckoning over past deeds. For this reason, ʿUmar — may God most high be pleased with him — said: "Call yourselves to account before you are called to account, and weigh yourselves before you are weighed." And in the report, a man came to him — peace be upon him — and said: "O Messenger of God, counsel me." He said: "Are you asking for counsel?" He replied: "Yes." He said: "When you resolve upon a matter, then ponder its consequence: if it be right guidance, proceed with it; and if it be error, desist from it." And in the report: "It behooves the intelligent man to have four hours: an hour in which he calls himself to account." And God most high said: {«وَتُوبُوا إِلَى اللَّهِ جَمِيعًا أَيُّهَا الْمُؤْمِنُونَ لَعَلَّكُمْ تُفْلِحُونَ»} (And turn in repentance to God all together, O believers, that you might succeed) — and repentance is a scrutiny of the deed after its completion, through regret over it. And he — peace be upon him — said: "Verily I seek forgiveness from God most high and turn to Him in repentance a hundred times a day." And God most high said: {«إِنَّ الَّذِينَ اتَّقَوْا إِذَا مَسَّهُمْ طَائِفٌ مِنَ الشَّيْطَانِ تَذَكَّرُوا فَإِذَا هُمْ مُبْصِرُونَ»} (Verily those who fear God, when a whisper from Satan touches them, they remember — and behold, they are seeing clearly). And it is related of ʿUmar — may God be pleased with him — that he would strike his own feet with a whip when night fell upon him, saying to himself: "What have you done today?" And it is related of Maymūn ibn Mihrān that he said: "A servant does not become one of the God-fearing until he calls himself to account more severely than he would his partner — and two partners reckon with each other after the work." And it is narrated from ʿĀʾishah — may God most high be pleased with her — that Abū Bakr — God's good pleasure be upon him — said to her at death: "There is no one among mankind more beloved to me than ʿUmar." Then he said to her: "How did I put it?" So she repeated to him what he had said, whereupon he said: "There is no one more honored by me than ʿUmar."
24:31.section_title_en: The Third Watch: Self-Reckoning After Deeds — Its Virtue and Its Reality
24:31.anchors:
- Root: ح س ب (ḥ-s-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of counting, reckoning, and sufficient estimation; al-ḥisāb is the act of numbering and settling accounts.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: muḥāsabah is the soul's voluntary audit of its deeds against divine command, prefiguring the eschatological reckoning (ḥisāb) by God.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): arithmetic counting; Metaphorical (majāz): self-interrogation and weighing of one's actions, as in "ḥāsaba nafsahu" (he called his soul to account).
- Root: ن ظ ر (n-ẓ-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To look, consider, reflect; naẓar implies deliberate examination with the eye or intellect.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: taḍabbur (deep reflection) on consequences of actions, aligning sight with insight (baṣīrah).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical gazing; Metaphorical: intellectual deliberation and foresight, as in "tadabbar al-amr" (he pondered the matter).
- Root: ن ف س (n-f-s)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The self, soul, or spirit; that which breathes and possesses volition.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: al-nafs al-lawwāmah (the blaming soul) is the conscience that reproaches its owner for misdeeds, distinct from the corporeal body.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the animate self; Metaphorical: the inner tribunal where the soul is both accused and judge.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Restriction and Focused Predication (باب الحصر والتقييد) — Constructions like "إنما" and conditional clauses (idhā... fa-) establish causal sequencing, as in "if a whim touches them, they remember" — the protasis governs the apodosis, binding reflection to action.
24:31.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Monitoring and Accounting'

34:3.arabic: إحاطة خارجة عن النهاية حتى لا يعزب عنه مثقال ذرة في السموات ولا في الأرض وقد خاطب الخلق كلهم فقال عز وجل وما أوتيتم من العلم إلا قليلا بل لو اجتمع أهل الأرض والسماء على أن يحيطوا بعلمه وحكمته في تفصيل خلق نملة أو بعوضة لم يطلعوا على عشر عشير ذلك ولا يحيطون بشيء من علمه إلا بما شاء والقدر اليسير الذي علمه الخلائق كلهم فبتعليمه علموه كما قال تعالى خلق الإنسان علمه البيان فإن كان جمال العلم وشرفه أمرا محبوبا وكان هو في نفسه زينة وكمالا للموصوف به فلا ينبغي أن يحب بهذا السبب إلا الله تعالى فعلوم العلماء جهل
34:3.english: As for knowledge — where is the knowledge of the first and the last among all creation compared to the knowledge of Allah, the Exalted, which encompasses all things with an encompassing that transcends all limit, so that not even the weight of an atom escapes Him in the heavens or on the earth? He has addressed all of creation, saying, the Mighty and Majestic: {«وَمَا أُوتِيتُم مِّنَ الْعِلْمِ إِلَّا قَلِيلًا»} (And you have not been given of knowledge except a little) (Q 17:85). Nay, even if all the inhabitants of the earth and the heavens were to gather together to encompass His knowledge and His wisdom in the detailed formation of a single ant or gnat, they would not attain to one-tenth of a tenth of that — {«وَلَا يُحِيطُونَ بِشَيْءٍ مِّنْ عِلْمِهِ إِلَّا بِمَا شَاءَ»} (And they do not encompass anything of His knowledge except what He wills) (Q 2:255). And the paltry measure that all creatures have learned, they have learned only through His teaching, as He, the Exalted, said: {«خَلَقَ الْإِنسَانَ عَلَّمَهُ الْبَيَانَ»} (He created man; He taught him eloquence) (Q 55:3-4). If, therefore, the beauty and nobility of knowledge is something beloved, and it is in itself an adornment and perfection for the one described by it, then it is not fitting that anyone be loved for this reason except Allah, the Exalted alone.
34:3.section_title_en: The Beauty of Divine Attributes and the Relative Nature of Human Perfection
34:3.anchors:
- Root: علم (ʿalima)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of perception, cognition, and certain apprehension of a thing's reality.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "العلم: إدراك الشيء بحقيقته" — knowledge is the apprehension of a thing in its true reality; it is twofold: apprehension of the essence, and judgment affirming or negating a predicate.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) usage denotes genuine cognition; metaphorical (majāz) usage extends to perception and awareness. Here, the comparative "أعلم/أجهل" (more knowing/ more ignorant) operates on a scale of relative apprehension.
- Root: قدر (qadara)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Root denotes measuring, determining, and the capacity to bring about an effect.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "القدرة إذا وصف بها الإنسان فاسم لهيئة له بها يتمكن من فعل شيء ما، وإذا وصف الله تعالى بها فهي نفي العجز عنه" — power in man is a disposition enabling specific acts; power in God is absolute negation of incapacity, unrestricted and infinite.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "هو قادر مقتدر ذو قدرة ومقدرة" — the possessor of power. Metaphorical: extended to strength and dominion. The text contrasts finite human power (maqdūr) with divine power that encompasses all things without limit.
- Root: نفس (nafs)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Self, soul, essence; the innermost reality of a thing.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "نفسه: ذاته" — God's "self" is His very essence. For man, nafs denotes the composite self that requires discipline and reform (iṣlāḥ).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the self as the seat of attributes; metaphorical: "دفق نفسه" — blood/life. Here, "سياسة نفسه" (governance of one's self) is the literal, ethical sense.
- Root: خلق (khalaqa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Root denotes measuring, smoothing, and fashioning; also moral character (khuluq).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الخلق أصله: التقدير المستقيم" — origination by precise measure; used for creation ex nihilo and for formation from existing matter.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "خلق الله الخلق: أوجده على تقدير أوجبته الحكمة" — God's creation is bringing into existence upon a measure required by wisdom. The text uses "الخبائث" (vices) as the corruption of this created nature.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — The phrase "فإنما غايته أن يقدر" restricts human power to a finite limit, emphasizing that the utmost reach of creaturely capacity is merely partial and derivative, never absolute.

34:22.arabic: إحاطة خارجة عن النهاية حتى لا يعزب عنه مثقال ذرة في السموات ولا في الأرض وقد خاطب الخلق كلهم فقال عز وجل وما أوتيتم من العلم إلا قليلا بل لو اجتمع أهل الأرض والسماء على أن يحيطوا بعلمه وحكمته في تفصيل خلق نملة أو بعوضة لم يطلعوا على عشر عشير ذلك ولا يحيطون بشيء من علمه إلا بما شاء والقدر اليسير الذي علمه الخلائق كلهم فبتعليمه علموه كما قال تعالى خلق الإنسان علمه البيان فإن كان جمال العلم وشرفه أمرا محبوبا وكان هو في نفسه زينة وكمالا للموصوف به فلا ينبغي أن يحب بهذا السبب إلا الله تعالى فعلوم العلماء جهل
34:22.english: As for knowledge — where is the knowledge of the first and the last among all creation compared to the knowledge of Allah, the Exalted, which encompasses all things with an encompassing that transcends all limit, so that not even the weight of an atom escapes Him in the heavens or on the earth? He has addressed all of creation, saying, the Mighty and Majestic: {«وَمَا أُوتِيتُم مِّنَ الْعِلْمِ إِلَّا قَلِيلًا»} (And you have not been given of knowledge except a little) (Q 17:85). Nay, even if all the inhabitants of the earth and the heavens were to gather together to encompass His knowledge and His wisdom in the detailed formation of a single ant or gnat, they would not attain to one-tenth of a tenth of that — {«وَلَا يُحِيطُونَ بِشَيْءٍ مِّنْ عِلْمِهِ إِلَّا بِمَا شَاءَ»} (And they do not encompass anything of His knowledge except what He wills) (Q 2:255). And the paltry measure that all creatures have learned, they have learned only through His teaching, as He, the Exalted, said: {«خَلَقَ الْإِنسَانَ عَلَّمَهُ الْبَيَانَ»} (He created man; He taught him eloquence) (Q 55:3-4). If, therefore, the beauty and nobility of knowledge is something beloved, and it is in itself an adornment and perfection for the one described by it, then it is not fitting that anyone be loved for this reason except Allah, the Exalted alone.

38:72.arabic: أمره بإضافته إليه إذ قال تعالى إني خالق بشرا من طين فإذا سويته ونفخت فيه من روحي فقعوا له ساجدين فنبه على أن الجسد منسوب إلى الطين والروح إلى رب العالمين والمراد بالروح والنفس في هذا المقام واحد فالخلق عبارة عن هيئة في النفس راسخة عنها تصدر الأفعال بسهولة ويسر من غير حاجة إلى فكر وروية فإن كانت الهيئة بحيث تصدر عنها الأفعال الجميلة المحمودة عقلا وشرعا سميت تلك الهيئة خلقا حسنا وإن كان الصادر عنها الأفعال القبيحة سميت الهيئة التي هي المصدر خلقا سيئا وإنما قلنا إنها هيئة راسخة لأن من يصدر منه بذل المال على الندور لحاجة عارضة
38:72.english: I say: Know that people have spoken concerning the reality of good character (ḥusn al-khulq) — what it is — yet they have not addressed its true nature; rather, they have addressed its fruits. Then they did not even exhaust all of its fruits, but each one mentioned only those fruits that occurred to him and were present in his mind. They did not direct their attention to mentioning its definition (ḥadd) and its reality (ḥaqīqah) that encompasses all its fruits in detail and with completeness. This is like the saying of al-Ḥasan: "Good character is a cheerful face, the giving of bounty, and the withholding of harm." Al-Wāsiṭī said: "It is that one neither disputes nor is disputed with, by virtue of his intense knowledge of God most high." Shāh al-Kirmānī said: "It is the withholding of harm and the bearing of burdens." Some said: "It is that one be near to people, yet a stranger among them." Al-Wāsiṭī said on another occasion: "It is the pleasing of creation in prosperity and adversity." Abū ʿUthmān said: "It is satisfaction with God most high." Sahl al-Tustarī was asked about good character, and he said: "Its lowest degree is forbearance, the abandonment of retaliation, mercy toward the oppressor, seeking forgiveness for him, and compassion toward him." He said on another occasion: "It is that one does not accuse the Truth concerning provision, but trusts in Him, and reposes in His faithfulness to what He has guaranteed, so that he obeys Him and does not disobey Him in all matters — both in what is between him and his Lord, and in what is between him and people." ʿAlī, may God be pleased with him, said: "Good character consists in three qualities: avoiding forbidden things, seeking what is lawful, and enlarging one's provision upon one's dependents." Al-Ḥusayn ibn Manṣūr said: "It is that the harshness of creation does not affect you after your contemplation of the Truth." Abū Saʿīd al-Kharrāz said: "It is that you have no concern other than God most high." This and the like of it is abundant — and it is an addressing of the fruits of good character, not of its very self. Nor is it even encompassing of all the fruits.
38:72.section_title_en: The Reality of Good Character (Ḥusn al-Khulq) — Its True Nature and the Four Pillars of the Soul
38:72.anchors:
- Root: خلق (Kh-L-Q)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "التقدير المستقيم" — precise measurement and fashioning; the outward form (khalq) and inward disposition (khuluq) as twin designations of the same root.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "إبداع الشيء من غير أصل ولا احتذاء" — origination without precedent; here extended to the soul's innate constitution, which God alone originates and proportions.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Haqiqah: "خلق الخراز الأديم" — the tanner measures the hide before cutting. Majaz: "خلق الله الخلق: أوجده على تقدير أوجبته الحكمة" — God's creation as measured origination. Thus khuluq is the soul's measured inward form, as khalq is the body's measured outward form.
- Root: حسن (Ḥ-S-N)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Beauty and comeliness in both visible and invisible orders.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الحسن: عبارة عن كل مبهج مرغوب فيه" — that which delights and is desired; three kinds: rational, appetitive, sensory. The good character is that which reason and revelation (ʿaqlan wa sharʿan) deem beautiful.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Haqiqah: "أنظر إلى محاسن وجهه" — visible beauties. Majaz: "فلان لا يحسن شيئا" — competence and virtue as moral beauty. The "beautiful" act is the metaphorical extension of visible comeliness to inward excellence.
- Root: نفس (N-F-S)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The self, soul, spirit; that which is valued and precious.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "النفس: الروح" — the soul as spirit; in the verse {«ونفخت فيه من روحي»} the soul is that which is divinely breathed, distinguished from the clay body.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Haqiqah: "شيء نفيس" — precious thing. Majaz: "دفق نفسه أي دمه" — the self as the whole living person. Here, the soul (nafs) perceived by inner vision (baṣīrah) is of greater rank than the body perceived by sight (baṣar).
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — The author's repeated "إنما قلنا" and "ليس الخلق عبارة عن..." employ restrictive predication to delimit the definition of khuluq against rival candidates (act, power, knowledge), each negated in turn before the fourth meaning is affirmed.
38:72.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Fear and Hope'

38:72.arabic: وحذرتك سخطى ألم أخلقك بيدى ونفخت فيك من روحى وأسجدت لك ملائكتى فعصيت أمرى ونسيت عهدى وتعرضت لسخطى فو عزتى وجلالى لو ملأت الأرض رجالا كلهم مثلك يعبدونني ويسبحونني ثم عصونى لأنزلتهم منازل العاصين فبكى آدم عليه السلام عند ذلك ثلثمائة عام وكان عبيد الله البجلى كثير البكاء يقول في بكائه طول ليله إلهى أنا الذى كلما طال عمرى زادت ذنوبى أنا الذى كلما هممت بترك خطيئة عرضت لى شهوة أخرى واعبيداه خطيئة لم تبل وصاحبها في طلب أخرى واعبيداه إن كانت النار لك مقيلا ومأوى واعبيداه إن كانت المقامع برأسك تهيأ
38:72.english: Following the example of your father Adam (upon him be peace). For Wahb ibn Munabbih related: When God caused Adam to descend from Paradise to the earth, he remained in a state where his tears would not dry. Then God—mighty and majestic is He—looked upon him on the seventh day, and he was sorrowful, dejected, and choked with grief, his head bowed low. So God—exalted is He—revealed to him: "O Adam, what is this anguish I see in you?" He said: "O my Lord, my calamity has become immense, my sin has encompassed me, and I have been expelled from the dominion of my Lord. I have come to dwell in the abode of humiliation after honor, in the abode of misery after happiness, in the abode of toil after rest, in the abode of tribulation after well-being, in the abode of transience after permanence, and in the abode of death and annihilation after immortality and endurance. How should I not weep over my sin?" So God—exalted is He—revealed to him: "O Adam, did I not choose you for Myself, settle you in My abode, single you out with My honor, and warn you of My wrath? Did I not create you with My hand, breathe into you of My spirit, and cause My angels to prostrate before you? Yet you disobeyed My command, forgot My covenant, and exposed yourself to My wrath. By My might and My majesty, were I to fill the earth with men, all of them like you, worshipping Me and glorifying Me, and then they disobeyed Me, I would cast them down to the stations of the disobedient." At that, Adam (upon him be peace) wept for three hundred years.
38:72.section_title_en: Section 1255 — The Supplication of the Distressed and the Path of the Devout in Private Confession
38:72.anchors:
- Root: ضرر (ḍ-r-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of hardship, harm, and dire necessity; al-muḍṭarr is one compelled by overwhelming distress.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance of existential neediness before God, where the creature’s incapacity meets divine sufficiency.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) sense of physical/compelling necessity; metaphorical (majāz) extension to spiritual desperation and supplication.
- Root: كرم (k-r-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Nobility and generosity as intrinsic qualities of character and divine action.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): When ascribed to God, denotes His manifest, overflowing beneficence; when to humans, praiseworthy acts and virtues.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: abundant giving; metaphorical: the "generosity" of rain-laden clouds or a land rich in bounty.
- Root: عفو (ʿ-f-w)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Erasure, pardon, and remission of a fault; to leave something unpunished.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Divine pardon as the effacement of sin and the restoration of the sinner to a state of grace.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: blotting out; metaphorical: comprehensive mercy that "covers" (shāmil) all transgressions.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب النداء والتضرع (The Chapter of Vocative Appeal and Supplication) — Governing the syntactic patterns of direct address (yā) with epithets of divine mercy, and the anaphoric repetition of "anā" (I am...) for emphatic self-abasement.
38:72.topic: Al-Ghazali on the journey of the soul, death, and the Hereafter, from 'Monitoring and Accounting'

41:46.arabic: ومجاهداتك أيضا هو مستغن عنها وإنما هى طريقك إلى نجاتك فمن أحسن فلنفسه ومن أساء فعليها والله غنى عن العالمين ويحك يا نفس انزعى عن جهلك وقيسى آخرتك بدنياك فما خلقكم ولا بعثكم إلا كنفس واحدة وكما بدأنا أول خلق نعيده وكما بدأكم تعودون وسنة الله تعالى لا تجدين لها تبديلا ولا تحويلا ويحك يا نفس ما أراك إلا ألفت الدنيا وأنست بها فعسر عليك مفارقتها وأنت مقبلة على مقاربتها وتؤكدين في نفسك مودتها فاحسن أنك غافلة عن عقاب الله وثوابه وعن أهوال القيامة وأحوالها فما أنت مؤمنة بالموت المفرق بينك وبين محابك أفترين أن من يدخل دار ملك ليخرج من الج
41:46.english: ...from creation, but rather you attain your goal through every stratagem. And by this ignorance you deserve the title of foolishness from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, where he said: "The shrewd one is he who holds his soul to account and works for what comes after death, and the foolish one is he who follows his soul's whims and harbors vain hopes upon God." {«الكيس من دان نفسه وعمل لما بعد الموت والأحمق من أتبع نفسه هواها وتمنى على الله الأماني»}
41:46.section_title_en: Section 1253 — The Soul's Self-Reproach and the Awakening from Negligence
41:46.anchors:
- Root: نفس (n-f-s)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The self, soul, or spirit; that which animates and is addressed as an independent moral agent.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The soul as the locus of divine address and self-knowledge; its essence (dhāt) is the referent of God's "self" in revelation, yet here it is the reproaching subject.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (haqīqah) usage as the speaking, desiring self; metaphorical (majāz) extension to blame and counsel, as in "self-accusation" (lawwāmah).
- Root: موت (m-w-t)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Death as the cessation of life; the inevitable terminus of every soul.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Death as separation (furqah) from worldly attachments and the transition to reckoning; linked to the soul's journey.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal death of the body; metaphorical "death" of the heart through heedlessness, contrasted here with physical death as the ultimate wake-up call.
- Root: جهل (j-h-l)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Ignorance as the absence of knowledge; folly and rashness.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Ignorance as the soul's failure to perceive true realities, leading to misplaced desires and false hopes.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal ignorance of facts; metaphorical ignorance as moral stupidity, as when the soul follows whims despite clear signs.
- Root: دنا (d-n-w)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Nearness in place, time, or rank.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Drawing near (dunūw) to God through obedience, contrasted with the soul's clinging to the near (dunyā) world.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal proximity; metaphorical use for the "lower" world (dunyā) as that which is nearer and inferior.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — Used to emphasize exclusive causation, e.g., "God's generosity is only in guiding you to the path," restricting divine favor to guidance, not exemption from effort.
41:46.topic: Al-Ghazali on the journey of the soul, death, and the Hereafter, from 'Monitoring and Accounting'
