28:60.arabic: الليل يتلذذ به في رجاء إنعامه والرجاء في حق الله تعالى أصدق وما عند الله خير وأبقى وأنفع مما عند غيره فكيف لا يتلذذ بعرض الحاجات عليه في الخلوات وأما النقل فيشهد له أحوال قوام الليل في تلذذهم بقيام الليل واستقصارهم له كما يستقصر المحب ليلة وصال الحبيب حتى قيل لبعضهم كيف أنت والليل قال ما راعيته قط يريني وجهه ثم ينصرف وما تأملته بعد وقال آخر أنا والليل فرسا رهان مرة يسبقني إلى الفجر ومرة يقطعني عن الفكر وقيل لبعضهم كيف الليل عليك فقال ساعة أنا فيها بين حالتين أفرح بظلمته إذا جاء وأغتم بفجره إذا طلع ما تم فرحي به قط وقال علي بن ب
28:60.english: That if the beautiful Beloved were behind a veil or in a dark house, the lover would still take delight in mere proximity to Him, without vision and without coveting any other matter besides Him — and he would find joy in displaying his love before Him and in mentioning Him with his tongue within His hearing, even though that too were already known to Him. For if you say: "He awaits His response" — then let him delight in hearing His response; yet he does not hear the speech of God, exalted be He. Know then that if he knows that He will not answer him and will remain silent toward him, there still remains for him a delight in presenting his states before Him and in raising his innermost secret to Him. How [could it be otherwise], when the one who is certain (al-mūqin) hears from God, exalted be He, everything that occurs to his mind during the course of his whispered communion (munājāh), and thus takes delight in it? Likewise, one who secludes himself with a king and presents his needs to him in the depths of the night takes delight in it through hope of his beneficence — and hope with respect to God, exalted be He, is more truthful, and what is with God is better, more enduring, and more beneficial than what is with anyone else. So how would he not delight in presenting his needs before Him in private seclusions (khalawāt)?
28:60.section_title_en: On the Delight of Night Vigil and Whispered Communion — Section 277
28:60.anchors:
- Root: ليل (layl)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Night; the period of darkness following sunset until dawn; its diminutive is 'luyaylah' and its plural is 'layālin' — indicating a temporal span marked by stillness and concealment.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Night (al-layl) is that which veils (yughashshī) and covers, as in {«وَاللَّيْلِ إِذَا يَغْشَى»} — a time when sensory distractions recede and the heart turns toward intimate communion (munājāh) with the Divine.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (haqīqah): the astronomical night. Metaphorical (majāz): the night of the heart — a state of spiritual wakefulness wherein the lover finds delight in solitude with the Beloved, as expressed in the sayings of the pious transmitted herein.
- Root: نور (nūr)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Light; illumination that renders things visible; also the fire-kindling and the beacon (manār) guiding travelers.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Light is of two kinds: sensory light perceived by the eye, and intellectual/spiritual light (nūr al-ʿaql, nūr al-Qurʾān) perceived by the inner eye of insight (baṣīrah). The Divine light cast into the hearts of the vigilant is of this latter kind — an immaterial radiance (laṭīfah nūrāniyyah) that transforms the inner state.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical illumination. Metaphorical: 'nawwara al-amr' — to clarify and illuminate a matter; here, the spreading of spiritual lights (anwār) from wakeful hearts to heedless ones is a metaphorical extension of this root, signifying the transmission of divine grace.
- Root: قلب (qalb)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The heart; also the turning and revolving of a thing from one state to another (taqlīb).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The heart is so named for its constant fluctuation (taqallub) between states; it is the seat of perception and understanding, the locus of divine address and the receptacle of spiritual lights.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the physical organ. Metaphorical: 'qallaba al-amr' — to examine and turn over a matter; here, the hearts of the vigilant are 'turned over' by divine light, and from them 'spread' (tantašir) blessings to others — a metaphorical extension of physical turning to spiritual transformation.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — The particle 'innamā' restricts and confines the predicate to the subject alone, as in the transmitted saying: "The delight of whispered communion is not of this world; it is only (innamā) of Paradise" — a focused predication that negates any worldly share of this pleasure and affirms its exclusive otherworldly origin.
28:60.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Arrangement of Litanies'

29:45.arabic: فعلة فيحرم بها قيام سنة وكما إن الصلاة تنهي عن الفحشاء والمنكر فكذلك الفحشاء تنهى عن الصلاة وسائر الخيرات وقال بعض السجانين كنت سجانا نيفا وثلاثين سنة أسأل كل مأخوذ بالليل أنه هل صلى العشاء في جماعة فكانوا يقولون لا وهذا تنبيه على أن بركة الجماعة تنهى عن تعاطي الفحشاء والمنكر وأما الميسرات الباطنة فأربعة أمور الأول سلامة القلب عن الحقد على المسلمين وعن البدع وعن فضول هموم الدنيا فالمستغرق الهم بتدبير الدنيا لا يتيسر له القيام وإن قام فلا يتفكر في صلاته إلا في مهماته ولا يجول إلا في وساوسه وفي مثل ذلك يقال يخبرني البو
29:45.english: **The fourth:** That one not accumulate sins (awzār) during the day, for sins are among the things that harden the heart and interpose between it and the causes of mercy. A man said to al-Hasan [al-Basrī]: "O Abū Saʿīd, I spend the night in sound health, I love night prayer, and I prepare my purification water — yet what is the matter that I do not rise [for prayer]?" He replied: "Your sins have bound you in chains." And al-Hasan — may God have mercy on him — when he entered the marketplace and heard their clamor and idle talk, would say: "I think that the night of these people is an evil night, for they do not take the midday nap."
29:45.section_title_en: The Revival of the Religious Sciences — Section 275: On the Conditions Facilitating Night Prayer (Qiyām al-Layl)
29:45.anchors:
- Root: ق-ي-م (Q-Y-M)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of standing upright, rising, and establishing; Qiyām al-Layl denotes the supererogatory night vigil of prayer and devotion.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Qiyām carries the sense of "rising up" in obedience and "standing" in worship, distinguished from mere physical posture by its intentional orientation toward the Divine.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah) usage denotes physical standing; metaphorical (Majaz) usage extends to "rising up" in resolve, vigilance, and spiritual exertion against the soul's inertia.
- Root: ن-و-م (N-W-M)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Sleep as the suspension of conscious activity; the root also yields "manām" (dream/sleep) and "nawm" as a state of repose.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "النوم: فسر على أوجه كلها صحيح بنظرات مختلفة" — Sleep is interpreted in multiple valid ways: as relaxation of the brain's nerves from ascending vapors, as God's "taking" of the soul without death {«الله يتوفى الأنفس»}, and as "a light death" while death is "a heavy sleep."
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "قوم نيام" (a sleeping people). Metaphorical: "نامت السوق" (the market slept = stagnated); "نام الثوب" (the garment slept = wore out). Here, sleep's dominance over the body is the literal obstacle, while spiritual heedlessness (ghaflah) is its metaphorical correlate.
- Root: ق-ل-ب (Q-L-B)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The heart as the seat of cognition and moral disposition; the root denotes overturning, turning from one state to another.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "قلب الشيء: تصريفه وصرفه عن وجه إلى وجه" — To turn a thing from one face to another. The heart's "turning" (taqlīb) is its oscillation between states of guidance and heedlessness, faith and hardness.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "قلب الثوب" (to turn a garment). Metaphorical: "قلب المعلم الصبيان" (the teacher turned the boys toward their homes); "رجل قلب حول" (a man who turns matters over, discerning). The heart's "overturning" (inqilāb) from its prior state of softness to hardness is the precise mechanism of sin's effect described herein.
- Root: ا-ذ-ا (I-DH-A)
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "إذا يعبر به عن كل زمان مستقبل" — "Idhā" denotes any future time, sometimes carrying conditional force. Its use here signals the recurrent, habitual nature of the described causes and effects.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The permissibility of interposing elements between a governing word and its governed prepositional phrase when the intervening material forms a complete, meaningful unit, as in the conditional structures "إذا ... فـ" that organize the causal sequences of this section.
29:45.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Arrangement of Litanies'

29:45.arabic: الرضا فوق جنات عدن كما رفع ذكره فوق الصلاة حيث قال {إن الصلاة تنهي عن الفحشاء والمنكر ولذكر الله أكبر} فكما أن مشاهدة المذكور في الصلاة أكبر من الصلاة فرضوان رب الجنة أعلى من الجنة بل هو غاية مطلب سكان الجنان وفي الحديث إن الله تعالى يتجلى للمؤمنين فيقول سلوني فيقولون رضاك (1) فسؤالهم الرضا بعد النظر نهاية التفضيل وأما رضا العبد فسنذكر حقيقته وأما رضوان الله تعالى عن العبد فهو بمعنى آخر يقرب مما ذكرناه في حب الله للعبد ولا يجوز أن يكشف عن حقيقته إذ تقصر أفهام الخلق عن دركه ومن يقوى عليه فيستقل بإدراكه من نفسه وعلى الجملة فلا رتبة فوق النظر
29:45.english: I say: As for the verses [indicating the supremacy of divine pleasure], there is the saying of the Exalted: {رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمْ وَرَضُوا عَنْهُ} [Allah is well-pleased with them and they are well-pleased with Him] {«God is well-pleased with them and they are well-pleased with Him»}. And the Exalted has said: {هَلْ جَزَاءُ الْإِحْسَانِ إِلَّا الْإِحْسَانُ} [Is the reward of goodness aught but goodness?] {«Is the reward of goodness aught but goodness?»}. The ultimate end of goodness is God's pleasure with His servant, and that is the reward for the servant's pleasure in God the Exalted.
29:45.section_title_en: The Reality of Divine Pleasure (Riḍā) and the Servant's Contentment with the Decree — Section 1189
29:45.anchors:
- Root: رضي (raḍiya)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning is "to be content, to approve, to be pleased." Al-Farahidi notes its usage in mutual accord and satisfaction, with the form *tarāḍin* indicating reciprocal consent.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In theological usage, *riḍā* denotes the will's acquiescence to the divine decree without resistance. It is the apex of the servant's station, being the fruit of *maḥabbah* (love) and the key to perpetual vision (*nazar*).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (*ḥaqīqah*) sense is "satisfaction of the heart." Metaphorical (*majāz*) extension applies to God, where *riḍwān* is not an emotional state but a volitional attribute signifying the bestowal of grace and the removal of the veil.
- Root: نظر (naẓara)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "To look, to behold, to consider." In the lexicon, *naẓar* implies directed vision with the eye or the intellect.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Elevated to the highest beatific vision (*ru'yat Allāh*) in the afterlife, the ultimate reward and the supreme object of the inhabitants of Paradise.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical sight. Metaphorical: intellectual contemplation or the unveiled witnessing of the Divine in the Hereafter.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب التفضيل والتشبيه (The Chapter of Preference and Comparison) — Governing the syntactic structures of *afʿala* (elative) forms like *akbar* ("greater") to establish hierarchical supremacy between two entities, as in the verse {وَرِضْوَانٌ مِنَ اللَّهِ أَكْبَرُ}.
29:45.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Love, Longing, Intimacy and Contentment'

32:16.arabic: يعلمون والذين لا يعلمون} وقال تعالى {تتجافى جنوبهم عن المضاجع يدعون ربهم خوفا وطمعا} وقال عز وجل {والذين يبيتون لربهم سجدا وقياما} وقال عز وجل {كانوا قليلا من الليل ما يهجعون وبالأسحار هم يستغفرون} وقال عز وجل {فسبحان الله حين تمسون وحين تصبحون} وقال تعالى {ولا تطرد الذين يدعون ربهم بالغداة والعشي يريدون وجهه} فهذا كله يبين لك أن الطريق إلى تعالى مراقبة الأوقات وعمارتها بالأوراد على سبيل الدوام ولذلك قال صلى الله عليه وسلم أحب عباد الله إلى الله الذين يراعون الشمس والقمر والأظلة لذكر الله تعالى (1) وقد قال تعالى {الشمس والقمر بحسبا
32:16.english: {«آناء الليل ساجدا وقائما يحذر الآخرة ويرجو رحمة ربه قل هل يستوي الذين يعلمون والذين لا يعلمون»} — "During the hours of the night, prostrating and standing, fearing the Hereafter and hoping for the mercy of his Lord. Say: Are those who know equal to those who do not know?" (Q. 39:9). And God Most High said: {«تتجافى جنوبهم عن المضاجع يدعون ربهم خوفا وطمعا»} — "Their sides forsake their beds, calling upon their Lord in fear and hope" (Q. 32:16). And God, Mighty and Majestic, said: {«والذين يبيتون لربهم سجدا وقياما»} — "And those who pass the night prostrating and standing before their Lord" (Q. 25:64). And God, Mighty and Majestic, said: {«كانوا قليلا من الليل ما يهجعون وبالأسحار هم يستغفرون»} — "They used to sleep but little of the night, and in the dawn-hours they would seek forgiveness" (Q. 51:17-18). And God, Mighty and Majestic, said: {«فسبحان الله حين تمسون وحين تصبحون»} — "So glory be to God when you enter the evening and when you enter the morning" (Q. 30:17). And God Most High said: {«ولا تطرد الذين يدعون ربهم بالغداة والعشي يريدون وجهه»} — "And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord morning and evening, desiring His Face" (Q. 6:52). All of this makes clear to you that the path to God Most High is the watchfulness over the times (murāqabat al-awqāt) and the cultivation of them with the appointed devotions (al-awrād) in a perpetual manner.
32:16.section_title_en: The Revival of the Religious Sciences — Section 258: The Virtues of the Watches (Awrād) and Their Ordering
32:16.anchors:
- Root: ورد (w-r-d)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning is "to arrive at water" — the quenching of thirst at a watering place; al-Wird (pl. Awrād) denotes a set portion or appointed round of devotional recitation, by extension from the regular "arrival" at a source.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-Wurūd is originally "the intending of water," then used for other things. The theological nuance: the awrād are the appointed "watering places" of the soul — fixed times at which the servant presents himself before God to drink from the fountain of remembrance (dhikr).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): "warda al-mā'a" — to arrive at water. Metaphorical (Majāz): "warada ʿalayhi amrun lam yuṭiqhu" — an affair he could not bear arrived upon him; "waradat-hu al-ḥummā" — fever came upon him. Here, the awrād are the appointed times that "come upon" the servant, demanding their due of devotion.
- Root: طلع (ṭ-l-ʿ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To rise, to appear above the horizon (of the sun); to ascend; to come upon suddenly.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Ṭalaʿa al-shams ṭulūʿan wa-maṭlaʿan" — the sun rose. From this is borrowed: "ṭalaʿa ʿalaynā fulān" — so-and-so came upon us. The maṭlaʿ is the place of rising.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "ṭalaʿat al-shams" — the sun rose. Metaphorical: "ṭalaʿa ʿalaynā fulān" — he descended upon us suddenly. The "rising of the sun" is the boundary-marker of the first watch.
- Root: ليل (l-y-l)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The night — from the time of sunset to sunrise; its root suggests "enveloping" and "concealing."
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The night (al-layl) and the day (al-nahār) are two signs (āyatān) of God; the night is for stillness and the day for seeking provision.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the period of darkness. Metaphorical: "layl al-hamm" — the night of anxiety (a dark affair). The night is divided into watches for the one who stands in prayer.
- Sibawayh Rule: Bāb al-ḥaṣr wa-al-taqyīd bi-innamā (Restriction and Focused Predication) — The particle innamā restricts the predicate to the subject alone, negating all else. Applied here: "the purpose of the sun and moon's course is not for worldly matters, but only (innamā) for knowing the measures of the times."
32:16.topic: Al-Ghazali on constant remembrance of God and contemplative invocations, from 'Arrangement of Litanies'

32:16.arabic: وقيل إنها المراد بقوله عز وجل تتجافى جنوبهم عن المضاجع وقد روي عنه صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال من صلى بين المغرب والعشاء فإنها من صلاة الأوابين (3) وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم من عكف نفسه فيما بين المغرب والعشاء في مسجد جماعة لم يتكلم إلا بصلاة أو بقرآن كان حقا على الله أن يبني له قصرين في الجنة مسيرة كل قصر منهما مائة عام ويغرس له بينهما غراسا لوطافة أهل الأرض لوسعهم (4) وسيأتي بقية فضائلها في كتاب الأوراد إن شاء الله تعالى القسم الثاني ما يتكرر بتكرر الأسابيع وهي صلاة أيام الأسبوع ولياليه لكل يوم ولكل
32:16.english: The eighth: Reviving the time between the two evening prayers (al-maghrib and al-ʿishāʾ). It is an emphatically confirmed sunnah. What has been transmitted of its number from the action of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) between the two evening prayers is six rakʿahs (2). This prayer has a tremendous virtue. It was said that it is what is meant by His saying, Mighty and Majestic: {«Their sides forsake their beds»} (Q. 32:16). And it is narrated from him (ﷺ) that he said: "Whoever prays between the maghrib and the ʿishāʾ, it is among the prayers of the penitent (al-awwābīn)" (3). And he (ﷺ) said: "Whoever confines himself between the maghrib and the ʿishāʾ in a congregational mosque, speaking nothing but prayer or Quran, it is incumbent upon Allah to build for him two palaces in Paradise, the journey of each palace being a hundred years, and to plant for him between them plantings that, if the inhabitants of the earth were to traverse them, would encompass them" (4). The remainder of its virtues will come in the Book of Liturgies (Kitāb al-Awrād), if Allah the Exalted wills.
32:16.section_title_en: Section 158 — On the Witr Prayer, the Forenoon (Ḍuḥā) Prayer, and the Prayer Between the Two Evening Prayers
32:16.anchors:
- Root: وتر (w-t-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The odd, the single; that which is not paired; to make odd; also vengeance or injury (watr/witar).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الوتر في العدد خلاف الشفع" — the odd in number as opposed to the even; al-ītār is to pray the witr; tawātur is succession one-by-one.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "وأوتر: صلى الوتر" — to perform the witr prayer. Metaphorical: "وترته حقه" — to deprive one of his right; "كأنما وتر أهله وماله" — as if bereft of family and wealth.
- Root: ركع (r-k-ʿ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To bow, to incline the head and body downward.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الركوع: الانحناء" — bowing; used for the specific posture in prayer and metaphorically for humility and submission.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "شيخ راكع: منحن من الكبر" — an old man bowed with age; "ركوع الصلاة" — the bowing of prayer. Metaphorical: "لغبت الإبل حتى ركعت" — camels fatigued until they sank to their knees.
- Root: ورد (w-r-d)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To arrive at water; to approach; to come to a place.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الورود أصله: قصد الماء" — its root meaning is to seek water; then used for other things; "الورد" — the daily portion of recitation or litany.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "ورد الماء وودا ووردا" — to arrive at water. Metaphorical: "وردت البلد" — to enter a land; "ورد عليه كتاب" — a letter arrived; "هو حسن الإيراد" — excellent in delivery; "الورد" — the daily litany.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد (Restriction & Specification) — The conditional and restrictive particles (إنما، إن، لو) govern the scope of legal validity, as seen in the precise conditions for the witr prayer's correctness.
32:16.topic: Al-Ghazali on the journey of the soul, death, and the Hereafter, from 'Arrangement of Litanies'

32:25.arabic: عالم الغيب والشهادة أنت تحكم بين عبادك فيما كانوا فيه يختلفون اهدني لما اختلف فيه من الحق بإذنك إنك تهدي من تشاء إلى صراط مستقيما (7) ثم يفتتح الصلاة ويصلي ركعتين خفيفتين ثم يصلي مثنى مثنى ما تيسر له ويختم بالوتر إن لم يكن قد صلى الوتر ويستحب أن يفصل بين الصلاتين عند تسليمه بمائة تسبيحة ليستريح ويزيد نشاطه للصلاة وقد صح في صلاة رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بالليل أنه صلى أولا ركعتين خفيفتين ثم ركعتين طويلتين ثم ركعتين دون اللتين قبلهما ثم لم يزل يقصر بالتدريج إلى ثلاث عشرة ركعة (1) وسئلت عائشة رضي الله
32:25.english: Then it is recommended, after the salutation of the witr, that he say: "Glory be to the King, the Most Holy, the Lord of the angels and the Spirit. You have enveloped the heavens and the earth with majesty and dominion. You have manifested Your might through power, and You have subdued the servants through death." It is related that he (peace and blessings be upon him) — until he died — most of his prayer was seated, except for the obligatory prayers (1). And he said to the one who prays seated: "Half the reward of the one who prays standing," and to the one who sleeps: "Half the reward of the one who prays seated" (2). This indicates the validity of the supererogatory prayer in all states.

33:35.arabic: الله عليه وسلم من استيقظ من الليل وأيقظ امرأته فصليا ركعتين كتبا من الذاكرين الله كثيرا والذاكرات (8) وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم أفضل الصلاة بعد المكتوبة قيام الليل (9) وقال عمر بن الخطاب رضي الله عنه قال صلى الله عليه وسلم من نام عن حزبه أو عن شيء منه بالليل فقرأه بين صلاة الفجر والظهر كتب له كأنما قرأه من الليل (1) الآثار روي أن عمر رضي الله عنه كان يمر بالآية من ورده بالليل فيسقط حتى يعاد منها أياما كثيرة كما يعاد المريض وكان ابن مسعود رضي الله عنه إذا هدأت العيون قام فيسمع له دوي كدوي النحل حتى يصبح ويقال إن سفيان الثوري رحمه
33:35.english: Know — may God guide you — that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "O Abū Hurayrah, if you desire the pleasure of your Lord, pray in the corners of your house, and the light of your house will be in the heaven like the light of the stars and the planets in the sight of the people of the earth." (7)
33:35.section_title_en: Section 273 — The Virtues of Night Prayer (Qiyām al-Layl) and the Narrations Concerning the Devotions of the Righteous
33:35.anchors:

  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Night is contrasted with day as a sign of divine order; "قيام الليل" (night vigil) is the specific act of standing in prayer during the night hours
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — the night-time period; Metaphorical — "أصبح" as awakening from heedlessness, used for spiritual awakening
- Root: صبح (Ṣubḥ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Dawn, morning; the time when the horizon reddens with the sun's approach
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الصبح والصباح، أول النهار" — the first part of the day; "أسحرنا" (has dawn approached?) is the question asked to determine the end of the night vigil
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — daybreak; Metaphorical — "أصبح يا رجل: انتبه من غفلتك" (awaken from your heedlessness), used for spiritual alertness
- Root: حتي (Ḥattā)
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): A preposition of termination — "until"; used to mark the endpoint of the night vigil at dawn
  * Sibawayh Rule: When ḥattā governs the subjunctive, it means "until such time as"; when followed by the indicative, it denotes a resulting state or concurrent circumstance
- Root: عله (ʿAlaha)
  * Lisan al-Arab: To be occupied with something; to be diverted from one's appointed task — as in the one who sleeps past his nightly devotion (wird)

37:99.arabic: وإليه الإشارة بقوله إني ذاهب إلى ربي سيهدين وهذه منتهى درجات الصديقين ولا وصول إليها إلا بعد ترتيب الأوراد والمواظبة عليها دهرا طويلا فلا ينبغي أن يغتر المريد بما سمعه من ذلك فيدعيه لنفسه ويفتر عن وظائف عبادته فذلك علامته أن لا يهجس في قلبه وسواس ولا يخطر في قلبه معصية ولا ترعجه هواجم الأهوال ولا تستفزه عظائم الأشغال وأنى ترزق هذه الرتبة لكل أحد فيتعين على الكافة ترتيب الأوراد كما ذكرناه وجميع ما ذكرناه طرق إلى الله تعالى قال تعالى قل كل يعمل على شاكلته فربكم أعلم بمن هو أهدى سبيلا فكلهم مهت
37:99.english: The fifth [category]: the ruler (al-wālī) — such as the Imām, the judge (al-qāḍī), and the one who administers the affairs of the Muslims. His undertaking the needs of the Muslims and their interests in accordance with the Sacred Law (al-sharʿ) and with the intention of sincerity (ikhlāṣ) is superior to the aforementioned litanies (al-awrād). It is fitting for him to occupy himself with the rights of the people by day, to content himself with the obligatory prayers (al-maktūbah), and to perform the aforementioned litanies by night — just as ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him, used to do, for he said: "What have I to do with sleep? If I sleep by day, I waste the Muslims; and if I sleep by night, I waste my own soul."
37:99.section_title_en: The Revival of the Religious Sciences — Section 269: On the Superiority of Transitive Acts of Worship and the Paths to God
37:99.anchors:
- Root: ورد (w-r-d)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning is "to arrive at water" — the quenching of thirst by reaching the source.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الورود أصله: قصد الماء" — theologically extended to mean the soul's approach to God; the "litany" (wird) is the appointed spiritual "watering" that sustains the traveler.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): "ورد الماء" (to arrive at water). Metaphorical (Majaz): "ورد عليه أمر لم يطقه" (an affair befell him) and "طرقني الخيال" (the phantom visited me) — thus the wird is the appointed visitation of the heart by divine remembrance.
- Root: نفس (n-f-s)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The self, the soul; that which breathes and has vital spirit.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "النفس: الروح" — the immaterial reality of the human; in the verse {«ويحذركم الله نفسه»} it denotes the very Essence (al-Dhāt), not a physical part.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "نفس سائلة" (flowing blood/life). Metaphorical: "أصابته نفس" (an evil eye afflicted him) — showing the soul's power to effect beyond its own bounds.
- Root: طرق (t-r-q)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To strike, to beat, to knock; a path beaten by feet.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الطريق: السبيل الذي يطرق بالأرجل" — then extended to every path (maslak) a man traverses in deed, whether praiseworthy or blameworthy.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "طرق الباب" (to knock at the door). Metaphorical: "طرقني الخيال" (the phantom came to me by night) — hence the "ways to God" (turūq) are the paths beaten by the feet of the seekers, each leading to the Door.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — Used to distinguish the exclusive rank of the muwaḥḥid whose sole concern is God, and to restrict the claim of such a station to those who have first traversed the ordered litanies.
37:99.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Arrangement of Litanies'

38:66.arabic: يقوله رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لا إله إلا الله الواحد القهار رب السموات والأرض وما بينهما العزيز الغفار (3) وليجتهد أن يكون آخر ما يجري على قلبه عند النوم ذكر الله تعالى وأول ما يرد على قلبه عند التيقظ ذكر الله تعالى فهو علامة الحب ولا يلازم القلب في هاتين الحالتين إلا ما هو الغالب عليه فليجرب قلبه به فهو علامة الحب فإنها علامة تكشف من باطن القلب وإنما استحبت هذه الأذكار لتستجر القلب إلى ذكر الله تعالى فإذا استيقظ ليقوم قال الحمد لله الذي أحيانا بعد ما أماتنا وإليه النشور إلى آخر ما أوردناه من أدعية التيقظ الورد الرابع يدخل بمضي النصف الأول
38:66.english: Then it is recommended, after the salutation of the witr, that he say: "Glory be to the King, the Most Holy, the Lord of the angels and the Spirit. You have enveloped the heavens and the earth with majesty and dominion. You have manifested Your might through power, and You have subdued the servants through death." It is related that he (peace and blessings be upon him) — until he died — most of his prayer was seated, except for the obligatory prayers (1). This indicates the validity of the supererogatory prayer in all states.

39:42.arabic: تعالى الله يتوفى الأنفس حين موتها والتي لم تمت في منامها {وقال} وهو الذي يتوفاكم بالليل فسماه توفيا وكما أن المستيقظ تنكشف له مشاهدات لا تناسب أحواله في النوم فكذلك المبعوث يرى ما لم يخطر قط بباله ولا شاهده حسه ومثل النوم بين الحياة والموت مثل البزخ بين الدنيا والآخرة وقال لقمان لابنه يا بني إن كنت تشك في الموت فلا تنم فكما أنك تنام كذلك تموت وإن كنت تشك في البعث فلا تنتبه فكما أنك تنتبه بعد نومك فكذلك تبعث بعد موتك وقال كعب الأحبار إذا نمت فاضطجع على شقك الأيمن واستقبل القبلة بوجهك فإنها وفاة وقالت
39:42.english: Then it is recommended, after the salutation of the witr, that he say: "Glory be to the King, the Most Holy, the Lord of the angels and the Spirit. 40:55.arabic: مأخوذ من قوله تعالى {واستغفر لذنبك وسبح بحمد ربك بالعشي والإبكار} والاستغفار على الأسماء التي في القرآن أحب كقوله أستغفر الله إنه كان غفارا أستغفر الله إنه كان توابا رب اغفر وارحم وأنت خير الراحمين فاغفر لنا وارحمنا وأنت خير الراحمين فاغفر لنا وارحمنا وأنت خير الغافرين ويستحب أن يقرأ قبل غروب الشمس والشمس وضحاها والليل إذا يغشى والمعوذتين ولتغرب الشمس عليه وهو في الاستغفار فإذا سمع الأذان قال اللهم هذا إقبال ليلك وإدبار نهارك وأصوات دعاتك كما سبق ثم يجيب المؤذن ويشتغل بصلاة المغرب وبالغروب قد انتهت أوراد
40:55.english: I say: And just as knowledge and remembrance are the nourishment of the heart, which can never be cut off from it, so too the measure of moderation is this; and deficiency from it may lead to the disturbance of the body — except for one who accustoms himself to wakefulness gradually, for he may train himself upon it without disturbance. And this litany (wird) is among the longest of the litanies and the most delightful for the worshippers, and it is one of the "evenings and mornings" (al-āṣāl) which God Most High mentioned when He said: {«ولله يسجد من في السموات والأرض طوعا وكرها وظلالهم بالغدو والآصال»} "And to God prostrates whoever is in the heavens and the earth, willingly or unwillingly, and their shadows, in the mornings and the evenings" (Q. 13:15). And when inanimate objects prostrate to God, Mighty and Majestic, how then can the intelligent servant be heedless of the varieties of worship?
40:55.section_title_en: The Seventh Daily Litany (Al-Wird al-Sābiʿ): The Time of Sunset — The Completion of the Day's Litanies and Self-Accounting
40:55.anchors:
- Root: ورد (warada)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The root denotes arriving at water, seeking it, and drinking from it; also the portion or share of water allotted for drinking at a specific time.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الورود أصله: قصد الماء" — the core meaning is the intentional approach to water; the litany (wird) is the appointed portion of devotional recitation, likened to the daily share of water that a person must take to sustain life.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): the act of arriving at water. Metaphorical (Majaz): "ورد علي كتاب سرني مورده" — a book arrived upon me whose arrival pleased me; likewise, the wird is the arrival of the appointed time for worship, and the soul's approach to the fountain of divine remembrance.
- Root: عصر (ʿaṣr)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The root denotes pressing, squeezing, and extracting; also the time of afternoon, so called because it is the pressing of the day's end.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The ʿaṣr is the latter part of the day; God swore by it in {«والعصر»} (Q. 103:1), indicating its great merit.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the afternoon time. Metaphorical: the pressing of one's life — as the day is pressed at its end, so the life of man is pressed at its term.
- Root: غرب (gharaba)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The root denotes disappearance, absence, and setting; the sun's setting (ghurūb) is its concealment from the eye.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The setting of the sun marks the boundary between the day's works and the night's; it is the terminus of the visible world's diurnal cycle.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the sun's descent below the horizon. Metaphorical: the setting of the sun of life — the death of man, after which there is no rising.
- Root: حاسب (ḥāsaba)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The root denotes reckoning, counting, and taking account; muḥāsabah is the mutual reckoning between two parties.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Self-accounting (muḥāsabat al-nafs) is the soul's reckoning with itself over its deeds before the Day of Reckoning, for "one who reckons himself before he is reckoned" is among the wise.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the arithmetic counting of sums. Metaphorical: the soul's audit of its own works, weighing the day's deeds against the standard of the Sacred Law.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The rule governing the separation of the prepositional phrase from its governing verb, as in the construction "فسبحان الله حين تمسون" where the adverbial clause is interposed to emphasize the temporal specification of the act of glorification.
40:55.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications, prayers, and their spiritual power, from 'Arrangement of Litanies'

42:36.arabic: الليل يتلذذ به في رجاء إنعامه والرجاء في حق الله تعالى أصدق وما عند الله خير وأبقى وأنفع مما عند غيره فكيف لا يتلذذ بعرض الحاجات عليه في الخلوات وأما النقل فيشهد له أحوال قوام الليل في تلذذهم بقيام الليل واستقصارهم له كما يستقصر المحب ليلة وصال الحبيب حتى قيل لبعضهم كيف أنت والليل قال ما راعيته قط يريني وجهه ثم ينصرف وما تأملته بعد وقال آخر أنا والليل فرسا رهان مرة يسبقني إلى الفجر ومرة يقطعني عن الفكر وقيل لبعضهم كيف الليل عليك فقال ساعة أنا فيها بين حالتين أفرح بظلمته إذا جاء وأغتم بفجره إذا طلع ما تم فرحي به قط وقال علي بن ب
42:36.english: That if the beautiful Beloved were behind a veil or in a dark house, the lover would still take delight in mere proximity to Him, without vision and without coveting any other matter besides Him — and he would find joy in displaying his love before Him and in mentioning Him with his tongue within His hearing, even though that too were already known to Him. For if you say: "He awaits His response" — then let him delight in hearing His response; yet he does not hear the speech of God, exalted be He. Know then that if he knows that He will not answer him and will remain silent toward him, there still remains for him a delight in presenting his states before Him and in raising his innermost secret to Him. How [could it be otherwise], when the one who is certain (al-mūqin) hears from God, exalted be He, everything that occurs to his mind during the course of his whispered communion (munājāh), and thus takes delight in it? Likewise, one who secludes himself with a king and presents his needs to him in the depths of the night takes delight in it through hope of his beneficence — and hope with respect to God, exalted be He, is more truthful, and what is with God is better, more enduring, and more beneficial than what is with anyone else. So how would he not delight in presenting his needs before Him in private seclusions (khalawāt)?
42:36.section_title_en: On the Delight of Night Vigil and Whispered Communion — Section 277
42:36.anchors:
- Root: ليل (layl)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Night; the period of darkness following sunset until dawn; its diminutive is 'luyaylah' and its plural is 'layālin' — indicating a temporal span marked by stillness and concealment.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Night (al-layl) is that which veils (yughashshī) and covers, as in {«وَاللَّيْلِ إِذَا يَغْشَى»} — a time when sensory distractions recede and the heart turns toward intimate communion (munājāh) with the Divine.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (haqīqah): the astronomical night. Metaphorical (majāz): the night of the heart — a state of spiritual wakefulness wherein the lover finds delight in solitude with the Beloved, as expressed in the sayings of the pious transmitted herein.
- Root: نور (nūr)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Light; illumination that renders things visible; also the fire-kindling and the beacon (manār) guiding travelers.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Light is of two kinds: sensory light perceived by the eye, and intellectual/spiritual light (nūr al-ʿaql, nūr al-Qurʾān) perceived by the inner eye of insight (baṣīrah). The Divine light cast into the hearts of the vigilant is of this latter kind — an immaterial radiance (laṭīfah nūrāniyyah) that transforms the inner state.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical illumination. Metaphorical: 'nawwara al-amr' — to clarify and illuminate a matter; here, the spreading of spiritual lights (anwār) from wakeful hearts to heedless ones is a metaphorical extension of this root, signifying the transmission of divine grace.
- Root: قلب (qalb)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The heart; also the turning and revolving of a thing from one state to another (taqlīb).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The heart is so named for its constant fluctuation (taqallub) between states; it is the seat of perception and understanding, the locus of divine address and the receptacle of spiritual lights.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the physical organ. Metaphorical: 'qallaba al-amr' — to examine and turn over a matter; here, the hearts of the vigilant are 'turned over' by divine light, and from them 'spread' (tantašir) blessings to others — a metaphorical extension of physical turning to spiritual transformation.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — The particle 'innamā' restricts and confines the predicate to the subject alone, as in the transmitted saying: "The delight of whispered communion is not of this world; it is only (innamā) of Paradise" — a focused predication that negates any worldly share of this pleasure and affirms its exclusive otherworldly origin.
42:36.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Arrangement of Litanies'

45:17.arabic: عالم الغيب والشهادة أنت تحكم بين عبادك فيما كانوا فيه يختلفون اهدني لما اختلف فيه من الحق بإذنك إنك تهدي من تشاء إلى صراط مستقيما (7) ثم يفتتح الصلاة ويصلي ركعتين خفيفتين ثم يصلي مثنى مثنى ما تيسر له ويختم بالوتر إن لم يكن قد صلى الوتر ويستحب أن يفصل بين الصلاتين عند تسليمه بمائة تسبيحة ليستريح ويزيد نشاطه للصلاة وقد صح في صلاة رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بالليل أنه صلى أولا ركعتين خفيفتين ثم ركعتين طويلتين ثم ركعتين دون اللتين قبلهما ثم لم يزل يقصر بالتدريج إلى ثلاث عشرة ركعة (1) وسئلت عائشة رضي الله
45:17.english: Then it is recommended, after the salutation of the witr, that he say: "Glory be to the King, the Most Holy, the Lord of the angels and the Spirit. You have enveloped the heavens and the earth with majesty and dominion. You have manifested Your might through power, and You have subdued the servants through death." It is related that he (peace and blessings be upon him) — until he died — most of his prayer was seated, except for the obligatory prayers (1). And he said to the one who prays seated: "Half the reward of the one who prays standing," and to the one who sleeps: "Half the reward of the one who prays seated" (2). This indicates the validity of the supererogatory prayer in all states.
45:17.section_title_en: The Fourth and Fifth Wirds (Portions of Night Devotion): On Sleep and the Final Sixth of the Night
45:17.anchors:
- Root: ليل (Layl)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Night; the period of darkness from sunset to dawn; its plural forms include layālī and layalāt.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Night is a divinely ordained sign (āyah) of Allah's power; sleep is described as a form of death (tawaffā) in the Qur'an, linking the nightly cycle to resurrection.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (haqīqah) for the astronomical night; metaphorical (majāz) for spiritual darkness or heedlessness.
- Root: نوم (Nawm)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Sleep; slumber; a state of rest.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Sleep is "death in a light form" (al-mawt al-khafīf), and death is "sleep in a heavy form" (al-nawm al-thaqīl). Allah says: {«Allah takes the souls at the time of their death, and those that die not during their sleep»} (Q. 39:42).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: bodily rest. Metaphorical: heedlessness (ghaflah) or spiritual inertia; "the market slept" means it stagnated.
- Root: عله (Alaha/Ilah)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To worship; to seek refuge; the root for ilāh (deity) and Allāh (the Supreme Deity).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The root denotes the act of devotion and the object of ultimate veneration; al-ulūhiyyah is the state of being worshipped.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: deity. Metaphorical: that which one is utterly devoted to or enslaved by (e.g., one's desires).
- Root: الي (Alā/Yalū)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To be occupied with; to manage; related to al-ālah (instrument) and ma'ālah (consequence).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The root conveys the idea of returning to a state or being entrusted with a matter; al-ālah is that by which one accomplishes an affair.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: instrumentality. Metaphorical: the means by which one draws near to Allah.
- Sibawayh Rule: Restriction and Focused Predication (al-Ḥaṣr wa al-Taqyīd bi-innamā) — Used to distinguish the specific legal scope of actions (e.g., the witr prayer's status) and to restrict general statements to their precise conditions.
45:17.topic: Al-Ghazali on constant remembrance of God and contemplative invocations, from 'Arrangement of Litanies'

45:21.arabic: الآية ليلة حتى أصبح أم حسب الذين اجترحوا السيئات أن نجعلهم كالذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات الآية وقال المغيرة بن حبيب رمقت مالك بن دينار فتوضأ بعد العشاء ثم قام إلى مصلاه فقبض على لحيته فخنقته العبرة فجعل يقول حرم شيبة مالك على النار إلهي قد علمت ساكن الجنة من ساكن النار فأي الرجلين مالك وأي الدارين دار مالك فلم يزل ذلك قوله حتى طلع الفجر وقال مالك بن دينار شهوت ليلة عن وردي ونمت فإذا أنا في المنام بجارية كأحسن ما يكون وفي يدها رقعة فقالت لي أتحسن تقرأ فقلت نعم فدفعت إلي الرقعة فإذا فيها أألهتك اللذائذ والأماني .
45:21.english: Know — may God guide you — that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "O Abū Hurayrah, if you desire the pleasure of your Lord, pray in the corners of your house, and the light of your house will be in the heaven like the light of the stars and the planets in the sight of the people of the earth." (7)
45:21.section_title_en: Section 273 — The Virtues of Night Prayer (Qiyām al-Layl) and the Narrations Concerning the Devotions of the Righteous
45:21.anchors:
- Root: ليل (Layl)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Night; the period of darkness from sunset to dawn; its plural forms include ليالٍ and ليائل
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Night is contrasted with day as a sign of divine order; "قيام الليل" (night vigil) is the specific act of standing in prayer during the night hours
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — the night-time period; Metaphorical — "أصبح" as awakening from heedlessness, used for spiritual awakening
- Root: صبح (Ṣubḥ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Dawn, morning; the time when the horizon reddens with the sun's approach
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الصبح والصباح، أول النهار" — the first part of the day; "أسحرنا" (has dawn approached?) is the question asked to determine the end of the night vigil
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — daybreak; Metaphorical — "أصبح يا رجل: انتبه من غفلتك" (awaken from your heedlessness), used for spiritual alertness
- Root: حتي (Ḥattā)
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): A preposition of termination — "until"; used to mark the endpoint of the night vigil at dawn
  * Sibawayh Rule: When ḥattā governs the subjunctive, it means "until such time as"; when followed by the indicative, it denotes a resulting state or concurrent circumstance
- Root: عله (ʿAlaha)
  * Lisan al-Arab: To be occupied with something; to be diverted from one's appointed task — as in the one who sleeps past his nightly devotion (wird)
45:21.topic: Al-Ghazali on the journey of the soul, death, and the Hereafter, from 'Arrangement of Litanies'

45:21.arabic: ليلة بهذه الآية {أم حسب الذين اجترحوا السيئات} الآية وقام سعيد بن جبير ليلة يردد هذه الآية وامتازوا اليوم أيها المجرمون وقال بعضهم إني لأفتتح السورة فيوقفني بعض ما أشهد فيها عن الفراغ منها حتى يطلع الفجر وكان بعضهم يقول آية لا أتفهمها ولا يكون قلبي فيها لا أعد لها ثوابا وحكي عن أبي سليمان الداراني أنه قال إني لأتلو الآية فأقيم فيها أربع ليال أو خمس ليال ولولا أني أقطع الفكر فيها ما جاوزتها إلى غيرها وعن بعض السلف أنه بقي في سورة هود ستة أشهر يكررها ولا يفرغ من التدبر فيها وقال بعض العار
45:21.english: Ali, may God be pleased with him, said: "There is no good in worship that lacks understanding (fiqh), nor in recitation that lacks reflection."
45:21.section_title_en: The Third Book on the Inward Acts During Recitation — Ten in Number
45:21.anchors:
- Root: دبر (d-b-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The rear, the back part; what comes after; to turn one's back; the end or sequel of a thing.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): That which is opposite of "front" (qabal); used metaphorically for what follows or comes after; "adbar al-nahar" — the latter part of the day; "adbar al-sujud" — the concluding portions of prayers.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the back or hind part. Metaphorical: what comes at the end, the sequel, the consequence of an affair.
- Root: قلب (q-l-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To turn over, to overturn, to transform; the heart as that which is constantly turning and fluctuating between states.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The turning and directing of a thing from one face to another; al-taqallub — the constant changing and fluctuation; the heart (qalb) is so named for its perpetual turning about of resolutions and states.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: to turn a thing over from its face. Metaphorical: to ponder, to examine thoroughly, to turn a matter over in the mind — "qallaba al-amr" — he examined the affair from all sides.
- Root: ختم (kh-t-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To seal, to stamp, to imprint; the seal or stamp itself.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Sealing and stamping — used both for the act of impressing and the impression left; metaphorically employed for securing a thing and preventing access to it, as in {«ختم الله على قلوبهم»} (God sealed their hearts).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: placing a seal upon something. Metaphorical: to conclude, to finish, to bring to an end — "khatama al-Qur'an" — he completed the recitation of the Quran.
- Root: بقي (b-q-y)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To remain, to endure, to persist; the lasting and continuing of a thing.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The persistence of a thing upon its original state; that which remains (al-baqi) is of two kinds: that which remains by itself without limit — and that is the Creator, may He be exalted — and that which remains by another, which is everything other than Him.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: to remain, to stay. Metaphorical: "baqiya al-shay'" — the enduring of a thing; "ma baqiyat minhum baqiyah" — not one of them remained.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — When the construction "innama" is employed, it restricts the predicate to the subject alone, excluding all else. This is pertinent here as the author delimits the inward acts of recitation to precisely ten, no more and no less.
45:21.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Etiquette of Quran Recitation'

50:39.arabic: بحمد ربك قبل طلوع الشمس وقبل الغروب ومن الليل فسبحه وأدبار السجود} وقال سبحانه {وسبح بحمد ربك حين تقوم ومن الليل فسبحه وإدبار النجوم} وقال تعالى {إن ناشئة الليل هي أشد وطأ وأقوم قيلا} وقال تعالى {ومن آناء الليل فسبح وأطراف النهار لعلك ترضى} وقال عز وجل {وأقم الصلاة طرفي النهار وزلفا من الليل أن الحسنات يذهبن السيئات} ثم انظر كيف وصف الفائزين من عباده وبماذا وصفهم فقال تعالى {أم من هو قانت}
50:39.english: This is what has been unveiled to those who gaze with the light of inner vision. But if you are not among its people, then look to the address of God Most High to His Messenger and derive it by the light of faith. For God Most High said to the nearest of His servants to Him and the highest of them in rank before Him: {«Indeed, for you in the day is prolonged occupation and [in the night] long travail. And remember the name of your Lord and devote yourself to Him with [complete] devotion»} (73:7-8). And He said Most High: {«And remember the name of your Lord [in prayer] morning and evening. And from [part of] the night, prostrate to Him and exalt Him a long [part of the] night»} (76:25-26). And He said Most High: {«And exalt [Allah] with praise of your Lord before the rising of the sun and before its setting, and during periods of the night [exalt Him] and after the [performance of] prostrations»} (50:39-40). And He said, Glorified be He: {«And exalt [Allah] with praise of your Lord when you arise. And during part of the night exalt Him and after the stars»} (52:48-49). And He said Most High: {«Indeed, the rising by night is more potent for directing the soul and more suitable for the recitation [of the Qur'an]»} (73:6). And He said Most High: {«And from [part of] the night, exalt Him and after the setting of the stars»} (52:49). And He said Most High: {«And during parts of the night, exalt Him and at the ends of the day, that you may be satisfied»} (20:130). And He said, Mighty and Majestic: {«And establish prayer at the two ends of the day and at the approach of the night. Indeed, good deeds do away with misdeeds»} (11:114).
50:39.section_title_en: The Virtue of the Liturgies of Remembrance (Awrād) and the Elucidation That Perseverance Upon Them Is the Path to God Most High
50:39.anchors:
- Root: ورد (w-r-d)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The root denotes arriving at water, approaching a watering-place; the awrād (pl. of wird) are the appointed portions of devotional recitation assigned to fixed times, as one approaches the fountain of divine mercy.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The wird is the allocated share of worship apportioned to a specific hour; its theological nuance is the systematic distribution of remembrance (dhikr) and reflection (fikr) across the昼夜 cycle to combat the soul's innate restlessness.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the portion of water one drinks. Metaphorical: the fixed liturgical portion one "drinks" from the fountain of gnosis—the shift from physical quenching to spiritual saturation.
- Root: لطف (l-ṭ-f)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Gentleness, subtlety, graciousness; to treat with kindness and refinement.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The divine subtlety (al-luṭf) by which God gently draws His servant; here, the soul's need for gentle management (talṭīf) through variety in worship, lest it weary.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical gentleness of touch. Metaphorical: the strategic, compassionate variation of devotional acts to sustain the soul's momentum—a haqīqah of spiritual governance.
- Root: سأم (s-'-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Weariness, boredom, satiety that breeds aversion; the soul's constitutional fatigue with a single monotonous mode.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The psychological impediment to perseverance; overcome only by the divine mercy of variety, as the Prophet said: «إن الله لا يمل حتى تملوا» — God does not weary, but He has ordained that you may.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the nausea of over-satiation. Metaphorical: the spiritual listlessness that overtakes the heart when devotion becomes mechanical—requiring the "turn" (tanqul) between genres of worship.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب التنويع والتقسيم (The Chapter of Division and Distribution) — The periodic structure here distributes predicates across multiple conditional clauses (fa-in... fa-in...), each governing a distinct outcome, requiring the translator to preserve the balanced, correlative syntax of proportional reward.
50:39.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications, prayers, and their spiritual power, from 'Arrangement of Litanies'

51:17.arabic: خوفا وطمعا} وقال عز وجل {والذين يبيتون لربهم سجدا وقياما} وقال عز وجل {كانوا قليلا من الليل ما يهجعون وبالأسحار هم يستغفرون} وقال عز وجل {فسبحان الله حين تمسون وحين تصبحون} وقال تعالى {ولا تطرد الذين يدعون ربهم بالغداة والعشي يريدون وجهه} فهذا كله يبين لك أن الطريق إلى تعالى مراقبة الأوقات وعمارتها بالأوراد على سبيل الدوام ولذلك قال صلى الله عليه وسلم أحب عباد الله إلى الله الذين يراعون الشمس والقمر والأظلة لذكر الله تعالى (1) وقد قال تعالى {الشمس والقمر بحسبان} وقال تعالى {ألم تر إلى ربك كيف مد الظل ولو شاء لجعله ساكنا ثم جعلنا الشمس عليه دليلا ثم قبضناه إلينا قب
51:17.english: {«آناء الليل ساجدا وقائما يحذر الآخرة ويرجو رحمة ربه قل هل يستوي الذين يعلمون والذين لا يعلمون»} — "During the hours of the night, prostrating and standing, fearing the Hereafter and hoping for the mercy of his Lord. Say: Are those who know equal to those who do not know?" (Q. 39:9). And God Most High said: {«تتجافى جنوبهم عن المضاجع يدعون ربهم خوفا وطمعا»} — "Their sides forsake their beds, calling upon their Lord in fear and hope" (Q. 32:16). And God, Mighty and Majestic, said: {«والذين يبيتون لربهم سجدا وقياما»} — "And those who pass the night prostrating and standing before their Lord" (Q. 25:64). And God, Mighty and Majestic, said: {«كانوا قليلا من الليل ما يهجعون وبالأسحار هم يستغفرون»} — "They used to sleep but little of the night, and in the dawn-hours they would seek forgiveness" (Q. 51:17-18). And God, Mighty and Majestic, said: {«فسبحان الله حين تمسون وحين تصبحون»} — "So glory be to God when you enter the evening and when you enter the morning" (Q. 30:17). And God Most High said: {«ولا تطرد الذين يدعون ربهم بالغداة والعشي يريدون وجهه»} — "And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord morning and evening, desiring His Face" (Q. 6:52). All of this makes clear to you that the path to God Most High is the watchfulness over the times (murāqabat al-awqāt) and the cultivation of them with the appointed devotions (al-awrād) in a perpetual manner.
51:17.section_title_en: The Revival of the Religious Sciences — Section 258: The Virtues of the Watches (Awrād) and Their Ordering
51:17.anchors:
- Root: ورد (w-r-d)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning is "to arrive at water" — the quenching of thirst at a watering place; al-Wird (pl. Awrād) denotes a set portion or appointed round of devotional recitation, by extension from the regular "arrival" at a source.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-Wurūd is originally "the intending of water," then used for other things. The theological nuance: the awrād are the appointed "watering places" of the soul — fixed times at which the servant presents himself before God to drink from the fountain of remembrance (dhikr).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): "warda al-mā'a" — to arrive at water. Metaphorical (Majāz): "warada ʿalayhi amrun lam yuṭiqhu" — an affair he could not bear arrived upon him; "waradat-hu al-ḥummā" — fever came upon him. Here, the awrād are the appointed times that "come upon" the servant, demanding their due of devotion.
- Root: طلع (ṭ-l-ʿ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To rise, to appear above the horizon (of the sun); to ascend; to come upon suddenly.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Ṭalaʿa al-shams ṭulūʿan wa-maṭlaʿan" — the sun rose. From this is borrowed: "ṭalaʿa ʿalaynā fulān" — so-and-so came upon us. The maṭlaʿ is the place of rising.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "ṭalaʿat al-shams" — the sun rose. Metaphorical: "ṭalaʿa ʿalaynā fulān" — he descended upon us suddenly. The "rising of the sun" is the boundary-marker of the first watch.
- Root: ليل (l-y-l)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The night — from the time of sunset to sunrise; its root suggests "enveloping" and "concealing."
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The night (al-layl) and the day (al-nahār) are two signs (āyatān) of God; the night is for stillness and the day for seeking provision.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the period of darkness. Metaphorical: "layl al-hamm" — the night of anxiety (a dark affair). The night is divided into watches for the one who stands in prayer.
- Sibawayh Rule: Bāb al-ḥaṣr wa-al-taqyīd bi-innamā (Restriction and Focused Predication) — The particle innamā restricts the predicate to the subject alone, negating all else. Applied here: "the purpose of the sun and moon's course is not for worldly matters, but only (innamā) for knowing the measures of the times."
51:17.topic: Al-Ghazali on constant remembrance of God and contemplative invocations, from 'Arrangement of Litanies'

52:49.arabic: سبحانه {وسبح بحمد ربك حين تقوم ومن الليل فسبحه وإدبار النجوم} وقال تعالى {إن ناشئة الليل هي أشد وطأ وأقوم قيلا} وقال تعالى {ومن آناء الليل فسبح وأطراف النهار لعلك ترضى} وقال عز وجل {وأقم الصلاة طرفي النهار وزلفا من الليل أن الحسنات يذهبن السيئات} ثم انظر كيف وصف الفائزين من عباده وبماذا وصفهم فقال تعالى {أم من هو قانت}
52:49.english: This is what has been unveiled to those who gaze with the light of inner vision. But if you are not among its people, then look to the address of God Most High to His Messenger and derive it by the light of faith. For God Most High said to the nearest of His servants to Him and the highest of them in rank before Him: {«Indeed, for you in the day is prolonged occupation and [in the night] long travail. And remember the name of your Lord and devote yourself to Him with [complete] devotion»} (73:7-8). And He said Most High: {«And remember the name of your Lord [in prayer] morning and evening. And from [part of] the night, prostrate to Him and exalt Him a long [part of the] night»} (76:25-26). And He said Most High: {«And exalt [Allah] with praise of your Lord before the rising of the sun and before its setting, and during periods of the night [exalt Him] and after the [performance of] prostrations»} (50:39-40). And He said, Glorified be He: {«And exalt [Allah] with praise of your Lord when you arise. And during part of the night exalt Him and after the stars»} (52:48-49). And He said Most High: {«Indeed, the rising by night is more potent for directing the soul and more suitable for the recitation [of the Qur'an]»} (73:6). And He said Most High: {«And from [part of] the night, exalt Him and after the setting of the stars»} (52:49). And He said Most High: {«And during parts of the night, exalt Him and at the ends of the day, that you may be satisfied»} (20:130). And He said, Mighty and Majestic: {«And establish prayer at the two ends of the day and at the approach of the night. Indeed, good deeds do away with misdeeds»} (11:114).
52:49.section_title_en: The Virtue of the Liturgies of Remembrance (Awrād) and the Elucidation That Perseverance Upon Them Is the Path to God Most High
52:49.anchors:
- Root: ورد (w-r-d)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The root denotes arriving at water, approaching a watering-place; the awrād (pl. of wird) are the appointed portions of devotional recitation assigned to fixed times, as one approaches the fountain of divine mercy.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The wird is the allocated share of worship apportioned to a specific hour; its theological nuance is the systematic distribution of remembrance (dhikr) and reflection (fikr) across the昼夜 cycle to combat the soul's innate restlessness.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the portion of water one drinks. Metaphorical: the fixed liturgical portion one "drinks" from the fountain of gnosis—the shift from physical quenching to spiritual saturation.
- Root: لطف (l-ṭ-f)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Gentleness, subtlety, graciousness; to treat with kindness and refinement.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The divine subtlety (al-luṭf) by which God gently draws His servant; here, the soul's need for gentle management (talṭīf) through variety in worship, lest it weary.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical gentleness of touch. Metaphorical: the strategic, compassionate variation of devotional acts to sustain the soul's momentum—a haqīqah of spiritual governance.
- Root: سأم (s-'-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Weariness, boredom, satiety that breeds aversion; the soul's constitutional fatigue with a single monotonous mode.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The psychological impediment to perseverance; overcome only by the divine mercy of variety, as the Prophet said: «إن الله لا يمل حتى تملوا» — God does not weary, but He has ordained that you may.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the nausea of over-satiation. Metaphorical: the spiritual listlessness that overtakes the heart when devotion becomes mechanical—requiring the "turn" (tanqul) between genres of worship.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب التنويع والتقسيم (The Chapter of Division and Distribution) — The periodic structure here distributes predicates across multiple conditional clauses (fa-in... fa-in...), each governing a distinct outcome, requiring the translator to preserve the balanced, correlative syntax of proportional reward.
52:49.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications, prayers, and their spiritual power, from 'Arrangement of Litanies'

53:31.arabic: يقول ليجزى الذي أساءوا بما عملوا ويجزى الذي أحسنوا بالحسنى وقال تعالى {ووضع الكتاب فترى المجرمين مشفقين مما فيه} الآية جعلنا الله وإياكم عاملين بكتابة متبعين لأوليائه حتى يحلنا وإياكم دار المقامة من فضله إنه حميد مجيد وقال بعض الحكماء الأيام سهام والناس أغراض والدهر يرميك كل يوم بسهامه ويخترمك بلياليه وأيامه حتى يستغرق جميع أجزائك فكيف بقاء سلامتك مع وقوع الأيام بك وسرعة الليالي في بدنك لو كشف لك عما أحدثت الأيام فيك من النقص لاستوحشت من كل يوم يأتي عليك واستثقلت ممر الساعة بك ولكن تدبير الله فوق تدبير ا
53:31.english: And indeed there has come the narration from him, from his Lord, Mighty and Glorious, that He said to Moses, peace be upon him: "When you see the rich man approaching, say: 'A sin whose punishment has been hastened.' And when you see the poor man approaching, say: 'Welcome to the badge of the righteous.'" And if you wish, you may follow the possessor of the Spirit and the Word, Jesus son of Mary, peace be upon him — for he used to say: "My condiment is hunger, my badge is fear, my garment is wool, my warmth in winter is the rising places of the sun, my lamp is the moon, my mount is my two feet, and my food and my fruit is what the earth brings forth. I pass the night and I possess nothing, and I rise in the morning and I possess nothing — and there is no one upon the earth richer than I."
53:31.section_title_en: The Revival of the Religious Sciences — Section 737: On the Censure of This World and the Description of Its Perils
53:31.anchors:
- Root: دنو (danuww)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "دنا فهو دانٍ" — proximity, nearness; the world (al-dunyā) is so named because it is nearer and lower, deferred from the Hereafter.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الدنو: القرب بالذات، أو بالحكم" — proximity by essence or by decree; used of place, time, and station. The "nearer" (al-adnā) is contrasted with the greater and the better.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical nearness. Metaphorical: the lower, contemptible station — "أهل الدناءة هم أهل الشناءة" (the people of baseness are the people of abhorrence).
- Root: يوم (yawm)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "اليوم" — a day; also any period of time.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "اليوم يعبر به عن وقت طلوع الشمس إلى غروبها. وقد يعبر به عن مدة من الزمان أي مدة كانت" — the day is the time from sunrise to sunset, or any duration whatsoever. "وذكرهم بأيام الله" — the days of God are His mighty deeds and calamities upon the disbelievers.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the solar day. Metaphorical: "أيام العرب" — their battles and vicissitudes; "أيام الله" — His punitive visitations.
- Root: وقد (waqada)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "وقدت النار تقد وقودا ووقدا" — the fire blazed; al-wuqūd is the fuel.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "وقودها الناس والحجارة" — the fuel of the Fire is men and stones; the one who kindles it for himself (istawqada) is he who seeks its light.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: kindling a fire. Metaphorical: "قلب وقاد" — a blazing, keen heart; "وقد الحصى" — the pebbles became scorching hot (i.e., the intensity of the sun's heat).
- Root: ألك (alaka)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "المألكة: الرسالة، لأنها تؤلك في الفم" — the message (risālah) is called ma'lakah because it is chewed/worked in the mouth.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الملائكة تقع على الواحد والجمع" — angels (malā'ikah) are so named as bearers of messages; "الله يصطفي من الملائكة رسلا" {«الله يصطفي من الملائكة رسلا»} — God chooses messengers from the angels.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: chewing (as a horse chews its bit). Metaphorical: delivering a message — the angel is the one who delivers the divine communication.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — "إنما" restricts the predicate to the subject alone, negating it of all else. Applied in the sermon: "إنما يتزين لي أوليائي بالذل والخوف" — My friends adorn themselves for Me ONLY with humility, fear, and submission — restricting their adornment to these alone, excluding all worldly ornament.
53:31.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Condemnation of the World'

53:31.arabic: قوله لله ما في السموات وما في الأرض إلى آخرها وقل هو الله أحد خمس عشرة مرة (3) وصف من ثوابه في الحديث ما يخرج عن الحصر وقال كرز بن وبرة وهو من الأبدال قلت للخضر عليه السلام علمني شيئا أعمله في كل ليلة فقال إذا صليت المغرب فقم إلى وقت صلاة العشاء مصليا من غير أن تكلم أحدا وأقبل على صلاتك التي أنت فيها وسلم من كل ركعتين واقرأ في كل ركعة فاتحة الكتاب مرة وقل هو الله أحد ثلاثا فإن فرغت من صلاتك انصرف إلى منزلك ولا تكلم أحدا وصل ركعتين واقرأ فاتحة الكتاب وقل هو الله أحد سبع مرات في كل ر
53:31.english: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him) said — according to what ʿĀ'ishah (may God be pleased with her) narrated: "Verily, the most excellent of prayers in the sight of God is the Maghrib prayer. He has not exempted from it either the traveler or the resident. By it He opened the prayer of the night, and by it He sealed the prayer of the day. Whoever prays the Maghrib and prays after it two units (rakʿatayn), God will build for him a palace (qaṣr) in Paradise."
53:31.section_title_en: The Book of the Revival of the Religious Sciences — Section 271: On the Virtue of the Maghrib Prayer and the Facilitating Causes for the Night Vigil (Qiyām al-Layl)
53:31.anchors:
- Root: غرب (gh-r-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of disappearance, setting, and the west; al-ghurāb is the setting of the sun.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الغرب: غيبوبة الشمس" — the occultation of the sun; the Maghrib prayer is named for its time, marking the transition from the day's light into the night's dominion.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah) usage denotes the sun's setting; metaphorically (Majaz), it signifies a boundary or point of transition — here, the temporal boundary between the daytime prayers and the night vigil.
- Root: رسل (r-s-l)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Sending forth with gentleness and ease; a messenger (rasūl) is one dispatched.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "أصل الرسل: الانبعاث على التؤدة" — the root denotes a measured, deliberate sending forth; from this derives the concept of the prophetic messenger.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "أرسل الله في الأمم رسلا" (God sent messengers to the nations). Metaphorical: "أرسل الله عليهم العذاب" (God loosed chastisement upon them) — here, the ḥadīth's "أرسل" (in the chain) is literal transmission.
- Root: ركع (r-k-')
  * Lisan / Ayn: Bowing; the physical posture of inclination in prayer.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الركوع: الانحناء" — used literally for the prayer posture and metaphorically for humility and submission before God.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "شيخ راكع: منحن من الكبر" (an old man bowed with age). Metaphorical: "لغبت الإبل حتى ركعت" (camels fatigued until they knelt) — in the ḥadīth, "ركعات" (units of prayer) are named for the bowing that defines them.
- Root: صلا (ṣ-l-w)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The root of prayer (ṣalāh); also linked to the fire of kindling (taṣliyah).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "أصل الصلي الإيقاد بالنار" — the root denotes kindling fire; the ṣalāh is so named for the "burning" of devotion or for the supplication that "kindles" the heart toward God.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): The term ṣalāh in the Sacred Law is a transferred (naql) technical designation for the specific acts of bowing, prostration, and recitation — distinct from its lexical sense of supplication (duʿā').
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The rule governing the permissibility of interposing elements between a preposition and its object, as in "لم يحطها عن مسافر ولا عن مقيم" where the pronominal object (ها) is separated from the second prepositional phrase (عن مقيم) by the conjunction, maintaining grammatical cohesion through parallel structure.
53:31.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'Arrangement of Litanies'

59:21.arabic: تعالى {لو أنزلنا هذا القرآن على جبل لرأيته خاشعا متصدعا من خشية الله} فالوجل والخشوع وجد من قبيل الأحوال وإن لم يكن من قبيل المكاشفات ولكن قد يصير سببا للمكاشفات والتنبيهات ولهذا قال صلى الله عليه وسلم زينوا القرآن بأصواتكم (3) وقال لأبي موسى الأشعري لقد أوتى مزمارا من مزامير آل داود عليه السلام (1) وأما الحكايات الدالة على أن أرباب القلوب ظهر عليهم الوجد عند سماع القرآن فكثيرة فقوله صلى الله عليه وسلم شيبتني هود وأخواتها (2) خبر عن الوجد فإن الشيب يحصل من الحزن والخوف وذلك وجد وروي أن
59:21.english:
**QUAD_ANCHORS:**
- Root: وجد (Wajd)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The root وجد encompasses multiple senses: finding/attaining (إدراك), intense love (الحب الشديد), grief (الحزن), and wealth/sufficiency (الغنى). Al-Khalil notes the range: "الوجد: الحب. والوجد: الحزن. والوجد: الغنى. والوجد: إدراك الشيء"
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الوجد: إدراك الشيء على خلاف ما يطلب" — and in the technical terminology of the Sufis: "ما يصادف القلب من واردات الأحوال" (what the heart encounters of the influxes of spiritual states)
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal sense is finding/attaining; metaphorical extension (majāz) in devotional context: "وجد فلان في العبادة وجدا: إذا أتى بها على وجهها مع حضور القلب"
- Root: طبع (Tabʿ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الطبع: السجية التي جبل عليها الإنسان" — the innate disposition upon which one is created; also "الختم" (sealing)
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الطبع: السجية التي جبل عليها الإنسان" — the original constitution
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Distinguishes "مطبوع" (innate/natural) from "متكلف" (deliberately acquired) — "فلان مطبوع على الكرم، ومتكلف له"
- Root: كلف (Kulfah/Takalluf)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "التكلف: تجشم ما لا يلزمك" — undertaking what is not incumbent upon you with effort and hardship
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "التكلف: تجشم ما ليس من شأنه" — burdening oneself with what is not one's natural concern
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "تكلفت الأمر: تجشمته على مشقة" — deliberate self-imposition of effort
- Root: سمع (Samāʿ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Auditory perception; also what is heard — recitation, song, remembrance
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "السماع عند الصوفية: ما يهيج الوجد من الأصوات الموزونة" — that which stirs ecstatic finding from measured sounds
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "السماع عند القوم: حضور مجلس يهيج الأحوال الشريفة" — attending an assembly that stirs noble spiritual states
- Root: عشق (ʿIshq)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "العشق: فرط الحب" — excessive love; from "العشقة" — a plant that twines around another
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "العشق: فرط الحب، وأصله من عشقة النبات وهي ما التف منه على غيره"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "العشق مجاز في حق الله تعالى" — metaphorical when applied to God
- Root: بكى (Bukāʾ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Weeping, shedding tears
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "البكاء: إجراء الدمع من عين لحزن أو غيره"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "تباكى: تكلف البكاء" — deliberate self-induced weeping
- Root: صعق (Ṣaʿq)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الصعق: الغشي. والصعق: الموت" — swooning/loss of consciousness; death
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الصعق: غشية تعرض من صوت شديد أو هول"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "صعق من هول الأمر: إذا غشي عليه من شدة الخوف"
- Root: خشع (Khushūʿ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الخشوع: الخضوع والتذلل" — humility and submissiveness
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الخشوع: التذلل والخضوع، وقيل: الخشوع في الصوت والبصر، والخضوع في البدن"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "خشعت الأصوات: سكنت. وخشع البصر: انكسر"
- Root: أنس (Uns)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الأنس: نقيض الوحشة" — the opposite of loneliness/estrangement
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الأنس: حضور القلب مع المحبوب" — the heart's presence with the Beloved
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "الأنس بالله: سكون القلب إليه"
- Root: وجل (Wajal)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الوجل: الخوف مع اضطراب القلب" — fear accompanied by cardiac agitation
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الوجل: الخوف مع اضطراب القلب"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "الوجل: أشد من الخوف، فإنه مع اضطراب"
- Root: طمأن (Ṭumaʾnīnah)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الطمأنينة: السكون" — tranquility
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الطمأنينة: سكون القلب بعد اضطراب"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "اطمأن القلب: سكن بعد اضطراب"
- Root: قشعر (Iqshirʿār)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "القشعريرة: تقبض الجلد من الخوف" — contraction of the skin from fear
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الاقشعرار: انقباض الجلد وتقبضه من الخوف"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "اقشعر الجلد من الخوف: إذا تقبض"
- Root: لين (Līn)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "اللين: ضد الخشونة" — softness, opposite of hardness
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "اللين: نقيض الخشونة"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "لان قلبه: إذا سكن وخشع"
- Root: غشي (Ghashy)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الغشي: الإغماء" — loss of consciousness
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الغشية: ما يغشى القلب من شدة الوجد"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "غشي عليه: إذا أغمي عليه من شدة وجد أو خوف"
- Root: زعق (Zaʿq)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الزعق: الصياح الشديد" — violent screaming
  * Al-Raghib (Al-Mufradat): "الزعق: الصياح الشديد"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "زعق: صاح بأعلى صوته"
- Root: أزيز (Azīz)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الأزيز: صوت النار والمرجل" — the sound of fire and boiling pot
  * Al-Raghib (Al-Mufradat): "الأزيز: صوت النار والمرجل ونحوهما"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "أزيز الصدر: صوت يسمع من شدة البكاء والوجد"
- Root: شهق (Shahīq)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الشهيق: رد النفس إلى الداخل بصوت" — drawing breath inward with sound
  * Al-Raghib (Al-Mufradat): "الشهيق: رد النفس إلى الداخل بصوت"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "شهق الرجل: إذا خرجت نفسه بصوت من شدة الوجد"
- Root: حزن (Ḥuzn)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الحزن: ضد السرور" — grief, opposite of joy
  * Al-Raghib (Al-Mufradat): "الحزن: ألم النفس"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "الحزن: ألم النفس، وهو مجاز من حزن الأرض" (metaphorical extension from rough ground)
- Root: شيب (Shayb)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الشيب: بياض الشعر" — whitening of hair
  * Al-Raghib (Al-Mufradat): "الشيب: بياض الشعر"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "شيبتني هود: أي: كبرتني وأحزنتني حتى شاب شعري"
- Root: ذرف (Dharf)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الذرف: سيلان الدمع" — flowing of tears
  * Al-Raghib (Al-Mufradat): "ذرفت العين: سال دمعها"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "ذرفت عينه: إذا سال دمعها من حزن"
- Root: فيض (Fayḍ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الفيض: سيلان الماء" — overflowing of water
  * Al-Raghib (Al-Mufradat): "الفيض: جريان الماء بكثرة"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "فاضت العين بالدمع: سالت. وفاض القلب: امتلأ"
- Root: نقر (Naqr)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "النقر: الضرب على الشيء حتى يصوت" — striking something until it sounds
  * Al-Raghib (Al-Mufradat): "الناقور: الصور" — the Trumpet
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "الناقور: الصور الذي ينفخ فيه إسرافيل"
- Root: رعش (Riʿshah)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الرعدة: الاضطراب" — trembling
  * Al-Raghib (Al-Mufradat): "الارتعداد: الاضطراب"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "ارتعدت فرائصه: اضطربت من شدة الخوف"
- Root: فرص (Farīṣah)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الفريصة: لحمة بين الجنب والكتف ترعد عند الفزع" — the flesh between the side and shoulder blade that trembles at fright
  * Al-Raghib (Al-Mufradat): "الفريصة: لحمة بين الجنب والكتف ترعد عند الفزع"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "ارتعدت فرائصه: من شدة الخوف"
- Root: عما (ʿAmā)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "العمى: ذهاب البصر. والعمى: ذهاب البصيرة" — blindness of sight; blindness of insight
  * Al-Raghib (Al-Mufradat): "العمى: آفة في البصر، وقد يستعار لآفة البصيرة"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "عمي القلب: ذهبت بصيرته"

73:6.arabic: {إن ناشئة الليل هي أشد وطأ وأقوم قيلا} وقال تعالى {ومن آناء الليل فسبح وأطراف النهار لعلك ترضى} وقال عز وجل {وأقم الصلاة طرفي النهار وزلفا من الليل أن الحسنات يذهبن السيئات} ثم انظر كيف وصف الفائزين من عباده وبماذا وصفهم فقال تعالى {أم من هو قانت}
73:6.english: This is what has been unveiled to those who gaze with the light of inner vision. But if you are not among its people, then look to the address of God Most High to His Messenger and derive it by the light of faith. For God Most High said to the nearest of His servants to Him and the highest of them in rank before Him: {«Indeed, for you in the day is prolonged occupation and [in the night] long travail. And remember the name of your Lord and devote yourself to Him with [complete] devotion»} (73:7-8). And He said Most High: {«And remember the name of your Lord [in prayer] morning and evening. And from [part of] the night, prostrate to Him and exalt Him a long [part of the] night»} (76:25-26). And He said Most High: {«And exalt [Allah] with praise of your Lord before the rising of the sun and before its setting, and during periods of the night [exalt Him] and after the [performance of] prostrations»} (50:39-40). And He said, Glorified be He: {«And exalt [Allah] with praise of your Lord when you arise. And during part of the night exalt Him and after the stars»} (52:48-49). And He said Most High: {«Indeed, the rising by night is more potent for directing the soul and more suitable for the recitation [of the Qur'an]»} (73:6). And He said Most High: {«And from [part of] the night, exalt Him and after the setting of the stars»} (52:49). And He said Most High: {«And during parts of the night, exalt Him and at the ends of the day, that you may be satisfied»} (20:130). And He said, Mighty and Majestic: {«And establish prayer at the two ends of the day and at the approach of the night. Indeed, good deeds do away with misdeeds»} (11:114).
