84:6.arabic: لهواه مودع لعمره سائر إلى مولاه كما قال عز وجل {يا أيها الإنسان إنك كادح إلى ربك كدحا فملاقيه} وقال تعالى {واتقوا الله ويعلمكم الله} وقال تعالى {واتقوا الله واعلموا أنكم ملاقوه} وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم من لم تنهه صلاته عن الفحشاء والمنكر لم يزدد من الله إلا بعدا (5) والصلاة مناجاة فكيف تكون مع الغفلة وقال بكر بن عبد الله يا ابن آدم إذاشئت أن تدخل على مولاك بغير إذن وتكلمه بلا ترجمان دخلت قيل وكيف ذلك قال تسبغ وضوءك وتدخل محرابك فإذا أنت قد دخلت على مولاك بغير إذن فتكلمه بغير ترجمان وعن عائشة رضي الله عنها قالت كان رسول الله صلى ا
84:6.english: God—Exalted is He—said: {«And establish prayer for My remembrance»} (Q 20:14). And He—Exalted is He—said: {«And be not among the heedless»} (Q 7:205). And He—Mighty and Majestic—said: {«Do not approach prayer while you are intoxicated until you know what you are saying»} (Q 4:43). It was said: "intoxicated" from the excess of worldly concern (al-hamm), and it was said: from love of this world.
84:6.section_title_en: The Virtue of Humble Devotion (Khusḥūʿ) in Prayer
84:6.anchors:
- Root: خشع (Khashaʿa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الخشوع: التواضع والسكون، وخشع بصره: غضه وأطرقه، وخشعت الأصوات: سكنت وخفضت"
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الخشوع: الضراعة والاستكانة، وأصله الانخفاض والتطامن، ويقال للصوت الخفيض والطرف المنكسر"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "Literal: خشع الرجل: خفض رأسه وتواضع. Metaphorical: خشع القلب: خضع وذل وسكن لله"
- Root: سكر (Sukr)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "السكر: نقيض الصحو، والسكران: الذي غطى عقله، وكل شيء غطى فقد سكر"
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "السكر: حالة تعرض بين العقل وبين إدراكه، ويستعار لما يغطي العقل من الهم وحب الدنيا"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "Literal: سكر من الشراب. Metaphorical: سكر الهم وحب الدنيا — ما يغطي العقل عن إدراك المقام"
- Root: ندم (Nadama)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الندم: التحسر على ما فات، والندامة: التوبة، والنادم: المتحسر"
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الندم: انكسار النفس لما فرط، وهو من لوازم التوبة"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "Literal: ندم على الشيء: تحسر. Metaphorical: تنادم في الصلاة: استحضار التقصير والانكسار بين يدي الله"
- Root: وجب (Wajaba)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "وجب القلب: اضطرب وخفق، ووجب الشيء: ثبت ولزم، والوجيب: صوت خفقان القلب"
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الوجيب: اضطراب القلب من هيبة الأمر وعظمته"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "Literal: وجب الباب: أغلقه. Metaphorical: وجيب القلب: خفقانه من الخوف والهيبة"
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — "إنما الصلاة تمسكن" restricts prayer's essence to humility, excluding distraction and heedlessness.
84:6.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications, prayers, and their spiritual power, from 'Mysteries of Prayer'

97:1.arabic: ركعة يفصل بين كل ركعتين بتسليمة يقرأ في كل ركعة بفاتحة الكتاب مرة وإنا أنزلناه في ليلة القدر ثلاث مرات وقل هو الله أحد اثنتي عشرة مرة فإذا فرغ من صلاته صلى علي سبعين مرة يقول اللهم صل على محمد النبي الأمي وعلى آله ثم يسجد ويقول في سجوده سبعين مرة سبوح قدوس رب الملائكة والروح ثم يرفع رأسه ويقول سبعين مرة رب اغفر وارحم وتجاوز عما تعلم إنك أنت الأعز الأكرم ثم يسجد سجدة أخرى ويقول فيها مثل ما قال في السجدة الأولى ثم يسأل حاجته في سجوده فإنها تقضى (4) قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لا يصلي أحد هذه الصلاة إلا غفر الله تعالى له
97:1.english: **The First:** The takbīr (declaration of Allah's Greatness). Its beginning is established by the saying of Allah, the Exalted: {«وَتُكْمِلُوا الْعِدَّةَ وَلِتُكَبِّرُوا اللَّهَ عَلَى مَا هَدَاكُمْ»} ("And that you complete the number and magnify Allah for having guided you") {Al-Baqarah: 185}. Its form is that one says: "Allāhu akbar, Allāhu akbar, lā ilāha illā Allāhu wa-Allāhu akbar, Allāhu akbar wa-li-Llāhi al-ḥamd" (Allah is Greater, Allah is Greater, there is no deity except Allah, and Allah is Greater, Allah is Greater, and to Allah belongs all praise). And it is said: "Allāhu akbar kabīran, wa-al-ḥamdu li-Llāhi kathīran, wa-subḥāna Allāhi bukratan wa-aṣīlā, lā ilāha illā Allāhu waḥdahu lā sharīka lah, mukhlisīna lahu al-dīn wa-law kariha al-kāfirūn" (Allah is Greater, abundantly great, and praise be to Allah, abundantly much, and glory be to Allah morning and evening. There is no deity except Allah alone, with no partner, sincere to Him in religion, even though the disbelievers detest it). One begins the takbīr on the night of Fiṭr until the commencement of the Eid prayer. In the second Eid (al-Aḍḥā), one begins the takbīr immediately after the dawn prayer on the Day of ʿArafah until the end of the day of the thirteenth [of Dhū al-Ḥijjah]. This is the most complete of the sayings. One pronounces the takbīr after the obligatory prayers and after the supererogatory prayers, though it is more emphatic after the obligatory ones.
97:1.section_title_en: The Book of the Revival of the Religious Sciences — Section on the Two Festivals (Eid), the Supererogatory Prayers of Rajab and Shaʿbān
97:1.anchors:
- Root: كبر (k-b-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of greatness in magnitude, age, or rank; al-takbīr is the utterance "Allāhu akbar" (Allah is Greater).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-kabīr and al-ṣaghīr are relative terms; takbīr in worship signifies declaring Allah's transcendence above all comparison, used in quantity (connected/disconnected) and in dignity.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): "Allāhu akbar" as magnification of Allah's majesty. Metaphorical (majāz): "takabbara" for prideful self-aggrandizement (blameworthy), distinct from the liturgical takbīr.
- Root: صلا (ṣ-l-w)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Root denotes supplication (duʿā'), blessing, and the ritual prayer; al-ṣalāh as worship with bowing and prostration.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-ṣalāh is fundamentally supplication and seeking forgiveness; in the Law it is the specific acts of worship comprising standing, bowing, and prostration, with the heart present in humility.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the prescribed prayer (al-ṣalāh al-maktūbah). Metaphorical: "ṣallā ʿalā" for invoking blessings (on the Prophet), and "muṣallīn" for those who pray or supplicate.
- Root: سجد (s-j-d)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Prostration; placing the forehead on the ground in worship.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-sujūd is fundamentally humility and self-abasement; it is made a term for humbling oneself before Allah in worship — two kinds: voluntary (for humans, deserving reward) and compelled/subjugated (for all creation).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: prostration in prayer. Metaphorical: "sajadat al-safīnah lil-riyāḥ" (the ship yields to the winds), and "ʿayn sājidah" (a languid eye) — indicating submission or stillness.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Restriction and Focused Predication (al-ḥaṣr wa al-taqyīd bi-innamā) — Used in the text's argumentation (e.g., "إنما أوردناها في هذا القسم لأنها تتكرر") to restrict the reason for inclusion, and in preference statements ("والمختار أن الجماعة أفضل") to assert a focused judgment.
97:1.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications, prayers, and their spiritual power, from 'Mysteries of Prayer'

107:5.arabic: الذين هم عن صلاتهم ساهون قال هو الذي يسهو في صلاته فلا يدري على كم ينصرف أعلى شفع أم على وتر وقال الحسن هو الذي يسهو عن وقت الصلاة حتى تخرج وقال بعضهم هو الذي إن صلاها في أول الوقت لم يفرح وإن أخرها عن الوقت لم يحزن فلا يرى تعجيلها خيرا ولا تأخيرا إثما واعلم أن الصلاة قد يحسب بعضها ويكتب بعضها دون بعض كما دلت الأخبار عليه وإن كان الفقيه يقول إن الصلاة في الصحة لا تتجزأ ولكن ذلك له معنى آخر ذكرناه وهذا المعنى دلت عليه الأحاديث إذ ورد جبر نقصان الفرائض بالنوافل (2) وفي ال
107:5.english: One person departed from this world [without ever having been present in prayer], and another was asked: "Do you find yourself thinking of anything of this world during the prayer?" He said: "No — neither in the prayer nor outside of it."
107:5.section_title_en: The Revival of the Religious Sciences — Book of Prayer, Section 142: On the States of the Humble (al-Khāshiʿīn) and the Lightening of Prayer
107:5.anchors:
- Root: صلا (ṣ-l-w)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root denotes the kindling of fire and burning; secondarily, the act of prayer (ṣalāh) as devotional worship.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The root's primary sense is "ignition by fire" (īqād bil-nār); its application to prayer is a transferred usage denoting the "burning" of the soul in devotion and the purification of the heart from heedlessness.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) sense is physical burning; metaphorical (majāz) sense is the spiritual "burning" of the heart in humble devotion before God.
- Root: خشع (kh-sh-ʿ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning is lowliness, submissiveness, and being humbled; applied to the earth as "low-lying" ground.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Al-Khushūʿ is supplication/abasing oneself (al-ḍarāʿah), and it is most frequently used for what appears upon the bodily members, whereas al-ḍarāʿah is most frequently used for what is found in the heart. Therefore it was said: 'When the heart is humble (ḍaraʿa), the bodily members become submissive (khashaʿat).'"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: to be low and submissive. Metaphorical: "an earth that is khāshiʿah" (low-lying, untilled), "voices hushed (khashaʿat al-aṣwāt)" — indicating the outward manifestation of inward humility.
- Root: سها (s-h-w)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning is heedlessness, forgetfulness, and inattention.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Forgetfulness (al-sahw) is the heart's neglect of what it is obligated to attend to; it is the opposite of presence of mind (ḥuḍūr).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: to be heedless of something. Metaphorical: the heart's "absence" from what the tongue and body are engaged in.
- Root: وري (w-r-y)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning is to conceal, to cover; also, to strike fire from a flint (warā al-zand).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "It is said: wāraytu kadhā — I concealed it. And the Prophet (peace be upon him) 'when he intended a raid, he would dissemble with something else (warā bi-ghayrihī)' — that is, he would conceal one matter and manifest another."
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: to cover/conceal. Metaphorical: "your fire-sticks have struck fire (warat zanādī)" — meaning your affair has become manifest and your condition evident.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — The particle innamā restricts the predicate to the subject alone, negating it for all else. This is critical for understanding the ḥadīth: "إنما يكتب للعبد من صلاته ما عقل منها" (Only that part of his prayer which he comprehended is written for the servant) — the restriction here is not on the act of prayer itself but on what is "written" (rewarded) of it, which is exclusively that portion attended to with understanding.
107:5.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications, prayers, and their spiritual power, from 'Mysteries of Prayer'

2:218.arabic: وقد شرح الله الرجاء فقال إن الذين آمنوا والذين هاجروا وجاهدوا في سبيل الله أولئك يرجون رحمة الله يعني أن الرجاء بهم أليق وهذا لأنه ذكر أن ثواب الآخرة أجر وجزاء على الأعمال قال الله تعالى جزاء بما كانوا يعملون وقال تعالى وإنما توفون أجوركم يوم القيامة أفترى أن من استؤجر على إصلاح أوان وشرط له أجرة عليها وكان الشارط كريما يفي بالوعد مهما وعد ولا يخلف بل يزيد فجاء الأجير وكسر الأواني وأفسد جميعها ثم جلس ينتظر الأجر ويزعم أن المستأجر كريم أفيراه العقلاء في انتظاره متمنيا مغرورا أو راجيا وهذا للجهل بالفرق بين الرجاء والغرة قيل للحسن قوم يقولون
2:218.english: I say: God—exalted is He—loves the obedient and hates the disobedient. So just as He does not hate the obedient father because of His hatred for the disobedient son, likewise He does not love the disobedient son because of His love for the obedient father. And if love were to flow from the father to the son, then hatred would likewise be bound to flow. Rather, the truth is: {«ولا تزر وازرة وزر أخرى»} — "And no bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another" {Quran 6:164, 17:15, 35:18, 39:7, 53:38}. And whoever supposes that he will be saved by his father's piety is like one who supposes he will be satiated by his father's eating, quenched by his father's drinking, become a scholar by his father's learning, and reach the Ka'bah and see it by his father's walking.
2:218.section_title_en: The Reality of Hope (Al-Rajā') and the Futility of Reliance on Another's Piety
2:218.anchors:
- Root: و ل د (walada)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Physical begetting and offspring; the father's generative act.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الولد: المولود" — offspring as a created entity; here used metaphorically for spiritual causation.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical birth. Metaphorical: "تولدت العصبية" — something generated or produced from another; Ghazali exploits this to refute the notion that a father's obedience "generates" salvation for the son.
- Root: ر ج و (rajā)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Expectation, hope, longing for a favorable outcome.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Hope tied to legitimate means; not mere wishful thinking (tamannī).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: awaiting rain. Metaphorical: "رجوت فلانا" — to expect from someone; Ghazali contrasts true hope (with action) vs. delusion (ghurūr).
- Root: غ ر ر (gharara)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Deception, heedlessness, being lured by a false appearance.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The state of one who is duped by Satan's plausible speech.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: a risky venture. Metaphorical: "اغتر بفلان" — to be deceived by outward charm while the inner reality is corrupt.
- Root: ك ي س (kays)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Intelligence, shrewdness, prudence.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The wise man who disciplines his soul and acts for the afterlife.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: alertness. Metaphorical: "الكيس من دان نفسه" — the prudent one who holds his soul to account; antonym of "الأحمق" (the fool).
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — "إنما يوفى الصابرون أجرهم بغير حساب" style; Ghazali uses "إنما" to restrict reward to personal action, and "ليس للإنسان إلا ما سعى" as a restrictive negative clause (nafy + illā) to deny any transfer of merit.
2:218.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Fear and Hope'

2:257.arabic: {يخرجهم من الظلمات إلى النور} وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم يا أيها الناس اعقلوا عن ربكم وتواصوا بالعقل تعرفوا ما أمرتم به وما نهيتم عنه واعلموا أنه ينجدكم عند ربكم واعلموا أن العاقل من أطاع الله وإن كان دميم المنظر حقير الخطر دنيء المنزلة رث الهيئة وأن الجاهل من عصى الله تعالى وإن كان جميل المنظر عظيم الخطر شريف المنزلة حسن الهيئة فصيحا نطوقا فالقردة والخنازير أعقل عند الله تعالى ممن عصاه ولا تغتر بتعظيم أهل الدنيا إياهم فإنهم من الخاسرين (2) وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم أول ما خل
2:257.english: The Book of Seclusion ('Uzlah) — its explanation, God Most High willing. For this reason, Yūsuf ibn Asbāṭ wrote to Ḥudhayfah al-Marʿashī: "What is your opinion of one who remains, finding no one with whom to remember God Most High except that he is either sinful, or his remembrance in company is itself an act of disobedience — and that because he finds no one of his own kind?" And indeed he spoke truly, for mixing with people is never free from backbiting (ghībah), or listening to backbiting, or remaining silent upon wrongdoing (munkar). And the best of his states is that he either imparts knowledge or acquires it. Yet were this poor wretch to reflect, and to know that his imparting of knowledge is never free from the taints of ostentation (riyā'), the seeking of followers, and the desire for leadership (ri'āsah), he would know that the one who acquires knowledge from him only seeks to make it an instrument for pursuing the world and a means toward evil — so that the teacher becomes his helper therein, his support and his backer, preparing its causes for him, like one who sells a sword to a highway robber. For knowledge is like the sword: its soundness for good is like the soundness of the sword for warfare. And for this reason, it is not permitted to sell it to one whom one knows, by the indications of his circumstances, intends to use it to aid in cutting off the road.
2:257.section_title_en: The Book of Seclusion ('Uzlah) — Section 65, and The Seventh Book: On the Intellect, Its Nobility, Its Reality, and Its Divisions
2:257.anchors:
- Root: عقل (ʿaql)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The root denotes binding, restraining, and holding back; the intellect is that which restrains the soul from base desires and prevents it from straying.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "العقل يقال للقوة المتهيئة لقبول العلم، ويقال للعلم الذي يستفيده الإنسان بتلك القوة عقل" — The intellect is said of the faculty prepared for the reception of knowledge, and it is also said of the knowledge which man acquires by means of that faculty.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): intellectual apprehension and understanding. Metaphorical (Majaz): "نخلة لا تعقل الإبار" — a palm tree that does not accept pollination, i.e., does not grasp or take in.
- Root: علم (ʿilm)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Knowledge as the mark or sign by which a thing is known; the trace or landmark that guides.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "العلم: إدراك الشيء بحقيقته" — Knowledge is the apprehension of a thing in its true reality; it is of two kinds: apprehension of the essence of a thing, and judgment upon a thing regarding what exists for it or is negated of it.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: certain awareness. Metaphorical: "هو من أعلام العلم الخافقه" — he is among the lofty banners of knowledge; knowledge as a guiding landmark (maʿlam).
- Root: نور (nūr)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Light; the first to set up beacons (manār) on his path in his campaigns to guide his return.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "النور: الضوء المنتشر الذي يعين على الإبصار" — Light is the diffused radiance that aids vision; it is of two kinds: that perceived by the eye of inner insight (baṣīrah) — such as the light of the intellect and the light of the Qur'an — and that perceived by the eye of the head, such as the celestial bodies.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: illumination. Metaphorical: "نور الأمر: بينه" — he illuminated the matter: he made it clear; "وهذا أنور من ذاك: أبين" — this is more luminous than that: more evident.
- Sibawayh Rule: Restriction and Focused Predication (al-ḥaṣr wa al-taqyīd bi-innamā) — governing the exclusive attribution of a predicate to a subject, as in the author's restriction of the scholar's condition to one of two men, and the exclusion of the third.
2:257.topic: Al-Ghazali on constant remembrance of God and contemplative invocations, from 'Condemnation of Delusion'

2:257.arabic: عز وجل {الله ولي الذين آمنوا يخرجهم من الظلمات إلى النور} وفي بعض الأخبار المؤمن أفضل من الكعبة (4) والمؤمن طيب طاهر (1) والمؤمن أكرم على الله تعالى من الملائكة (2) وفي الخبر خلق الله تعالى جهنم من فضل رحمته سوطا يسوق به عباده إلى الجنة (3) وفي خبر آخر يقول الله عز وجل إنما خلقت الخلق ليربحوا علي ولم أخلقهم لأربح عليهم (4) وفي حديث أبي سعيد الخدري عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ما خلق الله تعالى شيئا إلا جعل له ما يغلبه وجعل رحمته تغلب غضبه (5) وفي الخبر المشهور إن الله تعالى كتب على نفسه الرحمة قب
2:257.english: So it was said to him: "And what is in it of hope?" He said: "This world, all of it, is little, and a man's provision from it is little, and his religion is little in comparison to his provision. So look at how God Most High sent down in it the longest verse, to guide His servant to the path of caution in preserving his wealth — so how could He not preserve his religion, which has no substitute for him?"
2:257.section_title_en: The Book of Hope (Kitāb al-Rajā') — Section 1033: The Second Art — Surveying the Verses and Reports Concerning Hope
2:257.anchors:
- Root: وجود (w-j-d)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of "finding" and "existence"; here in the sense of what is present and available.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Existence as that which is found and realized; in theological context, the given order of creation.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) sense of "being found"; metaphorical (majāz) extension to the entirety of created things.
- Root: رجا (r-j-w)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To hope, to expect with desire; the opposite of despair (ya's).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Hope as a theological virtue — the heart's expectation of divine mercy, balanced against fear (khawf).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: expectation of a desired outcome; metaphorical: the soul's reliance on divine generosity.
- Root: غفر (gh-f-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To cover, to shield, to pardon; the root implies veiling the fault.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Divine forgiveness as the covering of sins and the effacing of their consequence.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: covering; metaphorical: God's remission of punishment.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — used to emphasize exclusive attributes of divine mercy and forgiveness.
2:257.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'Fear and Hope'

3:131.arabic: ومن تحتهم ظلل ذلك يخوف الله به عباده وقال تعالى واتقوا النار التي أعدت للكافرين وقال تعالى فأنذرتكم نارا تلظى لا يصلاها إلا الأشقى الذي كذب وتولى وقال عز وجل وإن ربك لذوا مغفرة للناس على ظلمهم ويقال أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لم يزل يسأل في أمته حتى قيل له أما ترضى وقد أنزلت عليك هذه الآية وإن ربك لذو مغفرة للناس ظلمهم (2) وفي تفسير قوله تعالى {ولسوف يعطيك ربك فترضى} قال لا يرضى محمد وواحد من أمته في النار وكان أبو جعفر محمد بن علي يقول أنتم أهل العراق تقولون أرجى آية في كتاب الله عز وجل قوله {قل يا عبادي الذين أسرفوا على أنفسهم لا تقنطوا م
3:131.english: So it was said to him: "And what is in it of hope?" He said: "This world, all of it, is little, and a man's provision from it is little, and his religion is little in comparison to his provision. So look at how God Most High sent down in it the longest verse, to guide His servant to the path of caution in preserving his wealth — so how could He not preserve his religion, which has no substitute for him?"
3:131.section_title_en: The Book of Hope (Kitāb al-Rajā') — Section 1033: The Second Art — Surveying the Verses and Reports Concerning Hope

  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: expectation of a desired outcome; metaphorical: the soul's reliance on divine generosity.

6:30.arabic: وقرئ عند يحيى البكاء {ولو ترى إذ وقفوا على ربهم} فصاح صيحة مكث منها مريضا أربعة أشهر يعاد من أطراف البصرة وقال مالك بن دينار بينما أنا أطوف بالبيت إذا أنا بجويرة متعبدة متعلقة بأستار الكعبة وهي تقول يا رب كم شهوة ذهبت لذاتها وبقيت تبعاتها يا رب أما كان لك أدب وعقوبة إلا النار وتبكى فما زال ذلك مقامها حتى طلع الفجر قال مالك فلما رأيت ذلك وضعت يدي على رأسي صارخا أقول ثكلت مالكا أمه وروي أن الفضيل رؤي يوم عرفة والناس يدعون وهو يبكي بكاء الثكلي المحترقة حتى إذا كادت الشمس تغرب قبض على لحيته ثم رفع
6:30.english: One of them said: "Would that my mother had never given birth to me."
6:30.section_title_en: The States of the Fearful — Accounts of the Companions and Early Saints (Section 1061)
6:30.anchors:
- Root: خوف (kh-w-f)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of dread and apprehension; the heart's agitation before an anticipated harm.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الخوف: توقع مكروه عن أمارة مظنونة، أو معلومة" — fear is the expectation of misfortune based on a probable or certain sign; it is the opposite of security (amn) and pertains to both worldly and otherworldly matters.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): "خفته على مالي خوفا وخيفة" — to fear for something. Metaphorical (Majaz): "تخوفه: تنقصه وأخذ من أطرافه" — fear that consumes one gradually, as in the verse of Zuhayr where the journey "wears away" the camel's hump little by little, as if in dread of it.
- Root: يوم (y-w-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: A measure of time from sunrise to sunset, or any period whatsoever.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "اليوم يعبر به عن وقت طلوع الشمس إلى غروبها. وقد يعبر به عن مدة من الزمان أي مدة كانت" — the Day is a term for any span of time; when added to God (أيام الله), it signifies His mighty acts and visitations upon the nations.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: a single day. Metaphorical: "ذكر في أيام العرب كذا أي في وقائعها" — "days" denotes battles and momentous events; "أيام الله" are His punitive calamities upon the disbelievers.
- Root: حتي (ḥ-t-y)
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): A particle of end-point (ghāyah), signifying the terminal limit of an action or state, as in {ليسجننه حتى حين} and {حتى مطلع الفجر}.
  * Sibawayh Rule: Prepositional and particle interposition (الفصل بين الجار والمجرور) — the particle ḥattā governs what follows as the culminating limit of the preceding narrative, marking the climax of an emotional or physical state (e.g., "until he fell unconscious," "until he died").
- Root: بكى (b-k-y)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Weeping with tears; the physical manifestation of inner anguish.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Weeping is the outward expression of the heart's grief (ḥuzn); in the fearful, it is the release of the soul's dread before God's majesty.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: shedding tears. Metaphorical: "بكاء الثكلي" — the weeping of a bereaved mother, intensified by burning loss, used here to describe the saints' weeping on the Day of Arafah.
6:30.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Fear and Hope'

6:107.arabic: أيضا {لو شاء الله ما أشركنا ولا آباؤنا} فانظر كيف كانوا صادقين في كلامهم وكيف هلكوا بصدقهم فسبحان من إذا شاء أهلك بالصدق وإذا شاء أسعد بالجهل {يضل به كثيرا ويهدي به كثيرا} فهؤلاء لما ظنوا أنهم استخدموا لأجل المساكين والفقراء أو جل الله تعالى ثم قالوا لا حظ لنا في المساكين ولا حظ لله فينا وفي أموالنا سواء أنفقنا أو أمسكنا هلكوا كما هلك الصبي لما ظن أن مقصود الوالد استخدامه لأجل
6:107.english: Likewise, if it were said: "Is oxymel (sikanjabīn) better, or the drink of the water-lily (sharāb al-līnūfar)?" — no unqualified answer could be correct at all. Indeed, if it were said to us: "Is oxymel better, or the absence of yellow bile?" — we would say: the absence of yellow bile, for oxymel is sought for the sake of something else, and that which is sought for its own sake is necessarily better than that which is sought for the sake of another.
6:107.section_title_en: The Superiority of Knowledge Over Action — The Parable of the Physician and the Child
6:107.anchors:
- Root: فضل (faḍl)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Excess or increase beyond what is required; superiority in degree.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الفضل: الزيادة عن الاقتصاد" — excess beyond moderation, divided into praiseworthy (like excess of knowledge) and blameworthy; comparative superiority of one thing over another by genus, species, or merit.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): "فاضلني فلان ففضلته" — to surpass in excellence. Here used comparatively: one act or state exceeds another in rank.
- Root: علم (ʿilm)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Knowledge as the apprehension of a thing's reality; the mark or sign by which something is known.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "العلم: إدراك الشيء بحقيقته" — apprehension of a thing's true reality, whether by direct perception of its essence or by judgment concerning it.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "هو من أعلام العلم الخافقه" — knowledge as a lofty, manifest sign; distinguished from mere action which is its instrument.
- Root: صدق (ṣidq)
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Truthfulness primarily in speech — correspondence of report with reality; may become blameworthy when it leads to ruin, as with the disbelievers who spoke truly about God's independence yet drew false conclusions.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "صدقته الحديث" — truthful in statement. Metaphorical (Majaz): "رجل صادق الحملة" — truthful in resolve. Here: the disbelievers were literally truthful in their words yet destroyed by that very truthfulness.
- Root: هلك (halak)
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Destruction on three levels: loss of something from one's possession, corruption and dissolution, and death. Used here for spiritual ruin through misapplied reasoning.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "وقعوا في المهلكة" — falling into destruction. Metaphorical: "تهالك على الشيء" — intense craving. Here: literal perdition of the soul through false inference.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The conditional structure "فإن قلت... فاعلم" (if you say... then know) governs the entire periodic sentence, requiring the apodosis to resolve the protasis with logical necessity, as in the physician analogy where praise of the medicine does not entail its intrinsic superiority.
6:107.topic: Classical commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya Ulum al-Din, from 'Fear and Hope'

7:99.arabic: واستدراجه فقال فلا يأمن مكر الله إلا القوم الخاسرون وقال تعالى ومكروا مكرا ومكرنا مكرا وهم لا يشعرون وقال عز وجل ومكروا ومكر الله والله خير الماكرين وقال تعالى إنهم يكيدون كيدا وأكيد كيدا فمهل الكافرين أمهلهم رويدا فكما لا يجوز للعبد المهمل أن يستدل بإهمال السيد إياه وتمكينه من النعم على حب السيد بل ينبغي أن يحذر أن يكون ذلك مكرا منه وكيدا مع أن السيد لم يحذره مكر نفسه فبأن يجب ذلك في حق الله تعالى مع تحذيره استدراجه أولى فإذن من أمن مكر الله فهو مغتر ومنشأ هذا الغرور أنه استدل بنعم الدنيا على أنه
7:99.english: As for knowing it by way of authoritative transmission and affirmation (taṣdīq): it is that one believes in the Book of God — exalted is He — and affirms His Messenger. For God — exalted is He — has said: {«أيحسبون أن ما نمدهم به من مال وبنين * نسارع لهم في الخيرات بل لا يشعرون»} — "Do they reckon that what We extend to them of wealth and sons — [that] We hasten for them good things? Nay, but they do not perceive" (Q. 23:55-56). And He said — exalted is He: {«سنستدرجهم من حيث لا يعلمون»} — "We shall draw them on by degrees from whence they do not know" (Q. 7:182). And He said — exalted is He: {«فتحنا عليهم أبواب كل شيء حتى إذا فرحوا بما أوتوا أخذناهم بغتة فإذا هم مبلسون»} — "We opened upon them the gates of everything, until when they rejoiced in what they were given, We seized them suddenly, and behold, they were in despair" (Q. 6:44). And in the interpretation of His saying — exalted is He: {«سنستدرجهم من حيث لا يعلمون»} — it is said: "Whenever they innovated a sin, We innovated for them a blessing, to increase their self-deception." And He said — exalted is He: {«إنما نملي لهم ليزدادوا إثما»} — "We only grant them respite that they may increase in sin" (Q. 3:178). And He said — exalted is He: {«ولا تحسبن الله غافلا عما يعمل الظالمون إنما يؤخرهم ليوم تشخص فيه الأبصار»} — "And do not reckon God heedless of what the wrongdoers do; He only delays them to a Day when eyes will stare fixedly" (Q. 14:42). And [there is] more of that kind which has come in the Book of God — exalted is He — and in the Sunnah of His Messenger. So whoever believes in it is delivered from this self-deception. For the origin of this self-deception is ignorance of God and of His attributes; for whoever knows Him does not feel secure from His stratagem (makr) and is not deceived by such corrupt fancies.
7:99.section_title_en: Section 888 — On the Remedy for Self-Deception (Ghurūr): Recognizing the Signs of Divine Honor (Karāmah) and Humiliation (Hawān)
7:99.anchors:
- Root: غرر (gh-r-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of an outward trace or mark; heedlessness in wakefulness; the blaze on a horse's forehead.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Ghurūr" is delusion stemming from heedlessness — the soul's being overtaken while imagining security, as in {«ما غرك بربك الكريم»} (Q. 82:6). It is the state of one who is deceived by apparent favors while blind to their underlying test.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): heedlessness and exposure to predation, like a gazelle deceived by moonlight. Metaphorical (Majaz): being "deceived by God" (ightirār billāh) — trusting in His mercy while persisting in disobedience.
- Root: لهم (l-h-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Swallowing whole; the gullet.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Ilhām" — God's casting a meaning into the heart (al-raw'), distinct from demonic whispering; the channel of inner vision for the knowers (ʿārifūn).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: to swallow. Metaphorical: the heart's receptive "swallowing" of divine inspiration.
- Root: حدث (ḥ-d-th)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Origination after non-existence; newness.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Ḥudūth" — a thing's coming to be after it was not; "muḥdith" — the originator, exclusively God for substances (jawāhir). "Iḥdāth" — bringing about a novel state or act.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: temporal newness. Metaphorical: "muḥaddath" — one inspired with correct discernment, as if newly spoken-to.
- Root: نعم (n-ʿ-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Softness, ease, well-being; a state of comfort.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Niʿmah" — the good state one inhabits; "naʿīm" — the act of living pleasantly. Blessings are both a test and a sign, per {«وإن تعدوا نعمة الله لا تحصوها»} (Q. 16:18).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: bounty and comfort. Metaphorical: "khafat naʿāmatuhum" — their prosperity vanished; blessings may signal either favor or gradual ruin (istidrāj).
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction and Focused Predication with "innamā")
  * In {«إنما نملي لهم ليزدادوا إثما»} (Q. 3:178) and {«إنما يؤخرهم ليوم تشخص فيه الأبصار»} (Q. 14:42), "innamā" restricts the purpose of divine respite exclusively to increase of sin and deferred reckoning — negating any reading of it as benevolent indulgence.
7:99.topic: Al-Ghazali on purifying the character, moral diseases, and spiritual remedies, from 'Fear and Hope'

7:154.arabic: والعلم والرضوان وهي مجامع مقامات أهل الجنان وقال الله تعالى وهدى ورحمة للذين هم لربهم يرهبون وقال تعالى {إنما يخشى الله من عباده العلماء} وصفهم بالعلم لخشيتهم وقال عز وجل {رضي الله عنهم ورضوا عنه ذلك لمن خشي ربه} وكل ما دل على فضيلة العلم دل على فضيلة الخوف لأن الخوف ثمرة العلم ولذلك جاء في خبر موسى عليه أفضل الصلاة والسلام وأما الخائفون
7:154.english: As for the path of derivation (iqtibās) from the verses and reports, what has been transmitted concerning the virtue of fear is beyond enumeration. And sufficient as an indication of its virtue is that God—may He be exalted—has gathered together for the fearful (khāʾifūn) guidance (hudā), mercy (raḥmah), knowledge (ʿilm), and good pleasure (riḍwān)—and these are the sum total of the stations of the people of Paradise. God—may He be exalted—said: {وهدى ورحمة للذين هم لربهم يرهبون} "And guidance and mercy for those who of their Lord are fearful" [Al-Aʿrāf: 154]. And He—exalted is He—said: {إنما يخشى الله من عباده العلماء} "Only those of His servants who possess knowledge fear God" [Fāṭir: 28]—describing them with knowledge on account of their fear [of Him].
7:154.section_title_en: Exposition of the Virtue of Fear (Khawf) and Encouragement Thereof
7:154.anchors:
- Root: خوف (Khawf)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root denotes trepidation, apprehension, and the state of being overtaken by dread of a feared outcome.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الخوف: توقع مكروه عن أمارة مظنونة، أو معلومة" — the anticipation of something detestable based on a probable or certain indication; it is the direct opposite of amn (security) and applies to both worldly and otherworldly matters.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): "خفته على مالي خوفا وخيفة" — fearing for something. Metaphorical (Majaz): "تخوفه: تنقصه" — to diminish gradually, as fear consumes the soul piecemeal.
- Root: فضل (Fadl)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Excess, superiority, or merit beyond the baseline of sufficiency.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الفضل: الزيادة عن الاقتصاد" — increase beyond moderation; the praiseworthy type is like the surplus of knowledge and forbearance, and it is measured by its end (ghāyah).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "مال فلان فاضل: كثير يفضل عن القوت" — surplus wealth exceeding necessity. The virtue of a thing is gauged by its instrumental efficacy toward a noble goal.
- Root: علم (ʿIlm)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Certain cognition and apprehension of a thing as it truly is.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "العلم: إدراك الشيء بحقيقته" — apprehension of a thing's reality; it is the root from which khawf branches as its fruit.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "ما علمت بخبرك: ما شعرت به" — to have cognizance. The scholars (ʿulamāʾ) are so named for their knowledge, which necessarily engenders fear of God.
- Sibawayh Rule: Restriction and Focused Predication (باب الحصر والتقييد) — governing the exclusive attribution in {إنما يخشى الله من عباده العلماء}, where the predicate restricts fear to the knowledgeable, and the syntactic fronting of "whom they fear" (لربهم يرهبون) emphasizes the object of reverential dread.
7:154.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Fear and Hope'

7:158.arabic: عز وجل فلما نظروا إلى داود عليه السلام نهضوا ليتفرقوا عنه فقال داود إني رسول الله إليكم جئتكم لأبلغكم رسالة ربكم فأقبلوا نحوه وألقوا أسماعهم نحو قوله وألقوا أبصارهم إلى الأرض فقال داود إني رسول الله إليكم يقرئكم السلام ويقول لكم ألا تسألون حاجة ألا تنادوني أسمع صوتكم وكلامكم فإنكم أحبائي وأصفيائي وأوليائي أفرح لفرحكم وأسارع إلى محبتكم وأنظر إليكم في كل ساعة نظر الوالدة الشفيقة الرفيقة قال فجرت الدموع على خدودهم فقال شيخهم سبحانك سبحانك نحن عبيدك وبنو عبيدك فاغفر لنا ما قطع قلوبنا عن ذكرك فيما مضى من أعمارنا وقال الآخر سبحانك سبح
7:158.english: And His saying, Glorified and Exalted is He: {نُورُهُمْ يَسْعَىٰ بَيْنَ أَيْدِيهِمْ وَبِأَيْمَانِهِمْ يَقُولُونَ رَبَّنَا أَتْمِمْ لَنَا نُورَنَا} ["Their light will run before them and on their right hands; they will say, 'Our Lord, perfect for us our light'"] (Q 66:8) — this is susceptible to the meaning that He bestows upon them the perfection of light whenever they had provisioned from the world the origin of light. And it is also susceptible that the intended meaning is the perfection of light in what was not illuminated in this world with an illumination that stands in need of further completion and radiance — so that this is what is meant by its perfection. And His saying, Exalted is He: {انْظُرُونَا نَقْتَبِسْ مِنْ نُورِكُمْ قِيلَ ارْجِعُوا وَرَاءَكُمْ فَالْتَمِسُوا نُورًا} ["Look upon us so we may borrow from your light. It will be said, 'Return behind you and seek light'"] (Q 57:13) — this indicates that the lights must have their origin provisioned in this world, then in the Hereafter they increase in radiance. But as for a light being newly generated [there without prior origin] — no. And the judgment in this matter is a venture of conjecture, perilous, and there has not been unveiled to us therein anything trustworthy. So we ask God, Exalted is He, to increase us in knowledge and right guidance, and to show us the truth as truth.
7:158.section_title_en: On the Ever-Replenished Delights of the Hereafter and the Yearning (Shawq) for the Divine Vision
7:158.anchors:
- Root: لذذ (Ladhdhah — Pleasure/Delight)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root denotes the sweetness of taste and the experience of sensory gratification; its verbal form (ladhdha) implies direct apprehension of what is agreeable.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In theological usage, true pleasure (al-ladhdhah al-ʿuẓmā) is the soul's perception of what is conformable to its nature — the highest being the vision of God (ru'yat Allāh) and the bliss of proximity to Him.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) for sensory delight; metaphorical (majāz) for intellectual and spiritual joys, where the "taste" is of gnosis (maʿrifah), not of the palate.

- Root: شوق (Shawq — Yearning/Longing)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The root signifies the soul's restless inclination toward a beloved; the "spurring on" of the heart toward reunion.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Shawq is the movement of the heart toward its ultimate Beloved (al-maḥbūb al-aʿlā) — a yearning that persists even in bliss, for the unveiling (kashf) of ever-greater divine self-disclosure.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal for human longing; metaphorical for the divine "yearning" attributed to God (as in the sacred reports), which is an expression of His loving acceptance and bestowal of grace, not an emotional lack.

- Root: نور (Nūr — Light)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root denotes illumination, radiance, and that by which one sees and is seen.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Twofold: sensory light (of the sun, stars) and intellectual/spiritual light (of reason, faith, and the Qur'an). The "light of the believers" on the Day of Resurrection is the latter — the radiance of their faith and works in the world.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal for physical luminosity; metaphorical (majāz) for guidance, clarity, and the illuminating power of divine truth in the heart.

- Root: قلب (Qalb — Heart)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root means to turn over, to flip, to transform — hence the heart is so-named for its constant fluctuation (taqallub) of states.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The heart is the seat of perception and understanding (al-ʿaql wa al-fahm); it is the subtle divine reality (al-laṭīfah al-rabbāniyyah) that apprehends God, not the physical organ.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal for the physical organ; metaphorical for the spiritual faculty of cognition and volition that turns toward or away from God.

- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — Governing the precise scope of statements like "the pleasure of what is renewed is only a distraction from the ache of yearning," ensuring the predicate is confined to the subject without overextension.
7:158.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications, prayers, and their spiritual power, from 'Love, Longing, Intimacy and Contentment'

7:158.arabic: يسمع أدناهم فيقول يا أيها الناس إني قد أنصت لكم مند خلقتكم إلى يومكم هذا فانصتوا إلي اليوم إنما هي أعمالكم ترد عليكم أيها الناس إني قد جعلت نسبا وجعلتم نسبا فوضعتم نسبي ورفعتم نسبكم قلت إن أكرمكم عند الله أتقاكم وأبيتم إلا أن تقولوا فلان بن فلان وفلان أغنى من فلان فاليوم أضع نسبكم وأرفع نسبي أين المتقون فيرفع للقوم لواء فيتبع القوم لواءهم إلى منازلهم فيدخلون الجنة بغير حساب (2) حديث رأس الحكمة مخافة الله رواه أبو بكر بن لال الفقيه في مكارم الأخلاق والبيهقي في الشعب وضعفه من حديث
7:158.english: For they possess the Highest Companion (al-Rafīq al-Aʿlā) in which none share with them. Consider how He singled them out for the companionship of the Highest Companion — and that is because they are the scholars (ʿulamāʾ), and the scholars hold the rank of companionship with the prophets, for they are the heirs of the prophets. And the companionship of the Highest Companion belongs to the prophets and to those who attach themselves to them. For this reason, when the Messenger of God — may God's blessings and peace be upon him — was given the choice during his death-illness between remaining in this world and proceeding to God — may He be exalted — he would say: "I ask of Thee the Highest Companion" {«الرفيق الأعلى»}.
7:158.section_title_en: On the Excellence of Fear (Khawf) and Its Inseparability from Faith — Section 1042
7:158.anchors:
- Root: خوف (Khawf)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root denotes trepidation, apprehension, and the state of being afraid; its opposite is amn (security).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الخوف: توقع مكروه عن أمارة مظنونة، أو معلومة" — anticipation of something disliked based on an indication, whether conjectural or certain; it is the direct opposite of amn (security), and applies to both worldly and otherworldly matters.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): "خفته على مالي خوفا وخيفة" — to fear for something. Metaphorical (Majaz): "تخوفه: تنقصه" — to diminish gradually, as fear erodes the soul's complacency.
- Root: حدث (Hadath)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Newness, origination after non-existence; also that which is recent in time.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الحدوث: كون الشيء بعد أن لم يكن" — the coming-to-be of a thing after it was not; true origination belongs to God alone.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "هو حدث من الأحداث" — one who is recent/young. Metaphorical: "كان عمر محدثا أي صادق الحدس" — one whose intuition is true, as if divinely inspired.
- Root: يوم (Yawm)
  * Lisan / Ayn: A day; a period of time from sunrise to sunset, or any duration whatsoever.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "اليوم يعبر به عن وقت طلوع الشمس إلى غروبها. وقد يعبر به عن مدة من الزمان أي مدة كانت" — used for the day proper or any extended period; "أيام الله" refers to His mighty deeds and visitations upon the wicked.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "ما رأيته اليوم" — temporal designation. Metaphorical: "ذكر في أيام العرب كذا أي في وقائعها" — "days" as battles and momentous events.
- Root: قوي (Quwwa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Strength, power, capability; the opposite of weakness.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "القوة تستعمل تارة في معنى القدرة" — power as capability; also potentiality, as when a date-stone is said to be "potentially" a palm-tree.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "هو قوي مقو" — physically strong. Metaphorical: strength of heart, of conviction, and of allies.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — When the particle innamā is employed, it restricts the predicate exclusively to the subject mentioned, negating it for all others. This governs the author's argument that taqwā is exclusively attributed to God's nearness and that the "Highest Companion" (al-Rafīq al-Aʿlā) is uniquely reserved for the prophets and their heirs.
7:158.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'Fear and Hope'

7:169.arabic: وبمثله أخبر عن النصارى إذ قال تعالى فخلف من بعدهم خلف ورثوا الكتاب يأخذون عرض هذا الأدنى ويقولون سيغفر لنا ومعناه أنهم ورثوا الكتاب أي هم علماء ويأخذون عرض هذا الأدنى أي شهواتهم من الدنيا حراما كان أو حلالا وقد قال تعالى ولمن خاف مقام ربه جنتان ذلك لمن خاف مقامي وخاف وعيد والقرآن من أوله إلى آخره تحذير وتخويف لا يتفكر فيه متفكر إلا ويطول حزنه ويعظم خوفه إن كان مؤمنا بما فيه وترى الناس يهذونه هذا يخرجون الحروف من مخارجها ويتناظرون على خفضها ورفعها ونصبها وكأنهم يقرءون شعرا من أشعار العرب لا يهمهم الالتفات إلى معانيه والعمل بما فيه وهل في العالم غرور يز
7:169.english: For if this matter were attained by wishful longing and reached by idle desire, then what was the meaning of the weeping of those [early believers], their fear, and their grief? We have already expounded the reality of these matters in the Book of Fear and Hope (Kitāb al-Khawf wa al-Rajā'). And the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, said — in what Muʿqil ibn Yasār narrated: "A time will come upon the people in which the Qur'an will wear out in the hearts of men just as garments wear out upon bodies. Their entire affair will be [one of] covetousness with no fear accompanying it. If one of them does good, he says: 'It will be accepted from me'; and if he does evil, he says: 'I will be forgiven.'" // The hadith of Muʿqil ibn Yasār: "A time will come upon the people in which the Qur'an will wear out in the hearts of men..." — This hadith was transmitted by Abu Mansur al-Daylami in Musnad al-Firdaws from Ibn ʿAbbas with similar wording, through a chain containing unknown narrators; I have not seen it from the hadith of Muʿqil.
7:169.section_title_en: The Reality of False Hope (Ghurūr) and Its Distinction from True Hope (Rajā') — Section 891
7:169.anchors:
- Root: غرر (gh-r-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning — an outward trace or mark; heedlessness in wakefulness; the blaze on a horse's forehead.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Ghurūr" is delusion arising from heedlessness — one is "folded upon his heedlessness" (ṭawāhu ʿalā gharrihi), as in {«ما غرك بربك الكريم»} (Q 82:6). It is the state of being deceived by wishful thinking while blind to warning.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): heedlessness/negligence. Metaphorical (Majaz): being deceived by false appearances — e.g., "a day white and blazing" (yawm agharr muḥajjal) for intense heat; the gazelle deceived by moonlight (agharr min ẓaby muqmir) that exposes it to predators.
- Root: خوف (kh-w-f)
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Al-Khawf" is the anticipation of something disliked based on a probable or certain indicator — the opposite of amn (security). It is paired with rajā' (hope) in {«يدعون ربهم خوفا وطمعا»} (Q 32:16).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: fear of loss or harm. Metaphorical: gradual diminishment — "takhawwafa al-sayr" (the journey wore away the camel's hump little by little), as if fearing it.
- Root: وقد (w-q-d)
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Fire blazing with fuel — {«وقودها الناس والحجارة»} (Q 2:24). Used for both the fuel and the flame.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: kindling fire. Metaphorical: "qalb waqqād" (a blazing, penetrating intellect); "waqada al-ḥaṣā" (pebbles becoming scorching hot).
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The permissibility of interposing elements between a governing word and its governed prepositional phrase, provided the intervening clause is complete in itself; here, the periodic structure of Ghazali's condemnation ("فترى الواحد...") suspends the subject across multiple clauses before resolution.

9:82.arabic: لفضيلة الخشية فإن البكاء ثمرة الخشية فقد قال تعالى {فليضحكوا قليلا وليبكوا كثيرا} وقال تعالى {يبكون ويزيدهم خشوعا} وقال عز وجل {أفمن هذا

- Root: حدث (Hadath)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Newness, origination after non-existence; also that which is recent in time.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الحدوث: كون الشيء بعد أن لم يكن" — the coming-to-be of a thing after it was not; true origination belongs to God alone.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "هو حدث من الأحداث" — one who is recent/young. Metaphorical: "كان عمر محدثا أي صادق الحدس" — one whose intuition is true, as if divinely inspired.
- Root: يوم (Yawm)
  * Lisan / Ayn: A day; a period of time from sunrise to sunset, or any duration whatsoever.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "اليوم يعبر به عن وقت طلوع الشمس إلى غروبها. وقد يعبر به عن مدة من الزمان أي مدة كانت" — used for the day proper or any extended period; "أيام الله" refers to His mighty deeds and visitations upon the wicked.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "ما رأيته اليوم" — temporal designation. Metaphorical: "ذكر في أيام العرب كذا أي في وقائعها" — "days" as battles and momentous events.
- Root: قوي (Quwwa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Strength, power, capability; the opposite of weakness.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "القوة تستعمل تارة في معنى القدرة" — power as capability; also potentiality, as when a date-stone is said to be "potentially" a palm-tree.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "هو قوي مقو" — physically strong. Metaphorical: strength of heart, of conviction, and of allies.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — When the particle innamā is employed, it restricts the predicate exclusively to the subject mentioned, negating it for all others. This governs the author's argument that taqwā is exclusively attributed to God's nearness and that the "Highest Companion" (al-Rafīq al-Aʿlā) is uniquely reserved for the prophets and their heirs.
9:82.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'Fear and Hope'

11:119.arabic: مني لأملأن جهنم من الجنة والناس أجمعين وقال تعالى وتمت كلمة ربك لأملأن جهنم الآية فكيف لا يخاف ما حق من القول في الأزل ولا يطمع في تداركه ولو كان الأمر آنفا لكانت الأطماع تمتد إلى حيلة فيه ولكن ليس إلا التسليم فيه واستقراء خفي السابقة من جلي الأسباب الظاهرة على القلب والجوارح فمن يسرت له أسباب الشر وحيل بينه وبين أسباب الخير وأحكمت علاقته من الدنيا فكأنه كشف له على التحقيق سر السابقة التي سبقت له بالشقاوة إذ كل ميسر لما خلق له وإن كانت الخيرات كلها ميسرة والقلب بالكلية عن الدنيا منقطعا وبظاهره وباطنه على الله مقبلا كان
11:119.english: Just as Abraham (peace be upon him), when he was placed in the catapult, said: "God is sufficient for me" {حسبي الله} — and this was among the greatest supplications — he was tested and was confronted by Gabriel in mid-air, who said to him: "Do you have any need?" He replied: "As for you, no." And that was the fulfillment of the very reality of his words: "God is sufficient for me." So God Most High informed us about him, saying: "And Abraham who fulfilled" {وإبراهيم الذي وفى} — that is, fulfilled the requirement of his saying "God is sufficient for me." And in like manner, He informed us about Moses (peace be upon him), where he said: "Indeed, we fear that he may assault us or that he may transgress" {إننا نخاف أن يفرط علينا أو أن يطغى}. He said: "Fear not; indeed, I am with you both; I hear and I see" {لا تخافا إنني معكما أسمع وأرى}. Yet despite this, when the sorcerers cast their sorcery, Moses conceived within himself a fear — because he did not feel secure from the deception (makar) of God, and the matter became obscure to him — until security was renewed for him, and it was said to him: "Fear not; indeed, you are the most exalted" {لا تخف إنك أنت الأعلى}. And when the strength of the Muslims weakened on the Day of Badr, he (peace be upon him) said: "O God, if You destroy this band, there will remain no one on the face of the earth who worships You" — a hadith reported on the Day of Badr: "O God, if You destroy this band, there will remain no one on the face of the earth who worships You," transmitted by al-Bukhari from the hadith of Ibn Abbas with the wording: "O God, if You will, You will not be worshipped after this day" — to the end of the hadith. So Abu Bakr (may God be pleased with him) said: "Leave off your importuning of your Lord, for He will surely fulfill what He has promised you." Thus, the station of al-Siddiq (may God be pleased with him) was the station of trust in God's promise, while the station of the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) was the station of fear of God's deception (makar) — and this latter is more complete, for it issues only from the perfection of knowledge of God's secrets, the hidden aspects of His acts, and the meanings of His attributes, some of whose manifestations are expressed as "deception" (makar). And no human being can stand upon the ultimate reality (kunnah) of God's attributes. Whoever knows the true nature of knowledge — that his knowledge falls short of encompassing the ultimate reality of things — his fear inevitably magnifies. For this reason, the Messiah (peace be upon him), when it was said to him: "Did you say to the people: 'Take me and my mother as two gods besides God?'" replied: "Glory be to You! It was not mine to say what I had no right to say. If I had said it, You would have known it. You know what is in my self, and I do not know what is in Your Self" {سبحانك ما يكون لي أن أقول ما ليس لي بحق إن كنت قلته فقد علمته تعلم ما في نفسي ولا أعلم ما في نفسك}. And he said: "If You punish them, indeed they are Your servants; and if You forgive them..." {إن تعذبهم فإنهم عبادك وإن تغفر لهم} — to the end of the verse. So he delegated the matter entirely to the divine will (mashī'ah) and removed himself completely from the equation, knowing that he had no say in the affair whatsoever, and that all matters are linked to the divine will in a linkage that exceeds the bounds of rational categories and habitual patterns — such that no judgment can be passed upon them by analogy, nor by conjecture, nor by reckoning (ḥisbān), let alone by verification and certainty. And this is precisely what has rent the hearts of the knowers (ʿārifīn) asunder — for the supreme calamity (al-ṭāmmah al-kubrā) is the linkage of your affair to the will of One who does not care about you: if He destroys you, He has destroyed countless others like you, and He has never ceased in this world to torment them with various kinds of pains and diseases, and to sicken their hearts thereby with disbelief and hypocrisy, and then to perpetuate the punishment upon them for all eternity. Then He informs us about this, saying: "And had We willed, We would have given every soul its guidance, but the word from Me has taken effect: I will surely fill Hell with jinn and people all together" {ولو شئنا لآتينا كل نفس هداها ولكن حق القول مني لأملأن جهنم من الجنة والناس أجمعين}. And He Most High said: "And the word of your Lord has been fulfilled: I will surely fill Hell..." {وتمت كلمة ربك لأملأن جهنم}. So how should one not fear what has been decreed as a word from eternity (al-azal), and not hope for its reversal? Had the matter been recent, then hopes might extend toward some stratagem regarding it — but there is nothing except submission to it, and the discernment of the hidden precedent (al-sābiqah) from the manifest outward causes upon the heart and the bodily members. For whoever is facilitated toward the causes of evil, and is barred from the causes of good, and whose attachment to this world is firmly secured — it is as if the secret of the prior decree that destined him to wretchedness has been unveiled to him with certainty, since "everyone is facilitated toward that for which he was created" {كل ميسر لما خلق له}. And even if all good things were facilitated, and the heart were entirely severed from this world, with its outward and inward aspects turned wholly toward God, this would necessitate a lightening of fear — were continuity in that state to be trusted. But the peril of the final end (khātimah) and the difficulty of steadfastness only fan the flames of fear into greater blaze and prevent them from being extinguished. For how can one feel secure from the change of state, when the believer's heart lies between two fingers of the fingers of the Merciful? And indeed, the heart is more prone to turning than a boiling pot. And the Turner of Hearts (Glory be to Him) has said: "Indeed, the punishment of their Lord is not to be felt secure from" {إن عذاب ربهم غير مأمون}. So the most ignorant of people is the one who feels secure from it, while He proclaims the warning against security. And were God to show kindness to His knowing servants by reviving their hearts with the spirit of hope (rajā'), their hearts would still burn from the fire of fear. Thus, the causes of hope are a mercy for God's elect, and the causes of heedlessness are a mercy upon the common folk of creation in one respect — for were the veil to be lifted, souls would perish and hearts would be torn asunder from the fear of the Turner of Hearts. One of the knowers said: "If fifty were to intervene between me and the One I have known through tawḥīd..."
11:119.section_title_en: The Reality of Fear and the Station of Abraham, Moses, and the Messenger (Peace Be Upon Them) — On the Inescapable Terror of the Divine Decree
11:119.anchors:
- Root: حسب (ḥ-s-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of counting, reckoning, and sufficiency; "ḥasbī Allāh" signifies God as the sufficient reckoner.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance of ḥisāb as divine accounting; "ḥasbī Allāh" is a declaration of total reliance on God's sufficiency, transcending mere numerical count.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) — reckoning by number; Metaphorical (majāz) — trusting in God's sufficiency as an act of spiritual accounting, where the servant counts God as enough against all else.
- Root: خوف (kh-w-f)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of fear, dread, and apprehension of harm.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Khawf is the expectation of a disliked outcome based on a probable or known sign; it opposes amn (security) and applies to both worldly and otherworldly matters.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — fear of loss or harm; Metaphorical — a "fearful path" (ṭarīq khā'if) where danger inheres in the object, and "takhawwuf" as gradual diminishment, implying fear's erosive effect on the soul.
- Root: نفس (n-f-s)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of self, soul, breath; the essence of a thing.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Nafs as the self or essence (dhāt), as in "ta'lamu mā fī nafsī" (You know what is in my self), denoting the innermost reality distinct from the body.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — the soul as animate essence; Metaphorical — "nafs sā'ilah" (flowing blood) as the life-principle, and the soul's hidden movements as the locus of divine knowledge.
- Root: قلب (q-l-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of turning, overturning, and transformation.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Qalb is the turning of a thing from one state to another; the heart is so named for its constant fluctuation (taqallub) between states.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — physical overturning; Metaphorical — the heart's perpetual oscillation, as in the prophetic hadith of the heart between two fingers of the Merciful, and the "turning" of affairs by divine decree.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Interposition and Apposition (al-ʿaṭf wa al-faṣl) — The periodic structure of "fa-kayfa lā yakhāfu..." (How then should one not fear...) employs a rhetorical question governed by an implied causal clause, where the apodosis is suspended across multiple subordinate clauses, requiring the translator to preserve the cumulative force of the argument without breaking the syntactic chain.
11:119.topic: Al-Ghazali on purifying the character, moral diseases, and spiritual remedies, from 'Fear and Hope'

12:13.arabic: لا قال لقولك لأخوته أخاف أن يأكله الذئب وأنتم عنه غافلون لم خفت عليه الذئب ولم ترجني ولم نظرت إلى غفلة أخوته ولم تنظر إلى حفظي له وتدري لم رددته عليك قال لا قال لأنك رجوتني وقلت {عسى الله أن يأتيني بهم جميعا} وبما قلت اذهبو فتحسسوا من يوسف وأخيه ولا تيأسوا وكذلك لما قال يوسف لصاحب الملك {اذكرني عند ربك} قال الله تعالى {فأنساه الشيطان ذكر ربه فلبث في السجن بضع سنين} وأمثال هذه الحكايات لا تنحصر ولم يرد بها القرآن والأخبار ورود الأسمار بل الغرض بها الاعتبار والاستبصار لتعلم أن الأنبياء عليهم السلام لم يتجا
12:13.english: The second type [of narratives that stir the heart toward repentance] concerns the stories of the prophets and the righteous predecessors, and what befell them of calamities by reason of their sins. For this is intensely impactful and manifestly beneficial upon the hearts of creation—such as the state of Adam (peace be upon him) in his disobedience and what he encountered of expulsion from Paradise. It is even narrated that when he ate from the tree, the [heavenly] garments (al-ḥulal) flew off his body and his nakedness became exposed. Then the crown and the diadem felt shame before his face to remain lifted above him, so Gabriel (peace be upon him) came to him, took the crown from his head, and loosened the diadem from his brow. And it was proclaimed from above the Throne: "Descend from My proximity, for none who disobeys Me dwells near Me." He said: Then Adam turned to Eve weeping and said: "This is the first ill-omen of disobedience—it has driven us from the proximity of the Beloved."
12:13.section_title_en: The Second Type: Narratives of the Prophets and Righteous Predecessors Concerning the Calamities That Befell Them Due to Their Sins
12:13.anchors:
- Root: ن ب أ (n-b-')
  * Lisan / Ayn: To inform, to announce with importance; the core sense of conveying news of significant import.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In theological usage, 'naba'' (نبأ) denotes divine communication of unseen realities—here, God's informing of events carrying moral and spiritual weight.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah) for direct announcement; metaphorical (Majaz) when used of the heart being 'informed' through reflection (i'tibar).
- Root: ذ ن ب (dh-n-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The tail of an animal; by extension, that which follows or trails behind—hence, a sin as the consequence that trails a soul.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الذنب في الأصل: الأخذ بذنب الشيء" — sin is fundamentally 'seizing the tail of a thing,' i.e., pursuing a wrongful act that drags one into its wake; used for minor offenses (sagha'ir) of prophets versus major ones (kaba'ir) of others.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the physical tail. Metaphorical: "هو من الأذناب" — one who trails behind; here, the prophets' sins are 'tails'—swiftly punished in this world to spare them the hereafter.
- Root: ع ج ل (ʿ-j-l)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Haste, swiftness; to expedite.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Haste in divine punishment ('uujila bil-'uqubah) signifies mercy for the elect—cleansing them before the afterlife.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: speed of action. Metaphorical: God's 'hastening' of retribution as a mark of honor, contrasted with the respite (imhal) granted to the wretched.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — Applied to "إنما نطيعك إذا أطعنت الله" (We only obey you when you obey God), where 'innama' restricts obedience to a conditional state, and to "إن هذا أمر كان من السماء" where 'inna' provides emphatic predication of divine decree.
12:13.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Fear and Hope'

12:96.arabic: ما أحب أن يجعل حسابي إلى أبوي لأني اعلم أن الله تعالى أرحم بي منهما وقال بعض السلف المؤمن إذا عصى الله تعالى ستره عن أبصار الملائكة كيلا تراه فتشهد عليه وكتب محمد بن صعب إلى أسود بن سالم بخطه إن العبد إذا كان مسرفا فاعلى نفسه فرفع يديه يدعو ويقول يا رب حجبت الملائكة صوته وكذا الثانية والثالثة حتى إذا قال الرابعة يا ربي قاله الله تعالى حتى متى تحجبون عني صوت عبدي قد علم عبدي أنه ليس له رب يغفر له الذنوب غيري أشهدكم إني قد غفرت له وقال إبراهيم بن أدهم رحمة الله عليه خلا لي الط
12:96.english: In the report (khabar): "Were you not to sin, God would create a creation who would sin, and He would forgive them." (1) In another wording: "He would take you away and bring a creation who would sin, and He would forgive them — verily, He is the Forgiving, the Merciful." And in the report: "Were you not to sin, I would fear for you what is worse than sins." It was said: "And what is that?" He said: "Self-amazement (al-ʿujb)." (2)
12:96.section_title_en: The Completion of the Matter — On the Preacher's Gentleness in Employing Reports of Fear and Hope
12:96.anchors:
- Root: لطف (luṭf)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Gentleness, subtlety, kindness in approach; to be gracious and delicate in manner.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Divine gentleness (luṭf) as an attribute of God's subtle providence; here, the preacher's emulation of prophetic gentleness in spiritual counsel.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) — physical softness; metaphorical (majāz) — refinement of speech and manner suited to the spiritual state of the listener.
- Root: رجا (rajā')
  * Lisan / Ayn: Hope, expectation of good; the opposite of despair (ya's).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Hope in God's mercy as a theological virtue balancing fear (khawf); the state of the believer who relies on divine generosity over personal merit.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — anticipation of a future good; metaphorical — the soul's reliance on God's pardon despite sin.
- Root: عجب (ʿajab)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Self-amazement, vanity, wonder at oneself.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Spiritual pride (ʿujb) — a hidden sin worse than overt transgression, as it nullifies deeds.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — astonishment; metaphorical — the heart's complacency in its own obedience, leading to ruin.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد (Restriction and Specification) — The conditional and exceptive structures (law lā... la-khalaqa, illā an yataghammadani) govern the precise scope of divine mercy and human agency.
12:96.topic: Al-Ghazali on the inner and outer dimensions of worship, from 'Fear and Hope'

13:6.arabic: وتولى وقال عز وجل وإن ربك لذوا مغفرة للناس على ظلمهم ويقال أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لم يزل يسأل في أمته حتى قيل له أما ترضى وقد أنزلت عليك هذه الآية وإن ربك لذو مغفرة للناس ظلمهم (2) وفي تفسير قوله تعالى {ولسوف يعطيك ربك فترضى} قال لا يرضى محمد وواحد من أمته في النار وكان أبو جعفر محمد بن علي يقول أنتم أهل العراق تقولون أرجى آية في كتاب الله عز وجل قوله {قل يا عبادي الذين أسرفوا على أنفسهم لا تقنطوا من رحمة الله} الآية ونحن أهل البيت نقول أرجى آية في كتاب الله تعالى قوله تعالى {ولسوف يعطيك ربك فترضى} وأما الأخ
13:6.english: So it was said to him: "And what is in it of hope?" He said: "This world, all of it, is little, and a man's provision from it is little, and his religion is little in comparison to his provision. So look at how God Most High sent down in it the longest verse, to guide His servant to the path of caution in preserving his wealth — so how could He not preserve his religion, which has no substitute for him?"
13:6.section_title_en: The Book of Hope (Kitāb al-Rajā') — Section 1033: The Second Art — Surveying the Verses and Reports Concerning Hope
13:6.anchors:
- Root: وجود (w-j-d)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of "finding" and "existence"; here in the sense of what is present and available.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Existence as that which is found and realized; in theological context, the given order of creation.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) sense of "being found"; metaphorical (majāz) extension to the entirety of created things.
- Root: رجا (r-j-w)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To hope, to expect with desire; the opposite of despair (ya's).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Hope as a theological virtue — the heart's expectation of divine mercy, balanced against fear (khawf).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: expectation of a desired outcome; metaphorical: the soul's reliance on divine generosity.
- Root: غفر (gh-f-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To cover, to shield, to pardon; the root implies veiling the fault.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Divine forgiveness as the covering of sins and the effacing of their consequence.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: covering; metaphorical: God's remission of punishment.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — used to emphasize exclusive attributes of divine mercy and forgiveness.
13:6.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Fear and Hope'

13:6.arabic: هذه الآية وإن ربك لذو مغفرة للناس ظلمهم (2) وفي تفسير قوله تعالى {ولسوف يعطيك ربك فترضى} قال لا يرضى محمد وواحد من أمته في النار وكان أبو جعفر محمد بن علي يقول أنتم أهل العراق تقولون أرجى آية في كتاب الله عز وجل قوله {قل يا عبادي الذين أسرفوا على أنفسهم لا تقنطوا من رحمة الله} الآية ونحن أهل البيت نقول أرجى آية في كتاب الله تعالى قوله تعالى {ولسوف يعطيك ربك فترضى} وأما الأخبار فقد روى أبو موسى عنه صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال أمتي أمة مرحومة لا عذاب عليها في الآخرة عجل الله عقابها في الدنيا الزلازل
13:6.english: So it was said to him: "And what is in it of hope?" He said: "This world, all of it, is little, and a man's provision from it is little, and his religion is little in comparison to his provision. So look at how God Most High sent down in it the longest verse, to guide His servant to the path of caution in preserving his wealth — so how could He not preserve his religion, which has no substitute for him?"
