23:60.arabic: والذي يدل على فضيلة هذه الخصلة قوله تعالى {يؤتون ما آتوا وقلوبهم وجلة أنهم إلى ربهم راجعون} أي أنهم يؤتون الطاعات وهم على وجل عظيم من قبولها وقال تعالى {إن الذين هم من خشية ربهم مشفقون} وقال تعالى {إنا كنا قبل في أهلنا مشفقين} وقد وصف الله تعالى الملائكة عليهم السلام مع تقدسهم عن الذنوب ومواظبتهم على العبادات على الدءوب بالإشفاق فقال تعالى مخبرا عنهم يسبحون الليل والنهار لا يفترون وهم من خشيته مشفقون فمتى زال الإشفاق والحذر مما سبق به القضاء في الأزل وينكشف عند خاتمة الأجل غلب الأمن من مكر الله وذلك يوجب الكبر وه
23:60.english: ...so he gave some of it in charity and fed his family with some of it. He then returned, saying: "This is good, but it is not like devoting oneself entirely to obedience of God." He came again in a dream a second time, and it was said to him: "Go to so-and-so, the cobbler, and say to him: 'What is this yellowness on your face?'" So he went to him and asked him. He replied: "I have not seen anyone among mankind except that it occurred to me that he would be saved — but you, I [saw] that you would perish." The worshiper said: "By this [very sign]..."
23:60.section_title_en: The Cure for Conceit (Kibr): Trials of the Soul and the Path to Humility
23:60.anchors:
- Root: وجل (wajila)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of fear, trepidation, and trembling of the heart.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance of reverential awe before divine majesty, distinct from mere terror; it is the state of the heart that accompanies acts of obedience when mindful of their acceptance.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah) usage denotes inward trembling; metaphorical (Majaz) extension applies to the soul's anxious state regarding its ultimate destiny.
- Root: شفق (shafaqa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The thin, delicate edge of twilight; also compassion mixed with fear.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الإشفاق: عناية مختلطة بخوف" — solicitous care blended with fear; when followed by (من) the sense of fear predominates, as in the cited verses.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal root refers to the redness of dusk; metaphorical usage denotes the soul's anxious solicitude, as in "مشفقون" (those who are apprehensive).
- Root: كبر (kabira)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of greatness, magnitude, and seniority.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الكبير والصغير من الأسماء المتضايفة" — relative terms; in moral theology, kibr (conceit) is the soul's self-inflation before others and before God.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah) denotes physical or quantitative greatness; metaphorical (Majaz) usage — "كبر علي ذلك" (it weighed heavily upon him) — extends to the heart's refusal to submit to truth, which is the essence of blameworthy pride.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — The particle "إنما" restricts and confines the predicate, as in "فإذن ما يفسده العابد..." where the structure emphasizes that the corruption caused by hidden pride exceeds any apparent rectification.
23:60.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Fear and Hope'

23:60.arabic: يواظبون على العبادات ويؤتون ما آتوا وقلوبهم وجلة أنهم إلى ربهم راجعون يخافون على أنفسهم وهم طول الليل والنهار في طاعة الله يبالغون في التقوى والحذر من الشبهات والشهوات ويبكون على أنفسهم في الخلوات وأما الآن فترى الخلق آمنين مسرورين مطمئنين غير خائفين مع إكبابهم على المعاصي وانهماكهم في الدنيا وإعراضهم عن الله تعالى زاعمين أنهم واثقون بكرم الله تعالى وفضله راجون
23:60.english: Every soul shall taste what it has earned. And {«وَأَنَّ كُلَّ نَفْسٍ بِمَا كَسَبَتْ رَهِينَةٌ»} — "And that every soul is a pledge for what it has earned." So what has deluded you concerning God, after you have heard and comprehended? They will say: "Had we but listened or reasoned, we would not be among the companions of the Blaze." Thus they will confess their sin. So away with the companions of the Blaze!
23:60.section_title_en: The Anatomy of Hope (Rajā') and Delusion (Ghurūr): A Kalamic Dissection of the Soul's Two States
23:60.anchors:
- Root: نفس (Nafs)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The self, soul, or spirit; that which desires proximity and discourse; the locus of breath and life.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Nafs denotes the rūḥ (spirit) and, in divine attribution, the very Dhāt (Essence) of God—as in {«وَيُحَذِّرُكُمُ اللَّهُ نَفْسَهُ»}—entailing no real multiplicity despite grammatical annexation.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah) usage refers to the living, breathing self; metaphorical (Majaz) usage extends to "blood" (nafs sā'ilah) and the "evil eye" (nafs as 'ayn). Here, it signifies the moral agent bearing responsibility.
- Root: توب (Tawb)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Return, repentance; the act of turning back from error.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Tawbah is abandoning the sin in the most excellent manner—the third and highest form of excuse (after denial and pretext). In Sacred Law: forsaking the sin due to its ugliness, remorse for the past, resolve against recurrence, and restitution of what can be restored.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "The servant repents to God from his sin; God turns in mercy to the servant." The reciprocal dynamic—God's acceptance (tawbah) meeting the servant's return (inābah)—is operative in this text.
- Root: ذنب (Dhanb)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The tail of an animal; what trails behind; by extension, a fault or crime as the "consequence" one drags after oneself.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In origin, "taking hold of a thing's tail"—i.e., seizing the outcome. Sin is that which trails the soul and binds it as a pledge (rahīnah).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Metaphorical: "He is among the tails (adhnāb) of the people"—the laggards. The sinner is one who follows his lower tail, and the verse {«كُلُّ نَفْسٍ بِمَا كَسَبَتْ رَهِينَةٌ»} makes the soul a hostage to its own trailing deeds.
- Root: غفر (Ghafr)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To cover, shield, or protect; the Ghifār tribe's name; a helmet (mighfar) that shields the head.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Ghufrān from God is His shielding the servant from the touch of chastisement—a protective covering, not mere erasure. It may also mean outward forbearance.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "O God, forgive (ghufrānan)!"—a covering over the stain. Metaphorical: Zuhayr's beasts "did not forgive" their negligence—i.e., did not shield the offspring from destruction. Hope of forgiveness without repentance is thus not ghufrān but ghurūr (delusion).
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين العامل والمعمول (Interposition between Operator and Operand) — The periodic structure of verses like {«إِنَّ اللَّهَ يَغْفِرُ الذُّنُوبَ جَمِيعًا»} delays the predicate to heighten rhetorical impact; the conditional "if you say... know that" (fa-in qulta... fa-'lam) governs the entire dialectical sequence, requiring the apodosis to resolve the protasis with logical necessity.
23:60.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Condemnation of Delusion'

24:9.arabic: ويقال إن لله تعالى ملائكة لم يضحك أحد منهم منذ خلقت النار مخافة أن يغضب الله عليهم فيعذبهم بها وقال ابن عمر رضي الله عنهما خرجت مع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم حتى دخل بعض حيطان الأنصار فجعل يلتقط من التمر ويأكل فقال يا ابن عمر مالك لا تأكل فقلت يا رسول الله لا أشتهيه فقال لكني أشتهيه وهذا صبح رابعة لم أذق طعاما ولم أجده ولو سألت ربي لأعطاني ملك قيصر وكسرى فكيف بك يا ابن عمر إذا بقيت في قوم يخبئون رزق سنتهم ويضعف اليقين في قلوبهم قال فوالله ما برحنا ولا قمنا حتى نزلت {وكأين من دابة لا تحمل رزقها الله يرزقها وإياكم وهو السمي
24:9.english: And he — may God's peace and blessings be upon him — said: "Never did Gabriel come to me except that he was trembling, in fear of the Almighty" (3).
24:9.section_title_en: The Fear of God and the Weeping of the Prophets — On the Terror of the Angels and the Lamentation of David (Peace Be Upon Him)
24:9.anchors:
- Root: وجل (wajila)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning is "to fear, to be apprehensive, to tremble inwardly." Al-Farahidi notes its intensity — a trembling that seizes the heart.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In theological usage, *wajal* is the fear born of awe before divine majesty (*haybah*), distinct from mere dread of punishment; it is the trembling of the heart at the threshold of the Sacred.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (*haqiqah*): physical trembling. Metaphorical (*majaz*): the soul's quaking before divine power — as in the *azīz* (boiling) of the breast during prayer, a sound likened to a cauldron.
- Root: بكى (baka)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "To weep, to shed tears." Ibn Manzur records the intensive forms *bakkā'* (much-weeping) and the noun *bukā'* as the outward expression of inward grief (*ḥuzn*).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Weeping is the physical sign of the heart's brokenness (*inkisār*); in the prophets, it is the overflow of *khashyah* — reverent fear — not mere sorrow.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: tears flowing. Metaphorical: the "weeping" of the sky (rain) and the "weeping" of the heart (contrition) — as in David's lament, where tears substitute for speech.
- Root: خطأ (khaṭi'a)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "To err, to commit a fault." Al-Farahidi distinguishes *khaṭī'ah* (a sin committed unintentionally or through weakness) from *ithm* (deliberate transgression).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In Kalam, *khaṭī'ah* for a prophet is a *tark al-awlā* — the abandonment of the more excellent course — not moral depravity; its gravity lies in the station of the one who errs.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: missing the mark. Metaphorical: the soul's deviation from the straight path of intimacy (*uns*) with God, producing *waḥshah* (estrangement).
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد (Restriction & Focused Predication) — The repeated conditional and vocative structures (*yā Dāwūd*, *idhā dhakartu khaṭī'atī*) serve to restrict the predicate to the speaker's subjective state, emphasizing the direct, unmediated dialogue between the prophet and his Lord.
24:9.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Fear and Hope'

24:62.arabic: فقد قال الله تعالى إنما المؤمنون الذين آمنوا بالله ورسوله ثم لم يرتابوا وجاهدوا بأموالهم وأنفسهم في سبيل الله أولئك هم الصادقون {فيكون}
24:62.english: If you say: "What is the meaning of the Salaf's statement, 'I am a believer, if God wills' — given that the exception (istithnā') implies doubt, and doubt in faith is unbelief? Yet they all refrained from giving an unqualified answer affirming faith and were cautious about it."
24:62.section_title_en: On the Meaning of the Salaf's Statement "I am a Believer, If God Wills" — Section 102
24:62.anchors:
- Root: نفس (n-f-s)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The self, the soul; that which is breathed; the innermost reality of a person.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): النفس is used for the rūḥ (spirit), for the dhāt (essence/self), and for the seat of intention and knowledge. When one says "he knows in himself (nafsihi) that he is a believer," it denotes certitude residing in the very core of one's being, not a corporeal faculty.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) usage refers to the soul's reflexive self-awareness; metaphorical (majāz) usage extends to "blood" (dam) or "the eye" (ʿayn) of envy. Here, "in himself" (fī nafsihi) is literal self-knowledge, not mere outward profession.
- Root: وجه (w-j-h)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Face, countenance; the foremost part; a mode, aspect, or direction.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The face is the most noble apparent part of a thing; hence it is used for the "aspect" or "manner" (wajh) of an affair. "Four aspects" (wujūh) means four distinct modes of interpretation or rational grounds.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the face of a person or object. Metaphorical: "the face of the matter" (wajh al-amr) — its most salient and honorable dimension. Here, the "aspects" are hermeneutical angles, not physical parts.
- Root: ايم (a-y-m)
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The unmarried state (aym); one who has no spouse. Not applicable here directly, but the root's semantic field of "being alone/without attachment" contrasts with īmān's root (a-m-n) — security and trust — which is the operative term in this text.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Not directly relevant; the operative root is أمن (a-m-n), meaning security from fear, and by extension, faith (īmān) as the state of being secure in God's truth.
- Root: كان (k-w-n)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To be, to exist; the copula of predication.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Kāna denotes existence and becoming; in theological usage, it grounds the distinction between what is (mawjūd) and what is merely asserted. The question "Are you a believer?" (a-mu'min anta?) uses kāna implicitly to ask about actual, present state — not future contingency.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: existence. Metaphorical: the "being-so" of a predicate. The istithnā' (exception) with "in shā' Allāh" suspends the copula's certainty, shifting from assertive existence to contingent hope.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الاستثناء والتعليق بالمشيئة (The Chapter of Exception and Suspension by the Divine Will) — When an exception clause (istithnā') follows a positive assertion, it grammatically suspends the universality or certainty of the predication. In theological discourse, this suspension may be semantic (doubt) or pragmatic (deference, etiquette, or self-deprecation), and Sibawayh's parsing of conditional suspension (taʿlīq) shows that the apodosis need not be negated — only its absolute, unqualified force is tempered.
24:62.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Fear and Hope'

25:23.arabic: عمل كان بإرادة غير الله مشوبا مغمورا {وقدمنا إلى ما عملوا من عمل فجعلناه هباء منثورا} وليت شعري كيف يصحح نيته من لا يعرف حقيقة النية أو كيف يخلص من صحح النية إذا لم يعرف حقيقة الإخلاص أو كيف تطالب المخلص نفسه بالصدق إذا لم يتحقق معناه فالوظيفة الأولى على كل عبد أراد طاعة الله تعالى أن يتعلم النية أولا لتحصل المعرفة ثم يصححها بالعمل بعد فهم حقيقة الصدق والإخلاص اللذين هما وسيلتنا العبد إلى النجاة والخلاص ونحن نذكر معاني الصدق والإخلاص في ثلاثة أبواب الباب الأول في حقيقة النية ومعناها الباب الثاني في الإخلاص وحق
25:23.english: We praise God with the praise of the thankful, and we believe in Him with the faith of the certain, and we affirm His Oneness with the affirmation of the truthful. And we bear witness that there is no god but God, Lord of the worlds, Creator of the heavens and the earths, and the One Who charges the jinn, mankind, and the angels brought near with the duty to worship Him with the worship of the sincere. For He, exalted, said: {«وما أمروا إلا ليعبدوا الله مخلصين له الدين»} — "And they were not commanded except to worship God, making their religion pure for Him" {Quran 98:5}. For God has no need except for religion that is pure and firm, for He is the Richest of the rich, beyond any need for the partnership of those who associate others with Him. And blessings upon His Prophet Muhammad, the Master of the Messengers, and upon all the prophets, and upon his family and companions, the good and the pure.
25:23.section_title_en: The Book of Intention, Sincerity, and Truthfulness — Book Seven of the Quarter of Deliverance from The Revival of the Religious Sciences
25:23.anchors:
- Root: نية (N-Y-Y)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root denotes intent, purpose, resolve directed toward an aim; the heart's orientation toward an act.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance — niyyah is the soul's decisive inclination (qasd) toward an act for a specific end, distinguishing voluntary acts from mere motions.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — resolved purpose; Metaphorical — the heart's turning toward an object of worship or obedience, making it the inner dimension of 'ibadah.
- Root: خلص (Khl-S)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root — purity after admixture; that which is sifted free of dross.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): ikhlas is the purification of an act from any motive other than God — the removal of shubah (adulteration) that was present.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — refining gold or clarified butter; Metaphorical — "akhlasa lillahi dinahu" (he made his religion pure for God), i.e., exclusive devotion.
- Root: صدق (Sd-Q)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root — firmness, veracity in speech and resolve.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): sidq is primarily in speech (khabar), but secondarily in action and resolve — truthfulness of the heart's commitment.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — truthful speech; Metaphorical — "sadaqa al-hamlata" (he was true in the charge), i.e., unwavering fulfillment of a covenant or act.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The periodic structure here interposes qualifying clauses between the governing verb and its object to layer conditions (e.g., "how can he purify... if he does not know..."), requiring the translator to preserve the conditional cascade without collapsing the hierarchy of epistemic prerequisites.
25:23.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Fear and Hope'

29:60.arabic: برحنا ولا قمنا حتى نزلت {وكأين من دابة لا تحمل رزقها الله يرزقها وإياكم وهو السميع العليم} قال فقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إن الله لم يأمركم بكنز المال ولا بإتباع الشهوات من كنز دنانير يريد بها حياة فانية فإن الحياة بيد الله ألا وإني لا أكنز دينارا ولا درهما ولا أخبأ رزقا لغد // حديث ابن عمر خرجت مع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم حتى دخل على حيطان الأنصار فجعل يلتقط من التمر ويأكل الحديث أخرجه ابن مردويه في التفسير والبيهقي في الزهد من رواية رجل لم يسم عن ابن عمر قال البيهقي هذا إسناد مجهول والجراح بن منهال ضعيف وقال أبو الدر
29:60.english: And he — may God's peace and blessings be upon him — said: "Never did Gabriel come to me except that he was trembling, in fear of the Almighty" (3).
29:60.section_title_en: The Fear of God and the Weeping of the Prophets — On the Terror of the Angels and the Lamentation of David (Peace Be Upon Him)
29:60.anchors:
- Root: وجل (wajila)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning is "to fear, to be apprehensive, to tremble inwardly." Al-Farahidi notes its intensity — a trembling that seizes the heart.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In theological usage, *wajal* is the fear born of awe before divine majesty (*haybah*), distinct from mere dread of punishment; it is the trembling of the heart at the threshold of the Sacred.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (*haqiqah*): physical trembling. Metaphorical (*majaz*): the soul's quaking before divine power — as in the *azīz* (boiling) of the breast during prayer, a sound likened to a cauldron.
- Root: بكى (baka)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "To weep, to shed tears." Ibn Manzur records the intensive forms *bakkā'* (much-weeping) and the noun *bukā'* as the outward expression of inward grief (*ḥuzn*).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Weeping is the physical sign of the heart's brokenness (*inkisār*); in the prophets, it is the overflow of *khashyah* — reverent fear — not mere sorrow.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: tears flowing. Metaphorical: the "weeping" of the sky (rain) and the "weeping" of the heart (contrition) — as in David's lament, where tears substitute for speech.
- Root: خطأ (khaṭi'a)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "To err, to commit a fault." Al-Farahidi distinguishes *khaṭī'ah* (a sin committed unintentionally or through weakness) from *ithm* (deliberate transgression).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In Kalam, *khaṭī'ah* for a prophet is a *tark al-awlā* — the abandonment of the more excellent course — not moral depravity; its gravity lies in the station of the one who errs.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: missing the mark. Metaphorical: the soul's deviation from the straight path of intimacy (*uns*) with God, producing *waḥshah* (estrangement).
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد (Restriction & Focused Predication) — The repeated conditional and vocative structures (*yā Dāwūd*, *idhā dhakartu khaṭī'atī*) serve to restrict the predicate to the speaker's subjective state, emphasizing the direct, unmediated dialogue between the prophet and his Lord.
29:60.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'Fear and Hope'

33:8.arabic: فقال قول الحق والعمل بالصدق (1) وعن الجنيد في قوله تعالى {ليسأل الصادقين عن صدقهم} قال يسأل الصادقين عند أنفسهم عن صدقهم عند ربهم وهذا أمر على خطر
33:8.english: God Most High has said: {«رجال صدقوا ما عاهدوا الله عليه»} — "Among the believers are men who have been true to the covenant they made with God" (Al-Aḥzāb 33:23). And the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Verily, truthfulness leads to righteousness (al-birr), and righteousness leads to Paradise. And verily, a man continues to speak truthfully until he is written with God as a supremely veracious one (ṣiddīq). And verily, falsehood leads to wickedness (al-fujūr), and wickedness leads to the Fire. And verily, a man continues to lie until he is written with God as a liar (kadhdhāb)." (1)
33:8.section_title_en: The Book of Truthfulness (Ṣidq): Its Virtue and Reality — Section on the Virtue of Truthfulness
33:8.anchors:
- Root: صدق (Ṣ-D-Q)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root denotes the firmness and soundness of a thing; a spear termed "ṣadq" is straight and rigid; truthfulness is speech that is firm, sound, and free of crookedness.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الصدق والكذب أصلهما في القول" — truthfulness and falsehood originate in speech, whether past or future, promise or otherwise; they occur by primary intent only in informative statements (khabar), not in other speech categories. Al-Raghib further notes the derived degrees: ṣidq (truthfulness), ṣiddīq (the supremely veracious — one whose truthfulness has become his very character), and ṣādiq al-waʿd (truthful in promise).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Haqiqah (literal): "صدقته الحديث" — to affirm someone's report as true. Majaz (metaphorical): "رجل صادق الحملة" — a man truthful in his charge (i.e., steadfast and unfaltering in battle), and "فرس ذو مصدق في الجري" — a horse with genuine exertion in running. Thus ṣidq extends metaphorically to any state of firmness, steadfastness, and correspondence between inner conviction and outward action.
- Root: بر (B-R-R)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Al-Birr: expansive goodness, piety, and obedience; the "barr" (land) is so named for its expanse. It encompasses all acts of righteousness and kindness.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-birr is the breadth of obedience to God through sincere intention and righteous action; it is the comprehensive term for all that God loves and approves.
- Root: فجر (F-J-R)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Al-Fujūr: the breaking forth and bursting open — the wickedness that breaks through the barrier of piety; the "fājir" is one who bursts out of obedience into transgression.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Fujūr is the violation of the covenant of obedience, the breaking open of the seal of God-consciousness; it is the opposite of birr.
- Root: كذب (K-DH-B)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Al-Kidhb: falsehood — informing of a thing contrary to its reality; the root also carries the sense of deficiency and weakness (as in "kadhaba" — to fall short).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Falsehood is the counterpart of ṣidq — it is reporting what does not correspond to reality, whether in past, present, or future tense.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The grammatical structure "يكتب عند الله صديقا" (he is written with God as a ṣiddīq) involves the prepositional phrase "عند الله" interposed between the verb and its predicate accusative, a construction permissible when the interposed element is semantically integral to the judgment, as here where divine decree is the ground of the designation.
33:8.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'Fear and Hope'

38:88.arabic: ولتعلمن نبأه بعد حين وعند ذلك يقولون كما أخبر الله عنهم ربنا أبصرنا وسمعنا فارجعنا نعمل صالحا إنا موقنون أي علمنا أنه كما لا يولد إلا بوقاع ونكاح ولا ينبت زرع إلا بحراثة وبث بذر فكذلك لا يحصل في الآخرة ثواب وأجر إلا بعمل صالح فارجعنا نعمل صالحا فقد علمنا الآن صدقك في قولك وأن ليس للإنسان إلا ما سعى وأن سعيه سوف يرى كلما ألقى فيها فوج سألهم خزنتها ألم يأتكم نذير قالوا بلى قد جاءنا نذير أي ألم نسمعكم سنة الله في عباده وأنه
38:88.english: I say: God—exalted is He—loves the obedient and hates the disobedient. So just as He does not hate the obedient father because of His hatred for the disobedient son, likewise He does not love the disobedient son because of His love for the obedient father. And if love were to flow from the father to the son, then hatred would likewise be bound to flow. Rather, the truth is: {«ولا تزر وازرة وزر أخرى»} — "And no bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another" {Quran 6:164, 17:15, 35:18, 39:7, 53:38}. And whoever supposes that he will be saved by his father's piety is like one who supposes he will be satiated by his father's eating, quenched by his father's drinking, become a scholar by his father's learning, and reach the Ka'bah and see it by his father's walking.
38:88.section_title_en: The Reality of Hope (Al-Rajā') and the Futility of Reliance on Another's Piety
38:88.anchors:
- Root: و ل د (walada)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Physical begetting and offspring; the father's generative act.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الولد: المولود" — offspring as a created entity; here used metaphorically for spiritual causation.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical birth. Metaphorical: "تولدت العصبية" — something generated or produced from another; Ghazali exploits this to refute the notion that a father's obedience "generates" salvation for the son.
- Root: ر ج و (rajā)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Expectation, hope, longing for a favorable outcome.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Hope tied to legitimate means; not mere wishful thinking (tamannī).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: awaiting rain. Metaphorical: "رجوت فلانا" — to expect from someone; Ghazali contrasts true hope (with action) vs. delusion (ghurūr).
- Root: غ ر ر (gharara)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Deception, heedlessness, being lured by a false appearance.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The state of one who is duped by Satan's plausible speech.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: a risky venture. Metaphorical: "اغتر بفلان" — to be deceived by outward charm while the inner reality is corrupt.
- Root: ك ي س (kays)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Intelligence, shrewdness, prudence.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The wise man who disciplines his soul and acts for the afterlife.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: alertness. Metaphorical: "الكيس من دان نفسه" — the prudent one who holds his soul to account; antonym of "الأحمق" (the fool).
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — "إنما يوفى الصابرون أجرهم بغير حساب" style; Ghazali uses "إنما" to restrict reward to personal action, and "ليس للإنسان إلا ما سعى" as a restrictive negative clause (nafy + illā) to deny any transfer of merit.
38:88.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications, prayers, and their spiritual power, from 'Fear and Hope'

39:16.arabic: النار أعدها لأعدائه وإنما خوف بها أولياءه فقال لهم من فوقهم ظلل من النار ومن تحتهم ظلل ذلك يخوف الله به عباده وقال تعالى واتقوا النار التي أعدت للكافرين وقال تعالى فأنذرتكم نارا تلظى لا يصلاها إلا الأشقى الذي كذب وتولى وقال عز وجل وإن ربك لذوا مغفرة للناس على ظلمهم ويقال أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لم يزل يسأل في أمته حتى قيل له أما ترضى وقد أنزلت عليك هذه الآية وإن ربك لذو مغفرة للناس ظلمهم (2) وفي تفسير قوله تعالى {ولسوف يعطيك ربك فترضى} قال لا يرضى محمد وواحد من أمته في النار وكان أبو جعفر محمد بن علي يقول أنتم أهل العراق تقولون أرجى آية في كتاب الله عز وجل قوله {قل ي
39:16.english: So it was said to him: "And what is in it of hope?" He said: "This world, all of it, is little, and a man's provision from it is little, and his religion is little in comparison to his provision. So look at how God Most High sent down in it the longest verse, to guide His servant to the path of caution in preserving his wealth — so how could He not preserve his religion, which has no substitute for him?"
39:16.section_title_en: The Book of Hope (Kitāb al-Rajā') — Section 1033: The Second Art — Surveying the Verses and Reports Concerning Hope
39:16.anchors:
- Root: وجود (w-j-d)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of "finding" and "existence"; here in the sense of what is present and available.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Existence as that which is found and realized; in theological context, the given order of creation.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) sense of "being found"; metaphorical (majāz) extension to the entirety of created things.
- Root: رجا (r-j-w)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To hope, to expect with desire; the opposite of despair (ya's).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Hope as a theological virtue — the heart's expectation of divine mercy, balanced against fear (khawf).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: expectation of a desired outcome; metaphorical: the soul's reliance on divine generosity.
- Root: غفر (gh-f-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To cover, to shield, to pardon; the root implies veiling the fault.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Divine forgiveness as the covering of sins and the effacing of their consequence.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: covering; metaphorical: God's remission of punishment.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — used to emphasize exclusive attributes of divine mercy and forgiveness.
39:16.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Fear and Hope'

40:71.arabic: يعمل خوصا فقرأت عليه {إذ الأغلال في أعناقهم والسلاسل يسحبون في الحميم ثم في النار يسجرون} فشهق الرجل شهقة وخر مغشيا عليه فخرجنا من عنده وتركناه على حاله وذهبنا إلى آخر فدخلنا عليه فقرأت هذه الآية فشهق شهقة وخر مغشيا عليه فذهبنا واستأذنا على ثالث فقال ادخلوا إن لم تشغلونا عن ربنا فقرأت {ذلك لمن خاف مقامي وخاف وعيد} فشهق شهقة فبدا الدم من منخريه وجعل يتشحط في دمه حتى يبس فتركناه على حاله وخرجنا فأدرته على ستة أنفس كل نخرج من عنده ونتركه مغشيا عليه ثم أتيت به إلى السابع فاستأذنا فإذا امرأة من داخل الخص تقول ادخلوا فدخلنا فإذا شيخ فان ج
40:71.english: And Fudayl was seen one day walking, and it was said to him, "Where are you going?" He said, "I do not know." And he was walking utterly bewildered (wālihan) from fear.
40:71.section_title_en: The Revival of the Religious Sciences — Section 1063: The Weeping of the Fearful and Their States of Awe
40:71.anchors:
- Root: وله (w-l-h)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning is bewilderment and distraction of the mind, losing one's wits due to intense grief or fear; a state where one wanders aimlessly, heedless of direction.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In the theological context of the fear of God (khawf), it denotes a profound psychological dislocation where the heart's composure is shattered by the overwhelming majesty of the divine threat.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Used here in its literal (haqiqah) sense of distracted wandering, but applied metaphorically (majaz) to describe the soul's journey bereft of worldly purpose, driven solely by dread.
- Root: روع (r-w-ʾ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The root signifies striking terror or alarm; "raw'ah" is a sudden fright that seizes the heart.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In the lexicon of the hereafter, it refers to the terrifying summons (al-nida') that strikes dread into the hearts of the sinful when they are paraded before God for reckoning.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): The phrase "raw'at al-nida'" is a literal construction denoting the specific terror of the call to the divine court, not a metaphorical embellishment.
- Root: بهت (b-h-t)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To be stunned, confounded, or speechless; to be rendered motionless and mute by an overwhelming sight or truth.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Describes the state of one who is struck dumb by a divine reality, a cessation of normal cognitive and physical function due to the sheer weight of the metaphysical vision.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Used literally to describe the physical and mental paralysis of the ascetics upon hearing verses of divine threat, distinguishing it from mere figurative astonishment.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Interrogative Retort (باب الاستفهام الإنكاري) — The question "بين يدي من ويحك" (Before whom, woe to you?) functions as a rhetorical denial and rebuke, structured to emphasize the absolute majesty of God by leaving the answer implicit and overwhelming.
40:71.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Fear and Hope'

41:23.arabic: الله له ذنبه قال لأن الله عز وجل عير قوما فقال وذلكم ظنكم الذي ظننتم بربكم أرداكم وقال تعالى وظننتم ظن السوء وكنتم قوما بورا وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم إن الله تعالى يقول للعبد يوم القيامة ما منعك إذ رأيت المنكر أن تنكره فإن لقنه الله حجته قال يا رب رجوتك وخفت الناس قال فيقول الله تعالى قد غفرته لك (4) وفي الخبر الصحيح أن رجلا كان يداين الناس فيسامح الغني ويتجاوز عن المعسر فلقي الله ولم يعمل خيرا قط فقال الله عز وجل من أحق بذلك منا (5) فعفا عنه لحسن ظنه ورجائه أن يعفو عنه مع إفلاسه عن الطاعات وقال تعالى إن الذين يتلون كتاب الل
41:23.english: The Prophet, peace be upon him, said: "Let not one of you die except while he holds a good opinion of God, the Exalted." (1) And he, peace be upon him, said: "God, the Mighty and Majestic, says: I am as My servant thinks of Me, so let him think of Me whatever he wishes." (2)
41:23.section_title_en: On the Excellence of Good Opinion of God and the Virtue of Hope (Section 1031)
41:23.anchors:
- Root: ظن (Ẓann)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning oscillates between certainty and doubt; in theological usage, predominates as "belief/opinion" regarding God's attributes and acts.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-ẓann denotes a preponderant belief (iʿtiqād rājiḥ) that admits of contrary possibility; when coupled with God (ḥusn al-ẓann billāh), it signifies the servant's confident trust in divine mercy and forgiveness, not mere conjecture.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) — doubt mixed with certainty; Metaphorical (majāz) — in the ḥadīth "I am as My servant thinks of Me," it is transferred to the heart's settled reliance on God's beneficence, for God's actual response is entailed by His own decree, not by the servant's thought.
- Root: رجو (Rajā')
  * Lisan / Ayn: Expectation of something desirable with attendant effort; opposite of yaʾs (despair).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Rajā' is the heart's aspiration toward a good whose attainment is possible; it is praiseworthy only when accompanied by fear (khawf) and action, for pure hope without works is delusion (ghurūr).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — awaiting rain (rajāʾ al-ghayth); Metaphorical — the soul's yearning for divine pardon, as in the verse {يَرْجُونَ تِجَارَةً لَنْ تَبُورَ} (they hope for a commerce that will never perish).
- Root: قنط (Qanaṭa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Despair of good; severance of hope.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Qunūṭ is the cessation of expectation of divine mercy, which is blameworthy and tantamount to disbelief in God's power to forgive.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — drought-stricken land yielding no vegetation; Metaphorical — the soul barren of hope, as in {وَكُنْتُمْ قَوْمًا بُورًا} (you were a ruined people).
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The ḥadīth "أنا عند ظن عبدي بي" employs the prepositional phrase "بي" as a complement to "ظن," governing the servant's cognitive stance toward God; the interposition of "عبدي" between the noun and its complement emphasizes the possessive intimacy of the servant's relation to his Lord.
41:23.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'Fear and Hope'

42:5.arabic: تعالى والملائكة يسبحون بحمد ربهم ويستغفرون لمن في الأرض وأخبر تعالى أن النار أعدها لأعدائه وإنما خوف بها أولياءه فقال لهم من فوقهم ظلل من النار ومن تحتهم ظلل ذلك يخوف الله به عباده وقال تعالى واتقوا النار التي أعدت للكافرين وقال تعالى فأنذرتكم نارا تلظى لا يصلاها إلا الأشقى الذي كذب وتولى وقال عز وجل وإن ربك لذوا مغفرة للناس على ظلمهم ويقال أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لم يزل يسأل في أمته حتى قيل له أما ترضى وقد أنزلت عليك هذه الآية وإن ربك لذو مغفرة للناس ظلمهم (2) وفي تفسير قوله تعالى {ولسوف يعطيك ربك فترضى} قال
42:5.english: So it was said to him: "And what is in it of hope?" He said: "This world, all of it, is little, and a man's provision from it is little, and his religion is little in comparison to his provision. So look at how God Most High sent down in it the longest verse, to guide His servant to the path of caution in preserving his wealth — so how could He not preserve his religion, which has no substitute for him?"
42:5.section_title_en: The Book of Hope (Kitāb al-Rajā') — Section 1033: The Second Art — Surveying the Verses and Reports Concerning Hope
42:5.anchors:
- Root: وجود (w-j-d)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of "finding" and "existence"; here in the sense of what is present and available.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Existence as that which is found and realized; in theological context, the given order of creation.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) sense of "being found"; metaphorical (majāz) extension to the entirety of created things.
- Root: رجا (r-j-w)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To hope, to expect with desire; the opposite of despair (ya's).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Hope as a theological virtue — the heart's expectation of divine mercy, balanced against fear (khawf).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: expectation of a desired outcome; metaphorical: the soul's reliance on divine generosity.
- Root: غفر (gh-f-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To cover, to shield, to pardon; the root implies veiling the fault.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Divine forgiveness as the covering of sins and the effacing of their consequence.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: covering; metaphorical: God's remission of punishment.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — used to emphasize exclusive attributes of divine mercy and forgiveness.
42:5.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Fear and Hope'

45:29.arabic: وقرأ مضر القارئ يوما هذا كتابنا ينطق عليكم بالحقالآية فبكى عبد الواحد بن زيد حتى غشي عليه فلما أفاق قال وعزتك لأعصيتك جهدي أبدا فأعني بتوفيقك على طاعتك وكان المسور بن مخرمة لا يقوى أن يسمع شيئا من القرآن لشدة خوفه ولقد كان يقرأ عنده الحرف والآية فيصيح الصحية فما يعقل أياما حتى أتى عليه رجل من خثعم فقرأ عليه {يوم نحشر المتقين إلى الرحمن وفدا ونسوق المجرمين إلى جهنم وردا} فقال أنا من المجرمين ولست من المتقين أعد على القول أيها القارئ فأعادها عليه فشهق شهقة فلحق بالآخرة وقرئ عند يحيى البكاء {ولو
45:29.english: One of them said: "Would that my mother had never given birth to me."
45:29.section_title_en: The States of the Fearful — Accounts of the Companions and Early Saints (Section 1061)
45:29.anchors:
- Root: خوف (kh-w-f)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of dread and apprehension; the heart's agitation before an anticipated harm.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الخوف: توقع مكروه عن أمارة مظنونة، أو معلومة" — fear is the expectation of misfortune based on a probable or certain sign; it is the opposite of security (amn) and pertains to both worldly and otherworldly matters.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): "خفته على مالي خوفا وخيفة" — to fear for something. Metaphorical (Majaz): "تخوفه: تنقصه وأخذ من أطرافه" — fear that consumes one gradually, as in the verse of Zuhayr where the journey "wears away" the camel's hump little by little, as if in dread of it.
- Root: يوم (y-w-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: A measure of time from sunrise to sunset, or any period whatsoever.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "اليوم يعبر به عن وقت طلوع الشمس إلى غروبها. وقد يعبر به عن مدة من الزمان أي مدة كانت" — the Day is a term for any span of time; when added to God (أيام الله), it signifies His mighty acts and visitations upon the nations.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: a single day. Metaphorical: "ذكر في أيام العرب كذا أي في وقائعها" — "days" denotes battles and momentous events; "أيام الله" are His punitive calamities upon the disbelievers.
- Root: حتي (ḥ-t-y)
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): A particle of end-point (ghāyah), signifying the terminal limit of an action or state, as in {ليسجننه حتى حين} and {حتى مطلع الفجر}.
  * Sibawayh Rule: Prepositional and particle interposition (الفصل بين الجار والمجرور) — the particle ḥattā governs what follows as the culminating limit of the preceding narrative, marking the climax of an emotional or physical state (e.g., "until he fell unconscious," "until he died").
- Root: بكى (b-k-y)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Weeping with tears; the physical manifestation of inner anguish.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Weeping is the outward expression of the heart's grief (ḥuzn); in the fearful, it is the release of the soul's dread before God's majesty.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: shedding tears. Metaphorical: "بكاء الثكلي" — the weeping of a bereaved mother, intensified by burning loss, used here to describe the saints' weeping on the Day of Arafah.
45:29.topic: Al-Ghazali on the journey of the soul, death, and the Hereafter, from 'Fear and Hope'

48:12.arabic: بربكم أرداكم وقال تعالى وظننتم ظن السوء وكنتم قوما بورا وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم إن الله تعالى يقول للعبد يوم القيامة ما منعك إذ رأيت المنكر أن تنكره فإن لقنه الله حجته قال يا رب رجوتك وخفت الناس قال فيقول الله تعالى قد غفرته لك (4) وفي الخبر الصحيح أن رجلا كان يداين الناس فيسامح الغني ويتجاوز عن المعسر فلقي الله ولم يعمل خيرا قط فقال الله عز وجل من أحق بذلك منا (5) فعفا عنه لحسن ظنه ورجائه أن يعفو عنه مع إفلاسه عن الطاعات وقال تعالى إن الذين يتلون كتاب الله وأقاموا الصلاة وأنفقوا مما رزقناهم سرا وع
48:12.english: The Prophet, peace be upon him, said: "Let not one of you die except while he holds a good opinion of God, the Exalted." (1) And he, peace be upon him, said: "God, the Mighty and Majestic, says: I am as My servant thinks of Me, so let him think of Me whatever he wishes." (2)
48:12.section_title_en: On the Excellence of Good Opinion of God and the Virtue of Hope (Section 1031)
48:12.anchors:
- Root: ظن (Ẓann)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning oscillates between certainty and doubt; in theological usage, predominates as "belief/opinion" regarding God's attributes and acts.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-ẓann denotes a preponderant belief (iʿtiqād rājiḥ) that admits of contrary possibility; when coupled with God (ḥusn al-ẓann billāh), it signifies the servant's confident trust in divine mercy and forgiveness, not mere conjecture.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) — doubt mixed with certainty; Metaphorical (majāz) — in the ḥadīth "I am as My servant thinks of Me," it is transferred to the heart's settled reliance on God's beneficence, for God's actual response is entailed by His own decree, not by the servant's thought.
- Root: رجو (Rajā')
  * Lisan / Ayn: Expectation of something desirable with attendant effort; opposite of yaʾs (despair).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Rajā' is the heart's aspiration toward a good whose attainment is possible; it is praiseworthy only when accompanied by fear (khawf) and action, for pure hope without works is delusion (ghurūr).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — awaiting rain (rajāʾ al-ghayth); Metaphorical — the soul's yearning for divine pardon, as in the verse {يَرْجُونَ تِجَارَةً لَنْ تَبُورَ} (they hope for a commerce that will never perish).
- Root: قنط (Qanaṭa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Despair of good; severance of hope.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Qunūṭ is the cessation of expectation of divine mercy, which is blameworthy and tantamount to disbelief in God's power to forgive.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — drought-stricken land yielding no vegetation; Metaphorical — the soul barren of hope, as in {وَكُنْتُمْ قَوْمًا بُورًا} (you were a ruined people).
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The ḥadīth "أنا عند ظن عبدي بي" employs the prepositional phrase "بي" as a complement to "ظن," governing the servant's cognitive stance toward God; the interposition of "عبدي" between the noun and its complement emphasizes the possessive intimacy of the servant's relation to his Lord.

52:7.arabic: وسمع عمر رضي الله عنه رجلا يقرأ إن عذاب ربك لواقع ماله من دافع فصاح صيحة وخر مغشيا عليه فحمل إلى بيته فلم يزل مريضا في بيته شهرا وأبو جرير من التابعين قرأ عليه صالح المري فشهق ومات وسمع الشافعي رحمه الله قارئا يقرأ {هذا يوم لا ينطقون ولا يؤذن لهم فيعتذرون} فغشي عليه وسمع علي بن الفضيل قارئا يقرأ {يوم يقوم الناس لرب العالمين} فسقط مغشيا عليه فقال الفضيل شكر الله لك ما قد علمه منك وكذلك نقل عن جماعة منهم وكذلك الصوفية فقد كان الشبلي في مسجده ليلة من رمضان وهو يصلي خلف إمام له فقرأ الإمام {ولئن شئ
52:7.english:
**QUAD_ANCHORS:**
- Root: وجد (Wajd)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The root وجد encompasses multiple senses: finding/attaining (إدراك), intense love (الحب الشديد), grief (الحزن), and wealth/sufficiency (الغنى). Al-Khalil notes the range: "الوجد: الحب. والوجد: الحزن. والوجد: الغنى. والوجد: إدراك الشيء"
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الوجد: إدراك الشيء على خلاف ما يطلب" — and in the technical terminology of the Sufis: "ما يصادف القلب من واردات الأحوال" (what the heart encounters of the influxes of spiritual states)
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal sense is finding/attaining; metaphorical extension (majāz) in devotional context: "وجد فلان في العبادة وجدا: إذا أتى بها على وجهها مع حضور القلب"
- Root: طبع (Tabʿ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الطبع: السجية التي جبل عليها الإنسان" — the innate disposition upon which one is created; also "الختم" (sealing)
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الطبع: السجية التي جبل عليها الإنسان" — the original constitution
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Distinguishes "مطبوع" (innate/natural) from "متكلف" (deliberately acquired) — "فلان مطبوع على الكرم، ومتكلف له"
- Root: كلف (Kulfah/Takalluf)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "التكلف: تجشم ما لا يلزمك" — undertaking what is not incumbent upon you with effort and hardship
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "التكلف: تجشم ما ليس من شأنه" — burdening oneself with what is not one's natural concern
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "تكلفت الأمر: تجشمته على مشقة" — deliberate self-imposition of effort
- Root: سمع (Samāʿ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Auditory perception; also what is heard — recitation, song, remembrance
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "السماع عند الصوفية: ما يهيج الوجد من الأصوات الموزونة" — that which stirs ecstatic finding from measured sounds
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "السماع عند القوم: حضور مجلس يهيج الأحوال الشريفة" — attending an assembly that stirs noble spiritual states
- Root: عشق (ʿIshq)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "العشق: فرط الحب" — excessive love; from "العشقة" — a plant that twines around another
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "العشق: فرط الحب، وأصله من عشقة النبات وهي ما التف منه على غيره"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "العشق مجاز في حق الله تعالى" — metaphorical when applied to God
- Root: بكى (Bukāʾ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Weeping, shedding tears
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "البكاء: إجراء الدمع من عين لحزن أو غيره"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "تباكى: تكلف البكاء" — deliberate self-induced weeping
- Root: صعق (Ṣaʿq)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الصعق: الغشي. والصعق: الموت" — swooning/loss of consciousness; death
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الصعق: غشية تعرض من صوت شديد أو هول"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "صعق من هول الأمر: إذا غشي عليه من شدة الخوف"
- Root: خشع (Khushūʿ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الخشوع: الخضوع والتذلل" — humility and submissiveness
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الخشوع: التذلل والخضوع، وقيل: الخشوع في الصوت والبصر، والخضوع في البدن"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "خشعت الأصوات: سكنت. وخشع البصر: انكسر"
- Root: أنس (Uns)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الأنس: نقيض الوحشة" — the opposite of loneliness/estrangement
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الأنس: حضور القلب مع المحبوب" — the heart's presence with the Beloved
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "الأنس بالله: سكون القلب إليه"
- Root: وجل (Wajal)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الوجل: الخوف مع اضطراب القلب" — fear accompanied by cardiac agitation
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الوجل: الخوف مع اضطراب القلب"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "الوجل: أشد من الخوف، فإنه مع اضطراب"
- Root: طمأن (Ṭumaʾnīnah)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الطمأنينة: السكون" — tranquility
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الطمأنينة: سكون القلب بعد اضطراب"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "اطمأن القلب: سكن بعد اضطراب"
- Root: قشعر (Iqshirʿār)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "القشعريرة: تقبض الجلد من الخوف" — contraction of the skin from fear
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الاقشعرار: انقباض الجلد وتقبضه من الخوف"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "اقشعر الجلد من الخوف: إذا تقبض"
- Root: لين (Līn)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "اللين: ضد الخشونة" — softness, opposite of hardness
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "اللين: نقيض الخشونة"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "لان قلبه: إذا سكن وخشع"
- Root: غشي (Ghashy)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الغشي: الإغماء" — loss of consciousness
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الغشية: ما يغشى القلب من شدة الوجد"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "غشي عليه: إذا أغمي عليه من شدة وجد أو خوف"
- Root: زعق (Zaʿq)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الزعق: الصياح الشديد" — violent screaming
  * Al-Raghib (Al-Mufradat): "الزعق: الصياح الشديد"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "زعق: صاح بأعلى صوته"
- Root: أزيز (Azīz)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الأزيز: صوت النار والمرجل" — the sound of fire and boiling pot
  * Al-Raghib (Al-Mufradat): "الأزيز: صوت النار والمرجل ونحوهما"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "أزيز الصدر: صوت يسمع من شدة البكاء والوجد"
- Root: شهق (Shahīq)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الشهيق: رد النفس إلى الداخل بصوت" — drawing breath inward with sound
  * Al-Raghib (Al-Mufradat): "الشهيق: رد النفس إلى الداخل بصوت"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "شهق الرجل: إذا خرجت نفسه بصوت من شدة الوجد"
- Root: حزن (Ḥuzn)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الحزن: ضد السرور" — grief, opposite of joy
  * Al-Raghib (Al-Mufradat): "الحزن: ألم النفس"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "الحزن: ألم النفس، وهو مجاز من حزن الأرض" (metaphorical extension from rough ground)
- Root: شيب (Shayb)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الشيب: بياض الشعر" — whitening of hair
  * Al-Raghib (Al-Mufradat): "الشيب: بياض الشعر"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "شيبتني هود: أي: كبرتني وأحزنتني حتى شاب شعري"
- Root: ذرف (Dharf)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الذرف: سيلان الدمع" — flowing of tears
  * Al-Raghib (Al-Mufradat): "ذرفت العين: سال دمعها"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "ذرفت عينه: إذا سال دمعها من حزن"
- Root: فيض (Fayḍ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الفيض: سيلان الماء" — overflowing of water
  * Al-Raghib (Al-Mufradat): "الفيض: جريان الماء بكثرة"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "فاضت العين بالدمع: سالت. وفاض القلب: امتلأ"
- Root: نقر (Naqr)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "النقر: الضرب على الشيء حتى يصوت" — striking something until it sounds
  * Al-Raghib (Al-Mufradat): "الناقور: الصور" — the Trumpet
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "الناقور: الصور الذي ينفخ فيه إسرافيل"
- Root: رعش (Riʿshah)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الرعدة: الاضطراب" — trembling
  * Al-Raghib (Al-Mufradat): "الارتعداد: الاضطراب"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "ارتعدت فرائصه: اضطربت من شدة الخوف"
- Root: فرص (Farīṣah)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الفريصة: لحمة بين الجنب والكتف ترعد عند الفزع" — the flesh between the side and shoulder blade that trembles at fright
  * Al-Raghib (Al-Mufradat): "الفريصة: لحمة بين الجنب والكتف ترعد عند الفزع"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "ارتعدت فرائصه: من شدة الخوف"
- Root: عما (ʿAmā)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "العمى: ذهاب البصر. والعمى: ذهاب البصيرة" — blindness of sight; blindness of insight
  * Al-Raghib (Al-Mufradat): "العمى: آفة في البصر، وقد يستعار لآفة البصيرة"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "عمي القلب: ذهبت بصيرته"
- Root: أبصر (Abṣara)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "البصر: حاسة الرؤية. والبصيرة: العلم" — sight; insight
  *Al-Raghib (Al-Mufradat): "الإبصار: إدراك البصر، وقد يستعار للبصيرة"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "أبصر الحق: علمه. ومنه: البصيرة"
- Root: كأس (Ka's)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الكأس: القدح إذا كان فيه شراب" — the cup when it contains drink
  * Al-Raghib (Al-Mufradat): "الكأس: الإناء المعروف، وقد يقال لما فيه"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "الكأس: القدح إذا كان فيه شراب"
52:7.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Fear and Hope'

53:59.arabic: واحتجوا بقوله تعالى أفمن هذا الحديث تعجبون وتضحكون ولا تبكون وأنتم سامدون قال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما هو الغناء بلغة حمير يعني السمد فنقول ينبغي أن يحرم الضحك وعدم البكاء أيضا لآن الآية تشتمل عليه فإن قيل إن ذلك مخصوص بالضحك على المسلمين لإسلامهم فهذا أيضا مخصوص بأشعارهم وغنائهم في معرض الاستهزاء بالمسلمين كما قال تعالى والشعراء يتبعهم الغاوون وأراد به شعراء الكفار ولم يدل ذلك على تحريم نظم الشعر في نفسه واحتجوا بما روى جابر رضي الله عنه أنه صلى الله عليه وسلم قال كان إبليس أول من ناح وأول من تغنى (1) فقد جمع بين النيا
53:59.english: And they argued with His saying—exalted is He: {«أَفَمِنْ هَٰذَا الْحَدِيثِ تَعْجَبُونَ وَتَضْحَكُونَ وَلَا تَبْكُونَ وَأَنتُمْ سَامِدُونَ»} (Do you then wonder at this statement, and laugh, and do not weep, while you amuse yourselves proudly? Q 53:59-61). Ibn 'Abbas—may God be pleased with him—said: "It (al-sumūd) is singing in the language of Himyar." So we say: then laughter and the absence of weeping should also be declared unlawful, because the verse encompasses them. If it is said: "That is specifically about laughing at the Muslims because of their Islam," then this [verse they cite] is also specifically about their poetry and their singing in the manner of mocking the Muslims, just as He said—exalted is He: {«وَالشُّعَرَاءُ يَتَّبِعُهُمُ الْغَاوُونَ»} (And the poets — the deviators follow them; Q 26:224), intending thereby the poets of the disbelievers. And that did not indicate the unlawfulness of composing poetry in itself.
53:59.section_title_en: On the Distinction Between Blameworthy and Permissible Singing, and the Refutation of Those Who Declare All Singing Unlawful
53:59.anchors:
- Root: حرم (ḥ-r-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of prohibition and sanctity; that which is rendered forbidden either by divine decree, legal ruling, or coercive force.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الحرام: الممنوع منه إما بتسخير إلهي وإما بشري" — prohibition is either by divine constraint, legal prescription, or rational necessity; the term carries degrees of restriction.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): that which is legally forbidden. Metaphorical (Majaz): "جلد محرم: لم يدبغ" — untanned hide; "أعرابي محرم: حاف لم يخالط الحضر" — a Bedouin who has not mixed with settled life. Thus, what is "unlawful" in the absolute sense must be distinguished from what is merely deficient or uncultivated.
- Root: ضحك (ḍ-ḥ-k)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The physical expansion of the face and baring of teeth from joy of the soul; the front teeth are called "الضواحك" (the smiling ones).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الضحك: انبساط الوجه وتكشر الأسنان من سرور النفس" — laughter is the expansion of the face from inner joy; "واستعير الضحك للسخرية" — metaphorically extended to mockery and derision.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: genuine joy and amusement. Metaphorical: "ضحكت الأرض عن النبات" — the earth "laughs" forth vegetation; "ضحك العارض: برق" — the cloud "laughs" with lightning. Thus, the Qur'anic condemnation of laughter (in Q 53:59-60) is contextually bound to mockery of revelation, not laughter per se.
- Root: روي (r-w-y)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To drink one's fill; satiation with water.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "ماء رواء، وروى، أي: كثير مرو" — abundant water that quenches; extended metaphorically to satiation with knowledge or beauty.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: quenching of thirst. Metaphorical: "هو ريان من العلم" — saturated with knowledge; "سحاب روي: عظيم القطر" — a cloud heavy with rain. The root carries the sense of fullness and completion, relevant to the "full" transmission of reports.
- Root: ثني (th-n-y)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To fold, double, or repeat; the second of a pair.
  * Al-Raghib (Al-Mufradat): "الثني والاثنان أصل لمتصرفات هذه الكلمة" — the root of duality and repetition; "الثنى: ما يعاد مرتين" — that which is repeated twice.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: folding one thing upon another. Metaphorical: "ثنيت فلانا على وجهه إذا رجعته إلى حيث جاء" — to turn someone back; "ثنى عنانه عني" — to turn away one's reins, i.e., to avert. This root governs the "Thaniyyat al-Wada'" (the mountain passes of farewell) in the famous song cited in the text.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد (Restriction and Specification) — When a general prohibition (like "all singing is unlawful") is advanced, the specification of particular instances (like the singing of the two girls on the day of Eid) restricts the general claim. Conversely, when a specific permission is established by an unambiguous act (fi'l), it cannot be overridden by ambiguous reports (aqwal) that admit of interpretation and specification.
53:59.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'Fear and Hope'

70:28.arabic: وجل إن عذاب ربهم غير مأمون فأجهل الناس من أمنه وهو ينادي بالتحذير من الأمن ولو أن الله لطف بعباده العارفين إذ روح قلوبهم بروح الرجاء لاحترقت قلوبهم من نار الخوف فأسباب الرجاء رحمة لخواص الله وأسباب الغفلة رحمة على عوام الخلق من وجه إذ لو انكشف الغطاء لزهقت النفوس وتقطعت القلوب من خوف مقلب القلوب قال بعض العارفين لو حالت بيني وبين من عرفته بالتوحيد خمسين
70:28.english: Just as Abraham (peace be upon him), when he was placed in the catapult, said: "God is sufficient for me" {حسبي الله} — and this was among the greatest supplications — he was tested and was confronted by Gabriel in mid-air, who said to him: "Do you have any need?" He replied: "As for you, no." And that was the fulfillment of the very reality of his words: "God is sufficient for me." So God Most High informed us about him, saying: "And Abraham who fulfilled" {وإبراهيم الذي وفى} — that is, fulfilled the requirement of his saying "God is sufficient for me." And in like manner, He informed us about Moses (peace be upon him), where he said: "Indeed, we fear that he may assault us or that he may transgress" {إننا نخاف أن يفرط علينا أو أن يطغى}. He said: "Fear not; indeed, I am with you both; I hear and I see" {لا تخافا إنني معكما أسمع وأرى}. Yet despite this, when the sorcerers cast their sorcery, Moses conceived within himself a fear — because he did not feel secure from the deception (makar) of God, and the matter became obscure to him — until security was renewed for him, and it was said to him: "Fear not; indeed, you are the most exalted" {لا تخف إنك أنت الأعلى}. And when the strength of the Muslims weakened on the Day of Badr, he (peace be upon him) said: "O God, if You destroy this band, there will remain no one on the face of the earth who worships You" — a hadith reported on the Day of Badr: "O God, if You destroy this band, there will remain no one on the face of the earth who worships You," transmitted by al-Bukhari from the hadith of Ibn Abbas with the wording: "O God, if You will, You will not be worshipped after this day" — to the end of the hadith. So Abu Bakr (may God be pleased with him) said: "Leave off your importuning of your Lord, for He will surely fulfill what He has promised you." Thus, the station of al-Siddiq (may God be pleased with him) was the station of trust in God's promise, while the station of the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) was the station of fear of God's deception (makar) — and this latter is more complete, for it issues only from the perfection of knowledge of God's secrets, the hidden aspects of His acts, and the meanings of His attributes, some of whose manifestations are expressed as "deception" (makar). And no human being can stand upon the ultimate reality (kunnah) of God's attributes. Whoever knows the true nature of knowledge — that his knowledge falls short of encompassing the ultimate reality of things — his fear inevitably magnifies. For this reason, the Messiah (peace be upon him), when it was said to him: "Did you say to the people: 'Take me and my mother as two gods besides God?'" replied: "Glory be to You! It was not mine to say what I had no right to say. If I had said it, You would have known it. You know what is in my self, and I do not know what is in Your Self" {سبحانك ما يكون لي أن أقول ما ليس لي بحق إن كنت قلته فقد علمته تعلم ما في نفسي ولا أعلم ما في نفسك}. And he said: "If You punish them, indeed they are Your servants; and if You forgive them..." {إن تعذبهم فإنهم عبادك وإن تغفر لهم} — to the end of the verse. So he delegated the matter entirely to the divine will (mashī'ah) and removed himself completely from the equation, knowing that he had no say in the affair whatsoever, and that all matters are linked to the divine will in a linkage that exceeds the bounds of rational categories and habitual patterns — such that no judgment can be passed upon them by analogy, nor by conjecture, nor by reckoning (ḥisbān), let alone by verification and certainty. And this is precisely what has rent the hearts of the knowers (ʿārifīn) asunder — for the supreme calamity (al-ṭāmmah al-kubrā) is the linkage of your affair to the will of One who does not care about you: if He destroys you, He has destroyed countless others like you, and He has never ceased in this world to torment them with various kinds of pains and diseases, and to sicken their hearts thereby with disbelief and hypocrisy, and then to perpetuate the punishment upon them for all eternity. Then He informs us about this, saying: "And had We willed, We would have given every soul its guidance, but the word from Me has taken effect: I will surely fill Hell with jinn and people all together" {ولو شئنا لآتينا كل نفس هداها ولكن حق القول مني لأملأن جهنم من الجنة والناس أجمعين}. And He Most High said: "And the word of your Lord has been fulfilled: I will surely fill Hell..." {وتمت كلمة ربك لأملأن جهنم}. So how should one not fear what has been decreed as a word from eternity (al-azal), and not hope for its reversal? Had the matter been recent, then hopes might extend toward some stratagem regarding it — but there is nothing except submission to it, and the discernment of the hidden precedent (al-sābiqah) from the manifest outward causes upon the heart and the bodily members. For whoever is facilitated toward the causes of evil, and is barred from the causes of good, and whose attachment to this world is firmly secured — it is as if the secret of the prior decree that destined him to wretchedness has been unveiled to him with certainty, since "everyone is facilitated toward that for which he was created" {كل ميسر لما خلق له}. And even if all good things were facilitated, and the heart were entirely severed from this world, with its outward and inward aspects turned wholly toward God, this would necessitate a lightening of fear — were continuity in that state to be trusted. But the peril of the final end (khātimah) and the difficulty of steadfastness only fan the flames of fear into greater blaze and prevent them from being extinguished. For how can one feel secure from the change of state, when the believer's heart lies between two fingers of the fingers of the Merciful? And indeed, the heart is more prone to turning than a boiling pot. And the Turner of Hearts (Glory be to Him) has said: "Indeed, the punishment of their Lord is not to be felt secure from" {إن عذاب ربهم غير مأمون}. So the most ignorant of people is the one who feels secure from it, while He proclaims the warning against security. And were God to show kindness to His knowing servants by reviving their hearts with the spirit of hope (rajā'), their hearts would still burn from the fire of fear. Thus, the causes of hope are a mercy for God's elect, and the causes of heedlessness are a mercy upon the common folk of creation in one respect — for were the veil to be lifted, souls would perish and hearts would be torn asunder from the fear of the Turner of Hearts. One of the knowers said: "If fifty were to intervene between me and the One I have known through tawḥīd..."
70:28.section_title_en: The Reality of Fear and the Station of Abraham, Moses, and the Messenger (Peace Be Upon Them) — On the Inescapable Terror of the Divine Decree
70:28.anchors:
- Root: حسب (ḥ-s-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of counting, reckoning, and sufficiency; "ḥasbī Allāh" signifies God as the sufficient reckoner.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance of ḥisāb as divine accounting; "ḥasbī Allāh" is a declaration of total reliance on God's sufficiency, transcending mere numerical count.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) — reckoning by number; Metaphorical (majāz) — trusting in God's sufficiency as an act of spiritual accounting, where the servant counts God as enough against all else.
- Root: خوف (kh-w-f)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of fear, dread, and apprehension of harm.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Khawf is the expectation of a disliked outcome based on a probable or known sign; it opposes amn (security) and applies to both worldly and otherworldly matters.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — fear of loss or harm; Metaphorical — a "fearful path" (ṭarīq khā'if) where danger inheres in the object, and "takhawwuf" as gradual diminishment, implying fear's erosive effect on the soul.
- Root: نفس (n-f-s)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of self, soul, breath; the essence of a thing.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Nafs as the self or essence (dhāt), as in "ta'lamu mā fī nafsī" (You know what is in my self), denoting the innermost reality distinct from the body.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — the soul as animate essence; Metaphorical — "nafs sā'ilah" (flowing blood) as the life-principle, and the soul's hidden movements as the locus of divine knowledge.
- Root: قلب (q-l-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of turning, overturning, and transformation.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Qalb is the turning of a thing from one state to another; the heart is so named for its constant fluctuation (taqallub) between states.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — physical overturning; Metaphorical — the heart's perpetual oscillation, as in the prophetic hadith of the heart between two fingers of the Merciful, and the "turning" of affairs by divine decree.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Interposition and Apposition (al-ʿaṭf wa al-faṣl) — The periodic structure of "fa-kayfa lā yakhāfu..." (How then should one not fear...) employs a rhetorical question governed by an implied causal clause, where the apodosis is suspended across multiple subordinate clauses, requiring the translator to preserve the cumulative force of the argument without breaking the syntactic chain.
70:28.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Fear and Hope'

71:13.arabic: بالرجاء فقال تعالى {ما لكم لا ترجون لله وقارا} أي لا تخافون وكثيرا ما ورد في القرآن الرجاء بمعنى الخوف وذلك لتلازمهما إذ عادة العرب التعبير عن الشيء بما يلازمه بل أقول كل ما ورد في فضل البكاء من خشية الله فهو إظهار لفضيلة الخشية فإن البكاء ثمرة الخشية فقد قال تعالى {فليضحكوا قليلا وليبكوا كثيرا} وقال تعالى {يبكون ويزيدهم خشوعا} وقال عز وجل {أفمن هذا
71:13.english: For they possess the Highest Companion (al-Rafīq al-Aʿlā) in which none share with them. Consider how He singled them out for the companionship of the Highest Companion — and that is because they are the scholars (ʿulamāʾ), and the scholars hold the rank of companionship with the prophets, for they are the heirs of the prophets. And the companionship of the Highest Companion belongs to the prophets and to those who attach themselves to them. For this reason, when the Messenger of God — may God's blessings and peace be upon him — was given the choice during his death-illness between remaining in this world and proceeding to God — may He be exalted — he would say: "I ask of Thee the Highest Companion" {«الرفيق الأعلى»}.
71:13.section_title_en: On the Excellence of Fear (Khawf) and Its Inseparability from Faith — Section 1042
71:13.anchors:
- Root: خوف (Khawf)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root denotes trepidation, apprehension, and the state of being afraid; its opposite is amn (security).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الخوف: توقع مكروه عن أمارة مظنونة، أو معلومة" — anticipation of something disliked based on an indication, whether conjectural or certain; it is the direct opposite of amn (security), and applies to both worldly and otherworldly matters.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): "خفته على مالي خوفا وخيفة" — to fear for something. Metaphorical (Majaz): "تخوفه: تنقصه" — to diminish gradually, as fear erodes the soul's complacency.
- Root: حدث (Hadath)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Newness, origination after non-existence; also that which is recent in time.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الحدوث: كون الشيء بعد أن لم يكن" — the coming-to-be of a thing after it was not; true origination belongs to God alone.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "هو حدث من الأحداث" — one who is recent/young. Metaphorical: "كان عمر محدثا أي صادق الحدس" — one whose intuition is true, as if divinely inspired.
- Root: يوم (Yawm)
  * Lisan / Ayn: A day; a period of time from sunrise to sunset, or any duration whatsoever.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "اليوم يعبر به عن وقت طلوع الشمس إلى غروبها. وقد يعبر به عن مدة من الزمان أي مدة كانت" — used for the day proper or any extended period; "أيام الله" refers to His mighty deeds and visitations upon the wicked.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "ما رأيته اليوم" — temporal designation. Metaphorical: "ذكر في أيام العرب كذا أي في وقائعها" — "days" as battles and momentous events.
- Root: قوي (Quwwa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Strength, power, capability; the opposite of weakness.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "القوة تستعمل تارة في معنى القدرة" — power as capability; also potentiality, as when a date-stone is said to be "potentially" a palm-tree.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "هو قوي مقو" — physically strong. Metaphorical: strength of heart, of conviction, and of allies.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — When the particle innamā is employed, it restricts the predicate exclusively to the subject mentioned, negating it for all others. This governs the author's argument that taqwā is exclusively attributed to God's nearness and that the "Highest Companion" (al-Rafīq al-Aʿlā) is uniquely reserved for the prophets and their heirs.
71:13.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Fear and Hope'

92:14.arabic: للكافرين وقال تعالى فأنذرتكم نارا تلظى لا يصلاها إلا الأشقى الذي كذب وتولى وقال عز وجل وإن ربك لذوا مغفرة للناس على ظلمهم ويقال أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لم يزل يسأل في أمته حتى قيل له أما ترضى وقد أنزلت عليك هذه الآية وإن ربك لذو مغفرة للناس ظلمهم (2) وفي تفسير قوله تعالى {ولسوف يعطيك ربك فترضى} قال لا يرضى محمد وواحد من أمته في النار وكان أبو جعفر محمد بن علي يقول أنتم أهل العراق تقولون أرجى آية في كتاب الله عز وجل قوله {قل يا عبادي الذين أسرفوا على أنفسهم لا تقنطوا من رحمة الله} الآية ونحن أهل البيت نقول أرجى آية في كتاب الله تعا
92:14.english: So it was said to him: "And what is in it of hope?" He said: "This world, all of it, is little, and a man's provision from it is little, and his religion is little in comparison to his provision. So look at how God Most High sent down in it the longest verse, to guide His servant to the path of caution in preserving his wealth — so how could He not preserve his religion, which has no substitute for him?"
92:14.section_title_en: The Book of Hope (Kitāb al-Rajā') — Section 1033: The Second Art — Surveying the Verses and Reports Concerning Hope
92:14.anchors:
- Root: وجود (w-j-d)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of "finding" and "existence"; here in the sense of what is present and available.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Existence as that which is found and realized; in theological context, the given order of creation.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) sense of "being found"; metaphorical (majāz) extension to the entirety of created things.
- Root: رجا (r-j-w)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To hope, to expect with desire; the opposite of despair (ya's).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Hope as a theological virtue — the heart's expectation of divine mercy, balanced against fear (khawf).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: expectation of a desired outcome; metaphorical: the soul's reliance on divine generosity.
- Root: غفر (gh-f-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To cover, to shield, to pardon; the root implies veiling the fault.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Divine forgiveness as the covering of sins and the effacing of their consequence.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: covering; metaphorical: God's remission of punishment.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — used to emphasize exclusive attributes of divine mercy and forgiveness.
92:14.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Fear and Hope'

2:78.arabic: ذلك من الآيات وكان داخلا في معنى قوله عز وجل ومنهم أميون لا يعلمون الكتاب إلا أماني يعني التلاوة المجردة وقوله عز وجل وكأين من آية في السموات والأرض يمرون عليها وهم عنها معرضون لأن القرآن هو المبين لتلك الآيات في السموات والأرض ومهما تجاوزها ولم يتأثر بها كان معرضا عنها ولذلك قيل إن من لم يكن متصفا بأخلاق القرآن فإذا قرأ القرآن ناداه الله تعالى مالك ولكلامي وأنت معرض عني دع عنك كلامي إن لم تتب إلي ومثال العاصي إذا قرأ القرآن وكرره مثال من يكرر كتاب الملك في كل يوم مرات وقد كتب إليه في عمارة مملكته وهو مشغول بتخريبها ومقتصر على د
2:78.english: And at the mention of God, His attributes, and His names, he bows low in humility before His majesty and in apprehension of His greatness. And at the mention of the disbelievers' sayings — those things impossible for God, Mighty and Majestic, such as their attributing to Him a son or a consort — he lowers his voice and inwardly recoils in shame at the ugliness of their speech. And at the description of Paradise, his innermost being surges forth with longing for it. And at the description of the Fire, his limbs tremble in fear of it. For when the Messenger of God, peace be upon him, said to Ibn Mas'ud, "Recite to me," he said: "I began reciting Surah al-Nisa'. When I reached {فكيف إذا جئنا من كل أمة بشهيد وجئنا بك على هؤلاء شهيدا} [How then shall it be when We bring from every nation a witness, and We bring you as a witness against these?] (4:41), I saw his two eyes overflowing with tears. He then said to me: 'That is enough for you now.'" And this was because the witnessing of that very state had wholly overwhelmed his heart.
2:78.section_title_en: The States of the Heart During Qur'anic Recitation — The Condition of the True Recieter
2:78.anchors:
- Root: وجل (w-j-l)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root meaning of trembling fear, trepidation of the heart
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الوجل: استشعار الخوف" — the inward apprehension of fear; cited in {إنما المؤمنون الذين إذا ذكر الله وجلت قلوبهم}
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): "رجل وجل، وقوم وجال" — a man fearful, a people fearful; the state of the heart's trembling before divine majesty
- Root: وصف (w-ṣ-f)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Describing a thing by its attributes and qualities
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الوصف: ذكر الشيء بحليته ونعته" — description is the mention of a thing by its adornment and attribute; may be true or false
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal vs Metaphorical: "وجهها يصف الحسن" — metaphorical usage where the face itself "describes" beauty; likewise, the tongue may "describe" falsehood, as in {ولا تقولوا لما تصف ألسنتكم الكذب}
- Root: وفي (w-f-y)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Completeness, fulfillment, reaching full measure
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الوافي: الذي بلغ التمام" — that which attains completion; "أوفى: إذا تمم العهد ولم ينقض حفظه" — fulfilled the covenant without breach
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "درهم واف" — a full-weight dirham; Metaphorical: "أوفى على المائة إذا زاد عليها" — surpassed the hundred
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The separation between the governing preposition and its object by intervening clauses, as in "فلما بلغت {فكيف إذا جئنا...}" where the temporal clause governs the narrative sequence

2:93.arabic: مبصرة ولم تكن عمياء ولم يدر أنهم بماذا ظلموا غيرهم أو أنفسهم وقوله تعالى وأشربوا في قلوبهم العجل بكفرهم أي حب العجل فحذف الحب وقوله عز وجل إذا لأذقناك ضعف الحياة وضعف الممات أي ضعف عذاب الأحياء وضعف عذاب الموتى فحذف العذاب وأبدل الأحياء والموتى بذكر الحياة والموت وكل ذلك جائز في فصيح اللغة وقوله تعالى واسئل القرية التي كنا فيها والعير التي أقبلنا فيها أي أهل العير فالأهل فيهما محذوف مضمر وقوله عز وجل ثقلت في السموات والأرض معناه خفيت على أهل السموات والأرض والشيء إذا خفي ثقل فأبدل اللفظ به وأقيم في مقام على وأضمر الأهل وحذف وقوله تعالى وتجعلون
2:93.english: I say: The Prophet (peace be upon him) was asked about the means of deliverance from these trials, and he said: "The Book of Allah — act by what is in it, for it is that which delivers one from them." The questioner repeated this three times, and he (peace be upon him) said three times: "Learn the Book of Allah, Mighty and Glorious, and act by what is in it, for in it is deliverance."
2:93.section_title_en: The Book of the Etiquette of Recitation — Section 233: On Understanding the Meanings of the Qur'an and the Limits of Interpretation
2:93.anchors:
- Root: ف-ه-م (f-h-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الفهم: هيئة للإنسان بها يتحقق معاني ما يحسن" — comprehension as an inherent faculty by which one ascertains meanings
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الفهم: هيئة للإنسان بها يتحقق معاني ما يحسن... وأفهمته: إذا قلت له حتى تصوره" — comprehension is a cognitive disposition; distinction between understanding (fahm) and making understood (ifhām)
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "تقول: من لم يؤت من سوء الفهم أتى من سوء الإفهام" — literal usage; failure of understanding often stems from failure of communication
- Root: ف-س-ر (f-s-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "وكل شيء يعرف به تفسير الشيء ومعناه، فهو تَفْسِرَتُه" — that by which a thing's meaning is made known
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "التفسير قد يقال فيما يختص بمفردات الألفاظ وغريبها، وفيما يختص بالتأويل" — tafsīr concerns lexical surface; taʾwīl concerns deeper meaning
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "هذا كلام يحتاج إلى فسر وتفسير" — literal: exposition of what is obscure
- Root: و-ج-ل (w-j-l)
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الوجل: استشعار الخوف" — the sensing of fear; used of hearts trembling at divine mention
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "لو واجلت فلانا لوجلته: لغلبته في الوجل" — literal sense of fear; metaphorical extension to overpowering in fear
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — the particle innamā restricts predication, essential for parsing the Prophet's saying "innamā al-aʿmālu bi-l-niyyāt" and analogous restrictive formulations in the ḥadīth cited herein

2:185.arabic: كقوله عز وجل شهر رمضان الذي أنزل فيه القرآن إذ لم يظهر به أنه ليل أو نهار وبان بقوله عز وجل إنا أنزلناه في ليلة مباركة ولم يظهر به أي ليلة فظهر بقوله تعالى إنا أنزلناه في ليلة القدر وربما يظن في الظاهر الاختلاف بين هذه الآيات فهذا وأمثاله مما لا يغني فيه إلا النقل والسماع فالقرآن من أوله إلى آخره غير خال عن هذا الجنس لأنه أنزل بلغة العرب فكان مشتملا على أصناف كلامهم من إيجاز وتطويل وإضمار وحذف وإبدال وتقديم وتأخير ليكون ذلك مفحما لهم ومعجزا في حقهم فكل من اكتفى بفهم ظاهر العربية وبادر إ
2:185.english: I say: The Prophet (peace be upon him) was asked about the means of deliverance from these trials, and he said: "The Book of Allah — act by what is in it, for it is that which delivers one from them." The questioner repeated this three times, and he (peace be upon him) said three times: "Learn the Book of Allah, Mighty and Glorious, and act by what is in it, for in it is deliverance."
