56:79.arabic: كلام الله عز وجل غاية الخطر فإنه تعالى قال {لا يمسه إلا المطهرون} وكما أن ظاهر جلد المصحف وورقه محروس عن ظاهر بشرة اللامس إلا إذا كان متطهرا فباطن معناه أيضا بحكم عزه وجلاله محجوب عن باطن القلب إلا إذا كان متطهرا عن كل رجس ومستنيرا بنور التعظيم والتوقير وكما لا يصلح لمس جلد المصحف كل يد فلا يصلح لتلاوة حروفه كل لسان ولا لنيل معانيه كل قلب ولمثل هذا التعظيم كان عكرمة بن أبي جهل إذا نشر المصحف غشى عليه ويقول هو كلام ربي هو كلام ربي فتعظيم الكلام تعظيم المتكلم ولن تحضره عظمة المتكلم ما لم يتفكر في صفاته وجلاله و
56:79.english: And one of the sages shone brilliantly in expressing the aspect of gentleness in conveying the meanings of speech — despite the exaltedness of its rank — to human understanding, and establishing it firmly despite the limitation of humanity's station. He struck for it a parable that fell short of nothing. That was when a certain sage was summoned by one of the kings to the law of the prophets — peace be upon them. The king asked him about matters, and he answered with what his understanding could not bear. The king said: "What do you say of what the prophets bring when they claim that it is not the speech of men, but that it is the speech of Allah — mighty and majestic is He? How then can people bear to carry it?"
56:79.section_title_en: The Ten Principles of Qur'anic Recitation — The Inward Realities of Recitation (Section 226)
56:79.anchors:
- Root: فهم (f-h-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Comprehension, understanding; the faculty by which one grasps meanings
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الفهم: هيئة للإنسان بها يتحقق معاني ما يحسن" — a disposition by which one ascertains meanings; divine favor in bestowing understanding
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "من لم يؤت من سوء الفهم أتى من سوء الإفهام" — distinguishes passive reception from active divine instruction
- Root: عظم (ʿ-ẓ-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Bigness of bone; then metaphorically extended to all magnitude, sensory or intelligible
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "عظم الشيء أصله: كبر عظمه، ثم استعير لكل كبير" — literal bone-magnitude extended metaphorically to majesty and grandeur
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "لا يتعاظمني أي لا يعظم في عيني" — what is too great for one's capacity to bear
- Root: حكم (ḥ-k-m)
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "حكم أصله: منع منعا لإصلاح" — restraint for the sake of rectification; hence the rein (ḥikmah) of the beast
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "أحكم الشيء فاستحكم" — to make firm so that it becomes firm; the penetrating authority of wisdom
- Sibawayh Rule: Interposition of the prepositional phrase (الفصل بين الجار والمجرور) — governing the periodic suspension between the divine attribute and its creaturely vehicle, as in "من كلام الله" where the genitive chain marks ontological descent without essential change
56:79.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Etiquette of Quran Recitation'

56:82.arabic: وقوله تعالى وتجعلون رزقكم أنكم تكذبون أي شكر رزقكم وقوله عز وجل وآتنا ما وعدتنا على رسلك أي على ألسنة رسلك فحذف ألسنة وقوله تعالى إنا أنزلناه في ليلة القدر أراد القرآن وما سبق له ذكر وقال عز وجل حتى توارت الحجاب أراد الشمس وما سبق لها ذكر وقوله تعالى والذين اتخذوا من دونه أولياء ما نعبدهم إلا ليقربونا إلى الله زلفى أي يقولون ما نعبدهم وقوله عز وجل فمال هؤلاء القوم لا يكادون يفقهون حديثا ما أصابك من حسنة فمن الله وما أصابك من سيئة فمن نفسك معناه لا يفقهون حديثا يقولون ما أصابك من
56:82.english: I say: The Prophet (peace be upon him) was asked about the means of deliverance from these trials, and he said: "The Book of Allah — act by what is in it, for it is that which delivers one from them." The questioner repeated this three times, and he (peace be upon him) said three times: "Learn the Book of Allah, Mighty and Glorious, and act by what is in it, for in it is deliverance."
56:82.section_title_en: The Book of the Etiquette of Recitation — Section 233: On Understanding the Meanings of the Qur'an and the Limits of Interpretation
56:82.anchors:
- Root: ف-ه-م (f-h-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الفهم: هيئة للإنسان بها يتحقق معاني ما يحسن" — comprehension as an inherent faculty by which one ascertains meanings
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الفهم: هيئة للإنسان بها يتحقق معاني ما يحسن... وأفهمته: إذا قلت له حتى تصوره" — comprehension is a cognitive disposition; distinction between understanding (fahm) and making understood (ifhām)
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "تقول: من لم يؤت من سوء الفهم أتى من سوء الإفهام" — literal usage; failure of understanding often stems from failure of communication
- Root: ف-س-ر (f-s-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "وكل شيء يعرف به تفسير الشيء ومعناه، فهو تَفْسِرَتُه" — that by which a thing's meaning is made known
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "التفسير قد يقال فيما يختص بمفردات الألفاظ وغريبها، وفيما يختص بالتأويل" — tafsīr concerns lexical surface; taʾwīl concerns deeper meaning
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "هذا كلام يحتاج إلى فسر وتفسير" — literal: exposition of what is obscure
- Root: و-ج-ل (w-j-l)
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الوجل: استشعار الخوف" — the sensing of fear; used of hearts trembling at divine mention
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "لو واجلت فلانا لوجلته: لغلبته في الوجل" — literal sense of fear; metaphorical extension to overpowering in fear
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — the particle innamā restricts predication, essential for parsing the Prophet's saying "innamā al-aʿmālu bi-l-niyyāt" and analogous restrictive formulations in the ḥadīth cited herein
56:82.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Etiquette of Quran Recitation'

72:1.arabic: إلى قومهم منذرين {فقالوا إنا سمعنا قرآنا عجبا يهدي إلى الرشد فآمنا به ولن نشرك بربنا أحدا} فكل من آمن به فقد وفق ومن قال به فقد صدق ومن تمسك به فقد هدي ومن عمل به فقد فاز وقال تعالى {إنا نحن نزلنا الذكر وإنا له لحافظون} ومن أسباب حفظه في القلوب والمصاحف استدامة تلاوته والمواظبة على دراسته مع القيام بآدابه وشروطه والمحافظة على ما فيه من الأعمال الباطنة والآداب الظاهرة وذلك لا بد من بيانه وتفصيله وتنكشف مقاصده في أربعة أبواب الباب الأول في فضل القرآن وأهله الباب الثاني في آداب التلاوة في الظاهر الباب الثالث في الأعمال الباطنة عند التلاوة الباب ا
72:1.english: Praise be to God, who has bestowed His favor upon His servants through His sent Messenger (peace be upon him) and His revealed Book — falsehood cannot approach it from before it or from behind it; it is a revelation (tanzīl) from the Wise, the Praiseworthy {«تَنْزِيلٌ مِنْ حَكِيمٍ حَمِيدٍ»}. Through it, the path of reflection (iʿtibār) has been widened for the people of understanding, by virtue of what it contains of narratives and reports; and through it, the way of the upright course and the straight path (al-ṣirāṭ al-mustaqīm) has been made clear, by virtue of what it details of rulings and distinguishes between the lawful (ḥalāl) and the unlawful (ḥarām). It is the illumination and the light; through it is deliverance from delusion; in it is healing for what is in the breasts. Whoever opposes it among the tyrants, God crushes him; and whoever seeks knowledge in other than it, God leads him astray. It is the firm rope of God (ḥabl Allāh al-matīn), His manifest light, the trustworthy handhold (al-ʿurwah al-wuthqā), and the most faithful refuge. It encompasses the little and the much, the small and the great. Its wonders do not come to an end, nor do its marvels reach a limit. No delimitation (taḥdīd) encompasses its benefits according to the people of knowledge, nor does the frequency of repetition wear it out according to the people of recitation. It is that which guided the first and the last. When the jinn heard it, they did not delay in turning to their people as warners, saying: {«فَقَالُوا إِنَّا سَمِعْنَا قُرْآنًا عَجَبًا * يَهْدِي إِلَى الرُّشْدِ فَآمَنَّا بِهِ وَلَنْ نُشْرِكَ بِرَبِّنَا أَحَدًا»} ("Indeed, we have heard a wondrous Quran; it guides to right conduct, so we have believed in it, and we will never associate anyone with our Lord.") So whoever believes in it has been granted success (tawfīq); whoever speaks by it has spoken truthfully; whoever clings to it has been guided; and whoever acts by it has attained felicity (fawz). And God, the Exalted, says: {«إِنَّا نَحْنُ نَزَّلْنَا الذِّكْرَ وَإِنَّا لَهُ لَحَافِظُونَ»} ("Indeed, We — it is We who have sent down the Remembrance, and indeed, We are its Preservers.") Among the means of its preservation (ḥifẓ) in hearts and in codices (maṣāḥif) is the constancy of its recitation (tilāwah) and perseverance in its study, along with the fulfillment of its etiquettes (ādāb) and conditions, and the safeguarding of what it contains of inward works (aʿmāl bāṭinah) and outward etiquettes (ādāb ẓāhirah). This cannot be done without its exposition and detailing; its aims unfold in four chapters (abwāb):
72:1.section_title_en: The Book of the Etiquettes of Quran Recitation — Section 220: The Excellence of the Quran and Its People
72:1.anchors:
- Root: نزل (n-z-l)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "نزل: انحطاط من علو إلى سفل" — descent from a height to a lower place; the setting down of a thing in a place.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "النزول في الأصل هو انحطاط من علو... وإنزال الله تعالى نعمه ونقمه على الخلق، وإعطاؤهم إياها" — the descent of the Quran is a divine act of sending down (tanzīl) from the highest station, carrying with it the very mercy and address of God.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Haqiqah (literal): "نزل من علو إلى سفل" — physical descent. Majaz (metaphorical): "وأنزل الله الغيث، وأنزل الكتاب" — the "sending down" of revelation is a metaphorical extension denoting divine bestowal and elevation of the recipient, not spatial movement.
- Root: حفظ (ḥ-f-ẓ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الحفظ: الحِراسة والاستظهار" — guarding, preserving, and keeping watch over a thing.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الحفظ: ضبط الشيء عن أن يذهب أو يضيع" — the securing of a thing against loss or corruption; divine preservation (ḥifẓ) is an act of sovereign care.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Haqiqah: guarding a physical object. Majaz: "حفظ الله فلانًا" — divine protection from spiritual harm and error.
- Root: تلو (t-l-w)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "التلاوة: الاتباع، ثم سميت القراءة تلاوة لأنها تتبع الآيات حرفًا حرفًا" — following in sequence; recitation is so named because the reader follows the verses letter by letter.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "التلاوة: الإتيان بالشيء متتابعًا" — the bringing of a thing in succession; recitation of the Quran is the sequential utterance of its verses in devotion.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Haqiqah: following behind. Majaz: "تلا الكتاب" — reciting, as the tongue follows the written text.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The rule governing the separation of a preposition from its object by an intervening clause, as in «لا يأتيه الباطل من بين يديه ولا من خلفه», where the prepositional phrases are distributed across the sentence for rhetorical emphasis and comprehensiveness.
72:1.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Etiquette of Quran Recitation'

3:28.arabic: القرآن والأخبار لا يحصى مثل قوله تعالى لا يتخذ المؤمنون الكافرين أولياء من دون المؤمنين وقال تعالى يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا تتخذوا اليهود والنصارى أولياء وقال تعالى وكذلك نولي بعض الظالمين بعضا وفي الخبر إن الله تعالى أخذ الميثاق على كل مؤمن أن يبغض كل منافق وعلى كل منافق أن يبغض كل مؤمن (3) وقال عليه السلام المرء مع من أحب (4) وقال من أحب قوما ووالاهم حشر معهم يوم القيامة (5) وقال عليه السلام أوثق عرى الإيمان الحب في الله والبغض في الله (6) وشواهد هذا قد ذكرناها في بيان الحب والبغض في الله تعالى من كتاب آداب الصحبة وفي كتاب الأمر
3:28.english: ...as a partner in his killing. And God—exalted be He—has commanded envy and competition in good things and the warding off of evils, for He said—exalted be He—{وَفِي ذَٰلِكَ فَلْيَتَنَافَسِ الْمُتَنَافِسُونَ} ["So for this let the competitors compete"] (Al-Muṭaffifīn 83:26). And the Prophet—peace be upon him—said: "There is no envy except in two: a man whom God has given wisdom, and he disseminates it among the people and teaches it; and a man whom God has given wealth, and he has been empowered over it to spend it in the truth." In another wording: "And a man whom God has given the Qur'an, and he stands with it through the hours of the night and the day; then a man says: 'If God had given me the like of what He gave this one, I would have done the like of what he does.'"
3:28.section_title_en: On the Reconciliation Between Hatred of Sinners and Satisfaction with Divine Decree — Section 1196
3:28.anchors:
- Root: بغض (b-gh-d)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root meaning of aversion, repugnance, and the soul's flight from what it disdains; al-baghḍā' as intense enmity.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "البغض: نفار النفس عن الشيء الذي ترغب عنه، وهو ضد الحب" — hatred is the soul's aversion from what it shuns, the exact opposite of love's attraction; used theologically for God's repudiation of the disobedient.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) usage denotes personal antipathy; metaphorical (majāz) extension applies to religiously mandated aversion (al-bughḍ fī Allāh) as an act of devotion, not private spite.
- Root: وجه (w-j-h)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The face as the foremost and noblest part; by extension, an aspect, direction, or respect under which a thing is considered.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "ولما كان الوجه أول ما يستقبلك، وأشرف ما في ظاهر البدن استعمل في مستقبل كل شيء" — the face is that which first confronts you, hence used for every aspect or angle of consideration.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the bodily face; metaphorical: "هذا وجه الثوب" (the face/right side of a garment) — i.e., a facet or dimension of a single act that may be evaluated differently.
- Root: كره (k-r-h)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Dislike, detestation, and unwillingness; karāhah as the soul's resistance to what befalls it.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Karāhah is the soul's repugnance toward something, distinguished from ridā (satisfaction) which is the soul's acquiescence and embrace.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): The rhetorical key here is that karāhah and ridā are contraries only when they "تواردا على شيء واحد من جهة واحدة" — converge on one thing from one single respect; from different respects, no contradiction arises.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — The resolution of the apparent contradiction hinges on precise restriction (taqyīd): the act is hated "من حيث إنه وصف العبد وكسبه" (insofar as it is the servant's attribute and acquisition) and loved "من حيث إنه مراد الله" (insofar as it is God's will and decree). The predicate is qualified by its aspect, eliminating the logical clash.
3:28.topic: Al-Ghazali on the journey of the soul, death, and the Hereafter, from 'Love, Longing, Intimacy and Contentment'

3:28.arabic: أكبر همه فليس من الله في شيء وألزم الله قلبه أربع خصال الحديث أخرجه الطبراني في الأوسط من حديث أبي ذر دون قوله وألزم الله قلبه وكذلك رواه ابن أبي الدنيا من حديث أنس بإسناد ضعيف والحاكم من حديث حذيفة وروي هذه الزيادة منفردة صاحب الفردوس من حديث ابن عمر وكلاهما ضعيف (5) حديث أبي هريرة ألا أريك الدنيا جميعها بما فيها قلت بلى يا رسول الله فأخذ بيدي وأتى بي واديا من أودية المدينة فإذا مزبلة الحديث لم أجد له أصلا // ويروى إن الله عز وجل لما أهبط آدم إلى الأرض قال له ابن للخراب
3:28.english: It has been related that the Messenger of God — may God's peace and blessings be upon him — passed by a dead sheep and said: "Do you see this sheep as contemptible to its owners?" They said: "It was due to its contemptibleness that they cast it away." He said: "By Him in whose hand is my soul, this world is more contemptible to God than this sheep is to its owners. And had this world weighed in God's sight the wing of a gnat, He would not have given a disbeliever from it a single drink of water." {«الدنيا سجن المؤمن وجنة الكافر»} (1)
3:28.section_title_en: The Verses and Reports Concerning the Blame of This World (Dhamm al-Dunyā)
3:28.anchors:
- Root: د ن ا (D-N-A)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The near, the lower, that which is immediate and proximate; the worldly abode as that which is "closest" in contrast to the Hereafter which is "farthest."
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الدنو: القرب بالذات، أو بالحكم" — proximity by essence or by judgment; the dunyā is so named for its temporal nearness, its inferior rank, and its being the "lesser" (adnā) in contrast to the greater and abiding.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): the nearest and lowest abode. Metaphorical (Majaz): the life of this world as a "dung-hill" (mazbalah) and a carcass — its worthlessness rendered sensibly perceptible.
- Root: ر س ل (R-S-L)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Sending forth with gentleness and ease; a messenger (rasūl) as one dispatched.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "أصل الرسل: الانبعاث على التؤدة" — the root is emission upon measured deliberation; the prophetic mission (risālah) as the sending of guidance to turn creation away from the dunyā toward the ākhirah.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: dispatch of a messenger with a message. Metaphorical: "أرسل الله عليهم العذاب" — the sending of punishment; here, the prophets were sent with the sole purpose of diverting hearts from the world.
- Root: ح د ث (H-D-TH)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Origination after non-existence; that which is new and temporal.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الحدوث: كون الشيء بعد أن لم يكن" — the world as muḥdath (originated/temporal), hence inherently perishable and contemptible before the Eternal.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: new occurrence. Metaphorical: "صاروا أحاديث" — becoming mere tales; the dunyā's ornaments become "rotten rags" and "withered bones."
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — The prophetic reports employ restrictive constructions (e.g., "The world is but a prison of the believer") to confine the dunyā's essence to a single defining attribute, negating all else.
3:28.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'Condemnation of the World'

4:87.arabic: الله تعالى لم ينظر إليها وتقول يوم القيامة يا رب اجعلني لأدنى أوليائك اليوم نصيبا فيقول اسكتي يا لا شيء إني لم أرضك لهم في الدنيا أرضاك لهم اليوم (1) وروي في أخبار آدم عليه السلام أنه لما أكل من الشجرة تحركت معدته لخروج الثقل ولم يكن ذلك مجعولا في شيء من أطعمة الجنة إلا في هذه الشجرة فلذلك نهيا عن أكلها قال فجعل يدور في الجنة فأمر الله تعالى ملكا يخاطبه فقال له قل له أي شيء تريد قال آدم أريد أن أضع ما في بطني من الأذى فقيل للملك قل له في أي مكان تريد أن تضعه أعلى الفرش أم على السرر أم على ا
4:87.english: It has been related that the Messenger of God — may God's peace and blessings be upon him — passed by a dead sheep and said: "Do you see this sheep as contemptible to its owners?" They said: "It was due to its contemptibleness that they cast it away." He said: "By Him in whose hand is my soul, this world is more contemptible to God than this sheep is to its owners. And had this world weighed in God's sight the wing of a gnat, He would not have given a disbeliever from it a single drink of water." {«الدنيا سجن المؤمن وجنة الكافر»} (1)
4:87.section_title_en: The Verses and Reports Concerning the Blame of This World (Dhamm al-Dunyā)
4:87.anchors:
- Root: د ن ا (D-N-A)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The near, the lower, that which is immediate and proximate; the worldly abode as that which is "closest" in contrast to the Hereafter which is "farthest."
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الدنو: القرب بالذات، أو بالحكم" — proximity by essence or by judgment; the dunyā is so named for its temporal nearness, its inferior rank, and its being the "lesser" (adnā) in contrast to the greater and abiding.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): the nearest and lowest abode. Metaphorical (Majaz): the life of this world as a "dung-hill" (mazbalah) and a carcass — its worthlessness rendered sensibly perceptible.
- Root: ر س ل (R-S-L)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Sending forth with gentleness and ease; a messenger (rasūl) as one dispatched.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "أصل الرسل: الانبعاث على التؤدة" — the root is emission upon measured deliberation; the prophetic mission (risālah) as the sending of guidance to turn creation away from the dunyā toward the ākhirah.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: dispatch of a messenger with a message. Metaphorical: "أرسل الله عليهم العذاب" — the sending of punishment; here, the prophets were sent with the sole purpose of diverting hearts from the world.
- Root: ح د ث (H-D-TH)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Origination after non-existence; that which is new and temporal.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الحدوث: كون الشيء بعد أن لم يكن" — the world as muḥdath (originated/temporal), hence inherently perishable and contemptible before the Eternal.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: new occurrence. Metaphorical: "صاروا أحاديث" — becoming mere tales; the dunyā's ornaments become "rotten rags" and "withered bones."
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — The prophetic reports employ restrictive constructions (e.g., "The world is but a prison of the believer") to confine the dunyā's essence to a single defining attribute, negating all else.
4:87.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Condemnation of the World'

10:94.arabic: بما يعرف به الإيمان البالغ فيكم فإن كنتم في شك مما جاء به محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم فائتونا لنبين لكم ولنريكم من النور ما تطمئن إليه قلوبكم والله ما أنتم بالمنقوصة عقولكم فنعذركم إنكم تستبينون صواب الرأي في دنياكم وتأخذون بالحزم في أموركم ما لكم تفرحون باليسير من الدنيا تصيبونه وتحزنون على اليسير منها يفوتكم حتى يتبين ذلك في وجوهكم ويظهر على ألسنتكم وتسمونها المصائب وتقيمون فيها المآتم وعامتكم قد تركوا كثيرا من دينهم ثم لا يتبين ذلك في وجوهكم ولا يتغير حالكم إني لأرى الله قد تبرأ منكم يلقى بعضكم
10:94.english: And lightning appeared one day, and he began seeking something to which he might take refuge. His eye fell upon a tent from afar, so he approached it — and behold, there was a woman within it. So he turned aside from her, and then there was a cave in a mountain. He came to it — and behold, there was a lion within it. So he placed his hand upon it and said: "My God, Thou hast made for every thing a refuge, and Thou hast made for me no refuge." Then God — exalted be He — revealed to him: "Thy refuge is in the resting place of My mercy. I shall surely wed thee on the Day of Resurrection to a hundred houris whom I created with My own hand, and I shall surely feed thee at thy wedding-feast for four thousand years — each day of which is like the age of this world — and I shall surely command a herald to proclaim: 'Where are the ascetics of the world? Come visit the wedding-feast of the ascetic of the world, Jesus son of Mary.'"
10:94.section_title_en: The Revival of the Religious Sciences — Book on the Remembrance of Death: On the Merit of Renouncing the World (Section 732)
10:94.anchors:
- Root: برق (b-r-q)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of shining, flashing, and appearing suddenly — from which "al-barq" (lightning) derives; also used for that which startles and alarms.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Used for sudden manifestation; here, the lightning serves as a natural sign prompting reflection on transience.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (haqiqah) for lightning; metaphorical (majaz) for the fleeting illumination of worldly life that vanishes instantly.
- Root: زهد (z-h-d)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To abstain from, to disdain, to regard as little; al-zuhd is the renunciation of something while it remains within one's power.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The theological virtue of renouncing the world (al-zuhd fi al-dunya) — not the mere abandonment of wealth, but the emptying of the heart from attachment to it.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: to turn away from a thing with aversion; metaphorical: the soul's disengagement from worldly allurements while the body remains present.
- Root: عرس (ʿ-r-s)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Wedding feast; the celebration of union; also used for the bridal chamber.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In the eschatological context, the "wedding" of the ascetic (al-zāhid) is a divine metaphor for the honor bestowed upon the renunciant in the Hereafter.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: a human marriage celebration; metaphorical: the spiritual recompense of intimacy with the Divine.
- Root: سخط (s-kh-t)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Displeasure, wrath, indignation; the opposite of ridā (satisfaction).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Divine displeasure (sakhat) as the cause of destruction; death by "wrath" (sakhtah) signifies a punishment visited upon a people for their disobedience.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: anger; metaphorical: the withdrawal of divine mercy and the sending of chastisement.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The permissibility of separating a prepositional phrase from its governed noun when the intervening element is semantically complete, as in the narrative transitions between reported speech and action.
10:94.topic: Al-Ghazali on the journey of the soul, death, and the Hereafter, from 'Condemnation of the World'

11:7.arabic: وخطب علي كرم الله وجهه يوما خطبة فقال فيها اعلموا أنكم ميتون ومبعوثون من بعد الموت وموقوفون على أعمالكم ومجزيون بها فلا تغرنكم الحياة الدنيا فإنها بالبلاء محفوفة وبالفناء معروفة وبالغدر موصوفة وكل ما فيها إلى زوال وهي بين أهلها دول وسجال لا تدوم أحوالها ولا يسلم من شرها نزالها بينا أهلها منها في رخاء وسرور إذا هم منها في بلاء وغرور أحوال مختلفة وتارات منصرفة العيش فيها مذموم والرخاء فيها لا يدوم وإنما أهلها فيها أغراض مستهدفة ترميهم بسهامها وتقصيهم بحمامها وكل حتفه فيها مقدور وحظه فيها موفور واعلموا عباد الله أنكم
11:7.english: And indeed there has come the narration from him, from his Lord, Mighty and Glorious, that He said to Moses, peace be upon him: "When you see the rich man approaching, say: 'A sin whose punishment has been hastened.' And when you see the poor man approaching, say: 'Welcome to the badge of the righteous.'" And if you wish, you may follow the possessor of the Spirit and the Word, Jesus son of Mary, peace be upon him — for he used to say: "My condiment is hunger, my badge is fear, my garment is wool, my warmth in winter is the rising places of the sun, my lamp is the moon, my mount is my two feet, and my food and my fruit is what the earth brings forth. I pass the night and I possess nothing, and I rise in the morning and I possess nothing — and there is no one upon the earth richer than I."
11:7.section_title_en: The Revival of the Religious Sciences — Section 737: On the Censure of This World and the Description of Its Perils
11:7.anchors:
- Root: دنو (danuww)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "دنا فهو دانٍ" — proximity, nearness; the world (al-dunyā) is so named because it is nearer and lower, deferred from the Hereafter.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الدنو: القرب بالذات، أو بالحكم" — proximity by essence or by decree; used of place, time, and station. The "nearer" (al-adnā) is contrasted with the greater and the better.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical nearness. Metaphorical: the lower, contemptible station — "أهل الدناءة هم أهل الشناءة" (the people of baseness are the people of abhorrence).
- Root: يوم (yawm)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "اليوم" — a day; also any period of time.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "اليوم يعبر به عن وقت طلوع الشمس إلى غروبها. وقد يعبر به عن مدة من الزمان أي مدة كانت" — the day is the time from sunrise to sunset, or any duration whatsoever. "وذكرهم بأيام الله" — the days of God are His mighty deeds and calamities upon the disbelievers.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the solar day. Metaphorical: "أيام العرب" — their battles and vicissitudes; "أيام الله" — His punitive visitations.
- Root: وقد (waqada)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "وقدت النار تقد وقودا ووقدا" — the fire blazed; al-wuqūd is the fuel.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "وقودها الناس والحجارة" — the fuel of the Fire is men and stones; the one who kindles it for himself (istawqada) is he who seeks its light.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: kindling a fire. Metaphorical: "قلب وقاد" — a blazing, keen heart; "وقد الحصى" — the pebbles became scorching hot (i.e., the intensity of the sun's heat).
- Root: ألك (alaka)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "المألكة: الرسالة، لأنها تؤلك في الفم" — the message (risālah) is called ma'lakah because it is chewed/worked in the mouth.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الملائكة تقع على الواحد والجمع" — angels (malā'ikah) are so named as bearers of messages; "الله يصطفي من الملائكة رسلا" {«الله يصطفي من الملائكة رسلا»} — God chooses messengers from the angels.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: chewing (as a horse chews its bit). Metaphorical: delivering a message — the angel is the one who delivers the divine communication.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — "إنما" restricts the predicate to the subject alone, negating it of all else. Applied in the sermon: "إنما يتزين لي أوليائي بالذل والخوف" — My friends adorn themselves for Me ONLY with humility, fear, and submission — restricting their adornment to these alone, excluding all worldly ornament.
11:7.topic: Al-Ghazali on purifying the character, moral diseases, and spiritual remedies, from 'Condemnation of the World'

17:108.arabic: لا إله إلا الله سبحان الله إن كان وعد ربنا لمفعولا قال فعجبت حين عرفني ولا والله ما رأيته قبل ذلك ولا رآني فقلت من أين عرفت اسمي واسم أبي وما رأيتك قبل اليوم قال نبأني العليم الخبير وعرفت روحي روحك حين كلمت نفسي نفسك إن الأرواح لها أنفس كأنفس الأجساد وإن المؤمنين ليعرف بعضهم بعضا ويتحابون بروح الله وإن لم يلتقوا يتعارفون ويتكلمون وإن نأت بهم الدار وتفرقت بهم المنازل قال قلت حدثني رحمك الله عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بحديث أسمعه منك قال إني لم أدرك رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ولم تكن لي م
17:108.english: And the gatherings of passion are five matters, which are what Allah, the Exalted, has gathered in His saying: {إنما الحياة الدنيا لعب ولهو وزينة وتفاخر بينكم وتكاثر في الأموال والأولاد} — "The life of this world is but play and diversion and adornment and boasting among yourselves and increase in wealth and children" (57:20). And the corporeal entities (al-aʿyān) from which these five are obtained are seven, gathered by His saying, the Exalted: {زين للناس حب الشهوات من النساء والبنين والقناطير المقنطرة من الذهب والفضة والخيل المسومة والأنعام والحرث ذلك متاع الحياة الدنيا} — "Adorned for mankind is the love of desires — of women and sons and heaped-up treasures of gold and silver and branded horses and cattle and tillage. That is the enjoyment of the life of this world" (3:14).
17:108.section_title_en: The Discipline of the Soul and the Restraint of the Passions — The Life of Uways al-Qarani and the True Boundary of the Worldly Life
17:108.anchors:
- Root: ن-ه-ي (N-H-Y)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "نهاه عنه نهياً: كفّه وردّه عنه. والنهي: خلاف الأمر."
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "النهي: الزجر عن الشيء، ويستعمل في الكفّ عن الفعل. قال تعالى: {ونهى النفس عن الهوى} — أي: كفّها وزجرها عن متابعة الشهوات."
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "نهاه عن كذا: كفّه. ومنه: انتهى عن الأمر إذا كفّ نفسه. والتناهي: التوقف عند الحد."
- Root: ه-و-ي (H-W-Y)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الهوى: ميل النفس إلى الشهوة. وهويته: أحببته. والهوى: ما تهواه النفس وتنزع إليه من غير هدى."
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الهوى: ميل النفس إلى ما تشتهيه، ويذمّ إذا لم يكن بعقل وشرع. قال تعالى: {أفرأيت من اتخذ إلهه هواه}."
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "هويته: أحببته. وهوًى: سقط. والهوى: اسم لما تهواه النفس من غير رشد. وقد غلب في الشرع على الميل المذموم."
- Root: د-ن-و (D-N-W)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "دنا يدنو دنواً: قرب. والدنيا: نقيض الآخرة، سميت بذلك لدنوّها وتقدّمها."
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الدنو: القرب بالذات أو بالحكم. والدنيا: الحياة العاجلة، سميت دنيا لدنوّها من الإنسان أو لتأخر الآخرة عنها."
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "الدنيا: الحاضرة العاجلة. وتقول: هو من أهل الدنيا إذا كان مقبلاً على شهواتها."
- Root: ن-ف-س (N-F-S)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "النفس: الروح، والذات. ونفس الشيء: عينه. والنفس: الدم. والنفيس: الثمين."
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "النفس: الروح، وتستعمل للذات. قال تعالى: {ويحذركم الله نفسه} أي: ذاته. وقد تكون النفس بمعنى الهوى والشهوة."
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "نفس الشيء: عينه وذاته. وأنفس الشيء: صار نفيساً. ومن المجاز: نفس عن كذا أي: فرّج عنه."
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين المبتدأ والخبر (Interposition between Subject and Predicate) — The periodic structure allows for extended parenthetical insertions between the subject and its predicate, as in the long narrative sequences here, where the subject (أويس) is introduced and its predicate follows after extensive descriptive clauses.
17:108.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications, prayers, and their spiritual power, from 'Condemnation of the World'

22:65.arabic: دعائه يا ممسك السماء أن تقع على الأرض إلا بإذنك أمسك الدنيا عني وقال محمد بن المنكدر أرأيت لو أن رجلا صام الدهر لا يفطر وقام الليل لا ينام وتصدق بماله وجاهد في سبيل الله واجتنب محارم الله غير أنه يؤتى به يوم القيامة فيقال إن هذا عظم في عينه ما صغره الله وصغر في عينه ما عظمه الله كيف ترى يكون حاله فمن منا ليس هكذا الدنيا عظيمة عنده مع ما اقترفنا من الذنوب والخطايا وقال أبو حازم اشتدت مؤنة الدنيا والآخرة فأما مؤنة الآخرة فإنك لا تجد عليها أعوانا وأما مؤنة الدنيا فإنك لا تضرب بيدك إلى شيء منها إ
22:65.english: Al-Hasan said: "By Allah, I have known people for whom the world was more insignificant than the dust upon which you walk. They cared not whether the world rose or set, whether it went to this one or to that one."
22:65.topic: Al-Ghazali on the journey of the soul, death, and the Hereafter, from 'Condemnation of the World'

33:38.arabic: ثبورا هذه صفتها وكان أمر الله قدرا مقدورا والصلاة والسلام على محمد عبده ورسوله المرسل إلى العالمين بشيرا ونذيرا وسراجا منيرا وعلى من كان من أهله وأصحابه له في الدين ظهيرا وعلى الظالمين نصيرا وسلم تسليما كثيرا أما بعد فإن الدنيا عدوة لله وعدوة لأولياء الله وعدوة لأعداء الله أما عداوتها لله فإنها قطعت الطريق على عباد الله ولذلك لم ينظر الله إليها منذ خلقها وأما عداوتها لأولياء الله عز وجل فإنه تزينت لهم بزينتها وعمتهم بزهرتها ونضارتها حتى تجرعوا مرارة الصبر في مقاطعتها وأما عداوتها لأعد
33:38.english: Praise be to God, who made His friends acquainted with the calamitous snares of this world and its afflictions, and uncovered for them its defects and its shameful parts, until they gazed upon its evidences and its signs, and weighed its evil deeds against its good deeds. Thus they came to know that its objectionable aspects exceed its commendable ones, that what is hoped from it does not fulfill what is feared from it, and that its rising is not safe from its eclipse. Yet it is in the likeness of a comely woman who draws people to herself by her beauty — while within her are hidden secrets of evil, ugly things that destroy those who yearn for union with her. Then she is a fleer from her seekers, niggardly in her turning toward them; and when she does turn, one is not secure from her evil and her pestilence. If she does good for an hour, she does evil for a year; and if she does evil once, she makes it her perpetual habit. So the cycles of her turning are ever more tightly drawn, and the commerce of her sons is losing and ruined, and her afflictions in succession strike the breasts of her seekers, and the courses of her states proclaim the humiliation of those who pursue her. Thus every one deluded by her is destined to abasement, and every one who waxes proud through her proceeds to regret. Her very nature is to flee from her seeker and to be sought by the one who flees from her. Whoever serves her, she eludes; whoever turns away from her, she comes to. Her clarity is never free of the admixture of turbidity, nor is her joy ever disentangled from what embitters it. Her soundness bequeaths sickness, her youth drives on to decrepitude, and her bliss bears no fruit but remorse and regret. She is deceitful, guileful, fleeting, evasive. She never ceases adorning herself for her seekers until, when they have become her lovers, she bares her fangs at them, disorders the ordered strands of their affairs, and uncovers for them the hidden store of her wonders — then she makes them taste the lethal poisons and strikes them with the piercing shafts of her arrows. While her companions are in joy and bounty from her, suddenly she turns away from them as though she were but scattered dreams; then she rushes upon them with her calamities, grinds them as grain is ground, and shrouds them in their winding-sheets beneath the dust. If she has possessed one of them with all that the sun has risen upon, she makes him as reaped harvest, as though he had not dwelt in plenty the day before. Her companions desire joy from her, and she promises them delusion — until they hope for much and build palaces, and then their palaces become graves, their gatherings become ruin, their striving becomes scattered dust, and their cry becomes "Woe and destruction!" Such is her description — and the command of God is a decree determined. And the prayer and peace be upon Muhammad, His servant and His Messenger, sent to the worlds as a bringer of glad tidings and a warner, and as an illuminating lamp; and upon those of his family and companions who were for him supporters in the religion, and against the wrongdoers helpers; and abundant peace.
33:38.section_title_en: The Book of Condemnation of This World — Being the Sixth Book of the Quarter of the Destructive Things from The Revival of the Religious Sciences
33:38.anchors:
- Root: لهم (l-h-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root meaning of swallowing, devouring, or ingesting wholly
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): الإلهام: casting something into the heart (al-rawʿ), specifically from God or the higher assembly; the root denotes the soul's complete reception, as one who swallows entirely
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: ألهمه الله الخير — God cast good into his heart. Metaphorical: جيش لهم — an army that engulfs and swallows whomever enters it
- Root: دنا (d-n-w)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Nearness in place, time, or rank; the world (al-dunyā) is so named because it is nearer and lower, deferred from the Hereafter
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): الدنو: proximity by essence or by judgment, used of place, time, and station; al-dunyā is the nearer, lower life
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: هو دانٍ — he is near. Metaphorical: الأدنى — the inferior, the baser, contrasted with what is better
- Root: حسر (ḥ-s-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Uncovering, stripping away a covering; exhaustion from exposure of one's strength
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): الحسر: uncovering what veils; al-ḥasīr: one whose strength is laid bare and spent; al-ḥāsir: the weary whose powers are uncovered as exhausted
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: حسر عن ذراعيه — he bared his forearms. Metaphorical: فلان كريم المحسر — so-and-so is noble when tested/examined (his hidden quality is uncovered)
- Root: سرر (s-r-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Concealment, the secret kept hidden in the breast; the innermost
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): الإسرار: opposite of declaration; al-sirr: the speech concealed in the soul
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: أسر الحديث — he concealed the speech. Metaphorical: أعطيتك سره — I gave you its choicest essence; هو في سر النسب — he is in the pure core of lineage
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The permissibility of interposing elements between a governing word and its governed prepositional phrase when the interposed element is complete in itself, as in the rhetorical suspensions of this oration
33:38.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications, prayers, and their spiritual power, from 'Condemnation of the World'

35:15.arabic: وخطب عمر بن عبد العزيز رحمه الله عليه فقال يا أيها الناس إنكم خلقتم لأمر إن كنتم تصدقون به فإنكم حمقى وإن كنتم تكذبون به فإنكم هلكى إنما خلقتم للأبد ولكنكم من دار إلى دار تنقلون عباد الله إنكم في دار لكم فيها من طعامكم غصص ومن شرابكم شرق لا تصفو لكم نعمة تسرون بها إلا بفراق أخرى تكرهون فراقها فاعملوا لما أنتم صائرون إليه وخالدون فيه ثم غلبه البكاء ونزل قال علي كرم الله وجهه في خطبته أوصيكم بتقوى الله والترك للدنيا التاركة لكم وإن كنتم لا تحبون تركها المبلية أجسامكم وأنتم تريدون تجديدها فإنما مثلكم ومثلها
35:15.english: And indeed there has come the narration from him, from his Lord, Mighty and Glorious, that He said to Moses, peace be upon him: "When you see the rich man approaching, say: 'A sin whose punishment has been hastened.' And when you see the poor man approaching, say: 'Welcome to the badge of the righteous.'" And if you wish, you may follow the possessor of the Spirit and the Word, Jesus son of Mary, peace be upon him — for he used to say: "My condiment is hunger, my badge is fear, my garment is wool, my warmth in winter is the rising places of the sun, my lamp is the moon, my mount is my two feet, and my food and my fruit is what the earth brings forth. I pass the night and I possess nothing, and I rise in the morning and I possess nothing — and there is no one upon the earth richer than I."
35:15.section_title_en: The Revival of the Religious Sciences — Section 737: On the Censure of This World and the Description of Its Perils
35:15.anchors:
- Root: دنو (danuww)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "دنا فهو دانٍ" — proximity, nearness; the world (al-dunyā) is so named because it is nearer and lower, deferred from the Hereafter.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الدنو: القرب بالذات، أو بالحكم" — proximity by essence or by decree; used of place, time, and station. The "nearer" (al-adnā) is contrasted with the greater and the better.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical nearness. Metaphorical: the lower, contemptible station — "أهل الدناءة هم أهل الشناءة" (the people of baseness are the people of abhorrence).
- Root: يوم (yawm)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "اليوم" — a day; also any period of time.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "اليوم يعبر به عن وقت طلوع الشمس إلى غروبها. وقد يعبر به عن مدة من الزمان أي مدة كانت" — the day is the time from sunrise to sunset, or any duration whatsoever. "وذكرهم بأيام الله" — the days of God are His mighty deeds and calamities upon the disbelievers.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the solar day. Metaphorical: "أيام العرب" — their battles and vicissitudes; "أيام الله" — His punitive visitations.
- Root: وقد (waqada)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "وقدت النار تقد وقودا ووقدا" — the fire blazed; al-wuqūd is the fuel.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "وقودها الناس والحجارة" — the fuel of the Fire is men and stones; the one who kindles it for himself (istawqada) is he who seeks its light.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: kindling a fire. Metaphorical: "قلب وقاد" — a blazing, keen heart; "وقد الحصى" — the pebbles became scorching hot (i.e., the intensity of the sun's heat).
- Root: ألك (alaka)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "المألكة: الرسالة، لأنها تؤلك في الفم" — the message (risālah) is called ma'lakah because it is chewed/worked in the mouth.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الملائكة تقع على الواحد والجمع" — angels (malā'ikah) are so named as bearers of messages; "الله يصطفي من الملائكة رسلا" {«الله يصطفي من الملائكة رسلا»} — God chooses messengers from the angels.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: chewing (as a horse chews its bit). Metaphorical: delivering a message — the angel is the one who delivers the divine communication.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — "إنما" restricts the predicate to the subject alone, negating it of all else. Applied in the sermon: "إنما يتزين لي أوليائي بالذل والخوف" — My friends adorn themselves for Me ONLY with humility, fear, and submission — restricting their adornment to these alone, excluding all worldly ornament.
35:15.topic: Al-Ghazali on purifying the character, moral diseases, and spiritual remedies, from 'Condemnation of the World'

35:35.arabic: عاملين بكتابة متبعين لأوليائه حتى يحلنا وإياكم دار المقامة من فضله إنه حميد مجيد وقال بعض الحكماء الأيام سهام والناس أغراض والدهر يرميك كل يوم بسهامه ويخترمك بلياليه وأيامه حتى يستغرق جميع أجزائك فكيف بقاء سلامتك مع وقوع الأيام بك وسرعة الليالي في بدنك لو كشف لك عما أحدثت الأيام فيك من النقص لاستوحشت من كل يوم يأتي عليك واستثقلت ممر الساعة بك ولكن تدبير الله فوق تدبير الاعتبار وبالسلو عن غوائل الدنيا وجد طعم لذاتها وإنها لأمر من العلقم إذا عجنها الحكيم وقد أعيت الواصف لعيوبها بظاهر أفعالها وما تأتي به من الع
35:35.english: And indeed there has come the narration from him, from his Lord, Mighty and Glorious, that He said to Moses, peace be upon him: "When you see the rich man approaching, say: 'A sin whose punishment has been hastened.' And when you see the poor man approaching, say: 'Welcome to the badge of the righteous.'" And if you wish, you may follow the possessor of the Spirit and the Word, Jesus son of Mary, peace be upon him — for he used to say: "My condiment is hunger, my badge is fear, my garment is wool, my warmth in winter is the rising places of the sun, my lamp is the moon, my mount is my two feet, and my food and my fruit is what the earth brings forth. I pass the night and I possess nothing, and I rise in the morning and I possess nothing — and there is no one upon the earth richer than I."

45:26.arabic: الله تعالى لم ينظر إليها وتقول يوم القيامة يا رب اجعلني لأدنى أوليائك اليوم نصيبا فيقول اسكتي يا لا شيء إني لم أرضك لهم في الدنيا أرضاك لهم اليوم (1) وروي في أخبار آدم عليه السلام أنه لما أكل من الشجرة تحركت معدته لخروج الثقل ولم يكن ذلك مجعولا في شيء من أطعمة الجنة إلا في هذه الشجرة فلذلك نهيا عن أكلها قال فجعل يدور في الجنة فأمر الله تعالى ملكا يخاطبه فقال له قل له أي شيء تريد قال آدم أريد أن أضع ما في بطني من الأذى فقيل للملك قل له في أي مكان تريد أن تضعه أعلى الفرش أم على السرر أم على ا
45:26.english: It has been related that the Messenger of God — may God's peace and blessings be upon him — passed by a dead sheep and said: "Do you see this sheep as contemptible to its owners?" They said: "It was due to its contemptibleness that they cast it away." He said: "By Him in whose hand is my soul, this world is more contemptible to God than this sheep is to its owners. And had this world weighed in God's sight the wing of a gnat, He would not have given a disbeliever from it a single drink of water." {«الدنيا سجن المؤمن وجنة الكافر»} (1)
45:26.section_title_en: The Verses and Reports Concerning the Blame of This World (Dhamm al-Dunyā)
45:26.anchors:
- Root: د ن ا (D-N-A)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The near, the lower, that which is immediate and proximate; the worldly abode as that which is "closest" in contrast to the Hereafter which is "farthest."
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الدنو: القرب بالذات، أو بالحكم" — proximity by essence or by judgment; the dunyā is so named for its temporal nearness, its inferior rank, and its being the "lesser" (adnā) in contrast to the greater and abiding.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): the nearest and lowest abode. Metaphorical (Majaz): the life of this world as a "dung-hill" (mazbalah) and a carcass — its worthlessness rendered sensibly perceptible.
- Root: ر س ل (R-S-L)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Sending forth with gentleness and ease; a messenger (rasūl) as one dispatched.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "أصل الرسل: الانبعاث على التؤدة" — the root is emission upon measured deliberation; the prophetic mission (risālah) as the sending of guidance to turn creation away from the dunyā toward the ākhirah.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: dispatch of a messenger with a message. Metaphorical: "أرسل الله عليهم العذاب" — the sending of punishment; here, the prophets were sent with the sole purpose of diverting hearts from the world.
- Root: ح د ث (H-D-TH)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Origination after non-existence; that which is new and temporal.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الحدوث: كون الشيء بعد أن لم يكن" — the world as muḥdath (originated/temporal), hence inherently perishable and contemptible before the Eternal.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: new occurrence. Metaphorical: "صاروا أحاديث" — becoming mere tales; the dunyā's ornaments become "rotten rags" and "withered bones."
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — The prophetic reports employ restrictive constructions (e.g., "The world is but a prison of the believer") to confine the dunyā's essence to a single defining attribute, negating all else.
45:26.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Condemnation of the World'

47:12.arabic: النسوان وجمع لذائذ الأطعمة يأكلون كما تأكل الأنعام ويظنون أنهم إذا نالوا ذلك فقد أدركوا غاية السعادة فشغلهم ذلك عن الله تعالى وعن اليوم الآخر وطائفة ظنوا أن السعادة في كثرة المال والاستغناء بكثرة الكنوز فأسهروا ليلهم وأتعبوا نهارهم في الجمع فهم يتعبون في الأسفار طول الليل والنهار ويترددون في الأعمال الشاقة ويكتسبون ويجمعون ولا يأكلون إلا قدر الضرورة شحا وبخلا عليها أن تنقص وهذه لذتهم وفي ذلك دأبهم وحركتهم إلى أن يدركهم الموت فيبقى تحت الأرض أو يظفر به من يأكله في الشهوات واللذات فيكون للجامع تعب
47:12.english: Another group supposed that happiness lies in a good name and the loosening of tongues in praise — through ostentation and manly virtue (murū'ah). These exhaust themselves in earning a livelihood and straiten themselves in food and drink, expending all their wealth upon fine garments and precious mounts, adorning the doorways of their houses and whatever falls under people's gaze — so that it may be said: "He is wealthy," and "He possesses riches" — supposing that this is happiness. So their aspiration, by day and by night, is the tending of the place where people's eyes fall.
47:12.section_title_en: The True Purpose of Food, Clothing, and Shelter — and the Deviation of the Errant Sects
47:12.anchors:
- Root: شغل (sh-gh-l)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Occupation, engagement, that which busies or diverts one
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): That which distracts and causes heedlessness (dhuhl) of the heart
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas - Haqiqah/Literal): "أنا في شغل شاغل" — being occupied with what diverts
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas - Majaz/Metaphorical): "دار مشغولة" — a house occupied by inhabitants; "مال مشغول" — wealth tied up in trade
- Root: نفس (n-f-s)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The self, the soul; that which desires and craves
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The soul as the seat of desire and passion (shahwah)
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas - Haqiqah/Literal): "شيء نفيس" — a precious thing; "نفس" as the essence of a thing
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas - Majaz/Metaphorical): "دفق نفسه" — to shed one's blood; the soul as that which is poured out in death
- Root: دنا (d-n-w)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Nearness, proximity; the nearer world (al-dunyā) as that which is close
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الدنو: القرب بالذات، أو بالحكم" — nearness by essence or by judgment; the lower world as the nearer abode
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas - Haqiqah/Literal): "هو دنيء من الأدنياء" — base and contemptible; the connection between the near world and baseness
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد (Restriction and Focused Predication) — The particle "إنما" restricts and confines the predicate to the subject alone, as in {«إِنَّمَا يَتَقَبَّلُ اللَّهُ مِنَ الْمُتَّقِينَ»}, establishing that acceptance is limited exclusively to the God-fearing.
47:12.topic: Al-Ghazali on purifying the character, moral diseases, and spiritual remedies, from 'Condemnation of the World'

66:3.arabic: رأيتك قبل اليوم قال نبأني العليم الخبير وعرفت روحي روحك حين كلمت نفسي نفسك إن الأرواح لها أنفس كأنفس الأجساد وإن المؤمنين ليعرف بعضهم بعضا ويتحابون بروح الله وإن لم يلتقوا يتعارفون ويتكلمون وإن نأت بهم الدار وتفرقت بهم المنازل قال قلت حدثني رحمك الله عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بحديث أسمعه منك قال إني لم أدرك رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ولم تكن لي معه صحبة بأبي وأمي رسول الله ولكن رأيت رجالا قد صحبوه وبلغني من حديثه كما بلغك ولست أحب أن أفتح على نفسي هذا الباب أن أكون محدثا أو
66:3.english: And the gatherings of passion are five matters, which are what Allah, the Exalted, has gathered in His saying: {إنما الحياة الدنيا لعب ولهو وزينة وتفاخر بينكم وتكاثر في الأموال والأولاد} — "The life of this world is but play and diversion and adornment and boasting among yourselves and increase in wealth and children" (57:20). And the corporeal entities (al-aʿyān) from which these five are obtained are seven, gathered by His saying, the Exalted: {زين للناس حب الشهوات من النساء والبنين والقناطير المقنطرة من الذهب والفضة والخيل المسومة والأنعام والحرث ذلك متاع الحياة الدنيا} — "Adorned for mankind is the love of desires — of women and sons and heaped-up treasures of gold and silver and branded horses and cattle and tillage. That is the enjoyment of the life of this world" (3:14).
66:3.section_title_en: The Discipline of the Soul and the Restraint of the Passions — The Life of Uways al-Qarani and the True Boundary of the Worldly Life
66:3.anchors:
- Root: ن-ه-ي (N-H-Y)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "نهاه عنه نهياً: كفّه وردّه عنه. والنهي: خلاف الأمر."
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "النهي: الزجر عن الشيء، ويستعمل في الكفّ عن الفعل. قال تعالى: {ونهى النفس عن الهوى} — أي: كفّها وزجرها عن متابعة الشهوات."
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "نهاه عن كذا: كفّه. ومنه: انتهى عن الأمر إذا كفّ نفسه. والتناهي: التوقف عند الحد."
- Root: ه-و-ي (H-W-Y)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الهوى: ميل النفس إلى الشهوة. وهويته: أحببته. والهوى: ما تهواه النفس وتنزع إليه من غير هدى."
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الهوى: ميل النفس إلى ما تشتهيه، ويذمّ إذا لم يكن بعقل وشرع. قال تعالى: {أفرأيت من اتخذ إلهه هواه}."
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "هويته: أحببته. وهوًى: سقط. والهوى: اسم لما تهواه النفس من غير رشد. وقد غلب في الشرع على الميل المذموم."
- Root: د-ن-و (D-N-W)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "دنا يدنو دنواً: قرب. والدنيا: نقيض الآخرة، سميت بذلك لدنوّها وتقدّمها."
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الدنو: القرب بالذات أو بالحكم. والدنيا: الحياة العاجلة، سميت دنيا لدنوّها من الإنسان أو لتأخر الآخرة عنها."
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "الدنيا: الحاضرة العاجلة. وتقول: هو من أهل الدنيا إذا كان مقبلاً على شهواتها."
- Root: ن-ف-س (N-F-S)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "النفس: الروح، والذات. ونفس الشيء: عينه. والنفس: الدم. والنفيس: الثمين."
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "النفس: الروح، وتستعمل للذات. قال تعالى: {ويحذركم الله نفسه} أي: ذاته. وقد تكون النفس بمعنى الهوى والشهوة."
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "نفس الشيء: عينه وذاته. وأنفس الشيء: صار نفيساً. ومن المجاز: نفس عن كذا أي: فرّج عنه."
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين المبتدأ والخبر (Interposition between Subject and Predicate) — The periodic structure allows for extended parenthetical insertions between the subject and its predicate, as in the long narrative sequences here, where the subject (أويس) is introduced and its predicate follows after extensive descriptive clauses.
66:3.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Condemnation of the World'

66:3.arabic: قال الله تعلى عرف بعضه وأعرض عن بعض وقال الجاحظ ما بقي من اللذات إلا ثلاث دم البخلاء وأكل القديد وحك الجرب وقال بشر بن الحارث البخيل لا غيبة له قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم إنك إذا لبخيل ومدحت امرأة عند رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فقالوا صوامة قوامة إلا أن فيها بخلا قال فما خيرها إذن // حديث مدحت امرأة عند النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فقالوا صوامة قوامة إلا أن فيها بخلا الحديث تقدم في آفات اللسان وقال بشر النظر إلى البخيل يقسي القلب ولقاء البخلاء كرب على قلوب المؤمنين وقال يحيى بن م
66:3.english: God—exalted be He—has said: {«وَمَن يُوقَ شُحَّ نَفْسِهِ فَأُولَٰئِكَ هُمُ الْمُفْلِحُونَ»} — "And whoever is saved from the miserliness of his own soul, it is those who are the successful" [Al-Hashr 59:9]. And He has said: {«وَأَمَّا مَن بَخِلَ وَاسْتَغْنَىٰ * فَسَنُيَسِّرُهُ لِلْعُسْرَىٰ»} — "And as for him who withholds and deems himself self-sufficient, We shall ease him toward hardship" [Al-Layl 92:8-9]. And the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: "Beware of miserliness, for it destroyed those before you. It commanded them to sever kinship ties, and they severed them; it commanded them to be miserly, and they were miserly; and it commanded them to commit wickedness, and they committed it."
66:3.book_title: Condemnation of Miserliness and Love of Wealth
66:3.section_title_en: Exposition of the Blameworthiness of Miserliness (Bayān Dhamm al-Bukhl)
66:3.anchors:
- Root: بخل (B-Kh-L)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning is withholding/restraining what one possesses from that which it is not lawful to withhold; al-Khalil notes the intensive form 'bakhīl' denotes one in whom miserliness is a dominant trait.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "البخل: إمساك المقتنيات عما لا يحق حبسها عنه" — miserliness is the withholding of possessions from that which it is not right to withhold; it is of two kinds: withholding one's own goods, and withholding what belongs to others (commanding others to be miserly), the latter being the more blameworthy, as in {«الذين يبخلون ويأمرون الناس بالبخل»} [Al-Nisa 4:37].
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (haqīqah): "فلان لم يبخل" — he did not act miserly. Metaphorical (majāz): "إذا السماء بخلت بالفطر" — the sky withheld its rain, extending the root to non-human agency.
- Root: قتل (Q-T-L) [as in 'qarama' — intense craving, related to being consumed by desire]
  * Lisan / Ayn: The root denotes intense longing that overcomes restraint; used here to describe Marwan's overpowering desire for meat after prolonged abstinence.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Interposition (al-Faṣl bayna al-Jār wa al-Majrūr) — governing the permissible separation between a preposition and its object for rhetorical emphasis, as in the construction "لقد صغر فلان في عيني" where the prepositional phrase is fronted for focus.
66:3.topic: Al-Ghazali on purifying the character, moral diseases, and spiritual remedies, from 'Condemnation of Miserliness and Love of Wealth'

100:10.arabic: الأمور وبعثرت القبور وحصل ما في الصدور وأوقفتم للتحصيل بين يدي الملك الجليل فطارت القلوب لإشفاقها من سالف الذنوب وهتكت عنكم الحجب والأستار وظهرت منكم العيوب والأسرار هنالك تجزى كل نفس بما كسبت إن الله عز وجل يقول ليجزى الذي أساءوا بما عملوا ويجزى الذي أحسنوا بالحسنى وقال تعالى {ووضع الكتاب فترى المجرمين مشفقين مما فيه} الآية جعلنا الله وإياكم عاملين بكتابة متبعين لأوليائه حتى يحلنا وإياكم دار المقامة من فضله إنه حميد مجيد وقال بعض الحكماء الأيام سهام والناس أغراض والدهر يرميك كل يوم
100:10.english: And indeed there has come the narration from him, from his Lord, Mighty and Glorious, that He said to Moses, peace be upon him: "When you see the rich man approaching, say: 'A sin whose punishment has been hastened.' And when you see the poor man approaching, say: 'Welcome to the badge of the righteous.'" And if you wish, you may follow the possessor of the Spirit and the Word, Jesus son of Mary, peace be upon him — for he used to say: "My condiment is hunger, my badge is fear, my garment is wool, my warmth in winter is the rising places of the sun, my lamp is the moon, my mount is my two feet, and my food and my fruit is what the earth brings forth. I pass the night and I possess nothing, and I rise in the morning and I possess nothing — and there is no one upon the earth richer than I."
100:10.section_title_en: The Revival of the Religious Sciences — Section 737: On the Censure of This World and the Description of Its Perils
100:10.anchors:
- Root: دنو (danuww)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "دنا فهو دانٍ" — proximity, nearness; the world (al-dunyā) is so named because it is nearer and lower, deferred from the Hereafter.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الدنو: القرب بالذات، أو بالحكم" — proximity by essence or by decree; used of place, time, and station. The "nearer" (al-adnā) is contrasted with the greater and the better.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical nearness. Metaphorical: the lower, contemptible station — "أهل الدناءة هم أهل الشناءة" (the people of baseness are the people of abhorrence).
- Root: يوم (yawm)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "اليوم" — a day; also any period of time.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "اليوم يعبر به عن وقت طلوع الشمس إلى غروبها. وقد يعبر به عن مدة من الزمان أي مدة كانت" — the day is the time from sunrise to sunset, or any duration whatsoever. "وذكرهم بأيام الله" — the days of God are His mighty deeds and calamities upon the disbelievers.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the solar day. Metaphorical: "أيام العرب" — their battles and vicissitudes; "أيام الله" — His punitive visitations.
- Root: وقد (waqada)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "وقدت النار تقد وقودا ووقدا" — the fire blazed; al-wuqūd is the fuel.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "وقودها الناس والحجارة" — the fuel of the Fire is men and stones; the one who kindles it for himself (istawqada) is he who seeks its light.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: kindling a fire. Metaphorical: "قلب وقاد" — a blazing, keen heart; "وقد الحصى" — the pebbles became scorching hot (i.e., the intensity of the sun's heat).
- Root: ألك (alaka)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "المألكة: الرسالة، لأنها تؤلك في الفم" — the message (risālah) is called ma'lakah because it is chewed/worked in the mouth.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الملائكة تقع على الواحد والجمع" — angels (malā'ikah) are so named as bearers of messages; "الله يصطفي من الملائكة رسلا" {«الله يصطفي من الملائكة رسلا»} — God chooses messengers from the angels.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: chewing (as a horse chews its bit). Metaphorical: delivering a message — the angel is the one who delivers the divine communication.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — "إنما" restricts the predicate to the subject alone, negating it of all else. Applied in the sermon: "إنما يتزين لي أوليائي بالذل والخوف" — My friends adorn themselves for Me ONLY with humility, fear, and submission — restricting their adornment to these alone, excluding all worldly ornament.

2:162.arabic: الدنيا بالآخرة فلا يخفف عنهم العذاب ولا هم ينصرون وإذا عظمت غوائل الدنيا وشرورها فلا بد أولا من معرفة حقيقة الدنيا وما هي وما الحكمة في خلقها مع عداوتها وما مدخل غرورها وشرورها فإن من لا يعرف الشر لا يتقيه ويوشك أن يقع فيه ونحن نذكر ذم الدنيا وأمثلتها وحقيقتها وتفصيل معانيها وأصناف الأشغال المتعلقة بها ووجه الحاجة إلى أصولها وسبب انصراف الخلق عن الله بسبب التشاغل بفضولها إن شاء الله تعالى وهو المعين على ما يرتضيه
2:162.english: Praise be to God, who made His friends acquainted with the calamitous snares of this world and its afflictions, and uncovered for them its defects and its shameful parts, until they gazed upon its evidences and its signs, and weighed its evil deeds against its good deeds. Thus they came to know that its objectionable aspects exceed its commendable ones, that what is hoped from it does not fulfill what is feared from it, and that its rising is not safe from its eclipse. Yet it is in the likeness of a comely woman who draws people to herself by her beauty — while within her are hidden secrets of evil, ugly things that destroy those who yearn for union with her. Then she is a fleer from her seekers, niggardly in her turning toward them; and when she does turn, one is not secure from her evil and her pestilence. If she does good for an hour, she does evil for a year; and if she does evil once, she makes it her perpetual habit. So the cycles of her turning are ever more tightly drawn, and the commerce of her sons is losing and ruined, and her afflictions in succession strike the breasts of her seekers, and the courses of her states proclaim the humiliation of those who pursue her. Thus every one deluded by her is destined to abasement, and every one who waxes proud through her proceeds to regret. Her very nature is to flee from her seeker and to be sought by the one who flees from her. Whoever serves her, she eludes; whoever turns away from her, she comes to. Her clarity is never free of the admixture of turbidity, nor is her joy ever disentangled from what embitters it. Her soundness bequeaths sickness, her youth drives on to decrepitude, and her bliss bears no fruit but remorse and regret. She is deceitful, guileful, fleeting, evasive. She never ceases adorning herself for her seekers until, when they have become her lovers, she bares her fangs at them, disorders the ordered strands of their affairs, and uncovers for them the hidden store of her wonders — then she makes them taste the lethal poisons and strikes them with the piercing shafts of her arrows. While her companions are in joy and bounty from her, suddenly she turns away from them as though she were but scattered dreams; then she rushes upon them with her calamities, grinds them as grain is ground, and shrouds them in their winding-sheets beneath the dust. If she has possessed one of them with all that the sun has risen upon, she makes him as reaped harvest, as though he had not dwelt in plenty the day before. Her companions desire joy from her, and she promises them delusion — until they hope for much and build palaces, and then their palaces become graves, their gatherings become ruin, their striving becomes scattered dust, and their cry becomes "Woe and destruction!" Such is her description — and the command of God is a decree determined. And the prayer and peace be upon Muhammad, His servant and His Messenger, sent to the worlds as a bringer of glad tidings and a warner, and as an illuminating lamp; and upon those of his family and companions who were for him supporters in the religion, and against the wrongdoers helpers; and abundant peace.
2:162.section_title_en: The Book of Condemnation of This World — Being the Sixth Book of the Quarter of the Destructive Things from The Revival of the Religious Sciences
2:162.anchors:
- Root: لهم (l-h-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root meaning of swallowing, devouring, or ingesting wholly
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): الإلهام: casting something into the heart (al-rawʿ), specifically from God or the higher assembly; the root denotes the soul's complete reception, as one who swallows entirely
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: ألهمه الله الخير — God cast good into his heart. Metaphorical: جيش لهم — an army that engulfs and swallows whomever enters it
- Root: دنا (d-n-w)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Nearness in place, time, or rank; the world (al-dunyā) is so named because it is nearer and lower, deferred from the Hereafter
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): الدنو: proximity by essence or by judgment, used of place, time, and station; al-dunyā is the nearer, lower life
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: هو دانٍ — he is near. Metaphorical: الأدنى — the inferior, the baser, contrasted with what is better
- Root: حسر (ḥ-s-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Uncovering, stripping away a covering; exhaustion from exposure of one's strength
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): الحسر: uncovering what veils; al-ḥasīr: one whose strength is laid bare and spent; al-ḥāsir: the weary whose powers are uncovered as exhausted
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: حسر عن ذراعيه — he bared his forearms. Metaphorical: فلان كريم المحسر — so-and-so is noble when tested/examined (his hidden quality is uncovered)
- Root: سرر (s-r-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Concealment, the secret kept hidden in the breast; the innermost
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): الإسرار: opposite of declaration; al-sirr: the speech concealed in the soul
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: أسر الحديث — he concealed the speech. Metaphorical: أعطيتك سره — I gave you its choicest essence; هو في سر النسب — he is in the pure core of lineage
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The permissibility of interposing elements between a governing word and its governed prepositional phrase when the interposed element is complete in itself, as in the rhetorical suspensions of this oration
2:162.topic: Al-Ghazali on the journey of the soul, death, and the Hereafter, from 'Condemnation of Status and Ostentation'

2:204.arabic: {ومن الناس من يعجبك قوله في الحياة الدنيا ويشهد الله على ما في قلبه وهو ألد الخصام وإذا تولى سعى في الأرض ليفسد فيها} الآية وقال تعالى {وإذا لقوكم قالوا آمنا وإذا خلوا عضوا عليكم الأنامل من الغيظ} وقال تعالى {يراؤون الناس ولا يذكرون الله إلا قليلا مذبذبين بين ذلك} والآيات فيهم كثيرة وكان النفاق يكثر في ابتداء الإسلام ممن يدخل في ظاهر الإسلام ابتداء لغرض وذلك مما يقل في زماننا ولكن يكثر نفاق من ينسل عن الدين باطنا فيجحد الجنة والنار والدار الآخرة ميلا إلى قول الملحدة أو يعتقد على بساط الشرع والأحكام ميلا إلى أهل الإباحة أو يعتقد كفرا أو بدعة وهو يظهر خلافه فهؤلا
2:204.english: The fourth [case]: that the people's seeing him should be a weighty factor (murajjihan) and a strengthener of his vigor, such that were it not for that, he would not abandon the act of worship; and were the intention of ostentation alone [present], he would not have ventured upon it. So what we hold — and knowledge is with God — is that it does not annul the root of the reward, but rather it diminishes it; or he is punished to the measure of his intention of ostentation and rewarded to the measure of his intention of reward. As for his saying — may God's peace and blessings be upon him — that God the Exalted says: "I am the most Self-Sufficient of the self-sufficient, free of all need for partnership (shirk)" — that is carried upon the case when the two intentions are equal, or when the intention of ostentation is the weightier.
2:204.section_title_en: On the Degrees of Ostentation in Worship — The Second Pillar: That by Which One Ostentatiously Displays (Al-Riya' bi al-Ta'at)
2:204.anchors:
- Root: قصد (Qasada)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of "intending, aiming toward a goal, directing one's purpose."
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "القصد: استقامة الطريق" — intention as the straight path of the soul toward its object; in moral theology, it denotes the deliberate orientation of the will that determines the moral value of an act.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): "قصدته وقصدت له" — direct aiming. Metaphorical (Majaz): "قصد في الأمر إذا لم يجاوز فيه الحد" — moderation; here, the "intention" (qasd) is the precise measure by which an act is weighed between reward and punishment.
- Root: راءى (Ra'a) — from Root: رأى (Ra'a)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الرياء: إظهار العمل ليراه الناس" — showing one's deed so that people may see it; derived from الرؤية (sight/seeing).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Riya' is a branch of shirk (associating partners with God), for the actor directs his deed not to God alone but to the gaze of creatures, thus dividing his intention between the Creator and creation.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: seeing with the eye. Metaphorical: "راءى فلان" — to perform an act for the sake of being seen, i.e., seeking the approval of onlookers rather than the sight of God.
- Root: خلق (Khalaqa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الخلق: التقدير المستقيم" — measuring and proportioning; also "خلق الثوب" — wearing out a garment until it is threadbare.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الخلق أصله: التقدير المستقيم" — creation as precise estimation; in moral context, the "خلق" (character) is the inward measure by which a soul is formed.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "خلق الخراز الأديم" — the leather-worker cutting and measuring hide. Metaphorical: "خلق الله الخلق: أوجده على تقدير أوجبته الحكمة" — God's creation of creatures upon a measure required by wisdom; here, the "creatures" (الخلق) whose blame (المقت) is feared by the ostentatious worshipper.
- Root: نفق (Nafaqa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "نفق الشيء: مضى ونفد" — to pass away, to be spent, to perish.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "نفق الشيء: مضى ونفد، ينفق، إما بالبيع نحو: نفق البيع نفاقا" — to find a ready market; "ومنها نفاق الأيم" — hypocrisy as the "passing" of a false coin in the market of religion.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "نفقت الدراهم" — coins circulating and being spent. Metaphorical: "نافق" — the hypocrite (munafiq) whose outward faith circulates among people while his inward disbelief is void; the ostentatious man "spends" his deeds on the market of human praise.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The syntactic separation between a governing preposition and its object, as in "له من الثواب مثل ما عليه من العقاب," where the prepositional phrases are interposed to balance two opposing clauses, mirroring the theological weighing of reward against punishment.
2:204.topic: Al-Ghazali on the journey of the soul, death, and the Hereafter, from 'Condemnation of Status and Ostentation'

3:9.arabic: ولميله إليه وغير محبب إليه فهل يكون في زمرة المرائين فاعلم أن الله لم يكلف العباد إلا ما تطيق وليس في طاقة العبد منع الشيطان عن نزغاته ولا قمع الطبع حتى لا يميل إلى الشهوات ولا ينزع إليها وإنما غايته أن يقابل شهوته بكراهة استثمارها من معرفة العواقب وعلم الدين وأصول الإيمان بالله واليوم الآخر فإذا فعل ذلك فهو الغاية في أداء ما كلف به ويدل على ذلك من الأخبار ما روي أن أصحاب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم شكوا إليه وقالوا تعرض لقلوبنا أشياء لأن تخر من السماء فتخطفنا الطير أو تهوي بنا الريح في مكان سحيق أحب إلينا من أن نتكلم ب
3:9.english: If you say: "Whoever finds in himself a dislike of ostentation (riyā'), and this dislike compels him to refuse it, yet he is not entirely free from the soul's inclination toward it, its love for it, and its striving after it — except that he dislikes his own love and his own inclination, and it is not beloved to him — is he then among the ranks of the ostentatious?" — Know that God has not burdened His servants except with what they can bear. It is not within the servant's power to prevent the Devil from his incitements (nazaghāt), nor to suppress nature entirely so that it neither inclines to lusts nor strives after them. His utmost limit is only that he confront his lust with a dislike born of his knowledge of consequences, his understanding of religion, and his roots of faith in God and the Last Day. When he does this, he has reached the utmost limit of performing what he has been charged with.
3:9.section_title_en: On the Degrees of Resistance to Ostentation and the Devil's Wiles — Section 829
3:9.anchors:
- Root: شيط (Shayṭ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of burning, scorching, or spoiling by fire; the Devil as that which burns and destroys.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): الشيطان as the one who leads astray and incites; his "نزغات" (incitements) are his piercing stings of temptation.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "شاط اللحم" (meat scorched/ruined). Metaphorical: "أشاط دمه" (shed his blood vainly) — the Devil's aim is to ruin the soul's deeds.
- Root: كره (K-R-H)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Dislike, aversion, abhorrence; the opposite of love (ḥubb) and desire (mīl).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The moral faculty of repulsion against sin; a trait of faith (īmān) distinguishing the believer's higher self from the lower nature.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "كرهت الشيء" (I disliked it). Metaphorical: The heart's rejection of the soul's base inclinations as an act of worship.
- Root: نفس (Nafs)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The self, soul, or spirit; the seat of desires and passions.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): النفس as the lower commanding soul (النفس الأمارة) that inclines to lusts, distinct from the intellect (عقل) and faith.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "نفس سائلة" (flowing blood/life). Metaphorical: The inner self that must be opposed when it inclines to ostentation.
- Root: جهد (J-H-D) / مجادلة (Jadal)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Striving, exertion, argumentation; from جدل (twisting ropes tightly).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): المجادلة as disputation that can distract from divine remembrance (ذكر الله).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "جادله" (he argued with him). Metaphorical: The soul's engagement with the Devil's whispers as a subtle trap, diverting from sincere worship.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — Used to delimit the four ranks of resistance, each defined by what it exclusively does or omits.
3:9.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Condemnation of Status and Ostentation'

- Root: لهم (l-h-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root meaning of swallowing, devouring, or ingesting wholly
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): الإلهام: casting something into the heart (al-rawʿ), specifically from God or the higher assembly; the root denotes the soul's complete reception, as one who swallows entirely
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: ألهمه الله الخير — God cast good into his heart. Metaphorical: جيش لهم — an army that engulfs and swallows whomever enters it
- Root: دنا (d-n-w)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Nearness in place, time, or rank; the world (al-dunyā) is so named because it is nearer and lower, deferred from the Hereafter
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): الدنو: proximity by essence or by judgment, used of place, time, and station; al-dunyā is the nearer, lower life
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: هو دانٍ — he is near. Metaphorical: الأدنى — the inferior, the baser, contrasted with what is better
- Root: حسر (ḥ-s-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Uncovering, stripping away a covering; exhaustion from exposure of one's strength
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): الحسر: uncovering what veils; al-ḥasīr: one whose strength is laid bare and spent; al-ḥāsir: the weary whose powers are uncovered as exhausted
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: حسر عن ذراعيه — he bared his forearms. Metaphorical: فلان كريم المحسر — so-and-so is noble when tested/examined (his hidden quality is uncovered)
- Root: سرر (s-r-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Concealment, the secret kept hidden in the breast; the innermost
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): الإسرار: opposite of declaration; al-sirr: the speech concealed in the soul
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: أسر الحديث — he concealed the speech. Metaphorical: أعطيتك سره — I gave you its choicest essence; هو في سر النسب — he is in the pure core of lineage
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The permissibility of interposing elements between a governing word and its governed prepositional phrase when the interposed element is complete in itself, as in the rhetorical suspensions of this oration
