7:27.arabic: منه جميع الخلق فقال الله تعالى يا بني آدم لا يفتننكم الشيطان كما أخرج أبويكم من الجنة وقال عز وجل إنه يراكم هو وقبيله من حيث لا ترونهم والقرآن من أوله إلى آخره تحذير من الشيطان فكيف يدع الأمن منه وأخذ الحذر من حيث أمر الله به لا ينافي الاشتغال بحب الله فإن من الحب له امتثال أمره وقد أمر بالحذر من العدو كما أمر بالحذر من الكفار فقال تعالى وليأخذوا حذرهم وأسلحتهم وقال تعالى وأعدوا لهم ما استطعتم من قوة ومن رباط الخيل فإذا لزمك بأمر الله الحذر من العدو الكافر وأنت تراه فبأن يلزمك الحذر من عدو يراك ولا تراه أولى ولذلك قال ابن محيريز صي
7:27.english: ...and the world, which is the source of trials and tribulations, the mine of forbidden pleasures and lusts. And Moses, peace be upon him, said—as God Most High has related concerning him—{«هذا من عمل الشيطان»} ("This is of Satan's doing" — Qur'an 28:15). For this reason, God warned all of creation against him, saying: {«يا بني آدم لا يفتننكم الشيطان كما أخرج أبويكم من الجنة»} ("O children of Adam, let not Satan tempt you as he brought your parents out of Paradise" — Qur'an 7:27). And He, Glorified and Exalted, said: {«إنه يراكم هو وقبيله من حيث لا ترونهم»} ("Indeed, he sees you, he and his tribe, from where you do not see them" — Qur'an 7:27). The Qur'an, from its beginning to its end, is a warning against Satan. So how could one claim security from him? And taking precaution against him, in the manner God has commanded, does not contradict occupation with the love of God. For part of loving Him is obeying His command. He has commanded vigilance against the enemy just as He commanded vigilance against the disbelievers, saying: {«وليعأخذوا حذرهم وأسلحتهم»} ("And let them take their precautions and their weapons" — Qur'an 4:102), and saying: {«وأعدوا لهم ما استطعتم من قوة ومن رباط الخيل»} ("And prepare against them whatever you are able of power and of steeds of war" — Qur'an 8:60). So if, by God's command, you are obligated to be wary of a disbelieving enemy whom you can see, then it is all the more fitting that you be obligated to be wary of an enemy who sees you while you do not see him.
7:27.section_title_en: On the Necessity of Vigilance Against Satan and Its Harmony with Trust in God and Remembrance of Him
7:27.anchors:
- Root: شيط (Shayṭ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root denotes burning, scorching, or spoiling (as meat over a fire), and by extension, perishing or being ruined.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الشيطان" (Satan) is derived from this root, signifying one who is burned, ruined, or cast away from mercy—the archetype of the adversary who destroys through temptation.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): "شاط دمه" — his blood went in vain (was wasted). Metaphorical (Majaz): "أشاط السلطان دمه" — the ruler declared his blood permissible (wasted). Thus, Satan is the one who causes spiritual ruin and waste.
- Root: حذر (Ḥadhar)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Caution, wariness, and taking precautions against a feared harm.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الحذر: احتراز من مخيف" — vigilance is a protective withdrawal from what is frightening. It is a commanded state, as in {«خذوا حذركم»} (Take your precautions — Qur'an 4:71).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "حذرته وحاذرته" — I was wary of him. Metaphorical: "حذار من أرماحنا حذار" — a poetic imperative to beware. Vigilance is both a physical and spiritual act of self-preservation.
- Root: قلب (Qalb)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To turn, overturn, or flip something from one state to another.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "قلب الشيء: تصريفه وصرفه عن وجه إلى وجه" — the heart (qalb) is so named for its constant turning and fluctuation between states.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "قلب الشيء قلبا: حوله عن وجهه" — to turn a thing from its face. Metaphorical: "رجل قلب حول: يقلب الأمور ويحتال" — a man who turns matters over and devises stratagems. The heart's occupation is decisive: it turns either toward God or toward the enemy.
- Root: وكل (Wakal)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To entrust, delegate, or rely upon another.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "التوكيل: أن تعتمد على غيرك وتجعله نائبا عنك" — trust (tawakkul) is reliance upon another as your deputy. God says: {«وكفى بالله وكيلا»} (And sufficient is Allah as Disposer of affairs — Qur'an 4:81).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "وكل إليه الأمر" — he delegated the matter to him. Metaphorical: "فلان وكل" — a weak man who leans on others. True tawakkul does not negate taking means; it purifies the heart's reliance.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد (Restriction & Focused Predication) — The particle "إنما" and restrictive constructions (e.g., "ليس ... إلا") are used to delimit predicates, as in the author's argument that vigilance is not a contradiction of love or trust but a fulfillment of the divine command.

10:58.arabic: تعالى {قل بفضل الله وبرحمته فبذلك فليفرحوا} فكأنه ظهر له أنه عند الله مقبول ففرح به الثاني أن يستدل بإظهار الله الجميل وستره القبيح عليه في الدنيا أنه كذلك يفعل في الآخرة إذ قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ما ستر الله على عبد ذنبا في الدنيا إلا ستره عليه في الآخرة (1) حديث قال لرجل قال صمت الدهر قال ما صمت ولا أفطرت أخرجه مسلم من حديث أبي قتادة قال عمر يا رسول الله كيف بمن يصوم الدهر قال لا صام ولا أفطر وللطبراني من حديث أسماء بنت يزيد في أثناء حديث فيه فقال رجل إني صائم قال بعض القوم إ
10:58.english: I say: The knowledgeable servant knows that God has made them aware and has manifested the beautiful aspects of their states, so that they may infer thereby the excellence of God's crafting of them, His regard for them, and His gracious kindness (luṭf) toward them — for He conceals both obedience and disobedience, then God conceals the disobedience and manifests the obedience. And there is no grace greater than concealing the ugly and manifesting the beautiful. Thus their joy is in the beauty of God's regard for them, not in the praise of people nor in the standing it procures in their hearts. God Most High has said: {Say: "In the bounty of God and His mercy — in that let them rejoice"} (Yūnus 10:58). It is as though it has become manifest to them that they are accepted before God, so they rejoice in that.
10:58.section_title_en: On the Sudden Intrusion of Ostentation (Riya') After the Intention of Worship — Its Rulings Before and After Completion
10:58.anchors:
- Root: ستر (s-t-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To cover, conceal, screen; the act of veiling something from perception.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Divine covering (satr) as an act of divine grace (luṭf) — concealing sin and manifesting obedience is a form of divine favor that draws the servant toward gratitude, not toward pride.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): physical covering. Metaphorical (majāz): God's veiling of faults in this world and the next, as in the prophetic tradition cited.
- Root: حبط (ḥ-b-ṭ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To become void, nullified, fruitless — said of deeds whose reward is rendered null.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Iḥbāṭ in the Quran denotes the nullification of a deed's reward due to a corrupting intention or action, particularly kufr or riyā'.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: a beast dying from overeating (inflating and perishing). Metaphorical: a deed perishing internally despite its outward form.
- Root: خطر (kh-ṭ-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To cross the mind; a passing thought (khaṭarah).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The sudden occurrence of an idea in the heart without deliberate acquisition — distinguished from firm resolve ('azm).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: something that comes and goes. Metaphorical: the fleeting incursion of ostentation into worship.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — Used to delimit the scope of riyā' rulings: e.g., "إنما قال ذلك لأنه أظهره" restricts the Prophet's rebuke to the case of publicized fasting, not the act itself.
10:58.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'Condemnation of Status and Ostentation'

11:15.arabic: وغبن خسرانا عظيما وقال عز وجل من كان يريد الحياة الدنيا وزينتها الآية وقال تعالى إن الإنسان ليطغى أن رآه استغنى فلا حول ولا قوة إلا بالله العلي العظيم وقال تعالى ألهاكم التكاثر وقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم حب المال والشرف ينبتان النفاق في القلب كما ينبت الماء البقل (1) وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم ما ذئبان ضاريان أرسلا في زريبة غنم بأكثر إفسادا فيها من حب الشرف والمال والجاه في دين الرجل المسلم (2) وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم هلك المكثرون إلا من قال به في عباد الله هكذا وهكذا وقليل ما هم (3) وقيل يا رسول الله أي أمت
11:15.english: Allah Most High said: {«يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا تلهكم أموالكم ولا أولادكم عن ذكر الله ومن يفعل ذلك فأولئك هم الخاسرون»} — "O you who believe, let not your wealth and your children divert you from the remembrance of Allah. And whoever does that — then it is they who are the losers." And He said Most High: {«إنما أموالكم وأولادكم فتنة والله عنده أجر عظيم»} — "Your wealth and your children are only a trial, and Allah — with Him is a mighty reward." So whoever chooses his wealth and his child over what is with Allah has indeed lost and been defrauded a tremendous loss. And He said, Mighty and Majestic: {«من كان يريد الحياة الدنيا وزينتها»} — "Whoever desires the life of this world and its adornment..." — to the end of the verse. And He said Most High: {«إن الإنسان ليطغى أن رآه استغنى»} — "Indeed, man does transgress when he sees himself self-sufficient." There is no might and no power except through Allah, the Exalted, the Magnificent. And He said Most High: {«ألهاكم التكاثر»} — "Vying in increase diverts you."
11:15.book_title: Condemnation of Miserliness and Love of Wealth
11:15.section_title_en: The Revival of the Religious Sciences — Book on Poverty and Abstinence: The Blame of Wealth and Its Perils
11:15.anchors:
- Root: لهو (l-h-w)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To divert, distract, or occupy oneself away from a matter of greater import; amusement that turns one from serious concern.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theologically, *lahw* denotes that which diverts the heart from Allah — the root cause of spiritual ruin, as wealth and children are here designated as distracting agents.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: play/amusement. Metaphorical: any engrossing worldly pursuit that veils one from the Hereafter.
- Root: كثر (k-th-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Abundance, multitude, increase in number or quantity.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): *Takāthur* (vying in increase) is censured as the competitive accumulation of worldly goods for pride, not need.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: seeking more. Metaphorical: the obsessive race toward worldly accumulation that hardens the heart.
- Root: غبن (gh-b-n)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To cheat, defraud, or suffer loss in a transaction; to be outwitted.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In the Hereafter, *ghubn* is the ultimate loss — exchanging eternal bliss for fleeting worldly gain.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: commercial deception. Metaphorical: the soul's self-deception in preferring the ephemeral over the everlasting.
- Root: فتن (f-t-n)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Trial, tribulation, test; that which sifts the sincere from the insincere.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): *Fitnah* is a divine test through which the heart's attachment to worldly goods is exposed.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: burning in fire (as gold is refined). Metaphorical: wealth as a crucible for faith.
- Sibawayh Rule: Restriction and Focused Predication (*Bāb al-Ḥaṣr wa al-Taqyīd bi-innamā*) — The particle *innamā* in {«إنما أموالكم وأولادكم فتنة»} restricts the predicate, affirming that wealth and children are solely a trial, not an end in themselves.
11:15.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications, prayers, and their spiritual power, from 'Condemnation of Miserliness and Love of Wealth'

11:15.arabic: فقال عز وجل ومن كان يريد الحياة الدنيا وزينتها نوف إليهم أعمالهم فيها وهم فيها لا يبخسون أولئك الذين ليس لهم في الآخرة إلا النار وحبط ما صنعوا فيها وباطل ما كانوا يعملون وهذا أيضا متناول بعمومه لحب الجاه فإنه أعظم لذة من لذات الحياة الدنيا وأكثر زينة من زينتها وقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم حب المال والجاه ينبتان النفاق في القلب كما ينبت الماء البقل (1) حديث ما ذئبان ضاريان أرسلا في زريبة غنم الحديث تقدم أيضا هناك وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم لعلي كرم الله وجهه إنما هلاك الناس باتباع الهوى وحب الثناء // حديث إنما هلاك الناس باتباع الهوى وحب الثناء لم أره بهذا اللفظ وقد تقدم في العلم من حديث أنس ثلاث مهلكات شح مط
11:15.english: And Allah Most High said: {«تلك الدار الآخرة نجعلها للذين لا يريدون علوا في الأرض ولا فسادا»} — "That abode of the Hereafter — We appoint it for those who do not desire exaltation upon the earth, nor corruption." He joined together the desire for corruption and the desire for exaltation [in a single condemnation], and [declared] that the Hereafter belongs solely to the one who is free of both desires together.
11:15.section_title_en: Section 794 — Exposition of the Blameworthiness of Prestige (Jāh) and Its True Meaning
11:15.anchors:
- Root: جاه (J-W-H)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root denotes "face, countenance, standing, rank, dignity" — the elevated position by which one is received with honor.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: jāh is the "station" (manzilah) in hearts, distinct from mere wealth (māl); it is a spiritual sovereignty over others' inward dispositions.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "place/standing before the king." Metaphorical: "possession of hearts" — the ruler's sway over subjects' wills, not their bodies.
- Root: ملك (M-L-K)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Possession, dominion, sovereign control over what one owns.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Two modes: (1) tamalluk — actual possession and disposal; (2) quwwah — capacity to possess, whether or not exercised.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: ownership of chattel. Metaphorical: "malaka nafsahu" (self-mastery), "malaka al-mar'ah" (marriage) — dominion over that which yields to one's authority.
- Root: قلب (Q-L-B)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The heart; that which fluctuates, turns, and overturns between states.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The heart is the seat of perception and volition; its "turning" (taqlīb) between conditions is its essential nature.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical turning over. Metaphorical: "qallaba al-umūr" — to scrutinize and manage affairs; the heart as the organ of belief and inclination.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — "إنما هلاك الناس..." restricts destruction solely to the two cited causes, excluding all others.
11:15.topic: Al-Ghazali on purifying the character, moral diseases, and spiritual remedies, from 'Condemnation of Status and Ostentation'

11:26.arabic: إن كان يريد أن يكون تعلمه طاعة فإن العباد أمروا أن لا يعبدوا إلا الله ولا يريدوا بطاعتهم غيره وكذلك من يخدم أبويه لا ينبغي أن يخدمهما لطلب المنزلة عندهما إلا من حيث إن رضا الله عنه في رضا الوالدين ولا يجوز له أن يرائي بطاعته لينال بها منزلة عند الوالدين فإن ذلك معصية في الحال وسيكشف الله عن ريائه وتسقط منزلته من قلوب الوالدين أيضا وأما الزاهد المعتزل عن الناس فينبغي له أن يلزم قلبه ذكر الله والقناعة بعلمه ولا يخطر بقلبه معرفة الناس زهده واستعظامهم محله فإن ذلك يغرس الرياء في صدره حتى تتيسر عليه العبادات في خلوته به
11:26.english: Ibrahim ibn Adham — may God have mercy on him — said: "I learned [true] knowledge (al-ma'rifah) from a monk called Sam'an. I entered upon him in his hermitage and said, 'O Sam'an, how long have you been in your hermitage?' He said, 'Seventy years.' I said, 'And what is your food?' He said — [marveling] — 'O Hanifi, what has brought you to this?' I said, 'I wished to learn.' He said, 'Each night, one chickpea.' I said, 'And what is it that stirs in your heart such that this single chickpea suffices you?' He said, 'Do you see that monastery facing you?' I said, 'Yes.' He said, 'They come to me once every year, on a single day. They decorate my hermitage, circumambulate around it, and magnify me. So whenever my soul grows sluggish toward worship, I recall that [moment] — the glory of that hour — and so I endure the toil of a whole year for the glory of a single hour. So do you, O Hanifi, endure the toil of a single hour for the glory of eternity.' And [this] settled knowledge (al-ma'rifah) into my heart. He said, 'Is that enough for you, or shall I add more?' I said, 'Yes [add more].' He said, 'Descend from the hermitage.' So I descended, and he lowered to me a small leather vessel (rakwah) containing twenty chickpeas. He said, 'Enter the monastery, for they have seen what I lowered to you.' When I entered the monastery, the Christians gathered around me and said, 'O Hanifi, what did the elder lower to you?' I said, 'Some of his provisions.' They said, 'And what will you do with it, when we have more right to it?' Then they said, 'Sell it.' I said, 'For twenty dinars.' So they gave me twenty dinars. I returned to the elder, and he said, 'O Hanifi, what did you do?' I said, 'I sold it to them.' He said, 'For how much?' I said, 'For twenty dinars.' He said, 'You erred. Had you asked them for twenty thousand dinars, they would have given you [that]. This is the glory of one whom you do not worship — so consider how must be the glory of One whom you do worship! O Hanifi, turn to your Lord, and abandon this coming and going.'"
11:26.section_title_en: On the Hidden Dangers of Seeking Status Through Worship — The Story of Ibrahim ibn Adham and the Monk
11:26.anchors:
- Root: زهد (z-h-d)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Abstinence, renunciation, turning away from something with deliberate disregard.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The virtue of the heart's detachment from worldly allurements; a state of the inner self, not merely outward acts.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: abandoning a thing as contemptible. Metaphorical: the ascetic's heart being present with God while absent from creation's regard.
- Root: راءى (r-'-y)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To show off, to display an act for the sake of being seen by others.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Riya' is the seeking of station (manzilah) in the hearts of creatures through acts of obedience, which nullifies sincerity to God.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: visual perception. Metaphorical: making one's worship a spectacle for onlookers, a hidden shirk.
- Root: خطر (kh-t-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To cross the mind, to occur to one; a passing thought.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Khatir denotes the fleeting suggestions that enter the heart, whether praiseworthy or blameworthy.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: to pace back and forth. Metaphorical: thoughts traversing the mind's terrain.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد (Restriction & Focused Predication) — The conditional and restrictive particles (إنما، لو، إلا) govern the precise scope of the author's rulings, distinguishing permissible intention from corrupting motive.
11:26.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Condemnation of Status and Ostentation'

11:115.arabic: فتح الباب والله لا يضيع أجر المحسنين وإن تك حسنة يضاعفها ويؤت من لدنه أجرا عظيما المقام الثاني في دفع العارض منه في أثناء العبادة وذلك لا بد من تعلمه أيضا فإن من جاهد نفسه وقلع مغارس الرياء من قلبه بالقناعة وقطع الطمع وإسقاط نفسه من أعين المخلوقين واستحقار مدح المخلوقين وذمهم فالشيطان لا يتركه في أثناء العبادات بل يعارضه بخطرات الرياء ولا تنقطع عنه نزعاته وهوى النفس وميلها لا ينمحي بالكلية فلا بد وأن يتشمر لدفع ما يعرض من خاطر الرياء وخواطر الرياء ثلاثة قد تخطر دفعة واحدة كالخاطر ال
11:115.english: So when the harm and injury of these causes is firmly settled in his heart, his desire [for them] slackens, and his heart turns toward God. For the intelligent person does not covet that whose harm is abundant and whose benefit is scant. It suffices him that if people knew what is in his inner self—the intent of ostentation (riyā') and the display of sincerity—they would abhor him. And God will surely expose his secret until He makes him odious to the people and makes them know that he is a show-off, abhorrent to God. Had he been sincere to God, God would have unveiled his sincerity to them, made him beloved to them, subjected them to him, and loosened their tongues in praise and commendation of him—even though there is no perfection in their praise, nor deficiency in their blame. As the poet of Banī Tamīm said: "My praise is an adornment, and my blame is a disgrace." The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said to him: "You have lied—that belongs to God, there is no deity but Him." // [Hadith: A poet of Banī Tamīm said, "My praise is an adornment, and my blame is a disgrace." He (the Prophet) said: "You have lied—that belongs to God." Ahmad narrated it from the hadith of al-Aqra' ibn Ḥābis—who was the speaker of that verse, excluding the phrase "You have lied"—and its narrators are trustworthy, except that I do not know of Abū Salamah ibn 'Abd al-Raḥmān having heard [directly] from al-Aqra'. Al-Tirmidhī narrated it from the hadith of al-Barā' and deemed it sound (ḥasan), with the wording: "A man said, 'Indeed, my praise...'"]
11:115.section_title_en: The Revival of the Religious Sciences — Section 827: The Second Station: Repelling the Accidental Promptings of Ostentation During Worship
11:115.anchors:
- Root: كذب (kadhaba)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: falsehood, lying, saying what is contrary to reality; also used for "to declare someone a liar."
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In theological context, kadhb is the antithesis of sidq (truthfulness); it is a moral and epistemic vice, often linked to hypocrisy (nifāq) and false claims.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (haqīqah): to report what did not occur. Metaphorical (majāz): attributing to God what is unworthy of Him, as in the Prophet's rebuke of the poet's self-praise.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Predicate Emphasis (Bāb al-Tawkīd) — The Prophet's reply "كَذَبْتَ" (You have lied) functions as an emphatic categorical refutation, structured as a nominal sentence with implied subject, establishing a permanent verdict rather than a transient rebuke.
11:115.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Condemnation of Status and Ostentation'

12:55.arabic: الله عليه وسلم فيما أخبر عنه الرب تعالى اجعلني على خزائن الأرض إني حفيظ عليم فإنه طلب المنزلة في قلبه بكونه حفيظا عليما وكان
12:55.english: If you say: "His seeking of rank and status in the heart of his teacher, his servant, his companion, and his sovereign — and of anyone with whom his affair is tied — is it permissible absolutely, however it may be? Or is it permissible up to a specific limit, in a specific manner?" — I say: This is sought in three modes: two modes are permissible and one mode is prohibited.
12:55.section_title_en: Exposition of What is Praiseworthy in the Love of Status (Jāh) and What is Blameworthy
12:55.anchors:
- Root: ج-و-ه (J-W-H)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning is "face" or "countenance"; al-jāh (الجاه) denotes "standing, dignity, rank, or status" — the weight one carries in the eyes of others.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-jāh is that which grants a person eminence and consideration among people; it is a relational quality subsisting in the hearts of others, not an intrinsic property of the self.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): "وجاهة" = honor/respect. Metaphorical (Majaz): "فلان له جاه" = he possesses influence and intercessory power; the term is transferred from the physical face (which faces people) to the social standing by which one "faces" others with authority.
- Root: م-ل-ك (M-L-K)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "To possess, to have dominion over something; to grasp and control."
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الملك: possession and disposal over a thing." When applied to hearts, it signifies the capacity to direct and dispose over the affections and wills of others.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: ownership of property. Metaphorical: "ملكت قلبه" — one has taken possession of another's heart, i.e., gained mastery over their inclination.
- Root: ق-ل-ب (Q-L-B)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The heart; also "to turn over, to flip, to transform."
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The heart is so named because of its constant turning (تقلب) between states; it is the seat of perception and intention.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the physical organ. Metaphorical: the locus of understanding, will, and affection — "فلان في قلبي محل" = he holds a station in my heart.
- Root: ن-ز-ل (N-Z-L)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "To descend, to alight, to settle."
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "النزول: انحطاط من علو" — descent from a height; also "to settle in a place."
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical descent. Metaphorical: "نزل فلان من قلبي منزلة" — he has taken up a station in my heart; the heart is conceived as a dwelling-place in which persons "alight" at varying degrees of honor.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين المبتدأ والخبر (Interposition between Subject and Predicate) — The periodic structure "مهما عرفت أن..." (Whenever you know that...) establishes a conditional frame governing the entire ensuing argument, requiring the translator to preserve the logical subordination across long sentences without fragmenting the author's unified reasoning.
12:55.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Condemnation of Status and Ostentation'

18:46.arabic: ولا هم ينصرون وهم الذين لم يفهموا قوله تعالى المال والبنون زينة الحياة الدنيا والباقيات الصالحات خير عند ربك ثوابا وخير أملا فالعلم والحرية هي الباقيات الصالحات التي تبقى كمالا في النفس والمال والجاه هو الذي ينقضي على القرب وهو كما مثله الله تعالى حيث قال إنما مثل الحياة الدنيا كماء أنزلناه من السماء فاختلط به نبات الأرض الآية وقال تعالى واضرب لهم مثل الحياة الدنيا كماء أنزلناه من السماء إلى قوله فأصبح هشيما تذروه الرياح وكل ما تذروه رياح الموت فهو زهرة الحياة الدنيا وكل ما لا يقطعه الموت فهو الباقيات الصالحات فقد عرفت بهذا أن كمال القدرة بالمال والجاه كمال ظني لا أصل له وأن من
18:46.english: Therefore, the perfections are three, if we count non-change through appetites and non-submission to them as a perfection—like the perfection of knowledge and the perfection of freedom. By "freedom" I mean non-enslavement to appetites and to willing worldly causes. The perfection of power for the servant is a path to acquiring the perfection of knowledge and the perfection of freedom, but he has no path to acquiring the perfection of power that endures after his death. For his power over the very substances of wealth and over subjugating hearts and bodies is cut off by death, whereas his knowledge and his freedom are not annihilated by death; rather, they both endure as perfection within him and as a means to nearness to God—may He be exalted.
18:46.section_title_en: On True Perfection: Knowledge and Freedom Over Power, Wealth, and Status
18:46.anchors:
- Root: قدر (q-d-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of measuring, determining, and enabling; power as capacity to bring about an effect.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): True power (qudrah) belongs absolutely to God alone; for humans, it is a relative capacity, never absolute, and is a means, not an end.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (haqiqah) power is God's; metaphorical (majaz) attribution of "power" to creatures is restricted and conditional, tied to specific acts.
- Root: علم (ʿ-l-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Knowledge as apprehension of a thing's reality; also traces and signs by which one is guided.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Knowledge (ʿilm) is the apprehension of a thing's true nature or the judgment of existence or non-existence regarding it; it is the enduring perfection of the soul.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "he knew" as direct awareness; metaphorical: "he knew" as perception or discernment of signs (maʿālim) leading to truth.
- Root: موت (m-w-t)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Death as the cessation of vital functions; also the state of being inanimate or lifeless.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Death is the opposite of life; in theological context, it marks the termination of worldly capacities but not of the soul's acquired knowledge or freedom.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical death; metaphorical: "death" of the heart through ignorance or enslavement to passion, and "revival" of the land through rain as a similitude for the fleeting world.
- Sibawayh Rule: Restriction and Focused Predication (الحصر والتقييد بإنما) — Used to confine true perfection exclusively to knowledge and freedom, negating it for power, wealth, and status.
18:46.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Condemnation of Status and Ostentation'

20:89.arabic: وسمعوا خواره تغيروا وسمعوا قوله هذا إلهكم وإله موسى ونسوا أنه لا يرجع إليهم قولا ولا يملك لهم ضرا ولا نفعا فكل من آمن بالنظر إلى ثعبان يكفر لا محالة إذا نظر إلى عجل لأن كليهما من عالم الشهادة والاختلاف والتضاد في عالم الشهادة كثير وأما عالم الملكوت فهو من عند الله تعالى فلذلك لا نجد فيه اختلافا وتضادا أصلا فإن قلت ما ذكرته من التوحيد ظاهر مهما ثبت أن الوسائط والأسباب مسخرات وكل ذلك ظاهر إلا في حركات الإنسان فإنه يتحرك إن شاء ويسكن إن شاء فكيف يكون مسخرا فاعلم أنه لو كان مع هذا يشاء إن أراد أن يشاء ولا يشاء إن لم يرد أن يشاء لكان هذا مزلة القدم وموقع ال
20:89.english: ...its mover is Power (al-qudrah) without any doubt. So the seeker (al-sālik) journeyed on to the world of Power, and there he beheld wonders before which all that had preceded seemed contemptible. He asked Power concerning the movement of the right hand, and it said: "I am but an attribute (innamā anā ṣifah) — ask the Powerful One (al-Qādir), for the reliance is upon the described substances (al-mawṣūfāt), not upon the attributes." At that point he almost deviated and unleashed the tongue of questioning with audacity, but he was steadied by the firm word (al-qawl al-thābit), and a caller cried out from behind the veils of the pavilions of the Divine Presence: "He is not asked about what He does, but they shall be asked" {«لَا يُسْأَلُ عَمَّا يَفْعَلُ وَهُمْ يُسْأَلُونَ»}. Then the awe of the Presence overwhelmed him, and he fell down stricken, convulsing in his swoon. When he regained consciousness, he said: "Glory be to You — how magnificent is Your majesty! I repent unto You, and I place my trust in You, and I believe that You are the Sovereign, the Compeller, the One, the Subduer. I fear none but You, I hope for none other than You, and I seek refuge only in Your pardon from Your punishment, and in Your good pleasure from Your wrath. I have nothing but to ask of You and to supplicate before You, and to plead humbly in Your presence, saying: 'Expand my breast that I may know You, and loosen the knot from my tongue that I may praise You.'"
20:89.section_title_en: The Unification of the Acts — The Journey of the Seekers to the Oneness of the Agent
20:89.anchors:
- Root: قدر (q-d-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of measuring, determining, and empowering; al-Qadir as the One whose power is absolute and unbounded.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Power (qudrah) when ascribed to God is the negation of incapacity ('ajz); when ascribed to man it is a contingent capacity limited by divine ordainment.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (haqiqah) — "He is Qadir, Muqtadir, possessor of power"; metaphorical (majaz) — "a far-reaching steed" (ba'id al-qadr), indicating extension of effect.
- Root: وحد (w-ḥ-d)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Oneness and singularity; al-Wahid as that which has no part whatsoever.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): True unity (wahdah) is absolute indivisibility; applied to God exclusively in the sense of unique sovereignty.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "He is one (wahid), and they are singular (wuhdan)"; literal unity versus numerical oneness.
- Root: علم (ʿ-l-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Knowledge as perception of a thing's reality; the mark or sign by which something is known.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Knowledge ('ilm) is the apprehension of a thing in its true reality — either grasping the essence or judging its attributes.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — "I knew not of your news" (ma 'alimtu bi-khabarika); the knower as one marked by discernment.
- Sibawayh Rule: Restriction and Focused Predication (al-ḥaṣr wa al-taqyīd bi-innamā) — "Innamā anā ṣifah" (I am but an attribute) restricts the speaker's essence to being a mere accident, redirecting inquiry to the substantive subject (al-mawṣūf).
20:89.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Monotheism and Reliance'

20:89.arabic: ضعيف لا يملك له ضرا ولا نفعا وهل ذلك إلا لأنه يظن أن ذلك العبد أقدر على تحصيل أغراضه من الله وأنه أولى بالتقريب إليه من الله إذ آثره على ملك الملوك فجعله مقصود عبادته وأي استهزاء يزيد على رفع العبد فوق المولى فهذا من كبائر المهلكات ولهذا
20:89.english: The evidence for this is what was narrated from ʿĀ'ishah, may God be pleased with her, that the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, intended one day to go out to the Companions, so he looked into the well-water [as a mirror] and straightened his turban and his hair. She said: "Do you do that, O Messenger of God?" He said: "Yes. Indeed God the Exalted loves that a servant beautify himself for his brothers when he goes out to them." // The ḥadīth of ʿĀ'ishah — he intended to go out to his Companions and looked into the well-water, straightening his turban and his hair — this ḥadīth was transmitted by Ibn ʿAdī in al-Kāmil, and it has already preceded in the Book of Purification.
20:89.section_title_en: On the Status (Jāh) Sought Without Greed, and the Ruling on Showing Off in Worldly Adornments
20:89.anchors:
- Root: جاه (w-j-h)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The root conveys "face, front, prominence, standing before others"; al-jāh is derived from wajh (face), denoting one's elevated position in the eyes of people.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-jāh is "al-manzilah 'inda al-sulṭān" — a station of honor before authority; in theological terms, it is a worldly accident (ʿaraḍ) tied to social estimation, not a spiritual virtue.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): "wajuhā" — to be honored; metaphorical (majāz): seeking jāh is "talab al-ri'āsah" (pursuit of leadership), which is permissible in itself but becomes blameworthy when it diverts the heart from God.
- Root: راءى (r-'-y)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Arā'a — to show, to display; riyā' is "al-taẓāhur bi al-ṭā'ah qaṣdan li al-ḥaqīqah" — feigning obedience for the sake of being seen.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Riyā' is a branch of shirk (associationism), because the actor directs his act toward a creature rather than the Creator; it nullifies the act's spiritual reward (thawāb).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "rā'āhu" — he saw him; metaphorical: "rā'ā bi 'amalihi" — he showed off his deed, i.e., he made the creature his qiblah (focus) in worship.
- Root: تلبيس (l-b-s)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Labasa — to clothe, to cover; talbīs is "khalṭ al-shay' bi ghayrihi" — confusing a thing with another, i.e., deception by cloaking falsehood in the garment of truth.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Talbīs is "ishkāl al-amr wa tashbīhuhu" — obscuring an affair and making it ambiguous; it is a moral vice because it corrupts epistemic trust.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "labastu al-thawb" — I wore the garment; metaphorical: "labbasa 'alayhi al-amr" — he made the matter obscure to him, i.e., he dressed falsehood in the appearance of sincerity.
- Sibawayh Rule: Bāb al-ḥaṣr wa al-taqyīd bi-innamā (Restriction and Specification with "innamā") — used to delimit the scope of permissibility, prohibition, and nullification in the conditional rulings below.
20:89.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'Condemnation of Status and Ostentation'

20:117.arabic: قال الله لهما إن هذا عدو لك ولزوجك فلا يخرجنكما من الجنة فتشقى إن لك ألا تجوع فيها ولا تعرى وأنك لا تظمأ فيها ولا تضحى ومع أنه لم ينه إلى عن شجرة واحدة وأطلق له وراء ذلك ما أراد فإذا لم يأمن من نبي من الأنبياء وهو في الجنة دار الأمن والسعادة من كيد الشيطان فكيف يجوز لغيره أن يأمن في دار
20:117.english: If you say: "Whoever finds in himself a dislike of ostentation (riyā'), and this dislike compels him to refuse it, yet he is not entirely free from the soul's inclination toward it, its love for it, and its striving after it — except that he dislikes his own love and his own inclination, and it is not beloved to him — is he then among the ranks of the ostentatious?" — Know that God has not burdened His servants except with what they can bear. It is not within the servant's power to prevent the Devil from his incitements (nazaghāt), nor to suppress nature entirely so that it neither inclines to lusts nor strives after them. His utmost limit is only that he confront his lust with a dislike born of his knowledge of consequences, his understanding of religion, and his roots of faith in God and the Last Day. When he does this, he has reached the utmost limit of performing what he has been charged with.
20:117.section_title_en: On the Degrees of Resistance to Ostentation and the Devil's Wiles — Section 829
20:117.anchors:
- Root: شيط (Shayṭ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of burning, scorching, or spoiling by fire; the Devil as that which burns and destroys.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): الشيطان as the one who leads astray and incites; his "نزغات" (incitements) are his piercing stings of temptation.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "شاط اللحم" (meat scorched/ruined). Metaphorical: "أشاط دمه" (shed his blood vainly) — the Devil's aim is to ruin the soul's deeds.
- Root: كره (K-R-H)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Dislike, aversion, abhorrence; the opposite of love (ḥubb) and desire (mīl).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The moral faculty of repulsion against sin; a trait of faith (īmān) distinguishing the believer's higher self from the lower nature.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "كرهت الشيء" (I disliked it). Metaphorical: The heart's rejection of the soul's base inclinations as an act of worship.
- Root: نفس (Nafs)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The self, soul, or spirit; the seat of desires and passions.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): النفس as the lower commanding soul (النفس الأمارة) that inclines to lusts, distinct from the intellect (عقل) and faith.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "نفس سائلة" (flowing blood/life). Metaphorical: The inner self that must be opposed when it inclines to ostentation.
- Root: جهد (J-H-D) / مجادلة (Jadal)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Striving, exertion, argumentation; from جدل (twisting ropes tightly).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): المجادلة as disputation that can distract from divine remembrance (ذكر الله).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "جادله" (he argued with him). Metaphorical: The soul's engagement with the Devil's whispers as a subtle trap, diverting from sincere worship.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — Used to delimit the four ranks of resistance, each defined by what it exclusively does or omits.
20:117.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Condemnation of Status and Ostentation'

22:31.arabic: تهوي بنا الريح في مكان سحيق أحب إلينا من أن نتكلم بها فقال صلى الله عليه وسلم أو قد وجدتموه قالوا نعم قال ذلك صريح الإيمان (1) حديث ابن عباس الحمد لله الذي رد كيد الشيطان إلى الوسوسة أخرجه أبو داود والنسائي في اليوم والليلة بلفظ كيده وقال أبو حازم ما كان من نفسك وكرهته نفسك لنفسك فلا يضرك ما هو من عدوك وما كان من نفسك فرضيته نفسك لنفسك فعاتبها عليه فإذن وسوسة الشيطان ومنازعة النفس لا تضرك مهما رددت مرادهما بالإباء والكراهة والخواطر التي هي العلوم والتذكرات والتخيلات للأسبا

22:52.arabic: عائشة وقرأ ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما وما أرسلنا من قبلك من رسول ولا نبي ولا محدث يعني الصديقين والمحدث هو الملهم والملهم هو الذي انكشف له في باطن قلبه من جهة الداخل لا من جهة المحسوسات الخارجة والقرآن مصرح بأن التقوى مفتاح الهداية والكشف وذلك علم من غير تعلم وقال الله تعالى وما خلق الله في السموات والأرض لآيات لقوم يتقون خصصها بهم وقال تعالى {هذا بيان للناس وهدى وموعظة للمتقين} وكان أبو يزيد وغيره يقول ليس العالم الذي يحفظ من كتاب فإذا نسي ما حفظه صار جاهلا إنما العالم الذي يأخذ علمه من ربه أي وقت شاء بلا حفظ ولا درس وهذا هو العلم الرباني وإليه الإشارة بقوله تعالى {وعلمناه من لدنا علما}
22:52.english: As for the evidences of the Sacred Law, there is His saying (Exalted is He): {«وَالَّذِينَ جَاهَدُوا فِينَا لَنَهْدِيَنَّهُمْ سُبُلَنَا»} ("And those who strive in Us, We shall surely guide them to Our paths") (Q. 29:69). So every wisdom that appears from the heart through persevering devotion to worship, without learning, is by way of unveiling and inspiration. And he (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Whoever acts upon what he knows, God bequeaths to him knowledge of what he does not know, and grants him success in what he does" — until he becomes deserving of Paradise. And whoever does not act upon what he knows wanders astray in what he knows and is not granted success in what he does, until he becomes deserving of the Fire. [The hadith "Whoever acts upon what he knows" has preceded in the Book of Knowledge, without his saying "and grants him success in what he does" — I have not found it with that addition.] And God (Exalted is He) said: {«وَمَنْ يَتَّقِ اللَّهَ يَجْعَلْ لَهُ مَخْرَجًا»} ("And whoever fears God, He makes for him a way out") (Q. 65:2) — from perplexities and doubts — {«وَيَرْزُقْهُ مِنْ حَيْثُ لَا يَحْتَسِبُ»} ("and provides for him from whence he does not reckon") (Q. 65:3) — teaching him knowledge without learning and granting him discernment without experience. And God (Exalted is He) said: {«يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا إِنْ تَتَّقُوا اللَّهَ يَجْعَلْ لَكُمْ فُرْقَانًا»} ("O you who believe, if you fear God, He will make for you a criterion") (Q. 8:29) — it is said: a light by which one distinguishes between truth and falsehood and by which one emerges from doubts. For this reason, he (peace and blessings be upon him) was abundant in his supplication in asking for light, saying (peace and blessings be upon him): "O God, grant me light, and increase me in light, and make for me light in my heart, and light in my grave, and light in my hearing, and light in my sight" — until he said: "and light in my hair, and in my skin, and in my flesh, and in my blood, and in my bones." [Agreed upon (by al-Bukhari and Muslim).] [The hadith concerning his being asked about His saying {«أَفَمَنْ شَرَحَ اللَّهُ صَدْرَهُ لِلْإِسْلَامِ»} ("Is he whose breast God has expanded for Islam") (Q. 39:22) — and in al-Mustadrak from the hadith of Ibn Masʿūd — has preceded in the Book of Knowledge.] And he (peace and blessings be upon him) said concerning Ibn ʿAbbās: "O God, grant him understanding in religion and teach him the interpretation (taʾwīl)." [The hadith of ʿAlī: "We have nothing with us that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) confided to us except that God grants a servant understanding in His Book" — has preceded in the Etiquettes of Qurʾanic Recitation.] And it is said in the interpretation of His saying (Exalted is He): {«يُؤْتِي الْحِكْمَةَ مَنْ يَشَاءُ»} ("He grants wisdom to whom He wills") (Q. 2:269) that it is understanding in the Book of God. And He (Exalted is He) said: {«فَفَهَّمْنَاهَا سُلَيْمَانَ»} ("And We made Solomon understand it") (Q. 21:79) — singling out what was unveiled with the name of understanding (fahm). And Abū al-Dardāʾ used to say: "The believer is one who sees by the light of God from behind a thin veil. By God, it is the truth that God casts into their hearts and causes to flow upon their tongues." And some of the Salaf said: "The believer's conjecture is like soothsaying."
22:52.section_title_en: The Unveiling of Knowledge Through Divine Inspiration and the Evidences of the Unseen
22:52.anchors:
- Root: علم (ʿalima)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning encompasses both perception of a thing's essence and judgment upon it—knowledge as direct apprehension or discursive ruling.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "العلم: إدراك الشيء بحقيقته" — knowledge is the apprehension of a thing in its true reality, divided into apprehension of the essence (transitive to one object) and judgment upon existence or non-existence (transitive to two objects).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal usage denotes certainty and awareness ("ما علمت بخبرك: ما شعرت به"); metaphorical extension applies to marks, signs, and beacons of guidance (معالم الطريق) — here, the inspired knowledge is a "mark" of the path.
- Root: كشف (kashafa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To remove a covering, unveil, disclose what was hidden.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Unveiling (kashf) in theological terms is the removal of the veil (ghishāwah) from the heart such that the realities of things become directly witnessed, not merely inferred.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: to lift a covering from a thing; metaphorical: the disclosure of inward states and hidden matters — the heart's eye perceives what the outward senses cannot.
- Root: فرس (farasa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To prey upon, devour; farāsah — the lion's pouncing upon its prey.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Discernment (farāsah) is a spiritual perception by which the believer penetrates into the inner states of others, a light cast by God into the heart.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the beast of prey seizing its quarry; metaphorical: the believer's insight seizing the truth of a matter or the hidden state of a person — "اتقوا فراسة المؤمن فإنه ينظر بنور الله."
- Root: حدث (ḥadatha)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To be new, originate after non-existence; muḥaddath — one who is spoken to, inspired with true speech from the unseen.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الحدوث: كون الشيء بعد أن لم يكن" — origination after non-existence; the muḥaddath is one to whom divine inspiration comes as a new, immediate occurrence without acquired means.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: newness of a thing; metaphorical: "كان عمر رضي الله عنه محدثا أي صادق الحدس، كأنما حدث بما ظن" — one whose intuition is so true it is as if he were directly spoken to.
- Sibawayh Rule: Restriction and specification (الحصر والتقييد) — the particle "إنما" and conditional clauses (إن/إذا) restrict predicates to their subjects, as in "إنما العالم الذي يأخذ علمه من ربه" — the true scholar is exclusively the one who takes knowledge from his Lord.
22:52.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Condemnation of Status and Ostentation'

28:15.arabic: موسى عليه السلام فيما أخبر عنه تعالى هذا من عمل الشيطان ولذلك حذر الله منه جميع الخلق فقال الله تعالى يا بني آدم لا يفتننكم الشيطان كما أخرج أبويكم من الجنة وقال عز وجل إنه يراكم هو وقبيله من حيث لا ترونهم والقرآن من أوله إلى آخره تحذير من الشيطان فكيف يدع الأمن منه وأخذ الحذر من حيث أمر الله به لا ينافي الاشتغال بحب الله فإن من الحب له امتثال أمره وقد أمر بالحذر من العدو كما أمر بالحذر من الكفار فقال تعالى وليأخذوا حذرهم وأسلحتهم وقال تعالى وأعدوا لهم ما استطعتم من قوة ومن رباط الخيل فإذا لزمك بأمر الله
28:15.english: ...and the world, which is the source of trials and tribulations, the mine of forbidden pleasures and lusts. And Moses, peace be upon him, said—as God Most High has related concerning him—{«هذا من عمل الشيطان»} ("This is of Satan's doing" — Qur'an 28:15). For this reason, God warned all of creation against him, saying: {«يا بني آدم لا يفتننكم الشيطان كما أخرج أبويكم من الجنة»} ("O children of Adam, let not Satan tempt you as he brought your parents out of Paradise" — Qur'an 7:27). And He, Glorified and Exalted, said: {«إنه يراكم هو وقبيله من حيث لا ترونهم»} ("Indeed, he sees you, he and his tribe, from where you do not see them" — Qur'an 7:27). The Qur'an, from its beginning to its end, is a warning against Satan. So how could one claim security from him? And taking precaution against him, in the manner God has commanded, does not contradict occupation with the love of God. For part of loving Him is obeying His command. He has commanded vigilance against the enemy just as He commanded vigilance against the disbelievers, saying: {«وليعأخذوا حذرهم وأسلحتهم»} ("And let them take their precautions and their weapons" — Qur'an 4:102), and saying: {«وأعدوا لهم ما استطعتم من قوة ومن رباط الخيل»} ("And prepare against them whatever you are able of power and of steeds of war" — Qur'an 8:60). So if, by God's command, you are obligated to be wary of a disbelieving enemy whom you can see, then it is all the more fitting that you be obligated to be wary of an enemy who sees you while you do not see him.
28:15.section_title_en: On the Necessity of Vigilance Against Satan and Its Harmony with Trust in God and Remembrance of Him
28:15.anchors:
- Root: شيط (Shayṭ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root denotes burning, scorching, or spoiling (as meat over a fire), and by extension, perishing or being ruined.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الشيطان" (Satan) is derived from this root, signifying one who is burned, ruined, or cast away from mercy—the archetype of the adversary who destroys through temptation.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): "شاط دمه" — his blood went in vain (was wasted). Metaphorical (Majaz): "أشاط السلطان دمه" — the ruler declared his blood permissible (wasted). Thus, Satan is the one who causes spiritual ruin and waste.
- Root: حذر (Ḥadhar)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Caution, wariness, and taking precautions against a feared harm.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الحذر: احتراز من مخيف" — vigilance is a protective withdrawal from what is frightening. It is a commanded state, as in {«خذوا حذركم»} (Take your precautions — Qur'an 4:71).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "حذرته وحاذرته" — I was wary of him. Metaphorical: "حذار من أرماحنا حذار" — a poetic imperative to beware. Vigilance is both a physical and spiritual act of self-preservation.
- Root: قلب (Qalb)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To turn, overturn, or flip something from one state to another.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "قلب الشيء: تصريفه وصرفه عن وجه إلى وجه" — the heart (qalb) is so named for its constant turning and fluctuation between states.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "قلب الشيء قلبا: حوله عن وجهه" — to turn a thing from its face. Metaphorical: "رجل قلب حول: يقلب الأمور ويحتال" — a man who turns matters over and devises stratagems. The heart's occupation is decisive: it turns either toward God or toward the enemy.
- Root: وكل (Wakal)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To entrust, delegate, or rely upon another.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "التوكيل: أن تعتمد على غيرك وتجعله نائبا عنك" — trust (tawakkul) is reliance upon another as your deputy. God says: {«وكفى بالله وكيلا»} (And sufficient is Allah as Disposer of affairs — Qur'an 4:81).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "وكل إليه الأمر" — he delegated the matter to him. Metaphorical: "فلان وكل" — a weak man who leans on others. True tawakkul does not negate taking means; it purifies the heart's reliance.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد (Restriction & Focused Predication) — The particle "إنما" and restrictive constructions (e.g., "ليس ... إلا") are used to delimit predicates, as in the author's argument that vigilance is not a contradiction of love or trust but a fulfillment of the divine command.
28:15.topic: Al-Ghazali on the journey of the soul, death, and the Hereafter, from 'Condemnation of Status and Ostentation'

35:10.arabic: المريدين والعمل كالشرط له وإليه الإشارة بقوله تعالى {إليه يصعد الكلم الطيب والعمل الصالح يرفعه} فالكلم الطيب هو هذا العلم والعمل كالحمال الرافع له الى مقصده فيكون المرفوع أفضل من الرافع وهذا كلام معترض لا يليق بهذا الكلام فلنرجع الى المقصود فنقول إذا عرفت فوائد العزلة وغوائلها تحققت أن الحكم عليها مطلقا بالتفضيل نفيا وإثباتا خطأ بل ينبغي أن ينظر الى الشخص وحاله والى الخليط وحاله والى الباعث على مخالطته والى الفائت بسبب مخالطته من هذه الفوائد المذكورة ويقاس الفائت بالحاصل فعند ذلك يتبين الحق ويتضح الأفضل وكلام الشافعي
35:10.english: For this reason, those who journey upon the road to the Hereafter and seek the purification of their hearts would put themselves to the test. Whoever sensed within himself pride strove to remove it — until some of them would carry a waterskin upon their backs among the people, or a bundle of firewood upon their heads, and would circulate through the marketplaces to test themselves thereby. For the hidden snares of the soul and the stratagems of Satan are subtle; few are they who perceive them. Hence it is related of one of them that he said: "I repeated the prayer for thirty years, even though I had been praying in the front row. But one day I lagged behind due to an excuse, and found no place in the front row — so I stood in the second row. Then I found my soul feeling shame at the gaze of the people upon me, since I had been accustomed to reaching the front row. Thus I knew that all my prayers which I had been performing were adulterated with ostentation (riyāʾ) and mingled with the pleasure of people's gaze upon me and their seeing me among the foremost in goodness."
35:10.section_title_en: On the Benefits of Social Intercourse and the Trials of Solitude — Section 462
35:10.anchors:
- Root: جرب (j-r-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Testing, proving, assaying — experience gained through trial
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Experiential knowledge as distinct from rational a priori knowledge; the testing of character through exposure
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Haqiqah — literal testing of metals by fire; Majaz — the testing of the soul through social friction
- Root: خلق (kh-l-q)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Inborn disposition, character, moral constitution
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The inward form (al-ṣūrah al-bāṭinah) of the soul, as opposed to the outward physical form
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Haqiqah — measuring/creating; Majaz — the ingrained pattern of moral response
- Root: عزل (ʿ-z-l)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Separation, withdrawal, retirement
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The deliberate severance from social intercourse for spiritual discipline
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Haqiqah — physical removal; Majaz — the heart's detachment from worldly concerns
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — used to distinguish categorical judgments from conditional ones regarding solitude and society
35:10.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Love, Longing, Intimacy and Contentment'

35:10.arabic: يراءون وقوله عز وجل والذين يمكرون السيئات لهم عذاب شديد ومكر أولئك هو يبور قال مجاهد هم أهل الرياء وقال تعالى إنما نطعمكم لوجه الله لا نريد منكم جزاء ولا شكورا فمدح المخلصين ينفي كل إرادة سوى وجه الله والرياء ضده وقال تعالى فمن كان يرجو لقاء ربه فليعمل عملا صالحا ولا يشرك بعبادة ربه أحدا // حديث نزول قوله تعالى فمن كان يرجو لقاء ربه الآية فيمن يطلب الآخرة بعباداته وأعماله أخرجه الحاكم من حديث طاوس قال رجل إني أقف الموقف أبتغي وجه الله وأحب أن يرى موطني فلم يرد عليه حتى نزلت هذه الآية هكذا في نسختي من المستدرك ولع
35:10.english: As for the verses: it is His saying, Exalted is He: {فويل للمصلين الذين هم عن صلاتهم ساهون الذين هم يراءون} — "So woe to those who pray, those who are heedless of their prayer, those who make a show" {Al-Ma'un 107:4-6}. And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: {والذين يمكرون السيئات لهم عذاب شديد ومكر أولئك هو يبور} — "And those who scheme evil deeds — for them is a severe punishment, and the scheming of those — it shall perish" {Fatir 35:10}. Mujāhid said: "They are the people of riyā'."
35:10.section_title_en: The Second Half of the Book on Seeking Status and Rank through Acts of Worship — Being on Riya' (Ostentation/Show), Its Blameworthiness, and Its Treatment
35:10.anchors:
- Root: راءى (rā'ā)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root is الرؤية (vision/sight); المراءاة is showing oneself to another, derived from mutual seeing (تفاعل) — the act of displaying one's deeds for another's observation.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): الرياء is the seeking of rank (الجاه) and station (المنزلة) in the hearts of men through displaying acts of obedience — it is the antithesis of الإخلاص (sincerity), which restricts intention solely to the Divine Face (وجه الله).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): mutual visual perception. Metaphorical (Majaz): the spiritual "seeing" of one's deeds by creatures, seeking their approbation — a transfer from physical sight to the heart's craving for social esteem.
- Root: سها (sahā)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Neglect, heedlessness, inattention; the one who is "sāhin" is oblivious to the essence and time of an act.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): السهو is the heart's vacancy from awareness of the true import of an affair; in the verse {الذين هم عن صلاتهم ساهون} it denotes neglect of the prayer's time and conditions, coupled with ostentation in performing it.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: distraction. Metaphorical: the soul's diversion from the Hereafter toward the gaze of creatures.
- Root: مكر (makara)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Crafty scheming, deception; the "makr" of the ostentatious is their covert corruption of good deeds.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): المكر is the turning of another from his intent by subtle concealment; the "sayyi'āt" (evil deeds) of the riyā' practitioners are their acts of worship corrupted by show — their scheming "yabūr" (perishes) because it is built on other than God.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: stratagem. Metaphorical: the hypocritical display of piety as a ruse to capture hearts — a "makr" that boomerangs to perdition.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — In {إنما نطعمكم لوجه الله}, the particle إنما confines the motive exclusively to God's Face, negating all secondary aims (جزاء or شكورا); this is the grammatical seal of ikhlāṣ against riyā'.
35:10.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'Condemnation of Status and Ostentation'

57:12.arabic: إلى لقاء الله تعالى إلا بأنوارهم قال الله تعالى يسعى نورهم بين أيديهم وبأيمانهم وقد روي في الخبر أن بعضهم يعطى نورا مثل الجبل وبعضهم أصغر حتى يكون آخرهم رجلا يعطى نورا على إبهام قدميه فيضيء مرة وينطفيء أخرى فإذا أضاء قدم قدميه فمشى وإذا طفيء قام ومرورهم على الصراط على قدر نورهم فمنهم من يمر كطرف العين ومنهم من يمر كالبرق ومنهم من يمر كالسحاب ومنه من يمر كانقضاض الكواكب ومنهم من يمر كالفرس إذا اشتد في ميدانه والذي أعطي نورا على إبهام قدمه يحبوحبوا على وجهه ويديه ورجليه يجر يدا ويعلق أخرى ويصيب جوانبه النار فلا يزال كذلك حتى ي
57:12.english: The hadith — and in it he said: "And what are the mufarridūn (المفردون)?" He said: "Those who remember God much, both men and women." Al-Hakim narrated it with the wording: "He said: 'Those who are engrossed in the remembrance of God.'" And he declared it sound upon the condition of the two Shaykhs (al-Shaykhayn). Al-Bayhaqi added in al-Shuʿab: "Remembrance lifts their burdens from them, and they come on the Day of Resurrection light." Al-Tabarani narrated it thus in al-Muʿjam al-Kabīr from the hadith of Abu al-Darda', without the addition that the author mentioned at its end — and both are weak in their chain of transmission.
57:12.section_title_en: The Clarification of the Difference Between the Two Stations by a Perceptible Example
57:12.anchors:
- Root: وحد (wḥd)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of singularity, solitude, and being alone; al-mufrad (المفرد) is the one who is isolated or unique.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In theological usage, refers to the state of devotional solitude or the unique devotion of the heart to God, often through remembrance (dhikr).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah) sense is "one who is alone"; metaphorical (Majaz) sense in this prophetic context denotes those who are "absorbed" or "engrossed" in the remembrance of God, to the exclusion of all else.
- Root: جلى (jly)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To polish, burnish, or make manifest; to clear away rust or impurity from a surface.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The act of purification of the heart (tajliyat al-qalb) as a spiritual operation that unveils the divine realities (jaliyyat al-ḥaqq).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal sense is the physical polishing of a mirror or blade; metaphorical sense is the purification of the inner self to receive divine illumination.
- Root: نور (nwr)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Light, radiance, illumination; that by which things become visible.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In Kalam, light (nūr) is the metaphysical illumination of knowledge and faith (maʿrifah and īmān) by which the believer perceives the unseen and is guided on the Path (ṣirāṭ).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal light is physical luminosity; metaphorical light is the spiritual illumination granted to the believers, varying in intensity according to their degrees of knowledge and faith.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Interposition (Bāb al-Faṣl bayna al-Jār wa al-Majrūr) — The separation between the prepositional phrase and its governed noun is permissible when the intervening clause is complete and independently meaningful, as in the structure "فإذا بجانبهم يتلألأ" where the sudden discovery clause (fājā'ah) interrupts the expected sequence for rhetorical emphasis.
57:12.topic: Al-Ghazali on the journey of the soul, death, and the Hereafter, from 'Condemnation of Status and Ostentation'

63:1.arabic: الإسلام وهو الذي ذكره الله تعالى في كتابه في مواضع شتى كقوله عز وجل {إذا جاءك المنافقون قالوا نشهد إنك لرسول الله والله يعلم إنك لرسوله والله يشهد إن المنافقين لكاذبون} أي في دلالتهم بقولهم على ضمائرهم وقال تعالى {ومن الناس من يعجبك قوله في الحياة الدنيا ويشهد الله على ما في قلبه وهو ألد الخصام وإذا تولى سعى في الأرض ليفسد فيها} الآية وقال تعالى {وإذا لقوكم قالوا آمنا وإذا خلوا عضوا عليكم الأنامل من الغيظ} وقال تعالى {يراؤون الناس ولا يذكرون الله إلا قليلا مذبذبين بين ذلك} والآيات فيهم كثيرة وكان النفاق يكثر في ابتداء الإسلام ممن يدخل في ظاهر الإسلام ابتداء لغرض وذلك مما يقل في زماننا ولكن يكثر نفاق من ينسل عن الدي
63:1.english: The fourth [case]: that the people's seeing him should be a weighty factor (murajjihan) and a strengthener of his vigor, such that were it not for that, he would not abandon the act of worship; and were the intention of ostentation alone [present], he would not have ventured upon it. So what we hold — and knowledge is with God — is that it does not annul the root of the reward, but rather it diminishes it; or he is punished to the measure of his intention of ostentation and rewarded to the measure of his intention of reward. As for his saying — may God's peace and blessings be upon him — that God the Exalted says: "I am the most Self-Sufficient of the self-sufficient, free of all need for partnership (shirk)" — that is carried upon the case when the two intentions are equal, or when the intention of ostentation is the weightier.
63:1.section_title_en: On the Degrees of Ostentation in Worship — The Second Pillar: That by Which One Ostentatiously Displays (Al-Riya' bi al-Ta'at)
63:1.anchors:
- Root: قصد (Qasada)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of "intending, aiming toward a goal, directing one's purpose."
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "القصد: استقامة الطريق" — intention as the straight path of the soul toward its object; in moral theology, it denotes the deliberate orientation of the will that determines the moral value of an act.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): "قصدته وقصدت له" — direct aiming. Metaphorical (Majaz): "قصد في الأمر إذا لم يجاوز فيه الحد" — moderation; here, the "intention" (qasd) is the precise measure by which an act is weighed between reward and punishment.
- Root: راءى (Ra'a) — from Root: رأى (Ra'a)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الرياء: إظهار العمل ليراه الناس" — showing one's deed so that people may see it; derived from الرؤية (sight/seeing).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Riya' is a branch of shirk (associating partners with God), for the actor directs his deed not to God alone but to the gaze of creatures, thus dividing his intention between the Creator and creation.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: seeing with the eye. Metaphorical: "راءى فلان" — to perform an act for the sake of being seen, i.e., seeking the approval of onlookers rather than the sight of God.
- Root: خلق (Khalaqa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الخلق: التقدير المستقيم" — measuring and proportioning; also "خلق الثوب" — wearing out a garment until it is threadbare.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الخلق أصله: التقدير المستقيم" — creation as precise estimation; in moral context, the "خلق" (character) is the inward measure by which a soul is formed.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "خلق الخراز الأديم" — the leather-worker cutting and measuring hide. Metaphorical: "خلق الله الخلق: أوجده على تقدير أوجبته الحكمة" — God's creation of creatures upon a measure required by wisdom; here, the "creatures" (الخلق) whose blame (المقت) is feared by the ostentatious worshipper.
- Root: نفق (Nafaqa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "نفق الشيء: مضى ونفد" — to pass away, to be spent, to perish.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "نفق الشيء: مضى ونفد، ينفق، إما بالبيع نحو: نفق البيع نفاقا" — to find a ready market; "ومنها نفاق الأيم" — hypocrisy as the "passing" of a false coin in the market of religion.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "نفقت الدراهم" — coins circulating and being spent. Metaphorical: "نافق" — the hypocrite (munafiq) whose outward faith circulates among people while his inward disbelief is void; the ostentatious man "spends" his deeds on the market of human praise.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The syntactic separation between a governing preposition and its object, as in "له من الثواب مثل ما عليه من العقاب," where the prepositional phrases are interposed to balance two opposing clauses, mirroring the theological weighing of reward against punishment.
63:1.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Condemnation of Status and Ostentation'

63:1.arabic: يشهد إن المنافقين لكاذبون} أي في دلالتهم بقولهم على ضمائرهم وقال تعالى {ومن الناس من يعجبك قوله في الحياة الدنيا ويشهد الله على ما في قلبه وهو ألد الخصام وإذا تولى سعى في الأرض ليفسد فيها} الآية وقال تعالى {وإذا لقوكم قالوا آمنا وإذا خلوا عضوا عليكم الأنامل من الغيظ} وقال تعالى {يراؤون الناس ولا يذكرون الله إلا قليلا مذبذبين بين ذلك} والآيات فيهم كثيرة وكان النفاق يكثر في ابتداء الإسلام ممن يدخل في ظاهر الإسلام ابتداء لغرض وذلك مما يقل في زماننا ولكن يكثر نفاق من ينسل عن ا
63:1.english: The fourth [case]: that the people's seeing him should be a weighty factor (murajjihan) and a strengthener of his vigor, such that were it not for that, he would not abandon the act of worship; and were the intention of ostentation alone [present], he would not have ventured upon it. So what we hold — and knowledge is with God — is that it does not annul the root of the reward, but rather it diminishes it; or he is punished to the measure of his intention of ostentation and rewarded to the measure of his intention of reward. As for his saying — may God's peace and blessings be upon him — that God the Exalted says: "I am the most Self-Sufficient of the self-sufficient, free of all need for partnership (shirk)" — that is carried upon the case when the two intentions are equal, or when the intention of ostentation is the weightier.
63:1.section_title_en: On the Degrees of Ostentation in Worship — The Second Pillar: That by Which One Ostentatiously Displays (Al-Riya' bi al-Ta'at)
63:1.anchors:
- Root: قصد (Qasada)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of "intending, aiming toward a goal, directing one's purpose."
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "القصد: استقامة الطريق" — intention as the straight path of the soul toward its object; in moral theology, it denotes the deliberate orientation of the will that determines the moral value of an act.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): "قصدته وقصدت له" — direct aiming. Metaphorical (Majaz): "قصد في الأمر إذا لم يجاوز فيه الحد" — moderation; here, the "intention" (qasd) is the precise measure by which an act is weighed between reward and punishment.
- Root: راءى (Ra'a) — from Root: رأى (Ra'a)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الرياء: إظهار العمل ليراه الناس" — showing one's deed so that people may see it; derived from الرؤية (sight/seeing).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Riya' is a branch of shirk (associating partners with God), for the actor directs his deed not to God alone but to the gaze of creatures, thus dividing his intention between the Creator and creation.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: seeing with the eye. Metaphorical: "راءى فلان" — to perform an act for the sake of being seen, i.e., seeking the approval of onlookers rather than the sight of God.
- Root: خلق (Khalaqa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الخلق: التقدير المستقيم" — measuring and proportioning; also "خلق الثوب" — wearing out a garment until it is threadbare.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الخلق أصله: التقدير المستقيم" — creation as precise estimation; in moral context, the "خلق" (character) is the inward measure by which a soul is formed.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "خلق الخراز الأديم" — the leather-worker cutting and measuring hide. Metaphorical: "خلق الله الخلق: أوجده على تقدير أوجبته الحكمة" — God's creation of creatures upon a measure required by wisdom; here, the "creatures" (الخلق) whose blame (المقت) is feared by the ostentatious worshipper.
- Root: نفق (Nafaqa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "نفق الشيء: مضى ونفد" — to pass away, to be spent, to perish.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "نفق الشيء: مضى ونفد، ينفق، إما بالبيع نحو: نفق البيع نفاقا" — to find a ready market; "ومنها نفاق الأيم" — hypocrisy as the "passing" of a false coin in the market of religion.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "نفقت الدراهم" — coins circulating and being spent. Metaphorical: "نافق" — the hypocrite (munafiq) whose outward faith circulates among people while his inward disbelief is void; the ostentatious man "spends" his deeds on the market of human praise.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The syntactic separation between a governing preposition and its object, as in "له من الثواب مثل ما عليه من العقاب," where the prepositional phrases are interposed to balance two opposing clauses, mirroring the theological weighing of reward against punishment.

76:9.arabic: وقال تعالى إنما نطعمكم لوجه الله لا نريد منكم جزاء ولا شكورا فمدح المخلصين ينفي كل إرادة سوى وجه الله والرياء ضده وقال تعالى فمن كان يرجو لقاء ربه فليعمل عملا صالحا ولا يشرك بعبادة ربه أحدا // حديث نزول قوله تعالى فمن كان يرجو لقاء ربه الآية فيمن يطلب الآخرة بعباداته وأعماله أخرجه الحاكم من حديث طاوس قال رجل إني أقف الموقف أبتغي وجه الله وأحب أن يرى موطني فلم يرد عليه حتى نزلت هذه الآية هكذا في نسختي من المستدرك ولعله سقط منه ابن عباس أو أبو هريرة وللبزار من حديث معاذ بسند ضعيف من صام رياء فقد أشرك
76:9.english: As for the verses: it is His saying, Exalted is He: {فويل للمصلين الذين هم عن صلاتهم ساهون الذين هم يراءون} — "So woe to those who pray, those who are heedless of their prayer, those who make a show" {Al-Ma'un 107:4-6}. And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: {والذين يمكرون السيئات لهم عذاب شديد ومكر أولئك هو يبور} — "And those who scheme evil deeds — for them is a severe punishment, and the scheming of those — it shall perish" {Fatir 35:10}. Mujāhid said: "They are the people of riyā'."
76:9.section_title_en: The Second Half of the Book on Seeking Status and Rank through Acts of Worship — Being on Riya' (Ostentation/Show), Its Blameworthiness, and Its Treatment
76:9.anchors:
- Root: راءى (rā'ā)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root is الرؤية (vision/sight); المراءاة is showing oneself to another, derived from mutual seeing (تفاعل) — the act of displaying one's deeds for another's observation.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): الرياء is the seeking of rank (الجاه) and station (المنزلة) in the hearts of men through displaying acts of obedience — it is the antithesis of الإخلاص (sincerity), which restricts intention solely to the Divine Face (وجه الله).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): mutual visual perception. Metaphorical (Majaz): the spiritual "seeing" of one's deeds by creatures, seeking their approbation — a transfer from physical sight to the heart's craving for social esteem.
- Root: سها (sahā)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Neglect, heedlessness, inattention; the one who is "sāhin" is oblivious to the essence and time of an act.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): السهو is the heart's vacancy from awareness of the true import of an affair; in the verse {الذين هم عن صلاتهم ساهون} it denotes neglect of the prayer's time and conditions, coupled with ostentation in performing it.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: distraction. Metaphorical: the soul's diversion from the Hereafter toward the gaze of creatures.
- Root: مكر (makara)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Crafty scheming, deception; the "makr" of the ostentatious is their covert corruption of good deeds.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): المكر is the turning of another from his intent by subtle concealment; the "sayyi'āt" (evil deeds) of the riyā' practitioners are their acts of worship corrupted by show — their scheming "yabūr" (perishes) because it is built on other than God.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: stratagem. Metaphorical: the hypocritical display of piety as a ruse to capture hearts — a "makr" that boomerangs to perdition.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — In {إنما نطعمكم لوجه الله}, the particle إنما confines the motive exclusively to God's Face, negating all secondary aims (جزاء or شكورا); this is the grammatical seal of ikhlāṣ against riyā'.

107:4.arabic: أما الآيات فقوله تعالى فويل للمصلين الذين هم عن صلاتهم ساهون الذين هم يراءون وقوله عز وجل والذين يمكرون السيئات لهم عذاب شديد ومكر أولئك هو يبور قال مجاهد هم أهل الرياء وقال تعالى إنما نطعمكم لوجه الله لا نريد منكم جزاء ولا شكورا فمدح المخلصين ينفي كل إرادة سوى وجه الله والرياء ضده وقال تعالى فمن كان يرجو لقاء ربه فليعمل عملا صالحا ولا يشرك بعبادة ربه أحدا // حديث نزول قوله تعالى فمن كان يرجو لقاء ربه الآية فيمن يطلب الآخرة بعباداته وأعماله أخرجه الحاكم من حديث طاوس قال رجل إني أقف الموقف أبتغي وجه الله وأحب أن يرى
