3:54.arabic: مكرا ومكرنا مكرا وهم لا يشعرون وقال عز وجل ومكروا ومكر الله والله خير الماكرين وقال تعالى إنهم يكيدون كيدا وأكيد كيدا فمهل الكافرين أمهلهم رويدا فكما لا يجوز للعبد المهمل أن يستدل بإهمال السيد إياه وتمكينه من النعم على حب السيد بل ينبغي أن يحذر أن يكون ذلك مكرا منه وكيدا مع أن السيد لم يحذره مكر نفسه فبأن يجب ذلك في حق الله تعالى مع تحذيره استدراجه أولى فإذن من أمن مكر الله فهو مغتر ومنشأ هذا الغرور أنه استدل بنعم الدنيا على أنه كريم عند ذلك المنعم واحتمل أن يكون ذلك دليل الهوان ولكن ذلك الاحتمال لا يوافق الهوى فالشيطان بواس
3:54.english: As for knowing it by way of authoritative transmission and affirmation (taṣdīq): it is that one believes in the Book of God — exalted is He — and affirms His Messenger. For God — exalted is He — has said: {«أيحسبون أن ما نمدهم به من مال وبنين * نسارع لهم في الخيرات بل لا يشعرون»} — "Do they reckon that what We extend to them of wealth and sons — [that] We hasten for them good things? Nay, but they do not perceive" (Q. 23:55-56). And He said — exalted is He: {«سنستدرجهم من حيث لا يعلمون»} — "We shall draw them on by degrees from whence they do not know" (Q. 7:182). And He said — exalted is He: {«فتحنا عليهم أبواب كل شيء حتى إذا فرحوا بما أوتوا أخذناهم بغتة فإذا هم مبلسون»} — "We opened upon them the gates of everything, until when they rejoiced in what they were given, We seized them suddenly, and behold, they were in despair" (Q. 6:44). And in the interpretation of His saying — exalted is He: {«سنستدرجهم من حيث لا يعلمون»} — it is said: "Whenever they innovated a sin, We innovated for them a blessing, to increase their self-deception." And He said — exalted is He: {«إنما نملي لهم ليزدادوا إثما»} — "We only grant them respite that they may increase in sin" (Q. 3:178). And He said — exalted is He: {«ولا تحسبن الله غافلا عما يعمل الظالمون إنما يؤخرهم ليوم تشخص فيه الأبصار»} — "And do not reckon God heedless of what the wrongdoers do; He only delays them to a Day when eyes will stare fixedly" (Q. 14:42). And [there is] more of that kind which has come in the Book of God — exalted is He — and in the Sunnah of His Messenger. So whoever believes in it is delivered from this self-deception. For the origin of this self-deception is ignorance of God and of His attributes; for whoever knows Him does not feel secure from His stratagem (makr) and is not deceived by such corrupt fancies.
3:54.section_title_en: Section 888 — On the Remedy for Self-Deception (Ghurūr): Recognizing the Signs of Divine Honor (Karāmah) and Humiliation (Hawān)
3:54.anchors:
- Root: غرر (gh-r-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of an outward trace or mark; heedlessness in wakefulness; the blaze on a horse's forehead.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Ghurūr" is delusion stemming from heedlessness — the soul's being overtaken while imagining security, as in {«ما غرك بربك الكريم»} (Q. 82:6). It is the state of one who is deceived by apparent favors while blind to their underlying test.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): heedlessness and exposure to predation, like a gazelle deceived by moonlight. Metaphorical (Majaz): being "deceived by God" (ightirār billāh) — trusting in His mercy while persisting in disobedience.
- Root: لهم (l-h-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Swallowing whole; the gullet.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Ilhām" — God's casting a meaning into the heart (al-raw'), distinct from demonic whispering; the channel of inner vision for the knowers (ʿārifūn).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: to swallow. Metaphorical: the heart's receptive "swallowing" of divine inspiration.
- Root: حدث (ḥ-d-th)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Origination after non-existence; newness.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Ḥudūth" — a thing's coming to be after it was not; "muḥdith" — the originator, exclusively God for substances (jawāhir). "Iḥdāth" — bringing about a novel state or act.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: temporal newness. Metaphorical: "muḥaddath" — one inspired with correct discernment, as if newly spoken-to.
- Root: نعم (n-ʿ-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Softness, ease, well-being; a state of comfort.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Niʿmah" — the good state one inhabits; "naʿīm" — the act of living pleasantly. Blessings are both a test and a sign, per {«وإن تعدوا نعمة الله لا تحصوها»} (Q. 16:18).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: bounty and comfort. Metaphorical: "khafat naʿāmatuhum" — their prosperity vanished; blessings may signal either favor or gradual ruin (istidrāj).
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction and Focused Predication with "innamā")
  * In {«إنما نملي لهم ليزدادوا إثما»} (Q. 3:178) and {«إنما يؤخرهم ليوم تشخص فيه الأبصار»} (Q. 14:42), "innamā" restricts the purpose of divine respite exclusively to increase of sin and deferred reckoning — negating any reading of it as benevolent indulgence.
3:54.topic: Al-Ghazali on purifying the character, moral diseases, and spiritual remedies, from 'Condemnation of Delusion'

3:198.arabic: الليل يتلذذ به في رجاء إنعامه والرجاء في حق الله تعالى أصدق وما عند الله خير وأبقى وأنفع مما عند غيره فكيف لا يتلذذ بعرض الحاجات عليه في الخلوات وأما النقل فيشهد له أحوال قوام الليل في تلذذهم بقيام الليل واستقصارهم له كما يستقصر المحب ليلة وصال الحبيب حتى قيل لبعضهم كيف أنت والليل قال ما راعيته قط يريني وجهه ثم ينصرف وما تأملته بعد وقال آخر أنا والليل فرسا رهان مرة يسبقني إلى الفجر ومرة يقطعني عن الفكر وقيل لبعضهم كيف الليل عليك فقال ساعة أنا فيها بين حالتين أفرح بظلمته إذا جاء وأغتم بفجره إذا طلع ما تم فرحي به قط وقال علي بن
3:198.english: That if the beautiful Beloved were behind a veil or in a dark house, the lover would still take delight in mere proximity to Him, without vision and without coveting any other matter besides Him — and he would find joy in displaying his love before Him and in mentioning Him with his tongue within His hearing, even though that too were already known to Him. For if you say: "He awaits His response" — then let him delight in hearing His response; yet he does not hear the speech of God, exalted be He. Know then that if he knows that He will not answer him and will remain silent toward him, there still remains for him a delight in presenting his states before Him and in raising his innermost secret to Him. How [could it be otherwise], when the one who is certain (al-mūqin) hears from God, exalted be He, everything that occurs to his mind during the course of his whispered communion (munājāh), and thus takes delight in it? Likewise, one who secludes himself with a king and presents his needs to him in the depths of the night takes delight in it through hope of his beneficence — and hope with respect to God, exalted be He, is more truthful, and what is with God is better, more enduring, and more beneficial than what is with anyone else. So how would he not delight in presenting his needs before Him in private seclusions (khalawāt)?
3:198.section_title_en: On the Delight of Night Vigil and Whispered Communion — Section 277
3:198.anchors:
- Root: ليل (layl)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Night; the period of darkness following sunset until dawn; its diminutive is 'luyaylah' and its plural is 'layālin' — indicating a temporal span marked by stillness and concealment.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Night (al-layl) is that which veils (yughashshī) and covers, as in {«وَاللَّيْلِ إِذَا يَغْشَى»} — a time when sensory distractions recede and the heart turns toward intimate communion (munājāh) with the Divine.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (haqīqah): the astronomical night. Metaphorical (majāz): the night of the heart — a state of spiritual wakefulness wherein the lover finds delight in solitude with the Beloved, as expressed in the sayings of the pious transmitted herein.
- Root: نور (nūr)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Light; illumination that renders things visible; also the fire-kindling and the beacon (manār) guiding travelers.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Light is of two kinds: sensory light perceived by the eye, and intellectual/spiritual light (nūr al-ʿaql, nūr al-Qurʾān) perceived by the inner eye of insight (baṣīrah). The Divine light cast into the hearts of the vigilant is of this latter kind — an immaterial radiance (laṭīfah nūrāniyyah) that transforms the inner state.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical illumination. Metaphorical: 'nawwara al-amr' — to clarify and illuminate a matter; here, the spreading of spiritual lights (anwār) from wakeful hearts to heedless ones is a metaphorical extension of this root, signifying the transmission of divine grace.
- Root: قلب (qalb)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The heart; also the turning and revolving of a thing from one state to another (taqlīb).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The heart is so named for its constant fluctuation (taqallub) between states; it is the seat of perception and understanding, the locus of divine address and the receptacle of spiritual lights.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the physical organ. Metaphorical: 'qallaba al-amr' — to examine and turn over a matter; here, the hearts of the vigilant are 'turned over' by divine light, and from them 'spread' (tantašir) blessings to others — a metaphorical extension of physical turning to spiritual transformation.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — The particle 'innamā' restricts and confines the predicate to the subject alone, as in the transmitted saying: "The delight of whispered communion is not of this world; it is only (innamā) of Paradise" — a focused predication that negates any worldly share of this pleasure and affirms its exclusive otherworldly origin.
3:198.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Condemnation of Delusion'

4:4.arabic: فإن طبن لكم عن شيء منه نفسا فكلوه هنيئا مريئا وطيبة النفس غير طيبة القلب فقد يريد الإنسان بقلبه ما لا تطيب به نفسه فإنه يريد الحجامة بقلبه ولكن تكرهها نفسه وإنما طيبة النفس أن تسمح نفسها بالإبراء لا عن ضرورة تقابله حتى إذا رددت بين ضررين اختارت أهونهما فهذه مصادرة على التحقيق بإكراه الباطن نعم القاضي في الدنيا لا يطلع على القلوب والأغراض فينظر إلى الإبراء الظاهر وأنها لم تكره بسبب ظاهر والإكراه الباطن ليس يطلع الخلق عليه ولكن مهما تصدى القاضي الأكبر في صعيد القيامة للقضاء لم يكن هذا محسوبا ولا مقيدا
4:4.english: ...with your heart, and there is no sound copy which you have verified in order to collate against it — so from where do you know that you have heard it? For God Most High has said: {«وَلَا تَقْفُ مَا لَيْسَ لَكَ بِهِ عِلْمٌ»} "And do not pursue that of which you have no knowledge" {«الإسراء/36»}. And the statement of all the shaykhs in this age — "We have heard what is in this book" — when the condition we have mentioned is not met, is outright falsehood.
4:4.section_title_en: On the Conditions of Valid Hadith Audition and the Deception of Those Who Neglect the Heart's Work
4:4.anchors:
- Root: سمع (s-m-')
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning is hearing/perception of sound; also used for understanding and acceptance (isti'mal fi al-qabul).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Hearing (al-sam') is the perception of sound; in the religious law it denotes the transmission of the Prophet's speech with retention (hifz) and comprehension (fahm), distinguishing it from mere acoustic reception.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (haqiqah) is the ear's reception of sound; metaphorical (majaz) is the heart's acceptance and compliance. The deception here lies in conflating acoustic presence with valid scholarly transmission.
- Root: غرر (gh-r-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The root denotes heedlessness (ghiflah) and being deceived by appearances; al-ghurur is false reliance on that which has no firm basis.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Gharrartu fulanan: I struck his heedlessness and obtained from him what I sought." The root implies an outward trace (athar) that misleads, as in the saying "he folded it upon its crease" — i.e., acted on an unexamined assumption.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: one who is heedless (ghafil). Metaphorical: the one who is deceived by the outer shell (qishr) of knowledge while missing its kernel (lubb), like the gazelle that ventures out on a moonlit night thinking it is day.
- Root: قلب (q-l-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The heart as the organ of fluctuation and turning (taqallub); its movement between states.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The heart (qalb) is that subtle reality (latifah) which is the locus of understanding (fahm) and discernment ('aql); it is the seat of intention (niyyah) and volition (iradah).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the physical organ. Metaphorical: the inner faculty of cognition and moral discrimination, which is the true addressee of the Law's commands.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — The construction "إنما المقصود كذا" restricts the predicate exclusively to the intended object, negating all else. This governs the author's repeated reframing of means (wasail) versus ends (maqasid).
4:4.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Condemnation of Delusion'

8:47.arabic: وأما هؤلاء فإنهم يصدون عن سبيل الله ويجرون الخلق إلى الغرور بالله بلفظ الرجاء فيزيدهم كلامهم جراءة على المعاصي ورغبة في الدنيا لا سيما إذا كان الواعظ متزينا بالثياب والخيل والمراكب فإنه تشهد هيئته من فرقه إلى قدمه بشدة حرصه على الدنيا فما يفسده هذا المغرور أكثر مما يصلحه بل لا يصلح أصلا ويضل خلقا كثيرا ولا يخفى وجه كونه مغرورا وفرقة أخرى منهم قنعوا بحفظ كلام الزهاد وأحاديثهم في ذم الدنيا فهم يحفظون الكلمات على وجهها ويؤدونها من غير إحاطة بمعانيها فبعضهم يفعل ذلك على المنابر وبعضهم
8:47.english: But as for these [deluded ones], they turn others away from the path of God and drag creation into self-deception concerning God (al-ghurūr billāh) by means of the word "hope" (al-rajāʾ). Thus their speech increases them in audacity toward sins and desire for this world — especially when the preacher is adorned with fine garments, horses, and mounts, for his very appearance bears witness from his hair to his feet to his intense greed for this world. So what this deluded one corrupts is more than what he reforms — nay, he reforms nothing at all, and he leads many people astray. Nor is the aspect of his being deluded hidden.
8:47.section_title_en: The Categories of the Deluded Among Preachers and Hadith Transmitters
8:47.anchors:
- Root: أ-ص-ل (ʾ-ṣ-l)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of foundation, root, and origin; to set right what is corrupt.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): اصلاح (iṣlāḥ) as the act of bringing something from a state of corruption (fasād) to soundness (ṣalāḥ), whether in belief, action, or speech.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) usage denotes rectifying a physical object; metaphorical (majāz) usage applies to moral and spiritual correction of others.
- Root: غ-ر-ر (gh-r-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: غرور (ghurūr) — deception, delusion, vanity; from غرّ (gharra), to be heedless or deceived by appearances.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): الغرور (al-ghurūr) is the delusion that leads one to rely on false hopes, particularly regarding God's mercy while persisting in sin; the state of one who is deceived by Satan or by his own vain fancies.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: a thing that deceives by its outward show; Metaphorical: the soul's self-deception through false reliance on divine forgiveness without repentance.
- Root: س-م-ع (s-m-ʿ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: السمع (al-samʿ) — hearing; the auditory faculty and its act.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Hearing as the means of acquiring transmitted knowledge (samāʿ); in hadith terminology, the formal act of hearing a tradition from a shaykh, which is the first stage of transmission.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the physical act of hearing; Metaphorical: attentive listening with the heart, as in "ألقى السمع وهو شهيد" {«وَأَلْقَى السَّمْعَ وَهُوَ شَهِيدٌ»} [Q. 50:37] — one who listens with full presence of mind.
- Root: ح-ف-ظ (ḥ-f-ẓ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: الحفظ (al-ḥifẓ) — preservation, guarding, memorization; keeping something safe from loss or alteration.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): الحفظ is the faculty of the soul by which what is understood is retained; its opposite is forgetfulness (nisyān). It also denotes vigilant care and protection.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: guarding a physical object; Metaphorical: committing knowledge to memory such that it is preserved from distortion.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The rule governing the separation of a preposition from its object by intervening clauses, as in the periodic structure "فإذا لم تحفظ لا بالقلب ولا بالكتاب وجرى على سمعك صوت غفل" where the conditional clause (فإذا) governs a sequence of coordinated conditions, each requiring its own apodosis, demonstrating the classical pattern of layered conditional sentences.
8:47.topic: Al-Ghazali on purifying the character, moral diseases, and spiritual remedies, from 'Condemnation of Delusion'

9:104.arabic: والله يعلم ما في أنفسكم فاحذروه فاستغفرت الله في سري فناداني وقال {وهو الذي يقبل التوبة عن عباده} ثم غاب عني ولم أره وقال زكريا بن داود دخل أبو العباس بن مسروق على أبي الفضل الهاشمي وهو عليل وكان ذا عيال ولم يعرف له سبب يعيش به قال فلما قمت قلت في نفسي من أين يأكل هذا الرجل قال فصاح بي يا أبا العباس رد هذه الهمة الدنية فإن لله تعالى ألطافا خفية وقال أحمد النقيب دخلت على الشبلي فقال مفتونا يا أحمد فقلت ما الخبر قال كنت جالسا فجرى بخاطري أنك بخيل فقلت ما أنا بخيل فعاد مني خاطري وقال بل أنت بخيل فقلت ما فتح اليوم علي بشيء إلا دفعته
9:104.english: As for the evidences of the Sacred Law, there is His saying (Exalted is He): {«وَالَّذِينَ جَاهَدُوا فِينَا لَنَهْدِيَنَّهُمْ سُبُلَنَا»} ("And those who strive in Us, We shall surely guide them to Our paths") (Q. 29:69). So every wisdom that appears from the heart through persevering devotion to worship, without learning, is by way of unveiling and inspiration. And he (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Whoever acts upon what he knows, God bequeaths to him knowledge of what he does not know, and grants him success in what he does" — until he becomes deserving of Paradise. And whoever does not act upon what he knows wanders astray in what he knows and is not granted success in what he does, until he becomes deserving of the Fire. [The hadith "Whoever acts upon what he knows" has preceded in the Book of Knowledge, without his saying "and grants him success in what he does" — I have not found it with that addition.] And God (Exalted is He) said: {«وَمَنْ يَتَّقِ اللَّهَ يَجْعَلْ لَهُ مَخْرَجًا»} ("And whoever fears God, He makes for him a way out") (Q. 65:2) — from perplexities and doubts — {«وَيَرْزُقْهُ مِنْ حَيْثُ لَا يَحْتَسِبُ»} ("and provides for him from whence he does not reckon") (Q. 65:3) — teaching him knowledge without learning and granting him discernment without experience. And God (Exalted is He) said: {«يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا إِنْ تَتَّقُوا اللَّهَ يَجْعَلْ لَكُمْ فُرْقَانًا»} ("O you who believe, if you fear God, He will make for you a criterion") (Q. 8:29) — it is said: a light by which one distinguishes between truth and falsehood and by which one emerges from doubts. For this reason, he (peace and blessings be upon him) was abundant in his supplication in asking for light, saying (peace and blessings be upon him): "O God, grant me light, and increase me in light, and make for me light in my heart, and light in my grave, and light in my hearing, and light in my sight" — until he said: "and light in my hair, and in my skin, and in my flesh, and in my blood, and in my bones." [Agreed upon (by al-Bukhari and Muslim).] [The hadith concerning his being asked about His saying {«أَفَمَنْ شَرَحَ اللَّهُ صَدْرَهُ لِلْإِسْلَامِ»} ("Is he whose breast God has expanded for Islam") (Q. 39:22) — and in al-Mustadrak from the hadith of Ibn Masʿūd — has preceded in the Book of Knowledge.] And he (peace and blessings be upon him) said concerning Ibn ʿAbbās: "O God, grant him understanding in religion and teach him the interpretation (taʾwīl)." [The hadith of ʿAlī: "We have nothing with us that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) confided to us except that God grants a servant understanding in His Book" — has preceded in the Etiquettes of Qurʾanic Recitation.] And it is said in the interpretation of His saying (Exalted is He): {«يُؤْتِي الْحِكْمَةَ مَنْ يَشَاءُ»} ("He grants wisdom to whom He wills") (Q. 2:269) that it is understanding in the Book of God. And He (Exalted is He) said: {«فَفَهَّمْنَاهَا سُلَيْمَانَ»} ("And We made Solomon understand it") (Q. 21:79) — singling out what was unveiled with the name of understanding (fahm). And Abū al-Dardāʾ used to say: "The believer is one who sees by the light of God from behind a thin veil. By God, it is the truth that God casts into their hearts and causes to flow upon their tongues." And some of the Salaf said: "The believer's conjecture is like soothsaying."
9:104.section_title_en: The Unveiling of Knowledge Through Divine Inspiration and the Evidences of the Unseen
9:104.anchors:
- Root: علم (ʿalima)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning encompasses both perception of a thing's essence and judgment upon it—knowledge as direct apprehension or discursive ruling.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "العلم: إدراك الشيء بحقيقته" — knowledge is the apprehension of a thing in its true reality, divided into apprehension of the essence (transitive to one object) and judgment upon existence or non-existence (transitive to two objects).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal usage denotes certainty and awareness ("ما علمت بخبرك: ما شعرت به"); metaphorical extension applies to marks, signs, and beacons of guidance (معالم الطريق) — here, the inspired knowledge is a "mark" of the path.
- Root: كشف (kashafa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To remove a covering, unveil, disclose what was hidden.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Unveiling (kashf) in theological terms is the removal of the veil (ghishāwah) from the heart such that the realities of things become directly witnessed, not merely inferred.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: to lift a covering from a thing; metaphorical: the disclosure of inward states and hidden matters — the heart's eye perceives what the outward senses cannot.
- Root: فرس (farasa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To prey upon, devour; farāsah — the lion's pouncing upon its prey.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Discernment (farāsah) is a spiritual perception by which the believer penetrates into the inner states of others, a light cast by God into the heart.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the beast of prey seizing its quarry; metaphorical: the believer's insight seizing the truth of a matter or the hidden state of a person — "اتقوا فراسة المؤمن فإنه ينظر بنور الله."
- Root: حدث (ḥadatha)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To be new, originate after non-existence; muḥaddath — one who is spoken to, inspired with true speech from the unseen.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الحدوث: كون الشيء بعد أن لم يكن" — origination after non-existence; the muḥaddath is one to whom divine inspiration comes as a new, immediate occurrence without acquired means.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: newness of a thing; metaphorical: "كان عمر رضي الله عنه محدثا أي صادق الحدس، كأنما حدث بما ظن" — one whose intuition is so true it is as if he were directly spoken to.
- Sibawayh Rule: Restriction and specification (الحصر والتقييد) — the particle "إنما" and conditional clauses (إن/إذا) restrict predicates to their subjects, as in "إنما العالم الذي يأخذ علمه من ربه" — the true scholar is exclusively the one who takes knowledge from his Lord.
9:104.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Condemnation of Delusion'

11:45.arabic: السفينة فلم يرد فكان من المغرقين فقال رب إن ابني من أهلي فقال تعالى يا نوح إنه ليس من أهلك إنه عمل غير صالح وأن إبراهيم عليه السلام استغفر لأبيه فلم ينفعه وأن نبينا صلى الله عليه وسلم وعلى كل عبد مصطفى استأذن ربه في أن يزور قبر أمه ويستغفر لها فأذن له في الزيارة ولم يؤذن له في الاستغفار فجلس يبكي على قبر أمه لرقته لها بسبب القرابة حتى أبكى من حوله // حديث أنه صلى الله عليه وسلم استأذن أن يزور قبر أمه ويستغفر لها فأذن له في الزيارة ولم يؤذن له الاستغفار الحديث أخرجه مسلم من حديث أبي هريرة فهذا أيضا اغترار بالله
11:45.english: As for knowing it by way of authoritative transmission and affirmation (taṣdīq): it is that one believes in the Book of God — exalted is He — and affirms His Messenger. For God — exalted is He — has said: {«أيحسبون أن ما نمدهم به من مال وبنين * نسارع لهم في الخيرات بل لا يشعرون»} — "Do they reckon that what We extend to them of wealth and sons — [that] We hasten for them good things? Nay, but they do not perceive" (Q. 23:55-56). And He said — exalted is He: {«سنستدرجهم من حيث لا يعلمون»} — "We shall draw them on by degrees from whence they do not know" (Q. 7:182). And He said — exalted is He: {«فتحنا عليهم أبواب كل شيء حتى إذا فرحوا بما أوتوا أخذناهم بغتة فإذا هم مبلسون»} — "We opened upon them the gates of everything, until when they rejoiced in what they were given, We seized them suddenly, and behold, they were in despair" (Q. 6:44). And in the interpretation of His saying — exalted is He: {«سنستدرجهم من حيث لا يعلمون»} — it is said: "Whenever they innovated a sin, We innovated for them a blessing, to increase their self-deception." And He said — exalted is He: {«إنما نملي لهم ليزدادوا إثما»} — "We only grant them respite that they may increase in sin" (Q. 3:178). And He said — exalted is He: {«ولا تحسبن الله غافلا عما يعمل الظالمون إنما يؤخرهم ليوم تشخص فيه الأبصار»} — "And do not reckon God heedless of what the wrongdoers do; He only delays them to a Day when eyes will stare fixedly" (Q. 14:42). And [there is] more of that kind which has come in the Book of God — exalted is He — and in the Sunnah of His Messenger. So whoever believes in it is delivered from this self-deception. For the origin of this self-deception is ignorance of God and of His attributes; for whoever knows Him does not feel secure from His stratagem (makr) and is not deceived by such corrupt fancies.
11:45.section_title_en: Section 888 — On the Remedy for Self-Deception (Ghurūr): Recognizing the Signs of Divine Honor (Karāmah) and Humiliation (Hawān)
11:45.anchors:
- Root: غرر (gh-r-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of an outward trace or mark; heedlessness in wakefulness; the blaze on a horse's forehead.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Ghurūr" is delusion stemming from heedlessness — the soul's being overtaken while imagining security, as in {«ما غرك بربك الكريم»} (Q. 82:6). It is the state of one who is deceived by apparent favors while blind to their underlying test.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): heedlessness and exposure to predation, like a gazelle deceived by moonlight. Metaphorical (Majaz): being "deceived by God" (ightirār billāh) — trusting in His mercy while persisting in disobedience.
- Root: لهم (l-h-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Swallowing whole; the gullet.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Ilhām" — God's casting a meaning into the heart (al-raw'), distinct from demonic whispering; the channel of inner vision for the knowers (ʿārifūn).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: to swallow. Metaphorical: the heart's receptive "swallowing" of divine inspiration.
- Root: حدث (ḥ-d-th)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Origination after non-existence; newness.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Ḥudūth" — a thing's coming to be after it was not; "muḥdith" — the originator, exclusively God for substances (jawāhir). "Iḥdāth" — bringing about a novel state or act.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: temporal newness. Metaphorical: "muḥaddath" — one inspired with correct discernment, as if newly spoken-to.
- Root: نعم (n-ʿ-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Softness, ease, well-being; a state of comfort.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Niʿmah" — the good state one inhabits; "naʿīm" — the act of living pleasantly. Blessings are both a test and a sign, per {«وإن تعدوا نعمة الله لا تحصوها»} (Q. 16:18).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: bounty and comfort. Metaphorical: "khafat naʿāmatuhum" — their prosperity vanished; blessings may signal either favor or gradual ruin (istidrāj).
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction and Focused Predication with "innamā")
  * In {«إنما نملي لهم ليزدادوا إثما»} (Q. 3:178) and {«إنما يؤخرهم ليوم تشخص فيه الأبصار»} (Q. 14:42), "innamā" restricts the purpose of divine respite exclusively to increase of sin and deferred reckoning — negating any reading of it as benevolent indulgence.
11:45.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'Condemnation of Delusion'

  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: bounty and comfort. Metaphorical: "khafat naʿāmatuhum" — their prosperity vanished; blessings may signal either favor or gradual ruin (istidrāj).
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction and Focused Predication with "innamā")
  * In {«إنما نملي لهم ليزدادوا إثما»} (Q. 3:178) and {«إنما يؤخرهم ليوم تشخص فيه الأبصار»} (Q. 14:42), "innamā" restricts the purpose of divine respite exclusively to increase of sin and deferred reckoning — negating any reading of it as benevolent indulgence.

12:38.arabic: الجميل بجماله وعجب الغني بغناه لأن كل ذلك من فضل الله وإنما هو محل لفيضان فضل الله تعالى وجوده والمحل أيضا من فضله وجوده فإن قلت لا يمكنني أن أجهل أعمالي وإني أنا عملتها فإني أنتظر عليها ثوابا ولولا أنها عملي لما انتظرت ثوابا فإن كانت الأعمال مخلوقة لله على سبيل الاختراع فمن أين لي الثواب وإن كانت الأعمال مني وبقدرته فكيف لا أعجب بها فاعلم أن جوابك من وجهين أحدهما هو صريح الحق والآخر فيه مسامحة أما صريح الحق فهو أنك وقدرتك وإرادتك وحركتك وجميع ذلك من خلق الله واختراعه فما عملت إذ عملت وما صليت إذ ص
12:38.english: ...and you were not pleased with it. Then He gave you a servant, and you became pleased with it, saying: "He only gave me a servant because I am a horse-owner; as for another, he has no horse." So it is said: He is the One who gave you the horse — there is no difference between His giving you the horse and the servant together, or His giving you one after the other. Since all of it is from Him, it behooves you to admire His bounty and favor, not yourself.
12:38.section_title_en: On the Vanity of Self-Admiration in Acts of Worship — The True Source of Grace and the Illusion of Personal Agency
12:38.anchors:
- Root: عجب (ʿajiba)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Astonishment, wonder, and self-amazement; the state of being struck by something marvelous.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Self-admiration (ʿujb) is blameworthy when directed at one's own acts, as it implies a false attribution of agency to the self rather than to God.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: wonder at a thing's beauty or rarity. Metaphorical: wonder at oneself, which is a delusion when all causes proceed from another.
- Root: خلق (khalaqa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To measure, fashion, and originate; creation as divine act of bringing into being.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Creation (khalq) is the origination of a thing from nothing without prior model, or the bringing forth of one thing from another by divine decree.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: shaping and proportioning. Metaphorical: God's absolute origination of all acts, attributes, and agents — exclusive to Him.
- Root: قدر (qadara)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Power, capacity, and measure; the ability to bring about an act.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Divine power (qudrah) is the negation of incapacity; human power is a created instrument, not an independent source of effect.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: ability over a specific thing. Metaphorical: the key (miftāḥ) to action, which is entirely in God's hand.
- Root: قلب (qalaba)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To turn, overturn, or transform; the heart as the seat of volition and understanding.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The heart (qalb) is the locus of knowledge and will; its turning is directed by God alone.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical turning. Metaphorical: the heart's inclination and the divine disposal of its states.
- Sibawayh Rule: Restriction and Focused Predication (باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما) — The particle "innamā" restricts the predicate to the subject alone, used here to expose the fallacy of self-attribution in the hypothetical objection.
12:38.topic: Al-Ghazali on purifying the character, moral diseases, and spiritual remedies, from 'Condemnation of Delusion'

14:1.arabic: {يخرجهم من الظلمات إلى النور} وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم يا أيها الناس اعقلوا عن ربكم وتواصوا بالعقل تعرفوا ما أمرتم به وما نهيتم عنه واعلموا أنه ينجدكم عند ربكم واعلموا أن العاقل من أطاع الله وإن كان دميم المنظر حقير الخطر دنيء المنزلة رث الهيئة وأن الجاهل من عصى الله تعالى وإن كان جميل المنظر عظيم الخطر شريف المنزلة حسن الهيئة فصيحا نطوقا فالقردة والخنازير أعقل عند الله تعالى ممن عصاه ولا تغتر بتعظيم أهل الدنيا إياهم فإنهم من الخاسرين (2) وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم أول ما خل
14:1.english: The Book of Seclusion ('Uzlah) — its explanation, God Most High willing. For this reason, Yūsuf ibn Asbāṭ wrote to Ḥudhayfah al-Marʿashī: "What is your opinion of one who remains, finding no one with whom to remember God Most High except that he is either sinful, or his remembrance in company is itself an act of disobedience — and that because he finds no one of his own kind?" And indeed he spoke truly, for mixing with people is never free from backbiting (ghībah), or listening to backbiting, or remaining silent upon wrongdoing (munkar). And the best of his states is that he either imparts knowledge or acquires it. Yet were this poor wretch to reflect, and to know that his imparting of knowledge is never free from the taints of ostentation (riyā'), the seeking of followers, and the desire for leadership (ri'āsah), he would know that the one who acquires knowledge from him only seeks to make it an instrument for pursuing the world and a means toward evil — so that the teacher becomes his helper therein, his support and his backer, preparing its causes for him, like one who sells a sword to a highway robber. For knowledge is like the sword: its soundness for good is like the soundness of the sword for warfare. And for this reason, it is not permitted to sell it to one whom one knows, by the indications of his circumstances, intends to use it to aid in cutting off the road.
14:1.section_title_en: The Book of Seclusion ('Uzlah) — Section 65, and The Seventh Book: On the Intellect, Its Nobility, Its Reality, and Its Divisions
14:1.anchors:
- Root: عقل (ʿaql)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The root denotes binding, restraining, and holding back; the intellect is that which restrains the soul from base desires and prevents it from straying.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "العقل يقال للقوة المتهيئة لقبول العلم، ويقال للعلم الذي يستفيده الإنسان بتلك القوة عقل" — The intellect is said of the faculty prepared for the reception of knowledge, and it is also said of the knowledge which man acquires by means of that faculty.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): intellectual apprehension and understanding. Metaphorical (Majaz): "نخلة لا تعقل الإبار" — a palm tree that does not accept pollination, i.e., does not grasp or take in.
- Root: علم (ʿilm)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Knowledge as the mark or sign by which a thing is known; the trace or landmark that guides.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "العلم: إدراك الشيء بحقيقته" — Knowledge is the apprehension of a thing in its true reality; it is of two kinds: apprehension of the essence of a thing, and judgment upon a thing regarding what exists for it or is negated of it.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: certain awareness. Metaphorical: "هو من أعلام العلم الخافقه" — he is among the lofty banners of knowledge; knowledge as a guiding landmark (maʿlam).
- Root: نور (nūr)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Light; the first to set up beacons (manār) on his path in his campaigns to guide his return.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "النور: الضوء المنتشر الذي يعين على الإبصار" — Light is the diffused radiance that aids vision; it is of two kinds: that perceived by the eye of inner insight (baṣīrah) — such as the light of the intellect and the light of the Qur'an — and that perceived by the eye of the head, such as the celestial bodies.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: illumination. Metaphorical: "نور الأمر: بينه" — he illuminated the matter: he made it clear; "وهذا أنور من ذاك: أبين" — this is more luminous than that: more evident.
- Sibawayh Rule: Restriction and Focused Predication (al-ḥaṣr wa al-taqyīd bi-innamā) — governing the exclusive attribution of a predicate to a subject, as in the author's restriction of the scholar's condition to one of two men, and the exclusion of the third.
14:1.topic: Al-Ghazali on constant remembrance of God and contemplative invocations, from 'Condemnation of Delusion'

19:77.arabic: فأنزل الله تعالى قوله أفرأيت الذي كفر بآياتنا وقال لأوتين مالا وولدا (1) حديث إن الله يحمي عبده من الدنيا وهو يحبه الحديث أخرجه الترمذي وحسنه والحاكم وصححه من حديث قتادة بن النعمان هكذا ورد في الخبر عن سيد البشر وكان أرباب البصائر إذا أقبلت عليهم الدنيا حزنوا وقالوا ذنب عجلت عقوبته ورأوا ذلك علامة المقت والإهمال وإذا أقبل عليهم الفقر قالوا مرحبا بشعار الصالحين والمغرور إذا أقبلت عليه الدنيا ظن أنها كرامة من الله وإذا صرفت عنه ظن أنها هوان كما أخبر الله تعالى عنه إذ قال فأما الإنسان إذا ما ابتلاه ربه فأكرمه ون
19:77.english: It was said of that sort, so they are falsehoods (akādhīb). And even if it were so, then "there will surely be for me in Paradise better than this" {«لَيَكُونَنَّ لِي فِي الْجَنَّةِ خَيْرٌ مِنْ هَذَا»}. Likewise, God Most High described the saying of al-ʿĀṣ ibn Wāʾil when he said, "I will surely be given wealth and children" {«لَأُوتَيَنَّ مَالًا وَوَلَدًا»}. So God Most High replied to him: "Has he looked into the unseen, or has he taken with the Most Merciful a covenant? No indeed (kallā)" {«أَطَّلَعَ الْغَيْبَ أَمِ اتَّخَذَ عِنْدَ الرَّحْمَنِ عَهْدًا كَلَّا»}. And it is related from Khabbāb ibn al-Aratt that he said: I had a debt owed to me by al-ʿĀṣ ibn Wāʾil, so I came demanding payment, but he did not pay me. So I said, "I will indeed take it from you in the Hereafter." He said to me, "When you come to the Hereafter, I will have there wealth and children, and I will pay you from it." So God Most High revealed His saying: "Have you seen the one who disbelieved in Our signs and said, 'I will surely be given wealth and children'?" {«أَفَرَأَيْتَ الَّذِي كَفَرَ بِآيَاتِنَا وَقَالَ لَأُوتَيَنَّ مَالًا وَوَلَدًا»}. (1) The hadith "God protects His servant from the world while loving him" — narrated by al-Tirmidhī who deemed it good (ḥasan), and by al-Ḥākim who deemed it authentic (ṣaḥīḥ), from the report of Qatādah ibn al-Nuʿmān. Thus it came in the report from the master of mankind (peace be upon him).
19:77.section_title_en: The Delusion of Wealth and the Reality of Divine Trial — Section 887
19:77.anchors:
- Root: كلا (Kalla)
  * Lisan / Ayn: An emphatic particle of denial and refutation; signifies categorical rejection of a prior claim.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Used to negate and refute utterly; here, it rebuts the deluded assumption that wealth signals divine favor.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah) — a decisive "No!"; Metaphorical (Majaz) — not merely denying words but the very presumption underlying them.
- Root: حدث (Ḥadatha)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To originate, to be new; in Kalam, that which comes into being after non-existence.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الحدوث: كون الشيء بعد أن لم يكن" — origination of a thing after it was not; divine acts of trial are originated events.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — new occurrences; Metaphorical — "محدث" as one whose inner state is renewed by divine testing.
- Root: كذب (Kadhaba)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To lie, to falsify; a false report or claim.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Falsehood in word and deed; here, the disbeliever's boast is exposed as self-deception.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — verbal lying; Metaphorical — "كذبهما جميعا" (he declared both of them liars) — attributing falsity to the two human assumptions about wealth and poverty.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — "إنما هو ابتلاء" restricts the reality of wealth and poverty solely to divine testing, excluding the deluded interpretations of honor or humiliation.

23:55.arabic: رسوله وقد قال تعالى أيحسبون أن ما نمدهم به من مال وبنين نسارع لهم في الخيرات بل لا يشعرون وقال تعالى سنستدرجهم من حيث لا يعلمون وقال تعالى فتحنا عليهم أبواب كل شيء حتى إذا فرحوا بما أوتوا أخذناهم بغتة فإذا هم مبلسون وفي تفسير قوله تعالى سنستدرجهم من حيث لا يعلمون أنهم كلما أحدثوا ذنبا أحدثنا لهم نعمة ليزيد غرورهم وقال تعالى إنما نملي لهم ليزدادوا إثما وقال تعالى ولا تحسبن الله غافلا عما يعمل الظالمون إنما يؤخرهم ليوم تشخص فيه الأبصار إلى غير ذلك مما ورد في كتاب الله تعالى وسنة رسوله فمن آمن به تخلص من هذا الغرور فإن منشأ هذا الغرور الجهل ب
23:55.english: As for knowing it by way of authoritative transmission and affirmation (taṣdīq): it is that one believes in the Book of God — exalted is He — and affirms His Messenger. For God — exalted is He — has said: {«أيحسبون أن ما نمدهم به من مال وبنين * نسارع لهم في الخيرات بل لا يشعرون»} — "Do they reckon that what We extend to them of wealth and sons — [that] We hasten for them good things? Nay, but they do not perceive" (Q. 23:55-56). And He said — exalted is He: {«سنستدرجهم من حيث لا يعلمون»} — "We shall draw them on by degrees from whence they do not know" (Q. 7:182). And He said — exalted is He: {«فتحنا عليهم أبواب كل شيء حتى إذا فرحوا بما أوتوا أخذناهم بغتة فإذا هم مبلسون»} — "We opened upon them the gates of everything, until when they rejoiced in what they were given, We seized them suddenly, and behold, they were in despair" (Q. 6:44). And in the interpretation of His saying — exalted is He: {«سنستدرجهم من حيث لا يعلمون»} — it is said: "Whenever they innovated a sin, We innovated for them a blessing, to increase their self-deception." And He said — exalted is He: {«إنما نملي لهم ليزدادوا إثما»} — "We only grant them respite that they may increase in sin" (Q. 3:178). And He said — exalted is He: {«ولا تحسبن الله غافلا عما يعمل الظالمون إنما يؤخرهم ليوم تشخص فيه الأبصار»} — "And do not reckon God heedless of what the wrongdoers do; He only delays them to a Day when eyes will stare fixedly" (Q. 14:42). And [there is] more of that kind which has come in the Book of God — exalted is He — and in the Sunnah of His Messenger. So whoever believes in it is delivered from this self-deception. For the origin of this self-deception is ignorance of God and of His attributes; for whoever knows Him does not feel secure from His stratagem (makr) and is not deceived by such corrupt fancies.
23:55.section_title_en: Section 888 — On the Remedy for Self-Deception (Ghurūr): Recognizing the Signs of Divine Honor (Karāmah) and Humiliation (Hawān)
23:55.anchors:
- Root: غرر (gh-r-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of an outward trace or mark; heedlessness in wakefulness; the blaze on a horse's forehead.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Ghurūr" is delusion stemming from heedlessness — the soul's being overtaken while imagining security, as in {«ما غرك بربك الكريم»} (Q. 82:6). It is the state of one who is deceived by apparent favors while blind to their underlying test.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): heedlessness and exposure to predation, like a gazelle deceived by moonlight. Metaphorical (Majaz): being "deceived by God" (ightirār billāh) — trusting in His mercy while persisting in disobedience.
- Root: لهم (l-h-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Swallowing whole; the gullet.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Ilhām" — God's casting a meaning into the heart (al-raw'), distinct from demonic whispering; the channel of inner vision for the knowers (ʿārifūn).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: to swallow. Metaphorical: the heart's receptive "swallowing" of divine inspiration.
- Root: حدث (ḥ-d-th)

  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: temporal newness. Metaphorical: "muḥaddath" — one inspired with correct discernment, as if newly spoken-to.
- Root: نعم (n-ʿ-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Softness, ease, well-being; a state of comfort.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Niʿmah" — the good state one inhabits; "naʿīm" — the act of living pleasantly. Blessings are both a test and a sign, per {«وإن تعدوا نعمة الله لا تحصوها»} (Q. 16:18).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: bounty and comfort. Metaphorical: "khafat naʿāmatuhum" — their prosperity vanished; blessings may signal either favor or gradual ruin (istidrāj).
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction and Focused Predication with "innamā")
  * In {«إنما نملي لهم ليزدادوا إثما»} (Q. 3:178) and {«إنما يؤخرهم ليوم تشخص فيه الأبصار»} (Q. 14:42), "innamā" restricts the purpose of divine respite exclusively to increase of sin and deferred reckoning — negating any reading of it as benevolent indulgence.
23:55.topic: Al-Ghazali on constant remembrance of God and contemplative invocations, from 'Condemnation of Delusion'

25:42.arabic: عدا هؤلاء فهم المغرورون بالله وسوف يعلمون حين يرون العذاب من أضل سبيلا ولتعلمن نبأه بعد حين وعند ذلك يقولون كما أخبر الله عنهم ربنا أبصرنا وسمعنا فارجعنا نعمل صالحا إنا موقنون أي علمنا أنه كما لا يولد إلا بوقاع ونكاح ولا ينبت زرع إلا بحراثة وبث بذر فكذلك لا يحصل في الآخرة ثواب وأجر إلا بعمل صالح فارجعنا نعمل صالحا فقد علمنا الآن صدقك في قولك وأن ليس للإنسان إلا ما سعى وأن سعيه سوف يرى كلما ألقى فيها فوج سألهم خزنتها ألم يأتكم نذير قالوا بلى قد جاءنا نذير أي ألم نسمعكم سنة الله في عباده وأنه
25:42.english: I say: God—exalted is He—loves the obedient and hates the disobedient. So just as He does not hate the obedient father because of His hatred for the disobedient son, likewise He does not love the disobedient son because of His love for the obedient father. And if love were to flow from the father to the son, then hatred would likewise be bound to flow. Rather, the truth is: {«ولا تزر وازرة وزر أخرى»} — "And no bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another" {Quran 6:164, 17:15, 35:18, 39:7, 53:38}. And whoever supposes that he will be saved by his father's piety is like one who supposes he will be satiated by his father's eating, quenched by his father's drinking, become a scholar by his father's learning, and reach the Ka'bah and see it by his father's walking.
25:42.section_title_en: The Reality of Hope (Al-Rajā') and the Futility of Reliance on Another's Piety
25:42.anchors:
- Root: و ل د (walada)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Physical begetting and offspring; the father's generative act.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الولد: المولود" — offspring as a created entity; here used metaphorically for spiritual causation.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical birth. Metaphorical: "تولدت العصبية" — something generated or produced from another; Ghazali exploits this to refute the notion that a father's obedience "generates" salvation for the son.
- Root: ر ج و (rajā)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Expectation, hope, longing for a favorable outcome.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Hope tied to legitimate means; not mere wishful thinking (tamannī).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: awaiting rain. Metaphorical: "رجوت فلانا" — to expect from someone; Ghazali contrasts true hope (with action) vs. delusion (ghurūr).
- Root: غ ر ر (gharara)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Deception, heedlessness, being lured by a false appearance.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The state of one who is duped by Satan's plausible speech.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: a risky venture. Metaphorical: "اغتر بفلان" — to be deceived by outward charm while the inner reality is corrupt.
- Root: ك ي س (kays)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Intelligence, shrewdness, prudence.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The wise man who disciplines his soul and acts for the afterlife.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: alertness. Metaphorical: "الكيس من دان نفسه" — the prudent one who holds his soul to account; antonym of "الأحمق" (the fool).
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — "إنما يوفى الصابرون أجرهم بغير حساب" style; Ghazali uses "إنما" to restrict reward to personal action, and "ليس للإنسان إلا ما سعى" as a restrictive negative clause (nafy + illā) to deny any transfer of merit.
25:42.topic: Al-Ghazali on the journey of the soul, death, and the Hereafter, from 'Condemnation of Delusion'
