32:17.arabic: وقيل في قوله تعالى {فلا تعلم نفس ما أخفي لهم من قرة أعين جزاء بما كانوا يعملون} قيل كان عملهم الصيام لأنه قال {إنما يوفى الصابرون أجرهم بغير حساب} فيفرغ للصائم جزاؤه إفراغا ويجازف جزافا فلا يدخل تحت وهم وتقدير وجدير بأن يكون كذلك لأن الصوم إنما كان له ومشرفا بالنسبة إليه وإن كانت العبادات كلها له كما شرف البيت بالنسبة إلى نفسه والأرض كلها له لمعنيين أحدهما أن الصوم كف وترك وهو في نفسه سر ليس فيه عمل يشاهد وجميع أعمال الطاعات بمشهد من الخلق ومرأى والصوم لا يراه إلا الله عز وجل فإنه عمل في الباطن بالصبر المجرد والثاني أنه
32:17.english: To proceed: Fasting is one quarter of faith, by virtue of his saying, peace and blessings be upon him: "Fasting is half of patience" — and by virtue of his saying, peace and blessings be upon him: "Patience is half of faith" {«الإيمان»}. Then it is distinguished by a particular characteristic of its attribution to Allah the Exalted, above all the other pillars — for Allah the Exalted said, in what His Prophet narrated from Him, peace and blessings be upon him: "Every good deed is multiplied tenfold up to seven hundred times, except fasting, for it is Mine, and I shall reward it." And Allah the Exalted has said: {«Only the patient shall be paid their reward in full without reckoning»} (Q 39:10). And fasting is half of patience — so its reward has surpassed the law of measure and reckoning. And sufficient for you in knowing its excellence is his saying, peace and blessings be upon him: "By Him in whose hand is my soul, the change in the breath of the mouth of the fasting person is more fragrant to Allah than the scent of musk. Allah the Exalted says: 'He only abandons his appetite, his food, and his drink for My sake — so fasting is for Me, and I shall reward it.'" And he said, peace and blessings be upon him: "Paradise has a gate called al-Rayyān, through which none shall enter except the fasting ones." And the fasting person is promised the meeting with Allah the Exalted as a portion of his fasting. And he said, peace and blessings be upon him: "For the fasting person there are two joys: a joy when he breaks his fast, and a joy when he meets his Lord." And he said, peace and blessings be upon him: "Everything has a gate, and the gate of worship is fasting." And he said, peace and blessings be upon him: "The sleep of the fasting person is worship." And Abū Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, narrated that he, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "When the month of Ramaḍān enters, the gates of Paradise are opened, the gates of the Fire are closed, the devils are chained, and a caller calls out: 'O seeker of good, come forth! O seeker of evil, desist!'" And Wakīʿ said concerning His saying, the Exalted: {«Eat and drink in satisfaction for what you sent forth in the days past»} (Q 69:24) — these are the days of fasting, for in them they abandoned eating and drinking. And the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, gathered in the rank of divine boasting (mubāhāh) between renunciation of the world and fasting, saying: "Allah the Exalted boasts to His angels of the young worshiper, saying: 'O young man who abandons his appetite for My sake, who devotes his youth to Me — you are to Me as some of My angels.'" And he said, peace and blessings be upon him, concerning the fasting person: "Allah the Exalted says: 'Look, O My angels, at My servant — he has abandoned his appetite, his pleasure, his food, and his drink for My sake.'" And it was said concerning His saying, the Exalted: {«No soul knows what comfort has been concealed for them, as a reward for what they used to do»} (Q 32:17) — it was said: their deed was fasting, because He said: {«Only the patient shall be paid their reward in full without reckoning»} — so the reward of the fasting person is poured out upon him without measure, and is dealt out to him in bulk, not falling under any imagination or estimation.
32:17.section_title_en: The Book of the Secrets of Fasting — Section 185: On the Excellence of Fasting and Its Distinction Among the Acts of Worship
32:17.anchors:
- Root: صوم (ṣ-w-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core linguistic root meaning — abstention from any act, whether eating, speaking, or walking; a horse that refrains from movement or fodder is called ṣā'im.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological/Kalam semantic nuance — "الصوم في الأصل: الإمساك عن الفعل" — fasting is fundamentally the restraint of the self from action; it is an inward act of the heart, invisible to creation.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal vs Metaphorical distinction — Haqiqah: the month of fasting, "فمن شهد منكم الشهر فليصمه" (Q 2:185); Majaz: "صام الفرس على آريه" — a horse standing still at its tether, refusing fodder, metaphorically "fasting."
- Root: عله (ʿ-l-h)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core linguistic root meaning — to feed or pasture; related to cultivation and nourishment.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological/Kalam semantic nuance — not directly attested in Mufradat for this root; the root pertains to the means by which the body is sustained, which is precisely what the fasting person abstains from.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal vs Metaphorical distinction — literal feeding and satiation; the fasting person's abstention from these becomes the very means of spiritual nourishment.
- Root: الي (a-l-y)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core linguistic root meaning — to convey a message; the angel (malak) is so named because the message is "chewed" (yu'lak) in the mouth, as a horse chews its bit.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological/Kalam semantic nuance — "المألكة: الرسالة" — the angelic function is the conveyance of divine communication; the fasting person's hunger narrows the channels through which the devil (who runs like blood through the veins) reaches the heart.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal vs Metaphorical distinction — literal conveyance of a message versus the metaphorical "message" of the devil's insinuation (waswās) through the pathways of the body.
- Root: صبر (ṣ-b-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core linguistic root meaning — to restrain, to hold back in constriction; "صبرت الدابة: حبستها بلا علف" — to hold an animal back without fodder.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological/Kalam semantic nuance — "الصبر: الإمساك في ضيق" — patience is restraint within constriction; it is the holding of the soul upon what reason and law require, or from what they require it to abstain. Its names vary by context: in battle it is courage, in calamity it is patience proper.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal vs Metaphorical distinction — Haqiqah: "صبرت على ما أكره وصبرت عما أحب" — patience upon the disliked and patience from the beloved; Majaz: "صبرت يمينه" — to bind one's oath severely, and "هو أصبر على الضرب من الأرض" — more enduring of striking than the earth.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — The particle innamā restricts and confines the predicate exclusively to its subject, as in the divine saying {«إنما يوفى الصابرون أجرهم بغير حساب»} and {«إنما يذر شهوته وطعامه وشرابه لأجلي»}, where the restriction elevates the restricted matter to a rank beyond all quantitative measure.
32:17.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Condemnation of Delusion'

33:43.arabic: {يخرجهم من الظلمات إلى النور} وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم يا أيها الناس اعقلوا عن ربكم وتواصوا بالعقل تعرفوا ما أمرتم به وما نهيتم عنه واعلموا أنه ينجدكم عند ربكم واعلموا أن العاقل من أطاع الله وإن كان دميم المنظر حقير الخطر دنيء المنزلة رث الهيئة وأن الجاهل من عصى الله تعالى وإن كان جميل المنظر عظيم الخطر شريف المنزلة حسن الهيئة فصيحا نطوقا فالقردة والخنازير أعقل عند الله تعالى ممن عصاه ولا تغتر بتعظيم أهل الدنيا إياهم فإنهم من الخاسرين (2) وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم أول ما خل
33:43.english: The Book of Seclusion ('Uzlah) — its explanation, God Most High willing. For this reason, Yūsuf ibn Asbāṭ wrote to Ḥudhayfah al-Marʿashī: "What is your opinion of one who remains, finding no one with whom to remember God Most High except that he is either sinful, or his remembrance in company is itself an act of disobedience — and that because he finds no one of his own kind?" And indeed he spoke truly, for mixing with people is never free from backbiting (ghībah), or listening to backbiting, or remaining silent upon wrongdoing (munkar). And the best of his states is that he either imparts knowledge or acquires it. Yet were this poor wretch to reflect, and to know that his imparting of knowledge is never free from the taints of ostentation (riyā'), the seeking of followers, and the desire for leadership (ri'āsah), he would know that the one who acquires knowledge from him only seeks to make it an instrument for pursuing the world and a means toward evil — so that the teacher becomes his helper therein, his support and his backer, preparing its causes for him, like one who sells a sword to a highway robber. For knowledge is like the sword: its soundness for good is like the soundness of the sword for warfare. And for this reason, it is not permitted to sell it to one whom one knows, by the indications of his circumstances, intends to use it to aid in cutting off the road.
33:43.section_title_en: The Book of Seclusion ('Uzlah) — Section 65, and The Seventh Book: On the Intellect, Its Nobility, Its Reality, and Its Divisions
33:43.anchors:
- Root: عقل (ʿaql)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The root denotes binding, restraining, and holding back; the intellect is that which restrains the soul from base desires and prevents it from straying.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "العقل يقال للقوة المتهيئة لقبول العلم، ويقال للعلم الذي يستفيده الإنسان بتلك القوة عقل" — The intellect is said of the faculty prepared for the reception of knowledge, and it is also said of the knowledge which man acquires by means of that faculty.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): intellectual apprehension and understanding. Metaphorical (Majaz): "نخلة لا تعقل الإبار" — a palm tree that does not accept pollination, i.e., does not grasp or take in.
- Root: علم (ʿilm)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Knowledge as the mark or sign by which a thing is known; the trace or landmark that guides.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "العلم: إدراك الشيء بحقيقته" — Knowledge is the apprehension of a thing in its true reality; it is of two kinds: apprehension of the essence of a thing, and judgment upon a thing regarding what exists for it or is negated of it.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: certain awareness. Metaphorical: "هو من أعلام العلم الخافقه" — he is among the lofty banners of knowledge; knowledge as a guiding landmark (maʿlam).
- Root: نور (nūr)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Light; the first to set up beacons (manār) on his path in his campaigns to guide his return.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "النور: الضوء المنتشر الذي يعين على الإبصار" — Light is the diffused radiance that aids vision; it is of two kinds: that perceived by the eye of inner insight (baṣīrah) — such as the light of the intellect and the light of the Qur'an — and that perceived by the eye of the head, such as the celestial bodies.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: illumination. Metaphorical: "نور الأمر: بينه" — he illuminated the matter: he made it clear; "وهذا أنور من ذاك: أبين" — this is more luminous than that: more evident.
- Sibawayh Rule: Restriction and Focused Predication (al-ḥaṣr wa al-taqyīd bi-innamā) — governing the exclusive attribution of a predicate to a subject, as in the author's restriction of the scholar's condition to one of two men, and the exclusion of the third.
33:43.topic: Al-Ghazali on constant remembrance of God and contemplative invocations, from 'Condemnation of Delusion'

40:3.arabic: {حم تنزيل الكتاب من الله العزيز العليم غافر الذنب وقابل التوب شديد العقاب} الآية ثم عاتبه تحت ذلك وعذله فلما قرأ الكتاب بكى وقال صدق الله ونصح لي عمر فتاب ورجع وحكي أن أخوين ابتلى أحدهما بهوى فأظهر عليه أخاه وقال إني قد اعتللت فإن شئت أن لا تعقد على صحبتي لله فافعل فقال ما كنت لأحل عقد أخوتك لأجل خطيئتك أبدا ثم عقد أخوه بينه وبين الله بأن لا يأكل ولا يشرب حتى يعافى الله أخاه من هواه فطوى أربعين يوما في كلها يسأله عن هواه فكان يقول القلب مقيم على حاله وما زال هو ينحل من الغم والجوع حتى زال الهوى عن قلب أخيه بعد الأربع
40:3.english: Abu Dharr (may Allah be pleased with him) held the view of severance, saying: "When your brother turns away from what he once was, then hate him from the very perspective from which you loved him." He considered this to be a requirement of loving for Allah's sake and hating for Allah's sake.
40:3.section_title_en: On the Error of a Friend: Between Severance and Gentleness in Brotherhood
40:3.anchors:
- Root: لطف (luṭf)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Gentleness, subtlety, refinement; the opposite of harshness and coarseness.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The subtle divine reality (laṭīfah) that perceives the finest nuances of affairs; also gentleness (rifq) in dealing.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: that which is not coarse. Metaphorical: "I was gentle with him" (laṭaftu bihi) — showing affection and gentleness in dealing, and "he is gentle with this matter" — skillful in managing it.
- Root: دين (dīn)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Religion, creed, judgment, recompense; the comprehensive term for one's obligatory practices and beliefs.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The root denotes indebtedness and obedience; the religion (dīn) is that by which one is bound to the Divine command.
- Root: عقد (ʿaqd)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To tie, bind, contract; the knot of brotherhood (ʿaqd al-ukhuwwah) as a binding covenant.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): A firm resolution or covenant that obligates its fulfillment.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — Used to distinguish the precise scope of a ruling, e.g., "I only hate his deed" (innamā ubghiḍu ʿamalahu), restricting hatred to the act, not the person.
40:3.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Condemnation of Delusion'

40:24.arabic: لا يأمن مكره ولا يغتر بأمثال هذه الخيالات الفاسدة وينظر إلى فرعون وهامان وقارون وإلى ملوك الأرض وما جرى لهم كيف أحسن الله إليهم ابتداء ثم دمرهم تدميرا فقال تعالى هل تحس منهم من أحد الآية وقد حذر الله تعالى من مكره واستدراجه فقال فلا يأمن مكر الله إلا القوم الخاسرون وقال تعالى ومكروا مكرا ومكرنا مكرا وهم لا يشعرون وقال عز وجل ومكروا ومكر الله والله خير الماكرين وقال تعالى إنهم يكيدون كيدا وأكيد كيدا فمهل الكافرين أمهلهم رويدا فكما لا يجوز للعبد المهمل أن يستدل بإهمال السيد إياه وتمكينه من النعم على حب السيد بل ينبغي أن يحذر
40:24.english: As for knowing it by way of authoritative transmission and affirmation (taṣdīq): it is that one believes in the Book of God — exalted is He — and affirms His Messenger. For God — exalted is He — has said: {«أيحسبون أن ما نمدهم به من مال وبنين * نسارع لهم في الخيرات بل لا يشعرون»} — "Do they reckon that what We extend to them of wealth and sons — [that] We hasten for them good things? Nay, but they do not perceive" (Q. 23:55-56). And He said — exalted is He: {«سنستدرجهم من حيث لا يعلمون»} — "We shall draw them on by degrees from whence they do not know" (Q. 7:182). And He said — exalted is He: {«فتحنا عليهم أبواب كل شيء حتى إذا فرحوا بما أوتوا أخذناهم بغتة فإذا هم مبلسون»} — "We opened upon them the gates of everything, until when they rejoiced in what they were given, We seized them suddenly, and behold, they were in despair" (Q. 6:44). And in the interpretation of His saying — exalted is He: {«سنستدرجهم من حيث لا يعلمون»} — it is said: "Whenever they innovated a sin, We innovated for them a blessing, to increase their self-deception." And He said — exalted is He: {«إنما نملي لهم ليزدادوا إثما»} — "We only grant them respite that they may increase in sin" (Q. 3:178). And He said — exalted is He: {«ولا تحسبن الله غافلا عما يعمل الظالمون إنما يؤخرهم ليوم تشخص فيه الأبصار»} — "And do not reckon God heedless of what the wrongdoers do; He only delays them to a Day when eyes will stare fixedly" (Q. 14:42). And [there is] more of that kind which has come in the Book of God — exalted is He — and in the Sunnah of His Messenger. So whoever believes in it is delivered from this self-deception. For the origin of this self-deception is ignorance of God and of His attributes; for whoever knows Him does not feel secure from His stratagem (makr) and is not deceived by such corrupt fancies.
40:24.section_title_en: Section 888 — On the Remedy for Self-Deception (Ghurūr): Recognizing the Signs of Divine Honor (Karāmah) and Humiliation (Hawān)
40:24.anchors:
- Root: غرر (gh-r-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of an outward trace or mark; heedlessness in wakefulness; the blaze on a horse's forehead.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Ghurūr" is delusion stemming from heedlessness — the soul's being overtaken while imagining security, as in {«ما غرك بربك الكريم»} (Q. 82:6). It is the state of one who is deceived by apparent favors while blind to their underlying test.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): heedlessness and exposure to predation, like a gazelle deceived by moonlight. Metaphorical (Majaz): being "deceived by God" (ightirār billāh) — trusting in His mercy while persisting in disobedience.
- Root: لهم (l-h-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Swallowing whole; the gullet.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Ilhām" — God's casting a meaning into the heart (al-raw'), distinct from demonic whispering; the channel of inner vision for the knowers (ʿārifūn).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: to swallow. Metaphorical: the heart's receptive "swallowing" of divine inspiration.
- Root: حدث (ḥ-d-th)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Origination after non-existence; newness.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Ḥudūth" — a thing's coming to be after it was not; "muḥdith" — the originator, exclusively God for substances (jawāhir). "Iḥdāth" — bringing about a novel state or act.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: temporal newness. Metaphorical: "muḥaddath" — one inspired with correct discernment, as if newly spoken-to.
- Root: نعم (n-ʿ-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Softness, ease, well-being; a state of comfort.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Niʿmah" — the good state one inhabits; "naʿīm" — the act of living pleasantly. Blessings are both a test and a sign, per {«وإن تعدوا نعمة الله لا تحصوها»} (Q. 16:18).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: bounty and comfort. Metaphorical: "khafat naʿāmatuhum" — their prosperity vanished; blessings may signal either favor or gradual ruin (istidrāj).
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction and Focused Predication with "innamā")
  * In {«إنما نملي لهم ليزدادوا إثما»} (Q. 3:178) and {«إنما يؤخرهم ليوم تشخص فيه الأبصار»} (Q. 14:42), "innamā" restricts the purpose of divine respite exclusively to increase of sin and deferred reckoning — negating any reading of it as benevolent indulgence.
40:24.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'Condemnation of Delusion'

42:25.arabic: والله يعلم ما في أنفسكم فاحذروه فاستغفرت الله في سري فناداني وقال {وهو الذي يقبل التوبة عن عباده} ثم غاب عني ولم أره وقال زكريا بن داود دخل أبو العباس بن مسروق على أبي الفضل الهاشمي وهو عليل وكان ذا عيال ولم يعرف له سبب يعيش به قال فلما قمت قلت في نفسي من أين يأكل هذا الرجل قال فصاح بي يا أبا العباس رد هذه الهمة الدنية فإن لله تعالى ألطافا خفية وقال أحمد النقيب دخلت على الشبلي فقال مفتونا يا أحمد فقلت ما الخبر قال كنت جالسا فجرى بخاطري أنك بخيل فقلت ما أنا بخيل فعاد مني خاطري وقال بل أنت بخيل فقلت ما فتح اليوم علي بشيء إلا دفعته
42:25.english: As for the evidences of the Sacred Law, there is His saying (Exalted is He): {«وَالَّذِينَ جَاهَدُوا فِينَا لَنَهْدِيَنَّهُمْ سُبُلَنَا»} ("And those who strive in Us, We shall surely guide them to Our paths") (Q. 29:69). So every wisdom that appears from the heart through persevering devotion to worship, without learning, is by way of unveiling and inspiration. And he (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Whoever acts upon what he knows, God bequeaths to him knowledge of what he does not know, and grants him success in what he does" — until he becomes deserving of Paradise. And whoever does not act upon what he knows wanders astray in what he knows and is not granted success in what he does, until he becomes deserving of the Fire. [The hadith "Whoever acts upon what he knows" has preceded in the Book of Knowledge, without his saying "and grants him success in what he does" — I have not found it with that addition.] And God (Exalted is He) said: {«وَمَنْ يَتَّقِ اللَّهَ يَجْعَلْ لَهُ مَخْرَجًا»} ("And whoever fears God, He makes for him a way out") (Q. 65:2) — from perplexities and doubts — {«وَيَرْزُقْهُ مِنْ حَيْثُ لَا يَحْتَسِبُ»} ("and provides for him from whence he does not reckon") (Q. 65:3) — teaching him knowledge without learning and granting him discernment without experience. And God (Exalted is He) said: {«يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا إِنْ تَتَّقُوا اللَّهَ يَجْعَلْ لَكُمْ فُرْقَانًا»} ("O you who believe, if you fear God, He will make for you a criterion") (Q. 8:29) — it is said: a light by which one distinguishes between truth and falsehood and by which one emerges from doubts. For this reason, he (peace and blessings be upon him) was abundant in his supplication in asking for light, saying (peace and blessings be upon him): "O God, grant me light, and increase me in light, and make for me light in my heart, and light in my grave, and light in my hearing, and light in my sight" — until he said: "and light in my hair, and in my skin, and in my flesh, and in my blood, and in my bones." [Agreed upon (by al-Bukhari and Muslim).] [The hadith concerning his being asked about His saying {«أَفَمَنْ شَرَحَ اللَّهُ صَدْرَهُ لِلْإِسْلَامِ»} ("Is he whose breast God has expanded for Islam") (Q. 39:22) — and in al-Mustadrak from the hadith of Ibn Masʿūd — has preceded in the Book of Knowledge.] And he (peace and blessings be upon him) said concerning Ibn ʿAbbās: "O God, grant him understanding in religion and teach him the interpretation (taʾwīl)." [The hadith of ʿAlī: "We have nothing with us that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) confided to us except that God grants a servant understanding in His Book" — has preceded in the Etiquettes of Qurʾanic Recitation.] And it is said in the interpretation of His saying (Exalted is He): {«يُؤْتِي الْحِكْمَةَ مَنْ يَشَاءُ»} ("He grants wisdom to whom He wills") (Q. 2:269) that it is understanding in the Book of God. And He (Exalted is He) said: {«فَفَهَّمْنَاهَا سُلَيْمَانَ»} ("And We made Solomon understand it") (Q. 21:79) — singling out what was unveiled with the name of understanding (fahm). And Abū al-Dardāʾ used to say: "The believer is one who sees by the light of God from behind a thin veil. By God, it is the truth that God casts into their hearts and causes to flow upon their tongues." And some of the Salaf said: "The believer's conjecture is like soothsaying."
42:25.section_title_en: The Unveiling of Knowledge Through Divine Inspiration and the Evidences of the Unseen
42:25.anchors:
- Root: علم (ʿalima)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning encompasses both perception of a thing's essence and judgment upon it—knowledge as direct apprehension or discursive ruling.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "العلم: إدراك الشيء بحقيقته" — knowledge is the apprehension of a thing in its true reality, divided into apprehension of the essence (transitive to one object) and judgment upon existence or non-existence (transitive to two objects).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal usage denotes certainty and awareness ("ما علمت بخبرك: ما شعرت به"); metaphorical extension applies to marks, signs, and beacons of guidance (معالم الطريق) — here, the inspired knowledge is a "mark" of the path.
- Root: كشف (kashafa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To remove a covering, unveil, disclose what was hidden.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Unveiling (kashf) in theological terms is the removal of the veil (ghishāwah) from the heart such that the realities of things become directly witnessed, not merely inferred.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: to lift a covering from a thing; metaphorical: the disclosure of inward states and hidden matters — the heart's eye perceives what the outward senses cannot.
- Root: فرس (farasa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To prey upon, devour; farāsah — the lion's pouncing upon its prey.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Discernment (farāsah) is a spiritual perception by which the believer penetrates into the inner states of others, a light cast by God into the heart.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the beast of prey seizing its quarry; metaphorical: the believer's insight seizing the truth of a matter or the hidden state of a person — "اتقوا فراسة المؤمن فإنه ينظر بنور الله."
- Root: حدث (ḥadatha)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To be new, originate after non-existence; muḥaddath — one who is spoken to, inspired with true speech from the unseen.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الحدوث: كون الشيء بعد أن لم يكن" — origination after non-existence; the muḥaddath is one to whom divine inspiration comes as a new, immediate occurrence without acquired means.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: newness of a thing; metaphorical: "كان عمر رضي الله عنه محدثا أي صادق الحدس، كأنما حدث بما ظن" — one whose intuition is so true it is as if he were directly spoken to.
- Sibawayh Rule: Restriction and specification (الحصر والتقييد) — the particle "إنما" and conditional clauses (إن/إذا) restrict predicates to their subjects, as in "إنما العالم الذي يأخذ علمه من ربه" — the true scholar is exclusively the one who takes knowledge from his Lord.
42:25.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Condemnation of Delusion'

46:14.arabic: وقيل في قوله تعالى {فلا تعلم نفس ما أخفي لهم من قرة أعين جزاء بما كانوا يعملون} قيل كان عملهم الصيام لأنه قال {إنما يوفى الصابرون أجرهم بغير حساب} فيفرغ للصائم جزاؤه إفراغا ويجازف جزافا فلا يدخل تحت وهم وتقدير وجدير بأن يكون كذلك لأن الصوم إنما كان له ومشرفا بالنسبة إليه وإن كانت العبادات كلها له كما شرف البيت بالنسبة إلى نفسه والأرض كلها له لمعنيين أحدهما أن الصوم كف وترك وهو في نفسه سر ليس فيه عمل يشاهد وجميع أعمال الطاعات بمشهد من الخلق ومرأى والصوم لا يراه إلا الله عز وجل فإنه عمل في الباطن بالصبر المجرد والثاني أنه
46:14.english: To proceed: Fasting is one quarter of faith, by virtue of his saying, peace and blessings be upon him: "Fasting is half of patience" — and by virtue of his saying, peace and blessings be upon him: "Patience is half of faith" {«الإيمان»}. Then it is distinguished by a particular characteristic of its attribution to Allah the Exalted, above all the other pillars — for Allah the Exalted said, in what His Prophet narrated from Him, peace and blessings be upon him: "Every good deed is multiplied tenfold up to seven hundred times, except fasting, for it is Mine, and I shall reward it." And Allah the Exalted has said: {«Only the patient shall be paid their reward in full without reckoning»} (Q 39:10). And fasting is half of patience — so its reward has surpassed the law of measure and reckoning. And sufficient for you in knowing its excellence is his saying, peace and blessings be upon him: "By Him in whose hand is my soul, the change in the breath of the mouth of the fasting person is more fragrant to Allah than the scent of musk. Allah the Exalted says: 'He only abandons his appetite, his food, and his drink for My sake — so fasting is for Me, and I shall reward it.'" And he said, peace and blessings be upon him: "Paradise has a gate called al-Rayyān, through which none shall enter except the fasting ones." And the fasting person is promised the meeting with Allah the Exalted as a portion of his fasting. And he said, peace and blessings be upon him: "For the fasting person there are two joys: a joy when he breaks his fast, and a joy when he meets his Lord." And he said, peace and blessings be upon him: "Everything has a gate, and the gate of worship is fasting." And he said, peace and blessings be upon him: "The sleep of the fasting person is worship." And Abū Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, narrated that he, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "When the month of Ramaḍān enters, the gates of Paradise are opened, the gates of the Fire are closed, the devils are chained, and a caller calls out: 'O seeker of good, come forth! O seeker of evil, desist!'" And Wakīʿ said concerning His saying, the Exalted: {«Eat and drink in satisfaction for what you sent forth in the days past»} (Q 69:24) — these are the days of fasting, for in them they abandoned eating and drinking. And the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, gathered in the rank of divine boasting (mubāhāh) between renunciation of the world and fasting, saying: "Allah the Exalted boasts to His angels of the young worshiper, saying: 'O young man who abandons his appetite for My sake, who devotes his youth to Me — you are to Me as some of My angels.'" And he said, peace and blessings be upon him, concerning the fasting person: "Allah the Exalted says: 'Look, O My angels, at My servant — he has abandoned his appetite, his pleasure, his food, and his drink for My sake.'" And it was said concerning His saying, the Exalted: {«No soul knows what comfort has been concealed for them, as a reward for what they used to do»} (Q 32:17) — it was said: their deed was fasting, because He said: {«Only the patient shall be paid their reward in full without reckoning»} — so the reward of the fasting person is poured out upon him without measure, and is dealt out to him in bulk, not falling under any imagination or estimation.
46:14.section_title_en: The Book of the Secrets of Fasting — Section 185: On the Excellence of Fasting and Its Distinction Among the Acts of Worship
46:14.anchors:
- Root: صوم (ṣ-w-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core linguistic root meaning — abstention from any act, whether eating, speaking, or walking; a horse that refrains from movement or fodder is called ṣā'im.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological/Kalam semantic nuance — "الصوم في الأصل: الإمساك عن الفعل" — fasting is fundamentally the restraint of the self from action; it is an inward act of the heart, invisible to creation.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal vs Metaphorical distinction — Haqiqah: the month of fasting, "فمن شهد منكم الشهر فليصمه" (Q 2:185); Majaz: "صام الفرس على آريه" — a horse standing still at its tether, refusing fodder, metaphorically "fasting."
- Root: عله (ʿ-l-h)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core linguistic root meaning — to feed or pasture; related to cultivation and nourishment.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological/Kalam semantic nuance — not directly attested in Mufradat for this root; the root pertains to the means by which the body is sustained, which is precisely what the fasting person abstains from.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal vs Metaphorical distinction — literal feeding and satiation; the fasting person's abstention from these becomes the very means of spiritual nourishment.
- Root: الي (a-l-y)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core linguistic root meaning — to convey a message; the angel (malak) is so named because the message is "chewed" (yu'lak) in the mouth, as a horse chews its bit.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological/Kalam semantic nuance — "المألكة: الرسالة" — the angelic function is the conveyance of divine communication; the fasting person's hunger narrows the channels through which the devil (who runs like blood through the veins) reaches the heart.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal vs Metaphorical distinction — literal conveyance of a message versus the metaphorical "message" of the devil's insinuation (waswās) through the pathways of the body.
- Root: صبر (ṣ-b-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core linguistic root meaning — to restrain, to hold back in constriction; "صبرت الدابة: حبستها بلا علف" — to hold an animal back without fodder.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological/Kalam semantic nuance — "الصبر: الإمساك في ضيق" — patience is restraint within constriction; it is the holding of the soul upon what reason and law require, or from what they require it to abstain. Its names vary by context: in battle it is courage, in calamity it is patience proper.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal vs Metaphorical distinction — Haqiqah: "صبرت على ما أكره وصبرت عما أحب" — patience upon the disliked and patience from the beloved; Majaz: "صبرت يمينه" — to bind one's oath severely, and "هو أصبر على الضرب من الأرض" — more enduring of striking than the earth.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — The particle innamā restricts and confines the predicate exclusively to its subject, as in the divine saying {«إنما يوفى الصابرون أجرهم بغير حساب»} and {«إنما يذر شهوته وطعامه وشرابه لأجلي»}, where the restriction elevates the restricted matter to a rank beyond all quantitative measure.

57:9.arabic: {يخرجهم من الظلمات إلى النور} وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم يا أيها الناس اعقلوا عن ربكم وتواصوا بالعقل تعرفوا ما أمرتم به وما نهيتم عنه واعلموا أنه ينجدكم عند ربكم واعلموا أن العاقل من أطاع الله وإن كان دميم المنظر حقير الخطر دنيء المنزلة رث الهيئة وأن الجاهل من عصى الله تعالى وإن كان جميل المنظر عظيم الخطر شريف المنزلة حسن الهيئة فصيحا نطوقا فالقردة والخنازير أعقل عند الله تعالى ممن عصاه ولا تغتر بتعظيم أهل الدنيا إياهم فإنهم من الخاسرين (2) وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم أول ما خل
57:9.english: The Book of Seclusion ('Uzlah) — its explanation, God Most High willing. For this reason, Yūsuf ibn Asbāṭ wrote to Ḥudhayfah al-Marʿashī: "What is your opinion of one who remains, finding no one with whom to remember God Most High except that he is either sinful, or his remembrance in company is itself an act of disobedience — and that because he finds no one of his own kind?" And indeed he spoke truly, for mixing with people is never free from backbiting (ghībah), or listening to backbiting, or remaining silent upon wrongdoing (munkar). And the best of his states is that he either imparts knowledge or acquires it. Yet were this poor wretch to reflect, and to know that his imparting of knowledge is never free from the taints of ostentation (riyā'), the seeking of followers, and the desire for leadership (ri'āsah), he would know that the one who acquires knowledge from him only seeks to make it an instrument for pursuing the world and a means toward evil — so that the teacher becomes his helper therein, his support and his backer, preparing its causes for him, like one who sells a sword to a highway robber. For knowledge is like the sword: its soundness for good is like the soundness of the sword for warfare. And for this reason, it is not permitted to sell it to one whom one knows, by the indications of his circumstances, intends to use it to aid in cutting off the road.
57:9.section_title_en: The Book of Seclusion ('Uzlah) — Section 65, and The Seventh Book: On the Intellect, Its Nobility, Its Reality, and Its Divisions
57:9.anchors:
- Root: عقل (ʿaql)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The root denotes binding, restraining, and holding back; the intellect is that which restrains the soul from base desires and prevents it from straying.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "العقل يقال للقوة المتهيئة لقبول العلم، ويقال للعلم الذي يستفيده الإنسان بتلك القوة عقل" — The intellect is said of the faculty prepared for the reception of knowledge, and it is also said of the knowledge which man acquires by means of that faculty.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): intellectual apprehension and understanding. Metaphorical (Majaz): "نخلة لا تعقل الإبار" — a palm tree that does not accept pollination, i.e., does not grasp or take in.
- Root: علم (ʿilm)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Knowledge as the mark or sign by which a thing is known; the trace or landmark that guides.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "العلم: إدراك الشيء بحقيقته" — Knowledge is the apprehension of a thing in its true reality; it is of two kinds: apprehension of the essence of a thing, and judgment upon a thing regarding what exists for it or is negated of it.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: certain awareness. Metaphorical: "هو من أعلام العلم الخافقه" — he is among the lofty banners of knowledge; knowledge as a guiding landmark (maʿlam).
- Root: نور (nūr)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Light; the first to set up beacons (manār) on his path in his campaigns to guide his return.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "النور: الضوء المنتشر الذي يعين على الإبصار" — Light is the diffused radiance that aids vision; it is of two kinds: that perceived by the eye of inner insight (baṣīrah) — such as the light of the intellect and the light of the Qur'an — and that perceived by the eye of the head, such as the celestial bodies.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: illumination. Metaphorical: "نور الأمر: بينه" — he illuminated the matter: he made it clear; "وهذا أنور من ذاك: أبين" — this is more luminous than that: more evident.
- Sibawayh Rule: Restriction and Focused Predication (al-ḥaṣr wa al-taqyīd bi-innamā) — governing the exclusive attribution of a predicate to a subject, as in the author's restriction of the scholar's condition to one of two men, and the exclusion of the third.
57:9.topic: Al-Ghazali on constant remembrance of God and contemplative invocations, from 'Condemnation of Delusion'

58:8.arabic: بالله كما قال تعالى ويقولون في أنفسهم لولا يعذبنا الله بما نقول حسبهم جهنم يصلونها فبئس المصير ومنها أن يأتي الذنب ويظهره بأن يذكره بعد إتيانه أو يأتيه في مشهد غيره فإن ذلك جناية منه على ستر الله الذي سدله عليه وتحريك لرغبة الشر فيمن أسمعه ذنبه أو أشهده فعله فهما جنايتان انضمتا إلى جنايته فغلظت به فإن انضاف إلى ذلك الترغيب للغير فيه والحمل عليه وتهيئة الأسباب له صارت جناية رابعه وتفاحش الأمر وفي الخبر كل الناس معافى إلا المجاهرين يبيت أحدهم على ذنب قد ستره الله عليه فيصبح فيكشف ستر الله ويتحدث بذنبه (1) وهذا لأن
58:8.english: Know that the minor sin (al-ṣaghīrah) is magnified by several causes. Among them is persistence (al-iṣrār) and continuous adherence (al-muwāẓabah). For this reason it was said: "No sin remains minor with persistence, and no sin remains major with seeking forgiveness." For a single major sin that comes to an end and is not followed by another like it—if such a thing could be conceived—forgiveness for it would be more hopeful than for a minor sin upon which the servant persistently continues. The example of this is drops of water falling upon a stone in succession: they effect an impression upon it, whereas that same quantity of water, if poured upon it all at once, would have no effect. For this reason the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: "The best of deeds are the most constant of them, even if few." {«خير الأعمال أدومها وإن قل»} And things are made distinct by their opposites. For even though the beneficial among deeds is the constant one, even if little, yet the abundant that is cut short is of little benefit in illuminating the heart and purifying it. Likewise, the little among evil deeds, when it persists, its effect in darkening the heart becomes immense—except that a major sin is rarely conceived as being rushed upon suddenly without prior antecedents. Even if it were exempted from the class of minor sins, the fornicator rarely fornicates suddenly without prior solicitation and preliminaries, and the murderer rarely kills suddenly without a preceding rancor and enmity. Thus every major sin is encompassed by minor sins preceding and following it. But were a major sin conceived entirely alone, suddenly, with no recurrence attending it, perhaps forgiveness in its case would be more hopeful than in the case of a minor sin upon which a man persists his entire lifetime.
58:8.section_title_en: On the Causes by Which Minor Sins Are Magnified
58:8.anchors:
- Root: صغر (ṣ-gh-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Smallness in magnitude, quantity, or station; the state of being lesser in measure or rank.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Smallness and greatness are relative correlatives (mutadāyifān)—a thing is small only in relation to another thing deemed great; applied to bodies, quantities, and moral weight.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) for physical diminutiveness; metaphorical (majāz) for moral degradation and abasement (ṣaghār) before God's majesty.
- Root: كبر (k-b-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Greatness in size, age, or dignity; also grievousness and gravity of a matter.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Bigness as a relative term—what is great in one respect may be small in another; in moral theology, magnitude of sin is measured against the majesty of the One disobeyed.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal for physical magnitude; metaphorical for what weighs heavily upon the heart and is grievous to bear.
- Root: ذنب (dh-n-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The tail of an animal; by extension, what follows behind, the rear, the last part.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "The sin (al-dhanb) in its origin is the taking hold of a thing by its tail (akhdh bi-dhanab al-shay')"—i.e., pursuing a consequence; used metaphorically for a fault that trails after the soul and seizes it from behind.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal for the tail of a beast; metaphorical (majāz) for sin as that which follows a person and clings to him—"he is among the tails (adhānāb) of the people," i.e., the followers.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد (Restriction and Specification)—the particle "إنما" confines predication to a single subject, as in "لا صغيرة مع إصرار" where the negation plus exception structure (lā + istithnā' implied) restricts absoluteness of the judgment.
58:8.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Condemnation of Delusion'

59:19.arabic: ومهما فعل ذلك فقد ظلم نفسه إذ قيل له ولا تكونوا كالذين نسوا الله فأنساهم أنفسهم أولئك هم الفاسقون أي الخارجون عن مقتضى طبعهم ومظنة استحقاقهم يقال فسقت الرطبة عن كمامها إذا خرجت عن معدنها الفطري وهذه إشارة إلى أسرار يهتز لاستنشاق روائحها العارفون وتشمئز من سماع ألفاظها القاصرون فإنها تضر بهم كما تضر رياح الورد بالجعل وتبهر أعينهم الضعيفة كما تبهر الشمس أبصار الخفافيش وانفتاح هذا الباب من سر القلب إلى عالم الملكوت يسمى معرفة وولاية ويسمى صاحبه وليا وعارفا وهي مبادي مقامات الأنبياء وآخر مقامات الأولياء أول مقامات الأنبياء ولنرجع إلى الغرض المطلوب
59:19.english: Rather, the world is two worlds: the world of Command (ālam al-amr) and the world of Creation (ālam al-khalq). And to God belongs the Creation and the Command {«ألا له الخلق والأمر»} (Q. 7:54). For bodies — those possessing quantity (kammiyyah) and magnitudes (maqādīr) — belong to the world of Creation, since "creation" (khalq) in linguistic usage is an expression for measuring and determining (taqdīr). And every existent that is exalted above quantity and magnitude belongs to the world of Command. The explanation of this is the secret of the Spirit (sirr al-rūḥ), and there is no license to divulge it, because of the harm most creatures would suffer upon hearing it — like the breaking of the vessel (kasr al-qidr) which prevented its contents from being spilled abroad.
59:19.section_title_en: The Two Worlds: The World of Command and the World of Creation — On the Spirit, Self-Knowledge, and the Delusion of the World
59:19.anchors:
- Root: امر (amr)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Command, affair, matter; al-amr as divine imperative opposed to al-khalq (creation).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Amr denotes the divine word of fiat (kun) by which things exist without mediate causation, contrasted with khalq as measured, quantified formation.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Haqiqah — amr is the unquantified, unmeasured divine decree; majaz would be applying it to corporeal extension.
- Root: قدر (qadr)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Measuring, determining, apportioning; al-taqdir is the assignment of quantity and limit.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Khalq is taqdir — the imposition of quantity and magnitude upon bodies; what is exempt from quantity belongs to the world of amr.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Haqiqah — taqdir as delimitation; majaz — the "measure" of destiny as divine ordainment.
- Root: فسق (fsq)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To emerge, to exit; said of a ripe date (rutabah) bursting from its sheath (kimam).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Fusuq is departure from the straight path — exiting one's natural, primordial locus (ma'din).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Haqiqah — physical emergence from a covering; majaz — moral transgression as deviation from innate disposition.
- Root: غرر (gh-r-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Negligence, heedlessness; the white blaze on a horse's forehead; being deceived while unaware.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Ghurur is delusion that seizes one in a state of ghaflah (unawareness), as in {«ما غرك بربك الكريم»} (Q. 82:6).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Haqiqah — the gazelle deceived by moonlight; majaz — the soul deceived by worldly allurements into false security.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين المبتدأ والخبر (Interposition between Subject and Predicate) — Long periodic sentences with parenthetical clarifications (e.g., "بل العالم عالمان...") require the predicate to be held in suspense, mirroring the rhetorical deferral of meaning until the full contrast is established.
59:19.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Condemnation of Delusion'

59:19.arabic: وفيه فهو ممن قال الله تعالى فيه نسوا الله فأنساهم أنفسهم أولئك هم الفاسقون فمعرفة القلب وحقيقة أوصافه أصل الدين وأساس طريق السالكين وإذ فرغنا من الشطر الأول من هذا الكتاب من النظر فيما يجري على الجوارح من العبادات والعادات وهو العلم الظاهر ووعدنا أن نشرح في الشطر الثاني ما يجري على القلب من الصفات المهلكات والمنجيات وهو العلم الباطن فلا بد أن نقدم عليه كتابين كتابا في شرح عجائب صفات القلب وأخلاقه وكتابا في كيفية رياضة القلب وتهذيب أخلاقه ثم نندفع بعد ذلك في تفصيل المهلكات والمنجيات فلنذكر الآن من شرح
59:19.english: And whoever does not know his heart so as to watch over it, to tend it, and to lie in wait for what shines upon it and within it from the treasuries of the Dominion (malakūt) — he is among those of whom God, exalted, said: {«They forgot God, so He caused them to forget their selves; those are the wicked»} (Q 59:19). So the knowledge of the heart and the reality of its attributes is the root of religion and the foundation of the path of the wayfarers.
59:19.section_title_en: The Exposition of His Miracles and Signs Indicating His Truthfulness — Being the Opening of the Book on the Marvels of the Heart, the First Book of the Quarter of the Destroyers
59:19.anchors:
- Root: قلب (q-l-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of turning, overturning, and revolving a thing from one face to another; the heart as that which is perpetually turned about between states.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "قلب الشيء: تصريفه وصرفه عن وجه إلى وجه" — the heart is that which is constantly diverted and turned; its very essence is fluctuation and transformation, making it the seat of divine turning (taqlīb).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): turning a thing over; metaphorical (majāz): "رجل قلب حول: يقلب الأمور ويحتال" — one who turns matters about. Here, the heart's turning between the two fingers of the Merciful is a metaphorical extension of this root meaning.
- Root: جهل (j-h-l)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Ignorance as the absence of knowledge; also foolish conduct.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الجهل على ثلاثة أضرب" — threefold: (1) the soul's emptiness of knowledge (the original sense), (2) belief contrary to what a thing actually is, (3) acting contrary to what a thing's right requires. The third sense applies here: "whoever is ignorant of his heart is more ignorant of other things."
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: lack of knowledge; metaphorical: "استجهلت الريح الغصن" — the wind made the branch move violently, i.e., rendered it unsteady. The ignorant man is one whose movements are ungoverned by knowledge.
- Root: نفس (n-f-s)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The self, the soul; that by which a thing is valued.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "النفس: الروح" — the self as the immaterial reality of the human; "وإذ فرغنا" — the self is the referent of divine address and the locus of self-knowledge which leads to knowledge of God.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the soul/spirit; metaphorical: "دفق نفسه أي دمه" — the self as the whole person. Here, "knowing oneself" (maʿrifat al-nafs) is the path to knowing one's Lord.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — The repeated use of "إنما" (only/indeed) throughout the opening establishes exclusive predication: the heart alone is the knower of God, the limbs are merely followers and instruments. This restrictive construction is deliberate and carries theological weight.
59:19.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Disciplining the Soul'

62:5.arabic: {مثل الذين حملوا التوراة ثم لم يحملوها كمثل الحمار يحمل أسفارا} أراد به علماء اليهود وقال في بلعم بن باعوراء {واتل عليهم نبأ الذي آتيناه آياتنا فانسلخ منها} حتى بلغ {فمثله كمثل الكلب إن تحمل عليه يلهث أو تتركه يلهث} قال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما أوتي بلعم كتابا فأخلد إلى شهوات الأرض أي سكن حبه إليها فمثله بالكلب {إن تحمل عليه يلهث أو تتركه يلهث} أي سواء آتيته الحكمة أو لم أوته لا يدع شهوته ويكفي العالم هذا الخطر فأي عالم لم يتبع شهوته وأي عالم لم يأمر بالخير الذي لا يأتيه فمهما خطر للعالم عظم قدره بالإضافة إلى الج
62:5.english: For this reason, Kaʿb al-Aḥbār said: "Knowledge has a tyranny like the tyranny of wealth."
62:5.section_title_en: The Sixth Cause of Pride: Pride in Knowledge — Its Danger and the First Remedy
62:5.anchors:
- Root: كبر (k-b-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of bigness in stature, age, or rank; "كبر عليه" = to be grievous/heavy upon one.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Al-Kabīr and al-ṣaghīr are relative terms (mutadāyifān) — a thing is small beside one thing and great beside another; used of both connected quantity (bodies) and disconnected quantity (number)."
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): "Kabar al-amr" = the matter became great; "kabura ʿalayhi" = it was burdensome. Metaphorical (majāz): applied to rank, honor, and station, not merely physical size.
- Root: علم (ʿ-l-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Perception and apprehension of a thing as it truly is; the root also yields "ʿalam" (sign/marker) and "maʿlam" (landmark) — knowledge as that by which one is guided.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Al-ʿilm: idrāk al-shayʾ bi-ḥaqīqatihi" — apprehension of a thing in its true reality; two kinds: (1) apprehension of the essence of a thing, (2) judgment upon a thing affirming or denying something of it.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "Huwa min aʿlām al-ʿilm al-khāfiqah" — he is among the lofty banners of knowledge; "maʿālim al-ṭarīq" = the traces by which the road is recognized. Knowledge is that which marks and distinguishes.
- Root: خطر (kh-ṭ-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To be in peril; "khaṭar" = danger, risk; also "khaṭara bi-nafsihi" = to hazard oneself.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Not separately glossed in the retrieved entry, but the Qur'anic usage (e.g., "akhṭara" in the sense of grave consequence) aligns with the notion of imminent peril.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "Khaṭar" = danger/risk; "rajul khaṭīr" = a man of great consequence — the same root yields both "peril" and "high station," a deliberate lexical pairing Ghazali exploits here.
- Sibawayh Rule: Bāb al-faṣl bayna al-jār wa-al-majrūr (Prepositional Interposition) — The periodic sentence structure here ("فإنهما كمالان في النفس جديران بأن يفرح بهما") employs embedded relative clauses and prepositional phrases that must be unpacked in English without losing the logical subordination.
62:5.topic: Classical commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya Ulum al-Din, from 'Condemnation of Delusion'

65:11.arabic: {يخرجهم من الظلمات إلى النور} وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم يا أيها الناس اعقلوا عن ربكم وتواصوا بالعقل تعرفوا ما أمرتم به وما نهيتم عنه واعلموا أنه ينجدكم عند ربكم واعلموا أن العاقل من أطاع الله وإن كان دميم المنظر حقير الخطر دنيء المنزلة رث الهيئة وأن الجاهل من عصى الله تعالى وإن كان جميل المنظر عظيم الخطر شريف المنزلة حسن الهيئة فصيحا نطوقا فالقردة والخنازير أعقل عند الله تعالى ممن عصاه ولا تغتر بتعظيم أهل الدنيا إياهم فإنهم من الخاسرين (2) وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم أول ما خل
65:11.english: The Book of Seclusion ('Uzlah) — its explanation, God Most High willing. For this reason, Yūsuf ibn Asbāṭ wrote to Ḥudhayfah al-Marʿashī: "What is your opinion of one who remains, finding no one with whom to remember God Most High except that he is either sinful, or his remembrance in company is itself an act of disobedience — and that because he finds no one of his own kind?" And indeed he spoke truly, for mixing with people is never free from backbiting (ghībah), or listening to backbiting, or remaining silent upon wrongdoing (munkar). And the best of his states is that he either imparts knowledge or acquires it. Yet were this poor wretch to reflect, and to know that his imparting of knowledge is never free from the taints of ostentation (riyā'), the seeking of followers, and the desire for leadership (ri'āsah), he would know that the one who acquires knowledge from him only seeks to make it an instrument for pursuing the world and a means toward evil — so that the teacher becomes his helper therein, his support and his backer, preparing its causes for him, like one who sells a sword to a highway robber. For knowledge is like the sword: its soundness for good is like the soundness of the sword for warfare. And for this reason, it is not permitted to sell it to one whom one knows, by the indications of his circumstances, intends to use it to aid in cutting off the road.
65:11.section_title_en: The Book of Seclusion ('Uzlah) — Section 65, and The Seventh Book: On the Intellect, Its Nobility, Its Reality, and Its Divisions
65:11.anchors:
- Root: عقل (ʿaql)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The root denotes binding, restraining, and holding back; the intellect is that which restrains the soul from base desires and prevents it from straying.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "العقل يقال للقوة المتهيئة لقبول العلم، ويقال للعلم الذي يستفيده الإنسان بتلك القوة عقل" — The intellect is said of the faculty prepared for the reception of knowledge, and it is also said of the knowledge which man acquires by means of that faculty.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): intellectual apprehension and understanding. Metaphorical (Majaz): "نخلة لا تعقل الإبار" — a palm tree that does not accept pollination, i.e., does not grasp or take in.
- Root: علم (ʿilm)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Knowledge as the mark or sign by which a thing is known; the trace or landmark that guides.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "العلم: إدراك الشيء بحقيقته" — Knowledge is the apprehension of a thing in its true reality; it is of two kinds: apprehension of the essence of a thing, and judgment upon a thing regarding what exists for it or is negated of it.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: certain awareness. Metaphorical: "هو من أعلام العلم الخافقه" — he is among the lofty banners of knowledge; knowledge as a guiding landmark (maʿlam).
- Root: نور (nūr)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Light; the first to set up beacons (manār) on his path in his campaigns to guide his return.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "النور: الضوء المنتشر الذي يعين على الإبصار" — Light is the diffused radiance that aids vision; it is of two kinds: that perceived by the eye of inner insight (baṣīrah) — such as the light of the intellect and the light of the Qur'an — and that perceived by the eye of the head, such as the celestial bodies.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: illumination. Metaphorical: "نور الأمر: بينه" — he illuminated the matter: he made it clear; "وهذا أنور من ذاك: أبين" — this is more luminous than that: more evident.
- Sibawayh Rule: Restriction and Focused Predication (al-ḥaṣr wa al-taqyīd bi-innamā) — governing the exclusive attribution of a predicate to a subject, as in the author's restriction of the scholar's condition to one of two men, and the exclusion of the third.
65:11.topic: Al-Ghazali on constant remembrance of God and contemplative invocations, from 'Condemnation of Delusion'

77:31.arabic: فكذلك سماع وصف الطاعات دون العمل بها لا يغني من الله شيئا فكل وعظ لم يغير منك صفة تغييرا يغير أفعالك حتى تقبل على الله إقبالا قويا أو ضعيفا وتعرض عن الدنيا فذلك الوعظ زيادة حجة عليك فإذا رأيته وسيلة لك كنت مغرورا فإن قلت فما ذكرته من مداخل الغرور أمر لا يتخلص منه أحد ولا يمكن الاحتراز منه وهذا يوجب اليأس إذ لا يقوى أحد من البشر على الحذر من خفايا هذه الآفات فأقول الإنسان إذا افترقت همته في شيء أظهر اليأس منه واستعظم الأمر واستوعر الطريق وإذا صح منه الهوى اهتدى إلى الحيل واستنبط بدقيق النظر خفايا ا
77:31.english: ...weeping over them, yet possessing no resolve. And perhaps he hears a terrifying discourse, yet does no more than clap his hands and say, "O Peace, grant peace!" or "We seek refuge in God!" or "Glory be to God!" — supposing that he has thereby brought forth all good, while he is utterly deluded (maghrūr).
77:31.section_title_en: The Revival of the Religious Sciences — Section 910: On the Delusions of the Self-Conceited Listener and the Threefold Means of Deliverance from Deception
77:31.anchors:
- Root: غرر (gh-r-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The manifest trace or mark of a thing; heedlessness (ghirrah) in wakefulness; the edge of a sword.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): To strike one's gharrah (forelock/vulnerable spot) — i.e., to take him unawares and attain one's aim from him; the root denotes an apparent effect, hence "delusion" (ghurūr) as being deceived by a surface appearance.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (haqīqah): heedlessness and being overtaken unawares. Metaphorical (majāz): "a day white (agharru) with blazing heat" — the deception of the self-deluded man is that he sees his mere listening as the very act of worship.
- Root: عقل (ʿ-q-l)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The intellect as a faculty prepared for receiving knowledge; also the knowledge acquired thereby; restraint and binding (as the camel is hobbled — ʿiqāl).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Al-ʿaql is said of the power disposed to accept knowledge, and is said of the knowledge which a man acquires by that power." It is the innate, God-given light.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "I have not done such-and-such since I attained reason (ʿaqaltu)." Metaphorical: "a palm-tree that does not accept pollination (lā taʿqil al-ibār)" — i.e., does not receive it. The intellect is that which receives and accepts guidance.
- Root: فطر (f-ṭ-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To split lengthwise; to originate and create a thing anew (faṭara Allāhu al-khalqa).
  * Al-Raghib (Al-Mufradat): "The origin of fatr is splitting lengthwise... Faṭara Allāh al-khalq: He originated them." The innate disposition (fiṭrah) is the original constitution upon which a thing is brought forth.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "Every newborn is born upon the fiṭrah" — i.e., upon the natural constitution receptive to the religion of truth. Metaphorical: "No good in a half-baked opinion (al-ra'y al-fatīr)" — that which has not been matured and perfected.
- Root: انس (a-n-s)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Sociability, familiarity, and the human being (insān) as a social creature.
  * Al-Raghib (Al-Mufradat): The jinn and mankind as creatures; the human being is distinguished by that which perceives realities.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "I found comfort in him (anastu bihi)." Metaphorical: "He is the intimate companion (ibn urns) of so-and-so" — his special confidant. The soul's turning toward God is its true intimacy (uns).
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication — Innamā)
  * The particle innamā restricts the predicate to the subject alone, negating all else. In the author's statement "he is delivered from it only by three things: action, knowledge, and gnosis," the restriction (ḥaṣr) establishes that these three are the exclusive and exhaustive means of salvation from delusion — nothing else avails.
77:31.topic: Al-Ghazali on purifying the character, moral diseases, and spiritual remedies, from 'Condemnation of Delusion'

86:15.arabic: الماكرين وقال تعالى إنهم يكيدون كيدا وأكيد كيدا فمهل الكافرين أمهلهم رويدا فكما لا يجوز للعبد المهمل أن يستدل بإهمال السيد إياه وتمكينه من النعم على حب السيد بل ينبغي أن يحذر أن يكون ذلك مكرا منه وكيدا مع أن السيد لم يحذره مكر نفسه فبأن يجب ذلك في حق الله تعالى مع تحذيره استدراجه أولى فإذن من أمن مكر الله فهو مغتر ومنشأ هذا الغرور أنه استدل بنعم الدنيا على أنه كريم عند ذلك المنعم واحتمل أن يكون ذلك دليل الهوان ولكن ذلك الاحتمال لا يوافق الهوى فالشيطان بواسطة الهوى يميل بالقلب إلى ما يوافقه وهو التصديق بدلالته على الكرامة وهذ
86:15.english: As for knowing it by way of authoritative transmission and affirmation (taṣdīq): it is that one believes in the Book of God — exalted is He — and affirms His Messenger. For God — exalted is He — has said: {«أيحسبون أن ما نمدهم به من مال وبنين * نسارع لهم في الخيرات بل لا يشعرون»} — "Do they reckon that what We extend to them of wealth and sons — [that] We hasten for them good things? Nay, but they do not perceive" (Q. 23:55-56). And He said — exalted is He: {«سنستدرجهم من حيث لا يعلمون»} — "We shall draw them on by degrees from whence they do not know" (Q. 7:182). And He said — exalted is He: {«فتحنا عليهم أبواب كل شيء حتى إذا فرحوا بما أوتوا أخذناهم بغتة فإذا هم مبلسون»} — "We opened upon them the gates of everything, until when they rejoiced in what they were given, We seized them suddenly, and behold, they were in despair" (Q. 6:44). And in the interpretation of His saying — exalted is He: {«سنستدرجهم من حيث لا يعلمون»} — it is said: "Whenever they innovated a sin, We innovated for them a blessing, to increase their self-deception." And He said — exalted is He: {«إنما نملي لهم ليزدادوا إثما»} — "We only grant them respite that they may increase in sin" (Q. 3:178). And He said — exalted is He: {«ولا تحسبن الله غافلا عما يعمل الظالمون إنما يؤخرهم ليوم تشخص فيه الأبصار»} — "And do not reckon God heedless of what the wrongdoers do; He only delays them to a Day when eyes will stare fixedly" (Q. 14:42). And [there is] more of that kind which has come in the Book of God — exalted is He — and in the Sunnah of His Messenger. So whoever believes in it is delivered from this self-deception. For the origin of this self-deception is ignorance of God and of His attributes; for whoever knows Him does not feel secure from His stratagem (makr) and is not deceived by such corrupt fancies.
86:15.section_title_en: Section 888 — On the Remedy for Self-Deception (Ghurūr): Recognizing the Signs of Divine Honor (Karāmah) and Humiliation (Hawān)
86:15.anchors:
- Root: غرر (gh-r-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of an outward trace or mark; heedlessness in wakefulness; the blaze on a horse's forehead.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Ghurūr" is delusion stemming from heedlessness — the soul's being overtaken while imagining security, as in {«ما غرك بربك الكريم»} (Q. 82:6). It is the state of one who is deceived by apparent favors while blind to their underlying test.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): heedlessness and exposure to predation, like a gazelle deceived by moonlight. Metaphorical (Majaz): being "deceived by God" (ightirār billāh) — trusting in His mercy while persisting in disobedience.
- Root: لهم (l-h-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Swallowing whole; the gullet.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Ilhām" — God's casting a meaning into the heart (al-raw'), distinct from demonic whispering; the channel of inner vision for the knowers (ʿārifūn).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: to swallow. Metaphorical: the heart's receptive "swallowing" of divine inspiration.
- Root: حدث (ḥ-d-th)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Origination after non-existence; newness.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Ḥudūth" — a thing's coming to be after it was not; "muḥdith" — the originator, exclusively God for substances (jawāhir). "Iḥdāth" — bringing about a novel state or act.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: temporal newness. Metaphorical: "muḥaddath" — one inspired with correct discernment, as if newly spoken-to.
- Root: نعم (n-ʿ-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Softness, ease, well-being; a state of comfort.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Niʿmah" — the good state one inhabits; "naʿīm" — the act of living pleasantly. Blessings are both a test and a sign, per {«وإن تعدوا نعمة الله لا تحصوها»} (Q. 16:18).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: bounty and comfort. Metaphorical: "khafat naʿāmatuhum" — their prosperity vanished; blessings may signal either favor or gradual ruin (istidrāj).
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction and Focused Predication with "innamā")
  * In {«إنما نملي لهم ليزدادوا إثما»} (Q. 3:178) and {«إنما يؤخرهم ليوم تشخص فيه الأبصار»} (Q. 14:42), "innamā" restricts the purpose of divine respite exclusively to increase of sin and deferred reckoning — negating any reading of it as benevolent indulgence.
86:15.topic: Al-Ghazali on purifying the character, moral diseases, and spiritual remedies, from 'Condemnation of Delusion'

89:15.arabic: أنها هوان كما أخبر الله تعالى عنه إذ قال فأما الإنسان إذا ما ابتلاه ربه فأكرمه ونعمه فيقول ربي أكرمن وأما إذا ما ابتلاه فقدر عليه رزقه فيقول ربي أهانن فأجاب الله عن ذلك كلا أي ليس كما قال إنما هو ابتلاء نعوذ بالله من شر البلاء ونسأل الله التثبيت فبين أن ذلك غرور قال الحسن كذبهما جميعا بقوله كلا يقول ليس هذا بإكرامي ولا هذا بهواني ولكن الكريم من أكرمته بطاعتي غنيا كان أو فقيرا والمهان من أهنته بمعصيتي غنيا كان أو فقيرا
89:15.english: It was said of that sort, so they are falsehoods (akādhīb). And even if it were so, then "there will surely be for me in Paradise better than this" {«لَيَكُونَنَّ لِي فِي الْجَنَّةِ خَيْرٌ مِنْ هَذَا»}. Likewise, God Most High described the saying of al-ʿĀṣ ibn Wāʾil when he said, "I will surely be given wealth and children" {«لَأُوتَيَنَّ مَالًا وَوَلَدًا»}. So God Most High replied to him: "Has he looked into the unseen, or has he taken with the Most Merciful a covenant? No indeed (kallā)" {«أَطَّلَعَ الْغَيْبَ أَمِ اتَّخَذَ عِنْدَ الرَّحْمَنِ عَهْدًا كَلَّا»}. And it is related from Khabbāb ibn al-Aratt that he said: I had a debt owed to me by al-ʿĀṣ ibn Wāʾil, so I came demanding payment, but he did not pay me. So I said, "I will indeed take it from you in the Hereafter." He said to me, "When you come to the Hereafter, I will have there wealth and children, and I will pay you from it." So God Most High revealed His saying: "Have you seen the one who disbelieved in Our signs and said, 'I will surely be given wealth and children'?" {«أَفَرَأَيْتَ الَّذِي كَفَرَ بِآيَاتِنَا وَقَالَ لَأُوتَيَنَّ مَالًا وَوَلَدًا»}. (1) The hadith "God protects His servant from the world while loving him" — narrated by al-Tirmidhī who deemed it good (ḥasan), and by al-Ḥākim who deemed it authentic (ṣaḥīḥ), from the report of Qatādah ibn al-Nuʿmān. Thus it came in the report from the master of mankind (peace be upon him).
89:15.section_title_en: The Delusion of Wealth and the Reality of Divine Trial — Section 887
89:15.anchors:
- Root: كلا (Kalla)
  * Lisan / Ayn: An emphatic particle of denial and refutation; signifies categorical rejection of a prior claim.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Used to negate and refute utterly; here, it rebuts the deluded assumption that wealth signals divine favor.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah) — a decisive "No!"; Metaphorical (Majaz) — not merely denying words but the very presumption underlying them.
- Root: حدث (Ḥadatha)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To originate, to be new; in Kalam, that which comes into being after non-existence.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الحدوث: كون الشيء بعد أن لم يكن" — origination of a thing after it was not; divine acts of trial are originated events.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — new occurrences; Metaphorical — "محدث" as one whose inner state is renewed by divine testing.
- Root: كذب (Kadhaba)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To lie, to falsify; a false report or claim.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Falsehood in word and deed; here, the disbeliever's boast is exposed as self-deception.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — verbal lying; Metaphorical — "كذبهما جميعا" (he declared both of them liars) — attributing falsity to the two human assumptions about wealth and poverty.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — "إنما هو ابتلاء" restricts the reality of wealth and poverty solely to divine testing, excluding the deluded interpretations of honor or humiliation.
89:15.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'Condemnation of Delusion'

2:206.arabic: يحمل ذلك على الأنفة من قبول الوعظ كما قال تعالى {وإذا قيل له اتق الله أخذته العزة بالإثم} وروي عن عمر رضي الله عنه أنه قرأها فقال {إنا لله وإنا إليه راجعون} قام رجل يأمر بالمعروف فقتل فقام آخر فقال يقتلون الذين يأمرون بالقسط من الناس فقتل المتكبر الذي خالفه والذي أمره كبرا وقال ابن مسعود كفى بالرجل إثما إذا قيل له اتق الله قال عليك نفسك وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم لرجل كل بيمينك قال لا أستطيع فقال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ل أستطيع فقال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لا فما منعه إلا كبره قال فما رفعها بعد ذلك (1) حديث قول ثابت بن قيس بن شماس إ
2:206.english: The second aspect by which the vice of pride is magnified is that it calls to opposing Allah the Exalted in His commands. For the arrogant man, when he hears the truth from a servant among the servants of Allah, disdains to accept it and girds himself for its denial. For this reason you see the disputants in matters of religion claiming that they are investigating the secrets of the religion, yet they engage in mutual denial—the denial of the arrogant. Whenever the truth becomes clear upon the tongue of one of them, the other refuses to accept it out of pride, girds himself for its denial, and resorts to every stratagem to repel it by whatever obfuscation he can muster. This is among the moral traits of the disbelievers and the hypocrites, for Allah the Exalted described them, saying: {«وَقَالَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا لَا تَسْمَعُوا لِهَذَا الْقُرْآنِ وَالْغَوْا فِيهِ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَغْلِبُونَ»} (And those who disbelieve said: "Do not listen to this Quran and make noise therein, perhaps you may prevail.") So whoever disputes for the sake of victory and silencing the opponent—not to seize the truth when it appears to him—has shared with them in this moral trait. Likewise, this pride drives one to refuse admonition, as Allah the Exalted said: {«وَإِذَا قِيلَ لَهُ اتَّقِ اللَّهَ أَخَذَتْهُ الْعِزَّةُ بِالْإِثْمِ»} (And when it is said to him, "Fear Allah," pride in sin seizes him.) It is narrated that ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him, recited this verse and then said: {«إِنَّا لِلَّهِ وَإِنَّا إِلَيْهِ رَاجِعُونَ»} (Indeed, we belong to Allah and to Him we return.) A man rose to enjoin good and was killed; then another rose and said: "They kill those who enjoin justice among the people"—and the arrogant one who opposed him and the one who commanded him was killed out of pride.
2:206.section_title_en: The Second Aspect by Which the Vice of Pride (Kibr) Is Magnified: That It Leads to Opposing Allah in His Commands
2:206.anchors:
- Root: كبر (K-B-R)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of bigness, magnitude, and seniority; al-kibr is the internal disposition of self-magnification.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-Kabīr and al-Ṣaghīr are relative terms (mutadāyifān); kibr as a moral vice is the soul's claim to a station above its due, entailing disdain for others.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) usage concerns physical or quantitative magnitude; metaphorical (majāz) usage here denotes arrogance and haughtiness—"كبر عليه" (he disdained it).
- Root: علم (ʿ-L-M)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Knowing a thing's reality; the root also carries the sense of a mark/trace (ʿalam) by which one is guided.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): True knowledge (ʿilm) is apprehension of a thing's essence or judgment about it; the highest form is knowledge of Allah, the self, and the Final End—this engenders fear (khashyah).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: perception and awareness; metaphorical: the "marks" (maʿālim) of religion—the distinguishing signs of guidance.
- Root: نفس (N-F-S)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The self, soul, or spirit; that which is valued and precious.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-Nafs denotes the soul or self; in theological usage it may refer to the essence (dhāt) of a thing.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the soul; metaphorical: self-worth and self-regard—the arrogant man "magnifies his own soul" (istaʿẓama nafsahu).
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — The verse {إِنَّمَا يَخْشَى اللَّهَ مِنْ عِبَادِهِ الْعُلَمَاءُ} restricts true fear of Allah exclusively to the learned, delimiting the predicate to the subject.
2:206.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'Condemnation of Pride and Conceit'

2:249.arabic: يتفكر في ضعفه وضعفهم وأن كلهم عبيد عجزة لا يملكون لأنفسهم ضرا ولا نفعا {كم من فئة قليلة غلبت فئة كثيرة بإذن الله} ثم كيف يعجب بهم وأنهم سيفترقون عنه إذا مات فيدفن في قبره ذليلا مهينا وحده لا يرافقه أهل ولا ولد ولا قريب ولا حميم ولا عشير فيسلمونه إلى البلى والحيات والعقارب والديدان ولا يغنون عنه شيئا وفي أحوج أوقاته إليهم وكذلك يهربون منه يوم القيامة {يوم يفر المرء من أخيه وأمه وأبيه وصاحبته وبنيه} الآية فأي خير فيمن يفارقك في أشد أحوالك ويهرب منك وكيف تعجب به ولا ينفعك في القبر والقيامة وعلى الصراط إلا عملك وفضل الله تعالى فكيف تتكل على من لا ينفعك وتنسى
2:249.english: If you say: "He, peace and blessings be upon him, said after his words to Fāṭimah and Ṣafiyyah: 'I cannot avail you against God in anything, except that you have a tie of kinship which I will moisten with its moisture'" — a ḥadīth [reported as]: "Do you hope for my intercession, while the Banū ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib do not hope for it?" — narrated by al-Ṭabarānī in al-Awsaṭ from the narration of ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jaʿfar, and in it is Uṣayrim ibn Ḥawshab from Isḥāq ibn Wāṣil, and both are extremely weak — so that indicates that he will single out his relatives for intercession.
2:249.section_title_en: Section 882 — On the Limits of Intercession, the Vices of Pride in Lineage, Numbers, Wealth, and Opinion, and Their Treatment
2:249.anchors:
- Root: شفع (Sh-F-')
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning is pairing or joining; intercession (shafā'ah) is the joining of one's plea to another's cause.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Intercession is the seeking of benefit for another; its acceptance is contingent upon divine permission and good pleasure, as restricted by the Qur'anic qualifiers.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (haqīqah) is the act of making a number even (from watr, odd); metaphorical (majāz) is the mediator's plea before authority.
- Root: عجب (ʿ-J-B)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Astonishment arising from an unknown cause; self-admiration (ʿujb) is a blameworthy state of being pleased with oneself.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "العجب والتعجب: حالة تعرض للإنسان عند الجهل بسبب الشيء" — a state that overtakes a person due to ignorance of the cause; hence, it is impossible regarding God.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: a wondrous thing; metaphorical: the one who performs marvels (taʿjābah). Self-admiration is the root of every error and innovation.
- Root: رأي (R-'-Y)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Opinion, view, or judgment formed through reflection.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Ra'y is the considered opinion that may err or hit the mark; it is blameworthy when it becomes an object of ʿujb (self-admiration).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: sight/vision; metaphorical: intellectual insight. The ḥadīth "إعجاب كل ذي رأي برأيه" (the admiration of every man of opinion for his own view) is cited as a sign of the age's corruption.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد (Restriction and Qualification) — The conditional clauses (in-sharṭ) governing intercession, e.g., {إلا لمن ارتضى} and {إلا بإذنه}, impose necessary restrictions that negate any absolute reliance on intercession.
2:249.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Condemnation of Pride and Conceit'
