3:59.arabic: الله من أرذل الأشياء ثم من أقذرها إذ قد خلقه من تراب ثم من نطفة ثم من علقة ثم من مضغة ثم جعله عظما ثم كسا العظم لحما فقد كان هذا بداية وجوده حيث كان شيئا مذكورا فما صار شيئا مذكورا إلا وهو على أخس الأوصاف والنعوت إذ لم يخلق في ابتدائه كاملا بل خلقه جمادا ميتا لا يسمع ولا يبصر ولا يحس ولا يتحرك ولا ينطق ولا يبطش ولا يدرك ولا يعلم فبدأ بموته قبل حياته وبضعفه قبل قوته وبجهله قبل علمه وبعماه قبل بصره وبصممه قبل سمعه وببكمه قبل نطقه وبضلالته قبل هداه وبفقره قبل غناه وبعجزه قبل قدرته فهذا معنى قوله
3:59.english: As for his knowledge of his Lord, His greatness, and His glory — the discourse thereon is lengthy, and it is the ultimate end of the science of unveiling (ʿilm al-mukāshafah). As for his knowledge of himself, that too is lengthy; but we shall mention therefrom that which benefits in arousing humility and lowliness. And it suffices him to understand the meaning of a single verse in the Book of God — for in the Qurʾān is the knowledge of the first and the last, for him whose inner sight has been opened. God, may He be exalted, has said: {«قُتِلَ الْإِنْسَانُ مَا أَكْفَرَهُ ۝ مِنْ أَيِّ شَيْءٍ خَلَقَهُ ۝ مِنْ نُطْفَةٍ خَلَقَهُ فَقَدَّرَهُ ۝ ثُمَّ السَّبِيلَ يَسَّرَهُ ۝ ثُمَّ أَمَاتَهُ فَأَقْبَرَهُ ۝ ثُمَّ إِذَا شَاءَ أَنْشَرَهُ»} [ʿAbasa: 17–22] — "May man be killed! How ungrateful he is! From what thing did He create him? From a drop of fluid He created him and proportioned him. Then the path He made easy for him. Then He causes him to die and buries him. Then when He wills, He raises him." The verse has pointed to the first origin of man, to the last of his affair, and to his middle state. Let man, then, look upon that, in order to understand the meaning of this verse.
3:59.section_title_en: Exposition of the Character Traits of the Humble and the Sum Total of Wherein the Effect of Humility and Arrogance Appears — and the Exposition of the Method of Treating Arrogance and Acquiring Humility
3:59.anchors:
- Root: تواضع (tawāḍuʿ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Root و-ض-ع: to place down, lower, set in a low position; al-tawāḍuʿ is self-lowering, the voluntary assumption of lowness.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-waḍʿ is placing a thing in a station; tawāḍuʿ is the soul's self-abasement before truth and before the Creator, opposed to takabbur (self-elevation).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Haqīqah: physical lowering of position. Majāz: the soul's humility and abandonment of claims to eminence.
- Root: كبر (kibr)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Root ك-ب-ر: bigness, magnitude; al-kibriyāʾ is exclusive divine majesty; al-kibr (arrogance) is the creature's false claim to that majesty.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-kibr is the soul's self-magnification, a claim to a station of greatness that belongs to God alone; it is the root of all disobedience.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Haqīqah: physical greatness. Majāz: the heart's disdain of others and refusal of truth — the blameworthy kibr.
- Root: نطف (nuṭfah)
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-nuṭfah: pure water, used for the seminal fluid. {«ثُمَّ جَعَلْنَاهُ نُطْفَةً فِي قَرَارٍ مَكِينٍ»} [Al-Muʾminūn: 13].
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Haqīqah: clear water, little or much. Majāz: "laylah naṭūf" — a night raining until morning.
- Root: خلق (khalaqa)
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-khalq: measured estimation (taqdīr mustaqīm); used for bringing forth from nothing without model, and for producing a thing from another thing.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Haqīqah: the tailor's cutting cloth to measure. Majāz: God's origination of creatures upon a measure necessitated by wisdom.
- Sibawayh Rule: Bāb al-ʿaṭf ʿalā al-ḍamīr al-marfūʿ al-muttaṣil (Coordination upon the connected nominative pronoun) — permissible when preceded by an explicit subject, as in "خلقه من نطفة فقدره" where the sequence of verbs coordinates without repetition of the pronoun, each verb governing its own object in ordered succession.
3:59.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Condemnation of Pride and Conceit'

3:59.arabic: الصحابة فقال صلى الله عليه وسلم لا تزرموه أي لا تقطعوا عليه البول ثم قال له إن هذه المساجد لا تصلح لشيء من القذر والبول والخلاء (1) وفي رواية قربوا ولا تنفروا وجاءه أعرابي يوما يطلب منه شيئا فأعطاه صلى الله عليه وسلم ثم قال له أحسنت إليك قال الأعرابي لا ولا أجملت قال فغضب المسلمون وقاموا إليه فأشار إليهم أن كفوا ثم قام ودخل منزله وأرسل إلى الأعرابي وزاده شيئا ثم قال أحسنت إليك قال نعم فجزاك الله من أهل وعشيرة خيرا فقال له النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم إنك قلت ما قلت وفي نفس أصحابي شيء من ذلك فإن أحببت فقل بين أيديهم ما
3:59.english: The Messenger of Allah (Peace Be Upon Him) was delicate of skin, subtle in his outward and inward being; his anger and his pleasure were known in his face. (7) And when his feeling intensified, he would increase his touching of his noble beard. (8) And he never addressed anyone with what he disliked. A man entered upon him with yellowness [of dye] upon him, and he disliked it, yet he said nothing to him until he left. Then he said to some of the people: "Would that you had said to this man: let him leave this" — meaning the yellowness. And a Bedouin urinated in the mosque in his presence, and the Companions (may Allah be pleased with them) rushed at him. The Prophet (Peace Be Upon Him) said: "Do not interrupt him" — that is, do not cut off his urination. Then he said to him: "These mosques are not fit for any filth, urine, or excrement." (1) And in another narration: "Draw near, and do not repel."
3:59.book_title: Etiquette of Living and Prophetic Character
3:59.section_title_en: The Revival of the Religious Sciences — Book on the Etiquette of Prophethood: Section on His (Peace Be Upon Him) Overlooking What He Disliked, and His Generosity
3:59.anchors:
- Root: رق ق (Raqq)
  * Lisan / Ayn: رقيق البشرة — delicate, fine, soft in skin; thin and subtle in substance.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Denotes fineness of the corporeal envelope, yet here extended to inward subtlety (al-latāfah al-bāṭiniyyah), indicating a divinely polished temperament.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (haqīqah) for skin; metaphorical (majāz) for character—"latīf al-ẓāhir wa al-bāṭin" shifts from the sensory to the moral-spiritual register.
- Root: وج د (Wajd)
  * Lisan / Ayn: وج د — intense emotion, found anger or grief; "ishdadda wajduhu" — when his feeling intensified.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In Kalam, wajd is an affective state of the soul, not a mere passing whim; here it denotes righteous displeasure.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: to find; metaphorical: the surge of an overpowering emotion that "finds" its object.
- Root: ز ر م (Zarama)
  * Lisan / Ayn: أَزْرَمَ — to cut off, sever, interrupt a flow; "lā tazrimūhu" — do not cut off his urine.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Not a Quranic root but a Prophetic usage; denotes abrupt cessation of a natural act, which is harmful.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: to sever a continuous stream; here applied to the Bedouin's urination—an act of interruption that would cause physical harm.
- Root: ع ض ه (Aḍah)
  * Lisan / Ayn: العَضَاه — thorny desert trees, the 'idāh (plural: ʿiḍāh) of the acacia type; used as a measure of abundance.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Not a theological term; in Prophetic rhetoric, it is a concrete, sensory metaphor for countless wealth.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the trees themselves; metaphorical: the sheer number of camels equal to these trees—hyperbole for limitless generosity.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The rule governing the placement of "la-hu" and similar particles, where the prepositional phrase is fronted for emphasis (takhrīb) or to avoid ambiguity, as in "لو كان لي عدد هذه العضاة نعما" — the interposition of "li" before the quantified noun clarifies the conditional scope.
3:59.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'Etiquette of Living and Prophetic Character'

4:172.arabic: ربكم الأعلى إذ استنكف أن يكون عبدا لله ولذلك قال تعالى إن الذين يستكبرون عن عبادتي سيدخلون جهنم داخرين وقال تعالى لن يستنكف المسيح أن يكون عبدا لله ولا الملائكة المقربون الآية وقال تعالى وإذا قيل لهم اسجدوا للرحمن قالوا وما الرحمن أنسجد لما تأمرنا وزادهم نفورا القسم الثاني التكبر على الرسل من حيث تعزز النفس وترفعها على الانقياد لبشر مثل سائر الناس وذلك تارة يصرف عن الفكر والاستبصار فيبقى في ظلمة الجهل بكبره فيمتنع عن الانقياد وهو ظان أنه محق فيه وتارة يمتنع مع المعرفة ولكن لا تطاوع
4:172.english: Know that the one against whom pride is directed is either God—mighty and majestic—or His messengers, or the rest of His creation. Man has been created unjust and ignorant {«وخلق الإنسان ظلوما جهولا»}, so at times he grows proud against the creation, and at times he grows proud against the Creator. Thus, pride, considered with respect to the one against whom it is directed, falls into three divisions.
4:172.section_title_en: Exposition of the One Against Whom Pride Is Directed, Its Degrees, Its Divisions, and the Fruits of Pride Within It
4:172.anchors:
- Root: كبر (k-b-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root denotes magnitude, whether physical size, age, or rank; "الكبرة" specifically marks the state of advanced age or an ingrained, chronic condition.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الكبير والصغير من الأسماء المتضايفة" — bigness and smallness are relative terms. In the theological context, pride (الكبر) is the soul's self-magnification against another, a relational vice that distorts the creature's standing before the Creator.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah) usage concerns physical or quantitative magnitude. Metaphorical (Majaz) usage transfers this to moral and spiritual stature, as in "كبر علي ذلك" (it weighed heavily upon him) — here, the soul's swelling against divine command is a metaphorical arrogation of greatness.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Prepositional Interposition (باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور) — Governing the syntactic tension between the agent of pride (المتكبر) and its object (المتكبر عليه), where the preposition "على" carries the full weight of opposition and elevation, structuring the periodic sentences that follow.
4:172.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Condemnation of Pride and Conceit'

4:172.arabic: عن عبادتي سيدخلون جهنم داخرين وقال تعالى لن يستنكف المسيح أن يكون عبدا لله ولا الملائكة المقربون الآية وقال تعالى وإذا قيل لهم اسجدوا للرحمن قالوا وما الرحمن أنسجد لما تأمرنا وزادهم نفورا القسم الثاني التكبر على الرسل من حيث تعزز النفس وترفعها على الانقياد لبشر مثل سائر الناس وذلك تارة يصرف عن الفكر والاستبصار فيبقى في ظلمة الجهل بكبره فيمتنع عن الانقياد وهو ظان أنه محق فيه وتارة يمتنع مع المعرفة ولكن لا تطاوعه نفسه للإنقياد للحق والتواضع للرسل كما حكى الله قولهم أنؤمن لبشرين مثلنا {وقولهم} إن أنتم إلا بشر مثلنا ولئن أطعتم بشرا مثلكم إنكم إذا لخاس

6:8.arabic: الملائكة أو نرى ربنا لقد استكبروا في أنفسهم وعتوا عتوا كبيرا وقالوا لولا أنزل عليه ملك وقال فرعون فيما أخبر الله عنه {أو جاء معه الملائكة مقترنين} وقال الله تعالى {واستكبر هو وجنوده في الأرض بغير الحق} فتكبر هو على الله وعلى رسله جميعا قال وهب قال له موسى عليه السلام آمن ولك ملكك قال حتى أشاور هامان فشاور هامان فقال هامان بينما أنت رب يعبد إذ صرت عبد تعبد فاسنكف عن عبودية الله وعن اتباع موسى عليه السلام وقالت قريش فيما أخبر الله تعالى عنهم {لولا نزل هذا القرآن على رجل من القريتين عظيم} قال قتاده عظيم القريتين هو الوليد بن المغ
6:8.english: Know that the one against whom pride is directed is either God—mighty and majestic—or His messengers, or the rest of His creation. Man has been created unjust and ignorant {«وخلق الإنسان ظلوما جهولا»}, so at times he grows proud against the creation, and at times he grows proud against the Creator. Thus, pride, considered with respect to the one against whom it is directed, falls into three divisions.

9:118.arabic: في الحر والشمس زمانا طويلا حتى إذا ضاق عليه الأمر وبلغ به المجهود أمر برفع حسابه
9:118.english: For this reason, Kaʿb al-Aḥbār said: "Knowledge has a tyranny like the tyranny of wealth."
9:118.section_title_en: The Sixth Cause of Pride: Pride in Knowledge — Its Danger and the First Remedy
9:118.anchors:
- Root: كبر (k-b-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of bigness in stature, age, or rank; "كبر عليه" = to be grievous/heavy upon one.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Al-Kabīr and al-ṣaghīr are relative terms (mutadāyifān) — a thing is small beside one thing and great beside another; used of both connected quantity (bodies) and disconnected quantity (number)."
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): "Kabar al-amr" = the matter became great; "kabura ʿalayhi" = it was burdensome. Metaphorical (majāz): applied to rank, honor, and station, not merely physical size.
- Root: علم (ʿ-l-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Perception and apprehension of a thing as it truly is; the root also yields "ʿalam" (sign/marker) and "maʿlam" (landmark) — knowledge as that by which one is guided.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Al-ʿilm: idrāk al-shayʾ bi-ḥaqīqatihi" — apprehension of a thing in its true reality; two kinds: (1) apprehension of the essence of a thing, (2) judgment upon a thing affirming or denying something of it.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "Huwa min aʿlām al-ʿilm al-khāfiqah" — he is among the lofty banners of knowledge; "maʿālim al-ṭarīq" = the traces by which the road is recognized. Knowledge is that which marks and distinguishes.
- Root: خطر (kh-ṭ-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To be in peril; "khaṭar" = danger, risk; also "khaṭara bi-nafsihi" = to hazard oneself.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Not separately glossed in the retrieved entry, but the Qur'anic usage (e.g., "akhṭara" in the sense of grave consequence) aligns with the notion of imminent peril.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "Khaṭar" = danger/risk; "rajul khaṭīr" = a man of great consequence — the same root yields both "peril" and "high station," a deliberate lexical pairing Ghazali exploits here.
- Sibawayh Rule: Bāb al-faṣl bayna al-jār wa-al-majrūr (Prepositional Interposition) — The periodic sentence structure here ("فإنهما كمالان في النفس جديران بأن يفرح بهما") employs embedded relative clauses and prepositional phrases that must be unpacked in English without losing the logical subordination.
9:118.topic: Al-Ghazali on the journey of the soul, death, and the Hereafter, from 'Condemnation of Pride and Conceit'

9:126.arabic: وقال تعالى أولا يرون أنهم يفتنون في كل عام مرة أو مرتين ثم لا يتوبون ولا هم يذكرون قيل يفتنون بأمراض يختبرون بها ويقال إن العبد إذا مرض مرضتين ثم لم يتب قال له ملك الموت:
9:126.english: Pain is an expiation for the day [of sins]. And when he—peace and blessings be upon him—mentioned the expiation of sins through fever, Zayd ibn Thabit asked his Lord—mighty and majestic—that he not cease to be feverish, and the fever did not leave him until he died—may God have mercy on him. A group of the Ansar also asked for that, and the fever did not cease to afflict them. And when he—peace and blessings be upon him—said: "Whoever God takes away his two precious things [his eyes]," he was not satisfied for him with a reward less than Paradise. The hadith: "Whoever God takes away his two precious things, He is not satisfied for him with a reward less than Paradise"—the marfuʿ portion of it has preceded without his saying: "He said: For indeed among the Ansar there were those who wished for blindness." And Jesus—peace be upon him—said: "He is not a scholar who does not rejoice at the entry of calamities and illnesses upon his body and his wealth, for what he hopes in that of the expiation of his sins." And it is related that Moses—peace be upon him—looked upon a servant of great affliction and said: "O Lord, have mercy on him." So He—exalted—said: "How shall I have mercy on him when through what afflicts him I have mercy on him?"—that is, through it I expiate his sins and increase his ranks.
9:126.section_title_en: The Sixth Cause for Not Seeking Medical Treatment: Fear of Returning to Negligence and Transgression Through Health
9:126.anchors:
- Root: مرض (m-r-ḍ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning is departure from the balanced state of the body—sickness, ailment, malady.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Twofold: (1) corporeal illness, and (2) metaphorical expression for moral vices—ignorance, cowardice, avarice, hypocrisy—as in {«فِي قُلُوبِهِم مَّرَضٌ»} (Al-Baqarah 10).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): bodily sickness. Metaphorical (Majaz): "مرض في الأمر" (to be weak/lax in a matter), and "تمارض" (to feign illness). Here, the text uses the literal sense for bodily fever, but the underlying spiritual cure is freedom from the "disease" of disobedience.
- Root: حمي (ḥ-m-y)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: heat, fever; to protect, guard, or forbid.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الحمي: الحرارة المتولدة من الجواهر المحمية" — heat generated from heated substances; also "حميت على فلان" (to become angry/incensed). Fever (الحمى) is the specific bodily heat-illness.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "حماه حماية" (to protect him). Metaphorical: "حمي عليه إذا غضب" (to be angry), and "شديد الحميا" (fierce in self-respect). In this text, الحمى (fever) is literal, but its purpose is protective—guarding the servant from sin.
- Root: عفو (ʿ-f-w) [implied in كفارة]
  * Lisan / Ayn: كفارة derives from كفر (to cover, expiate); the root عفو means to pardon, obliterate sins.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): كفارة الذنوب — the expiation that covers sins, removing their punitive trace.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: covering. Metaphorical: expiation as a "covering" of the sin's record.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد (Restriction & Specification) — The phrase "إنما قال فرعون: أنا ربكم الأعلى لطول العافية" restricts the cause of Pharaoh's claim to prolonged well-being, using "إنما" to confine the reason. Also, the conditional structures "إذا أراد الله بعبد خيرا" and "إذا كان في المرض حبس" employ the syntactic pattern of temporal-condition clauses (ظرفية شرطية) to link divine will to consequent states.
9:126.topic: Al-Ghazali on the journey of the soul, death, and the Hereafter, from 'Monotheism and Reliance'

9:126.arabic: مباح على معنى أن من أكله مرة أو مرتين لم يعص ومن دام عليه أيضا فلا يعصي بتناوله ولكن تتربى نفسه بالنعيم فتأنس بالدنيا وتألف اللذات وتسعى في طلبها فيجرها ذلك إلى المعاصي فهم شرار الأمة لأن مخ الحنطة يقودهم إلى اقتحام أمور تلك الأمور معاص وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم شرار أمتي الذين غذوا بالنعيم ونبتت عليه أجسامهم (2) وإنما همتهم ألوان الطعام وأنواع اللباس ويتشدقون في الكلام وأوحى الله تعالى إلى موسى عليه السلام اذكر أنك ساكن القبر فإن ذلك يمنعك من كثير الشهوات وقد اشتد خوف السلف من تناول
9:126.english: Indeed, the sustenance (qūt) of a group of the Companions was a ṣāʿ of wheat every Friday. When they ate dates, they took as their sustenance a ṣāʿ and a half of them. The ṣāʿ of wheat is four mudds, so each day would be nearly half a mudd — which is what we mentioned as the measure of one-third of the stomach. An increase was needed for dates because of the pits that are discarded from them. Abū Dharr, may Allah be pleased with him, used to say: "My food every Friday is a ṣāʿ of barley, on the covenant of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him. By Allah, I will not increase upon it anything until I meet him, for I heard him say: 'The nearest of you to me in seating on the Day of Resurrection, and the most beloved of you to me, is the one who dies upon what he is upon today.'" He used to say, disapproving of some of the Companions: "You have changed — barley is sifted for you, though it was not sifted; you bake thin bread; you combine two condiments; foods of various colors are set before you; one of you goes out in one garment and returns in another. They were not like this in the era of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him."
9:126.section_title_en: The Revival of the Religious Sciences — Section 645: On Hunger and the Discipline of Eating
9:126.anchors:
- Root: جوع (j-w-ʿ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of emptiness of the belly, hunger as opposed to fullness (shabaʿ)
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Hunger as a spiritual discipline (riyāḍah) that purifies the heart and weakens the sway of sensual appetite
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) — bodily hunger; Metaphorical (majāz) — the soul's longing and deprivation as spiritual training
- Root: قوت (q-w-t)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Sustenance, nourishment that maintains life; measure of food sufficient for survival
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Provision (rizq) in its minimal necessary form; the qūt is that which sustains the body's constitution without excess
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — food that sustains; Metaphorical — the spiritual sustenance of the heart through remembrance
- Root: أدم (ʾ-d-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: That which is eaten with bread to make it palatable; condiment or relish
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The adornment of food; in spiritual discourse, the craving for variety and relish beyond bare necessity
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — condiment; Metaphorical — the soul's attachment to luxuries and embellishments of worldly life
- Root: سرف (s-r-f)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Excess, extravagance, going beyond the proper limit
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Transgression of the mean (iʿtidāl) in expenditure or consumption; blameworthy in all affairs
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — exceeding the measure; Metaphorical — spiritual extravagance in indulging desires

9:126.arabic: وقال الحسن العجب من ابن آدم يغسل الخرء بيده كل يوم مرة أو مرتين ثم يعارض جبار السموات وقد قيل في وفي أنفسكم أفلا تبصرون هو سبيل الغائط والبول وقد قال محمد بن الحسين بن علي ما دخل قلب امرئ شيء من الكبر قط إلا نقص من عقله بقدر ما دخل من ذلك أو كثر وسئل سليمان عن السيئة التي لا تنفع معها حسنة فقال الكبر وقال النعمان بن بشير على المنبر إن للشيطان مصالي وفخوخا وإن من مصالي الشيطان وفخوخه البطر بأنعم الله والفخر بإعطاء الله والكبر على عباد الله واتباع الهوى في غير ذات الله نسأل الله تعالى العفو والعافية
9:126.english: Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq, may God be pleased with him, said: "Let no one belittle any one of the Muslims, for the lowliest of the Muslims is great in the sight of God."
9:126.section_title_en: On the Vice of Pride (Section 849) — The Narrations and Sayings Concerning Arrogance
9:126.anchors:
- Root: كبر (K-B-R)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root meaning of greatness in size, age, or rank; the verbal noun *kibr* denotes arrogance as an internal disposition of self-magnification.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): *Al-Kibr* is a blameworthy self-elevation whereby one deems himself greater than others, opposing the divine attribute of *al-Kibriyā'* (Supreme Greatness) which belongs to God alone.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (*haqīqah*) usage pertains to physical or temporal magnitude; metaphorical (*majāz*) usage transfers this to moral and spiritual arrogance, as in "كبر عليه" (it weighed heavily upon him).
- Root: كنز (K-N-Z)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To amass and hoard treasure; the noun *kanz* refers to accumulated wealth kept in reserve.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In Quranic usage, *kanz* is condemned when wealth is withheld from obligatory expenditure, as in {«والذين يكنزون الذهب والفضة»} (those who hoard gold and silver).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): The variant reading discussed here hinges on orthographic confusion between *kibr* (كبر) and *kanz* (كنز), a textual-critical point affecting the reported hadith.
- Root: بطر (B-T-R)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Extravagant joy and insolence arising from abundance; to be ungrateful for blessings through reckless behavior.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): *Al-Baṭar* is a moral corruption where one misuses divine favors, failing to recognize their source, leading to transgression.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal sense is "to be cut off" or "perish"; metaphorical sense is the arrogance that severs one from gratitude and humility.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد (Restriction & Focused Predication) — The phrase "إنما هو الكنز" employs *innamā* to restrictively correct the transmitted wording, confining the true reading to *kanz* over *kibr*.

14:15.arabic: على كل قلب متكبر جبار} وقال تعالى {واستفتحوا وخاب كل جبار عنيد} وقال تعالى {إنه لا يحب المستكبرين} وقال تعالى {لقد استكبروا في أنفسهم وعتوا عتوا كبيرا} وقال تعالى {إن الذين يستكبرون عن عبادتي سيدخلون جهنم داخرين} وذم الكبر في القرآن كثير وقد قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لا يدخل الجنة من كان في قلبه مثقال حبة من خردل من كبر ولا يدخل الجنة من كان في قلبه مثقال حبة من خردل من إيمان (1) حديث أبي هريرة يقول الله تعالى الكبرياء ردائي والعظمة إزاري فمن نازعني واحدا منهما ألقيته في جهنم أخرجه مسلم و
14:15.english: To proceed: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said — God, exalted be He, said: "Pride (al-kibriyāʾ) is My cloak, and greatness (al-ʿaẓamah) is My wrapper; whoever contends with Me over either of them, I crush him." {«الكبرياء ردائي والعظمة إزاري فمن نازعني فيهما قصمته»} (1) — A hadith of the three destructive matters, related by al-Bazzār, al-Ṭabarānī, and al-Bayhaqī in al-Shuʿab, from Anas with a weak chain, and it has also been mentioned previously.
14:15.section_title_en: The Book of Condemnation of Pride and Self-Admiration — Being the Ninth Book of the Quarter of Destructive Matters from The Revival of the Religious Sciences

- Root: عجب (ʿ-j-b)

15:96.arabic: الله ولقوله ولا تجعلوا مع الله إلها آخر فمن لم يره في كل شيء فقد رأى غيره وكل ما التفت إليه العبد سوى الله تعالى تضمن التفاته شيئا من الشرك الخفي بل التوحيد الخالص أن لا يرى في كل شيء إلا الله عز وجل العاشر التبري وأعني به أن يتبرأ من حوله وقوته والالتفات إلى نفسه بين الرضا والتزكية فإذا تلا بآيات الوعد والمدح للصالحين فلا يشهد نفسه عند ذلك بل يشهد الموقنين والصديقين فيها ويتشوف إلى أن يلحقه الله عز وجل بهم وإذا تلا آيات المقت وذم العصاة والمقصرين شهد على نفسه هناك وقدر أنه المخا
15:96.english: For this reason, Yūsuf ibn Asbāṭ said: "I intend to recite the Qur'an, but when I recall what is in it, I fear abhorrence (al-maqt), so I turn instead to glorification (al-tasbīḥ) and seeking forgiveness (al-istighfār)."
15:96.section_title_en: ** The Revival of the Religious Sciences — Section 231: On the Inward Conditions of Qur'anic Recitation (Continued)
15:96.anchors:
**
- Root: وجل (w-j-l)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الوجل: استشعار الخوف" — the stirring of fear/apprehension within
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الوجل: استشعار الخوف. يقال: وجل يوجل وجلا، فهو وجل. قال تعالى: {إنما المؤمنون الذين إذا ذكر الله وجلت قلوبهم}" — the theological state of the heart's trembling upon remembrance of God
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): "رجل وجل، وقوم وجال، وقد وجل وجلا" — the physical/emotional state of fear. Metaphorical (Majaz): The heart's trembling as the seat of spiritual perception
- Root: قلب (q-l-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "قلب الشيء: تصريفه وصرفه عن وجه إلى وجه" — turning and transforming
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "قلب الشيء: تصريفه وصرفه عن وجه إلى وجه، كقلب الثوب، وقلب الإنسان" — the heart as that which is constantly turning/transforming between states
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "قلب الشيء قلبا: حوله عن وجهه" — physical turning. Metaphorical: "قلب المعلم الصبيان: صرفهم إلى بيوتهم" — the heart's turning toward or away from spiritual realities
- Root: نفس (n-f-s)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The self, soul, spirit — that which is breathed
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "النفس: الروح" — the soul as the animating principle; also the self as the locus of blameworthy attributes
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "شيء نفيس ومنفس" — preciousness. Metaphorical: "دفق نفسه أي دمه" — the self as that which must be transcended in spiritual realization
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد (Restriction & Focused Predication) — governing the precise delimitation of spiritual states (أحوال) and their hierarchical gradation (درجات)

16:22.arabic: وقال تعالى فالذين لا يؤمنون بالآخرة قلوبهم منكرة وهم مستكبرون وقال عز وجل يقول الذين استضعفوا للذين استكبروا لولا أنتم لكنا مؤمنين وقال تعالى إن الذين يستكبرون عن عبادتي سيدخلون جهنم داخرين وقال تعالى سأصرف عن آياتي الذين يتكبرون في الأرض بغير الحق قيل في التفسير سأرفع فهم القرآن عن قلوبهم وفي بعض التفاسير سأحجب قلوبهم عن الملكوت وقال ابن جريج سأصرفهم عن أن يتفكروا فيها ويعتبروا بها ولذلك قال المسيح عليه السلام إن الزرع ينبت في السهل ولا ينبت على الصفا كذلك الحكمة تعمل في قلب المتواضع ولا تعمل في قلب المتكبر أل
16:22.english: When this [pride] appears upon the bodily limbs, it is called "behaving arrogantly" (takabbur); and when it does not appear [outwardly], it is said that in his soul there is pride (kibr). The root [of the matter] is the moral trait (khuluq) that resides in the soul — namely, the soul's taking comfort and repose in seeing itself as above the one over whom it acts proudly. For pride necessarily requires an object over whom one is proud and a quality by virtue of which one is proud; and by this [requirement], pride is distinguished from self-conceit ('ujb), as will come later. For self-conceit does not require an object other than the self-conceited one. Indeed, were a human being created alone, it is conceivable that he would be self-conceited, but it is not conceivable that he would be proud except when there is another alongside him, and he sees himself as above that other in the attributes of perfection. Only at that point does he become proud. Nor is it sufficient that he deem himself great in order to be proud — for a man may deem himself great yet see another as greater than himself or equal to himself, and so he does not act proudly toward him. Nor is it sufficient that he hold another in contempt — for even so, if he saw himself as more contemptible [than that other], he would not be proud; and if he saw the other as his equal, he would not be proud. Rather, he must assign to himself a rank and to the other a rank, then see his own rank as above the other's rank. Upon these three beliefs, the trait of pride comes to be in him. It is not that this perception alone negates pride; rather, this perception and this conviction blow into him [a wind of vanity], and there arises in his heart self-complacency, a thrill, joy, and repose in what he has come to believe, and a sense of vainglory in himself on account of that. That vainglory, that thrill, and that repose in the belief — that is the trait of pride. For this reason, the Prophet — God's peace and blessings be upon him — said: "I seek refuge in You from the puff of pride (nafkhat al-kibriyā')." And the hadith has preceded: "None shall enter Paradise who has in his heart the weight of a mustard seed of pride."
16:22.section_title_en: The Reality of Pride (Kibr) and Its Manifestation in the Soul and Limbs
16:22.anchors:
- Root: كبر (K-B-R)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of bigness, greatness, and seniority in age or rank; al-Farahidi notes its use for physical growth and maturity.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الكبير والصغير من الأسماء المتضايفة" — great and small are relative terms, applied by comparison; in Kalam, pride (kibr) is a state of the soul that esteems itself above another in perfection.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): "كبر الأمر، وخطب كبير" — to be great in magnitude. Metaphorical (Majaz): "كبر عليه" — to find something burdensome or grievous; the moral-spiritual sense of kibr is a metaphorical extension of physical magnitude to the soul's self-assessment.
- Root: نفس (N-F-S)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The self, soul, or spirit; that which animates and is the seat of inner states.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "النفس: الروح" — the soul; also the very essence (al-dhat), as in "ويحذركم الله نفسه" {آل عمران/ 30}, where His "self" is His essence.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "شيء نفيس" — precious thing. Metaphorical: "دفق نفسه أي دمه" — "his self" for "his blood"; here, the soul's inner disposition (khuluq) is the locus where pride takes root before it appears on the limbs.
- Root: وفي (W-F-Y)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Completeness, fulfillment, and reaching full measure.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الوافي: الذي بلغ التمام" — that which attains completion; "أوفى بعهده" — to fulfill one's covenant fully.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "درهم واف" — a full-weight dirham. Metaphorical: "أوفى على المائة" — to exceed a hundred; in this text, the "full measure of a mustard seed" (مثقال ذرة) of pride is the complete, realized quantity that bars one from Paradise.
- Root: خلق (Kh-L-Q)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Measuring, shaping, and fashioning; also innate disposition and moral character.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الخلق أصله: التقدير المستقيم" — its root is right measure and estimation; used for God's origination of things and for the moral constitution of the soul.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "خلق الخراز الأديم" — the leatherworker measures the hide before cutting. Metaphorical: "خلق الله الخلق" — God originated creation upon a measure dictated by wisdom; hence khuluq is the soul's fixed moral form.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction and Focused Predication) — used to delimit the precise definition of kibr as a specific soul-state distinct from 'ujb (self-conceit), and to restrict the cause of exclusion from Paradise to the presence of pride in the heart.

16:128.arabic: الله تعالى المنزل إن الله مع الذين اتقوا والذين هم محسنون قال يحيى بن كثير فنظرنا
16:128.english: Among these manifestations is pride in loving that people stand up for him, or rise before him. ʿAlī — may God honor his face — said: "Whoever wishes to look upon a man of the Fire, let him look at a man seated while people stand before him."
16:128.section_title_en: The Book of Pride and Self-Conceit — Section 862: Manifestations of Pride (Takabbur) in Bearing, Speech, and Conduct, and the Prophetic Model of Humility (Tawāḍuʿ)
16:128.anchors:
- Root: كبر (k-b-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of greatness, magnitude, and elevation in rank or stature; takabbur (تَكَبُّر) is the assumption of greatness over others, the comportment of one who deems himself above his fellow creatures.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-istikbār is the soul's refusal of truth out of disdain for its bearer, and its haughty rejection of what is right; it is the root of every blameworthy trait, for Iblis's fall was his refusal to prostrate out of pride.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): physical height and elevation. Metaphorical (majāz): the heart's self-elevation above others, manifesting in bodily postures — the "ṣaʿar" (turning the cheek away) being its visible sign.
- Root: وضع (w-ḍ-ʿ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To place down low, to lower, to set something down; tawāḍuʿ (تَوَاضُع) is the lowering of oneself, the opposite of elevation and haughtiness.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-tawāḍuʿ is humility before God and His creatures — the soul's recognition of its true station and its refusal to claim what it does not deserve; it is the root of every praiseworthy trait.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical lowering. Metaphorical: the soul's self-abasement in conduct — sitting where one is bid, serving oneself, and accepting invitation from the poor.
- Root: شمل (sh-m-l)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To encompass, to include all parts; shamāʾil (شَمَائِل) are the innate dispositions and outward traits that encompass a man's character.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The outward marks and habitual bearing through which inner moral states become visible to observers.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Used here in its literal sense of comprehensive outward features — the face, gait, voice, and gestures that betray the inner state.
- Root: بذذ (b-dh-dh)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Al-badhādha (البَذَاذَة) is the roughness and plainness of dress and appearance, the state of one who does not adorn himself.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In the prophetic tradition {البَذَاذَةُ مِنَ الإِيمَانِ}, it signifies the believer's indifference to worldly finery — a mean and unadorned appearance that reflects the heart's detachment.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: shabbiness of garment. Metaphorical: the soul's refusal to seek honor through dress, distinguishing genuine humility from affected squalor.

17:37.arabic: أما سمعت قول الله تعالى {ولا تمش في الأرض مرحا إنك لن تخرق الأرض ولن تبلغ الجبال طولا} ومر بالحسن شاب عليه بزة له حسنة فدعاه فقال له ابن آدم معجب بشبابه محب لشمائله كأن القبر قد وارى بدنك وكأنك قد لاقيت عملك ويحك داو قلبك فإن حاجة الله إلى العباد صلاح قلوبهم وروى أن عمر ابن عبد العزيز حج قبل أن يستخلف فنظر إليه طاوس وهو يختال في مشيته فغمز جنبه بأصبعه ثم قال ليست هذه مشية من في بطنه خراء فقال عمر كالمعتذر يا عم لقد ضرب كل عضو مني على هذه المشية حتى تعلمتها ورأى محمد بن واسع ولده يختال فدعاه وقال أتدري من أنت أما أمك فأشت
17:37.english: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Allah does not look at a man who drags his lower garment out of vainglory (baṭaran)." (1) Hadith: "While a man was strutting proudly in his two striped garments, admiring himself..." — agreed upon (muttafaq ʿalayh), from the narration of Abū Hurayrah.

  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-Ikhtiyāl is the display of self-importance in carriage, a blameworthy trait opposed to humility (tawāḍuʿ); it is a spiritual sickness of the heart manifesting in the limbs.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) — the physical strut; Metaphorical (majāz) — the inner state of arrogance that the gait reveals, as the Prophet said: "Walking is the display of the heart's condition."
- Root: ج ر ر (Jim-Ra-Ra)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To drag or trail along the ground; dragging the garment (jarr al-izār) was a pre-Islamic mark of boastful pride.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The prohibition targets not the garment itself but the intention (niyyah) of self-glorification; the act becomes sin when coupled with khuylā' (vainglory).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — trailing cloth; Metaphorical — the heart's dragging toward worldly esteem.
- Root: م ش ي (Meem-Shin-Ya)
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-Mashy is intentional locomotion; al-mayṭīṭā' is a specific censured gait of arrogant swaying, condemned in hadith.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — walking; Metaphorical — al-tamashī fī al-arḍ (strutting) as the bodily sign of inner pride.
- Sibawayh Rule: Bāb al-Faṣl bayna al-Jār wa al-Majrūr (Prepositional Interposition) — The conditional clauses and parenthetical warnings (e.g., "لا ينظر الله إلى...") are structured to allow rhetorical emphasis through fronting, preserving the threat's gravity.

18:34.arabic: وإليه الإشارة بقوله تعالى {فقال لصاحبه وهو يحاوره أنا أكثر منك مالا وأعز نفرا} حتى أجابه فقال إن ترن أنا أقل منك مالا وولدا فعسى ربي أن يؤتيني خيرا من جنتك ويرسل عليها حسبانا من السماء فتصبح صعيدا زلقا أو يصبح ماؤها غورا فلن تستطيع له طلبا وكان ذلك منه تكبرا بالمال والولد ثم بين الله عاقبة أمره بقوله {يا ليتني لم أشرك بربي أحدا} ومن ذلك تكبر قارون إذ قال تعالى إخبارا عن تكبره {فخرج على قومه في زينته قال الذين يريدون الحياة الدنيا يا ليت لنا مثل ما أوتي قارون إنه لذو حظ عظيم} السادس الكبر بالقوة وشدة البطش والتكبر ب
18:34.english: All of this is the very character of pride (أخلاق الكبر) and its effects, which self-exaltation through knowledge and action (التعزز بالعلم والعمل) produces. And where is the one who is free of all of that, or even of some of it? Would that I knew! Who is it that has recognized these traits within himself, and has heard the saying of the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him: "None shall enter Paradise who has in his heart the weight of a grain of mustard-seed of pride" {«لا يدخل الجنة من في قلبه مثقال حبة من خردل من كبر»} — a hadith already cited earlier — how then can he magnify himself and behave arrogantly toward others, while the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, declares him to be among the people of the Fire? Rather, the truly great (العظيم) is only the one who is free of this; and whoever is free of it has in him no self-magnification and no arrogance. And the learned man (العالم) is the one who understands that God, Exalted is He, has said to him: "You have with Us a standing, so long as you do not see for yourself any standing; for if you see for yourself a standing, then you have no standing with Us."
18:34.section_title_en: The Fruits of Pride in Knowledge and Lineage — Section 860 of the Revival of the Religious Sciences
18:34.anchors:
- Root: كبر (K-B-R)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root denotes magnitude, size, and seniority — whether in age, rank, or physical dimension; "الكبرة" is the burden of advanced age.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الكبير والصغير من الأسماء المتضايفة" — great and small are relative terms, assessed by comparison; pride (الكبر) is the soul's self-magnification vis-à-vis another, a theological vice when it entails disdain for God's creatures.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): "كبر الأمر" — the matter became grave. Metaphorical (Majaz): "كبر عليه" — it weighed heavily upon him; here, the physical sense of "bigness" is transferred to the moral-spiritual state of self-inflation (التعاظم) against others.
- Root: حدث (H-D-TH)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Denotes newness, origination after non-existence; "الحديث" is speech that is newly articulated or conveyed.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الحدوث: كون الشيء بعد أن لم يكن" — origination of a thing after it was not; the "حديث" (Prophetic report) is so named as newly transmitted discourse bearing authority.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "حدث من الأحداث" — a youth among youths. Metaphorical: "صاروا أحاديث" — they became the talk of the town; here, the scholar's memorization of hadiths (ألفاظها وأسانيدها) is a means of self-aggrandizement, perverting the transmitted word into an instrument of rivalry.
- Root: نفس (N-F-S)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The self, soul, or spirit; that which breathes and animates; also blood (نفس سائلة) as the seat of life.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "النفس: الروح" — the soul is the spirit; in "ويحذركم الله نفسه" (آل عمران/30), His "Self" is His very Essence (ذاته), showing that self-regard (رؤية النفس قدرًا) is a subtle disease of the innermost reality.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "شيء نفيس" — a precious thing. Metaphorical: "أصابته نفس" — the evil eye struck him; the proud man's gaze upon his own rank is a form of self-inflicted blindness, extinguishing the light of insight (نور البصيرة).
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — The Prophet's words "إنما العظيم من خلا عن هذا" restrict greatness exclusively to the one free of pride, negating it for all others; likewise "ليس لابن البيضاء على ابن السوداء فضل" employs negation (ليس) to nullify any pretension of superiority by lineage, a syntactic structure of absolute denial.

  * Lisan / Ayn: The self, soul, or spirit; that which breathes and animates; also blood (نفس سائلة) as the seat of life.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "النفس: الروح" — the soul is the spirit; in "ويحذركم الله نفسه" (آل عمران/30), His "Self" is His very Essence (ذاته), showing that self-regard (رؤية النفس قدرًا) is a subtle disease of the innermost reality.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "شيء نفيس" — a precious thing. Metaphorical: "أصابته نفس" — the evil eye struck him; the proud man's gaze upon his own rank is a form of self-inflicted blindness, extinguishing the light of insight (نور البصيرة).
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — The Prophet's words "إنما العظيم من خلا عن هذا" restrict greatness exclusively to the one free of pride, negating it for all others; likewise "ليس لابن البيضاء على ابن السوداء فضل" employs negation (ليس) to nullify any pretension of superiority by lineage, a syntactic structure of absolute denial.
18:42.topic: Al-Ghazali on purifying the character, moral diseases, and spiritual remedies, from 'Condemnation of Pride and Conceit'

19:69.arabic: عتيا على الله تعالى فقال ثم لننزعن من كل شيعة أيهم أشد على الرحمن عتيا وقال تعالى فالذين لا يؤمنون بالآخرة قلوبهم منكرة وهم مستكبرون وقال عز وجل يقول الذين استضعفوا للذين استكبروا لولا أنتم لكنا مؤمنين وقال تعالى إن الذين يستكبرون عن عبادتي سيدخلون جهنم داخرين وقال تعالى سأصرف عن آياتي الذين يتكبرون في الأرض بغير الحق قيل في التفسير سأرفع فهم القرآن عن قلوبهم وفي بعض التفاسير سأحجب قلوبهم عن الملكوت وقال ابن جريج سأصرفهم عن أن يتفكروا فيها ويعتبروا بها ولذلك قال المسيح عليه السلام إن الزرع ينبت في السهل ولا ينبت على الص
19:69.english: When this [pride] appears upon the bodily limbs, it is called "behaving arrogantly" (takabbur); and when it does not appear [outwardly], it is said that in his soul there is pride (kibr). The root [of the matter] is the moral trait (khuluq) that resides in the soul — namely, the soul's taking comfort and repose in seeing itself as above the one over whom it acts proudly. For pride necessarily requires an object over whom one is proud and a quality by virtue of which one is proud; and by this [requirement], pride is distinguished from self-conceit ('ujb), as will come later. For self-conceit does not require an object other than the self-conceited one. Indeed, were a human being created alone, it is conceivable that he would be self-conceited, but it is not conceivable that he would be proud except when there is another alongside him, and he sees himself as above that other in the attributes of perfection. Only at that point does he become proud. Nor is it sufficient that he deem himself great in order to be proud — for a man may deem himself great yet see another as greater than himself or equal to himself, and so he does not act proudly toward him. Nor is it sufficient that he hold another in contempt — for even so, if he saw himself as more contemptible [than that other], he would not be proud; and if he saw the other as his equal, he would not be proud. Rather, he must assign to himself a rank and to the other a rank, then see his own rank as above the other's rank. Upon these three beliefs, the trait of pride comes to be in him. It is not that this perception alone negates pride; rather, this perception and this conviction blow into him [a wind of vanity], and there arises in his heart self-complacency, a thrill, joy, and repose in what he has come to believe, and a sense of vainglory in himself on account of that. That vainglory, that thrill, and that repose in the belief — that is the trait of pride. For this reason, the Prophet — God's peace and blessings be upon him — said: "I seek refuge in You from the puff of pride (nafkhat al-kibriyā')." And the hadith has preceded: "None shall enter Paradise who has in his heart the weight of a mustard seed of pride."
19:69.section_title_en: The Reality of Pride (Kibr) and Its Manifestation in the Soul and Limbs
19:69.anchors:
- Root: كبر (K-B-R)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of bigness, greatness, and seniority in age or rank; al-Farahidi notes its use for physical growth and maturity.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الكبير والصغير من الأسماء المتضايفة" — great and small are relative terms, applied by comparison; in Kalam, pride (kibr) is a state of the soul that esteems itself above another in perfection.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): "كبر الأمر، وخطب كبير" — to be great in magnitude. Metaphorical (Majaz): "كبر عليه" — to find something burdensome or grievous; the moral-spiritual sense of kibr is a metaphorical extension of physical magnitude to the soul's self-assessment.
- Root: نفس (N-F-S)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The self, soul, or spirit; that which animates and is the seat of inner states.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "النفس: الروح" — the soul; also the very essence (al-dhat), as in "ويحذركم الله نفسه" {آل عمران/ 30}, where His "self" is His essence.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "شيء نفيس" — precious thing. Metaphorical: "دفق نفسه أي دمه" — "his self" for "his blood"; here, the soul's inner disposition (khuluq) is the locus where pride takes root before it appears on the limbs.
- Root: وفي (W-F-Y)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Completeness, fulfillment, and reaching full measure.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الوافي: الذي بلغ التمام" — that which attains completion; "أوفى بعهده" — to fulfill one's covenant fully.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "درهم واف" — a full-weight dirham. Metaphorical: "أوفى على المائة" — to exceed a hundred; in this text, the "full measure of a mustard seed" (مثقال ذرة) of pride is the complete, realized quantity that bars one from Paradise.
- Root: خلق (Kh-L-Q)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Measuring, shaping, and fashioning; also innate disposition and moral character.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الخلق أصله: التقدير المستقيم" — its root is right measure and estimation; used for God's origination of things and for the moral constitution of the soul.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "خلق الخراز الأديم" — the leatherworker measures the hide before cutting. Metaphorical: "خلق الله الخلق" — God originated creation upon a measure dictated by wisdom; hence khuluq is the soul's fixed moral form.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction and Focused Predication) — used to delimit the precise definition of kibr as a specific soul-state distinct from 'ujb (self-conceit), and to restrict the cause of exclusion from Paradise to the presence of pride in the heart.

21:28.arabic: وعنه العبارة بقوله تعالى {ولا يشفعون إلا لمن ارتضى} وبقوله {من ذا الذي يشفع عنده إلا بإذنه} وبقوله {ولا تنفع الشفاعة عنده إلا لمن أذن له} وبقوله {فما تنفعهم شفاعة الشافعين} وإذا انقسمت الذنوب إلا ما يشفع فيه وإلا ما لا يشفع فيه وجب الخوف والإشفاق لا محالة ولو كان ذنب تقبل فيه الشفاعة لما أمر قريشا بالطاعة ولما نهى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فاطمة رضي الله عنها عن المعصية ولكان يأذن لها في اتباع الشهوات لتكمل لذاتها في الدنيا ثم يشفع لها في الآخرة لتكمل لذاتها في الآخرة فالانهماك في الذنوب وترك ا
21:28.english: If you say: "He, peace and blessings be upon him, said after his words to Fāṭimah and Ṣafiyyah: 'I cannot avail you against God in anything, except that you have a tie of kinship which I will moisten with its moisture'" — a ḥadīth [reported as]: "Do you hope for my intercession, while the Banū ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib do not hope for it?" — narrated by al-Ṭabarānī in al-Awsaṭ from the narration of ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jaʿfar, and in it is Uṣayrim ibn Ḥawshab from Isḥāq ibn Wāṣil, and both are extremely weak — so that indicates that he will single out his relatives for intercession.
21:28.section_title_en: Section 882 — On the Limits of Intercession, the Vices of Pride in Lineage, Numbers, Wealth, and Opinion, and Their Treatment
21:28.anchors:
- Root: شفع (Sh-F-')
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning is pairing or joining; intercession (shafā'ah) is the joining of one's plea to another's cause.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Intercession is the seeking of benefit for another; its acceptance is contingent upon divine permission and good pleasure, as restricted by the Qur'anic qualifiers.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (haqīqah) is the act of making a number even (from watr, odd); metaphorical (majāz) is the mediator's plea before authority.
- Root: عجب (ʿ-J-B)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Astonishment arising from an unknown cause; self-admiration (ʿujb) is a blameworthy state of being pleased with oneself.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "العجب والتعجب: حالة تعرض للإنسان عند الجهل بسبب الشيء" — a state that overtakes a person due to ignorance of the cause; hence, it is impossible regarding God.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: a wondrous thing; metaphorical: the one who performs marvels (taʿjābah). Self-admiration is the root of every error and innovation.
- Root: رأي (R-'-Y)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Opinion, view, or judgment formed through reflection.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Ra'y is the considered opinion that may err or hit the mark; it is blameworthy when it becomes an object of ʿujb (self-admiration).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: sight/vision; metaphorical: intellectual insight. The ḥadīth "إعجاب كل ذي رأي برأيه" (the admiration of every man of opinion for his own view) is cited as a sign of the age's corruption.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد (Restriction and Qualification) — The conditional clauses (in-sharṭ) governing intercession, e.g., {إلا لمن ارتضى} and {إلا بإذنه}, impose necessary restrictions that negate any absolute reliance on intercession.
21:28.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Condemnation of Pride and Conceit'

21:28.arabic: يسبحون الليل والنهار لا يفترون وهم من خشيته مشفقون فمتى زال الإشفاق والحذر مما سبق به القضاء في الأزل وينكشف عند خاتمة الأجل غلب الأمن من مكر الله وذلك يوجب الكبر وهو سبب الهلاك فالكبر دليل الأمن والأمن مهلك والتواضع دليل الخوف وهو مسعد فإذن ما يفسده العابد بإضمار الكبر واحتقار الخلق والنظر إليهم بعين الاستصغار أكثر مما يصلحه بظاهر الأعمال فهذه معارف بها يزال داء الكبر عن القلب لا غير إلا أن النفس بعد هذه المعرفة قد تضمر التواضع وتدعي البراءة من الكبر وهي كاذبة فإذا وقعت الواقعة عادت إلى طبع
21:28.english: ...so he gave some of it in charity and fed his family with some of it. He then returned, saying: "This is good, but it is not like devoting oneself entirely to obedience of God." He came again in a dream a second time, and it was said to him: "Go to so-and-so, the cobbler, and say to him: 'What is this yellowness on your face?'" So he went to him and asked him. He replied: "I have not seen anyone among mankind except that it occurred to me that he would be saved — but you, I [saw] that you would perish." The worshiper said: "By this [very sign]..."
21:28.section_title_en: The Cure for Conceit (Kibr): Trials of the Soul and the Path to Humility
21:28.anchors:
- Root: وجل (wajila)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of fear, trepidation, and trembling of the heart.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance of reverential awe before divine majesty, distinct from mere terror; it is the state of the heart that accompanies acts of obedience when mindful of their acceptance.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah) usage denotes inward trembling; metaphorical (Majaz) extension applies to the soul's anxious state regarding its ultimate destiny.
- Root: شفق (shafaqa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The thin, delicate edge of twilight; also compassion mixed with fear.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الإشفاق: عناية مختلطة بخوف" — solicitous care blended with fear; when followed by (من) the sense of fear predominates, as in the cited verses.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal root refers to the redness of dusk; metaphorical usage denotes the soul's anxious solicitude, as in "مشفقون" (those who are apprehensive).
- Root: كبر (kabira)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of greatness, magnitude, and seniority.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الكبير والصغير من الأسماء المتضايفة" — relative terms; in moral theology, kibr (conceit) is the soul's self-inflation before others and before God.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah) denotes physical or quantitative greatness; metaphorical (Majaz) usage — "كبر علي ذلك" (it weighed heavily upon him) — extends to the heart's refusal to submit to truth, which is the essence of blameworthy pride.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — The particle "إنما" restricts and confines the predicate, as in "فإذن ما يفسده العابد..." where the structure emphasizes that the corruption caused by hidden pride exceeds any apparent rectification.
21:28.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Condemnation of Pride and Conceit'

22:70.arabic: وبيان ذلك في كتاب البيع والسلم والإجارة والحوالة والضمان والقراض والشركة والمساقاة والشفعة والصلح والخلع والكتابة والصداق وسائر المعاوضات الخامس ما يؤخذ عن رضا من غير عوض وهو حلال إذا روعي فيه شرط المعقود عليه وشرط العاقدين وشرط العقد ولم يؤد إلى ضرر بوارث أو غيره وذلك مذكور في كتاب الهبات والوصايا والصدقات السادس ما يحصل بغير اختيار كالميراث وهو حلال إذا كان الموروث قد اكتسب المال من بعض الجهات الخمس على وجه حلال ثم كان ذلك بعد قضاء الدين وتنفيذ الوصايا
22:70.english: These, then, are the comprehensive gateways of the lawful and the unlawful. We have gestured toward their totality so that the seeker may know that if his sustenance is scattered, coming not from a single specified source, then he is not free from need of knowledge of these matters. For everything he eats from any of these categories, he ought to seek a formal legal opinion (istiftāʾ) from the people of knowledge, and not proceed upon it in ignorance (jahl). For just as it is said to the scholar, "Why did you contravene your knowledge?" so too is it said to the ignorant one, "Why did you cling to your ignorance and not learn, after it was proclaimed to you that seeking [knowledge] is an obligation (farīḍah) upon every Muslim?"
22:70.section_title_en: The Book on the Divisions of Alms, Endowments, and Maintenance — The Five Categories of Acquisition
22:70.anchors:
- Root: فرق (farraqa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Separation, division, distinguishing between things; al-furqān is that which distinguishes truth from falsehood.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-farq is the separation of one thing from another, and al-furqān is the criterion by which truth is distinguished from falsehood — hence the Qur'an is called al-Furqān.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: dividing and separating. Metaphorical: "وقفته على مفارق الحديث" — I made him stand upon the clear aspects of the matter.
- Root: صدق (ṣadaqa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Truthfulness in speech and action; al-ṣadaqah is that which is given seeking reward from Allah, verifying one's faith.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-ṣidq is primarily in speech, whether past or future, and by extension in action — a man is ṣādiq al-ḥamlah (truthful in attack) when his action matches his intent.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: truthfulness in speech. Metaphorical: "رجل صادق الحملة" — a man whose attack is sincere and effective.
- Root: وقف (waqafa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Standing still, halting; al-waqf is the endowment of property for charitable purposes, withholding it from circulation.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Waqaftu al-qawm — I made them stand. From this is derived the endowment of a house (waqf al-dār): restraining it from being sold or inherited.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: standing. Metaphorical: "وقفت الأرض على ولدي" — I endowed the land upon my children, restraining it from transfer.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The governing rule permits separation between the operative word and its object where clarity is maintained, as in the periodic structure of enumerating conditions before their governing verb.
22:70.topic: Al-Ghazali on purifying the character, moral diseases, and spiritual remedies, from 'Condemnation of Pride and Conceit'

23:53.arabic: وبذلك هلكت الأمم السالفة إذ افترقت فرقا فكل معجب برأيه وكل حزب بما لديهم فرحون وجميع أهل البدع والضلال إنما أصروا عليها لعجبهم بآرائهم والعجب بالبدعة هو استحسان ما يسوق إليه الهوى والشهوة مع ظن كونه حقا وعلاج هذا العجب أشد من علاج غيره لأن صاحب الرأي الخطأ جاهل بخطئه ولو عرفه لتركه ولا يعالج الداء الذي لا يعرف والجهل داء لا يعرف فتعسر مداواته جدا لأن العارف يقدر على أن يبين للجاهل جهله ويزيله عنه إلا إذا كان معجبا برأيه وجهله فإنه لا يصغي إلى العارف ويتهمه فقد سلط الله عله بلية تهلكه وهو يظنها نعمة فكيف يمك

23:57.arabic: وقال تعالى {إن الذين هم من خشية ربهم مشفقون} وقال تعالى {إنا كنا قبل في أهلنا مشفقين} وقد وصف الله تعالى الملائكة عليهم السلام مع تقدسهم عن الذنوب ومواظبتهم على العبادات على الدءوب بالإشفاق فقال تعالى مخبرا عنهم يسبحون الليل والنهار لا يفترون وهم من خشيته مشفقون فمتى زال الإشفاق والحذر مما سبق به القضاء في الأزل وينكشف عند خاتمة الأجل غلب الأمن من مكر الله وذلك يوجب الكبر وهو سبب الهلاك فالكبر دليل الأمن والأمن مهلك والتواضع دليل الخوف وهو مسعد فإذن ما يفسده العابد بإضمار الكبر واحتقار ال

  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah) denotes physical or quantitative greatness; metaphorical (Majaz) usage — "كبر علي ذلك" (it weighed heavily upon him) — extends to the heart's refusal to submit to truth, which is the essence of blameworthy pride.

25:21.arabic: تعالى {إنه لا يحب المستكبرين} وقال تعالى {لقد استكبروا في أنفسهم وعتوا عتوا كبيرا} وقال تعالى {إن الذين يستكبرون عن عبادتي سيدخلون جهنم داخرين} وذم الكبر في القرآن كثير وقد قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لا يدخل الجنة من كان في قلبه مثقال حبة من خردل من كبر ولا يدخل الجنة من كان في قلبه مثقال حبة من خردل من إيمان (1) حديث أبي هريرة يقول الله تعالى الكبرياء ردائي والعظمة إزاري فمن نازعني واحدا منهما ألقيته في جهنم أخرجه مسلم وأبو داود وابن ماجه واللفظ له وقال أبو داود قذفته في النار وقال مسلم عذبته وقال رداؤه وإزا
25:21.english: To proceed: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said — God, exalted be He, said: "Pride (al-kibriyāʾ) is My cloak, and greatness (al-ʿaẓamah) is My wrapper; whoever contends with Me over either of them, I crush him." {«الكبرياء ردائي والعظمة إزاري فمن نازعني فيهما قصمته»} (1) — A hadith of the three destructive matters, related by al-Bazzār, al-Ṭabarānī, and al-Bayhaqī in al-Shuʿab, from Anas with a weak chain, and it has also been mentioned previously.
25:21.section_title_en: The Book of Condemnation of Pride and Self-Admiration — Being the Ninth Book of the Quarter of Destructive Matters from The Revival of the Religious Sciences
25:21.anchors:
- Root: كبر (k-b-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root denotes magnitude, whether physical size, age, or rank; "al-kibriyā'" is the supreme majesty exclusive to God.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "al-kabīr wa al-ṣaghīr" are relative terms; used for quantity, quality, and dignity. "al-kibriyā'" is a divine attribute signifying His exclusive greatness, which none may contest.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): "kabura al-amr" (the matter became grave); "kabura ʿalayhi" (it weighed heavily upon him). Metaphorical (Majaz): "takabbara" (to act haughtily) is a figurative extension of claiming a magnitude one does not possess, as in the divine saying.
- Root: عجب (ʿ-j-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Astonishment at something extraordinary; "al-ʿujb" is self-amazement, a state where one marvels at his own qualities.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Astonishment arises from ignorance of the true cause; self-admiration (ʿujb) blinds one to one's own defects and to the divine origin of all good.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "ʿajiba minhu" (he marveled at it). Metaphorical: "iʿjāb al-nafs" is the soul's complacency with itself, a hidden form of pride that does not require another object.
- Root: هلك (h-l-k)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Perishing, destruction, ruin; "al-muhlikāt" are the things that cause perdition.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Destruction is of three kinds: loss, corruption, and death. Here it is spiritual perdition — the ruin of the soul's eternal felicity.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical ruin. Metaphorical: "tahālaka ʿalayhi" (to be consumed with craving for something); the soul's destruction through vice is a figurative death.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Apposition and Parenthetical Clauses (al-badal wa al-iʿtirāḍ) — The opening doxology employs extended appositional chains (badal) and parenthetical invocations that delay the main clause, requiring the translator to preserve the periodic structure without collapsing the theological weight of each divine epithet.
25:21.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'Condemnation of Pride and Conceit'

25:21.arabic: مثلكم إنكم إذا لخاسرون وقال الذين لا يرجون لقاءنا لولا أنزل علينا الملائكة أو نرى ربنا لقد استكبروا في أنفسهم وعتوا عتوا كبيرا وقالوا لولا أنزل عليه ملك وقال فرعون فيما أخبر الله عنه {أو جاء معه الملائكة مقترنين} وقال الله تعالى {واستكبر هو وجنوده في الأرض بغير الحق} فتكبر هو على الله وعلى رسله جميعا قال وهب قال له موسى عليه السلام آمن ولك ملكك قال حتى أشاور هامان فشاور هامان فقال هامان بينما أنت رب يعبد إذ صرت عبد تعبد فاسنكف عن عبودية الله وعن اتباع موسى عليه السلام وقالت قريش فيما أخبر الله تعالى عنهم {لولا نزل هذا القرآن على رجل من القريتين عظيم} قال قتاده عظيم
25:21.english: Know that the one against whom pride is directed is either God—mighty and majestic—or His messengers, or the rest of His creation. Man has been created unjust and ignorant {«وخلق الإنسان ظلوما جهولا»}, so at times he grows proud against the creation, and at times he grows proud against the Creator. Thus, pride, considered with respect to the one against whom it is directed, falls into three divisions.
25:21.section_title_en: Exposition of the One Against Whom Pride Is Directed, Its Degrees, Its Divisions, and the Fruits of Pride Within It
25:21.anchors:
- Root: كبر (k-b-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root denotes magnitude, whether physical size, age, or rank; "الكبرة" specifically marks the state of advanced age or an ingrained, chronic condition.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الكبير والصغير من الأسماء المتضايفة" — bigness and smallness are relative terms. In the theological context, pride (الكبر) is the soul's self-magnification against another, a relational vice that distorts the creature's standing before the Creator.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah) usage concerns physical or quantitative magnitude. Metaphorical (Majaz) usage transfers this to moral and spiritual stature, as in "كبر علي ذلك" (it weighed heavily upon him) — here, the soul's swelling against divine command is a metaphorical arrogation of greatness.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Prepositional Interposition (باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور) — Governing the syntactic tension between the agent of pride (المتكبر) and its object (المتكبر عليه), where the preposition "على" carries the full weight of opposition and elevation, structuring the periodic sentences that follow.
25:21.topic: Al-Ghazali on purifying the character, moral diseases, and spiritual remedies, from 'Condemnation of Pride and Conceit'

25:34.arabic: القيامة وقد تعلق الخصماء بهم والملائكة آخذون بنواصيهم يجرونهم على وجوههم إلى جهنم في مظالم العباد لتبرأ إلى الله منهم ولكان انتسابه إلى الكلب والخنزير أحب إليه من الانتساب إليهم فحق أولاد الظلمة إن عصمهم الله من ظلمهم أن يشكروا الله تعال على سلامة دينهم ويستغفروا لآبائهم إن كانوا مسلمين فأما العجب فجهل محض السادس العجب بكثرة العدد من الأولاد والخدم والغلمان والعشيرة والأقارب والأنصار والأتباع كما قال الكفار {نحن أكثر أموالا وأولادا} وكما قال المؤمنون يوم حنين لا نغلب اليوم من قلة وعلاجه ما ذكرناه في الكبر وهو أن ي
25:34.english: If you say: "He, peace and blessings be upon him, said after his words to Fāṭimah and Ṣafiyyah: 'I cannot avail you against God in anything, except that you have a tie of kinship which I will moisten with its moisture'" — a ḥadīth [reported as]: "Do you hope for my intercession, while the Banū ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib do not hope for it?" — narrated by al-Ṭabarānī in al-Awsaṭ from the narration of ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jaʿfar, and in it is Uṣayrim ibn Ḥawshab from Isḥāq ibn Wāṣil, and both are extremely weak — so that indicates that he will single out his relatives for intercession.
25:34.section_title_en: Section 882 — On the Limits of Intercession, the Vices of Pride in Lineage, Numbers, Wealth, and Opinion, and Their Treatment
25:34.anchors:
- Root: شفع (Sh-F-')
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning is pairing or joining; intercession (shafā'ah) is the joining of one's plea to another's cause.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Intercession is the seeking of benefit for another; its acceptance is contingent upon divine permission and good pleasure, as restricted by the Qur'anic qualifiers.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (haqīqah) is the act of making a number even (from watr, odd); metaphorical (majāz) is the mediator's plea before authority.
- Root: عجب (ʿ-J-B)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Astonishment arising from an unknown cause; self-admiration (ʿujb) is a blameworthy state of being pleased with oneself.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "العجب والتعجب: حالة تعرض للإنسان عند الجهل بسبب الشيء" — a state that overtakes a person due to ignorance of the cause; hence, it is impossible regarding God.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: a wondrous thing; metaphorical: the one who performs marvels (taʿjābah). Self-admiration is the root of every error and innovation.
- Root: رأي (R-'-Y)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Opinion, view, or judgment formed through reflection.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Ra'y is the considered opinion that may err or hit the mark; it is blameworthy when it becomes an object of ʿujb (self-admiration).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: sight/vision; metaphorical: intellectual insight. The ḥadīth "إعجاب كل ذي رأي برأيه" (the admiration of every man of opinion for his own view) is cited as a sign of the age's corruption.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد (Restriction and Qualification) — The conditional clauses (in-sharṭ) governing intercession, e.g., {إلا لمن ارتضى} and {إلا بإذنه}, impose necessary restrictions that negate any absolute reliance on intercession.

  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "شيء نفيس ومنفس" — preciousness. Metaphorical: "دفق نفسه أي دمه" — the self as that which must be transcended in spiritual realization
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد (Restriction & Focused Predication) — governing the precise delimitation of spiritual states (أحوال) and their hierarchical gradation (درجات)

26:215.arabic: فالعلم من أعظم ما يتكبر به ولذلك قال تعالى لنبيه صلى الله عليه وسلم واخفض جناحك لمن اتبعك من المؤمنين وقال عز وجل ولو كنت فظا غليظ القلب لانفضوا من حولك ووصف أولياءه فقال أذلة على المؤمنين أعزة على الكافرين وكذلك قال صلى الله عليه وسلم فيما رواه العباس رضي الله عنه يكون قوم يقرءون القرآن لا يجاوز حناجرهم يقولون قد قرأنا القرآن فمن أقرأ منا ومن أعلم منا ثم التفت إلى أصحابه وقال أولئك منكم أيها الأمة أولئك هم
26:215.english: The second aspect by which the vice of pride is magnified is that it calls to opposing Allah the Exalted in His commands. For the arrogant man, when he hears the truth from a servant among the servants of Allah, disdains to accept it and girds himself for its denial. For this reason you see the disputants in matters of religion claiming that they are investigating the secrets of the religion, yet they engage in mutual denial—the denial of the arrogant. Whenever the truth becomes clear upon the tongue of one of them, the other refuses to accept it out of pride, girds himself for its denial, and resorts to every stratagem to repel it by whatever obfuscation he can muster. This is among the moral traits of the disbelievers and the hypocrites, for Allah the Exalted described them, saying: {«وَقَالَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا لَا تَسْمَعُوا لِهَذَا الْقُرْآنِ وَالْغَوْا فِيهِ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَغْلِبُونَ»} (And those who disbelieve said: "Do not listen to this Quran and make noise therein, perhaps you may prevail.") So whoever disputes for the sake of victory and silencing the opponent—not to seize the truth when it appears to him—has shared with them in this moral trait. Likewise, this pride drives one to refuse admonition, as Allah the Exalted said: {«وَإِذَا قِيلَ لَهُ اتَّقِ اللَّهَ أَخَذَتْهُ الْعِزَّةُ بِالْإِثْمِ»} (And when it is said to him, "Fear Allah," pride in sin seizes him.) It is narrated that ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him, recited this verse and then said: {«إِنَّا لِلَّهِ وَإِنَّا إِلَيْهِ رَاجِعُونَ»} (Indeed, we belong to Allah and to Him we return.) A man rose to enjoin good and was killed; then another rose and said: "They kill those who enjoin justice among the people"—and the arrogant one who opposed him and the one who commanded him was killed out of pride.
26:215.section_title_en: The Second Aspect by Which the Vice of Pride (Kibr) Is Magnified: That It Leads to Opposing Allah in His Commands
26:215.anchors:
- Root: كبر (K-B-R)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of bigness, magnitude, and seniority; al-kibr is the internal disposition of self-magnification.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-Kabīr and al-Ṣaghīr are relative terms (mutadāyifān); kibr as a moral vice is the soul's claim to a station above its due, entailing disdain for others.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) usage concerns physical or quantitative magnitude; metaphorical (majāz) usage here denotes arrogance and haughtiness—"كبر عليه" (he disdained it).
- Root: علم (ʿ-L-M)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Knowing a thing's reality; the root also carries the sense of a mark/trace (ʿalam) by which one is guided.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): True knowledge (ʿilm) is apprehension of a thing's essence or judgment about it; the highest form is knowledge of Allah, the self, and the Final End—this engenders fear (khashyah).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: perception and awareness; metaphorical: the "marks" (maʿālim) of religion—the distinguishing signs of guidance.
- Root: نفس (N-F-S)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The self, soul, or spirit; that which is valued and precious.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-Nafs denotes the soul or self; in theological usage it may refer to the essence (dhāt) of a thing.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the soul; metaphorical: self-worth and self-regard—the arrogant man "magnifies his own soul" (istaʿẓama nafsahu).
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — The verse {إِنَّمَا يَخْشَى اللَّهَ مِنْ عِبَادِهِ الْعُلَمَاءُ} restricts true fear of Allah exclusively to the learned, delimiting the predicate to the subject.
26:215.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'Condemnation of Pride and Conceit'

27:14.arabic: {وجحدوا بها واستيقنتها أنفسهم ظلما وعلوا} وهذا الكبر قريب من التكبر على الله عز وجل وإن كان دونه ولكنه تكبر على قبول أمر الله والتواضع لرسوله
27:14.english: Know that the one against whom pride is directed is either God—mighty and majestic—or His messengers, or the rest of His creation. Man has been created unjust and ignorant {«وخلق الإنسان ظلوما جهولا»}, so at times he grows proud against the creation, and at times he grows proud against the Creator. Thus, pride, considered with respect to the one against whom it is directed, falls into three divisions.
27:14.section_title_en: Exposition of the One Against Whom Pride Is Directed, Its Degrees, Its Divisions, and the Fruits of Pride Within It
27:14.anchors:
- Root: كبر (k-b-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root denotes magnitude, whether physical size, age, or rank; "الكبرة" specifically marks the state of advanced age or an ingrained, chronic condition.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الكبير والصغير من الأسماء المتضايفة" — bigness and smallness are relative terms. In the theological context, pride (الكبر) is the soul's self-magnification against another, a relational vice that distorts the creature's standing before the Creator.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah) usage concerns physical or quantitative magnitude. Metaphorical (Majaz) usage transfers this to moral and spiritual stature, as in "كبر علي ذلك" (it weighed heavily upon him) — here, the soul's swelling against divine command is a metaphorical arrogation of greatness.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Prepositional Interposition (باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور) — Governing the syntactic tension between the agent of pride (المتكبر) and its object (المتكبر عليه), where the preposition "على" carries the full weight of opposition and elevation, structuring the periodic sentences that follow.
27:14.topic: Al-Ghazali on purifying the character, moral diseases, and spiritual remedies, from 'Condemnation of Pride and Conceit'

28:39.arabic: تعالى {واستكبر هو وجنوده في الأرض بغير الحق} فتكبر هو على الله وعلى رسله جميعا قال وهب قال له موسى عليه السلام آمن ولك ملكك قال حتى أشاور هامان فشاور هامان فقال هامان بينما أنت رب يعبد إذ صرت عبد تعبد فاسنكف عن عبودية الله وعن اتباع موسى عليه السلام وقالت قريش فيما أخبر الله تعالى عنهم {لولا نزل هذا القرآن على رجل من القريتين عظيم} قال قتاده عظيم القريتين هو الوليد بن المغيرة وأبو مسعود الثقفي طلبوا من هو أعظم رياسة من النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم إذ قالوا غلام يتيم كيف بعثه الله إلينا فقال تعال
