30:32.arabic: وبذلك هلكت الأمم السالفة إذ افترقت فرقا فكل معجب برأيه وكل حزب بما لديهم فرحون وجميع أهل البدع والضلال إنما أصروا عليها لعجبهم بآرائهم والعجب بالبدعة هو استحسان ما يسوق إليه الهوى والشهوة مع ظن كونه حقا وعلاج هذا العجب أشد من علاج غيره لأن صاحب الرأي الخطأ جاهل بخطئه ولو عرفه لتركه ولا يعالج الداء الذي لا يعرف والجهل داء لا يعرف فتعسر مداواته جدا لأن العارف يقدر على أن يبين للجاهل جهله ويزيله عنه إلا إذا كان معجبا برأيه وجهله فإنه لا يصغي إلى العارف ويتهمه فقد سلط الله عله بلية تهلكه وهو يظنها نعمة فكيف يمك
30:32.english: If you say: "He, peace and blessings be upon him, said after his words to Fāṭimah and Ṣafiyyah: 'I cannot avail you against God in anything, except that you have a tie of kinship which I will moisten with its moisture'" — a ḥadīth [reported as]: "Do you hope for my intercession, while the Banū ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib do not hope for it?" — narrated by al-Ṭabarānī in al-Awsaṭ from the narration of ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jaʿfar, and in it is Uṣayrim ibn Ḥawshab from Isḥāq ibn Wāṣil, and both are extremely weak — so that indicates that he will single out his relatives for intercession.
30:32.section_title_en: Section 882 — On the Limits of Intercession, the Vices of Pride in Lineage, Numbers, Wealth, and Opinion, and Their Treatment
30:32.anchors:
- Root: شفع (Sh-F-')
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning is pairing or joining; intercession (shafā'ah) is the joining of one's plea to another's cause.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Intercession is the seeking of benefit for another; its acceptance is contingent upon divine permission and good pleasure, as restricted by the Qur'anic qualifiers.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (haqīqah) is the act of making a number even (from watr, odd); metaphorical (majāz) is the mediator's plea before authority.
- Root: عجب (ʿ-J-B)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Astonishment arising from an unknown cause; self-admiration (ʿujb) is a blameworthy state of being pleased with oneself.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "العجب والتعجب: حالة تعرض للإنسان عند الجهل بسبب الشيء" — a state that overtakes a person due to ignorance of the cause; hence, it is impossible regarding God.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: a wondrous thing; metaphorical: the one who performs marvels (taʿjābah). Self-admiration is the root of every error and innovation.
- Root: رأي (R-'-Y)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Opinion, view, or judgment formed through reflection.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Ra'y is the considered opinion that may err or hit the mark; it is blameworthy when it becomes an object of ʿujb (self-admiration).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: sight/vision; metaphorical: intellectual insight. The ḥadīth "إعجاب كل ذي رأي برأيه" (the admiration of every man of opinion for his own view) is cited as a sign of the age's corruption.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد (Restriction and Qualification) — The conditional clauses (in-sharṭ) governing intercession, e.g., {إلا لمن ارتضى} and {إلا بإذنه}, impose necessary restrictions that negate any absolute reliance on intercession.
30:32.topic: Al-Ghazali on purifying the character, moral diseases, and spiritual remedies, from 'Condemnation of Pride and Conceit'

32:7.arabic: وجده البعيد تراب ذليل وقد عرفه الله تعالى نسبه فقال {الذي أحسن كل شيء خلقه وبدأ خلق الإنسان من طين ثم جعل نسله من سلالة من ماء مهين} فمن أصله التراب المهين الذي يداس بالأقدام ثم خمر طينة حتى صار حمأ مسنونا كيف يتكبر وأخس الأشياء ما إليه انتسابه إذ يقال يا أذل من التراب ويا أنتن من الحمأة ويا أقذر من المضغة فإن كان كونه من أبيه أقرب من كونه من التراب فنقول افتخر بالقريب دون البعيد فالنطفة والمضغة أقرب إليه من الأب فليحقر نفسه بذلك ثم إن كان ذلك يوجب رفعة لقربة فالأب الأعلى من التراب فمن أين رفعته وإذا لم يكن له رفعة فمن أين جاءت الرفعة لولده فإذن أصله من التراب وفصله من النطفة
32:7.english: The second [remedy] is that he should come to know his true lineage, and thus know his father and his grandfather. For his near father is a filthy drop [of semen], and his distant grandfather is abject dust. Indeed, Allah Most High has made known to him his lineage, saying: {«الذي أحسن كل شيء خلقه وبدأ خلق الإنسان من طين ثم جعل نسله من سلالة من ماء مهين»} — "He who perfected everything He created, and began the creation of the human being from clay, then made his progeny from an extract of despicable water" {Quran 32:7-8}. So when his origin is the abject dust that is trodden underfoot, and then his clay was fermented until it became stinking black mud — how can he be arrogant? For the most contemptible of things is that to which his lineage traces back, since it is said: "O you more abject than dust! O you more foul than stinking mud! O you more filthy than a clot of blood [chewed flesh]!"
32:7.section_title_en: The Second Cause of Pride: Pride of Lineage and Its Remedy — Section 866
32:7.anchors:
- Root: نطف (naṭafa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Water that flows and drips; the seminal fluid; pure water.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "النطفة: الماء الصافي، ويعبر بها عن ماء الرجل" — The drop of fluid, clear water, used technically for the male seminal emission; a Quranic term for the origin of human creation.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: pure water, whether little or much. Metaphorical: "ليلة نطوف: مطرت حتى الصباح" — extended to anything flowing; here, the base material of human origin.
- Root: نسب (nasaba)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Lineage, kinship, relation by descent.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "النسب والنسبة: اشتراك من جهة أحد الأبوين" — Participation through one of the two parents; two types: longitudinal (ancestry) and transverse (collateral kinship).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "له نسب في بني فلان" — genealogical connection. Metaphorical: "بين الشيئين مناسبة وتناسب" — proportion and correspondence; here, the true metaphysical lineage of man is contrasted with the false social one.
- Root: مهن (mahana)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To be contemptible, lowly, despicable; weakness and abasement.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Water that is weak and despicable — "ماء مهين" {Quran 32:8}; the seminal fluid described as lowly in the Quranic discourse on human origin.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: despicable, contemptible. Metaphorical: the moral abasement that follows from recognizing one's material origin.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — The rhetorical structure "فإذن أصله من التراب وفصله من النطفة فلا أصل له ولا فصل" uses restrictive predication to annihilate any ground for pride, confining man's origin to dust and a drop.

34:23.arabic: يشفع عنده إلا بإذنه} وبقوله {ولا تنفع الشفاعة عنده إلا لمن أذن له} وبقوله {فما تنفعهم شفاعة الشافعين} وإذا انقسمت الذنوب إلا ما يشفع فيه وإلا ما لا يشفع فيه وجب الخوف والإشفاق لا محالة ولو كان ذنب تقبل فيه الشفاعة لما أمر قريشا بالطاعة ولما نهى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فاطمة رضي الله عنها عن المعصية ولكان يأذن لها في اتباع الشهوات لتكمل لذاتها في الدنيا ثم يشفع لها في الآخرة لتكمل لذاتها في الآخرة فالانهماك في الذنوب وترك التقوى اتكالا على رجاء الشفاعة يضاهي انهماك المريض في شهواته اعتمادا على طبيب حاذق قريب م

34:31.arabic: وجل يقول الذين استضعفوا للذين استكبروا لولا أنتم لكنا مؤمنين وقال تعالى إن الذين يستكبرون عن عبادتي سيدخلون جهنم داخرين وقال تعالى سأصرف عن آياتي الذين يتكبرون في الأرض بغير الحق قيل في التفسير سأرفع فهم القرآن عن قلوبهم وفي بعض التفاسير سأحجب قلوبهم عن الملكوت وقال ابن جريج سأصرفهم عن أن يتفكروا فيها ويعتبروا بها ولذلك قال المسيح عليه السلام إن الزرع ينبت في السهل ولا ينبت على الصفا كذلك الحكمة تعمل في قلب المتواضع ولا تعمل في قلب المتكبر ألا ترون أن من شمخ برأسه إلى السقف شجه ومن طأطأ أظله وأكنه فهذا مثل ضربه
34:31.english: When this [pride] appears upon the bodily limbs, it is called "behaving arrogantly" (takabbur); and when it does not appear [outwardly], it is said that in his soul there is pride (kibr). The root [of the matter] is the moral trait (khuluq) that resides in the soul — namely, the soul's taking comfort and repose in seeing itself as above the one over whom it acts proudly. For pride necessarily requires an object over whom one is proud and a quality by virtue of which one is proud; and by this [requirement], pride is distinguished from self-conceit ('ujb), as will come later. For self-conceit does not require an object other than the self-conceited one. Indeed, were a human being created alone, it is conceivable that he would be self-conceited, but it is not conceivable that he would be proud except when there is another alongside him, and he sees himself as above that other in the attributes of perfection. Only at that point does he become proud. Nor is it sufficient that he deem himself great in order to be proud — for a man may deem himself great yet see another as greater than himself or equal to himself, and so he does not act proudly toward him. Nor is it sufficient that he hold another in contempt — for even so, if he saw himself as more contemptible [than that other], he would not be proud; and if he saw the other as his equal, he would not be proud. Rather, he must assign to himself a rank and to the other a rank, then see his own rank as above the other's rank. Upon these three beliefs, the trait of pride comes to be in him. It is not that this perception alone negates pride; rather, this perception and this conviction blow into him [a wind of vanity], and there arises in his heart self-complacency, a thrill, joy, and repose in what he has come to believe, and a sense of vainglory in himself on account of that. That vainglory, that thrill, and that repose in the belief — that is the trait of pride. For this reason, the Prophet — God's peace and blessings be upon him — said: "I seek refuge in You from the puff of pride (nafkhat al-kibriyā')." And the hadith has preceded: "None shall enter Paradise who has in his heart the weight of a mustard seed of pride."
34:31.section_title_en: The Reality of Pride (Kibr) and Its Manifestation in the Soul and Limbs
34:31.anchors:
- Root: كبر (K-B-R)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of bigness, greatness, and seniority in age or rank; al-Farahidi notes its use for physical growth and maturity.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الكبير والصغير من الأسماء المتضايفة" — great and small are relative terms, applied by comparison; in Kalam, pride (kibr) is a state of the soul that esteems itself above another in perfection.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): "كبر الأمر، وخطب كبير" — to be great in magnitude. Metaphorical (Majaz): "كبر عليه" — to find something burdensome or grievous; the moral-spiritual sense of kibr is a metaphorical extension of physical magnitude to the soul's self-assessment.
- Root: نفس (N-F-S)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The self, soul, or spirit; that which animates and is the seat of inner states.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "النفس: الروح" — the soul; also the very essence (al-dhat), as in "ويحذركم الله نفسه" {آل عمران/ 30}, where His "self" is His essence.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "شيء نفيس" — precious thing. Metaphorical: "دفق نفسه أي دمه" — "his self" for "his blood"; here, the soul's inner disposition (khuluq) is the locus where pride takes root before it appears on the limbs.
- Root: وفي (W-F-Y)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Completeness, fulfillment, and reaching full measure.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الوافي: الذي بلغ التمام" — that which attains completion; "أوفى بعهده" — to fulfill one's covenant fully.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "درهم واف" — a full-weight dirham. Metaphorical: "أوفى على المائة" — to exceed a hundred; in this text, the "full measure of a mustard seed" (مثقال ذرة) of pride is the complete, realized quantity that bars one from Paradise.
- Root: خلق (Kh-L-Q)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Measuring, shaping, and fashioning; also innate disposition and moral character.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الخلق أصله: التقدير المستقيم" — its root is right measure and estimation; used for God's origination of things and for the moral constitution of the soul.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "خلق الخراز الأديم" — the leatherworker measures the hide before cutting. Metaphorical: "خلق الله الخلق" — God originated creation upon a measure dictated by wisdom; hence khuluq is the soul's fixed moral form.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction and Focused Predication) — used to delimit the precise definition of kibr as a specific soul-state distinct from 'ujb (self-conceit), and to restrict the cause of exclusion from Paradise to the presence of pride in the heart.
34:31.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Condemnation of Pride and Conceit'

34:35.arabic: والأنصار والأتباع كما قال الكفار {نحن أكثر أموالا وأولادا} وكما قال المؤمنون يوم حنين لا نغلب اليوم من قلة وعلاجه ما ذكرناه في الكبر وهو أن يتفكر في ضعفه وضعفهم وأن كلهم عبيد عجزة لا يملكون لأنفسهم ضرا ولا نفعا {كم من فئة قليلة غلبت فئة كثيرة بإذن الله} ثم كيف يعجب بهم وأنهم سيفترقون عنه إذا مات فيدفن في قبره ذليلا مهينا وحده لا يرافقه أهل ولا ولد ولا قريب ولا حميم ولا عشير فيسلمونه إلى البلى والحيات والعقارب والديدان ولا يغنون عنه شيئا وفي أحوج أوقاته إليهم وكذلك يهربون منه يوم القيامة {يوم يفر المرء من أخي
34:35.english: If you say: "He, peace and blessings be upon him, said after his words to Fāṭimah and Ṣafiyyah: 'I cannot avail you against God in anything, except that you have a tie of kinship which I will moisten with its moisture'" — a ḥadīth [reported as]: "Do you hope for my intercession, while the Banū ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib do not hope for it?" — narrated by al-Ṭabarānī in al-Awsaṭ from the narration of ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jaʿfar, and in it is Uṣayrim ibn Ḥawshab from Isḥāq ibn Wāṣil, and both are extremely weak — so that indicates that he will single out his relatives for intercession.
34:35.section_title_en: Section 882 — On the Limits of Intercession, the Vices of Pride in Lineage, Numbers, Wealth, and Opinion, and Their Treatment
34:35.anchors:
- Root: شفع (Sh-F-')
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning is pairing or joining; intercession (shafā'ah) is the joining of one's plea to another's cause.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Intercession is the seeking of benefit for another; its acceptance is contingent upon divine permission and good pleasure, as restricted by the Qur'anic qualifiers.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (haqīqah) is the act of making a number even (from watr, odd); metaphorical (majāz) is the mediator's plea before authority.
- Root: عجب (ʿ-J-B)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Astonishment arising from an unknown cause; self-admiration (ʿujb) is a blameworthy state of being pleased with oneself.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "العجب والتعجب: حالة تعرض للإنسان عند الجهل بسبب الشيء" — a state that overtakes a person due to ignorance of the cause; hence, it is impossible regarding God.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: a wondrous thing; metaphorical: the one who performs marvels (taʿjābah). Self-admiration is the root of every error and innovation.
- Root: رأي (R-'-Y)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Opinion, view, or judgment formed through reflection.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Ra'y is the considered opinion that may err or hit the mark; it is blameworthy when it becomes an object of ʿujb (self-admiration).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: sight/vision; metaphorical: intellectual insight. The ḥadīth "إعجاب كل ذي رأي برأيه" (the admiration of every man of opinion for his own view) is cited as a sign of the age's corruption.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد (Restriction and Qualification) — The conditional clauses (in-sharṭ) governing intercession, e.g., {إلا لمن ارتضى} and {إلا بإذنه}, impose necessary restrictions that negate any absolute reliance on intercession.
34:35.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Condemnation of Pride and Conceit'

38:62.arabic: فقالوا {ما لنا لا نرى رجالا كنا نعدهم من الأشرار} قيل يعنون عمارا وبلالا وصهيبا والمقداد رضي الله عنهم ثم كان منهم من منعه الكبر عن الفكر والمعرفة فجهل كونه صلى الله عليه وسلم محقا ومنهم من عرف ومنعه الكبر عن الاعتراف قال الله تعالى مخبرا عنهم {فلما جاءهم ما عرفوا كفروا به} وقال {وجحدوا بها واستيقنتها أنفسهم ظلما وعلوا} وهذا الكبر قريب من التكبر على الله عز وجل وإن كان دونه ولكنه تكبر على قبول أمر الله والتواضع لرسوله
38:62.english: Know that the one against whom pride is directed is either God—mighty and majestic—or His messengers, or the rest of His creation. Man has been created unjust and ignorant {«وخلق الإنسان ظلوما جهولا»}, so at times he grows proud against the creation, and at times he grows proud against the Creator. Thus, pride, considered with respect to the one against whom it is directed, falls into three divisions.
38:62.section_title_en: Exposition of the One Against Whom Pride Is Directed, Its Degrees, Its Divisions, and the Fruits of Pride Within It
38:62.anchors:
- Root: كبر (k-b-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root denotes magnitude, whether physical size, age, or rank; "الكبرة" specifically marks the state of advanced age or an ingrained, chronic condition.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الكبير والصغير من الأسماء المتضايفة" — bigness and smallness are relative terms. In the theological context, pride (الكبر) is the soul's self-magnification against another, a relational vice that distorts the creature's standing before the Creator.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah) usage concerns physical or quantitative magnitude. Metaphorical (Majaz) usage transfers this to moral and spiritual stature, as in "كبر علي ذلك" (it weighed heavily upon him) — here, the soul's swelling against divine command is a metaphorical arrogation of greatness.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Prepositional Interposition (باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور) — Governing the syntactic tension between the agent of pride (المتكبر) and its object (المتكبر عليه), where the preposition "على" carries the full weight of opposition and elevation, structuring the periodic sentences that follow.
38:62.topic: Al-Ghazali on purifying the character, moral diseases, and spiritual remedies, from 'Condemnation of Pride and Conceit'

40:35.arabic: عن آياتي الذين يتكبرون في الأرض بغير الحق} وقال عز وجل {كذلك يطبع الله على كل قلب متكبر جبار} وقال تعالى {واستفتحوا وخاب كل جبار عنيد} وقال تعالى {إنه لا يحب المستكبرين} وقال تعالى {لقد استكبروا في أنفسهم وعتوا عتوا كبيرا} وقال تعالى {إن الذين يستكبرون عن عبادتي سيدخلون جهنم داخرين} وذم الكبر في القرآن كثير وقد قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لا يدخل الجنة من كان في قلبه مثقال حبة من خردل من كبر ولا يدخل الجنة من كان في قلبه مثقال حبة من خردل من إيمان (1) حديث أبي هريرة يقول الله تعالى الكبرياء ردائي والعظمة إزاري فمن نازعني و
40:35.english: To proceed: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said — God, exalted be He, said: "Pride (al-kibriyāʾ) is My cloak, and greatness (al-ʿaẓamah) is My wrapper; whoever contends with Me over either of them, I crush him." {«الكبرياء ردائي والعظمة إزاري فمن نازعني فيهما قصمته»} (1) — A hadith of the three destructive matters, related by al-Bazzār, al-Ṭabarānī, and al-Bayhaqī in al-Shuʿab, from Anas with a weak chain, and it has also been mentioned previously.
40:35.section_title_en: The Book of Condemnation of Pride and Self-Admiration — Being the Ninth Book of the Quarter of Destructive Matters from The Revival of the Religious Sciences
40:35.anchors:
- Root: كبر (k-b-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root denotes magnitude, whether physical size, age, or rank; "al-kibriyā'" is the supreme majesty exclusive to God.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "al-kabīr wa al-ṣaghīr" are relative terms; used for quantity, quality, and dignity. "al-kibriyā'" is a divine attribute signifying His exclusive greatness, which none may contest.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): "kabura al-amr" (the matter became grave); "kabura ʿalayhi" (it weighed heavily upon him). Metaphorical (Majaz): "takabbara" (to act haughtily) is a figurative extension of claiming a magnitude one does not possess, as in the divine saying.
- Root: عجب (ʿ-j-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Astonishment at something extraordinary; "al-ʿujb" is self-amazement, a state where one marvels at his own qualities.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Astonishment arises from ignorance of the true cause; self-admiration (ʿujb) blinds one to one's own defects and to the divine origin of all good.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "ʿajiba minhu" (he marveled at it). Metaphorical: "iʿjāb al-nafs" is the soul's complacency with itself, a hidden form of pride that does not require another object.
- Root: هلك (h-l-k)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Perishing, destruction, ruin; "al-muhlikāt" are the things that cause perdition.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Destruction is of three kinds: loss, corruption, and death. Here it is spiritual perdition — the ruin of the soul's eternal felicity.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical ruin. Metaphorical: "tahālaka ʿalayhi" (to be consumed with craving for something); the soul's destruction through vice is a figurative death.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Apposition and Parenthetical Clauses (al-badal wa al-iʿtirāḍ) — The opening doxology employs extended appositional chains (badal) and parenthetical invocations that delay the main clause, requiring the translator to preserve the periodic structure without collapsing the theological weight of each divine epithet.
40:35.topic: Al-Ghazali on purifying the character, moral diseases, and spiritual remedies, from 'Condemnation of Pride and Conceit'

41:15.arabic: {من أشد منا قوة} وكما اتكل عوج على قوته وأعجب بها فاقتلع جبلا ليطبقه على عسكر موسى عليه السلام فثقب الله تعالى تلك القطعة من الجبل بنقر هدهد ضعيف المنقار حتى صارت في عنقه وقد يتكل المؤمن أيضا على قوته كما روي عن سليمان عليه السلام أنه قال لأطوفن الليلة على مائة امرأة ولم يقل إن شاء الله تعالى فحرم ما أراد من الولد // حديث قال سليمان لأطوفن الليلة بمائة امرأة
41:15.english:
PageV03P373
...and they forgot the favor of God—Exalted is He—upon them, and said: {«لَا نَغْلِبَ الْيَوْمَ مِنْ قِلَّةٍ»} ["We shall not be overcome today by scarcity"] (Q 26:54 — from the story of Pharaoh's host). The hadith: "There is not one of you whom his deed will save" — the hadith is agreed upon (Muttafaq ʿalayh) from the narration of Abu Hurayrah.
41:15.section_title_en: The Remedy that Uproots the Source of Self-Admiration from the Heart, and the Exposition of the Categories of What One Admires in Himself with the Detailed Cure for Each
41:15.anchors:
- Root: نسي (N-S-Y)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To forget, to abandon; the core sense is the mind's lapse from retaining something previously known.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Forgetfulness (Nisyān) is the soul's neglect of what it has grasped; contrasted with Dhikr (remembrance), it is a moral failing when it concerns divine favors.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): "نسي الشيء" — he forgot it. Metaphorical (Majaz): "نسي نفسه" — he neglected his own soul's welfare, as in the Quranic usage.
- Root: عجب (ʿ-J-B)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Astonishment; a state where the cause of a thing is hidden from the perceiver.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "العجب: حالة تعرض للإنسان عند الجهل بسبب الشيء" — self-admiration (ʿUjb) is a state that overtakes a man due to ignorance of the true cause of his state or action; hence it is impossible for God, the Knower of all.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "قصة عجب" — an astonishing matter. Metaphorical: "أبو العجب: الشعوذي" — the "father of wonders" is the trickster who produces marvels; here, the admirer is deceived by his own act.
- Root: قمع (Q-M-ʿ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To beat down, to suppress, to subdue; to strike something on its head to force it down.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Suppression of a passion or vice at its root, so that it does not sprout again.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "قمعت الشيء" — I beat it down. Metaphorical: "قمع الشهوة" — he crushed the desire, i.e., extinguished its material cause.
- Root: سلب (S-L-B)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To strip away, to divest; to take away a garment or an attribute from someone.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Deprivation of a blessing (Niʿmah) as a divine act of justice or trial; the removal of what was previously granted.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "سلبته ثوبه" — I stripped him of his garment. Metaphorical: "سلب نعمة الله" — God divested him of His favor, i.e., withdrew His grace.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The rule governing the separation of the prepositional phrase from its governed noun, as in "فإذن هذا هو العلاج القامع لمادة العجب من القلب" where the prepositional phrase "من القلب" is postponed for emphasis and rhetorical closure, clarifying the locus of the disease and its cure.
41:15.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'Condemnation of Pride and Conceit'

41:26.arabic: التلبيس وذلك من أخلاق الكافرين والمنافقين إذ وصفهم الله تعالى فقال {وقال الذين كفروا لا تسمعوا لهذا القرآن والغوا فيه لعلكم تغلبون} فكل من يناظر للغلبة والإفحام لا ليغتنم الحق إذا ظفر به فقد شاركهم في هذا الخلق وكذلك يحمل ذلك على الأنفة من قبول الوعظ كما قال تعالى {وإذا قيل له اتق الله أخذته العزة بالإثم} وروي عن عمر رضي الله عنه أنه قرأها فقال {إنا لله وإنا إليه راجعون} قام رجل يأمر بالمعروف فقتل فقام آخر فقال يقتلون الذين يأمرون بالقسط من الناس فقتل المتكبر الذي خالفه والذي أمره كبرا وقال ابن مسعود كفى بالرجل إثما إذا قيل له اتق الله قال عليك نفسك وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم لر
41:26.english: The second aspect by which the vice of pride is magnified is that it calls to opposing Allah the Exalted in His commands. For the arrogant man, when he hears the truth from a servant among the servants of Allah, disdains to accept it and girds himself for its denial. For this reason you see the disputants in matters of religion claiming that they are investigating the secrets of the religion, yet they engage in mutual denial—the denial of the arrogant. Whenever the truth becomes clear upon the tongue of one of them, the other refuses to accept it out of pride, girds himself for its denial, and resorts to every stratagem to repel it by whatever obfuscation he can muster. This is among the moral traits of the disbelievers and the hypocrites, for Allah the Exalted described them, saying: {«وَقَالَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا لَا تَسْمَعُوا لِهَذَا الْقُرْآنِ وَالْغَوْا فِيهِ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَغْلِبُونَ»} (And those who disbelieve said: "Do not listen to this Quran and make noise therein, perhaps you may prevail.") So whoever disputes for the sake of victory and silencing the opponent—not to seize the truth when it appears to him—has shared with them in this moral trait. Likewise, this pride drives one to refuse admonition, as Allah the Exalted said: {«وَإِذَا قِيلَ لَهُ اتَّقِ اللَّهَ أَخَذَتْهُ الْعِزَّةُ بِالْإِثْمِ»} (And when it is said to him, "Fear Allah," pride in sin seizes him.) It is narrated that ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him, recited this verse and then said: {«إِنَّا لِلَّهِ وَإِنَّا إِلَيْهِ رَاجِعُونَ»} (Indeed, we belong to Allah and to Him we return.) A man rose to enjoin good and was killed; then another rose and said: "They kill those who enjoin justice among the people"—and the arrogant one who opposed him and the one who commanded him was killed out of pride.
41:26.section_title_en: The Second Aspect by Which the Vice of Pride (Kibr) Is Magnified: That It Leads to Opposing Allah in His Commands
41:26.anchors:
- Root: كبر (K-B-R)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of bigness, magnitude, and seniority; al-kibr is the internal disposition of self-magnification.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-Kabīr and al-Ṣaghīr are relative terms (mutadāyifān); kibr as a moral vice is the soul's claim to a station above its due, entailing disdain for others.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) usage concerns physical or quantitative magnitude; metaphorical (majāz) usage here denotes arrogance and haughtiness—"كبر عليه" (he disdained it).
- Root: علم (ʿ-L-M)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Knowing a thing's reality; the root also carries the sense of a mark/trace (ʿalam) by which one is guided.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): True knowledge (ʿilm) is apprehension of a thing's essence or judgment about it; the highest form is knowledge of Allah, the self, and the Final End—this engenders fear (khashyah).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: perception and awareness; metaphorical: the "marks" (maʿālim) of religion—the distinguishing signs of guidance.
- Root: نفس (N-F-S)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The self, soul, or spirit; that which is valued and precious.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-Nafs denotes the soul or self; in theological usage it may refer to the essence (dhāt) of a thing.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the soul; metaphorical: self-worth and self-regard—the arrogant man "magnifies his own soul" (istaʿẓama nafsahu).
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — The verse {إِنَّمَا يَخْشَى اللَّهَ مِنْ عِبَادِهِ الْعُلَمَاءُ} restricts true fear of Allah exclusively to the learned, delimiting the predicate to the subject.
41:26.topic: Al-Ghazali on purifying the character, moral diseases, and spiritual remedies, from 'Condemnation of Pride and Conceit'

43:53.arabic: وقال فرعون فيما أخبر الله عنه {أو جاء معه الملائكة مقترنين} وقال الله تعالى {واستكبر هو وجنوده في الأرض بغير الحق} فتكبر هو على الله وعلى رسله جميعا قال وهب قال له موسى عليه السلام آمن ولك ملكك قال حتى أشاور هامان فشاور هامان فقال هامان بينما أنت رب يعبد إذ صرت عبد تعبد فاسنكف عن عبودية الله وعن اتباع موسى عليه السلام وقالت قريش فيما أخبر الله تعالى عنهم {لولا نزل هذا القرآن على رجل من القريتين عظيم} قال قتاده عظيم القريتين هو الوليد بن المغيرة وأبو مسعود الثقفي طلبوا من هو أعظم رياسة من النبي صلى الله عليه وسل
43:53.english: Know that the one against whom pride is directed is either God—mighty and majestic—or His messengers, or the rest of His creation. Man has been created unjust and ignorant {«وخلق الإنسان ظلوما جهولا»}, so at times he grows proud against the creation, and at times he grows proud against the Creator. Thus, pride, considered with respect to the one against whom it is directed, falls into three divisions.
43:53.section_title_en: Exposition of the One Against Whom Pride Is Directed, Its Degrees, Its Divisions, and the Fruits of Pride Within It
43:53.anchors:
- Root: كبر (k-b-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root denotes magnitude, whether physical size, age, or rank; "الكبرة" specifically marks the state of advanced age or an ingrained, chronic condition.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الكبير والصغير من الأسماء المتضايفة" — bigness and smallness are relative terms. In the theological context, pride (الكبر) is the soul's self-magnification against another, a relational vice that distorts the creature's standing before the Creator.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah) usage concerns physical or quantitative magnitude. Metaphorical (Majaz) usage transfers this to moral and spiritual stature, as in "كبر علي ذلك" (it weighed heavily upon him) — here, the soul's swelling against divine command is a metaphorical arrogation of greatness.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Prepositional Interposition (باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور) — Governing the syntactic tension between the agent of pride (المتكبر) and its object (المتكبر عليه), where the preposition "على" carries the full weight of opposition and elevation, structuring the periodic sentences that follow.
43:53.topic: Al-Ghazali on purifying the character, moral diseases, and spiritual remedies, from 'Condemnation of Pride and Conceit'

48:13.arabic: القبائل من لم يؤمن بالله واليوم الآخر وكانوا عند الله شرا من الكلاب وأخس من الخنازير ولذلك قال تعالى {يا أيها الناس إنا خلقناكم من ذكر وأنثى} أي لا تفاوت في أنسابكم لاجتماعكم في أصل واحد ثم ذكر فائدة النسب فقال {وجعلناكم شعوبا وقبائل لتعارفوا} ثم بين أن الشرف بالتقوى لا بالنسب فقال {إن أكرمكم عند الله أتقاكم} ولما قيل لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم من أكرم الناس من أكيس الناس لم يقل من ينتمي إلى نسبي ولكن قال أكرمهم أكثرهم للموت ذكرا وأشدهم له استعدادا (1) حديث إن الله قد أذهب ع
48:13.english: The fourth: pride in noble lineage, like the pride of the Hashimite, to the point that some of them imagine that they will be saved by the nobility of their lineage and the salvation of their forefathers, and that they are forgiven; and some of them fancy that all of creation are their clients and slaves. Its remedy is that he should know that whenever he contradicts his forefathers in their deeds and their moral traits, yet imagines himself to be joined with them, he has indeed been ignorant. And if he emulates his forefathers, then their moral traits were not pride, but rather fear, self-contempt, magnifying others, and self-blame. For they were ennobled by obedience, knowledge, and praiseworthy qualities — not by lineage. So let him seek honor through that by which they were honored. For those who shared their lineage and participated with them in their tribes, yet did not believe in God and the Last Day, were in God's sight worse than dogs and viler than swine. For this reason God (Exalted is He) said: {«يا أيها الناس إنا خلقناكم من ذكر وأنثى»} — "O mankind, indeed We have created you from a male and a female" — that is, there is no disparity in your lineages because you all share a single origin. Then He mentioned the benefit of lineage, saying: {«وجعلناكم شعوبا وقبائل لتعارفوا»} — "And We made you peoples and tribes that you may know one another." Then He clarified that honor is by piety, not by lineage, saying: {«إن أكرمكم عند الله أتقاكم»} — "Indeed, the most noble of you in the sight of God is the most righteous of you." And when it was said to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him), "Who is the most noble of people?" — he did not say, "Whoever traces himself to my lineage," but rather he said, "The most noble of them is the one most mindful of death and the most prepared for it." (1) A hadith: "Indeed, God has removed from you the pride of the Age of Ignorance" — this hadith was transmitted by Abu Dawud and al-Tirmidhi, who deemed it sound (ḥasan), from the narration of Abu Hurayrah; al-Tirmidhi also narrated it from the narration of Ibn ʿUmar and said it is gharīb (uncommon).
48:13.section_title_en: The Book of the Revival of the Religious Sciences — Section 881: On the Wonders of Pride in Strength, Intellect, and Lineage, and Their Remedies
48:13.anchors:
- Root: عقل (ʿaql)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The faculty of restraint and comprehension; the intellect as that which binds one from error.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "العقل يقال للقوة المتهيئة لقبول العلم، ويقال للعلم الذي يستفيده الإنسان بتلك القوة عقل" — the power prepared for receiving knowledge, and the knowledge acquired thereby.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: sound judgment after folly; Metaphorical: "نخلة لا تعقل الإبار" — a palm that does not accept pollination, i.e., lacks receptivity.
- Root: نسب (nasab)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Lineage and kinship through forebears.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "النسب والنسبة: اشتراك من جهة أحد الأبوين" — participation through one of the two parents; two types: vertical (through ancestors) and horizontal (through collaterals).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "فلان حسيب نسيب" — noble in deed and lineage; Metaphorical: "بين الشيئين مناسبة" — proportionality or correspondence between things.
- Root: حدث (ḥadath)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Origination after non-existence; newness.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الحدوث: كون الشيء بعد أن لم يكن" — a thing's coming to be after it was not; "المحدث: ما أوجد بعد أن لم يكن" — the originated.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: recent events; Metaphorical: "كان عمر رضي الله عنه محدثا" — one inspired with true discernment.
- Root: نفس (nafs)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The self, soul, or spirit; that which animates.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "النفس: الروح" — the spirit; also the very essence (dhāt) when attributed to God.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: preciousness; Metaphorical: "دفق نفسه" — poured out his blood, i.e., his life.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Interposition (الفصل بين الجار والمجرور) — governing the permissible separation between a governing word and its governed prepositional phrase, applied here to parse the conditional and relative clauses conveying causal relations between pride and its consequences.

50:26.arabic: الله ولقوله ولا تجعلوا مع الله إلها آخر فمن لم يره في كل شيء فقد رأى غيره وكل ما التفت إليه العبد سوى الله تعالى تضمن التفاته شيئا من الشرك الخفي بل التوحيد الخالص أن لا يرى في كل شيء إلا الله عز وجل العاشر التبري وأعني به أن يتبرأ من حوله وقوته والالتفات إلى نفسه بين الرضا والتزكية فإذا تلا بآيات الوعد والمدح للصالحين فلا يشهد نفسه عند ذلك بل يشهد الموقنين والصديقين فيها ويتشوف إلى أن يلحقه الله عز وجل بهم وإذا تلا آيات المقت وذم العصاة والمقصرين شهد على نفسه هناك وقدر أنه المخا
50:26.english: For this reason, Yūsuf ibn Asbāṭ said: "I intend to recite the Qur'an, but when I recall what is in it, I fear abhorrence (al-maqt), so I turn instead to glorification (al-tasbīḥ) and seeking forgiveness (al-istighfār)."
50:26.section_title_en: ** The Revival of the Religious Sciences — Section 231: On the Inward Conditions of Qur'anic Recitation (Continued)
50:26.anchors:
**
- Root: وجل (w-j-l)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الوجل: استشعار الخوف" — the stirring of fear/apprehension within
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الوجل: استشعار الخوف. يقال: وجل يوجل وجلا، فهو وجل. قال تعالى: {إنما المؤمنون الذين إذا ذكر الله وجلت قلوبهم}" — the theological state of the heart's trembling upon remembrance of God
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): "رجل وجل، وقوم وجال، وقد وجل وجلا" — the physical/emotional state of fear. Metaphorical (Majaz): The heart's trembling as the seat of spiritual perception
- Root: قلب (q-l-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "قلب الشيء: تصريفه وصرفه عن وجه إلى وجه" — turning and transforming
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "قلب الشيء: تصريفه وصرفه عن وجه إلى وجه، كقلب الثوب، وقلب الإنسان" — the heart as that which is constantly turning/transforming between states
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "قلب الشيء قلبا: حوله عن وجهه" — physical turning. Metaphorical: "قلب المعلم الصبيان: صرفهم إلى بيوتهم" — the heart's turning toward or away from spiritual realities
- Root: نفس (n-f-s)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The self, soul, spirit — that which is breathed
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "النفس: الروح" — the soul as the animating principle; also the self as the locus of blameworthy attributes
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "شيء نفيس ومنفس" — preciousness. Metaphorical: "دفق نفسه أي دمه" — the self as that which must be transcended in spiritual realization
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد (Restriction & Focused Predication) — governing the precise delimitation of spiritual states (أحوال) and their hierarchical gradation (درجات)

52:26.arabic: وقال تعالى {إن الذين هم من خشية ربهم مشفقون} وقال تعالى {إنا كنا قبل في أهلنا مشفقين} وقد وصف الله تعالى الملائكة عليهم السلام مع تقدسهم عن الذنوب ومواظبتهم على العبادات على الدءوب بالإشفاق فقال تعالى مخبرا عنهم يسبحون الليل والنهار لا يفترون وهم من خشيته مشفقون فمتى زال الإشفاق والحذر مما سبق به القضاء في الأزل وينكشف عند خاتمة الأجل غلب الأمن من مكر الله وذلك يوجب الكبر وهو سبب الهلاك فالكبر دليل الأمن والأمن مهلك والتواضع دليل الخوف وهو مسعد فإذن ما يفسده العابد بإضمار الكبر واحتقار الخلق والنظر إليهم بعين الاستصغار أكثر مما يص
52:26.english: ...so he gave some of it in charity and fed his family with some of it. He then returned, saying: "This is good, but it is not like devoting oneself entirely to obedience of God." He came again in a dream a second time, and it was said to him: "Go to so-and-so, the cobbler, and say to him: 'What is this yellowness on your face?'" So he went to him and asked him. He replied: "I have not seen anyone among mankind except that it occurred to me that he would be saved — but you, I [saw] that you would perish." The worshiper said: "By this [very sign]..."
52:26.section_title_en: The Cure for Conceit (Kibr): Trials of the Soul and the Path to Humility
52:26.anchors:
- Root: وجل (wajila)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of fear, trepidation, and trembling of the heart.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance of reverential awe before divine majesty, distinct from mere terror; it is the state of the heart that accompanies acts of obedience when mindful of their acceptance.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah) usage denotes inward trembling; metaphorical (Majaz) extension applies to the soul's anxious state regarding its ultimate destiny.
- Root: شفق (shafaqa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The thin, delicate edge of twilight; also compassion mixed with fear.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الإشفاق: عناية مختلطة بخوف" — solicitous care blended with fear; when followed by (من) the sense of fear predominates, as in the cited verses.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal root refers to the redness of dusk; metaphorical usage denotes the soul's anxious solicitude, as in "مشفقون" (those who are apprehensive).
- Root: كبر (kabira)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of greatness, magnitude, and seniority.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الكبير والصغير من الأسماء المتضايفة" — relative terms; in moral theology, kibr (conceit) is the soul's self-inflation before others and before God.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah) denotes physical or quantitative greatness; metaphorical (Majaz) usage — "كبر علي ذلك" (it weighed heavily upon him) — extends to the heart's refusal to submit to truth, which is the essence of blameworthy pride.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — The particle "إنما" restricts and confines the predicate, as in "فإذن ما يفسده العابد..." where the structure emphasizes that the corruption caused by hidden pride exceeds any apparent rectification.
52:26.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Condemnation of Pride and Conceit'

74:48.arabic: وبقوله {فما تنفعهم شفاعة الشافعين} وإذا انقسمت الذنوب إلا ما يشفع فيه وإلا ما لا يشفع فيه وجب الخوف والإشفاق لا محالة ولو كان ذنب تقبل فيه الشفاعة لما أمر قريشا بالطاعة ولما نهى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فاطمة رضي الله عنها عن المعصية ولكان يأذن لها في اتباع الشهوات لتكمل لذاتها في الدنيا ثم يشفع لها في الآخرة لتكمل لذاتها في الآخرة فالانهماك في الذنوب وترك التقوى اتكالا على رجاء الشفاعة يضاهي انهماك المريض في شهواته اعتمادا على طبيب حاذق قريب مشفق من أب أو أخ أو غيره وذل
74:48.english: If you say: "He, peace and blessings be upon him, said after his words to Fāṭimah and Ṣafiyyah: 'I cannot avail you against God in anything, except that you have a tie of kinship which I will moisten with its moisture'" — a ḥadīth [reported as]: "Do you hope for my intercession, while the Banū ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib do not hope for it?" — narrated by al-Ṭabarānī in al-Awsaṭ from the narration of ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jaʿfar, and in it is Uṣayrim ibn Ḥawshab from Isḥāq ibn Wāṣil, and both are extremely weak — so that indicates that he will single out his relatives for intercession.
74:48.section_title_en: Section 882 — On the Limits of Intercession, the Vices of Pride in Lineage, Numbers, Wealth, and Opinion, and Their Treatment
74:48.anchors:
- Root: شفع (Sh-F-')
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning is pairing or joining; intercession (shafā'ah) is the joining of one's plea to another's cause.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Intercession is the seeking of benefit for another; its acceptance is contingent upon divine permission and good pleasure, as restricted by the Qur'anic qualifiers.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (haqīqah) is the act of making a number even (from watr, odd); metaphorical (majāz) is the mediator's plea before authority.
- Root: عجب (ʿ-J-B)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Astonishment arising from an unknown cause; self-admiration (ʿujb) is a blameworthy state of being pleased with oneself.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "العجب والتعجب: حالة تعرض للإنسان عند الجهل بسبب الشيء" — a state that overtakes a person due to ignorance of the cause; hence, it is impossible regarding God.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: a wondrous thing; metaphorical: the one who performs marvels (taʿjābah). Self-admiration is the root of every error and innovation.
- Root: رأي (R-'-Y)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Opinion, view, or judgment formed through reflection.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Ra'y is the considered opinion that may err or hit the mark; it is blameworthy when it becomes an object of ʿujb (self-admiration).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: sight/vision; metaphorical: intellectual insight. The ḥadīth "إعجاب كل ذي رأي برأيه" (the admiration of every man of opinion for his own view) is cited as a sign of the age's corruption.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد (Restriction and Qualification) — The conditional clauses (in-sharṭ) governing intercession, e.g., {إلا لمن ارتضى} and {إلا بإذنه}, impose necessary restrictions that negate any absolute reliance on intercession.
74:48.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Condemnation of Pride and Conceit'

75:39.arabic: عليه فقال {فخلق فسوى فجعل منه الزوجين الذكر والأنثى} ليدوم وجوده بالتناسل كما حصل وجوده أولا بالاختراع فمن كان هذا بدؤه وهذه أحواله فمن أين له البطر والكبرياء والفخر والخيلاء وهو على التحقيق أخس الأخساء وأضعف الضعفاء ولكن هذه عادة الخسيس إذا رفع من خسته شمخ بأنفه وتعظم وذلك لدلالة خسة أوله ولا حول ولا قوة إلا بالله نعم لو أكمله وفوض إليه أمره وأدام له الوجود باختياره لجاز أن يطغى وينسى المبدأ والمنتهى ولكنه سلط عليه في دوام وجوده الأمراض الهائلة والأسقام العظيمة والآفات المختلفة والطباع المتضادة من
75:39.english: As for his end and his final destination — it is death, indicated by the saying of God Most High: {ثم أماته فأقبره ثم إذا شاء أنشره} — "Then He caused him to die and buried him; then, when He wills, He shall raise him." Its meaning is that He strips from him his spirit, his hearing, his sight, his knowledge, his power, his sense, his perception, and his movement — so he returns to being an inert thing (jamād), just as he was the first time, with nothing remaining except the shape of his limbs and his form — no sense in him, no movement. Then he is placed in the earth, and becomes a putrid, filthy carcass, just as he was at first a contemptible drop. Then his limbs decay, his parts crumble, his bones rot, and he becomes dust and fragments; the worm eats his parts — beginning with his two pupils, plucking them out; then his cheeks, cutting them away; then the rest of his parts — until he becomes dung in the bellies of worms, a carcass from which the animal flees, which every man deems filthy and shuns for the intensity of its stench. And the best of his states is that he returns to what he was: he becomes earth, from which jugs are made and from which buildings are made. So he becomes nonexistent after having been existent, and becomes as though he had never flourished yesterday — reaped down — just as he was in his first affair for a long span. And would that he had remained so — how good it would be if he were left as earth!
75:39.section_title_en: On the Baseness of Man's Origin and the Folly of Pride — Section 864 of The Revival of the Religious Sciences
75:39.anchors:
- Root: ض ل ل (ḍ-l-l)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core sense of going astray, being lost, or perishing; also used for being concealed or obliterated.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In theological context, denotes deviation from the straight path (al-ṣirāṭ al-mustaqīm) and the state of being bereft of divine guidance — here, the primordial state of non-existence is framed as utter loss.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) for physical straying; metaphorical (majāz) for spiritual ruin — applied here to the pre-creation void.
- Root: ن ط ف (n-ṭ-f)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Water that flows or drips; a drop; specifically the seminal fluid.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "النطفة: الماء الصافي، ويعبر بها عن ماء الرجل" — pure water, used as a euphemism for male semen; also the pearl (al-luʾluʾah) in its purity, but here contrasted with filth (qadhir).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal for clear water; metaphorical for the base origin of man — the drop is both physically and morally negligible.
- Root: م ل ك (m-l-k)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Possession, dominion, and control; the hand that grasps and holds.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Ownership and sovereign power; in Kalam, distinguishes the Creator's absolute dominion (mulk) from the creature's borrowed, contingent capacity.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal for legal possession; metaphorical for self-mastery — man "does not possess his own heart" (lā yamliku qalbahu), a rhetorical denial of autonomous agency.
- Root: ك ب ر (k-b-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Greatness in size, rank, or dignity; also arrogance (kibr) as its blameworthy derivative.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Grandeur (kibriyāʾ) is exclusively divine; human pride is a usurpation of an attribute that belongs to God alone.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal for physical magnitude; metaphorical for moral haughtiness — the text pivots on this tension.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — The repeated use of "إنما" (only, solely) in the opening lines restricts the cause of man's creation and blessing to a single purpose: self-knowledge and knowledge of God, not self-glorification.

80:21.arabic: قتل الإنسان ما أكفره من أي شيء خلقه من نطفة خلقه فقدره ثم السبيل يسره ثم أماته فأقبره ثم إذا شاء أنشره فقد أشارت الآية إلى أول خلق الإنسان وإلى آخر أمره وإلى وسطه فلينظر الإنسان ذلك ليفهم معنى هذه الآية أما أول الإنسان فهو أنه لم يكن شيئا مذكورا وقد كان في حيز العدم دهورا بل لم يكن لعدمه أول وأي شيء أخس وأقل من المحو والعدم وقد كان كذلك في القدم ثم خلقه الله من أرذل الأشياء ثم من أقذرها إذ قد خلقه من تراب ثم من نطفة ثم من علقة ثم من مضغة ثم جعله عظما ثم كسا العظم لحما فقد كان هذا بداية وجوده حيث كان شيئا مذكورا فما صار شيئا مذكورا إلا وهو ع
80:21.english: As for his knowledge of his Lord, His greatness, and His glory — the discourse thereon is lengthy, and it is the ultimate end of the science of unveiling (ʿilm al-mukāshafah). As for his knowledge of himself, that too is lengthy; but we shall mention therefrom that which benefits in arousing humility and lowliness. And it suffices him to understand the meaning of a single verse in the Book of God — for in the Qurʾān is the knowledge of the first and the last, for him whose inner sight has been opened. God, may He be exalted, has said: {«قُتِلَ الْإِنْسَانُ مَا أَكْفَرَهُ ۝ مِنْ أَيِّ شَيْءٍ خَلَقَهُ ۝ مِنْ نُطْفَةٍ خَلَقَهُ فَقَدَّرَهُ ۝ ثُمَّ السَّبِيلَ يَسَّرَهُ ۝ ثُمَّ أَمَاتَهُ فَأَقْبَرَهُ ۝ ثُمَّ إِذَا شَاءَ أَنْشَرَهُ»} [ʿAbasa: 17–22] — "May man be killed! How ungrateful he is! From what thing did He create him? From a drop of fluid He created him and proportioned him. Then the path He made easy for him. Then He causes him to die and buries him. Then when He wills, He raises him." The verse has pointed to the first origin of man, to the last of his affair, and to his middle state. Let man, then, look upon that, in order to understand the meaning of this verse.
80:21.section_title_en: Exposition of the Character Traits of the Humble and the Sum Total of Wherein the Effect of Humility and Arrogance Appears — and the Exposition of the Method of Treating Arrogance and Acquiring Humility
80:21.anchors:
- Root: تواضع (tawāḍuʿ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Root و-ض-ع: to place down, lower, set in a low position; al-tawāḍuʿ is self-lowering, the voluntary assumption of lowness.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-waḍʿ is placing a thing in a station; tawāḍuʿ is the soul's self-abasement before truth and before the Creator, opposed to takabbur (self-elevation).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Haqīqah: physical lowering of position. Majāz: the soul's humility and abandonment of claims to eminence.
- Root: كبر (kibr)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Root ك-ب-ر: bigness, magnitude; al-kibriyāʾ is exclusive divine majesty; al-kibr (arrogance) is the creature's false claim to that majesty.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-kibr is the soul's self-magnification, a claim to a station of greatness that belongs to God alone; it is the root of all disobedience.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Haqīqah: physical greatness. Majāz: the heart's disdain of others and refusal of truth — the blameworthy kibr.
- Root: نطف (nuṭfah)
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-nuṭfah: pure water, used for the seminal fluid. {«ثُمَّ جَعَلْنَاهُ نُطْفَةً فِي قَرَارٍ مَكِينٍ»} [Al-Muʾminūn: 13].
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Haqīqah: clear water, little or much. Majāz: "laylah naṭūf" — a night raining until morning.
- Root: خلق (khalaqa)
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-khalq: measured estimation (taqdīr mustaqīm); used for bringing forth from nothing without model, and for producing a thing from another thing.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Haqīqah: the tailor's cutting cloth to measure. Majāz: God's origination of creatures upon a measure necessitated by wisdom.
- Sibawayh Rule: Bāb al-ʿaṭf ʿalā al-ḍamīr al-marfūʿ al-muttaṣil (Coordination upon the connected nominative pronoun) — permissible when preceded by an explicit subject, as in "خلقه من نطفة فقدره" where the sequence of verbs coordinates without repetition of the pronoun, each verb governing its own object in ordered succession.

90:8.arabic: ولذلك امتن عليه فقال ألم نجعل له عينين ولسانا وشفتين وهديناه النجدين وعرف خسته أولا فقال {ألم يك نطفة من مني يمنى ثم كان علقة} ثم ذكر منته عليه فقال {فخلق فسوى فجعل منه الزوجين الذكر والأنثى} ليدوم وجوده بالتناسل كما حصل وجوده أولا بالاختراع فمن كان هذا بدؤه وهذه أحواله فمن أين له البطر والكبرياء والفخر والخيلاء وهو على التحقيق أخس الأخساء وأضعف الضعفاء ولكن هذه عادة الخسيس إذا رفع من خسته شمخ بأنفه وتعظم وذلك لدلالة خسة أوله ولا حول ولا قوة إلا بالله نعم لو أكمله وفوض إليه أمره وأدام له الوجود باختياره لجاز أن يطغى وينس
90:8.english: As for his end and his final destination — it is death, indicated by the saying of God Most High: {ثم أماته فأقبره ثم إذا شاء أنشره} — "Then He caused him to die and buried him; then, when He wills, He shall raise him." Its meaning is that He strips from him his spirit, his hearing, his sight, his knowledge, his power, his sense, his perception, and his movement — so he returns to being an inert thing (jamād), just as he was the first time, with nothing remaining except the shape of his limbs and his form — no sense in him, no movement. Then he is placed in the earth, and becomes a putrid, filthy carcass, just as he was at first a contemptible drop. Then his limbs decay, his parts crumble, his bones rot, and he becomes dust and fragments; the worm eats his parts — beginning with his two pupils, plucking them out; then his cheeks, cutting them away; then the rest of his parts — until he becomes dung in the bellies of worms, a carcass from which the animal flees, which every man deems filthy and shuns for the intensity of its stench. And the best of his states is that he returns to what he was: he becomes earth, from which jugs are made and from which buildings are made. So he becomes nonexistent after having been existent, and becomes as though he had never flourished yesterday — reaped down — just as he was in his first affair for a long span. And would that he had remained so — how good it would be if he were left as earth!
90:8.section_title_en: On the Baseness of Man's Origin and the Folly of Pride — Section 864 of The Revival of the Religious Sciences
90:8.anchors:
- Root: ض ل ل (ḍ-l-l)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core sense of going astray, being lost, or perishing; also used for being concealed or obliterated.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In theological context, denotes deviation from the straight path (al-ṣirāṭ al-mustaqīm) and the state of being bereft of divine guidance — here, the primordial state of non-existence is framed as utter loss.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) for physical straying; metaphorical (majāz) for spiritual ruin — applied here to the pre-creation void.
- Root: ن ط ف (n-ṭ-f)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Water that flows or drips; a drop; specifically the seminal fluid.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "النطفة: الماء الصافي، ويعبر بها عن ماء الرجل" — pure water, used as a euphemism for male semen; also the pearl (al-luʾluʾah) in its purity, but here contrasted with filth (qadhir).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal for clear water; metaphorical for the base origin of man — the drop is both physically and morally negligible.
- Root: م ل ك (m-l-k)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Possession, dominion, and control; the hand that grasps and holds.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Ownership and sovereign power; in Kalam, distinguishes the Creator's absolute dominion (mulk) from the creature's borrowed, contingent capacity.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal for legal possession; metaphorical for self-mastery — man "does not possess his own heart" (lā yamliku qalbahu), a rhetorical denial of autonomous agency.
- Root: ك ب ر (k-b-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Greatness in size, rank, or dignity; also arrogance (kibr) as its blameworthy derivative.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Grandeur (kibriyāʾ) is exclusively divine; human pride is a usurpation of an attribute that belongs to God alone.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal for physical magnitude; metaphorical for moral haughtiness — the text pivots on this tension.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — The repeated use of "إنما" (only, solely) in the opening lines restricts the cause of man's creation and blessing to a single purpose: self-knowledge and knowledge of God, not self-glorification.

2:94.arabic: لأحببته وتلا قوله تعالى فتمنوا الموت إن كنتم صادقين فقال الرجل فقد قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لا يتمنينأحدكم الموت (3) فقال إنما قاله لضر نزل به لأن الرضا بقضاء الله تعالى أفضل من طلب الفرار منه فإن قلت من لا يحب الموت فهل يتصور أن يكون محبا لله فأقول كراهة الموت قد تكون لحب الدنيا والتأسف على فراق الأهل والمال والولد وهذا ينافي كمال حب الله تعالى لأن الحب الكامل هو الذي يستغرق كل القلب ولكن لا يبعد أن يكون له مع حب الأهل والولد شائبة من حب الله تعالى ضعيفة فإن الناس متفاوتون في الحب ويدل على ا
2:94.english: He, peace be upon him, said: «من أحب لقاء الله أحب الله لقاءه» — "Whoever loves the meeting with God, God loves meeting with him." And Ḥudhayfah said at the moment of death: "A beloved has come upon the occasion of need; he who regrets has not succeeded."
2:94.section_title_en: The Signs and Proofs of Love for God — Section 1175
2:94.anchors:
- Root: ح ب ب (ḥ-b-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root meaning: to love, to cherish; al-ḥabīb is the beloved; maḥabbah denotes the inclination of the heart toward that which pleases it.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Maḥabbah of God for the servant is His willing good for him and drawing him near; the servant's love for God is his inclination toward obedience and his yearning for vision (ru'yah) of Him.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): the heart's attachment; metaphorical (majāz): love as expressed through action and sacrifice, since mere claim without proof is empty.
- Root: م و ت (m-w-t)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Death as the cessation of corporeal life; the transition from this abode.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Death is not annihilation but departure from the body — a relocation of the soul; hence the believer's love of death is love of meeting God.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: biological death; metaphorical: the "death" of appetites and the severance of worldly attachments as a spiritual state.
- Root: ق ت ل (q-t-l)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Killing, slaying; qitāl is combat.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Martyrdom (shahādah) in God's path is the supreme proof of sincere love, as it offers the self entirely.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical combat; metaphorical: the struggle against the lower self (jihād al-nafs) as the greater warfare.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — Used to distinguish genuine love from mere claim, restricting true love to that which is evidenced by action.
2:94.topic: Al-Ghazali on the journey of the soul, death, and the Hereafter, from 'Love, Longing, Intimacy and Contentment'

2:165.arabic: لله تعالى قوله عز وجل يحبهم ويحبونه وقوله تعالى والذين آمنوا أشد حبا لله وهو دليل على إثبات الحب وإثبات التفاوت فيه وقد جعل رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم الحب لله من شرط الإيمان في أخبار كثيرة إذ قال أبو رزين العقيلي: يا رسول الله ما الإيمان قال أن يكون الله ورسوله أحب إليك مما سواهما (1) حديث لا يؤمن أحدكم حتى يكون الله ورسوله أحب إليه مما سواهما متفق عليه من حديث أنس بلفظ لا يجد أحد حلاوة الإيمان حتى أكون أحب إليه من أهلاه وماله وذكر بزيادة (2) حديث لا يؤمن العبد حتى أكون أحب إليه من أهله وماله ونفسه والناس أجمعين وفي رواية ومن
2:165.english: Know that the Community (al-ummah) is in unanimous agreement (mujmiʿah) that love for Allah — exalted is He — and for His Messenger — may Allah bless him and grant him peace — is an obligation (farḍ). Yet how can something be obligated whose existence is [questioned]? And how can love be interpreted as obedience, when obedience is but a consequence (tabʿ) of love and its fruit (thamaratu-hu)? Thus love must necessarily precede, and only then does the one who loves obey [the beloved]. Evidence for the affirmation of love for Allah — exalted is He — is His saying — mighty and majestic is He: {«يُحِبُّهُمْ وَيُحِبُّونَهُ»} "He loves them and they love Him" [Al-Ma'idah: 54], and His saying — exalted is He: {«وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا أَشَدُّ حُبًّا لِلَّهِ»} "And those who believe are more intense in love for Allah" [Al-Baqarah: 165]. This is proof of the affirmation of love and the affirmation of gradation (al-tafāwut) within it. And the Messenger of Allah — may Allah bless him and grant him peace — made love for Allah a condition (sharṭ) of faith (al-īmān) in numerous reports (akhbār). For Abu Razīn al-ʿUqaylī said: "O Messenger of Allah, what is faith?" He said: "That Allah and His Messenger be more beloved to you than all else besides them." (1) The hadith: "None of you believes until Allah and His Messenger are more beloved to him than all else besides them" — agreed upon (muttafaq ʿalayhi) from the hadith of Anas, with the wording: "None finds the sweetness of faith until I am more beloved to him than his family and his wealth" — mentioned with an addition. (2) The hadith: "No servant believes until I am more beloved to him than his family, his wealth, his own self (nafsihi), and all people" — and in one narration: "and than his own self" — agreed upon from the hadith of Anas, the wording being Muslim's, except for his saying "and than his own self." Al-Bukhari said: "from his father and his child." And from him — from the hadith of ʿAbdullah ibn Hishām: ʿUmar said: "O Messenger of Allah, you are more beloved to me than everything except my own self." He said: "No, by Him in whose hand is my soul, until I am more beloved to you than your own self." ʿUmar said: "Then now, by Allah, you are more beloved to me than my own self." He said: "Now, O ʿUmar." PageV04P294
2:165.section_title_en: ** The Reality of Love for God and His Messenger — Its Obligation, Proof, and Fruits
2:165.anchors:
**

- Root: ح ب ب (ḥ-b-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الحب: الوداد والمحبة، والحبيب: المحبوب. وأصل الحب: ثبات المحبة في القلب ولزومها، ومنه حَبَّ البعير: برك فلم يثر، وحَبَّ الماء في الإناء: لزم وثبت."
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "المحبة: إرادة ما تراه خيرا، وتكون من العبد لله بمعنى إرادة طاعته واتباع أمره، ومن الله للعبد بمعنى إرادة تكريمه وإثابته. والحب الحقيقي لا يكون إلا لمن يستحق الإحسان لذاته، وهو الله تعالى."
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "Haqiqah (Literal): حببته فأحبني، وتحاب القوم. Majaz (Metaphorical): أحب البعير: برك، وأحبت الناقة: لزمت مكانها فلم تبرح — فاستعير اللزوم والثبات للمحبة التي تلزم القلب."
- Root: أ ل ه (ʾ-l-h)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الإله: الله تعالى، وأصله إلاه على وزن فعال بمعنى مألوه أي معبود، يقال: أله يأله ألاهة وإلاهة: عبد، وتأله: تعبد."
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الإله: هو المعبود، وقد يقال لكل ما يتخذ معبودا، والله تعالى هو الإله الحق الذي تألهه القلوب محبة وخوفا ورجاء."
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "Haqiqah: الإله: المعبود بحق. Majaz: أله الرجل إلى فلان: فزع إليه والتجأ — فالإله هو المفزع الملجأ الذي تسكن القلوب إليه."
- Root: ر س ل (r-s-l)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الرسول: النبي المبعوث برسالة، والجمع رسل. وأصل الرسل: الانبعاث على تؤدة ورفق."
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الرسول: من يبعث برسالة، ويقال للقول المتحمل وللشخص المتحمل. والرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم هو المبلغ عن الله تعالى."
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "Haqiqah: أرسل الله في الأمم رسلا. Majaz: أرسل يده عن يده: خذله، وأرسل الفحل في الإبل — فالرسول من أرسله الله انبعاثا بالهداية."
- Root: ن ف س (n-f-s)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "النفس: الروح، والذات، والشيء بعينه. ونفس الشيء: حقيقته وذاته."
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "النفس تقال لمعان: منها الروح، ومنها الذات، قال تعالى: ويحذركم الله نفسه [آل عمران/28] أي ذاته. وتطلق النفس على الدم، وعلى العين."
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "Haqiqah: النفس: الروح والذات. Majaz: دفق نفسه أي دمه، وأصابته نفس: عين."
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — "إنما" تحصر الخبر في المبتدأ وتنفي ما عداه، كما في قوله تعالى: {إنما المؤمنون الذين آمنوا بالله ورسوله} — فالحصر هنا يقتضي أن المحبة شرط الإيمان لا يتم إلا بها.

---
