33:62.arabic: سنة الله تعالى في خلقه ولن تجد لسنة الله تبديلا فلا يخلق الله حركة اليد بكتابة منظومة ما لم يخلق فيها صفة تسمى قدرة وما لم يخلق فيها حياة وما لم يخلق إرادة مجزومة ولا يخلق الإرادة المجزومة ما لم يخلق شهوة وميلا في النفس ولا ينبعث هذا الميل انبعاثا تاما ما لم يخلق علما بأنه موافق للنفس إما في الحال أو في المآل ولا يخلق العلم أيضا إلا بأسباب أخر ترجع إلى حركة وإرادة وعلم فالعلم والميل الطبيعي أبدا يستتبع الإرادة الجازمة والقدرة والإرادة أبدا تستردف الحركة وهكذا الترتيب في كل فعل والكل من اختراع
33:62.english: Know that the obligation of repentance is made evident by the transmitted reports (1) and the Quranic verses, and it is clear by the light of inner vision (nūr al-baṣīrah) for the one whose insight has been opened and whose breast God has expanded with the light of faith, until he is able to walk by his light which is before him through the darknesses of ignorance, independent of a guide to lead him at every step. For the wayfarer is either blind, not independent of a guide in his steps, or sighted, guided to the beginning of the road and then guided by himself. Likewise, people on the path of religion are divided according to this division. There is the deficient one who cannot surpass emulation (taqlīd) in his steps, and thus needs to hear at every footfall a text from the Book of God or the Sunnah of His Messenger — and perhaps that fails him, and he becomes bewildered. The journeying of this one, even if his life is long and his effort great, is short, and his steps are deficient. And there is the fortunate one whose breast God has expanded for Islam, and he is upon a light from his Lord. He is alerted by the slightest indication to traverse a rugged path and to cut through exhausting obstacles, and the light of the Quran and the light of faith shine in his heart. Due to the intensity of the light of his inner being, he is satisfied with the slightest explanation, as if his oil were about to glow even if fire did not touch it — and when fire touches it, it is light upon light. {«يَهْدِي اللَّهُ لِنُورِهِ مَنْ يَشَاءُ»} God guides to His light whom He wills. This one does not need a transmitted text in every occurrence. So whoever is in this state, when he wishes to know the obligation of repentance, he looks first with the light of inner vision at what repentance is, then at what the meaning of obligation is, then he combines the meaning of obligation with repentance and does not doubt its being established for it. That is, by knowing that the meaning of "the obligatory" is that which is necessary for reaching the felicity of eternity and for deliverance from the perdition of eternity. For were it not for the attachment of felicity and misery to the doing of a thing or its abandonment, there would be no meaning to describing it as obligatory. And the saying of one who says, "It became obligatory by an act of imposition," is pure idle talk. For that in whose doing or abandoning we have no interest, whether in the hereafter or in this world, has no meaning for our occupying ourselves with it, whether another imposed it upon us or did not impose it. So when he knows the meaning of obligation — that it is the means to the felicity of eternity — and knows that there is no felicity in the abode of permanence except in the encounter (liqāʾ) of God Most High, and that everyone veiled from Him is miserable without exception, cut off from what he desires, burned by the fire of separation and the fire of Hell; and knows that nothing distances from the encounter of God except the following of passions and intimacy with this perishing world and clinging to the love of what must inevitably be parted from; and knows that nothing brings near to the encounter of God except severing the heart's attachment from the ornament of this world and turning wholly to God, seeking intimacy with Him through the constancy of His remembrance, and love for Him through knowledge of His majesty and beauty to the extent of one's capacity; and knows that sins — which are a turning away from God and a following of what the devils, the enemies of God who distance from His presence, love — are the cause of one's being veiled and distanced from God Most High — then he does not doubt that turning away from the path of distance is obligatory for reaching proximity. And turning away is only completed by knowledge, remorse, and resolve. For as long as he does not know that sins are causes of distance from the Beloved, he will not regret nor feel pain due to his traveling the path of distance; and as long as he does not feel pain, he will not return; and the meaning of returning is abandoning and resolving. So he does not doubt that the three meanings are necessary for reaching the Beloved. And such is the faith that results from the light of inner vision.
33:62.section_title_en: The Obligation of Repentance: Its Reality, Its Proofs, and the Reconciliation of Divine Decree with Human Agency
33:62.anchors:
- Root: توب (T-W-B)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning is "return" (rujūʿ) — the act of turning back from a path one was on.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In theological usage, it signifies returning from sin (dhamb) to obedience, and from distance (buʿd) from God to proximity (qurb) to Him. It is the servant's reversion to his original, sound nature.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) sense is "returning"; metaphorical (majāz) extension applies it to the heart's turning away from the pursuit of worldly desires (shahawāt) toward the remembrance of God.
- Root: وجب (W-J-B)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning is "to be established, fixed, or necessary" — something whose non-existence entails a contradiction or harm.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The obligatory (wājib) is that which, if neglected, incurs blame; it is divided into what is obligatory by reason (ʿaql) and what is obligatory by revelation (sharʿ).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal sense: "to be due" or "to fall" (as in a price being fixed); metaphorical sense: the soul's "falling" into action out of necessity.
- Root: خلق (Kh-L-Q)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning is "measuring" or "estimating" (taqdīr) — bringing something into existence according to a precise measure.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Used for creation from nothing (ibdāʿ) and for bringing something forth from another thing; all of God's acts are measured by His eternal decree.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the artisan's measuring of leather before cutting; Metaphorical: God's origination of creation upon a measure necessitated by wisdom.
- Root: كسب (K-S-B)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning is "to acquire" or "to earn" — an act that returns a benefit or harm to the agent.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In Kalam, acquisition (kasb) denotes the creature's relation to an act that is entirely God's creation, yet is attributed to the servant by way of his being the locus of its occurrence.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: to gather wealth; Metaphorical: the soul's "gathering" of deeds that cling to it as its own.
- Sibawayh Rule: Restriction and Focused Predication (al-ḥaṣr wa al-taqyīd bi-innamā) — used to delimit the meaning of "obligation" to its true referent (the means to eternal felicity), and to restrict the attribution of acts to God alone as their sole Creator.
33:62.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Love, Longing, Intimacy and Contentment'

36:58.arabic: تعالى {سلام قولا من رب رحيم} والثالثة يقول الله تعالى إني عنكم راض فيكون ذلك أفضل من الهدية والتسليم فذلك قوله تعالى {ورضوان من الله أكبر} أي من النعيم الذي هم فيه فهذا فضل رضا الله تعالى وهو ثمرة رضا العبد وأما من الأخبار فقد روي أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم سأل طائفة من أصحابه ما أنتم فقالوا مؤمنون فقال ما علامة إيمانكم فقالوا نصبر على البلاء ونشكر عند الرخاء ونرضى بمواقع القضاء فقال مؤمنون ورب الكعبة (2) وفي خبر آخر أنه قال حكماء علماء كادوا من فقههم أن يكونوا أنبي
36:58.english: I say: As for the verses [indicating the supremacy of divine pleasure], there is the saying of the Exalted: {رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمْ وَرَضُوا عَنْهُ} [Allah is well-pleased with them and they are well-pleased with Him] {«God is well-pleased with them and they are well-pleased with Him»}. And the Exalted has said: {هَلْ جَزَاءُ الْإِحْسَانِ إِلَّا الْإِحْسَانُ} [Is the reward of goodness aught but goodness?] {«Is the reward of goodness aught but goodness?»}. The ultimate end of goodness is God's pleasure with His servant, and that is the reward for the servant's pleasure in God the Exalted.
36:58.section_title_en: The Reality of Divine Pleasure (Riḍā) and the Servant's Contentment with the Decree — Section 1189
36:58.anchors:
- Root: رضي (raḍiya)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning is "to be content, to approve, to be pleased." Al-Farahidi notes its usage in mutual accord and satisfaction, with the form *tarāḍin* indicating reciprocal consent.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In theological usage, *riḍā* denotes the will's acquiescence to the divine decree without resistance. It is the apex of the servant's station, being the fruit of *maḥabbah* (love) and the key to perpetual vision (*nazar*).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (*ḥaqīqah*) sense is "satisfaction of the heart." Metaphorical (*majāz*) extension applies to God, where *riḍwān* is not an emotional state but a volitional attribute signifying the bestowal of grace and the removal of the veil.
- Root: نظر (naẓara)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "To look, to behold, to consider." In the lexicon, *naẓar* implies directed vision with the eye or the intellect.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Elevated to the highest beatific vision (*ru'yat Allāh*) in the afterlife, the ultimate reward and the supreme object of the inhabitants of Paradise.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical sight. Metaphorical: intellectual contemplation or the unveiled witnessing of the Divine in the Hereafter.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب التفضيل والتشبيه (The Chapter of Preference and Comparison) — Governing the syntactic structures of *afʿala* (elative) forms like *akbar* ("greater") to establish hierarchical supremacy between two entities, as in the verse {وَرِضْوَانٌ مِنَ اللَّهِ أَكْبَرُ}.
36:58.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Love, Longing, Intimacy and Contentment'

39:29.arabic: ظاهرا من الحياة الدنيا وهم عن الآخرة هم غافلون الحمد لله بل أكثرهم لا يعلمون فالحب بهذا السبب أقوى من الحب بالإحسان لأن الإحسان يزيد وينقص ولذلك أوحى الله تعالى إلى داود عليه السلام إن أود الأوداء إلى من عبدني بغير نوال لكن ليعطي الربوبية حقها وفي الزبور من أظلم ممن عبدنى لجنة أونار لو لم أخلق جنة ولا نارا ألم أكن أهلا أن أطاع ومر عيسى عليه السلام على طائفة من العباد قد نحلوا فقالوا نخاف النار ونرجو الجنة فقال لهم مخلوقا خفتم ومخلوقا رجوتم ومر بقوم آخرين كذلك فقالوا نعبده حبا له وتعظيما لجلاله فقال أنتم أولياء الله حقا معكم أ
39:29.english: ...power except through the enabling of his Master, just as He said concerning the greatest of the kings of the earth, Dhul-Qarnayn, when He said: {«إنا مكنا له في الأرض»} — "Indeed, We established him firmly upon the earth" (Q. 18:84). For all his kingship and sovereignty was nothing but the enabling of God Most High granted to him over a portion of the earth — and the entire earth is but a speck of dust in relation to the bodies of the world. And all the dominions that people attain from the earth are but a mote from that speck of dust. Then that mote, too, is from the bounty of God Most High and His enabling. It is therefore impossible that a servant should love one of God's servants for his power, his governance, his enablement, his dominion, and the completeness of his strength, yet not love God Most High for that very reason. And there is no might and no power except through God, the Exalted, the Magnificent. For He is the Compeller (al-Jabbār), the Subduer (al-Qāhir), the All-Knowing (al-'Alīm), the All-Powerful (al-Qādir). The heavens are folded in His right hand, and the earth with its kingdom and all that is upon it is in His grasp. The forelock of all creatures is in the grip of His power. If He destroyed them all, from the first to the last, not a single atom would diminish from His sovereignty and kingdom; and if He created their like a thousand times, He would not be wearied by their creation, nor would fatigue or languor touch Him in inventing them. So there is no power and no powerful one except that it is a trace of the traces of His power. To Him belongs beauty (al-jamāl), splendor (al-bahā'), majesty (al-'azamah), grandeur (al-kibriyā'), subjugation (al-qahr), and dominion (al-istīlā'). If, then, it is conceivable that a powerful one be loved for the completeness of his power, then none whatsoever deserves love for completeness of power save Him alone.
39:29.section_title_en: The Fifth Cause of Love: Essential Beauty and Inner Affinity (Section 1156)
39:29.anchors:
- Root: قدر (q-d-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of measuring, determining, and enabling power; al-Farahidi notes its application to divine ordainment and human capacity.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Divine power (qudrah) is negation of incapacity ('ajz) in God; for humans, it is a contingent capacity granted by God's enabling (tamkīn), never absolute.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: measured capacity and enablement; Metaphorical: "far-reaching stride" (ba'īd al-qadr) — here, all creaturely power is but a trace of divine power.
- Root: قدس (q-d-s)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Purity and sanctity; being set apart from defilement.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Transcendence (taqdīs) as absolute purity from all deficiency — applicable in full only to God, the Holy (al-Quddūs).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical cleansing; Metaphorical: moral and ontological transcendence from every imperfection.
- Root: مثل (m-th-l)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Likeness, similarity, and representation.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Tamthīl (assimilation) and tashbīh (anthropomorphism) are impossible for God; munāsabah (affinity) is not likeness in form but in inner meaning.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: visual resemblance; Metaphorical: spiritual congruence (munāsabah) between the servant and God through acquired divine attributes.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — Used to confine absolute beauty, perfection, and lovability exclusively to God, e.g., "the Beautiful absolutely is the One who has no equal."
39:29.topic: Al-Ghazali on the journey of the soul, death, and the Hereafter, from 'Love, Longing, Intimacy and Contentment'

41:53.arabic: وإليه دعا الله سبحانه بقوله {سنريهم آياتنا في الآفاق وفي أنفسهم} وبقوله تعالى {وفي الأرض آيات للموقنين وفي أنفسكم أفلا تبصرون} وعلى القعود عن هذا السفر وقع الإنكار بقوله تعالى {وإنكم لتمرون عليهم مصبحين وبالليل أفلا تعقلون} وبقوله سبحانه {وكأين} {من آية في السماوات والأرض يمرون عليها وهم عنها معرضون} فمن يسر له هذا السفر لم يزل في سيره متنزها في جنة عرضها السماوات والأرض وهو ساكن بالبدن مستقر في الوطن وهو السفر الذي لا تضيق فيه المناهل والموارد ولا يضر فيه التزاحم والتوارد بل تزيد بكثرة المسافرين غنائ
41:53.english: And to this journey God — exalted be He — has summoned [us] by His saying: {«سَنُرِيهِمْ آيَاتِنَا فِي الْآفَاقِ وَفِي أَنْفُسِهِمْ»} [We shall show them Our signs in the horizons and in their own selves — Fussilat 41:53], and by His saying — exalted be He: {«وَفِي الْأَرْضِ آيَاتٌ لِلْمُوقِنِينَ * وَفِي أَنْفُسِكُمْ أَفَلَا تُبْصِرُونَ»} [And in the earth are signs for those who are certain; and in your own selves — do you not then see? — Dhāriyāt 51:20-21]. And upon sitting back from this journey, censure fell by His saying — exalted be He: {«وَإِنَّكُمْ لَتَمُرُّونَ عَلَيْهِمْ مُصْبِحِينَ * وَبِاللَّيْلِ أَفَلَا تَعْقِلُونَ»} [And indeed you pass by them in the morning, and by night — do you not then comprehend? — Ṣāffāt 37:137-138], and by His saying — exalted be He: {«وَكَأَيِّنْ مِنْ آيَةٍ فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ يَمُرُّونَ عَلَيْهَا وَهُمْ عَنْهَا مُعْرِضُونَ»} [And how many a sign in the heavens and the earth do they pass by, while they are from it turning away — Yūsuf 12:105]. So whoever is facilitated this journey, he never ceases in his traveling to take pleasure in a Garden whose breadth is the heavens and the earth — while he is still with his body at rest, settled in his homeland.
41:53.section_title_en: The Book of the Etiquettes of Travel — Being the Seventh Book of the Quarter of Customs from The Revival of the Religious Sciences
41:53.anchors:
- Root: سفر (s-f-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning is "unveiling/disclosure" (kashf al-ghitā'); also denotes journeying across land, and a group of travelers (safar/qawm musāfirūn).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-safar: "the removal of a covering," specialized to physical unveiling (e.g., removing a turban from the head). Its theological extension: the journey as a means of unveiling hidden realities — both outward horizons (āfāq) and inward selves (anfus).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (haqīqah): physical travel with the body, provisions for a journey (sufrah). Metaphorical (majāz): "a face radiant with joy" (wajh musfir); "the morning brightening" (asfara al-ṣubḥ) — the inner journey as illumination of the heart's countenance.
- Root: وفي (w-f-y)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Fullness, completion, fulfillment of a measure or covenant.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-wāfī: "that which has reached completion/perfection." Awfā bi-ʿahdihi: to fulfill one's covenant completely without breach. Theologically: the complete fulfillment of the servant's journey — arriving at the full measure of human perfection.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: a full-weight dirham, complete measure. Metaphorical: "to reach completion of years" (māta wa-ant bi-wafā'); "to come upon/arrive at" (awfā ʿalā) — the journey's end as arrival at full term.
- Root: نفس (n-f-s)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The self, soul, spirit; that which is precious and valued.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-nafs: the spirit (rūḥ); in God's speech "He knows what is in your selves" — the inner dimension of the human being, the seat of the divine secret.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: a precious thing (shay' nafīs). Metaphorical: "the soul's blood" (nafsuhu = damuhu); the inner landscape (āfāq al-anfus) as the terrain of the inward journey.
- Sibawayh Rule: Prepositional Interposition (al-faṣl bayna al-jār wa-al-majrūr) — governing the periodic suspension of meaning across clauses, as in the verse {سَنُرِيهِمْ آيَاتِنَا فِي الْآفَاقِ وَفِي أَنْفُسِهِمْ}, where the dual prepositional phrases (fī al-āfāq / fī anfusihim) are syntactically parallel yet semantically interposed, requiring the translator to preserve the balanced suspension of the two terrains of divine signs.
41:53.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Etiquette of Travel'

41:53.arabic: لما عرفت ربي وإلى الثاني الاشارة بقوله تعالى {سنريهم آياتنا في الآفاق وفي أنفسهم حتى يتبين لهم أنه الحق} الآية وبقوله عز وجل أولم ينظروا في ملكوت السموات والأرض وبقوله تعالى قل انظروا ماذا في السموات والأرض وبقوله تعالى الذي خلق سبع سموات طباقا ما ترى في خلق الرحمن من تفاوت فارجع البصر هل ترى من فطور ثم ارجع البصر كرتين ينقلب إليك البصر خاسئا وهو حسير وهذا الطريق هو الأسهل على الأكثرين وهو الأوسع على السالكين وإليه أكثر دعوة القرآن عند الأمر بالتدبر والتفكر والاعتبار والنظر في آيات خارجة عن الحصر فإن قلت كلا الطريقين مشكل فأوضح لنا منهما ما يس
41:53.english: Those who arrive at this rank divide into two groups: the strong, whose first knowledge is of God, exalted be He, and then through Him they come to know other than Him; and the weak, whose first knowledge is of [His] acts, and then they ascend from them to the Agent. To the first points His saying, exalted be He: {أو لم يكف بربك أنه على كل شيء شهيد} [Is it not sufficient concerning your Lord that He is over all things a Witness], and His saying, exalted be He: {«شهد الله أنه لا إله إلا هو»} [God bears witness that there is no god but He]. And of this kind is the saying of one of them, when it was said to him: "By what have you known your Lord?" He said: "I have known my Lord — and were it not for my Lord, I would not have known my Lord."
41:53.section_title_en: The Two Paths to Knowledge and Love: The Higher Way of Witnessing the Truth and the Easier Way of Contemplating Creation
41:53.anchors:
- Root: طيب (ṭ-y-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Pure, good, wholesome; free from defilement
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): That which is pure and agreeable in both sensory and intellectual registers; the "good word" (al-kalim al-ṭayyib) is the declaration of divine unity
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal for sensory purity; metaphorical for spiritual purity of heart and speech
- Root: عرف (ʿ-r-f)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To know by reflection and discernment of traces/effects
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Maʿrifah is knowledge of God attained through contemplation of His effects, not through direct apprehension of His essence; it is more specific than ʿilm
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: to recognize someone; metaphorical: knowledge of God through His signs
- Root: شهد (sh-h-d)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To witness, testify, be present
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Bearing witness to the truth of something based on direct presence or evidence
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: ocular presence; metaphorical: intellectual certitude
- Root: نظر (n-ẓ-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To look, gaze, contemplate
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Contemplative reflection (naẓar) directed toward creation to derive knowledge of the Creator
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: visual perception; metaphorical: intellectual consideration and inference
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — used to restrict the purpose of works to purification of the heart, and to restrict the ultimate end to knowledge of unveiling
41:53.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Love, Longing, Intimacy and Contentment'

41:53.arabic: الأرض والسموات ثم قال أو لم يكف بربك أنه على كل شيء شهيد {وقال} شهد الله أنه لا إله إلا هو فبين أنه الدليل على نفسه وذلك ليس متناقضا بل طرق الاستدلال مختلفة فكم من طالب عرف الله تعالى بالنظر إلى الموجودات وكم من طالب عرف كل الموجودات بالله تعالى كما قال بعضهم عرفت ربي بربي ولولا ربي لما عرفت ربي وهو معنى قوله تعالى أو لم يكف بربك أنه على كل شيء شهيد وقد وصف الله تعالى نفسه بأنه المحيي والمميت ثم فوض الموت والحياة إلى ملكين ففي الخبر أن ملكي الموت والحياة تناظرا فقال ملك الموت أنا أميت الأحياء وق
41:53.english: ...the killing — rather, He stated explicitly, and He, exalted, said: {فَلَمْ تَقْتُلُوهُمْ وَلَٰكِنَّ اللَّهَ قَتَلَهُمْ} ("You did not kill them, but God killed them") and He, exalted, said: {وَمَا رَمَيْتَ إِذْ رَمَيْتَ وَلَٰكِنَّ اللَّهَ رَمَىٰ} ("You did not throw when you threw, but God threw"). This is a combination of negation and affirmation in appearance, but its meaning is: "You did not throw" in the sense by which the Lord is a thrower, "when you threw" in the sense by which the servant is a thrower — for the two are two distinct meanings.
41:53.section_title_en: On the Unification of Divine Agency and the Foundation of Trust (Tawḥīd as the Root of Tawakkul)
41:53.anchors:
- Root: ق-ت-ل (Q-T-L)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: "to kill, to slay" — the act of causing death by direct agency.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In the Qur'anic context {فَلَمْ تَقْتُلُوهُمْ وَلَٰكِنَّ اللَّهَ قَتَلَهُمْ} (8:17), the verb is negated for the creature and affirmed for the Creator, indicating that true creative agency (ījād) belongs to God alone, while the creature's act is merely instrumental and attributive.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) usage assigns the verb to the true originator; metaphorical (majāz) usage assigns it to the proximate instrument, as in "the king killed" when the executioner strikes.
- Root: ر-م-ي (R-M-Y)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "To throw, to cast" — physical projection of an object.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In {وَمَا رَمَيْتَ إِذْ رَمَيْتَ وَلَٰكِنَّ اللَّهَ رَمَىٰ} (8:17), the dual affirmation and negation show two distinct meanings of "throwing": the human act (kasb) versus the divine act (khalq).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): The literal sense belongs to the agent who originates the act ex nihilo; the metaphorical sense belongs to the one through whom the act occurs as a vessel.
- Root: ع-ل-م (ʿ-L-M)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "Knowledge, perception, cognition" — the apprehension of a thing as it truly is.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Knowledge is of two kinds: (1) apprehension of the essence of a thing, and (2) judgment about a thing's existence or non-existence of attributes. Divine knowledge (ʿilm) is the source of all teaching, as in {عَلَّمَ بِالْقَلَمِ} (96:4).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "to know" as direct cognition; also "to teach" (ʿallama) as the transmission of that cognition.
- Root: و-ك-ل (W-K-L)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "To entrust, to delegate, to rely upon" — the act of appointing another as deputy and placing one's affair in their hands.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Tawakkul is to rely upon another and make them one's agent. The Wakīl (Trustee) is He who undertakes the affair of His servant, as in {وَكَفَىٰ بِاللَّهِ وَكِيلًا} (4:81).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "to entrust an affair to someone." Metaphorical: "to rely upon" in the sense of inner confidence and tranquility of heart.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — The particle "innamā" restricts the predicate to the subject alone, excluding all others. Also applicable: the rule of negation and affirmation (nafy wa-ithbāt) in a single sentence, where the negation applies to one sense and the affirmation to another, requiring semantic disambiguation (taṣrīf al-maʿnā).
41:53.topic: Al-Ghazali on the journey of the soul, death, and the Hereafter, from 'Love, Longing, Intimacy and Contentment'

48:23.arabic: سنة الله تعالى في خلقه ولن تجد لسنة الله تبديلا فلا يخلق الله حركة اليد بكتابة منظومة ما لم يخلق فيها صفة تسمى قدرة وما لم يخلق فيها حياة وما لم يخلق إرادة مجزومة ولا يخلق الإرادة المجزومة ما لم يخلق شهوة وميلا في النفس ولا ينبعث هذا الميل انبعاثا تاما ما لم يخلق علما بأنه موافق للنفس إما في الحال أو في المآل ولا يخلق العلم أيضا إلا بأسباب أخر ترجع إلى حركة وإرادة وعلم فالعلم والميل الطبيعي أبدا يستتبع الإرادة الجازمة والقدرة والإرادة أبدا تستردف الحركة وهكذا الترتيب في كل فعل والكل من اختراع
48:23.english: Know that the obligation of repentance is made evident by the transmitted reports (1) and the Quranic verses, and it is clear by the light of inner vision (nūr al-baṣīrah) for the one whose insight has been opened and whose breast God has expanded with the light of faith, until he is able to walk by his light which is before him through the darknesses of ignorance, independent of a guide to lead him at every step. For the wayfarer is either blind, not independent of a guide in his steps, or sighted, guided to the beginning of the road and then guided by himself. Likewise, people on the path of religion are divided according to this division. There is the deficient one who cannot surpass emulation (taqlīd) in his steps, and thus needs to hear at every footfall a text from the Book of God or the Sunnah of His Messenger — and perhaps that fails him, and he becomes bewildered. The journeying of this one, even if his life is long and his effort great, is short, and his steps are deficient. And there is the fortunate one whose breast God has expanded for Islam, and he is upon a light from his Lord. He is alerted by the slightest indication to traverse a rugged path and to cut through exhausting obstacles, and the light of the Quran and the light of faith shine in his heart. Due to the intensity of the light of his inner being, he is satisfied with the slightest explanation, as if his oil were about to glow even if fire did not touch it — and when fire touches it, it is light upon light. {«يَهْدِي اللَّهُ لِنُورِهِ مَنْ يَشَاءُ»} God guides to His light whom He wills. This one does not need a transmitted text in every occurrence. So whoever is in this state, when he wishes to know the obligation of repentance, he looks first with the light of inner vision at what repentance is, then at what the meaning of obligation is, then he combines the meaning of obligation with repentance and does not doubt its being established for it. That is, by knowing that the meaning of "the obligatory" is that which is necessary for reaching the felicity of eternity and for deliverance from the perdition of eternity. For were it not for the attachment of felicity and misery to the doing of a thing or its abandonment, there would be no meaning to describing it as obligatory. And the saying of one who says, "It became obligatory by an act of imposition," is pure idle talk. For that in whose doing or abandoning we have no interest, whether in the hereafter or in this world, has no meaning for our occupying ourselves with it, whether another imposed it upon us or did not impose it. So when he knows the meaning of obligation — that it is the means to the felicity of eternity — and knows that there is no felicity in the abode of permanence except in the encounter (liqāʾ) of God Most High, and that everyone veiled from Him is miserable without exception, cut off from what he desires, burned by the fire of separation and the fire of Hell; and knows that nothing distances from the encounter of God except the following of passions and intimacy with this perishing world and clinging to the love of what must inevitably be parted from; and knows that nothing brings near to the encounter of God except severing the heart's attachment from the ornament of this world and turning wholly to God, seeking intimacy with Him through the constancy of His remembrance, and love for Him through knowledge of His majesty and beauty to the extent of one's capacity; and knows that sins — which are a turning away from God and a following of what the devils, the enemies of God who distance from His presence, love — are the cause of one's being veiled and distanced from God Most High — then he does not doubt that turning away from the path of distance is obligatory for reaching proximity. And turning away is only completed by knowledge, remorse, and resolve. For as long as he does not know that sins are causes of distance from the Beloved, he will not regret nor feel pain due to his traveling the path of distance; and as long as he does not feel pain, he will not return; and the meaning of returning is abandoning and resolving. So he does not doubt that the three meanings are necessary for reaching the Beloved. And such is the faith that results from the light of inner vision.
48:23.section_title_en: The Obligation of Repentance: Its Reality, Its Proofs, and the Reconciliation of Divine Decree with Human Agency
48:23.anchors:
- Root: توب (T-W-B)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning is "return" (rujūʿ) — the act of turning back from a path one was on.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In theological usage, it signifies returning from sin (dhamb) to obedience, and from distance (buʿd) from God to proximity (qurb) to Him. It is the servant's reversion to his original, sound nature.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) sense is "returning"; metaphorical (majāz) extension applies it to the heart's turning away from the pursuit of worldly desires (shahawāt) toward the remembrance of God.
- Root: وجب (W-J-B)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning is "to be established, fixed, or necessary" — something whose non-existence entails a contradiction or harm.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The obligatory (wājib) is that which, if neglected, incurs blame; it is divided into what is obligatory by reason (ʿaql) and what is obligatory by revelation (sharʿ).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal sense: "to be due" or "to fall" (as in a price being fixed); metaphorical sense: the soul's "falling" into action out of necessity.
- Root: خلق (Kh-L-Q)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning is "measuring" or "estimating" (taqdīr) — bringing something into existence according to a precise measure.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Used for creation from nothing (ibdāʿ) and for bringing something forth from another thing; all of God's acts are measured by His eternal decree.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the artisan's measuring of leather before cutting; Metaphorical: God's origination of creation upon a measure necessitated by wisdom.
- Root: كسب (K-S-B)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning is "to acquire" or "to earn" — an act that returns a benefit or harm to the agent.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In Kalam, acquisition (kasb) denotes the creature's relation to an act that is entirely God's creation, yet is attributed to the servant by way of his being the locus of its occurrence.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: to gather wealth; Metaphorical: the soul's "gathering" of deeds that cling to it as its own.
- Sibawayh Rule: Restriction and Focused Predication (al-ḥaṣr wa al-taqyīd bi-innamā) — used to delimit the meaning of "obligation" to its true referent (the means to eternal felicity), and to restrict the attribution of acts to God alone as their sole Creator.
48:23.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Love, Longing, Intimacy and Contentment'

54:55.arabic: في جنات ونهر في مقعد صدق عند مليك مقتدر ينظرون فيها إلى وجه الملك الكريم وقد أشرقت في وجوههم نضرة النعيم لا يرهقهم فتر ولا ذلة بل عباد مكرمون وبأنواع التحف من ربهم يتعاهدون فهم فيما اشتهيت أنفسهم خالدون لا يخافون فيها ولا يحزنون وهم من ريب المنون آمنون فهم فيها يتنعمون ويأكلون من أطعمتها ويشربون من أنهارها لبنا وخمرا وعسلا في أنهار أراضيها من فضة وحصباؤها مرجان وعلى أرض ترابها مسك أذفر ونباتها زعفران ويمطرون من سحاب فيها من ماء النسرين على كثبان الكافور ويؤتون بأكواب وأي أكواب بأك
54:55.english: For God Most High has said: {«إن الأبرار لفي نعيم وإن الفجار لفي جحيم»} — "Indeed the righteous are in bliss, and indeed the wicked are in Hellfire." So present yourself before these two verses, and you will have known your resting-place between the two abodes. And God knows best.
54:55.section_title_en: Section 1351 — On the Description of Paradise and the Varieties of Its Bliss
54:55.anchors:
- Root: نعم (n-ʿ-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root denotes softness, ease, and pleasant living; al-Ayn notes it among names of the leopard and tiger, while Lisan records "Nuʿm" as a proper name.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "النعمة: الحالة الحسنة" — niʿmah is the excellent state/condition one inhabits; niʿīm is the experience of delight. The verse {«إن الأبرار لفي نعيم»} designates the abiding state of bliss as a settled condition, not a transient act.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): "في النعمة والنعيم" — dwelling in bounty and bliss. Metaphorical (Majaz): "خفت نعامتهم: ذهبوا" — ostriches departing; here the root's literal sense of softness is transfigured into the theological state of perpetual ease, free from all harshness.
- Root: وجه (w-j-h)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root: face, front, direction; al-Ayn cites "وجه الصواب" — the face/course of correctness.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The face is the noblest part of the outward body, hence used for the essence (al-dhāt) of a thing; in {«ويبقى وجه ربك ذو الجلال والإكرام»} it signifies the Divine Essence. Here "وجه الملك الكريم" — the Face of the Generous King — denotes the Beatific Vision of God's Essence, not a corporeal organ.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical face. Metaphorical: "وجه القوم، وهؤلاء وجوه البلد" — the foremost, noblest of a people; thus the "face" of the King is His most august presence.
- Root: مرج (m-r-j)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root: mixing, confusion, letting loose; al-Ayn: "المرج: الشهد" — also pure honey; Lisan: "مرج أمرهم: اختلط" — their affair became disordered.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "أصل المرج: الخلط" — mixing; "أمر مريج" — a confused affair (Q. 50:5). In this text, the rivers of Paradise "مطردة" (flowing) are not "ممرجة" (mixed/confused) — rather they run pure and distinct, each in its channel.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "مرج الدواب: أرسلها في المرج" — releasing beasts into pasture. Metaphorical: "مرج الله البحرين" — God let the two seas flow freely; "مرجت عهودهم" — covenants became disordered. The contrast sharpens the purity of Paradise's rivers.
- Root: امن (a-m-n)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root: safety, freedom from fear; al-Ayn treats it under the hamzah chapter as the state of security.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "أصل الأمن: طمأنينة النفس وزوال الخوف" — tranquility of the soul and removal of fear. In the Hereafter, "آمنون" is not mere absence of threat but the positive, settled peace of the soul in the Divine presence.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "أمنته وآمننيه" — to grant safety. Metaphorical: "فرس أمين القوى" — a horse whose strength is trustworthy; here the blessed are "آمنون من ريب المنون" — secure from the vicissitudes of fate, a security that is trustworthy and unbreachable.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The rule permits separation between a preposition and its object by an element upon which speech may properly pause, as in "إن به لضرًا" — here "فهم فيما اشتهت أنفسهم خالدون" (in what their souls desire, abiding eternally) interposes the clause of desire between the prepositional phrase and its predicate, heightening rhetorical emphasis on the soul's fulfillment.
54:55.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Love, Longing, Intimacy and Contentment'

57:13.arabic: بتمامه وقوله تعالى {انظرونا نقتبس من نوركم قيل ارجعوا وراءكم فالتمسوا نورا} يدل على أن الأنوار لابد وأن يتزود أصلها في الدنيا ثم يزداد في الآخرة إشراقا فأما أن يتجدد نور فلا والحكم في هذا برجم الظنون مخطر ولم ينكشف لنا فيه بعد ما يوثق به فنسأل الله تعالى أن يزيدنا علما ورشدا ويرينا الحق حقا فهذا القدر من أنوار البصائر كاشف لحقائق الشوق ومعانيه وأما شواهد الأخبار والآثار فأكثر من أن تحصى فمما اشتهر من دعاء رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه كان يقول اللهم إني أسألك الرضا بعد القضاء وبرد العيش بعد الموت ولذة النظر إلى وجهك الك
57:13.english: And His saying, Glorified and Exalted is He: {نُورُهُمْ يَسْعَىٰ بَيْنَ أَيْدِيهِمْ وَبِأَيْمَانِهِمْ يَقُولُونَ رَبَّنَا أَتْمِمْ لَنَا نُورَنَا} ["Their light will run before them and on their right hands; they will say, 'Our Lord, perfect for us our light'"] (Q 66:8) — this is susceptible to the meaning that He bestows upon them the perfection of light whenever they had provisioned from the world the origin of light. And it is also susceptible that the intended meaning is the perfection of light in what was not illuminated in this world with an illumination that stands in need of further completion and radiance — so that this is what is meant by its perfection. And His saying, Exalted is He: {انْظُرُونَا نَقْتَبِسْ مِنْ نُورِكُمْ قِيلَ ارْجِعُوا وَرَاءَكُمْ فَالْتَمِسُوا نُورًا} ["Look upon us so we may borrow from your light. It will be said, 'Return behind you and seek light'"] (Q 57:13) — this indicates that the lights must have their origin provisioned in this world, then in the Hereafter they increase in radiance. But as for a light being newly generated [there without prior origin] — no. And the judgment in this matter is a venture of conjecture, perilous, and there has not been unveiled to us therein anything trustworthy. So we ask God, Exalted is He, to increase us in knowledge and right guidance, and to show us the truth as truth.
57:13.section_title_en: On the Ever-Replenished Delights of the Hereafter and the Yearning (Shawq) for the Divine Vision
57:13.anchors:
- Root: لذذ (Ladhdhah — Pleasure/Delight)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root denotes the sweetness of taste and the experience of sensory gratification; its verbal form (ladhdha) implies direct apprehension of what is agreeable.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In theological usage, true pleasure (al-ladhdhah al-ʿuẓmā) is the soul's perception of what is conformable to its nature — the highest being the vision of God (ru'yat Allāh) and the bliss of proximity to Him.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) for sensory delight; metaphorical (majāz) for intellectual and spiritual joys, where the "taste" is of gnosis (maʿrifah), not of the palate.

- Root: شوق (Shawq — Yearning/Longing)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The root signifies the soul's restless inclination toward a beloved; the "spurring on" of the heart toward reunion.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Shawq is the movement of the heart toward its ultimate Beloved (al-maḥbūb al-aʿlā) — a yearning that persists even in bliss, for the unveiling (kashf) of ever-greater divine self-disclosure.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal for human longing; metaphorical for the divine "yearning" attributed to God (as in the sacred reports), which is an expression of His loving acceptance and bestowal of grace, not an emotional lack.

- Root: نور (Nūr — Light)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root denotes illumination, radiance, and that by which one sees and is seen.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Twofold: sensory light (of the sun, stars) and intellectual/spiritual light (of reason, faith, and the Qur'an). The "light of the believers" on the Day of Resurrection is the latter — the radiance of their faith and works in the world.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal for physical luminosity; metaphorical (majāz) for guidance, clarity, and the illuminating power of divine truth in the heart.

- Root: قلب (Qalb — Heart)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root means to turn over, to flip, to transform — hence the heart is so-named for its constant fluctuation (taqallub) of states.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The heart is the seat of perception and understanding (al-ʿaql wa al-fahm); it is the subtle divine reality (al-laṭīfah al-rabbāniyyah) that apprehends God, not the physical organ.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal for the physical organ; metaphorical for the spiritual faculty of cognition and volition that turns toward or away from God.

- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — Governing the precise scope of statements like "the pleasure of what is renewed is only a distraction from the ache of yearning," ensuring the predicate is confined to the subject without overextension.
57:13.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications, prayers, and their spiritual power, from 'Love, Longing, Intimacy and Contentment'

61:4.arabic: ويحبونه} وقال تعالى {إن الله يحب الذين يقاتلون في سبيله صفا} وقال تعالى {إن الله يحب التوابين ويحب المتطهرين} ولذلك رد سبحانه على من ادعى أنه حبيب الله فقال {قل فلم يعذبكم بذنوبكم} وقد روى أنس عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال إذا أحب الله تعالى عبدا لم يضره ذنب والتائب من الذنب كمن لا ذنب له ثم تلا إن الله يحب التوابين (1) ومعناه أنه إذا أحبه تاب عليه قبل الموت فلم تضره الذنوب الماضية وإن كثرت كما لا يضر الكفر الماضي بعد الإسلام وقد اشترط الله تعالى للمحبة غفران الذنب فقال {قل إن كنتم تحبون الله فا
61:4.english: Know that the evidences of the Qur'an are manifest and numerous that God—exalted is He—loves His servant; thus, it is imperative to understand the meaning of this [love]. Let us first present the evidences of His love. God—exalted is He—said: {«يُحِبُّهُمْ وَيُحِبُّونَهُ»} [He loves them, and they love Him] (Q 5:54). And He said: {«إِنَّ اللَّهَ يُحِبُّ الَّذِينَ يُقَاتِلُونَ فِي سَبِيلِهِ صَفًّا»} [Indeed, God loves those who fight in His cause in a row] (Q 61:4). And He said: {«إِنَّ اللَّهَ يُحِبُّ التَّوَّابِينَ وَيُحِبُّ الْمُتَطَهِّرِينَ»} [Indeed, God loves those who repent and loves those who purify themselves] (Q 2:222). For this reason, He—glorified is He—rebuked the one who claimed to be God's beloved, saying: {«قُلْ فَلِمَ يُعَذِّبُكُمْ بِذُنُوبِكُمْ»} [Say: Then why does He punish you for your sins?] (Q 5:18). It is narrated that Anas reported the Prophet—peace be upon him—as saying: "When God—exalted is He—loves a servant, no sin harms him, and the one who repents from sin is like one who has no sin." Then he recited: {«إِنَّ اللَّهَ يُحِبُّ التَّوَّابِينَ»} [Indeed, God loves those who repent] (Q 2:222). Its meaning is that when He loves him, He grants him repentance before death, so past sins do not harm him, however numerous they may be—just as past disbelief does not harm one after embracing Islam. God—exalted is He—has made the forgiveness of sin a condition for [this] love, saying: {«قُلْ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ تُحِبُّونَ اللَّهَ فَاتَّبِعُونِي يُحْبِبْكُمُ اللَّهُ وَيَغْفِرْ لَكُمْ ذُنُوبَكُمْ»} [Say: If you love God, then follow me; God will love you and forgive you your sins] (Q 3:31). The Messenger of God—peace be upon him—said: "God—exalted is He—gives the world to those He loves and those He does not love, but He does not give faith except to those He loves." And the Messenger of God—peace be upon him—said: "Whoever humbles himself before God, God raises him; whoever is arrogant, God lowers him; and whoever remembers God much, God loves him." And he—peace be upon him—said, relaying from God—exalted is He: "The servant continues to draw near to Me with supererogatory acts until I love him; and when I love him, I become his hearing with which he hears, and his sight with which he sees" (ḥadīth). Zayd ibn Aslam said: "God indeed loves a servant until, from the intensity of His love for him, He says: 'Do what you wish, for I have forgiven you.'" The expressions of love [in scripture] are beyond enumeration.
61:4.section_title_en: On the Reality of God's Love for His Servant and Its Interpretation
61:4.anchors:
- Root: ح ب ب (ḥ-b-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: to love, to cherish; the root denotes inclination and attachment of the heart.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In theological usage, love (maḥabbah) toward God is a real inclination of the soul toward what is agreeable; toward creation, it is metaphorical, signifying divine will, favor, and the unveiling of veils.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) for creatures—an emotional inclination; metaphorical (majāz) for God—expressing volitional acts like drawing near, forgiving, and honoring.
- Root: ق ر ب (q-r-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Proximity, nearness; both spatial and relational.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Qurb denotes nearness in station, rank, and favor, not physical location; God's "nearness" to a servant is by unveiling and honor.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: spatial closeness; metaphorical: closeness in rank, virtue, or divine acceptance (e.g., "qaruba min Allāh" = drew near to God by obedience).
- Root: و ل ي (w-l-y)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To be near, to govern, to befriend; walāyah implies closeness and guardianship.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Wilāyah of God for the believer is His care and guidance; the servant's wilāyah for God is loyal adherence.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: adjacency; metaphorical: protective friendship and love.
- Sibawayh Rule: Restriction and specification (bāb al-ḥaṣr wa-l-taqyīd bi-innamā)—used to delimit meanings when terms are applied to God versus creatures, ensuring no equivocation.
61:4.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Love, Longing, Intimacy and Contentment'

61:5.arabic: عز وجل فلما نظروا إلى داود عليه السلام نهضوا ليتفرقوا عنه فقال داود إني رسول الله إليكم جئتكم لأبلغكم رسالة ربكم فأقبلوا نحوه وألقوا أسماعهم نحو قوله وألقوا أبصارهم إلى الأرض فقال داود إني رسول الله إليكم يقرئكم السلام ويقول لكم ألا تسألون حاجة ألا تنادوني أسمع صوتكم وكلامكم فإنكم أحبائي وأصفيائي وأوليائي أفرح لفرحكم وأسارع إلى محبتكم وأنظر إليكم في كل ساعة نظر الوالدة الشفيقة الرفيقة قال فجرت الدموع على خدودهم فقال شيخهم سبحانك سبحانك نحن عبيدك وبنو عبيدك فاغفر لنا ما قطع قلوبنا عن ذكرك فيما مضى من أعمارنا وقال الآخر سبحانك سبح
61:5.english: And His saying, Glorified and Exalted is He: {نُورُهُمْ يَسْعَىٰ بَيْنَ أَيْدِيهِمْ وَبِأَيْمَانِهِمْ يَقُولُونَ رَبَّنَا أَتْمِمْ لَنَا نُورَنَا} ["Their light will run before them and on their right hands; they will say, 'Our Lord, perfect for us our light'"] (Q 66:8) — this is susceptible to the meaning that He bestows upon them the perfection of light whenever they had provisioned from the world the origin of light. And it is also susceptible that the intended meaning is the perfection of light in what was not illuminated in this world with an illumination that stands in need of further completion and radiance — so that this is what is meant by its perfection. And His saying, Exalted is He: {انْظُرُونَا نَقْتَبِسْ مِنْ نُورِكُمْ قِيلَ ارْجِعُوا وَرَاءَكُمْ فَالْتَمِسُوا نُورًا} ["Look upon us so we may borrow from your light. It will be said, 'Return behind you and seek light'"] (Q 57:13) — this indicates that the lights must have their origin provisioned in this world, then in the Hereafter they increase in radiance. But as for a light being newly generated [there without prior origin] — no. And the judgment in this matter is a venture of conjecture, perilous, and there has not been unveiled to us therein anything trustworthy. So we ask God, Exalted is He, to increase us in knowledge and right guidance, and to show us the truth as truth.
61:5.section_title_en: On the Ever-Replenished Delights of the Hereafter and the Yearning (Shawq) for the Divine Vision
61:5.anchors:
- Root: لذذ (Ladhdhah — Pleasure/Delight)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root denotes the sweetness of taste and the experience of sensory gratification; its verbal form (ladhdha) implies direct apprehension of what is agreeable.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In theological usage, true pleasure (al-ladhdhah al-ʿuẓmā) is the soul's perception of what is conformable to its nature — the highest being the vision of God (ru'yat Allāh) and the bliss of proximity to Him.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) for sensory delight; metaphorical (majāz) for intellectual and spiritual joys, where the "taste" is of gnosis (maʿrifah), not of the palate.

- Root: شوق (Shawq — Yearning/Longing)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The root signifies the soul's restless inclination toward a beloved; the "spurring on" of the heart toward reunion.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Shawq is the movement of the heart toward its ultimate Beloved (al-maḥbūb al-aʿlā) — a yearning that persists even in bliss, for the unveiling (kashf) of ever-greater divine self-disclosure.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal for human longing; metaphorical for the divine "yearning" attributed to God (as in the sacred reports), which is an expression of His loving acceptance and bestowal of grace, not an emotional lack.

- Root: نور (Nūr — Light)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root denotes illumination, radiance, and that by which one sees and is seen.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Twofold: sensory light (of the sun, stars) and intellectual/spiritual light (of reason, faith, and the Qur'an). The "light of the believers" on the Day of Resurrection is the latter — the radiance of their faith and works in the world.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal for physical luminosity; metaphorical (majāz) for guidance, clarity, and the illuminating power of divine truth in the heart.

- Root: قلب (Qalb — Heart)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root means to turn over, to flip, to transform — hence the heart is so-named for its constant fluctuation (taqallub) of states.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The heart is the seat of perception and understanding (al-ʿaql wa al-fahm); it is the subtle divine reality (al-laṭīfah al-rabbāniyyah) that apprehends God, not the physical organ.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal for the physical organ; metaphorical for the spiritual faculty of cognition and volition that turns toward or away from God.

- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — Governing the precise scope of statements like "the pleasure of what is renewed is only a distraction from the ache of yearning," ensuring the predicate is confined to the subject without overextension.
61:5.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications, prayers, and their spiritual power, from 'Love, Longing, Intimacy and Contentment'

61:5.arabic: زاغوا أزاغ الله قلوبهم وما الله بظلام للعبيد ولكنهم يظلمون أنفسهم ومن لم يؤهل للجولان في هذا الميدان والتطواف في متنزهات هذا البستان ربما سافر بظاهر بدنه في مدة مديدة فراسخ معدودة مغتنما بها تجارة للدنيا أو ذخيرة للآخرة فإن كان مطلبه العلم والدين أو الكفاية للاستعانة على الدين كان من سالكي سبيل الآخرة وكان له في سفره شروط وآداب إن أهملها كان من عمال الدنيا وأتباع الشيطان وإن واظب عليها لم يخل سفره عن فوائد تلحقه بعمال الآخرة ونحن نذكر آدابه وشروطه في بابين إن شاء الله تعالى
61:5.english: And to this journey God — exalted be He — has summoned [us] by His saying: {«سَنُرِيهِمْ آيَاتِنَا فِي الْآفَاقِ وَفِي أَنْفُسِهِمْ»} [We shall show them Our signs in the horizons and in their own selves — Fussilat 41:53], and by His saying — exalted be He: {«وَفِي الْأَرْضِ آيَاتٌ لِلْمُوقِنِينَ * وَفِي أَنْفُسِكُمْ أَفَلَا تُبْصِرُونَ»} [And in the earth are signs for those who are certain; and in your own selves — do you not then see? — Dhāriyāt 51:20-21]. And upon sitting back from this journey, censure fell by His saying — exalted be He: {«وَإِنَّكُمْ لَتَمُرُّونَ عَلَيْهِمْ مُصْبِحِينَ * وَبِاللَّيْلِ أَفَلَا تَعْقِلُونَ»} [And indeed you pass by them in the morning, and by night — do you not then comprehend? — Ṣāffāt 37:137-138], and by His saying — exalted be He: {«وَكَأَيِّنْ مِنْ آيَةٍ فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ يَمُرُّونَ عَلَيْهَا وَهُمْ عَنْهَا مُعْرِضُونَ»} [And how many a sign in the heavens and the earth do they pass by, while they are from it turning away — Yūsuf 12:105]. So whoever is facilitated this journey, he never ceases in his traveling to take pleasure in a Garden whose breadth is the heavens and the earth — while he is still with his body at rest, settled in his homeland.
61:5.section_title_en: The Book of the Etiquettes of Travel — Being the Seventh Book of the Quarter of Customs from The Revival of the Religious Sciences
61:5.anchors:
- Root: سفر (s-f-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning is "unveiling/disclosure" (kashf al-ghitā'); also denotes journeying across land, and a group of travelers (safar/qawm musāfirūn).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-safar: "the removal of a covering," specialized to physical unveiling (e.g., removing a turban from the head). Its theological extension: the journey as a means of unveiling hidden realities — both outward horizons (āfāq) and inward selves (anfus).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (haqīqah): physical travel with the body, provisions for a journey (sufrah). Metaphorical (majāz): "a face radiant with joy" (wajh musfir); "the morning brightening" (asfara al-ṣubḥ) — the inner journey as illumination of the heart's countenance.
- Root: وفي (w-f-y)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Fullness, completion, fulfillment of a measure or covenant.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-wāfī: "that which has reached completion/perfection." Awfā bi-ʿahdihi: to fulfill one's covenant completely without breach. Theologically: the complete fulfillment of the servant's journey — arriving at the full measure of human perfection.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: a full-weight dirham, complete measure. Metaphorical: "to reach completion of years" (māta wa-ant bi-wafā'); "to come upon/arrive at" (awfā ʿalā) — the journey's end as arrival at full term.
- Root: نفس (n-f-s)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The self, soul, spirit; that which is precious and valued.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-nafs: the spirit (rūḥ); in God's speech "He knows what is in your selves" — the inner dimension of the human being, the seat of the divine secret.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: a precious thing (shay' nafīs). Metaphorical: "the soul's blood" (nafsuhu = damuhu); the inner landscape (āfāq al-anfus) as the terrain of the inward journey.
- Sibawayh Rule: Prepositional Interposition (al-faṣl bayna al-jār wa-al-majrūr) — governing the periodic suspension of meaning across clauses, as in the verse {سَنُرِيهِمْ آيَاتِنَا فِي الْآفَاقِ وَفِي أَنْفُسِهِمْ}, where the dual prepositional phrases (fī al-āfāq / fī anfusihim) are syntactically parallel yet semantically interposed, requiring the translator to preserve the balanced suspension of the two terrains of divine signs.
61:5.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Etiquette of Travel'

62:6.arabic: لأحببته وتلا قوله تعالى فتمنوا الموت إن كنتم صادقين فقال الرجل فقد قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لا يتمنينأحدكم الموت (3) فقال إنما قاله لضر نزل به لأن الرضا بقضاء الله تعالى أفضل من طلب الفرار منه فإن قلت من لا يحب الموت فهل يتصور أن يكون محبا لله فأقول كراهة الموت قد تكون لحب الدنيا والتأسف على فراق الأهل والمال والولد وهذا ينافي كمال حب الله تعالى لأن الحب الكامل هو الذي يستغرق كل القلب ولكن لا يبعد أن يكون له مع حب الأهل والولد شائبة من حب الله تعالى ضعيفة فإن الناس متفاوتون في الحب ويدل على ا
62:6.english: He, peace be upon him, said: «من أحب لقاء الله أحب الله لقاءه» — "Whoever loves the meeting with God, God loves meeting with him." And Ḥudhayfah said at the moment of death: "A beloved has come upon the occasion of need; he who regrets has not succeeded."
62:6.section_title_en: The Signs and Proofs of Love for God — Section 1175
62:6.anchors:
- Root: ح ب ب (ḥ-b-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root meaning: to love, to cherish; al-ḥabīb is the beloved; maḥabbah denotes the inclination of the heart toward that which pleases it.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Maḥabbah of God for the servant is His willing good for him and drawing him near; the servant's love for God is his inclination toward obedience and his yearning for vision (ru'yah) of Him.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): the heart's attachment; metaphorical (majāz): love as expressed through action and sacrifice, since mere claim without proof is empty.
- Root: م و ت (m-w-t)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Death as the cessation of corporeal life; the transition from this abode.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Death is not annihilation but departure from the body — a relocation of the soul; hence the believer's love of death is love of meeting God.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: biological death; metaphorical: the "death" of appetites and the severance of worldly attachments as a spiritual state.
- Root: ق ت ل (q-t-l)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Killing, slaying; qitāl is combat.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Martyrdom (shahādah) in God's path is the supreme proof of sincere love, as it offers the self entirely.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical combat; metaphorical: the struggle against the lower self (jihād al-nafs) as the greater warfare.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — Used to distinguish genuine love from mere claim, restricting true love to that which is evidenced by action.
62:6.topic: Al-Ghazali on the journey of the soul, death, and the Hereafter, from 'Love, Longing, Intimacy and Contentment'

67:3.arabic: وبقوله تعالى الذي خلق سبع سموات طباقا ما ترى في خلق الرحمن من تفاوت فارجع البصر هل ترى من فطور ثم ارجع البصر كرتين ينقلب إليك البصر خاسئا وهو حسير وهذا الطريق هو الأسهل على الأكثرين وهو الأوسع على السالكين وإليه أكثر دعوة القرآن عند الأمر بالتدبر والتفكر والاعتبار والنظر في آيات خارجة عن الحصر فإن قلت كلا الطريقين مشكل فأوضح لنا منهما ما يستعان به على تحصيل المعرفة والتوصل به إلى المحبة فاعلم أن الطريق الأعلى هو الاستشهاد بالحق سبحانه على سائر الخلق فهو غامض والكلام فيه خارج عن حد فهم أكثر الخلق فلا فائدة في إيراده في الكتب وأما الطريق الأسهل الأدنى فأكثره غير خارج عن حد الأفهام وإنما قصرت ال
67:3.english: Those who arrive at this rank divide into two groups: the strong, whose first knowledge is of God, exalted be He, and then through Him they come to know other than Him; and the weak, whose first knowledge is of [His] acts, and then they ascend from them to the Agent. To the first points His saying, exalted be He: {أو لم يكف بربك أنه على كل شيء شهيد} [Is it not sufficient concerning your Lord that He is over all things a Witness], and His saying, exalted be He: {«شهد الله أنه لا إله إلا هو»} [God bears witness that there is no god but He]. And of this kind is the saying of one of them, when it was said to him: "By what have you known your Lord?" He said: "I have known my Lord — and were it not for my Lord, I would not have known my Lord."
67:3.section_title_en: The Two Paths to Knowledge and Love: The Higher Way of Witnessing the Truth and the Easier Way of Contemplating Creation
67:3.anchors:
- Root: طيب (ṭ-y-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Pure, good, wholesome; free from defilement
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): That which is pure and agreeable in both sensory and intellectual registers; the "good word" (al-kalim al-ṭayyib) is the declaration of divine unity
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal for sensory purity; metaphorical for spiritual purity of heart and speech
- Root: عرف (ʿ-r-f)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To know by reflection and discernment of traces/effects
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Maʿrifah is knowledge of God attained through contemplation of His effects, not through direct apprehension of His essence; it is more specific than ʿilm
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: to recognize someone; metaphorical: knowledge of God through His signs
- Root: شهد (sh-h-d)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To witness, testify, be present
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Bearing witness to the truth of something based on direct presence or evidence
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: ocular presence; metaphorical: intellectual certitude
- Root: نظر (n-ẓ-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To look, gaze, contemplate
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Contemplative reflection (naẓar) directed toward creation to derive knowledge of the Creator
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: visual perception; metaphorical: intellectual consideration and inference
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — used to restrict the purpose of works to purification of the heart, and to restrict the ultimate end to knowledge of unveiling
67:3.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Love, Longing, Intimacy and Contentment'

68:48.arabic: وقيل له فاصبر لحكم ربك ولا تكن كصاحب الحوت إذ نادى وهو مكظوم وهذه الاختلافات بعضها لاختلاف الأحوال والمقامات وبعضها لما سبق في الأزل من التفاضل والتفاوت في القسمة بين العباد وقد قال تعالى ولقد فضلنا بعض النبين على بعض وقد قال منهم من كلم الله ورفع بعضهم درجات فكان عيسى عليه السلام من المفضلين ولإدلاله سلم على نفسه فقال والسلام علي يوم ولدت ويوم أموت ويوم أبعث حيا وهذا انبساط منه لما شاهد من اللطف في مقام الأنس وأما يحيى بن زكريا عليه السلام فإنه أقيم مقام الهيبة والحياء فلم ينطق حتى أثنى عليه خالقه فقال
68:48.english: As for Adam (peace be upon him), it was said concerning him: {«وعصى آدم ربه فغوى»} "And Adam disobeyed his Lord, so he went astray" (Q. 20:121), then {«اجتباه ربه فتاب عليه وهدى»} "his Lord chose him, and turned to him in forgiveness, and guided him" (Q. 20:122).
68:48.section_title_en: On the Varieties of Divine Proximity (Al-Inbisāṭ) and Awe (Al-Haybah) in the States of the Prophets and Saints
68:48.anchors:
- Root: بسط (B-S-T)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning is "to spread out, extend, expand" — both physically (basting a garment) and metaphorically.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: "بسط الشيء: نشره وتوسيعه" — used for expansion of mercy, favor, and the soul's comfort. In Kalam, it contrasts with *qabḍ* (contraction/withholding).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): "بسط الثوب والفراش إذا نشره." Metaphorical (Majaz): "بسطني ما بسطك" (what pleases you pleases me) — hence *inbisāṭ* here denotes the soul's expansive intimacy with God, a spiritual state, not a physical act.
- Root: أبلس (B-L-S)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "أبلس: انقطعت حجته ويئس" — to be reduced to silence, to despair.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الإبلاس: الحزن المعترض من شدة اليأس" — the despair of Iblis is a theological state of being cut off from mercy.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: despair/silence. Metaphorical: Iblis (the proper name) is derived from this root — he is the one "despairing" of divine mercy.

83:18.arabic: فقال إن كتاب الأبرار لفي عليين {ثم قال} يشهده المقربون فكان أمارة علو كتابهم أنه ارتفع إلى حيث يشهده المقربون وكما أن الأبرار يجدون المزيد في حالهم ومعرفتهم بقربهم من المقربين ومشاهدتهم لهم فكذلك يكون حالهم في الآخرة ما خلقكم ولا بعثكم إلا كنفس واحدة كما بدأنا أول خلق نعيده وكما قال تعالى جزاء وفاقا أي وافق الجزاء أعمالهم فقوبل الخالص بالصرف من الشراب وقوبل المشوب بالمشوب وشوب كل شراب على قدر ما سبق من الشوب في حبه وأعماله فمن يعمل مثقال ذرة خيرا يره ومن يعمل مثقال ذرة شرا ير
83:18.english:
...twenty years.
And al-Junayd said: "The mark of the lover is the constancy of vigor and cheerfulness with a passion that wearies his body but does not weary his heart."
And some of them said: "Labor borne out of love — languor does not enter into it."
And one of the scholars said: "By God, no lover of God is ever fully quenched by His obedience, even if he were to attain to the most immense of means."
All of this and its like is found in observable experience, for the passionate lover does not find burdensome the pursuit of his beloved's desire, and he savors with his heart the service of the beloved even if it is arduous upon his body. And whenever his body falls short, the dearest of things to him is that his capacity should return to him and that incapacity should depart from him, so that he may occupy himself with it. Such, likewise, is the love of God the Exalted — for every love that becomes dominant inevitably subdues whatever is beneath it. So whoever's beloved is dearer to him than his sloth abandons sloth in serving him; and if the beloved is dearer to him than his wealth, he spends his wealth in his love.
And it was said to one of the lovers — who had expended his very self and his wealth until nothing remained to him — "What was the cause of your state in love?" He said: "One day I heard a lover who had secluded himself with his beloved, saying: 'By God, I love you with my whole heart, while you turn away from me with your whole face.' The beloved said to him: 'If you truly love me, what will you spend upon me?' He said: 'O my master, I put you in possession of all that I own, and then I spend upon you my very spirit until it is destroyed.'" So I said: "This is a creature loving a creature, and a slave loving a slave — how then with slaves loving the Worshipped One?" All of this is by His cause.
And among them is that he be compassionate toward all of God's servants, merciful to them, and severe against all of God's enemies — and against everyone who commits something of what God dislikes — as God the Exalted said: {«أشداء على الكفار رحماء بينهم»} "Harsh against the disbelievers, merciful among themselves." No reproach of any reproacher seizes him, and no diverting force turns him from wrath for God's sake. With this God described His friends, saying: "Those who are enamored with My love as a child is enamored with a thing, and who take refuge in My remembrance as the eagle takes refuge in its nest, and who rage for the sake of My sanctities as the leopard rages when provoked — for then he cares not whether the people are few or many."
So consider this example: the child, when enamored with a thing, does not part from it at all; if it is taken from him, he has no occupation but weeping and crying out until it is returned to him. If he sleeps, he takes it with him into his clothes; when he awakens, he returns and clings to it. Whenever he is parted from it, he weeps; whenever he finds it, he laughs. Whoever contends with him over it, he hates; whoever gives it to him, he loves. As for the leopard, he does not master himself at the moment of rage, until he reaches such a pitch of fury that he destroys himself. These, then, are the marks of love. Whoever's marks are perfected in him, his love is perfected and his affection is purified — so in the Hereafter his drink is clear and his draught is sweet.
But whoever's love is mingled with the love of other than God, he delights in the Hereafter in proportion to his love, for his drink is mingled with a measure of the drink of the Near Ones (al-muqarrabūn), as God the Exalted said concerning the righteous (al-abrār): {«إن الأبرار لفي نعيم»} "Verily the righteous are in bliss," {ثم قال} then He said: {«يسقون من رحيق مختوم * ختامه مسك وفي ذلك فليتنافس المتنافسون * ومزاجه من تسنيم * عينا يشرب بها المقربون»} "They are given to drink of sealed nectar, whose seal is musk — and in that let the competitors compete — and its mixture is of tasnīm, a spring from which the Near Ones drink." So when the drink of the righteous is sweetened by the admixture of the pure drink which belongs to the Near Ones...
And "drink" is an expression for the totality of the bliss of the Gardens, just as the Book expressed by it all deeds, for He said: {«إن كتاب الأبرار لفي عليين»} "Verily the book of the righteous is in 'Illiyyūn," {ثم قال} then He said: {«يشهده المقربون»} "The Near Ones bear witness to it." So it was a sign of the loftiness of their book that it ascended to where the Near Ones bear witness to it. And just as the righteous find increase in their state and their knowledge by their proximity to the Near Ones and their beholding of them, so likewise is their state in the Hereafter — {«ما خلقكم ولا بعثكم إلا كنفس واحدة»} "Your creation and your resurrection are but as a single soul," just as He said — as we began the first creation, We shall repeat it — and as the Exalted said: {«جزاء وفاقا»} "A recompense fully matching" — that is, the recompense matched their deeds. So the pure was met with the unmixed of the drink, and the mingled was met with the mingled.
And the admixture of every drink is in proportion to what preceded of admixture in his love and his deeds. For {«من يعمل مثقال ذرة خيرا يره * ومن يعمل مثقال ذرة شرا يره»} "Whoever does an atom's weight of good shall see it, and whoever does an atom's weight of evil shall see it." And {«إن الله لا يغير ما بقوم حتى يغيروا ما بأنفسهم * إن الله لا يظلم مثقال ذرة وإن تك حسنة يضاعفها وإن كان مثقال حبة من خردل أتينا بها وكفى بنا حاسبين»} "Verily God does not change what is in a people until they change what is in themselves. Verily God does not wrong an atom's weight; and if it be a good deed, He multiplies it, and if it be a grain of mustard-seed, We bring it — and sufficient are We as reckoners."
So whoever's love in this world was his hope for the bliss of the Garden, the wide-eyed houris, and the palaces — he is granted the Garden to settle therein wherever he wishes, to sport with the immortal youths and take pleasure with the women. There his delight in the Hereafter reaches its end, because every man is given in love only what his soul desires and his eye delights in.
But whoever's aim was the Lord of the Abode and the Owner of the Kingdom, and nothing overcame him save His love with sincerity and truthfulness — he is lodged in the seat...
83:18.section_title_en: The Marks of True Love and the Degrees of the Hereafter
83:18.anchors:
- Root: نشط (n-sh-ṭ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of vitality, energy, and alacrity in action.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Activity of the soul (nafs) in pursuing what it loves, unflagging in its ardor.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: bodily vigor; Metaphorical: the heart's persistent zeal that overrides physical exhaustion.
- Root: شرب (sh-r-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Drinking; the act of imbibing liquids.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In Quranic usage, a metaphor (majaz) for the soul's reception of spiritual bliss and states.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical quenching; Metaphorical: the tasting of paradisiacal delight, graded by purity (safā') versus admixture (shawb).
- Root: صفو (ṣ-f-w)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Purity, clarity, and freedom from turbidity or mixture.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The unalloyed state of sincere love (mahabbah) and its corresponding reward.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: clear liquid; Metaphorical: the soul's exclusive devotion to God, yielding unmixed bliss.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — Used to delimit the final reward strictly by the object and purity of one's love, as in "إنما يعطى كل إنسان في المحبة ما تشتهيه نفسه."

  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: bodily vigor; Metaphorical: the heart's persistent zeal that overrides physical exhaustion.
- Root: شرب (sh-r-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Drinking; the act of imbibing liquids.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In Quranic usage, a metaphor (majaz) for the soul's reception of spiritual bliss and states.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical quenching; Metaphorical: the tasting of paradisiacal delight, graded by purity (safā') versus admixture (shawb).
- Root: صفو (ṣ-f-w)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Purity, clarity, and freedom from turbidity or mixture.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The unalloyed state of sincere love (mahabbah) and its corresponding reward.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: clear liquid; Metaphorical: the soul's exclusive devotion to God, yielding unmixed bliss.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — Used to delimit the final reward strictly by the object and purity of one's love, as in "إنما يعطى كل إنسان في المحبة ما تشتهيه نفسه."
83:25.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Love, Longing, Intimacy and Contentment'

89:6.arabic: تر كيف فعل ربك بعاد إرم ذات العماد ألم تر كيف فعل ربك بأصحاب الفيل ولايعدو القرآن هذه الأقسام الثلاثة وهي الإرشاد إلى معرفة ذات الله وتقديسه أو معرفة صفاته وأسمائه أو معرفة أفعاله وسنته مع عباده ولما اشتملت سورة الإخلاص على أحد هذه الأقسام الثلاثة وهو التقديس وازنها رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بثلث القرآن فقال من قرأ سورة الإخلاص فقد قرأ ثلث القرآن (1) حديث دعائه لابن عباس اللهم فقهه في الدين وعلمه التأويل متفق عليه دون قوله وعلمه التأويل ورواه أحمد بهذه الزيادة وتقدم في العلم ###
89:6.english: And in the report [it is said]: Verily God—exalted is He—revealed to a servant whom He had taken by the hand after he had been on the brink of destruction: "How many a sin did you commit against Me, and I forgave it for you—sins for the sake of which I destroyed entire nations among the nations!" So this is the way (sunnah) of God—exalted is He—with His servants, by way of favor (tafḍīl), and bringing forward (taqdīm), and deferring (taʾkhīr), according to what the eternal will (al-mashīʾah al-azaliyyah) had previously decreed.
89:6.section_title_en: On the Meaning of Contentment with God's Decree (Al-Riḍā bi Qaḍāʾ Allāh), Its Reality, and What Has Been Reported Concerning Its Virtue
89:6.anchors:
- Root: رضي (Raḍā)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of being pleased, satisfied, consenting; the opposite of anger (sakhaṭ). Its object is that which is agreeable and harmonious with one's will.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Raḍā is a state of the heart (ḥāl min aḥwāl al-qalb) signifying the soul's inclination toward what is pleasing, and its cessation of opposition. In theological terms, it is the soul's acquiescence to the divine decree (qaḍāʾ) after the removal of inner resistance.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): "رَضِيَ عَنْهُ" — to be content with someone. Metaphorical (majāz): "رَضِيَ بِالكَوْنِ" — submission to what is, even when it opposes the appetites, which is the higher spiritual usage.
- Root: قضي (Qaḍā)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To decree, determine, execute, or finish a matter; the cutting off of a thing decisively.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Qaḍāʾ is the divine determination (taqdīr) and execution of affairs according to prior eternal knowledge; it encompasses both what is feared and what is hoped for.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the completion of a judgment. Metaphorical: the divine decree as the all-encompassing will of God, which the believer must embrace.
- Root: ولي (Waliya)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Nearness, guardianship, and governance; the one who manages affairs.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Walī is the one who is near to God through obedience, and God is the Walī of the believer through grace and protection.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: proximity. Metaphorical: friendship and divine patronage.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Predicate Emphasis (Bāb al-Taʾkīd bi al-Ḍamīr al-Munfaṣil) — The repetition of the pronoun for emphasis, as in "اللهُ هُوَ" structures, to affirm the exclusivity of divine attributes without ambiguity.
89:6.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'Love, Longing, Intimacy and Contentment'

112:4.arabic: بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم أعيذك بالله الأحد الصمد الذي لم يلد ولم يولد ولم يكن له كفوا أحد من شر ما تجد قالها مرارا (6) ودخل صلى الله عليه وسلم على علي بن أبي طالب رضي الله عنه وهو مريض فقال له قل اللهم إني أسألك تعجيل عافيتك أو صبرا على بليتك أو خروجا من الدنيا إلى رحمتك فإنك ستعطي إحداهن (7) ويستحب للعليل أيضا أن يقول أعوذ بعزة الله وقدرته من شر ما أجد وأحاذر وقال علي بن أبي طالب رضي الله عنه إذا شكا أحدكم بطنه فليسأل امرأته شيئا من صداقها ويشتري به عسلا ويشربه بماء السماء فيجتمع له الهنيء والمريء والشفاء P
112:4.english: A man defended him, and the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: "Whoever defends the honor of his brother shall have it as a shield for him against the Fire." (1)
112:4.anchors:
- Root: رد (r-d-d)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To return, repel, defend, avert; al-radd ʿan al-ʿirḍ is to repel defamation from one's honor
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Defense against false accusation; the theological nuance of divine recompense (al-mukāfaʾah) for defending a brother's honor
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal repulsion of physical harm extended metaphorically to verbal defense of honor (ḥaqīqah vs. majāz)
- Root: عطس (ʿ-t-s)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Sneezing; al-tashmīt is the invocation of mercy upon the sneezer
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The sneeze is attributed to God (min Allāh) as a sign of divine favor, while yawning is attributed to Satan
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): The response "yarḥamukallāh" is a supplication, not an assertion — distinguishing literal invocation from mere congratulation
- Root: عاد (ʿ-w-d)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To visit repeatedly; al-ʿiyādah is the visitation of the sick
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Returning to someone in his affliction; the reward is measured by the intensity of compassion shown
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): The "return" (ʿawd) is literal in visitation, but the reward is spiritual — a metaphorical extension of recompense
- Root: شيع (sh-y-ʿ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To accompany, follow; al-tashyīʿ is the funeral procession
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Following the bier with the intention of honoring the deceased and taking admonition (al-iʿtibār)
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): The qīrāṭ is a measure of reward — metaphorical weight, not literal coin
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Conditional Protasis (Bāb al-sharṭ) — The construction "man ... fa-..." (whoever does X, then Y) establishes a causal nexus requiring the apodosis to be a new sentence, often carrying the force of divine decree.
