2:243.arabic: كمن قال الله تعالى فيهم ألم تر إلى الذين خرجوا من ديارهم وهم ألوف حذر الموت فرجعوا إلى عمر فسألوه عن رأيه فقال نرجع ولا ندخل على الوباء فقال له المخالفون في رأيه أنفر من قدر الله تعالى قال عمر نعم نفر من قدر الله إلى قدر الله ثم ضرب لهم مثلا فقال أرأيتم لو كان لأحدكم غنم فهبط واديا له شعبتان: إحداهما مخصبة: والأخرى مجدبة أليس إن رعى المخصبة رعاها بقدر الله تعالى وإن رعى المجدبة رعاها بقدر الله تعالى فقالوا: نعم ثم طلب عبد الرحمن بن عوف ليسأله عن رأيه وكان غائبا فلما أصبحوا جاء عبد الرحمن فسأله عمر عن ذلك فقال:
2:243.english: If someone were to say: "The Messenger of God, peace be upon him, only did this (i.e., used medicine) to establish the precedent for others — otherwise, it is the way of the weak; whereas the station of the strong necessitates trust in God (tawakkul) by abandoning medicine" — then it is said to him: It would follow that abandoning cupping (ḥijāmah) and venesection (faṣd) at the time of blood excess should also be a condition of trust in God.
2:243.section_title_en: The Subtle Distinction Between Trust in God and the Use of Means — The Plague Narrative and the Prophet's Example
2:243.anchors:
- Root: وبأ (waba')
  * Lisan / Ayn: [Pestilence, widespread deadly disease; from 'wabi'a' — land afflicted with plague]
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): [Divine affliction sent as trial; carries theological weight of predestined calamity]
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): [Literal: epidemic illness; Metaphorical: the 'sting' of destiny penetrating the land]
- Root: فرر (farara)
  * Lisan / Ayn: [Flight, escape from danger]
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): [Contrasted with 'firar min al-zahf' (flight from battle ranks) — a grave sin; here nuanced as permissible avoidance]
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): [Literal: physical fleeing; Metaphorical: fleeing from one decree of God to another decree of God]
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الاستفهام التقريري (Interrogative of Acquiescence — 'a-laysa...'): [Rhetorical question demanding assent, used by 'Umar to establish the parity of all divinely ordained means]
2:243.topic: Al-Ghazali on the journey of the soul, death, and the Hereafter, from 'Monotheism and Reliance'

2:260.arabic: السلام {أو لم تؤمن قال بلى ولكن ليطمئن قلبي} فالتمس أن يكون مشاهدا إحياء الميت بعينه ليثبت في خياله فإن النفس تتبع الخيال وتطمئن به ولا تطمئن باليقين في ابتداء أمرها إلى أن تبلغ بالآخرة إلى درجة النفس المطمئنة وذلك لا يكون في البداية أصلا وكم من مطمئن لا يقين له كسائر أرباب الملل والمذاهب فإن اليهودي مطمئن القلب إلى تهوده وكذا النصراني ولا يقين لهم أصلا وإنما يتبعون الظن وما تهوى الأنفس ولقد جاءهم من ربهم الهدى وهو سبب اليقين إلا أنهم معرضون عنه فإذن الجبن والجراءة غرائز ولا ينفع اليقين مع
2:260.english: So when you have understood tawakkul in this example, then measure upon it the tawakkul upon Allah — exalted be He. For if there is established in your soul — through unveiling (kashf) or through decisive belief (iʿtiqād jāzim) — that there is no agent (fāʿil) except Allah, as has preceded; and you believe, along with that, in the completeness of [His] knowledge and power (al-ʿilm wa al-qudrah) sufficient for the servants; then the completeness of [His] care, affection, and mercy (al-ʿināyah wa al-ʿaṭf wa al-raḥmah) toward all the servants and each individual; and that there is no power beyond the limit of His power, no knowledge beyond the limit of His knowledge, and no care and mercy beyond the limit of His care for you and His mercy to you — then your heart will inevitably rely upon Him alone, and will not turn to any other in any respect, nor to itself, nor to its own might and strength. For there is no might and no power except through Allah (lā ḥawla wa lā quwwata illā billāh), as has preceded in [the book of] Tawḥīd at the mention of movement and power — for "might" (al-ḥawl) is an expression for movement, and "power" (al-quwwah) is an expression for capability (al-qudrah).
2:260.section_title_en: The Reality of Tawakkul — The Interplay of Certainty (Yaqīn), Heart's Stillness (Ṭuma'nīnah), and the Four Attributes of the Trustee (Al-Wakīl)
2:260.anchors:
- Root: وكل (W-K-L)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of delegating, entrusting, and appointing a deputy (wakīl) to act on one's behalf; the wakīl is the one relied upon for a task.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Tawakkul is to rely upon another and make him a deputy over your affair; true tawakkul on Allah is to deem Him sufficient (ḥasbunā Allāh) as the sole Guardian of your state.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) usage is delegation of a concrete task; metaphorical (majāz) usage is the heart's utter dependence on the trustee, even to the point of describing a weak man as "tikl" (one who leans entirely on others).
- Root: قلب (Q-L-B)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The heart as the organ of constant turning and overturning (taqlīb); its states fluctuate and shift.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Qalb is the turning of a thing from one state to another; the heart's "turning" (inqilāb) is its movement between conditions of fear, hope, certainty, and agitation.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: to flip a thing over; metaphorical: the heart's disposition is "turned" by overwhelming fancies (awhām) and fears, just as a merchant "turns over" goods to inspect their true condition.
- Root: نفس (N-F-S)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The self or soul; that which is the seat of inclination and emotional response.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The soul (nafs) is the subtle spiritual reality (laṭīfah) that follows imagination (khayāl) and finds rest only through it; the "tranquil soul" (al-nafs al-muṭma'innah) is its final perfected state.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the self as animate essence; metaphorical: the soul's "flowing out" (nafāsah) as preciousness, and its agitation as a type of "breathlessness" from fear.
- Root: يقن (Y-Q-N)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Certainty as the absence of doubt; firm conviction.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Yaqīn is a quality of knowledge above mere cognition (ma'rifah); it is the stillness of understanding with the fixity of judgment — as in "knowledge of certainty" (ʿilm al-yaqīn), "eye of certainty" (ʿayn al-yaqīn), and "truth of certainty" (ḥaqq al-yaqīn).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: to be certain of a matter (yaqina al-amr); it is the firmest form of knowing, distinct from mere opinion (ẓann).
- Sibawayh Rule: Restriction and Focused Predication (al-ḥaṣr wa al-taqyīd bi-innamā) — The sentence "فالسكون في القلب شيء واليقين شيء آخر" (Stillness in the heart is one thing, and certainty is another thing) uses two nominal sentences with contrastive focus to establish a strict ontological distinction between two distinct realities (ṭuma'nīnah vs. yaqīn), each with its own predicate, preventing conflation.
2:260.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Monotheism and Reliance'

4:143.arabic: فما أراك إلا مخنثا بين فحولة التنزيه وأنوثة التشبيه مذبذبا بين هذا وذا لا إلى هؤلاء ولا إلى هؤلاء فكيف نزهت ذاته وصفاته تعالى عن الأجسام وصفاتها ونزهت كلامه عن معاني الحروف والأصوات وأخذت تتوقف في يده وقلمه ولوحه وخطه فإن كنت قد فهمت من قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم إن الله خلق آدم على صورته الصورة الظاهرة المدركة بالبصر فكن مشبها مطلقا كما يقال كن يهوديا صرفا وإلا فلا تلعب بالتوراة وإن فهمت منه الصورة الباطنة التي تدرك بالبصائر لا بالأبصار فكن منزها صرفا ومقدسا فحلا واطو الطريق فإنك بالواد المقدس طوى واستمع بسر قلبك لما يوحى فلعلك تجد على النار ه
4:143.english: The Seeker (al-sālik) then said: "I have opened my eye and sharpened its gaze. By God, I see neither reed nor wood, nor do I know any pen except in that manner."
4:143.section_title_en: A Door from the Doors of the Kingdom Unveiled by the Pen
4:143.anchors:
- Root: قلم (Qalam)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The reed/implement of writing; also the clipping of something hard (nail, spear-shaft, reed). Al-Farahidi: "القلم: ما كتب به."
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The Pen is a corporeal instrument, yet in divine attribution it is stripped of material composition—its reality is spiritual (ma'nawī), not wooden or reed-like.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (haqiqah) = writing implement; metaphorical (majaz) = the divine pen as a subtle reality (laṭīfah) in the malakūt, transcending physical attributes.
- Root: علم (ʿIlm)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Perception of a thing by its true nature; knowledge as a divine gift.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): ʿIlm is "إدراك الشيء بحقيقته" — apprehension of a thing's reality; here, the Pen writes sciences (ʿulūm) into hearts, not as ink on tablets but as immaterial impressions.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal = knowing facts; metaphorical = the unveiling (kashf) granted to the seeker, where knowledge becomes a living guide.
- Root: يمن (Yamin)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The right hand; blessing; oath.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Divine "right hand" (yamin) in {«والسماوات مطويات بيمينه»} is not a limb but a metaphor for divine power (qudrah), as with "hand" (yad) — see Al-Zamakhshari: "هو ملك يمينه" (He is the possessor of His right hand).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal = physical hand; metaphorical = sovereign power and disposal, as in "ضربها بالميمون" (euphemism for union).
- Root: قلب (Qalb)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Turning, overturning; the heart as the seat of fluctuating perception.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Qalb = "تصريفه وصرفه عن وجه إلى وجه" — the heart is where the Pen inscribes, and it turns between tanzih (transcendence) and tashbih (assimilation).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal = physical heart; metaphorical = the inner faculty (basirah) that perceives the malakūt.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — Used in "إنما الفرق في ظاهر الصورة" to restrict difference to outward form alone, negating any difference in the reality of subjugation (taskhir).

5:23.arabic: أما من الآيات فقد قال تعالى وعلى الله فتوكلوا إن كنتم مؤمنين وقال عز وجل وعلى الله فليتوكل المتوكلون وقال تعالى ومن يتوكل على الله فهو حسبه وقال سبحانه وتعالى إن الله يحب المتوكلين وأعظم بمقام موسوم بمحبة الله تعالى صاحبه ومضمون كفاية الله تعالى ملابسه فمن الله تعالى حسبه وكافيه ومحبه ومراعيه فقد فاز الفوز العظيم فإن المحبوب لا يعذب ولا يبعد ولا يحجب وقال تعالى أليس الله بكاف عبده فطالب الكفاية من غيره والتارك للتوكل هو المكذب لهذه الآية فإنه سؤال في معرض استنطاق بالحق كقوله تعالى هل أتى على الإنسان
5:23.english: Praise be to God, the Disposer of the dominion (mulk) and the spiritual sovereignty (malakūt), the One alone in majesty (ʿizzah) and omnipotence (jabarūt), Who raised the heaven without any pillar, and apportioned therein the provisions of His servants; Who turned the eyes of those possessed of hearts and intellects away from the observation of intermediaries and causes (al-wasāʾiṭ wa-l-asbāb) toward the Causer of causes (musabbib al-asbāb); and Who lifted their concern from turning toward anything other than Him, and from relying upon any disposer besides Him. Thus they worshipped none but Him alone — in knowledge that He is the One, the Unique, the Eternal Refuge (al-ṣamad), the God — and in verification that all classes of creatures are servants like themselves, from whom no provision is sought, and that there is no atom but God created it, and no beast but upon God is its sustenance. When they verified that He is the Guarantor of His servants' provision and the Surety for it, they relied upon Him and said: {«حسبنا الله ونعم الوكيل»} — "God is sufficient for us, and what an excellent Guardian!" (Q. 3:173).

5:23.anchors:
- Root: وكل (w-k-l)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of delegating, entrusting, and appointing a deputy (wakīl) to manage one's affairs.

  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): appointing an agent; Metaphorical (majāz): the weak man who leans on others (وكل ووكلة تكلة). In the divine context, tawakkul is a real, not figurative, transfer of one's trust to God as the sole efficient cause.
- Root: سبب (s-b-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: A rope, cord, or means by which one ascends or reaches something; extended to any intermediary cause.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "سمي كل ما يتوصل به إلى شيء سببا" — Every means by which one reaches a goal is termed a cause (sabab); God is the "Musabbib al-Asbāb" (Causer of causes), transcending the causal ropes He suspends.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: a physical cord; Metaphorical: any linkage or connection. Here, the "gaze upon causes" (mulāḥaẓat al-asbāb) is a metaphorical veiling of the true Agent.

  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: reckoning by number; Metaphorical: "احتسبت ما عند فلان: اختبرته وسبرته" — to test and probe. God's being "Ḥasb" for the believer is a tested, verified sufficiency, not a mere claim.
- Root: غمض (gh-m-d)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To close the eye, to be obscure, low-lying, or hidden ground.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "يستعار للتغافل والتساهل" — closing the eye is metaphorically used for overlooking; here, the "ghumūḍ" (obscurity) of tawakkul is its conceptual hiddenness from the intellect.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: a low, concealed place; Metaphorical: "أمر غامض" — a subtle, difficult affair. The text uses it for the doctrinal opacity of tawakkul.

6:46.arabic: رزقك بالمغازل أرأيت إن أخذ الله سمعك وبصرك الرزق على من فوقع ذلك في قلبه فأخرج آلة المغازل من يده وتركها وقيل تركها لما نوهت باسمه وقصد لأجلها وقيل فعل ذلك لما مات عياله كما كان لسفيان خمسون دينارا يتجر فيها فلما مات عياله فرقها فإن قلت فكيف يتصور أن يكون له بضاعة ولا يسكن إليها وهو يعلم أن الكسب بغير بضاعة لا يمكن فأقول بأن يعلم أن الذين يرزقهم الله تعالى بغير بضاعة فيهم كثرة وأن الذين كثرت بضاعتهم فسرقت وهلكت فيهم كثرة وأن يوطن نفسه على أن الله لا يفعل به إلا ما فيه صلاحه فإن أهلك
6:46.english: If you say: "What is more excellent — that a man sit in his house, or go out and earn?" — Know that if he is able to devote himself fully, by abandoning earning, to reflection, remembrance (dhikr), sincerity (ikhlāṣ), and the complete occupation of his time with worship, and earning would disturb that for him — and while he is in this state, his soul does not yearn expectantly toward people, waiting for someone to enter upon him and bring him something — but rather he is strong-hearted in patience and reliance upon God most High — then the intended goal (al-maqṣūd) is more appropriate for him. But if his heart is agitated in the house and he yearns expectantly toward people, then earning is more appropriate, because the heart's yearning toward people is a request made by the heart, and abandoning that is more important than abandoning earning.
6:46.section_title_en: On the Superiority of Earning vs. Seclusion, and the Signs of True Reliance (Tawakkul)
6:46.anchors:
- Root: كسب (Kasaba)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning is seeking provision and acquiring benefit through effort; "الكسب: طلب الرزق" (earning is the seeking of sustenance).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Kasb is what one pursues for gain, applicable to both self and others; iktisāb is specifically for oneself. Al-Zamakhshari notes the literal sense is acquisition of wealth, while the metaphorical usage distinguishes "كسبت خيرا واكتسبت شرا" (earned good, acquired evil) — aligning with Ghazali's distinction between lawful earning and covetous accumulation.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah) — earning through trade or craft; Metaphorical (Majaz) — earning spiritual merit or blameworthy attachment to means.
- Root: قلب (Qalaba)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To turn, overturn, or transform a thing from one state to another.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "تصريفه وصرفه عن وجه إلى وجه" — the turning of a thing from one aspect to another; hence the heart (qalb) is so named for its constant fluctuation.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — physical overturning; Metaphorical — "قلب المعلم الصبيان" (the teacher dismissed the boys), and "رجل قلب" (a man who turns matters over, i.e., discerning). Here, Ghazali uses "قلبه" (his heart) and "يطمئن" (is tranquil) to denote the inner disposition of reliance versus agitation.
- Root: سكن (Sakana)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To be still, tranquil, or dwell; the opposite of agitation (iḍṭirāb).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Sakīnah is divine tranquility; sukūn denotes the absence of restless motion, both physical and spiritual.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — physical stillness; Metaphorical — the heart's repose in God, as opposed to "استشراف" (yearning/looking expectantly toward creatures).
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The rule permits separation between a governing verb and its governed prepositional phrase for rhetorical emphasis, as in Ghazali's periodic constructions like "فإن قلت فما الأفضل أن يقعد في بيته أو يخرج ويكتسب" where the conditional structure delays the apodosis for dramatic effect.

7:124.arabic: حقيقة الأمر فلم يكترثوا بقول فرعون لأقطعن أيديكم وأرجلكم من خلاف {بل} قالوا لن نؤثرك على ما جاءنا من البينات والذي فطرنا قاقض ما أنت قاض إنما تقضي هذه الحياة الدنيا فإن البيان والكشف يمنع التغيير وأما أصحاب السامري لما كان إيمانهم عن النظر إلى ظاهر الثعبان فلما نظروا إلى عجل السامري وسمعوا خواره تغيروا وسمعوا قوله هذا إلهكم وإله موسى ونسوا أنه لا يرجع إليهم قولا ولا يملك لهم ضرا ولا نفعا فكل من آمن بالنظر إلى ثعبان يكفر لا محالة إذا نظر إلى عجل لأن كليهما من عالم الشهادة والاختلاف والتضاد في عالم الشهادة كثير
7:124.english: ...its mover is Power (al-qudrah) without any doubt. So the seeker (al-sālik) journeyed on to the world of Power, and there he beheld wonders before which all that had preceded seemed contemptible. He asked Power concerning the movement of the right hand, and it said: "I am but an attribute (innamā anā ṣifah) — ask the Powerful One (al-Qādir), for the reliance is upon the described substances (al-mawṣūfāt), not upon the attributes." At that point he almost deviated and unleashed the tongue of questioning with audacity, but he was steadied by the firm word (al-qawl al-thābit), and a caller cried out from behind the veils of the pavilions of the Divine Presence: "He is not asked about what He does, but they shall be asked" {«لَا يُسْأَلُ عَمَّا يَفْعَلُ وَهُمْ يُسْأَلُونَ»}. Then the awe of the Presence overwhelmed him, and he fell down stricken, convulsing in his swoon. When he regained consciousness, he said: "Glory be to You — how magnificent is Your majesty! I repent unto You, and I place my trust in You, and I believe that You are the Sovereign, the Compeller, the One, the Subduer. I fear none but You, I hope for none other than You, and I seek refuge only in Your pardon from Your punishment, and in Your good pleasure from Your wrath. I have nothing but to ask of You and to supplicate before You, and to plead humbly in Your presence, saying: 'Expand my breast that I may know You, and loosen the knot from my tongue that I may praise You.'"
7:124.section_title_en: The Unification of the Acts — The Journey of the Seekers to the Oneness of the Agent
7:124.anchors:
- Root: قدر (q-d-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of measuring, determining, and empowering; al-Qadir as the One whose power is absolute and unbounded.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Power (qudrah) when ascribed to God is the negation of incapacity ('ajz); when ascribed to man it is a contingent capacity limited by divine ordainment.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (haqiqah) — "He is Qadir, Muqtadir, possessor of power"; metaphorical (majaz) — "a far-reaching steed" (ba'id al-qadr), indicating extension of effect.
- Root: وحد (w-ḥ-d)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Oneness and singularity; al-Wahid as that which has no part whatsoever.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): True unity (wahdah) is absolute indivisibility; applied to God exclusively in the sense of unique sovereignty.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "He is one (wahid), and they are singular (wuhdan)"; literal unity versus numerical oneness.
- Root: علم (ʿ-l-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Knowledge as perception of a thing's reality; the mark or sign by which something is known.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Knowledge ('ilm) is the apprehension of a thing in its true reality — either grasping the essence or judging its attributes.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — "I knew not of your news" (ma 'alimtu bi-khabarika); the knower as one marked by discernment.
- Sibawayh Rule: Restriction and Focused Predication (al-ḥaṣr wa al-taqyīd bi-innamā) — "Innamā anā ṣifah" (I am but an attribute) restricts the speaker's essence to being a mere accident, redirecting inquiry to the substantive subject (al-mawṣūf).

8:49.arabic: الدهر لم يكن شيئا مذكورا وقال عز وجل ومن يتوكل على الله فإن الله عزيز حكيم أي عزيز لا يذل من استجار به ولا يضيع من لاذ بجنا به والتجأ إلى

9:35.arabic: كيتين من النار كما قال تعالى تكوى بها جباههم وجنوبهم وظهورهم وذلك إذا كان حاله إظهار الزهد والفقر والتوكل مع الإفلاس عنه فهو نوع تلبيس والثاني أن لا يكون ذلك عن تلبيس فيكون المعنى به النقصان عن درجة كماله كما ينقص من جمال الوجه أثر كيتين في الوجه وذلك لا يكون عن تلبيس فإن كل ما يخلفه الرجل فهو نقصان عن درجته في الآخرة إذ لا يؤتى أحد من الدنيا شيئا إلا نقص بقدره من الآخرة وأما بيان أن الادخار مع فراغ القلب عن المدخر ليس من ضرورته بطلان التوكل فيشهد له ما روي عن بشر قال الحسين المغازلي من أصحابه كنت عنده
9:35.english: ...and its end. Those who possess ends are called "the foremost" (al-sābiqūn), and those who possess beginnings are called "the companions of the right" (aṣḥāb al-yamīn). Then the companions of the right also have degrees, and likewise the foremost; and the highest degrees of the companions of the right adjoin the lowest degrees of the foremost. So there is no meaning to precise estimation in such matters. Rather, the verified truth is that tawakkul (reliance on God) through abandoning provision-storing (tark al-iddikhār) is not perfected except by the shortening of hope (qaṣr al-amal). As for the total absence of hopes for survival, its being stipulated is remote — even in a single soul — for that is as if impossible to exist. As for people, they vary in the length and shortness of hope. The least degree of hope is a day and a night, and what is less than that of hours; and its utmost is what can be conceived to be a man's lifespan. Between these are degrees beyond enumeration. Whoever does not hope for more than a month is closer to the goal than one who hopes for a year. And restricting it to forty [days] on account of the appointed time of Moses (peace be upon him) is far-fetched, for that incident was not intended to clarify the measure of what hope has been permitted. Rather, Moses' worthiness to attain the promised [encounter] was not completed except after forty days, due to a secret by which — and by its like — the sunnah of God most High proceeds in the gradual unfolding of matters, just as he (peace be upon him) said: "Indeed God kneaded the clay of Adam with His hand for forty mornings" {«إن الله خمر طينة آدم بيده أربعين صباحا»} — because the worthiness of that clay for kneading was dependent upon a period reaching what was mentioned. Therefore, whatever is beyond a year is not stored except by virtue of the heart's weakness and its leaning toward the outward aspects of causes; such [storing] falls outside the station of tawakkul, [the person] not being confident in the encompassing governance of the True Deputy (al-wakīl al-ḥaqq) over the hidden dimensions of causes. For the means of income — through harvests and alms — recur with the recurrence of years, generally speaking. Whoever stores for less than a year has a degree proportionate to the shortness of his hope; and whoever's hope is two months — his degree is not like the degree of one who hopes for a month, nor the degree of one who hopes for three months; rather, he is between them in rank. Nothing prevents storing except the shortness of hope. So the most virtuous is that one not store at all — even if his heart is weak — for the less his storing, the greater his merit. It has been related concerning the poor man whom the Prophet (peace be upon him) commanded ʿAlī (may God honor his face) and Usāmah to wash — so they washed him and shrouded him in his own cloak. When he buried him, he said to his companions: "He will be raised on the Day of Resurrection with his face like the full moon on the night of the full moon; and were it not for one trait in him, he would be raised with his face like the radiant sun." We said: "And what is it, O Messenger of God?" He said: "He was a frequent faster, a frequent prayer-stancer, and abundant in the remembrance of God most High — except that when winter came, he stored the summer garment for his summer; and when summer came, he stored the winter garment for his winter." But if he senses within himself a restlessness that occupies his heart away from worship, remembrance, and reflection, then storing is more appropriate for him. Indeed, even if he held onto an estate whose income sufficed for his needs, and his heart would not be free except through it, then that is more appropriate for him — because the goal is the rectification of the heart so that it may be emptied for the remembrance of God. There is a person whom the existence of wealth occupies, and a person whom its absence occupies; and what is harmful is whatever occupies one away from God (mighty and majestic). Otherwise, this world in itself is not harmful — neither its existence nor its absence. For this reason, the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) was sent to all classes of creation, among them merchants, craftsmen, and people of trades and industries. He did not command the merchant to abandon his trade, nor the craftsman to abandon his craft, nor did he command the one who had abandoned both to occupy himself with them. Rather, he called everyone to God most High and guided them to the fact that their triumph and salvation lie in the turning of their hearts away from this world toward God most High. The pillar of occupation with God (mighty and majestic) is the heart. 19:17.arabic: فيها حبا وعنبا وقال عز وجل فأرسلنا إليها روحنا فتمثل لها بشرا سويا ثم قال تعالى فنفخنا فيها من روحنا وكان النافخ جبريل عليه السلام وكما قال تعالى فإذا قرأناه فاتبع قرآنه قيل في التفسير معناه إذا قرأه عليك جبريل وقال تعالى قاتلوهم يعذبهم الله بأيديكم فأضاف القتل إليهم والتعذيب إلى نفسه والتعذيب هو عين
19:17.english: Thus should you understand the issuance of determined things (al-maqdūrāt) from eternal power — even though the power is eternal (qadīmah) and the objects of power are originated (ḥādithah). And this is a knocking upon another door of another world among the worlds of unveilings (mukāshafāt). So let us leave all of that, for our purpose is only to alert to the path of unification (tawḥīd) in the act — for the agent in truth (al-fāʿil bi-al-ḥaqīqah) is One. He is the feared and the hoped, and upon Him is reliance and trust. And we have not been able to mention from the seas of tawḥīd save a drop from the ocean of the third station among the stations of tawḥīd. And exhausting that within the lifetime of Noah is impossible — like exhausting the water of the sea by taking droplets from it. And all of that is subsumed under the saying: "There is no god but God" (lā ilāha illā Allāh). How light is its burden upon the tongue, how easy is the belief in the meaning of its utterance upon the heart, and how precious is its reality and its kernel (lubbuhu) among the scholars firmly rooted in knowledge — so how [much more so] with others?
19:17.section_title_en: The Oneness of the Actor (Tawḥīd al-Fiʿl) — Reconciling Divine and Human Agency
19:17.anchors:
- Root: قدر (q-d-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root denotes measure, decree, and capacity; al-Farāhīdī anchors it in the physical act of measuring or sizing, extended to divine determining.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Al-qudrah" when ascribed to God negates incapacity (ʿajz) absolutely; when ascribed to man, it names a state (hayʾah) enabling a specific act — never absolute power, but restricted capacity over particular objects.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): "He is qādir, possessing power." Metaphorical (majāz): "faras baʿīd al-qadr" (a far-striding horse) — power's "reach" extended figuratively; here, divine power's "presence" with its objects is literal for God, metaphorical for creatures.
- Root: حدث (ḥ-d-th)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "Al-ḥudūth": coming-to-be after non-existence; al-ḥadath: ritual impurity (as in this text's water analogy); al-muḥdath: the originated thing.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Al-ḥudūth: the thing's being after it was not — whether accident or substance. Its iḥdāth (bringing-about) is exclusive to God." Creaturely acts are originated, but their origination is divine.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: recent, newly arisen. Metaphorical: "ʿUmar was muḥaddath" (inspired in judgment) — as if spoken to by unseen truth; here, the "newly arisen" (ḥādith) effect is tied to a condition (sharṭ), not a new power.
- Root: ماء (m-ā-ʾ)
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Water as the origin of life ({وجعلنا من الماء كل شيء حي}); its root is m-w-h, with hāʾ dropped and wāw shifted — a paradigm for how a thing's "presence" (mulāqāh) does not entail its "effect" (taʾthīr) absent a condition.
  * Kitab al-Ayn: Water's essence is unchanged; the analogy hinges on its constancy.
- Root: وجه (w-j-h)
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Al-wajh" is the face; then extended to the "foremost" or "noblest" part of any thing, and to the self (dhāt) in {ويبقى وجه ربك}. Here, "washing the face" is the specified condition (sharṭ) — the "foremost" ritual act — not the efficient cause of purification.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the bodily face. Metaphorical: "wajh al-qawm" (the leaders), "wajh al-thawb" (the surface of a garment) — the "face" as the operative locus; in the analogy, the face's washing is the trigger, not the agent.
- Sibawayh Rule: Al-Faṣl bayna al-jār wa-al-majrūr (Prepositional Interposition) — Governing principle: a dependent element (here, divine power's "attachment" to objects) can be separated from its governor by an intervening condition, just as grammatical separation is permissible when the intervening clause is complete; analogically, the "link" (irṭibāṭ) of power to its effect is mediated by conditions without altering the agent's nature.

20:27.arabic: وأبتهل بين يديك فأقول اشرح لي صدري لأعرفك واحلل عقدة من لساني لأثني عليك فنودي من وراء الحجاب إياك أن تطمع في الثناء وتزيد على سيد الأنبياء بل ارجع إليه فما آتاك فخذه وما نهاك عنه فانته عنه وما قاله لك فقله فإنه ما زاد في هذه الحضرة على أن قال سبحانك لا أحصي ثناء عليك أنت كما أثنيت على نفسك (1) فقال إلهي إن لم يكن للسان جراءة على الثناء عليك فهل للقلب مطمع في معرفتك فنودي إياك أن تتخطى رقاب الصديقين فارجع إلى الصديق الأكبر فاقتد به فإن أصحاب سيد الأنبياء كالنجوم بأيهم اقتديتم اهتديتم أما سمعته يقول العجز ع
20:27.english: ...its mover is Power (al-qudrah) without any doubt. So the seeker (al-sālik) journeyed on to the world of Power, and there he beheld wonders before which all that had preceded seemed contemptible. He asked Power concerning the movement of the right hand, and it said: "I am but an attribute (innamā anā ṣifah) — ask the Powerful One (al-Qādir), for the reliance is upon the described substances (al-mawṣūfāt), not upon the attributes." At that point he almost deviated and unleashed the tongue of questioning with audacity, but he was steadied by the firm word (al-qawl al-thābit), and a caller cried out from behind the veils of the pavilions of the Divine Presence: "He is not asked about what He does, but they shall be asked" {«لَا يُسْأَلُ عَمَّا يَفْعَلُ وَهُمْ يُسْأَلُونَ»}. Then the awe of the Presence overwhelmed him, and he fell down stricken, convulsing in his swoon. When he regained consciousness, he said: "Glory be to You — how magnificent is Your majesty! I repent unto You, and I place my trust in You, and I believe that You are the Sovereign, the Compeller, the One, the Subduer. I fear none but You, I hope for none other than You, and I seek refuge only in Your pardon from Your punishment, and in Your good pleasure from Your wrath. I have nothing but to ask of You and to supplicate before You, and to plead humbly in Your presence, saying: 'Expand my breast that I may know You, and loosen the knot from my tongue that I may praise You.'"
20:27.section_title_en: The Unification of the Acts — The Journey of the Seekers to the Oneness of the Agent
20:27.anchors:
- Root: قدر (q-d-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of measuring, determining, and empowering; al-Qadir as the One whose power is absolute and unbounded.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Power (qudrah) when ascribed to God is the negation of incapacity ('ajz); when ascribed to man it is a contingent capacity limited by divine ordainment.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (haqiqah) — "He is Qadir, Muqtadir, possessor of power"; metaphorical (majaz) — "a far-reaching steed" (ba'id al-qadr), indicating extension of effect.
- Root: وحد (w-ḥ-d)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Oneness and singularity; al-Wahid as that which has no part whatsoever.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): True unity (wahdah) is absolute indivisibility; applied to God exclusively in the sense of unique sovereignty.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "He is one (wahid), and they are singular (wuhdan)"; literal unity versus numerical oneness.
- Root: علم (ʿ-l-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Knowledge as perception of a thing's reality; the mark or sign by which something is known.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Knowledge ('ilm) is the apprehension of a thing in its true reality — either grasping the essence or judging its attributes.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — "I knew not of your news" (ma 'alimtu bi-khabarika); the knower as one marked by discernment.
- Sibawayh Rule: Restriction and Focused Predication (al-ḥaṣr wa al-taqyīd bi-innamā) — "Innamā anā ṣifah" (I am but an attribute) restricts the speaker's essence to being a mere accident, redirecting inquiry to the substantive subject (al-mawṣūf).
20:27.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Monotheism and Reliance'

20:72.arabic: حقيقة الأمر فلم يكترثوا بقول فرعون لأقطعن أيديكم وأرجلكم من خلاف {بل} قالوا لن نؤثرك على ما جاءنا من البينات والذي فطرنا قاقض ما أنت قاض إنما تقضي هذه الحياة الدنيا فإن البيان والكشف يمنع التغيير وأما أصحاب السامري لما كان إيمانهم عن النظر إلى ظاهر الثعبان فلما نظروا إلى عجل السامري وسمعوا خواره تغيروا وسمعوا قوله هذا إلهكم وإله موسى ونسوا أنه لا يرجع إليهم قولا ولا يملك لهم ضرا ولا نفعا فكل من آمن بالنظر إلى ثعبان يكفر لا محالة إذا نظر إلى عجل لأن كليهما من عالم الشهادة والاختلاف والتضاد في عالم الشهادة كثير وأما عالم الملكوت فهو من عند الله تعالى فلذلك لا نجد فيه اختلافا وتضادا أصلا فإن قلت ما ذكرته من الت

So the seeker (al-sālik) journeyed on to the world of Power, and there he beheld wonders before which all that had preceded seemed contemptible. He asked Power concerning the movement of the right hand, and it said: "I am but an attribute (innamā anā ṣifah) — ask the Powerful One (al-Qādir), for the reliance is upon the described substances (al-mawṣūfāt), not upon the attributes." At that point he almost deviated and unleashed the tongue of questioning with audacity, but he was steadied by the firm word (al-qawl al-thābit), and a caller cried out from behind the veils of the pavilions of the Divine Presence: "He is not asked about what He does, but they shall be asked" {«لَا يُسْأَلُ عَمَّا يَفْعَلُ وَهُمْ يُسْأَلُونَ»}. Then the awe of the Presence overwhelmed him, and he fell down stricken, convulsing in his swoon. When he regained consciousness, he said: "Glory be to You — how magnificent is Your majesty! I repent unto You, and I place my trust in You, and I believe that You are the Sovereign, the Compeller, the One, the Subduer. I fear none but You, I hope for none other than You, and I seek refuge only in Your pardon from Your punishment, and in Your good pleasure from Your wrath. I have nothing but to ask of You and to supplicate before You, and to plead humbly in Your presence, saying: 'Expand my breast that I may know You, and loosen the knot from my tongue that I may praise You.'"

20:132.arabic: أمرني ربي عز وجل قال عز وجل {وأمر أهلك بالصلاة واصطبر عليها} (5) الآية وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم لم يتوكل من استرقى واكتوى (6) وروي أنه لما قال جبريل لإبراهيم عليهما السلام وقد رمي إلى النار بالمنجنيق ألك حاجة قال أما إليك فلا وفاء بقوله حسبي الله ونعم الوكيل إذ قال ذلك حين أخذ ليرمى فأنزل الله تعالى {وإبراهيم الذي وفى} وأوحى الله تعالى إلى داود عليه السلام يا داود ما من عبد يعتصم بي دون خلقي فتكيده السموات والأرض إلا جعلت له مخرجا وأما الآثار فقد قال سعيد بن جبير لدغتني عقرب فأقسمت علي أمي لتسترقين فناولت الرا
20:132.english: His protection and His sanctuary, and He is a Wise One who does not fall short in managing the affairs of one who entrusts His management to Him. And He, exalted is He, said: {إِنَّ الَّذِينَ تَدْعُونَ مِن دُونِ اللَّهِ عِبَادٌ أَمْثَالُكُمْ} — "Indeed, those you call upon besides Allah are servants like yourselves" — thereby making clear that everything other than Allah, exalted is He, is a subjugated servant, whose need is like your need; so how then can one rely upon him?
20:132.section_title_en: Section 1103 — On the First Part Concerning Divine Unity (Tawḥīd) and the Perfection of Trust in Allah
20:132.anchors:
- Root: وكل (W-K-L)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of delegating, entrusting, and appointing another as a deputy or guardian over one's affairs.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "التوكيل: أن تعتمد على غيرك وتجعله نائبا عنك" — Trust (tawakkul) is to rely upon another and make him a deputy; the true Wakīl is Allah alone, as in {وَكَفَىٰ بِاللَّهِ وَكِيلًا}.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): "توكل على الله ولا تتكل على غيره" — reliance on Allah. Metaphorical (majāz): "وكل همه بكذا" — one who delegates his care to a thing, implying abandonment by Allah of those who turn to other than Him.
- Root: عبد (ʿ-B-D)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Servitude, submission, and humble obedience; the created being as subjugated servant.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "العبودية: إظهار التذلل، والعبادة أبلغ منها" — servitude is the display of humility; worship is its utmost degree, due only to Allah. All besides Allah are "عباد أمثالكم" — servants like yourselves, incapable of independent provision.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "عبد بين العبودية" — a slave bound in servitude. Metaphorical: "استعبده الطمع" — greed enslaves a man, just as reliance on creatures enslaves the heart.
- Root: رسل (R-S-L)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Sending forth with ease and gentleness; a messenger dispatched with a message.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "أصل الرسل: الانبعاث على التؤدة" — the root is gentle dispatch; the messenger is one sent, and the verse {وَأْمُرْ أَهْلَكَ بِالصَّلَاةِ} is a divine sending of command.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "أرسل الله في الأمم رسلا" — Allah sent messengers to nations. Metaphorical: "أرسل الله عليهم العذاب" — Allah loosed punishment upon them, showing His sole agency.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The rule governing the separation of the preposition from its object for rhetorical emphasis, as in "على ربهم يتوكلون" where the preposition "على" is fronted before its governed noun "ربهم" to highlight exclusive reliance, a construction permissible when the clause is semantically complete and the fronting serves emphasis (takhrīṣ).

21:91.arabic: قال تعالى فنفخنا فيها من روحنا وكان النافخ جبريل عليه السلام وكما قال تعالى فإذا قرأناه فاتبع قرآنه قيل في التفسير معناه إذا قرأه عليك جبريل وقال تعالى قاتلوهم يعذبهم الله بأيديكم فأضاف القتل إليهم والتعذيب إلى نفسه والتعذيب هو عين
21:91.english: Thus should you understand the issuance of determined things (al-maqdūrāt) from eternal power — even though the power is eternal (qadīmah) and the objects of power are originated (ḥādithah). And this is a knocking upon another door of another world among the worlds of unveilings (mukāshafāt). So let us leave all of that, for our purpose is only to alert to the path of unification (tawḥīd) in the act — for the agent in truth (al-fāʿil bi-al-ḥaqīqah) is One. He is the feared and the hoped, and upon Him is reliance and trust. And we have not been able to mention from the seas of tawḥīd save a drop from the ocean of the third station among the stations of tawḥīd. And exhausting that within the lifetime of Noah is impossible — like exhausting the water of the sea by taking droplets from it. And all of that is subsumed under the saying: "There is no god but God" (lā ilāha illā Allāh). How light is its burden upon the tongue, how easy is the belief in the meaning of its utterance upon the heart, and how precious is its reality and its kernel (lubbuhu) among the scholars firmly rooted in knowledge — so how [much more so] with others?
21:91.section_title_en: The Oneness of the Actor (Tawḥīd al-Fiʿl) — Reconciling Divine and Human Agency
21:91.anchors:
- Root: قدر (q-d-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root denotes measure, decree, and capacity; al-Farāhīdī anchors it in the physical act of measuring or sizing, extended to divine determining.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Al-qudrah" when ascribed to God negates incapacity (ʿajz) absolutely; when ascribed to man, it names a state (hayʾah) enabling a specific act — never absolute power, but restricted capacity over particular objects.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): "He is qādir, possessing power." Metaphorical (majāz): "faras baʿīd al-qadr" (a far-striding horse) — power's "reach" extended figuratively; here, divine power's "presence" with its objects is literal for God, metaphorical for creatures.
- Root: حدث (ḥ-d-th)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "Al-ḥudūth": coming-to-be after non-existence; al-ḥadath: ritual impurity (as in this text's water analogy); al-muḥdath: the originated thing.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Al-ḥudūth: the thing's being after it was not — whether accident or substance. Its iḥdāth (bringing-about) is exclusive to God." Creaturely acts are originated, but their origination is divine.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: recent, newly arisen. Metaphorical: "ʿUmar was muḥaddath" (inspired in judgment) — as if spoken to by unseen truth; here, the "newly arisen" (ḥādith) effect is tied to a condition (sharṭ), not a new power.
- Root: ماء (m-ā-ʾ)
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Water as the origin of life ({وجعلنا من الماء كل شيء حي}); its root is m-w-h, with hāʾ dropped and wāw shifted — a paradigm for how a thing's "presence" (mulāqāh) does not entail its "effect" (taʾthīr) absent a condition.
  * Kitab al-Ayn: Water's essence is unchanged; the analogy hinges on its constancy.
- Root: وجه (w-j-h)
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Al-wajh" is the face; then extended to the "foremost" or "noblest" part of any thing, and to the self (dhāt) in {ويبقى وجه ربك}. Here, "washing the face" is the specified condition (sharṭ) — the "foremost" ritual act — not the efficient cause of purification.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the bodily face. Metaphorical: "wajh al-qawm" (the leaders), "wajh al-thawb" (the surface of a garment) — the "face" as the operative locus; in the analogy, the face's washing is the trigger, not the agent.
- Sibawayh Rule: Al-Faṣl bayna al-jār wa-al-majrūr (Prepositional Interposition) — Governing principle: a dependent element (here, divine power's "attachment" to objects) can be separated from its governor by an intervening condition, just as grammatical separation is permissible when the intervening clause is complete; analogically, the "link" (irṭibāṭ) of power to its effect is mediated by conditions without altering the agent's nature.
21:91.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Monotheism and Reliance'

22:18.arabic: إلى السماء والأرض والشمس والقمر والنجوم والغيم والمطر وسائر الجمادات والثانية النظر إلى اختيار الحيوانات وهي أعظم العقبتين وأخطرهما وبقطعهما كمال سر التوحيد فلذلك عظم ثواب هذه الكلمة أعني ثواب المشاهدة التي هذه الكلمة ترجمتها فإذا رجع حال التوكل إلى التبري من الحول والقوة والتوكل على الواحد الحق وسيتضح عند ذكرنا تفصيل أعمال التوكل إن شاء الله تعالى
22:18.english: If you say: "Does there remain with the servant any management (tadbir) or attachment to causes (asbab) in these states?" — Know that the third station negates management entirely (rafʿan li-l-tadbir), so long as the state persists; rather, its possessor becomes like one stupefied (mabhut). The second station negates every management except that which pertains to fleeing unto Allah through supplication (duʿa) and earnest entreaty (ibtihal) — like the management of an infant in clinging to its mother alone. The first station does not negate the root of management and choice (ikhtiyar), but negates certain managements — like one who relies on his deputy (wakil) in a lawsuit: he abandons his own management with respect to what is not the deputy's concern, but he does not abandon the management which his deputy has indicated to him, nor the management which he knows from the deputy's custom and established practice (sunnah), apart from his explicit indication.
22:18.section_title_en: The Reality of Reliance (Haqiqat al-Tawakkul) — Degrees of Trust and the Station of Witnessing
22:18.anchors:
- Root: دبر (d-b-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "دبر الشيء: خلاف القبل" — the rear, the back; by extension, the management of affairs as one turns away from one thing toward another (tadbir: to manage, to deliberate over outcomes).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "دبر الشيء: خلاف القبل، وكني بهما عن العضوين المخصوصين" — used literally for spatial orientation; metaphorically for the ordering of one's own affairs (tadbir al-amr), which is the very faculty that tawakkul suspends or redirects.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "أدبر النهار ودبر دبورا" (the day passed away). Metaphorical: "ما يعرف قبيلا من دبير" — one who cannot distinguish front from back, i.e., total loss of self-direction; relevant to the state of the "bewildered" (mabhut) one.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — applies to the phrase "لا حول ولا قوة إلا بالله" where the restriction (hasr) confines all power (hawl) and strength (quwwah) exclusively to Allah, negating any independent creaturely agency.
22:18.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Monotheism and Reliance'

22:58.arabic: أمضى السبيل فقلت وما إمضاء السبيل فقيل لي كنت تقول للشيء إنه في سبيل الله ثم ترجع فيه فلو كنت أمضيت السبيل لأمضينا لك وحكي عن بعض العباد بمكة أنه كان نائما إلى جنب رجل معه هميانه فانتبه الرجل ففقد هميانه فاتهمه به فقال له كم كان في هميانك فذكر له فحمله من البيت ووزنه من عنده ثم بعد ذلك أعلمه أصحابه أنهم كانوا أخذوا الهميان مزحا معه فجاء هو وأصحابه معه وردوا الذهب فأبى وقال خذه حلالا طيبا فما كنت لأعود في مال أخرجته في سبيل الله عز وجل فلم يقبل فألحوا عليه فدعا ابنه وجعل يصره صررا ويبعث به إلى الفقراء حتى لم يبق منه شيء فهكذا ك
22:58.english: ...his wealth being for him a deterrent from sin — for perhaps he would become independent by means of it and thus grow lax about theft afterward, while his disobedience had already ceased by his consuming the unlawful, since [the owner] had made it lawful for him. The second [intention] is that he not wrong another Muslim, such that his wealth becomes a ransom for the wealth of another Muslim. And whenever he intends thereby to protect another's wealth with his own wealth, or intends to repel sin from the thief or to lighten it upon him, then he has indeed advised the Muslims sincerely and has complied with his saying, peace and blessings be upon him: {«انصر أخاك ظالما أو مظلوما»} — "Help your brother whether he is the wrongdoer or the wronged." And helping the wrongdoer is that you prevent him from wrongdoing. His pardoning of him is an annihilation of the wrongdoing and a prevention of it. And let him be certain that this intention does not harm him in any way whatsoever, for there is nothing in it that empowers the thief or alters the eternal decree. Rather, let him verify his intention by means of renunciation (zuhd). For if his wealth is taken, he shall have for every dirham seven hundred dirhams, because he intended it and aimed at it. And if it is not taken, he still obtains the reward — as it was related from the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, concerning one who abstained from coitus interruptus and thus left the drop of semen in its place, that he would have the reward of a boy born to him from that intercourse who lived and was then killed in the path of Allah, the Exalted — even if no boy was actually born to him. For the matter of the child is nothing but the intercourse itself; as for the creation, the life, the provision, and the survival, these are not up to him. So had the child been created, his reward would have been upon his own act, and his act was not annihilated. Likewise is the matter of theft.
22:58.section_title_en: On the Etiquettes of Reliance (Adab al-Tawakkul) — Section 1134: Concerning One Whose Wealth is Stolen
22:58.anchors:
- Root: ظلم (Ẓ-L-M)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning is "to place something in other than its proper place"; darkness (ẓulmah) as its physical correlate.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Ẓulm is "transgression against right" and is expressed as darkness (ẓulumāt) versus light (nūr) — ignorance, shirk, and fisq.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): "He wrongs and is wronged." Metaphorical (majāz): "A land ẓalīm" — one never dug; the wrongdoer's darkness is like the darkness of the grave.
- Root: سبل (S-B-L)
  * Lisan / Ayn: A clear, easy path (sabīl); its plural subul.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "The way in which there is ease"; when used absolutely, it designates the path of truth (ṭarīq al-ḥaqq).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "Take this path, for it is the most even of paths." Metaphorical: "He let down (asbala) the rain" — as if lowering a curtain; "he let flow tears."
- Root: سرق (S-R-Q)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Taking what is not one's own covertly.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Theft is the taking of what one has no right to take, in secret"; legally specified by place and amount.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "A thief between thefts." Metaphorical: "He stole the hearing" (listened secretly); "a stolen voice" (hoarse).
- Sibawayh Rule: Bāb al-Ḥaṣr wa al-Taqyīd bi-innamā (Restriction and Specification with innamā) — Used to confine a predicate to a subject, as in the dream narrative: "It is only for him who carried the path through (amḍā al-sabīl)."
22:58.topic: Al-Ghazali on constant remembrance of God and contemplative invocations, from 'Monotheism and Reliance'

25:38.arabic: وكان الربيع بن خثيم أصابه فالج فقيل له لو تداويت فقال قد هممت ثم ذكرت عادا وثمود وأصحاب الرس وقرونا بين ذلك كثيرا وكان فيهم الأطباء فهلك المداوي والمداوى ولم تغن الرقي شيئا وكان أحمد بن حنبل يقول أحب لمن اعتقد التوكل وسلك هذا الطريق ترك التداوي من شرب الدواء وغيره وإن كان به علل فلا يخبر المتطبب بها أيضا إذا سأله وقيل لسهل متى يصح للعبد التوكل قال إذا دخل عليه الضرر في جسمه والنقص في ماله فلم يلتفت إليه شغلا بحاله وينظر إلى قيام الله تعالى عليه فإذا منهم من ترك التداوي وراءه ومنهم من كرهه ولا يتضح وجه الجمع بين فعل رسولالله صلى الله عليه وسلم وأفع
25:38.english: It has been related that Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq (may Allah be pleased with him) — when it was said to him, "Shall we call a physician for you?" — replied: "The Physician has already looked upon me and said: {«إني فعال لما أريد»} — 'Indeed, I am the Doer of whatsoever I will' [Q. 11:107]."
25:38.section_title_en: On the Reasons for Abandoning Medical Treatment Among the Righteous Predecessors
25:38.anchors:
- Root: دوي (d-w-y)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root denotes treating illness, administering remedy (al-dawā'), and the act of seeking cure (al-tadāwī).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance: tadāwī pertains to corporeal ailments (amrāḍ jismāniyyah), distinct from spiritual maladies (amrāḍ qalbiyyah) which require the remedy of repentance and remembrance.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): "تداوى من مرضه" — to seek medical treatment. Metaphorical (majāz): "تداوى من الجهل" — to cure ignorance through knowledge; here, the literal sense governs bodily medicine, while the metaphorical extends to spiritual healing.
- Root: كل (k-l-l) [as in توكّل]
  * Lisan / Ayn: Root k-w-l; tawakkul: to entrust one's affair wholly to another, to rely upon a guardian (wakīl).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "التوكل: أن تعتمد على غيرك وتجعله نائبا عنك" — reliance upon God as the sole agent (wakīl) in all matters, including health and sustenance.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: appointing a deputy. Metaphorical: "توكل على الله ولا تتكل على غيره" — the believer's utter dependence on God, which may override secondary causes like medicine.
- Root: شغل (sh-gh-l)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Occupation, preoccupation that diverts the mind (al-shughl: al-ʿāriḍ alladhī yudh-hilu al-insān).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الشغل: العارض الذي يذهل الإنسان" — a state that causes forgetfulness of other concerns; here, spiritual preoccupation (shughl bi-ḥālihi) with one's standing before God eclipses bodily pain.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: being busy with affairs. Metaphorical: "دار مشغولة: فيها سكان" — a heart "occupied" by divine awe, leaving no room for attending to physical ailments.
- Root: كشف (k-sh-f)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Unveiling, disclosure; mukāshafah: the removal of the veil (kashf al-ghitā') granting direct perception of unseen realities.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological: mukāshafah is the divine unveiling granted to saints (awliyā') whereby they perceive what is hidden from ordinary senses — here, knowledge of the appointed term (ajal).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: removing a covering. Metaphorical: "كشف الأمر" — the revelation of a hidden truth; in Sufi terminology, a verified unveiling (kashf muḥaqqaq) of one's death-hour.
- Sibawayh Rule: Bāb al-ḥaṣr wa-al-taqyīd bi-innamā (Restriction & Focused Predication) — The particle innamā restricts the predicate exclusively to the subject, as in "إنما هن أختاك" (they are only your two sisters), used to correct ʿĀ'ishah's misapprehension regarding inheritance, and "إنما أشتكي ذنوبي" (I complain only of my sins), restricting Abū al-Dardā''s complaint to spiritual, not bodily, ailment.
25:38.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Monotheism and Reliance'

26:49.arabic: حقيقة الأمر فلم يكترثوا بقول فرعون لأقطعن أيديكم وأرجلكم من خلاف {بل} قالوا لن نؤثرك على ما جاءنا من البينات والذي فطرنا قاقض ما أنت قاض إنما تقضي هذه الحياة الدنيا فإن البيان والكشف يمنع التغيير وأما أصحاب السامري لما كان إيمانهم عن النظر إلى ظاهر الثعبان فلما نظروا إلى عجل السامري وسمعوا خواره تغيروا وسمعوا قوله هذا إلهكم وإله موسى ونسوا أنه لا يرجع إليهم قولا ولا يملك لهم ضرا ولا نفعا فكل من آمن بالنظر إلى ثعبان يكفر لا محالة إذا نظر إلى عجل لأن كليهما من عالم الشهادة والاختلاف والتضاد في عالم الشهادة كثير
26:49.english: ...its mover is Power (al-qudrah) without any doubt. So the seeker (al-sālik) journeyed on to the world of Power, and there he beheld wonders before which all that had preceded seemed contemptible. He asked Power concerning the movement of the right hand, and it said: "I am but an attribute (innamā anā ṣifah) — ask the Powerful One (al-Qādir), for the reliance is upon the described substances (al-mawṣūfāt), not upon the attributes." At that point he almost deviated and unleashed the tongue of questioning with audacity, but he was steadied by the firm word (al-qawl al-thābit), and a caller cried out from behind the veils of the pavilions of the Divine Presence: "He is not asked about what He does, but they shall be asked" {«لَا يُسْأَلُ عَمَّا يَفْعَلُ وَهُمْ يُسْأَلُونَ»}. Then the awe of the Presence overwhelmed him, and he fell down stricken, convulsing in his swoon. When he regained consciousness, he said: "Glory be to You — how magnificent is Your majesty! I repent unto You, and I place my trust in You, and I believe that You are the Sovereign, the Compeller, the One, the Subduer. I fear none but You, I hope for none other than You, and I seek refuge only in Your pardon from Your punishment, and in Your good pleasure from Your wrath. I have nothing but to ask of You and to supplicate before You, and to plead humbly in Your presence, saying: 'Expand my breast that I may know You, and loosen the knot from my tongue that I may praise You.'"
26:49.section_title_en: The Unification of the Acts — The Journey of the Seekers to the Oneness of the Agent
26:49.anchors:
- Root: قدر (q-d-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of measuring, determining, and empowering; al-Qadir as the One whose power is absolute and unbounded.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Power (qudrah) when ascribed to God is the negation of incapacity ('ajz); when ascribed to man it is a contingent capacity limited by divine ordainment.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (haqiqah) — "He is Qadir, Muqtadir, possessor of power"; metaphorical (majaz) — "a far-reaching steed" (ba'id al-qadr), indicating extension of effect.
- Root: وحد (w-ḥ-d)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Oneness and singularity; al-Wahid as that which has no part whatsoever.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): True unity (wahdah) is absolute indivisibility; applied to God exclusively in the sense of unique sovereignty.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "He is one (wahid), and they are singular (wuhdan)"; literal unity versus numerical oneness.
- Root: علم (ʿ-l-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Knowledge as perception of a thing's reality; the mark or sign by which something is known.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Knowledge ('ilm) is the apprehension of a thing in its true reality — either grasping the essence or judging its attributes.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — "I knew not of your news" (ma 'alimtu bi-khabarika); the knower as one marked by discernment.
- Sibawayh Rule: Restriction and Focused Predication (al-ḥaṣr wa al-taqyīd bi-innamā) — "Innamā anā ṣifah" (I am but an attribute) restricts the speaker's essence to being a mere accident, redirecting inquiry to the substantive subject (al-mawṣūf).
26:49.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Monotheism and Reliance'

29:59.arabic: تعالى فاصبر كما صبر أولي العزم من الرسل وقال تعالى {نعم أجر العاملين الذين صبروا وعلى ربهم يتوكلون} وهذا في أذى الناس وأما الصبر على أذى الحيات والسباع والعقارب فترك دفعها ليس من التوكل في شيء إذ لا فائدة فيه ولا يراد السعي ولا يترك السعي لعينه بل لإعانته على الدين وترتب الأسباب ههنا كترتبها في الكسب وجلب المنافع فلا نطول بالإعادة وكذلك في الأسباب الدافعة عن المال فلا ينقص التوكل بإغلاق باب البيت عند الخروج ولا بأن يعقل البعير لأن هذه أسباب عرفت سنة الله تعالى إما قطعا وإما ظنا ولذلك قال صلى الله عليه وسلم للأعرابي لما أن أهمل البعير وقال ت
29:59.english: ...and its end. Those who possess ends are called "the foremost" (al-sābiqūn), and those who possess beginnings are called "the companions of the right" (aṣḥāb al-yamīn). Then the companions of the right also have degrees, and likewise the foremost; and the highest degrees of the companions of the right adjoin the lowest degrees of the foremost. So there is no meaning to precise estimation in such matters. Rather, the verified truth is that tawakkul (reliance on God) through abandoning provision-storing (tark al-iddikhār) is not perfected except by the shortening of hope (qaṣr al-amal). As for the total absence of hopes for survival, its being stipulated is remote — even in a single soul — for that is as if impossible to exist. As for people, they vary in the length and shortness of hope. The least degree of hope is a day and a night, and what is less than that of hours; and its utmost is what can be conceived to be a man's lifespan. Between these are degrees beyond enumeration. Whoever does not hope for more than a month is closer to the goal than one who hopes for a year. And restricting it to forty [days] on account of the appointed time of Moses (peace be upon him) is far-fetched, for that incident was not intended to clarify the measure of what hope has been permitted. Rather, Moses' worthiness to attain the promised [encounter] was not completed except after forty days, due to a secret by which — and by its like — the sunnah of God most High proceeds in the gradual unfolding of matters, just as he (peace be upon him) said: "Indeed God kneaded the clay of Adam with His hand for forty mornings" {«إن الله خمر طينة آدم بيده أربعين صباحا»} — because the worthiness of that clay for kneading was dependent upon a period reaching what was mentioned. Therefore, whatever is beyond a year is not stored except by virtue of the heart's weakness and its leaning toward the outward aspects of causes; such [storing] falls outside the station of tawakkul, [the person] not being confident in the encompassing governance of the True Deputy (al-wakīl al-ḥaqq) over the hidden dimensions of causes. For the means of income — through harvests and alms — recur with the recurrence of years, generally speaking. Whoever stores for less than a year has a degree proportionate to the shortness of his hope; and whoever's hope is two months — his degree is not like the degree of one who hopes for a month, nor the degree of one who hopes for three months; rather, he is between them in rank. Nothing prevents storing except the shortness of hope. So the most virtuous is that one not store at all — even if his heart is weak — for the less his storing, the greater his merit. It has been related concerning the poor man whom the Prophet (peace be upon him) commanded ʿAlī (may God honor his face) and Usāmah to wash — so they washed him and shrouded him in his own cloak. When he buried him, he said to his companions: "He will be raised on the Day of Resurrection with his face like the full moon on the night of the full moon; and were it not for one trait in him, he would be raised with his face like the radiant sun." We said: "And what is it, O Messenger of God?" He said: "He was a frequent faster, a frequent prayer-stancer, and abundant in the remembrance of God most High — except that when winter came, he stored the summer garment for his summer; and when summer came, he stored the winter garment for his winter." Then he (peace be upon him) said: "Rather, the least of what you have been given is certainty (al-yaqīn) and the resolve of patience (ʿazīmat al-ṣabr)" — the hadith. The jug and the knife and whatever is needed continuously — that is not the meaning of this; for storing such does not diminish the degree. As for the winter garment, it is not needed in summer. And this [censure] applies to one whose heart is not disturbed by abandoning storing, and whose soul does not look longingly toward the hands of creatures; rather, his heart turns to nothing except the True Deputy. But if he senses within himself a restlessness that occupies his heart away from worship, remembrance, and reflection, then storing is more appropriate for him. Indeed, even if he held onto an estate whose income sufficed for his needs, and his heart would not be free except through it, then that is more appropriate for him — because the goal is the rectification of the heart so that it may be emptied for the remembrance of God. There is a person whom the existence of wealth occupies, and a person whom its absence occupies; and what is harmful is whatever occupies one away from God (mighty and majestic). Otherwise, this world in itself is not harmful — neither its existence nor its absence. For this reason, the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) was sent to all classes of creation, among them merchants, craftsmen, and people of trades and industries. He did not command the merchant to abandon his trade, nor the craftsman to abandon his craft, nor did he command the one who had abandoned both to occupy himself with them. Rather, he called everyone to God most High and guided them to the fact that their triumph and salvation lie in the turning of their hearts away from this world toward God most High. The pillar of occupation with God (mighty and majestic) is the heart. So the correct course for the weak is to store the measure of his need, just as the correct course for the strong is to abandon storing.
29:59.section_title_en: On Reliance (Tawakkul): Degrees of Hope, Provision-Storing (Iddikhār), and the Means of Repelling Harm
29:59.anchors:
- Root: أمل (ʾ-m-l)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Prolonged expectation or hoping for something; the extension of one's aspiration toward a future state.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Hope (amal) is the soul's expectation of a beloved matter; its opposite is yaʾs (despair). In the Kalam context, it is tied to the length of one's expectation of worldly continuance, which directly governs the validity of tawakkul.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (haqīqah) usage denotes the temporal span of expectation; metaphorical (majāz) usage applies to the soul's attachment to causes. Here, Ghazali uses it literally to measure degrees of trust.
- Root: ذكر (dh-k-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To remember, to mention; the opposite of forgetfulness (nisyān).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Dhikr is the presence of the remembered thing in the heart; its highest form is absorption in the remembrance of God, which is the very purpose of heart-rectification (iṣlāḥ al-qalb).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: verbal mention; metaphorical: the heart's unwavering orientation toward the object of remembrance, as in "the heart's distraction from worship and dhikr."
- Root: سبب (s-b-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: A rope by which one climbs; a means or connection to something.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Everything by which one reaches something else is called a sabab. God has ordained causes (asbāb) as the customary channel (sunnah) of His decree; reliance is placed not on the cause itself but on the Causer of causes (musabbib al-asbāb).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: a physical cord or link; metaphorical: any means, whether certain (maqṭūʿ), probable (maẓnūn), or illusory (mawhūm). Ghazali's tripartite division of causes rests on this rhetorical distinction.
- Root: وكل (w-k-l)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To entrust, to delegate; one who relies upon another as a deputy.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Tawakkul is to depend upon another and make him a deputy over one's affair. The true wakīl is God alone, for He alone encompasses the hidden dimensions of causes.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: delegation of authority; metaphorical: the heart's utter confidence in the deputy's sufficiency, as in "he entrusted his burden to God." Ghazali contrasts the strong (qawī) who abandons storing with the weak (ḍaʿīf) who stores out of necessity.
- Sibawayh Rule: Bāb al-ḥaṣr wa-l-taqyīd bi-innamā (Restriction and Focused Predication) — Used to delimit the conditions of tawakkul, e.g., "the one who stores is not excluded from tawakkul except by the length of his hope," and to distinguish what nullifies reliance from what does not.
29:59.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Monotheism and Reliance'

32:11.arabic: بعينها مرة أخرى إلى نفسه فقال الله تعالى في الموت قل يتوفاكم ملك الموت ثم قال عز وجل الله يتوفى الأنفس حين موتها وقال تعالى أفرأيتم ما تحرثون أضاف إلينا ثم قال تعالى أنا صببنا الماء صبا ثم شققنا الأرض شقا فأنبتنا فيها حبا وعنبا وقال عز وجل فأرسلنا إليها روحنا فتمثل لها بشرا سويا ثم قال تعالى فنفخنا فيها من روحنا وكان النافخ جبريل عليه السلام وكما قال تعالى فإذا قرأناه فاتبع قرآنه قيل في التفسير معناه إذا قرأه عليك جبريل وقال تعالى قاتلوهم يعذبهم الله بأيديكم فأضاف القتل إليهم والتعذيب إلى نفسه والتعذيب هو عين
32:11.english: Thus should you understand the issuance of determined things (al-maqdūrāt) from eternal power — even though the power is eternal (qadīmah) and the objects of power are originated (ḥādithah). And this is a knocking upon another door of another world among the worlds of unveilings (mukāshafāt). So let us leave all of that, for our purpose is only to alert to the path of unification (tawḥīd) in the act — for the agent in truth (al-fāʿil bi-al-ḥaqīqah) is One. He is the feared and the hoped, and upon Him is reliance and trust. And we have not been able to mention from the seas of tawḥīd save a drop from the ocean of the third station among the stations of tawḥīd. And exhausting that within the lifetime of Noah is impossible — like exhausting the water of the sea by taking droplets from it. And all of that is subsumed under the saying: "There is no god but God" (lā ilāha illā Allāh). How light is its burden upon the tongue, how easy is the belief in the meaning of its utterance upon the heart, and how precious is its reality and its kernel (lubbuhu) among the scholars firmly rooted in knowledge — so how [much more so] with others?
32:11.section_title_en: The Oneness of the Actor (Tawḥīd al-Fiʿl) — Reconciling Divine and Human Agency
32:11.anchors:
- Root: قدر (q-d-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root denotes measure, decree, and capacity; al-Farāhīdī anchors it in the physical act of measuring or sizing, extended to divine determining.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Al-qudrah" when ascribed to God negates incapacity (ʿajz) absolutely; when ascribed to man, it names a state (hayʾah) enabling a specific act — never absolute power, but restricted capacity over particular objects.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): "He is qādir, possessing power." Metaphorical (majāz): "faras baʿīd al-qadr" (a far-striding horse) — power's "reach" extended figuratively; here, divine power's "presence" with its objects is literal for God, metaphorical for creatures.
- Root: حدث (ḥ-d-th)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "Al-ḥudūth": coming-to-be after non-existence; al-ḥadath: ritual impurity (as in this text's water analogy); al-muḥdath: the originated thing.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Al-ḥudūth: the thing's being after it was not — whether accident or substance. Its iḥdāth (bringing-about) is exclusive to God." Creaturely acts are originated, but their origination is divine.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: recent, newly arisen. Metaphorical: "ʿUmar was muḥaddath" (inspired in judgment) — as if spoken to by unseen truth; here, the "newly arisen" (ḥādith) effect is tied to a condition (sharṭ), not a new power.
- Root: ماء (m-ā-ʾ)
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Water as the origin of life ({وجعلنا من الماء كل شيء حي}); its root is m-w-h, with hāʾ dropped and wāw shifted — a paradigm for how a thing's "presence" (mulāqāh) does not entail its "effect" (taʾthīr) absent a condition.
  * Kitab al-Ayn: Water's essence is unchanged; the analogy hinges on its constancy.
- Root: وجه (w-j-h)
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Al-wajh" is the face; then extended to the "foremost" or "noblest" part of any thing, and to the self (dhāt) in {ويبقى وجه ربك}. Here, "washing the face" is the specified condition (sharṭ) — the "foremost" ritual act — not the efficient cause of purification.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the bodily face. Metaphorical: "wajh al-qawm" (the leaders), "wajh al-thawb" (the surface of a garment) — the "face" as the operative locus; in the analogy, the face's washing is the trigger, not the agent.
- Sibawayh Rule: Al-Faṣl bayna al-jār wa-al-majrūr (Prepositional Interposition) — Governing principle: a dependent element (here, divine power's "attachment" to objects) can be separated from its governor by an intervening condition, just as grammatical separation is permissible when the intervening clause is complete; analogically, the "link" (irṭibāṭ) of power to its effect is mediated by conditions without altering the agent's nature.
32:11.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Monotheism and Reliance'

37:40.arabic: هذا زل أقدام الأكثرون إلا عباد الله المخلصين الذين لا سلطان عليهم للشيطان اللعين فشاهدوا بنور البصائر كون الكاتب مسخرا مضطرا كما شاهد جميع الضعفاء كون القلم مسخرا وعرفوا أن غلط الضعفاء في ذلك كغلظ النملة مثلا لو كانت تدب على الكاغد فترى رأس القلم يسود الكاغد ولم يمتد بصرها إلى اليد والأصابع فضلا عن صاحب اليد فغلطت وظنت أن القلم هو المسود للبياض وذلك لقصور بصرها عن مجاوزة رأس القلم لضيق حدقتها فكذلك من لم ينشرح بنور الله تعالى صدره للإسلام قصرت بصيرته عن ملاحظة جبار السموات والأرض ومشاهدة
37:40.english: The one who writes is the scribe. But the truth is that God — Blessed and Exalted is He — is the Scribe, for He said — Exalted is His word: {«وما رميت إذ رميت ولكن الله رمى»} ["And you did not throw when you threw, but God threw"] {Al-Anfal: 17}. So when it is unveiled to you that everything in the heavens and the earth is subjugated (musakhkharāt) in this manner, Shaytan departs from you disappointed and despairs of adulterating your tawḥīd (divine unity) with this [first] shirk (associationism). Then he comes to you with the second deadly trap (al-muhlikah al-thāniyah), which is the turning of attention to the choice (ikhtiyār) of animals in their voluntary acts (al-afʿāl al-ikhtiyāriyyah). He says: "How do you see everything as from God, yet this human being gives you your sustenance by his own choice? If he wills, he gives you; and if he wills, he cuts it off from you. And this person is the one who severs your neck with his sword, and he has power over you — if he wills, he severs your neck, and if he wills, he pardons you. So how do you not fear him? And how do you not hope for him, when your affair is in his hand, and you witness this and do not doubt it?" He also says to him: "Yes — if you do not see the pen because it is subjugated, then how do you not see the scribe with the pen, while he is the one subjugated to it?"
