53:23.arabic: أصلا وإنما يتبعون الظن وما تهوى الأنفس ولقد جاءهم من ربهم الهدى وهو سبب اليقين إلا أنهم معرضون عنه فإذن الجبن والجراءة غرائز ولا ينفع اليقين معها فهي أحد الأسباب التي تضاد حال التوكل كما أن ضعف اليقين بالخصال الأربعة أحد الأسباب وإذا اجتمعت هذه الأسباب حصلت الثقة بالله تعالى وقد قيل مكتوب في التوراة ملعون من ثقته إنسان مثله وقد قال صلى الله عليه وسلم
53:23.english: So when you have understood tawakkul in this example, then measure upon it the tawakkul upon Allah — exalted be He. For if there is established in your soul — through unveiling (kashf) or through decisive belief (iʿtiqād jāzim) — that there is no agent (fāʿil) except Allah, as has preceded; and you believe, along with that, in the completeness of [His] knowledge and power (al-ʿilm wa al-qudrah) sufficient for the servants; then the completeness of [His] care, affection, and mercy (al-ʿināyah wa al-ʿaṭf wa al-raḥmah) toward all the servants and each individual; and that there is no power beyond the limit of His power, no knowledge beyond the limit of His knowledge, and no care and mercy beyond the limit of His care for you and His mercy to you — then your heart will inevitably rely upon Him alone, and will not turn to any other in any respect, nor to itself, nor to its own might and strength. For there is no might and no power except through Allah (lā ḥawla wa lā quwwata illā billāh), as has preceded in [the book of] Tawḥīd at the mention of movement and power — for "might" (al-ḥawl) is an expression for movement, and "power" (al-quwwah) is an expression for capability (al-qudrah).
53:23.section_title_en: The Reality of Tawakkul — The Interplay of Certainty (Yaqīn), Heart's Stillness (Ṭuma'nīnah), and the Four Attributes of the Trustee (Al-Wakīl)
53:23.anchors:
- Root: وكل (W-K-L)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of delegating, entrusting, and appointing a deputy (wakīl) to act on one's behalf; the wakīl is the one relied upon for a task.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Tawakkul is to rely upon another and make him a deputy over your affair; true tawakkul on Allah is to deem Him sufficient (ḥasbunā Allāh) as the sole Guardian of your state.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) usage is delegation of a concrete task; metaphorical (majāz) usage is the heart's utter dependence on the trustee, even to the point of describing a weak man as "tikl" (one who leans entirely on others).
- Root: قلب (Q-L-B)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The heart as the organ of constant turning and overturning (taqlīb); its states fluctuate and shift.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Qalb is the turning of a thing from one state to another; the heart's "turning" (inqilāb) is its movement between conditions of fear, hope, certainty, and agitation.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: to flip a thing over; metaphorical: the heart's disposition is "turned" by overwhelming fancies (awhām) and fears, just as a merchant "turns over" goods to inspect their true condition.
- Root: نفس (N-F-S)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The self or soul; that which is the seat of inclination and emotional response.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The soul (nafs) is the subtle spiritual reality (laṭīfah) that follows imagination (khayāl) and finds rest only through it; the "tranquil soul" (al-nafs al-muṭma'innah) is its final perfected state.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the self as animate essence; metaphorical: the soul's "flowing out" (nafāsah) as preciousness, and its agitation as a type of "breathlessness" from fear.
- Root: يقن (Y-Q-N)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Certainty as the absence of doubt; firm conviction.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Yaqīn is a quality of knowledge above mere cognition (ma'rifah); it is the stillness of understanding with the fixity of judgment — as in "knowledge of certainty" (ʿilm al-yaqīn), "eye of certainty" (ʿayn al-yaqīn), and "truth of certainty" (ḥaqq al-yaqīn).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: to be certain of a matter (yaqina al-amr); it is the firmest form of knowing, distinct from mere opinion (ẓann).
- Sibawayh Rule: Restriction and Focused Predication (al-ḥaṣr wa al-taqyīd bi-innamā) — The sentence "فالسكون في القلب شيء واليقين شيء آخر" (Stillness in the heart is one thing, and certainty is another thing) uses two nominal sentences with contrastive focus to establish a strict ontological distinction between two distinct realities (ṭuma'nīnah vs. yaqīn), each with its own predicate, preventing conflation.
53:23.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Monotheism and Reliance'

54:53.arabic: واجب الحصول بعد سبق المشيئة فلا راد لحكمه ولا معقب لقضائه وأمره بل كل صغير وكبير مستطر وحصوله بقدر معلوم منتظر وما أصابك لم يكن ليخطئك وما أخطأك لم يكن ليصيبك ولنقتصر على هذه المرامز من علوم المكاشفة التي هي أصول مقام التوكل ولنرجع إلى علم المعاملة إن شاء الله تعالى وحسبنا الله ونعم الوكيل
54:53.english: ...the killing — rather, He stated explicitly, and He, exalted, said: {فَلَمْ تَقْتُلُوهُمْ وَلَٰكِنَّ اللَّهَ قَتَلَهُمْ} ("You did not kill them, but God killed them") and He, exalted, said: {وَمَا رَمَيْتَ إِذْ رَمَيْتَ وَلَٰكِنَّ اللَّهَ رَمَىٰ} ("You did not throw when you threw, but God threw"). This is a combination of negation and affirmation in appearance, but its meaning is: "You did not throw" in the sense by which the Lord is a thrower, "when you threw" in the sense by which the servant is a thrower — for the two are two distinct meanings.
54:53.section_title_en: On the Unification of Divine Agency and the Foundation of Trust (Tawḥīd as the Root of Tawakkul)
54:53.anchors:
- Root: ق-ت-ل (Q-T-L)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning: "to kill, to slay" — the act of causing death by direct agency.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In the Qur'anic context {فَلَمْ تَقْتُلُوهُمْ وَلَٰكِنَّ اللَّهَ قَتَلَهُمْ} (8:17), the verb is negated for the creature and affirmed for the Creator, indicating that true creative agency (ījād) belongs to God alone, while the creature's act is merely instrumental and attributive.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) usage assigns the verb to the true originator; metaphorical (majāz) usage assigns it to the proximate instrument, as in "the king killed" when the executioner strikes.
- Root: ر-م-ي (R-M-Y)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "To throw, to cast" — physical projection of an object.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In {وَمَا رَمَيْتَ إِذْ رَمَيْتَ وَلَٰكِنَّ اللَّهَ رَمَىٰ} (8:17), the dual affirmation and negation show two distinct meanings of "throwing": the human act (kasb) versus the divine act (khalq).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): The literal sense belongs to the agent who originates the act ex nihilo; the metaphorical sense belongs to the one through whom the act occurs as a vessel.
- Root: ع-ل-م (ʿ-L-M)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "Knowledge, perception, cognition" — the apprehension of a thing as it truly is.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Knowledge is of two kinds: (1) apprehension of the essence of a thing, and (2) judgment about a thing's existence or non-existence of attributes. Divine knowledge (ʿilm) is the source of all teaching, as in {عَلَّمَ بِالْقَلَمِ} (96:4).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "to know" as direct cognition; also "to teach" (ʿallama) as the transmission of that cognition.
- Root: و-ك-ل (W-K-L)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "To entrust, to delegate, to rely upon" — the act of appointing another as deputy and placing one's affair in their hands.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Tawakkul is to rely upon another and make them one's agent. The Wakīl (Trustee) is He who undertakes the affair of His servant, as in {وَكَفَىٰ بِاللَّهِ وَكِيلًا} (4:81).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "to entrust an affair to someone." Metaphorical: "to rely upon" in the sense of inner confidence and tranquility of heart.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — The particle "innamā" restricts the predicate to the subject alone, excluding all others. Also applicable: the rule of negation and affirmation (nafy wa-ithbāt) in a single sentence, where the negation applies to one sense and the affirmation to another, requiring semantic disambiguation (taṣrīf al-maʿnā).
54:53.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Monotheism and Reliance'

56:15.arabic: لما ذكر في سورة الواقعة المقربين السابقين تعرض لسرير الملك فقال {على سرر موضونة متكئين عليها متقابلين} ولما انتهى إلى أصحاب اليمين ما زاد في ذكر الماء والظل والفواكه والأشجار والحور العين وكل ذلك من لذات المنظور والمشروب والمأكول والمنكوح ويتصور ذلك للبهائم على الدوام وأين لذات البهائم من لذة الملك والنزول في أعلى عليين في جوار رب العالمين ولو كان لهذه اللذات قدر لما وسعت على البهائم ولما رفعت عليها درجة الملائكة أفترى أن أحوال البهائم وهي مسيبة في الرياض متنعمة بالماء والأشجار وأصناف المأكولات متمتعة بالنزوان والسفاد أعلى وألذ وأشرف وأجدر بأن
56:15.english: If you say: "Does there remain with the servant any management (tadbir) or attachment to causes (asbab) in these states?" — Know that the third station negates management entirely (rafʿan li-l-tadbir), so long as the state persists; rather, its possessor becomes like one stupefied (mabhut). The second station negates every management except that which pertains to fleeing unto Allah through supplication (duʿa) and earnest entreaty (ibtihal) — like the management of an infant in clinging to its mother alone. The first station does not negate the root of management and choice (ikhtiyar), but negates certain managements — like one who relies on his deputy (wakil) in a lawsuit: he abandons his own management with respect to what is not the deputy's concern, but he does not abandon the management which his deputy has indicated to him, nor the management which he knows from the deputy's custom and established practice (sunnah), apart from his explicit indication.
56:15.section_title_en: The Reality of Reliance (Haqiqat al-Tawakkul) — Degrees of Trust and the Station of Witnessing
56:15.anchors:
- Root: دبر (d-b-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "دبر الشيء: خلاف القبل" — the rear, the back; by extension, the management of affairs as one turns away from one thing toward another (tadbir: to manage, to deliberate over outcomes).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "دبر الشيء: خلاف القبل، وكني بهما عن العضوين المخصوصين" — used literally for spatial orientation; metaphorically for the ordering of one's own affairs (tadbir al-amr), which is the very faculty that tawakkul suspends or redirects.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "أدبر النهار ودبر دبورا" (the day passed away). Metaphorical: "ما يعرف قبيلا من دبير" — one who cannot distinguish front from back, i.e., total loss of self-direction; relevant to the state of the "bewildered" (mabhut) one.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — applies to the phrase "لا حول ولا قوة إلا بالله" where the restriction (hasr) confines all power (hawl) and strength (quwwah) exclusively to Allah, negating any independent creaturely agency.
56:15.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Monotheism and Reliance'

63:7.arabic: الله الرزق واعبدوه وقال عز وجل ولله خزائن السموات والأرض ولكن المنافقين لا يفقهون وقال عز وجل يدبر الأمر ما من شفيع إلا من بعد إذنه وكل ما ذكر في القرآن من التوحيد فهو تنبيه على قطع الملاحظة عن الأغيار والتوكل على الواحد القهار وأما الأخبار فقد قال صلى الله عليه وسلم فيما رواه ابن مسعود أريت الأمم في الموسم فرأيت أمتي قد ملأوا السهل والجبل فأعجبتني كثرتهم وهيأتهم فقيل لي أرضيت قلت نعم قيل ومع هؤلاء سبعون ألفا يدخلون الجنة بغير حساب قيل من هم يا رسول الله قال الذين لا يكتوون ولا يتطيرون ولا يسترقون وعلى ربهم يتوكلون فقام عكاشة و
63:7.english: His protection and His sanctuary, and He is a Wise One who does not fall short in managing the affairs of one who entrusts His management to Him. And He, exalted is He, said: {إِنَّ الَّذِينَ تَدْعُونَ مِن دُونِ اللَّهِ عِبَادٌ أَمْثَالُكُمْ} — "Indeed, those you call upon besides Allah are servants like yourselves" — thereby making clear that everything other than Allah, exalted is He, is a subjugated servant, whose need is like your need; so how then can one rely upon him?
63:7.section_title_en: Section 1103 — On the First Part Concerning Divine Unity (Tawḥīd) and the Perfection of Trust in Allah
63:7.anchors:
- Root: وكل (W-K-L)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of delegating, entrusting, and appointing another as a deputy or guardian over one's affairs.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "التوكيل: أن تعتمد على غيرك وتجعله نائبا عنك" — Trust (tawakkul) is to rely upon another and make him a deputy; the true Wakīl is Allah alone, as in {وَكَفَىٰ بِاللَّهِ وَكِيلًا}.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): "توكل على الله ولا تتكل على غيره" — reliance on Allah. Metaphorical (majāz): "وكل همه بكذا" — one who delegates his care to a thing, implying abandonment by Allah of those who turn to other than Him.
- Root: عبد (ʿ-B-D)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Servitude, submission, and humble obedience; the created being as subjugated servant.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "العبودية: إظهار التذلل، والعبادة أبلغ منها" — servitude is the display of humility; worship is its utmost degree, due only to Allah. All besides Allah are "عباد أمثالكم" — servants like yourselves, incapable of independent provision.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "عبد بين العبودية" — a slave bound in servitude. Metaphorical: "استعبده الطمع" — greed enslaves a man, just as reliance on creatures enslaves the heart.
- Root: رسل (R-S-L)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Sending forth with ease and gentleness; a messenger dispatched with a message.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "أصل الرسل: الانبعاث على التؤدة" — the root is gentle dispatch; the messenger is one sent, and the verse {وَأْمُرْ أَهْلَكَ بِالصَّلَاةِ} is a divine sending of command.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "أرسل الله في الأمم رسلا" — Allah sent messengers to nations. Metaphorical: "أرسل الله عليهم العذاب" — Allah loosed punishment upon them, showing His sole agency.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The rule governing the separation of the preposition from its object for rhetorical emphasis, as in "على ربهم يتوكلون" where the preposition "على" is fronted before its governed noun "ربهم" to highlight exclusive reliance, a construction permissible when the clause is semantically complete and the fronting serves emphasis (takhrīṣ).
63:7.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Monotheism and Reliance'

75:18.arabic: تعالى فإذا قرأناه فاتبع قرآنه قيل في التفسير معناه إذا قرأه عليك جبريل وقال تعالى قاتلوهم يعذبهم الله بأيديكم فأضاف القتل إليهم والتعذيب إلى نفسه والتعذيب هو عين
75:18.english: Thus should you understand the issuance of determined things (al-maqdūrāt) from eternal power — even though the power is eternal (qadīmah) and the objects of power are originated (ḥādithah). And this is a knocking upon another door of another world among the worlds of unveilings (mukāshafāt). So let us leave all of that, for our purpose is only to alert to the path of unification (tawḥīd) in the act — for the agent in truth (al-fāʿil bi-al-ḥaqīqah) is One. He is the feared and the hoped, and upon Him is reliance and trust. And we have not been able to mention from the seas of tawḥīd save a drop from the ocean of the third station among the stations of tawḥīd. And exhausting that within the lifetime of Noah is impossible — like exhausting the water of the sea by taking droplets from it. And all of that is subsumed under the saying: "There is no god but God" (lā ilāha illā Allāh). How light is its burden upon the tongue, how easy is the belief in the meaning of its utterance upon the heart, and how precious is its reality and its kernel (lubbuhu) among the scholars firmly rooted in knowledge — so how [much more so] with others?
75:18.section_title_en: The Oneness of the Actor (Tawḥīd al-Fiʿl) — Reconciling Divine and Human Agency
75:18.anchors:
- Root: قدر (q-d-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root denotes measure, decree, and capacity; al-Farāhīdī anchors it in the physical act of measuring or sizing, extended to divine determining.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Al-qudrah" when ascribed to God negates incapacity (ʿajz) absolutely; when ascribed to man, it names a state (hayʾah) enabling a specific act — never absolute power, but restricted capacity over particular objects.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): "He is qādir, possessing power." Metaphorical (majāz): "faras baʿīd al-qadr" (a far-striding horse) — power's "reach" extended figuratively; here, divine power's "presence" with its objects is literal for God, metaphorical for creatures.
- Root: حدث (ḥ-d-th)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "Al-ḥudūth": coming-to-be after non-existence; al-ḥadath: ritual impurity (as in this text's water analogy); al-muḥdath: the originated thing.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Al-ḥudūth: the thing's being after it was not — whether accident or substance. Its iḥdāth (bringing-about) is exclusive to God." Creaturely acts are originated, but their origination is divine.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: recent, newly arisen. Metaphorical: "ʿUmar was muḥaddath" (inspired in judgment) — as if spoken to by unseen truth; here, the "newly arisen" (ḥādith) effect is tied to a condition (sharṭ), not a new power.
- Root: ماء (m-ā-ʾ)
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Water as the origin of life ({وجعلنا من الماء كل شيء حي}); its root is m-w-h, with hāʾ dropped and wāw shifted — a paradigm for how a thing's "presence" (mulāqāh) does not entail its "effect" (taʾthīr) absent a condition.
  * Kitab al-Ayn: Water's essence is unchanged; the analogy hinges on its constancy.
- Root: وجه (w-j-h)
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Al-wajh" is the face; then extended to the "foremost" or "noblest" part of any thing, and to the self (dhāt) in {ويبقى وجه ربك}. Here, "washing the face" is the specified condition (sharṭ) — the "foremost" ritual act — not the efficient cause of purification.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the bodily face. Metaphorical: "wajh al-qawm" (the leaders), "wajh al-thawb" (the surface of a garment) — the "face" as the operative locus; in the analogy, the face's washing is the trigger, not the agent.
- Sibawayh Rule: Al-Faṣl bayna al-jār wa-al-majrūr (Prepositional Interposition) — Governing principle: a dependent element (here, divine power's "attachment" to objects) can be separated from its governor by an intervening condition, just as grammatical separation is permissible when the intervening clause is complete; analogically, the "link" (irṭibāṭ) of power to its effect is mediated by conditions without altering the agent's nature.
75:18.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Monotheism and Reliance'

80:26.arabic: الدقيق الذي يقصرون عن فهمه إذ قال تعالى {أنا صببنا الماء صبا ثم شققنا الأرض شقا فأنبتنا فيها حبا وعنبا} الآية وأما الحكمة في سائر الكواكب السيارة منها والثوابت فخفية لا يطلع عليها كافة الخلق والقدر الذي يحتمله فهم الخلق أنها زينة للسماء لتستلذ العين بالنظر إليها وأشار إليه قوله تعالى {إنا زينا السماء الدنيا بزينة الكواكب} فجميع أجزاء العالم سماؤه وكواكبه ورياحه وبحاره وجباله ومعادنه ونباته وحيواناته وأعظاء حيواناته لا تخلو ذرة من ذراته عن حكم كثيرة من حكمه واحدة إلى عشرة إلى ألف إلى عشرة آلاف وكذا أعضاء الحيوان تنقسم إلا ما يعرف حكمتها
80:26.english: ...and there is no omnipotent one save the King, the Compeller. And when the covering is lifted from the eyes of the heedless, and they behold the matter to be thus, they will hear at that time the call of the Proclaimer: {«لِمَنِ الْمُلْكُ الْيَوْمَ لِلَّهِ الْوَاحِدِ الْقَهَّارِ»} — "To whom belongs the sovereignty this Day? To God, the One, the Compeller" {Q 40:16}. And indeed sovereignty belonged to God, the One, the Compeller, every single day — not exclusively on that day — but the heedless do not hear this proclamation save on that day. Thus it is tidings of what is renewed for the heedless of the unveiling of states, at a time when the unveiling will not benefit them. So we seek refuge in God, the Forbearing, the Generous, from ignorance and blindness, for it is the root cause of destruction.
80:26.section_title_en: The Unveiling of Sovereignty and the Discernment of What God Loves from What He Abhors
80:26.anchors:
- Root: كشف (kashafa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Removal of a covering; disclosure of what was hidden.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Unveiling of the unseen realities (mukāshafah) — the lifting of the veil from the heart's eye to perceive things as they truly are.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): removal of a physical covering. Metaphorical (majāz): the disclosure of intellectual or spiritual realities to the percipient.
- Root: ملك (malaka)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Possession, dominion, sovereignty; the one who possesses is malik (king).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): True sovereignty (mulk) belongs exclusively to God; all created dominion is borrowed and ephemeral.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: royal authority. Metaphorical: absolute, unshared dominion — as in the Qur'anic proclamation of sole kingship on the Day of Judgment.
- Root: شكر (shakara)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Gratitude; acknowledgment of beneficence.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Thankfulness is the recognition of the Benefactor and the employment of His blessings in that which pleases Him — not mere verbal praise.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: requital of favor. Metaphorical: the use of blessings in obedience to the Giver, which is the true meaning of gratitude.
- Root: كفر (kafara)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Covering, concealing; ingratitude that veils the recognition of favor.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Kufr is the covering of blessings by failing to employ them in the manner intended by the Giver, or by employing them in what He abhors.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: covering a seed in the earth. Metaphorical: the concealment of God's blessings through misuse or neglect.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Restriction and Focused Predication (al-ḥaṣr wa al-taqyīd bi-innamā) — restricting the means of gratitude to two exclusive cognitive faculties, and the restriction of creation's purpose to the sole end of attaining unto God.
80:26.topic: Al-Ghazali on purifying the character, moral diseases, and spiritual remedies, from 'Monotheism and Reliance'

96:5.arabic: لحصول نقش العلوم في قلوب البشر قال الله تعالى {الذي علم بالقلم علم الإنسان ما لم يعلم} وقلم الله تعالى لا يشبه قلم خلقه كما لا يشبه وصفه وصف خلقه فليس قلمه من قصب ولا خشب كما أنه تعالى ليس من جوهر ولا عرض فالموازنة بين البصيرة الباطنة والبصر الظاهر صحيحة من هذه الوجوه إلا أنه لا مناسبة بينهما في الشرف فإن البصيرة الباطنة هي عين النفس التي هي اللطيفة المدركة وهي كالفارس والبدن كالفرس وعمى الفارس أضر على الفارس من عمى الفرس بل لا نسبة لأحد الضررين إلى الآخر ولموازنة البصيرة الباطنة للبصر الظاهر سماه الله تعالى باسمه فقال {ما كذب
96:5.english: And the washing of the eye is forbidden. The first [meaning of intellect] is what is intended by his saying — peace and blessings be upon him — to ʿAlī: "God created no creature more noble before Him than the intellect." The second is what is intended by his saying — peace and blessings be upon him — to ʿAlī, may God be well pleased with him: "When people draw near to God — exalted be He — through various kinds of righteousness, draw near you through your intellect." For it is not possible to draw near through innate instinct (al-gharīzah al-fiṭriyyah) nor through necessary sciences (al-ʿulūm al-ḍarūriyyah), but rather through acquired sciences (al-muktasabah). Yet the likes of ʿAlī — may God be well pleased with him — is one who is able to draw near through the use of the intellect in hunting out the sciences by which nearness to the Lord of the Worlds is attained.
96:5.section_title_en: The Washing of the Eye is Forbidden — The Rational and Religious Sciences Compared
96:5.anchors:
- Root: عقل (ʿaql)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of binding, restraining, and holding back — the intellect as that which restrains the soul from base desires and grasps realities.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "العقل يقال للقوة المتهيئة لقبول العلم، ويقال للعلم الذي يستفيده الإنسان بتلك القوة عقل" — the intellect is the power prepared for receiving knowledge, and the knowledge acquired through that power is also called ʿaql.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal sense of binding and holding; metaphorical extension to the rational faculty that restrains and perceives consequences (al-ʿawāqib).
- Root: بصر (baṣar)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Sight, vision; the faculty of the eye.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "البصر يقال للجارحة الناظرة... ويقال لقوة القلب المدركة: بصيرة وبصر" — baṣar applies to the seeing organ and to the heart's perceiving power (baṣīrah).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — "أبصر الشيء" to see something; Metaphorical — "هذه آية مبصرة" a clarifying sign; "أعمى القلب" blindness of the heart as spiritual blindness.
- Root: قلب (qalb)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The heart; that which turns and fluctuates.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "قلب الشيء: تصريفه وصرفه عن وجه إلى وجه" — the heart as the seat of understanding that turns between states.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — the physical organ; Metaphorical — "قلب المعلم الصبيان" the teacher turns the boys [to their homes], i.e., directs them; the heart as the center of rational perception.
- Root: علم (ʿilm)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Knowledge, perception of a thing as it truly is.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "العلم: إدراك الشيء بحقيقته" — knowledge is the apprehension of a thing in its true reality; two types: apprehension of the essence, and judgment upon a thing.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "ما علمت بخبرك: ما شعرت به" — to know is to perceive; "معالم الطريق" — the landmarks by which the path is known.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب التشبيه والتمثيل (The Chapter of Similitude and Analogy) — the balanced comparison (al-muwāzanah) between two domains using parallel grammatical structures (ka-... ka-...) to establish proportional equivalence while preserving distinction.
96:5.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'Monotheism and Reliance'

2:225.arabic: الشهادة ومن يكتمها فإنه آثم قلبه} وقوله تعالى {لا يؤاخذكم الله باللغو في أيمانكم ولكن يؤاخذكم بما كسبت قلوبكم} والحق عندنا في هذه المسألة لا يوقف عليه ما لم تقع الإحاطة بتفصيل أعمال القلوب من مبدأ ظهورها إلى أن يظهر العمل على الجوارح فنقول أول ما يرد على القلب الخاطر كما لو خطر له مثلا صورة امرأة وأنها وراء ظهره في الطريق لو التفت إليها لرآها والثاني هيجان الرغبة إلى النظر وهو حركة الشهوة في الطبع وهذا يتولد من الخاطر الأول ونسميه ميل الطبع ويسمى الأول حديث النفس والثالث حكم القلب بأن هذا ينبغي أن يفعل أي ينبغي أن ينظر إليها فإن الطبع إذا مال لم تنبع
2:225.english: Know that this is a subtle matter, and there have come down concerning it verses and reports that are mutually conflicting, such that the way of reconciling between them becomes obscure — save for the master-brokers of the scholars of the Sacred Law. For it has been related from the Prophet — peace and blessings be upon him — that he said: "God has pardoned my community for what their souls whisper to them, so long as they do not speak of it or act upon it." (1) And Abū Hurayrah said: The Messenger of God — peace and blessings be upon him — said: "God — exalted is He — says to the guardian angels: When My servant intends a sin, do not write it against him; but if he commits it, then write it as one sin. And when he intends a good deed and does not perform it, write it for him as one good deed; but if he performs it, write it for him as ten." (2) This has been recorded by al-Bukhārī and Muslim in the two Ṣaḥīḥs, and it is evidence for the pardon of the heart's act and its intending of a sin. And in another wording: "Whoever intends a good deed and does not perform it, it is written for him as a good deed; and whoever intends a good deed and performs it, it is written for him as up to seven hundred multiples. And whoever intends a sin and does not perform it, it is not written against him; but if he performs it, it is written." And in yet another wording: "When My servant speaks within himself of committing a sin, I forgive him for it so long as he does not commit it." And all of this indicates the pardon.
2:225.section_title_en: The Heart's Whisperings and the Divine Pardon — On the Four Stages of Inner Acts
2:225.anchors:
- Root: نفس (n-f-s)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The self, soul, or inner being; that which breathes and harbors concealed thoughts.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-nafs denotes the soul or self (al-rūḥ), and in divine address, "what your souls whisper" (mā ḥaddathat bihi nufūsuhā) refers to the inner promptings that arise without deliberate volition.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) usage pertains to the soul's essence; metaphorical (majāz) usage extends to inner speech and inclination, as in "ḥadīth al-nafs" (self-talk), which is not yet resolved action.
- Root: حدث (ḥ-d-th)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To originate or bring forth something new; an event or occurrence that comes to be after non-existence.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-ḥudūth is the coming-to-be of a thing after it was not; "ḥadīth al-nafs" is the newly arising thought that occurs to the heart without prior acquisition.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: a recent matter or speech; metaphorical: the inner utterance of the soul, as in the prophetic report, "God has pardoned my community for what their souls whisper to them."
- Root: هم (h-m-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To intend, resolve, or purpose; the stirring of the will toward an act before its execution.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-hamm is the resolved intention (al-ʿazm) that precedes the deed; it is distinguished from mere inclination (mayl) and passing thought (khāṭir).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the soul's determination; metaphorical: the initial resolve that, when strengthened, becomes a firm will (irādah jazīmah).
- Root: قلب (q-l-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The heart; to turn or overturn, signifying its fluctuating nature between states.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The heart is the seat of cognition and volition; its "acts" (aʿmāl al-qulūb) include thought, belief, and resolve, which are subject to divine reckoning.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the physical organ; metaphorical: the spiritual faculty that perceives, believes, and intends, as in "the heart's sin" (ithm al-qalb).
- Sibawayh Rule: Restriction and Focused Predication (al-ḥaṣr wa al-taqyīd bi-innamā) — The prophetic and Quranic statements employ restriction to delineate the boundary between what is pardoned (the passing thought) and what is reckoned (the resolved intention), requiring precise parsing of the conditional clauses (law, idhā, man) to distinguish the stages of inner acts.
2:225.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Disciplining the Soul'

2:225.arabic: الله تعالى {لا يؤاخذكم الله باللغو في أيمانكم} هذا ما نقل من الأقاويل ومن طلب الحق في التقليد فمهما استقصى تعارضت عنده هذه الأقاويل فيبقى متحيرا أومائلا إلى بعض الأقاويل بالتشهي وكل ذلك قصور بل ينبغي أن يطلب الحق بطريقه وذلك بالبحث عن مدارك الحظر والإباحة كما سنذكره بيان الدليل على إباحة السماع اعلم أن قول القائل السماع حرام معناه أن الله تعالى يعاقب عليه وهذا أمر لا يعرف بمجرد العقل بل بالسمع ومعرفة الشرعيات محصورة في النص أو القياس على المنصوص وأعني بالنص ما أظهره صلى الله عليه وسلم
2:225.english: And it was related from Ṭāhir ibn Bilāl al-Hamadānī al-Warrāq, who was among the people of knowledge, that he said: I was in spiritual retreat (muʿtakif) in the congregational mosque of Jeddah by the sea, and one day I saw a group reciting poetry (yaqūlūn qawl) in one corner of it and listening. I disapproved of that in my heart and said: In a house among the houses of God they recite poetry? He said: Then I saw the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, that night, seated in that very corner, and beside him was Abu Bakr al-Ṣiddīq, may God be pleased with him — and behold, Abu Bakr was reciting something of poetry, and the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, was listening to him and placing his hand upon his chest like one overcome with ecstasy (al-wājid) thereby. So I said to myself: It was not fitting for me to disapprove of those who were listening — for here is the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, listening, and Abu Bakr reciting. Then he [the Prophet] turned to me and said: "This is true by truth" — or he said: "True from truth" — I am doubtful about it [the exact wording].
2:225.section_title_en: The Revival of the Religious Sciences — Section 488: On the Lawfulness of Auditory Samaʿ (Spiritual Listening)
2:225.anchors:
- Root: سمع (s-m-ʿ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root meaning: hearing, listening, perceiving by the ear; also used for answering/accepting a supplication.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Hearing as a physical sense perception; in theological usage, al-samʿ (revelation/textual report) is contrasted with al-ʿaql (reason) as a source of knowledge — precisely the dichotomy Ghazali invokes here.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): auditory perception. Metaphorical (majāz): obedience, acceptance, or the revealed text itself (al-samʿ = the transmitted revelation).
- Root: طيب (ṭ-y-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root meaning: goodness, pleasantness, purity, lawfulness.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "That which the senses and the soul find pleasurable"; in legal-theological terms, what is lawful (ḥalāl) and wholesome — both immediately and in its ultimate consequence.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: pleasant to the senses. Metaphorical: lawful (ḥalāl), pure, free of taint — as in "ṭāba lī kadhā" (this became lawful/pleasant for me).
- Root: قيس (q-y-s)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root meaning: measuring, estimating, comparing.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Qiyās in juristic theology: analogical extension of a ruling from an original case (al-aṣl) to a subsidiary case (al-farʿ) based on shared effective cause (ʿillah).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: measurement by measure or rod. Metaphorical: intellectual analogy and juridical reasoning.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — governing the periodic suspension of grammatical completion to allow for parenthetical or conditional insertions, as in Ghazali's layered conditional structures.
2:225.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Audition and Ecstasy'

2:284.arabic: فأما ما يدل على المؤاخذة فقوله سبحانه إن تبدوا ما في أنفسكم أو تخفوه يحاسبكم به الله فيغفر لمن يشاء ويعذب من يشاء وقوله تعالى {ولا تقف ما ليس لك به علم إن السمع والبصر والفؤاد كل أولئك كان عنه مسؤولا} فدل على أن عمل الفؤاد كعمل السمع والبصر فلا يعفى عنه وقوله تعالى {ولا تكتموا الشهادة ومن يكتمها فإنه آثم قلبه} وقوله تعالى {لا يؤاخذكم الله باللغو في أيمانكم ولكن يؤاخذكم بما كسبت قلوبكم} والحق عندنا في هذه المسألة لا يوقف عليه ما لم تقع الإحاطة بتفصيل أعمال القلوب من مبدأ ظهورها إلى أن يظهر العمل على الجوارح فنقول أول ما يرد على القلب الخاطر كما لو خطر له مثلا صو

2:284.arabic: تعالى {وإن تبدوا ما في أنفسكم أو تخفوه يحاسبكم به الله} جاء ناس من الصحابة إلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فقالوا كلفنا ما لا نطيق الحديث أخرجه مسلم من حديث أبي هريرة وابن عباس نحوه فأنزل الله الفرج بعد سنة بقوله {لا يكلف الله نفسا إلا وسعها} فظهر به أن كل ما لا يدخل تحت الوسع من أعمال القلب هو الذي لا يؤاخذ به فهذا هو كشف الغطاء عن هذا الالتباس وكل من يظن أن كل ما يجري على القلب يسمى حديث النفس ولم يفرق بين هذه الأقسام الثلاثة فلا بد وأن يغلط وكيف لا يؤاخذ بأعمال القلب من الكبر والعجب والرياء و
2:284.english: The proof that the mere thought and the initial inclination are not held against the servant is that which is firmly established from the Messenger of God — peace be upon him — that he said: "God has pardoned my community for what their souls whisper to them, so long as they do not speak of it or act upon it." And he said — peace be upon him: "When two Muslims meet with their swords, then the killer and the killed are both in the Fire." It was said: "O Messenger of God, this is the killer — but what of the killed?" He said: "Because he intended to kill his companion." {«التقى المسلمان بسيفيهما فالقاتل والمقتول في النار»} — and his being held accountable was solely for his intention (niyyah) and his resolution, not for the mere thought that crossed his heart, for the thought of killing is not within one's capacity to prevent, while the resolution to kill is.
2:284.section_title_en: Exposition of What the Servant is Held Accountable For from the Whispers of the Hearts, Their Anxieties, Their Thoughts, and Their Intentions — and What is Pardoned and Not Held Against Him
2:284.anchors:
- Root: وسوس (w-s-w-s)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The faint, concealed sound; the subtle, indistinct voice that inclines one toward something
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The insinuation that enters the heart covertly, whether from Satan or from the self's inclination
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — the faint jingling of an ornament; Metaphorical — the secret prompting that stirs within the breast
- Root: خطر (kh-t-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To come to mind; the passing of a thought across the heart without deliberate pursuit
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The sudden occurrence of a notion in the mind, whether invited or uninvited
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — something that presents itself; Metaphorical — the fleeting thought that crosses the heart like a passing traveler
- Root: هم (h-m-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The intention that inclines one toward an act before resolution is firmly settled
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The initial stirring of the will toward an action, preceding the firm resolve ('azm)
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — to intend; Metaphorical — the heart's leaning that, if unchecked, hardens into determination
- Root: قصد (q-s-d)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The deliberate aiming toward a goal; the firm resolution that governs the limbs
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The settled intention that directs action and for which one is justly held accountable
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — to walk a straight path to a destination; Metaphorical — the will's firm orientation that constitutes the essence of moral agency
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين المبتدأ والخبر (The Interposition Between Subject and Predicate) — governing the periodic structure of conditional accountability clauses where the protasis (condition) and apodosis (result) are separated by explanatory parentheticals, preserving the logical dependency of moral judgment upon the specification of the act's nature.

3:139.arabic: الموقن فإنه خير من ألف قلب من العوام وقد قال تعالى وأنتم الأعلون إن كنتم مؤمنين تفضيلا للمؤمنين على المسلمين والمراد به المؤمن العارف دون المقلد وقال عز وجل يرفع الله الذين آمنوا منكم والذين أوتوا العلم درجات فأراد ههنا بالذين آمنوا الذين صدقوا من غير علم وميزهم عن الذين أوتوا العلم ويدل ذلك على أن اسم المؤمن يقع على المقلد وإن لم يكن تصديقه عن بصيرة وكشف وفسر ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما قوله تعالى والذين أوتوا العلم درجات فقال يرفع الله العالم فوق المؤمن بسبعمائة درجة بين كل درجتين كما بين السماء والأرض وقال صلى الله عليه و
3:139.english: The Hadith—and by this the disparity of people in faith becomes manifest. For if the faith of Abū Bakr were weighed against the faith of all the worlds, save the prophets and messengers, it would preponderate. This too resembles the saying of one who says: "If the light of the sun were weighed against the light of all lamps, it would preponderate." For the light of the common folk (al-ʿawāmm) is like the light of the lamp, and some of them have light like the light of the candle, while the faith of the sincerely truthful (al-ṣiddīqīn) has light like the light of the moon and the stars, and the faith of the prophets is like the sun. And just as in the light of the sun the forms of the horizons are disclosed—[Page V03P022]—with the vastness of their regions, while in the light of a lamp nothing is disclosed save a narrow corner of the house, so likewise is the disparity in the expansion of the breast (sharḥ al-ṣadr) by the gnoses (maʿārif) and the unveiling of the vastness of the Kingdom (malakūt) to the hearts of the knowers (ʿārifīn). For this reason it has come in the report that it will be said on the Day of Resurrection: "Bring forth from the Fire whoever has in his heart the weight of a grain of faith, and half a grain, and a quarter of a grain, and a barley-corn, and an atom" (1)—agreed upon (2).
3:139.section_title_en: The Disparity of People in Faith and the Degrees of the Hereafter
3:139.anchors:
- Root: نور (n-w-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of light, illumination, and that by which one sees; the lamp, the moon, the stars—all termed nūr in varying intensities.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Light is of two kinds: sensory light perceived by the eye, and intellectual/spiritual light perceived by the eye of insight (baṣīrah)—the latter being the light of reason, of the Qur'an, and of divine illumination granted to hearts.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): the radiant light of celestial bodies and lamps. Metaphorical (majāz): "nawwara al-amr" (he illuminated the matter)—i.e., he made it clear and manifest; thus faith's light is spoken of as illumination of the heart by knowledge.
- Root: وزن (w-z-n)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To weigh, to measure, to balance; the act of comparing weights to determine preponderance (rujḥān).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Weighing in the metaphysical sense denotes the just assessment of worth and degree; the preponderance of one thing over another in measure or excellence.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the physical act of weighing on scales. Metaphorical: the weighing of deeds and faiths in the balance of divine justice, as in the scales of the Hereafter.
- Root: درج (d-r-j)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Degrees, steps, ascending ranks; the path of ascent from one station to a higher one.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Degree (darajah) is a station considered by ascent, not horizontal extension—used for lofty ranks and elevations in honor and proximity.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: stairs and steps climbed. Metaphorical: "li-fulān darajah rafīʿah" (so-and-so has an exalted degree)—i.e., high standing and rank; "imshi fī madārij al-ḥaqq" (walk in the paths of truth).
- Root: علم (ʿ-l-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Knowledge, perception, and the mark or sign by which something is known; the scholar (ʿālim) is one distinguished by the sign of knowledge.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Knowledge is the apprehension of a thing in its true reality (idrāk al-shayʾ bi-ḥaqīqatihi)—either apprehension of the essence itself, or judgment upon it affirming or negating a predicate.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: perception and awareness. Metaphorical: the "aʿlām" (landmarks) of guidance—the traces by which the seeker is directed; the scholar is a living landmark of the religion.
- Sibawayh Rule: Restriction and Specification (al-ḥaṣr wa al-taqyīd)—the use of syntactic structures to distinguish categories, as in the verse {«Allah will raise those who have believed among you and those who were given knowledge, by degrees»} (58:11), where the two groups are syntactically distinguished to show that faith without knowledge is one rank, and knowledge added to faith is another.

3:160.arabic: ومن يرد أن يضله يجعل صدره ضيقا حرجا كأنما يصعد في السماء إن ينصركم الله فلا غالب لكم وإن يخذلكم فمن ذا الذي ينصركم من بعده فهو الهادي والمضل يفعل ما يشاء ويحكم ما يريد لا راد لحكمه ولا معقب لقضائه خلق الجنة وخلق لها أهلا فاستعملهم بالطاعة وخلق النار وخلق لها أهلا فاستعمله بالمعاصي وعرف الخلق علامة أهل الجنة وأهل النار فقال إن الأبرار لفي نعيم وإن الفجار لفي جحيم ثم قال تعالى فيما روى عن نبيه صلى الله عليه وسلم هؤلاء في الجنة ولا أبالي وهؤلاء في النار ولا أبالي (1) فتعالى الله الملك الحق لا يسئل عما يفعل وهم يسئلون ولنقتصر على هذا القدر اليسير من ذكر عجائب القلب فإ
3:160.english: I say: Know that when the Shayṭān prevails and the heart inclines to its own kind among the parties of the Shayṭān, turning away from the party of God—Exalted is He—and His saints, and aiding the party of the Shayṭān and His enemies, then there flows upon its bodily members, by virtue of the prior decree, that which is the cause of its distance from God—Exalted is He. But if the angelic attributes are predominant over the heart, the heart does not lend its ear to the Shayṭān's seduction, nor to his incitement toward the immediate world, nor to his belittling of the matter of the Hereafter. Rather, it inclines to the party of God—Exalted is He—and obedience appears upon its members in accordance with what has preceded in the decree. Thus, the heart of the believer is between two fingers of the fingers of the All-Merciful—that is, between the mutual tugging of these two hosts—and this is the meaning of "turning" (taqlīb): the transition from one party to another. As for perpetual constancy, whether with the party of the angels or with the party of the Shayṭān, that is rare on both sides. These acts of obedience and disobedience emerge from the treasuries of the Unseen into the world of witness by way of the treasury of the heart, for it is among the treasuries of the Malakūt. And when they do emerge, they become signs by which the masters of hearts recognize the prior decree. For whomever is created for Paradise, the means of obedience are made easy for him; and whomever is created for the Fire, the means of disobedience are made easy for him, and evil companions are given sway over him, and the rule of the Shayṭān is cast into his heart. For by various kinds of deceptions he beguiles the foolish, saying: "God is Merciful, so do not care"; and "All people do not fear God, so do not oppose them"; and "Life is long, so be patient until you repent tomorrow." He promises them and fills them with desires—{يَعِدُهُمْ وَيُمَنِّيهِمْ وَمَا يَعِدُهُمُ الشَّيْطَانُ إِلَّا غُرُورًا} "He promises them and fills them with desires, and the Shayṭān promises them nothing but delusion" {النساء/120}. He promises them repentance and fills them with hopes of forgiveness, and thus destroys them, by God's permission, through these ruses and what runs in their course. So he expands their hearts to accept delusion and constricts them from accepting the truth. And all of that is by God's decree and destiny: {فَمَن يُرِدِ اللَّهُ أَن يَهْدِيَهُ يَشْرَحْ صَدْرَهُ لِلْإِسْلَامِ وَمَن يُرِدْ أَن يُضِلَّهُ يَجْعَلْ صَدْرَهُ ضَيِّقًا حَرَجًا كَأَنَّمَا يَصَّعَّدُ فِي السَّمَاءِ} "Whomsoever God wishes to guide, He expands his breast to Islam; and whomsoever He wishes to lead astray, He makes his breast narrow and constricted, as though he were climbing into the sky" {الأنعام/125}. {إِن يَنصُرْكُمُ اللَّهُ فَلَا غَالِبَ لَكُمْ وَإِن يَخْذُلْكُمْ فَمَن ذَا الَّذِي يَنصُرُكُم مِّن بَعْدِهِ} "If God helps you, none can overcome you; and if He forsakes you, who is there to help you after Him?" {آل عمران/160}. He is the Guide and the Misleader; He does what He wills and decrees what He desires. There is no repeller of His judgment and no reverser of His decree. He created Paradise and created for it its people, and employed them in obedience; and He created the Fire and created for it its people, and employed them in disobedience. And He made known to creation the mark of the people of Paradise and the people of the Fire, saying: {إِنَّ الْأَبْرَارَ لَفِي نَعِيمٍ وَإِنَّ الْفُجَّارَ لَفِي جَحِيمٍ} "Verily, the righteous shall be in bliss, and verily, the wicked shall be in the Blazing Fire" {الانفطار/13-14}. Then He—Exalted is He—said, as related from His Prophet, peace be upon him: "These are in Paradise, and I do not care; and these are in the Fire, and I do not care." Exalted is God, the King, the Truth! {لَا يُسْأَلُ عَمَّا يَفْعَلُ وَهُمْ يُسْأَلُونَ} "He is not questioned about what He does, but they shall be questioned" {الأنبياء/23}.
3:160.section_title_en: The Explanation of the Heart's Rapid Fluctuation and the Division of Hearts Between Change and Constancy
3:160.anchors:
- Root: قلب (q-l-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of turning, overturning, and revolving a thing from one face to another; the heart is so named for its constant oscillation.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "قلب الشيء: تصريفه وصرفه عن وجه إلى وجه" — the heart's essence is its perpetual turning and redirection; its fluctuation is not accidental but constitutive of its nature.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): physical overturning. Metaphorical (Majaz): "رجل قلب حول: يقلب الأمور ويحتال" — the heart's movement between the two hosts (jundān) is a real, dynamic turnover of allegiance.
- Root: شيط (sh-y-t)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Burning, scorching, or spoiling meat by over-smoking; blood going to waste.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The Shayṭān is so named for his being burned and banished from mercy.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Metaphorical: "شاط دمه إذا بطل" — the Shayṭān's work is to render the servant's spiritual life wasted and nullified, as blood spilled in vain.
- Root: حزب (ḥ-z-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: A group or party with cohesion and strength; al-Ḥayzabūn (the old woman) shows the root's extension to a gathered mass.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الحزب: جماعة فيها غلظ" — the party of God (ḥizb Allāh) versus the party of the Shayṭān (ḥizb al-Shayṭān) are two opposing, organized camps in cosmic conflict.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: a band of partisans. Metaphorical: "قرأ حزبه من القرآن" — a portion assigned; here, the heart is assigned to one of the two parties by divine decree.
- Root: خلق (kh-l-q)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Measuring and smoothing; creating as precise estimation.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الخلق أصله: التقدير المستقيم" — creation is origination upon a just measure; God's creative act entails the pre-ordainment of ends.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: shaping leather before cutting. Metaphorical: "خلق الله الخلق: أوجده على تقدير أوجبته الحكمة" — God's creation of Paradise and Hellfire and their inhabitants is an act of wise, pre-eternal determination.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — The phrase "إنما ذكرنا منه ما يحتاج إليه" restricts the author's purpose: only the necessary measure of the heart's wonders is expounded, not exhaustive treatment, signaling a deliberate boundary of the science of practical religion (ʿilm al-muʿāmalah).

7:100.arabic: كانوا يكسبون وقال عز وجل أن لو نشاء أصبناهم بذنبوهم ونطبع على قلوبهم فهم لا يسمعون فربط عدم السماع بالطبع بالذنوب كما ربط السماع بالتقوى فقال تعالى واتقوا الله واسمعوا واتقوا الله ويعلمكم الله ومهما تراكمت الذنوب طبع على القلوب وعند ذلك يعمى القلب عن إدراك الحق وصلاح الدين ويستهين بأمر الآخرة ويستعظم أمر الدنيا ويصير مقصور الهم عليها فإذا قرع سمعه أمر الآخرة وما فيها من الأخطار دخل من أذن وخرج من أذن ولم يستقر في القلب ولم يحركه إلى التوبة والتدارك أولئك يئسوا من الآخرة كما يئس الكفار من
7:100.english: As for the praiseworthy effects that we have mentioned, they increase the mirror of the heart in clarity (jalā'), radiance (ishrāq), light (nūr), and brilliance (ḍiyā'), until the clear truth (jalīyat al-ḥaqq) gleams within it and the reality of the sought-after matter in religion is unveiled in it. And it is to such a heart that the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, pointed when he said: "When God desires good for a servant, He appoints for him an admonisher from his own heart." (1) The hadith: "Whoever has from his heart an admonisher, upon him is from God a protector" — I have not found for it a source (aṣl).
7:100.section_title_en: The Heart as a Mirror: The Effects of Virtues and Vices upon Spiritual Perception
7:100.anchors:
- Root: قلب (q-l-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To turn over, to overturn, to transform from one state to another; the heart as that which is constantly fluctuating and turning between states.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "قلب الشيء: تصريفه وصرفه عن وجه إلى وجه" — The heart is that which is perpetually turned about, and its rectitude or corruption depends upon the direction of its turning.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): physical turning over. Metaphorical (Majaz): "قلب المعلم الصبيان: صرفهم إلى بيوتهم" — the turning of a thing toward its proper end. Here, the heart is a mirror (مرآة) turned toward either the light of truth or the darkness of sin.
- Root: رين (r-y-n)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Rust, tarnish, or filth that overcomes a polished surface, veiling its original brightness.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The covering of the heart by accumulated sin, such that it becomes rusted over and incapable of receiving the light of truth.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the tarnishing of a blade or mirror. Metaphorical: the veiling of the heart's perceptive faculty by the accumulation of transgressions, as in {«كلا بل ران على قلوبهم ما كانوا يكسبون»} (The Mutaffifin: 14).
- Root: طبع (t-b-')
  * Lisan / Ayn: To stamp, to seal, to impress upon; the imprinting of a seal that renders the surface impermeable to further impression.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The sealing of the heart by God as a consequence of persistent sin, rendering it deaf to admonition and blind to truth.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the physical stamping of a seal. Metaphorical: the divine sealing of the heart as a just consequence of willful persistence in transgression.
- Root: ذكر (dh-k-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Remembrance, recollection, mindfulness; the opposite of forgetfulness (نسيان).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The presence of the thing remembered in the mind; the highest form being the remembrance of God which brings tranquility to the heart.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: verbal invocation. Metaphorical: the state of spiritual presence and awareness that polishes the heart's mirror and unveils the reality of truth.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The syntactic connection between cause and effect, as in the verse {«واتقوا الله واسمعوا»}, where hearing (spiritual perception) is grammatically and semantically linked to piety (تقوى), just as the sealing of the heart (طبع) is linked to the accumulation of sins (ذنوب).
7:100.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Disciplining the Soul'

10:6.arabic: والقرآن مصرح بأن التقوى مفتاح الهداية والكشف وذلك علم من غير تعلم وقال الله تعالى وما خلق الله في السموات والأرض لآيات لقوم يتقون خصصها بهم وقال تعالى {هذا بيان للناس وهدى وموعظة للمتقين} وكان أبو يزيد وغيره يقول ليس العالم الذي يحفظ من كتاب فإذا نسي ما حفظه صار جاهلا إنما العالم الذي يأخذ علمه من ربه أي وقت شاء بلا حفظ ولا درس وهذا هو العلم الرباني وإليه الإشارة بقوله تعالى {وعلمناه من لدنا علما} مع أن كل علم من لدنه ولكن بعضها بوسائط تعليم الخلق فلا يسمى ذلك علما لدنيا بل اللدني الذي ينفتح في سر القلب من غير سبب مألوف من خارج فهذه شواهد النقل ولو جمع كل ما و
10:6.english: As for the evidences of the Sacred Law, there is His saying (Exalted is He): {«وَالَّذِينَ جَاهَدُوا فِينَا لَنَهْدِيَنَّهُمْ سُبُلَنَا»} ("And those who strive in Us, We shall surely guide them to Our paths") (Q. 29:69). So every wisdom that appears from the heart through persevering devotion to worship, without learning, is by way of unveiling and inspiration. And he (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Whoever acts upon what he knows, God bequeaths to him knowledge of what he does not know, and grants him success in what he does" — until he becomes deserving of Paradise. And whoever does not act upon what he knows wanders astray in what he knows and is not granted success in what he does, until he becomes deserving of the Fire. [The hadith "Whoever acts upon what he knows" has preceded in the Book of Knowledge, without his saying "and grants him success in what he does" — I have not found it with that addition.] And God (Exalted is He) said: {«وَمَنْ يَتَّقِ اللَّهَ يَجْعَلْ لَهُ مَخْرَجًا»} ("And whoever fears God, He makes for him a way out") (Q. 65:2) — from perplexities and doubts — {«وَيَرْزُقْهُ مِنْ حَيْثُ لَا يَحْتَسِبُ»} ("and provides for him from whence he does not reckon") (Q. 65:3) — teaching him knowledge without learning and granting him discernment without experience. And God (Exalted is He) said: {«يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا إِنْ تَتَّقُوا اللَّهَ يَجْعَلْ لَكُمْ فُرْقَانًا»} ("O you who believe, if you fear God, He will make for you a criterion") (Q. 8:29) — it is said: a light by which one distinguishes between truth and falsehood and by which one emerges from doubts. For this reason, he (peace and blessings be upon him) was abundant in his supplication in asking for light, saying (peace and blessings be upon him): "O God, grant me light, and increase me in light, and make for me light in my heart, and light in my grave, and light in my hearing, and light in my sight" — until he said: "and light in my hair, and in my skin, and in my flesh, and in my blood, and in my bones." [Agreed upon (by al-Bukhari and Muslim).] [The hadith concerning his being asked about His saying {«أَفَمَنْ شَرَحَ اللَّهُ صَدْرَهُ لِلْإِسْلَامِ»} ("Is he whose breast God has expanded for Islam") (Q. 39:22) — and in al-Mustadrak from the hadith of Ibn Masʿūd — has preceded in the Book of Knowledge.] And he (peace and blessings be upon him) said concerning Ibn ʿAbbās: "O God, grant him understanding in religion and teach him the interpretation (taʾwīl)." [The hadith of ʿAlī: "We have nothing with us that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) confided to us except that God grants a servant understanding in His Book" — has preceded in the Etiquettes of Qurʾanic Recitation.] And it is said in the interpretation of His saying (Exalted is He): {«يُؤْتِي الْحِكْمَةَ مَنْ يَشَاءُ»} ("He grants wisdom to whom He wills") (Q. 2:269) that it is understanding in the Book of God. And He (Exalted is He) said: {«فَفَهَّمْنَاهَا سُلَيْمَانَ»} ("And We made Solomon understand it") (Q. 21:79) — singling out what was unveiled with the name of understanding (fahm). And Abū al-Dardāʾ used to say: "The believer is one who sees by the light of God from behind a thin veil. By God, it is the truth that God casts into their hearts and causes to flow upon their tongues." And some of the Salaf said: "The believer's conjecture is like soothsaying."
10:6.section_title_en: The Unveiling of Knowledge Through Divine Inspiration and the Evidences of the Unseen
10:6.anchors:
- Root: علم (ʿalima)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning encompasses both perception of a thing's essence and judgment upon it—knowledge as direct apprehension or discursive ruling.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "العلم: إدراك الشيء بحقيقته" — knowledge is the apprehension of a thing in its true reality, divided into apprehension of the essence (transitive to one object) and judgment upon existence or non-existence (transitive to two objects).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal usage denotes certainty and awareness ("ما علمت بخبرك: ما شعرت به"); metaphorical extension applies to marks, signs, and beacons of guidance (معالم الطريق) — here, the inspired knowledge is a "mark" of the path.
- Root: كشف (kashafa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To remove a covering, unveil, disclose what was hidden.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Unveiling (kashf) in theological terms is the removal of the veil (ghishāwah) from the heart such that the realities of things become directly witnessed, not merely inferred.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: to lift a covering from a thing; metaphorical: the disclosure of inward states and hidden matters — the heart's eye perceives what the outward senses cannot.
- Root: فرس (farasa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To prey upon, devour; farāsah — the lion's pouncing upon its prey.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Discernment (farāsah) is a spiritual perception by which the believer penetrates into the inner states of others, a light cast by God into the heart.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the beast of prey seizing its quarry; metaphorical: the believer's insight seizing the truth of a matter or the hidden state of a person — "اتقوا فراسة المؤمن فإنه ينظر بنور الله."
- Root: حدث (ḥadatha)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To be new, originate after non-existence; muḥaddath — one who is spoken to, inspired with true speech from the unseen.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الحدوث: كون الشيء بعد أن لم يكن" — origination after non-existence; the muḥaddath is one to whom divine inspiration comes as a new, immediate occurrence without acquired means.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: newness of a thing; metaphorical: "كان عمر رضي الله عنه محدثا أي صادق الحدس، كأنما حدث بما ظن" — one whose intuition is so true it is as if he were directly spoken to.
- Sibawayh Rule: Restriction and specification (الحصر والتقييد) — the particle "إنما" and conditional clauses (إن/إذا) restrict predicates to their subjects, as in "إنما العالم الذي يأخذ علمه من ربه" — the true scholar is exclusively the one who takes knowledge from his Lord.
10:6.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Disciplining the Soul'

11:40.arabic: وفاحشا فقد روي أن نوحا عليه السلام لما ركب السفينة حمل فيها من كل زوجين اثنين كما أمره الله تعالى فرأى في السفينة شيخا لم يعرفه فقال له نوح ما أدخلك فقال دخلت لأصيب قلوب أصحابك فتكون قلوبهم معي وأبدانهم معك فقال له نوح أخرج منها يا عدو الله فإنك لعين فقال له إبليس خمس أهلك بهن الناس وسأحدثك منهم بثلاث ولا أحدثك باثنتين فأوحى الله تعالى إلى نوح أنه لا حاجة لك بالثلاث فليحدثك بالاثنين فقال له نوح
11:40.english: Among his great gates are anger (ghaḍab) and lustful desire (shahwah). For anger is the ghoul of the intellect — when the soldier of the intellect weakens, the soldier of Satan attacks. Whenever a man becomes angry, Satan plays with him as a boy plays with a ball. It has been narrated that Moses, peace be upon him, was met by Iblis, who said to him: "O Moses, you are the one whom God chose for His message and to whom He spoke directly (taklīman). I am a creature among God's creatures. I sinned, and I wish to repent. So intercede for me to my Lord that He might accept my repentance." Moses said: "Yes." When Moses ascended the mountain and spoke with his Lord, Mighty and Majestic, and wished to descend, his Lord said to him: "Deliver the trust." Moses said: "O Lord, Your servant Iblis wishes that You accept his repentance." So God, exalted be He, revealed to Moses: "O Moses, I have already granted your request — that he prostrate before the grave of Adam so that his repentance might be accepted." Moses then met Iblis and said to him: "I have secured your request — you have been commanded to prostrate before the grave of Adam so that your repentance might be accepted." But he became angry and arrogant, saying: "I did not prostrate to him while he was alive — shall I prostrate to him dead?" Then he said to him: "O Moses, you have a right upon me because you interceded for me to your Lord. So remember me at three occasions, and I shall not destroy you in them: Remember me when you become angry, for my spirit is in your heart and my eye is in your eye, and I flow through you like the flow of blood. Remember me when you become angry — for when a man becomes angry, I blow into his nostrils, and he does not know what he does. And remember me when you encounter the battle-line (zaḥf), for I come to the son of Adam when he encounters the battle-line and remind him of his wife, his children, and his family, until he turns and flees. And beware of sitting with a woman who is not a close relative (dhāt maḥram), for I am her messenger to you and your messenger to her — I shall not cease until I tempt you with her and tempt her with you."
11:40.section_title_en: The Detailed Exposition of the Entrances of Satan into the Heart
11:40.anchors:
- Root: شيط (Shayṭ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning relates to burning, scorching, or being consumed by fire — that which is burnt and spoiled.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): الشيطان refers to the rebellious one among jinn and mankind; the term denotes one who has deviated from truth through pride and disobedience.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): "شاط اللحم" — meat that is burnt and spoiled. Metaphorical (Majaz): "شاط دمه" — his blood was spilled in vain; "أشاط السلطان دمه" — the ruler declared his blood lawful to shed. Thus the Shayṭān is so named because he is consumed by fire, or because he causes others to be consumed/destroyed.

- Root: غضب (Ghaḍab)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The boiling and agitation of the blood of the heart, seeking vengeance.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الغضب: ثوران دم القلب إرادة الانتقام" — anger is the surging of the blood of the heart desiring vengeance. When attributed to God, it means only retribution and punishment, not an emotional state.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: anger as a human emotional state. Metaphorical: "غضبت له قوائم عوج" — even inanimate things are described metaphorically. The Prophet said: "اتقوا الغضب فإنه جمرة توقد في قلب ابن آدم" — anger is a burning ember kindled in the heart of the son of Adam.

- Root: قلب (Qalb)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The heart; also the turning and revolving of a thing from one state to another.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "قلب الشيء: تصريفه وصرفه عن وجه إلى وجه" — the turning of a thing and its conversion from one aspect to another. The heart is so named because of its constant turning and fluctuation of states.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: to turn something over, to flip it. Metaphorical: "قلب المعلم الصبيان" — the teacher dismissed the boys (turned them back to their homes); "رجل قلب حول" — a man who turns matters over and devises stratagems. The heart is the seat of understanding and discernment, and its protection is the fortress against Satan.

- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The permissibility of interposing elements between a preposition and its object when the meaning remains clear, analogous to how the heart's defenses may be interposed between Satan and his objectives.
