12:31.arabic: الله تعالى عن صواحبات يوسف عليه السلام بقوله ما هذا بشرا إن هذا إلا ملك كريم ومن صرف همته إلى اتباع اللذات البدنية يأكل كما تأكل الأنعام فقد انحط إلى حضيض أفق البهائم فيصير إما غمرا كثور وإما شرها كخنزير وإما ضربا ككلب أو سنور أو حقودا كجمل أو متكبرا كنمر أو ذا روغان كثعلب أو يجمع ذلك كله كشيطان مريد وما من عضو من الأعضاء ولا حاسة من الحواس إلا ويمكن الاستعانة به على طريق الوصول إلى الله تعالى كما سيأتي بيان طرف منه في كتاب الشكر فمن استعمله فيه فقد فاز ومن عدل عنه فقد خسر وخاب وجملة السعادة في ذلك أن يجعل لقاء الله تعالى
12:31.english: Know that just as the rational person does not know the necessary sciences (al-ʿulūm al-ḍarūriyyah) nor what distinguishes the state of the rational one from what he has acquired of the theoretical sciences, so too does the rational person not know what Allah has opened for His friends (awliyāʾ) and His prophets of the prerogatives of His gentleness (luṭf) and mercy. Whatever mercy Allah opens to people, none can withhold it. This mercy is dispensed by the decree of bounty and generosity from Allah, Glorified and Exalted, not grudged to anyone. But it only appears in hearts that expose themselves to the wafts of the mercy of Allah, Exalted — as he, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Indeed, your Lord has, in the days of your time, wafts of mercy — so expose yourselves to them." (1) Hadith: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: "Long has been the yearning of the righteous for My meeting" — the hadith. I found no source for it except that the author of al-Firdaws transmitted it from the hadith of Abū al-Dardāʾ, and his son did not mention for it in the Musnad of al-Firdaws an isnād.
12:31.section_title_en: The Revival of the Religious Sciences — Section 579: The Human's Distinguishing Property is Knowledge and Wisdom; The Heart as the Seat of the King
12:31.anchors:
- Root: قلب (q-l-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of turning over, revolving, and transformation from one state to another; the heart as that which is constantly turning and fluctuating.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The heart (qalb) is so named for its constant turning (taqallub) between states; it is the seat of perception and understanding, the faculty by which one grasps realities.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: turning a thing over. Metaphorical: the heart as the seat of understanding and the center of the human kingdom, that which governs and directs the faculties.
- Root: علم (ʿ-l-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Knowledge, perception, and certainty; the mark or trace by which a thing is known.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Knowledge is the apprehension of a thing as it truly is; it is the distinguishing property of the human being and the purpose of his creation.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: knowing. Metaphorical: the light by which the heart perceives realities, the noblest of which is knowledge of God.
- Root: ملك (m-l-k)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Possession, sovereignty, and dominion; a king who rules over a domain.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The king is one who possesses authority and commands; the heart is the king of the human body, ruling over its faculties.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: a king. Metaphorical: the heart as the sovereign of the human kingdom, with the faculties as its subjects, messengers, and servants.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب التشبيه والتمثيل (The Chapter of Simile and Analogy) — The use of extended analogies (tamthīl) to clarify abstract realities through concrete images, where the comparison is drawn between the relations of parts, not merely individual attributes.
12:31.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Disciplining the Soul'

12:53.arabic: قال الله تعالى إخبارا عن يوسف عليه السلام أو امرأة العزيز {وما أبرئ نفسي إن النفس لأمارة بالسوء} وقد يجوز أن يقال المراد بالأمارة بالسوء هي النفس بالمعنى الأول فإذن النفس بالمعنى الأول مذمومة غاية الذم وبالمعنى الثاني محمودة لأنها نفس الإنسان أي ذاته وحقيقته العالمة بالله تعالى وسائر المعلومات اللفظ الرابع العقل وهو أيضا مشترك لمعان مختلفة ذكرناها في كتاب العلم والمتعلق بغرضنا من جملتها معنيان أحدهما أنه قد يطلق ويراد به العلم بحقائق الأمور فيكون عبارة عن صفة العلم الذي محله القلب والثاني أنه قد يطلق ويراد به المدرك للعلوم فيكون هو الق
12:53.english: The second meaning [of nafs] is the subtle reality (al-laṭīfah) which we have mentioned — that which is truly the human being. It is the soul of man and his very essence (dhāt), but it is described by different attributes according to the variation of its states. When it settles under the command [of God] and the agitation caused by the opposition of the passions departs from it, it is called the tranquil soul (al-nafs al-muṭma'innah). God Most High said concerning its like: {«يَا أَيَّتُهَا النَّفْسُ الْمُطْمَئِنَّةُ ارْجِعِي إِلَىٰ رَبِّكِ رَاضِيَةً مَّرْضِيَّةً»} — "O tranquil soul, return to your Lord, well-pleased and well-pleasing." But the soul in the first meaning cannot be conceived to return to God Most High, for it is banished far from God and is of the party of Satan.
12:53.section_title_en: The Comprehensive Principle of Blameworthy Traits and the True Nature of the Soul, Spirit, and Intellect
12:53.anchors:
- Root: نفس (n-f-s)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The self, soul, breath; that which animates and individuates a being
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-nafs denotes the rūḥ (spirit) in certain Quranic usages, but also the very dhāt (essence/self) of a thing—as in {«وَيُحَذِّرُكُمُ اللَّهُ نَفْسَهُ»} where "His Self" means His Essence, not a separate entity
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) usage denotes the blood of life ("nafs sā'ilah" — flowing blood); metaphorical (majāz) usage extends to the inner self, the eye of envy, and the puerperal woman
- Root: قلب (q-l-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To turn over, to flip, to transform from one state to another
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Taqlīb is the constant turning and disposition of a thing from one state to another; the heart is so named because of its perpetual fluctuation of states
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: turning a thing over, inverting it; Metaphorical: the heart as the seat of understanding and discernment—"قلب المعلم الصبيان" (the teacher turns the boys [toward their homes]) extends to directing the intellect
- Root: علم (ʿ-l-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Knowledge, perception, discernment; the mark or sign by which something is known
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): ʿIlm is the apprehension of a thing in its true reality (idrāk al-shay' bi-ḥaqīqatihi)—two kinds: (1) apprehension of the essence of a thing, (2) judgment upon a thing affirming or denying something of it
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: to know, to be aware of; also used for the landmarks (aʿlām) and traces by which one is guided on the path
- Root: انس ('-n-s)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To perceive, to become familiar with, to find comfort in
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The ins (human) is so called for his sociability and perceptive nature, contrasted with the jinn (from tajannun — hiddenness)
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: to find comfort and familiarity with someone; Metaphorical: "ibn urns" — the intimate companion, the special confidant
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The rule governing the permissibility of interposing elements between a governing word and its governed prepositional phrase, relevant here for parsing the grammatical relationships in complex attributive constructions distinguishing the various referents of the terms under discussion.
12:53.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Disciplining the Soul'

15:42.arabic: عبادي ليس لك عليهم سلطان} والسماع سبب لصفاء القلب وهو شبكة للحق بواسطة الصفاء وعلى هذا يدل ما روى أن ذا النون المصري رحمه الله دخل بغداد فاجتمع إليه قوم من الصوفية ومعهم قوال فاستأذنوه في أن يقول لهم شيئا فأذن لهم في ذلك فأنشأ يقول صغير هواك عذبني .
15:42.english: For this reason, he (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Beware the discernment of the believer, for he looks with the light of God." (2)
15:42.section_title_en: The Revival of the Religious Sciences — Section 509: On the Vision of Spiritual Realities Through Purity of Heart
15:42.anchors:
- Root: صفا (ṣafā)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of clarity, purity, and transparency — free from turbidity or admixture.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Denotes the heart's purification from base attributes, rendering it receptive to divine disclosures (mukāshafāt).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: clarity of water or wine. Metaphorical: purity of the heart as the condition for spiritual perception.
- Root: مثل (mathala)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To stand before, to appear, to take shape or form.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Used for representation and formation — the appearing of a thing in a form (ṣūrah) that may or may not correspond to its true reality.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: standing erect before someone. Metaphorical: the self-representation of spiritual beings (arwāḥ) in sensible forms perceptible to the purified heart.
- Root: نظر (naẓar)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Vision, sight, and also reflection and consideration.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Distinguishes between baṣar (physical sight) and baṣīrah (insight); the latter perceives spiritual realities (malakūt).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: seeing with the eye. Metaphorical: "looking with the light of God" (al-naẓar bi-nūr Allāh) — perception through divine illumination.
- Root: فرس (farasa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To prey upon, to seize — the ferāsah (discernment) is so named because it seizes upon the inner reality.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The intuitive perception of inner states — a form of inspired knowledge (ʿilm ladunī).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the lion preying on its quarry. Metaphorical: the believer's discernment that pierces through outward appearances to inward truths.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — Used to confine the activity of devils to hearts filled with blameworthy attributes, and to restrict the vision of the Kingdom of Heaven to purified hearts.
15:42.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Disciplining the Soul'

17:65.arabic: عبادي ليس لك عليهم سلطان} والسماع سبب لصفاء القلب وهو شبكة للحق بواسطة الصفاء وعلى هذا يدل ما روى أن ذا النون المصري رحمه الله دخل بغداد فاجتمع إليه قوم من الصوفية ومعهم قوال فاستأذنوه في أن يقول لهم شيئا فأذن لهم في ذلك فأنشأ يقول صغير هواك عذبني .
17:65.english: For this reason, he (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Beware the discernment of the believer, for he looks with the light of God." (2)
17:65.section_title_en: The Revival of the Religious Sciences — Section 509: On the Vision of Spiritual Realities Through Purity of Heart
17:65.anchors:
- Root: صفا (ṣafā)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of clarity, purity, and transparency — free from turbidity or admixture.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Denotes the heart's purification from base attributes, rendering it receptive to divine disclosures (mukāshafāt).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: clarity of water or wine. Metaphorical: purity of the heart as the condition for spiritual perception.
- Root: مثل (mathala)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To stand before, to appear, to take shape or form.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Used for representation and formation — the appearing of a thing in a form (ṣūrah) that may or may not correspond to its true reality.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: standing erect before someone. Metaphorical: the self-representation of spiritual beings (arwāḥ) in sensible forms perceptible to the purified heart.
- Root: نظر (naẓar)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Vision, sight, and also reflection and consideration.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Distinguishes between baṣar (physical sight) and baṣīrah (insight); the latter perceives spiritual realities (malakūt).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: seeing with the eye. Metaphorical: "looking with the light of God" (al-naẓar bi-nūr Allāh) — perception through divine illumination.
- Root: فرس (farasa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To prey upon, to seize — the ferāsah (discernment) is so named because it seizes upon the inner reality.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The intuitive perception of inner states — a form of inspired knowledge (ʿilm ladunī).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the lion preying on its quarry. Metaphorical: the believer's discernment that pierces through outward appearances to inward truths.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — Used to confine the activity of devils to hearts filled with blameworthy attributes, and to restrict the vision of the Kingdom of Heaven to purified hearts.
17:65.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Disciplining the Soul'

18:65.arabic: الإشارة بقوله تعالى {وعلمناه من لدنا علما} مع أن كل علم من لدنه ولكن بعضها بوسائط تعليم الخلق فلا يسمى ذلك علما لدنيا بل اللدني الذي ينفتح في سر القلب من غير سبب مألوف من خارج فهذه شواهد النقل ولو جمع كل ما ورد فيه من الآيات والأخبار والآثار لخرج عن الحصر وأما مشاهدة ذلك بالتجارب فذلك أيضا خارج عن الحصر وظهر ذلك على الصحابة والتابعين ومن بعدهم وقال أبو بكر الصديق رضي الله عنه لعائشة رضي الله عنها عند موته إنما هما أخواك وأختاك وكانت زوجته حاملا فولدت بنتا فكان
18:65.english: As for the evidences of the Sacred Law, there is His saying (Exalted is He): {«وَالَّذِينَ جَاهَدُوا فِينَا لَنَهْدِيَنَّهُمْ سُبُلَنَا»} ("And those who strive in Us, We shall surely guide them to Our paths") (Q. 29:69). So every wisdom that appears from the heart through persevering devotion to worship, without learning, is by way of unveiling and inspiration. And he (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Whoever acts upon what he knows, God bequeaths to him knowledge of what he does not know, and grants him success in what he does" — until he becomes deserving of Paradise. And whoever does not act upon what he knows wanders astray in what he knows and is not granted success in what he does, until he becomes deserving of the Fire. [The hadith "Whoever acts upon what he knows" has preceded in the Book of Knowledge, without his saying "and grants him success in what he does" — I have not found it with that addition.] And God (Exalted is He) said: {«وَمَنْ يَتَّقِ اللَّهَ يَجْعَلْ لَهُ مَخْرَجًا»} ("And whoever fears God, He makes for him a way out") (Q. 65:2) — from perplexities and doubts — {«وَيَرْزُقْهُ مِنْ حَيْثُ لَا يَحْتَسِبُ»} ("and provides for him from whence he does not reckon") (Q. 65:3) — teaching him knowledge without learning and granting him discernment without experience. And God (Exalted is He) said: {«يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا إِنْ تَتَّقُوا اللَّهَ يَجْعَلْ لَكُمْ فُرْقَانًا»} ("O you who believe, if you fear God, He will make for you a criterion") (Q. 8:29) — it is said: a light by which one distinguishes between truth and falsehood and by which one emerges from doubts. For this reason, he (peace and blessings be upon him) was abundant in his supplication in asking for light, saying (peace and blessings be upon him): "O God, grant me light, and increase me in light, and make for me light in my heart, and light in my grave, and light in my hearing, and light in my sight" — until he said: "and light in my hair, and in my skin, and in my flesh, and in my blood, and in my bones." [Agreed upon (by al-Bukhari and Muslim).] [The hadith concerning his being asked about His saying {«أَفَمَنْ شَرَحَ اللَّهُ صَدْرَهُ لِلْإِسْلَامِ»} ("Is he whose breast God has expanded for Islam") (Q. 39:22) — and in al-Mustadrak from the hadith of Ibn Masʿūd — has preceded in the Book of Knowledge.] And he (peace and blessings be upon him) said concerning Ibn ʿAbbās: "O God, grant him understanding in religion and teach him the interpretation (taʾwīl)." [The hadith of ʿAlī: "We have nothing with us that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) confided to us except that God grants a servant understanding in His Book" — has preceded in the Etiquettes of Qurʾanic Recitation.] And it is said in the interpretation of His saying (Exalted is He): {«يُؤْتِي الْحِكْمَةَ مَنْ يَشَاءُ»} ("He grants wisdom to whom He wills") (Q. 2:269) that it is understanding in the Book of God. And He (Exalted is He) said: {«فَفَهَّمْنَاهَا سُلَيْمَانَ»} ("And We made Solomon understand it") (Q. 21:79) — singling out what was unveiled with the name of understanding (fahm). And Abū al-Dardāʾ used to say: "The believer is one who sees by the light of God from behind a thin veil. By God, it is the truth that God casts into their hearts and causes to flow upon their tongues." And some of the Salaf said: "The believer's conjecture is like soothsaying."
18:65.section_title_en: The Unveiling of Knowledge Through Divine Inspiration and the Evidences of the Unseen
18:65.anchors:
- Root: علم (ʿalima)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning encompasses both perception of a thing's essence and judgment upon it—knowledge as direct apprehension or discursive ruling.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "العلم: إدراك الشيء بحقيقته" — knowledge is the apprehension of a thing in its true reality, divided into apprehension of the essence (transitive to one object) and judgment upon existence or non-existence (transitive to two objects).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal usage denotes certainty and awareness ("ما علمت بخبرك: ما شعرت به"); metaphorical extension applies to marks, signs, and beacons of guidance (معالم الطريق) — here, the inspired knowledge is a "mark" of the path.
- Root: كشف (kashafa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To remove a covering, unveil, disclose what was hidden.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Unveiling (kashf) in theological terms is the removal of the veil (ghishāwah) from the heart such that the realities of things become directly witnessed, not merely inferred.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: to lift a covering from a thing; metaphorical: the disclosure of inward states and hidden matters — the heart's eye perceives what the outward senses cannot.
- Root: فرس (farasa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To prey upon, devour; farāsah — the lion's pouncing upon its prey.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Discernment (farāsah) is a spiritual perception by which the believer penetrates into the inner states of others, a light cast by God into the heart.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the beast of prey seizing its quarry; metaphorical: the believer's insight seizing the truth of a matter or the hidden state of a person — "اتقوا فراسة المؤمن فإنه ينظر بنور الله."
- Root: حدث (ḥadatha)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To be new, originate after non-existence; muḥaddath — one who is spoken to, inspired with true speech from the unseen.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الحدوث: كون الشيء بعد أن لم يكن" — origination after non-existence; the muḥaddath is one to whom divine inspiration comes as a new, immediate occurrence without acquired means.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: newness of a thing; metaphorical: "كان عمر رضي الله عنه محدثا أي صادق الحدس، كأنما حدث بما ظن" — one whose intuition is so true it is as if he were directly spoken to.
- Sibawayh Rule: Restriction and specification (الحصر والتقييد) — the particle "إنما" and conditional clauses (إن/إذا) restrict predicates to their subjects, as in "إنما العالم الذي يأخذ علمه من ربه" — the true scholar is exclusively the one who takes knowledge from his Lord.
18:65.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Disciplining the Soul'

20:114.arabic: في الجنة ولا أبالي وهؤلاء في النار ولا أبالي (1) فتعالى الله الملك الحق لا يسئل عما يفعل وهم يسئلون ولنقتصر على هذا القدر اليسير من ذكر عجائب القلب فإن استقصاءه لا يليق بعلم المعاملة وإنما ذكرنا منه ما يحتاج إليه لمعرفة أغوار علوم المعاملة وأسرارها لينتفع بها من لا يقنع بالظواهر ولا يجتزئ بالقشر عن اللباب بل يتشوق إلى معرفة دقائق حقائق الأسباب وفيما ذكرناه كفاية له ومقنع إن شاء الله تعالى والله ولي التوفيق تم كتاب عجائب القلب ولله الحمد والمنة ويتلوه كتاب رياضة النفس وتهذيب الأخلاق والحمد لله وحده وصلى الله على ك
20:114.english: I say: Know that when the Shayṭān prevails and the heart inclines to its own kind among the parties of the Shayṭān, turning away from the party of God—Exalted is He—and His saints, and aiding the party of the Shayṭān and His enemies, then there flows upon its bodily members, by virtue of the prior decree, that which is the cause of its distance from God—Exalted is He. But if the angelic attributes are predominant over the heart, the heart does not lend its ear to the Shayṭān's seduction, nor to his incitement toward the immediate world, nor to his belittling of the matter of the Hereafter. Rather, it inclines to the party of God—Exalted is He—and obedience appears upon its members in accordance with what has preceded in the decree. Thus, the heart of the believer is between two fingers of the fingers of the All-Merciful—that is, between the mutual tugging of these two hosts—and this is the meaning of "turning" (taqlīb): the transition from one party to another. As for perpetual constancy, whether with the party of the angels or with the party of the Shayṭān, that is rare on both sides. These acts of obedience and disobedience emerge from the treasuries of the Unseen into the world of witness by way of the treasury of the heart, for it is among the treasuries of the Malakūt. And when they do emerge, they become signs by which the masters of hearts recognize the prior decree. For whomever is created for Paradise, the means of obedience are made easy for him; and whomever is created for the Fire, the means of disobedience are made easy for him, and evil companions are given sway over him, and the rule of the Shayṭān is cast into his heart. For by various kinds of deceptions he beguiles the foolish, saying: "God is Merciful, so do not care"; and "All people do not fear God, so do not oppose them"; and "Life is long, so be patient until you repent tomorrow." He promises them and fills them with desires—{يَعِدُهُمْ وَيُمَنِّيهِمْ وَمَا يَعِدُهُمُ الشَّيْطَانُ إِلَّا غُرُورًا} "He promises them and fills them with desires, and the Shayṭān promises them nothing but delusion" {النساء/120}. He promises them repentance and fills them with hopes of forgiveness, and thus destroys them, by God's permission, through these ruses and what runs in their course. So he expands their hearts to accept delusion and constricts them from accepting the truth. And all of that is by God's decree and destiny: {فَمَن يُرِدِ اللَّهُ أَن يَهْدِيَهُ يَشْرَحْ صَدْرَهُ لِلْإِسْلَامِ وَمَن يُرِدْ أَن يُضِلَّهُ يَجْعَلْ صَدْرَهُ ضَيِّقًا حَرَجًا كَأَنَّمَا يَصَّعَّدُ فِي السَّمَاءِ} "Whomsoever God wishes to guide, He expands his breast to Islam; and whomsoever He wishes to lead astray, He makes his breast narrow and constricted, as though he were climbing into the sky" {الأنعام/125}. {إِن يَنصُرْكُمُ اللَّهُ فَلَا غَالِبَ لَكُمْ وَإِن يَخْذُلْكُمْ فَمَن ذَا الَّذِي يَنصُرُكُم مِّن بَعْدِهِ} "If God helps you, none can overcome you; and if He forsakes you, who is there to help you after Him?" {آل عمران/160}. He is the Guide and the Misleader; He does what He wills and decrees what He desires. There is no repeller of His judgment and no reverser of His decree. He created Paradise and created for it its people, and employed them in obedience; and He created the Fire and created for it its people, and employed them in disobedience. And He made known to creation the mark of the people of Paradise and the people of the Fire, saying: {إِنَّ الْأَبْرَارَ لَفِي نَعِيمٍ وَإِنَّ الْفُجَّارَ لَفِي جَحِيمٍ} "Verily, the righteous shall be in bliss, and verily, the wicked shall be in the Blazing Fire" {الانفطار/13-14}. Then He—Exalted is He—said, as related from His Prophet, peace be upon him: "These are in Paradise, and I do not care; and these are in the Fire, and I do not care." Exalted is God, the King, the Truth! {لَا يُسْأَلُ عَمَّا يَفْعَلُ وَهُمْ يُسْأَلُونَ} "He is not questioned about what He does, but they shall be questioned" {الأنبياء/23}.
20:114.section_title_en: The Explanation of the Heart's Rapid Fluctuation and the Division of Hearts Between Change and Constancy
20:114.anchors:
- Root: قلب (q-l-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of turning, overturning, and revolving a thing from one face to another; the heart is so named for its constant oscillation.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "قلب الشيء: تصريفه وصرفه عن وجه إلى وجه" — the heart's essence is its perpetual turning and redirection; its fluctuation is not accidental but constitutive of its nature.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): physical overturning. Metaphorical (Majaz): "رجل قلب حول: يقلب الأمور ويحتال" — the heart's movement between the two hosts (jundān) is a real, dynamic turnover of allegiance.
- Root: شيط (sh-y-t)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Burning, scorching, or spoiling meat by over-smoking; blood going to waste.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The Shayṭān is so named for his being burned and banished from mercy.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Metaphorical: "شاط دمه إذا بطل" — the Shayṭān's work is to render the servant's spiritual life wasted and nullified, as blood spilled in vain.
- Root: حزب (ḥ-z-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: A group or party with cohesion and strength; al-Ḥayzabūn (the old woman) shows the root's extension to a gathered mass.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الحزب: جماعة فيها غلظ" — the party of God (ḥizb Allāh) versus the party of the Shayṭān (ḥizb al-Shayṭān) are two opposing, organized camps in cosmic conflict.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: a band of partisans. Metaphorical: "قرأ حزبه من القرآن" — a portion assigned; here, the heart is assigned to one of the two parties by divine decree.
- Root: خلق (kh-l-q)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Measuring and smoothing; creating as precise estimation.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الخلق أصله: التقدير المستقيم" — creation is origination upon a just measure; God's creative act entails the pre-ordainment of ends.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: shaping leather before cutting. Metaphorical: "خلق الله الخلق: أوجده على تقدير أوجبته الحكمة" — God's creation of Paradise and Hellfire and their inhabitants is an act of wise, pre-eternal determination.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — The phrase "إنما ذكرنا منه ما يحتاج إليه" restricts the author's purpose: only the necessary measure of the heart's wonders is expounded, not exhaustive treatment, signaling a deliberate boundary of the science of practical religion (ʿilm al-muʿāmalah).
20:114.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Disciplining the Soul'

20:114.arabic: لنبيه صلى الله عليه وسلم {ولا تعجل بالقرآن من قبل أن يقضي إليك وحيه} وهذا لأن الأعمال ينبغي أن تكون بعد التبصرة والمعرفة والتبصرة تحتاج إلى تأمل وتمهل والعجلة تمنع من ذلك وعند الاستعجال يروج الشيطان شره على الإنسان من حيث لا يدري فقد روي أنه لما ولد عيسى بن مريم عليه السلام أتت الشياطين إبليس فقالوا أصبحت الأصنام قد نكست رءوسها فقال هذا حادث مكانكم فطار حتى أتي خافقي الأرض فلم يجد شيئا ثم وجد عيسى عليه السلام قد ولد وإذا الملائكة حافين به فرجع إليهم فقال إن نبيا قد ولد البارحة ما حملت أنثى قط ولا وضعت إلا وأنا
20:114.english: And among its great gateways is satiety from food, even if it be lawful and pure. For satiety strengthens the lusts, and the lusts are the weapons of Satan. It has been related that Iblis appeared to Yahya ibn Zakariyya (peace be upon them both), and he saw upon him attachments of every kind of thing. He said to him: "O Iblis, what are these attachments?" He said: "These are the lusts by which I overcome the son of Adam." He said: "Is there anything among them [that you use against me]?" He said: "Perhaps I make you satiated, and so I weigh you down from prayer and from remembrance." He said: "Is there anything other than that?" He said: "No." He said: "Upon God, I shall never fill my belly with food ever again." Iblis then said to him: "And upon God, I shall never advise a Muslim ever again."
20:114.section_title_en: The Revival of the Religious Sciences — Book on Hope and Fear, Section 601: The Great Gateways of Satan's Ingress into the Heart
20:114.anchors:
- Root: كذب (kadhaba)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To lie, to falsify; the core sense of contradicting reality with speech.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In theological usage, denotes the antithesis of ṣidq (truthfulness) — a rupture in the correspondence between inward conviction and outward expression.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) — utterance contrary to fact; metaphorical (majāz) — the breaking of a promise or covenant, as when Satan says "they will not belie me" meaning they will not break their word to me.
- Root: حرص (ḥaraṣa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Intense eager desire for something, covetousness; the soul's grasping beyond its need.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): A blameworthy trait in the Quranic lexicon, being the unrestrained appetite of the soul for worldly increase; it is the root of Adam's transgression.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — the eager pursuit of provision; metaphorical — the soul's insatiable craving that overrides rational restraint.
- Root: شبع (shabi'a)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Satiety, fullness of the stomach; the cessation of hunger.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In the moral theology of the Revival, satiety is not merely physical but a state that invigorates the lower appetites (shahawāt), which are the very weapons of Satan.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — fullness of the belly; metaphorical — the satiety that breeds heedlessness (ghaflah) and weighs down the limbs from obedience.
- Root: عجل (ʿajila)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Haste, urgency; acting before the proper time.
  * Al-Raghib (Al-Mufradat): "العجلة: طلب الشيء وتحريه قبل أوانه، وهو من مقتضى الشهوة، فلذلك صارت مذمومة في عامة القرآن حتى قيل: «العجلة من الشيطان»" — Haste is the seeking of a thing before its due time, and it proceeds from lust, therefore it is blameworthy throughout the Quran.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — swiftness of movement; metaphorical — acting without deliberation (tathabbut), which opens the door to Satan's deception.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The permissibility of interposing elements between a governing word and its governed prepositional phrase when the intervening clause is complete in itself, as in the periodic constructions of this section where conditional clauses and parenthetical citations are interposed between the subject (the gateways) and their explanatory predicates.
20:114.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications, prayers, and their spiritual power, from 'Disciplining the Soul'

21:37.arabic: وقال عز وجل {خلق الإنسان من عجل} وقال تعالى {وكان الإنسان عجولا} وقال لنبيه صلى الله عليه وسلم {ولا تعجل بالقرآن من قبل أن يقضي إليك وحيه} وهذا لأن الأعمال ينبغي أن تكون بعد التبصرة والمعرفة والتبصرة تحتاج إلى تأمل وتمهل والعجلة تمنع من ذلك وعند الاستعجال يروج الشيطان شره على الإنسان من حيث لا يدري فقد روي أنه لما ولد عيسى بن مريم عليه السلام أتت الشياطين إبليس فقالوا أصبحت الأصنام قد نكست رءوسها فقال هذا حادث مكانكم فطار حتى أتي خافقي الأرض فلم يجد شيئا ثم وجد عيسى عليه السلام ق
21:37.english: And among its great gateways is satiety from food, even if it be lawful and pure. For satiety strengthens the lusts, and the lusts are the weapons of Satan. It has been related that Iblis appeared to Yahya ibn Zakariyya (peace be upon them both), and he saw upon him attachments of every kind of thing. He said to him: "O Iblis, what are these attachments?" He said: "These are the lusts by which I overcome the son of Adam." He said: "Is there anything among them [that you use against me]?" He said: "Perhaps I make you satiated, and so I weigh you down from prayer and from remembrance." He said: "Is there anything other than that?" He said: "No." He said: "Upon God, I shall never fill my belly with food ever again." Iblis then said to him: "And upon God, I shall never advise a Muslim ever again."
21:37.section_title_en: The Revival of the Religious Sciences — Book on Hope and Fear, Section 601: The Great Gateways of Satan's Ingress into the Heart
21:37.anchors:
- Root: كذب (kadhaba)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To lie, to falsify; the core sense of contradicting reality with speech.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In theological usage, denotes the antithesis of ṣidq (truthfulness) — a rupture in the correspondence between inward conviction and outward expression.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) — utterance contrary to fact; metaphorical (majāz) — the breaking of a promise or covenant, as when Satan says "they will not belie me" meaning they will not break their word to me.
- Root: حرص (ḥaraṣa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Intense eager desire for something, covetousness; the soul's grasping beyond its need.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): A blameworthy trait in the Quranic lexicon, being the unrestrained appetite of the soul for worldly increase; it is the root of Adam's transgression.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — the eager pursuit of provision; metaphorical — the soul's insatiable craving that overrides rational restraint.
- Root: شبع (shabi'a)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Satiety, fullness of the stomach; the cessation of hunger.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In the moral theology of the Revival, satiety is not merely physical but a state that invigorates the lower appetites (shahawāt), which are the very weapons of Satan.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — fullness of the belly; metaphorical — the satiety that breeds heedlessness (ghaflah) and weighs down the limbs from obedience.
- Root: عجل (ʿajila)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Haste, urgency; acting before the proper time.
  * Al-Raghib (Al-Mufradat): "العجلة: طلب الشيء وتحريه قبل أوانه، وهو من مقتضى الشهوة، فلذلك صارت مذمومة في عامة القرآن حتى قيل: «العجلة من الشيطان»" — Haste is the seeking of a thing before its due time, and it proceeds from lust, therefore it is blameworthy throughout the Quran.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — swiftness of movement; metaphorical — acting without deliberation (tathabbut), which opens the door to Satan's deception.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The permissibility of interposing elements between a governing word and its governed prepositional phrase when the intervening clause is complete in itself, as in the periodic constructions of this section where conditional clauses and parenthetical citations are interposed between the subject (the gateways) and their explanatory predicates.
21:37.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications, prayers, and their spiritual power, from 'Disciplining the Soul'

22:4.arabic: قلب} وقال تعالى {كتب عليه أنه من تولاه فإنه يضله ويهديه إلى عذاب السعير} ومن ساعد الشيطان بعمله فهو مواليه وإن ذكر الله بلسانه وإن كنت تقول
22:4.english: If you say: "What then is the remedy for repelling Satan, and is the remembrance of God—exalted is He—and one's saying 'There is no might and no power except through God' (lā ḥawla wa lā quwwata illā billāh) sufficient for that?" — Know that the remedy of the heart in this matter is to seal these entry points by purifying the heart of these blameworthy traits. And that is something whose full exposition would be lengthy; our purpose in this quarter of the book is to explain the remedy for the destructive traits (al-ṣifāt al-muhlikāt), and each trait requires a separate book, as will be explained later. Yes — when the roots of these traits are severed from the heart, Satan may still make incursions (ijtiyāzāt) and pass through it with fleeting thoughts (khaṭarāt), but he has no stability therein. And what prevents him from passing through is the remembrance of God—exalted is He—because the reality of dhikr cannot take firm hold of the heart except after the heart is built up with God-consciousness (taqwā) and purified of blameworthy traits. Otherwise, the dhikr is but the whisper of the self (ḥadīth nafs), having no authority over the heart, and so it does not repel the dominion of Satan. For this reason, God—exalted is He—said: {إِنَّ الَّذِينَ اتَّقَوْا إِذَا مَسَّهُمْ طَائِفٌ مِنَ الشَّيْطَانِ تَذَكَّرُوا فَإِذَا هُمْ مُبْصِرُونَ} "Indeed, those who fear God — when an impulse touches them from Satan, they remember [Him], and at once they are insightful" (Q 7:201). He specified thereby the God-fearing (muttaqī).
22:4.section_title_en: The Revival of the Religious Sciences — Section 603: On the Remedy for Evil Presumption and the Repelling of Satan
22:4.anchors:
- Root: شيط (Shayṭ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of burning, scorching, or being consumed by fire; also used for one who is destroyed or whose blood is shed in vain.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): الشيطان (Satan) — the one who is far removed from divine mercy, derived from the root indicating his being burned or destroyed.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): "شاط اللحم" — meat that is burnt or spoiled by fire. Metaphorical (Majaz): "شاط دمه" — his blood was shed in vain (i.e., destroyed); "أشاط السلطان دمه" — the ruler declared his blood lawful to shed. Thus, Satan is so named for his being "burned" or "destroyed" by divine curse, and for his causing others to be destroyed.
- Root: قلب (Qalb)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The heart; also the act of turning, overturning, or revolving a thing from one state to another.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "قلب الشيء: تصريفه وصرفه عن وجه إلى وجه" — the turning and directing of a thing from one aspect to another. The heart (qalb) is so named for its constant fluctuation and turning between states.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "قلب الشيء قلبا: حوله عن وجهه" — to turn a thing from its face. Metaphorical: "رجل قلب حول: يقلب الأمور ويحتال" — a man who turns matters over and devises stratagems. The heart's "suwaydāʾ" (core/blackness) is its innermost center where Satan seeks to establish his seat.
- Root: ذكر (Dhikr)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Remembrance, mention, recollection; the opposite of forgetfulness (nisyān).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): الذكر is the presence of a thing in the mind, whether by utterance or by heart; true dhikr is that which takes root in the heart, not mere speech of the tongue.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: uttering with the tongue. Metaphorical: the heart's presence with God, which alone has authority over the soul and repels Satan's incursions.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — The verse {إِنَّ الَّذِينَ اتَّقَوْا إِذَا مَسَّهُمْ طَائِفٌ مِنَ الشَّيْطَانِ تَذَكَّرُوا} restricts the efficacy of dhikr in repelling Satan to the God-fearing (muttaqūn), whose hearts are emptied of passions, thereby specifying the condition for its effectiveness.
22:4.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Disciplining the Soul'

23:27.arabic: وفاحشا فقد روي أن نوحا عليه السلام لما ركب السفينة حمل فيها من كل زوجين اثنين كما أمره الله تعالى فرأى في السفينة شيخا لم يعرفه فقال له نوح ما أدخلك فقال دخلت لأصيب قلوب أصحابك فتكون قلوبهم معي وأبدانهم معك فقال له نوح أخرج منها يا عدو الله فإنك لعين فقال له إبليس خمس أهلك بهن الناس وسأحدثك منهم بثلاث ولا أحدثك باثنتين فأوحى الله تعالى إلى نوح أنه لا حاجة لك بالثلاث فليحدثك بالاثنين فقال له نوح
23:27.english: Among his great gates are anger (ghaḍab) and lustful desire (shahwah). For anger is the ghoul of the intellect — when the soldier of the intellect weakens, the soldier of Satan attacks. Whenever a man becomes angry, Satan plays with him as a boy plays with a ball. It has been narrated that Moses, peace be upon him, was met by Iblis, who said to him: "O Moses, you are the one whom God chose for His message and to whom He spoke directly (taklīman). I am a creature among God's creatures. I sinned, and I wish to repent. So intercede for me to my Lord that He might accept my repentance." Moses said: "Yes." When Moses ascended the mountain and spoke with his Lord, Mighty and Majestic, and wished to descend, his Lord said to him: "Deliver the trust." Moses said: "O Lord, Your servant Iblis wishes that You accept his repentance." So God, exalted be He, revealed to Moses: "O Moses, I have already granted your request — that he prostrate before the grave of Adam so that his repentance might be accepted." Moses then met Iblis and said to him: "I have secured your request — you have been commanded to prostrate before the grave of Adam so that your repentance might be accepted." But he became angry and arrogant, saying: "I did not prostrate to him while he was alive — shall I prostrate to him dead?" Then he said to him: "O Moses, you have a right upon me because you interceded for me to your Lord. So remember me at three occasions, and I shall not destroy you in them: Remember me when you become angry, for my spirit is in your heart and my eye is in your eye, and I flow through you like the flow of blood. Remember me when you become angry — for when a man becomes angry, I blow into his nostrils, and he does not know what he does. And remember me when you encounter the battle-line (zaḥf), for I come to the son of Adam when he encounters the battle-line and remind him of his wife, his children, and his family, until he turns and flees. And beware of sitting with a woman who is not a close relative (dhāt maḥram), for I am her messenger to you and your messenger to her — I shall not cease until I tempt you with her and tempt her with you."
23:27.section_title_en: The Detailed Exposition of the Entrances of Satan into the Heart
23:27.anchors:
- Root: شيط (Shayṭ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning relates to burning, scorching, or being consumed by fire — that which is burnt and spoiled.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): الشيطان refers to the rebellious one among jinn and mankind; the term denotes one who has deviated from truth through pride and disobedience.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): "شاط اللحم" — meat that is burnt and spoiled. Metaphorical (Majaz): "شاط دمه" — his blood was spilled in vain; "أشاط السلطان دمه" — the ruler declared his blood lawful to shed. Thus the Shayṭān is so named because he is consumed by fire, or because he causes others to be consumed/destroyed.

- Root: غضب (Ghaḍab)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The boiling and agitation of the blood of the heart, seeking vengeance.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الغضب: ثوران دم القلب إرادة الانتقام" — anger is the surging of the blood of the heart desiring vengeance. When attributed to God, it means only retribution and punishment, not an emotional state.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: anger as a human emotional state. Metaphorical: "غضبت له قوائم عوج" — even inanimate things are described metaphorically. The Prophet said: "اتقوا الغضب فإنه جمرة توقد في قلب ابن آدم" — anger is a burning ember kindled in the heart of the son of Adam.

- Root: قلب (Qalb)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The heart; also the turning and revolving of a thing from one state to another.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "قلب الشيء: تصريفه وصرفه عن وجه إلى وجه" — the turning of a thing and its conversion from one aspect to another. The heart is so named because of its constant turning and fluctuation of states.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: to turn something over, to flip it. Metaphorical: "قلب المعلم الصبيان" — the teacher dismissed the boys (turned them back to their homes); "رجل قلب حول" — a man who turns matters over and devises stratagems. The heart is the seat of understanding and discernment, and its protection is the fortress against Satan.

- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The permissibility of interposing elements between a preposition and its object when the meaning remains clear, analogous to how the heart's defenses may be interposed between Satan and his objectives.

23:27.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'Disciplining the Soul'

23:116.arabic: في الجنة ولا أبالي وهؤلاء في النار ولا أبالي (1) فتعالى الله الملك الحق لا يسئل عما يفعل وهم يسئلون ولنقتصر على هذا القدر اليسير من ذكر عجائب القلب فإن استقصاءه لا يليق بعلم المعاملة وإنما ذكرنا منه ما يحتاج إليه لمعرفة أغوار علوم المعاملة وأسرارها لينتفع بها من لا يقنع بالظواهر ولا يجتزئ بالقشر عن اللباب بل يتشوق إلى معرفة دقائق حقائق الأسباب وفيما ذكرناه كفاية له ومقنع إن شاء الله تعالى والله ولي التوفيق تم كتاب عجائب القلب ولله الحمد والمنة ويتلوه كتاب رياضة النفس وتهذيب الأخلاق والحمد لله وحده وصلى الله على ك
23:116.english: I say: Know that when the Shayṭān prevails and the heart inclines to its own kind among the parties of the Shayṭān, turning away from the party of God—Exalted is He—and His saints, and aiding the party of the Shayṭān and His enemies, then there flows upon its bodily members, by virtue of the prior decree, that which is the cause of its distance from God—Exalted is He. But if the angelic attributes are predominant over the heart, the heart does not lend its ear to the Shayṭān's seduction, nor to his incitement toward the immediate world, nor to his belittling of the matter of the Hereafter. Rather, it inclines to the party of God—Exalted is He—and obedience appears upon its members in accordance with what has preceded in the decree. Thus, the heart of the believer is between two fingers of the fingers of the All-Merciful—that is, between the mutual tugging of these two hosts—and this is the meaning of "turning" (taqlīb): the transition from one party to another. As for perpetual constancy, whether with the party of the angels or with the party of the Shayṭān, that is rare on both sides. These acts of obedience and disobedience emerge from the treasuries of the Unseen into the world of witness by way of the treasury of the heart, for it is among the treasuries of the Malakūt. And when they do emerge, they become signs by which the masters of hearts recognize the prior decree. For whomever is created for Paradise, the means of obedience are made easy for him; and whomever is created for the Fire, the means of disobedience are made easy for him, and evil companions are given sway over him, and the rule of the Shayṭān is cast into his heart. For by various kinds of deceptions he beguiles the foolish, saying: "God is Merciful, so do not care"; and "All people do not fear God, so do not oppose them"; and "Life is long, so be patient until you repent tomorrow." He promises them and fills them with desires—{يَعِدُهُمْ وَيُمَنِّيهِمْ وَمَا يَعِدُهُمُ الشَّيْطَانُ إِلَّا غُرُورًا} "He promises them and fills them with desires, and the Shayṭān promises them nothing but delusion" {النساء/120}. He promises them repentance and fills them with hopes of forgiveness, and thus destroys them, by God's permission, through these ruses and what runs in their course. So he expands their hearts to accept delusion and constricts them from accepting the truth. And all of that is by God's decree and destiny: {فَمَن يُرِدِ اللَّهُ أَن يَهْدِيَهُ يَشْرَحْ صَدْرَهُ لِلْإِسْلَامِ وَمَن يُرِدْ أَن يُضِلَّهُ يَجْعَلْ صَدْرَهُ ضَيِّقًا حَرَجًا كَأَنَّمَا يَصَّعَّدُ فِي السَّمَاءِ} "Whomsoever God wishes to guide, He expands his breast to Islam; and whomsoever He wishes to lead astray, He makes his breast narrow and constricted, as though he were climbing into the sky" {الأنعام/125}. {إِن يَنصُرْكُمُ اللَّهُ فَلَا غَالِبَ لَكُمْ وَإِن يَخْذُلْكُمْ فَمَن ذَا الَّذِي يَنصُرُكُم مِّن بَعْدِهِ} "If God helps you, none can overcome you; and if He forsakes you, who is there to help you after Him?" {آل عمران/160}. He is the Guide and the Misleader; He does what He wills and decrees what He desires. There is no repeller of His judgment and no reverser of His decree. He created Paradise and created for it its people, and employed them in obedience; and He created the Fire and created for it its people, and employed them in disobedience. And He made known to creation the mark of the people of Paradise and the people of the Fire, saying: {إِنَّ الْأَبْرَارَ لَفِي نَعِيمٍ وَإِنَّ الْفُجَّارَ لَفِي جَحِيمٍ} "Verily, the righteous shall be in bliss, and verily, the wicked shall be in the Blazing Fire" {الانفطار/13-14}. Then He—Exalted is He—said, as related from His Prophet, peace be upon him: "These are in Paradise, and I do not care; and these are in the Fire, and I do not care." Exalted is God, the King, the Truth! {لَا يُسْأَلُ عَمَّا يَفْعَلُ وَهُمْ يُسْأَلُونَ} "He is not questioned about what He does, but they shall be questioned" {الأنبياء/23}.
23:116.section_title_en: The Explanation of the Heart's Rapid Fluctuation and the Division of Hearts Between Change and Constancy
23:116.anchors:
- Root: قلب (q-l-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of turning, overturning, and revolving a thing from one face to another; the heart is so named for its constant oscillation.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "قلب الشيء: تصريفه وصرفه عن وجه إلى وجه" — the heart's essence is its perpetual turning and redirection; its fluctuation is not accidental but constitutive of its nature.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): physical overturning. Metaphorical (Majaz): "رجل قلب حول: يقلب الأمور ويحتال" — the heart's movement between the two hosts (jundān) is a real, dynamic turnover of allegiance.
- Root: شيط (sh-y-t)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Burning, scorching, or spoiling meat by over-smoking; blood going to waste.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The Shayṭān is so named for his being burned and banished from mercy.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Metaphorical: "شاط دمه إذا بطل" — the Shayṭān's work is to render the servant's spiritual life wasted and nullified, as blood spilled in vain.
- Root: حزب (ḥ-z-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: A group or party with cohesion and strength; al-Ḥayzabūn (the old woman) shows the root's extension to a gathered mass.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الحزب: جماعة فيها غلظ" — the party of God (ḥizb Allāh) versus the party of the Shayṭān (ḥizb al-Shayṭān) are two opposing, organized camps in cosmic conflict.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: a band of partisans. Metaphorical: "قرأ حزبه من القرآن" — a portion assigned; here, the heart is assigned to one of the two parties by divine decree.
- Root: خلق (kh-l-q)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Measuring and smoothing; creating as precise estimation.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الخلق أصله: التقدير المستقيم" — creation is origination upon a just measure; God's creative act entails the pre-ordainment of ends.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: shaping leather before cutting. Metaphorical: "خلق الله الخلق: أوجده على تقدير أوجبته الحكمة" — God's creation of Paradise and Hellfire and their inhabitants is an act of wise, pre-eternal determination.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — The phrase "إنما ذكرنا منه ما يحتاج إليه" restricts the author's purpose: only the necessary measure of the heart's wonders is expounded, not exhaustive treatment, signaling a deliberate boundary of the science of practical religion (ʿilm al-muʿāmalah).
23:116.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Disciplining the Soul'

28:27.arabic: الورد بلغنا أن إبليس تمثل ليحيى بن زكريا عليهما السلام وقال إني أريد أن أنصحك قال لا حاجة لي في نصحك ولكن أخبرني عن بني آدم قال هم عندنا ثلاثة أصناف أما صنف منهم وهم أشد الأصناف علينا نقبل على أحدهم حتى نفتنه ونتمكن منه فيفزع إلى الاستغفار والتوبة فيفسد علينا كل شيء أدركنا منه ثم نعود إليه فيعود فلا نحن نيأس منه ولا نحن ندرك منه حاجتنا فنحن منه في عناء وأما الصنف الآخر فهم في أيدينا بمنزل الكرة في أيدي صبيانكم نقلبهم كيف شئنا قد كفونا أنفسهم وأما الصنف الثالث فهم مثلك معصومون لا نقدر منهم على شيء فإن قلت ف
28:27.english: As for the reports (al-akhbār), Mujāhid said: Iblīs has five offspring, each of whom he has appointed over a certain aspect of his affair: Thabr, al-Aʿwar, Mabsūṭ, Dāsim, and Zalanbūr. As for Thabr, he is the master of calamities, commanding [people] to cry "Woe and destruction" (al-thubūr), to tear their collars, to strike their cheeks, and to make the claims of the Age of Ignorance (daʿwā al-jāhiliyyah). As for al-Aʿwar, he is the master of fornication (al-zinā), commanding it and beautifying it. As for Mabsūṭ, he is the master of lying. As for Dāsim, he enters with a man to his family, casting blame upon them in his presence and angering him against them. As for Zalanbūr, he is the master of the marketplace, and because of him people never cease to be mutually aggrieved and complaining. The Satan of prayer is called Khinzab, and the Satan of ablution is called al-Walhān.
28:27.section_title_en: On the Visions of Satan and the Angel — Between True Form and Symbolic Representation
28:27.anchors:
- Root: مثل (maththala)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To stand before, to represent, to form an image or likeness of something.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-mathal (the similitude) is the saying that depicts the state of the thing; al-tamthīl is the act of representing a meaning through a sensory form that corresponds to it.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Haqiqah: "maththala" means to stand erect before someone. Majaz: To set forth a parable (daraba mathalan) — the transfer from physical standing to the representation of an abstract meaning through a concrete image.
- Root: صور (ṣawwara)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To form, to shape, to give a figure or image to something.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الصورة: ما ينتقش به الأعيان، ويتميز بها غيرها، وذلك ضربان: أحدهما محسوس يدركه الخاصة والعامة... والثاني: معقول يدركه الخاصة دون العامة" — Form is twofold: sensory form perceived by all, and intelligible form perceived only by the elite.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Haqiqah: physical shaping and bending. Majaz: The inclination of the heart toward something — "وأرى لك إليه صورة: ميلة بالمودة" — a metaphorical "form" is an inclination of affection.
- Root: كشف (kashafa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To uncover, to reveal, to remove a covering.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-kashf is the removal of the veil (al-ḥijāb) between the perceiver and the perceived, whether sensory or intellectual.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Haqiqah: removing a physical covering. Majaz: Unveiling of spiritual realities (mukāshafah) to the hearts of the purified.
- Root: خنس (khanasa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To withdraw, to shrink back, to lurk.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-khunūs is the retreat of the whisperer (al-waswās) when God is remembered — as in {«الْخَنَّاسِ»} (Q. 114:4).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Haqiqah: physical retreat. Majaz: The withdrawal of Satan's influence from the heart upon the remembrance of God.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد (Restriction & Focused Predication) — The use of "إنما" and restrictive constructions to distinguish the exclusive means of perceiving true forms (only through prophetic light) from the general means of symbolic perception.
28:27.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Disciplining the Soul'

35:2.arabic: ورحمته ما يفتح الله للناس من رحمة فلا ممسك لها وهذه الرحمة مبذولة بحكم الجود والكرم من الله سبحانه وتعالى غير مضنون بها على أحد ولكن إنما تظهر في القلوب المتعرضة لنفحات رحمة الله تعالى كما قال صلى الله عليه وسلم إن لربكم في أيام دهركم لنفحات ألا فتعرضوا لها (1) حديث يقول الله عز وجل لقد طال شوق الأبرار إلى لقائي الحديث لم أجد له أصلا إلا أن صاحب الفردوس خرجه من حديث أبي الدرداء ولم يذكر له ولده في مسند الفردوس إسنادا وبقوله تعالى من تقرب إلي شبرا تقربت إليه ذراعا (2) حديث لولا أن الشياطين يحو
35:2.english: Know that just as the rational person does not know the necessary sciences (al-ʿulūm al-ḍarūriyyah) nor what distinguishes the state of the rational one from what he has acquired of the theoretical sciences, so too does the rational person not know what Allah has opened for His friends (awliyāʾ) and His prophets of the prerogatives of His gentleness (luṭf) and mercy. Whatever mercy Allah opens to people, none can withhold it. This mercy is dispensed by the decree of bounty and generosity from Allah, Glorified and Exalted, not grudged to anyone. But it only appears in hearts that expose themselves to the wafts of the mercy of Allah, Exalted — as he, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Indeed, your Lord has, in the days of your time, wafts of mercy — so expose yourselves to them." (1) Hadith: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: "Long has been the yearning of the righteous for My meeting" — the hadith. I found no source for it except that the author of al-Firdaws transmitted it from the hadith of Abū al-Dardāʾ, and his son did not mention for it in the Musnad of al-Firdaws an isnād.
35:2.section_title_en: The Revival of the Religious Sciences — Section 579: The Human's Distinguishing Property is Knowledge and Wisdom; The Heart as the Seat of the King
35:2.anchors:
- Root: قلب (q-l-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of turning over, revolving, and transformation from one state to another; the heart as that which is constantly turning and fluctuating.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The heart (qalb) is so named for its constant turning (taqallub) between states; it is the seat of perception and understanding, the faculty by which one grasps realities.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: turning a thing over. Metaphorical: the heart as the seat of understanding and the center of the human kingdom, that which governs and directs the faculties.
- Root: علم (ʿ-l-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Knowledge, perception, and certainty; the mark or trace by which a thing is known.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Knowledge is the apprehension of a thing as it truly is; it is the distinguishing property of the human being and the purpose of his creation.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: knowing. Metaphorical: the light by which the heart perceives realities, the noblest of which is knowledge of God.
- Root: ملك (m-l-k)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Possession, sovereignty, and dominion; a king who rules over a domain.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The king is one who possesses authority and commands; the heart is the king of the human body, ruling over its faculties.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: a king. Metaphorical: the heart as the sovereign of the human kingdom, with the faculties as its subjects, messengers, and servants.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب التشبيه والتمثيل (The Chapter of Simile and Analogy) — The use of extended analogies (tamthīl) to clarify abstract realities through concrete images, where the comparison is drawn between the relations of parts, not merely individual attributes.
35:2.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'Disciplining the Soul'

36:7.arabic: كالأنعام بل هم أضل سبيلا وبقوله عز وجل لقد حق القول على أكثرهم فهم لا يؤمنون وبقوله سواء عليهم أأنذرتهم أم لم تنذرهم لا يؤمنون ورب قلب هذا حاله بالإضافة إلى بعض الشهوات كالذي يتورع عن بعض الأشياء ولكنه إذا رأى وجها حسنا لم يملك عينه وقلبه وطاش عقله وسقط مساك قلبه أو كالذي لا يملك نفسه فيما فيه الجاه والرياسة والكبر ولا يبقى معه مسكة للتثبت عند ظهور أسبابه أو كالذي لا يملك نفسه عند الغضب مهما استحقر وذكر عيب من عيوبه أو كالذي لا يملك نفسه عند القدرة على أخذ درهم أو دينار بل يتهالك عليه تهالك الواله المستهتر فينسى فيه ال
36:7.english: Know that the heart, as we have mentioned, is surrounded by the attributes we have described, and the traces and states pour into it from the gateways we have set forth. It is as if it were a target perpetually struck from every side. When something afflicts it, it is affected by it; then it is struck from another side by that which opposes it, and so its state changes. If the devil descends upon it and calls it to passion (hawā), the angel descends upon it and turns it away from that. If one devil drags it toward evil, another devil drags it toward something else; and if one angel draws it toward good, another draws it toward something else. Thus at times it is contested between two angels, at times between two devils, and at times between an angel and a devil — it is never, ever left neglected. To this points the saying of the Exalted: {وَنُقَلِّبُ أَفْئِدَتَهُمْ وَأَبْصَارَهُمْ} (And We turn their hearts and their visions) {«الأنعام/110»}. And because the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) was privy to the wondrous handiwork of Allah the Exalted in the marvels of the heart and its overturning, he used to swear by it, saying: "No, by the Turner of the hearts." (1)
36:7.section_title_en: The Wonders of the Heart: Its States of Stability, Inclination, and Fluctuation Between the Two Attracting Forces
36:7.anchors:
- Root: قلب (q-l-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To turn a thing over, to revolve it, to divert it from one face to another; the heart is so named for its constant turning and fluctuation.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "قلب الشيء: تصريفه وصرفه عن وجه إلى وجه" — the heart's perpetual overturning is its very essence; its states are never fixed, and its rectitude or corruption follows its turning.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): "قلب الشيء قلبا: حوله عن وجهه" — physical overturning. Metaphorical (Majaz): "رجل قلب حول: يقلب الأمور ويحتال" — one who turns matters over and manages them; the heart's fluctuation between the two attractants is a real, continuous overturning.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The periodic structure of the opening sentence, with its cascading circumstantial clauses, requires careful tracking of the governing verb and its dependent states to preserve the causal sequence of the heart's affliction and response.
36:7.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Disciplining the Soul'

36:10.arabic: يؤمنون وبقوله سواء عليهم أأنذرتهم أم لم تنذرهم لا يؤمنون ورب قلب هذا حاله بالإضافة إلى بعض الشهوات كالذي يتورع عن بعض الأشياء ولكنه إذا رأى وجها حسنا لم يملك عينه وقلبه وطاش عقله وسقط مساك قلبه أو كالذي لا يملك نفسه فيما فيه الجاه والرياسة والكبر ولا يبقى معه مسكة للتثبت عند ظهور أسبابه أو كالذي لا يملك نفسه عند الغضب مهما استحقر وذكر عيب من عيوبه أو كالذي لا يملك نفسه عند القدرة على أخذ درهم أو دينار بل يتهالك عليه تهالك الواله المستهتر فينسى فيه المروءة والتقوى فكل ذلك لتصاعد دخان الهوى إلى القل
36:10.english: Know that the heart, as we have mentioned, is surrounded by the attributes we have described, and the traces and states pour into it from the gateways we have set forth. It is as if it were a target perpetually struck from every side. When something afflicts it, it is affected by it; then it is struck from another side by that which opposes it, and so its state changes. If the devil descends upon it and calls it to passion (hawā), the angel descends upon it and turns it away from that. If one devil drags it toward evil, another devil drags it toward something else; and if one angel draws it toward good, another draws it toward something else. Thus at times it is contested between two angels, at times between two devils, and at times between an angel and a devil — it is never, ever left neglected. To this points the saying of the Exalted: {وَنُقَلِّبُ أَفْئِدَتَهُمْ وَأَبْصَارَهُمْ} (And We turn their hearts and their visions) {«الأنعام/110»}. And because the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) was privy to the wondrous handiwork of Allah the Exalted in the marvels of the heart and its overturning, he used to swear by it, saying: "No, by the Turner of the hearts." (1)
36:10.section_title_en: The Wonders of the Heart: Its States of Stability, Inclination, and Fluctuation Between the Two Attracting Forces
36:10.anchors:

  * Lisan / Ayn: To turn a thing over, to revolve it, to divert it from one face to another; the heart is so named for its constant turning and fluctuation.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "قلب الشيء: تصريفه وصرفه عن وجه إلى وجه" — the heart's perpetual overturning is its very essence; its states are never fixed, and its rectitude or corruption follows its turning.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): "قلب الشيء قلبا: حوله عن وجهه" — physical overturning. Metaphorical (Majaz): "رجل قلب حول: يقلب الأمور ويحتال" — one who turns matters over and manages them; the heart's fluctuation between the two attractants is a real, continuous overturning.

36:60.arabic: تعالى ألم أعهد إليكم يا بني آدم أن لا تعبدوا الشيطان إنه لكم عدو مبين فينبغي للعبد أن يشتغل بدفع العدو عن نفسه لا بالسؤال عن أصله ونسبه ومسكنه نعم ينبغي أن يسأل عن سلاحه ليدفعه عن نفسه وسلاح الشيطان الهوى والشهوات وذلك كاف للعالمين فأما معرفة ذاته وصفاته وحقيقته نعوذ بالله منه وحقيقة الملائكة فذلك ميدان العارفين المتغلغلين في علوم المكاشفات فلا يحتاج في علم المعاملة إلى معرفته نعم ينبغي أن يعلم أن الخواطر تنقسم إلى ما يعلم قطعا أنه داع إلى الشر فلا يخفى كونه وسوسة وإلى ما يعلم أنه داع إلى الخير فلا يشك في كونه إلها
36:60.english: He said — and by my father, a face that will not prosper (1) — the hadith that Satan runs through the son of Adam like the running of blood has already been mentioned. That is because hunger breaks the appetite, and the course of Satan is through the appetites. And because the appetites surround the heart from all its sides, God—exalted is He—said, informing of Iblis: {«I will surely sit in wait for them on Your straight path. Then I will come to them from before them and from behind them and from their right and from their left»} (7:16-17). And he—peace and blessings be upon him—said: "Verily, Satan sat in wait for the son of Adam on his paths. He sat for him on the path of Islam and said: 'Will you submit and abandon your religion and the religion of your forefathers?' But he disobeyed him and submitted. Then he sat for him on the path of emigration (hijrah) and said: 'Will you emigrate and abandon your land and your sky?' But he disobeyed him and emigrated. Then he sat for him on the path of jihad and said: 'Will you strive? For it is the destruction of the soul and wealth — you will fight and be killed, your women will be married and your wealth divided.' But he disobeyed him and strove." (2) The hadith "There is no one among you except that he has a companion from the jinn" has already been mentioned.
36:60.section_title_en: The Revival of the Religious Sciences — Section 598: On the Whisperings of Satan, the Divine Subtleties, and the Means of Defense
36:60.anchors:
- Root: شيط (Shayṭ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of burning, scorching, or being consumed by fire; also one who is destroyed or perishes.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): الشيطان refers to the rebellious one among jinn and mankind who leads astray; the term denotes one distanced from divine mercy.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): burning or scorching of meat. Metaphorical (Majaz): "شاط دمه" — his blood was spilled in vain; "أشاط السلطان دمه" — the ruler declared his blood forfeit. Thus Satan is so named for his being consumed by divine wrath and for his causing others to perish.
- Root: لهم (Lahm)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Swallowing or devouring greedily; the larynx or throat (al-lahāt).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): الإلهام is the casting of something into the heart (al-rawʿ), specifically from God or the higher assembly (al-malaʾ al-aʿlā). It is akin to the "touch" (lamah) of the angel or the "breathing" (nafth) into the heart.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: to swallow or gulp down. Metaphorical: a horse that "swallows the ground" (i.e., devours distance with speed); a generous man who "swallows" the needs of others. Thus ilhām is the soul's swift reception of divine inspiration, like swallowing.
- Root: علم (ʿAlima)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Knowledge as the mark or trace by which something is known; a signpost (ʿalam).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): العلم is the apprehension of a thing in its true reality (idrāk al-shayʾ bi-ḥaqīqatihi), divided into apprehension of the essence and judgment upon it.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: knowledge as direct cognition. Metaphorical: "أعلام الدين" — the towering landmarks of the religion; "معالم الطريق" — the traces by which the road is recognized. Thus knowledge is the signpost illuminating the path of salvation.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد (Restriction and Specification) — The particle "إنما" restricts the predicate to the subject alone, excluding all else. This is crucial for understanding statements like "إنما يدعو حزبه" — Satan calls only his party, restricting his influence to those who follow him.
36:60.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Disciplining the Soul'

51:49.arabic: مقابلة الخذلان وإليه الإشارة بقوله تعالى {ومن كل شيء خلقنا زوجين} فإن الموجودات كلها متقابلة مزدوجة إلا الله تعالى فإنه فرد لا مقابل له بل هو الواحد الحق الخالق للأزواج كلها فالقلب متجاذب بين الشيطان والملك وقد قال صلى الله عليه وسلم في القلب لمتان لمة من الملك إيعاد بالخير وتصديق بالحق فمن وجد ذلك فليعلم أنه من الله سبحانه وليحمد الله ولمة من العدو إيعاد بالشر وتكذيب بالحق ونهي عن الخير فمن وجد ذلك فليستعذ بالله من الشيطان الرجيم ثم تلا قوله تعالى الشيطان يعدكم الفقر ويأمركم بالفحشاء (1) أخرجه الترمذي والنسائي (2) ح
51:49.english: The angel is an expression for a created being (khalq) whom God, Exalted is His majesty, created—whose very attribute is the effusion of good, the bestowal of knowledge, the uncovering of truth, the promising of good, and the commanding of what is right. He created him and subjugated him to that. The Satan is an expression for a created being whose attribute is the opposite of that—namely, the promising of evil, the commanding of indecency, and the frightening with poverty at the moment of resolving upon good. Thus whispering stands in opposition to inspiration, the Satan in opposition to the angel, and divine success in opposition to abandonment. And to this points His saying, Exalted is He: {«وَمِن كُلِّ شَيْءٍ خَلَقْنَا زَوْجَيْنِ»} (And of all things We have created pairs) [Quran 51:49]. For all existent things are paired and opposed—except God, Exalted is He, for He is the One (al-Fard) who has no opposite. Rather, He is the One, the True, the Creator of all pairs.
51:49.section_title_en: The Heart's Attraction Between the Angel and the Satan: On Inspiration and Whispering
51:49.anchors:
- Root: خطر (khaṭara)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The passing of something through the mind; the occurrence of a thought or notion.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The initial stirring of the heart toward an action—the first movement of intention.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the striking of an idea upon the heart. Metaphorical: the very inception of volitional acts.
- Root: ملك (malaka)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Possession, dominion; the angel as a created being entrusted with a function.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The angel is a subtle spiritual reality (laṭīfah) created for the effusion of good and the conveyance of divine command.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: one who possesses and governs. Metaphorical: the spiritual power that inclines the heart toward truth.
- Root: وسوس (waswasa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The faint, hidden sound; the subtle, insinuating call.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The whispering of the Satan—the evil suggestion that invites to transgression.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the quiet, indistinct voice. Metaphorical: the insinuation of evil into the heart.
- Root: لطف (laṭufa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Gentleness, subtlety, refinement.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The divine subtlety (al-luṭf) by which the heart is prepared to receive inspiration—a spiritual, immaterial reality.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: that which is fine and delicate. Metaphorical: the divine grace that disposes the heart toward good.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — The restriction of each cause to its specific effect, and the pairing of contrasting terms (inspiration vs. whispering; angel vs. Satan; success vs. abandonment) to establish the precise correspondence between spiritual causes and their consequences.
51:49.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'Disciplining the Soul'

59:16.arabic: ظل إلا ظله وعد منهم رجل دعته امرأة ذات جمال وحسب إلى نفسها فقال إني أخاف الله رب العالمين (2) وقصة يوسف عليه السلام وامتناعه من زليخا مع القدرة ومع رغبتها معروفة وقد أثنى الله تعالى عليه بذلك في كتابه العزيز وهو إمام لكل من وفق لمجاهدة الشيطان في هذه الشهوة العظيمة وروي أن سليمان بن يسار كان من أحسن الناس وجها فدخلت عليه امرأة فسألته نفسه فامتنع عليها وخرج هاربا من منزله وتركها فيه قال سليمان فرأيت تلك الليلة في المنام يوسف عليه السلام وكأني أقول له أنت يوسف قال نعم أنا يوسف الذي هممت وأنت سليمان الذي لم تهم أشار إلى قوله
59:16.english: ...which one is ashamed of and fears to plunge into. And the abstention of most people from its requirements is either due to incapacity, or fear, or shame, or concern for preserving one's body — and in none of these is there any reward, for that is merely preferring one share of one's worldly desires over another share. Yes — from divine protection (al-ʿiṣmah) is that one is not able [to sin]; so in these obstacles there is a benefit, namely the repulsion of sin. For whoever abandons fornication, its sin is repelled from him by whatever cause his abandonment occurred. Rather, the virtue and abundant reward lie in abandoning it out of fear of God — may He be exalted — while possessing the ability, with the removal of obstacles, the facilitation of means, and especially at the height of genuine desire. And this is the station of the veracious (al-ṣiddīqīn). For this reason, the Prophet — peace be upon him — said: "Whoever loves passionately, then remains chaste, then conceals [his love], then dies — he dies a martyr."(1)
59:16.section_title_en: The Book of Breaking the Two Desires — Section 654: On Chastity, Guarding the Gaze, and the Virtue of Restraining Desire
59:16.anchors:
- **Root: ع ف ف** (ʿaffa)
  * **Lisan / Ayn**: Core meaning of abstaining from what is unlawful, refraining, and remaining chaste; al-ʿafāf is the state of one who abstains from forbidden things.
  * **Al-Raghib (Mufradat)**: Theological nuance — ʿiffah (chastity) is a virtue of the soul that restrains the appetitive faculty from pursuing what is not permissible; it is a station of the ṣiddīqūn (veracious ones).
  * **Al-Zamakhshari (Asas)**: Literal (ḥaqīqah) — physical abstention from unlawful acts; Metaphorical (majāz) — the heart's abstention from coveting what God has forbidden, which is the higher reality of chastity.

- **Root: غ ب ق** (ghabaqa)
  * **Lisan / Ayn**: The evening drink (al-ghabūq) — the milking or drink given at nightfall; contrasted with al-ṣabūḥ (the morning drink).
  * **Al-Raghib (Mufradat)**: In the hadith of the three men in the cave, the term marks the temporal precision of filial devotion — serving parents before any other claim, even at the boundary of night.
  * **Al-Zamakhshari (Asas)**: Literal — the evening milking; the narrative use in the hadith is literal, denoting the exact act of service delayed out of reverence.

- **Root: ه م م** (hamma)
  * **Lisan / Ayn**: To intend, to resolve upon a matter; al-hamm is the initial stirring of intention before full determination.
  * **Al-Raghib (Mufradat)**: In Q. 12:24 {«وَلَقَدْ هَمَّتْ بِهِ وَهَمَّ بِهَا لَوْلَا أَنْ رَأَى بُرْهَانَ رَبِّهِ»} — "And certainly she desired him, and he would have desired her, had it not been that he saw the proof of his Lord" — the term distinguishes between a passing inclination (hamm) and a settled resolve; Yūsuf's hamm was repelled by divine proof, while Zulaykhā's was consummated in action.
  * **Al-Zamakhshari (Asas)**: Literal — the inward movement of intention; the rhetorical force lies in the contrast between the two hamm-s, one punished and one pardoned.

- **Root: ن ظ ر** (naẓara)
  * **Lisan / Ayn**: To look, to gaze; al-naẓar is the act of sight, whether physical or intellectual.
  * **Al-Raghib (Mufradat)**: The gaze (naẓar) is the gateway to desire; the Quranic phrase {«يَعْلَمُ خَائِنَةَ الْأَعْيُنِ»} — "He knows the treachery of the eyes" (Q. 40:19) — indicates that the look which steals toward the forbidden is itself an act of betrayal recorded by God.
  * **Al-Zamakhshari (Asas)**: Literal — the first glance that occurs unintentionally; Metaphorical — the second glance is the "treachery of the eyes," for it is a deliberate return to what the first glance stumbled upon by accident.

- **Root: ر و د** (rāwada)
  * **Lisan / Ayn**: To seek, to desire, to solicit; murāwadah is the act of soliciting someone for an unlawful purpose.
  * **Al-Raghib (Mufradat)**: In the Yūsuf narrative, murāwadah denotes the persistent solicitation toward sin; the term carries the weight of repeated, deliberate pursuit.
  * **Al-Zamakhshari (Asas)**: Literal — the physical act of solicitation; the narrative contexts in this section use the term literally for the woman's pursuit of the young man.

- **Sibawayh Rule**: **Bāb al-ḥaṣr wa-l-taqyīd bi-innamā** (Restriction and Focused Predication with innamā)
  * The particle innamā restricts and confines the predicate to the subject alone, negating all else. In the woman's statement "innamā urīdu mā yakūnu min al-rajuli ilā ahlihī" — "I only desire what comes from a man to his wife" — the restriction (ḥaṣr) intensifies the gravity of the solicitation, making the young man's resistance all the more virtuous.
