2:171.arabic: يؤثر فيه أصلا ف مثله كمثل الذي ينعق بما لا يسمع إلا دعاء ونداء صم بكم عمي فهم لا يعقلون بل صاحب القلب تؤثر فيه الكلمة من الحكمة يسمعها قال جعفر الخلدي دخل رجل من أهل خراسان على الجنيد وعنده جماعة فقال للجنيد متى يستوي عند العبد حامده وذامه فقال بعض الشيوخ إذا دخل البيمارستان وقيد بقيدين فقال الجنيد ليس هذا من شأنك ثم أقبل على الرجل وقال إذا تحقق أنه مخلوق فشهق الرجل شهقة ومات فإن قلت فإن كان سماع القرآن مفيدا للوجد فما بالهم يجتمعون على سماع الغناء من القوالين دون القارئين فكان ينبغي أن يكون اجتماعهم وتواجدهم في حلق القراء لا حلق
2:171.english: Some of the Sufis said: "One night I was reciting this verse: {كُلُّ نَفْسٍ ذَائِقَةُ الْمَوْتِ} «Every soul shall taste death» [Q. 3:185]. I kept repeating it, and lo, a caller cried out to me: 'How long will you repeat this verse? You have killed four of the jinn who have not raised their heads to the sky since they were created.'"
2:171.section_title_en: On the Ecstatic States (Wajd) Produced by Qur'anic Recitation and the Superiority of Song (Ghinā') in Stirring the Heart
2:171.anchors:
- Root: وجد (w-j-d)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of finding, attaining, and also denoting the emotional state of ecstasy or rapture that "finds" the heart.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In the theological context, 'wajd' is the state of spiritual finding—a direct, overwhelming apprehension of divine realities that bypasses discursive reasoning.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah) usage denotes "finding" a lost object; metaphorical (Majaz) usage denotes the heart "finding" its spiritual state, leading to agitation and ecstasy.
- Root: سمع (s-m-')
  * Lisan / Ayn: The faculty of hearing; also the ear itself.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Hearing can be literal (perception of sound) or figurative (understanding, obedience, acceptance). The heart's "hearing" is a deeper comprehension.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "سمعته" (I heard him). Metaphorical: "سمع الله لمن حمده" (God answers/he accepts the one who praises Him), indicating a responsive, transformative hearing.
- Root: موت (m-w-t)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Death; the opposite of life.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Death is the cessation of the soul's governance over the body, a separation. In the spiritual context, it can be a metaphorical death to worldly desires.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical death. Metaphorical: "أحيا الله البلد الميت" (God revives the dead land), indicating spiritual revival or the death of the ego.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — Used to emphasize that the stirring of the heart is exclusively through what is appropriate to its state, as in the phrase "إنما المحرك لما في القلب ما يناسبه" (The only thing that moves what is in the heart is that which is suitable to it).
2:171.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Audition and Ecstasy'

5:83.arabic: وقد أثنى الله تعالى على أهل الوجد بالقرآن فقال تعالى {وإذا سمعوا ما أنزل إلى الرسول ترى أعينهم تفيض من الدمع مما عرفوا من الحق} وروي أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كان يصلي ولصدره أزيز كأزيز المرجل (7) وأما ما نقل من الوجد بالقرآن عن الصحابة رضي الله عنهم والتابعين فكثير فمنهم من صعق ومنهم من بكى ومنهم من غشي عليه ومنهم من مات في غشيته وروى أن زرارة بن أوفى وكان من التابعين كان يؤم الناس بالرقة فقرأ {فإذا نقر في الناقور} فصعق ومات في محرابه رحمه الله وسمع عمر رضي الله عنه رجلا يقرأ إن عذاب ربك لواقع ماله من دافع فصاح صيحة وخر مغشيا عليه فحمل إلى بيته فلم يزل مريضا في بي
5:83.english:
**QUAD_ANCHORS:**
- Root: وجد (Wajd)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The root وجد encompasses multiple senses: finding/attaining (إدراك), intense love (الحب الشديد), grief (الحزن), and wealth/sufficiency (الغنى). Al-Khalil notes the range: "الوجد: الحب. والوجد: الحزن. والوجد: الغنى. والوجد: إدراك الشيء"
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الوجد: إدراك الشيء على خلاف ما يطلب" — and in the technical terminology of the Sufis: "ما يصادف القلب من واردات الأحوال" (what the heart encounters of the influxes of spiritual states)
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal sense is finding/attaining; metaphorical extension (majāz) in devotional context: "وجد فلان في العبادة وجدا: إذا أتى بها على وجهها مع حضور القلب"
- Root: طبع (Tabʿ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الطبع: السجية التي جبل عليها الإنسان" — the innate disposition upon which one is created; also "الختم" (sealing)
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الطبع: السجية التي جبل عليها الإنسان" — the original constitution
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Distinguishes "مطبوع" (innate/natural) from "متكلف" (deliberately acquired) — "فلان مطبوع على الكرم، ومتكلف له"
- Root: كلف (Kulfah/Takalluf)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "التكلف: تجشم ما لا يلزمك" — undertaking what is not incumbent upon you with effort and hardship
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "التكلف: تجشم ما ليس من شأنه" — burdening oneself with what is not one's natural concern
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "تكلفت الأمر: تجشمته على مشقة" — deliberate self-imposition of effort
- Root: سمع (Samāʿ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Auditory perception; also what is heard — recitation, song, remembrance
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "السماع عند الصوفية: ما يهيج الوجد من الأصوات الموزونة" — that which stirs ecstatic finding from measured sounds
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "السماع عند القوم: حضور مجلس يهيج الأحوال الشريفة" — attending an assembly that stirs noble spiritual states
- Root: عشق (ʿIshq)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "العشق: فرط الحب" — excessive love; from "العشقة" — a plant that twines around another
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "العشق: فرط الحب، وأصله من عشقة النبات وهي ما التف منه على غيره"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "العشق مجاز في حق الله تعالى" — metaphorical when applied to God
- Root: بكى (Bukāʾ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Weeping, shedding tears
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "البكاء: إجراء الدمع من عين لحزن أو غيره"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "تباكى: تكلف البكاء" — deliberate self-induced weeping
- Root: صعق (Ṣaʿq)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الصعق: الغشي. والصعق: الموت" — swooning/loss of consciousness; death
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الصعق: غشية تعرض من صوت شديد أو هول"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "صعق من هول الأمر: إذا غشي عليه من شدة الخوف"
- Root: خشع (Khushūʿ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الخشوع: الخضوع والتذلل" — humility and submissiveness
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الخشوع: التذلل والخضوع، وقيل: الخشوع في الصوت والبصر، والخضوع في البدن"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "خشعت الأصوات: سكنت. وخشع البصر: انكسر"
- Root: أنس (Uns)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الأنس: نقيض الوحشة" — the opposite of loneliness/estrangement
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الأنس: حضور القلب مع المحبوب" — the heart's presence with the Beloved
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "الأنس بالله: سكون القلب إليه"
- Root: وجل (Wajal)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الوجل: الخوف مع اضطراب القلب" — fear accompanied by cardiac agitation
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الوجل: الخوف مع اضطراب القلب"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "الوجل: أشد من الخوف، فإنه مع اضطراب"
- Root: طمأن (Ṭumaʾnīnah)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الطمأنينة: السكون" — tranquility
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الطمأنينة: سكون القلب بعد اضطراب"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "اطمأن القلب: سكن بعد اضطراب"
- Root: قشعر (Iqshirʿār)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "القشعريرة: تقبض الجلد من الخوف" — contraction of the skin from fear
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الاقشعرار: انقباض الجلد وتقبضه من الخوف"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "اقشعر الجلد من الخوف: إذا تقبض"
- Root: لين (Līn)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "اللين: ضد الخشونة" — softness, opposite of hardness
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "اللين: نقيض الخشونة"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "لان قلبه: إذا سكن وخشع"
- Root: غشي (Ghashy)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الغشي: الإغماء" — loss of consciousness
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الغشية: ما يغشى القلب من شدة الوجد"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "غشي عليه: إذا أغمي عليه من شدة وجد أو خوف"
- Root: زعق (Zaʿq)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الزعق: الصياح الشديد" — violent screaming
  * Al-Raghib (Al-Mufradat): "الزعق: الصياح الشديد"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "زعق: صاح بأعلى صوته"
- Root: أزيز (Azīz)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الأزيز: صوت النار والمرجل" — the sound of fire and boiling pot
  * Al-Raghib (Al-Mufradat): "الأزيز: صوت النار والمرجل ونحوهما"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "أزيز الصدر: صوت يسمع من شدة البكاء والوجد"
- Root: شهق (Shahīq)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الشهيق: رد النفس إلى الداخل بصوت" — drawing breath inward with sound
  * Al-Raghib (Al-Mufradat): "الشهيق: رد النفس إلى الداخل بصوت"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "شهق الرجل: إذا خرجت نفسه بصوت من شدة الوجد"
- Root: حزن (Ḥuzn)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الحزن: ضد السرور" — grief, opposite of joy
  * Al-Raghib (Al-Mufradat): "الحزن: ألم النفس"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "الحزن: ألم النفس، وهو مجاز من حزن الأرض" (metaphorical extension from rough ground)
- Root: شيب (Shayb)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الشيب: بياض الشعر" — whitening of hair
  * Al-Raghib (Al-Mufradat): "الشيب: بياض الشعر"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "شيبتني هود: أي: كبرتني وأحزنتني حتى شاب شعري"
- Root: ذرف (Dharf)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الذرف: سيلان الدمع" — flowing of tears
  * Al-Raghib (Al-Mufradat): "ذرفت العين: سال دمعها"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "ذرفت عينه: إذا سال دمعها من حزن"
- Root: فيض (Fayḍ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الفيض: سيلان الماء" — overflowing of water
  * Al-Raghib (Al-Mufradat): "الفيض: جريان الماء بكثرة"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "فاضت العين بالدمع: سالت. وفاض القلب: امتلأ"
- Root: نقر (Naqr)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "النقر: الضرب على الشيء حتى يصوت" — striking something until it sounds
  * Al-Raghib (Al-Mufradat): "الناقور: الصور" — the Trumpet
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "الناقور: الصور الذي ينفخ فيه إسرافيل"
- Root: رعش (Riʿshah)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الرعدة: الاضطراب" — trembling
  * Al-Raghib (Al-Mufradat): "الارتعداد: الاضطراب"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "ارتعدت فرائصه: اضطربت من شدة الخوف"
- Root: فرص (Farīṣah)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الفريصة: لحمة بين الجنب والكتف ترعد عند الفزع" — the flesh between the side and shoulder blade that trembles at fright
  * Al-Raghib (Al-Mufradat): "الفريصة: لحمة بين الجنب والكتف ترعد عند الفزع"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "ارتعدت فرائصه: من شدة الخوف"
- Root: عما (ʿAmā)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "العمى: ذهاب البصر. والعمى: ذهاب البصيرة" — blindness of sight; blindness of insight
  * Al-Raghib (Al-Mufradat): "العمى: آفة في البصر، وقد يستعار لآفة البصيرة"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "عمي القلب: ذهبت بصيرته"
- Root: أبصر (Abṣara)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "البصر: حاسة الرؤية. والبصيرة: العلم" — sight; insight
  *Al-Raghib (Al-Mufradat): "الإبصار: إدراك البصر، وقد يستعار للبصيرة"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "أبصر الحق: علمه. ومنه: البصيرة"
- Root: كأس (Ka's)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الكأس: القدح إذا كان فيه شراب" — the cup when it contains drink
  * Al-Raghib (Al-Mufradat): "الكأس: الإناء المعروف، وقد يقال لما فيه"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "الكأس: القدح إذا كان فيه شراب"
5:83.topic: Al-Ghazali on the journey of the soul, death, and the Hereafter, from 'Audition and Ecstasy'

5:89.arabic: الله تعالى {لا يؤاخذكم الله باللغو في أيمانكم} هذا ما نقل من الأقاويل ومن طلب الحق في التقليد فمهما استقصى تعارضت عنده هذه الأقاويل فيبقى متحيرا أومائلا إلى بعض الأقاويل بالتشهي وكل ذلك قصور بل ينبغي أن يطلب الحق بطريقه وذلك بالبحث عن مدارك الحظر والإباحة كما سنذكره بيان الدليل على إباحة السماع اعلم أن قول القائل السماع حرام معناه أن الله تعالى يعاقب عليه وهذا أمر لا يعرف بمجرد العقل بل بالسمع ومعرفة الشرعيات محصورة في النص أو القياس على المنصوص وأعني بالنص ما أظهره صلى الله عليه وسلم
5:89.english: And it was related from Ṭāhir ibn Bilāl al-Hamadānī al-Warrāq, who was among the people of knowledge, that he said: I was in spiritual retreat (muʿtakif) in the congregational mosque of Jeddah by the sea, and one day I saw a group reciting poetry (yaqūlūn qawl) in one corner of it and listening. I disapproved of that in my heart and said: In a house among the houses of God they recite poetry? He said: Then I saw the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, that night, seated in that very corner, and beside him was Abu Bakr al-Ṣiddīq, may God be pleased with him — and behold, Abu Bakr was reciting something of poetry, and the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, was listening to him and placing his hand upon his chest like one overcome with ecstasy (al-wājid) thereby. So I said to myself: It was not fitting for me to disapprove of those who were listening — for here is the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, listening, and Abu Bakr reciting. Then he [the Prophet] turned to me and said: "This is true by truth" — or he said: "True from truth" — I am doubtful about it [the exact wording].
5:89.section_title_en: The Revival of the Religious Sciences — Section 488: On the Lawfulness of Auditory Samaʿ (Spiritual Listening)
5:89.anchors:
- Root: سمع (s-m-ʿ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root meaning: hearing, listening, perceiving by the ear; also used for answering/accepting a supplication.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Hearing as a physical sense perception; in theological usage, al-samʿ (revelation/textual report) is contrasted with al-ʿaql (reason) as a source of knowledge — precisely the dichotomy Ghazali invokes here.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): auditory perception. Metaphorical (majāz): obedience, acceptance, or the revealed text itself (al-samʿ = the transmitted revelation).
- Root: طيب (ṭ-y-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root meaning: goodness, pleasantness, purity, lawfulness.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "That which the senses and the soul find pleasurable"; in legal-theological terms, what is lawful (ḥalāl) and wholesome — both immediately and in its ultimate consequence.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: pleasant to the senses. Metaphorical: lawful (ḥalāl), pure, free of taint — as in "ṭāba lī kadhā" (this became lawful/pleasant for me).
- Root: قيس (q-y-s)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root meaning: measuring, estimating, comparing.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Qiyās in juristic theology: analogical extension of a ruling from an original case (al-aṣl) to a subsidiary case (al-farʿ) based on shared effective cause (ʿillah).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: measurement by measure or rod. Metaphorical: intellectual analogy and juridical reasoning.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — governing the periodic suspension of grammatical completion to allow for parenthetical or conditional insertions, as in Ghazali's layered conditional structures.
5:89.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Audition and Ecstasy'

11:123.arabic: قدم وذكر بلا ذكر إذ كان هو المبتدئ بالنعم والمتولى وإليه يرجع الأمر كله فهذا ظاهر علم الوجد وأقوال الصوفية من هذا الجنس في الوجد كثيرة وأما الحكماء فقال بعضهم في القلب فضيلة شريفة لم تقدر قوة النطق على إخراجها باللفظ فأخرجتها النفس بالألحان فلما ظهرت سرت وطربت إليها فاستمعوا من النفس وناجوها ودعوا مناجاة الظواهر وقال بعضهم نتائج السماع استنهاض العاجز من الرأي واستجلاب العازب من الأفكار وحدة الكال من الأفهام والآراء حتى يثوب ما عزب وينهض ما عجز ويصفو ما كدر ويمرح في كل رأي ونية فيصيب ولا يخطىء ويأتي ولا يبطىء وقال آ
11:123.english: As for the Sufis: Dhū al-Nūn al-Miṣrī, may Allah have mercy on him, said concerning audition: "It is a divine arrival (wārid ḥaqq) that comes, agitating the hearts toward the Truth. Whoever listens to it with truth becomes realized (taḥaqqaqa); whoever listens to it with his ego becomes a heretic (tazandaqa)." It is as though he expressed ecstasy as the agitation of hearts toward the Truth — and that is what one finds upon the arrival of the arrival of audition, since audition is named "a divine arrival."
11:123.section_title_en: The Science of Spiritual Wayfaring — On the Reality of Ecstasy (Wajd) in Audition (Samāʿ)
11:123.anchors:
- Root: و ج د (w-j-d)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To find, to attain, to experience; existence (wujūd) and ecstasy (wajd) derive from the same root — that which is "found" in the heart upon encounter with divine realities.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Wajd denotes the soul's discovery of what was previously absent — a finding that transforms the finder. In theological usage, it signifies the heart's direct apprehension of spiritual realities through unveiling (mukāshafah), not through discursive reasoning.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): to find a lost thing. Metaphorical (majāz): the heart's finding of divine presence — an ecstatic state that overwhelms the seeker upon the arrival (wurūd) of spiritual influx.
- Root: و ر د (w-r-d)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To arrive at water — the quenching source. The "arrival" (wurūd) of that which refreshes the soul.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Al-wurūd is originally: the intending of water, then used for other things." The arrival of audition (samāʿ) upon the heart is likened to the arrival of a traveler at a watering-place — it quenches, revives, and stirs.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: arriving at water. Metaphorical: the arrival of divine intimations upon the heart — "warda ʿalayhi amrun lam yuṭiqhu" (an affair arrived upon him that he could not bear) — the overwhelming nature of ecstatic arrival.
- Root: س م ع (s-m-ʿ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Hearing, audition; the ear's reception of sound.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Hearing that penetrates beyond the ear to the heart — the difference between mere audibility and attentive listening (istiṣghāʾ).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: auditory perception. Metaphorical: the soul's inner hearing of subtle divine addresses — "hearing with an attentive ear and a witnessing heart."
- Root: ق ل ب (q-l-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The heart; that which turns about, fluctuates, and transforms.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Qalb al-shayʾ: to turn it about and divert it from one face to another." The heart's being "turned" (inqilāb) toward the Truth — its agitation and upheaval upon the arrival of audition.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: to turn a thing over. Metaphorical: "qallaba al-amra ẓahrahu wa-baṭnahu" (he turned the matter over, back and front) — the heart's being overturned, stirred, and convulsed by ecstatic arrival.
- Root: ظ ه ر (ẓ-h-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To appear, to be manifest; the back/surface (ẓahr) as opposed to the hidden (bāṭin).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The outward (ẓāhir) and the inward (bāṭin) — the visible and the hidden dimensions of reality.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the back of a thing. Metaphorical: "qalabtu al-amra ẓahrahu wa-baṭnahu" — to examine a matter thoroughly, turning it over in all its aspects. In the Sufi lexicon: the outward form of audition (fitnah — trial) versus its inward meaning (ʿibrah — lesson).
- Sibawayh Rule: Bāb al-faṣl bayna al-jār wa-al-majrūr (Prepositional Interposition) — The permissibility of interposing elements between the preposition and its object when the intervening clause is complete in itself, as in the construction "fa-man aṣghā ilayhi bi-ḥaqqin taḥaqqaqa" — the prepositional phrase "ilayhi" governs the hearing, while the qualifying clause "bi-ḥaqqin" specifies the mode of attentive listening.
11:123.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Audition and Ecstasy'

12:50.arabic: عين الشهود الذي يضاهي حاله حال النسوة اللاتي قطعن أيديهن في مشاهدة جمال يوسف عليه السلام حتى دهشن وسقط إحساسهن وعن مثل هذه الحالة تعبر الصوفية بأنه قد فنى عن نفسه ومهما فنى عن نفسه فهو عن غيره أفنى فكأنه فنى عن كل شيء إلا عن الواحد المشهود وفنى أيضا عن الشهود فإن القلب أيضا إذا التفت إلى الشهود وإلى نفسه بأنه مشاهد فقد غفل عن المشهود فالمستهتر بالمرئي لا التفات له في حال استغراقه إلى رؤيته ولا إلى عينه التي بها رؤيته ولا إلى قلبه الذي به لذته فالسكران لا خبر له من سكره والمتلذذ لا خبر له من التذاذه وإنم
12:50.english: **The second meaning** — that he descends it upon himself with respect to God Most High. For when he reflects, his knowledge is ignorance, since {«ما قدروا الله حق قدره»} (They did not measure God with His true measure) [Al-Anʿām 6:91]; and his obedience is ostentation (riyāʾ), since he does not {«يتقي الله حق تقاته»} (fear God as He deserves to be feared) [Āl ʿImrān 3:102]; and his love is defective, since he does not abandon any of his lusts in his love [of God]. And whoever God desires good for, He shows him the faults of his own soul, so he sees the confirmation of this verse in himself, even if he is upon a [high] rank in relation to the heedless. For this reason, the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "I do not enumerate praise upon You; You are as You have praised Yourself." (2) And he, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "I indeed seek God's forgiveness seventy times in the day and the night." (3) His seeking forgiveness was only for states that are degrees [of closeness] in relation to what is beyond them, even though they are closeness in relation to what precedes them. For there is no closeness except that behind it remains a closeness that has no end, since the path of journeying to God Most High is without termination, and reaching the utmost limits of closeness is impossible.
12:50.section_title_en: The Book of the Revival of the Religious Sciences — Section 505: On the Hidden Maladies of Praise and Blame (Continued)
12:50.anchors:
- Root: سرر (s-r-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The concealed essence of a thing; that which is hidden from perception, whether good or evil.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-sirr (secret) is that which is concealed in the heart, and its plural asrār denotes the innermost hidden realities of the soul's states.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (haqīqah) for what is veiled from the senses; metaphorical (majāz) for the hidden motives and subtle deceptions of the self.
- Root: عيب (ʿ-ī-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: A defect, blemish, or imperfection; to find fault with something, exposing its deficiency.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In the theological context, ʿayb denotes moral and spiritual deficiency that distances the servant from God, often concealed by self-deception.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal for physical blemish; metaphorical for moral faults that the soul conceals from itself.
- Root: شهد (sh-h-d)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To witness, to be present; shuhūd is presence with the eye or the heart.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الشهود والشهادة: الحضور مع المشاهدة، إما بالبصر، أو بالبصيرة" — witnessing is presence with observation, either by the eye or by inner insight (basīrah).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal for physical presence; metaphorical for the heart's absorption in contemplation of the Divine, where the witness is annihilated in the witnessed.
- Root: فني (f-n-y)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To perish, to cease; fanāʾ is the passing away of a thing.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In the Sufi lexicon, fanāʾ ʿan al-nafs is the passing away of self-awareness, not ontological annihilation, but the cessation of attending to oneself.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Metaphorical (majāz) for the extinction of sensory and self-referential perception in the state of total absorption.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد (Restriction and Specification) — The particle إنما restricts predication, and the construction "فكأنه فنى عن كل شيء إلا عن الواحد المشهود" employs exception (istithnāʾ) to affirm total annihilation save the One Witnessed, a syntactic structure that emphasizes exclusive focus.
12:50.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Audition and Ecstasy'

17:86.arabic: له فقرأ الإمام {ولئن شئنا لنذهبن بالذي أوحينا إليك} فزعق الشبلي زعقة ظن الناس أنه قد طارت روحه وأحمر وجهه وارتعدت فرائصه وكان يقول بمثل هذا يخاطب الأحباب يردد ذلك مرارا وقال الجنيد دخلت على سرى السقطي فرأيت بين يديه رجلا قد غشي عليه فقال لي هذا رجل قد سمع آية من القرآن فغشي عليه فقلت اقرءوا عليه تلك الآية بعينها فقرئت فأفاق فقال من أين قلت هذا فقلت رأيت يعقوب عليه السلام كان عماه من أجل مخلوق فبمخلوق أبصر ولو كان عماه من أجل الحق ما أبصر بمخلوق فاستحسن ذلك ويشير إلى ما قاله الجنيد قول الشاعر وك
17:86.english:
**QUAD_ANCHORS:**
- Root: وجد (Wajd)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The root وجد encompasses multiple senses: finding/attaining (إدراك), intense love (الحب الشديد), grief (الحزن), and wealth/sufficiency (الغنى). Al-Khalil notes the range: "الوجد: الحب. والوجد: الحزن. والوجد: الغنى. والوجد: إدراك الشيء"
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الوجد: إدراك الشيء على خلاف ما يطلب" — and in the technical terminology of the Sufis: "ما يصادف القلب من واردات الأحوال" (what the heart encounters of the influxes of spiritual states)
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal sense is finding/attaining; metaphorical extension (majāz) in devotional context: "وجد فلان في العبادة وجدا: إذا أتى بها على وجهها مع حضور القلب"
- Root: طبع (Tabʿ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الطبع: السجية التي جبل عليها الإنسان" — the innate disposition upon which one is created; also "الختم" (sealing)
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الطبع: السجية التي جبل عليها الإنسان" — the original constitution
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Distinguishes "مطبوع" (innate/natural) from "متكلف" (deliberately acquired) — "فلان مطبوع على الكرم، ومتكلف له"
- Root: كلف (Kulfah/Takalluf)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "التكلف: تجشم ما لا يلزمك" — undertaking what is not incumbent upon you with effort and hardship
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "التكلف: تجشم ما ليس من شأنه" — burdening oneself with what is not one's natural concern
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "تكلفت الأمر: تجشمته على مشقة" — deliberate self-imposition of effort
- Root: سمع (Samāʿ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Auditory perception; also what is heard — recitation, song, remembrance
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "السماع عند الصوفية: ما يهيج الوجد من الأصوات الموزونة" — that which stirs ecstatic finding from measured sounds
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "السماع عند القوم: حضور مجلس يهيج الأحوال الشريفة" — attending an assembly that stirs noble spiritual states
- Root: عشق (ʿIshq)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "العشق: فرط الحب" — excessive love; from "العشقة" — a plant that twines around another
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "العشق: فرط الحب، وأصله من عشقة النبات وهي ما التف منه على غيره"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "العشق مجاز في حق الله تعالى" — metaphorical when applied to God
- Root: بكى (Bukāʾ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Weeping, shedding tears
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "البكاء: إجراء الدمع من عين لحزن أو غيره"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "تباكى: تكلف البكاء" — deliberate self-induced weeping
- Root: صعق (Ṣaʿq)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الصعق: الغشي. والصعق: الموت" — swooning/loss of consciousness; death
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الصعق: غشية تعرض من صوت شديد أو هول"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "صعق من هول الأمر: إذا غشي عليه من شدة الخوف"
- Root: خشع (Khushūʿ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الخشوع: الخضوع والتذلل" — humility and submissiveness
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الخشوع: التذلل والخضوع، وقيل: الخشوع في الصوت والبصر، والخضوع في البدن"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "خشعت الأصوات: سكنت. وخشع البصر: انكسر"
- Root: أنس (Uns)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الأنس: نقيض الوحشة" — the opposite of loneliness/estrangement
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الأنس: حضور القلب مع المحبوب" — the heart's presence with the Beloved
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "الأنس بالله: سكون القلب إليه"
- Root: وجل (Wajal)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الوجل: الخوف مع اضطراب القلب" — fear accompanied by cardiac agitation
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الوجل: الخوف مع اضطراب القلب"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "الوجل: أشد من الخوف، فإنه مع اضطراب"
- Root: طمأن (Ṭumaʾnīnah)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الطمأنينة: السكون" — tranquility
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الطمأنينة: سكون القلب بعد اضطراب"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "اطمأن القلب: سكن بعد اضطراب"
- Root: قشعر (Iqshirʿār)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "القشعريرة: تقبض الجلد من الخوف" — contraction of the skin from fear
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الاقشعرار: انقباض الجلد وتقبضه من الخوف"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "اقشعر الجلد من الخوف: إذا تقبض"
- Root: لين (Līn)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "اللين: ضد الخشونة" — softness, opposite of hardness
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "اللين: نقيض الخشونة"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "لان قلبه: إذا سكن وخشع"
- Root: غشي (Ghashy)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الغشي: الإغماء" — loss of consciousness
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الغشية: ما يغشى القلب من شدة الوجد"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "غشي عليه: إذا أغمي عليه من شدة وجد أو خوف"
- Root: زعق (Zaʿq)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الزعق: الصياح الشديد" — violent screaming
  * Al-Raghib (Al-Mufradat): "الزعق: الصياح الشديد"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "زعق: صاح بأعلى صوته"
- Root: أزيز (Azīz)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الأزيز: صوت النار والمرجل" — the sound of fire and boiling pot
  * Al-Raghib (Al-Mufradat): "الأزيز: صوت النار والمرجل ونحوهما"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "أزيز الصدر: صوت يسمع من شدة البكاء والوجد"
- Root: شهق (Shahīq)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الشهيق: رد النفس إلى الداخل بصوت" — drawing breath inward with sound
  * Al-Raghib (Al-Mufradat): "الشهيق: رد النفس إلى الداخل بصوت"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "شهق الرجل: إذا خرجت نفسه بصوت من شدة الوجد"
- Root: حزن (Ḥuzn)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الحزن: ضد السرور" — grief, opposite of joy
  * Al-Raghib (Al-Mufradat): "الحزن: ألم النفس"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "الحزن: ألم النفس، وهو مجاز من حزن الأرض" (metaphorical extension from rough ground)
- Root: شيب (Shayb)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الشيب: بياض الشعر" — whitening of hair
  * Al-Raghib (Al-Mufradat): "الشيب: بياض الشعر"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "شيبتني هود: أي: كبرتني وأحزنتني حتى شاب شعري"
- Root: ذرف (Dharf)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الذرف: سيلان الدمع" — flowing of tears
  * Al-Raghib (Al-Mufradat): "ذرفت العين: سال دمعها"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "ذرفت عينه: إذا سال دمعها من حزن"
- Root: فيض (Fayḍ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الفيض: سيلان الماء" — overflowing of water
  * Al-Raghib (Al-Mufradat): "الفيض: جريان الماء بكثرة"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "فاضت العين بالدمع: سالت. وفاض القلب: امتلأ"
- Root: نقر (Naqr)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "النقر: الضرب على الشيء حتى يصوت" — striking something until it sounds
  * Al-Raghib (Al-Mufradat): "الناقور: الصور" — the Trumpet
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "الناقور: الصور الذي ينفخ فيه إسرافيل"
- Root: رعش (Riʿshah)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الرعدة: الاضطراب" — trembling
  * Al-Raghib (Al-Mufradat): "الارتعداد: الاضطراب"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "ارتعدت فرائصه: اضطربت من شدة الخوف"
- Root: فرص (Farīṣah)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الفريصة: لحمة بين الجنب والكتف ترعد عند الفزع" — the flesh between the side and shoulder blade that trembles at fright
  * Al-Raghib (Al-Mufradat): "الفريصة: لحمة بين الجنب والكتف ترعد عند الفزع"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "ارتعدت فرائصه: من شدة الخوف"
- Root: عما (ʿAmā)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "العمى: ذهاب البصر. والعمى: ذهاب البصيرة" — blindness of sight; blindness of insight
  * Al-Raghib (Al-Mufradat): "العمى: آفة في البصر، وقد يستعار لآفة البصيرة"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "عمي القلب: ذهبت بصيرته"
- Root: أبصر (Abṣara)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "البصر: حاسة الرؤية. والبصيرة: العلم" — sight; insight
  *Al-Raghib (Al-Mufradat): "الإبصار: إدراك البصر، وقد يستعار للبصيرة"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "أبصر الحق: علمه. ومنه: البصيرة"
- Root: كأس (Ka's)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الكأس: القدح إذا كان فيه شراب" — the cup when it contains drink
  * Al-Raghib (Al-Mufradat): "الكأس: الإناء المعروف، وقد يقال لما فيه"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "الكأس: القدح إذا كان فيه شراب"
17:86.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Audition and Ecstasy'

25:26.arabic: وكذلك سمع مرة قوله تعالى {الملك يومئذ الحق للرحمن} فاضطرب فسأله ابن سالم وكان من أصحابه فقال قد ضعفت فقيل له فإن كان هذا من مضعف فما قوة الحال فقال أن لا يرد عليه وارد إلا وهو يلتقيه بقوة حاله فلا تغيره الواردات وإن كانت قوية وسبب القدرة على ضبط الظاهر مع وجود الوجد استواء الأحوال بملازمة الشهود كما حكي عن سهل رحمه الله تعالى أنه قال حالتي قبل الصلاة وبعدها واحدة لأنه كان مراعيا للقلب حاضر الذكر مع الله تعالى في كل حال فكذلك يكون قبل السماع وبعده إذ يكون وجده دائما وعطشه متصلا وشربه مستمرا بح
25:26.english: And it is related that Moses — peace be upon him — was preaching among the Children of Israel, and one of them tore his garment or his shirt. So God — exalted be He — revealed to Moses — peace be upon him: "Say to him: Tear for Me your heart, and do not tear your garment."
25:26.section_title_en: The Revival of the Religious Sciences — Section 517: On the Steadfastness of the Strong in the Face of Ecstatic Samaʿ, and the Degrees of Manifestation and Restraint
25:26.anchors:
- Root: قلب (q-l-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To turn over, to overturn, to transform from one state to another; the heart as that which is perpetually fluctuating and being overturned between states.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "قلب الشيء: تصريفه وصرفه عن وجه إلى وجه" — the heart's turning and overturning is its being diverted from one disposition to another. The heart (qalb) is so named for its constant fluctuation (taqallub) between states.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): "قلب الشيء قلبا: حوله عن وجهه" — to turn a thing from its face. Metaphorical (Majaz): "قلب المعلم الصبيان: صرفهم إلى بيوتهم" — to turn pupils back to their homes; and "رجل قلب حول: يقلب الأمور ويحتال" — a man who turns matters over and manages them. Here, the heart's being "split" (inshaqqa) and its "turning" (taqallub) in the unseen realm (malakūt) are majaz for the soul's profound transformation.
- Root: ظهر (ẓ-h-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The back; the outward, visible surface as opposed to the hidden interior.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الظهر الجارحة" — the back as a bodily limb; used metaphorically for the outward aspect of the earth: "ظهر الأرض وبطنها" — its surface and its interior.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "رجل مظهر: قوي الظهر" — a man strong of back. Metaphorical: "قلبت الأمر ظهرا لبطن" — to turn the matter over, back and belly, i.e., to examine it thoroughly. In this section, the "outward" (zāhir) is the domain of the bodily members (jawāriḥ) which must be restrained, while the "inward" (bāṭin) is the domain of the heart's ecstasy (wajd).
- Root: حول (ḥ-w-l)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To change, to turn, to shift from one state to another; power and capacity to effect change.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "أصل الحول تغير الشيء وانفصاله عن غيره" — the root meaning is the changing of a thing and its separation from another. "حال بيني وبينك كذا" — something intervened between me and you.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "حال عليه الحول" — a year passed over it. Metaphorical: "لقحت الحرب عن حيال" — war conceived after a period of barrenness. Here, "ḥāl" (state/condition) and "taḥawwul" (transformation) denote the changing spiritual conditions that assail the heart, and the power (ḥawl) to restrain the outward members.
- Root: نفس (n-f-s)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The self, the soul; breath; that which is precious and valued.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "النفس: الروح" — the self is the spirit; "نفسه: ذاته" — His Self is His Essence. The soul is that which is breathed out and drawn in, and by extension, the living self.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "شيء نفيس ومنفس" — a precious thing. Metaphorical: "دفق نفسه أي دمه" — he poured out his self, i.e., his blood. In this text, "nafsahu" (his self/soul) departs at death when the heart is split by suppressed ecstasy.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين المبتدأ والخبر (Interposition between Subject and Predicate) — The periodic structure of al-Ghazali's conditional sentences (fa-in qulta... fa-'lam) follows the classical pattern of protasis and apodosis, where the apodosis is introduced by the particle fa- to mark the resumption of the main clause after a lengthy conditional protasis, preserving syntactic cohesion across extended theological arguments.
25:26.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Audition and Ecstasy'

31:6.arabic: احتجوا بقوله تعالى ومن الناس من يشتري لهو الحديث قال ابن مسعود والحسن البصري والنخعي رضي الله عنهم أن لهو الحديث هو الغناء وروت عائشة رضي الله عنها أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال إن الله تعالى حرم القينة وبيعها وثمنها وتعليمها (1) فنقول أما القينة فالمراد بها الجارية التي تغني للرجال في مجلس الشرب وقد ذكرنا أن غناء الأجنبية للفساق ومن يخاف عليهم الفتنة حرام وهم لا يقصدون بالفتنة إلا ما هو محظور فأما غناء الجارية لمالكها فلا يفهم تحريمه من هذا الحديث بل لغير مالكها سماعها عند عدم الفتنة بدليل
31:6.english: Yūnus ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā said: I asked al-Shāfiʿī — may God have mercy on him — about the people of Medina permitting audition (samāʿ). Al-Shāfiʿī said: "I know of no one among the scholars of the Ḥijāz who disapproved of audition, except what pertains to descriptive verses [of women]. As for the camel-driver's chant (ḥudāʾ), the mention of ruined abodes and resting places, and the beautifying of the voice with the melodies of poetry — this is permissible."
31:6.section_title_en: On the True Reality of His Essence — The Permissibility of Audition (Samāʿ) and Refutation of Its Prohibitors
31:6.anchors:
- Root: لهو (lahw)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of diversion, play, and that which distracts from serious purpose
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): That which occupies one without benefit; distinguished from mere idleness by its capacity to divert the heart
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal sense of play/amusement; metaphorical extension to anything that turns one from weighty matters
- Root: بطل (baṭal)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Falsehood, nullity, that which has no reality or benefit
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The opposite of truth (ḥaqq); that which yields no fruit nor enduring consequence
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: falsehood; metaphorical: any act devoid of genuine utility
- Root: كره (kariha)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Dislike, aversion; al-karāhah as that which one finds repugnant
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Two types: what nature abhors, and what intellect or Law deems repugnant
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: dislike; metaphorical (karāhat al-tanzīh): disapprobation short of prohibition
- Sibawayh Rule: Restriction and qualification (taqyīd) — how qualifiers like "in the descriptions" (fī al-awṣāf) narrow general rulings
31:6.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'Audition and Ecstasy'

31:19.arabic: وقول الله تعالى {إن أنكر الأصوات لصوت الحمير} يدل بمفهومه على مدح الصوت الحسن ولو جاز أن يقال إنما أبيح ذلك بشرط أن يكون في القرآن للزمه أن يحرم سماع صوت العندليب لأنه ليس من القرآن وإذا جاز سماع صوت غفل لا معنى له فلم لا يجوز سماع صوت يفهم منه الحكمة والمعاني الصحيحة وإن من الشعر لحكمة فهذا نظر في الصوت من حيث أنه طيب حسن الدرجة الثانية النظر في الصوت الطيب الموزون فإن الوزن وراء الحسن فكم من صوت حسن خارج عن الوزن وكم من صوت موزون غير مستطاب والأصوات الموزونه باعتبار مخارجها ثلاثة ف
31:19.english: As for the scriptural text (al-naṣṣ), it indicates the permissibility of hearing a beautiful voice as a grace (imtinān) from God Most High upon His servants, for He said: {«يَزِيدُ فِي الْخَلْقِ مَا يَشَاءُ»} ("He increases in creation what He wills" — Qurʾān 35:1). And it was said: "It is the beautiful voice." And in the ḥadīth: "God never sent a prophet but with a beautiful voice." And he (peace be upon him) said: "God listens more intently to a man with a beautiful voice reciting the Qurʾān than does the master of a singing-girl to his singing-girl." And in the ḥadīth, in the mode of praising David (peace be upon him): he had a beautiful voice in his lamentation over himself and in his recitation of the Psalms, such that humans, jinn, wild beasts, and birds would gather to hear his voice, and four hundred funeral biers would be borne to his assembly, and none would approach it during those times. And he (peace be upon him) said in praise of Abū Mūsā al-Ashʿarī: "He has indeed been given a flute from the flutes of the family of David." And the saying of God Most High: {«إِنَّ أَنكَرَ الْأَصْوَاتِ لَصَوْتُ الْحَمِيرِ»} ("Indeed, the most disagreeable of sounds is the voice of donkeys" — Qurʾān 31:19) indicates, by its implication (mafhūm), praise of the beautiful voice.
31:19.section_title_en: The Revival of the Religious Sciences — On the Hearing of Melodious Sounds and the Degrees of Their Permissibility
31:19.anchors:
- Root: صوت (ṣ-w-t)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Sound as the vibration of air produced by the percussion of two bodies; encompasses both the unarticulated cry of animals and the articulated speech of humans.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Sound is compressed air from the striking of two bodies; it is either purely natural (as from inanimate objects or animals) or volitional (as from humans, whether by hand, like the lute, or by the mouth, whether articulate speech or not).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal usage (ḥaqīqah) denotes the audible sound itself; metaphorically (majāz), one says "he has a voice (ṣawt) among the people" meaning reputation and renown.
- Root: حرم (ḥ-r-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To forbid, prohibit, or render sacred; the protected precinct (ḥimā) surrounding a sanctuary.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Prohibition (taḥrīm) is of two kinds: by divine decree (takhlīq) or by human law; the sacred law's prohibitions are protective barriers around what is unlawful.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: what is unlawful to approach; Metaphorical (majāz): "the sanctities of the night" (maḥārim al-layl) — its terrors and perils that make travel unlawful (dangerous).
- Root: حسن (ḥ-s-n)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Beauty, goodness, excellence; that which pleases the eye or the intellect.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The good (al-ḥasan) is that which is desirable and pleasing, whether by reason, by passion, or by sense perception.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical beauty; Metaphorical: "he does not do anything well" (lā yuḥsinu shay'an) — i.e., he lacks skill or virtue.
- Root: طيب (ṭ-y-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: That which is good, pure, pleasant, lawful.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The root meaning is what the senses and the soul find pleasurable; in Sacred Law, "lawful good things" (ṭayyibāt) are those obtained from permissible sources in permissible ways.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: pleasant to the senses; Metaphorical: "it became good (ṭāba) for me" meaning lawful, and "good spoils" (saby ṭayyib) meaning lawful, not obtained by treachery.
- Sibawayh Rule: Restriction and Focused Predication (al-ḥaṣr wa-l-taqyīd bi-innamā) — The particle "innamā" restricts the predicate to the subject alone, a crucial tool for understanding the precise scope of legal prohibitions (e.g., "forbidden is only the lute and the flute").
31:19.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'Audition and Ecstasy'

37:171.arabic: ولقد سبقت كلمتنا لعبادنا المرسلين وقال عز وجل ولكن حق القول مني لأملأن جهنم من الجنة والناس أجمعين وقال تعالى إن الذين سبقت لهم منا الحسنى أولئك عنها مبعدون فإن خطر ببالك أنه لم اختلفت السابقة وهم في ربقه العبودية مشتركون نوديت من سرادقات الجلال لا تجاوز حد الأدب فإنه لا يسئل عما يفعل وهم يسئلون ولعمري تأدب اللسان والظاهر مما يقدر عليه الأكثرون فأما تأدب السر عن إضمار الاستبعاد بهذا الاختلاف الظاهر في التقريب والإبعاد والإشقاء والإسعاد مع بقاء السعادة والشقاوة أبد الآباد فلا يقوى
37:171.english: Among the masters of ecstatic finding (arbāb al-wajd), there is one whom a state overwhelms like intoxicating drunkenness (sukr mudhish), so his tongue loosens with reproach (ʿitāb) toward God Almighty, and he finds objectionable (yastankiru) His overwhelming (iqtihār) of hearts and His apportioning of noble states differentially. For He is the One who elects (mustaṣfā) the hearts of the veracious (ṣiddīqīn) and distances the hearts of the deniers and the deluded (jāḥidīn wa-l-maghrūrīn). There is no preventer of what He gives, and no giver of what He withholds. He did not cut off divine success (tawfīq) from the disbelievers due to some prior transgression, nor did He extend to the Prophets, peace be upon them, His success and the light of His guidance due to some preceding means. Rather, He said: {«وَلَقَدْ سَبَقَتْ كَلِمَتُنَا لِعِبَادِنَا الْمُرْسَلِينَ»} "And Our word has already preceded for Our servants, the messengers" [Al-Ṣāffāt/171]. And He said, Mighty and Majestic: {«وَلَٰكِنْ حَقَّ الْقَوْلُ مِنِّي لَأَمْلَأَنَّ جَهَنَّمَ مِنَ الْجِنَّةِ وَالنَّاسِ أَجْمَعِينَ»} "But the word from Me has taken effect: I will surely fill Hell with jinn and people all together" [Al-Sajdah/13]. And He said, Exalted: {«إِنَّ الَّذِينَ سَبَقَتْ لَهُمْ مِنَّا الْحُسْنَىٰ أُولَٰئِكَ عَنْهَا مُبْعَدُونَ»} "Indeed, those for whom the best [reward] has preceded from Us — they are from it far removed" [Al-Anbiyāʾ/101].
37:171.section_title_en: The Peril of Listening (Samāʿ) for the Novice and the Reality of Divine Transcendence Beyond Change
37:171.anchors:
- Root: لون (L-W-N)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of color, hue, and physical appearance; also used for types and kinds.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "اللون معروف، وينطوي على الأبيض والأسود وما يركب منهما، ويقال: تلون: إذا اكتسى لوناً غير اللون الذي كان له" — indicating acquisition of a new state or attribute.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): physical coloring and change of hue. Metaphorical (Majaz): "عنده لون من الثياب: صنف منه" — a type, kind, or varying disposition; hence "mutalawwin" (متلون) as one who shifts between states and moods.
- Root: قلب (Q-L-B)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To turn over, overturn, transform, or redirect from one face to another.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "قلب الشيء: تصريفه وصرفه عن وجه إلى وجه" — the continuous turning and overturning of a thing; God as "Muqallib al-Qulūb" (Turner of hearts).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical overturning. Metaphorical: "رجل قلب حول: يقلب الأمور ويحتال" — one who manages and disposes affairs; divine action of disposing hearts.
- Root: حول (H-W-L)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Change, transformation, power, and capacity.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "أصل الحول تغير الشيء وانفصاله عن غيره" — change and separation from another state; "يحول بين المرء وقلبه" {«الأنفال/ 24»} — divine interposition between a man and his heart.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: passage of time, transformation. Metaphorical: "حال عليه الحول" — the changing of conditions; "حائل" as that which has altered.
- Root: قرب (Q-R-B)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Nearness in place, time, or rank.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "القرب والبعد يتقابلان... ويستعمل ذلك في المكان، وفي الزمان، وفي النسبة، وفي الحظوة، والرعاية، والقدرة" — including nearness in honor and station (zulfā).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical proximity. Metaphorical: "فلان يقرب أمراً لا يتسهل له" — drawing near in rank and favor; divine drawing near (taqrīb) and distancing (ibʿād).
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The permissibility of interposing elements between a preposition and its object when the meaning remains clear, paralleling how divine attributes may be qualified without compromising essential unity.
37:171.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'Audition and Ecstasy'

39:67.arabic: أن ينزله على نفسه في حق الله تعالى فإنه إذا تفكر فمعرفته جهل إذ ما قدروا الله حق قدره وطاعته رياء إذ لا يتقي الله حق تقاته وحبه معلول إذ لا يدع شهوة من شهواته في حبه ومن أراد الله به خيرا بصره بعيوب نفسه فيرى مصداق هذا البيت في نفسه وإن كان على المرتبة بالإضافة إلى الغافلين ولذلك قال صلى الله عليه وسلم لا أحصي ثناء عليك أنت كما أثنيت على نفسك (2) وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم إني لأستغفر الله في اليوم والليلة سبعين مرة (3) وإنما كان استغفاره عن أحوال هي درجات بعد بالإضافة إلى ما بعدها وإن كانت قربا بالإضافة إلى ما قبلها فلا قرب إلا ويبق
39:67.english: **The second meaning** — that he descends it upon himself with respect to God Most High. For when he reflects, his knowledge is ignorance, since {«ما قدروا الله حق قدره»} (They did not measure God with His true measure) [Al-Anʿām 6:91]; and his obedience is ostentation (riyāʾ), since he does not {«يتقي الله حق تقاته»} (fear God as He deserves to be feared) [Āl ʿImrān 3:102]; and his love is defective, since he does not abandon any of his lusts in his love [of God]. And whoever God desires good for, He shows him the faults of his own soul, so he sees the confirmation of this verse in himself, even if he is upon a [high] rank in relation to the heedless. For this reason, the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "I do not enumerate praise upon You; You are as You have praised Yourself." (2) And he, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "I indeed seek God's forgiveness seventy times in the day and the night." (3) His seeking forgiveness was only for states that are degrees [of closeness] in relation to what is beyond them, even though they are closeness in relation to what precedes them. For there is no closeness except that behind it remains a closeness that has no end, since the path of journeying to God Most High is without termination, and reaching the utmost limits of closeness is impossible.
39:67.section_title_en: The Book of the Revival of the Religious Sciences — Section 505: On the Hidden Maladies of Praise and Blame (Continued)
39:67.anchors:
- Root: سرر (s-r-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The concealed essence of a thing; that which is hidden from perception, whether good or evil.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-sirr (secret) is that which is concealed in the heart, and its plural asrār denotes the innermost hidden realities of the soul's states.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (haqīqah) for what is veiled from the senses; metaphorical (majāz) for the hidden motives and subtle deceptions of the self.
- Root: عيب (ʿ-ī-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: A defect, blemish, or imperfection; to find fault with something, exposing its deficiency.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In the theological context, ʿayb denotes moral and spiritual deficiency that distances the servant from God, often concealed by self-deception.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal for physical blemish; metaphorical for moral faults that the soul conceals from itself.
- Root: شهد (sh-h-d)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To witness, to be present; shuhūd is presence with the eye or the heart.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الشهود والشهادة: الحضور مع المشاهدة، إما بالبصر، أو بالبصيرة" — witnessing is presence with observation, either by the eye or by inner insight (basīrah).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal for physical presence; metaphorical for the heart's absorption in contemplation of the Divine, where the witness is annihilated in the witnessed.
- Root: فني (f-n-y)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To perish, to cease; fanāʾ is the passing away of a thing.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In the Sufi lexicon, fanāʾ ʿan al-nafs is the passing away of self-awareness, not ontological annihilation, but the cessation of attending to oneself.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Metaphorical (majāz) for the extinction of sensory and self-referential perception in the state of total absorption.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد (Restriction and Specification) — The particle إنما restricts predication, and the construction "فكأنه فنى عن كل شيء إلا عن الواحد المشهود" employs exception (istithnāʾ) to affirm total annihilation save the One Witnessed, a syntactic structure that emphasizes exclusive focus.
39:67.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Audition and Ecstasy'

53:5.arabic: وهو المراد بقوله تعالى {علمه شديد القوى ذو مرة فاستوى وهو بالأفق الأعلى} إلى آخر هذه الآيات وفي مثل هذه الأحوال من الصفاء يقع الإطلاع على ضمائر القلوب وقد يعبر عن ذلك الإطلاع بالتفرس ولذلك قال صلى الله عليه وسلم اتقوا فراسة المؤمن فإنه ينظر بنور الله (2) وقد حكى أن رجلا من المجوس كان يدور على المسلمين ويقول ما معنى قول النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم اتقوا فراسة المؤمن فكان يذكر له تفسيره فلا يقنعه ذلك حتى انتهى إلى بعض المشايخ من الصوفية فسأله فقال له معناه أن تقطع الزنار الذي على وسطك تحت ثوبك فقال صدقت هذا معناه وأسلم وقا
53:5.english: For this reason, he (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Beware the discernment of the believer, for he looks with the light of God." (2)
53:5.section_title_en: The Revival of the Religious Sciences — Section 509: On the Vision of Spiritual Realities Through Purity of Heart
53:5.anchors:
- Root: صفا (ṣafā)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of clarity, purity, and transparency — free from turbidity or admixture.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Denotes the heart's purification from base attributes, rendering it receptive to divine disclosures (mukāshafāt).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: clarity of water or wine. Metaphorical: purity of the heart as the condition for spiritual perception.
- Root: مثل (mathala)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To stand before, to appear, to take shape or form.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Used for representation and formation — the appearing of a thing in a form (ṣūrah) that may or may not correspond to its true reality.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: standing erect before someone. Metaphorical: the self-representation of spiritual beings (arwāḥ) in sensible forms perceptible to the purified heart.
- Root: نظر (naẓar)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Vision, sight, and also reflection and consideration.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Distinguishes between baṣar (physical sight) and baṣīrah (insight); the latter perceives spiritual realities (malakūt).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: seeing with the eye. Metaphorical: "looking with the light of God" (al-naẓar bi-nūr Allāh) — perception through divine illumination.
- Root: فرس (farasa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To prey upon, to seize — the ferāsah (discernment) is so named because it seizes upon the inner reality.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The intuitive perception of inner states — a form of inspired knowledge (ʿilm ladunī).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the lion preying on its quarry. Metaphorical: the believer's discernment that pierces through outward appearances to inward truths.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — Used to confine the activity of devils to hearts filled with blameworthy attributes, and to restrict the vision of the Kingdom of Heaven to purified hearts.
53:5.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'Audition and Ecstasy'

57:15.arabic: قرأ رجل بين يديه {فاليوم لا يؤخذ منكم فدية} الآية فرأيته قد ارتعد وكاد يسقط فلما عاد إلى حاله سألته عن ذلك فقال نعم يا حبيبي قد ضعفنا وكذلك سمع مرة قوله تعالى {الملك يومئذ الحق للرحمن} فاضطرب فسأله ابن سالم وكان من أصحابه فقال قد ضعفت فقيل له فإن كان هذا من مضعف فما قوة الحال فقال أن لا يرد عليه وارد إلا وهو يلتقيه بقوة حاله فلا تغيره الواردات وإن كانت قوية وسبب القدرة على ضبط الظاهر مع وجود الوجد استواء الأحوال بملازمة الشهود كما حكي عن سهل رحمه الله تعالى أنه قال حالتي قبل الصلاة وبعده
57:15.english: And it is related that Moses — peace be upon him — was preaching among the Children of Israel, and one of them tore his garment or his shirt. So God — exalted be He — revealed to Moses — peace be upon him: "Say to him: Tear for Me your heart, and do not tear your garment."
57:15.section_title_en: The Revival of the Religious Sciences — Section 517: On the Steadfastness of the Strong in the Face of Ecstatic Samaʿ, and the Degrees of Manifestation and Restraint
57:15.anchors:
- Root: قلب (q-l-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To turn over, to overturn, to transform from one state to another; the heart as that which is perpetually fluctuating and being overturned between states.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "قلب الشيء: تصريفه وصرفه عن وجه إلى وجه" — the heart's turning and overturning is its being diverted from one disposition to another. The heart (qalb) is so named for its constant fluctuation (taqallub) between states.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): "قلب الشيء قلبا: حوله عن وجهه" — to turn a thing from its face. Metaphorical (Majaz): "قلب المعلم الصبيان: صرفهم إلى بيوتهم" — to turn pupils back to their homes; and "رجل قلب حول: يقلب الأمور ويحتال" — a man who turns matters over and manages them. Here, the heart's being "split" (inshaqqa) and its "turning" (taqallub) in the unseen realm (malakūt) are majaz for the soul's profound transformation.
- Root: ظهر (ẓ-h-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The back; the outward, visible surface as opposed to the hidden interior.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الظهر الجارحة" — the back as a bodily limb; used metaphorically for the outward aspect of the earth: "ظهر الأرض وبطنها" — its surface and its interior.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "رجل مظهر: قوي الظهر" — a man strong of back. Metaphorical: "قلبت الأمر ظهرا لبطن" — to turn the matter over, back and belly, i.e., to examine it thoroughly. In this section, the "outward" (zāhir) is the domain of the bodily members (jawāriḥ) which must be restrained, while the "inward" (bāṭin) is the domain of the heart's ecstasy (wajd).
- Root: حول (ḥ-w-l)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To change, to turn, to shift from one state to another; power and capacity to effect change.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "أصل الحول تغير الشيء وانفصاله عن غيره" — the root meaning is the changing of a thing and its separation from another. "حال بيني وبينك كذا" — something intervened between me and you.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "حال عليه الحول" — a year passed over it. Metaphorical: "لقحت الحرب عن حيال" — war conceived after a period of barrenness. Here, "ḥāl" (state/condition) and "taḥawwul" (transformation) denote the changing spiritual conditions that assail the heart, and the power (ḥawl) to restrain the outward members.
- Root: نفس (n-f-s)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The self, the soul; breath; that which is precious and valued.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "النفس: الروح" — the self is the spirit; "نفسه: ذاته" — His Self is His Essence. The soul is that which is breathed out and drawn in, and by extension, the living self.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "شيء نفيس ومنفس" — a precious thing. Metaphorical: "دفق نفسه أي دمه" — he poured out his self, i.e., his blood. In this text, "nafsahu" (his self/soul) departs at death when the heart is split by suppressed ecstasy.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين المبتدأ والخبر (Interposition between Subject and Predicate) — The periodic structure of al-Ghazali's conditional sentences (fa-in qulta... fa-'lam) follows the classical pattern of protasis and apodosis, where the apodosis is introduced by the particle fa- to mark the resumption of the main clause after a lengthy conditional protasis, preserving syntactic cohesion across extended theological arguments.
57:15.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Audition and Ecstasy'

73:13.arabic: أنكالا وجحيما وطعاما ذا غصة وعذابا أليما} فصعق (4) وفي رواية أنه صلى الله عليه وسلم قرأ {إن تعذبهم فإنهم عبادك} فبكى (5) وكان صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا مر بآية رحمة دعا واستبشر (6) والاستبشار وجد وقد أثنى الله تعالى على أهل الوجد بالقرآن فقال تعالى {وإذا سمعوا ما أنزل إلى الرسول ترى أعينهم تفيض من الدمع مما عرفوا من الحق} وروي أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كان يصلي ولصدره أزيز كأزيز المرجل (7) وأما ما نقل من الوجد بالقرآن عن الصحابة رضي الله عنهم والتابعين فكثير فمنهم من صعق ومنهم من بكى ومنهم من غ
73:13.english:
**QUAD_ANCHORS:**
- Root: وجد (Wajd)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The root وجد encompasses multiple senses: finding/attaining (إدراك), intense love (الحب الشديد), grief (الحزن), and wealth/sufficiency (الغنى). Al-Khalil notes the range: "الوجد: الحب. والوجد: الحزن. والوجد: الغنى. والوجد: إدراك الشيء"
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الوجد: إدراك الشيء على خلاف ما يطلب" — and in the technical terminology of the Sufis: "ما يصادف القلب من واردات الأحوال" (what the heart encounters of the influxes of spiritual states)
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal sense is finding/attaining; metaphorical extension (majāz) in devotional context: "وجد فلان في العبادة وجدا: إذا أتى بها على وجهها مع حضور القلب"
- Root: طبع (Tabʿ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الطبع: السجية التي جبل عليها الإنسان" — the innate disposition upon which one is created; also "الختم" (sealing)
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الطبع: السجية التي جبل عليها الإنسان" — the original constitution
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Distinguishes "مطبوع" (innate/natural) from "متكلف" (deliberately acquired) — "فلان مطبوع على الكرم، ومتكلف له"
- Root: كلف (Kulfah/Takalluf)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "التكلف: تجشم ما لا يلزمك" — undertaking what is not incumbent upon you with effort and hardship
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "التكلف: تجشم ما ليس من شأنه" — burdening oneself with what is not one's natural concern
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "تكلفت الأمر: تجشمته على مشقة" — deliberate self-imposition of effort
- Root: سمع (Samāʿ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Auditory perception; also what is heard — recitation, song, remembrance
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "السماع عند الصوفية: ما يهيج الوجد من الأصوات الموزونة" — that which stirs ecstatic finding from measured sounds
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "السماع عند القوم: حضور مجلس يهيج الأحوال الشريفة" — attending an assembly that stirs noble spiritual states
- Root: عشق (ʿIshq)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "العشق: فرط الحب" — excessive love; from "العشقة" — a plant that twines around another
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "العشق: فرط الحب، وأصله من عشقة النبات وهي ما التف منه على غيره"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "العشق مجاز في حق الله تعالى" — metaphorical when applied to God
- Root: بكى (Bukāʾ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Weeping, shedding tears
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "البكاء: إجراء الدمع من عين لحزن أو غيره"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "تباكى: تكلف البكاء" — deliberate self-induced weeping
- Root: صعق (Ṣaʿq)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الصعق: الغشي. والصعق: الموت" — swooning/loss of consciousness; death
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الصعق: غشية تعرض من صوت شديد أو هول"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "صعق من هول الأمر: إذا غشي عليه من شدة الخوف"
- Root: خشع (Khushūʿ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الخشوع: الخضوع والتذلل" — humility and submissiveness
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الخشوع: التذلل والخضوع، وقيل: الخشوع في الصوت والبصر، والخضوع في البدن"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "خشعت الأصوات: سكنت. وخشع البصر: انكسر"
- Root: أنس (Uns)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الأنس: نقيض الوحشة" — the opposite of loneliness/estrangement
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الأنس: حضور القلب مع المحبوب" — the heart's presence with the Beloved
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "الأنس بالله: سكون القلب إليه"
- Root: وجل (Wajal)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الوجل: الخوف مع اضطراب القلب" — fear accompanied by cardiac agitation
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الوجل: الخوف مع اضطراب القلب"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "الوجل: أشد من الخوف، فإنه مع اضطراب"
- Root: طمأن (Ṭumaʾnīnah)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الطمأنينة: السكون" — tranquility
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الطمأنينة: سكون القلب بعد اضطراب"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "اطمأن القلب: سكن بعد اضطراب"
- Root: قشعر (Iqshirʿār)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "القشعريرة: تقبض الجلد من الخوف" — contraction of the skin from fear
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الاقشعرار: انقباض الجلد وتقبضه من الخوف"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "اقشعر الجلد من الخوف: إذا تقبض"
- Root: لين (Līn)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "اللين: ضد الخشونة" — softness, opposite of hardness
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "اللين: نقيض الخشونة"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "لان قلبه: إذا سكن وخشع"
- Root: غشي (Ghashy)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الغشي: الإغماء" — loss of consciousness
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الغشية: ما يغشى القلب من شدة الوجد"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "غشي عليه: إذا أغمي عليه من شدة وجد أو خوف"
- Root: زعق (Zaʿq)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الزعق: الصياح الشديد" — violent screaming
  * Al-Raghib (Al-Mufradat): "الزعق: الصياح الشديد"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "زعق: صاح بأعلى صوته"
- Root: أزيز (Azīz)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الأزيز: صوت النار والمرجل" — the sound of fire and boiling pot
  * Al-Raghib (Al-Mufradat): "الأزيز: صوت النار والمرجل ونحوهما"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "أزيز الصدر: صوت يسمع من شدة البكاء والوجد"
- Root: شهق (Shahīq)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الشهيق: رد النفس إلى الداخل بصوت" — drawing breath inward with sound
  * Al-Raghib (Al-Mufradat): "الشهيق: رد النفس إلى الداخل بصوت"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "شهق الرجل: إذا خرجت نفسه بصوت من شدة الوجد"
- Root: حزن (Ḥuzn)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الحزن: ضد السرور" — grief, opposite of joy
  * Al-Raghib (Al-Mufradat): "الحزن: ألم النفس"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "الحزن: ألم النفس، وهو مجاز من حزن الأرض" (metaphorical extension from rough ground)
- Root: شيب (Shayb)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الشيب: بياض الشعر" — whitening of hair
  * Al-Raghib (Al-Mufradat): "الشيب: بياض الشعر"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "شيبتني هود: أي: كبرتني وأحزنتني حتى شاب شعري"
- Root: ذرف (Dharf)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الذرف: سيلان الدمع" — flowing of tears
  * Al-Raghib (Al-Mufradat): "ذرفت العين: سال دمعها"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "ذرفت عينه: إذا سال دمعها من حزن"
- Root: فيض (Fayḍ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الفيض: سيلان الماء" — overflowing of water
  * Al-Raghib (Al-Mufradat): "الفيض: جريان الماء بكثرة"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "فاضت العين بالدمع: سالت. وفاض القلب: امتلأ"
- Root: نقر (Naqr)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "النقر: الضرب على الشيء حتى يصوت" — striking something until it sounds
  * Al-Raghib (Al-Mufradat): "الناقور: الصور" — the Trumpet
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "الناقور: الصور الذي ينفخ فيه إسرافيل"
- Root: رعش (Riʿshah)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الرعدة: الاضطراب" — trembling
  * Al-Raghib (Al-Mufradat): "الارتعداد: الاضطراب"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "ارتعدت فرائصه: اضطربت من شدة الخوف"
- Root: فرص (Farīṣah)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الفريصة: لحمة بين الجنب والكتف ترعد عند الفزع" — the flesh between the side and shoulder blade that trembles at fright
  * Al-Raghib (Al-Mufradat): "الفريصة: لحمة بين الجنب والكتف ترعد عند الفزع"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "ارتعدت فرائصه: من شدة الخوف"
- Root: عما (ʿAmā)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "العمى: ذهاب البصر. والعمى: ذهاب البصيرة" — blindness of sight; blindness of insight
  * Al-Raghib (Al-Mufradat): "العمى: آفة في البصر، وقد يستعار لآفة البصيرة"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "عمي القلب: ذهبت بصيرته"
- Root: أبصر (Abṣara)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "البصر: حاسة الرؤية. والبصيرة: العلم" — sight; insight
  *Al-Raghib (Al-Mufradat): "الإبصار: إدراك البصر، وقد يستعار للبصيرة"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "أبصر الحق: علمه. ومنه: البصيرة"
- Root: كأس (Ka's)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "الكأس: القدح إذا كان فيه شراب" — the cup when it contains drink
  * Al-Raghib (Al-Mufradat): "الكأس: الإناء المعروف، وقد يقال لما فيه"
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): "الكأس: القدح إذا كان فيه شراب"
73:13.topic: Al-Ghazali on the journey of the soul, death, and the Hereafter, from 'Audition and Ecstasy'

5:28.arabic: ظل إلا ظله وعد منهم رجل دعته امرأة ذات جمال وحسب إلى نفسها فقال إني أخاف الله رب العالمين (2) وقصة يوسف عليه السلام وامتناعه من زليخا مع القدرة ومع رغبتها معروفة وقد أثنى الله تعالى عليه بذلك في كتابه العزيز وهو إمام لكل من وفق لمجاهدة الشيطان في هذه الشهوة العظيمة وروي أن سليمان بن يسار كان من أحسن الناس وجها فدخلت عليه امرأة فسألته نفسه فامتنع عليها وخرج هاربا من منزله وتركها فيه قال سليمان فرأيت تلك الليلة في المنام يوسف عليه السلام وكأني أقول له أنت يوسف قال نعم أنا يوسف الذي هممت وأنت سليمان الذي لم تهم أشار إلى قوله
5:28.english: ...which one is ashamed of and fears to plunge into. And the abstention of most people from its requirements is either due to incapacity, or fear, or shame, or concern for preserving one's body — and in none of these is there any reward, for that is merely preferring one share of one's worldly desires over another share. Yes — from divine protection (al-ʿiṣmah) is that one is not able [to sin]; so in these obstacles there is a benefit, namely the repulsion of sin. For whoever abandons fornication, its sin is repelled from him by whatever cause his abandonment occurred. Rather, the virtue and abundant reward lie in abandoning it out of fear of God — may He be exalted — while possessing the ability, with the removal of obstacles, the facilitation of means, and especially at the height of genuine desire. And this is the station of the veracious (al-ṣiddīqīn). For this reason, the Prophet — peace be upon him — said: "Whoever loves passionately, then remains chaste, then conceals [his love], then dies — he dies a martyr."(1)
5:28.section_title_en: The Book of Breaking the Two Desires — Section 654: On Chastity, Guarding the Gaze, and the Virtue of Restraining Desire
5:28.anchors:
- **Root: ع ف ف** (ʿaffa)
  * **Lisan / Ayn**: Core meaning of abstaining from what is unlawful, refraining, and remaining chaste; al-ʿafāf is the state of one who abstains from forbidden things.
  * **Al-Raghib (Mufradat)**: Theological nuance — ʿiffah (chastity) is a virtue of the soul that restrains the appetitive faculty from pursuing what is not permissible; it is a station of the ṣiddīqūn (veracious ones).
  * **Al-Zamakhshari (Asas)**: Literal (ḥaqīqah) — physical abstention from unlawful acts; Metaphorical (majāz) — the heart's abstention from coveting what God has forbidden, which is the higher reality of chastity.

- **Root: غ ب ق** (ghabaqa)
  * **Lisan / Ayn**: The evening drink (al-ghabūq) — the milking or drink given at nightfall; contrasted with al-ṣabūḥ (the morning drink).
  * **Al-Raghib (Mufradat)**: In the hadith of the three men in the cave, the term marks the temporal precision of filial devotion — serving parents before any other claim, even at the boundary of night.
  * **Al-Zamakhshari (Asas)**: Literal — the evening milking; the narrative use in the hadith is literal, denoting the exact act of service delayed out of reverence.

- **Root: ه م م** (hamma)
  * **Lisan / Ayn**: To intend, to resolve upon a matter; al-hamm is the initial stirring of intention before full determination.
  * **Al-Raghib (Mufradat)**: In Q. 12:24 {«وَلَقَدْ هَمَّتْ بِهِ وَهَمَّ بِهَا لَوْلَا أَنْ رَأَى بُرْهَانَ رَبِّهِ»} — "And certainly she desired him, and he would have desired her, had it not been that he saw the proof of his Lord" — the term distinguishes between a passing inclination (hamm) and a settled resolve; Yūsuf's hamm was repelled by divine proof, while Zulaykhā's was consummated in action.
  * **Al-Zamakhshari (Asas)**: Literal — the inward movement of intention; the rhetorical force lies in the contrast between the two hamm-s, one punished and one pardoned.

- **Root: ن ظ ر** (naẓara)
  * **Lisan / Ayn**: To look, to gaze; al-naẓar is the act of sight, whether physical or intellectual.
  * **Al-Raghib (Mufradat)**: The gaze (naẓar) is the gateway to desire; the Quranic phrase {«يَعْلَمُ خَائِنَةَ الْأَعْيُنِ»} — "He knows the treachery of the eyes" (Q. 40:19) — indicates that the look which steals toward the forbidden is itself an act of betrayal recorded by God.
  * **Al-Zamakhshari (Asas)**: Literal — the first glance that occurs unintentionally; Metaphorical — the second glance is the "treachery of the eyes," for it is a deliberate return to what the first glance stumbled upon by accident.

- **Root: ر و د** (rāwada)
  * **Lisan / Ayn**: To seek, to desire, to solicit; murāwadah is the act of soliciting someone for an unlawful purpose.
  * **Al-Raghib (Mufradat)**: In the Yūsuf narrative, murāwadah denotes the persistent solicitation toward sin; the term carries the weight of repeated, deliberate pursuit.
  * **Al-Zamakhshari (Asas)**: Literal — the physical act of solicitation; the narrative contexts in this section use the term literally for the woman's pursuit of the young man.

- **Sibawayh Rule**: **Bāb al-ḥaṣr wa-l-taqyīd bi-innamā** (Restriction and Focused Predication with innamā)
  * The particle innamā restricts and confines the predicate to the subject alone, negating all else. In the woman's statement "innamā urīdu mā yakūnu min al-rajuli ilā ahlihī" — "I only desire what comes from a man to his wife" — the restriction (ḥaṣr) intensifies the gravity of the solicitation, making the young man's resistance all the more virtuous.
