11:80.arabic: مسكين وقيل لإبراهيم بن أدهم رحمه الله لم لا تشرب من ماء زمزم فقال لو كان لي دلو شربت منه وقال سفيان الثوري رضي الله عنه من أنفق من الحرام في طاعة الله كان كمن طهر الثوب النجس بالبول والثوب النجس لا يطهره إلا الماء والذنب لا يكفره إلا الحلال وقال يحيى بن معاذ الطاعة خزانة من خزائن الله إلا أن مفتاحها الدعاء وأسنانه لقم الحلال وقال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما لا يقبل الله صلاة امرىء في جوفه حرام وقال سهل التستري لا يبلغ العبد حقيقة الإيمان حتى يكون فيه أربع خصال أداء الفرائض بالسنة وأكل الحلال بالورع واجتناب ال
11:80.english: God Most High has said: {«كلوا من الطيبات واعملوا صالحا»} — "Eat of the good things and do righteous deeds." (Q. 23:51) He commanded eating from the good things before [commanding] righteous deeds. And it is said that what is meant by "the good things" is the lawful (al-ḥalāl).
11:80.section_title_en: The Revival of the Religious Sciences — Book of the Etiquette of Eating: Section 336 — The Virtue of Lawful Sustenance and the Blameworthiness of the Forbidden
11:80.anchors:
- Root: اكل (akl)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root meaning of eating, consuming, and tasting food; the act of taking nourishment into the body.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الأكل: تناول المطعم" — eating is the taking of food; used metaphorically for fire consuming wood, and extended to mean lawful provision (ḥalāl) as the sustenance of the soul's soundness.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) for physical ingestion; metaphorical (majāz) for consuming wealth unlawfully, as in "أكل مال اليتيم" (devouring the orphan's wealth).
- Root: طعم (tuʿm)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Food, sustenance, and the act of tasting; also used for bait and that which is eaten.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Sustenance as that which nourishes the body; in the Kalam context, the lawful (ḥalāl) is that which purifies the heart, while the forbidden (ḥarām) corrupts it.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal for food; metaphorical for the moral state of the soul — "طعمه حرام" (his food is forbidden) signifies the corruption of one's entire being.
- Root: ورق (waraʿ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Abstinence, scrupulousness, and piety; refraining from doubtful matters.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The theological virtue of cautious avoidance of all that is suspect, as the foundation of true worship and the key to answered supplication.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal for refraining; metaphorical for the heart's purity achieved through guarding the limbs from the unlawful.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The syntactic structure of conditional and consequential clauses, where the protasis (e.g., "من أكل حراما") governs the apodosis ("لم يقبل منه صرف ولا عدل"), demonstrating the causal nexus between action and divine recompense.
11:80.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Harms of the Tongue'

14:17.arabic: ذلك كلما أردت ذلك ذكرت قوله تعالى {يتجرعه ولا يكاد يسيغه} الآية قال صالح فبكيت وقلت في نفسي أنا في واد وأنت في واد آخر وقال السري السقطي نفسي منذ ثلاثين سنة تطالبني أن أغمس جزرة في دبس فما أطعمتها وقال أبو بكر الجلاء أعرف رجلا تقول له نفسه أنا أصبر لك على طي عشرة أيام وأطعمني بعد ذلك شهوة أشتهيها فيقول لها لا أريد أن تطوى عشرة أيام ولكن اتركي هذه الشهوة وروي أن عابدا دعا بعض إخوانه فقرب إليه رغفانا فجعل أخوه يقلب الأرغفة ليختار أجودها فقال له العابد مه أي شيء تصنع أما علمت أن في الرغيف الذي رغبت عنه كذا
14:17.english: I left it upon a loaf of bread, then I met a boy and said: "Are you not the son of so-and-so, whose father has died?" He replied: "Yes." So I handed it to him. They said: And he came forward weeping and reciting: {«وَيُطْعِمُونَ الطَّعَامَ عَلَىٰ حُبِّهِ مِسْكِينًا وَيَتِيمًا وَأَسِيرًا»} — "And they give food, despite their love for it, to the poor, the orphan, and the captive" {«الإنسان: 8»}. Then he did not taste it after that, and he remained craving dates for years. Then one day, he bought dates for a qīrāṭ and raised them until nightfall to break his fast upon them. He said: Then a violent wind blew until the world grew dark, and the people were terrified. So ʿUtbah turned upon his self, saying: "This is for my audacity against You, and my buying of dates for a qīrāṭ." Then he said to his self: "I do not think that the people were seized except by your sin—on condition that you do not taste them." And Dāwūd al-Ṭāʾī bought greens for half a fals and vinegar for a fals, and he spent his entire night saying to his self: "Woe to you, O Dāwūd! How long is your reckoning on the Day of Resurrection!" Then after that, he ate nothing but dry bread. And ʿUtbah al-Ghulām said one day to ʿAbd al-Wāḥid ibn Zayd: "So-and-so describes of himself a station that I do not recognize in myself." He said: "Because you eat dates with your bread, while he adds nothing to his bread." He said: "If I abandon eating dates, will I recognize that station?" He said: "Yes, and others besides it." So he began to weep, and one of his companions said to him: "May Allah not make your eye weep—do you weep over dates?" ʿAbd al-Wāḥid said: "Leave him, for his self has recognized the sincerity of his resolve in abandonment, and when he abandons a thing, he does not return to it." And Jaʿfar ibn Naṣr said: Al-Junayd ordered me to buy for him the Wazīrī figs. When I bought them, he took one at the time of breaking the fast and placed it in his mouth, then he threw it out and began to weep. Then he said: "Carry it away." I said to him concerning that: "Why?" He said: "A caller called out to me: 'Are you not ashamed? You abandoned it for My sake, then you return to it?'" And Ṣāliḥ al-Murrī said: I said to ʿAṭāʾ al-Sulamī: "I am going to trouble myself for your sake with something, so do not reject my kindness." He said: "Do what you wish." He said: So I sent to him, with my son, a drink of sawīq which I had kneaded with butter and honey, and I said: "Do not leave until he drinks it." When the next day came, I prepared for him something similar, and he returned it and did not drink it. So I reproached him and blamed him for that, and I said: "Glory be to Allah! You have rejected my kindness." When he saw my distress over that, he said: "Do not let this grieve you. I did drink it the first time, and I tempted my self the second time to drink it, but I could not do so—whenever I wanted that, I remembered the saying of Allah the Exalted: {«يَتَجَرَّعُهُ وَلَا يَكَادُ يُسِيغُهُ»} — 'He will gulp it but will hardly swallow it' {«إبراهيم: 17»}." Ṣāliḥ said: So I wept and said to myself: "I am in one valley, and you are in another valley." And al-Sarī al-Saqaṭī said: "My self has been demanding of me for thirty years that I dip a carrot in molasses, and I have not fed it that." And Abū Bakr al-Jallāʾ said: "I know a man whose self says to him: 'I will be patient for you through ten days of hunger, then feed me after that a craving I desire.' He says to her: 'I do not want you to endure ten days of hunger, but abandon this craving.'" And it is related that a worshiper invited some of his brothers, and he placed before him loaves of bread. His brother began turning over the loaves to choose the finest among them, so the worshiper said to him: "Stop! What are you doing? Do you not know that in the loaf you have turned away from there is such-and-such wisdom, and such-and-such a maker worked upon it—until it was rounded from the cloud that carries the water, and the water that irrigates the earth, and the winds, and the earth, and the beasts, and the sons of Adam—until it reached you? Then after all this, you turn it over and are not satisfied with it?" And in the report: "A loaf is not rounded and placed before you until three hundred and sixty makers have worked upon it—the first of them is Michael (Mīkāʾīl), peace be upon him, who measures out the water from the treasuries of mercy, then the angels that drive the clouds, and the sun, and the moon, and the spheres, and the angels of the air, and the beasts of the earth, and the last of them is the baker. {«وَإِن تَعُدُّوا نِعْمَةَ اللَّهِ لَا تُحْصُوهَا»} — 'And if you should count the favors of Allah, you could not enumerate them' {«إبراهيم: 34»}." — A hadith: "A loaf is not rounded and placed before you until three hundred and sixty makers have worked upon it—the first of them is Michael." — I have not found any basis for this hadith. And some of them said: I came to Qāsim al-Jurʿī and asked about asceticism (al-zuhd)—what it is. He said: "What have you heard about it?" So I enumerated various sayings, and he fell silent. Then I said: "What do you yourself say?" He said: "Know that the belly is the world (dunyā) of the servant. To the extent that he masters his belly, he masters of asceticism; and to the extent that his belly masters him, the world masters him." And Bishr ibn al-Ḥārith was once ill, so he came to ʿAbd al-Raḥmān the physician, asking him about something that would suit him among foods. He said: "You ask me, and when I describe something for you, you will not accept it from me." He said: "Describe it so that I may hear." He said: "Drink oxymel (sikanjabīn), suck on quince, and eat..."
14:17.section_title_en: The Revival of the Religious Sciences — Book on Trust (Tawakkul), Section 646: Ascetic Restraint in Food and the Discipline of the Self
14:17.anchors:
- Root: نفس (n-f-s)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The self, soul, or spirit; that which animates and carries the essential identity of a person.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In theological usage, النفس denotes the inner reality of a person—whether the rational soul or the lower appetitive self (al-nafs al-ammārah)—which must be disciplined and opposed in its cravings.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) refers to the soul/self as the seat of volition; metaphorical (majāz) usage extends to the "blood of life" (نفس سائلة), indicating that which, when spilled, renders impurity—here, the self is that which must be "broken" of its desires.
- Root: اكل (a-k-l)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To eat, consume, or take nourishment; the act of ingesting food.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): الأكل is the taking of food; metaphorically extended to fire consuming wood (أكلت النار الحطب). In ascetic contexts, it signifies the permissible boundary of bodily sustenance versus the indulgence of appetite.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: eating for survival. Metaphorical: "He ate my wealth" (أكل مالي) meaning he squandered it; here, the narratives pivot on the literal act of eating as the arena where the self's discipline is tested—whether one eats for need or for pleasure.
- Root: قال (q-w-l)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To say, speak, or utter; a statement or discourse.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In Quranic and theological contexts, القول is not mere speech but the articulation of conviction or resolve—often used to contrast outward claims with inward reality.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: verbal utterance. Metaphorical: the "speech" of the self (حديث النفس) as internal dialogue, where the lower self addresses a person and must be answered with resolve.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The rule governing the separation of a preposition from its governed noun by an intervening clause, as seen in complex periodic sentences where the narrative flow is interrupted by parenthetical exhortations or Quranic citations, requiring precise parsing to maintain grammatical coherence.
14:17.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Harms of the Tongue'

24:30.arabic: بني إسرائيل كانت من قبل النساء (3) وقال تعالى {قل للمؤمنين يغضوا من أبصارهم} الآية وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم لكل ابن آدم حظ من الزنا فالعينان تزنيان وزناهما النظر واليدان تزنيان وزناهما البطش والرجلان تزنيان وزناهما المشي والفم يزني وزناه القبلة والقلب يهم أو يتمنى ويصدق ذلك الفرج أو يكذبه (4) وقالت أم سلمة استأذن ابن أم مكتوم الأعمى على رسول الله وأنا وميمونة جالستانفقال صلى الله عليه وسلم احتجبا فقلنا أو ليس بأعمى لا يبصر فقال وأنتما لا تبصرانه (5) وهذا يدل على أنه لا يجوز للنساء مجالسة العميان كما جرت به العادة
24:30.english: Know that the seeker (al-murīd), at the beginning of his affair, ought not to occupy himself with marriage (al-tazwīj), for that is a distracting occupation (shughl shāghil) that prevents him from the Path (al-sulūk) and drags him toward intimacy (al-uns) with the wife. And whoever is intimate with other than God — exalted — is distracted from God. Let him not be deceived by the multiplicity of the marriages of the Messenger of God — may God bless him and grant him peace — for his heart was not occupied by all that is in this world away from God — exalted. So the angels are not to be compared with the blacksmiths (lā tuqās al-malā'ikah bi-l-ḥaddādīn). For this reason, Abū Sulaymān al-Dārānī said: "Whoever marries has inclined to this world." And he said: "I never saw a seeker who married and then remained steadfast upon his former state." And it was said to him once: "How much you need a woman with whom you might find intimacy!" He replied: "May God not grant me intimacy with her" — meaning that intimacy with her would prevent intimacy with God — exalted. He also said: "Everything that distracts you from God — of family, wealth, and children — is ill-omened (mash'ūm) upon you." So how can anyone other than the Messenger of God — may God bless him and grant him peace — be compared to him? For his absorption in the love of God — exalted — was such that he would find his burning within it to a degree that he feared, in some states, that it might spread to his body (qālibihi) and destroy him. For that reason, he would sometimes strike his hand upon the thigh of ʿĀ'ishah and say: "Speak to me, O ʿĀ'ishah" — to distract himself with her speech from the immensity of what he was in, due to the insufficiency of his body's capacity for it. For his natural disposition (ṭab'uhu) was intimacy with God — mighty and majestic — and his intimacy with creatures was merely incidental (ʿāriḍ), as an act of gentleness toward his body. Then, when he could not bear to remain with people if he sat with them, and his breast became constricted, he would say: "Give us rest by it, O Bilāl" — until he returned to what was the delight of his eye. The hadith that prayer was the delight of his eye has also preceded. So the weak one, if he observes his own states in such matters, is deluded (maghrūr), for intellects fall short of grasping the secrets of his actions — may God bless him and grant him peace. Therefore, the condition for the seeker is celibacy (al-ʿuzbah) at the beginning, until he grows strong in gnosis (al-maʿrifah). This is [the ruling] when lust does not overcome him. But if lust overcomes him, let him break it with prolonged hunger and continuous fasting. If lust is not subdued by that, and he is in a state where he cannot guard his eye — for example — though he can guard his private parts, then success (al-najāḥ) is more appropriate for him, so that lust may be calmed. Otherwise, if he does not guard his eye, his thought (fikruhu) will not be preserved for him, his concern (hammuhu) will be scattered, and perhaps he will fall into an affliction (balīyah) he cannot bear. For the adultery of the eye (zinā al-ʿayn) is among the greater of the minor sins (kabā'ir al-ṣaghā'ir), and it leads to the approach to the great obscenity, which is the adultery of the private parts (zinā al-farj). And whoever cannot lower his gaze cannot guard his private parts.
24:30.section_title_en: On the Seeker's (Murīd) Beginning: Concerning Marriage, the Gaze, and the Trials of Youth
24:30.anchors:
- Root: زوج (z-w-j)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Pairing, coupling; each of the two mates in a pair.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Used for each of the two companions (male and female) in animals that copulate, and for every two things that are paired, whether similar or opposite. "زوجة" is a poor (radī'ah) dialectal form.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): "He is her husband (zawj) and she is his wife (zawj/zawjah)." Metaphorical (Majaz): "The two speeches paired (tazāwajā) and harmonized (izdawajā)."
- Root: عين (ʿ-yn)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The eye (the organ); also the spring of water.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The eye is the organ. "He is under my eye (bi-ʿaynī)" means: I guard and watch over him, as in {«فإنك بأعيننا»} [Q. 52:48].
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "He is watchful (ʿayyān)." Metaphorical: The gaze (al-naẓar) as the act of the eye, and its extension to the heart's desire.
- Root: قلب (q-l-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To turn, overturn, or flip a thing from one face to another.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Qalb al-shay': to turn it and divert it from one face to another, like turning a garment." The heart (qalb) is so named for its constant turning (taqallub).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "He turned the thing over." Metaphorical: "A man of turning (qalb) and resourcefulness (ḥawal): one who turns matters over and devises stratagems."
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — The particle "innamā" restricts the predicate to the subject alone, negating any share for others. This governs the critical distinction in the text between the Prophet's ﷺ unique state and that of all others.
24:30.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Harms of the Tongue'

26:80.arabic: يميته ويحييه وإذا مرض فهو يشفيه وإذا ضعف فهو يقويه وهو الذي يوفقه للطاعة ويرتضيه وهو الذي يطعمه ويسقيه ويحفظه من الهلاك ويحميه ويحرسه بالطعام والشراب عما يهلكه ويرديه ويمكنه من القناعة بقليل القوت ويقربه حتى تضيق به مجاري الشيطان الذي يناويه ويكسر به شهوة النفس التي تعاديه فيدفع شرها ثم يعبد ربه ويتقيه هذا بعد أن يوسع عليه ما يلتذ به ويشتهيه ويكثر عليه ما يهيج بواعثه ويؤكد دواعيه كل ذلك يمتحنه به ويبتليه فينظر كيف يؤثره على ما يهواه وينتحيه وكيف يحفظ أوامره
26:80.english: And praise belongs to God alone, and blessings upon our master Muḥammad, upon his Family, his Companions, and upon every chosen servant from among the people of the earth and the heavens. And my success is only through God; upon Him I rely and unto Him I turn in repentance.
26:80.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Harms of the Tongue'

40:18.arabic: بصدق المسألة فإني مشغول عنك بقوله تعالى {وأنذرهم يوم الآزفة إذ القلوب لدى الحناجر كاظمين ما للظالمين من حميم ولا شفيع يطاع يعلم خائنة الأعين وما تخفي الصدور} فأين المهرب من هذه الآية ثم جاءت بعد ذلك بأيام فوقفت له على الطريق فلما رآها من بعيد أراد الرجوع إلى منزله كيلا يراها فقالت يا فتى لا ترجع فلا كان الملتقى بعد هذا اليوم أبدا إلا غدا بين يدي الله تعالى ثم بكت بكاء شديدا وقالت اسأل لك الله الذي بيده مفاتيح قلبك أن يسهل ما قد عسر من أمرك ثم إنها تبعته وقالت امنن علي بموعظة أحملها عنك وأوصني بوصية أعمل عليها فقال لها أوصيك بحفظ نفسك من نفسك وأذكرك قوله تعالى {وهو الذي يتوفاكم بالليل ويعلم ما جرحتم بالنهار} قال
40:18.english: ...which one is ashamed of and fears to plunge into. And the abstention of most people from its requirements is either due to incapacity, or fear, or shame, or concern for preserving one's body — and in none of these is there any reward, for that is merely preferring one share of one's worldly desires over another share. Yes — from divine protection (al-ʿiṣmah) is that one is not able [to sin]; so in these obstacles there is a benefit, namely the repulsion of sin. For whoever abandons fornication, its sin is repelled from him by whatever cause his abandonment occurred. Rather, the virtue and abundant reward lie in abandoning it out of fear of God — may He be exalted — while possessing the ability, with the removal of obstacles, the facilitation of means, and especially at the height of genuine desire. And this is the station of the veracious (al-ṣiddīqīn). For this reason, the Prophet — peace be upon him — said: "Whoever loves passionately, then remains chaste, then conceals [his love], then dies — he dies a martyr."(1)
40:18.section_title_en: The Book of Breaking the Two Desires — Section 654: On Chastity, Guarding the Gaze, and the Virtue of Restraining Desire
40:18.anchors:
- **Root: ع ف ف** (ʿaffa)
  * **Lisan / Ayn**: Core meaning of abstaining from what is unlawful, refraining, and remaining chaste; al-ʿafāf is the state of one who abstains from forbidden things.
  * **Al-Raghib (Mufradat)**: Theological nuance — ʿiffah (chastity) is a virtue of the soul that restrains the appetitive faculty from pursuing what is not permissible; it is a station of the ṣiddīqūn (veracious ones).
  * **Al-Zamakhshari (Asas)**: Literal (ḥaqīqah) — physical abstention from unlawful acts; Metaphorical (majāz) — the heart's abstention from coveting what God has forbidden, which is the higher reality of chastity.

- **Root: غ ب ق** (ghabaqa)
  * **Lisan / Ayn**: The evening drink (al-ghabūq) — the milking or drink given at nightfall; contrasted with al-ṣabūḥ (the morning drink).
  * **Al-Raghib (Mufradat)**: In the hadith of the three men in the cave, the term marks the temporal precision of filial devotion — serving parents before any other claim, even at the boundary of night.
  * **Al-Zamakhshari (Asas)**: Literal — the evening milking; the narrative use in the hadith is literal, denoting the exact act of service delayed out of reverence.

- **Root: ه م م** (hamma)
  * **Lisan / Ayn**: To intend, to resolve upon a matter; al-hamm is the initial stirring of intention before full determination.
  * **Al-Raghib (Mufradat)**: In Q. 12:24 {«وَلَقَدْ هَمَّتْ بِهِ وَهَمَّ بِهَا لَوْلَا أَنْ رَأَى بُرْهَانَ رَبِّهِ»} — "And certainly she desired him, and he would have desired her, had it not been that he saw the proof of his Lord" — the term distinguishes between a passing inclination (hamm) and a settled resolve; Yūsuf's hamm was repelled by divine proof, while Zulaykhā's was consummated in action.
  * **Al-Zamakhshari (Asas)**: Literal — the inward movement of intention; the rhetorical force lies in the contrast between the two hamm-s, one punished and one pardoned.

- **Root: ن ظ ر** (naẓara)
  * **Lisan / Ayn**: To look, to gaze; al-naẓar is the act of sight, whether physical or intellectual.
  * **Al-Raghib (Mufradat)**: The gaze (naẓar) is the gateway to desire; the Quranic phrase {«يَعْلَمُ خَائِنَةَ الْأَعْيُنِ»} — "He knows the treachery of the eyes" (Q. 40:19) — indicates that the look which steals toward the forbidden is itself an act of betrayal recorded by God.
  * **Al-Zamakhshari (Asas)**: Literal — the first glance that occurs unintentionally; Metaphorical — the second glance is the "treachery of the eyes," for it is a deliberate return to what the first glance stumbled upon by accident.

- **Root: ر و د** (rāwada)
  * **Lisan / Ayn**: To seek, to desire, to solicit; murāwadah is the act of soliciting someone for an unlawful purpose.
  * **Al-Raghib (Mufradat)**: In the Yūsuf narrative, murāwadah denotes the persistent solicitation toward sin; the term carries the weight of repeated, deliberate pursuit.
  * **Al-Zamakhshari (Asas)**: Literal — the physical act of solicitation; the narrative contexts in this section use the term literally for the woman's pursuit of the young man.

- **Sibawayh Rule**: **Bāb al-ḥaṣr wa-l-taqyīd bi-innamā** (Restriction and Focused Predication with innamā)
  * The particle innamā restricts and confines the predicate to the subject alone, negating all else. In the woman's statement "innamā urīdu mā yakūnu min al-rajuli ilā ahlihī" — "I only desire what comes from a man to his wife" — the restriction (ḥaṣr) intensifies the gravity of the solicitation, making the young man's resistance all the more virtuous.

40:18.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Harms of the Tongue'

56:33.arabic: لنا من هذه الفاكهة المقطوعة الممنوعة لعلنا نذهب إلى الفاكهة التي لا مقطوعة ولا ممنوعة فلما اشتراها وأتى بها إليه قال لنفسه قد خدعتيني حتى نظرت واشتهيت وغلبتيني حتى اشتريت والله لأذقتيه فبعث بها إلى يتامى من الفقراء وعن موسى الأشج أنه قال نفسي تشتهي ملحا جريشا منذ عشرين سنة وعن أحمد بن خليفة قال نفسي تشتهي منذ عشرين سنة ما طلبت مني إلا الماء حتى تروى فما أرويتها وروي أن عتبة الغلام اشتهى لحما سبع سنين فلما كان بعد ذلك قال استحييت من نفسي أن أدافعها منذ سبع سنين سنة بعد سنة فاشتريت قطعة لحم على خبز وشويتها
56:33.english: Indeed, the sustenance (qūt) of a group of the Companions was a ṣāʿ of wheat every Friday. When they ate dates, they took as their sustenance a ṣāʿ and a half of them. The ṣāʿ of wheat is four mudds, so each day would be nearly half a mudd — which is what we mentioned as the measure of one-third of the stomach. An increase was needed for dates because of the pits that are discarded from them. Abū Dharr, may Allah be pleased with him, used to say: "My food every Friday is a ṣāʿ of barley, on the covenant of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him. By Allah, I will not increase upon it anything until I meet him, for I heard him say: 'The nearest of you to me in seating on the Day of Resurrection, and the most beloved of you to me, is the one who dies upon what he is upon today.'" He used to say, disapproving of some of the Companions: "You have changed — barley is sifted for you, though it was not sifted; you bake thin bread; you combine two condiments; foods of various colors are set before you; one of you goes out in one garment and returns in another. They were not like this in the era of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him."
56:33.section_title_en: The Revival of the Religious Sciences — Section 645: On Hunger and the Discipline of Eating
56:33.anchors:
- Root: جوع (j-w-ʿ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of emptiness of the belly, hunger as opposed to fullness (shabaʿ)
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Hunger as a spiritual discipline (riyāḍah) that purifies the heart and weakens the sway of sensual appetite
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) — bodily hunger; Metaphorical (majāz) — the soul's longing and deprivation as spiritual training
- Root: قوت (q-w-t)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Sustenance, nourishment that maintains life; measure of food sufficient for survival
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Provision (rizq) in its minimal necessary form; the qūt is that which sustains the body's constitution without excess
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — food that sustains; Metaphorical — the spiritual sustenance of the heart through remembrance
- Root: أدم (ʾ-d-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: That which is eaten with bread to make it palatable; condiment or relish
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The adornment of food; in spiritual discourse, the craving for variety and relish beyond bare necessity
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — condiment; Metaphorical — the soul's attachment to luxuries and embellishments of worldly life
- Root: سرف (s-r-f)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Excess, extravagance, going beyond the proper limit
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Transgression of the mean (iʿtidāl) in expenditure or consumption; blameworthy in all affairs
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — exceeding the measure; Metaphorical — spiritual extravagance in indulging desires
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد (Restriction & Specification) — The conditional and restrictive constructions (inna-mā, law, idhā) governing the precise boundaries of permissible and blameworthy eating
56:33.topic: Al-Ghazali on the journey of the soul, death, and the Hereafter, from 'Harms of the Tongue'

69:24.arabic: تعالى {كلوا واشربوا هنيئا بما أسلفتم في الأيام الخالية} هي أيام الصيام إذ تركوا فيها الأكل والشرب وقد جمع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في رتبة المباهاة بين الزهد في الدنيا وبين الصوم فقال إن الله تعالى يباهي ملائكته بالشاب العابد فيقول أيها الشاب التارك شهوته لأجلي المبذل شبابه لي أنت عندي كبعض ملائكتي (9) وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم في الصائم يقول الله عز وجل انظروا يا ملائكتي إلى عبدي ترك شهوته ولذته وطعامه وشرابه من أجلي (10) وقيل في قوله تعالى {فلا تعلم نفس ما أخفي لهم من قرة أعين جزاء بما كانوا يعملون
69:24.english: To proceed: Fasting is one quarter of faith, by virtue of his saying, peace and blessings be upon him: "Fasting is half of patience" — and by virtue of his saying, peace and blessings be upon him: "Patience is half of faith" {«الإيمان»}. Then it is distinguished by a particular characteristic of its attribution to Allah the Exalted, above all the other pillars — for Allah the Exalted said, in what His Prophet narrated from Him, peace and blessings be upon him: "Every good deed is multiplied tenfold up to seven hundred times, except fasting, for it is Mine, and I shall reward it." And Allah the Exalted has said: {«Only the patient shall be paid their reward in full without reckoning»} (Q 39:10). And fasting is half of patience — so its reward has surpassed the law of measure and reckoning. And sufficient for you in knowing its excellence is his saying, peace and blessings be upon him: "By Him in whose hand is my soul, the change in the breath of the mouth of the fasting person is more fragrant to Allah than the scent of musk. Allah the Exalted says: 'He only abandons his appetite, his food, and his drink for My sake — so fasting is for Me, and I shall reward it.'" And he said, peace and blessings be upon him: "Paradise has a gate called al-Rayyān, through which none shall enter except the fasting ones." And the fasting person is promised the meeting with Allah the Exalted as a portion of his fasting. And he said, peace and blessings be upon him: "For the fasting person there are two joys: a joy when he breaks his fast, and a joy when he meets his Lord." And he said, peace and blessings be upon him: "Everything has a gate, and the gate of worship is fasting." And he said, peace and blessings be upon him: "The sleep of the fasting person is worship." And Abū Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, narrated that he, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "When the month of Ramaḍān enters, the gates of Paradise are opened, the gates of the Fire are closed, the devils are chained, and a caller calls out: 'O seeker of good, come forth! O seeker of evil, desist!'" And Wakīʿ said concerning His saying, the Exalted: {«Eat and drink in satisfaction for what you sent forth in the days past»} (Q 69:24) — these are the days of fasting, for in them they abandoned eating and drinking. And the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, gathered in the rank of divine boasting (mubāhāh) between renunciation of the world and fasting, saying: "Allah the Exalted boasts to His angels of the young worshiper, saying: 'O young man who abandons his appetite for My sake, who devotes his youth to Me — you are to Me as some of My angels.'" And he said, peace and blessings be upon him, concerning the fasting person: "Allah the Exalted says: 'Look, O My angels, at My servant — he has abandoned his appetite, his pleasure, his food, and his drink for My sake.'" And it was said concerning His saying, the Exalted: {«No soul knows what comfort has been concealed for them, as a reward for what they used to do»} (Q 32:17) — it was said: their deed was fasting, because He said: {«Only the patient shall be paid their reward in full without reckoning»} — so the reward of the fasting person is poured out upon him without measure, and is dealt out to him in bulk, not falling under any imagination or estimation.
69:24.section_title_en: The Book of the Secrets of Fasting — Section 185: On the Excellence of Fasting and Its Distinction Among the Acts of Worship
69:24.anchors:
- Root: صوم (ṣ-w-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core linguistic root meaning — abstention from any act, whether eating, speaking, or walking; a horse that refrains from movement or fodder is called ṣā'im.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological/Kalam semantic nuance — "الصوم في الأصل: الإمساك عن الفعل" — fasting is fundamentally the restraint of the self from action; it is an inward act of the heart, invisible to creation.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal vs Metaphorical distinction — Haqiqah: the month of fasting, "فمن شهد منكم الشهر فليصمه" (Q 2:185); Majaz: "صام الفرس على آريه" — a horse standing still at its tether, refusing fodder, metaphorically "fasting."
- Root: عله (ʿ-l-h)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core linguistic root meaning — to feed or pasture; related to cultivation and nourishment.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological/Kalam semantic nuance — not directly attested in Mufradat for this root; the root pertains to the means by which the body is sustained, which is precisely what the fasting person abstains from.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal vs Metaphorical distinction — literal feeding and satiation; the fasting person's abstention from these becomes the very means of spiritual nourishment.
- Root: الي (a-l-y)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core linguistic root meaning — to convey a message; the angel (malak) is so named because the message is "chewed" (yu'lak) in the mouth, as a horse chews its bit.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological/Kalam semantic nuance — "المألكة: الرسالة" — the angelic function is the conveyance of divine communication; the fasting person's hunger narrows the channels through which the devil (who runs like blood through the veins) reaches the heart.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal vs Metaphorical distinction — literal conveyance of a message versus the metaphorical "message" of the devil's insinuation (waswās) through the pathways of the body.
- Root: صبر (ṣ-b-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core linguistic root meaning — to restrain, to hold back in constriction; "صبرت الدابة: حبستها بلا علف" — to hold an animal back without fodder.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological/Kalam semantic nuance — "الصبر: الإمساك في ضيق" — patience is restraint within constriction; it is the holding of the soul upon what reason and law require, or from what they require it to abstain. Its names vary by context: in battle it is courage, in calamity it is patience proper.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal vs Metaphorical distinction — Haqiqah: "صبرت على ما أكره وصبرت عما أحب" — patience upon the disliked and patience from the beloved; Majaz: "صبرت يمينه" — to bind one's oath severely, and "هو أصبر على الضرب من الأرض" — more enduring of striking than the earth.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — The particle innamā restricts and confines the predicate exclusively to its subject, as in the divine saying {«إنما يوفى الصابرون أجرهم بغير حساب»} and {«إنما يذر شهوته وطعامه وشرابه لأجلي»}, where the restriction elevates the restricted matter to a rank beyond all quantitative measure.
69:24.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Harms of the Tongue'

113:3.arabic: وفي نوادر التفسير عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما {ومن شر غاسق إذا وقب} قال قيام الذكر وهذه يلية غالبة إذا هاجت لا يقاومها عقل ولا دين وهي مع أنها صالحة لأن تكون باعثة على الحياتين كما سبق فهي أقوى آلة الشيطان على بني آدم وإليه أشار صلى الله عليه وسلم بقوله ما رأيت من ناقصات عقل ودين أغلب لذوي الألباب منكن (1) وإنما ذلك لهيجان الشهوة وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم في دعائه اللهم إني أعوذ بك من شر سمعي وبصري وقلبي وشر مني (2) وقال أسألك أن تطهر قلبي وتحفظ فرجي (3) فما يستعيذ منه رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كيف يجوز التساهل فيه لغي
113:3.english: وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم: "لا يلقى الله أحد بذنب أعظم من جهالة أهله."
113:3.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications, prayers, and their spiritual power, from 'Harms of the Tongue'

4:35.arabic: أمرهما {إن يريدا إصلاحا يوفق الله بينهما} وقد بعث عمر رضي الله عنه حكما إلى زوجين فعاد ولم يصلح أمرهما فعلاه بالدرة وقال إن الله تعالى يقول {إن يريدا إصلاحا يوفق الله بينهما} فعاد الرجل وأحسن النية وتلطف بهما فأصلح بينهما وأما إذا كان النشوز من المرأة خاصة فالرجال قوامون على النساء فله أن يؤدبها ويحملها على الطاعة قهرا وكذا إذا كانت تاركة للصلاة فله حملها على الصلاة قهرا ولكن ينبغي أن يتدرج في تأديبها وهو أن يقدم أولا الوعظ والتحذير والتخويف فإن لم ينجح ولاها ظهره في المضجع أو انفرد عنها
4:35.english: I say: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, has said: «من كان له امرأتان فمال إلى إحداهما دون الأخرى» — "Whoever has two wives and inclines toward one of them to the exclusion of the other" — and in another wording: «ولم يعدل بينهما جاء يوم القيامة وأحد شقيه مائل» — "and does not act equitably between them, he shall come on the Day of Resurrection with one of his sides leaning."
4:35.section_title_en: The Revival of the Religious Sciences — Book on the Etiquette of Marriage: Section 305 (On Justice Between Co-Wives, Nushuz, and the Etiquette of Intercourse)
4:35.anchors:
- Root: عدل (ʿadl)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning is "to be equal, to balance, to straighten" — the root denotes equity and even-handedness in distribution.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In theological usage, ʿadl is the mean of justice, opposed to jawr (tyranny) — it is the act of placing things in their proper stations.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah) usage pertains to measurable distribution (ʿatāʾ, mabīt); metaphorical (Majāz) usage extends to that which is not under voluntary control, such as love (maḥabbah) and inclination of the heart.
- Root: نشز (nushūz)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The root denotes "rising up" or "elevation"; in marital context it signifies a rising of one spouse against the other in discord or recalcitrance.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Nushūz is the rebellion of one spouse against the bond of obedience and harmony, a moral elevation against the other.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal usage is the physical rising from a place; metaphorical usage is the spiritual/moral rising in defiance.
- Root: وقع (waqʿ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The root denotes "falling" or "occurrence"; in the marital context, it is a euphemism for sexual intercourse.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The term is used in the Quran for the "falling" of an event; here it is a euphemistic transfer (naql) for coitus.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal usage is physical falling; metaphorical usage is the act of intercourse, as in the hadith "لا يقعن أحدكم على امرأته" (Let none of you fall upon his wife like a beast).
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — The particle innamā restricts the predicate to the subject alone, as in the hadith "إنما عليه العدل في العطاء والمبيت" (Upon him is only justice in expenditure and overnight stays), confining the obligation to what is within human capacity.
4:35.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'Intention, Sincerity and Truthfulness'

4:146.arabic: لله الدين الخالص وقال تعالى إلا الذين تابوا وأصلحوا واعتصموا بالله وأخلصوا دينهم لله وقال تعالى فمن كان يرجو لقاء ربه فليعمل عملا صالحا ولا يشرك بعبادة ربه أحدا نزلت فيمن يعمل لله ويحب أن يحمد عليه وقال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ثلاث لا يغل عليهن قلب رجل مسلم إخلاص العمل لله (1) وعن مصعب بن سعد عن أبيه قال ظن أبي أن له فضلا على من هو دونه من أصحاب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم إنما نصر الله عز وجل هذه الأمة بضعفائها ودعوتهم وإخلاصهم (2) وعن الحسن قال قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول الله تعالى الإخلا
4:146.english: God Most High said: {وما أمروا إلا ليعبدوا الله مخلصين له الدين} "And they were not commanded except to worship God, devoting their religion purely to Him." And He said: {ألا لله الدين الخالص} "Verily, to God belongs the pure religion." And He, Most High, said: {إلا الذين تابوا وأصلحوا واعتصموا بالله وأخلصوا دينهم لله} "Except those who repent, and make amends, and hold fast to God, and make their religion pure for God." And He, Most High, said: {فمن كان يرجو لقاء ربه فليعمل عملا صالحا ولا يشرك بعبادة ربه أحدا} "So whoever hopes for the meeting with his Lord, let him do righteous work, and not associate anyone in the worship of his Lord." This was revealed concerning the one who works for God but loves to be praised for it.
4:146.section_title_en: The Book of the Revival of the Religious Sciences — Section on Sincerity (Ikhlas): Its Virtue and the Peril of Ostentation (Riya')
4:146.anchors:
- Root: أخلَصَ (akhlaṣa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning is purity and clarity; khāliṣ is that which is unmixed and free from adulteration—pure gold, pure milk, pure friendship.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In theological usage, ikhlāṣ is the purification of one's act and intention (niyyah) exclusively for God, stripping away every other motive or partner. It is the essential condition for the acceptance of worship.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah) usage refers to the physical purity of a substance; metaphorical (Majaz) usage transfers this to the heart and deed, signifying the purification of intention from all that is not God.
- Root: دين (dīn)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning includes obedience, recompense, judgment, and the established way or custom.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The "religion" (dīn) of God is the way of obedience and submission to Him; "pure religion" (al-dīn al-khāliṣ) is that which is free from shirk (associationism) and hypocrisy.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the debt or obligation one owes; Metaphorical: the total submission and worship owed exclusively to the Creator.
- Root: راءى (rā'ā)
  * Lisan / Ayn: From the root رأى (ra'ā), to see. The third form implies showing off, making one's deeds seen by others.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Riya' is the seeking of status and praise from creatures, which nullifies the sincerity of the act directed to the Creator.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: to make something visible to the eye; Metaphorical: to perform an act of worship not for God, but so that people may see it and praise the doer.
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Restriction and Focused Predication (باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما) — The particle "innamā" (إنما) restricts the predicate to the subject alone, negating all else. This is critical in the opening verse: "وما أمروا إلا ليعبدوا الله" — the restriction (hasr) via "illā" (except) confines their command solely to the worship of God with pure sincerity.
4:146.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Intention, Sincerity and Truthfulness'

15:40.arabic: وإليه الإشارة بقوله تعالى إلا عبادك منهم المخلصين وبقوله تعالى {إن عبادي ليس لك عليهم سلطان} والسماع سبب لصفاء القلب وهو شبكة للحق بواسطة الصفاء وعلى هذا يدل ما روى أن ذا النون المصري رحمه الله دخل بغداد فاجتمع إليه قوم من الصوفية ومعهم قوال فاستأذنوه في أن يقول لهم شيئا فأذن لهم في ذلك فأنشأ يقول صغير هواك عذبني .
15:40.english: For this reason, he (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Beware the discernment of the believer, for he looks with the light of God." (2)
15:40.section_title_en: The Revival of the Religious Sciences — Section 509: On the Vision of Spiritual Realities Through Purity of Heart
15:40.anchors:
- Root: صفا (ṣafā)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of clarity, purity, and transparency — free from turbidity or admixture.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Denotes the heart's purification from base attributes, rendering it receptive to divine disclosures (mukāshafāt).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: clarity of water or wine. Metaphorical: purity of the heart as the condition for spiritual perception.
- Root: مثل (mathala)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To stand before, to appear, to take shape or form.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Used for representation and formation — the appearing of a thing in a form (ṣūrah) that may or may not correspond to its true reality.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: standing erect before someone. Metaphorical: the self-representation of spiritual beings (arwāḥ) in sensible forms perceptible to the purified heart.
- Root: نظر (naẓar)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Vision, sight, and also reflection and consideration.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Distinguishes between baṣar (physical sight) and baṣīrah (insight); the latter perceives spiritual realities (malakūt).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: seeing with the eye. Metaphorical: "looking with the light of God" (al-naẓar bi-nūr Allāh) — perception through divine illumination.
- Root: فرس (farasa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To prey upon, to seize — the ferāsah (discernment) is so named because it seizes upon the inner reality.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The intuitive perception of inner states — a form of inspired knowledge (ʿilm ladunī).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the lion preying on its quarry. Metaphorical: the believer's discernment that pierces through outward appearances to inward truths.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — Used to confine the activity of devils to hearts filled with blameworthy attributes, and to restrict the vision of the Kingdom of Heaven to purified hearts.
15:40.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Intention, Sincerity and Truthfulness'

16:66.arabic: تقويم وأتم اعتدال ثم غذاه في أول نشوه بلبن استصفاه من بين فرث ودم سائغا كالماء الزلال ثم حماه بما آتاه من طيبات الرزق عن دواعي الضعف والانحلال ثم قيد شهوته المعادية له عن السطوة والصيال وقهرها بما افترضه عليه من طلب القوت الحلال وهزم بكسرها جند الشيطان المتشمر للإضلال ولقد كان يجري من ابن آدم مجرى الدم السيال فضيق عليه عزة الحلال المجرى والمجال إذ كان لا يبذرقه إلى أعماق العروق إلا الشهوة الماثلة إلى الغلبة والاسترسال فبقي لما زمت بزمام الحلال خائبا خاسرا ما له من ناصر ولا وال والصلاة على محمد الهادي من ال
16:66.english: To proceed: The Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, said: «Seeking the lawful is an obligation upon every Muslim» — narrated by Ibn Masʿūd, may God be pleased with him. And this obligation, among all the other obligations, is the most resistant to the intellects in comprehension and the heaviest upon the bodily members in action. For this reason it has become utterly effaced, both as knowledge and as practice. The obscurity of its knowledge became the cause of the effacement of its practice, since the ignorant supposed that the lawful is nonexistent, that the path to reaching it is blocked, and that nothing remains of the good things save fresh water and the herbage growing in dead land — and whatever is beyond that, the transgressing hands have corrupted it and corrupt transactions have spoiled it. And when contentment with the herbage of plants proved impossible, no course remained save expansion into the unlawful. So they abandoned this pole of the religion entirely, and they did not perceive between properties any distinction or difference. Nay, far from it! Far from it! For the lawful is clear and the unlawful is clear, and between them are ambiguous matters; and these three remain ever conjoined, however the states may turn.
16:66.section_title_en: The Book of the Lawful and the Unlawful — Being the Fourth Book of the Quarter of Customs from The Revival of the Religious Sciences
16:66.anchors:
- Root: حمد (ḥ-m-d)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To praise, to laud, to commend; the core sense of acknowledging beneficence with reverence and gratitude.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Praise (ḥamd) is the acknowledgment of favor (niʿmah) with veneration; it is the fitting response to the Divine, who is praised for His essence and His acts alike.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): "Aḥmad Allāh" — to praise God with all His praises. Metaphorical (majāz): "Aḥmadtu al-arḍ" — to find the land commendable as a dwelling; thus praise may be directed to that which is not a rational agent by way of extension.
- Root: طلب (ṭ-l-b)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To seek, to request, to pursue; the exertion of effort toward obtaining something, whether a physical object or a meaning.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Seeking (ṭalab) is the investigation into the existence of a thing, whether it be an entity or a concept; it implies a directed striving of the soul toward its object.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "Ṭalaba al-shayʾ" — to seek a thing with diligence. Metaphorical: "Al-sirāj yaṭlubu an yanṭafiʾ" — the lamp seeks to be extinguished, i.e., it is on the verge of it; thus seeking may denote an inherent inclination toward an end.
- Root: ربع (r-b-ʿ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Four; a quarter; a dwelling-place; to remain in a place.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The root denotes the number four and its derivatives; the quarter (rubʿ) is one of four parts, and the revival of the sciences is divided into four quarters (rubūʿ), each containing books.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "Rabbaʿa al-qawm" — to be the fourth of a people. Metaphorical: "Rabbaʿahu Allāh" — God raised him up and set him aright; thus the quarter (rubʿ) is that which structures and orders the whole.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The permissibility of interposing elements between a preposition and its object when the intervening phrase is semantically complete, allowing for rhetorical expansion without syntactic rupture.
16:66.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'The Lawful and Prohibited'

16:66.arabic: ويسمى الفعل المصفى المخلص إخلاصا قال الله تعالى من بين فرث ودم لبنا خالصا سائغا للشاربين فإنما خلوص اللبن أن لا يكون فيه شوب من الدم والفرث ومن كل ما يمكن أن يمتزج به والإخلاص يضاده الإشراك فمن ليس مخلصا فهو مشرك إلا أن الشرك درجات فالإخلاص في التوحيد يضاده التشريك في الإلهية والشرك منه خفي ومنه جلي وكذا الإخلاص والإخلاص وضده يتواردان على القلب فمحله القلب وإنما يكون ذلك في القصود والنيات وقد ذكر حقيقة النية وأنها ترجع إلى إجابة البواعث فمهما كان الباعث واحد على التجرد سمي الفعل الصادر عنه إخلاصا بالإضافة إلى المنوي فمن تصدق وغرضه محض
16:66.english: Know that every thing which can be conceived as having something else mixed into it — when it becomes clear of that admixture and is purified from it — is called *khāliṣ* (pure/sincere). And the act that has been purified and rendered sincere is called *ikhlāṣ* (sincerity). God Most High has said: {«مِن بَيْنِ فَرْثٍ وَدَمٍ لَّبَنًا خَالِصًا سَائِغًا لِّلشَّارِبِينَ»} ("From between filth and blood, pure milk, palatable to the drinkers") {Sūrat al-Naḥl: 66}. For the purity of milk consists only in there being no admixture in it of blood or filth, nor of anything else that could possibly be mingled with it.
16:66.section_title_en: ** The Reality of Sincerity (Al-Ikhlāṣ) and Its Adversaries — Purifying Works from Worldly Motives
16:66.anchors:
**
- Root: خلص (Khalasa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of becoming pure, clear, and free from admixture after having been mixed; the state of a thing being unmixed with any foreign element.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-Khāliṣ is that which has been stripped of its impurity *after* having contained it — distinguished from ṣāfī which may describe what never had impurity. Theologically: sincerity is the purification of intention from all that is not God.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Ḥaqīqah): "خلوص اللبن" — milk's purity from blood and filth. Metaphorical (Majāz): "أخلص لله دينه" — devoting one's religion exclusively to God; the customary transfer of the term from physical purity to spiritual purity of intention.
- Root: شرك (Sharaka)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Mixing or sharing between two parties in a single thing; partnership.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الشركة: خلط الملكين" — the intermingling of two ownerships; applied to associating another with God in worship or intention.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: partnership in property. Metaphorical: "أشرك بالله" — ascribing a partner to God; the hidden degrees of which are the concern here.
- Root: نفس (Nafs)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The self; that which desires and inclines toward worldly gratification.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The soul as the seat of appetites and worldly attachments — the internal obstacle to pure devotion.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the self. Metaphorical: "نفس سائلة" — flowing blood; here, the soul's "shares" (ḥuẓūẓ) are its cravings for worldly benefit.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد (Restriction and Specification) — The construction "إنما الإخلاص تخليص العمل" effects exclusive restriction, confining the reality of sincerity to the sole purification of the act from all admixture, with the predicate grammatically restricted to the subject alone.

---

19:41.arabic: الصديق مشتق منه والله تعالى وصف الأنبياء به في معرض المدح والثناء فقال {واذكر في الكتاب إبراهيم إنه كان صديقا نبيا} وقال واذكر في الكتاب إسمعيل إنه كان صادق الوعد وكان رسولا نبيا وقال تعالى {واذكر في الكتاب إدريس إنه كان صديقا نبيا} وقال ابن عباس أربع من كن فيه فقد ربح الصدق والحياء وحسن الخلق والشكر وقال بشر ابن الحارث من عامل الله بالصدق استوحش من الناس وقال أبو عبد الله الرملي رأيت منصور الدينوري في المنام فقلت له ما فعل الله بك قال غفر لي ورحمني وأعطاني ما لم أؤمل فقلت له أحسن ما توجه العبد به إلى الله ماذا قال الصدق و
19:41.english: God Most High has said: {«رجال صدقوا ما عاهدوا الله عليه»} — "Among the believers are men who have been true to the covenant they made with God" (Al-Aḥzāb 33:23). And the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Verily, truthfulness leads to righteousness (al-birr), and righteousness leads to Paradise. And verily, a man continues to speak truthfully until he is written with God as a supremely veracious one (ṣiddīq). And verily, falsehood leads to wickedness (al-fujūr), and wickedness leads to the Fire. And verily, a man continues to lie until he is written with God as a liar (kadhdhāb)." (1)
19:41.section_title_en: The Book of Truthfulness (Ṣidq): Its Virtue and Reality — Section on the Virtue of Truthfulness
19:41.anchors:
- Root: صدق (Ṣ-D-Q)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root denotes the firmness and soundness of a thing; a spear termed "ṣadq" is straight and rigid; truthfulness is speech that is firm, sound, and free of crookedness.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الصدق والكذب أصلهما في القول" — truthfulness and falsehood originate in speech, whether past or future, promise or otherwise; they occur by primary intent only in informative statements (khabar), not in other speech categories. Al-Raghib further notes the derived degrees: ṣidq (truthfulness), ṣiddīq (the supremely veracious — one whose truthfulness has become his very character), and ṣādiq al-waʿd (truthful in promise).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Haqiqah (literal): "صدقته الحديث" — to affirm someone's report as true. Majaz (metaphorical): "رجل صادق الحملة" — a man truthful in his charge (i.e., steadfast and unfaltering in battle), and "فرس ذو مصدق في الجري" — a horse with genuine exertion in running. Thus ṣidq extends metaphorically to any state of firmness, steadfastness, and correspondence between inner conviction and outward action.
- Root: بر (B-R-R)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Al-Birr: expansive goodness, piety, and obedience; the "barr" (land) is so named for its expanse. It encompasses all acts of righteousness and kindness.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-birr is the breadth of obedience to God through sincere intention and righteous action; it is the comprehensive term for all that God loves and approves.
- Root: فجر (F-J-R)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Al-Fujūr: the breaking forth and bursting open — the wickedness that breaks through the barrier of piety; the "fājir" is one who bursts out of obedience into transgression.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Fujūr is the violation of the covenant of obedience, the breaking open of the seal of God-consciousness; it is the opposite of birr.
- Root: كذب (K-DH-B)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Al-Kidhb: falsehood — informing of a thing contrary to its reality; the root also carries the sense of deficiency and weakness (as in "kadhaba" — to fall short).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Falsehood is the counterpart of ṣidq — it is reporting what does not correspond to reality, whether in past, present, or future tense.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The grammatical structure "يكتب عند الله صديقا" (he is written with God as a ṣiddīq) involves the prepositional phrase "عند الله" interposed between the verb and its predicate accusative, a construction permissible when the interposed element is semantically integral to the judgment, as here where divine decree is the ground of the designation.
19:41.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'Intention, Sincerity and Truthfulness'

19:56.arabic: واذكر في الكتاب إسمعيل إنه كان صادق الوعد وكان رسولا نبيا وقال تعالى {واذكر في الكتاب إدريس إنه كان صديقا نبيا} وقال ابن عباس أربع من كن فيه فقد ربح الصدق والحياء وحسن الخلق والشكر وقال بشر ابن الحارث من عامل الله بالصدق استوحش من الناس وقال أبو عبد الله الرملي رأيت منصور الدينوري في المنام فقلت له ما فعل الله بك قال غفر لي ورحمني وأعطاني ما لم أؤمل فقلت له أحسن ما توجه العبد به إلى الله ماذا قال الصدق وأقبح ما توجه به الكذب وقال أبو سليمان اجعل الصدق مطيتك والحق سيفك والله تعالى غاية طلبتك وقال رجل لحكيم ما رأيت صادقا فقال له لو ك
19:56.english: God Most High has said: {«رجال صدقوا ما عاهدوا الله عليه»} — "Among the believers are men who have been true to the covenant they made with God" (Al-Aḥzāb 33:23). And the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Verily, truthfulness leads to righteousness (al-birr), and righteousness leads to Paradise. And verily, a man continues to speak truthfully until he is written with God as a supremely veracious one (ṣiddīq). And verily, falsehood leads to wickedness (al-fujūr), and wickedness leads to the Fire. And verily, a man continues to lie until he is written with God as a liar (kadhdhāb)." (1)
19:56.section_title_en: The Book of Truthfulness (Ṣidq): Its Virtue and Reality — Section on the Virtue of Truthfulness
19:56.anchors:
- Root: صدق (Ṣ-D-Q)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root denotes the firmness and soundness of a thing; a spear termed "ṣadq" is straight and rigid; truthfulness is speech that is firm, sound, and free of crookedness.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الصدق والكذب أصلهما في القول" — truthfulness and falsehood originate in speech, whether past or future, promise or otherwise; they occur by primary intent only in informative statements (khabar), not in other speech categories. Al-Raghib further notes the derived degrees: ṣidq (truthfulness), ṣiddīq (the supremely veracious — one whose truthfulness has become his very character), and ṣādiq al-waʿd (truthful in promise).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Haqiqah (literal): "صدقته الحديث" — to affirm someone's report as true. Majaz (metaphorical): "رجل صادق الحملة" — a man truthful in his charge (i.e., steadfast and unfaltering in battle), and "فرس ذو مصدق في الجري" — a horse with genuine exertion in running. Thus ṣidq extends metaphorically to any state of firmness, steadfastness, and correspondence between inner conviction and outward action.

33:23.arabic: فضيلة الصدق قال الله تعالى {رجال صدقوا ما عاهدوا الله عليه} وقال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم إن الصدق يهدي إلى البر والبر يهدي إلى الجنة وإن الرجل ليصدق حتى يكتب عند الله صديقا وإن الكذب يهدي إلى الفجور والفجور يهدي إلى النار وإن الرجل ليكذب حتى يكتب عند الله كذابا (1) ويكفي في فضيلة الصدق أن الصديق مشتق منه والله تعالى وصف الأنبياء به في معرض المدح والثناء فقال {واذكر في الكتاب إبراهيم إنه كان صديقا نبيا} وقال واذكر في الكتاب إسمعيل إنه كان صادق الوعد وكان رسولا نبيا

And the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Verily, truthfulness leads to righteousness (al-birr), and righteousness leads to Paradise. And verily, a man continues to speak truthfully until he is written with God as a supremely veracious one (ṣiddīq). And verily, falsehood leads to wickedness (al-fujūr), and wickedness leads to the Fire. And verily, a man continues to lie until he is written with God as a liar (kadhdhāb)." (1)

38:83.arabic: وإليه الإشارة بقوله تعالى إلا عبادك منهم المخلصين وبقوله تعالى {إن عبادي ليس لك عليهم سلطان} والسماع سبب لصفاء القلب وهو شبكة للحق بواسطة الصفاء وعلى هذا يدل ما روى أن ذا النون المصري رحمه الله دخل بغداد فاجتمع إليه قوم من الصوفية ومعهم قوال فاستأذنوه في أن يقول لهم شيئا فأذن لهم في ذلك فأنشأ يقول صغير هواك عذبني .
38:83.english: For this reason, he (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Beware the discernment of the believer, for he looks with the light of God." (2)
38:83.section_title_en: The Revival of the Religious Sciences — Section 509: On the Vision of Spiritual Realities Through Purity of Heart
38:83.anchors:
- Root: صفا (ṣafā)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of clarity, purity, and transparency — free from turbidity or admixture.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Denotes the heart's purification from base attributes, rendering it receptive to divine disclosures (mukāshafāt).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: clarity of water or wine. Metaphorical: purity of the heart as the condition for spiritual perception.
- Root: مثل (mathala)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To stand before, to appear, to take shape or form.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Used for representation and formation — the appearing of a thing in a form (ṣūrah) that may or may not correspond to its true reality.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: standing erect before someone. Metaphorical: the self-representation of spiritual beings (arwāḥ) in sensible forms perceptible to the purified heart.
- Root: نظر (naẓar)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Vision, sight, and also reflection and consideration.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Distinguishes between baṣar (physical sight) and baṣīrah (insight); the latter perceives spiritual realities (malakūt).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: seeing with the eye. Metaphorical: "looking with the light of God" (al-naẓar bi-nūr Allāh) — perception through divine illumination.
- Root: فرس (farasa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To prey upon, to seize — the ferāsah (discernment) is so named because it seizes upon the inner reality.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The intuitive perception of inner states — a form of inspired knowledge (ʿilm ladunī).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the lion preying on its quarry. Metaphorical: the believer's discernment that pierces through outward appearances to inward truths.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — Used to confine the activity of devils to hearts filled with blameworthy attributes, and to restrict the vision of the Kingdom of Heaven to purified hearts.

39:48.arabic: بقوله تعالى وبدا لهم من الله مالم يكونوا يحتسبون وبدا لهم سيئات ما كسبوا وبقوله تعالى قل هل ننبئكم بالأخسرين أعمالا الذين ضل سعيهم في الحياة الدنيا وهم يحسبون أنهم يحسنون صنعا وأشد الخلق تعرضا لهذه الفتنة العلماء فإن الباعث للأكثرين على نشر العلم لذة الاستيلاء والفرح بالاستتباع والاستبشار بالحمد والثناء والشيطان يلبس عليهم ذلك ويقول غرضكم نشر دين الله والنضال عن الشرع الذي شرعه رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وترى الواعظ يمن على الله تعالى بنصيحة الخلق ووعظه للسلاطين ويفرح بقبول الناس قوله وإقبالهم عليه
39:48.english: Know that every thing which can be conceived as having something else mixed into it — when it becomes clear of that admixture and is purified from it — is called *khāliṣ* (pure/sincere). And the act that has been purified and rendered sincere is called *ikhlāṣ* (sincerity). God Most High has said: {«مِن بَيْنِ فَرْثٍ وَدَمٍ لَّبَنًا خَالِصًا سَائِغًا لِّلشَّارِبِينَ»} ("From between filth and blood, pure milk, palatable to the drinkers") {Sūrat al-Naḥl: 66}. For the purity of milk consists only in there being no admixture in it of blood or filth, nor of anything else that could possibly be mingled with it.
39:48.section_title_en: ** The Reality of Sincerity (Al-Ikhlāṣ) and Its Adversaries — Purifying Works from Worldly Motives
39:48.anchors:
**
- Root: خلص (Khalasa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning of becoming pure, clear, and free from admixture after having been mixed; the state of a thing being unmixed with any foreign element.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-Khāliṣ is that which has been stripped of its impurity *after* having contained it — distinguished from ṣāfī which may describe what never had impurity. Theologically: sincerity is the purification of intention from all that is not God.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Ḥaqīqah): "خلوص اللبن" — milk's purity from blood and filth. Metaphorical (Majāz): "أخلص لله دينه" — devoting one's religion exclusively to God; the customary transfer of the term from physical purity to spiritual purity of intention.
- Root: شرك (Sharaka)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Mixing or sharing between two parties in a single thing; partnership.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الشركة: خلط الملكين" — the intermingling of two ownerships; applied to associating another with God in worship or intention.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: partnership in property. Metaphorical: "أشرك بالله" — ascribing a partner to God; the hidden degrees of which are the concern here.
- Root: نفس (Nafs)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The self; that which desires and inclines toward worldly gratification.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The soul as the seat of appetites and worldly attachments — the internal obstacle to pure devotion.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the self. Metaphorical: "نفس سائلة" — flowing blood; here, the soul's "shares" (ḥuẓūẓ) are its cravings for worldly benefit.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد (Restriction and Specification) — The construction "إنما الإخلاص تخليص العمل" effects exclusive restriction, confining the reality of sincerity to the sole purification of the act from all admixture, with the predicate grammatically restricted to the subject alone.

---

39:60.arabic: وقال الثوري في قوله تعالى {ويوم القيامة ترى الذين كذبوا على الله وجوههم مسودة} قال هم الذين ادعوا محبة الله تعالى ولم يكونوا بها صادقين وأوحى الله تعالى إلى داود عليه السلام يا داود من صدقني في سريرته صدقته عند المخلوقين في علانيته وصاح رجل في مجلس الشبلي ورمى نفسه في دجلة فقال الشبلي إن كان صادقا فالله تعالى ينجيه كما نجى موسى عليه السلام وإن كان كاذبا فالله تعالى يغرقه كما أغرق فرعون وقال بعضهم أجمع الفقهاء والعلماء على ثلاث خصال أنها إذا صحت ففيها النجاة ولا يتم بعضها إلا ببعض الإسلام الخالص عن البدعة والهوى

47:31.arabic: إذا قرأ {ولنبلونكم حتى نعلم المجاهدين منكم والصابرين ونبلو أخباركم} يبكي ويرددها ويقول إنك إن بلوتنا فضحتنا وهتكت أستارنا وقال الحسن إنما خلد أهل الجنة في الجنة وأهل النار في النار بالنيات وقال أبو هريرة مكتوب في التوراة ما أريد به وجهي فقليله كثير وما أريد به غيري فكثيره قليل وقال بلال بن سعد إن العبد ليقول قول مؤمن فلا يدعه الله عز وجل وقوله حتى ينظر في عمله فإذا عمل لم يدعه الله حتى ينظر في ورعه فإن تورع لم يدعه حتى ينظر ماذا نوى فإن صلحت نيته فبالحري أن يصلح ما دون ذلك فإذن عماد الأعمال بالنيات ف
47:31.english: God Most High said: {«وَلا تَطْرُدِ الَّذِينَ يَدْعُونَ رَبَّهُمْ بِالْغَدَاةِ وَالْعَشِيِّ يُرِيدُونَ وَجْهَهُ»} — "And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord morning and evening, desiring His Face." And the meaning of that "desiring" (irādah) is the intention (niyyah).
47:31.section_title_en: The Pillar of Deeds is Intention — Section 1206 of The Revival of the Religious Sciences
47:31.anchors:
- Root: نوي (N-W-Y)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning is "intention, purpose, resolve" — the inward aim that directs an act; from the sense of "distance" (nāya) implying the goal one sets one's course toward.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-niyyah is the resolve of the heart that distinguishes the moral identity of an act; it is the internal specification (takhṣīṣ) that renders an act either obedience or disobedience, sincerity or hypocrisy.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) usage denotes the heart's determination toward a goal; metaphorical (majāz) extension applies it to the act's value in the afterlife — "he is raised according to his intention."
- Root: عمل (ʿ-A-M-L)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Deliberate, purposeful action issuing from a living agent — contrasted with mere occurrence.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): ʿAmal is every deed done by an animal with intent; it is more specific than fiʿl (act), and applies to both good and evil works. Its moral weight is entirely contingent upon the niyyah that animates it.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: exertion of effort in a task. Metaphorical: the deed's acceptance or rejection before God, determined by what the heart intended.
- Root: قتل (Q-T-L)
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Removal of the soul from the body; when attributed to the agent, it is "killing" (qatl). In the verse {فلم تقتلوهم ولكن الله قتلهم} [Al-Anfāl/17], killing is metaphorically ascribed to God as the true Creator of all acts.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas - Majaz): "A heart slain (qalb muqattal)" — destroyed by love; "slain by the jinn" — possessed. The root extends metaphorically to total spiritual ruin or salvation depending on the intention behind the physical act.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — The Prophet's saying {إنما الأعمال بالنيات} restricts all deeds to their intentions, making niyyah the exclusive determinant of an act's moral and eschatological value.
47:31.topic: Al-Ghazali on the journey of the soul, death, and the Hereafter, from 'Intention, Sincerity and Truthfulness'

2:188.arabic: وقال تعالى ولا تأكلوا أموالكم بينكم بالباطل وقال تعالى إن الذين يأكلون أموال اليتامى ظلما الآية وقال تعالى يا أيها الذين آمنوا اتقوا الله وذروا ما بقي من الربا إن كنتم مؤمنين {ثم قال} فإن لم تفعلوا فأذنوا بحرب من الله ورسوله {ثم قال} وإن تبتم فلكم رءوس أموالكم {ثم قال} ومن عاد فأولئك أصحاب النار هم فيها خالدون جعل آكل الربا أول الأمر مؤذنا بمحاربة الله وفي آخره متعرضا للنار والآيات الواردة في الحلال والحرام لا تحصى وروى ابن مسعود رضي الله عنه عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال طلب الحلال
2:188.english: God Most High has said: {«كلوا من الطيبات واعملوا صالحا»} — "Eat of the good things and do righteous deeds." (Q. 23:51) He commanded eating from the good things before [commanding] righteous deeds. And it is said that what is meant by "the good things" is the lawful (al-ḥalāl).
2:188.section_title_en: The Revival of the Religious Sciences — Book of the Etiquette of Eating: Section 336 — The Virtue of Lawful Sustenance and the Blameworthiness of the Forbidden
2:188.anchors:
- Root: اكل (akl)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root meaning of eating, consuming, and tasting food; the act of taking nourishment into the body.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الأكل: تناول المطعم" — eating is the taking of food; used metaphorically for fire consuming wood, and extended to mean lawful provision (ḥalāl) as the sustenance of the soul's soundness.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) for physical ingestion; metaphorical (majāz) for consuming wealth unlawfully, as in "أكل مال اليتيم" (devouring the orphan's wealth).
- Root: طعم (tuʿm)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Food, sustenance, and the act of tasting; also used for bait and that which is eaten.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Sustenance as that which nourishes the body; in the Kalam context, the lawful (ḥalāl) is that which purifies the heart, while the forbidden (ḥarām) corrupts it.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal for food; metaphorical for the moral state of the soul — "طعمه حرام" (his food is forbidden) signifies the corruption of one's entire being.
- Root: ورق (waraʿ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Abstinence, scrupulousness, and piety; refraining from doubtful matters.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The theological virtue of cautious avoidance of all that is suspect, as the foundation of true worship and the key to answered supplication.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal for refraining; metaphorical for the heart's purity achieved through guarding the limbs from the unlawful.

2:275.arabic: وإن تبتم فلكم رءوس أموالكم {ثم قال} ومن عاد فأولئك أصحاب النار هم فيها خالدون جعل آكل الربا أول الأمر مؤذنا بمحاربة الله وفي آخره متعرضا للنار والآيات الواردة في الحلال والحرام لا تحصى وروى ابن مسعود رضي الله عنه عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال طلب الحلال فريضة على كل مسلم ولما قال صلى الله عليه وسلم طلب العلم فريضة على كل مسلم (1) قال بعض العلماء أراد به طلب علم الحلال والحرام وجعل المراد بالحديثين واحدا وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم من سعى على عياله من حله فهو كالمجاهد في سبيل الله ومن طلب الدنيا حلالا في عفاف كان في
2:275.english: God Most High has said: {«كلوا من الطيبات واعملوا صالحا»} — "Eat of the good things and do righteous deeds." (Q. 23:51) He commanded eating from the good things before [commanding] righteous deeds. And it is said that what is meant by "the good things" is the lawful (al-ḥalāl).

4:10.arabic: وقال تعالى ولا تأكلوا أموالكم بينكم بالباطل وقال تعالى إن الذين يأكلون أموال اليتامى ظلما الآية وقال تعالى يا أيها الذين آمنوا اتقوا الله وذروا ما بقي من الربا إن كنتم مؤمنين {ثم قال} فإن لم تفعلوا فأذنوا بحرب من الله ورسوله {ثم قال} وإن تبتم فلكم رءوس أموالكم {ثم قال} ومن عاد فأولئك أصحاب النار هم فيها خالدون جعل آكل الربا أول الأمر مؤذنا بمحاربة الله وفي آخره متعرضا للنار والآيات الواردة في الحلال والحرام لا تحصى وروى ابن مسعود رضي الله عنه عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال طلب الحلال فريضة على كل مسلم ولما قال صلى الله عليه وسلم طلب
