5:19.arabic: وسلم على فترة من الرسل وكان شرع عيسى عليه السلام قد مضى عليه قريب من ستمائة سنة والناس منقسمون إلى مكذبين له من اليهود وعبدة الأوثان وإلى مصدقين له قد شاع الفسق فيهم كما شاع في زماننا الآن والكفار مخاطبون بفروع الشريعة والأموال كانت في أيدي المكذبين له والمصدقين أما المكذبون فكانوا يتعاملون بغير شرع عيسى عليه السلام وأما المصدقون فكان يتساهلون مع أصل التصديق
5:19.english: As for the third [possibility]—namely, restricting oneself to the measure of necessity without any increase upon it, while making no distinction between one property and another, whether it be taken by usurpation (ghaṣb), theft (sariqah), mutual consent (tarāḍī), or however it may happen—this is the removal of the Law's barrier between the corrupters and the kinds of corruption. Hands would then stretch forth in usurpation, theft, and varieties of injustice, and there would be no way to deter them from it, for they would say: "The possessor of a hand is not distinguished from us by any entitlement, for it is forbidden to him and to us alike. The possessor has only the measure of his necessity. If he is in need, then we too are in need; and if what you have taken in my right exceeds your necessity, then you have stolen it from one who exceeds his need for his day." And if the need of the day and the year is not to be regarded, then what are we to regard? And how is this to be regulated? This leads to the nullification of the Law's governance and the incitement of the people of corruption to corruption. Thus nothing remains but the fourth possibility—namely, that it be said: Every possessor of a hand has a right to what is in his hand, and he has priority over it; it is not permissible that it be taken from him by theft or usurpation, but rather it is taken with his consent. And mutual consent (tarāḍī) is the path of the Law. And since it is not permissible except by mutual consent, mutual consent itself has a detailed methodology (minhāj) in the Law, upon which the [worldly] interests depend. For if this detail is not taken into account, then the very foundation of mutual consent would not be established, and its elaboration would be rendered inoperative.
5:19.section_title_en: On the Limits of Acquisition and the Necessity of Legal Proprietary Norms
5:19.anchors:
- Root: قدر (qadr)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core measure, extent, limit, or decree; that by which a thing is measured or determined.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): When applied to God, absolute power (qudrah) negates incapacity; when applied to man, it denotes a capacity restricted by need and circumstance—never absolute, always qualified.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (haqiqah): "measure, amount, destiny." Metaphorical (majaz): "a far-reaching steed" (faras baʿīd al-qadr)—extension beyond the ordinary, applicable here to the overreach of tyrants' hands.
- Root: حاج (ḥāj)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Need, want, necessity—entailing both lack and longing for fulfillment.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Al-ḥājah ilā al-shay': al-faqr ilayhi maʿa maḥabbati-hi"—poverty toward a thing coupled with desire for it; collective: ḥājāt, ḥawāʾij.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: genuine exigency. Metaphorical: not applicable here—remains strictly literal in juristic discourse.
- Root: شرع (sharaʿa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: A clear, well-trodden path; the source from which one drinks.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Al-sharʿ: nahj al-ṭarīq al-wāḍiḥ"—the manifest way; then transferred (istiʿārah) to the divine law (sharīʿah) as the path of God's command.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the revealed law and its ordinances. Metaphorical: "the camel extends its neck" (sharraʿa al-baʿīr sharāʿahu)—likened to a ship's sail; here, the law's detailed provisions (tafṣīl) are the operative extension of its foundational principle (aṣl).
- Root: ايد (ayd)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Strength, power, support; to fortify.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "Ayyadtu-hu bi-rūḥ al-qudus"—I strengthened him; God's ʾayd is His mighty power. "Wa-al-samāʾa banaynāhā bi-ayd"—by [Our] strength.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical or metaphysical might. Metaphorical: "abundant hospitality" (ādat ḍiyāfatuhu)—an overflowing provision; here, the "hand" (yad) of possession as the locus of legal entitlement.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition)—The permissibility of interposing elements between a governing word and its governed prepositional phrase depends on whether the intervening clause can stand independently; likewise, the law's foundational principle (aṣl al-tarāḍī) cannot be severed from its detailed application (tafṣīl) without rendering the whole inoperative.
5:19.topic: Al-Ghazali on purifying the character, moral diseases, and spiritual remedies, from 'The Lawful and Prohibited'

6:1.arabic: وإذا قربت من الإنزال فقل في نفسك ولا تحرك شفتيك الحمد لله الذي خلق من الماء بشرا فجعله نسبا وصهرا وكان ربك قديرا وكان بعض أصحاب الحديث يكبر حتى يسمع أهل الدار صوته ثم ينحرف عن القبلة ولا يستقبل القبلة بالوقاع إكراما للقبلة وليغط نفسه وأهله بثوب كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يغطي رأسه ويغض صوته ويقول للمرأة عليك بالسكينة (2) وفي الخبر إذا جامع أحدكم أهله فلا يتجردان تجرد العيرين (3) أي الحمارين وليقدم التلطف بالكلام والتقبيل قال صلى الله عليه وسلم لا يقعن أحدكم على امرأته كما تقع البهيمة وليكن بينهما رسول قي
6:1.english: I say: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, has said: «من كان له امرأتان فمال إلى إحداهما دون الأخرى» — "Whoever has two wives and inclines toward one of them to the exclusion of the other" — and in another wording: «ولم يعدل بينهما جاء يوم القيامة وأحد شقيه مائل» — "and does not act equitably between them, he shall come on the Day of Resurrection with one of his sides leaning."
6:1.section_title_en: The Revival of the Religious Sciences — Book on the Etiquette of Marriage: Section 305 (On Justice Between Co-Wives, Nushuz, and the Etiquette of Intercourse)
6:1.anchors:
- Root: عدل (ʿadl)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning is "to be equal, to balance, to straighten" — the root denotes equity and even-handedness in distribution.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In theological usage, ʿadl is the mean of justice, opposed to jawr (tyranny) — it is the act of placing things in their proper stations.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah) usage pertains to measurable distribution (ʿatāʾ, mabīt); metaphorical (Majāz) usage extends to that which is not under voluntary control, such as love (maḥabbah) and inclination of the heart.
- Root: نشز (nushūz)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The root denotes "rising up" or "elevation"; in marital context it signifies a rising of one spouse against the other in discord or recalcitrance.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Nushūz is the rebellion of one spouse against the bond of obedience and harmony, a moral elevation against the other.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal usage is the physical rising from a place; metaphorical usage is the spiritual/moral rising in defiance.
- Root: وقع (waqʿ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The root denotes "falling" or "occurrence"; in the marital context, it is a euphemism for sexual intercourse.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The term is used in the Quran for the "falling" of an event; here it is a euphemistic transfer (naql) for coitus.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal usage is physical falling; metaphorical usage is the act of intercourse, as in the hadith "لا يقعن أحدكم على امرأته" (Let none of you fall upon his wife like a beast).
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — The particle innamā restricts the predicate to the subject alone, as in the hadith "إنما عليه العدل في العطاء والمبيت" (Upon him is only justice in expenditure and overnight stays), confining the obligation to what is within human capacity.

9:109.arabic: البنيان وارتفع وإذا ضعف الأساس واعوج انهار البنيان ووقع وقال الله عز وجل أفمن أسس بنيانه على تقوى من الله الآية وفي الحديث من اكتسب مالا من حرام فإن تصدق به لم يقبل منه وإن تركه وراءه كان زاده إلى النار (11) وقد ذكرنا جملة من الأخبار في كتاب آداب الكسب تكشف عن فضيلة الكسب الحلال وأما الآثار فقد ورد أن الصديق رضي الله عنه شرب لبنا من كسب عبده ثم سأل عبده فقال تكهنت لقوم فأعطوني فأدخل أصابعه في فيه وجعل يقيء حتى ظننت أن نفسه ستخرج ثم قال اللهم إني أعتذر إليك مما حملت العروق وخالط الأمعاء (12) وفي بعض الأخبار أنه صلى الله عليه وسلم أ

11:113.arabic: شهده قال تعالى {ولا تركنوا إلى الذين ظلموا} قيل لا ترضوا بأعمالهم فإن كنت في القوة بحيث لا تزداد حبالهم بذلك فلا بأس بالأخذ وقد حكي عن بعض عباد البصرة أنه كان يأخذ أموالا ويفرقها فقيل له ألا تخاف أن تحبهم فقال لو أخذ رجل بيدي وأدخلني الجنة ثم عصى ربه ما أحبه قلبي لأن ما الذي سخره للأخذ بيدي هو الذي أبغضه لأجله شكرا له على تصخيره إياه وبهذا تبين أخذ المال الآن منهم وإن كان ذلك المال بعينه من وجه حلال محذور ومذموم لأنه لا ينفك عن هذه الغوائل
11:113.english: Wahb ibn Munabbih related that a man was brought before a king in the sight of the people, to be compelled to eat the flesh of swine — and he did not eat. Then roasted sheep's flesh was presented to him, and he was compelled by the sword — and he did not eat. So it was said to him concerning that, and he replied: "The people have come to believe that I was demanded to eat swine's flesh. So if I come out safe, having eaten, they will not know what I ate — and they will be led astray."
11:113.section_title_en: ** Section 393: On Accepting Wealth from Rulers for Distribution — The Three Perils
11:113.anchors:
**
- Root: أ-ل-ك (ʾ-l-k)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The root denotes "to carry a message" (al-ulūkah/al-alūkah = the message). Al-Farahidi: "al-maʾlakah: the message, because it is carried in the mouth."
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "al-malāʾikah" (angels) derives from this root — one who carries the message between the Divine and creation. The term "malak" (angel) is a contraction of "maʾlak."
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal usage: "alkani ilā fulān" (carry my message to so-and-so). The metaphorical extension applies to any commission of trust.
- Root: و-ق-د (w-q-d)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "To kindle, to burn, to blaze." Al-Ayn: "waqadat al-nār" (the fire blazed).
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "al-wuqūd" is both the fuel and the act of burning. In the Quranic verse {«وَقُودُهَا النَّاسُ وَالْحِجَارَةُ»} ("whose fuel is men and stones"), the term denotes that which feeds the fire.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas - Majaz): Metaphorical: "qalbun waqqād" (a blazing heart — i.e., sharp, penetrating intellect). The "blazing" of the heart in love or zeal is a metaphorical extension of the physical burning of fire.
- Root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "To be, to exist, to come into being." The root denotes existence and becoming.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "kāna" in its full sense denotes coming into being after non-existence; in its defective (nāqiṣah) usage, it links predicate to subject without implying temporal origination.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): The literal sense is "to be"; the metaphorical extension applies to any state or condition that "comes to be" for a person.
- Sibawayh Rule: Bāb al-Ḥaṣr wa-al-Taqyīd bi-innamā (Restriction and Focused Predication with innamā) — When the construction "innamā" is used, it restricts the predicate to the subject alone, excluding all else. This is critical for understanding the author's restrictive statements about when taking is permissible.

18:19.arabic: شيء يسير فقال له عمر حسبك بصحبته يوما أو بعض يوم شؤما وشرا وقال الفضيل ما ازداد رجل من ذي سلطان قربا إلا ازداد من الله بعدا وكان سعيد بن المسيب يتجر في الزيت ويقول إن في هذا لغنى عن هؤلاء السلاطين وقال وهيب هؤلاء الذين يدخلون على الملوك لهم أضر على الأمة من المقامرين وقال محمد بن سلمة الذباب على العذرة أحسن من قارئ على باب هؤلاء ولما خالط الزهري السلطان كتب أخ له في الدين إليه عافانا الله وإياك أبا بكر من الفتن فقد أصبحت بحال ينبغي لمن عرفك أن يدعوا لك الله ويرحمك أصبحت شيخا كبيرا قد أثقلتك
18:19.english: As for the reports: When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, described the tyrannical rulers, he said: "Whoever opposes them is saved, whoever withdraws from them is safe — or nearly safe — and whoever falls in with them in their worldly affairs is of them." (1)
18:19.section_title_en: The Sixth Chapter: On What is Lawful and Unlawful in Associating with Tyrannical Rulers, and the Ruling on Frequent Their Assemblies, Entering Upon Them, and Showing Them Honor
18:19.anchors:
- Root: ظلم (Ẓ-L-M)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning is placing something in other than its proper place; darkness as the absence of light.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الظلمة: عدم النور" — darkness is the absence of light; used metaphorically for ignorance, polytheism, and transgression, as opposed to light (نور) which represents knowledge and justice.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): "الظلم ظلمة كما أن العدل نور" — injustice is darkness just as justice is light. Metaphorical (Majaz): "أرض مظلومة" — land never dug or watered, indicating the deprivation of benefit.
- Root: وهي (W-H-Y)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Weakness, fissure, or slackening in a structure; a crack in leather or a wall.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الوهي: شق في الأديم والثوب" — a rent in hide or cloth; "وكل شيء استرخى رباطه فقد وهي" — anything whose binding slackens has become weak.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "وهى الحائط" — the wall cracked. Metaphorical: "واهي العزالي" — clouds pouring forth rain, i.e., their water-skins have burst open.
- Root: خبر (KHB-R)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Knowledge of a thing from report or direct experience; testing and ascertaining.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الخبر: العلم بالأشياء المعلومة من جهة الخبر" — knowledge of things from the channel of report; "الخبرة المعرفة ببواطن الأمر" — experiential knowledge of the inner realities of affairs.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "خبرت الرجل واختبرته خبرا وخبرة" — I tested the man and gained knowledge of him. Metaphorical: "تخبر عن مجهوله مرآته" — one's mirror reveals his unknown state.
- Root: وفي (W-F-Y)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Completeness, fulfillment, and reaching full measure.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الوافي: الذي بلغ التمام" — that which has attained completion; "أوفى: إذا تمم العهد ولم ينقض حفظه" — fulfilled the covenant and did not breach its preservation.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "درهم واف" — a full-weight dirham. Metaphorical: "أوفى على المائة" — he surpassed a hundred; "توفاه الله" — God took him in full, i.e., completed his term.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — Governing the exclusive restriction of predication, as in "فليس مني ولست منه" (he is not of me, nor am I of him), where the negation establishes complete disassociation.
18:19.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'The Lawful and Prohibited'

22:78.arabic: حرام قطعا لا يلزمه ترك الشراء والأكل فإن ذلك حرج وما في الدين من حرج ويعلم هذا بأنه لما سرق في زمان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم مجن (1) وغل واحد في الغنيمة عباءة (2) لم يمتنع أحد من شراء المجان والعباء في الدنيا وكذلك كل ما سرق وكذلك كان يعرف أن في الناس من يربي في الدراهم والدنانير وما ترك رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ولا الناس الدراهم والدنانير بالكلية (3) وبالجملة إنما تنفك الدنيا عن الحرام إذا عصم الخلق كلهم عن المعاصي وهو محال وإذا لم يشترط هذا في الدنيا لم يشترط أيضا في بلد إلا إذا وقع بين جماعة محصورين بل
22:78.english: If you say: "But every number is restricted (maḥṣūr) in God's knowledge — so what is the limit of the restricted? And if a man wished to enumerate the people of a town, he could do so as well, if he were able" — then know that defining the likes of these matters is not possible; rather, they are only regulated by approximation (taqrīb). So we say: every number which, if all its individuals were gathered upon a single plain, would be difficult for the observer to count by mere glance — like one thousand or two thousand — is unrestricted (ghayr maḥṣūr). And whatever is easy — like ten or twenty — is restricted (maḥṣūr). And between the two extremes there are intermediate cases (awsāṭ) that resemble one another, attaching to one of the two extremes by conjecture (al-ẓann). And whatever falls into doubt, one should seek a ruling from the heart concerning it, for sin is the pricking of the hearts (ḥazāz al-qulūb). And in a station like this, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to Wābiṣah: "Seek a ruling from your heart, even if they give you a ruling — and they give you a ruling — and they give you a ruling." {«استفت قلبك وإن أفتوك وأفتوك وأفتوك»}
22:78.section_title_en: The Second Division: The Forbidden Mixed with the Unrestricted Permissible
22:78.anchors:
- Root: حصر (ḥaṣara)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To confine, restrict, restrain, or hem in; al-ḥaṣūr is one who abstains; the root carries the sense of encircling and binding within limits.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الحصر: التضييق" — restriction is a form of constriction or narrowing; in the Qur'anic context {«واحصروهم»} it means to tighten around someone, and {«حصيرا»} denotes that which confines or restrains.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): "حصرتهم حصرا: حبستهم" — to detain or imprison. The term "maḥṣūr" (restricted/limited) is applied to what is countable and bounded, while "ghayr maḥṣūr" (unrestricted) applies to what exceeds the capacity of enumeration.
- Sibawayh Rule: Restriction and Focused Predication (al-ḥaṣr wa-al-taqyīd bi-innamā) — the syntactic structure of "إنما" confines the predicate to the subject, and here the legal reasoning confines the ruling to the conjunction of two effective causes (ʿillah): preponderance (ghalabah) and necessity (ḥājah).

- Root: بلد (balad)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "البلَدُ: كل موضع مستحيز من الأرض عامر أو غير عامر" — any circumscribed tract of land, inhabited or uninhabited; the plural is bilād.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "البلد: المكان المحيط المحدود المتأثر باجتماع قطانه وإقامتهم فيه" — a place that is encompassed, bounded, and affected by the gathering and residence of its inhabitants.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: a town or land; Metaphorical (majāz): "هي بلدة بيني وبينك" — a severance or separation, indicating distance and disconnection.
- Sibawayh Rule: The syntax of exception and exclusion (al-istithnāʾ) — the phrase "إلا إذا وقع بين جماعة محصورين" restricts the general ruling through a conditional exception, marking the sole case where the prohibition applies.

- Root: رسل (rasala)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To send forth gently and deliberately; a messenger (rasūl) is one dispatched; the root conveys measured, orderly emission.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "أصل الرسل: الانبعاث على التؤدة" — the origin is a calm, measured sending forth; from it derives the sense of proceeding with composure.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "أرسل الله في الأمم رسلا" — God sent messengers to the nations; Metaphorical: "أرسل الله عليهم العذاب" — God loosed chastisement upon them, and "القيح سوء الذكر رسيله" — foul repute is the companion of sin.
- Sibawayh Rule: The construction of legal hypotheticals (al-sharṭ wa-al-jawāb) — "فإن قلت... فاعلم أن" structures an objection-response dialectic, a hallmark of juristic reasoning (uṣūl al-fiqh).

- Root: فتي (fatā)
  * Lisan / Ayn: A young man in his prime; by extension, a servant or slave; the root carries the sense of fresh vigor and capacity.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الفتى الطري من الشباب" — the fresh youth; used metaphorically for the servant, as in {«تراود فتاها عن نفسه»}.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "هذا فتي بين الفتوة وهي الحرية والكرم" — one who is noble and generous; Metaphorical: "لا أفعل ذلك ماكر الفتيان" — an oath formula meaning "as long as the two new moons (the days and nights) alternate," i.e., forever.
- Sibawayh Rule: The derivation of verbal nouns from roots (al-maṣdar) — the term "فتوى" (legal opinion) derives from this root, signifying the authoritative pronouncement of one qualified to clarify what is obscure.
22:78.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'The Lawful and Prohibited'

44:42.arabic: فقال يا رسول الله أهكذا يكون قال نعم والذي نفسي بيده إلا من رحم الله قال فوالذي بعثك بالحق لا أعمل على شيء أبدا (1) وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم إني لا أخاف عليكم أن تشركوا بعدي إنما أخاف عليكم أن تنافسوا (2) وإنما خاف التنافس في المآل ولذلك قال عمر رضي الله عنه في حديث طويل يذكر فيه مال بيت المال إني لم أجد نفسي فيه إلا كالوالى مال اليتيم إن استغنيت استعففت وإن افتقرت أكلت بالمعروف وروي أن ابنا لطاوس افتعل كتابا عن لسانه إلى عمر بن عبد العزيز فأعطاه ثلثمائة دينار فباع طاوس ضيعة له وبعث من ثمنها إلى عمر بثلثمائة دينا
44:42.english: Ibn Abī Thābit said: "I indeed saw the gift of al-Mukhtār to Ibn ʿUmar and Ibn ʿAbbās, and they both accepted it." It was said: "What was it?" He said: "Wealth and clothing."
44:42.section_title_en: On the Permissibility of Accepting Gifts from Tyrannical Rulers — The Evidences of the Permissive School and the Refutation
44:42.anchors:
- Root: قبل (qabila)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To accept, receive, take what is offered; acceptance with the hand or with assent.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Acceptance (qubūl) in the theological sense implies receiving what is due or permissible without transgression; its opposite is rejection (radd).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): taking hold of something offered. Metaphorical (majāz): assenting to a claim or gift.
- Root: ظلم (ẓalama)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To place something in other than its proper place; darkness; wrongdoing.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Ẓulm is the act of transgression against another's right; its root meaning connects to darkness (ẓulmah), as injustice obscures truth.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: deprivation of right. Metaphorical: the tyrant (ẓālim) is one who acts in darkness of judgment; "the ẓālim is in the meaning of the usurer" — a legal analogy (qiyās).
- Root: وزر (wizr)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Burden, heavy load; sin as a burden carried on the back.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The sin (wizr) is that which weighs down the soul; the one who bears it carries its consequence.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: a heavy load. Metaphorical: the burden of transgression borne by the wrongdoer alone.
- Root: ورع (wariʿa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To abstain, refrain from what is doubtful or forbidden; scrupulous piety.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Waraʿ is the abstention of the soul from what is not clearly permissible, a station above mere lawfulness.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: keeping away from filth. Metaphorical: the scrupulous one (wariʿ) keeps his religion pure from doubtful gains.
- Sibawayh Rule: Bāb al-ḥaṣr wa al-taqyīd bi-innamā (Restriction and Focused Predication) — The particle innamā restricts the predicate to the subject alone, as in "their abstention does not indicate prohibition but rather scrupulousness," delimiting the cause.
44:42.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'The Lawful and Prohibited'

111:1.arabic: عيسى وكنى أعداءه فقال {تبت يدا أبي لهب} وأما قولك جلست بإزائي فإني سمعت أمير المؤمنين عليا رضي الله عنه يقول إذا أردت أن تنظر إلى رجل من أهل النار فانظر إلى رجل جالس وحوله قوم قيام فقال له هشام عظني فقال سمعت من أمير المؤمنين علي رضي الله عنه يقول إن في جهنم حيات كالقلال وعقارب كالبغال تلدغ كل أمير لا يعدل في رعيته ثم قام وهرب وعن سفيان الثوري رضي الله عنه قال أدخلت على أبي جعفر المنصور بمنى فقال لي ارفع إلينا حاجتك فقلت له اتق الله فقد ملأت الأرض ظلما وجورا قال فطأطأ رأسه ثم رفعه ف
111:1.english: As for supplicating for him, it is not lawful except to say: "May God set you aright," or "May God grant you success in good deeds," or "May God prolong your life in His obedience," or whatever runs in this course. As for supplicating for his protection, long continuance, and the lavishness of divine favor, along with addressing him as "My master" (al-mawlā) and what is in its meaning, that is not permissible. The Prophet, peace be upon him, said: {«Whoever supplicates for the continuance of a tyrant has loved that God be disobeyed in His earth»} (1)
111:1.section_title_en: On the Etiquette of Entering Upon Tyrannical Rulers and the Obligation of Forbidding Wrong
111:1.anchors:
- Root: ظلم (ẓ-l-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning is to place something in other than its proper place; darkness (ẓulmah) as the privation of light.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Ẓulm (injustice/tyranny) is the act of transgressing the proper boundary (ḥadd) and placing a thing in other than its due locus; it is a form of spiritual darkness.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): to act unjustly. Metaphorical (majāz): "A land that has been wronged" (arḍ maẓlūmah) meaning never dug or cultivated—thus the tyrant leaves the land of justice barren and uncultivated.
- Root: سكن (s-k-n)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To be still, to rest, to dwell; the opposite of motion and agitation.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Sukūn (silence/rest) can be praiseworthy when it is a cessation from falsehood, or blameworthy when it is an abandonment of an obligatory act of forbidding wrong.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical stillness. Metaphorical: the silence of the tongue from speaking the truth, which is a blameworthy stillness of the heart's faculty of command.
- Root: أمر (a-m-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To command; a matter, affair, or situation.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Al-amr bi-al-maʿrūf (commanding the right) is the obligation to enjoin what is recognized as good by the Sacred Law and sound reason.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: to issue a command. Metaphorical: the "command" (amr) of a thing is its very essence or situation, as in "the matter of the polity" (amr al-siyāsah).
- Sibawayh Rule: Rule of Restriction and Focused Predication (Bāb al-Ḥaṣr wa al-Taqyīd bi-innamā) — Used to restrict predicates to specific subjects, as in the author's exclusive focus on the conditions and obligations of entering upon rulers.
111:1.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'The Lawful and Prohibited'

3:105.arabic: احتج هؤلاء بقوله تعالى {ولا تكونوا كالذين تفرقوا واختلفوا} الآية وبقوله تعالى {فألف بين قلوبكم} أمتن على الناس بالسبب المؤلف وهذا ضعيف لأن المراد به تفرق الآراء واختلاف المذاهب في معاني كتاب الله وأصول الشريعة والمراد بالألفة نزع الغوائل من الصدور وهي الأسباب المثيرة للفتن المحركة للخصومات والعزلة لا تنافى ذلك واحتجوا بقوله صلى الله عليه وسلم المؤمن آلف مألوف ولا خير فيمن لا يألف ولا يؤلف (1) وهذا ضعيف لأنه إشارة إلى مذمة سوء الخلق تمتنع بسببه المؤالفة ولا يدخل تحته الحسن الخلق الذي إن خالط ألف وألف و
3:105.english: They (the advocates of total seclusion) argued by His saying, the Exalted: {«And be not like those who became divided and differed»} (3:105) — to the end of the verse. And by His saying, the Exalted: {«And He brought their hearts together»} (8:63) — He bestowed a favor upon mankind through the cause that unites. But this is weak, because what is meant thereby is the divergence of opinions and the disagreement of schools of thought concerning the meanings of the Book of God and the foundations of the Sacred Law. And what is meant by "bringing together" (al-ulfah) is the removal of rancors (al-ghawāʾil) from the breasts — those being the causes that provoke sedition and stir up contentions. And seclusion does not contradict that.
3:105.section_title_en: Section 444 — Refutation of the Isolationists' Proof-Texts from the Qur'an and Sunnah
3:105.anchors:
- Root: هجر (hajara)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To abandon, forsake, or sever relations — whether by body, tongue, or heart; the root carries the sense of definitive separation.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): الهجران is the separation of one from another — by body, by tongue, or by heart. The Quranic usages distinguish between physical abandonment (as in {«واهجروهن في المضاجع»}), verbal/mental rejection (as in {«اتخذوا هذا القرآن مهجورا»}), and the comprehensive sense in {«واهجرهم هجرا جميلا»} — a noble forsaking that avoids harm.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): physical separation and cutting off of contact. Metaphorical (Majaz): the she-camel that refuses the stallion (هجر الفحل) — a cessation of a natural function, applied here to the cessation of social intercourse.
- Root: عله (ʿaliha)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To be bewildered or distracted; related to being occupied away from something. (Contextual note: the root appears in the hadith materials concerning the Prophet's withdrawal from his wives.)
- Root: ضعف (ḍaʿufa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Weakness, feebleness — whether in body, intellect, or resolve.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): الضعف is the opposite of strength; it may be in the soul, the body, or one's condition. Al-Khalil distinguished: الضعف (with dammah) is bodily weakness, while الضعف (with fatḥah) is weakness in intellect and judgment.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical or moral weakness. Metaphorical: "in the folds of the book" (في أضعاف الكتاب) — hidden within the inner recesses, as the isolationists' arguments are weak in their inner structure.
- Root: خلط (khalata)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To mix, blend, or intermingle — whether liquids, solids, or persons in society.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): الخلط is the joining of parts of two or more things; it is more general than al-mazj (fusion). Applied to persons, it denotes social mixing, partnership, and companionship.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: mixing substances. Metaphorical: social intercourse and companionship (خالطت فلانا) — the very thing the isolationist abandons, yet which the believer of good character can undertake without harm.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد (Restriction and Specification) — When a general prohibition (like the hadith against hajr beyond three days) is followed by specific exceptions (the two cases of perceived benefit or safety), the general is carried (maḥmūl) upon the specific, per the established principle of takhṣīṣ al-ʿāmm.
3:105.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'Etiquette of Seclusion'

19:48.arabic: احتجوا بقوله تعالى حكاية عن إبراهيم عليه السلام {وأعتزلكم وما تدعون من دون الله وأدعو ربي} الآية ثم قال تعالى فلما اعتزلهم وما يعبدون من دون الله وهبنا له إسحق ويعقوب وكلا جعلنا نبيا إشارة إلى أن ذلك ببركة العزلة وهذا ضعيف لأن مخالطة الكفار لا فائدة فيها إلا دعوتهم الى الدين وعند اليأس من إجابتهم فلا وجه إلا هجرهم وإنما الكلام في مخالطة المسلمين وما فيها من البركة لما روي أنه قيل يا رسول الله الوضوء من جر مخمر أحب إليك أو من هذه المطاهر التي يتطهر منها الناس فقال بل من هذه المطاهر التماسا لبركة أيدي المسلمين (1) وروي أنه صل
19:48.english: They argued by the saying of Allah Almighty, narrating of Abraham, peace be upon him: {«وَأَعْتَزِلُكُمْ وَمَا تَدْعُونَ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ وَأَدْعُو رَبِّي»} [And I will withdraw from you and what you call upon besides Allah, and I will call upon my Lord] — to the end of the verse. Then Allah Almighty said: {«فَلَمَّا اعْتَزَلَهُمْ وَمَا يَعْبُدُونَ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ وَهَبْنَا لَهُ إِسْحَاقَ وَيَعْقُوبَ وَكُلًّا جَعَلْنَا نَبِيًّا»} [So when he withdrew from them and what they worshipped besides Allah, We granted him Isaac and Jacob, and each We made a prophet] — indicating that this was by the blessing of seclusion.
19:48.section_title_en: Section 446 — On the Evidences for and Against Seclusion (Al-ʿUzlah) and the Refutation of Both Extremes
19:48.anchors:
- Root: عزل (ʿ-z-l)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core root meaning of separation, withdrawal, setting apart; al-iʿtizāl is to remove oneself from company or affairs.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الاعتزال: تجنب الشيء" — seclusion is the shunning of a thing, whether by body or by heart, whether as an act of piety, innocence, or otherwise. It is used in the Qur'an for withdrawing from idolaters {«وَإِذَا اعْتَزَلْتُمُوهُمْ وَمَا يَعْبُدُونَ إِلَّا اللَّهَ»} and from women during menses {«فَاعْتَزِلُوا النِّسَاءَ»}.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah): physical separation from a place or people. Metaphorical (majāz): withdrawal of the heart from worldly concerns or from the company of the corrupt.
- Root: خلط (kh-l-ṭ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Mixing, blending, intermingling; a companion or partner is called khalīṭ because of shared association.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الخلط: هو الجمع بين أجزاء الشيئين فصاعدا" — mixing is the joining of parts of two or more things; extended metaphorically to social mixing (mukhālaṭah) with people.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: mixing substances. Metaphorical: social intercourse, companionship, partnership — "خالطت فلانا، وهو خليطي" (I mixed with so-and-so, and he is my companion).
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد (Restriction and Specification) — The particle innamā restricts predication to a single referent, as in the Prophet's ﷺ saying "إنما العلم بالتعلم" (Knowledge is only attained by learning), which confines the means of acquiring knowledge to learning alone.

25:20.arabic: الحكم في موكبه فبهره ما رأى من حسن حاله وحسن هيئته فتلا قوله تعالى {وجعلنا بعضكم لبعض فتنة أتصبرون} ثم قال بلى أصبر وأرضى وكان فقيرا مقلا فالذي هو في بيته لا يبتلى بمثل هذه الفتن فإن من شاهد زينة الدنيا فأما أن يقوى دينه ويقينه فيصبر الى أن يتجرع مرارة الصبر وهو أمر من الصبر أو تنبعث رغبته فيحتال في طلب الدنيا فيهلك هلاكا مؤبدا أما في الدنيا فبالطمع الذي يخيب في أكثر الأوقات فليس كل من يطلب الدنيا تتيسر له وأما في الآخرة فإيثاره متاع الدنيا على ذكر الله تعالى والتقرب إليه ولذلك قال ابن الإعرابي إذا كان باب الذل من جانب الغنى .
25:20.english: As for the cutting off of people's hope in you, therein lie benefits. For the satisfaction of people is a goal that can never be attained; thus a man's occupation with reforming his own soul is more fitting. Among the easiest and lightest of obligations are attending funerals, visiting the sick, and attending banquets and wedding feasts — yet in these there is the squandering of hours and exposure to afflictions. Moreover, obstacles may hinder one from some of them, and excuses arise in facing them, yet one cannot disclose every excuse. So they say to him: "You fulfilled so-and-so's right, but you fell short regarding our right" — and this becomes a cause of enmity. For it has been said: Whoever does not visit the sick at the time of visiting — they wish for his death, fearing the shame he would bring upon them if he recovered, on account of his having fallen short.
25:20.section_title_en: The Revival of the Religious Sciences — Section 455: On the Fourth through Sixth Benefits of Seclusion
25:20.anchors:
- Root: طمع (ṭamaʿ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core lexical sense of craving, eager desire, and longing for something.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الطمع: نزوع النفس إلى الشيء شهوة له" — the soul's inclination toward a thing out of desire; often censured when it exceeds bounds, for "الطمع طبع" (greed is an innate disposition).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) usage denotes the soul's craving; metaphorical (majāz) usage extends to "أطماع الجند" (soldiers' rations) — that which is hoped for and expected. Here, the term oscillates between the blameworthy craving for worldly goods and the cutting off of such craving as a spiritual virtue.
- Root: دنا (danā)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Nearness in place, time, or rank; the world (al-dunyā) is so named because it is the nearer, lower abode.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الدنو: القرب بالذات، أو بالحكم" — proximity by essence or by judgment; used of place, time, and station. The "lower" (adnā) is contrasted with the "better" (khayr) in {«أتستبدلون الذي هو أدنى بالذي هو خير»} [Al-Baqarah: 61].
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Distinguishes dunuww (nearness) from danāʾah (baseness) — a crucial distinction, for the seclusion sought here is not base withdrawal but a drawing near to God through cutting worldly attachments.
- Root: جنب (janb)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The side or flank; extended metaphorically to mean "beside," "alongside," or "avoiding."
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "ثم يستعار من الناحية التي تليها" — the side is used metaphorically for the region adjacent to it. From this root derives ijtināb (avoidance) — the act of keeping oneself to the side, away from harm.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Majāz: "اتق الله الذي لا جنيبة له" — fear God who has no equal; and "فرطت في جنب الله" — I fell short in God's side (i.e., His due). The root thus carries both the sense of physical separation and the higher spiritual connotation of keeping oneself apart for God's sake.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — The rule governing permissible separation between a preposition and its object, allowing for rhetorical emphasis and periodic sentence structure. Applied here in the extended conditional and causal constructions (fa-inna... fa-fīhi fawāʾid) where the apodosis is deferred for effect.
25:20.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Etiquette of Seclusion'

39:26.arabic: عناء حاضر في الدنيا {ولعذاب الآخرة أكبر لو كانوا يعلمون} فإذن لا تستحب العزلة إلا لمستغرق الأوقات بربه ذكرا وفكرا وعبادة وعلما بحيث لو خالطه الناس لضاعت أوقاته وكثرت آفاته ولتشوشت عليه عباداته فهذه غوائل خفية في اختيار العزلة ينبغي أن تتقي فإنها مهلكات في صور منجيات
39:26.english: Abu Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him, used to say while he was the governor of Medina with firewood upon his head: "Make way for your commander!"
39:26.section_title_en: The Hidden Perils of Seeking People's Approval and the True Nature of Seclusion
39:26.anchors:
- Root: سقط (saqaṭa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To fall, to drop, to be cast down from a height
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The falling away of something from its proper station; used metaphorically for the diminishment of a thing's worth or standing
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: physical falling. Metaphorical: the falling away of esteem, as in "سقط من عينه" (he fell from his eye), meaning he lost all regard in that person's estimation
- Root: رقب (raqaba)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To watch, to observe, to lie in wait for; the watcher who awaits an outcome
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The vigilant observation of one's own soul before God, and the watching of others' opinions as a form of servitude to creation rather than the Creator
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: to watch over something. Metaphorical: to be in anxious expectation, to be held in suspense by the gaze of others
- Root: طمع (ṭamiʿa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To covet, to desire eagerly, to hope for something
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The inclination of the soul toward what it desires; blameworthy when directed toward creation, praiseworthy when directed toward God's mercy
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: the craving of appetite. Metaphorical: the aspiration of the heart toward a hoped-for good
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين المبتدأ والخبر (The Interposition Between Subject and Predicate) — The periodic suspension of the sentence's completion to allow for qualifying clauses, as in "فإذن لا تستحب العزلة إلا لمستغرق الأوقات" where the restriction (istithnāʾ) governs the entire preceding argument.
39:26.topic: Al-Ghazali's epistemic insights into the spiritual heart and inner faith, from 'Etiquette of Seclusion'

44:21.arabic: واحتجوا أيضا بقول موسى عليه السلام {وإن لم تؤمنوا لى فاعتزلون} وأنه فزع إلى العزلة عند اليأس منهم وقال تعالى في أصحاب الكهف وإذا اعتزلتموهم وما يعبدون إلا الله فأووا إلى الكهف ينشر لكم ربكم من رحمته أمرهم بالعزلة وقد اعتزل نبينا صلى الله عليه وسلم قريشا لما آذوه وجفوه ودخل الشعب وامر أصحابه باعتزالهم والهجرة الى أرض الحبشة (3) ثم تلاحقوا به الى المدينة بعد أن أعلى الله كلمته وهذا أيضا اعتزال عن الكفار بعد اليأس منهم فإنه صلى الله عليه وسلم لم يعتزل المسلمين ولا من توقع إسلامه من الكفار وأهل الكهف لم يعت

63:4.arabic: على أمر {يحسبون كل صيحة عليهم هم العدو فاحذرهم} وقد اشتد حرصهم على الدنيا فلا يظنون بغيرهم إلا الحرص عليها قال المتنبي إذا ساء فعل المرء ساءت ظنونه .
63:4.english: For this reason, one of the sages said to another: "Shall I teach you two verses better than ten thousand dirhams?" He asked, "What are they?" He said:
63:4.section_title_en: The Book of Seclusion (Kitāb al-ʿUzlah) — Section 454: The Harms of Social Mixing and the Wisdom of Withdrawal
63:4.anchors:
- Root: جمع (j-m-ʿ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To gather, assemble, bring together; the core sense of drawing things near one another.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theological nuance of communal gathering (ijtimāʿ) as the arena where envy, hypocrisy, and mutual harm are generated; contrasted with the spiritual safety of solitary withdrawal.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (ḥaqīqah) — physical assembly of people; Metaphorical (majāz) — the "gathering" of hidden grudges and stored grievances against a person, as in "أمر بني فلان بجمع" (a concealed matter).
- Root: ظهر (ẓ-h-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The back; to appear, become manifest.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Used metaphorically for bearing burdens — sins weigh upon the back; here, the "back" of a camel or horse is the vehicle of transport that the wicked "break" (ʿaqarū) through misuse, symbolizing how evil companions destroy what carries them.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — the physical back of a riding beast; Metaphorical — "قلبت الأمر ظهرًا لبطن" (turning a matter over), and the notion of people being "mounted" upon one's trust, only to betray it.
- Root: وقد (w-q-d)

  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Fire that burns with intense heat; here, the "fire" of slander (ghībah), envy, and malice that evil companions kindle against the believer.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — kindling a physical fire; Metaphorical — "وقد الحصى" (the pebbles became scorching hot), i.e., the burning intensity of hostility; "قلب وقاد" (a blazing heart) — the inflamed passions of the envious.

  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal — bodily hair; Metaphorical — "استشعر خوفًا" (he felt a deep-seated fear), i.e., the internalization of harmful traits from bad company without conscious awareness.

4:21.arabic: وقال الله تعالى وعاشروهن بالمعروف وقال في تعظيم حقهن وأخذن منكم ميثاقا غليظا {وقال} والصاحب بالجنب قيل هي المرأة وآخر ما وصى به رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ثلاث كان يتكلم بهم حتى تلجلج لسانه وخفي كلامه جعل يقول الصلاة الصلاة وما ملكت أيمانكم لا تكلفوهم ما لا يطيقون الله الله فإنهن عوان في أيديكم يعني أسراء أخذتموهن بأمانة الله واستحللتم فروجهن بكلمة الله (8) وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم من صبر على سوء خلق امرأته أعطاه الله من الأجر مثل ما أعطى أيوب على بلائه ومن صبرت على سوء خلق زوجها أعطاها الله مثل ثواب آسية
4:21.english: The first point of etiquette is the wedding feast (walīmah), and it is recommended (mustaḥabbah). Anas, may God be pleased with him, said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, saw upon ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf, may God be pleased with him, a trace of yellow dye, so he said: {«What is this?»} He replied: "I have married a woman for the weight of a date-stone in gold." He said: "May God bless you. Hold a wedding feast, even if with a single sheep." {«...»} And the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, held a wedding feast for Ṣafiyyah with dates and sawīq (barley porridge). {«...»} And he, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: "The food of the first day is an obligation (ḥaqq), the food of the second day is a Sunnah, and the food of the third day is for show (sumʿah); and whoever seeks to be heard, God will make his deeds heard." {«...»} None raised this hadith except Ziyād ibn ʿAbd Allāh, and it is anomalous (gharīb). It is recommended to offer congratulations to him, and the one who enters upon the husband should say: "May God bless you and shower blessings upon you, and may He bring you both together in goodness." {«...»} Abū Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him, reported that he, may God bless him and grant him peace, commanded this. It is also recommended to make the marriage public (iẓhār al-nikāḥ). He, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: "The distinction between the lawful and the unlawful is the drum and the voice." {«...»} The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: "Announce this marriage, hold it in the mosques, and beat drums for it." {«...»} And on the authority of al-Rubayyiʿ bint Muʿawwidh, she said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came and entered on the morning of my wedding night, and he sat upon my bedding, and we had young girls with us who were beating their drums and lamenting those of my forefathers who had been killed—until one of them said: "And among us is a Prophet who knows what will be tomorrow." He said to her: "Stop this, and say what you were saying before." {«...»}
4:21.section_title_en: On What is Incumbent Upon the Husband and What is Incumbent Upon the Wife
4:21.anchors:
- Root: و ل م (w-l-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The core meaning pertains to the wedding feast (walīmah), derived from the concept of gathering and union.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In theological usage, it signifies the communal meal marking the consummation of a marriage contract, a recommended act of public gratitude.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah) usage denotes the specific feast; metaphorical (Majaz) extension applies to any act of publicizing a joyous occasion.
- Root: ع ش ر (ʿ- sh-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The root denotes association, companionship, and intimacy; the tenth (ʿasharah) of a thing is related, but the primary social sense is cohabitation and mutual dealing.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In the Quranic context of {وَعَاشِرُوهُنَّ بِالْمَعْرُوفِ}, it signifies a sustained, equitable mode of social intercourse grounded in moral rectitude, not mere physical proximity.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah) usage is the act of living together; metaphorical (Majaz) usage elevates it to a standard of ethical conduct (maʿrūf) that defines the marital bond.
- Root: ق س م (q-s-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The root indicates division, apportionment, and distribution; in the marital context, it refers to the equitable division of time among co-wives.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theologically, it is tied to justice (ʿadl) as a divine attribute; for the husband, it is a legal obligation to maintain fairness in material and temporal allotments.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah) usage is the physical act of dividing; metaphorical (Majaz) usage applies to the moral duty of impartiality in affection and provision.
- Root: غ ي ر (gh-y-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The root conveys alteration and change, but in the moral register, it denotes protective jealousy (ghayrah), a state of aversion to the violation of honor.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In Kalam, ghayrah is a praiseworthy emotion when aligned with divine law—jealousy for the sanctity of the family—and blameworthy when it stems from unjust suspicion (sūʾ al-ẓann).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah) usage is the emotional state; metaphorical (Majaz) usage is attributed to God (al-Ghayyār) as a figure for His prohibition of indecencies, distinguishing human passion from divine will.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — Used to isolate specific obligations (e.g., "the third is that he should increase...") and to distinguish categories of jealousy and pride, ensuring precise legal and moral demarcation.

4:34.arabic: وأما إذا كان النشوز من المرأة خاصة فالرجال قوامون على النساء فله أن يؤدبها ويحملها على الطاعة قهرا وكذا إذا كانت تاركة للصلاة فله حملها على الصلاة قهرا ولكن ينبغي أن يتدرج في تأديبها وهو أن يقدم أولا الوعظ والتحذير والتخويف فإن لم ينجح ولاها ظهره في المضجع أو انفرد عنها بالفراش وهجرها وهو في البيت معها من ليلة إلى ثلاث ليال فإن لم ينجح ذلك فيها ضربها ضربا غير مبرح بحيث يؤلمها ولا يكسر لها عظما ولا يدمي لها جسم ولا يضرب وجهها فذلك منهي عنه وقد قيل لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ما حق المرأة على الرجل قال
4:34.english: I say: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, has said: «من كان له امرأتان فمال إلى إحداهما دون الأخرى» — "Whoever has two wives and inclines toward one of them to the exclusion of the other" — and in another wording: «ولم يعدل بينهما جاء يوم القيامة وأحد شقيه مائل» — "and does not act equitably between them, he shall come on the Day of Resurrection with one of his sides leaning."
4:34.section_title_en: The Revival of the Religious Sciences — Book on the Etiquette of Marriage: Section 305 (On Justice Between Co-Wives, Nushuz, and the Etiquette of Intercourse)
4:34.anchors:
- Root: عدل (ʿadl)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning is "to be equal, to balance, to straighten" — the root denotes equity and even-handedness in distribution.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In theological usage, ʿadl is the mean of justice, opposed to jawr (tyranny) — it is the act of placing things in their proper stations.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah) usage pertains to measurable distribution (ʿatāʾ, mabīt); metaphorical (Majāz) usage extends to that which is not under voluntary control, such as love (maḥabbah) and inclination of the heart.
- Root: نشز (nushūz)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The root denotes "rising up" or "elevation"; in marital context it signifies a rising of one spouse against the other in discord or recalcitrance.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Nushūz is the rebellion of one spouse against the bond of obedience and harmony, a moral elevation against the other.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal usage is the physical rising from a place; metaphorical usage is the spiritual/moral rising in defiance.
- Root: وقع (waqʿ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The root denotes "falling" or "occurrence"; in the marital context, it is a euphemism for sexual intercourse.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The term is used in the Quran for the "falling" of an event; here it is a euphemistic transfer (naql) for coitus.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal usage is physical falling; metaphorical usage is the act of intercourse, as in the hadith "لا يقعن أحدكم على امرأته" (Let none of you fall upon his wife like a beast).
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — The particle innamā restricts the predicate to the subject alone, as in the hadith "إنما عليه العدل في العطاء والمبيت" (Upon him is only justice in expenditure and overnight stays), confining the obligation to what is within human capacity.

4:130.arabic: {وإن يتفرقا يغن الله كلا من سعته} الرابع أن لا يفشي سرها لا في الطلاق ولا عند النكاح فقد ورد في إفشاء سر النساء في الخبر الصحيح وعيد عظيم (1) ويروى عن بعض الصالحين أنه أراد طلاق امرأة فقيل له ما الذي يريبك فيها فقال العاقل لا يهتك ستر امرأته فلما طلقها قيل له لم طلقتها فقال مالي ولا مرأة غيري فهذا بيان ما على الزوج
4:130.english: Among those whose many divorces were mentioned from the Messenger of God — peace be upon him — was ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Ḥārith ibn Hishām. Al-Ḥasan entered upon him in his house, and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān honored him greatly, seated him in his own place, and said: "Would you not have sent for me, and I would have come to you?" Al-Ḥasan said: "I have a need." He said: "What is it?" He said: "I have come to you as a suitor for your daughter." ʿAbd al-Raḥmān lowered his head, then raised it and said: "By God, there is no one upon the face of the earth who walks upon it more beloved to me than you. But you know that my daughter is a piece of me (baḍʿah minnī) — what grieves her grieves me, and what delights her delights me — and you are a frequent divorcer (miṭlāq). I fear that you will divorce her, and if you do, I dread that my heart would change toward you in my love — and I would hate for my heart to change toward you, for you are a piece of the Messenger of God — peace be upon him. If you will stipulate that you will not divorce her, I will marry her to you." Al-Ḥasan remained silent, then rose and went out. One of his household said: "I heard him walking and saying: 'ʿAbd al-Raḥmān only wanted to make his daughter a collar around my neck.'"

4:130.anchors:
**
- Root: بضع (baḍʿa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "بضع من الشاة بضعة إذا قطع قطعة" — to cut a piece; the piece itself
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الأصل في هذه الكلمة: البضع وهو جملة من اللحم تبضع، أي: تقطع... وكني بالبضع عن الفرج" — the root denotes a piece of flesh cut off; metaphorically extended to the pudendum, and by further extension to the child as "a piece" of the parent
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas - Majaz/Metaphorical): "من رضع معك رضعه، فهو منك بضعه، أي هو بعضك" — the child is "a piece" (baḍʿah) of the father, as though cut from him, sharing his substance and nature
- Root: طلق (ṭalaqa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "متحرك. وطَلْقٌ وطَلَق: اسمان" — the core sense of release from a tether
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "أصل الطلاق: التخلية من الوثاق... ومنه استعير: طلقت المرأة، نحو: خليتها فهي طالق، أي: مخلاة عن حبالة النكاح" — divorce is the release from the bond of marriage, as releasing a camel from its hobble
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas - Haqiqah/Literal): "أطلقت الأسير، وهو طليق" — literal release of a captive; "طلقت المرأة وطلقت فهي طالق وهن طوالق" — metaphorical extension to the divorced woman
- Root: حسن (ḥasana)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "المَلقَة" — beauty, goodness
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الحسن: عبارة عن كل مبهج مرغوب فيه" — that which pleases and is desired; "الحسنة يعبر عنها عن كل ما يسر" — a good thing is what brings joy
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas - Majaz/Metaphorical): "اجلس حسنا" — used adverbially for "well"; "فلان لا يحسن شيئا" — to do well, to master
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — the permissibility of interposing elements between a governing word and its governed prepositional phrase when the intervening material constitutes a complete, self-sufficient clause, as in the conditional constructions employed in the marriage stipulation narrative

6:151.arabic: ولأجل غيرة الله تعالى حرم الفواحش ما ظهر منها وما بطن ولا أحد أحب إليه العذر من الله ولذلك بعث المنذرين والمبشرين ولا أحد أحب إليه المدح من الله ولأجل ذلك وعد الجنة وقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم رأيت ليلة أسري بي في الجنة قصرا وبفنائه جارية فقلت لمن هذا القصر فقيل لعمر فأردت أن أنظر إليها فذكرت غيرتك يا عمر فبكى عمر وقال أعليك أغار يا رسول الله (6) وكان الحسن يقول أتدعون نساءكم ليزاحمن العلوج في الأسواق قبح الله من لا يغار وقال عليه الصلاة والسلام إن من الغيرة ما يحبه الله ومنها ما يبغ
6:151.english: The first point of etiquette is the wedding feast (walīmah), and it is recommended (mustaḥabbah). Anas, may God be pleased with him, said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, saw upon ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf, may God be pleased with him, a trace of yellow dye, so he said: {«What is this?»} He replied: "I have married a woman for the weight of a date-stone in gold." He said: "May God bless you. Hold a wedding feast, even if with a single sheep." {«...»} And the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, held a wedding feast for Ṣafiyyah with dates and sawīq (barley porridge). {«...»} And he, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: "The food of the first day is an obligation (ḥaqq), the food of the second day is a Sunnah, and the food of the third day is for show (sumʿah); and whoever seeks to be heard, God will make his deeds heard." {«...»} None raised this hadith except Ziyād ibn ʿAbd Allāh, and it is anomalous (gharīb). It is recommended to offer congratulations to him, and the one who enters upon the husband should say: "May God bless you and shower blessings upon you, and may He bring you both together in goodness." {«...»} Abū Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him, reported that he, may God bless him and grant him peace, commanded this. It is also recommended to make the marriage public (iẓhār al-nikāḥ). He, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: "The distinction between the lawful and the unlawful is the drum and the voice." {«...»} The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: "Announce this marriage, hold it in the mosques, and beat drums for it." {«...»} And on the authority of al-Rubayyiʿ bint Muʿawwidh, she said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came and entered on the morning of my wedding night, and he sat upon my bedding, and we had young girls with us who were beating their drums and lamenting those of my forefathers who had been killed—until one of them said: "And among us is a Prophet who knows what will be tomorrow." He said to her: "Stop this, and say what you were saying before." {«...»}
6:151.section_title_en: On What is Incumbent Upon the Husband and What is Incumbent Upon the Wife
6:151.anchors:
- Root: و ل م (w-l-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The core meaning pertains to the wedding feast (walīmah), derived from the concept of gathering and union.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In theological usage, it signifies the communal meal marking the consummation of a marriage contract, a recommended act of public gratitude.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah) usage denotes the specific feast; metaphorical (Majaz) extension applies to any act of publicizing a joyous occasion.
- Root: ع ش ر (ʿ- sh-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The root denotes association, companionship, and intimacy; the tenth (ʿasharah) of a thing is related, but the primary social sense is cohabitation and mutual dealing.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In the Quranic context of {وَعَاشِرُوهُنَّ بِالْمَعْرُوفِ}, it signifies a sustained, equitable mode of social intercourse grounded in moral rectitude, not mere physical proximity.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah) usage is the act of living together; metaphorical (Majaz) usage elevates it to a standard of ethical conduct (maʿrūf) that defines the marital bond.
- Root: ق س م (q-s-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The root indicates division, apportionment, and distribution; in the marital context, it refers to the equitable division of time among co-wives.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theologically, it is tied to justice (ʿadl) as a divine attribute; for the husband, it is a legal obligation to maintain fairness in material and temporal allotments.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah) usage is the physical act of dividing; metaphorical (Majaz) usage applies to the moral duty of impartiality in affection and provision.
- Root: غ ي ر (gh-y-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The root conveys alteration and change, but in the moral register, it denotes protective jealousy (ghayrah), a state of aversion to the violation of honor.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In Kalam, ghayrah is a praiseworthy emotion when aligned with divine law—jealousy for the sanctity of the family—and blameworthy when it stems from unjust suspicion (sūʾ al-ẓann).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah) usage is the emotional state; metaphorical (Majaz) usage is attributed to God (al-Ghayyār) as a figure for His prohibition of indecencies, distinguishing human passion from divine will.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — Used to isolate specific obligations (e.g., "the third is that he should increase...") and to distinguish categories of jealousy and pride, ensuring precise legal and moral demarcation.

8:73.arabic: وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا أتاكم من ترضون دينه وأمانته فزوجوه إلا تفعلوه تكن فتنة في الأرض وفساد كبير (7) وهذا أيضا تعليل الترغيب لخوف الفساد وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم من نكح لله وأنكح لله استحق ولاية الله (8) وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم من تزوج فقد أحرز شطر دينه فليتق الله في الشطر الثاني (9) وهذا أيضا إشارة إلى أن فضيلته لأجل التحرز من المخالفة تحصنا من الفساد فكأن المفسد لدين المرء في الأغلب فرجه وبطنه وقد كفى بالتزويج أحدهما وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم كل عمل ابن آدم ينقطع إلا ثلاث ولد صالح يدعو له (10)
8:73.english: As for the verses [of the Qur'an], God Most High has said: {وانكحوا الأيامى منكم} ("And marry the unmarried among you") — and this is a command. And He Most High said: {فلا تعضلوهن أن ينكحن أزواجهن} ("Then do not prevent them from marrying their husbands") — and this is a prohibition against prevention (al-ʿaḍl) and a forbiddance of it.
8:73.section_title_en: Section 294 — Encouragement of Marriage (الترغيب في النكاح)
8:73.anchors:
- Root: رغب (raghiba)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning denotes "capacity/amplitude" — a vessel or receptacle that is wide and receptive; by extension, the inclination of desire toward something with expansive longing.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الرغبة والرغب والرغبى: السعة في الإرادة" — the amplitude of the will. When said "رغب فيه" it necessitates eagerness for it; when said "رغب عنه" it implies the turning away of desire and renunciation (zuhd) of it.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): "هو راغب فيه وراغب عنه" — one is desirous of a thing or averse to it. Metaphorical (Majaz): "واد رغيب: كثير الأخذ للماء" — a valley that takes much water; thus the Prophet's "من رغب عن سنتي" is a metaphorical extension: one who turns his desire away from the Sunnah, refusing its amplitude.
- Root: زوج (zawj)
  * Lisan / Ayn: A pair; each of the two counterparts in a mating couple. Al-Raghib: "يقال لكل واحد من القرينين من الذكر والأنثى في الحيوانات المتزاوجة زوج" — each of the two paired ones, male and female, is called a zawj.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "ولكل ما يقترن بآخر مماثلا له أو مضاد زوج" — everything that is coupled with another, whether similar or opposite, is a pair. "وزوجة لغة رديئة" — the form zawjah is a poor dialectal variant.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "هو زوجها وهي زوجه وزوجته، وهما زوجان" — he is her pair and she is his pair. Metaphorical: "تزاوج الكلامان وازدوجا" — two speeches are paired/coupled; thus marriage is the pairing of two complementary beings.
- Root: منع (manaʿa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To withhold, prevent, or protect. Al-Raghib: "المنع يقال في ضد العطية" — said in opposition to giving; and "يقال في الحماية" — said of protection/defense.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "مكان منيع" — an impregnable place; "فلان ذو منعة" — one who is mighty, protected against those who seek him.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "منعه الشيء ومنعه منه وعنه" — to prevent someone from a thing. Metaphorical: "فلان يمنع الجار: يحميه من أن يضام" — he protects the neighbor from being wronged. Thus "عضل" (prevention of marriage) is the withholding of a woman from her lawful marriage — a form of harmful prevention.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد (Restriction & Focused Predication) — The Prophet's statements "النكاح سنتي" and "من رغب عن سنتي فقد رغب عني" employ restrictive predication: the Sunnah is defined by marriage, and aversion to it is equated with aversion to the Prophet himself — a rhetorical equation establishing identity between the act and its source.

12:23.arabic: فقالت له التي هو في بيتها لقد أقمأتك إذ ردت عليك هديتك (5) أي أذلتك واستصغرتك فقال صلى الله عليه وسلم أنتن أهون على الله أن تقمئنني ثم غضب عليهن كلهن شهرا إلى أن عاد إليهن العاشر في آداب الجماع ويستحب أن يبدأ باسم الله تعالى ويقرأ قل هو الله أحد أولا ويكبر ويهلل ويقول بسم الله العلي العظيم اللهم اجعلها ذرية طيبة إن كنت قدرت أن تخرج ذلك من صلبي وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم لو أن أحدكم إذا أتى أهله قال اللهم جنبني الشيطان وجنب الشيطان ما رزقتنا فإن كان بينهما ولد لم يضره PageV02
12:23.english: I say: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, has said: «من كان له امرأتان فمال إلى إحداهما دون الأخرى» — "Whoever has two wives and inclines toward one of them to the exclusion of the other" — and in another wording: «ولم يعدل بينهما جاء يوم القيامة وأحد شقيه مائل» — "and does not act equitably between them, he shall come on the Day of Resurrection with one of his sides leaning."
12:23.section_title_en: The Revival of the Religious Sciences — Book on the Etiquette of Marriage: Section 305 (On Justice Between Co-Wives, Nushuz, and the Etiquette of Intercourse)
12:23.anchors:
- Root: عدل (ʿadl)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning is "to be equal, to balance, to straighten" — the root denotes equity and even-handedness in distribution.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In theological usage, ʿadl is the mean of justice, opposed to jawr (tyranny) — it is the act of placing things in their proper stations.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah) usage pertains to measurable distribution (ʿatāʾ, mabīt); metaphorical (Majāz) usage extends to that which is not under voluntary control, such as love (maḥabbah) and inclination of the heart.
- Root: نشز (nushūz)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The root denotes "rising up" or "elevation"; in marital context it signifies a rising of one spouse against the other in discord or recalcitrance.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Nushūz is the rebellion of one spouse against the bond of obedience and harmony, a moral elevation against the other.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal usage is the physical rising from a place; metaphorical usage is the spiritual/moral rising in defiance.
- Root: وقع (waqʿ)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The root denotes "falling" or "occurrence"; in the marital context, it is a euphemism for sexual intercourse.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): The term is used in the Quran for the "falling" of an event; here it is a euphemistic transfer (naql) for coitus.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal usage is physical falling; metaphorical usage is the act of intercourse, as in the hadith "لا يقعن أحدكم على امرأته" (Let none of you fall upon his wife like a beast).
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — The particle innamā restricts the predicate to the subject alone, as in the hadith "إنما عليه العدل في العطاء والمبيت" (Upon him is only justice in expenditure and overnight stays), confining the obligation to what is within human capacity.
12:23.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications, prayers, and their spiritual power, from 'Etiquette of Marriage'

12:25.arabic: فقال تعالى وألفيا سيدها لدى الباب فإذا انقلب السيد مسخرا فقد بدل نعمة الله كفرا ونفس المرأة على مثال نفسك إن أرسلت عنانها قليلا جمحت بك طويلا وإن أرخيت عذارها فترا جذبتك ذراعا وإن كبحتها وشددت يدك عليها في محل الشدة ملكتها قال الشافعي رضي الله عنه ثلاثة إن أكرمتهم أهانوك وإن أهنتهم أكرموك المرأة والخادم والنبطي أراد به إن محضت الإكرام ولم تمزج غلظك بلينك وفظاظتك برفقك وكانت نساء العرب يعلمن بناتهن اختبار الأزواج وكانت المرأة تقول لابنتها اختبري زوجك قبل الإقدام والجراء

It is recommended to offer congratulations to him, and the one who enters upon the husband should say: "May God bless you and shower blessings upon you, and may He bring you both together in goodness." {«...»} Abū Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him, reported that he, may God bless him and grant him peace, commanded this. It is also recommended to make the marriage public (iẓhār al-nikāḥ). He, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: "The distinction between the lawful and the unlawful is the drum and the voice." {«...»} The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: "Announce this marriage, hold it in the mosques, and beat drums for it." {«...»} And on the authority of al-Rubayyiʿ bint Muʿawwidh, she said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came and entered on the morning of my wedding night, and he sat upon my bedding, and we had young girls with us who were beating their drums and lamenting those of my forefathers who had been killed—until one of them said: "And among us is a Prophet who knows what will be tomorrow." He said to her: "Stop this, and say what you were saying before." {«...»}
12:25.section_title_en: On What is Incumbent Upon the Husband and What is Incumbent Upon the Wife
12:25.anchors:
- Root: و ل م (w-l-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The core meaning pertains to the wedding feast (walīmah), derived from the concept of gathering and union.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In theological usage, it signifies the communal meal marking the consummation of a marriage contract, a recommended act of public gratitude.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah) usage denotes the specific feast; metaphorical (Majaz) extension applies to any act of publicizing a joyous occasion.
- Root: ع ش ر (ʿ- sh-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The root denotes association, companionship, and intimacy; the tenth (ʿasharah) of a thing is related, but the primary social sense is cohabitation and mutual dealing.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In the Quranic context of {وَعَاشِرُوهُنَّ بِالْمَعْرُوفِ}, it signifies a sustained, equitable mode of social intercourse grounded in moral rectitude, not mere physical proximity.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah) usage is the act of living together; metaphorical (Majaz) usage elevates it to a standard of ethical conduct (maʿrūf) that defines the marital bond.
- Root: ق س م (q-s-m)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The root indicates division, apportionment, and distribution; in the marital context, it refers to the equitable division of time among co-wives.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): Theologically, it is tied to justice (ʿadl) as a divine attribute; for the husband, it is a legal obligation to maintain fairness in material and temporal allotments.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah) usage is the physical act of dividing; metaphorical (Majaz) usage applies to the moral duty of impartiality in affection and provision.
- Root: غ ي ر (gh-y-r)
  * Lisan / Ayn: The root conveys alteration and change, but in the moral register, it denotes protective jealousy (ghayrah), a state of aversion to the violation of honor.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): In Kalam, ghayrah is a praiseworthy emotion when aligned with divine law—jealousy for the sanctity of the family—and blameworthy when it stems from unjust suspicion (sūʾ al-ẓann).
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah) usage is the emotional state; metaphorical (Majaz) usage is attributed to God (al-Ghayyār) as a figure for His prohibition of indecencies, distinguishing human passion from divine will.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد بإنما (Restriction & Focused Predication) — Used to isolate specific obligations (e.g., "the third is that he should increase...") and to distinguish categories of jealousy and pride, ensuring precise legal and moral demarcation.

13:38.arabic: وقال تعالى في وصف الرسل ومدحهم ولقد أرسلنا رسلا من قبلك وجعلنا لهم أزواجا وذرية فذكر ذلك في معرض الامتنان وإظهار الفضل ومدح أولياءه بسؤال ذلك في الدعاء فقال والذين يقولون ربنا هب لنا من أزواجنا وذرياتنا قرة أعين الآية ويقال أن الله تعالى لم يذكر في كتابه من الأنبياء إلا المتأهلين فقالوا إن يحيى صلى الله عليه وسلم قد تزوج ولم يجامع قيل إنما فعل ذلك لنيل الفضل وإقامة السنة وقيل لغض البصر وأما عيسى عليه السلام فإنه سينكح إذا نزل الأرض ويولد له وأما الأخبار فقوله صلى الله عليه وسلم النكاح سنتي فمن رغب عن سنتي فق
13:38.english: As for the verses [of the Qur'an], God Most High has said: {وانكحوا الأيامى منكم} ("And marry the unmarried among you") — and this is a command. And He Most High said: {فلا تعضلوهن أن ينكحن أزواجهن} ("Then do not prevent them from marrying their husbands") — and this is a prohibition against prevention (al-ʿaḍl) and a forbiddance of it.
13:38.section_title_en: Section 294 — Encouragement of Marriage (الترغيب في النكاح)
13:38.anchors:
- Root: رغب (raghiba)
  * Lisan / Ayn: Core meaning denotes "capacity/amplitude" — a vessel or receptacle that is wide and receptive; by extension, the inclination of desire toward something with expansive longing.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الرغبة والرغب والرغبى: السعة في الإرادة" — the amplitude of the will. When said "رغب فيه" it necessitates eagerness for it; when said "رغب عنه" it implies the turning away of desire and renunciation (zuhd) of it.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal (Haqiqah): "هو راغب فيه وراغب عنه" — one is desirous of a thing or averse to it. Metaphorical (Majaz): "واد رغيب: كثير الأخذ للماء" — a valley that takes much water; thus the Prophet's "من رغب عن سنتي" is a metaphorical extension: one who turns his desire away from the Sunnah, refusing its amplitude.
- Root: زوج (zawj)
  * Lisan / Ayn: A pair; each of the two counterparts in a mating couple. Al-Raghib: "يقال لكل واحد من القرينين من الذكر والأنثى في الحيوانات المتزاوجة زوج" — each of the two paired ones, male and female, is called a zawj.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "ولكل ما يقترن بآخر مماثلا له أو مضاد زوج" — everything that is coupled with another, whether similar or opposite, is a pair. "وزوجة لغة رديئة" — the form zawjah is a poor dialectal variant.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "هو زوجها وهي زوجه وزوجته، وهما زوجان" — he is her pair and she is his pair. Metaphorical: "تزاوج الكلامان وازدوجا" — two speeches are paired/coupled; thus marriage is the pairing of two complementary beings.
- Root: منع (manaʿa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: To withhold, prevent, or protect. Al-Raghib: "المنع يقال في ضد العطية" — said in opposition to giving; and "يقال في الحماية" — said of protection/defense.
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "مكان منيع" — an impregnable place; "فلان ذو منعة" — one who is mighty, protected against those who seek him.
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas): Literal: "منعه الشيء ومنعه منه وعنه" — to prevent someone from a thing. Metaphorical: "فلان يمنع الجار: يحميه من أن يضام" — he protects the neighbor from being wronged. Thus "عضل" (prevention of marriage) is the withholding of a woman from her lawful marriage — a form of harmful prevention.
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الحصر والتقييد (Restriction & Focused Predication) — The Prophet's statements "النكاح سنتي" and "من رغب عن سنتي فقد رغب عني" employ restrictive predication: the Sunnah is defined by marriage, and aversion to it is equated with aversion to the Prophet himself — a rhetorical equation establishing identity between the act and its source.
13:38.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications, prayers, and their spiritual power, from 'Etiquette of Marriage'

15:5.arabic: الباعث في حقه ويبقى ما سبق من أمر الولد فإن ذلك عام إلا للممسوح وهو نادر ومن الطباع ما تغلب عليها الشهوة بحيث لا تحصنه المرأة الواحدة فيستحب لصاحبها الزيادة على الواحدة إلى الأربع فإن يسر الله له مودة ورحمة واطمأن قلبه بهن وإلا فيستحب له الاستبدال فقد نكح علي رضي الله عنه بعد وفاة فاطمة عليها السلام بسبع ليال ويقال إن الحسن بن علي كان منكاحا حتى نكح زيادة على مائتي امرأة وكان ربما عقد على أربع في وقت واحد وربما طلق أربعا في وقت واحد واستبدل بهن وقد قال صلى الله عليه وسلم للح
15:5.english: وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم: "لا يلقى الله أحد بذنب أعظم من جهالة أهله."
15:5.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'Etiquette of Marriage'

23:43.arabic: الباعث في حقه ويبقى ما سبق من أمر الولد فإن ذلك عام إلا للممسوح وهو نادر ومن الطباع ما تغلب عليها الشهوة بحيث لا تحصنه المرأة الواحدة فيستحب لصاحبها الزيادة على الواحدة إلى الأربع فإن يسر الله له مودة ورحمة واطمأن قلبه بهن وإلا فيستحب له الاستبدال فقد نكح علي رضي الله عنه بعد وفاة فاطمة عليها السلام بسبع ليال ويقال إن الحسن بن علي كان منكاحا حتى نكح زيادة على مائتي امرأة وكان ربما عقد على أربع في وقت واحد وربما طلق أربعا في وقت واحد واستبدل بهن وقد قال صلى الله عليه وسلم للح
23:43.english: وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم: "لا يلقى الله أحد بذنب أعظم من جهالة أهله."
23:43.topic: Prophetic traditions and scholastic commentary by Al-Ghazali, from 'Etiquette of Marriage'

24:32.arabic: الغنى في الفراق والنكاح جميعا فقال {وأنكحوا الأيامى منكم والصالحين من عبادكم وإمائكم إن يكونوا فقراء يغنهم الله من فضله} وقال سبحانه وتعالى {وإن يتفرقا يغن الله كلا من سعته} الرابع أن لا يفشي سرها لا في الطلاق ولا عند النكاح فقد ورد في إفشاء سر النساء في الخبر الصحيح وعيد عظيم (1) ويروى عن بعض الصالحين أنه أراد طلاق امرأة فقيل له ما الذي يريبك فيها فقال العاقل لا يهتك ستر امرأته فلما طلقها قيل له لم طلقتها فقال مالي ولا مرأة غيري فهذا بيان ما على الزوج
24:32.english: Among those whose many divorces were mentioned from the Messenger of God — peace be upon him — was ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Ḥārith ibn Hishām. Al-Ḥasan entered upon him in his house, and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān honored him greatly, seated him in his own place, and said: "Would you not have sent for me, and I would have come to you?" Al-Ḥasan said: "I have a need." He said: "What is it?" He said: "I have come to you as a suitor for your daughter." ʿAbd al-Raḥmān lowered his head, then raised it and said: "By God, there is no one upon the face of the earth who walks upon it more beloved to me than you. But you know that my daughter is a piece of me (baḍʿah minnī) — what grieves her grieves me, and what delights her delights me — and you are a frequent divorcer (miṭlāq). I fear that you will divorce her, and if you do, I dread that my heart would change toward you in my love — and I would hate for my heart to change toward you, for you are a piece of the Messenger of God — peace be upon him. If you will stipulate that you will not divorce her, I will marry her to you." Al-Ḥasan remained silent, then rose and went out. One of his household said: "I heard him walking and saying: 'ʿAbd al-Raḥmān only wanted to make his daughter a collar around my neck.'"
24:32.section_title_en: ** On the Husband's Obligations: The Fourth Duty — Concealing the Wife's Secrets, and the Narratives Concerning al-Ḥasan's Many Divorces
24:32.anchors:
**
- Root: بضع (baḍʿa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "بضع من الشاة بضعة إذا قطع قطعة" — to cut a piece; the piece itself
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الأصل في هذه الكلمة: البضع وهو جملة من اللحم تبضع، أي: تقطع... وكني بالبضع عن الفرج" — the root denotes a piece of flesh cut off; metaphorically extended to the pudendum, and by further extension to the child as "a piece" of the parent
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas - Majaz/Metaphorical): "من رضع معك رضعه، فهو منك بضعه، أي هو بعضك" — the child is "a piece" (baḍʿah) of the father, as though cut from him, sharing his substance and nature
- Root: طلق (ṭalaqa)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "متحرك. وطَلْقٌ وطَلَق: اسمان" — the core sense of release from a tether
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "أصل الطلاق: التخلية من الوثاق... ومنه استعير: طلقت المرأة، نحو: خليتها فهي طالق، أي: مخلاة عن حبالة النكاح" — divorce is the release from the bond of marriage, as releasing a camel from its hobble
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas - Haqiqah/Literal): "أطلقت الأسير، وهو طليق" — literal release of a captive; "طلقت المرأة وطلقت فهي طالق وهن طوالق" — metaphorical extension to the divorced woman
- Root: حسن (ḥasana)
  * Lisan / Ayn: "المَلقَة" — beauty, goodness
  * Al-Raghib (Mufradat): "الحسن: عبارة عن كل مبهج مرغوب فيه" — that which pleases and is desired; "الحسنة يعبر عنها عن كل ما يسر" — a good thing is what brings joy
  * Al-Zamakhshari (Asas - Majaz/Metaphorical): "اجلس حسنا" — used adverbially for "well"; "فلان لا يحسن شيئا" — to do well, to master
- Sibawayh Rule: باب الفصل بين الجار والمجرور (Prepositional Interposition) — the permissibility of interposing elements between a governing word and its governed prepositional phrase when the intervening material constitutes a complete, self-sufficient clause, as in the conditional constructions employed in the marriage stipulation narrative

---
